question: Is a child who will even do a favor for a stranger considered a pleasing personality?
description: Is it considered a pleasing personality when a child sees an adult helping to hold the door as he or she exits the front door of the neighborhood?

answers.answer_text: Subject, hello wow hugs to you* Is a child who will even do favors for strangers considered a pleasing personality? I don't think it can be judged in such a one-sided way. -First of all, what is a pleasing personality? (Often trying to take care of other people's emotions, paying too much attention to others at the expense of themselves, and not learning to say no even when they are uncomfortable. The most important characteristic of the people pleaser is that they hide their emotions and are so afraid of conflict that they suppress their own needs. Pleasing personalities also often apologize, pretend to agree with others, etc.). So one of the biggest bases for judging is how the child felt after she did the behavior. Was she uncomfortable? Did she do it voluntarily? Did she do the behavior purely out of pleasure? ...... So we can't tell if a child is a pleasing personality based on one behavior alone. If you find that your child has a tendency to be a people pleaser, it is recommended that you ① set small goals for your child and accomplish them step by step. The reason for this is that behind the pleasing personality is a lack of self-confidence. So when a small goal is accomplished, the child's self-confidence will gradually increase. ②Cultivate your child to say "no" Tell your child that she can reasonably refuse to do something she doesn't want to do. If someone hates her because of this, it is that person's problem, not her own, and it will not affect her ability to be a popular person. ③ Let your child try some more equal interpersonal communication usually with your child also learn to try to communicate as equals, listen to her ideas, and do not pass on the idea that if she doesn't please you, you can abandon her at any time. Good luck!

When I read your description, my first thought was that the child is very understanding and good at taking care of others, so I'm curious as to why you would interpret this behavior as a "pleasing personality". question: What about a knot that wasn't created and doesn't accept being less than human?

After all these years, I'm still very afraid of feeling less than others, and I realize now that I was caught up in a feeling of being less than others, which turned out to be less than him. Ugh, almost didn't make me angry, what should I do, I can't possibly get him here anymore, than once, right, is my life going to be full of regrets until old age

The important thing is not the fact but the feeling that you are well aware and have realized that "I am stuck in a feeling of inferiority". This made you very depressed for a while. So you bravely came to ask for help. You feel that "the feeling of being less than others is too hard", so you have been in a state of defense against being less than others. I'm curious, you think I've gotten over it, but you're really just forgetting about it. So, has anything happened recently that made you relive the past? Did you have a similar feeling or encounter a similar situation? There is a saying that there is nothing new under the sun. Psychology says: It's not the facts that matter, it's how the facts feel. The past incident back then may have left you with low self-esteem, and over the years, you may have been good enough to feel that you have overcome this trauma. But because it didn't address the trauma and feelings that the incident brought you, it formed an emotional button, psychologically called a [complex]. As soon as something similar happens, this emotional button is triggered and activates this feeling that sticks with you. Seeing is Healing expression is healing well in that you have become acutely aware of this complex. Seeing is Healing begins, you don't need to get the person back, you just need to see that feeling of low self-esteem from that year and heal it to bring yourself back. ****** You can use the empty chair technique to set up an empty chair in a room, imagine that the person from that year is sitting in this chair and you are standing across from him, and express what you want to say to him from that year, mainly expressing your feelings. When the emotions are out, you may have a different experience. ****** I noticed in your reply that you expressed the idea of wanting to outdo him for once. This can be expressed by positively visualizing a scenario where you surpass the other person to heal yourself and release your feelings. ****** everyday situations, you can further increase your awareness. Recognize emotions through positive thinking meditation, etc. Understand where emotions come from and what kind of impact they have on the past and present. Seeing is the beginning of healing, good luck.

question: It's hard for me to force myself to be nice to my husband and he doesn't accept it, what should I do?

It was late and I saw that the flesh of the grapefruit was still there and he hadn't eaten it, so I got very angry and said that I had worked hard to bring it back to you, and if you didn't eat it, I would never bring you good food again. The fact that you are able to realize that this is your mistake proves that you are not a unreasonable person. The question is how you change your perception. I can sense that you don't want to put the cart before the horse every time your good intentions or occasional thoughtfulness are met with an argument! @ Here I recommend a book to you, The Courage to be Hated. At first you may think the statements in the book are ridiculous or incomprehensible, but as you keep reading you may come to agree with them. The book says that the world is so simple, if only we change some of our perceptions. The book talks about the issue of life issues, that is, the issue of separating oneself from others, drawing boundaries but not separating them. Doing so allows one to become free and less prone to emotions or distress over others. ○All of one's altruistic behaviors are actually for the benefit of oneself. We reap the benefits of fulfillment, happiness, and belonging when we feel that we are in a place in society that brings value to others. Imagine when you think, "Hubby likes it, no one wants the rest, bring it back." When you make this move, your heart is not an anticipation, the mental expectation of the other person to receive a happy smile, praise you, and the pleasure of tasting; at the same time you also avoid wasting food ...... If you do not expect these, then the other person did not respond or accept the reason why you will be angry? Why can't you be consistent if your original intention was to love and care for the other person? You could very well look at it from the subject's point of view. You are acting altruistically which is your own choice, a move you are making for some need of your own, (even if it is to take care of your family) which is a desire of yours; and your husband's response to that is his own subject matter, which is about how he feels about it, as well as about a lot of factors you are not sure about. <<When we separate the issues we don't agonize over them, you just take charge of your own and you've accomplished what you need to. It is only when you are not attached to the feedback of others that you can be truly free. @You may feel that you are angry because you feel that having your good intentions rejected hurts your self-esteem. When you come across results that don't fulfill expectations, you may start to get anxious and angry, especially with people close to you. Because of the panic of insecurity you will spontaneously attack. ○But subject you seem to have neglected to ask the other person why, maybe they are too full, maybe they just don't have an appetite, maybe they are having a bad day, or maybe they don't like to eat food that has been left out ...... even if they are really demeaning and ungrateful. question: How do you fix being overly sensitive and caring too much about other people's feelings and judgments?
description: Too sensitive, too concerned about other people's feelings of evaluation, walking on the road is also very concerned about other people's eyes. What to do? Is there any solution?

answers.answer_text: Hello! People with sensitive personalities usually have a phenomenon of over-interpretation of what is happening in the outside world. Each of us will inevitably have the psychological tendency to be sensitive to how others perceive us. This psychological trait is the self-protection instinct of human beings, is the result of the social development of human animal attributes, as an individual human being to obtain progress, integration into society as a guarantee mechanism. However, if a person is too sensitive and suspicious, heavily entangled in other people's views of their own, then not only live a very tired, but also will be cocooned, difficult to extricate themselves. Obviously a small insignificant thing, but in the eyes of people with sensitive character, as if holding a magnifying glass to see the world. All the small things become big things, all the unhappy are infinitely enlarged. In fact, everyone's character has this or that problem, some people are born sensitive, some people are born big. But there is no perfection in every personality.  Trying to gain validation and presence from external judgment is no longer about you, but about being a "puppet" of others, who can control your emotions with a casual remark. But in fact, others may not care so much about you, maybe just a casual comment, for yourself, you are the most important, do not have to live for other people's views and evaluation. Psychologist Adler said: our troubles and sufferings are not because of the things themselves, but because of the perceptions we put on these things. Other people's comments in itself is nothing, mainly in their own feelings, for example, for negative comments, nervous people feel like how to say how to say it, and continue to do what I do; low self-esteem and sensitive people will be thinking I am not doing what is not good enough, what can I do to make the other side satisfied? This often puts you in a painful situation, while the person making the comment is not affected at all. ️ Acknowledge and accept your imperfections, embrace the strengths and weaknesses in yourself yourself, recognize them and accept them yourself. Thus giving yourself the opportunity to build on what you have in yourself and improve what you don't have in yourself. Thus, you will be able to listen to the true monologue of your own heart, and you will be able to reach the depths of your heart with happiness. In this way, you don't have to deeply disguise yourself, hide the deficiencies in yourself, and let yourself live with a tired heart and body. 🧡 Encourage yourself constantly. Mentally suggest to yourself that I am the best, I am unique in this world. When you start valuing yourself and focusing on your inner self, you keep giving yourself confidence in all parts of your life. When you have self-confidence, you will naturally work hard and smoothly, and that inner ease and joy will also flow from your heart in your speech, mannerisms and all kinds of behavior. 🧡 Study more, enhance their self-confidence. Learning is to improve our cultural quality, armed with an excellent way to our minds, our knowledge of the draw, we can make us a good way to open up our minds, in the event of a problem, will not be baffled, worried, not looking for ways to solve the problem, the path. And the continuous use of knowledge in reality, and will play a positive role in our lives, so that they are full of self-confidence, and continue to run forward. Attention to their own inner feelings, others are motivated to live a better helper. In contact with you, no matter what role this person plays in your life, but not let you live without self, without your own independent personality. You have to realize that each of us exists independently, with our own complete system of thought, and we can't be so concerned about the other person that we lose sight of our own existence because of the other person's importance. You have to let yourself always have a sense of existence, are to others irreplaceable important position, you can really get the respect and like others. You don't need to prove to others that you are worthy of being loved If you are constantly trying to make yourself worthy of being loved, then the thing you should do now is to stop; if you are taking great pains to hide and not let others find out your shortcomings, then the thing you should do now is also to stop. Deep down, everyone desires to be loved for who they are as a person without trying to prove to others that they are worthy of being loved. The first step you need to take to make this happen is to gather the courage to show your true self to people. Let go of your carefully disguised facade of glitz and glamor, even if you may worry that your real self will scare them off. I know it's pretty hard to change at first, hang in there, learn to love yourself and respect your feelings, start by learning to say no, go for it, I believe in you.

question: Read a lot of books, hear a lot of stories, but can't live a good life, why?
description: Read a lot of books, listen to a lot of stories, but still anxious and unable to live well

answers.answer_text: Hello subject, in fact, such a phenomenon is very common, and there is no need to be too anxious about it. Why is this phenomenon? ️There is no correlation between "getting it" and "doing it"️ Allan Wicker did a study and found that students' attitudes towards cheating had little to do with their actual cheating behavior, and that there was little correlation between people's self-described racial attitudes and their actual behavior. behavior had similarly little correlation. These two studies suggest that it is easy to equate [knowing] with [being able to do] in most people's perceptions. But the truth is that people are often influenced by a number of factors in the process of transforming [know how] into [can do]. I️ now come to think about whether there is such an encounter such a situation?1. False understanding of the so-called false understanding, that is, our understanding of the knowledge or reasoning only stay in the surface meaning or external links, not really internalized them into our own knowledge experience, the error of the [understand] as [understand]. Cognitive scholars believe that stimuli and behavior are not directly linked, there is also the influence of schema, that is, a kind of psychological cognitive structure that can help people perceive, organize, access and use information. 2. Cognitive dissonance Sometimes, we understand and can understand what should be done, but in fact, we still can not do it, and will also feel anxious, contradictory and distress for this. This may be the result of cognitive dissonance, where new cognitions conflict with existing ones. For example, people already know that it is okay to sleep late, but if they are really sick and the doctor tells them to rest early, they realize that they should rest as soon as possible. But whenever it is time to get ready for a break, the consistent idea that it is okay to sleep late and the idea that staying up late is bad for your health will be in contradiction or even in conflict. The way to balance the contradiction is to change the original cognition or add new cognition, such as the idea that [getting sick is not necessarily due to staying up late], or to emphasize that [I can have more time if I sleep later, and I can't sleep if I sleep earlier], and so on. And often people out of the protection mechanism of self-affirmation, it is difficult to deny their own or their own original cognitive and thinking patterns. 3. human instinctive short-sightedness human eyes can see the field of vision is limited, and in fact, we also have short-sightedness of the future phenomenon. We often can't imagine our future selves, but care more about the feelings of the present. That is, the short-sightedness of human instincts separates the present [I] from the future [I]. Therefore, even if we understand some of the reasoning, our brain will send out signals such as [it is useless] and so on, ultimately leading to our unwillingness and failure to do what we want to do.4. Weak mental ability "to deal with people more", "to be confident and optimistic point ", "Be enthusiastic and cheerful, take the initiative to communicate with others" ...... Maybe we also often hear these words, they will have similar expectations, but feel it is difficult to do, and even more will feel inferior for this. But in fact, it is not that we do not understand, just the lack of a mental capacity, so that [want to do] and [can do] there is still a long distance between. The reasoning is someone else's, while the ability is their own. This so-called mental ability is the cognitive ability to recognize and perceive things in the world, as well as the ability to cope with the psychological suitability of environmental change and internal motivation. ️What you should do 1. Practice and act more to break false understanding. Take the initiative to learn and understand instead of reacting passively.2. Step outside your comfort zone. People tend to get used to formed ways of thinking and it's harder to change them. We can try some new ways to break out of the original comfort state in order to really apply the truth in practice.3. Realize your instinctive short-sightedness. See more and think more in order to connect the behavior with the result and enhance the motivation of the behavior.4. Enhance your mental ability. Mental ability is acquired, some past experiences may have led to our mental ability to have deficiencies, but there is no need to complain, because the efforts of the present can also create tomorrow's you. We can learn from our classmates and friends, dare to try, and also seek help from professional "guides" - counselors, and constantly improve our internal mental ability. I hope this helps you, (ง-̀_-́)ง.

answers.answer_text: Hello subject I personally think that your situation, can not be regarded as cold, perhaps as you say "heartless" "emotional coldness", I think, at most, may be regarded as more sensible, rationalization it. For example, you mentioned the parents emotional and sister education problems, your approach is to help them analyze the problem, give advice, which is a very rational way to solve the problem. Because at least you still cared about them and didn't ignore them, so it can't be considered heartless. Our attention, energy, memory, etc., are often limited, so we tend to focus only on those things we want to pay attention to, while for other things, we may ignore, not deliberately to remember. For example, one of my coworkers, she cares a lot about her coworkers, which coworkers have what relationship with each other, what has happened, and so on, she knows everything. She also knows who owns most of her coworkers' cars, and can remember a lot of license plates. And I just the opposite, for these things I do not care, occasionally overheard, may also quickly forget, license plate is almost do not remember a few people. It's not that I'm heartless, or that she's affectionate, it's just that we don't have the same focus. So, I think, you are the same. It's not that you don't care about the people around you, it's just that there are some things that you don't feel like you have to care about as much, and you're better at analyzing things rationally than trying to put more emotion into them, and your focus, probably, is on other things above all else. If you don't see anything wrong with that yourself, and everyone around you is used to it, then it's okay to continue to be that way. Psychology has a defense mechanism called "rationalization", to avoid investing too much emotion, so will behave very sensible, very rational, perhaps, your behavior belongs to this category of defense mechanism. You don't want to owe favors, you need AA for meals, you don't want to get too emotionally entangled with people, and you want to maintain your emotional independence: you don't owe others, and you don't seem to need others. However, deep relationships are often emotionally invested, paying for others' feelings and energy, and allowing others to pay for themselves, so that the relationship can go deeper. If you wish to maintain deep relationships with some people, it may be necessary to invest more emotionally as appropriate, and not be afraid to owe others. After that, I took a weekend off and asked my best friend to go for a day trip around the neighborhood: hiking in the mountains. The scenery was beautiful, and I felt healed in that moment. The second week back to work, people are like a new life, the whole person's state is very full. 3, the relationship between coworkers. There are still small frictions, but we laugh it off every time, and there is no need to argue about a lot of things.4. What if I don't have time to do what I like? I can tell you very responsibly, there will be time, I will be asked to write scripts every day, the highest record is 6 days to write 51 scripts. I've accomplished goals that I didn't dare to think about last year, but I still have time to write PLOGs for beauty reviews, and all kinds of copy for food scouting. Usually there is still time to read books, write today's headlines and Zhihu. You can use your time to write down what comes to mind in your cell phone's notepad, and then when it's time to actually start writing, you can come up with a complete piece of writing. Lastly, I hope you get out of this state soon. Good luck, and I hope you get out of it soon.

question: Some small conflicts in interpersonal relationships, at the time to tolerate, but later in the heart can not let go?
description: In life, I have encountered some minor conflicts, such as being stepped on by someone, being cut in line, having someone's juice spilled on me, and so on. Generally I would choose to tolerate at that time, do not make a sound or say it's fine. But after a long time, I can't let go of it, my heart is still full of anger, and I have been repeatedly torn between what I should do, and I also imagine the quarrels that will happen after the conflict with other people, which makes me anxious, but also tell myself to be generous and not to quarrel with other people, so I think about it again and again and again, and it's painful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand your current confusion, I can see that you are a sensitive person, when you encounter some conflicts, you will always stand in the other people's point of view and interpersonal relations to think, you don't want to make interpersonal relations affected because of some small things, this kind of considerations and thoughts are worthy of affirmation. However, at the moment, this kind of thinking makes you have a lot of confusion, because you feel the anger that arises within yourself, but you use your own reason to repress this anger, and you can't find the right way to deal with these emotions, so these negative emotions have been fermenting and spreading inside, so that you have been stuck in the emotional quagmire. How should we recognize and look at this psychological state of our own? In reality, how should I help myself to regulate it? From your question, I can see that you are always able to "tolerate" small conflicts in your life, but this "tolerance" does not seem to be a real letting go, but only at the level of mind consciousness, letting go of your emotions. Emotions. I don't know if you've noticed? Behind this kind of behavior may be hidden some of your inherent beliefs. For example, you believe that you should be an amiable person, or that you should be a generous and tolerant person, and so on. These personas that you give yourself seem perfect and laudable, though it also means that you put a shackle on yourself. This is like a star halo, as a star, in the enjoyment of everyone's worship at the same time, but also to bear the pressure and responsibility brought by the star halo, your words and deeds, every move will be subject to a high degree of attention, therefore, we can learn that many stars are actually reflecting a common problem is: psychological pressure is too large. And your way of thinking, it is very likely that the initiative to put a halo, but you do not enjoy the benefits of the halo, only to bear the pressure of the halo, because after all, this halo is their own self-persona imagined in the mind. If the previous assumption is not the internal cause of your current situation, then we can also consider whether you have excessive guilt experiences in interpersonal relationships. Imagine that in the face of a conflict between you and another person, you want to express your dissatisfaction, you want to lash out at the other person, you even want to rant and rave, but there is a voice in your head that says, "You are doing it wrong, anger is an unexpressed emotion, it's extremely wrong! As a result, you end up choosing to hold back, choosing to suppress your feelings of anger. This voice is the inner root of what makes you feel difficult and confused; it feels guilt and remorse, it feels self-doubt. So where does this inner voice come from? This is an area we need to think about and be aware of. Perhaps it may have come from your family of origin, or from teachers or other authority figures who have influenced you a great deal since childhood. They have planted a steel seal in your heart, so that when you encounter such scenarios later in life, you will always be restrained by this voice, like an invisible "spell" on your head. Being aware of and discovering this inner voice or belief is a key step in helping yourself out of the confusion. Whether to choose "generous" patience or "narrow-minded" calculating] It seems that at the level of social morality, we will call for generosity, patience, and not to be calculating, and there is nothing wrong with the propagation of such virtues. However, from a psychological point of view, our so-called "generosity" does not mean to suppress oneself and give up expression, but contains a deeper wisdom, which is a kind of life manifestation of the ancient people's open-mindedness and cheerfulness. In other words, it is not that "generosity" itself is wrong, but because as young people, their wisdom and state of mind have not yet reached a certain level, and their understanding of this word is greatly deviated. To put it simply, we have probably only learned the skin of the matter (the outward expression) without really understanding its inner meaning. I think those ancient sages expressed generosity in a way that was truly a letting go from the inside out, an inner connotation that doesn't even require saying to yourself internally, "Be generous." Rather, this emotion of anger simply does not arise in relationships. Therefore, as a young person whose mental intelligence is still growing, it is important to express yourself authentically. When you encounter these kinds of problems in relationships, you should care more about your inner feelings and emotions, rather than choosing to suppress, or even ignore, the fact that anger is normal and natural. [Does expressing emotions mean that you are indulging in a "no holds barred" approach? Of course, we are wary of the conflict that our true expression will bring. There is an old saying that "no fight, no acquaintance", which has a certain psychological basis, because when two people express their true selves, in fact, it is also a kind of deep communication, even if this form seems to be a more violent and extreme approach. But in this process, it is the real collision of two people, compared to cover up, people prefer to get along with the real people. Those who can really do "generosity", is also true to express themselves, because they really do not produce anger from these things, so they express, but still to maintain their internal feelings and external behavior of the same. Does the expression of emotions mean that one must "get into a fight"? In fact, this kind of behavior is a good state of mind to pursue truthfulness, but in reality, it may still bring us some other harms, such as physical injuries, and school sanctions and so on. Therefore, we still need to find a more balanced approach, and that approach is positive communication and communication. [Learning to communicate positively is both an important way to fulfill the expression of one's inner emotions and to ease relationships] There is a book called "Positive Communication" that is recommended here about the skills of positive communication, and here I will focus on some key points. The significance of positive communication lies in the fact that you can satisfy the expression and disclosure of your negative emotions, and at the same time resolve interpersonal conflicts in a correct and reasonable way. The main thing you need to do in positive communication is to be quick to recognize your negative emotions and to deal with them quickly. For example, when you are angry, you should quickly take the "five minutes to calm down method", so that you can ease the anger just when the outburst period. Don't communicate with your emotions. When your negative emotions have been alleviated, you can communicate with two people, do not bring emotions into the conversation, which will only escalate the conflict. Be alert to your own value assessment. Watch your language, tone of voice, etc. to prevent value evaluations and even life attacks. Keep a neutral and objective presentation of the facts. In communication, just express what you see and hear and your inner feelings objectively. For example, in the small matter in your question, we can say, "Classmate, excuse me, just now you accidentally stepped on my foot when you were eating, maybe you didn't realize it at that time, but this behavior of yours still made me feel angry inside, and now I'd like to tell you about this matter." Lastly, I want to emphasize that if what is described above does not happen by accident, but is repeatedly done to you by one person, it may have involved school harassment or even school violence, a situation that should be promptly communicated to parents and teachers for help. I hope the above responses will help you.

"Psychological internal conflict" is probably one of the things that most affects the quality of our lives. In your question, I see a very deep internal conflict. Simply put, your internal conflict comes from the conflict between your inner "Self" and "Superego", or in other words, your "Ego" is unable to balance the conflict between your Self and Superego, and therefore The feeling of pain arises. We all know that the superego comes from the moral plane, which is closely related to some social rules and judgmental rules. The ego, on the other hand, comes from your real needs. Therefore, to resolve this conflict, we can start from this perspective, and see what can be dealt with. 1. Listen: the voice of judgment within your heart What does your "superego" come from? I think it comes from your inner voice called "self-judgment". I noticed that you mentioned the word "generosity" in your question - this is actually a judgment. In your mind, you probably have a judgmental standard: if you show that you are uncomfortable with a minor conflict with someone, it means that you are a "calculating" and "petty" person. Therefore, in order to appear "generous", most of the time, you will "tolerate", "do not say or say nothing". So, behind your behavior, you are actually fulfilling a psychological need, which is "you want to be a generous person". Identify this judgmental voice, we can work on it. 2, identify: the fear in the heart of the question comes, why do you need to become a generous person? What will happen to you if you don't become one? Behind this self-requirement may lie a deep fear. For example, if I am not a generous person, I will be punished, including being criticized by my parents, isolated from others, etc. Therefore, this self-requirement may be an effective means to fight against "being rejected" or "broken relationships". In your subconscious, there is probably a voice that says, "If I don't do something, it will be done. ..... This fear is the root cause of your current behavior. 3. Seeing: The Foundation of Self-Healing Many emotions and feelings are healed once they are seen. When you feel anxious, can you see your own repression? Can you see the fear behind your repression? Do you see your true anger and aggression? If you see them, maybe you feel better about yourself. Seeing your repressed emotions and recognizing that they are real is the first step to getting out of the rut. Beyond that, you need to see another hidden feeling: the feeling of victimization. Simply put, why do you "mind" being spilled juice, cut in line, or stepped on so much? It's likely that there's a sense of victimization involved in being "offended". First of all, all of these things happened out of your expectation, so for you, it hurts your narcissism to have it happen. Secondly, although most of these people do not do it on purpose, if you feel very intense emotions, it is probably because in your subconscious mind, you default to the idea that they are "on purpose" and "hostile" to you. This way of thinking is derived from the self-centered "victim mindset", which may be deeply hidden, but if you are deeply aware, you may be able to find their clues. 4, change: from the acceptance of their own emotions and try to truly express the beginning of the aforementioned to see their own emotions, is the beginning of acceptance of themselves. The root of your internal conflict and conflict comes from a lack of acceptance of your emotional feelings and behavior. However, contained within this non-acceptance are many irrational perceptions, such as that if you express your emotions authentically, you will be hurt by others. Perhaps this irrational belief came from an implantation earlier in your life, but can we link to the real world and see if this belief actually happens? (Verify your imagination in reality) You can try using the Authentic Expression Technique to say what you really feel without accusation, e.g. I feel a little uncomfortable when you get juice on me. You can see for yourself if you will actually be told you are petty if you express yourself authentically? Or break off a relationship with you because they think you're petty? Maybe you'd be greeted with an apology. Of course, perhaps not. But the purpose of your expression is just to be true to yourself, not to demand that the other person has to apologize, and if you can see it that way, maybe you'll be less bothered about what attitude the other person has. The prerequisite for authentic expression is to be true to your feelings. And this expression technique is often effective for emotionally repressed people. All it takes is for you to let go a little of your own judgment of yourself, and your fear of judgment from others, and give it a try. Blessings. After reading the responses of other counselors who responded to you with great care, I wanted to offer a little more perspective as well. #In life there are some minor conflicts like being stepped on by someone, being cut in line, having someone's juice spilled on me, etc. I usually choose to tolerate it at the time and keep quiet or say it's fine. #What concerns me about this description is that you didn't speak up or say it was okay. I don't know what emotions you were feeling at the time, but you were able to accept the situation as it was, and said "nothing" or "it's okay", so that things could pass calmly at the time. This is your ability to cope with emergencies and to cope better with various situations. #But you can't let go of it for a long time after the incident, your heart is still full of anger, and you keep torn between what you should do and what you should do, and you also imagine the quarrels that will happen after the conflict with other people, which makes you feel anxious and uneasy, and you also tell yourself that you have to be generous, and don't fight with other people, and you keep thinking over it again and again. #Angry, is such an emotion dissatisfaction with the way things have been handled in the past? So the thing that concerns me is when did you start having this way of thinking? What were you going through that would give you this constant going back over? But you did a thinking simulation in your brain, which is a good way to go. Now that you've simulated it you know what happens after an argument put? It could get so loud that it makes you uncomfortable for the rest of the day, or it could escalate into a fight that puts you in the hospital or the other person in the hospital; are these outcomes acceptable to you? Are you willing to try to take on a bigger price for this next friction? In your simulation, you tell yourself to be generous, but you don't seem to mention the part where you "take" responsibility; whatever choice you make, you have a price to pay. For example, if you keep quiet or say it's okay, you minimize the cost. If you choose to argue, then the stakes start to rise, if you choose to argue or it escalates to pushing and shoving, or even to a fight, and the police come, and it could affect your job, etc.; then the responsibility you take on is positively correlated to the outcome of your reaction, are you willing to take it on? If you are willing to do that you can do whatever you want without holding back; you can even send the other person flying, right? When you only look at the "behavior" or only consider whether or not to suppress your "emotions", of course it is very hard, difficult, uncomfortable, and you will think that there are other choices and ways to release yourself. However, you ignore the "consequences" of the corresponding behavior! When you think about the consequences of your behavior in the context of a thought simulation, you'll still be #thinking over and over again, in pain. #? The reluctance to argue with others and the fear of conflict is actually a fear of expressing our aggressiveness. Living out aggression can assert your boundaries and defend your rights. Aggressiveness is daring to raise your voice, to voice your needs, to express them. But we just don't dare sometimes! What to do? My personal experience is to express myself through non-violent communication. For example, if you are stepped on by someone, and they probably apologized, you can say it's okay, but you can also express: my foot really hurts, you should be more careful next time. When you are spilled juice by someone, you can make a request and ask the other person what they want to do to solve the problem. You can say it: I am very unhappy and so on. When what we think and what we do don't match, inner conflict can easily occur. It's not the thing itself that's bothering you right now, it's the conflicting thoughts inside you. There is a famous ABC theory in psychology: A stands for event; B stands for belief; C stands for reaction. How we react is because of our inner beliefs. This is how many people feel differently when faced with the same thing. Whenever there is conflict, tell yourself: you have a choice. Express your aggressiveness when you don't want to be generous. Aggressiveness is not cursing, it is daring to be yourself. Mr. Cong says: a person who is afraid to live out aggression is doing so for self-protection. There are some benefits to us in not expressing aggression, but when we have suppressed a lot of negative emotions within us, we can learn to understand anger and the thoughts behind our behavior. When we sort through that, we can be much more comfortable. Let's become a little bit stronger inside, and when we are truly strong inside, we are being ourselves no matter how we make our choices. Wanting to fight is being yourself, not bothering to fight is equally being yourself. There is only one principle, do not condemn yourself. I know what kind of person I am, I know what I do right or wrong, good or bad, other people's opinions do not interfere with my opinion of myself at all. Although I still seldom quarrel with others, I am more courageous than before to express my feelings, for example, if I feel violated, I will say so; if I am unhappy, I will say so, and my emotions are no longer suppressed. I recommend "The Power of Self-Growth" by Mr. Cong Fei from Mr. Cong to you, and I wish you also find a method that suits you. I hope you will find the right way for yourself and get out of the trouble soon!

answers.answer_text: Hello owner, in reading your question, I sense that you have angry feelings. Regarding the development of your probing character, and the conflict about the bailout incident, you have a great deal of resentment towards your parents, especially your dad. But the last sentence of your question, "How can I adjust my mindset?" With this sentence it was clear that you felt your emotions retreating again, your momentum going down to self-doubt. So in this one short question, a very strong self-conflict has been exposed. On the one hand, you want to be independent and feel very dissatisfied with your parents' interference; on the other hand, you worry that your parents are right and that it is your own bad heart. As a spectator, I find this state of conflict very difficult to bear. Not to mention you, the person concerned. Hugs to you. Have you ever wondered if you are still compromising your parents as you have been for the past 20+ years if you are not depressed. Depression is just an outburst of conflict manifested. Physical illness is a reminder that a bad habit should be changed. Mental illness is also a reminder that it's time to make a change. I am a baby mama. My favorite book on positive discipline says that the best gift we can give our children is not just to give them security and help them grow. More equally important is to develop a sense of strength and a sense of autonomy. Only when children feel empowered and capable will they be able to adapt better to this society. So I do disagree with your father's approach. But the good thing is that you are a very much your own person, and although in the past you usually suppressed your thoughts, your sense of autonomy is on the verge of being overwhelmed, and this conflict is inevitably hard. But compared to a lifeless "baby". The uncertainty and pain of such a collision is the inevitable price of growth, right?

question: Will the rebellious period be delayed? Freshman Year Rebellion
description: I was basically a more introverted child who listened to his parents since he was a child, the rebellious period is also relatively well-behaved, but by the senior year of high school, the first year of college, he began to rebel, and think that parents do not care about what is best, the more I care about the more difficult it will be difficult to throw a tantrum, quarrel!

answers.answer_text: Instead of rebellion, it is the awakening of the subject's self-awareness, you are no longer the good boy who always listens to his parents, but has his own ideas and opinions. Happens in the senior high school, freshman year of such a period is actually still very normal, the end of adolescence, and almost just adult, personally I think it is not too late, because it has to do with the character, experience, for example, the subject said he is more introverted obedient, then it is not easy to have so much rebelliousness. Many people don't even have this awakening until they have been adults for a long time and have experienced things. The awakening of self-awareness is that we know that we are an independent individual, and not a little baby that mom and dad can protect for the rest of their lives, we gradually have a set of their own understanding of things and solutions, and gradually form their own worldview, you begin to understand yourself more clearly, and want to do some things independently. Congratulations to the subject, you are starting to grow up. Tantrums and quarrels may be a necessary stage for children and parents, to alleviate this status quo, you can think about whether the things you argue about are beneficial to you, think about whether this thing is done for me or for my parents. For example, if you are eating instant noodles and your parents tell you to eat well and not to eat instant noodles, you feel angry because you just want to eat instant noodles. But when you think about it eating well is good for who? Isn't it also for your own good health, better growth, and resistance to disease? That's when you might be more tolerant. Think about doing everything for yourself, not for others. If it's a parent who is one of those extraordinarily controlling ones who like to mindlessly interfere with their children, then it's even more of a problem for the subject, and only if you have a mind of your own, you're going to have a hard time feeling controlled. For example, you obviously like liberal arts, but your parents said that you want to study science, saying that it is good to find a job in the future. Because this is contrary to your inner desire, of course you have to feel unhappy, because they don't respect your opinion and viewpoint, but just impose their own will on you. If this is the case with such parents, you can only try to keep a good distance and show that you cater to them, but you have to be firm in your heart. Quietly wait for the day when you can support yourself and be independent, then you can live the life you want. So you can think about what you want, what is really good for you, and whether your parents respect you, support your opinion, and try to help you reach what you want. Are they really doing what's good for you, or are they just imposing their own views on you, even if you feel miserable.

question: My father-in-law was diagnosed with terminal cancer, how can I help him to make the pain less painful?

Today the test results are not so good, the cancer cells have increased a bit, and the hospital said he needs chemotherapy. answers.answer_text: Hello, subject! Seeing the words is like seeing the face. In the face of the fact that an elderly person is suffering from cancer, I believe that as a family member, you must have very complicated emotional feelings, and also feel depressed because you cannot say anything. Psychologically, there are 5 stages in the development of psychological activities for patients suffering from cancer: 1. Denial stage, in which the patient denies the fact that he is sick. 2. Anger stage, in which the patient tends to express his inner unwillingness by giving vent to his anger. 3. Agreement stage, in which the patient hopes that the doctor can help him to cure his disease. 4. Melancholy stage, in which the patient will be in a depressed state when he learns that his condition has worsened. 5. The patient will be in a depressed state. 5. Acceptance phase, before facing death, the patient is quietly accepting and waiting for that day to come. The order of each stage is not in any particular order, but in general it can help the patient's family understand the patient's psychological trends. It is important to provide the right companionship and comfort at the right time. Helping the elderly to get through these periods is something that children can take care of. According to psychology, everyone needs "verbal expressions" of love, which can be categorized into five ways: words of affirmation, moments of care, acceptance of gifts, acts of service, and physical contact. For cancer patients, this still applies, such as words full of love, tolerance and support, carefully creating some ritualistic situations for the elderly, giving the elderly things that they like and that are pleasing to the eye, taking care of the elderly physically with dedication and responsibility, and finally increasing the physical contact between the children and the elderly, such as hugs and forehead touch, etc., which can psychologically, and even physically, alleviate the pain and suffering of the elderly. . As to whether a miracle will be produced, it requires the willpower of the patient and the heartfelt efforts of the family members in taking care of the patient to increase the probability of a miracle occurring. Also, as a caregiver, it is more important to care for one's own heart, and the patient needs the strength of the family as a backbone to heal the disease. I hope my answer has inspired and helped you a little!

Hello, dear subject. Life is impermanent and what we can do seems insignificant in the face of the great events of life, death and sickness. Regarding the question you posed, I have seen a number of respondents give their replies. As a counselor with a similar experience, what I can offer are some of the parts that I think are more important. When I read your question, I felt how unforeseen news like this can seem to us. It may be that we are going through this process, still denying the possibility of the illness and trying to find an explanation for it; we are also still trying to bargain if there is another way, if there is a miracle ...... Our first step in going to give our loved ones attention and support may be to first be able to go to our own hearts. Our denial and fear may also become a denial for those who are actually experiencing these illnesses. In a sense, the illness is a display that the mind and body are one and the same, but it also just means that we can try to understand ourselves through the symptoms at the time of the illness, rather than seeking an explanation that could have prevented this from happening. What happens may be more a matter of facing the situation as it is, respecting the doctor's professional opinion and diagnosis, and giving the best medical treatment we can, which may be the "best" effort we can actually make. Then, you also need to settle your own life and that of your family. When a father-in-law is ill, the whole family life is affected and changed. The impact of this is not always clear to the casual observer, and it can be a matter of long-term healing. It is also important for you and your significant other to try and figure out how to settle it all from a family life perspective, how to treat it, who is going to be with you for these treatments, etc., and to give the patient as much peace of mind as possible in a recuperative environment. In addition, in terms of emotional support, the father-in-law may need more care and companionship from his significant other, or his son. And this means that we need to give our husbands a little more support, or also take on a little more of the family business, which is something we need to be prepared for. Finally, speaking of treatment and support. Whether or not the cancer can be stabilized and controlled varies from person to person. Keep an optimistic and positive expectation and also plan for the worst. Lifestyle wise, respect the patient's own choices. There are two books, Grace and Courage and Staying with You to the End, which are about the process of accompanying cancer patients, and they are recommended to you, so you can try to read them when you have time. We can draw some adjustments from them, but don't think that we can necessarily find answers from them. Good luck.

Hello subject, first of all, from the doctor's point of view, I would like to explain to the subject about lung cancer. Lung cancer includes several pathological types, and you should be able to diagnose which type it is after the surgery! Some types of lung cancer are more sensitive to chemotherapy and targeted drugs, and if treated properly, there is no problem to prolong the survival time, so in this regard, you should still actively cooperate with the hospital for the next treatment! Of course, if it is really advanced and has already metastasized, there is really no good way out, and we can only take one step at a time, which is both a component of luck and the patient's own mentality! The subject mentioned in the description, has not yet told your father-in-law's real condition, three good think for the time being or do not tell, because a strong person, when suddenly received a death notice, it is also very difficult to adjust their own state of mind, that if the adjustment is not good, may rapidly aggravate the deterioration of the condition, played a counterproductive role, we encountered a lot of such a situation in the hospital, the family members are generally to the deterioration of the condition is really can not control the time to tell the patient, of course, but also to tell the patient, the patient can not be controlled. We have encountered many such cases in the hospital, usually the family is to the deterioration of the disease, really can not control the time to tell the patient, of course, there have been until the death of the disease do not tell the patient. The three good personally believe that the early can not tell the patient the truth, but to the moment of death, or should tell the patient the truth, because the patient also has the right to know their own real condition, the old saying "can not die as a ghost ah", and the old man may have a lot of last wishes to account for, should be given to him the right to do so. What I said just now is a bit off-topic. The questioner wants to ask: "Is there any psychological explanation for cancer, and is there any way to make the patient's suffering less painful, or is there any possibility of a miracle?" Psychology has no solution to cancer, but only requires us to face the disease and pain with a correct mindset. The patient mainly suffers from both psychological and physical aspects in the later stages. Psychological aspect: then if we didn't tell him the truth, we have to make a show of not having this thing in our usual behavior, and try not to let him notice the abnormality. If chemotherapy is needed, we can tell him a little lie, tell him that this is a malignant early lesion, in order to prevent malignant changes, chemotherapy should be prevented. Usually, we can distract the patient's attention and explain to him the effects of chemotherapy on the body, such as hair loss, inability to eat and so on, and do some easy-to-digest things, so as to help him through this period of chemotherapy easily. Treat him in the same way as an ordinary patient, don't intentionally surround him, as acting too fake will cause his suspicion. Physical aspect: The pain of advanced lung cancer comes from two aspects, one is the chest fluid, which makes it impossible to breathe, and you can only sit in a sitting position. One is cancer pain. These two conditions usually do not occur at the same time. There is no good solution for these, only symptomatic treatment, diuresis and asthma or pain relief. As for the last question the subject asked if there will be a miracle? SanShan told you, work more than 20 years, SanShan also saw the diagnosis of cancer, and finally nothing happened, but that kind of situation is not to do surgery to determine the pathology of cancer, are to do CT or some other tests identified as cancer, in the end, 100% is not cancer? Or is there any misdiagnosis? The three good also do not know! In fact, we should not be entangled in these, we should be open to accept what life has given us, positively face, do our best both peace of mind!

Grandfather has advanced lung cancer, although his mental state is good after the surgery, it has been found that the cancer cells have increased again. I can feel the concern of the original poster and their desire to share the burden for their grandfather. Hugs to the original poster. As for the relationship between physical illnesses and psychology, including the causes of cancer, there have been quite a few studies. For example, the C-type personality characterized by habitual self-repression is associated with a higher cancer rate. Traditional Chinese medicine believes in the impact of emotions on disease. Freud mentioned the death instinct. Family dynamics also play a role in following death. There are also many theories about self-destructive mechanisms in the subconscious mind. Although there is no specific scientific evidence so far, maintaining a positive and optimistic attitude and allowing oneself to coexist with cancer are generally recognized as beneficial for recovery or prolonging survival time. Therefore, the original poster【Here are a few things that can be done】: 1. Inform the patient of the condition gradually, and extend the time for revealing bad news. At the same time, provide companionship and guide the patient to express their thoughts or feelings. Focus on understanding and accepting, and do not force comfort if unsure how to respond. 2. Actively alleviate physical pain. Late-stage cancer, including chemotherapy reactions, often come with various physical discomforts that greatly impact the patient's emotional state and quality of life. Therefore, it is advisable to avoid treatment plans that cause significant harm to the body in pursuit of killing cancer cells. This may include the need for pain-relief measures. Consult with the doctor to be prepared. 3. Guide attention diversion and relieve stress. If the physical condition allows, maintaining moderate physical exercise, encouraging participation in activities of interest, and engaging in conversations about topics that the grandfather likes with family members can be effective ways to reduce stress. 4. Consider professional psychological support. This support is not only for the grandfather but also for other family members in emotional guidance and attitude adjustment. After all, the atmosphere affects everyone and it is necessary for everyone to collectively create a supportive environment. The involvement of professionals will make the overall coping process more organized and comforting. I hope this can be helpful to you.

Hello, Mr. Owner. As a family member how to help your father-in-law with cancer, it is indeed very difficult and heartbreaking, but also worried about the fear of aggravation of the disease, there will be a variety of disturbances, in addition to taking care of the patient's daily care, diet, but also to sympathize with the patient's mood mentality, to prevent the patient's mentality collapsed, to speak carefully. Whether or not you can trust your loved ones' explanations also depends on the state of the individual. This will be a process that occurs secondarily, and some patients may pass away without surviving to full acceptance. Whether or not you can survive to accept the fact that you are seriously ill, relax your mind, and actively cooperate with the treatment depends on your own ability to psychologically resist setbacks and catastrophes. Say it, in case your father-in-law's inner resistance to stress is not enough, the mind collapsed, resulting in aggravation of the condition, will inevitably blame themselves for telling the truth, it is possible that this guilt and self-blame accompany themselves for a long time, it is also quite difficult. To say or not to say, or to discuss within the family, first, different members of the family will have a different understanding of the eunuch, together collision of good ideas, must be better than the individual idea, but also can disperse a person's pressure and responsibility, to avoid possible excessive self-blame in the future. Secondly, no matter which decision is made, it is necessary for everyone to participate and help together. If it's going to be said, how it's going to be said and who's going to say it and how they're going to react afterward is going to be discussed. If it's not said, there's also a guideline in place for how everyone can work with each other. In addition, no matter what, how to take good care of the patient, so that the patient's mood to relax a little, is the need for the patient's own participation, to understand the patient's needs at the moment, and to cooperate with the patient's needs and care. Instead of forcing the patient to take care of what he or she feels he or she needs to take care of, it makes the patient unhappy. The understanding and support of the family is very important to the patient and will naturally reduce the patient's suffering. About how to understand cancer psychologically, this is not a few words can explain, there is a book called "Hope for the Disease", the author of all the physical diseases have their own unique understanding, some of them are more extreme, but it can be done as a psychological perspective, a view of the physical disease. It could be that you see the pain that illness brings to your family and you want so badly to do something for your family and for your father-in-law to ease that pain. Sometimes we have to recognize and accept our limitations, there are things that are beyond our capacity, even beyond human capacity. The only way we can face and accept it is together. Good luck.

The owner of the good to the relatives have cancer, this is indeed a very upsetting situation, but also can understand the family to hide the patient's approach. After all, death is a difficult topic. You alleviate your father-in-law's pain and want to perform a miracle. This is not for the whole family to ease the pain, to create a miracle. When it comes to life and death, in fact, psychology is quite useless; it can neither change fate against the heavens nor predict the future. We often hear that XXX lived for many years after his cancer diagnosis because he had a good state of mind. ...... Based on these cases alone, we can only speculate that being in a good mood may have a beneficial effect on prolonging one's life, but we can't be sure that it's 100% applicable to everyone. The only thing psychology has taught me is "acceptance". Accept everything that happens and live with it. Your father-in-law may be facing chemotherapy, and once that starts, not only will his body change, but you may not be able to hide it any longer. If you want him to suffer less, maybe he needs to be informed about his condition before second-guessing his suspicions. In the book Tales of Sickness and Pain, the author, Dr. Arthur Kleiman, mentions an incident when he himself was just starting out as an internist, when he encountered a seven year old female patient with massive, severe burns all over her body, a little girl who had to go through painful whirlpool bath treatments every day and needed to have the burned flesh removed from the blossoming wounds. It was an extremely painful event, and she made shrill wailing noises and resisted manipulation by the medical staff. Dr. Arthur Kleiman wished he could help her by calming her down, he tried all sorts of things to distract the little patient, talking about her family and school in the hope of calming her down, but to little avail, the child could not be calmed at all. Dr. Arthur Kleiman was feeling clumsy and incompetent when he realized that the little girl herself was asking him to listen to her, to let her tell him how she was enduring the pain, to let him know how she was feeling during this terrible treatment. So Dr. Arthur Kleiman listened to the little girl, and as she talked, she quieted down and gradually was able to endure the pain of the debridement operation. The author says, "Whereas almost all cultural views of healing, such as those of religion and morality, draw the patient and those around them into a preoccupation with issues of frustration and confusion, the narrow vision of modern biomedicine avoids this aspect of suffering, as it does in treating the disease and not hearing the pain." So perhaps all we can do is be there and listen to the suffering of others and ourselves. Even if we will eventually face suffering and death alone, we are not alone. In closing, I hope my response has inspired you.

Hello, owner: Once diagnosed, patients with cancerous tumors are under great psychological pressure, and they may suffer from anxiety and depression, or even have suicidal thoughts, at this time, they must be given correct psychological intervention and psychotherapy. Hi, thank you for your trust, I have cancer patients in my family as well. I've learned a bit about the connection between this disease and psychology, just as an FYI. There is a term called cancer type personality. If a person has a part of their personality by which they are intransigent and continually function in a negative energy almost childish way. This part of the personality is as difficult as an invisible cancer. Then there is a possibility that this part will manifest physically. A certain part will have problems. The same logic applies to a family or a clan (a statement that has gotten some sideways corroboration from Liu Yousheng and Louise Hay in the US.) For example, if you blow up your lungs with anger, would it be related to anger? Does heartlessness have anything to do with indifference? Would the lungs, which are responsible for respiration and exhalation and his interaction with the world, have feelings of despair towards the world? If this part of the emotion is stored in the heart for a long time, and can not be expressed and catharsis, it will inevitably show up in the form of physical disease. You can find out more about this on your own. If you need in-depth communication, you can send me a private message.

"Lazy, no appetite, poor sleep, no interest, low libido, unwilling to communicate, always want to sit and lie down", from the symptoms, there are indeed some symptoms of depression, such as "reduced interest" "reduced verbal activity ", but this does not mean that it is depression. The three common lows of depression are persistent "depressed mood," "decreased interest or loss of interest," "decreased verbal activity," and generally there are two lows that can be said to have a tendency to depression, but it is not certain that it is depression. Tendency, but not sure is depression, but also need to further understand the details of the situation, such as the duration of physical symptoms, the degree of impact, the degree of internal pain, normal diet, sleep and mental state and so on, these are done to assess the degree of depression as an important basis. Therefore, the owner can do scl-90 test on the platform to see what the results are, according to the test results to book an appointment with a suitable teacher to provide a more detailed and specific situation to do the assessment, to see whether there is an organic lesion, and then consider accepting the systematic psychological counseling.

question: What is the psychological mechanism of asking rhetorical questions about every question someone asks?

question: Surround yourself with friends, everything will see the dark side, why do some people like to question it?
description: I have this kind of friend around me, and he questions everything that is told to him. For example, when he fell on his arm and broke it and needed surgery, he said it wasn't that serious and the hospital was just trying to make money! Everything sees the dark side! What kind of mentality is that? Why do people always question? How to avoid it!

answers.answer_text: I thought of my mom when I saw your question. Mom always suspects that everyone hurts her, that hospitals are all about earning money, that people have something to gain by being nice to you, that people look down on her if they don't offer to say hello, and other situations. Every time I hear my mom say that, I can't help but get angry. Then I think about the reason that her sense of self-worth is so low that she thinks she doesn't deserve better, so she feels that everything is bad. Mom is very sensitive and feels hurt once people don't take the initiative to greet her or initiate a conversation with her. According to mom's upbringing, she was brought up by her older brother and her parents passed away at a very early age, and in this such a situation, it was inevitable that she tasted all the flavors of life. In addition, she came to work in the big city at a very young age, the gap between the rich and the poor, naturally inevitably encountered some people who looked down on her, the inner very low self-esteem. So in his heart, she remembers all the people who are not good to him. And as a result, feels that the world is mostly full of bad people and that he does not deserve to meet good people. There is nothing we can do about meeting such people, and we argue with our mom every time. Finally told myself that there is nothing we can do to change others, we can only influence. Let him feel the goodness of others.

question: Why on earth would someone with no aspirations and no pursuits want to work hard?

keywords: Growth, Self-Growth, Self-Acceptance, Meaning of Life

answers.answer_text: Whenever it's late at night, or when I'm in trouble, I often ask myself what I'm fighting for. I know very well that it is for the expectation of my parents! My parents came from the countryside, and both of them came to the city to work hard, and also had to take care of our siblings and the four old people in our hometown, which was very hard. Although their education to us is very simple and rough, but it cultivated our tough and unyielding character! My brother and I both worked hard in our respective positions through our own efforts, and our incomes were more than adequate! Our parents seldom praise us, only often can be heard from neighbors or relatives from our parents and they praise the two of us! So I can't let my parents down! My mother often nagged me, we must fight for ourselves, do not be looked down upon, do not follow her old path, no stable job and income, how to support themselves and future children can not talk about their own hobbies and dreams to pay for! We came to this world, not a person alone to come, is the mother and we struggle together to come to this world! So I hope you can work hard for yourself and your family!

question: Not part of the expression, conflict with people, I hate myself for not being brave enough?
description: I hate myself for not being articulate, I hate myself for being afraid to reach out to the opposite sex of my heart, I hate myself for being afraid of conflict with people, and I hate myself for not being brave enough.

answers.answer_text: Although there are only a few words, I can feel that you are dissatisfied with yourself, and you use the word "hate" with strong feelings. But at the same time, I also see that behind the hate, you still have expectations, you expect yourself to be good at expression, you expect yourself to dare to contact with the opposite sex of the heart, expect yourself not to be afraid of conflict with others, expect yourself to be brave. When these expectations are not fulfilled by yourself, you blame yourself. Can blaming yourself help you to fulfill your expectations? When things don't happen as we want them to, we often like to respond by blaming ourselves. For example, if you go on stage and don't perform as expected, you will unconsciously start blaming yourself for not saying XX at the time when you get off the stage. When you are late for something important, you blame yourself for not going out earlier. There are a lot of examples of this kind of thing, and by blaming yourself, the matter seems to be over. But why do we form such "habits"? Think back to when you were a child, how did your parents respond when you did not do well in a test? If parents were faced with a situation where they "didn't do well", they would have lectured and taught, "Why didn't you do this question correctly? This is how you should solve the problem." Or, they may teach with a stick. By making yourself physically or psychologically uncomfortable in this way, the situation of "not doing well in the exam" will be over. But is it really over? Not really. The next time you take the test, the situation occurs again. By making oneself physically and mentally uncomfortable over and over again, this pattern of blaming oneself is reinforced, thus forming a "habitual" pattern, and when one grows up and encounters similar events, this button is triggered to protect oneself from the low mood of "not doing well". Emotions. When I was young, I didn't know how to deal with it, so I was forced to learn such a coping pattern. Now that I'm grown up, do I still need to use such an ineffective coping pattern? When you want to express yourself, you have the strength to do so, but you use it to attack and blame yourself, so you don't have the strength to think about how to express yourself. Everyone has the power within them to be a better version of themselves, they just use it in different directions. Good luck Karen.

Just bold on the exchange, only in practice you can grow. question: What if my parents keep harassing me about dating?
description: When my boyfriend and I go on shopping dates, my parents always call and harass me, asking where I am and why I'm not back yet. I actually explained to them before I left the house, but they still had to harass me. When I got home, they asked me like a prisoner for half an hour. I know they are doing it for my own good, but I feel annoyed again, what should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, owner, you can never have enough of our parents' concern for us, because in their eyes, we are still children and can be hurt. From your description, you can feel that you are upset and helpless due to your parents' excessive interference with you and your boyfriend during and after their dates. That is, you can relate to your parents' concern and care, but you would love to have a lot of space and freedom for yourself. It's not clear if your parents are as inquisitive and caring when it comes to other things you do? Or are they only like that when it comes to things involving your boyfriend? If it's the former, maybe your parents are more spoiled and aren't very comfortable with your autonomy and independence, and maybe you're also more dependent on your parents, being well-protected and having enough love under their care in everything. If it is the latter, your parents may be a little dissatisfied or concerned about the boyfriend you have, afraid that you will be hurt or not be able to do a good job of self-protection, or maybe you do not have a lot of experience in relationships, they are worried that you will be at a disadvantage. It's great that you can understand your parents' behavior, and it shows that you have the ability to push yourself to be aware, which is good. Allow yourself to grow to the point where they are comfortable enough to reduce the interference between them with concrete proactive actions. After understanding your parent's behavior, it may be that your emotions will calm down a bit, but if you still feel that their words and actions are more than a little worrying, try some ways to reassure them. First, inwardly, express their feelings, that is, they have grown up, have good self-protection ability, also know some of the methods of getting along between men and women, when encountering problems, they will take the initiative to inform them, they can rest assured; and, they are serious about this relationship, the boyfriend's character and love for you, are trustworthy, and I hope that they believe in their own choices. Secondly, every time you go out, you can roughly tell them what places you will go to, probably at what time to come back, in arriving and leaving a place, you can send a simple message, take the initiative to give them some signals, maybe they will not bother you many times. When you get home, you can also take the initiative to express some of your feelings about going out to play, whether it's good or bad, you can talk to them more about it, if you are an only child, there may be no other center of gravity in their life except you. If you choose to take the initiative to communicate and share, not only will your parents find you reliable, but they will probably ask a lot of questions the next time you go out. Good luck.
