question: There are so many things to do but none of them want to be done, nothing to do?
description: Final exams are coming soon, looking at the date is getting closer and closer, looking at a pile of homework papers, but what spirit can not lift, do not want to do anything at all, do not know what to do!

answers.answer_text: Hi owner, the ultimate way to deal with procrastination and anxiety is to convince yourself to get moving, and all the outwardly specific ways to do so point to the question of how to get things done. From your description, I can sense that you are feeling anxious and irritated and conflicted because you have a lot going on, near the end of the semester, a lot of homework, and probably other things. On the one hand, you know that avoiding and procrastinating just makes things, and your mood, worse and worse; on the other hand, there is absolutely no motivation to start anything. I understand how you feel, and many people feel the same way you do many times, wishing they could have someone to help them with their homework or that for some reason it was suddenly canceled, etc.; all sorts of fantasies that are just avoidance. You can try to let yourself rest for a day, do something you really want to do, want to play and want to eat, use this day to completely relax yourself, do not need to think about anything, just let yourself get pleasure to the fullest. After you've rested, make a plan for yourself, dividing the things you need to accomplish along two axes: importance and urgency. Plan your time by doing things that are both important and urgent first, and things that are neither important nor urgent last. In the meantime, the key thing is that you need to take action. From the moment you start doing the first thing, make yourself do it instead of continuing to avoid it, you must act for all the planning to make sense. There are specific ways in which you can get yourself to act, or you can seek help from family and friends. For example, when you are working on a paper, set yourself a time to finish one paper and then take a break to work on another, just as you would for an exam. Be sure to minimize or block out distractions, such as clutter on your desk, snacks, or cell phones. You can let your family and friends to supervise yourself, when you finish, give yourself a certain reward or other so that you can produce the motivation of their own efforts and perseverance, to recognize, do not underestimate this behavior, will allow you to gradually form self-discipline. Behind all the procrastination and avoidance lies our laziness and fear, we want to relax all the time, we don't want to work or study, we fear failure, even after we try exceptionally hard. But the good thing about us is that we can overcome them through our control and rationality, and I am sure you too will get rid of your procrastination and pick up your pen to do your papers as soon as possible. Good luck.

question: Why is everything around us disappointing?
description: I used to think that trust is the most important and precious thing, recently more than a year of big and small things happened, I began to misanthropy, so I'm the only one who valued trust so much, this society is really not half of the lovely place. The temper itself is not good, emotions come and go, and from time to time I feel sad, always think of myself as a child, think of the most reluctant to part with the deceased, but I also know that many of the emotions have nothing to do with the people around me, so I have to restrain my own emotions. From time to time, I also lash out at those closest to me and then force myself to calm down. I can have a good laugh, but I'm only really myself when I'm on my own, stuck in that memory with its happy and sad moments. Whenever I want to try to take a step outward, I always encounter a bad thing that brings up bad memories from the past, drawing a blank and becoming more and more disappointed in this society. I don't want to be an optimistic and positive person (even though on the surface everyone thinks I am), I just want to be able to sleep well at night and not have to cry secretly behind someone's back.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Thank you for your trust and for inviting me to listen to your heart! Honesty is the foundation of a person's foundation, and the fact that you can regard trust as so important and feel that it is the most important and precious thing is a supreme character within a person's heart and is invaluable! Over the past year or so, the big and small things that have happened have made you realize the loss of trust of the people around you, and such an experience, no matter who it happens to, will feel endless sadness and heartbreak. It's just that if you hide yourself deeply because of these disappointing and unhappy experiences, you will indeed miss out on a lot of beauty in the world. Don't want to be even more disappointed in society is it, please let me come with you to see what we can do in the past experience. ** about trust ** trust itself is not wrong, trust needs mutual understanding, the need for long-term interaction, the need for a tacit understanding of the heart, the maintenance of trust, but also the need for the same heart of the two people! Trust in human interaction is based on a person's values, attitudes, moods, emotions, personal charisma interaction. Trust in others also means that you must bear the risk of being harmed by the behavior of the other party, that is to say, the willingness to bear the risk of being harmed is also the core of the trust between people. So you see, when you choose to trust others and suffer betrayal and the pain that comes with it, it only means that you need to improve your ability to recognize others when you interact with them. This ability is not something that can be acquired overnight; it takes days and months of study, practice, reflection, and contemplation. Here are a few thinking paths for your reference: [Rational Decision Making] If you trust the other person wishfully, without the slightest suspicion, it can easily lead to a crisis or exacerbate a situation of trust abuse. So when you think about whether or not to trust a person, to obtain sufficient evidence of the other party's trustworthiness, such as: word of mouth, intention, ability, reliability, and so on, in order to determine whether the other party is trustworthy. [Goodwill] When the other person has goodwill, they usually prioritize you or your mutual interests. When you choose to trust the other person, you will be able to work with them and neither you nor your interests will be harmed. [Emotional State] An individual's emotional state affects the judgment of the other person's trustworthiness. This is why many people are usually blind and overwhelmed by emotion when they fall into a relationship (romance). Keeping yourself in a cool head is conducive to making appropriate judgments. And trust is usually the result of the interaction of emotions and rational thinking. Based on the above, together with your past experience, practice more. I think soon you will be able to figure out the right way to act in your interactions with people. **About Kindness** There is nothing wrong with being kind to people, but you can't be blindly kind; kindness is not being pinched as a soft target. "Kindness with teeth" is an important rule for dealing with interpersonal problems. The so-called goodness with teeth is good enough to cooperate with others, but also enough principles to violate their own bottom line of the people hard. Let's say for example, you helped a friend, and then this friend just kicked you: "Kindness" is the next time you meet other people need help, still stop to help this person in need of help; "Kindness with teeth" is to no longer help this person who once stepped on you, (emphasis added) unless he has stepped on you. Kindness with teeth" means not helping the person who has stepped on you, unless he chooses a cooperative strategy afterward. **On Optimism** Finally, a word about optimism. You also talked about hurting people close to you because of your emotional problems. I think this is mostly because of the unpleasant things that happened outside, touching the bottom of your heart once left behind the pain, when you return to the familiar feel safe in the environment, these deposition of the pain of the brain came up, so that you can not afford to take it, all the catharsis in the closest people. Often the reason for being hard on those closest to you is because inwardly you know it's safe to do so. So why did I choose to say optimism in the end? It's because optimism itself is having a positive attitude towards the future and towards others. It's also a surefire way to support us in walking with conviction. Jack Ma said, "All the big people I've ever met are optimistic at heart." So you see, it's not about who has experienced less than whom, but who is more able to hold on to goodness in life, and who also understands the complexities and contradictions of human nature better, and at the same time is able to give the world a little bit more tolerance, always believing in the goodness of the world, believing that where there is darkness, there must be light, and believing that mankind will eventually move forward through the twists and turns. This is the so-called optimism! Do not be afraid of the floating clouds to cover your eyes, since you are in the highest level. answers.answer_text: Hello owner,1 First of all, I'm sorry to say that in order to better explain your situation, I need to give you a label: narcissistic personality disorder. According to modern object relations theory, people with narcissistic personality disorder are characterized by "self as object". They are unable to project feelings of love, care, and concern onto other people and things, but instead internalize them and turn them into a form of egoism. Such a personality can arise because, in their early years, they have experienced traumas in interpersonal relationships, such as prolonged separation from their parents, poor parental relationships, or parents who were too rough or too spoiled in their attitudes, and so on. Such experiences make them [feel safe and justified in loving themselves].2 But, with Narcissistic Personality Disorder, the label only goes halfway for you. The process of forming your personality should not have been a pleasant experience, and the fact that grandma and grandpa were the best for you is an indirect indication of the absence of your parents at a crucial moment in your life. Your egoism is for your own [protection], but your protection is not complete, you don't get the [security] you want. You say that you were not attracted to your romantic partner, but were just in a position to take advantage of him. Perhaps in that moment, as soon as a person expressed good feelings for you, you clung to them. You didn't realize this: that [our own thoughts are really important], that we don't need to be completely objective, that we can be ourselves. But when it comes to being with people, you're probably in a state of tightness and can't bring yourself to let down your defenses.3 If that's the case, the past is the past and can't be changed. But we can do what we can for our present and our future.4 Our brains are selective in how they process and connect information, and everyone has their own way of associating things. Perhaps you have been accustomed to, in the face of a thing a person, first from the [God's perspective] to see it, observe, analyze, and finally define, deduce conclusions. This habit makes you [no sense of participation], feel indifferent and objective. When something happens that is directed at you, you are immediately in a state of stress, turning on your defense mode and offering up this set of weapons.5 The first thing you need to do is to make an observation about your habit. The fact that you have asked this question and described yourself in detail means that you have already made some observations about yourself, but you need to go further and [feel your tension and wariness]. For example, when you read what I have written, you subconsciously analyze my purpose and attempts, thinking that I am trying to get your bounty. Yes, that is indeed one of my purposes. But my deeper purpose is to use what I have learned to bring you help and to consolidate my body of knowledge.6 Secondly, after observing your own behavior for a while, you may think, "Why is this person named "I" so strange? By asking this question, you should have observed yourself for a period of time and have noticed how strange you are. If you observe your own stress pattern, this strange feeling will be more obvious - why every moment I am on the defense of others, calculating in my brain, which is very tiring and creates problems in our interpersonal interactions. Most importantly, we don't get the security we want in this way. If you realize this and understand what you really want, you will want to make change yourself. Of course, if that's fine with you, then being yourself is also an option. There is no optimal choice in the world; remember that how you feel is most important.7 If you want to make a change, you can use your brain's habit pathways to build new associations. The building of associations requires deliberate training, and we can practice this on a regular basis. For example, let's say that you think that you, yourself, have no love for the person you used to be in love with. So, would you say yes to everyone who asked you for love? Another example: you think that when your grandma and grandpa died, all you thought about was weekly fodder. You can go through your weekly journal and see if you wrote anything, and I think you probably didn't. Because you were probably just consoling yourself and giving yourself a reason to be less sad. The fact that your favorite person left you still makes it hard, doesn't it?8 When you replace the habit of indifference with new associations, you'll feel more engaged, and more confident about building new relationships, too.9 Finally, when you fall in love, even ordinary people become extraordinary in your eyes. question: What is the point of counseling when you have been struggling with depression for two years?
description: I don't understand the significance of heart counseling, two years have been struggling with depression, struggling, the counselor said the most words is what? It seems that every time I said, she used Morita therapy on me to let nature take its course? From the initial torment struggle do not want to live to now have no power to struggle to also do not want to live, is it progress or regression?

answers.answer_text: Hello! From my understanding, the meaning of counseling is that the counselor accompanies the visitor to face the difficulties in life, provides unconditional positive attention and support, and enables the visitor to find his/her own strengths and resources to face the difficulties as well as to achieve personality growth. In other words, the ultimate goal of counseling is for the visitor to be independent, not dependent on the counselor. You've been in counseling for two years for depression, but it seems that you haven't made much progress in terms of your status, so you're skeptical and unsure about the counselor and the counseling. On the one hand, it is true that depression is a condition that requires long-term companionship, so the counseling time will be longer overall; on the other hand, your counselor has been letting you talk, and perhaps he has taken a counseling approach that is centered on you, and more on supporting you through your confidences and his listening. I can't say that this approach is not effective, depressed people need to be supported, but after two years, maybe this approach is not very effective for you. That's why you have developed the above doubts. I would suggest you to try to find a counselor of a different school of thought and see if there is one for you. Because different schools of counselors his counseling assumptions are not the same, then take a different approach, perhaps the key to your depression needs another suitable key to open. In our usual work, we also received many depression patients, some are severe. But then also cured. On the one hand, follow the doctor's advice to take medication to take medication, and secondly, have the will to treat actively go to psychological counseling. With the combination of these two aspects, there is definitely hope. I am a family therapy counselor, and in my opinion, there are many factors that contribute to a person's depression. But everyone has an initial environmental factor that has the greatest impact, and that is the family. Patterns of interaction in the family, parenting styles, etc., basically have a big impact, so it's at that level that a big part of it can go away and be addressed. Specializing in the use of cards, dolls and other small objects for the precise presentation and transformation of cases, to share with you the knowledge of psychology, welcome to pay attention to, have questions can be private message me!

Hi, depression is all about intolerance of hurting others and attacking oneself inwardly. It is easy to see this in counseling for depression, where the source of the visitor's pain, many times, is the aggression directed at themselves. This inward attack characterizes their inability to do anything well, and what they don't do well in turn becomes a source of self-blame for their guilt. I don't understand the point of heart counseling, two years of struggling and agonizing with depression. It means that you have been attacking depression and not accepting it for two years, which in fact means that you are attacking yourself and aggravating the pain caused by depression. You may think, I've been counseling all this time, I've been working on it, but why is it still like this, nothing has changed. It's like falling into a quagmire, the struggle and struggle will only get you deeper and deeper into it. One direction of counseling is acceptance, learning to see yourself as you are, accepting yourself as you are in depression, which means not judging, not blaming, just seeing your struggles, seeing your thoughts, but knowing that there is no good or bad, it's just the way you are. From the initial tormenting struggle of not wanting to live to now being powerless to struggle to not wanting to live either, is that progress or regression. No change does not mean no change. Many people can keep the status quo unchanged, has exhausted all the strength, you can see that you have not become bad, is their own biggest change and efforts, learn to affirm themselves. It is because you feel that you are not good enough now, so you do not accept yourself, you want to try to change, but you can not change, you feel bad, bad, vicious circle. This also shows that you can't accept yourself yet, when you can accept yourself as bad, it's not good enough to attack yourself as bad, it's good enough. Remember, you are good enough, you don't have to be better to be good enough. Learn to see your goodness, be aware of yourself, and not be carried away by your attacks.

Hi, I am worried for you to see that you are still struggling and suffering from the symptoms of depression. I don't know much about Morita therapy, I learned cognitive behavioral therapy myself, and the best psychological treatment for depression in hospitals at home and abroad is cognitive behavioral therapy. The so-called cognitive-behavioral therapy, one is cognitive change, one is behavioral activation. Depression is a mental illness, first of all, we have a lot of distorted cognition, need to go to correct his automatic thinking, middle beliefs and core beliefs. For example, there is no way to recover, all counseling methods are useless to me, I am incompetent, unlovable, the world is dangerous, no one else can help me, and so on. In addition, depressed patients will also have some, such as sleep disorders, anxiety, procrastination and other co-morbid symptoms, and it's very important to motivate them to change their behavior while making cognitive changes. I see that you have a strong determination to heal, which is very good. The main body of counseling is you, as long as your motivation is strong enough, I believe that together with the help of the counselor, you will be able to get out of depression.

question: 20 years old, confused about relationships and having a hard time building relationships with others quickly?

answers.answer_text: Hi subject, I'm looking up at the stars, first of all hugs to you. Everyone grows up in different environments, which creates different personalities in each person. Sometimes these differences are quite obvious. For example, as you described in your question, some people are "easy to get acquainted with" and can become buddies after a couple of lines of conversation, while others are "slow to warm up" type. That's why psychology roughly categorizes people into two types, introverts and extroverts. Different personalities are not good or bad, each has its own advantages. Characteristics of introverts: they don't like to socialize and prefer to be alone. Socializing, or specifically, the kind of socializing that builds relationships just for the sake of a one-sided relationship, can be stressful for introverts. Introverts prefer to be alone, reflect on themselves, and look "inward" (into their own hearts) rather than "outward" (into the company of others). Introverts are better at deep thinking. Introverts don't like meaningless, superficial socializing, so they spend their time alone and thinking. Historically, Napoleon, Einstein, Van Gogh, Picasso, Chaplin, Tolstoy, etc., they were all introverts. They possessed extraordinary creativity and imagination, and I have to say that this was closely related to their preference for solitude and reflection. Introverts are more likely to reflect and improve themselves. When faced with interpersonal conflicts, introverts think first of all about whether they have done anything wrong, so it is easier for them to reflect on themselves in order to improve. Of course, sometimes introverts often attribute problems to themselves, which may trigger emotional reactions such as self-blame and guilt. Characteristics of extroverts: they like to make friends and socialize. Instead of being stressful for them, socializing is the most effective way to release internal stress. You said in your question that you don't quite understand why some people enjoy small talk and the feeling of quickly building relationships with others. In fact, this is exactly how they release their inner pressure and recharge themselves. The opposite is true for introverts. There are no good or bad personalities, all we have to do is build on our strengths. Introverts may not be good at building relationships quickly, but they don't have no relationships, and their network is often filled with friends or girlfriends who have shared experiences, know each other well, and trust each other. Relationships are not about quantity, but quality. It is enough to have one or two people around you who can help in times of trouble and are willing to listen to what you have to say. You said in your question that you feel bad about the "small talk" atmosphere. If you don't feel comfortable with this kind of "chit-chat", you don't need to involve yourself in it, except for work. Making a cup of tea at home, picking up a book to read, or looking out the window and thinking about life may be the best way for introverts to let go of stress and recharge their batteries. So follow your heart, learn to please yourself, and make yourself happy and joyful is the most important task.

There are three ways to cascade your way from blocking anxiety to achieving a cure for it. The first way: is to quickly interrupt anxiety by shifting your attention. An easy way to train yourself to be flexible with your attention is to start by just focusing ahead and letting your attention focus on a point on the wall for a few seconds. Then, shift your attention and start paying attention to your surroundings while you are looking ahead. While you're paying attention to your surroundings, try to recall the anxiety, which you'll find difficult. This is because you have turned on a state of calm. The authors also suggest a method of "mind wandering", which in layman's terms means letting your brain "wander". For example, when you have to make an important decision, you may feel anxious in the process of weighing the pros and cons, at this time, you can try to steal a break from the busyness of problem solving, take a break for a moment. Then let your mind wander around and think about a beautiful view you once saw or recall a pleasant experience. This approach quickly calms your brain, alpha brainwaves are greatly increased, anxiety is interrupted, which in turn stimulates your creative thinking and helps you find solutions, pointing you in new directions and new ideas. Taking it a step further requires us to learn to switch emotional modes and thus control the dissolution of anxiety. The second way: when you feel anxious again, or when a scary movie starts to play in your head again, you can try to follow these steps: The first step is to ask yourself. The first step is to ask yourself, "What's going on?" "What am I worried about?" Replace anxiety and fear with "curiosity" and take some time to answer these questions, which can immediately reduce the intensity of your anxiety and give yourself a chance to get rid of it. The second step is to stop exercising and check in with your body. question: Curious, does doing negative type questionnaires have an effect on mood?
description: While listening to a class, the instructor talked about the ethics of psychological experiments and wanted to know if doing a negative type of questionnaire would have an emotional impact on the average person? Will it make people feel uncomfortable? What do the subjects need to be aware of?

answers.answer_text: Hi owner, I recently read Elliot . Aronson's The Social Animal, a textbook on social psychology, and in Chapter 9: Social Psychology as a Science of the book, there is a reference to ethical issues regarding social psychology experiments. Social psychology is the study of human behavior, and social psychology researchers observe social phenomena and formulate hypotheses, design experiments, recruit volunteers to conduct the experiments, summarize the data, and support our hypotheses with scientifically sound results. All the cases in our social psychology textbooks are results obtained from statistical data by researchers recruiting volunteers to conduct experiments. The Milgram electroshock experiment was even more egregious in nature than the negative questionnaire. In order to study the relationship between evil and subordination in humans, Milgram recruited volunteers to play the role of prison guards, who were required to inflict electric shock punishment on inmates. The electric shocks were simulated, but to make the scene more realistic, Milgram simulated the screams of the prisoners so that the real volunteers, playing the role of prison guards, would think that they were actually hurting another human being. The results of the electroshock experiment were invaluable in proving that we all have the potential to have extreme personalities. But after this experiment was over, the volunteers involved experienced inner torture. Chapter 9 of The Social Animal describes the results of the follow-up of the volunteers in the experiment, which showed that, although some of the volunteers said that the experiment had caused them distress. However, the greater part of the volunteers, after learning the significance of the experiment and the final results, understood the defects of human beings as social animals, and the experience, on the contrary, allowed him to improve his self-knowledge, which helped him to a certain extent in his life. Turning back to your question. Negative questionnaires do affect volunteers, so the experimenter needs to do a good job of explaining and channeling, informing the volunteer of the real purpose of the survey after he has done the questionnaire, and giving the results back to the subject. As for the subjects, after doing such questionnaires, they can follow up the follow-up to understand the statistics and the final results, and according to the results, examine themselves, face up to the deficiencies they have as social animals, and make improvements to their selves.

answers.answer_text: It sounds like you have a lot of anger within you. Even if sometimes your reason agrees that it's your fault, your emotions still feel angry and can't be calmed. Anger is a very powerful emotion, but in our culture it's often the easiest to invite criticism, and criticism tends to lead to more anger that doesn't go away, but just gets buried and waits for an opportunity. When something comes along that can still be angry, it's easier to take advantage of the opportunity to explode all together, and from an outside perspective it looks as if the person is out of control with unreasonable rage, which brings more blame and lack of understanding, which creates a vicious cycle. If you grew up feeling more intense anger, it is also very easy to be treated as an emotional child inviting criticism, such as the above cycle continues, and may even develop emotional control problems. First of all, we need to know that there are cultural factors, there are factors in the family environment, and then there are also factors related to our own innate traits, and knowing this, we can differentiate between them. The best way to deal with anger is to be gentle but firm, principles and reason need not be denied, but emotionally as friendly as possible to yourself, understanding that dealing with anger is really not an easy thing to do, if this can let a little bit of anger to vent out, dispersed, the emotional pattern of the gradual calm, that's very good, if you still feel that they are alone difficulties, especially affecting the life of work and study, then you can also consider seeking professional If you still find it difficult to be alone, especially if it affects your life, work or study, then you may also consider seeking professional help, such as a counselor who specializes in emotional problems or has a background in autopsychology may be able to help you.

question: What can I do if I've been working for 4 years and still have character flaw issues with people?

answers.answer_text: I think you have two concerns, one is that you won't be able to do things well, and the other is that you won't be valuable. To address the first point, I suggest you do more things. You say you are very unsure of yourself and worried about doing things with others. What are you worried about? Is it the fear that if you don't do things right you will suffer particularly terrible consequences, and that you won't be able to bear the consequences. These fantastical fears often haunt you and keep you from taking action. So the most important thing is to take action and do more. Yohji Yamamoto once said, "You can't see yourself, but when you hit something else and it bounces back, you can understand yourself. Therefore, if you do more work and collide with other people and things, you will know yourself better. Go hard. By doing things more often, you will experience different situations and gain different experiences: what will happen if I do this in this situation, what will happen if I do that? What else can I do in a different situation, and what is the difference in the results I get? When you experience more, you won't be scared by your own imagination. It's like a pony crossing a river, always take two steps forward yourself, try it out, and maybe realize that the river isn't as scary as you thought it was. Do more, start with something that is a little bit of a challenge for you. Success is the affirmation of their own, write it down, look it up from time to time, encourage yourself. Failure to do the wrong thing is an even more valuable experience, and you'll realize that the outcome wasn't even as scary as you thought it was going to be. Although you do not do the right thing, but the world is still running, things will continue to go on, it turns out that in your eyes the sky big thing, may be a few words of other people to bring over, no big deal. Mistakes that you thought you could never make don't really matter much. Put yourself in someone else's place and consider how much you care about what someone else did or said wrong, how many days can you think about it? When you have the experience of doing something wrong, you will be braver. To address the second point, love yourself more. You have low self-esteem when you ask people to do things, and you always want to finish quickly when you talk to people. Are you afraid that you are not valuable enough to hold others back? In fact, everyone in the world has a unique value, you fully believe in your own value, feel good enough, the other party will also value you, respect you. And while you may now feel that your sense of worth is inadequate, an effect of your parents' attitudes on you since you were a child, you can now go about changing your views, discovering your own value, and respecting yourself. Start by loving yourself, by honoring your feelings. Like what you want, what you want to do, fulfill your needs, and value your requests. Or compliment and affirm yourself every day, and compliment each other with your friends. The more important you see yourself as, the more important you really are in a relationship. All of these concepts are formed over time, so it may take some time to change, don't rush, a little action, change will happen without you realizing it.

Therefore, setting a counseling goal is a very important thing, and only when a person has a goal will he be motivated to understand where his own problems are. The pilot first asked the subjects to fill out scales of meaning of life, life satisfaction, psychological stress, etc., and gave each subject a camera to take 9-12 photos of objects they thought were "meaningful" to them within a week. The camera was returned one week later with a brief description and report of the photographs, after which the scales were refilled. By analyzing the data from both the pre-test and post-test, the researchers found that after the week of photographing, the subjects' sense of meaning in their lives became clearer, and their life satisfaction increased significantly. Due to space constraints, the researchers didn't list exactly what the meaningful objects were that everyone photographed, but if I were to photograph them, I'd photograph the cutest doll above my bed, the cat's butt floor cushion in the entryway of my room, and the whale lamp on my bookshelf. question: I always listen to others, but no one listens to me, and I feel very lonely.
description: I am essentially a cowardly person, I also worry about various things, but I can never speak up. I have tried, but I am disappointed time and time again. It seems like most people cannot understand or care about my feelings. Sometimes when I talk to my mother, she ignores me and starts talking about unrelated topics. When I confide in someone I know, she just laughs and says, "I thought you had something important to say." I know I am too sensitive, even a small hurt can sting me, so I no longer confide in people because I don't want to be let down. All my emotions are buried inside me, but I am actually very lonely.

answers.answer_text: Hello, as a high school student, you can not only handle the heavy pressure of academics, but also be a listener for others, easing their worries. You're truly amazing! Thumbs up to you~ However, while you help others, you find yourself in a difficult situation, struggling to resolve your own negative emotions, which makes you sensitive and uncomfortable. I feel for you, and I hope my answer can help you. Recognize your own abilities and only do what you're capable of. Not everyone who appears gentle is suitable to be a listener. Before becoming a listener, we need to learn to sort out our own troubles. If we can't handle our own issues, then how can we help others? There's a saying, "Take care of yourself first, and then help others when you can." As a listener, you should have this awareness. You need to take care of your own mental health first before absorbing the unhealthiness of others and having the energy to resolve it. So, the initial problem is that you took on the role of a listener, which you weren't good at and didn't qualify for, resulting in a series of subsequent troubles. It's okay to politely decline someone's confiding in you. You can choose to listen, but you can also choose to refuse. You need to have the courage to refuse without feeling guilty or accepting verbally just to make yourself uncomfortable. In your description, it can also be seen that you often attract people inexplicably. It's because of the facade you put on. Perhaps many times we say we need to learn to disguise ourselves and not easily reveal our inner world to others. But dear, you are yourself. If you bury even your most genuine thoughts and can't hear your own voice, how can you reconcile with your heart and hope for its growth, to be strong enough? Value your inner self, respect it, ask yourself if it's willing before agreeing to someone's request. Then let go of the disguise and be your true self. You don't have to pretend in front of everyone all the time, you can also express your anxiety about studying, your worries about exams, and not be constantly positive and sunny. Build your own support system. I'm too sensitive and even a little hurt can sting me, so I no longer confide in others because I don't want to be disappointed. All my emotions are buried in my heart, but in fact, I'm so lonely. I pity you for encountering frustration while seeking help which didn't ultimately alleviate your negative emotions, causing you to doubt seeking help and feeling disappointed. But I want to tell you that good listeners who can truly help you aren't found overnight, and not everyone is capable of it. You need to learn to bear the risk of failure and not be disappointed. It's hard to find someone who truly understands, but it doesn't mean they don't exist. Keep hope in your heart, and only then can you see the moonlight breaking through the clouds, find that person who will patiently listen to your inner voice, and bring warmth into your lonely heart! Best wishes!

Hello, baby! Every time you dare to open your heart and express your problems, it is a manifestation of your need for self-improvement, which is very good. I completely understand your distress. You need someone to confide in, but you haven't found the right listener, so your loneliness and unhappiness cannot be resolved. It seems contradictory. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Taking yourself seriously requires courage to face your inner feelings. It's easy to see that you, baby, are intelligent and attractive, which can easily win the trust of friends around you. This is indeed an advantage and can be considered a talent. If used correctly, it will definitely help us grow and be happy. From the current situation, it seems that baby has not discovered the real problem behind the problem. That is, you need to take yourself seriously, experience your unhappiness, face your loneliness, and understand whether you should embrace or reject the need for external listening at the moment. Have you ever asked yourself why you pretend to be understanding. This is guiding you to explore yourself. I believe that you will definitely benefit from listening in one of those times. This benefit may be the appearance of not being lonely surrounded by people around you, or it may be personal affirmation after a listening session. Now you need to examine the essence. Is this pretense completely fake? 1. Is it your own personality, but you are feeling unbalanced because you can't find a listener now? 2. Or are you really pretending, and you always feel irritable after listening, resisting during the listening process? You need to seriously experience this feeling and bravely face the answers in your heart. Accepting your perfection and imperfection. After being aware of yourself, maybe you have discovered your perfection and also realized your imperfections. It's okay, tell yourself, that is who you are, your true self. Therefore, we must first serve ourselves. Listen to your own thoughts. If you don't like being approached or asked to be a listener, then boldly express your refusal. Of course, just as we don't want to be rejected when we want to be listened to, we should express it in a tactful way. "Afraid of hurting others, feels cowardly", this may simply mean that you, baby, need to be listened to, surrounded, and cared for. However, it doesn't mean that you don't like being a listener, but that your inner strength is not enough to become the person you need to be. Accepting your imperfections requires self-affirmation. Even if you don't become a listener, you can still confide in yourself and deserve to be listened to and cared for by others. A piece of advice: Many times, when our needs cannot be met by ourselves, we tend to seek externally. If we get it, everyone is happy and everything feels natural. But sometimes we can't find it, and now we see that not finding it is also a common thing. In that case, let's continue to serve ourselves. This is different from "I no longer confide in others because I don't want to be disappointed with all my emotions buried in my heart." We can express our feelings through a journal or become stronger through exercise, broaden our horizons through music. Come on, baby. Maybe one day, you will find that while you are growing, you have gained your own fans. .................................... In high school, we have the enviable youth and the unique melancholy of youth. We need to let go of ourselves and also to be able to express ourselves. The most important thing is self-growth and reflection. Our goal may not be to become a rare genius, but we can grow into our own confidant. The sky is blue, you are here, life can be beautiful! The world, I love you!

Hello, dear friend. It pains me to see what you're going through, so first, I want to give you a hug. For many people, they may be good at expressing their desires and thoughts, such as what they are currently thinking and what they need. However, not everyone is capable of truly stopping and listening to others' thoughts and feelings. And I think you're probably one of these gentle and self-restrained individuals. You have a strong sense of empathy and are willing to understand others' perspectives, and it's no wonder that you are well-liked. However, you may be too focused on other people's opinions of you and trapped by their expectations, forgetting to listen to your own needs. Even the kindest and most compassionate person has the right to say no when faced with unreasonable requests from others. This is your right, and it has nothing to do with others' opinions. I understand that someone with a pure and delicate heart like yours may feel upset and hurt when faced with the neglect of their own needs and thoughts. But it is precisely because of this that you should try bravely to express your thoughts to others. Personally, I strongly agree with your decision to cut ties with the person who treated you as an emotional dumping ground. However, you shouldn't let your grievances and discontent accumulate to the point of wanting to vent it all out. Acting out of anger often leads to irrational actions and may even harm yourself. If you want to receive genuine attention, you need to courageously communicate your thoughts and feelings clearly. Start with small things in your daily life, such as what you want to eat or not eat today. No matter how others initially react, you must begin to express your inner needs. Take it slow, and things will eventually get better. Wishing you well, from a little mushroom who hopes for a gentle world and wishes you the time to grow freely.

Hi, Loulou! This is Aliang, someone who is willing to be your little ray of sunshine. Here, Aliang wants to give you a big hug. Hug you! After reading Loulou's words, Aliang also understands Loulou's anxiety because in many cases, Aliang actually plays an opposing role to Loulou. In real life, Aliang is more of a storyteller and rarely acts as a listener because the listener is easily influenced by the other person's emotions. If one does not have good self-control, it is actually not suitable to be a listener. Regarding the problems that trouble Loulou, Aliang wants to analyze them from a personal perspective: "How to solve the identity of being a listener." From Loulou's words, Aliang sees that Loulou is actually someone who is easily regarded as a venting object by others, and this is largely related to Loulou's "personality." In real life, people tend to show their negative side to someone who appears "gentle" in character. When they completely vent their grievances, they experience a great sense of relief in their own hearts. However, most of the time, a person venting does not consider what the listener feels. They need to say everything and hope to be understood and recognized by the listener, needing the listener to have the same "empathy" as them. They hope you will comfort them. At this time, the suggestions you give may not necessarily be accepted by the other person. Loulou does not like this feeling, so communication is necessary with them. Because Loulou is not their exclusive audience, you also have your own things to deal with, so when they talk to you about something, Loulou can refuse them. We are not obligated to listen to other people's negative energy, so Loulou does not need to be anxious. Loulou also doesn't need to pretend to be a very kind person. Sometimes, being your true self can also gain friendships. "Saying goodbye to inner insecurity," Loulou understands why they have these troubles themselves, because of insecurity and fear. These negative emotions, to some extent, exist in each of us. However, sometimes we need to overcome our own inner insecurities. Loulou also mentioned their tendency to avoid problems, but sometimes we understand that avoiding problems is not useful. The existence of these problems is largely due to our spiritual world not being rich enough. Because when we have a sense of abundance in a certain aspect, we will not fear our inner insecurities and anxieties. Sometimes, if we really don't know how to take that step forward, we can read more books, find a common point among those examples, and proceed based on that in conjunction with reality. The above is Aliang's personal insight for Loulou, hoping it can be helpful. In the future, Aliang will be here together with Loulou, encouraging each other. Keep up the good work!

First of all, let me commend you, the author of the original post. You are able to express your thoughts sincerely, which shows that you have taken a step towards self-improvement. Reading your description, I can understand and empathize with you. Here are some suggestions that I hope can help you. First, be true to yourself. You have been living according to the opinions of others for a long time. They think of you as a good listener, so your kind heart has led you to compromise and become the person they want you to be. But what about yourself? You have considered their feelings but neglected your own true emotions. Over time, this has become a habit, which may result in suppressed emotions and sensitivity. Therefore, what you need to do now is no longer be a listener in the eyes of others, get rid of your emotional baggage, and rediscover your true self. Secondly, when you confide in others, make them realize that you do need help. Because the people around you are used to confiding in you, and you simply accept without seeking a solution. So when you start confiding in others, they subconsciously feel that you can handle it on your own and don't need their response. As a result, they may appear indifferent. Over time, you will feel heartbroken, lost, disappointed, and stop having any expectations of the people around you, feeling lonely. Therefore, when you want to confide in someone, change your previous compliant attitude, be a bit more firm, and let others realize that you do indeed face difficulties that cannot be digested or solved on your own, and that you need their help. These are the solutions I propose for this situation. I hope they can help you. Wishing you an intimate friend soon and happiness always with you!

Before analyzing your problem, I’d like to share a true story with you. I believe this story may provide some insights into your current situation. One day, a customer called the human resources department and said, "All the products I bought in your store yesterday have expired. How do you manage your products? How could expired goods be sold?" Employee Xiao Li replied, "Expired goods? That's impossible. How could our store have expired goods? We have dedicated staff members who check the shelf life of products." The customer said, “Are you implying that I’m lying?” Xiao Li answered, “It’s hard to say.” The customer persisted, “I want to speak to the person in charge and demand a reasonable explanation.” Xiao Li apologized and said, “I work in the human resources department and I’m not responsible for product management. I don't know the specific details. I suggest you call the customer service hotline.” Okay, the dialogue scene ends here. You might think Xiao Li’s actions were unnecessary because this issue was beyond their department’s scope, and they couldn't provide the customer with a satisfactory solution. Why didn't they immediately interrupt and provide the correct complaint channel to the customer when they heard the customer’s first sentence? Why make the customer go around in circles? Why play the role of a middleman? Now, let's return to your question, why do others always tell you things you don't want to hear? You have already analyzed it clearly. You pretend to understand and sympathize. Simply put, you want to be seen as a kind person who is willing to listen to others' complaints. Whatever others throw at you, you won’t stop them at the first moment. Have you heard of the "broken windows theory"? This theory comes from an experiment conducted by psychologist Phillip Zimbardo at Stanford University in 1969. He took two identical cars, one parked in a middle-class neighborhood in Palo Alto, California, and the other parked in the relatively disorderly Bronx area of New York. The license plate was removed from the car in the Bronx, and it was stolen on the same day. The car in Palo Alto was ignored for a week. Later, Zimbardo smashed the window of the car in Palo Alto with a hammer. What happened? A few hours later, it disappeared. Based on this experiment, they concluded: if someone breaks a window of a building and it is not repaired, others may tolerate and break more windows. Ultimately, these broken windows create a sense of disorder. The broken windows theory suggests that if negative phenomena in the environment cannot be effectively resolved, people may imitate or even exacerbate these phenomena. This phenomena is referred to as the broken windows effect in the field of criminal psychology. Finally, I want to correct a misunderstanding: feeling lonely is not necessarily related to whether one has companionship. The feeling of loneliness is related to a lack of nonverbal communication and the ability to feel loved. This means that loneliness and emptiness cannot be solved solely through verbal companionship. I hope you can let go of the "masks" and "roles" in social situations and truly listen to your inner voice, opinions, and thoughts. When helping others, consider your own abilities, but don't portray yourself as a "savior" - that will only exhaust you!

Title owner, hello! After carefully reading your question, I feel so sorry for what you're going through. Here's a strong hug for you, and I hope my answer can be helpful to you. The fact that you're a high school student and already a good listener shows that you are worthy of others' reliance. However, you are also trapped in distress: firstly, no one is willing to listen to others, and secondly, you don't want to always be the emotional dumping ground. I have had a similar experience to yours. People often confide in me, thinking that I am trustworthy, and they unload their negative emotions on me to digest by myself, which makes me very distressed. The most memorable instance was one morning when I was in a good mood. After breakfast, I was preparing to go to work happily when a friend called me repeatedly. Worried that something was wrong, I hung up and called back. It turned out that he hadn't completed his work due to his own problems, and the boss had criticized him by name in the group chat. He told me how difficult his work was and how the boss was unsympathetic. He kept talking on the phone, forgetting to bring the books he had prepared for the students the night before. He poured all the negative emotions onto me, and my mood also became negative. Forgetting to take the books made me unable to give the students their class, leading me to have a terrible mood for the rest of the day. I realized that this was not a healthy situation. #Politely refuse# If you are not a very close friend who is willing to listen to his venting, when he pours negative emotions onto you, you can politely refuse. When someone pours negative emotions onto you, you can say, "I'm sorry, I just remembered that I haven't finished my homework yet. I have to go and do it." Find a suitable listener# It seems that you have not found a listener who understands and is willing to listen to you. Even your mother is not good at listening to you, which is really disappointing. Not everyone is capable of being your listener, but it doesn't mean you can't find one. Get to know more friends, communicate with more people, and you will definitely find someone. Take care! You are loved by me and the whole world!

Hello, first of all, I would like to thank you on behalf of those who trust you. It is not your obligation or responsibility to listen, but rather your kindness and appreciation for these emotional connections that make you willing to be their emotional dumping ground. So, when you no longer want to be someone's emotional dumpster, be direct and honest about it, without overly worrying about other people's feelings or feeling guilty. You are not obligated to listen to them. If you can't find someone willing to listen to you, you can speak up on this platform. There are many people in this world who are willing to listen to you, and there are also many strangers who are willing to accept and encourage you. May you always be treated with gentleness in this world!

Others confide in you because they trust you and see you as reliable. Being trusted by others is a blessing. If you have your own things to do or don't feel like listening, you can politely let them know and suggest an outlet for them to confide in, like this platform. That way, you can focus on your own affairs while still receiving gratitude from others. I am a high school student, and it seems that I am naturally a good listener, which makes it easy for others to depend on me. One of my classmates is immature and emotional, and because I always listen to him, he sees me as a gentle person and relies on me as a shoulder to lean on. When you become aware of your kindness, try not to have any negative thoughts about others or end the friendship because of it. In fact, being relied on by others can make you feel responsible for a life. Through the process of listening and providing guidance, you will deeply experience this responsibility. It will make you feel needed and bring you a sense of peace and happiness. However, if you feel disconnected or even disgusted by others' dependence, perhaps it's not a need that comes from within you. I understand. You say that no one listens to you and you feel lonely. That's because some love must start from ourselves first, and then we will receive in return. Treat others as you wish to be treated. We must understand that negative experiences from the past only affect us because we allow them to control our current behavior. We can start making changes from small details in the present, showing kindness to others, doing good deeds, or even just smiling. The more gentle we speak, the more likely we are to receive kind responses.

You will find many older brothers, sisters, uncles, and aunts who care for you, love you, have the ability to calm down and listen to your voice, give you professional advice, and heartfelt "hugs" above. You are more mature and introverted than your peers, and they rely on you. You really want to grow up quickly and manage your emotions well, but the emotional trash can also has its limits. If it goes beyond that range, it will hurt yourself and others like a volcanic eruption. You are very clever, able to discern the difference between sympathy and liking in your heart. This potential is not seen by others, so you think you are being liked and sensitive, which makes you angry and isolated. In fact, you are really kind (this is not a disguise, it is an advantage that others truly see). Because you are afraid of hurting others, you can only find excuses to evade. When you were young, you always wanted to grow up and have invincible abilities to help others, but when you grow up, you find the insignificance and powerlessness of human beings. Everyone has different worries at different stages. Some people like to vent and hope that someone will listen and help, while others prefer to read and digest things on their own without speaking out. There is no right or wrong, just different traits, different growth environments, and different processes and costs of growth. If you always feel hurt and don't want to be disappointed by not sharing with others, then learn how to avoid getting hurt first. This ability to learn in solitude may become a charm (your unique charm), or letting capable people see your emotions is also a way~ then you won't be disappointed anymore. Change your way of thinking, whether to speak or not is your own choice, and avoiding anger and escaping from the emotional trash can is also a method.

question: It is not appropriate to provide guidance or support for self-harm or harmful behaviors. If you or someone you know is struggling with self-harm or mental health issues, it is important to seek professional help from a healthcare provider or counselor.
description: "I am a 12-year-old girl in the sixth grade. The day before yesterday, I self-harmed by cutting my arm with my art knife. Today, my scar was accidentally seen by my mom. At that time, I made up excuses to brush it off, but I'm afraid of being caught again in the future. Where are some places where self-harm is less likely to be noticed by others?"

answers.answer_text: Dear questioner, hello! Sending you a big hug. I'm not sure what you're going through that's causing you so much stress and leading you to self-harm. But I think what you need is not figuring out ways to avoid your family finding out, but rather taking care of yourself. 1. Think about the recent negative emotions and try to identify the specific reasons or events behind them. Consider discussing your emotional issues with your family or teacher to see if they have any solutions or suggestions for you. 2. Protect yourself. No matter what difficulties you encounter, you shouldn't direct your emotions towards self-harm. Put away any tools that could be used to harm yourself, and avoid adding any further stimulation to yourself. 3. Use healthy methods to regulate your emotions, such as talking to friends, doing things you enjoy, going for a walk, exercising, or picking up your interests and hobbies again. I hope you can adjust your state as soon as possible. Looking forward to seeing the sunny side of you. Take care! The world and I love you.

question: Is it necessary to persist in a relationship when both parties have failed their college entrance examination and are unwilling to let go?
description: I am a girl, and both of us failed in the college entrance examination. We have had a sexual relationship and I am reluctant to let go, but he is avoiding me. Is it necessary for me to continue entangling in this relationship?
keywords: Love, dependency, attachment, arguments, sexual behavior.

answers.answer_text: Hello girl, although it is just a few words, I can see the conflicting emotions you are facing right now. Along with the disappointment in the college entrance exam, your relationship is also facing a crisis. Sending you a big hug, hoping to provide you with some warmth and support! I want to ask you, what made you start dating in the first place? What attracted and valued each other the most? And what led to the current situation? When you ask, "Is it necessary to entangle anymore?", why did you use the word "entangle"? Can we replace it with "continue"? And is the decision to continue based solely on "not willing to let go after being physically intimate"? Have you carefully considered these questions? Don't rush, give yourself some time to sort things out before making a decision. Take care of yourself.

question: I have never experienced it before, so why did I suddenly lose control after drinking recently?
description: I have always had a high alcohol tolerance and have never lost control after drinking. The day before yesterday, my girlfriend invited friends over to our house, and midway through, she called one of her ex-husband's friends. I had some objections in my mind but didn't say anything. They kept discussing her ex-husband, so I told my girlfriend to stop mentioning him. She completely ignored my words, and in that moment, I don't know why, but I suddenly said, "Stop mentioning him, for f**k's sake" (it could also be because her daughter was there, and I found this topic distasteful. I really adore her daughter - she's naughty and cute). That friend of her ex-husband then snapped at me, and I don't remember anything after that. The next day, they said that I physically attacked him, and even my girlfriend. Despite my deep love for my girlfriend, even though she is much older than me, I am willing to give up everything for her and have been striving for her. I never thought I would physically attack him, and this is the first time in my life that I have acted so out of control after drinking. I have been everywhere apologizing, but I have not been forgiven. I am overwhelmed with shame.

answers.answer_text: Hello, pre-marital violence? Or after drinking alcohol? A woman's second marriage is already a painful and harmful thing. When seeking love again, one must proceed with caution. Your violence has already shattered her defenses, especially since she has a young daughter and needs a rational and safe support system. From the perspective of a psychological counselor, if there is violence, the advice for women is to support them in getting divorced. This is in line with laws, ethics, protection of the vulnerable, and saying no to violence and male privilege. Because if there is violence once, there will definitely be a second and a third time. Only by quitting drinking and cultivating one's own inner self can the need for irreparable harm be avoided. If reconciliation is possible, her first marriage would not have fallen apart. Please restrain yourself and seek new relationships. Best wishes.

question: How to improve the relationship when there is no common language and communication with my husband?
description: My husband is always out and rarely comes home. Today he's hanging out with this friend, tomorrow he's going to drink with that friend, and it's a common occurrence for him to come home at one or two in the morning. We have had many unpleasant arguments about this, and I've even mentioned divorce, but he continues to do as he pleases. I'm anxious about his health on one hand, and on the other hand, I'm angry because we can't communicate and have nothing to say to each other. This has been going on for three or four years, and I don't know how much longer I can endure it. I don't know how to break this stalemate.

answers.answer_text: The OP and her husband have no common language and he is unwilling to communicate with her. They have had many unpleasant incidents because he doesn't come home at night and goes out with friends. I want to improve their relationship, and I think the first step is for them to understand each other. It is obvious that although the OP and her husband live under the same roof and have been married for many years, they do not understand each other. A simple question, why does the OP's husband go out with friends and drink every night? Is it to relax or is he avoiding coming home? If he felt relaxed and loved at home, why would he not want to come home? The OP should also show more concern for his work and life. Replace quarrels with gentle words and accusations with being cute, truly try to understand each other from each other's perspective and understand what the other person needs.

question: Feeling extremely shy at work and fed up with everything in the world? Want to break free?
description: Social anxiety disorder, I am extremely shy at work, always feeling like others are staring at me. It's even worse during social gatherings, my heart beats fast, I don't know where to look or where to put my hands, everything I say feels awkward. I hope my colleagues don't notice me, and I become even more shy around male colleagues, quickly blushing and feeling embarrassed. It seems like others think I have ulterior motives, but I don't! And I feel like my colleagues don't like me. The physical symptoms of this illness make me tired and miserable. If I were to donate my organs after death, can I avoid going to hell? I've had enough of everything in this world, whether it's people or things, I just feel unhappy and want to find relief.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! *Social anxiety, shyness, always feeling like others are watching you, heart pounding during social gatherings, feeling awkward about where to look or place your hands, feeling embarrassed about what to say, and thinking that your colleagues don't like you. It's exhausting and painful, feeling unhappy and wanting to break free. The symptoms you mentioned are classic symptoms of social anxiety disorder. People with social anxiety disorder often have a pounding heart and feel uncomfortable in crowded places. This is not caused by your personality itself, but rather unresolved psychological issues. Once you overcome social anxiety, you can return to normal social interactions. If possible, I suggest you communicate with your supervisor about your situation and try to reduce some social gatherings. If it's necessary for your job to handle these situations, you can consider finding a less stressful job where you don't have to interact with so many people. In your free time, you can focus on therapy for social anxiety disorder. Social anxiety is a psychological problem that can be alleviated or cured through psychological counseling, so please don't do anything desperate. You need to recognize the problem and then find a solution. As the saying goes, illness comes like a mountain and leaves like a thread. Once your social anxiety is relieved, you may not feel so uncomfortable anymore! Keep going! Best wishes!

question: My parents rarely care about me. My academic performance is not good, and I want to leave this world.
description: Dad and mom rarely care about me. When they do, it's usually when I've made a mistake. They often send me to cram school at night. I know they are busy with work, but they hang out with friends of the opposite sex and my academic performance is not good. I just want to give up.
keywords: Treatment, pathological personality, psychological counseling, sharing and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, you mentioned three issues: parenting, friendships with the opposite sex, and academic performance. Let's discuss each of them separately. First, the issue of parenting. It seems that many parents only pay attention to their children when they make mistakes. However, this does not mean that they do not love you. As you mentioned, they are busy with work. Moreover, many parents, although they love their children, may not necessarily know how to express their love. They have their limitations. If they did not receive much love or attention when they were younger, they may not know how to give their children more care. I can understand your grievances and dissatisfaction with your parents' neglect, but if you cannot change them, you can try to adjust your own attitude and try to understand your parents. You can also make an effort to communicate with them, express your feelings and expectations. If you don't speak up, your parents may not necessarily know. They might think that by paying attention to you when you make mistakes, they have fulfilled their parental responsibilities. Secondly, the issue of friendships with the opposite sex. Friends are not the only ones in life. Since they are just friends, you must accept this fact. They are your friends, but they can also have their own circle of friends. Are you concerned that your opposite-sex friend is getting close to others because you have feelings for them that go beyond friendship? Do you want to take the relationship further? If you have other thoughts, perhaps you can make an effort to pursue it. Lastly, the issue of academic performance. Academic performance is not innate or unchangeable. If you care about it, maybe you can work harder. Your parents send you to tutoring classes, which can be a valuable resource. Maybe you can take advantage of this resource and put in more effort. However, academic performance is not the most important thing in life, and it should not be the reason to give up on your own life. Sending you hugs, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: I think I have good qualities, so why am I still single while everyone around me is in a relationship?
description: Girls, who think that their conditions are not bad and have always been praised as beautiful and elegant since they were young. They have good relationships with others and perform well in their studies. However, it seems that their luck in love has always been poor. Several roommates who I feel have average conditions either have had boyfriends for a long time or have been confessed to multiple times. Why am I always single? I can't understand it. Am I really that bad?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Your own conditions are pretty good, you are beautiful and have a good temperament, overall you are doing great. However, your romantic luck has been poor. Even roommates who are average-looking already have boyfriends, but you have been single all along without anyone pursuing you. This makes you feel very confused and a little inferior. Generally, we would think that attractive girls must have a constant stream of admirers around them. But that's not the case. In most situations, those girls who are average-looking or have above-average conditions tend to have more pursuers. This is because before boys pursue someone, they also consider how compatible the girl is with them. If the girl's conditions are too good, they will definitely hesitate. If the girl's conditions are similar to their own, boys will feel more confident in pursuing her. Besides, those love-at-first-sight situations are very rare. If you want to meet the boy you like, staying in the dormitory every day is definitely not enough. You should go out more, participate in activities, and have the chance to interact with more boys and showcase yourself to others. This is the way to win love. So, OP, there's no need to be self-pitying and feel sad about this. If you want to be in a relationship, you can try to be more outgoing, go out more often, make some friends, and more people will get to know you. Best wishes~.

Personality also matters. If a woman is slightly outgoing, men will tend to like her more. Maybe you want a boyfriend, but the men you meet are not very outstanding or you don't find them attractive. When someone pursues you and you show no response, they will stop pursuing, or if you are more aloof and someone approaches you to talk or start a conversation, you always act aloof, and they feel that there is no hope and stop pursuing.

question: Should I go to the breakup dinner proposed by the man because our personalities don't match?
description: We got engaged and lived together for a year and a half. During that time, we constantly quarreled and broke up and got back together. Now we have finally decided to break up. I am going back to my hometown and my boyfriend has suggested meeting one last time for a meal before I leave. Actually, I am very sad and reluctant to do so. I really want to see him, but I know I will cry and lose even the last bit of dignity. Should I go?

answers.answer_text: Hello! First of all, I'm really sorry to hear about your experience. It sounds like you have been engaged to your ex-boyfriend for quite a long time, but have been constantly arguing and breaking up. This time, your ex-boyfriend suggested having a farewell dinner and you are torn about whether to go or not. First of all, if you know that going would make you cry, feel sad, or be reluctant to let go, then I suggest you not go. Because if you give in to your softer emotions, you may end up getting back together, but the problems will still exist and you might break up again shortly afterwards. This relationship will continue to torment you endlessly. So, my suggestion this time is that you don't go, and I also suggest that you don't get back together. Why? Because from what I understand, you mentioned that you have been living together for a year and a half, which is not a short time, but the constant arguments indicate that you two are truly incompatible. I believe you have tried many times to change, but without success. The disappointments have taken a toll on your mental and emotional well-being. Personally, I think the chances of the two of you reconciling are really low. If you couldn't resolve the issue of incompatible personalities even when you were talking about marriage, it means that this problem is truly irreconcilable. However, you are very rational, as you have chosen to separate instead of forcing yourselves to get married. Because if you do, it will be a lifetime of frustration. Since you have already taken the brave step of breaking up, don't look back anymore. Most of us will encounter more than one person we like in our lifetime, but not everyone we meet can go the distance. So cherish the beautiful memories from the past and confidently move forward. Don't give yourself the chance to turn back anymore. The better things that belong to you are ahead, so just keep moving forward. Best wishes!

If possible, it is beneficial for you to have a formal farewell when you break up so that you can move on from the sadness. The original poster said that we were engaged and lived together for a year and a half, during which we constantly argued and broke up and got back together. Now we have finally decided to break up, and I will return to my hometown. My boyfriend suggested meeting one more time for a meal before I leave. Actually, I am very sad and reluctant, I really want to see him, but I know I will cry, and I will lose even the last bit of dignity. Should I go? Natural and pure sadness is a form of healing. If you want to cry when you see him, just cry! Don't suppress yourself, life is too bitter, and we are easily confronted with some tragedies. If we have no guidance, the first emotion we will naturally experience is sadness. This natural emotional process is actually the most natural way of healing. When we cry for the tragedies in our lives, it is the most natural process of embracing the truth of our own lives. Of course, besides this, we should also try to think about the problem with a positive cognitive pattern, like this: he also has the right to choose his loved one, and I should not blame him; after breaking up with him, I will have the opportunity to find a better person. This kind of cognitive shift will bring you a completely new feeling, you will gain a long-lost sense of freedom, feel that the world is spacious and bright, and be able to shift your focus to work and interests, starting a new life.

Hello, questioner. Through your short text, I can still feel your sadness, pain, sorrow, and the urgent desire to see your ex-fiancé. Because of what you have experienced, I have also experienced it vividly 10 years ago. I really want to give you a hug. You said that there were constant arguments during cohabitation, and finally, after breaking up multiple times, you have decided to separate. Finally, I think this must have been a very difficult decision for you. Perhaps, countless times in your heart, you wanted to break up and countless times you overturned that thought. Finally, you made the decision to break up, and I think you must have gathered a tremendous courage to start a new life. Your ex-boyfriend suggested having a meal together before you leave, and I think he also feels reluctant to let you go. Perhaps both of you understand in your hearts that you are not suitable for each other, but for those people whom we have loved (maybe you still love him at this moment), having a meal together before leaving may be considered as a perfect ending for this relationship. Because once some people turn around, they may never meet again in this lifetime. However, the memories that this person brought to you will not be wiped away from your life with his departure. Since the moment you met him, he has already become a part of your life. Now that you have decided to separate, this meal may be a blessing to each other. Although your separation has caused mutual harm, at least in the end, you both bless each other. You said you were afraid that you would cry and it wouldn't be dignified. In my opinion, shedding tears while bidding farewell to each other also proves that you have truly and deeply loved each other. Don't be afraid of tears, as they not only serve as evidence of your past love, but they will also bring new life to you. I wish you happiness.

Hello there~ I understand your feelings very well, sending you a hug~ It's unfortunate that it ended up like this, with the guy suggesting a farewell dinner, leaving you unsure whether to go or not. In my opinion, either choice is fine. If it were me facing this decision —1. If the breakup is already certain and it feels like there's no possibility of continuing, I would lean towards not going. Because going would be awkward, sad, and tearful, but it's already destined to separate, so why put myself through this? If he doesn't want to accompany you anymore, believe that there are people willing to be with you and believe that you deserve to be loved.
