You still need to love yourself on the path to the future, and right now, it seems better to let go a little. 2. If you feel that there may still be a chance and that having the farewell dinner might lead to reconciling, I suggest you go and give it another try. "Leaving was heartbreaking, and I thought I would collapse, but at the most painful moment, I felt the clearest." If you want to reconcile, you must address those issues, which may be related to communication or personalities. But these are all things that can be resolved, requiring effort from both individuals. Reconciliation should not involve compromising yourself. Whether you decide to go or not, it's your own choice, and it's okay. Good luck~.

question: The mayor of the United States is crying in pain and being criticized. Why do I feel empathy for him alone?
description: I don't understand why the mayor of America is criticized for crying for Floyd, they say he is a politician putting on a show, and they even say he wants to be president and go to Washington. I feel like he is smiling and laughing with tears in his eyes. Why doesn't anyone think he genuinely loves the people when he is so young and handsome? They're all mocking him. I feel sorry for him. Am I too sympathetic and not rational enough? He doesn't even know me, how can I stop being so presumptuous?

answers.answer_text: First of all, I give you a thumbs up, you really deserve it. Remember, this is empathy, not sympathy. Even sympathy is not a bad thing, he does not lack confidence. In fact, sometimes people who look good also have a good-hearted and kind personality. Keep being kind, fill the world with love, the world is loving you.

question: In a relationship for 4 years, I want to have a physical relationship with my girlfriend, but she has always been unwilling.
description: I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for four years. I want to have sexual intercourse, but she doesn't want to. Two years ago, I brought up the idea, and I have been patient for over two years now. I feel like I can't bear it anymore and I want to ask for advice from you guys. Is there any way to change my girlfriend's mind? I really love her. She says she loves me too, but she can't do it.

answers.answer_text: I understand your pain, and it's clear that you two are deeply in love. Men and women have different physiological structures, so it's important to understand and communicate with each other. While sexual intercourse may not be possible, you can still engage in activities like kissing, holding hands, and hugging. Additionally, you can communicate your inner thoughts and feelings, engage in shared interests and hobbies, and develop a strong emotional bond. In my personal opinion, there are many forms of love and intimacy that don't necessarily involve being intimate in bed. (Of course, if it were possible, that would be ideal, haha!) As a woman, I can understand your girlfriend's perspective. Some girls prefer to wait until marriage to engage in sexual activities. Personally, during my student years, I also didn't want to engage in sexual behavior. Women tend to have a more noticeable sexual desire after the age of 25, as their sexual organs are internal and more shielded, unlike men. So, it's important to understand and respect these differences. On a deeper level, societal expectations and norms can make women hesitant about having sex. For instance, if an unexpected pregnancy were to happen, the physical burden and potential health risks usually fall on the woman. Additionally, society tends to judge and criticize girls for not being virtuous enough, although this is not my personal view and everyone is entitled to their own opinions. Moreover, abortion can have psychological effects. Even if precautions are taken, there are still risks involved. This cautious approach towards sex among girls is also due to the fact that after the hymen, which serves to protect the vagina, is stretched (it already has a natural opening), it becomes easier for bacteria and other microorganisms to enter the woman's body (for example, when using the restroom or if underwear isn't properly cleaned). As a result, women are more prone to various gynecological issues, which can be quite challenging and worrying. Changing the mindset around sex is not an easy task, but you can try to communicate and understand the differences in physiological structures between men and women, as well as the importance of sex in a relationship. However, if your girlfriend is still not willing to discuss this topic, it's best to respect her boundaries, especially considering her student status. Maybe... if a boy were to get a vasectomy, it might alleviate some of the concerns for the girl (as there are many cases of unintended pregnancies and abortions nowadays)? Oh, but that's just a hypothesis. At the same time, I wish both of you a future filled with happiness, and I hope that one day women can truly enjoy sexual pleasure and freedom just like men! Amen.

Hello! Have you discussed each other's values ​​on sex during such a long period of being together? What are your views and feelings about sex? And within the four years, the other party has consistently refused to have sexual relations with you. What is their explanation? The other party's values ​​on sex are that it should only happen within marriage. Or maybe they are not ready to have sex with you yet, as they feel that your relationship has not progressed to that stage? Or is it possible that they do not actually enjoy having sex, but they still want to have a marital or partnership relationship?

It has been four years since I started dating my girlfriend. Besides thinking about having a sexual relationship, should we also consider getting married? For women, marriage is like a safe shell for sexual relationships, not just love. It is difficult to change this mindset, unless society progresses further and truly connects sex with love, instead of marriage. In order for sexual attitudes to progress without traditional cultural support, young men and women need to break through through their experiences, and there needs to be individuals who propose corresponding ideas and slogans to defend and support them from a deeper cultural level, such as freedom, happiness, and rights. However, currently, strict regulations make everyone fear for their own safety, and we haven't reached a point where people willingly take that step forward.

question: "I am a 20-year-old female college sophomore, and recently I have been constantly feeling down. Could it be depression?"
description: Recently, but actually thinking about it carefully, it has been a long time, even back in junior and senior high school, it would often happen. I always thought it was because of my parents always talking about me and finding faults. In junior and senior high school, I had planned suicide and running away from home several times. I even wrote two suicide letters, but it didn't happen in the end. After starting college, I tried to avoid contacting my family as much as possible, so I rarely went home. My condition improved a lot. Recently (around three to five months), due to the pandemic, I was forced to attend online classes at home, which inevitably led to me feeling like before. It's fine during the day if nothing happens, but if I'm criticized, my mood will become low. I don't want to sleep at night and want to stay up. Sometimes I feel really uncomfortable. Nowadays, during the day, besides attending classes, I usually watch anime or play games to entertain myself. I procrastinate on my assignments and don't want to do anything. At night, I stay up and don't sleep. I feel like I've been watching anime and playing games all the time because it allows me to not think about anything and stay foolish. I stay up late at night because I feel like that's the only time I have to myself when I'm alone in bed. However, now I always feel low and uncomfortable at night and want to die. Because of this, I've also self-learned a lot about psychology, but I still don't know if what I have can be considered depression. Sigh, I want to seek counseling but don't have the money, and I want to tell someone but I'm afraid to say it, especially to my parents (I can't write anymore, let it be like this).
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text:
The original message is: 
"Lately, the OP's mood has not been good. Hugs to you! Actually, you have been trying to regulate yourself! Going to college means getting away from the things that bother you at home, but the circumstances of the epidemic have made you upset again. Actually, your parents care about you, and maybe they just find fault as a way to vent their work-related problems. But they definitely love you. It seems like you have been relatively idle at home, maybe you haven't been helping your parents with household chores, so you receive a lot of complaints. And you have been constantly binge-watching and entertaining yourself, which shows a lack of self-discipline. When you realize that you don't like this situation, your mood becomes low. Don't think that feeling down means you have depression. This kind of thinking is incorrect. When you are dissatisfied with the current situation, you are eager to find a breakthrough to prove that you are not like this, and then depression becomes your excuse. What are your interests and hobbies? You can subconsciously develop yourself during this abundant time. It's the best opportunity for self-improvement! During the epidemic, I studied programming and writing and also worked out, which earned me some earnings and gave me abs. When I felt lost and wanted to change but didn't take action, my mood also became low. But after putting in effort, this kind of mood became positive and optimistic! I hope the OP can overcome this slump soon. I hope this can help you."

question: Worried about whether to quit and switch jobs due to concerns about my ability, I am truly torn.
description: I am a designer, and my professional skills are average, which has led to being fired from my previous jobs after just one month. I do study in my spare time, but my progress is slow. I currently have a difficult relationship with my boss at my current job. My boss likes to micromanage and communication at work is challenging. My boss isn't very pleasant and gets impatient when asked questions, sometimes it's because they didn't explain things clearly themselves. As a result, I am feeling very unhappy every day. Seeing my boss's tense expression makes me even more unhappy. Therefore, I am thinking of quitting and finding another job, but I'm afraid that my skills won't be good enough and I will be fired again. I have a lot of credit card debt that needs to be repaid, and without a job, I won't be able to do so. So, I'm really torn between what to do.
keywords: Occupation, career management, career selection skills, work pressure.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Currently, you feel uncomfortable dealing with your boss in your new job, and communication is not smooth, making you unhappy every day. You want to change jobs now, but you also worry about repaying your credit card and being fired again due to your design skills. You are currently in a state of self-contradiction due to practical reasons, but you dare not change jobs rashly, and you are in a conflicting and uncomfortable state. Warm hugs to you. ※Adjust your mood and strive to improve your design skills. Currently, it is better to focus on your work before finding a suitable job. You can try to adjust your mood and state first. In the workplace, we inevitably have interactions and exchanges with colleagues and superiors. The boss hires us hoping that we can solve work problems and bring benefits to the company. As mentioned, "If you ask too many questions, the boss may get annoyed. Sometimes it's because the boss did not explain clearly." In the situation you mentioned, are these questions about design or other issues? If it is design-related, the boss may think you have design skills and do not want to say too much. After all, the boss is not our teacher. If we ask questions about design techniques, the boss will indeed become impatient. Therefore, I also suggest that you work hard to improve your design skills, such as studying online through relevant resources. Considering your current financial situation, you can find free learning resources online. I think Bilibili is the website with better quality and all the resources there are free. You can select and do self-learning there. ※Is frequent job hopping really due to lack of ability? It seems that your previous jobs did not last long, and you attribute this to your average design skills, even if progress is slow after learning. Perhaps you need more reflection. When you were fired after only about a month of work, were there other problems besides your design skills? Based on your description of your current job, there is also room for improvement in your interactions with colleagues and superiors. Adjust your attitude towards work and become the person who solves problems in the workplace, rather than someone who needs a lot of support and assistance from others to complete your job. Regarding slow learning progress, you may also need to consider whether your learning methods are incorrect and if there are areas for improvement. Adult learning is different from student days and requires flexible application. Try to understand and comprehend more, summarize what steps and optimized processes are needed for a certain job, and improve efficiency. ※Manage your finances and spend rationally. You mentioned that you owe a lot on your credit card, and I wonder if it is caused by borrowing to repay debts? Robbing Peter to pay Paul may temporarily alleviate the pressure of repayment, but I suggest you immediately stop borrowing to repay debts so that the deterioration of debt can be stopped in a timely manner, and then focus on clearing your credit card balance through income and expense management. If you feel stressed, I also suggest that you be honest with your family and friends and seek their help. Practice rational spending and keep track of your expenses. The road ahead is still long for young people, but if you continue to sink deeper into the quagmire of bad credit card usage and face constant harassment from debt collectors, you will become more overwhelmed. I'm not blaming you because I've been there too, and I have felt the pain. Stop borrowing to repay debts and find ways to earn more money.

Hello OP, from your description, it can be seen that you are in a dilemma. I hope my answer will be helpful to you. Firstly, let's analyze the current problems. You think your work performance is average - you are already studying, but progress is slow. You don't get along well with your current job and boss - you're not happy at work and want to change jobs, but you're afraid of being fired. You have credit card debts and can't afford to be unemployed. 

To solve the key problem, we need to be tougher on ourselves and make a determination to improve our skills. Everyone knows that companies don't keep idle people. If you don't make significant contributions to your work, you may face the risk of being fired. Even if you quit now and encounter other problems that make you unhappy in your next job, will you quit again? Therefore, we need to solve the fundamental problem, which is to improve our skills. It's impossible to improve in just ten days or half a month if you're studying design. So persistence is needed, and you need to be tough on yourself. Whether you study online or offline, you must learn, otherwise you may continue to face similar problems, which is only treating the symptoms but not the root cause.

Try to communicate in a different way and learn from colleagues who have good performance. In reality, some bosses are easy to get along with, but most bosses are not. This requires some skills and methods of interpersonal communication. If you can't learn it yourself, you can observe how people around you interact with their bosses. It requires more patience and observation to improve emotional intelligence, which will make you more at ease. The current situation is making you unhappy, and coupled with the tough job market, quitting may not necessarily lead to a better job. You are currently facing difficulties, so try to solve them first. If you really want to leave, find another job first and tell your current employer after you have passed the interview. Otherwise, you may face the dilemma of having no job, which will affect your life. Deal with your emotional problems and try to communicate with people around you. Sometimes you can seek help from your friends, preferably those who are around your age or slightly older. This way, communication will be better without generation gap, and they can help you with suggestions. It's normal to encounter difficulties in any job; it's all about having the right mindset and emotions. Quitting will bring many problems, and not quitting will also have uncertainties. But only by facing them can you progress and become better. When you truly have more choices, you won't have to go through these things anymore. If it were me, my personal advice would be to stay and actively solve these problems. Especially, don't complain and resent, as this will only magnify your dissatisfaction with the company. Sometimes, if you change your perspective, you will find that things are not as bad as you think. For example, if you were the boss, what kind of people would you want? Or think about how your boss treats you on a daily basis, is there really no benefit at all? Or have you overlooked the good and only magnified the bad? I hope you can handle this matter well and become more and more outstanding. I believe you can do it! Keep going!

Hello there~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug~ It seems that you are currently in a rather awkward and conflicting situation. Your work is not going well, and you want to quit but also need to pay off your credit card debt. Sometimes, when we are in a bad state (like facing work difficulties), yet we don't choose to leave immediately (by quitting), it is because we are avoiding what we believe to be an even worse situation (not being able to pay off the credit card). So, to some extent, staying in this bad state is also a way to protect ourselves. Your inner self needs to weigh the pros and cons of these two difficulties and choose the better one. Should you continue to struggle with your current job or quit directly and face the dilemma of paying off the credit card? Sometimes, we can only choose one or compromise. Of course, you can also step out of this choice and see more possibilities. If you can make significant progress in your professional skills and communication with your leaders, or if you can find a job that suits you better, the problem will be solved. However, this requires trying and exploring, and of course, there are risks involved. You can consider every possibility, choose the lesser of two evils, and make a decision. Best wishes~.

If the post owner still has debts, it is better not to quit abruptly before finding a new job. If you can't find a job for a while, how will you repay these credit cards? Even if you are currently employed, it won't affect your ability to interview for other jobs. During interviews, be cautious and consider whether your skills match the job requirements. You can interview with several companies, there's no rush. If you really can't continue, then look for more basic positions that don't require high qualifications or a lot of work experience, but positions that you can handle. You can temporarily take a step down to gain some experience. Additionally, can you find some part-time design work online? This can increase your income and help you get out of the credit card debt predicament quickly. When working for someone, the boss will certainly have many requirements for you. Put yourself in their shoes - if you were the boss of a company, spending a lot of money to support employees, you would surely want their work to create value. Maybe you can change your mindset. The boss currently has many requirements for you, but once you persevere, you may overcome many challenges you never thought possible. Treat your 8-hour workday as selling your time to the boss, after all, not many people can be extremely happy at work. Make your off-work time happier by exercising, reading, going out, or chatting with friends. These activities can bring joy and make it less difficult to endure. Apart from the difficulties with the boss, does this job give you a sense of achievement? Do you feel that your worth is being realized? If so, then hang in there until you have paid off your credit card debt or have accumulated enough capital. If you don't feel a strong connection to your profession, have you considered changing direction? Do you have other goals in mind? Even if you want to change jobs, you should wait until you have enough experience and know your own worth, so that you can have a goal-oriented job change and improve with each change. If you only want to change jobs because you don't like the current boss, then the next job may have different problems. Working for someone else can never be perfect. If you always think of changing jobs when faced with problems, you will never accumulate experience, and HR will consider you an unstable employee with insufficient loyalty. Of course, it also depends on the post owner themselves, whether they can persevere or if they are already so miserable that they don't want to stay even a minute longer. At the same time, it's important to understand that every decision comes with consequences, such as quitting a job means no source of income, but it might provide some relief. In addition to finding a job that you are satisfied with, you should also learn to budget and spend within your means to avoid falling into a debt crisis.

The main post is not happy with their job and wants to quit and change jobs. However, when they look at the reality of the situation, they have credit card debt to pay off and are worried about being fired again due to their lack of skills. From the description, it can be seen that the main attraction of this job is not the job itself, but the salary that allows them to pay off their credit card debt. If we exclude this additional value, what attracts you to the job itself? "I have an average level of expertise in my field, which is why I was fired from my previous jobs after only a month." Having an average level of expertise means being at an average level, and most employers hire people based on this level. However, you were fired from several jobs before reaching one month. This is a contradiction. Having had several jobs indicates that you meet the standards of employers, so why do you find yourself unsuitable after being hired? This is what needs to be explored. Perhaps what you consider to be your business capabilities is not what the employers find unsuitable. "I want to quit and find another job, but I'm afraid I won't meet the requirements and will be fired." I don't know if you have noticed, but when you wrote this sentence, you had a thought in your mind, "I might be fired soon, I just don't know when." Before something happens, you can prepare yourself, for example, by taking the initiative to resign, which might make it easier for you. But is this your idea or the company's? If there are colleagues in the company who are more supportive, try talking to them and see how they view you. Do they think your level of expertise is so bad that you need to be fired? If not, what reasons make you have this idea? I hope this answer can be helpful to you! Karen.

We all want to solve problems by avoiding them, but in the end, we find that the problems still exist. When it comes to workplace issues, we can discuss them from two aspects: objective environment and subjective abilities. 1. In the post-pandemic era, the employment environment is extremely bad, and it is not easy to have a job. If possible, try to improve your abilities during this time to plan for a broader future. The best time to plant a tree is ten years ago, followed by now. It is recommended not to quit easily, but to find your own strengths, magnify them, and improve your competitiveness in the workplace. Look at your previous jobs, all of which were fired, which is quite serious. The boss is unwilling to tolerate you anymore. In this job, the boss is willing to "oversee everything", which is actually a good sign. Parents often say, "If you weren't my own child, who would care about you so much?" If the boss is willing to care, it means there is still hope. It means that the other party is also waiting for you to improve. If you leave this job because of emotions, maybe the next job won't have such a good opportunity. 2. Self-ability. You know that you need to learn, but progress is slow. You can also communicate with your boss about your state: "I have the willingness and attitude to do things well, but my abilities are improving slowly. Please give me time and space." Having a boss who shares your values at work is actually not easy. As an "authority" figure, the boss represents the difficulties we face every day. When we were young, we can treat these as workplace trials, as pressure brings motivation. Moreover, you still owe a lot of credit card debt. Work is your only way to solve the problem now. Getting through it is the turning point, and it also improves your abilities. Isn't that great? I suggest you read more workplace books, such as Stephen Covey's "The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People" and Peter Drucker's "The Effective Executive", to understand the workplace and try to understand the state of bosses. In addition, improving your professionalism is paramount. Sometimes it doesn't necessarily mean learning more, but looking at good works, imitating, and then surpassing them. Or maybe you have discovered that your strengths lie in other areas, so you don't have to struggle with design. In the workplace, recognizing your own strengths and then leveraging them while avoiding weaknesses is the best method. I also recommend that you take the Gallup StrengthsFinder test to truly understand your strengths. Only then can you develop yourself in the workplace and truly achieve a better life through your own efforts! Keep it up, I believe in you!

Changing jobs is a normal thing, and there is no need to have negative emotions. All of this stems from the lack of confidence after being fired. If you have been fired twice, analyze the reasons why others have a bad impression of you. Identify and improve them promptly. Become better step by step through these experiences. Then, figure out which field you are best at and start from there to regain your confidence. If you have credit card debt, temporarily find a stable job that allows you to make repayments. Prioritize jobs that you like and are good at, even if they are temporary. Then, carefully consider what suits you and do it in the long run. The world is bright, and everything is lovely.

If you are indeed in urgent need of money at the moment, then just do it first. After paying off the debt, relieve some of the burden on yourself, and then make other plans. If possible, take on some freelance work as a way to improve your skills. In my opinion, being a designer requires great patience and a calm mind, a good ability to withstand pressure. It might be a little more difficult to find a job right now, but if you are feeling down, go ahead and vent your frustrations a bit. Once you get past the emotional point, you'll feel better.

Improve work skills + open-source and save money. For various difficulties and dissatisfaction encountered in work, I think we should find ways to solve them from the root: we need to improve our work skills to be taken seriously by our bosses. Strive to enhance our scarcity and become the most valuable person in the company, which should be the direction of our efforts in the coming years. In other words, we need to find ways to make ourselves valuable. Regarding the quality of life and desires, they should match our income level. The key to solving financial problems such as credit cards is to increase income and reduce expenditure. Best regards!

question: Psychogenic vascular headache, headaches occur when feeling anxious, what should I do?
description: From the second year of high school, I developed a habit of having headaches. At that time, I was misdiagnosed with depression, but I actually have vascular headaches. It was the first time I had heard of it, and I felt like I had a vascular disease like an elderly person. In high school, because of the headaches, I almost gave up on college entrance exams. After graduation, it got better, but now in my third year of college, the headaches have started again. They make me feel dizzy and unable to focus on reading. I constantly feel tired and even after waking up, the pain lingers making me feel like I haven't fully woken up. I estimate that it's caused by stress, as lately the stress has been quite overwhelming. I'm quite worried about relapsing because I'm currently preparing for postgraduate exams, and the headaches will also affect me. I don't know what to do. Medication can provide some relief, but I understand that only when the stress disappears will I be normal again, although that seems unlikely.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give you a virtual hug. From your description, it is understood that you are experiencing headaches and excessive sleep due to the stress of taking exams. You are aware that this is all caused by stress, but you do not know how to relieve it. [A little analysis and advice] 1. The relationship between stress and effectiveness is generally a U-shaped curve. Both excessive and insufficient stress are not conducive to completing tasks. For you, reducing stress is the most important thing. Taking exams is not something you can only do once in your lifetime. If it is unlikely for you to not retake the exam, try looking at it from a different perspective and boosting your confidence. Tell yourself every day, "Even if I perform poorly on the exam, I can take it again. It's okay even if I am nervous or haven't rested well, I can still perform to the best of my ability." Will this make you feel better? 2. It is important to let go of studying and take breaks when you are feeling uncomfortable, experiencing headaches, or unstable emotions. Forcing yourself to study during these times will not be productive. Instead, engage in activities that help you relax, such as exercise, reading books, or watching a movie with friends. Take a break from studying, and when you go back to it, make sure not to burden yourself with too much work. Hopefully, this will be helpful to you.

question: Students living on campus who experience anxiety and fear towards sounds, how can they resolve this issue?
description: I have always had a fear of sudden noises, such as slamming doors, children screaming, toilet flushing, etc. When I encounter noises that mask environmental sounds, I unconsciously scream, experience irregular heartbeats, and sweat. Since moving out of my home and living in a dormitory, I can hear every move my neighbor makes, such as opening and closing doors, making phone calls, moving chairs, etc. All these noises prevent me from concentrating on studying or paying attention. I am always worried that another noise will occur in the next second. Even when I wear headphones, I can still hear them. I have to wait until around one o'clock every day for everyone to rest before I can fall asleep. I think this may be a psychological disorder and I really hope to find a suitable solution. Thank you.

answers.answer_text: Hello, don't be nervous. How long have you been in this state? Is there a stimulus source? Normal fear and anxiety have positive significance, as they can prompt us to mobilize our own powers to cope with external changes and adapt to the environment. Excessive fear affects learning and daily life and needs to be regulated. Seek support and help from others, or seek the assistance of a professional therapist or counselor. Medication can also be used for a period of time with the help of a psychotherapist. Now that you have self-awareness of your inner conflict state, irregular heart rate may be a somatic response to psychological problems. You can seek medical attention to rule out organic conditions. Your sensitivity and fear of sounds are also common phenomena, which are related to the lack of secure attachment in your infancy and early childhood, as well as the weak sense of security. This has been prolonged and now causes intense reactions to the surrounding environment, triggering excessive nervousness in the nervous system and discomfort. Engage in regular exercise, reading, mindfulness meditation, shift your focus, do things you enjoy, and avoid excessively absolute demands on yourself and others. Do not blame yourself excessively and allow for mistakes and imperfections. Exercise your willpower and reassure yourself that as long as you do not harm yourself or others, there is nothing to fear. Consciously put yourself in a state of fear, fully experiencing and accepting your true feelings, and gradually self-suggesting to relax your emotions. Focus on your breathing or imagine yourself as a powerful superhero or an invincible lion.

Hi there! The reason behind this situation must be related to your upbringing and life experiences. Your description only reveals the outcome without providing more helpful information for others to pinpoint the real cause. I have two suggestions for you to consider: 1. Seek help from the school's counselor (it's free, and the effectiveness may vary from person to person). 2. Seek assistance from a mental health consultant (both offline and online options are available. As it is a paid service, theoretically, it would be more professional). Take care!

question: At 19 years old, this girl feels anxious because she feels like she has wasted her time studying.
description: I used to be proactive and always wanted to study hard. I chose a major that required a lot of reading, and I really liked my major. However, I also wanted to improve my skills, which made it difficult for me to focus on both my major and skill development. Now I still try to do what needs to be done in my major every day, but I feel like it's too late. I'm already in my senior year, and I still feel like I haven't achieved anything, just being mediocre. This feeling of anxiety has been accompanied by a month-long depressive mood. I feel anxious and tortured no matter what I do now. I need a way out, but I don't feel like doing anything. I don't know if I have explained myself clearly, I hope someone experienced can answer my dilemma.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, I understand that 1. You love your major and also love learning, but recently you have been feeling anxious. 2. Your major requires a lot of time, and it's difficult for you to balance it with honing your skills. 3. You want to do something, but you're not sure what. [A little analysis and suggestions] 1. If you persist in doing the same thing for a long time, even if it is something you initially liked and enjoyed, if you don't make appropriate adjustments along the way, you will eventually feel tired and exhausted. This is very normal. So, you can try changing the pace, set aside some time to rest, adjust your mindset by confiding in friends about your recent troubles, or go to places close to nature to relax and change your mood. 2. By being able to consistently do your own job well until your junior year, in fact, you are already stronger than 80% of college students. Maintaining your learning spirit and doing your own thing well after entering college is already a remarkable achievement. These persistence also bring benefits to you. For the honing of your skills, perhaps you can adjust your time, think more critically about which activities can be done in less time or can be eliminated altogether. I hope this helps you.

question: Recently, it seems that the mental health of a 16-year-old girl has been getting worse.
description: I don't know, how to say... a 16-year-old girl, recently, it seems like her mental state is getting worse?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, it seems like something has been bothering you and you're having trouble sorting out your thoughts. I'm not sure what you've been through, but I can sense that you've accumulated some negative emotions that haven't been released in a timely manner. Have you tried finding a healthy way to express these negative emotions? Take a moment to think if there have been any useful methods in the past that you can continue using. Also, try to think about what activities truly help you relax. Could it be singing, painting, doing crafts, or traveling? You can brainstorm and write down all the ideas that come to mind, then choose a few to try out. Have you attempted to confide in your family or trusted friends about your frustrations? When faced with difficulties, it's necessary to seek support and help from those around you. Of course, being able to reach out here for help is also commendable. These are my suggestions, and I hope they can assist you. Take care!

question: There is tension in the dormitory, why has life fallen into a vicious cycle?
description: I have been feeling very nervous in the dormitory, unable to speak and feeling anxious to talk. I am afraid and constantly unable to blend in with the dormitory. Can you please advise on how to change this?

answers.answer_text: Let's try to think about it from the current position of standing. It's very tense in the dorm, and we can't even say a word, so our interpersonal relationships are a mess. What do we expect? We expect to be able to go out with the people in the dorm. It would be nice to have one or two close friends. What can we do to make friends? We can communicate with others, talk about common interests, and get to know each other. You see, we have many ways to meet new people. You might think that even though you say this, I'm still nervous, so what should I do? So you can think about two questions. First, what am I nervous about? Am I afraid of being rejected by the other person or afraid that my stumbling speech will make them dislike me, and so on. What am I worried about behind the nervousness? Second, will these reasons behind the nervousness hinder me from communicating normally with others? If so, can I overcome them, even if it's just starting with a simple greeting like "good morning" or "good afternoon"? Do we need to take more action, because only through action will we know what we can achieve. Don't get caught in the vicious cycle you mentioned because in this cycle, we can't see a clear result.

question: Why do my parents always insist on making me apologize? It's clearly her who is getting angry but she blames me.
description: Here is the original text my mother sent me. I want to consult with you about what is going on in her mind. Why does she use this as a threat when she clearly knows that my child needs to be picked up and dropped off? This has happened before, constantly neglecting the child. I have a job and cannot quit to take care of the child. I have truly realized this and I am prepared to move out and hire a nanny after. (In just one year, we have had three arguments. It feels like helping to take care of the child has turned us into villains. If we still want to live together in the future, then put away your ways and handle your own family matters. Don't bother us. We have said it long ago: if we are willing to help, we will help, but if we are unwilling, it's our prerogative. Our obligation is simply to raise XX to adulthood. If you don't want to live together, then move out on October 1. We also want some peace and quiet. Remember, helping is not something we owe you. Don't be ungrateful.)
keywords: Family, family trauma, parental communication, family control.

answers.answer_text: Because the OP's parents believe that their obligation and responsibility lie only with the OP's generation, they think they are helping to lighten the OP's burden, but it does not mean that they must comply with everything the OP says. Just like the OP's mother said, they indeed have no obligation to help us take care of our children, it's just that it's a common practice in our country and many elderly people around us do help with child-rearing. So subconsciously we assume that parents should help raise their grandchildren. However, in the process of raising children, due to differences in beliefs and various aspects, it is inevitable that various problems will arise. If both parties have strong personalities, many problems are indeed difficult to solve immediately. Therefore, we can think back to the contradiction points every time we argue with our parents. If we really can't live with our parents and our financial conditions allow, we can indeed seek help from professionals because sometimes problems that can be solved with money are not too big of a deal, so we need to weigh it ourselves. Because parents feel that they are here to help, we need to learn to be grateful instead of pushing all problems onto them or finding excuses for ourselves, so we don't need to take it too seriously. Sometimes, when beliefs do not align, many problems can arise, so we can focus on managing our own small family and handle larger issues on a case-by-case basis. The world and I love you.

Hello! The problem you raised is very common now. It is indeed very difficult for young people to work and take care of their children. It is normal for parents to seek help from them, which has also caused many family conflicts. I have a friend whose situation is similar to yours. Both of their parents come to help take care of their children, but their lifestyle habits and dietary habits are different. Over time, many differences have arisen, but they are not easy to speak out. Both feel aggrieved. The young people think it is natural for grandparents to help take care of their children, while the elderly think they have worked hard all their lives and finally retired to enjoy life, but now they have to help the young people take care of their children and do household chores every day. They already feel uncomfortable, and when they encounter things they can't figure out, they feel even more upset. At this time, it is necessary for both sides to have open and honest communication. If they are your parents, you should mainly communicate with them. If they are the other person's parents, let the other person mainly communicate with them. Speak out about your difficulties, emphasize their role, and appropriately exaggerate the positive and negative impacts that not getting their help will bring to your future lives. No matter what kind of parents they are, they all have a heart that hopes their children will live well. As children, you also need to understand your parents' intentions, adjust your mindset, and avoid bias. As long as you have time, do household chores together and take care of the children together. When there are differences, communicate and resolve them in a timely manner. Once the family harmony is achieved, everything will be fine.

It seems like your mother is not refusing to take care of your children, but rather you are demanding too much from them during the child-rearing process. Your small family may face difficulties and rely on the assistance of the elderly, but young people should not burden the elderly with all responsibilities. It's important to establish appropriate boundaries. Young people should be grateful for the help from the elderly instead of considering it as something that is owed to them. Without knowing the specific details, this is the reasoning I can provide.

question: The damage caused by my ex-boyfriend has resulted in my inability to trust my current boyfriend. What should I do?
description: I was in a relationship with my ex for almost four years. A few months before we broke up, I found out that he was being ambiguous with another girl. That girl didn't know he had a girlfriend. After I caused a scene, she left, possibly due to family reasons. I couldn't trust my ex anymore, and even when that girl secretly visited my social media, I would get furious. I started doubting and distancing myself from him. We would almost break up every two days, and eventually we did break up. At first, I felt relieved. Then I met my current partner who treats me with great care. However, I always have this feeling that after some time, he will become like my ex. I start doubting him every day. I don't believe what he says. We both struggle every single day. It's exhausting. Later on, my own personality started becoming extreme. I would get angry and say hurtful things whenever I found something upsetting. I closed my social media and stopped replying to his messages. After everything happened, I felt regretful. I'm so miserable. I'm wondering if there's something wrong with my mental health.
keywords: Love, sense of security, love management

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Not all wounds can heal easily, but if you encounter someone who can help you heal, you should cherish and treat them seriously. From your description, I can sense that you have developed a sense of distrust towards your current partner due to betrayal by your ex. Your inner doubts and contradictions constantly create conflicts, making your current relationship extremely painful and agonizing. Being aware that this is a problem is the beginning of change. Perhaps you have not taken your state after being betrayed seriously enough. Did you question your self-worth at that time? Did you think there was something wrong with you or have feelings of inferiority? How much of your sadness and grief is due to betrayal, and how much is due to self-doubt and insecurity in intimate relationships? Take the time to carefully sort out your thoughts and approach the problem rationally. Is there any factual basis for your suspicions? Before saying hurtful words, have you tried to calm down? Besides extreme approaches, have you tried to communicate and approach the issue gently? Did you only find peace of mind when your current partner left you, believing that your suspicions were indeed correct, engaging in self-fulfilling prophecy? Try facing and resolving issues in a positive way instead of resorting to extreme and painful methods. Learn to trust yourself and trust your partner. In fact, when you have doubts, you can have an open conversation with your current partner about your feelings and what behaviors of theirs make you feel uneasy. Is your extreme behavior aimed at seeking more care and reassurance, rather than them leaving? Does your partner know when you regret your own words and actions? In an intimate relationship, both people need to be willing to understand each other's worlds, reveal their own wounds to each other, and let the other person know where it hurts, so they won't touch it and will know how to help and protect you. Silence and arguments will only make the relationship worse, causing harm to both individuals, instead of being a game of winning or proving certain suspicions. Express your emotions sincerely, and honestly admit your shortcomings and weaknesses, accompanying each other in overcoming difficulties and finding the most suitable way to be together. Best wishes.

You are currently experiencing extremes in your life, so it would be better to take it seriously. It's best to talk to a counselor to untie the knot in your heart. Although you have conversations and friendships with your current partner, you have never let go of your ex in your consciousness. Your ex still influences you internally, so it is quite difficult to maintain a good relationship among the three of you. Only when you deal with your inner self and let go of your ex, can you possibly live a peaceful life with your current partner.

Appearance: The ex-boyfriend had ambiguous relationships with other girls, causing a lack of trust and a breakup. The current boyfriend is attentive but still unable to let go, leading to emotional instability, hurting others and experiencing pain. The truth: 1) It is possible that the person has not yet recovered from the painful experience mentioned in the first paragraph, or the trauma has not been healed. 2) They have a lack of security, self-confidence, and emotional instability, causing them to worry about gains and losses in their relationships. In need of reflection: In a four-year relationship, if it did not get better and you discovered your partner's ambiguity, have you ever reflected on what went wrong in the relationship? Ending it by getting angry and suspicious. At the very least, it shows that you are immature in handling relationships, and you may not realize the role and responsibilities you played in the previous relationship, including the breakup. I usually do not recommend entering into a new relationship without any reflection or growth after leaving a previous one. It is not only unfair to your current partner but may also be a repetition of harm to yourself. In fact, you are now seeing the consequences of that. Currently, I suggest you find a counselor and make some efforts in personal growth. When you truly grow psychologically, when you are willing to take responsibility for your own happiness or unhappiness and feel confident, your troubles will naturally diminish. Of course, a relationship requires the effort of two people. Any one-sided effort will not last long. We all need to adapt to each other in various interactions. No one is a perfect match. Mutual respect, support, and progress together are the best state. When you feel nourished in a relationship and your own state is improving, and interactions become more natural and comfortable, it indicates that you are making the right efforts, and the possibility of finding the right person is also greatly increased.

question: Sophomore student, feel homesick every day, is this normal? How to relieve it?
description: Sophomore student, still have a strong desire to go home every day and feel somewhat depressed, lacking enthusiasm for studying and life. Is this normal? How can I relieve it?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Poster, hello~~~ Give the questioner a warm hug. It is normal for anyone, regardless of age or identity, to miss home. However, we also need to balance our feelings of homesickness with our studies at school. The questioner might consider whether they are naturally more attached to home or if the intensity of homesickness has increased due to certain things at school or academic pressure. We can start by identifying the reasons behind these feelings in order to better address the issue. On the other hand, there is no need to burden ourselves with pressure regarding homesickness. We can try to increase the time we spend communicating with our parents or family members, expressing our inner emotions and feelings to them. Additionally, we can also try to find activities at school that can divert our attention and serve as a substitute for feelings of homesickness.

question: Parents have objections to the boyfriend, how can the relationship be improved?
description: I have been dating my boyfriend for almost three years. I am in Jiangsu, and he is in Inner Mongolia. My parents don't want me to marry someone from a faraway place, and they also require the guy to buy a house. But the guy talked to my parents about getting married sooner, and my dad said no marriage without buying a house. The guy said it's not easy to buy a house in Xuzhou, and my dad misunderstood, thinking he wouldn't buy a house. The guy actually agreed to buy a house in Xuzhou, but in installments, not to stay there. Last year, I opened a store and got into a lot of debt due to the pandemic. I didn't dare to tell anyone about it. My parents think I spent the money on the guy, and even after I explained, they still don't believe me. Because of this money issue, my dad asked us to break up. I haven't told the guy how much debt I owe, but he has helped me repay the money. He just graduated from college. I want to ask how to handle this? How to improve the relationship?
keywords: Marriage, pre-marriage, and concepts of marriage.

answers.answer_text: Your parents are just looking out for you, but you have to be honest about your boyfriend helping you with things. It's already the modern age, and a simple observation can tell a lot, right? Make your parents change their perspective on your boyfriend, can you? Your boyfriend really has nothing to say about them. Even if he doesn't have money, he should still make installment payments, right? You can't let him down either. You need to consider the lifestyle of being a slave to a mortgage when you're together. Can you both work together to improve your lives? This should also be a concern for your parents. Once you've considered this, it's up to you to resolve the misunderstandings between your boyfriend and your parents. It's such a simple matter, right?

You are all mommy's babies, your own lives are bound by your parents' beliefs. Really, it's very difficult to live like this. Love itself is beautiful, two people with pure hearts, establishing a family, starting their own lives, how wonderful. But now, it has become a burden demanded by parents. I think it's better to make your own decisions, and if it doesn't work, just go out and explore. As long as the two of you are together, everything will be fine, really. I've tried it myself, 23 years have passed, and I'm doing well. Three children, life may be tough at times, but there is a lot of happiness.

question: What else can I do to survive when nothing goes right?
description: Family is unhappy, work is not going well, love life is not going well, basically nothing is going well.
keywords: Emotions, depressive mood, panic and helplessness, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello! When I read your words, my heart aches and tears well up in my eyes. I understand that the various frustrations you are experiencing may be overwhelming and that the final straw has led to these thoughts, right? In fact, I believe that it is quite normal for people to have thoughts of not wanting to live, and most people have had such thoughts at some point. Ultimately, they either find their own way to cope, receive help from others, or have something that holds them back. I like that I can help you, but I like it even more when you can help yourself. Although the world is not perfect, we can heal ourselves! I understand that you may have these thoughts, but I won't allow you to act on them. I hope you can take care of yourself. Here are a few ways to relieve your feelings: 1) Have a good cry. You can find a quiet place or do it in a crowd; don't worry about what others think, just let yourself cry freely. It will help you relax and maybe bring you some comfort. 2) Go on a trip and see beautiful scenery, enjoy good food. It's another way to relieve stress. When you go out and see things, you will realize how big the world is and how small we are. Many things we once enjoyed might help fill the void in your heart. 3) Go for a run. When you're feeling particularly bad, run as hard as you can until you're exhausted. This will help release those feelings. 4) Find someone to talk to, or you can seek help from a mental health counselor to help manage your emotions. I came across an article with this conclusion, and I want to share it with you: Everyone experiences emotions, and when we realize we are experiencing negative emotions, we need to face them and then manage them well. We need to find a healthy outlet to release these bad emotions instead of suppressing them. When faced with negative triggers, we should learn to redirect them. Take care, my friend. Venting out negative emotions allows us to work, study, and live happily, and interact with others normally. Don't spread bad emotions to others. Keep going; we're all the same, but that's okay. You have a lot of people supporting you, so live well and you will encounter opportunities along the way.

question: Had a dream, scared to go back to sleep, very bizarre?
description: Yesterday afternoon, I had a day off and took a nap. I had a dream within a dream, which was quite eerie. In my dream, I woke up to find a woman next to me, whispering in my ear not to get up because there was someone on my bed. Naturally, I didn't consider that person as a human being, but rather as something unclean. Then, I played a couple of games with my classmates, and by around eleven o'clock, I went to sleep again. I had another dream where I saw myself coming back from outside and taking the elevator. In the dream, the elevator in my residential area had changed. The lowest level was now negative six floors. There were two women waiting for the elevator with me, one of them was older, like an auntie. On the wall opposite to the elevator, where the fire hydrant was, she talked to us, saying that the elevator had changed and that it was difficult to take. She said that the negative floors were for parking and that she had been waiting for a long time since the afternoon. At that time, I had a sense of time and realized that she had been waiting for about three hours. The girl next to me didn't say anything during this process, but I responded with "uh-huh" or something like that when the auntie spoke. I felt like I had to respond. Then the elevator arrived, and in the corner of the elevator, there was a dark, strong-looking man with a stern face. After the girl and I entered the elevator, the auntie suddenly started frantically searching through her bag outside the elevator. It felt like she was procrastinating or buying time for something. The decision was in my hands. I could press the elevator button to go up.

answers.answer_text: I'm afraid to sleep. I know there are no ghosts or spirits in the world. I woke up around three o'clock, and I don't feel that there is anything unclean about the darkness. I know that the change between day and night is caused by the Earth's rotation. I need to use the bathroom, but when I flush the toilet, the sound of the flushing water sounds like a person's wailing and screaming. I'm so scared. I'm so scared that someone wants to kill me. I searched online to find out what this dream is about, but all the answers are about being chased or killed. But I suspect that someone wants to kill me, and I woke up before anything happened. Now, I'm afraid to even turn off the lights.

Later events, I do not know if they were real or dreams. I told myself not to be afraid and went up to the top floor of the rooftop to find someone, even though I knew I couldn't find anyone. At that time, I had already reached my own floor, outside my own apartment. But I thought that I had to pass the top floor, just in case that woman was chasing that girl. If I passed by, I would die too. Then, I thought that I should have regained my senses. I believed that I could float silently like they described in fantasy novels, and disappear. Hmm, I'm sure I was awake at that time. It was already so fantastical. Later, I regained my clarity. I kicked away my blanket, and I imagined being chased by a man on my way home after school. I thought of carrying a fruit knife with me. If he dared to attack me, I would stab him over a dozen times and then run back home, tell my parents, and call the police.

Close the elevator and go upstairs directly with that girl, or help the auntie press the door-opening button to let her in. The girl lives on the top floor, and I naturally live on my own floor, a few floors lower than her. I don't know why even though I clearly know that the auntie is very strange, my brain seems to not be under my control. I frantically press the elevator button to let any auntie come in. After seeing my behavior, the man in the elevator, who has been like an elevator attendant, leans his arms on both sides of the elevator door and looks at the auntie. The auntie enters the elevator under his particularly fierce gaze. Note: This man has always been in a similar position to that of an elevator attendant. Then the auntie gets in, and when I ask which floor she wants, she says the minus one floor. After I press the button, she asks who the good person is. My subconscious mind immediately thinks that she wants to kill someone. The elevator starts going up, and I have a subconscous feeling that she wants to kill the girl on the top floor. I am very scared, and when we reach my floor, I have made up my mind. When I get off the elevator, I won't walk to my own door, I will pretend to take out my keys and open the door on the opposite side of my home. And then the dream ends. I have not yet reached my own floor.

question: Discovering that your mother has an ambiguous relationship with someone else can be mentally distressing. How can you relieve this pressure?
description: I found that my mom has an ambiguous relationship with someone. I had been suspicious before, but I confirmed it in the past few days. I can't talk to anyone about it, and I can't let her know that I know. We don't communicate much in the first place. I really can't accept it, and I feel very oppressed and uncomfortable. How can I find some relief?
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication

answers.answer_text: Short reply: I found out that my mom has an ambiguous relationship with someone, I had suspicions before, but it was confirmed these few days. (What does it mean to you that your mom is having an ambiguous relationship with someone? Do you have a moral evaluation of your mother? Does it hurt your father, hurt your adoptive father? Do you despise your mother? Or... write it down. See what emotions and cognitions are influencing you.) I can't confide in anyone, I can't let her know that I know, we don't communicate frequently anyway. (If she knew that you knew, what would happen? Has the situation of not communicating always been there, or is it a certain degree of agreement reached between your mother and you? Take some time to think about these questions, as they are key to the current relationship we have) I really can't accept it, I feel very suppressed and uncomfortable. How do I resolve this? (Find a platform, express yourself anonymously. Allowing yourself to express will release the suppression. Of course, it is also important to quietly think and reply to the questions I gave earlier.) Best wishes.

Hello, the questioner. You didn't mention your own family situation in your question, only saying that you discovered your mother's ambiguous relationship with someone else and didn't know your age and gender. As for the current state of your parents' relationship and some personal advice, I hope it can help you. Since you confirmed that your mother had an ambiguous relationship, you can find a suitable time to ask her about your doubts. If it's not what you think, it can quickly solve your confusion. Many things can only be resolved by clearly speaking out your concerns.

I'm sorry, I don't understand the situation of the questioner's family. However, I would like to share some personal opinions and hope to offer some help. First of all, there is no doubt that parents love us, and our love for them is unconditional. No matter what situation we are in, our mother loves us. She gave us life, and we are a part of her. Just like other parents, she will always give us the right to be loved. Secondly, everyone has the right to make choices for their own lives and pay the corresponding price for it. So, parents have the right to choose the life they want, and this has nothing to do with the love they give us. In the future, you also have to make choices for your own life, and regardless of the outcome, you have to bear the consequences of your own choices. You are connected to your mother, but you are also independent. The connection comes from the love and unique relationship between you, and the independence comes from the fact that both you and your mother have to face your own lives independently, and no one can replace that. You might as well take the first step and talk to your mother about your thoughts, express your inner feelings, and try to communicate. Also, let your mother open her heart and talk about her own thoughts.

My relationship with my mother is very good, but later I discovered the same thing as you and confirmed it too. What can I do? For the past six months, I have been struggling and feeling miserable, even wanting to distance myself. Later, I indirectly made it clear that I knew everything, those dirty things hidden in my heart. Now, we have a lukewarm mother-daughter relationship, occasionally getting close. I can only say that I can't change anything. Adults' affairs, children are always bystanders and victims.

question: 30 years old, mother of two, physically and mentally exhausted, feeling quite depressed, how to adjust?
description: Both children were accidents, and my mental state during pregnancy was not good. It greatly affected my career development and caused irreversible damage to my body. I now suffer from chronic tinnitus. I understand that I should take responsibility for my choices, but when it is quiet at night and I can't fall asleep, I often entertain thoughts of suicide. How can I adjust myself?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotion regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP: It sounds like you are currently very anxious. question: Can a failed relationship really change one's sexual orientation?
description: After breaking up with my ex-boyfriend, I was very miserable for a while because he blamed me for the breakup and denied my feelings and efforts towards him. He even said how heartless I was and how good he had been to me. This made me lose hope in relationships, and I no longer saw dating as something beautiful. I became very reluctant to pursue love and even unwilling to start a new relationship. Recently, I realized that I have developed feelings for a girl. I am scared to face this, and I can't believe in these emotions. We have only had a few interactions and don't know each other well. I am extremely afraid of this budding feeling and unsure if it is love or not. I've also been constantly thinking about how I suddenly changed my sexual orientation. I have been suppressing these feelings and I'm afraid to let others know.
keywords: Love, sexual orientation, attachment and dependence

answers.answer_text: Hi, OP. Breaking up with your boyfriend and being subjected to unwarranted blame and denial can indeed be disappointing and infuriating. This disappointment and anger may affect your confidence in rebuilding relationships, and it may even lead to feelings of insecurity towards men. Have you ever experienced this kind of insecurity with other men in the past? How is your relationship with your father? If you have also experienced similar disappointment and anger in the past, it is possible that it could trigger stronger aversion towards the opposite sex. If this insecurity extends beyond close relationships to include more individuals of the opposite sex, you might find yourself being attracted to individuals of the same sex, as they may have certain qualities that make you feel warm and safe. If you find yourself developing feelings for a girl, it would be helpful to observe what exactly you like about her. If it's just a fondness, there is no need to worry excessively. In fact, psychological research suggests that each of us, even heterosexual individuals, can experience attraction and desire towards individuals of the same sex. However, whether or not to take further action is a decision that requires rational judgment on your part. The trauma from your previous relationship that you mentioned may require more attention and processing in order to restore your trust in the opposite sex and intimate relationships.

Because for a period of time, you may feel that there is a law of attraction where people with similar characteristics tend to gather. Perhaps certain girls' personalities have attracted you, so you are drawn to their unique personal traits, creating a positive impression. This is neither right nor wrong, it simply means maintaining a principle of no regrets in whatever you do. Well, it's about choosing the lesser of two evils and prioritizing the greater of two benefits.

Hello OP, sending you warm hugs~ In some cases I have come across, there have been changes in sexual orientation due to past romantic failures. In the timeframe you described, you have experienced some hurt from your ex-boyfriend. During the breakup, he placed a lot of blame on you, which must have made you feel really upset. It's difficult to have loved someone so deeply and then receive hurt from them when you part ways. In recent times, you have realized that you seem to be developing feelings for another girl. However, this liking may stem from certain qualities she possesses. For example, her sense of responsibility or her kindness and patience, etc. It's possible that these attributes attract you, making you feel like you like this girl. Changing one's sexual orientation involves emotional attachment as well as impulsive changes. If you feel a sexual attraction to the same sex, it may indicate a greater inclination towards homosexuality. Wishing you the best~.

question: 22 years old, currently studying for exams, parents say I am being extreme, what should I do?
description: For example, right now I am preparing for exams, but whenever my mom brings up the topic of getting married and bringing a dowry, I feel very uncomfortable. I have mentioned to her that I don't want to get married and she shouldn't talk about this aspect. But she still brings it up. As for being radical, it means that I often express different views from them about things. My dad says I am just like he was when he was 20 and that it's not good. I want to express my own opinions. Am I sick?

answers.answer_text: Hello, first of all, I'd like to give you a small hug, hoping to bring you some warmth. One: Let's summarize your problems. First, you have different opinions from your parents, which makes you very uncomfortable. Second, your father doesn't agree with you and thinks you are still too young. Two: My analysis of this matter is that there is indeed a generation gap every three years. Although it's not necessarily about who is right, the generation gap does exist. In our mother's generation, they got married relatively early. Although 22 is still young, in their eyes, taking a few years after graduating from school, it becomes a bit risky for your lifelong decision. Parents hope that you can have a stable and happy family early, so even though you don't like this topic, your mother can't help but bring it up. As for your father, he may see his own reflection in you, but he failed back then, so he doesn't want you to repeat the same mistakes. Of course, I also support you. We are all independent individuals with the right to pursue what we want and live a life that truly belongs to us. Three: Here are my suggestions. Firstly, have a good conversation with your parents. Perhaps when you mentioned not wanting to get married, your parents felt a great sense of crisis. But is it because you haven't met the right person yet? You can talk to your parents about your true thoughts, or change the phrase "not wanting to get married" to "I want to continuously improve myself through my efforts and meet better people." I believe your parents will definitely support you. Secondly, analyze it rationally. Cao Cao once said, "Remember not to get angry, as anger diminishes wisdom." Have you ever thought that your strong desire to study and even the statement of not wanting to get married are a kind of anger and resistance towards your family? At least, I have experienced that when I argue with my partner, even though I know that what I'm doing may not be good, because it came from his mouth, I insist on doing it well. So I think you should carefully consider whether these thoughts are the most genuine calls from your heart or acts of rebellion under anger. Lastly, be slightly more firm in your attitude. If you are determined to study, then your attitude needs to be a little more firm. Your father told you that he was the same at 20, so you can also tell him: your experience was earned by yourself, and my experience should also be earned by myself. So, when I'm twenty, I want to make my own decisions, regardless of success or failure. Please do not disturb me, as I am no longer a child. Finally, I hope my suggestions can help you and wish you a happier life.

Don't worry, it's okay. (^▽^) Hug you, hug you who are not understood by your parents. You are a girl with opinions, you have your own thinking, which is great! You must be a smart and innovative girl who likes and is good at thinking! I understand your need to express your views. I am the same as you, always expressing different opinions to my parents. As for being extreme, it means that I will present different views from them. According to the dictionary, being extreme refers to thoughts, beliefs, speech, behavior, etc., being excessive, inappropriate, or beyond the scope of common understanding and acceptance, thus unable to be accepted and recognized by the public. Nowadays, marriage is a matter of personal choice. With the liberation of thoughts, non-marriage ideology is gradually accepted by the public. For example, the famous dancer Yang Liping. Dad said you are like him when he was 20 and that it's not good. You also think that this version of yourself is not good. On one hand, parents can't understand why you feel uncomfortable about the topic of marriage and your resistance to it. On the other hand, Dad may be worried that your tendency to present unconventional ideas will lead to setbacks in your future social life. Why would Dad think this way? In social psychology, Asch's conformity experiment explains the following: "Information Pressure: Through experience, people tend to believe that the majority is more likely to be correct. In ambiguous situations, due to the lack of reference framework, they have more faith in the majority and conform more. Normative Pressure: Individuals in a group often do not want to violate the group standards and be seen as deviants by other members. They are afraid of being different and becoming "outliers," experiencing isolation. Therefore, they adopt the opinions of the majority." (Baidu) Dad is worried that having opinions and perspectives different from the majority will lead to social isolation and a lack of support in your social life. Therefore, Mom and Dad communicate with you and evaluate you this way because they love you and are concerned about you. -------------------------------------------------- ---------------- Why do you feel uncomfortable when Mom brings up your marriage? Everyone has their own thoughts. Perhaps Mom's tone still carries a slight "authoritarian" demand while you, an adult with opened wings, want to fly freely. Are you afraid that Mom will interfere in your marriage? Are you afraid that Mom will still control you like when you were a child? Therefore, you refuse to bring up this topic that may lead to parental control? In terms of romance and marriage, you want your own privacy space and do not want parents to interfere. We, in our early twenties, may be the generation that enjoys expressing our self-awareness the most. In this information age, the generation gap between us and our parents is getting deeper. The thoughts of the previous generation still deeply influence their every word and action. For example, some people believe that Yang Liping's life is incomplete without having children. I also feel uncomfortable about this topic, and my mom also believes that women should get married and have children. (I will tell my mom when she brings up the topic of romance and marriage: "Mom, if you have any questions about this, you can ask me." I will let Mom know that I already know and don't need her reminders and suggestions.) Communicate well with your parents, use a more tactful tone, and quote authoritative sources to tell your parents that your ideas are also reasonable, or say that you currently don't have such thoughts and that academic achievement is the priority, and let's talk about it later. I wish you success in your postgraduate entrance examination, and keep up the good work! The world and I love you.

Hello, giving you a warm hug. It is normal to focus on academic matters and not think about marriage at the age of 22, especially since the topic of "marriage" is still far away for you. Moreover, as a 22-year-old, you must be under a lot of academic pressure. It is understandable that you may feel impatient and resistant when discussing topics that seem distant to you. You don't have to feel anxious or doubt your own well-being. Everyone grows up with a limited understanding at an appropriate age, and no one sees the world with the same perspective as their future self. Those days would be boring. It is normal for us to have different viewpoints from our parents due to our different ages and environments. You are not wrong in feeling this way. You are you, and you are 22 years old now, an adult who needs to think for yourself and have the ability to discern right from wrong. Dealing with relationships when opinions differ is a challenge that many people face. They complain about the inability to communicate with their family and the lack of shared values, which leads to poor family relationships. I have complained about this too. However, differing values are not the main cause of strained relationships; it is often due to communication. As long as individuals with differing values respect and understand each other's perspectives, without demanding or troubling the other from their own standpoint, I believe it will not affect their relationship even if their values do not align. On the contrary, some people argue and constantly debate due to different ideologies, insisting on determining a winner or loser based on their views on a particular matter. This is what really damages relationships. When facing disagreements with your parents, it might be helpful to guide them more and try to understand them, while also attempting to make your parents understand you! This will be good for everyone! Best wishes!

I am also 22 years old this year. When I was younger, I looked forward to growing up, but as I grew up, I realized that it was not what we wanted. Instead, I preferred when I was younger. After all, people are never satisfied and have a tendency to avoid. I hope my sharing can bring you some help~ First of all, do appropriate things at the appropriate age.
