"Live to old age, learn to old age." In fact, learning has no end, so we still need to learn because self-improvement is not achieved overnight. With the development and needs of society, our abilities should also be in line with it. Secondly, learn to communicate with parents. At the age of 22, it is normal for parents to bring up topics such as marriage and having children. After all, parents cannot always be with us. However, lifelong decisions need to be carefully considered. You can try to think from their perspective and have a good communication with your parents. The reason why conflicts arise between us and our parents is because we live in different times. They have experienced more and gone through worse things, so their way of expressing love may not be satisfactory. But their original intention is for our own good. Lastly, learn to plan your own life. Although plans cannot keep up with changes, we still need our own plans. It can give us a direction to strive for, and it can also prove to our parents that we have a reasonable arrangement and can handle these things well. This way, when our parents see our achievements, they will also feel relieved, and we will also feel delighted. Accompanying you with love and words, best wishes.

Hello, after understanding your situation, I want to start by giving you a warm hug~【Problem】1) There is a contradiction with your parents regarding marriage - your parents want you to get married early, but you have been focused on studying and don't want to consider this matter right now. 2) Your parents say you are being extreme - you have your own views and opinions about marriage, but in your parents' eyes, having a different perspective is considered extreme. 【My Analysis】1) You are only 22 years old, which is the age for pursuing your dreams. We are young people of the new era and naturally have our own thoughts about marriage and starting a family. So, you are definitely not being extreme, it's just that your parents don't understand the mindset of our young generation. What we lack is communication and understanding between us. 2) You are currently in the stage of preparing for exams, and it's inevitable to feel stressed and emotionally tense. On top of that, your parents' expectations regarding marriage add to the emotional instability. This is something that anyone would feel under such circumstances. So, try not to let your parents' words affect you too much and focus on studying for now, as that is the most important thing at the moment. 【My Suggestions】1) Communicate with your parents sincerely and make them understand your thoughts. There is an age gap between us and our parents, naturally resulting in differences in mindset. You can choose a suitable time to have a good talk with your parents about your thoughts, which are also the thoughts of many young people in today's society. What we need is to have the ability to be independent before seeking a life partner. Of course, you can also ask your trusted friends to help persuade your parents. 2) Focus on exam preparation and clear away your worries. Since you are currently in the exam preparation stage, it means that studying is the top priority. Don't let other trivial matters affect you. If you feel tired or upset, go outside for a walk, jog, or change your environment to change your mood and clear away your worries. 3) Seek a conducive learning environment to improve study efficiency. You can study in a quiet place like a library or a café to achieve a highly productive state of revision. 4) Believe in yourself and believe in the future. The destiny of your life is in your own hands. We shouldn't let other people's opinions dictate our decisions. Believe that you can achieve your career goals and believe that the person for your future is waiting for you not far away. However, right now, you still need to keep striving and pushing yourself. Best wishes~

Hello, understand the conflicting feelings you have after having conflicts with your parents. Core issue: doubting whether or not to express your opinions at home. Analysis: Firstly, as the OP, you are already 22 years old, which means you are an adult. Being an adult means being independent, so whenever you express your thoughts and ideas in front of your parents, you will face strong opposition, and even your father may attribute your actions to extremism. In fact, this is a common desire for control that most parents have to some extent. They want to protect you completely, fearing that you may take the wrong path. However, they fail to realize that everyone has their own thoughts and preferences. Advice: Since you are still preparing for exams and financially dependent on your parents for survival, the control they exert over you is their inherent desire for protection and control, and they fail to realize the discomfort it causes you. First, you can try to communicate with them and express how their excessive concerns make you feel uneasy. Generally, parents care about their children, so if you feel uncomfortable, it contradicts their original intention. Perhaps a calm and peaceful conversation can resolve your worries. However, some parents are more stubborn and do not care about their children's true feelings. That's okay too. When you become financially independent and can move out, it's good to maintain a certain physical distance from your parents and live according to your own wishes. By then, your parents will also gradually accept your independence and show respect.

Hello, I would like to respond to you on several aspects and see if it can give you some inspiration. 1. First, you need to understand that parents always hope for the happiness of their children's marriage. You're 22 years old, and it's normal for your mother to worry about your marriage. On the other hand, I think it's more of a problem if your parents don't ask about your marriage. 2. Have you talked to your parents about not wanting to get married? I think this is the focal point of the problem. When parents hear their child say they don't want to get married, they will naturally have more worries. As for why you don't want to get married, I didn't see a serious discussion between you and your parents about this issue. If it's because you're studying and don't have the energy to focus on marriage and family, then I believe if you explain it clearly to your parents, they won't force you to find a partner and start dating right away. However, if you truly have no intention of getting married, then it is a matter worth discussing in depth with your parents. 3. Because you often express different opinions from your parents on certain matters, they say you're radical. I think this may be due to a lack of deep communication between you and your parents, where the reasons and results of things have not been clearly expressed. I guess your mother is someone who cares a lot about her children and you might often feel frustrated because of her excessive fussing. Therefore, your communication with them may be more perfunctory. But you are concerned about them saying you're radical, especially your father's opinion of you. Therefore, in your daily life, it is important for you to learn patience and actively listen to your mother's nagging and patiently communicate and explain things to them. 4. When you hear your mom mention "dowry" and "getting married," it makes you very uncomfortable. I think this is also a worth exploring issue. If it's because you're tired of hearing your mom nagging, to the point where anything she says annoys you, then I think you need to seriously evaluate whether you should overcome this issue on your own or seek help from a qualified psychologist. If it's only when the topic of marriage comes up that you feel uncomfortable and annoyed, then you really need a qualified psychologist to help analyze what this discomfort means, when it started, and whether it has other impacts on you.

Hello, good evening! First of all, I send you a warm hug. I can sense that you have plans and goals for your life and you're currently in a state of studying and preparing. I'm not sure which exam you're going to take, but I can feel the pressure and expectations you have. It seems like you're having difficulties communicating with your parents and there are significant differences in your views on marriage. This is causing you distress and there's no outlet for you to relieve it. You're questioning if something is wrong with you. I'm curious about what happened that led you to have such thoughts. Through your text, I can also feel the love your parents have for you. Your father is using his life experiences to tell you that you remind him of his younger self. He wants to prevent you from making the same mistakes, which is something most parents do. We are both 22 years old this year and considered adults. We have our own independent thinking, ability to consider and solve problems. We can take our parents' opinions as suggestions and we don't have to rebel or blindly obey. We can consider the good and make judgments about the things that are not. Believe in yourself, you have the ability to handle this. It's essential to not label ourselves when we have unpleasant events with people in our relationships. We may think, "Am I sick? What's wrong with me?" If you feel that your emotions are problematic, you can seek medical help promptly or seek assistance from a professional psychologist to adjust your mindset. Every situation has a positive aspect. I wish you success in your exams! The world and I love you.

Everyone has the right to express their true feelings, so you are not wrong, oh, and you are not sick either, hug you. Before graduation, parents always say, don't fall in love, study seriously; after graduation, they urge us to fall in love and get married. Actually, I have talked to my parents about not wanting to get married during certain stages of my life, but my mom would say who will take care of you in the future, you will know when you get older. Then I would say, "I can live in a nursing home," and my mom would say, "There are many abusive nursing homes." But actually, they are just worried that if we don't get married, there won't be anyone to take care of us when we get old, or what will we do after they are gone? My mom often brings this up, and I know when you hear these things, you feel uncomfortable, and I do too, but if you stand in your mom's shoes, you will understand why she is so worried about you not getting married. It might be helpful to calmly discuss the topic of marriage with your mom and reveal your true feelings to her. You can also tell her about your future plans and goals, letting her know that you are capable of taking care of yourself and she doesn't need to worry unnecessarily. As for the exam preparation you mentioned, I understand that it comes with a lot of mental pressure, so in your daily life, you can listen to music, exercise a little, and try meditation to relax yourself and release your emotions in a healthy way instead of bottling them up inside. Parents often use "oppressive education" or "comparative education," which can be really hurtful to us as their children, but it might be challenging for them to change their mindset right away, so let's take it slowly. We don't have to agree with all their beliefs, and likewise, they don't have to agree with everything we think. This is a relationship of equality and freedom of dialogue. When we are in an unequal relationship with our parents, conflicts naturally arise. Handling this situation requires effort from both sides. As for being "extreme," it doesn't seem to be reflected in your description, but we can also learn to recognize our own "extreme" language from daily conversations with our parents, which we may not be aware of. If there isn't any, then we can think about why Dad thinks I'm "extreme" and whether it's just based on what he sees on the surface. We can have a thorough conversation with Dad and reflect on why he used the word "extreme." It might be unintentional, but it could also be a wake-up call. Hope I can help you. Good morning, good afternoon, good night.

question: 16-year-old girl, how can I sprint and improve my grades in 10 days?
description: Now there are 10 days left until the biology and geography final exams, with a maximum score of 60. I currently have around 40 points in these two subjects. If I sprint for the next 10 days, how can I reach 50-55 points? I am seeking methods. I am willing to stay up late and study extremely hard (although I'm not sure if it will be successful).
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that 1. It is not far from graduating in biogeography, hoping to improve grades. 2. To achieve this, one can squeeze their own energy and adjust their daily schedule. [A little advice] 1. First, it is not advisable to study until late at night and exhaust one's energy. In a tired state, the brain's ability to absorb knowledge weakens, and the efficiency of learning is lower than the original planned method. Especially staying up late and sleeping less is not beneficial for the brain's ability to recover and learn. 2. There is a fairly effective method - doing exercises and analyzing wrong answers. Approaching exams, finding wrong answers through doing exercises, and then analyzing these mistakes to supplement one's knowledge is a recommended and effective way to improve one's learning. Hope this helps OP.

question: How should I communicate with my 11-year-old daughter who put a pen in her pants?
description: I watch my daughter's selfie video. At the beginning, she was playing with the slime by herself. Then, after a while, she took a pen and put it in her pants. I don't know how to communicate with her about this.
keywords: Family, family relationships, growing up process, communication between parents and children.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I see that you mentioned your daughter's behavior, and it made me a little curious. However, what differs from you is that I am not curious about the child's behavior, but rather curious about why you raised this question. What are you worried about? And why can't you just ask your child directly why she did such a thing? From your trust, I can see that you are a very loving mother to your daughter, and you pay special attention to her every word and action. So when you see this behavior that you don't quite understand, it's understandable that you have some doubts. At times like this, the best way to find answers is to communicate directly with your child, using objective and descriptive statements to ask questions such as, "I just saw you... and I'm curious, why did you do that?" These are just my personal thoughts to share with you, for reference only.

question: People in crowded places often find it difficult to be themselves. How can they alleviate this situation?
description: Every time there is a crowded situation, like when the boss treats us to a meal, family gatherings, or class reunions, I feel confident and comfortable expressing myself when I'm at home alone, singing and dancing without hesitation. But when it comes to big occasions, I become self-conscious and nervous. How can I alleviate this situation? Is it because of the fear of judgement? How can I convince myself?
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, communication, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: I'm the same way, but when I was working before, my manager would also assign me some training tasks, such as giving lectures to dozens of people. 1- Prepare the script and revise it until I can read it smoothly or even memorize it. 2- Practice speaking in front of a mirror and observe my own performance, whether it's appropriate and confident. Practice repeatedly. 3- Treat the audience as a row of colorful balloons, as if I am giving a speech to the balloons. 4- Don't care about others' opinions, just perform. Whether it's good or bad, it's a form of personal growth. If you can do these basics, you won't be so nervous, and with more experiences, you will gradually improve.

question: I am overly concerned about others' opinions and often worry about making mistakes afterwards. Do you have any suggestions?
description: I have always been very concerned about negative evaluations from others. Sometimes, in order to prevent others from having a negative opinion of me, I intentionally do things. Afterwards, I am always afraid of having done something wrong. Does anyone have similar experiences and any good suggestions?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! After reading your description, I have a certain understanding of the question you want to ask, and I also give you a virtual hug in four-dimensional space. From your description, I can see that you care a lot about other people's opinions, especially those negative ones. Actually, being overly concerned about other people's negative opinions is, to some extent, a lack of self-confidence, and it may also stem from a fear of not being liked by others, or even perfectionism. Therefore, people like this may pay too much attention to negative comments and sometimes even go to great lengths to change those comments. You also mentioned in your description that sometimes you intentionally do things to prevent others from having negative opinions about you. I have experienced similar situations myself, where I deliberately do things that others ask of me in order to leave a good impression on them, and after doing those things, I even ponder about whether I did well and left a good impression on that person. So, I have summarized some methods to help you alleviate the current situation. (1) Try to accept the imperfect aspects of yourself, because there are no perfect people in this world, everyone has flaws. (2) Try to adjust your mindset and approach life and people with a positive attitude. (3) When we have made efforts but still fail to change others' opinions of us, don't dwell too much on it, learn to be yourself and walk your own path. Let others say what they want to say! Because we cannot control others' thoughts, so just be ourselves. (4) When you feel too much pressure, you can release that stress through exercise or listening to music. (5) Talk to the people close to you about the things you encounter, express your thoughts, and release your emotions in the process. (6) Try to shift your attention, redirecting it from others to things that interest you, and engage in meaningful activities. The world and I love you. Best wishes!

Hello, OP. I understand your dilemma. Many times, we care a lot about negative evaluations from others, sometimes to the point that ten positive evaluations are worth less than one negative evaluation. Because we fear negative evaluations from others, we intentionally do things and also fear making mistakes. So, what should we do in these situations? How do we face this issue? I will share my understanding with you, hoping to inspire you. Everyone desires recognition and attention, and this is completely normal. However, the key point is that we should have a strong understanding of ourselves and know who we are as individuals. We shouldn't let others' evaluations change our own evaluations of ourselves. We should have a clear and stable self-perception. This brings up the topic of self-identity. The formation of self-identity is an extremely important task in one's life. During the process of forming self-identity, we may encounter crises of self-identity. These crises may include feelings of defeat when others have negative evaluations of us, which leads to doubt and denial of ourselves, as well as rejecting the existing values we have. An individual gains self-identity when they can take responsibility for themselves, accommodate contradictions and imperfections, and exhibit more stability and positivity in their life and life approach. So, from this perspective, you will know that when your self-identity is stable enough, others' evaluations of you will not have such a strong impact on you. When we face failure, we can forgive ourselves because even the most outstanding individuals make mistakes. Moreover, we can view ourselves more positively and tell ourselves, "I forgive myself for not being able to do it for now." It's okay. Regarding intentionally doing things and then fearing that we did something wrong, we should tell ourselves that those are just "thoughts." Every time that voice appears in your mind, try using this six-word mantra: "Thoughts are just thoughts." They do not equal facts. No matter how convincing they may be, just ignore them. If you are interested and have the time, you can participate in a self-identity training camp to help you grow. After completing the training camp, I no longer care about the evaluations from others as much. The world and I love you! Best wishes to you!

Hello! Being too concerned about others' evaluations shows that on one hand, you have certain expectations for yourself and hope to receive approval from others; on the other hand, it indicates that you lack sufficient self-confidence and worry about negative evaluations from others. Everyone to some extent desires recognition from others and hopes for positive evaluations. Life is always about living for oneself. Intentionally doing things to make your life better reflects your attitude towards life. However, if you do things just to please others, you will always be afraid of making mistakes, which can create pressure for you to some extent. It is recommended to be more natural in life. The world is so big, and you are a unique individual. Recognize your strengths, pay attention to others' evaluations but don't overly concern yourself with them. Add some fun to your life, enrich yourself, and feel the inner fulfillment. Smile at yourself and others. When you have positive evaluations of yourself, others' evaluations, whether good or bad, will become less important.

Hello OP, giving you a big hug. I can totally understand how you feel. Firstly, it's worth celebrating that you have realized the problem and want to change it. I hope my analysis and suggestions can help you. From your description, I sense that you care a lot about how others perceive you. In essence, you probably have a psychological need to be respected and acknowledged. This in itself is completely normal, but if you become overly concerned about others' opinions and it burdens you mentally, it can lead to anxiety. Therefore, regarding others' opinions, I suggest that you strive to "embrace constructive criticism and ignore baseless gossip". First, **assess the nature of the criticism**. For those that are constructive, you can reflect on yourself and continuously improve. For those that are idle gossip, just listen and don't let those words waste your time or upset you. ---- It can be seen that you fear making mistakes afterwards, indicating a lack of self-confidence in the outcome of your actions. "Lack of self-confidence is in fact a lack of self-worth." I recommend that you engage in activities that can help you find a sense of worth, such as things you are interested in or good at. This will enhance your self-confidence. Everyone is unique and has their own shining points, you just haven't discovered them yet. It will take some time and observation for you to find your own strengths. "It's not that things aren't beautiful, it's just a lack of eyes to see the beauty." Wishing you well.

OP, hello, I hope my response can bring you some help. I used to be very concerned about other people's opinions and would often worry about whether I had done something wrong. However, I have changed now. So, I believe that after a period of adjustment, you will also be like me. In the Yue Lu Academy, there is a pair of couplets with the first three lines: judge right and wrong based on one's own conscience, listen to praise or criticism from others, and accept gains and losses as fate. This means that right and wrong should be measured using one's own conscience, we should have an inner scale to evaluate ourselves; it's better to listen to how others praise or criticize us; accept gains and losses in life as part of destiny's arrangement. In the book "A Change of Thought," it says there are only three things in the world: one's own business, other people's business, and heaven's business. People become troubled because they do not manage their own affairs well and worry about other people's and heaven's affairs. When we do what we want to do and have done our best, we may still face negative criticism. At this point, we need to adjust our mindset. We have already done our best to complete the task, we have done what we should do, but we cannot control how others evaluate us. Therefore, we should not be concerned about other people's opinions because we truly cannot control others' behavior and thoughts. So, we need to face all evaluations calmly. We cannot make everyone like us, even great people may not be liked by everyone. Therefore, we should do our best and let things take their own course. Regarding mistakes, we need to have the right perception. It is impossible to go through life without making mistakes; making mistakes is normal because we grow gradually while resolving mistakes. No one is born without making any mistakes, everyone grows through mistakes. If we make mistakes, we shouldn't be afraid, we should actively find ways to resolve them. Additionally, the most important thing is to have sufficient self-awareness. We need to know what we want, we can evaluate ourselves accurately, and we can accept our strengths and weaknesses objectively. This way, we won't negate ourselves because of a few comments from others. Best wishes.

Hug the original poster! This is a common problem. In this society, it is inevitable for people to come into contact with others. From infancy, we observe changes in the external environment and pay particular attention to our direct caregivers, which shows that we are naturally concerned about the evaluations of those around us. Proper consideration of others' evaluations can contribute to our healthy growth, help us establish self-esteem, and improve our shortcomings. Overly valuing others' evaluations can potentially bring us trouble. When we find ourselves feeling anxious or tense because of worrying about evaluations, we can try to think, "I am who I am, no one is perfect, nobody is flawless, and I accept my imperfections." Just some humble thoughts, hope it helps you!

Hello, questioner! After reading your question, I want to give you a comforting hug. Perhaps your current state is due to being overly sensitive, lacking a sense of security, and having low self-confidence. In light of this, I have a few suggestions that I hope can help you! Adjust your mindset and build self-confidence: Recognize your own worth and encourage yourself more. Believe in your own value, acknowledge your strengths and weaknesses, and only by honestly accepting both can you improve yourself. Lacking self-confidence leads to excessive self-doubt and caring too much about others' opinions and fear of negative evaluations. This will hinder your self-improvement and plunge you into negative emotions or even self-doubt. (Give yourself positive affirmations to effectively build self-confidence). Face your weaknesses honestly: Don't avoid others' evaluations of you out of fear. View others' evaluations of you with a positive attitude and the ability to discern. Constructive feedback from others helps you to promptly identify your weaknesses and make improvements, which is beneficial to continuously improve yourself and become a better version of yourself. Find a good position and avoid falling into the spotlight effect: The spotlight effect refers to the tendency of people to see themselves as the center of attention and overestimate the degree to which others pay attention to them. In reality, no one will constantly focus on you; people generally care about themselves. Find your own position, work diligently, and accumulate substantial progress. Handle all unpleasant things with an objective, realistic attitude in order to accept them better. You tend to focus too much on others' evaluations of you, which consumes a lot of your attention and thinking and even makes you feel displeased and doubtful of yourself. Consequently, you have no time to deal with more important matters and thoughts. Please focus more on yourself. Believe in yourself, affirm yourself. Embrace courage, push forward, and become a better version of yourself. Your personal mental health advisor is by your side. May my words bring warmth to you! Also, thank you to occasional readers passing by. Please feel free to follow me and mark it as "helpful"!

Hello. Did your parents criticize you a bit during your upbringing? Were they stingy with praising your language? Our self-evaluation initially comes from the evaluations of important people around us during our growth process. So, can you reflect on the interactions you had with your parents in some past scenes? You can remember a mantra: walk your own path and let others say what they want. In fact, no one can gain approval from everyone, nor can anyone go through life without making any mistakes. Do you agree with this? Your "fear of making mistakes" actually means that you want everything you do to be right, to be perfect. Your "fear of receiving negative evaluations from others" actually means that you wish to obtain approval and likability from "everyone" through your efforts. So, take a closer look, is your worry itself an unrealistic obsession? China alone has 1.3 billion people, even if you receive praise and likability from 1.2 billion people, the probability of the remaining 100 million people who don't care about you randomly appearing around you is still quite high. After all, we usually only know a few dozen or a few hundred people. Understanding this, can you tell yourself to relax a bit, let go of the obsession, and not care about what the random "others" say that appear around you, just focusing on doing things to your own satisfaction? Moreover, I want to tell you that those who casually criticize and evaluate others' actions are often the ones who haven't done anything themselves or can't do things well. So, let the passing gossip go with the wind, and just happily walk your own path.

question: 37-year-old mother, her parents leaving their hometown but experiencing cold violence and insults from their son-in-law.
description: I met my husband in 2009 and got married in 2013. Our child was born in 2014. From pregnancy until now, my mother has been taking care of me and my family meticulously. My mother is a kind person who knows how to handle things and speak appropriately. However, I can't help but feel discontent because my husband has been making very little contribution to the family and disregarding any advice given to him. But I have been putting up with it. Recently, my husband even swore at my mother, saying "it's none of your business". I can't tolerate his attitude anymore. I asked him to apologize, but he either doesn't respond to my messages or avoid coming home. The parenting styles between our two families are worlds apart. My parents have been frugal to support us through college, afraid that we would suffer even a little. When we started our own family, my parents also made great efforts to support us. My mother has been suffering from rheumatism for a long time and can't sleep at night due to the pain. On the other hand, his parents have never shown any care or concern for our family. They have never called us in all these years. When our child was six months old, my husband went abroad. He only came back when our child turned five, and even then, he went to work in a neighboring city. He comes home once or twice a month, but he acts like a master at home and never does any housework. He doesn't listen to any of my advice. What should I do?
keywords: Marriage, concepts of marriage, mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, son-in-law.

answers.answer_text: Hello, facing parents who are willing to work hard and endure, but are not respected and even scolded, as a daughter, you must be very sad. The sadness filled with guilt is something you cannot let go of. You can tolerate your husband's indifference, but it is unbearable to be hurt by your own parents, isn't it? Perhaps it's time for you to consider your relationship with your husband when he behaves like this towards your parents. Why have you never considered your own feelings in this ongoing family situation, and instead encouraged your husband's long-term neglect of the family? If both you and your parents rely on your husband for financial support, then ask yourself, would he think he shouldn't have to care about anything? His parents would think even more that their son is supporting your entire family, so they would naturally think it is his responsibility to not care, right? Even if your parents are financially independent, I can sense that they are too involved in your life. They cross the boundaries of a family, where the basic composition of a family should be you, your husband, and children. In this family dynamic, your husband seems more like an outsider from your original family, so how could he possibly have the desire to be more involved? Your parents are not at fault; it's just that their efforts towards you have become a habit, causing you to rely on them more than your husband. The main issue is your state of mind, whether you have enough strength to let your parents live their own lives and take on the responsibility of your own family. This is a process of self-growth. Can you detach your emotional dependence on your parents and your financial dependence on your husband, and have the courage to face independent challenges? This is your homework. Good luck!

Hello: I'm sure you must be feeling very painful being caught in the middle, with your parents on one side and your husband on the other. Your parents have been working hard to take care of you and your family, even swallowing their pride, while your husband is often away and doesn't seem to appreciate their efforts. From this point of view, your emotions lean towards your parents. However, I can also see that you seem to understand why your husband behaves this way: the family values and education between the two families are completely different. You say that your husband doesn't listen to your suggestions, and I guess these suggestions are for the sake of harmonizing the relationship between your parents and your husband. Obviously, your husband is unwilling to accept them, and of course, you don't want your parents to suffer. What should you do? I don't know if you realize that your parents are suffering because they are taking care of you in your home. In other words, if you leave your family, your parents won't face this kind of suffering anymore. What do you think? Best wishes!

OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I understand that the attitude and behavior of the OP's husband towards the OP's parents make the OP uncomfortable. Different family backgrounds and personalities can lead to different ways of handling the same matter. Although there is no obligation for a son-in-law to respect his parents-in-law, the current situation is indeed very detrimental to the relationship and married life. I can also feel that the OP is a very filial person. In this regard, the OP may try to communicate more with her husband, clarify these issues and your family situation, and express the expectation of giving parents the respect they deserve. On the other hand, we can also try to organize more family activities to increase mutual understanding and strengthen the relationship between each other.

Hello: You must be feeling very miserable being caught in the middle, with your parents on one side and your husband on the other. Your parents have been doing their best to take care of you and your family, even swallowing their pride, while your husband is often absent and doesn't show gratitude even when he returns. From this, it seems like your emotional attachment leans more towards your parents. However, I can also see that you seem to understand why your husband behaves this way: the upbringing and values in both families are completely different. You mentioned that your husband doesn't listen to your advice, and I assume that these suggestions were made to facilitate a harmonious relationship between your parents and your husband. Clearly, your husband is unwilling to accept them, and you certainly don't want your parents to be mistreated. What should you do? I wonder if you realize that your parents only experience this mistreatment because they are in your household. In other words, if they were apart from your family, they wouldn't face such mistreatment. What do you think? Take care!

question: 25-year-old woman is afraid to make eye contact with others, how to develop the ability to have normal communication with people?
description: I have always been afraid to make direct eye contact with others, especially with the opposite sex, because I'm afraid that the moment our eyes meet, it will be interpreted as a "desire for physical intimacy." Maybe it's because I'm aware of my own vulnerability at home and in society that I always have this fantasy of a powerful opposite sex figure who can "conquer" my body, acting as my protector to help me overcome external troubles and fully develop myself. However, I also understand that in reality, someone who tries to "conquer" your body may not protect you; instead, they may take advantage of you, which is why I'm so afraid. I keep myself tightly enclosed. With strangers, I'm afraid to easily express my feelings of loneliness. With those who are kind to me, I also try to reciprocate, but I can't get closer to them because I set limits for myself, and they also have their own mature and stable social circles. They can also quickly sense my inner uneasiness and may try to hurt me by feigning affection. I really want to overcome my fear of making eye contact with others, and I want to have the ability to communicate with people normally and stop enclosing myself. Can everyone please help me?
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, communication, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: This young lady, hello, I patiently read through the long background story you wrote in the comments section, to be honest, it touched my heart! It's really hard to imagine how you've managed to get through all these years! Sending you a warm hug (づ●─●)づ Judging from the length of your story, I can imagine that during your growth process, you have accumulated a tremendous amount of negative emotions in your subconscious, forming an emotional "dam" in your heart that has become overwhelming! Now that you have poured out all of these emotions, do you feel better in your heart? It is evident that the union between your parents was based more on "talent" and "family wealth," these visible and tangible material interests, rather than "emotions." Moreover, after marriage, your father often quarreled with your mother over these material interests and frequently vented his anger on you and your mother, transferring his frustrations from work onto the two of you. This is a typical "kick the cat effect." It can be imagined that from childhood to adulthood, you have not experienced any "parental love" from your parents. The "love box" in your innermost being has long been empty! In addition, your mother does not understand love, does not know how to love, and either does not care or interferes indiscriminately in your interpersonal relationships, resulting in severe setbacks in your social interactions. "I dared to make eye contact with my mother, but I was afraid to do so with my father. My father once had the experience of having sex with my mother while I was asleep beside them. When I woke up, I felt incredibly scared, and he also put his hand on my chest while buying clothes for me, which made me have a strong resistance towards him and dare not look at him, and even blush sometimes. His reaction was very proud, he would come out in only underwear after taking a shower and look at himself in the mirror behind me. Because of this, I have argued with him many times, but he would say I am sick and not listen to my advice to put on some clothes. So since I entered university until now, I try to go back home as little as possible." From this, it can be seen that your father lacks clear "psychological boundaries" in terms of male-female relationships, and has even had similar "sexual implications" towards you, causing you to feel unsafe in front of him! Combined with what you mentioned in your writing, "I have always been afraid to make direct eye contact with others, especially with the opposite sex," you have unconsciously expanded this "fear" of your father to all the opposite sex. In the language of behavioral psychology, this is called "stimulus generalization" or "emotional response generalization." The saying, "Once bitten by a snake, one is afraid of well ropes for ten years," comes to mind! "With the same sex, maybe it's the influence of movies with same-sex themes and online public opinion. I have blushed and had an accelerated heartbeat with a girl before. Maybe I have the potential to be bisexual, but I understand that the feeling at that time wasn't love. Besides longing for attachment, I had nothing else for her," in fact, your situation is also a longing for "motherly love." Because, although your mother has raised you more, due to her "lack of understanding and inability to love," you have never truly felt genuine "motherly love." In short, the problem lies with you, but the root cause is in your original family. And, as you mentioned, your problem has affected your daily relationships and work. Because this problem is not a temporary one, but the result of "deep and long-term immersion" in your original family, it will not be resolved in just a day or two. As a personal recommendation, if you have the financial means, consider finding a good psychotherapist for long-term and systematic counseling! Starting from your relationship with your mother, try to repair the "emotional connection" between you and your mother. If possible, you can also involve your mother and do "family system therapy" together. Try to change your mother's mindset and repair the "intimacy" between your parents, dissolve the "long-standing emotional knots" in your entire family, and ignite the hope of your entire family's vitality. Hope this can help you.

Hello~ It is not easy for someone like you, who doesn't dare to express their inner feelings, to speak out on such a public platform. Facing such immense internal pressure, I imagine you feel both the desire for others' care and the fear of their potential harm, making you feel both uncomfortable and helpless. As you continue to describe your experiences, you will gradually discover and explore your own inner self, specifically the feeling of "inner restlessness." This is very positive. (I encourage and appreciate the process of self-exploration and speaking about these feelings.) In your description, you mentioned "enclosing yourself tightly," but as you express yourself, you are gradually opening up. Slowly, you are learning to articulate your innermost thoughts. This is very significant. (When someone's inner thoughts enclose themselves, it is to protect oneself from getting hurt by things around them.) Based on your description, I have some questions and thoughts: - You mentioned not daring to make eye contact with others. How is it with your parents and close friends? Do you also experience "physical desire" towards individuals of the same gender? - When you mentioned "wanting to engage in cheap ambiguity that would hurt me," what kind of "cheap ambiguity" are you referring to? Why does it make you feel hurt? - You are aware of these issues within yourself. What prevents you from facing others directly? - You know that you impose limitations on yourself. What hinders you from breaking those limitations? - How do you feel when you look directly at others? Why do you feel resistant during that moment of "desire for communication"? (During your narration, the focus appears to be on the situation, seemingly without your internal feelings.) Usually, these questions are discussed with therapists. Here, due to the limitations of the platform and privacy concerns, the help provided is limited. It is essential to be patient with yourself and the counselor given your circumstances. Building a relationship is not an easy task for you. Your inner being is afraid and tries to protect itself through self-isolation. When snails encounter external stimuli, they retract, only carefully venturing out when they feel safe. Give yourself some encouragement and recognition; you have the ability to empower yourself. Since the Q&A format and public platforms have their restrictions and privacy concerns, the assistance provided is limited. I hope you understand. If possible, and conditions permit during this difficult phase, consider seeking a suitable therapist to talk about recent events in your life. In a counseling setting, due to the nature and professionalism of their work, they can provide you with support and remind you that you are not alone. Feel free to private message me if you have any questions. I hope this can stimulate your thoughts and provide some assistance.

Hello, first of all, allow me to give you a warm hug. From your narrative, it can be seen that you have some self-esteem sensitivities and fear of being hurt by others. You yearn for someone to enter your world but are afraid to open yourself up, so you end up wearing thick protective armor to safeguard your soul. I can understand how you feel because I, too, have reasons for not daring to communicate with others, but I do have some expectations when it comes to the opposite sex. Because you desire to be cared for and loved, you have more imaginations in your mind, but negative experiences in life have made you afraid of being deceived, so you never dare to take that step. However, you also don't like being this way, right? One is already hurt, the other is potentially hurt. If possible, I suggest you give it a try. What I mean is not to find that person, but rather to make an effort to familiarize yourself with the people around you and amaze yourself with your courage. Here are my suggestions for you: love yourself first in order to be loved by others. In fact, the person we most care about is ourselves. We may envy what others have, but that is also what we hope to have. We all hope to be better, so let's not rush to deny ourselves. Give yourself some courage, and you will discover that you can do more. Building a woman's sense of security comes from ourselves. Recently, "Sisters Who Make Waves" has been quite popular, and Zhang Yuki has gained many fans. Many fans admire her personality, which is brave, open, and forthright. A big part of this comes from her own confidence - she has wealth, beauty, and strength. However, if you carefully search, you will find that her emotional journey has not been smooth. But this does not hinder her from shining brightly. When you become outstanding, what will you be afraid of? Communicating with classmates more. The most difficult thing in the world is often taking that first step. As someone who also didn't dare to communicate with others for a long time, I can understand your feelings very well. I used to walk with my head down, afraid of running into acquaintances, and reluctantly had to disguise myself with coldness and arrogance. As a result, many people saw me as someone difficult to get along with. Maybe it was my unwillingness. I didn't want to be much worse than others, so I had to force myself to lift my head, greet people, and play together. In fact, many times things are not so difficult, it's just our inner fears that add more chains, making us afraid to face them. The worst result is simply going back to the starting point, isn't it? Let go of your fears, gather courage, and defeat them. Participating in group activities and team building exercises can bring people closer together. When we participate in group activities, our goal is to stand united against the outside and defeat our opponents. In these situations, we will be more willing to invest trust in each other and more easily discover each other's shining points through cooperation. You will also easily develop a sense of satisfaction and usefulness. Finally, I wish you to overcome this trouble soon and become a joyful little fairy. Believe in yourself and keep going!

Hello, questioner: People say that eyes are the windows to the soul, and through the eyes, one can understand your inner world to a certain extent. For example, when you are happy, sad, thinking, or anxious, your eyes will behave differently. Perhaps you are afraid to look into other people's eyes because you are afraid of being seen through, afraid of being hurt by others! Let's first analyze your problem: you are afraid of making eye contact with others, especially the opposite sex. Because you believe that eye contact will turn into a communication of desire. At home and in society, you are in a vulnerable position, so you hope to be conquered by a powerful member of the opposite sex, and then protected by them. However, you are even more afraid that the person who "conquers your body" will take advantage of you. So you want to protect yourself by closing yourself off. Let's talk about same-sex first. Imagine two girls who are similar in physical condition and psychological thinking, there is certainly no communication of desire between them. Maybe they will take advantage of you, but what do you have that is worth their exploitation? Your body? First of all, you are a person with thoughts, and you can judge whether others are using you or not. And there shouldn't be any emotional confusion between people of the same sex. So, at least with people of the same sex, you should be able to learn how to communicate normally. At first, you may not dare to look directly at each other, but if you try several times, you will gradually get used to it. As for the opposite sex, it is normal for you to be truly afraid. This is especially true for introverted and conservative girls. They have expectations of the opposite sex and hope that the other person will be strong enough to protect themselves, but at the same time, they are afraid that the other person will be too strong and hurt them. In fact, it is very necessary for girls to maintain normal vigilance because you are inherently at a disadvantage to some extent. Perhaps the limitations you impose on others are just because others have not truly entered your heart, and it is not a problem with yourself. As you said, "if others treat you well, you will treat them well too." Moreover, there can also be friendship between the opposite sex. Even if someone does have those intentions towards you, it is understandable. It just depends on how you feel about the other person whether it will develop into something more. Furthermore, we will all fall in love and get married and have children. Can you really go your whole life without falling in love or getting married? Obviously, that's impossible. The reason why your relationships with others can't progress further may also be that the "right person" hasn't appeared in your life yet. Lastly, let's talk about your fear of making eye contact. There are actually many people around us who have a fear of making eye contact. People who dare to make eye contact exude a certain aura that can be intimidating, and you instinctively feel fear and have to avoid it. This situation can only be improved through some training. You can start by trying with the people closest to you, such as family, best friends, and close friends. Gradually increase the time spent making eye contact. Perhaps after a period of time, you will get used to this feeling of making eye contact and the fear will not be as strong. When you feel that you no longer feel pressured when making eye contact with someone close to you, you can intentionally try it in public places without talking to them, just look into people's eyes. Start with short periods of time and then gradually increase. The more fearful something is, the less scary it becomes once you have tried it and nothing serious happened. I hope these suggestions can give you some inspiration, and I hope you can have more and better friends.

This girl, hello, I am very honored to meet you on this platform. I hope my words can bring sunshine to you and warm your heart. Remember this phrase: "The eyes are the windows to the soul." The fact that you dare not make eye contact with others today indicates that the "door" of your inner world is closed to the outside world. You have a deep resistance in interpersonal communication. "Maybe because you are aware of your own weak situation at home and in society, there has always been a powerful opposite sex figure in your fantasy who can 'conquer' your body, act as your protector, help you get rid of external troubles, and help you fully develop yourself." From this sentence, it can be seen that your ability of "self-awareness" is quite good. Because of your "weakness" in family and even society, you lack a sense of security, so you long for a "protective umbrella" to protect you, even at the cost of sacrificing your own body. I believe this is the fundamental reason for your "closed heart". "I also understand that the people who 'conquer' your body in real life may not protect you, but are more likely to take advantage of you, so I am always afraid and keep myself tightly wrapped. I am afraid to easily open up to strangers who come close, and I feel lonely in my heart. For those who treat me well, I will also treat them well, but I cannot get closer to them because I set limits for myself, and they also have their mature and stable social circles." You crave a boyfriend who can be like a "protective umbrella", but you have seen and heard too many "jerks" in reality, which deepens your sense of insecurity, causing you to close your heart even tighter! Even if you encounter someone who treats you well, you are not willing to completely open your heart. To sum it up, you long to open your heart to others, but for various reasons, you find it difficult to overcome the barriers in your heart. Right? What I want to say is: if you want others to love you, first learn to love yourself! You can try to quantify your fears or insecurities: 1. What are you afraid of? 2. What is the likelihood of that fearful thing happening? If expressed in percentages, what would you say? 3. Even if it actually happened, what would be the impact on you? 4. Can you try to explore or utilize some kind of resources to cope with this impact? Believe me, when you have truly sorted out these questions, those things you worry about will no longer be called "problems"!

This is my background story. If you are willing to help me, please read the following content. Thank you for your help. My mother has always raised me since childhood, so I have always lived with them until before going to college and have never been away from them. Therefore, I have relied on them a lot in my daily life. Their only requirement for me is to study well. When I have problems with my classmates, they don't care about my feelings and the interpersonal relationships in my class. Instead, they criticize everyone in a way that brings everyone down to "hell". They instill in me the idea that I don't need to adapt to others, that it is always others who have problems, and that the only thing I need to do is to manage my own studies. So, until before going to college, I didn't have any long-term friends, and my mental state remained at the elementary school stage. I didn't like going out shopping with classmates, and I didn't have ways to stay in touch with them like QQ. My usual entertainment was watching cartoons at home on television, or occasionally watching some youth idol dramas when I felt a bit moved. I didn't participate in listening to popular songs, discussing gossip, liking/disliking teachers, reading idle books, or forming small groups during adolescence, so I didn't have a window or capability to connect with them. My parents went through a stock market crash when I was in junior high school, which caused our relatively affluent family to face difficulties and also led to conflicts and arguments. My parents met through an arranged marriage. My father was attracted to my mother's wealth, and my mother was attracted to my father's talents. However, after marriage, my father's "male chauvinism" and my young age meant I lacked care. My father made my mother stop working and focus on raising me, and from that moment, my mother gradually lost her financial status. In recent years, she has become the representative of waste in my father's eyes. The stock market crash and subsequent continuous arguments may have affected my father's standing among his colleagues. Coupled with his arrogance and his refusal to listen to superiors, he was later met with some difficulties at work and would take it out on us when he returned home. I started to be ignored in junior high school. My mother only focused on arguing with him, and my father only focused on taking back her financial rights and making a comeback in the stock market. Although my parents had conflicts in junior high school, my grades were still relatively good. I always ranked in the top three of my grade, and I had a male classmate who constantly ranked first. But later on, I had a small conflict with a classmate. My mother stood up for me and went to the school to fight her, but she fought the wrong person and fought the staff instead of the main person. Afterwards, she didn't apologize and spread rumors everywhere. She even went to her parents and spoke ill of her. As a result, I was isolated by my classmates. My grades declined, and my crush started doing homework with other girls instead. In high school, I didn't have QQ and didn't actively make friends. My life revolved only around school and family, leading to a monotonous existence. However, because our homeroom teacher would often change our seating arrangements, I had some interactions with my desk-mate and the students in front and behind me. They invited me to go shopping together, but my mother didn't allow it, saying that they were not good people. Although I now realize it was just an excuse for my mother to prevent me from spending money, I believed her at the time. They shared snacks during break time, but my mother didn't buy them for me, saying that snacks from the school supermarket were rubbish and I couldn't eat theirs. But my mother also bought me very little, just a little bit each time, so I couldn't "repay" them. I felt embarrassed to eat their snacks and didn't have enough snacks to satisfy my own cravings, so the smell of those snacks during break time always made me find an excuse to go outside for fresh air. They wanted to add me as a QQ friend, but I didn't know what that was. I told my father, but he didn't allow me to use his computer and didn't give me an account, saying it would affect my studies. So at that time, I couldn't expand my online interaction with classmates, and I lost out on many common interests and shared memories. After graduation, I also lost many ways to stay in touch with friends. My university life was especially lonely, even though I later added some friends, we didn't have much to talk about. In high school, many classmates had their own cell phones, and I wanted one too, but in the end, I only received an old-style phone from my grandfather that couldn't access QQ. My desire to be conquered by a strong person of the opposite sex may stem from a long-term lack of paternal love. The fear of making eye contact with others may be due to a heightened awareness of my disadvantaged position. The presence of sexual desire in eye contact may also stem from coming of age and a desire to experience such things. I dare to make eye contact with my mother, but there was a time when I didn't dare with my father. My father once had a sexual experience with my mother while I was sleeping next to her. When I woke up, I felt extremely scared. He also had an experience of putting his hand on my chest while shopping for clothes, which made me develop a strong resistance towards him and even made me unable to look at him. Sometimes, I would blush. His reaction to this was very proud. He would come out after taking a shower, wearing only underwear, and go to the mirror behind me to look at himself. Because of this, I tried to avoid going home as much as possible from the time I started university till now. Towards the same sex, it may be due to the influence of movies with same-sex themes and online discussions. I once felt red-faced and accelerated heartbeat towards a female classmate. Perhaps I have the potential for bisexuality, but I understand that what I felt at the time was not love. Besides longing, I had nothing else for her. Towards the opposite sex, it may be due to dual reasons: my father's bad influence and my own awakening after reaching adulthood. I both desire and fear having a relationship. I am not good at hiding myself. When I interacted with boys before, I would always feel nervous, my mind would go blank, and sometimes I would even blush and have an accelerated heartbeat, making it difficult to maintain eye contact. But now I have gradually been able to chat and have conversations with them normally, and I can also maintain eye contact with some people, but I can't deepen relationships with them. Some male colleagues can keenly sense my desires and insecurities and deliberately flirt with me, wanting to take advantage of me for cheap thrills. After a while, when they can't get what they want, they start giving me a hard time, causing me a lot of trouble at work. I don't know what kind of reputation I have gained among my male colleagues. No male colleague has given me positive feedback, and I have been at a loss. Gradually, I have transformed my inferiority complex into a defiant attitude. Fortunately, I have always had strong work abilities, mainly because I don't have a personal life and work occupies almost all of my life. As a result, my superiors have promoted me several times and even tried to have me lead a small team. However, due to the jealousy of some female colleagues, they targeted me for a long time, causing me to feel like a stranded fish in a small pond on a beach. I am thirsty but can't swim back to the embrace of the sea. This is my background story. My life now feels like a knot. Can you please help me find a way to untie it? I am deeply grateful!

question: I feel that the people around me look down on me, but I know it is because I look down on myself.
description: I have always felt inferior, introverted, and shy, and I also have social anxiety disorder. Recently, I just got a job as a teacher at a new school, and there is another teacher with me. I feel that she is more outgoing and talkative than me, and I feel that she is more popular. Suddenly, I feel a sense of imbalance in my heart. I feel that I am not as good as her, and I feel that some teachers look down on me. But sometimes I think maybe it's because I am too insecure and introverted, and I dislike myself and look down on myself. However, I don't know what to do. For example, today when we went to get our food, me and the other new teacher, she was chatting with other teachers and I occasionally tried to join the conversation, but no one really paid attention to me. And I feel like the principal has a certain look in his eyes when he sees me being timid and nervous, I feel like he looks down on me and thinks I'm easy to be taken advantage of. I suddenly feel very uncomfortable, and I feel so inadequate. What should I do?
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, colleagues, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Please allow me to give you a warm hug and gently tell you that you are doing great and you deserve to be happy. You have passed your teacher certification exam, which is a stable career achievement for someone like you and me, who are in a similar situation at the age of 30 and still striving for stability. In fact, since the moment we entered society, we have hoped to find a place for ourselves, to find a sense of belonging, and to yearn for the respect of others. [Recognize your own needs] First of all, you need to clarify whether you "do not want to" or "cannot" fit in. The former means that you actually do not want to fit in, but due to the pressure of conformity, you mistakenly think that you want to fit in. The latter means that you do want to fit in and join the conversations, but you just don't know how. At this point, it's quite simple, you just need some techniques. The difficult part is the first one, where you haven't realized that you actually don't want to fit in. Most people don't have conversations with themselves to reflect on their deeper needs. For example, when everyone is gossiping about other colleagues, you actually have been repelled by these topics, finding them meaningless and boring. So why bother torturing yourself? Recognize your true needs and understand the price behind them, and many things that trouble you won't bother you as much. If you don't want to fit in by pleasing others, then the price is not being part of the group, and you need to decide which is more important to you. If it's the former, then don't force yourself to fit in. In other words, I'll give you this saying: Sheep stick together, but tigers and leopards go their own way. If you do want to fit in and the topics others talk about are genuinely interesting to you, you just lack the conversation skills. My suggestion is to read more books on psychology when you have free time, because everyone is different, and it's important to understand yourself.

Awareness is the first step towards change, and you have bravely taken that first step. You have become aware that you are too insecure, too introverted, and you dislike yourself. Since you believe that you are the root of the problem, put more energy into yourself and see how you can become more confident. The more confident you are, the faster your progress will be in your work, and the principal and colleagues will appreciate you more. Confidence will also make you more and more beautiful. Being able to pass the teacher's exam proves that you have good professional skills and sufficient social abilities. You need to look at your strengths more and the resources you have. Among colleagues, there is not only competition but also cooperation. Since you and your colleagues who started at the same time are both newcomers, there is indeed a certain level of competition between you, but it is also easier to become friends and help each other. People may compare you two and it can be frustrating sometimes. Frustration often comes from inappropriate comparisons. Feeling inferior or jealous because you find yourself lacking in certain areas and seeing the gap with others can also motivate you to learn from them, constantly improve yourself, surpass yourself, and achieve your own success. Learning from competitors makes you more competitive, and learning to cooperate makes you more skillful in teamwork. It takes time to adapt to a new environment, so take it slow! Start by learning to appreciate yourself. You can do some exercises, such as listing your strengths and keeping track of every little success you achieve.

question: Feeling uncomfortable being on the edge of the group photo while standing in the center position?
description: Today, my workplace took a group photo. I was positioned on the side in the center, and I had my arm around a leader who often criticizes me. When I saw the photo, I couldn't describe the mixed feelings in my heart. Looking at myself in the picture, I felt nauseated and disliked. The person in the photo had zero self-confidence and seemed a bit ingratiating. Psychology often talks about loving oneself, so why can't I seem to love myself?

answers.answer_text: Title holder, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description, it's evident that the positioning in a photo has been bothering you, and it's clear that your mood has been affected negatively. I truly sympathize with your experience. Based on your description, your appearance in a group photo has led to self-disgust. One way to no longer focus on this photo might be to distance yourself from it. I suggest placing it in a less noticeable area of your home. Although I don't have much knowledge about your behavior in real life, I still believe that this self-disgust is unnecessary, as many of us actually don't truly understand our own personalities. Not understanding oneself can lead to misunderstandings and even self-disgust. Perhaps you can reflect on your performance in your work. If you have done things you didn't want to do due to environmental circumstances, it is normal. In such environments, where choices are limited, we automatically make choices that benefit ourselves and are advantageous for survival.

question: A monthly salary of 5,000 yuan, enjoys using brand-name products, otherwise, will feel unhappy.
description: Monthly salary of 5,000, likes to use luxury brands, otherwise will be unhappy, how to define this behavior?

answers.answer_text: I have read a story about a girl who liked to buy luxury goods for herself. She just wanted to prove to everyone that "she is worth it, and only through this way can she feel respected, admired, and have a sense of existence." She bought things for others, lived for the opinions and views of others. She accumulated a lot of luxury goods that she hardly used, and she still had to repay the loan every month. The pain inside, only she herself knew, which is why she sought help from a mental health consultant to change her consumption patterns. If you, as the questioner, have no restraint in buying things that you don't really need for yourself, then you have a similar mentality as this girl. If you are only for a good quality of life, it is still necessary to buy some high-quality necessities or invest in improving your own abilities.

The monthly salary of five thousand is not really high, so in order to balance income and expenses, it is advisable to carefully consider the purchase of luxury goods. Unless you have the ability to earn more money and can afford to buy them once in a few months to satisfy your inner desires. If it were me, I would also want to buy a lot of beautiful clothes and bags, but after all, life is practical. I would put my wishes aside and strive to live a good life in the present. When the income is sufficiently high, I can buy something as a reward for my hard work. However, on the flip side, there are many ways to satisfy oneself, not limited to buying luxury goods. Are they really useful? Cooking a delicious meal, going out on a trip with family or friends, appreciating the beauty of nature, or indulging in an exciting experience can also be great pleasures. Making one's life more diverse and enriching it. There's no need to compete with others or seek a sense of existence and security solely from appearances. I think it's not reliable. Feeling the practicality of life steadfastly, in my opinion, is the real deal. At least, that's how I see it. We don't have to care too much about what others think.

question: I have previously experienced fear of madness and fear of AIDS. Recently, I am afraid of mad cow disease. What should I do?
description: I have previously experienced both fear of madness and fear of AIDS, but I have recovered from them. Recently, I have been deeply afraid of mad cow disease because I accidentally ate a piece of raw beef at a buffet. Unlike rabies and AIDS, there is no vaccine for mad cow disease and it cannot be detected through tests. I am extremely panicked and neither the Sontag therapy nor the methods I have tried have actually resolved the problem. Could you please advise me on what to do? I am feeling desperate. I used to live a happy life.

answers.answer_text: Title, hello, when I saw this question, I felt sorry for you. Sending you a hug and hoping to bring you some warmth and strength through the screen. [Feedback summary] First, let me summarize what I saw. Firstly, recently, you have been unhappy in your life. Secondly, you feel that the reason for your unhappiness is the fear of mad cow disease. Thirdly, you used to fear AIDS and rabies, but now you are better. Fourthly, you believe that your fear of mad cow disease is justified because it cannot be diagnosed, prevented, or treated. Fifthly, the techniques you have tried, such as Senda therapy and acceptance, have not truly solved the problem and have caused you a lot of pain. [Understanding and analysis] Let me explain my understanding and opinion. Firstly, the whole question gives me a sense of "fate". It seems like fear is your destiny, and if the problem of fearing mad cow disease is solved, I feel that there will be other problems appearing. Secondly, mad cow disease. I looked up some information, and basically no cases of this disease have been found in our country. Mad cow disease is caused by feeding cows mutant proteins or using the protein from the meat of infected cows and sheep as feed. But we all know that cows eat grass, and while they might also eat feed, it is very difficult for such abnormal feed to pass inspections. Even if it can, it's not easy to find cows and sheep with the disease. So, with all these difficulties combined, finding cows and sheep with the disease, being able to sell them, being able to sell them to feed manufacturers who make abnormal feed, being able to sell the abnormal feed to cattle farmers, passing all inspections along the way, getting a green light the whole way, and you just happen to eat it, what are the chances? It's practically zero. Thirdly, the issue of therapy. I'm not very familiar with Senda therapy and acceptance methods, but I think it's good that you can recognize the problem in a timely manner and seek treatment. In my experience, this symptom is like a form of "defense," fear is a form of "defense" against greater fears or sadness arising. [Recommended approaches] Here are a few suggestions: Firstly, I recommend psychoanalysis therapy. Whether it's breaking free from "fate" or seeing the truth beneath the "defense," they both fall within the realm of psychoanalysis. Secondly, I suggest meditation. The meditation planet has plenty of content, both free and paid, and it's all very good. Thirdly, I recommend the book "The Hidden Side of Yourself." I hope my answer can be helpful to you.

The steak provided by the restaurant should be edible. Some Westerners like to eat rare meat with blood, but Chinese chefs will try to cook the food thoroughly because Chinese people prefer well-done steak. There are many levels of doneness for steak: rare, medium rare, medium, and well-done. Beginners can start with medium rare, which means the steak is cooked 70%. 1. Rare steak: The inside of the steak is blood-red and maintains a certain temperature, it can be either rare or medium rare. 2. Medium rare steak: When cut open, the upper and lower sides are browned, turning pink towards the center, with the center being red. There will be blood seeping out when the steak is cut. The beef used for medium rare steak must be fresh and have a thick texture. Frozen or thin steak cannot achieve the same effect. 3. Medium steak: The inside of the steak is pink, with light gray and brown colors mixed with cooked meat. The temperature and texture of the steak are well balanced, and it doesn't taste too raw or chewy. 4. Medium well steak: This is the most popular doneness, with the inside of the steak being a mixture of light gray and brown, with a small amount of pink. The texture is slightly heavier and chewier. 5. Well-done steak: The entire steak is cooked to a brown color, and the beef is fully cooked. It may have a heavy texture, so it is generally not recommended to order a well-done steak. In the past, our ancestors and people from Northwest China also ate raw beef. Some people worry about parasites, but nowadays beef goes through strict inspections and should not be a problem. If you take a bite and feel something is wrong, you can ask the waiter to reheat it. I also suggest that you order a steak that is at least medium well in the future. If you haven't had any stomach problems so far, it means that it hasn't had any impact on you and won't harm your future health.

question: After giving birth to a child, I always can't help but burst into tears at night in the past year.
description: After giving birth to a child, I feel like a completely different person. I always have a terrible mood and no interest in anything. I constantly feel exhausted.
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, prenatal and postnatal.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand from your description that you feel helpless at night. Having a baby changes you, and it can be difficult at night when no one else is around to see the struggle. You work hard, and only you know how tough it is. Tears might flow uncontrollably sometimes. But these are things that all mothers go through, so relax. As the child grows up, all the difficulties will pass. First of all, you need to understand why you are crying. Is it because your body has changed, because it's hard and there's no one to replace you, because you weren't prepared to go from being a girl to a mother, or because of other family conflicts? Identify the root cause of your tears. Once you have identified it, try to think positively. If your body has changed, remember that it's temporary and can be restored. If you feel it's hard, remember that it's worth it because you have nurtured a little life, which is a great thing. If you feel unprepared and unable to be a mother, remember that everything can be learned. Keep a calm mindset and avoid anxiety. If you have other negative thoughts, remember to view the problem in a positive light. Lastly, learn to adjust yourself and overcome the difficulties. Raising a child is a process of role transformation. Learn to adapt to and accept the child. There's no reason to feel aggrieved. Your child is a part of you, and the selfless love of a mother can make you forget your worries and exhaustion. When you're tired, look at your sleeping child and the smile on her face. What difficulties do you still have? In conclusion, crying is a way to release emotions. There's no absolute right or wrong. Crying a little is understandable, but crying excessively is exhausting. I hope you can figure everything out, and everything will go smoothly.

question: Feeling difficulty in communicating with others, afraid to make direct eye contact with others.
description: Since the second year of junior high, I feel like everyone around me is paying attention to me. When I walk on the street, I think people's gazes are strange.
