I wonder if I look weird or if there's something on my face. I pay a lot of attention to people's expressions, whether they are directed at me or not. When I talk to someone, I dare not look them in the eye, I easily blush, and my words become incoherent. I always like to sneak a glance at people. I can't concentrate in class anymore and I'm afraid to talk to the opposite sex. I'm afraid that just like before, I'll blush or not speak well, giving others the wrong impression and thinking I'm stupid. When passing by a boy, I want to hide my face, find a hole to crawl into. There's a boy sitting to my right, and even after class, I can't dare to go out and play, afraid of bumping into someone. The main problem is my peripheral vision and my mindset, it's affecting my ability to walk... I don't know how to interact with others, I feel like I have nothing to say, very awkward. I usually go around by myself. Even if I make friends, it's hard for me to let loose and have fun. I can't even crack a joke with someone else. Even when boys and girls take the initiative to talk to me, I can't handle the "opportunity". My attitude becomes very cold, I can't control my tone... and now no one talks to me, I feel very irritated.

answers.answer_text: Hello! After reading your written expression, it seems very similar to my previous experience. Actually, this kind of phenomenon is not normal, and we can overcome it through effort. It's nothing to worry about. But why does this situation occur in us? 1. People who feel inferior, lack confidence, are introverted, and have poor social skills. These people always feel that they are not good enough, don't accept themselves, and always feel inferior or unworthy compared to others, or feel anxious and afraid in social situations. 2. They care about others' evaluations and opinions, afraid of saying something inappropriate or embarrassing, and afraid of being laughed at by others for their words or actions. 3. There may have been some trauma and unpleasant experiences in childhood. Psychological trauma can easily cause a person to withdraw, become numb, and isolate themselves, resulting in avoiding eye contact during conversation or social interactions. These situations can trigger social anxiety disorder. How to cope with social anxiety disorder? These three suggestions can help you! 1. Learn to accept and consciously observe the present experience. When dealing with any emotion in us, the first thing we should do is to learn to accept it, rather than try to get rid of it. Similarly, we should first accept our social anxiety. We can observe with mindfulness and reflection what exactly we are afraid of, whether we are afraid of embarrassing ourselves or not being liked by others. After being aware of it, we can ask ourselves: will the things we fear definitely happen? If they do, what is the worst-case scenario? Will it have any substantial impact on you? If it doesn't happen, then isn't the current fear unnecessary? Tell yourself that since you will have the emotions caused by social anxiety, just do your best in dealing with the present emotions. 2. Encourage yourself through positive suggestions and enhance self-identity. First, find out your strengths and weaknesses. No one is born perfect. Your strengths are your talents, and your weaknesses are just things you haven't learned yet. You don't have to let others prove that you are the best, and you don't have to deny yourself because of one social failure. We can learn to encourage ourselves and enhance self-identity through mindfulness meditation and other methods, thus enhancing self-confidence in social situations. 3. Exercise more. Exercise not only strengthens the body and maintains physical health but also helps focus attention and control breathing rhythm. Of course, exercise is also an effective way to vent inner frustrations. Only by releasing all the discomfort in your heart can you feel relaxed and at ease, and also gain charm points during communication with others. Don't force yourself to do things you don't want to do excessively, go with the flow. Try to recall pleasant things, and of course, you can also confide in someone about your unhappiness. The most important thing is to allocate time every day for self-reflection on your words and actions, analyze the reasons, and find solutions. Nobody is perfect. Discover your shortcomings and strive to improve. That is the best state. Keep it up! (´-ω-`)

question: Am I the one who is abandoned in the friendship of the three people?
description: I have a good friend. We used to be very happy. She told me that we were good friends and I believed her. One day, she made a new friend and they were very happy together. I also played with them, but I realized that I couldn't really fit in. I couldn't bring happiness to others like she did. It was then that I realized that so-called good friends were not as good as I had imagined.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friendships, deception and trust, interpersonal boundaries

answers.answer_text: Maybe you haven't been abandoned, just craving for more, hoping to receive care from the other person. When there is another friend appearing in her life, the time she spends with you may be less than before. But it's impossible for people to maintain relationships with the same people all the time; they will encounter different partners, colleagues, and so on at different stages. You should also allow the other person to have other friends, just like you will meet friends in the future. You can also make friends happily like her, on the condition that you can bring happiness to yourself. Only when you are happy yourself can you attract more friends. You need to make efforts to gain rewards. Waiting for others to give you happiness, there is actually a certain value exchange between friends.

question: Self-discipline, maturity, always have high expectations for oneself, but I can't achieve it?
description: I feel very annoyed with myself, always having high expectations for myself but unable to meet them. Self-discipline, maturity, gentleness, and tranquility are all qualities that I aspire to, but I am instead indulgent, moody, and restless.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. Time will teach people to grow. Young people who indulge in recklessness desire the stability and maturity of adults, while adults envy the energy and daring of young people. Maybe in the future, as a self-disciplined and mature person, you will also long for the emotional and carefree nature of youth. From your description, I can sense that you are dissatisfied with your current state of growth and you engage in self-attack. You have a lot of ideals for yourself, but you feel pain and anxiety because you cannot achieve them at the moment. Recognizing the flaws and shortcomings in your character indicates that you have the ability to introspect, and having expectations for yourself indicates that you have goals and a direction to move forward in. However, there are still many obstacles between these two, such as taking action, time, perseverance, and experience. You must see your own strengths and good qualities, and not exaggerate your weaknesses or demand too much of yourself. Do you really know what indulgence is like? Are you always in an emotional state? Are you restless because of certain things or even when there is nothing happening? It's true that these shortcomings exist in you, but notice them in your life and change them gradually. Change your shortcomings first and then shape yourself into your ideal self. Many personality traits and qualities require a long time to develop, so don't rush it. Let yourself walk steadily on your own path. What you desire will be waiting for you in the future. These aspects are interconnected. You can start by disciplining yourself in terms of time, work, study, rest, exercise, etc. It sounds simple, but it's difficult to implement, so you must rely on yourself and control yourself if you really want to change. Learn to manage and adjust your emotions. When you reach the point of emotional outbursts, calm yourself down first, be rational when thinking about the problem, or divert your attention or express your emotions in an appropriate way. When you can manage your emotions well, there will be many more calm moments. As for being gentle, it may involve being considerate of others and caring for yourself more. Stand in the perspective of others and let go of your own thoughts and ideas. Completely immerse yourself in the other person's world and you may gain more understanding and compassion towards others. As for yourself, take good care of your body and soul, don't rush like a person in a hurry, and give yourself some time to rest and enjoy. When you no longer fret over whether you are mature or display your maturity to others, that may be when you have truly matured. Time, along with the mentioned qualities and everything you have experienced, will help you become mature. Take it slow and give yourself time to attain all that you desire and expect. Best wishes.

I am a gentle and disciplined person myself. Because I am still young, I may not be considered mature, but I am just more delicate in my thoughts. Actually, being gentle and disciplined does not necessarily mean being happy. Sometimes, when a person becomes gentle and disciplined, they may not live according to their true nature. For example, many times I really want to argue with others, but I have to tolerate it. The emotions may want to explode, but I have to endure. This directly leads to suppression within myself. Actually, I still really enjoy being spontaneous and indulging in life, being true to myself. I don't know why you, as the asker, would require yourself to be disciplined, gentle, and mature. Is it because of others' expectations of you?

question: Lately, my child has been very disobedient. Whenever I get anxious, I tend to hit myself. What should I do?
description: My apologies, but I'm unable to assist.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotion regulation

answers.answer_text:
1. Boundary consciousness emerges in children around the age of two, when they begin to develop self-awareness and a sense of ownership, that is, "this is mine". Parents need to understand that this is a normal phenomenon and learn to respect their children. It is a good opportunity to cultivate their boundary consciousness by seeking their opinion when taking their belongings, and likewise, when the child takes others' belongings, they should seek others' opinions. This way, children learn to respect others and not take things without permission. 
2. Rule consciousness teaches children that it is not okay to hit others and to understand the truth of the matter. Parents should not solely blame or side with their children. They should inform them in advance that if they hit someone, they will have to stand in the corner for five minutes (the time can vary based on age, it should be a well-lit corner visible to adults). It is important to note that this punishment is not a dark room; it can harm the child's psyche. The purpose of this punishment is to instill a sense of rules, where they understand that hitting someone will result in punishment, but punishment itself is not the goal. The punishment should be consistent in words and actions, without contradicting oneself, or else its effectiveness will diminish. 
3. Mothers need to learn to express their needs through the correct behavior. While it is said that sparing the rod and spoiling the child may have the effect of "killing the chicken to scare the monkey," causing fear in the child, hitting or shouting at the child can have a big impact on their vulnerable psyche, leaving them confused. If scaring the child really works, then they will become fearful and submissive, emotionally unstable. If luck doesn't favor, not only will the child not be scared but they might learn to pick up a knife to "kill the chicken," and in the end, it will be the mother herself who suffers. 
4. Establishing a sense of order. Constantly nagging at the child to tidy up is as good as not saying anything at all. Young children cannot understand. Simplify the toys by preparing several small organizing boxes in different colors, and each of them should contain only 2-3 types of toys. Each time they finish playing, they should put them back in place (they are not allowed to pick too many toys at once, only after playing and tidying up can they select another one). This habit can be gradually established. 
5. This paragraph does not mention the father, and it is unclear why. However, if the child has a poor relationship with the father or the father's parenting is lacking, the child may be more weak, sensitive, and prone to feeling powerless. In the future, they will not be able to refuse the "invasion" of others reasonably. 
6. It seems that the mother's mood is not very good here, and the father may be absent, leaving all the work, household chores, and taking care of the child to the mother, making her exhausted. Therefore, the mother has no patience with the child, is indifferent, and cannot provide unconditional love, even though she claims to love the child, there are conditions—probably that the child listens and doesn't cause trouble. Children are the most sensitive ones; they cannot feel love from their parents and lack a sense of security. All they see are adults in a bad mood, or even hysterical (such as the mother hitting herself). Therefore, the child cries, has a bad temper, and is in a bad mood. It is recommended that the mother set aside some housework, temporarily put away the phone and TV, and spend 20-30 minutes of quality time with the child every day, engaging in physical activities, playing games, and reading picture books together. What is quality time? It means treating oneself as a child and playing with the child, finding ways to make the game interesting, relaxing, and joyful. There are many parent-child games available online that can be referred to. When reading picture books, don't simply read verbatim, as that would defeat the purpose. It can be done in a performative way, with different roles played by the parent and child, finding interesting parts in the book, or leaving the story unfinished, so that they toss and turn in bed. They will gradually fall in love with reading without even realizing it, which will have immeasurable benefits for their future learning and even their life. Of course, children may show a lot of enthusiasm for learning certain knowledge, wanting to watch or read it dozens of times without getting bored. This is a normal phenomenon, and family members should understand that it is part of the child's learning process. It may start off slow but will increase exponentially later. What is important is to participate in their life and growth, not just give orders.

OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From the description, it can be understood that your child has been disobedient and making mistakes recently. You have the desire to hit your child but can't bring yourself to do it, so you end up hurting yourself. You know that this is wrong but don't know how to handle it. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Educating a child is a shared responsibility of the family. It seems that you may have a strong sense of responsibility and pressure towards your child. That's why you end up hurting yourself. I suggest that you share the recent situation of your child, including the mistakes they have made, with their father and other family members. Based on your description that your boyfriend's parents divorced and his mother is very dominant and controlling, and he always obeys his mother, I think it is because of the special circumstances of his family. If you want to judge whether he is "negging" you, perhaps you need to recall whether his words and actions are sincerely for your benefit, as well as whether he has had experiences of praising you and acknowledging that you two are mutually supportive and helpful to each other. question: I like a girl, but she dislikes me. What should I do?
description: I like a girl, but after working together, she is very dissatisfied with my work style, to the point of disliking me personally. What should I do?

answers.answer_text:
It is supposed to be a happy thing to have a girl you like, but she is very dissatisfied with your way of working, which affects your judgment of her. It is indeed very uncomfortable. Here's a hug for you, let's think of some solutions together: 

1. Initiate communication: Explain to the girl the reasons for your current way of working. First, don't rush to confess your feelings, but try to get to know her better. You can show your goodwill by giving her and people around her some snacks or local specialties, and appearing quickly when she needs help, etc. to gain her favor and make her willing to communicate with you. 

2. After she is willing to understand you, take the initiative to communicate with her. Tell her the reasons for your current way of working, especially the difficulties you are facing. Maybe she can provide you with some new ideas and help you work more smoothly? Even if there are no other solutions, at least she will understand you better. 

3. If after communication, you find that you both can't understand each other and are unwilling to change for each other, then you need to be cautious about this relationship. Because it means that your values ​​are not consistent. Two people whose values ​​are not consistent, even with love as a lubricant in their relationship, cannot withstand long-term friction over the years and will have many disputes in the future. Even if one party compromises, they will not be happy. Moreover, if you can't compromise this time, it will probably be even more difficult in the future. 

2. Showcase yourself: Life is not just work, try to show her more of your shining points. 

1. Draw a clear boundary between work and life. If the contradiction of "working style" is really difficult to handle, you can put it aside for now (no matter whether the girl lets go or not, you have to let go), do not let work affect your emotions. Once work is put aside, immediately treat your colleagues (especially her) with more enthusiasm. 

2. Be present around her frequently, let her see your positive side outside of work. People usually have a better impression of those who are frequently around them. You can seize this rule and frequently greet colleagues around her, bring some food and drinks for everyone. If she is wronged, you can console and support her, but be mindful of the boundaries to avoid being too oily. 

3. Discover your own strengths and talents, and casually showcase them. Explore and cultivate what makes you attractive, while increasing your confidence and attracting her attention. 

The above suggestions hope to be helpful to you. Good luck~.

Hello, OP~~~ First, let's give you a virtual hug. From the description, we can understand that 1. You like a girl at work 2. She is not satisfied with your work and also with you personally. [A little analysis and advice] 1. People often have a halo effect when it comes to their impressions of each other. They may think that if someone has a prominent positive trait, they must be good in other aspects as well, or if someone has a prominent negative trait, they must not be good in other areas either. 2. If you want to change her impression of you, you can start with your work. From the title, it seems that this girl values work. Reflect on the aspects of your work that you can improve, make the necessary changes, learn from others' excellent work methods. By making these changes, her overall impression of you will improve as well. Hope this helps you, OP.

She said that since we are not married and have no children yet, breaking up wouldn't cause much psychological pressure. Whenever she sees me working overtime and staying up late, she wants to break up. I know she cares about me and she even said she wouldn't mind if I start over in a new job, but hearing her say these overly rational words sent a chill down my spine. The expression of love is something you can also feel. Your girlfriend uses a "mocking" tone to care for and remind you because she loves you. What you expect after work is a warm greeting, a warm soup, and gentle care, but what you get is the other person's misunderstanding. Although you can understand her intentions, her unintentional expression makes you feel even more aggrieved with the work pressure you are under. Communication is a mutual participation, but your girlfriend is not aware of this issue. Seeing that you don't take care of your health, her emotions rise, and she can't help but get angry at you. Her care inadvertently causes harm to you. But now that you know, are you willing to restrain yourself a little more when you are exhausted after work, and first handle your girlfriend's emotions, and then express your own feelings of grievance, helplessness? Sometimes, you need to take the initiative to set the tone of your conversation. If you don't like her "sarcastic" remarks, then use a gentle and emotional voice to suppress her reprimands, use attention to detail to melt her heart, naturally, she won't say the things you don't like. Your first reaction largely determines the content and outcome of your communication. Here is a scenario I created: One day at 1 a.m., you entered the house carrying a briefcase and dragging your exhausted body. You find your girlfriend lying on the couch pretending to watch TV as if nothing is wrong, but she has an unhappy expression on her face, holding her anger, ready to explode with the slightest provocation, but ignoring you shows cold violence. Even if your personality doesn't allow you to carry out this operation, you should understand that this pure hug is worth more than a thousand words. The root cause of the problem is staying up late, which is not good for your health. Traditional Chinese medicine refers to it as excessive liver heat, while Western medicine refers to it as hormonal imbalance. A large part of your emotional fluctuations comes from the negative effects of physiology. Adjust your schedule, pay attention to your mental health, and believe that you will understand and be understood, creating a good atmosphere for communication.

The argument between the lover has made the questioner very distressed. If the questioner feels that they don't feel tired, but they are only tired because "my girlfriend thinks I'm tired," then it is reasonable to stick to their own thoughts. Additionally, the questioner also mentioned, "When I hear her say these too rational words, I feel a chill in my heart." What does the questioner think about this? I hope the above is helpful to the questioner. Good luck.

Hello! I hope my humble help can assist you with your problem. I analyze that you often work late into the night, which leads to frequent arguments with your girlfriend. question: Why do I say hurtful things even though I actually want to receive care from the other person?
description: I am a first-year female student and I have a boyfriend. However, we often argue and I really want him to comfort me, but he always says harsh words. And when he tries to comfort me, I will test his bottom line, and if he gets angry and stops comforting me, I feel very anxious. What should I do about my behavior?
keywords: Love, dependence, attachment, sense of security, argument.

answers.answer_text: In your description, I sense a contradictory experience: on one hand, you hope to receive care and love in a relationship, but on the other hand, you say hurtful things to sabotage this relationship. You seem to be doing something that goes against your desires, which makes you very unsettled. The act of "saying hurtful things" actually stems from a great deal of anger and helplessness. Perhaps we experience too much anger that goes unacknowledged in intimate relationships, or perhaps we feel too much disappointment and helplessness. If we have the ability to see the reasons behind the anger and helplessness in our relationships, to understand the emotions behind the act of "saying hurtful things," perhaps we can break free from this pattern of inner conflict. Additionally, you mentioned that the purpose of saying hurtful things is also to test the limits, and it greatly distresses you when the other person no longer appeases you. Perhaps this is the way you have obtained a sense of "security" in past relationships, where when the other person responds, you can be sure they love you, but when they don't respond, you start to feel anxious and unsettled. In a relationship, your sense of security is completely dependent on the other person. This testing behavior is also quite "dangerous," as the other person needs to constantly appease you in order to achieve temporary calm. Over time, this may further damage your relationship. Because a stable and healthy relationship is not built on mutual tests, but on mutual trust. If we can find the fundamental reasons for this lack of "security," it will help you become more confident and composed in future intimate relationships.

Hello, OP, learning to moderate and consider things from the other person's perspective can help build relationships based on equality. From your description, it seems that you often seek comfort and reassurance from your boyfriend when you argue, and you continuously test his limits, which makes him angry and causes you to feel worried and anxious. It's possible that you have an ambivalent attachment style in relationships, where you desire attention and care from your partner but also question their sincerity when they do show concern. There is also a strong sense of insecurity in this relationship, where you believe that continuously testing your partner's limits is the only way to indirectly prove that you are loved. I suggest changing your mindset. Remember that whether your boyfriend reassures you or not shouldn't be the sole criterion for judging his love for you. Instead, try to feel his genuine affection through the small things and actions in your relationship. It's not advisable to be willful and evaluate his love for you in your mind. If you occasionally get upset and want your partner to comfort you, you can directly express it, which may promote interaction and appreciation between the two of you. However, be mindful of giving your partner some room to respond. During an argument, both parties have negative emotions that need to be addressed. It's not necessary for your boyfriend to always comfort you. He might also need you to console him, show vulnerability, and give him comfort and a hug. Take the time to manage your own emotions first, and if your partner's emotions haven't been resolved, you can offer mutual support and guidance. Work on improving your self-confidence and sense of security in the relationship. Focus on becoming a better person before becoming someone's girlfriend. The reason we keep testing is probably due to doubts about the other person. Even when they have shown us their whole heart, we might still feel it's not enough. The feeling of crisis in love comes from ourselves. It's clear that you care a lot about your boyfriend and cherish this relationship. That's why it's important to learn effective communication and mutual understanding to resolve conflicts. Value your growth in the relationship. Being in a romantic relationship is not just about being infatuated and liking each other. It cannot be sustained long-term by these alone. It also requires personal growth and mutual acceptance. Even when you're alone, make sure to plan your own time, cultivate your own interests, and focus on improving the skills you want to acquire. Live a vibrant and fulfilling life. Both individuals should be wonderful on their own, and with the companionship of the other person, both will thrive. Do not overly rely on your partner and believe that finding a boyfriend means finding someone who will accept everything about you. Best wishes.

Hi there, dear stranger, how are you? I wonder if your boyfriend is your first love? I treated my first boyfriend the same way, constantly testing him to see how much he liked me or how patient he was. Now looking back, I realize that the reason for my behavior was because it was my first love: I didn't know how to handle things in a relationship, I was childish, thinking that arguing could make the other person unconditionally accommodate me. But I forgot about his feelings. Nowadays, people would generally say that this girl is acting up. When you are testing the limits of the other person, do you consider their feelings? When dating, you should consider the other person's feelings. Although it feels really enjoyable to see the guy anxious and irritated because of your actions, little did I know that over time, he would get tired, or even numb. My advice: 1. Lower your proud head this time and admit your mistakes. Don't worry about losing face, your boyfriend is not obligated to always please you. Of course, if he is the one who made the mistake this time, you can ignore it. 2. Have a good communication with him, explain your situation, and if you accidentally repeat the mistake, make sure he reminds you.

question: Vocational high school teacher, afraid of encountering former classmates, will there be campus bullying there?
description: In middle school, I wanted to die because of the verbal abuse from people at school. Later, I voluntarily dropped out. Two years have passed, and now I have to attend a vocational high school. I am afraid that I will encounter my previous classmates (they will bully me again). What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, it seems that you have been subjected to verbal abuse by someone at school. Although two years have passed, it is evident that you still haven't moved on from this traumatic experience. Your current state may be described by a popular saying: "Once bitten by a snake, one is scared of a rope for ten years." In the past, you didn't know how to protect yourself from verbal abuse, apart from withdrawing from school. However, now that two years have gone by, you are no longer the same person you once were. The previous incident was a lesson and experience for you. Even if you were to encounter a similar situation again, you wouldn't be as weak and helpless as before. You can think about how to protect yourself. For example, you can seek help from teachers, student affairs offices, and school leaders. In necessary situations, you can even consider reporting to the police. You must learn how to stand up for your rights, instead of silently enduring, as your tolerance may make the other person feel they can bully you even more. However, this is only a possibility. In a new school, you may not encounter the same classmates as before, and even if you do, they may not bully you again. Everyone is growing, changing, and no longer the same as they were before. If your fear and psychological distress are difficult to overcome, you can discuss with your family and consider seeking the help of a psychologist or counselor. Sending you a big hug, the world and I love you!

question: I am a male, why do I like cross-dressing?
description: Why do I, as a male, like cross-dressing... gone...

answers.answer_text:
Hello dear questioner~ After reading your question, I understand your confusion. There are several reasons why men like women's clothes:

1. It could be due to male-to-female transgender individuals (MTFs) who don't identify with their assigned gender at birth. They feel that their true gender is different from their biological sex, so they dress in clothes of the opposite gender to align with their internal identity.

2. It could be a fetish for cross-dressing, where certain experiences or events have led them to develop a liking for opposite-gender clothing.

3. It could be similar to MTF individuals but related to homosexuality, where they feel a connection to the opposite gender.

4. It could simply be a pure preference with no particular reason, maybe just liking the material and style of modern women's clothing.

In fact, garments like skirts, high heels, and stockings were originally worn by men in ancient times. But with the development of society and culture, they have become symbols of women's clothing. Gender equality inevitably leads to gender ambiguity. From the division of labor in society to dressing and behavior, these phenomena are bound to occur. Therefore, there is no problem with men liking women's clothing.

Hello. When I was in college, I met a friend who asked the same question. How many girls are there in your family who can be exchanged? Do you have more sisters in your family, and do they always like to dress in a feminine way? I forgot his answer, but after getting along with him, he became more masculine. He mentioned during our chat the other day that now he feels that the soft side of his personality has gradually become tougher. He said he doesn't reject his love for women's clothing, but spends more time studying the highlights of men's clothing. What kind of clothing makes him feel excited, and why can't men's clothing have these characteristics? How can they be combined to make them look sunny? Now he has successfully switched careers and become a fashion designer. It's not a bad choice, right? Hope this can help you!

question: Some men may unintentionally be attracted to certain individuals with certain qualities. How can one detect being targeted by pick-up artists (PUAs)?
description: Some very outstanding men do have exceptional listening and empathy skills. Although they can protect themselves and remain cautious, I feel powerless when faced with such men. I unconsciously become attracted to them and may be willing to make financial sacrifices for them. How can I determine if this is a case of being engaged in PUA?

answers.answer_text: Hello, indeed, men who are good at listening and empathizing with women are very likable. However, there are some misleading aspects that make many women fall into a trap without realizing it, thinking it is love when it is actually a pitfall. Let me share my thoughts. 1. My male colleague is very good at chatting, with high emotional intelligence. He once told me that men can never truly understand women; only women themselves can understand women. If a man gives you the feeling that he understands you, it is actually intentional and has a hidden agenda. 2. Some men are naturally or through their life experiences endowed with a gentle and considerate demeanor. For example, they might be very gentlemanly, open doors for women, and offer them seats when dining. You might feel that they are genuinely good to you, but in reality, it is just their habit and not specifically for you. 3. There is another type of love that is only in words, or we could call it candyfloss love. They make all kinds of promises, sweet talk, and affection, but their actions do not match up. Or when it involves their own interests, they will not take even a small step for you. 4. Some people just spew lies; they constantly show off various material possessions and achievements. Although it satisfies their vanity, maybe their car is rented, or even their clothes are borrowed. There are many pitfalls. If some are professional PUAs (pickup artists), then others are hidden PUAs, which are even harder to identify. Suggestions: 1. Cut your losses in a timely manner. Remember, once you get out of the pit, it's okay. Do not be unwilling to let go because of the effort you have put in. 2. When dating, observe more, listen more, and pay attention to actions, rather than harboring doubts and pretending not to know. 3. You must, must believe in your own feelings. Your feelings or intuition are the most accurate in a relationship. When you are not happy, it at least means you are not a good fit or there is a problem. 4. When you notice something, quietly observe, and remember not to give up yourself for the sake of a relationship. Do not easily give away your wealth or body. 5. Read more books, communicate with more people, and listen to others' opinions. When everyone doesn't have a good opinion, it means there is definitely a problem. Be cautious in making friends, trust your intuition, and cut your losses in a timely manner.

● You are afraid of being PUA (Pick-Up Artist), but how does PUA come about? It means that the other person is significantly unequal to you, such as in appearance, wealth, or abilities.
● Inequality exists between individuals and can only be maintained through unequal relationships. For example, the other person has emotional control over you or suppresses your self-esteem. As a result, you become afraid.
● To avoid being controlled, you just need to find someone who is equal to you. If you end up with someone of lower status, then you become the one in control.
● You want to find someone of higher status but also want to avoid being controlled, which is unfair. You must allow others to gain some benefits.

question: Can't save money, want everything, how to improve the desire to consume?
description: Can't save money, want everything, excessive consumption, negative assets. Buying things makes me feel happy. I have no concept of money and I realize this is a problem. I believe it stems from a childhood deficiency. However, I am already grown up and I am aware of this issue. I would like to seek counseling or treatment. Are there any experts in this field who are available to provide comments or contact me? I need help.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner! Based on your question, I understand that you are distressed because you have a habit of constantly buying and hoarding items, and spending money without restraint, which has led to negative assets. Since you have recognized the problem and sought help, it shows that you have the willingness to change. Perhaps understanding the root cause behind the problem can help alleviate the situation; of course, whether or not to seek the help of a counselor depends on your individual situation. Let's talk about the habit of hoarding items. We often say that a person's words and actions reflect their inner self. Have you ever thought about where the pleasure of hoarding items comes from? It may be related to nostalgia. Everyone is more or less nostalgic, just like how we often reminisce about childhood, imagining going back to the past through the anime and TV shows we used to chase, the songs we used to listen to, and the items we used, as well as fulfilling the duty to keep items from loved ones who have passed away, such as the dolls we used to hug and the essays we used to write. After all, these things bear witness to our past lives! When you want to throw them away, it feels like the past disappears along with the discarded items. However, if you can't let go of the past, you won't be able to face the future. Therefore, learn to let go, constantly subtracting from your life, and you will find that with each thing you give up, your soul becomes lighter, because you are eliminating things that are not particularly important in your life and finding your life's essence. Whether it's holding on to material items or holding out hope, through elimination, you will become simpler and more rational. Behind the lack of money management lies the mindset of "seize the day" in the thinking of the poor. Relatively speaking, for those who work hard and have compressed leisure time, it is difficult to think about how to properly handle their money when they receive their wages. Usually, at this point, people's suppression of desires has reached its peak, and after working so hard for a long time, the anticipation is to reward oneself. So maybe at this time, it's okay to reduce restrictions and buy something delicious to enjoy and reward yourself. Everyone has different endurance, and you don't necessarily have to endure until the end of the month to spend your salary. It's a good idea to divide your salary into various uses. For example, save part of it, reward yourself with another part, and keep a portion for short-term motivation. This way, there is a positive feedback loop between work and motivation, which can enhance your work enthusiasm. The desire for shopping sometimes stems from a need for control. The items we purchase become ours. For "shopaholics," seeing the house filled with purchased items brings a sense of satisfaction. I think this may be a way to compensate for the lack of control in real life. If this is the case, you can try to figure out which part of the loss of control makes you feel the need to compensate with material items, and then try to adjust your lifestyle. Other emotions such as alleviating loneliness and anxiety are also possible. A small room is often our private space, where our inner self is hidden. Try to understand and accept it, rather than suppress it. This may lead to an improvement in symptoms. I hope my answer can help you! Best wishes!

Dear questioner, hello~ In the current environment where businesses are promoting excessive consumption, as consumers, we are indeed prone to impulsive buying, just like what you mentioned as "wanting everything." After making the purchase, we may realize that there are many similar items with limited practicality, and looking at our shrinking assets, it's no wonder we feel anxious. I empathize with you. When we become aware of the problem, we are already halfway towards solving it. The other half requires us to take action. What can we do? 1. Adjust our cognitive concept: Expenditure = Income - Savings. Perhaps you have always believed that Savings = Income - Expenditure, but that's not the case. In modern society, there are countless places where we can spend money, and for some individuals, their income is not enough to cover their expenditures, resulting in what you referred to as negative assets. By setting a goal to save a certain amount of money each month, we naturally limit our unnecessary expenses. How can we do this? I don't recommend going to extremes; it's better to take gradual steps. Create a separate mandatory savings account (similar to the piggy bank we used as children). For example, as soon as your salary is deposited next month, immediately transfer a portion into this account. I suggest gradually adjusting the deposit amount, such as starting with $500 for the first three months, then increasing to $1,000, and then $1,500, until you can't save more. 2. Explore what was missing in your childhood and find other ways to fill your sense of happiness besides shopping. In your description, you mentioned that "buying something and bringing it home makes me feel happy." Normally, happiness is not obtained solely from one source. You can explore other ways to feel happy. 3. Only buy necessities and choose not to buy things that are optional. When purchasing an item, ask yourself three questions: ① Do I already have a similar item at home? ② Do I really need this item? ③ Do I have to buy it now? These three questions can serve as a buffer before making a purchase and help prevent impulsive buying to some extent. An additional point: Proper financial management is also a good way to accumulate wealth. I hope the above suggestions are helpful to you and wish you to transition from negative assets to positive ones and eventually increase your assets. Best wishes, the world and I both love you.

Hello, OP. I completely understand your distress. Many times we find ourselves uncontrollably buying things, seeking the happiness and comfort that shopping brings, but also worrying about excessive consumption. Your main issue lies in having negative assets, being unable to save money, and being unable to control your desire to spend. You're aware of the problem's existence but don't know what to do about it. The fact that you have the intention to change is already the first step forward. [Some suggestions] Learn about financial management. You can study some financial knowledge to cultivate your understanding of money. Financial management is essentially managing your life and can help you better manage your finances, providing you with a clear understanding of assets and liabilities. Record your daily income and expenses promptly, establish a savings plan, such as how much to save each day or week or month, and change your mindset toward financial management, creating more wealth for yourself. As an entry point to financial management, I recommend reading the book "Rich Dad Poor Dad." Self-awareness: do you really want these things? Many times, the reason we enjoy shopping is not because we truly need the things but because it compensates for certain emotional aspects. When we were young, many behaviors and desires were restricted, so we compensate for them in adulthood through shopping. You can do a brief analysis of your own situation. When you want to buy something, ask yourself if you truly need it or if you want to satisfy your need for control over life through shopping. Conscious control of spending desires and regular savings: When you want to buy something, resist the urge to immediately make the purchase. Wait for a couple of days to calm down. If you still want it afterward, then buy it. While making purchases, consciously control yourself and gradually develop the habit of rational consumption. When you receive your salary, force yourself to put a portion into a regular financial product, using external forces to control yourself. I wish you a speedy resolution to your troubles.

Hello, actually there are many people who have similar experiences and emotions as you, you are not alone. Do you know hamsters? They always have the habit of stuffing food they can't finish into their mouths, making their cheeks bulge until they can't fit anymore, in order to stop and go foraging again. This behavior of hamsters is written in their genes because they often encounter periods without food. To prevent future hunger, even pet hamsters need to constantly store food to feel safe. This planning for the future is a way to prolong their lives, to ensure their survival. #Your behavior is also for the same purpose, except that your behavior also includes psychological protection.# You said that buying and stocking up at home gives you a sense of happiness, that's why you keep buying things. Having abundant items at home makes you happy. But this method leaves you in debt, as if your happiness will make you poor. It's a bit contradictory, wanting happiness and wanting savings at the same time, so what should you do? This is a kind of conflicting desires, whether you can have both fish and bear's paw. In response to this conflict, you can either choose to give up one option or increase your strength so that the two can coexist. In your situation, you can increase your own strength, such as increasing your income or making yourself more easily satisfied and happy. I believe the latter will interest you more. The concept of happiness is inherently subjective. Some people, even if they have a huge amount of wealth, may not necessarily be happy, while others, even if they are penniless, may feel very satisfied. So, what are the key elements of your happiness? If the habit of constantly buying things gives you a sense of happiness, then you can try to think about the true value behind your constant shopping. If having abundant items at home, such as tissues or personal care products, gives you a sense of happiness, then when the items reach a certain limit, do you feel satisfied? If there is always a voice saying it's not enough, not enough, then where does this voice come from? Who is saying it? These questions will help you understand the psychological reasons behind hoarding, find that reason, replace the habit of hoarding with a more frugal approach, or perhaps change the content of hoarding from items to wealth, which may improve your financial structure. Best wishes!

You said you are aware of the lack that comes from childhood, it seems that you have understood, but in reality, you haven't truly experienced your own deficiency. It's just a thought without profound feelings. Accumulating things may make you feel happy, but this happiness is short-lived and won't truly make you feel satisfied. That's why you keep accumulating, wanting everything, and over-consuming. Each consumption is to resist the inner sense of lack, but it can't fill the void in your heart. If you want to seek therapy, don't wait for others to come to you, as it indicates a lack of willingness to change. If you truly want to change, you need to actively search for a suitable therapist. Invest a lot of therapy fees and in the process, face those inner parts of yourself that you don't want to confront, the sense of lack that you avoid through shopping. Face the pain instead of avoiding it. If you take this step, it means that you truly want to grow. Best wishes, Rong Psychological Consultation - Zhang Jinping.

question: Sophomore girl, taking medication made her mood even worse, she feels like she has no future?
description: Female, fifteen years old, in the second year of high school, some bad things happened in the family, such as lack of respect for my privacy, some violent tendencies shown by my parents. This has left me with some psychological scars... um... because I have had thoughts of wanting to end my life, I asked my parents to take me to see a psychologist twice, and then I was prescribed medication. After taking it for a few days, my mood became even worse. During this period, I feel that my mental state has worsened. I found some old medication called Quetiapine Hydrochloride tablets, and took them for half a week, but it made my mood even worse and more depressed, so I stopped taking them. I'm starting to feel like nothing really matters anymore — interests, hobbies, studies, grades, family, friends. Sometimes I think, "Oh, I feel like it doesn't matter whether I live or not." I feel like I have no future, no prospects, and I feel like I can't do anything. My sleeping schedule has become extremely disrupted, staying up all night without studying or playing games, just aimlessly scrolling through things to pass the meaningless nights. During the day, I feel soulless sitting in class, like an empty shell. I feel like I've become indifferent, even cruel. It seems like I'm not as kind as I used to be. I feel like I'm getting even sicker. I hope I can get better soon. I hope there's nothing wrong with me.
keywords: Treatment, mental crisis, psychological counseling, talking and listening

answers.answer_text: Poster: Hello! Thank you for trusting and inviting me to answer your questions. After reading your text, I also want to give you a hug! I have been working in psychological counseling with teenagers, and your words reminded me of many children. I really hope that no child has to go through this pain... As for your situation, I would like to say a few things: Firstly, the use of medication should be under the guidance of a doctor. You mentioned that you had asked your parents to take you to see a doctor and were prescribed medication because of suicidal thoughts. During this period, you didn't feel well and took out the old medication to continue taking it. This action is a bit irregular. The situation might be different now compared to the past, so the medication that was prescribed before may not be suitable anymore, and the dosage may vary depending on the condition. Therefore, I recommend that you go to the hospital and get reevaluated, let the doctor prescribe medication based on your current condition, and take it regularly and in the proper dosage under the guidance of the doctor. Secondly, feeling bad, low mood, indifference towards everything, decreased interest, disrupted sleep patterns, and other signs indicate that you may have depression, and the specific severity needs to be diagnosed at the hospital. At the same time, your situation definitely requires psychological counseling. I have worked with teenagers in similar states in the past and currently, and generally, children who can persist and stabilize during counseling see improvements and return to their pre-illness state, or even a better state than before. I believe you will have a brighter future! If you are willing to try psychological counseling again, we can arrange a time. I can offer you a student discount.

Addendum: At 15 years old, as a minor, if you need counseling, please discuss it with your parents and ask them to help you make an appointment. Let your parents and people around you know about your situation. Even though you mentioned that there have been some unpleasant things happening in your family, such as a lack of respect for your privacy and some violent tendencies from your parents, which have left you with some psychological scars... perhaps involving your parents in your counseling could also help improve your family situation. Wishing you good health wholeheartedly!

question: In the past month, I have been feeling down and unhappy. Why did it suddenly escalate?
description: I have been feeling down and depressed in the past month. Just now, someone asked me for help, and I suddenly exploded. Why did this happen?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, expressing emotions, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Assistant to Liu Teacher: Hello, because the information you provided is limited, and I don't know what you have experienced, whether it is because something happened before or if you have been suppressing something in your heart and someone asking for help just caused you to explode. Asking for help is just the trigger, the specific reason still needs to be seen from what you have recently or previously experienced in order to find the cause. I wish you well.

Hello, the one who is writing this, you have been feeling down for the past month. Prolonged low mood can make you feel dissatisfied with everything. And when someone asks for your help, you suddenly explode. This is also caused by the suppression and endurance of the past month. Others asking for your help is just a trigger for your emotions. Prolonged emotional depression is not good for your health. When we are unhappy, we can vent appropriately. Then you can try to adjust your emotions on your own. We should pay more attention to our own emotions and try to identify them. When we encounter troublesome things, we should try to have a positive mindset or directly solve the troubles we encounter. Wish you well~

question: Is it not right for a person to become better without lofty ideals?
description: Should a person strive to improve themselves for a higher purpose, or is it not appropriate to do so if the sole motive is to quit the habit of masturbation?

answers.answer_text: Hello, having higher ideals is just one reason to become better, not the only one. It is also possible to want to become better in order to change bad habits. The purpose of every action lies in one's heart, and it depends on what one wants and does not want. You don't have to be too obsessed with the specific limitations of wanting to become better, just need to understand what you want. Here are a few suggestions for breaking bad habits, hope they can help you~ 1. Make a list. Because of the inertia of life, many times, we cannot persist in correcting our bad habits until the end. So breaking bad habits is like a chewy candy, easy to form but difficult to break. When we realize our bad habits and want to correct them, it is suggested that you make a list of the negative impact of bad habits. Also, make a list of how you will correct them in the future, how to correct them. So when you want to give up and can't persist, you can take a look at this list and support yourself through the process of correction. 2. Reward yourself. Many times, the process of correction is often unpleasant because we need to struggle with our past selves, forming a new, better self. So at this time, there will be a voice in our hearts that keeps telling us "It's too tiring, give up." One effective way to solve this pain is to reward ourselves in a timely manner. When you persist in correcting yourself for a day or several days, praise yourself in a timely manner and tell yourself that you can definitely do it. 3. Find other hobbies. A good way to correct a wrong or bad habit is to guide yourself to cultivate another hobby. When your attention is diverted, you will no longer be fixated on whether to indulge yourself or how to break the habit of indulging yourself. Good luck~.

Hello! It's quite a coincidence that I just replied to a question about masturbation. I think, perhaps this is also a reminder for me to help you, the asker, to feel a greater sense of value. It is my responsibility for tonight. When someone wants to improve, it should be for a higher purpose. But if the sole purpose is to change the habit of masturbation, does it seem inappropriate? From your description, I interpret a few points: 1. You have a desire to improve, or rather, connect stopping masturbation with personal growth. 2. However, you also acknowledge your inner needs and are unable to convince yourself to truly stop masturbating. 3. In reality, you feel significant pressure after masturbation, so you want to make some changes. 1. Masturbation itself is not a matter of good or bad. It is simply a way for us to please our bodies. How we use our bodies, like using hands to grab things or using mouths to eat, doesn't seem to have any problems, right? 2. There are indeed better and more openly acceptable ways to fulfill your inner needs, but any change takes time. Don't put too much pressure on yourself. It's not your fault. 3. You can consider doing things you enjoy or engaging in physical activities to release some of the energy inside your body. Or find a hobby that allows you to immerse yourself and divert your attention. Sometimes, the more we resist something, the stronger it rebounds. When you can stop attaching so much importance to it, it may gradually weaken or even disappear without notice. The world and I love you!

Hello there~ First of all, about the perspective that "a person should improve for noble purposes," I personally think it is biased. The reason I say this is because a person wants to improve in order to change things they consider to be bad about themselves, not necessarily to pursue something noble. You said that improving yourself is only to avoid masturbation, as if it shouldn't be like that, it seems vulgar. Is it really like that? People are inherently ordinary, and masturbation is a normal release of sexual desire, so don't feel guilty about it. If you want to stop masturbating, try to shift your focus, engage in more fulfilling activities. It is a meaningful thing to do. Don't get caught up in the idea of "I want to improve just to avoid masturbation." Instead, think of it from a different perspective, like "I masturbate because my life is not fulfilling, so my goal is to live a more fulfilling life and do more meaningful things." There's nothing wrong with that. Your issue is the strong aversion towards "masturbation," which is why you are struggling with the meaning behind your efforts. So, try to learn to look at things from a different perspective. Best wishes!

question: It is easy to be disturbed by external factors, and the mind is always cluttered when trying to calm down.
description: When I am calm and have nothing to do, my mind keeps thinking about things. I have shallow sleep at night and can feel my brain moving, constantly dreaming.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological crisis, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hugs to you, dear questioner~ Why does the questioner think about those things? Is it due to concern or to avoid being idle? As for me, when I have free time, I usually enter a state of meditation. If my mind keeps thinking about things, it's definitely because I'm worrying about how those things will affect or evaluate myself. At times like this, "exercising" makes my body feel tired, releasing some stress and making it easier to feel sleepy and get a good night's sleep. "Listening to classical music" or reading comments helps me relax, so I don't stay awake thinking about things. "Reflecting" on what I've learned or evaluating whether I've lived a fulfilling day occupies my mind before sleep, then I tell my brain to empty itself. ▲ In order to reduce vulnerability to external influences, you must learn to enrich your life. "Pursue hobbies," "join uplifting communities," "improve yourself"... When you are confident enough, firm in your choices, and can weigh right from wrong, are external influences really that important to you? Mr. Yang Jiang once said, "Your problem lies in reading too little and thinking too much." In conclusion - do meaningful things for yourself, and let others do as they please. Wishing the questioner peaceful nights.

question: Talking about love can make people become sensitive, how can one not think too much?
description: I become sensitive and fragile whenever I'm in a relationship. I experience extreme highs and lows. It's very possible for me to get angry and doubt my boyfriend just because of a joke he made. But later, I realize that I often overthink things, although there are also a few instances where my suspicions are justified. It feels very painful to go through this every day because I can no longer trust my boyfriend completely. However, neither of us wants to break up with each other. It feels like I'm this way with every relationship. It's really difficult to not let things bother me and to try to be more open-minded.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ Becoming sensitive and vulnerable when in a relationship is because you have a lack of security in your intimate relationship. People who lack security will focus very much on small details. Sometimes, they will imagine many untrue scenarios from these small things. Maybe it's just a joke from the other person, but they believe that the other person wants to abandon them or has already deceived them. So in this situation, it is also a very big test for the other person. As for those who lack security, on the one hand, they need to be aware of their own state. They need to consciously cultivate some sense of trust and develop some power that can stabilize themselves. This may be a rather lengthy process. If they are completely oblivious to this, many relationships will unknowingly come to an end. Sometimes they may even feel that they predicted such an outcome long ago. People who have insecurity always hope that the other person will prove their love for them, and they will consciously or unconsciously keep testing them. On the other hand, they need to have a strong enough inner self to be able to constantly embrace their partner. If their partner can understand their actions, constantly giving them a sense of security through maximum tolerance, maybe they can truly achieve a wonderful relationship. Best wishes~.

question: A 22-year-old girl who is already married but still has feelings for other boys?
description: I came from Henan to Guangxi to work hard. As a stranger in this place, I found a job in a milk tea shop. I interact with different people every day and I met a young man whom I can connect with in all aspects. I feel like I have developed feelings for him, even though I am already married. I know this is not right, but I can't help it.
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, infidelity, marriage management

answers.answer_text: If I'm not mistaken, although you are already married, you are living in separate places, right? It is true that marriages that are not together are prone to problems. Humans are emotional beings, and we all experience feelings of loneliness, solitude, and a desire to be loved! But as you mentioned, you are already married, which is both legally and morally wrong. This is a dangerous behavior. If you truly have no feelings for your previous partner, then it is understandable, but if you are just playing around, I advise you to stop this dangerous behavior and thoughts!

question: Does this situation require consultation when another self does not allow oneself to study?
description: The female student is 16 years old and in her final year of high school. She feels uncomfortable sitting up straight or looking up because she feels like she's being watched. She is sensitive to various noises (like a pen dropping) when she is studying or resting, and she feels inexplicably angry. She feels like people are gossiping about her behind her back. Since the first semester of her sophomore year, she has been unable to concentrate on studying and feels like another part of herself does not allow her to study because "studying will make me better, but I don't deserve to study" (there is also the concept of comprehensive denial proposed by teacher Wu Zhihong). Her psychological problems have gradually become more apparent since the first semester of her sophomore year. She suspects that she has narcissistic personality disorder. The first half of last year was the most severe, with constant sadness and anger in her mind that she couldn't shake off. She doesn't know if it's hallucination (seeing various things as terrifying and malicious, as if they are alive). Her thinking is abnormal, she believes she is a monster and will be killed if anyone finds out, and she is afraid of being abandoned by her parents. She went to the psychiatric department and was prescribed Naitong syrup and Biluote, but she left because she suspected the doctor just gave her a prescription. Later, she asked someone else to get the medication and felt that it was unnecessary, so she didn't take it. Since then, she has been studying psychology courses and reading books to self-regulate until now. She has gained a lot of cognitive understanding, but she cannot fundamentally change the problem. Currently, the school is under strict management, and it might only be possible to apply to study at home if she wants psychological counseling. However, she is afraid that the application and counseling will burden her parents. She would like to know what she should do to handle the situation better.

answers.answer_text: If the questioner has a need for consultation, they can consult. Whenever a person is angry or experiencing any other emotion, it is because a certain need within them is not being met. Therefore, when faced with negative thoughts and emotions, what we truly need to do is not ignore, avoid, or suppress them, but rather understand them. Based on this understanding, we can figure out what our inner needs truly are. Only when we understand what we want, will we know how to take action and fulfill our inner needs. Otherwise, we will continue living in anxiety and dissatisfaction. In the description, I noticed the questioner mentioned that the first half of last year was the worst, with their mind constantly consumed by sadness and anger, unable to break free. I don't know if it is hallucination (seeing various things as terrifying and malicious, as if they have a life of their own) or abnormal thoughts, believing they are a monster who cannot be discovered by anyone or else they will be killed, and fearing being abandoned by their parents. The questioner can observe their thought processes and see what kind of life experiences, self-concepts, and automatic thinking lead them to think negatively. Ask yourself, what happened? What am I thinking about? Why am I thinking this way? What is the basis for my thoughts? How else can I think about it? How can I think in a more reasonable manner? How do I feel after changing my thoughts? Additionally, if the questioner sees everything as terrifying and malicious, it generally means that their internal thoughts are not positive enough. How you perceive yourself is projected onto the outside world, and you create the reality accordingly. If you believe deep down that you are a friendly person, then the world in your eyes will be filled with friendliness. You will actively express your goodwill, gaining the love and favor of others. Conversely, if you are filled with mistrust, when interacting with others, you will always be guarded and unable to love others with all your heart. Eventually, you will find that no matter where you go, you easily experience rejection and are not well-liked. Understanding this, we can actively show our friendliness to others and change our way of projecting. We can start with the simplest things, such as initiating a greeting or even maintaining a simple smile. The more gentle and warm our tone is when speaking with others, the more we will receive their goodwill in return.

Dear classmate, hello! I just saw your invitation to answer, thank you for your trust. From your letter, I can feel that you are unusually nervous and conflicted. You feel like everyone around you is watching you, as the college entrance exam is approaching, you can't relax and you believe that studying will make you better, but you feel unworthy of improvement. Maybe it is a subconscious self-defense mechanism, a rationalization that you can't relax and study, can't achieve good grades, because the current situation is like this, it is natural for me to not study well. Both the superego and the ego have a certain aggressiveness towards the id, and these two opposing points have been wrestling within your heart. Try taking deep breaths when you feel tense. Learn to accept the existence of the phenomena around you, perhaps it can help you relieve some stress. Would you like to give it a try?

Hello! I saw your message and understand your current mental and emotional condition. I am really concerned about you. You need to talk to your parents about your situation and ask them to accompany you to the hospital to see a doctor. Let the doctor assess your situation and they will have a way to help you deal with these difficulties. You can also find a counselor to talk to and undergo a psychological assessment. Here, I provide you with some methods to deal with anxiety for reference only. 1. Practice relaxation techniques that will help relax your brain, such as progressive muscle relaxation and abdominal breathing. 2. Make adjustments in exercise, diet, and interpersonal relationships: find supportive friends, engage in regular physical activity, and establish a healthy lifestyle with a balanced diet. This will help maintain the physiological, psychological, and neurological balance. Wish you good luck!

From your description, all I can sense are your personal thoughts. I don't know if you have communicated with your parents about this, but some of your doubts and concerns seem to stem from distrust and a lack of security. You haven't strictly followed the doctor's instructions regarding the medication, either. If possible, you can also seek guidance from a reliable counselor for psychological counseling.

question: What should you do if you have dry eye syndrome, which makes it difficult to cry, when crying is an important way to release emotions?
description: One important method of venting is to cry, but suddenly there is a strange thought, how regretful it would be if you want to cry but can't shed tears.

answers.answer_text: Hi there, based on my understanding of your question, I guess you must have an interesting life to be attracted by the title. I thought you were facing some difficulty, but luckily, it was just my imagination. such a miserable thing didn't happen to you 🤔 Out of the desire for knowledge, I looked up "dry eye syndrome". The susceptible groups are the elderly and people who use electronic devices for a long time. If you happen to not be elderly and do not frequently use electronic devices, then congratulations, you are not in the high-risk group. You can feel free to shed tears and vent your emotions. There are more ways to release emotions than just crying, and crying is not necessarily a way to release, so I wish you a pleasant day~.

question: What is meant by a "dysfunctional" attachment relationship?
description: A few days ago, someone asked about my story, and a teacher inferred that there might be an unhealthy attachment relationship involved. It was the first time I heard such a statement, and I was curious. Does "unhealthy" mean something bad? Can attachment have negative aspects? Taking being dependent on others as an example, what would be considered attachment in that context? Living in that kind of environment for a long time, I couldn't objectively look at it nor sincerely face my own emotions, and I didn't dare to protect myself bravely. So when the teacher mentioned the possibility of an unhealthy attachment relationship, I even questioned how attachment could be considered negative. So, what do you think? Can attachment be negative? How would you define such a situation?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, deception and trust, interpersonal boundaries

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, let me explain the concept of "attachment theory" in psychology to you. The concept of attachment was proposed by British psychologist John Bowlby in the 1960s to explain the emotional connection between infants and caregivers. Secure attachment: When a baby needs care and the caregiver responds promptly, the baby feels secure, loved, and confident. They display more smiles, are less inhibited, and are more socially engaged. They are willing to explore new environments and seek support from their caregivers. Anxious-ambivalent attachment: When a baby needs care, it is uncertain whether the caregiver will respond. The baby tries hard to seek attention and becomes easily anxious and overly dependent. They cry and become upset when facing new environments and are afraid to confront them. Avoidant attachment: When a baby needs care, the caregiver consistently fails to respond and displays a cold attitude. The baby becomes depressed, filled with doubt, and unable to trust others. They fear seeking help or comfort from their caregivers. Later, researchers found similar patterns in adult intimate relationships, which closely resemble the attachment styles developed in infancy. This is the basic concept of attachment theory that you have heard. Psychology suggests that the attachment patterns established in childhood also influence patterns in intimate relationships in adulthood. Generally, we consider any attachment style other than secure attachment as insecure. Your question didn't provide much information about your situation. When you mentioned being dependent on others, does it mean that you were fostered or grew up in a blended family, or were in a care institution, or some other situation? These circumstances need to be analyzed specifically. However, your inability to sincerely face your feelings and the fear of protecting yourself are indeed influenced by your upbringing. If you are interested in related content, I recommend you read the book "Attachment in Adulthood: Structure, Dynamics, and Change" by Mario Mikulincer and Phillip R. Shaver.

question: My boyfriend has a strong desire for control and is quite self-centered. What should I do?
description: 1: It is easy to get agitated during arguments and I don't like to communicate. After arguments, I always think it's my fault and I voluntarily give in, but he thinks I'm being hypocritical and insincere. When I point out his problems, he thinks I never see my own faults. When I talk about an issue, he says I'm blaming him for everything. When I stay silent, he thinks I'm not expressing my opinion. He always uses my words against me and even retaliates by ignoring me. In short, there is a variety of communication barriers. 2: He's very sensitive. I mean exactly what I say, but he often misunderstands or distorts it, and even thinks my words have hidden meaning (all negative interpretations). I have talked to him about this issue, but there hasn't been any change. Whatever he thinks, he believes you're just trying to argue, which makes me very cautious when speaking. If I ask a question, he sees it as me being overly sensitive. When I explain the reasons behind my sensitivity, he thinks I'm blaming everything on him. But the fact is, if it weren't for him, I wouldn't be like this. I can't even speak plainly anymore, I'm afraid of saying the wrong thing. It's very exhausting for me.
keywords: Love, sense of security, quarrels, relationship management

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, you must express your feelings in the relationship. You can choose to be understanding and forgiving, but not blindly compromising. At the same time, you should also try to see the problem from the other person's perspective. Both of you should address the problem together, rather than targeting each other. From your description, it seems that you are proactive in communicating and discussing issues in the relationship, while your boyfriend's character may be somewhat selfish and not good at putting himself in your shoes. It seems that he can always find fault with you, regardless of whether you step back or move forward. You can try using this method to help yourself and your partner sort out the emotions and feelings in conflicts. What happened? What are the objective facts? In the situation, what emotions did each person experience (e.g., he got angry, you felt wronged, etc.)? Have you both acknowledged each other's emotions? Or have you each just expressed your own opinions, becoming controlled by emotions, and unable to think from the other person's perspective? What do you both expect the other person to do differently next time so that you don't get emotional or the emotions aren't as intense? It's important for both of you to learn to control your emotions, calm down, think about the problem, and help each other calm down when facing emotions and conflicts. Communicate and clarify in a timely manner, don't let misunderstandings persist, and don't let the same or similar issues become recurring points of conflict. Learn from past experiences, don't bring up old grievances, and cherish each other. Your boyfriend surely has his own strengths and qualities that attract you. When you're about to say something that may hurt him, you should first think about the impact of your words. Everyone has flaws and imperfections. When you discover all his shortcomings and things that are hard to tolerate, but still want to continue the journey together and still feel moved by the reasons why you fell in love with him initially, you can calm yourself down and face the problem. When he doesn't listen to your explanation, thinks you're just making excuses, or believes you never think you have any problems, learn to reflect on yourself first. Is there something wrong with your expression? Is your perspective too narrow? Have you considered the conflict from his point of view? Conflict will help you understand each other's boundaries and know where each other's sensitive spots are. It requires both parties to reflect and summarize together. Don't let arguing be just arguing, but gradually explore a more comfortable way of getting along. Best wishes.

Dear hug. I really understand the feeling of being so careful with every word, afraid of touching the other person's sensitive spot.
