This can make you very tired. *During the honeymoon period and adjustment period, I believe you must have had a very sweet time, where you were each other's perfect parents. But as time goes on, you start regressing, reverting back to your childhood selves, and you both hope that the other person can nurture you again according to your own desires. In other words, to fill the emptiness in your hearts with love, how much love do you need? To some extent, it depends on how deep your emptiness is. *The reason why you are still maintaining this relationship in the father's transformation plan is not only because you cherish the good things the other person has done for you, but also because you want to change your father. He must carry the shadow of your father, which makes you feel that as long as you change him, you can get a perfect father. Perhaps this is one of the reasons why you say you can't communicate with your boyfriend. *What do you want? If you want to implement your transformation plan, then you must accept the consequences, besides the ones you are currently experiencing, there may be even more serious ones. If you don't want to bear these consequences, then you choose to leave. Best wishes, I and the world love you.

question: The visitor's emotions suddenly got out of control. How should a novice counselor handle this?
description: If during the counseling process, the client becomes emotionally overwhelmed while telling their story, such as crying loudly, cursing, or becoming extremely angry, what should a novice counselor do in this situation? Should they give the client some time to vent? Or should they redirect the client's attention? Or is there another approach?

answers.answer_text: Hi there, thank you for your invitation and trust. ■ "If during the counseling process, the visitor becomes emotionally overwhelmed due to the things they are discussing, such as crying uncontrollably, cursing, or being extremely angry, what should a novice counselor do in such a situation?" ▲ Firstly, this is a great question. From my understanding, as a counselor, it is a positive thing for both the counselor and the visitor. The counselor can discuss the situation with the visitor and help them progress towards their counseling goals. (The personal growth of the counselor is also important.) If the counselor is a novice, it's best to let the visitor cry first. At this moment, the visitor is open and in need of listening and support. In Morita therapy, there is a mountain-shaped curve, so novice counselors shouldn't worry. Crying is a way for the visitor to release and self-reflect. In general, counselors will let the visitor cry freely without trying to stop them but providing some verbal comfort at appropriate times and preparing tissues. Don't think that whether they cry is a good or bad situation, it would be the counselor's "I thought" or "I believed" rather than being together with the visitor. Therefore, considering the individual reasons, it may be necessary for novice counselors to receive supervision from a senior counselor. ▲ Furthermore, based on the visitor's behavior, I think the counselor's skills and communication with the visitor are commendable. The visitor has felt acceptance, inclusiveness, neutrality, empathy, positive attention, and respect from the counselor, which are necessary conditions for the personal growth and learning of a psychological counselor. Therefore, the visitor is relaxed and feels safe, and the counselor-visitor relationship is good. ■ "Should the counselor give the visitor time to vent, or divert their attention, or do something else?" ▲ Besides crying, the visitor may also express anger. These are all normal emotions that exist because they are needed at this time. This reminds me of a frequently asked question: Can you avoid depression or anger if you study counseling psychology? I won't answer directly but instead, I will ask a question: "Are counselors humans too?" "Of course." "Then, as humans, why shouldn't we have normal emotions? When sad, we should be sad. When angry, we should be angry. Only humans can empathize with one another." Visitors are in their own events, experiences, and situations, so they have every reason to express any emotion. Therefore, what visitors express in counseling may be precisely what they lack and need. On the contrary, we often find it difficult to express our true emotions in life. For example, when confronted with conflict, sometimes, to save face, we pretend to be kind; when we know we are being taken advantage of, we act generously; when being arranged or bullied, sometimes due to societal reasons, we have to flatter and accommodate, even though these behaviors have their own functions and purposes, but many times, you are suppressing yourself. If even in the one place where you can safely release, there is none, people would feel even more frustrated. How wonderful would it be to have a place where there is no judgment, no criticism, where you can be yourself and express yourself safely? So I also said that the counselor's professionalism is very important, and the definition of novice counseling is also worth exploring. On the other hand, the visitor's emotional expression is also valuable information for analysis. The excessive crying might be what the visitor needs but has not yet achieved, or it could also be a meaningful and functional behavior. Of course, these are all just speculation. It is only by actively asking and providing feedback that we can further progress once a good counseling relationship has been established. ■ The path of a counselor is not easy, and personal growth is especially important. Investing in personal growth is necessary. Helping others also helps oneself. We are companions on this journey.

question: We both have strayed mentally, and now I want to break up with her, how should I go about it?
description: She said that her feelings for that guy were getting stronger, so I suggested breaking up. We broke up that same night, but the next day, she kept coming to me trying to get back together. She said she misunderstood their friendship and that it was just a "bromance." But I couldn't accept it anymore. I don't blame the guy, and I don't blame her either. Love is between two people. So I think this is a relationship problem. I couldn't accept it in my heart, and she kept trying to get back with me, but I kept refusing. One day, she came to my dormitory building, and I stubbornly went back to my room. She cried and even threatened suicide. I was so tired at that moment, both physically and mentally drained. To avoid any harm, I compromised and temporarily got back together with her. But my heart was already dead. Now that we've graduated, how should I go about breaking up?
keywords: Love, dependence, attachment, arguments, love management.

answers.answer_text: Sorry, I sent it before finishing. Let me continue writing. Just mentioned, you described the current state of your relationship. First, your girlfriend initiated the breakup, citing that she has stronger feelings for someone else. Then she proposed getting back together, claiming that it was just a friendship. Furthermore, your girlfriend even threatened to commit suicide in order to restore the relationship. So now you are in a temporary reconciliation state. However, as you mentioned in the question, you are mentally and physically exhausted and clearly stated that you want to break up, but you are unsure how to do it. In your description, you mentioned that both parties had emotional infidelity, but it seems that it was the girlfriend's emotional infidelity that caused the change in your relationship. I wonder what significance it has when you mentioned you also had emotional infidelity. I think there may be a few possibilities: 1) You have also experienced emotional infidelity, so you don't excessively blame your girlfriend and can understand her actions. 2) You are possibly hesitant and considering whether you can make an effort to forgive her unfaithful behavior and repair the relationship. Regarding these questions, I think you already have your own thoughts in your heart. You no longer have confidence in this relationship, so you want to end it. You don't blame your girlfriend's actions, but this kind of relationship makes you feel weary. I agree with the previous responder who suggested that when faced with your girlfriend's method of using threats to maintain the relationship, it is necessary to contact her family to have them play a supervisory role. Additionally, I think you should try to explain as clearly as possible to the other person your feelings, your perspective, and your plans for the relationship. Maintaining a relationship is a matter for two people, and forcing it will always lead to an end. Stay clear-headed and independent, and I hope you have the strength to deal with this relationship. Good luck!

Hello: From your description, what I sense is that you both used to love each other, but now it's just in the past, right? According to the logic, you both had emotional affairs, right? But now she doesn't want to leave you, while you want to leave her. It's just that you don't love her anymore, right? Are you determined to break up now? If so, let's analyze from this perspective. Analyzing the problem: 1. She said she has developed stronger feelings for that guy, and you said then let's break up. (From your state of mind, I feel that you don't feel reluctant, nor are you angry. If that's the case, this breakup is basically done.) 2. You broke up that night, and the next day, she kept coming to you for reconciliation, saying that she misunderstood their friendship, that it was just a buddy type of relationship. But you can't accept it anymore, you think it's not the guy's fault, nor her fault, because love is between two people. (Although you say you can't accept it anymore, but in reality, you already don't love her anymore, right? Because you are so indifferent, love involves jealousy and blame, but you don't have that, right? You already don't love her, even if this incident hadn't happened, right?) 3. So you think it's a relationship problem. And you can't accept it in your heart. She keeps coming to you for reconciliation, but you keep refusing. One day, she came to your dormitory downstairs, and you stubbornly went back to your room. (From an emotional principle, it's understandable that you can't accept it. But the later part of the conversation, especially the way it sounds like a rational decision without love. If there's no love, then leave, that's also fine, not loving her anymore is great.) 4. She cried and started using the threat of self-harm, at that time you were too tired, that feeling, truly physically and mentally exhausted. In order to prevent any accidents, you compromised and temporarily got back together with her. But your heart was already dead. Now that you've graduated, how should you bring up the breakup? (Under those circumstances, anyone would compromise, after such a long time, her emotions should have calmed down, right? Just directly bring up the breakup, say you don't love her anymore. Graduation is already breakup season, it's normal. Don't tell well-intentioned lies, just admit that you don't love her anymore.) Face the problem: "We both had emotional affairs, and now I want to give up on her. How should I bring up the breakup?"~ Does she know about your emotional affair? If she does, then you're on equal footing, neither of you owe the other anything. If she doesn't know, she will have a sense of owing you, even if she doesn't love you as much anymore, she won't want to let go because she doesn't want to be seen as the bad person. Then you can tell her that you also had an emotional affair.~ If you want to give up, but don't know how to bring it up, if you're going to different cities, just gradually drift apart! If you're in the same city and she's still pursuing you aggressively, just express it directly, "I don't love you anymore, I want to break up." Any girl would understand the meaning of this sentence. Just be a responsible man and bring it up. Closing words: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you find someone you can cherish soon! If you have any specific concerns, feel free to send a private message!

Hello! This is a paragraph about the dynamics of a relationship. In the first half, your choices were wise, but in the second half, you clearly fell into a passive position, being led by someone else's threats. Her feelings towards others have become increasingly intense, and based on reason, it is unlikely that it is merely a "misunderstood friendship." The boundary between friendship and romantic love is actually very clear, just as no one would mistake a flashlight for a power generator. Her claims of misunderstandings can be boldly interpreted as being explicitly rejected by someone else, and in order to avoid losses from both sides in a short period of time, she chose to rekindle the old flame. Emotionally, you cannot accept her deviation, and rationally, you are well aware that such matters cannot be forced. In terms of action, you refuse to reconcile, and your perspective on the whole situation is clear and insightful. The situation did not end because of your clear attitude; the other party has entered a state of crying and threatening self-harm, pressuring you to re-enter the game with her. Firstly, this has depleted your energy and spirit, and then, in a state of exhaustion and unable to fight back, you automatically raised the white flag. "In order to avoid trouble," you have been successfully held hostage by her fragile facade. Now, how do you untangle yourself? Even if she knows clearly that your agreement to reconcile is temporary, for the sake of pride and face, she is unlikely to calmly accept that you have suddenly changed your mind again. If you take control of her life, it is equivalent to committing to responsibility. It is not advisable to break up in the midst of conflict and intense emotions. If you have no intention of fighting, then refrain from participating. Cold treatment can be a method. That is, first detach yourself from your emotions, maintain clear thinking and a firm attitude, and avoid being led by her emotions. Communicate calmly and honestly at the appropriate time. Avoid strong emotional stimulation, and do not force immediate resolution. Strategically withdraw step by step, otherwise, it will lead to a cycle of crying and being unable to escape. Compassion is often useless, and even compassion itself is pitiful. The morally righteous side in emotional entanglement is often controlled by others. Even if our willingness is strong, it is difficult to take responsibility for other people's actions. The worst thing is when our hearts are unwilling, yet we are powerless. Wishing you well!

question: No one can understand or support me. I feel like there is no place to accommodate me.
description: As I prepare for the postgraduate entrance exam, my boyfriend broke up with me because of the long distance between us. My parents also disapprove of my future plans. Whenever I am determined to do something, they will tell me their thoughts, criticize my past actions, and warn me about my plans. Instead of offering me encouragement and support, they tell me that I spent too much time on my phone in the past, so it will be difficult for me to pass the entrance exam this year. However, they also expect me to focus solely on getting admitted, and if I fail, to follow their instructions. It feels like no one understands or supports me. Every time I try to rely on myself, someone interferes. It's like I thought we could be together in the end, and I believed that by following the path I've chosen, I would eventually reach my goal. But it seems like there are always external influences, particularly from people close to me, that hurt me. Each time I encounter this, it feels like my support system crumbles, and I feel utterly shattered. It feels like there's no place that accepts me, understands me, and truly supports me, except for myself.

answers.answer_text: Hello, after carefully reading your question, I understand that when you are facing a major life decision, the person you love the most chooses to leave. You hoped for understanding from your parents, but their response was almost negating. This has greatly impacted you and even made you feel disappointed in the world, feeling as if you are not worthy of being accepted by it. Thinking about your experience reminds me of Mr. Yu Minhong in the movie "China's Partner", who kneeled on the ground after performing poorly in the college entrance exam, hoping for another chance from his family. He often self-deprecates in his lectures, saying that his girlfriend 'slept with' him before going abroad. As adults, we realize that the world does not operate according to the rules we imagined when we were younger. We may think that certain things should be a certain way, but they turn out differently. We believe that our loved ones should understand, support, and accept us, but the reality is that our loved ones are also ordinary people. They have their own joys, sorrows, anxieties, and pressures from life, and they may act in ways that conform to the pressures of reality. Returning to your question, your family proposes to follow their plan if you fail the exam. From another perspective, it could be seen as them supporting your plan to take the postgraduate entrance exam, but also wanting you to hear their plan in case you fail. However, when your family expresses this, it seems to make you feel as if they do not support you taking the exam and that they do not trust you. Does the support and trust of loved ones seem more important than what you currently want to do? In life, we often see that some students feel that studying is not for themselves, but for their parents. If their parents do not meet their requirements, they will attack their own studies and develop resistance towards learning. As adults, when we do the things we like, we can also fall into a similar pattern. Even though we are doing something we like, we always hope for our parents' complete approval, as if this will absolve us of responsibility for what we are doing. It is all because of our parents' lack of support that our goals cannot be achieved. (This might sound uncomfortable, but it is worth considering). Personal development occurs gradually from a sense of security to a sense of autonomy and eventually a sense of competence. In a secure environment, we try to interact with the real world and gradually accumulate a sense of accomplishment in a tolerant environment. We develop a sense of competence, feeling capable of dealing with reality. If we did not gain a sense of security and autonomy during our early lives, we may easily become trapped in the pursuit of security and autonomy later on. On one hand, we hope for support, but on the other hand, we worry about negative outcomes. We hope someone else can handle the uncertain future on our behalf. Regarding your boyfriend, is it possible that the breakup was due to communication problems between the two of you? If the relationship truly is not suitable, could breaking up be beneficial for both parties? Do you feel like there is no place where you can truly belong? Regarding your doubts, you may be falling into a self-defensive 'should' mindset. After graduating, Xiao Ming joined a start-up company. Due to the company's high survival pressure and high personal competency requirements, Xiao Ming was fired for failing to meet the assessment. This experience of being fired caused Xiao Ming to doubt himself, thinking that he is not suitable for working in a start-up company. He then broadened this belief to thinking he is not suitable for working in private companies at all, and eventually that he is not suitable for work in general. As a result, he became fearful of going to work and stayed at home. What was originally a relatively common work situation became magnified in his mind. This does protect him from harm by isolating himself from the outside world, but it also limits his growth and interaction with reality. I really like a quote from a teacher, "Change the world with actions, let the world change me with my mind." Everything we do is to obtain an ideal life, to change the world through our actions. However, the reality is that there are things we can control and things we cannot. Our minds need to develop the ability to flexibly respond to reality. The more complex our minds become (accepting multiple dimensions of the world, developing multi-dimensional strategies to deal with it), the better we can cope with the complex world. With our original intention in mind, let's embark on our journey home. We are together on the path of growth. I hope this helps and wish you good luck.

Hello, it seems that the original poster (OP) is feeling very depressed and hurt, and very lonely, as if there is no one, especially their family, supporting or approving of them. We all need the support, companionship, recognition, and encouragement of others, this is a normal need. When you want to pursue your goals and work hard for them, they cannot give you much and even discourage you. This reminds me of a term in psychology called "gaslighting," which is a form of invisible manipulation and harm, and it is most likely to occur between family members. Maybe they don't mean it on purpose, like the things your parents say to you, and it really hurts you, this feeling is real, but it seems like you can't refute them because they are your family, maybe what they say is indeed true. I see that you have a good plan for yourself, and you are a person with aspirations and energy. That's great! Remember: do not identify with criticism from anyone. When you are confused and wavering, ask yourself: who am I? What do I want? Advice: the most important thing to remember is that you are already an excellent, capable, and likable person, you don't need the approval of an idealized object. First, have the willingness and determination to leave, even if you don't actually need to leave. Secondly, clarify your goals, don't argue or explain, arguing means manipulation, and explaining can easily lead to a cycle of manipulation. Instead, always remember what you want in this relationship. Thirdly, rewrite your response, express your dissatisfaction and needs directly. For example: you always say I have bad memory due to menopause, which makes me feel inferior. If you say it again, I won't continue talking to you. If the other person continues to pester, just leave directly. Lastly, consider the future, focus on a future away from gaslighting, choose new relationships as a source of self-awareness, vitality, and happiness, and use your energy for goals and dreams that truly matter to you. In "Emotional Blackmail," it is written: the harm of this type of relationship lies in the loss of the victim's self-integrity—a healthy relationship should be based on mutual love, consideration for each other, and the desire for the other person's improvement; otherwise, it is harmful to both parties. Whenever, please believe in your own feelings, say "no" bravely, and firmly leave. Good luck, Qi Xiaoqi.

Seeing your title, my heart feels a pang of distress, which actually also happens to me from time to time. Because humans are social beings, we are almost inevitably influenced by the outside world. Currently, you are facing the "heartbreak" from an intimate relationship (your boyfriend) and the biased influence of your family (parents), along with the pressure of preparing for the postgraduate entrance examination. All of this has made you suddenly feel powerless and self-doubt. In fact, this is a normal reaction. Right now, you are temporarily stuck in a "quagmire." Various distressing memories from the past are being reenacted, causing you to lose direction and fall into deep pain. Actually, what you are troubled by is the "helpless version of yourself." Assuming that you truly cannot receive support from the people close to you, would you really become a different person? Actually, you are still yourself. Now, let's separate the "helpless version of yourself" from the true you. If it were the true you facing the same difficulties, what attitude and mindset would you use to confront them? I hope that in your future life, you can use this statement to find clearer answers.

Hi, OP. I understand your helplessness. It seems that your parents always judge the plans you propose and expect you to do things their way. From their perspective, they believe their experiences and wisdom are more mature and reliable than yours, so they want you to follow their advice, which may be more conservative but safer. However, you are already at the stage of preparing for postgraduate examination, which means you are an adult with independent thoughts. But it's difficult for you to deal with your parents' worries and control. Breaking up with your boyfriend also feels like it's beyond your plan, as if neither love nor postgraduate examination is under your control, and it feels like nobody understands or supports you, and you feel very lonely. Have you only been accustomed to accepting your parents' opinions? In fact, you can express your true emotions and feelings to your parents and tell them that their actions have made you uncomfortable. You are already an adult who can take responsibility for your own life. If you lack a sense of recognition, you can also confide in a trusted friend. Friends can empathize with you and see things from your perspective. But the most important thing is to strive for your own autonomy and make independent choices. Show your parents positive results of your decisions. When they see that you can lead a fulfilling life through your own choices, they might be more willing to compromise. Best wishes.

Long-distance relationships do put a strain on both individuals involved. However, if the other person is not even willing to make an effort, it means that they truly don't love enough. In a way, we should also be grateful to them because they made us realize that they are not the person we are searching for. For most parents, their expectations for their daughters are not very high. They may even want their daughters to follow their own plans for development. Therefore, when we present our own plans, they don't always consider our perspective. Instead, they point out our shortcomings and believe that we haven't truly understood ourselves. And when we fail, they are quick to tell us that we wouldn't have faced so many problems if we had followed their path. However, we are not machines; we have our own thoughts and considerations. So, when others fail to understand us, we need to learn to understand ourselves first. For example, we pursue higher education to find a better platform, which can provide us with more opportunities. So, regardless of success or failure, let's focus on experiencing the pursuit itself rather than thinking about the ultimate outcome. We can choose to ignore some of the doubts and judgments from the outside world because, until we succeed, all explanations can be seen as mere excuses. And perhaps, their attitude will change once we do succeed. Therefore, we need to temporarily shield ourselves from external distractions. For instance, we can find a relatively quiet place to study and minimize external influences. Of course, if there are any unhappy events, we can also confide in this place. The person who loves us the most may not necessarily be the one who understands us best. But it's important for us to know what we truly want to do. The world and I love you.

question: A 30-year-old man wants to get a divorce, but he cannot escape from his responsibilities. This is not the life I want.
description: I am 30 years old this year. After quarreling with my wife over trivial matters at the age of 26, we got divorced. In 2019, considering the healthy growth of our child, we decided to remarry. However, we still cannot enter into a marital state. I want to get divorced again, but I can't escape my family responsibilities. I feel troubled and oppressed, this is not the life I want.
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, divorce, marriage management

answers.answer_text: First of all, let's give a big hug to the person asking the question, as we can feel their distress. I turned 30 this year and got divorced from my wife four years ago, when I was 26, due to trivial matters. Looking at the outcome, it is regrettable, but from a psychological growth perspective, do you still love her? Managing a marriage may require more than just love, it also requires great tolerance and understanding. If it was really just a minor issue, I think it might not necessarily have led to the current result. This question is worth deep contemplation together (are there deep-seated differences in character and values?). In 2019, considering the healthy growth of our child, we decided to remarry, but we still couldn't enter into a marital state. I want to get divorced again, but I can't escape the responsibilities of the family. I feel frustrated and suppressed, which is not the life I want. Every marriage deserves blessings. As the saying goes, it is better to try to reconcile than to encourage separation. However, from a psychological perspective, a continuing unhappiness in a marriage may cause greater harm than the consequences of divorce to the children. Children are the product of the love between two people. When you hold each other's hands and make vows regardless of poverty, illness, or adversity, have all those sweet and romantic moments disappeared? Perhaps you and your wife can seek further counseling from a marriage consultant, and if you really don't want to continue, then don't force it. I hope the above is helpful. Every couple experiences countless challenges. I've even imagined separating from my partner countless times in my mind. But from a behavioral perspective, love is an action, not just a feeling. If you really still want to save the relationship, everything is still possible.

Actually, parents' love for their children is not because they love them and take care of them, but because they take good care of them that makes you love them. Similarly, if you no longer have feelings for your wife and don't love her anymore, there are generally two situations: either you expect her to love you, or you don't love her enough. The original poster says that the current marital situation is not the life they want. I wonder what kind of life the original poster wants? As long as you know what kind of marital status you want, as long as you can communicate openly and honestly with your partner, it is entirely possible to achieve your ideal life status. Here are a few methods for reference: First, establish a sense of family ritual, such as celebrating each family member's birthday, organizing regular family gatherings at fixed times, and engaging in brief daily communication after dinner. The more you care about the little things in life, the stronger the connection you can build in an intimate relationship. Second, clarify each other's roles in life. When both husband and wife agree on their roles, it will promote the development of the relationship and avoid boundary issues caused by unclear roles. For example, for a family with children, when both the father and mother have the same views on parenting and are willing to take responsibility, the marital life will gain more meaning. Third, share your personal goals with your partner. This not only makes the marriage more intimate, but also promotes the realization of goals. Whether it's a man or a woman, everyone is pursuing excellence, and no one likes a partner who has no goals or pursuits. As for the different aspects of your marriage, such as dreams and goals, there is no need to pursue consensus, it can be different, but you need to accept and respect each other. For example, if you enjoy the present moment while your partner likes to plan ahead, as long as you accept each other's attitudes towards life, simply accepting can improve the marital relationship.

Hello OP: From your words, I can see your deep contradictions. You are a responsible father, but you have an unhappy relationship with your wife, and yet you chose to remarry for the sake of the child. Now that you're back in the marriage, you still want a divorce, so you're caught in endless confusion and bewilderment. I understand your feelings very well, and I hope the following words can help you. 1. Find the reasons why you can't enter the marital state You mentioned that before, you divorced your wife mainly due to quarrels over trivial matters. If the quarrels over trivial matters do not involve principled issues, maybe for this reason, you are willing to remarry for the sake of the child. So what about now? What are the reasons why you can't enter the marital state after remarrying? In fact, there are many reasons why a couple's relationship is not harmonious and they cannot enter the marital state. If the issues causing disharmony can be repaired, then life can still go on. For example, a wife complains that her husband is not considerate of the family and does not take good care of the child; or the wife's tension with her parents-in-law leads to a tense atmosphere with her husband, if they can move out and live separately or ask the parents-in-law to return to their hometown, the problem can be solved. But if the husband is always abusive, or if both parties have extramarital affairs, then it involves principled issues. If it is not a principled issue, if you are willing to make concessions for the sake of the child, to make changes for each other, the relationship between husband and wife can actually improve one day. After all, marriage is different from being in love, it requires mutual adjustment. I suggest that you communicate well with your wife and find out where the problems lie. If these problems cause less pressure on you than the love for your child, then I believe that in the future, there is a possibility of repairing your relationship. Therefore, if you feel that you cannot enter the marital state, you may as well sort out the reasons first and see if there is a possibility of remedy. 2. Weigh the pros and cons based on the current situation, is it better for the child if you divorce, or if you don't? Children are their parents' soft spot, and many parents choose to swallow grievances in the marriage for the sake of their children. Many parents believe that as long as mom and dad are with the child, they are good to the child, but they don't realize that the child actually wants their parents to be happy. If the atmosphere at home is filled with constant arguing or silent treatments, the harm that the child suffers from being in that environment is greater than if they were just with one parent. Finally, what I want to tell you is to find the real reason behind your marital disharmony and see if both of you can make changes to resolve these problems. When you find the reason, then ask yourself if the marriage should continue. Best wishes.

question: After three years of divorce, we have been sleeping in separate rooms. How can I reconcile with my ex-wife?
description: After divorcing for three years, we have been living together, but in separate rooms. Now, I really want to reconcile, but my ex-wife does not agree. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: I cannot make predictions about the possibility of you and your ex-wife getting back together because I don't know more about your situation, and this idea is currently yours alone. You should find time to talk to her about it. If you have children, you can mention the idea of getting back together for the sake of their growth and a complete family, but always respect your ex-wife's opinion. If you feel that your ex-wife no longer wants to reconcile or wants to start a new relationship, then you should not force it. There is a saying: if a woman leaves you, it means she truly doesn't love you anymore. Women are very devoted in relationships, once they make up their minds, they won't easily give up, but if they do, they will be determined and not easily turn back. I hope you can handle this matter with the right approach. Meeting and getting married again is your fate, but you should let go when it's time to. I wish you a smooth life. Best wishes.

question: 19-year-old girl, recently feeling really upset and don't know why.
description: A few days ago, it started (previously planned to go to Hebei Province in July to see a classmate, but the plan might be ruined due to the pandemic, and my parents have been talking about it. I don't know if that's the reason for feeling upset or if there's something else. Then, I became even more unhappy since yesterday, dissatisfied with everything. I just wanted to play games to relax, but ended up being blamed. Suddenly, I broke down and started crying, and the thought of taking sleeping pills suddenly came to my mind. I'm a bit scared and don't know what to do. I want to become happier.
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. It's a coincidence that I'm also 19 years old and have had a similar experience. After the college entrance exam last year, I wanted my parents to take me on a trip, the three of us together. But it never happened. First, we argued because of my exam score, then because of choosing my major, and then because of studying vocabulary. I mentioned wanting to go out and play, and then my dad shouted at me, and in the end, we didn't go anywhere. After starting college, I felt really sad about the research I was doing, and I wanted to make an appointment for counseling, but they said I had to wait until Friday, and it was only Tuesday at the time. I had no one to talk to about my sorrows. I wanted to play a game called "King of Glory" to distract myself, but I got criticized for being bad at it. It was a really helpless feeling. In reality, when we feel down, it's often not because of one specific thing. When your emotions are low, you become very sensitive and feel like everything is not going well recently. You feel like everyone is happy and can't understand you. When you wear sunglasses, everything looks dark; when you're unhappy, everything around you seems gloomy. OP, think about it, when you're in a good mood and playing games with classmates, do you care if someone criticizes you? You might just brush it off as friendly banter with your classmates. So, this situation with your emotions is normal. Sometimes when I feel sad, I also think, what's the point of living when I feel so down? Maybe everyone has thought about taking sleeping pills to end it all; it's not that scary, and it's just a way to vent your emotions when you're feeling low. Negative emotions also serve a purpose. Perhaps this experience will make you stronger, and when you look back a few years later, you might say, "Ah, I was so immature back then." Hang in there, OP!

Hello, thank you for the warm hug and invitation! I had been planning to go to Hebei in July. I had some rough and even detailed plans, and I was looking forward to this "trip". But now everything has to be put on hold, and I can't help but feel disappointed. On top of that, my parents have been talking about it, which has made me even more upset and down. Hugs to you. I had also planned to have hot pot on the weekend, but I couldn't go because something came up, and I ended up crying. There are many meanings behind this sadness. I feel sad about my plans falling through, about my arrangements not being appropriate, about feeling out of control in this situation and being upset about it. I have some isolated and unresolved emotions. But don't be afraid, this is normal. It's also normal to have feelings of collapsing, or to think about taking sleeping pills. But it also reveals that I'm afraid of losing control and have poor coping abilities. In fact, as the saying goes: change is the only constant. We should try to accept small changes in life. Things will not always go exactly as we imagine. It's okay to be upset and let out our anger. After venting, we can continue with our lives. This year, we need to prioritize our physical health. As a person from Hebei, we welcome you to visit anytime!

question: If I eat too much and then take laxatives, I don't know if I have developed binge-eating disorder.
description: Hello, I used to lose about 20 kilograms through diet and exercise. Now I weigh 86 kilograms and I am very thin, but I am still quite strict with myself. Previously, I was eating quite normally, and my diet was also controlled, but recently I have been indulging in high-calorie foods such as bread and cake, and eating quite a lot. After eating, I would take laxatives and take a large amount of medication to help eliminate it, and then I would try to filter out the fact that I took the medication in my mind and convince myself that I didn't take anything. Every time I eat, I tell myself that it's the last time. I am very concerned about my weight and I may weigh myself every day. I can't bear gaining even a little weight, and lately I feel like I have lost control over my eating. I crave sweets and when I eat a lot, I would take laxatives. The next day, I won't eat anything at all, only drink water. I am starting to think that I may have a binge eating disorder or some other problem.
keywords: Behavior, hypochondria, binge eating and dieting.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! First of all, I'm really happy for you. It's great to see that you have achieved your ideal weight through your hard work. Could it be due to recent stress? And what is the reason for choosing high-calorie foods? Do you simply find them delicious, or do they give you some other kind of feeling? We first need to understand the reason behind your sudden indulgence in order to better solve the problem. If it's simply a matter of having a "craving," we can look for other snacks that are suitable for fitness enthusiasts - low in calories and healthy. On the other hand, weight and dietary control is a good habit, but many people tend to fall into the trap of pursuing "being light and thin" excessively. We must approach the issue of weight reasonably and strive for a healthy weight rather than simply pursuing a low weight, as it is not beneficial for our health. It may be helpful for you to seek professional help or consult with professionals to assess your condition and develop a weight control plan that suits you. If you still find it difficult to control your impulse to eat high-calorie foods, it may be helpful to seek assistance from people around you, allowing external forces or third parties to help you overcome your impulses. question: I am approaching the age of 60 and I detest my mother's control. How can I break free from it?
description: I am almost 60 years old, but my mother still calls me every day, saying that I need to take care of her because she's getting old. She started saying this when I was 30 years old, and my brother has always been taking care of her. Hearing this, I became less and less willing to go home, and my heart drifted further away.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication

answers.answer_text: Hello! You are nearly 60 years old, and your mother must be at least 80 years old. According to common sense, this is the time to show filial piety. But you haven't said why you are unwilling to take care of your elderly mother. Is it just because she calls you every day asking for your care? We are not here to make moral judgments. Perhaps you have your own difficulties. Maybe you had a difficult relationship with your mother in your childhood, or maybe you just don't like her and find her old age and constant nagging annoying. But there is no way around it; in life, there are many responsibilities that we must bear. Taking care of our parents is a legal obligation for everyone unless they have seriously abandoned, abused, or harmed them, and have had their parental rights revoked. Otherwise, the obligation to support our parents cannot be waived. So, facing an elderly mother, we need to be more understanding and tolerant, and understand how difficult it is for a mother to raise her children. Understanding the psychological characteristics of the elderly is important. For the elderly, the biggest change is loss - loss of beauty, loss of health, loss of social status, loss of the ability to earn money - in short, their constant experience is one of loss. As the elderly age, they will experience more physical problems, which can lead to illness. The feeling of loneliness in old age becomes increasingly noticeable, and it is easy for them to develop mental illnesses. Growing old is pitiful, and everyone will experience old age one day, when the care and companionship of children become even more important. With understanding, perhaps in the last days of your mother's life, your companionship can thaw the emotional knots in your heart that have built up over the years, bringing you closer to her and achieving reconciliation with both her and yourself. Best wishes! The above are just some of Red Rain's insights, hoping they can be helpful to you. If you find them useful, please remember to click "Useful." Thank you for your question.

question: After graduation, should you first look for a job or find a boyfriend?
description: After graduation, should one first find a stable job and then find a boyfriend and get married, or should one go with the flow? Should one take a suitable job if one comes across it? Should one start a relationship if one finds a suitable partner?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Have you already answered the question you raised yourself? That is, "Just go with the flow, find suitable jobs and partners."## There's no need to plan your life too strictly. Being too strict with your life plans may cause you to miss out on some beautiful things. Of course, you can start now to make yourself better, so that you will have more qualifications to find a better job in the future and meet a better version of yourself. The above is my suggestion, hope it can help you. Best wishes!

question: Every day at work is very unpleasant, how can I break free from this quagmire and regain happiness?
description: My job is based on commission. The base salary is relatively low, and the company's commission rate has gradually decreased from 40% to 10% now, and sometimes even less than 10%. The take-home pay has also decreased from the original 7k to just over 4k. The profits from the products I previously accumulated are no longer counted as mine. I feel very angry, anxious, and disgusted with the company's unpredictable behavior. I want to quit and I'm preparing for it. But right now, I'm feeling down and lacking confidence. I don't know how to become happy again. I request my friends to comfort and advise me.
keywords: Occupation, career management, work pressure, job fatigue.

answers.answer_text: #I feel very angry, anxious, and disgusted by the company's behavior of changing its mind and making decisions without consulting you. #The company changes its tune without any discussion and simply issues announcements? Can I understand it this way too? This kind of behavior from the company is indeed disrespectful to you, and that is the fundamental reason for your anger. #The salary has also decreased from the original 7k to just over 4k. This change is also the source of your anxiety, right? It means you have to bear the risk of uncertainty in the future. Choosing to stay means you have to endure the company's ever-changing behavior, along with the accompanying anxiety, anger, and possibly other things that might happen later. But you can set a deadline for yourself, like three months, and if there is no improvement by then, you can consider quitting and looking for other opportunities. The benefit of doing this is not having to face the hassle of changing jobs, although switching jobs also comes with its own risks. For example, the salary and benefits offered by the new company, the unknown work environment, and adapting to a new company's policies. Choosing to switch jobs means you have to bear the risk of changing jobs and may encounter similar problems as with your current company. You also need to evaluate your overall competitiveness, whether your strengths will still be relevant in a different job. You will also have to accept that your salary may not necessarily improve, and there will be a certain transition period. But you may have to spend a lot of time evaluating the company, and at the same time, the company will be evaluating you. You may also encounter situations similar to the current company... The benefit of doing this is that you may find a job that suits your needs and encounter many new opportunities. You have always had choices, but you need to realize that behind every choice, there are costs and risks. And the more information you gather, the more detailed your analysis of the costs and benefits of each choice will be.

I feel that the source of your anger is not only due to a decrease in income, but also more so because of the company's lack of "credibility." What's even more contemptible is that you have nowhere to reason with this "lack of credibility." You can't find a proper place or way to vent, so on one hand, you suppress yourself, and on the other hand, you express your anger and resistance indirectly by resigning. Although this expression partially relieves your anger, it also makes your instincts vaguely feel uneasy, coming from the uneasiness of reality... Originally, the intermittent COVID-19 epidemic this year has already caused pressure on the overall social environment. Coupled with the repression you are currently facing, the pressure of finding a new job, it's natural for your mood to be poor. When you're in a bad mood, forcing yourself to be happy is actually inhumane. Respect your own feelings, make some preparations for "tomorrow" that you can think of, and confidence will naturally slowly build up, and happiness will gradually return. Best wishes!

Due to the impact of the epidemic, many companies have indeed been adjusting the benefits and treatment of their employees, so we can objectively analyze it. 1. Are the lower commissions for all employees or targeted? If it is for all employees and the company has provided a reasonable explanation, although the practice may not be acceptable, as long as the company's development prospects are still good, as long as we can get through this cold winter, there is still a possibility of a comeback, we can understand it. If it is only for some employees, it may be a disguised way of laying off employees. After all, such salaries are unacceptable to many people. After all, the cost of layoffs and voluntary resignation are different. In this case, we need to be rational. If it is a comprehensive change for all employees but the company no longer has development opportunities, then we can prepare in advance because when disaster strikes, everyone is on their own. 2. An immutable company has its own processes and systems, and these systems are not something we can easily change, so when encountering such things, although it is helpless, we also need to be prepared for the worst. If the questioner himself has some savings and has accumulated resources and connections over the past few years, then we should have good development in another place, so we don't need to be too anxious because we still have a way out. If we don't have anything left, don't worry either. Take a few days to prepare well. If there is a suitable opportunity, seize it, after all, there are always more solutions than difficulties. The world loves you.

Hello, to understand the overall situation of the company, if it is doing well, everyone can benefit from it; if it is not doing well, we can only make do with less. Only when this pattern deviates, should we consider how to respond, either by demanding better treatment or by finding another job that offers market prices. In sales, it depends on your importance. In some companies, 2-3 core salespeople can account for 80% of the performance. They walk in and out of the company like big shots and the boss has to please them. In other companies, everyone does similar sales work and anyone can be replaced at any time. Even if they were given a sweet deal initially, it will eventually be taken back. Some commission bonuses are only made as an investment to boost sales initially and are not meant to last. Cost-cutting is a skill that every company needs to practice. Sales is a position with a large income disparity. So, it is better for you, the original poster, to focus on improving future performance. Only top performers have the right to confront the boss.

Hello, OP! From your description, it seems that you are dissatisfied, angry, and anxious about the current adjustment of your salary, as well as the situation at your company. You are also considering preparing to quit your job. I can see that you are going through a tough time, sending you a virtual hug! You also mentioned that you are feeling down and lacking confidence. I would like to understand if you are concerned about finding a new job after quitting?

question: Because the worldly values are too cheap, I feel strongly that I want to attain liberation.
description: Currently, I have the following future choices: psychologist, artist, writer, master's degree holder, and pilgrim. Then I realized that besides being a writer or a master's degree holder, all the other options require me to have a formal education to pursue further. Therefore, I don't want to go through the hassle anymore. I plan to find a lifeline and instantly leap to the highest point.
keywords: Growing up, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, thank you for the invitation. Psychologists, artists, writers, monks, and pilgrims. These are also things I like. It seems that we both belong to a category of people who focus on spiritual cultivation. Perhaps, like me, you are very ambitious and therefore often set "high standards strict requirements" for yourself, so you are very prone to self-blame and self-esteem, and I used to be particularly concerned about what others think... These "inborn" traits derived from life experiences often make us feel sensitive in the fields of psychology, art, and other spiritual accomplishments, so we increasingly like to pursue things on the spiritual level. The problem is that you and the "expected self" need to reconcile. I don't know if you like the concept of "parallel universes," which means that in another time and space, another "identical me" lives a completely different life from me. That me in that time and space, is the life I yearn for deep down. That me in that time and space, is the me I have been anticipating. So, the me at this moment is just a very unsatisfactory "existence," and the current life is simply not worth living... I have had such a split before, and I also feel that if I kill the me in "this time and space," perhaps the me in another time and space will become real... Whenever I encounter difficulties, I can't help but imagine this. And so, I continue to live in this way, at odds with myself... until a friend I have been dating for over a decade was unfortunately hit by a drunk driver while on a business trip, leaving behind a 5-month-old child, but did not have time to say a word... Everything just came to a "crashing halt"... I may still not have come out of the shadow of his death, my heart still hurts... The real death has shown me only his "abrupt end," the world goes on as usual, just with one less him... I don't know if it was from that shock and pain, but suddenly I no longer envy the me in parallel universes and other possible lives... I started to believe in fate, I started to believe in hard work, I started to greedily enjoy every bite of food, I started to intentionally cherish every moment of joy: the scent of flowers, the sound of birds singing, the dappled light and shade under the trees, the smile of a child, the warmth given by a stranger, understanding the mother's difficulties... Everything mundane, rare, difficult, with laughter and tears in life... all those are what my friend can no longer touch, an incredibly cruel reality. My parallel universe shattered and fell apart, after I started living seriously, wanting to live as two true selves. One for myself and one for my friend who will never live again. I am still far, far away from being a psychologist, artist, or author, but now I think seeing my own smile in the mirror is not important. I have made peace with myself, and now I am my best self. It doesn't matter if I haven't become the person I wanted to be. No matter what I look like, I will love myself well. Being alive itself is a difficult practice. I hope you can also grow from it slowly, it's already great if you can keep going.

question: I keep thinking about the mistakes I made in the past, how can I adjust my mindset?
description: Just as I feel that nothing has changed, my classmates around me have gone from being friendly at the beginning to pretending not to see me and constantly reminding me of the mistakes I made in the past. I always feel more depressed.

answers.answer_text: I would also do this, and my visitors would do this too. My visitors have even asked me, "Do you ever think about the past or blame yourself?" I said yes because I'm just a regular person. I think about the mistakes I've made in the past and have regrets about certain things. However, I still try to focus on the present! So, I believe it's not a problem to think about the past, but considering it a problem is the actual problem! 1. You treat your classmates with an unchanging attitude as if they're not very friendly. In other words, you expect them to be friendlier towards you, right? Have you talked to them about your relationship, interests, or attitudes towards interpersonal relationships? 2. You always think about the mistakes you've made. It was mentioned earlier, but here's an additional point: if you keep thinking about it, why not try to feel your emotions and thoughts in the process, and try to have a dialogue with yourself? 3. You feel oppressed. Is there something that you're dissatisfied with but can't let go? Find a hobby for yourself, like singing, painting, or writing, or even find a place where no one is around and scream, anything goes. Of course, the important thing is to be able to express yourself in words when you're emotional. For example, when you're angry, instead of smashing things or making others angry, learn to express your feelings in words and tell others how you feel. In conclusion, I hope you can express your emotions, seize the present, and study with peace of mind.

Hello, thank you for the invitation. Are you describing a situation that occurs when you start school or transfer to a new school? When people establish and maintain relationships in various scenarios, there are generally stages such as the "honeymoon period" and the "ordinary period" - when meeting new people, individuals often make an effort to show their enthusiasm and goodness, with a tendency to present themselves in a certain way, in order to make a good first impression. As people become more familiar with each other, they gradually relax, and their true selves will be revealed more often. If acquaintances always act like they are meeting for the first time, the cost of the interaction becomes too high and life becomes too exhausting. "Pretending not to see" is a strategy - it's too troublesome to greet the same person multiple times in a day. So it's not necessarily something you did wrong, and continually thinking about possible "mistakes" may itself be a mistake. It is better to focus your attention on studying. Are you feeling depressed due to this "indifferent" social environment? Is it because you were used to being "cared for" at home and now feel "lost" at school, leading to depression? If so, you can try to work hard and achieve outstanding results to make yourself shine. This way, you will have the opportunity to be respected outside of your family, and this is a pursuit in life - "winning respect".

question: 19-year-old female, recently feeling confused. Am I supposed to feel ashamed about something like this?
description: Recently, I have seen a lot of exposés of indecent videos involving female and male college students, as well as news about some women who have fallen into unfortunate situations. It confuses and upsets me, especially when I see videos related to female college students because I am also a college student and a girl. It makes me feel ashamed, as if being labeled with a stigma. Once these things are exposed, the headlines directly label women and college students in a certain way. I feel ashamed and confused about why people would engage in such activities when they have hands, feet, and decent intelligence. Isn't it better to earn money through legitimate means? Seeing many outstanding women and comparing myself to them, my mood inexplicably becomes low and I feel down.
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, the main questioner, nice to meet you. From your statement, it is not difficult to see that you are a person with your own beliefs, and you acknowledge that you can exchange your life through your own labor and efforts. As for feeling puzzled and upset about seeing "bad news about female college students," one reason is that you cannot understand their concept of money and life values ​​and another reason is that you feel that you may have some biases and stereotypes against them. In every industry, there are people who want to seek so-called "shortcuts" to reach their goals, just taking different approaches. However, the news actually amplifies certain characteristics of this group of people or makes generalized generalizations, so what we see is: what are college students like, or what are women like. This itself uses some stereotypes to arouse readers' more extreme emotions, thus attracting more readership. In fact, any industry has ways to take shortcuts, and relatively objective and rational ones are actually able to generate quite a bit of feedback, even the insults themselves generate traffic. So it's good to understand that the real world is not as one-sided as the news portrays, remain objective and rational without overly identifying, and there is no need to feel ashamed of your identity, as you have not done anything wrong. Adjust your cognition and focus on doing your best. 1. There are many identities in the world, and many people play these roles, and their personalities, upbringing, etc., are all different, so the interpretations of the same identity are also different. In this process, some people may not stick to their true selves and may make some irrational behaviors. However, this does not mean that everyone with this identity is the same as him/her. It is not uncommon for the news to magnify and define certain situations for the sake of clicks and readership. At this point, we need to rationally and objectively distinguish which things are worth being vigilant about and which are manufactured anxieties. 2. If you disagree with the actions of certain college students and girls, then take it as a reminder: tell yourself to stick to your own goals and gain through labor. 3. As for feeling down when seeing certain outstanding women, it is suggested to find the reason that suits you and ask yourself what you think when you see them: maybe you think of the girls in the news; maybe you think of your own efforts? However, no matter what, being outstanding is always a benchmark, a framework set by the external environment. Not all women can become so-called "outstanding women," but every girl has the opportunity to become a person who can deal with everything in her life, someone who strives and is optimistic. Best wishes~ a little mushroom that hopes for a gentle world and gives itself time to grow freely.

question: It's the third year of high school, and I want to study hard, but why do I find it hard to calm down?
description: Since high school, my grades have been consistently declining. At first, I didn't pay much attention to it, but later on, my performance suddenly plummeted, and I haven't been able to improve it since. Now, I'm already in my senior year, and I feel like I haven't been putting much effort into studying these past two years. Now, when I try to study hard, I find that I can't focus at all. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. Calmly analyze the reasons for your current state and start with things you can do to slowly get back on track and resume normal studying and living. From your description, it is clear that you are feeling anxious and troubled because of declining grades in your senior year. You want to improve your grades but find it difficult to concentrate. It is apparent that you are aware of the reasons, namely not putting your mind at ease for studying. So, where is your mind focused instead? Are those things important to you? How do you plan to improve your grades in your senior year? Specifically, what are your daily plans and schedules? When you feel agitated and unable to study, how do you adjust yourself? Don't avoid the problem, nor give yourself too many excuses. Recognize the things you can do, then take practical steps to tranquilize yourself, reduce anxiety, and take action, which is the best way to alleviate anxiety. Give yourself a certain plan, seek help from those who can assist you, do your best, don't dwell on the results, and treat it seriously step by step. Maybe because you haven't put effort into studying, collect your thoughts and diminish some desires and increase resistance to temptation. Make a plan and stick to it. In the beginning, it might be very painful and difficult to endure, and there might be moments of restlessness, just like now. That's okay. Let yourself learn as much as you can, and try your best to do it. The backlog of studying from the past two years cannot be changed overnight. Slow down, don't be impatient, it won't help. Adjust your mindset, and if you really need help, you can seek assistance from classmates with good grades or teachers to help you sort out your mindset and quickly get back into the groove. Take studying seriously, as well as rest and exercise, and do your best in the final year. Good luck.

question: How to relieve work pressure and anxiety in the mind?
description: 1. Just started working for almost half a year, I can't balance work and life. The company says it's from 10am to 6pm, but they also emphasize task-oriented work, which means a lot of overtime without extra pay. It makes me feel like I have no space for personal life. 2. Moreover, many things I encounter at work are new to me, so I end up spending much more time than planned, making it feel like work has no end in sight. 3. Career development is also troubling me because I can only work at this company for one year due to personal reasons. I'm worried that I won't be able to find a suitable job after leaving. 4. The stress from work has caused new health issues for me, which terrifies me and makes me feel hopeless. However, I won't give up on the job I have chosen for the next few years, and I won't switch to a government job or become a teacher. I want to know how to help myself with psychological development or how to better organize my life.
keywords: Occupation, career management, work stress, work fatigue

answers.answer_text: A valuable job that gives individuals a sense of achievement and fulfillment is likely to help them overcome difficulties. The key is to believe that the hard work is worth it, so that the difficulties and pressure appear bearable in the face of significant benefits. The three points mentioned earlier by the author are all aspects of work that are unbearable. However, the author mentions in the last point that they will not give up in the coming years due to personal choice. Why can't they give up? Is it because this job itself has great value to them? Do they feel that their own worth can be realized, or can they receive good rewards, or do they feel that they are very suitable for this job and receive praise from others? Or is it because they fulfill their own values, such as helping others and contributing to society? What do they think is most important in their life? Does their current job help them achieve their goals? Let me give you a few examples from my own experience. When I was a student, I interned at a foreign company, and my supervisor was a workaholic. He worked until late at night every day and started working early in the morning, but he seemed to be filled with energy. Every time he talked about his work and his vision, he was full of passion and enthusiasm. He said that he had built up this company from scratch and he was determined to make it a leading company. In order to maintain energy for work, he went to the gym at six in the morning every day to exercise. He said that he couldn't bear such high-intensity work if he didn't exercise. For him, work was the most important thing. It could be said that he merged with it, and he was striving for himself. Another friend of mine who is a counselor faced a lot of pressure in the early stages of her career. She often dealt with visitors who had serious mental illnesses and even suicidal tendencies. What a tremendous responsibility it was. To some extent, other people's lives depended on her. She was under a lot of pressure, but fortunately, she was very good at her job and she had her own mission, which was to do her best to help others. In the face of such a mission and values, she also couldn't give up her job, because this was what she wanted, and valuable things often come with risks and pressure. In both of the above examples, they were not just working for the sake of work, but to achieve a purpose and pursue what they wanted. They were doing exactly what they wanted to do, and it was valuable to them, so the risks and pressure could be tolerated. If you ask them to do something that they are not willing to do and that has no meaning to them, then who would be willing to endure such great pressure for no reason? So, the author should first ask if this job is really of such great value to them. If it is just a mechanical job and does not have much meaning to them, then giving up may also be an option. Perhaps finding something that you are truly willing to put effort into will make everything less difficult. Of course, career planning is a complex issue, seeking help from a professional career planner may also be a good idea.

Hello, after carefully reading your description, I can roughly understand your current situation. You have a job that always requires overtime and you can't see any prospects. Additionally, your colleagues are also falling ill, which makes you feel uncertain. However, you don't plan to quit and all these problems are making you feel uneasy. So, I'll provide you with some small strategies that you can use to further improve your situation. First, you need to relax and think about the positive aspects of your job. I'm sure there must be some, such as the salary or the alignment with your expertise. Think about the good aspects and also list your own strengths, such as being responsible, having a strong sense of duty, and being enthusiastic about learning. Write down ten of these strengths. Once you've completed the list, I think your mood will improve. Recently, I've been reading some books on positive psychology and attending lectures. They often mention that successful and responsible individuals tend to focus on their weaknesses and areas where they have yet to reach their goals. However, in reality, we should focus on how we can become happier and more relaxed. Happy people are adaptable; they may not be perfect, but they can identify their advantages and disadvantages, and strive to fulfill their potential. As a result, they are content. This can be a reference for you: relax completely and tap into your potential. Secondly, when you have a better mindset, you can consider your job from a different perspective. For example, if the company has clearly defined working hours and unless your immediate supervisor asks you to work overtime, you can leave on time. I believe that's according to the contract, and HR cannot say anything about it. Unless there are unspoken rules in your workplace, such as everyone working overtime, as long as your immediate supervisor and HR have no objections, you can leave on time, as we cannot always be stuck there, which is also not efficient and creates a vicious cycle. If you find it difficult to complete your work, you can enhance your learning. For instance, read books or seek advice from senior colleagues with humility. This will help improve your work efficiency, so don't rush. The third point is about building good relationships with colleagues, as having a good working environment is important. While performance is crucial, the degree of harmony with the people around us may be even more important for our long-term work. You can give it a try. The fourth point is to build a solid support system outside of work, such as maintaining regular contact with family and friends. Find some hobbies or interests, such as playing sports or reading books, etc. It is essential to have your own leisure activities and arrange your life in a way that balances work and play, so that you don't strain yourself too much. If a string breaks, and we don't have any other support systems, it's very easy for us to encounter problems. This could be a reason why your friend Hao fell ill, but you need to analyze the specific situation. These are the small pieces of advice I have for you. You can try them out based on your own situation. In any case, I hope you can have a positive mindset and overcome this soon. Good luck!

question: College student, recently my roommate is always together with my good friend?
description: My good friend is my roommate in my freshman year. Now we are interning and no longer live together in the dormitory. I have made a new friend in the new dormitory. At first, I thought he was very introverted, so I wanted him to hang out with me and my friend. However, I later noticed that whenever he saw my friend, he would warmly greet her, linking arms with her, but he never initiatively linked arms with me. I suddenly feel like my friend has been taken away from me, and that I have misjudged him.
keywords: Interpersonal, roommates and classmates, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hi there! I can totally understand how you feel. It must be disappointing for you to realize that despite your efforts to include your introverted friend, there may be some ulterior motives behind their actions. First of all, I suggest that you observe the situation for a while. "Actions speak louder than words." Is your friend really treating you as a friend or are they just coincidentally being friendly to someone else? How do they behave towards you? People's true intentions can be revealed over time, and I believe you will be able to sense their sincerity and warmth in certain details. I think after spending some time getting to know them better, you will have an answer deep down inside. Alternatively, you can choose to have an honest conversation with them. It seems like you already have this concern and worry in your mind, and expressing your thoughts might provoke a response from them. However, the premise of communication is "whether you trust the other person." Do you believe in the response they give you, or do you trust your own feelings more? I hope you consider this carefully. From a different perspective, if your friend does indeed have ulterior motives, it can further prove the authenticity of your original friendship. Have you discussed your concerns with your friend? Are they still the same as they used to be towards you? Through comparison, you might be able to see the true colors of the people around you and appreciate them more. Throughout life, we encounter people of all sorts, whether they genuinely consider us as friends or have their own hidden motives. I hope you can approach this with a calm mind. Take care!

Hello, because your roommate has become closer with your good friend, you may feel a sense of discrepancy and disappointment in your heart, and this is a normal psychological reaction. Trust is very important in interpersonal relationships, and timely communication is also an effective way to maintain friendship. Therefore, I would like to give you a few suggestions in the hope of helping you solve the problem and alleviate your mental distress! Take the initiative to communicate with your roommate and good friend: be open about your inner thoughts and hope to gain support and understanding. Timely communication can effectively resolve issues, help you open up, become closer, and better understand each other's personalities and ways of dealing with things, making your future interactions more comfortable and harmonious. Adjust your mindset: they are both your good friends, so you can try to establish friendship among the three of you, without feeling ignored due to oversensitivity. Give your friends enough trust and have confidence in yourself. Learn to be alone and focus more on yourself: each of us is an independent individual, and while we need friends, we also need to have the ability to enjoy being alone. We have the right to choose our own way of life and choose a comfortable lifestyle for ourselves. In life, we will meet many people, and we walk together with like-minded friends. Good relationships require maintenance, understanding, and trust. At the same time, we also need to recognize the importance of being alone, improve ourselves, and make ourselves better. Believe that you can solve this problem well, and I wish the three of you can open your hearts and become closer. Your personal mental health consultant is by your side. May my words bring you warmth! I would also like to thank the occasional passing readers for reading. Feel free to follow me and click "Helpful"!

Title, hello! Your roommate always hangs out with your good friend, making you feel less close to your friend than before. This must make you feel a little disappointed! Friendships during college are precious, and good friendships are built slowly. Your good friend was previously your roommate in freshman year, and now your roommate has become your friend. While it may not be as close as your relationship with your good friend, to some extent, you have formed a friendship with each other. Between these two, you are both good friends to them. The reason why you feel disappointed is because they got close to each other because of you, but now they have become close to each other, which feels like your emotional territory has been invaded. It feels like your good friend has been stolen away by someone else, and this is a normal psychological reaction.
