It shows that while you care about your good friend, you also expect your good friend to belong to you. The enthusiasm of your roommate towards your good friend makes you feel like your emotions are being violated, and you had the intention of having them all hang out together, but your roommate's enthusiasm towards your good friend makes you feel ignored. I suggest that you communicate with your roommate and good friend together, express your feelings to them, and discuss the desired interaction pattern between friends. This will help you avoid shouldering this sense of disappointment alone. The three of you can enjoy playing together, occasionally getting closer or distancing yourselves, as it falls within the scope of your friendship. You can adjust your expectations for friendship appropriately. I hope you can have a comfortable relationship and mutual understanding with your roommate and good friend!

question: 19, how to deal with being easily irritable and only being able to calm down through self-harm?
description: I constantly feel that there are bugs crawling on my body, and I have difficulty sleeping. I am easily irritable, and if I suppress it, I can't control my trembling hands and numbness, and I can't speak. I have to bite myself to calm down. Now I have developed a habit of forcefully swallowing things to feel the sensation of them getting stuck in my throat. I have had this problem before, frequently washing my hands and self-harming to relieve stress, but I managed to stop. However, recently, this problem has reappeared.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I'm sorry to hear about your situation. I can understand how you must be feeling. It's easy to become irritable in daily life and not know how to control it. So, you turn to self-harm as a way to release the stress. However, even when you try to calm yourself down, the issue keeps coming back, which is very distressing. If the situation is severe, I suggest seeking professional help and receiving relevant treatment. You mentioned that the self-harming behavior resurfaces and, if repressed, you experience physiological reactions such as trembling hands and numbness, making it difficult to speak. Only through self-harm can you find temporary relief. If your situation is severe, I recommend seeking professional help as soon as possible to find the root cause of the problem and receive treatment. Look for other ways to vent your emotions and take care of yourself. Self-harm is a way to release emotions, but ultimately, it's not the best solution. It can cause significant harm to your body, leaving scars, and causing pain to those who care about you. Try finding less harmful ways to release your emotions, such as going for a run, exercising in a gym, or finding a quiet place to shout out your frustrations. In summary, engage yourself in activities that help you relax and don't get fixated on your current situation. Reflect on yourself when you are calm and without this irritability. Analyze why you experience such emotions and what factors ignite them. Is it because of accumulated negative emotions, excessive stress in your current life, or for some other reasons? Identify the root cause of your irritability and make adjustments in your daily life. Practice meditation, read books, travel, and make new friends to bring about fundamental changes in your mindset. Strive to lead a happier life and prevent the occurrence of irritability. Remember, your emotions are a reflection of your inner self. Only when you have a clear understanding and acceptance of yourself can you better resolve your problems. I wish you the best in overcoming your troubles and achieving a healthy state of mind.

Hello~ First, let me give you a big hug and I hope you can feel a little warmth. After reading your description, I feel really sorry for you. Being 19 years old, you should be happy and carefree. Promise me that you won't hurt yourself anymore. I hope my advice can help you a little bit. Try regulating yourself. The Jungian school of thought believes that self-harm has a long history in human development. In extreme group behavior, the opposite of primitive worship is "self-harm". Idealizing the other person and demeaning oneself, hoping for their pity, attention, and salvation. Actually, in the past month, I have also been irritable, easily getting angry over small things and snapping at people close to me. So, if you feel uncontrollable shaking or numbness in your hands when you suppress your anger, it might be because you're getting too angry but not releasing it. You can try using breathing techniques to relax a bit, and then choose some suitable exercises, such as jogging or skipping rope, to divert your attention. Maybe this situation will be alleviated. Learn to share. You can also consult a relevant psychological counselor to find out the reason and then find the appropriate remedy. No matter what, life is the most important thing, and you are also great, deserving all the beauty in the world. I wonder if you're willing to share some of your feelings with others usually? Actually, sometimes when we encounter annoying things, sharing with friends can make us feel a bit better. Whether it's joy or sadness, sharing can make us better. Don't put too much pressure on yourself. You mentioned that self-harm can relieve stress, but it might be because you're under too much pressure and don't know how to release it. So, why not make a daily plan that is achievable, and don't give yourself too many tasks, so as not to overwhelm yourself. "There is only one me in the world, everyone else is someone else," so sweetheart, you should love yourself. Do you know that you deserve all the happiness? You should know that you are worthy of everything good. Life at 19 should be colorful, and you will get there too. Finally, I hope you can get out of your current state soon. Take care.

As someone who is emotionally very unstable, I would like to share my inner thoughts with the questioner and hope to offer some inspiration. I often find myself shedding tears over seemingly ordinary things that most people wouldn't even notice, and I don't even understand why I'm crying. For example, when a classmate accidentally touches my book or when I stand up to answer a question in class. My parents are very worried about me, and I'm trying my best to control myself. However, the more I try to control it, the more I feel like crying. When I got older, I learned to pinch myself when I wanted to cry, using the pain to hold back my tears. Gradually, I realized that I started to enjoy the stimulation of pain. I developed a liking for spicy food and sometimes even wanted to eat bitter things, such as pills without a sugar coating. This made me very anxious, and I was afraid that everyone would notice how different I am from others. Fortunately, I have a very open-minded mother who also has some medical knowledge. From a physiological perspective, she helped me analyze my symptoms. She told me that the body is a very intricate machine, and the nervous and endocrine systems are what connect all the senses together. It's possible that my body releases hormones like adrenaline and thyroxine more easily than others, making me more sensitive and irritable. The stimulation of pain triggers a protective response in my nerves, which in turn regulates the hormone levels in my body. So, my dear, don't be afraid. We simply have a body that is more sensitive to the outside world. Let the body take care of its own matters, and don't put too much psychological pressure on yourself. You are a wonderful person, you just haven't found a way to live in harmony with your body yet. If you're feeling impulsive, exercise is definitely a great way to release those feelings. You can even redirect the excess energy through stimulating acupuncture points or massaging your muscles, which is beneficial to your physical health. Eventually, you will come to enjoy this feeling. If you want to know more details, feel free to message me. I love the world, and I love you too. I wish you well.

question: I always lose interest in things after a short period of time, what should I do?
description: I have a long reading list, but now I'm struggling to continue after finishing one-third of it. It has been abandoned for half a month already. I want to finish reading it, but recently every time I try to open it, I unconsciously browse other things or even feel sleepy as soon as I start reading. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hi there! When I clicked on this question, I thought that you really did only spend three minutes on something and then set it aside without doing anything. That's definitely not good, since three minutes isn't enough time to accomplish anything! But after reading your question, I was surprised. You have a long book list, and you said you stopped reading after one-third. And my thought is: you've actually finished one-third! That's really impressive! You see, I have many book lists on my reading app, but it's very possible that I haven't finished a single book from those lists. Please take a moment to look back at the books you've already finished, think about the effort you put into reading them, and the benefits you gained from them! It seems like you're ignoring your success and magnifying your failure, focusing too much on the unfinished two-thirds and feeling anxious about not completing them. Take some time to think carefully: do you really need to finish the other two-thirds? Making a book list is just a process of listing, and when we make these lists for our future selves, we think that doing these things will benefit us. However, the true benefits can only be known once we actually do them. In this list, we usually choose the ones we're interested in or the ones that are easier to do first. The one-third that you finished must be the books that you were most interested in and eager to learn about, right? So please take a look at the remaining two-thirds and select the books that you're still interested in learning about as your starting point. If you find them boring, just discard them and move on to the next one. You should know that it's not necessary to finish every book. Some books may not be worth reading, either because the language is too difficult or they don't offer much valuable knowledge. It's better not to read them at all! Understand the fundamental purpose of your reading. If you're just reading books to tick off the list, let me teach you a good trick- read book reviews on Douban, read the foreword, then read the table of contents, and select the sections you're interested in from there. That way, you can consider the book as finished. Many people who skim through books do it this way. The resulting insights and knowledge are quite shallow, and I don't really recommend this approach. But if you really want to complete the list and develop a reading habit, it's a pretty good method. Personally, I believe that reading is for the instant joy of it. Opening a book and immersing yourself in the reading moment is what matters most. For me, making a book list is just a reminder- this book I haven't read yet, these are the books you might be interested in. But if a book list becomes an obstacle that restricts my reading, causing me anxiety and unrest, then it's better to just let go and, amidst the vast sea of books, go find my own Mr. Right. Completing one-third is already quite amazing. It's not just a fleeting interest or a failure. Please don't let the book list limit your reading journey. Go do what interests you, read the books you're interested in! Keep it up~

Hello. People don't like the feeling of "not being in control". When you made a "long reading list" plan and couldn't keep up with your original plan, you would feel "I can't control myself" and then start to question yourself, which leads to dissatisfaction and stress, resulting in "internal exhaustion". For example, from reading itself, it escalates to why you are not the person you want to be, causing such "mental struggle". However, internal conflicts are more exhausting than reading itself, so your plan is shelved. So, you don't not want to read, you don't want to face yourself - the real you who didn't keep up with the plan. The real you looks much worse than the imagined you, so what's the use of striving as the real you? It's better to just lie down. However, it is the real you who made the "long reading list", it is the real you who has already earnestly completed one-third of the long reading list. The imagined you hasn't done anything, just standing by and mocking you, that's it. Who is better, can you see it clearly? Let go of the internal conflicts with yourself. Reward yourself, the one who has completed one-third of the reading list, with a short vacation. (In the plan, remember to schedule leisure time to reward yourself after each completion, not just full of "tasks"). It's already August, so you can subtract two-thirds of the reading list, so that every book you finish afterwards is extra, outside of your "planned book list" for this year. This way, the pressure would be much smaller if you only consider what has been completed or exceeded. Your self-evaluation will also increase rapidly, right? Loving oneself is a lesson for a lifetime. The world and I love you.

Hug you, hope my answer can help you. Why does the phenomenon of "three-minute enthusiasm" occur? This is because you don't genuinely like the thing or you don't really want to change deep down. When you see your friends make progress, you feel a little tempted, but when faced with other things, you forget about that temptation. Especially in this rapidly developing era, many people have no idea what they truly like and just go along aimlessly. With unclear goals, they don't know what they should or shouldn't pursue. They keep vacillating in their goals, ultimately missing out on opportunities time and time again. They lack the breakdown of goals and always want to become experts all at once. Don't forget, all experts keep their eyes on the goal and work hard step by step, overcoming many difficulties and accomplishing small goals before becoming experts. Lacking confidence, worrying about being mocked by others for making mistakes. Have you ever thought that when you are not as good as others, you are always afraid of being mocked or looked down upon from within. If you want to avoid being ridiculed, you need to become confident and make yourself stronger. Lack of self-discipline, always relying on others to push yourself to do things. We have been guided by our parents and teachers since childhood, and over time, we become accustomed to lacking self-discipline. We don't tempt ourselves or motivate ourselves. When the temptation of change surpasses the defense line within you, when ideals and desires coexist, you will unhesitatingly do things to the extreme. Because you know that only by changing yourself, succeeding, rewarding yourself, and realizing your ideals can you satisfy your desires. At this point, you will go all out to make changes and the phenomenon of "three-minute enthusiasm" will not occur. How to change the habit of always having "three-minute enthusiasm"? Cultivate a liking for something before you attempt to change it, then you won't experience "three-minute enthusiasm." Break down the big goal into several small goals, starting from easy to difficult. Over time, you will develop a liking for the thing you are about to change. This way, the phenomenon of "three-minute enthusiasm" won't occur in you. After completing a small goal, you need to constantly provide feedback to yourself and give yourself a small reward. In this way, you can repeat the cycle of "goal-action-good results-feedback-reward" and persist. This way, you will definitely be able to change and not experience the phenomenon of "three-minute enthusiasm" again. Cultivate your self-discipline. Without self-discipline, you won't be able to persevere and won't accomplish anything in the end. Cultivate good habits because 95% of your behavior is determined by your personal habits. Good habits are cultivated slowly. Cultivate good habits and start by changing your behavior patterns, especially the ones that aren't good. If you persist for three months, your behavior patterns will improve significantly. If you persist for three years, you will become one of the top experts.

You have an extroverted personality, and the problem does not lie in your willpower, but rather in your attitude. An extroverted personality is often in line with one's environment. The danger of extroversion is that it can easily be constrained by external factors, causing one to lose oneself in toil. It forces the individual to impose self-restriction spontaneously. Either extroverted individuals forcefully put pressure on themselves, without considering whether they genuinely enjoy those things, or the stronger the suppression, the more childish and primitive the desires become. 1. Understand the root cause and think about what you truly enjoy. What are you best at? Do you genuinely enjoy what you are good at? Once you understand what you enjoy the most, reflect on your past experiences. Then set goals for yourself, what do you want to achieve? What is the purpose behind it? The more detailed, the better. 2. Self-positioning. Quickly find your position by thinking about someone who truly enjoys what they do. How would they handle situations? Could they persevere? What kind of mindset would they have? Would they be happy? Ponder over these types of questions and ultimately tell yourself that you are someone who genuinely enjoys doing something. 3. Have confidence. Prepare to embrace failure, but remember that failure is not meant to discourage you, but rather to make you understand your limitations and do better. If you can show enough confidence, you can exude a strong sense of presence. The taste of self-assurance is wonderful. It not only enhances your comfort level of existence but also influences others. When you find your own style, do not easily change it, regardless of how others may scorn, unless you believe that a change is truly necessary.

question: Usually it takes a long time to show, with a significant lag in emotional perception.
description: I feel like a dog trapped in a pit with a nail tethered nearby. I can jump and escape, but either I will get buried or the nail will be gone. It's like burying myself while feeling unhappy and having slow emotional perception. Usually, it takes a long, long time for me to realize my own emotions. Then I start feeling sad and never proactively showing my weaknesses, fearing I will be rejected. When I was feeling uncomfortable before (my mother was putting pressure on me and criticizing my friends), I would crazily scratch my own legs, causing bruises. I want to know what symptoms this is.

answers.answer_text: Both the mind and body are trapped. It is not to say that these are symptoms, but rather a manifestation of emotional repression. Perhaps in severe cases, there is even an emotional isolation defense mechanism in order to protect your inner self from devastating blows. Only through using these defense mechanisms unconsciously can one self-protect. However, over time, the defense mechanisms that originally protected us become constraints on our emotional perception and the development of the mind and body.

Title owner, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description, it seems that you feel your emotional perception has become dull, unable to feel happiness, and delayed perception of pain. These certainly make your life very painful, and I truly sympathize with your experience. Based on your description, I feel that your current emotional characteristics seem to have become a bit numb. I noticed that you mentioned your mother "pressuring me and slandering my friends" beside you, and I think her influence on you must be significant, even causing you to become accustomed to suppressing your own feelings. In fact, when discussing the origin of the family, we often tend to attribute all misfortunes to it, but this is a mistaken notion. Even if the origin of the family has caused us pain, we can rely on our own strength to change rather than stagnate. I feel that your emotions are indeed delayed due to being suppressed, so I hope you can seek help from people around you, not bear it alone. It would be best to receive psychological counseling and avoid harming yourself.

question: I killed the fish that my stepfather raised, but now I feel full of guilt about it...
description: My stepfather keeps his fish in a large fish tank with a water pump in my bedroom, and the noise is very loud and disturbing during my rest and study. The fish tank makes my room very humid and increases the number of bugs. Furthermore, my mom and him have a difficult relationship, but I have to keep enduring it for the sake of my younger brother. Also, because I will be taking a high school entrance exam next year, I am under a lot of psychological pressure and my anxiety is unstable. Finally, yesterday, my mom and I argued over a minor issue on the phone, and I realized all the things they have done to me and the harm they have caused me over the years. So, I decided to implement my plan in advance, putting a large amount of salt and sugar in the fish tank to kill those fish. This way, my stepfather will no longer come to my room, and the water pump from the fish tank will no longer affect my studying and resting. After all, I can't kill him, but killing his fish is a form of revenge. (He molested me when I was younger, but I have never told my mom. His gaze towards me is often that of a pervert, and he would touch me when my mom isn't around. I haven't told my mom because she would face domestic violence and might leave her son). I can endure a few more years of revenge against that terrible old man, but now I feel guilty towards the fish. I actually really like them, but they shouldn't be looking at me dying in my room. I also feel very upset about it. I know that my mental state is abnormal, but I will disguise it and protect myself. Lastly, please tell me what illness I have. Please help me!

answers.answer_text: Every person has emotions, and I understand why you want to retaliate against him, why you choose to retaliate against his belongings, and the despair of silently swallowing the disgust after being molested by a foster father. You need a healthy and reasonable way to release these emotions and heal this trauma, like a birthmark. The problem of child sexual abuse is much more serious than we imagine, and it is mostly committed by acquaintances. Among the 107 people I served in the pandemic public welfare, 28 people were victims of sexual abuse, molestation, or rape, which shocked me. Many of them, like you, are telling others for the first time, enduring this trauma for decades, unable to speak out, enduring the disgust as if their bodies were crawling with maggots, but unable to remove it or seek help from others. Killing the foster father's fish today is your retaliation when the disgust becomes unbearable for you. This is also the greatest self-protection you can do within your ability because you cannot protect yourself at the moment. What you can do is retaliate subtly without causing domestic violence, and those dead fish are quite innocent. If you really feel guilty and remorseful, you can engage in self-reflection. I know you didn't intend to harm those fish; you just couldn't find a reasonable way to retaliate while protecting yourself. Go back to the trauma to heal yourself, learn to forgive yourself and protect yourself. Now, feelings of guilt, shame, fear, and remorse repeat and intertwine. I know you are particularly suffering. On the one hand, the trauma of being molested needs healing. They will constantly remind you that you are a victim, and the fear of your mother being abused hangs over your head like a sword. The guilt of killing the fish makes you feel like a murderer. I can understand how these emotions torment you every day. Honestly, treating sexual abuse and molestation requires seeking help from a hypnotist or a psychotherapist. Psychological counseling may be slower, but with your college entrance examination approaching, your emotions are exploding, and you definitely need to find a local professional healer or therapist as soon as possible to help you through this dark phase of life. If your financial situation does not allow for it, you can find a safe and quiet space to try the "empty chair technique," the specific operating methods can be researched on Baidu videos, which can also provide some relief. You can also search for self-healing meditation audio online and give yourself some guidance. I recommend purchasing a subscription for "Meditation Planet" to practice daily. It will be helpful when you feel helpless in protecting yourself and unable to seek help from your mother. Leave the person and environment that make you fearful and anxious, and stick it out for another year. You need to devote all your energy to your studies. You can gradually digest your emotions through the meditation exercises on Meditation Planet. Only when you leave this home will you be safe. I know you must have thought about studying in another city, far away from this terrible person and place, so now you must persevere. If you can live on campus, apply for it so that you can ensure that there are no setbacks in your college entrance examination. I believe you can do it. I look forward to hearing the good news that you will be attending college in another city next year.

OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, I can understand that 1. The relationship between OP and their parents is not good and there have been many unhappy incidents. 2. OP's father keeping fish in OP's room has affected OP's studying, and OP killed these fish and now feels very guilty about it. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Psychological energy accumulates in a person's inner self and is difficult to vanish into thin air. The past unhappiness between OP and their parents, such as the dissatisfaction and grievances that OP mentioned and didn't dare to tell their mother, have been accumulating in OP's heart without release, causing a lot of pressure. Perhaps telling a trusted family member or friend about these grievances and thoughts, or writing them in a diary to express one's thoughts, will make OP feel a little better. 2. Emotions can be transferred. The actions OP took towards the fish make OP feel guilty and wondering if they have mental issues, but that may not necessarily be the case. When people can't release their inner emotions on the objects that caused those emotions, they tend to choose to vent their anger on weaker objects. For example, a husband who was criticized by his boss at work and couldn't argue back might come home and innocently scold his wife, who then can't confront her husband and ends up scolding their child, and the child feels even more helpless and doesn't know what to do. At that moment, the family cat passes by and the child kicks it. OP's emotions and the act of killing the fish may also stem from this kind of feeling. 3. However, the most stable and effective way to solve family problems is to communicate with parents. If OP feels like they can't say these things face-to-face with their mother, writing a letter to their mother to express the grievances of these years and explain the reason for killing the fish is also a method that can help their mother understand them.

First, give yourself a hug. Okay, don't immediately assume that there's something wrong with you. In the situation you described, anyone would have a reaction, although it might be different from what you did. After all, facing these things can be tough. The first thing you need to do is protect yourself. If the incidents of harassment happened a long time ago and there is no evidence, it may be difficult to pursue. However, if it happens again or if there are signs, consider telling your mom or calling the police, or using it as a warning to your stepdad. Maybe it's because you rely on this family due to your mother and younger brother, or maybe you have no other choice for living, which makes it difficult for you to make more decisions and you can only bear the humiliation. I empathize with you.

1. "The sound is very loud and it disturbs my rest and studying. The fish tank makes my room very humid and attracts more bugs." "He molested me when I was young, but I never told my mom." "He touched me when my mom wasn't around, and I didn't tell her." These are violations of your rights by your stepfather, and you have the reasonable and lawful right to protect your legitimate interests. However, you are weak and not standing up for yourself, allowing the abuser to continue. The reasons given were "my mom and he have a bad relationship but she has to tolerate it for the sake of my little brother" and "she would leave her son if she were to experience domestic violence." None of these reasons are for yourself, isn't that scary? Clearly, you are living for your mother, but if your mother tells you to hit someone, would you do it? In these past ten years, it seems like you haven't truly lived, you have no sense of self, is your sense of self just your mother? Is that not pathetic? Only when you have a sense of self and the ability, can you protect the people around you. If you can't even take care of yourself, how can you protect others? When you were still a small fry, worrying about another small fry being eaten by a big shark? You yourself have already caught the attention of the big shark. As for the fish tank issue, you could have resisted, told your stepfather directly that it disturbs your studying and you can't sleep because of the noise, and if he doesn't move it, threaten to smash the fish tank and actually do it a few times. If he dares to hit you, call the police. If he molests you, call the police. If he abuses your mother, also call the police, or post evidence of the abuse on the media to expose him and make him leave. These are all solutions. 2. Your actions, on the other hand, do not defend your rights, nor protect your mother, nor fight against the stronger party. Instead, you bully the weaker one, as evidenced by the fact that you argued with your mother over a small matter on the phone yesterday. Therefore, it's like the old saying in China, "bullying the weak while fearing the strong." So your behavior is extremely despicable, and it leaves one with a chilling feeling. 3. There have been numerous reports of domestic violence in recent years, haven't you seen any of the news? And the online revelations of domestic violence and molestation of elementary school students, with so many examples, what have you learned? Have you only learned to submit to the strong (your stepfather) and then bully the weak (your mother)? I hope you will take care of yourself.

question: Because of the lack of trust from the parents, how to deal with study aversion and anxiety?
description: Because I used to have good grades, I didn't study hard, but in recent years, my grades have been declining. I've realized the importance of studying and plan to catch up on what I missed before. However, when I mentioned it to my parents, they showed distrust and believed that I wouldn't take the initiative to study (they didn't say it directly, but I think that's what they meant). Yet, they still want me to do well. I've talked to them about it three times, and each time their reaction was similar, either indifferent or distrustful. But my teacher believes in me and has high expectations for me. I'm torn and feeling low. On one hand, I don't want to disappoint my teacher, but on the other hand, due to my parents' constant discouragement, I've lost enthusiasm for learning. I've even lost interest in the hobby I've been persisting in for more than ten years. I've started experiencing insomnia, not feeling like eating all day, and then waking up in the middle of the night to eat a lot. I don't feel like doing anything and have a sense that it doesn't matter whether I'm alive or dead. I've lost passion for anything, experience extreme mood swings, feeling very down, and I don't know what's going on.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From the description, I understand that 1. Your grades are dropping, and you are planning to review previous materials. 2. Your parents don't trust you and haven't provided the support you need. 3. You feel very sad but don't want to disappoint your teacher. [Some analysis and suggestions] 1. First of all, it's normal to feel upset when facing difficulties and being discouraged by them. The key is how to deal with these feelings. 2. Communicating with your parents is crucial. Perhaps your parents' lack of trust is due to your past lack of focus on studying. So maybe you can give your parents another chance. Talk to your teacher and find suitable study methods. After a few days of studying, show your parents your determination, and maybe then you can get their support. I hope this helps you.

question: Why is it that the more books I read, the more I look down on the people around me?
description: I am a college student and I have always loved reading books. After reading some books, I feel out of place with my classmates and unable to connect with them. I find them very ordinary and childish, and sometimes I find their actions ridiculous. How should I face this? Is the problem with myself? I feel like interacting with them is a waste of time, but at the same time, I feel that I shouldn't act too superior.

answers.answer_text: Reading can broaden a person's horizons, deepen their thoughts, and provide a more comprehensive perspective on issues. If you read more and learn more, it will naturally show in your communication with classmates, and you can openly acknowledge and face this difference, while also affirming your own gains and growth. It is natural to feel out of place and unable to relate to others. You may think they are "immature," and this viewpoint is not wrong. You don't need to blame yourself or see it as a problem. Different people have different perspectives, which naturally leads to different behaviors. However, an individual is complex and multifaceted. If you simply feel superior to your classmates because of different views on certain matters, considering them all as inferior or immature, it would be overly one-sided. You can widen your gaze and look at the bigger picture, for example, recognizing that some classmates have beautiful singing voices or are excellent at playing sports, or that some colleagues are kind and gentle, and so on. See their other shining qualities. If communicating with them doesn't satisfy you, it's okay to not have too much interaction with them and maintain basic politeness. Instead, you can find like-minded companions through platforms like Douban or book clubs and engage in more in-depth discussions and learning together.

Hello, reading books is helpful for one's growth, cognition, and decision-making. However, it requires critical thinking. It's better to have no books than to blindly believe in them. You need to integrate your own theories with practice. (1) In interpersonal relationships, while you immerse yourself in the world of books, there is still a gap between that world and reality. The beauty depicted in books is often the result of various conditions coming together. You need to experience the truths from books in the real world. The truths also have an impact on the real world. When it comes to human relationships, finding common ground and similar interests is what makes conversations flow easily. Currently, the people around you, including your classmates, might have different focuses and interests. While you gain higher intellectual enlightenment from books, your classmates are still living in the real world, playing games, listening to music, talking about food, relationships, weight loss, and gossip. You might find them immature. In reality, they are just a reflection of most people in the real world, whom you will encounter most frequently in the future. In interpersonal relationships, what do you hope to gain? Finding a companion to share life with is something they can fully provide. However, if you seek a partner who connects with you spiritually and shares your pursuit of a higher purpose, then they are not suitable. They are not wrong; they just don't meet your specific needs in that aspect. Therefore, when interacting with them, it's alright to seek commonalities while accepting differences. You don't need to impose your pursuits on them or judge them based on your own standards. (2) In terms of self-awareness, if you have goals you want to pursue, you must focus on them and find ways to achieve them. In this process, you need to identify a comfortable state for yourself, free from external disturbances. Determine which problems and matters you can ignore and which ones you care about. Understand your goals and abilities in various aspects, and approach problems and other people with a diverse mindset and perspective. Look for shining points and places worthy of learning from others. Try to reduce your focus on others' shortcomings, and you will also reduce your own self-inflicted worries. I hope you can adjust yourself well. Be confident, independent, decisive, and love life, embracing it fully.

Hello, hope you continue to enjoy reading, as it is an excellent habit. Reading extensively will bring the books to life, and you will definitely have a good mood and your own unique temperament. Analyze the "distance" between you and your classmates: ◆ You like reading, and you can surely see that most of your classmates around you don't like reading. Some high school students who liked reading in high school don't like it anymore in college. College offers too many temptations, more food, drinks, and recreational activities compared to high school. In high school, there are fewer things to do, so reading becomes the only pastime. But in college, it's different. There are more ways to relax, so reading is no longer a priority. You can say that in college, those who continue to read are doing it out of passion. ◆ While you read, your classmates may prefer playing games, watching anime, and other otaku-related activities. Because you have different interests, the intersection between each other is reduced and the things you can communicate about are also few. You don't understand what your classmates like, and your classmates don't understand what you like. ◆ I hope you don't see yourself as superior, there's no need to. It's not that continuing to read and enriching oneself in college is the only thing worth being proud of. Others in college may excel in playing games, have extensive knowledge of anime, and keep up with current events... These are also things worth being proud of. Reading is not the only option and not necessarily the best one. Your choice is just what you like, everything is based on "what I like is good enough". ◆ On the other hand, by isolating yourself from your classmates, you easily make yourself feel isolated. You are just one person while your classmates are a group of people. Ask yourself if you can bear being isolated. Actually, people with different personalities and interests can coexist peacefully. You can do your thing, and I can do mine. Have a conversation, have a meal together, there's no problem. Being considerate of others is also being good to yourself. I hope you think about it carefully. Best wishes!

Hello, you seem to have a lot of superiority in your question, which will motivate you to study harder, and having a sense of superiority will also make you more confident. These are things that young people go through. Young and reckless, enjoy it. At the same time, I am glad that you can realize these things, and you are not indulging in your sense of superiority. You hope to find answers and grow more. I am happy for you. Reading more is definitely good. The internal conflicts you have are caused by conflicting thoughts from others, not by reading too much. They don't want to take that blame. I don't know if the books you read are integrated into your life. Learning that 1+1 equals 2 is like learning that one apple plus one apple equals two apples, while one apple plus one pear equals two fruits. They may look similar but are different. The former is an abstract concept or a general truth, while the latter is the real knowledge and skills that help in life. What is the true meaning of the former if it doesn't take root anywhere, just like castles in the air? Children study hard for what? Ultimately, it's to return to life. Of course, maybe those people you look down upon don't have more insights in life, or they just haven't learned, or they don't need it. Learning something and using it well is what truly becomes one's own. Otherwise, why spend so much time learning something that everyone can easily find with a quick internet search on their phone? The cost-effectiveness is too low. I hope these fragmented answers have been helpful to you. Good luck!

Hello, my friend. It is a great pleasure to meet you on this platform. I hope my words can bring you sunshine and warm your heart. It's very good that you enjoy reading because in this commercialized society, many people are eager for quick success and instant benefits, and they don't have time to calm down and read. Just for this reason, I'll give you a thumbs up and applause. However, you mentioned that after reading, you find the people around you "very vulgar and childish." This indicates that you have gained a lot from those books, and unconsciously you start to demand others to meet the standards in the books, and even want to "change" others with it. This is also a "good" thing about you towards others, and this should be affirmed! However, there are only three things in this world - one's own affairs, others' affairs, and the affairs of the heavens. You like reading and what you have gained from these books is your own affair. Whether others are "vulgar" or "childish" and whether they are willing to change is their own affair! Judging others based on your own perspective is interfering with "others' affairs"! This is a form of overstepping boundaries! So, now you only need to do two things: 1. Take care of your own affairs and don't meddle in other people's affairs! People only want to change themselves, they don't like being changed by others! 2. Read. If one can't get in, they are a "tramp"; if one can't get out, they are a "prisoner". In regards to reading, it's important to be able to enter and also to exit! It is better to have no book at all than to blindly believe in books. Try to "step out" of it! I hope this can help you.

I have had similar situations where I didn't feel a connection with others, but it wasn't during my time in school. During that time, because my classmates were also studying together, there wasn't much of a barrier between us. Instead, it was after I started working, when my colleagues were mostly workers with lower cultural levels. That's when what you described happened, where it was difficult to connect and have meaningful conversations, feeling like a waste of time. However, for someone like you, who has also experienced not being able to relate well with classmates in college, with interests diverging too much from your own, I recommend reflecting on your professional interests and future life planning.

question: Married for 3 years, I feel like I'm the only one making an effort. How can this marriage continue?
description: Married for 3 years, our daily life is generally good, but there is no intimacy between us. It is basically a sexless marriage, and sometimes he even avoids me when I try to get close to him. I have tried to communicate and express my desire for him to share his thoughts, but he always chooses to remain silent, and in the end, we part ways without happiness. If it's my fault, I'm willing to change, and if it's a physical issue, he can see a doctor. I have always believed that life is about two people working together and making efforts, but now I feel like I'm the only one trying while he locks himself in his own world. I have thought about giving up, but at the same time, I feel reluctant and unwilling because it hasn't been easy for us to come together. What should I do?
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, concept of childbirth, sexual life.

answers.answer_text: Hello! 1. Seeing your question, I feel very sorry for you and I can also understand your helplessness and confusion in this situation. The relationship between husband and wife is a typical intimate relationship, but it seems that there is no intimacy, which is really sad. I believe it must be very difficult for you to be caught in this situation. 2. Facing such a difficult problem, it's great that you can take the initiative to communicate, seek help, and think positively. It shows that you are very responsible and serious about yourself and your family. I believe that regardless of how your marriage develops, this attitude towards life will help you find your own life. 3. From the description you gave about your husband, maybe he has some hidden concerns in terms of sexuality. This may be related to his physical condition, family background, or past experiences. For him, the best solution is to seek help from a professional doctor or psychotherapist. You are his closest and most intimate partner, so what you can do is to give him enough support and a sense of security. Maybe he will gradually open up to you about his troubles and burdens. 4. As a psychotherapist, if you were my client, perhaps I would discuss more with you about how your husband's behavior makes you feel and any similar experiences you have had. Perhaps we can find the limitations of our own beliefs. When we understand what happened to you from a multi-dimensional perspective, maybe you will be able to understand and accept yourself more, and then your goals for your marriage will become clearer. 5. You mentioned that your daily life is still fine. Can you think about what specific aspects are good? Can you give your husband more affirmation and encouragement in these aspects, and enhance the intensity of these things in your married life, creating more sweetness that belongs to the two of you? These can all be considered as "foreplay" for your sex life. Over time, I believe you will have more wonderful experiences. This is my answer, I hope it helps you. Lingting Counselling, listening to you. Best wishes.

question: Hiding my actual age and being in a relationship with my boyfriend for a year, I feel so embarrassed about myself.
description: My actual age is seven years older than my boyfriend, but I only lied to him about being one year older. However, he saw my passport and felt really ashamed. I don't know what to do. I want to die to escape and find relief. What should I do? I feel disgusted and embarrassed about hiding my age!

answers.answer_text: The past experiences mentioned by the original poster have had a certain impact on their current emotional state. Therefore, the concerns about marriage and the lack of trust in their boyfriend are reasonable and, as the original poster mentioned, may be a form of avoidance. Age will not be an obstacle to love, but deceit will be. Therefore, the original poster should communicate reasonably. In addition, doubts about the other person and the relationship often stem from a lack of security, an inability to fully trust the other person's sincerity, and an inability to fully trust one's own ability to choose a partner. It is not advisable to maintain a doubtful attitude in a relationship. The following suggestions are recommended: Communication and dialogue are worthwhile methods to try. The original poster may be open about their feelings and doubts with their boyfriend. Of course, if the boyfriend is not willing to fight for the relationship and does not want to give up, it is best for the original poster to apologize to the boyfriend afterwards. This doubt is something that originated from themselves. The original poster doesn't want to doubt whether they can have a long-lasting relationship with the boyfriend or fear that the boyfriend will dislike their age. The boyfriend will show understanding, and in the future, the original poster should strengthen communication when doubts arise. This may help the original poster feel more secure about this relationship.

Is concealing your age because you want to maintain this relationship and prevent it from being disturbed or influenced by the age difference? If that's the case, although lying is not good, it can be understood. But this matter makes you feel ashamed and even leads to extreme thoughts. It seems like it would be helpful to talk to a counselor about this, maybe it can help you better understand yourself and thus face the world around you better.

question: What should a therapist call a visitor who wants to hug them, and how should they handle it?
description: How do you address visitors as a counselor? If someone expresses a desire to hug you, how would you respond? Would you discuss it or give them a hug? As a visitor, how do you address your counselor? How do you like to be addressed by your counselor? Would you secretly give your counselor a nickname? Speaking as a visitor, I would like to share my personal opinion. Both of the counselors I have seen before referred to themselves as "teacher" and they were both online counselors who asked me how I would like to be addressed. One counselor compared to the other often used "you" and in the two sessions I had with her, I didn't feel she was very professional. She often lectured me and relentlessly asked about my childhood, which "forced" me to recall many painful memories that had been forgotten. It felt a bit too rushed, so I didn't continue with her. The other counselor, however, felt like a good match and was quite professional. But it can be a bit uncomfortable, that kind of heart-wrenching feeling where there is warmth and pain. I feel respected in our conversations and that we are equals. Personally, I don't care about the address we use for each other, it's just a code name. Calling her "teacher" doesn't mean she is self-centered, and calling her that doesn't mean I see her as an authority figure, it's just an analysis based on a title, which could be seen as a form of violence. I hope you can help me answer this, teachers.

answers.answer_text: Although many times, calling someone by a certain name is just a code, but this code can also have different meanings. Just as an example, I have been active in the Q&A area for over a year, and sometimes people call me Teacher Xiaofan. However, personally, I prefer being called Xiaofan Guoguo or Xiaofan the Scum. The same words can have different meanings in different people's minds. For me, Teacher implies having certain achievements in a specific area. Maybe it's because of strict upbringing, so I always have a certain fear of teachers, and there is always a bit of restraint when talking to them. Guoguo and the Scum are internet slang. Since most of the people using online counseling are experienced internet users, they are more accepting of new things. Fun nicknames can create a lively atmosphere during our communication, making it less formal. However, different people have different needs, so when interacting with visitors, we can actively ask them which title they prefer, which can help us to build closer relationships and make them feel valued. As for the request of a hug from a visitor, it depends on the individual. If the visitor is emotionally excited and happens to be of the same gender, we can give them a simple hug to reassure them and let them know that they can take their time to speak up. If the visitor is highly dependent and happens to be of the opposite sex, we need to learn to set boundaries and can discuss with them the feelings a hug can bring. If the therapy is going well, we can reward them with a simple hug, helping them gradually become more independent. The world and I love you.

Regarding names: Many parents have consulted me about this. I haven't paid much attention to how I should be addressed. Maybe it's because I am very approachable, haha! People of similar age call each other "dear". Younger people call me "sister", and I call older people "sister". Some people call me Teacher Wang. The name doesn't matter, the most important thing is the attitude of the person seeking advice, whether they are sincere and genuinely want to solve the problem, and it's okay to not answer irrelevant questions. 
Regarding hugs: In fact, the majority of people have intimacy issues and don't like physical contact with others. If someone wants a hug, it's not a problem! If it's a lady, a longer hug is also possible. Once, a sister hugged me and cried for over half an hour. By that time, we had known each other for six months and had become friends. When I go to class, every classmate hugs each other when they meet, and also when saying goodbye. The purpose is to break down the barrier of intimacy, and it's very effective.

Hello, OP. As you mentioned, addressing each other is like using a code name. In the counseling room, it is important to find a way to address each other that both parties feel comfortable with, while also considering the setting of the counseling room. For example, you can address the counselor as "teacher" or simply by their name or nickname, but using certain relational pronouns like "brother/sister" might not be appropriate. As for a visitor expressing a desire to hug, the counselor should respond according to the visitor's motives behind wanting to hug. Of course, this can be clarified and understood through communication with the visitor to determine how best to respond.

I previously discussed this issue with a teacher and came to the conclusion that it would be helpful to ask the visitor how they would like to be addressed. As the original poster mentioned, the name we call someone is just a symbol, and as long as it doesn't hinder regular communication, any name can be used. However, asking the visitor's preference in advance can make them feel cared for and can help establish a closer connection from the beginning.

question: The contradiction has been repeated many times, and I really don't know what I'm doing?
description: I want to pursue higher education, but in terms of this matter, I keep getting stuck in the same place, unable to move forward or to take action. I am very afraid of certain things, such as not having enough time or the fear that time and money spent won't bring any returns or success. Maybe if I tried more times, but I don't have money. I want to work, but I am worried about spending more money, so I can't move forward and can't go backward. I can only keep going in this cycle of contradiction. This contradiction has been repeating for a long time. I don't know what to do about myself and the people around me. I also can't control it.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, careful consideration is a good quality, but indecisiveness is torturous. All choices in reality come with certain risks and costs. From your description, it can be seen that you are wavering at the crossroads between furthering your education and finding a job, and you have been contemplating for a long time, but still can't make a decision. You feel very conflicted and trapped in this choice, unable to extricate yourself. Escaping and procrastinating will only make you more miserable and helpless. Analyze the pros and cons of both options seriously and rationally, rather than just focusing on their downsides and risks. There are no life choices that do not require time or money. Consider which of these two options you are more willing to "invest" in. Furthering your education may give you better job opportunities, better treatment, and higher pay, while starting to work directly will accumulate certain experience, financial gains, and personal and professional development. Alternatively, you can use the "regret test" to help you make a determination. Imagine your future life and look back at the decision you made today. Which one will you regret more for not having tried or worked hard for? Can it be made up for in the future? What will be the cost and price of making a choice then? Avoid the "camel effect" and make a decision as soon as possible after careful consideration to avoid exhausting your willpower and action. When faced with two piles of equally tempting grass, a camel hesitates and doesn't know which pile to eat, and in the end, it starves while hesitating. Many times our hesitations stem from the high cost of choice or the lack of confidence in the future outcome, but these things will only be known after we have made the choice. Stop hesitating and make a decisive choice, analyzing the possible costs in terms of time, money, and other aspects, and be prepared for them. Choosing the right path is just the beginning; what's more important is to persevere on the chosen path. If we hesitate for so long at the beginning, many competitors may already have chosen a path and gone far ahead. Do not fear making the wrong choice; what you should truly worry about is not having the ability to deal with mistakes. Not all paths are shortcuts, and regardless of which path you choose, it may be extremely difficult and challenging. Prepare yourself to endure hardships and cultivate the courage to face difficulties. Do not evade or shrink back; move forward instead. Moving forward is always better than staying in one place. Best wishes.

question: What to do if a 15-year-old has autism? Lack of emotions and emotions?
description: In social situations, there is a fear of socializing and avoiding eye contact. The gaze appears dull and unable to comprehend the content of others' conversations. There is a reluctance to engage with others and it feels strange to interact and unable to speak. There is a lack of willingness to participate in activities, being socially withdrawn, and experiencing a lack of emotions and mood. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, character improvement, self-growth, student growth.

answers.answer_text: The title mentioned that the individual has autism, was this condition diagnosed in a hospital? The individual mentioned experiencing social anxiety and fear eye contact. They have a vacant gaze and struggle to pay attention to others' conversations. They avoid contact with others and find it strange to interact and struggle to speak. They are unwilling to participate in activities, are very reclusive, and lack emotions and emotions. What should they do? At the age of 15, you should still be in school. Are these conditions you mentioned long-term or occasional? From the description, it can be seen that the individual fears social interactions and avoids interpersonal relationships. You should carefully think about whether this is because you are afraid of being rejected, looked down upon, or having your weaknesses exposed by others. Perhaps subconsciously, you have made the decision to avoid any contact with others so as to not get hurt. This mindset is detrimental. We must understand that the past experiences of not being liked by others only affect us because we allow it to dictate our behavior today. We can start changing from the smallest details in the present, by proactively being kind to others, showing goodwill, and even just a simple smile! The gentler our tone, the more likely it will be met with kindness.

question: Sometimes when I recall many past unpleasant things, how can I come out of the abyss of darkness?
description: Again and again filled with hope, again and again plunged into despair. On and on it goes. I am afraid, I avoid, I want to escape. Time and time again I tell myself not to be afraid, tell myself it's not as bad as I imagine, but soon I fall into self-doubt, self-denial, and think that it's better to give up (often have this kind of thought). Clearly, I know I should be hopeful, but still unable to... I don't like to communicate with others, I am afraid of communicating with others, I don't know how to get along with others, to communicate. I am very sensitive, even to details that others may not pay attention to, I will think about for a long time. I am afraid that my inattentive words or actions might hurt others. Maybe I just overthink too much. Sometimes I would recall many unpleasant things from the past. Every time I am in pain and on the verge of collapse, I feel suffocated and just want to shut myself away. I don't like being with people, I dislike crowded places. I don't know what I like, I am not clear... Sometimes it seems like I don't want to have any emotions at all. I don't even want to feel pain, sadness, or despair. I wish I could have no emotions at all, so I wouldn't be in so much pain.
keywords: Emotion, depressed mood, expressing emotions, panic helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Dear friend: Seeing your words, I feel that you must have had many unhappy things in the past that made it difficult for you to live in the present and not feel hopeful for the future. Everyone has a sad past, hug. Because there have been too many negative things in the past, your subconscious mind is filled with despair, disappointment, and pain. When similar things happen again, the worst result will come to mind. You have forgotten that there are other possibilities in life. In addition, your psychological habit is to blame yourself when encountering negative things, so you will question yourself. Maybe you can't distinguish between what is your responsibility and what is just a worry. Breaking this vicious cycle is possible, but it requires your cooperation: [First], say goodbye to the past. I know you have had many painful experiences in the past, and perhaps some are your responsibility and some are not. What belongs to your boundaries is your responsibility, but others' opinions, thoughts, and behaviors towards you are their responsibility. Don't step into other people's boundaries, nor do you need others to approve or recognize you. Because you can affirm yourself. [Second], regain yourself. If you always doubt yourself when something happens, it's because you really think you are not good enough. 1. Find your essence. You need to know that human value is not defined by external factors, but by human nature. No matter what happens to you, you are valuable, you are worthy of love. You are originally pure, bright, complete, precious, unique, and irreplaceable. You are perfect and good enough because you are the miraculous child of the universe. You are the source of affirmation, and you are the center of happiness. The past events made you unhappy, please don't be easily assimilated. Encountering unhappy things does not mean that you have to be controlled by these things for the rest of your life. You are you, and things are things. 2. Focus on your strengths. To get rid of doubt, you need to get to know yourself again. Start understanding yourself, especially your strengths. Redefine yourself. [Third], focus on happiness. You can't change the past, but happy things will also cheer you up. As long as you are willing to pay attention, there are many things that can make people happy and warm. Maybe our circle is too small, thinking that the world is so cold and dark, but in fact, it is more beautiful than we imagine. It's just that we are often assimilated by negativity, which inadvertently makes us focus on the negative. [Fourth], see the positive meaning it brings. After experiencing darkness and pain, the next time you encounter such things, you will have the experience to deal with them. We come to Earth to learn all kinds of things, and growth is an inevitable lesson. With your experience, you will have confidence and wisdom in the future. This will also increase your empathy, and you will understand people who are also living in pain. You will become a person with love. No one and nothing can control you. Maybe it will make you unhappy in the moment, but it absolutely cannot control you. Focus on happiness, and you will be much happier!

I don't know what things the questioner thinks are bad about themselves, but I know that you won't say it because the things you want to keep secret will bring you more pain. I can understand that those bad things may bring you insecurity and make you avoid facing them. You said that you are filled with hope time and time again, but also filled with despair time and time again. It's a cycle. You are afraid, you avoid, and you want to escape. You keep telling yourself not to be afraid, not to be as you imagine, but soon you will fall back into self-doubt and self-denial, thinking that it's better to give up altogether (I often have this thought). Even though you know you should be hopeful, you still can't...I can understand that feeling of hope and despair repeating time and time again. When you choose a goal that you are incapable of achieving, you will feel a sense of loss, which can be called inferiority. Inferiority is self-denial, lack of confidence in oneself, and a psychological expression of not identifying with oneself. From the description, it can be seen that you have an inferiority complex. Once someone forms an inferiority complex, they often become timid in social interactions and isolate themselves. They can't see the brilliance and hope in life, can't appreciate the joy of living, and don't dare to envision a better tomorrow. What should you do? I don't know what you have hope in but also despair about. If you consider this experience as an attempt and failure, then okay, you have failed now and you have two options. The first option is a pattern called try-fail-give up. The other pattern is try-fail-try again. Which one do you choose? I suggest you choose try again. Why? Because you can go back to the origin of our life. How does a child learn to walk? If a child falls while trying to walk and says, "I will never walk again," then it is impossible for them to learn to walk. It's because a child walks, falls, walks again, falls again, and slowly learns to walk. But as we grow up, our common pattern is "I failed, I will never try again." This is unacceptable. So if you allow yourself to fail, make mistakes, and accept that you are not perfect, once you accept that, you will come out of that abyss of darkness.

Hello! According to your description, I can truly sense your pain and I really want to help you. Here are my suggestions. First, start by accepting your emotions. It's normal for all of us to have low moods and the desire to avoid social interactions. It's just that your low mood may last a bit longer, and that's okay. Don't pressure yourself too much, just accept it. The most effective way to combat negative emotions is not to tell yourself to "cheer up", but to genuinely find ways to resolve them. Second, emotions are a response to objective events and our relationship with ourselves, based on our desires and needs. Are you eager to break free from these negative emotions? Do you long to regain happiness, hope, and joy? I have also been trapped in depressive emotions, and it took me a lot of struggle to finally see the bright sunshine. Take it step by step, don't rush yourself. Sometimes, by not being in a hurry, you'll find that the pressure eases. Third, try therapeutic writing. You have many suppressed and negative things in your mind that continue to harm you. You can write down whatever comes to mind, just write freely. This writing process is a form of healing. Once you've written it down, it will have a relieving effect on your stress and emotions. Fourth, try to focus more on the outside world. Only a few people can proactively step out of their own whirlpool, because it is a difficult psychological struggle to shift your focus from yourself to the people and things around you. Rest assured, confidently speak and act, because no one is that concerned. Sensitivity is often our own imagination. Take it step by step, find your own way to love yourself. Don't force yourself, for example, at the moment, you may not know what you like. When you occasionally think of something you like, try to engage in that activity a little. It's commendable that you are aware of your feelings of sadness and avoidance, and that you know how to seek help. If possible, you can try seeking help from a mental health counselor. Lastly, I deeply wish you the strength to emerge from the darkness and embrace the light.

Dear friend, hello! I just saw your description and I don't know how you are doing now. Do you still feel like you're in a deep abyss? I feel like you were in a low state at that time. If this state continues to affect you, I sincerely recommend that you seek professional psychological help in a timely manner, so that professionals can help you get through this difficult time. You mentioned that you have had hopeful moments followed by moments of despair, what processes have you gone through? I sense that you have been trying hard. But could this disparity between hope and despair be related to your high expectations or unrealistic hopes for yourself? Sometimes we need to see more of our own efforts. Seeing ourselves making efforts is our wealth, it is the place where we deserve self-recognition. Enjoy the process of pursuit, enjoy the process of doing. That's when you truly feel your existence. You said you don't like to communicate with others because you're afraid of hurting them with inappropriate words or actions, is that right? If so, I want to say that this way of thinking is projection. Of course, there are situations where our inappropriate words or actions can hurt others, but not everyone is as fragile or easily hurt as we imagine. On the contrary, the more we think this way, the more we are afraid of being hurt ourselves. So, is it actually because you're afraid of being hurt that you don't dare to communicate and interact with others more? In this regard, I want you to know that a blade is only sharp when it's sharpened, and people also need training and immunity. Other people's inappropriate words and actions are just a negative example for us to avoid. As long as you don't feel it's hurtful, then it's not hurtful. Do you agree? I'm not sure what you consider to be bad things in your mind. I sincerely hope that you can have more detailed communication with a professional whom you trust. Perhaps you can sort out the things you consider to be bad, and realize that they are not as bad as you think. At the same time, gain a new understanding of the chaotic and painful emotions you feel. I wish you to dispel the clouds and see the sunshine again soon!

After carefully reading your confession, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1 Your symptoms are somewhat similar to schizophrenia. However, the main manifestations of schizophrenia are delusions and hallucinations. Nonetheless, you should also be cautious and take preventive measures. Nip the problem in the bud. 2 If schizophrenia can be compared to college, then mental health issues are like primary school. Nurturing a disease is like raising a tiger, when the tiger grows big, it will surely harm people. Small illnesses should not be left untreated, as big illnesses are difficult to cure. Just like psychologists, they also have their own worries. The difference is that they resolve their worries in advance, which is why they appear worry-free. 3 The law is impermanent, doctrines are impermanent, water has no constant state, the great Tao is natural. We humans have defense mechanisms that can help resist the invasion of illness, including mental disorders. The best way to activate these mechanisms is to go with the flow. Do whatever you feel like doing, and if you don't feel like doing something, then don't do it. As long as you don't harm others, it's all good. Thank you for your question, and may all the beauty in the world come to you as expected.

question: Getting married soon, feeling a lot of pressure and having difficulty fitting into other people's families.
description: Just feel that the personality is not compatible with the parents, there is no common language to live together. I am more lively, and his parents are more introverted. There are always some conflicts between him and me. We initially agreed not to get married and informed each other's parents. Later, we still decided to get married, but I always feel unhappy.

answers.answer_text: Marriage is a matter involving two families, but the relationship between the husband and wife is crucial. If the husband can be on the same side as the questioner, clearly establish boundaries between the new nuclear family and his parents' extended family, and show understanding when the questioner expresses disagreement with his parents instead of constantly demanding that the questioner "understand them, as they are this way, just tolerate it", then the conflicts between the couple can be gradually resolved and communicated between them. However, if the husband involves these conflicts within the extended family and interferes with the parents, prioritizing the interests of the nuclear family after the extended family, such a life is destined to be chaotic. In fact, there is really no need to interact with in-laws in the same way as with one's own parents because after all, they have been strangers for more than twenty years, with completely different personalities and lifestyles. Everyone comes together for the same reason ("love for the husband"), and this reason even leads to the "struggle" between daughters-in-law and mothers-in-law, posing a huge challenge to the relationship. Therefore, if everyone, for this same reason, allows the person they love to live a relaxed and happy life and maintains a mindset of "agree to disagree", then they can peacefully coexist. Disappointment and conflicts often stem from our overly high and unreasonable expectations. Adjusting our expectations to a reasonable level, we might find that things are actually quite simple.

Marriage is like a mixed gift, containing things you like and things you don't. But they come together as a comprehensive gift in front of you. Marriage involves two people, and even their parents, as well as the combination of their respective family and ancestral cultures. When we enter into marriage, we also step into the culture of the other person's family. Of course, the core is the couple themselves, two people who love each other, supporting a new family. As long as your relationship is strong enough, you will be more flexible in dealing with issues related to other surrounding families and can overcome them through communication and effort. Your lively personality is your strength. Despite hurdles, the two of you have decided to get married, which means that you still have feelings for each other. So cherish it as you go and learn to face and solve problems. Happiness is a subjective feeling, and we can make ourselves happier.

question: 18-year-old girl, extremely sensitive, lacks a sense of security, has interpersonal difficulties.
description: 18-year-old female. My inner self is extremely sensitive. I am used to pretending to be strong and unconsciously imitating others to hide my true self in order to seek self-protection. I am not good at socializing and find it difficult to trust and rely on others from the bottom of my heart, always feeling that I will be abandoned. The state of being alone started in middle school (after my best friend transferred schools). At first, I used studying to cover up my feelings of loss and being friendless. Later, everyone formed the impression that I was a bookworm, thinking that I was naturally quiet and introverted. (I was a popular child in primary school). In high school, I rarely take the initiative to socialize with people, only responding when others approach me. On the one hand, I long to socialize with people, but on the other hand, I feel that this or that aspect of myself is not good enough, constantly thinking that others will not like me. I believe that someone like me cannot attain true friendship, so my interactions with others always remain superficial. There are people who genuinely want to be friends with me, but my reservation and lack of initiative repeatedly deter them. Honestly, I often envy groups of friends. As the college entrance examination ended, I gradually developed an affection for solitude. I do not feel the joy of socializing, I only see it as a necessity, like eating and drinking. Socializing, to me, feels more like a formality. Every social interaction is painful, but I am also afraid of not being able to adapt to society. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello: Actually, from your words, I can tell that you don't really not want to make friends or socialize. The reason you are unwilling to socialize is because you don't want others to see your flaws and imperfections. The less you socialize, the more afraid you become of socializing. Deep down, you have a vague desire for social interaction, but your self-doubt and habitual loneliness make you repel socializing. Now, your heart must be conflicted and confused. Hugs to you, I really understand how you feel. Don't worry, hopefully the following words can help you. Question 1: Regarding your lack of self-confidence, when others want to get close to you, you feel that you are not good enough in this aspect or that aspect. You think others won't like you, that someone like you won't get friendship. When you were in elementary school, you were a popular kid, but later on, you became accustomed to being alone. Before answering your question, I hope you can ask yourself the following three questions. (1) Are you really not good enough? Are others definitely not going to like you? If you have absolutely no strengths, then why would others want to get close to you? OP, no one will voluntarily approach someone they dislike. When someone approaches you, it's because they see something in you that they find attractive or intriguing. In fact, when others approach you, it's because they want to be friends with you, because you are worth starting this friendship with. Besides, nobody is perfect. We like someone and want to be friends with them not because they are perfect or without flaws, but because our personalities and interests align and we are mutually attracted to one another. Your belief that you are not good enough is actually an erroneous cognition that is influencing you. (2) Engaging with others superficially and fearing their departure when getting close. You mentioned that you engage with others superficially and then stop there. I think this has to do with your best friend transferring schools during middle school. You are a sensitive person, and it made you cautious in subsequent interpersonal relationships when a friend you genuinely bonded with left due to external circumstances. You fear that no matter how much you invest in a friendship, it will ultimately result in separation. You worry that the friendship won't last.
