Rather than experiencing loss after gaining something, it's better to not start at all, right? In our life journey, we will meet many people, and we will also part ways with many people. The passage of time, changes in our environment, including the transfer you mentioned, can lead to someone's departure. First of all, the separation from your friend in middle school was not caused by your actions but by objective reasons. So why should you shoulder the blame for someone else's departure? Friendship is also a matter of fate. Even if a close friend leaves later on, those memories will still be cherished. By rejecting all possibilities from the start, you won't experience the pain of loss, but you also won't experience the happiness that friendship brings. Moreover, with the development of technology, we grow up and have more tools to maintain connections. Perhaps when we were young, we didn't have phones to stay in touch, resulting in the loss of a friend when transferring schools. But now? You are an adult, capable of maintaining friendships, and these relationships will no longer disappear just because you change cities or schools. Question 2: Social anxiety caused by prolonged solitude. Currently, you have social anxiety. Social anxiety doesn't develop overnight, so before deciding to change, I also hope you can give yourself some time. The first time, when someone talks to you, respond actively, give yourself positive mental affirmations, try to replace old erroneous cognitions with new ones; the second time, try to initiate conversations with others, talk about topics both of you enjoy; the third time, try to engage in social activities with others, like watching movies, going shopping, etc... Start with small things, and when you accomplish each small task, your self-affirmation will be the greatest, and your self-confidence will also be greatly enhanced. Lastly, I want to say to you that it is very important to change your cognition before changing your behavior. Once your cognition changes and you start doing these small things, you will experience the joy of socializing and boost your self-confidence. You deserve to have friendships and also deserve to experience more happiness. Best wishes.

Hello! After reading your question, I want to give you a virtual hug. It seems that your inner sensitivity and insecurity have led you to build a protective shield that makes you appear strong, but also keeps you closed off. The fear of being abandoned makes you reluctant to open up and truly connect with others. First of all, please believe that you are loved and deserving of all the good things in life. Love yourself. I have a few suggestions that I hope can help you. Adjust your mindset and build self-confidence: Recognize your own worth and avoid feeling inferior or weak. Each of us is unique and has our own strengths. Don't compare your weaknesses to other people's strengths and deny your own value. Encourage and affirm yourself, and practice positive self-talk to gradually build self-confidence. Open your heart and make peace with yourself: Your fear of being abandoned causes you to close yourself off and not give others a chance to get close to you. Take a brave step forward and open up your heart. You will discover that you have friends who care about and appreciate you. Give each other a chance and start an intimate relationship. Rather than outright rejecting connections, get to know people and make choices based on understanding. Proactively communicate with others: Good communication helps us understand each other and strengthens our relationships. Develop your own interests and hobbies: Cultivating personal interests and hobbies can make your life more interesting and help you find self-worth, giving you motivation. Shared hobbies can also help you find like-minded friends. Learn to be alone: While we all need friends, we also need to be able to enjoy our own company. Reading and thinking more can enrich our inner selves. When we have a strong inner self, we can bravely face anything. Whatever lifestyle you choose, remember to make yourself happier! I am your personal mental health counselor. May my words bring warmth to you! I also appreciate it when friends drop by and read this. Feel free to follow me. Don't forget to click "Helpful"!

Questioner, hello! I carefully read your question and can sense your distress between the lines. I want to give you a strong embrace and hope that my answer can help you. Your concern is that you want to make friends but are afraid that people won't like you, so you hesitate to approach them. In reality, you lack self-confidence. How do you know that people don't like you if you never try? How can you change the current situation? Change your perception. You're afraid to make friends because you think people won't like you. This perception has always been in your mind. Ask yourself why people don't like you. But in reality, people don't dislike you. It's just your own feeling. You need to remove this idea from your mind and change your perception of the situation. You can learn how to communicate with others by reading books on social skills or learn from people around you who are skilled at socializing. Be bold and try. Because you always appear very quiet, others may think you prefer to be alone and are hesitant to approach you. You can take the initiative to make friends with others, have conversations, go out together, and genuinely treat them with sincerity. You will definitely make sincere friends who will treat you sincerely. I hope you can overcome your concerns soon! Best wishes!

It's really easy to relate to when I read this. I've also envied others for having many friends and being socially adept, able to navigate various situations with ease. Meanwhile, I struggle with talking and making new friends. In gatherings with more than three people, I find myself burying my head in my phone, disguising the fact that I don't know how to handle myself in such situations. But in reality, not everyone is naturally good at socializing. Some people may have many friends and confidants, while others may have many friends but no confidants. Some may have few friends but one or two confidants, while others may have few friends and no confidants. It all varies from person to person and not everyone can achieve having many friends with confidants. Ultimately, it comes down to personality. Assuming our personality remains unchanged (which is mostly the case), it's best to first accept ourselves. Currently, I can't manage to have a good rapport with most people and maintain those relationships. Secondly, we should strive to improve ourselves. Having many friends isn't necessary, but having a confidant is something everyone needs in terms of emotional fulfillment. Let's not focus on making a lot of friends right now, but rather start with the people around us. It could be roommates, classmates, or even our parents. Be a little kinder and more proactive towards them, express your care, accept their care, express your emotional needs, and accept theirs. This includes, but is not limited to venting, seeking help, and engaging in activities together. When we have a confidant, we can learn how to interact with different people. At that point, it will become easier to maintain acquaintances, make new friends, and keep in touch with old friends. In the case of a major change in personality, I hope it will be beneficial to your life and survival, and then we'll see how things turn out.

Hello, OP: First of all, I want to tell you that enjoying solitude can be quite a good thing. Being alone brings its own happiness, just as being with a group of people brings theirs. You don't have to worry about not being good at socializing. When you have to interact with others, you can try to slowly open up your heart, be genuine, and show your true self. It may be difficult for you at first, but you will gradually get used to it and learn some tips for dealing with others. Also, I want to tell you that two similar small stones will eventually meet. This means that you will definitely meet like-minded good friends. They may not have appeared yet, but they are waiting for you somewhere. I hope you can be happy every day! Take care.

1. "On one hand, I desire to socialize with others, but on the other hand, I feel that there is something wrong with me. The crucial point of this inner conflict lies in the belief that 'others would not like me, someone like me would not obtain friendship.' In the struggle between 'wanting' and 'not deserving,' you habitually choose to 'proactively give up' - hence, you always maintain superficial relationships with others."
2. "There are people who genuinely want to be friends with me, but they are discouraged by my reservedness and lack of initiative time and time again." - This is how you 'actively discourage' others, telling them that you are 'undeserving.'
3. Whether through 'proactively giving up' or 'actively discouraging,' there are traces of your active choices. You choose to distance yourself from others or make them stay away from you because you feel 'undeserving.'
4. Therefore, you need to identify the aspects of yourself that are already good and the areas in which you can improve. Then, armed with these 'good' qualities (remember to define what is considered 'good' as a normal person), you can choose a new way of interacting with others.

It is very simple. Just buy a book on "social skills" and read it, and you may even come up with some methods yourself. You must overcome some difficulties, but I don't think it's a problem for you. You just need a little courage and time management. Once you have new friends, all the problems you have already discovered will naturally be solved as well. Because you are very smart.

question: 25-year-old female, why has she been avoiding social interactions in the past year?
description: Start to avoid socializing, stay at home, do not go out or communicate, preferring to just stay at home.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's nice to meet you. I would like to communicate some thoughts with you. "Recently, I have been avoiding social interactions." I find the expression of this time frame meaningful - it's not that I have been avoiding social interactions all along, but only in the past year. This suggests that it is not a characteristic inherent to my personality. So what was my social state like "a year ago", and how has it changed compared to now? There must have been something that happened at that time point "a year ago" that led to a change in my social state. You can try to "search forward" from a year ago to the present, or "search backward" from the present to a year ago, relying on your first instincts to find that special event. "Not going out, not contacting anyone" corresponds to "used to be in contact". So what do those people that I used to be in contact with mean to me? Where are they now? Since when did we stop contacting each other? Did something bad happen? You need to find the answers yourself. "Willing to stay at home" can be done in many ways, such as lying in bed all day watching dramas, scrolling through Weibo, playing games, studying, and so on. What is your current state while staying at home? Are you satisfied with your current state? If you are, then you don't need to worry about your social state. Maybe you just haven't met someone you want to contact or discovered a place you want to go outside. If you are not satisfied, then you need to first understand what kind of life state you want. You can break down your goals into smaller pieces and work on achieving them gradually without forcing yourself to achieve everything at once. Lastly, I want to say that the process of growing up for young people nowadays is becoming increasingly lonely. Physical distance reduces common topics between friends, and we have so many problems to deal with in life that we are too busy to care about some things... Growing up is probably like this, gradually becoming distant and losing touch... We are all experiencing the same journey.

Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs. From your description, I understand that you have been wanting to avoid social interactions recently. Here's my analysis and advice in hopes of helping you: Today, I came across a saying that roughly means what we try to escape from might be exactly what we fear. I wonder if this saying applies to you? Perhaps it can provide you with a new perspective. We are around the same age, and I have also experienced a similar situation. Whenever this happens to me, I write or go out by myself for a walk, just to see things around me. I find that when I come back, I feel much better. I suggest you try doing the same. #The world and I love you. Take care~

question: Unable to accept work adjustments, always unable to pull oneself back?
description: Recently, there have been some adjustments in my work, and I just can't accept it. I worry every day that I won't be able to handle the current work arrangement. I have trouble sleeping and feel anxious. I don't know how to overcome the fear in my heart.

answers.answer_text: Hugs to the OP~ When faced with new job responsibilities, and the possibility of a new work environment, we all feel anxious and worried. I have also been temporarily reassigned to a completely unfamiliar position, with only two days to transition. I used to be so anxious that when I was on the bus, I hoped it would never stop so that I wouldn't have to face it. Of course, I eventually got off the bus and went to the new job, forcing myself to adapt to the new position and new work. And in the end, I did well. Let me share my feelings: Firstly, you have to believe in your ability to handle the new job arrangements. Think about the work we did before. Didn't we do it well? We went from not knowing to knowing, from being unfamiliar to mastering it. We will gradually become familiar with the new job arrangements, and it might even become our strength. Don't doubt yourself, believe that you can handle the new job arrangements. Secondly, start with the easiest aspects. If the new job arrangements are truly difficult to adapt to, start with the simplest aspects, make progress step by step, and gradually gain mastery. Once you achieve a little, you will start to have confidence in yourself and it will become easier. Thirdly, ask for advice and think more. If you find it difficult to grasp on your own, ask others for help. Sometimes, even after pondering for a long time, we still can't find a solution, but when we ask an experienced person for advice, they can often point us in the right direction and solve the problem. At the end of each day, summarize what you have learned, what problems you have encountered, and what experiences you have gained. I think work is sometimes like a jigsaw puzzle. At the beginning, it's difficult, and we don't know where each piece should go. But gradually, we will figure out where each fragment fits, and once we complete the puzzle, we will handle the work with ease.

question: 14, it seems like a lot has happened, and it feels like you want to leave?
description: Oh, I don't know what's wrong with me. During this holiday, I don't know what happened. My parents got divorced, separated, moved, the company closed down, and we have loans to pay. They ignore the law, curse at me, and take away my hope. Many friends left, and I feel isolated. My grades have plummeted... It seems like so many things have happened. But actually, I didn't really care about all these things. I'm naturally cold. I just feel inexplicably sad, unable to feel happiness. It's like I grew up, like I really want to leave. Cutting my arm, it feels like only when the blood flows out and I feel pain, can I feel that I'm still alive. My heart seems to hurt a lot, like a walking corpse. I don't know what I should do, what I can do. I feel like jumping off a building, really wanting to leave. But I kind of don't want to leave my favorite idol, I still want to see him become popular. But at the same time, I'm very clear-headed and rational about everything. I also know who I am, the gaps, the distance, the problems... I understand that even if I die, he won't know, and it has nothing to do with him being popular. Reading those inspirational quotes only gives me temporary excitement. Watching funny videos, I can laugh too, but after laughing, everything still feels empty. Everything is fake, I'm fake too. How long will I continue to exist in this world? Does my future still exist... I don't know if I have some strange illness, but not telling anyone would cost a lot of money, right.

answers.answer_text: Hello, this holiday, I suddenly experienced a lot of things: my parents divorce and separate, the company closing down, friends leaving, being isolated by others, and so on. I feel sad and unhappy, but these are normal emotions, right? It seems abnormal if you don't feel sad or upset at all. It's okay, if you feel sad and want to cry, you can let it out. If you have someone you trust, you can talk to them, and if you don't, you can write in a diary. When you express these things, your thoughts and feelings, it seems like a burden is lifted from your shoulders and can make you feel much lighter. Don't hurt yourself, don't cut your arms; the feeling of pain will only temporarily make you feel your existence, but it won't help you solve problems or improve your emotions. It might even trap you in negative emotions. Doing something positive, something you like, something relaxing, something valuable, can better help you feel alive, feel your worth and significance. You have a favorite idol, and I think the greatest meaning of idols is that they provide us with spiritual support, showing us that life can be so wonderful and brilliant, encouraging us to continue striving and working hard, striving to get closer to idols and become excellent people like them. So, no matter who your idol is, accompany them on their journey and strive together, watching them succeed and watching your own life become more colorful. It's okay to have differences and distance. Everyone's starting point, conditions, and opportunities are different. If we can do our best with our current conditions, then at least our efforts and endeavors are on the same level as the idols, not much worse than them. Believe in yourself, you are also amazing! Your future definitely exists and can be wonderful. You must believe in this! Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Dear asker, hello! Sending you a warm hug! Your favorite celebrity really needs your support! Please do pay attention to them and wait for them to become famous all over the country! I can also support them together with you! Take good care of your body, stay healthy, and maybe we can even meet up once the epidemic is over! We all go through many things that help us grow. I don't know which parent you are currently with, but maybe you could talk to them? Don't worry, don't be afraid, the world and I love you!

question: I want to date, but I feel extremely repelled whenever someone approaches me. What should I do?
description: I am a female, a senior in college, about to graduate. Before I even started college, I would tell people that I wanted to experience campus dating. But now, in the blink of an eye, I'm already in my third year and I still haven't had a romantic relationship. Sometimes, when I see couples together, I feel very envious and long for a sweet romance. Especially when my friends are slowly getting into relationships, this feeling becomes stronger. However, when other guys show interest in me, I start to push them away. I am afraid that if they like me and express a desire to be with me, my mind starts to overthink and I convince myself that we are not compatible. Then, I slowly distance myself from them. But deep down, I still envy others and really want to experience a romantic relationship. What should I do?
keywords: Love, single, sense of security, relationship management

answers.answer_text: Hi, have you heard of lithromanticism? It refers to a sexual orientation where one develops romantic feelings for someone but does not desire reciprocation. First, ask yourself a few questions: 1) Do you consider being in a romantic relationship necessary for your life? 2) How do you envision "being in love"? Is this the kind of love you desire? 3) What is the reason behind your fear of boys liking you? Is it because of the boys themselves or something within you? 4) If it is due to something within you, think about where your fear of intimacy comes from. By answering these questions, you will gain a deeper understanding of your lithromantic tendencies. For instance, you may discover that while you long for an intimate partner, you also have a strong fear of getting hurt in a close relationship, possibly stemming from your upbringing. Lithromanticism is a common sexual orientation, and the most important thing is to first accept and understand yourself. Once you have analyzed the reasons, you can then address them accordingly.

Also registered in the Chinese Psychological Association registration system as a registered psychologist, I would like to offer the following insights: The establishment of intimate relationships in adulthood actually tests the solidity and flexibility of our personalities. In other words, it tests whether we are capable of accepting someone into our inner selves while maintaining our independence. From your description, it seems that subconsciously you may feel that being intimate with someone implies losing yourself. In other words, once an intimate relationship is established, you may feel inherently unsafe and distance yourself from romantic relationships in order to protect yourself. The most likely reason for this is past traumatic experiences. Healing from trauma still requires intimate relationships. If you want to avoid the harm that comes from establishing intimate relationships in an unstable state, I suggest starting with professional counseling relationships, focusing on personal growth first, and then gradually establishing high-quality intimate relationships.

question: Ask for a friend: What should I do when I have disputes with my parents about money matters?
description: A close friend of mine recently confided in me that her parents are demanding she give them 1000 yuan from her salary every month, or else they won't let her live at home. The situation now is that she has just started working for 2 months and also needs to pay for her own insurance, meals, transportation, daily necessities, cosmetics, etc. (Her monthly salary is 5000 yuan). She told me her parents keep mentioning how they spent a lot of money on her education abroad and now they want her to "pay back" those expenses with her salary. I feel that the main issue now is the communication between her and her parents, but I don't know how to help her.

answers.answer_text: If there are only two choices, or it's a black or white situation, it seems that what you're describing is a dilemma. But if you adjust your thoughts and perspectives, perhaps the dilemma won't be a dilemma anymore. Ask your friend: 1) First, focus on how your parents are doing? If your family is financially tight because of your studying abroad, or even has debts, it wouldn't be excessive for your friend to pay 1000 yuan after starting work, especially considering the cost of living at home. If the family conditions are good, but parents still demand your friend to pay 1000 yuan for living expenses, and the condition is to move out if they don't pay, I think it's reasonable for parents to ask your friend to take on some basic family responsibilities once they are capable of earning money. What do you think? We might have an ingrained mindset that says, "I'm the child, you love me, so you should..." and once it's not that way, we start to doubt if our parents still love us. But that's really overthinking it. When we lack the capability, our parents support us, and that's great. When we have the ability, we should share the family responsibilities. Isn't it normal? How did it become a source of distress? Ask yourself if there are certain ideas that parents should absolutely... in your unhappiness. Remind your friend that when they grow up and become adults and start earning money, they need to gradually embody the attitude of an adult and understand what responsibility means. 2) Your friend mentioned the practical difficulties of just starting work for 2 months. They need to pay for their own insurance, meals, transportation, daily necessities, cosmetics, etc. (their salary is 5000 yuan per month). It might not seem like much, but even if it's not a lot, it's still not a reason to not take responsibility, right? Change roles and mentally prepare yourself for having your own family in the future: taking on responsibilities. You can ask your parents how they managed when they didn't have money, and how they managed to support your friend in completing their education. Being an adult means learning to solve problems rather than shifting blame or avoiding them. 3) When parents talk about repayment, are they really asking your friend to repay? Or are they using it as an excuse to push your friend to grow, save money, and take on responsibilities? A parent's love for their child is the only form of love that guides toward separation. Parents love their children because they hope that one day their child can live independently, and independence brings great happiness. This love is truly profound, and children may not understand until they reach a certain age or gain certain experiences. So you can chat with your friend about what would happen if they're not willing to pay the 1000 yuan and choose to live independently. If there are no issues, they can give it a try. Of course, moving out doesn't mean cutting off contact with parents; it's just to see how they would fare without their parents. Going back to what I said earlier, between moving out and not moving out, there are still many other choices. Ask your friend if they can think of anything else.

Thank you for trusting me to answer your question. It is evident that you are a helpful person who cares about your friend. Let's discuss:
1. Your friend coming out to work means that she is already an adult and an independent individual. At the same time, she is still living at home, and it is reasonable and necessary for her to contribute to the household expenses. This is her part of taking responsibility for the family.
2. As for whether she can meet her parents' request of 1000 yuan, it depends on the family's situation and her own daily expenses. If she can afford this expense, she may need to reduce other expenditures in her daily life. If she is willing to do so, or if she really cannot afford it, she should communicate and negotiate with her family to see if they would agree to lessen the amount for now and increase it later when her salary increases. Both sides should reach a mutual understanding, so that her parents understand that she is not avoiding her responsibility but is facing actual difficulties.
3. If her parents accumulated a lot of debt for her to study abroad, she must take on that obligation and repay it together. However, this depends on the specific situation and requires a good negotiation and understanding with her parents about each other's practical needs. I wish you all the best!

Title owner, hello: You described that your friend confided in you about this issue, but you don't know how to help her. Usually, when we encounter problems, we face and deal with them based on our own past experiences and values. If you don't know how to help her, can you not handle it? Your friend has previously received financial support from her family to study abroad. Her family has spent a lot of money for her education abroad, which shows that her parents have put in a lot of effort and money to cultivate her. Now her parents require her to give them money every month. Is it really because her parents love money or because the family is short of money? There is an old saying in China, "It is not until one has his own children that he truly understands the love of parents." What is this love? Anna Quindlen, a bestselling author of The New York Times and a Pulitzer Prize winner, once said, "There is a kind of love that is meant for separation. In this world, all love is meant for bringing people together, except for one kind of love, which is the love of parents for their children. The true success of parents' love is not keeping their children by their side, but fostering their independence and letting them go." This love is about truly making the child independent and becoming themselves. I believe if you can help your friend see and understand this kind of love from her parents, she will naturally know how to handle this matter. Above all, I hope this is helpful to you.

Hmm... when I saw this question, honestly, I was taken aback for a moment. Because in my understanding, there shouldn't be parents who are so difficult to tolerate. If the question is asked on behalf of a friend, I suggest you find out more about your friend's family situation to see if it's really as strange as you described. Now, I will respond based on the situation you mentioned. If it is indeed the case, then: 1) Firstly, if a family is able to afford to send their child abroad, the financial situation should not be so difficult that they have to pressure their child for 1,000 yuan. If there have been any changes in the family, shouldn't the child, who has always enjoyed excellent conditions provided by the family, take on the responsibility proactively? Since you have studied abroad, there should be more than one way to make money, right? Even if it's just a salary, spending should be prioritized. If the family is asking you for living expenses, shouldn't you remove luxury items like cosmetics from your budget and opt for a more frugal lifestyle? 2) Secondly, if there haven't been any changes in the family, why would parents, who have always been tolerant, suddenly exert such pressure on their child for 1,000 yuan? As a child, shouldn't you care about whether something is wrong with your parents or if there are any problems in your relationship with them? 3) Lastly, personally, I find it extremely difficult to believe that the situation you described is real life. Hmm?

Hello, I guess you must be someone who is really good to their friends. It's truly fortunate to have you as a friend. The question you raised is something that many people may have encountered. So, in your opinion, what could be the reason that your friend's parents insist on having your friend give them 1000 dollars every month? Is it because their family really needs the money, or could there be other reasons behind it? When your friend is feeling relaxed, as a friend, it's easy to want to give her some advice to help her. At the same time, you may also be concerned about how you can help her since "it's hard for an outsider to understand domestic affairs." In situations like this, as a friend, just listening to her vent and providing companionship is already a way to help her. Besides being there for her, you can also share your opinions on the matter based on your judgment and experience, and discuss possible strategies with her. The above is just my personal viewpoint, for your reference only. Take care of yourself.

question: Do some small actions reflect one's psychological state?
description: A 10-year-old child picks at the hangnails on their fingernails, resulting in small wounds. From what I understand, this kind of involuntary behavior could be indicative of anxiety, is that correct?

answers.answer_text: In addition to the possibility of anxiety, the main reason is the dryness and lack of oil in the skin. When caring for a child's mental health, it is important to consider other aspects as well: whether they are reluctant to speak, love to be alone, or have difficulty making eye contact while speaking. Do they engage in self-talk? Are they unusually stubborn? Nowadays, life is fast-paced, and some parents are unable to be with their children, leaving many children in the care of others. Therefore, the physical and mental well-being of children should not be neglected, after all, in China, we work hard and endure hardships for the sake of the next generation.

question: The pressure for the future is overwhelming, and I am very worried about ending up in the lower class of society. How can I relieve my mindset?
description: My mom has always taught me to never be lazy because it's sad to end up in the lower class of society. So I'm a bit scared because I'm not excellent enough. How can I improve my mindset?

answers.answer_text: Main topic, hello, I think I can understand your feelings very well. Parents always tell themselves that if you don't work hard, you will end up at the bottom, and even say that I don't have the strength and strong body to even do the lowest level of work. Because I was introverted since I was young, I didn't have much contact with people and things, so I naturally believed my parents' words very easily. But I have a great inertia and I don't really like studying, so I often play while feeling anxious, always thinking that I am not outstanding enough and won't be able to support myself in the future. But when I went to college, others told me that in this developed era, as long as you are not particularly picky and lazy, you can naturally get by in life. Maybe it won't be too comfortable, but at least you won't be unable to support yourself. So, from this aspect, you can also understand that at least we can be self-reliant. Then, the main topic may think that being at the bottom is not good because of the influence of parents. Actually, I think there is no such thing as the so-called bottom. What people generally think of as the bottom probably refers to those with low wages, hard work, and getting dirty every day. However, every profession has its unknown and arduous side. There is really a big social bias. Some people earn money through physical strength and some through intellect, and there is a hierarchy of disdain. However, everyone is making efforts to rely on their brains and does not want to do dirty or tiring work, but there will always be people who do it. These are also indispensable professions in life. In such a discriminatory society, none of us can completely avoid it. If the main topic cannot achieve a completely unbiased mindset, then strive to do a glamorous job. If you are not afraid of others' opinions, just be yourself. It's good to have an easy job, and it's perfectly fine to work harder if you don't. Best wishes~.

Hello, OP, sending you warm hugs~ In almost all the education we receive, we are asked to be an upward, positive, and outstanding person. Many people, however, don't feel that they are exceptional. Your perception of yourself may not align with how others see you, as they may recognize your strengths and believe you excel in certain areas. So, maybe you should consider giving yourself more confidence, discover your own strengths, and jot them down. This kind of behavior can reinforce your self-esteem. If you feel that you are not an outstanding person, what areas do you think you can improve on? It is also a way to stand up for yourself. Believe that everyone feels they are not the most perfect; their imperfections are areas for personal growth. Reducing self-doubt and anxiety may help you improve yourself and lead a better life. Best wishes~.

question: My 7-year-old niece, her mother passed away, and recently she always cries for her mother.
description: My niece's mother passed away when she was three years old. Now she lives with her grandmother. When she was little, she was very reliant on others, especially her mother. She would always want someone to hold her and would cry for a long time if no one did. But sometimes she seems mature for her age, which is heart-wrenching. Even when she was very young, she knew her mother was gone and never mentioned her. Recently, she has been calling out for her mother, calling any female figure around her "Mom." There was even a period of time when she told us, "I only want Dad, not Mom." I think she is very sensitive and stubborn. Sometimes, when she is upset, she will hide in her room and cry alone. She is easily saddened and when asked what's wrong or why she's like this, she remains tight-lipped and doesn't say a word. What can I do to help her grow up happy?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~~~ From the description, we can understand that 1. OP's niece lost her mother when she was young and now occasionally shows emotional confusion. 2. OP is very concerned about her niece and hopes to be able to help her a little bit. Analysis and suggestions: 1. When a child loses their mother at a time when they still need parental care and attachment, they may experience a lack of security, sensitivity, suspicion, distrust of others, and insecurity about others' care. It can be seen that OP is a gentle and kind person who sincerely hopes to help her young niece. However, it is not very likely that all these symptoms will disappear in a short period of time. 2. When dealing with such children, it is not wise to ask what is on their mind or what makes them unhappy. Even if asked, she probably won't say. Most of the time, genuine care and companionship are more important. The child is still at an age where they love to play, so OP should often accompany her, play her favorite games, bring her some favorite snacks, and toys she likes. If the child wants to say something to OP, just be a gentle listener, comfort her, and give her a hug. Hopefully, this will be helpful to OP.

question: Why do I want to talk to someone when I'm alone, but then I don't feel like talking after a while?
description: Many times, I find myself alone in the room, whether I have nothing to do or something to keep busy, I often think about finding someone to chat with. But after chatting for a while, I don't feel like continuing the conversation, I feel a little annoyed or I have the thought of wanting to be alone again. I find this very strange.

answers.answer_text: Hello, give you a warm hug, whether you want someone to accompany or want to be alone, it is our freedom and our choice. But what actually causes us to have different thoughts and results is the purpose of our actions, whether it is simply boredom or habit? Or feeling lonely? Or finding it interesting? Or wanting to work with others? Different purposes naturally lead to different results, resulting in different behaviors. For example, there can be several reasons for what you mentioned: wanting someone to accompany, but also worrying that your safety zone will be violated, so while accepting, you will also be on guard and keep your distance. Wanting to maintain good communication or habits, but lacking patience, or feeling disturbed and annoyed when you are busy, causing you to not want to chat. Being easily excited for a short period, feeling happy to chat with someone one moment, but feeling uninterested and bored when someone actually starts chatting, thinking that being alone is more suitable. Lastly, there is a possibility that is almost unlikely but does exist: fluctuations caused by mental illness. I hope my answer can help you (･ω･)ﾉ.

question: I'm already 17 years old, why can't I live without my mom?
description: I was raised by my mother alone. I have a deep emotional bond with her since childhood. Every time I have to leave her and go far away (especially at night when I can't come back home), my mood would plummet, I can't stop crying, I lose motivation in everything, and all I can think about is "I want to go home, I want my mom". I cannot eat or sleep well, and I even start to break down and cry uncontrollably. The first time this happened was when I went to a summer camp for three days in elementary school. I realized that I couldn't be apart from her, and after returning home, my emotions were so low that I cried continuously and even took a two-week break from school. I thought it was because I was young at the time, but in high school, during the year when I had military training and had to leave home, the same thing happened again. However, I managed to get through it because I had close friends. She knows that I have this problem, so she purposely chose a university close to home for me to attend. But because of the pandemic, the university might be closed, and I don't know when I can go home and see her. My emotions are on the verge of breaking down again. These past few days, I have cried several times and can't pack my bags at all because I will cry so much that I can't do anything. As soon as I think about not being able to determine when I can go home, I feel desperate. Thinking of the scene when I said goodbye and cried to her at school, tears stream down my face. I'm almost an adult and I still can't be independent from her. What should I do? Is this a mental illness? How can I be happy again?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, growth process.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, your deep bond with your mother is evident as she single-handedly raised you. Since elementary school, you have always felt exceptionally distressed when separated from her. I understand your feelings very well. I hope the following questions will be helpful to you. First, I want to clarify that your situation is not a psychological problem. In your upbringing, your mother has provided you with more than enough love. Due to her being the only person in your life, you have not had the opportunity to interact with the outside world. Your world revolves around your mother, and over time, your dependence on her has become significant. Therefore, when you are separated, you feel extremely sad and upset. This is very normal, and I completely understand. After all, your mother is your whole world, and leaving her leaves you feeling lonely and sorrowful. However, at 17 years old, if you still cannot be independent from your mother, it means that you have not yet developed enough independence of your own. Suggestions: 1. Try taking the first step towards independence. The first attempt at separation is the most painful. However, if you do not take that initial step, you will not be able to truly grow up, nor will you be able to put your mother's mind at ease. I remember on the first day of university, that was the first time I didn't live with my family. At that time, my parents and grandparents accompanied me to the school, and after they left, I felt so sad in my dorm room. I wanted to go back home and didn't even want to stay at school. But can I not go to college? Obviously, I can't. So, I tried to calm down, called my good friends, and vented my feelings of sadness. Gradually, I adapted to the unfamiliar environment and my college life. When you go to college, you have to physically leave your mother; this is an inevitable choice. When you bravely take the first step towards independence, you will become more and more mature and independent over time. 2. Shift your focus. OP, being separated from your mother is very difficult for you. When you are sad, why not try doing something else? For example, talking to your good friends on the phone, watching your favorite TV shows, or going out for a run? When your attention is no longer fixated on the separation, your emotions will be greatly relieved. 3. Try building a new social circle for yourself. In your first 17 years of life, your mother has been the center of your world, and all you have seen is her. Now that you are in college, you have to grow up. You can meet new friends and classmates at school to expand your social circle. When you no longer feel lonely at school, your feelings of sadness will diminish. Lastly, I want to say that most of the time, our growth is not something we are prepared for, and sometimes it is not even what we truly want. If possible, we all want to stay by the side of our loved ones forever, never to be separated. However, as individuals in society, we are pushed forward by time. So, we have to learn to be independent, face separation, and deal with sadness. I believe that when you find happiness and success in your college life, your mother will also be very happy. Moreover, even if you cannot meet in person for a short period, you can express your yearning for your mother through phone calls, right? May you become an independent and better version of yourself. Take care.

Hello, in the Safe Haven, especially for family members who have been living together for a long time, we have a sense of dependence. Their presence is a psychological comfort zone for us. You grew up with your mother, and it was just the two of you in this home, which made this sense of dependence even stronger. Because you are each other's emotional support. Therefore, the discomfort you feel due to the separation will be even stronger. I can understand the psychological discomfort you are experiencing at the moment. However, dear, separation is also a normal part of life. What we can do is learn to grow through separation. As you said, you are almost an adult and need to step out of the comfort zone that your mother has provided for you. You need to learn to be independent because, after all, your mother cannot accompany you forever. What you need to do is not resist this separation but learn to accept it. I hope you can find the courage to be strong and brave, to learn to communicate with other people around you, to adapt to new roles and environments, and to grow up well even without your mother's presence. After all, your mother, as the saying goes, "a son travels a thousand miles, but the mother worries." She hopes that everything will be fine for you. Good luck!

Hello, I'm sorry to see that you're feeling sad. Even though we are 17 years old physically, deep down we still have the heart of a little girl who needs her mother's company. Your mother has raised you all by herself, and you can say that you and your mother have always relied on each other. Not only can you not be without your mother, but your mother also sees you as the strength that supports her to keep going. Your mother must have sacrificed a lot for you. However, as we grow older, children eventually have to grow up and leave home to start their own independent lives. We have to face the fact of separating from our caregivers. In fact, you have had a successful experience of separation before, when you went through military training in high school with the companionship of your dear friends. This is a very good experience. You have been able to do it before, which fully demonstrates that you can do it again. However, because we are not used to it, the experience brings us unfamiliar and even painful feelings. It might be helpful to review that experience, your own emotional journey, and how you managed to get through it. Are there any methods that can be applied again? In addition, we can ask our mother to help us. Mothers often can't bear to see their children in distress and unconsciously want to protect you and indulge your personality. But this actually deprives you of the opportunity for personal growth and can bring more troubles to your future life. Let your mother help you, for example, by extending the time you spend with each other or changing face-to-face meetings to video calls, etc., with your mother supervising the execution. During this period, it might be difficult to endure the emotions that come from restraining ourselves. We might feel sad, helpless, and even cry like before. In this case, you can seek help from trustworthy classmates and friends to help you get through this period. Mothers are the sacred harbor for everyone, but at the same time, mothers and we are also independent individuals. Finding like-minded friends, nurturing our social circles, and cultivating our own interests and hobbies will help us better adapt to our independent lives outside of the family and discover the beauty of this world beyond the family.

Hug the original poster. OP's statement reminds me of myself during adolescence. At that time, my social circle was not wide, and I was introverted and sensitive. I was very afraid of living without a mother. The first time I left home to board, as someone who was not good at making friends, I felt lonely, bored, and wronged. At that time, I couldn't imagine that I would adapt well to a life without family around. As I gradually grew physically, I transformed from a weak and easily ill state to a strong and robust young adult. I began to have a strong curiosity about the world and desired to go out and see a broader world. Because OP was raised by a mother since childhood and lacked the necessary care from a father during their growth, they often had to rely on their mother. Over time, they found it increasingly difficult to be separated from their mother, and this state gradually accumulated. Sudden environmental changes can easily bring huge psychological impacts to OP, which is why they have shown signs of psychological breakdown several times. So, how to solve the accumulated problems gradually? I think a gradual dissipation method is more suitable for OP's situation. There are multiple aspects that contribute to this problem, and having control over the causes is beneficial for OP's future growth. On one hand, the reliance on the mother may be due to a lack of awareness of the need to gradually become independent, a lack of independence consciousness. On the other hand, it is also possible that the mother is not aware of the independence issues that OP is facing in their growth. Perhaps, for other reasons, the mother feels sorry for OP and gives most of her love to OP, but may overlook the importance of OP's independence. The mother may have her own limitations from her perspective, especially in the absence of a father. We often say that most love in the world is directed towards reunion, only the love of parents points to separation. How to gradually resolve this issue? OP can start with themselves, focusing on small things, such as independently solving things within their ability, summarizing their problem-solving experiences, expressing to the mother the desire to try things on their own when the mother habitually offers help, expanding their social circle with peers (regardless of gender), seeking communication with teachers and elders when encountering problems, exercising and improving physical fitness, participating in activities to shift attention... Every time OP completes a small task, give themselves a big encouragement. A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. When you start doing this, the future will quietly have opportunities for change, until one day when you look back at your past self, you will benefit greatly!

Lou Lou, hello️️ I really understand the issues you are facing, as I am also someone like you.️ First of all, the problem Lou Lou is facing is not being able to be separated from their mother. We can dig deeper into this, why can't Lou Lou be separated from their mother? Lou Lou said they got through it because of their close friends during military training, so it's not necessarily that Lou Lou can't be separated from their mother. It could be that their mother takes care of them in every way, or perhaps their mother can accompany them in everything they do, or maybe Lou Lou can't adapt to the unfamiliar environment outside. Lou Lou needs to think carefully about these reasons!️ Next, let's try to resolve this!️ No matter what the reason is, first Lou Lou needs to try to accept the reality of going to school and being away from their mother. These are things that can't be avoided just by not wanting to go. Actually, I always feel unhappy before the start of school, just like Lou Lou.️ But as time goes on, everything will slowly happen and I won't feel so bad anymore, so it's important to learn to face it.️ Then, consciously exercise your independence. Think about how you managed to get through things without your mother before, and repeat that feeling. So this time, you can also overcome it.️ Finally, interact more with people, participate in activities to divert your attention, so that you won't dwell too much on this matter. Maybe you will discover that even without your mother, you can take care of yourself.️ I hope my answer can help you️ Take care.

Hello: Child, temporary departure is nothing, do not always immerse yourself in longing, learn to overcome it, people will grow up, try to make some friends to distract your attention, or focus on studying. It is not easy for mom to take care of you alone, if you love mom, you must learn to grow up, learn to be strong, only then can mom be reassured.

question: Is it true that people are all alike? Is our uniqueness just self-comfort?
description: Sometimes we may come across people who are similar to ourselves or certain "types" of people. This kind of categorization makes people feel bored, as if there are only a few types of people in the world. It can be disappointing, but the educational belief is that every person is unique and has their own value, which is definite. However, this seems contradictory. How should we deal with such thoughts?

answers.answer_text: From what perspective, from a human perspective, our structure is the same. When we see a creature approaching, we can determine if it's a human being. If it's about personality or spirit, there are no repetitions, everything is unique. When you talk about categorizing, it is only some people who are similar in certain places, such as values or other areas, like the intersection in mathematics (don't know if you've studied it). Multiple sets may only have some overlap, so everyone is different, and so are you.

question: It has been 45 days since I've been depressed. What is the meaning of life?
description: I have been depressed for 45 days now. In the past week, as soon as I wake up in the morning, I can't help but ask myself: What is the purpose of living? I increasingly don't want to live anymore, and I feel like someone wants to kill me, including my parents and myself... So, the day before yesterday, I almost attempted suicide for real. I want to ask you, what are people really living for? Why do those disabled people desperately want to live in this unbearable world? Thank you for your answer.
keywords: Emotions, depressive feelings, guilt, shame, panic, and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello ~ What is the meaning of being alive? Perhaps being alive is to find this meaning. Being alive means that you can still see the sun tomorrow, you can still have expectations for tomorrow, because you can never imagine what might happen tomorrow. Being alive is like a journey, where we experience joy, feel sadness, and we can go see beautiful scenery, drink milk tea, watch movies, read books and follow TV shows. If you were to leave forever, all of these possibilities would cease to exist. You ask, "Why do those disabled people desperately want to live in this unbearable world?" Because in their eyes, this world is not unbearable, but still worth looking forward to. Perhaps someone sitting in a wheelchair finds it enjoyable to bask in the sun in the courtyard every day, and someone who is blind finds satisfaction in being able to hear music and the sounds of nature... Maybe one day, with advancements in medical technology, they can stand up again and see once more. Why not wait a little longer and have some more expectations? You say you have been depressed for 45 days, but what were you like before those 45 days? Were there no moments worth looking forward to during that time? If you feel terrible after a breakup, you can still look forward to a sweet romance. If you have experienced something unpleasant at home or encountered problems at work, those are only temporary. It's better to make more efforts and look forward to life in ten or eight years. Stay positive, anything is possible. Best wishes ~.

Depression is really a terrifying illness, not because it can make people have suicidal thoughts, but because it can make people unable to control their thoughts even when they know they shouldn't be. If you feel that someone wants to kill you, it means that deep down you still have a desire to live. It's just that you can't figure out why you should live, so why not stop thinking about it altogether. The question of why people live is a question without an answer. The high-level white-collar workers in big cities are always in a hurry every day, the elderly in rural areas sunbathe every day, the workers on construction sites sweat profusely every day, and there are also young people lying in bed playing with their phones all day...These people all say they don't understand why they live for! The reason why people feel depressed is because they are extremely disappointed in certain things. I know a friend who became depressed because he couldn't stand this society. For a long time, he didn't do anything and was extremely impulsive towards suicide. His family sent him to a mental hospital for four months, and he said that the days inside were the most painful for him. When he came out, he called his parents and went to the park to drink pesticide. It took a long time to find the police, and his father was about to give up. Fortunately, his mother was unwilling to let her child go like this, and she searched everywhere with tears in her eyes before finally saving him. The doctors said that it was a miracle that he survived. Later, he embarked on the path of spirituality. In his own words: since he doesn't know why he's alive, he'll live for others! He doesn't ask for a great life, just to stay alive. This friend is not someone else, he is my own brother. I am very grateful that he has been reborn, and I hope you can overcome all difficulties and obstacles soon!

question: 21 years old and having a boyfriend, is it wrong for my mother to excessively interfere in my intimate relationship?
description: I am now 21 years old and have a boyfriend, this is my third one. I have broken up with the previous two. I feel like there is always an obstacle in every relationship I have, this obstacle prevents me from enjoying love and makes me afraid of love. My mother gets too involved in my love life. Every time I come home, I have to explain to her what I did with my boyfriend, where we went. She even tries to control our intimacy and teaches me what to do. The more she does this, the more scared I become. I'm afraid if I did something wrong. So every time I have to make a decision about love, I feel conflicted, torn between listening to myself or listening to my mother. Am I wrong?
keywords: Family, communication with parents, growth process, family control.

answers.answer_text: You are facing the excessive intervention and interference of a controlling mother, losing your autonomy and judgment, which brings confusion and fear in your love life. Many parents have a natural desire to control their children, interfering in many aspects of their lives, making arrangements and decisions for them, especially when it comes to dating, they cannot trust their children's choices and want to screen and evaluate potential partners on their behalf. Perhaps your mother has been constantly interfering in your emotional life, as well as controlling and arranging many aspects of your life since you were young. Growing up under the parenting style of controlling parents, children are deprived of their autonomy, making it difficult for them to develop independent, self-confident personalities and abilities. They struggle to establish their own cognitive standards for many things, making confident decisions is also challenging, and they often do not know how to say "no" to their parents or lack the courage to reject and resist their control and interference. Therefore, when your mother constantly interferes in your and your boyfriend's affairs, giving unsolicited advice and making numerous comments, you feel dependent on her and increasingly lack confidence in your own relationship. You also don't know how to face, judge, and make decisions for yourself. On one hand, you lack self-confidence and do not believe that your judgment is correct; on the other hand, you are afraid of making choices that go against your mother's will and facing criticism and blame if anything goes wrong. As a result, you find yourself in a state of uncertainty and turmoil, unable to establish a healthy, trusting intimate relationship with your boyfriend. Your compliance and concessions also make your mother unaware that her interference is invasive and controlling behavior, causing harm to you. In fact, you have already seen your mother's control and interference, and her intrusive behavior has caused you great distress and discomfort. You are already 21 years old, an adult with the ability, rights, and qualifications to be independent and assert your own rights, and to achieve psychological separation from your parents. For you, who are suffering, the first thing you need to change is yourself - no longer easily giving in and obeying, and learning to say "no" to your mother, rejecting her interference and control, expressing your thoughts and feelings, stating your attitude, and protecting your boundaries. Perhaps for your mother, who is used to controlling and managing everything about you, she may not immediately accept your protest, and it may be difficult to see immediate results from your resistance, but taking this step is the first step towards change and gives your mother the opportunity to see your stance. Establishing these boundaries and asserting your autonomy will require prolonged and repeated "battles". It requires your courage, confidence, and persistence.

Hi there! ※From your description, I understand that your mother is overly involved in your love life, always telling you what you should and shouldn't do. This interference makes you feel anxious and conflicted whenever you have to make decisions regarding your relationships. You're unsure whether this is your problem or your mother's, which is causing you a lot of confusion. From what you've described, it is clear that your mother is a cautious, responsible, and loving person. She is afraid of you getting hurt in relationships, so she wants to give you advice to protect you from being deceived. It's commendable that your mother has good intentions, but her actions have become overwhelming for you and are crossing boundaries! At 21 years old, you are already an adult, and even at the age where marriage is acceptable. When it comes to love and marriage, you should have your own beliefs and thoughts, rather than always living under your mother's shadow. It's natural for you to feel uncomfortable in such a situation. We all hope to live in a free environment, so you can try communicating with your mother. Share your feelings with her, and most importantly, let her know that you have grown up and are no longer an ignorant little girl. You have your own ideas and want to make independent decisions. In the eyes of our parents, no matter how old we are, we will always be children. However, we must recognize that while we are growing up, our parents are getting older. Growing up means we have to face life independently, make decisions independently, and can't always rely on our parents. You need to first be aware of this issue yourself and then make your mom aware of it. It would be best to have a good discussion with your mom about this issue, and perhaps there will be some improvement! Best wishes!

question: What should I do if I spend 10 hours a day reading novels and always immerse myself in fantasies?
description: Ever since I started reading romance novels in high school, I have become addicted and unable to quit. In university, I can spend up to 10 hours a day reading novels, and on weekends, besides eating and sleeping, I only like to hide at home and read novels. I estimate that I have read tens of thousands of books by now, and I probably understand all the clichés, but I am still addicted to my own fantasies. I always feel that reality is too real, and only novels have the kind of beauty I yearn for. However, I feel guilty about spending so much time reading novels and I want to quit. How can I break free from this addiction?

answers.answer_text: ~~From the description given by the questioner, I understand that the problem they face is the inability to restrain their habit of reading novels. They always immerse themselves in this unreal and fantasy world. Indeed, novels have a unique charm, and many people love reading novels because they can fulfill what we cannot achieve in reality. It is also a way to relieve stress. However, we often easily fall into the trap of this "beautiful effect". In this regard, we may first reduce our exposure to online novels through direct means. For example, when studying or doing other things, we can put our phones in other places (lock them away), or choose other activities to replace and divert our attention when we want to read novels. In addition, we can also choose to seek help from others, relying on external assistance to help us control these behaviors. After taking these direct measures, we should also try to solve the habit of being addicted to novels from the root. Indeed, life is not as wonderful as novels, fulfilling our fantasies and expectations. But there are many wonderful aspects of life that novels do not have. After all, novels come from life. So we might as well discover the beauty of life more and explore the excitement of life.

question: My husband said that our 14-year marriage is not what he wanted? How to overcome the confusion in our marriage?
description: After three years of dating and fourteen years of marriage, my husband said that the way our marriage has been and the way we interact is not what he desires. Moreover, he has lost interest in me and feels that he can no longer appreciate me. He has also come to the conclusion that I will never become the person he hopes me to be. Should I consider letting go?
keywords: Marriage, concepts of marriage, divorce, marriage management.

answers.answer_text: Hello, seeking help with great inner turmoil and even pain requires a lot of courage, and I can also see your inner longing. Firstly, let's summarize the situation you described: ▲ Three years of dating and fourteen years of marriage, ▲ Your husband says that marriage is not what he wants, ▲ Feeling that he can no longer appreciate you, should you let go? Learn to see the essence through phenomena. After fourteen years of marriage, if your husband is saying this, what does it indicate? On one hand, does it mean that these fourteen years were not what he wanted and he has been struggling with pain for a long time? Why does he say that he is no longer interested in his wife and can no longer appreciate her? On the other hand, in this kind of relationship, are both of you compromising? Does he believe that you will never become the person he hopes for? It seems that you have been continuously changing for him too. Is that right? From this, we can infer that you are also in great pain, constantly changing for him and unable to be yourself, but what's worse is that he does not appreciate it and cannot see it! Looking at it from the perspective of a marital relationship, passion, commitment, and intimacy are particularly important in a marital relationship according to Sternberg's triangular theory of love. So in your marriage, what else is there? Do all three sides exist, and how long are they? In this period of marital confusion, whether to choose to let go or not may be a secondary question. What's more important is whether your heart can bear the psychological conflicts caused by this decision and take responsibility for your own growth. Facing this, perhaps what you need to do is: ## Re-examine yourself, starting from the psychological level, and first achieve self-reflection, what has led to the current state? ## In communication and interaction with him, do you truly understand his internal needs? ## What other possibilities does this marriage have? ... These require specialized counseling and discussion to obtain help. I am here, the world and I love you.

Hey baby, how are you? After 14 years of marriage, your husband suddenly said that these 14 years were not what he wanted. It must feel very unfair and you may even feel worthless at times. Sending you a big hug, sweetheart. But actually, marriage is a partnership between two people, and you shouldn't put yourself in a position to be judged. You can consider the following: 1. Determine your husband's attitude. Is he just feeling emotional at the moment, or has he firmly decided to give up on your marriage? Does he want to face the issues in your marriage together, have open communication, and work together to adjust your thoughts and actions, in order to build a happy marriage together? 2. Were you happy in these 14 years of marriage? It's been quite a journey for your marriage to last this long, but only you know the ups and downs you've experienced. Ask yourself if you have been living the life you wanted in these 14 years. Is the way you and your husband interact and get along what you wanted? 3. Reach a consensus. Once you confirm your husband's thoughts and clarify your own, it is important for both of you to have thorough communication without emotions, expressing your thoughts to find practical ways to improve the situation. For example, if your husband says these 14 years were not what he wanted, what specifically does he want? If he wants both of you to be better, then he needs to express that... Regardless of the final outcome and whether you choose to continue this marriage or not, I hope you can live for yourself, knowing what you want, and then wholeheartedly work towards achieving it. In a marriage, there are compromises to be made, but it's also important to stand firm on those things that are important to you. The above is for reference. May we all live the way we want... Wishing you, the one reading this, all the best as you become better and better!

He said that the marriage and relationship patterns of these years were not what he wanted. Why didn't he speak up at the beginning? He kept silent for over a decade before finally expressing his feelings. Or is it that you have been stagnant for these years, unwilling to make any compromises or changes, causing the distance between you to grow? What does your husband actually want you to become? Does he have a specific template to reference? Is it difficult to achieve or unimaginable? It's impossible that there has been no improvement in fourteen years, right? Or has he been constantly trying to change you, but always dissatisfied? I can understand how painful it is for someone to be transformed into someone they are not, not because of the continuous act of transformation, but because of loving him, that you allowed this lengthy process of transformation. You have tried your best to accept and change, but he keeps raising the bar, exhausting both of you, with no end in sight. Is he finally tired and impatient, or has he found his ideal person? It seems like he wants to let go, and you also want to let go. But that doesn't mean you don't still love him. A good relationship and marriage do require effort. A true intimate relationship is a mutual effort, not one side transforming the other or one side making progress while the other remains stagnant. It involves accepting each other's differences, making an effort to appreciate each other, understanding each other's needs and desires, cultivating shared interests, sharing family responsibilities, not avoiding, not complaining, not judging, in order to create a better future together.

question: I am always particularly averse to the toilet. Do I have OCD?
description: Always have a strong aversion to toilets, especially toilet seat covers that feel like they are covered in bacteria and very dirty. After using the bathroom, always feel like there are bacteria on my body as well. I always wash my hands very carefully multiple times after using the bathroom, and even after some time has passed, I still think about the environment in the bathroom and start to worry. This feeling is very uncomfortable, what should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Based on the behavior you described, it seems like you have behavior similar to obsessive-compulsive disorder. However, to what extent does this behavior reach? Do you wash your hands repeatedly for a long time? Does it affect your daily life and work? If this repetitive behavior is affecting your normal life, I suggest you seek active treatment from a psychiatrist. Generally speaking, most people wouldn't directly sit on a toilet seat in public places. They would usually choose a squat toilet unless the restroom provides disposable seat covers, in which case they might use them if they are in a hurry. However, if you're at home or in a reputable hotel, most people wouldn't be too concerned and would use the toilet directly. The reason for this is that the cleanliness of one's home and high-end hotels is generally trustworthy. I'm not sure which situation you are referring to. If you're concerned about bacteria on the toilet seat cover at home, you can wash it frequently. You can change it as often as you think it won't accumulate bacteria or even have a dedicated one for yourself. Ultimately, as long as you feel comfortable, it's fine. Washing hands after using the restroom is a necessary hygiene habit and it shouldn't have much to do with whether or not you use a toilet seat. The duration of handwashing can vary from person to person, as long as it doesn't take up too much time and doesn't disrupt your normal daily routine, it's not a problem. Relax and remember that having a slight obsession with cleanliness is not a bad thing.

OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. Feeling disgusted by the toilet and thinking there are germs on it, even after using it, and constantly thinking about whether there are germs on it, is it normal or not. First of all, it is normal to feel disgust and think there are germs on the toilet seat since it directly touches the skin. Do you realize that there are reasons for this? Outside public toilets, most of them are squat toilets, rarely with a regular toilet. On one hand, it is due to cost issues, and on the other hand, it considers the unsanitary factor of public items that are touched by multiple people, so OP's thoughts are justified. However, at home, we usually don't need to think about it because usually there are only a few people in the house and less contact with others, relatively cleaner. So, OP's suspicion or resistance to other people's toilets outside is correct, but if OP also thinks this way at home, it will bring some mental burden. If these suspicions of germ-related thinking and the behavior of constantly washing hands have already affected OP's normal life and work, it is recommended that OP seek professional counseling to diagnose the situation and see if there are ways to change their thinking.

question: It has been two years and I have been living in the shadow of my ex-boyfriend, who was a scumbag. What should I do?
description: I am a 98's, my ex-boyfriend is a 97's. We knew each other for seven years. We were together for six months. I liked him when I was in school, and later when I started working, I had a decent monthly income. I rented a house and supported him financially. Everything was paid by me. Later, I didn't have the energy to work anymore, and he cheated on me again. He had already cheated on me once when we first got together, and although I forgave him, this time he went too far. I rented a house for him, but because of work, I rarely went there. When I finally went to see him one day after work because I missed him, I was greeted with a bed full of surprises... I can't forget it. He said he would never deceive me and that everything would be alright. But even now, I still hate him. It has been two years since the incident, how can I let go of this hatred?

answers.answer_text: Hello, it seems that you are feeling heartache and hatred. In this relationship, you have given too much - emotionally, financially, and in terms of understanding. However, all you received in return was deception. Your hatred is understandable and justified. However, it is important to realize that harboring hatred only hurts yourself, not the other person. Therefore, letting go of hatred is not about forgiving the other person, but about freeing yourself and moving forward. You can find a suitable way to release your feelings of resentment and grievances. For example, you can write a long letter, expressing all your experiences and emotions from this relationship, venting all your complaints or curses, as long as you feel cathartic. This letter can be sent to the other person or torn up and burned. This way, you can bring closure to this relationship and bid it farewell. If you find it truly difficult to let go, consider seeking the help of a therapist who can provide a safe and supportive environment for you to express your pain. This experience can serve as a lesson and a part of your personal growth. Relationships should be based on equality and mutual care, rather than one side taking care of the other. When one person gives too much and does too much, it often does not lead to gratitude from the other person. Instead, it may create a sense of entitlement, as the other person has never had to make any sacrifices and thus does not understand the value of what they have. Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

The topic really hates him—it's actually hating oneself for not being able to judge people clearly; hating why it's always you who gives, but in return, you get betrayal again, and perhaps even more betrayals that you haven't seen or don't know about; hating all these years of emotions and selfless giving, yet not receiving his sincerity in return; hating oneself for still thinking about him after two years have passed; why is all of this so unfair? Why is he the one who made mistakes, while you are the one who gets hurt? But in his view, you were willing to give, he never asked you to give! He even thinks that you use various sacrifices to control him and trap him! What's the difference between this feeling and being a mother? He likes the feeling of being taken care of, but it doesn't mean he wants another mother. An adult male wants to get rid of his mother, to create his own world, to be admired by others, to hold his head up high in front of other women, and to be invincible! Before the topic did all these things for him, did you ever consider his feelings, ask about his needs, give him this opportunity? In his view, he also gave for you— he felt that you were so lacking in love, so lacking in a sense of existence, and he tried his best to do many things for you—like being by your side when your work wasn't going well, comforting and encouraging you, like sweet words and embraces when you were unhappy, like being there for you when you needed him, taking care of your feelings, always putting you first...
