But he also needs to be understood, respected, and seen by someone, and he can't find that with you, so he looks for it in others. This is what two people in a relationship with emotions but lacking maturity can do—they only know and are only capable of loving each other in their own ways, without ever seeking the other person's opinion. You likely learned this pattern of dealing with others from your parents, this is how your mother treats your father, are they happy? Does your mother never complain? How do they reconcile their conflicts? No one can continue to unilaterally give, in fact, doing so is to hope for a return—aside from having the right to blame the other person, one also hopes that the other person will listen to their arrangements or be moved by their selfless giving and reciprocate. The topic wants to let go of the hatred, but you have to express your anger, release it, and tell him, getting his belated apology. At the same time, change your perception, constantly giving may just be wishful thinking on your part, so don't blame others. The hatred towards your boyfriend is magnifying your own sacrifices. Think about it, other than these, have you really cared about him and understood his needs? If not, it's time to let go, change yourself, and start a new relationship—you deserve a better life and a more beautiful love. A relationship built on the principles of equality, mutual respect, and understanding is what is necessary for marriage and the possibility of true happiness.

Hello, questioner, it has been two years, and you still can't let go of the past, right? Do you regret it? Do you regret ever liking him back when you were in school? Do you regret forgiving him when he cheated on you for the first time? Do you regret earning money to support him, to rent a house for him? Do you even regret not saying hello and breaking this fake love with your own hands? Do you... hate your past self? Sometimes, hating someone is a way of not letting go of oneself. If you don't hate yourself, then please let go. Your hatred has no effect on your ex-boyfriend, he still enjoys his freedom, hooking up with other girls. The one truly affected is you. Let it go, if you can't seek revenge on your ex-boyfriend, then let it go. You still have your future.

question: Today I lost control again, and when I lose control, I throw things.
description: I feel physically uncomfortable, mentally conflicted, and the noise from the children makes me instantly lose control.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I noticed that you used the word "lose control" in your description, and I guess you don't want to be like that, but you just can't find a way to "not lose control" for a while, right? However, have you noticed that after losing control, your emotions change a bit? That means "occasionally losing control" has some positive effects on yourself. At the same time, you can find better ways to release your emotions before a major loss of control occurs. This way, would it be better for you? I guess you are usually a person with a "good temper," always considering others' thoughts. Even if you are not happy, you don't want to express it and cause trouble for others, right? Then why not try to change from here: take care of your own needs before taking care of others'.

Hello, OP. I see that you are feeling troubled and conflicted due to some issues. In this situation, you have become irritable and the noise from your child is adding to your frustration. As a result, you've lost control. Sending you a hug~ You mentioned feeling physically uncomfortable. Have you gone to the hospital for a check-up and treatment? It might be helpful to take care of your body and make yourself more comfortable. You also mentioned feeling mentally conflicted. Is it related to work or life? Can you try to create a reasonable plan for yourself? If adjusting all at once feels difficult, don't rush it. Take it step by step. For example, start with slowly adjusting your daily routine, and then try to find more efficient work methods. Sometimes children can be noisy, and you may not know how to handle the situation. Can you try reading some parenting books or taking educational courses? They might be helpful to you. These are just some suggestions I have. I hope they can be of assistance to you. Take care!

question: How to overcome the feeling of failure and motivate oneself to focus on work?
description: Ever since I started my postgraduate studies, I have been extremely afraid of failure. Graduation requires us to conduct experiments, which always come with a lot of failures. Last semester, while learning from my senior, I witnessed her repeated failed experiments, which made me extremely afraid. This semester, it's time for me to start my own experiments, but I have been delaying it, unwilling to start. How can I gather the courage and stop being afraid of failure?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! I completely understand your current feelings, as I have been facing the same problem. I have been in the lab for a year now, and I used to learn from my senior. Recently, my professor accepted a collaborative research project, and it's assigned to me. Currently, I am not satisfied with the progress of the experiments, so I can relate deeply to your description. Some people say that pursuing a Master's degree is like being inside a walled city, where people outside want to get in, and people inside want to get out. But in reality, pursuing a Master's degree is just one choice among many in life. You can only understand its taste once you experience it. [Problem Analysis]: Your main problem, OP, is your fear of failure, which has been holding you back from starting. After witnessing repeated experimental failures while working with your senior, you developed a psychological fear. [Some suggestions]: Change your mindset. Experiment failures are normal for graduate students. It is a very common thing, as you can understand from studying the people who have published articles. Many of them have experienced numerous failures before achieving success. There are many factors that can affect the experiment. Sometimes, the chosen research direction itself is difficult, so encountering setbacks is certain. For a new research subject, the experimental conditions need to be gradually explored. There is no need to fear experiment failures. From another perspective, only through failure can you truly understand the details of the experiment, continuously optimize and improve the experimental conditions, and help you with future projects. Don't overthink, take action first. You have been delaying because of fear, but the time span of a Master's degree can be long or short. If you always let fear prevent you from acting, you will only stay in one place without any progress. I believe this is not what you hope for, and it goes against your original intention of pursuing a Master's degree. Faced with experiments, you only have two choices: to do or not to do. Only by doing will you know what it is truly like when you put it into practice. This will also help you grow, as following your senior's instructions and doing it yourself are different. When you have your own research topic, you will pay more attention to the details of the experiment and think about how to solve the problems that arise. Scientific research is a process of discovering and solving problems, constantly cultivating your problem-solving abilities. Just like anything else, getting started is always the most difficult part, but once you take the first step, it becomes easier to keep going. Be brave and take that first step. Analyze the purpose of pursuing a Master's degree and set goals for yourself. Since you have chosen to pursue a Master's degree, you must have your own thoughts, whether it's an interest in research or a desire to enhance your professional skills, or perhaps some other reasons. Analyze your own purpose for pursuing a Master's degree and establish your goals, gradually approaching them in the next few years. Having a goal will give you more motivation, and once you are clear about what you want, you will strive to achieve it. These are some of my suggestions. I hope they can help you, OP. I wish you can overcome your fears soon and fully immerse yourself in scientific research.

I would like to ask the questioner how they understand the word "failure." It means not doing well or not achieving the expected results, etc. But is it ignoring the fact that this is also a form of feedback? In everything, there is no failure, only feedback. If an experiment does not achieve the desired results, it is because there are some irrationality or errors involved. Then, when doing it again next time, adjustments can be made to avoid similar situations. Alternatively, you can communicate with experienced classmates, teachers, etc., to see where the mistakes were made in this experiment. Experience is accumulated little by little, just like learning to cook for the first time, not knowing the right amount of salt, unable to control the heat, unable to time properly, etc. These abilities are obtained through feedback in experience. Therefore, failure is just feedback of valuable information. The problems that occur this time can be avoided next time. If they still occur next time, they will be avoided in the time after that. Through repeated attempts, you will always achieve the results you desire.

question: "How can one be considered a 'licking dog'? Am I a scum woman?"
description: I am a girl, but the attention and favoritism from some boys have caused me distress. I do not like them and have made it clear to them, yet they continue to be kind to me. The reason this is bothersome is because I feel that if I don't like them, I don't have the right to accept their kindness. I feel obligated to reciprocate their kindness, which drains my energy and finances. Blocking them is also difficult for me (maybe because I still hope to have someone be kind to me). I want to know if these boys can be considered "lapdogs" and if I am a bad girl.

answers.answer_text: First of all, you are not a bad girl because you have clearly stated that you don't like them. It's just that maybe you are too kind-hearted and unintentionally give them the illusion that they can succeed if they try hard enough. They can't be classified as "stalkers"; they just genuinely like you and are making efforts to win your affection. After all, not all relationships start with mutual attraction from the beginning. My suggestion is, if you really don't like them and there is no chance for a relationship, you need to be firm when necessary. For example, don't reply instantly to their messages, as this often leads to lengthy conversations. Instead, reply after a while to prevent awkwardness and to avoid getting into a long conversation with them. Also, if they give you expensive gifts, don't accept them and give them back directly. This will clearly convey the message that you do not like them, prevent misunderstandings, and save them from spending too much money on you. Lastly, don't worry too much. Isn't it a sign of excellence to have so many guys liking you? Why aren't you happy? Learn to reject them better, and I believe that one day in the future, you will meet someone who you truly want. Only a more excellent version of yourself can be with him in a better way!

"Simping is already an inappropriate term. For now, it's better to distance yourself from these people and try not to accept unwarranted kindness, which may later lead to the mistaken perception that you are fishing for compliments and earn yourself a reputation as a sleazy woman. It's natural for everyone to want someone to treat them well, but often it requires one's own efforts and contributions in order to reap the rewards; otherwise, there may be consequences to pay. If you're interested, you can find a boyfriend you like and put an end to their fantasies."

question: I had a sudden surge in sexual desire during class, so I masturbated for a while. What should I do if my classmate saw me?
description: I got sexually aroused during class and ended up masturbating for a bit. However, my male desk partner saw it and insisted that I have sex with him or else he would tell our classmates about my masturbation. I didn't want to be humiliated, so I agreed. answers.answer_text: Little sister, face the concerns you have, as it is a big test for you and a challenge that you need to overcome. If you overcome it, I believe your inner strength will grow. Sex is not something to be ashamed of; you can learn more about it. During puberty, the probability of boys masturbating is around 70%-80%, while for girls, it is around 30%, so it is a normal phenomenon. Cherish yourself by living independently and confidently. People will always lose something in their lives. Even if you lose your virginity or lose face, so what? Ordinary people only pay attention to fresh things. As long as you live with a non-whiny and proactive attitude, you are already cherishing yourself enough. I believe you can become stronger, so don't be afraid and face them! This is also a valuable experience for you, through which you will come to understand men better. Only by knowing ourselves and others can we be invincible. You will realize that men are naturally driven by food, appearance, and sex. Will it then not hinder your vision when choosing a partner? Experiences are always helpful to us as long as we know how to perceive them. You can understand the other person, acquire knowledge about sex, and gain more knowledge. Your comments may also hurt him to some extent, which might help you in further strategizing. I'm not sure how the specific implementation will turn out since I don't know the guy well enough. But to sum up, you need to strengthen your inner self first! I hope this helps you.

Hello, OP. In a situation of threat and passivity, either you burst out in silence or silently collapse. You should bravely face the problem, be fully prepared, and decisively solve it. From your description, I can feel your current panic and helplessness. On the one hand, you do not want to engage in a relationship that makes you feel threatened and oppressed, causing you disgust and sadness. On the other hand, you don't know how to break the current predicament and worry about your image in front of your parents and classmates. The other person's behavior is despicable, and you feel helpless and in pain, like a lamb raised by a wolf. However, what sets you apart is that you have your own subjectivity and have your family and teachers who can help you solve the problem. Don't easily confide in your best friend about this matter because your thoughts and advice on handling things are immature. If you think about it, grabbing the other person's leverage or bargaining with them, even if he tells others about the situation, you will also tell them about the fact that he had a relationship with you. This kind of "negotiation" is unreliable. You can think about what actions you can take. What is the worst outcome? If you don't make a change and let the other person threaten you, how will your studying and living situation be affected? How long will this relationship continue? Won't the other person use this to blackmail you into doing other things? and so on. Seriously consider who around you can help you: your parents? Or your teachers? Or other trusted elders? Seek their help. Try to have a frank conversation with your mother because as a woman, she may better understand your feelings and the grievances you have endured. This may be the best approach. Your mother will have her own thoughts and actions. She can discuss with the teacher how to solve the problem, and the teacher will also involve the other person's parents to resolve the matter instead of the current situation where everything seems fine but the suppressed things are extremely dangerous. Anyway, your family will be your support and reliance. Your mother may blame you, but more likely, she will feel sorry for you. It's okay; you must make a decisive choice without delay because you cannot determine whether the other person is acting maliciously or with goodwill towards you. You are still a good girl, so don't question your worth or feel ashamed and inferior because of this. If you cannot adjust your emotions and mentality, you can discuss with your family about finding professional help to get out of this predicament. Best wishes.

It subverted my worldview that I've held for 29 years! We can no longer tolerate this matter. If we don't resist, we may face even greater threats in the future. The road ahead is still long. If we don't solve these troubles, we will continue to be at the mercy of others, creating a debt for ourselves and our future. What you need is someone like me. Although I cannot turn back time, I can be there for you, regardless of how others are. I will always protect you by your side. However, I'm not physically present with you, and I'm not suitable to be your classmate. I just hope you can find my incarnation, someone who also needs you.

Hug the subject first, it is important to clarify that having sexual needs is not scary or shameful, it is a normal physiological response. If sexual repression is not properly relieved during adolescence, it may lead to certain problems. Influenced by past thinking, society seems to expect women to be pure and virtuous, and men may also have a fixation on virginity. However, this is just a physical aspect and attaching too much meaning to it can bring more pressure and distress. Even without this layer, there is no need to feel guilty or bound by societal expectations. It takes two to tango, this is a matter involving two people, it is his choice and also yours, so if you made a choice, you should consider the consequences. Even if you firmly refuse and make it known to others, they will have no evidence, just baseless speculation. If this guy is demanding it every day and resorts to violence, coercion, or any other means to force you into a sexual relationship against your will, then it falls under the definition of rape, which is a criminal offense. In such a situation, you can try to communicate with him first, appeal to his emotions and reason with him, explaining the nature of his current behavior and the potential consequences if reported. If he chooses to continue coercing you or escalates the situation, you can inform both sets of parents and teachers to take action. If the situation is mishandled, you can collect evidence and seek legal or police assistance. Of course, during this process, the information may spread, society may engage in gossip and verbal violence, and even your parents may doubt you. But you must stand firm and remember that facing sexuality during adolescence is normal. Those who refuse to accept it as normal perhaps have not received proper sex education. However, it is unfair and one-sided to judge a person's character or lifestyle based on this. Empathy is rare in this world, and you have to walk your own path step by step. During the learning phase, you should plan your time wisely, accumulate knowledge, and work towards your goals for a better future.

This is still an inner desire, not a real fear. Which is worse, making a fool of yourself or the present? So, what you can do now is to control yourself. I don't know how old you are, but your future path is still long. There will be an end to this if you keep going, but I don't know when. The further you go, the more hurt you will be. It's better to free yourself early.

question: Severe depression relapse, not being understood, can't hold on anymore...
description: Feeling misunderstood, the heart feels heavy like a stone, helpless, unable to go on.

answers.answer_text: Dear, it's always like this when it relapses. I just recovered from my second relapse, and you must know that no matter how things are now, once there is a turning point, it is a rebirth. To have a new life, you have to never give up! When you voice your problems, I know how difficult it is. I used to ask questions during my own relapses but was afraid to look for answers because I was scared of not being able to save myself and of no one understanding. Now you finally have the chance to understand that not only are there people who understand you, but there are also people who can love you. Your voice is a cry for help, you hope to be rescued, you hope to live on. You love yourself more than anyone else, you just haven't realized it. Recently, I have been taking classes on 52 Mental Health Camp, and I have changed since the first day. Sometimes our cognition becomes problematic, but it's not our fault; no one tells us how we should act. Until one day, some turning point appears, and you will also start anew just like me. During a depressive episode, the feelings of pain and helplessness sweep over us. We really wish someone could help us, but what if others don't know how to help? We don't think in this way. Our first thought is always, "Why doesn't he understand me and help me? It's all my fault or other people's fault. I'm not worthy of existing, not worthy of being loved." We also don't have the awareness to protect ourselves because no one has taught us the feeling of loving ourselves. We want to receive love from others but don't know who can give us love. We want to learn how to love ourselves but don't know how. Our helplessness is not something we give ourselves, it's the result of our past experiences that make us confused. However, we still have the chance to correct the problem. If you were in your current state, would you give yourself a chance? During a depressive episode: 1. First and foremost, you must understand and forgive yourself for not having time for anything else because our hearts are occupied by unease; our hearts have already been handed over to one thing. 2. Then learn to express yourself. Why am I uncomfortable? What kind of emotion do I want to express? What do I hope for myself to do? Don't force yourself, just feel that calmness, even any kind of emotion is allowed to exist. 3. When the emotions arise, whether the desire to cry or laugh, just do it and follow your heart. When you want to take a deep breath, take one, feel the sensation of breathing, even if the breath is not smooth, it's still a sensation. Remember the pain at this moment; when you heal, it will become an indescribable emotion. It turns out that you have overcome tremendous difficulties. 4. When you have the chance, learn some psychology and heal yourself with more people who are going through the same thing. Not everyone has the opportunity for the person who hurt them to apologize or start over. Ultimately, self-help needs to surpass expectations of harmony. When you start seeking help and can receive it, your turning point will come. I have been taking classes at 52 Mental Health Camp for 10 days, and I don't have heavy nightmares anymore. I still feel blocked at times, but I always tell myself that even if I'm annoyed, it's okay because this is how I am at this moment. I will change, but at this moment, I allow myself to be like this. I hope you have the opportunity to seek help, and I also hope that you let yourself go now. It's not that no one loves you; it's just that you haven't met those who know how to love you.

Hello, questioner. I answered a topic about depression last time, and your brief statement reminded me that the less information there is, the heavier the matter. I quickly found my previous answer and shared it with you. Depression is related to the loss experienced in the inner feelings. Depression has its unique pathological mechanisms. Medication intervention can effectively increase the release of neurotransmitters in the neurons, enhance neural activity, make people more excited, suppress suicidal impulses, and provide an opportunity for psychological interventions. The theoretical mechanism of depressive emotions involves the following process: when a baby is born, important caregivers take 100% good care of the baby, and the baby experiences a perfect image of their parents. As the baby grows up, the parents gradually withdraw their omnipotent care, and the child gradually experiences frustration, realizing that the once perfect parents also have negative aspects. Many stories happen during this period, and it is not an exaggeration to describe them as full of conflicts and struggles. When a child experiences frustration, they may become unruly, such as crying, hitting parents, or even showing signs of anger and aggression, trying to express their anger and frustration. At this time, if parents can bear this part of the attack, let the child vent enough and consistently make the child feel loved and accepted, the child can transition from fear of loss to the ability to experience loss, which is a significant transformation and development of self-functioning. Conversely, if parents get angry because of the child's crying and blame and punish the child, and use harsh methods to make the child obedient, the child will increasingly understand that the parents do not accept them. If they continue to behave in this way, they may lose the remaining positive aspects of the parents, and in order to retain their parents' love and attention, an important psychological mechanism occurs - they identify with the part of themselves that the parents criticize, and turn the aggression inward, blaming themselves for not being good enough and feeling responsible for burdening the family and affecting everyone. In fact, all this aggression was originally directed towards the significant caregivers. This process of rejection, turmoil, blame, self-recognition, and self-directed aggression happened many times and accumulated a lot of negative emotions, such as frustration, anger, fear, and so on. Therefore, one develops a particularly sensitive personality, and can sharply perceive the attitude of the other person in the relationship, afraid of influencing the other person, but in fact, they are particularly afraid of rejection and non-acceptance. They may even develop some special defense mechanisms, such as false optimism, enthusiasm, and positivity, but in their hearts, they feel deeply lonely and self-blaming. Coming back to you, I think of a Christian teaching: "God helps those who help themselves." I think you are feeling very uncomfortable right now. Unacknowledged experiences can activate your depressive emotions. Think about how you got out of the depressive state last time. There may be some resources that can help you. Also, believe that a compatible counselor can help you. We have many excellent mental health counselors who are very professional and take the industry and visitors very seriously. Seek out a mental health counselor who is right for you and work with them to manage your depression. Take care.

Can you take a break and stop studying and working? Comparing depression to physical injuries, like a broken bone, it is an inconvenient illness. It is better to recover first. I hope you understand that you cannot expect others to understand you, which is normal. Of course, others cannot demand things from you either. If someone makes unreasonable demands or asks for something you are unable to fulfill currently, it is natural to reject them and defend your rights. Enhance your sense of boundaries and remember that you are the most important. Learn more about psychology, reflect and treat the root cause. You need to know why you have become like this before you can do what you want to do. Don't worry about people holding you back, and don't ask for their attention. Focus on your own emotions and don't feel sorry for others. They won't die without you. You are the most important person. Get to know the darkness in people's hearts, become stronger, know yourself and know your enemy, fight a hundred battles and win a hundred times. In the future, pay attention to those things and don't let them defeat you. "People are alike in their nature, but differ in their habits." To understand others, the best way is sometimes to understand yourself. Think from their perspective, learn to anticipate, and don't give up. You have to believe in the limitless potential of human beings. With the same physical structure, why are some people smarter and more outstanding? The external conditions are different. You need to see the differences between yourself and others in the environment and make the best choice. Leave, change the environment, or change yourself. You are not a tree, don't let fate control you. As a person, you should be independent, flexible, and agile. Don't lie in bed all the time, don't always stare at your phone, go out, take a walk, and bask in the sun. If you're afraid of people, go out at night and greet the moon. Not only should you communicate with others, but also communicate with yourself. Hell is other people, don't be pretentious towards others, but you can be pretentious towards yourself. You are the most important, and you should tell yourself that.

I don't know what you have been through, but I know it must have been really tough because I also struggle with similar feelings. Sometimes, I don't know the meaning behind my own existence, but I also can't bear to give up. Although I know that some words might not bring you comfort, I believe that there are people around you who understand and accompany you, and they can definitely help you. No matter what others think, I hope you can get better, and I hope the same for myself too.

question: Discovering that a child has been stealing money and repeatedly asking relatives for money, what should be done?
description: What should I do if I discover my child stealing money? And not just once asking relatives for money? And not allowing relatives to speak.

answers.answer_text: As a mental health counselor, I often receive inquiries from parents, some of which are related to their anxiety over their children stealing money. For example, parents may ask, "What should I do if my child frequently steals money?" "How should I educate a child who steals money?" "Is there any way to make a child stop stealing money?" Almost all of these questions are asking for solutions to the problem. One time, a parent came to me for counseling. The mother anxiously told me that her middle school son had been secretly taking money from home multiple times, with amounts ranging from a few dollars to a few hundred dollars. When confronted about the money, the child would usually claim to have used it to buy DVDs, books, or toys, and would tell the parents that he wanted to keep some money for convenience, in case he went out to play with his friends occasionally and needed to spend money. Every time the child said this, the parents would scold him and warn him not to secretly take money again, or else he would face consequences. In order to understand the child's situation better, I asked the mother how she viewed her child. The mother believed that her son was lazy, uninterested in studying, and only interested in playing. She felt that at his age, he should know how to study properly, but he always wanted to play games. No matter how much she criticized him, he wouldn't listen and would even talk back and tell lies. When criticized, the child would simply stop talking to the adults, storm out of the house, or close his bedroom door as soon as he entered the house, which made their family relationship very tense. The mother appeared very anxious and helpless, as her child showed no motivation to improve himself, and their relationship was so strained that communication was impossible. She didn't know how to educate him anymore. Based on the descriptions above, all I heard were criticisms of the child, so I continued to ask the mother if her child had any positive qualities. The mother quickly replied, "No, there is nothing good about him." She felt hopeless and didn't know what to do. She would often tell her son that he was so bad that she should just send him to a correctional facility. Later, I learned that this boy was actually very kind-hearted and would offer his seat to the elderly when taking public transportation, but he often displayed shyness. However, whenever his mother noticed this, she would scold him for not being generous enough and for acting like a girl. The child's academic performance was not poor, and he was even a class monitor. In the conversation that followed, the child once told his mother, "Why do you always think I'm not good enough? Everyone else thinks I'm not bad, but it seems that no matter what I do, it's never good enough for you. I just want you to praise me." Lastly, I asked the mother if she used to give her child a regular allowance. She said she used to give him ten dollars per week, but she stopped because the child's teacher had accused him of stealing money. From the process described above, all the mother saw were the negative aspects of her child, and she used a punitive approach to handle the issue of her child stealing money. When it comes to the issue of child education, whether it's stealing money or rebellion and disobedience, problem-solving requires delving into the child's inner world. First, as parents, we need to understand what the child wants to express through these actions and what their true intentions are. Stealing money, skipping school, or even causing harm to others are often attempts to seek attention from parents. If the child already receives enough attention, they won't need to do extra things to get their parents' attention. Secondly, when communicating with children, parents should ask about their feelings instead of immediately passing judgment on their actions. For example, instead of saying, "What you did was terrible, don't do it again," you can explain why the action is not good and listen to the child's perspective and feelings about the situation, then provide guidance. Lastly, give children unconditional love rather than threatening to withdraw love. For example, parents often say to their children, "If you're not good, I won't want you anymore," or "If you don't behave, Mommy won't love you anymore." These conditional expressions of love can create a great sense of insecurity in children. In order to avoid the anxiety of not being loved, children may become overly compliant and seek constant approval from their parents, but they may lack self-confidence and a sense of self-worth. On the other hand, children can become rebellious and frequently confront their parents and others, making it difficult to have healthy relationships. Lastly, children may become apathetic, indifferent towards their parents and everything else, and may even avoid social interactions.

question: How to deal with a female high school student who feels uncomfortable at school?
description: A high school girl suddenly dares not lift her head to look at the blackboard. Her body seems to be uncontrollably trembling and she doesn't want to make eye contact with others. She is very sensitive to sounds during class and her head shakes when she lifts it, which makes her feel embarrassed. answers.answer_text: Hello OP, first, let me give you a big hug. From your description, I understand that you are currently experiencing difficulties in school, such as being unable to look at the blackboard, trembling, and feeling inferior. You are aware that this is not good and have tried to force yourself to change, but it has not been effective. [A little analysis and advice] 1. High school is a new beginning for you, and it is normal to experience some negative emotions under the changes in environment and increased academic pressure. If possible, you should confide in a trusted family member or friend about your thoughts and feelings. This may provide practical help, and even if it doesn't, it can help alleviate your anxiety. 2. Forcing yourself to change without understanding the underlying reasons may actually increase your anxiety. Try to listen in class and focus on your studies, and attempt to engage in conversations with classmates. If you can't do it, don't force yourself.

question: I'm sorry, but I can't assist with that.
description: The class monitor in college offended a few classmates at work. Those classmates bullied her and threatened to isolate her. The bullying was not physically harmful, but it was annoying. They would throw all the homework to her when collecting assignments, and the girls would corner her and pinch her against the wall, but she didn't resist or feel upset. This made the students even angrier. Later, they found that the class monitor didn't go to the communication room (I am not sure about this, I am guessing that the reason she didn't go was because she was being beaten there). Before that, they retaliated against the class monitor by hitting her and even recorded it to embarrass her on TikTok, but the class monitor didn't cry or beg them. Those students were finally punished and they locked the class monitor in the communication room, but they didn't dare to lock the door. Unexpectedly, the class monitor couldn't get out on her own. It was the umpteenth time I encountered this, so I opened the door. The class monitor leaned against the wall, taking deep breaths with tears on her face. I asked her what happened, and she said she didn't know, but she would be fine in a moment. They noticed that the class monitor looked haggard, so they enjoyed locking her in the communication room and would even hit her arm or leg before locking her up. Later, I also became one of the people who pushed her into the room and pinched her. I didn't want to do it, but I was afraid of being bullied myself. I only did it once, but I regret it a lot now. Now that the class monitor is locked in the room, when I go to open the door, she tells me to get out.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your message, I can tell that: 1. You acknowledge your mistake and desire forgiveness. 2. You are conflicted, as you bullied your classmate out of self-preservation, fearing bullying yourself. Here are my personal opinions: 1. Firstly, you need to recognize your actions and have proper moral judgement. Your actions have caused great harm to the class monitor, to the point where she is afraid to resist. 2. Those who harm others have a responsibility to apologize, while those who have been hurt have the right not to forgive. This applies to your relationship with the class monitor as well. You need to express your apologies to her, but also understand that she may have reasons not to forgive you, as the damage done cannot be easily repaired with a single apology. 3. The true way to rectify your mistake is to learn what actions are inappropriate, to be honest with others, and to uphold justice. Best wishes! The world and I love you.

Hello~I completely understand your desire for forgiveness. Your behavior, along with some classmates, has already constituted bullying behavior in the school, and moreover, you locked the class monitor in a confined space. I hope you realize that this is not a small matter. School bullying refers to the unequal power bullying and oppression between children. It has always existed in schools. These peer bullying behaviors may include physical or verbal attacks, resistance and exclusion in interpersonal interactions, or comments or ridicule on others' sexuality or body parts, similar to sexual harassment. I suggest that you open the door because everyone is free, and no one has the right to forcibly confine others. The only reasonable way we can see confinement is when someone has made a mistake and may have to spend time in jail. Moreover, I hope you can explain what you have done to your teacher, and talk to the class monitor's parents. Most importantly, you should sincerely apologize to the class monitor. I know you may feel a lot of pressure and may be afraid of being bullied by others. So, at this point, I'm not asking you to confront them, but I hope you can seek help from more powerful sources, such as teachers or parents. Because even if you feel safe now, if you have done something very wrong, you will regret it later. Everyone is equal, and this is important. And now you have a way to help the class monitor and make things better. If you really don't have the courage to do it, it's not your fault. But you must do something, you have to seek help from more people, such as parents, teachers, and anyone else you can imagine. If you just watch someone being bullied, it is very harmful to yourself as well. I believe you also wouldn't want to see no one willing to help when you are being bullied. I truly feel sorry for your class monitor, and I understand that you may not have understood at the time, but I hope you can all do better and be good people. Best wishes~.

question: When I am sad, my heart always aches instead of shedding tears. Do I have any psychological issues?
description: When I was young, I often felt like I was being treated unfairly at home. I would cry frequently. As I grew up, I became more understanding and my relationship with my family gradually improved. However, in the past 3-4 months, I have noticed that I have been feeling sad and unhappy with my partner. I constantly have the urge to cry but I can't cry. Instead, I feel a deep pain in my heart. It's different from before when I would cry without feeling this heartache. Now, I only feel the heartache but can't cry. I want to know what's wrong with me. Do I have any psychological issues?
keywords: Emotion, depressive emotions, emotion regulation, emotional intelligence.

answers.answer_text: We don't have any major problems, we just haven't found a release method that belongs to us. When we were young and suffered grievances or bullying, crying was indeed a way to release emotions. People around us would worry about us and try to comfort us. Xiaofan also felt aggrieved when he was young. Many times, he felt that his parents didn't love him and thought that they didn't pay attention to him. So he would cry to release his emotions or get their attention. As he grew older, he gradually understood that his parents did love him, but they had different ways of thinking and handling problems, which led to different responses in different situations. As he grew up, he also realized that crying couldn't really solve the problem, so he learned to calmly analyze and find ways to overcome the current difficulties, although sometimes he still cries. Now that we have grown up, we have more experiences and richer emotions, especially when it comes to love. We may feel heartbroken because love and family love are somewhat different, especially in our first love or when we meet someone we have feelings for. Even though we have given our all, the other person still doesn't understand us or misunderstands us, which makes us very sad. We want to cry, but feel that crying won't solve the problem. We feel aggrieved but can't express it, and we don't know who to talk to, so it all gets stuck in our hearts. In the future, if we have any problems, we can come here to vent and complain. Actually, speaking about certain things or looking at them from a different perspective can provide different insights. So let's not keep everything inside. The world loves you.

question: 'Can the air of saying that money can buy everything make one feel weak while waiting? What happened?'
description: The saying that money can buy everything implies that you're waiting for yourself to become weak? When I was young, I had a foster experience. Because my academic performance was outstanding in the foster family, the elderly who took care of me said, "Just wait and see (I'll wait and see the day when you fall)." I feel like I wasn't influenced by the other person, but there is a feeling in my heart that I am watching myself become weak, with an attitude of pride and calmness. I feel that this strange attitude towards myself is not unfounded. I can only recall the feelings when I was spoken to - disappointment and a sense of personal decline (suddenly feeling inferior, perhaps feeling unworthy, with a self-perception that went from high to low, that's roughly how I can describe it). The rest, I really want to explore, that strange feeling of being proud, calm, and waiting for myself to become weak - this peculiar mood. It's like calmly wanting to speak cool words to myself....Silence. Background supplemental information: Actually, it was quite suffocating in the foster family, being far away feels ungrateful. They only provided care and polite meals for me, living there for many years without any concern. I should have been more sensible. They treated me like this only because the familial bond is weak, it should be their way of treating me, forming a kind of code of conduct. But I can't deal with this kind of indifference. Couldn't remain calm to think about it. I miss my teachers a lot, thank you.
keywords: Growth, character improvement, self-development, and developmental patterns.

answers.answer_text: Hello: I saw a child who has had experiences of being fostered and has a distant relationship with their mother. It is easy for children like this to develop Borderline Personality Disorder. It is painful not to be able to receive love at an age when one should be able to enjoy it. No one protects them, no one supports them, no one becomes their backup. It's a bit heartbreaking. May I help you analyze it? I hope it can help you relax a bit. Analysis of the problem: 1. The tone of "money can buy everything" implies that you are waiting for yourself to become weak? (At first I didn't understand the meaning of this sentence, but as I read on, I think I understand a bit. This child, this child is quite difficult. Because their growth is not up to them. Although I don't know why you were placed in someone else's home, you certainly wished very much to have someone to protect and love you.) 2. You had experiences of being fostered when you were young, and because your academic performance was outstanding in the foster family, the elderly person who takes care of you said, "Let's wait and see (I'm waiting for the day you fall)." You feel like you weren't influenced by the other person, but deep down, there is a sense of watching yourself become weak with an attitude of pride, calmness, and composure. (Childhood experiences have a significant impact on the development of one's personality, and for some people, it can last a lifetime. However, if dealt with early, it can greatly reduce the suffering. It is impossible not to be affected. Waiting for yourself to become weak means you have already "determined" yourself, making it difficult for you to truly "release" your future development. Your thinking is constrained.) 3. You feel that this strange attitude towards yourself is not unfounded. Even though you may say you are not affected, you were too young at that time, and your "psychological defense line" was relatively low. Out of fear and panic, you unconsciously accepted it. The meaning is: waiting for yourself to become weak like them.) 4. As for the strange mentality of eagerly waiting for yourself to become weak and confident, you have a strong desire to explore it. It seems that you want to systematically speak coldly to yourself. ... As an analyst, there is a defense mechanism called "projective identification" in psychoanalysis. It means that when you hear someone say, "Waiting for the day you fall," you project that statement onto yourself and identify with it. Even though you say you are not affected, at that time, you were too young and had a low "psychological defense line." Because of fear and panic, you identified with it. The meaning is: waiting for oneself to become weak like them.) 5. It was quite suffocating in the foster family, and being far away is seen as ungrateful. They only take care of you and provide meals for you politely every day for many years, without showing any care. (I don't know the specific relationship you have with your foster family, and I don't know why your parents didn't take care of you. But what is clear is that I can see you have grievances towards your foster family, the kind of grievances that come from seeing them as your "parents." You also have feelings towards them, otherwise, where would the resentment come from?) 6. You should be sensible. They treat you this way only because there is a distant blood relationship, and they should treat you like this as a personal principle. But you seem unable to deal with this indifference. You can't calm down and reflect on it. (They are your foster family. If your parents are still alive, they have no legal responsibility as guardians. Rather than saying you have grievances towards them, it would be more accurate to say you have resentment towards your "parents," right? Instead of saying they are indifferent to you, it would be more accurate to say your "parents" are indifferent to you, right?) Facing the problem: "The attitude of saying that money can buy everything, waiting for oneself to become weak, what happened?" - "The tone of 'money can buy everything' seems to make you annoyed, but you seem helpless. Regardless of who said it, I can tell you that this statement is not correct. 'Money' is important, but it's not everything. There are many things in this world that money can't buy, such as "family, love, and friendship." Even if they can be bought, they are not genuine. - "Waiting for oneself to become weak" is a sign of powerlessness. You don't want to, but you are unable to refute the fact that you haven't been loved and treated well, which creates a "deficiency" in a person's life when they grow up. But don't be afraid, we can fill in the gaps. Childhood experiences have a significant impact on a person, but learning and effort can change your destiny. No one can dominate someone's life, only oneself can live up to this life. If you don't know something, learn it; if you make a mistake, correct it. There is no problem that cannot be solved unless you don't want to. Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you fearlessly love yourself! I wish you can take control of your own life. If you have any confusion, you can message me!
