question: What should I do if I've reached the age to get married but have never been in love?
description: I have reached the age of marriage, but I have never met someone that I truly love. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: From the problem, one can feel the burden and fear of being left behind from the author. Age doesn't seem to be the biggest concern, the biggest worry seems to be "never having loved someone." "Love" is something both abstract and real. It can be hard to define, but it can also be felt physically. Moreover, everyone has their own understanding and feelings about it. How does the author understand and feel about "love"? Do they have their own standards? What does "loving deeply" mean to the author? Embrace the feeling of "love" and believe that your "true love" is already on its way to find you!

I can understand that there is no age limit for marriage in your situation. The reason you have such thoughts is because your environment makes you feel like you should get married once you reach a certain age, but you haven't found someone you truly love. I'm not sure if you mean that someone else loves you or you love someone else when you say "truly love". Love is a mutual feeling, and only when you open your heart can you meet your loved one. Maybe it's just a matter of fate, and you can be the best version of yourself, and then meet the person you should love at the best age. If you want to solve this problem, the internet is very developed nowadays, and there are many ways to meet people. It depends on whether you are willing to try and love yourself before meeting your loved one. I hope my answer can help you. I wish you well.

Hug you! Don't rush into finding a boyfriend and getting married just because of your age, as it is not responsible to yourself. Love should be based on when it's right, not on your age. The right time will come naturally. If you haven't found love yet, it just means you haven't encountered it or it's not the right time yet. Fate will take its course, so love yourself first and you will eventually meet someone who loves and understands you. Never give up hope, believe that you will find someone who truly loves and understands you in the future. In the meantime, take good care of yourself and love yourself. Keep going, you can do it. I'm with you.

question: Feeling deceived emotionally, I started doubting myself and feeling incomplete. What should I do?
description: Encountering someone who deceives emotions and manipulates the body has caused me to start doubting myself, feeling incomplete, and extremely suppressed. What should I do?
keywords: Love, heartbreak, sexual behavior, virgin complex.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Personal opinion: One wrong step in life is like falling into an abyss. In this abyss, whether you create light or get swallowed by darkness, it depends on the depths of your own heart. What is lost cannot be regained. If you feel that you and that person have conflicts, find a way to resolve them. See through the situation and understand the essence. If you truly discover that the person is deceiving your feelings and there is no way to salvage the situation, then leave. Since what is lost cannot be regained, bury the loss in your heart. There is a saying, "turn grief and anger into strength." Indeed, not every thing can be laughed off. This incident will leave scars in your heart, which are difficult to heal and fade away. It lingers like smoke, making you sad and cry, and the world seems gloomy. But keep looking ahead! You cannot control the past, so become the master of your future! Achieve something and bring them to a state of self-disgrace, make them realize how foolish their decision was. Confront the sharp edge of "incompleteness" that you speak of. Even if it is sharp, you must be willing to be deeply wounded. Starting from tomorrow, a phoenix that has risen from the ashes will appear before everyone's eyes. Life may not be magnificent, but it should be lived fully without betraying oneself. You may think that my words are exaggerated, that I am speaking without understanding the pain. But in reality, the next move in life can only be taken by oneself. Be the champion of this game, the master of this chessboard. Losing the first knot may make you feel incomplete... girl, you must remember that every girl is an angel and should not despair just because a bit of "paint" has stained you. But this "paint" can never be washed away! - - Even if it can't be washed away, it doesn't matter! It's not worth it to give up everything for a man who has tainted your pure and beautiful soul. Someday, you will meet someone who loves you, accepts everything about you, treats you with tenderness and delicacy. You can completely give your heart to him and even show him your emotional scars. With him, time won't seem dull anymore, everything will be fine as long as he is there. It's destined that he loves you!

Hello, OP. Sending you warm hugs~ I can feel that you must be in a lot of pain. Besides the emotional investment, you trusted the other person, but didn't expect to be deceived by them, including being deceived in your own emotions. However, don't punish yourself with someone else's mistakes. Perhaps this is a not-so-good experience, but will it bring you some warnings? For example, in future interpersonal relationships, you can reduce your interactions with such people and protect yourself more. You can trust others, but you need to establish a relationship after mutual understanding. When I am deceived by someone, I also feel that they are being unreasonable and that I am being foolish. But in reality, it is the other person's fault, their actions causing harm to you. You're already feeling sad, so don't blame yourself too much and add more troubles to yourself. Try to do things that make you happy, invest more in enriching your life, it can help reduce the impact of this matter on you. Best wishes~.

question: Why do parents always say "getting married will be better"? Can it really be better?
description: Why do parents always say, "Just get married, and everything will be fine"? Can it really solve the problem? Is getting married the ultimate solution?

answers.answer_text: First, let me give you a hug. Talking about marriage in this way is not appropriate. Firstly, phrases like "everything will get better after getting married" are just like saying "everything will get better if you have money." They are just expressions. Secondly, just like whether someone will become wealthy or not depends on various factors, we also need to consider many factors when it comes to marriage. Just like those who say "everything will get better if you have money" may not be wealthy themselves, or may not necessarily become better off after becoming wealthy. Similarly, those who say "everything will get better after getting married" cannot guarantee that you will definitely become better off after marriage. Therefore, it is just an expression. Whether you want to believe it or make any decisions based on it is your own right.

question: Feeling overwhelmed by academic pressure and high expectations from parents, I feel completely inclined to give up on myself. What should I do?
description: Recently, I have been under a lot of academic pressure, which may be partially due to my parents' high expectations. As a result, I have lost interest in studying. Since I attended a boarding school in junior high, I have had limited communication with my parents. Currently, my academic ranking has dropped by over two hundred places compared to before, and I have completely lost the desire to study. I mentioned wanting to take a break from school before, but my parents did not allow it. They only think that my decline in grades can be improved with more effort. But deep down, I know that's not the case. I have no interest in anything now and often inexplicably feel low. On top of that, my mom has a really bad temper. She always criticizes me over trivial matters and compares me to other children who performed better in exams. She even says that I'm like a hedgehog, always ready to prick people. I don't want to be like this, but now I just feel like giving up completely. Maybe it's better if I didn't exist in this world, so they wouldn't have to bear my moodiness all the time.
keywords: Growth, work, learning, self-acceptance, student growth

answers.answer_text: Hello! I understand how you feel. Parents' high expectations, criticism, and comparisons can bring you a lot of psychological pressure. Under too much pressure, it's natural to feel overwhelmed and want to give up or avoid it. I agree with your idea that you need to rest and not push yourself too hard right now. However, your parents may not know your true feelings and situation. If talking directly to them doesn't work, you can consider other methods. For example, schools usually have counselors who you can talk to. The counselor will assess your situation and if they think it's necessary to take a break from school, they can communicate with your parents. Counselors are professionals, and their words may convince your parents better. You can also ask your parents to take you to see a psychologist or a counselor. Their diagnosis and advice might be more easily accepted by your parents. Perhaps with the explanation from professionals, your parents can realize that your current behavior, such as losing interest in everything or declining academic performance, is not something you can control, but rather, you need help instead of being blamed. Don't give up on yourself. Your parents may not understand you for now, but at least you need to understand and love yourself. Hugs to you, the world and I love you!

question: How can I sleep better if I have insomnia and a headache and can't fall asleep?
description: I often have insomnia and can't fall asleep. I have difficulty falling asleep and wake up easily. Sometimes, even when I do fall asleep, it is only for 4 or 5 hours. My mind feels very tired and I cannot sleep well. Especially when I can't fall asleep at night, I feel very sad and not at all happy. Taking herbal supplements for sleep or drinking milk with honey doesn't help either. I really wish I could get better sleep every day.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ From your description, it seems that your sleep quality is indeed quite poor, such as having difficulty falling asleep and easily waking up after falling asleep. If none of the measures I suggest are effective for you, you may consider seeking help from a doctor. It is possible that you are sensitive mentally, which may affect your ability to fall asleep. It could also be due to certain issues with your physical functions that make it difficult for you to fall asleep. A professional doctor can help you understand the causes of your insomnia and assist you in adjusting your sleep schedule through medication or psychological therapy. If your sleeplessness is caused by stressful events, you may consider seeking help from a psychologist to address your psychological issues. Wishing you well~.

question: I recently started dating a girlfriend, how do I talk to her about splitting expenses equally?
description: Hello everyone, recently I started dating a girlfriend for two months and we often go out on dates. Although being in a relationship can be financially demanding, I was able to manage it before because of work. However, recently the company went bankrupt and I suddenly became unemployed, which made me financially tight. She is aware of this situation, but every time we go out, I still end up paying the bill. I don't know what her thoughts are on this matter. I really want to communicate about it, but I don't know what to do or how to express it. After all, we have only known each other for two months, and if we communicate poorly, she might think that I am unwilling to spend money in a new relationship. Moreover, this is a difficult topic for me to bring up. I don't know how to deal with this contradiction. I would like to know if anyone has any good suggestions.

answers.answer_text: Poster, hello~~~ First, give you a hug. From the description, it can be understood that: 1. The poster has been having financial problems recently and hopes that both parties can split the bill when dating. 2. But the poster doesn't know how to bring up this matter to their girlfriend. [A little analysis and advice]: 1. In a relationship, guessing the other person's thoughts or waiting for the other person to guess your own thoughts can lead to conflicts and arguments. So it's highly unlikely that the poster's desire to wait for the other person to take the initiative and understand their current situation and provide help will yield results. It's not to say that the girlfriend necessarily values money and doesn't consider the poster's situation; she could also be slow to catch on or simply not paying attention, among other reasons. 2. If the poster is in a relationship with the goal of long-term development and marriage, then being open and honest is actually an behavior that can earn more favor. Clearly tell the other person about the recent financial problems and hope to reduce the frequency of dates or implement a split-bill system for dates. Hope this can help the poster.

It may be better for you to wait until you have a better financial situation before considering a girlfriend. When you have little to no income, finding someone willing to share the ups and downs with you, and even covering basic expenses, may be difficult. Maybe you should consider a different time or perhaps someone from a wealthy background, where you won't have to pay for everything. In this society, not only in relationships but also in friendships, everything requires a giving heart. If you go through life being calculating and focused only on material things, it truly loses its meaning. A good man aspires to explore the world, and money, once earned, can be spent, but at the end of the day, it's true that wealth can come and go.

question: What should I do if I have some problems such as insomnia, mild depression, lack of social interaction, and feelings of inferiority and self-blame?
description: Due to some traumas, I fell into a state similar to mild depression (not major depressive disorder) during high school. As a result, I graduated from high school without any interpersonal relationships. When I entered college, I became isolated and defensive, in a state of self-abandonment (approaching moderate depression, but not major depressive disorder), and my late nights (quietly getting ready for bed) and late waking hours disturbed my roommate. In addition, my roommate was not very friendly, so I often suspected that they were targeting me (which they actually were), leading to a strong hostility and isolation towards them. Now I feel that I have misunderstood their behavior to an excessive degree (although there was some targeting, it wasn't as extreme as I thought), and it was indeed me who initially excluded and disrespected them (with my sleep schedule). I truly feel remorseful and believe that if it wasn't for me falling into darkness, it wouldn't have turned out this way. This also applies to what happened in high school. Furthermore, my interpersonal relationships are not good now. Although some classmates have a decent impression of me, I already have low self-esteem. Living in the dormitory has made my self-esteem even lower. Although I have stood up for myself, it has only reinforced my people-pleasing personality. I try to please classmates who are relatively close to me, but I can't truly blend in with others and be warm towards them. I'm also not very brave in greeting others. Moreover, my interpersonal relationships are still very weak, and only a few people show a positive attitude towards me. It's not particularly good yet.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, friends, roommates, classmates.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's a significant issue worth paying attention to and discussing. Personally, I'm also still exploring and can only share some advice on interpersonal relationships based on my own experience, hoping to help you, the original poster. 1. Start improving interpersonal relationships by changing your self-perception. No one will be stuck in a state of poor interpersonal relationships forever. If you are willing, you have the opportunity to improve them. When you posed this question, it's assumed that you are willing to make changes. Therefore, dear person, you have the ability to improve and will improve your interpersonal relationships. It may be a bit challenging, but if you persist, you will see improvement. You need to learn to encourage yourself and establish a self-awareness that you can improve and are capable of it. 2. Establish the correct way to make friends. Interactions between people must be based on equal conditions in order to be long-lasting. You may not know how to get along with friends because of your long-term difficulties in making friends. Hence, initially, you might choose to lower your self-esteem and conform to others in order to gain their approval. This approach may make your friendship process smoother initially, as obedient and compliant friends are less likely to reject you. However, dear person, with such an approach, although you've made friends, you will still feel lonely and helpless when encountering difficulties, not knowing who to turn to for help and who to trust. As mentioned in your description, you are not truly familiar with others, unable to be friendly, and afraid to greet others. In reality, you have only made superficial friends, and when the moment comes, you will still be alone. If you want to make real friends, close friends, first, you need to find people who have similar interests and common topics with you. That's the only way to have further development. In fact, you need to approach making friends with an attitude of equality for the other person to respect you and sincerely help you when you are in need. Finally, cultivate your self-confidence and be more open when making friends. Interactions between people involve sensing each other's attitudes towards oneself. If you are more open, others will feel relaxed and natural. If you are too reserved, it will make others cautious and unwilling to interact with you. Finding a good friend to chat about daily life and genuinely care for each other is not easy, but it is achievable. Keep going and good luck.

Hello, dear questioner, after carefully reading your descriptions, I have gained some understanding of your current troubles. Next, let's analyze the recent events together. You mentioned a history of depression and difficulties getting along with classmates and roommates. However, you had a crucial self-reflection moment where you realized that you had misunderstood their actions and had initially excluded and disrespected them. This cognition is excellent, as it will gradually improve your state of mind. So, I encourage you to reflect on this cognition more deeply. Whenever you have negative thoughts, remind yourself of this cognition, reinforce it several times, and you will be less likely to think negatively about your classmates. This will also increase your self-confidence and willingness to socialize. Give yourself some time, don't expect to have many friends or be familiar with everyone immediately, as this transformation also takes time. Provide yourself with opportunities. You can also use some strategies to get along with everyone. For example, buy them some delicious food or borrow books from them. When you gradually release this goodwill, they will feel it. Gradually, your interpersonal relationships will become more harmonious. I think this is foreseeable, so don't worry too much. You can do it!

question: Am I being too dramatic if I frequently get angry in relationships?
description: My personality is quite good. Since I started dating, everything was fine at first. Whenever we had conflicts, I would sulk and ignore him, and he would come over and softly ask what was wrong. After half a year, I felt that he was not as attentive to me anymore. I expressed my dissatisfaction, but instead of coming to comfort me, he turned around and walked away. A few minutes later, he came back and asked why I was angry. I didn't know what to say, I just felt more and more upset, with increasing feelings of dissatisfaction, and the number of times I sulked also increased. Gradually, after we had arguments, he stopped talking and started giving me the silent treatment. After seven days, on 520 (May 20th), I endured it until the afternoon and spoke to him, sent a red envelope, trying to ease the tension, but his attitude remained cold. I told him I missed him, and he said he was conflicted. I just want to ask, in this situation, am I being immature? Am I being too dramatic? It seems like constantly throwing fits is a sign of depression, but I don't know how I became like this. Am I just not good enough? I just want him to pay more attention to me and spend more time with me...

answers.answer_text: Hugs to the OP (๑•.•๑) Actually, girls are prone to being hesitant and insecure in relationships. This is the side effect of love. However, when this kind of emotion occurs too frequently, it is necessary to regulate it yourself! My boyfriend and I are in a long-distance relationship due to military service. When we were apart for two months, I also felt this way. I worried that our relationship would become less strong and that the love would fade away when we finally met. With various factors at play, my emotions were unstable. But I didn't want to constantly transfer negative energy to him. When I realized that I was overthinking, I found things to do, like writing and working out, to keep myself busy and engaged in my interests. When I shared these with him, I felt that he was also happy. No partner wants to constantly receive negative energy from the other half! Two people should progress and grow together, rather than being trapped in emotions and pulling each other down. As for your boyfriend's attitude, I think it's time to clarify whether he still loves you. It's been seven days without contact, which is enough for you to overthink. You should weigh your options. In fact, there's no need to be indirect if you want to care. Just say, "I want you to be more attentive, please spend time with me." That's enough. Boys don't understand hints too well. I hope you find happiness.

question: I feel anxious and agitated when working, feeling nervous and uneasy, and afraid of making mistakes.
description: I am 19 years old and have just started working. I don't know why, but I feel extremely afraid of making mistakes at work. I also feel inexplicably nervous. I work as an HR and my job involves making phone calls and sending messages to communicate with others, as well as inviting them for interviews at our company. However, during conversations, I feel a great deal of anxiety and urgency (I believe I have obsessive tendencies). I am very afraid of making mistakes, and I am afraid that people won't reply to my messages or that I will encounter any negative attitudes from them (I think I am a very sensitive person). Even a slight change in someone's expression can make me feel very unsettled. I get very nervous when making phone calls. I feel that others are much stronger than me, and I am afraid of encountering unfriendly attitudes from them, which has led to many negotiations falling through. So, I often avoid looking at my phone or chatting on WeChat at work to avoid contact with people who make me afraid. I have never been liked by others since I was young, and the most common feelings I have had during my growth process are loneliness and being ostracized. What should I do? How can I solve this problem?

answers.answer_text: You can start working at the age of 19, I have to say, compared to your peers, you are already very worthy of encouragement. Most people at this age are not yet capable of handling things on their own, and you need to realize that you have already started your career earlier than them. Keep up the good work. Let's look at your issue again: "I am very afraid of making mistakes and inexplicably nervous while working." First of all, this is a stage that anyone would go through when encountering new things. It is a phase of adjustment and a natural expression. The fundamental reason is that you lack experience and are unaware of the upper and lower limits of your ability in this matter. This stage will gradually improve as you accumulate a certain number of working days in this position. I work as an HR, and my job involves making phone calls and sending messages on the phone to communicate with others, as well as inviting them to come for interviews at our company. Being able to describe your job responsibilities shows that you have reached a stage of reflection, where you can step back from the nervousness of working and evaluate your job state. This is great. Being able to see your state is the first step in improving it. However, you need to examine your internal thoughts. While chatting, I feel a sense of anxiety and urgency (I think I have compulsive tendencies). I am very afraid of making mistakes, afraid that they won't reply to my messages, and very scared to see any attitude from them (I think I am a very sensitive person). Even a simple expression from someone can make me feel very uneasy. When making phone calls, I am very nervous. I feel that others are much stronger than me, and I am afraid of seeing an unfriendly attitude from them, which has caused many things to fail. The core of your job is communication with others, and the main obstacle is that you dare not and fear facing others' feedback. Compulsive anxiety is one aspect, but more importantly, your obstacle lies in the fact that you may subconsciously confuse the "psychological state that should exist in work" with the psychological state of "life." Because HR is a job that involves communication and interaction, please note that it is a job, but "communication and interaction" itself is also a part of our daily life. Therefore, it is possible that in your daily communication with family and friends, there are tendencies to please others, such as being unable to face and deal with differences, conflicts, or even confrontations with others, or not knowing how to proactively adjust bad interpersonal relationships. The reasons behind this require you to carefully review your past experiences and think: if you have encountered really terrible interpersonal relationships, intimate relationships, let's not worry about how these relationships actually were, ask yourself: were you at fault in these bad relationships? Was it your problem? (Your answer:) I have never been liked by others since I was young, and the most common feelings I have throughout my growth process are loneliness and being excluded. You feel that you are not liked by others, lonely, and excluded, which is actually a self-consciousness of low self-esteem and high self-denial. So, I think your answer to the previous question may be: yes. However, the feeling of "not being liked by others, being excluded" is fundamentally subjective. You are a very sensitive person, so you may be very perceptive to the emotions of others, which leads to you feeling excluded. Sensitivity is a double-edged sword: the benefit is that being aware of others' emotions is a natural advantage for HR work. You should use your sensitivity to better communicate with others and overcome the psychological impulse to avoid challenges based on your own successful experiences. The downside is that you may unconsciously magnify others' emotional reactions. In fact, to your work subjects, you are not you. In their eyes, you are a dedicated recruiter, someone with prestige. So don't immerse yourself in your work, it's the HR you in conversation with others, not your personal self. You just need to learn how to effectively utilize your sensitive trait and reconcile it with your work; then your job will definitely go smoothly.

Social anxiety disorder is a common psychological issue that many people experience. It primarily depends on the individual's experiences from birth until now, including interactions with parents, friends, teachers, classmates, and colleagues, among others. In order to fundamentally change this lack of confidence, the key is to trust oneself completely and provide sufficient self-encouragement. When facing superiors or loved ones, it is important not to excessively focus on their evaluation. Instead, freely express one's own thoughts. I once heard about a self-motivation course on unlocking one's potential, and I would like to share some of the main exercises with you. 1. Speaking in front of a mirror is more challenging than speaking in front of others. Each of us finds it difficult to identify our own flaws. Therefore, practice speaking in front of a mirror every day. Present the information that needs to be reported to superiors and pay attention to facial expressions and body language reflected in the mirror. Additionally, use a mobile phone to record your speech, and then listen to identify any inappropriate aspects, making necessary improvements. Although it may feel awkward to speak in front of oneself, it is much easier to discover and correct shortcomings compared to being told by others to improve. This exercise can greatly help in building confidence. 2. Exercise is always the easiest way to demonstrate confidence. Continuously set fitness goals for oneself. For example, today I will run one kilometer and do fifty push-ups. Tomorrow I will run one thousand two hundred meters and do seventy push-ups. These goals can be achieved with a little effort, and with persistence, confidence will naturally radiate from within. The person's overall state of mind will be filled with vitality. 3. Engaging in communication and interaction with others. For example, when working on a particular task or engaging in sports, engage in conversations with those who excel in those areas. Absorb their strengths and improve one's own weaknesses. Engage in discussions with those who are slightly less skilled, both helping them improve their weaknesses and strengthening one's own self-confidence. Building and optimizing interpersonal relationships is the bridge to effective communication. When getting along harmoniously with colleagues and loved ones, one will feel more at ease when giving presentations or reports. I hope my answer can be of assistance.

Hello, this problem has a huge impact on you. Working at the age of 19 is considered early, and you may not understand many interpersonal issues yet. It is not easy for you. You have a strong self-esteem, but at the age where you still lack work experience, it is indeed difficult for a young adult to cope with. Let's analyze together and hope it helps you. Analyzing and understanding the problem: 1. You are 19 years old this year and just started working. You don't know why you feel extremely scared of making mistakes at work and you also feel inexplicably nervous (because you are young, because you lack work experience, because you are afraid of making mistakes, because you are afraid of being disliked by others, because it hurts your self-esteem, because of too many unknowns, resulting in anxiety). 2. Your job is in HR and your tasks include making phone calls and sending messages to communicate with others, as well as inviting them to come for interviews at your company (Ideally, your position is more proactive, and the interviewees should come to you. You shouldn't worry too much. However, it seems that your issue is not related to your job, but rather a psychological one. Is that right?). 3. However, during conversations, you feel anxious and in a hurry (you feel like you have an obsessive tendency). You are very afraid of making mistakes, of them not replying to your messages, and you are very afraid of seeing any negative attitudes from them (you think you are a very sensitive person). Even a facial expression from others can make you feel very uneasy (you have a severe fear of the unknown. If we talk about obsessive tendencies, they can be divided into obsessive thinking and obsessive behaviors. Afraid of making mistakes, afraid of people not replying to your messages, we can talk about the extent of it some other time. It seems like there are some obsessive behaviors, as if there are defensive mechanisms of "offsetting". However, the information is not particularly accurate, so I dare not make further comments). 4. When making phone calls, you are very nervous and you feel like others are much stronger than you, and you are afraid of seeing unfriendly attitudes towards you, so many things end up going wrong (Do you often have a need to please others psychologically? Ideally, everyone is just human, they might have more experience than you, but it doesn't mean that everything they do is better than you. But if you have such inferiority, it will affect your confidence and influence your actions). 5. Therefore, you often avoid looking at your phone and avoid chatting on WeChat during work, to avoid contact with those who make you feel scared. Throughout your life, you have never been liked by others, and your most common experiences while growing up have been loneliness and being excluded. What should you do? How to solve this problem? (Avoiding looking at your phone is not a solution because work needs to continue. Can you really avoid contact? If you have never been liked by others throughout your life, do your parents not like you either? When you experience loneliness and exclusion, don't your parents help you or comfort you? Don't worry, it's okay. You're only 19 years old, and it's still very possible to adjust your personality. Don't be afraid, I will help you.) Facing the problem: "When working, feeling anxious, irritable, nervous, and uneasy, afraid of making mistakes" ~ Is it just at work? What about other times? If it's only at work, that's easier to handle. It will probably only take a couple of consultations to solve the problem. But if it's not just at work and it has already affected your life or intimate relationships, you may need to start investigating from your "family background". Presumably, there were problems during your childhood growth ~ Anxiety, irritability, nervousness, uneasiness, and fear of making mistakes are common when people start working. I was the same, trembling even worse than you. Of course, later on, I found a solution and it was fine. Making mistakes is normal, how could a person never make mistakes? They're not gods. If you think you shouldn't make mistakes, then if you do make a mistake, it would be a huge deal. If you think making mistakes is normal, and that you can learn from them and continuously improve, then making mistakes is not scary. It's an essential part of your growth. Because being afraid of making mistakes doesn't mean you won't make them. Have those people who don't like you and exclude you never made mistakes? Haven't they thought it was a big deal either? You need to adjust some of your thoughts and experiences, so you can gain more positive and successful experiences inside you and then you won't fear anymore. Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you open up yourself and grow up quickly! No more fear! No more anxiety! If you have any doubts, you can private message me!

Growth is finding a breakthrough in this circle, changing the trajectory, spiraling growth, and becoming a better self. Journey of the heart: Beginning: The poster is 19 years old this year and has just started working in HR, with daily tasks involving communicating with others and inviting them for interviews at the company. Crisis: This avoidance, tension, and fear in their work and life have led to many things falling apart for them and to missing out on many things. Treasure: The current state of their work reminds them of not being liked when they were young. The most common feeling they have had throughout their growth process is loneliness and exclusion. They suspect they have symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Conclusion: The anxiety in their work and life is like a stone pressing on their heart, severely affecting their life and work, and causing significant psychological pressure. Life circle: The circle they have created for themselves is being afraid of making mistakes, and the more they fear making mistakes, the more they make mistakes. This leads to them feeling a great deal of psychological pressure, which in turn worsens their anxiety, and they continue to work in this state. Circle: Work – Fear of making mistakes – Making mistakes at work – Avoidance – Anxiety – Work. Exploring the reasons: Lack of self-confidence: The poster has just started working and is unfamiliar with everything. They can say that they were not ready to work, but work has already started. They lack confidence in their work, leading to their worries and fears. The nature of their work presents a great challenge to their innate personality. Breaking through innate personality: The poster realizes that their personality may be related to their experiences from childhood to adulthood. This is actually a challenge for themselves. In their innate personality, they may take themselves too seriously, thinking that their slightest actions would be viewed with strange eyes by others. They need to learn to view others and themselves with equality. They are not as important in others' eyes as they think, and the same goes for others. They don't need to be too concerned about how their actions affect others or how others' actions affect them. Very few people truly care about these things. Similarly, when inviting others for interviews, the same applies. Other people will also face invitations from others, and the probability of mutual selection is very low. Learning to communicate: Communication is something that can be learned. In communication, listening is important. They should listen to identify problems and needs, and then express their own needs in a way that others prefer. They can buy books on communication and try to learn communication skills. Building confidence – Breaking through innate personality – Learning to communicate – Changing the trajectory – Spiral growth – Becoming a better self. I'm 19 years old and have just started working. I don't know why I feel extremely afraid of making mistakes while working, and I also inexplicably feel very nervous. I work as an HR and my tasks involve making phone calls and sending messages on my phone to communicate with others for work, as well as inviting them to come for interviews at our company. But when chatting, I feel a sense of anxiety and urgency (I think I have obsessive tendencies). I'm afraid of making mistakes, and I'm very scared that people won't reply to my messages. I'm also afraid of seeing any attitude from them (I think I'm a sensitive person). Even a simple expression from others makes me feel unsettled. I feel very nervous when making phone calls. I feel that others are much stronger than me, and I'm afraid of seeing unfriendly attitudes from them. As a result, many things fall apart for me. So, I often avoid looking at my phone and chatting on WeChat during work to avoid contact with people who make me afraid. Throughout my life, I've always been disliked by others, and the most common feeling I have during my growth process is loneliness and being excluded. What should I do? How can I solve this problem?

You are still young and just starting to look for a job. Typically, the people being hired are older and more experienced than you, so it's normal to feel nervous due to your lack of experience. Don't put too much pressure on yourself and remind yourself that even if you make small mistakes, it's not a big deal. You are still growing and as you gain more experience and interact with more people, you will naturally become more confident. Your fear of not receiving a reply or seeing the other person's reaction is all in your imagination. Perhaps it is because of your past experiences of being excluded that subconsciously make you feel that every action the other person takes is directed towards you negatively. But the reality is not like that, and you know it. You are just struggling to change your way of thinking. So, you need to constantly remind yourself of what reality truly is. For example, if the candidate you reached out to doesn't reply to your message, it could be because they have sent out multiple applications and don't think this position is suitable for them, or maybe they have already found a job. It is highly unlikely that they are not responding because they dislike you as an HR representative since their main concern is the job's salary and responsibilities, not your relationship with them. As for interpreting other people's expressions, you must resist and rationalize your initial thoughts. For example, if you feel that the other person is being rude to you because they have something against you, their behavior is likely influenced by other factors such as what they have experienced that day, their own thoughts, and their personal goals. Everyone is self-focused, so it is rare for someone to genuinely target you specifically. Therefore, you need to continuously convince yourself that they do not have ill intentions. Additionally, since you are young and inexperienced, facing failure in the workplace is normal. So, you need to continuously improve your professional skills and expertise with a humble attitude. View your current failures as learning experiences, even if they are indeed caused by your actions. If so, you will understand why it happened, and you can take note of the solution to this problem and consult with more experienced colleagues. Eventually, you will internalize these skills and accumulate a wealth of experience in five or ten years. By then, you will be in your early thirties but have a significant amount of experience that you cannot compare to now. Many people start over in their thirties, so why not treat these ten years as practice? Maybe having this mindset will make you feel better. Young people should be patient and tolerant with themselves. Approach everything with rational and growth-oriented thinking, and believe that one day you will reap the fruits of your efforts.

Thank you for your trust. I suggest considering the problems you encounter from three perspectives. 1. The job itself: HR is a profession that requires frequent contact with strangers and constant interaction with various people. For whatever reason, you chose this job, and it has indeed presented you with some challenges. 2. Ourselves: "I have never been liked by others since I was young, and the most common feelings I have had during my growth are loneliness and exclusion." Regardless of the job we engage in, there may be some differences in interacting and communicating with others, but it is inevitable. Therefore, we need to make efforts and adjustments to adapt better. 3. Compatibility with our job: Among the basic skills required for HR, which ones do we possess or even excel at? Which ones do we currently lack but are willing to change? Which ones do we currently lack and cannot change? All of these are worth pondering.

Starting to work at the age of 19 is already quite challenging, considering how young you are. You shouldn't put too much pressure on yourself. Compared to many people your age, you have entered the workforce earlier, which is an advantage for you. It's also a moment for gaining experience and personal growth. Working in HR requires dealing with people, conducting interviews, and managing interpersonal relationships, which test your ability to handle and coordinate such relationships. As an individual, you need confidence and independence. If you feel that you haven't been liked since you were young and have experienced exclusion, it might be due to certain events that have made you feel fearful and lacking in security, resulting in difficulties in interacting with others. If that's the case, you need to strengthen your communication skills and ability to express yourself. Engage in more communication with colleagues at work, interact with others in a friendly and open manner, and be able to express yourself in a genuine way. You can also read books on interpersonal relationships and communication, learn from experiences, and find ways to adjust yourself. Additionally, if you find it difficult to adjust and lack problem-solving skills, it may be helpful to seek professional help to face your own issues, get counseling, and work on resolving the conflicts between your thoughts and emotions. This will help you find ways to change this series of difficulties. With time and the accumulation of experience and improvement in your work, you will gradually see improvements in this issue.

A college student majoring in human resource management passed by, firstly I express understanding and sympathy for your situation. Following your line of thinking, since this job has been tormenting you and you want to avoid making mistakes, why not just switch to another job and completely bid farewell to this unpleasantness? It's not that you aren't good, it's just that this job is not suitable for you! Stop blaming yourself, it's not your fault at all! In my opinion, the simplest and most effective solution is to recommend switching to a different job. Enhancing yourself is the best way to alleviate anxiety and tension. Shift your attention to self-improvement, and I believe you will be much better. Keep it up!

First, give yourself a hug. The impression I get is that you seem to have an unfair judgment about your own self-worth. You have already assumed that you won't be liked, so you unconsciously undervalue your own worth at work. This has also caused physical reactions in your body. The next time you experience physical reactions, maybe you can stay with your emotions for a while and ask yourself what you're really thinking. Are these thoughts really valid? Allow yourself to acknowledge the existence of negative emotions, don't avoid them. Tell your emotions that you see them and that you allow their presence. These negative emotions yearn for your acknowledgment, letting you know they exist. Only by acknowledging them can you bring about change.

question: Recently in a state of low depression, I often stay up late reading novels, and I am not engaged in my work. What should I do?
description: Recently, I have been staying up late reading novels and not being fully engaged in work. What should I do? It has been seven to eight months.

answers.answer_text: Seeing that this is the latest problem, let me start. I have encountered this problem myself, and perhaps most people are also facing this problem. So, I can relate to it and based on my own experience, I would like to give some advice to the original poster. Let's start with online novels. Nowadays, there are various types available and they are indeed very enjoyable to read. They can be so captivating that you can't stop reading, and some well-written ones can make readers feel like they are immersed in the story, fantasizing themselves as the protagonist of the novel. Looking forward to the updates. Let's take the popular fantasy novels as an example. It's basically about a weak male protagonist who overturns his destiny. However, if we look at it from a different perspective, doesn't this also represent opportunities in real life? These weak protagonists often possess qualities such as not giving up, daring to take risks, and being willing to work hard, which is why they are favored. What about the readers themselves? Perhaps they lack those qualities that the protagonist possesses. This may be the appeal of these novels, as they make readers also anticipate the possibility of encountering great opportunities and soaring to new heights someday. But you have to understand that nobody's success happens overnight. Ordinary people can't achieve everything without making efforts. Now, let's talk about the readers. Why do you read novels? Just for the sake of spiritual satisfaction? Why do you postpone doing things that you can do at the age of 80 to when you should be working hard? What can you gain from reading novels? Yeah, you say that you are already working. Then, isn't it time to consider your career? Isn't it time to think about the future? Shouldn't you set some plans and goals for yourself? The most important point I want to emphasize is that you mentioned being in a depressed state recently. Is it because of relationship issues or work problems? Actually, no matter what the problem is, no matter what hardships you face, as long as you believe in yourself, have dreams in your heart, and the spark in your eyes, you will definitely overcome it. Find the root cause of the problem and try to solve it. If you have any questions, you can leave a message for me. Keep going, original poster. I believe you can get through this period of depression. Good luck~.

question: Good friends have been working hard recently and I am afraid that she will surpass me. What should I do?
description: I am always stingy with my good friends, but I am very nice to ordinary classmates. Previously, my good friend did not study hard, so my grades are better than hers. She has been studying hard recently, but I am afraid she will surpass me. I don't want to interact with her much lately. What should I do? I'm really afraid of her surpassing me.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I completely understand how you feel, sending you a big hug~ Let's talk through your thoughts and hopefully give you some insight~ You mentioned that you're very scared of your close friend achieving better grades than you. So, an important question to ask is, what would happen if she surpasses you? In other words, why do you feel afraid of her surpassing you? Ask yourself this question and I believe you'll have some answers. What do you think will happen after she surpasses you? Will she mock you or look down on you? Will she show off and annoy you? But regardless of what happens, what you're truly afraid of is your imagination. You think that something unpleasant will happen, but it's very likely that it won't. From an objective standpoint, whether her grades surpass yours or not, it doesn't have a direct impact on you, you are still you. Moreover, since she is a good friend, you should hope that she achieves even better grades not just for the sake of blessing her, but also because her success can serve as motivation for you. You can see her as a fair competitor or a role model, and you can learn from each other and progress together. So, it's necessary to examine your thoughts and beliefs and consider whether her surpassing you truly affects you. Will her surpassing you bring positive effects to yourself? Try looking at this issue from a different perspective, and don't let something that is completely the responsibility of others affect you. Ultimately, what matters most is your own achievements, rather than seeking affirmation or even superiority through comparisons. Wishing you well~

question: Feeling like always telling "lies" for work, feeling frustrated, not liking it like this?
description: We cannot avoid dealing with others and collaborating with them in work. However, when I become a project planner, I always have to allocate tasks to other colleagues. I worry that if I directly assign tasks to them, they may not feel engaged, but if I don't assign tasks directly, there may be some discrepancies. Sometimes, my colleagues don't cooperate, and I really want to get angry, but I have to go against my own feelings and say thank you to everyone for their cooperation and appreciate their hard work... I don't like these kinds of situations, and I don't like myself in these situations either...

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~ First, let me give you an encouraging hug. I completely understand how you're feeling right now. As a project planner, it's natural to feel worried that your employees might not be motivated or engaged in their work. That's why you might find yourself saying things that seem like you're seeking help from others, which can make you feel uncomfortable. This is a very normal phenomenon because we lose ourselves and no longer feel like ourselves. Whether it's in our family or in society, as members of society, many things we do are not driven by our inner feelings. For example, in our family, when our parents argue, we are forced to choose sides or mediate between them, but deep down, it's not what we want to do, we may actually want to leave home at that moment. At work, we have to deal with our bosses and lead our employees, and many of our words and actions are not truly heartfelt. Of course, if you are really feeling uncomfortable, you can completely change your leadership and organizational style. For example, you can learn how other planners lead their teams. Or you can take a lazy approach, which is to refuse to be a planner, but this method is not recommended. I hope you can adjust yourself soon, succeed in your career, and rise up step by step. Best wishes~.

question: There is a particularly sensitive person in the self-study room. How can one adjust their mentality? How can one find a balance?
description: The study room has a girl who is particularly sensitive to noise. She makes very loud noises when flipping through books and often sighs loudly. However, as soon as others make any noise, she immediately criticizes them like a moral warrior. I really dislike her psychologically, and I have confronted her about it. I am quite direct and haven't shown complete patience. She doesn't seem to notice my dissatisfaction and continues to make loud noises. Moreover, I feel like she is somewhat targeting me as she always insists on closing the window that I opened. However, in order to avoid conflicts with her, I make very little noise, which makes it difficult for me to fully concentrate, and my studying speed has also slowed down. How can I adjust my mindset? Teachers or experienced friends, how do you balance this?

answers.answer_text:
Hello, based on the situation you described, I'd like to share my thoughts with you, is that okay? 
1. "There is a girl in the study room who is particularly sensitive to noise. She makes loud noises when flipping through books and often sighs loudly. But when others make noise, she immediately acts like a moral warrior and goes to criticize them." From the situation you described, it seems that you have encountered someone who is only willing to satisfy themselves without understanding or empathizing with others. 
2. "I really dislike her psychologically, and I have dealt with her before. I tend to be straightforward and not completely tolerant." It is normal to dislike her in this situation: in public places, she should also have some moral qualities. It is not wrong for you to express your thoughts correctly. 
3. "She seems to not notice my dissatisfaction, and she still makes loud noises. Moreover, I feel that she is targeting me because she always wants to close the window I opened." She should have noticed your dissatisfaction and is now taking a confrontational approach by using her actions to resist your "dealings" with her. 
4. "But in order to avoid conflicts with her, I keep my voice very low, which makes it difficult for me to fully concentrate and slows down my learning speed." It is evident that you are very considerate of others. Although you don't want to disturb others, she still flips books loudly. This world is inherently diverse, and there will be people with different personalities. We go to the study room to find a quiet and undisturbed environment. If the studying atmosphere is not good, what is the point of going to that study room? Why don't we look for a new study room within our own range of life? We can think about things differently in some aspects, and perhaps our emotional state will be different. In psychology, there is a theory called the ABC theory of emotions: it was created by American psychologist Albert Ellis. He believes that the triggering event (A) is only an indirect cause of emotions and behavioral consequences (C), and the direct cause of C is the individual's cognitive evaluation and belief (B) about the triggering event. That is to say, the negative emotions (C) of a person are not directly caused by a particular triggering event (A), but are directly caused by the individual's cognition and evaluation of it, which leads to beliefs (B). In other words, the same behavior of the same person may be interpreted differently by different people, thus leading to different emotional outcomes. Think about it: if you brush off her rude behavior, this matter will not create ripples in your heart. You may find another study room to get away from her, and she will not be a bother to you. I hope this can be of help to you. Good luck!

question: Bizarre roommate, who ignores everything and comes and goes early, how to continue living with her?
description: Junior student, I have a roommate. When we first started living together in my freshman year, I thought her personality was okay. If you talk to her, she will chat with you, and if you ask her for help with things like taking food, she will also help you. But over time, I noticed that she is a bit sensitive. answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) Recently, you have been coming home late and not interacting with anyone. (2) You want to know how to continue getting along with him. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: (1) First, you mentioned that your roommate's personality is generally okay, but after spending time together, you noticed that he may be sensitive and easily gets upset. This is actually quite normal, as everyone has different points of concern and ways of expressing emotions. It is just that her way of expressing emotions is different from others. (2) Secondly, you said that recently your roommate has been coming home late and not talking to anyone. You are concerned about why this is happening. I suggest sending her a text message to ask how she's been lately, just to show your care. However, try to avoid using a confrontational tone, as it may not only hurt her but also help you understand the truth of the situation. (3) Lastly, you are unsure how to get along with him. I understand that you hope for a peaceful atmosphere, but remember that your roommate cannot be forced into being a friend. Alongside showing concern, it is important for us to live our own lives well, don't you think? #The world and I love you, wishing you all the best~

question: I am curious about myself and would like to understand the reasons behind my thoughts and behaviors.
description: For example, during the process of memorizing, I always have self-doubt and feel that what I am memorizing is useless. Either I want everything or I feel that it is not important. I want to pursue perfect memorization, where I only memorize what will be tested. But this is unattainable, and it makes me anxious. I find myself unable to continue memorizing halfway through, and there is a faint voice in my mind saying, "Forget it, just leave it like this." What is even stranger is that when I can't continue memorizing, I expect my roommates to be the same as me, unable to continue. And when they are studying and I'm not, I get nervous and afraid that they will surpass me. This happens in many aspects of my life. I feel like there's something wrong with me. I know these thoughts are not right when they come up, but they persist every time. Also, I only have shallow relationships with others, without deeper connections. Is this related to these thoughts? I am afraid of failure, being forgotten, people knowing my weaknesses, and being lonely. I think about changing every day, but I never take action. How can I start moving and find my own direction?
keywords: Growth, character development, personality traits, self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the questioner always has various thoughts in his mind when facing uncertain things. Everyone experiences this situation, so there is no need to judge oneself too harshly. The ultimate choice of which voice to listen to determines the outcome of the situation. It is evident that you have been listening to the noise rather than the voice of your heart. From the description of your living and studying situation in the dormitory, it is clear that your past family has made many judgments about you, using comparisons to evaluate your worth. This has caused you to determine your own value in comparison with others. When it comes to studying, there will be various distractions. It is like the clouds that cover the sun. You have identified with the clouds and cannot see the sun. This is related to the fact that your past feelings and thoughts were not allowed. It is a task you need to clean up and face. Pay more attention to your own feelings in daily life, and do more of what makes you feel peaceful and joyful. Allow your inner feelings to be expressed. In the constant accumulation of certainty, you will hear the voice of your heart. This voice will be what you truly want, an unshakable presence like the sun. I wish you can return to your inner self and regain the strength to be yourself.

question: Why does someone's appearance feel different?
description: The photos were taken in 2011, 2015, and 2020, respectively. Although I didn't do much makeup, I feel different in each photo. Why is that?

answers.answer_text: Hello, as they say: "A woman changes a lot by the time she turns 18". As time goes by, our bodies undergo some changes, such as changes in facial appearance, the emergence of forehead wrinkles, skin aging with the appearance of wrinkles, the decline in the functioning of body organs, and the inconvenience in leg movements, among other common things. Life, aging, sickness, and death are all natural laws, and we should accept them with a positive attitude and face them calmly. I believe that as long as our mindset is good and we have a youthful heart, age doesn't matter. I wish the original poster a happy and carefree life, forever 18!

question: There is considerable variation among individuals in their degree of extroversion, self-esteem, and fear of others, as well as their propensity for comparing themselves to others.
description: I am a Leo girl, very insecure, and I think I look ugly and fat. However, I like to compare myself with others. I feel envious and sad when I see girls who are very beautiful. Why can't I be so good-looking? I also feel that I'm not likable, only outgoing and talkative people are likable. I feel like a failure, very lonely, sobbing.
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello. I noticed your inner uneasiness and I'm sending you a hug. In the process of growth and awakening, we often experience anxiety and self-doubt. Leo is said to be the most confident zodiac sign, but it seems that we can't fully rely on astrology. Let me give you some advice: try to see yourself from a different perspective. You mentioned that you like to compare yourself to others, and it made me wonder, what standards do you use for comparison? How do you define beauty? We can only say that some people align more with the mainstream aesthetic. Does having double eyelids automatically make someone more attractive than those with single eyelids? Does being thin automatically make someone more attractive than someone who is overweight? There are people who will appreciate you for who you are. Make a change. The person who is in pain should be the one to change. If you've read the previous suggestion and still can't accept yourself as you are, then make a change. If you feel fat, start exercising; if you feel ugly, learn about fashion and makeup; if you feel unlikeable, learn how to interact with others and improve your emotional intelligence. If you want to compare yourself, please do so in a comprehensive manner and don't just focus on the aspects where others surpass you. Some people may be more attractive than you, but their work abilities may not be as strong as yours; some people may excel in their work, but their personalities may not be as good as yours. Everyone has their own unique characteristics, and no one can outshine you completely. I hope you can find your own strength.

I am also a Leo sign and I enjoy comparing myself to others. Why are other people's legs longer, why are others fairer, why do others have such good memory, why do others have a better family environment, why can others act cute? There are many questions and comparisons. However, after chatting with classmates and friends, I learned that we also have qualities that they want. We often see the better parts of others, but we often overlook our own outstanding qualities. Let's magnify our own strengths, write down 10 good qualities about ourselves every day, and tell ourselves that we are great. As for the areas that we envy in others, let's start with the most urgent part, set a plan, and gradually improve ourselves.

question: The mother's unwillingness to let her daughter get married or work denotes what psychological state?
description: I see a report about a mother who does not allow her daughter to marry and does not want her to work either. She only hopes to keep her by her side and never leave her. What kind of mentality is this?

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, I am also curious about why this mother "does not allow her daughter to marry and does not want her to work, only wants to keep her by her side". Returning to the psychological factors, from the surface or conscious level, the most likely possibility is that this mother is too attached to her daughter and cannot bear the emotional void that would arise if her daughter were to leave home. However, from the subconscious level, there may be different reasons, which would require more comprehensive information for analysis. These specific cases require specific analysis.

question: How can I deal with excessive suspicion that prevents me from forming intimate relationships with others?
description: I tend to maintain a skeptical attitude towards the people around me, afraid of others disliking me and afraid of being deceived by others. I am a perfectionist in terms of emotions and extremely sensitive, so I am unwilling to trust anyone and always feel that others have ulterior motives. I have difficulty establishing intimate relationships, but on the other hand, I yearn for good friends and the ability to establish close relationships with others. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory states that individuals always have a strong emotional and belonging need, and they long to establish good and enduring intimate relationships with others. This need allows us to build friendships, experience love, and increase our sense of well-being. We all hope to establish good intimate relationships and feel the companionship and true love within these relationships. However, during this process, we will inevitably encounter various challenges and difficulties. Intimate relationships require learning and practice. Firstly, we need to clarify which type of intimate relationship we belong to. Psychological research suggests that the attachment characteristics exhibited by children will continue to manifest in adulthood, so adults have attachment classifications similar to those of children. A. Secure attachment: It is easy for them to get close to others and they do not feel distressed due to excessive dependency or abandonment by others. Such lovers also enjoy love in safe and loyal interactions, and their relationships can be satisfying and long-lasting. They make up about 70% of the population. B. Anxious-ambivalent attachment: They lack trust in others and tend to have strong possessiveness and jealousy. Their relationships with the same person may repeatedly break, and they tend to become easily agitated and angry during conflicts. They make up about 10% of the population. C. Avoidant attachment: They are prone to avoiding intimate relationships, showing less interest in such relationships, and have a tendency to escape from them. They are both afraid of and reject others. They may end up in purely sexual relationships without love. They make up about 20% of the population. Traces of childhood experiences can be found in adult behavior. In addition, the interaction between parents in childhood will also be internalized into the child's heart, exerting a significant influence on their future intimate relationships. Perhaps you can find some clues from your childhood experiences and interactions with your parents. Finally, here are a few suggestions: 1. First, establish an intimate relationship with yourself. When you truly know yourself, understand yourself, and accept yourself, and establish a good self-identity and sense of value, only then can you truly love yourself and accept your imperfections. This will be an important foundation for us to love others and accept their perfection and imperfection. 2. Understand the importance of giving and dare to self-disclose. Because it is not easy to cultivate intimate relationships, there are not many truly meaningful intimate relationships in a person's life. If we can maintain mutual connection, share, understand, and accept each other while retaining our own individuality, then the intimate relationship will be more enduring and fulfilling.

Hello, OP. Through your description, I can sense your insecurity in interpersonal relationships. This yearning yet fearful feeling is indeed quite tormenting. So what can we do? Take it little by little, step by step, and open up gradually. Building healthy interpersonal relationships is a skill that needs to be learned and practiced. When should we open up? How much should we open up? How do we protect our boundaries? How do we handle conflicts?... Fear and anxiety can hold us back, but what we can do is: 1. Improve our self-protective ability, 2. Enhance our resilience against pressure, 3. Enhance our self-healing ability. These are all things we can slowly explore and find the communication and interaction style that suits us best, where we feel comfortable and at ease. Just thinking without taking action only adds to our worries. By getting out and about, we may find our own little corner of the world. If, by any chance, you encounter setbacks and feel upset, come back here and confide in us. We will face it together, discuss it together, and accompany you through it.

Good evening! In psychology, there is a term called projection. The projection effect refers to the tendency to attribute one's own characteristics to others. When perceiving and forming impressions of others, there is a phenomenon of assuming that others have similar traits to oneself, projecting one's emotions, will, and characteristics onto others and imposing them on others, which is a cognitive barrier known as the "doom-loop". For example, a kind-hearted person may believe that others are also kind-hearted. So, are you unwilling to believe in yourself? In building intimate relationships, I think it is important to first learn to love yourself, listen to your own feelings, encourage and accept yourself. When we see our own strengths, we can also see the strengths of others. Everyone wants to be noticed, praised, and respected. Likewise, when we have these qualities in our hearts, we can give them to others. So, my dear, try to praise yourself every day, acknowledge what you can do, change your mood, and it will change your energy field. When you look into the eyes of others, they will look back at you differently. Give it a try and good luck!

question: Every time I argue with my mother, I feel like I'm unnecessary and want to die.
description: Lately, I have been having thoughts of whether I am unnecessary and have had a few suicidal tendencies.

answers.answer_text: Hello, topic master, hello, give you a hug~ After reading many studies, in the eyes of most children, the mother always ranks first. Even if the mother sometimes scolds the child, the child still loves the mother very much. This is due to instinct, which determines from birth that the child has an inseparable connection with the mother. So I can understand why you feel so sad when you have conflicts with your mother, because you love your mother, and you also believe that your mother is the person who loves you the most in the world. From your description of "feeling redundant every time you argue with your mother," I can imagine that when you argue with your mother, she has said some hurtful things that have made you doubt your own existence, or you have said some things that have saddened your mother. I know that the words spoken when you are angry are not what you really wanted to express. You are just temporarily blinded by emotions and speak without thinking. Gratitude increases happiness. Studies have shown that gratitude can reduce individual psychopathological symptoms and increase happiness. When you argue with your mother, the emotion of anger fills your minds and hearts, causing you to make many wrong decisions and even forget the joy and happiness that you bring to each other, as well as forgetting gratitude. Understanding gratitude is important, not only for children to be grateful to their parents, but also for parents to be grateful for the happiness and pride their children bring to them. If we only focus on being dominated by angry emotions and forget the efforts we have made for each other, our behavior will be like an out-of-control beast, doing things that we will regret, and in the end, it is our family that gets hurt. So you must communicate with your parents calmly and always remember the joy and comfortable life that your parents have brought to you, maintain a grateful heart, and then you will not be clouded by anger.

question: Why does the mind feel so noisy at night? It's like many people are talking.

keywords: Treatment, somatic response, disease diagnosis, abnormal behavior.

answers.answer_text: Hello! This situation really needs to be carefully assessed to rule out the possibility of hallucinations. question: What is the psychological reason behind the inability to let go of peculiar emotional experiences?
description: I have a long-distance relationship with a boy, and I always feel like he doesn't care about me. He is always busy with work, studying, or other things. We have very little time to chat, and I'm always the one initiating the conversation. However, he never seems interested. Now, I want to reconnect, but I feel irresponsible towards him, so I haven't contacted him. However, I've been having trouble sleeping lately and can't seem to let go. What kind of messed up mentality is this?
keywords: Dating, winning back an ex, arguing, relationship management.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, I can understand that 1. You feel insecure in your online relationship and it seems like the other person doesn't care about you. 2. You feel reluctant to cut off contact, but also feel that maybe the two of you are not suitable for each other. [A little analysis and advice] 1. In any romantic relationship, it is possible to have this kind of anxious and insecure feeling. Especially for girls who are more sensitive, this mindset is even more common. It is normal to hope for a response from the other person because you have always been the one taking the initiative and feel uncomfortable. 2. When you cannot make a decision about the relationship, you might consider the advice of friends and family. Think back to your exchanges with the other person, what kind of person are they? What are their strengths and weaknesses? Is it worth investing your emotions in them for a long time? Then make a decision about the relationship, which might be more prudent. I hope this helps you.

question: How to deal with always having a hesitant attitude towards what others say?
description: For example, during a job interview, when discussing salary, performance, and vacation time with a company, if uncertainties arise, the topic may be postponed until later or until after the probation period. Wishing you a smooth job search! Good luck!

question: Why is my boyfriend's mother always interfering in our relationship, even after dating for 4 years?
description: During the four years of dating, my boyfriend's mother always likes to come and stay at the place where we live. She would stay for a week and only go back on weekends, then automatically return the following Monday. She also tells my boyfriend about many of her opinions towards me, which has caused long-term arguments between me and my boyfriend. Additionally, it has almost completely killed our sex life, to the point where we only have it once every two to three months. My boyfriend and I are only 26 years old, yet we are already in a state of almost no sexual activity. Please advise on what to do in this situation.
keywords: Love, arguments, relationship management, sexual behavior.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! You have been in a relationship with your boyfriend for 4 years, and his mother has always been involved, creating a triangular relationship. Or maybe they have a symbiotic relationship, and you are seen as an outsider. As a result, there has been a long period of no sex and constant fighting. Is that correct? It seems like the mother sees her child as "absolutely dependent" on her, which is a pathological symbiosis. I think your boyfriend might have tried to break free from his mother's control and attempted to leave, but ultimately failed and completely gave up his boundaries, allowing his mother to freely control him. And this mother might feel a sense of "being deprived," knowing that her child might become intimate with another woman, which is something she cannot accept internally but cannot prevent in reality. So, she constantly instills negative thoughts about you, causing you two to fight. This has become their long-term way of interacting, and your boyfriend's psychological development is not that of an adult. He is unable to think and solve problems independently, leaving your relationship to continue deteriorating. Being in a relationship with someone who has a severely symbiotic relationship with their parent requires you to first accept it, make the mother let go of her hostility, and give the child the courage and motivation to be independent. This requires tremendous patience and psychological capacity. It's difficult to change in a short period of time. I suggest that, if possible, you seek family counseling to help you adjust your way of interacting.

question: My friend's wife is saying she doesn't want to live anymore, what should I say to persuade her?
description: A friend and his wife have a strained relationship.
