Recently, due to some trivial family matters, his wife has been crying and screaming at home, saying that life is unbearable and even mentioning suicide. My husband and I have a good relationship with them. How should we persuade them at their home? Can anyone help?

answers.answer_text: Seeing your description, I suggest that you not meddle in other people's affairs. If you are taking the man's side to persuade, you will surely not be biased towards the woman. If you stand from the woman's perspective, you will not be biased towards the man. As the saying goes, it is difficult for an impartial official to judge a family matter. You do not know what the wife of your friend has been through, so it is difficult to persuade from an objective point of view. It is best to let them solve the matters of their marriage and family by themselves, and outsiders should not interfere. The more outsiders interfere, the more chaotic it becomes, and ultimately, you may lose this friend. If his wife really shows signs of self-harm or desperation, it is still advisable for your friend to accompany his wife and find a counselor. This can help relieve his wife's emotions and provide better assistance to them.

This depends on the specific situation. For example, emotions are just part of life, and marriages always have their ups and downs. We have encountered all sorts of things. In the past 16 years, we have had our fair share of challenges. One thing that still bothers my partner is that I once contacted my ex from college. Apart from that, she is not satisfied with the amount of time I spend with her shopping. As for the children, I am an essential father figure. I have to work to support them and provide them with emotional support. I also help with their studies, especially my high school child who struggles with chemistry. My arrogant son only comes to me for validation at times like this, while my cautious daughter occasionally makes grammatical mistakes in her compositions, which I do not let slide. As for my wife, she is satisfied with our life together. So, let's approach these matters slowly. Wishing you all the best, my kind-hearted friend.

question: I don't trust my therapist that much either, feeling cold inside and isolated?
description: I read an article that said one's inner self is like a house with drafts, but one day, they finally held hands with a therapist and could peacefully appreciate the world. My inner self is like an empty concrete floor, curled up in the center while stray cats roam around. Occasionally, someone finds me cute and gives me food, and sometimes other cats see me as attractive and try to take advantage. Most of the time, I try to please this world. I don't have the privilege to be willful because there is an older cat beside me who thinks I shouldn't just stay in an empty space. I have to catch mice and pay protection fees so the older cat won't bully me. I am very sad, but I can't cry because I don't have a hut to cry in. I also don't fully trust my therapist, even though she is very good. I have to work hard to earn money to see her, it's a particularly powerless life.

answers.answer_text: Please believe that you are the expert of your own life, and the counselor is merely an assistant and an expert in psychology. From your description, it is clear that you feel it is difficult for yourself, needing to please the world and lacking the right to be willful. There are also people around you rushing you, making you feel like you want to cry, but have no space to do so. So let's imagine what kind of life we actually want. A comfortable space where we can feel at ease, with no need to rely on others to live comfortably and easily. You see, when we see what we truly desire, what our inner needs are, we already have a clear direction in our hearts. So the question is, what can we do to strive towards this desired direction? If we imagine that this desired life is worth 10 points, how many points do we currently have? And what can we do to increase that score? Even if it's just by 0.1 or 0.5, someday we will get closer to the kind of life we want.

question: Unfortunately, the parents may not be compatible individuals, yet they are still bound together.
description: Suddenly discovered that my father is a scumbag, belittling and treating my mother like a slave all his life. It's probably just a case of being with the wrong person, but we, the children, are the unlucky ones. I went crazy once. Sigh.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, sending you virtual hugs. Breaking an egg from the outside represents death, while breaking it from the inside symbolizes growth. In reality, the original family does not have a decisive role in a person's growth or the formation of their character. It also cannot determine whether your future will be happy and fulfilling. The decisive role is played by yourself – how you treat your original family, how you approach your future life, and how you value yourself. The issues within your original family objectively exist, whether in the present or the past – you can no longer change them. The pain you experience is not caused by the pain itself, but rather by your thoughts about it. Now that you have grown up, your ability to overcome this pain depends on how you address it and how you find a resolution. Staying stuck in the same place, entangled with no progress, won't lead to any improvement. True reconciliation within the original family begins when you take responsibility for your own life. You must find a way to resolve these issues, allowing yourself to move past the pain. In fact, you can view your parents' incorrect and unhealthy way of relating to each other as a negative example, a mirror that reflects potential future problems. It serves as a wakeup call and provides guidance for the future. This is your asset, something that many people do not have. In this regard, you are better off than many others, and that is something to be happy about. With this asset, you can make more appropriate and positive changes that will be helpful. Hang in there – you will definitely get better. Wishing you good health, happiness, and joy.

question: I have a very strict set of standards and feel that my mentality is very dark, what should I do?
description: I'm a bit unsociable because I'm a bit arrogant, so I have few friends. I have very strict standards for myself and others, although there are indeed some requirements that I haven't met. But I often can't stand the behavior of some people around me, such as shifting blame, cutting in line, always bothering others, pretending to be weak, telling obvious lies, mocking others, saying things that make people want to kill them, such as "the more mistakes you make, the better", showing superiority in front of the exam-takers, throwing other people's books around, and having extremely bad attitudes, etc. But I restrain myself from showing disgust, so I often feel frustrated by myself. At extreme times, I even hope that others would die. I know this sounds very scary, and I sound very cold-blooded, but sometimes I really do hope that others would die. There are many people around me who have various habits that I find repulsive (but not everyone, and not one person has them all). Although I know that when you feel that everyone around you has a problem and is annoying, it may be you who has a problem and is annoying. Maybe I'm just narrow-minded, but they do have problems indeed. And my desire for others to die is indeed excessive, which makes me very frustrated. I feel like I'm mentally unhealthy. Please help me analyze it, thank you.

answers.answer_text: Hello. I understand your feelings. And most people feel disgusted when they see someone who "doesn't follow the rules," especially when these people's negative behavior encroaches upon and harms their own interests. For example, road rage or when a loved one is hit by a car running a red light. Who wouldn't feel the urge to curse and direct negative energy towards them? Blaming others, cutting in line, constantly bothering others for help, pretending to be weak, telling lies, mocking, ridiculing, and taunting others, being vain, showing off superiority, throwing other people's books away, having an extremely bad attitude, and so on – these are all behaviors that the majority of people don't like. Your mindset is actually quite normal; the problem lies in whether or not you can find the right "balance." There's nothing wrong with wanting to curse someone to death in your mind. Thoughts themselves are not illegal; as long as you like it, you can even make a voodoo doll at home or secretly cast a curse on someone – it's all "magical attacks against the other person" to relieve the hatred in your heart. As long as your actions aren't illegal and don't cause actual physical harm, but rather stay within the boundaries of the law, and your goal is just to make yourself feel better, it's okay. Besides, you're only silently cursing in your heart. Furthermore, if everyone could have a strong sense of justice like you, or if people like you ruled the world, the world might be a little better. The problem is, as you've also noticed, the people around you don't act according to your will, your likes and dislikes. As a result, it often falls solely on you. Looking at it this way, maybe you can teach your heart to set boundaries and throw back to others what doesn't belong to you, what belongs to others, so that your heart can be much more at ease.

question: A 13-year-old boy feels uncomfortable every time someone is kind to him?
description: Always trying to please others, feeling uncomfortable when others are nice to me, can only constantly give and conform. What's going on with this?

answers.answer_text: Because you haven't experienced others being kind to you, or you haven't experienced others' love and kindness towards you. You need to consider your interaction patterns with your parents. It makes you uncomfortable when others are kind to you because you feel unworthy deep down inside. You believe that if you don't do anything, you don't deserve others' love. So, you constantly give and cater to others, thinking that this is what gives you value and makes you worthy of love. In a relationship, accepting and giving are like saving and withdrawing money. You keep depositing in the other person's account but never make any withdrawals, which puts pressure on the other person. Try accepting and appreciating others' kindness towards you, it will make the relationship stronger and the emotional bond deeper. You deserve others' kindness, and your existence has value.

question: My mother has told all my secrets to someone, what should I do in the future? I want to die.
description: My mom suddenly told my aunt about my depression. The secret I have kept for over twenty years is now known to others. I have been bullied and discriminated against by classmates at school. My aunt dislikes me, and I don't like her either. I'm afraid I won't be able to handle her sudden kindness when she knows about my illness. She can't keep her mouth shut and will say anything. Soon, all my relatives around me might know as well. What should I do in the future? How do I face everyone? I want to die. Is it comfortable to just fall asleep? I promised to take care of myself, but it's highly likely that I won't be able to do it.
keywords: Emotions, depressive feelings, anxious feelings, feelings of guilt and shame.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm sorry to hear about what you're going through. Sending you a virtual hug! It must have been difficult for you to keep this secret for over 20 years, and it seems that your mom didn't view it as a secret, which is why she told your aunt. This behavior indeed did not take your feelings into consideration. If we can handle the worst possible outcome of a problem, then there's nothing to be afraid of. Imagine what the worst-case scenario could be in this situation. Maybe the worst-case scenario is that your aunt tells everyone around her, and all your relatives and friends find out. But how would that affect you? Being bullied or discriminated against were only past experiences, and even if your relatives find out, they will likely view it as something in the past and not constantly dwell on it or talk about it. You should know that each of us cares mainly about ourselves. If something doesn't directly concern them, people might briefly talk about it but won't pay constant attention to it. For example, no matter how big a news event is or how sensational it is at the time, it tends to fade away after a few days. They know you have depression, and if they understand depression, they will surely show more concern, which is actually a good thing for you, right? From your description, you're worried that if your aunt finds out about your depression, she will suddenly start treating you nicely, and you won't be able to handle it. Do you dislike being pitied? Being pitied indeed doesn't feel great, but wouldn't it be better than being disliked by your aunt? You promised yourself to treat yourself well, so love yourself and focus on your own matters. Don't worry too much about what others think. Those things are beyond our control, so there's no need to dwell on them. If you have depression, just cooperate with the doctor's treatment, and believe that you can gradually recover. Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-)

Please do not break your promise when you commit to taking care of yourself! It doesn't matter if others find out, everyone is only concerned about their own world. Do you think they will think about your illness and ridicule you every day? You may be overestimating yourself. Just think, if your aunt had depression, would you mock her? Would you think about it every day? Each of us should focus on living our own lives. The past is in the past, let go of the humiliation, the discrimination. Depression is nothing to be ashamed of, it's like having a cold. It just takes advantage of your weaker resistance. Take medication when necessary and exercise to overcome it. Everyone faces psychological issues. Treat them with a normal mindset. Hugs! Mom didn't mean any harm, she has her own struggles, which is why she couldn't help but tell your aunt. So don't blame mom. I don't know why you think your aunt dislikes you, but then you say you're afraid she will suddenly treat you well. If she dislikes you, she won't care about you, right? Relatives are the same, those who truly love you will fully accept you. Those who don't accept you, you don't need to care about them. Many TV shows and novels often have lines from villains like, "If there's a next life, I will make it up to you." When you can say such things, why not cherish this life? Living is much simpler than dying. Breathe, breathe. Look at how grass and trees live. If you're not afraid of death, why fear gossip? In the end, it's still the same plea: please do not break your promise when you commit to taking care of yourself!

Hugs to the little one. It must feel terrible to have our long-held secret exposed by the person we trust the most, especially if Auntie is not someone who can keep a secret. So it's understandable that we are worried and concerned. However, what's done is done, so maybe we can try to adapt and see how we can keep things under control. We can start by talking to Mom and understanding why she revealed our secret so easily to others. If Mom has a valid reason, then maybe we can listen to her thoughts and find a solution together. If Mom simply spoke without considering the consequences, we can gently remind her and make her understand the potential impact this may have on us. I believe Mom wouldn't play with her own child's life like this, so once she realizes the seriousness of the situation, we can discuss with her and suggest that she communicate with Auntie, explaining what can and cannot be said, especially considering the potential harm it may cause to a child with depression. We need to make the other person aware of the consequences, as there might be some things we cannot handle alone. Moreover, we also need to learn to take care of ourselves. Actually, depression is not as scary as we imagine. It seems that the original poster has been doing much better lately and can already face many things independently. It's just that this sudden event caught us off guard, so we need to adjust our mindset. It's not as frightening for others to know, because we can overcome depression. If there are any problems or things we don't understand, we can work together to find a solution. Okay? The world and I love you.

question: 16-year-old student, started having suicidal thoughts three years ago, is this the only way to go on?
description: I don't know what to say. I feel very anxious and sad. I often cry or make crying noises at night. I also need to manage my relationships in the dormitory. I don't want to socialize with them, but I don't want to be ignored either. I have experienced campus violence and cyberbullying. My parents love me very much, but I have a hard time understanding their way of showing love. My dad is not good at expressing himself and says hurtful things when he's angry, telling me to die. My mom always defends me, but she can't understand me. I can't explain my feelings to her. I don't know why I'm anxious, it's just strange. I urgently want to solve it, really want to, but I can't. I don't know where the root of the problem lies, which makes me even more anxious. I want to resolve it on my own, but my parents are holding me back, so I can't jump off. Is this the only way I can go on? Is this all I can do?

answers.answer_text: Hug yourself tightly, my child! I see your efforts, your exploration of yourself, and this world! When facing problems you cannot solve, knowing to seek help from others and refusing to give up on yourself, it is a sense of responsibility towards yourself, your family, and your life. I give you a big thumbs up! You said you feel extremely anxious, that you feel overwhelmed by this emotion and find it hard to calm down, like a trapped animal. This is the image I have in my mind. You are really in a hurry, wanting to find a breakthrough and break free from this situation. I feel so sorry for you! When you read my response, please follow my lead and do the following: find a quiet and undisturbed space, sit down, gently close your eyes, focus on your breath, take a deep breath in and slowly exhale, breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth. After three long breaths, shift your focus to your body, pay attention to any discomfort you may feel and direct your attention to that area. If there are no uncomfortable sensations, scan your body from head to toe, allowing yourself to slow down and become still. You can also utilize some meditation techniques to help you relax. Take care of your body and try to slow down the rhythm of your life. If there is any progress, reward yourself with a small treat. If you feel you still cannot communicate well with your parents, you can seek help from a school counselor. Nowadays, every school has dedicated counselors for consultation, and face-to-face counseling should be more effective. You are a responsible and diligent child, believe in yourself. This is just a minor episode in life, there are more wonderful things awaiting you to discover!

question: Attempted Graduate School Exam three times, all ended in failure, each time falling just short. How can I fully accept it?
description: The questioner is 24 years old. In the final year of college, they took the postgraduate entrance exam but failed the interview. They then found an internship but came up short by two points. They were unable to transfer because of the minimum required score. In early May, they started looking for a job, but it didn't go well. After working for a few months, they resigned and went home to prepare for a third attempt at the postgraduate entrance exam and also took the national civil service exam. However, they missed the mark for the civil service exam by one spot and missed the postgraduate entrance exam by one point. Although they know they have to look forward, they can't seem to get over this hurdle. Whenever someone mentions taking the postgraduate entrance exam or hears that people around them are going to graduate school, they feel very sad. They feel like it's a lifelong regret and that their life feels incomplete, especially when it's difficult to find a job and most of their classmates and friends are going to graduate school. They feel like they've completely lost their confidence, self-discipline, and dislike themselves. They feel lost and aimless. They also hope to face life with optimism and positivity, but nothing seems to make them happy. The feeling of failure for not getting into graduate school for three years and the financial and job issues constantly weigh on their heart. However, the more depressed they are, the lower their efficiency in studying and doing things, creating a vicious cycle. Although they know that even if they get into graduate school, it doesn't guarantee a great future, they still can't let it go. But due to age, financial, and other practical factors, they must give up. How can they completely accept the fact that they can't pursue a postgraduate education?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, the choices we make in life always come with opportunities. What is lost will inevitably return in other forms. Accept what cannot be changed and focus on what you can accomplish at the present moment. I sympathize with you deeply. From your description, I can feel your pain and dilemma. On one hand, you have failed to pass the postgraduate entrance exams three times, which has left you feeling extremely defeated. This sense of defeat has also extended to your work, life, and personal value. On the other hand, due to your age and financial factors, you have decided to give up on further studying, but you feel a deep sense of regret and unwillingness in your heart. Reflect seriously on your inner thoughts. Even if you find a suitable job, will you be able to let go of your regrets regarding the exams? Perhaps, whether you pass or fail is no longer that important to you. What matters more is that it has become a symbol that constantly reminds you of your pain and defeat. Maybe only by truly conquering it can you let go. After careful thought, you can communicate with your family and see if you have one more chance to give it your all and make a final effort. Furthermore, many times what may seem like a narrow margin is actually a wide gap, requiring you to exert even more effort, not letting up or entertaining any thoughts of luck, but embracing a determined and persevering attitude of victory. There are many paths ahead of you, and what you are currently seeing may not be all that there is. Regardless of the path, as long as you put your heart and effort into it, it will become wider and wider. Learning to accept regret may be a sign of growth. If you are unable to attempt the postgraduate entrance exams again, you may need to find a different path. Long-term studying for exams can change your mindset and energy level, not to mention the financial and work pressures you have. If succeeding on the exams is your ideal, then you have already done everything you can to achieve it and put in all your effort and hard work. That is enough. Even if you don't achieve good results, it does not diminish the sweat and time you have put in. Not passing the exams does not make others laugh at or look down on you; it is your own self-depreciation and comparing yourself to others. Those who succeeded on their first attempt may seem to be doing better, but in your ongoing journey, you have also honed your patience and perseverance. This is also a kind of achievement. I truly admire your spirit of refusing to admit defeat. If you can approach finding a good job and creating your own life with the same patience and good preparation as you did for the exams, there is absolutely no problem. The road has its ups and downs; there will be upslopes and downslopes. Let go of the burden of the exams and bravely step onto a new path. Best wishes.

question: How to maintain motivation when staying at home and being unemployed for nearly a year, with constant emotional ups and downs?
description: I have been unemployed for almost a year at home, and my mood has been fluctuating, mostly low. Especially when I am with my parents, I don't have to do many things because they take care of me. However, they often criticize me with their words, which sometimes puts me in a bad mood. Now I have the idea of ​​confronting them. The more they don't want me to do something, the more I want to do it. I am becoming more and more disgusted with my own state. I have no motivation for anything, occasionally there will be some motivation, but it quickly disappears due to procrastination. How can I maintain motivation for life?
keywords: Emotion, expressing emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: I understand from the OP's description that they are unemployed at home and feeling down. Their parents take care of their daily life, but they often criticize them with words, which sometimes leads to a bad mood. Now OP has a thought of confronting them. The more they don't want me to do something, the more they want to do it. They have also become more and more disgusted with their own state. Now they have no motivation for anything. I can understand the OP's low emotions and rebellious psychology towards their parents, but objectively speaking, the current state of the OP, although it makes them feel miserable, is not caused by the family, but by themselves. I think your parents may say some critical words, but deep down, they love you the most. Their criticism may be their high expectations for you, hoping that you can have your own career, but now you can only stay at home unemployed. They are just venting, but they still love you in their hearts. Try to think from their perspective. If you were the father, working hard for your child for twenty years, what kind of person would you like your child to be? Even if you don't expect them to achieve great success, at least you hope they have a stable job！But even so, you still love your child. When they are hungry, you feel heartbroken; when they are sad, you feel sad too, but you might say some hurtful words to provoke them. This is a psychological reaction that every parent may experience. I believe you are not a person who is content with relying on your parents. It may be due to the pandemic that you haven't found a job temporarily. Focus your emotions and energy on finding a job, concentrate your efforts, and I think maybe you won't resist your parents so much.

question: What do people live for, family, friendship, love, or just material possessions?
description: I don't know where the meaning of life lies for myself. Is it family, friendship, love, or just material possessions?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner~ Seeing words is like seeing a face. First of all, I'm curious about your age and how much life experience you've had before starting to think about this question. Almost everyone will face this important question in life: what is the purpose of living? Different age groups have different motivations for thinking about this question. I have also deeply pondered this question, and the conclusion I reached is quite simple: there is no conclusion. Because I can never find an answer to verify the meaning of my life, in other words, life itself has no meaning, and living is not necessarily for anything. This kind of thinking may seem negative, but in reality, it is a good way of self-regulation, because without meaning, I can assign any meaning I want to everything. We are used to finding a goal or meaning to validate the significance of our actions, because this makes us feel that everything is worthwhile. However, not everything can be assigned meaning, such as the existential dilemma in life. Everyone is born and grows up according to certain rules, goes to school at a certain age, works, gets married, has children, and all of this seems very natural. No one tells us that we should do it this way, but everyone does it, so naturally, we do it too. What are we doing this for? Is it for something we will eventually obtain? What each person wants at different stages of life varies, and different age groups have different needs. Most people are not easily satisfied because desires are endless. Therefore, attributing the meaning of life to some ultimate material thing is unrealistic. The so-called family affection, love, and friendship are not the meaning of our existence either. Yu Hua once said, "Being alive in itself has no meaning, being alive is being alive itself." I don't know if you can understand, but being alive, this state, this real and present feeling, experiencing various ups and downs, is all brought about by being alive. It's quite magical. Even though it can be bitter at times, it can also be sweet. The underlying color of life is too heavy, and we are not qualified to define it, but each person's life, we are entitled to give it different meanings. And each experience will bring us different answers. Moving forward, pausing sometimes and contemplating the meaning of life, this is life. So, questioner, don't be too perplexed. Just walk each step earnestly, and some answers will come naturally. Best wishes.

Hello, it is worth discussing the question you raised. Thank you for asking~ This question has countless answers. Some people live to chase their dreams, some for social status, and some for money. It depends on what individuals want to pursue throughout their lives. The concept of "meaning of life" itself has various interpretations and can be different for each person. However, one crucial thing, in my opinion, is to live for the sake of being alive, to enjoy the impact and emotions brought by happiness and sadness in the limited time we have. Bi Shumin once replied to a student, saying, "Life itself doesn't have much meaning, but you can give it meaning." When we enter this world, we are destined to experience many things, such as the family, friendship, and love you mentioned, which can bring beautiful sparks into our lives. When do we usually contemplate this question? Most often during moments of confusion, when we can't find our self-worth or when we have negative emotions towards the world. We can set this question aside and choose to live in the present, to realize our self-worth and strive for better goals in life. Encounter different versions of yourself and embrace the impact and confusion that this world brings to you. Lastly, I would like to share a quote I really like from the philosopher Max Weber: "Man is an animal suspended in webs of significance he himself has spun." Best wishes!

The host raised a question of profound philosophical significance, a question that has been pondered and sought by human beings throughout history, yet without a definitive answer. Because the answer itself may require us to experience and find it on our own. As I am the unique individual in the world, there is no second me. Therefore, the answer to how I should live lies in my own search, which is the mission of our lives. In the deepest sense, our purpose is to live as ourselves and take responsibility for ourselves. As Sartre said, we are the authors of ourselves. Through choices, actions, and even inaction, we design ourselves. Be true to yourself, live your own life, and have the courage to embark on the journey. Not for the sake of family, friendship, love, or material possessions, but for yourself. I hope this message is helpful to you. Good luck.

Hello, asker. What is the meaning of life? This is a grand proposition that has puzzled philosophers for centuries. The three fundamental questions of philosophy - Who am I? Where do I come from? Where am I going? - have troubled many people. In simple terms, what is the meaning of life? Some may attribute it to friendships, family, or material possessions. Everyone has their own perspective, but the meaning of life is actually how you perceive your own existence. What do you think your life is? What is the meaning of your own life? It is not defined by others; everyone has a different meaning to their life. We can especially feel this difference when watching war films. For example, when I watched "The Eight Hundred," some people chose to escape, believing that the meaning of their life was to marry someone, have children, and live a peaceful and happy life. On the other hand, some people chose to strap themselves with grenades and bravely jump into battle. Their meaning of life lay in their willingness to sacrifice their lives to defend their country, putting their own families after their nation. Some people transformed from being meek to bravely holding up a flag, and their meaning of life changed. In fact, everyone is the same. At a certain time, in a certain place, at a turning point, you will discover what you truly desire. From then on, you will know the meaning of the first half of your life and what you want to pursue in the second half. Perhaps, in our final moments, when we reflect on our life, we still do not know what our life was truly for. Maybe we lived an ordinary life, perhaps it was uneventful. However, the meaning of life lies in these few short decades that we personally construct. It cannot be accurately defined; it is our experiences.

Hello! In the face of death, meaning may seem insignificant as it can vanish instantly like a bubble. However, you can also see its vibrant colors and give it significance. Owen Yang once said that relationships in this very moment are the key, and the true meaning lies in the moments you spend with the people you cherish. When you look back on your life so far, the actions you have taken, the memories you have left behind, and the hopes for the future are all meaningful. Perhaps the meaning of life lies in simply being alive. Being alive brings countless possibilities. The experience of being alive is precious. However, why do you seek meaning? The reasons behind why you ask this question may be more important than the question itself.

All the problems in life come from interpersonal relationships, including family, friendship, and love. The reason the questioner is exploring the meaning of life is probably because they are troubled by interpersonal relationships, leading to a low mood. The questioner said that they don't know where the meaning of life lies for themselves. Life is long, so let's explore it together. I have found two points. First, the reason we don't know where the meaning of life lies for ourselves is that the emergence of meaning requires us to do something that benefits others in advance. You should make efforts in the areas where you want to expand your life. Then you will naturally give yourself a satisfying meaning. If you don't know where the meaning of life lies for yourself, it's probably because you haven't done that thing yet or haven't reached a satisfactory state. Just start or persist, this is the first point. The second point is that it's normal for people to occasionally feel lost, procrastinate, and have low moods. Everyone will have these moments, so we should accept our own situations appropriately. Because we tend to compare our ideal self with our real self and always feel that our real self is not good enough or that we haven't used our time well. But remember, humans are not machines, and our willpower is not entirely subjective. Occasional relaxation is normal and is an objective limitation of willpower. So we should accept it and then implement the first point.

Hello, the reason why people live has always been an eternal topic, just as you mentioned, living for emotional fulfillment or for material satisfaction are both partial answers to this question. Why we live does not have a fixed answer. When people come into this world, they do not have a specific purpose. Sartre said that the existence of everything in the world is accidental. In other words, without any reason, human beings and the world exist as they are. When we consider this question, we might think about what we truly need deep inside, that is, "why should we live, and how can we live more meaningfully?" I believe that we should live for happiness. Throughout our lives, we are constantly pursuing happiness, pursuing a better life, from personal happiness to the happiness of our families, countries, and all of humanity. Our pursuit of happiness is the source and motivation of our existence. At the beginning, human nature is inherently good. Deep inside all of us, there is goodness and through the continuous pursuit of happiness, we can enrich our own lives and understand the meaning and value of life better. Living is about pursuing and enjoying happiness. Continuously progressing towards a better emotional and material life is one of the answers as to why we live. In the process of enriching ourselves, we will naturally find the true meaning of life for ourselves. I hope my answer can be helpful to you!

Hi there! I understand that you may be having conflicts with your family and friends, or facing challenges in your studies or career, feeling lost and seeking help but feeling isolated. I empathize with you. For each of us, love, friendship, and family are crucial. However, we must also realize that each person is an independent individual and lives for themselves. Family and friends are just additions to our lives. Having them may bring us happiness but can also exhaust us, but it doesn't mean we can't live for ourselves. It is now 11:38, let's imagine that you only have a little over 11 hours left in your life. What would be your most desired thing to do? Hug your family, reconcile with a friend, express your love to someone, or work hard for your dreams? Ask your heart, and perhaps you can discover the desires you urgently and passionately seek but haven't realized yet. If you find them, then go for it! If you haven't found your dreams and desires, think about what in your life is worth living for. For example, even when I feel isolated, thinking about delicious food that makes my life worth living until tomorrow motivates me to keep striving. Even if you still haven't found a reason worth living for, you should know that in the hearts of strangers, there is care and love for you. Even if you lose everything, each and every one of us will do our best to help and love you. We must live our lives for this world. Perhaps the current situation is not ideal, but don't forget the expectations the world has for you. Lastly, I would like to share a quote I really like: "May you remember your worth and resist malicious intent when you're being struck down. May you believe in your worth and love what you love, do what you do, follow your heart, no matter the cost." Keep going!

Hmm~ friend, when I saw your question, it reminded me of my past. I used to always ask about the purpose of life and engage in discussions about dreams and the meaning of life with others. Actually, what I want to tell you is that the meaning of life is simply to live well. You say you don't know why people exist, but I want to tell you that people exist to live well and find happiness for themselves. Why bother pondering so much about why? If you really think about it, isn't this the truth? Maybe you want to say it's for your parents, loved ones, or children. But in reality, these individuals want to see you happy more than anything else. They can't bear to see you burdened by existential thoughts because of them. Your happiness is their happiness, so relax and live a good life, pursuing your own dreams. That's how you fulfill your own life's value. Of course, when faced with your own choices, there may be times when your family doesn't understand. This requires good communication to find a balance or understanding of what you love and strive for. Don't have regrets, achieve success, and convince your family. In the end, I hope you live a happy life!

question: Every night I suffer from insomnia and I don't know what the future will be like. I feel scared.
description: After graduating and entering the workplace, I have always been doing repetitive work, thinking that I was very capable. Then I would change jobs and end up unemployed. Now I have been unemployed for over 4 months, and I have started to fear the workplace. However, I have to face the workplace because of life and the need to earn money. But because I can't find a job, I am restless and anxious.
keywords: Career, career selection skills, work pressure, work fatigue.

answers.answer_text: Hug the OP~ OP, you are not alone. I still feel terrible when I think back to the anxiety during my job search. Constantly experiencing rejection and being denied is really distressing. But if we look at it from a different perspective, maybe it's because we put in so much effort to obtain something that we will cherish job opportunities even more in the future, right? Regarding your current situation, I think we can make efforts in the following aspects: identifying our strengths. Most of us do repetitive work, so we can dig deeper into the strengths we demonstrate in our jobs. For example, are we conscientious and responsible at work? Do we step up during critical moments? Are we good at cooperation and have strong teamwork skills? Do we adapt well to new environments and find it easy to handle any job? And so on. Then we can think about examples that prove these abilities. When writing resumes and going for interviews, we can emphasize these aspects and highlight our strengths. Mobilize our friends. You can ask your friends if their companies have any job openings and if they can help you with referrals. Sometimes, when we go for interviews directly, HR may have more requirements, but if we have a reliable person who can help with referrals, it will be easier to secure a job. Boost our spirits and approach job searching with the best attitude. I remember when I was job searching, I would have interviews during the day and cry at night, but the next day, I would gather myself and go for another interview. I was exhausted during that period, and finding a job was particularly difficult. Then my friend told me that if she were an HR, she wouldn't hire me with such lack of confidence. After that, I adjusted myself for a while. During that time, I analyzed my own characteristics and motivated myself a lot. Later, I felt ready and started searching for jobs again. This time, I successfully found a job. I think we must believe in ourselves, no matter how many setbacks we encounter. We should believe that it's just that this job and I are not a perfect match, and it doesn't mean that I am not capable enough. If we feel exhausted, it might be helpful to take a break and relax, and then continue the job search with a refreshed spirit. OP, let's keep going~ The job is waiting for you in front. Let's boost our spirits, let go of worries and anxieties, and believe that we can do it!

Loulou, it's nice to meet you! Hugs to you! I can feel your helplessness and confusion about the future through your words. You don't like the monotonous life you have now, and you don't want your life to be ordinary. This is understandable, hugs to you! I think there may be a few reasons why you have these thoughts. The disparity between ideals and reality: You mentioned in your writing that you "thought you were great," which shows that when you entered the workplace, you were full of confidence and believed that you could make a career for yourself. However, when you actually started working, you realized that the reality of the workplace was different from what you had imagined, creating a disparity. Other people's shining lives: Whether it's the influencers in videos or the people around you, they may make you feel like, why are they so excellent while I'm just ordinary? Other people's accomplishments seem to highlight your own lack of excellence. I think this is a problem that probably exists all the time because everyone wants to present their best side to others, just like when writing a resume. No one will write a bad resume about themselves, so maybe you need to look at this from a neutral perspective. Life limitations: Your current biggest source of confusion may be the inability to find a suitable job. Four months of unemployment has made you increasingly fearful and directionless about the future. Based on these reasons, I have a few suggestions that I hope will be helpful to you. Take it slow to go faster: Regarding these disparities, it's important for you to approach them with a calm mindset. The workplace is a completely new place for you, so it's normal to feel anxious or lost. However, I believe that being impatient won't solve the problem, and it may even make the situation worse as you get caught up in overthinking. So my suggestion is to take things slow first, and once you find a direction that suits you, you can speed up. Let's not be impatient, okay? Career planning or changing direction: You are already feeling confused about the current workplace, and I think one of the reasons for this confusion may be that you lack a detailed career plan or direction. Planning is undoubtedly a good thing for us, and career planning, in particular, can give us purpose and direction. As for how to create a career plan, you can make full use of the internet and watch relevant videos or read related books. I highly recommend the YouTuber "Xiaosu" - she has a video specifically about career planning that is very comprehensive, and she even shares her own career plan. I hope you can check it out. Get moving: When I was studying, I often had trouble sleeping, and my teacher told me, "That's because you're not moving enough." I think it makes sense - during the day, I either daydream or rest, without fully utilizing my time, so naturally, I'm not tired enough to sleep. So I suggest you do some exercise, which not only helps relieve stress but also gradually improves your mood. Additionally, meditation is also a good option! Finally, I hope everything goes well for you and that you can find your direction! Keep up the good work!

Actually, your question is very common for the unemployed population. The reason why we change jobs is because we are confident that even if we change jobs, we can find a better one. But when we face frustration in job hunting, our confidence takes a hit. This blow makes us doubt ourselves, and once we start doubting ourselves, we become fearful of the unknown. We fear the unknown for our future, for the unknown of the workplace, and for the unknown of development in this current era. Moreover, this fear gradually erodes our confidence over time, and as our confidence is eroded, the fear only grows stronger. We begin to doubt whether we can keep up with progress in the era and worry about being left behind. This is a problem and fear that every unemployed person has to face. It is a terrifying vicious cycle, and if one continuously immerses oneself in this fear, they will find themselves becoming depressed and anxious. These emotions will only grow stronger, and eventually, they may even fear going for job interviews, to the point where they are unable to attend interviews at all. However, it is easy to imagine that the results of an interview for a person in a confident state versus a person filled with fear would be quite different. If you were the interviewer, which one would you choose? Thus, this leads to another negative cycle. If one continues to be trapped in this vicious cycle, in the end, they will slowly wear themselves down. Therefore, we need to learn how to break this cycle. The best way to break this cycle is to make progress, to focus on self-improvement. If you truly fear, you can set a learning goal for yourself - to continuously progress during this unemployment process. Do not fear unemployment, and do not see unemployment as the low point of your life. You should consider your career as a hidden period of your life. In the process of learning, the most important thing is not to focus on the speed of your progress, but on the progress itself. If we focus on the speed of our learning progress, we often fall into a wrong mindset - we set ourselves a high goal, set a fast learning pace or requirement, and therefore always feel that our progress is too slow, which easily brings us down. This can make us dislike studying and detest learning, once again falling into a negative cycle. However, if we focus on progress itself, we will constantly have a sense of accomplishment. It will make us passionate and motivated to continue learning. When we focus on progress itself, we will have passion and motivation to study, which will make our learning speed faster and our progress greater. It will further stimulate our sense of accomplishment, creating a positive cycle. This will help us build confidence. This is a technique that I personally find very useful. I hope it can help you recover quickly, find a job, and become happier.

Hug the subject, every newcomer in the workplace is prone to encounter such psychological and situational challenges. After all, being young, it's difficult to accept the repetition of tasks day after day. Then, changing jobs one after another, but any profession is built on work experience. Only through accumulation can you have the opportunity for promotion and have the power to make your own choices. Throughout history, many successful individuals or craftsmen of great nations have achieved their success through the simple yet difficult secret of "repetition and accumulation." I suggest that the subject adjusts their mindset and faces their career with a calm attitude. ▲ If you don't easily abandon your career, then your career won't abandon you. Many employers are hiring, but with so many talented individuals available, do you think they choose the person with the highest education or the most outstanding abilities? No, they select someone who can focus on their work and contribute to the company's benefits. ▲ The greatest mistake for newcomers in the workplace is to "shun the tools" and have "high expectations but low abilities". No matter the field, you won't know what kind of work suits you until you try it; without a certain level of experience, why would others trust you with the highest position? Put yourself in the boss's shoes, would you dare to let a novice in the workplace directly take on the role of CEO? Finally, I hope my answer can help the subject, thank you!

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. When just graduating and entering the workplace, many people have this experience. They may feel very capable and think that they can handle anything they don't like. However, after several job searches and actual work, they realize that it's not as easy as they imagined. At this time, they may feel panic, confused, and even start doubting themselves. How can we deal with this situation? First, we need to calm down and think about what we really want. What kind of person do we want to become? What are our ideals? How achievable are they? Second, we need to assess what skills and abilities we need for our goals. What do we need to do? Third, we need to evaluate the skills and abilities we currently possess. What can we do right now? Fourth, how can we bridge the gap between our current state and what we need? What can we do before reaching our goals? How can we assess our abilities? We can use assessments such as the Four Quadrants of Competence, Holland's vocational interests assessment, and the Edwards Personal Preferences Schedule.

Hello, OP. Everyone faces different pressures when it comes to work, so you don't need to feel that you are different from others or burden yourself too much. Regarding your question, I have some thoughts to share with you: Most jobs have repetitive tasks. If we always look at things in chunks of time, we will feel that both our life and work/study are repetitive. In this case, we need to shorten our focus and see the changes in them, treating these changes as new challenges every day. In today's highly competitive society, many people are waiting for a job, which brings along stress related to competition. If you can't find a job immediately, don't panic. Take it slow. It will work out eventually. Work life can sometimes be resistant because we often face pressures related to work content and beyond. However, we need to remember that whether it's work or study, they both belong to life. We shouldn't entirely focus on work, as it will affect our mood and quality of life. If our life is not good, we will start to dislike our work. Maintaining a positive mindset is crucial. In life, we will always face some difficulties. Being anxious will only have negative effects on problem-solving. It might help to go out and explore the outside world. When you see how big the world is, you will realize how small your current difficulties are. Relax, stay calm, and solutions will come. Keep going! I hope you find a comfortable way of living and overcome your current difficulties as soon as possible. Grateful to meet you!

Hello, having a humble attitude is very important in the workplace. "After graduating and entering the workforce, I always found myself doing repetitive work, thinking that I was very capable, then changing jobs, and eventually becoming unemployed." After graduation, it is easily for us to approach work and the challenges in the workplace with a student mindset. As you mentioned, we often find ourselves doing repetitive tasks and after a while, we become proficient at them, creating a sense that we are really good and that the work is not difficult. "Instead, view work from a developmental perspective and create a career plan." When you find yourself constantly doing repetitive tasks, take a step back and ask yourself why you are doing those tasks and how you can progress within your current position. Observe how more experienced colleagues handle their work. "I have been unemployed for over four months now and I've realized that I am afraid of returning to the workplace. However, I need to face it because I have to make a living, but not being able to find a job is making me anxious." The reason for your fear of the workplace is largely due to the impact of long-term unemployment and the inability to find a job, causing a significant gap between reality and your ideal expectations, leading to a loss of confidence. What you need to do now is to reassess your career direction. There is fierce competition for jobs at the moment, with many highly talented individuals. What you can do is focus on enhancing your own skills and making yourself valuable. Make the most of this period of unemployment by improving your skills, adjusting your mindset, and avoiding impatience for immediate success. Good luck.

Thank you for the invitation and trust, OP! I see your confusion and feel your desire to find a suitable job, to take responsibility for yourself, and to realize your own value. Insomnia is caused by unresolved problems during the day. When your brain senses your stress and a strong desire, it becomes overly excited or nervous, preventing you from entering a relaxed state. Unemployment impacts one's sense of security and self-worth. On the surface, it may seem like a fear of the workplace, but it could be that you are avoiding the feeling of not being recognized for being good enough. Therefore, what hinders you is not external, but whether you have the courage to break through yourself. It's not that you can't find a job, but rather that you want to prove yourself in a certain profession too much. Suggestions: First, clarify your goals. What do you want? If you want to prove yourself, be prepared to accept the pain and helplessness that comes with it. If you need income, earnestly search for a job that matches your abilities, solve your survival problems first, and then aim to improve your skills. Second, increase exercise and physical fitness to activate and enhance your inner strength. Third, consider seeking professional psychological counseling to support your adjustment when necessary. Best wishes to you!

I can understand how the original poster feels. Insomnia is caused by anxiety, and the pressures of life make me eager for income. However, the future seems uncertain, and it is difficult to find a job, so I often worry and lose sleep at night. Realizing the reality of work and accepting it, many people have dreams about work when they first graduate, but the actual work in real life is repetitive and mundane. No matter how creative or interesting a job may seem, when you actually invest time in it, especially after becoming skilled, it ultimately becomes mundane. Work and career can be separate. Think carefully about what work is really for? Mainly to find a stable income. Work is only a part of life, lower your expectations of work and try to develop your own interests. In fact, work and career can be separate. Work pursues stability. You may as well lower your expectations of work, accept this simplicity, and at the same time look for something you can really do and work hard to develop it. Why not ask yourself, what else do you want to do besides work? After all, work is not the only thing, it's just for making money, there's no need to have too high expectations. Work hard to further your education, constantly learn and strive for better income. If you can't find a job for a while, continue to strengthen your studies, try taking more exams, and have more interviews. After all, just graduated and still relatively young, there are still many opportunities waiting for you. Make the most of your youth, seize various opportunities. Having a stable job will make life easier. Instead of thinking too much, take action. Many times, effort is not something that comes from thinking, but from continuous action and practice. Thinking too much will only increase worries. The best way to stop thinking is to take decisive action. When you actually take action, you will find that you focus on something and reduce the anxiety caused by unnecessary imagination.

question: Middle school student, often sees unclean things at night, what should I do?
description: Mood will inexplicably become low, will see those terrifying things, will have insomnia.

answers.answer_text: I have also had similar experiences, although I didn't have trouble sleeping. High school life can be very stressful. Being overwhelmed by all the studying and daily tasks, I rarely get the chance to lose myself in my own thoughts or daydream. Time gradually passes by. My suggestion is, if you don't have any free time, that's actually better. Being busy can help distract you from a lot of things. If you're not busy, you may feel empty, bored, helpless and lost. If you do have free time, I recommend reading some motivational books or watching inspirational TV shows. Hang in there, little brother.

question: How to change the emotions from playing games and bring them into real life?
description: Recently, I have been playing a game that I just learned, but I am not very good at it. However, the people in the game would insult me, calling me things like stupid and saying I don't know anything. There were even worse things they said. After that, I was too scared to continue playing. Later on, I started feeling uncomfortable about it and I realized that I am not the person they described me as. So, I tried playing a few more times, but I still couldn't win. I feel frustrated but I can't express it. As a result, whenever something doesn't go my way, I randomly get angry and end up hurting my friends unnecessarily. What should I do? If I continue like this, I might lose my friends. I know this is wrong, but I can't control myself. I get angry over trivial things and it's not even a big deal, but I still feel very angry. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: In games, there will always be people seeking a sense of existence. They elevate themselves by belittling others. Therefore, when facing insults from others, we need to have a dialectical perspective. First, we can ask ourselves why we play games. If it's to win, there are many ways to achieve that, such as relying on teammates or spending money, or learning gaming skills or even hiring someone to play for you. If it's for enjoyment, then we can ignore the criticisms from others or confront them directly. After all, games are meant to be played for fun. If we are not happy in the end, it's better to find another form of entertainment. Secondly, let's think about why we get angry. Is it because we are not satisfied with our gaming abilities, so we keep playing hoping to improve, but in the end, we are not as good as we imagined, or even get criticized by teammates, leading to a burst in our mentality. In fact, games require practice sometimes, especially those with strong operational elements. Each character's skills and their combination require certain techniques. If we really want to improve, we can learn from other skilled players, use our brains more during the game, instead of mindlessly rushing in. Lastly, we need to learn how to regulate our emotions because no one can always win. So when we lose, we shouldn't be too discouraged. After all, we can't blame ourselves for everything. Sometimes, we can blame others. If I'm bad, I'm just bad, but I'm happy. If you think you're good, come and carry me. If you can't, then don't talk nonsense. After all, we play games not for the sake of winning, but for the sake of enjoying ourselves. The world loves you and me.

question: 13 years old, why do I always cry uncontrollably at night in the past two years?
description: Previously my sleep was good and I was happy every day, but for the past two years, I don't know why I feel particularly uncomfortable at night and not very happy during the day. It's very distressing, very distressing.

answers.answer_text:
Hello, OP! After reading your description, I have gained some understanding of the question you want to ask. Therefore, I'm sending you a virtual hug. From your description, I can gather that you are 13 years old and have been feeling emotionally down for the past two years, often crying at night without knowing the reason for your distress. Additionally, your sleep quality is also poor, leading to a series of unfortunate events. In light of this, I extend a warm hug to you. In your description, you mentioned that you were happy and had good sleep before the age of 11, but after turning 11, you started feeling emotionally down and experiencing poor sleep. I think this may be related to stress. Before the age of 11, there is minimal stress or worries, and doing well in school is all that mattered, with lax expectations from parents. However, after turning 11, the pressure of academics increases significantly as the number of subjects grows and managing interpersonal relationships becomes more complex. Therefore, experiencing increased stress during this period is quite normal. To help alleviate your current situation, I have summarized some methods:
(1) Try to identify the causes of your emotional distress, both external and internal, to address the problem at its root.
(2) Communicate with loved ones (i.e., actively confide in them), whether it is your parents or friends, and share the thoughts that have been weighing on your mind, further releasing your emotions.
(3) Learn to release stress in a healthy way, such as through exercise or listening to music.
(4) When you're feeling down, you can try journaling to record your emotions and gradually analyze the reasons behind your emotional distress.
(5) When your mood is low, learn to proactively regulate it by distracting yourself, such as reading books, watching shows, or playing games for entertainment. The world and I care about you. Take care!

question: When emotions arise, tell yourself to accept them, but how can you truly achieve self-acceptance?
description: Every time emotions come, I always tell myself to accept them first, but I don't know what true acceptance really means.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ It's a great idea to tell yourself to accept the presence of emotions when they arise. For example, when we face a high-pressure world, we may feel a lot of stress and anxiety. Sometimes, we may tend to suppress these emotions, fearing that they will affect our individual behavior. However, the more we try to suppress them, the more anxious we become. So, acceptance plays a significant role at this time. We need to allow the existence of negative emotions, as it can help us resolve them better. The first step of acceptance is to face them directly, allowing them to exist objectively without overly judging them. After accepting the presence of these emotions, try to relieve them based on your own thoughts. Consider how you would like to release these emotions or even how they can bring positive effects to yourself. Wishing you well~.

question: Is the cage too small? Is this an act of cat abuse?
description: Alas, the cause of this issue was because of a cat, a common stray cat we used to see in our childhood. We also had one at home, but two months ago it got infested with fleas, which burdened our family greatly. Everyone in the family got bitten, including my pregnant sister-in-law. We all felt that this couldn't go on, so my brother decided to get rid of the cat. However, my mom stopped him and kept the cat in a small cage. That cage was really, really small, just like those used for transporting cats. The cat couldn't move its body properly, only hunching or lying down. It has been two months like this, and amazingly, the cat gave birth. I suspect that maybe the cage was accidentally opened before and it ran out to meet other cats, causing this situation. It gave birth to two kittens. Initially, this should have been a happy event, but when I think about how small the cage is, it's simply impossible for the three cats to live in there. Even feeding the kittens is a problem. I suggested changing the cage, but my mom strongly objected. She thinks the small cage is convenient to manage. But I believe it's cruel to the cats. So, I ordered a new, larger cage on Taobao and now I fear that a family conflict will soon erupt... What should I do?
keywords: Family, parent-child communication, and communication among children.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. If a house is too small, humans will feel cramped, and animals may feel the same way. Whether it amounts to animal cruelty or not, only the animal itself would know. From your description, it can be seen that you are quite concerned about this cat, and there is nothing wrong with your family's actions. Maybe for them, the cat is considered livestock rather than a pet. Different attitudes towards treatment can be understood. If your mother is responsible for cleaning the cage or feeding the cat, her perspective may be what you need to convince. If you can take care of the large cage and properly look after the cat, giving them baths and cleaning up after them, so that they don't cause trouble for your family, then maybe everyone will have no objections. But if no one takes responsibility for the cat, it will likely fall on your mother's shoulders, and it's understandable that she may still consider them livestock and not take care of them as carefully or thoughtfully. If you don't want to raise the kittens, you can give them to a friend or a pet center to reduce the minor troubles they bring and provide them with a better home. Don't worry or feel guilty. You can discuss with your family and at least get them to agree to put the cat in a large cage, so that the cat can live more comfortably and not feel wronged. It may also become more obedient and cause less trouble. The cat may feel uncomfortable in a small house, but if you gradually put them in a large cage, they will adapt. Going from frugality to luxury, they probably won't "hold a grudge," right? Best wishes.

question: 19-year-old male, why has he been suppressing himself since he turned 18?
description: During my middle school years, like many others my age, I went through a rebellious phase in adolescence, spreading negative emotions to those close to me and expressing my emotions online. At that time, I rarely reflected on myself, nor did I often communicate my true feelings and thoughts with others. As I grew older, I learned some things along the way and gradually learned to control my outward emotions. Most of the time, I am polite to others. However, I don't believe that this is true personal growth of the mind. Because at the same time, my inner self became extremely sensitive, often transmitting negative emotions to myself due to external factors. In other words, I started attacking and suppressing myself, feeling unworthy of better things and without the right to pursue what I want. This self-repression and even inferiority may be a result of excessive self-contemplation, bringing about feelings of anxiety and fear. I tend to feel constrained in many things and wonder what is holding me back. Although I have seen glimpses of myself in movies, books, and many other media, I am still hesitant to confidently express my feelings in the real world, such as my likes, dislikes, inner thoughts, and opinions about others.
keywords: Growth, perfecting one's personality, self-development, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: Hello, starting from venting externally and then turning inward to seek answers, this is the beginning of personal growth. Although the answers obtained are all self-judgment and only part of the trial-and-error process before finding the correct answer, allow yourself to experience the growth process. Everyone seeks self-exploration, self-understanding, and self-discovery throughout their lifetime. The feelings of oppression and judgment you see within yourself are often influenced by the family environment. The occurrence of rebelliousness can be seen as a resistance to the ideas imposed on you in the past, and also as a way to prove your own strength. Inner uncertainties stem from oneself, and after the rebellious phase, these uncertainties turn into compromises, allowing oneself to indulge in them. First of all, understand that uncertainties about oneself exist in everyone. It's just that the causes of these uncertainties differ. Physical appearance, family, wealth, relationships, dreams, and many other aspects trouble everyone to some extent, leading to different life experiences. So, in which aspect do your own uncertainties lie? Is it about courage or self-trust? Take notice of that. Knowing where the problem lies allows you to know what you want, and then what can you do to achieve what you want? Will you continue to compromise and indulge, or will you take a brave step forward? This requires your decision. In relationships, there are boundaries between people. While allowing the expression of one's feelings, one should not harm others. This is the basic bottom line. You can share with those you like and distance yourself from those you dislike or can't stand. Doing things you enjoy is the most comfortable way to express yourself. When your mind is filled with various random thoughts, consciously detach yourself, go outside for a walk, and exercise regularly as it will reduce internal noise. Doing things you enjoy is the best way to boost your energy because it brings a sense of conviction, which gradually becomes the norm and naturally leads to a sense of control and greater self-confidence.

Hello. I'm glad to have the opportunity to answer your question. Based on your situation, I would define your psychological state as ruminative thinking, which is simply excessive contemplation. As we grow older and experience more, our psychology also matures, transitioning from being a transmitter of emotions to a bearer of emotions. In the past, we didn't need to think too much because we felt at ease every day without much worry. But now, after becoming more mature, we need to pay attention to many things. In interpersonal relationships, we naturally treat others with courtesy, and the things we must do can confine us. We become more inclined to think from others' perspectives, unable to release our own emotions in a timely manner, leading to increasing repression, which is not conducive to psychological development. The more we suppress, the more subjective color we give ourselves. When we are afraid to do something, we hesitate to take the first step. You don't need to be great to start, but by starting, you will become great. What you need is to have the courage to face yourself honestly and navigate the balance of being true to yourself in front of others. My suggestion is to understand the context and learn to adapt. Different situations require different approaches. For example, when dealing with tasks from your boss, you need to execute them diligently, even if you have complaints, you must not act impulsively. However, you can choose a trusted person to confide in your displeasure, or simply write it down. Among friends, speak your mind and be brave, because pretending to be someone you're not will not bring true friendship. Being a good person often means enduring hardships. Don't hesitate or agonize over what you want to do. Boost your confidence and challenge yourself to develop your abilities. Showcase your unique qualities and actively participate in activities. When you feel your own emotions being suppressed, don't rush to analyze yourself. Instead, engage in rational analysis when you're happy, or seek objective analysis from others, such as a counseling professional. In dealing with aversion towards someone, you can choose to be tolerant and avoid arguments, or you can point out their mistakes. Differentiate between positive and negative approaches, and believe that you are a person of positive energy, so the choices you make are correct, but pay attention to how you communicate. I hope my answer is helpful to you. Wishing you all the best.

OP, you don't want to burden others with too much negativity, so you choose to keep it all inside. However, this has resulted in an abundance of negative emotions within yourself, impacting your normal psychological functioning, as well as your confidence and cognition. Maybe you need to find a way to release or relieve the stress in your heart, such as taking a walk, going to the gym, or listening to music to relax. Perhaps you can also try changing your mindset when faced with certain things, as adopting a different perspective might help you see things more clearly or feel better. If there are confusions that you can't resolve, consider talking to your parents or friends, as I believe that having more conversations can also strengthen your relationships. Best wishes!

question: Should couples tell each other everything they do?
description: I met my partner ten years ago, and we have been together for less than five years. Just one and a half years into our relationship, she cheated on me. After two years of breaking up, we got back together by chance. I thought she would change and we could be together properly. Little did I know, during our time together, she cheated on me once again with a coworker who had just joined her company. They were together for three years, and I lost all hope. After three years, this coworker found someone else. One morning, she suddenly turned to me and apologized, regretting everything that had happened. She realized my goodness and faced consequences. This time, I chose to forgive her once again. I know that everything depends on me, but for some reason, I still choose to be with her. My heart is conflicted. Every argument brings back all her shortcomings, and I can't help but think about the person she cheated on me with. It's not something I want to remember. The problem is, she hasn't deleted any of her ex's contact information, and occasionally still contacts them. I asked her to delete them, and she did so in front of me, but they reappear in her contacts shortly after. I know it has been a long time, but I can't seem to get rid of this scar in my heart. I am someone who lacks a sense of security, and once bitten by a snake, I'm afraid of even a rope made of grass. It's a painful inner struggle.
keywords: Love, infidelity, sense of security, managing relationships.

answers.answer_text: You have been with your partner for less than 5 years, during which she has cheated on you twice but then returned. You have accepted her both times and started again, but deep down you feel hurt and tormented by her infidelity. Relationships are often selfish and cannot accommodate a third person. Your willingness to accept her again shows that you love her very much, but you don't know how to face her cheating. Your emotions are contradictory - on one hand, you love her and want to be with her, but on the other hand, you mind her infidelity and feel resentment towards her. Generally, a partner's infidelity is a difficult behavior to accept and causes great emotional harm. Perhaps your partner has certain qualities that make you want to continue with her and you cannot let go. Actually, this also reveals that you have a strong desire and need for intimacy, fearing losing your partner's attention and care, fearing abandonment. These emotional needs are greater than the emotional impact of the infidelity, so you are more willing to choose to continue accepting her and endure the torment caused by her infidelity. Just like a child, being punished by their parents causes pain, but they are more afraid of being abandoned. Compared to being scolded, they cannot bear the pain of being abandoned, so they would rather silently endure the pain of being scolded than rebel and leave their parents. Your partner's infidelity brings agony, but leaving her, giving up on her, or being abandoned by her would be even more painful. Therefore, you have made your own choice to continue to be with her and continue to endure the pain of betrayal. Actually, this is a reflection of your inner emotional inclination and choice. Since you choose not to give up, you must be mentally prepared to endure the pain she brings you. Your attitude of accepting and tolerating her twice also makes your partner think that her infidelity is not a big problem since you can accept it, so she will continue her behavior and disregard your feelings. In order to resolve this pain, there are only a few options: first, encourage your partner to change. Have a good conversation with her, express your feelings and thoughts, convey your expectations and demands. Hope she can respect you, cherish your relationship, demonstrate her sincerity to you through practical actions, cut off contact with ambiguous individuals as soon as possible, and resolve your emotional distress. Second, continue to silently endure and maintain the status quo.
