If your partner cannot change and you are unwilling to give up, then you can only accept and tolerate her behavior, not interfere with her freedom, and not focus too much attention on that aspect. Instead, comfort and adjust yourself psychologically, maintain a peaceful relationship, use your tolerance and understanding to influence her. Third, gather the courage to leave. If she cannot change and you cannot accept or tolerate it, then why are you still together? Are you both just hurting each other? Gather the courage to leave, let go of her, release her, and also release yourself. Perhaps you are afraid of the pain of separation and unwilling to let go, lacking the courage to face it and the confidence to obtain emotional intimacy and care elsewhere. Therefore, you hold onto what you currently have. Please face your inner needs. If you long for love and care, does it mean that only she can provide it? Do you have the courage and ability to seek this emotional fulfillment from other places or other people? Let go and be willing to let go. The pain of separation will certainly be there, but it won't last long. There will undoubtedly be many setbacks in the search for new love, which requires courage, time, willingness to take responsibility, and daring to try and explore. This is also a test and opportunity for your inner strength to grow. The only person who can change your current state of pain is yourself. It's up to you whether you want to continue being trapped in unbearable pain or try for a chance to escape it. Best wishes.

Hello! You are free, and I personally think this kind of approach is more suitable for most couples, the key is whether we can achieve it. Some things should not be probed deeply, knowing them may not be good. With respect for each other, I believe we should have our own privacy, as long as it doesn't harm the relationship between the two. It's okay to have secrets, as long as we don't lie. Secrets that can be told are not secrets at all, everyone has their own stories. You love me very much, and I love you too. But we all have inconvenient things, if we can talk about them, we should, if not, we shouldn't force it. As long as both sides are comfortable, it's fine. As a couple, we are seen as a unit to the outside world, but for each individual, we are still independent entities. Regardless of how loving the relationship between the couple is, there should still be relative independence. Therefore, both men and women can have their own secrets. However, this should not be an excuse for not telling the other person important things. First of all, boyfriends and girlfriends establish trust in each other once they enter into a romantic relationship. On this premise, we should consult each other and keep each other informed. Of course, in order to strengthen the bond, we should tell each other when we encounter something. Secondly, it is unrealistic to expect to share every single detail with each other. For example, if you met someone at work today, it is understandable if you don't tell every single word of the conversation. Both sides should not demand it and instead give each other sufficient trust. Thirdly, important matters concerning both sides should be shared. For example, if one party wants to quit their job or change companies, or if you meet someone important who could create misunderstandings for the other person, it is best to inform them in advance and not intentionally conceal it. Also, if one party encounters something unpleasant and doesn't tell the other person out of concern for not wanting them to worry, at this time, the other person should be understanding. After understanding the situation, they should not complain too much and should let the other person know that they are willing to share the burden together. In summary, boyfriends and girlfriends should trust each other, with the premise of strengthening the bond, and not do anything that undermines the relationship between the two.

Hello, as a newcomer to the industry, I hope my answer can provide you with some insights. Firstly, your question is whether couples should disclose everything to each other. In my opinion, this depends on the stage and duration of the relationship. However, based on what you have described, you have known your partner for ten years, so normally you should be able to share everything. But it seems that your relationship lacks progress and issues have arisen. With the two instances of infidelity in the past and your description of "I asked her to delete it, she deleted it right in front of me, but it reappeared in her contacts after a short while," it seems that your partner is not willing to engage in honest communication when dealing with these issues, and instead resorts to habitual deceit. This is not beneficial for the development of a relationship, and due to her habitual deceit, it is doubtful whether she has truly changed. This might be the reason why you lack a sense of security. As long as this situation persists, it will be an ongoing "hidden danger" for you, which could have a long-term impact on your mental well-being. I hope my perspective as an outsider can help you objectively consider this issue and find happiness as soon as possible.

OP, hello~~~ First, give you a hug. From the description, we can understand that 1. You and your girlfriend have known each other for a long time, but she has cheated on you multiple times. 2. During arguments with your girlfriend, you can't forget about her infidelity, and you feel conflicted and in pain about this relationship. [Some analysis and advice] 1. In the process of a relationship, if you feel extremely uncomfortable and the reasons for your discomfort cannot be resolved, it may indicate that the relationship itself is unhealthy. Regarding your girlfriend's infidelity, it seems that it has not been fully resolved before, and there's no indication in the description that she is genuinely remorseful. There is a possibility of a repeat in the future, so you may consider reevaluating your relationship with her. 2. It is normal to have thoughts of feeling betrayed, unable to forget, and experiencing emotional turmoil. If you are struggling and unable to make a judgment about your own emotions, consider confiding in close and trusted friends or family members. Sharing your feelings can help alleviate anxiety and you may also receive some advice from them. Hope this helps you, OP.

question: Why does my mother always ignore my feelings?
description: In the morning, my mom was using a vacuum cleaner to clean the floor. I clearly expressed that I have a dust allergy and asked her to wait for me to enter the room before vacuuming. I repeated it four times, but she continued vacuuming as if she didn't hear me. Eventually, I couldn't bear it anymore and told her that her behavior made me very uncomfortable. She said I was overreacting. I want to know what should I do? It feels really hurtful to be ignored like this! Moreover, I do have a dust allergy and she knows that. Don't tell me to talk to her calmly, it's useless. Even when I talk to her, she just impatiently tells me that I'm overreacting.
keywords: Family, communication with parents, the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Why does my daughter always ignore my feelings? In the morning, when my daughter saw me using the vacuum cleaner to clean the floor, I wanted to express my hope that she could help me with some housework so I could take a break. I thought about it in my mind four times, but I didn't say it out loud. I hoped that she would come over and lend a hand on her own initiative. But she just ignored it and continued walking into her room, saying she was allergic to dust and asked me to wait until she went inside before cleaning. If she doesn't want to help, then she doesn't have to, but she still has so many demands. It feels like my daughter always sees things from her own perspective and doesn't consider my feelings. I really feel hurt when I'm ignored like this. Don't tell me to talk to her nicely, it's useless. Even when I do talk to her, she just impatiently tells me that she has other things to do and that cleaning the house is my responsibility.

Haha! First, let's applaud Teacher Zalongo's answer! In the world, there are only two motivations for people's actions: to seek love and to give love. 1. When Mom vacuums the floor, she wants to provide you with a clean environment. She is "giving love" to you. 2. Due to her own limitations, such as her understanding, knowledge, communication abilities, emotional state, physical condition, etc., she can only make the greatest effort to vacuum the floor and impatiently tell you that you are being noisy when communicating with you. 3. Mom used an "inappropriate way of expressing herself," which made you feel hurt and upset. Please reflect on yourself: Have you ever used inappropriate behaviors or expressions in order to seek love or give love, causing similar effects that made yourself or others feel upset and hurt? For example, have you ever used inappropriate behaviors or expressions to upset and hurt your parents or others in order to seek love or give love? You will definitely find a similar event like this if you focus on important people in your life, such as parents or loved ones. 4. Since you have done similar things to others, causing similar effects, take action to deal with the situation caused by you. Express apologies, gratitude, forgiveness, love, etc., to that person. After doing so, see if the impact of this incident on you has changed. I hope the above is helpful to you!

Hello there, I think everyone has a different level of concern for physical discomfort. If your mother doesn't have a "double standard," then it means she doesn't disregard your feelings. My mother is the kind of person who doesn't pay much attention to physical discomfort. When I had a cold and coughed, she would ignore it unless I had a fever, then she would take me to see a doctor. There was a period of time when I had a severe cough, and even the neighbors couldn't bear to see it anymore. They asked why my mother didn't take me to the hospital. Only then did my mother take me to see a doctor. I always felt that she didn't love me or care about me. But as I grew up, I realized that my mother is just that kind of person. She doesn't go to the doctor unless her illness is extremely severe. She treats me and herself the same way, so it's not a "double standard". If she gets very worried when she has a minor ailment, but doesn't care about me when I'm sick, then that would be a "double standard". Allergies to dust can be either very severe or just minor symptoms like itchy nose and sneezing. I know it's uncomfortable for you, but in your mother's eyes, she might genuinely think, "It's nothing, just a minor issue, no need to worry." That's why she might say such things. Since your mother is not considerate in this regard, you can take care of yourself. When your mother is using the vacuum cleaner to clean the floor, take the initiative to leave. In my house, my dad smokes. I used to get very angry and asked him to stop smoking, but my dad would get upset and say, "I smoke in the living room/dining table, if you don't like it, just walk away." After thinking about it, he's not smoking in my bedroom, so I started finishing my meal early and leaving on my own (I used to stay at the table and chat with everyone). My dad also puts up with it and waits until I finish eating, then jokingly asks me, "Have you finished eating? I want to smoke after you're done." Deal with it on a case-by-case basis, don't escalate the situation, try to understand each other with your mother, and take good care of yourself~.

Hello! When I saw Professor Longbar's response, please forgive me, but I laughed. This statement does have a certain significance. But there is no exaggeration here. Everyone desires to be cared for and valued, and everyone experiences the need to avoid allergens. If we understand the severity of allergic reactions caused by dust when vacuuming, we can promptly avoid dust sources or wear masks and goggles. If your mother knows that dust will trigger more severe allergic reactions for you but still continues to vacuum in front of you, then she is indeed neglecting you, not only your feelings but also your health and safety. Expressing discomfort about this without receiving attention can make one feel uneasy, breaking our fundamental expectation of being cared for. On the other hand, it is clear that you hope to receive as much attention as possible from your mother, regardless of what she is doing. You hope she can prioritize your feelings, emotions, and matters. Perhaps she needs to pay attention to your dust allergies when mopping the floor, and when cooking, she needs to consider whether you prefer sweet or salty flavors... In your description of the incident, you didn't mention why you didn't go into your room when your mother was about to vacuum, and you didn't mention why she insisted on reminding you "four times repeatedly." It is also unclear whether vacuuming will cause more severe allergic reactions for you, so it is not possible to evaluate whether your mother truly disregarded your feelings or if she had reasons that prevented her from avoiding it this time. If you are capable, you can choose to take care of yourself; if you have the energy, you can also make an effort to take care of your mother. She undoubtedly hopes that you can recognize her hard work and empathize with her efforts.

Hello, through your description, I can sense your sensitivity and the feeling of being ignored. You mentioned that you are allergic to dust, but I am not sure about the severity of your allergy. Do you need to wear a dust mask? You asked your mom to wait for you to enter the house before she vacuums, but she didn't listen. You said you repeated it four times, but she didn't stop, and you felt ignored. Based on this incident alone, it may not be able to explain much. I wonder if there are other things that make you feel ignored? Regarding this matter, perhaps you can try a different approach: wait inside the house for your mom to finish vacuuming before going out, or wear a dust mask. Because if you are outside and encounter someone cleaning, you cannot ask them to wait for you to leave before they clean, right? We always have to think about how to deal with dust allergies. Learn to adapt to the outside world instead of expecting others to adapt to you.

question: 24-year-old woman, first time resigning, feeling extremely nervous about the upcoming interview, what should she do?
description: Last night I sent a WeChat message to my boss saying that there was something going on at home, but she didn't respond to my message last night. I'm sure my boss will want to talk to me about it today, and I'm feeling really nervous right now. I don't know how to lie, and I'm really scared.
keywords: Career, career management, workplace interpersonal relationships

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand that: (1) This is your first time resigning and you feel nervous. (2) The upcoming interview makes you scared. Here is my analysis and suggestion, hope it helps you: (1) Firstly, there's always a first time in life, and it is normal to feel nervous and anxious. Especially when facing an authoritative figure, it's natural to feel uneasy. (2) Secondly, having a pre-resignation interview is normal. Just provide a suitable reason, not to encourage lying, but to let you know that working here is your choice. As long as you communicate clearly and maintain a cooperative attitude, there won't be any problems. (3) Lastly, don't fear authority, trust your judgment, and believe in yourself. #The world and I love you, wishing you the best~.

question: My parents don't understand me at all, I'm really disappointed. I want to die.
description: My parents are really not happy with me, They really don't understand me at all. They only know how to criticize me based on one thing. I really don't understand. I have been working hard. When I play with my phone, they say I am just wasting time. They say I stay at home all day, but when I go out for a walk, why do they say that? And this kind of thing from them is not just happening once. They only remember the bad things I have done for several years. Every time I do something they are not satisfied with, they talk about it like this. I am really disappointed. They can always criticize me based on one thing. They say I am not good at studying but I am also trying hard. I am really trying to change myself but they haven't seen it at all, not at all, really not at all. This time, I did not do well in my exams. Because my parents went out to work and my grandparents took care of me. They have been raising me and bringing me up. I did not do well this year and my grandma sent my dad a picture. My dad and they just started scolding me, using a lot of bad words, maybe I really have to leave.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the main topic, I give you a big hug and thank you for sharing your troubles with me. Your parents left to work, and you live with your grandparents. Your academic performance is not currently ideal, and combined with your parents' lack of understanding of your studies and life, they constantly criticize and blame you, which makes you feel more frustrated. 1. Parents' expectations: Your parents care about your achievements even when they are working outside. This shows that they genuinely care about you and have high expectations for you. Perhaps they believe that working outside is difficult, but if their child receives education, they won't have to work as hard in the future. Therefore, they attach great importance to your achievements. Sometimes repeating the same thing can really annoy a child, but behind the nagging, it is their way of expressing concern, and they may not know how to reason with you. Therefore, when communicating with you, they mix in their own emotions. 2. Communication with parents: Child, your parents don't participate in your life and can't see your changes. Maybe it's because of the distance between you. Your grandparents may pay more attention to the areas where you need improvement and therefore provide more information to your parents in this regard. You can try to communicate with your parents through your grandparents, let your grandparents see your progress, and inform your parents about your situation. You can also ask your teacher for help, ask the teacher to report your progress to your parents. Additionally, you can take the initiative and set achievable small goals for yourself, and actively tell your parents about your goals. Once you achieve them, let them see your changes. Give yourself and your parents some time. In terms of getting along with your parents, try changing your way of communication and ask them to solve problems with you instead of venting emotions to each other. In terms of your studies, you can ask teachers and classmates for help to improve your learning efficiency, allowing your parents to see more tangible changes in you. Keep it up! Believe that you can handle the communication problem with your parents and adjust your study status. Best wishes! You are loved by the world and me.

question: 4-year-old girl is injured and doesn't allow anyone to see. How should parents provide guidance?
description: My daughter is 4 years and 2 months old. A few days ago, she was injured in her right hand by a car and has a slight abrasion on her face. She doesn't allow anyone other than her parents to see her now. As parents, how should we provide guidance?
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, and psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, after carefully reading your question, I understand your concerns as parents for your child. From the analysis of your question, it can be seen that your child's current behavioral reactions are a result of traumatic experiences from the accident. [Try to avoid contact with strangers and protect her sense of safety] I believe that she must be filled with fear from that incident, and it will take some time for her young mind to gradually heal from such trauma. Although her physical injuries may heal quickly, the internal shock she endured requires the slow guidance and companionship of her parents. She currently lacks a sense of safety in her heart, but luckily, as parents, you have always given her enough love and care, and she can still feel secure by your side. Therefore, at this stage, it's best to try to respect her preferences and avoid too many people visiting, especially those she is not familiar with, because it will make her feel intense unease, which will not be beneficial to her recovery from internal trauma. [More positive care and effective companionship] To help the child overcome the shadows in her heart as soon as possible, the responsibility falls on the parents because you are her ultimate security. Therefore, parents should provide her with more positive care, try to fulfill her wishes and thoughts, and listen more patiently. Additionally, she needs more effective companionship. Nothing can relieve a child's inner fear more than interactive games. You can play card games and tell stories together, doing everything possible to help her overcome her fears as soon as possible. I hope the above response is helpful to you.

Children may feel ashamed and believe that their injuries make them look imperfect or unattractive. They may be afraid of being mocked or rejected by others. Children may struggle to accept these wounds. Parents need to first stand on a foundation of acceptance and help the child overcome these psychological obstacles. In my mind, I can imagine some scenarios where parents carefully observe their own imperfections with their child and say, "Look, what is this? This is a part of us that is different from others, it's a special gift from God. See, when you got run over by a car, it must have hurt a lot. This is something that adults experience but other children don't. Mom and Dad feel sorry for you, but also feel lucky for you. Because we only have some bruises and abrasions, it's not more serious than that! But that's okay, your swollen arm is actually a bit cute, does it look like Patrick Star's arm? The scraped part on your face will heal quickly too, it's like it's been painted with some colors. Mom and Dad will never dislike you, and neither will others. If you feel that others are looking at you with negative eyes, it's because they can't understand this kind of beauty. Mom and Dad still love you, and will love you even more, take good care of you. Others will cherish you even more!" Perhaps my words may not be suitable for your child, but you can try considering this approach. A child's heart is pure, and sometimes all they need is for us to help them change their perspective, so they can gain the strength to face setbacks. You are a parent who cares deeply about your child's inner world. I hope your child recovers soon!

Hello OP! I really understand your daughter's situation and can imagine that the physical pain she is experiencing must be difficult for her. And her emotional pain may be even harder... After hearing your description, I still have some questions that I need to clarify in order to better help you and your daughter. Firstly, do you believe that she doesn't want others to see the wounds on her face, or does she simply not want to see anyone other than her parents? Do you think she feels self-conscious and doesn't want to be seen by others? I ask these questions because a four-year-old girl may not have fully developed an understanding of how others perceive her appearance. In other words, she may not care about how others see her, except for her parents. At this age, children can be shy simply because they are unfamiliar, not because they are concerned about their appearance. So, this leads to my second question: how do you and your family view her wounds? Do you think they are unattractive? Do you unintentionally show a slightly displeased expression? Perhaps, on a subconscious level, the child interprets this as not being liked by her parents and that they don't want her to embarrass herself in front of others. (Please note: all of these processes occur on a subconscious level, so no matter how much you try to reassure her verbally, she may not be able to internalize it.) These factors may contribute to her desire to avoid others. However, I also think that we might overlook the fear and anxiety she feels about the traumatic event of being hit by a car. This might also be a reason why she doesn't want to see people. After experiencing a traumatic event, children tend to seek refuge with their trusted parents and reject interaction with outsiders. This also relates to how the incident happened, whether there were any external factors, etc. Her subconscious avoidance of others may also stem from a fear of getting hurt again. Lastly, what are your concerns about this situation? Is it because your child doesn't want to go to preschool? Or are you worried that she might be criticized for being impolite? Or is it that her unwillingness to see people makes you feel ashamed in front of your relatives and friends? Generally speaking, this kind of situation usually doesn't last too long, and you don't need to do anything special. It will naturally improve over time. Children have strong self-healing abilities. Wishing your child a healthy and happy growth!

After reading your narrative, the child has already started to learn to hide their weaknesses. This is a normal psychological mechanism for humans, just like how a person does not want to show their painful or negative side to others. For the child, she just feels that she is not beautiful, hurt, and does not want others to see it, so there is no need to overcorrect. Just need to convey some concepts, for example, these traumas will completely heal in a few days as if they never happened. After the wound heals, she will naturally improve and does not need excessive education. You can tell your child that some traumas require help from others, so she cannot completely hide herself. If you want your child to be able to be happy even if she is hurt, you can guide her to interact with others and play with some wounds. Because when a 4-year-old child has some external injuries, the behavior she exhibits must be related to the people around her, which also catches your attention. So, how to guide the child in dealing with accidental injuries with your words and actions in the future. At least for now, your child has entered an avoidance mode, and there is no right or wrong. She will make adjustments based on her own cognition and experience in the future. You, as parents, are crucial in this process of forming cognition and experience. Take this current situation as an example, you can stick a band-aid on your hand and show it to her. In everyday life, when you show some imperfections or flaws, and you can still be seen by others, she will think that it is okay, it is not a big deal. This will slowly influence her behavior. Leading by example is still crucial.

question: Having impulsive sexual relationships with someone you don't genuinely like, and then breaking up abruptly, do you feel regret afterward?
description: Ended a relationship that lasted for over a year. Afterwards, I wanted to find someone to fill the emotional void, so I connected with a senior student online whom I had never met. We chatted for a few days and then met up. But I soon realized that this person didn't meet my expectations in various aspects. However, I wasn't good at rejecting people face to face, so I thought I could adapt to being together. After we became intimate, I realized that I still couldn't accept it, so I decisively broke up. Now, school is about to start, and I'm afraid this situation will affect my future school life. I don't want to have any ties with this person again. Please help me relieve my concerns.

answers.answer_text: Sending you a warm hug (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You had a relationship with someone you disliked due to impulsivity. (2) You have now broken up and want to have no further contact with that person. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: Entering a relationship impulsively will usually lead to dissatisfaction. However, regardless of whether it was impulsive or not, it was still your choice. So when you feel that you have made a wrong decision and want to completely distance yourself from that choice, it is important to have a clear and honest conversation with the other person, allowing them to understand your feelings. When you return to school, do not let this situation affect you. Regardless of whether it was impulsive or not, you simply had a romantic relationship that didn't work out with the right person, and that's it. Don't overthink it. #The world and I love you.

question: The college entrance exam is coming up and my grades are at the bottom. I feel trapped and very uncomfortable.
description: The college entrance examination is approaching, and my grades are at the bottom of the class, which makes me feel terrible. I feel very depressed every day. The only time I feel relaxed is when I play on my phone at home. But I know that I need to set goals and make plans, but I don't want to do any of it. It feels really bad when I see my grades being worse than others and I attack myself. The average scores of everyone else are getting higher and higher, and if I manage my time well, I feel like I can do well in Chinese and math. I know that I am weak in English, but I really don't want to do it because I know I will be scolded. The thing that I can't tell anyone is that I know where I am weak. If I tell others that I want to study hard and they give me advice, I don't want to follow it. I feel like all my attention is focused on my mental state, trying to make myself happy and not collapse. If studying hard is painful, I choose to make myself more comfortable, but I may face a lot of incomprehension from others. I understand all the great theories, but I can't explain the pain I feel. I only know that once I choose to study, I may look good on the outside, but inside I will definitely feel depressed and in great pain, not allowing myself to make any mistakes. If I choose my mentality, I have to accept that my grades will not be too high, not like my ideal. I feel like I can't move, and it's very uncomfortable. I dare not do anything and I hope to adjust my mentality in college and then work hard. That would be at least fulfilling and happy, unlike the present suffering.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, I'm glad to answer your question. According to your description, I understand that: 1. The college entrance examination is approaching and your grades are not good. 2. You are afraid of putting in effort and just want to maintain a relaxed and pleasant mindset. 3. You don't know how to make an effort and are feeling stuck. The pressure before the college entrance examination is the biggest challenge that all students will face. The fear of mental breakdown that you mentioned is something that needs attention. Your main concern now is the visible distress caused by the pressure of studying and the psychological burden of choosing between putting in effort or prioritizing mental relaxation. This burden may be even greater than the pressure of studying courses and needs to be resolved urgently. In this dilemma, you are contemplating whether to study hard or prioritize mental relaxation, wasting time, which will only increase the mental burden and ultimately leave you without a solution. With the college entrance examination approaching, time is the most valuable resource, so you cannot continue to hesitate. In fact, you want to put in effort, but you feel overwhelmed by the backlog of coursework and don't know where to start. You believe that moments of relaxation while playing with your phone are the most effective way to relieve the burden and distress academically and mentally. This approach is actually an evasive behavior, which is normal for a student of your age who hasn't fully developed strong willpower. Perhaps you fear the frustration that failure may bring while making an effort. In reality, the process of realizing self-worth involves experiencing and learning from failures, as success often comes with setbacks. By learning from these experiences and discovering the study methods that suit you best, you can improve your academic performance practically. Facing the upcoming college entrance examination or university life, you will gain insights into studying and improve the efficiency of your learning. Moreover, the willpower developed when making an effort and overcoming difficulties in studying is an important quality to face future challenges in life. The joy in your heart can be achieved from different perspectives. After putting in effort and achieving excellent results, the psychological pleasure you experience will undoubtedly be greater than when playing with your phone. Based on your description, you care a lot about your academic performance, but you currently lack the courage to face the challenges and effort required when your grades are not good. The most difficult part in the process of studying is to calm down and get into the studying state. Once you get through this initial period, you will be able to focus on studying. The problem you are facing now is whether you can resist the temptation of outside entertainment, which is also known as self-control. To develop self-control, you first need to have the determination to resist the temptations around you. This determination can be motivated by long-term goals, such as wanting to become an outstanding individual. Then, consciously stay away from activities that may tempt you and start by cultivating self-control in areas that you enjoy and are neutral stimuli for you. Then, transfer this self-control to subjects in which you struggle. Divide your goals into smaller segments, and each time you complete a goal, reward yourself promptly to reinforce positive learning behavior. One important fact is that taking immediate action is the most effective way to reduce anxiety when you feel uncertain about whether or not to put in effort. Finally, I hope the world treats you with kindness!

question: Why do I feel so lonely, have difficulty expressing myself, and feel distant from many people?
description: Lately, there are times when I think about unhappy past events and when combined with current unhappy situations, I always end up crying. I feel very lonely and helpless. There is also no outlet, I don't want to talk to my family, friends, or even my partner. I feel that even if I did talk to them, they wouldn't truly understand and I feel very vulnerable. But honestly, I am mentally exhausted.

answers.answer_text: Honey, give me a kiss and a hug. You mentioned that recently, whenever you think of something unhappy, you always cry, but the people around you don't want to talk to you because they feel they can't relate. Indeed, this feeling is very uncomfortable. You feel like you want to share or seek help from others, but the people around you can't assist you, so you end up feeling trapped in a sad mood. But now you have reached out on this platform to share, seeing so many strangers offering you suggestions, I don't know how you feel now. Everyone is trying to bring warmth to you. However, all we know is that you are very sad, and we don't know what happened to you, so it's difficult to give you specific steps, and we can only comfort you with words as much as possible. Your family, friends, and loved ones are just like us, hoping to help you. So when you confide in them, they also want to support you. Do you think they can't relate because they can't understand your feelings? Have you tried explaining your emotions in detail to them? If they don't have enough information, it's also hard for them to comprehend your inner world. Indeed, everyone goes through vulnerable periods, feeling sad and isolated. But all of this is normal, and each time we rely on our own strength and the support of the people around us to courageously move forward. I hope I can assist you. The world and I love you!

Even the closest people to us often cannot empathize with us and sometimes even misinterpret what we are trying to express, ultimately causing us to gradually close off our inner selves. In fact, we can also sense the same situation from others, such as when our lover is in a bad mood today, and the thing that has caused their bad mood has nothing to do with us at all. So, should we choose to watch coldly from the sidelines, or quietly accompany them? Let's consider from a different perspective. If, at this moment, the other person truly cannot understand our mood, but they silently accompany us, giving us a simple hug and encouragement when appropriate, telling us that no matter what happens, they're here for us, then even though they may not be able to offer substantial help, having someone like that by our side seems like a good thing. Previously, when I had problems, I was unwilling to confide in others, and often rejected their help, causing me to always feel like no one understood me. Later, I started to gradually accept myself and understand others, and I am grateful for every person who has accompanied me, even though they may not offer me substantial help, their presence is a form of emotional support. The feeling of loneliness is indeed painful, but we can be more proactive, perhaps leading to different rewards. The world loves you and so do I.

Loneliness is an internal emotional experience rather than a response to external circumstances. It is related to a lack of love and also a longing for love. Lately, have you been thinking about unhappy past events? Did something unpleasant happen that reminded you of the past? Those unhappy experiences in the past were borne silently by you alone, right? Your family may rarely understand you, and they may even be the ones causing your unhappiness. As a result, you no longer trust them, nor do you trust friends or lovers, right? Actually, everyone's personality is different when it comes to friends and lovers. If someone doesn't understand you, it doesn't mean ten people won't. It's just that you have built a wall in your heart, keeping them at a distance. They can't get close to you, and you don't want to give your heart away, so you feel isolated and helpless. It's exhausting to face your loneliness, sadness, and vulnerability all by yourself. If you don't trust your family, friends, or lover and worry that they won't empathize with you, there is another outlet, such as professional mental support. Asking questions here today is one of those outlets. Although you haven't mentioned the details, it may not be convenient to discuss them in detail on this platform, but at least it makes you feel that there is a solution to every problem. You don't have to bear it alone and cry. We often feel distant from others because we ourselves aren't willing to be close. We may unconsciously create emotional barriers with others, so how can we expect to get closer to each other? You can try to establish trust with those few people you feel close to, such as your best friend and your lover. If you don't trust them, they might feel uncomfortable. If they are unable to provide support for deeper psychological issues, then seek professional mental help. In any case, there will be a way. I hope you can relax a little. There is no insecurity outside, only your own imagination. Best wishes!

I have heard a saying before that there is nothing that can make someone truly understand unless the needle is pricked into their own body; others will never know the pain. Friends and family are important to us as we grow. Family raises us as we grow up, while friends are the ones who grow with us on our journey. Generally, the ones who can become our good friends are those who have similar personalities or are similar in many aspects, which is why we can have good conversations. If you haven't met such friends yet, don't worry, because one day you will. Friends are often the garbage bin for our emotions. Although sometimes they may not be able to truly understand the feelings you express, they can be good listeners. They can also give us appropriate advice when we are in distress and need to make choices. Sometimes, shedding tears is a special way to release the pressure in our hearts. But if possible, it is necessary to open up to our good friends and have a heart-to-heart conversation. You can give it a try.

It is difficult to truly understand someone else's feelings. Maybe you just hope that the people around you can show some concern when you most need help. If you don't feel like talking to your family, try talking to your partner and see how they respond. Perhaps they don't really understand you. We all have some kind of connection with the people around us. When it comes to intimate relationships, opening up your heart is maybe what you need to learn. Some things can be done alone, but others require others' help. I had a situation before where I needed to make copies at a print shop. I didn't ask my friends because I thought it might be inconvenient for them. So I found a nearby print shop on a map app and took a taxi there. Later, when I told my friend about it, they said there was actually a print shop right next to where I live. I had unnecessarily gone in circles. Being strong alone, occasional moments of vulnerability are seen as emotional, and the person involved feels like they still need to be strong. But in reality, sometimes they are already stronger than others.

@Hello friend, I understand your feelings and I hope I can help you! First of all, your way of dealing with things is related to your personality. When you encounter many things, you are unable to digest them internally and shedding tears is a way for you to release your emotions at the moment. Secondly, your sense of loneliness mainly stems from feeling that you have no friends or family members to confide in. In fact, your parents will always love you and they are your harbor, while choosing a lover or friends requires careful consideration. Lastly, if you have concerns about confiding in familiar people, I suggest you seek counseling with a therapist, as it can be a very helpful approach. I wish you can find an outlet for your emotions and if my words can help you, that would be great!

question: How should one let go of a mentality of comparison, knowing that envy makes people ugly?
description: "I know that jealousy makes people ugly, but I am deeply trapped in it. I feel like I am just garbage."

answers.answer_text: Hello, from a human perspective, especially when two individuals are starting from the same starting line and are familiar with each other, and the gap between them is not too wide, the psychological changes experienced by the one who falls behind often accompany an overestimation or underestimation of self-development. This is what we often refer to as the "sour grapes" law. From an objective standpoint, we usually believe that if we don't succeed, we think that others are just lucky and only see their glory, while ignoring the reality of their suffering behind the scenes. Based on factual evidence, when society has developed to a certain extent, it is difficult for us to surpass our understanding of cognitive things, and sometimes we only believe in the limited illusion we see in front of us. Although the existence of jealousy can indeed make people deviate from the right path, in itself, it is also a manifestation of ambition and a refusal to accept defeat. The fear is not of being ignorant, but of being compared to others. The desire to win and the sense of competition arise in this premise. Therefore, it is very normal for such situations to exist. It is just that there will be a period of contradiction and entanglement in specific circumstances. The contradiction lies in understanding oneself but being unable to resolve the issue, while the entanglement lies in being deeply trapped and unable to free oneself. Here are a few points for your reference: 1. Starting now, adjust your mindset and calm yourself down. Solve your emotions first, then solve the problem. 2. Under certain time and conditions, achieve a goal and gain a sense of accomplishment. 3. Expose yourself to external matters more, cultivate some good interests, or participate in outdoor public welfare activities to divert your attention. 4. The best way to avoid overestimating or underestimating yourself is to be down-to-earth and calmly face everything around you, attracting positive energy. 5. The true change in oneself does not necessarily lie in the result of the problem, but often the process we go through in dealing with the problem. Inspire yourself and influence others. Best wishes.

question: What is the psychology behind my husband not liking me dressing up?
description: Some men do not like their wives to dress up, is it because they genuinely dislike it or because they have other thoughts? Should wives dress up in front of their husbands?

answers.answer_text: In regards to this matter, I have also heard several of my friends discuss it. Here are my personal thoughts and insights, hoping they can be helpful to you. There is a saying, "There are no ugly women in the world, only lazy women." I believe that every woman can learn to enhance her appearance and make herself look more beautiful. From the perspective of genetic evolution, men naturally gravitate towards "beauty". This doesn't mean that men are shallow, but rather because "beauty" conveys the idea that the opposite sex possesses good genetic qualities. This can be explained through biological instincts. Therefore, men are sensitive to and prefer "beauty". However, when it comes to your husband not liking you to dress up, it clearly conflicts with men's instinctive desires. The most likely reason for this conflict is your husband's inferiority complex. This complex arises from a cognitive belief, possibly subconsciously thinking that if a woman is too attractive, it will attract competition from other men. Yet, he feels inadequate to compete, so ultimately, he chooses to compromise in this conflict. In my opinion, for this issue, you can assist your husband in the following ways: 1. Provide him with more affirmation and encouragement, making him feel appreciated by his woman, gradually helping him build confidence. 2. Engage in open communication with him, expressing your true thoughts, making him understand that you dress up to make him happier and more secure.

question: The money that was borrowed isn't being returned, and I'm very angry. Why aren't they paying it back?
description: First, I lent nearly 100,000 yuan to my older brother for hair transplantation, marriage, and having children. I also lent over 30,000 yuan to my cousin for his business (which failed and cost me 1 million yuan in the past year). My ex-boyfriend, who owes me 10,000 yuan, has only paid back half. I have been feeling very depressed in recent years. It seems like my brother, cousin, and ex-boyfriend all have difficulties repaying the money they borrowed. Why is it that other people can repay their debts, but they don't seem to have the concept of repaying their debts? And they are all men, why didn't they consider their ability to repay before borrowing the money? It has been three to five years, which is too long of a time.
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand from your question that you are currently confused about why others never return the money they borrow. In fact, when we think about why someone doesn't repay a loan, we can also think about why someone doesn't repay us when we lend them money. If a phenomenon happens to the same person many times, there is likely a problem with that person that we have not seen. So let's think: what is the character of the people who borrowed money from you? Are they only not repaying you? Did you happen to encounter a few untrustworthy people, or do you tend to associate with these types of people? In the end, we will find that the answers are within ourselves.【Boundaries in Relationships - Territory Awareness Everyone Needs】In interpersonal relationships, especially in close relationships, we often blur our psychological boundaries. From your question, we can see that these people who don't repay their debts are close to you, and you seem to have not guarded your own psychological boundaries. You keep stepping back and making compromises, ultimately allowing them to encroach on your psychological territory, making it normal for them not to repay their debts. Because in their hearts, they do not feel guilty about owing you money, as you have blurred the boundaries and your interests are their interests, so this sense of guilt naturally diminishes.【The Face We Can't Let Go - The "Cause and Effect" of Lost Boundaries】So, when it comes to not repaying debts, have you actively asked them to repay? Have you been passively waiting for the money to be returned? There is a fundamental difference between these two scenarios. If you consistently ask for repayment, then the problem may lie with them. However, if you are only passively waiting, there may be another psychological phenomenon behind the loss of boundaries, which is not being able to let go of face. Behind the reluctance to let go of face hides the logic of "How can I ask my family for money? They are my family." This is a typical state of "blurring the boundaries between you and me." It is also another result of the loss of psychological boundaries. Therefore, please reflect on yourself, be aware of yourself. Even if you get your money back, a similar problem may arise next time. If you want to address the root cause, start by working on yourself. I hope this response will inspire you.

Hello, OP~ It's clear that you are a kind and loyal person. You willingly helped your older brother, cousin, and ex-boyfriend when they were in need. However, it seems that they have taken your help for granted and haven't shown any signs of repaying the money even after a long time. I completely understand your feelings. It's not easy for anyone to earn money, and the amount you lent out is not a small sum. I can sense your frustration and anger. Have you ever considered why they haven't repaid the money for such a long time? Is it because they see you as family and don't have clear boundaries in their minds, or do they think you are too lenient and forgiving? Or perhaps they simply don't have the means to repay the debt. You question why you didn't consider their ability to repay before lending them money, but the same goes for borrowing money: when you lend money to someone, you should also consider their ability to repay and assess their trustworthiness. [Some advice] Be cautious and learn to say no. When faced with someone asking to borrow money again in the future, you can consider their creditworthiness and ability to repay, and learn to decline. Your older brother, cousin, and ex-boyfriend have already demonstrated their bad behavior towards you, so it's only natural not to lend them money anymore. The same goes for others - while emotions are important, careful consideration is necessary when money is involved. Remind them proactively. It has indeed been three to five years. For personal loans without any written agreement or promissory note, whether to repay and when to repay entirely depends on the individual's integrity and character. You can proactively remind them and observe how they respond. Have a good conversation with them. If they are truly facing difficulties, you can let them repay gradually. Pay attention to the other person's financial situation when lending money. After lending money, keep an eye on their financial information. If their financial situation worsens, promptly reclaim the money, and be mindful of the loan's duration, making sure it doesn't extend for too long. I hope you can resolve this situation as soon as possible~.

# Why don't they repay? Do they not have the concept of repaying debts in their hearts? # Let me explain, because you don't understand this society, and you choose to trust them, that's why they come to you for loans. The power of choice lies with you! Suppose you choose to lend, don't you sign an agreement when you borrow? Just like borrowing from a bank, they always require a signed agreement, including interest rates, repayment methods, and repayment deadlines. If you don't sign an agreement, does that mean you are burying hidden dangers for lending them money that they don't have to repay? In other words, you are giving them this confidence, because without an agreement, you cannot sue them legally and make them bear the consequences of not repaying. Whether or not they return the money depends entirely on their character... If you still have to lend, you can choose to lend 20% of the amount they need (for example) to test their integrity. The cost is the potential risk that exists if you don't have a way to bind them. Whether or not they repay depends entirely on their character...If banks had to borrow money from people like you, they wouldn't have to ask you for loans, right? Suppose you don't lend, can't you find a reason to refuse? The cost may be that your relationship with them may not be good in the short term, but having a meal together, giving gifts during the New Year, should be able to ease the situation. It's still better than the current situation. Looking at this matter from a different perspective, each time you lend money, the amount becomes less. This shows that you are consciously reducing losses. Isn't this growth? The final loss of a few thousand yuan allowed you to see your boyfriend's credibility issue. Isn't that great? In the future, it's best to have everything in black and white when dealing with money matters. This way, trust can be maintained through the law, which is better than relying on emotions. In the end, if a breakup occurs, at least emotions can remain emotions and money can remain money. Everything is clear and straightforward. So why choose to trust relationships over contracts?

Good evening, Questioner! I am impressed by your generosity and righteousness. Compared to those three guys, you appear even more manly. However, it is obvious that money doesn't just appear out of thin air, right? It is the result of hard work and labor. Your anger is justified. But looking at the problem from a different perspective, why do your brother, cousin, and ex-boyfriend all come to you to borrow money? There's a saying: "Help those in need, not the ones in poverty." If they were truly trustworthy individuals, maybe they wouldn't have lost so much money due to greed or carelessness in business. If they have money in hand but still refuse to repay it, consider it as paying tuition to learn more about each person's true character. Once, twice, but not three times. You need to reflect on why you keep stumbling in the matter of lending money. Unless it's not your hard-earned money, be cautious in making friends and protect yourself. Only then can you take care of others. It seems that their trust in you has been overdrawn, and they are repeatedly reminding you not to easily trust someone. A wise person knows others, while an enlightened person knows oneself. Let's strive together to become wise individuals.

This is really frustrating. I loaned money to people close to me, but they haven't paid me back for a long time. Do they even understand the concept of repaying debts? Everyone knows the importance of repaying debts, but some people just don't follow the rules, just like how everyone knows to stop at a red light, but there are always people running the red light. It's hard to say if they considered their ability to repay before borrowing money. When they borrow money, they are always in a rush, and whether they will actually repay or not is something that comes later. If they had thought about the consequences and planned ahead, they wouldn't have asked for money for certain things. Borrowing money itself is a learning experience that allows us to understand human nature better. The only way to handle it now is to protect our rights if we are also concerned about our own financial situation. If the money itself isn't our main worry, but rather their behavior, we should communicate with them to understand their attitude and learn their true character.

Thank you everyone, after reading your responses, I feel much better. I really can't let go of family ties. I helped my cousin because his father had helped me financially for my education. My older brother is really pitiful, he's older but still unable to get married. I initially thought that borrowing and repaying money was common. But I didn't expect it to become such a difficult problem. My plan is that from now on, I probably won't lend any money at all. Like that friend said, reality has worn away my trust in others. I wouldn't even give a penny to a beggar anymore, even if they are my own relatives, I would ask for it back. But that is not the real me.

It is not easy to recover borrowed money. Here are a few suggestions to consider: As the saying goes, if you lend money and it's not returned, you must pursue the debt. Call and talk in person, explaining that you urgently need the money. Keep following up with phone calls, and if necessary, visit them in person if they refuse to return it. Since these people you lent money to are relatively close to you, you should be able to get it back sooner or later. It's not worth getting frustrated and upset over helping them with your kind heart. Nowadays, it's best not to lend money. Even your closest relatives may be difficult to reach, let alone strangers. If you really must lend, don't lend too much and be prepared for the possibility that you won't get it back, so you won't feel too sad. The best advice is not to lend at all. Can you manage to do that?

question: Feeling lost in life, not staying true to one's original intention, unable to maintain a calm mindset.
description: Because of the postgraduate entrance examination, I seem unable to get over this negative event. I constantly feel like crying, like dying, regretting my choices. Here's what happened: when I was preparing for the postgraduate examinations and adjustments, I received interview notifications from School A and School B. School A has a bigger reputation and a higher ranking, so I always wanted to go there. Both schools originally had interviews on the same afternoon, so I told my teacher that I would give up the interview at School B. Later, the teacher at School B changed the interview time to the same morning, and after the interview, they sent me a pre-admission notice that required an immediate reply. If I didn't respond, it would be considered as giving up the admission qualification. At that time, maybe because I didn't have full confidence in School A, in a moment of panic, I chose to accept School B. Afterwards, I felt like everything was spinning, filled with regret and self-hatred. I hated myself for not sticking to my original intention, for not even giving myself a chance to try. It seems like my depression has relapsed. I really hate myself, also hate the behavior of School B for snatching students, and I am filled with dissatisfaction and resentment towards School B. My parents, as well as classmates and friends, are all urging me to go to School B and earn a graduate degree. I don't know if I want to go or not. I really dislike the atmosphere of this school, and I feel like I can't accept School B with a calm mindset. I have thoughts of death. I feel like I have no value in this world...
keywords: Emotions, guilt and shame, panic and helplessness, tender and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I totally understand how you feel, sending you a hug~ The person who posted this feels regretful for choosing school B out of desperation. Now, I hope you can calm down and ask yourself, "If you were given another chance, under the same circumstances, would you hesitate to choose school A?" I'm afraid you wouldn't, and even if you had chosen A, you wouldn't have been so confident. Objectively speaking, although you were in a hurry at the time, choosing school B still had some logical basis, rather than being arbitrary. You also know that you didn't have a guarantee for school A, and going to school B, although not as good as A, is still better than missing out on both schools, right? At least that's probably what you were thinking at the time. As for the resentment towards school B, that came later, because you felt like you missed the opportunity to go to school A because of school B. You can't have your cake and eat it too, maybe that was the most correct choice in that moment. I'm not sure how much difference there really is between school B and school A, that might be the key reason why you're feeling regret. But, life doesn't have so many certainties, is going to school A always better? Is going to school B a guaranteed failure? They're both unknown variables. From this incident, you're completely negating school B, it seems a bit unfair, doesn't it? Are your own thoughts a bit extreme and generalizing? Most things don't go as planned. It's better to accept your current choice because being able to pursue a postgraduate degree is already a very fortunate thing. Your future won't be determined by which school you chose, you still have a bright future ahead of you. Prove yourself through your actions that you deserve a better life. Best wishes~

Thank you for the invitation, and congratulations on your success in the postgraduate entrance exams. I personally wanted to go to a more prestigious school, A University, but I have received an admission offer from B University. I feel frustrated about the competition among schools for top students. First of all, you have to admit that you are exceptional to be sought after by schools. So, any school, regardless of which one, would be willing to have you. I feel regretful recently because I couldn't attend the interview at A University. I wonder if I should try to go to A University for the interview. Life always moves between regret and satisfaction, and regret can be a beautiful scenery. If I can't go to A University, I should believe that no matter which school it is, it's just a threshold. What matters is how I develop myself with my own abilities and knowledge. Regret can also be a beautiful chapter in our lives, so why not accept it and let myself flourish in the current environment? Best wishes.

After reading your story, I must say that every decision we make carries our own responsibility and consequences. I would like to point out that it may not be the best choice, but rather a relatively good one. Have you ever considered what those who have failed the graduate entrance exam would do if they didn't even have the right to choose? In fact, this incident reflects a person's cognitive processing pattern. If we look at it from the perspective of positive versus negative psychology, it is about having a positive mental state versus a negative one. So, based on this premise, how would you convince yourself to have a better mindset regarding your current decision? I don't know if you have thought about the underlying patterns behind this behavior. Let me expand on it and see how you would respond in a similar situation, such as comparing jobs instead of schools, where both companies are facing the same circumstances as mentioned earlier. If you were to make the same choice, what would happen? Let's say two exceptional young men come into your life at the same time, and if you were to compare them, you might choose the latter. What would you do in that case? In the future, your life will have more choices. Learning how to make better decisions when you are relatively independent is something you should strive for. Choosing a relatively good school does not threaten your life, but when the choices you make in your future life can impact the quality of your life, what will you do?

Hello: After carefully reading the issue you posted, I understand your frustration and helplessness towards the actions of School B. They have gone to extreme lengths to attract students, losing the original purpose of learning and the school. I also feel angry on your behalf. However, at present, "a hero does not suffer losses" — if there are no other remedies, studying at School B is still an option. Analyzing the problem: 1. Due to the graduate entrance exam, it seems like you can't get out of this negative event and constantly feel like crying and even wishing to die, regretting your choice. The situation is as follows: when preparing for the graduate entrance exam, you received interview invitations from School A and School B. School A has more prestige and a higher ranking, and you have always wanted to go there. (You are a serious and responsible person with aspirations, so it is understandable that you want to go to School A. But this negative event is not something you can control, right? Life is full of countless choices, and no one knows for sure which choice is definitely right, right? Of course, passive choices are what you "don't want.") 2. Originally, both schools had their interviews on the same afternoon. So you informed the teachers that you would give up the interview at School B. Later, the teachers at School B changed the interview time to the next morning, and after the interview, they sent a preliminary admission notice, requiring you to respond immediately, otherwise it would be considered giving up the qualification for preliminary admission. (From the school's perspective, they all want to attract outstanding talents, which is understandable. But a true gentleman knows what to do and what not to do, and School B did not act like a true gentleman.) 3. Under the circumstances at that time, perhaps because you didn't have full confidence in School A, out of desperation, you chose to accept School B. Afterwards, you felt as if the world was spinning, filled with regret and remorse. It seems like your depression has relapsed. (You are an excellent person, which is why you have excellent worries. But do you know? Everyone in this world worries in countless choices, and most of the worries are not about School A or School B, but about School C or School D. Your choice is not wrong either; you always have to secure one option, right? This is also your cautious choice, isn't it? We, as human beings, cannot break the rules of the school. We also need to learn to "go with the flow," right?) 4. You really hate yourself and also hate the behavior of School B for trying to attract students, harboring resentment towards School B. Your parents, as well as classmates and friends, are all urging you to go to School B to pursue a master's degree, but you don't know if you want to go or not. You strongly dislike the style of this school, and it seems impossible for you to accept School B with a clear mind. You have thought about death and feel that you have no value in this world... (I can feel how painful negative thinking is for you, but negative thinking can be resolved gradually. As long as you are willing, that sense of "resenent and dissatisfaction" can also be gradually resolved. After all, we live our lives for ourselves, right? The future still holds infinite possibilities, and if you die, you really will have nothing left.) Facing the problem: "Feeling lost in life, wanting to die, feeling worthless, what should I do?" ~ Feeling lost in life means that you have fallen into a "pit." Since it is a pit, you need to get out of it. If it is difficult for you to do it on your own, you need to seek professional psychological counseling. If you do not understand something, we can try to understand it, and if there is something you cannot overcome, we can find a way to get through it, and then you won't feel lost anymore, right? ~ Wanting to die is not worth it; if you die, you will have nothing left, while being alive offers many possibilities. It is impulsive to make life decisions based on a one-time choice. After you graduate, there will be work, marriage, and children to keep you busy. Why would you want to die? If you have depression, we can seek treatment. I have so many successful cases, and this is not something that cannot be overcome. ~ Feeling worthless? "Value" is determined by you, not others. Since it is determined by you, if you say it has value, then it has value, and if you say it has no value, then it has no value. Perhaps the same thing can be seen as valuable by me, but you see it as worthless. Who can definitively say whether it has value or not? It should be a matter of perspective, so just adjust your perspective. Closing Remarks: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you can overcome your feeling of being lost soon! I wish you physical and mental health! If you have any confusion, feel free to privately message me!

Hello, I can feel the dilemma you faced when making this choice, as well as the deep regret you felt when you reluctantly chose School B under pressure. I would like to understand what thoughts led you to consider School B in the first place. I also want to discuss with you what would happen if you chose School A but didn't pass. Additionally, if you really don't want to go to School B, is it possible to select School A next year? Right now, it seems like we're only focusing on one possibility and excluding all other options, which can make you feel trapped. I hope we can have a detailed discussion and sort things out together.

Thanks for everyone's patient answers. I have gained strength to move forward from your replies. I will accept the treatment at b-school while actively treating depression, and living my life with great effort. I am just an ordinary person, and regrets may be unavoidable in life, but living is where infinite possibilities lie. Thank you all again! I will live well!

question: When there is nothing to do, I always think about playing video games. How can I break free from the allure of gaming?
description: When there's nothing to do, I always think about playing games. Even if I uninstall them for a few days, I end up downloading them again. I want to know how to break free from gaming and quit playing. I want to immerse myself in studying and real-life activities.

answers.answer_text: I understand how you feel. I also enjoy watching TV shows. I can get really engrossed in them and won't stop until I finish watching. Sometimes, I can go on for an entire day and night without taking a break. However, I have found a greater interest and started gradually replacing it. You don't have to try to replace it all at once. Take it step by step and make gradual changes. Don't set high goals or put too much pressure on yourself, because if you do, you'll feel miserable when you can't meet those expectations. Your new interest and the game can coexist. Let them both gradually become part of your life, and eventually, the game won't make you feel as uncomfortable or painful. Playing games is not only addictive, but it's also a habit that we develop. And habits can only be changed gradually. It's like a temperature difference. If the difference is small, we hardly notice it. But if today it's 30 degrees and tomorrow it's 10 degrees, the sudden change becomes difficult to accept. If you're used to warm weather and suddenly it becomes really cold, it's hard to accept. Give it a try, I believe in you. Keep going!

Hello, child! Do you often think about playing games when you have nothing to do? I can totally understand that feeling. There was a time when I was obsessed with playing King of Glory. I uninstalled it countless times, but then I would download it again. Every time I uninstalled it, I would get idle and want to play again. I would tell myself that it's just this one time and I won't do it again, but I couldn't resist the temptation each time! Actually, this is a very common phenomenon. Otherwise, there wouldn't be so many students skipping school or climbing over school walls just to play games. Maybe now you realize that you can't keep playing games all the time because it will hinder your studies and even lead you down the wrong path. The fact that you are aware of this and want to change is a good beginning and worth encouraging! How can you make a change? Firstly, it's crucial because once you have the idea, the next step is to take action. And the first step in taking action is to set goals for yourself and establish dreams. I don't know what grade you are in right now, but have you ever thought about what kind of life you want to have in the future? What kind of life do you imagine for yourself? What kind of job do you want? What is your dream? You can write down the answers to these questions and then think about how you can achieve them. When you have goals and directions, you will have a clearer idea of what you want to do next, how to do it, and how to use your time to achieve your dreams. Secondly, reward yourself. With goals in mind, you can reward yourself. For example, if I go without playing games for a month, I will reward myself with a piece of clothing or something else that I desire. By using this incentive, you can ignite your interest in studying and break the habit of playing games. If you want to change, you need to have the determination to change and believe that you can do it. Keep it up!

question: 23-year-old girl, always very unhappy with her boyfriend, what is the reason?
description: Background: I met my boyfriend online, and we have been living together in Hangzhou for a year now. He is from Chengdu, and I am from Jiangxi, but I moved to Hangzhou. During our time together, we are often very unhappy. He often doesn't consider my feelings, so I end up getting upset, and we give each other the silent treatment for several days. He is more introverted, while I am more outgoing, but I have a quick temper. Issue: Recently, he has been having a lot of trouble with his job and has quit without receiving his salary. So, I suggested that he go back to Chengdu next month. Therefore, I asked him if he would like to do some part-time work to make up for our living expenses. After discussing it, he agreed with my idea and said he would start delivering food. However, during the day, he said it would be too sunny, and at night, he said he couldn't see well. He is nearsighted, but not severely. Still, we decided that he would wear glasses at night when going out for deliveries and spend the day studying for next month's interviews (this was also my suggestion because I am worried that he will continue like this after spending three months looking for a job in Hangzhou). He can also cook dinner during the day. But yesterday, I checked the computer history and found that he hadn't been studying at all. I'm really unhappy about this (he told me yesterday morning that he was studying). Am I being too demanding? Or are we just not compatible anymore? We are trying to adjust to each other, but I still feel so exhausted.

answers.answer_text: ~~ First, give the OP a hug. From the description, we can understand that 1. The OP feels that the boyfriend doesn't pay enough attention to their feelings in the process of getting along. 2. After the boyfriend became unemployed, he should have been studying during the day, but the OP discovered that he had deceived them and didn't study during the day. [A little analysis and advice] 1. It is normal for conflicts and the need for adjustments to arise in the process of a couple's relationship, and the OP's thinking about the relationship is reasonable. From the description, it is indeed a problem that the OP's boyfriend has deceived them, but in this process, is there a lack of communication between the OP and the boyfriend? In any relationship, the most important method of problem-solving is communication, expressing one's thoughts, and dealing with problems together. Perhaps after communicating, the OP will find that there are some misunderstandings in each other's perspectives. 2. A couple is a relationship that is about to enter into marriage in the future. If problems arise between them as a couple, it is to some extent a good thing because it allows for the early discovery and resolution of some issues before marriage. The OP and the boyfriend may try to resolve these issues, but if the same problems continue to arise several times, and they have tried various methods but cannot solve them, then perhaps the OP should reconsider whether they are suitable for each other. Hope this helps the OP. Good luck.

1. You mentioned that you had a very unpleasant relationship with him, where he didn't take your feelings into consideration and you responded by giving him the silent treatment. Do you know why he doesn't care about you in that way? It's because he believes that you don't require much care from him. You also mentioned that you are friends on the internet, so when internet friends meet in person, everyone understands the situation. Since you have already made it easy for him to have you, why would he bother caring for you, cherishing you, or considering you? A person must love themselves first in order to have the ability to receive love from others. Love yourself, respect yourself, and before fully trusting someone, engaging in a relationship with that person should not be called dating, it's just a casual encounter. And since you have already engaged in a casual encounter, don't forget your initial intentions, so you can continue. Why transform a casual encounter into dating or even living together? This is the consequence of not sticking to your original intentions. The guy does not respect, value, care for, or even consider the woman. That's the most important reason why he doesn't care about you. 2. When he didn't consider you, you simply got upset. Has the issue been resolved? If he continues to not care about you next time, will you still get upset? In theory, if he doesn't respect you and doesn't even consider you, why do you still hold onto him and not leave? It's because you have become emotionally dependent on him in your romantic history. If you rely on others and depend on them, they will need to carry the burden, so why would they let you depend on them for no reason? It's all about control. For instance, allowing you to give him money, isn't it like you supporting him when he's not working? 3. Regarding the issue of pooling money together, there's another problem: you lack principles and boundaries, so when others see that you don't have principles, they simply quit their job and let you take care of them at home.

question: When people reach middle age, they have many choices. What should they do if they have selective disorder?
description: In middle age, there are many choices. At this age, I don't know how to handle things well, with low emotional intelligence and a lack of intellectual abilities.
