It always seems to be me who ends up at a disadvantage. I feel so disgusted with myself. Actually, I don't really care about being taken advantage of, but I'm afraid of being bullied because of being honest. I really want to live a carefree life without having to think about anything, but deep down, I still feel unsatisfied. When I try to change myself, I realize that the more I try, the worse it gets. I don't recognize myself anymore and I feel exhausted. I'm afraid of getting old, getting sick, and being disliked by others. I'm tired, life feels exhausting.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, social anxiety, social adjustment.

answers.answer_text: Poster, hello, after reading your question and some of your responses, I want to give you a hug. Actually, from the time we were born until now, there have always been many things around us that require us to make choices. But at the beginning of life, many of these choices are made by our parents. They hold our hands, make us go to school, tell us to study hard, strive to make money, and find someone who will love and care for you. When we grow up and let go of our parents' hands, we will be surprised to find that many of the things our parents said make sense, even if they themselves may not understand it. Then, when we have children, we become the same kind of people as our parents: speaking big clichés we don't even believe in, living a boring, monotonous, and painful life. Smiling and pleasant while facing others, but shedding tears when alone. Being able to recognize our own shortcomings and realize our own inadequacies is already remarkable! The beginning of self-growth is often painful and desperate. In this stage, we will discover our shortcomings, become aware of our flaws, and understand that we are trapped, and our abilities are unable to solve this problem. This anxiety will send a warning signal to our brains, forcing us to find ways to solve the problem: we can't continue like this, we must find a way to change ourselves and improve our situation! If we think radiantly about the problems, we will feel that there are many issues we need to face, and our abilities are very limited. When faced with problems, we must learn to tackle them one by one, think about them with focus, weigh our own abilities, and come up with strategies to solve them. You have many aspects of distress, and if you want to solve them all together, it can be very difficult and daunting. If you analyze them one by one and solve them individually, you won't feel as anxious. Let me give you my own story as an example! Current situation: I can't speak well, I'm not good at socializing, and I feel boring and uninteresting in everyday conversations. Scenario: During a gathering, everyone is laughing and having a good time, the girls around me are engaged in lively conversations, but I always struggle to fit in. Analysis of reasons: The girls around me are discussing cosmetics, but I have no knowledge about cosmetics and can't think of any interesting and novel topics. Solution: Observe those who are good at communication, analyze their daily topics, and search for information on similar topics in my free time. Fundamental reason: My everyday life is uninteresting, I don't have my own hobbies, so I should cultivate my own interests and have something I enjoy, in order to have enthusiasm when engaging in conversations. It's not necessary to fit in with others, what's most important is for me to feel comfortable. Throughout this entire process, scenario simulations can help you recall past experiences, and simulating the process is equivalent to reviewing mistakes. It may be painful, but it's crucial as it helps you understand yourself. The analysis of reasons, solutions, and fundamental reasons are the three steps. If you lack confidence, you can seek help from experienced people. Psychological counseling can help us find the fundamental reasons and greatly alleviate our anxiety. As we reach middle age, our appearance won't change much, but as time passes, we are still growing, and we also need to progress. You mentioned that change can make things worse. In that case, please set a long-term goal, and use that goal as an anchor. You need to give yourself a direction, a benchmark, otherwise, you may get lost on the path of change. Keep going, friend! On the road of wind and rain, you have yourself as company! Don't dislike yourself, believe that every decision you have made before had its reasons. You will become better!

I feel that the negative self-evaluations you have are mostly derived from comparing yourself with others. "I always end up with the short end of the stick, and I find myself very irritating." I think you may be angry with yourself: not standing up for yourself, not advocating for your rights. "Actually, I don't mind being taken advantage of, but I'm afraid of always being bullied because I am honest." Indeed, as you mentioned, you don't mind being taken advantage of, but perhaps what you care more about is whether others "see you" and whether they consider your feelings and existence. This is about respecting you as a person, especially since you are now in middle age. "I want to change myself, but I find that the more I try to change, the worse it gets. I don't know myself, and it feels exhausting." It is indeed quite challenging to change oneself. When you first start trying to change, it's easy to go overboard and become a "weirdo" in your own and others' eyes. Moreover, deliberately wanting to change is a matter of mental awareness, but it doesn't necessarily sync up with your mind and body, so it feels exhausting. Perhaps you fear growing old, fear falling ill, fear being disliked by others, and when you need help, no one reaches out a helping hand to you. So you end up thinking about a lot of things, striving for perfection in everything you do. However, reality is not perfect, so you have to hold back bottled-up resentment, sacrifice your own interests and demands, in order to avoid being disliked by others, and in hopes that someone would lend you a hand in the future. The physical functions of middle-aged people are constantly deteriorating, coupled with the uncertainty and lack of self-confidence caused by past experiences, undoubtedly making it even more difficult for you to make choices now. Try to embrace and accept your current situation. You have reached middle age, and you have weathered the storms of half a lifetime. So what is there left to fear? At the same time, I suggest seeking help from a professional psychologist for personal growth, if you want to see significant improvements. As a middle-aged person myself, I hope my response can help you. Best wishes!

Hello, dear OP. Regarding the issue you mentioned, "fear of aging, fear of getting sick, fear of being disliked, and handling things around you poorly," you may have also realized that this is perhaps an "excessive worry," since it exists, it must have its meaning. At the moment when these emotions appear, what is the inner feeling like? If one day these problems really occur, what kind of trouble will they bring to your life, and how will you deal with them? Perhaps in life and work, you are originally a thoughtful person, so in the future, no matter what kind of problems you face, I believe you will have the ability to face and handle them well. I am an assistant to Teacher Ming, sharing some personal thoughts, hoping to be of some help to you. Finally, I would like to share a message from Teacher Chen: "Having lived in the city for a long time, I still yearn for the tranquility and serenity of the countryside. I enjoy the peaceful moments of reading and the exhilarating feeling of sweating on the sports field. I also enjoy the sense of accomplishment after completing a full marathon of over 40 kilometers. However, it is only after traveling through dozens of countries in Asia and Europe, experiencing various local customs, that I realized that my home is the deepest, most beautiful, and warmest place in my soul. Furthermore, only through experiencing the ups and downs of life and witnessing the various aspects of humanity can one truly understand that the inner self is the source of life's vitality and the refuge for rest."

Hello, there are also people in their 50s who say that their brilliant life is just beginning. Age is not the criteria for evaluation, mentality is. No matter who it is, encountering continuous setbacks is inevitable to lower morale. And on the long road of life, there will always be a series of bad luck moments. If you don't believe it, flip a coin 1000 times and see if the results are evenly distributed or if there are 10 consecutive heads or tails. Be more confident, good people won't always have bad luck. In addition, you can engage in some long-term activities to boost morale, such as running, writing, painting, learning, or anything else that has accumulated value. Record something for yourself every day, at first it may seem insignificant, but after a while, 50 days, 100 days, 300 days, 1000 days, soon every day will bring you a lot of confidence. If you can't compete with young people in other aspects, then compete on who can persist for more days. There's no need to fear being overtaken, right? :)

question: Every day, for various reasons, I don't want to live and think about death.
description: After all, life is quite interesting. If you are feeling unmotivated to live every day for various reasons, how can you quickly end it?

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's nice to see your statement "life is quite interesting". I think having such feelings seems to surpass many people. I often hear people around me say, "Life is meaningless, boring, and has no purpose..." You think that life is meaningful, and I think your life must be interesting, fun, and bring you happiness and joy. Even if there are reasons that make you not want to live, aren't these interesting aspects worth staying for? You said that you don't want to live every day for various reasons. I don't quite understand the word "don't need." Does it mean useless, unimportant, or something else? Whatever it means, this part may be what you don't like or want to see. However, life is like this, it can't always be smooth, and there are inevitably various problems and troubles. It's like a yin-yang symbol, with black and white within each other. But if because of these negatives, we negate all the beauty and interesting aspects, wouldn't that be a pity? Life is not easy, but if there is a trace of beauty, it is worth our efforts to persist! We can pay more attention to positive and beautiful things, and try to expand the experience of positive emotions as much as possible. With these experiences, all other negative emotional experiences seem to be tolerable. Don't give up! Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Feeling unable to be happy, thinking that there is nothing good to look forward to in the future, fearing the future.
description: Starting from junior high school, my self-awareness gradually became clear, which brought me ongoing pain. I don't think I'm good-looking, my personality is average, and my grades, even if I put in effort, are just mediocre. This has led to an unchangeable sense of inferiority in me. I am always hesitant in social interactions, constantly worrying about which action of mine might have caused others' disgust. I am well aware that I can't do anything well, as I have been proven countless times. I am scared of the future that awaits me and can't imagine if I can endure it after experiencing real setbacks. After all, even a trivial setback now is enough to depress me for the whole day. I know that one's joys and sorrows are something that can never be truly understood by others, so I am afraid of confiding everything, as it might dampen others' spirits and make myself fearful.

answers.answer_text: OP hello, hugs. You feel like you're worthless, you feel inferior, you've hit rock bottom. All of this stems from a lack of validation. There's a saying that goes, "Everyone has their own unique talents and abilities." But your light has been overshadowed by thick smog, so much so that you can't even see it yourself. What you need to do from now on is to dispel all the layers of smog and find your true self. So, start loving yourself from now on. If no one else loves you, then love yourself wholeheartedly. Pay attention to your feelings and simply acknowledge them, without passing any judgment. If you're in a lot of pain and can't escape it, I recommend seeking professional help.

Hello, OP, give you a hug. I believe many people may feel the same as you. When our own life reaches a low point, we may feel that we are incapable of anything and think that we are worthless. But that's not the case at all. Each of us has our own strengths; it's just a matter of whether you have the patience to discover them. In daily life, as long as you are good at discovering, you will definitely find your own shining points. In fact, as long as you make efforts, many things can be achieved. I believe you will always be rewarded. I suggest that in daily life, no matter what you do, set goals and make plans for yourself. And strive towards that direction, the days will definitely get better and better. We must not encounter even the slightest difficulty or setback and shy away and escape. At the same time, you should also have confidence. When doing anything, don't get discouraged before you even start. Believe that you can do it well. Best wishes~.

question: I feel that my mind is so fragile, sometimes even a casual remark from others can make me cry.
description: I feel that my soul is very fragile. Sometimes, when someone says something to me, tears will flow uncontrollably. Or when something bad happens and someone comes to comfort me, even if tears weren't flowing before, they will start again for some reason when they ask. I wonder if this is good or not. T^T But I can't control it. I'm already an adult, and I really don't want to cry. What should I do? T_T

answers.answer_text: I feel that the OP's description may reflect someone who is emotionally sensitive but not particularly adept at expressing themselves. I sense that crying is their characteristic trait. From childhood to adulthood, others always tell you what to do and how to do it... Gradually, you become overly reliant on others and lack independent thinking. People tend to enjoy instilling their own ideas in others in order to gain recognition from others, such as the influence caused by marketing accounts, which unconsciously affects the public's perspectives. Those who lack critical thinking are easily led by the nose in such an environment. Regardless of age, as long as you believe that what you are doing is not wrong, you can express yourself in a way that suits your own habits. If you feel that shedding tears is not suitable for this issue, then you can train yourself in emotional management, so that crying becomes more appropriate in appropriate situations.

question: It is difficult for people with low self-esteem to engage in romantic relationships. What should they do if they have concerns but don't want to lose their partner?
description: From a young age, I always felt ordinary and didn't dare to imagine what I would be like when I grew up, fell in love, and got married. This year, I went on a blind date and met a boy who has a prosthetic leg on his left foot. We got along quite well, and after three months, we decided to enter into a relationship. Because we are both not young anymore, our parents want us to get engaged in lunar June. He is also inclined towards this idea, but I refused. I don't know what he likes about me that makes him so certain I am the one he can spend the rest of his life with. I don't have that much confidence. He spoke to me today and suggested getting married in August. Additionally, he told me that he couldn't wait for me for two or three years before getting married. I do have some feelings for him, but after hanging up the phone, I felt a great deal of pressure. I never considered meeting his friends and family or having children. I still have some concerns, but I also don't want to lose him. This late night, I can't sleep and keep thinking about what to do. I hope everyone can help me. How can I approach a relationship with a positive mindset? How can I build a healthy intimate relationship? I probably won't be able to sleep tonight. It's just my lack of progress. I hate myself for being like this.

answers.answer_text: Hello, first of all, I want to give you a little hug, hoping to bring you some warmth. Everyone is like a bright pearl, just not realizing it yet. From your description, it is clear that you have low self-esteem, mainly manifested in the following points: 1) feeling that you don't have any outstanding qualities that people would like, 2) not daring to pursue the things you like, and 3) disliking yourself. I want to tell you that feeling insecure is a normal thing. Many people, including myself, experience some degree of insecurity, just with varying intensity. However, this doesn't mean that we are not worthy of being liked or that we don't have qualities that people appreciate. I used to be extremely insecure, just like you. I thought I was ordinary and didn't know what people would like about me, and I couldn't even imagine if someone would dislike me once they discovered the real me. However, when I got to high school, I realized how naive that thinking was. The people we envy may not necessarily envy us in the same way. I can say that high school was the period in which I received the most compliments. People praised my hair, liked my eyes, envied my skin, and said many kind things... of course, these don't necessarily mean that I am outstanding or anything, but it made me realize that even though we may be ordinary, we also have our own little sparkle. It may not shine as bright as the sun or illuminate like the moon, but it can be like a candle flame—small, yet enough to make the people around you feel your warmth. Here, I want to give you the following advice: affirm yourself and say to yourself every day, "I am great." The fact that your boyfriend wants to propose to you also indicates that you have qualities that make him want to spend his life with you. We, too, are pretty good. We just tend to magnify other people's strengths and minimize our own, which leads to a one-sided sense of failure in our hearts. If we want to change this situation, the first step is to affirm ourselves. Love yourself first. For a lifetime, most of us may just be ordinary people in the world, but if the world doesn't see us, we need to see ourselves first so that more people can see us. Be brave and pursue the things you like. Regrets in the world are not mistakes, they are missed opportunities. Our lives are just a short few decades, a drop in the vast universe. Even the bird Jingwei wanted to fill the sea and the mantis wanted to shake a tree. Why don't we try our best in places within our reach? Even if we fail,at least we made a great effort and have no regrets, right? If we don't even have the courage to try, how can the beauty of the world come to us? Make efforts to improve yourself, lose weight if you're overweight, memorize if your English is poor, practice if your handwriting is bad. Whatever unhappiness we have is mostly caused by our own lack of excellence. What we need to do is turn our own unhappiness into our pride. Keep going every day, and one day, you will be proud of yourself. We may be ordinary, but we also shine brightly! Let's cheer each other on.

"Seeing your words is like seeing you in person. First, let me give you a warm hug and I hope my answer can help you. First and foremost, let's get to the point. What are your true feelings inside? You don't want to lose him, do you? Then accept him, don't miss out on him. It's really difficult to find another suitable person once you miss this chance, so please cherish it. Moreover, if you keep thinking like this, even if you meet the next suitable person, you will still have many concerns. What will you do if you miss out again? Should you keep missing out forever? Instead, it's better to cherish this opportunity tightly and overcome the problems in yourself. Next, let's address your concerns. You don't know the reasons why he truly likes you, there could be many. You need to reflect on yourself, maybe you are a suitable partner for him. You are gentle and down-to-earth, you won't cause any trouble, you will make a good wife and take care of household chores, etc. He is also not young anymore, so his thinking should be mature. If he wants to marry you, it's definitely not a momentary impulse. You need to trust him. You haven't thought about how to get in touch with his friends and family, but this shouldn't be a reason for rejecting him. You can agree to him first, but ask for more time so that he can introduce you to his friends and family, see if you get along well and if any major issues arise. Even if there are real issues, you can still reject him then, it won't be too late. You haven't thought about how to have and raise children, but that's something both of you should discuss. See if you can negotiate and find a compromise, see how he feels about it. If there are problems at this stage, you can also reject him, there's really no need to refuse without any communication or effort. I hope you can cherish the person in front of you, absorb my advice, overcome yourself, and I wish you happiness."

Hello, don't be afraid to imagine what it would be like to grow up, fall in love, and get married. Some people say: A person lives their whole life just to be an ordinary person, living an ordinary life. Ordinary doesn't mean average. If you have goals in life, if you can actively strive for what you want and be self-sufficient, then you're already great! There's no need to compare yourself with others, because they are not you and cannot understand your feelings. Everyone will grow up and want to fall in love; this is a normal development in life. OP is not afraid of imagining, but rather afraid that a certain stage of growth will be meaningless, without any progress, and no change compared to their former self. OP is afraid of being among the few who are not in a relationship or married at the appropriate age, and afraid of others' judgment. Dear, I suggest you make a life plan based on your abilities and strive for some level of personal development. Even if it's ordinary, make sure you live up to each day and each moment of your life. You can daydream and make plans for the future, like getting married and having children, even though it feels unfamiliar to you. That's why you feel pressure, but dear, this is also a path everyone goes through in life. Don't avoid it because of pressure. You can also seek help from family and friends, let those who have gone through similar experiences share their wisdom. Have more courage and sincerity, and less worries; everything will become simpler. Dear, in this complicated world, sincerity and courage are the most precious. "Follow your heart" and give yourself room to think about what you want. When you have figured it out, be brave and go for it. Keep it up! Best wishes!

Hello, thank you for the invitation! It seems that you are feeling conflicted about the current situation: on one hand, you have never been sure about how entering an intimate relationship would be, but on the other hand, you are afraid of missing the opportunity to enter into an intimate relationship. It appears that you are facing a series of pressures without being fully prepared psychologically. You are uncertain whether you should follow your own pace or follow the pace of others. You want to balance both but find it difficult, and perhaps you are also afraid of the potential losses that may come with making a choice. You mentioned that you have always felt "ordinary" since childhood and haven't dared to envision what it would be like to grow up, fall in love, and get married. I wonder what kind of experiences have led you to link being "ordinary" with the difficulty of growing up, falling in love, and getting married. What is your imagination of growing up, falling in love, and getting married like? I believe that when people are about to enter a new stage in life, they will have certain expectations and concerns. When you are too scared, perhaps some experiences or imaginations related to this are hindering you. Despite your fear of thinking about it, you still went on blind dates. I'm curious about the circumstances under which you went on these blind dates. Did your own expectations increase, or did your concerns decrease, or were you pressured by reality and external forces? How do you feel about blind dates? You mentioned that the boy has a prosthetic limb on his left foot. I wonder what your thoughts and feelings are about this? Does it somewhat affect your feelings towards the boy and your decision to spend your life with him, including having children? You are curious about what the other person likes about you, and I'm wondering if this pace is too fast for you. Are you worried that other factors are pushing the other person and their family to want you to start a family quickly? I think that before being curious about the other person, it is also important to understand your own thoughts and feelings about the other person. When you understand yourself better, perhaps you will be ready to transition from a relationship with yourself to a relationship with another person. For example, when you are clearer about your concerns and the reasons why you are afraid of losing the other person, you can consider whether to share your desires and worries with the other person, and see if it is possible to involve the other person in facing and resolving the issue together. After all, if getting married and starting a family makes you feel like it is a "demand from the other person," this feeling of being "compelled" may make you doubt the relationship even more, rather than feeling confident. It might also make you feel very risky and lonely. Even if communication doesn't necessarily lead to a unanimous outcome, a sufficient and effective process of communication can make you more clear and reduce your confusion and unease. This is also part of considering your relationship with each other and future intimate relationships. Of course, the above is just a superficial response based on your current question, and a more in-depth exploration requires a relatively longer process. Consider seeking professional psychological counseling if needed. Best wishes!

Hello there~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug~ What makes a good intimate relationship? 1. Trust, even when there are issues, being willing to believe that harm is not intentional. 2. Reflectiveness, being willing to think about what exactly is going on between the two people and what personal shortcomings need to be adjusted. 3. Being willing to restrain impulsive reactions in order to make more long-term changes for better coexistence. 4. Being willing to believe that both parties value each other and the relationship itself, and after calming down, discussing together how to solve problems instead of blaming each other or attacking each other. 5. Although good relationships may also involve pain, you can feel yourself growing and maturing within the relationship. A good relationship allows you to feel at ease to be yourself and develop yourself. Learning how to build a good relationship is something that can be enhanced through learning. I suggest reading relevant books, listening to courses, or having deeper conversations with a mental health counselor. Best wishes~.

Hello, OP! Seeing the description you provided, I can sense your hesitation and reluctance. Let's try summarizing the key points of the events to see if it sparks any new ideas for you. 1. Insecurities and reluctance: Based on your title, it's clear that you feel hindered in your romantic endeavors due to your own insecurities. Your self-doubt leads to concerns, yet you also have a desire to not let go. On one hand, you perceive yourself as ordinary and insecure, failing to see any outstanding qualities that would make someone want to enter into a marriage with you so quickly. Rather than solely blaming yourself for feeling inadequate, it may be more appropriate to say that the other person has not expressed or done enough to make you willingly walk alongside them. On the other hand, this brief encounter may not have given you enough security to rapidly enter into marriage. Perhaps you are not prepared for a long-term commitment yet, as marriage and dating are fundamentally different. While you have a degree of satisfaction in the other person, it might not be enough to push you towards marriage. 2. Lack of preparation: You are not ready to meet the other person's family and friends, have children, and have unresolved concerns. You need more time to prepare, especially emotionally. Many times, if you enter a situation without proper psychological preparation, you may find yourself unprepared for the battlefield. As a mother myself, I remember on the morning of my marriage registration, before entering the venue, I considered sitting on the curb to soberly think about it. However, I didn't wait to make a decision and simply went ahead with the registration. If you want to have a healthy relationship and willingly enter into a marriage, consider the following suggestions: [Acceptance] Accept yourself for who you are and trust the other person's choice. Don't compare your shortcomings with those of others. You are you, and every individual in this world is unique. To a certain extent, everyone has their own outstanding qualities. [Communication] If you are not yet ready for marriage and fear missing out on the other person, you can express your concerns to them in the hope of receiving understanding and patience. Only through communication can problems be better resolved. Good luck, OP!

Hi, I think you're currently mostly troubled by the pressure from your partner, because you're not at the stage of getting married and having children yet. The pressure from your surroundings and your partner makes you doubt yourself, so you're feeling troubled, right? I don't think your issue is directly related to insecurities. According to Freud, insecurities exist in people since birth and are inherent instincts. When children are born, their skills in various aspects are not fully developed, so they inevitably feel insecure. In your situation, you also don't have much dating experience and social experience, so it's normal to feel some level of insecurity. After all, it's hard to be confident about controlling the future. Therefore, insecurity is something that most ordinary people experience and it doesn't affect the development of our relationships. It might even trigger our partners' desire to protect us. In your case, it seems that the core issue is that it's not yet time to discuss marriage and settling down. Based on your description, it seems like the man is more anxious and wants to rush into marriage and having children without truly understanding each other. On the other hand, as a woman, you consider the future more, while the man is more focused on obtaining and possessing. At this critical moment, it seems like your family hasn't provided enough understanding and support, so now you're starting to doubt yourself - wondering if your insecurities have affected the pace of your relationship. Actually, I don't think so. It's just that the timing may not be right for discussing marriage and settling down. We still want to get to know each other more deeply and establish a stronger sense of security before taking the next step, right? Take care, and feel free to private message me if you have any questions or need further clarification.

Hello, OP. I completely understand your anxiety about love, marriage, and personal growth, as we are in the same age group and going through a transition period. Feeling ordinary is something we all experience, but who isn't? We are all both ordinary and exceptional because there are undoubtedly many remarkable individuals in the world, but we are also unique and have our own value. So what we need is an accurate assessment and understanding of ourselves, and then strive to enrich ourselves to become better and better, and that is sufficient. I believe you are exceptional, and it has nothing to do with others. Being born human means you already possess a natural sparkle. So there's no need to dwell on your mediocrity. As for the issue of engagement and marriage, it is normal to feel anxious if we are not ready and lack sufficient understanding. You mentioned not knowing what the other person likes about you, but since you are already discussing engagement, you can definitely have that conversation. You can talk about what he likes about you, what aspects, and what you like about him. After all, love is something that can be discussed. If you still like him based on your description, then there must be qualities about him that you appreciate. Speak up and express your admiration because everyone likes to be praised. I sense that you are under a lot of pressure, such as meeting his friends and family, and even the idea of having children. I also have some concerns. We always feel nervous and uneasy about things we have not experienced before, but there is always a first time for everything, and practice makes perfect. You can share your anxieties with your boyfriend and see how he can help you. This will not only promote your intimacy and communication but also prepare you for the many more communication challenges that come with marriage. We are all first-time children, first-time spouses, and first-time parents, but we will all go through these experiences, so learn more and practice. A healthy intimate relationship requires cultivation, which also necessitates various abilities such as respect, understanding, tolerance, the ability to love, and the ability to give and receive, among others. We need to learn these skills. My suggestion for you is to read more books about intimate relationships, such as "The 5 Love Languages," "Intimate Relationships," "Nonviolent Communication," "The Power of Empathy," and so on. Additionally, communicate more about your anxieties with your boyfriend, family, and friends. I wish you a fulfilling marriage. Best wishes!

question: Seventh grade, already a big kid, but my mom doesn't give me any privacy, what should I do?
description: I have a younger cousin who recently confided in me. He is in his second year of junior high, and in the eyes of others, he is already a big kid. He wants his own privacy because he has to be extremely careful every time he chats with classmates, which has resulted in him having very few friends. His mother doesn't give him any privacy at all, which makes him feel very upset and speechless. Whether it's his photo albums, chat records, or the apps he downloads, anything that his mother disapproves of gets deleted. She also doesn't allow him to bring his phone to school, which makes my cousin feel very inferior. All his classmates have phones, so he feels quite awkward being the only one without. Sometimes, the teacher will notify the class about certain information through a group chat, but he doesn't see the message because he doesn't have a phone, and he ends up getting scolded the next day at school. He feels like his mother doesn't understand him or consider his feelings. He wonders what he should do to have his own privacy.

answers.answer_text: The first year of middle school is already a rebellious phase. The so-called rebellious phase is actually named by adults, but for children, it is a period of self-growth. At this age, children's bodies mature rapidly and they accumulate a lot of knowledge and skills, experiencing significant personal growth and developing their own ideas. As a result, they may have different perceptions from their parents, leading to inevitable conflicts. In my opinion, privacy is a right that belongs to every individual, and no one, including parents, should violate it. From this perspective, your cousin's request is very reasonable. So, how can his goal be achieved? First, it is necessary to assess the behavior of the parents. Without the right to investigate, there is no right to speak. If one is unaware of the other party's situation, they cannot strive for victory, making accurate assessment crucial. Why do parents monitor us? It's simple - parents have guardianship rights. In any country, because children do not have independent civil responsibilities, they do not have to bear the consequences individually. Many consequences need to be borne by parents, so the government recognizes the right of guardianship. Children also have the right to privacy, which the government acknowledges. Therefore, within a family, whether the child's right to privacy outweighs the parents' right to guardianship depends on the interaction between parents and children. If the parents are dominant and disregard your cousin's legitimate rights, nonviolent communication is one approach. However, if the parents are communicative and their aim is not to violate your cousin's privacy but to control phone usage, then a different approach must be taken. From your narration, your cousin's desire or primary goal is to have exclusive use of the phone. The first year of middle school is a critical period for learning. Is your cousin a person who can exercise self-control? Can he be disciplined? Can he take responsibility for his choices and results? I think your cousin has not done enough in this regard because having fewer friends and being cautious in chatting are not necessarily related. After all, making friends is easier through real-life interactions than through online conversations. Second, do not be afraid of conflict. Conflict is beneficial because it is a form of non-verbal communication. When children have conflicts with their parents, parents become aware of the boundaries of their children's individuality. Many well-behaved children, out of fear of conflict, often do not establish clear boundaries for themselves. As a result, they are easily invaded, and their rights can only be obtained through competition. Third, make commitments. If parents' intentions are good but do not align with the children's perspective, making commitments and following through on them is the only way to gain privacy rights. Parents love their children and want to protect them from harm. How can parents realize that their children have grown up? The best approach is to make commitments and keep them. At this point, trust is established between parents and children, and parents can let go. Fourth, respect and understanding. Respect parents' guardianship rights and understand their good intentions, but also protect one's own rights. Be objective and gentle, maintaining a strong stance.

From the description, it is evident that the original poster strongly disagrees with and doesn't understand the behavior of their cousin's mother. I cannot fathom why the cousin's mother would act in such a manner. My speculation is that she may still lack trust in your cousin and views him as a child, fearing that he will be exposed to the harsher side of the world. Indeed, a student in the second year of junior high school is nearly an adult and should be afforded some independence. Perhaps his mother hasn't noticed or refuses to accept that he has grown up, leading her to treat him as a child. Although it may be difficult to accept, I believe you should advise your cousin to make an effort to comprehend his mother's actions. Our mothers are the people who love us the most in the world, and their love is selfless. Even if their expressions of love may not align with our expectations, we should strive to understand their love for us. I suggest you propose that your cousin have an open conversation with his mother, explaining that he has matured and also requires some privacy. Clearly articulate the challenges posed by the current situation in regard to his studies and daily life, as well as the negative impact on his personal growth. Although his mother may still fail to understand him, attempt to engage her in a rational discussion to gradually find a resolution, allowing her to slowly come to terms with his growth. I hope this advice proves helpful to you. Good luck!

question: How to balance the differences in lifestyle between generations with parents?
description: The lifestyle of the older generation may differ significantly from that of the younger generation, whether it's regarding daily routines or dietary habits.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I think what you're referring to isn't just about the differences in "daily routines, eating habits, etc." between generations and their parents' lives. It's just that these issues come up every day, so they're easier to discuss. However, on the other hand, although these are just small things in life, they become irritating when mentioned repeatedly, don't they? So, when they talk about these "petty things," they might actually mean something else. Perhaps if you understand this, you might find the answer to your own question. Take care of yourself.

question: 21-year-old male, has been heartbroken for over six months, constantly connects unrelated things together.
description: Breakup for over half a year, since the breakup, I have developed OCD and always connect unrelated things and things I don't know together. Although I know there is no connection, I still find myself overthinking, panicking, and constantly overgeneralizing the forced connections. How can I deal with this issue as it is affecting my daily life?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand that you have not been able to recover from the state of heartbreak and your mind is filled with many thoughts, even impacting your daily life with helplessness. Regarding your question, here is my response. Problem analysis: *Obsessive thinking, affecting life: a basic phenomenon is the neural pathways in our brain, similar to muscles in our body. When you exercise continuously, your muscles become stronger. Similarly, when you constantly ruminate, it strengthens the activity of neural pathways. When you pay too much attention to certain matters and allow your brain to freely think and connect unrelated things, you become more dependent on this feeling, gradually reinforcing this behavior. In your case, this condition only appeared after the breakup, so the root cause is the trauma caused by the breakup. It is crucial to learn how to view the breakup with a calm mind and accept this reality. A breakup signifies the end of the energy and emotional investment you put into the other person, resulting in a loss of a part of yourself. Constantly generalizing thoughts is also a way of not accepting this loss, attempting to make connections with the ended relationship through any traces, avoiding the sense of loss and pain brought by the relationship's end. Some suggestions: 1. If it has been half a year since the breakup and you are still immersed in pain and uncontrollable thoughts, you need to ask yourself if your brain and attention are too idle. When you have no goals or directions, naturally your brain will still think about the loss. Only when your brain's attention and energy are occupied and replaced by meaningful things, your aimless thoughts won't have the chance to flood your mind. 2. You can choose to practice mindfulness meditation to improve your concentration and learn how to control your thoughts. When you are unable to control yourself, using scientific methods can greatly help you.

Hello: Hmm, many young people nowadays have symptoms of OCD, including obsessions and compulsions. Based on your current situation, it seems like you have more obsessions than compulsions. Typically, this can result in emotional isolation and difficulty forming intimate relationships. From what I gather, the breakup might have triggered these symptoms, but it's not the only cause of your OCD, right? Analyzing the issue: 1. It's been over half a year since the breakup, and since then, you have developed OCD. You constantly link unrelated things and concepts together, even though you know they're unrelated. However, you still ponder and panic, even going as far as generalizing and overthinking. How can this be managed? (Due to the limited information, I will ask you some related questions: Do you have a diagnosis from a hospital? Or do you simply think it's OCD? Did you develop OCD before or after the breakup? Are these unrelated things truly unrelated to making friends? It's normal for all of us to have areas where we lack knowledge, and it's okay. Even though you know they're unrelated, you still tend to make many associations and even experience panic, then generalize. Yes, this is the basic manifestation of OCD. However, the problem itself, as well as any symptoms, are not the scariest part. The key is, when you read my message, ask yourself sincerely if you truly want to solve this problem (you must seriously ask yourself and give yourself a clear answer). If the answer is "yes," then there are many solutions. If you hesitate, then let's wait until you truly want to solve it, and then we can address it. Closing statement: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you can overcome this disturbance soon! If you have any confusion, feel free to message me!

Although it may be easy for bystanders to offer advice, it is not always as simple for someone in the midst of it all to break free. While sadness will eventually diminish over time, there are many rituals that can help you let go more quickly. For example, 1) go to a scenic spot to feel the breeze, 2) stay up all night watching the rain outside the window, 3) take a long walk (try not to go in circles - you can cover a good distance in an hour, and in half a day, you can walk quite far). The common point is to clear your mind and take the time to reflect on the past in a comfortable environment. Imagine packing these memories into a box of recollections and envision starting a new life with these memories. After going through such a ritual, even if sadness comes knocking again, don't let it consume you as before. Instead, treat it like taking out a cherished item to savor and then put it back. It's like reflecting on both bitter and sweet memories, just like having a cup of coffee. There's nothing wrong with it.

question: How to live with a roommate whose values do not align with yours and with someone you dislike?
description: I used to be a happy and positive girl, starting from my college dormitory. There were three of us in the dormitory: me, A, and another girl B. Because A and I had different values, we gradually drifted apart. As for B, she was introverted, but I considered her a friend. However, she gradually started to prefer A over me. Later on, I often found myself being criticized by AB, which made me feel like they didn't like me. I always wished for others to like me, so I often paid attention to people's expressions, which made me tired and sensitive. In my junior year, my relationship with A completely broke down because he badmouthed me to others. I never talked to my other dormmates about this incident, and after that, I completely gave up on trying to salvage the relationship. Now, we have another girl, C, in our dormitory. When she first came, we got along well, but as a result of the pandemic, we are now in our senior year, and C has instead become close to AB. Because I dislike A, I often return to the dormitory without saying a word. I used to be talkative, but now I feel oppressed every day. During my graduate school entrance exam preparation, I feel uneasy whenever I think of A in my dormitory. What should I do?
keywords: Interpersonal, conflicts, roommates, classmates, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Title, hello, I'm sending you a hug ~ From your description "I used to be a positive and upbeat girl", I feel that you have a positive self-description, so I think that now the majority of your problems come from external factors. There shouldn't be any major psychological issues, but rather more problems with differing beliefs. From your description, you mentioned that you and A have differing values, so you chose not to associate with her. However, personally, I think that when you have differences, you should consider that you will be living together for four years, and many things require mutual support and assistance. You may also try to understand her, find other strengths and common ground, and try not to make the relationship too tense. But now that things have come this far, it seems that there is no room for regret. However, you can still make some effort for your relationship. Now, you may feel uncomfortable because you have doubts about yourself. However, I feel that both of your roommates who actively sought to befriend A ended up getting along well with her, so there must be a reason for it. But we may not be able to guess this reason, so you can only actively ask them. Communication is the best way to solve problems. If you feel that it is affecting your academic life now, you must find a way to know the reason. No one would distance themselves from someone for no reason.

question: Often not trusting others, how to make oneself less easily hurt?
description: I have found that I often distrust others, especially men. It seems that I rarely encounter situations where women are treated well. When my male colleagues show disgust towards me, I feel hurt. Although my rational mind tells me that they are insignificant, my true feelings inside cannot deny the hurt. I have also noticed that if a man shows acceptance or trust towards me, I will constantly try to test what he really wants and then try to please him. This reminds me of my relationship with my father. In my memories, I often shout at him, asking why he doesn't believe in me. Yes, every time I need him, my father always withdraws. It doesn't matter if it's my younger sister complaining that I didn't play with her when we were young, or when I applied to high school and my dad unilaterally changed my choice of major, or even when he told me not to go to distant Northeast China for college before I went, all of these actions were not with my consent and did not respect my wishes. So I became very rebellious after entering college, unwilling to go home, not actively asking for living expenses, not sharing my joys or sorrows. Later during the holidays, I bought him a hat with the money I earned from my part-time job, and he seemed very happy, showing it off everywhere. But deep down, I felt very uncomfortable. It seemed that what he wanted was just others being kind to him.
keywords: Growth, character development, personality traits, self-improvement

answers.answer_text: Hi, OP, hello. Hug the little you from childhood. From your description, it is obvious that you know the problem lies in your relationship with your father. As a girl, the father is the first opposite-sex relationship we have in our lives, so the relationship with the father often affects our relationships with other opposite sexes in adulthood. However, when we were children, we didn't have the ability to actively create a desired good relationship, and it all depended on our parents. But parents cannot be chosen, so we can only passively bear everything our parents bring us, including relationships. But you are different now. Do you know what's different? You have grown up, you have become an adult, and you can decide everything that belongs to you. That's the biggest difference. So you can decide the pattern and appearance of the relationship you want, such as what kind of pattern you hope to have with the opposite sex. Do you trust others? Not afraid of being hurt for no reason? Or just like being with the same sex, more casual. With direction and goals, you can muster the courage to try. It just takes time, and it takes slowly overcoming your unconscious fear or even fear emotions. Similarly, it is necessary to deal with the relationship with your father at the right time. This involves some rules and phenomena at a deeper psychological level. We know it is easy, but it is difficult to do because the past experiences have left emotional energy in our deeper hearts. We need to face and deal with it in order to truly no longer be affected. I'll teach you some attempts to make changes at different levels. First, when dealing with the opposite sex, when you have emotions of distrust or even fear that you used to have, try to detach yourself from these emotions and the other person. Tell yourself that it has nothing to do with the other person, it's just the influence of your relationship with your father that makes you feel this way. So I can interact with the other person normally. Second, when you see your father or talk on the phone, try to have deep communication with him and express your true emotions and feelings. If possible, you can gradually break the deadlock in your relationship with your father and move towards the direction you want. Third, if the second method is too difficult or even difficult to achieve, it is recommended to seek professional psychological counseling to directly assist you in dealing with your relationship with your father. Keep it up, OP!

Actually, from start to finish, you didn't notice one thing, that is, the hat your so-called father bought to show off to you. For your father, a plain hat represents your growth, your understanding, and your love for your parents. When you explained why you didn't believe me, did you ever carefully observe your father's trembling lips or his silent expression? I guess at that moment, your mind was filled with anger, but you didn't know what your father wanted to say at that moment. He believed in you, he wanted to teach you and protect you from being bullied outside when you grow up, in his own way. Maybe some of his methods were wrong, but his intentions came from love for you. Who among us is perfect, let alone our own father? Have you ever thought about the school fees that they paid for your education? They saved money and even refused to buy themselves new clothes, all for the sake of you and your sister's education. We never saw or experienced their hardships, but we should empathize instead of complaining blindly. Regarding your father changing your college application without consulting you, it was indeed wrong. But have you ever tried to see things from his perspective? Maybe at that time, your father believed that the chosen major was good and he didn't want you to regret it in the future, so he changed it for you. It was definitely a mistake, but did your father pay for your miscellaneous fees when you went to school? So as children, we should talk to our parents more often. Maybe then, incidents like changing college applications against our will wouldn't happen. Cherish the present and love your parents well, because when you start working, you will have less and less time to be with them. By that time, your parents will be old, and the time spent with you will also be limited. The tree desires tranquility but the wind continues to blow, and the child desires to support their parents but they are no longer there. Don't let such regrets happen to us, because everyone will have regrets!

You have analyzed it very thoroughly, but you lack a spiritual connection with your father, failing to absorb the masculine energy from him, resulting in unfamiliarity, resistance, and inability to accept men. It will be difficult for you to have smooth romantic relationships in the future, and even if you get married, it will be hard to be intimate with your spouse. You need to delve deeply into what is hindering your spiritual connection with your father. After healing your father-daughter relationship, you will be able to communicate with men normally. Please follow this account.

question: Is it my fault to ask my parents for money when they can't afford to send me to tutoring classes?
description: Tutoring fees range from 15,570 to 22,200. However, my parents' combined monthly income is less than 5,000. But if I attend tutoring classes, it's the only way I can possibly improve my scores and avoid having a second-tier educational background for the rest of my life. I am a science student and the teacher's instruction is really inadequate. I can't learn anything at school. I don't know how to communicate this with my parents. Thank you for your response.
keywords: Family, family relationships, the process of growing up, communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: Wanting to improve oneself is a sign of progress and a positive thing, but it is not necessary to pressure your parents. If you explain the advantages and disadvantages clearly and your parents still choose not to borrow money to support you, don't feel discouraged. Because after completing undergraduate studies, there are still graduate studies, and after graduate studies, there are still doctoral studies. Life is like a marathon, and a temporary setback doesn't mean a complete loss. Let's try to understand each other. If you are truly determined to make progress, take action to push yourself. Put in your best effort, regardless of whether you receive external help. If your parents see your hard work, they may be willing to do their best for you as well. However, if you are not putting in the effort yourself and only rely on your parents' hard work, even attending tutoring classes may not guarantee good results. And even if you succeed this time, it doesn't mean your life will be successful, as accomplishments gained through others are not permanent. One's character often has a greater impact on their life than achievements.

Poster, hello, we need to first accept what already exists in the environment. When considering a new environment, we need to think about whether we can afford the corresponding costs. From your description, I can sense that you are experiencing conflicts and confusion due to the issue of paying for tutoring classes with your parents. You feel upset and unsure. From your perspective, you want to improve your education, but the school environment and the quality of education cannot meet your needs. Therefore, you want to attend tutoring classes and believe this is the only way, so you hope your parents can support you and borrow money. From your parents' perspective, the financial resources of the family are limited and they cannot afford the corresponding fees. They may also worry about whether this money is "worth it" and that the family's living standard may decline significantly. You may think that borrowing money for your education is "necessary" or reasonable, while your parents believe that your academic performance can improve through your own efforts and it is not "necessary" to spend so much money, which could put financial strain on the family. You can communicate and talk to your parents seriously, tell them your motivations and needs, and assure them that your grades will improve after attending the tutoring classes (however, the effectiveness of tutoring classes for you is still uncertain and you still need to work hard yourself). Hopefully, they can understand and support you. At the same time, you can discuss with your parents whether there are other tutoring classes with good teaching quality and lower costs. Sometimes, only when you become independent can you truly appreciate the value of essentials in life. I believe you also understand the hardships and efforts your parents have made for you, so you must work hard. If the school's education is not sufficient, there are always classmates with good grades, so you can learn from them. But ultimately, you still need to work extremely hard, think positively, not be afraid of hardships, and focus on your studies if you really want to improve your education. Good luck.

Yes, there is not a direct correlation between attending tutoring classes and academic performance. Attending a prestigious university or being in a top-ranked institution is not a prerequisite for experiencing happiness. Additionally, the cost of attending tutoring classes is quite high. Our oldest child decided not to take the college entrance exam and is satisfied with their choice. Our second child was accepted into a top-ranked institution without any tutoring classes. Both of them performed well without attending any tutoring. Everyone has their own unique path, and as adults, we cannot force our parents' expectations onto us. One should focus on self-improvement. Best wishes to you.

question: 29-year-old male, recently has developed an interest in using social networking apps to seek sexual encounters. Is this psychologically normal?
description: 29-year-old man, recently found some free time and developed a liking for engaging in sexual activities on social media platforms?! Previously (rarely masturbated during high school, but watched adult films, also did it during the summers of 2016 and 2018, now for the past six months), he would use his hand when feeling idle and would experience sexual urges upon seeing attractive women in his community. However, he knows that it is not appropriate to act on those urges, so he turns to social media platforms to engage in sexual activities, share non-explicit private photos, or eventually engage in video calls with women he has known for a while. He is aware that relying on his hand frequently is not healthy, but he can't resist the desire. Does he have a psychological problem? Do other men or women also use their hands frequently for this purpose? Are there many men or women like him?

answers.answer_text: Kneading is allowed as long as it does not harm the other person. However, try not to engage in kneading with strangers during video chats. On one hand, there is a concern that you may develop an addiction to it, and on the other hand, it poses a risk to your privacy and security. Because you never know who is on the other side of the screen, be cautious of being threatened, blackmailed, or asked for money through screen recording or screenshots. As for using your hands, both boys and girls will use their hands to address this issue, which is considered normal behavior. However, pay attention to the frequency and limit it to 1-2 times a week. Excessive frequency can harm the brain, lead to addiction, and the belief that it is harmless to the body online is self-deception. If you are already addicted, it is recommended that you redirect your attention to other activities. Engaging in exercise or physical labor can help expend energy. I hope the above answers are helpful to you. Best wishes.

question: What should I do if I feel that the person I am dating does not love me enough?
description: The person I am dating has a previous girlfriend who he was in a relationship with for three years. He still has her name tattooed on his body and has talked about covering it up, but he hasn't done it yet. We've been together for eight months and I feel like he doesn't love me as much as he loved her. Sometimes when we're together, he will hum songs, and there are two instances where the lyrics he hummed made a deep impression on me. One time in July, he hummed "Just let go, stop thinking about her" twice, once in front of me and once when he thought I couldn't hear him. And just the other day, he hummed "Love even more what you can't obtain." Whenever he sings these lyrics in front of me, he always adds a following line like "No, that's not it" or "Why am I singing this," maybe because he's afraid I would overthink it. Actually, seeing his tattoo always makes me sad, but I don't want to force him to cover it up. Maybe his ex truly left a permanent pain in his heart.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! I can sense your emotions. Most of us have had a few relationships before finding the right one. Each relationship may be long or short, deep or superficial, but in the end, they become part of the past. Many people believe that what they can't have is better, but what you have now is more deserving of appreciation. Your boyfriend had a three-year relationship with his ex-girlfriend, and it takes time to forget someone. Regarding the tattoo, have you discussed your thoughts and feelings with him? If you let him know that it would hurt you to see his tattoo and that you don't want to see reminders of other women on him, even if it doesn't need to be covered with your name, you hope he can remove it as soon as possible. If he cares about you, he will make time to handle it promptly. As for the songs he likes to sing, maybe they have lyrics that remind him of the past, and he has grown accustomed to them. I don't think you should worry too much about this sensitivity as it will only compound your sadness. If you have expressed your thoughts to him and he still refuses to remove the tattoo, I think you should reconsider your relationship. I hope you find the happiness you desire.

How did you and your boyfriend meet and decide to fall in love initially? Where does the feeling of "not feeling loved enough" come from? Is it because he has a tattoo of his ex-girlfriend's name and still keeps it? Is it because he sings "let go, don't think about her" and "love even more when you can't get it"? What is your standard of "enough"? Are you using his love for his ex-girlfriend as a reference? If you use his love for his ex-girlfriend as a reference, I feel like you're already at a disadvantage in terms of momentum. Love is exclusive, but the condition is to not dwell on the past that has already happened. Maybe you're not really sure if your boyfriend is the right person for you? Whether he's worth your emotional investment? Perhaps you are not so certain about your own feelings either. That's why you need to bring up the ex-girlfriend to talk about the relationship between you and your boyfriend. On a rational level, you want your boyfriend to forget about his ex-girlfriend, but subconsciously, it seems like you want him to not forget about her so quickly. Just imagine, if one day you and your boyfriend broke up, would you want him to constantly think about you like he does with his ex-girlfriend now, or would you want him to forget about you as soon as possible? The fact that your boyfriend could walk away from his ex-girlfriend and come to you means that you possess qualities that his ex-girlfriend doesn't have, qualities that attract your boyfriend. Believe in yourself and be content with being yourself. Never lose the confidence to be yourself, no matter when.

question: Cannot maintain focus to complete a task, how can one be more focused?
description: I always have trouble maintaining focus on one task and often get distracted or daydream.
keywords: Growth, character improvement, self-development, work and study.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, you often struggle to focus on one thing and find your attention easily getting diverted, which leads to distress. Here are some suggestions for you: 1. Clarify the purpose of the task. Before starting something, it is important to understand your motivation and the purpose behind why you are doing it. Only with a clear motivation can you find the drive to complete the task. 2. Cultivate indirect interest in the task. Interest is the best teacher, but we often lack interest in things we have to do. Therefore, we need to find ways to cultivate indirect interest in the task through various methods. 3. Organize activities properly. When working on a task, it is necessary to find a balance between work and rest, allocate time for work and studying, and plan for breaks. Learn to relax and allow your brain to rest so that you can concentrate better. 4. Avoid distractions from unrelated factors. If you decide to do something, create a quiet and organized environment, turn off your phone or disconnect from the internet, and avoid distractions from unrelated factors. Lastly, you can also train your attention through games and activities. Best wishes~.

question: "What should a counselor do when a client has sexual fantasies about the counselor during a therapy session?"
description: There is a male client who, during his first counseling session, said that he is easily agitated and cannot calm down, often feeling the urge to become angry. During his second session, he revealed to me that he feels psychologically abnormal and imagines me as his sexual partner. He feels ashamed of these thoughts but cannot control them. Before his second session, he asked me out, but I politely declined. During our conversation, he shared his psychological experiences with me. In response, I told him that his subconscious thoughts are not his fault and he has not done anything wrong. I advised him to face these thoughts without judging them as right or wrong because they are not his own thoughts. He mentioned that he will gradually try to adjust, but he cannot guarantee his mental stability. I reiterated my previous point and subtly implied to him that he is still a strong and optimistic young man who would not harm himself or his family. I encouraged him to have faith in himself, and assured him that I believe in him as well. We have not spoken since then. How should I handle this situation, and what should I do if he brings up the topic again someday?

answers.answer_text: I have also encountered this problem before. It is the transference of the visitor towards you. Actually, it's perfectly fine to discuss this issue openly. Sexual fantasies can have various reasons. It may be a need for love and understanding, or perhaps a certain action or piece of clothing triggered their defense mechanism. The problem itself is not about sexual fantasies, nor is it about shame. When their inner needs are exposed, these feelings will disappear. It will be a significant transformation for the visitor. Of course, it cannot be ruled out that the counselor themselves are very charming and can handle the visitor with ease and humor.

question: Being a full-time mom every day, but still not doing well, what does it take to be a qualified mother?
description: What does it mean to be a qualified mother? Even though I spend all day with my child, I still feel like I'm not being a good mother. Is it really so difficult to be a qualified mother?
keywords: Family, family relationships, growing up process.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the topic is hello, being a full-time mom is not easy, hard work, give you a full hug! What is the standard of a good mother? For children, the requirements of each child are different. "Being a full-time mom every day, but still not being a good mother" can be seen that the topic has put all her heart and soul into her child, but the final result is still unsatisfactory. The result of the hard work is that the child thinks that the mother is incompetent or the mother thinks that she is incompetent, or other family members think so? To be honest, being a full-time mom is not easy to be a qualified mother. 1. Moms need to learn, learn parenting concepts, and finally practice. 2. Keep up with the pace of the children. The education of children is the biggest problem. Learn the development rules of children and be a good life mentor for children, influencing life with life. 3. In addition to taking care of life and learning, we must also cultivate personality and quality. 4. The most important thing is that mothers should be themselves. Even full-time mothers cannot lose themselves. I wish you can successfully be a good mother!

question: Being talked about by others is distressing, and I wonder why there is such a discrepancy between what I think and what I actually do.
description: I have experienced betrayal from friends and feel that my family no longer cares about me. I am afraid to trust anyone easily and am often misunderstood. I don't want to explain myself and often feel like being alone. It hurts me when others gossip about me, and it is difficult for me to bear it emotionally.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, psychological counseling, psychological assessment

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner. It feels as if we are face to face right now. I am truly sorry for your current state. Actually, you can also perceive that you haven't completely lost faith in the external environment. You yearn to have good friends and for your family to care about you. However, due to experiencing betrayal from friends and feeling that your family doesn't care about you, you may have developed a sense of disappointment towards the outside world. But can simply adopting a negative approach truly protect yourself? I don't think so. Moreover, just because you have experienced betrayal from friends, does that mean all friends are like that? So, sometimes it may be helpful to step out of this framework, allowing yourself to express your emotions and engage in positive actions to explore whether this negative perception is really as you think it is. By focusing on positive actions that can be accomplished, one can address negative experiences. Our brains are inherently biased towards negativity. For survival, the brain amplifies any negative emotions and information, helping humans avoid harm as much as possible. However, the downside of this physiological design is that people can let their emotions be influenced by excessive attention to negative information, and as a result, lose courage to live their lives. Therefore, you should first understand and accept your current negative state. At the same time, you should also understand that it is not irreversible. For example, believing that your family no longer cares about you has caused you great negative experiences. But is it true that your family no longer cares about you? Where did we perceive that they no longer care about you? This is something to consider, and even communicate about. By exploring a certain aspect of your perception, you can truly obtain real answers from reality, rather than panicking and speculating. Being betrayed by friends does indeed make it easy for one to fall into distrust towards friendship. But not all friends will betray you. The person who betrayed you did so based on their own values and standards. "If the person you are facing shows unwarranted discrimination or exclusion towards you, it only reflects their values and standards, and it actually has nothing to do with the person being discriminated against." Allow yourself to vent your emotions. Actively suppressing your emotions to cater to the preferences of others doesn't actually help you become a likable person. It makes you feel repressed and gradually lose your own personality traits. In order to have close and good relationships, first you need to become an independent person, someone who has their own boundaries and can control their own emotions. So when emotions arise, it is still important to bravely express them, and express your anger to those who have hurt you. This way, your energy will expand outward instead of inwardly attacking yourself. You are a little mushroom that hopes for a gentle world and also needs time to grow freely.

Hello, dear questioner! I have a habit of not easily speaking ill of others. Does that mean the other person is perfect? Of course not. We are all selfish creatures. The reason we don't speak ill of others is mostly because we hope that they won't speak ill of us behind our backs. But how is that possible? Everyone will be talked about, betrayed, or deceived by others... Matters of the heart are really complicated, and a few sentences or even thousands of words will not explain it clearly. You mentioned feeling like your family doesn't care about you, which might be due to your sensitivity. Most parents love their children very much. You said you enjoy being alone, which is normal. Personally, I think being alone allows you to contemplate many issues and improve your thinking ability. People who enjoy being alone have more character and are not easily influenced by others. When you feel upset, try going for a walk or doing something to keep yourself busy instead of keeping it all inside. Being idle and having an empty mind can easily lead to boredom and sadness. In short, be more confident, don't be afraid of getting hurt in relationships, and don't constantly overthink. Use your spare time to do things you enjoy, and things will get better. You can also talk to your parents more and open up to them. Many problems have solutions. Good luck!

Hello, have you ever experienced betrayal from a friend? The word "betrayal" is your own definition of a rupture in your relationship with your friend. When you put the word "betrayal" back into the context at that time, think again whether it was really betrayal or something else! If you feel that your family is no longer concerned about you, it may just be your own perception. So what is the reality? How do you define concern? Is it appropriate care or excessive attention? Is it about them nagging you or the need for more communication with yourself? You need to tell your family the kind of family interaction you like and be open to their objections, and then together come up with a mode that everyone can enjoy. Not daring to trust anyone easily, who does "anyone" specifically refer to? Relatives, friends, or colleagues? If it's just strangers, I wouldn't trust them easily either, because strangers have no connection to us! So what does this "anyone" specifically refer to? Being misunderstood and not wanting to explain, misunderstandings happen every day, and explaining can indeed be troublesome. Time will prove everything. However, some misunderstandings must be explained immediately and clearly, especially regarding personal character, because rumors can be really scary. Sometimes I really want to be alone. Solitude is the beginning of maturity, and in the end, it's a process of playing with oneself. When you comfort yourself and make yourself happy, you become happy. Being talked about by others and feeling uneasy in your heart, but you're too lazy to explain, why should you feel uneasy? Obviously, you care, and if you care, you should speak up for yourself... As I always say, a person has a thousand faces when dealing with others, how I treat you depends on how you treat me.

question: I feel that the teacher who does the psychological counseling is not quite suitable for me.
description: I found a mental health teacher to accompany me through the most difficult journey. However, at the beginning, there were quite a few settings on the platform, so I paid for multiple counseling sessions in advance. But later on, I felt that the teacher was not suitable for me during the counseling sessions. I'm not sure if it's possible to cancel the order and get a refund on the platform.

answers.answer_text: It should be fine. In addition, it is best to pay for each consultation individually next time, as it is more beneficial for the counseling process. The payment process for each session is meaningful and worth discussing. If you pay for multiple sessions at once, you will miss out on good opportunities for discussion.
