The setting of counseling fees is an important indicator of professionalism. I am not sure who initially proposed paying for multiple sessions at once, but if it was you, we need to discuss and understand the underlying needs behind this payment method. If it was the counselor's suggestion, I think it needs to be reconsidered.

question: Why do I always lack my own opinion when others have different thoughts?
description: Why is it that whenever I encounter a problem, I start to waver in my previous thoughts? Just a few words from others can change my mindset and make me conform to their ideas. When others have different opinions, I become indecisive and anxious inside.

answers.answer_text: I feel that you are somewhat blaming yourself, and you are also very confused about why you always lack assertiveness. First, I would like to invite you to try to explore your own thoughts: When you say that you waver in your previous thoughts when faced with a problem, does it mean that when you try to express your opinions and you find some errors or difficulties in the process of expression, you would want to change your viewpoint? When others have different opinions, does it make you feel flustered? Is this flustered feeling caused by fear of being different from others? Or is it due to conflicting with others? Or is it a fear of being invalidated or refuted by others? Lastly, I want to tell you that it is normal to have differences with others. Everyone has different perspectives, so your thoughts are also precious. Next time, you can try to express yourself boldly. I hope this helps you.

question: 17, the heart is like a stagnant water without any ripples, how can it be changed?
description: Lately, I feel like my cognitive abilities have declined. Emotions like happiness, sadness, and anger seem to be fleeting and superficial, and I don't even know if they have actually occurred. I have no desires or ambitions, and my heart feels stagnant, as if my life only exists in the present and the future. I don't reminisce about the past or look forward to the future. This feeling has been with me constantly, and I usually feel gloomy. I don't consciously feel much, but the thought of it only leads to fatigue and slight irritability. This situation has left me without motivation, and even though I know what consequences this state could lead to, I remain stuck in simply being aware of it. I go through the motions of studying mechanically every day, but my heart lacks any feeling or investment. I only know to fill my time with actions, without considering efficiency or quality. I can't seem to recapture the feeling of willingly learning from morning till night. In my daily interactions with those around me, everything feels unrelated to me. No one knows what's going on inside me, and I don't feel like sharing. I want to change this lifeless state; I'm only 17, yet I already feel like I've lost my passion.

answers.answer_text: The opposite of depression is vitality. You just lack vitality. Grab everything you love. No matter how much time it takes to find, no matter how different it is from this world. Finding what you love is finding yourself. Love yourself well. Don't be afraid to be honest with yourself because of the fear that others won't accept it. (Communicate with your parents.)

People's energy fluctuates, their mental energy rises and falls like tides, and I believe this is a common state for many people. The fast-paced lifestyle leaves one feeling empty, confused, and lost. Depression, a mental cold, occurs when the immune system of the mind weakens. I believe that improving mental immunity can be approached from three aspects: 🤔1. Focus on your inner self and learn to appreciate yourself. Encourage yourself or have your best friend compliment you. It's also good to drink some spiritual chicken soup. Take a look at other people's difficulties; there is nothing new under the sun. There are people who are experiencing your pain and feeling what you feel. Some have already overcome similar difficulties, so see if there are any experiences you can learn from. 🤔2. Take care of your body and mind as one. Pay attention to your physical health, maintain a regular schedule, have a balanced diet, and engage in moderate exercise. 🤔3. Restore your mental energy. If you still have some interests or hobbies, draw strength from them. If not, try writing a journal to sort out your inner journey. Have a chat with someone, watch variety shows, listen to comedy sketches, or talk to a professional counselor. Best wishes~ To gather energy during ebb tide and strive during high tide is the only way to thrive continually.

question: Lately, I've been under a lot of stress. Whenever I think about something upsetting, I feel like crying, and when something makes me happy, I feel like laughing.
description: Sometimes my mood is bad, and other times I feel like laughing. When I think of something upsetting, I want to cry, but when something makes me happy, I want to laugh.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Hugs to you~ Every person in life will face stress from various aspects. When feeling tired, take a break, relax, and adjust your mood appropriately. So how do you deal with pressure? The way we interpret and handle stress is more crucial than the stress itself. The same thing, viewed from a different perspective, can be either a burden or a motivation. You can discover the positive aspects of stress, treating it as an opportunity and a challenge for yourself. Facing stress directly, we can choose to escape or courageously confront it. If we keep avoiding it, the problem will always be there. We can wait until our emotions are adjusted and then solve it accordingly. Take it easy, believe that everything will pass. It's helpful to confide in family and friends when feeling overwhelmed and in a bad mood. Find a quiet place to talk and chat with them. Expressing oneself can lighten the burden. Going for a walk can take a break from work and go out for a walk, get close to nature, go hiking, cycling, or just explore the surroundings. Temporary distance from stress allows the mind and body to relax. Wishing you can get rid of your worries and live a happy and joyful life~.

Hello. I think your current state isn't too bad, and you still have positive thoughts. Personally, when I'm under a lot of stress, I usually only think of negative things. You should now identify the sources of your stress and analyze what is causing it. Is it from external factors or is it self-imposed? Most of the time, stress comes from within ourselves. I recently came across a saying: Our troubles and pain are not caused by the things themselves, but by the interpretations we attach to them. Reflect on recent events and determine if our perception of them is causing our stress. If so, adjust your mindset. Often, we give too much importance to things, making them more complicated than they actually are. If the stress is caused by external factors, then adapt yourself to deal with the impact from the outside. Since you can still think of positive things, engage in activities that bring you joy. Stress needs to be released; bottling it up won't solve the problem. Keep going!

It's like seeing each other in writing ~ The original poster mentioned that they have been under a lot of stress recently. Has something happened? I want to give the original poster a big warm hug ~ If the original poster is willing, they can talk about the source of their stress. I am willing to listen. If the original poster doesn't want to talk, they can write down their thoughts with pen and paper, describing the things that are causing them stress and their feelings about it. Or, if you like drawing, you can illustrate your feelings. The original poster mentioned their current state as follows: "Feeling bad one moment, and feeling like laughing the next. Crying when thinking about something upsetting, and smiling when something makes you happy." We are all the same; we will always encounter happy or upsetting things. Allow yourself to cry freely when you feel like it, and laugh wholeheartedly when you are happy. There is nothing wrong with that. Accept your emotions, whether they are good or "bad." After accepting them, if you are willing, you can also think about why something makes you happy or upset. Do you have any problems that need to be addressed? How will you solve them? We will accompany you through the screen - keep going!

Sorry for the late response. I'm curious how you're feeling now? From your description, it seems like your reactions are quite normal - feeling like crying when something bad happens and wanting to laugh when something good happens. However, it may be a bit concerning when these emotions switch rapidly and make it difficult for you to adapt. Maybe we can understand your needs and make adjustments based on the state you desire. Lastly, I want to emphasize that everything we do now is for the future, as the past is already behind us.

question: Depression seems to have made me feel neither human nor ghostly. How can I possibly regulate myself?
description: I am a junior college student majoring in literature and I feel increasingly depressed. Many times, I can even resonate with the tragic characters in literary works, and I become more and more withdrawn. I used to enjoy writing sad texts, but instead of finding solace, I sink deeper and deeper, identifying myself with those characters and becoming less and less social. I immerse myself in my own world. I have also started experiencing insomnia and low mood. I feel like I used to be a cheerful person in middle school, but now that I am in college, I feel like I hardly talk or interact with people, and I can only express my emotions through writing. So, I want to ask whether this persistent manifestation of depression can affect my appearance? How can I change this?
keywords: Therapy, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You have strong empathetic abilities and often resonate with tragic stories. (2) You used to be cheerful but now you've become unhappy. (3) You are worried that this depression might manifest outwardly and you want to make a change. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: (1) First, you possess a strong empathetic ability, which allows you to often resonate with literary works. This helps you understand the deeper meaning behind these works, but such intense empathy has started to affect your own life. Additionally, since the texts you read are sad, it seems you've fallen into a self-created cycle of sadness, finding it difficult to break free and sinking even deeper. (2) Secondly, you used to be cheerful but underwent a change in university. Is it because of the change in environment or the literary atmosphere you are currently in? I suggest you make full use of your empathetic ability and read some positive literary works, placing yourself in a more positive environment so you can gradually adapt. (3) Lastly, long-term depressive moods can potentially lead to symptoms of depression or outward behaviors. I recommend seeking professional help from a school counselor or therapist to receive specialized intervention and guidance. #The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

question: It is easy to feel nervous during exams, resulting in a blank mind and even trembling hands. How can this be improved?
description: From a young age, I have cared a lot about the achievements I have made and have a strong desire to prove myself. Usually, I am fine, but when it comes to formal exams or competitions, my mind goes blank with nervousness. I even tremble, and my actual performance often differs greatly from my expectations. When I was younger, I used to get very anxious while waiting for exam results, fearing that they would not meet my standards. This also happened when I participated as a seeded player in table tennis tournaments. Now, as I approach the high school entrance examination, I am experiencing the same thing. I would like to know the reasons behind this and if there are others who have had similar experiences. How can I improve?
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, treatment methods, trauma treatment.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Your learning ability is pretty good, and you usually study hard and are good at understanding knowledge and skills. However, every time you have a major test or competition, you feel nervous and anxious, and your mind goes blank, causing you to not perform well. Is that right? There are two key factors to achieve good results in tests or competitions: one is the level of regular learning and skill mastery, and the other is the mental state or psychological qualities during the test. Both are essential. However, in China, many students, including myself when I was a student, and maybe you as well, have decent skills but struggle with poor mental resilience in the test environment. Why is that? It's because we care too much about the outcome. We feel superior only when we achieve good results, and our self-esteem and self-confidence suffer if the results are not satisfactory. Once our self-esteem is undermined, we feel a kind of death anxiety. We don't study because we enjoy it, or out of curiosity, or for the pleasure of acquiring knowledge; we study out of fear, self-centeredness, and the desire for superior results. Think about it, if we approach tests with a mindset of "fear of death and escaping for survival," our mental state will definitely collapse and our mind will go blank. How can we alleviate this? First, we need to reduce the importance we place on the test results. It doesn't mean we shouldn't care about the results, but we should lower the significance of test results from a matter of "life or death" to a measure of our regular learning. Second, focus on controlling what is within our control. Test results are not entirely in our control. What we can control is solid preparation and doing our best to answer the questions in the test. Third, we can improve our mental resilience through frequent simulation exercises. By simulating tests, we can become familiar with the test environment and also identify and address our weaknesses in regular studying. When our foundation is solid, it will help stabilize our mental state during major tests. One test or competition does not determine our whole life, and performing well in one test does not necessarily prove our superiority. True learning is ongoing and a process. Let go of your fear, and I hope you can enjoy the test experience!

Hello! Your analysis of the beginning of the sentence is very good. You care too much about grades, rankings, and what others think of you, to the point where you become excessively anxious about exams and only focus on the future results. Consequently, you are unable to fully concentrate during exams, resulting in unsatisfactory grades. Test anxiety is a common issue among most students. After all, it has a significant impact on our future. Moderate nervousness can put us in a sprint mode, with heightened concentration and full focus on the exam process, leading to the best results. Excessive nervousness, however, can cause a blank mind and an inability to concentrate and complete the exam. During the exam, before it begins, focus your attention on your breathing. Concentrate on your own breathing, and after a few minutes, your whole body will relax. You can also practice deep breathing exercises, and after doing them 3-5 times, you will start to feel more relaxed. Once the exam starts, shift your attention to answering the questions. Regardless of the outcome, the process is important. Take each step seriously so that you can strive for the best results. It's worth noting that practicing deep breathing exercises is great for relaxation and it's beneficial to prepare yourself in advance.

question: What should I do with masturbation addiction? It particularly affects my studies.
description: Every day, my mind is filled with thoughts of sexual things. Whenever I'm in class, I suddenly get distracted and start thinking about such things. It greatly affects my ability to concentrate and learn.

answers.answer_text: I hope the following information can help you: Are you a teenager? It is common to experience strong sexual desires during this stage of development. However, due to traditional cultural values and beliefs about sexuality, many teenagers have misconceptions and misunderstandings about the process of sexual development. For example, there is the idea of being addicted to masturbation, the belief that masturbation is harmful, the notion that a drop of sperm is equivalent to ten drops of blood, and the belief that masturbation has significant negative effects on the body. In reality, we should acknowledge and accept our sexual desires as a natural part of being human, similar to eating. So, what's wrong with masturbation? Masturbation can actually help relieve sexual desires and reduce stress. There is no such thing as excessive masturbation, as it varies for each individual depending on their own physical condition. Therefore, there is no need to make a big deal out of it. As for addiction, the term "addiction" implies a disease. Is it a disease? Clearly not. So, accept it, masturbate when you feel the need, and focus on your studies the rest of the time. The so-called psychological mechanism of addiction is being afraid of excessive masturbation, which leads to anxiety, and then the need to masturbate for relief, thus creating a cycle. ε Wishing you a happy National Day. The world and I love you.

question: The child is still young, and my wife and I have been living apart for 10 months. How can I win back my wife and save our family?
description: Because the communication between my wife and I was not very good during our time together, I slowly began to suspect that she might be having an affair. My suspicions led to us living separately for ten months, and on October 3rd, during a face-to-face meeting, my wife verbally expressed her desire for a divorce. How can I salvage this family and win back my wife?
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, relationship management, mother-in-law and son-in-law.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner. I can tell that you are very confused about how to reconcile your family and don't know what to do. I really sympathize with your current situation. According to your description, your suspicion of your wife having an affair has led to your separation. Although I don't know the exact details of your relationship, at present, you have a suspicious opinion about this matter. As a woman, your wife values her reputation, and it is not appropriate to make accusations without concrete evidence. Perhaps you can gather evidence first and then discuss this matter with her. It may be that her decision to separate from you is also for the sake of her reputation. If you are determined to save your wife and your family, I suggest seeking help from other family members or relatives. Appeal to her emotions and reason with her. After fully understanding her views, explain to her the importance of parents' participation in the child's future and the need to provide the child with a complete family. Perhaps these factors can change her mind.

question: 25-year-old female, why do I always feel like my partner is tired of me in the past year?
description: In the past, we used to argue and fight, but recently the fights have become worse. Divorce is often mentioned. He has changed the password for everything on his phone, and I don't know any of them. He says it's nothing. But why lock it up and not let me know? He even says he's tired of our life together. I don't know if the problem is with me or with them. It's giving me a headache. I can't eat or sleep well. I want to communicate with him, but he always avoids it by saying he doesn't want to talk to me.

answers.answer_text: Hello: I see that you have made some efforts in this relationship. Do you hope that your relationship can be improved? In that case, you need to pay more attention to what you can do to make the other person willing to communicate with you on this issue. I suggest you think back to how you used to get along happily. Can you find that happy way of getting along again and make your relationship more harmonious?

question: How can I forget the nightmares of my childhood that I don't want to remember anymore? I'm 35 years old now.
description: When I was 7 years old, I was raped by a teacher. It was really painful, and there was a lot of bleeding. Now, at the age of 35, I still think about it every day. How can I forget?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. The childhood painful memory is unforgettable until now, and OP also wants to walk out of this pain, but cannot forget it, and does not know how to forget these things. [Analysis and suggestions] 1. Emotions and feelings sometimes accompany events, but they will not disappear if not dealt with, they will only be buried in the heart like an unremovable thorn. When OP encountered that thing in childhood, did OP tell the family? Did OP report it? Did the teacher involved receive punishment? If not, it is normal for this heart knot to exist for so many years. On the one hand, the person involved did not receive the punishment they deserved, on the other hand, OP alone bears this feeling of repression and pain. 2. fundamentally, OP is in a victim's position in this kind of thing, and may consider speaking out about this to mom or trusted family members, telling them about their inner pain and grievances. After emotional release, it will feel better. If these emotions seriously affect OP's learning and work life, it is still advisable for OP to seek professional help to deal with this kind of childhood trauma.

question: Being mocked by classmates for as long as two years, it has led to post-traumatic stress. How can one self-rescue from this situation?
description: Because of appearance issues during high school adolescence, I was overweight and formed a fake relationship with another male classmate who shared the same concerns as me. We were teased and ridiculed by our classmates for up to two years. Due to my submissive personality, I endured it and didn't express my feelings or discuss it with my parents, who didn't consider it a big deal and took no action. As a result, I have long lacked self-confidence in my appearance and even developed post-traumatic stress. I would enter a negative mental state, feeling mentally tense and fearful for 3 to 4 days when encountering certain triggers, such as the name of the boy or certain scenarios. This has had a long-term impact on my academic performance and mindset, leading to lack of confidence, lazy behavior, and learned helplessness. I am currently deeply trapped in a state of low self-esteem. The problem is that although the adolescence phase has passed, this incident still deeply affects my current life. It prevents me from getting into a state of flow during studying, resulting in low efficiency and a diminished sense of happiness in life.
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Sending you warm hugs. Experiencing bullying at school, such as being mocked, subjected to verbal violence, and facing aesthetic bullying, can be extremely painful and have a negative impact. It may take time to process and overcome the pain and effects of these negative experiences. The trauma you mentioned, where certain words or scenes associated with the name of a male student trigger negative psychological states of anxiety and fear, can lead to negative associations and flashbacks. Therefore, it would be beneficial to work on blocking negative associations and desensitizing yourself to past incidents, in addition to utilizing other coping measures for better results. Entangled in trauma-induced stress during high school and adolescence, being teased for appearance and weight, enduring class-wide mockery without timely expression or retaliation, long-term lack of confidence in appearance, and adopting behaviors of laziness and helplessness have all been influenced by the ongoing effects of that trauma. It may be necessary to seek professional help to address these past experiences. Your low learning efficiency and lack of happiness in life indicate that the trauma from the past is affecting your life. It would be best to conduct a comprehensive and systematic review, breaking away from past experiences and establishing new positive associations. Although those past events occurred, they inflicted a certain amount of trauma on you, and it seems like the pain from that verbal violence trauma still lingers. It would be helpful to attempt a new relationship with that period of history. Regarding post-traumatic stress disorder, cognitive reprocessing and dialectical behavioral therapy are recommended. The unstable emotional state you are experiencing seems to have a negative impact on your adaptation to life. As long as you are willing, there are still plenty of opportunities to re-engage with the outside world. When negative flashbacks occur, remind yourself that you are now safe and that those past events were the fault of others, not yours. Amidst the chaotic world, it is crucial to maintain inner resilience when dealing with setbacks. Under the motivation of cultivating empathy, warm yourself and engage with the world. Now, try to consider the things that worry or concern you, including traumatic events. If anxiety arises, silently repeat in your mind: "This is just the way the world is, constantly changing and separating. I am capable of protecting myself now." Additionally, keep objects that make you feel safe nearby as reminders, slowly dissipate the stress and flashbacks, and seek ways to reduce adaptation pressure. All you need to do is change your thoughts and responses to upcoming sources of stress. The past may be unchangeable, but you can restructure how you deal with it. Human vitality is strong. With persistent practice, you can reap great benefits that will enable you to tackle future difficulties. Therefore, resilience demonstrates that you care about your inner feelings and have the confidence to handle them, as well as accumulating courage and positive experiences within yourself. If possible, it is recommended to seek psychological counseling.

Well, if I'm fat, so what? I'm not eating your food anyway. Why should others worry when I don't? As a chubby person, I have indeed faced some criticism regarding my body shape and height. However, we can take a dialectical view of things, as ultimately, nothing is more important than our health. I remember during high school, my height was only around 1.5 meters, which was looked down upon in the male community. Walking around school, people often mistook me for a middle schooler, and it felt really uncomfortable. Especially during break time or when queuing, I was put in the girls' line several times, and I can't express how disheartening that felt. Later, when I vented my feelings online, someone told me that height is something we can't control, but our body shape and abilities can be changed by ourselves. So I slowly understood that certain things are predetermined, like our appearance and height, which is largely influenced by genetics. However, our temperament and the ability we rely on for survival are things we strive for ourselves. Although looks may be a bonus, it doesn't mean it determines everything. Even if we are a little overweight, we can exercise more and as long as our bodies are healthy, being a bit fat doesn't matter. We can't make others stop talking, but our abilities are something they can't take away. Have confidence, and you'll meet the best version of yourself. The world and I love you.

Hello, thank you for sharing! First of all, I think you shouldn't label yourself. We all have our own insecurities — being too fat, too thin, too short, too tall, having poor grades, unattractive appearance, etc. We are born being attacked, and at the same time, we consciously or unconsciously attack others as well. Adler wrote a book called "Inferiority and Superiority," which explains this well. How to transcend these insecurities is the issue at hand. Those who have achieved some level of success and accomplishment are the ones who have figured out this problem. On one hand, if you feel inferior to others, accept it, and then develop another aspect. Our appearance is given to us by our parents, our academic achievements are our own, friends are our own, and the future path is also our own.

question: Different regions, my boyfriend is resistant to the bride price, what should I do?
description: I haven't been with my boyfriend for very long, but we recently discussed marriage. In my family, the bride price is quite high, while his family's is low. The bride price would be four or five years' savings for him. I'm willing to work hard and save up this money, because I know my parents will need this much for the bride price, and there won't be any dowry because my family isn't well off. My parents are expecting this money and counting on me to work and earn it, so my boyfriend is afraid that my family is like a bottomless pit. I feel guilty in my heart. On one hand, I feel sorry for my parents and want to support them in their old age. However, when my parents clearly state that they want me to earn money or when they're just demanding money, I really want to avoid it. I'm willing to treat them well, but when it becomes about demanding, I feel scared. So I told my boyfriend that it's okay if he doesn't have much money, but the bride price is inevitable, and I made it clear that I would earn that money myself. But even what I said made him scared. I'm conflicted. Will he truly love me if I give the bride price money myself? When we weren't together, I mentioned being short on funds inadvertently and said I needed support. He offered, but I refused. But later, when I mentioned lacking money once, he started saying that he doesn't have money either and is reluctant to spend it himself. I'm scared that he might not be worthy of my love. I'm the kind of person who will be good to the person I like without being asked. I'm afraid his family won't agree. I don't know what to do now.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ Many people say that money is the "enemy" of all emotions, that talking about money hurts relationships, and so on. I can feel the inner conflict of the OP. On the one hand, there is the family, on the other hand, there is the beloved person. Faced with financial pressures from both sides, the OP starts to worry about the relationship with the boyfriend. Firstly, I don't know if the OP cares about the custom of dowry. From the OP's description, I feel that parents attach more importance to the dowry as a sense of "security". On the one hand, it's like a guarantee for their old age, and on the other hand, it's also a guarantee from the groom to the bride. This is one of the reasons why dowry exists in China. Therefore, when facing the parents' request for dowry, the OP may first analyze what the parents really want: is it just money for their old age, or do they see the dowry as a proof of the groom's attitude towards this marriage? Then, the OP can respond to their request accordingly. If it's just about money, the OP can directly explain the situation to the parents and express the intention to take care of them as much as possible, but not to be under too much pressure. If it serves another purpose, to prove the groom's attitude towards the marriage, then the OP needs to communicate with the boyfriend. Some people may think that spending money on the other person is a way to test if they truly love you, but my opinion is: everyone has different views on money, and spending money on us doesn't necessarily mean they truly love us. Conversely, not spending money doesn't necessarily mean they don't love us. The important thing is whether the person is willing to take responsibility. As for the difference in views on money, I think the OP can find out through communication with the boyfriend. To know if the other person genuinely treats the OP, it depends on their attitude: mutual understanding should exist between each other.

question: Can a man who has cheated on his partner change his ways and stop cheating?
description: After my boyfriend cheated and asked for forgiveness, I'm slowly starting to alleviate my suspicions. His behavior has been decent, but I've read many articles and comments online saying that once a cheater, always a cheater. However, I also believe that there are no absolutes in life. Are there any cases where someone has stopped cheating after one incident? We both want to enter into marriage. How can we prevent infidelity, or are there any examples or methods that can truly help a wanderer change their ways?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Every relationship is dynamic, and whether or not someone will cheat is related to the person's character as well as the state of your relationship. It also depends on the cost of betraying the relationship. If he is someone who is consistently unfaithful or has a habit of cheating, no matter what you do, he will cheat. If your relationship has many problems and cannot meet each other's emotional needs, and if he cannot find fulfillment through hobbies or contentment with himself, he will seek external means to satisfy his emotional needs, either through physical or emotional infidelity. If the cost of betraying the relationship is low, for example, if he knows that you won't leave no matter how he betrays you, then the likelihood of him cheating will be higher. The most uncontrollable situation can be managed with a set of methods, not that it is impossible, but it will cause mental and physical exhaustion, and you may not necessarily achieve satisfactory results. Instead of trying to control the uncontrollable, it is better to focus on yourself, on how to improve the current state of your relationship, and to focus on the present without fearing the future. Based on the points mentioned above, here are a few suggestions for reference: First, understand what type of person you have chosen. Women who want to change a "wild" man often have a nurturing mindset. The relationship between a nurturing person and a "big baby" is that the nurturing person repeatedly holds onto the hope of a final change, while the "big baby" keeps making "mistakes" to balance the relationship. Analyze whether the person you have chosen is a "big baby" or a "wild" person, and whether you have the mentality to save him or change him. Second, prioritize self-improvement rather than monitoring the other person. Yang Lan said, "A girl should be like a flower, and men will be attracted like butterflies. Instead of constantly pleasing and chasing after the other person, that kind of life is too dreadful." Always prioritize self-value improvement. When you become excellent, beautiful, and charming, even if this man cheats, there will be better ones waiting for you, or you can live well on your own. When you have the confidence and ability to leave him, he will be the one who dares not leave. Third, reduce the weight of love. Since emotional betrayal is a high-risk situation, how can you mitigate the risk or have a better attitude when facing a crisis? That is, reduce the importance of love in your life. When you have many sources of happiness (such as your career, friendships, and interests), and when you are not "ALL IN" on love, even if it fails, you will not fall apart, and your life will not be "ruined." When facing unexpected events, it's better not to try to control them. Shift your focus to yourself. The happier and more confident you become, with a stable sense of self and the confidence to leave, the higher the cost for your boyfriend to lose you, and the more afraid he is of losing you. Only then can he possibly control himself and not destroy the relationship. Not cheating is the result of nurturing yourself and the relationship, not the goal.

It should be possible to change and start fresh, but confessing to an affair can be challenging. Prevention is impossible. Many things rely on self-awareness. Because you cannot watch him 24 hours a day, right? The future is also uncertain. So, all we can do is try to minimize the chances. The future is not absolute, so it is possible that he will not have an affair, but it is also possible that he will continue to have affairs. However, the likelihood of having an affair will definitely increase because the future is longer. I can accurately say that the rate of infidelity is higher for women than men because there are more men than women. Only women are more discreet. So sometimes, you need to educate them on how to reduce the chances. You need to control his finances to some extent. If he has no money, he cannot afford hotel rooms or chase after other women, right? If he wants to have an affair, he will have to live at someone else's place. So, you need to get hold of his work schedule. Know when he rests and when he goes to work. You need to have a clear understanding of his daily life and work routine. And then, it is very important to monitor his business trips because you cannot keep an eye on him during those times, so you must inquire about them. Checking is crucial. I don't need to go into detail about checking his phone, QQ, WeChat, etc., right? Completely avoid him spending the night outside. Discourage him from spending time outside. Every time he goes on a trip or something, exhaust him first. If he has no energy left, how can he go out? It's like going to war, right? Even when he returns, you should check the smell or marks on his pants or clothes. These can be clues to look for. In any case, start with the details. Educate him more about sexually transmitted diseases and safety. Make him a little scared. It's good for both of you. In case he sneaks out without you knowing, at least he won't bring any diseases home. Of course, it's even better if he doesn't sneak out at all. It means safety, but we should still educate and make him feel a little scared.

Hello, OP: Thank you for the invitation, and I apologize for taking so long to respond! I can sense that you are torn apart because of your boyfriend's infidelity. On one hand, your boyfriend, as a prodigal son, has shown sincere remorse and repentance. On the other hand, you are afraid that forgiving him too easily will lead to a repeat of his actions, causing inner conflict and torment. First of all, let's determine how long you have known your boyfriend and what your relationship foundation is like. What happened that caused him to cheat? Since you haven't provided detailed and objective information, let's make a few assumptions and answer your question based on those assumptions. If your boyfriend is inherently promiscuous and frequently engages in infidelity, then whether you choose to forgive him or not, he will definitely continue to hurt you. If your boyfriend is genuinely a gentleman and this incident was a rare occurrence, such as a result of being drunk, then perhaps he has learned his lesson and can genuinely change for the better, given that you have enough trust in him and a solid relationship foundation. Furthermore, if your boyfriend has no character issues, but your romantic relationship has problems or there are cracks in your emotional connection due to poor communication, his infidelity may be driven by the deficiencies in your relationship, satisfying either his physical or emotional needs. In this case, the probability of future infidelity is inevitable. Additionally, what you said is not wrong – there are always exceptions. We need to understand, what is our attitude towards love, relationships, and commitments when exceptions occur? If we maintain a "sit back and enjoy" attitude, then once the honeymoon period is over, our true nature may resurface. If we approach the relationship with the attitude of reestablishing and preserving love, then the outcome may be as we hope for. As for how to prevent infidelity, it depends on each other's personalities and the level of trust. If both you and your partner are sensitive individuals, regardless of what meaningful actions you take for the relationship, it will continually cast doubt and shadows. For example, if you approach the relationship with a vigilant mindset, where you cannot trust anything he does, just imagine how he would react to your feelings. There are methods, of course, but the chain reaction that occurs once they are implemented may be unforeseeable. For example, you can reach an agreement with your boyfriend that if he makes a mistake after marriage, all your shared assets will be transferred to your name, leaving him with nothing. But just think about it – even as you attempt to use a set of theories and methods to defend against your boyfriend, the foundation of trust that you both have starts to crack. So, if you want to continue this relationship, you can tell your boyfriend about your inner conflict and struggle clearly and state explicitly that there will be no second chances. What is your bottom line in terms of endurance? Additionally, I think you shouldn't forgive him easily at first. Ignore him for a while to let him know how angry and upset you are this time, and also to show him the depth of pain that his infidelity has caused you. As for how long, you need to tell him specifically that it's an observation period as well as a punishment period. Good luck, and remember that I will always love you!

Just like what the OP said, nothing in this world is absolute. There are definitely cases of infidelity as mentioned by the OP, but we need to consider a question: Can this act of infidelity really be forgiven and forgotten? Because trust is sometimes like a piece of paper, it will still have wrinkles even if we crumple it and then unfold it. Although time is the best medicine, trust between two people cannot be restored all at once. Moreover, due to the other person's job situation, many things may not develop as we expect. Therefore, we need to prepare for the worst. We can analyze the reasons for the other person's infidelity. Are there other problems between the two of us? If it was just a momentary impulse and the other person has not invested genuine emotions, and they can also recognize their own mistakes and have some plans for our future, and have made many precautions to give us some confidence, and we are also unwilling to give up this relationship, then we can give them another chance. However, this time we must think carefully, if the other person commits the same mistake again, will we forgive them? We can make an agreement with the other person: if they have similar thoughts again, we hope they will end this relationship first instead of cheating on us. If they are planning to deceive us, then be prepared to be deceived for a lifetime, otherwise, we should not continue. If we can truly learn to let go slowly, and during this time we don't need to have too much suspicion, entrusting some things to the other person to handle, and some behaviors to be proven by time, what we need to do is to become a better version of ourselves. The world and I love you.

Do you know that men often have affairs after getting married? You are still in the early stages of dating, and he has already cheated. What will happen in the future? It is inevitable that it will happen again. But according to what I've read online, many articles and comments say that infidelity can happen once or multiple times. Personally, I think this statement is true. If he is not faithful to you even before marriage, then even if he claims to like you, you are not held in higher regard than anyone else in his heart. Once the excitement fades, your relationship and feelings will change. Even if it happens only once, it is still a betrayal. If you are already married and he cheats, there is a possibility of him being faithful in the future if you forgive him. But since you are still in the dating phase, it is different. He might become faithful to you later, but I think you should still be cautious. There are no absolutes in reality, but you should also take precautions. Are there cases where someone does not commit infidelity anymore after cheating? It depends on the specific situation and how strong their willpower is. Both of you want to get married, so why would the other person still cheat? You should consider how much love and sincerity the other person has for you. Two people who are ready for marriage are definitely a good match. If you truly love each other, there is no need for measures or forcing your way into marriage. It seems a bit too demanding and restrictive. Moreover, in today's society, wealthy men are more prone to infidelity. If you can't control them, it may be better to first try to improve yourself. A woman who is outstanding in her own right will naturally attract many men. Interactions between men and women need to have a certain degree of appropriateness. Zhou Guoping once said, "Don't care too much about a person. The more you care, the more inferior you become." Do you know the concept of the threshold effect? The more you compromise, the more disrespectful the other person will become. Instead of worrying about how to get married, it's better to focus on improving yourself. There are many men in the world, and there will always be someone who treats you well and cherishes you. So, work hard to change yourself. An excellent woman will naturally exude charm. Keep going, and you will find happiness.

When I was young, I used to work in the field with my parents. There was someone in the neighboring plot plowing the land with oxen. I saw him holding a whip, vigorously swinging it at the ox's buttocks, trying to pull and make it move forward. But the ox wouldn't budge, it even stepped back! At that time, I wondered, why doesn't it move? Besides, the ox is so big, how can you pull it? Now, maybe you hold the whip that makes it move forward, but if it wants to go off track, can you stop it by holding the whip? If it wants to move forward with you, you don't need to forcefully pull it.

question: 20-year-old girl, recently over the past year, always feels suppressed at home and wants to escape.
description: I didn't feel anything at home before. I knew that my parents' relationship was always bad. My mom loved to complain and my dad ignored her. But I was used to it. Since I went to university, I have seen my boyfriend's happy family with good parental relationship, a happy household and cheerful personalities. I really envy that. This may be one of the triggers for my stress. As my parents' conflicts become more and more intense, I feel sorry for my younger brother. I don't want to stay at home anymore, but my mom will restrict my actions and express dissatisfaction with my behavior anytime and anywhere. It's like she's controlling me. When we go out to eat, she actively asks me to order the dishes and then completely overturns my choices. My dad has a strange personality and a strong self-esteem. He tries to make others respect him by adopting a superior attitude. But I really can't respect him when he relies on being older and more experienced. What's wrong with me? How can I change?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, family control.

answers.answer_text: After reading the author's confessions, I deeply understand the pain in your heart. I give you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1. "What's wrong with me?" You lack self-awareness. In other words, you don't know how to plan your own life, and you don't know how to choose your own way of life. In life, you are a person without a strong will. When faced with problems, you always have no idea what to choose. You feel very confused and don't know what you really want. 2. Firstly, the problems in every child can be traced back to their parents. In the past, maybe the disharmony in your family caused you a lot of harm. It also led to your lack of confidence and sensitivity. It's okay, now you have grown up and have a boyfriend. You have the ability to choose the life you want. As long as you don't give permission, no one can harm you. 3. "I really, really envy, and this may be a trigger for my stress." Don't underestimate your boyfriend's intelligence. He loves you, he chose you not because he is stupid. And, this is precisely the wisest decision he has made in his life. In a relationship, if you feel inferior, then the end of this relationship is not far away. Try to be independent. Work-study, manage your studies, hobbies, friendships, love, and family relationships well. This way, you can reduce the impact your original family has on you. When you become independent and no longer rely on your family, it will be difficult for your parents to control you. Thank you for your question, may all the beauty in the world come to you as expected.

question: Why does feeling unsafe in one's environment lead to social anxiety?
description: I became introverted and even seemed aloof in the eyes of others after joining a new company. When I feel a sense of safety in the environment (or feel appreciated for my abilities by others), I am still cheerful, talkative, and confident in unfamiliar surroundings. However, when I sense that the environment does not provide a feeling of security (perhaps due to the excellence of people around me or the fear of saying something wrong and feeling embarrassed), I experience social anxiety. I become silent and don't speak. But deep down, I really want to integrate into the new team, yet I don't know where to start. I feel like there are "two me" - one confident, the other insecure and timid. I don't know what happened to me and why I am like this. I really hope to find ways to resolve this inner conflict. Thank you very much.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, colleagues, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: The topic owner's personal abilities are unquestionable, but they belong to the slow warm-up type, so they need an adaptation period when encountering some problems, and this period is not easy to control. When entering a new company, a period of adaptation is definitely needed. We don't need to be overly anxious. Inner self-confidence is definitely necessary. In fact, a sense of security is never given by others, so we can make adjustments according to the current situation. Look at what our position and responsibilities are, we can roughly understand the current situation, see what needs to be learned, what are our strengths and weaknesses, and how to cooperate with others. For problems that can be solved by Baidu or oneself, we can solve them on our own. If it is indeed a problem that cannot be solved by oneself alone, we can think about it ourselves, express our thoughts, and find a team member when the other person is not too busy, try to avoid multiple rework. The world and I love you.

Hello, I see that you're feeling anxious and uneasy. You have a strong self-awareness and sensitivity to your own emotions. You care about how the environment and others perceive you. But it's important to note that your self-worth should not come from others' opinions. You worry that others might not think highly of you and doubt if you are good enough, perfect enough, or strong enough. This leads to self-blame and a mindset of trying to please others. The truth is, everyone is focused on themselves and has limited mental energy to focus on others. We all focus on three things: other people's matters, our own matters, and matters beyond our control. Confucius once said, "At seventy, I could follow my heart's desires without transgressing the boundaries." When we reach the age of seventy, we can follow our inner desires without deliberately conforming to others' judgments and thoughts, as long as we don't cross legal and moral boundaries. This is the state of natural harmony. We need to integrate and accept our inner conflicts and pains, understand and respect ourselves, and love ourselves in order to love others properly. Start by acknowledging your own inner needs, avoiding absolute demands on yourself and others, and avoiding extreme negative thinking patterns that view things as either black or white, this or that. Even in separation, loss, trauma, and pain, there can be positive aspects. Childhood anxiety caused by an impatient mother or a father who focuses only on pleasing news can lead to a personality trait of seeking approval and withholding bad news. Double standards and emotional manipulation, like saying "I'm doing this for your own good, you should do this and that, and if you know you're wrong, why don't you change?" can have a controlling influence. As adults, it's important to establish our own identity, reduce the impact of intergenerational transmission from our parents, understand their upbringing and parenting shortcomings, and integrate our own feelings from that experience. Engaging in exercise, practicing mindfulness meditation, reading and learning about psychology, and seeking the company of a therapist can all be helpful choices. I wish you well.

Actually, you could say that everyone cares a lot about what others think of them, but if you care too much, then that small self will pop up and start worrying about what others might think of you. The real self becomes hidden, preferring not to take any action or make any mistakes. In reality, there's no need for that. You are yourself, and no matter how you approach things, it reflects your true abilities and methods. If someone's evaluation is fair, then thank them. If it's negative, use it as an opportunity to recognize and improve upon your weaknesses. Don't let others influence you. Work diligently, interact sincerely, and you will find security within yourself. Overcome the small self and embrace a confident life.

question: 33-year-old woman, who has severe OCD and sleep disorders, what should she do?
description: In high school, I had a lot of academic stress, which affected my sleep. I would often have nightmares during nap time. In college, I have never been able to fall asleep during the afternoon. I developed OCD, initially avoiding sitting in places I considered unclean. In recent years, I have felt that pen ink is impossible to wash off, and just seeing it makes me uncomfortable. I also need to feel safe at all times, regardless of how far away someone is behind me. Sometimes, my back feels tight, and I have been struggling with sleep disorders for over 10 years. I work in the IT industry and I feel like I can't handle it anymore. I am seeking help to find relief.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, mental disorders.

answers.answer_text: Poster, hello~~~ First, give the poster a hug. From the description, it can be understood that the poster has some obsessive behaviors and sleep disorders, and it has been going on for a long time, causing a lot of pain. [Analysis and Suggestions] 1. Problems caused by long-term mental stress are difficult to change on their own. The poster may try to find a professional counseling office for treatment, using systematic treatment methods, and may need to use medication to have an effective targeted symptom treatment, etc. 2. Sleep problems: consciously exerting oneself during the day is helpful for sleep at night, such as exercise, or reading some difficult books before bed to consume energy. With a regular plan and schedule, it can have some effect. I hope this helps the poster.

question: A 20-year-old young man recently has been having trouble falling asleep at night and experiencing unexplainable panic and fear.
description: Even when I fall asleep, I always have dreams and wake up in a fright. I don't know what I am afraid of in my mind, and I am always worried that I will go crazy. Do I have anxiety disorder? What should I do?
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, mental disorders.

answers.answer_text: ~Want to have a warm hug~ Dreaming is a normal phenomenon. Maybe you have been under a lot of stress recently, which has led to waking up from dreams and poor sleep quality, resulting in short-term sleep disorders. Feeling scared or afraid of going crazy may be due to excessive worry about your current situation. Perhaps you can go for more walks to relax and improve your mood, which will help with your sleep. Maybe you can go to the gym more often or engage in other sports, which can help you get tired and sleep better. Maybe you can also communicate more with family and friends, go out and do activities to release psychological stress, and lighten your burden, which may also contribute to better sleep.

question: Drawing gives me a sense of well-being, but what should I do when I am greatly discouraged after asking others for their opinions?
description: I thought I was pretty good at drawing, but when I shared my artwork, I didn't receive any comments. No one asked me to collaborate on any projects, and my classmates told me to practice more. I used to believe that I wasn't too bad at drawing, but now I feel like I have been overly positive about myself. Things that I used to be good at have suddenly become my weaknesses, and I have lost confidence. I don't know if there is anything else I am good at, and I don't understand my own worth anymore. It's just a small matter, but I'm thinking too much about it. Should I start considering things I like as things I am not good at and then try to improve slowly? But if I see things as something I am not good at, I will gradually start disliking them and become even worse at them. I don't want that. But I have lost my confidence because no matter how good I think my work is, there are always many problems with it. I feel so upset.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and learning, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! From different perspectives, there are different standards, so you don't have to be deeply affected by other people's opinions. Of course, as human beings, we have our own set of standards, just like "no rules, no standards." We need these indicators to guide the public's lives, just like fashion has its own aesthetic standards. Sometimes, the release of a new product can lead a trend for a period of time. Indeed, we often believe that what the majority likes is correct. Psychologist Asch's famous conformity experiment regarding line judgment is similar to this experiment. Have you ever noticed that some of the new products introduced at Paris Fashion Week in recent years make you doubt your own taste? At the same time, the reason why we can compare and determine value is because we use these indicators as reference points for comparison. But who can bravely claim that their standards are absolutely correct? Late period works by Picasso are considered to be the pinnacle of art by artists, but from the perspective of an ordinary person like myself, I can't figure out its appeal. However, I'm not advising you to ignore the external evaluations, but rather not to attach your own value to them. So how should you balance it? Everyone has different self-awareness and evaluation methods, and here I'll only provide some suggestions: 1. First, you need to clarify why you paint. If you paint for profit, to realize your value (meaning external recognition), then you may have to pay more attention to external evaluations. For example, the requirements of the client, market acceptance, and popular trends, etc. 2. You mentioned that when others think your art is not good, you lose motivation to paint. This is largely because you value external evaluations and see praise from others as motivation. If you want to continue pursuing your interest, then you have to objectively view evaluations. If many people believe that you need more practice, it means that you haven't reached the level that the public loves yet, but it doesn't mean that you're worthless. Don't you find the process of improvement interesting? It's not embarrassing to strive in an area you love, and admitting your shortcomings doesn't mean you're incompetent. Having self-worth independent of external factors can achieve a stable mental state. 3. You can think about what standards you rely on to believe that your art is good, what is good about it, and whether you have overestimated it. Maybe you will find that your unique perspective is being buried, or perhaps you can create new areas of painting. Before Jay Chou debuted, he composed and wrote songs for many people, but they were all rejected because the style was strange. However, he got a chance to perform his own works and found his own position.

I can definitely understand how the author feels. Sometimes on Q&A platforms, I also feel that my answers are good, but after half an hour or an hour passes without anyone giving me a thumbs up, I start to doubt if my answers are not good enough, or if my abilities are lacking, and so on. Luckily, I have taken some courses on cognitive behavioral therapy, which enables me to adjust my thoughts and emotions. In cognitive behavioral therapy, it emphasizes examining automatic thinking. I don't know if the author has noticed, but in their description, there are actually a lot of "all or nothing" and "generalization" thoughts. For example, after external evaluation, they directly perceive drawing, which they originally believed they were good at, as something they are not good at. Or for example, if their drawing doesn't meet their ideal standards, they invalidate their own worth. If we use a scale of 0-10 as reference, where 0 represents extremely low drawing skills and 10 represents the highest level of drawing skills, the people around may have a standard of 8+, they might think the author's artwork hasn't reached 8 points, and there is room for improvement. But the author gives themselves a heavy blow: "I haven't reached 8 points, so my skill level is 0," which is a typical "all or nothing" thinking pattern. If the author, due to this kind of automatic thinking and self-defeat, gives up their love for drawing, then I think it would be a pity. Besides, the same applies to one's own worth. Even if we take it to the extreme and say that their drawing is indeed below the standards of those around them, it doesn't mean that they have no worth. Not being good at something doesn't equal to one's worth as a person. This is something we should remind ourselves of all the time. Even if drawing is not good, I still respect my parents and contribute to society... I still have worth. What's even more important is that we should take back the power to determine our own worth, and never let others decide whether we have worth or not. Finally, I think artistic creation requires modifications based on others' feedback. For example, in our country's classic novel "Dream of the Red Chamber," the book went through additions, deletions, and modifications for almost ten years after it was first published. Even such a great work needs to be finely polished. Or perhaps we can try to adopt a different attitude or perspective towards the evaluation of those around us, not seeing these evaluations as monstrous floods, but as suggestions for our potential improvement. The end~.

Hello there~ It's important to understand that everyone has their own perspective when it comes to looking at the same thing. This means that no matter how good your drawing is, you cannot please everyone. There will always be people who say your drawing is good, and there will always be people who say it's not good. Moreover, when others evaluate your work, you need to realize that it is from their own perspective and with their own experiences. This means that their evaluation may not necessarily be true. Furthermore, instead of seeking praise from others, I think it is more valuable to encourage others to give honest feedback on your work, both the good and the bad. If you already draw really well, then what is there for you to improve? It is precisely because your work still has many imperfections that you should put effort and time into making those shortcomings better. Actually, whether it's drawing or doing anything else, initially, most people are at a relatively low level, and it is through step-by-step progress that they become stronger and more skilled. This is a necessary process. Of course, hoping for affirmation from others is very normal, but if you can only accept affirmation and cannot accept criticism, then it means your room for improvement will be limited, because you cannot see where your drawing is not good. Isn't that worse? It's not about seeing what you like as something you're not good at, but rather realizing that when you do something you like, it also cannot be perfect just because you like it. It's precisely because you like it that you should make those areas where you are not doing well better. I like this thing, so I am willing to spend time and energy to make it better - thinking in this way seems more conducive to improving your skills. And from another perspective, I cannot dislike something just because I am not good at it, and I cannot choose to like something just because I am good at it, because liking and being good at something actually have no necessary connection. And precisely because you like it, you can slowly become good at the things you are not good at. In this process, you will also experience a lot of joy. So, the next time someone says your drawing is not good, you should acknowledge that your drawing is indeed not particularly outstanding, and there's no shame in that. Then, you should tell yourself in your heart - yes, there are still many areas where I need improvement in this drawing, but I will definitely make good improvements because I enjoy doing this. And I will definitely get better. Don't focus too much on how others perceive you externally, instead, think more about what changes you can make for yourself in this matter. Best wishes~

Hello, I also like to draw. I believe it is one of my strengths, although I have not received formal training and I am not an art major. In fact, drawing as a hobby has excellent effects on personal growth and character development. If you want to make money by taking commissions, you will need to put in more effort. In return, you will also gain a greater sense of achievement. You should carefully consider whether you want to make a career out of drawing or if you simply have a passion for it. If it is a passion, don't worry too much about gains and losses. By persevering in what you love, you will definitely reap rewards in this field. Keep up the good work!

Hello OP! When it comes to drawing, I feel that it is more about expressing ourselves, expressing our inspiration or certain emotions. If we are too focused on others' opinions, it may hinder our ability to draw well. Moreover, others' opinions are not completely objective, especially in the realm of art. Everyone may have their own opinions, likes or dislikes, good or bad, and these judgments are highly subjective. We don't need to rely too much on others' judgments to determine our actions. My suggestion is: focus on yourself and improve your drawing skills. OP should shift their focus back to themselves, not placing too much importance on external commissions or evaluations, but rather on improving their drawing abilities. When your skills improve, other opportunities will come naturally. Additionally, it's important to have confidence in yourself. If drawing is something you enjoy, then have the determination to pursue it and don't let others' opinions affect you. I believe in you!

question: Does love exist in this world? I will never understand what love is.
description: I do not understand what the love of family is, or what the love of friendship is. I also do not understand what the love of romantic relationships is. I no longer expect anyone to love me because I am not good and I also do not know how to love others. Therefore, I will never understand what love is... For some people, the meaning of life is to have no love at all.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, emotional regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, listening to your description, I feel sorry for you. I can sense that you have a deep desire for love, to be loved by others, and to be able to love others. It is like the seed of love sprouting within you. 01. Feeling a lack of love may be because the love is not as strong. People have different expectations when it comes to love. Some need to feel happy through being loved and loving others, while for some, love is only enough to keep themselves alive. The environment in which a person is born and grows up is like soil. Some people land in fertile soil, while others land in barren soil. However, even in the barren soil, there is still some sustenance for survival. I don't know what you have experienced, maybe as you said, the environment did not make you feel more love. But the fact that you have grown up shows that this seed within you is resilient. Did anyone praise you during your growth? Did anyone care about you? It could be someone familiar, someone you happened to meet, or even strangers like us, who all hope to see you become happy. 02. Feeling like you are not good enough may be influenced by the environment. After a baby is born, all their needs are provided by the primary caregiver. As they grow older, their needs increase. However, when the primary caregiver fails to meet the baby's needs in a timely manner, the baby may develop thoughts like "Am I not good enough? Is it because of me that they didn't meet my needs?" Another common phenomenon is when parents argue or when the family experiences unexpected changes, people around might vent their emotions and say it's all your fault. But in reality, it is just an emotional expression, and it truly has nothing to do with a child. 03. The ability to love can also change. You mentioned that you may never understand love, but as long as you start to face this issue and take care of yourself first, filling up your own cup of love little by little, then you can nourish others. Taking care of yourself can start with taking care of your physical health and then your emotional well-being. As your inner strength grows, you naturally gain the ability to accept others' emotions, which is a form of expressing love. You can also seek professional help through psychological counseling to replenish your cup of love more quickly. 04. The meaning of life is a choice and definition made by individuals with their own will. Some people live for love and to be loved. They are more suited to being teachers, social workers, and the like. Some people live to create, such as writers and artists, as well as individuals in various fields who love hands-on work and making changes. There are also people whose meaning of life is to experience. For example, cyclists or ordinary people who try to experience different lives and see each experience as a rare opportunity in life. As long as you yearn for love in your heart and learn to love yourself first, you can definitely experience a meaningful and loving life. Take it slowly! Best wishes.

question: What to do when being isolated by college roommates? Worried that other classmates will also isolate me.
description: I usually like to study alone and have a personality that doesn't interfere with others. My roommate likes to gather in the dormitory. This semester, I found myself being isolated by a very popular and noisy roommate in the dormitory (she started isolating me with two other people). Specifically, when I return to the dormitory, everyone basically ignores me while they play together. I feel somewhat uncomfortable, what should I do?
keywords: Interpersonal, conflicts and conflicts, roommates, classmates, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Dear~ Sometimes we care too much about other people's opinions or their approval of ourselves. But the most important thing is to ask yourself, do you enjoy being alone? Let me share a hypothetical story to ponder: In college, there were four roommates. One of them relished solitude, spending her time in the library, studying, working part-time, and exploring the world. Another roommate was outgoing and effortlessly made friends, always surrounded by a group of people. They spent their days forming small cliques, doing little else. However, after graduation, the introverted person interned at a Fortune 500 company and crossed paths with successful professionals. On the other hand, the other roommates didn't plan their careers well and felt lost in life after graduation, unsure of their direction or desires. So, compared to the others, do you think being alone isn't actually so bad? Concentrate on your long-term goals and future plans. Why bother concerning yourself with these few individuals? Turn around, and there are billions of people behind you. I believe that if what I mentioned above is true, you won't have time to worry about others' opinions!

OP, hello~~~ Sending you a warm hug;) Indeed, being isolated by roommates is a very uncomfortable thing, and I can truly understand your feelings, and also feel that you actually want to establish a good relationship with them. For this, let's try the following methods. Since you mentioned that you are someone who is accustomed to being alone, I think this may have given others the wrong signal, making them think that you "do not want to socialize." So, let's communicate directly with your roommates, express your thoughts and attitude to them. This way, we can avoid misunderstandings between each other. On the other hand, we can actively express our desire to make friends through actions, and make our attitude known. It is the same with classmates in the class. Maintain a positive mindset~ Try not to let these things affect our mood when dealing with other matters.

question: I always feel very suppressed and want to escape when faced with problems, what should I do?
description: Time passes day by day, but there is always something stuck in my heart, always feeling suppressed and unable to truly smile. I am already in my twenties, but I always feel like I haven't grown up and don't want to. When faced with problems, I always want to escape and keep thinking about it. How can I truly let go of everything and forgive myself?

answers.answer_text: #Always feeling very depressed, wanting to escape when faced with something, what should I do?#Is it because of the environment that you can't handle situations no matter how hard you try? #Time keeps passing day by day, yet there always seems to be something lingering in your mind. #Regarding the "stuck" mentioned in this paragraph, is it caused by someone in your environment or is it related to multiple people? #Feeling constantly depressed makes it difficult to genuinely laugh. #Your emotions are reminding you that your mental state is not good. And if you cannot resolve the "stuck" on your own, then escaping is a normal human reaction. Because if you can't face it, all you can do is avoid it. Do you need methods or suggestions to deal with the "stuck"? If you need help, you can message me privately.

question: A boy says he likes me, but is afraid of breaking up and unwilling to be together? Is this a mindset of a scumbag?
description: It has been about a month since we met through a blind date. We have gone out together three or four times, held hands and hugged, but we haven't defined our relationship. When I try to guide him, he says, "It's not that I don't like you, but I'm afraid that I will be the one who gets dumped in the end, so I want to continue developing things." Is this kind of mindset indicative of a scumbag man?
keywords: Love, single, sense of security, liking.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. OP met someone of the opposite sex through a blind date, and the person is interested in you but is unwilling to enter a relationship because they are afraid of getting rejected. OP is confused by their behavior. There could be two possible reasons for their actions. First, they might genuinely be afraid of rejection, so they are hesitant to start a new relationship because they may have been hurt before and are being cautious about their feelings. Second, they may not actually want to start a new relationship and are using it as an excuse. Currently, you are in a state of uncertainty, which only benefits them and has no drawbacks. They really enjoy this phase. This person may not necessarily be a bad person, but they do lack commitment. It is unfair for OP to be unsure about being in a relationship. It is suggested that OP communicates openly with them and gives them two options: either commit to being together or end all contact. OP should strive to protect their own rights. Best wishes~.

question: Boyfriends may not understand us as well as our girlfriends do. What is the purpose of having a boyfriend?
description: It seems that we really like to discuss our personal matters with our sisters, who can understand us. However, our boyfriends seem to not understand us. So what is the purpose of having a boyfriend then?

answers.answer_text: Your question reminds me of why we need intimate relationships. According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs, after we meet our physiological and safety needs, we have a need for a sense of belonging, and intimate relationships fulfill that need. Intimate relationships are fundamental because humans are social beings with a need for belonging. We need love and to be loved, and the quality of our intimate relationships has significant impacts on both our physical and mental health. Whether your intimate relationship is with a man or a woman depends on your own choice, and there is a significant difference between friendship and an intimate relationship, inherent in their nature.

First and foremost, there will inevitably be differences between boys and girls in terms of physiological interests, hobbies, and habits. It is important to acknowledge and understand these differences. Even though there may be moments when you feel powerless around him, if he is willing to put in effort for you and can assist you in certain situations, despite having numerous reasons not to like him, you should be able to identify his positive qualities. When it comes to matters of the heart, no one can make decisions for you. Only you know what kind of emotions you truly desire.

question: What should one do when faced with a difficult and unhappy marriage due to being with the wrong person?
description: My wife and I didn't get along well before we got married. We only saw each other once every 1-2 weeks and we always had nothing to talk about. She is different from other girls, she rarely checks her WeChat and Moments. Sometimes when I send her a message, she either doesn't reply or takes several hours to reply. Despite all this, we still got married because she has good character and decent conditions. I thought we would become closer after marriage, but it turns out that our relationship has become even more painful. We can never be intimate with each other.
