I feel like she has no feelings for romantic relationships. At night, I like to cuddle while sleeping, but she says she can't fall asleep and always turns her back to me out of habit. She always locks the door when using the bathroom, as if she's afraid I will enter. I tell her I won't, but she insists on locking it anyway. Is it necessary for a husband and wife to be like this? Anyway, she will never make any intimate gestures towards me. It's been over a year since we got married, and we sleep in separate rooms about 3/4 of the time, and she doesn't seem to have any objection. It's probably hard to find a couple as odd as us. I think about divorce every day, but she is already pregnant, so it's really painful.
keywords: Marriage, concepts of marriage, divorce, marital management.

answers.answer_text: Hello! This is a topic about "how to turn wrong decisions into correct outcomes." It is evident in your relationship that there is a lack of passion and enthusiasm from start to finish. However, without any sweet additives in shared life, long-term coexistence will inevitably be accompanied by dullness, leading to either a dissatisfied separation or spending the rest of your lives without any ripple. Marriage is one of the significant events in life and brings about explicit transformations for both parties involved. Most people approach this matter with caution and choose a partner who matches them within their range of options. Few people would deliberately choose someone they can't get along with as a long-term partner, even though they have the freedom to decide. Before marriage, if you can't get along well and lack topics of conversation, it is already a clear sign of "incompatibility." It is unheard of for any successful union to start off with a cold relationship and then achieve harmony and intimacy through the binding of marriage. Locking the bathroom door is a personal habit and has nothing to do with whether or not you have a close relationship. Therefore, it's unnecessary to interpret it as a defense against you and make a fuss about closeness and not locking the door while using the toilet. It seems a bit childish. Besides, it is all about biological excretion, there is nothing to be curious about. She has good character and favorable conditions, honestly speaking, these are her assets, not yours. In other words, it seems that she holds the power of choice between the two of you. If she doesn't want to talk, she can choose not to. If she doesn't want to sleep together, she can choose to sleep in a separate room. Your communication and interaction patterns do not synchronize. When you feel miserable in married life and consider ending the relationship, unfortunately, the power of choice still doesn't lie with you because you mentioned that she is pregnant. Article 34 of the Marriage Law stipulates that during the pregnancy, within one year after childbirth, or within six months after termination of pregnancy, the husband cannot file for divorce. If the wife requests a divorce or the People's Court deems it necessary to accept the husband's divorce petition, this limitation does not apply. If you want to divorce now, she has to initiate it. Otherwise, according to the normal procedure, you have to wait until your child is one year old to be eligible to file for divorce. However, ending your suffering does not necessarily require ending the marriage. The key skill to make a marriage sustainable and stable lies in understanding how to manage it. She has her personality traits, lifestyle habits, and her own space. Likewise, you also have these aspects. Mutual respect is essential. She possesses the character traits and conditions that you value, but do you know what she values? Do you possess those qualities? Do you have any advantages over her? Can you utilize these advantages to gain a certain degree of dominance in the marriage relationship? Good luck!

Title owner, hello! Seeing these words is like seeing you in person, carefully listening to your story, feeling the long-standing turmoil in your intimate relationship, and feeling deeply helpless about your wife's behavior. [Hope to help you sort out the phenomena to discover opportunities for change]-Before getting married, you had already noticed that your wife was distant in your interactions: low frequency of meetings, few common topics, slow or no response on social media. -You observed these behaviors of your wife but still chose to marry her because you felt that she had good character and good conditions. There is nothing wrong with this, but it seems that you overlooked the fact that a harmonious and happy marriage requires deep and meaningful communication. -At the same time, based on your observations of the problem, you did not help your wife further think and explore her attitude towards intimate relationships and the possible reasons behind her distant behavior. -After getting married, you noticed even more that your wife seems to have no feelings towards romantic relationships. She has a different sleeping position than you, locks the bathroom door, has no intimate gestures with you, and often sleeps in separate rooms without any objections. -This constantly makes you endure the feeling of being "close strangers" in your marriage, and you strongly doubt your own value, especially now that your wife is pregnant, which makes you agonize over whether to divorce or not. [We need to take action regarding intimate relationships]-To have a healthy and mature intimate relationship, a key point between men and women is to "express oneself actively and reduce suspicion." If you want the other person to meet your expectations, you need to express your feelings and expectations proactively based on what you observe. Start your conversations with phrases like "Wife, I feel that you seem to... and I hope we can...". -To have an ideal partner, you should not enter into a marriage with the intention of changing the other person, but with the attitude of "influencing others with your own life." We can hardly control others, but we have the opportunity to influence others. Take the details of your daily interactions as an opportunity to "practice being a lover" and gradually correct each other's behavior that may have issues and confusion. -As a reliable man, I wonder if you can approach your wife's behavioral confusion with an attitude of "empathetic reflection" and try to understand the growth experiences she may not have expressed to you. This may include her difficulties, past traumas, and the distant upbringing style of her parents towards her, etc. This is worth considering. -Lastly, and most importantly, for a wife who is already pregnant, I think you wouldn't want to give up on your child. Therefore, only by actively facing the problems in the relationship and giving yourself and your wife a chance to change, can you avoid regretting impulsive decisions in the future. I hope you do not rush to make regrettable decisions without figuring out the confusion. -In addition, if you find it difficult to escape from this turmoil on your own, I strongly recommend seeking help from a professional and reliable marriage and family counselor. With the counselor's involvement, you can support your communication more effectively and orderly, so that the problems in your marriage become opportunities to enhance intimacy. I hope my humble advice can provide you with some inspiration and help. I wish you happiness soon!

Hello, it is normal for someone who is not familiar with psychology to feel extremely distressed by your wife's attitude towards you. If we analyze this from a psychological perspective, your wife may be in a state of emotional defense and isolation in intimate relationships. It is not only towards you, but may also stem from not being treated correctly in her childhood family or early interpersonal relationships, which has led to her remaining guarded and alert towards people and situations. On the other hand, you are someone who strongly desires emotional and intimate relationships. Your wife's distance and lack of trust make you feel uncomfortable. Some of her behaviors can be understood more, for example, when she uses the restroom, if she doesn't close the door, she feels extremely anxious, fearing someone will intrude. Even if you assure her that you won't enter, subconsciously she still feels like someone could burst in at any moment, so closing the door makes her feel secure. If you cuddle to sleep at night, it keeps her in a constant state of tension, causing her to have difficulty falling asleep. Not responding to or reading messages puts her in a passive state during interpersonal interactions. There are actually many couples like you. According to attachment theory, your wife may have an avoidant attachment style, which is the most common attachment style and even surpasses other attachment styles. What should you do in this situation? Divorce is not the solution, especially since your wife is already pregnant. Firstly, respect some of your wife's habits and slowly build her sense of security. Help her relax more and give her some space, so she can trust you more. Then, in daily life, show her subtle acts of intimacy. Use humor and jokes to break down her inner barriers. Gradually bridge the gap between you two and eliminate her alertness and defensive mindset. Only when the heart is engaged can people come closer! I wish you happiness!

Dear friend: From your words, I can feel your helplessness and pain. Before we fully grow up, we always yearn for the love of the people around us, hoping that the people around us have this ability to make us feel loved. However, this desire hinders our growth and also hinders this relationship. The desire to maintain intimacy is undeniable. Maybe you feel lonely or insecure. But you can only wait in place without the right to control, and because of this, you feel very disappointed and frustrated. So you really want a divorce. Or maybe your marriage needs to take a step forward. [First], share your vulnerability. You can share your feelings of loneliness with your wife. Maybe she will still reject you and continue to sleep in separate rooms, but at least your inner vulnerability will be released and she will have recognition and understanding of your feelings. [Second], understand each other's limitations. In fact, your wife does not not love you, but she also has her own limitations. Even under the same roof, she cannot fill your emptiness. From the beginning, the idea of functionality I proposed means that you see her as something to fill your emptiness and loneliness. Similarly, you are also a human being. You need to be loved and not treated coldly. You cannot be seen as an item placed here. It is this emptiness that exists because of the limitations of each other's abilities, which makes you feel lost. [Third], rely on a greater power. You can calm down and feel the universe, because the love it gives you is complete and can fill the regrets in relationships between people. And its power is always there, inexhaustible, and unconditional. Feel this power and experience the warmth of motherly love again. [Fourth], accompany yourself and develop your own interests. Interests, other interesting things, can also bring you the experience of being loved, not necessarily from a relationship. You can try to develop your own interests, feel nurtured, and feel accompanied. [Fifth], intimate relationships ultimately involve being the best version of yourself individually. In fact, your wife also lacks a sense of security and is afraid of losing herself in an intimate relationship. If you push her too close, she will be afraid and avoid you. Forgive your wife's limitations, and forgive your own limitations. Accept and respect yourself, and also accept and respect your wife. You should know that love is not about changing the other person, nor is it about using the other person to fill something within yourself. Love is about feeling the love that comes from everything, including the love that comes from yourself, and then sharing that love with others. I hope you and your wife can get through this difficult time together! Your friend, Audrey ---------------------------------------------- Unity, love, respect, forgiveness. ♥

Honey, give you a kiss and a hug. I see that you and your wife have a hard time feeling intimate in your relationship, and you feel that she is distant from you, so you feel very uncomfortable. I can see that before you got married, you didn't feel very intimate with each other, you didn't meet often, and you didn't reply to messages on WeChat very often either. However, you still chose to get married. I wonder if you had a conversation about the purpose of getting married before? Why did you choose to be together? Your thoughts were that she had good conditions and a good character, so you wanted to give it a try, but what did she think? Have you ever understood her thoughts? From a utilitarian perspective, relationships are a process of fulfilling each other's needs. Your need is intimacy, but she finds it difficult to fulfill. What is her need then? Have you ever understood her views on marriage and your needs? Couples are actually a whole, living together and facing the difficulties of life together. You can talk about your concerns with her and discuss her needs, and see how you can adjust in the future. If it's not suitable and you feel that neither of your needs can be fulfilled, then consider divorce. Lastly, you mentioned that your wife is already pregnant. I hope you can make cautious decisions and not let the child become an excuse to bind you. It's also irresponsible to let a child grow up in an unhappy family! I hope I can help you, the world and I love you!

Hello, OP! I can sense your distress. You want to establish an intimate relationship with your wife, but her behavior in this relationship creates a sense of distance for you. You don't know how to handle your relationship with her. It's clear that you really like your wife, even though you recognize that you both have many differences. You choose to be understanding and see the attractive qualities in your wife. However, as time goes on, the differences in your lives as a married couple slowly become magnified, which has left you feeling troubled. You mentioned that your wife is different from other girls, as she rarely uses WeChat or posts on Moments (a social media feature in China). Sometimes, she doesn't reply to your WeChat messages or takes hours to respond. It's evident that your wife doesn't enjoy communicating with others and doesn't make an effort to maintain online social interactions. At night, you like to cuddle while sleeping, but she says she can't fall asleep and always turns away from you. She also always locks the bathroom door when using it. It seems your wife lacks a sense of security and likes to keep herself tightly wrapped up. These behaviors from your wife make you feel that your relationship is distant and you are tired of this state. Acceptance and mutual understanding are essential for a marriage. You and your wife just have different personalities. You desire intimacy, while your wife may not be ready for it yet. From your description, it's apparent that your wife is not good at expressing emotions, which makes you feel that she is indifferent. First of all, accept your wife as she is and try to see things from her perspective. Generally, a person's personality is influenced by their upbringing, so understanding her experiences can help you comprehend her better and give her more care. Take it slow and give her some time. Building intimacy in a short period is difficult for her as she has become accustomed to an independent life and hasn't fully transitioned from being alone. To protect herself, she may resist contact with others. Take it slow and give her some time. Start by strengthening your communication and gradually building intimacy. Communication in a marriage requires joint effort. Since you're facing issues in your relationship, it's important to solve them together. Find a suitable time to have a heartfelt talk with your wife and express your concerns. Each person has a different way of expressing emotions and fears. Try to understand each other and discuss ways to improve. You can take the initiative in everyday life to reassure your wife, to make her feel protected and safe at home, and gradually open up her heart. I wish you can get rid of your troubles as soon as possible.

Hello, OP, first I want to give you a big hug~ The main issue you are currently facing is: How to deal with the distance between you and your wife? Based on your description: "She is different from other women, rarely checking WeChat and Moments. Sometimes, when I send her a message, she either doesn't reply or takes hours to respond." "I like to cuddle when sleeping, but she says she can't sleep and always turns her back to me out of habit." "She always locks the bathroom door as if she is afraid that I will come in. I told her that I won't, but she insists on locking it." Your wife seems to be independent but lacking a sense of security. Humans are social beings who need socializing and communication, as well as affirmation and recognition from others, which is why people tend to talk with others. Your wife appears to not pay much attention to this aspect and maintains her own characteristics, indicating that she has a strong inner world and may prioritize spiritual communication. Therefore, your wife may yearn for a deeper connection in the spiritual realm rather than just physical intimacy. However, this is only one possibility based on limited information, and a thorough understanding requires more communication between you and your wife. From your description, it seems that you have an accepting attitude towards your wife but feel that the relationship is lacking excitement. In regard to this, you can express your thoughts to your wife and discuss her thoughts as well. You can also share your expectations, such as ways to celebrate anniversaries or improve your relationship. Looking at it from another perspective, you may not have provided enough security for your wife. In the upcoming days, you can pay closer attention to your wife's daily life, immerse yourself in her world, and actively participate in each other's lives. If you have the time and energy, you can also prepare surprises for your wife (assuming you know her preferences well), engage in meaningful activities together, and more. Best wishes.

Title holder~ sigh~ How should I put it. Let me talk about my feelings, hoping to bring you some thoughts: Have you talked to your wife? You mentioned that in your opinion, you got married because she has good character and conditions are not bad. But why did she? Why did she marry you if it seems like she has no interest in you at all? In your description, you have been talking about your feelings, but what about her feelings? What are the reasons behind her behavior? Without knowing her feelings and opening up the knots in her heart, it would be difficult for your relationship to develop further. So my advice to you is: have a good long talk with her. She is pregnant. My suggestion is to have a good conversation before deciding whether or not to have a child. Don't let the child be born into an unhappy family just because of a moment of weakness or compromise. At that time, you got married out of compromise, which led to the problems in your marriage now. So, you can't just compromise again. Try to solve your current issues as much as possible before the baby is born. It is indeed very hot to sleep while cuddling, making it difficult to fall asleep. At least personally, I don't sleep cuddling with my partner. So, as I said, there are reasons behind various behaviors, and only by understanding the reasons can you prescribe the right medicine. Have a good talk with your wife, and I hope you can resolve the problem as soon as possible, allowing the baby to be born in a loving family.

question: The primary school teacher's physical and verbal abuse left a deep emotional scar on me, causing me to feel inferior and lacking in self-confidence.
description: The homeroom teacher in elementary school, although not tall, is particularly fierce. He often physically assaults students, punching and kicking them. During that time, my parents got divorced, and I didn't want to study, so I deliberately misbehaved and caused trouble. As a result, I became the target of the homeroom teacher's attention. He often physically abused and verbally scolded me, kicking my bottom and twisting my ears. He called me a troublemaker and said I would be like this for the rest of my life, which has led to my long-lasting low self-esteem.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give you a hug. Indeed, teachers have a significant impact on children. When you encounter an irritable teacher at the beginning of your learning, it can have a negative effect on yourself. The fact that you can realize this and recognize your own feelings of inferiority may already be a positive signal, indicating that you have the potential to change. Firstly, the environment does have a great impact on us. When you were young, you faced great setbacks, both in terms of family issues and the temper of the teacher, which made you feel very uncomfortable and unforgettable until now. However, the environment is not the determining factor for a person's development, especially their abilities. Ultimately, what kind of person you become is decided by yourself. In other words, it is determined by your subjective initiative. What kind of person do you want to become? Read more books and learn from the people around you. Find the aspects you want to learn from them, then actively accept the influence of those things. As you grow older, perhaps the past pain and childhood sorrow will transform into a treasure that motivates you to move forward.

question: How to look at the harm suffered in activities that are participated in together with others?
description: I voluntarily signed up for an activity with two other people. Each person had their own tasks to do, and initially, everyone agreed to their responsibilities. I was in charge of the images, while the other person was responsible for checking and making changes. Not only did they have a bad attitude when speaking, but even after communicating with them politely and attentively, they still asked me in a rude manner as if they couldn't understand simple things that were obvious to everyone. It's not a big deal, maybe they thought I was the one issuing tasks from the higher-ups and that I had more information. However, they kept saying that they couldn't do any task and asked me directly to do it for them. They also criticized my image editing, saying it wasn't up to standard, so they couldn't make any changes. Honestly, I couldn't control my thoughts anymore. I started to wonder if they were given too many tasks, and if they were venting their frustration through this behavior, or if they thought I had no abilities and questioned why I was assigning tasks. Of course, I know this is just my subjective imagination. Nevertheless, their attitude and behavior truly hurt me.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and disputes, personal boundaries, empathy.

answers.answer_text: When there are disagreements during team collaboration, it is normal because everyone has not worked together before, so it is not clear what each person's strengths and weaknesses are, and it is inevitable that there will be inappropriate division of labor. In the current situation, we can first calm our emotions because sometimes the other party is indeed being unreasonable. Don't bother others with things that can be easily found on Baidu. In life, there are often people who don't use their brains or try to find solutions. If the other party encounters any problem and instead of solving it themselves, they just throw it into the group, then we don't need such a teammate. After all, we are not afraid of opponents who are like gods, but we are afraid of teammates who are like pigs. Therefore, if the other party really cannot handle this task, we can let her choose again. If the other party continues to push excuses or blame others, we can discuss it with another teammate and ask for her opinion and thoughts. If necessary, we can complete it together with the other party or, if there is time and opportunity, form a new team. 2. Identify which problems are our own and which ones the other party is trying to avoid. We can conduct a simple analysis to see which mistakes are ours and which are caused by the other party's lack of seriousness. Also, observe her interaction pattern and attitude toward the other teammate to determine if she behaves this way towards everyone or is deliberately targeting us. Identify the root of the problem and find a way to solve it. We can reassign tasks, try to coordinate internally first, and if it is really unsuitable, we shouldn't rush. If it is the other person's personal problem, changing teams will just bring about new problems. If the assignment is truly unreasonable, then we can redistribute it properly. Don't let other people's mistakes hurt ourselves. The world and I love you.

I can understand your frustration and anger towards your ability to handle the job. Your coworker seems to be incapable of handling her responsibilities, which is causing her to feel restless and emotional, but it has nothing to do with you. I recommend practicing open communication so that you can express your feelings honestly and feel more at ease. For instance, you can say something like, "I can see that you're feeling anxious and eager to perform well. However, when you rush me, it makes me feel uncomfortable. I hope we can communicate patiently and work together efficiently to solve problems and improve our collaboration." You can use this template as a reference and practice effective communication.

question: My 15-year-old cousin has begun a relationship with a troublemaking boyfriend of the same age and has run away from home twice. What should I do?
description: My 15-year-old cousin, due to careless friendships, has associated herself with thuggish classmates and a boyfriend, and has run away from home twice, living with her boyfriend for a week. Now she has developed a reluctance to study. She has only one more year before the high school entrance exam. Is there any way to help her get back on track?

answers.answer_text: 15 years old is indeed a rebellious age, so we need to first understand the cousin's upbringing environment, and then slowly guide her back on the right track. 1. What did the boyfriend provide her that made her disregard everything else? Many parents have a very negative impression of troublemakers, and every time they see their children with the other person, they are truly furious. Especially for parents who care about their reputation, their ways of preventing their children's association may be extreme, either completely cutting off contact or cutting off their financial resources. Therefore, we need to first clarify how the cousin views her boyfriend and what attitude she has towards him. If he truly likes her and treats her with enough respect, and even provides her with meticulous care, we must not have a biased perspective; we need to analyze comprehensively. In reality, children are sometimes simple; they are not as complicated as adults. They just hope to have someone who can listen to their thoughts, think from their perspective, and help them analyze problems, instead of forcing them to do things. 2. The parents' attitude is particularly important. If the parents' communication with the child always starts with "I have given you the best material life, so you should study harder and not disappoint the efforts we put in", then this kind of communication is meaningless. Therefore, we need to first have a conversation with the cousin's parents to see how they handle education in everyday life. We can also have a chat with the cousin to see what she thinks. Then, after considering all the circumstances, we can conduct a simple analysis, so that they have a basis for communication. This process will definitely be lengthy and will require a lot of effort from everyone involved. Therefore, we need to be prepared for a prolonged battle, learn to understand and tolerate each other, and learn to empathize. The world loves you.

Hello, it is clear that you are very concerned and worried about your cousin's "future," and I believe that her family and loved ones share the same concern. The behaviors you mentioned, which deviate from the "right path," often occur during adolescence and serve as signals and reflections of the difficulties teenagers face in terms of family relationships, academics, interpersonal relationships, and school adaptation. Sometimes, these behaviors can be directly linked to significant life events such as parental divorce or major losses. Therefore, the first thing her parents (or primary caregivers/guardians) need to do is examine what happened in the family or school before and after these behaviors occurred. Only by adjusting the family functioning (parents' mental and behavioral patterns, family and parent-child relationships, parenting styles, etc.) is there a chance to change the child's inner experience and self-awareness, thus leading to different behavioral choices. This is a systematic process that needs to start with parental introspection. Otherwise, relying on some external force (like a magical method) to hope that the child will "return to the right path" is risky and unlikely to succeed.

Hello, what can be the response of her parents to these behaviors of her cousin? What state was she in when she first befriended the troublemaking classmate and boyfriend? You can try to communicate with her to understand the feelings she had towards the troublemaking classmate and boyfriend. It is difficult to give direct advice here, as much information about her is needed. You can make an appointment for a consultation if necessary. Take care!

In American English:

Who knows what the right path is in this world? When we were young, we used to walk through fields of wheat, listening to the sounds of insects around us. We would pass by bamboo forests, hearing the sounds of bamboo growing, and walk by the mountainside, greeted by the smiling faces of trees. We would spend the whole day outside, not knowing when to return home. When we got hungry, it was easy to find something to eat - sour jujubes, wild apricots, walnuts. And when we were thirsty, there was always a small stream nearby. We used to be afraid of the dark at night, so naturally, we would go home. It was the darkness that allowed our body and soul to rest together. The concept of illness was almost non-existent. However, now children are constantly being vaccinated, constantly drinking water, constantly consuming various foods for nourishment. One group of mentally ill people creates another group of physically ill people. These illnesses interact with and differ from each other, striving to make everyone sick, and they call it "ideal." Staying up late, hanging out at bars, the flashy lights, and the lure of wealth and pleasure are all incompatible with the human body. Can you say that there won't be illnesses? Nowadays, problems begin with parents and then affect children. Let's search for the reasons starting from the parents.

question: Even small things can make one anxious, what should be done if someone is particularly prone to anxiety?
description: Even a small thing can make oneself feel irritable and restless, and when faced with sudden events, one may cry and be unable to explain. Recently, I have also noticed that when alone, those awkward moments that happened before occasionally flash in my mind, and I uncontrollably make sounds like "no, oh..." I have tried meditating to relieve these symptoms, but perhaps due to lack of consistency, the effect is minimal.
keywords: Growing up, developing one's character, personality traits, and self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner: It seems like you are experiencing unbearable pain due to anxiety, is that correct? I am not aware of your age. Are you a male friend or a female friend? When did the intense anxiety begin? I wonder if the current anxiety is affecting your sleep and daily work-life? When it comes to using meditation to alleviate anxiety, it requires long-term training. Generally speaking, normal feelings of anxiety have a positive function as they can help us deal with crises, maintain a sense of alertness, and protect us in challenging environments. Furthermore, moderate anxiety can drive us to be more efficient and motivated. However, if someone has an anxiety disorder due to excessively sensitive personality traits, it is a different matter. Generally speaking, treating severe anxiety involves evaluating a person's personality traits and identifying sources of stress. If anxiety is linked to a person's personality traits, psychoanalysis may be considered for systematic treatment. If anxiety is related to real-life stress, short-term cognitive-behavioral therapy may be considered. Additionally, practicing diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation training can also help alleviate anxiety. Mindfulness, introspection, meditation, yoga, and other practices can also be used therapeutically after a period of training. However, everyone's personality traits and family background are different, so the chosen treatment methods may vary. Given the limited understanding of your situation, the above analysis is for reference only.

question: Should I delete the photos in the old photo album that I am hesitant about? Is it repetitive action?
description: I am a person who especially likes taking photos, it's actually not bad. I am sensitive. I like to take photos of beautiful scenery. But I don't know if I have some perfectionism, I want to capture anything beautiful. And I want to document my beautiful life from various angles, finding the most beautiful perspective. Sometimes I even feel disappointed when the effect is not what I expected. Later, I tell myself that there are many beautiful things and many worth remembering, I don't have to capture everything. I have a hard time choosing and I'm indecisive when selecting photos at home. I want to keep them all, but then I feel like I've burdened myself too much, as there are too many beautiful things, should I document every one of them? I hesitate to delete them. Deleting them would bring relief, but I am reluctant to do so. Deleting would make me feel lighter, but keeping them all feels heavy. I upload them all to the cloud, but then realize that the photo album is empty, and I am afraid of mixing the recovered ones with newly taken ones. It's so confusing. When I'm playing, I think of the album, when I'm walking, I think of organizing the album. I delete and recover, delete and recover. I rely on my intuition to judge whether to keep this photo or not. Is this a disease? What should I do? I despise the emptiness of the album, so I recover some of the previously deleted photos. I'm afraid to take photos now. Taking too many photos makes me feel heavy, is it because of perfectionism? What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Guess. Deleting or not deleting may just be a matter of action. You also described how you felt when you were struggling with whether or not to delete the rain in the mountains. But there may be an important reason behind this. What does deleting or not deleting mean to you? Or what happened and how did you feel when you first realized that you had this situation?

question: How can I motivate myself to make progress? Does buying gifts as a self-motivation work?
description: Lack of motivation and drive due to a lack of ambition. I've heard that buying gifts can motivate oneself, is this effective? Are there any other methods?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Is buying gifts enough to motivate oneself? It seems that some people can be motivated and more willing to make efforts under the motivation of gifts. However, such external motivation is very short-lived and can easily cause a loss of interest in learning or work itself. In the book "Drive", it is mentioned that material rewards such as promotions and salary increases are temporary and ineffective when it comes to creative work. Personally, a lack of drive is likely because you haven't found something you truly love, or you have been severely frustrated by studying and working in the past, or you simply haven't mastered the method of making progress, or you haven't experienced the sense of achievement that comes from hard work paying off. So, how can one enhance their drive? First, find something you truly enjoy doing and have the potential to excel at, let that passion become your internal drive. Second, turn drive into a habit. There are many books on developing habits, such as "The Power of Habit", which I recommend you study for methods. Then, set a goal, use the loop of "goal, cue, feedback" to develop a habit of making progress. Third, cultivate a sense of responsibility. In fact, drive often has to do with a sense of responsibility. You need to be responsible for the people close to you, your work, and the people you collaborate with. You also need to be responsible for yourself, so you need to better fulfill tasks and provide value to others and yourself. Drive is a trait that everyone has and needs to explore and cultivate, and it requires internal motivation.

question: I keep dreaming that I haven't studied for exams and haven't completed my assignments. How can I relieve anxiety?
description: Every night, I dream about anxious and stressful things, such as having an exam without studying, or starting school without completing assignments (I am already working). In my dreams, I often wander repeatedly in dark corridors. I frequently wake up in the middle of the night, finding my hands tightly clenched with thumbs tucked inside, feeling extremely anxious. Meditation helps me fall asleep quickly, but my sleep quality is poor. How can I alleviate this?
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, anxiety emotions, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Hello, my dear, sending you a hug. After reading your description, I can see that even though you have started working, you still have dreams about unfinished school tasks, which are causing poor sleep and severe anxiety. I really understand and sympathize with your current situation. Based on what you've said, it seems that your recent feelings of nervousness and anxiety may be due to high work pressure or some minor setbacks in life that are difficult for you to forget. This has resulted in bringing this anxiety into what should be a restful sleep. If you feel that this situation is seriously affecting your work and personal life, it is important to seek medical treatment promptly to rule out the possibility of mental illness. Regarding your desire to improve the quality of your sleep, I suggest creating a quiet and comfortable sleep environment for yourself. Avoid having work-related objects, such as your phone or laptop, near you as they can remind you of work pressure. I hope this advice can be helpful to you.

question: An unintentional action made me feel uncomfortable, is it a sign of paranoia?
description: In the morning, his phone rang while he was in the bathroom getting ready to take a shower. I told him his phone was ringing and he said to ignore it for now. As I was about to go see who was calling and pass him the phone, I don't know when exactly, but he quickly took the phone from behind me. Wasn't he supposed to be showering? Hahaha, is it just my excessive suspicion or is something wrong? Why do I suddenly feel uncomfortable?

answers.answer_text: Host, good Thursday morning! I can sense that while the host appears suspicious, there is also a sense of detached humor. At the moment, there doesn't seem to be any substantial issues in this relationship. #In the morning, his phone rang while he was in the bathroom getting ready to take a shower. I told him his phone was ringing, and he said to ignore it. I was about to go see who was calling and hand him the phone, but at some point, he had already taken the phone from behind me. Wasn't he supposed to be showering? Hahaha, is it just my excessive suspicion, or is there something else going on that makes me feel uncomfortable? It is a normal reaction for the host to feel uncomfortable because the host might think that there shouldn't be any privacy between them. However, the actual situation may be different from the host's boyfriend's perspective. Whether each person should have their own privacy, even in front of their closest person, is a question that the host and the boyfriend have to answer together. This is also one of the things you both need to work on in your future relationship. Some things exist if you believe in them, and don't exist if you don't. This principle is based on the fact that your suspicion pushes the other person towards that assumption, and that assumption confirms your suspicion. As a result, trust between the two of you becomes more distant. Some things, when you "know" them, should be treated as if you don't know. The other person is yours and will eventually come back. Some things do not need to be exposed and talked about, because in the end, both parties will be harmed. This is another level of conducting oneself. The host's current problem may not necessarily be related to this, but I'm saying all this just to express that each person interprets, handles, and reaches different levels of understanding regarding a behavior or an event. Right? I believe that someone as smart as you understands these principles. Managing a relationship is like planting a big tree, it's not something that can be completed in a day or two or through a single action. It requires little by little, slowly experiencing, sincerely expressing, and caring wholeheartedly. That's it. Best wishes to you! The world and I love you!

question: Someone wants to maliciously expel me from school, what should I do?
description: The teacher wants to maliciously expel me because I have experienced verbal violence on campus. Every night during evening study, they shout and curse outside the classroom. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Are you sure the teacher was scolding you? Do you remember what they were scolding you about? Did any classmates hear the teacher scolding you too? If you are certain, I suggest you record the audio as evidence. Then, inform your parents about it. I believe they will help you handle this properly. As a victim of campus violence, don't be afraid. You must speak up to your parents and trustworthy individuals. In this world, no one has the right to intentionally harm others, and no one is born to be bullied. Do you understand? If the teacher is really trying to force you to drop out of school, don't fall into their trap. In the course of growing up, we will encounter kindness as well as malice. When we encounter kindness, we should be grateful and warm ourselves. When we encounter malice, we should choose to accept what is useful and block out what is not. In other words, when someone stabs us with a knife (uses hurtful words), we can choose to fight back (respond in kind) or choose to ignore it (remove the knife and heal ourselves). But never pull out the knife and stab ourselves (get upset, sad, regretful, blame ourselves, self-harm, etc.).

question: I don't know how to establish an emotional connection with the world, what should I do?
description: I am a high school student. This issue has been bothering me for several years. I feel like I have no emotional connection with this world. I am always a serious person and the topics I discuss with others are always about studying and planning. Most of my social interactions are with teachers because I call them once a week to do something like a work report and discuss the feasibility of some plans. I am more familiar with the path to success, but my relationships with classmates are a bit awkward. Although my classmates trust my problem-solving abilities, no one wants to spend time with me. It feels like we only talk about business matters and there is no emotional exchange. I am studying abroad, so I only call my parents once every few months because they are only interested in hearing about my academic progress and not my personal life. No one cares about how I feel or what I think, which makes me feel exhausted. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello! The phrase "how to establish an emotional connection with the world" is quite abstract. People are the world and the world is people, so what we are actually discussing is how to establish an emotional connection with others. The statement "the essence of interpersonal relationships is the exchange of social value" may sound cold, but what is social value? And what is self-worth? These questions have been debated by humans for thousands of years without a definitive answer. Why? Because these questions themselves don't have answers. Some people are willing to spend a month's salary to attend a concert of their favorite celebrity because, in their heart, the value of meeting that celebrity is much higher than their own hard work for a month. So you see, some values cannot be measured. Artificial intelligence can defeat all the top Go players in the world but it cannot even tell a joke. This clearly demonstrates that human emotions are the most complex and precious. The biggest problem with utilitarianism is that it only emphasizes results and overlooks the process, overlooking the emotions that humans possess as humans. The reason why we are human is that our ancestors were "wise humans," we have free will, and we have complex and diverse emotions. Kant said: "Man is an end in itself, not a means." Jung said: "The least significant but meaningful things in life are more valuable than the greatest but meaningless things." Have you ever thought about why we strive to study? We strive to study to have a better life experience, but if we lose the beautiful life experience because of studying, isn't that a paradox? "No one cares about my feelings, no one cares about my thoughts, and it makes me feel tired. What should I do?" Interpersonal relationships are mutual. If you want to receive care from others, then you must first learn to care about others' feelings and thoughts. As a high school student, it should be easy to understand the concept of putting oneself in another person's shoes, right? In fact, from a certain perspective, there is a subtle "opposition" relationship between teachers and students, just like most people would be happy when they know they don't have to go to school on vacation. Being too close to teachers will instinctively cause classmates to "distance" themselves from you. Many times, right and wrong are not absolute but relative. Occasionally making small mistakes when being with classmates can increase trust and friendship. Take some time to participate in social activities, interact with peers more, listen to their thoughts, even if they may be different from yours, but accepting others with a "gentlemanly harmony and difference" attitude may be the beginning of a wonderful relationship. I wish you a happy life!

"Topics of conversation with others always revolve around studying and making arrangements. First of all, your understanding of conversation is incorrect. Conversations are casual, leisurely, enjoyable, and free-flowing. They have no specific purpose, are lighthearted, and filled with positive energy. These characteristics are not desirable in work communication, but they are essential in conversations. The topics you mentioned are still work-related, serious, and formal, with a sense of suppression and negativity in order to get things done. Thinking that work communication equals conversation is a cognitive error. "I feel like I have no emotional connection with this world." Conversation is a social instinct that can also be developed into a skill. It is the foundation for building relationships, including family, friendship, and romantic relationships, all of which are based on conversation. Without conversation, there can be no emotional connection. Furthermore, since it is an instinct, it is as simple as eating and drinking, but because you haven't used this instinct for a long time, you have suppressed it. What you need to do is not "learn" to have a conversation, but to "unleash" it. This requires actively solving interpersonal communication problems encountered in daily life. "Most of my social interactions are with teachers..." These are all social interactions in the context of work, and they tend to be somewhat cold. "I am more familiar with the paths of the higher-ups, but the relationships between classmates are a bit awkward." The consequence of this is becoming a workaholic and living a dull life. If life is compared to a meal, workaholics will only have plain rice while everyone else has a variety of dishes. Moreover, workaholics also use work to avoid interpersonal relationships and hobbies in real life. It is awkward between you and your classmates, but not between other classmates, because classmates give and listen to each other, and listening is also a form of giving. God has given us two ears and one mouth so that we can listen more and speak less. As long as you are willing to listen to others, the problem of conversation will be solved by 80%. Helping classmates is also a form of giving. It is evident that you have various abilities, so give more to your classmates. "Because they only listen to my academic content and don't care about my life. Nobody cares about my feelings, nobody cares about my thoughts, it makes me feel exhausted." If your parents don't care about your emotions, you can't change them. In that case, let go of your dependence on them and become independent. What they can't give you, earn it yourself. Treat others the way you want to be treated. If you want others to care about you and your feelings and thoughts, then treat others the same way."

Hello, questioner! Feeling lonely and helpless can indeed be awful. When you want to get close to someone, you suddenly realize that there is no one around whom you can confide in. It is often said that no man is an island, and emotional connections are important in our lives. Here are a few small suggestions that you can consider. 1. Acknowledge yourself. From your description, it is evident that you are more exceptional than most people of your age. You are familiar with working at higher levels (as a teacher), possess strong problem-solving abilities, and have good creative thinking skills (discussing plans with teachers). Your ability to communicate with teachers is also quite good. It must be said that you are truly outstanding. 2. In your description, you mentioned being a serious person. I wonder if that means you don't like to laugh, don't enjoy joking around with others, or don't take on the role of being the one who lightens the atmosphere? Strong individuals often become leaders within a group. So, imagine constantly working under a serious leader - would you also become serious? Your classmates see you this way, as more of a leader-subordinate relationship. 3. Class activities can help improve relationships between classmates. If appropriate, you can plan class activities in collaboration with teachers. This will allow everyone to participate together, fostering closer relationships and providing a chance to relax. 4. Being alone in a foreign country can make you feel detached from the outside world and disconnected from emotional connections. Parents are often the people we are closest to, so staying in touch with them is inevitable. I'm not sure if your parents are very busy, but instead of being passive, taking the initiative to regularly video chat with them and share photos of your life abroad can help them understand your life outside of school. I hope this is helpful to you. Whenever you have time, go out and explore the world. Sometimes, you may also come to appreciate the joy of being alone.

Hello! Thank you for the invitation! You are a high school student who is already studying abroad alone, and you have smooth communication with your teachers. This shows that your academic situation is very good! Although you don't have much interaction with your classmates, your classmates trust you, which is really impressive! It shows that your independent way of doing things is recognized by everyone. However, why do you still have the confusion of "no one cares about my feelings, no one cares about my thoughts, which makes me feel tired. What should I do"? Let's analyze it together: in interpersonal communication, everyone has their own style. Some people are outgoing and enjoy interacting with others naturally. Others will contact him more actively because they know he likes to interact with others, so they don't feel like they are burdening him. People with your style, like you, may be seen as preferring to be alone, so others will respect you and think that bothering you less is most in line with your personality. But this does not mean that they are unwilling to interact with you or that they don't care about you. It's just that your independent personality doesn't give them more opportunities to express themselves. In addition, outgoing people also have their own troubles because interacting with people takes time. In a sense, they have to sacrifice their independent and free time to socialize with friends. Are you willing to do that? We cannot expect that when we need someone, they will appear, and when we need to be alone, they will leave. This is impossible in interpersonal communication. From your self-description, you have earned recognition from your teachers and classmates. If you want to have more interaction with them, just take the initiative. When you convey this message, your teachers and classmates will approach you because you have given them the impression that you are trustworthy. So, don't be pessimistic, accept yourself as you are now, and make some efforts towards the direction you want to change. You are the best!

Yes, if you have not experienced emotional communication at home since childhood and have not learned it at school, where everything is focused on achieving goals, it is natural to feel that there is a missing part in your life, but you do not know how to describe it. I understand your confusion very well. The first step in establishing emotional communication with others is to open yourself up to the world, just like a baby learning to walk, taking small steps and practicing repeatedly. Find someone you trust the most, it doesn't have to be your parents, but preferably someone you trust enough, could be a mentor who understands people or a close friend. Opening up does not mean talking about things, but expressing your feelings, your emotions, sharing your joy and unhappiness, what kind of joy, what kind of unhappiness, what expectations and worries you have, what dreams and setbacks you have, tell them little by little. Learn to express your feelings, not to discuss things. When others feel your emotions, they will respond accordingly. If you cannot find such a person in your life, you can seek professional psychological counseling support and learn from them. There is a feeling that you should allow yourself to cry, even in front of others; of course, you should also allow yourself to laugh uncontrollably.

I guess you are probably a good student. You mentioned that your classmates trust you to handle problems, which suggests that you are indeed better than them in this aspect. I'm not sure if your daily way of doing things or speaking is too serious. If that is the case, you may not come across as approachable, and your classmates may not feel comfortable joking around with you. It depends on how you view relationships among classmates and how you approach friendships. I'm not sure if your focus is more on studying or if you have high expectations for yourself. Apart from studying, you could take some time to chat with the people around you about other things. Sometimes, chatting may feel like a waste of time, but on the other hand, it is also a way to expand your network and improve your communication skills. Slow down and observe what the people around you are doing, and then compare what you might be missing. Try to enter into their conversation topics. In certain aspects, you may be better than the people around you, which creates a gap between you, such as in daily conversation topics. Are those the kind of conversations you want to have, or are you open to other topics? Start by expanding your topics for everyday conversation.

Hello, from your description, I see that you may not be very satisfied with your current interpersonal communication skills, especially in the aspect of emotional communication. Is that correct? At the same time, I also noticed that you have a good communication with your teachers, because you mentioned being "familiar with the senior route". Is that so? Usually, young people of your age tend to have difficulty getting along with their teachers, but you seem to have a different feeling. I guess you must have accumulated some experience in this regard. Perhaps you can also apply your experience to your interactions with peers, what do you think? Take care of yourself.

question: It is very uncomfortable to think that one has grown up already?
description: Reluctant. And have a deep fear of independence, so deeply rely on others.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, meaning of life

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, I understand that 1. OP feels fearful about growing up 2. OP is afraid of independence and has a reliance on others internally. [Some analysis and suggestions] 1. These feelings are normal. On one hand, you are facing a completely new growth environment, which can make people feel uneasy and panicked. On the other hand, growing up means that you will have to make some changes that may currently be unknown, and you will have to face more difficulties. So, it is normal and common for you to feel fearful and not want to grow up. 2. But actually, if you think about it from a different perspective, you also understand that you cannot avoid growing up. Growing up is a problem that you must face. However, growing up does not necessarily mean complete independence. There is a long transitional period from being a child to becoming an adult. It's not just you who needs to go through this transition, but parents also need a transition to realize that their child has grown up. During this stage, you can still rely on others, but you can also try to learn from observing how your elders handle things and accumulate your own experience. From this perspective, is it not so difficult? I hope this helps you.

question: Why do I always feel unfair? Thinking about these things at night will cause insomnia.
description: Sometimes, I feel depressed and can't fall asleep. My mind keeps racing, unable to stop thinking about things. I toss and turn for hours without being able to sleep.
keywords: Behavior, anxiety, confusion, staying up late.

answers.answer_text:
Hello, I see that you are feeling very distressed because you are unable to sleep at night due to thinking about something. Here's a big hug for you. 🤗 Every one of us experiences situations where we are unable to sleep because of thoughts running through our minds. I sometimes go through the same thing. If something is causing you to lose sleep, the best solution is to resolve that issue. I don't know what has been happening in your real life as you haven't provided much information. But based on your title, it seems like you have been facing some unfair treatment in life. When we encounter unfairness, we feel a sense of injustice and anger. Expressing this unfairness can help us feel better. However, it seems like you have been silently enduring it on your own, which can make you feel suppressed and lead to overthinking, resulting in sleepless nights. Based on my experience, I have the following suggestions for you: 
First, when you can't sleep at night because of thoughts, don't force yourself to sleep. You'll find that the more you try to sleep, the more difficult it becomes, which then triggers anxiety. So, accept the fact that you can't sleep. 
Second, when you can't sleep, try writing down the things that are on your mind. It can be anything, such as events that happened during the day, your emotions, and even expressing your anger towards others on paper. Letting out your inner frustrations can provide emotional release. When you're in a better emotional state, you can reflect on why this situation has triggered such emotions in you. What unfulfilled needs of yours might be involved? What can you learn from this situation? Once you identify your needs and the lessons you can take from this, your perspective will change, and your emotions will greatly decrease. 
Third, you can also talk to friends or family members, as sharing and confiding in others is a great way to release emotions. Perhaps your loved ones can provide you with more solutions. Alright, I hope my response is helpful to you.

Hello! There are always things in life that can bother us and make it difficult to let go. When these things accumulate and weigh heavily on our hearts without an outlet for release, they can potentially affect us, making us feel somewhat depressed and impacting our sleep and quality of life. So how can we learn to release these emotions? 1. Understand the concept of "impermanence." Realize that everything in life is constantly changing, including our thoughts. Just like a waterfall, our thoughts flow and shift. What we think today may change tomorrow, and something that seems bad today may turn into something good tomorrow. As Confucius said, "All things pass like this." The past is gone, and no matter how much we think about it, we can't change it. The only option is to let go. 2. Live in the present moment. People who dwell in the past are prone to depression, while those who focus on the future tend to be anxious. Therefore, we need to learn to live in the present moment. What does it mean to "live in the present"? In my understanding, it means doing what needs to be done at the moment. For example, during work hours, focus solely on work and do it well; when eating, concentrate on the taste of each bite; when sleeping, completely relax the body and mind, allowing yourself to enter a state of peaceful sleep. 3. Establish goals in life. Ask yourself what kind of life you want. Everyone has their own roles, so set long-term and short-term goals for yourself. Having goals gives life direction, allowing you to single-mindedly move towards them rather than drifting aimlessly like a floating duckweed. Anchor yourself like a tree with deep roots. 4. Develop regular habits and cultivate action through habits. Determine what tasks can be done at specific times each day - when to wake up, exercise, study, work - and engage in activities that promote physical health, build skills, and strengthen the mind. Develop habits and experience personal growth day by day. Keep yourself busy and fulfilled, so there's no time to dwell on unnecessary things. You will also find that each day you become more capable and happier. 5. Regarding sleep, there's a little trick: when you go to bed, tell yourself, "I'm going to sleep now. I will count 20 breaths, and with each breath, I will become more relaxed." You can also find some relaxation or guided sleep audio online to listen to. Regular exercise every day can also help reduce excessive thinking and improve sleep. Wishing you happiness and joy every day! I hope my reply can be helpful to you. Thank you for your question.

question: Graduate students, I feel like it will not be easy to find a job after graduation, it feels very uncertain.
description: I am a graduate student from a non-prestigious school, and I don't think I will have good job prospects after graduation. I have no idea what to do! Even though I am only in my first year of graduate school, I still feel helpless. I feel like there is no hope.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ From your description, it seems like you're going through a lot of stress. I can relate as I've been preparing to find a job myself, and I understand how overwhelming the pressure can be. It could be that I lack some personal qualities, as there is a significant salary difference between graduate and undergraduate students. So, being a graduate student might give you an advantage in that regard. Since you're still in your first year of graduate school, it might be best to focus on your studies for now. There is still so much to learn, and once you can master the material you need to study, it might boost your confidence and help you become more self-assured. As a graduate student, you have plenty of options for job hunting, and you can also explore opportunities in academic research. Believe in yourself more and try to reduce your anxiety, as it might help you overcome the challenges that lie ahead more effectively. Best of luck~.

question: Son is in third grade of elementary school, how to deal with the child's refusal to study?
description: I am about to collapse. My son is in third grade and he is very clever, but he doesn't like studying. Every night, I have to shout and coax him to finish his homework. I have tried everything - hitting, scolding, praising, and even pushing him out of the door. Nothing works. Last night, it got so bad that I had to look up the answers for him while he sat there motionless. I got angry and beat him up really badly. It exhausted me. But tonight, he still refuses to do his homework. I look at the bruises on his body and I can't help but blame myself for not having a good son. I don't know how to educate him anymore. Is it possible that people are just born different? Isn't he just not cut out for studying?
keywords: Family, family relationships, growing up process, communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: Although the original poster is already furious and exhausted, I have to say that the problem lies with the original poster. Of course, this whole situation is not entirely the original poster's fault, but it is their problem that it has reached this point of deadlock. [They are very smart but just don't like studying], this judgment needs to be retracted because it already reflects the original poster's mindset. The relationship in this situation is between the child and studying. Imagine if the original poster is an embroiderer who is also a helpless servant with no place to go. As an embroiderer, the original poster is highly skilled, but they just don't want to take action. Is it because the embroidery is too difficult? If it's because the embroidery is too difficult, wouldn't it be better if the master put in efforts to help (like "I'll search for answers in the book for him")? Now the master has tried everything, from scolding to coaxing, hitting, scolding, praising, and even pushing the original poster out of the door, but the original poster would rather endure a beating than pick up the needle. So, at this time, who is the original poster fighting against? Is it the embroidery or the master? Most likely, the original poster is using the embroidery as a way to resist the parents. Do they want to achieve something? No way. The more they want to achieve something, the less I will take action. As an embroiderer of the original poster, if they are dissatisfied, why don't they rise up and resist? Of course, it's because they are powerless and incapable, and even if they are willing to shed blood, there is no chance of victory. When India wanted to gain independence from the British Commonwealth, why didn't they have an armed uprising and instead chose a form of non-violent non-cooperation? As for the specific problems faced by the original poster, the one who needs to figure it out is the original poster themselves, they need to carefully consider, put themselves in others' shoes, and think about how this situation gradually formed and how to untie it.

question: Always treating myself as an outsider, not knowing what's wrong with myself...
description: Due to the divorce of my parents, many complicated things happened, and maybe I thought too much and it became too complicated. I didn't know how to face it, so I chose to escape. I avoided facing these things, avoided facing my biological father, and avoided facing everyone at my grandma's house. I think there is already a stepdaughter who has replaced my position. My existence is redundant, a burden. I believe that these people will always be a family with my father, and they have also hurt me together with my father. I don't know how to respond when my cousin is friendly to me. I think they only have superficial relationships with me. On the one hand, I don't know how to interact with them normally. On the other hand, they have a bad relationship with my mom, and I worry that my mom will raise me alone and I'm afraid of losing her. I cut off all contact with these people. I simply thought that I had completely disappeared from their lives, and their lives would be cleaner and easier without me. I called my aunt yesterday and found out that they have been thinking about me all these years. They have never treated me as an outsider. Even though we haven't been in touch for many years, they still mention me and think about me. When my grandpa passed away, they couldn't reach me either because they didn't have my WeChat. Grandpa must have left with regrets... I wonder what grandpa would have advised me if we could have been in contact at that time.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: I think you must feel regretful, guilty, and remorseful now - because you made the presumptuous choice to avoid it, leading to your grandfather's regretful passing. I want to give you a hug and comfort you - you don't have to be too hard on yourself, feeling that you were willful or something. I'm not sure how old you were when your parents divorced, but it feels to me that you were probably still underage at the time, and with your father already having a stepdaughter, most people in your situation would have made a similar choice. There is a book called "Letters from Heaven." If possible, I hope you can take some time to regain your spirits, reminisce about the time you spent with your grandfather, slowly write it down, write down the regrets in your heart and the words you want to say to your grandfather, then choose a day to burn the letter. I think, in this way, your letter and thoughts will surely reach your grandfather in heaven. I believe that while you feel remorse and regret, you must also feel a little warmth. All along, you thought you were extra, a burden, but now you have discovered that there are actually many people always thinking of you, worrying about you. This feeling of being loved is beautiful, like suddenly seeing a sky full of stars when lost in darkness, like encountering a bonfire in the biting cold wind. In the past, you chose to avoid, but now that you have suddenly realized, they still care about you. I think, maybe this time you don't have to choose to avoid anymore, try to respond to their love, respond to their care. At the beginning, it will surely be a bit awkward and uncomfortable, after all, you haven't seen each other for so many years, but avoiding will only make you feel more remorseful. I'm not sure if you called your second aunt yesterday, but you can think back, actually, sometimes rebuilding connections isn't that difficult, and it's not as bad as you think. Whether it's love between lovers or care between relatives and friends, they all need mutual responses. Don't let love cool down. Finally, I think this incident is also a warning for you and me, for everyone - don't make presumptions, especially about the strong bond of blood. Of course, when I write this, I realize that I seem to have overlooked what role your mother would play. But I think even if parents divorce, they shouldn't interfere with a child's love for their father/mother. Parents' divorce is their own matter and has nothing to do with the child. I believe your parents will understand, and you will be able to handle this relationship well. That's all.

Hello! After reading your description, I feel somewhat saddened for you. Regardless of whether the way it was handled was good or not, the divorce of your parents inevitably has some impact, no matter how old the child is. You mentioned that many complicated things have happened, although you didn't specifically mention what they are, I can imagine that these things have had a profound effect on you. Perhaps you feel a sense of loss, a breakdown of trust, and insecurity, among other negative emotions. However, divorce is originally an issue between parents, but in the failed marriage of your parents, you experience a strong sense of abandonment. I feel that this sense of being abandoned is partly a substitution for your mother's feelings and trauma. You worry about your mother, worry about her sadness and grief, empathize with her pain. You even feel that maintaining contact and a good relationship with your father's side of the family would be betraying your mother. So, you put yourself in a position where you truly feel abandoned, imagining that they don't care about your existence, don't care about you, or have already replaced you with someone else. You are unwilling to contact your father's relatives, unwilling to acknowledge their friendliness. When you found out that they had always been thinking about you, even when your grandfather passed away with regrets, your inner self was both distressed and bewildered. I feel sorry for you. As children, sometimes we cannot influence our parents' decisions. What we can do, besides accepting, there is nothing more. However, for ourselves, we will always be free and able to make choices. We cannot choose to live in an intact family or a single-parent family. But we can choose our attitude when faced with imperfections. Return your mother's life to her, you are your own person. Allow your parents to truly make a choice about their marriage, and we must find our own suitable existence in this turbulent situation. When you can be yourself in addition to being your mother's child, you will know that, at the same time, you have many relationships that are also trustworthy. They will also give you warmth. They are also relationships you can try to give and depend on each other. Best wishes to you!

Hello! As a child, you are innocent in your parents' separation. Your parents did not manage this marriage well, and your father chose to remarry and form a new family. You feel hurt and isolated, and you may wonder if your mother feels abandoned and that is why you have this feeling. Are you avoiding facing the root cause of your father's actions? Marriage should be equal, and your mother also has the right to choose her own life. The parent-child relationship does not break because of the breakdown of the marriage relationship. The parent-child relationship also needs to be nurtured. Is your father's love different from the love for his stepdaughter? Love and material things are not the same, love does not diminish because it is shared. If it diminishes, it means that two people's hearts have drifted apart. You and your father and your grandparents will always be a family. Recent events have made you realize that you are deeply concerned about this family. Your relationship with this family will not change because of your father's remarriage. It's heartbreaking that the relationship between your mother and your father's family is not good, and it makes you sad. You are worried that getting close to your grandparents will hurt your mother's feelings. In fact, you can discuss with your mother: "Mom, can I get closer to Grandma and Grandpa's house? Do you mind?" In your heart, you may be concerned that your mother's love is possessive or demanding. Mothers usually want their children to receive love from more people, rather than possessive love. Sometimes relatives may not bring you much joy, but they are the ones who care about you. A mother's love for you should not be possessive. Being close to Grandma and Grandpa's house is not a betrayal of your mother's emotions. Your love for your father should not be possessive either. Your father's remarriage is not an emotional abandonment of you. Only independent love is long-lasting and happy love. When we need each other's company, we should speak up; when we need space, we should let each other be brave enough to be ourselves. You are amazing for being able to express your feelings. I hope you are healthy and happy! Love yourself, love your father, love your mother, love your family, love your nation!

Hello, I understand what you're going through. It's really difficult to see how you constantly blame yourself for all the mistakes, while it seems like others don't make any. But the truth is, you are the one who is vulnerable, the one who gets hurt. If you truly feel that someone is good to you, and you know that they would worry if they couldn't find you, would you cut off contact with them for no reason? The answer is definitely no. It's clear that your dad's side of the family doesn't make you feel that way, at least they haven't made you feel that you can still experience their love after your parents' divorce. Instead, they make you feel like they hurt you along with your dad. You might think that your feelings are unfounded, but I can assure you that regardless of whether others intentionally or unintentionally give you this feeling, they definitely do. Otherwise, why haven't you felt that they care about you? It's simply because they haven't made you feel that they genuinely care about you. As for caring and missing you, I think it's natural for elders to feel some degree of it, but for you, who has been affected by your parents' divorce, it's far from enough. Because you, who have been hurt, need more, and they just haven't given you that. So you don't need to blame yourself for the care that should naturally be there, because when you needed more care, they didn't provide it. Lastly, I want to emphasize the most important point: in your description, you mention the concern of many people towards you, but you don't mention your father. Honestly, the influence of parents on us is the most significant, and obviously, your father hasn't done what he should have, otherwise you wouldn't have missed out on the concern from others. Originally, your parents' divorce is something that only concerns them, but clearly, as a child, you have become the victim of their strained relationship. You have lost the care and love that should have been yours. Maybe when you were younger, you didn't have the ability to make decisions.
