But now that you've grown up, you can decide whether or not to maintain the relationships that are rightfully yours. For example, with your cousin, grandmother, aunt, etc. If you want to, then reply and stay in touch with everyone, because you already have a blood relationship with them and you don't necessarily have to go through your father. But if deep down you still don't want that, or if you're not ready yet, then for now, don't reach out. You have the power to decide everything on your own. And as for your grandfather's regrets, you are the most vulnerable and the victim of your parents' divorce, you should never have to bear them. So don't burden yourself with responsibilities that should be carried by adults.

Seeing your experience, it's very heart-wrenching. I imagine that most children from divorced families go through this stage. It's not your fault; it's probably what you could do at that age. "You feel like your step-sister, who already has a father, has replaced you and that your existence is redundant and burdensome, believing that these people are forever a family with your father." Maybe you feel that your parents' divorce is somehow caused by your "badness". You feel like you deserve to be "abandoned" and not worthy of being "a family" with your father. So you question your cousin's kindness towards you and believe that their kindness towards you is just a facade. "Their relationship with my mother is not good, and I worry that my mother will raise me alone and fear losing me." Being the "superfluous" and "burdensome" one who is fortunate enough to be "taken in" by your mother, you are grateful and indebted to her, how can you engage in relationships with these people who have a difficult relationship with your mother? Being in a relationship with them may, to some extent, indicate that you are not in sync with your mother. As a result, you may lose your mother, and at the same time, she may lose you (abandon you). The hearts of many children from divorced families are caught in-between their parents and do not know how to handle the emotions from their parents. They are afraid of inadvertently "offending" them and suffering the fate of being "abandoned" again. How old are you now? Having such awareness shows that you have realized that thinking of yourself as an outsider is inappropriate. Your parents' divorce is an issue between the two adults and has nothing to do with you. The new family formed by your parents can be considered your family as well. In reality, living with one parent for a long time may cause some unfamiliarity when interacting with the other parent. But "blood is thicker than water," that is an undeniable fact. In reality, there are also some divorced "immature" parents who pull their children to their side and speak ill of the other party. In such a situation, children do not need to argue or defend for either parent. If capable, they can help calm the emotions of both sides. If not, it's great to try to shield themselves from the influence of their parents.

Hello, OP! First, let me give you a big hug. Let's take a look at your issue: your parents divorced, and you chose to avoid your father's side of the family, feeling that your existence is unnecessary after the divorce. In fact, this is a common problem faced by many people today, including myself. Fortunately, I have a good relationship with both sides of my parents and extended family. They did not neglect me because of the presence of new people in our family. I believe your parents are the same. Whether your parents divorce is not something we can decide. What we can do is to focus on ourselves, live our own lives, and fulfill our own responsibilities. Your belief that your existence is unnecessary is based on your own thoughts. Your actions may make you feel more relaxed, as you don't have to face what you perceive as unpleasant relationships. However, your father's side of the family may feel hurt. After all, people have emotions. If you put yourself in their shoes, I believe you would also feel upset. I suggest you try to maintain contact with your father's side of the family. Don't worry about stepdaughters and other issues. Just go with the flow and follow your heart. No matter what, your father's side of the family are your relatives. You share the same blood, and you are a family. Your concern for your mother's feelings regarding her relationship with your father's side of the family shows your filial piety and your love for your mother. However, it is natural for us to need both a father's love and a mother's love. But regardless of which aspect is missing, it can cause psychological problems. In this situation, I suggest you communicate with your mother and ask about her feelings. The most important thing is to let your mother understand that even if you have a better relationship with your father's side of the family, your love for her is the greatest. This will increase your mother's sense of security. Discovering that your father's side of the family still remembers you, even after many years of no contact, and wanting to know about regrets when your grandfather passed away, shows that your father's side of the family cares about you. Your grandfather, cousin, and even your father. I believe you can accept the kindness from your cousin and your father's side of the family and reciprocate with your love. They want to make up for regrets and guilt by treating you well. Why not fulfill their wishes? At the same time, this can help alleviate the lack of paternal love within you. As for your grandfather, the regrets have already happened. I think his advice is simply to let you let go of the issue of your parents' divorce. This has nothing to do with you. Don't get stuck in it and start your own life. In my opinion, the best thing you can do is to live your own life, no longer affected by your parents' divorce, and find happiness and joy. Meanwhile, regardless of which side of the family, follow your own heart, cherish the present moment and the people in front of you, so that there will be no regrets. This is just my personal opinion, and I hope it can help you. Best wishes!

question: Do boys really get so busy that they can't spare a minute to send a message in 24 hours?
description: My boyfriend has started to have a feeling of fatigue. He often plays by himself and ignores me. Is it really possible to go 24 hours without sending a message? What is he doing exactly?
keywords: Love, sense of security, arguments, relationship management

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your brief description, it is clear that you are currently in a difficult situation and feeling frustrated. First of all, I have to tell you that it is unlikely for a guy to be so busy that he can't reply to your messages for 24 hours. Some of them might just think that they can temporarily set you aside. I'm not saying that he doesn't like you, but sometimes, they may not realize that they have done something to hurt the other person. Some guys are carefree, so he might just want to reply to your message later but accidentally forgets. However, this also indicates that you may not be as important to him as he is to you. He might not realize that it's a message from his girlfriend, so he should reply quickly. If you still want to continue this relationship, it would be beneficial to have a good conversation with him. Share your concerns, understand why he can't reply to your messages promptly, and timely reminders will be more helpful for the relationship. Of course, it is also possible that both of you are currently in a stage where you are a bit tired of each other. At this time, you need to have more surprises and understanding for each other, and take good care of this relationship. Lastly, I want to tell you, don't be miserable for a long time just because he doesn't reply to your messages. The premise for others to love us is that we must love ourselves. Love yourself, become a positive and optimistic person, and naturally, more people will love you.

Hello, friend, sending you a warm hug. Most guys usually have time to reply within 24 hours. If he's feeling burnt out, as you mentioned, he might not have been paying much attention to your messages. You can try talking to him and ask what he's been busy with lately. If he's genuinely busy, give him some space to handle his things. If he feels that your relationship has become a bit dull, you can find ways to liven it up and create a sense of novelty. For example, you can do things together like cooking, watching the sunrise, or going to an amusement park to create shared memories and engage in different activities together. This way, you can also bring some freshness into the relationship. Best wishes to you.

Hello, questioner, is it possible for a guy to be so busy that he doesn't have time to send messages for 24 hours? I can't say for sure. Firstly, you are not asking about an individual, but rather describing a group of people with the term "guy". So there is definitely a possibility of special cases. So, is your "Ta" a special case? The answer is, it's possible. Being busy can also have different situations. You didn't specify whether the person is busy with work, busy playing games, thinking about things, or even daydreaming, which can all be defined as "being busy". In any case, the person's mind is already occupied by something else and they have no time to contact you, perhaps not even enough to take care of themselves. Most of us are not superhuman, so how can we have time to deal with others? Therefore, my advice is, don't worry too much about how often he contacts you. If you haven't argued or had a falling out, you can shift your attention to whether he is attentive when you are together. If you feel that he is attentive and not just going through the motions, then when he doesn't contact you, he is probably thinking about something unrelated to you or more urgent, in other words, he has something on his mind. He just thinks that it's not necessary to let you know temporarily and doesn't know how to explain it. If the situation is like this, then you can observe more and give each other some time to adjust. Of course, you can also choose to have an open and honest conversation with him about your conflicts and see if there is a better way to resolve them. Honestly, men usually have their pride and don't want to bring too much pressure to their partners or share the hardships they are going through. But, the situation of not contacting you cannot exclude some individuals who resort to emotional manipulation, not refusing, not breaking up, not opposing. Therefore, it is still general advice. Observe more and don't act rashly. Take care of yourself first, your own feelings and emotions. That is the most important thing you need to solve right now, maybe you have already forgotten about this matter. Take care of yourself first, no matter what the situation is in the end, slay the demons when they come, fight the monsters when they arrive, and explain everything when the gods appear~ I'm sorry, but I must say that saying these things to someone in love without considering their feelings is actually very inconsiderate. Especially since I have also experienced the pain of love, having one person's attention or lack thereof determining one's daily emotions is very cruel, I know. But sometimes pain is a remedy. I truly hope you can redirect your energy back to yourself. It's harsh but true: love yourself first, then you will know how to love.

question: I really don't want to live anymore.
description: For the last two or three years, since my father got sick, I have been arguing with my husband. I have been feeling suffocated and uncomfortable in my heart. I don't want to live anymore.

answers.answer_text: #A sentence for the disheartened# Have you ever stored a memory in an object? For example, this beautiful memory can be stored on a train ticket. Keep this ticket and whenever you see it, you will recall those days. You can also seal away unpleasant memories in an item, like a small glass bottle. Write down the incident, put it in the bottle, and use a permanent marker to write "Open again on November 25, 2029".

question: I have a case of chickenpox and a fever. Chickenpox is contagious. What should I do if my parents insist that I go to school?
description: When I told my dad I had just caught a cold, he didn't care at all. It took him several days to remember to treat me, by which point it had turned into a fever. He then gave me expired medicine. I had a high fever at night, and my mom suggested that I take a leave of absence from school. However, from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m., he berated my mom and forced me to go to school, saying things like "Don't you care about your grades anymore?" I felt so sick and exhausted during the four classes in the morning. I lost all the will to cry. I wonder, what is more important, my health or studying? Will you only realize how much I can't take it anymore when I actually attempt suicide? After I was diagnosed with chickenpox, I found out that it is over 90% contagious. And yet, they still forced me to go to school. I asked them what we would do if I infected someone else, and they said they would simply deny that it was due to me. They even said that I only brought this up because I didn't want to go to school. Please, wake up and realize, I am sitting in the classroom feeling dizzy and itchy all over my body. Who am I doing this for? How can you be so selfish? My parents have long treated me like a study machine. I spend two-thirds of my time in the classroom thinking about cutting my arteries. It's so painful, so sad. Can you please give me some comfort and encouragement? I beg you.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I can sense from your description that you are feeling very distressed. Many parents use the excuse of being good to their children to make them study like machines, which puts a lot of pressure on the children. Sometimes, children feel that their parents care more about their grades than their own well-being and feelings, which can create emotional distance between them and their parents. In addition, children may feel the need to repay their parents' kindness by performing well academically, but this can actually have a negative impact on their learning. In such cases, children need to adjust their mindset, try their best in their studies, but also let go of the burden. Having chickenpox is really uncomfortable and it can also affect your ability to focus in class. Usually, it takes about a week to ten days for the symptoms to ease. Since you are in the first year of high school, you can definitely discuss with your parents about taking some time off to recover at home before going back to school. However, while at home, you can still engage in self-directed learning and make an effort to catch up on any missed lessons. Otherwise, if you continue to feel conflicted and resentful while also not taking care of your health or catching up on schoolwork, it won't be beneficial for you.

Hug OP. When I was in high school, as we were approaching the college entrance exams, there were several cases of chickenpox in our class, one after another. In the end, around three or four people got it after the exams. At the time, I was quite anxious, not because I was afraid of getting it myself, but because I was worried about not being able to take the exams on time. One of our classmates got chickenpox during the exams, and she went home afterward. Going home would be better. If possible, see if you can persuade your father to change his mind and agree to let you go home to recover before returning. Even though you would be at home recovering, you can still study, as learning knows no boundaries. Besides, it has already affected your regular class attendance, so going home is still better given the current circumstances. Pay attention to personal protection and diet in your daily life. Be in a well-ventilated environment. If you can go home, remember to have your classmates and teachers disinfect your seat. You should also have a light diet, eat more fruits that can cool and detoxify the body, and avoid eating fruits that can generate internal heat. Drinking mung bean soup regularly is also beneficial. Remember not to scratch the chickenpox, as it can leave scars and not look good. Now, take good care of yourself and try your best to go home or visit the homes of relatives and friends where you can stay. Take good care of yourself and stay strong.

OP, hello! It's hard to understand how you're feeling right now. When you were feeling unwell (with a cold) and told your father, he didn't take it seriously, which led to a fever and later chickenpox. Your father's words and actions forced you to go to school despite feeling unwell. In your 11th-grade year, you've been through a lot, and I can understand the desperation and helplessness you mentioned, even the moments when you thought about cutting a major artery. From what you've described, it seems like you're seeking attention from your father. It appears that even your mother can only follow his decisions at home, like when your mother wanted to help you take a leave of absence but your father didn't allow it. Is the communication and interaction between you and your father always like this? Clearly, there is a lack of care. I'm not sure if it's because your father isn't good at expressing himself or if he doesn't consider certain things important, like having a cold. Before getting chickenpox, it's possible to have a fever, so it wasn't necessarily because you didn't take medicine for the cold on time. Would it make you feel a little better if you analyze it this way? Adolescence is a sensitive period where you have sensitive thoughts and think a lot. I hope you can express your specific needs to your parents. For example, when you have a cold and don't feel well, you can say that your body feels uncomfortable and ask if there's any medicine that can provide some relief. You want to alleviate the discomfort caused by the cold by taking medicine early. When I was in middle and high school, my mom would always say, "When I have a cold, I just lie down and won't move. She never knew what it feels like to have a cold." However, I realized that when I have a cold, my symptoms are much worse than others', feeling weak, muscle aches, dizziness, and a throbbing head. Even though we've lived together as a family for over ten years, understanding and accommodation may not always be possible. Effective communication is crucial. I hope this is helpful to you. Take care of your health.

Thank you for your question. If you are a high school freshman, you should be 16 years old, right? That means you are going through puberty. Actually, in terms of legal and practical abilities, you can't fully make decisions for yourself yet. So, when you have a cold and your dad doesn't immediately help you get better, can't you take care of yourself first? It seems like there are some medications at home that are about to expire, so even if you don't have money, you can still find a solution, right? If you are not satisfied with these medications, have you tried asking for new ones? Your dad yelling at your mom from 5am to 7am seems like he sacrificed you to avoid the conflict between him and your mom. The conflict among family members is probably not just because of your illness. Excluding your factors, it seems that they have different perspectives. So, the choices you feel forced to make here have a sense of sacrifice and compromise. But this is not a sacrifice you should actively choose. They should be responsible for their own differences. Sacrificing you doesn't fundamentally solve the issue. So why is it difficult for you to endure their arguments? Do you love your mom? But their issues still need to be resolved by them, not drained out of you. Being selfish, yes, not being selfish is something you need to defend for. It requires some effort. Arterial incision. Are you really not planning to take responsibility for yourself? Dear high school freshman classmate, or is it just to retaliate against your stubborn father and your mother's inability to protect you? You can protect and take care of yourself, which will make your parents feel more at ease and reduce the arguments between them over you. If your father is worried about your academics, can't you alleviate that concern as a freshman? For example, even when you are sick, you can still complete your assignments on time, do some extra exercises, or discuss with your teachers to get some resources to keep up with the class. Are there any methods that allow you to take time off without affecting your studies? It seems like you are hoping for your father's attention. The more you hope for it, the more your father's neglect of you will be magnified. But his wish for your academics to not be delayed is also his way of showing care, albeit with a stubborn attitude. Do you have the courage to communicate your expectations (your father's care) to him? At least before you have the courage to make an arterial incision. As Jane Eyre said, "If a mountain will not come to Muhammad, then Muhammad must go to the mountain." Stubborn people need someone who is not stubborn to set an example for them. I hope this helps you.

Chickenpox is contagious, and if it worsens, it can be life-threatening. My little brother had a viral case of chickenpox before and had to stay in bed for several days, missing school for more than two weeks. For my family, physical health is the most important thing. You should communicate properly with your parents. Maybe your emotions got the better of you, and you were not able to communicate effectively, huh? Be good! It's best to communicate and exchange ideas with your parents!

question: I heard that medication has side effects. How can schizophrenia be cured without medication?
description: I heard that the medication has side effects and can make people foolish. I'm a little afraid to take it now, and online there are people saying that it just makes you numb. Now my mom believes that whenever I cry or get angry, it means I have a illness. I'm feeling really tough.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Schizophrenia involves physiological changes and typically requires medication for effective treatment. Psychiatric medications work by adjusting hormone levels in the body to alleviate symptoms such as delusions and depression, but they may also cause some side effects. These side effects can be more significant during the initial stage of medication, but they usually improve after a certain period. The key is to continue with medication treatment to aid in symptom relief. I understand your pain, but in order to return to your family and society, and lead a normal life and work, it is important to try to overcome it. You can seek help on this platform, explaining that your self-awareness, insight, and ability to test reality are still intact, and your condition is not very severe. Seeking treatment early will help alleviate your suffering sooner. Keep going! We are here with you! Best wishes!

question: Why do I always want to break up when I feel uncomfortable in my heart, and then regret it after the breakup? (Same-sex female)
description: 1: The partner and the ex are good friends because they work and live together under the same roof. Deep down, they always feel that she still loves her ex. 2: The partner rarely shows that they care about me. I always feel like I'm optional and there are no commitments. They don't take initiative in our relationship. 3: We have broken up and gotten back together many, many times, I've lost count. But we are still together, just not as good as before. I am becoming less willing to take the initiative. (Before, it felt like I was the one taking the initiative.) 4: I don't want to break up with her, I just want our relationship to get better. I want my needs to be fulfilled. (We've been together for two years and haven't progressed at all.) 5: If we're going to break up, is there any effective way for me to forget? I'm afraid it will hurt like losing a piece of myself, which is uncomfortable and painful. 6: Does she really love me? When she says she loves me, I can't feel it. When she says she doesn't love me, she still wants to get back together after all the times we've broken up. 7: Lastly, I want to know how I should approach dating and loving someone in the most suitable way. (I no longer understand what love is and how to love.)
keywords: Love, dependence, attachment, sense of security, and love management.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I want to have a simple chat with you about the topic of "love," just for reference. Love refers to the deep level of liking and the emotions that people voluntarily give and devote to. It refers to the satisfaction and happiness that humans actively provide or consciously expect. It refers to the proactive or conscious cherishing, nurturing, or satisfying of certain human needs that others cannot achieve independently, including thoughts, mental experiences, behavioral states, material needs, etc. Love is an emotion that comes from the heart. In a relationship, the more proactive someone is, the more they care and love the other person. People do not willingly devote too much to a stranger because there is not much love between them. Love is different from liking. Liking includes "wanting to possess, wanting to obtain." Liking represents personal feelings. When seeing someone or something they like, they feel happy. When liking reaches a certain intensity, people will devote material, time, emotions, and even give everything they have, and at this point, it becomes love. The feeling of liking may not be long-lasting, just like how today I like/want to eat fried rice with eggs, but I may not feel like eating it tomorrow. If I love to eat fried rice with eggs, I may be willing and even happy to eat it continuously for a week. In the movie "Love is Not Blind," it is said, "Liking is indulgent, but love is restrained." This is also a unique distinction. Many times, your feelings are only your feelings and not necessarily the truth. You feel that she still loves her, but it doesn't mean that she really loves her in reality. There is no special method to forget about someone after a breakup, especially when you deliberately try to forget. Forgetting always takes time, which also proves from a certain perspective the little bits and pieces you once put into the relationship. So, some people say that perhaps the cure is only time and a new love. As for the most suitable way for oneself, it needs to be explored together by the two people. In addition to emotional satisfaction, dating often has practical constraints, such as having less time to meet if both are working. However, fortunately, love is never measured by how long you can stay together. If you're happy, be together; if you're unhappy, separate. It's better to be carefree, but more importantly, seek a stable relationship pattern, which requires introspection. Best wishes~.

Title owner, hello. Seeing words is like seeing faces, so let me give you a warm hug first. I hope my answer will be helpful to you. Your partner and their ex are good friends and even live together. As a girl, I feel a little sense of crisis. Do you know the reason why your partner and their ex broke up? Do you think there is a possibility that they will get back together? If your partner has deeper feelings for their ex than for you, my dear, I suggest you cut your losses and end it in a timely manner. It's better to have a short pain than a long one. Your partner seems to care very little about you and hardly takes any initiative. From your description, it seems that your partner doesn't love you very much. There are many reasons why she might be willing to get back together with you. For example, she might not really care, it doesn't matter to her whether she breaks up or gets back together with you. She can go with whatever you say. Maybe you're the one who likes her, and if she gets back together with you, she can satisfy her need to be loved and get something from you. If getting back together has benefits, she will do it. You don't want to break up with her, you just want your relationship to get better and better. My dear, when it comes to relationships, it's not something you can achieve just by wanting to, and it's not something you can achieve through your efforts alone. You have to understand that "it takes two to tango". So you have to admit that your relationship has problems, and she may not love you that much. Being together will not benefit you, it will only torture you and make you unhappy, to the point where you have to come to the internet for help. I really feel sorry for you, and I hug you tightly. My dear, you like her, so breaking up with her is definitely going to hurt. But it's better to have a short pain than a long one. Continuing to hang on with her will only cause greater harm to yourself. There's a term called "sunk cost", which means that the more people invest in something, it doesn't necessarily mean that the likelihood of achieving the desired result is greater, but it makes people less willing to give up because they feel that they have put so much effort into it and it's hard to let it go. But continuing to hang on will waste your emotions and delay your youth, which is a greater cost and not worth it. How to love someone? In fact, I think it's best to be with someone you enjoy and feel comfortable with in a relationship. Being in a relationship is about two people, and there's nothing wrong with loving someone and treating them well, but the other person should respond to you and accept your intimacy, and also treat you well. My dear, just wait a little longer, you will meet the right person for you. Good luck.

In the process of being together, couples often have this feeling: are we really not compatible with each other? Would it be better to break up? Everyone handles their emotions differently, just like the main topic mentioned, you care about certain details, and your partner is 8 years older than you, so your partner may be more rational in dealing with many things. We also love each other in our own way, but the other person does not return it in the same way. Actually, most of the time, what we want is not much, just hoping that the other person can give us a little more greetings and care. But every time we communicate, the other person will say that's just their personality and they can't change. So we start to doubt this relationship. Therefore, we can ask ourselves, if the other person is unwilling to change, should we continue? In order to be with her, you must have made a lot of changes. From the beginning to now, does the other person often make some changes for us? If the other person has never changed, and most of the time it is just us adapting to the other person, then we really need to seriously consider it, after all, love is not something that can be done by one person alone. If she has indeed made some concessions, and has gradually become more tolerant towards us in terms of personality, then we can have regular heart-to-heart conversations with each other and plan our future lives, adjusting our direction in a timely manner. As for how to love someone, I think it means including the other person in our future plans, being able to recognize their strengths and accept their weaknesses, gradually changing ourselves in regards to things that the other person cares about, and giving the other person some little warmth because we care about them. Sometimes we need to learn to love ourselves, if the other person does not take our feelings into account in many things, then we need to learn to protect ourselves, after all, being proactive alone can be tiring. The world and I love you.

Hello. Same-sex love is also love, although it encounters different problems compared to opposite-sex relationships, but the feeling of love in the heart is the same. I have found that you are a very organized person, so let's go through it step by step according to your description. 1: Your partner and their ex are good friends because they live under the same roof due to work. You always feel that she still loves her ex. If you do not have concrete evidence that they still keep in touch and have an ambiguous relationship, then this problem may stem from your own insecurity and lack of self-confidence. Therefore, what needs adjustment is not the behavior of your partner, but your psychological state and the way you perceive her. Reflect on the idiom "suspecting others of one's own inadequacy". 2: Your partner rarely shows that she cares about you, and you always feel that you are disposable and she does not commit to you. She does not take the initiative to show affection. First of all, you need to clarify for yourself what it means for your partner to care about you. Quantify the degree of care, such as how many times she takes the initiative to contact you in a week for you to feel satisfied with the relationship. Do not rely on "feelings" alone - people tend to only care about their own efforts and usually think that they have given more while the other person has given less. The words "disposable, no commitment, and lack of initiative" indicate that you are dissatisfied with the relationship. However, you haven't mentioned any specific instances, and you are still speaking from your "feelings". Consider whether your personal understanding and interpretation of the relationship are objective enough. Children who were often ignored, unrecognized, and unappreciated when they were young often have similar feelings. Similarly, because there are no specific instances, it is also possible that your partner is simply someone who is not very emotionally expressive. 3: We have broken up and gotten back together many, many times, and I have lost count. But we are still together, just not as good as before, and I am becoming less and less willing to take the initiative. (Before, it always felt like I was the one taking the initiative) Regardless of whether it is out of anger or hoping to use the breakup as leverage to make the other person love you more, the act of breaking up itself only indicates that you lack confidence and interest in the other person and the relationship, and you want to continue moving forward together. Therefore, whether you take the initiative to break up or get broken up with, it is a blow to love. Your on-and-off relationship, hearts are not like felt wool, being poked and prodded, the two hearts are full of wounds, how can they be as good as before? It is normal for you to feel tired and unwilling to take the initiative. But the problem is not who takes the initiative, but why do you often break up? And why do you get back together? I suggest you make a list of these specific reasons for the back-and-forth, so that we can analyze them more rationally, isn't it? 4: I don't want to break up with her, I just want our relationship to get better and my needs to be satisfied (we have been together for two years and it doesn't feel like there has been any improvement). The same problem arises again, what are your needs and what specific aspects of the relationship do you hope to see improvement in? Can you write them down like filling in blanks? You can't expect the other person to meet a need that you yourself are not clear about, right? 5: If I want to break up, are there any special methods to help me forget? I am afraid of losing a piece of myself, it feels uncomfortable and painful. Breaking up, unless there is no love left at all, otherwise it will always feel uncomfortable.... Since you cherish this relationship so much, like being afraid of losing a piece of yourself, why not try to find the problems within the relationship and find ways to address them? 6: Does she really love me? She says she does, but I can't feel it. She says she doesn't love me, but she is willing to get back together even after so many breakups. 7: Finally, I want to know how I should be in a relationship and how to love someone in the most appropriate way (I don't understand what love is anymore, how to love). Analytically, it may be true that she says she loves you but you can't feel it. (Because if she doesn't love you, she could refuse to get back together. There is no need to waste each other's time with pulling and tugging.) And it seems that you have initiated breakups more times? Maybe you have always been the one to say breakup whenever you are unhappy? It's a bit cute, like playing house as a child. Love has countless forms, but I can only speak about the way I like: to love someone is to learn to accept them, appreciate them, and allow them to be their true selves when they are with me. Find a way to interact with each other that makes both of us feel free and comfortable, to accompany each other through the ups and downs of life. I'll end with a quote I found online: love is cuddling up in the arms of your beloved while feeling lonely

Hello. In an intimate relationship, not being able to love and be loved well is a highly tormenting experience. The constant fear of losing and feelings of insecurity are truly painful, as if there is no sense of safety at all. I can see the torment in your heart and the helplessness of not being able to control yourself and your emotions. But don't worry, let's analyze it together and take it slowly, okay?

Analyzing the problem:
1. Your partner and their ex are good friends because they work and live together. Deep down, you always feel that she still loves her ex. (In situations where exes can still be friends, it could mean that they are truly unable to be together or that there are still lingering feelings. Your concerns are not unfounded, but a judgment should be based on the specific circumstances. Guessing alone is not accurate enough.)

2. Your partner rarely shows that she cares about you, and you always feel like you are either important or insignificant, with no commitment. She is not affectionate. (It could also be because of her personality, that she is a bit indifferent. But that doesn't mean she doesn't love you. This also requires observation and judgment in daily life, right? Don't scare yourself without reason.)

3. You and your partner have broken up and gotten back together many, many times, to the point where you can't even count anymore, but you are still together, just not as good as before, and you are becoming less and less willing to take the initiative. (Before, it seemed like you were the one taking the initiative) (Yes, doesn't a person's willingness to be with someone else at least indicate that you are their top choice? Any kind of relationship that experiences breaking up and getting back together multiple times will hurt each other's feelings. It doesn't necessarily have to do with other things, right? You still need to make judgments.)

4. You don't want to break up with her, you just want your relationship to get better and your needs to be satisfied (You've been together for two years and it feels like there hasn't been any progress) (It seems like you really care about her and don't want to leave her. The lack of progress in the relationship has many reasons, such as not yet understanding what "love" is, not being able to love each other or yourself properly. When the perspective is too limited, there won't be enough tenderness. Over time, expectations for each other increase and there is less personal growth, which will affect the relationship.)

5. If you want to break up, is there any effective way to forget her? I'm afraid of losing a part of myself, which is uncomfortable and painful. (Habit is a terrible thing, it makes it very difficult to change. You two are like a part of each other's lives, just like you said, "a part of yourself." Therefore, breaking up means losing a part of yourself. I want to tell you, if you can't change the other person, isn't it better to change yourself?)

6. Does she really love me? She says she loves me, but I don't feel it. She says she doesn't love me, but she still wants to get back together after so many breakups. (To be honest, someone who constantly demands to break up in a relationship is being "dramatic." And the fact that the other person still wants to reconcile shows great tolerance. Perhaps you need to understand yourself more or maybe you already know something, but try looking at yourself from your partner's perspective, and you will realize that what you thought was love was just constantly "tormenting yourself and the relationship.")

7. Lastly, you want to know how you should date and love someone in the most suitable way (You no longer understand what love is and how to love) (Yes, this is a good question: love does not involve force, including towards yourself or your partner. Love should bring joy and comfort to both parties, it should be based on respect, and there should be a "comfortable boundary." Small dramas bring joy, but excessive drama only causes hurt. When love is constantly tormented and lost, staying together is not because of love, but a "painful connection.") If you cannot feel the presence of love as described above, perhaps you need psychological guidance. Perhaps the intimate relationship needs to be clarified.

In conclusion, I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you can love and be loved well! If you have specific concerns, you can private message me!

I'll answer the sixth question! Does she really love me? Saying she loves me but not feeling it, saying she doesn't love me and I've broken up with her so many times but she still wants to get back together. The OP says that they will only love her if she loves you back. Or maybe you love her and also expect her to love you, but you're not sure if she does, so you want to clarify this, right? To figure this out, you might have to ask yourself or let her ask herself, when you're together, not only are you happy but she also feels pain when she's away from you? If only the first one is true, you probably just like her. If both are true, you probably have fallen in love with her; or, being together with her is simply about supporting her, or if you will actively and unconditionally take care of and help her even if it causes you losses when she encounters difficulties? If you only want to support her, but this support doesn't cause any losses to you, then you probably just like her. If you are willing to devote yourself to her unconditionally, then you probably have fallen in love with her. We all hope to have a fulfilling love relationship, just like the princess marrying the prince and living happily ever after. We all try to live in an ideal fairy tale-like state, but the fact is, chaos is the true portrayal of real life. In love, there are romance and troubles, sweet words and arguments. There is mutual support and betrayal. In your relationship experience, when two people with different backgrounds come together in an intimate relationship, conflicts and adjustments are natural occurrences, and breaking up and getting back together is not unusual. The key is for you to understand how to communicate, to express your needs and feelings honestly to each other, and of course, you also need to learn and grow, to focus most of your energy on yourself, to develop your strengths and show your value. This way, you can not only grow independently but also rely on each other, isn't this what you have always wanted?

Hug the host, feel conflicted and confused in love. Love itself is a difficult thing, our usual understanding of love is not just sweet. It is also mixed with suspicion, pain, jealousy, grievances, and love does not only have a bright side. I think you may have experienced these feelings in love, so how can you say that you don't understand love? Hug you, let's not be in a hurry, let's take our time to sort things out. 1. This time, I want to set aside the analytical part and come up with a possible suggestion for point 5. Maybe you can set a "breakup countdown" agreement, such as another 30 days together, or three months. When the time is up, we break up. And during this designated time, you can treat it as a proper farewell, even if you get angry or suffer during the process, don't mention breaking up (that's the only taboo). How to maintain the relationship without breaking up within the designated time, let time decide. 2. Let's first look at how you perceive your partner. My partner rarely shows that she cares about me, always feeling like I am replaceable, not committed. Not taking the initiative to show affection. Saying that she doesn't love me, after breaking up so many times, she still wants to get back together. First of all, if you have brought up breaking up so many times and she still wants to reconcile, I believe she at least has some feelings for you, accommodating your impulsive decisions, time after time. And she rarely shows that she cares about you, I would lean towards the possibility that she doesn't know how to respond to you, and is temporarily at a loss when it comes to unresolved issues (such as commitment), she also feels the conflict. 3. Not committed. My needs cannot be satisfied (we've been together for two years and I feel like there hasn't been any progress). In your description, you mentioned the importance of commitment and emotional development. It is clear that you care about whether there is a future for the two of you. Can you please tell me if the disagreements over "commitment" have caused the occasional breakup and reconciliation between you? As far as I know, same-sex relationships currently lack legal protection. This may be a significant obstacle to the progress of your relationship. Have you thought about how to resolve these issues? (For example, registering in another country?) This not only requires your partner's response but also your own reflection. 4. I believe everyone has a different understanding of love. In addition to Sternberg's triangular theory of love, I believe that a good love is when both parties sincerely listen to their inner voice in this relationship, embrace each other's differences and grow together. It is a mutual healing of two constantly changing and growing souls. Deep down, you always feel that she still loves her ex. You may think that she still loves her ex, but at the same time, you need to ask yourself, "Do I feel like I am a unique individual? Do I feel important?" If you are uncertain or deny this answer, then no matter how your partner responds, you may not be able to convince yourself. The potential psychological implications of this possible evaluation may damage your self-confidence, and in a relationship, we need to have confidence in ourselves. I believe you can do it. 5. Let me tell you about a same-sex couple I know. They were my high school classmates, from a spicy southwestern provincial capital city. Their relationship has lasted for 7 years. They often show affection for each other on social media. Both of them are now teachers, one teaches English and the other teaches physical education. They are financially independent. From what I know, their parents and families have met each other and are aware of their situation. Perhaps an open family environment has provided great support for their relationship. Moreover, the city we live in is nationally known for its tolerance and openness, and friends and neighbors have a non-judgmental and accepting attitude towards this. So I think being in an environment where people respect each other might be advantageous for the development of your relationship. I wish you all the best.

Hello, OP: Feeling confronted with this emotion, it makes you struggle and feel conflicted. You don't know how to choose, and you don't know where your love is heading. You want to break up, but you can't gather the courage. I don't know how you fell in love with each other and got together in the first place. I also don't know your personality traits and communication patterns, so it's difficult to give you an objective and accurate answer. I can only try to help you sort things out based on the information presented. First, the internal conflict you are currently experiencing, what part of it is caused by her? What part is inherent to yourself? For example, your excessive sensitivity and suspicion, the lack of sufficient inner security, whenever she ignores or acts cold towards you, it triggers your defense mechanisms, and you choose to leave in advance for fear of being abandoned by her. For example, you are always worried that she still cares about her ex. When you maintain this kind of suspicion, how can you enter her inner world with defense and caution? Next, let's talk about what she brings to you. For example, her love for you is indecisive and ambiguous. You cannot see her whole-hearted care for you, and no matter how much effort you put in, you find that you can't enter her inner world. Maybe these are the fortresses of her defense? How to break through the impasse? Love itself is an ability. When we love someone, is it based on our own needs or the other person's needs? If your love carries too many expectations and utilitarianism, only satisfying your own desire to be taken care of while neglecting the other person's feelings, then the power emanating from this kind of love may be a form of control, achieving your own needs through controlling others. If your love is based on giving to the other person and letting them feel the warmth, acceptance, and trust behind your love, then believe that the other person will also invest their love into your inner world. Additionally, if you want to better maintain this romantic relationship, you need to consider what love connection points exist between you. What interests and hobbies do you share? What commonality is there in your personalities? How can you share and enjoy together? Where do your values align? How can you share and enjoy together? As for feeling like wanting to break up but not being able to, it may be related to the trauma you experienced in your early attachment relationships. In your early attachment relationships, there were traumatic experiences of separation, and now, breaking up only triggers your early experiences of separation anxiety. Of course, the above analysis is only for reference. Keep going, and know that I will always love you!

Before I help you, I have a question to ask: You mentioned that your partner and their ex are very good friends because they work and live together. But deep down, you always feel like she still loves her ex. When you say "ex," are you referring to her ex-girlfriend? Your question is: Does she really love me? To love someone, there are generally three criteria: rational love (height, financial conditions, etc.), emotional love (comfort when being together), and physical love (sexual intimacy). If you meet two or more of these criteria, it indicates a strong love for someone. 2. There is no specific step-by-step guide on how to be in a relationship. question: My long-distance girlfriend has mild depression, and I feel like it's affecting me too. What should I do?
description: I am a very cheerful guy, and I'm generally happy almost every day. My girlfriend is a college classmate, and we have been in a long-distance relationship for a long time due to the pandemic. She has mild depression, so she often has bad moods from time to time. When she's in a bad mood, she ignores me and doesn't respond no matter what I say. At first, I thought I could slowly influence her with my happiness, but now I realize that my own emotions have also been affected. I feel powerless and don't know how to interact with her anymore; I'm also confused about what I should do...

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, thank you for inviting me. Actually, your post mentioned two points: long-distance relationship and girlfriend's depression. You love her very much and want to help her through this difficult time. People with depression often experience low mood and can have a negative impact on those around them during episodes. I understand your feelings, but don't worry, let's look at the issues you mentioned together. 1. Low mood is a main characteristic of depression. You mentioned that when your girlfriend is in a bad mood, she won't respond to you no matter what you say. In fact, people with depression tend to have reduced energy during low moods and are not willing to communicate with anyone. Your girlfriend's behavior is not because she doesn't want to respond to you, but rather a manifestation of her illness. Understanding this is an important step. 2. Depression requires communication and companionship. You mentioned that due to the pandemic, you are in a long-distance relationship. Long-distance relationships themselves can bring a lot of insecurity to couples, which is why many people breakup due to distance. In your girlfriend's case, she has mild depression, which means her feelings of insecurity and loneliness will be heightened. You are an optimistic person and want to influence her with your positivity, which shows how much you love her. However, what brings joy to ordinary people may not necessarily bring joy to someone with depression. (For example, we may feel happy because we had a delicious meal, but someone with depression, due to reduced energy, may not see it as something worth being happy about. Even in the eyes of someone with severe depression, there may be nothing worth feeling happy about). What people with depression need the most is companionship and understanding. When your girlfriend's mood is not too bad, you can communicate with her more often (such as phone calls or video chats) and ask about her feelings or what she has been doing. You can also surprise her in daily interactions. When she confides in you about her low mood, first, show understanding (what may seem normal to us ordinary people can have a big impact on someone with depression). Secondly, gently guide and inspire her to think about things from different perspectives, and encourage her to do other activities to shift her attention (like listening to music or writing in a journal to express negative emotions). At the same time, during your conversations, be careful not to be influenced by negative emotions (if you are affected, you can distract yourself with things you enjoy, like listening to music or engaging in physical activity). Finally, due to the limitations of distance, you can also rely on the support of her parents or friends to accompany her and listen to her negative emotions, helping her through this difficult time. I hope the above answer can be helpful to you. Take care.

Hello, because of the epidemic, many people at home will have emotional problems. If your girlfriend's emotions are only more obvious during this period, this is an influence under the big environment, so you don't have to worry too much. You mentioned that you are college classmates and you have been together basically all the time except during winter and summer vacations. Facing such changes, it is a test for both of you and requires you to face it together. It is clear that you care about your girlfriend and want to make her happy. You want your happiness to infect her, but your strength is not enough, and you are instead affected by her. At this time, if you feel particularly powerless, what you need to do is to give yourself some space to replenish your own energy, and then let your girlfriend feel that you are with her and give her strength. You may be too eager to make your girlfriend happy quickly, and you have too high expectations for the impact of your emotions, which leads to feelings of frustration. It might be helpful to lower your goals a bit. If you just accompany her, this in itself is a transmission of strength, which may be better. I am giving some suggestions boldly, and you know the specific situation best, so you need to evaluate it yourself.

question: If the grades are not good, it can lead to special depression. How should I prepare for the college entrance examination?
description: Unable to sleep well, unable to eat well, not feeling energized. Don't know how to continue studying.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text:
Hello! Based on your description, I think you are experiencing pre-exam anxiety, and I have a few suggestions for you:
- Motivate yourself with ambitious goals. As the saying goes, "Without far-sightedness, one is bound to be troubled in the near future." In other words, if we only focus on immediate concerns and don't have long-term goals, we will constantly be plagued by worries. By setting lofty ideals and continuously motivating and inspiring ourselves with distant goals, we can forget about current troubles, disregard temporary difficulties, and reduce the tension and anxiety in our minds.
- Encourage yourself with small successes. If a person idles away without doing anything and has no purpose in life, they naturally will have many idle worries, concerns, and anxieties. By continually giving ourselves realistic tasks, setting achievable short-term goals, and using moderately challenging and not overly burdensome tasks to push ourselves, we can find practical successes that may not be magnificent but are real, which can encourage us to forget about tension and anxiety amidst the "busy" activities.
- Learn to release your emotions. We must recognize that a certain level of tension and anxiety is not harmful but beneficial for our learning. The problem is that we must keep this mental adjustment of stress within a controllable range. This stress must be transformed into motivation in order to facilitate our learning. When the pressure becomes too great, we can relieve and alleviate it appropriately by shifting our focus or engaging in intense physical exercise. This can help us adjust tension and anxiety to a reasonable level. 
- Make a feasible revision plan. 
- Learn self-relaxation techniques to optimize emotions. When the stress becomes too high and affects our study efficiency, we need to learn self-relaxation techniques. Self-expression: candidates can confide their frustrations and nervous emotions to family members, friends, or teachers, or they can vent their emotions through activities such as running or crying. Learn deep breathing: candidates can sit or lie down, take slow breaths, hold for a few seconds, and then exhale, repeating this process several times. Positive visualization: candidates can recall their past successes as much as possible and visualize themselves in a bright and comfortable environment accompanied by soothing music. Learn positive self-affirmation: candidates should learn to positively affirm themselves, saying things like "I can do it! There's nothing special about it, it's just a test!" "I believe in myself! I've reviewed these questions many times, no matter how difficult they are, I won't give up, I can get through it!" "No matter how I perform in the exam, I have no regrets as long as I've tried my best!" For candidates who are seriously affected by anxiety and it impacts their daily life and studies, seeking help from family members, teachers, or counseling professionals is important. If necessary, seeking assistance from professional psychologists for effective psychological adjustment is recommended. And of course, I think it is important for you to communicate with your parents. Take some time to talk to them, express your true thoughts and feelings. Good luck!

From the brief description provided by the questioner, it appears that they are experiencing anxiety due to the upcoming college entrance exam, which is impacting their daily life and causing a loss of appetite and sleep disturbances. This, in turn, affects their performance in the exam, creating a vicious cycle. Firstly, I suggest that the questioner gains a clear understanding of their own abilities and then develop a practical and feasible plan. Since the college entrance exam is approaching, their current studying should aim to maintain a learning state and prevent slacking off. However, the questioner's current situation is precisely what teachers are most concerned about, as it affects their daily life and places excessive mental pressure due to the impending college entrance exam. It is important to appropriately relax their mindset, maintaining a mental state that is moderately tense - not too tight to break, but not too loose that they become slack. Only with correct understanding can one make the right judgments. Secondly, the questioner should adjust their daily routine, ensuring sufficient sleep, maintaining a healthy and light diet, and engaging in appropriate physical exercise to prepare their body for the exam. Additionally, the home environment is also crucial. I recommend communicating with parents, mutually influencing each other, and creating a healthy atmosphere for exam preparation. Lastly, as mentioned earlier, the current grades have already reached a relatively stable level. I am unsure if the questioner is studying at home or at school, but it is important to maintain a consistent study routine. For example, when I was preparing for the college entrance exam, our teachers required us to study and practice questions in sync with the exam schedule. Wishing the questioner success in their exam!

question: Recently, staying up late has become more and more severe, and I feel very anxious, unable to control myself.
description: Everything makes people anxious. Lately, staying up late has become more and more severe. I set multiple alarms to remind myself to sleep, but it doesn't work. I can't control myself.

answers.answer_text: Hello! In fact, staying up late is more like a kind of healing for young people. After experiencing exhaustion and anxiety during the day, lying in bed at home is the most relaxing time of the day. Whether it's browsing Weibo, watching dramas, or playing games, the feeling of being in control of your own time always keeps people addicted. Every person who stays up late actually has anxiety about tomorrow and fear of the future. In today's fast-paced life, most of our time is occupied by work, and we have very little time for ourselves. For us, nothing is more healing than quietly staying still and having a space for solitude. We all understand that staying up late is bad for our health, makes us look ugly, and affects our work the next day. But the pleasure that staying up late brings makes these things seem insignificant. Staying up late has become a normal thing for people nowadays. Before we know it, it's already eleven or twelve o'clock at night, and we only realize we should go to sleep, but we keep thinking of playing a little longer. The reasons for staying up late may be playing with our phones, using computers, reading books, or working overtime, etc. We just can't fall asleep, even if we want to. If possible, avoid using your phone before going to bed. In the half hour before you plan to sleep, stop playing with your phone, put it away from yourself, and take care of everything related to sleep, such as adjusting the air conditioning temperature, going to the bathroom, and washing up. Once you've taken care of everything, lie down on the bed, and try not to think about anything that happened during the day. Because this will make it even harder for you to fall asleep. Reading books at night is a good idea. Read a dozen pages or so and gain some knowledge. Gorky once said, "Books are the ladder of human progress." So, if you have time, try to read more books. Don't read novels because they will make you more engrossed. Read some classics, sometimes it will make you sleepy, and then you can go to bed. This way, you not only gain knowledge but also successfully bring the desire to sleep. Many people may have the habit of taking a nap, and then they find it difficult to fall asleep at night. So, it is best not to have the habit of taking a nap. No matter what you do psychologically, if you can't overcome it, then it's useless. So we should try our best to overcome our own psychology. Whatever we say, we should stick to it and not let the various psychological problems disturb our sleep. Finally, I hope you have no fear, no panic, and in every corner of the big city, in every quiet late night, you can still see hope and live a fulfilling life.

question: 18-year-old male, always dislikes his own gender, would be happy if someone said he looks like a girl?
description: Always disgusted with one's gender, including one's own body. Will be very happy when someone says they look like a girl.

answers.answer_text: Dear friend, hello! Thank you for your trust, allowing me to see your inner confusion on this platform. I also value the opportunity to communicate with you and hope to be of help to you. [1. Why seek help?] You mentioned that you dislike your gender and wish to be perceived as a girl by others. It is everyone's right to dislike or like something. At first glance, it may seem simple to dislike something, and there doesn't appear to be any internal conflict that would cause you distress. Upon further reflection, there seems to be an internal conflict of wanting to be a girl, but in reality, you are physiologically male. This almost unchangeable physical structure has created obstacles for you to fulfill the "female" role, and perhaps your inner turmoil is caused by this, leading to feelings of hatred towards your own sexual organs. So, I would like to know what answers you expect to get through this inquiry? Why do you detest your male identity? Or, how can you adjust the feelings of hatred towards yourself? [2. Why detest your male identity?] Dear, do you know? There are many reasons for your confusion about your gender role. So, what are the reasons that make you more inclined to be a woman? I would like to attempt to explore this dilemma with you from the perspective of family relationships. Do your father's contributions to the family stand out? If your father is lazy, it may lead to a deep-rooted resentment towards males from within you. In this case, if your mother happens to exhibit many qualities that appeal to you, it is also understandable that you would prefer the female role. If your father is hardworking and works very diligently, and if your mother is a more dependent woman, it may lead to a sense of compassion towards males from within you, feeling that the pressure of being a male is too great, and it is easier to fulfill the responsibilities of being a female. Remember to make a comprehensive assessment, as both genders have their advantages and disadvantages. [3. How to adjust feelings of self-hatred] According to psychological research, children form their gender roles in two steps: the first step is distinguishing between males and females, and the second step is categorizing themselves into one of these groups. You are clear about the first step, but now you are having confusion in the second step. It seems that you are unsure which category to belong to. In response to this situation, you can approach it with a more relaxed mindset. You are currently at a critical period of forming gender identity, and many adolescents have similar concerns. It's not shameful to want to be a girl; it is your true feeling. The fact that you are aware of this confusion is already valuable. In regard to your aspiration for the female role, you can gain some insights from the second point, the causes, and examine the motivations behind your desire for the female role. Finding adjustment strategies based on the causes will be more effective. Understanding the causes can also lead you to further and more comprehensive exploration of the responsibilities and benefits associated with being male or female in society, allowing you to make your own choices. In the past, psychologists have assumed that masculinity and femininity exist on opposite ends of a single dimension. These rigid definitions of gender roles have limitations because they restrict male and female behavior. In modern theories, masculinity and femininity are considered independent dimensions of personality. Each of us has a gender identity. When an individual scores high in both masculine and feminine traits, this gender identity is referred to as androgynous. Under current pressures, androgynous individuals are actually more common, and compared to individuals who conform to traditional gender roles, they exhibit more flexibility and adaptability in their behavior. For example, androgynous males may display "masculine" characteristics such as resistance to pressure and having unique perspectives, as well as "feminine" traits such as actively engaging with a baby. This has led to the emergence of a range of gender roles such as "tomboys" and "nice guys" in different individuals. The above is my thinking on your concerns. I hope it can be helpful to you. If you have any further confusion, feel free to ask. Best wishes!

Hello, I'm not sure what you ultimately want to express with this question. Do you want to "correct" this aversion towards your own gender and return to liking your male gender and body? Or do you feel conflicted because you were born male but feel like you might be a "girl," causing you to be afraid of being perceived as "abnormal" by others or even yourself, without knowing which direction to turn for a solution? You're only 18 years old now, and gender shouldn't be such a confusing concept for you anymore. Based on your statement that you "always" feel aversion towards your gender and body but feel happy when others say you resemble a girl, I conjecture that you identify more with femininity in terms of gender identity. In the book "Psychology and Life," it is mentioned that gender refers to learned psychological phenomena related to gendered behaviors and attitudes. Gender identity refers to an individual's degree of recognition and acceptance of masculinity and femininity, including awareness and acceptance of their own gender. Gender roles refer to the behavior patterns considered appropriate for males and females in a specific society. Without knowing your experiences and why you feel aversion towards your body, and also not knowing the demographics of the people you interact with on a daily basis, I cannot tell you which gender direction you should pursue. However, personally, I believe that there are no absolutes in life, and there are two terms: "androgyny" and "hermaphrodite." Everyone's external expressions (speech, clothing, appearance, etc.) are just a gender, and internal acceptance and recognition are your true gender identity. Not everyone will follow societal norms steadfastly. You may have heard of a tattooed muscular man who likes Barbie dolls, or seen someone with a loli face but a muscular body. Of course, these are just two extreme examples of gender presentation. As long as it doesn't harm society or yourself, do what you love. Don't bother or struggle; your body and mind are yours, and they can coexist harmoniously. PS: I hope this can help you (although I'm not sure if I hit the mark (*^▽^*)ヾ(◍°∇°◍)ﾉﾞ). Everything will be fine.

"Hello, dear 'girl in psychological distress,' I am very honored to have crossed paths with you on this platform. I hope my words can bring you sunshine and warm your heart. Your message is very short, but there is a saying, 'The fewer the words, the greater the importance.' I believe that behind these brief words, there must be rich stories and experiences of growth. Because I don't know the cause and effect of your 'disgust towards your own gender,' I can only speak a few words to the 'heavens' based on my personal experience and see if it can be helpful to you. I have encountered many boys on this platform who do not identify with their gender as 'males.' Their problems often stem from their families of origin. In their own families, there may be a situation of 'strong mother, weak father' or an overbearing mother and a passive father, where female energy completely overwhelms male energy, causing them to lack a sense of security as a male within their family. In such cases, they often arrive at this 'irrational' cognition: 'Male' = 'insecurity'! Recall that Kierkegaard, the founder of existential psychology, once said, 'Regardless, what is believed in the heart is the most important.' What a person perceives as 'true' in their heart often has a greater impact on their emotions and behaviors than objective reality, and these emotions and behaviors often further reinforce their inherent cognition. Over time, their behaviors, emotions, and other aspects tend to become 'feminized.' It can be said that this is a negative 'defense mechanism,' a way to protect themselves from harm. During their upbringing, they may have experienced violence from fathers or certain males. Because, at first glance, the occurrence of violence often appears related to the gender characteristic of 'male.' Consequently, from the perspective of behavioral psychology, a 'stimulus substitution' is created, associating the male gender characteristic with violence, terror, and other negative emotions. They themselves are also male and fear becoming violent and terrifying, thus leading to self-denial of their own gender. In summary, all these are 'irrational' behaviors born out of a sense of 'insecurity,' and they can be understood! However, these approaches cannot fundamentally solve the problem. Because if you cannot find 'peace of mind,' even if you really become a 'female,' you will still experience various 'resentments, annoyances, and anger'! Of course, I am just speaking to the heavens! I don't know if you belong to these cases. Can you share with me a bit more about your experiences of growth? Of course, if it involves your personal privacy, I will respect your wishes!"

Hello OP! Hugs to you. Physically, you are a boy, but deep down, you want to be referred to as a girl. What is the reason behind this? Based on your description, you seem to be transgender! Unlike the LGBT community, you were born wanting to be a girl, but unfortunately, you were born as a boy. It's truly a natural pity, as if there was a misplaced component when you were created, causing some changes in your original self and now you're seeking to find that true self again. However, in reality, you are still a boy, so you may feel conflicted at the moment. At the age of 18, I wonder if you have the financial means to undergo gender reassignment or if you can start by changing your appearance through clothing. You should also be aware that regardless of which method you choose to become your true self, it will require a great deal of courage. Family, friends, and society may have different perspectives, but the world is becoming more accepting. The key is whether you have the courage yourself. To you, a girl at heart.

question: 32-year-old single woman, facing the failure of her business venture and burdened with a huge debt, feeling anxious and terrified, thinking that life is not worth living?
description: I am 32 years old, single, and my parents are farmers. I am living alone and struggling in a nearby city. Two years ago, I started a business. Since my family had some issues, I borrowed my first online loan to help them. However, my business did not go smoothly. To repay the loan and cover the business expenses, I started borrowing more money. By the end of last year, my business completely failed, I closed my shop, lost my source of income, and now I have a high debt of 300,000 yuan from online loans. I managed to recover 50,000 yuan from selling my shop, a friend lent me 50,000 yuan, but my parents cannot help me. I found a job with a low salary, but it can barely sustain my life. I barely made it until the beginning of this year, but then the pandemic hit, the company closed down, and I lost my job, my only source of income. The online loan is now three months overdue, and I receive daily phone calls and text messages threatening and harassing me. If it weren't for the money I owe to my friend and the fear of debt collectors bothering my parents, I might have died a long time ago. Nowadays, every day is spent in anxiety and panic. I feel that life is not worth living, but I can't afford to die either. I feel like a walking dead, working overtime until late at night for a meager salary that is not enough to pay off my debts. It's too painful. When I walk on the road, I have the impulse to run into the middle of the street, and when I stand on a pedestrian overpass, I have the impulse to jump off. I feel like I can't hold on any longer.
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I feel sorry for what you're going through. You are working hard and have a lot of courage, it's just that luck hasn't been on your side. I understand how stressed you must be, but you need to know that no matter how much debt you have, it doesn't compare to the value of your life. Your life is priceless. This difficulty you're facing is only temporary, as long as you keep going and keep repaying your loans, your days will definitely get better. I recommend you watch a movie that I believe will give you courage and strength to keep going. It's a classic movie based on a true story called "The Pursuit of Happyness". The protagonist also faced difficulties similar to yours. He used to sell medical equipment and invested all his savings in buying a lot of instruments. However, these instruments turned out to be difficult to sell, and his life fell into hardship. He struggled to pay rent and his wife couldn't bear the difficulties, so she left him. One day, he passed by a stock brokerage firm and saw people there seemingly successful and living the life he desired. Through his efforts, he got an internship opportunity, but it didn't pay a salary for six months, and after that, only one person would be kept on. He persisted and during this time he even slept with his son in a subway station restroom and sought help from a shelter. He went through many hardships, but in the end, he succeeded and became the only one who was kept on. I believe you are currently facing a similar situation to the protagonist, but you have to believe that this problem is temporary. As long as you don't give up, you will overcome this difficult situation sooner or later. Work hard, and if possible, take on part-time jobs to tackle the loans. I believe you can do it! Sending hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: How to deal with a controlling person in the workplace?
description: How to deal with a controlling person in the workplace? What to do in case of conflicts?

answers.answer_text: Good evening! I would like to ask if this controlling person is your boss? What are your own feelings? Because our evaluation of others is based on our own subjective feelings. In other words, you think he is controlling, but some people may not think so. So, the important thing is not what you should do? but what kind of relationship do you want to have with him? If you resist this person, then find out what you resist about him and expand on this idea from a belief perspective.
