For example, a child jumping on the sofa, the mother may think the child is naughty. But if the child is jumping on a trampoline in the playground, the mother will think the child is cute. The same child will be perceived differently by the mother in two different situations. So, what are the benefits of dealing with a controlling person? We cannot change others, we can only change our own mindset. So, try to consider this aspect and see if it can be helpful to you. A coin has two sides, both the heads and the tails make up the whole coin, so everyone has strengths and weaknesses, it depends on how you use them, whether it's the strengths or weaknesses, it's up to you to choose.

question: How can we help children maintain their enthusiasm for learning as they continue to take online classes?
description: Given the current situation of the epidemic, online classes will continue for a period of time, and even exams that usually have a sense of ritual will be canceled. Children may encounter difficulties and have poor performance in online classes. How can we help them get through this stage of online learning?
keywords: Growth, developmental patterns, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text: I don't know what age group you are teaching. Let me share my teaching experience this semester first. I teach a professional design course for freshmen. Most of the time, we use audio and screen sharing to conduct online classes. I found it difficult to achieve the same process and effect as offline teaching. Especially for our design major, it is challenging to provide detailed one-on-one guidance and interaction. At this point, I remembered someone saying, "What makes a good teacher? A good teacher is someone who can make students feel like they are at the forefront in the shortest time possible." I think it is about enabling children to quickly gain a sense of self-efficacy and make them feel that they can do it. So, I adjusted the teaching goals and process, not strictly adhering to previous professional requirements, but constantly seeking and affirming the strengths of the students. For the issues they encountered, I encourage them to make improvements little by little and then acknowledge their progress. As a result, the students gave very positive evaluations at the end of the semester, and they presented better assignment results than previous years. Each of them saw their own progress in this teaching process and outcome. I cannot see them for most of the class time, and I know they are not always completely attentive, but they did make efforts to complete assignments and made progress, which is enough. In the end, they were very reluctant to leave and ended this semester of learning with affirmation of their profession and themselves. I think this is a satisfactory teaching process. As for the knowledge points that may have been overlooked, they do exist, but with self-efficacy, any knowledge and skills can be learned in the future. So, my advice is twofold: 1. Do not overly emphasize discipline. It's normal for children to be less attentive during online classes and not fully engage. I experienced this myself when holding online meetings. I cannot sit quietly and listen to the leader's speech, and I am constantly distracted doing other things. So how can we expect children to sit still all the time? Let's look at them with understanding. Of course, we can demand discipline, but we should not blame them. 2. Provide timely feedback to students so that they can see their own progress. Why can exams promote student learning? Because they provide feedback on learning activities. Why are games so appealing? Because games provide feedback within minutes or seconds, showing the consequences of your actions, whether you win or lose. This feedback continuously stimulates you to take the next action. Therefore, in online teaching, if every student can receive timely feedback, their motivation will be greatly enhanced. The reason why students enter a period of exhaustion during long hours of online teaching is that they do not receive feedback for a long time. It is challenging to stimulate students with only persistence, lectures, and requirements. The feedback we provide to students can be positive or negative. But try to let each student see their own progress. After all, if you can't move forward in a game, you won't want to play anymore. Allowing students to see their own progress and feel that they can do it is a more valuable asset than any knowledge, which can stimulate their current learning enthusiasm and facilitate their future learning.

Hello, indeed as you said, this sudden pandemic caught us all off guard, especially students who have been affected the most. Unlike before, students used to attend classes in classrooms, where they were supervised by classmates, teachers, and school administrators. Regardless, the quality of online classes will certainly be affected compared to in-person classes. Being mischievous is a normal phenomenon for children, and each age has its own characteristics. In order to improve the efficiency of online classes, you can try the following methods to a certain extent: implementing a system of rewards and punishments, for example, rewarding a small sticker or exchanging it for a small prize for attending online classes diligently, organizing notes, and reviewing materials on a daily basis. Accumulating a certain number of stickers can be rewarded with a wish fulfillment, such as going to an amusement park or watching a movie. However, it is necessary to be cautious and find a balance to not diminish the child's motivation while considering practical issues such as family situation and its impact on the child's future. When the child encounters difficulties, guiding education can be adopted instead of just scolding them, focusing on encouragement. It is also important to find the child's interests, as life is not always about school. Each person has their own areas of strength and weakness, and it is necessary to identify the child's strengths and amplify them, as it will greatly help their life. Finally, I wish your child better and better grades! Thank you.

I don't know what age group the original poster is teaching. As a college student, I would like to share my personal thoughts based on my own experience.① The teacher's teaching level can also affect the students' listening level. The teaching content should not be simply read from the PowerPoint slides. The teacher should provide their own insights to help us understand and grasp the material better. It would also be helpful to incorporate relevant examples that align with the students' interests and age group, making the class more interesting and engaging.② Teachers can set requirements for students, such as random questioning or assignments. This helps to assess the effectiveness of the class and encourages those who are not paying attention to focus and grasp the material. Although this approach may cause some students to feel dissatisfied, it is indeed effective.③ When a teacher takes responsibility, students can feel it. Carefully correcting students' assignments and patiently answering their questions make students feel valued. As I don't have any teaching experience, these suggestions are solely from my perspective as a student and may have some limitations. However, I hope they may be helpful in some way.

Hello, OP! First, give you a virtual hug. From your description, it can be understood that due to the pandemic, students have to continue taking online classes, and exams have been canceled. You have noticed that students are being lazy and uninterested during classes, and you want to find ways to help them improve and maintain their enthusiasm for learning. Here are a few analysis and suggestions: 1. It is indeed difficult for online teachers to monitor and check the attendance of each student. However, during breaks in class, you can use some entertaining games to make the course material more interesting and stimulate student interaction during questioning. This can help prevent exhaustion and boredom caused by long hours of classes. 2. Let parents share the responsibility of supervision and companionship. You can assign practical assignments that require active involvement from the students. Since many students spend long hours at home in front of the computer for online classes, it's beneficial to have assignments related to the outdoors, such as collecting leaves or observing nature, to help adjust the students' state of mind.

Hello, this is a very realistic issue that has given us a new challenge despite the significant improvement in the epidemic situation. We are currently in the summer vacation period but also need to deal with the problem of children learning at home independently and managing their time properly. As parents, it is very important to provide guidance and supervision. First, it may be helpful to create a schedule, similar to a class timetable. Secondly, an detailed execution plan can be established, including "responsibilities of the executor and supervisor, methods of rewards and punishments, and measures to be taken in special circumstances." The section on special circumstances can be discussed and agreed upon by parents and children. List all possible situations in as much detail as possible to avoid any confusion or disputes during execution. These are just some of my personal thoughts, and please take them as reference.

You mentioned helping children maintain their enthusiasm for learning, which means you believe that enthusiasm for learning is something that exists in a certain amount and will gradually decrease over time unless there is external intervention. This enthusiasm will not be restored. And it is necessary to maintain this amount of enthusiasm in order to be considered normal and acceptable. Is that what you mean?

question: I was busy with exams and work before, how can I now adjust this lazy state a bit?
description: I was busy with exams, work, and daily life before. But now that I'm done with all that, I always feel out of sync and a bit lazy~ I want to relax, but the weather outside is so hot that I'm starting to doubt life! How should I adjust my state of mind~

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. We should aim to live each day like a spring, with moments of tension and moments of relaxation, without putting too much pressure on ourselves but also not becoming too relaxed. I can totally understand your feelings. When you're really busy and suddenly have some leisure time, it can make you either want to keep relaxing or become lazy. This is perfectly normal. It's great that you can think of ways to relax, but the weather might dampen your enthusiasm. You can try doing some indoor activities or projects with friends, such as handicrafts, archery, escape rooms, painting, board games, etc. Choose activities based on your and your friends' interests. Even if you don't go out, there are still plenty of fun things you can do. If you want to adjust your state of mind while at home, the same principles apply. Think about what activities and tasks you can realistically accomplish. What are you interested in and can focus on? For example, watching movies, reading books, watching documentaries, doing flower arrangements, etc. Give yourself a plan and schedule your time well. It doesn't have to be too tight, but make sure you're actually doing something instead of being lazy all the time. Best wishes.

question: I'm about to graduate from university, but everything is going wrong. I'm trapped in endless self-doubt...
description: In the past few years of college, I have been working hard. I have achieved good grades, conducted research, and participated in social activities. I have won many awards and have been enjoying myself with friends. I am an optimistic person and have always felt lucky to have been favored by fate. However, recently it feels like my life has suddenly hit a dead end. I missed the chance to be recommended for graduate school by just one position, and my national scholarship was manipulated by the college. I prepared for an important certification exam for more than a month, but I ended up getting acute gastroenteritis the night before the exam. I endured the pain and went to take the exam, but I still didn't pass. I also participated in an interview for a 20,000-dollar scholarship. The staff responsible for the PowerPoint presentation made a mistake on the spot. I tried to smile but couldn't control myself, and once I left, I started crying, and the opportunity slipped away. I also worried that I wouldn't be able to get into graduate school because I started preparing late. I called my mom, and although she loves me, she has always thought of me as outstanding, so she was disappointed that I didn't receive these awards. She also blamed me a little. I lie in bed, suffering from insomnia throughout the night. Some classmates in my class also discuss me privately, saying that I have bad luck and I'm just keeping up. Even though I always appear calm and relaxed in front of others, telling them it's okay, I can't bear it anymore. I try to console myself and be more open-minded, but I don't know where the future lies. Do I really have to compromise with each failure?
keywords: Emotions, depressed emotions, emotional regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I think you are a hardworking and diligent student. Although things haven't been going smoothly these days, it seems like you've encountered some setbacks. I don't deny your past achievements. Don't worry too much about things you've missed. Psychological stress can also affect your physical health. You are a very ambitious person, maybe even a bit of a perfectionist, but these negative emotions always burden your body. Although your friends have said a lot of pessimistic things next to you, it doesn't mean they don't care about you. They just think you are a little regretful. Actually, your experiences are more enriching than the average college student. There are plenty of classmates who just sit in their dorms, wait to eat and drink, or rely on their parents even as adults. If you feel tired, take a rest for a while. After all, personal growth is like a marathon. As long as the end result is good, it doesn't matter if you go slow or take it easy in the middle.

Let's organize and chat at the same time: #Just missed the opportunity for graduate recommendation, and the national scholarship was also brushed off by the college's black-box operation# Personal efforts are indeed important in society, but when it comes to competing for certain resources, it is crucial to understand the situation and the relationships involved before making choices. The phase you are currently in is the time when your comprehensive abilities are most tested for the graduate entrance exam. In addition to your efforts, you also need to understand your competitors, their situations, and the people responsible for allocating these resources, as well as their relationships with your competitors. Once you have a clear understanding of these factors, you will likely have a clearer idea of the outcome and be able to make other choices. Life is unpredictable and not everything will go smoothly. You may hope that your mother can understand, comfort, and support you. However, from your description, it seems that she may not be able to provide what you desire due to her own understanding and perspective. She may believe that as long as you work hard, you can solve any problem, but society is not like that. Society is much more complex and multi-dimensional, and success requires a holistic approach and effort in multiple areas. It is not like before high school where only academic performance mattered. Therefore, be prepared that your mother may not be able to provide you with more support in the future. This is not compromising on failure, but let's try to change our perspective. Through these experiences, you need to realize that excelling academically alone is not enough. In order to achieve what you want, you not only need to focus on your academic performance, but also understand how the social system operates. Given the resources you currently have, what is the likelihood of success in obtaining what you want? When you analyze a situation from multiple dimensions, you will discover a different world. As for classmates discussing you, this is normal. Just like when you look at something on the internet, there will be various perspectives and opinions that cannot be controlled. This is part of freedom of speech. However, what I'm concerned about is that you rarely mention friends, mentors, senior students, or senior sisters. How are your interpersonal relationships at school? If you are still feeling down and have time, we can talk about it.

question: How can a sophomore girl persuade her father, who plays Douyin (TikTok) with loud sound, to lower the volume?
description: I am a sophomore girl. My father loves to turn up the volume of his phone's external speaker very loudly, whether he is watching videos on Douyin, listening to voice messages on WeChat, at home or outside. I feel very embarrassed about it, but I don't know how to communicate with my father about it.
keywords: Family, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~~~ First, give OP a hug, because it's embarrassing when older people speak loudly in public, but after all, they are one's own father, and one doesn't know how to advise them. During the time when the older generation was growing up, there were not many functions even on the mobile phones themselves, let alone these mobile apps. So, the rules and manners among young people now, such as "not playing the sound too loudly", etc., are probably unknown to fathers. In their eyes, it is as natural as answering a phone call. OP wants to express their advice, but perhaps it can be done in a more gentle and subtle way, compromising on the rules a little bit. OP can sincerely tell their father that playing the sound of the phone in public can affect others and suggest that they not do it, but it is better to take a step back and tell their father that they don't have to restrain themselves at home, but they should still pay attention to the impact on others outside. Or they can buy headphones for their father and gently remind them about this issue while explaining how to use the headphones.

question: "Obsessive-compulsive thinking, what should I do if I can't find a reliable doctor?"
description: "Obsessive thinking" (found online, seems to fit) has reached the point where I am desperate and want to die. I am not afraid of death at all anymore. I wanted to make one last struggle. About a year ago, when my symptoms were still relatively mild, I tried going to a psychiatric doctor. The doctor's professional smile has been lingering in my mind. I could tell from our conversation that she thought my symptoms were just a result of overthinking, a problem with my own mindset, and there was nothing she could do about it. I felt like the doctor was just trying to get rid of me, and I understood that she was busy and didn't have the patience to deal with patients. Since then, I have no desire to see a doctor anymore. I have asked online a few times, but most of the respondents were not professionals, and some of their comments actually worsened my discomfort. I have been told that out of one hundred consultants in China, ninety-nine are unqualified, and some have only received one year of training before opening a psychology clinic. I am afraid that I won't be able to find a good psychologist and that it will worsen my condition. If I don't obtain the treatment results I want, I am relying on doctors as my last hope, but what if I'm not lucky enough? Fear, desperation, and fearfulness. I feel like I am the worst person in the world. Even Lin Yihan chose death despite being admitted to the hospital for treatment. If the thing I fear is actually true, I would be in great agony. I really don't want to leave my loved ones behind, but the burden on my mental health is too heavy, and I don't have the strength to carry on.
keywords: Treatment, mental crisis, psychological counseling, hospital institutions.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I sense that your distress has reached a painful level, causing you to feel anxious and enter a state of excessive negative thinking. It is important for you to recognize that your current state of mind is characterized by excessive and negative thinking, rather than a positive, proactive, and normal thinking state. Therefore, it is good that you have realized that your state needs adjustment and that you need the help of a doctor. This is a positive sign, indicating that your mind is still clear and your thinking is intact. So, what you need to do first is to be aware. Be aware of your state, your thoughts, your environment, and your true existence. Ask yourself, are your current thoughts really true? Do you believe that your thinking is realistic and objective?

What are the specific manifestations of obsessive thoughts? Do you constantly repeat certain behaviors? How do you feel now? Do you find it difficult to accept your own condition? You want to stop, but it feels like ants on a hot pan, unable to stop. I also had a period of time like that, feeling anxious and unable to stop even for a moment. I had no control over myself. This belongs to the realm of psychology. When you go to the hospital to see a doctor, especially a psychiatrist, their thinking often leans towards diagnosing and prescribing medication. They can't truly listen, understand, and see your needs like a psychological counselor can. It might be better to find a suitable counselor than to see a doctor. If you really need it, I can recommend my counselor to you.

question: I don't know how to face it for a moment. Is it really my fault to be scolded by the teacher?
description: Because I went to get vaccinated during the first English class last Friday afternoon, I didn't know about the English homework. I only heard others say that there was only one homework assignment for English class. So I just did that assignment and handed it to my group leader. My group leader asked me for another assignment, but I had no idea about it. Today at noon, the English teacher scolded me. I don't know how to explain to her. The teacher sent the list to the parent group chat in the evening. I feel like I have lost all my dignity. My dad also called me, and my mother-in-law told my aunt about it. I don't know how to face it all at once.

answers.answer_text: Title owner, hello, hug you~ After reading your description, it seems that you only neglected another English assignment while doing homework, and as a result, you were punished by the English teacher. I really sympathize with your situation. Based on your description of "today at noon, the English teacher beat me up. I don't know how to explain it to her," I'm not sure if you made a typo or if that's exactly what happened, but I think students' rights are important. Teachers should not randomly use physical punishment on students. If the teacher hit you because you didn't submit your assignment, your rights have been violated. I hope you can inform your family about this incident and protect your rights. After understanding the context you described, personally I think this is a small matter that just needs to be explained clearly. But it seems that it has caused a lot of concern from your parents. I think it's making a mountain out of a molehill. If you have already explained to the teacher that you didn't do it on purpose and she doesn't believe you, then it's not your fault. So I hope you can explain it clearly to your parents and let them understand that you are a serious and good child, and don't put too much pressure on yourself.

question: Is it wrong for me to just want to be a smart person, playing the role of a good person?
description: I used to be the class leader in elementary school, but later I found out that many classmates did not accept me, but had no choice because of my abilities and academics. I also had the support of the homeroom teacher. Afterward, I was afraid of getting on the bad side of both the teachers and students, so I focused on studying and didn't run for class leader again. In high school, my confidence was shattered and I suffered from depression. In college, I didn't dare to run for class leader and chose to focus on cultural and sports activities instead. In the recent chorus competition, I often gave advice to the class leader, but I felt that her way of handling things seemed too dominant and caused dissatisfaction among many people. It reminded me of my past. I made suggestions behind the scenes and discussed the division of labor with her, even though it wasn't my responsibility and I wanted to distance myself from it. When classmates asked if I was afraid, I just said that it was what the class leader said, and I even advised them not to waste their efforts. But when someone asked me, I explained myself and made sure not to criticize the class leader. Am I a bad person? I just want to be a smart person, but I feel like I'm being a troublemaker. I didn't speak ill of the class leader, but if you ask me, I won't say it wasn't me. I just think that I have strong organizational abilities. After all, I was one of the top ten squad leaders in elementary school. Moreover, the chorus competition falls under the category of cultural and sports activities, which I'm supposed to handle. I just gave the responsibility to the class leader and took on the role of conductor myself. Am I a bad person?
keywords: Growth, work, and learning are all important aspects of a student's development.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I understand your concerns. You were a class monitor in elementary school and stood out, which caused some students to resent you. In high school, you lacked confidence. Now that you're in college, you didn't run for class monitor, but you're always willing to give advice to the monitor. However, you're too afraid to show your abilities and hide yourself. You want to be a good person and doubt if you are a bad person. Hugs to you, dear child. Each of us encounters various problems in the process of growing up. By seeking help here, you have given yourself the possibility to become a better version of yourself. You are currently at a crucial period of self-identity formation. Self-identity develops through interactions with peers because we need to identify our social roles, such as how we appear to friends or classmates. It is normal to have doubts. You both want to showcase your abilities and fear drawing dissatisfaction from classmates. Acting differently in front of classmates and the class monitor makes you wonder if you are a bad person. Children who cannot obtain sufficient self-identity often dwell on past grievances, but in fact, our past experiences are meant to surpass them. The more a person understands how their early years were limited, the less constrained they are by those experiences. You may have fallen behind later, leading to a lack of self-confidence. As we grow up, we realize that we can gradually take responsibility for ourselves and accept contradictions and imperfections. There is no need to strive for perfection or for everyone to like us. The key is to learn to like ourselves, firmly believe that we are good people, willing to contribute to the class with a good heart. You are a young person of the new era and you want to live as yourself. You can try to find things that interest you and constantly practice. Also, learn to develop a strong sense of self, self-reliance, and dare to express your opinions bravely. See what changes occur. In this process, try to separate others' desires from your own and discover your strengths, such as your organizational and communication skills. Develop a sense of competence from small things. Competence represents our sense of value, feeling capable of achieving what we want when faced with difficulties and challenges in life, and feeling confident and happy. For example, being the conductor of a choir is great! I always admired our conductor when I was in school. Now let me share with you about the issue of people-pleasing. In our cultural background, we have been instilled with various concepts of "pleasing others" since childhood, such as "being a likable child will make you more popular." Therefore, we learn to observe others' expressions and act accordingly. We learn not to argue with others, to be humble, and to see disadvantages as blessings. We learn to be compliant and weak... We are willing to do anything to win love! Over time, this forms our personality traits, and we develop some automated responses. Wearing the mask of a good person uncontrollably causes us to lose ourselves and be afraid to express our true feelings, frequently abandoning our own thoughts just to please others. This feeling of discrepancy between our actions and our inner selves causes us great distress. Can we truly be happy like this? The answer is definitely no! Let us gradually learn to respect our inner feelings and no longer withhold our expressions due to others' feelings, and start living as our true selves. When a person learns to be their true self, helping others becomes a genuine joy rather than superficially trying to please them. This is something we need to practice step by step. There are too many people in life who enjoy pleasing others and being a people-pleaser! I recommend a book called "The Amazing Power of Being Yourself". Finally, I wish you gradual self-acceptance, self-identity, and growth!

question: What should I do when I feel like we're running out of common topics to talk about after being in a relationship for a long time?
description: I have been in a relationship for almost two years, and we initially built our connection through chatting. But now, I always feel like there's nothing to talk about, and it scares me. What should I do if someone else comes along and can have the same enjoyable conversations that we used to have? How can I change the current situation?

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, it seems like you are in a long-distance relationship or unable to meet frequently. After being in a relationship for two years, the main way of maintaining it is through chatting. It is necessary to feel concerned about the fragility of this situation, and your intuition is correct. From a deeper perspective, it's likely that the two of you came together because of a certain "familiarity." However, in order to sustain and deepen the relationship, it requires a deeper understanding of each other and becoming a role that the other person needs and relies on. These roles could be a lover, a close friend with mutual understanding, caretaker-like parents, a lively and creative child, or a broad-minded mentor, etc. If you feel that your interaction is becoming stagnant, you can try changing roles and see if it increases the other person's satisfaction and trust in you. This is a perspective adjustment from yourself, and also from the perspective of gaining a deeper understanding of the other person to increase your "intersection." For example, what does she like to eat, what games does she enjoy, what books and movies does she like, who are her friends, and who doesn't she like, and any memorable experiences from her childhood. You can also explore these aspects in yourself and have more conversations on this level with each other. I believe it can make your interactions more "meaningful" and more "exclusive".

question: Why do some people enjoy being alone but also fear what others think of them?
description: What is the reason for liking to be alone but fearing others' opinions of oneself?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I think in this society, there are many biases towards people's personalities, especially towards introversion and extroversion. People often believe that only extroverted and outgoing personalities are good, while introversion is considered bad and even abnormal, needing to be changed. But in reality, there is no good or bad when it comes to personality, introversion and extroversion are just two different characteristics. Introverted individuals prefer being alone and feel comfortable and at ease when they are by themselves, while extroverted individuals enjoy social interactions. In fact, both introversion and extroversion have their own advantages. There is a book called "Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking" which specifically discusses the strengths of introverted personalities. You mentioned that you like being alone but also fear how others perceive you. I think maybe you have an introverted personality; you feel more comfortable when you're alone. However, you also know that society has biases towards introversion, and you fear negative judgments about your preference for solitude, wishing to gain acceptance from others. But personality is difficult to change, and societal biases are hard to overcome, creating a seemingly contradictory situation. Perhaps you can find a balance point within this. Respect your own feelings while also making some concessions. You can spend most of your time alone but occasionally participate in group activities and engage in social interactions, so you don't completely isolate yourself from the community, and others won't perceive you as "antisocial." Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Sometimes, I am good at comforting others, but I don't know how to comfort myself when I'm sad.
description: I used to go out and have fun often, always laughing. Now I have a cold expression on my face. I don't know when I started to dislike smiling, I'm afraid of the dark but I like staying up late. I enjoy being in lonely places. I love listening to music, especially sad ones. It's like I am not myself again.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Give you a big hug first~ Let's take a look at your problem: in the past, you used to smile a lot, but now you have a cold face and don't like to smile. As we grow older, we encounter more and more things, and face increasing pressure. We learn to hide our emotions and not show our joy or laughter. After doing this for a long time, we start to dislike smiling and forget how to smile. We are afraid of the dark but have the habit of staying up late. We like places with no people and find a sense of safety in the darkness and solitude. At this time, we are usually more sensitive, because we can let go of our pressure and masks, not having to consider others and can be our true selves. We are good at comforting others, but we don't know how to comfort ourselves when we are sad. They say that bystanders see more clearly than those involved. When a problem happens to someone else, we can think calmly and choose the most favorable method. But when we face our own pain, we tend to magnify it, trapping ourselves with our own unhappiness and discomfort. So what should we do? Remain calm and adjust our mindset. First, we need to adjust our mindset and give ourselves some time to regain composure when encountering something that makes us sad. Without being calm, we won't be able to find a solution. It is crucial to stay calm and adjust our mindset. Venting, just like how OP comforts others, OP can also seek comfort from others. Through venting, OP can relax their mood and perhaps find a solution from a friend. The above is just my personal opinion, hoping to help you. Take care~.

Hello there~ I completely understand how you feel. *hugs* I have also experienced similar feelings, where I am able to comfort others with ease, but when it comes to comforting myself, I am at a loss for words. Sometimes, I hear that bittersweet phrase, "Since you are so good at comforting others, you must have also gone through many days of self-comfort." Slowly, I started to dislike smiling, my thoughts increased, and I began to feel more pressured... perhaps these changes are a proof of growth. But my kind friend, please don't lose the ability to be happy. Often, we need to change our perspective and look at everything happening to us in a different light. We need to find things that bring us joy and people who make us happy. Even if you like staying up late, make sure to take care of yourself. If you enjoy listening to sad songs, take a break and rest while listening to the music. Learn to treat each new day as a fresh start. Maybe yesterday was not particularly pleasant, and many unpleasant things happened, but don't let yesterday's unhappiness affect your life today. Sometimes, the sky may rain, and some people rush to wait for the rain to stop, while others take the opportunity to listen to the sound of raindrops, and some happily run into the rain laughing... there is always a positive side to everything. Let's look at that positive side together, and occasionally, if things don't go well, don't blame yourself. If you're feeling down, just wait a little while and then smile happily again. Best wishes~.

To help others without neglecting oneself, and as a doctor who does not treat oneself, no matter how reluctant we are to admit it, offering comfort, care, and support requires a certain amount of mental energy. Showing self-care is a kind thought towards oneself. As a helper, one becomes sensitive to the emotions of others and uses compassion to soothe them. This reminds me of a role: a ritualist. I wonder what image comes to your mind, but in my heart, the ritualist symbolizes the moon, dressed in a light blue robe. In the quiet of the night, I empty myself and pray to the moon. While providing warmth and healing to others, it also gives everyone the power and energy for self-healing, self-growth, and warming others. Giving too much requires giving oneself some space and time, perhaps to encounter other warm-hearted individuals who can provide strength. Rest is necessary after working so hard. I believe that you are still the person who radiates with a smile. May these words accompany you.

question: Should I prioritize helping others or focus on myself?
description: I am someone who doesn't like to bother others, and also doesn't like others to bother me. In today's society, it is often emphasized that you should be yourself. Sometimes, I can't distinguish when I should stick to being myself and when I should help others. I don't want to help when others ask for it, but what should I do in the end? Should I help or just be myself? If I refuse to help with anything, surely nobody will like me. If I help, I feel annoyed and like I'm only pleasing others. How do I find the right balance?

answers.answer_text: --Give the OP a big thumbs up. The OP has raised a thought-provoking question: when faced with things we don't want to help with in life, should we follow our hearts and learn to refuse? Or should we reluctantly help for the sake of maintaining harmony with colleagues? In this regard, I will share my humble opinion in the hope of inspiring the OP. 1. Stick to one's bottom line and principles: when faced with others' requests, many times we don't know whether we should do it or if it is the right thing to do. Therefore, we often feel conflicted, confused, and unsure. To eliminate this unpleasant mental state, my personal suggestion is that the OP needs to have a comprehensive understanding of themselves and clearly know what their bottom line and principles are, including what is not to be violated. With a bottom line and principles, when facing others' requests, we have a reference point to consult and judge right from wrong. If we cannot always follow our hearts and do everything as we wish, at least we can ensure that everything we do is right. This way, the inner conflict and confusion about handling things will also be reduced to some extent. 2. Learn to help others and enjoy being helped: #I am someone who doesn't like to trouble others, nor do I like to be troubled by others.# From the OP's description, it can be seen that the OP is a relatively independent person, so most of the time, they feel that they can be self-reliant and competent in everything without relying on others. However, the reality is that we live in society and no one can completely detach themselves from the community and be independent of the world. We always have to constantly adapt to others and help each other in our respective fields, growing together. While a person can certainly grow, a group of people can grow faster and go further. The OP must first recognize this and eliminate their resistance to mutual help and cooperation within the group. Many times, the insistence on being oneself or helping others is simply a bias in our thinking and cognition. Helping others may not bring immediate rewards, and it may make you feel like you're wasting time and life, and it's not even your own task, giving you a sense of "irrelevance" and rejection. However, the saying "giving flowers to others leaves fragrance on one's hands" is not empty talk. Helping others may not bring you immediate rewards, or you may never get any rewards in your lifetime, but perhaps it will give you a return at some moment in your life. Therefore, appropriately helping others is not against your heart, it is not a lack of perseverance in being oneself, but rather it broadens the scope of your life, making your life more meaningful and making the world a warmer place. If you change perspective, perhaps it won't be so difficult.

This seems to be a choice. Throughout our lives, it seems that we are constantly oscillating between self and role, between freedom and conformity, between loneliness and relationships. There is no right or wrong, only choices, each corresponding to different experiences and outcomes. Being oneself is an important mission in our journey in this world. But what is oneself? How to be oneself? Indeed, these are topics that linger throughout our lives. Oneself, purely and clearly, free and transparent, seems to be such a simple existence. No matter if you are standing, walking, or sitting at this moment, no matter where you are. However, where can we find such purity? We are born helpless, we learn to walk unsteadily, we babble and learn to speak, we are small yet precious, and we have so many things that we cannot do on our own. We are always in relationships, even as the wind blows us into adulthood, our survival, our basic needs still rely on the relationships around us. A person is the sum of all social relationships. Freedom always exists relatively within a framework. Without problems, there are no relationships. Without relationships, we are stuck in place. Once we enter into relationships, freedom will disappear completely. We need to consider the current situation, the needs of the current relationships, the feelings of others, and so on. Should we rely on others or follow our inner truth? There is no right or wrong, only choices. Is life a play? In this grand play of life, whether smooth sailing or filled with difficulties, we must participate, whether we like it or not. Oneself, beyond everything and within nothing? After experiencing the years gone by, the only thing left is just an experience, whether it is sweet or bitter, varied flavors or mixed emotions, it is merely a series of precious and wonderful experiences. That's all. Hello, focus on personal growth, I am here, the world and I love you.

Hello! Warm hug to you. When I read your description, I feel that you are very anxious and conflicted. In fact, many things can be done following your heart. Instead of thinking too much about it, it's better to take action. For example, if you are someone who doesn't like to help others and also dislikes others helping you because you find it troublesome, then don't help! However, you also fear that others will distance themselves from you and neglect you, which makes you anxious. Based on the analysis above, it can be seen that: 1. You have confused the spirit of helping others with being true to yourself. Learn to differentiate it. If you help someone and receive gratitude or if the other person doesn't respond at all, that's the action of helping! It comes from the heart, an act of selfless dedication without expecting anything in return. This is different from what you think of as being true to yourself. Truly being true to yourself means being someone who can control themselves, propel themselves forward, and have their own thoughts and opinions. Helping others, on the other hand, is to some extent, an act of altruism, a polite gesture, and a virtue. 2. Reduce your fantasies and self-definitions. If you feel that helping others is troublesome or that it is a way to please others, these thoughts are not based on reality. The only time helping others might give a sense of pleasing others is when there is a purpose behind approaching and helping them. This is not unconditional help, it is maintaining a relationship. 3. Learn to understand that helping others is helping yourself. Everyone has different circles and environments. Perhaps by helping others in unfamiliar situations, they will also lend you a helping hand when you need it. No one can live independently without an organization or society. In summary, adjust your mindset. If it is not illegal or against discipline, help as much as you can. However, if it goes beyond the general limits of what people can handle, if the demands are too much or too high, then it should be decided based on the situation. I hope this sharing will be helpful to you!

Hello, OP. I can really sense your emotions and dilemma through your words. It can be frustrating to help others while feeling burdened, but at the same time, not helping others may make you feel disconnected from society. However, humans are social beings and cannot live completely independently. We are interconnected with others in various ways, and there will be times when others seek help from us, just as we may seek help from others. You mentioned feeling like helping others is like seeking their approval. Let's differentiate between seeking approval and helping others: seeking approval involves acting out of fear of how others perceive us, offering help before being asked for it because of our own sensitive reactions. Helping others, on the other hand, is about providing assistance when others genuinely need it and willingly transmitting our own energy to them. Based on your words, it seems that you do not belong to the category of seeking approval. Therefore, you don't need to think this way and unnecessarily burden yourself. So, it's okay to help, but it depends on how you do it. Not everyone deserves to be helped. Some people, after receiving help, understand gratitude and acknowledge the good you have done for them, while others may burn bridges and make you feel unappreciated. When it comes to situations, it's important to assess your own capabilities. Some requests for help can be tackled appropriately, but there are cases where you can't help or where helping might backfire. It is important to consider the consequences. If you want to help others but are not in the right mood or not willing to lend a hand, even if you help, you won't find true happiness. In those situations, it's best to find polite reasons to decline. Wishing you well.

I am a people pleaser. As the saying goes, when you start pleasing others, you start offending the whole world. People cannot be pleased enough; the more you please, the more you get bullied. If it's among colleagues, you can assess if they are worth accommodating. If they are ungrateful and unreciprocating, you can politely decline by making up a plausible excuse. You don't have to worry about offending them because they won't remember your kindness even if you help them. Another type of people are genuine and honest individuals. If you genuinely like someone and they have a good heart and are reasonable, helping them would also mean they would help you. Only these people are worthy of your assistance.

Dear, you are just like my former colleague in character, a typical people-pleaser. Because you feel uncomfortable refusing, others have gotten used to coming to you. Why do they come to you? Because you are easy to talk to and won't say no. How can we change this? First: put away your embarrassment and bravely say no. Secondly: abandon the fear of rejection and set clear goals! Thirdly: be brave in overcoming psychological barriers. Finally: if you achieve this, not only will your mind find balance, but you will also feel unprecedented relaxation in your body! Keep going, be brave and be yourself!

Dear: Hugs to you. Being able to ask this question, I can feel that you must be feeling tired recently. Since you mentioned "helping," it means that this matter, or these matters, are not your obligation. Since it is not your obligation, then helping is a favor, and not helping is staying within your limits. If it is convenient for you and you are willing, then you can do it freely, according to your mood. If it is difficult and goes against your will, I think it is perfectly acceptable to politely and tactfully refuse, or directly and plainly tell the other person that you will help, but there are difficulties or inconveniences. This way, the other person will also understand your difficulties and it won't cause any estrangement. Hugs to you once again. It seems you have been feeling distressed lately. Be brave and refuse for the sake of your own heart, and love yourself and your body more. To put it succinctly, I don't want to be too verbose. Please bravely and wisely reject unreasonable demands. It is your right.

This is a problem that many people might have, and it's indeed difficult to grasp and explain clearly. Each person has their own boundaries. Let me try to answer it. Generally, the people who have this confusion are those who don't have a deep understanding of themselves yet. That's why you might feel conflicted because of the seemingly contradictory statements in society. "Nowadays, society says we should be ourselves...and not willing to help with anything, for sure nobody would like me." Seeing everything in a binary way is indeed a collective characteristic of our nation. Many times, we unconsciously use simple thinking such as right or wrong, good or bad, to judge. From the way you asked the question, it seems like you have set helping others and being yourself in opposition, but these two are not contradictory. Helping others doesn't hinder you from being yourself, and being yourself doesn't hinder you from helping others. When you help others, if there are "emotions," carefully feel where these "emotions" come from. Are they truly detrimental to being yourself? Or are they from other reasons? Gradually, you will understand what you truly care about. Acting in order to appear as if you want to be yourself can be seen as imitation and becomes a laughingstock. By asking this question, it shows that you have already noticed that something is "off." The road ahead is long, I will seek and explore from top to bottom. Keep it up, best wishes!

question: Diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago, how to establish a good communication relationship with dad?
description: My father has been single all along. Three years ago, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and has been dealing with anxiety and depression. I feel like he rarely talks and is not particularly interested in conversations. I want to know how I can have a deeper connection with him.
keywords: Family, parental communication, family members' health.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I hope my answer can help you. It's tough for you, sending you a hug. Problem: Your father doesn't like to communicate with you much due to Parkinson's disease? Reason: Due to cell death, the brain of Parkinson's disease patients has difficulty transporting the neurotransmitter dopamine to the basal ganglia, resulting in basal ganglia dysfunction. Most people with Parkinson's disease are unable to produce dopamine. Dopamine, as another neurotransmitter in the brain, is also important for maintaining intimate relationships. So the reason why your father is not interested in chatting with you is because his illness prevents him from establishing an intimate relationship with you. Solution: Parkinson's disease has depressive symptoms, so it is important to seek medical help as early as possible, do early screening, and track the progress actively for treatment. You need to go to the hospital to evaluate the severity of your father's depression. If the symptoms are mild, he may need to take antidepressant medication. You should pay close attention to your father's depressive symptoms. If the severity of depression is high, the patient may have strong suicidal thoughts and behaviors. In addition to medication, psychological therapy is also necessary to increase the patient's awareness, adjust mindset, enhance and correct their understanding of the disease, and adopt an optimistic attitude towards the disease. It's really tough for you, so stay strong!

Many times, it's not that fathers don't want to communicate with us, but rather due to the influence of illness and some burdens in their hearts, they don't want to become a burden to their children. 1. Many parents don't want to be a burden to their children. People really can't avoid growing old, especially when they reach a certain age, the functions of their body will decline, and Parkinson's disease cannot be truly cured. It must be supplemented with medication. Therefore, fathers often cannot subjectively control their words and actions. So if there's a chance, we can spend more time talking with our father, reminiscing about the good times together, and let him know that we are always concerned about him. Sometimes we need to let our family members stay active. Once a person has nothing to do, they will start to overthink, especially when they can't do anything for their children. Parents often worry that they will cause trouble for their children, especially for those who have a strong personality, this is particularly serious. So what is the reason why father has remained single all these years? If it's for us, then sometimes we need to learn to help father open up his heart. 2. Give father some personal space. We care because we worry, and because we worry, we want to integrate faster. Father may have gotten used to being alone after all these years, so he tends to handle many things by himself. Therefore, based on father's personality and our usual interaction, we can analyze whether father has the ability to self-regulate. If necessary, we can take father to see a professional psychological counselor. At the same time, we can ask father what he is anxious and worried about, and we can discuss it together to see if there are better solutions. If necessary, let father make the decision himself, and we, as children, can play a supportive role. The world and I love you.

Hello, OP. I also sense your deep love and concern for your father, but Qianqian doesn't really understand Parkinson's, so I looked up some information. Parkinson's is a common neurodegenerative disease in middle-aged and elderly people, and it is also the most common extrapyramidal disease in this age group. The prevalence rate among people over 65 is 1,000 per 100,000, with slightly more males than females as age increases. The main clinical features of the disease are resting tremor, bradykinesia, increased muscle tone, and postural instability. Some nursing methods include: 1. Safety care: Due to these main features, many patients intentionally reduce their activities in order to minimize the risk of falls and other accidents. Therefore, it is important to create a safe environment for the patients, such as ensuring there are no obstacles on the ground and adding handrails in hallways to increase the safety of opening and closing doors. Items that can be grasped should be added in toilets and bathrooms to facilitate urination, defecation, and changing clothes. 2. Dietary care: Food should be diverse and soft, and small frequent meals are recommended. Grains, vegetables, fruits, and foods such as melon seeds, almonds, and black sesame that contain a lot of tyrosine, can promote the synthesis of levodopa and are the best food choices for patients. Due to swallowing difficulties, food should be cut into small pieces or ground. 3. Rehabilitation exercise care: This is important to prevent and delay joint stiffness and limb contractures. If conditions permit, activities such as practicing Tai Chi or taking walks can help patients move their joints and massage their limbs to promote blood circulation and prevent joint stiffness and limb contractures. Movements should be gentle. 4. Psychological care: Depression is the most common emotional disorder in people with Parkinson's disease, with a prevalence rate ranging from 40% to 50%. Although the rate of comorbid depression in Parkinson's disease is quite high, the treatment of depression is often overlooked in clinical practice. Therefore, it is important for families to give more care and communicate with warm language, understand his pain, and know the help he needs. Ask him questions like, "How have you been feeling recently?" "Is there anything we can do to help you?" "Have you encountered any difficulties recently?" Even though sometimes he may still lack facial expressions or may not say much, he can actually sense your care for him. After all, so much of it is conveyed through your words and actions.

Hello there! I completely understand how you feel, sending you a virtual hug. It's evident that you are a very filial child and deeply care about your father. You mentioned that your father was diagnosed with Parkinson's syndrome three years ago. I wonder if he has been actively receiving treatment? As far as I know, Parkinson's syndrome can be improved with medication. In terms of treatment, it would be helpful to talk to the treating doctor to understand the situation and encourage your father to seek treatment. Due to this condition, your father may not be able to have a normal conversation with you, what he needs the most is your understanding and care. Spend more time with him, even if there are moments of silence. Show more concern and ask him if there's anything he'd like to do or eat. Find out what he's interested in or if he would like to take walks around the neighborhood regularly, it can also be beneficial. I'm not entirely sure about your father's current condition, but I understand your desire to communicate with him normally. However, it's important to adjust your expectations based on the reality. Being there for him is the most caring thing you can do, perhaps he just wants to see you grow up healthy by his side. Best wishes!

Hello, you are a filial child, and I admire you. I hope my answer can help you! Your dad has been single for a long time as you grew up, and he often neglects taking care of his family due to work. For your dad, he is aging in a relatively lonely environment. This is not a good thing for elderly people or those who are about to enter old age. After all, as we get older, our physical functions start to decline, and we need to adapt to the role transition and slowly accept that we are getting old. At this time, feeling lonely without anyone to accompany us in old age can be even more distressing. I suggest that when your dad's health improves, you should contact the community neighborhood committee and let your dad join their activities, interact more with people of his age, and participate in activities among peers. This will be beneficial for his physical and mental well-being. Seeking help, although your dad has been single, does he have close relatives or friends? You can seek their help because it may be overwhelming for you to take care of him alone, especially considering his current condition with anxiety, depression, and poor health. Having more family and friends visit him will make him feel valued and accompanied, providing him with comfort and strengthening his belief in recovery. How to have deeper communication with your dad? Communication and finding ways to get along between father and son are actually a long process of cultivation. You have been having this confusion of not knowing how to chat or have deep conversations, and I believe this is not a problem that can be solved in a day or two. Just as "it takes years to freeze three feet of ice," the thawing process also takes time and effort. If you want to have deep communication and topics to talk about with your dad, you can try the following: 1) Find his interests and research them, then integrate into his routine to cultivate common topics. 2) Share your current situation. No dad doesn't want to know about his child, sometimes it's just a generation gap or not knowing where to start the conversation. So, you can proactively share your recent experiences and let your dad understand you, bringing you closer. 3) Encourage your dad to speak. In any relationship, there is always one person who is more enthusiastic and can set the mood. Since your dad doesn't talk much and you want to change this situation, you can try asking him questions and asking him more. Over time, as you ask more questions, naturally, there will be more conversations. Finally, I wish you and your dad a better relationship. Good luck!

Hello, after reading your description, I can feel your concern for your father, which reflects the deep bond between you as father and son. I hope you and your father can have a better life. Based on your description, I will share my personal opinion. Dealing with a father who has Parkinson's disease is extremely challenging for you. You are doing a dance with a storm. Hang in there! 1⃣️ Gain knowledge about Parkinson's disease. You can find reliable resources to learn about it and learn how to help manage the condition. (Each Parkinson's patient is different.) 2⃣️ Communicate openly with your father, which can help relieve emotions and avoid big emotional fluctuations caused by anger. Regularly communicate with doctors, as they can provide valuable information about Parkinson's disease and opportunities for treatment resources. (This advice is based on the experience of netizens on Zhihu.) 3⃣️ Take care of yourself while taking care of your father. When your own mindset is good, you will have a better mindset and more energy to take care of your father, which can further promote communication between you. 4⃣️ Encourage your father to participate in social activities. Finally, I hope your father's symptoms can gradually lessen or even recover completely. You are a young person who communicates with hearts. It's not easy to type all this out, so give it a thumbs up!

Hello there: Sending you a warm hug. It's evident that you are a very filial child. I can understand your feelings. Our parents give us life and selfless love, but when they grow old and need us, there's often little we can do for them. I will do my best to answer your questions and hopefully provide you with some help. Parkinson's disease is primarily characterized by the degeneration and death of dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra of the brain. This leads to a significant decrease in dopamine content in the striatum, resulting in the symptoms of the disease. Parkinson's disease can have a significant impact on a person's daily life, such as limb stiffness, mobility difficulties, and facial masking. Patients may feel different from those around them and gradually develop negative emotions such as anxiety and depression. From what you've mentioned, your father has been living alone and was diagnosed with Parkinson's syndrome three years ago. He is currently experiencing anxiety and depression. Most of his anxiety likely comes from concerns about his own health. With so much uncertainty, it's understandable that he is anxious. I suggest you do some research on Parkinson's disease and provide your father with some knowledge about it. This way, he can have a better understanding of his condition and hopefully feel less anxious. I once had a severe case of chronic nephritis, and the doctor told me it was difficult to cure. If not properly controlled, it could lead to uremia. I was very scared at the time and felt anxious every day. Then I did a lot of research and gained a systematic understanding of the disease. As a result, my anxiety decreased, and with active cooperation with the doctor's treatment, I recovered in six months. Although it's difficult for Parkinson's disease to be cured, it can be managed with medication, so there's no need to be overly anxious. Now, let's talk about the communication issue with your father. Companionship is the most heartfelt declaration. Your father has been single for many years, and he must feel very lonely deep down. You should spend more time with him. During your conversations, you can update him about your current situation. Parents are most concerned about their children, and I don't believe for a moment that he has no interest in your life. Also, try to seek outside assistance. You can invite some old friends of your father's age to keep him company and engage in activities that he is interested in. Only people of the same generation truly understand their likes and thoughts. If his physical condition allows, take him out for a walk. Regularly seeing the outside world and the beauty of nature can help relax the mind.

question: Broke up with my ex-girlfriend, feeling regretful and miserable, I even feel like I don't want to live anymore...
description: We were in an online relationship. After initially dating, we broke up, and then after two years, I went back to her to try and reconcile. At the beginning, I didn't really feel like I liked her when we broke up. This time around, we were doing well at first, and I treated her well. But later on, I became indifferent towards her, and she kept persisting. Then she suggested breaking up, and suddenly I felt regret. I regret not paying attention to her unhappiness, and not cherishing her properly. We've met in person. Now I feel very upset, to the point where I even have thoughts of dying. I feel so sorry for her.
keywords: Love, heartbreak, and how to win back an ex.

answers.answer_text: Friend, hello! Facing a breakup with your girlfriend, your heart must be filled with immense sadness. It's clear that you also have deep regrets and hope to reconcile with her. However, it seems like you're also torn and unsure of how to have a good relationship with your girlfriend. It gives the impression that you need an intimate connection, but one that you must control. To put it simply, you should be there when you're needed and step back when you're not. (Of course, this is just my personal speculation, so please don't take it personally.) I want to suggest that in the realm of interpersonal relationships, perhaps you should first understand how you interact with others and what kind of relationship you want. By understanding your own inner needs, you can better handle situations. Do you agree? Additionally, if you truly feel sorry for your ex-girlfriend, would it be possible to do something to make amends? Even if you don't know if you can reconcile, at least letting her understand your feelings towards her can leave a better impression in both of your minds. After all, love is a destiny, regardless of whether you stay together or not. Lastly, I want to say that life is full of setbacks, occurring at all times. It's not just your experience, it's everyone's. Death is both a release and a way of letting go. Your expression of regret reminded me of a saying: the regrets of life come not from what you've done, but from what you haven't done. Regardless, the world and I love you.

question: I always get involved in relationships that hurt me, what should I do?
description: Because since childhood at home, my parents did not respect my independence, liked to control, liked to blame with words, now I always make friends with people who have strong control desires and like to blame others. After making friends with them, I always get hurt in their words and actions. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, learn to see the world with your own eyes. While the environment can certainly influence our choices, when such choices harm us, we should know how to refuse. From your description, I can sense the conflicting and uncomfortable feelings you have when making friends. It may be due to the authoritarian and controlling education you received from your parents, which has shaped your character to be fragile and dependent. Being with friends of the same type may make you feel familiar and secure because you are being pushed and restrained, giving you a sense of care. Parenting styles cannot be changed overnight, but you still need to communicate and express your position and feelings to your parents, especially when you feel they do not respect you or blame you. Making mistakes can result in blame, but they should also listen to your feelings and thoughts. When you make a mistake, they should educate you on how to avoid similar ones in the future, rather than just blaming you. Therefore, you must learn to communicate and exchange ideas with your parents, gradually making them aware that you are not a tool to be manipulated by them but a person with your own feelings and thoughts, and that you also need encouragement and affirmation. It is essential to clarify your needs and boundaries in friendships, allowing for mutual tolerance and growth, but you should not suppress or hide your thoughts and be in a passive position. Ask yourself why you always make friends like this. What are the qualities that attract you to them, and what do you want to gain from these relationships? How do you truly feel when they control and blame you? Do you clearly express your feelings and reactions when their words hurt you? Perhaps you have become accustomed to being treated in this way, even though it causes you pain, and you may be unable to break free from this pattern, which is the issue you need to confront and change. Change your unreasonable beliefs; there are many ways in which the friends you make can show that they care for you. You should be equal and loving towards each other. You may have conflicts and make mistakes that hurt each other, but you should not always hide your wounds and suffer silently. Only you can change this situation, do not be afraid, action needs to be taken for things to change. Truly express yourself, value your feelings, whether with friends or parents. Good luck.

question: Do all symptoms of depression match, does that mean it is definitely depression?
description: The condition will change in periods, sometimes it aligns with severe symptoms, sometimes it aligns with moderate symptoms, and in between there are a few days of normalcy.

answers.answer_text: Hello, first let me give you a hug and support for your confusion. I'm not sure if you are talking about these symptoms in yourself or someone else? According to the latest version of DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition), depressive disorders include major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder. The diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder are as follows: A. Presence of five or more related symptoms during the same 2-week period, representing a change from previous functioning, with at least one of the symptoms being (1) depressed mood or (2) loss of interest or pleasure. B. The symptoms cause clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. C. The symptoms are not attributable to the physiological effects of a substance or another medical condition. It can be seen that the diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder can be viewed from three aspects: symptom criteria, time criteria, and functional criteria. Simply looking at the time criteria, it requires "at least the same 2-week period," while you mentioned that "the condition changes in different periods," and "there are a few normal days." Based on the statements you described, if it is about yourself and you are still able to seek help online, it indicates that social functioning is not significantly impaired. Therefore, the statement in your title that "all symptoms of depression match" is not accurate. From the information currently provided, there is not enough evidence to suggest that it is major depressive disorder, let alone stating that it is definitely major depressive disorder. However, similar symptoms may indicate the presence of depressive emotions. It is recommended to seek professional diagnosis from a specialized hospital and treat accordingly based on the professional diagnosis and the advice of a doctor. I hope my answer can provide you with some advice and thoughts. The world and I love you.

Hello, according to the answers provided, it appears that your current symptoms are consistent with the symptoms of depression. Additionally, the intermittent nature and diverse manifestation of these symptoms may indicate a combination of various conditions. The questions raised are concise, and we need a more in-depth understanding. I would suggest that you go to a hospital for psychological diagnosis. It would be better for a doctor to have a face-to-face consultation to accurately determine the specific situation.

question: Does the control of sexual desire depend on having a correct understanding of oneself?
description: "The control of sexual desire lies in having a correct understanding of oneself. If one cannot have a clear understanding of one's own perceptions and needs regarding sex, it is naturally impossible to control oneself in this area or there will indeed be situations where one cannot control it, even though they may have a good understanding of sex, but lack understanding of oneself."

answers.answer_text: Sexual desire is the result of the comprehensive interaction of various factors. Not only are factors such as thinking, consciousness, emotions, and environment related to sexual desire, but language, words, pictures, and music also have a significant impact on it. On the surface, men's sexual desire seems stronger than women's because women who take the initiative in sexual activities are relatively rare. This is influenced by both physiological and psychological factors. Many women are accustomed to repressing their sexual needs, so in most cases, men appear more proactive in expressing their sexual desire than women. However, this does not mean that men's sexual desire is stronger than women's. First, when your sexual desire arises, you should learn to be aware of its presence. Second, you should accept it. You can handle it through self-deprecation or use methods to divert your attention and ignore it. Third, you should tell yourself to let go of it. Perhaps what I am about to say may be difficult for you to understand, but you can carefully consider it: is the arousal of sexual desire a separate entity from the arousal of your emotions? If you are angry, your body also feels uncomfortable; if you are sad, there is also a dual reflection of emotions and the body. In fact, sexual desire is also an emotion. Therefore, you can also let go of it. There are many ways to do this, such as reciting mantras or meditating, observing your breath, or entering your own inner world. Once you let go of various emotions (including sexual desire) and enter the deeper level of your being, you will discover a new world where everything is calm and yet full of vibrant colors. It is better than shallow sex and ordinary emotions.

Hello, how are you? Seeing words is like seeing each other. My understanding of this statement is: You should have a correct understanding of sexuality and understand yourself correctly. First of all, sexuality is not everything in life. If one is frequently addicted to sex, it can easily ruin a person. On the other hand, for many people, sex is essential. Don't think that discussing these things is shameful. We should look at it with the right perspective. So, what does understanding yourself mean? First, you need to understand what kind of person you are. What does sex mean to you? What are your goals? How much energy do you put into sex? Learn to face all of this instead of avoiding it. For any mistakes you have in this area, correct them if you have them and strive for improvement if you don't. By doing all this, you will successfully understand sex and yourself.

question: What causes anxiety? Why is it always present?
description: Students will feel anxious before exams, anxious while writing papers, and anxious when looking for jobs. Pregnant women will feel anxious about giving birth and will continue to feel anxious after having a child. So what exactly is anxiety for individuals? Why does it persist at all times?

answers.answer_text: Anxiety is a state of sustained tension. We feel anxious because we care about the final outcome, crave praise and recognition, and strive for excellence. There are too many uncertainties in anything we do, and we cannot guarantee success. Although anxiety can cause discomfort, mild discomfort confirms our importance. Mild anxiety can also motivate us to move forward, to gather energy and face the challenges with all our might, resulting in exceptional performance. Anxiety actually signifies the presence of a crisis, and sometimes a crisis can be an opportunity, inspiring our unlimited potential.

question: Female, 11, the age of carefree elementary school yet always suffering from insomnia?
description: Since I was a child, I always had a habit of digging deep into questions. Whenever I think about something, even after I've figured it out, I continue to think about other things related to it. If no one interrupts me, I can spend a whole day just thinking. I only noticed this pattern in the past few years. I began using this pattern to combat nightmares. The method I used was forcing myself to change my thoughts and not think about things that would cause nightmares, but rather focus on other interests. This method stopped working two years ago. No matter what, I would always think about scary things, and then it became uncontrollable. It was difficult to forcibly change my thoughts, and I couldn't describe the discomfort I felt. I would also get headaches. Once the lights were off and I went to sleep, everything I saw reminded me of something scary. Taking a nap during the day didn't affect me, and everything was smooth sailing when the lights were on at night. The only way I could sleep peacefully was staying up late to read novels or sleeping with someone else. However, if I fell asleep by myself, I would worry about not being able to sleep and having random thoughts. I think I might have some mental or psychological problems, such as delusional disorder, because I tend to overthink a lot. In my daily life, I have a lot of internal struggles, and not only do I tend to overthink, but I also always think about the worst case scenarios.
