I should be carefree at this age, still in primary school, but I keep experiencing these phenomena. I am very scared, should I see a psychologist or something?
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, treatment methods, mental disorders.

answers.answer_text: OP, it shows that you are a focused person. There are fewer and fewer people who can concentrate like you these days. After reading your situation, it seems that you tend to think of negative things at night, but when you sleep with someone else or fall asleep, you don't experience this. Taking a nap also doesn't affect you. Maybe it's because you're afraid of being alone in a dark environment. Thinking a lot and having an active mind is not a bad thing. Feeling afraid and thinking of negative things in a dark environment is not delusional. Maybe you can ask your parents to turn off the lights after you fall asleep. Maybe you can try to overcome the fear that the darkness brings you. Perhaps after turning off the lights, try listening to relaxing music, close your eyes, and slowly ease into sleep. In time, you may become desensitized to the dark environment. Maybe after thinking of something negative, you'll open your eyes and realize that nothing actually happened in reality. Those thoughts were all fake, and maybe you will gradually overcome your fear. Best wishes!

question: It is better to have some activity in the room in order to feel more at ease. Why do you feel exceptionally scared when you are alone?
description: In recent days, I have been at home by myself. My childhood experience was mostly that I felt like a very bad child. I had a bad temper as a child and offended many people around me. Maybe because of this, I have no ability to handle things. Recently, at home during the day, I feel dull and the only thing that brings me some peace is watching TV. Otherwise, I feel uncomfortable and start having random thoughts. This goes on every day until I can't bear it anymore and go to sleep late at night. At night, I have a sense of fear, like being afraid of the dark, feeling depressed, and having a feeling of fear. In short, I need some movement or noise in the room to feel more at ease. Now I can't concentrate on studying or doing things anymore. Can you please tell me what should I do? Are there any material or psychological methods?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. The ability to be alone needs to be cultivated over a long period of time, and it does not mean that a person should always live alone at home, but rather that one can spend time alone as well as integrate into a group. Many adults cannot tolerate living alone for a long time, let alone a child. Fear of darkness and fear of being alone at home are instinctual fears we had as children because we fear danger, being abandoned, and not being liked by our parents. This is a normal situation and can be gradually overcome, so don't worry. I suggest that during the day, you take care of your studies, you can play soft music or turn on the TV with a low volume, so that you won't be easily affected, or open the window to let in the outside sounds, to establish a connection between yourself and the surrounding environment, rather than being isolated alone. Watching TV all the time is a way to avoid the situation, making yourself numb and no longer have fear and worry in your heart. However, the more you watch TV, the more difficult it will be for you to face problems and the more restless and uncontrollable you will become. I have also had similar experiences. When I was young, I used to live in a place with the TV on with a loud volume, all doors and windows open, as if only in this way I would feel a little "lively" and being paid attention to. When you go to sleep, soak your feet, then play some music, set a time, and try to remember some happy things to slowly fall asleep. You can also try this method, or find a suitable method on your own, to make yourself feel better. When you are alone, you must give yourself some positive suggestions or find joy in your daily life, such as raising plants and meditating or painting, practicing calligraphy, reading, or doing other things that can make you calm down. The most important thing is to make sure you eat well, have a balanced diet, buy groceries yourself, and learn to cook some dishes. Ensure the quality of your sleep, do not indulge yourself just because there are no restrictions, and never stay up late or pull an all-nighter. It is best to maintain the same state as when you are with your family or at school, to live a disciplined life, rather than resting whimsically for a week and then trying hard for two or three days. I hope you can find joy in living alone at home, and I hope you can have a happy and fulfilling time during this period. Best wishes.

question: I am homosexual and want to come out to my family, but I am afraid. I feel very repressed. What should I do?
description: It was okay before I realized I was gay. Suddenly one day, I discovered that I am gay and I also have feelings for a girl. I want to come out to my family, but they have more traditional and conservative beliefs, so they may not accept it. I am starting to feel anxious now. I have trouble sleeping, and I am losing a lot of hair. I also have difficulty controlling my temper. I get angry every day and often feel chest tightness and unexplained fear. I frequently start crying for no reason. I thought it was a physical problem, but I have been checked many times and nothing is wrong. Now, what should I do...
keywords: Emotions, depressed emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods.

answers.answer_text: Hug the topic owner. In your description, I can see your worries and anxiety about this matter. Having feelings for someone and exploring your own sexual orientation should actually be a happy thing. However, because your parents are more traditional and the current situation of same-sex relationships in society is not that optimistic, it is understandable that you have such concerns and anxiety. Moreover, parents' opinions and thoughts are very important to everyone. Especially when it comes to love and choosing a future partner, these "life-changing events". If you can gain their understanding and blessings, it will definitely make your future life much easier. From your description, there isn't much information about it. I don't know if you have tried to communicate with them and what their feedback was. I also don't know if you are still in school or already working. Could it be that your parents' disagreement is because they are worried that such a relationship, which may not be widely accepted by society, would make your future life difficult? Regardless of how old your child is, parents may always feel that they need to be taken care of. And for parents who are more traditional, they may feel that for girls, marrying a suitable person of the opposite sex is a "normal" way to improve their lives. If you are already an adult and have the ability and right to decide what kind of partner you want and what kind of life you want, it is just that liking the same sex is completely different from the cognitive of traditional parents, so accepting it may be more difficult for them. It might be better to slowly let them know that liking someone can actually be independent of gender, and let them gradually understand that liking the same sex is not a strange thing. At the same time, work hard and manage your own life well, let your parents see that you are already an adult and can take care of your own life, and let them feel that you have the ability to handle the things you will face in the future, as well as the pressure you may encounter in society. I believe that parents definitely hope that their children can live a better and easier life, which is why they want to demand it in a way they consider to be right. If you can see the concerns behind your parents' disagreement, then take care of your own life first, and then patiently communicate with them. The result will definitely change. If what they see is that you have been anxious and unhappy because of this matter, they may become even more determined that their ideas are right. Coming out of the closet is really a patient process. To make parents change their ideas and beliefs that they have firmly believed in for decades is even more difficult. Therefore, take care of your own life first. Also give yourself some time to clarify your thoughts, think about what your parents' agreement and approval mean to you, and how important they are. Then, with your determination and efforts, show your parents your growth and determination. I believe that the situation will definitely improve.

Hello, I completely understand your current feelings of helplessness. You have met someone you like, but your shared gender is hindering your relationship from progressing. However, the issue of being of the same gender is no longer a problem in today's society, which is increasingly accepting of same-sex relationships. Therefore, this shouldn't be causing you such distress. The biggest problem is that your family may not accept you for being your true self. Sexual orientation is something innate and cannot be changed. Although your family holds traditional beliefs, it is not impossible for their mindset to change. You are caught between love and family, and the internal conflict is causing you anxiety, which is manifesting in physical symptoms. Your body is already warning you. It requires you to make a decision as soon as possible. Being anxious about the problem alone is not very meaningful; what we need to do is to contemplate how to solve it. Let's clarify your goal first -- you have found love and your goal is to obtain love. Your family is the obstacle you encountered, and it is the problem you need to address. If you are willing to disregard everything for love, then naturally you won't need to consider these problems and can bravely be yourself. However, you have been influenced by your family's traditional and ingrained thinking since childhood, and this thinking is somewhat restraining you, making it difficult for you to muster the courage. When you mentioned "not daring," I knew it was the result of your family's ongoing suppression, which I truly sympathize with. I think what you should consider is not your family, but your own life. Are you willing to sacrifice your entire life for your family? This might be a choice because there are already many people who sacrifice themselves out of fear. If you want to have love, if you want to have the life you desire, then you must stand up for yourself! Ask yourself -- what do I truly want? Uphold family traditions? Or the life I want? This decision belongs to your own life. If you want love, then you cannot avoid confronting your family. I hope you can come up with clever methods to persuade your family. If you want your family, then upholding the family legacy will become your mission. May your family be worthy of your sacrifices and everything you give. Best wishes.

Hello, OP~ ※ From OP's description, I understand that after realizing being homosexual, they really want to come out, but because their family has a more conservative traditional mindset and cannot accept it, they are now becoming restless, experiencing insomnia, hair loss in large amounts, and losing control of their temper. They get angry every day, often experience chest tightness and inexplicable fear, and often start crying for no reason. OP's condition should be caused by psychological reasons. They want to come out but are afraid that their family will not agree. This conflicting feeling has resulted in a psychological imbalance, leading to physical reactions. In contemporary society, although homosexuality is gradually being accepted by others, this group of people is mainly concentrated among young people. For the older generation, homosexuality is still unacceptable. However, everyone's sexual orientation is difficult to change. This is your only life, and how you balance this issue may determine your future direction. The best method, of course, is to communicate with your family and try to gain their understanding. But if you are extremely sure that your family will not accept it, you can choose to deceive them indirectly. However, this lie may require a great deal of effort to make up for, or it may likely be uncovered. Some people are born with unique existences, and such people are often not understood by others. Perhaps you are one of them! Although we want to be obedient children, sometimes there may be conflicting beliefs between insisting on oneself and being filial to parents. At this time, the best choice is to make the most comfortable choice for yourself! Respect your own heart and don't let yourself continue to be in an unhappy situation! Good luck!

question: Studying abroad, always feeling like having few friends and feeling lonely, what should I do?
description: I am a international student studying abroad, and maybe there were some issues with my social interactions before, so I feel that there aren't many people I can hang out with and go out together, maybe just one or two. So I often use social networking apps to meet new people, but most of them are just one-time encounters and not long-lasting. And recently, the pandemic has worsened, and I have to stay indoors. I live alone, so the feeling of loneliness becomes even stronger. When I see others posting on social media, like having friends over for dinner or going on trips, I feel really envious. I start wondering why no one invites me, why do I have to actively ask others to do things with me. Sometimes, I just feel tired, lost, and I don't have many channels to make friends... I read some advice telling me to find something I enjoy doing, but even when I do, these problems still come to mind and it's really frustrating. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello there, classmate. Regardless of which stage of life we are in, we must face and understand the meaning of "loneliness" as a topic for personal growth. Loneliness is not entirely negative or scary. When we no longer reject or fear it, and choose to enjoy loneliness, it can bring surprises. It may help us see ourselves more clearly, or inspire creativity, or make it easier to understand the lessons of growth. Furthermore, the existence of loneliness does not disappear just because we have friends. I hope you understand that. "I am an international student studying abroad. It may be that there were some issues with my socializing methods before, and I feel that there aren't many people I can meet up with and hang out together, maybe one or two at most." What I am even more curious about is what you mean by "issues with socializing methods". In fact, maintaining interpersonal relationships can sometimes be simple and sometimes complex. It depends not only on whether personalities, upbringing, and values align, but also on whether both parties have the same level of commitment to maintaining the relationship and whether they can accept the costs of maintaining it. In terms of your circle of international students, most cities have channels for Chinese students to meet and organize gatherings and activities. So, if you really want to have friends, you can also proactively make friends through these channels. You have one or two companions, but no one to share your innermost thoughts with. I suggest you think about what is preventing you from establishing deeper connections with others. "So I often use social networking apps to meet new people, but most of the time, it's just one-time encounters, and it's not long-lasting. And recently, the pandemic has worsened, and I have to stay in my room. I live alone, so the feeling of loneliness has become even stronger. When I see others posting on their social media, hanging out with their friends or going on trips, I feel envious and wonder why no one invites me or why I have to ask around to find someone to do something together. Sometimes I feel tired and lost, and I don't have many avenues to make friends." The reason why the people you meet through social networking apps are not long-lasting is because neither party has the intention to continue the relationship. In other words, your desire for friends may not be as strong and urgent as you imagine. This is something you need to think about. You envy the friendships of others and want to passively receive the kindness of friends. But have you realized that every relationship requires effort and maintenance? When you see others with companionship, it's because both parties have sacrificed their own boundaries to maintain that relationship. Perhaps they have sacrificed their time, energy, or money. If these sacrifices are inevitable in any interpersonal relationship, would you still choose to make friends? You can ask yourself that question. You mentioned that you need someone to accompany you in doing things, but you should also recognize your own abilities. In life, 90% of things can be done independently, and in case it's not possible, businesses now have amazing customer service. Many needs can be met just by speaking up, and there are plenty of people who can help. Of course, what I want to express is not a rejection of making friends but to tell you that you have great potential within yourself and there is plenty of support in society. You don't have to be overly anxious just because you don't have friends and let it affect your self-worth. Interpersonal relationships are indeed important, but they are not the most important thing. Having companionship can enhance happiness, but every thing has its pros and cons. Maintaining relationships comes with its own troubles, and so does loneliness. It's hard to say which is better. Which one do you think is better? "I see suggestions about finding things I enjoy doing, but even when I do those things, I still think about these problems and it bothers me. What should I do?" You have things you enjoy doing, but even when you do them, you are not fully focused because you are bothered by "not having friends". What is the root cause of this bother? Is it because I don't have friends, so I am not as good as others? Or is it that I don't have friends, so it must be my own fault, and I am just incompetent? Do you truly want friends, or do you simply not want to face life's challenges alone? I hope you can think it through. Loneliness is a constant in everyone's life. Sometimes it's internal loneliness, sometimes it's a lack of people around us. Acknowledging it is the first step, and embracing rather than fighting it is the second step. By embracing loneliness, we can receive its gifts and feel more fulfilled internally. Keep going! Best wishes~.

Hello~ Haruki Murakami said, "No one likes loneliness, they just don't make friends easily. That's how it ends up being disappointing." Loneliness is something that everyone has to face--yes, everyone! Writer Qijinnian said, "Perhaps a person needs to go a long way and experience countless sudden prosperity and desolation in life to become mature." First, we need to realize that loneliness doesn't only happen to us, it often appears and it's not scary. Love and loneliness are actually the same emotion, they go hand in hand and cannot be separated. The more we feel lonely, the stronger our desire for love becomes. So, when we feel lonely, it may be because we haven't temporarily felt loved by someone, or there's no one to love. Establishing some good social relationships can greatly alleviate your sense of loneliness. People often regard "socializing" as a skill but overlook the fact that "being alone" is also a skill, and in a certain sense, it is even more important than socializing. If being unable to socialize well is a weakness in character, then not being able to tolerate loneliness is simply a deficiency in the soul. Don't reject it, instead, focus on managing your own life and interpersonal relationships well, and loneliness will quietly go away. Best wishes~.

Hello, I understand how you feel being abroad with no close relatives. Here's a warm hug for you. Being abroad is different from being in your home country. In your home country, you have familiar places, familiar family and friends, but when you go abroad, many people need to readjust. Firstly, analyze the situation - there may have been some issues with your social interactions before, feeling that there aren't many people to meet up and hang out with, maybe only one or two. I wonder what issues you have encountered in your social interactions? Have you analyzed and reflected on them? In my opinion, it's not about having many friends, having one true friend is enough! It's not about quantity, but about usefulness, trustworthiness, and being able to confide in each other. The pandemic has worsened, we can only stay indoors. I still live alone, so that feeling of loneliness becomes even stronger. However, there's actually nothing serious about feeling lonely. Heidegger once said, "Man exists in the world, and exists alone. Our existence is our own business, no one can replace us, no one can live our lives for us, and no one can face death on our behalf. Each person's existence is unique." Therefore, don't feel lonely. Loneliness is also a form of growth. When faced with loneliness in life, it provides you an opportunity to make choices, allows you to balance and adjust, and makes you feel at ease in life, just like a fish in water. It's a self-reliant and independent attitude towards life, which makes you realize what you truly need and don't need, and focus on life and work, elevating yourself. Some people live a fulfilling life, and it can be equally exciting. Why no one invites me, and why do I have to ask around to find someone to accompany me when I want to do something? In fact, friendships are similar to relationships, they require mutual effort. Some friends are naturally more passive, so it's okay for us to take the initiative. Here are a few suggestions: Understand loneliness correctly and enrich yourself. Don't think that being alone means feeling lonely. Choose a lifestyle that suits you and live a clear and fulfilled life, then it will be exciting. Find the reason. You often mention that it's difficult to make friends. Have you thought about the reasons behind that? Reflect on them, find the reasons, and then find ways to overcome them. Actively participate in social activities. If there aren't many opportunities to make friends, you can actively participate in social activities. There must be events at school, so join in actively and give yourself a chance to make friends. Set a plan and find your own value. Set a daily plan, read a certain number of pages, learn a certain number of words, exercise for a certain amount of time, try cooking new dishes, learn new skills, and find your own value. It will help you understand yourself better and strengthen your self-identity.

Hello: Well, the pandemic does have a big impact on people's lives, not just you, but everyone in the country is facing these trends. Another thing is that the online circle makes things easier, while the real-life circle becomes smaller. Everyone has a defensive mindset and it's hard to fully trust others. So it's difficult to maintain long-term relationships. However, it still depends on your own judgment. If you truly feel that a friend is worth having, then you should invest more time and effort into getting to know them, just be cautious with financial transactions and ensure your safety. Now let's analyze the problem: 1. You are an international student studying abroad, and maybe there were some issues with your previous social interactions, finding people to hang out with and go out with wasn't easy, maybe just one or two people. (Being an international student is not easy, being alone in a foreign country can be very lonely. It would be great to have one or two friends to connect with, it's about quality, not quantity. A social app is just one way to socialize, it's not a big deal, just be mindful of your safety.) 2. So you often use social apps to meet new people, but most of the connections are short-lived. And lately, with the pandemic getting worse, you have to stay inside, and since you live alone, the feeling of loneliness is even stronger. (If social apps can bring you temporary happiness with friends, that's fine, but it depends on what you really want. If you want long-term friendships, social apps may not be reliable, it's not that people are unreliable, it's that their mentality is not reliable, no one is interested in long-term connections, everyone is guarded. The pandemic is affecting not only overseas but also in the country, during this time when you can't go out and hang out, you can still engage in online activities and personal hobbies. For example, some people draw, cook, play musical instruments, read books in certain areas. Many people are learning new skills during this period. For example, I am learning financial management skills, which brings me happiness and enjoyment.) 3. When you see others posting on Moments, one friend comes over for dinner, another goes on a trip, you feel envious and wonder why no one invites you and why you need to actively ask people to hang out. (As long as you want, it's possible, so there's nothing to be upset about, right? If they don't invite you, don't you also not invite them? Some people enjoy being alone, while others enjoy being with a group. If you really like having company, then invite others, I believe you can find someone to hang out with. Yes, if you don't ask, others won't know that you have a need.) 4. Sometimes you feel exhausted, lost, and don't have many channels to make new friends... You read some suggestions that you should engage in activities you enjoy, but even when you do them, you still think about these problems and it bothers you. What should you do? (Well, it's natural to feel tired because you're trying to compete with yourself... If you still think about these things while doing activities, it means you don't really like them, you're just pretending. Of course, you won't enjoy it. Don't be upset, it's totally normal. Once you find something you truly enjoy, you won't feel bothered. Immersing yourself in an activity is a process. Some people like doing things with a group, while others prefer doing things alone. Just do what you prefer. If you really don't want to, then it's just a battle with yourself, not any other problem.) Conclusion: Wishing you happiness and joy! May you understand yourself sooner! If you have any confusion, feel free to private message me!

Hello, dear. Living abroad and being far away from family and old friends, it's natural to feel lonely when living alone. I completely understand your feelings. Loneliness is a problem that everyone faces. You mentioned being envious of others' posts on social media, envying others being invited by friends, and envying others traveling. But in reality, these are just the good moments that everyone likes to show. When you can't see them, others also have moments of loneliness. Loneliness is a very normal emotion. Learning to accept it, everyone will experience loneliness. No one can always live in a lively environment. The key is how we view loneliness with the right mindset. Learn to accept it, adapt to being alone, without the disturbance of others, and enjoy the process of solitude. Be proactive. Friendship requires effort and maintenance. You mentioned trying to meet people through social media, but they don't last. Have you thought about the reasons why these relationships end after just one meeting, and how to maintain friendships? Continuously analyze and summarize. Take the initiative to meet people with similar interests, integrate into certain social circles, and stay active and positive. Be proactive in interacting with others. While accepting the goodwill of others, also understand the importance of giving. You don't need a lot of friends, but you should treat each one seriously. Change your perspective on loneliness and let it flow naturally. Is life lonelier when living alone or in a bustling crowd? What is the definition of loneliness? Is it just having someone around or someone who understands you? Thoreau wrote in "Walden": "I found that to be alone was still more wearisome than to be in company, for conversation. I love to be alone, I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude." So what is loneliness? As we experience more in life, our mindset will change. Don't actively seek friends, live your own life well, and let things happen naturally. I wish you well.

Hello, OP. Sending you a big hug. After reading your description, I can feel your helplessness and loneliness. Studying abroad is not an easy task. But remember, we are born to be alone, and we must face loneliness with courage and find ways to overcome it. In a foreign country, to have true friends, we can be more proactive. It's okay to ask for help and don't always feel burdened. Ask more questions, seek help occasionally, and respond with a small gesture of gratitude. This will make people think highly of you and be willing to socialize. It's best to expand your social circle and once you have made friends, put effort into maintaining those relationships, reciprocate kindness, and help each other. You can also read some books on socializing to learn and make progress more efficiently. Wishing you happiness and joy!

Hello, it's nice to "meet" you here. Your friend Qi Qi is here to greet you 🤗. I hope to provide you with help through words: I believe you have heard of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs. Maslow believes that human needs consist of five levels: physiological needs, safety needs, love and belonging needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs. Love and belonging needs refer to the emotional connections and relationships people establish with others. We need to make friends and pursue love. When this need is not fulfilled, it can make us feel lonely and isolated. Especially for you, who are studying abroad, it must be difficult without familiar people and things around you. Also, for various reasons, our social interactions may not be going smoothly, and it must be tough for you. 🤗 Here's a virtual hug for you. Know that we are here for you, we are your friends who love you. In fact, loneliness is also a path to maturity. During the process of being alone, we can try to reduce restlessness. Just as Feng Zikai said: "Do not be disturbed by emotions, do not fear the future, do not dwell in the past, so be it." What we really need to do is to truly understand ourselves. But that doesn't mean we should avoid socializing. As you mentioned, you've met some people through social apps, but most of them were short-lived and not lasting. I wonder if you've encountered any problems in offline socializing. We can socialize partially online and partially offline. But what's more important is being sincere in our interactions with others, and constantly enriching ourselves based on their interests. Because people are usually attracted to each other due to similarities, interesting qualities, or mutual benefits. Either we have similar hobbies and interests with others, or we are "useful" to them, they can see something novel or learn something from us. To achieve this, we need to improve ourselves and become more interesting. And what we need is initiative. Write a letter or send a message to friends you haven't talked to in a long time, call some relatives, invite colleagues for a cup of coffee, or participate in activities you usually don't dare or feel too lazy to join. Instead of relying on others' advice, it's better to take action and practice it yourself. So go ahead and face your fears and do what you want. I believe that with your genuine and sincere efforts, you will find the people who can accompany you, bring you joy, and travel with you. Wishing you a happy life!

Hey dear, have you ever asked yourself why you are so eager to connect with others? Why are you so afraid of being alone? Is it because you think everyone else has a group, and you're afraid of being abandoned or not liked? We crave connection with others, we fear loneliness because maybe we don't have a stable long-term relationship. In such a stable relationship, we don't have to fear being abandoned, worry about not being liked, or be afraid of doing something wrong. It is precisely because we lack this stable connection that we try to compensate with many shallow relationships, just like what you described: "often using social networking apps to meet people, but most of them end after one meeting." Actually, building relationships and intimacy takes courage and requires self-exposure. In this process, we may also fear not being accepted and getting hurt. Are you willing to take the risk of being hurt? If you find a long-lasting and stable relationship, congratulations, you are lucky. When a person is loved, they don't care about others' opinions and don't feel lonely. Just like a couple in love, they can openly kiss on the street without any worries. To break free from this feeling of loneliness, you can try to take the initiative and seek out potential connections. At the same time, try to maintain a relatively long-term and stable relationship with them. Meanwhile, be mentally prepared that: 1. In this relationship, I might get hurt. 2. In this relationship, I might be abandoned. 3. But for this intimate relationship, I am willing to take these risks. If you are ready, take action!

Hello, the main problem you are currently facing is feeling lonely because you think you have few friends. To make new friends, you need to spend more time socializing and treating people kindly. If you are a student, try sitting at a table with other people instead of alone. You might want to be friends with popular people, but true friends are rare and can last a lifetime. Sometimes, even popular people can become your friends once they get to know you. Joining organizations or clubs with shared interests is also a great way to meet new people. Social networking sites like Facebook, Weibo, and WeChat can also help you make new friends. When talking to strangers, you can ask if they have a Facebook account or what their username is on Weibo. Temples and churches are also great places to meet new friends since you share the same religious beliefs. Joining sports clubs is another option, as not all sports are competitive, and supporting your teammates can help you make friends. If you play a musical instrument or enjoy singing, joining a band or choir is also a good idea. Volunteering can also help you meet people from different age groups and find like-minded individuals. When participating in social activities like joining clubs, going to church, or attending school, take the initiative to initiate conversations. However, if you don't speak up, you won't make friends. Don't be picky and try to talk to anyone. Even a brief chat with someone can lead to a lifelong friendship. Smile more and make eye contact, as your body language can affect how approachable you appear to others. Don't be detached, frown, or have a vacant gaze. Stand in the corner with crossed arms. Your body language sends signals that you don't want to talk to others. Initiative is essential, and casual topics like weather, asking for help, or compliments can help you start conversations. Pay attention to the 30-70 rule, speaking 30% of the time and listening 70% of the time. Remember to leave your name after a conversation ends. You can simply say, "By the way, my name is..." Usually, if you introduce yourself, the other person will also introduce themselves. Remembering people's names and previous conversations shows that you are attentive, and people will be more willing to befriend you. Creating opportunities for future meetings is also important. Even if you have a deep conversation, one interaction is not enough to become friends. Therefore, actively suggest future activities or events. If you find common interests, ask if they are part of any related organizations or clubs. If they are, ask how to join, as this is a great opportunity to make more friends. If you manage a club, church, or have a band, and you find someone suitable, you can also leave your phone number or email address and invite them to join. Inviting someone to lunch or afternoon tea allows for more time to get to know each other. Say something like, "Hey, I have to go, but let's exchange phone numbers/email addresses and find a time to have lunch or tea together." Even if the other person doesn't leave their contact information, at least you have created an opportunity for them to contact you. Leaving your contact information with potential friends can lead to unexpected results. Don't force someone to be your friend just because they didn't invite you to a party. Don't repeatedly call them or visit them frequently. Don't overstay your welcome. Developing a friendship takes time and shouldn't be rushed. If you are unsure about the stage of your friendship, you can ask the person directly. Pushing for a friendship too quickly or demanding too much can make people feel overwhelmed and push them away. Cherish those friends who bring positive energy into your life and strive to bring positive energy to others. Show your unique and outstanding qualities. Are you humorous? If yes, congratulations. Funny people can create a relaxed and enjoyable atmosphere for conversations, and people enjoy being around positive individuals. If your sense of humor is dark, it's best to let people know in advance that you enjoy joking, so as not to cause any discomfort. People may also be interested in you because of your uniqueness, so don't be afraid to show it! In addition to making friends, there are many other ways to reduce loneliness. The best way is to focus on self-improvement. Engage in activities you enjoy, such as exercise, writing, playing a musical instrument, and so on. By pursuing your passions, you'll enhance your skills and encounter more like-minded friends. Finally, I wish you all the best in life, and may your future be bright!

question: How to regulate being easily influenced by people and things from the outside and affecting emotions?
description: I am especially sensitive, and I tend to overthink and become immersed in words spoken by those around me, as well as books, movies, and music that I have encountered. How can I regulate myself in such a state?
keywords: Growth, perfecting personality, personality traits, self-development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! After reading your description, I have gained some understanding of the question you want to ask, and I would like to give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can tell that you are someone who is easily influenced by your environment and others. You tend to overthink and get stuck in a loop due to offhand remarks made by others. It is normal to care about how others perceive us because most of us want to present ourselves in a positive light. However, it is important to find a balance. Excessive concern about others' opinions can have negative effects on your mental and emotional well-being. In most cases, being overly concerned about what others think is a manifestation of lack of self-confidence and insecurity. Therefore, I have summarized some methods to help you alleviate the current situation: (1) Learn to shift your focus by developing your interests, engaging in physical activities, or reading books, among other things. (2) Confide in close friends or family members who you have a good relationship with and express your concerns, which can help you release your emotions. (3) Try to reasonably filter out opinions that do not align with your own. For opinions that are useful to you, consider making changes, but do not put too much pressure on yourself during this process. (4) Objectively recognize your strengths and weaknesses. Embrace your strengths and develop plans to improve on your weaknesses, as nobody is perfect in this world. (5) Practice positive self-affirmation, and try to approach situations with a positive and optimistic mindset. (6) Accumulate knowledge and experience to enhance your reservoir of knowledge. This way, the degree to which others can influence you will greatly decrease. (7) Establish boundaries between yourself and others. When someone's emotions affect you, remind yourself that it is their emotions, and while you can offer help and comfort, resolving their emotions primarily depends on them. You are not responsible for other people's emotions. When we can distinguish between our own emotions and those of others, we can reduce unnecessary emotional exhaustion. The world and I love you. Take care and best wishes.

question: Do you have to force yourself to go to social events you don't want to go to?
description: A long time ago, I promised a not very familiar friend to go on a team-building activity. Initially, I also thought that team-building activities were too frequent, but I agreed in order to appear active. At the time, I didn't mention the details of the activity and the specific date. Later on, when I found out about the time and content, I didn't really want to go anymore. I feel awkward because I'm not close to them, and even after the team-building, we won't become much closer. Also, it's right after the Singles' Day sales and I don't have much money left. If I don't go last minute, will I be seen as unsociable? This team-building activity doesn't seem to have any specific requirements or tasks. Should I still go?

answers.answer_text: Let's talk while sorting things out: Your demand: You don't want to go. But you already agreed to the other party. No matter what your reason is, the point is that you agreed. This is the current situation. Of course, now you can choose not to go, but the cost may be that the other party may not invite you to similar activities in the future. If you want to participate in the future, you will need to actively ask the other party. Looking at it from a different perspective, if you go, what you can experience is completely unknown, but of course, you will have to pay and exert effort. Secondly, you may be able to sustain this circle, and then you can participate in corresponding activities in the future. So the choice has always been in your hands, it depends on how you choose. Whether you go or not, you still have a way to maintain this relationship.

question: Since I was very young, I have always wished for my mother to become pregnant... Is this a sickness?
description: I probably had such thoughts when I was in third or fourth grade, and I still have them now. I want to have a baby with my mom through AI... I don't know if anyone else has such thoughts, or if it's just me being ill.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello there~ In psychoanalysis, there is a very important concept called the Oedipus complex, also known as the love for the mother. It originates from the Greek mythological character Oedipus, who accidentally killed his father and married his mother. Your current psychological state can be explained using this story. The Oedipus complex originally refers to the mixed emotions of a boy's affection for his mother and resentment towards his father. According to the ancient Greek myth, Prince Oedipus unintentionally killed his biological father and married his mother due to a prophecy. Freud used this to illustrate the characteristics of children's sexual psychology. He believed that during the phallic stage (around 3-5 years old), boys develop feelings of love for their mother and jealousy towards their father, as they subconsciously desire to replace their father and have exclusive love from their mother. However, because the father is more powerful and stronger than the child, the child tends to identify with the father and imitate his behavior and attitude. This impulse may still arise during adolescence, and it is only resolved when the individual finds a sexual partner. Freud believed that boys have a fear of castration from their fathers, which gradually eliminates the Oedipus complex. For girls, the development of the Electra complex signifies a shift of love objects from the mother to the father, and this complex reaches its peak when girls become aware of their lack of a "phallus". If not resolved effectively, this complex can become the root of future neuroses. The essence of the Oedipus complex is not actual matricide and patricide, but rather similarity and complementarity. Taking boys as an example, they are of the same sex as their fathers, so they are similar; similarity leads to identification, and boys look up to their fathers as role models and adopt their psychological traits and qualities as part of their own. Boys are of the opposite sex as their mothers, which allows them to complement each other, rely on each other, and this is what love is. Therefore, boys form the most fundamental interpersonal relationship with their parents, which can be summarized as love for the mother and imitation of the father. Love for the mother and imitation of the father often mutually reinforce each other. When the father loves the mother, boys imitate the father, and they will love the mother even more. When the mother loves the father, boys must become more like the father in order to win the mother's affection. Freud believed that "children often take their mothers or fathers as their sexual objects, and fathers love their daughters more than their sons, while mothers love their sons more than their daughters. Children respond accordingly, sons wanting to occupy the father's position, and daughters wanting to occupy the mother's position. The pleasure derived from these parent-child relationships and the relationships between children also carry a sense of both tenderness and hostility." If you are experiencing this situation, it may be because the Oedipus complex has not been resolved. You can read some relevant books to understand this complex, or you can consult a professional psychoanalytic counselor who can help you change your feelings towards your mother and transfer this emotional attachment to other females. This is my analysis and suggestion, hope it helps you! Best wishes!

question: A 15-year-old girl, her learning ability has deteriorated, and she is on the verge of a breakdown. What should she do?
description: At fifteen years old, female, I did well in my studies in the first year of junior high school, but in the second year, I clearly couldn't keep up. I can understand the lessons, and I am diligently memorizing and answering questions, but I make a lot of mistakes, and my accuracy is not even half of what it was in the first year. My friends and teachers say that I am a good student, I read as many books as them, and I do as many exercises as them, but there is still such a big difference. I'm about to break down, it's like my brain has stopped working, I can't think anymore, and everything feels like I only understand the superficial meaning.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner. Through your words, I can sense your anxiety, helplessness, confusion, and stress. I want to give you a big hug, as it's not easy. If you didn't have any difficulties in your previous studies, and there were no obvious problems with your study methods or diligence, but your grades have significantly declined, it is possible that your psychological motivation is the issue. It seems like we are studying very hard and seriously, but our study efficiency is actually very poor. This is because our psychological motivation is not focused on studying. Perhaps your subconscious is resisting studying, or maybe your subconscious is focused on other things. You need to reflect and become aware of what has happened. You can also find a counselor to chat with. They can help you understand your confusion and overcome your difficulties with their expertise. Lastly, studying is your own business. You should sincerely give as much effort as you can, and only expect to harvest according to your own abilities, rather than comparing yourself to others in terms of how many books you've read or how many questions you've done. Everyone has their own pace of learning. Just follow your own rhythm. If you do your best, then that's enough!

question: I am a male, 18 years old this year, and I want to commit suicide. I'm sorry, parents.
description: I am a boy, I am 18 years old this year, and I don't want to grow up. I broke up with my online girlfriend yesterday and I feel very sad o(╥﹏╥)o. I have been having insomnia every day and can't stop overthinking. I don't like myself at all. I really have no hope in life. I miss my grandmother and want to be with her. I really want her, I want to know how to let my parents know that I am not suicidal but just feeling helpless. My heart hurts so much, I just don't want to make my parents sad. I want to commit suicide before I become an adult. It's all my fault, I'm sorry parents, I'm not filial!

answers.answer_text: Hello, you just broke up yesterday and now you're feeling very sad. This is a normal reaction. However, you have to know that this state won't last forever. I have encountered many people who have gone through a breakup, and in the initial stages, they might feel just like you, sad and even contemplating suicide, thinking that they will never love again, and exhibiting all kinds of extreme reactions. But the majority of them eventually manage to adjust and their intense emotions gradually subside. Especially after a long period of time, when they have their own new lives and even new partners, when they look back on the time of the breakup, everything seems light and insignificant. They will be grateful for their perseverance at that time. I believe you will also be the same. Don't rush, give yourself some time. Allow yourself to feel sad. When you feel uncomfortable, cry, talk about it, write it down, or even shout it out, but do not give up on yourself in a moment of impulsiveness. You miss your grandmother a lot, but have you ever thought that if there really is heaven after death, would your grandmother want you to join her there? No, she would silently bless you and hope that you live a good and happy life. Living well should be the greatest filial piety to your grandmother. You have mentioned a few times about being sorry to your parents. Is it possible not to hurt them? I believe the greatest pain in the world is when white-haired parents bury their black-haired children, their hard-earned children who lose their lives in the prime of youth. Such a blow is truly cruel. So, if you feel sorry, then live well. I believe that in the future, you will still meet someone you love, someone who loves you. You will have your own career, your own family, and your own wonderful life. Don't just give up on yourself like this, okay? Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Is constantly wanting to check many things a compulsion? What should I do?
description: I always have the tendency to check many things. (It has always been there, but recently it seems a bit worse.) For example, the water faucet, the arrangement of books, shoes, gas valves... I often check several times, until I can imagine a visual of it being done and forcefully convince myself not to check anymore and tell myself that it's already okay, only then do I stop. Is this OCD, and what should I do?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling

answers.answer_text: Hello there, first of all, I want to give you a warm hug. It must be exhausting for you to constantly check things and it probably decreases your efficiency as well. I feel for you. Secondly, you mentioned that you always want to check many things (it has always been there but recently seems to have gotten worse). For example, taps, the arrangement of books, shoes, gas valves...you often check multiple times. Have you ever thought about what repetitive checking means to you? When did this start happening and why has it become worse recently? What does repetitive checking represent? Have you explored this part of yourself? As for solving the problem: 1. From your description, it seems that you already have a relatively suitable method for yourself. I wonder if you have noticed it yourself. You mentioned imagining a "checked" symbol and forcibly stopping yourself from checking and telling yourself it's already okay. Try slowing down the process when you become aware of the urge to repeat the checking, reflect on what you are currently doing and the purpose behind it, and gradually reach a point where checking once is enough. This might help reduce the need for repetitive checking. 2. Your description didn't mention the impact that repetitive checking has on yourself. If you don't see it as a problem, you can let it be and not put too much pressure on yourself or label yourself. It will be better to accept yourself and make changes from that place. I hope this can help you. Best wishes!

Hello. In fact, in life, most of us have some compulsive behaviors, such as worrying that the door is not closed or the lights are not turned off after going out, and we may repeat checks. As long as these compulsive behaviors are not too frequent or extreme, they are actually normal. But from your description, it seems that you have some compulsive behaviors towards many things, which may indicate mild symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD): Before talking about OCD, let's talk about compulsive phenomena first. Almost everyone may experience compulsive phenomena, such as a song constantly playing in your head or worrying if the house door is locked after going out. Children and adolescents may also experience compulsive phenomena, such as taking 1 extra step for every 4 steps when walking on the street. It can be said that everyone may have compulsive phenomena. Generally, if these compulsive phenomena are mild, short in duration, and do not cause severe anxiety or other emotional disorders, they are considered normal. OCD is a neurosis characterized by the main clinical manifestations of obsessions and compulsions. OCD is not uncommon in clinical practice. A survey in the United States showed that the prevalence rate of OCD is about 1%. In 1982, a survey was conducted in 12 regions in China, and the results showed a prevalence rate of OCD of 0.3‰. In fact, this number is much lower than the actual prevalence rate. Based on clinical practice, it is estimated that there are about 5 to 10 million people with OCD in China, with a prevalence rate of about 5‰ to 10‰. 80% of OCD cases occur before the age of 25, and it is more common in men than women. Typical symptoms of OCD include: 1) patients repeatedly thinking about certain ideas, such as doubts, memories, and worries; 2) patients repeatedly performing unnecessary behaviors, such as checking, washing hands, counting, and ritualistic actions. Obsession and anxiety are like twins, OCD patients often have obvious symptoms of anxiety. The symptoms of OCD generally have the following characteristics: 1. The patient is aware that the OCD symptoms are irrational but cannot control them. If they do not do them, they will experience severe anxiety symptoms such as tension and palpitations. In order to avoid anxiety, patients can only keep thinking and doing them. This feature is called conscious self-compulsion and counter-compulsion. 2. Patients can realize that the conscious thoughts and impulses of these compulsions come from themselves, not from the external world, and are their own thoughts. I suggest you consider going to a relevant hospital for examination and listen to the diagnosis of a professional doctor.

Hello dear, sending you hugs~ Based on your descriptions, your state seems to resemble the symptoms of OCD. However, from my experience, I have friends around me who exhibit similar behaviors, or even worse, but they are okay with it and it does not greatly affect their lives. Hopefully, you don't worry too much about your condition. Based on your description of "it's always been there, but recently it seems a bit worse," since you've been able to deal with these symptoms before, it might be a good idea to seek help from a mental health professional to rule out other possible psychological disorders and give yourself some peace of mind. I once had a friend who had severe OCD during her senior year, where no one could touch her desk, and she had to thoroughly wash her chopsticks before eating in the cafeteria. She would be the last one to leave the classroom because she had to double-check if she brought all the important materials home. She also had severe compulsions for cleanliness. However, she enjoyed it and didn't care what others thought. She calmly completed each task meticulously. I once gave advice to another individual with OCD and suggested taking photos of the things they had checked with their phone, so they could look at the photos when they remembered it again. You could try this method too, since we always have our phones with us and it's convenient to take a quick look.

OP, from your description, it seems that you often have the urge to check many things, and recently the frequency of checking seems to have increased. And then you have to force yourself not to check in order to stop. It appears to be some obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors. How do you view the current situation yourself? Do you think it's manageable or unbearable? Has this phenomenon had any impact on you, in reality or mentally? Has anything happened recently that has increased these checking behaviors? What are you worried about? Usually, people with compulsive behaviors tend to be more serious and strive for perfection, like Sheldon in "The Big Bang Theory." If it is affecting your life, such as work or study efficiency, interpersonal relationships, and causing you distress, you can visit the psychiatric department of a hospital to have a doctor evaluate and diagnose you. For OCD, you can learn about Morita Therapy by Dr. Shoma Morita. The core concept of the therapy is to go with the flow and do what needs to be done. You can take a look at "The Way of Self-Acceptance and Realization" and other works on Morita Therapy to understand the nature of OCD. You can also seek counseling with a therapist, and I believe they will be able to assist you. Wishing you well.

question: I have liked a boy for six years, but we have never been together. I don't understand my own feelings.
description: I have liked a boy for six years, but we are not together. This year, I met another boy and I don't know why, but I just want to look at him all the time. Even though I think he looks average, I don't understand why I want to see him. I get really nervous when I pass by him, and he seems very gentle. I like it when he smiles. But his behavior is very much like the sea king. I kind of want to be with him, but I really don't understand my own heart. I clearly like the boy I have liked for six years more.

answers.answer_text: Title holder, hello, sending you a hug~ After reading your description, it seems that you're not clear about your feelings and have put yourself in a dilemma. I genuinely sympathize with your situation. According to your description, you have liked a boy for six years, but you are not together. Now you have met someone else, and you feel that you care about him, but you can't really explain why you like him. Perhaps, when you start to like someone else, there is a feeling of betraying your previous feelings. In essence, it is not a betrayal. The six years of liking someone made you remember more of your own efforts rather than the other person. When we feel that we like someone, without communication, it is mostly based on our own imagined filters. So if you want to fully understand the other person, it is important to actually interact with them.

question: Can expressing love through sexual intimacy be a way to fulfill sexual needs?
description: Feeling satisfied with sexual needs, there is an element of love in sex, just like satisfying the needs of eating and drinking. From this perspective, it is a form of care. However, if satisfying sexual needs and expressing love through sex can also create a sense of confusion.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm glad to discuss the topic of sex and love with you. I believe that as someone who has thought about this topic, you must understand the importance of sex in romantic relationships. This is a great progress. So, I would like to share my understanding with you. "Sexual needs are inherent basic needs for everyone." In Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory, physiological needs serve as the foundation of the pyramid, and sexual needs are an important component of these physiological needs. Therefore, sexual needs are actually mutual states of satisfaction. In intimate relationships, sexual love is about meeting each other's inner needs, rather than one-sided satisfaction. Of course, everyone's needs may vary, with some having more needs and some having relatively fewer. Therefore, it is important for both parties to adjust and satisfy each other's needs to find a balance. Thus, mutual fulfillment of sexual needs does involve elements of care. "Subjective experience takes priority in sexual love, with appropriate attention to the partner's feelings." In your question, you mentioned feeling "confused" about expressing love through sex. What is the cause of this confusion? Is it because expressing love through sex makes you feel ashamed? Regardless of the reason, sex should be considered a right and a way to obtain inner pleasure. As we discussed earlier, sexual needs are basic needs for everyone, so sexual love should be viewed as a basic right for everyone. Therefore, caring in sexual love or satisfying sexual needs should not be done solely to please the other person, but rather as an opportunity for oneself to be the subject in sexual love and to boldly enjoy it. If we view sex as a way to satisfy and please the other person, we are actually suppressing and depriving ourselves of our sexual rights, making ourselves passive participants in sexual relationships. In the long run, this can lead to feelings of shame and discomfort. Such an attitude is extremely harmful to intimate relationships. On the surface, it may seem like we are satisfying the other person's sexual needs, but this suppression and compromise of our own feelings will gradually build up inside us and eventually cause problems in the relationship. "Become aware of the underlying intention behind the deliberate satisfaction." From what we discussed above, it seems that there is a cognitive perspective of "deliberate satisfaction" behind this type of behavior. How did this perspective develop? It may be related to the beliefs you acquired from your upbringing, but from a broader perspective, our society's past concept of "male superiority and female inferiority" seems to deliberately diminish women's feelings and rights in sex, thus making it easy for women to develop subconscious beliefs of "I should satisfy my partner more in sex". This subconscious belief can turn women into mere accessories in sexual relationships without their realizing it. This belief actually also harms men's positive experiences in sexual life, leading to a situation of "both parties suffer losses." I hope the above response is helpful to you.

Questioner, good Monday morning! It's fortunate to meet in this question. Seeing your confusion, it mainly revolves around the relationship between sex and love. I'll try to discuss it with you explicitly, hoping to provide some insight and help.

(1) Is sex equivalent to love? From Sternberg's Triangular Theory of Love, we can see that intimate relationships primarily consist of three components: passion (which leans towards what you mentioned as sex), intimacy (which focuses on mental and emotional communication), and commitment. Based on this, we can roughly conclude that your assertion that sex is equivalent to love may not be fully comprehensive, complete, or accurate. From Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, we can also see that satisfying basic physiological needs, such as eating and drinking (which is more related to physical needs), might overlap to some extent with the need for sex, but it is not entirely the same. Therefore, when it comes to the higher-level safety, belongingness, and love needs, we can observe that if the process of sex aligns with expressions of love or emotional support, then there may be some match with the third level of needs. However, if it is solely about sex without any elements of "love," then it is difficult to claim that it includes the component of "care." In conclusion, if we insist on connecting the two, it may indeed lead to the confusion you mentioned, "But if satisfying sexual needs and expressing love through sex causes a sense of disorder." Therefore, in terms of the actual question and problem, have we achieved a certain degree of consensus?

(2) What needs are not being fulfilled behind this confusion or problem? This is perhaps what I am more interested in exploring with you. Is it that in a relationship, you are not experiencing satisfaction in areas other than sex? Or is it that in the process of providing sex, you believe that as long as you give sex, it includes love, but the other person cannot recognize this? Or is it that you are independently conducting some sort of research or satisfying curiosity related to this question? These three possibilities could lead us in different directions for further discussion. In order to respect your privacy, I won't make assumptions about these possibilities. As long as you don't feel more confused, I believe it won't be a very serious problem because we are all constantly growing and updating our understanding. It's a dynamic process. If you have more confusion, I suggest starting by reading some related books, some popular ones like "Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus," "The Happiness of Marriage," or more academic ones like "Happy Together," "Intimate Relationships." There are also many resources on this topic available on various platforms. Let's learn and improve together. That's all. The world and I love you!

Hello, from your description, I can sense a feeling of contradiction and confusion. As you said, sex is a physiological need, just like eating and drinking. However, in a relationship, the need for sex goes beyond just the physical level. Sex is a part of a relationship, but it's only a part. If we want to care for someone and provide for their basic needs, such as food and drink, it can indeed be seen as a way of expressing care. But the acceptance of such care, and considering it as a form of love, is based on the emotional connection between both parties. In a relationship, sex is also a manifestation of deep connection. If one person only has a sexual need for another person, without an emotional bond, then such a relationship is actually unhealthy. In other words, in your relationship, you might ask yourself: Why do you emphasize sex so much as a way to express love? In your relationship, does the other person only have a need for sex from you? Or do you only feel the sexual aspect in your relationship? How do you define a relationship in your own heart? Besides the sexual aspect, what other aspects do you expect in your relationship? In your relationship, what other needs of the other person can you fulfill? What kind of fulfillment do you expect from the other person? Perhaps contemplating on these questions will help you clarify your relationship.

Hello! Can we use sexual intercourse as a way to fulfill our sexual needs to express love? This is a great way for lovers or partners to express themselves. Sexual intercourse is usually present in romantic relationships, which are the most intense form of interpersonal attraction and a sophisticated romantic emotion that occurs when the individual is mentally and physically mature enough to be attracted to someone of the opposite sex. The characteristics of romantic love mainly include the following aspects:

1. Romantic love generally occurs between individuals of the opposite sex and specifically refers to heterosexual love, excluding same-sex love.

2. Romantic love is an emotional experience that occurs when individuals are relatively mature in their physical and mental development.

3. Romantic love is a high-level emotion, not a low-level sentiment. It does not belong to love when emotions are purely sexual and devoid of love.

4. Romantic love has a physiological basis, including sexual factors, and is not purely a spiritual connection.

5. The basic inclination of romantic love is devotion. Therefore, it is completely reasonable to use sexual intercourse as a way to express love within a romantic relationship. It is just that in traditional culture, people are ashamed to discuss sexual culture. However, it is a normal feeling experience to feel confused about how to balance fulfilling sexual needs and expressing love. According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory, basic physiological needs include sex, and it is the pursuit of every individual to fulfill these basic physiological needs. Of course, this should be based on self-protection and not harming others, and it is acceptable to express love through sexual intercourse in a rational manner.

Sex and care are actually somewhat different. If it is just to satisfy one's sexual needs, there are many ways to do so, such as through masturbation, sex toys, a partner, or dolls, it depends on whether we are seeking the release of physiological desires or striving for mutual consent with a partner. Care generally has more emotional components, it can be said to be about concern and nurturing, and the ways of care are diverse, such as a simple embrace, an encouraging look, or doing something for each other. The confusion of the questioner is because they have taken sex as a way of care and perceive it as improper and inappropriate, thus falling into distress. In fact, it is best for sex to have emotional elements, the maintenance of a relationship and sex are definitely related, as people often say that men fall in love through sex while women fall in love and then desire sex, which does have some truth to it. Therefore, the questioner's assertion that sex and care are not in conflict is valid. For example, in our interactions with our partner, if they are tired today, we would feel sorry for them and take the initiative to cook for them or prepare a bath for them, which is an expression of care. If both parties have been busy for a while and have not had sex for a long time, and suddenly the questioner feels desire but sees that their partner is exhausted, would they disrupt their partner's rest just for their own desire? This is also an expression of love. However, if both parties are not very busy recently and both have a certain desire, this process is a pleasurable experience for both and is an expression of love, but it is not care, rather it is an indescribable feeling. Sex is a part of our life, but not everything, we need to consider each other's emotions and state, therefore, sex is just one way of expressing ourselves. Care, on the other hand, is woven into our daily lives, it can serve as a pivot, making our relationship more intimate, so strictly speaking, sex and care have a certain intersection, but they are not entirely encompassing. The world and I love you.

Hello, in the mental health domain, sex is a powerful force, especially when it is initiated by the other person's need. It can greatly score points. Like Rika in Tokyo Love Story, she starts with a kiss, which is really exciting! Just like eating and drinking, it can be appetizing when you're hungry, but overindulging can cause vomiting. There is a diminishing marginal effect, so it's important to control the frequency. Furthermore, the most important thing is one's own conditions. If you are someone who needs to spend money to attract others, it would be inappropriate to talk about expressing love haha :)

question: Chasing after an ex for 7 years, broke up after 2 months, now in a current relationship, but still can't forget the ex?
description: After pursuing my ex for seven years, I finally succeeded... We dated for two months and then broke up. I knew she didn't like me, but I genuinely liked her... After the breakup, I convinced myself that I had moved on and started a new relationship. However, a few days ago, I accidentally saw photos of my ex and me, and I realized that I still like her. But now I have a girlfriend, and I feel guilty about my current partner. I feel like I've emotionally cheated, and I'm really upset right now.
keywords: Love, infidelity, winning back the ex.

answers.answer_text: If I had committed a thought crime, I would have probably been arrested a long time ago. Do you feel guilty about it? You can't forget your ex, and you also feel a sense of responsibility towards your current partner, including conflicting interpretations of faithfulness in your mind. Let's analyze it together and see if it can be helpful to you. 1. Unable to forget your ex - you pursued her for seven years, which is not a short period of time. Let's imagine losing seven years of memories, do you think it's possible? When you finally won her over, it would have been for the best if you didn't, at least then you would have closure. Liking someone and being suitable for each other are two different things. If you can't forget, then treat it as a beautiful memory. 2. Sense of responsibility and interpretation of faithfulness, and the feeling of guilt - you have a sense of duty, believing that when you are in a relationship, you shouldn't think about other people. Regarding emotional infidelity, if possible, perhaps you can talk to your current girlfriend about it. From what I know, some women can accept emotional infidelity, disregarding moral judgments. The feelings of both parties are important in a relationship. Furthermore, don't rush to label yourself. If your longing for your ex becomes stronger and starts to affect your relationship with your current partner, then it might be necessary to consider further actions. From my perspective, it seems more like a self-directed annoyance and guilt. Feeling guilty and apologizing to your current partner won't truly bring you closer together; it's love that can do that. So ask yourself, do you love her? What do you love about her? If you do, then take action rather than just thinking about it.

Hey, every relationship teaches us how to grow. Remember, no one can stay with you till the end. Let the past go. Otherwise, your life will be filled with goodbyes every day. Maybe today you lost a bunch of keys, and tomorrow you lose a friend. Do you need to be sad and upset about everything? I believe that during the time you pursued the other person, you must have changed many bad habits in order to become the person they wanted. Actually, no one loses in this relationship. The other person understands that they don't like you and doesn't want to hold you back. You become a better person, isn't that good? Living in the present is the key to making yourself happier and more content.

question: After achieving success, my parents are not as happy as I imagined. I feel very disappointed and sad.
description: I used to be someone who wasn't very hardworking and was average in many aspects. I thought that if I worked hard and achieved success, my family would genuinely be happy and proud of me. However, when I surpassed my goals (even ones I couldn't imagine), I found that my family (including my parents, who have been separated for decades but not divorced) seemed to congratulate me on the surface but actually didn't seem as happy as I had imagined. I feel very disappointed that no one can truly share in my happiness, and I feel very lonely. Is this a normal reaction when children become independent, or is it some kind of life issue that I have encountered?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, family control

answers.answer_text: Hello there! Hugs to you! @First of all, have you carefully observed your own description and feelings? "I thought that if I achieved success, my family would be happy." "I feel disappointed, as no one is truly happy for me." ○ You need to realize that your so-called success is for yourself. Since childhood, we have been taught that parents are the ones who wholeheartedly love us, who worry about our pain and rejoice in our success. From childhood to adulthood, teachers, parents, and society have instilled in us the belief that good deeds are rewarded and bad deeds are punished. However, we gradually come to realize that parents' love for us is not entirely pure; after all, they are also individual beings who love themselves. The one who should feel happy for your success should be yourself. Perhaps you should understand that what you have accomplished is not to gain rewards, but to fulfill a personal life goal. ○ As for not receiving a positive response, when you focus on your own feelings, you won't care whether others' feedback is good or bad, and you will still be happy! It is good if you can bring joy to others, you can see it as a gift you give to the people around you, but it should not be used as a judgment of whether you have done well or not. We are not other people, we cannot understand their feelings. Maybe they are currently going through something troubling, and that's why they cannot be happy. Or maybe there are other reasons. Try your best not to assume that it is because they dislike you, as many misunderstandings arise from this. ○ Dear friend, never say, "No one is truly happy for me." That's such a worrying and absolute statement. You need to accept yourself and believe that people are not that fragile; even when you don't receive the kind of love you need, you still have the ability to love yourself. @Everyone expresses love in different ways, and I don't know how you found out about your parents' separation without divorce. Perhaps this decision was made out of concern for you. I couldn't help but think of a movie I watched earlier this year called "Cats and Mouse Game." While watching it, I felt deeply touched and heartbroken, realizing that maybe I was also someone who constantly sought my parents' attention. The protagonist, in order not to lose his parents' love, keeps making wrong choices, thinking that if he becomes wealthy, his mother won't leave his destitute father. The scene on Christmas Eve is particularly heart-wrenching. The lesson in life is about you, not about seeking the approval of others. I hope my answer can help you! Take care~

Hi, I understand your feelings very well and I hope I can help you. From what I can see, the main reason why you feel disappointed and sad is that your parents' behavior doesn't match your expectations of happiness. I'm curious, what does happiness look like in your imagination? I believe this is the answer that your parents don't know.
