It's like if I say I imagine a very beautiful house and ask you to draw it, you might not know where to start because you can only draw the beautiful house as you imagine it, and you don't know what the beautiful house as I imagine it looks like. Similarly, your parents can only express the happiness as they imagine it, but they cannot express the happiness as you imagine it. Now that we know the happiness you imagine and the happiness your parents imagine might be different, how can we close this gap? My suggestion is to transform our imagination into language. Language has a magical power. You can communicate with your parents by 1. Expressing your own feelings, saying something like "I thought you would be so happy that you'll jump for joy!" or "In my imagination, after hearing this news, you would take me out for a big meal." This can help your parents understand the distance between your feelings and their expressions. 2. Communicate their specific feelings, asking questions like "Are you happy for me? How happy are you?" or "If you had to rate your current level of happiness out of 100, what would it be?" 3. Communicate the distance in feelings, saying something like "I feel 100% happy right now, but it seems like you only feel 10%. So there's a 90% gap between us?" I believe that after such communication, your parents will give you feedback about their feelings, which can help you understand their feelings and emotions more specifically, as well as the reasons for the gap between their feelings and yours. For example, maybe from their perspective, the happiness they express is already their 100%, or maybe they have restrained their own happiness for various reasons, or maybe they are genuinely not very happy at the moment and there are reasons for that. But no matter what the reason is, after communication, the gap in imagination between you has already been reduced. Lastly, I remember a saying, "Language may be the fastest shortcut to reach each other's souls."

Hello! Hugs to you, dear! From your statement, I can sense that you feel a bit down, but here I still want to congratulate you on your achievements. As children, when we succeed, I think we all hope to receive praise and blessings from our parents, but it seems that your parents didn't sincerely congratulate you, which made you feel disappointed. For our parents, it's their first time being parents, and maybe they don't know how to express themselves. I believe they must have noticed your success. For you personally, you have achieved success, even exceeding your goals. However, how much do your parents understand about your goals and what you consider as success? There's a saying that different fields are like different mountains. Perhaps for your parents, they don't know how difficult it is for you to achieve this success. Is it possible that part of the reason is because we have too high expectations of our parents? Every parent has their own way of expressing themselves, and some parents may not express happiness to avoid their children becoming arrogant, which may affect their future path. Your parents may also have their own thoughts about expressing themselves. From your statement, I learned that your parents have been living separately for decades, even though they are not divorced. Regardless of how your parents get along, I believe they love their children and treat them with their own ways and expressions, expressing their love for their children. Finally, I hope you will become more and more successful on your future path. I hope this helps. Take care!

Hello, from your description, I can see that you have transformed from someone who was not very hardworking and ordinary to someone who can achieve their goals beyond their imagination. This is a remarkable transformation, congratulations! You wanted to share these achievements and joy with your parents, but you didn't feel their happiness. You feel disappointed and lonely, as if nobody can truly be happy for you. Here, you mentioned the phrase "in your imagination," how do you imagine they would be happy for you? It's difficult to determine the degree of this emotion based on appearance alone. For example, we all know that comedians perform joyful emotions on stage, but how can the audience differentiate whether their happiness is genuine or fake? This can lead to an interesting phenomenon: there is only one comedian on stage, but there could be 300 different interpretations from the 300 audience members. Some may say a slight smile is happiness, others may say relaxed body language is happiness, while others may argue that the smile is fake and the comedian is not truly happy. But in reality, only the comedian knows whether they are truly happy or not. So how do you judge your parents' happiness when you cannot sense it? Did they definitely react in the way you judged? I hope this answer can provide you with some inspiration! Karen.

Hello, I saw your concerns and I hope I can help you. I see that you mentioned that you used to be someone who wasn't very diligent and was average in many ways, but recently, through hard work, you have surpassed your own goals and achieved success that you couldn't even imagine. You've noticed that your family, including your parents, don't seem as happy as you imagined and you feel disappointed and lonely. I'm glad to see that you have achieved success through your own efforts, and I applaud you. I also understand your feelings and emotions very well, and I hope I can help you. First and foremost, acknowledge yourself. From your success, it is clear that you are someone who has expectations for yourself, looks forward to the future, and is willing to work harder for it. Through this success, see your own strengths, actively summarize your experiences, and don't easily let external emotions and environments affect you. Maintain your advantages and strive for higher goals. Secondly, lower your expectations. Here, expectations refer to your expectations of your family, including your parents. From your description, I can see that they genuinely congratulate you. What makes you feel that they are not as happy? It may be because you have set too high expectations for them. From your description, it seems that your parents' separation has also had some impact on you, and there may already be some barriers between you. Remember that everyone expresses happiness in different ways, and there may be many other factors involved, such as the state of mind of your parents and your own condition. Don't pay too much attention to the formality. Take the initiative to communicate with them more and try to understand them more. Success may be an added bonus to the parental relationship, but it is by no means a prerequisite. What would make your parents happier is probably your growing maturity. Thirdly, learn to be independent. Gradually build your own social support system so that you have friends whom you can share your success and pain with, apart from your family. Loneliness is normal, and learning to overcome it is something that everyone needs to continuously learn. Additionally, cultivating hobbies that are beneficial for your physical and mental well-being can help you enrich yourself and gain more nourishment. I wish you new achievements every day.

Hello there~ I totally understand how you feel, sending you a hug~ I think your feelings of disappointment and sadness are quite normal. When we have high expectations for something and the result doesn't meet our expectations, we feel disappointed. The higher the expectation, the greater the disappointment. In your case, you expected your parents to be very happy and proud of your progress, but they weren't, so you feel disappointed and sad. It's not necessarily their fault, maybe they just didn't feel particularly happy or they wanted to encourage you to keep working hard without praising you, fearing that you might become arrogant. Maybe you don't communicate with your parents very often, which is why you need their emotional support and have such expectations. Keep up the good work, my friend! If you feel lonely, you can make more reliable friends. You can also visit home more often and talk to your parents more. Best wishes~.

Hello, I understand your feelings. Every parent treats their child differently. Some parents get very happy and constantly praise their child even for small progress. While some parents may not show much reaction no matter how big the achievements are. There are even parents who have never praised their child at all. You mentioned that you exceeded the goals, even beyond your imagination. Maybe your parents don't really understand your industry and are not able to appreciate your achievements to the fullest. In their eyes, it might just be a small improvement, so they didn't show it. I understand that you want to share your joy with them, but they didn't react as you expected. It's okay, trust that parents love us very much. When we grow up and become independent, as long as our parents have their own lives and are safe and healthy, that is the greatest comfort to us. Don't overthink it, a wonderful life has just begun! Take care!

Title: Hello! From your question and description, it seems like you are eager to share the joy of success with your parents, and you feel disappointed and puzzled about the gap between their reaction and your expectations. Is that right? This gap between reality and desire may be influenced by several factors: typically, people naturally, quickly, and intensely react to negative news compared to positive news (which is why many media outlets prefer to use negative news to attract readers). Sharing a bad news discreetly may have the same impact as a shocking one, while sharing good news may require more pomp and circumstance to draw equal attention. Due to this common human tendency, it appears that intimate relationships seem to be more common and easily appreciated when faced with difficulties (the power of tragedy?). Therefore, it is not difficult to understand why people are accustomed to sharing burdens but not so accustomed to proactively sharing or reciprocating happy news. In terms of the interactivity of interpersonal relationships, strong interactivity, in addition to the influence of emotional intimacy, often depends on the sense of "connection" between each other, which is usually manifested as a sense of responsibility between parents and children. It is precisely this sense of responsibility that makes parents more likely to pay attention to communication that requires them to take responsibility, while communication beyond responsibility may not have the same level of conscious participation due to unfamiliarity or lack of experience. In other words, your success may not be the first thing to catch their attention because it is unrelated to their habitual sense of responsibility. The so-called connectivity in interactive relationships, between loved ones, if not related to a sense of responsibility, perhaps the expressing party needs to use a special way of expression or prompt the other party to feel involved during the expression process in order to make them pay attention to it. I believe that even individuals who are not used to expressing enthusiasm may be touched by vivid joy when they can personally see or experience the joy that you feel.

Hello, dear asker, hugs to you~ I can understand your feelings very well and can sense your disappointment and sadness. Congratulations on your success, and I hope my answer can help you. [Problem Analysis] The main issue you have is that you used to not put in much effort and considered yourself an average person. Recently, through your own efforts, you have achieved success, but your family cannot truly understand and be happy for your success. Therefore, you feel a sense of loneliness and disappointment. [Advice] Focus on yourself and make yourself happier. Throughout our lives, we strive to make ourselves happy; it is not about gaining recognition and understanding from others. Everyone has their own life, and even though family members are the closest to us, they won't always pay attention to us. Perhaps they are going through something unhappy recently and cannot fully consider your feelings. Don't worry too much, keep a positive outlook, and remember that you have to walk your own path in the future. Be stronger and get used to facing things alone. In the process of growth, we all hope to be noticed, but once others show neglect or indifference towards us, we feel disappointed. However, that's how life is, and only we can truly understand ourselves. Regardless of whether we are happy or sad, others cannot truly empathize with us, so there is no need to pay too much attention to it. Growing up means gradually getting used to facing things alone. Relax and understand that everyone's expectations are different; what may be a hard-earned success in your eyes may only be a small ripple in your parents' life experiences. Due to different life experiences, their mindset may also change, and they may not be as happy for a long time as we are when we achieve something through hard work. Relax and understand that they may actually be happy, just not showing it. I wish you a happier and more joyful life in the future.

Hello, OP, to achieve your goals. As for the disappointment you feel because your parents are not as happy as you imagined, I think it may be due to the following reasons: high expectations, the higher the expectations, the easier it is to feel a gap in the mind. From your words, it can be seen that the achievements you have made are very great, and in your perception, your parents did not show the happiness and pride you imagined, which can lead to a feeling of "disappointment" in your psychology. Continued excitement for one thing, when we are constantly excited about something, once we calm down, it will appear more barren and gloomy, which is actually a very common psychological dynamic change. The expression of parents, what you think your parents are not happy, is only your own perception. Parents have their own ways of expressing themselves, they also have their own lives and thoughts. How could they not be happy when their own children succeed? You may just be overly worried. I am grateful to meet you and I hope this can help you!

question: When looking for a job, why do people with low self-esteem choose to lie on their resumes?
description: When looking for a job, I realized that due to low self-esteem and poor abilities, I tend to underestimate myself and consequently end up applying for lower quality jobs.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, I understand that 1. You underestimate yourself in your resume. 2. You are looking for relatively low-paying jobs, and you feel inferior. [Some analysis and suggestions] 1. When making judgments about yourself, you can refer to the opinions of friends and family, rather than allowing yourself to subjectively degrade yourself. Ask others about your strengths and do a comprehensive and as objective as possible analysis of yourself, which will help improve your self-esteem. 2. If the lower-paying jobs are the most suitable ones you can find at the moment, then improve your skills in these job positions, learn more, and lay a foundation for future better job opportunities. It is also a good career choice. I hope this helps you.

question: I have been diagnosed with anxiety disorder and have been taking medication for over two weeks.
description: I (29 years old, male) developed an anxious state and dizziness for over a month after reading negative news on August 4th. I couldn't sleep well. Many tests showed no problems, so I went to a traditional Chinese medicine hospital for treatment. Later on, another mental health clinic diagnosed me with anxiety disorder, and the dizziness symptoms eased after taking medication. However, sometimes I still feel restless and agitated when I think about certain things, and I rely on sleeping pills to fall asleep. Sigh, I don't know when I will get better. Currently, I am living alone and working in a different city, without many good friends. The friends I used to think were close have become critical of me. I no longer want to contact them, and sometimes I even have the urge to argue or physically confront them... It is distressing to think about this.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, I've read your description. Currently, it has been over two weeks since you started taking medication for anxiety, and some of your symptoms have improved, indicating that the medication is starting to take effect. Treating anxiety is a long-term and systematic process. As you continue to take the medication, your sleep and emotional problems will gradually improve, and your condition will be better than it is now. Therefore, please cooperate with the doctor and continue taking the medication. Additionally, if conditions allow, it is recommended to receive psychological counseling. Explore the underlying causes of anxiety. It is also helpful to learn breathing relaxation, mindfulness, and other methods and practice them daily. They can effectively alleviate symptoms when you have an anxiety attack. Moreover, exercise, socializing, and developing hobbies can also help improve your mood and relieve anxiety.

It is very distressing to see your current diagnosis of anxiety disorder. Your reaction to negative news may be the source of this anxiety. I wonder if you have had particularly anxious moments in the past. As for the negative news you mentioned, it may be helpful to interpret and sort through them. Right now, what you can do is to follow medical advice and cooperate with treatment. If necessary, you can also consider psychological counseling and actively engage in self-regulation to deal with things that make you uncomfortable and plan your life comprehensively. It seems that you have been experiencing dizziness and insomnia after being diagnosed with anxiety disorder. Although the dizziness has reduced after taking medication, you still occasionally feel restless and uneasy. You rely on sleeping pills to fall asleep, and living alone in another city without close friends makes you irritable and picky. Maybe your friends have higher expectations of you, and as a result, you no longer want to connect with them. There may also be some obvious negative emotions within you. Although I don't know exactly what has happened between you, changes in friendships are something we often have to face in life. Keep a record of your feelings of restlessness and anxiety and try to regulate them. You are already receiving treatment, and your restlessness must be related to the things you do or experience. It may even lead to some anxiety and sleep disturbances because of excessive thinking. If this phenomenon affects your life, you may consider comprehensive mindfulness training. There may be many judgments regarding your thoughts and life that can be discussed in counseling. Moderate restlessness and anxiety can let you know what you should and should not do and can improve brain vitality. But if you continue to immerse yourself in it, your energy will be depleted. Please note that our restlessness and stress begin with our cognition. This kind of anxious reaction can cause accelerated heartbeats, increased pulse rates, and muscle tension. You can identify the types of thoughts that cause you excessive stress. You may be experiencing obvious negative thoughts that trigger excessive worry, which can lead to the release of stress hormones, just like experiencing a nightmare. We need to recognize them, including statements like "should" or "must". Everyone has their own choices, and others have expectations of you, so you can also judge yourself. Think about what you have been telling yourself. Try to turn negative thoughts into positive ones. Accepting stress is inevitable, but you can take measures to reduce it and learn how to cope with restlessness and anxiety. You can also try to avoid stress as much as possible. If you know for sure that a certain person or activity is the source of your restlessness and anxiety, try to eliminate the stress from your life, including taking appropriate breaks and readjusting to the existence of this thing, or reducing contact with it as much as possible. Before taking action, think carefully and be aware that your behavior needs appropriate consideration.

question: Married and have children, want to change myself and regain self-confidence, what should I do?
description: It has been more than three years since we got married, but we didn't have a wedding ceremony and didn't ask for any dowry. Now we have two children, the older one is two and a half years old, and the younger one is five months old. We live together with my mother-in-law at home, while my husband and father-in-law work outside. I have been living with my mother-in-law all this time. She is quite dominant, while I am not very talkative. The customs in Yunnan, where I am from, are different from those in Sichuan, where my husband is from. There is a generation gap between me and my mother-in-law in terms of child education. Over the past three years, I have had quite a few conflicts with my mother-in-law, and these accumulations have led me to complain and discuss with others. I will feel inadequate and that everything I do is wrong. I will have a negative outlook on life, easily cry, get angry, and have a bad temper. Sometimes, I feel that life is meaningless and don't want to live anymore. I know that I have serious issues in my heart, and I know that this cannot continue, it's not right. But I can't help myself, and I don't know why I have gradually become like this and why I have made my life so miserable... How can I change?
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, prenatal and postnatal, views on childbirth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, it seems that you are in a complex emotional state, perhaps feeling aggrieved, angry, unwilling, and helpless. There may also be some other indescribable feelings, all of which accumulate and come one after another, causing great distress. Your understanding of this would be deeper. You mentioned that you are currently still living with your mother-in-law, and there have been differences in living habits since getting married. How have you adjusted and adapted over the years, and what are the results? Have you considered moving out of your mother-in-law's house and living independently with your own small family? Whether living with the mother-in-law or living independently with your own small family, both situations come with problems and challenges. You may assess which situation is better for you at this stage, and it would be helpful to have a good discussion with your husband as his help and support are crucial to you. Take care of yourself.

question: A freshman girl often has a desire to date, but doesn't know where to start.
description: Freshman girls, I used to get nervous and shy when talking to boys in high school. In college, every time I take a walk on campus, I see couples everywhere, and my roommates are also still single, talking about getting into relationships. I've also made friends with some guys, but whenever I talk to them, my mind goes blank. I really want to be in a relationship, but no one is pursuing me, and there isn't anyone I particularly like either. I also feel like my views on love are too simplistic. Today, I quietly like one guy, and then after a while, I start liking another guy. Sometimes, even after just a short interaction, not knowing much about the other person, I might just chat with them for a bit and develop feelings for them.

answers.answer_text: Hello! First of all, I would like to thank you for asking such a great question! I think many single girls have the same concerns as you. Actually, I am in the same boat as you and have been waiting for my own love story! I'm not afraid to admit that I'm already 27 years old and still searching! And I'm perpetually single, haha! I don't have any dating experience to teach you, but I would like to share my feelings with you! In fact, I used to be just like you, eager to be in a relationship but never had any guys chasing after me. I didn't have anyone I particularly liked, felt like anyone would do but also didn't want to settle. Although my standards for choosing friends were not high, there were always certain factors holding me back from taking the first step! Often, even before a relationship started, I already had an idea of how it would end. This reveals the contradiction in psychology known as avoidant conflict, where the same thing or person has both what you desire and what you fear. This contradiction is like two evenly matched little people in your heart playing tug-of-war, neither willing to give in, just stalling. Because I study psychology myself, I took some questionnaires and read some books to explore myself. Later, I found the reasons behind this state: (1) I haven't developed a mature view of love and have a limited understanding of intimate relationships. (2) A lack of security within myself and a fear of stepping out of my comfort zone. (3) Always predicting outcomes, fearing hurt and unable to handle losing. (4) Lack of self-confidence. Because I am an ordinary looking girl with average height, I have always felt insecure about my appearance. The above is my analysis of myself, and once I knew the reasons, I started making changes! The first and third reasons are relatively easy to solve and can be changed gradually through reading. The difficult ones are 2 and 4. Developing security and self-confidence don't happen overnight, so when faced with these reasons, I set a three-year goal for myself. In these three years, I started focusing on my inner self, reading many books on psychology, such as "Intimate Relationships" trilogy, "Marriage Psychology," "Why Love Hurts," "The Heidi Chronicles," and others. Through reading, you will understand different types of intimate relationships and the problems that arise in them. You will gradually form your own view of love and find the right way to love for yourself. Apart from reading, I also observe the interaction patterns of couples in real life. I used to think that in a relationship, two people should always present their best sides to each other, but later I slowly discovered that two people in love actually give each other their true selves. Love is not as perfect as imagined, love is about acceptance, understanding, and being there for each other! Realizing this, I found that I am not as insecure anymore. In fact, I am quite cute, at least some guys have complimented my eyes! Thinking about this, I am not so insecure anymore! When a person overcomes their insecurities and builds self-confidence, they will find a sense of security! I used to think that security should be given by the man, but now I understand that in any relationship, only when both individuals have a complete sense of self, will there be a sense of security! Although I haven't entered a romantic relationship yet, I have already stepped out of my comfort zone, and I now have some great male friends around me that I can freely communicate with! And, there are people who have started liking me! I think that is the change brought by self-confidence! So, my advice to you is to also try self-exploration, find the reasons, face them, and I believe that deep down, every girl has a beautiful and confident angel, believe in yourself, make changes, step out of your comfort zone, and you will definitely meet your destined partner! That's my sharing and advice, I hope it helps you! Keep it up, young girl!

Freshman girl, when talking to boys in high school, would feel nervous and shy. In college, every time she takes a walk on campus, she sees couples and her roommates are all talking about being single. Every girl yearns for love, and each has a princess dream, fantasizing about meeting their Prince Charming. I also have male friends, but whenever I talk to them, my mind goes blank. Eating, drinking, chatting, these are all subconscious actions. If you pay attention to them, they'll go wrong. The more afraid you are of saying the wrong thing, the more likely you will. The more afraid you are of making a fool of yourself, the easier it is to do so. Chatting is just chatting, talking is just talking. If you insist on adding expectations, then you will gain anxiety. This is the psychology of perfectionism. How do you solve this problem? You have to let go. Tell yourself that you're just going to chat aimlessly and randomly. Anyway, your mind is not very clear when you chat normally and you're not likable. So just try whatever you want, make yourself happy. I really want to be in love, but there are no boys pursuing me. You have to chase after the goddess, what if she's blind? You also have to pursue the god, what if he's foolish? But I don't really like any particular boy, and I feel that my views on love are too simplistic. Today, I silently like a boy, but in a while, I like another boy. Sometimes, even though I haven't interacted with someone for long, I don't know what kind of person they are, but I might feel a fondness for them just by chatting. This is what you call infatuation. Everyone has a need to be loved, and a need to give love. When you don't receive love for a long time, the river of love in your heart dries up. Naturally, you start to become infatuated. How do you solve this problem? You have to give love. Those who give love will receive love in return, and those who send blessings will receive blessings. The people who only focus on giving without asking for anything in return will gain the most. Those who only focus on receiving without giving will gain nothing.

Everyone has a different pace. Some people mature early, while others mature late. There is no right or wrong, as long as you find your own comfortable pace. Just like in school, there are always some girls who are outgoing and mature early, starting to date at a young age, while others are more introverted and shy, blushing when talking to boys. This is related to personal experiences and confidence levels, and we cannot expect everyone to be the same. You mentioned that you want to be in a relationship, but have you thought about what kind of guy you should be looking for? What kind of guy would be suitable for you and make you feel comfortable? Dating is not easy. We always hope to find someone we love and who is right for us, but it is actually quite difficult and requires effort, such as controlling our temper and considering others. Perhaps some people think that dating casually is fine, why take it seriously if it's not marriage. This requires you to understand the purpose of dating. Are you just playing around or do you want something more serious? Being clear about what you like and what is suitable for you increases the chances of success. If you enter into a relationship blindly without knowing anything, you may not gain anything, and both you and the other person may get hurt, physically or emotionally. The fact that no guys are pursuing you right now and there isn't anyone you particularly like indicates that the timing is not yet right. You don't have to force yourself to date. Dating should come naturally, from the heart. Besides dating, there are many other things in life worth experiencing. Focus on building yourself, doing things you enjoy and nurturing yourself. When you learn to love yourself, attracting a partner becomes easier because the self-loving you will radiate from the inside out. Think about the kind of life you want in the future and then work hard to study and strive for it. This will give you confidence and determination. When you know what you want, you will feel very certain in your heart, and you will no longer feel so nervous, shy, or mentally dull when communicating with guys. Perhaps at that time, your suitable Prince Charming will appear.

Hello (^_^)/ Everyone wants to have a sweet relationship when they enter college, but they find that it is not as easy as they think. What kind of guy do you like? What are your criteria for choosing a partner? Do you focus more on a guy's appearance or other aspects? ##Psychological Mechanisms of Mate Selection## ①Similarity ②Complementary differences ③Social exchange. Think about what kind of guy you want in your mind. Set a goal and take it step by step. ①Expand your social circle and make new friends. ②Interact more with the opposite sex and improve yourself. ③Identify your ideal person and focus your emotions on him alone. ④Increase contact, chat more, and take things slow. ⑤When the opportunity arises, make your feelings clear through actions. Love cannot be forced, and it may succeed or fail. Maintain the right attitude and make decisions that you feel are worthwhile. Let it happen naturally, and if it doesn't, wait patiently. What is meant for you will come. Best wishes!

"Hi, OP! The phase of 'wanting to be in love+no one pursuing+falling in love easily' is quite classic! I've experienced it too. It's clear that you have a longing for love, but you lack personal experience, and those around you (at least your roommates) do not provide a clear reference. At this stage, your imagination about love is still in the fantasy stage, so it's not a 'superficial view of love,' but rather an undeveloped view of love. I suggest you observe real love stories around you to enrich your understanding of love; it's not advisable to rely solely on fictional love from literature and movies to shape your own imagination of love. Also, there is no need to feel pressured when interacting with boys; you should not feel pressured in any respectful interpersonal relationships. Everyone is different, and individual differences outweigh gender differences. If you encounter someone you hope to develop feelings for and want to have more interactions with, make sure to understand him as an individual rather than applying so-called 'general characteristics' of a certain group to him. As for feeling nervous, I suggest trying to see the other person as a 'person,' rather than someone of a specific gender, and then engage in conversation. Maybe you won't feel as nervous that way. I hope you can have a happy romantic relationship when the time is right! Good luck~."

Hello, OP. After reading your description, I can totally relate. I'm a sophomore this year and I also have no dating experience at the age of 20. However, I have always wanted to be in a relationship, although I'm not really sure what kind of person I'm looking for. It feels like anyone could be a potential partner. I'm sharing my experience to let you know that this kind of thinking is normal. Firstly, because our current age is in early adulthood, we yearn for intimacy and our hormones are more active, leading to a stronger desire for love. Seeing many happy couples around us also stimulates our desire for intimate relationships. Therefore, it's common to often have thoughts of wanting to be in a relationship. Secondly, you mentioned that your understanding of love is shallow, but that's because you haven't experienced it yet and don't know what you want. Even if you have feelings for certain boys, actually being in a relationship with them might not necessarily be what you truly want. I believe you don't want to casually enter a relationship. So don't rush and wait patiently. Your Prince Charming will come soon. Just focus on yourself and become the best version of yourself while waiting for him. I hope my answer can help you and I hope you find sweet love.

In relationships, I believe that as long as you use sincerity, you can exchange for sincerity, even if it is a sincere rejection, it is much better than fake procrastination. Don't try to manipulate people's hearts with tricks, showing off skills and cunning won't last. Respect is the most fundamental principle in two people's interaction. You should constantly strive to understand each other, to be considerate of each other, to compromise and accommodate each other. It's not about one-sided self-sacrifice, but the joint effort of both individuals. One more thing, if you want someone to love you, then you have to learn to love yourself. Self-love is not selfishness, but confidence. Otherwise, how can you face the person you like? I recommend books like "How to Make Someone Fall in Love with You," "Men are from Mars, Women are from Venus," and "Intimate Relationships." These books provide both theoretical and practical guidance!

Hello miss. Through reading your question, I understand that your main issue is desiring to find love and get out of being single. However, nobody is pursuing you and the people you are interested in are not consistent. Actually, not being pursued by anyone doesn't necessarily mean that you are not excellent. It could be because certain aspects of your personality make guys perceive you as less gentle, or perhaps you display some aggression in certain areas, causing guys to hesitate in pursuing you. It could also be that your way of speaking and behaving is not very gentle, like being a bit tomboyish. The specific reasons vary for each person, so you can discuss your personality and mannerisms with classmates and friends. As for your lack of consistency in liking someone, this is actually a common occurrence. My classmates have also expressed similar thoughts to me. Of course, this doesn't mean being promiscuous; it is rather an expression of distress. In fact, you can question yourself about the people you simply think are good in your daily life, there must be many. But what does it mean to like someone? I think firstly, it's about attraction, a certain quality about him that captivates us. Secondly, it's being willing to sacrifice for him, not a huge sacrifice, but something we wouldn't do for anyone else, something unique to him. And finally, it's being willing to become a better person for him, improving oneself in various aspects. Of course, this is just my personal viewpoint and not very mature. Professional miss, you can refer to some books, and this learning process is also a way of improving oneself. Finally, I hope you have the courage to break through and challenge yourself. If you want some changes in your life, you have to step out of your comfort zone. Actually, it applies to other things as well, stepping out of the comfort zone to meet a better version of yourself. Keep it up!

question: Review clock, savings exhausted, heart also panicked, how to deal with anxiety and impatience?
description: Reviewing, no job. Living off of past achievements. If I continue like this and don't pass the exam, I won't be able to take it next year. I'll have to start working. I don't even know if working will be satisfying. After all, the career I've envisioned is in the direction of the current exams. Time is precious, money is precious, once used they can't be regained. But my foot is injured, resting for half a month, wasting half a month, it feels like my heart is bleeding. Facing parents, loved ones, classmates, neighbors, constantly being pressured for marriage... Resting at home, the more I rest, the more exhausted I become... I'm also worried about my review plan... During my student years, I was good at studying, but because I had too much on my mind, it affected my academic performance and caused me to miss the best study opportunities. Resting for one day, I'm anxious for one day. I've been resting for half a month now, at this moment, time is more precious than money.
keywords: Emotions, expression of emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Give you a big hug. If it is a profession that you truly love, you must persevere and not give up. If you give up because of your current difficulties and the opinions of others, you will regret it for a lifetime. These problems will naturally be solved once you succeed, but if you give up, you will live under the shadow of these problems.
