question: 20-year-old female, has always had a tendency for self-harm, what should she do?
description: Since primary school until now, I have always engaged in self-harm behaviors. Specifically, this includes repeatedly rolling off the bed, pinching and scratching myself (unable to break the skin), strangling myself, hitting walls, and pounding different parts of my body. Every time I am under a lot of stress, such as not being able to finish homework in middle school or arguing with my significant other, I engage in self-harm. Do I have a psychological problem? What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, have you had breakfast? People who engage in self-harm are often people who have fallen into despair, enduring harsh living conditions and filled with uncertainty, fear, pain, and hopelessness. They resort to self-harm as a way to combat a highly dissociative state and to reconnect with reality. I have been engaging in self-harm since elementary school. Specifically, it includes rolling off the bed repeatedly, pinching and scratching myself [not breaking the skin], choking myself, hitting walls, and pounding different parts of my body. Is this considered a psychological problem? Honestly, I am not sure because the determination of "psychological problem" is based on multiple criteria, usually assessed based on the duration of the problem, the degree of impairment in social functioning, and the level of mental distress. Every time I experience great stress, like when I couldn't finish my homework in middle school or had an argument with my partner. It seems more like an extreme form of emotional release or a self-punishing, self-deprecating emotional release. It is a way to exchange self-harm and self-deprecation in order to obtain concessions and compliance from others. I guess there are some characteristics in my personality structure that involve unequal power struggles in my relationships with others. So, whether there is a psychological problem or not, it depends on whether there are any obvious conflicts and distortions in other aspects of my personality. OP, you are a kind person who would rather harm yourself than others. Every time, you choose to redirect your anger towards yourself and transfer your pain from your mind to your body. I think, most of the time, the pain in your heart surpasses the limits you believe you can bear. You didn't mention what has happened to you from childhood to now, so I can't understand your pain from my own perspective. However, I believe that every choice you make is certainly the best for yourself in order to protect yourself. Because fear, pain, and stress are all psychological energy for us. No matter what method we choose, there must be a reasonable need underlying the thoughts and actions of self-harm. Since you want to solve your self-harm problem and suspect it may be a psychological disorder, consider going to the hospital and letting doctors diagnose you based on your clinical symptoms, and then follow their guidance. Psychological problems are the result of comprehensive judgments, and self-harm is not just a problem. So, can you try to look at the meaning behind your self-harm impulses from a different perspective? Or maybe we can delve deeper into the psychological truth behind our self-harm? The world and I embrace you warmly.

Hello! Subject, it's nice to meet you here! Let me share some of my thoughts that I hope will be helpful to you. From your description, it can be seen that you are aware of your self-harming behavior when facing difficulties in studying or emotions. The emotions at that time cannot be relieved, perhaps because the subconscious is at work. What is the subconscious? It is a long-term suppressed and hidden consciousness, which can be positive or negative. The positive subconscious can promote our growth and learning, resolve inner troubles, while the negative subconscious is prone to self-harm and affects our lives. Your self-harming behavior belongs to the negative behavior of the subconscious. If you want to change, you must activate a positive sense of self. When faced with difficulties or things that you find difficult to solve, you should face them bravely. If you have limited abilities, seek help from your family and friends instead of fighting alone. Because when you lack the ability to overcome your emotions or difficulties, your subconscious will retreat, and you will harm yourself to soothe your inner self. Sometimes, this pain may transfer to the body, but it is not advisable. You need to face the pain in your heart actively and heal it through self-motivation, seeking help, and other methods, allowing your inner self to calm down. Step by step, overcome the child within you, do not fear, consciously overcome it slowly, and you will definitely get better. If it is indeed difficult to control your emotions, then it is necessary to seek professional psychological help, find some methods that suit you, and help yourself in relieving stress. I hope this sharing can be helpful to you.

It seems that the poster has developed a habit of releasing emotions. The poster says that whenever they are under great stress, they tend to self-harm, such as when they can't finish their middle school homework or when they argue with their significant other. Emotions can lead to different behaviors and external expressions. Emotions themselves are neither good nor bad, but behaviors can be categorized as good or bad. Often, we may not dislike our own emotions, but rather dislike our emotional behaviors. For example, when we get angry, we may break things or even self-harm. Anger as an emotion is neither right nor wrong. It exists for a reason. However, the behaviors triggered by anger, such as breaking things or self-harm, are not good and can be replaced with more reasonable alternatives, such as going for a run. Therefore, when faced with our own emotions and emotional behaviors, we must be mindful to differentiate between them. When you are feeling agitated or angry, simply take a cup of tea, touch it with your hand, feel the touch of your fingers on the cup, and experience its temperature. Is it hot or not? Can you drink it? Just feel it and return to the present moment. When you can connect with the present moment, your emotions can be immediately controlled, and you will no longer trigger emotional behaviors.

After carefully reading your confession, I deeply understand your pain and give you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1 When a person is mentally suffering to the point of contemplating suicide, they may resort to self-harm as a way to transfer their mental pain to physical pain. As the mental anguish is alleviated, a sense of pleasure arises, leading to repetitive self-harm that becomes hard to stop. 2 So, how can this problem be resolved? Learn to confide in someone. Whenever you feel the pain, find someone to express the negative energy in your heart. Once it is spoken out, it will be okay. The internal suffering will diminish. 3 If you cannot find someone to confide in or want to eliminate negative emotions within yourself, it would be best to seek a psychologist. Through psychological counseling, you can achieve unprecedented growth. They will help you identify the root of the problem, target the issues, and guide you in cultivating a peaceful mind. Thank you for your question. May the beauty of the world come to you as expected.

question: 27-year-old male, got into a fight after arguing with his father. His father initiated the physical altercation, accusing him of being disrespectful.
description: My older brother and I went out to drink at Starbucks, and later my brother said he needed to pick up a child and sent me home. In the meantime, my brother talked to me about my job. When we got home, I was a bit angry. He was also very angry and started hitting me. We had two arguments in between. I threw his phone at him, and he then punched my neck by going around the tea table. We fought near the tea table. My godfather, Mr. Jiang, pulled me away. He kept knocking me down and violently hitting my neck. I grabbed his private area, and then he let go. I stood up and picked up the lid of the tea can next to me to hit him, but I only hit the ground. I broke the clay pot on the ground to create obstacles. He rushed towards me, and I picked up a broken piece and hit him on the head. He pulled me onto the armrest of the sofa, pressed my head against the wooden armrest, and struck the back of my head violently, causing me to suffocate. I reached for his eyes with my hand. My godfather mentioned that there was blood. It was only then that he realized it and took me and my godfather to see a doctor. He didn't take me to see a doctor though. I ran to my grandmother's house, and my sister even contacted me and said not to go back home. If I go back home, she will call 911. I said, "Go ahead, call them. I'll tell them about my injuries, and at least it can get my dad locked up for 10 years for attempted murder. He has no family except himself. He still talks to me about humanity. Every time we fight, he's the one who starts it. Afterward, he pitifully claims that I hit him and that I'm not filial."
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello: As the saying goes, "Tigers fight, brothers unite; father and son soldiers on the battlefield." How did it turn into infighting? However, from a psychological perspective, every child's problems must have the influence of their biological parents. From your words, I can sense that you have a strong dislike for your father, and it is likely that he has done many things that have made you unhappy. Also, if you truly respected your father, why would you fight with him? Don't worry, we can analyze the situation. Perhaps you have a lot to say but don't know how to express it and analyze the problem. 1. You went out for Starbucks with your brother, and he said he would take the kids and send you home. During the ride back, there was some tension, and both of you got angry. This argument (mentioned here) refers to the argument with your father after returning home, right? Does your father often have grievances about your work? The arguments between you and your father may have been accumulated over a long time. 2. You threw his phone at him, and he dodged it, then hit your neck on the edge of the tea table. A fight broke out. Your godfather, Mr. Jiang, pulled you away. He kept knocking you down and hitting your neck relentlessly. You grabbed his groin to make him let go. You stood up and picked up the lid of the tea canister to hit him, but of course, you didn't hit him, it hit the floor. Actually, from a physical strength perspective, your father certainly couldn't beat you, and it seems that he also saw your "restraint" because you didn’t really hit him. It seems like you both have a lot of resentment towards each other, but continuing like this will only be detrimental to both of you. 3. The clay pot was smashed on the ground to create obstacles. He rushed towards you, and you picked up a shard to hit him on the head. He pulled me onto the sofa armrest, pressed your head against the wooden armrest, and fiercely hit the back of your head, causing you to choke. You reached for his eyes. Your godfather said from behind, "There is blood." Only then did he realize it and took you and your godfather to see a doctor. (These two paragraphs describe the details, and it seems like it is still fresh in your memory. I want to ask: Does your father behave this way towards others? Do you behave this way towards others as well? Or is it only between you and your father?) 4. He didn't take you to see a doctor. You ran to my grandma's house, and your sister contacted you and said not to go home, threatening to call the police (110) if you did. You said, "Go ahead, call. Just tell them about your injuries. At least it can put Dad in prison for 10 years for attempted murder." (Both sides are family, why is your sister taking your father's side? In the process of fighting, it is obvious that your father can't beat you, so she must be afraid that you will go back and attack him again, right? But you also feel wronged, so you said, "No one took you to see the injuries." You and your father hurt each other (both physically and verbally), which is not good for anyone. Can you choose a different way to communicate in the future?) 5. He only has himself and no family. He talked to me about humanity. Every time we fight, he is the one who starts it. Afterwards, he pitifully claims that I hit him and that I am not filial. (It seems that you have had fights more than once, and he is always the one who starts it. Does he think that when he hits you, you shouldn't fight back? Then, since you can't handle the relationship well, you can create some distance between you, so that you won't end up fighting. Otherwise, you will just get the reputation of being unfilial. Isn't that right?) Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you can ease your emotions and learn to respect each other! If you have any confusion, feel free to message me!

Growth is about finding breakthrough points, changing trajectory, and spiraling growth to become a better version of oneself. The protagonist of this personal journey describes a scene that seems like a fragment from a Jin Yong martial arts drama, telling the story of getting into a physical altercation with an elder brother and godfather. After the altercation with the godfather, because the godfather is an elder, the protagonist is criticized by family members and receives feedback that they did something wrong and were not filial. Faced with this feedback, the protagonist feels very aggrieved because they believe it was the godfather who initiated the conflict and they were only defending themselves. Social circle: The protagonist cannot bear this injustice from the altercation, mainly because they believe in revenge. They struggle with the contradiction between traditional respect for elders and the desire for revenge in society. In the context of the father-son relationship, we generally believe that the father is superior and has the right to discipline the child, but the son cannot strike back at the father. The protagonist's belief is that if the father strikes first, then he shouldn't blame the son for being heartless. So the protagonist applies the principles of interacting with friends to their relationship with their father, which brings them deep distress. Changing trajectory: Cognitive reshaping: The protagonist's belief is "I won't harm others, but if others harm me, I will harm them back." But the protagonist hasn't differentiated between different situations and relationships in this belief. They should reflect on the specific circumstances of the altercation. On the other hand, they are facing their own father, their own family. They should put aside this belief at this moment and consider the problem from the perspective of the family, making sacrifices for the betterment of the family. Emotion control: The altercation between the protagonist and their father is also caused by emotions. The protagonist's emotions led them to not recognize themselves and do something they didn't intend to do, even though they felt regret later on. But the protagonist doesn't allow themselves to admit their mistake, so they use the excuse of their father striking first. The protagonist can learn to control their emotions, especially when they feel angry, by being aware of their emotions and then controlling them. Emotions can lead the protagonist to do things they don't want to do. Cognitive reshaping - Emotion control - Changing trajectory - Spiraling growth - Becoming a better version of oneself.

After carefully reading your vent, I deeply understand your pain. Here's my analysis: 1. I sympathize with your unfortunate situation. Dealing with such a violent father is difficult. You are now an adult, but he still doesn't show the slightest respect a father should have. He continues to resort to physical punishment without any mercy. He has never considered your feelings or understood the emotions you go through. He only releases his own anger. 2. Having a father like that is truly unlucky for you. However, every age group has responsibilities that come with their age. As you mentioned, you are already 27 years old. At this age, you should be getting married and starting a family, and then focus on building your own household. 3. If we were still underage, we could blame our original family for the pain they caused us. But now that we have grown up and become adults, we need to take responsibility for our own lives. If your father has caused you harm, you can choose to distance yourself from him and the original family. Focus on pursuing your own happiness. Rely on yourself for strength and support, as they say, "A person who doesn't rely on themselves will be forsaken by the heavens and earth." Keep going! A stranger from afar wishes you success in exploring the world, and may you return home in glory. You will discover that the world becomes much more pleasant and welcoming. Thank you for your question, and may all the beauty in the world come to you as expected.

It's a bit incoherent and possibly too excitedly written. Whoever initiates physical violence is at fault. However, it is a grave mistake to use excessive force. I cannot imagine a father who can lay hands on his own son without considering the seriousness of the act. It is unfortunate that it seems you don't have the opportunity to reason with him or others. However, since you're already 27 and can support yourself, you don't need to care about anything, right?

Liu Feng's analysis: 1. Fighting. If you win, you go to jail; if you lose, you end up in the hospital. 2. Fighting itself is a harmful and self-destructive behavior. 3. Why does fighting happen? When talking doesn't solve the problem, people resort to physical violence. However, in reality, physical violence doesn't solve the problem, but instead exacerbates it. 4. When it comes to fighting, it takes two to tango. So the cause of fighting is not only one-sided, but both sides have their reasons and both need introspection. 5. How can we effectively prevent fighting? When someone wants to physically harm you, the best strategy is to quickly dodge and walk away. Without someone to fight against, a fight cannot occur. 6. You are younger than your father, and your reaction speed and agility are definitely higher than his. So when your father wants to hit you, you can quickly dodge and choose to walk away, which will prevent a fight. Without a fight, there will be no mutual harm.

question: How to persuade my father to quit smoking or reduce the frequency of smoking?
description: My father used to drink heavily when he was young, but he quit drinking after my grandmother passed away. However, he has been a long-term smoker, which has caused him to cough frequently recently. I am very worried because my grandmother died of lung cancer, and there have been many conflicts due to his smoking habit. My father is a very sensitive person. He often believes that when people around him laugh or chat, they are mocking or talking about him. Now, whenever I mention the issue of smoking, he gets angry. I don't know what to do anymore, and I want him to seek psychological counseling.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent-child communication, and sibling communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello, first of all, I can tell that you are a very filial child and are very worried about your father's health. If your father is already at a point where he gets angry at the mere mention of smoking, I think it is necessary to seek psychological counseling. Psychological counseling has a great power, and I believe that under the guidance of a professional counselor, your father's situation will improve. Here are my personal opinions, and I hope they can also be helpful to you: If your father gets angry at the mention of smoking, it means that he subconsciously believes that smoking is harmful to his health, and he may also want to quit but find it difficult. If that's the case, I think you don't necessarily have to directly tell him to quit smoking or only emphasize the negative effects of smoking. Instead, you can talk more about the benefits of quitting smoking, such as (1) even just one day without smoking, the benefits to the heart, blood pressure, and circulatory system will become apparent. After one year of quitting smoking, the excess risk of coronary heart disease decreases by half compared to continued smokers. (2) After 5 to 15 years of quitting smoking, the risk of stroke drops to the level of a non-smoker. There are also benefits after 10 or 15 years of quitting smoking, and you can mention them from time to time. If one day or one morning you notice that your father smokes less than usual, you can praise him. Encouragement is also needed for elders, and perhaps under your praise, he will smoke less the next day, gradually reducing it even more. In your writing, you mentioned that your grandmother passed away from lung cancer. On one hand, your father may be under too much stress due to grieving for his mother, and he may be using nicotine to numb himself. On the other hand, we all know that smoking harms the lungs the most. There is a symptom in psychology called "conversion disorder." You can consult a professional counselor about this, as I am still a student and cannot provide a more in-depth explanation. These are my suggestions, and I wish you and your family a happy and healthy life.

question: I have attempted suicide before, but failed. Now, my temper has become very irritable and unpredictable. I tend to enjoy being alone, avoiding social activities, and feeling overwhelmed easily. I often feel hopeless, restless, and have trouble sleeping.
description: I have attempted suicide before but didn't succeed. Now my temper has become very explosive and unpredictable. I prefer being alone and don't like communicating with others. Whenever I'm in a bad mood, no matter when or where, I engage in self-harm. I even have dreams about killing people. I feel very insecure and always keep a knife by my side. Is there something wrong with my mental health?

answers.answer_text: Dear questioner, at this moment you still feel pain. When we let the pain flow through our bodies, it will gradually nourish us, and perhaps in the future, we will gain a new strength from it. Don't forget that you can take a break, pause for a moment. Time is meant to be felt, and we still have time. When you're tired, take a rest.

question: Should there be privacy space in relationships between men and women?
description: After entering college, my girlfriend and I were separated by distance, and we would call and video chat multiple times every day. Recently, she asked me to provide her with my WeChat and QQ passwords, but I also want to have some personal space. So, should I give her my passwords or keep my privacy?

answers.answer_text: Hello. I saw your question. Should there be privacy space between boyfriend and girlfriend? The answer is yes. Not only between boyfriend and girlfriend, but even between spouses, there should be some privacy space. However, the boundaries in intimate relationships are often an issue that we easily overlook. It seems that when the relationship becomes closer, the space for privacy is squeezed. Otherwise, it is seen as mistrust or lack of honesty. But it is not like that. Privacy space is also our own space. A good relationship should be both intimate and independent. However, in your specific situation, you and your girlfriend are in a long-distance relationship, which can bring feelings of insecurity for both parties. The fact that you have multiple phone calls and video chats every day shows that you are trying to compensate for the feelings of insecurity in this way. However, it may not be enough for the girl, so she may expect more control, such as needing your WeChat password. You can discuss this part with her. How to lower her anxiety while preserving your personal space. This is an opportunity for both of you to face the reality together, whether it will increase trust and emotions between each other or destroy it, will depend on how you communicate. Alright. Best wishes to both of you.

Sharing passwords is merely symbolic, and you may need to have a deeper discussion about what your girlfriend really needs. Certainly, everyone needs their personal space, so normally, I think it's not a problem to share passwords once the relationship reaches a certain level of intimacy. Of course, not sharing is also your right. If sharing can make the other person feel more at ease, why not? If the other person feels at ease, they may not necessarily go snooping around your information. However, if after sharing, she accesses your information without your consent, that's a lack of trust and respect. This should be clarified before sharing, because a relationship without trust and respect is hard to sustain. Moreover, without trust and respect, giving out all your passwords is pointless. In long-distance relationships, it's normal for both partners to have insecurities and worries. How do you resolve them? 1)Both parties should try to actively share their daily or recent life and study situations, as well as some information about the people around them. Additionally, they can engage in proactive video calls. Here, I emphasize being proactive. 2)Avoid discussing uncertain or groundless matters to prevent causing unnecessary distress to the other person. 3)When the frequency of calls and video chats becomes too burdensome for your life and studies, sincerely communicate your feelings and find a mutually acceptable way to address the situation, rather than avoiding it. 4)If you are unable to respond to the other person in a timely manner, explain the possible circumstances and the expected response time in different situations, so that the other person is clear in advance. If you did not respond, it could be because you were... 5)Take the initiative to create opportunities to meet in person. 6)Try to remember and commemorate the special dates between the two of you, and remember to send greetings or gifts, even if it's just ordering takeout. 7)Express missing each other every day, affirm each other more, and give encouragement. 8)When the other person needs you, try to respond proactively. When you cannot fulfill a request, sincerely explain that you're unable to do so, without compromising your own well-being... In short, put in more effort, understand each other's needs, and let each other know your own boundaries. If you follow these basic principles, there shouldn't be any major issues. This is for your reference.

️**This is undoubtedly her control desire at work. Behind it may be her security issues. Of course, this may depend on the level of trust between you two or whether there have been any recent trust incidents. From the perspective of a marital relationship, in Sternberg's Love Triangle, passion, commitment, and intimacy are all particularly important in a romantic relationship. Therefore, to maintain a love relationship, it is necessary to consider these relevant factors. Trust is in the realm of commitment and requires mutual trust. This means there needs to be appropriate privacy space for emotions to last. ε I wish you well. I am here, the world and I love you.

Hello! I would like to share my thoughts on this matter and hope that it can help you! Reflection: Why does the other party want the password? Is it because there is not enough trust between each other, or do you lack a sense of security and want to demonstrate your importance through this, or is there another reason? Speak honestly about your thoughts and seek the underlying reasons behind the incident. Ask yourself: What is your bottom-line principle in this matter? If the attribution is inaccurate, there will still be other behavior that continuously expands boundaries. Principle-based freedom brings security and love!

question: Some issues are always heavily influenced by others, with unstable self-identity.
description: Recently, I have been lacking interest in my new job and feeling unsure about whether I am suitable for it. I feel confused and torn. A few days ago, a colleague casually said something that caught my attention. She said, "This job is not bad, at least it offers freedom, more freedom than being a regular teacher, and it's better in many aspects than being a school teacher." Upon hearing that, my interest in the job unexpectedly sparked. I felt that this job is indeed suitable for me and started to experience the enjoyment it brings. My mood has been extremely good these past few days. Ah, am I extremely unstable in terms of self-identification?
keywords: Growth, personality improvement, character traits, self-development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, how are you? Here, the host gives you a hug, which is also good for you. It helps you to adapt and comfort yourself in a timely manner. When facing a new job, the host is not interested and feels confused. You only take this job to make a living. The unintentional words of colleagues actually serve as guidance. Because you can't figure out or know what interests this job brings you. But the words from colleagues are like pointing the way, enlightening you and helping you find the interest in this job. At least it makes you feel good in the short term, and you have passion and motivation for this job. You can quickly accept it. Although you were initially uninterested in this job, you didn't resist it either. The words of colleagues also gave you an epiphany and comforted you, allowing you to quickly accept this job. If you had resisted this job from the beginning, no matter what your colleagues said, you wouldn't have liked this job. Even if you eventually got convinced, you would still reluctantly accept this job. Instead of reluctantly accepting it, it is better to take the initiative to accept it, comfort yourself, and be able to work efficiently. You can continue with this job until you find something you are interested in. Colleagues' words also provide a source of self-comfort. You don't reject this job, but you are not interested in it. You feel somewhat lost, and when doing the work, you just mechanically complete your tasks. "This job is pretty good, at least it's more flexible than being a regular teacher, and it's better in various aspects than being a school teacher." By comparing this job and putting yourself in a better frame of mind, you accept this job. Hobbies and interests don't necessarily have to be work-related. Hobbies and interests are developed in your free time. In that sense, this job is relatively free, and you have more time to develop your existing interests. From this perspective, your instability brings you more benefits, giving you motivation and eliminating the lack of interest in your work. If your instability continues to benefit you in important matters, then it's not a bad thing. As long as you're not indecisive about major decisions, it's all good.

question: Three years ago, when we added our ages together, we were 30 years old. I can't forget her, what should I do?
description: Three years ago, she started liking me because of an "accident". I felt both excited and nervous, not knowing what to do and feeling lost. I didn't understand what it meant to like someone. Time passed slowly, and we remained in this ambiguous state. On Halloween in eighth grade, she confessed her feelings to me. I rejected her, though I don't remember the reason. We continued in this ambiguous state, why did I reject her? Perhaps it was because I cared about her past, or maybe it was because of my own insecurities. Perhaps it was both. After the high school entrance exam, she confessed again. I truly don't know why, not even I myself know why I rejected her. It was as if I had become a different person. (I once thought maybe it was due to my self-protection.) Afterwards, we had no contact. I had a decent summer vacation. I thought I was heartless. But gradually, I began to think of her. During a gathering in my freshman year of high school, I got drunk and sent her an email, trembling as I typed it. After that conversation, I thought I had let go. But time still slapped me in the face, not heavily, but it hurt deep inside. Now, three years later, I'm thinking of her again, not like the prolonged pain in my sophomore year of high school. This time, the pain hits me directly in the heart, even affecting my normal studying. Why can't I forget her? What should I do? No matter how hard I try to avoid this pain, it still comes. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: After reading OP's confession, I deeply understand your pain of longing. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1 At the age of third grade of junior high school, both the inner emotional world and the external body are not that mature. Your love is also a bit confused, full of the awkwardness of puberty. Therefore, you rejected her, and you couldn't clearly explain the reasons behind it. As you said, it may be because you care about her past, or it may be your own self-doubt. 2 Your actions at that time were correct. Because love is like a tide. If the channel is not yet formed and the water comes first, it will flood and become a disaster. That will no longer be a sweet love. However, even though you rejected her, this relationship is deeply engraved in your heart. 3 You can't forget her, just like nobody can forget their first love. Jay Chou once said, the taste of first love is like a Pacific saury, both cats and you want to know. What is luxury? It is something we didn't care about in the past, but now we can no longer get it. When we lose it, we feel it is even more precious. What should we do to break free from this pain? That is to salvage this relationship or start a new love. Thank you for your question, and may all the goodness in the world come to you as expected.

question: It feels good to be alone at home, but when I go back to school, I feel like I've lost myself again.
description: These past two weeks, I've felt like I've lost myself again when I returned to school. It's really awkward in the dorm. When I wake up, my roommates are already sleeping and they close the curtains, making the room pitch black. At night, when they sleep and it's dark again, it's really annoying. I can't do anything, like skincare or applying face masks, in the dark. It's frustrating. Originally, our daily routines weren't that different, but now they're becoming more and more different. They only follow their own rhythms and it's so annoying. Plus, they wake up early in the morning to study. First of all, they talk loudly and wake me up several times. Secondly, their early morning studying makes me really anxious. I'm productive, but I just can't wake up early. It completely messes up my rhythm! It was nice being alone at home, but when I came to school, the overall noise from them was just too much. Some of them make exaggerated jokes and pretend to agree with everything. I don't even want to talk to them, but it feels disturbing. Sometimes, I have no choice but to listen and it's so annoying...
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and disagreements, roommates and classmates, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. The rhythm of your life with your roommates is different, and your own life is always disrupted by them, making you feel anxious and annoyed. This is the nature of living together as a group in a dormitory. It is easy to be influenced by them. Living on campus also requires tolerance for each other and the need to accommodate their lives, even if it may be involuntary. Let's discuss the issues you have encountered one by one. When you wake up, your roommate wants to take a nap and the room is pitch black. You can place a small desk lamp on your desk so that when you need to do something, you can turn on your own lamp. The light is not very strong, but it is enough for your makeup needs. Your roommate wakes up early in the morning to go to class. You can try to wake up early yourself, as it is also a good habit to sleep and wake up early. If you really can't wake up, you can discuss with them and ask them to be quieter when they leave in the morning. You feel that your well-organized life has been disrupted by them, and seeing them makes you feel annoyed. However, you can also try to integrate yourself with them. You can chat with them and you may find that your roommates are actually quite interesting. Being together with a group of people can also be enjoyable. But we must think in a positive direction. Living in a dormitory is inevitable in college. So we can only change our mentality and make ourselves happier in college life. Best wishes~.

question: The man said he wants a divorce, and he has always been passively resistant. What should I do?
description: I asked him how long he had been having these thoughts, and he said it had been around two to three years. I didn't bring up this idea with him before, and he has been passively resisting it all along. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello there~ In fact, the state of two people during the process of marriage will not always remain on the same frequency. There will always be fluctuations in emotions. Maybe over time, the things that attracted each other will gradually be lost to the trivialities of life. It is not someone's fault, but something that happens in every relationship. It will eventually return to being mundane. So, actually, you can calmly communicate with your partner, whether it's a passionate new person or not, you will always experience the same mundaneness again. Ask if there are any unacceptable issues in your marriage, if the two of you can overcome them, and if you can talk about them and solve them together. It sounds simple, but it is very difficult to do.

question: Difficulty concentrating while reading, eyes wandering, and an uncontrollable mind filled with scattered thoughts.
description: From the beginning of my sophomore year, I had trouble concentrating in class and couldn't really pay attention to the teacher's lectures. In my senior year, I started to have frequent daydreams and my mind would wander. I also kept thinking about negative things. Over the past year, I've noticed that my eyes seem unfocused, and when I read, the words start to blur. What is happening to me?

answers.answer_text:
After carefully reading your confession, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 
1. "What is wrong with me?" Judging from your symptoms, my conclusion may be that you have overexerted yourself. For example, not getting enough rest, lack of leisure activities, and not balancing work and rest. 
2. Each class is 45 minutes long, and there is a 10-minute break to relax. However, you use this time to do homework, read, and review notes. You haven't allowed your mind to rest and prepare for the next class. This results in your mind being constantly under tension without relaxation. 
3. Because your mind is under too much pressure, it starts to malfunction. The problem is lack of concentration, wandering thoughts, and even blurred vision when reading. Therefore, you need to learn to relax during breaks. Take a walk in the corridor, chat with classmates, and give yourself a break. Only then can you study more efficiently. Thank you for your question, and may all the goodness in the world come to you as planned.

question: Why do men make video calls on WeChat when talking to their parents?
description: Why do men make video calls on WeChat when talking to their parents, but only use voice calls when talking to their wives?

answers.answer_text: When children are young, they are afraid of their parents. As they grow older, they become afraid of their loved ones. This fear stems from the inconvenience it brings. Different perspectives lead to different expectations. To live a more comfortable life, one must hide various things. As one grows older, the control of parents diminishes, making it possible to video chat freely. However, it is different with loved ones. Various problems can arise from seeing the background through video chats. It may even spark arguments. It becomes difficult to hide even a small lie. Naturally, video chats need to be avoided. Sometimes, it is unnecessary to pay too much attention. It is important to give each other space.

question: Should you choose someone you like yourself or listen to your parents' opinions?
description: I am attracted to a 35-year-old man, but I am 22 years old. Is this not normal? My mother yelled at me today, saying that his family background is not good and that I only like him because I lack fatherly love. But that's not true. I feel like I lack happiness. I grew up in an environment of domestic violence and have always had poor mental health. He makes me happy and can always cheer me up. I have dated many people before, but it never worked out. I am very conflicted about what to do. I can't say that I love him, but I do really like him. I used to love someone very seriously, so now I can't love anyone else. But it would still be difficult for me to break up with him.

answers.answer_text: In love, age is not a problem. He is several years older than you, and that is not the key issue. However, your mother opposes your relationship because his family's financial situation is not good and she believes that you are attracted to him because you lack paternal love. While I don't know the specifics of his situation, based on your description, it seems that you grew up in an environment of domestic violence and it appears that your father has not treated you well and has engaged in violent behavior, am I right? Growing up in such a family environment, you may lack normal and sufficient paternal love, leading to an unhappy life and the inability to establish secure attachment patterns. Internally, you may have a certain longing for a father figure and paternal love that has never been satisfied. These unmet needs and attachment patterns remain hidden within you and, as you grow into adulthood, they influence your pursuit of intimate relationships and love. Many of us experience this, as the influence of our parents on us occurs unconsciously, and our perception and impression of our parents is also stored in our subconscious. When we search for a romantic partner, we unconsciously look for a reflection of our opposite-sex parents, namely our father or mother, and tend to choose a partner who is similar to them or has complementary characteristics in order to compensate for the absence of a parental role. Therefore, this older individual who can make you happy, provide a sense of maturity and reliability, and care for you, fulfills your inner need for paternal love. From this perspective, your mother's opinion is also reasonable. Although you mentioned that it is because you lack happiness, in fact, happiness is included in the feeling of reliability, attention, care, dependability, and safety. Regarding your statement that you can't love someone else, in addition to having been hurt in past relationships, the negative image established during your father's violent upbringing also affects your perception of and relationships with the opposite sex, hindering you from establishing healthy and normal intimate relationships with them. This aspect requires self-awareness on your part and understanding of your psychological state. As for your romantic relationship with this man, you need to understand what your true emotional needs are and if happiness is just one of them. In love and intimate relationships, there are more factors to consider. For example, what are his personality traits? What is his character like? Do your values align? Can you both respect, tolerate, and understand each other when you're together? If you plan to get married, you also need to consider his financial situation, future plans, and so on. Are you truly compatible? Can you accept and mentally prepare yourself for it? Age is indeed not the problem; the key is to consider multiple factors to see if they are suitable. Perhaps it sounds practical, but it is also to avoid discovering certain aspects that are incompatible or causing conflicts, or even emotional harm, after being together. I hope my answer can give you some inspiration. Best wishes.

Hello, based on your description, I would like to say that in matters of emotions, your own experience is the deepest and most genuine. Trust your inner feelings, after all, it's you who will spend the rest of your life with this person, not your parents. Perhaps your parents are concerned about your well-being and fear that you may suffer in the future. However, when it comes to the future, it is ultimately your own choice. Perhaps this person gives you a different feeling compared to your family environment, allowing you to experience something new. As long as you have enough confidence and strength in this person and in your future together, I believe you will find happiness. These are just my personal thoughts, and I hope they provide you with some guidance.

Hello! Loving someone is a personal matter, and marriage can become a matter of two families. Sometimes it is difficult to find a balance point. When both the left and right paths have problems, perhaps you can choose either left or right, or you can choose not to choose. Maybe you need to ask yourself what you really want. What will your choice bring you? Because this is your marriage, this is your life. A marriage with an age difference of more than ten years can be called a "cross-age marriage," which naturally brings some problems. When you are in your prime, he may age before you, his health may decline before yours, and the age difference may bring anxiety to the older party about the security and certainty of the marriage. These things may disrupt the quality and stability of the marriage, and these are things you need to consider. Here, let's try to step out of the question of whether to choose him and see what you really want. You described that you lack happiness and have been living in an environment of domestic violence, and you have always had poor mental health. You also mentioned that you used to love someone very sincerely, so you find it difficult to love someone else and it's hard for you to move on after the breakup. This may be an important reason for you to choose a cross-age marriage. Your psychological wounds have not healed, and it seems like you are unable to love. These can all be significant factors affecting the quality of your marriage. If you enter a cross-age marriage with these conditions, do you think it will be a good start? It should be acknowledged that some cross-age marriages are indeed filled with love and happiness. Compared to those marriages with an age difference of two or three decades, your situation can only be considered average in cross-age marriages. By asking questions and expressing that you are unable to feel love, you may be expressing your concerns about this marriage. Before entering the marriage, you may need to consider the possible impact of the factors mentioned above. Once you genuinely decide to enter into marriage, both of you should dedicate yourselves to managing the marriage well. A marriage that is jointly managed by both parties will be more reliable in quality.

#I like a 35-year-old man, I am 22, is that not normal?# It is your freedom and right to like a 35-year-old man at 22; from your personal perspective, there is no problem. #My mom yelled at me today, saying that his family conditions are not good.# Your mom pointed out an objective reality, his family conditions are not good. Dear OP, seeing your situation, I think although your boyfriend is a bit older, that is not a problem. The main thing is how your relationship develops. As long as you feel that you are suitable for each other and genuinely want to be together, then your mother's concerns will no longer exist. Take some time to quiet your mind and truly feel your emotions before making a decision. Wishing you all the best.

It is easy to be happy together, and often people in love think that being happy together is true love, and that they truly like each other. But real love often comes down to whether you can be unhappy together, whether you can face problems together. You are currently involved with a man who is 13 years older than you, he may like you and you like him too. But if you encounter real problems, can you face them together? Can you integrate into his world? What will be left after the passion fades? Can you face all the future challenges? Is he really worth entrusting yourself to? If all the answers are positive, then go ahead (it's your heart's answer, not what he tells you verbally). question: Female college senior, attributes success to external factors and failure to internal factors, how to change?
description: As mentioned above, when I achieve good results, I tend to attribute it to luck, the simplicity of the questions, or the lack of competition. However, when I fail, I tend to believe it is because of my own lack of ability. I am currently feeling very unhappy and have low self-esteem. How can I change this?

answers.answer_text:
Hello, I think you are a person who is very self-aware and seeks personal growth and self-improvement. Your question resonates with my state of mind during my junior and senior high school years, and at that time, I firmly believed that this kind of thinking was correct. I remember one time when I did well on a test, the teacher asked me to share my experience on stage. I said, "This time was just luck, maybe I'll do poorly next time." The teacher was very angry after hearing this. In fact, you are much better off than I was at that time because I never doubted that my belief was wrong and never had the idea of wanting to change. Since you mentioned internal and external attributions, let me talk to you about Weiner's attribution theory: Weiner's theory consists of three dimensions and four factors. The three dimensions are: locus of control (internal attribution + external attribution), controllability (controllable + uncontrollable), and stability (stable + unstable). The four factors are: 
- Ability - stable internal attribution
- Effort - unstable internal attribution (controllable)
- Task difficulty - stable external attribution (uncontrollable)
- Luck - unstable external attribution (uncontrollable)
When there is success, attributing it to internal factors generates a sense of pride and increases motivation, while attributing it to external factors creates a sense of luck and reduces the feeling of success. Attributing failure to internal factors leads to guilt, while attributing it to external factors leads to anger. Attributing success to stable factors generates a sense of pride, while attributing it to unstable factors creates a sense of luck. Attributing failure to stable factors leads to despair, while attributing it to unstable factors leads to anger. Attributing success to controllable factors motivates further effort, while attributing it to uncontrollable factors does not generate much motivation. Attributing failure to controllable factors leads to continued effort, while attributing it to uncontrollable factors leads to despair. I think a good attribution style can enhance self-efficacy and increase motivation, creating a positive psychological state for future learning and life. Of course, this does not mean that success should be attributed to internal factors and failure to external factors. I believe it is more important to focus on the controllable components, as individuals have different attitudes towards ability, which can be divided into a growth mindset and a fixed mindset. Having a fixed mindset is more conducive to personal development. Analyzing the psychology behind attributing success to external factors and failure to internal factors: 
1. Early education and environmental influence with immature educational concepts, promoting modesty and suppressing pride and self-confidence, have a significant impact on current attribution styles. Moreover, your current attribution style may be reinforced and supported by people around you.
2. It is essentially due to self-doubt and the belief that one is not good enough. Although you did not specify the specific internal and external factors, I believe you see both internal and external factors as stable, unchangeable, and uncontrollable.
3. Maintaining self-worth and self-esteem. When success is attributed to internal factors, the underlying psychological belief may be that because it is an internal factor, I should succeed next time as well, otherwise others will mock me and I will perceive myself as lacking ability. Therefore, I believe that my success is accidental, so even if I fail next time, it will not affect my sense of self-worth. When failure is attributed to internal factors, the underlying psychology may be that because my ability itself is not good enough, that's why I failed. If it were due to lack of effort, it would be a moral judgment, while lack of intelligence is not. Alternatively, it could be because I didn't put in enough effort that I failed, and if I make an effort, I will surely succeed, rather than believing it's because I lack ability. The specific reason may vary from person to person and may require further exploration on your part. As for how to change, firstly, you can learn about various attribution theories, as well as self-efficacy and the growth mindset, through the internet or professional books. Then, have a clear understanding of your current state. Secondly, accept yourself in this state instead of blaming or excluding yourself. Then, reflect on the benefits you have gained from your current attribution style, which are the underlying psychological motives that lead you to continue using this kind of attribution. Finally, believe that you can make a change, and believe in your own courage to withstand the discomfort or pain that change may bring. In other words, you can reattribute past experiences and consciously attribute future events. Of course, it will be uncomfortable and you may struggle at first, but don't doubt yourself. What matters is not how many times you fall, but how many times you get back up. What matters is not where you are, but the direction you are heading in.

Hello, in your narrative, it seems that you are not willing to give yourself a high evaluation, or it seems that giving yourself a negative evaluation will make you feel more secure. The idea of "attributing success to external factors and attributing failure to internal factors" must have its meaning in your life. You are willing to maintain this kind of self-denial pain, and relatively speaking, it will bring you something. If you can notice this part of yourself, perhaps you can find better ways to change or replace it. I am an assistant to Teacher Hui Ming, and I would like to send you a message from Teacher Chen: "Having lived in the city for a long time, I still long for the tranquility and serenity of the countryside. I enjoy the peaceful time of reading books and also love the feeling of sweating on the sports field. I enjoy the pleasure of finishing a full 40-kilometer marathon. However, only after traveling to dozens of countries in Asia and Europe and experiencing various local customs, did I realize that my home is in the depths of my soul, the most beautiful and warmest haven. And, through experiencing the ups and downs of life and reading about various aspects of human society, only the inner self is the source of vitality in life, the harbor of peace."

How can this be changed, you have already mastered a very important mindset. This mindset will benefit you greatly in your future life. Really. It will help you make more progress and achievements. Do you think about it, turning yourself into an arrogant and self-centered college student, someone who is disliked. No way, you are fine as you are. Because this mindset has been instilled in you since childhood, hoping that you will become successful. You cannot lose, you must always win. So you often put too much pressure on yourself, and you are constantly on guard against others. Always trying to surpass others but finding it difficult to do so. In fact, those of us who have come to realize this now know that success first requires understanding oneself, finding one's own abilities, not always thinking about exclusive competition, but cooperation and win-win situations. The scenery on the sunny road and on the single-plank bridge both have their own beauty, one is not better than the other. Then you become yourself, become yourself on the future path of life, which may bring you many temptations. You may quickly achieve the goal of becoming someone else, like the current trend of counterfeits, clones, and plagiarism, which can bring overnight fame, but those things do not belong to you and will only burden you. Finally, it is about surpassing yourself. Sometimes, I think surpassing oneself is already an ideal situation. Adults being enthralled by games is actually a form of spiritual escapism, the number of people who can truly surpass themselves in society is truly rare, so it is better to consider becoming oneself as already a success.

question: 17-year-old girl, why do I always have some inexplicable possessiveness?
description: It is clear that we are just friends. However, I don't like it when he (she) jokes around with other people, as I always feel abandoned. And when they have someone else, I feel sad and upset. I will slowly distance myself from him. Slowly cut off all contact with him. But deep down, I still can't let go. What is the reason behind it all? I wonder. It seems that every person I accept into my life will eventually have someone else. They forget about me, no longer need me. Or maybe I feel like I am just an extra person.

answers.answer_text: Well, you are very concerned about relationships and afraid of losing them. The feeling of being abandoned is a very devastating feeling, even though it won't actually happen. Perhaps these feelings have a deeper history. In previous relationships, there was a lack of solid trust. It's quite a profound issue. It is very meaningful and valuable for you to be able to feel and express these things. Don't rush, take your time to observe the changes in the relationship, don't rush to escape (try to stay in place, afraid of getting hurt, you can set boundaries between yourself and others, what you can give and what you can't give, only give what you can give comfortably without hurting yourself), and don't rush to give too much to the other person (sometimes, a person who fears losing a relationship may also compromise themselves).

question: How to alleviate work and study stress? I hope to have specific answers.
description: Can you analyze the causes of stress from a psychological perspective? I really want to solve these problems for myself and the people around me. Thank you...

answers.answer_text: Let's not talk about the definition of stress. Stress is everywhere in life, but I believe that you must have had moments when you didn't feel any stress while doing something. There must be differences between those moments and the times when you feel a lot of pressure at work or in school. These differences are the directions in which you think and face stress. You mentioned wanting to solve these problems for people around you, which shows that you are a very caring person. However, you need to know that everyone perceives stress differently. What you think is a lot of pressure may not be the same for others, and what you think is no pressure may be overwhelming for others. Additionally, the methods you find effective in relieving stress may not necessarily work for others. You can consider ways to help people around you release stress, such as venting, talking, exercising, etc.

Hello, OP, give you a thumbs up for thinking so much. Stress, that love-hate buddy of ours. Let's first take a look at the definition of stress. Stress is a cognitive and behavioral experience process formed by the combination of psychological stressors and psychological stress responses. In simple terms, stress is a negative feeling and negative belief that a person experiences when they feel unable to cope with environmental demands. It seems that stress is usually associated with negative emotions and negative beliefs. When negative emotions transform into positive emotions and negative beliefs turn into positive beliefs, stress can turn into motivation. Here, you mainly want to understand how stress is formed in studying and working, and how to effectively relieve it. From the definition of stress, we know that when our performance is lower than the demands of the environment, that is, our performance fails to meet the requirements of the environment, we may experience negative emotions such as doubt, embarrassment, shame, and develop negative beliefs like "I'm not good enough" or "I am a failure". So how to effectively relieve stress? Either improve our abilities or reduce/change the demands of the environment on us. Clearly, enhancing our own abilities is a proactive method that promotes positive cycles. Best wishes.

question: Can music with alpha waves really help in the treatment of depression?
description: Would playing music with alpha waves while sleeping at night help with depression?

answers.answer_text: Hello~ According to research abroad, it has been found that listening to alpha wave music can keep the brain awake and relaxed, improve concentration, stabilize emotions, and enhance memory, focus, creativity, and imagination. It also has helpful effects in treating insomnia. Therefore, from this perspective, alpha wave music can play a supportive role in treating depression. During your leisure time, you can relax a bit by listening to music in this way and keep your mood calm. The recovery process of depression may be lengthy, so it requires a lot of patience. But we must believe that eventually we will come out of that shadow. Don't feel bad about yourself or think that you have done something wrong. You are really good; you just have a little psychological cold. So let's wait together for this little cold to get better. Regardless of what makes you happy in your daily life or the people who make you happy, spend more time with them.

question: Are the strange thoughts and suffocating feeling before the exam a psychological problem?
description: The exam is important to me, but because my previous registration photo was strange, I asked the teacher to help me replace it. Now I am constantly worried that there might be a problem with the registration system, even though I have already paid the registration fee. However, my name is listed on the final registration list announced by the teacher. Am I having a mental problem? I hope everyone can provide some answers.

answers.answer_text: Hello there~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug~ Having strange thoughts before an exam is probably because this exam is important to you, so you may feel some anxiety. This is a fairly normal phenomenon and not a psychological problem. It is unnecessary to worry about the registration system malfunctioning because the chances of such an event happening are almost zero. Even if there is a problem, it is not your fault and there is nothing you can do about it. The fact that everything is going fine indicates that your worries are somewhat unnecessary. The key is to adjust your mindset and face the exam with a calm and composed attitude. Before the exam, it's good to relax a bit and review the exam content. Have reasonable expectations for yourself and tell yourself that as long as you perform normally, it's okay. Don't focus too much on things that you can't change. Engaging in some relaxation meditation exercises will be helpful. Believe that everything will go smoothly. Best wishes~

Dear, you don't have any issues, it's all very normal psychology! Just like how some people get stomachaches when they're nervous, you don't need to worry. When thoughts come, embrace them kindly and say thank you to them. Tell them they must be here to help me, to love me, and to transform any thoughts into positive ones. Imagine thoughts as light, dissolving in sunlight. No matter what thoughts they are, they come because they love you, and you have no issues, you are very healthy. Gently tell yourself, I am fine. Right now, what you need to focus on is being present. When any distractions come, dissolve them and turn them into motivation for your studies. Love you, wish you well. Allow the appearance of thoughts, it's all very normal phenomena.

question: High school, do you want to be selfish and not face your middle-aged and elderly self? Do you want to live selfishly until the age of 30?
description: I am a high school student, and my school life is very happy. My grades are not bad. My parents are in a same-sex marriage, and I come from a large family where I don't have to inherit or take on any responsibilities (I also don't have much to inherit). I don't have any psychological disorders, and my mood is very stable. I don't empathize with my parents. I have friends that I keep in contact with both at school and outside of school. I don't have any financial problems in my family. I have never encountered anyone that I like romantically. I want to buy life insurance at an early age. I want to live alone, have a cat, take exams, study the major I'm interested in at university, and then pursue postgraduate and even doctoral studies. I want to be financially independent and ultimately die at around the age of 30. I don't want any accidents to disrupt my plans. I don't want to face my middle-aged or elderly self, get married, or have children. I don't want to see my former teachers or classmates. I want to remain young forever, but I also want to experience something beyond that.
keywords: Growth, development patterns, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Sometimes, some of a person's thoughts may seem nonsensical and without reason on the surface, but if examined closely, the underlying subconscious can be revealed. Just like with physical health, many people believe they are in good health, but few can truly be considered healthy, as there are various minor issues. Minor psychological issues are even harder to detect and are often misunderstood or misinterpreted. Your current thoughts do not seem to indicate a positive and healthy psychological state. You express a desire to die at the age of 30 and to remain young forever. Freud's psychoanalytic theory identified the concept of fixation, which suggests that if a person's needs are not met during a specific stage of psychological development, they will be unable to move on to the next stage in a normal manner. You mentioned that your parents have a "marriage of convenience," which may suggest that they have little emotional attachment to the institution of marriage and may not provide you with enough love and care. This could lead to your unfulfilled longing for love and a desire to remain in a youthful state. The state of your parents' marriage has also exposed you to the unhappy side of marriage, causing you to avoid facing the adult world and wishing to die at the age of 30. These are all speculations based on your description, and the specific reasons will need to be discovered and realized by yourself. I wish you the ability to discover your true self, the hidden self beneath consciousness.

①Living alone in college, raising a cat, taking exams, studying the major you love, and even pursuing a master's or a PhD, achieving financial independence, all of these are absolutely possible. However, as young people, we are most passionate about planning. I also really like it. When I decided to ride a bicycle to school every day to exercise, it often rained during that time. You must be mentally prepared for accidents, but there are solutions to accidents, and if you are determined, you can achieve them. ②I know that you are full of enthusiasm now, thinking that it would be great to live a passionate life. I used to be the same, happy and carefree. The reason why I don't want to grow old in middle age is because it is completely different from the present life, and it is scary because it is unknown. But later I found out that plain and simple life is also happy, and different lives have different flavors, just like being in your teens or thirties. And for the age of 30, I can almost guarantee that you won't do that. Because when you really reach the age of 30, you won't bear to say, "I have never met someone I like" in high school, it's still early, it doesn't mean that everyone has already paired up in school, and you have missed out. When you truly meet that person, you will cherish them even more. It's not just about meeting the person you like, it's the same with many other things, you just haven't met them yet. 30 is different from being a teenager, but don't you really want to experience it? You have perfect plans, an independent personality, maybe your life right now is exciting, and you handle your friendships with ease. But don't you want to know what you will be like after 30? You don't have to think about it so far away right now. When that day comes, what you want to do, you will naturally do it as your heart desires.

During junior high school, I used to believe that living until the age of 30 was the maximum limit of life that I could accept. I even made a pact with my friends on how to leave this world at the age of 29. Now that I am 40 years old, I am still living without any purpose, and I think I will probably live for a long time. Of course, those friends of mine are all living exciting lives. Qian Xuantong, a writer in the Republic of China, once angrily said, "A person should die at 40, and if not, they should be executed." He said this too early and later he probably forgot, but his friends did not forget. On September 12, 1927, Qian Xuantong celebrated his 40th birthday. In response to Qian Xuantong's past bragging, Hu Shi gathered a group of well-known literati, including Zhou Zuoren, to plan a special issue of the magazine "Yu Si" titled "Qian Xuantong's First Step Towards Becoming a Benevolent Person". When Qian Xuantong turned 41, Hu Shi sent him a song. He said, "You are now 41 years old, and I have made a commemorative song for the anniversary of our deceased friend Qian Xuantong's journey towards becoming a benevolent person. I hope you will like it." In the end, Qian Xuantong passed away suddenly from a cerebral hemorrhage at the age of 52. If it weren't for his sudden illness, Qian Xuantong would still be leading a purposeless life. After all, at that time, he was living quite comfortably. From the description given by the topic creator, according to secular standards, it can be considered as a relatively good life. However, it feels like there is a hole in your heart, an empty hole that you don't know how to fill and you don't want others to step into. I think the biggest problem lies in your original family. You mentioned that your parents had a sham marriage, and you don't empathize with them. With this kind of family relationship, coupled with a sensitive personality, it is very easy to develop hidden depression. It's like watching someone smiling, but deep inside they are in extreme pain. I suggest that the topic creator seek counseling from a psychologist. Seeking psychological counseling is not only for those with mental illnesses. The world loves and cares about you.

question: I don't want to burden others anymore, I'm really tired, and I want to commit suicide.
description: I hope someone can give me a painless way to commit suicide. I don't want to burden others anymore. I'm really scared and tired. I'm afraid of being ridiculed by others, afraid of the disappointed looks from teachers and parents. I constantly trouble others and burden them. I really don't want to live anymore. I want to be a good student, but I can't do it. I also thought about being a bad student, but I can't even do that. I don't want to let them down. I'm tired, living is really exhausting. I don't even have goals or ideals. I don't know what kind of person I am. It's so tiring, really tiring. Can you please tell me a painless suicide method? I don't want to burden others anymore.

answers.answer_text: "#A sentence for the disheartened# Have you ever stored memories in an object? For example, storing a beautiful memory on a train ticket. Keep this ticket, and when you see it in the future, you will recall those days. You can also seal away unpleasant memories in an item, like a small glass bottle. Write down this experience, put it in the bottle, and use a permanent marker to write 'Open on November 25, 2029'."

You can choose a special day and do something that has a sense of ritual. After doing it, treat it as if you have already died once. From then on, every day is the second chance to live. This time, live for yourself without caring about others' expectations and take a good look at this world. If you still cannot control yourself, you can call the 95 Hope Hotline for help.

question: 20-year-old sophomore girl, struggling to tolerate her roommate's behavior, how should she adjust?
description: We have a close relationship and usually eat together during class. She often falls asleep during class and doesn't take notes. When she wakes up, she looks at mine. It happens too frequently. When she needs to look up the meaning of a word, she doesn't use her own phone and asks me first. If I don't know, she asks me to look it up. It really affects my concentration in class. She likes to argue with me or speak in a confrontational manner, and I'm afraid to refuse her. It makes me frustrated every time I attend class. How should I adjust?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, conflicts and disputes, roommates and classmates.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, it can be seen that you have a close relationship with your roommate. The advantage of this "grouping together" feeling is having a companion, but the relationship should be equal and have boundaries. Some of your roommate's behaviors sound like a needy baby and a bossy master. This clingy and unequal relationship not only violates your psychological boundaries, making you feel angry and annoyed, but also a form of psychological exploitation and control, making you feel powerless and exhausted. Recommendation: Learn to set boundaries for yourself. When the other person makes unreasonable demands, learn to refuse. Refusing requires inner strength, so when you clearly feel angry but cannot refuse, it is because you have fear. Therefore, try to first return to your own inner self and become aware of what fear is present within you at this moment. Seeing the fear, allows you the possibility to resolve it and gain the power to refuse. Try expressing your true feelings to the other person. For example, when you ask me to look up words for you, I feel very distressed because agreeing to your request would affect the quality of my own listening in class, but if I refuse, it will make you unhappy. I hope next time you can look them up by yourself.

Hello, it is evident that you have a lack of security. In this group relationship, you have always been in a weaker position, unable to refuse, afraid that refusing will break the relationship and afraid of being alone. Your relationship is imbalanced, with you always accommodating her, and she takes your kindness for granted. This unbalanced relationship makes you feel uncomfortable. A healthy relationship should be equal, and both parties should feel comfortable together, being able to express themselves without suppressing their thoughts because of the other person's needs. If you want to change, start by refusing one of her requests, such as asking her to look up words herself, and see how she reacts. If she is unhappy with your refusal, you may need to reconsider your relationship. Dare to express your thoughts and feelings instead of suppressing yourself and seeking approval from others. If you don't speak up, others will never know what you are thinking. Don't assume that just because our relationship is good, she will understand what I'm thinking. Additionally, don't limit yourself to just one friend, focus on personal growth and make more friends. I hope my answer can help you.

Let's break it down: not being able to refuse—establishing bottom-line thinking—establishing a countermeasure against others' offenses. It is important for students to establish bottom-line thinking. At the very least, friends should be the icing on the cake, not disturb your studies. So, what is your definition of a friend? Can you accept a friend who challenges you, disturbs you, but can also stick together with you? No matter who it is, we all need to have a bottom line, which is not allowing others to maliciously degrade us and trample on our dignity. If someone does so, you need to apply your wisdom and either explicitly counterattack or quietly distance yourself. Changing her behavior towards you, we don't need to save anyone's soul. You are all adults, and she has her own thoughts, but we can change her behavior towards you. The best way to handle her without losing face is to firmly and gently tell her your feelings, telling her she can ask you questions after class (without disturbing you), and telling her you don't like how she challenges others. If she still doesn't understand, then next time, you can sit one seat away from her. This way, you can put pressure on her behavior while maintaining a range where you can control how you present yourself. Your fear of refusing others or expressing your own opinions to some extent indicates that your self-personality needs further improvement. So, you can practice the feeling of connecting with others with anyone you have the chance to interact with, and practice the self-value and self-feeling you get from interpersonal relationships. And she is a good choice. If you see her as a personal trial, would you still be afraid to express your own opinions? Enjoy the time alone, develop other friends, and engage in activities like running and reading. I wish you a good college life.

Today, you talked about your relationship with your roommate, which has reached an unbearable point. I feel sorry for you, who have always compromised for the sake of friendship. You have worked hard in this relationship. How should you adjust? I don't know either, perhaps comforting yourself with a few words like: "How big of a deal is it? Let it go. Forget about it." Then have a good meal and a good night's sleep. The sun will rise as usual tomorrow, and the unhappiness in your heart may dissipate. But what I'm afraid of is that it won't be long before your roommate creates trouble for you again... "A stitch in time saves nine," establishing personal boundaries is especially important.
