They also make us wonder if we should live up to others' expectations, which is worth exploring and can inspire us to rethink the meaning of life. Thank you!

If she continues to disregard your feelings, you can distance yourself from her. The premise of having a deep friendship is feeling comfortable when together. Perhaps you are afraid of rejecting her because you don't want to strain your relationship, and that's understandable. However, if a friend causes you a lot of trouble and it seriously affects your classes, it may not be worth it. What do you think? Best wishes!

Simply put, there is a roommate who always annoys you and even argues with you. Although you are unhappy about it, you dare not show it and continue to maintain a close relationship with her. question: Why is the impression of first love so deep?
description: Not only me, but several of my friends are also like this, as if we have been cursed.

answers.answer_text: First love is pure for everyone. Most people take their first relationship seriously, so it leaves a deep impression. First love is a beautiful term that encompasses many wonderful things, so it leaves a deep impression. It may not be the best or the most beloved, but the past beauty is truly unforgettable, so it leaves an especially deep impression!

question: What can I do if there is nothing to support me and I have no motivation or hope?
description: I have no motivation to live anymore, and I don't know what I want. There is nothing to sustain me. One by one, my friends around me have been diagnosed with mental problems, but they are not themselves anymore once they start taking medication. I always feel like I won't live until graduation, and everyone just makes my life worse. I went to a temple to ask for a divination, and the result was bad. My first reaction was that it's good, that something should happen quickly to make me die. With the current state I am in and the upcoming pressure, it feels like I can only rely on medication to keep me alive. However, I don't have enough income, and my parents strongly oppose me seeing a doctor and getting treatment because "being diagnosed with issues will affect future job applications." I don't even know what I mean to them. As long as there's a breath left in me, it doesn't matter how broken I become mentally, right?
keywords: Emotions, depressed mood, emotion regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Give you a warm, long embrace... Parents may focus more on the future, they have you in their hearts, that's why they consider your future. It's like someone with depression, outsiders cannot truly empathize, we need to understand that. They may not understand the extent of your current situation. Based on their own experience, they know that finding a job and working are important to you. They can ensure that you live longer and go further. For most people, they cannot see or experience the mental and psychological problems, they can only see concrete realities, so naturally they believe those are more important. Are you still a college student? Do you know how much time and money your parents have invested in you from the moment you were born until now? Have you thought about it? What will happen to them if you decide to end your life? Have you considered that? How will you repay the debt you owe them? Is it really true that everyone is only making your life worse? Why do you have the right to let others interfere and influence your life? What about yourself? Have you helped yourself to live a better life? I can see that you have. It's just that your abilities and strength are not enough. It's worth considering going to see a doctor, actually, you don't really want to die, you want to live, and you want to live better. Your friends around you may have given you negative feedback, further deepening your concerns about yourself. In fact, you're afraid of being like them, you want to be different from them. I know, in your current state, every day and every moment is difficult for you, I'm not sure why you have reached this point, but there must be some reason, can you think about it? When did your connection with your parents weaken? How are your relationships with friends and classmates? Is there something you want to do? Are there any dreams you haven't fulfilled? Interact more with people and things, establish connections, and naturally you'll find more support and energy. You're not only living in the present, you're also living in the future, subconsciously worried about the future. You haven't even reached the future yet, how do you know it will be filled with stress? If you're not afraid of death, why are you afraid of future pressure? Strive to live, live well, the future you will definitely thank the present you! I also want to see the future you.

Don't worry, parents' thoughts are always so simple and rough. They only care about whether you can survive or not. It's already 9012, and you can make money to support yourself by doing anything casually, right? Don't pay attention to their old-fashioned mindset. It's okay to have mental problems. Who isn't anxious nowadays? I am 28 now without a job, partner, or children. I am also so anxious that I am about to die. Even a few years ago, I was depressed to the point of almost jumping off a building. At that time, I didn't know why I was alive. My work was unsatisfactory, my father was abusive, even after divorcing, my mother only complained about my father and criticized me. As a child, I couldn't argue with her or change her thoughts, actions, or words. I was in great pain and got stuck in my own thoughts. But one day, I suddenly emerged from my stuck thoughts—I thought, if it was the end of the world, and all of humanity was extinct, leaving only me, without parents, partners, children, jobs, bosses, or even ecological environments with animals and plants, what should I live for? Yes, at that time, I should live for myself! Anyway, living, isn't it all about living for the sake of living? This is the most basic thing. Life is long, we can slowly find the reason to keep ourselves alive. If we want to live an advanced life, don't we all have to find that reason to survive and make it our driving force to keep going? Of course, before finding it, we should keep striving to live!

question: Is it appropriate for a parent to prioritize cooking for their adult child and neglecting their work?
description: I am a mom, and I go to work. My child eats takeout at home. Sometimes, in order to personally cook for my child, I will postpone work because I think takeout is not hygienic, and my child does not spend much time at home due to school. However, my behavior always puzzles my child. They believe that they are independent already, and my actions are overly doting. They strongly oppose me postponing work to cook. Should I follow myself or listen to my child's advice?
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between children, and family health.

answers.answer_text: Thank you for the invitation! Based on your description, let me respond point by point. I go to work, and the child eats takeout at home. This is the current situation, after multiple adjustments and compromises. It may sound fine, but there are countless problems underneath. Perhaps after hearing my understanding, you will think in reverse: Wow! This is actually the best arrangement and state at present. 🤔🤗Line 2⃣️ - Sometimes, in order to personally cook for the child, I will postpone work because I feel that takeout is not hygienic, and the child does not spend much time at home due to school. - "Mother's perspective" • You are willing to sacrifice your work time for the sake of the child. That is very thoughtful. • When the child is not at home, you want to cook something delicious for them. This is your way of showing love to the child. It seems that you put him first in all relationships during his growth process. This is the mother-child relationship, this is how you love him. "Neutral speculation from the child's perspective" • Takeout is not hygienic. This is common knowledge, and the child knows it, too. But, it is their choice. They have their own reasons and needs for choosing it. The nutritional value of food is seemingly objective, but it is also subjective psychological needs. Some people, when they are bored, like to lick ice cream and feel happy. Some people really love instant noodles and spicy snacks, even though they have the means to have fancy hotel food every day, but it reminds them of their childhood. The child's taste and dietary habits have their own needs and preferences. If you understand what kind of takeout they like, what kind of flavors they enjoy, rather than simply saying, "You should eat what I cook, it is more nutritious," it may be easier for you to understand the child and make them happy with their meals. Just as no two chefs can make exactly the same taste, no two people have exactly the same taste. The food you cook is delicious and nutritious, and they like it. But they also have the freedom to choose takeout. 🤗Line 3⃣️ - my actions always confuse the child. He thinks he is independent and my actions are too indulgent, and he strongly opposes me postponing work because of cooking. - The child needs to grow and become independent, but the mother can't let go. You can remember what he says and write it down, but your heart is still attached. I think your child also remembered the reasons why you cook, but there is also some resistance in his heart. This is what you called "the child's confusion." 🤗Line 4⃣️ - Should I follow myself or listen to my child's advice? - Stick to both of them. Possible methods include: 1. Make simple meals without affecting work. Whether it's steamed rice or cooking a dish they love, just one is enough, you don't have to cover everything, and then let them have the opportunity to order their favorite takeout as a supplement. The key point is to help you continue cooking nutritious meals for them without affecting your work. 2. Exposure therapy, simply stop cooking and eat takeout with your son every day. See for yourself what makes this not nutritious takeout so delicious, and ask your child why they like ordering from a particular restaurant, what do they like about it? It can help you understand their psychological state and preferences when ordering food even more. 🤗Return to the initial state at the beginning - I am a mother, I go to work, and the child eats takeout at home. - In various situations where you can't move, the state you initially mentioned is the best. You have done what you wanted to do for your son, and after complaining, he lessens his guilt and throws it back at you, making him think that it is your indulgence that hinders his growth. And that's true. How could you support and acknowledge his "ordering takeout" when you don't truly understand what he likes? Of course, he needs to compromise and listen to your traditional opinions on "nutritious" food, and reluctantly eat it. How can he grow without the freedom to choose? Thank you for your effort and love as a mother. Although sometimes, letting go is another form of love, it carries pain, making us unable to resist the urge to intervene. That's all.

You are confused between taking care of your child and working. I understand you, as I have also been confused about this. At this moment, I even remember a time when I was studying outside and my child was in the hospital receiving an IV drip. I skipped the long-awaited class with a professional teacher and hurriedly rushed back home. At that moment, I chose to be a mother. In life, we have many roles, we hurry through them, experiencing both joy and exhaustion, walking through each role with stumbling steps, and sometimes not knowing what to do. Perhaps, this is life, full of choices, whether we like it or not. Returning to the situation at hand, I don't know the age of the child, but it seems he has already seen and felt how difficult it is for you. When he feels capable, choose to believe in him, okay? Maybe he needs us to let go and give him the opportunity to grow. Although it is not easy. We may feel guilty compared to other parents and other children. We may blame ourselves when he walks slower towards independence than others. Letting go is also an act of love, as the parent-child relationship is destined to be a journey that gradually distances itself. Love is strength, not weakness. We can never give our children something we don't have. Believe in him, and bless him with strength, okay? As a mother who loves her child, I am here. The world and I love you.

Hello, it seems like the discussion is about the balance between work and children, as well as the differences in values between two generations. However, I would like to share my understanding from the perspective of parent-child communication. As a mother, I understand your love for your children and the sacrifices you make for their well-being, even if they don't understand it. You show restraint and do not express your feelings of being hurt. From your perspective, "what you want to give your child is not just a meal, but compensation from a mother who is away from home. Takeout lacks nutrition and the warmth of a home. What you want to give your child is the 'taste of a mother.'" Perhaps as your child spends more time away from home and grows older, he/she will come to appreciate and deeply miss his/her mother's care. I also understand your child's perspective. At his/her age, he/she longs for independence, their own space, and the ability to take care of their own life. This is more important to them than what they eat, because it brings them a sense of empowerment. Work brings them a sense of value, and they will feel grown-up, capable of leaving the warmth of home, and taking on social responsibilities. Your child is very mature. According to psychological theories of personality development, at his/her age, the developmental task is to move from the family to society. At your age, the developmental task is to gradually face the reality of your child becoming an adult and enrich your own life. In fact, it is not easy for both the child and the parent, and both need to adapt. There are no right or wrong ways to love. There is a saying that only a child who has been warmed by love can become independent. It is only with plenty of love that a child can communicate so openly with you. As parents, we always need to consider our child's needs. Long Yingtai has written about the mixed feelings a mother experiences when seeing her child off, and only parents who deeply love their children can understand it. It is said that the relationship between fathers and daughters and mothers and sons only means that your connection with him/her will continue throughout this lifetime as you constantly watch them walk away. You stand at one end of the path, watching as he gradually disappears around the bend, and he silently tells you with his back: "There's no need to chase after me." - Long Yingtai, "Watching as he Leaves".

Hello, dear OP~ I totally understand how you feel. It's clear that you are torn between work and cooking for your child, and I can sense the deep concern you have for your child's health as a mother. Actually, many moms, just like you, always prioritize their children above everything else. A mother's love for her child is instinctive; no matter where they are or what they are doing, their child is always in their thoughts. I know a lot of moms who have quit their jobs and chosen to be stay-at-home moms, dedicating their time and energy to taking care of their children's lives and education. Moms always worry that their children won't eat well or be warm enough. They worry about not being around to take care of their children and feel the need to do everything themselves. I understand the emotions of being a mom, but as children grow up, there are certain things they need to face on their own. Moms can't be by their side forever, and they will have to rely on themselves as they walk their own paths in the future. [You would postpone work because you believe take-out food is unsanitary.] Compared to homemade meals, take-out food is indeed less sanitary, but you have your own job and can't take care of everything every day. Postponing work to cook for your child is not a long-term solution. [Your behavior has caused your child's unhappiness, as they believe they are already independent.] Your child is already an adult and has their own opinions and thoughts. They need to learn to live independently. From your description, it's clear that your child has a sense of independence and understands how to be considerate towards their parents without overly depending on them. Before reaching adulthood, children lack the ability to take care of themselves, and there are many aspects that require their parents' care and help. But once they become adults, children have grown up, and as parents, we need to slowly let go and give them space to grow freely. You can teach your child how to cook some simple and easy dishes, as they will have their own lives in the future, and knowing how to cook will be very helpful. The time you don't spend working can be used to make a delicious meal for your child. With more time available, you won't be hurried or stressed because of work afterwards, and your child will be more receptive. I wish you can overcome your worries, give your child some space, and reduce your own stress~.

Hello~ I noticed a key piece of information, which is that your child has come of age. Being an adult means needing to lead an independent life and have personal space, so he no longer wants you to take care of his meals, especially since it affects your own work. Of course, your concerns are valid, as frequently eating takeout may not be very healthy. If we consider only the health aspect, I think it is best to listen to your child's suggestion because being an adult means taking on responsibilities, and he is surely aware of the issues with eating takeout, so he can handle this responsibility on his own. If you want more opportunities to communicate with your child and have meals together, you can occasionally cook a meal for him. "Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime." Actually, the best solution for this difference of opinion is to teach your child how to cook for himself, which is both healthy and won't affect your work. Of course, whether or not he is willing to learn may require further communication between you. Best wishes~

I think your differences with the child must go beyond just cooking. So no matter whether you choose to do it or not, you will feel conflicted. The problem lies in the following aspects: first, differences in lifestyle habits. Second, differences in cognitive values. You believe health is the most important, and the healthiest meals are made at home. But the child may think: there's no need to waste time on cooking. Third, differences in behavior philosophy. You believe that all the efforts for the child are worthwhile. Delaying work to take care of the child actually puts pressure on her, and she will feel that it deprives her of the right to make independent choices, resulting in suspicion of interference with her freedom. In other words, your actions make her feel guilty. As parents, as the child grows up, they will feel that they can do less and less, so they will give their all; while as a child, they will enjoy the right to be in control and make choices during the process of growing up. Parents will feel that the child is drifting away, which may cause some anxiety, but trust that they will grow up in an instant at a certain time and gradually appreciate the greatness of their parents. So don't worry too much.

Hello, dear reader: First, I would like to ask you a question - who gets to decide whether someone is a good mother? In the book "Watching and Seeing Off" by Long Yingtai, there is a wonderful description that I would like to share with you: I gradually came to understand that the so-called relationship between parents and children is simply the fate of constantly watching their backs disappear in this lifetime. You stand at one end of the path, watching them gradually vanish around the bend, and they silently tell you with their backs: there's no need to chase after me. As children grow up, as parents, how long can we provide meticulous care? When parents are not around, how should children take care of themselves? Perhaps this is a question we should think about more. We all understand the principle of giving a fish versus teaching how to fish, but when it comes to the people we love the most, we often forget this principle. Children will all grow up, and we also need to learn to see them with the perspective of their growth. Many times, the efforts of parents satisfy the needs of adults, not children. Being a good parent can start with letting go. May your efforts be visible to your children.

Seeing the points you raised, there are a few areas where you have differences with your child: 1) Your child prefers to order takeout for meals at home, while you prefer to cook for them because you believe takeout is not hygienic. While it is understandable that you are concerned about your child's food health, perhaps you are overestimating the dangers of takeout. After all, your child orders takeout at home without experiencing any specific issues like diarrhea, which suggests that it is generally safe. Moreover, the existence of takeout itself implies its own reasoning, as it provides a convenient solution when one is too busy to cook. If you look at it from a different perspective, could you perhaps offer suggestions to your child on how to choose healthy takeout options? 2) Sometimes, you delay your work in order to personally cook for your child, while they consider themselves independent, viewing your behavior as overly indulgent. From this disagreement, it can be seen that either cooking has already exceeded your life arrangements, or you are using it as a way to prove your care and love for your child. The fact that you have brought up this question shows that you are already aware of the impact that cooking has on you. Perhaps you also do not want it to hinder your work. But why can't you let go? This is related to the second issue, which is that you believe cooking can express your love and care for your child. However, your child has made it clear that they are independent now, so it is necessary to moderately let go and allow them to cook or order takeout to solve their meal needs. Additionally, you can express your care through other means. I believe that by providing your child with the genuine care they truly desire, they will feel genuinely happy and comfortable. I wish you and your child a harmonious relationship.

The child has already given you a clear answer, but you turn to the outside world to ask if it is appropriate. If you receive a positive response from the outside world, you continue to ignore the child's viewpoint. If you receive a negative response from others, you are being persuaded by others instead of respecting the child's opinion. Can you see the relationship between yourself and the child?

question: Negative emotions, then relax, and negative emotions, revenge others, what's the difference?
description: After having conflicts with others, some people may experience negative emotions and choose to take a walk outside to relax. However, others, when experiencing negative emotions, may develop a hatred towards others and seek opportunities to seek revenge. What is the difference between these two reactions?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I am giving my analysis and I hope it can help you! The first sentence, "When conflicts arise and negative emotions emerge, go for a walk outside to relax," belongs to normal psychological emotions. Each of us will experience negative emotions for various reasons in life. At such times, we need to release our emotions and regulate our mood. By taking a walk alone, we can calm down and reflect, helping us to calm our emotions and view the situation objectively and realistically, thus achieving a relieving effect. Here, we are under rational control and can well manage our emotions. The latter sentence, "After experiencing negative emotions, hating others and seeking revenge," is an extreme, excessive thought influenced by negative emotions. Usually, we are not under rational control and our emotions are manipulated, leading to extreme emotions and the inability to think calmly and correctly. Here, we are controlled by extreme emotions and may engage in excessive behavior. In order to avoid acting excessively due to extreme emotions, we should learn to control our emotions. Your private mental counselor by your side. I hope my words can bring warmth to you! I also thank the occasional passing readers for their attention and welcome you to follow me and click "useful"!

The emotions generated by the former are very normal, because in real life, it is impossible for everything to develop according to one's own wishes. Conflicts with others can arise, and sometimes these conflicts may be beyond one's control and cannot be resolved through arguments. It is normal to feel negative emotions in such situations. At this time, it is good to know that one has negative emotions and go for a walk outside. This is also a good way to alleviate negative emotions, much better than keeping them bottled up inside. We also know that accumulating negative emotions is not good for one's physical and mental well-being. As for the latter, such individuals may have extreme minds and not know how to process negative emotions. They only rely on emotions to solve problems. In times of negative emotions, any slight lack of control can often result in serious mistakes and cause more harm than benefit. Having negative emotions and then hating others and seeking revenge in this situation is a sign of immaturity. It is important not to overly attribute one's own mistakes to oneself or bear the burden of negative emotions excessively. Instead, one should learn to reduce stress. Therefore, sometimes patience is also a form of tolerance. Life is not always perfect, and when negative emotions arise, one should consider the reasons behind them and avoid taking drastic actions.

Hello, the issue you raised may be relatively "abstract," with less specific events and details described, so it is also unclear what contradiction or negative emotions are being generated. The occurrence of emotions resulting from the "conflict with others" can be seen as a "neutral" process itself. The "difference" you mentioned may depend on different perceptions of this matter, which in turn triggers different behaviors, leading to different outcomes. For example, if the "conflict with others" is seen as a "conflict caused by people," one may develop hatred towards others, seek revenge, and escalate the contradiction. On the other hand, if the "conflict with others" is seen as a "conflict caused by the situation," both parties may calm down under emotionally intense circumstances, take a walk, relax, focus on what they can do, and then consider how to resolve the issue or try to turn negative situations into positive outcomes or minimize the damage... This difference lies in the "difference in perception" and "difference in behavioral response," which leads to the "difference in the final outcome."

question: How to treat cold violence when the husband refuses to communicate during every argument?
description: After marriage, my husband is very stingy. Every time we argue, he resorts to cold violence and refuses to communicate. He also has a quick temper, getting angry easily when someone talks to him. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Wow, you are literally describing my husband. Refusing to communicate and using cold violence has been the norm for every conflict in our marriage. I consider myself a patient person, but he is even more patient when it comes to cold violence. Not only does he refuse to communicate, but after every argument, he tries to let it go without any clear discussion or resolution. He pretends like it never happened, but I really don't like it. My husband naturally dislikes communication, which is a result of his upbringing. I can't completely change him, so I'll give you my current approach in the hope that it can help you. I don't have a better solution at the moment. 1. Choose a suitable time, such as after a period of cold violence has passed and your relationship has improved, to talk to him about what happened last time and have a conversation. Regardless of the obstacle, it needs to be communicated. 2. Understand his history of growth. I don't know if you live with your parents-in-law, but everyone's personality is shaped for a reason and has a history. Even if it is irritable, it is not innate. By understanding his history of growth, you can find these reasons and help you find a better point to communicate with him and get him to open up. For example, my husband's refusal to communicate is because his family had a one-word rule, where whatever the parents said was final. Making demands or expressing other opinions would result in worse outcomes. Therefore, he doesn't like to communicate and is not accustomed to it. 3. Listen as much as possible and encourage him to speak and have deep conversations. Over time, he will start to enjoy confiding in you. 4. Adapt to his habits to a certain extent. After being married for a certain number of years, you should have enough understanding of each other. So, for many avoidable arguments or minor matters, it's okay to turn a blind eye. I hope this can help you.

question: My family is harmonious, and I don't have any emotional baggage, but I have been diagnosed with moderate depression. I don't feel like living anymore.
description: There are no emotional issues, my family is very harmonious, my parents don't quarrel, and my younger brother is very well-behaved and sensible. There's no blockage in my mind. I went to the hospital for psychological counseling for moderate depression and was prescribed medication. I have been taking them, and my mom says it seems to be helpful based on my behavior, but I still can't control self-harm. I want to take all the nitrazepam and ordered euthanasia pills online, thinking of taking them. Now I have thoughts of self-harm and suicide. The doctor said to come for a follow-up examination in two weeks during the check-up, but I feel it's useless. I don't want to continue living anymore.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from reading your question carefully, I understand that you have been diagnosed with depression by the hospital. However, from your description, it seems that there are no problems related to emotions or family relationships. But you seem to still have thoughts of self-harm or even suicide, that urge to destroy yourself. Since the external environment is good, what are these hidden desires to destroy yourself expressing? Because there is not much information in your question, here I will provide you with a few perspectives to explore, hoping it can help you find the root of your inner self. [Tracing the family, whether there is a hereditary trait of depression] You can try to understand your family history, which includes not only the immediate three generations, but even further extended relatives, whether there are similar cases of severe depression. At the same time, also understand that within the family, there may be some serious internal conflicts and contradictions. Understanding the above information will help you determine whether your depression comes from genetic traits. Do you have a tendency towards depression? You can even explore whether your current impulsive desire to "destroy oneself" is related to some hidden major events in the family? These perspectives may help you identify some underlying causes and help you discover the inner drive behind these desires to destroy oneself. [In-depth exploration, whether there are past traumas "forgotten" by yourself] Although in your question, there is no obvious traumatic experience mentioned, but it is possible that you consciously believe so, while deep down in your heart, there might be a traumatic experience that you deliberately "forgot". The human brain protects itself by automatically forgetting and blocking those past traumas. Although you may not remember the events themselves, they still have a deep impact, and those emotional experiences will keep replaying. Therefore, with the help of psychological techniques, you can explore past experiences and find those scars hidden beneath the dusty memories. Let yourself explore and understand what emotions those desires to "destroy oneself" are trying to express, and embrace the self with numerous scars. [Learn to release outwardly, express the energy that attacks oneself] Since you have the courage to destroy yourself, why not channel that energy outward? You should know that depression is most likely the accumulation of negative energy in your inner self, and you have been using this energy as a weapon to attack yourself. "I dare not express these emotions outwardly, so I can only attack myself." This is the subconscious signal language you use. Instead of being a good girl for too long, why not indulge yourself once in a while and release all these emotions, those desires to cry, curse, or even hit something? Pour them out, empty out the dirt in your heart. Your heart is like a cup, when it is filled with this "dirty water", no matter how much comfort and healing "clean water" is poured in, it will still be contaminated. Therefore, brave expression and getting rid of this "dirty water" is the first real step towards change. Of course, all the above suggestions need to be done with the help of a professional clinical psychologist. I hope you can embrace the sunlight as soon as possible.

Hello, after reading your description, I feel sorry for you. First, I want to give you a warm hug. Depression has become a very common disease now, and the whole society attaches great importance to it. There are also many medications available for treating depression. It was correct for you to go to the hospital for diagnosis and cooperate with the doctor in taking medication, which is very helpful for you! Generally speaking, the antidepressant medications usually take two to four weeks to take effect. Due to individual differences and the severity of the condition, this period of time for the medication to take effect and for symptoms to improve is a process that requires perseverance. From your description, perhaps you haven't had the chance to feel it yourself, but your mother has already noticed the improvement after you started taking medication. This is the reason why you must continue and not give up! You need to tell yourself that my emotions are currently ill, and I may feel despair and have thoughts of death, but that's only because my emotions are sick. I want to die, but I can't. I cannot be completely controlled by these emotions caused by the illness.

Hello, dear reader. Sending you a virtual hug through the screen. From your description, it seems like you come from a good family background, which makes you luckier than many others. What could be causing your depression? I heard from a expert that in this fast-paced era, almost everyone experiences some level of depression and anxiety, they just haven't been diagnosed. Negative emotions drain our energy, so in order to relax, we need to stop feeling anxious, sad, or angry. Accepting our own state and accepting the way things are around us and in the world is the key, but depression sufferers usually find it hard to do so. I suggest that you try to minimize the time you spend alone and communicate more with your parents and friends. Voice out all of your emotions, both positive and negative. Engage in activities that you enjoy and connect with nature. This can help relax your body and mind. Exercise is also a good method. When you have negative thoughts, engage in intense exercise. It can make you forget all your troubles and give you a feeling of rebirth while working up a sweat. Exercise can also generate dopamine, which improves your mood. If you really don't feel like doing anything, just stay calm and watch some TV shows or movies, or have a snack. Give yourself some time and space, but don't remain stagnant for too long. After a while, you should start thinking about your next steps. Some things can be helped by others, but some things can only be overcome by ourselves. If you enjoy reading, I recommend reading some positive books. Some people say books can cure everything. Many depression sufferers have been cured by reading. If you're taking medication, make sure to follow the doctor's instructions and don't flush any unnecessary medication down the toilet. In this process, don't rush for immediate results. It will take time, but believe that everything will get better. In the most ordinary days, I'll accompany you with warmth to see the world. Wenyi.

Hug little cutie, let's start with a simple self-introduction. Those who know me well call me Xiaofan Guo, but I like to refer to myself as a warm-hearted little chubby. Many people often tell us not to care too much about others' opinions, but how many people can truly do so? When I first started high school, I had a baby face and was less than 5 feet tall, so my height was my biggest insecurity. I minded it a lot when people called me shorty, little kid, etc. But often, the more we care, the more people seem to do or say things. In high school, I always heard others calling me that way, so many times I would hide in a corner, not wanting to interact with them. Perhaps fate was playing a joke on me, after the second year of high school, I suddenly grew taller and gained some confidence. I also started to slowly learn to accept myself. During the process of acceptance, I realized that sometimes I had fallen into misconceptions. Other people's opinions are only what they see, but they don't know what I have experienced in the past or what will happen in the future. If I live in the eyes of others every day, I may not be able to survive. Self-deprecating is just a hint to ourselves to not care so much about others' opinions, but it doesn't mean we give up on ourselves because we still have many people who love us and grow with us. Hurting ourselves may bring temporary psychological comfort, but it doesn't fundamentally solve the problem. Pursuing beauty is a common desire for many people, but not everyone can meet society's beauty standards, so we need to have our own criteria, as long as we approve of ourselves. I wonder if the OP feels a little better after expressing their feelings. If possible, we can explore other ways to relieve stress. This place will be your sanctuary for the soul. Can we grow together? The world and I love you.

Give the OP a hug! I can feel the OP's inner depression, anger, anxiety, and fear. The OP's issue is quite interesting. They feel like they don't have any emotional knots, yet they can't control their self-harm and even have thoughts of suicide. Their visit to the hospital's mental counseling center revealed moderate depression, indicating that there are some underlying issues in the OP's subconscious that they haven't consciously acknowledged. These problems may be causing immense pressure, making it difficult for the conscious self to face, understand, and endure. As a result, they choose to "isolate" and "ignore" to protect themselves and avoid facing these pressures, which brings a sense of relief and ease. For individuals with depression, it serves as both self-expression and self-preservation. Using low mood, reduced verbal activities, or self-harm is a way to express the inner repression, anxiety, fear, powerlessness, and the desire to gain attention, understanding, acceptance, and love from those around them. At the same time, it avoids contact and communication with others to prevent the risk of being ridiculed or hurt, allowing them to freely live in their own space. On one hand, they want others to understand them, while on the other hand, they are preventing themselves from being understood. These two conflicting forces constantly struggle and fight within the self, leading to continuous vacillation between their thoughts, similar to two people fighting, sometimes one gaining the upper hand, sometimes the other, not knowing how to proceed. The OP mentioned not wanting to continue living. Does the OP really no longer want to live, or do they simply not want to continue living in such a repressed, painful, and uncomfortable state? For many individuals with depression, suicide is just a means to escape the pain, not necessarily an actual desire to die. It's their conscious self unable to bear the emotional and psychological pressures from the unconscious self, wanting to kill the extremely weak, helpless self, and allow the conscious self to live a carefree, natural, and pleasant life. The fact that the OP believes they don't have any emotional knots, yet engage in self-harm and contemplate suicide, clearly indicates conflicting symptoms and highlights the extreme vulnerability and helplessness of their subconscious self.

Hello, questioner. Hugs to you, the world is colorful, let's share together! I am very eager to chat with you, as if we are meeting face to face. You mentioned that your depression is not caused by family reasons and there are no emotional barriers. This means that you have a clear understanding that this is a disease and you have rational acceptance of this problem. This is good. Although you still have thoughts of despair and self-harm, you have not closed yourself off and have come here to find us. Dear questioner, since you accept the fact that depression needs treatment, why not be more courageous and follow the advice of doctors and counselors to gradually enter a positive cycle? You can feel your pain, but if you really want to get better, you must rely on the strength of doctors, family, and friends to help you come out and fundamentally accept treatment and the progress it brings. With the deepening of treatment, I believe you can start to completely control your will and move towards deeper recovery. Firstly, I hope you can avoid taking excessive medication. Taking too much medication can make you feel unconscious and have difficulty breathing, causing you to feel drowsy. This will make your state worse and unable to take interest in other things in life, only intensifying the pain caused by depression. Secondly, you can think about what prompted you to seek help here, you want to understand why depression is troubling you, how it is troubling you, and hope to relieve or even eliminate it. Maybe you haven't realized it yourself, but this shows that you have not completely fallen into despair because of depression. You are interested in life, but negative emotions have taken over. Dear questioner, everyone must go through a good experience in this world. You are not worthless. You are the son/daughter of your parents, the brother/sister of your siblings, the student of your teacher, the companion of your friends, and your own god! In the future, you will also be a wife/husband, a father/mother of a girl or boy. You are the unique you that I know! Lastly, for someone as unique as you, someone who wants to get better, we all don't want to miss out. Also, I hope some suggestions can help you: 1. Observe the cycle of negative emotions caused by your depression, be your own doctor, record it, actively communicate with professional doctors and counselors, and adopt an attitude of fighting against depression. Avoid excessive medication, follow medical advice, depression is not scary, what is scary is avoiding it. You have already bravely accepted the fact that you have depression, why not be even more mighty and overcome it! Maybe you think I can't fully understand your pain, but this is how I solve my own difficulties, I believe you can do it too. 2. Understand the cycle of negative emotions you experience, try to be with family and friends as much as possible, mobilize everyone's strength to fight against depression together. When a person is in an open environment, their mood will also become brighter, which is conducive to self-regulation of emotions. 3. Painting, Sudoku games, and regular exercise in moderation can help alleviate depression, nurture one's sentiments, stabilize emotions, and create a sense of well-being. It can even become a profession. Finally, when negative emotions are very severe, always be brave and actively respond psychologically. Seek help from loved ones and friends. Sometimes depression may make you unable to control your true thoughts, but with each improvement, you will definitely make progress. I hope you are happy and joyful every day. The world and I love you. Good luck.

Hello, OP, first of all, a big hug for you~ The main issue you are currently facing is being diagnosed with severe depression and having thoughts of not wanting to live~ Depression~ Self-harm. You emphasize that you don't have any relationship problems and that your family is harmonious, with your parents not arguing and your younger brother being well-behaved. On the surface, your life seems to be going well and beautiful, so could the desire to self-harm or commit suicide be related to the emotional feeling of "being ignored" in the past? Generally speaking, when there are more than two children in a family, the eldest child may feel resentful because the younger siblings have arrived, believing that they have taken away the parents' love or hindered their own display. Even if they are well-behaved, they may still have varying degrees of negative emotions like this. OP, you went to the hospital for psychological counseling and were diagnosed with moderate depression. Medication was prescribed, but you still can't control the self-harming behavior. You want to take all the Nitrazepam pills and ordered euthanasia pills online. You have thoughts of self-harm and suicide now. The doctor said to come back for a follow-up in two weeks, but OP feels that it's useless and doesn't want to continue living. Since your upbringing environment is not bad, is there a fear of 'social' interaction or a reluctance to seek cooperation with others? If so, when did it start? Given your current situation, Nuan Nuan suggests that you avoid being alone and communicate more with your parents or friends. Try to do things you enjoy, and if you don't feel like doing anything, try your best to avoid doing things you don't like. Gradually find your interests and seek cooperation with others in the process. Also, Nuan Nuan hopes that you can actively cooperate with professional doctors' treatment and strive to recover as soon as possible, rediscovering the sunshine in life. Best wishes.

question: I really want to get out of this relationship, but I am too deeply involved. What should I do?
description: This year, at the age of 39, I have an unfortunate marriage. After experiencing my husband's numerous affairs and domestic violence, my love for him has turned to ashes. In early May, I unexpectedly met a man in his 20s who is 9 years younger than me. We had a physical relationship on our first meeting. Actually, we didn't initially plan to continue dating, but later we developed feelings for each other and gradually fell in love. He didn't make any unrealistic promises to me, he just told me that he never wants to hurt me and will not hurt me. He is a Scorpio man who is not good at expressing emotions, and he is clear about the difference between liking and loving someone. He wouldn't say "I love you" against his will just because I'm unhappy. Finally, on May 20th at 13:14, he confessed his love to me. To be honest, I was touched, because we are in a long-distance relationship and have few opportunities to be together. Because I missed him, I traveled far to meet him in Shanghai, Yichang, and Huanggang. Due to his work, he often goes on business trips. In my heart, I truly hope that one day he will come to my city just to see me, but due to the nature of his work, this is unlikely. However, every time he returns to his home in Beijing, he still keeps in touch with me and cares about my mood through the posts I share on social media. (To be continued)

answers.answer_text: Big sister, are you feeling conflicted and distressed? The same situation can lead different people to make different choices. You can ask yourself: 1. Do you need to divorce your current husband? 2. Do you want to continue being with this man in his 90s? 3. Does this man in his 90s want to continue being with you? You mentioned that your husband had an affair and was abusive, which likely made you feel trapped. His appearance and your encounter allowed you to experience long-lost love and care. But now you want to escape. Ask yourself why exactly? If he has a family and you had this kind of experience, what do you think about the relationship between the two of you? If you truly want to move on from this relationship, there are two options: 1. Take it further, if you both genuinely love each other, try to overcome the difficulties in life and openly walk together. 2. Step back, first handle your original relationship well, and it's best if you don't contact or see each other anymore. The most painful thing is to complicate all relationships and simultaneously enjoy and suffer.

Dear, you are already 39 years old, not 19, so why are you still so innocent and naive? If he really likes you, how could it be that you have to go the distance to see him, instead of him coming to see you? This can only mean one thing! It means that you haven't reached that level of importance in his heart. Imagine if you were his wife, or the woman he intended to marry, would he treat you like this? How many women can tolerate him like this?

question: After being discharged from the military, S's desires have become stronger and harder to control, causing a lot of frustration. What should they do?
description: After first encountering SM, I discovered that I had a tendency in that area. Later on, I even took assessments and confirmed that I am an S. Now, I am gradually losing control over my thoughts, with many strange ideas, and sometimes I feel a bit bothered.

answers.answer_text: Has there been any abusive behavior? Have you ever laid hands on your loved ones, family members, or animals? Having a tendency towards violence is a manifestation of losing control of one's emotions and projecting inner insecurities and repression. Perhaps life after leaving the military is not as good as expected. If your situation is not severe, you can calm down and reflect on the reasons for the problem. The behavior patterns of seeking immediate pleasure do not solve the root of the problem.

question: I feel a little awkward with the behavior of students who are ten years younger than me.
description: The student is ten years younger than me and has been following me for a long time. I have been teaching him wholeheartedly for a long time. Recently, because of his poor performance, I have educated him twice and sincerely shared some wisdom with him. In the past month or two, this child often intentionally or unintentionally pinches my hand, grabs my shoulder or waist. Sometimes, when I'm tired from wearing high heels, he would say to let me rest my legs on his lap to reduce swelling. He has also joked half-seriously several times about carrying me, which makes me feel a little awkward. Am I overthinking or is it really inappropriate?
keywords: Interpersonal, deception and trust, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello! From your description, I can sense your feelings. On one hand, you feel angry about the students' frivolous behavior, but at the same time, you are afraid that you may be overthinking and feel conflicted. First, let's analyze the students' behavior based on your description. I think your students are probably high school students or above. "Pinching hands," "grabbing shoulders and waist," and their casual language. Regardless of age, these actions should not be done to girls of the same age, let alone a teacher of the opposite sex. On one hand, the students may genuinely appreciate and admire you, which is why they want to care for you. But on the other hand, these inappropriate words and actions also imply a romantic connotation, indicating that they may have a crush on you. Now, I will share my suggestions. Firmly refuse and maintain distance. Some of these actions may be difficult to determine whether the students do them intentionally or not. However, when students say inappropriate things, you can firmly ask them not to say such things to you, as it shows a lack of respect. Focus more on other students. Based on your description, it seems that the students started behaving this way after multiple times of your guidance. It is likely that the student believes he has a special connection with you. Therefore, it would be better to divert your attention to other students, so that they don't have such thoughts. I hope these suggestions are helpful to you!

Hello, I personally think that this kind of interaction between teachers and students is somewhat inappropriate, but I would like to know the age range of the student. If the student is younger, he may see you as a confidant or even family member, and his actions may be unconscious. He may just hope to help you as you have helped him and be grateful to you. However, nowadays children tend to mature earlier, especially for older age groups like high school students, there is a possibility that some emotions are involved, but this is simply because he feels someone is being kind to him. You don't need to feel burdened, after all, what you are doing is within your responsibility. I suggest maintaining an appropriate distance from him or stopping him the next time he makes such jokes, and make it clear to him that you don't like this kind of joking attitude. After all, there should be a certain level of respect between teachers and students. If necessary, you can have a talk with him and express your opinion. I hope this can help you.

Hello! From your description, I feel that your student has indeed crossed the line a bit, and there should not be any physical contact between teachers and students. Perhaps it is because you have been too kind to him as a teacher, being a good teacher, which leads to his dependency and liking towards you. This liking may be purely liking the teacher, or it may be the restlessness of adolescence. But no matter what, if you feel very bothered by it, you need to address his thoughts. 1. You can tell him each time he has physical contact with you that you don't like it, clearly refuse it, with a serious expression and a firm tone that doesn't allow for any argument, making him understand that you are not joking. 2. Try to reduce the time you spend alone with him, being alone with the opposite sex can affect one's emotions, this is called the proximity effect. Perhaps spending too much time alone with him has led to some misunderstandings, so you should try to reduce the time spent alone. 3. If your student is still an adolescent and continues to show affection between a man and a woman towards you, you should clearly tell him that such thoughts are beautiful, but they should not be the most important thing at this age. Thank him for his love, but the most important thing for him now is studying and improving, so that he can achieve what he wants in the future. If your student is an adult and there is a ten-year age difference between you that you cannot accept, it is best to keep your distance and only discuss academics, avoiding other topics too much. He will gradually understand your intentions. Good luck~.

Hello, I'm giving you a warm hug and sincerely teaching him, and he has been performing well. There was a period of time when he didn't behave well, but I talked to him openly and honestly. From here, you can see that your relationship is still very good. You have always had a pure teacher-student relationship with him, and you have been very dedicated to him as well. Your efforts are felt by the child, so the child is willing to have a good relationship with you and listen to you. Recently, the student will unintentionally touch his own shoulder, waist, and legs. When he is tired, he will even help himself relieve the swelling. He jokes that he wants to carry himself. Because of your efforts, the child can feel it, so the child is also very understanding towards you. However, considering the child's current stage of adolescence, it is normal to have other thoughts about you. As someone who has gone through adolescence, I can understand. If we, as teachers, provide correct guidance, then he will gradually establish a better position for this relationship. So, what matters most is not how he currently thinks, but the correct guidance we provide. Best wishes!

question: Like to save money but lack strong desire to make money? How to have a correct attitude towards money?
description: I really like saving money, and I feel anxious when my money decreases. However, I don't have a strong sense of purpose when it comes to making money, and I don't enjoy doing sales. How can I develop a healthy attitude towards money?

answers.answer_text: Questioner, Hello! You mentioned that you like to save money, but when it comes to making money, you lack a strong sense of purpose and dislike sales. How should we view money correctly? This is a really great question because everyone relies on money. I would like to share my understanding with you. Firstly, it's important to clarify that money itself is neither good nor bad. "Money is a good servant, but a bad master." I used to dislike the idea of making money and thought that as long as I had enough for daily expenses, money wasn't important. It was only after listening to a lecture by Mr. Huang Qituan about money that I realized that subconsciously, I had a negative view of money. I always thought that people with a lot of money were too focused on personal gain, lacked empathy, and were unhappy. These were all one-sided beliefs, so I never paid much attention to money matters. Once I became aware of the hidden beliefs in my subconscious, I started to repair my relationship with money. Money truly has no inherent value or qualities, and earning money is not the ultimate goal. Money can help us enjoy life more fully. It is merely a tool that serves us. People who earn money seriously are admirable and can help us accomplish many desires, such as showing filial piety to our parents, providing better material conditions for our children, or helping those in need. Now, let's briefly discuss saving money. Saving money provides us with a certain sense of security to deal with unexpected events in the future, such as illness, child education, or retirement, and it's perfectly normal to enjoy saving money. But there's no need to worry excessively about having little money because we should believe that we can earn money. Mr. Huang Qituan also said that psychological factors have a significant impact on earning money. We should enhance our sense of deservingness and believe that earning money can be easy and joyful. Earning money and putting in effort do not necessarily have a direct correlation. We need to let money flow and be bold in earning it. I used to fear losing myself in front of money because I had never received financial education. Being able to enjoy life while earning money is the true way to become a winner. I used to only know how to make money but not how to enjoy it, and my inner self felt deprived. However, after reading Mr. Huang's book, I felt enlightened. I will make money and gradually increase my own value. Wealth not only flows but is also limitless. You mentioned that you don't like sales, and I wonder what thoughts you have in your heart about this. It is easier to earn money by doing something you enjoy and are good at. I recommend the book "Rich Dad's Guide to Investing" and wish you much wealth and a life that you desire!

Hello, are you the one who earned a lot of money:)? When you are in need of money, your desire for money will be strong. If you have saved a lot of money, then you can increase your level of consumption. When you feel that this amount of money is still not enough, your desire will come back. Generally, you can consider the following points for money: 1. Whether your savings are sufficient to bring you a sense of security. There is a saying that you should have enough money in your account to sustain your life for half a year. 2. It is a waste to leave extra money in the account, whether you invest it in yourself or in assets. 3. Balance points 1 and 2.

question: Want to go to bed early, why do I feel inexplicably annoyed or excited at night?
description: I want to go to bed and wake up early, but every night I either feel inexplicably annoyed or inexplicably excited. Sometimes I feel very tired in the morning. Why is it like this? What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Dear OP, you used the term "mó míng" twice. May I ask if it refers to the unclear source of these emotions, or not knowing what exactly is causing the annoyance or excitement? Your conscious mind is well aware of the importance of getting enough sleep and waking up early, but your subconscious is hindering you from doing so. What message is your subconscious trying to convey? Your post conveys a strong message: I want to understand myself, to explore myself! When a person has the desire to explore themselves, they have the possibility to make changes. However, it may require seeking counseling. Best wishes!

Hello, OP. However, in the evenings, you tend to have some emotional fluctuations that affect your normal rest and, consequently, have an impact on your daily life. I can sense that you want to change your mood. Have you recently experienced anything that made you feel agitated or excited in the evenings? Could you try brainstorming and using divergent thinking to record as many possible solutions as you can, and then slowly select the most feasible ones to implement? Before going to bed, you can try meditation to gradually calm yourself down. There are many related audio resources available online. These are my suggestions, and I hope they can help you. Take care!

question: Is my reaction normal when my ex-boyfriend has a new girlfriend?
description: Ex-boyfriend, seven years in a relationship. It has been one year since the breakup. When I heard that he has a new girlfriend, I started to have persistent insomnia, feeling nauseous when eating, feeling weak all over, slow in reaction, as if my mind is imprisoned and unable to coordinate with my body. Do I love him, to what extent? If I love him, why haven't I firmly chosen to stick with him during the three breakups in these seven years, without making a definite choice for him? I do not believe that I do not love him.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, disease diagnosis, psychological counseling

answers.answer_text: Hello! I have been intermittently with my ex-boyfriend for seven years. During these seven years, it's not just a matter of time coming and going, but also the daily and nightly memories, the ups and downs of emotions, and of course, our continuous understanding and reflection of each other. These scattered fragments unconsciously piece together the emotional picture and spiritual world between you and him. As one of the listeners, what can I provide for you? This is the dilemma we both need to face at this moment, just like you chose to post your question here for us to see. Like the bettors who come and go in the lottery store, whether we will win five million or five hundred yuan, or just make a contribution, none of us knows. However, there is a hidden path in all of this - we have all walked into the lottery store and bought a ticket. The future has already completed a certain fixed match, and we have completed our workflow. All that is left is the waiting process for the draw and whether it matches our previous efforts to some extent. Can I use the trauma caused by the separation of a child from their mother to explain this beautiful and blooming self-acknowledgment? Whether it is a child or a "lost" adult, what will instantly heal that "wanderer"? I think the arrival of the mother or her return can instantly soothe the trauma caused by years of separation and heal the child or adult. (In fact, we don't even need imagination to understand this. It is one of our instincts.) Let's reverse from the next node to the previous node and see what happens. Can we continue to move forward without evading it like this? "I don't think I don't love him..." There have also been separations of varying lengths, and in the end, I chose to separate... In love, some people say, "When you suspect whether I have feelings for someone, you probably already do..." But this sentence, this phenomenon, how do you see it? Do you believe in such descriptions, or do you think it is factual? Conversely, if we reverse the beginning and the end of this sentence, does it still hold true? Would you allow such an interchange? It's like a kind of advertising slogan that only needs to replace the name of the city it is in, and it becomes valid. For example: livable city, charm (you can fill in any city name we desire). Does love also have a similar template-like formula? We will pause the discussion on this question for now and continue a little further. When you separated from him after being together for seven years and found out about his new emotional life, you experienced physical symptoms, such as vomiting, as you mentioned in the question. Here, it is necessary for us to clarify one question, which is where this problem comes from - is it a response from the body itself or is it a process of the mind affecting the body? Understanding the source of this problem may help us avoid going in circles and gradually accelerate our progress, heading north with determination and invincibility. In the days of having inner dialogues and coexisting with external forces, slowly reconcile with yourself, just like the changing of seasons, the renewal of all things, and embark on a new journey, a new life. This is just a little of what I can see at the moment, the rest, occasionally, you may need to walk alone, and occasionally, we may still walk together for a while.

OP, being together for seven years, this kind of relationship cannot be simply let go. In these seven years of being together, apart from deep emotions, there are also long-formed habits. You may have become accustomed to this person's presence and developed a routine with them. The emotions, habits, and little things that have occurred over the past seven years cannot be forgotten easily. So even after a year of breaking up, it is still difficult and tormenting. Maybe you still love him, or perhaps your passion for him has slowly diminished over the past seven years, and now only habits remain. When you broke up three times in the past, perhaps it was due to the environment you were in at the time and both of your emotional states were not normal. It is normal to suggest a breakup and not persist when negative emotions outweigh positive ones in problematic situations. Not persevering may mean that after a long period of being together, you realized that you are not very compatible, but this doesn't deny the fact that you still have feelings for him. Whether it is love or habit, you both have your own lives now. I hope that after the pain, you can focus on building your own fulfilling life. Try to spend less time thinking about him, perhaps engage in more social activities, and maybe you will meet more people and even encounter your Mr. Right. I wish you can truly let go of these seven years soon and I wish you a happy life of your own! Best wishes!

question: My sister has a conflict with our family and she came to me to talk about it. How can I help her?
description: I have a sister who is only 26 years old. Maybe she went back to our hometown to work. Our parents think she is getting old and they are extremely worried. They always bring up the topic of why she doesn't have a boyfriend or why she hasn't found a partner yet. My sister feels a lot of pressure every day and doesn't even want to go home on weekends. She currently has a car, a house, and a stable income in Leshan. She has her own hobbies and friends she can confide in. Maybe she occasionally feels lonely, but she never sees herself as pitiful. However, people around her always look at her with a pitiful gaze and constantly backbite about her in front of her parents. Her relationship with our parents has become confrontational right after they meet, and she also rejects meeting them. She even feels that life is too exhausting. She wants to tell our parents that she is fine and they don't need to worry, but every time it ends up in an argument. My sister asked me how she should communicate with our parents, but I haven't experienced these things yet so I don't know what to do. How can I comfort her?
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between parents.

answers.answer_text: There are significant differences in mindset and priorities between the older generation and our younger generation. The older generation's starting point is to hope that their children can have a stable and happy life with a family. In their mindset, getting married and having children early is the key to a stable and happy life. Your sister, as a young person, has her own career and life, her own aspirations, and her own views on marriage, which naturally differ from those of the older generation. It is common for the two generations to experience differences and conflicts, and it is difficult to reconcile them immediately. Therefore, both sides should start from their own perspectives. If they approach the conversation with the intention of persuading or refuting the other person, or trying to change their perspective, it will inevitably lead to arguments, conflicts, and ultimately, no one can convince the other. However, from both sides' standpoint, they both want their children to have a better life. It's just that the definition of "better" is different for the older generation and the younger generation. Therefore, both sides should not have an antagonistic identity and state, but should seek mutual understanding, accommodate differences, find consensus in the midst of disagreements, and adapt to each other's personality and psychological state for coordination. Firstly, let go of the intention to refute and persuade the other person's thoughts because this kind of argument leads to no results and it is difficult to have a positive outcome. As children, on the basis of understanding the good intentions of the older generation, it would be worthwhile to take a step back and show good manners and language that harmonize with the older generation's intentions. In simple terms, the older generation is like children; sometimes they also need to be "pacified." Because, at this time, the older generation is not trying to immediately make the child take action or get married and have children, it is just a habitual behavior to nag a few words when they see their child, expressing their worries and concerns. At the same time, they may feel a bit embarrassed due to idle gossip, so they unconsciously shift the conflict and hope to save face. As children, we can understand the behavior of our parents. At this time, there is no need to aggressively refute or argue face-to-face. Instead, you should learn to make appropriate concessions and show vulnerability in front of your parents, expressing an attitude of accepting their opinions, and also expressing that you accept their concern. This kind of empathy can give parents a sense of comfort. Then, you can shift the topic appropriately, and maybe they will forget to continue nagging. For example, you can respond, "I understand that Mom, you care about me and hope I can marry a good man, right? So, I am also carefully selecting, hoping to find a good man to marry and not make you worry too much. What dishes are we having tonight? Do you need my help in cooking?" In interpersonal communication, including communication between relatives, some skills need to be taken into account. When there is a conflict between the two sides, both parties' emotions are in a stress state, making it difficult to think calmly and rationally. If a tough attitude and language are adopted, it is not conducive to resolving conflicts. At this time, only by calming emotions first and then solving the problem can be achieved. Try to consider each other's thoughts from their perspective, find common ground that both sides can agree on, in order to persuade with care, take care of the other person's emotions, and appropriately make concessions. This can resolve conflicts and make the contradiction cease to be a contradiction. In addition to using communication skills, it would also be helpful to show more initiative in caring for parents, actively communicating, and actively showing parents the happy and fulfilling aspects of your life. This way, parents can understand you better and not be affected by idle gossip, thinking that their child is not doing well and worrying unnecessarily. Ultimately, parents worry because they care about their children, which leads to various thoughts and interference in their lives. I believe your sister is an understanding person who can understand her parents' intentions and thoughts and can communicate and get along well with them. Best wishes!

I'm not sure about the relationship between the original poster (OP) and their parents. If their relationship with their parents is better than their sister's, then perhaps the sister's goal is to seek enlightenment. If their relationship with their parents is similar to their sister's, then the sister's goal is simply to express herself and seek comfort. Of course, this comparison should be based on the sister's perception. Therefore, it is recommended to offer comfort first and then analyze the situation.

question: I just found out that my mom is having an affair, what should I do?
description: Mom had an affair. I discovered it at home last month. She is in her thirties. What should I do?
keywords: Family, family relationships, and communication between parents

answers.answer_text: It seems like you are a girl. True love, in essence, is a combination of wisdom and sentiment, while love and hatred in life are merely the result of the protagonist's lack of cultivation. Love, as spoken of, has no comparative degree and there is no "love more". Because love is already the highest level. With love, all problems are not difficult and there is no feeling of being wronged. Feeling wronged and feeling burdened, that is not love, but only an exchange. I have always believed that whether I love you or not is my own business, and whether you love me or not is your own. I don't love you because you love me, and it doesn't affect my love for you if you don't love me. Love is just a fill-in-the-blank question. There is no exchange or choice. Look to see if mom has the strength to come out.

question: I feel mentally stuck, as if there is a big knot inside me. What should I do?
description: A dormitory, my roommate in the same class and I often go to class together, but she has a really good relationship with my other roommate. I remember one time, the three of us walked back to the dormitory together, I looked at my phone while walking to avoid awkwardness, and they walked together. At that time, my roommate and I walked in front, but later they walked together behind us. Later, when we left the dormitory, I was behind, and they walked and chatted without looking back, making me feel really awkward. During evening study, I was originally going to sit with that classmate I play with, but I arrived at the classroom first. Then my roommate encountered her close roommate and they ended up being in the same classroom. When I came back with water, that classmate told me that they walked in front of me. I actually felt really disappointed, like there was a big lump in my heart. You see, when I walk with my other close roommate and that classmate, I always consider her feelings, but in the end... how should I view this situation?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! First, I want to give you a warm hug. I completely understand how you feel. It's normal to feel upset when your close friend spends more time with another friend and leaves you behind. Firstly, I hope you can be clear about one thing: in your friend's mind, who is more important to them, you or the other roommate. It's possible that they have more in common or they assume you're busy and don't want to bother you. We can't demand how others treat us, so it's important to learn to enjoy solitude. Additionally, if you're still feeling uncomfortable, you can sit down and talk with the two roommates, telling them how their behavior of excluding you makes you feel really uncomfortable, and express your hope that in the future they can wait for you and do things together. I hope you can resolve the conflict soon. Wishing you well.

question: Is there nothing to talk about if we don't discuss relationship issues? Should I break up with him or not?
description: We have actually been dating for over a month, but it seems like if we don't talk about some issues regarding relationships, he doesn't have much to say to me. And he says that it affects his mood. I am feeling quite unhappy... Should we break up?

answers.answer_text: Hello! On the journey of love, you have discovered some thought-provoking questions, and I commend your wisdom! After about a month of getting to know each other, both parties may still only have surface-level understanding. From your description, it seems that you don't know what topics to talk to him about, and can only discuss the topics that he deems important. Being in a relationship means discussing each other's views on life, values, and worldviews, and talking about each other's ideals and beliefs. People tend to associate with those who share similar views and values. Only when your perspectives align can you become like-minded individuals! Only then can you become true friends and potential life partners in the future! After a month of being together, you are still in the stage of getting to know each other, and it can't be said whether you are boyfriend and girlfriend yet, as the relationship hasn't reached that level of commitment. Time reveals one's true nature, so gradually deepen your understanding of each other and evaluate whether the other person meets your standards and expectations based on your values. Then decide whether to continue developing your friendship into a romantic relationship.

question: Why do some people feel the urge to harm animals when they see them?
description: As soon as I see the ducklings, chicks, and kittens, I want to squeeze them to death and abuse them to the point of death.
