answers.answer_text: Hug the host. I have also had such behaviors and confusion before. I would like to share my thoughts and hopefully provide you with some inspiration. When I was in elementary school, I raised two small turtles. I had thoughts of killing one of them and even applied force to pinch its shell, but I was afraid of the bloody scene so I controlled the intensity. At that time, I felt so cruel and perverted. I think these thoughts of wanting to harm small animals must also have been troubling for you, right? My situation at the time was that I was an only child, my father was fully devoted to work, and my mother had a strong desire for control and had fluctuating emotions. I felt that the atmosphere at home was very oppressive and my mind seemed to be filled with negative emotions. But I had nowhere to vent or confide, so I took it out on the small turtles that were unable to resist and were weaker than me. I don't know what has happened in your life, but you can consider if you have encountered a similar situation: accumulating a lot of negative emotions in your heart, but not being allowed to express or see them, and lacking outlets for release, so you would only take it out on small animals who are even weaker than you. This is the reason I saw from my own behavior at that time, and I hope it can give you some inspiration and help you understand your own thoughts. My small suggestion is: thoughts do not equal actions. I may want to do it, but I can choose not to do it. I suggest that the host can focus more on "what has happened to make me have such thoughts," pay attention to the emotional changes and physical reactions caused by the facts. We have all sorts of thoughts every day, so we don't need to be overly anxious about them. Secondly, find a suitable outlet for the accumulated emotions. You can try writing a diary, confiding in someone, painting, practicing yoga, listening to music, meditation, etc. There are many methods that can help us release emotions and calm our restless hearts. You can make decisions based on your preferences and actual situation.

From the perspective of abnormal psychology/pathological psychology, it is possible that the person has been subjected to bullying, blame, and insults from others. They then project the harm they have suffered onto smaller and weaker creatures. Some of the reasons may be inherited from domestic violence. They may actually hope that the weak victims of domestic violence can resist (in their place) to alleviate their own feelings of cowardice. (Information is sourced from the internet, books, and my own summaries, which may not be accurate.) If a person is still easily angered even without experiencing these terrible things, they should go to the hospital for examination, possibly due to neurological issues. In other words, their brain may be different biologically. Recommendations: 1. Exercise restraint. It can become addictive. Gradually, they will become unsatisfied with their imagined and existing desires for stimulation, which will make them become the kind of person they originally dislike. 2. Seek help from someone you trust. 3. Keep going! Learning self-restraint will make you a better person. I hope this is helpful.

question: How to balance between raising a successful child and letting things take their course? How to control a child's education?
description: Is it more appropriate to expect one's child to achieve great success or to let things take their natural course?

answers.answer_text: Hello, this is my feedback: (1) Firstly, every parent hopes for their child to achieve great success. However, we need to distinguish whether we want our children to become better individuals, fulfill our own desires, or to become receptacles of knowledge and machines for learning. What does it mean for a child to "become a dragon"? This is something that parents need to ponder over. (2) Secondly, learning to go with the flow does not mean letting things take their course blindly. We should respect our children's desires for growth but not indulge their unreasonable ideas. We can communicate with them frequently, but we should not neglect them. Apart from providing resources, love and companionship are even more important. (3) Lastly, there is no progress without rules. As early as the 19th century, Freud proposed that parents play different roles in the family. The mother needs to embody warmth, while the father needs to establish rules. Therefore, it is necessary for parents to have a reasonable division of labor and provide love and guidelines. #The world and I love you, take care~.

question: Married into my husband's family for nearly 2 years, now their true colors are revealed, feeling mentally unbalanced, what should I do?
description: It has been nearly two years since I got married and moved into my in-laws' house. At first, they treated me quite well, but now their true colors are showing. They speak in a bad tone, are aggressive, and love to interfere in everything. Because I married into a lower social position, I feel really unfair and unhappy. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, give you a hug. I believe you must be feeling very upset now, feeling that your family is not treating you as well as before, so you feel very uncomfortable and unbalanced in your heart, and you are not happy. I remember hearing a saying before, that over time, we always save our worst temperament for those closest to us. I think they may also have this kind of thinking, that now that you're officially married, they have less concern for you. Or perhaps it's because you haven't been doing well in certain aspects, so they treat you like this. You can take a moment to reflect on yourself. See what you have done wrong, whether it is your own fault or others'. If you feel that it's not your fault, I suggest you find some time to communicate with your husband because he is the best medium between you and his family. I believe he will help you ease the relationship between you. Take care~.

Hello, it is evident that you feel frustrated and unable to resolve the problem with your mother-in-law. You are unsure of how to make yourself feel better. I empathize with you. Have you discussed this issue with your spouse? Have you talked to him about the difficulties his mother has caused you? In a family, the relationship between husband and wife should be a priority for happiness. You should share any unhappiness with your husband and let him be on the same page as you. Of course, you don't have to have a strained relationship with your mother-in-law, but you should consult each other when there are issues. If you feel that talking to her directly is useless or awkward, you can ask your spouse to act as an intermediary at an appropriate time to reach a consensus and set boundaries calmly. Clearly state what behavior you dislike and hope she will refrain from doing in the future. Don't think that you cannot stand up for yourself just because you married into the family. Since you are married, you are one family and you should value your position and love yourself. Don't sacrifice yourself! You are also a precious member of the family. Hugs to you! You mentioned that you have been unhappy since the second year of marriage. If you don't address this issue earlier, your mother-in-law might take further advantage, making your life even more difficult. Don't be afraid that she will hold a grudge after communication, after all, you haven't done anything wrong, you are just expressing your feelings and needs, so you don't need to be afraid. You can also seek advice from your family and friends, I believe they will all help you. Wishing you all the best and a happy life. 🧡

The relationship with the mother-in-law is something every woman needs to work on after getting married. As a wife, you may not be familiar with your husband's mother, so she has her own temperament and personality, while you have your own upbringing. Therefore, it is important to respect the elderly and their ways while also maintaining your own life, friends, and new hobbies. Instead of investing more energy into the relationship with the mother-in-law, if you find it difficult to get along with her, try to minimize contact and focus on doing things that you want to do and help yourself grow. By doing so, you can have a harmonious relationship with your mother-in-law.

question: 28-year-old woman, recently, why do I always tend to blame myself?
description: Recently, I have been reconnecting with old friends and participating in a group activity. During the activity, I noticed that I was slower compared to others, and it was really frustrating. Every time, my good friend is always the first one to finish. I used to be able to fully engage and give it my all, but slowly, I started noticing that I was feeling emotional and inadequate.

answers.answer_text: Hello there. As you mentioned, when participating in a group activity with old friends, you were initially able to fully engage yourself. However, because you were slower during the process and your good friend finished first, you gradually started experiencing emotional issues. So, when you became aware of your emotional problems, did you further examine the situation? For example, when your friend finished first and you were slower, how did you feel? Was it because you were holding the group back and that's why the emotional problems arose, or was it because you felt inferior to others? This can help you better understand the reasons behind your emotions. Considering your current situation, I suggest the following: 1. When you notice your emotions, first try to relieve yourself by shifting your attention or practicing breathing exercises, for example. 2. Adjust your perspective. We all gradually discover our own issues and then proceed to solve them through the process of interacting with others. So, you need to accept your shortcomings, identify your strengths, and make the most of them. 3. When encountering problems, if you tend to blame yourself, it's necessary to consider whether you highly value others' opinions of you and whether you constantly set high demands on yourself. This can also contribute to your emotional issues. I hope this can help you. Best wishes!

Although the information you provided is brief, I can still see that you are a very reflective girl and I give you a big thumbs up. First of all, we need to have a purpose in everything we do. We play to have fun, work to earn money, without a purpose, we will lose direction. No matter if you participate in activities to socialize, prove your abilities, or for other reasons, you need to think clearly, what is my purpose? If you want to be the fastest, that's great, you can take first place as your standard. Even if others put in 10% of their effort, can you not keep up? Secondly, speed is a criterion, but the standard of ability is not just speed. Can you find anything in this world that only requires speed other than sports competitions? 1. If all your standards are excellent, but only speed is lacking, then it's great. You want to strive for excellence, this is a higher pursuit. 2. If all your standards are not great, what's the point of focusing only on speed? Even if you have the fastest speed, does that make you the best? Finally, regardless of who you compare yourself to, winning or losing is temporary. Our only opponent is ourselves. On one hand, the path we have walked to become who we are now is only because of ourselves. On the other hand, all the negative emotions, self-blame, and worries are imposed by ourselves, the source of our unhappiness is also ourselves. Will you defeat that annoying self or make peace with it? This is still our own business. I can tell that you are someone who has high expectations for yourself, and I believe that you can definitely find your most comfortable state through adjustment. Keep going!

question: Sometimes, my mindset is not very good because I feel like crying over small things that upset me.
description: Sometimes, my mood becomes inexplicably irritable and I feel upset. I even start to feel aggrieved and want to cry over very small things.

answers.answer_text: Hello there, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ From your description, I can sense that your emotional state is quite low. Have you recently encountered significant stressors? If you are feeling "irritated for no reason and getting upset over very small things", it might be due to the accumulation of negative emotions, making it difficult to regulate your emotions and easily resulting in emotional breakdowns. It would be helpful to consider seeking a psychotherapist for emotional guidance to help release these pent-up negative emotions. Additionally, you can also try some self-regulation techniques such as confiding in friends or finding ways to release negative emotions. It is crucial to learn how to regulate your emotions promptly after encountering negative events. We all possess a certain level of self-regulation ability. However, when you find that you are unable to regulate yourself, it is important to seek help from others. Best wishes~.

question: I am interested in cooking, but I am afraid to show it at home because I'm afraid of being discouraged.
description: I am quite interested in cooking. This year, during the pandemic, I successfully tried steaming mantou at home. However, I only want to experience it myself and not showcase it to others because I am afraid of the judgment from my family. Even though I know I can do certain things well, I still don't want my family to evaluate me. I'd rather have them think I'm lazy and incapable of anything. I don't want even the slightest bit of derogatory comments on something I truly take seriously.
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between parents.

answers.answer_text: It sounds like what you mean is that you would rather do nothing at home and not give your family the opportunity to evaluate you, because if you do nothing, you are like a blank sheet of paper that others have nothing to evaluate about. This on the other hand reflects that your family likes to evaluate things and people, but these evaluations make you feel unappreciated and more often than not, degrade you. In order to adapt to this atmosphere within your family, you have taken the approach of doing nothing. So, when you have the opportunity and freedom, go ahead and fully express yourself.

People who achieve great things often do things that others do not recognize. Even if they see the potential and have a strong conviction, the people around them are all against it, and no one has the same vision and perspective. Once they fail, everyone jumps out and says, "See, I told you so. He just can't do it, he just likes to daydream, he just loves to mess around..." But once they succeed, the negative evaluations from before disappear, and everyone can understand them: "So he was quietly accumulating all along, his vision is so unique, we were all wrong..." Look, success makes heroes. The original poster says, "I don't want even the slightest bit of depreciation for the things I take seriously." Does that mean those successful people are not serious every time they do something? Are they just perfunctory, and only serious when they succeed? How do they know which thing will succeed? Will they stop doing what they want to do and should do because of others' opinions? The original poster occasionally succeeds in doing something, like steaming buns, and can ensure proficiency in all aspects of cooking, does it come easily? Different professions are like different mountains, being good at one thing (the original poster surely won't rely on steaming buns to make a living in the future) doesn't mean you can do other things well too. If that were the case, why would we need teachers, books, or the internet? If you don't take care of small things, it's difficult to do big things well, because big things are made up of accumulated small things. I know a saying: "The lazier, the dumber; the dumber, the lazier." Don't think that if you don't do it normally, as long as you want to do it, you will definitely do it well, and you can always do it well as before. Especially for complex things, without a lot of practice, thinking about each step, repeatedly pondering, trying and starting over, it's basically impossible to do well, impossible to achieve excellence. Otherwise, there won't be phrases like "familiarity breeds skill," "practice makes perfect," "the 10,000-hour rule," and "improvement." "Immature Parents" wrote that children can stay true to themselves as long as their elders support them. However, if they are criticized or humiliated for being true to themselves, they may feel embarrassed because of their genuine needs. Children believe that by pretending to be the way their parents like, they can win their parents' love. They choose to keep their true selves silent and then follow the guidance of their role-playing self and healing fantasies. In this process, they become distant from their inner selves and external reality. The original poster is afraid of family evaluations, afraid of criticism, probably because family members habitually have a negative and skeptical attitude towards anything you do, this is their own problem, they always see you as a child, fortunately maintaining their own image of being tall and mighty in front of you; they don't want to exit your life, don't want to stop interfering and controlling you. The more you evade and show vulnerability, fear of criticism, the more satisfied they are, the more they like criticism and interference. On the other hand, even if the original poster starts off poorly, but doesn't give up, doesn't retreat, works harder, always strives, it will make them take notice of you and withdraw to an appropriate boundary. (At first, they will definitely not give up their control, it takes multiple times to do well, consolidate, and persevere). I hope this can help you!

Caring too much about others' opinions may cause us to miss out on many opportunities. I don't know if you're in that situation as well. I also care about opinions, especially from parents and family, but not so much from strangers. So, at home, in the eyes of my parents, I am someone who can't do anything. But outside, in the workplace, I am a contradictory person. Sometimes I try to perform well, sometimes I shrink back. There may be several reasons for this result. First, parents don't want us to be independent. They need us to rely on them, so in some situations, they subconsciously belittle our achievements, making us think we can't live without them. Secondly, lack of encouragement from parents during childhood makes us lack self-confidence, so we easily believe others' opinions. Lastly, we may have been struck by relatives or encountered certain difficulties in childhood, so we want to excel among familiar people. Dear, we can't control others, and parents also have their limitations. The simplest thing we can do is to love ourselves and have confidence. If you enjoy cooking, you can start by cooking privately.

question: 25-year-old man, feeling very uncomfortable after learning that his partner was sexually harassed in high school.
description: Just three months into our relationship, she shared her deepest secret with me. At the time, she seemed quite indifferent, as if she had already come to terms with it herself. She told me that she had been involved with the same person multiple times without resisting, which made me very uncomfortable. The problem is that this matter has become a burden for me, and I haven't been able to let go of it. I don't want this issue to affect our relationship, so how should I accept it?

answers.answer_text: Hello. I feel very sorry for her experience, and also very uncomfortable. The fact that she can tell you her deepest secrets and expose her unknown humiliation shows that she already sees you as the most trustworthy and reliable person. But on the other hand, this burden originally belonged to her alone, and after telling you, it becomes a story and emotion that needs to be shared with you. Although it is incorrect to say that this is just a story, as the emotional impact it causes far exceeds what words can convey, I truly hope that the harm it brings will only remain at the story level. It's difficult to determine whether she has already adjusted, but it can be certain that she is also finding balance in some way, otherwise she would be suffering to the point of being unable to move forward. Lin Yihan's "The Little Reunion" is based on personal experiences, using a novel format to tell the story of herself and classmates being repeatedly seduced by a teacher, with understated words carrying an irreparable pain. Finally, she suffered from severe depression, choosing to end a life that could no longer continue. She said: Life is like clothes, so easily stripped away. She said: I'm not disappointed in you, it's this world, or life, fate, call it what you will, it's good and bad. Now I read novels, and if I come across a good ending that rewards good and punishes evil, I will cry. I prefer everyone to recognize that some pain in the world cannot be reconciled; I hate it when people say that only through suffering can one become a better person, I desperately wish for everyone to acknowledge that some pain is destructive; I hate the sentimental tradition of a happy ending, positive thinking is so vulgar! But you know what I hate even more? I would rather be a vulgar person, I would rather be ignorant, than to see the backside of the world. If there was a choice, no one wants to go to the backside of the world, or maybe if they had the ability, everyone would want to erase those unbearable stains, and then live in the light forever. Your partner's experience is a normal issue for you, but for her, it is an enormous scar that cannot be shown to anyone. As Lin Yihan said, we must recognize that some pain in the world cannot be reconciled, and acknowledge that some pain is destructive. But I hope her trust and reliance on you will allow her to be reborn, and her rebirth will allow both of you to heal and bid farewell to the past. If you are the right person for each other, you will choose to cherish her even more. Best wishes.

Hello! I understand your confusion and I'd like to share my thoughts with you. You mentioned that your girlfriend was sexually assaulted in high school, and it has been causing you a lot of mental discomfort. I would like to discuss my views from three aspects:

Firstly, I feel extremely sympathetic towards your girlfriend's experience. It must have been very painful for her to go through such a situation during high school, especially if she couldn't tell her parents due to family reasons and had to endure the suffering alone. It breaks my heart to think about it. It's not that she didn't want to resist, but at that age, both physically and mentally, she may not have been capable of knowing what was the right thing to do. She felt hopeless and helpless, and the abuse happened repeatedly. Can you imagine how much pain she must have been going through?

Secondly, you mentioned that you feel uncomfortable yourself. I understand that you feel empathetic towards her experience, but if you create a distance and mind her ordeal, then that is unfair. If that's the case, it means you don't truly love her. You have no idea how much she loves and trusts you to share her deepest wounds with you. If you truly don't love her, at least be honest with her and don't cause her further pain, because what she went through was a severe trauma, and it's not her fault.

Lastly, I see that you're already 25 years old, an adult with the right values and understanding. Although I can understand your possessiveness towards your girlfriend and not wanting her to have been intimate with other men, it really is not her fault. If it weren't for that beast who took advantage of her... Lastly, I hope that you can comfort her and reassure her that the pain is in the past, and encourage her to lead a positive and optimistic life. If possible, I hope you can love her even more, without selfish motives, so she can understand that her true feelings haven't been betrayed. Best wishes!

Give the OP a hug! I can understand the OP's feelings of repression, anxiety, and conflict. Being together for three months, the girlfriend revealed that she had been sexually harassed by someone multiple times without offering any resistance. Any man hearing this would be shocked and find it difficult to understand and accept. It's like being suddenly "attacked," caught off guard, and feeling very uncomfortable and unsure of how to respond, feeling powerless and helpless. For the OP's girlfriend, this happened during her high school years, a transition from adolescence to adulthood, a period of rapid physical and emotional development. She may have had feelings of attraction towards the opposite sex and a certain level of sexual desire, wanting to establish intimate relationships with the opposite sex to satisfy her physical and emotional needs. Being sexually harassed during that period could make her feel accepted and validated by others, as if she already possessed enough charm to attract the attention of men. At the same time, it also negates her, making her feel that others think she lacks the ability to protect herself as an adult, leading to such violations. So her lack of resistance is both unwillingness and fear. It can be said that she lacks self-confidence and a sense of security, and the conflict is intense. She only told the OP after three months of being together, which reveals her inner needs. After three months of getting closer and more intimate, their relationship has developed into a stable and harmonious romantic relationship. This intimacy is both a need and a pressure for her. On one hand, she wants to establish a stable and harmonious intimate relationship with the OP, and on the other hand, she is afraid and unwilling to develop a more intimate relationship with the OP. Therefore, she threw this "heavy bomb" at the OP, leaving him "dizzy" and feeling uncomfortable, temporarily "stopping" the intimate development of their relationship and giving herself a chance to "take a breather" and rest. At the same time, by telling the OP, it shows her inability to bear the pressure and is also a "test" attack on the OP. She "needs" to see how the OP reacts and understand his bottom line. In other words, certain words and actions from the OP in their interaction have made her feel unsafe, and now the pain and confusion the OP is experiencing reflect the lack of mutual understanding and trust between them. Therefore, my personal advice to the OP is to no longer repress oneself and express these thoughts and feelings to the girlfriend, listen to her thoughts and feelings, find out how she views the past events, release and alleviate the pressure in the OP's heart, promote deeper communication and understanding between the two individuals, and resolve misunderstandings between them, ensuring the stable and harmonious development of their relationship.

It is indeed a bit difficult to accept such news suddenly, but sometimes we also need to learn to consider things from the other person's perspective. If the other person does not trust us enough and has already adjusted themselves, I believe they would not easily enter into a relationship or reveal their inner secrets to the questioner. The fact that they are able to do so indicates that they have also gone through a struggle in their hearts, and it is just because they want to be with the questioner that they do not want to hide things forever. Many times, when we see certain things, we often say, "Why didn't you do this? Why didn't you resist?" But if we put ourselves in their shoes, in certain specific circumstances or threats, how many can remain calm and composed? Not to mention that sometimes girls are inherently disadvantaged, often not because they don't want to resist, but because they do not have the ability to protect themselves, so sometimes they have to compromise under pressure. If the other person says they did not resist, are there other factors involved? Of course, we should never force the other person to reveal all the details, because often we tend to think from our current standpoint. So we can give ourselves some time, tell the other person what concerns us, but also give them a sense of trust, let them know that we still want to be with them, so we are willing to bear some things together with them. When we keep fixating on something, we put all our attention on that matter and neglect the relationship between each other. Therefore, we can put more effort into building a shared future. Since we cannot change the past, can we focus on nurturing our common future? The world loves you and so do I.

Hello: In theory, we all understand that "that was a long time ago, so there's no need to worry about it anymore," but emotionally, you still hold the role of current boyfriend, making it difficult to overcome. This is indeed a problem, as carrying this burden will inevitably affect the relationship, and pretending that everything is fine is not a solution. Therefore, instead of avoiding it, it's better to face it head-on. Let's analyze and understand the problem slowly: 1. It has only been three months since you got together, and this is her deepest secret. She told you about it in a nonchalant manner, thinking that she had already adjusted herself. She told you that it happened many times with the same person and she didn't resist, which makes you uncomfortable. (Boy, let's first explore what this means for the girl and what it means for you. Because I can't have a conversation with you, let's think about the following questions together, okay? Girl: "Deepest secret," she has suffered in silence for a long time, for reasons unknown. She didn't dare to tell anyone else, and it happened multiple times. But I think she must have been terrified, and that person may be an acquaintance (at least someone she knows). She didn't dare and didn't know how to resist. Boy: Is it because she went through this experience or because she didn't resist? What is the reason for your discomfort? This girl may be the closest person to you without any blood relation, do you feel pity or anger towards her?) 2. The problem lies in the fact that this matter has become a burden for you, and you haven't been able to let go of it. You don't want it to affect your relationship, so how do you accept this? (Yes, it's the word "burden." What is it that you can't let go of? If this matter continues to be in your heart, it will indeed impact the relationship, right? Boy, when you use the word "accept," if you still can't let go of it, then what do you need to accept about her, and what can't you accept? If you love her, your persistent attitude towards this matter, even though it's only in your mind, will be more damaging to her than the harm that person caused her back then. If you love, love deeply; if you don't love, please leave. Although the words may be direct, the underlying principle is correct. Because this girl has never done anything wrong, and you seem to have forgotten that she is the victim.) Conclusion: I wish you happiness! I hope you can resolve this burden soon! If you have any confusion, feel free to message me privately!

Hello, first of all, give a hug to your partner for their unfortunate experience. 1. Regarding the multiple incidents of harassment your partner faced in high school, it is important to note that high school is a time of emotional confusion and impulsiveness for many, and often during this time, boys and girls may not fully understand or be clear about the meaning and appropriateness of their sexual actions. Many times, these actions may occur due to misguided influence. The fact that your partner experienced multiple incidents of harassment is undoubtedly a significant hurdle in her life. Throughout the years, she must have endured a lot of emotional torment to be able to accept her past now. By choosing to tell you about it, it demonstrates her seriousness in considering your relationship and future together. In doing so, she must have felt anxious and conflicted. 2. As for your concern about his past, I believe that most guys have a preference for a partner who hasn't had previous sexual experiences, and I understand that you may share this preference. This is a normal thought, and many of my male friends feel the same way. However, in this situation, I think it's more important for you to consider whether this aspect holds significant weight in your relationship. Does this girl impress you in other aspects and do you both have compatible personalities? If so, maybe these qualities can overshadow your concern and turn it into compassion. Personally, I believe that while sex is important, the integration between two people is even more vital. On the other hand, have you had sexual experiences with your ex? Considering this from a different perspective might help you understand better. 3. As for your concern about your partner not resisting during the harassment, there are many things during adolescence that are difficult to explain why certain actions were taken at the time. Of course, the actions of the harasser were undoubtedly wrong. I believe that the girl was probably extremely frightened and unsure at the time, not knowing what to do. Is it really necessary to delve deeply into the past? In fact, she could have chosen not to tell you about it, but she did, which indicates that she genuinely wants to be in a relationship with you. 4. If you truly have a strong concern about this matter, it's best to end the relationship now, while your feelings are still in the early stages. Otherwise, this issue might cause future conflicts between you both. If possible, end the relationship while avoiding hurting the girl. If you decide to continue together, please give her a warm, loving embrace.

In the #incident of being molested# , as an audience, the original poster (OP) is already feeling very uncomfortable, let alone the person who was molested herself, right? She must have a lot of trust in you and care about you in order to muster up the courage to tell you about this incident, right? We've only been together for three months, and this is her deepest secret. When she told me, she seemed calm, as if she had already dealt with it herself. I can feel her trust and love for me here. Even though it hasn't been a very long time since we got together, she chose to tell me about this. Isn't that trust and love? There may also be another possibility that this incident is not as insignificant to her as she portrays it. It could still be a trauma for her, and maybe she chose to tell me now to see to what extent my love for her can accept it. She told me that it happened multiple times with the same person, and she didn't resist, which made me very uncomfortable. She experienced this during high school and maybe didn't resist because she was afraid or didn't know how to resist, right? So, OP, you might want to think about whether what makes you uncomfortable is the #incident of her being molested# or the #fact that she didn't resist#. The problem is that this incident has become a burden for me and I haven't been able to let it go. I don't want this incident to affect our relationship, so how should I accept it? As the OP, who is the boyfriend of the person involved, it's definitely uncomfortable to hear, right? Look, you're only together for three months, and you probably want everything about her to belong to you, don't you? Her being molested is like someone taking away your favorite cheese, so feeling #uncomfortable, suppressed, and uneasy# is very normal, right? Although this incident has had a big impact on you, you still care about her. Therefore, I suggest that you try to see this incident from the perspective of the female protagonist and feel her fear and unease. This way, you might not think that this incident is related to her own weakness. Also, the OP can think about whether you love her. What do you love about her? Can you accept both her strengths and weaknesses? If you are sure that you truly love her, then you can find an opportunity to talk to her about this. I think this issue is not just a burden for you, but perhaps also for your partner. The world and I love you. Best wishes to the OP, Jingjing Ting.

Hello~ I can sense that the topic creator feels uncomfortable because of this situation. You can ask yourself, what is it that you care about her? Is it because you feel she has been harassed a lot, or you feel she is no longer pure? Or do you feel that the "perfect" image of her in your mind is gone? As for this matter, how do you view it? Actually, in this relationship, you hope to continue and quickly accept this matter, so that it can quickly pass and not affect your own feelings and the relationship between each other. But also, hope you understand that this matter is beyond your original understanding, knowledge, and feelings. It is also "new" to you. When certain things happen to you for the first time, you will also feel lost and need some time. When you heard about this matter, what were your feelings? What happened in your mind? It's important to know your feelings. Try to express your feelings at that time. Because feelings belong to oneself and are the true content. If you avoid your feelings, you are also telling yourself to avoid this matter and the impact it has on you. As a result, you will gradually avoid interacting and communicating with her, and feel even more helpless. You can also give yourself some time to calm down and tell your partner that you are learning to accept it slowly. If she has already accepted it, you can talk to her about what concerns you and let her know why you want to discuss it. You can also think more about why you care so much about this matter. What does this matter mean to you? Perhaps for your partner, showing her true self will make her feel relieved, instead of pretending. Because it is not easy for her to talk about these experiences with others. The fact that she is willing to share them with you shows her honesty towards you. So, you can also try to be honest about your worries, fears, and various thoughts (because this is about being harassed, not knowing if it is sexual assault, not knowing which step has occurred. So it is important to identify which part of the content the topic creator cannot accept). Because this will involve whether the "bad" part is allowed to exist in the object relationship. That is, only allowing the partner to be perfect and allowing oneself to be perfect. These possibilities exist. If you want to explore in further detail, I recommend seeking professional counseling from a mental health professional.

question: 14 years old, introverted personality, feels like an outsider, doesn't know what to do?
description: 14-year-old girl. Because of her introverted personality, she has been beaten by her mother since childhood. I have also tried to change, actively talking to a group of people, but no one cares at all, it's really embarrassing. I don't know why, sometimes I am more outgoing when facing strangers. I used to be cheerful when I was younger, but it changed when I entered first grade, I dare not answer questions in class, my voice is also quiet. I have always had good grades, and my parents have high expectations for me. But when I think about my personality, what's the use of good grades if I can't speak in the society? It's hard to survive. I don't know what to do, and I have even thought about suicide. I really hate myself like this, so much. Of course, I also have cheerful moments, when talking about things I'm interested in or playing games with classmates, I can be outgoing, but it's only temporary.

answers.answer_text: Hello, little sister, after listening to your troubles, I really hope you can become more confident. You're only 14 years old, life has just begun, and all the good things are waiting for you to embrace. 1. Don't give yourself negative suggestions that you can't do it. You can do it. Look, you have your own interests and hobbies. Go ahead and develop them, and connect with people who share the same interests. 2. Don't worry about the future that hasn't arrived yet. Everyone has their own strengths, and people can change. Focus on studying now, and when it's time to work, you will naturally adapt to the work environment. You don't need to worry too much. 3. Don't force yourself to fit into other people's circles. Eventually, you will find people who click with you. Before that happens, just focus on doing what you need to do.

question: A 28-year-old woman developed feelings for her uncle and had an affair. How can she express herself after 2 years?
description: He is 14 years older than me. We met two years ago, and when I first met him, he liked me a lot. However, at that time, I was still considering and maybe he thought I rejected him, but I just thought it wasn't the right time. After two years, I still can't forget him and think he is the best. But suddenly he told me that he has already found someone else who is in a long-distance relationship with him. I'm really unhappy about this. I want to ask, does this mean I have no chance at all? I just haven't mustered the courage to say these words. He should understand now that maybe I still haven't forgotten him. Is it necessary for me to tell him that I really like him? Can he consider me?
keywords: Love, winning back an ex, relationship management, feelings

answers.answer_text: # I met him two years ago. When I met him, he really liked me, but at that time I was still considering and maybe he felt rejected by me, but I just felt that it was not suitable for the time being. # There was a chance for you to be together, but you felt it was not suitable so you rejected him. # Maybe I still can't forget him # He has something that attracts you, and after two years of experience, you may also appreciate him, so you feel that he is currently your best choice. That's probably why you can't forget about him slowly. Am I understanding this correctly?# But he suddenly told me that he already has a partner who is in a long-distance relationship # It's definitely bad news for you, but you still have a chance. # Is it necessary for me to tell him that I really like him and ask him to consider me? # This is your genuine need. I think you still have a chance and options. Option one: You can continue to maintain a friendship and not rush into a romantic relationship. You can do anything you want for him. If you truly like him, he will gradually feel your affection. He does have a girlfriend now, but it doesn't prevent you from expressing your care and liking for him. However, you shouldn't rush to define the relationship. This involves ethical issues. The cost: for you, you need to accept the fact that he already has a girlfriend. Your ongoing efforts may not necessarily result in him choosing you in the end. It will test your psychological endurance. Of course, you can choose to give up at any time during this process. So, you will spend more time struggling with yourself, overcoming negative emotions, and the constraints of moral beliefs. Also, many of his actions may not meet your expectations. Option two: You can continue to stay in contact with him until he breaks up with his current girlfriend. Then, you can express your admiration for him. The cost: this option is also agonizing for yourself, and the psychological test is not lower than the first option. Slightly better, there is almost no ethical test. The higher risk is that it will be difficult to define the relationship with him, and the chance of losing him is higher. He may marry the other person. Of course, there are other options that would require further communication and more information with you.

Hello! Good afternoon! I can sense your inner dissatisfaction. It's perfectly fine to have feelings for someone. However, liking someone doesn't necessarily mean we have to spend our lives with them, right? You and this uncle come from different generations. Although he liked you back then and now you like him, there are bound to be certain differences in thinking patterns and other aspects due to age. We must be aware of this. It is not an absolute obstacle, but it does remind us to give each other more time to understand one another. If a relationship develops solely because of liking each other, without a deep understanding or a commitment to the future, the outcome of this relationship may not be satisfactory. In matters of the heart, there is no right or wrong, only who gets hurt and who finds solace in the end. As the person in a more vulnerable position, I hope you proceed with caution, take it slow, and strive for a balance between rationality and emotional preferences. Best wishes, the world and I love you!

question: Just moved to a new city and want to make new friends, but don't know how to start?
description: I have been feeling very tired lately. Every day, it's just work and then back home. I read novels at home. I just moved to a new city and don't have any friends. I don't know where to start in making new friends, especially since I am quite introverted. I'm 29 years old, and I don't earn much money. I have a bad relationship with my father, and we often argue. Sometimes, I feel helpless because he says hurtful things. Does that mean I should just stay home and read novels until I die? It's also miserable not being able to make new friends. I really want to find new friends! Every day, people tell me to go out and find friends after work. Do they expect me to randomly approach someone on the street and ask if they want to be friends with me? I am really exhausted from this. Sometimes, I even think about just giving up and dying.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, expressing emotions, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello ~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that 1. OP lives and works outside and has no friends in the new place. 2. Parents are dissatisfied with OP's lifestyle, and OP has had thoughts of wanting to change, but doesn't know how to do it. 【A little analysis and advice】 1. Working alone, many times one does feel lonely. Socializing outside or staying at home reading and resting are different lifestyle choices for everyone, depending on personal preferences and inclinations. In this regard, perhaps the father's criticism is unreasonable. If OP wants to make friends, it must be because one truly desires to have friends, and not because of parental pressure. Friendships obtained in such a manner will be more enduring. 2. Making friends is indeed not about randomly talking to someone on the street. The source of friendships often starts with common interests and social interactions, such as meeting someone while exercising every day, or having good chemistry with a colleague during a conversation, or even neighbors. Observe the people around and perhaps one will meet compatible friends.

question: I feel exhausted, and I don't want to live anymore. I feel like I'm being hypocritical.
description: I'm always being told by my parents to do things I don't want to do. They never talk about the painful things they've done in the past, especially the ones that hurt me. The things they want me to do are never acknowledged or praised, no matter what I do, it's always just a sentence to keep trying. This confuses me and I don't know what I want or what I'm striving for. They never see the efforts I put in, but only focus on my flaws. Being criticized every day is really painful for me. Maybe this is my final message, goodbye to this world. I hope my family and I all disappear and blame this world.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner. It's heartbreaking to hear about your experiences. Sending you a virtual hug! Regarding your current problem: You are always being asked by your parents to do things that you don't want to do, and even when you do them well, there is no praise or recognition. Plus, your family only sees your flaws and never acknowledges your efforts, constantly criticizing you to the point where it becomes unbearable. I have a few suggestions for you: Try to communicate your thoughts with your family. It seems like your family has high expectations and wants you to excel. They may believe that criticizing and being strict with you will make you better. However, they may not realize that everyone has their limits and too much obedience without expressing your own needs can prevent them from knowing how much you can handle. Thus, the pressure keeps building up. Find a time when both you and your family are emotionally stable, and explain your needs, what you want to do, and your own plans. Speaking honestly is a way to release your inner emotions. If communication is impossible, there's no harm in being a little rebellious. You seem to be someone who is very obedient and dedicated in your family's eyes, which has also led to them neglecting your needs. If communication is not possible, don't always prioritize accommodating your family's feelings. Do what you truly want, love, and find useful for yourself. Don't worry about disappointing your family; they may be a little upset at first. But rather than seeing their child overwhelmed and falling into despair, they would prefer to see a happy and healthy baby. If you're feeling unhappy, go out and explore the world. I've also been someone who has been excessively demanded by my family. Although I eventually clarified things with my family and gained their understanding, there was a time when things got really bad, and I broke down and cried all night, throwing books everywhere and ending up with swollen eyes the next day. It was my classmates who brought me back from running away from home and took me shopping and out to eat. At first, my mood was really low, but seeing everyone happy and my friends patiently listening to me vent, I started to feel better. We all have moments when it's difficult to escape our emotions, so it's better to not dwell on them for now and go explore the world, enjoy good food and drinks, and then think about ways to solve the problem. No matter what, don't lose hope in yourself. The world and we all love you. Keep striving to be happy, my little mushroom who hopes for a gentle world and gives yourself the time to grow freely.

After reading your words, I feel deeply saddened. In fact, every family will have their own problems. I am not you and cannot truly understand from your perspective. But let me try to empathize. I think if there are problems within a family, the most effective method is communication. You have to believe that your parents actually love you, even if their actions may not show it. You need to understand that happiness and sadness are both part of life, and if you want to make a change, you have to start with yourself. Although what I'm saying may sound a little less emotional, I believe that there is nothing that cannot be resolved through good communication. Don't be pessimistic anymore, sweetheart. There are still people who love you in this world, and you need to love yourself as well. Keep going!

Hello, Yiyemingxin, and one word knows you. I don't know how old you are. Can you tell me? You mentioned your pain, not being understood by your family, lacking support and encouragement, and only receiving negative evaluations. I can tell that you feel quite suppressed. You're not living happily and feel lost, not knowing what you want. What I want to say is, "Don't punish yourself for other people's mistakes." If you think your family is at fault, let's be objective and recognize the boundaries between others' mistakes and our own responsibilities. Actually, if you browse through the questions and answers, you can see many people who, like you, have family troubles. We all have many troubles, trivial ones mostly, and most are difficult to resolve. I believe you are the same. It's difficult to accept an imperfect family, and it's difficult to accept oneself. But I hope you know that "you are not alone." There are many people in the world who have similar troubles as you. We are all struggling, trying our best, and helping each other. If all else fails, you can come here to talk, you are not alone.

Take it as a lesson. If both parents are constantly focusing on their child's flaws, the child will indeed feel suppressed. However, it would be a waste to commit suicide because of this. After all, there is still a long life ahead, and there will be plenty of good times to let yourself soar. Instead, treat this current hardship as an anchor. If you anchor this as the norm of life, then all the future moments will be filled with happiness. Don't blame your parents too much. It seems that most adults are similar. The more expectations they have for their children, the more anxious they become about the competitive education around them. In this way, parents are more likely to overlook their child's strengths. In fact, there are many lovely aspects to a child's growth, and there are many sweet moments filled with happiness. It's just that sometimes adults are blinded by their anxieties and fail to see the beauty. Keep this in mind. When you have your own child, don't forget to compliment them more :).

question: Six months ago, I experienced three consecutive setbacks. How can I overcome this slump in life?
description: Six months ago, I experienced three consecutive blows. I was diagnosed with thyroid cancer, my beloved family member suddenly passed away, and I broke up with my partner. Recently, my trusted boss also resigned, which has made me feel even more distressed and lost. I'm feeling very low and just want to be alone. It feels like everyone who loved me has left me... What should I do?
keywords: Emotions, depressive mood, emotion regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: In your description, I see your pain, helplessness, confusion, and feeling lost... How to overcome these confusion and pain and reach another level of life is indeed a test. However, life still belongs to you. Take leaving a job with a trusted boss as an example, it is actually a fate to encounter in the workplace. He cannot be your boss forever, and you cannot be his subordinate forever either. This is similar to a romantic relationship, if there is no fate, it is destined to be just a passing guest, no longer staying. In such a low point in life, what needs to be considered more is to regain self-confidence, regain a healthy self-love, fight against the illness, and courageously stand up, so that the self will no longer be weak. When you become strong, learn to love yourself, and those who love you will naturally not need to worry. There was a young woman who failed to pass the postgraduate entrance exam twice, and she was already 28 years old. When she was struggling, her mother told her, "It's never too late to change yourself." This young woman is Jing Yidan, who entered the graduate school of Beijing Broadcasting Institute at the age of 29. So, it's never too late to change yourself. ε I wish you the best. I am here, and the world loves you.

question: What is love in this world, that makes people willing to live and die for each other?
description: It's because I love you that I don't want to influence you. It's because I like you that I have to give up.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the paragraph is very touching. Because you love someone, you don't want to influence them; because you like them, you have to let go. I think this is a high level of love. However, the quote you used conveys a strong sense of sadness. Although you tell yourself to let go rationally, you may be very reluctant emotionally, enduring great pain. I don't know why you don't want to influence them. If there are various objective reasons that make it impossible for you to be together, then it is rational to give up in advance, to stop losses in time, and to avoid falling into greater pain. But if the problems between you can be overcome, perhaps you can make an effort, have a conversation with the other person, listen to their thoughts, and not give up too early. "What is love in the world? It teaches people to surrender their lives." Emotions are often so intense, so if it's worth fighting for, don't miss it. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Since I used to have cold hands and feet at night, I have been more and more afraid as the night gets later.
description: Ever since that one night when my hands and feet became ice-cold and my heart felt chilly, I have developed a fear of getting more scared as the night gets later. This has been torturing me for nearly 5 months now. I have been to the hospital for examination, but they didn't find any major problems. However, I still feel scared. I frequently suffer from insomnia, sometimes waking up at 1 am after falling asleep at midnight and then being unable to sleep again. I stay up late and become fearful. I have no idea what state I fall asleep in every day and feel tired during the day, but I'm afraid to sleep too much. I have to go to the hospital every week, and my family is already fed up. I measure myself using a fingertip pulse oximeter every day at home. I'm also afraid to go far away and constantly worry my friends. I wonder what will happen to me. This only happens at night, and it becomes more severe as the night progresses.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, pathological personality, abnormal behavior.

answers.answer_text: Give the host a hug! You can feel the host's inner suppressed anxiety and fear. The cold hands and feet and the chilly feeling in the heart are just stimuli that trigger the host's suppressed emotional feelings, thus affecting the host's normal sleep and life. From a physiological perspective, cold hands and feet indicate that the host has heavy coldness in the body, especially in the limbs, poor circulation of Qi and blood, and relatively weak kidney yang. The chilly feeling in the heart indicates insufficient heart yang and qi. The kidneys are the foundation of innate vitality, and insufficient kidney yang leads to insufficient heart qi and gallbladder qi, which can cause timidity and fear. Conversely, timidity and fear further deplete kidney yang, affecting other internal organs and causing varying degrees of pathology, thus affecting the host's normal sleep and life. From a psychological perspective, the host has a lot of suppressed anxiety and fear, reaching the limit of psychological endurance. Insomnia is a subconscious warning for the host to pay attention to these emotional feelings and give them appropriate freedom and satisfaction. Therefore, personally, I think the host can consider a holistic approach to both the body and mind. The host has previously had examinations and did not find any problems. Medical instruments generally only check for inflammatory tumors or organ damage and cannot check the flow and weakness of Qi and blood. Therefore, it may be helpful to consider seeing a suitable traditional Chinese medicine doctor, who can regulate the body's warmth, nourish kidney yang, and adjust the host's diet, daily routine, and lifestyle to restore the body to a normal balanced state. On the other hand, it may be beneficial to make an appointment with a suitable teacher for systematic psychological counseling, release the suppressed emotional feelings, repair internal trauma, and solve the problems that are troubling the host.

question: 26-year-old girl, got rejected, why do I keep dreaming about him?
description: Just recently, he found out that I liked him, and he sort of indirectly rejected me. Since then, I've been dreaming about the two of us doing various things every day, some good and some not so good. I would have multiple dreams in one night, causing me to have a disrupted sleep pattern. My sleep quality has become very poor.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~~~ Dreams sometimes reflect our subconscious mind, and people often say "what you think about during the day, you will dream about at night" and there is some truth to it; recently, you keep dreaming about that guy and the things that happened between you two, I think it's related to recent experiences. I wonder how your mood is during the day? Does your mood fluctuate greatly after being rejected by the guy? If your mood also has a significant reaction during waking hours, it is possible that our minds continue to think about this matter at night. In order to deal with this, we can exercise moderately and regulate our emotions in our daily lives, and maintain a stable mood before falling asleep. This also helps to improve the quality of our sleep~.

question: A 16-year-old girl is having a hard time adjusting to school life since it started and is considering becoming a day student.
description: Since the beginning of school, I have been feeling homesick every day and wanting to go back home to live. I cry every night and feel unhappy in the morning. The only time I feel better is when I exercise, but as soon as it's over, I feel even worse. I become emotionally unstable over trivial matters and tend to avoid social interactions. Should I choose to live off-campus or should I adapt?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: First of all, I understand your current situation, and it's completely normal to feel this way when you first start boarding school! Sending virtual hugs ️️ [Missing home] [Crying every night] There is a big difference between being a day student and living on campus. After a long day of studying, it's comforting to have family waiting at home. When you first start living on campus, it's common to feel insecure and have difficulty adjusting to the sleeping arrangements. I assume your sister just started high school? It's a new class with new classmates, and you haven't built a social network yet, so feeling lonely and helpless is completely normal. Don't suppress these emotions. Just like how you've found exercise as a way to release stress, try exploring other activities as well! See if there's anything you enjoy doing at school, and distract yourself with those activities. It might help improve the situation. [Mood instability due to small things] "Small things" are just triggers, but the real problem is your struggle to adapt to the environment, which makes you highly sensitive. As a result, those small things become outlets for your emotions. This emotional state has always been there; it just happened to surface. It's beneficial as long as you don't harm yourself or your friends, so don't burden yourself too much. Moreover, since you've recognized that your emotions are spiraling out of control, let's find a way that you enjoy to release those emotions even better. [Social withdrawal] Actually, the quickest way to adapt to communal living is to establish your own social network within the community. I'm not saying you have to make a lot of effort to fit in, but just find one or two friends you somewhat like and slowly spend time with them. Communal living is also a mandatory course in our lives, as you will have dorm life in college too. So if possible, I hope you can try to open up and gradually integrate yourself without rushing it. If it's really difficult to adjust, please communicate with your parents and teachers as soon as possible. Learning is already hard enough, and being happy is more important!️ I hope you can adapt to the new environment quickly and make friends with people whose personalities match yours. Rooting for you (ง•̀_•́)ง (If this has been helpful to you, please encourage me by clicking "Helpful"!)

question: There is no emotional fluctuation, only feelings of fear and dread?
description: Previously, when watching videos or reading articles that could evoke emotional fluctuations, I would react just like any ordinary person. But now, as soon as those fluctuations arise, they are immediately suppressed by an unknown force, and I no longer feel anything. I can only sense fear and dread. The feeling of sadness is also gone. I don't know why. Additionally, I no longer have any desire for sexual activities.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, mental disorders, behavioral abnormalities.

answers.answer_text: Hello, this is probably part of growing up. We become more and more invincible, harder to empathize, and with a stronger and tougher heart. In a way, this is not necessarily a bad thing, right? Of course, I also understand that it's not easy to feel yourself becoming "heartless." At times like this, it is necessary to return to our inner selves, gradually peel away the layers of "experiences" and "maturity" that wrap around our hearts, and become more sensitive and attentive. What is needed is a concerted effort to seek empathy. Take the time to immerse yourself in stories about life and human nature, as well as other people's comments. Digest those emotions repeatedly, slowly, and with an immersive experience. Eventually, the capacity for empathy will return. Best wishes.

OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From the description, I understand that 1. Things that used to cause emotional fluctuations no longer affect you. 2. Now you have no interest in anything and only feel fear. [Some analysis and suggestions] 1. With the development of the internet, there are more and more channels to access information, and the stimuli we get from online sources are also increasing. People's emotions have a threshold. For example, if you occasionally see a disabled beggar on the street, you may feel sympathy, but if you see beggars every day through various channels, the threshold for this emotion will increase, which means you become numb to such things. There may be a similar reason why you no longer have feelings towards things that used to cause emotional fluctuations. 2. My suggestion is to try to reduce the intake of external information, pay less attention to Weibo, news, and other sources of information. Take a break from your emotions in ordinary social life and use more leisure activities like reading or exercise. If these symptoms persist, I recommend seeking professional psychological counseling. I hope this helps you.

question: I always feel like everything is my fault, sorry mom and dad, I feel like I'm so useless.
description: Today my friend messaged me saying that she passed her piano exam, which is no big deal. But in the evening, which is now, I've been crying and I don't know why. I constantly feel like everything is my fault and I'm sorry to my parents. There was even a moment where I wanted to die. After a while, I calmed down, but now it's starting again. Do I have a mental problem?

answers.answer_text: Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You feel like everything is your fault. (2) You feel guilty towards your parents. Here are my analysis and suggestions, hoping to help you: It seems that all of your emotions stem from the news of your friend's piano achievement. Logically, you should be happy for your friend's success, so why do you feel sad and self-critical? Is it because you also pursued the same thing and feel inferior to your friend? Actually, everyone is striving and working hard on their own path, and everyone has their own unique way of doing things. So, even if you didn't achieve the same as your friend, it doesn't mean you're worthless, do you agree? As for feeling guilty towards your parents, being not outstanding doesn't mean you let them down. Love doesn't require such things. Lastly, if you're not feeling comfortable, you can reach out to a mental health counselor. It's not that you have a problem, but with the help of professionals, your emotional state can recover faster. #The world and I love you, take care.

question: I stood behind someone, wanting to push them down, feeling very confused in my mind, inexplicably uncomfortable.
description: Always want to push the person standing behind me, my mind is particularly chaotic. It's fine when I'm alone, but when there are many people around, I start to feel anxious. Now I just don't go out anymore. Sometimes, inexplicably, I feel really distressed mentally, but it gets better after crying it out.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I see that there is not much information in your words, so I can only guess based on some of my own observations, which is for reference only. Are you always thinking about pushing others when others are ahead of you? This indicates that you are tired of others or that your inner peace is disturbed. If you have experienced something negative in the past, such as something that has hurt you deeply, or if you have seen something negative, then your cognition may be influenced by that and you may think that everything is like that. Do you have any illusions that someone wants to harm you, or do you feel disconnected from the world, or feel like you don't fit in, or feel that someone is treating you badly and you resent them? If you have these situations, they may cause you to think like this. These thoughts are not good and can be dangerous, so you need to gradually change them. Also, if you are not going out anymore, it can easily lead to problems. Because by staying indoors for a long time, your inner emotions cannot be released, and if you frequently think about something, it can easily lead to depression or anxiety. So you must not continue like this, you need to slowly change. If you continue like this, it will cause significant obstacles to your mental health, and you will become increasingly unable to adapt to society. Recommendation: No matter what you have experienced, you shouldn't think like this. The world is beautiful, and if you continue like this, it will cause problems in your cognition, and I believe you don't want that. I hope you can be happy and go out to see the beautiful scenery! Believe in yourself, gradually change yourself, and be happy. If heaven closes one door for you, it will surely open a window. Keep it up.

The description provided by the questioner is brief, but contains a lot of information, yet it is not clear enough. For example, when it says "always wanting to push him," is "him" referring to everyone, or to a specific person or group of people? What does "okay" mean in the statement "it's okay when alone"? What is the fear behind not wanting to go out? And what kind of situations make one feel "unexplainably uncomfortable"? When did these feelings start? How long has it been going on? When was the first time you noticed it, and in what circumstances? In the question, it is mentioned that you "just don't go out anymore," and it seems that this idea of wanting to harm others scares even yourself. You fear that you might turn these thoughts into actions and hurt others. It is evident that the questioner is worried, afraid, and troubled, and that these issues have already caused difficulties in daily life. It is recommended that you seek out a psychiatrist or a professional mental health counselor to talk about it. They will be able to assist you better once they have a deeper understanding of your situation. Best wishes.

question: Is it either to endure or to explode? Are there any other solutions?
description: Hello, can I consult about a problem that has been bothering me for a long time? Recently, I have been having some tension with my colleague. Although she is my coworker, she always likes to correct my mistakes and tell me how to do things, which I find interfering. I don't think she has the right to criticize others since she is not the manager. I dislike it when others try to control me, and it makes me develop a rebellious mentality. I used to have a good impression of her, but after she told me what to do several times, I started to hold a grudge against her. I really want to vent my feelings and tell her that I don't like her interference, but at the same time I worry that others will think I'm being petty and difficult if I say something, which could lead to a strained relationship and eventually leaving my job. Recently, even the manager keeps pointing out my mistakes, and I feel like it's all targeted towards me because she never says anything to my colleague. This has caused me to have a strong objection towards her and believe that she is singling me out and treating me differently. In my previous jobs, I always had problems with interpersonal relationships, and almost every time I ended up quitting after arguments. The same thing happened with my relationships with coworkers before. At first, I always kept things to myself and didn't express my own stance, thinking that expressing myself would make me seem too concerned about trivial matters. As a result, others might think I'm easy to pick on. This resentment always ends up building up until it explodes, and when it does, I quit my job. I'm very afraid that this cycle will continue and affect my professional future. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Questioner, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description, I can really understand how you feel about your colleague's suggestions that go beyond their normal responsibilities and make you uncomfortable. Based on your description, you are bothered by your colleague's repeated suggestions, but you're not sure if you should communicate this to them. Indeed, in the workplace, the relationship between colleagues is more about competition and cooperation, but that does not mean that they can dictate your actions. Personally, if you feel very distressed, you must bring it up in a timely manner and let the other person know how you feel in order to better resolve the issue. Perhaps the other person doesn't mind you addressing this matter, as most solutions to problems are found through communication.

question: How can I get along with my family members happily when my two sisters often argue and I can't concentrate on studying?
description: I have two older sisters, and due to the pandemic, we are all working from home. Since our house is small, conflicts often arise between them because they don't have suitable work environments. I also find it difficult to concentrate on my studies. In the face of this problem, how can I get along happily with my sisters?
keywords: Family, family relationships, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. You want a quiet study environment, but your sister's constant arguments make you feel annoyed. On the other hand, you do hope that your sisters can get along harmoniously. You mentioned that the space at home is small and there is no suitable working environment. Without an environment, can you try to create one? For example, if the table is not enough, what about buying a space-saving folding table? If there are not enough power outlets, what about buying another one? Don't worry, take your time to think, there may be many solutions that you haven't thought of before. These are just my suggestions, I hope they can help you. Take care!

question: After being married for 5 years without any sexual intimacy, the marriage has become very painful. Should they get a divorce?
description: Teacher, hello. Marriage is very painful. Should I get a divorce? 1. We have been married for over five years, but we have never been able to have a sexual relationship. The reason is that I was very scared the first time, and my husband has a slight problem with erection. Now, my in-laws are eager for grandchildren and constantly urging us to do IVF. I'm not very willing because on the one hand, the doctor said there is nothing majorly wrong with our bodies and advises against it, and on the other hand, IVF can be harmful to the body to some extent. Moreover, my husband is not a very good man to me. 2. My husband and I argue over trivial things every now and then (our arguments are not related to our sexual relationship, but because my husband often messes around with me), and sometimes it escalates to physical violence. Every time it gets serious, my husband threatens divorce, and I feel very insecure. 3. My husband's family is from a remote rural area, and they are very traditional. My father-in-law is very serious, and I don't like living with them. However, my husband has limited abilities and can't afford to buy a house for now, so I can't see a future.
keywords: Marriage, beliefs about marriage, divorce, marriage management

answers.answer_text: Give you a hug. These days are so torturous, but believe me, there must be more solutions than problems when it comes to marriage stability. Love, sex, money, shared values, and nurturing the soul are all important aspects of an adult's marriage. Without the romantic colors of love, a marriage becomes more realistic and secular, which is the ugliest but most realistic part. Even the marriage of a prince and princess involves mundane matters like eating, sleeping, and making money. If legendary love stories like Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, Romeo and Juliet were to survive, they would also face the worldly reality. So first of all, do not assume that other people's marriages are always happy. My marriage is the most tragic, with flaws and shortcomings on both sides. It's just that some people's flaws are more visible than others. Sex is the premise of marriage, and a sexless marriage will only work if there's a consensus in a utopian style. Considering your sexless five-year marriage, based on your current way of having sex, it is definitely challenging to maintain your marriage. I haven't seen anything else besides love, money, and sex that can provide a foundation for your marriage. So, you need to go back to the core and see what pillars support your marriage. What kind of support can you and your husband provide for a stable marriage? If the lack of sexual desire is due to psychological problems or organic causes, you need to seek treatment. I once had a client who suffered from impotence for two years and could not have sex with his partner. In the process of counseling, we discovered that his impotence was caused by an abusive past relationship. After three hours of therapy to address the emotional trauma, the client's psychological impotence disappeared, and now he's about to become a father. So, what I want to say is, you need to seek help from a therapist or hypnotherapist to address your fear of starting sex. Find out what is blocking you. Is it a fear of men, a feeling that sex is dirty, or trauma from being abused? You need to find out the specific reasons and seek help from a therapist you trust to help you overcome your fear of sex. Because many times, resolving sexual issues can also improve many aspects of a marriage. If your fear of sex is not resolved, any man you try to be with may not be able to begin a sexual relationship. Your sexual life is currently resolved by avoiding sex and just rubbing together; this can lead to problems like premature ejaculation and impotence for your husband in the long run. A large part of your disputes and arguments actually stem from the unsatisfactory sexual relationship. Both you and your husband may need to seek help from professionals.
