If you resolve your sexual issues, it is highly possible that your current problems of arguing and the husband frequently threatening divorce will be resolved. Deep down, you don't want to divorce him and you fear his threats of divorce during arguments. So instead of waiting for him to change, it's better to take the initiative to address the core issues. Solve the sexual problems and many answers to your marriage will fall into place. Your fears of sex, divorce, and an uncertain future will disappear one by one. I wish you happiness.

Hello, from your description, I can sense your confusion and pain. First, let me give you a warm hug. Regarding your marriage, I can see that you have summarized it very systematically. The first issue is the disharmony in your sexual life. This is influenced by both your psychological factors and your husband's physical conditions. But overall, if it weren't for the pressure of pregnancy, you and your spouse have already adjusted your sexual life to a level and pattern that both of you can accept. The key contradiction lies in whether or not to have a child. Thinking about this question also involves your evaluation and consideration of your marital status. I think it is very necessary for you to first consider the issue of your marital status at this time. Secondly, in the process of your interaction as a couple, I can see that the way you handle conflicts has escalated to physical violence. Your husband also mentions divorce when conflicts get serious. This probably reflects that both of you need to improve your ability to handle relationships and resolve conflicts. Your understanding of marriage is still not mature enough. Thirdly, the reality of not being able to independently form a small family due to economic pressure and having to live with your elders also seems to have brought some negative impact on your marriage. Therefore, facing the question of whether or not to get a divorce, you need to understand some answers within yourself. What kind of marital relationship do you expect? Currently, in your marital relationship, what satisfies your expectations and what doesn't? In terms of those aspects that are not satisfied, based on the current reality, which ones can be adjusted and improved? Which ones are currently unchangeable, but you can't compromise on? In your current marriage, what do you feel attached to and what can't you accept? In those aspects that you can't accept, which ones can be adjusted and improved? Which ones will never change and you must endure? If you list out the answers to the above questions one by one, perhaps you can find the answers in your heart.

You are currently seeking help online, which means that neither getting a divorce nor maintaining the current situation has an absolute advantage. There are three reasons for this situation: conflicts between emotions and reason. You know that you would gain more benefits from getting a divorce, but because you still have feelings for each other, you don't want to get divorced. Or, there is a conflict between emotions and reason: you no longer have much affection for your husband, but because the benefits of getting a divorce are not obvious or even nonexistent, you want to get a divorce but don't dare to. It's not as absolute as 1 or 2, you still have some feelings for your husband, and the benefits of getting a divorce are not that significant, so you hesitate. My advice for the above situations is: first, create a very detailed spreadsheet listing the advantages and disadvantages of divorce vs. maintaining the current situation. Since you can't write down all the details of your daily life here, this spreadsheet can only be completed by yourself. Score these advantages and disadvantages, and you can also discuss and evaluate the scoring with close friends to make the table as comprehensive and rational as possible. Love can solve many problems, but love is two-sided. If you ultimately stay in a marriage because of love, observe whether your partner will also reciprocate the same love. Only two-way love can stimulate energy and is the driving force to change the current situation. (For the first situation) Improve yourself to gain the courage to have more choices. (For the second situation) When you hesitate, it means that you cannot make a choice because you do not want to bear the risk. At this time, no matter how much you think, you cannot find an answer. My advice at this time is, instead of using this useless thinking time, make the most effort to actively change yourself (improve your abilities, like in point 3), and change the current situation of the marriage (use the remaining love to repair the problems in the marriage). In the end, whether to leave or not, the answer will definitely be clear. Maybe you will be skeptical about point 4: I am the only one making an effort, what about my husband? Yes, you can only change yourself. In the process of your own change, in the process of making efforts for your family and marriage, your husband also needs to realize this and make changes. If he doesn't change, then after you make changes (become better and better), divorce is inevitable, and that person will leave your world. Of course, not everyone will make changes. You may also stay in the first half of point 4, that is, hesitate to make a choice because you don't want to bear the risk, and then spend your life. How to choose depends on you, keep it up.

Hello, dear reader. After being married for five years, there has been no sexual intimacy between the couple. On one hand, the reader is afraid of the first time, and on the other hand, there are issues with the spouse. Both parties have a certain responsibility, so why not try to communicate about it? [Pressure from the in-laws] "The in-laws are eager for a grandchild and want the reader to undergo in-vitro fertilization. On one hand, the doctor says there is no major health problem and advises against it, but on the other hand, in-vitro fertilization can still be harmful to the body. Moreover, the husband is not a very caring man." From a self-cognitive perspective, the reader can analyze their current situation and explain the reasons for not seeing a future. The in-laws' thoughts cannot represent everything. The reader needs to consider whether they want a child and if they are ready. Having a child is a major lifelong decision for women. Many families consider it a given, but I believe it should be discussed together. However, having a child comes with responsibility and increased stress, with more attention focused on the child. The reader must think carefully about it. If the reader is ready to have a child, they need to learn about sexual health and bravely face the situation instead of avoiding it out of fear. [The husband does not love you enough] The husband is not treating the reader well, getting into arguments over trivial matters, which is hard to imagine. In the five years, the reader has suffered many grievances. The husband has limited abilities and you cannot see the future, and perhaps the current life is not what the reader desires. As a woman, my advice is that we must learn to love ourselves and give ourselves a sense of security. It is natural to seek comfort and warmth from our husbands and gradually transform love into familial love. However, this should not encompass our entire lives. Do not restrict yourself due to family obligations. You can also pursue activities you enjoy and become the person you want to be. As for divorce, I hope you make a choice that aligns with your heart and have no regrets. Do not insist, and even more so, do not compromise. Finally, I wish the reader all the best.

#My husband's family lives in a remote rural area with traditional values. My father-in-law is a very stern person, and I don't like living with them. However, my husband's financial capabilities are limited, and we can't afford to buy a house for now. I can't see a future. ##Every time we have a serious fight (even physical), my husband threatens divorce. #Now, my in-laws are eager to have grandchildren and constantly encourage us to do IVF. I'm not very keen on it. #We haven't been able to have a normal marital life. 

#I rearranged your language. Can I understand it this way? You have the option to get a divorce. But do you have a direction? Are you hesitating because you don't have a direction after divorce? Assuming you want to choose divorce but just don't have a direction. Let me help you imagine. If you and your husband don't have any assets, then divorcing means starting from scratch. The basic prerequisite or urgent problem to solve for divorce is income and accumulating some savings, so you can have the confidence to start a new life. You need to choose the city you want to go to and the type of work you can do. If you plan to stay in your current city, then you need to start looking for work. Start collecting this information in your daily life. If your finances are tight, you can start with a job that offers room and board and accumulate savings for a year. After that, you'll have more options. Understand the divorce process and the way assets are divided clearly, so you can make preparations in advance and implement your plan. As for remarriage, in today's society there is a gender imbalance, so as a woman, having a divorce experience does not affect your choice to remarry or just find a life partner. Single women are still considered scarce resources, and if you have strong economic capabilities, you have an advantage in choosing a partner. Assuming your husband divorces you, based on the description you provided, the cost of remarriage for him will be very high, with few options and a low success rate. He may not have realized this, which is why he is behaving so stubbornly and threatening divorce. You can choose not to divorce and continue observing this family and looking for areas of improvement. At the same time, prepare for divorce based on the hypothetical scenario I mentioned above. This way, you have control and can make choices based on your situation.

1. The couple has no sexual life, and the husband is not treating you well either. 2. They often argue and even get physical, and the husband sometimes threatens divorce. 3. There is no money, so you have to live with the traditional in-laws. It seems that any of these situations would be quite agonizing. Please think about what has kept you going in this marriage for five years? What can you gain from this marriage? What is the most challenging aspect for you? It seems like the in-laws pressuring you to have a test tube baby is a significant event that makes you contemplate divorce. Your two reasons for not wanting a test tube baby seem quite valid, but they can't convince your in-laws. It's understandable that older people are eager for grandchildren, but it shouldn't be ignored that many elderly people see having children as a way to control their daughters-in-law. Children can make a happy marriage even happier, but they cannot save an unhappy marriage. If you can't improve your marital relationship, even if you have a child through medical means, you won't be able to provide the child with a good life, and it will only make you more exhausted. Whether you choose to continue this marriage or not, it is necessary for you to clearly understand what you want and find ways to achieve the life you desire.

Hello, from your description, I can sense your confusion and pain. It's not easy to live in such a marriage. Maintaining a sexless marriage is very difficult, and it needs to be compensated for in other ways: more intimacy in daily life, such as holding hands while walking, hugging at home, relying on each other... Choosing common interests, cultivating common interests between spouses can increase their feelings for each other... Communicate with each other and seek medical help. Generally speaking, harmonious "sexual" relationships are very important in a marriage. I suggest you and your husband find a competent doctor to regulate your bodies, cooperate with marital counseling, and improve the quality of your sex life. Sit down and have a good talk to solve this problem. After all, you once loved each other, even if you separate in the future, helping each other cure the disease is also a bond of marriage. You said "your husband can find a way to relieve his desires," so what are your sexual needs? Are they being met? Regarding test-tube babies, it is becoming more common. As for the extent of harm to women's bodies, you can consult a professional doctor. The harm to the body can be endured, just like the dilemma you're struggling with: Do I love him that much? Do I want to spend my life with him? I agree with your point: a harmonious and happy marriage is a reserve of strength for the healthy development of children; it is necessary to adjust the marriage harmoniously before having children. As for fighting, you can explore. Most couples argue, and it escalates to both parties resorting to violence. Is it the result of being emotionally triggered by something, or the accumulation of emotions? If it is the accumulation of emotions, what is it related to that is not being resolved? I hope this is helpful to you!

Hello, whether to get divorced or not is a decision only you can make, just like only you know if a pair of shoes fits and is comfortable. We can provide some responses based on your description. 1. If you've been unable to have a married life for five years and your husband doesn't have any health issues, then what is the reason for this? Find the reason and deal with it positively. If your husband is unwilling to cooperate, then you need to consider if this marriage is suitable for you. 2. "Quarreling with your husband over trivial matters and even mentioning divorce every now and then." How old is your husband and is he emotionally mature? What is his perspective on this marriage, and how did you two enter into it in the first place? Have you planned for the future of this marriage? 3. Family is very important for a child's growth, including the atmosphere at home, the relationship between husband and wife, and the overall environment. So, when there are conflicts or adjustments in the early stages of marriage, see how you handle them and if you can handle them well before making a decision to welcome a new life. Best wishes!

Based on the description provided by the poster, it seems like the poster already has an answer in their mind, but they still decided to ask the question. What is the poster seeking by asking this question? I can't remember where I read or heard it, but some people have discussed from a psychological perspective whether there can be a marriage without sex but with love, and whether such a marriage can last or if it can be considered a true marriage. The conclusion is not optimistic, because sex is not only a basic physiological need for humans, it is also the most fundamental and only way for natural organisms to reproduce and survive (to pass on their genes and offspring). It seems that there is no species in nature that is not willing to propagate and perpetuate its existence from generation to generation, becoming stronger and stronger. Therefore, to some extent, a marriage without love but with sex might potentially last longer than a marriage with love but without sex. Personally, I don't think whether to divorce or not is currently the most pressing issue for you. What you need to think about and face right now is perhaps why you are particularly afraid of sexual intimacy. Once you resolve this issue, everything may fall into place. "Having arguments with your husband over trivial matters every few days, even resorting to physical violence" can be seen from a psychodynamic perspective as another form of expression related to sexual intimacy. A marriage without sex is a psychological torment and torture for both your husband and you. By asking this question, it shows that you have already taken the courage to take the first step. Be even braver, face and resolve this issue! Best wishes!

question: Feeling easily trampled upon by others makes me very sad, how can I improve my self-esteem?
description: Recently, I've been constantly reminded of my first job. At that time, I lived and ate together with the boss's wife. She was a Buddhist and a vegetarian, and often advised me to become a vegetarian and believe in Buddhism. I didn't dare to refuse her. We used the same skincare products, shampoo, and shower gel, all placed on the left and right sides of the washbasin. Due to financial difficulties, I would only use a little each time, so a bottle could last me a long time. Many times, she would intentionally or unintentionally suspect me of stealing her things, asking why her things were being used up so quickly while mine lasted so long. I didn't dare to offend her too much, so even though I denied it, she seemed to take it as an admission that I had indeed stolen from her. In reality, she had forgotten that she never hesitated to use her things and often invited her friends and mother to come and stay, and they all used her things. How could her things not be used up quickly? Every time I think about this past experience, I feel that I have such low self-esteem and feel so stifled. Since then, I have been studying psychology and thinking about how to improve my self-esteem and self-love, so that I won't easily let others trample on my self-esteem. That feeling of being easily trampled upon by others makes me very sad.

answers.answer_text: Hug to the original poster. It really doesn't feel good to be suspected and wrongly accused. You didn't dare refuse the boss lady's request; she suspected and falsely accused you of stealing things, and you denied it, but it made her assume her suspicion. You felt unjust and unhappy inside, but you didn't, or rather, you didn't dare express it clearly to her. This happened in your first job when you just entered society, you were relatively young, and didn't know how to handle this kind of social relationship, didn't dare offend others, and didn't dare resist authority. This behavior is normal and also shows that you are sensitive and have a strong self-preservation instinct. Now you can reflect and be aware of the negative impact of this incident and your own behavior, and want to make changes and improvements, which is rare. This process is painful and difficult, but it is also a necessary step for you to change and improve yourself. The enhancement of self-esteem first requires recognizing your inner needs, improving self-confidence, having a firm will in your beliefs and pursuits; you need to have a correct understanding of yourself, see your strengths and advantages, and not neglect your weaknesses. Set goals for your own efforts in life, and then use your strengths and advantages one by one to achieve them, gain successful results, this process and the experience of success can strengthen your confidence and enhance your self-esteem. In addition to focusing on improving self-esteem, there is a need to pay attention to the issue of boundaries. You feel frustrated by the boss lady's behavior, not only because she falsely accused you, but also because she invaded your boundaries, making you feel uncomfortable, even disgusted and afraid. Whether it's family, friends, colleagues, or bosses, it is necessary to establish certain boundaries, maintain a certain social distance with others, maintain one's independence, not interfere with each other's lives and emotions, not overly intrude into others' lives or be intruded by others. If someone invades excessively, they should consider how to distance themselves in order to get out of this easily violated environment. This can also protect your self-esteem. The past is like a thorn stuck in your heart, always feeling uncomfortable, even painful. However, no matter how uncomfortable or regretful you are, the matter is already in the past. Excessive retrospection or getting trapped in it will only intensify your pain and regret, and cannot change the past facts. What you need to do is to quickly ignore the negative impact of this past event on you, focus on the present and the future, and make plans and take action for your own growth. Keep it up!

question: At 13 years old, I was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and I have always been alone.
description: Please, help me, I can't take it anymore. Who am I, really? Don't... don't! Go away! I hate this world!! Stay away! Stay away! I'm begging you! Give up on me!! Phew, I feel better now. It feels so much better to say it out loud. It's been weighing on my mind. Sometimes, I really want to scream, "I want to kill myself, why won't you save me?!" I've always been alone, talking to myself, eating alone, sleeping alone, playing on the computer alone, taking walks alone, wanting to jump off a building alone... Why haven't you come to save me? Am I not worth saving? Or did I do something wrong... Mother, why did you leave me all alone? Why did you fly away like a bird, never to return? I really miss you. Maybe if I wake up from this sleep, you'll come back. Maybe life is just a dream and you woke up before me. I really don't know what to do. I don't want to live, I don't want to do anything, I'm not interested in anything. Maybe I have depression? Well, that's okay. I can finally get some sleep alone. Goodnight, mother.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological crisis.

answers.answer_text: Seeing words as if we are face to face, I hope these words can bring you a little warmth. Child - I hope this term does not offend you - I am glad to see you on this platform, which means you still have hope in life, hoping that someone can lend you a hand. And today is my first day here, this is my first answer. I happen to be 26 years old, twice your age. This is probably our fate - so you see, you are not alone, there is a stranger who saw you at a glance, chose you, you are not alone. Sometimes in life, there are too many things that we cannot understand. It doesn't mean that you are without fault, you are not necessarily loved. I can't just tell you through words that your mother loves you, but she may have her reasons. But I can tell you, "The world is so big, there will always be someone who loves you." If you are in pain, do something else, don't immerse yourself in pain. Read a book, the world in the book is vast and boundless, it can warm you, or maybe make you more sad, but even the most tragic stories have a bit of warmth, the worst life can have a touch of light. Listen to music, it embodies the emotions of many people, whether sad or happy, you can always find a song that resonates with you. Go study - yes, go study, whether it is school subjects or things you love, if you can immerse yourself in learning, you will be completely focused and not think about other problems; it will also allow you to improve and slowly overcome the current difficulties. The road of life is still long, do not give up easily, and do not give up on life. This world is beautiful - I promise. I hope I can say good morning to you tomorrow.

Hello, if you say it out loud, shout it out loud, you might feel a little better, able to take a quiet nap. So when you feel uncomfortable, just say it out loud, shout it out loud. It's okay to cry when you want to, you will feel a little lighter. You mentioned being diagnosed with a split emotional disorder, so have you been persistently seeing a doctor and following their treatment? Don't be afraid, actively cooperate with treatment, and you will gradually improve. At the beginning, when you shouted "Don't come over," who were you shouting at? Another version of yourself? Later, when you mentioned "Why aren't you being saved?", were you talking to another version of yourself as well? Maybe you can tell these things to your family, to someone you trust around you, would that be better? Perhaps someone can help you. You miss your mother a lot, don't you? No matter where your mother has gone, I believe she wants you to live well, to live happily. So, for yourself and for your mother, actively cooperate with the doctor's treatment, believe in yourself, everything will get better and better. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Hug you When you feel life is tough, think of those who are in even more difficult situations but still strive hard. They are not just fighting for themselves, but also for their families. Those children who continue to live on after losing their parents, those left-behind children who don't see their parents for a whole year and have to rely completely on themselves. The original intention of our parents bringing us into this world is for us to be healthy and happy. During our growth, families will go through many things, and parents are ordinary people who have to make choices and face uncontrollable situations. Are you thinking about "death" because you want to gain your mother's love through extreme means? It must be said that during childhood, parents are the most important reliance for children, and it is difficult for children to adjust when this close relationship suddenly breaks. At this moment, any words may seem weak and powerless. I hope you actively cooperate with the doctor's treatment and recover soon. Believe me, besides your parents, there are many people in this world who love you, and you are also worth being loved.

question: How to rescue yourself from habitual staying up late? I feel like I have no self-control, how can I adjust?
description: The bad habit of staying up late has been going on for many years. Sometimes, I feel sleepy around 7 or 10 pm, but I have to stay awake because I haven't finished some work. However, most of the time, I just don't want to sleep early and end up using my phone, unknowingly letting time pass by. I have tried to adjust my schedule before, like trying to turn off the lights at 11 pm for a month. Although I didn't fall asleep as soon as I lay down, I still managed to resist turning on the lights and using my phone. But later, due to some events, I stayed up late once or twice and started to relax, continuing the habit of staying up late. I feel like I have no self-control. How can I adjust myself better?
keywords: Behavior, smartphone addiction, staying up late.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ Firstly, let me give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can understand that: 1. You have a habit of staying up late playing with your phone. 2. You are aware that it's not good for your health, but despite multiple attempts, you lack self-control and cannot change this habit. [A little bit of analysis and advice] 1. Staying up late and constantly using your phone is a common problem among many young people nowadays. It starts with enjoying watching shows, reading novels, and playing games, and eventually becomes a habit. Even when there isn't much to do, you still stay up late browsing Weibo and other content on your phone. Many netizens also understand that this is not good, but find it difficult to improve. 2. It's difficult to resist the allure of smartphones without self-control. On one hand, all the settings on phone apps are designed to make people hold and use their phones for longer periods of time, creating a strong temptation for young people. On the other hand, you mentioned that you have already developed a habit of staying up late. So, perhaps you can consider seeking help from others or using certain apps. For example, after 11:30 PM, you can give your phone to someone else to keep for you, without allowing yourself to have it back under any circumstances. Alternatively, you can use timed locks or set your phone to automatically shut down at a certain time to control yourself. I hope this helps you, OP.

question: I was the victim of phone fraud this afternoon and I feel really upset. What should I do?
description: Today is June 25, 2020. It's Dragon Boat Festival. At 15:00 in the afternoon, I fell victim to a telephone scam and lost 1600 RMB. This might not be a significant amount for most people, and even when I reported the case to the police, they said to me, "Why are you crying? It's not a large sum of money." But I am still a student, with no other source of income other than my parents. My family is not well-off, and I can't even be considered comfortably off. That money was my scholarship and financial aid for this semester, which I worked hard to obtain. I always hesitated to spend it. I deeply regret falling for the scam so easily. Looking back, there were many red flags, but I still fell for it. Was I so naive and stupid? After reporting the case, I didn't want my family to worry, so during our dinner gathering, I pretended to be as usual and enjoyed the Dragon Boat Festival. However, after it ended, I was alone in my room, thinking about the scam today, and I felt really sad and upset. I couldn't control my tears. I really hate the scammers. I am truly heartbroken now. Normally, I am always optimistic and cheerful, but since that scam phone call this afternoon, I haven't been able to find happiness, even when watching my favorite anime. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: My friend, a psychology student, are you feeling more stable now? I don't know if my response is too late or too late, but I wanted to offer you a virtual pat on the back. Because when I was in my third year of college, I also experienced a telecommunications fraud, and at the time, the amount of money I was swindled out of was 3000 yuan. I wasn't able to recover it even after reporting it to the police, and I know the feeling of regret and self-blame. I really want to offer you some comfort. Because I am also an ordinary student, I understand the value of this money even more. As a student, 1600 yuan is indeed not as small as 16 yuan, and it has the added significance of coming from your scholarship. From a psychological perspective, it is normal for unpleasant things to happen and for people to experience negative emotions. It is normal for you to feel sad because it has happened to you. There is no need to force yourself to immediately feel happy. It's okay to give yourself some more time to feel down. This is your moment of sadness, and you can experience it fully. Then give yourself a hug and say, "Hmm, this thing happened, and it's normal for me to feel sad. If it were someone else, they would feel sad too." You mentioned that you need to hold it together in front of your parents, eat well, and speak well. From these behaviors, it seems that I can see your small worries about your parents. Are you afraid of being blamed by them? If you feel afraid of being blamed, then don't tell them, it's okay. After weighing the options, deciding to face hardships alone is also a sign of maturity. If the financial loss from this incident is still within your manageable range, you have the right to choose to bear it yourself. Many adults also do the same. Oh, and about being deceived, no matter how many cases there are, it's not the same as experiencing it personally. Many people are knowledgeable about fraud cases, but it's always difficult to avoid falling for scams. The reason for this is that empathy is a difficult thing. Before being scammed, we cannot truly understand the professionalism and rigor of the scammers' words, nor can we truly experience the change in our state of mind when fraud occurs. Fraud groups usually work as a team, creating a tense atmosphere and challenging us in various ways. Our individual strength is easily conquered by fraud groups. However, after this experience, your "immune system" against fraud will be greatly improved. Congratulations, you have completed an experience of being scammed. I believe that after this small scam, your alertness will be higher. I think that if similar scams happen to you in the future, you will be more calm and composed.

You may not believe it, but 12 years ago, I went to Shanghai to work and got scammed for 100 yuan. I discovered it right away, but I didn't dare to speak up because there were many men around, similar to thugs. At that time, my salary was 2000 yuan and rent was 500 yuan, so 100 yuan was a considerable expense for me. Moreover, I didn't dare to tell anyone for fear of being laughed at, as it was my greed that caused it. That afternoon, I returned to the rented house, filled with regret, fear, worry, anger, and sadness. I couldn't calm down from these various emotions. But today, with a monthly salary of 8000 yuan, that incident is already in the past. I can truly understand your feelings, as I deeply regret it and feel extremely sad. I feel so foolish, but since that incident, I have never been scammed again. Friends of mine were scammed for thousands of yuan due to brushing orders or other reasons, but not me, because I can never forget the pain I felt at that time. This lesson was bought with money, and it was truly worth it. What you need to do now is to take out your phone, watch a happy movie, distract yourself slowly, and don't keep thinking about this incident. I guarantee that you will feel better when you wake up tomorrow. In a year, you won't even feel anything. After ten years, you will realize that this lesson was worth buying.

Good morning, classmate. This reminds me of a time between 2004 and 2005. Oh! It was more than ten years ago. I don't know if you are familiar with a communication device called "xiaolingtong". Although it wasn't expensive back then, I had only one when I graduated from college. I was facing difficulties in my job, no money, and no successful entrepreneurship. It was the most frustrating time of my life, but I couldn't talk to my parents about it and I had thousands of dollars in debt to repay. Looking back now, I realize that I am facing a similar situation, but the debt now is due to my studies. It has brought me a different kind of wealth though. Anyway, the point is that we can look at things from a different perspective. Going back to that time more than ten years ago, perhaps because I was young, I didn't think much of being in debt. I believed that as long as I worked hard, I would be able to repay it and start again. So I thought about how to earn income and find a job. At that time, the internet was not as developed as it is now, so we didn't have much communication. Through a newspaper, I found a job related to my field of study, accounting. In the specialized job section, I saw a company with good working hours, location, and salary, so I called the boss. I went for an interview, but back then I only had a few dollars in my pocket. I don't remember the exact amount, but it wasn't my money. It was borrowed from my best friend, who was still a university student at the time but doing part-time jobs. When I met the so-called boss, I had a feeling that something wasn't right, and I believe you may have experienced a similar intuition in your own situation. However, for some reason, we tend to ignore those intuitions and I don't know why. Maybe it's related to our desires. At that time, I was desperate for a job. The person claiming to be the boss said their phone was broken, out of battery, and asked to borrow my "xiaolingtong" to make a call. I told them my phone could only receive calls because I hadn't paid the bill. They said it was alright and just needed to make one call, then asked me to wait while they went to find someone. They never came back after using my phone. I vividly remember standing there like a fool for half an hour before I realized that I had probably been scammed. I went to the location mentioned in the newspaper, but there was no such company. And I wasn't the first one, and now I realize that I probably wasn't the last one either. Later, I reported it to the police, but even after more than ten years, there has been no result. Afterward, I got sick with anger and couldn't recover. Now, thinking back to that time, I feel really miserable and heartbreaking. But during that difficult time, I gained good friends. One of them cooked for me when I was bedridden and I even considered drinking porridge a luxury. She searched all the nearby restaurants near our rented apartment in the afternoon but didn't find any rice available. Eventually, she found a place that served rice and brought me a bowl of porridge and some food (we were living together at that time), and she also helped me with a large portion of the rent. Another friend gave me advice. At that time, I was doing carpet business for night markets. In the city I am in now, there is a famous night market where people take trendy photos. There was a spot there that didn't require fighting for space, so I could set up my stall there. I didn't have the money, but she lent me 200 yuan (she was already working at that time, making less than 800 yuan a month). I don't know where she got that money from. I set up my carpet stall right in front of her glasses store, and I remember it was from October until the following year's Spring Festival. I was selling my products in front of her store for the whole winter, and after closing, I left my items inside her shop. Her boss at that time was also a good person. At that time, I didn't have the "xiaolingtong" anymore, and I didn't have money to buy a new one. I knew her boyfriend had a spare phone, so I borrowed it. It didn't have a phone number, so she bought a new one for me and prepared a phone card. I used that phone for two years and returned it to her only after I had repaid all my debts. Actually, this may not directly answer your question but rather shed light on my own experience and finding healing through reexamining it. I also realize my current situation and that I can still strive like I did fifteen years ago because I am more capable now. The difficulties I encounter now are not a problem for me. Here are my suggestions for you: 1. Change your mindset. Just because we encounter such situations doesn't mean we cannot overcome them. It can actually serve as a reminder for us to face and solve problems. I saw that you reported it to the police (even though it didn't have a big impact), but at least I believe your self-protection awareness will be heightened in the future. 2. Move forward. This money is important to you because it represents recognition for your hard work. So think about how you obtained and lost the money and consider how you will handle financial matters in the future. I sense that you value money a lot, but you've overlooked your own abilities. 3. Share your feelings. Find someone you trust and confide in them about the whole experience. This kind of release can provide you with more insights and help you find peace within yourself regarding the situation. 4. Improve your self-protection awareness. Nowadays, with advanced communication technology, scammers are becoming more sophisticated. We can't prevent all of it, but you can search online for information on how to deal with these situations. Lastly, it's not the setbacks that are scary, but the lack of ability to solve problems after encountering difficulties. I hope you can face and resolve the challenges you currently face and emerge from them with a positive attitude. Thank you for your question, it made me confront my own past experience, and I see it as the beginning of change.

question: How can I deal with the recurring fantasies about sexual psychology issues that are driving me crazy?
description: I am a girl, in my twenties. When I was a child, I accidentally watched my parents' adult videos. At that time, I felt a mix of excitement and shame, and I even felt a bit addicted to the thrill. Once, when playing house with friends, I wanted to discreetly reenact certain actions, but I had to give up because my playmates objected. Because I was young back then, after a long time passed, I didn't feel anything about it anymore. I could play with friends normally and didn't think about it anymore. However, after starting middle school, my younger sister showed me a romance novel, and there was a small part that described a sexual encounter. It was like opening the door to a new world for me, I never knew books could also contain love and that kind of content. After that, I started reading online novels, mainly those with similar explicit scenes. I even searched for videos from TV dramas and movies with erotic content. Nowadays, I feel mentally exhausted every few days, fantasizing about being intimate with someone and even engaging in simple self-stimulation. But right now, I want to focus on my studies and not pursue romantic relationships. However, these recurring sexual fantasies are driving me crazy. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, after reading your description, I can sense your confusion regarding the issue of "sex". From your description, I have summarized a few points: you have unintentionally been exposed to some scenarios related to "sex" in the past, which allowed you to experience the physical stimulation caused by "sex" at an early age. Now you feel troubled by frequent "sexual fantasies" and want to know if there is a way to resolve this distress. Based on your description, I would like to share my opinion: "sex" is a mechanism that exists in human instinctive survival. In certain contexts, our bodies generate impulses, which is a very normal phenomenon. "Sex" needs to objectively exist because, as members of a diverse species, humans also need to survive. In order for humans to survive normally, reproduction is necessary (human life is finite and humans also need to undergo evolution). Therefore, when our bodies generate impulses in special contexts, there is no need to be overly anxious. It is a survival mechanism that we, as members of life, must possess. We need to correctly understand the "sexual impulses" that occur from time to time. The frequent occurrence of "sexual fantasies" can indeed disrupt the order of our daily lives. We need to learn to recognize it properly and, when necessary, redirect or release it. 1⃣️ When "sexual fantasies" occur, we can divert their impact on our bodies through physical exercise. Physical exercise consumes energy and can also result in a healthier physical condition. After engaging in physical exercise, the impulses caused by "sexual fantasies" will decrease along with the energy consumption's influence on our bodies. 2⃣️ When necessary, we can learn to appropriately release the impulses caused by "sexual fantasies". This can be achieved through "masturbation" as a way to release that impulse. (If the frequency is controlled well, it can effectively reduce pressure and release the impulse). Best wishes.

Hello: Sexual fantasies generally arise from unfulfilled sexual desires or delayed satisfaction. Our culture is inherently conservative, so many children are not allowed to talk about sex or ask questions related to sex, as it is considered "shameful". As a result, most children can only suppress their curiosity and dare not inquire further. However, as the saying goes, "where there is oppression, there will be resistance." Analyzing the problem: 1. You are a woman in your 20s. When you were a child, you accidentally watched your parents' adult films and found them exciting but also slightly shameful. There was even a sense of addictive pleasure. One time, while playing house with friends, you wanted to discreetly reenact certain actions, but you gave up due to your playmate's opposition. (Playing house is a childhood game. This happens to be what Freud called the "Oedipus complex" stage, the first stage of sexual development in which children become curious about their opposite-sex parents and exhibit sexual reactions. However, they themselves do not know what it means. At this stage, parents need to provide proper guidance to children without blame or using words like "shame", slowly helping them understand that sex is a normal matter. They are just young.) 2. Because you were young at that time, you forgot about this matter after a long period of time. You could play normally with friends and no longer thought about it. (Childhood matters can be forgotten over time, but the feelings stay in the heart and may resurface in certain images or events.) 3. However, after starting middle school, your younger sister showed you a romance novel that included a few explicit descriptions, which opened a whole new world for you. You didn't know that such content could be written in books. (Middle school is the adolescence period, the second stage of development, when hormone levels are unstable. The scenes and settings described in novels trigger vague memories from your childhood, but what's most important is the "feeling" you mentioned. It attracted you, especially the mysterious aspect of the invisible words.) 4. After that, you started reading online literature, mainly focusing on novels that contained similar explicit scenes. You even searched for videos from erotic TV shows and movies. Now, you feel mentally drained every few days and fantasize about intimate moments with someone, occasionally engaging in masturbation. (I am a sex counselor and a sexual education counselor for adolescents. Many people think it's wrong to discuss sex, but if we don't talk about it, do children not want to understand? They have too many methods and ways, just like the Internet being so accessible now. Learning about sex through the Internet can easily lead to an incorrect understanding of sex, making many children believe they are mature and knowledgeable, when in reality, it accelerates their development prematurely. Because they didn't engage in sexual activities and enjoy sex or understand its meaning at the right age.) 5. However, you now want to prioritize your studies and don't want to pursue romantic relationships, but the constant urges from sexual fantasies are driving you crazy. What should you do? (It's great that you prioritize your studies. Sexual fantasies themselves are not a problem; just like everyone has fantasies, why is it suddenly not okay when it comes to sex? Perhaps what you need to think about is not the pain caused by the sexual fantasies, but the pain caused by not allowing yourself to have sexual fantasies. If you have the opportunity, we can communicate and delve into this matter.) Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you can find peace and resolution soon! If you have any concerns, feel free to message me!

Hello~ I understand your feelings very well. Hugs to you~ Regarding sex education, most of us have limited exposure to it, so there are many misconceptions about sex. Having occasional sexual fantasies is not a big problem, so don't worry too much. Healthy sexual fantasies are perfectly normal. Sexual fantasies are not only for a few people; research shows that 98% of adults continuously have, or at least have had, some sexual fantasies. When you have sexual fantasies, there's no need to feel ashamed or think that you are the only one who thinks that way, or even blame yourself. "Having some fantasies about sex is actually a normal human behavior, it can be seen as a manifestation of imagination, just that this imagination is about sex, or it can generate sexual arousal or desire for you." If you can control your sexual fantasies and they do not harm yourself or others, then you can relax. Your sexual fantasies are healthy and something that most people experience. Take care~

First of all, your curiosity and desire for sex are normal physiological and psychological phenomena, which are not problems in themselves and should not be overly concerned about. However, the shame and guilt that arise from this have had a significant impact on your normal life, which is the problem. The focus should be on why something that should be normal causes you intense shame and embarrassment. It's important to understand that people your age are naturally exposed to sexually related information and fantasies and masturbation are also normal phenomena. However, due to societal moral beliefs, human sexuality has been artificially mystified and made private, making it something that is not suitable for open discussion or exploration. As a result, most people are more discreet when it comes to sex and handle their sexual desires in a hidden manner, which easily leads to associating sex with shame. Your current problem is that you have magnified the sense of shame, causing internal conflicts and an inability to accept your own needs and behaviors, which in turn prevents you from integrating your physiological and psychological needs with your practical learning and daily life. Therefore, you need to try to treat sexual desires correctly: recognize that as an adult, the need for sexual love, the desire for the opposite sex, and the satisfaction of sexual desires are all normal and natural. There is no need to label them with moral condemnation. Once you have a correct understanding, the sense of secrecy and stimulation will decrease, gradually normalizing it, without falling into obsession. So as long as you develop a proper understanding and gradually diminish the influence of sexual desires on yourself, refrain from excessive masturbation, you will gradually integrate them with a normal academic and daily life, no longer being troubled by them.

Hello. From the comprehensive feedback on your mental health issues, it seems that you feel ashamed or guilty about having sexual fantasies and engaging in masturbation. However, it is important to understand that sexual desires are natural instincts, just like the need for water. Occasionally having sexual thoughts or indulging in self-pleasure is normal and does not go against our inherent desires. The problem lies in our cognitive distortion, specifically, the evaluation mechanism of events, which affects our emotional state. If deep down you believe that a girl should not have sexual fantasies or engage in masturbation, then when you have these thoughts or masturbate, you will experience inner conflict, shame, and even self-denial. Who we should be and who we actually are are two completely different aspects. The former is the ideal self, while the latter is the real self. Accepting yourself and letting go of internal constraints will lead to inner liberation. Internally, we need to recognize that having sexual fantasies or engaging in masturbation is a normal expression for adults. Only when you think this way can you let go of the burden in your heart. Treat yourself well, as sex is pure. You don't need to feel conflicted or guilty about your sexual thoughts. Maintain a calm mind and accept, recognize, and embrace yourself. Cultivate new interests for yourself, plan your life well, and when desires are strong, you can reduce exposure to similar videos, cut down on alone time, engage in exhilarating exercise, or develop hobbies to enrich your life, as life is not only about sex. Let's encourage each other.

Give the OP a hug! You can feel the OP's inner suppression, anxiety, and conflict. It seems that the issue of "sex" has brought a lot of distress to the OP. These pressures have become unbearable for the OP's heart. When the OP was young, they accidentally saw their parents' adult videos. As a child, they didn't understand what it was and couldn't comprehend the content of the videos. They didn't know what their parents were doing. They just instinctively felt that being naked in front of the opposite sex was "embarrassing" and "shameful." At the same time, the content of the videos stimulated the OP, especially the facial expressions and sounds made by the people in them, which gave the OP some pleasure. At this point, a new cognition indirectly formed in the OP's brain: feeling ashamed can lead to pleasure, so feeling ashamed equals pleasure. For the OP's conscious self, being naked and exposing their body to the opposite sex is embarrassing and shameful. They might be laughed at and looked down upon by others, and their conscious self needs to protect themselves, so they reject accepting themselves doing that. However, in adult sexual relationships, it is necessary to fulfill one's physiological needs by exposing the body and having intimate contact. These behaviors should take place in a relatively closed and private space, which is also a way to protect oneself. But for the subconscious self, taking off one's clothes is a "liberation" of their body. They no longer have to endure the sense of confinement brought by clothes and can freely have physical contact with others. This kind of contact is purely a connection and does not involve any sexual desire. It is the "sexual" contact of a minor. In other words, the issue that troubles the OP is that they have mixed adult sexual desires with the physical contact of a minor. They can't figure out whether they are seeking adult sexual satisfaction or satisfaction from the physical contact of a minor. They simply instinctively do it, such as the details mentioned by the OP when reading "network novels". This kind of physical contact can be said to be the demand of the OP's subconscious self, meaning that what they want is more physical contact. At the same time, as an adult, the OP also has physiological needs and needs to have intimate physical contact with the opposite sex. This kind of intimate contact overlaps and confuses with the physical intimate contact needed by the subconscious self, which makes the OP feel extremely "ashamed" of their needs. However, this "shame" in the OP's heart also reflects their negative perception of themselves, their thoughts are somewhat paranoid, and they have a pursuit of perfection. They can try to accept these troubles first, and be aware of the emotional feelings behind these troubles, what they want to achieve, write down these emotional feelings, and annotate the corresponding emotional projection objects behind them, release and relieve the pressure in their hearts. So that their needs can be fulfilled, and the troubles they bring to themselves can be reduced, allowing the OP to face studying and life with ease and naturalness.

Hello, I hope the following answer can help you: "Food and sex are both natural instincts of human beings. However, due to societal development and certain needs, sex has become a product of social gender roles, leading to a sense of secrecy and concealment. Sex is not a sin, and sexual fantasies are not a sin either. Love is not a sin, and making love should not be seen as a sin either. Why do people feel "driven crazy" because of sexual fantasies? It is because sex violates the taboos deeply ingrained in traditional culture. However, just like eating, sex is a basic human need and desire. Seeking something you cannot openly pursue creates both conflict and joy - it is a "forbidden" pleasure. Looking at the history of sexual development, the "stigmatization" of sex has always been a part of human progress, particularly evident in patriarchal societies. This can be summed up as the "sexual stigma syndrome" (Fang Gang). For example: the belief that sex is dirty, that sexual organs are dirty, that sexual behavior is dirty, that all words and actions associated with sex are bad, that menstruation is bad and dirty, that only virgins are pure and non-virgins are impure... By adjusting our sexual beliefs, we no longer need to fear sexual fantasies. Without fear, we can even enjoy the feeling of sexual fantasies and no longer feel the "driven crazy" sensation. Perhaps we won't even crave sexual fantasies as much. Then we can address our love problems and focus on our studies. Wishing you the best and I suggest seeking specialized counseling for psychological development (such as sexual psychology). I'm here and the world loves you."

Hello, OP, first of all, here's a big hug for you~ The main problem you are facing now is that you need to focus on your studies and don't want to have a romantic relationship, but you feel confused by frequent sexual fantasies. ◆ Embarrassment ◆ Fantasizing When you were young, you accidentally watched your parents' adult movies, and at that time, you found it exciting but also felt slightly ashamed. It seemed to give you a kind of addictive pleasure. Since few of us had the opportunity to receive comprehensive sex education when we were young and were still in a stage of innocence and curiosity regarding the topic of "sex", it's understandable that you had thoughts about watching adult movies. When you were in middle school, your sister showed you a romance novel that included some explicit scenes. This was like opening the door to a new world: you didn't know that books could also contain love and that kind of content. After that, you started reading online novels, mainly those with explicit descriptions, and even searched for erotic videos from some TV shows and movies. Now, you feel mentally exhausted every few days and experience pleasurable sensations while fantasizing about being intimate with someone, even to the point of masturbating. During the period of middle school, your body was going through puberty and you started experiencing primal sexual impulses, so the phenomena you mentioned are quite normal. According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory, human needs can be categorized into five levels, from basic to higher-level needs: physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs. In other words, once a person's basic needs like hunger, thirst, and elimination are satisfied, they start seeking higher-level needs for safety, social interaction, approval, and self-fulfillment. Sex belongs to one of the physiological needs; it is the most basic need. Therefore, when no one is around to answer your questions or relieve your confusion about sex, you resort to fantasy. This is also why sexual fantasies can impact your normal life. According to Freud's theory of psychoanalysis, he believed that sexual desire and its energy (libido) are inherent in all individuals, including infants, although their manifestations differ from adults. He suggested that during adolescence, sexual consciousness awakens, a fascination with the opposite sex emerges, and there is a fixed pattern of desire for union with them, which indicates the maturation of sexual psychology. Freud also believed that as individuals develop and age, there are significant differences in the expression of sexuality and libido. This can also explain your current situation. So, having sexual awareness and fantasies is actually quite normal. It might be due to the influence of social norms that sex is seen as such a prominent issue, but fundamentally, sex is no different from appetite or the urge to eliminate waste, and there is no standard for which one is higher or lower. Nuan Nuan thinks you can have some understanding of sex, grasp its essence, not overly concern yourself with it, and ensure that it doesn't harm your body. Maintaining sexual fantasies is a normal thing. If your attention is not focused on studying because of these fantasies, you can put down your phone and make detailed plans. Put the plan somewhere visible, and once you complete a task, cross it off and replace the urge for sex with a sense of satisfaction and achievement. Finally, Nuan Nuan wishes you success in your studies and a promising future.

Dear, give me a hug. I feel like I see my past self in you. I believe there are thousands of girls who are just like us. From your description, I think there are a few areas in which you need to improve. First, have a positive attitude towards sexuality and face it directly. It is because of sex that humans reproduce and culture is passed down. Sexual desire is just like any other desires we have. As Confucius said, "Food and sex are the primal desires." Don't treat it as something overly serious or shameful. We feel ashamed mainly because of the environment we grew up in and traditional education that taught us to be embarrassed about sex. Second, self-awareness. It's commendable that you are aware of and reflect on your past experiences. Many of our current habits and ways of thinking are influenced by our upbringing. Now that we understand how our past experiences have shaped us, we should detach ourselves from those experiences and let the past be the past. Since we now have needs and desires, what's wrong with admitting it? Let's first acknowledge it, then accept it, and finally find ways to improve. Third, balancing learning and sexual desires. We should first acknowledge that it's normal to have thoughts, fantasies, and even masturbate. Secondly, if we have these thoughts, then occasionally fulfill ourselves. Put effort into our studies, make progress, and occasionally reward ourselves. Read a book, masturbate, just be mindful of the frequency. It's okay to make ourselves happier occasionally, and when we are unhappy, we can console ourselves, vent a little, and distract ourselves. Loving oneself starts with being honest with oneself. Wishing you learn how to please yourself and accept your whole self with courage.

question: Why is it that the ex is always so unforgettable? Is it because I haven't met someone I really like?
description: I like a boy, but it seems like he has not yet healed from the damage caused by his ex. However, he doesn't reject my contact with him, including my confession to him. He also says that the current situation is not suitable. So, is he really not over it yet, or is it just an excuse?

answers.answer_text: Hello, the brave confession from the questioner deserves praise, but I can also sense your confusion because we have had too much "chicken soup for the soul." I believe you have also heard similar statements, such as exes being unforgettable because the current one is not good enough. In reality, it depends on the dynamics between the two individuals. Firstly, if he broke up with his ex, it means that they had reasons why they couldn't continue together. But because they loved each other, he needs time to heal his wounds, which also shows that he is a loyal and sentimental guy. Even if you can be together later, you cannot demand that he completely forget his ex, which is something we can't do. Secondly, he doesn't reject your contact, accepts your confession openly, and honestly tells you that he is not in the right state at the moment. The positive side is that he also has the attitude and intention to move on from the past, but the downside is that he hasn't moved on yet, so he can't promise to be with you immediately. The above is a brief analysis based on the description you provided. The specific reasons depend on the attitudes he shows when you spend time together. As a girl, while making efforts, don't be too fixated and don't let yourself get hurt. May everything be well! True love will prevail in the end.

question: What should be done if a 17-year-old girl, who has a tendency towards violence, has already seriously harmed her family?
description: My mother used to say that I had a problem with my personality, but I never really realized it. However, I have, to some extent, known that I have a tendency towards violence. Today, I finally understand that I cannot let it continue to develop, especially because I have hurt my family members several times. I have been experiencing insomnia for a long time now. What should I do?
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, pathological personality, abnormal behavior.

answers.answer_text: I am not sure what you have been through, nor do I know the circumstances under which you are experiencing this. I suggest that you can go to a hospital for a comprehensive examination. Most larger tertiary hospitals have psychological departments where you can first check if it is due to physiological reasons, and then explore your own psychological reasons. If you find it difficult to regulate yourself, I recommend seeking a psychological counselor. I hope my answer can help you. I wish you well.

It appears that you are somewhat worried about your inability to control your "violent tendencies". You are very anxious about this issue. Is there really a problem with violence? Would you like to describe in detail the situations where this issue arises? How do you feel when your mother says you have a personality problem? Do you feel hurt? And it seems that you also agree with your mother's remarks. I think behind "violence" lies an unfulfilled desire. Would you be willing to carefully consider what you hope to achieve through "violence"?

question: Can I use housework to supplement my husband's low income?
description: My husband is from out of town, and we live in a first-tier city. Both my husband and I are working class, and we didn't buy a house when we got married. Now we have a two-year-old son, and I am the one who covers most of the daily expenses. My husband owed 100,000 yuan after renting a house for a year, and his family helped to cover most of it. Now we are living in my parents' house. The monthly expenses for our son's nursery school are high, and my husband and I split the cost equally. He voluntarily helps with washing dishes and taking care of our child, which I think is acceptable. However, recently he mentioned wanting to buy a car, and I got a little angry because I would be the one paying for it. I initially wanted to buy one too, but him suggesting it made me upset. I told him that I am already covering most of the household expenses on my own. Utilities and groceries are small expenses, but there are also expenses for our child's early education. Over time, these small expenses add up. Can't you earn more? He said he hadn't thought about it, and now I don't know what to say. He asked if washing dishes after work every day and helping out weren't enough to make up for it. I'm a bit confused and would like to ask everyone how to deal with this.

answers.answer_text: Hello, and after carefully reading your question description, I understand that your current dilemma is the troubles with your husband in family life. [The conflicts and misunderstandings may arise from different perspectives] From your question, I see that you are the main financial provider for the family, while your husband is more responsible for the household chores. From a time cost perspective, both of you have contributed equally to the family because you both spend the same amount of time working or busy with household tasks. However, this issue has caused conflicts because your husband believes that he has also worked and invested time, which is the time cost perspective. Your perspective, on the other hand, focuses more on the economic income and expenses. You feel that your husband does not contribute enough financially. Therefore, due to these different perspectives, there is a deviation in comparison. If we calculate everything in terms of economic costs, neither of you have time to do the housework, which means you need to hire someone to help. In that case, your husband's income can be supplemented by the cost of hiring help. This would be a reasonable calculation. [In the family, there should be more understanding and encouragement to maintain emotions] In the family, we often fall into invisible power struggles such as "who contributes more." Especially traditional women are often considered to have little contribution to the family. However, in reality, doing housework and taking care of children are significant hidden expenses. Especially the companionship and care for children are priceless. Good parenting and companionship are very valuable for a child's growth. Therefore, the emotional connection between spouses is very precious, and any form of comparison only erodes the emotions between each other. There should be more understanding and less comparison and complaint. If possible, pay attention to your husband's abilities at work and encourage him to do work that he is good at earning money. Less complaining does not mean not saying anything, but rather presenting suggestions and discussing ideas in a way that considers the long-term perspective of the family, helping him brainstorm and strategize, rather than blaming and venting emotions. This will actually heat up your marital relationship.

In your description, I noticed a sentence that says, "Can you earn more money?" He said he hadn't thought about it, and you were speechless. From this sentence, it is possible that my feeling is he hasn't understood his responsibility yet, or maybe in daily life, you have also shared some things, so he doesn't feel the pressure. In general, within a family, men may have more financial responsibilities, and it seems like the other person may not be as aware or as worried as you. If you want him to earn more money, you can make him spend more on daily expenses and see if it can motivate him to make more money. Instead of wanting to buy a car and using your money, which will also make you very tired. You would have to work harder. So you can let him take on more responsibilities as the head of the family. Also, he owes 100,000, which his family has helped him pay off. From this perspective, his family may also provide him with some support, so when you ask him if he can earn more money and he says he can't, it may be because he has the support behind him, and it is not known whether it has formed a dependency. Maybe some people really can't make money, and the money they make may not be as much as the woman's, but that does not mean it is impossible. It just means they have no advantage in this aspect. However, it requires the woman to put in more effort and bear more daily hardships. If they really can't earn that much money but haven't forgotten to do household chores, it is actually okay because some people may really not be good at making money. Another thing is that some things that a person didn't know before can be learned in certain emergencies. It's like a person who has nothing to eat and their stomach is growling. To avoid being hungry, they may go pick up things to eat, collect bottles and cardboard to sell. Certain abilities of a person need to be stimulated in certain situations.

Hello, after reading your account, I would like to give my opinion. Both of you are now a family, already parents, and both are working-class. Your family's financial situation is not affluent, and sometimes you even struggle to make ends meet. You rely on support from your elderly family members, but it truly seems there is no other way. Housing, children's education, and even buying a car are all necessary. If you hope for your husband to earn more money, it may prove difficult since both of you are in the same workforce. You should understand his situation and ensure that the quality of life is not too poor. In such times, it is unnecessary to argue over who contributes more financially or who does more household chores. You are already one family, so each person should do their best and contribute what they can for the future of the family. As for whether or not to buy a car, it would be best for both of you to discuss it together. Whether you contribute the money or your husband does, as long as you live a good life, it shouldn't matter who pays. Furthermore, he does understand you and even takes the initiative to do household chores after work every day. This shows that he is also very willing to contribute to the family. He is just temporarily unable to do so financially, and it must be difficult for him mentally, with a lot of pressure. Give him some encouragement and support, and he will understand your concerns. There is nothing more important than a harmonious and happy family. Best wishes to you both.

Hello, based on your description, I have a general understanding of your current concerns. You mentioned that there are some differences between you and your spouse regarding finances. For example, he wants to buy a car, but you may feel that he doesn't fully appreciate the hard work you put into earning money. In an intimate relationship, apart from emotional commitment, day-to-day communication, especially regarding financial matters, can greatly affect the relationship. If not handled properly, these issues will keep resurfacing. You mentioned that both of you split expenses, but it's unclear in what aspect, such as living expenses or other aspects. I don't have a clear understanding of how your family's finances are managed. Since you have children and you both have no major problems between you, this is the premise. Now, let's discuss how to improve the situation together. When two people have a good relationship and can calm down, they can discuss future plans together. For example, if you feel that you're not earning enough money, maybe you can consider doing some part-time work or looking for opportunities on top of your stable job. Of course, this depends on the circumstances around you, and there's no need to force anything. Secondly, regarding your daily expenses, it's advisable to list down the family's expenses, such as education expenses, living expenses, rent, and other future plans like purchasing a house. In terms of savings, it would be best to divide the money into several portions, preferably pooling both of your incomes together and entrusting one person to manage the finances. For any major expenses, it's better to consult each other. This approach is beneficial for the stability of your relationship in the long run. The specifics of how to proceed need to be discussed between you and your spouse. Don't let money become a reason for conflicts or say things out of spite. All the best!

question: I cannot participate in the high school entrance examination. How should I face my future?
description: It's been less than a month since school started, and I haven't started reviewing yet. I have wasted two years of my education. I dropped out before due to depression, and now I don't even know if I can go to school or what grade I should be in. Last semester, I was supposed to start attending school and repeat a grade, but right before it started, they said I couldn't go and to wait for the next semester. And now I heard that because of my situation, I won't be able to take the entrance exam and will have to repeat another grade. The thing that bothers me the most is my extreme procrastination. Sometimes I even put off brushing my teeth and washing my face until the afternoon or simply skip it altogether. If I do shower, I procrastinate until daytime. As for my education, year after year has been wasted by me. I tried making a plan to overcome procrastination, but because of my unstable condition, I can't seem to settle down. I have been staring at the paper for two days without being able to write anything. Now even the plan itself has been put off until today, and I truly don't know how to start my future.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, first of all, give you a hug, it is said that hugs can give people strength, I hope you can feel this strength and then improve procrastination. Yes, it is to improve procrastination, not to conquer it. You should know that procrastination is something that everyone experiences. It is possible to have procrastination emotions in every task. This is a difficult problem to cure, so we can only improve this procrastination habit while still procrastinating. So, OP, don't feel discouraged. You are able to seek help now, which shows that you have the mindset to change. There is a theory that a person's decision to do something is influenced by internal motivation and external factors, with internal motivation being the most important factor. And your desire to change is internal motivation. Maintain this motivation and start with small things, such as deciding to brush your teeth when you wake up in the morning, or to take a shower when it gets dark in the evening. I believe that after you do these small things, you will gain some insights on how to resolve your situation. When I saw that you decided to write a plan, I wanted to share my experience with you. Today is a rare weekend, and I wanted to make the most of this time to do more things. I made plans for the morning and afternoon, and the schedule was very tight. I did have a lot of motivation in the morning, but in the afternoon, I just didn't feel like doing anything. I didn't do any of the planned tasks for the afternoon. At that moment, I understood that when making plans, it is important to set aside time for rest. Only by balancing work and rest can we accomplish more. I also recommend that you take a look at the book "The Psychology of Procrastination". It provides a detailed insight into the emotions of procrastination and is very enlightening. You mentioned not knowing if you will be able to attend school because of the uncertain situation and the inability to settle down. These are external factors that are difficult to control. It might be better for you to focus on the present. Look up the curriculum outline for middle school subjects online and start reviewing. This way, when the day comes to find a good school, you can calmly catch up with the learning progress. I don't know if your depression has improved. You must face it positively and work towards healing it. In the movie "3 Idiots", there is a line that says, "Everything will be fine." OP, you should also believe that everything will be fine. Best wishes~.

question: After entering college, my emotions have been fluctuating greatly, especially in terms of daily life. What is wrong with me?
description: I am a sensitive and fragile person. Now I am in college. Before college, when I interacted with classmates or people of the same age, although I would feel sad because of their actions, there wasn't anything that I couldn't bear. In college, at the beginning of the dormitory, there were eight people. I would think about finding someone I felt was relatively good to be friends with for a long time. We would get angry with each other sometimes, but arguing is normal. There isn't a perfect match. I also know that many times, the things I care about, others don't feel. Every time, the point that makes me sad is when she clearly knows what I care about, but sometimes she still does it, and when I'm upset and silent, she tells others that it's okay, give it some time and she'll be fine. When I'm feeling down, I want to go out and relax, so I asked another friend who went to the same school if she can come out and accompany me, after making sure she doesn't have anything else to do. I was really sad at that time, crying and texting while walking, but she refused. She said maybe tomorrow, but I didn't say anything after that. It was clear that she said we were the closest, but it's difficult. I tried to not care about anything, but later I realized that if you don't care, nobody will care about you. And I feel like if I don't care about anything, it's not me anymore, but I also don't want to not care about anything. Sigh.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear reader, sending you a virtual hug~ Based on your description, it seems that you have been experiencing sensitive and fragile emotions during your time in college. It's understandable that recent conflicts with friends have led to significant fluctuations in your mood. I empathize with your situation. From your description, it seems that there are certain concerns you have that others may not easily perceive.
