However, I believe that if you don't clearly communicate these concerns to your friends, they may simply forget about them. After all, in college, everyone is busy with their own priorities and concerns. It's important not to have excessively high expectations of ordinary friendships. I'm aware that your recent emotional sensitivity is a cause for concern. Sudden changes in personality and emotional stability in one's life require attention. If possible, you could consider seeking medical or psychological counseling to help you through this.

question: In college, being isolated by roommates, no matter how hard you try to improve the situation, it seems futile. What should I do when it hurts so much?
description: In college, I have been isolated by my roommate, experiencing various forms of neglect and emotional abuse. Despite my efforts, they continue to disregard me and isolate me, playing mind games with me. I am sincere to others, but I constantly get hurt. What should I do? I feel very uncomfortable and hurt in college. What should I do?
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, trauma therapy, counseling and listening.

answers.answer_text: Dear OP, hello! From your words and between the lines, I can sense a lonely child seeking warmth in their own embrace. Allow me to give you a big hug. Facing isolation may be extremely difficult for you, dear OP, but remember, the beginning is always the hardest part. In college, within the confines of a small room, we encounter people from all walks of life, each with their own unique experiences. We cannot demand acceptance from others, but what can we do? We can improve ourselves and maintain our own integrity. The first step to overcoming isolation is to strengthen ourselves. College is a microcosm of society, and perhaps you haven't found like-minded friends in your dorm, but does that mean you won't meet others around the next corner? Try to find new friends, establish a new support system, and gain new strength from it. Friends may not be numerous but genuine friends are precious. We don't need friends all over the world; we just need to treat others with sincerity. Believe that in the future, you will still meet more people and selectively make friends with them, creating an even better connection. Looking for new interests doesn't mean your life is lacking. OP, you can start exploring new hobbies. Life is colorful because of the existence of various things. Through these new interests, vent your negative emotions and gain positive energy, using them to propel yourself further in the future.

Give you a comforting hug. The world is so big, you don't need to live to please your roommate, you need to live for yourself first. When I was in college, at first it was difficult for me to fit in with my college group, especially with my roommates, because we came from different cities, different educational backgrounds, and had different personalities. The first year of adjustment was very, very difficult. Everyone needs to restrain themselves and adapt to this group, try to be accepted by everyone, and work hard to become the popular person. But I found that this process consumes a lot of myself. It's like, in order to fit into the group, someone who never eats spicy food has to repeatedly eat spicy hot pot to please everyone. As a result, I ended up in the ICU with acute gastritis caused by the spiciness. I also had to stay up all night at an internet cafe with the group, not knowing what to talk about with strangers online for a whole night. But I still went, just to make everyone like me. It was too exhausting. So in the end, I broke free from the mistaken belief of pleasing the group and being popular. I focused on my studies, on finding a job early, on participating in club activities. I felt so much better. So your grievances and embarrassments are the same. Whose youth isn't confused? But youth is for exploring the world, for changing the world. Only then will this world have hope. If we focus on pleasing roommates every day, we still won't be liked by them. It's better to live brilliantly, to live youthfully. Perhaps your brilliance will attract like-minded companions to explore the world together. I recommend a book called "Change, Starting from the Heart" in hopes of helping you truly change your life.

Isolated, cold violence, they just don't like to care about you! Be sincere and honest in dealing with people, can you observe the micro-expressions of everyone? We should not rush to please anyone or make friends with anyone, in the end, we still have to be our own friends. A group of people's revelry is always short-lived. Instead of worrying about why they are ignoring me, it's better to ask yourself from the bottom of your heart, why do you need their recognition and acceptance? There are so many people in college, why are you fixating on the people in your dormitory? Isn't the dormitory just a place to rest after class? Do you need so many people to accompany you while resting? Learn to be alone and you will receive extraordinary interpersonal relationships. Especially useful connections...

question: A 24-year-old woman constantly feels like she has no worth and doubts if she has done things well enough.
description: For example, if I communicate with a colleague or supervisor about a task I completed at work and they read the message without responding, I will start to wonder if I did something wrong or if there was something I missed. If a supervisor asks me how I completed a task, I will start to question if I made a mistake somewhere, even though the supervisor may just be asking about my process without any intent to blame me.

answers.answer_text: ~~Give the asker a comforting hug. I can understand the asker's feelings very well. They may be more sensitive to others' reactions and worried if their behavior is related to these reactions. When it comes to determining one's worth, we should not only rely on others' judgments but also rely on our own judgments. However, subjective judgments may contain errors, especially when it comes to others' judgments, which can easily lead to misunderstandings. We can try to understand others' reactions better by communicating directly with them to understand their true thoughts, rather than just guessing. We can start by asking trusted colleagues, family, and friends about their true intentions behind their words in these situations.

question: Anxiety, unwilling to be ordinary but content with the current situation.
description: Hello expert! I'm 24 years old and already have three children. I found a son-in-law who came to our home. I live next to my mother's house, and my parents control a lot. I don't want them to control me, but they say I don't know what's good for me. They have always been involved in everything and don't let me worry about anything. I get irritated for no reason every day, even when looking at my children. I want to go out and live my own life, but I'm afraid my parents won't agree and I also feel reluctant to leave them. Seeing so many live streams on the internet, I really want to earn some money, but I never succeed, and I feel useless. The family doesn't feel like a home, and we have so many children. My husband works every day, but he never flushes the toilet when he gets home and he often throws cigarette butts everywhere. He also doesn't empty the footbath water and never closes the door when entering the house. It's been six years, and I talk about these things every day. He always says I nag too much, but why won't he listen? I'm tired of these days. Whenever I get angry, I feel useless. Enough is enough. I spend every day in anxiety. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I see that you are anxious. There are advantages to finding a son-in-law or daughter-in-law from your own parents' home. Parents can help with household chores, take care of children, and children can take care of the elderly. Of course, like any other family, there will be conflicts, which is normal. "Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way." There are no perfect relationships or individuals. Accepting yourself and others, understanding and respecting oneself and others, not demanding too much from oneself and others, and considering others' perspectives can all be good ways to alleviate anxiety. Think more about the positive aspects of your parents. When feelings of anger, dissatisfaction, or frustration arise, immediately become self-aware and use rational thinking to control yourself for five minutes before reacting, allowing time for buffering. Take deep breaths, exercise, do things you enjoy, practice mindfulness meditation, do yoga, read books, and don't let negative emotions control you. Yesterday's matters, past events, today's matters, current matters, tomorrow's matters, future matters, only focus on the present moment, today's matters. Don't dwell on the past, don't worry about the future. Focus on your own affairs, not others', not what God decides, only focus on your own matters. You cannot control others' affairs. Accept what you can't change and change what you can. The principle is that whoever is in pain is responsible for change. Change yourself, accept the current situation, or accept the responsibility to change the current situation. Best wishes.

question: I have a friend who has been good to me, but I am increasingly disinterested in him.
description: Ten years ago, I moved from the south to the north for work and life. Through my company's business, I met a male supplier. Even now, after getting married and having a child, we still maintain a good level of contact. I don't have many friends, so he is considered my best friend apart from my colleagues. Although he only has an elementary school education, he is very hardworking and has a good personality. We often chat on WeChat and sometimes go out for meals together. However, recently, during our conversations, I have noticed that he speaks in a crude and uncultivated manner. He often talks about topics that are more suitable for conversations between men. I feel like I am wasting my time when I have any communication with him beyond work-related matters. On the other hand, I look down on myself for being this way. I realize that I have lost many of my old friends because of my own actions, and now I am finding fault with the only one that's left. Since the beginning of the year, I have been avoiding going out to eat with him. It's not because I'm afraid of what others might say or gossip about me. I stand tall and I don't care about what others say about me. I just don't want to communicate with him anymore, but I'm also afraid that he might sense this. If he does, he might not want to hang out with me in the future either.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug because the behavior and actions of an old friend are increasingly making you feel dissatisfied and disgusted. But you also feel that it's wrong to have such thoughts about an old friend, so you dare not go out and eat with them, for fear that they will notice your disdain. [A little analysis and advice] 1. It is normal for everyone to have expectations of their friends. OP hopes that their friend is someone with elegant speech and manners, which is a normal desire. However, the fact is that not everyone has the same social background and life experiences. OP has developed their own moral standards and the other person may still have a different way of handling interpersonal relationships. In other words, the crude conversations and behaviors that OP sees as impolite are not a lack of respect towards OP, but rather a reflection of the person's own social experiences. From this perspective, could we be a little more understanding and tolerant towards the friend as an old friend? 2. As for the issue of gradually losing other friends and only having this one left, OP themselves mentioned this in the title. Maybe you can carefully recall how you grew distant from your other friends? What were the reasons for no longer keeping in touch? If you can find the underlying reasons and expand your circle of friends, make new acquaintances, perhaps you will have a deeper understanding of interpersonal relationships and find more suitable ways to handle them.

question: I really want to give up, but I can't. Can you encourage me?
description: It's really tough to keep going every time, I really want to give up, but I can't.

answers.answer_text: Love you, giving you a warm hug. Persistence may be the most difficult thing in the world. I have also cut my wrists and strangled myself with a rope until I had no strength, but I am still here, saying this to you. Whenever it becomes unbearable, find a random reason to at least hold on for a little longer, even if it's just for a second. For example, I still want to see if there will be a beautiful sunrise tomorrow morning, so hold on for one more night. I want to know if next week will be a minute happier than this week, just a little bit better, so hold on for one more week. As long as you have the slightest hesitation, don't hesitate, continue on your path. The worst outcome is only death, but being alive means being able to see more scenery, and contemplate the ever-changing world again. Since you know that you can't give up, why not be a little happier? Sadness and happiness are both parts of a day, and deep down in your heart, you already have the answer. I hope you can let go of your burdens, set clear goals, and embark on your journey filled with hope and determination. May these words help you find the strength within yourself, and know that the world and I love you. These were words someone else said to me, and now I pass them on to you. May you be worry-free.

question: College graduate, recently said she wants to go out and have fun. Is she joking or serious?
description: Recently, my girlfriend has been hearing a lot of news about scumbags, and she suddenly asked whether she should go out and have casual sex or seek financial support while she's still young. I jokingly said, "Sure, go ahead," but I don't know if she was joking or being serious.

answers.answer_text: Is it a joke or serious? If you want a definite answer, you have to ask the person directly. The fact that you, as the questioner, are asking this question probably means that you don't have much confidence in your girlfriend yet. Perhaps you are also holding back in front of your girlfriend. This statement from your girlfriend may be a test for you. You can discuss your respective opinions on current events, engage in mutual discussions, and seize the opportunity to further understand yourselves and each other. Don't be afraid of conflicts and contradictions, because it is through real clashes that people who truly love each other will get closer. Best wishes!

question: I feel like I am doing well in my side job, but I don't want to work on my studies.
description: I feel like I'm doing well in my side job, but my academic progress seems to be not going smoothly. I keep procrastinating and don't feel like reading papers. I'm so frustrated. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, student growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the original poster mentioned that they are good at their side job but tend to procrastinate when it comes to their studies. I believe there must be a reason behind this. Perhaps the original poster is naturally good at and enjoys doing their side job, but not so much when it comes to their studies. If that's the case, the original poster can consider aligning their future development towards this aspect. However, in our lives, there are many things that we cannot do as we please. Even if we don't want to, we must force ourselves to do them. The original poster can create a plan for themselves, such as reading a certain number of papers every day. Little by little, studying each day is much better than staying stagnant. Start taking action now, and you will realize that everything is not as difficult as it seems. Best wishes~.

question: What should I do if I care too much about the opinions of my superior and colleagues and cannot be myself?
description: In a new job position, one may be concerned about the opinions and judgments of their superiors and colleagues. It's common to feel afraid to be oneself, fearing that others won't accept the real you or may dislike you. What should be done?

answers.answer_text: Arriving in a new place, even as a guest, one should be cautious and considerate, let alone in a new workplace where it is essential to become familiar with the environment. The atmosphere in each workplace differs, closely tied to the company culture and leadership style. Polite and thoughtful smiles, not rushing to take sides, and especially not rushing to assert oneself, gradually highlighting one's own qualities while adapting to the environment. After completing several tasks independently, one's own style will naturally become apparent to others. Many difficulties arise from disapproval and resistance. Acceptance can start with a smile and a nod, gradually trying to respond with "okay" and "sure," making changes bit by bit.

Hello~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug~ The fear of not being accepted by others for who you truly are actually stems from your own inability to accept yourself. It is a projection, attributing your own thoughts onto others. Being concerned about others' opinions and not daring to be your authentic self is because you lack a sense of self-identity and harbor some insecurity. I'm not sure if something unfavorable has happened in the past that made you believe that your true self is not good enough. But regardless of what has happened, you should and need to slowly accept your true self. The past is in the past, and now you are welcoming a new job and a new life. Accepting yourself also includes accepting the aspects of yourself that you feel are not good enough, accepting your imperfections. In reality, no one can be perfect and flawless, so we are all equal, and we all should accept ourselves. Although your true self may have some shortcomings, at least it is genuine. And authenticity is power because people will see your sincerity. Accept yourself. Affirm yourself more and let your inner self become stronger. Best wishes~

question: Why do people treat other people's children kindly and gently, but are harsh and rough with their own children?
description: Why do people treat others' children with kindness and patience, but are rough and harsh with their own children? Where does their good mood go?
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods, anxiety emotions

answers.answer_text: Hello! #Why do we treat other people's children kindly, but are rough with our own children? Where does our good mood go? # Many people have this situation, but some people are not aware of the problem. You, on the other hand, have noticed your own shortcomings, which is commendable! As for your question, why does this happen? Let's analyze it from the following aspects: ----Being strict with oneself and kind to others is one of the traditional virtues of the Chinese nation and reflects a collective consciousness. This helps establish harmonious relationships with others. Therefore, treating other people's children with kindness and politeness is a sign of high cultivation. ----Similarly, due to the influence of Confucianism in Chinese culture, there is a deep-rooted belief that children are subordinate to their parents. Therefore, being rough with one's own children is seen as a form of self-discipline. Many parents believe that disciplining is equivalent to educating, so it is not surprising that they are not kind and polite to their own children. With the progress of society, people's perspectives have undergone tremendous changes. The idea that children are not the possessions of parents is increasingly recognized. Advocating positive appreciation in the process of child-rearing is becoming more accepted by everyone. [Appreciation education means learning to appreciate the strengths of children, encouraging and praising their excellent behaviors, instead of constantly criticizing their shortcomings in the hope of correcting them.] If you can apply this educational concept, you will be able to discover more of your child's strengths and give timely praise and encouragement, naturally leading to more kindness and politeness towards your child.

question: How to deal with issues such as sexuality, anxiety, fear, and being blackmailed with nude photos?
description: I'm 18 and in my final year of high school. Recently, I found a guy online and we started chatting. At first, we both liked each other and played some flirtatious games. But later on, I didn't like him anymore and I became disgusted with myself for engaging in that kind of behavior. I felt really gross and decided to break up with him. However, he couldn't get over me and wanted to meet up, but I rejected him. In order to make him give up, I started insulting him. He then said he was willing to break up with me, but he wanted me to accompany him for a month as a transition period. I had to help him three times a week and send him videos and pictures, or else he would threaten to show my naked photos to my friends and teachers. I feel really uncomfortable and disgusted. Lately, I've been feeling anxious about this situation, and combined with the pressure of studying, I feel like I'm on the verge of a breakdown. Can you please tell me what to do? Help me, please?????
keywords: Emotions, guilt and shame, emotional regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hug the OP, encountering such a situation is indeed speechless, especially in dealing with such scoundrels, sometimes it is not possible to use more civilized methods. 1. Reporting to the police is not as effective as imagined. Although we say to look for the police when there is a problem, the other party has not taken any real action at the moment, and it is also across provinces. Therefore, because a threat is not likely to be filed just like that due to time and manpower costs. But we still need to keep relevant evidence for future use. Of course, we should not easily compromise, because if we agree this time, will the other party really let us go? The OP mentioned having an agreement with the other party, but can we expect a person who is not even afraid of going to jail to abide by it? I believe this is just the other party's delaying tactic. We agreed to some unreasonable demands from the other party and even sent video photos, isn't this another time walking into the lion's den? As for the so-called compensation, I believe it is just an excuse. Therefore, this time we must not compromise. First of all, we need to understand how much of our real information the other party knows and has. At the same time, we can also tell the other party: How much of the sexual chat online do you think is real information? In fact, what we told the other party before was all fake. You can send it if you want, but who would believe something that is unreal? 2. We need a reliable person. Although this matter is our privacy, and we don't want people around us to know about it, we cannot bear all the burden on ourselves because we may overlook something. Therefore, the best way is to find a relatively reliable person to discuss and solve any new developments together. We can also recall how much information the other party has from the previous records. Never send our own videos to the other party. As for our real information, we can confuse it a bit. For example, with the other party's information, we can search for it ourselves to see how much can be found. I believe the OP knows the difficulty of this. But we indeed need to be prepared for the matter of sending photos, such as how much real information the other party knows, who they will send it to, and we can also firmly deny it. After all, there are many things that can be synthesized online nowadays. If we don't compromise, at least we still have the chance to turn things around. If we compromise, then we really lose. The world loves you.

Hello, young lady. It is sad to hear about your experience. Regarding the question you raised, I agree with the answer provided by the respondent Tianxin, who also listed many suggestions that you can refer to. Here are my thoughts on the matter, which may differ from your own, but remember that the choice is always in your hands: 1. You are the one who has been harmed, but it is not your fault. At 18 years old, during your senior year of high school, it is normal to be curious about sex. If it was done willingly and did not harm yourself or others, there is nothing wrong with exploring sexuality in certain ways. So, you need to know that it is not wrong or shameful to be curious or even to try certain things; what is wrong is when someone takes advantage of this curiosity and threatens or harms you. 2. Find a way to stop further harm. Now that he has your threatening material, if you go along with his plan and satisfy his demands during this transition period, there is a greater possibility that he will have more material in his possession, and the risks may be even greater after the so-called end. What has already happened cannot be changed, but efforts can be made to minimize the impact. Generally speaking, when someone talks about going to jail for years, it is often just a bluff. Moreover, he may have noticed that you do not want to involve the police. Someone who resorts to such methods to threaten others as soon as a breakup is mentioned probably just has empty promises and agreements. Whether his actions and the WeChat information you have can be used as evidence in a legal context, that is something you need to consult with professionals. This includes whether the evidence you currently have can determine if he is engaging in extortion through threats, and whether your agreement has legal enforceability. Let me also add this: even if the agreement is valid, can you be sure it will be enforced? Additionally, by the time you reach that stage, you will have already suffered significant harm. 3. Seek help from trustworthy individuals. When facing danger, people often want it to stop immediately, but sometimes the actions they take only prolong the harm and create more hidden dangers for the future. I believe in the goodness of human nature, but I also cannot ignore the evil that exists within it. In your situation, if I were to make the worst assumption, it would be that a month from now, he will have more material to threaten you with and will continue to harm you. This could include continuing your relationship, illegally distributing or selling material, and even more extreme behaviors. Although I am only making the most extreme assumption, I cannot deny that it is a possibility. Therefore, find the most trusted people around you and seek substantial help. This situation has undoubtedly affected your mental state, but currently, you are just internet acquaintances, without any substantial contact. Think about it: would it be worse if your family and friends knew about the harm after it has escalated, or would it be worse if they were unaware temporarily? 4. Increase your awareness of personal safety. If this issue can be resolved, in the future, you need to increase your awareness of personal safety. To put it bluntly, when it comes to privacy matters, you need to be cautious. Not everyone is a bad person, but it is important to be on guard. If it involves real-time sexual contact, you must take protective measures, and this applies at any time. Forgive me for being direct and serious in my words, but I rarely feel so indignant when responding to the questions of the original poster. When it involves minors or individuals who have just reached adulthood, I truly cannot remain calm. However, ultimately, the decision on what to do is in your hands. If you seek help from your family or other trusted individuals, it becomes a matter of communicating with them. I hope you have the opportunity to engage in dialogue with everyone on this level. I sincerely hope that you can soon overcome your troubles. Best wishes.

Hello! I can understand the current situation you are in, and it is understandable that anyone would feel a great deal of pressure. The current situation seems more like a "coward's game," where his chips are your "nude photos," and you seem to have no chips, completely passive. But that is not the case. To briefly introduce the legal aspects related to this matter: it is illegal to publish someone's photos on the internet or in the media without consent; publishing nude photos that harm someone's reputation can lead to criminal liability. Spreading nude photos extensively, such as on Weibo, forums to the public, or disseminating them to the person's family and friends, causing serious impact on the person's life, constitutes the crime of insult. Insult is a criminal self-prosecution case, and the victim can collect relevant evidence and file a criminal complaint with the court to pursue criminal liability for the infringer. In addition, spreading someone else's nude photos is a serious circumstance of insult, different from ordinary illegal acts, and falls under criminal cases. According to Article 246 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, if a person openly insults another person by violence or other means, or fabricates facts to slander others and the circumstances are severe, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment, criminal detention, control, or deprivation of political rights for up to three years. This is your first chip. It has just been mentioned that there is a "coward's game" between you two. Whoever is afraid first loses. Therefore, "a resolute and tough attitude" is your second chip. Also, it is very necessary to save your conversations, especially portions where he threatens you. question: Why does my wife never initiate sexual activity and refuse to share her feelings with me?
description: We have been married for 10 years, and my wife never initiates intimacy. It's always me who takes the lead, but most of the time, it feels like she is not interested and not responsive. I want to have a heart-to-heart conversation with her, but even when I pour my heart out and express my feelings, she doesn't share her own thoughts and feelings with me! I love her very much!
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, marriage management, and sexual life.

answers.answer_text: Hello! This description looks like a riddle, and the answers given by the respondents are mostly guesswork, so that's the problem. The troubles you are facing are clearly caused by communication problems. We often say that the key to communication lies in listening, not speaking, because if we "don't understand", we cannot have valuable conversations. "We have been married for 10 years, and my wife never takes the initiative in intimate relationships. It's always me initiating, but the process often feels uninteresting and unresponsive." This problem may be caused by biological factors or psychological factors. In uncertain situations, let's assume it's caused by psychological factors. Intimacy is an important factor that affects the harmony of intimate relationships, so if there is disharmony in this aspect, the first consideration should be the level of intimacy between the two people. "I want to talk to her, but even when I open my heart and share my innermost thoughts with her, she doesn't do the same with me! I love her so much!" The factors that affect the level of intimacy between two people include individual psychological tendencies and the ability to fulfill each other's needs. Maslow divided human needs into five layers: physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs. In theory, if one person can fulfill the other person's corresponding needs, the level of intimacy in this relationship will be high. In most marriages, people's requirements for their partners include physiological needs, safety needs, esteem needs, and social needs. Here, "social needs" specifically refers to whether communication is smooth. Generally speaking, this situation does not happen overnight. Usually, there is a gradual process. One important reason why two people go from sharing everything to having nothing to say is that one or both parties cannot accept each other's emotions. Emotions are often illogical, and any attempt to judge the reasonableness of emotions with values is meaningless. This is why people often say that "reasoning does not work at home", at least not on certain issues and at certain times. So, please recall what happened in these ten years. How did the situation of you being active and her passive come about? Did you become too active, forcing her to be passive, or was she always passive from the beginning, causing you to be active? Love can be an individual matter, but marriage is definitely a matter between two people. Don't "guess blindly" when any problems arise in marriage. Make sure to seek confirmation from the other person and do not be confrontational. Understanding the other person is not difficult, just have less judgment. I wish you a happy life!

Hello! It's clear that you really hope to have a closer relationship with your wife! You haven't provided much information, so it's difficult to give specific advice. However, from your description, a few points can be seen: 1. Your 10-year marriage is relatively stable. Although the quality of your sex life is not high, you still have a normal sexual relationship, and your wife doesn't refuse. It's just that you can't accept the usual way and have higher expectations now. 2. You have very little understanding of your wife, and you may not be good at understanding others through non-verbal cues in daily life. Women are more likely to engage in sexual activities when there is enough romantic time before sex, to feel fully cared for and loved. Even in situations where she doesn't feel good, she still chooses to satisfy your needs, possibly because she is unable to express her own requirements for sex due to her personality. You can evaluate whether you are doing enough in this regard. Another possibility is that your wife expresses her emotions and needs in a passive way, hoping that you can understand her but never feeling understood. The original question from the author seems tailor-made for me, and the respondent seems to have the same difficulties. Many efforts are now being made to achieve this small goal. It may have seemed like she didn't harbor any resentment at that time, but she also felt that she couldn't rely on me and had to do everything herself, even if I did help, she still wouldn't appreciate it. So, I focused on work. There was a time when the emotional accumulation between us was severe. I was quite happy at work and looked forward to coming home, but as I approached the front door, my mood would start to sour. Back then, she didn't think highly of me, and I didn't think highly of her either, especially when it came to the children. I didn't pay much attention, but I always criticized her for spoiling the children and being unable to discipline them. Later, I insisted on having a second child. Of course, after having the second child, our situation didn't improve. Instead, it worsened to the point where we couldn't go on living like this. However, in my heart, I have always loved her very much and have made countless sacrifices for her. The problems mostly came from her, and you can imagine her reaction. Fortunately, things were halted before reaching a dangerous edge. Now, when I look back, everything that happened seems like a dream or a story happening to someone else. Although I know that many people would like to scold me, I can still calmly share these stories. It was in April last year when I completely woke up because of a TV series called "All Is Well." Even if she cannot change her habits immediately, we should be more understanding. I believe your wife will understand.

After reading your description, after being married for 10 years, do you know what your wife's current thoughts are? What does she want? You mentioned that you love her very much and are willing to have deep conversations with her. However, her response seems ordinary and distant, not willing to open her heart. If you haven't figured out the underlying psychological motives behind this behavior, even if you appear to be trying hard, the effect might not be significant if she already has a rejecting attitude. I don't know what your partner's personality, interests, and hobbies are, so don't expect me to give you specific advice because I have no information. You only talked about the intimacy between the two of you, including the issues reflected in your sexual relationship, which is only superficial. If you want to truly understand each other in a deeper way, you may need to give up some of your current position. In our lives, when we want to get closer to others, we choose to adapt to their preferences. This behavior is sometimes reflected in psychological relationships. You might as well start by imitating his behaviors, body language, and expressions in your daily life. Delay a few seconds and don't completely copy them. Sometimes you can imitate, and sometimes you don't need to. In life, we often hear that a couple looks good together. In fact, it is a manifestation of both parties being assimilated. The aforementioned imitation is actually formed unconsciously. Only then will you become inseparable. The method seems simple, but if you truly implement it, the results will surprise even yourself.

question: If someone dislikes dogs and abuses my dog, will they face consequences for mistreating the dog?
description: I used to take my small dog out for a walk. I came across an old lady who didn't like dogs. She tried to hit my dog, and I couldn't stand it, so I argued with her. Then she hit me and pretended to be injured, calling the police for an examination. I was panicked and ended up compensating her with money. But I feel really wronged in my heart. It still upsets me when I think about it. Was it wrong for me to protect my dog? Won't she face consequences for mistreating dogs?

answers.answer_text: Hello, after reading your question description, I can understand that your beloved dog was bullied by someone for no reason, and it was someone very difficult to deal with. Your anger at that moment must have been overwhelming, and you may have even had thoughts of wishing that person would disappear from the face of the earth. I myself am a dog lover (although there is a lot of criticism online towards dog lovers nowadays). When I was a child, my dog passed away and I was so heartbroken that I couldn't eat for a week. After spending a long time with dogs, I feel that dogs are like family, and sometimes I even think they understand emotions better than some people in real life. I have experienced the death of my dogs twice (once from old age and once from being hit by a car), and each time it deeply saddened me. It has been almost ten years since I last had a dog as a pet. If I were to experience my beloved dog being hurt, I would definitely feel a lot of anger. I often can't understand how someone could dislike such a cute animal. According to the analysis of data on juvenile delinquency in the United States, teenagers with tendencies of animal abuse often develop antisocial tendencies in adulthood. The perpetrators of multiple school shootings in America had a history of animal abuse. What kind of experiences lead these people to be so heartless? Research shows that the decrease in human crime rates does not have a corresponding data relationship with economic development and educational advancement. Instead, it is after the legalization of abortion that overall crime rates have improved. The reason is that many children with criminal tendencies were basically "strangled in the cradle". So why is this the case? Nowadays, we are gradually realizing the importance of family education. In the past, many people had children without planning, and before they were prepared, the children were already born. The parents' self-growth and the family itself seemed unprepared to welcome the children's arrival. Many parents' original families were harsh, violent, and lacked love. In educating their own children, due to the lack of corresponding continued learning, they usually continue to follow the incorrect concepts of their own families. Children should have grown up in a nurturing environment, but they become the psychotherapists of adults, accepting the psychological trauma of their parents. After all, children are children, and in the face of their parents' emotional outbursts, they often develop a defense of emotional isolation and even jealousy towards those who receive love, whether they are humans or animals. They believe that this is a world without love, and that suffering is the essence of life. So, you asked if those who harm small animals will face consequences? The answer is definitely yes, but the consequences here do not mean that they are caused by others, but rather an unconscious influence. People who lack love certainly experience problems in interpersonal relationships, especially intimate relationships, and various aspects of their lives are affected to varying degrees. I sympathize with those who have had unfortunate childhood experiences, but I do not agree with them treating this misfortune as something normal and imposing it on others. Let's keep our original intentions and journey back to where we belong. Along the path of growth, let's go together. I hope this helps you.

Hello, after carefully reading your description, I would speculate that if there is a way to seek justice or if someone can mediate and ensure justice, you might feel better. I wonder why someone cannot tolerate such a small dog, and it is right for me to protect my own dog. There must be reasons behind the actions of that elderly person, and we can try to understand, but we cannot support such behavior. I also wonder what kind of experiences led the elderly person to handle things this way and to harm others so recklessly.

question: It's common for major and minor tasks to become a mess when there are too many goals. What should be done in this case?
description: There are multiple targets, and the importance of each one is often unclear and chaotic. How to handle each task corresponds to a method, but it is easy to get confused and forget.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a virtual hug. From your description, I understand that you are unclear about managing tasks of different sizes, which leads to difficulty in completing them effectively. 【A little advice】By using the Eisenhower Matrix, you can effectively manage your tasks. If you categorize your tasks into four quadrants based on their urgency and importance, it will help you gain a deeper understanding of time and manage it effectively. The first quadrant includes urgent and important tasks. These tasks are time-sensitive and have significant impact. They cannot be avoided or postponed and need to be addressed as a priority. Examples include negotiating major projects or important meeting work. The second quadrant is different from the first. The events in this quadrant may not be urgent, but they have significant impact. They are of great importance for personal or business existence, development, and the establishment and maintenance of the surrounding environment. The third quadrant mainly consists of trivial matters. They are not time-sensitive nor important. Such events are purely time-wasting and life-squandering. Activities like daydreaming, browsing the internet, chatting, and aimlessly wandering around are typical for those who have nothing substantial to do. The fourth quadrant includes events that are urgent but not important. These tasks may seem urgent, but in reality, they are not important. Many people have a misconception and believe that urgent matters are always important. In fact, events like meaningless phone calls, conforming to others' expectations, or playing mahjong with three players are not important. However, since they are urgent, they often end up occupying people's precious time.

question: I feel anxious and distressed all the time, constantly overthinking. What should I do?
description: I am constantly thinking about various questions, such as why am I me and whether the people around me truly exist. Many things lead me to endless questions.

answers.answer_text: Hi there! Hugs to you~ Based on your description, I can understand why you feel confused about your uncontrollable thoughts. It's actually a kind of philosophical pondering or even existential questioning. Perhaps these thoughts have caused you to feel anxious and in great distress. The contemplation of philosophical questions can sometimes lead to anxiety about life or even general psychological issues. If you feel that this has started to affect your daily life and work, you might consider seeking the support and guidance of a psychologist or counselor. If it doesn't feel that severe, you can also try talking to friends or family as a way of venting. Regarding the contemplation of philosophical questions, if you want to address these issues, you can explore the answers provided by the ancient philosophers. They might be able to help you solve some of the fundamental philosophical questions you have. In fact, even before we have any knowledge of philosophy, we often engage in contemplation about philosophical questions. And believe it or not, the gap between our own thoughts and those of philosophers is not as significant as one may think. Everyone can become their own philosopher and resolve certain existential ponderings. So, it's quite common for people to engage in philosophical thinking.

question: Do you feel unable to trust men because you haven't established a secure attachment relationship?
description: Around the age of nine, only a few families in the village had bought a television. After dinner, I would run to their houses to watch TV. One time, while watching "Gangster Boss," there was a scene of murder. On the way home, I was particularly scared and ran quickly to my house. My mother looked at me with a disgusted look in her eyes, without saying a word. Even if she scolded or scolded me, I would still share my feelings with her. But she didn't say a word, and I felt that she didn't love me at all. She saw how scared I was, but didn't pay any attention to me. Now, whenever I think of that scene, I still want to cry. I can't understand her. I didn't feel a sense of security from the person closest to me. As I grew up, I don't trust men because I didn't establish a good attachment relationship, right?

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, it seems quite simple and it is difficult to make useful inferences. Currently, all we can say is that the attachment relationship with your parents and not trusting men after growing up may not be closely related, or at least not the main factor. Furthermore, in terms of attachment relationships, they are formed at a very young age, and the form of these relationships is generally stable after the age of 3. Therefore, I think it is unlikely that the form of attachment relationships could be completely changed by a single incident that occurred at the age of 9. It is more likely that your family's parenting style has had an influence all along. As for not trusting men, it may be more complicated. Your family's parenting style, your mother's attitudes towards these matters and their influence on you, your relationship with your father, your parents' way of interacting and their relationship, as well as your own experiences in love and relationships, classmates, and friends, could all have an impact on you. To determine the exact cause would require a thorough analysis. If you feel that the issue of "not trusting men" has indeed caused emotional and life difficulties for you, it is advisable to seek psychological counseling, rather than making unfounded speculations on your own.

Whether it matters or not, because whether it is or not, you can choose whether the future you believes in men or not. (I think you also know that there will not only be bad people in the world, because you have started to think about this question) In any case, live a good life (at least to the extent of being able to buy the things you like), and then think about what kind of life you want to live in the remaining years. (No matter what, as long as you like it and have no regrets) Think about how many years you can live, ask yourself how to live the remaining time so that you can leave the world with no regrets. The answer lies within your heart.

question: My ex-boyfriend has openly revealed a new relationship, and their sweet interactions have struck me like a thunderbolt.
description: I am a girl who used to be very confident. It has been one year and eight months since I broke up with my ex-boyfriend. Two years ago, during our relationship, he used "PUA" on me, often giving me a slap and then a sweet talk. At that time, I had no concept of PUA and was an ignorant and innocent girl. I only knew that I loved him very much, but I became increasingly self-doubting and sensitive in front of him. When we were about to get married, I discovered that he had cheated on me, lied to me countless times, and deceived me. Ignorantly, I foolishly tried to save the relationship. He said that as long as I gave him 700,000 RMB for home renovation, he would marry me. I struggled for half a month, washing my face with tears, and finally decided to sell my property under my name. However, just on the second day after selling the house, before I had a chance to tell him that I had the money, I received abusive and defamatory calls and WeChat messages from the other woman. I was so angry that my whole body trembled, but he didn't defend me. He even said that it was my own fault for attracting unsavory men. I completely broke down. My parents took me to a psychiatric hospital where I was diagnosed with severe depression. I underwent a year-long treatment for depression, and now I have stopped taking medication and my mindset has improved a lot. However, when I clicked on his Weibo just now, I discovered that he was showing off his new relationship, and his new girlfriend is very beautiful. Their sweet interaction struck me like a bolt from the blue. All the efforts I have made seem to have crumbled in an instant.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP.※ Boyfriend's new relationship exposed, intimate actions make you very sad. It's difficult to truly let go of someone you once loved, especially when you haven't completely moved on, and you see the intimate interactions between him and his new girlfriend. It's normal to feel upset. But have you ever thought that this girl might be you from the past? You only see their current happiness, but have you considered that they might be facing the same problems you once encountered? When it comes to marriage, the boy even asks you to give him 700,000 yuan before agreeing; when it comes to slander, he not only doesn't trust you but also suspects you. Are you sure this boy really loves you? In the past, you made concessions to please him, but he repeatedly hurt you. Young lady, you need to open your eyes and see what kind of man you have encountered. Is he worth your lifelong devotion? As the saying goes, "The state of a person's character is difficult to change." Once someone's character is formed, it's hard to change. Even if this man gets married, he won't be faithful. You should be thankful that you discovered his true colors early on and didn't suffer more harm from him! So, you need to sort out your emotions, focus on psychological treatment, and quickly restore your physical and mental health, returning to a normal life! This is the greatest love you can give yourself! Best wishes!

If you are sure that you have been catfished, then you are lucky now. Besides the emotional manipulation you went through, your losses aren't huge. After all, he didn't get any money from you. In fact, another girl is about to find herself on the same path as you, and what you see now is what he once gave you. So, there's no need to envy. What you need now is to break free from the illusion of that manipulated love, find your confident self, and start anew.

question: Emotional problems, infidelity issues, does it mean he no longer wants to continue the relationship?
description: In June of this year, I discovered that my husband had used his credit card to give another woman 160,000 yuan. In the past year, he hasn't spent much money on me and has been sleeping with other women, not just one. When I asked my husband, he said he had never met her and it was all lies. But I don't believe him. They call each other "husband" and "wife" when they chat, and he even sent her money on Valentine's Day and bought her things online, like phones and watches. He insists he has never met her and hasn't done anything to betray me. Last year, when we bought a car, he even gave it to the other woman. Now he won't explain the situation with that woman. I got so angry that I went back to my parents' home. Before I found out, he used to care about me a lot, calling me every day. But after I discovered what he was doing, he stopped calling. He didn't even try to make it up to me. Later, using his WeChat account, I contacted the other woman, and she admitted they had met. She kept saying she would return the money to my husband. I told her that my husband is married and has a child, and she should return the money because she spent some of it. At first, she agreed to return it, but then she said she only found out my husband was married and now he won't return the money because it was voluntarily given. She blocked my husband and now I can only call him. But he rarely contacts me on his own. When I mention divorce, he won't agree. Does he not care about me anymore?
keywords: Marriage, divorce, infidelity, and marriage management.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Discovered that your husband has cheated, and expected the other person to confess and apologize, begging for forgiveness, and make amends for his mistakes through practical actions. You hoped that he would fear losing you, treat you well, take the initiative to care for you, and show doubled affection. Is that right? When one person in an intimate relationship cheats, the person who has been betrayed inevitably experiences some degree of pain. To determine whether you see your partner as a loved one or a tool, a small indicator is your initial reaction when you first found out about your husband's infidelity - did you feel sadness or anger? If anger was your primary and strongest feeling, it is likely that your husband has always been seen as a tool in your relationship. He can perceive that his emotional needs are not being met, which is why he sought fulfillment outside the relationship, causing your intense anger and frustration. In emotional counseling, it is often said that infidelity seems like a third-party problem, but upon careful observation, it is actually a problem within the relationship itself that leads to the involvement of a third-party external force (assuming your husband is not a playboy). When you have treated your partner as a tool for a long time, there is no true emotional connection between you. Your partner can feel it, and when his emotional needs are not met, he will search for channels outside the relationship to satisfy them. Therefore, it is even more important for the person in the relationship to first sit down and calmly reflect and examine. Where were the problems in your relationship? What communication issues did you have? Did you give him enough attention in the relationship? Did you emotionally blackmail him too much? What is your own emotional pattern like? If your partner were to return to the family, would you accept him without criticism? Do you understand your husband's emotional needs? Take the time to think carefully, use this experience to reflect on your intimate relationship, and both parties need to adjust and grow in order to rebuild a "new" intimate relationship. May you penetrate your own emotions, approach the situation with love and rationality, and consider the path ahead for both of you~.

question: Can a relationship that starts for the sake of love last long?
description: Sophomore year, female, in a dormitory with six people, and five of them are in relationships. Sometimes, when I am in the midst of them, I feel like I don't fit in. Every time they talk about relationship issues, they start sharing how they met their boyfriends and how sweet their relationships are. Every time this happens, I feel like I don't belong, and even feel a bit lonely. The other five people seem to be very eager to persuade me to get a boyfriend. In this situation, I have indeed had a relationship before, but there were no feelings involved. He pursued me, and I agreed to be in a relationship just for the sake of being in one. It seemed from the beginning that it wouldn't have a good outcome. I started feeling bored in the first week of being officially together and felt like it was a waste of time being with him. As a result, this relationship quickly ended. I returned to the state I was in at the beginning, living amidst my roommates' flaunting and happiness. Suddenly, I feel a bit confused. Is it really necessary to be in a relationship just for the sake of being in one?

answers.answer_text: Does the questioner's class only have six girls? If not, are the other girls in the dormitory all in relationships? If there are others who don't want to be in a relationship right now like the questioner, can they hang out together? In our class, we can't find any girls to hang out with. What about the girls from other majors in the neighboring dormitory? What about the girls from other colleges in the clubs? The university is an open and free place that provides enough space for every idea and behavior to flourish. If you want to be in a relationship, go ahead (of course, protect yourself). If you want to read, go to the library. If you want to take photos, write poetry, or dance, there are various clubs where you can find like-minded friends. Of course, if you don't want to be in a relationship, don't be. If you don't want to help a classmate pick up a package, just refuse directly... Only you know what you want. If classmates and friends offer advice out of concern, we should express gratitude and possibly consider it. If it's purely for showing off or even jealousy, just ignore it and laugh it off. There are so many interesting things waiting to be done. Where is the time to be bothered by these meaningless words? Love is beautiful, it's a romantic experience between two individuals with independent thoughts, who are attracted to each other. Whether it's love at first sight or feelings that develop over time, it's a genuine feeling from the hearts of the two people involved. It has nothing to do with a third person. Arrange your own life, do things you enjoy with compatible friends, and savor the wonderful time in college. Love could be just around the corner.

Hello there! In college, I don't feel ashamed at all for not dating. Not dating means you haven't found the right person yet. Many people feel that dating is a respectable thing after entering college, so they have a yearning for love deep down. They always wish to find someone to share their joy with and spend the rest of their lives together. But we are not always so lucky. It's not possible for us to meet the most suitable person in a short time. So, many people date just for the sake of it, watching their friends one by one getting into relationships, they get anxious too. Thus, they end up being with someone they don't even like. Do you think this kind of love is meaningful? So, don't feel embarrassed for still being single. Believe that you deserve the best. If you haven't met the right person yet, don't rush. You can work on becoming stronger first. Believe that if you bloom as a butterfly, the right opposite sex will naturally be attracted to you. Then, won't you find a better partner? So, don't worry about these things. If a person can become stronger and find a better partner at the same time, they truly can be called a winner in life. So, just focus on your efforts. Don't be in a hurry if you haven't met anyone yet. They will eventually appear. Love doesn't tolerate hastiness. Hasty love is bound to be unhappy. You should first calm yourself down and become more knowledgeable. Don't pay attention to their mockery. They may seem to be lovey-dovey every day, but only they know if they are truly happy. They aren't so happy either.

question: Work has no meaning, resigned, but still feel empty?
description: I work in a railway company. This year, they implemented a selection process for employees and I got laid off. For the past six months, I have been earning a monthly salary of only 1600 RMB, which is not enough to sustain myself. Today, I resigned. Someone told me that I should hang on, but I feel hopeless as there is no job security and no future prospects. I don't know what to do now, and I feel lost and empty. I don't even know if I should find a new job. My loved ones are also unaware of my situation.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello! Thank you for inviting me to answer. After reading your description, I have a certain understanding of the question you want to ask, so I give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can understand to some extent that you are currently filled with confusion about the future and unsure of what kind of job you will be able to handle. It is normal to feel confused at this stage because some things tend to come when you least expect them. Therefore, it is necessary to approach the problem from a different perspective. By going through this experience, you will gain a clearer understanding of what you truly want and have a more comprehensive understanding of yourself. So why not embrace it? In your description, you also roughly analyzed the reasons for quitting your job, feeling that your current income is not enough to support yourself and others, so you decided to resign. After all, considering the reality, there are many things one still has to do instead of avoiding them. Only by doing so, we can prevent ourselves from becoming weaker. So when you consider various reasons, you made a brave choice. I want to give you a thumbs up for that, well done. However, after quitting your job, you started to worry if you will be able to find work and have a better and stable income. Therefore, I have summarized some methods to help alleviate your current situation, hoping to help you to some extent. (1) It was already very courageous of you to gather the courage and resign, and you have probably thought about the consequences of quitting, but you still took that step, which is really great. Since you have come this far, just keep moving forward and try not to worry too much about the future. (2) Communicate with close friends or family members and talk about your problems to further release your emotions. However, make sure to choose the right person to communicate with and don't exhaust yourself even more through this conversation. (3) I think you have been working in the railway unit for quite a long time, so to some extent, you have accumulated a lot of experience. Therefore, you still have the ability to find a job that is comparable to your previous one. If it is difficult to find such a job, consider switching to a completely new field. The adaptation process might be long, but as long as you persist, you will definitely reap great rewards. (4) Have you considered working in another city? It may be tiring, but the effort you put in and the rewards you receive are generally proportional. Moreover, the salary could be several times higher than what you currently earn; it is entirely possible. However, if you really make such a choice, you will temporarily have to give up what you currently have to some extent because everything in life comes with a cost. (5) This society is always about survival of the fittest, so for your own sake, you should continuously improve your abilities in order to gain more of what you desire and protect the things or people you treasure. (6) Spend more time reading books to broaden your horizons and increase your knowledge. The world is cheering for you. Good luck!

OP, you have your own choices. Since you have made a decision, there's no need to dwell on the past anymore. From now on, strive to start a new life. Maybe you can go out more often and have a look at industry information, or browse job websites to see if there are suitable positions available. Perhaps you can also discover things you are interested in in your daily life and consider developing them into your career. Maybe you can talk to your family about your current difficulties and find solutions together. No matter what, I hope you can overcome the confusion, have confidence in yourself, give yourself positive psychological suggestions, and believe that you can do it. This will be more conducive to finding a new job and starting a new life. Best wishes!

question: I have depression! How do I deal with my relationship with a female classmate?
description: I have depression! I seek help from a female classmate, and whenever I have any unpleasant issues, I write her letters. But how can I better get along with her in such a situation?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ For someone with depression like you, writing letters to release negative emotions can be a good method. #However, you should also consider the other person's feelings: how is their emotional state? Can they handle your negative emotions? Are you in a relationship where you can talk about anything? Will your confessions burden them? These are all things to consider. #If you want to have a better relationship with the other person, it is important to understand their thoughts. For example, they may also have unhappy moments, so you can both become each other's confidants. #If your behavior becomes a burden to the other person, you can consider finding other channels or methods to express yourself, like creating an anonymous platform. Best wishes~.

question: "My husband is having ambiguous interactions with members of the opposite sex online, and I can't let go of it. What should I do?"
description: Dated for ten years, married for one year, I have always believed that we trust each other and thought there were no problems in our relationship. However, I accidentally discovered that he was flirting with others online. After I found out, I cried, apologized, and reconciled with him. We even deleted each other's WeChat contacts. However, later I found out that he was liking posts from another person on Douyin (a social media platform). I questioned his behavior, but he didn't think it was a big deal and said that liking a post doesn't mean anything. What is his mentality? I can't let go of it and feel that I can't fully trust him anymore. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Rarely muddled up! After 10 years of dating, they've been married for one year. Have they grown tired of each other? Can they only see each other's flaws and have lost all attraction? Women should always be vigilant and work on improving themselves. Learn something you've always wanted to learn, do some yoga every day to relieve your current anxieties. Spend some quality time together to observe his every move. Cry, apologize, and make up. Have the composure to face the situation; those who care about you won't make you cry, and those who make you cry won't care. Make him aware of the consequences of his actions, rather than just apologizing and getting back together. Stay calm. Continue observing, how far have they progressed? In addition to improving yourself, communicate calmly with him and find your own flaws to improve on. Men like to be admired, taken care of, surrounded, pampered, and understood. Are you fulfilling any of these points? Has his career encountered a bottleneck recently, needing some relief and someone to talk to? After 11 years together, you know him best. If it was just a momentary confusion, don't torment yourself anymore! If he hurt you once, how long will you continue to hurt yourself? Dating for 10 years and only married for 1 year. May your union be based on love. It's just a vague stage now. Don't push him into the other camp; slowly bring him closer to you. If you know he is flirtatious, you would not have trusted him for so long! If you know he has always been unfaithful, why did you marry him? If you know he is flirtatious and you can't change him, then live your own life well. If you feel one day you can't continue, let go! Walk alone. Do you have a celebrity crush? Do you think he's handsome? Then go give him a thumbs-up!

question: Want to get rid of the shadow of childhood and feel helpless?
description: I was bullied by a boy who had no connection to me for seven years during my childhood, from kindergarten to elementary school graduation. I don't know why he always targeted only me, as I never provoked him. He was always a troublemaker and constantly belittled me. Even now, in 2020, when I'm 20 years old, I still don't have any friends because of what I went through in the past. I don't have any friends in any aspect of life, and it's true, I really have no friends. I have always wanted to break free from this, but I just can't do it. Every time I meet a new friend, I'm too scared to send a message or say hello and chat. I hesitate for a long time before sending even a single sentence, and in the end, I still can't bring myself to send it. I long for good friends to chat with, but I'm afraid of being rejected or ignored when I send messages. The reason for this fear is still connected to my childhood experiences. I really want to solve these problems, but I feel powerless.
keywords: Growing up, improving one's character, self-growth, self-acceptance

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope the author can feel more relaxed. 1. [When I was a child, I was bullied by a boy who had no connection with me for seven years, from kindergarten to elementary school graduation.] School bullying incidents are common, and every time I hear about them, I feel heartbroken and sympathize with the author's experience. I also lament that I haven't done enough and can only console the author through words here, hoping to be helpful. "Childhood misfortunes require a lifetime to heal" is indeed true. Childhood is a stage for shaping one's personality, and the things encountered in childhood will deeply imprint in our memories, becoming indelible. The author's misfortune has resulted in difficulties in making friends. How can this vicious cycle be stopped? Learn to reconcile with your past self. The author has grown up, at 20 years old, which means being an adult. The author is no longer the girl who used to be bullied. Holding onto past pain and struggling will only make oneself more helpless. What the author needs to do is to reconcile with the past self and accept the fact that the past self was not strong enough to protect oneself. To become strong, it can be seen from the author's description that the author is still sensitive and weak inside, and has not gained corresponding growth in self. Although the author has reasons, it is still recommended for the author to cultivate themselves. You can enrich yourself through reading, learning, and exercise, giving yourself a strong inner self and a healthy body, so that you can deal with all kinds of people in the future society. Break through yourself and be brave. This is the most important and the point that the author wants to change the most at present. The fact that the author can raise this question shows that there is a desire to solve it, which is already moving towards a positive direction. Since you have taken a small step, why not be more courageous and take a big step forward? There are more kind-hearted people in this world. Don't be afraid that no one will pay attention to you. When you send a message, if you encounter setbacks, don't be discouraged. Out of ten people, there will definitely be sincere ones who are willing to make friends with you and treat you sincerely. You need to be proactive and welcome their arrival. Don't be afraid and have the courage, keep going! I hope you can find friends in June. If you treat others sincerely, they will also treat you sincerely. Good luck!

Hug the original poster! It must be so difficult to have childhood traumas! I don't know why that boy has been slandering you for 7 years, it's truly a psychological crime! Is it because you can't distance yourself from him, or because you can't let go of the past? I noticed that you are more shy and timid when it comes to socializing, but being proactive is the fastest way to make friends. If you can't even send a message or say a single word, how can you make friends? The best method is to start with just one sentence. If you can't gather the courage to say too much, then start with saying "hello" today, just a normal greeting. The second time, ask how their day was. Take a step further the third time and ask if you can talk with them. That should be enough. When you truly make good friends, they won't consider it a bother. The person who dares to start a conversation will surely receive more warmth! Please don't worry too much, sincere conversations won't hurt each other. Also, don't care too much about what others think. As long as you haven't offended anyone, be straightforward. If you do get hurt, don't dwell on it too much because everyone is imperfect. You've already experienced the harm of hurtful words, so you won't hurt others. Please take the brave step and make friends!

Our childhood experiences have a significant impact on the formation of our cognition. You were bullied by a boy for seven years in your childhood, and the impact of these seven years on you was devastating. It is likely to cause two aspects of influence: on the one hand, it will affect your basic attitude towards others. You were not familiar with this boy, but he targeted and hurt you, not in a friendly way, but arrogantly and aggressively. As a result, you formed a basic impression of others: that they are all dangerous, they will harm you, and they only care about themselves and take pleasure in attacking others, being malicious. To make matters worse, after experiencing this harm, you didn't have good enough friends, so you didn't have the chance to correct this impression. There are people in this world who are malicious, but there are also kind ones. Without good friends, it means you haven't experienced the positive, kind, and accepting side of interpersonal relationships, only the negative information. Therefore, avoiding intimate relationships became a means for you to protect yourself. Although it made you lonely, it could also protect you. This was the best method you could think of as a child, and after seven years or even longer, it should have been one of the ways you protected yourself. On the other hand, it will affect your self-confidence. Self-confidence, also known as self-efficacy, means that when you do something, your evaluation of the results and whether you are competent or not are influenced by past experiences. When you were powerless in the face of harm during your childhood, it caused you to always have negative evaluations in interpersonal relationships. You feel that you don't have the ability to resolve conflicts. So, you're afraid of disagreeing with others, and you might even think that as long as there are differences, others will hurt you and you can't do anything about it. So how to solve it? First, you have to believe that most people are still worth trusting. This must be obtained through interacting with others. Generally speaking, a counselor can play this role. For example, the counselor is friendly, accepting, and patient towards you. Slowly, you will realize that although there are many bad people in this world, most people are still trustworthy. Counselors, parents, and even internet friends can all play this role. Internet friends have a small advantage over real friends in that even if you argue with them, they won't crawl through the internet to physically harm you, which is relatively safer. Second, you have to learn to discern which people are worth trusting. You have to learn what trust is, and understand that trustworthy people are not necessarily perfect. By interacting with trustworthy people, you will gradually learn how to handle differences. Then you will enjoy the benefits that trust brings, and your doubts and fears will decrease, and you may even develop a sense of competence, thereby increasing your sense of security. Third, you need to learn to protect your own interests when necessary. During those seven years, did you ever seek help from your parents? And although you were powerless as a child, now you may have the opportunity to help yourself. You can use imagination. In your imagination, you, as an adult, can help the powerless little girl from your childhood cope with difficulties and solve problems. When you can't come up with a solution, a counselor can assist you. If you can think of one, it will greatly improve your situation.

Good afternoon! OP, from your description, I can sense your feeling of helplessness and your desire to change the situation. I also had a similar experience in elementary school, so I want to share it with you in the hopes that it might help. In my class, there were several boys who didn't like studying and enjoyed fighting. They would often bully classmates who didn't resist, and eventually they wanted to bully me too. However, I foolishly confronted them and even took the initiative to stand up to them. Whenever I stood up to them, they would back down. Eventually, they started to be a little afraid of me. Seeing their fear, I became even more brave and daring. But this approach was also dangerous, thankfully they never seriously hurt me. I'm sharing this experience with you to offer some advice. "Be brave." When facing bullying, make sure to protect yourself, but when confronted, the one who is brave will win. Dare to stand up, sometimes bullies have no reason to pick on others, and the more you don't fight back, the more arrogant they become. They'll keep bullying because it becomes a habit. Considering the current situation, I think there are several ways to improve it. First, "make peace with the past." The childhood experience caused you great trauma, resulting in difficulties in forming relationships. Now that you've grown up and have the ability to protect yourself, the things that happened in the past were not your fault, but the fault of the other person. You shouldn't continue to punish yourself with their mistakes.
