Moreover, when confronted by the other party, they claimed that you had agreed and tried to distance themselves. Afterwards, you would think, even if you knew and agreed to it, what could you do? But if we look at the beginning of the situation, were you really willing? No, you were coerced. If you hadn't gone along with them, they might have caused you even greater harm. So this behavior actually protected you to some extent. Also, before you tried to escape, did you know you could? No, you didn't. And if you hadn't escaped, you might have experienced further violations. So actually, by escaping, you prevented future harm. It can be seen that many times your reactions and actions are actually to protect yourself from more serious harm, and in the current situation, it's difficult for you to have a clear mind. You are probably in a state of panic and confusion. So don't blame yourself, dear, it's not your fault, it's the fault of those people. In fact, they have also violated the law to a serious extent!! But seeing you bravely speaking out and seeking to overcome this issue, and wanting to eliminate its impact on you, you have already made great efforts. And for so many years, you have been living under this shadow, which is really not easy. Hugs to you. Actually, there is no specific advice, just hoping that you can try to love yourself more. Because you are already amazing, you have already made great efforts, you are not at fault. I hope this can help you, the world and I love you~.

question: How should I handle my panic when I worry about leaving a bad impression on my friends?
description: Hello everyone, I am a college student. I would like to ask everyone a question. It's about a friend whom you trust a lot, but you've done something that she finds very childish and nonsensical, like offending other people by arguing. Although it's my own fault and I've brought trouble upon myself, I don't know if she will feel very disappointed in me? She has helped me a lot before and has cared about me. I'm really scared and panicked. My anxiety has flared up again. I don't want to leave a bad impression on her. What should I do? Please help.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friendships, deception and trust.

answers.answer_text: Hello, hello, how are you, question asker? I'm here to give you a hug as a good friend. Wanting to have a good relationship also requires honesty. If you are afraid that some childish behavior will disappoint your friend, observe if your friend shows clear signs of dislike when you exhibit such behavior. Or is it just your own perception that your friend finds these behaviors annoying and disappointing? Differentiate your friend's attitude and then communicate. If your friend directly expresses dislike for your childish behavior, then you should remember not to make these mistakes again in the future. You can communicate with your friend, admit your mistakes, and express a sincere attitude. Let your friend know how important they are to you and that you hope they won't be disappointed. If it's just your own perception that these behaviors might disappoint your friend, then don't keep this thought to yourself. Don't speculate about your friend's attitude. Just bring it up and ask if your friend dislikes these behaviors. If your friend says yes, then you can express your own thoughts and admit your mistakes. If your friend says no, then you can express your fear of losing such a good friend and ask what behaviors they don't like, so you can avoid them in the future. It can be like having a chat with each other. ▼▼▼ In fact, no matter what, the question asker has already acknowledged their mistake, which is a good start. Only by recognizing the mistake can you make an effort to correct it. The question asker also doesn't like these childish behaviors deep down, but once they happen, there's nothing they can do except blame themselves. Nobody is perfect. Even a rabbit will bite when it gets agitated, let alone a person. Everyone has their imperfections, and everyone has the right to dislike others. It's impossible not to offend anyone; the question is whether it happens more or less often. The question asker shouldn't put too much pressure on themselves, they should relax and tell themselves to be more mindful in the future. Making friends means opening up and having conversations, getting to know each other better.

Hello, OP. OP thinks that they have done some things that make their friends feel very childish and ridiculous, and they are afraid of leaving a bad impression on their friends. It seems like OP cares a lot about them and cares about their opinion of OP. After doing something wrong, not only do they feel anxious, but they also care about whether their friend's opinion of them has changed for the worse. Friendship also requires mutual acceptance. If they are disappointed with OP or have negative opinions of them just because of this one thing, then they are not truly a friend. And maybe the other person didn't even think much about this thing and just sees it as a small matter. Nobody is perfect, and we all have the potential to make mistakes or have bad moods. In these situations, it is inevitable that we may act impulsively, and afterwards, we may feel regret. Therefore, OP should try to relax and open their mind, as other people may not care about these small things as much. Good luck~.

question: Middle school girl, feels uncontrollable fear when seeing a knife, unsure of the reason.
description: Because of being exposed to some negative news, I now feel scared every time I see a knife. I even have imaginary scenes of murder in my head. And I feel guilty for having these thoughts. It's like my brain is uncontrollably fixated on negative things, and I'm really afraid that one day I might accidentally harm someone. This is the most troubling problem for me right now, and I've been feeling distressed for several months. I don't want to think about this, but I still feel uneasy. It's just that I randomly have thoughts of causing harm to others, even when I'm not angry and others treat me well. I don't know why I have these thoughts. Now I'm starting to doubt if there's something wrong with me mentally. I have been struggling for a long time, and I sincerely ask for your help. Can you please analyze the reasons behind this based on the paragraph I wrote? I hope someone can help me, as no one has answered me so far.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, mental crisis, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can understand that you feel scared when you see a knife and have thoughts of killing someone. You worry if one day you will actually commit murder and you don't know why these thoughts appear. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Fantasizing about dangerous situations when seeing dangerous objects is actually our own consciousness protecting ourselves. Just like how standing at a great height may make people feel the urge to jump, many people advise against standing on high platforms. Being near a lake or sea may make people feel the urge to jump in, and when seeing a knife, you may feel like it will harm you... These thoughts are actually a way for our selves to protect us. When you see these things, the first scenes that come to your mind are related to danger, thus making you feel scared and preventing you from taking action. 2. Additionally, there is an inherent sense of fascination with blood, knives, and danger deep inside people. This involves the archetype of the dark side of our inner selves. Sometimes, people develop a curious interest in learning about terrifying things. That's why sometimes horror movies attract people, the more afraid they are, the more they want to watch. 3. If these thoughts are affecting your daily life, I would recommend seeking a professional mental health counselor to understand the situation and obtain more systematic and effective solutions. I hope this is helpful for you.

question: Is the unconscious desire for others to feel happy, people-pleasing?
description: Why do we hope that everyone around us can feel happy, and why do we care so much about other people's emotions? It can be exhausting, but we can't control it.

answers.answer_text: Hello cutie! First of all, let's determine whether you have a people-pleasing personality. The main characteristics of this trait are: the motivation behind their behavior is a lack of self-worth and fear of not being loved, even to the point of being afraid of being abandoned. This becomes an unhealthy, compulsive, and painful pattern of behavior. It seems like you're saying that you find it exhausting to focus on other people's emotions, which could indicate a people-pleasing personality. #Why do I want to make others happy? Bringing joy to others is a valuable part of life. Our elders have also taught us this, and taking care of and loving others is one of the highest forms of spiritual practice. Making others happy is an effective way to convey our own worth, gain a sense of value, and experience happiness. But are you truly experiencing this sense of value and happiness from it? It seems not. So where is the problem? It lies in our motivation. We pay attention to others' emotions not out of a desire for "I am happy and I also want them to be happy," but out of a desire for "I am not happy, I feel invaluable, and I hope to receive a feeling of love and acceptance by making them happy." In other words, we treat love and acceptance as a transaction. I must pay a price that causes me pain in order to receive it. And when we don't get the expected response, our inner balance is disrupted. This behavior pattern is an unhealthy, compulsive, and painful one. The formation of a people-pleasing personality is due to childhood trauma, specifically the lack of unconditional love from our original family. But I'm not asking you to blame your parents! That would only make us more miserable. Instead, let's explore the reasons behind this behavior and then find the right solutions to heal ourselves slowly, to become the person we want to be rather than the person we're forced to be. This is our ultimate goal. #Only when we make ourselves happy, when we have inner strength, can we pass on happiness to others. Everyone has their own life issues to face. Our main issue at the moment is the self-healing of our people-pleasing personality. It's a long but meaningful journey. Once you embark on this path, you will gradually discover that your pain is slowly dissipating, and you will learn to love yourself more and more. Here are a few suggestions: 1) Practice mindfulness: Mindfulness is being aware of your present state without biases or a closed mindset. Because our thoughts are often clouded by past "traumas" and the fear of being rejected, criticized, or even denied if we don't please others, through mindfulness, we can establish a connection with our bodies and minds, and bravely face difficult experiences, including the feeling when the emotions of needing to please others overwhelm us. 2) Remember that our thoughts are just thoughts, not facts: Through a period of mindfulness practice, we focus on the present moment. When pleaser thoughts arise in our minds, instead of immediately acting on them based on instinct, we gently greet them as an adult would greet a love-deprived child, saying, "Oh, you're here! Hello!" Rather than engaging with these thoughts, because behind them is the love-deprived version of yourself! If we resist these thoughts, we are essentially rejecting our past selves. But what is wrong with the love-deprived child? They only want unconditional love. 3) You have the power to give unconditional love to this love-deprived child within you: Regardless of our age, when we realize that we are responsible for our own lives and that we want to make ourselves happy, we actually have the ability to take care of this love-deprived child. When there aren't so many ups and downs within you, set aside a "Children's Day" for yourself. On this day, do what the child inside you wanted to do at that time, spend time with them, talk to them, and assure them that you will meet their needs and give them unconditional love. Because this unconditional love already exists within us, we just accidentally lost it when we were young. When you can give yourself happiness, you will find it easy and joyful to bring happiness to others. However, whether others truly receive this happiness is up to them! It is their responsibility, not ours. Lastly, I hope that in the future, you can truly be happy and truly find joy in the process of bringing happiness to others!

question: I am in my third year of high school, and recently I have been feeling overwhelmed and unable to focus on studying. Could this be a mental health issue?
description: The college entrance examination is approaching, but recently I feel like giving up. I feel very uncomfortable and low in mood. In the past week, I have been impatient with my friends and even had a falling out with my best friend because of my irritability. My mindset is exploding and I can no longer concentrate. I thought about seeking counseling at the psychological counseling center, but I am introverted and too timid to go. I feel like I'm going crazy. Do I have a psychological problem?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: Hello dear questioner! Thank you for inviting me to answer! I understand your current feelings and mood very well. I have experienced the stress of the college entrance examination twice before, and that excessive concern and anxiety can push us in the opposite direction of our desires. It's terrible – irritability, anger, impulsiveness, even friends may be affected. Everything is planned, but everything seems to deviate from the track. Here, I am also glad for you. In our time, we didn't understand psychology and didn't know how to seek help. The fact that you can think of and find this place shows that you are capable of learning and applying what you've learned to become independent and self-loving. High tension is also the right state, so there is no need to worry too much. The college entrance examination, how many people talk about it without changing their expression. Our current state is precisely because we care a lot about the college entrance examination. Uncle Kai once said that it is the right state to be nervous in important moments. It means that we have entered a stage of high focus on this matter, where our whole body, mind, and brain are all focused on this. The benefit of this is that it helps us utilize all our resources and energy to face and experience this matter. The downside is that it consumes too much energy and can have negative effects on our emotions. Understanding that high tension is the right state, we can pay less attention to this phenomenon. Knowing that it is like the wind and rain before the rainbow appears, it will naturally pass, and after it passes, there will be many beautiful things, just like the rainbow after the rain. Whether the one-month delay in the epidemic is a blessing or a disaster depends on our mindset. Each era has its unique memories. This year's epidemic has given all human beings a common memory. The college entrance examination during the epidemic, online classes, might be a historical anomaly that has no precedent. The policy given by the Ministry of Education, delaying the college entrance examination by one month, is seen by some as a blessing and by others as a disaster. Let's take a well-known example. Before Bai Niangzi transformed into a human form, she had to overcome the tribulation of thunder in the Jade Pool in order to succeed. Is that tribulation a blessing or a disaster? The answer should be obvious – without experiencing pain, there can be no improvement. So, let's follow suit and bravely await our tribulation. Of course, the test environment for the college entrance examination should be comfortable, at least not worse than our own classrooms. Ultimately, it's all about mindset. Take more deep breaths, insist on morning jogging exercises to keep your brain, heart, and body in a state of tension. Through the magical synergy, I believe you can experience the confidence that comes from having everything under control. Friendship is also tested, and it is a two-way street. To be selfish, the special task of the college entrance examination comes with certain high pressure. Under high pressure, everything is tested – our mental resilience, physical and academic results, as well as parents' mental and logistical abilities. Of course, friends around us are also being tested, whether they can help each other through the college entrance examination. Therefore, I believe that friendship at this stage should not be afraid of being tested. There should be more understanding between each other. Of course, this should not be an excuse to vent our anger on friends. Instead, we should be tolerant and understanding, encouraging and affirming each other's goals and learning strengths, helping to improve learning and overcome weaknesses. Since it is a two-way street, if there is a derailment, I think everything can be explained after the college entrance examination. Of course, if you realize there is a problem, it is best to explain it as soon as possible. Lifelong friends do not need too many, but at critical moments, they will definitely stand by our side, and we should also stand up for our friends when they need us. Just like the saying in the martial arts world, we would lay down our lives for a friend. It makes sense! .................................................. Comprehensive advice, for now, it is still important to relax your mood appropriately. When you are in a bad mood, exercise or indulge in your hobbies a little more. At this time, don't worry too much about wasting time because it's a waste to sharpen the axe without cutting the wood. Also, don't worry too much about mistakes, even in friendships or even romantic relationships. At this time, they should become like angels helping us, rather than blocking our path and demanding things from friends. Lastly, it is important to have clear goals in mind. When there is a goal, match it with confidence and determination. By focusing on the goal, you will naturally spend less time paying attention to other things. In the end, believe that there is luck beyond effort. Now, despite your efforts, leave the result to luck. No matter what, be satisfied with yourself. Wishing you all the best! May your dreams come true! When the sky is blue, life can be beautiful! The world is loved by me!

Hello: From your brief description, I can sense your irritability, confusion, and feelings of suffocation! Take a moment to relax, take deep breaths, listen to soothing music! Or engage in some moderate exercise, like running or playing sports, to alleviate your irritability and suffocation! I can feel your impatience, what else besides your friends is causing your impatience? Is it related to studying, family, or relationships with classmates? What is troubling you to the point where you can't concentrate on your studies? With the college entrance examination approaching, you can seek the help of a counselor to receive emotional adjustment and relaxation training, and adjust your mindset to prepare for the college entrance examination! Feel free to reach out to me for consultation, I hope I can be of help to you!

question: 34 years old, about to have the first child, considering divorcing?
description: I used to think that my married life was going well. When she got pregnant, ever since the other night when she hit me because of a communication issue, I feel like I am a useless burden. Because we work in different towns, when I used to visit her, she would get angry and tell me to leave. Sometimes, even in front of my family, she would tell me to go away. I have always chosen to tolerate it and thought it wasn't necessary to argue with her. But until a few days ago when she hit me and left multiple scratches on my face, and then kicked me out in the middle of the night, and I ended up spending the night at a hotel, I finally realized that I am not important. Even though the baby is about to be born, I really feel like there is no need to persist anymore. I want to start over.

answers.answer_text: Give the OP a hug! I can understand the OP's feelings of depression, suffocation, loneliness, and discomfort. Being a husband who is physically abused by his own wife and being told to leave in front of his own relatives, it's a complete loss of face. Any man would find it difficult to understand, accept, and endure such a situation. Generally, when men encounter such situations, they feel angry and may argue or even resort to physical violence against their wives. As a wife, her words and actions are a denial, attack, insult, and disrespect towards her husband. It is pushing the boundaries and provoking her husband, or one could say it is tempting the OP to respond with the same violence, insults, and attacks as a way of communication. The OP's reaction has always been to tolerate and feel that it is unnecessary to argue with her. Perhaps, the OP feels that suppressing and tolerating can make his wife feel his love for her, and he hopes to gain her understanding, acceptance, and approval. However, for the wife, if her "heavy blow" is met with no response from her husband, it is either because her "heavy blow" lacks enough impact, or her husband has secretly practiced a "golden armor". In either case, it makes her feel rejected, denying her ability and value as an adult and a wife, causing her to feel extremely anxious and fearful. When the stress brought by these emotions exceeds the control of conscious self, it instinctively manifests in ways that conscious self cannot understand, accept, or approve, such as her physical abuse, scolding, and insults towards the OP. The communication and interaction between spouses are based on equality, respect, trust, understanding, acceptance, and approval of each other. These conditions are all necessary and any missing element would hinder the development of the emotional relationship between spouses. At the same time, in many cases, the communication between spouses can also influence each other. One party's words and actions can affect the psychological and emotional state of the other party, and vice versa. From the information provided by the OP, it can be seen that the communication between the OP and his wife lacks these conditions. Even the most basic element of equality and respect is absent. The wife is "superior" and can physically abuse and scold her husband, while the husband is "inferior" and submissive, suppressing and enduring. With such a "distance" between the two, how can there be a sense of safety, security, and stability in their interactions? How can it guarantee the stable and harmonious development of the emotional relationship between spouses? The OP wants a divorce now, which indeed allows him to no longer face the pain caused by his wife's violent treatment and the problems in their relationship. However, the issues in their communication and interaction will still persist and continue to affect the development of the OP's emotional and marital relationship. Therefore, I personally suggest that the OP make an appointment with a suitable therapist to receive systematic psychological counseling, to gradually solve the problems that trouble him, improve the way he communicates and interacts with his wife, and help stabilize and harmonize the emotional relationship between the OP and his wife.

Hello, OP, seeing your words is like seeing you in person. I can understand your feelings and sense that you feel disposable and relatively unimportant. However, I still hope that you can consider it carefully. First, before getting divorced, OP should think carefully about several questions. Why did something like this happen when the previous married life was good? Where exactly is the communication problem between the couple? Has all the past happiness disappeared? Do you not miss it at all now? The child is about to be born. What will happen to the child after the divorce? What are your plans after the divorce? Can't you tolerate your wife's current state? Why do you feel disposable? Second, analysis -- when she gets angry, she also tells me to leave and tells me to get lost in front of my family. From OP's words, it can be seen that OP's wife is a relatively irritable person, but OP has mentioned that you had a good relationship in the past, which shows that you were able to accept certain shortcomings of your wife. In the state of anger, many people are irrational and don't think too much. A few days ago, she hit me and scratched my face in several places, and she kicked me out in the middle of the night. From OP's words, it is unclear whether OP's wife has always been irritable or has become irritable since getting pregnant. She even injured OP. Third, during pregnancy, pregnant women are prone to unstable emotions and temper. Perhaps OP doesn't know that each pregnant woman is different during pregnancy, but many pregnant women are emotionally unstable and easily get angry. After getting pregnant, the hormones in a woman's body change, causing the pregnant woman's emotions to become more sensitive and affecting their mental state. If it is serious, they may even experience "prepartum depression." In addition, this is your wife's first pregnancy, so the pressure on women increases and they may fear that something might go wrong with the baby. Many expectant mothers feel anxious because they worry that they won't be able to handle the role of a new mother, or they may have fear of childbirth, leading to emotional instability and easily getting angry. During pregnancy, the emotions of pregnant women can be overly sensitive, and sometimes even slight improper communication can make them feel a little aggrieved, even if you feel it's not a big deal or she didn't think it was a big deal before, many emotions can be exaggerated during pregnancy. A few suggestions: Stay calm and communicate harmoniously. Since you and your wife don't live in the same town, there may be communication problems, resulting in your thoughts being different and not fully in sync. Put yourself in her shoes, think from her perspective, and communicate harmoniously with your wife, letting her know your needs and your attitude. The child is about to be born. If possible, I don't recommend getting divorced. This is not only being irresponsible to the family and the child, but also to yourself. Understand your wife and find your own value. You mentioned several times that you feel disposable, so you need to do a self-evaluation. In fact, during your wife's pregnancy, the husband plays a very important role. During pregnancy, wives really hope to receive understanding and love from their husbands, and to have their husbands by their side to listen to their complaints or vent their stress. So sometimes you shouldn't take your wife's words too seriously, she may just say something without really meaning it. Have a correct understanding and open-mindedness. Deal with your wife's actions correctly. You mentioned "wanting a rebirth" in your words, but do you know, being together as a couple, getting married and having children is not easy. It's not like being in a romantic relationship, where you only talk about the beautiful moments. In a marriage, there will always be some difficulties that cannot be avoided. If you can get married, it means that both you and your wife are capable of accepting each other's minor flaws and have gone through a period of adjustment. Understanding and mutual consideration are truly necessary in a marriage. As the saying goes, "It takes a hundred years to build a ship to sail together, and a thousand years to build a pillow to sleep together." Hope you will carefully consider it!

Although people often say that they should encourage reconciliation rather than separation, some fundamental issues still need to be communicated clearly in advance. 1. Physical aggression is truly the bottom line. Most of the time, people subconsciously believe that domestic violence is something done by men, but there are indeed many unreasonable women in life. Therefore, we can reflect on our own problems first, after all, some things are definitely brought about by our own indulgence. The poster mentioned that the other party was spoiled since childhood, so she does not consider the feelings of others in many matters. Therefore, in certain situations, she will act recklessly, especially when it comes to physical aggression - if it happens once, it will happen again. Therefore, this time we must be firm. Some things can be tolerated, but some things are the bottom line. Of course, in this process, we must protect ourselves and prevent the other party from doing something extreme that may harm herself or the child. We really cannot resort to physical aggression, but when the other party's emotions are unstable, we should also show a bit of assertiveness and let them know where our bottom line is. Sometimes, accommodating is not love. 2. Some problems need to be faced together. It is evident that the other party is indeed dominant. If we truly want a divorce, will the other party compromise? Moreover, there are still some restrictions on getting a divorce during pregnancy. If the relationship between both parties can be improved or adjusted, is the poster willing to start over again? We can recall whether both parties had a certain emotional foundation before and at what point did they become somewhat incompatible? If there was no emotional connection and understanding right from the beginning, it would indeed be very difficult to change. We need to be prepared for the worst. If there were only some changes that occurred later, we can find a time to calmly discuss and talk about future plans with the other party. See if they can accept them and then proceed with the next adjustment. The world and I love you.

Hello! I saw your distress and I hope to offer you some warmth. You described your wife as hot-tempered and even physically abusive. Your first child is about to be born and you are considering divorce. First of all, I want to say that domestic violence is wrong regardless of gender, and in severe cases, it can be reported to the police. Now, let's analyze your wife's behavior. Was she always like this from the beginning or did something happen that caused her to change? If she was like this from the beginning, why were you able to accept her before but not now? Besides, your child is about to be born. If something happened that caused her to change, you need to address the underlying issues. If her behavior changed because she is pregnant, it could be due to hormonal influences and she may be feeling distressed. Have you taken good care of her and understood the difficulties of pregnancy? Carrying a child for ten months is extremely exhausting for a woman, and that child is also yours, so you don't have to bear any physical hardships. However, you can sincerely show care and concern for her, and she will be able to feel it. There is no inexplicable hatred or love in this world. If your marriage can still be salvaged, try to communicate with your wife, figure out where the problem lies. Your child is about to be born, and divorcing now would be extremely cruel for your wife. If there is hope for reconciliation, I encourage you to give it your best effort. Stay strong and good luck!

Hello, first of all, I sympathize with you and understand your distress. When we are conducting couples therapy, our goal is not just to address the present issues, but to find deeper problems within the marital relationship, specifically whether each other's attachment needs are being met. When exploring the attachment needs of both parties, we must first determine which type of attachment relationship each belongs to. Attachment relationships are influenced by one's upbringing and significant attachment figures (parents, caregivers, siblings), and these attachment styles tend to persist throughout one's life, particularly manifesting in marital relationships in adulthood. The current state of your relationship with your wife may appear to be caused by various events and personality differences, but in reality, it is the emotional connection between you two that is experiencing problems. Healthy marital relationships primarily depend on a close emotional bond between partners. Even if partners have completely different personalities, a strong intimate bond can be maintained. This requires both individuals to maintain a positive and constructive interaction pattern. Specifically, both individuals should be able to express their attachment needs without obstacles, and both should be able to see and actively respond to each other's needs. Even if their viewpoints differ, they should be able to accept and understand each other, soothe each other's emotions, and pay attention to the underlying needs and desires. By doing so, conflicts can be timely resolved and problems can be addressed in a more positive manner. Therefore, I hope that you can sincerely recognize your own inner needs and honestly express them to your wife. At the same time, try to understand your wife's true needs and respond positively. By changing the established interaction patterns, perhaps your relationship can take a turn for the better. After all, with the imminent arrival of a child, it is crucial to actively repair the emotional connection and provide a complete and happy family for the child.

I have finished reading your description. There are a few things I would like to clarify. First, you mentioned that in the past, you felt that your relationship with your spouse was quite good. However, later you mentioned that your wife would directly insult you in front of your family or at work when she was angry. These two pieces of information contradict each other. Can you help me clarify again? On one hand, you say that the relationship between you and your spouse is good, but on the other hand, she insults you without regard for your dignity. It just doesn't seem right. Secondly, the relationship between you and your spouse should have gone through a process to develop to the current situation. From the beginning of your relationship until now, what behaviors and words of yours do you think have caused her to become worse? I see a change in her behavior from your description. Have you ever thought about why this change occurred? Thirdly, how much do you understand about the psychological changes that occur in a pregnant woman during pregnancy? Divorce is not difficult; it can be resolved with a trip to the civil affairs bureau. However, it does not guarantee a fresh start for you. Even after the divorce, there may be various disputes that need to be resolved. It would be better to postpone this decision for now. Let's see what you can do first. In your description, you mention that your spouse is dominant, and accordingly, you appear weak. Of course, you can give yourself a reasonable explanation, such as not caring about petty matters, being tolerant as a man, and so on. But you have also seen that things have not been developing in a positive direction. This proves that your behavior and thinking need to change. How did you react when the problem first arose and she crossed the line? If you tolerate it the first time, there will be a second time, and even a third time, and the next time she will become more and more outrageous. This is your current situation. You now feel that you are dispensable, but in her eyes, your behavior does not make you a man. Do you understand this? This is also the tragedy of a good man. From a male perspective, you are not a bad person, and many of your actions are those of a good man. I believe you have also seen a joke, when a girl rejects a guy, what does he say? He says, "You're a good person, I don't deserve you." But think about it, does she really think you're a good person and feel unworthy of you? This is why I want you to put the idea of divorce on hold, because even if you choose this path, it doesn't mean your behavior patterns will change, and it doesn't mean you will avoid the same things happening in the future. If you don't take the time to think about which behaviors and thoughts have led to your current situation, you may fall into the same pit in the future. The female brain has an instinctive detection system. It's called a loser test. This detection system will test you from time to time. If you respond well to her and pass the test, she will stop, but if you fail the test, the frequency will increase. You need to understand how she perceives you. In conclusion, you lack a certain aura and masculine leadership. The ultimate outcome of allowing a woman to always take the lead is that she will lose interest.

Hello, OP: Previously, your married life was quite good, so why has her temper become a bit bigger after getting pregnant? She gets angry easily and even becomes physically violent towards you. You feel like you want to divorce because you feel dispensable. I suggest that you don't rush to make a decision, OP. When she gets angry, you feel unfairly treated. I recommend that you communicate calmly and well. You are going to be a father soon, so think carefully whether you really want a divorce. First, I suggest understanding why a pregnant woman's temper changes. After pregnancy, due to the influence of estrogen and progesterone, as well as hCG levels, pregnant women sometimes feel irritable and depressed. Nausea and aversion to oily foods during pregnancy can also affect a pregnant woman's mood. Additionally, pregnant women are more emotionally fragile, and at this time, they hope that their husband and people around them will pay more attention to them. So, OP, you need more understanding and tolerance. I suggest you spend more time with her. No matter what happens and no matter what she says, give her the best care. Take some time to go for a walk with her or listen to music together. Doing some light exercise can also help relieve stress. I believe you will get through this difficult period. Wishing you happiness.

Hello, from your description, it seems that your wife has a somewhat irritable temperament and does not give you face in front of your family. She gets angry whenever she wants and you feel that you are dispensable. I'm not sure if your wife's behavior is due to her pregnancy or if it is her natural personality. If it is due to pregnancy, she may be experiencing some prenatal depression and mood swings. During pregnancy, every mother's physiological reactions and personality can undergo changes, so she needs your care and understanding. If it is her natural personality, I suggest expressing your feelings to your wife, letting her know that you don't like being treated this way and that it makes you feel dispensable. Try to suppress thoughts of divorce for now, as expectant mothers cannot handle too much emotional upheaval. When the child is born, have a good conversation with your wife, without being too assertive or feeling overly aggrieved. Try to communicate calmly and rationally. Once you become parents, every decision you make together is important.

question: High school studying, changed to a new desk and new teacher, feeling very irritable and uncomfortable recently, what should I do?
description: I did well in my first year of high school and could rank in the top 100 of my grade. In my sophomore year, I got a new desk mate and a new teacher. Now, I don't know why, but I find myself dozing off in class every day, unable to finish my homework, and I don't have time to review or prepare for lessons. I'm falling behind in my understanding of the subject matter. I don't even talk to my desk mate anymore. Initially, we used to chat, but I realized she is very selfish. When I feel sleepy in class, she doesn't remind me, even if the teacher notices me, she doesn't say anything. She doesn't inform me about any important class announcements. She won't even let me know when it's time to turn in assignments. And she is so disciplined and smart, understanding the lessons every day and completing her assignments. I feel even more useless being around her, and it makes me feel upset and irritated. In the mid-term exam, she ranked second in the class, while I ranked 40th...
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hey there, I feel you, based on what you described, you seem really dissatisfied with some of your desk mate's actions. You feel like there's a lack of camaraderie and warmth among classmates, and you don't like people who ignore others' difficulties and are irresponsible. I truly sympathize with your situation. According to your description, you've been facing difficulties in your studies recently and really want someone to help or guide you. You may be hoping your desk mate could play that role, but maybe not everything can go as planned. We shouldn't expect others to take responsibility for our own matters too much. Maybe the other person isn't as indifferent as you think. It could be just because your relationship hasn't developed to a close level yet, and they may not know how accepting you are towards them. So, they might not want to do anything that could potentially restrict you and are following a moderate social boundary. Perhaps you can find an opportunity to communicate with them, ask their opinion, or if they'd be willing to remind you about assignments and not falling asleep. Maybe after getting to know each other better, you can break the barrier and develop a deep friendship.

question: How can I stop arguing and hurting others?
description: Junior year, female student, recently had a homework assignment that led to inconsistent opinions and couldn't persuade my classmates to agree with my own viewpoint. It has also resulted in a strain on our relationship. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, in a group setting, it is normal to have different opinions on the same matter. Continue to communicate until both sides reach a mutual agreement or one side acknowledges the other. From your description, it can be observed that conflicts and contradictions have arisen due to disagreements with your classmates, which have affected your relationship. Try to communicate with the other person again, clearly express your views on the assignment, and highlight the benefits and strengths of your own approach. Also, allow the other person to express their opinions and try to think from their perspective. It is difficult for us to consider a problem from the other person's point of view due to our inherent thinking patterns, unless we consciously remind ourselves to see the problem from their perspective. However, our own opinions still carry greater weight. On the basis of ensuring sufficient communication, both of you can compromise and incorporate each other's opinions into the assignment, finding a middle-ground solution, while also eliminating unnecessary elements or areas of major disagreement. Since both of you value your own thought processes, it is understandable that you may be unwilling to concede. That is why it is important to include efforts and contributions from both parties in the assignment. Additionally, it is important to communicate with the other person that the assignment is just an assignment. Even if neither of you ultimately compromises with the other, agree not to let it affect your relationship. You both need to face the assignment together, rather than considering each other as enemies. Separating the issue from the emotions involved may also help in dealing with the assignment. Actively discussing and considering each other's perspectives will certainly lead to shared opinions. Maintain an open attitude towards your own ideas about the assignment, accept others' opinions, and preserve your own. Best wishes.

question: I hope I don't have any family members, so that no one will take care of me and I won't have to be so afraid.
description: Family refers to my grandmother, mother, and father. My parents divorced when I was 1 year old. I was raised by my aunt since I was young, so I can say that I have been living aimlessly. It has been 3 years since I graduated, and I can say that I am careless about life, and life is careless about me. I graduated from junior college, and my unstable personality has always been a barrier for me in terms of work. I am afraid of facing society, and even more afraid of the criticism from others in society. I am afraid of being hurt by others. My child is over a year old, and I have not been a good role model as a mother. I have very little initiative, and my family says that I am lazy, and that my husband will not be able to support me for a lifetime. Although my husband is okay with me and accepts my history of mental illness, I may focus too much on gains and losses. I attach too much importance to other people's rejection, so my emotions are always up and down. I hate my sensitivity and I cannot see a future. My mother said she will beat me when I go back for the Lunar New Year, and my father has a severe mental disorder and is violent. I hope they die so that no one will control me anymore, and I won't be so scared. I really feel powerless.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, family control.

answers.answer_text: The lack of emotional connection and patterns of interaction from childhood makes us feel insecure, even now that we have become mothers ourselves, we still worry about bad things happening. Firstly, if our parents resort to violence, we are no longer children and we can choose to leave or resist. Although our parents gave us life, it does not mean they have the right to do whatever they want. We can start by becoming psychologically independent. Now that we are mothers, I believe we do not want our children to follow the same path, so we need to eliminate certain methods of parenting from within ourselves. Secondly, being a full-time housewife, it is indeed difficult to find a job during breastfeeding period, but it is not appropriate to put all the financial pressure on our husband. If there is an opportunity and our parents-in-law can help take care of the child, we can go out and find a job to realize our own worth and achieve financial freedom. Lastly, it is important to have conversations with our husband and plan for our shared future, such as our child's education and the family's future development. We should not rely on each other for everything, we can work together to find solutions and overcome challenges. Our little family is maintained by ourselves, and we can face and overcome problems together. Don't worry, you are not alone, you have your children and your husband who love you. The world and I love you.

question: My parents scold me, and my relatives also look down on me. I feel really tired of living. What should I do?
description: It's really mentally exhausting to live like this. My father and mother scold me and look down on me. Even my relatives look down on me.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, we can understand the following: 1. OP feels that their parents and relatives look down on them. 2. OP feels sad and upset about this, lacking motivation. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Other people's opinions of oneself sometimes have subjective distortions based on their own mood at the time. Do OP's parents and relatives really look down on them completely? Is there really nothing about OP that they appreciate? OP needs to think about this themselves or directly communicate with their parents and relatives, sincerely asking for their opinions of oneself, and what are their strengths and weaknesses. Then, make improvements accordingly. 2. Moreover, even if OP's parents and relatives have certain opinions of OP due to various reasons, it does not mean that OP is a terrible person. OP's future is in their own hands, and they are also a multifaceted individual. Their parents and relatives only have knowledge of the part of OP's life at home, and they may only see OP's shortcomings or exaggerate certain mistakes OP has made. It is important for OP to reflect on what kind of person they are and take action accordingly. Hope this is helpful to OP.

question: What is true love? I have been with my boyfriend for over two years, but I still don't know what it truly means.
description: I have been with my boyfriend for over two years, but because he is my first love, I don't know if I truly love him. Sometimes I think this is good, we understand each other and he accommodates me. But I am really scared that one day he won't treat me well anymore, so I don't dare to fully invest myself. Until now, I don't know if I love him or not, and I don't know what it feels like to truly love someone.

answers.answer_text: Congratulations on gaining a first love that is destined to be profound and lasting. I think this might be a bit like traveling to a new place, fearing missing out on something, fearing getting lost, and wanting to quickly and efficiently acquire local knowledge. I believe you really want to cherish this romantic relationship, right? If so, you can imagine two scenarios: if your future self from 10 years later came back to the present, what tips would she give you? And if your future self from 30 years later came back, what would she say to you? I hope you can enjoy the process earlier and wait patiently for the flowers to bloom and the fruits to ripen.

question: 17-year-old girl, always thinking about doing that kind of thing? Dislike herself for being like this.
description: It used to be okay, sometimes I would reminisce and masturbate. Lately, the desire is getting stronger and stronger, it suddenly comes, and then I would search for manga novels myself and masturbate while reading. No matter what the environment or situation is, once the desire arises, I can't suppress it. I also fantasize about having a man do those things to me in real life, but I am too scared, and I have no intention of dating, yet I really want it. Is there something wrong with my mental health? What should I do? I am very worried, every time I act like that, I really hate myself.

answers.answer_text: Hug hug, we don't have any mental problems, just that after suddenly coming into contact with certain things, we may have certain associations, so sometimes it makes it difficult for us to think calmly. 1. Masturbation is something that most people engage in. Since we didn't receive proper sex education when we were young, and our elders also avoided talking about sex openly, when we first encountered it, it felt like we were opening a new door for ourselves. And everyone's level of desire is different, so we shouldn't label ourselves deliberately. Teenagers who engage in masturbation are not bad kids in the eyes of others. In fact, many people have similar behaviors during adolescence, but everyone suppresses their emotions, and due to some external views, we believe that this behavior is immoral. In fact, masturbation is understandable, but we need to learn to distinguish between reality and fantasy, and sometimes we need to pay attention to the occasion, after all, some things are quite private. 2. Sometimes we need to learn to distinguish clearly. In fact, many comics and novels are deliberately exaggerated, because people are curious, and the more suppressed we are, the more other desires we will have. So what we see is just a trigger, but we shouldn't act on it easily, because some things may not be true. Just like when we read some fantasy novels, we can have different images and scenes in our minds through the description in the text, but many adaptation dramas produced in reality cannot meet our expectations because each reader has their own ideas. Desire is something that many people engage in, but sometimes we also need a little rationality, understand what we truly want, and learn to protect ourselves. Of course, in the future, if you have any troubles, you can talk to Xiaofan Guoguo, we can find a solution together. The world and I love you.

This kind of thing is very normal. We humans all have the right to enjoy the pleasures in life. Being excessively attached only indicates a lack of self-discipline. It's not that there's something wrong with you; it may be that your life is relatively boring and monotonous. I suggest finding some new and interesting hobbies for yourself. For example, I enjoy doing bullet journaling and playing with colored clay. When your attention is diverted to other beautiful things, your day will become more colorful, and naturally, your desire for such things will decrease, sweetheart. You're great, keep striving to make yourself even better.

question: Did I join the wrong group? Can psychology make people speak in plain language?
description: Staying in a psychology group, when the host asked everyone to introduce themselves and communicate with each other, it seemed like everyone was being pretentious, using various jargon that was incomprehensible, and showing off in various ways, as if they were trying to prove who was more impressive. But very few people talked about their feelings or their learning experiences. Looking at this, I started to wonder if I joined the wrong group. Isn't communication about understanding, listening, and feeling each other? Or perhaps those who act pretentious actually have feelings and thoughts that they can't express?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, social networking applications

answers.answer_text: A month ago, I had the same distress as you. Joining a psychology group was to communicate and share with others, to understand others' learning progress, and to share my own experiences. I couldn't understand why those people in the group always talked about some high-level things. After observing and summarizing the group members' speeches over a month, I found that this situation was caused by the diversity and large number of members in the group. The group I joined had over a hundred people, and there were five to ten active speakers every day. It was considered an active group. During group study and discussions, due to the close relationships among members, the chat content could be more in-depth and specific. However, in a large group, people didn't know each other, so when speaking, they needed to explain the cause and effect and couldn't achieve a telepathic understanding. That's why specialized terminology plays a role in simplifying conversation by describing the cause and effect. Because these specialized terms are common codes used by psychology students, they don't need much explanation; everyone can understand their meanings and start chatting happily. For those who don't understand, they can search on Baidu to find answers. So, using specialized terms is not showing off. If you don't understand these contents, you can learn and understand them bravely, and overcome this barrier. Keep it up! If you want to get feedback on your studies or enjoy more in-depth, specific, and private communication, I suggest forming a small group and finding some peers who are at a similar learning stage to carry out themed readings of books.

question: What does it mean when a man says to a woman "I am willing to do things for you willingly"?
description: The relationship is generally normal, without any ambiguity. The man is much older than the woman, and both have families.
keywords: Love, infidelity, attachment and dependence, affection.

answers.answer_text: I think it is difficult for us to give you a definite answer to your question, but since you have raised this question, I suggest that you do some self-reflection: You can try to answer the following questions: 1. What specific things does this man mean when he says "I am willing to do things for you"? 2. Since you have this thought and doubt, what do you think is the purpose of the other person's willingness to help you? Or what do you hope the other person's thoughts are? You also mentioned that there is no ambiguity between the two of you, and you both have families. Is it possible that you are overthinking? I suggest that you don't get too anxious and nervous, maybe it's just mutual help, right? The world and I love you, blessings to you, Jingjing.

The listener might not have intentions, but the speaker does. If the listener doesn't perceive any ambiguity, what about the speaker? Do they also think the same way? If both parties are in relationships, it is recommended to maintain a certain distance. Just because you have no intentions doesn't mean the speaker doesn't either. Both parties have families, so it's important to be mindful of the boundaries when speaking to avoid unnecessary worries at home, right? When the person uttered that sentence, aren't you also pondering its meaning now? Since you already have doubts, it's better to approach with caution.

question: How to protect oneself and children from family conflicts?
description: My mother-in-law is very dominant. Both my father-in-law and mother-in-law conspire against me, especially when they have their own agenda. They constantly use underhanded tactics and bully me. My husband doesn't stand up for me, instead he listens to his mother. I'm particularly afraid of her. My mother-in-law once said that as long as she is around, she won't let me cause trouble. She never stops to consider what she's doing. She often tries to sow discord. Even though it's them who started bullying, they always blame me. When I got married, they cheated me out of the bride price and didn't give it to me. After getting married, they kept coming to my house to cause trouble. When my father passed away, they acted indifferent as if it had nothing to do with them. After having a child, the three of them conspired to destroy the bond between me and my child. Whatever I say is wrong, but whatever they say is right. They won't let my child eat anything I prepare, but they give my child anything they want without saying anything. I'm very angry. Every time I argue with my husband, my in-laws come out and stare at me, trying to intimidate me and suppress me. What should I do? I really want a divorce.
keywords: Family, family relationships, family control, mother-in-law and daughter-in-law relationship.

answers.answer_text: There are generally two approaches to solving a dilemma. One is to solve it externally, such as in the case of the OP facing seemingly unsolvable family conflict, they can divorce as they suggested, so at least their family cannot bully them anymore. Alternatively, they can seek powerful external assistance, making sure they are treated well. It is important to see if there are sufficient external resources available to resolve the dilemma. The other approach is to solve it internally, which few people choose because facing oneself can be painful. However, the benefit is that you will have autonomy and control over the situation, as it will change based on your own changes. Based on what you mentioned about your husband not supporting you and instead listening to his mother, it seems like both of you are still in a childish state of "he is not married, you are not married". In describing the situation, you actually avoided discussing your own behavior and responsibility in the current relationship status. For example, I wonder what role you play in their eyes that makes them feel the need to concentrate their efforts and come up with strategies to deal with you. I am just giving an example because the relationships involved here could be very complex, and because you also mentioned your own family, many of the feelings you have may not solely belong to you. Every dilemma is an opportunity; it just requires facing it.

question: Why didn't so many things in my childhood leave me with any emotional scars, despite my fragile mental state?
description: I suddenly remembered now that I experienced so many terrible things in my childhood, why didn't they cause a serious impact on me? For example, one day when I was sleeping, I suddenly found my cousin lying on my bed and I wasn't wearing pants. I was 14 years old that year and I was scared, so I ran to my grandmother's room. For example, when I went to my aunt's house with my grandmother, I encountered a kind stranger who gave me a ride. Because the motorcycle was carrying goods, I could only sit next to him and he reached his hand below me. I was afraid, so I got off the car before reaching my grandmother and waited for her. For example, the father of the girl next door would always speak inappropriately to me when there was no one around. There was even one time when I passed by their bathroom, he exposed himself and I quickly fled disgusted. And there was an old man behind my house who lacked respect for the elderly and tricked me into going to his room. I panicked and ran out again. There was also a middle-aged uncle in the village, a lame man. We usually went to the river together to pick snails to sell. One time in the river, it seemed like he touched me. Why haven't these things affected me?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life

answers.answer_text: Sexuality is a natural instinct of human beings. So, it is normal for men to behave that way towards you. It is just a matter of character and moral cultivation. People with good character choose to leave you and keep their distance. People with good moral cultivation would not do such things. Only those with weak willpower cannot resist exposing their true nature. When those people treat you that way, it automatically triggers your self-protection awareness, which is also good for you and others. In life, it is unavoidable to encounter obstacles. Although you can avoid those people who treat you that way, there may be some people whom you cannot escape from, and they will treat you the same way. The reason why these things have not affected you is because you have not reached that stage that would affect you. If you haven't experienced it, don't fantasize about going through it and see if you can escape from it. You should know that the reason why doctors can cure various diseases is not because they have the ability to predict the future or have clairvoyance. It is because many people have suffered from certain diseases, and by treating those people, doctors have developed methods and experience. If the things you have experienced would affect you, then all the girls in the world would have psychological problems.

Hello ma'am, thank you for your recognition and invitation. When I read your description of the things you have experienced, I also feel that they may have more or less influenced your inner feelings in interpersonal interactions. It's a good thing that you say it hasn't affected you. I'm just curious, if it hasn't affected you, why would you think of and leave these things in a comment here?

question: How to overcome psychological trauma when precious metals are trapped and cut, and the market reverses three days later?
description: Making a deal on precious metals with colleagues, I suffered a huge loss of over ten thousand yuan by selling at a high price. I kept the loss a secret from my colleagues and family. Unexpectedly, the market reversed two days later, and I couldn't bear the shock. I didn't dare to disclose the truth to my colleagues or family and silently endured the regret. My focus at work has been affected, and I feel hopeless. How can I overcome this psychological shadow?
keywords: Emotions, depressive feelings, anxious feelings, guilt and shame.

answers.answer_text: If there were no reversal, and even the market became worse, you would definitely be glad about your wise decision. But now that there's a reversal, you are starting to feel uncomfortable. Have you realized it? These two situations do not make any economic difference to you, as the substantial loss of tens of thousands is a fact regardless of the reversal. Therefore, what makes you distressed is merely the difference in mindset. If there were no reversal, you would think, "Luckily I cut my losses, I am truly wise." If there is a reversal, you would think, "Why am I so foolish? I'm not suited for investing, I've never seen someone as foolish as you, couldn't you wait a little longer?" If only I had persevered, then... Can you see it? The reason you're in pain is that after making your decision, your inner self is filled with blame, regret, and self-doubt. These voices make you feel very uncomfortable. Of course, you feel distressed because you've lost money and also because you're being blamed! We often say that for things we cannot change, we must learn to accept and let go. Pain will inevitably exist for a period of time, but if possible, please stop criticizing and blaming yourself, try to see the successful investment experiences you've had in the past, try to see that even though you've lost tens of thousands, you've made profits in the past, so on balance, the loss doesn't seem significant. And this relatively small loss has allowed you to gain valuable investment experience again. Without such an experience, perhaps the next time you cut losses, the loss would be more than tens of thousands. Return to your original intention, why do you want to make money? To be happy, to create a better life. But it seems that you're not happy now, just because of one failed attempt at making money, you've made yourself like this. What happened to creating a better life? Think about it, while money is important, without money, if you also lose your health, wouldn't the loss be even greater? Aren't you more important than money?

The market is merciless, and I sympathize with the sufferings of the original poster. I have made the same mistake before, but I confessed in the end and received forgiveness from my family. I hope the original poster will quickly regain their spirits. [Mental setback - Making the same mistake twice and feeling regretful] ① Contrary trend: Investing in the market is to make money, but when the market trend goes against expectations, it leads to a psychological discrepancy. ② Cutting losses - Bearing the burden alone: The market situation makes the original poster feel that their investment is a wrong decision, so they want to correct it by cutting losses. ③ Feeling regretful: After the original poster cuts losses, the market starts to reverse, making them realize that cutting losses was a mistake and causing them to feel regret while suffering significant losses. [Unsolvable problem - Caught between a rock and a hard place] In the situation of making the same mistake twice and feeling regret, the original poster also faces the challenge of bearing substantial losses and solving the problem. ① Going forward - Facing the problem directly: Being honest with family members and colleagues would prove that their actions were wrong, which is embarrassing and may lead to ridicule from others, while also potentially affecting the happiness of their family and marriage. ② Retreating - Keeping it hidden: Based on the current reactions, the original poster's choice is to not be able to focus on work, feeling discouraged, which is obviously a great psychological test. In the middle of going forward or retreating, the original poster continues to invest in precious metals to recover the losses, but this single-minded approach will likely lead to even greater mistakes and severely impact the family. [Problem-solving methods are the best medicine] In the process of our personal growth, we usually develop in a linear manner, encountering problems, solving them, and then continuing to grow. However, when faced with unsolvable problems, we often resort to indirect and circuitous ways to solve them. From the current situation, if the losses do not have a significant impact on the family, being honest with family members is the least damaging way to the family and allows the original poster to avoid significant psychological pressure. However, if the losses are of a significant amount to the family and are unacceptable to loved ones, especially the spouse, it could also affect the marriage. I advise the original poster to use caution.

Dear Friend: Good afternoon! It seems like you have just experienced a "roller coaster of life." The stock market is indeed a very exciting place, and I have seen it too. Hmm, you have lost money, which is definitely a cause of anxiety for you. Several hundred thousand is a significant amount for an average person. Dealing with such a big issue alone must make you feel very lonely. You are unable to focus on work now, so you must be brooding over this matter. I see your difficulties and pain. Let's analyze why this happened. 1. The greater the loss, the greater the emotional fluctuations, as I mentioned earlier, the loss amount is not small, and it is normal for you to feel worried and anxious about it. 2. You dare not tell your family and friends because you are afraid they won't understand you and might even blame you for trying to take shortcuts. 3. You are unable to focus on work because you are still brooding over this matter and have lost confidence in the future and yourself. It's okay, let's solve this problem together. [Firstly], let go of shame. Perhaps this failure has made you feel embarrassed. Actually, we come to Earth to learn, to learn about love, to learn to support ourselves, and to learn many things. In this process, there will always be failures, and failure is not a punishment from God, but a way for us to continue striving to do better. Failure and mistakes are also part of our learning. You don't need to blame yourself. Everyone makes mistakes, we all have flaws, and we are all learning, you know? [Secondly], appreciate your past self. I believe you have had successful investments in the past, and you have done things very well and been successful. Look, this is something you can be proud of and praise yourself for. It is your efforts that have made all of this happen. Appreciate yourself! [Thirdly], implement proper risk management. Although I am not an investment expert, I know that stocks and funds come with risks. It is best to gather information and control risks before investing. You learn from experiences and mistakes, and this is more important than self-blame! [Fourthly], there will always be plenty of money in the world. Even though you have lost money, there is still an endless amount of money in this world, so you don't need to worry. If you fail, you can start over! [Fifthly], there are many things in life that bring you happiness and joy. Apart from money, there is also a healthy body, delicious food, fluttering butterflies, beautiful seasonal views, children's laughter, people's greetings, blooming flowers... these are all worth seeing and experiencing. Always look on the bright side. Best wishes! Your friend, Audrey.

A few hundred thousand yuan is not a small amount for many people, and I believe it must have been hard-earned for you, the original poster. In the precious metal trading, being trapped at a high position and cutting losses to exit the market can make hard-earned money disappear in an instant, casting a shadow over your head. From the description, I see several layers of problems. Firstly, the most expensive metal investment was done together with colleagues. This involves interpersonal relationships, and I don't know who was leading whom. In China, everyone has their own social circle, which can provide resources and information but can also intensify harm. Many people prefer to work with acquaintances. Success brings temporary happiness, but failure not only hurts financially but also impacts interpersonal relationships. If you and your colleagues all suffer losses, the feeling may be slightly better. However, if others have made profits while you have incurred losses, the comparison makes the blow not limited to money. Secondly, there is an economic loss because it's unclear where you obtained the few hundred thousand yuan from. If it was borrowed or secretly taken from home, as well as the comparison between this sum of money and your income, and how much you value money, all of these will determine the extent of your pain. Thirdly, you sold at a high price to cut losses, but a few days later, the market reverses, leading to regret on top of heartache. Therefore, the stimulation is multi-layered, and the emotional reactions it generates are complex. In this distressing situation, your coping strategy is to silently bear the resentment and not express it. Perhaps it is because of your personality that you handle problems on your own, which reflects how difficult it is for you. Many people will give you direct advice, but I think if you don't understand the various emotions that arise when facing setbacks and your own ways of coping, all advice will be ineffective. What does this mean? It means that in order to solve your current situation, you need to shift your focus back to yourself and use objective inquiry, critical thinking, and decision-making to help yourself. Firstly, objectively inquire about the problem: multiple types of stimulation, economic losses, subtle changes in interpersonal relationships, and the resulting emotions are inevitable, and the intensity is not low. We will doubt ourselves, regret our past decisions, have difficulty concentrating, and even our sleep and physical health will be affected. The brain has been exposed to dangerous stimuli and needs a buffering time. This is a biological characteristic of human beings. From the pattern of experiencing stimulation, the brain needs time to brake and switch to a calm and safe state. Secondly, analyze the problem. Your problem is not just the pain and heartache from the financial loss, but more importantly, it may lead you to doubt your abilities and hate yourself, attacking your wrong decisions, and regretting the past. You are used to handling pressure and taking responsibility yourself, perhaps because past experiences have taught you that even if you speak up, it won't make a difference, or if you told others, they wouldn't be able to help and would only add to the chaos, or perhaps no one has ever told you that it's okay. Your attention is focused on this matter, and your brain seems to be using this way to make you remember this moment, and even wants to explain this matter through thinking and self-hatred. We call this condition "ruminative thinking". Thirdly, make decisions. When you can see the problem for yourself and give yourself space for acceptance and allowance, I don't know what decisions you will make. When Chinese people are in a prosperous situation, they often embrace the positive and proactive mindset of Confucianism, but in times of setbacks, they tend to lean towards the natural and Taoist way. Analyzing your current situation, you can learn from the Taoist philosophy instead of adopting active thinking and fighting back at this time. By using the opposite approach, you will achieve the opposite effect, just like when traditional Chinese medicine says that for wind-cold and wind-heat colds, you should not use the opposite medicine. The specific strategies are as follows: 1. Allow yourself to feel bad because no matter how much you struggle, the discomfort will persist for a period of time, usually around three months, and for some, it can be even longer. This is due to differences in resilience. Understand that this is temporary and not permanent. It does not mean you are foolish or stupid. It's just that this particular matter has gone wrong, so don't generalize it. 2. Reduce ruminative thinking. Mindfulness practices can help you. When your thoughts are racing, allow yourself to pause. 3. Spend a certain amount of time each day, such as an hour, deliberately thinking about the investment failure, but try to pause and bring yourself back to the present during other times. 4. Talk to someone you trust about this matter and make good use of resources. At the same time, if you can, try to find valuable life lessons from this painful experience. However, this is a difficult task, so don't force yourself. 5. Bottom-line thinking. Consider whether the worst-case scenario matches your thoughts and whether your brain is engaging in too much deduction, such as thinking that you are stupid. Also, can you bear the actual worst-case scenario? These are just my thoughts, but the most important thing is you. Because you know yourself best, you need to believe in yourself. Learning from failure is more important than blaming yourself continuously. This is more important and more useful than fantasizing about a miraculous recovery.

Hello, I can understand your feelings very well. It is indeed heartbreaking when, after selling at a loss, the market unexpectedly rebounds. The huge psychological gap can trigger various emotions such as anxiety and anger, which can complicate your life. I still remember when the Chinese stock market was booming, it kept rising and I thought I could make a big profit. But in the end, it plummeted and I lost a large portion of my capital. I had to sell at a loss, and it still saddens me when I think about it now. My friend, what I want to tell you is that investing is full of ups and downs. Even someone like Warren Buffett has had his share of failures. Behind the market's fluctuations, there are countless variables in addition to capital. So, don't be discouraged by one failure. Perhaps you haven't told your family because you don't want them to feel the same sadness, or maybe you fear their disappointment in you. However, it may be beneficial to confide in your family, such as your partner, at this time. They can help you alleviate your emotions, and it will be much easier than keeping it all to yourself. Lastly, I have two small suggestions for you. First, if you're not a full-time investor, don't use money that you need for daily expenses to invest. Use "extra money" that you have on hand. This way, even if you lose your capital, it won't greatly impact your life. Second, maintain a peaceful mindset. Life always has its ups and downs, and investing comes with risks. Don't become arrogant when you make a profit, and don't be overly worried when you experience losses. Only by maintaining a calm mindset can you steer through the dangerous reefs and safely navigate the ups and downs. I wish you great success in your next investment, and I hope my answer can be helpful to you. That's all.

Hello OP. Although you have been saying that you want to keep things to yourself and not tell your wife and family, wanting to bear the consequences alone and digest them on your own, I do not agree with this approach because hiding it cannot minimize the impact of this matter. Firstly, your emotions cannot be hidden. The loss of money has already happened, causing you to toss and turn and have difficulty sleeping. You may think that you have hidden it from your wife and that she is unaware of this matter.
