But she is your sleeping companion, and you have been together day and night for so long, so she actually sees everything you do. Women are very sensitive, and if you don't tell her about this matter, she will be anxious on her own and speculate with her own thoughts. What will she guess? Originally, it was just a matter of losing money, but under her wild guesses, if it becomes a speculation that affects family conflicts, wouldn't it be worse? Secondly, the change in your financial situation cannot be hidden. People who have lost money will find an instantaneous change in their consumption concept, especially if they have lost a large sum. Before, the whole family may have regular trips. But now, after experiencing losses, when your wife and children have travel plans, you will start to hesitate and consider, right? When you are out shopping and see something you want to buy, you used to not hesitate to buy it, but now, are you starting to have concerns? The most frightening thing is, if you hide the fact that you have lost money, and coincidentally, a family member asks to borrow money, your wife doesn't know and agrees on your behalf, then what will you do? The loss has already been made, and the matter of losing money has already happened. What you can do now is to minimize the subsequent impact of this matter. Hiding everything and allowing family members to guess randomly while you bear the responsibility alone, hurting your wallet and feeling sad and physically hurt, is actually not very wise. I feel that what is currently impacting you the most is not the matter of losing money itself, but the suppression, self-blame, and grievances that come with hiding this matter. So, I suggest you temporarily set aside the feeling of being the head of the family and speak up, tell your closest and most loved ones, and when you feel at ease, they will also feel at ease. In addition, the financial market is constantly changing, and investment and financial management require caution. Here's a joke: Ever since I got into the stock market, I've been queuing up on the rooftop every day. Regardless, I hope you can untie the knot in your heart, dissolve your troubles, and have a good night's sleep!

Friend, hello! Thank you for the invitation. I can tell that the recent event has had a significant impact on you, and you are unable to let go of it. You cannot get out of this influence in a short period of time. You came here hoping to find a way to quickly overcome this pain. This is itself a painful thing, not only the actual financial loss, but also inner torment. The loss of money is easy to understand, but what kind of impact does this loss bring? Will it bring you immense pressure? When we can see the effects behind the loss, we can better understand our pain. The purpose of understanding is acceptance. You said you hide it from your family and colleagues, what is behind this secrecy? What are you worried about? Not being able to let others know means you have endured a lot of invisible pressure, and this pressure itself will bring you pain. Secrets that no one knows can only be borne by ourselves, and in this situation, they will inevitably affect our work and life. This does not mean that something is wrong with you, but it simply shows that the burden you are currently carrying has exceeded your capacity. You need support. The fact that you are here shows that you have realized that you need help from others. You have started seeking resources just like you would in making investments. Your previous sacrifices were also your efforts to protect and manage your resources. In this process, there are always things that we cannot control. Gain and loss are not only related to ourselves but also to the larger environment. Often, accepting this uncertainty is difficult, but at the same time, we must remember that it is precisely this uncertainty that sometimes brings unexpected surprises. It is natural for us to be affected for a period of time, but eventually, we and our lives will return to tranquility. However, the reflection brought to us by this event can make us more calm and at ease when dealing with similar situations in the future. Wishing you a good world and with love, Psychologist Luo Qin.

Hello, giving you a warm hug. It's normal to feel distressed when investment is a loss. Investment comes with risks, so it's normal to experience losses. This failure should not be seen as a reflection of future failures. After experiencing a loss, the market may experience a significant reversal, which can be hard to accept psychologically. After all, it was our own money that we couldn't hold onto till the end. However, as the saying goes, "failure is the mother of success." This investment failure happened because of a lack of understanding of the market and its trends. Let's consider it a lesson and accumulate strength for future successful investments. While you may feel regret, dwelling on it won't change anything about the loss. Instead, let's focus on learning from this failure, studying investment techniques and knowledge, and preparing for the next investment. Lastly, here's a phrase to share: any money gained through shortcuts in investments will be taken back in another way, so there's no need for regrets. Keep going! Good luck!

question: Unable to integrate into college life, feeling a lack of belonging in college, what should I do?
description: I am a junior in college, but I still feel a lack of belonging here. Even small things that don't go well make me want to go home. I constantly long for home and feel that there is nothing at school worth staying for. I have a peculiar personality and it's hard for me to become attached to anything. I am quite independent and don't really care about anything, so I feel that my college years are meaningless and I just want to go home. However, I always feel like I can't fit into college life and my personality doesn't match well with my roommates. I am that kind of strange person who attracts a lot of attention when walking on the street - some people think I'm weird, while others think I'm cool. In short, I am different from many people, which leads to my loneliness. The dorm conditions are poor and my relationship with my roommates is average. Even the fact that I had good friends and relationships in the past doesn't make me feel attached. I always want to go home and can't integrate into college life. I'm seeking solutions.
keywords: Development, personality traits, work and study, student growth.

answers.answer_text: ~~Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I understand that the OP is facing a problem regarding how to establish a sense of belonging in college. For this, I have the following suggestions, hoping to help the OP~ Firstly, the OP can start by maintaining good academic performance in college, which is also our main goal in college~ Start by studying and getting in touch with the subjects that interest us, this can help us feel the "contribution" and the meaning that this place has for us. Secondly, establishing a sense of belonging in college requires interacting with others. We can try to open up our thoughts and ideas, learn to share our lives with others. On the other hand, it is important to enhance our tolerance and acceptance towards new things and new friends in college. We must maintain sufficient openness to accept things that we may not be familiar with or do not fully agree with, because we cannot always be in an environment that we completely endorse and are familiar with. Therefore, we need to maintain enough openness, in order to continually accept and adapt to new environments.

question: First love has arranged a blind date and rejected me. I can't face this situation, what should I do?
description: My first love has found a blind date partner and said that they are very compatible. I asked if they still have feelings for me, but they rejected me and told me to delete them from their rights. I am in great pain, should I bravely face it or delete them? Will it feel better if I delete them, or will it make me even more miserable?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, I can sense that you still have strong feelings for your first love and you are still holding onto those emotions, unable to let go of that relationship. From a perspective of psychological analysis, each of us has both masculine and feminine traits within us. If you are female, then you have masculine traits within you, known as animus, which is an archetype and the male image within the female collective unconscious. When we establish an intimate relationship, we project these traits onto our partners. For example, your inability to let go of your first love may not be because of the person themselves, but rather the traits of your inner animus that you see in them. You are attracted to the animus traits that belong to you. If you can understand this, you may come to realize that the person you love may not be the true objective version of themselves, but rather the version you have created in your own mind. Similarly, he also has a collective image of femininity within him, known as anima, which represents his inner feminine traits. He may be the objective embodiment of your inner animus, which is why you love him and cannot let go, but you may not be his anima, which is why he feels you are not suitable for him. If you can understand this part, you can then understand the deeper motivations for establishing and maintaining an intimate relationship, and that first love is often the first stage of projecting our inner animus and anima. It may be passionate, intense, and focused on external factors. However, as we grow, our anima or animus also evolves to the next stage and we have different needs towards the opposite sex. When that person no longer meets the needs of our next stage, the relationship may break apart. It seems that your boyfriend has entered the next stage of intimacy needs while you have not been able to separate yourself from the relationship. It would be helpful to seek psychological analysis and work with a therapist to deal with the pain of separation.

Hello there! I totally understand how you feel and I send you a virtual hug. It's tough to see your first love move on and ask you to delete him, especially when you still have feelings for him. Objectively speaking, he has the right to choose who he wants to be with. So, for you, it's important to face this reality and accept that you will be separated. Actually, if you can let go of the past and accept the current outcome, whether you delete him or not is not that important or crucial. Of course, considering the current situation, what may be more important for you is how to make yourself feel better. The key is to accept the reality. I would suggest you delete him because, as the saying goes, out of sight, out of mind. If you want to cut off contact, it's better to do it cleanly. It will avoid triggering any sentimental feelings when you come across his contact information in the future. If you find it hard to let go and feel sad, try thinking about how he managed to move on from you. You still have a bright future ahead of you. Best wishes!

Dear questioner, hello there~ It can indeed be quite painful when two people who were once in love suddenly choose to let go and hold another person's hand. Here's a warm hug for you. Was the fact that your first love has a blind date partner something that happened after you broke up, or did it lead to your breakup? The sequence of events is quite important. If it happened after your breakup and he rejected your idea of getting back together, then it means that he is someone who takes relationships seriously. Since you have already separated, it's better to wish him well. If you can't adjust for a while, try to think of him as a passing moonlight, look up at it when you miss him, but please don't disturb it. If it's a missed opportunity, learn to let go if you can't salvage it. You will meet the person who will come to meet you next. If his having a blind date partner happened during your relationship and led to the breakup, it is recommended to make a clean break and cut off ties with him. No matter how much love or reluctance you have, don't linger in the past. After all, he was able to accept being arranged a blind date in a relationship, whether due to family pressure or other reasons, it at least shows one thing: love is not that important to him. He can choose a blind date partner between you and a suitable blind date partner, so if he meets someone more suitable in the future, would he make the same choice? It's not worth feeling sad and painful for such a person. It does take time to digest the end of a relationship, and it's okay to allow yourself some time to say goodbye, but don't take too long. Then tidy up your mood and get ready to welcome the right person. After all, the unique you deserves to be treated well, and before that person appears, remember to love yourself. Best wishes, the world and I love you~.

Hello, it's nice to have the opportunity to answer your question. First love is indeed a beautiful term. When you first experience love, you are naive and don't understand many things. What do you think is the true meaning of love? When love becomes a responsibility, it is no longer just the sweetness of being together, but also considering the families of both parties. It's not as easy as simply liking each other anymore. Many people break up because they are defeated by reality, such as differences in family conditions, parents' disapproval, long-distance relationships, etc. Sometimes, it's not that you don't want to be together, but that you don't love him that much. If he no longer loves you, there is really no need to force it, because it will ultimately have no result, and it will make you seem cheap. You have also made efforts for it, and his rejection is already very clear, so don't hesitate and don't contact him anymore. The pain you feel is only because you still like him, so you impose reasons on it. When you truly don't care anymore, you will ignore everything about him. Be a carefree girl! As for whether to delete or not, regardless of which option you choose, don't take the initiative to contact him, keep it, let him know how well you will live in the future, make yourself outstanding, and live a colorful life. If you delete him, choose to forget him, no longer contact him, and don't feel regretful. Some people, maybe you won't meet them again in your lifetime. But some people may be walking on the road waiting for you. You will gradually meet and finally love each other. I hope my answer is helpful to you, and I wish you all the best~.

Hello, questioner. After reading the entire passage, I didn't see anything about your emotions, only mentioning the pain. So, do you like your first love or not? Does this kind of liking still exist now? Firstly, I thought about some practical problems. Since it's your first love, why did you break up? Was the breakup due to more practical factors or more emotional factors? For example, you've been together for a long time, but the feelings haven't reached that stage, so you decided to break up. Or maybe there is a geographical distance, and neither of you can go to the other's place, or you couldn't get past the hurdle of parents, and so on. Since you have already broken up, if you decide to get back together, do you still need to face the same problems as before? Are there irreconcilable issues? Because I think since you've reached this step, it must be for the long run. If it cannot go on for the long term and is only for immediate happiness, similar pain is possible to fall into the same pit for the second time. Secondly, regarding the blind date with a girl, what is the real point that makes you sad? Is it possible that it's the feeling of "belonging to someone else"? What makes you sad is not the girl herself, but the feeling that what used to belong to you now belongs to someone else. I think this feeling needs a little more discernment. Another significant reason why there are few successful relationships that were formed during the first attempt at dating is that relationships themselves involve smoothing each other's edges and going through the process of being together. Once two people have blended together, if they want to separate, there will always be a sense of tearing. Could this feeling also be one of the causes of pain? Finally, since you have reached this point, I think you should analyze and summarize the experience and lessons learned from your previous relationship. Maybe there was a lack of emotional fulfillment, or maybe something was missing in real life. Or maybe both individuals were great, but they simply weren't compatible. Actually, think about it, with over 7 billion people in the world, it's really a miraculous thing to instantly encounter someone who is a perfect match. Personally, if you feel truly sad, first determine whether the source of your sadness is the girl or yourself. If it's because of the girl, you can try to fight for it, and if it doesn't work out, consider it as a valuable experience. Best wishes.

Hello, the author gives you a warm hug. First love is a beautiful thing, where two naive individuals delicately cherish each other and have wonderful aspirations for each other. However, often due to being inexperienced in relationships and not knowing how to communicate and meet each other's needs, the relationship ends with a goodbye. I'm not sure about your emotional state with your first love at that time, but this relationship and this person are still important to you, important to the point where you don't know how to face it. Don't worry or feel anxious, you will find your own way to handle this relationship and this person. They found a suitable match through arranged marriage and say they like the other person. But perhaps they are just suitable for marriage. They rejected you. Although it is heart-wrenching, we must face the reality that they no longer have feelings for us. Whether you are a man or a woman, and regardless of the reasons for giving up a relationship, there will always be some sense of guilt towards the other person. In order to alleviate their guilt, they may do things to make the other person "happy" or to make the other person "make a decision." For example, in your case, your first love said you have the right to delete their contact. But in reality, you don't need their permission to delete it; it's your own decision. They only said it to make themselves feel better. So don't overthink it; they have already moved on from your relationship. Therefore, you can keep their contact on WeChat or delete it, depending on your own heart. Regardless of the outcome, they have chosen to move forward, so why should we torture ourselves by staying in the same place? Treasure the beauty and pain of your first love in your memories and encourage yourself to move forward. Don't worry, don't be afraid, both the good and the bad will pass. Wishing you all the best!

question: Disliking people who study seriously, feeling as if they are trying to surpass me and become my enemies?
description: In high school, I developed anxiety and depression due to competing with my desk mate in studying. I also have a bit of OCD. Now in college, whenever I see someone in my class or roommate studying diligently, I start to dislike that person. I feel unhappy and miserable. It irritates me to see that person putting in so much effort. I feel like they are my enemy and want to defeat me, so I start hating that focused individual. In reality, they haven't done anything wrong, but I still feel uncomfortable. I feel like I have a dark side, but I can't escape from it. As a result, I avoid making friends with others. I want to change my mindset, but I really struggle with it. Please help me, thank you!

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Give you a big hug. "I feel that people who work hard are my enemies, and I have a sense of being defeated, so I refuse to make friends." I can understand OP's feelings because I have also had similar thoughts. When I see others working hard, I feel a bit discouraged and feel that I will be surpassed and become a "loser." But after reading what Adler said, I gradually learned to let go. Adler said, "If you want to live in harmony, you must treat others as equals." The reason why we feel that hardworking people are our enemies is that we always consider interpersonal relationships from a competitive perspective and see other people's success as "my failure," so we cannot be happy for others' achievements, and it is difficult to be friends with them. However, once we break free from the "competition" cycle, we can free ourselves from the competitive psychology of "maybe losing," view others as equals, and not be led by competition. As the master of the emotion of "competition," you can definitely do it! Focus on yourself. I understand that the "comparison system" in society makes us constantly feel "compared," always wanting to be a better person. The first thing to affirm is that OP has a competitive spirit because they are motivated, which is a very admirable quality. I know it's difficult to live without comparisons, but think about it, what we really want is to "be better than our past selves." You can compare, but compare yourself. If you have made progress compared to yesterday, then you are one step closer to success! Don't focus too much on other people's actions and neglect your true inner desires and aspirations. I hope my answer can help you. Live a happy life!

Dear OP, hello~ Jealousy towards those who work harder than oneself is not uncommon, just more or less severe. Appropriate jealousy can be a driving force for competition, but once it exceeds that limit, it can turn into malicious intent towards the person we envy, or even self-harm. Decreasing attention on that person: Once we start paying extra attention to someone, we magnify their behaviors. For example, if we see them in the study room, we may think they spend the whole day studying there; if we see them carrying a backpack on the street, we may think they are secretly studying, and so on. In reality, they may just be passing by the study room or carrying a backpack for other reasons. But when we decrease our attention on them, perhaps these actions won't cause as much resentment in our eyes. Psychological adjustment: If you feel uncomfortable when classmates and roommates in your class are studying more diligently, what about senior students who are preparing for postgraduate entrance exams? They may be even more serious than them. Consider them as the same as senior students; their dedication doesn't hold any special meaning for you. Distance yourself from that person: If you can't achieve psychological adjustment, then distance yourself from that person. If they are in study room 1, go to study room 2; if they sit in the front to listen to lectures, sit in the back. Think more about what you want. Do you want to be the person who works the hardest? The person who is most serious about studying? Or the person who performs the best in their studies? In college, there are many people who only appear diligent. They go to the classroom before dawn with a backpack but end up feeling sleepy. Some people take neat and beautiful notes, but remember very little. When competing with others in terms of effort becomes an arms race, you will become exhausted. In addition to busy studying, think about your reasons for doing so. When you have a clear answer in your mind, you naturally reduce your focus on external factors. Life is not just about studying. Our lives are not solely about studying; there are many wonderful things. But learning can be found everywhere in life. Going on a trip with friends is learning social skills, going for a run is learning fitness, even watching dramas is learning how to relax. If we confine learning only to sitting at a desk and studying in the study room, then learning loses its true meaning. Finally, I hope that you, as the OP, can overcome these troubles soon!

When I saw your question, I was reminded of the friend I lost due to jealousy. My friend was better academically, had a better social life, and everything in her life seemed well-organized. I was really jealous of her. I didn't admit it at the time, but now I dare to face these feelings because I realize that admitting our darkness is not shameful. Just like you, acknowledging your darkness actually shows that you are an honest person. Back then, I really saw her as my rival and thought that I would win if I surpassed her. I also did many things that I now regret as they were too petty and childish. Ultimately, I pushed my friend away to a point where she no longer wanted to tolerate me. Now I can be honest about all of this because I have my own job and a broader perspective. I have met more talented people and realized that my circle was too small and my vision too narrow. So, I would unconsciously compare myself to her, but when you elevate yourself and look around, there are many others who are even more outstanding than her. Do I have to compare myself to each and every one of them? Ah, that would be really exhausting. Moreover, if I consider the whole world as my rival, then I am standing on the opposite side of the world and end up isolated and alone. The change in my mindset began when I gave up comparing myself to others and started seeing them as teachers. How does this friend manage to be so likable with a smiling face every day? How can my colleague handle so many tasks efficiently without making any mistakes? And how can that sister have a happy family and cute children, while I am still solo? I started learning from them, praising their strengths, asking them how they achieve what they do, and reflecting on what I can learn from them. When we see others as teachers and role models, we won't feel envy or make comparisons, and our mindset will become more open. Others will also be willing to be friends with us. Also, don't feel guilty just because of your dark thoughts. Everyone has their own dark side because we are all ordinary people.

Hello, the person who posted the question, nice to meet you. Let's talk about Lan Yingying, who has recently been criticized severely. What is your opinion on this matter? In my opinion, Lan Yingying is a very hardworking, dedicated, and outstanding person. "Whenever he says I can't do it, I will ignite my fighting spirit," as Lan Yingying said. Indeed, in the show "Youth With You," Lan Yingying may not have been the hardest working contestant, but her efforts have been talked about the most. So, many people criticized her for being "overly competitive" and "overly focused on marketing." Overall, there are many people who dislike her. However, was Lan Yingying's effort fake? No, it wasn't. Before this, she was a very disciplined person who exercised and read regularly. So why did Lan Yingying, who ranked first on the stage and received high praise, receive more criticism later on? The reasons can be boiled down to two points. Firstly, compared to other contestants, Lan Yingying has slightly lower emotional intelligence. But this is not the main reason and at most is just a minor factor. The main reason is the second point. Lan Yingying doesn't fit the current trend. Why did NetEase Cloud Music get turned into "Depressing Cloud Music"? Why do people admire the "Buddha-like Youth"? Ultimately, it's because this kind of "depressed" state has gained everyone's recognition. However, Lan Yingying is not this kind of person. She is ambitious, proactive, and highly goal-oriented. This kind of attitude does not match the aesthetics of the majority nowadays. So I say, as a celebrity, I admire and like Lan Yingying a lot. But if she were my friend, I would definitely hate her. She is too ambitious and too hardworking, which gives me an overly intense sense of crisis. Now let's get back to the topic you raised. The hardworking people you mentioned are very similar to Lan Yingying. And you said you are jealous of those hardworking people. In fact, the root cause is because they make you feel threatened, and as a result, you have complex emotions of jealousy and fear. So how can you resolve this dilemma? Firstly, learn to transform. Others are just temporary enemies, while you are your own biggest opponent. Convert the emotions towards others into self-reflection. There is no need to compare yourself to others. As long as you make progress compared to yesterday, then you are successful. Both emotions and goals should be learned to be transformed. You can review your progress or regression every day and compare yourself to your past self. If you constantly see others as enemies, when you surpass them, you may also lose your motivation. Secondly, learn to make friends, but make friends with hardworking people. Since you feel unhappy when they study, then go and study with them. When you experience the motivation that comes from studying together, the feeling of jealousy will gradually diminish or turn into a determination to not be outdone. Studying together with a few people is more joyful than envying others. If you make friends with a group of lazy people who don't know how to study, and you keep idling with them, but your competitiveness makes you envy those who are striving to learn, then you are really in a predicament. In fact, jealousy is a common human emotion, but your jealousy won't be ridiculed by others only when your abilities become strong enough to match those you envy. If you don't work hard and only envy others, you will always remain stuck and frustrated in your current situation.

Hello, I'm glad that you have recognized that your emotions are negative and are actively working to improve them. Way to go! So, how can you overcome these emotions? Start by reflecting on the meaning of life, the kind of person you want to be, and how you can achieve your goals. For example, if you don't want to be a jealous person, be vigilant when jealousy arises. Think about what success and happiness mean to you. When you see someone who is diligent in their studies but not happy, can we say that this reveals your approval of academic achievements as the definition of success? While academic achievements are important, we should strive for holistic development. As we enter university, we should gradually transition from a student mindset and become our own mentors, rather than simply playing the role of a "student." I believe that for a person to be happy, they need to be physically and mentally healthy, possess ideals, and have good conduct. Your jealousy towards people who work hard actually suggests that you also have aspirations. Being able to recognize your shortcomings and actively correct them indicates that you can also become a mentally and physically healthy individual. Set short, medium, and long-term goals for yourself. Connect your short and medium-term goals with your long-term goals so that you can focus your energy on self-improvement, reducing your focus on others. Furthermore, as you make progress and become a better person, your jealousy will diminish. Take time to recognize your own strengths and make a balanced evaluation of yourself and others. Sometimes, we admire others because we overlook our own strengths or ignore the difficulties others are facing. In high school, I used to envy a girl who was attractive, had nice handwriting, and was academically successful. However, after getting to know her, I discovered that she didn't feel happy due to her family background. It made me realize that the person I admired also had her own difficulties and desires. Our suffering often stems from the difficulty of reconciling our desires with reality, doesn't it? So, daily, write down three things that bring you happiness or that you have done something good. For example, "I noticed that I was jealous, but I made an effort to adjust myself" or "I have a bad temper, but I didn't get angry today" or "I helped someone and felt really happy." Practice calligraphy, devote time to reading to expand your knowledge and broaden your horizons, and reflect on your childhood. Why did you develop a competitive spirit? Why do you care about this aspect? Reflect on which characteristics match your own. Do you dislike studious people because, when you were young, your parents often used phrases like "Look at other people"? Or is it because you see others studying hard and envy their strong determination? Set an idol for yourself. For example, someone as great as Premier Zhou Enlai. Since you want to "compete," why not compete for a more ambitious goal? Transform your negative emotions into positive actions. Your competitiveness in academics is a breath of fresh air in the competitive world. Competition leads to progress, so make good use of your competitive spirit to make yourself more determined. But don't put too much pressure on yourself. You are now a college student, a time of youth and vitality. I wish you can overcome your negative emotions, seize opportunities, and propel yourself to a better future. If you want to chat about anything, feel free to send me a private message.

【Other people's success will not hinder one's own success】 Dear friend: Hello! You seem conflicted and confused, as if you have entered a dead end and don't know how to get out. It seems that you are trapped in a mindset of comparison and competition, without knowing how to resolve it. Well, many people have had similar experiences and struggles, so let's take a look together. Why is competition necessary? Actually, I didn't understand it before either. It seems like everyone is no longer friends and has become enemies. Later on, I observed that there is a big reason behind it, and it stems from a mistaken belief. 1. "Other people's success will hinder my own success." Many people hold onto the belief that competition is necessary, that it's either you die or I die, simply because they mistakenly think that others will hinder their success. But in reality, this is just a false belief. 2. Haven't found one's own position and value. It's because they don't know who they are, what their coordinates are on Earth, and what kind of person they want to become, like a lost soul wandering on this earth. It's difficult for people to see who they really are, so they mistake "comparison and competition" as the only way to see themselves. But in fact, there are many ways to "see oneself." 3. Lacking confidence or satisfaction in one's own success. People dislike not the external world, but rather the masks they wear. Or to put it differently, you appreciate your classmates' excellence because you yourself are excellent; you appreciate your classmates' hard work in studying because you yourself work hard in studying. If you dislike your classmates' efforts, well... you get what I mean. Regardless of the reasons, let's not blame ourselves first. The most important thing is to find solutions, right? 【Firstly】, realize one's own position and unique value. Everyone has their own place in life, even identical twins have different lives. The older twin cannot replace the younger twin, and the younger twin cannot replace the older twin; your classmates cannot replace you, and you cannot replace your classmates. This is the nature of each person's life position, and it is also their unique and irreplaceable place. This forms each person's unique value. 【Secondly】, establish horizontal relationships and see that "everyone is just different." The reason why people want to be the "best" and are obsessed with a sense of superiority is because they are afraid that one day they will be at a lower position, losing their sense of value and self-confidence. In order to be the "best," they fall into the trap of "competition" to maintain their "sense of superiority." If we let go of this vertical relationship and instead establish horizontal relationships, you will find that everyone is striving in their own position without judgment of higher or lower. It's just that positions, responsibilities, talents, and tasks differ. 【Thirdly】, understand one's own needs and develop an understanding of others' needs. You desire to achieve success, and your classmates do too. You desire the joy of success, and your classmates do too. When you long to stand on the stage and receive applause and praise, your classmates also long for the same. We are all human beings, and our needs sometimes overlap! You can understand yourself, and you can understand others too. 【Fourthly】, trust others. Sometimes competition and the fear of having one's possessions taken away stems from a lack of security. It's because of this lack of security that the belief "other people's success will hinder my own success" arises. It is a defensive mindset in the subconscious. Only when you see security in interpersonal relationships can you let go of this mistaken belief. Or perhaps, you can dismantle this belief first, which will also provide you with a sense of security. "Other people's success will not hinder my own success." You are not a bad person; you simply planted a false belief which led to some negative behaviors. You don't need to blame yourself so much, and you don't need to worry excessively. Just remember, you and others are like different snowflakes in the world, there is no higher or lower, just differences.️ Quoting a line from my favorite movie: "Be kind, because everyone's life is not easy." Your academic achievements do not come easy, and neither does your classmates'. God bless you! Your friend, Audrey.

Hello, I understand your feelings well. When I see others working hard, I also feel restless and sometimes anxious that I can't focus on studying. First, try to calm your mind and engage in simple communication with them about studying. After the exchange, you will feel different. Don't rush, gradually get to know them. They are not as scary as you imagine. Being with more outstanding people can make you become better too. Because everyone has different experiences, hobbies, and ambitions, you will gain more things, more knowledge, and become a better version of yourself. Don't let them surpass you. Only by constantly surpassing yourself in life can you avoid being surpassed by others. Walking alone may be a bit slow, but if we walk together, we can go much further and take care of each other along the way. So try to accept and interact with them. Perhaps you will become good friends! I hope my answer can help you. I wish you the strength to break through the wall in your mind soon. You can do it!

Sweetie, from your question, I can see your distress and agony. In fact, you don't really want to hate or be at odds with others, you actually want to get along well with them, right? This distress doesn't just come from your relationship with others, but also a bit from your "disgust" with yourself. ["Competition with 'excellence'"] The competition with excellent classmates actually stems from your pursuit of "excellence" as well. When you see diligent students, you also hope to be like them, so you want to "surpass" them. ["Disgust for 'excellence'"] Some of the disgust for "excellence" also comes from your own "disgust." You disdain the fact that you are not as excellent as them, and you despise the fact that you can't compete with them. This part needs to be "acknowledged." The "awkwardness," "darkness," "disgust," and "rejection" that you see in this part actually come from yourself. ["How to change?"] You really want to change these thoughts. The most important thing is to accept yourself, accept your helplessness, accept that you may not be as good as others, and accept that you don't necessarily have to be better than others. So, accepting all of yourself is crucial. Regardless of how you are, you need to accept yourself. If you can accept yourself, perhaps those "unhappiness" and "pain" will automatically disappear. Wishing you can free yourself from this little demon, the world and I love you, and you should love yourself too!

Hello, when I read your description, the first thing I feel is that you may be a high-achieving classmate who has high expectations of me. Because when you see classmates or roommates who study seriously, you tend to dislike them. However, this "dislike" may not be a true dislike, but rather a worry. You worry that your grades won't be as good as theirs. I think if they invite you to study together at this time, and you work hard together, you may have a different feeling. Besides, you may be very concerned about your own grades and the level of effort you put in, but when your classmates' efforts are beyond your control, it may make you feel a bit insecure. Try to gradually become aware of yourself. When you feel angry seeing classmates working hard, see what you can do or how you can make an effort so that you don't have such emotions. "I feel very dark about myself." We don't need to feel dark or ashamed because we have such emotions. After all, everyone wants to be the best. What do you think?

Hello, Lou Lou. Forcing yourself to change your inner thoughts is like covering your ears while stealing a bell because at this stage, forcing your mind is equivalent to not accepting yourself. I have a small suggestion, I don't know if it's appropriate. First, you need to accept yourself as you are now. You have to believe that you are normal, and these dark thoughts in your mind have not led you to do anything bad. Don't be overly self-critical. Who requires us to be morally pure while being legally upright? No one! People live in society with all kinds of emotions, desires, and distractions. These are all normal. Not just you, everyone has their own dark side to some extent. For example, right now, as I answer questions on this platform, if I receive fewer likes than others, I also feel uncomfortable. I may even check what the popular answers look like. But I don't think I'm doing anything wrong. You are too harsh on yourself. You need to recognize who you are at this stage and make peace with yourself. You don't need a moral guardian to supervise yourself. It's too exhausting. Secondly, broaden your perspective and look at a larger and wider picture. There are so many outstanding people in the world, and each person chooses a different path. If you are firm in your own direction, you won't compare yourself to people on different paths. For example, if you don't play badminton, you won't envy Lin Dan; if you don't play basketball, you won't envy Yao Ming. I can't remember which book said it, but the best way to eliminate weeds on a piece of grassland is not to keep pulling them out, but to plant crops on it. When you gradually reconcile with yourself and see a bountiful harvest on your own grassland, running on your own path, you will laugh at the old you who used to envy such things in your heart. The small demons of the past will no longer be a problem.

question: Alone and clueless, not understanding anything, what is the meaning of life?
description: Others are vibrant and full of flavor, look at myself, all alone, knowing and understanding nothing, and struggling to learn. It feels like no matter what I ask, everyone else can handle it, why can't I? What is the meaning of life? Is it to highlight the goodness of others?
keywords: Growth, work, learning, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: There are two possibilities when we see others as "energetic and vibrant." First, in different relationships, we naturally put on corresponding masks. For example, the mask and behavior of a teacher would be different from that of a lover. We show different aspects and parts to those we trust intimately and to acquaintances. Second, it could be because we have made an assumption or judgment about others and are using a magnifying glass to search for the "energetic and vibrant" parts in them. As unique individuals, we never need to compare ourselves to others. We just need to be ourselves: understanding what kind of seed we are, what resources we need, and what we will grow into. I don't believe in the idea that "everyone else can, but I can't." For example, many people cannot ask for help like you did here. Perhaps we can be more tolerant of ourselves, take a positive outlook, and give ourselves small affirmations every day. I hope this helps. Take care.

question: Once something goes wrong, it is common to attribute the reasons to oneself.
description: Once something goes wrong and doesn't go as planned, I always tend to blame myself. It's really exhausting, and I don't know what to do.
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-growth

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. The main problem you face is that when something goes wrong, you tend to attribute it to yourself. To a certain extent, you are accustomed to blaming yourself for failures, which can lead to the exhaustion you mentioned. However, if we extend this further, we can see that it is also the beginning of self-improvement. Often, it is through recognizing our shortcomings that we strive to improve. For example, the mock exams we experience from childhood serve this purpose. If we score low in math and high in language, excluding random factors, it means we need to invest more time and effort in studying math. The same applies to how we approach tasks. It is precisely because you are good at introspection that you continue to make efforts to improve yourself. When faced with failure, some people tend to attribute it to luck, difficulty, and other objective factors, while others, like you, tend to blame their own abilities and shortcomings, among other subjective factors. As a basic human instinct, people are prone to attribute success to their own abilities and failure to luck, among other things. The reason why you, as a person with such good qualities, still feel exhausted is because you rarely attribute successful outcomes to yourself. American psychologist Bernard Weiner believes that people's analysis of the causes of success or failure can be summarized into six factors: 1) ability, whether one's abilities are sufficient for the task at hand; 2) effort, whether one has put in the necessary effort in the process; 3) task difficulty, judging the level of difficulty based on one's own experience; 4) luck, considering whether luck played a role in success or failure; 5) physical and mental conditions, the impact of one's physical or psychological state on the outcome; 6) other factors, such as the influence of other people or circumstances during the process (e.g., others' help or unfair grading). There are many factors that can influence the success or failure of a task. OP, you can try analyzing the reasons for success or failure from these six perspectives. In doing so, you will gradually realize that the outcome of a task is not determined solely by one-sided factors. This will provide you with an objective and clear understanding of the nature of the task, allowing you to find confidence and overcome the feeling of exhaustion. Finally, I wish you confidence, optimism, and a smooth life.

OP, hello. Learn to objectively and rationally look at failure, considering both external and internal factors. Choose whichever perspective allows you to feel relaxed and positive. When facing our own failures, we tend to use two cognitive approaches: external attribution and internal attribution. External attribution means attributing failure to unstable and uncontrollable external factors, while internal attribution is the opposite. For example, if Xiao Ming and Xiao Li did poorly on a test, Xiao Ming might blame himself for not studying well and not carefully reading the questions, feeling guilty and unhappy, and anxious about future exams. On the other hand, Xiao Li might think that the test questions were too difficult and it was raining heavily on the day of the exam, which made her uncomfortable with wet shoes and affected her performance. Xiao Li believes that as long as she studies hard and checks the weather forecast in advance next time, she will definitely make progress. Thus, she hopes to start working hard now and prove herself in the next exam. When facing setbacks, you may tend to use internal attribution excessively, which puts a lot of pressure on yourself and makes you fear failure and feel lost. Try to be more objective when facing such situations, understanding both internal and external factors, and seeking solutions instead of constantly blaming yourself and thinking of yourself as a failure. When you can't affirm or support yourself, you can confide in close people, seeking comfort and strength from them, so that you can face failure and muster the courage to start again. Best wishes.

question: Married for 8 years, with a second child who just turned 1 year old, my husband gets angry and throws things, and it's getting increasingly worse.
description: Living together for three years, married for eight years, and now the second child has just turned one year old. My husband gets angry and throws things, and it's getting worse. There have been two instances of him throwing things this year. At the time, I closed the bedroom door and went back to my room, and he went to work after throwing things outside. He is busy with work, working overtime every day, cooking in the morning before going to work, and doing laundry and tidying up the kitchen when he comes home from work. The situation has become more serious than when we only had one child, and I don't know if it can be saved.
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, prenatal and postnatal.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! Your husband is getting angrier and throwing things, and it's getting worse. This is causing you some worries, and I think your concerns are valid. Moreover, if your husband's condition continues without effective resolution, it will inevitably be harmful to him and your family. Analysis of the reasons: Your husband is under a lot of pressure due to a busy work schedule and having to do a lot of household chores when he comes home. Psychology suggests that when stress events exceed an individual's coping abilities, it can easily lead to an anxious state. From a physiological perspective, stress is the degree of exhaustion and torment the body undergoes. Therefore, based on your husband's current condition, it is likely due to excessive stress that he can't effectively alleviate or relieve, resulting in a series of emotional and behavioral reactions when his psychological, physiological, emotional, and mental well-being feel threatened. So, how do we deal with the current situation regarding your husband? 1. Create a pleasant family atmosphere: We often say that home is a warm harbor, but many families never experience the warmth this harbor brings to its members. To create this warm harbor, it requires both the responsibility and mutual understanding and tolerance of both spouses, as well as effective communication. Currently, both you and your spouse are experiencing significant stress, and your husband may not be aware of this problem yet. You are able to recognize the issue, which shows your clarity on the matter. Therefore, I think improving your current situation should start with you, even though it's challenging for you to manage the two children on your own. There always has to be a beginning. As the saying goes, “The hardest part is getting started.” So, how do you create a pleasant family atmosphere? In my opinion, first, you need to avoid blame and criticism and listen attentively and patiently to your husband's innermost thoughts and feelings. Only by understanding his inner world can you effectively communicate with him, further promoting mutual understanding and empathy. 2. Take on the burden of life actively: I understand that taking care of two children is very challenging, and you also hope to get help. However, in the current situation, if neither side sacrifices their ego, you won't be able to overcome the current difficulties. Therefore, one party must make continuous improvements to drive the other party's improvement, ultimately leading to improvement on both sides and overcoming the difficulties together. You may feel aggrieved, wondering why you have to change and improve rather than your partner. From my perspective, it doesn't matter who changes first from both sides; however, the issue is that your husband isn't aware of the problem yet. Thus, starting with you in initiating improvement and change would be more beneficial to easing and resolving the problem. 3. Step out of the house and experience the outside world together: Psychology suggests that if you have shared experiences or secrets, it strengthens the relationship and intensifies the level of intimacy. By going on outings as a family, shopping at the mall, and dining out at restaurants, you can enhance the intimacy between family members, relieve the tension among them, and soothe everyone's emotional well-being. Therefore, no matter how difficult your current situation is, make a determined effort to step out of the house and organize frequent family outings. This will be more conducive to easing and resolving the problem.

Husband throwing things, you must be a little scared, let me hug you. After reading the whole topic, my feeling is that your husband is very good to you and responsible for the family, and you also rely on him quite a bit. The topic says that your husband's anger and throwing things have been getting worse. He has thrown things twice this year. That means, in serious situations, it's been more than half a year, with an average of throwing things every three months or so. So before the situation got serious, he either didn't throw things or only did it once a year or so. Also, he works overtime every day, makes breakfast in the morning, comes back and does the laundry and cleans the kitchen. I don't know if you live alone or if there are elderly people to help? There's also a second child who is now one year old, which means your husband's change happened after the arrival of the second child. Let's analyze the reasons for your husband's change. In terms of environment, there hasn't been any physical changes, but in terms of human environment, there's a new child, and in terms of psychological environment, the pressure of raising a child, time pressure, household chores pressure, and energy pressure are all changing. I guess your communication between each other has also decreased. With so many changes happening, I think your husband's change is normal from a rational perspective. We also have two children in our family, and our second child is now two and a half years old. My body has not been the same since giving birth to the second child. Occasionally, I also throw things, but in our family, it's me who throws things. I usually do it when I'm too tired and feeling very annoyed, wanting some peace and quiet, but the conditions don't allow for it, and at the same time, my husband and children keep demanding things from me. In that moment, I feel that they don't love me, don't understand me. I have tried my best to control myself before throwing things, but sometimes I can't, and I feel very uncomfortable. If I don't vent a little, I will collapse. When I throw things, I especially hope that someone can understand my hardships, even if they don't understand me, they can at least take care of my feelings. Of course, I know the child is still young and needs care, and my husband is very tired and needs rest, but what about me? Am I not working hard? It's okay to work hard for the people you love, but when no one understands, no one cares, that's something I can't accept. But what I mentioned above is about myself, I think men may care more about their pride, he may not say that he needs to be taken care of, but from the topic, it seems that he doesn't have much time to rest either. Being so tired, if he can't rest, he at least needs understanding, affirmation, and comfort. The least lovable moment for a person is when they need help the most. That's the situation your husband is in now. He can't express it in words, but he's using his actions to say that he can't bear it anymore. Let me give you some suggestions. First, if possible, you can find a professional psychological counseling center and do some family therapy. Second, if he throws things, make sure the children are safe, and show him more care, don't isolate him or blame him out of fear. Third, if you're not too busy, try to share some household chores, if you are also tired, you can regularly hire a housekeeper to help clean. Fourth, the husband-wife relationship is the center of a family, spend some time every day talking with your husband about things unrelated to the children, reminisce about the past, don't let your feelings cool down because of the arrival of the child. Life is not easy, and it's even more so for families with two children, so cooperation between the two people needs to be closer. Look at the angelic child, think about the beautiful past, the current days are just a phase. I hope my answer can help you.

Hug the topic owner~ It's indeed not good for your husband to throw things. Not only does it cause financial loss to the family, but more importantly, the loud noise can frighten you and also scare the children. It's possible that your husband is under a lot of pressure, after all, he has to work and take care of household chores, and having two children increases the pressure on him even more. We also need to understand his negative emotions. However, the habit of throwing things needs to be changed. My suggestion is: [Find a time to have a good chat with your husband] When your husband's mood calms down, you can have a good talk with him. You can start by asking if he has encountered any difficulties at work recently. If he needs to vent, you can be his listener. After your husband vents, you can ask him what you can do for him or if there's anything you can share the burden with. For example, if you feel too exhausted with household chores, you can help him or hire a cleaning service regularly. You also need to talk to your husband about how throwing things is really not good because it not only scares the children, but they may also pick up the habit. We still need to set a good example. [Allocate some of your energy to your husband] I know you must be very tired taking care of two children, but if possible, allocate some of your energy to your husband and take care of his emotions. For example, during the weekends, take your husband and children for a picnic in the countryside or engage in some leisure activities to relax everyone's mood. After putting the children to sleep at night, have a chat with your husband and ask about his work and his mood, share interesting things together. Family members need to grow together, and your husband may not have fully adapted to the situation of having a family of four, but the stress arrived earlier than his adaptation process. The topic owner is the same, you must also feel very tired taking care of the children. You can chat more with your husband, vent your feelings to each other, support each other, get through this adjustment period, and believe that the future will be better~.

Hello~ First, let me give you a warm hug. I can imagine that the situation must be tough for you, but don't worry, let's analyze it together in detail. I hope these words can bring you some help. First, let's try to find possible reasons. It seems that you and your husband have been through a long journey together and have experienced a lot. It must not have been easy all the way, and now you may be facing a tricky problem. You may want to think about whether your husband is under a lot of pressure or has encountered some issues. Hello, I hope my response can help you. After being married for 8 years, it can be said that the honeymoon phase between the two of you has long passed. The relationship between the two of you has become more about familiarity. When two people are familiar enough with each other, we tend to expose our negative sides. Take a moment to reflect on how your communication with your husband has been. Has the emotional communication between the two of you been neglected due to you taking care of the family and children while he is busy with work? If the feelings between two people are ignored for a long time, there will be a sense of emptiness inside because both of you hope to be understood by each other. Not feeling understood for a long time leads to not feeling valued or cared for, and the accumulation of dissatisfaction, anger, resentment, and sadness. At this time, he may choose an extreme way to vent his emotions, such as throwing things. On the other hand, he may also be experiencing a lot of work pressure and financial stress, and when negative emotions become overwhelming and he doesn't know how to express them properly, his behavior, like your husband's, may occur. It's crucial not to overlook each other's feelings due to being too familiar or being too busy with your own matters. Emotional fulfillment is essential.

Throwing things is a form of release, mainly due to emotional distress that has been lingering and unable to be relieved, trapped in the heart. In cases like this, the first step is to find the reason behind the outburst. Is it because work is not going well, or is it due to increased stress from the pandemic, making it difficult to adjust after returning home? Or perhaps it is the result of having children, with the added pressure at home causing an overwhelming feeling that cannot be suppressed. Generally speaking, throwing things and getting angry are the result of accumulated and unresolved emotions, combined with poor rest and sleep, which cause a loss of control over emotions. This is something that can be adjusted and remedied. You can start by communicating and sitting down to have a good talk about what is going on. Seeking help from professionals, such as a psychological counselor, for emotional guidance is also an option, allowing the emotions to be released and alleviated. Sometimes, holding emotions inside for too long is not a solution, and it may be necessary to let them out in order to feel better.

How do you feel right now when talking about this?
