question: I never proactively contact people, and now I don't even contact my parents. Why is that?
description: I don't know why, but I've always been introverted and have trouble communicating since I was little, hiding in the corners. After starting to work, I don't contact anyone and don't want anyone to know me. I just want to live a quiet life alone. I don't even want to contact my parents, but I feel that I am being too cold-hearted. It must make my parents very sad to raise a child like me.
keywords: Growing up, personality traits, self-growth, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: Hello there, good Thursday night! It's a fortunate encounter to meet in this question, and I can sense the loneliness in your heart. In this limited time and space, let's open up to each other and speak freely. If you just want to be alone quietly, then why ask this question? The emergence of this question must stem from confusion and a lack of understanding of why you have become like this, which is something you cannot accept and feel puzzled and distressed about. The fact that you don't even want to contact your parents shows that your current mental state is not very good. I am not sure about your age, so I can only speculate from the limited text that you may just be feeling down and wanting to ponder some things on your own. Humans are social beings, and it is impossible to truly become an island without any contact with others. Start by finding some like-minded friends and try to open up and find joy in the process of communication. Maybe that's the next step we need to take. That's all. The world and I love you.

Hello, from a young age, you have been introverted, not good at communication, hiding in a corner, and there has always been a sense of loneliness in your childhood. After starting to work, you do not contact anyone and do not want anyone to know. You just want to live a quiet and peaceful life alone. This is a state of loneliness combined with independence. Now you are struggling because you don't want to contact even your parents, but you feel that this is cold-hearted and don't want to make your parents sad. You feel like a kind and lonely person, immersed in this state of loneliness. Yes, you have the right to enjoy your own state. Loneliness is a sign of maturity. Everyone feels lonelier as they grow older. Even Long Yingtai said, "Children use their backs to silently tell their parents: there is no need to chase." I think you have a lot of love for your parents, but you are not good at expressing it. As a result, this guilt is accumulated in your heart and becomes a struggle. If possible, you can try to maintain a formalized contact with your parents through written letters, for example, by sending a postcard or a selfie during holidays. It is powerful to have the ability to be lonely and take care of yourself in this state. Support yourself. Having the ability to break away from familiar crowds and have the strength to grow on your own is also a satisfactory attitude towards life. In conclusion, I wish you to step out of the haze soon. The world and I love you!

When you have such a feeling of guilt, you actually want to proactively contact your parents, but it's more that you don't know how to talk to them or communicate about certain things, and that's what you need to find out. So now let's think together about what your parents want to chat with you about. Or what aspects of you are they interested in? Can you tell them about the things you have observed and felt that they might also be interested in? Try to do some simple sharing. Also, in this process of sharing, listen to your parents' expectations of you and the things they want you to accomplish that you have not yet completed. If what these events bring to you is not all positive, then you can express your thoughts in an appropriate way. In this process of communication, you and your family will have more topics. I hope this answer is helpful to you.

Good evening, it is an honor to be invited to answer this question, or rather, to share my personal thoughts. In the limited description, I see a state of contradiction. On one hand, you desire a life undisturbed, on the other hand, you desire to be disturbed. There are many different states of a quiet life, so which state of tranquility do you desire? What is it that makes you want to live this kind of life? It may seem callous to not be in contact with your parents, but the truth is, you don't want to contact them. What is preventing you from reaching out to them? And what would happen if you did contact them? I think these are the answers you need to find for yourself.

question: Expose her true face? How should I treat my incredible mother?
description: I have an extraordinary good mother, what makes her extraordinary? The following points: 1. I was raised by my father since I was young, even after my two younger sisters were born, my father's love for me did not diminish (I should be grateful, otherwise I would truly have an uncaring father and unloving mother). But under the "persuasion" of my extraordinary good mother, my father successfully abandoned me. 2. She enjoys disturbing my sleep. I am growing up now, but I suffer from insomnia every day, and my extraordinary good mother is always involved. So, after being awakened by my extraordinary good mother in the early hours of the morning, I sit in front of the computer and type (yesterday I finally managed to fall asleep before 12 o'clock). 3. She loves to pretend. In the eyes of others, she is an extraordinary good mother, and I am an ungrateful child. No one knows the truth, including my father, and I dare not speak up, even if I do, no one will believe me. People surrounded by maternal love, I believe, will not believe my words, but I have been pushed into depression and insomnia from being a happy and healthy person, and my grades have also been affected. This is my extraordinary good mother! Can someone tell me how to expose her true face?
keywords: Family, family trauma, parental communication, growth process.

answers.answer_text: Hello. Allow me to first talk about my impression of you: *I don't know your gender or exact age, but I assume you are underage.* Your relationship with your father is much better than with your mother, but you also feel that your father seems to be gradually distancing himself from you, probably due to some influence from your mother. *You usually have poor sleep quality, and your mother often wakes you up when you're already asleep, but you haven't mentioned why or provided specific details.* You find the image of your mother that she presents to others to be fake and pretentious, and it seems like others see you as an ungrateful child who doesn't understand maternal love. But you dare not tell anyone about all this, including your father, because you think no one would believe you. *Now, you feel that the person you used to be was healthy and happy, but now you feel overall terrible, with declining academic performance and a depressed state of mind, reaching the severity of depression (I'm not sure if a professional doctor has diagnosed you or if it's your own belief).* You attribute all these negative changes to your mother. *You seem to want to expose your mother's true nature to others. But I'm not sure if you have any other plans, such as trying to adjust your own state without changing the current situation or finding a way to distance yourself from your mother, etc. Now, allow me to share my thoughts: *I feel sorry for what you're going through. If what you say is true and your mother has caused you a lot of pain, I'm glad you can come here to vent. I believe you're not a lying child. *However, I'm also willing to continue the conversation with you in order to better help you, especially to learn more about you and your mother, to understand what other things besides disturbing your sleep she has done that bother, embarrass, and distress you. This additional information is crucial because helping you depends on understanding you and your situation, and I think you should be able to understand that. *As for the depression and insomnia you mentioned, I hope you're just exaggerating. But if the situation is really severe, such as feeling constantly low, lack of interest in anything, and if this condition has persisted for a long time, I suggest seeking help from a professional counselor or psychiatrist. If it's not convenient, you can seek help from your homeroom teacher, the school's counseling teacher, or any other person you trust. I believe they will help you. *If unfortunately, they don't believe you or refuse to help you, at least there are people here willing to listen to your experience and help you get out of this predicament. Stay well.

question: Will mental illnesses send signals to the body? For example, will pimples and rashes appear on the body?
description: Recently, I watched a psychological interview where the interviewee had white spots all over their body, which was very distressing. However, I didn't finish watching it, as the teacher mentioned that it caused some mental health disorders.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! After experiencing certain psychological issues, some physical symptoms may occur. In psychology, this phenomenon is called somatization, which refers to a situation where a person has emotional or psychological problems but does not manifest them as psychological symptoms, instead, they are converted into various physical symptoms. For example, a patient with anxiety disorder may often experience insomnia, headaches, and other problems. Alternatively, some people may experience stomachaches when they are particularly stressed. It is important to note the causal and correlational relationships between somatization symptoms and psychological problems. Causality means understanding whether certain somatization symptoms are caused by psychological problems or if the psychological problems are caused by certain physical factors. Correlation refers to the fact that psychological problems and somatization symptoms do not always occur simultaneously. Specific situations require specific analysis.

question: Always repeating these conflicts, every time I encounter them, my first reaction is to think about divorce.
description: Trying to conceive, my husband can't quit smoking and occasionally drinks alcohol... I'm very distressed about this and have communicated with him, made arrangements, but ultimately all failed! Over the past few months, his old problem has resurfaced. He wants to play mahjong every week and plays it on his phone when he comes home from work every day. I told him I wanted a life where we are both busy with work during the day and can spend time together at night chatting, cooking, and exercising. He occasionally does it, but still can't resist playing mahjong on his phone regularly. I've had heartfelt conversations with him about these two issues, gentle communication, sad confessions, arguments, negotiations... but they only have temporary effects! Now he has started to avoid communication. He drinks, smokes continuously, and stays up late playing mahjong... He no longer wants to hear what I have to say, no matter how calm or what tone I use, he just turns around and walks away without saying a word! Last year, I had a miscarriage because the gestational sac didn't develop properly, so I really want a healthy child. But I always feel like I'm the only one making an effort. He has also tried, but it's intermittent. He can't control himself. We have been married for three years, and it has been a three-year adjustment. Now, I'm really tired and conflicted. I want a divorce, but I also have many concerns!

answers.answer_text: Hello! Hearing about your current life situation, I understand the pain you are going through. Facing problems in your marriage and repeatedly trying with disappointing results has left you feeling conflicted and doubting the commitment to your marriage. Let's talk together and see if there are any areas where we can improve your current situation, okay? You are currently trying to conceive and, due to a previous miscarriage, you hope to have a healthy baby. You are concerned about anything that could harm the baby, such as your husband's smoking and drinking. You have asked him to quit smoking and drinking, but he hasn't done so, which disappoints you. Maybe he is trying, but not meeting your expectations in quitting smoking and drinking. Your request is understandable as it is for the well-being of your baby. I believe your husband understands this fact and knows that it is not good for the baby. Quitting smoking and drinking is not easy, perhaps you need to try to understand his perspective, talk to him, and understand the underlying reasons for his continued smoking and drinking habits. No matter the reason, try to show him some understanding, as it may help him improve. He has resumed his old habits of smoking, playing mahjong, and not spending time with you, which is not what you want. You have communicated with him many times, but in the end, he avoids the conversation and refuses to communicate. This makes you feel unaccepted and helpless, as if you are the only one making an effort while he doesn't seem to care. You want him to spend more time with you and have the kind of life you desire, but he can't seem to do it. Have you considered his needs and desires while only expressing your own? Both partners in a marriage should strive to satisfy each other's needs and rely on each other. If you can't see his needs or meet them, he will surely be dissatisfied, even though men may not express it as directly as women. So, when you make demands, you should also consider his thoughts, pay attention to his needs, and respect him, providing a certain response and satisfaction. Love flows in both directions, he will feel your love and express his love to you. His refusal to communicate makes you feel that he is not putting effort into your family, which causes your dissatisfaction. Regarding his behavior, you think that he can't control himself. Why does he refuse to communicate? This depends on how you communicated in the past. If he ultimately refuses to communicate, it means that your communication approach is ineffective. Therefore, improving your communication pattern is vital. Building effective communication: First, you need to listen. You need to listen to his perspective and feelings towards the issue. Ask if he has considered the harm smoking and drinking can cause to the baby, and what worries or concerns he has. Listen attentively and take this opportunity to fully understand him. Secondly, offer understanding. Put yourself in his shoes and empathize with his emotions. Agree with his feelings and provide reassurance. Thirdly, directly express your requirements to him. Tell him that you hope he can work together with you to raise a healthy baby, spend more time with you, and create the kind of home you desire. Fourthly, acknowledge his efforts and provide feedback. Thank him for his contributions and let him see the positive impact he has had on your life. This will make him feel supported and motivated to continue his efforts. Feeling helpless and resentful has led you to doubt your marriage. After three years of trying to make it work, your marriage still makes you sad and exhausted. So you now consider divorce but have concerns. The truth about marriage is that harmony can bring sweetness and happiness, while pain can make you want to leave. Divorce is not a wise choice for pain because the pain is not the root of the problem. Just like in your marriage, the pain you feel is not the issue, but rather the conflicting approaches and actions when dealing with your husband and resolving problems, which causes your pain. We all say that marriage requires effort, and this effort has no time limit. Whatever problems arise, they must be bravely faced and resolved together so that the marriage can move towards greater happiness. I am sure that once you and your husband can resolve this issue and work together to welcome a healthy baby, the intimacy between you and your spouse will greatly increase. I wish you a happy life and take good care of yourself. The world and I love you, and this is a secret base for your questions anytime.

OP, hello, sending you hugs. I hope my answer can bring you some help. As a wife, I understand your feelings, because I have had a similar experience. My husband also likes to play mahjong and smoke. Sometimes, even when I was sick and in pain, he would go play mahjong with his friends instead of taking me to the hospital or taking care of me at home. At that time, I also didn't understand. Clearly, he loves me and I love him, so why wouldn't he change for me? Later on, I learned a lot of truths and established a new mindset, which made our relationship more harmonious and our life happier. Combining my own experience with your question, I would like to give you the following suggestions: 1. Accept your husband. Do you know? It is very difficult to change a person because he is who he is. He likes smoking and playing mahjong because these things have benefits and attractions for him. Smoking can relieve stress and anxiety and help him think. Sometimes, it is also a social need. Playing mahjong may be a way for him to relax. Maybe it doesn't feel good to you, but he enjoys it. So, we need to see that he does these things for his own reasons. If he doesn't want to change himself, it is difficult for us to change him. "The Power of Now" once said, "There are only three things in the world: your own business, other people's business, and the business of the universe. The reason why we are troubled is that we don't handle our own business well and instead worry about other people's business and the business of the universe. Your husband smoking and playing mahjong is his business, something we cannot control. If we try to change him forcefully, conflicts will arise and affect the relationship. However, you can do what you can do. You can express your concerns and fears, telling him that you're afraid his lack of attention to his health will affect your fertility plans. Let him know that you really want to have a healthy child with him and hope he can cooperate with you. You can also ask him why he wants to smoke and play mahjong. What do these activities bring to him? What needs does it fulfill for him? You can explore together if there are better alternatives to smoking and playing mahjong. When you communicate with him with respect and love, when you adopt an accepting attitude without seeking deliberate change, perhaps change will actually happen. 2. Love yourself. Pay more attention to your feelings and needs. Take care of yourself first. Only when we take good care of ourselves can we have a more positive state of mind. When you have emotions, examine where they come from and identify the needs that haven't been met. Then, meet those needs. For example, if you crave others' approval, you need to give yourself approval first. If you need others' trust, start by trusting yourself...because when we have a lack, we strive to seek outside, to try to prove ourselves. However, external feedback is uncertain, so we will experience setbacks and setbacks. Therefore, seeking from within is the most stable and can bring us a sense of security. However, this self-acceptance and self-affirmation is not something that can be achieved overnight. It takes a long time to practice. But as long as we are on the path, we will become better and better. Love yourself, take good care of your diet and daily life, take care of your emotional feelings, and treat yourself like an intimate friend. This will put you in a good state, and you will face the challenges of life with more ease and calmness. 3. Enrich your life and divert your attention. Life is colorful, and nothing can be the entirety of our lives. Your husband is a part of your life, and getting pregnant is only a part of life. Besides these, your life has many other parts. You can do things that make you happy, things that make you relax. Go on trips with friends, spend more time in nature, listen to music you like, read books you enjoy... When you no longer focus all your energy on the things that bother you, you will discover that there are many wonderful aspects in life. When you relax, maybe the things you've been expecting will come to you. Best wishes.

Hello! I see that in this marriage, many of the husband's actions are making you dissatisfied and frustrated, especially during the pre-pregnancy period, where you are more sensitive to smoking and drinking behaviors. His actions may give you the feeling that he doesn't care about you, the marriage, or your future, which can be disappointing and exhausting for you. I noticed that you have made some efforts, such as communication, vulnerability, arguments, and negotiations, but they only have temporary effects and you soon fall back into old patterns, which can make you feel powerless. First, let's talk about when your husband's behaviors started. Were they like this from the beginning of your relationship, or did they begin later on? Generally, smoking, drinking, playing mahjong, or doing so on the phone are ways people seek enjoyment. Everyone has their own hobbies, such as binge-watching dramas, watching variety shows, or drinking bubble tea. Occasionally indulging in these activities can relieve stress and provide temporary relaxation and happiness, which is understandable. If someone becomes addicted to these activities for a long period, it may indicate that something in their real life is causing them to want to escape or that life is too boring, and smoking, drinking, and playing mahjong are more appealing options. For example, the activities you hope for, such as chatting, cooking, and exercising together, may not be of interest to your husband. This difference can be influenced by inherent gender traits and a lack of love in your relationship. So, if your husband wasn't like this from the beginning, there's a high possibility that your marriage has encountered problems. Your pattern in the relationship leans towards communication and expressing, while your husband seems to prefer remaining silent, causing differences and conflicts. If the marriage is to continue, there must be more understanding and respect from both sides towards each other's true selves. Then, finding common ground and compromises, which are based on both parties' love, can be achieved. Hence, a crucial question is whether there is still love between you both? Additionally, I noticed a key event last year when you had a miscarriage. I don't know if your husband's behavior changed after the miscarriage. Losing a child, whom both spouses have nurtured, whether due to congenital impairments or intentional abortion, can damage the relationship. Perhaps your husband grieved for the loss of your previous child but didn't express it and chose smoking, drinking, and playing mahjong as a way to escape. On the other hand, your way of downplaying this sorrow may involve wanting a healthy child again. It creates a difference in your attitudes and behaviors towards nurturing new life. You may feel that your husband is not making as much effort and that you're the only one exerting yourself and feeling exhausted. Therefore, the aforementioned points aim to provide you with a new perspective on your marriage and your husband's actions. If there is still love and attachment between you, I suggest seeking marriage counseling to address the underlying issues, adjust the interaction patterns, and move towards a more positive cycle in your marriage. Many people can't even change themselves, let alone others. If someone wants to change you, I don't think you would willingly agree to it. Secondly, your husband's efforts remind me of parent-child relationships. Many parents tell their children that they can do whatever they want if they achieve a certain score. However, many children still fail to meet their parents' standards, despite having great temptations. Many parents get angry, thinking their children are not working hard, but the person who wants to achieve good results is not the parent, it is the child. I think your husband's efforts also prove that he wants to change, but due to many reasons, he can't, and he is under great pressure. I believe the current situation is not the result he wants. Thirdly, multiple communication attempts have yielded no results. If you want your husband to change, or in other words, if you want your child to get good grades, just telling him about the benefits of good grades, these are common sense that I believe everyone understands. If your husband also wants to change but somehow can't, then you should find out the reasons why he can't change and the problems he encounters in the process of change, and solve them together. If the purpose of communication is not to solve problems, but to ignore his efforts and difficulties, I don't think any communication methods would be effective. Fourthly, regarding the issue of trying to conceive, did you rush into it after the miscarriage last year? Has your body fully recovered? The key relationship in a family is the relationship between husband and wife, and having a child before your relationship is stable may bring endless problems even if the child is healthy. Any couple will encounter many problems, after all, everyone comes from different families and has different experiences, so it's normal to have different opinions, attitudes, and abilities towards many things. However, how to seek common ground while respecting differences is the key to maintaining a relationship. Family relationships need to be nurtured, they don't naturally exist with love and harmony, and even if you divorce or find someone else, you will encounter similar problems. [Methods and Suggestions] Here are a few suggestions: First, if possible, seek family therapy together with your husband, let a counselor help identify deeper reasons and solutions. Second, educate yourself with some basic knowledge of psychology, which will help you understand yourself and others. Third, consider temporarily setting aside trying to conceive and focus on rebuilding your relationship with your husband. I hope my answer can be helpful to you.

The paragraph talks about the frustration and helplessness of the questioner. It seems that the questioner has tried their best to reach a consensus with their husband regarding their daily interactions and habits, but it has always ended in failure. This makes the questioner feel tired and conflicted, unsure of what to do. For an adult, it is generally difficult to change someone else's behavior through external means. I believe the questioner has come to realize this through three years of adjusting to their marriage with their husband. The questioner's husband has even reached the point of refusing to communicate (regardless of whether it is done calmly or not, he just turns around and walks away without saying a word!), making it even more difficult for the questioner. If the questioner feels that they have already put in their maximum effort and exhausted all possible methods, but still cannot achieve their expected state, then they need to shift their focus back to themselves. Have they analyzed these so-called concerns, how many are from themselves, and how many are from external factors and pressures? However, this does not mean that external factors should be the main factor in our decision-making. Although external factors affect our lives in various ways, we are still the core of our lives. We are the ultimate decision-makers and bearers of our own lifestyles. Therefore, I suggest that the questioner, in the face of the current situation, regardless of what choice they make, they must first clarify their deepest inner needs. Only by starting from our fundamental needs will we not fall into a state of internal conflict and constantly feel "tired". I hope this is helpful to the questioner.
