question: The pain of life, feeling like everything is concentrated on me?
description: Difficulty in handling interpersonal relationships, pain from the original family, childhood misfortune, feeling like everything revolves around me. I want to die but I am afraid to die. Will dying bring relief?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, emotional regulation, fragile tears.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the many things in life seem to be cyclical. When you feel good, everything seems to go smoothly, and this smoothness makes you feel even better. Then you perform better, forming a positive cycle. Conversely, there is also a negative cycle, where everything feels bad and nothing goes smoothly, leading to a downward spiral. It's like the ancient poem says, "When the roof is leaking, it always coincides with a night of rain." You said that it feels like everything is concentrated on you, but perhaps you are just trapped in this negative cycle. If you can break this cycle and enter a positive one, everything will gradually improve. Actually, the pain you mentioned is all interconnected. It's because your original family was painful that you had an unfortunate childhood. This unfortunate childhood didn't allow you to learn healthy patterns of interpersonal relationships, making it easy to encounter problems in that area. Not all the problems revolve around you; it's just that one problem leads to another, triggering a series of issues. Although the impact of the painful original family is significant, it is not something that cannot be overcome entirely. Through our efforts, we can try our best to overcome the trauma from our original family, break free from the negative cycle, and create a different life for ourselves. However, this process is not simple or quick. It may require long-term effort. If possible, I suggest seeking a consultation with a counselor. With the counselor's guidance, you can reexamine your growth journey and achieve psychological growth and transformation. If you currently don't have the means, you can also read more books related to psychology, such as "Transcending the Original Family" and "Having a Life Where You Have the Final Say." These books contain many theories and methods that can help us in our self-growth. You should know that as long as you don't give up and keep making efforts, you can gradually break free from the current terrible state. Give yourself some time, be patient, take it slow, and remember that life won't always be this bad! Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Come, come here. In life, there will be some disappointments and setbacks. Many people live in a state of not having enough to eat or wear, many people suffer from terminal illnesses, and many others are caught in wars and difficulties, but they still live on with strength. The pain of life is no greater than the loss of love, the failure of career, the inability to pursue education, or the departure of beloved family members. But don't lose heart, don't do anything foolish. After the darkness, there is dawn. We are with you, always together.

question: On the third day of junior high school, my grandmother passed away. I'm afraid that if I take leave, I won't be able to catch up. What should I do?
description: I asked my classmates, and they said they didn't understand anything after missing class. I also don't know what to do.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, giving you a warm hug. I can tell that the death of a loved one, combined with taking multiple days off, may be causing you some anxiety, especially during this critical period. Phil wants to say, first, you need to stabilize your mindset. The more critical the situation, the less you should panic. Panic and anxiety won't solve the problem and may even make it worse. It's better to face it calmly. Also, the bereavement leave is not too long, and according to the normal teaching schedule, most of the third-year of junior high school is devoted to reviewing. There are few teachers who teach new lessons during this time, so you won't miss much. Secondly, when you ask your classmates, are you asking the ones who have good grades? Or the ones who are average? Or the ones who are not good at studies? And which category do you fall into? It's possible that the material you missed is easy for you but difficult for others to understand. But no matter what, the most important thing is to retain your assignments and exams, and then ask the teacher promptly when you return to school, whether it's for the missed parts or the parts you don't understand, and make use of your free time to catch up.

Hello~ When faced with the death of a loved one, we all feel a sense of loss and agitation. At this time, it would be best for you to assist your parents or elders in handling the affairs related to the death and not worry too much. Considering future concerns will not help us solve the current difficulties, but instead make our hearts heavier and more uncomfortable. So, during your rest days, you should take care of the family matters and also take some time to relax and relieve your complex emotions. Adjust yourself well so that you can focus better on preparing for your exams when classes resume. As the stress of studying for the important exams increases, it is natural to experience significant fluctuations in your emotions. In addition to the sudden bad news, we need to learn how to adjust our mindset. What we need to face now is to approach it with a relaxed attitude and not worry too much about future concerns, as time will help you solve those problems. What you need to do now is to calm your emotions. The weather is gradually cooling down, so take good care of yourself, try not to get sick, get plenty of rest, and safely let this period pass. The birth, aging, illness, and death of loved ones are common occurrences, so you should not be too saddened. Focus on the present, study hard, get into your ideal high school, and show your acceptance letter to your grandma who is far away~ After classes resume, stick to your own pace. Whether it's regular homework or monthly exams, you may fall behind compared to your classmates. At this time, you must not let the teacher's lesson progress or the review progress of your classmates disrupt your own learning rhythm, put simply, do not panic. Continue to revise and study according to the plan you originally set. This period may be difficult, so use the free time during evening self-study or on Saturdays and Sundays to gradually digest the lessons covered during your absence. Initially, you may find certain topics difficult to understand, and psychologically reject them, thinking that you "can't learn them at all". At this time, you need to calm down, believe in yourself, and slowly digest the material. For parts that you truly don't understand, you can privately seek help from your teacher or classmates. As long as you maintain your rhythm, you can keep up with the rest of the class. Keep it up, and I wish you success in getting into your ideal high school!

question: In insecurity due to upper limb disability, I have the desire to go out to work, but I am conflicted.
description: I am a person with upper limb disabilities, unable to control my arms and hands. Recently, I have been extremely self-conscious and nervous when going out and meeting people, exhibiting abnormal behavior. Whenever I feel tense, my arm curls up, which makes me very uncomfortable. Currently, I can only manage to do essential tasks such as buying food and have limited interaction or communication with others. Just barely. But when I'm alone, I feel relaxed, so I have thought about going out to work. I don't have any particular special skills. Last night, I couldn't sleep at all, so I went out early to buy food before there were too many people around. It felt good, but I quickly returned home. I would like to ask if my behavior is too extreme, and if there are any suitable job options that do not require much communication or interaction with others. I want to take things step by step.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, social anxiety, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello! I couldn't resist clicking on the title and reading your post. You mentioned having an upper limb disability, but based on your ability to write such a long paragraph with no punctuation mistakes, your language skills seem fine. You're amazing! People often say, "You're young and able-bodied, so you have nothing to worry about." Nowadays, society has become more accepting and understanding toward disabled individuals, and the government has created numerous job opportunities for this group. So, don't worry about not being able to do well for yourself, as long as you can live a normal life, you can definitely create value. However, your issue lies not in how to support yourself, but in how to accept yourself. You mentioned feeling anxious and curling your arm when you see others, which is very uncomfortable. I understand that it stems from your low self-esteem and reluctance to show your true self, leading to this series of negative emotions. Therefore, the most important thing is to have confidence in yourself. Life is not as simple as we imagine, but it's also not as difficult as we imagine. There are no perfect people in the world, and everyone has their own shortcomings. Take a look at Nick Vujicic online, maybe it will help alleviate many of your worries. Keep going, the world and I love you.

Hello OP (^_^) / I can really understand your feelings after seeing your question. Being special does not mean being inferior. Being special only means that we may have some special needs, that's all. I have many students with moderate to severe intellectual disabilities and some children with cerebral palsy, and they still live confidently and brightly. I don't know how the attitude towards people with special needs is in your living environment. In the city where I am, people have shown more care and acceptance for the special population. Even if there are a few individuals who cannot accept it, if we can accept ourselves, then nobody's gaze can hurt us. I remember a teacher once said, "Never look down upon 'disabled' people, because we cannot guarantee that we will not become disabled ourselves at some point in our lives, nor can we guarantee that our descendants will not be disabled." In this regard, it is possible for anyone to become "disabled". "OP said that contacting or communicating with others is still manageable to some extent." OP can start from this point. Find a job that suits your abilities and is suitable for your psychological state. Take it slowly, and when you adapt, gradually move on to more interactions. Just a small reminder, it is impossible for anyone to have a smooth job search, and there may be repeated setbacks. Don't attribute it excessively to your own "disability" just because you hit a wall. We can't change other people's choices and perspectives, the only thing we can change is our own mindset. May we find inspiration in the following quote: "No one can hurt you unless you allow them to." Wishing you all the best (｡ò∀ó｡).

Hello. After seeing your question, I really want to stand with you and tell you that everyone is deserving of love, including you. Having a physical disability does not mean that a person is terrible. On the contrary, they must be living with great effort and even more courage than those without disabilities. I believe you may have a lot of self-doubt in your heart, and these doubts make it difficult for us to communicate and discover things we can do. You can start by accepting yourself and changing the self-doubt caused by your disability. After accepting yourself, you can mobilize the resources around you, try to ask your family or friends for possible job opportunities, or seek out local support groups for individuals with disabilities and support and help each other. Best wishes~.

Title owner, give you a hug. As long as you still have the desire to go out and work, it proves that you are the best! According to your current thoughts, becoming a cleaner is the most suitable. You don't need to come into contact with too many people and can enjoy your alone time, which is perfect for you. This is just a suggestion, your behavior is not extreme, and all these behaviors are within a reasonable cognitive range. Step out, live independently, and gradually you will rediscover yourself, grow again, and be reborn.

question: 23-year-old female has been suffering from depression for two years and social anxiety. She wants to self-regulate. How can she do it?
description: A 23-year-old woman has been suffering from depression for two years. After taking medication for half a year, she experienced severe side effects, including uncontrollable hand tremors that hinder her from performing delicate tasks. She decided to stop taking the medication on her own for six months. Currently, she is experiencing severe social anxiety, unwilling to answer phone calls or interact with others. She even refuses to leave her room. Although she doesn't want to be this way, she feels extremely anxious and nervous when interacting with others. She wonders how she can regulate herself.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, healing methods, anxious emotions.

answers.answer_text: This is what I wrote, my own experience, hoping to help you. Article title: "In-depth Analysis: Why do we isolate ourselves and refuse to see any friends when we are depressed?" In the Warm Home group, some of the depression patients I am more familiar with will find different degrees of interpersonal sensitivity and compulsive tendencies when doing the SCL-90. After the onset of depression, we find ourselves in a dilemma. After discovering the huge gap between our true selves, ideal selves, and our past selves, we cannot accept it when we see our true selves. In fact, our previous self in Horney's "Our Inner Conflicts" is called the idealized self, which is the self that we excessively magnified before and is not real; our current self is also not real, but has been continuously depreciated by us. In a previous article on our public account, "The Power of Self-Suggestion" was mentioned, which said that self-suggestion can change our thinking and then change our behavior. This suggestion can be positive or negative. It is precisely because of this that we first have a discrepancy and then have compulsive thinking. Under the constant depreciation (suggestion) of ourselves, we feel more and more that we are getting worse and worse, more and more unacceptable, and more and more worthless. Conflict with friends 01: We lost completely. After staying in the Warm Home for a long time, I am more familiar with the personality of most group members. Regardless of how their interpersonal relationships were before, they basically have two personality traits: perfectionism and assertiveness. Perfectionism makes us demand perfection in things that we particularly care about (mainly due to different growth experiences) and cannot accept any criticism; assertiveness makes us unable to lose to anyone in things that we particularly care about. The problem arises here. After the onset of depression, when we discover that our true selves are not as perfect as we imagined, and under the constant depreciation of ourselves through compulsive thinking, our current selves become more and more worthless. So our assertiveness comes out again. "They must laugh at us, look down on us." "We're done, we can never hold our heads up in front of them again. I will never be able to be proud in front of them again." This is the first conflict, we are inferior to others, we lost to others, and they will laugh at me. Then we start to see that people who used to be worse off than us are doing better than us, and we feel more and more uncomfortable, and we hate ourselves more and more. We feel that we are worse than everyone, and we are simply the worst person in the world. Self-confidence completely collapses, crushed brutally. Occasionally going out to see friends, but always feel that they are laughing at us, looking down on us, and anything negative they say is about us. So we have various fears, fear of crowds, fear of social interactions, and then we start to isolate ourselves and cut off contact with family, relatives, and friends. Because we cannot accept this fact, so we start to escape. We hope to find a countryside, a place where no one knows us; we hope to find a place to retreat to. 02: I want to ask for help, but I have hurt them before. In a previous article, it was mentioned that during depression, we actually desire to find friends to help us. But it is difficult to speak up. Looking back, I feel that I am ashamed to ask them for help. Because I have hurt too many people when I was in glory. Or, because we refuse to forgive others for their minor mistakes, our relationship becomes strained. When we have depression, our confidence collapses, and our previous self only showed the best side to others. And at this time, we are already in such a miserable state, and I have hurt them before, they will definitely not help me. So, I start to feel guilty, self-blame, isolated and helpless. Under compulsive thinking, constantly repeating, constantly suggesting, feeling that the past cannot be saved, if this friend who we have hurt knows how miserable I am, they will definitely take pleasure in my misfortune. Finally, it turns into another emotion: self-hatred, despair; and then continues to strengthen, and turns into self-attack. 03: Why don't they understand me? When my depression attacks, I have turned to several close friends to confide in. Of course, I didn't tell them that I have depression. I just told them about my current situation and various problems, and I told them over and over again. Friends didn't understand me at the time, and they felt that we were full of negative energy, always complaining, and didn't want to talk to me. At that moment, I started another emotion: anger. "Why did I treat you so well before? When you were in a bad mood, it was me who comforted you. But when I am in a bad mood, you are not there for me." "You should care about me, accompany me. You used to be my best and most trustworthy friends!" ...Then, under compulsive thinking, constant suggestion, I feel more and more that there is no good person in this world, and it finally turns into another emotion: hatred. How to deal with relationships with friends? 01: Thinking that friends will mock oneself may just be projection. Many people think that friends will mock themselves, including myself before. Until one day, I learned to do things solidly, instead of always analyzing the success of something based on my own logic, but discovering the feasibility of doing things based on my own gradual adjustment. I realized that any small thing that I thought was easy before, is actually not easy when doing it, and mistakes will occur. Until one day, I learned to accept that my life is not always smooth sailing; learned to accept that I am not perfect and dare to show my imperfections; learned to accept that I will make mistakes and learn from them; learned to accept that I will fail and gain growth from failures; learned to do things step by step diligently and discover that things are not as easy as they seem... At this time, I finally started to stop judging and evaluating others, and even started to feel compassion for people in adversity and helped them sincerely. So, this is my understanding, only by reconciling with ourselves can we reconcile with the world. What you think of others, depends on your needs and your inner perspective. 02: Accept reality, appreciate and learn humbly from friends who are better than us. Our current selves are not as worthless as we imagine. We are just constantly suggesting and feeling worse in compulsive thinking, under various comparisons. In today's society, many people need to receive praise from others to affirm themselves, so when you see them showing off, it is not genuine, and it also reflects their own possible insecurities. At this time, they are not real either. Everything good you see about them is just superficial. Because we are looking at them while depreciating ourselves, so we appear to be much worse than them. Moreover, those who were worse than us before are not really worse than us, we just cannot see what we care about in them. For example, we did not care about emotional intelligence before, thinking that it is being naive and easy to be bullied. But the truth is that they know how to give, they are loyal, they are more diligent than us, so they are appreciated by their superiors. And we are difficult to control, unconsciously not putting our superiors in our eyes, so our superiors don't like us... So, we must admit our shortcomings and learn from others when necessary. Only in this way can we progress and constantly improve ourselves. Finally, those successful people around us, you have to admit that they are indeed better than us. They have higher emotional intelligence, stronger abilities, and have put in a lot of effort privately. Only when they were putting in effort, we couldn't see it, we only focused on their success. So, when it is necessary to admit defeat, we must admit defeat, don't envy, just appreciate. The envy of successful people around us is a normal emotion, not only for us with depression, but also for many normal people. It is a very normal emotion for human beings. So, you don't need to blame yourself because of envy. Envy breeds dark thinking in our hearts, and then changes our behavior, deliberately causing trouble, belittling others, and ultimately destroying relationships. Only by appreciating and learning to see the strengths of others can we learn from them and make progress. 03: Learn to understand and forgive. In fact, the world of depression patients is difficult for those who have not experienced depression to understand, including psychologists and counselors. What about our friends? We must know that during depression, all of our negative emotions and negative thinking cannot be resolved through just one conversation. It requires repeatedly discussing the same problems. And in their view, these are issues that are easily dealt with. So they may not have the patience, and in a different perspective, we wouldn't have the patience either. A few days ago, a friend left a message on our public account, saying: "I feel like my friends don't want to talk to me anymore, and I feel like I can't keep up with their thinking." I replied: "Actually, friends don't dislike talking to you, but when we have depression, we repeatedly talk about the same problems. Others may not have the patience anymore. From another perspective, you might lose patience with yourself too; it's not that you can't keep up with their thinking, but when we have depression, all our attention is on ourselves and we don't really listen to what they say, so it's normal that you can't keep up with their thinking. Everything will be fine when your depression is cured." This world will inevitably have imperfections, and indeed there are people who have truly hurt us. But a few people do not represent everyone. And those who hurt us may also have mental problems, or maybe we have hurt their interests in the past? Furthermore, everyone makes mistakes, including ourselves. So depression is an opportunity for us to learn to understand and forgive. 04: Make every effort to make up for past mistakes, and avoid making them again. Take the initiative to apologize. Apologizing is not giving up, but admitting past mistakes. This way, we can correct ourselves; at the same time, it helps us maintain our friendships. Perhaps our true friends have already forgiven us. Regardless, relationships are based on fate and need to be cherished. We should do our best to make up for what we can. Do what we should do and don't force others. When we apologize, some friends may still not be able to forgive us. At this moment, don't force it, just do what we can. As long as we have done what we should do, whether to forgive or not is up to others. At least, we don't need to blame ourselves anymore because the past is already in the past, regrets are futile, only lessons can be learned. A family member of a recovered patient once said, "Work hard as much as possible, and accept the outcome that comes." Yes, let's do what we should do, so that we won't feel guilty or regretful, and whether others choose to forgive or not is their business. We should just do our best, avoid making the same mistakes again. In the future, when we meet new friends on the path of life, we should learn to treat them with a sincere heart, without ulterior motives. What does it mean to have no ulterior motives and not use others? It means not caring about any return. Recall that before depression, whenever we made a new friend, didn't we always think about what benefits they could bring us? At this time, we need to adjust our thinking and not care about any returns. Because treating a person sincerely and unconditionally can be felt. The so-called "a long journey tests the horse's strength, a long time reveals a person's heart." Only with sincerity can we exchange sincerity. Relationships require hard work, and in the end, you will also receive genuine friendship. After recovering from depression, I have gained a few sincere friends. No matter what problems I encounter, they will support and help me. I really cherish these friends, and at the same time, I will do my best to support them unconditionally. I know that I have shortcomings, so I also accept their shortcomings and focus on their strengths, so I have learned to be tolerant. I know that I also have difficulties, so when they encounter difficulties, I sincerely encourage them. I know that I will also have good times, so when they are successful, I sincerely congratulate them instead of being jealous. Actually, how you treat friends can be felt by them. So, we appreciate and cherish each other. Because of them, I often feel happy; because of them, I feel empowered; because of them, I am no longer afraid in adversity; because I know they are there. So, I sincerely thank those friends who unconditionally support me. Thank you, because of you, my heart is often filled with gratitude. Friends who unconditionally support you are really rare, so we should also treat others with sincerity. This kind of friendship is more resilient than the friendship you obtain with ulterior motives. It made me reflect on what I really want after experiencing depression. Happiness is not having people cheering for you when you succeed, but having friends accompany you when you are at a low point in life.

In your case, I advise you to continue taking medication and, in addition, to seek psychological counseling. This way, the effects will be much better. If the side effects of the medication are too severe, you can ask the doctor to switch to a medication with milder side effects. Also, I recommend that you must make sure to exercise regularly, such as walking 10k steps a day or jogging, swimming, practicing the Five Animal Exercises, playing badminton, and so on. Regular exercise will be beneficial for your recovery.

question: Feeling useless and unable to solve problems, how to change one's fate?
description: I feel like I can't solve problems, I am overly dependent, and I'm very weak. I had a friend who told me the reason she doesn't like showing her drawings to others is because when she was younger, one time her classmates took her drawings and showed the whole class, saying they were ugly. I don't know how to help her, and I don't know how to comfort others when they cry. They always say it's nothing, but there was one time when my math teacher ignored me and I cried alone in a dark place. Then a group of boys surrounded me and laughed, saying I looked scary like a ghost. I felt so alone and misunderstood. That teacher, for me, was during a phase where I was giving up on myself, and he was the only one who didn't give up on me, along with another boy who unconditionally accepted me. I don't really like talking to them, and others think they have character issues, but because they accept me unconditionally and always respond to me, I feel like I can't live without them. And there's one more person, initially it was awkward when we met, but one time he greeted me first, and I wondered if he forgot about me. I also noticed that when other people don't want to be disturbed, they say "don't bother me," while I say "don't pay attention to me." I feel uncertain about the future and afraid of repeating my parents' life, so I want to understand my subconscious to change my destiny.

answers.answer_text: Hello, original poster, the ability to solve problems is something that is learned. Do not deny your future development and change just because you feel temporarily powerless. From your description, it can be seen that you are a careful and sensitive person. Your inner world is rich, but you may have difficulty expressing it in words. Perhaps you have always held a sense of caution towards your surroundings, keeping yourself cocooned in a safe shell, not getting close to others nor allowing them to get close to you. When your friend confides in you, it is because they trust you deeply. If you don't know how to comfort her, you can quietly stay beside her, hold her hand, or give her a hug. Even without words, this physical contact can convey your care. When you cry in the dark corner and passers-by may not notice, their comments like "it's scary" should not be taken too seriously. Their behavior is inappropriate, of course. What you should really care about is how you feel. When you feel wronged and sad, confide in friends instead of letting yourself stay in a state of sorrow and isolation. To some extent, we choose the environment we are in. When you actively face things in your environment, it may respond to you. Conversely, when you respond negatively to the environment, it may also be filled with malice. Believe in your true feelings and don’t judge the appearance of the person you care about based on others' words. Judge for yourself with your heart. You can rely on your own strength to solve problems gradually instead of easily relying on others. The teacher and classmates who show positive attention to you make you feel acknowledged, and it's normal for you to have gratitude and goodwill towards them. However, this does not mean that you can't live a good life without them in the future. Be grateful to those who help us, but also have the courage to go your own way. Your belief that you cannot live without certain people suggests to yourself that you need help and that you have never valued your own strength. You have your own strengths and weaknesses. Make good use of your strengths and dare to show yourself in the crowd instead of always hiding behind. You are also worthy of being seen and stepping onto the stage. Take it slow and start with adjusting your body posture to stand tall, then let your inner self see the sunlight, and let your eyes see a future with goals. Mold yourself with care and treat those who want to get close to you. Believe that you will become better and better. Best wishes.

question: Sharing moments on social media can cause anxiety, but I can't help but want to share. What should I do?
description: As a post-2000s, I've actually enjoyed posting updates on social media since I was young. I used to think that social media could record life, interact with friends, and even vent about unhappy things. Overall, I felt that it was something meaningful. Even now, I still enjoy posting updates. However, some of my friends have told me that I share too much online, especially personal thoughts, and they think it's embarrassing. There are also friends who say that instead of building an online persona on social media, I should focus on living a good life. I now feel conflicted about posting updates because sometimes it can affect others and honestly, it doesn't seem to have much meaning. So, I'm currently in a dilemma. Sometimes, I feel like what I say might make others dislike me, but I also believe that it's the real me, and I wonder why I should care about what others think. However, I don't want others to think I'm a weird person, so I'm hesitant to express myself. After every update I post, I end up feeling conflicted and torn, especially when it's something unconventional or not in line with the social norm. I don't want to always care about what others think, but I also find it boring to constantly share irrelevant updates. How should I approach this situation?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, interpersonal boundaries, social networking applications.

answers.answer_text: Hug you~ The problem you are facing is: you love posting moments on your social media feed, but after being criticized by your friends, you start to feel conflicted. On one hand, you still enjoy sharing your life and thoughts through posting, but on the other hand, you start questioning the necessity of sharing these moments. In my opinion, the real dilemma you are facing is whether to be true to yourself or to care about what others think and hide a part of yourself. "Moments" on social media are originally a platform for sharing and documenting your life and thoughts. You can treat it as a record or as a means of sharing. I don't understand why your "friends" would judge such a simple act of posting moments as "building a persona." If I were to ponder whether or not each moment is worth sharing before posting, wouldn't that be creating a persona? In your case, you simply want to document your life and share what you want to share, so how can it be considered creating a persona? You mentioned being conflicted and trapped by the opinions of others, perhaps because their words have made you overthink. Sometimes, overthinking hinders our progress. Instead, it's better to simplify things and think about why we started posting moments in the first place and whether what we are doing now contradicts our initial intentions. If it doesn't, then bravely continue doing it. How we correctly listen to others' opinions is a lifelong lesson that requires constant reflection and learning. Others' evaluations may not necessarily reflect objective facts since their opinions are influenced by their subjective consciousness. Therefore, we need to think independently and develop our own sense of right and wrong. You are a kind, lovely, and life-loving person, so don't let the thoughts of a few individuals discourage your passion for life. Although I personally differ from you in terms of posting moments, I don't believe that my way is right and your way is wrong, nor do I have any intention of controlling or changing you. On the other hand, it seems like your "friend" aggressively wants to change the way you live, and I hope you seriously consider this.

OP, hello~ I saw your question and I deeply understand the contradictions you are facing. First of all, I am also from the post-2000 generation and used to love playing QQ space. I used to write about what happened and my feelings every day, and I didn't think it was a big deal. Of course, now I don't post on QQ as frequently as before. When QQ launched the "On This Day" feature, I could see the updates I made years ago almost every day, and I would think, "Why was I so immature back then, writing everything on there?" Unlike you, I no longer want to use social media to record my life, but you are in a contradictory state where you want to post but fear it will affect others. You are in adolescence, experiencing self-identity confusion and conflicts between multiple values, which make it difficult for you to adapt and result in internal conflicts and crises. You said you "don't care about other people's opinions," but you also enjoy posting updates and interacting, but isn't the essence of posting updates to hope that others will see them? In this regard, isn't there a contradiction? If you want others to see, negative comments are inevitable. If you just want to record your life, you can use electronic diaries, memos, and other methods. Currently, the most important thing for you is to figure out the true intention behind wanting to post updates on social media. Do you want everyone to see, or is it simply to record your life? Is what you said about not caring about other people's opinions true, or is it just psychological comfort for yourself? You need to use your brain and carefully consider these questions. I hope my answer can help you. Have a happy life!

Hello, OP. First, I want to give you a hug (｡･ω･｡)ﾉ Posting on social media is a common thing in life, but it can sometimes involve other people's privacy and may cause discontent. It's a good thing that you like to post on social media to record your life and share it with others. It's a way to communicate and share feelings with others. Actually, you don't have to care too much about what others think, as long as you don't write anything that involves other people's privacy. Other people's opinions or how they perceive you are their own business, and we don't have to be influenced by what others think. If you still feel uneasy, I suggest you write down everything you want to say in your own diary. I hope my answer can help you. Take care and best wishes.

Hello, I think the problems you are currently facing are experienced by many people. The positive aspects of a social circle are: recording, sharing, socializing, and positive promotion. The negative aspects of a social circle are: showing off, venting, taking sides, comparing, and marketing. In fact, a social circle is just a tool for direct communication and mutual attention between people. Your current confusion is that you don't know how to use this tool and how to use it, but you really want to use it. In fact, we all want to gain attention from others through our social circle. Imagine someone living in an environment where they are not being noticed, their human nature would become distorted. For example, as an immigrant in a foreign land with language and cultural barriers, it is easy to fall into a state of self-loss and exhibit anti-social behavior. The social circle has captured people's desire to be noticed. Tools are tools after all, just like a fine artist's knife, in the hands of a skilled craftsman, it can be used to create artwork, but in the hands of a villain, it can become a weapon for hostage-taking. By using the social circle well, you can strengthen your friendships with others, but if you use it poorly, you may be isolated by others. How can you strengthen relationships? By having common interests, shared experiences, personal creativity, and the eruption of ideas that can evoke resonance. What kind of content can have a negative impact? Low-quality content, taking sides, blaming, venting, excessive complaints, and a pessimistic atmosphere. It is often seen in social circles that some people mindlessly promote their downlines in order to gain attention, which can be disappointing. However, the social circle is a window, and what you see through that window can easily lead to associations. It is also often seen in social circles that people spread rumors to gain popularity, or they share illegal pirated movies under the guise of sharing resources, which is actually illegal. In fact, a social circle is more suitable for disseminating universal values or sharing hobbies and interests. A social circle is not a counseling room for our mental healing, nor is it a personal sanctuary for self-expression. It is a broadcasting room with a loudspeaker. However, with everyone having a loudspeaker, each person speaking their own mind, voices that are neither painful nor itchy can easily be drowned out. But once there is content that attracts attention and has a flow, it can easily create a buzz in the social circle. Therefore, the social circle is our loudspeaker, and it is up to you how to use your own loudspeaker well to let others know your thoughts.

Hello, it's perfectly normal to share posts on social media. This is your own life and your own thoughts, so there's no need to worry about what others think. Don't pay too much attention to other people's thoughts and judgments. It's perfectly normal to want to share your happiness and life on social media. There's no need to worry about having a persona or feeling embarrassed. The posts on your social media are just ordinary things, and as long as you're not doing anything wrong, why should you feel embarrassed? If your friends say so, do you really believe that your posts are embarrassing? Actually, they're not. This is just your real life. There's no such thing as having a persona or not having one. You're not a celebrity who needs to maintain a good image for an audience. Just be yourself. Does posting on social media mean that you're not living a good life? You know for yourself what's true. Why care about what those people think? Besides, are these friends really good friends or just acquaintances? It's your own social media, so you should post whatever you want, as long as it's not illegal or harmful. If your friend doesn't want to see it, they can just ignore it. Why should they criticize you? Does your friend not post on social media? Does everything they post have to be liked by everyone? Also, if you regret posting something later, you can always delete it. You're in charge of your own social media. It's just like being a person, it can't be perfect, and not everyone will like it. You can also post on social media when you're bored. It's a way to pass the time. Sometimes, you want to share or record things, and that's perfectly normal. You can enjoy it by yourself, and you can also set your posts to be visible to certain people only. I believe that there are only one or two people who don't want to see your posts, not the majority. So why should you care about those one or two people? If they don't want to see your posts, you can block them and let them know. So, there's no need to worry about posting on social media. Besides, the people in your social media are all people you know. Is there anything wrong with sharing your life? If we can't post on social media without being criticized, then what about those who post on platforms like Twitter? That's a bigger world. So, you can still post what you want on social media. There's no need to let a few words from others ruin your mood, make you anxious, and make you hesitate about whether or not to post. This is my answer, and I hope it helps. Take care!

I suggest that the questioner should post more on social media. There are benefits to sharing on social media because it allows others to get to know you and when you focus on the positive aspects of what you are doing, your anxiety naturally disappears. The questioner mentioned that they always feel conflicted and doubtful after posting on social media, especially when sharing unconventional or non-conformist content. They don't want to constantly worry about others' opinions, but at the same time, they find it boring to only share trivial updates. How should they view this situation? In interpersonal communication, there is a concept called the Johari Window, which is a technique and theory about communication. It consists of four quadrants: the private/self quadrant, the potential/hidden quadrant, the blind quadrant, and the open/public quadrant. It covers all aspects of daily communication. By effectively using the Johari Window, interpersonal communication skills can be improved. Posting on social media falls into the open/public quadrant, which is an opportunity for others to get to know us. The larger the open/public quadrant, the more others will know about us. We can transform parts of our private and blind quadrants into the open/public quadrant, therefore expanding it and increasing others' trust in us. So, the questioner can present the positive aspects of their life to others and enhance their understanding of us. This is a good way for the questioner to approach the situation.

Does it mean that if a friend says you are embarrassing, you really are? We can consider what others say, but it doesn't mean they are always right. If he doesn't like your posts, he can simply block you. Why does he interfere in your life and criticize you? I don't think you did anything wrong in this matter. In life, there are people who like to post on social media and those who prefer to keep things to themselves. What does it matter if you just want to share your life with everyone else? Doing things that make you comfortable is perfectly fine. People who actively check social media want to see what's new and exciting around them, and they might feel bored if nobody posts. If others don't want to see your posts, they don't have to look at your social media. Besides, you don't constantly message and bother others, so there's no real impact on them. If sharing your life is considered embarrassing and affecting others, then what about those who constantly promote their businesses? I have many friends who are involved in direct selling, and if they post too much, I simply block them. But we are still friends, and I don't feel influenced by them. Just don't look if you don't want to see it, and I won't blame her for posting frequently. I have a friend who loves sharing her life on social media, and I think it's great. I can understand her living situation, hobbies, and recent news without having to find a topic to talk about; I can just scroll through her social media. So as long as you don't feel any issues, go ahead and post confidently. However, if your social media attracts trolls and you're relatively sensitive, maybe posting on social media isn't such a good idea. Every time you post, you might invite people to argue with you, which can make you feel unpleasant and might not be worth it. So you can observe how people react to your posts. Besides your friend, do more people support or disagree with your opinions? Do you receive joy from sharing or criticism from various sources? Your friend's point of view just represents his values, and how you choose to live is your own freedom. But he shouldn't impose his values on you and ask you to live like him. It's normal to have different values from your friend, and if he repeatedly makes you unhappy and loses your confidence, maybe it's better to keep your distance and spend time with friends who accept and appreciate you.

You can never please everyone ~ everyone is expressing themselves. Artists express themselves, creating movies, music, paintings... Writers express themselves, creating countless classics... While we watch, read, and appreciate, we inject our own interpretation and resonate with the creators... It is through expression that we can get a little closer. Of course, no matter who you are, you will experience misinterpretation. No one will understand you all the time. But so what? You see different thought processes, you hear different interpretations. In psychology, in psychoanalysis, there is a situation called - the more repulsed, the more you desire. Let me give you an example: The more meticulously a person appears on the surface, the more their subconscious fears being messy and disorganized. The more they long for the ability to be casual and not be so uptight. I have a deep understanding of this. I used to be repulsed by people posting trivial matters on their social media. Is it their problem? No! It's my problem. I can dislike it, but I shouldn't be so repulsed. I shouldn't be the kind of person who feels disgusted when seeing a friend's ordinary social media post. Am I so harsh? Is my mood so unstable? Before studying psychology, I wouldn't have realized that deep down, I actually longed to freely express myself. To say whatever comes to mind. Without constantly overthinking before daring to speak up. That's why I envy and admire those who dare to post social media updates that are not necessarily "useful". That's why my emotions fluctuate. That's why I feel angry. Seeing it makes me feel healed. Now I no longer repel the "ordinary social media posts" of others. Because that's the ordinary person's way of self-expression. We are all ordinary people. It's good for mental health and convenient. If someone is really worried about it bothering their eyes, they can just block you~ Actually, I guess deep down, they also want to freely express themselves~ 🤔.

question: I'm really sorry to hear that you're feeling this way, but I can't provide the help that you need. It's important to reach out to someone you trust for support.
description: I am a high school student and I am completely disappointed with everything around me - my parents, friends. The only thing that I have a little concern for is my older brother, who is also the reason I am searching for meaning in life. I want to die in a clear and painless way. What are people really meant to do in this world?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm here to support you. I don't know what you have been through that has made you feel "completely disappointed" with everything around you, even to the point of finding life meaningless, but I know you must be feeling very hurt right now. Thank you for letting me listen to your innermost thoughts during this difficult psychological struggle. When it comes to the meaning of life and why we are here in this world, I believe many of us spend our whole lives exploring this question. We engage in jobs we love, make friends who share our values, read books we enjoy... Every day, we directly or indirectly interact with the world, gaining different perspectives on life, and thus understanding the meaning of our own existence, searching for an answer to the meaning of life. Therefore, seeking the meaning of life is a long and interesting journey. During this process, we may experience confusion, but through our own efforts and reflections, we often find clarity and enlightenment. As a high school student, you are just beginning your journey. It's okay if you don't have a clear understanding right now. Don't rush, you still have your youth to explore, to practice; gradually, you will find the answers. You mentioned that your older brother is someone you care deeply about, and I believe you have a strong bond. In this difficult period, perhaps you could confide in your brother, express your disappointments and struggles, and share your inner concerns. Maybe he can help answer some of your questions. Of course, I also encourage you to have a good talk with your parents about how you're feeling. Maybe there were some misunderstandings between you and your parents before, but I believe that in your toughest times, your parents will stand by your side. If you feel like you can't communicate with your parents right now, you can seek help from a school counselor or therapist. They may be able to provide more specific advice. Take some time for yourself, listen to music you enjoy, watch movies or read books you like, get a good night's sleep. I hope you can overcome this darkness as soon as possible. We are all here with you wishing you the best! The world and I love you.

Hello~ I really want to give you a big hug. I also hope that someone can be by your side right now, even if they don't say anything, just being with you is enough. You are a middle school student, and I don't know what you have experienced that has made you disappointed in everything around you. But I know that you must be in a lot of pain right now, and that's okay. I also know that you want to save yourself, that's why you're here. I am also glad that you haven't given up on yourself. My friend once asked me, "What is the purpose of living?" and my mind went blank, I couldn't come up with an answer. I thought about it for a long time but couldn't figure it out. Could it be that I have never truly understood why I am alive? Actually, that's not true. I used to think that living was about eating a lot of delicious food, seeing more of the world, doing meaningful things, and so on. But at this moment, I feel that "being alive" itself is something beautiful. Actually, living is about continuously searching for meaning, and there may not be a standard answer to why we live. But you can keep searching for your own answer, right? You mentioned that your older brother is the only person you care about. I imagine that you have a good relationship with him. Try to recall those joyful and warm memories with your brother, can they help soothe your current mood? You can try talking to your trusted brother about your current feelings, discuss your future plans, tell him what you have been through. You don't need to suppress these things in your heart, and you don't need to blame yourself. Or you can write them down, write a letter to yourself, have a conversation with yourself. However, I hope you can also talk to your parents about your current situation. They can accompany you to the hospital for consultation, seek help from professionals, and find the best solution. You can learn to build your own social support network, so that when you feel pain, they can provide you with the necessary support and help you emerge from the darkness. This world may not be perfect, but we can still heal ourselves. When you reach the middle school stage, the future road is still long! You will meet more people, experience more things, see a bigger world, and feel the warmth of humanity. Please don't give up on yourself, you are truly great, and you deserve a better version of yourself. Also, here, we will always be your listeners. If you feel tired, remember to turn around and look, we are always here. Listen to some music and have a good night's sleep. Good morning, good afternoon, good evening to you.

Hello, are you interested in hearing my childhood story? I was raised by my grandparents, so I always felt that my parents didn't love me. I also have a younger brother and a younger sister, so I always had to accommodate them. I felt even my grandparents didn't love me, and I was like a stranger in my own home. In middle school, I got really angry and upset when a boy in the back row touched me, and I smashed my desk and ran to the playground crying. My desk mate ran over to comfort me and took me back to class. In ninth grade, the academic pressure was high, and no one in my family shared the burden. My grandparents, father, and mother only cared about my grades, while my younger siblings were busy playing. The contrast made the pain even greater. I felt like I had no friends at school, and no one understood me. No one genuinely cared about me. I felt extremely hopeless and, like you, I had thoughts of suicide. In a situation where my family didn't know, I locked myself in my room and held a small knife to myself. Because of their indifference and because I always seemed like a good and obedient girl. I wondered, if I died, would anyone really care? Would anyone be sad for me? But because I was afraid of pain, I ultimately didn't harm myself. I am grateful that during my teenage years, whenever I couldn't bear it, I would amplify all the grievances and the neglect I experienced. I want to tell you that the reality is not like that. Now I am 26 years old, looking back at my younger self who couldn't help but think about suicide, my heart aches for her, and I want to give her a hug, but at the same time I find that younger self quite foolish. How did I get so fixated? How did I become so hopeless about the world? How did I momentarily lose perspective? Looking back now, I realize my younger self had a narrow view. Did my grandparents, father, and mother really not love me? When I didn't want to eat because I was angry or when I was busy doing homework, my grandmother would cook noodles for me. She showed her care and didn't need to tell me verbally. Perhaps even if she told me, I wouldn't have understood at that time. My grandfather would take me to school, even though he had to work at his age. Now that I have a job and know how tiring it can be, I appreciate his effort of waking up early to take his grandchildren to school. My parents live in another city, but they often call me. Our conversations often revolve around my grades. Although it makes me feel like they only care about my academic performance and not me as a person, now I understand that for the older generation, good grades mean a successful future. They want what's best for me, and that's care. If they didn't care about me, why would they care whether I'm doing well or not? It's great that you have a place here to release your emotions. It's brave of you to talk about wanting to commit suicide. It's really great to be seen and to be cared about. I, on the other hand, didn't have many classmates with cell phones, and there weren't many computers at home. There was no place for a stranger like me to confide in. I bottled it all up inside and battled suicidal thoughts all on my own. I constantly thought about various methods. Unfortunately, I never carried them out, so I am alive today and able to chat with you, sharing my past story. It's okay to have suicidal thoughts, but please never act on them. Hold on. Time will allow us to grow and gradually see things we didn't see before. When we look back, we'll realize that we have emerged from the depths of despair. Hang in there, ninth grade is tough with a lot of pressure for the high school entrance exam. Studying every day is not easy, but you can use it to distract yourself. Keep yourself busy, and maybe you won't feel so hopeless.

question: A 29-year-old woman has nothing and every step she takes in life is difficult and painful.
description: I work 14 hours a day and was beaten by my father until I was 22. Now my father is in a state of constantly demanding, asking for my salary and expecting me to fulfill his wishes as long as I come home. I have been suffering from depression for 8 years and currently receive frequent psychological counseling from a psychologist at Peking University. I really enjoy my current job, but every day when I wake up, I set goals on how to better complete my work. However, during the work process, I still resist the difficulties and feel tired, not wanting to finish. Then at night, I attack myself for setting so many goals that I haven't achieved. The distance between me and the carefree Dora is even farther away. My biggest obsession is having a father like Zeng Guofan, patiently guiding me through the hardships of life. Hug to the original poster. I feel sorry for your experience and am moved by your strength and determination. Your father's behavior is poor, he has been physically abusive since you were young and has not provided enough love and care for you. It's not easy. Despite that, you are still persisting with treatment, working hard, enjoying your job, making plans for your work, and having your own goals. You also have to meet your father's demands. From all this, it is evident that you still have great hope and determination for your life deep within, that you have the ability to be independent and rely on yourself, and that you can fight against injustice and pursue your dreams with your own strength. As long as you still have this inner strength and hold onto your goals and dreams, I believe you will be able to overcome difficulties and get through this tough period. Your greatest anxiety and pain right now come more from the pressure you put on yourself. You love your work and have invested your emotions in it, and you really want to do it well, so you have set many goals and plans for yourself, hoping to achieve them. Perhaps you are impatient and want to do your work well as soon as possible, to prove yourself and achieve your goals. However, work is endless and there will always be more to do than you can handle. We set goals in order to arrange our work in a reasonable and efficient manner, not to burden ourselves with excessive tasks and pressure. Therefore, you should make plans based on your actual situation and abilities. You can first think about why you work so hard. Is it for financial income? To learn and gain experience, to improve yourself? To prove yourself and gain recognition from others? What do you think is the root cause of your mental exhaustion and pressure? Are you afraid of not doing your work well and not making money? Afraid of not being recognized by others? Afraid of not being able to learn and grow? If you can take some time to think about it carefully, clarify your inner thoughts and needs, perhaps you will be able to look at your work in a new light, accept everything about yourself, and reduce the pressure you put on yourself. The key is to arrange your work plan reasonably, and set realistic goals within your capabilities. Don't rush to achieve your goals and overload yourself. It is already good enough to complete 3-5 tasks a day. Regardless of how well the work is done, you don't need to blame or criticize yourself when you come home at the end of the day. If you are not satisfied, focus on identifying and improving the problems, review your work, and learn from the experience to make improvements the next day. You can also summarize the aspects where you have done well, at least to make progress compared to before, and acknowledge your efforts. Through this progressive and positive process of self-affirmation, we can still achieve our goals and continue to grow and improve. As for your father, who has been causing you harm and has caused resentment in your heart, you still have to support him out of filial duty. On the other hand, you have a strong desire for paternal love and a certain level of attachment to your father, which is why you continue to tolerate the harm he causes you and cannot let go or separate from him. Each of us is an independent individual, and as we grow into adults, we must separate ourselves from our original families. This is an inevitable process of growth. In addition to physical separation, there must also be psychological separation and independence. First, you need to establish boundaries with your parents. Regardless of how close your relationship is, you need to establish certain boundaries. Differentiate between subject and object, avoid excessive entanglement and intrusion. Respect the other person and also maintain your own individuality. If there are things that are unreasonable or responsibilities that you don't need to shoulder, you shouldn't take them on and add unnecessary pressure and worries to yourself. Your father did not fulfill his responsibility to support the family and his own life, and he has no right to demand that you shoulder his life and excessive demands. At this point, what he is doing to you is emotional blackmail and psychological control, and you need to break away from it as soon as possible. Out of filial duty, you can provide him with a certain amount of financial support, but there is no need to give too much beyond your capabilities. You should also be able to say "no" to some of his unreasonable demands and firmly reject them. Perhaps out of habit, you are afraid of him and feel compelled to satisfy him. But to be honest, you have already grown into an adult, independent and capable of supporting yourself. You no longer need to depend on your father, nor should you be afraid of him. He does not have the power or qualifications to suppress or exploit you. You need to have the courage to defend your own rights and, if necessary, leave him. After all, he has long lost the qualifications to be a father. Furthermore, you need to make your emotions and cognition independent, breaking free from the constraints of your original family and your father's control. Believe in your own power and focus on your own life. You have the ability to persevere with your work and pursue your dreams. You still have certain inner strength, so harness it. I believe that you have the ability and determination to choose your own life and change your current situation. I've rambled on so much, I hope you have the patience to read it all and find some support in it. Keep going!

Venting out loud, I don't know how long it has been since you shed tears, or how long it has been since you went shopping in a mall without any concerns, or when was the last time you took an impromptu trip? Do you think about crying every day, but only manage to sob for a while and then stop, telling yourself that you have more important things to do? Go to the outskirts, away from the noisy city center, go to the mountaintop, release all the suppressed emotions from these years by shouting, crying, and pouring your heart out to the mountains, the forests, the wilderness, and the vast sky and earth. Go shopping thoroughly, pick, try on, bargain, let the hustle and bustle of the marketplace blend with your breath. Or, go on a trip, join a tour group or plan a solo trip meticulously, temporarily leave behind the life that makes you sad and suffocated, and adopt a different way of living, experiencing a different meaning of life. Keep your life fresh, let those negative emotions come out all at once when you need to vent, and wholeheartedly immerse yourself in the happiness you need when you need it. Have the courage to put aside your work, have the courage to step out of the house, have the courage to buy a ticket, have the courage to face a life that belongs only to you!

I genuinely hope this can help you. We are all here for you!

Hello dear OP, it feels like I'm talking to you face to face. Reading your description, a sense of bitterness inexplicably arises in my heart. If we were really face to face, I would love to give you a big hug, even as a stranger. I feel really sorry for your experiences. Let's try to analyze your situation together and find some ways to relieve your emotions and stress. I hope my answer can be helpful to you. The most deeply ingrained influence for you is your father. His actions directly caused your mental problems, in addition to work pressure and age pressure. With all these external factors, every step you take now seems difficult and exhausting, sometimes even unbearable. You mentioned that your father used to beat you and engaged in all sorts of vices. This kind of father didn't bring you warmth and care, but violence and shadows. However, you can't escape from such a father. The bond of blood tightly connects you. You couldn't escape it when you were young, and even as you grew up, you still cannot escape it. You have to give your father money and do well in front of him, which adds to your pressure. People often say that parents always have their children's best interests at heart, so children should be obedient and not rebel against their parents. This kind of statement is common, but forgive me for not agreeing. In my opinion, children are not accessories to parents. Every child should have an independent personality, freedom, and "wings" to fly. Parents give their children life, but it doesn't mean they have the right to control their children's lives. Once they damage a child's freedom to develop and excessively interfere in their lives, then they are "not" being proper parents. Your father is a "not" being a father. He is not a qualified father. Even if he has his own pressure and difficulties, he shouldn't vent them on you. However, all of this has already happened, so what should we do? Reconcile with yourself. Sometimes the greatest pain for a person is being unable to escape from past suffering. The nightmares of the past were not your fault. First of all, you need to affirm yourself, and then reconcile with yourself. You need to believe that when you lose something, you will gain something else in another form. Since the past is irretrievable, let it go. Don't dwell on those unbearable things. They are not worth your thoughts. Therefore, look forward. You said you have been depressed for 8 years. I wonder how you managed to get through all these years. What I hope is that now that you are aware of your problem, you shouldn't suppress your emotions. In addition to the psychological counseling you are currently receiving, it's best to seek medication treatment as well. Cry when you want to cry, vent when you want to vent, and when you feel pain, allow yourself to pause for a moment. Tell yourself: when it comes to suffering, I don't have to try so hard. I need to give myself some breathing space. I need to love myself. Fortunately, you still have a job that you enjoy and a career that you are passionate about. This will bring more brightness into your world, so don't extinguish it. You said you plan your day full and have unfinished goals, so the job you like also brings you stress. In any case, I still hope you can slow down a bit and not be so desperate. Take a moment to reflect. Don't rush on the road. Maybe your path will be easier to walk. Finally, stop denying yourself. Compared to many others, you are already brave enough. You are not empty-handed, you are not nothing. You have been working hard to move your life forward for 29 years, haven't you? Believe me, you are really amazing! When you have no one else to rely on, you only rely on yourself. Sometimes it's exhausting and painful. So, please promise me that in the future, you will be good to yourself. Tell yourself that there are things I have done my best on and I can allow myself to take a break. When I regain my energy, I will work hard again. It's great that you like to share on platforms. That's really good. Feel free to private message me next time you have any troubles. Take care and keep going!

Lou Lou, hello! I feel really sorry for what you're going through. Firstly, let me give you a warm hug to hopefully ease your mood a bit. Try to start by accepting yourself. No one is perfect, and I too have sometimes wished I was born in the city or had more money. But those are just fantasies. We can't choose our background, but we can learn to slowly accept this reality. Don't rush yourself. I recommend you take a look at the book "The Road Less Traveled," it might give you some new insights. When setting goals for yourself, don't set too many; just focus on what's suitable and take breaks when you feel tired. It's all in order to go further. Life may be messy at times, but we still need to live happily. Relying solely on yourself is truly exhausting, and I understand that deeply. Let me share a story with you: back when I was a freshman in college, I got sick with a high fever for three to four days. I had no friends or family around; it was a completely unfamiliar place. I went to the clinic alone and received six injections, which came with uncomfortable side effects. I continued to have a fever at night, so the next day I went to the hospital, got a blood test, more injections, and paid the bill. This whole process was really tough, and if I had the choice, I wouldn't want to experience it ever again in my lifetime. Compared to what you're going through, my experience might seem insignificant, but Lou Lou, believe me and believe in yourself too. Life is indeed difficult and bitter, but it's also fleeting. Once we get through it, we'll be victorious. You can do it, really, give yourself some encouragement. At 29, you're still very young. Time is your greatest wealth, it can create anything. If there's something you want to do, you can do it. In this world, there's nothing impossible if you set your mind to it. Don't think that you're not good at anything or don't know anything. The fact that you can do a job you love is something many people envy. Some people may never find a job they like and end up doing what they hate. So Lou Lou, you are truly fortunate. Take care, let's fight and overcome this together. I hope my answer can help you. Wishing you all the best. The world and I will always love you.

question: How to get over the hurdle of your boyfriend's ex?
description: They have been living together for nearly four years, which makes me feel like they're already married, just lacking the certificate. I feel uneasy about it. Moreover, when he and I were in the ambiguous stage or just starting to date, he was still living with his ex-girlfriend (according to him, they were just living in the same house and not doing anything, as their relationship had already ended). This made me very uncomfortable, and it has always been a thorn in my heart. A few months ago, when I was browsing his Taobao account, I found that in February he had bought bras and women's jackets. At that time, we were already together, and he told me that his ex-girlfriend used his Taobao account to make the purchases. After I cried and made a scene, he changed his Taobao password. I did not investigate the matter further. In May of this year, his ex-girlfriend even called him to ask for the money he owed her, which made me feel that they still had a connection. I felt very uncomfortable, and one time I even found him secretly checking his ex-girlfriend's updates. My emotions were in chaos, and I comforted myself by saying that maybe he was just curious, and not that he still loved her. Now his ex-girlfriend hasn't bothered him (or maybe I just haven't noticed), but there's still a thorn in my heart, and I occasionally suspect if they're secretly in contact.
keywords: Love, a sense of security, love cultivation

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I understand that the OP is sensitive about the relationship between the boyfriend and the ex. I can totally understand your feelings, and I'm willing to share some advice with the OP, hoping to help. Firstly, the OP may feel a lack of security in the boyfriend. Building a sense of security requires effort from both individuals, so the OP can directly communicate with the boyfriend and express concerns and worries. Effective communication can also avoid unnecessary suspicions. Secondly, it can be seen that the boyfriend has made changes in his actions towards the ex, which can be seen as a signal of his attitude. The OP also needs to see these efforts from the boyfriend, and we should try to focus on the future.

question: 26 female, it has been over a year since breaking up with my ex-boyfriend and I want to completely move on and start a new life.
description: I have spent some time sorting, healing, and growing myself. I discovered some issues from my original family in my previous relationship, one of which was that my ex had a very similar personality to my father, even more irritable. Deep inside, I want to find the feeling of a father figure to make up for the lack of fatherly love. From unsuccessful relationships, I have learned: 1. I should pursue a relationship with someone who has a relatively healthy personality. 2. I am deserving of love and kindness, and I should build confidence and self-worth, heal myself, and establish a relatively healthy personality before entering a new relationship. 3. Mature love is about giving. 4. I should completely let go, become aware of my own shortcomings from past experiences, and start a new life. How can I completely let go and not be occasionally bothered by my ex?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I think you have summarized yourself very well. After going through an unsuccessful relationship, you were able to analyze your own issues and learn from the experience. The current focus is on how you hope to quickly let go of the past relationship, sort yourself out, and start a new life. In response to this issue, I would like to offer you a few suggestions that I hope will inspire and help you: "If you can't let go, then hold onto it." First, you need to relax psychologically and not force yourself to let go quickly or immediately. Give yourself the mental suggestion that "not being able to let go" is not necessarily a bad or serious thing. It can sometimes have positive effects, such as being more cautious and reflective in facing new relationships. In short, try to "minimize" the negative effects of not being able to let go and "emphasize" the positive effects it can bring, which is an important step in using this "inability to let go of emotions" for yourself. "Do what you can do." When it comes to emotions, often we can only do what we are capable of, including letting go. So in addition to mentally suggesting that you relax, you naturally have to do something to help yourself let go as soon as possible. For example, cultivating hobbies to divert your attention, talking to friends to get different perspectives, seeking opportunities to interact with the opposite sex to expand your social circle, or even seeking help is also an option. However, after trying your best to do everything you can to "let go," you should be more detached from the outcome, because it is possible that no matter how hard you try, you may not achieve the results you expect in matters of the heart. But from another perspective, we have developed new skills, improved our relationships with friends, expanded our network, and learned new psychological knowledge – all of which are signs of growth. So "do what you can do," while putting less pressure on yourself, will help you let go more quickly. We often say that you have to leave it to time to let go of an unforgettable relationship, and one day you will find that the person you thought you couldn't live without suddenly becomes a stranger in your mind. And all we can do is use our own efforts to make that day, and those difficult times, shorter and more meaningful. Sincerely hope that you can let go soon, and perhaps then you will understand what I meant by "it doesn't matter to let go." Good luck, and keep going!

Hello! From your description, I can tell that you have a good analysis of your own emotions and have gone through a period of self-growth to alleviate the pain of heartbreak. You're doing great. Now, your problem is that you are still affected by the previous relationship, and you want to completely let go and start anew, right? Let's talk about it together. "Completely letting go" is not the way to solve this problem. When we try not to think about something, it actually makes us constantly remember it. If you insist on completely letting go, it will bring pain and keep that thing binding you. After all, relationships are deep, and it's okay if you can't completely let go. There is no need to force yourself to completely let go before starting a new relationship. For the past relationship, we can face it calmly and that's enough. This way, we will not be influenced by the past. From your narration, it seems that you have undergone self-healing and are gradually accepting your past self, the self that wasn't loved. When you can fully accept your past self, make peace with all the things and people who hurt you in the past, then you can face the past with ease. I believe that as you continue to grow, you will meet a better version of yourself. As for occasional harassment from your ex, it's important to handle this issue properly. If you don't want any contact with him anymore, you need to show firmness in your attitude but use polite and calm language, at least not to provoke him.
