As for his persistent disturbance, you can choose not to respond or pay attention. Over time, he may feel that it's pointless and stop bothering you. Regarding starting a new life, I think you have already started a new life. You began a new life from the moment you started healing and growing after the heartbreak, becoming a different version of yourself from the past. So, please don't rush, and don't put pressure on yourself. Focus your energy and time on self-growth, living your life, working, and socializing. Let everything develop naturally, and I believe that one day you will have a satisfying relationship. In this relationship, you and your partner will rely on and care for each other, becoming better versions of yourselves. The world and I love you. I wish you a happy and fulfilling love life as soon as possible.

It is said that time is the best medicine, but it is indeed not so easy to completely let go of someone. Letting go is indeed difficult because an unintentional moment can easily evoke memories deep within our hearts, especially for some unforgettable things that are hard to forget. Therefore, it is better for us to learn to accept. Even if we meet him again in the future, we will know that it is just a simple segment in our lives, and that we were not suitable for each other, which may cause a slight ripple but will not have much impact on our current life. In fact, from the moment we separated from each other, we have already begun a new life. It is just that some previous experiences have kept us from letting go, so we engage in reflection and self-healing. The questioner has grown a lot from the previous experiences, also understanding what kind of partner they want and what emotional maintenance relies on, but we should not have too high expectations. After all, everyone goes through a process from being immature to mature, so even mature partners will have various problems. Therefore, in the end, we must be mentally prepared. A good partner is not one without arguments, but they will handle the problems that arise and make it acceptable for both parties. Our experience with the other person is the same. Only after really getting along will we understand whether we are compatible or not. Whether we can continue requires mutual understanding, tolerance, and a willingness to change ourselves. Letting go means accepting our past selves, recognizing our own shortcomings, and understanding where the issues with the other person lie. For some people, the past is truly in the past. They have brought us beautiful moments and left us with negative impressions, but we have grown up and can face many things calmly now. The world loves you and so do I.

Friend, hello. From your description, I can tell that you are a motivated and eager-to-learn person. You are aware of your emotions and have analyzed the reasons behind them, which is a good start. However, sometimes we cannot fully overcome these emotions on our own and need someone to lend us a helping hand. Have you ever heard of the Oedipus complex? The Oedipus complex, also known as the Electra complex or Orestes complex, is a term in psychoanalysis coined by Sigmund Freud. It refers to the complex emotions a girl experiences in the third stage of her sexual development, where she develops intense feelings of love for her father and resentment towards her mother. She sees her father as her primary object of sexual desire and considers her mother as unnecessary, often desiring to replace her in her father's affections. This complex can make us seek partners who resemble our father when we grow up, and it seems that many girls' boyfriends have similarities to their fathers. My husband is also very similar to my father. My father smokes, has a gentle temper, and doesn't argue, and my husband is almost a carbon copy of him. It's strange, the feeling of both of them treating me well, even though they don't express it verbally, they both show it through their actions. Finding someone similar to our father is not necessarily a bad thing, and it doesn't mean that a person similar to our father is psychologically unhealthy. It just depends on whether you can accept such a person. When you enter a new relationship, you need to be able to move on from your previous one and accept the new relationship with the best version of yourself to have a chance of finding the best person. It is often difficult for women to move on from a relationship in which they have sincerely invested. If it is not suitable, there is no need to stubbornly hold on to it. You can cherish it as a beautiful memory, as everyone has unforgettable memories in their lives. When we grow old, we can share these memories with our children and grandchildren. Even when we were young, we had our own charm. Keep going, friend. Believe that you can move forward, the world and I love you!

To completely let go of a relationship, time and distance play a big role. Any relationship will gradually fade with the passage of time until it no longer stirs any emotions within oneself. However, in order to achieve this, it is imperative to not frequently contact an ex-partner, occasionally chat, or still see their updates on social media. These little things deepen the connection between each other, making it difficult to forget each other and even maintain a lingering attachment. Therefore, if the original poster has confirmed that there is no longer any connection with the ex-partner, deleting each other and forgetting about them in the dating pool is the best approach. No one has a perfect family background, and we all live our lives with imperfections. However, this is not the most crucial aspect. What matters most is that we recognize our own problems and consciously make changes, no longer walking the same path and becoming wiser. This is how we can free ourselves from the confinement of our original family. Just like the original poster believed they chose their ex-partner because they reminded them of their father, but their father was a very hot-tempered person. So, what kind of problems do you think might arise from being with a hot-tempered partner? Would you both struggle to communicate, with the other only resorting to violence and causing harm to you? I believe that your desire to start a new life is because the feelings brought by the ex-partner were not pleasant. Therefore, when selecting a partner, should you choose someone with a gentle personality and good communication skills? Now that you have realized this, in your future life, you need to tell yourself that you deserve to be treated kindly. Your father and ex-partner's hot temper caused you a lot of pain, so you should find a partner who is emotionally stable so as not to repeat the same mistakes. No one is perfect, we all make mistakes, but that's okay as long as you don't continue to fall into the same hole. The original poster is now able to reflect and learn from their experience, gradually growing. You are learning to break free from the limitations imposed by your original family, not allowing your emotions to control you like your father or ex-partner did. You have learned to live using your intellect. You are right, you deserve to be loved and treated well. Only when you are whole will you attract someone like-minded, leading to a healthy and beautiful relationship, rather than hurting each other and blaming one another. Mature love indeed requires effort. Of course, it is also important for the other person to be able to reciprocate that same effort. Mutual giving is what creates a balanced relationship. If you are the only one giving while the other person greedily accepts, it is not a good relationship and will only make you lose confidence. I believe that a good relationship can bring you confidence because your partner genuinely appreciates and cares for you, making you feel less alone in this life. There will always be someone standing by your side, supporting and encouraging you. When conflicts arise, instead of blaming each other, you will learn to communicate honestly and consider the problem from the other person's perspective. Let the past be in the past. The original family cannot determine a person's entire life. Crying over spilled milk is pointless, but the experience and lessons you can learn from it are precious. Just like the original poster has gained a deeper understanding of love and life, and is evolving towards a better place, that is already enough. Even if you can't completely let go right now, it's okay. People gradually grow and heal. Give yourself some time, be patient, and believe in your potential. You are already doing great.

question: Am I finding it difficult to be self-disciplined because I've gotten used to being lazy?
description: In the past year and a half, I have been wanting to take the graduate entrance exam at the end of this year. However, due to my limited self-discipline, it is difficult for me to go to bed and wake up early without external constraints. My study plan is also hardly implemented. I think it may be because I have already become accustomed to a lazy lifestyle, which is why I lack perseverance in the exam preparation process. I can only focus and study for a short period of time when under intense mental pressure and barely make progress. Is this viewpoint reasonable?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, developmental principles, work and study.

answers.answer_text: Hello, if you have been spending a lot of time on your phone recently, it is very likely that it will become increasingly difficult for you to focus and concentrate on studying. This is because your brain has become accustomed to high-intensity stimulation, and activities like reading, which provide less stimulation, no longer satisfy you. Regarding your difficulty in achieving a consistent sleep schedule and sticking to your study plan, the truth is that the challenge lies more in going to bed early than waking up early. Based on my recent experience, once I start a plan and fill my days to the brim, I often get caught up in one task and keep extending the time allocated to it, ultimately sacrificing rest time. I end up pulling all-nighters and feel tired the next day, which causes me to be unable to complete the plan for that day. This has been the result of my recent practice, and I have come to the conclusion that sometimes you won't know what kind of study plan is suitable for you unless you try it. There is no one-size-fits-all study plan; it needs to be flexible and adjusted based on the daily tasks at hand, gradually refining it to fit your needs. Regarding your description of being able to concentrate only under high mental stress, I don't think this is entirely reasonable. Prolonged periods of mental stress are not helpful for learning; they can instead lead to a dislike for studying. Additionally, it seems that you are not familiar with the categorization of tasks in psychology. Psychology categorizes tasks into four types, and it is clear that you have not prioritized the most important category, which is important and urgent tasks. As long as you lack this awareness, you will not feel a sense of urgency and will develop a habit of procrastination instead of taking immediate action.

question: I feel like my life is a failure, very bad, and I can't find a purpose.
description: I have a severe case of OCD and anxiety disorder. When I was a child, my father treated me very well, and my family also showered me with love. However, he would hurt my mother, even though their relationship seemed fine. I once witnessed him stabbing my mother with a knife, and she was covered in blood. I intervened and ever since then, I started to engage in compulsive behaviors. I also suspect that I have been exposed to drugs through him, so I constantly go to the police station to verify. Even after using testing strips, I still can't rest assured. Later on, when I come into contact with people, I have to change clothes, wash my hands eight hundred times a day. As I grew up, I met a very understanding boyfriend who tolerates my actions. I hit him whenever I want to and often pinch and slap him. Occasionally, when he reacts and gets frustrated, he pulls my arm and worries about my safety. I doubt if he has violent tendencies and constantly seek confirmation from various websites. Everyone tells me that he doesn't and he is very good, but I still ask other people repeatedly. I think I am terrible. Even when I set goals, I still lack motivation. I am afraid to take the medication prescribed by the doctor. I have severe hypochondria and live in constant fear. I feel like I have inherited too much from my parents, being dominant and doing whatever I want. I am always reluctant to do anything and lack enthusiasm for many things. The compulsive behaviors have already had a significant impact on my life. I really want to give myself a break.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, psychological counseling, trauma therapy.

answers.answer_text: Hello: It's not easy! Listening to your description is like being on the scene, and your suffering is not only physical but also mental torture. You have experienced several categories of the five major traumas in childhood: important people using drugs and violence, which can bring great shadows to a child's growth. Your unstable personality and the origins of various symptoms are closely related to these. Analyzing the problem: 1. You have a very severe obsessive-compulsive disorder and anxiety disorder. When you were young, your father was very good to you, and your family also spoiled you, but he would hurt your mother. Their relationship seemed very good, but you once witnessed him stabbing your mother with a knife and she was covered in blood. You stepped in to stop it, and since then you have developed compulsive behavior (growing up as a child who has received love and a child who has not experienced it will have different outcomes. Look at you, you have parents and family who show you "doting love" but also extreme violence in front of you. Imagine which child can handle that. It is the combination of "ice and fire" and is easily explosive. A child's capacity for tolerance is limited; either they love deathly or they are bloody deathly. They cannot bear it. It will transform into an "extreme character." "Anxiety" is the precursor to depression, and "compulsion" is caused by things that cannot be controlled.) 2. Your suspicion of being exposed to drugs from being around him caused you to continuously seek confirmation at the police station, and even after testing with test paper, you still weren't reassured. Later, when you were in contact with them, you had to change clothes and wash your hands eight hundred times a day. As you grew up, you met a boyfriend who was very tolerant of you, and you would hit and pinch him often (violence can be learned. "Drug" is not just a substance for you; it is a "painful memory." You passionately reject this kind of pain in your heart. You detest it and detest the harm it has brought to your family. So you're afraid you might accidentally be contaminated too, so you constantly seek verification and test it to prevent any mishaps. You wash your hands eight hundred times a day, which has turned into a "compulsive habit." Meeting a boyfriend who is so tolerant of you is your luck, but this luck is not always there; sometimes it runs away. He will be there when he can bear everything you throw at him, but what happens when he can't bear it? Do you think he might run away?) 3. Occasionally, when he was pushed to his limit, he would react, and he would grab your arm when you went out in the middle of the night, worried about your safety. He would knock the paper ball out of his hand when you hit his head and so on. You would doubt if he had a violent tendency and constantly seek confirmation from various websites. Everyone tells you he doesn't, that he is very good, but you still ask others repeatedly (because you can't "determine" if a man has a violent tendency. You understand the reasoning, but emotionally you can't understand it. Because you once had such a good father who treated your mother so badly, you witnessed all of it, so you "don't believe" that the man in front of you could love you so much. Therefore, you keep seeking confirmation, keep "testing his boundaries," and as soon as he even slightly deviates from your perception, you "start suspecting" whether he has a violent tendency.) 4. You feel that you are too terrible, even after setting goals, you still have no motivation, and you are afraid to take the medicine prescribed by the doctor. You have severe hypochondria and live in the shadow all the time. You feel that you have too much influence from your parents, being domineering, doing things as you want, always unwilling to move, lacking enthusiasm for many things. Compulsive behavior has already affected your life, and you really want to let go of yourself (yes, you have also realized it. You have learned both the good and the bad from your original family, but you forgot that you are not them; you are just yourself. To understand this simple truth, you need to undergo "psychological healing," you need to take medication in conjunction with a doctor, it requires a two-pronged approach. I can feel your pain and the psychological and life impacts brought by various neurotic symptoms. You are right; you are not letting others go; you are "hurting yourself." It is also a subconscious "revenge" against your parents.) Conclusion: Wishing you happiness and joy! Wishing you to live the life that belongs to you as soon as possible! If you have any confusion, you can private message me!

Title, hello. Understanding your concerns, I want to share some new ideas with you, hoping it will be helpful. You have now clearly realized that you have a problem because it has been affecting your life. Actually, seeing it is the beginning of healing. When we speak out the problems that have been piling up in our hearts, change becomes possible. When we experience some compulsive behaviors, let's not label ourselves too easily. At this time, we are just being cautious and careful to avoid feeling hurt. It simply means that you are being very cautious and careful in using this method to reassure yourself. But you know that you feel like it's excessive. It only shows that you have experienced some unbearable trauma, such as domestic violence and drug abuse from your father. This has made you too fearful. According to Cong Fei from the Talent Education Center, when we imagine that fear to be very strong, even if there may be minor harms that may not actually happen, we become very afraid because that fear is activated. When you become aware of these things, ask yourself, what ways can you use now to protect the parts of yourself that were hurt in childhood? Ask yourself what is different between your current self and your past self? When we believe in our own healing power, both physical and psychological, when we have immunity, we are no longer the child we were back then. We can face it. Compulsive hand washing may help alleviate some of it. Things that could harm you in the past cannot harm you now. However, repeated confirmation can make you feel more at ease, but the more times you confirm, the more it reinforces our negative mental and emotional states. The solution is to seek help from professionals and take medication regularly. In addition, relaxation exercises can be helpful. The specific method is as follows: for example, sit on a chair or sofa, place both hands on the armrests or by your sides, let your shoulders drop, let your arms naturally hang down, let your fingers bend naturally, keep all your muscles relaxed and in a state of relaxation, focus your attention on your breath. Breathe slowly and deeply, aiming for a steady and long breath. Finally, I wish you the best in overcoming your troubles soon.

Honey, I see that you're facing some confusion in your life. You mentioned having severe obsessive-compulsive disorder and anxiety, and your family is not perfect either. It seems like you also feel insecure around your friends. Furthermore, you feel that your life is terrible, lacking motivation, and not following the doctor's advice to take medication. Actually, for diagnosed individuals, regular medication is crucial. Like you mentioned, the compulsive behaviors are already greatly impacting your life, and you really want to give yourself a break. There is still motivation for change within you. You hope to improve yourself. But it seems like you can't help yourself right now. Who can you rely on then? The professional advice from doctors is something you can definitely trust. So, as the first step, you can take medication regularly under the doctor's guidance and seek treatment. If possible, you can also find a long-term counseling therapist for psychological counseling. It's clear that the issues you are facing haven't accumulated overnight, but rather over a long period of time. That's why you may need the support of external professionals to gradually move past this shadow. I hope this can help you. The world and I love you~.

Hello, how are you? It is undeniable that the original family will influence a person's life to a large extent. As you mentioned, your behavior has been influenced by your parents, but the influence of the original family does not represent everything. When you mentioned letting go of yourself, it actually shows that you already have a clear awareness of wanting to change, which is a good thing. So how can you make changes? 1) Step out of the circle of the original family. Your personality is largely influenced by the original family, and even many aspects tend to be consistent with your parents' behavior. Since you are aware of the drawbacks of this situation, you should try to "escape" from it. You can try to leave your parents for a while or live separately for a period of time, interact with people with good personalities, and let them influence you to change the problems you currently have. Personality is something that influences each other. If you really want to change, you can try to make friends with good people and let their behavior subtly change you. 2) Let go of your attachments and don't take things too seriously. There must be attachments in your heart, although I can't say for sure what they are, but I can clearly feel that you have something you can't let go of. No matter what it is, you should try or learn to let go of it. When you look at yourself from the perspective of an observer, you will find that many things are actually insignificant. You are just limited by your current self. Therefore, don't take things too seriously, try to let go, and learn to let go, which will make you feel lighter. 3) Cherish the people around you. Your boyfriend must love you very much. But the problems you currently have will easily hurt him unintentionally. You must sincerely explain your situation to him, and any misunderstandings between the two of you must be cleared up in person. Furthermore, when interacting with the people around you, you can try to let go of your inner conflicts, be more open, and simplify things. Sometimes, when you can't control your emotions, you can try meditation to change your current situation, which will make things much better. 4) Learn to love yourself. You have to love yourself. No matter how imperfect, stubborn, or unsatisfied you are with yourself, you must first accept yourself and then try to change yourself. Nothing can be achieved overnight. You don't need to rush, it's fine to change slowly, as long as you keep changing and striving to become better, you will eventually succeed. I hope my advice is helpful to you. Best wishes!

Hello! From your description, I can tell that you are actually a very fortunate person: 1. Your father loved you when you were a child, although he was abusive to your mother, he loved you very much. 2. Your current boyfriend also loves you, despite the fact that you are abusive towards him, he has always been good to you. You are indeed someone that people envy. But I also understand your pain. 1. The influence of your father during your childhood has caused you to worry about becoming involved with drugs, which has led to compulsive behavior. 2. You can't control yourself and are abusive towards your boyfriend. Let's analyze the reasons together: 1. It is not difficult to see that from your perspective, the influence of your family environment during your childhood was significant. 2. I don't know what you have experienced later on, but obviously the influence from your childhood was deeply ingrained, and I don't know if subsequent educational and other environments have had an impact on you. How can we become better? 1. Accept from the depths of your heart that you have a father like this, it is not your fault, nobody can choose their birth environment. 2. Apparently, you have your own judgment and understanding of your father's state, and I believe you also have an inexplicable desire to escape from it, but you can't get rid of it. 3. In that case, don't try to get rid of it, instead, accept the underlying influences in this environment, while also trying to expose yourself to more diverse and enriching environments to dilute inappropriate thoughts. 4. Try to love the people around you, don't harm yourself and don't harm others.

Hello OP, many psychological pressures can be released by simply speaking out, and it is clear that you have gained an objective understanding of the situation regarding your boyfriend's violent tendencies. Personally, I am not inclined to make a connection between your childhood experiences and your current psychological issues. It's like watching a detective movie and giving commentary afterward, which often feels like hindsight bias. I hope you don't develop a mindset that says, "Because of what happened in my childhood, I am now dependent on others." As adults, we are responsible for our own choices. We can't choose our parents, but we can choose how to face them. The same experiences can lead to different outcomes for different people. For example, some children from broken families may lack security and be more vulnerable or suspicious, while others may mature early, become rational and strong, and even become a source of support for their parents. The difference lies in whether they understand the concept that "the cost of staying silent is not cost-effective." Holding onto past losses and constantly agonizing over one's misfortunes is not helpful. On the other hand, one should focus on how to reap future benefits, quickly bounce back from setbacks, and work harder to move forward. As a mature person, you have a logical mind and believe that you have a clear understanding of your own feelings. I suggest you repay those who have hurt you and express gratitude to those who have shown kindness. If you can't get past your father's hurdle, you can consider taking up taekwondo or women's self-defense and find an opportunity to teach your father a lesson. However, using this as an excuse to confront your boyfriend is not fair. It seems like you're about to lead a good young man astray. Why bother? Furthermore, if you are diagnosed with depression or any other physical brain condition, I strongly recommend seeking medical help and taking medication. However, based on your situation, it doesn't seem likely. Have you ever had an MRI scan at the hospital to check for physical brain abnormalities? Such conditions cannot be effectively addressed through psychological methods alone, so please be cautious.

question: Unsatisfied with blind date partners, always hesitating, how to make choices when it comes to dating?
description: Older woman, many people around her have gotten married, she feels very anxious. She has been on many blind dates, rejecting those who contacted her while it's impossible to ignore those who didn't. She always manages to find faults in those who contact her, either they don't know how to communicate or their conditions are not good. This has made her a bit pessimistic. She wants to find someone who is optimistic and doesn't take things too seriously. She wants someone who can help her when she encounters difficulties, but she hasn't met anyone like that. She just wants both of them to be happy, but some people always complain about their own misfortunes when they meet, which she finds very annoying. Is finding a partner supposed to be exhausting? She used to always think the next one would be better, but there hasn't been anyone who fully meets her expectations, whether it's their conditions or compatibility in terms of personality. Now she sometimes has insomnia and hair loss, feeling a lot of pressure. Because she is dissatisfied with her blind date partners, she is always hesitant and then rejects them. What should she do? She is on the verge of depression.

answers.answer_text: I do not recommend the OP to delay it until later, especially if you have similar values, are concerned about each other, and have feelings for him. If that's the case, then get married. The longer you wait, the worse it will be for you. Age becomes a factor. The OP can lower their expectations and not be too demanding in material conditions. Marriage is for one's own happiness, for both parties to progress together and face future difficulties together. A boyfriend should be your support, but that doesn't mean he is a garbage bin for you to vent your frustrations. He has the right to share your burdens, and you have the obligation to understand and care for him when he is going through a tough time. Instead of feeling down and increasing your own stress, it would be better to take care of yourself, manage your time effectively, and stop waiting for your lover. Can you take the initiative to pursue what you want and become a better version of yourself? Only then will you have more choices.

question: 21-year-old girl, who has experienced domestic violence since childhood, how to comfort the inner child?
description: I have experienced domestic violence since I was young, and my parents are emotionally unstable. I am always easily nervous and have a tense nervous system. I easily fall into negative emotions and always recall the negative memories that have happened since I was young. I even doubt if I have any happy memories. Because I feel like my parents, especially my mother, are always involved in everything I do, and she always makes me unhappy, making my memories unpleasant as well. These days, I suddenly feel the inner child in me, and she always wants to make me unhappy. But I want to get along well with her. I used to rely on my mother a lot, but I would always be disappointed. I have a strong need for reliance, and I always want to rely on friends, constantly seeking validation. I always feel lonely and immature internally, and I always feel like I'm burdening my friends because I always seem to spread negative energy to them. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Good evening, the author sends a hug to you. Childhood experiences are recorded in our hearts. The author feels the helplessness and sadness in your little self. The author wants to say that you, as a child, can believe in yourself and be happy. You have the ability to make yourself happy. "We have the same world, the same mother." Our mother carried us for ten months and nurtured us with her blood transformed into milk. Despite this, mothers often become the people we least like and least want to be around. The author feels that the little child within you is thinking about how to grow up, become strong, independent, mature, and no longer feel lonely. You have a lot of positive energy. Rather than saying that the inner child needs to grow, it is better to say that the current you needs to become your own person. A friend in my circle of psychology often says, "Seeing is the beginning of change." The author says that it is the mission of each person to nurture the inner child and engage in self-improvement in life. However, on the path of self-improvement, there are often accompanying confusion and repetitive turmoil, and it is difficult to break free from them. To find the source of the problem, we must trace our childhood growth process. Only by understanding who we are and where we come from can we better answer where we are going. It must be said that the inner parents and the inner child: 1. The inner parents are actually part of our social personality. 2. The inner child is the part of our own personality. The inner parents are rational, calm, wise, and follow the rules, while the inner child governs our feelings and emotions. If we truly want to achieve happiness, we must achieve a win-win situation for both. When the inner parents follow the rules, they must also meet the needs of the inner child. Only then can we truly experience love, happiness, joy, and success. Faced with the inner child, it seems that we have lost it for a long time. The world is changing, and we are growing up. Many emotions, curiosity, enthusiasm, and exploration that children should have are worn away by us. We walk through the world wearing armor, afraid that others will see our vulnerability and collapse. But can you deny it yourself? You can't. Since this is the case, let us start to nurture ourselves and find the inner child who is full of enthusiasm, dares to speak and get angry, and quickly experiences emotions. Maybe they have been waiting for you for a long time! It's time for you to embark on this journey. It is recommended to undergo hypnotic therapy to heal the inner child. This technique can help you understand where your confusion lies and explore how powerful your inner parents are. Let them rest and release the true inner child, awakening the adult in you. Don't rush the process of growth. I don't know if you are a psychology major or an enthusiast, but regardless of who you are, you can "immerse" yourself in growth here. Wishing you a happy journey of growth! The world and I love you.

There is a saying that men are forever young, and so are women. You are only 21 years old, still at an age where nobody mentions Children's Day. What's wrong with treating yourself like a child? In physics, there is a saying, "When in doubt, use quantum mechanics." In psychology, there is a joke, "When lacking ability, blame it on the family of origin." In fact, most people had an unsatisfactory childhood. Our generation's children generally do not lack financially, but emotionally. Generation gap, lack of parental love, excessive interference, we have all experienced it. When we recall our childhood, instead of saying that we are not good enough, we should say that we didn't do it right, besides the factors of strong parental interference or lack of companionship. Our childhood memories, which were not good, can serve as guidance for our growth by reflecting on what choices we did not make correctly. Use history as a mirror to understand rise and fall, and use people as a mirror to understand gains and losses. The inner child is both a person and history. She illuminates the path for you to move forward, rather than simply entangling you. Turning 20 is also a turning point, a new starting point to achieve one's own life and improve and perfect one's own family of origin. Find something you love, enrich yourself, achieve some accomplishments, and accumulate some income; all of this will make your family better. Dependence is not a big problem either, as humans are social creatures. It is a habit to seek recognition and security within a collective. Share more with friends, there is no harm in communicating. It is also okay to express oneself appropriately, and share the happiness in life, new discoveries in work, new insights from reading a book, or opinions on a movie. Keep going! Make yourself fulfilled, and you will have more and more friends, and more happiness!

@Want to be your baby, through your narrative, I can feel the interference from your parents, as well as your internal disgust and helplessness. As the younger generation with new ideas of the modern era, it is difficult for parents to understand their thoughts. In fact, this is a result of the differences in cognition between different generations, causing confusion. This kind of confusion is something that everyone will face in their lives. No matter how old we grow, it is also difficult to completely free ourselves from the interference of our parents. One of the aspects of growing up is gradually separating from our parents and becoming an independent and complete self, free from their interference. At this stage, you may only be considering certain issues from your own perspective. If you were to consider it from your parents' perspective, they may have such thoughts based on more conservative thinking from their time. It is understandable to have such thoughts. What is important is what is most important to you as an independent individual. What do you want? If you can determine that this relationship is stable and can promote your growth, and both parties are operating this relationship on the basis of mutual understanding and tolerance, then I think you can handle this problem well. You can try to take the initiative to communicate with your parents, express your true thoughts from your heart and most importantly, talk about your feelings. Let them know how their lack of understanding and excessive interference have caused you great pain. Then, explain your reasons to them and hope to gain their support. Of course, if they still cannot accept it, you can firmly state your decision, but remember to maintain a gentle attitude and make it clear that you will take responsibility for your actions. When you bravely express your thoughts, your parents may gradually accept it and reduce their interference. I hope the above advice will be helpful to you.

question: Sophomore year, I encountered a very strange person. What kind of mindset is this?
description: I got to know a guy online these two days who is 11 years older than me. I'm a sophomore in college and he is working in Beijing. We started chatting quickly because we had many common topics. On the second day, he spoke to me in a very indulgent tone and looked through my photo album and old posts. We continued chatting for two more days like that. His tone showed some level of affection towards me, but after I responded to him, he didn't pay much attention to me. However, he still talks to me. I find him very strange, what kind of attitude is this?

answers.answer_text: I am glad to answer your questions. From your question, there are a few key pieces of information: meeting online, being 11 years older than you, starting off with being very indulgent but then becoming cold two days later. [Brief analysis and speculation] Firstly, since you only know each other online and have no offline interactions, you have no idea of what kind of person he really is, and you have no knowledge of his basic information. From browsing his photo album and using indulgent language when chatting with you, it can be inferred that he likely has strong motives and purposes. These motives and purposes are very likely malicious unless you have sufficient reasons to believe that a stranger you met online would care for you out of some kind of goodwill. These motives may include common online scams, deception for sexual purposes, and other malicious intentions. Secondly, the drastic change in his attitude towards you may be due to him feeling cautious and concerned about certain information you shared. I am not clear about the content of your conversation, but it is certain that his initial "liking" was a disguise for some purpose, and once he realized that achieving his purpose would be difficult, he no longer expressed "liking." [Precautions] From your question, it can be seen that you have a limited awareness of the risks online. You need to be cautious and protect yourself when making friends online, especially not disclosing your true personal information to prevent exploitation by criminals.

Hello! You are a girl, right? What is his mentality? It is considered a normal mentality because you can only be considered as online friends! How did you meet? Through a game or some social platform? You can try to guess his situation based on this platform! You just met, but you happened to get along well. He wants to know more about you, so he checked your history. This is also human nature. Of course, he may also have some thoughts about you! You can feel all of this from your conversation, just like you mentioned being indulgent! After you responded, you could feel his change! This is also normal. Your response was obviously negative, so his fantasy was shattered, and naturally, he wouldn't care about you as much anymore! He will still talk to you, of course, because he has nothing better to do and chatting with a younger girl is still okay! Someone like him could be called a creepy older guy if we want to be harsh, and if we want to be nicer, he could just be a normal single man, looking to cast a wide net and focus on cultivating someone! This incident reflects that you still lack experience. Be careful not to be deceived! As you go through more experiences in the future, you will gradually become indifferent to these things! Good luck to you!

From your description, I can sense your curiosity and nervousness as you explore the process of interpersonal relationships. This is an experience that most young people go through. However, it is commendable that you are actively seeking help online to avoid falling into emotional relationship pitfalls. Let's go back to the process of your interaction. There are a few key points that you need to pay attention to: expressing your likes and receiving the likes of the opposite sex can be a happy thing, especially when you also have feelings for that person. When we meet new people, we generally have curiosity, and it is easy to imagine the other person as all good and ignore the bad aspects. Confirming your liking for someone still requires a process. Also, some people like to flirt online, so it is advisable to adopt a cautious attitude towards this. I don't know what your response was, but his subsequent actions can be understood. You haven't known each other for long, and your level of understanding is not deep. After the initial curiosity is satisfied, if the other person wants to develop a romantic relationship, it may require the right timing to naturally progress the relationship forward. It is also possible that he is considering his own environment and is not eager to develop a relationship. Or perhaps he is just a more passive person in relationships, etc. The above is for your reference. I recommend a book to you called "The Five Love Languages." I wish you the best!

Hello. If you are in your second year of college, you would be in your early twenties. If the other person is really 11 years older than you, then they would already be in their thirties. They might already be married and established, or they could still be single. If they are already married and established, and they are looking through your social media posts and updates to gather information about you, it could be out of curiosity or possibly have ulterior motives. As a girl, you must protect yourself. While you shouldn't harbor ill intentions towards others, you should also be cautious of others. If the other person is still single, then they are still available. They could be interested in you out of curiosity or a genuine liking. However, if they stop contacting you afterwards, it may be because they are considering their own age and would prefer to find a partner with marriage in mind. Since you are too young and not suitable for them, they choose to end this mutual interest. Lastly, here are some tips. Think about your criteria for a partner and what kind of person you like. This will help you avoid getting into a wrong relationship. Also, be patient, observe more, wait more, and interact more. Time will reveal one's true intentions. If things don't work out, it's alright. Life is long, you should always look forward and not look back. Lastly, I wish you academic success and that you find a desired husband soon.

A sentence that can be considered a truth in relationships is that if someone likes you, they will make it clear and let you know. They would want to proclaim your relationship to the world and even think about marrying you. Instead of playing games and hiding their feelings. If someone intentionally plays games, it just proves that they are immature and insincere. I have a friend who has a happy marriage. She told me that on their first date, her husband told her that he couldn't live without her. It may have been partly a joke, but his sincerity touched my friend. So, all the chatting, flirting, and physical contact, even if there is some response from him, as long as he doesn't clearly show his attitude, invite you out, and tell you that he likes you and wants to establish a relationship with you, it's all just playing around. By playing around, it means that he may be bored and have a slight liking for you, but it's not to the extent of wanting to establish a serious relationship with you, and he doesn't intend to be responsible for you. Especially when you respond to him, he suddenly starts ignoring you. How can a guy who likes you not respond? He should be excited and eager to talk to you, maybe even willing to fly to your city. Most likely, he doesn't have any thoughts about you, and whether you respond to him or not doesn't matter to him. This is not surprising, as someone who doesn't value you will give you that feeling. His flirting with you is just based on his own needs, not yours. So, what's the point of trying to understand that guy's mentality? A guy who is 11 years older than you has more relationship experience, making it easier for him to manipulate a girl's emotions. Before confirming the relationship, it's best for the questioner not to give away her heart. Just treat him as a normal friend and interact with him accordingly. Friends sometimes chat with you, sometimes focus on their own things. When the other person clearly expresses their seriousness and commitment, then you can respond. If the other person doesn't even have that level of commitment, would the questioner dare to entrust herself to him?

Hello, because you have common topics to chat about, you can quickly become familiar with each other. Through chatting and by viewing your space and updates, this person who is older and more experienced than you will generally have an understanding of your life situation, thought patterns, and values. It's not good to judge his intentions towards you, but the initially indulgent tone may make you happy and bring positive emotions. However, after you respond, he may not pay much attention to you anymore, and there are several possible reasons that you can consider: 1. At the beginning, he did have a good impression of you and expected a continuation, but after getting to know you, he realized that it's not suitable, so he stopped continuing the conversation. 2. Your quick response made him lose interest in the "hunt" and he no longer contacts you. 3. He is skilled and realized that you "took the bait," so he no longer puts effort into it. Regardless of which possibility it may be, I still want to remind you to be cautious about online relationships, especially considering the significant age difference between you two. At your age, with little life experience, you are like a young lamb, while he, with many years of experience in the world, is more like a seasoned hunter. He understands what you need and knows how to approach you from the perspective that will make it easier for you to become invested. At your age, in your second year of college, it's better to go out and play with people your own age! I hope everything goes well for you!

OP, hello. Nowadays, with the advancement of the internet, we are getting to know more and more people online, but we actually have very few close relationships. We get along with each other because of common interests and shared hobbies, which is a good thing. A person you met online who is 11 years older than you and shares common interests, talks to you in a somewhat indulgent tone, and shows clear ambiguity. This person's psychological basis is based on a sense of playfulness and novelty. As a sophomore, you are still in a state of incomplete physical and psychological maturity, and you are also in the stage of adolescent development, which makes it easy for you to find the information from the external world refreshing. This person's attitude may change later on after you respond, perhaps because they are aware of the distance between them and your age, or for other reasons, there is no need to care too much. Everyone should have a sense of self-protection, not just in the present, but also in the online world.

question: Why do I care so much about other people's attitudes towards me?
description: Because of past traumatic experiences, I have social anxiety and even some learned helplessness. In my daily life and work, I find myself very concerned about how others evaluate me and their attitudes towards me. I am highly sensitive and cannot tolerate negative attitudes such as attacks, hostility, denial, questioning, contempt, and disdain from others. Whenever I encounter such situations, I easily get provoked, become emotionally agitated, and want to fight back. I also feel deeply hurt, like I have a fragile heart. This is particularly evident in a workplace environment, where I am very sensitive, and my emotions and nerves are constantly strained. It feels like any minor friction could make me lose my temper with my colleagues. Everyone thinks I have a bad temper. Actually, I am very distressed. Who doesn't want to harmoniously coexist and enjoy work in their surroundings? At the same time, I am also very anxious about damaging my relationships with colleagues, creating negative impacts on myself, and hindering personal growth. Someone told me that this is because I have expectations for the external environment. I have realized that I constantly lack a sense of security and belonging and I am also very eager to gain recognition and respect from my surroundings. I don't know if it's because of these reasons. I would like to ask for advice from you teachers. Regarding my current mindset, why am I like this? What can I do to help myself in this situation and mindset? Thank you all!

answers.answer_text: Hello, after carefully reading your question description, it appears that you have been living in a state of insecurity, which has caused your personality traits to become sensitive and vulnerable. Your daily life is like a rabbit constantly on alert, easily startled by any movement and always on the lookout for unnecessary stimulation. Although this lifestyle makes you uncomfortable, it has been a form of self-protection for many years, shielding you from further pain and distress. However, it seems that this protective mechanism is no longer serving you as you have gradually grown and now find yourself in awkward situations because of it. You desire change. It is certain that your patience for self-awareness and courage to constantly challenge and change yourself are commendable. I would like to provide some inspiration through the following aspects: [Do not perceive "every little movement" as a threat to oneself] If you want to make internal changes, the simplest first step is to reevaluate external judgments and perspectives because inner growth is a slow process, and cognitive changes cannot happen overnight. However, by reconsidering others, you can quickly learn ways to dissipate negative emotions, laying a solid foundation for reconstructing new beliefs. You may interpret others' opinions as attacks or criticisms towards yourself, but it is important to understand that many people carry psychological trauma and may either project it onto others or silently bear the burden. The "opinions and judgments" that make you uncomfortable, are they really directed at you? This is worth questioning because in reality, others are often reacting to particular viewpoints or circumstances, which most of the time have nothing to do with you, even if it involves your ideas. More accurately, others often express dissatisfaction or disagreement due to previous bad experiences or traumas that have been triggered in the current situation; they are actually directing their hatred towards their own inner resentments. [Try the "three-minute" cooling-off method and avoid communicating with others when in a negative emotional state] Of course, reevaluating others' opinions and judgments does not mean that you will not experience negative emotions. When faced with unpleasant remarks from others, it is advisable to employ the three-minute cooling-off method. Quickly remove yourself from the conflicting situation, take a few deep breaths to adjust and alleviate your inner emotions. Once the point of emotional outburst has passed, it becomes easier to calm down. At this point, you can engage in face-to-face conversations without encountering much awkwardness. [Stay committed to continual self-awareness and self-exploration] In your question, I can see that you have already developed a good level of self-awareness and made discoveries about your own situation. I hope you will continue to persist because self-awareness is the key to personal growth. Nevertheless, it is a slow process that requires everyone's perseverance and endurance. If possible, I would suggest seeking a suitable psychological counselor on the platform for long-term consultations. With the assistance of professionals, you can achieve faster and better self-awareness and exploration.

Hello, if there are 84,000 people in the world, then there are 84,000 versions of you in their eyes, but which one is the real you? First, an event is just an event and its occurrence is neutral, unrelated to emotions. Separate emotions from events. We often start telling stories in our brains because of one thing. Let me give you an example. "Today, you rushed out without putting on makeup. You went to a restaurant to eat, and sitting at the next table were a man and a woman. They looked in your direction from time to time, whispered something, and occasionally laughed." What would your mind think? "What are they laughing at? Is there something on my face that I didn't clean?" "These two just want to show off their love. I'd better change tables so I don't have to see them."... Many thoughts like this arise. And why does this happen? It's because there are emotions and thoughts behind our actions. If we can separate events from emotions, the situation will be completely different. When something happens, we say to ourselves, "Yes, I see this thing, it did happen, and I allow its existence. I also allow myself to vent. And I can control my emotions. I can choose a more beneficial emotion to deal with this matter." First, acknowledge that you have seen the event and respect your emotions. It's okay to feel bad, it's okay to have emotions, respect them all, and then tell yourself, "Yes, I can face it with a better emotion." Second, we project our emotions onto others, and then others treat us based on the emotions we project. This becomes reality, it becomes your experience. To put it more simply, your reality is created by yourself. Something happens, you think others look down on you, but in fact, others didn't think that at the beginning, but if you think that for a long time, it will cause others to truly look down on you. After doing something, you can say to yourself, "I am just expressing my true self. How others perceive me is just their version of me, and their version is not the real me. Let it be, let them think whatever they want." You can also give blessings in advance to an event. You can say to yourself, "Thank you, let this matter go smoothly, my relationship with XX is getting better, and I feel that others appreciate me, even if they don't say it on the surface, I can feel their appreciation for me." Doing this will give a positive label to the event and the relationship. Third, relax and accept your emotions, love yourself. Loving yourself is not just about giving good things to yourself, but more importantly, accepting your emotions and everything about yourself, refraining from criticizing yourself. When you have emotions, accept them, feel them, and calmly say to the emotion, "Hi, you've come, I feel you, I fully accept you, I accept your current existence," instead of saying to yourself, "How can I be like this, I should..." Emotions and events appear in a cycle, appearing repeatedly, because we resist them. The more we resist, the more they persist. Until you see it, feel it, stop resisting it, only then can you truly experience it. I suggest doing more meditation and redirecting your attention back to yourself.

Hello, we are all influenced by external factors, but it seems that you are more affected. Your past traumatic experiences have made you feel like you have social anxiety disorder. [Social anxiety disorder refers to the persistent and intense fear and avoidance behaviors in one or more interpersonal situations. The object of fear can be a specific person or group of people, or it can be quite generalized to include everyone except for a few close friends and family members.] I'm not sure which one of the above situations you belong to! But I used to be afraid to talk to strangers, especially in crowded situations. I was even more afraid of people I barely knew. Many times, I felt like a hedgehog, hoping to protect myself, but at the same time, I wanted to be accepted by people around me. Little did I know, I had scared away the people who wanted to care about me with my spikes. Whether it's social anxiety or social disorder, I think it's a serious problem because we can't live in isolation from society. I suggest you seek professional help from a mental health counseling agency for professional treatment. I hope this can help you.

Hello. Friend, I am somewhat like you. We are both sensitive individuals. In fact, we should pay more attention to ourselves in our work. Perhaps you can focus your attention on your own work. Whenever there is an emotional change, you can jot it down and see the cause. Does it correspond with objective facts? This way, gradually, your perception of the people around you will be different!

question: I enjoy the feeling of being abnormal.
description: I am aware of my confused behavior and I know that having a "perverted" mentality is not a positive mindset. However, I enjoy this perverted psychology. When I see the word "perverted," I know what kind of person I want to become. Yes, I like it, it's awesome. The reason is that I believe being perverted can become darkness, so I am no longer afraid of darkness. Haha, it's my foolish idea, but it has indeed given me the courage to face things that I've never dared to face before... to become the kind of perverted that scares others!

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, have a warm hug~ OP is afraid of darkness, so they hope to become darkness themselves, so as not to fear darkness anymore. OP has twisted thoughts because they are also afraid of being twisted. In psychology, being twisted refers to abnormal manifestations of psychological factors such as perception, thinking, emotions, intelligence, thoughts, and personality. There are many types of twisted or near-twisted psychology, such as hallucinations, hypnotic states, sleepwalking, sexual perversions, and various mental and neurological diseases. From this perspective, OP really doesn't need to worry about becoming twisted. Unless they have experienced severe trauma or long-term suppression, it is generally impossible for a person to suddenly become twisted. Moreover, the best way to combat fear is to face it directly. Twisted behavior is not as terrifying as we imagine, and it can be cured through professional psychological treatment. In daily life, we can also pay more attention to our mental state and emotions, so that our psychology can be in a relatively stable and healthy state. Take care~.

question: I am someone who seeks treatment when I am sick, but why do I become resistant after depression?
description: I am someone who seeks treatment when I am sick, but now even though I know it, I really dislike hospitals and doctors. I know it's not the doctors' or hospitals' fault, but I may dislike going out and not wanting to go to work. Still, I can't bring myself to give up social interactions and be alone. Nowadays, I often seek medical advice online. The doctor said they hope to see me at the outpatient clinic next week.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's clear that you are someone who takes responsibility for your own well-being and believes in seeking treatment when you're ill. When it comes to going to the hospital, it's understandable that everyone might feel uncomfortable there because the hospital environment constantly reminds you that you're a patient. This reminder can be a blow to our self-esteem. It's normal for everyone to experience feelings of depression or low mood, and what we need in those times is support and help. Many of my visitors don't like the atmosphere and environment of hospitals, so if you feel that way too, you can try finding a treatment room that is not in a hospital. Keep up the good work!

question: 30-year-old woman, why can't every relationship be long-lasting?
description: I am a woman who is 30 years old. Every time I have a relationship, it doesn't last long. I lack a sense of security, so I often message others, worrying about this and that. I don't have confidence and fear that others won't want me. As a result, there are no positive outcomes.

answers.answer_text: Hello! @ Whether it's love or other interpersonal relationships, the success or failure of maintaining the relationship depends on both individuals. However, we cannot change other people, but we can change ourselves. It is a good thing that you are looking inward for the reasons, reflecting and approaching the situation objectively. However, because your description is short, I don't know your understanding of this distress, and what understanding you have about the situation. @ I don't know if you are like me, but I always feel that as I grow older, especially in relationships, no matter how different the people I meet are, it always ends up developing into the same patterns as with someone from the past, or always falling into the same pit. There is a concept in psychology called "self-fulfilling prophecy." It means that everyone tends to summarize some beliefs based on past life experiences and then unconsciously develop according to these beliefs, which eventually become treated as prophecies. It's like the behavior of labeling people; regardless of whether the description is positive or negative, the labeled person tends to develop towards fitting the label, or it's like a psychological suggestion, thinking that it will mess up, therefore being nervous, anxious, and causing the prophecy to come true. ○ Moreover, people often unconsciously strive to fulfill it to experience control over certain aspects of life. << Whether it's external comments or past experiences, they are not as important as beliefs. Since you asked this question, I believe you still have hope for love, of course, for a long-lasting love. Perhaps you need to experience the definition of love, the art of love through life or books, and then look back to assess previous losses. << You can compare past romantic experiences to see which patterns you have repeated that have led to relationship breakdown. After all, many people's romantic tragedies come from the influence of their own relationship patterns. Good luck! Learn how to love in order to attain lasting relationships.

Hello! You really want to have a long-lasting and stable relationship, but you always fail to achieve it. There are a lot of worries and anxieties, afraid of being abandoned. Although you are not aware of it consciously, the subconscious message you convey to the other person is "you will eventually abandon me", so the other person conspires with you to break up in the end. Then you will once again say to yourself that I really can't establish a long-term relationship with others. This cycle repeats, making it harder to break this established pattern. You need to carefully look back at your feelings in each relationship, what is this feeling? What are your worries? Afraid of being abandoned? Worried about the other person's safety? Feel that the other person is better than yourself? Or any other specific feelings? Have you had similar feelings before? Where do these feelings come from? Many of a person's initial feelings are related to their mother. You can also take a look at your interaction pattern with your mother, especially whether there are many unclear boundaries and influences on your current life. Are the feelings of worry in your romantic relationships related to the feelings your mother has given you? In addition, take a look back at the relationship patterns of important family members, such as parents or people who were close to you during your upbringing. These can all affect your sense of self and interpersonal interaction patterns. One more thing, you mentioned that you often send messages to the other person, it sounds like one is chasing and the other is escaping. What you desire is a deeply integrated relationship, without distinctions between you and the other person, with many expectations and dependencies on your partner. But actually, for two people to build a relationship, they first need to be independent individuals, which means having their own subjectivity and boundaries. Start by differentiating your feelings and gather the ones that belong to you. Best regards, Rongxin Psychology, Liu Mi.

question: 16-year-old girl, recently, has been feeling low and numb for the past two months, and has lost her appetite a bit.
description: Previously, I used to fall asleep within the specified time, but since the beginning of July, I have been experiencing insomnia and only slept for four hours consecutively for two weeks. At that time, I was feeling really down. Towards the end of July, I started to lose my appetite and became irritable. I would get angry for no reason. Recently, I feel like I have no appetite to eat anything and I don't feel like talking either. But I feel really lonely and there's no one I can talk to.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, disease diagnosis, treatment methods

answers.answer_text: OP, thanks for inviting me. From your description, I can see that you have a keen awareness of your body and emotions. You are able to clearly see the changes happening within yourself and know to seek psychological help, which is something that most 16-year-old girls may not be able to do. Based on your description, the major changes started in early July. I wonder if anything important happened during that time? Even if nothing specific happened, even the small change of going from school to being at home during summer vacation can have a significant impact on our routines and state of mind. When you mentioned feeling lonely, it conveyed a message: despite experiencing various difficulties, you cannot share these problems with the people close to you (such as your parents). You have to face everything alone, feeling helpless, like being stranded on a deserted island. My suggestion to you is to first seek help from a hospital. Professionals should handle professional matters. Your physical symptoms and emotional expressions first need a professional evaluation. Based on the assessment and diagnosis, the doctor will advise whether medication is necessary. Secondly, you can seek help from psychological counseling and confide in a counselor about things you can't discuss with your loved ones and friends. You can seek assistance from a teacher at your school's psychological center. They have met many visitors of your age group and can provide the support you need. If the school's psychological center is not available during the vacation, you can also search for a counselor or listener on a platform that you feel comfortable with, to accompany you through this difficult time. In addition, I'm sure you have tried many other ways to feel better. Record the actions that have helped you, repeat them, and document them. Try to help yourself. Wishing you the best.

Thank you for your trust. 1. At the age of 16, during the rapid period of physical and psychological development, there are things that you can't understand on your own and you don't know who is the right person to talk to, which can easily make you feel lonely. In normal circumstances, academic pressures can also be heavy, and if you can't receive appropriate understanding from your parents, you may feel like you are fighting alone. Therefore, you need friends of the same age. 2. Being a girl and based on your description, it seems that you have a more delicate personality, which makes it easier for you to be sensitive in interpersonal relationships and can also make it a bit difficult for you to make friends with peers. 3. Your insomnia has lasted for nearly a month and you haven't been able to improve it through your own efforts. It is recommended that you find a trusted counselor for face-to-face counseling and also try to spend more time with peers.

OP, or if you have been in the same environment for a long time and lack freshness, you may inevitably feel that life is dull and tasteless. Poor sleep and mental health can easily lead to loss of appetite and worsening mood. Maybe you can try to relax your mood, go out for a walk, participate in some activities, or go to the gym, swim, etc., to release negative emotions, and exercising more may also have a fatigue-assisting sleep effect. Perhaps you can also do more things that interest you in your daily life, find your own hobbies, which can help make your life more fulfilling and possibly make you feel more comfortable. If you feel lonely, maybe you can start by communicating with your parents and talking about your frustrations and distress. In addition to parents, there are other family members. After gradually getting used to communicating with others, maybe you can take the initiative to chat with classmates and invite them to hang out, which can also promote your friendship. Good luck!

question: I want to study and read more books, but I can't finish reading them. What should I do if I can't calm down?
description: Although I am a beginner, I still have an eager heart for learning sometimes. I hope to study well. Whenever I want to learn, my mind becomes chaotic and I can't focus. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, personality traits, self-development, work and study.

answers.answer_text:
Let me tell you two stories. The first story is one that I heard from Teacher Huang Zhangjin. He said that during the Sino-Vietnamese border war in the 1980s, many soldiers who had stayed in the frontline bunkers for a long time could recite the instructions for using medicated oil by heart. The instructions on the bottle were printed in incredibly small letters, with nearly 2000 words packed onto it. Some soldiers also memorized the instructions for skin ointment, which only had about 400 words, and they could recite it backwards. It was truly impressive.

The second story happened in 2008 when I took a train from Changchun to Wuhan. I was on a green train, which took 39 hours to reach the destination. It was my first time on such a long train journey, and I was alone and introverted. There were no beautiful women around to strike up a conversation with, and even if there were, I wouldn't have dared. Back then, mobile phones didn't have as many functions, and internet access wasn't as easy as it is now. Therefore, those 39 hours were truly arduous. At first, I could still enjoy the scenery and sleep a bit, but as time went on, I became increasingly bored. I had brought only one book with me, "Research Methods in Psychology." Just by looking at the title, you know it's a dry book. When I couldn't bear it any longer, I finally took out the book and started reading, surprisingly finding it less boring and even engaging. By the time I got off the train, I had finished several chapters. In the past, the basic contradiction in our mental life was between the growing demand for mental stimulation and the scarcity of activities to satisfy it. Now things are different – a smartphone can solve this contradiction, offering countless ways to pass the time. So, I had a revelation – if I want to read more books and learn more, I need to create an environment that is boring enough to make me crave reading and studying as a way to kill time. Though it may sound extreme, the results are remarkable. So, how can you achieve this? It's actually very simple. Phase 1: Bring the book you want to read, but leave your computer and phone behind. Go to the library or any other suitable place for studying. Limit your water intake to avoid going to the restroom, and set a small goal for yourself: "I, XXX, will sit here for three hours." During these three hours, you don't have to study at all – that's not a problem. But remember, you absolutely cannot do anything else, just sit there and endure it. Soon enough, your instinctual resistance to boredom will make you start studying. Phase 2: For this phase, you don't need to go to the library or leave your computer and phone behind. Anytime you want to start studying or working, apply the principle of "for the next period of time, I will only do this one thing, even if I don't do it, I will sit here without doing anything else" – don't strive for perfection, just remember, don't do anything else. Based on experience, after a while of feeling bored, daydreaming, and being distracted, you will return to focusing on your current study material. We often think that we need to calm our minds before we can read, but that's not the case. This method will force you to start reading with an extremely restless mind, and eventually, your mind will calm down. Interested friends can give it a try.

question: Are people inherently evil from the beginning?
description: I have an irresponsible mother who has never been married. She found a house that she liked and borrowed money from relatives. It should be a considerable amount. She acts pitiful and destitute when she's outside. And those relatives who lent her money are probably not happy about it. Their attitudes towards me have also changed for the worse. Just the other day, my uncle inexplicably yelled at me. They have all helped my mother, so they feel entitled to yell at me. I'm actually very helpless. I don't even live in the house my mother bought. I'm sure my mother has complained to those relatives about her hardships and used me as a scapegoat. I know that my mother always plays these tricks, seemingly good to everyone's face, acting like a saint, but actually using me as a shield behind my back. Those relatives, on the surface, want to help my mother, but deep down, they're all afraid that my mother won't be able to repay them. They see that my mother is weak and can't vent their anger on her, so they vent it on me. I want to say, "Get out of here, all of you."

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a big hug. From the description, I understand that you strongly disagree with your mother's behavior and feel that what she is doing is wrong. At the same time, relatives sometimes get angry at you because they borrowed money, and you don't know what to do. 【A bit of analysis and advice】1. When it comes to resolving problems between parents and children, communication is usually the first step. After all, mothers still have some concern for their children. Although you are ashamed of your mother's behavior, it may be helpful to understand her thoughts through communication. Find some time to sit down calmly with your mom and express your dissatisfaction with her behavior. Even if the problem cannot be solved, it can make you feel better. 2. In the long run, you may consider seriously studying and improving your life, and then try to choose to live in a city far away from your relatives, which will help you get rid of these troubles. I hope this advice will be helpful to you.

question: Met online and have been chatting happily. Is online dating reliable?
description: We met online and had a great time chatting. We exchanged photos and were happy about it. We have been chatting online for over two months. He updates me about his work schedule and tells me what he ate for lunch. Gradually, our relationship became closer, and we developed feelings for each other. He expressed his liking towards me and we started video chatting. He would share his cooking live streams, and I feel that his life is simple yet meaningful. Later on, he started video calling me every time he goes to work and finishes work, and even during his lunch break, he would spend 2-3 minutes video chatting with me. He mentioned that we should meet in person, and he sees me as his potential marriage partner. He wants to have a good future with me, and he tells me every day how much he loves me and misses me. Sometimes, we would talk about previous relationships and matters related to romantic relationships. However, when it comes to discussing romantic relationships, I feel scared and anxious. He mentioned that after we meet and establish our relationship, we can go on trips together. But I feel afraid and worried that he might be dishonest about his feelings or that he could be an online scammer. I don't know what to do, but I have grown accustomed to this person over the past few months.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP: The internet has indeed brought us a lot of conveniences and changes in our lives, including dating. However, the internet is virtual, and we cannot fully trust each other without actually meeting. So, I think your concerns are very necessary in this regard. Let's talk about your relationship: you have known each other online for more than two months and have had enjoyable conversations. He keeps you updated on his work, what he eats, etc. There is mutual attraction and you have both expressed liking each other. He always wants to video chat with you, even during his few minutes of lunch break. But whenever you talk about gender relations and being together in the future, you feel fear and afraid of being deceived. So, OP, have you ever been deceived or hurt by someone in relationships or other aspects before? Because chatting normally with each other but feeling fear when it comes to gender relations and defining the relationship might be triggered by recalling some unpleasant experiences and creating an instinctive reaction. If it is indeed because of past experiences, OP should face this issue head-on. Take some proper psychological tests and analysis to overcome the fear in your mind so that you can better face life.
