Of course, if you are simply afraid of the internet's unreliability, afraid that the other person is not sincere or has ulterior motives, there is no need to be overly scared either. Because we are currently in a society governed by the rule of law, as long as you learn to protect yourself and have your own judgement, there shouldn't be any major problems. For example, when you first meet the other person, you can bring your friends or best friends along and choose relatively safe public places. Avoid being alone or engaging in intimate activities when meeting for the first time because there is a difference between the internet and reality. You need to further understand the other person in real life to avoid being deceived. If the other person truly likes you, they will surely understand. As for going on trips after defining the relationship, I think the condition is that you have lived together in real life for a period of time before making that decision. Otherwise, if you go out together without truly knowing each other, you won't have anyone around to ask for help in case of an unexpected situation. I hope these suggestions can be helpful to OP, and I also hope that OP can find happiness. You are a good girl who deserves a beautiful love.

Hello, dear reader. I can understand how you're feeling right now, and I genuinely hope that my words can help you. Here's a brief summary of your situation: You met an online friend and have been chatting with him for two months. You've exchanged photos and had video chats together, and you both have developed feelings for each other. Your conversations have become increasingly personal, including discussions about past relationships, gender dynamics, and the future. However, because you met online, you feel unsure and are afraid that he might be a scammer. When it comes to online relationships, many people's first reaction may be to assume the other person is a scammer, which shows that our awareness of safety has increased. But is online dating reliable? That's a difficult question to answer. This is true for any kind of relationship, even those formed in real life. Nowadays, our lives are fast-paced, and our social circles are either large or consist of the same people. Online dating can be a great way to meet someone new and interesting who shares your interests. However, we should also be cautious. Whether we meet someone in person or online, we should always approach new relationships with caution. People are always the most reliable and the most unreliable factor. So, what can we do when it comes to online dating? Take it slow. Slow down a bit and don't place too much trust in your excitement and the rush of falling in love. We all want to be loved, and if someone often shows you care and tells you sweet nothings, it's natural to be easily smitten. But at this point, pay attention and understand his motives and character. I agree with the saying, "The person who loves you will make sacrifices for you." The simplest way to determine this is through his actions. Are his words reflected in his actions? Take the time to understand his character before committing to a whirlwind romance. Take it slow and protect your wallet first. If money matters frequently arise during your conversations, be cautious. Don't impulsively risk your resources on an uncertain future. Take it slow and evaluate his character. Assessing a person's character and values will determine if you can have a harmonious relationship in the future. When evaluating his character, also consider his identity. Not everything you see online is necessarily true. If possible, meet in person to confirm his identity and, if you can, get to know his friends as well. It is often said that having a meal together reveals compatibility, which is true. After meeting and interacting in person, if you feel compatible, then decide whether to continue the relationship. Of course, safety is paramount during the meeting. Choose a daytime meeting in a crowded public place to ensure your safety. Once you're certain that he is reliable, you can feel at ease. Wish you a happy life!

Seeing words is like seeing a person face-to-face. The question of whether online dating is reliable or not is actually more about whether the person themselves is reliable or not. The OP has been chatting with the online friend for more than two months, having a great time. From the beginning, they have exchanged photos, report to each other every day, and even had video chats, expressing affection. But in this process, how much do you really know about him in real life? The OP feels conflicted. On one hand, they have become accustomed to this person, but on the other hand, they are afraid that maybe he is an online scammer. Online relationships are mostly from the virtual world, and what you see is mostly what they want you to see. What is he like beyond the camera? So, it's important to be cautious. I suggest the OP: 1. Observe and understand more, try not to meet in person too easily. Even if you do meet, don't easily go on trips alone with him. 2. If you choose to meet, protect your personal safety and assets. Don't lend money to him easily, and don't meet in secluded places alone. It's better to have a friend accompany you and meet in crowded public places.

Whether someone is reliable or not is not absolute. But if two people are aiming for marriage, they can be tested through many practical things: 1) If you want to meet, you can go with good friends and meet in public places. In any case, the first meeting should not be too intimate because there are too many unknowns. 2) Besides talking about love, it is also important to talk about work, various friends around you, each other's families. You need to see this person through more people and things, whether your views on life and values are consistent, and so on. 3) If you are purely talking about feelings and not discussing marriage, it is better not to have any financial transactions until you have enough trust. 4) Without enough trust, do not accept individual appointments with the other person, and definitely do not go on trips together. 5) You can look at each other's identification documents, ID cards, work permits, and find out the truth from multiple sources. 6) Going through things together and discussing matters will make it easier to see a person clearly. In short, prioritize mental communication and put physical contact afterwards. Only with sufficient mental communication, will it be easier for you to judge. Best wishes.

OP, hello! I understand your concerns and I hope my answer can provide you with some help. People we meet online indeed have an element of imagination. We tend to attach positive imaginations to people we meet online, but whether they are true or not remains to be seen. Based on your description, the person you are talking to is indeed a very warm-hearted person, which is why you have developed feelings for him. If you feel attracted to him and you can't determine for sure that online relationships always lead to deception, why not try meeting in person? If we are eventually going to live together, we must transition from virtual communication to real-life interaction. OP, you can try spending more time with him offline. Gradually, those elements of imagination will diminish, and you will see a more genuine version of him. At that time, it won't be too late to make a decision. In fact, I know some couples around me who met online. Some became friends on QQ, others met on dating platforms, and now they have children and live happily. The internet was just the platform where they met, but it was deep offline interaction that allowed them to get to know each other better and ultimately come together. Therefore, OP, you should determine your relationship based on the time you spend with him in real life in the future. Life ultimately returns to reality and must withstand the test of reality. I wish you all the best (*￣︶￣).

Hello, after chatting online for over two months, you have a great time and the conversation feels like being in a romantic relationship. However, you are also worried that this might not be reliable and whether you can trust a relationship formed through the internet. First and foremost, online acquaintances are just one way of meeting friends, similar to being introduced by offline friends or colleagues or meeting at social gatherings. This method indeed carries some risks, but so does meeting people offline. Therefore, it is not appropriate to judge the reliability solely based on the way you met. Secondly, the term "reliable" has different definitions in different people's minds. Some consider wealth as reliability, some consider frequent companionship, and others consider sincerity, and so on. What is your definition of reliability? Lastly, once you know the definition of reliability, how do you judge it? For example, if wealth is considered reliable, how much money is considered reliable? If frequent companionship is considered reliable, is it twice or three times a week? How can we truly determine a person's sincerity? Is speaking the truth at all times enough to be considered sincere? Once you understand your own definition of reliability, it is necessary to establish evaluation criteria to make it more clear. Best wishes, Karen.

Hello~Is online dating reliable? Generally speaking, it is not reliable, although some people do find true love through online dating, but the probability is low. It is normal to worry whether he is a scammer or someone who plays with emotions. This is the pressure and responsibility that must be faced in online dating. From a psychological perspective, online dating is related to the "projection effect". The projection effect refers to the tendency to attribute one's own characteristics to others. When forming cognitive impressions of others, one assumes that others have similar characteristics to oneself and projects one's own emotions, will, and traits onto others, creating a cognitive barrier of attributing oneself to others. For example, a kind-hearted person may assume that others are also kind-hearted. The saying goes "know someone's face but not their heart". To truly understand a person, you need time and direct interaction. Online, most things you see can be disguised and deceptive. This doesn't mean that everything he does is fake, but it means that if he wants to deceive you, he has countless ways to do so. I suggest starting with people you know in real life to find a partner. Online dating carries risks, so be cautious when meeting in person. Best wishes~

Hello, although it can be seen from the description that the original poster is attracted to someone, rationality has overcome emotions. You are conflicted about your rationality and don't know whether this rationality is right or wrong! I hope my response can help you. 1. First, rationally evaluate the other person. From the description, it is not difficult to see that you and the other person have mutual attraction, which is why you are gradually being drawn to them. Based on the way they chat, they're not bad, really good. They are willing to spend time sharing daily life with you, and make it meaningful. Being with someone like this, undoubtedly, every girl would be attracted. But dear, the person you know is only through the internet, you cannot touch them, and you don't know if this is their normal life in the unseen places. Therefore, the evaluation based on chat content can only be a reference and cannot be a reason for further development and being together. 2. Return to reality. I have also had online relationships, to be honest, the unreal feeling of online relationships brought me more anxiety than the sweet words of the other person. Therefore, no matter how good the person in the online relationship is, as a girl, we must first learn to protect ourselves and learn to recognize reality. If the other person really cares about you, you might consider letting them take the initiative, come to the city you are familiar with and meet you. Through offline meetings, you can get to know each other better and then determine whether to be together and whether the other person is safe enough to travel with. 3. Relationships between genders. In fact, sexual education is also a required course in life that everyone needs to encounter sooner or later. You may want to think about why mentioning relationships between genders makes you feel scared. Is it because the uncertainty of the relationship makes you feel insecure? Only by finding out the reason why you are scared and resolving this fear can you gain freedom and talk openly about sex. 4. Time reveals true character. Actually, whether online or offline, two months is not enough to fully understand a person. So, if you are afraid that the other person is a fraud, you might give each other some time and let the relationship develop further. Someone who truly loves you will be willing to spend time with you to understand whether they are good or bad. 5. Learn to live your own life well. Developing habits is not something that can be done overnight, and quitting habits is not something that can be done overnight either, but it is not impossible. Compared to the few months you have been used to the other person's presence, haven't you also been used to being alone before you met them? So, the other person is not that important. If they are not good enough, you can learn to let go of them. As long as you want to, it is not difficult. Give yourself some courage so that you can resist the various tests of love and learn to grow in love. Good luck!

Hello, the key to this question is not about online relationships, but about the people you meet online, whether they are reliable or not is the crucial point. With the development of the internet and the obstacles to emotional needs in real life, online relationships have become a emerging trend. Most people tend to have negative views of online relationships, and there are many reasons for this, such as what you mentioned, the fear of the other person being an online scammer, deceiving emotions, or other forms of fraud. Online relationships are formed by meeting through the internet, with vast oceans of the web separating us, only emotional communication can take place on screens, without the physical contact, which can easily create a sense of illusion and make people feel unreliable. So it's normal for you to have such concerns. From your description, it seems that you have both expressed interest in each other and have entered a deeper stage of communication. It can be seen that the other person has stronger feelings for you and is more passionate, while you seem to be more cautious and reserved. So what should you do now? You also realize that because of daily contact, you are becoming more and more accustomed to their presence. Therefore, you should carefully consider what feelings you have towards them, whether it's liking, dependence, or just a simple habit. If you have a liking for them, it might be worth trying to get to know them better, gradually understanding whether they are suitable for you, and then considering whether to take the relationship offline. If it's just a habit or dependence, it is important to let go in time, as it is also a form of respect for the other person. In reality, many people who started online relationships have successfully materialized their relationship, so if you meet someone you both like, it's better to be a bit courageous and make efforts for love, without worrying too much. But the key is to protect yourself, no matter how far the relationship goes, always have a sense of self-protection. Good luck.

Dating is a wonderful thing, it is the establishment of a relationship between two people. In this era of developed internet, it's hard to distinguish what is real and what is fake. Online dating relies on words to express affection, but in real life, love and care for you are not expressed through words, but through actions. It is through spending 365 days a year together and getting along with each other that you can truly know if the other person is suitable for you. If it's just online chatting, don't invest too much emotion into it, what if the other person is an online scammer? In that case, you will be the one who loses out. You can tell that he's not a great person in real life either, after all, you haven't even met each other yet and he's already talking about sex. This clearly implies that when you meet in person, he just wants to get you and he can only low-cost flirt with girls online, casting a wide net, and whoever he can flirt with, he will. The more girls he hooks, the more desires he will have, it's as simple as that. Don't think about marrying this person before meeting in person online, you don't even know if the person on the other side is real. You must understand each other and see the truth before further engagement. The most important step in online dating is to meet as quickly as possible. Moreover, the meeting must be in a familiar and safe environment. Avoid going to places specified by the guy, and you can bring a friend along. After meeting, get to know each other more and then decide whether or not to start this relationship. There are differences between online and real life, and risks exist as well. Safety always comes first, protect yourself.

question: In the past six months, I have been relying on medication to help me sleep every day. I worry every day that my insomnia will affect my work.
description: I used to sleep well, but in the past six months, due to my husband getting sick and being hospitalized, the pressure of the mortgage, and my child also getting sick and being hospitalized, I have completely developed insomnia. I work diligently but always worry about how my superiors perceive me. After developing insomnia, I worried about how it would affect my work, so I quickly started taking sleeping pills. Now I worry every day about not being able to sleep, what should I do?
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, anxiety, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear OP, sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ (1) In the OP's description, it can be seen that the OP is under a lot of pressure recently. With their husband falling ill, the pillar of the family has collapsed all of a sudden. This is undoubtedly devastating for a family. As the half of the sky in the family, the OP not only has to take care of their husband and child, manage household chores, but also continue working. It is understandable that the OP feels exhausted and stressed. (2) The OP mentioned relying on medication for sleep recently, which might be harmful to the body. I suggest that the OP try a different method to improve sleep. I have been using the app "Meditation Planet" recently, which provides various meditation audios, including ones for sleep and stress relief. The OP can give it a try. Remember, everything will pass, and things will get better. Keep up the good work! #The world and I love you, wishing you all the best~.

question: How to control as much as possible, or what to do if you keep getting angry with your child?
description: I have strict expectations for my child's academic performance. My child is five and a half years old. I am someone who doesn't speak well, influenced by my upbringing. But I try my best to control myself, yet I still can't control it. Whenever my child does poorly and throws tantrums, I always scold loudly. During the pandemic, I have been taking care of my two children for over half a year, and I feel like I'm breaking down. Recently, when my child doesn't practice the piano well, I often push or slap him a few times. I deeply regret it, but I can't control myself the next time. I feel very frustrated. I feel like a failure and a bad mother. Now, everything my child does seems magnified in my eyes. Actually, sometimes it's not a big deal, but I make it into a big deal myself. I don't know what's wrong with me.
keywords: Family, family relationships, the process of growing up, communication between parents and children

answers.answer_text: During the pandemic, conflicts and tension often arise in many families, which is indeed a huge challenge for many parents. From your description, it seems that you have a self-aware perspective, which is a great resource. Your self-awareness of your own growth will bring about a change in understanding the conflicts that occur at present. Indeed, many parents bring in the patterns from their own families of origin into their interactions with their children. I can sense that perhaps your parents were not very patient during your upbringing, so you unconsciously bring this aspect into your communication with your own child. If you have the time and financial resources, I suggest you consider seeing a psychoanalyst for some personal exploration.

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. Your question is about how to encourage your child to study well, but you always lose control and get angry at your child, causing you to feel regret afterwards, but unable to change yourself. [My analysis] 1) You have acknowledged that this personality trait may come from the influence of your family of origin, so you shouldn't blame yourself too much. You are also affected by a difficult childhood, which is why you behave this way. The key question is how to control yourself and not let your emotions affect your child. 2) Your intention is definitely good, hoping that your child can succeed and become an outstanding person in the future. So you have high expectations for your child, but when they don't perform well, you become anxious. Let's consider the situation from the perspective of the child. Even if you lose your temper, they will definitely be afraid of you and create a barrier between you, which will further decrease their enthusiasm for learning. They may feel that learning the piano is only to please you and to avoid your anger. This is an incorrect way of guidance. We need to guide them properly from their perspective. [My advice] 1) Learn to gradually control your emotions. For example, pay more attention to the shimmering qualities in your child and think about the issues from their perspective. If you were them, would you accept this educational approach? 2) Lead by example and study together with your child. Merely lecturing without taking practical actions is not effective. Try studying the piano together with your child, which will not only enhance your own skills, but will also strengthen the bond between you and your child. By being in a student-student relationship, you can better discover your child's interests and help them flourish. 3) Always remember to treat your loved ones well. Being able to have close relationships with family members is a wonderful fate. The time you spend together with them is limited, especially with your child. Your every word and action, your educational approach, and your attitude in speaking all have a subtle influence on them. I hope you can maintain a habit of reading, as it can calm the mind. I recommend the book "Intimate Relationships," which discusses techniques for how to get along with family members and friends. Finally, I hope you can overcome yourself and have a happy family. Best wishes.

You will know the consequences of your harsh criticism when you look at me. I still have my sanity, but my dad almost killed me. What you are constructing now is a prison. Are you now forcing him to study hard, then force him to work hard, force him to get married, and force him to have children? What can heal the relationship between you and your child? Let your own child love his own life. Don't be too impatient for quick success. At the same time, your emotional intelligence is too low. Your responsibility as a father is to give love and guidance, not to force him to study hard. Now my relationship with my father is not good like yours. Why does he want me to shamelessly go work with my brother? Because he believes that money is everything, just like how grades can evaluate a child. Actually, you forgot about this polyp. Take your child out for exercise and spend a good weekend together. You should go create opportunities for both of you to learn together. Actually, you don't understand at all. Some children's excellence is not because of their parents' forcing, but because of their own interests. He plays video games not because he hasn't finished his tasks, but because there are too few tasks. If there are too few tasks, give him some joyful time. If your child likes playing video games, take him to the arcade. Because he made the choice, let him pay for his own choices. If he wants to give up, you can only encourage and guide him, not use harsh words. Let me tell you a psychological theorem, poor elementary students don't represent anything. Teachers know this. Elementary students who are average will improve to be above average in middle school, and will become one of the top students in high school. It's just a matter of time. And don't talk about other children. Let me ask you, can you find someone with the same job, life, and even genes as you? People are human because they have differences. Can the person who is first in chemistry be the same as the person who is first in biology? His path is not planned by you, but by himself.

Hugs to the original poster! You've worked hard! I am also a mother and can completely understand the feeling of getting angry and then regretting it later. It's really tough to take care of two children all day during the pandemic, and the situation can unintentionally affect our emotions. When multiple events come together at a certain moment, an outburst is inevitable. Throughout the whole process, you may feel frustrated and guilty. Let's try to review the whole process again and perhaps gain new insights. 1. You have high expectations for your child's learning. Your child is five and a half years old, and when they don't do well and you get angry, you lose control and scold them. Since you have strict requirements for your child's learning, it's possible that you have high expectations for yourself as well. That's why you set the same standards for your child. For example, when your child doesn't practice the piano well and gets angry, you may not agree with their way of doing things. Perhaps you think they should continue practicing even if they're not doing well, and getting angry won't help. Maybe you have tried to coax your child kindly, but they still get angry. At that point, you lose control of yourself. At this moment, your anger is not actually directed at the child, but at their way of handling problems. On a deeper level, it may be a frustration with your own lack of control, because the child is not conforming to what we consider the right way. A five and a half year old child may not be able to express their feelings accurately, such as when they are practicing the piano and feel frustrated. They express their dissatisfaction with themselves through crying, or their sense of powerlessness. When a child doesn't do well and gets angry, it's more likely to mean that they need the help of their parents. At this time, parents usually can't feel the child's inner needs, and all that's left is anger. Only when parents realize the child's needs and ignore their way of expressing themselves can they control their anger instead of being controlled by anger. 2. After getting angry, you regret it and feel frustrated. You think you are a failure and not a good mother. You also realize that your child's issue was blown out of proportion and it wasn't a big deal to begin with. You might be a mother who holds very strict standards for herself, hoping to control yourself and educate your child better. In fact, all mothers probably have these hopes. Nobody is perfect, and raising children is difficult and far from flawless. But as a mother, you have already done your best. Why did you act like this? On the surface, you got angry, but in reality, you are just exhausted and need to take a breather, rest, and be loved. Unfortunately, the reality is that no one is there to provide these things for you. Therefore, you need to practice self-care first. When you nurture yourself and meet your inner needs, you will naturally be in a better state to give your children and establish a better parent-child relationship. I hope this is helpful to you. Good luck!

Subject: Hello! Your situation, as I understand it, actually involves two things: firstly, how to manage your quick temper and tendency towards violence, and secondly, how to discipline your children. The most important thing in disciplining children is to do it calmly and ensure that the entire process is calm. If you cannot remain calm, then it's best not to discipline them. Set clear boundaries and your future impression on them will become gentle and amicable. In regards to your quick temper, you need to gradually cultivate your personality. When you feel like you're about to lose your temper, try spending some time alone and avoid giving yourself opportunities to vent your anger. Even if your child has made a genuine mistake, it should not be used as a reason to unleash your anger. One needs to face their anger alone, which may be difficult at first. But after enduring a few times, you will come to understand anger and slowly learn to coexist with it, effectively controlling it. Anger will come and go. As long as you don't hop on the bandwagon of anger and do nothing, just experiencing the process of anger rising and subsiding without taking any action, anger will not cause any excessive damage. If needed, and if you are initially uncomfortable being alone, you can also have a trusted person accompany you. You are not allowed to vent your anger towards the accompanying person, but they can hold your hands and feet when you are impulsive to prevent you from harming yourself. In theory, anger is a source of energy. Some people believe that anger reveals their spirit or dignity, but nonetheless, anger is very difficult to control. When people act out of anger, they often lose control, and this loss of control will only scare others and result in estrangement. Anger is not suitable for education. The purpose of education is to teach the learner through example. If a parent's anger and violence are tolerated, it sends the message to the child that anger and physical aggression are the main ways to solve problems. For young children, repeatedly experiencing anger and physical punishment can imprint upon them an easily irritable temperament. I saved the reasoning for last because I truly hope that you do not blame yourself because of this, but rather, understand the potential consequences of being easily angered and make an effort to separate anger from discipline.

This is a very good question. In the usual consultations, many mothers have expressed similar concerns - "I understand the principles of parenting, but I can't control myself." When we were children, the material conditions were generally average. For our parents, meeting our basic needs for food, clothing, and shelter was already good enough, and there was rarely any extra energy to think about meeting our psychological needs. When we became parents, material conditions became greatly abundant, and our children began to have needs for self-esteem and love. The difficulty lies in the fact that we understand how we "should" treat our children, but it is difficult to actually do so. Because cultivating a secure attachment relationship and gently but firmly setting rules are related to critical periods of development. We experienced this when we were young, and as we grow up, we naturally treat others in the same way. If we didn't experience it when we were young, it takes a lot of effort to catch up, just like learning to correct pronunciation after not learning English when we were young. So don't blame yourself. This is the mission of our generation of parents: self-growth and then breaking the cycle of intergenerational transmission for our children, right? Have you ever thought that you can have a different relationship with yourself: no longer demanding perfection from yourself, patiently encouraging yourself when you lose control, seeing your efforts and achievements in the face of frustration, recognizing the hardships of taking care of two children continuously, and finding ways to appropriately address the exhaustion of parenting. Of course, building such a relationship requires repeated experiences. You can try psychological counseling, and let a counselor nurture you once. Afterward, you can also treat your children in the same way, helping them overcome difficulties encountered when they cannot persist in learning to play the piano, and using wisdom to help them develop habits. Thank you for the question, and best wishes!

After carefully reading your vent, I deeply understand your pain. Here's my analysis: 
1. "I don't even know what's wrong with me." Firstly, anyone who has this thought lacks self-awareness. It means you are not aware of your own shortcomings and why you make mistakes. 
2. So where exactly is your problem? *Control=losing control *Control=oppression *Oppression=resistance *Resistance=pain *Acceptance=happiness *Happiness=healing. It is because you have been constantly trying to control yourself that you eventually lost control. Trying to control your emotions is actually oppressive. Oppression leads to resistance, which then causes pain. In the end, you lose your sanity and self-control. 
3. Therefore, you need to accept your negative emotions. You can tell yourself, "I allow myself to get angry." Then shift your focus to doing household chores, video chatting with family and friends, or engaging in activities you enjoy. Cultivate a hobby that doesn't require too much time and energy, like gardening, embroidery, or yoga. As long as you love it, it's fine. Through your hobby, you can alleviate your negative emotions, relieve stress, and dissipate negative energy. Thank you for your question, and may all the goodness in the world come to you as expected.

question: In work, if one insists on principles, they may find themselves at odds with their superiors, which can be somewhat unsettling.
description: When working, sometimes there are disagreements among leaders, many of which differ from the requirements of the company. If I insist on company principles but disagree with the so-called leaders, they will say that I haven't done anything wrong. However, when something goes wrong, they push the blame onto me. If I stick to my principles and speak up to them, they will badmouth me to the company. The leaders will definitely believe them because their influence and connections are stronger than mine. But if I secretly report to higher-level leaders and the immediate leader gets scolded, they will definitely know I'm the one who spoke up. It's a dilemma, and I don't know how to handle it. I have stumbled a few times because of this and I feel anxious. Even though I understand, I still can't do well and I have a temper, but I believe it's temporary. I seek advice and comfort.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and disputes, colleagues, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hug the original poster. You must be troubled with work recently, right? If the company's principles haven't violated the law, then just listen to the boss! Because you can't beat those experienced in the workplace. They know the rules and are using them, even using you too! If there's a risk, I suggest you ask them again on WeChat, and once you get a response, you can screenshot and save it, or record it. Keep evidence, as it's difficult to be used and make mistakes all the time! Report directly to higher management, if the direct supervisor is not reliable, just forget it. You can ask your direct supervisor on WeChat, and once you get a reply, ask the senior management. With evidence and confidence! If the direct supervisor is not reliable, then it's natural to be scolded. Isn't the workplace about abilities? If besides this issue, the company is still good, then you can stay. If other aspects are difficult too, then you can consider changing jobs, as interpersonal relationships at work can greatly affect your mood! The most important thing is to be happy in life. Hope this can help you.

Hello! Let me first understand your problem: 1. I don't know what job you do. How many leaders are you referring to? How many leaders do you report to? Why do the leaders oppose your adherence to company principles? 2. Does this situation happen often? Do other colleagues have similar situations as you? 3. First of all, do you think the work we do is basically correct and without mistakes? If so, you can ask the leaders to point out where we can make improvements. 4. If you have explained but still can't do it well, try to find the reasons. Do these difficulties affect your sleep and meals? Are you getting along well with your colleagues? If you still feel troubled, I suggest seeking one-on-one counseling. Thank you for your question!

question: It's about the college entrance exam, but I feel lost and unmotivated all day. How can I cheer up?
description: I'm not sure what's wrong with me now. I have nothing to do all day, daydream in class, overthink things, and have no interest in studying. When I get home, I just grab my phone and don't put in any effort. I used to be different, but now I've become this way and it's scary. I have the college entrance exam coming up and I want to succeed, but it's so hard to overcome myself. Can you all help me? How can I get back on track?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, healing methods, anxious emotions.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Hugs to you! After reading your description, it seems that you are currently facing exam anxiety related to the college entrance examination (gaokao). You want to prepare for the exam in the best state possible but haven't found effective ways to deal with it. I truly understand your concerns. When facing academic pressure, it's important to learn how to shift your focus. I recall an experience of one of my friends who also suffered from severe anxiety before the gaokao. She even needed medication to alleviate her anxiety. However, her parents made a wise decision to take her on a trip to relax and visit university campuses. In just one week, her anxiety that had troubled her for nearly a year was relieved. Perhaps you can consider following my friend's example. Just imagining our future plan might not have a significant impact, and such daydreaming cannot sustain our beliefs. We need to step out of the confines of our study desks and have a broader view of the world. By doing so, our perspectives will also expand.

question: A 9th-grade girl is having difficulty studying during the National Day holiday, what should she do?
description: I have been on vacation for four days and haven't done anything. I feel anxious and really want to go to school. I don't feel like studying at all when I'm at home, but deep down I still want to study well. I always can't control myself. I don't particularly want to play with my phone, but whenever I try to study, I feel sleepy.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text: Hello there! I completely understand how you feel. Hugs for you! You seem to be very anxious, most likely due to academic matters but it could also be from other sources of pressure. You're feeling anxious, so you have a strong desire to study, but when you actually start studying, you find reasons to give up. It could be because you find it too difficult or you simply don't enjoy doing homework. You may have a tendency to pursue perfection and feel that you must achieve unparalleled results in your tasks. Undoubtedly, such high expectations are too perfectionistic and difficult to attain, resulting in constant procrastination...and the eventual outcome can be easily imagined. In fact, you could slow down and give yourself some proper rest time. It's important to maintain a healthy sleep schedule and ensure you get enough sleep. You can plan some vacation time for yourself, for example, decide to take a day off to rest and then resume studying. However, it's important to follow through with your plans. When studying, we need immediate feedback, as it is difficult to stay motivated for long-term goals that don't offer immediate rewards. Therefore, remember to set some rewards and consequences for your daily studying. If you complete your tasks diligently, reward yourself with something, but if you fail to finish them, impose some penalties.

question: 16-year-old female, lately frequently recalls those past events, always feeling very wronged?
description: In middle school, I was molested by a teacher and the person was punished, but I don't know why I often think about it during this period. I know it wasn't my fault, but I can't help feeling very aggrieved and wanting to cry. Because of these things, I've become very insecure. At the time when it happened, I didn't think so much, but now when I'm alone, I can't help but think about it and feel very uncomfortable. I tell myself that it will all pass and that the bad person has already been punished, but I still feel very sad and afraid of men. At home, there's only my brother and my dad. If my mom isn't around, I find ways to avoid them. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hug the questioner. After we have experienced certain traumatic events that have a significant impact on ourselves, causing us to feel sad, hurt, or even embarrassed, we may not want to express our feelings about it for various reasons at that time, or even be unwilling to mention it at all. However, the various effects caused by the event itself cannot be erased, especially the intense negative emotions at that time. In order to protect ourselves and minimize the impact of this event on our future lives, we often choose to bury this memory along with the emotions felt at that time deep inside us, suppressing it into our subconscious. However, in fact, we have not dealt with this event well, especially our negative emotions have not been released. This is actually a self-protective psychological mechanism called "isolation". The impact of the event itself still exists and will not gradually be forgotten because we intentionally choose not to remember it. And specific times in life may trigger our memories of these traumatic events and the emotional experiences at that time. The questioner is now trapped in such a situation. In daily life, we may not be able to find someone who fully accepts us as a confidant and helps us release the suppressed emotions inside us. Therefore, I still recommend that the questioner find a suitable psychologist. With their help, the two of you can work together to deal with this memory. I hope you can overcome your current difficulties soon. Keep going!

Hello. Your issue is that a past experience has made it difficult for you to let go and even to face men, including your father and brother. This is causing you a lot of distress, right? First of all, I want to say that it is not your fault. 1. This is likely a trauma response because the incident, although in the past, has not truly concluded for you and has triggered a trauma response. It is reminding you to pay attention to your inner self and acknowledge that it is hurt. 2. The mind cannot grasp the truth. Many events not only leave memories in our minds but also cellular memories in our bodies. For example, fear, anger, and sadness all leave traces in our bodies, resulting in long-term tension, contraction, and stiffness. So, while the mind thinks it's in the past, the body and soul have not fully recovered. 3. Things you can do: ① Seek help from family and friends. ② Seek assistance from professional teams and doctors. ③ Despite feeling scared, still believe that you can find ways to face your fears. I wish you the best. I hope you find peace, health, beauty, and bravery.

question: Is a girl's first time important?
description: I am currently a freshman. Today, while chatting with my roommate, our conversation shifted to girls' first time experiences. They all seemed to think it's normal to lose it for the first time, especially if it's with someone you really like; maybe my thinking is more conservative, but I believe a girl's first time should only happen after marriage, not casually. I think it's important to respect oneself. I find their viewpoint a bit extreme and different from my usual way of thinking, so I'm quite surprised. Should I agree with their perspective?

answers.answer_text: OP, you can maintain an open attitude towards different viewpoints and thoughts. You can acknowledge others' opinions while also standing firm in your own beliefs. These two aspects are not conflicting because things themselves are multifaceted. It can be seen that you are a girl who loves to contemplate and draw nourishment from every aspect of life, which is great. Regarding whether a girl's first time is important or not, every girl may have her own inner thoughts influenced by her personality and upbringing experiences. Your thoughts are also shaped by your personality and experiences. There's no need for anyone to agree with or validate others' thoughts, nor is there a universal standard for what is better or correct. When it comes to such matters with different viewpoints, it is good to follow your own inner thoughts. You can accept different perspectives, but it doesn't mean you have to change your own viewpoint. It's like how people perceive a rainy day: some may find it cool and refreshing, quiet and relaxing, while others may see it as inconvenient for transportation or disruptive to their work schedule. For you, the first time is important and should be saved for marriage, while for others, it is also important to give it to someone they truly love, as it is a sign of self-respect. You are looking at the same matter from different angles and naturally have different thoughts. Moreover, as you encounter more diverse people and things, you might change your own thoughts and believe it's okay to entrust yourself to someone you like. On the other hand, they may at some point look back on their first experience and feel that it would have been nice to save it for marriage, to share it with the person who will be their lifelong partner. So, if you believe that your current mindset is fine and correct, then follow your principles and thinking without worrying about others' opinions. Everyone has their own unique soul, so allowing for different thoughts and perspectives while acknowledging your own is what compassion and acceptance are all about, isn't it? Best wishes.

Title: Hello! From your description, it seems that you are a more conservative person. Regarding a girl's first time, I think I may have something in common with you. Currently, I believe that a girl's first time is very important and should happen after marriage. However, by the time you reach that stage, you may not think the same way anymore. Time changes, people change, so we may stick to our current beliefs, but when we are overwhelmed by emotions, it doesn't matter anymore. It may still be important, as we are giving ourselves to the person we love the most, which is also a form of significance. So, there doesn't necessarily have to be a requirement to wait until after marriage; it could also happen before. You don't need to agree with their perspectives, as everyone has their own views on things. You can stick to your own viewpoint. I hope this can help you. The above is just my personal opinion, for reference only. Best wishes!

question: Should I suspect something if I notice red marks on my husband's face after his shift at work?
description: After my husband had dinner, he went to work at the office until 11pm. When he came back, I noticed lipstick marks on his face. I asked him how it happened, but he refused to say anything. This made me suspect that my husband was seeing someone else behind my back, and now we suddenly have nothing to talk about. Although I have no evidence, I try to convince myself that maybe it was just an accidental encounter with something red. But I still can't shake off my suspicion towards my husband. I wish someone could tell me the truth of what happened. Should I really be suspicious?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Honest communication and maintaining a calm attitude to solve problems would be a better way to address potential conflicts in intimate relationships. From your description, it seems that you are not an impulsive woman. Even when you noticed your husband coming home late with lipstick marks on his face, you were able to think calmly and respond calmly, which is good. You can analyze whether there have been any abnormalities in your relationship recently, or any unusual behavior from your husband, including his dress, normal working hours, or socializing with friends, etc. Has everything been as usual? Has there been any change in your relationship and intimacy recently? Has his attitude towards you been better or worse, or the same as before? If he is truly having an affair or cheating, it wouldn't happen in just one day. There may have been signs and signals that you just haven't noticed. After contemplating the worst possible outcome and considering how to deal with it, you can have a calm conversation with your husband. Present the facts, express your feelings, convey your expectations, and give him an opportunity to speak and express his feelings, rather than having an emotional outburst. I'm not sure how you asked him about the lipstick marks on his face. If he didn't say anything, it could be because he can hide it, or it may be nothing and he's just too lazy to explain, or he doesn't know how the lipstick marks got there, etc. Only through open and honest communication can you find out. You can start by casually mentioning that you saw something on his face, which is a definite event that has occurred; express your doubts and opinions about it, feeling anxious and conflicted, both afraid of wrongly accusing him and afraid that he may actually be having an affair. Finally, express your expectations that he can honestly tell you the truth and that you will also try to calm down and handle your emotions, hoping to avoid the internal struggle and to give yourself a definite result. Whether there is or isn't an affair, you will think about the problems in the relationship. Do not conceal your suspicions in the relationship, nor deprive each other of the opportunity to explain and express feelings. Even if there is a negative outcome, it must be faced. Pretending to be deaf and mute will not help with emotions. Good luck.

question: 26-year-old male, tends to sulk and not resolve issues when faced with certain situations.
description: Recently, I discovered that I have always been prone to avoiding things that I care about. Due to the pandemic, our workplace is under closed management, and we need to get a leave form signed by both N (direct supervisor) and the director (higher-level supervisor) before taking time off. However, I didn't get the leave form signed for this weekend, and now I want to go out but feel frustrated about it. Actually, I had planned to go out this weekend to get a haircut, but on Friday, N said there was no need to get the form signed and that I could just inform the security guard when going out. I didn't say anything and thought that I probably wouldn't be able to go out. Then, over the weekend, N mentioned having a meal at a restaurant, so I asked him how I could go out. He still said I should inform the security guard. Our relationship with the security guard is fine, so I should be able to get their permission, but I just don't want to rely on personal connections. So, I'm feeling frustrated here and thinking maybe I shouldn't go out and just skip dinner. I don't know what kind of obstacle this is.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. The reasons for avoiding problems may appear to be varied, but behind them seems to be fear. When we repeatedly choose to expose ourselves to fearful environments, such avoidance behaviors may decrease. From your description, it can be seen that you are conflicted and confused about constantly evading things that matter to you internally. On one hand, you believe that you should do certain things, but on the other hand, the voice in your mind always makes you procrastinate or run away. To solve the inherent mindset of avoiding situations, you need to repeatedly and bravely confront problems. You may have also noticed that while you can escape temporarily and achieve relaxation and inner peace, such things you evade will eventually come back to you in another way, causing more pressure and anxiety. For example, when you go to work, your boss asks why you didn't go out to eat last night. Didn't you say you would inform the security guard? What happened? etc. Maybe the boss won't think much of it at first, but your inherent thinking of avoidance may make you do many similar things again, and at that time, your boss may not be as accommodating. Face the things you truly fear, then practice facing them multiple times, give yourself positive psychological suggestions, and overcome the habit of avoiding and deal with problems normally. Perhaps you not only have similar issues in this matter but also in other interpersonal events. Maybe you are afraid of those scenes or formalities in interpersonal relationships, feeling restricted and constrained at the dining table or when asking for help, and having some concerns about losing face, etc. The true reasons require your serious analysis and introspection. Only by identifying what you truly fear can you confront them. Discovering the reasons is not enough. You need to try and experience it more in social situations. When you feel the urge to retreat, you can encourage and motivate yourself, telling yourself that these things are not a big deal, even if you say something wrong or make small mistakes. You are in a process of development and change, so give yourself some time to adapt and integrate. When you repeatedly confront problems, you may find that you have quietly changed a lot. Best wishes.

question: Is it possible to have two counselors at the same time?
description: Previously, in a lecture, it was mentioned that visitors with unstable emotions need a counselor to help sort out their emotions, while another counselor helps to deal with the problem. Some may even request two counselors for a personal experience. What is this situation? What should be noted?

answers.answer_text: I understand that you want to quickly resolve your state or problem, but I think it needs to be divided into two judgments. 🤩 It requires someone to take responsibility for the visitor. 🤩 For me, sometimes if the client is in a state of depression or even a more serious state with suicidal tendencies, then we cannot judge: - Whose consultation is ineffective? - Whose consultation is effective? - Who is responsible for this emotional loss of control? - Who is responsible for this crisis? However, if there are physical illnesses present, it requires the intervention of traditional Chinese medicine or Western medicine, and I will advise them to seek a doctor to collaborate with our consultation. Also, when I encounter a visitor whom I am not competent to handle, I will refer them to someone else. 🤩 Emotions and problems cannot be separated. 🤩 Behind all emotions, there are deep-seated issues, and all problems will bring about emotions. These two cannot be separated: one person to solve emotions, one person to solve problems. Problems and emotions are like twin sisters. A good counselor should see the deep-seated issues behind emotions and find out what drives the problem. We also need to see what uncontrollable emotions are brought about by the problem for this visitor. How to solve this problem and emotion requires us to work diligently on both fronts. 🤩 Work with the visitor, not just their problems and phenomena. A good counselor works with the visitor themselves, not just their emotions and problems. Our goal in working with visitors is to accompany them in facing themselves, facing the outside world, and facing problems that may arise at any time, rather than just solving the problems and emotions they are currently facing. We should focus on working on their personality, habits, subconscious, worldview, and cognition. We should emphasize a systematic approach to personal growth, rather than just fixing what is immediate and superficial. 🤩 By starting with the corrections of the original family, visitors won't fall back in a second. 🤩 If our individual problems overlap with family systems or if individual problems lead to significant family problems, then family therapists may need to intervene, and separate treatments may be required. In this case, we can suggest finding a different type of therapist to help with synchronous counseling for you and your family. I have found that if a child's problems are caused by their parents' problems, and we only work on the child's part without addressing the issues with the parents and the original family, the parents and the long-accumulated environment of the original family will cause our visitor to regress in an instant, rendering all counseling ineffective. That's why we need to bring in additional family therapists to provide counseling for the parents, resolving the issues at the root, and naturally solving the child's problems. I recommend the book "Change Starts from the Heart."

question: Three years ago, I experienced depressive emotions. After being diagnosed with depression, what are the benefits of knowing about the condition?
description: I often feel unhappy when going to school, probably because I am not adapted to the new environment, haven't made any friends, and my parents argue, resulting in a suppressed mood. I have been experiencing depressive emotions for about three years, but it comes and goes. Recently, I cry frequently, maybe because of the change in environment or other factors. However, my mood improves a lot during summer and winter vacations. I feel like I might have mild depression, but what benefits would it bring if I were diagnosed with depression? Sometimes I feel that if I were diagnosed with depression, I would attribute all my shortcomings to the depression. Being diagnosed doesn't seem to have a positive impact on my life. Moreover, it would disrupt the original situation within the family, and life would be completely different.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, and psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, from your words and between the lines, I can sense that you are facing some difficulties and have fears and worries about diagnosis. Everyone has moments of being stuck in the mud, and everyone has different abilities to withstand stress. When external struggles exceed our capacity to bear, our bodies will show symptoms. The existence of these symptoms reminds us to seek help from the outside and to seek support. The diagnosis of depression exists in order to be better helped, and professional doctors will give professional advice based on our own situations, helping us to navigate through the current muddy situation psychologically and physically. Of course, we should also believe in our own strength. Diagnosis is not about being stigmatized or labeled. Just like you said, we cannot attribute everything to depression. When we have a cold, we take medicine. Depression is a psychological disruption caused by external factors. It is like our own immune power being temporarily suppressed. We should believe that we have inner strength to overcome difficulties. Think about whether the new environment is really that terrible. Who can provide us with spiritual support, or who in our existing relationships can help us? We can utilize these resources to build a support network for ourselves, even seeking professional help, including doctors and therapists, who can become sources of energy for us. Additionally, it's not your fault. Your problems are not a burden on your family. The current situation of your parents is the result of choices they made. They, as adults, chose this marriage and relationship pattern. Even if they noticed some changes due to your problems and broke the original pattern of life, these responsibilities should not be shouldered by you. Adults are much stronger than you think. They are not so fragile. You may feel like your world is collapsing, but they may not even be aware of this issue yet. Facing the problem instead of avoiding it is the best way to solve the problem. Let your parents understand your situation and obtain some support, which I believe is important for you. I think you need to be understood.

question: Can I have some comforting words? I'm 13 years old and in my first year of junior high.
description: At 13 years old, in the first year of junior high school. At home, no matter what happens to me, no matter how others treat me, the only words that come out of my parents' mouths are "you deserve it." This world is too noisy and not suitable for me.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. Your parents answered you with "deserve it". You are very hurt inside. The use of attacking language by your parents is actually their mode of interaction, communication, and communication. They don't know how to express love, and they are used to it. They don't even need to think about it. Just like pressing a button, they will immediately retort you in their habitual thinking mode. They are not even aware that this way of speaking can hurt you. Perhaps in their eyes, it is still a normal way of response. "I'm worried about you because I love you, I feel sorry for you. I feel it's not worth it, that's why I'm angry." Because you are their child, they are not good at using the correct way to express themselves without hurting you. Your parents probably also inherited the wrong interaction pattern from their parents, which you cannot accept and makes you feel unloved. Instead, you only feel rebuked. Actually, love is hidden in this situation. For example, a daughter pours the books in her backpack on the ground and does not pick them up for two days. During this time, her mother told her not to panic if the book is lost. The child did not take her mother's words seriously. Sure enough, on Monday when school started, her math workbook was nowhere to be found. The child cried in a panic and sought help from her mother. The mother was both angry and worried but she was also helpless. So she resorted to blaming, saying "You brought this upon yourself. I told you to pick it up, but you didn't listen." Could it be that parents have reminded you many times about many things? And you still continue to repeat the same mistakes. This kind of situation occurs frequently in the past, and parents don't know what to do either. They only know how to express their anger and frustration because you keep repeating those mistakes, such as throwing away your red scarf, misplacing your bus card, or losing your school uniform. They see you get anxious and distressed, and their hearts become chaotic. Every set of parents is imperfect. It's just that each parent has a different way of expressing love. If you stand at a level of understanding and accept their emotions, you won't feel angry. You will feel that they are not attacking or hurting you, but rather because they care about you and love you.

Hello, OP~ It's really concerning to hear you say that. I want to give you a big hug. In the journey of life, most of the time it's filled with challenges, while moments of ease are rare. From what you mentioned, it's really heart-breaking to hear that your parents neglect you and always think you deserve whatever happens to you. Because I don't know the specific circumstances that led your parents to speak like that, maybe they have their own thoughts, or perhaps they didn't mean to say things that way, but sometimes they just can't control it, and they don't know how to express "love" to you. Firstly, release your emotions. If you're feeling mentally distressed, you can have a good cry or confide in someone you trust. Secondly, distract yourself. You can go for a run, listen to music, or go swimming, engaging in activities that can change your unpleasant mood and psychological pressure. Adjust your emotions and keep striving! Wishing you well~.

question: Why do people want to avoid exams after registering?
description: It's frustrating that I signed up for the exam myself, but now I don't feel like taking it anymore. I know that passing the exam would benefit me, but I'm just too lazy to go and take it. The thought of exams makes me feel anxious, stressed, and uncomfortable. I worry about what would happen if I fail, and I would also be wasting time and money. How can I motivate myself to study for my exams? I have two subjects to study, and currently, I've quit my job and stay at home, but all I do is watch TikTok videos and anime every day.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. It's clear that you are feeling conflicted right now. You don't know what you should do. You know that passing the exam would be beneficial for you, and everyone knows that. But you just can't control yourself. I think the reason you don't want to go is because you feel unprepared. You mentioned that you have two exams, but you are lying in bed at home playing TikTok now. If you keep wasting your time on these things, I think you will never be prepared. Learning is endless, and knowledge is infinite. We can never learn everything, but we should try to learn the knowledge around us within the infinite time we have. If you study hard for the exam, I believe that one day you will be rewarded, and you will be admitted. Set yourself a small goal, precise enough to have a learning task for every day, every hour, every moment. This will give you some motivation and a little bit of pressure. Good luck~.

question: 22-year-old girl, recently experiencing anxiety and even contemplating avoiding practicing due to her driving lessons. What should she do?
description: I have always been sensitive in interpersonal communication, caring about my own image, and easily influenced by others' opinions, so I often feel stressed. Recently, during the one-on-one driving lessons, due to the coach's blame and criticism (such as terrible coordination, definitely won't pass, too rigid and inflexible), my mentality fluctuated greatly, and I made more mistakes during training, leading to a vicious cycle. Now, even the thought of practicing driving makes me more anxious, my heart beats faster, and when I see the coach asking if I want to practice, I want to avoid it. Can you please advise on how to improve? I hope to receive guidance, thank you!
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation, panic helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear reader. I can truly understand the anxiety you feel when learning to drive. I believe the main reasons for this anxiety stem from two aspects. Firstly, you are very sensitive to others' opinions, and after being criticized by your instructor, you tend to make more mistakes, creating a vicious cycle that even makes you want to escape from the situation. Our self-image is generally formed through self-perception and the opinions of others, so it is necessary to pay attention to others' evaluations. However, excessive focus on others' comments can easily lead to being influenced by their thoughts, resulting in an inaccurate understanding of oneself. After all, each person is a unique individual, and others' opinions may not necessarily apply to you entirely. Additionally, everyone has their own path to follow. As long as we carefully consider and choose the right path for ourselves, and earnestly complete it, we can maintain a calm attitude toward others' evaluations. Because your life is truly not heavily influenced by others, they cannot make decisions for you. Secondly, regarding the criticism from your instructor, I want to assure you that even the most competent individuals encounter this during their initial learning phase. Therefore, you shouldn't be too concerned, as the instructor's intention is definitely to see you pass and have high expectations for you, which is why they may use some provocative words to motivate you. When I was practicing for the driving test, even when I became quite stable in the later stages, I still received negative feedback from my instructor, warning me not to be overconfident and to be cautious during the actual test. Of course, if you still feel that the instructor's comments are making you worried about the test, you can communicate with them after the practice session and ask for any suggestions they may have for the exam. Lastly, I wish you good luck in obtaining your driver's license! Best regards, a little mushroom that hopes for a gentle world and gives yourself the time to grow freely.

Self-confidence includes trusting oneself and trusting others. However, blind self-confidence is also undesirable. Anxiety and confusion come from the unknown and uncertainty. When facing anxiety and confusion: 
① The first thing to do is to ask yourself questions. Why am I so anxious? Afraid of criticism? Afraid of not being able to complete training quickly and accurately? In fact, these issues are all trivial. It is normal for girls to have poor motor skills and a weak sense of direction. It is normal to have slow movements or mistakes. Apologize to the coach and ask him to explain more carefully if there is a problem. When you show enough respect to the coach, he will also feel uncomfortable giving a bad attitude. 
② When you know why you are anxious, you should think about how to reduce the source of anxiety. Practice is necessary to improve movements, and progress can only be made with the coach's help. However, you can spend some extra time watching videos or reading tutorials to better understand the operation of the movements. When you have a good understanding, your performance during practice will be smoother. If that's still not enough, you can directly ask the coach for other methods to assist your learning besides movement training. 
In fact, the issue of mindset is not that difficult to solve. Being humble and actively learning can solve many problems. Remember not to be too eager for quick results. I don't know if the above answer can be helpful. Good luck!

Hello, from signing up to getting your license, you need to overcome many obstacles, which really tests a person's confidence. So here, I want to affirm the author who is brave enough to learn how to drive. You are great and courageous. Next, let's analyze your issues and hopefully provide you with some help. 1. Learning how to resolve the source of stress: "Being sensitive during interpersonal communication and caring about self-image makes me easily influenced by others' opinions, which often causes stress." Our sources of stress come not only from ourselves but also from the outside world, namely other people's opinions. Negative comments can make us feel unhappy and stressed. The most effective way to deal with stress is to learn how to resolve it. The author should understand that you can only reduce your own stress, and others' opinions become irrelevant to you. For example, if the instructor blames you for poor coordination, you can confidently confront him: "It's precisely because I am not good at it that I chose one-on-one lessons. I need your patient teaching. Otherwise, what's the point of paying the expensive fees for these personalized lessons?" Or, you can consult the driving school and request a change of instructor. In conclusion, you don't have to silently bear it and accumulate negative energy every day. 2. Frequent mistakes: When I was learning to drive, before taking the second stage exam, I spent two weeks just driving straight. I chose a manual transmission and in the first week, the car stalled as soon as I started. I couldn't even control starting the engine properly. Many people thought that I wouldn't pass the second stage. But later on, I learned to reverse and other maneuvers quickly because I had a good foundation. I made all the mistakes that could be made in the beginning, so I was confident during the exam. To evaluate your future state based on your past and negate you is actually the instructor's irresponsibility. You should not deny yourself because of this. The more others doubt you, the more you need to prove yourself and show your achievements. You should learn to affirm your progress every day. For example, if today I stalled the car one less time compared to yesterday, I would consider it as progress. We must practice if we are not good at something. Let me share an inspirational quote with you: "Know your shame and then be brave." Just think about how in the future, you can proudly show your report card to the instructor and say, "I passed! It feels so good!" So don't be afraid! Avoiding problems will never solve them. If you make mistakes, correct them and take it slow. We may learn a bit slower, but we will definitely learn! Keep going! I wish you an early success in getting your license!

I hope my answer can bring you some insights. Firstly, what I can see is that the lovely questioner has already realized their existing problems and has the desire to change, which is already great! When we become aware of our problems, we should immediately seek proactive change. Here are a few small suggestions for your question: Part 1 - Get to know yourself again and fully utilize your strengths. After identifying your strengths, make the most out of them. This will help improve your self-identity and boost self-confidence. Don't pursue perfection. No one is perfect, so don't completely deny yourself over a little failure. If you immerse yourself in the sense of defeat, you will feel disappointed, frustrated, or even helpless. Therefore, shift your focus to what you are good at instead of fixating on your weaknesses. Accept yourself. Regardless of what kind of person you are, you are unique, and you should learn to be happy with yourself. For example, if you tend to label yourself as shy, you may not dare to speak in social situations. However, being shy doesn't mean being strange or abnormal, and you should accept your uniqueness. Because you don't need everyone's approval, nor do you need to live the same as others. Embrace the real you. Part 2 - Confident behavior and appearance changes. They say people are visual creatures, so your clothing and hairstyle will also influence you. Of course, this doesn't mean you have to buy expensive clothes or get a fancy hairstyle, but rather being neat and presentable. Join courses or clubs. Cultivate a hobby to feel more fulfilled. Read more. "Within books lies a house of gold, within books lies beauty" is not without reason (not literally a house of gold and beauty). Reading more can improve your inner qualities, which cannot be achieved through other means. I hope this can help you. If you have more questions or concerns, feel free to send me a private message or follow our WeChat official account: Mental Health Pro.

Hello, hug you! From your description, I can tell that you are quite sensitive in interpersonal communication. You care about how others perceive you and are afraid of being criticized. You also seem to be worried about making the other person annoyed during a conversation. Driving instructors have usually been working in society for a long time and they have to teach all kinds of students every day, dealing with students who have different personalities. The job has worn down their patience, leaving them with only mechanical teaching methods. However, we should also understand the difficulties faced by the instructors. There are fast learners among students, but there are also slower ones. It is not possible for the instructors to adapt to every student's learning characteristics, so they choose to make the students adapt to them. The instructors teach everyone the same way, using the same rules, and then observe us as we try to grasp the key points of the rules, such as where to stop the car and when to turn the steering wheel. I hope you know that learning to drive on the road is a very serious matter! Very serious! Because if we are not careful, it can lead to an accident, and how can we ensure our own lives and the lives of others? Therefore, the seriousness of the instructor is telling us that we cannot be careless while driving, we cannot just get by. I guess you are not unable to learn to drive, it's just that the instructor has put too much pressure on you with their words, causing you to doubt yourself and want to avoid the instructor and stay away from danger. This is indeed not conducive to our learning. We cannot change the instructor, but we can change ourselves and change our mindset. The instructor is like this with everyone, not just you, but also other students. So, you can discount the reproaches from the instructor. If you are really afraid of the instructor, you can consider changing to a different one. Maybe you can find out what kind of person the instructor is in private, whether they are as strict in their interactions with other instructors as they are in teaching. As I mentioned earlier, learning to drive is not a trivial matter! I don't recommend dragging along with learning to drive because you have already spent money, time, and energy. In the end, you still have to learn and face it. So it's best to learn well and get your license as soon as possible. Avoidance will only prolong the pain. The pain that should have been brief will be extended infinitely by you... Finally, I hope you grit your teeth, memorize the rhymes taught by the instructor during your driving lessons, and discount everything else they say. After you finish learning, go back and vent your dissatisfaction with the instructor to your friends, scold them. Good luck! Best wishes!

Hello, dear questioner. Ahahaha, if you want me to recall what I was like when I first started learning to drive, I would still find the second phase of the exam quite difficult. The first time I touched the steering wheel, the instructor only asked me to practice going forward and backward between two straight lines, and to maintain a steady speed. I couldn't even do that properly and of course, I received a lot of criticism. At that time, I thought it was impossible for me to do well. After one or two days, I suddenly got the hang of it and even learned how to parallel park. I even felt like a genius teenage girl! I passed both the second and third phases of the exam on my first try. I can share some tips with you: the day before the exam, you can go through the operational procedures in your mind or write them down, which will give you a greater sense of confidence. If you have particularly poor mental resilience, the instructor may recommend purchasing an exam insurance policy. The insurance fee is 100 yuan, and if you fail to pass the exam five times in a row, you can get a refund of your tuition fee.
