So, you hesitate to share certain thoughts that are hidden in your mind, doubting whether or not to discuss them with a counselor. If you were to express these thoughts and receive some reasonable explanations, I believe that many things would truly be released. However, if you were to express these thoughts and not receive any feedback from the counselor, it could potentially cause a second round of harm to you. As a result, you would hesitate about whether or not to speak up about certain things. In making decisions, we often consider them thoroughly. In reality, it takes a considerable amount of time for a counselor and client to establish a relationship and for the counselor to gain the client's trust, in order to better help the client resolve their problems. Therefore, regarding the idea of trauma that you mentioned in your description, whether or not to speak about it is your decision, and the counselor's role is merely to guide you. If you have already convinced yourself in your mind to share this matter, then go ahead and speak up. For you, it can be considered a kind of relief, because the longer something is suppressed in your mind, the greater the harm it will cause you. The reason why some things are difficult to articulate is because subjectively, we define these matters as shameful, and society's judgment of these matters also leads us to repress certain things, keeping them hidden in our hearts without expressing them. In reality, some traumas are not what we seek to experience, but are inflicted on us by others. We don't want them, and we shouldn't blame ourselves. The blame lies with those who cause us harm, or with the environment. So, for things that have already happened, we can gradually let go and reduce their impact on ourselves. With that, I have also summarized some methods to help alleviate your current situation: (1) Try to trust yourself and the counselor, as a good counseling relationship is essential for problem resolution. (2) Share your thoughts with someone close to you, further relieving your current emotions. (3) You can also keep a journal to record your emotions, allowing you to better observe their occurrence and development. (4) Don't put too much pressure on yourself, and at the same time, find ways to release this pressure when it becomes overwhelming. The world loves you, and I wish you well.

Hello, this is really a confusing and difficult situation. I don't know why you entered into psychological counseling, but I wonder if the question you raised might also be a factor in seeking psychological help. Maybe you are not aware that this problem may be unconsciously troubling you. From a psychodynamic perspective, I will try to discuss some thoughts on this and see if it can bring you some reflections. Your description is not very long, but it contains rich content, especially the feelings triggered by conflicts. I don't know if you have felt anxiety, uneasiness, conflict, and fear? I found two conflicts. The first is the conflict between the desire to overcome the fear of shame and the avoidance of shame caused by fear, which is indeed a difficult choice. The second conflict is between doubt about the reliability of the counseling relationship and the denial of this doubt. You have used rationalization and justification to persuade yourself to trust the counselor, but of course, this cannot eliminate your doubts in your feelings, which may lead to even greater anxiety. I believe that psychological counseling is precisely working in these anxieties, uneasiness, and nervousness. Through the cooperation of the counselor and the visitor, we can discover the meaning behind the emotions, so that the visitor can see the truth. When the visitor allows oneself and dares to see the truth, the symptoms may fundamentally disappear. So, if possible, tell your counselor these real feelings happening inside you and discuss these feelings and the associations they evoke with the counselor. Perhaps there will be some new insights.

First of all, the questioner needs to understand why they are seeking counseling. Just like going to the doctor when we are physically ill, psychological counseling is also aimed at healing certain problems. Therefore, it is necessary to disclose one's issues to the counselor. If you don't say anything, how can the counselor treat you? How can you recover and live a healthy life? When we have physical illnesses, we go to the doctor and need to expose ourselves, especially when it involves sensitive areas of pain. If we feel shy and don't let the doctor see, our illness cannot be treated. But when we can correctly see our own body and pain, we know that these are physiological problems and there is nothing to be shy about. Doctors see us just like they see an anatomical model, the human body structure is just a collection of knowledge points in their eyes. Only after overcoming this psychological barrier can you obtain healing. So when you feel very shy and want to hide away, think about your purpose, why are you seeking counseling? Is it to resolve your emotional burdens? Heal your traumas? Do you want to become more confident and resilient? If you have a goal, you can better overcome your psychological obstacles. Or if you currently don't have the courage, you can tell the counselor that you feel a lot of shame and although you want to share some things with them, you just can't do it yourself. You hope they can help you. Listen to how the counselor will guide and comfort you. A professionally competent counselor will help you slowly break free from your own emotional prison. Sometimes you feel ashamed because you are too hard on yourself. Your inner dialogue is too negative and you always blame and torment yourself, making the actual situation seem much worse than it really is. For example, some people were bullied when they were young, everyone called them stupid and they didn't have any friends. They feel ashamed, as if it was their own fault. But is that the reality? Isn't being bullied the fault of the bullies? Why should you shoulder this burden yourself? So you need to tell yourself that you haven't done anything wrong. Even if you were bullied, you are still a person with value and dignity. Other people's definitions of you and external standards cannot determine who you are. Only you have that right. Take it slow, gradually build your self-confidence, and healing yourself takes a little bit of courage. Tell yourself that there is nothing wrong, as long as you are clear in your heart, no one can make you feel ashamed.

Hello, let me share my thoughts and suggestions on this topic in order to hopefully help you. It is important to trust the professional ethics of a legitimate psychological counselor. Confidentiality is the most basic requirement. If you have chosen a legitimate psychological counselor with some experience, you can gradually build trust and relax yourself, fully immersing yourself in the counseling environment. Confidentiality is a principle that every legitimate psychological counselor will and must adhere to, and it may take some time for you to gradually accept this. Trust takes time to build, so don't rush it. The effectiveness may be compromised if you rush the process. Psychological counseling is divided into different sessions based on the severity of the psychological issue. The client needs to take the time to gradually describe their state, and the counselor needs to sincerely understand the client's issue and strive to empathize. Then, together, they can discuss how to solve the problem. This requires time and process, and sufficient trust is the basis for being able to speak freely. So take some time to adapt yourself and let both of you adapt. When trust reaches a certain level, many deep-seated thoughts will naturally be expressed. You can also change the counseling time, space, and other factors to achieve a comfortable and relaxed state. Perhaps you won't fear avoidance due to sharing. Different environments will affect the relaxation level of the client. Some people prefer evening, some prefer sunlight, some prefer a greater distance from the person they're talking to, and so on. These preferences are normal, as long as they help you relax. The most important thing is to clearly and thoroughly describe the problem, which will also help the counselor identify the problem and provide solutions and advice.

Hello, I understand your psychological feelings. This is a fear of exposing the extremely sensitive part of your inner vulnerability and escaping from it. You think it will make you experience pain again, so you don't want to face it and expose yourself. My personal advice to you is to have courage to face your inner self and have a brave dialogue between your brave and vulnerable selves. Let your vulnerable self speak out all the negative emotions, worries, and shame, and let your brave self participate as well. You will realize that this is not a problem. A counselor is a helper who will walk into your soul with you, explore, discover, and provide solutions.

Hello, the topic is the mental health counselor. Based on your description, I understand that you know the principle of confidentiality and trust that the counselor will abide by it. However, you still hesitate to speak about it due to two psychological reasons: (1) the significance of this trauma to you is immense, and from your own moral perspective, it is a secret that could create a huge impact, either resolving the issue or exposing it further, and you haven't balanced the relationship yet. (2) The relationship between you and your counselor is either lacking trust or has developed transference. Either way, the timing is not ideal at the moment. In summary, the timing is not right yet, and further exploration is needed. My advice is: (1) find the right timing to gradually discuss your moral beliefs related to the event. (2) Find an anonymous platform to initially share it secretly, and then treat your counselor as such a platform. (3) Wait patiently for the best moment; through conversation, many things naturally change for the better. That's all, wishing you a happy life and good luck!

Hello there! I completely understand your feelings. For many people, childhood trauma is something they don't want to remember or disclose, and that's perfectly normal! If this trauma doesn't have a significant impact on your current life and is just a bad memory, then let it go. But if your past childhood trauma does affect your present life and you need to confront it and release it from your inner self in order to slowly achieve healing, then if you're unwilling to face yourself and disclose your inner pain in counseling, it means that you're not ready to release the pressure within and you're not prepared to express your narrative. At this point, try to empty your mind, trust the counselor's guidance, and dare to speak up. Don't overthink it! The past is already gone. It's like a malignant tumor in our bodies, and it's inevitable that removing it will be painful. But think about how liberating it feels to speak out. Why be nervous? Relax your body, take a deep breath, and follow the counselor's guided questions to express yourself truthfully! Don't make it too difficult for yourself. If you still can't speak up, try talking to a wall at home! See if you can express yourself and make it clear. In summary, if you want to maintain good physical and mental health, it's important to keep a positive state of mind and find joy in life, among other things!

After reading your description, it seems unnecessary to force yourself in matters of privacy. In my opinion, either you are not mentally prepared yourself or the level of trust between you and the therapist has not reached a point where you feel comfortable disclosing such private matters. So, if the therapist can find a way to resolve or alleviate some of your psychological emotions, your desire to express yourself will naturally come about. The concern you have raised on this platform today is whether hiding certain highly private matters would have a significant impact on your psychological healing process. In fact, when you seek a therapist, it is already a state of mutual connection. You have the right to choose whether to tell them or not. Or perhaps you are wondering when it would be appropriate to share these things with them? These are decisions you can make. Have you ever thought about what you would do if you were to disclose these very private matters to them now and not achieve the desired results? Ultimately, it means that the relationship between you and the therapist has not progressed to that point, so there is no need to worry about it. Someday, when you feel ready to tell a certain therapist, you can go ahead and do so.

question: Do I have depression if I constantly hurt myself, feel worthless, and have suicidal thoughts?
description: Always unable to control hurting oneself. Feel worthless. Want to die. Experiencing hallucinations and hearing voices. Excessive sleepiness. Insomnia. Enjoy being in dark places.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Hugs to you. When you feel like reading OP's words, OP is feeling very helpless right now. I don't know what disappointed or even desperate you. Our lives are given to us by our parents who raised us to adulthood. We also have so many friends and family members. If they know that you are constantly hurting yourself, they would be so sad. You should love yourself first and then love others. Feeling useless is because you haven't discovered your own potential yet. You can try to work hard on things you like and believe that you can do well. When you see your achievements, you won't feel this way anymore. Try various ways to enrich your life every day, besides work, you can also travel to relax. Best wishes~.

question: 27 years old, 2020, life is at a low point, why is life so difficult?
description:
1. There has been a major upheaval in my family, and every day I wake up with a soul-wrenching feeling. 
2. I have a mentally unstable mother who calls me dozens of times a day to complain about how difficult her life is or to ask for help with her latest mess.
3. I graduated from a good school and got a job, but I can't keep up with the demands. I want to study and improve myself, but I am constantly weighed down by family matters and my own unhealthy mindset.
4. Currently, my ability to understand and remember things is failing, especially compared to my peers who just graduated and are full of vitality. All I feel is endless pressure. My family doesn't give me any support; they only drain me.
5. Today, I arrived late for class and there were no seats available, so I had to sit in a corner at the back. My mother kept calling me, and when I answered a call from an unknown number, it was my mother's voice, sounding like a death sentence, saying that something had gone wrong at home. Every time my mother says something, I feel like jumping off a building. I truly hate my mother, I hate that she gave birth to me. I'm so tired. I feel like a clown. Every day, I try my best to appear normal, work hard, and treat the people around me well, hoping to gradually become better. But it's so difficult. Every day, I cry, tears flow uncontrollably. It's so hard. I'm sorry.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, panic and helplessness, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hugs to you for being in such a difficult period. Thank you for being willing to come to this platform to confide in us and allowing us the chance to offer you support. It sounds like you are currently in a very lonely and confused state. There is no one around who can understand the hardships you are going through and the emotions you are experiencing. Your family is unable to respond to you and provide you with warmth and support. Additionally, you are facing significant pressure at work and in your personal life. In this situation, it is possible for us to experience sustained feelings of sadness, lack of focus, and disrupted sleep and appetite, which can also affect our work. From your description, it seems that recent major changes have occurred and there have been some changes in your life, such as starting work. When we encounter major changes in life and find it difficult to adjust, feeling lost and lacking support can lead us to a low point. In this stage, I hope we don't be too hard on ourselves. We could try to tell ourselves that we are currently in a difficult period, but there will be a day when the difficulties will pass and our wounds will slowly heal. We can try to replace negative thoughts such as "nothing will ever get better" and "I will always be in pain" with positive self-suggestions like "difficulties will pass" and "I will be able to overcome this pain". We can write them down or say them to ourselves before getting up and before going to bed, giving ourselves these affirmations. This can help us regain confidence and a sense of control. How can we better alleviate our emotions and break free from a negative cycle? It may require us to change the way we perceive negative events and how we respond to them. Perhaps we are now afraid of our mother's phone calls and have internalized her negative emotions and family issues as our own sources of stress and negative feelings. When we fully accept and internalize them, we may easily feel overwhelmed and drained. By setting an invisible boundary and telling ourselves that our mother is a separate individual, we cannot transform ourselves into her and solve all her problems. Accepting the existence of boundaries and recognizing that everyone has their own limitations and worries can allow us to stop burdening ourselves with our mother's troubles. This may help us gradually learn not to see our mother's phone calls and voice as sources of pressure or to transfer this pain, and even learn to say no. Of course, I understand that everyone has their own concerns, and perhaps your conscience doesn't allow you to ignore your mother's calls, or you have put a lot of pressure on yourself to meet others' needs. However, just as it is mentioned in the safety instructions when we board an airplane - we need to put on our own oxygen masks first before helping others. Similarly, we need to learn to take care of our own physical and mental well-being first so that we can respond to those around us with full energy. Before that, we can adopt some ways to show others our boundaries and communicate our more important needs that require attention. Learning to prioritize ourselves and care for ourselves is a topic we need to gradually learn. I hope this is helpful to you. If you have any questions, feel free to interact with me.

People often say that when God closes a door for you, He also opens a window. 2020 has been a difficult year indeed, with the outbreak of the pandemic at the beginning of the year and the overall economic downturn. Many families have also faced a lot of difficulties, and the same goes for the OP. These unpleasant events have been affecting us for a long time. However, there have also been some happy moments, such as successfully graduating and getting a job in a good company. These are all good beginnings. It's just that my mother's phone calls feel like an endless reminder of urgency. Whenever we are exhausted and in need of comfort from others, my mother always complains and vents her frustration. Home used to be a place filled with love, but now it makes us feel repelled and helpless, even making us want to escape. However, our sense of morality compels us to choose to comply. Actually, when people have a burst of negative emotions, they need to let it out. Unfortunately, my mother sees us as her emotional dumping ground, without considering our situation or feelings. She just pours all her thoughts and emotions onto us and expects us to clean up the mess afterward. However, our energy is limited, and we have a weak foundation ourselves. We want some personal time to improve ourselves, but the other person doesn't give us that time. Therefore, we can set some ground rules with our mother, such as telling her who she can ask for help with certain matters, and we can spare half an hour each day to chat with her, listen to her complaints. But for the rest of the time, unless it's something extremely urgent, we will choose to focus on our own matters first. We will let her know that we also have things to deal with and solve, and it's not possible for us to be with her all the time. We hope she can understand. If necessary, we can find something for our mother to do. I'm not sure if she has any friends or hobbies, but we can give her some time to do her own things and shift her attention. If we have any problems that we can't figure out in the future, we can come here to seek comfort and support, or list out the problems we encounter and the possible solutions we come up with. We can work together to find a way to solve them. In reality, life is all about encountering and solving problems. Sometimes, we just need to step out of our previous difficulties and take a different perspective to see the problems. The world and I love you.

question: I broke up with my boyfriend, why do I feel guilty?
description: I broke up with my boyfriend, and my avoidance might have hurt him. But when I think about how he used to treat me earnestly, I feel like I didn't do enough back then, but it's already too late to go back. I feel like I did something wrong by agreeing to be with someone as my savior, and it's uncomfortable in my heart. I don't know what else we can do to improve our relationship. I originally wanted to see him again, but when I see him, I don't know what to do, and it feels indescribable. I hope he's doing well and that I don't leave a lasting negative impact on him. Seeing his profile picture, which is from when we were together, brings up an indescribable feeling. I feel like if I want to do something, it's better to do it soon, or else it will feel like a scar that's harder to heal. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: OP, here's a comforting hug for you. You and your partner broke up, but what was the reason for it, and is there hope for reconciliation? I feel like neither of you have truly moved on from each other, and it seems like there are unresolved regrets and unfinished business that have become deep emotional wounds. Your idea is correct - complete all the things pertaining to this relationship, without leaving any regrets or scars that will continue to hurt when mentioned. Only by completing these things can you truly say goodbye to this relationship. I noticed that you have mentioned a phenomenon of avoiding contact. Now that you're aware of this, try to understand yourself first, accept yourself, and why such a phenomenon has occurred and formed. Then, try to communicate with him and explain to him. Make an effort for him to understand you. If he truly loves and cares for you, he will find a way to truly understand you and most importantly, he will cherish you. He won't think about leaving you because of this characteristic or anything of that sort, if he truly loves you. Regardless of whether you are preparing to reconcile or let go, it is important to address this unfinished business. This is a technique from "Gestalt Therapy" called "unfinished business." It emphasizes fully learning, understanding, and experiencing the present moment. Every event in life, big or small, especially when it comes to love relationships, can only be truly absorbed and experienced when we complete every step and say goodbye to the past, moving towards the next stage. However, sometimes, when things are suddenly interrupted, the unfinished business continues to persist, and sometimes it may take a lifetime to make up for it. For example, if a loved one leaves without saying goodbye or if we constantly fail to obtain something we like. In contrast, there is the completeness of an event. In one's life, we are constantly pursuing complete experiences. Once the "unfinished business" is formed, the usual methods of correction are catharsis and compensation. Unfinished business often persists until individuals are brave enough to face and deal with these unexpressed emotions. Only by increasing awareness of one's current state, recognizing and clearing repressed emotions and needs, can one integrate the fragmented parts of their personality and achieve a complete self. 1. Improve self-awareness. Pay attention to your interactions with others in life and work, enhance self-awareness of your emotions, thoughts, bodily sensations, beliefs, and behavioral manifestations, in order to avoid self-defeat and achieve personal growth. 2. Learn to face and accept your past, find constructive ways to solve problems, practice positive attributions, and reduce the negative impact of "unfinished business." 3. Continuously improve oneself through lifelong learning. Should you try to reconcile or let go as soon as possible? The following four questions can help you clarify your thoughts and make the best choice for yourself. Question 1: Are the issues that led to the breakup not crossing any boundaries and can be resolved? Question 2: Do you want to return to this relationship because you genuinely like them? Question 3: Are you truly willing to invest time and effort in rebuilding the relationship? Question 4: Is your partner just as willing as you to make an effort to fix this relationship?

#I broke up with my boyfriend. My aversion to contact may have hurt him.# This means that at least in some aspects, you are not compatible, so you broke up. #I hope he will be well and not be haunted by me.# Breaking up will have emotional effects on both parties, but these are issues that each person has to face. No one can help the other person face them. This is also part of love, it requires experience and growth through experience. Of course, you can also choose to waver between letting go and not letting go. If you choose not to let go, there must be a reason for it. #I feel like I did something wrong by accepting someone as my savior and being in a relationship with them. I feel uncomfortable and don't know how we can have a better relationship. I originally wanted to see him again, but now I don't know what to do when I see him. # This is a dangerous behavior! Being together should be based on mutual consent, not conditions for being together. Once there are conditions, the relationship between the two parties is inherently unequal, which can easily lead to psychological burdens on the sacrificing party. However, it is also a choice, there is no right or wrong. You have already experienced it, I don't know how you feel. But judging from the outcome, it is probably not good, otherwise you wouldn't be posting here. From the perspective of respecting yourself and respecting the other person, if love can be together, you have to be prepared for the possibility of breaking up. Since you have already broken up, you have to face various tests, such as sadness, pain, and unhappiness, on your own. If you find that you truly like him now or in the future, then you can consider reconciling. But if you want to reconcile out of pity, then be prepared to bear the corresponding consequences. The choice is always in your hands, think carefully before taking action.

question: I'm 20 now, why do I only remember all the bad things that happened to me since I was little?
description: My upbringing was not bad, and I remember that my family treated me well. However, all the good things I could only feel at that time, and I can't remember them anymore as time passes. On the other hand, I can't forget the things that hurt me and have a negative impact. I remember every reason and circumstance when my parents scolded me, but they think I am making up stories and that those things never happened. It's like how they tell me about their care and all the good things, but I have no memory of them and instead think they are making them up. Moreover, I find it difficult to find happiness or emotional feedback in life. My mood doesn't fluctuate much, and I never lose my temper. I've learned to disguise myself, but I am unusually sensitive to emotions such as the separation and death of small animals, and I feel sadness. However, I don't feel the same way towards people. I'm starting to doubt whether I will have any emotional response if my parents pass away one day. I believe that caring for family is a responsibility, but I lack the corresponding emotions. No matter how much people around me love me, I still can't feel the emotions of family, friendship, or a racing heart. I want to know why this is happening.

answers.answer_text: Putting a sugar cube in water won't make it too sweet, but adding a spoonful of vinegar will make it very sour. Finding money won't make you ecstatic, but losing money can make you feel regretful. People don't stay happy for an entire year because of one joyful event, but they may be affected by a trauma and feel depressed their whole lives. That's why we can never forget those moments when our parents lose their temper, even if it's just once. People tend to hold onto unpleasant things and ignore the happy times. As long as you have the impression that your family treats you well, cherish these small moments of happiness. Don't dwell on what's real and what's fake. The past is the past, and we cannot live in it forever. If you learn to take these things lightly, you will gradually feel the warmth of family, friendship, and even the beating of your heart. Try hugging others first, and they will give you a warm embrace. There's nothing in this world that we cannot let go of. Good or bad, everything eventually becomes a memory. Don't always carry it in your heart. I believe you can do well because you're a very kind person.

question: Growing up in a family with domestic violence, I have developed a severe fear of marriage and lack self-confidence. How can I overcome this fear of marriage?
description: Growing up in a household with domestic violence, combined with my sensitive personality, I have developed a fear of marriage. I lack a sense of security and confidence. I am afraid of repeating the past and constantly think about focusing on my career before considering marriage. The pressure to get married has been significant in recent years. I would like to ask if the fear of marriage is a problem and how to alleviate it.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP: Do you feel the pressure of marriage and your fear of marriage makes you very conflicted? I don't know how old you are. Are you a male friend or a female friend? You mentioned that you lack confidence, security, and are afraid of repeating the same mistakes. It sounds like you are a very perceptive and insightful person, who clearly understands that your current fear of marriage stems from a turbulent family environment. Since I have limited information about you, the following explanations are only for reference: The so-called fear of marriage can be explained from the following aspects: Firstly, the unhappy marriage of parents affects the formation of our own marriages, causing a lack of trust in marriage and fear of getting married; secondly, the sensitive interpersonal relationship caused by childhood experiences leads to conflicts in interpersonal relationships, making it difficult to have a normal love life and resulting in a fear of marriage; thirdly, the experience and trauma of sexual assault can also lead to a fear of marriage due to the fear of intimacy. As for how to break through this, it is necessary to consider professional and formal psychological therapy to help your inner child grow up. Keep going, and remember, I will always love you!

question: 18-year-old girl, recently has been emotionally unstable, feeling unworthy of being liked.
description: I feel like the atmosphere at home is heavy. It doesn't feel like a real home, just a place to live together. There is no warmth of a home. I don't know what it feels like to be loved, or how to love. Lately, I've been feeling inexplicably unhappy at school. I feel like I'm not worth being liked by others, that I don't deserve anyone's kindness.

answers.answer_text: First, let me give you a big hug. For you, what kind of behavior or language can make you feel loved? Parents have been together for so many years, perhaps they are not very good at expressing their emotions, and there seems to be no warmth between them. But even so, they have chosen not to separate, there must be something they rely on and need from each other. If there is something you need your parents to do or say to make you feel warm, you can try talking to them about your thoughts and feelings and involve them in the conversation.

question: Joining the debate club but ending up as a substitute, am I just doing it for show?
description: Reason tells me that even as a substitute, I should still prepare well, just like Lang Lang who came off the bench. But I feel very uncomfortable and in pain. I have to comfort the classmate who replaced me. Others sent messages saying they were afraid I would be unhappy, but I reassure them that it's alright. We will be the strongest reserve force in our class. I am also part of the debate club, but I forgot. I thought it was an opportunity to showcase myself, but it's gone now. They say even substitutes should prepare well so they can go in at any time. But I feel like maybe I won't get a chance anymore. Maybe at first, I wanted to prove myself in the debate club and be the best debater, but now... I might as well participate in a recitation competition since I can't get on stage. However, maybe...What should I do? Am I only doing this for the sake of showing off? I just wanted to showcase myself. That person said they were from the debate club and insisted on adding themselves, so they replaced me. But I am also from the debate club. It's just that their club is at a higher level than mine, so... three debate clubs plus one amateur. When I realized that, I forced a smile.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friends, roommates, classmates, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: The development of events often differs from what we expect, which can be momentarily surprising, but this is a normal human reaction. It's like a process of saying, "Oh? Okay." Oh? Someone got replaced? Many times, things unfold differently than we imagine. You think today will be a good day, but then it starts raining shortly after you step out; you think you're leaving early today, but you still encounter traffic... Oh. Not going on stage for now. Oh, there's a long line to wait in; oh, there's no direct transportation available; oh, the flight is delayed... Okay. It's fine to be a substitute, it's not like there's only one debate. It's fine to wait a bit; it's fine to listen to music first; it's fine, think of it as a workout... The attitude towards unexpected events reflects one's resilience and flexibility in problem-solving. Each emergency response is a full manifestation of adaptation to the environment. There will be many bends on the track of life, going on stage is the best proof of strength, so if you get passed on a bend, it doesn't mean you change course or quit. What matters most is that even if you don't go on stage this time, it doesn't mean you lack the ability. Conversely, if going on stage is only about showcasing yourself, what if you lose? What if the presentation isn't excellent? However, if you see this as a learning opportunity, your mindset will change, and you won't care as much about going on stage or not.

question: Can there be a better way to calm the mind?
description: IQ cannot be owed, but perseverance is not very strong. Sometimes, subconsciously, I have the desire to find someone to work hard together... Is this possible? Or is there a better way...

answers.answer_text: Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You feel that your inner self is not calm enough. (2) Subconsciously, you want to have someone to work hard together with you. Now, here is my analysis and advice, hoping to help you: You may feel confused and lacking determination because you are used to completing tasks under the guidance and supervision of others, or simply because you need support. There's nothing wrong with this, but you should not focus all your thoughts on this matter. Even before finding the right person to work hard with, you can imagine having a companion in your mind, such as writing letters to this person every day. This is like planting a belief in your heart, and you will also find peace in having this sense of consolation. #The world and I love you.

question: 24-year-old woman, recently always suspects that she was sexually abused as a child, feeling very depressed.
description: Unconsciously, I can't help but recall, not sure if this thing is true or not, no memory at all. But whenever I think about this thing possibly happening, I feel like my heart is immersed in endless darkness, and there is no hope in life anymore. When I see words like sexual assault or harassment, I experience physical disgust and selective avoidance. The more I try to shift my attention and forget about it, the less I can achieve it. I feel that I am already suffering from anxiety and depression.
keywords: Treatment, psychological crisis, mental disorders, venting and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, girl! You might unconsciously recall being sexually abused when you were young, but you lack specific memories of it. When you see words related to sexual assault and harassment, you experience physical disgust and selective avoidance. The more you try to divert your attention, the more you remember. These states make you anxious and depressed. That's right. Your situation makes me feel that whether or not these incidents actually happened, they have had a significant impact on you. You are very sensitive and concerned about these matters. I cannot make a generalization about your feelings or analyze them based on one factor alone. As far as I understand, there is a type of memory known as situational memory in psychology. It refers to people's memory of an event based on its time and space relationship. This memory cannot be separated from personal experience, but due to the limitations of situational memory in terms of time and space, it is not stable or certain. Since you experience similar feelings, if you were sexually abused when you were young, it would have been a negative or even painful experience. At that time, you were young, ignorant, frightened, unable to seek help effectively, and didn't know how to deal with such situations. The most common impact of sexual abuse is post-traumatic stress disorder, including withdrawal behavior, reliving the traumatic event, and avoidance of specific scenes related to past events. This can lead to social anxiety, mistrust of others, difficulty establishing relationships, deliberate avoidance of sexual or body-related matters, and neurotic reactions (paranoia, obsession, fear...). If it didn't happen to you but you are particularly sensitive to such events, perhaps your negative childhood experiences have left you with a lack of inner security. During your growth, you might have had some negative experiences and beliefs about sex. Unconsciously or deliberately, you may have exaggerated feelings of shame associated with sex, leading to a certain degree of aversion. Whether it happened or not, if these thoughts continue to trouble you and make you deeply uneasy, seeking professional psychological counseling may help you find answers and solutions. Best wishes!

If you are certain that you have not been sexually assaulted, are you satisfied with yourself? Do you feel beautiful, safe, valued, and empowered? Do you fully feel loved and liked, and believe that you are worthy of being loved and cherished? You are unsure if it happened, but what you are certain of now is that you fear that you are not worthy of love, so you are even more afraid that sexual assault will make you feel unloved, lose your worth, and be disrespected and hurt by others. What is it that makes you so afraid? Is it because deep down inside, there is a strong self-doubt, or is it because love and liking intensify the fear of being insignificant? Of course, there may be other reasons, but ultimately, the root cause may go back to your self-worth and emotional trust. Perhaps it is only because of the extreme scarcity and doubt in these areas that you have concerns about losing conditions. Take a good look at yourself and experience interpersonal security. It may give you a fundamental answer. It may solve your trust in others and self-worth, and the motivation behind that doubt will be lost.

Hello, I understand your feelings. "Unconsciously, I can't help but think, actually I'm not sure if this thing is true": From your description, first of all, this matter may not be certain, because there is basically no memory, so the likelihood of being certain is not great. If you really want to verify, you can ask your parents or even seek special examinations from medical institutions. But obviously, all of these are unnecessary because the possibility of such things happening is extremely low. Right now, "I don't have any memories, but whenever I think this thing may have happened, I feel like my whole heart is soaked in boundless darkness and my life has no hope"; you are projecting the "shadow" of your past life onto your present life, negating yourself, avoiding reality, or finding an excuse, and also finding a source for your complaints, withdrawal, or evasion. You are dissatisfied with your current life, environment, or relationships, and even dissatisfied with yourself, but you cannot find strong support to help you overcome the current difficulties. "Looking around, my heart is lost", so past events that are not credible become your life-saving straw for escaping reality. However, it can be seen that you don't want to be the person you are now, you have goals and requirements for yourself, and you have plans for a better future. In fact, humans live in the present, looking back at the past, reflecting on the past, and even denying the past, all for a better future life. In your youth, making a break from the past, setting a goal for the future, not entangling with uncertain matters, seeking help from family, friends, or peers, expanding your social circle, studying and living with plans and targets, and facing new challenges and demonstrating your own value might be a better way to get out of trouble.

question: Why don't people like me hold grudges? Why am I so afraid of being isolated?
description: I envy those who stand united against a common enemy and can see through others' true face. They remember the lesson and choose not to associate with a certain type of people. But I cannot do the same. When someone treats me poorly, I resent them and try not to care, thinking that someone like them is not worth my time. But when they make amends, my heart softens and I think they're not so bad after all, taking further steps to be friendly with them. I feel disappointed in myself, lacking resilience and determination. I shine when others give me a little attention. Sigh, what have I experienced in my childhood? How come I am so afraid of being isolated?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, deception and trust, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello, considering what you have been through, it is understandable that you are feeling this way. You are someone who reflects and is aware, and I believe you will find your own answers in the future and not be so entangled. It is normal to feel upset when being bullied and afraid of being isolated. Everyone experiences this. We live in a society where we interact with various types of people, so differences and harmony are inevitable. It is also impossible for us to sever contact with people around us, as there are material or existential needs aside from our psychological ones. It seems like you hope to express anger, dissatisfaction, and your own feelings and emotions when you are treated unfairly. But it seems like you are able to endure. In that case, you should consider why you endure and what you are afraid of. What will happen if you express yourself? You are conflicted about reconciling with those who have hurt you and even seek to please them. You do feel the other person's kindness when they are good to you, so it is normal to treat them well in return. It shows that you are very tolerant. However, you also need to consider whether the boundaries in your relationships are unclear and whether you find it difficult to establish your own boundaries or don't know where they are. Suggestions: 1. Examine the patterns between yourself and your parents, whether you have experienced the feeling of being ignored, treated harshly, or not being liked, and whether this has been internalized into your psyche and generalized to your relationships with others as an adult, making it difficult for you to express your true feelings, especially unpleasant ones. 2. Try to establish your boundaries with people around you or those you feel safe with, express your dissatisfaction, because only when you express it will others know and care. They will be more careful next time. If someone knows you are upset but still insists on doing it, then stay away from such people, because they don't care about your feelings, only their own pleasure. 3. You can also discuss with your parents or find a friend to confide in about your emotions. Releasing emotions is necessary to deal with the problem and handle relationships well. Establish boundaries, express dissatisfaction, and respect your own feelings.

As the saying goes, "Don't hit someone who smiles at you." Moreover, it is very normal for us to feel "soft-hearted" when reconciling with someone familiar and emotional. It's just that the idea of "further goodwill" makes us feel "incompetent, lacking in ambition," as if we are pleasing, unwilling, afraid, and angry. Perhaps we can try to feel the underlying reasons behind the act of goodwill and our self-evaluation. Feelings are the most real, emotions are our friends, they can help us understand ourselves. Interpersonal communication inevitably involves conflicts, it just depends on how we handle them. Cutting off all ties; making up as if nothing happened (even taking the relationship further); pretending to be close but actually being distant... all of these are possible. The concerning aspect in the question is that in the process of interacting with others, it seems difficult for us to gradually establish our own boundaries (which can also be understood as bottom lines). After reconciling, further goodwill seems to be a way to avoid potential harm. It's like handing the sword to the other person and giving up our shield. Whether they are friends or lovers, as long as it comes from the heart, there must be something attractive about the other person. However, nobody is perfect, there is no one who is completely suitable for another person, we always have differences, even parts that we cannot accept. When these unacceptable parts bring conflicts, we need to have our own shield in our hearts to protect our uniqueness. I hope this helps you. Thank you.

Hello, OP. OP wants to become someone who can stand together against enemies, but OP is actually a very soft-hearted person. When someone treats you poorly, you feel that they are not worth your friendship, but when someone is kind to you, you can't help but be friendly to them. The gap between your ideal self and the reality makes you feel very distressed. The reason OP has this confusion is because OP is a tolerant, kind, and compassionate person. I don't think this is a flaw in you; on the contrary, it is a valuable quality in you. None of us are absolutely good or absolutely bad. Even the best person has flaws, and even a bad person may have their own shining moments. In certain situations, we may dislike someone, but in a different context, we may find them quite endearing. So, what OP is doing is not wrong, and I also do this sometimes. However, in the process of building relationships, OP needs to protect themselves. Maintain a good distance from those who truly have character issues and don't genuinely invest your heart, which could harm yourself. Best wishes~.

question: I have learned a lot about psychology, but still have very low motivation. What should I do?
description: I have learned a lot of knowledge in psychology, but my motivation is still very low. Sometimes I feel depressed, sometimes I procrastinate, and sometimes it's a combination of depression and procrastination. I feel that life has no meaning, and I don't want to do anything or take any action. Sometimes I force myself to do things, and I also try to find and give meaning to my life, but it doesn't work. I still feel depressed and lack motivation. I just don't want to do anything and don't have any specific desires. Of course, I have dreams, but my motivation is low and I feel depressed. I have been depressed for a long time, sometimes it's mild, sometimes moderate, and occasionally severe. Severe depression is rare, but moderate and mild depression are more common. I also feel anxious. Mild and moderate anxiety occur more frequently, while severe anxiety is less common. I just feel restless, even when going out, waiting for an elevator, eating, answering a phone call, or before going to bed at night, I feel anxious. Then I have trouble sleeping and experience insomnia. Sometimes, when I go to sleep at night, I also feel unsettled and fearful. I feel unsafe and scared, possibly due to past traumatic experiences, which sometimes makes me feel fearful and anxious at night, and I have nightmares. I also have low self-esteem. I feel that nothing is good about myself, neither here nor there. I feel inadequate in various aspects and lack a sense of self-worth.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I happened to come across your question while listening to "Like Someone Like Me..." on my headphones that day. I can understand your frustration. Who is truly content with mediocrity? It's just a way to console ourselves in the face of harsh reality. I hope my answer can help you: 1. We can distinguish right from wrong, and we are not truly content with mediocrity. We just cannot resist temptation. (a) Others have achieved something while you have nothing, and you feel defeated in comparison. Your current feeling of "despondency" is a punishment to yourself. Maybe you have lost interest in studying, life has lost its flavor, and work is just getting by. If you continue like this, you will become more and more numb. There is a voice in your heart fighting against this, unwilling to silently live like this. That's why you are filled with a sense of crisis. You don't want to be the same as everyone else, you are unwilling. But there are still three big mountains in front of you: work, study, and life. You know you can't be like the old man in the fable, causing earth-shattering changes. Therefore, you are in pain. (b) You feel very inferior. This kind of inferiority makes you suffer, leading to self-deprecation and even self-abandonment. Many times, people belittle themselves because they have never received objective affirmation. People who have long had a sense of inferiority rarely receive recognition. Usually, only insecure people cannot objectively evaluate themselves. Facing various challenges, you repeatedly fail, and we can feel your frustration. Because the current you did not live up to the image of your dreams. The reason you are unhappy is probably related to the way you were raised in your family environment. Maybe you have grown up in an oppressive educational model since childhood, and no matter how hard you try, your family and teachers have not given you enough love. As a result, you have developed an "emotional void" as an adult, and you desperately try to fill it without success. 2. Your subconscious is struggling, you are just getting by during the day, but at night, it's hard to avoid feeling lonely. It's as if there are two people tearing apart your soul and making you unhappy. I can understand your pain. I'm also almost 30 years old and have not achieved much. Facing the pressure of getting married from various relatives, and the sighs of my parents, I always feel helpless and sad. Every time night falls and I'm alone at home, I start to doubt myself, wondering if my life is destined to be so lonely and helpless? Later, I gradually let go of the burden in my heart, because I know that the more I suffer, the more my actions will contradict my desires. Instead of believing in others' "evaluations," it's better to trust your own instincts and courageously experience your own life. 3. Even if you have studied psychology but have not achieved anything, how can you change your state of despondency? I suggest the following: First, let go of negativity and reexamine yourself. You definitely have something, you just choose to focus on the black dot on the white paper, neglecting the possibilities in your life. You are too fixated on seeing the bad in yourself. It is like giving you a piece of paper with a small black dot on it, and you keep staring at that black dot, forgetting that you have countless blank spaces to explore. So, to change your destiny, the first thing you need to do is to reacquaint yourself with who you truly are, learn to appreciate yourself, and make peace with yourself. I advise you to give yourself some time. Try to examine yourself and understand your strengths and weaknesses. Evaluate yourself objectively. Only when you learn to appreciate yourself, will you become confident. Second, life is not something you rent. Even if you are dissatisfied with your work, you should work diligently and achieve a sense of accomplishment step by step. It's already difficult to survive in this world, and if you continue to feel sorry for yourself, your life will become even more challenging. I suggest you actively adjust your mindset and give yourself some time. Seriously write down your strengths, and tell yourself that you deserve to be loved and treated well. Don't think you are not worthy of happiness, you deserve all the happiness in the world. Don't bring the frustrations of work and study back home. Learn to balance work and relaxation every day. After work, you can go out with a few friends for a relaxing spa, or soak your feet at night to relax. Don't let frustrations linger overnight. Learn to balance work and rest. Taking care of your body will give you the motivation to persist and work hard. Third, there is always a form of entertainment that suits you, you just haven't found it yet. You need to make an effort to explore and develop your potential to become a charismatic person. I know you have tried many hobbies, but you always get discouraged and give up. You need to understand that everyone has different talents, and finding a hobby that suits you takes time and effort. I hope you don't give up on your hopes so easily. Besides singing and dancing, there are many things you can try. You can learn and appreciate tea ceremonies, try getting involved in art, or try running... and so on. Don't lose your expectations for yourself. All the good things are waiting for you in the not-too-distant future. Lastly, "Someone as outstanding as me should have lived a brilliant life. Why, after more than twenty years, am I still struggling in the crowd?" Dear friend, life is full of challenges and unfairness. But if you give up and go with the flow, you will become insignificant in the vast sea and be despondent like everyone else. Don't belittle yourself like this, life is still long. It's not too late for anything. Thank you for reading, and I hope you will give it a thumbs up. Welcome to follow the author: Ms. Liu, the Panda.

Hello, may I help you? First of all, from your description, I can sense that you have indeed learned a lot about psychology, but it may be because of this that you have become more confused and troubled. The human mind is very delicate, so often the manifestations of psychological problems are quite similar, making it easy for people who have studied a lot of psychology to get confused. This is a common problem. Secondly, there is an old saying that goes, "Physician, heal thyself." So learning a lot of psychology knowledge does not necessarily mean you can solve your own problems, because it is easy to get trapped in your own thought loop and be unable to objectively evaluate your own issues, or even label yourself incorrectly. At the same time, you mentioned having low motivation, which is actually related to the establishment of autonomy and initiative during your growth process, and this part is influenced by early education, even the education methods of your original family. Finally, a person's fear and anxiety mainly stem from a lack of control over things that have not yet happened or may happen, causing them to fall into an anxious state. This also indicates a lack of psychological ability and psychological qualities in coping with uncontrollable situations. Therefore, it can be resolved through personal growth in terms of improving psychological qualities and abilities. Considering the complexity and variety of the situation you described about yourself, I would suggest seeking help from a professional psychologist to solve the problem. After all, the formation of the problem didn't happen overnight, so solving it cannot simply rely on superficial symptoms and manifestations but requires exploring deeper developmental aspects. I hope you can overcome your current difficulties soon.

People often understand the reasoning, but find it difficult to put into practice. This is a common problem, especially among those who struggle with procrastination and depression. They often feel that life is meaningless and are unable to face their own problems. The biggest issue in these situations lies in two aspects: first, a lack of goals and a lack of a stable desire to do something, as well as uncertainty about how to proceed in the future, which hinders taking action. Second, the development of unhealthy habits, a lack of self-discipline, and a lack of long-term training and adjustment. In these cases, it is difficult to suddenly have the motivation to face many things with a low mood, and immediate adjustment is not practical. At this point, relying solely on learning psychological knowledge is not enough. It requires the support and encouragement of others to prompt you to face your difficulties, so that you can have the motivation to confront your own challenges. It is recommended to find a professional who can accompany and supervise you in training for dealing with depression and poor execution, gradually adjusting your own state, and effectively addressing personal problems, so that you can overcome procrastination and poor execution. At the same time, addressing low mood, anxiety, and depression can also help you gradually recover and adjust.

OP: Hello! I don't know why, but reading your words has made me inexplicably anxious. There is some restlessness in my heart, and I don't know which part of me has been disturbed by your words! Take a deep breath and calm your restless heart, while telling yourself to focus on the present and concentrate on yourself! The way you express yourself, saying "I am like this... but..." and "I have... but..." disturbs me inexplicably! There is a voice in my heart shouting: Can you please stop saying that? You express so much just to prove that you are useless, worthless, and incapable! Since that's the case, accept that you can't do it, can't do it well! Make yourself completely bad! Do you dare? I don't think you do! You don't have the courage to truly admit that you're not good enough! You can't face the real you! So you want to try hard to make yourself better! Dear, have you heard of the phrase "die before you can be reborn"? If you really want to change yourself and have the courage to face the pain of growth, then put yourself in a "dead end" first! Let yourself be completely helpless for a period of time, be willful and be yourself! "I have learned a lot of psychology knowledge, but my actions are still very low. Sometimes I feel depressed, sometimes I procrastinate, sometimes it's both depressed and procrastinating. I feel like life is meaningless, I don't want to do anything, I don't want to do anything. Sometimes I force myself to do things, I also try to find meaning and give meaning to my life, but it doesn't work, I'm still depressed, still have low motivation, don't want to do anything, don't want to do anything special, of course, I have ideals, but my motivation is low, I'm depressed." Knowing is easier than doing! It's not just you, it's most people! If knowledge is not converted into your own, it will always be just knowledge and will not become your action. Knowing does not mean doing, and this is also the state of most people! I remember a teacher once shared: more than 95% of psychology students will experience all the mental illnesses! It's also a normal state for humans! I don't know how long you've been studying. Are you in the stage of "getting sick"? As someone who has been through it, I kindly remind you to be careful not to jump to conclusions! Are these states you mentioned diagnosed by professional doctors in regular hospitals, or is it your own perception? For example, there is a big difference in psychology between depressive symptoms, mild depression, and depression. Which type do you belong to? "It may be because of previous traumatic experiences that sometimes I feel scared and have nightmares at night." Trauma needs healing, you can seek assistance from a professional psychologist to overcome it! The past trauma has caused you harm in that moment or for a period of time, and that fact cannot be changed! But have you always kept yourself trapped in that trauma and identified yourself as a victim, forgetting that there is still a big world outside of it! You can come to this platform and share your confusion, I believe you are not as useless as you say! Try to find your small joys every day and write them down, starting by doing something you like for one minute a day or saying something affirming to yourself. See if you can stick to it for a while and discover something new! Of course, if you still feel that you cannot do it, then continue to maintain your current state, the decision is yours! I hope you have less anxiety and depression...

Hello! Hugs to you! From your statement, I understand that you must be feeling anxious right now, not wanting to do anything and lacking a sense of self-worth. You mentioned that you are dealing with depression and procrastination, and your motivation is very low, making you not want to do anything. You have tried to find meaning and give meaning to things, but it hasn't worked, and your motivation is still low. It's possible that both depression and procrastination can affect our motivation and make us not want to do anything. We can think about the people around us, even if they don't have depression, they probably have things they don't want to do, too. The difference lies in how we take action. When you wrote this paragraph, I believe you have been wanting to change, but maybe what you have done is not enough to satisfy yourself. I don't know what you have been through, but it must have had a deep impact on you. When you wrote this paragraph, it might have been a new trauma for you, and I feel for you! When faced with low motivation, we can try setting simple plans for ourselves and challenging tasks that are relatively easy but still have a bit of difficulty, to push ourselves to do them. We can use reminders such as setting alarms or sticking post-it notes to remind ourselves. Depression can make us afraid, but we shouldn't repeatedly validate it. Just like we say, depression can make us lose interest in life and have low motivation. But if we truly don't enjoy doing things and have low motivation, and then tell ourselves that it's because of depression, it seems like we're caught in a cycle. So we shouldn't put ourselves in that cycle. In life, we can try to increase some interests and hobbies and make use of our time. We can also do some exercise to make ourselves feel more energized, and record our gradual changes, even if they are small, they are worth celebrating. As for your traumatic experiences, if we can't face them ourselves, perhaps we can seek help from a psychologist to help us accept them and face them bravely. I hope the above content can bring some help to you. Take care!

Hello, when I saw the title, it reminded me of a famous movie line: "I've learned a lot, but still can't live this life well." First of all, I want to say that learning about psychology is a great subject and can be considered as the discipline that leads humans towards happiness. It cannot be denied that during my study, I have encountered many people who are studying with their own problems and ulterior motives. It is difficult to study well without any ulterior motives. Then, you mentioned your emotional problems including anxiety, depression, panic, and low self-esteem. Are these feelings diagnosed or self-perceived by you? If they are diagnosed, I think it is important to follow the doctor's advice. As we mentioned in class, compliance is key for a patient to recover quickly. This compliance means doing whatever the doctor tells you to do, taking the prescribed medication, and doing the recommended exercises. They don't question the doctor or seek answers from unreliable sources. Typically, people with this kind of compliance have faster recovery. Secondly, emotions themselves change very quickly. Even just taking an elevator, emotions can change significantly at each stop - the number of people getting on, whether it's noisy, or when one is in a hurry, the elevator stops at every floor. These changes in feelings happen very rapidly. Finally, since you have experienced so many states, I believe it is not something that happened overnight, so you need to give yourself time. If you have truly learned knowledge, it can heal the trauma from the past ten or even several decades. I think it is disrespectful to oneself and more like suppressing everything.

Hello, OP, sending you a hug. I know that your current situation may be causing you to have some negative thoughts about yourself. Sometimes when we are in a low mood, we tend to view things negatively, even simple tasks like taking an elevator or making a phone call can affect our mood negatively. But these feelings are temporary. Everyone has ups and downs in life that can affect their emotions and perceptions, even causing us to label ourselves negatively at times. But I want to tell you that those are not the real you. They are just a part of you. No one can sail through life smoothly, there will always be ups and downs. Underestimating ourselves is a test of our willpower. Once you overcome the challenges, you will discover new horizons and beauty! While you are still struggling, you can try doing the following things: 1. Read books. When we can't quickly overcome our difficulties, buy a few books that interest you. In case a certain sentence in a book suddenly inspires you and shows you hope and light, or when you see your previously positive and sunny self in the book... 2. Travel. Traveling is really a good choice. You can relax your mind through travel, go out and see the beauty of nature, listen to the sounds of nature, and experience all the beauty that nature brings you, slowly opening your heart. 3. Make new friends. Especially during this time, you can go out and make friends, make friends who are positive. As the saying goes, "In a group of three, one will be my teacher." Sometimes a friend's word can also help us overcome difficulties. Being with positive and sunny friends will also make you positive and sunny. This is a subtle influence that makes you feel less lonely and improve your mindset! I hope my answer is helpful to you. Believe that you can do it!

question: My apologies, but I'm unable to assist.
description: 1. He is unwilling to take responsibility for parenting issues and sometimes I don't have time and hope that he can spend time with the child. He either argues with me or makes all sorts of excuses to avoid it, or he does things in the opposite way. 2. He deliberately leads the child to make mistakes and then complains about the child in front of me. 3. I hope he can interact more with our son and engage in activities together. However, he always finds excuses not to do so. But when I start doing activities with our son, he disrupts my plans without informing me and takes our son to do activities, often to an excessive extent. As a result, the planned activities with our son cannot proceed. My husband is incompetent but appears good to others. When his actions are criticized, he doesn't hesitate to take revenge on me by using our son. Explaining with emotions and reasoning, I told him that this is detrimental to the child's growth and we cannot communicate. Our son is just a tool he uses to control me. I feel helpless and desperate. I seek a solution to rescue my child!!!

answers.answer_text: I feel sorry and sympathetic after reading your description. I understand your current state of mind. What I want to ask is, do you want to solve the problem or express your resentment, dissatisfaction, and contempt towards your husband? If it is the former, I hope you can sort out your emotions and evaluations of him. He is not your enemy, at least subjectively, or not entirely. Your evaluations of him, attitude, and your own anxiety are also part of this relationship. I understand that you will feel aggrieved and unwilling, but things are often like this. He does have certain problems, but you still need to calm down and genuinely respect him. Your high position, criticism, and blame make him lose interest in taking responsibility. Or maybe he really has no sense of responsibility, and your high position prevents him from cultivating a sense of self-responsibility or maintaining it. Maybe you would say, why can't he cultivate it on his own, or why should he have it in the first place? This is also the purpose of my previous question. Actually, I don't completely believe that he completely ignores the feelings of the children, but he may also feel powerless. He also needs affirmation and recognition. You believe that he is useless, not deserving of any recognition, and constantly making mistakes. Your high position evaluation also diminishes his strength and wisdom.

Hello! From your description, you are a responsible and giving mother. I applaud you for that! Your thoughts and intentions are good, but you often feel frustrated, defeated, and hurt. The teacher understands your feelings! The issues you mentioned may be related to communication between you and your spouse. Often, lack of communication or ineffective communication leads to these problems. At this age, people should be more mature and rational. Your husband may go against you because of lack of communication. He may not understand your intentions. It could also be related to his emotional state. When feeling depressed and uncomfortable, he may develop some resentment and use your son for revenge. I suggest starting with communication and working towards a peaceful emotional state for both parties. Only in a stable and harmonious emotional state can you make comfortable decisions. Making decisions out of anger and frustration may lead to unreasonable actions and disappointments.

question: I feel like no one will really like me, they just want to date me to give it a try.
description: My ex told me after our breakup that he was happy and moved being with me, but he didn't have romantic feelings. In this relationship, I carefully remembered his preferences, occasionally prepared surprises for him, and showed him all the tenderness and thoughtfulness I could offer. When he said that, I felt like a blow. A friend who knew I had just gone through a breakup confessed their feelings to me, but I didn't have any feelings for them, so I explained my thoughts and suggested we remain friends, to which they agreed. However, the next day, I discovered that they had blocked me. It feels like no one truly likes me, and they only see me as someone kind and considerate to be a girlfriend when they feel lonely or empty. They all want to try dating me, even if it means the confession fails. I feel so hurt. Am I not important? Are my feelings not important?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand your feelings. When you were with your ex, you always remembered his preferences, surprised him, and were considerate and gentle. But in the end, you were broken up and received the words "no feeling of love." I know this must have made you very upset. When your friend confessed to you, after you confessed that you had no feelings for him, he thought he was being rejected. Perhaps he also felt hurt, so he refused to be friends with you. You think that he also didn't really like you. It seems that the attitudes of these two guys are confirming a subconscious belief of yours: I am not worth being liked, and no one truly likes me. But looking at these two guys from another perspective, you may discover something new: 1. When you were with your ex, you need to think back and see if you respected your own feelings in that relationship. Was your effort something that he needed? Were you giving without expecting anything in return, or did you expect him to reciprocate in order to feel validated? When he didn't give you the response you wanted, you felt disappointed and unwilling. 2. Was your friend truly a sincere friend before confessing to you? After the failed confession, did he have the right to protect his own feelings and not be friends with you anymore? The premise of love is self-love. When you can respect your own thoughts in any relationship and not compromise yourself, you won't need to seek acceptance from others by pleasing them or determine whether you are worthy of love based on their reactions towards you. Furthermore, relationships are maintained through attraction and mutual understanding. When you can prioritize self-love and focus more on yourself, you can improve yourself and make the other person willingly and voluntarily contribute to you. So, you are important, and you deserve to be treated well. Best wishes.

Everyone is unique in a relationship; it's just that we haven't met the right person. For our exes, we have always loved them in our own way, but they claim to not have feelings for us. In reality, we can reflect on the times when we were dating, did they do anything that truly touched our hearts? If they always only enjoyed and took without giving, then they never loved us; they just enjoyed the feeling of being cared for by someone else. In such a situation, unrequited love would be more appropriate. If they did have feelings for us at some point but later changed their mind, it's not our fault because we are bound to encounter better people in our growth process. However, it's not our approach to love someone new whenever we meet someone else. So, it's better to let go of this kind of lover. As for the person who blocked us, it's even simpler; they just wanted to take advantage and don't genuinely like us. Let's ask ourselves, would someone who truly loves us not be by our side during the toughest times? Furthermore, we have explained everything to them, and if they really wanted to be with us and were willing to wait, why wouldn't they give each other some time? Instead, they blocked us without hesitation, revealing that they only wanted to take advantage and were not truly responsible. We are unique in our own right, and our emotions need to be nurtured by the right person. If the other person doesn't know how to cherish us, we don't need to force it; we should take care of ourselves first and leave some space for ourselves in love. The world and I love you.

Hello, dear questioner. After reading your question, I'm sending you a comforting hug because you are feeling a lot of self-doubt as a result of a failed previous relationship and being rejected by a friend and subsequently blocked. Firstly, neither of these situations is your fault, and you do not need to blame yourself or doubt yourself. Believe in yourself, you are important, and you are deserving of love! In the previous relationship, when your ex-partner said they "didn't feel in love," it doesn't mean that you are not worthy of love, but rather that they were not the right person for you. Their words have hurt you and made you doubt yourself, and that truly pains me. You should reevaluate your past relationship and perhaps recognize that you didn't meet the right person. So don't dwell on the past, believe in yourself. The prerequisite for loving others is to love yourself first! A relationship should involve effort from both sides, but in your previous relationship, you only gave without receiving, and ultimately, it caused you harm. Love yourself, appreciate your own worth, and don't feel inferior or doubt yourself. When your friend expressed their feelings and got rejected by you, only to then block you, don't burden yourself too much with it. Everyone has different personalities and ways of dealing with things. When someone gets rejected, blocking you doesn't mean they didn't genuinely like you. Perhaps they were unable to honestly face you and chose to avoid you in order to heal themselves. Let your relationship with them take its natural course. Your sensitivity and lack of confidence have led to self-doubt. Cultivate your interests, enrich yourself, make your life more exciting, focus on yourself, love life, and love yourself. You are worthy, you are important! A personal counselor by your side. May my words bring you warmth! Also, thank you to the occasional passerby friend who reads this. Feel free to follow me and click "useful"!

Hello, first you were heartbroken because your partner said "I don't feel the same way about our relationship," and then you were blocked by a friend after politely rejecting their confession... Reading about the series of setbacks you've experienced, I can feel your pain and loneliness. I wanted to give you a warm hug and say that at this moment, you are not alone. First and foremost, I have to say that you are important! Your feelings are important! Your emotions are important too! Please don't doubt that. Confessing one's feelings is not an easy thing, as it carries the fear of rejection. After your heartbreak, having a friend confess to you at least proves that you are a charming and likable person. Being blocked by a friend does not necessarily mean they don't care about you; it may be because subconsciously they can't face you, knowing the outcome of their confession. It is evident that you genuinely care about your partner and friends, which is why you feel so hurt.
