However, we need to know that any relationship, be it romantic or friendship, is closely related to both parties involved and influenced by many complex factors for it to be established and sustained. In other words, if a relationship falls apart, it is not solely the fault of one party, and it does not mean that no one "truly likes you." So, what does it mean to "truly like" someone? Different people have different interpretations of "liking" someone. Based on your description, it seems like what you need is a beautiful, long-lasting relationship that won't easily break. Is that correct? Your partner gave the reason for ending the relationship as "not feeling the romantic spark." But what exactly is the "romantic spark"? It may be a familiar feeling associated with past experiences for some people. For others, it could be a romantic and thrilling sensation. And for some, it could be feeling "happy" and "moved," with your "gentleness and thoughtfulness" being the "romantic spark." However, it is possible that we cannot immediately determine what kind of love we need, what kind of person we "truly like." It's not something that can be figured out in an instant. This is why we try to start a relationship, try to make it work, but then we might gradually realize that it's not the relationship we need, that we're not compatible with each other. In that case, we can choose to end it and continue to explore new possibilities. And in the future, we might gradually realize that what we had before was the most suitable, and we can try to rekindle it. This is how human relationships are, flexible and full of various possibilities. So please believe in yourself, keep trying to find the "relationship" that truly suits you, and give yourself more opportunities and possibilities. You can do it!

question: Everyday chores, how can one live their own life?
description: Everyday, it's the same old routine of basic necessities and mundane life. There is no sense of novelty in any given day. Suddenly, it feels incredibly boring! I don't know what I truly want, and I have no idea what the purpose of my existence is. How can I live for myself?

answers.answer_text: Hello, sending you a warm hug. It is true that our daily life can be monotonous, but the monotony lies in the daily tasks we have to do, not in our entire life. Otherwise, we would become robots, wouldn't we? We can create a sense of novelty ourselves. If life feels meaningless, we can think of some fun ways to change it up. For example, occasionally read our favorite books or watch our favorite shows, or slightly modify the structure and arrangement of our room, adding some "little joys" to our life, which can effectively adjust our life. Of course, the most important thing to understand the meaning of our existence is to know why we are alive. Some people find happiness in earning money, although it may sound mundane, diving headfirst into making money can also bring joy. Some people strive for higher ideals, improving themselves to help others, engaging in charity work, spreading love, and some people hope to excel in their fields...and so on. So, what are you enduring this kind of life for? Do you already have a goal or not yet? The results of proactive acceptance and passive acceptance are completely different.

question: I like a girl, but suddenly, I don't know how to make a decision when looking back on the past.
description: I recently developed a liking for a girl and it's bothering me. I don't know if she is seeing someone or how she feels about me. At the same time, I have a good relationship with another girl, but it seems like I just can't develop that kind of liking for her. As I was thinking about it, I suddenly recalled two similar experiences I had in high school. Both times, there was a girl who liked me and our relationship was ambiguous, but at the same time, I would develop feelings for another girl. I don't know if it's because of the pressure or because I'm weak, but from my previous experiences, I regretted rejecting the girls who liked me and they suddenly became very attractive to me, yet I couldn't get close to them again... I don't know what choice to make now. Should I give it a try with the girl who likes me? Or should I continue pursuing the girl I currently have a 'feeling' for (even though it seems like she's out of reach)?
keywords: Love, single, sense of security, liking.

answers.answer_text: "What you need is not these two girls, but facing yourself. Confused people tend to create ambiguity because they don't even know what they want. First of all, the fear of rejection is actually the fear of facing your own insecurities and lack of confidence, being afraid of being rejected by others. A man who knows what kind of girl he wants will usually have the courage to ask the other person if they already have a partner. If they don't, he will try to pursue them; if they do, he will immediately let go and find someone else. He is straightforward, even if he is rejected, he knows the answer. But what about you? You are afraid of being rejected, prefer to waste your own and other people's time, and stay in an ambiguous relationship. You are willing to waste time and procrastinate rather than face the truth. You lack the courage to face reality and lack confidence in dealing with rejection. If you find out that the other person has a partner, you feel like you are not good enough, so the other person didn't choose you. If that's the case, you are avoiding facing yourself, afraid of facing your own insecurities. Second, ambiguity is not love. 1. Love is not a cure for your deficiencies. We all enjoy being loved, even if we know we don't like that person, we still want them to like us. Why? We yearn for attention, care, and love from someone. But love is not a tool for healing, using someone else's admiration to heal yourself without loving them back is taking advantage of them. 2. Wasting someone else's time and emotions is equivalent to invading their boundaries because time and emotions belong to someone else, and it's only fair to respect them as you would want yours to be respected. 3. Loving someone is about fulfilling them and wishing them well, not worrying about whether you will fail. If you find out that the other person has a partner and you truly love her, you would congratulate her and be happy for her. Many people have the misconception that jealousy is a manifestation of love. Jealousy is only about possession and wanting to have someone, but that's not love. If you really liked these two girls so much, I think you would have confessed your feelings long ago. Third, what you need is not these two girls, but facing yourself. 1. Facing your insecurities makes you react negatively to the outside world, which leads to your avoidance and procrastination. Solution: Use daily journaling to record the areas where you deserve praise until you develop positive reactions to the outside world. No longer feeling insecure, taking responsibility for your actions, and recognizing your inner worth. 2. Independent satisfaction of your emotional needs. Respect your emotional needs and learn to satisfy them independently. Understand the emotional needs behind all your motives and learn to satisfy them independently, rather than seeking emotions from others through ambiguity. 3. Think about what you really want. Everyone experiences confusion, but ambiguity is definitely not the way out or the solution. Think about whether you want a relationship to fulfill your own needs or if you genuinely love someone. Because love is about giving and gratitude, not about taking and entitlement. When someone's emotions become independent, you really don't need to seek love through taking advantage or being selfish. I remember a famous psychotherapist said: 'Immature love says, "I love you because I need you." Mature love says, "I need you because I love you."' If you truly love someone, you don't need to worry about being rejected because you will fulfill and wish them well. If you truly love yourself, you don't need to fear rejection because even if the outside world rejects you, it doesn't define you. You are who you are, and whether the outside world rejects you or not has nothing to do with your worth. Your existence itself is an achievement. Love yourself, and at the same time, cherish the people who like you. Wishing you well, namaste!"

---If you choose a girl that you like, you must be prepared for the possibility of failure. The girl may not like you back. At the same time, pursuing a girl you are interested in requires a lot of time, energy, and money. Of course, the most important thing is to give love. There is nothing wrong with liking someone, it is your right. However, it is also the other person's right to not like you. Just because you give everything for someone doesn't mean they have to accept you. One-sided love is painful. True happiness comes from mutual love. So, you can choose the girl you like, but be prepared for failure, and that will be enough. Accept that capturing water in a bamboo basket leads to empty results, and that will be enough. If you choose a girl who likes you, it is much simpler. If she loves you, she will naturally give more for you, and you just need to cherish her love for you, and that will be enough. In fact, the happiest thing in life is to be loved. If a girl loves you, it may be a blessing from a previous life. It is said that it takes five hundred years of encounters in a past life to earn a glance in this life. Not to mention if the girl has already let go of her reservations and expressed her love for you. Learn to cherish it and give her a chance. Perhaps she is the right person for you. If it really doesn't work out, there's no need to force it. But no matter what, you have to actively make the choice. Because if we don't make choices, life will press the default button for us and choose the lesser option. So, our lives should be in our own hands. We make our own choices. We are responsible for our choices. And that will be enough. May your life be filled with sunshine. I have always been here.

Hello, the same experience that happened before is happening again! There are two things that need to be clear: 1. Do you think the girl who currently likes you really likes you, or do you believe that she likes you? 2. Do you like the girl you like because you genuinely like her, or because you are dissatisfied with the girl who has feelings for you and have shifted your focus to someone else? The two experiences are very similar, and there is a kind of feeling that you only like this ambiguous feeling. Just like after rejecting the girl who likes you, you may find her very charming. So you need to think about it, perhaps what you have been seeking is this elusive feeling! You can follow and consult with me, hoping to help you!

question: Is the likelihood of dying from jumping into a river high?
description: I just want to understand, when you jump into a river, how long will it take to die? Can you die completely, without any chance of being saved?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm curious as to why you would ask about the likelihood of death from jumping into a river. Do you have suicidal thoughts yourself? How long have you been feeling this way? Do people around you know about this? Have you considered reaching out to a mental health professional or counselor? I believe that there is no suicide method that guarantees a hundred percent success, especially with jumping into a river in a public place. There are various possibilities and accidents that could occur, and the likelihood of being saved is also very high. I once watched a TED talk called "Breaking the Silence for Suicide Survivors," where the speaker actually attempted to jump into a river to commit suicide. He bravely shared his experience and hoped to tell everyone that if they have suicidal thoughts or if someone around them does, they should speak up and seek help. "This is a topic that can be discussed." I agree with this perspective. I think the reason we consider suicide is because we feel hopeless and believe that death is the only way out. But by speaking out and seeking help, we may realize that there are many other options and not just the path of death. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Feeling uncomfortable when seeing others doing well?
description: It feels uncomfortable when I see others doing well. Today, my sister also went to get a double eyelid surgery, and my aunt says it looks good on her. This makes me particularly uncomfortable.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, jealousy is something everyone has, and it depends on how we deal with it. If we can transform jealousy into motivation to improve ourselves, we may touch upon something even better. On the other hand, if we let jealousy drive us, the shadows in our hearts will only grow. I understand your feelings very well, especially when you and your sister do the same things and she receives praise while you don't, this feeling can be even stronger. Perhaps because both of you are girls, your family unconsciously compares you, one being better in one aspect and the other being slightly worse in another, and so on. Your family must have praised you more than your sister in other areas as well. They are not intentionally dissatisfied with you, it is your inner jealousy causing trouble. Take a moment to reflect, does this jealousy happen frequently? Not only with your sister, but do you also feel uncomfortable when you see others doing better than you? Maybe your family's encouragement and validation are not enough, making you really want recognition in different aspects. Try to look at your own strengths and advantages positively, you also have qualities that others envy and are jealous of, discover those points. When your own feeling of inferiority or envy arises, use these points to give yourself positive suggestions. It is indeed best when your jealousy can motivate you to make positive changes. For example, if your family compliments your sister's beautiful eyelids, remember that beauty is not just external, it also comes from within. If you cannot generate confidence externally, try to cultivate your own temperament and talents. However, it is important to understand that following other people's evaluations and opinions will not help you find your own path. Just because they are not satisfied with certain aspects of us or hope we conform to certain standards, does not mean we have to change. For example, if someone tells us today that all our features are good, but our nose is a little big, you might fixate on that aspect, becoming very agitated internally until one day, you get surgery. This applies not only to appearance but also when people clash with our values and beliefs. If their suggestions or opinions are objective and rational, then we should strive to improve ourselves. However, if we believe we are worthless because of such suggestions from others, this kind of perception needs to change. Best wishes.

question: What women ultimately pursue, love or material wealth?
description: Just finished watching "The Great Gatsby" and was confused by Daisy's emotions in the movie. Is it because of the changes in age or different experiences that have turned her into a different person from the past? Materialism seems to have gained the upper hand in her heart, and in the end, she still relies on material possessions. Is materialism the only guarantee?
keywords: Growth, character development, and the meaning of life

answers.answer_text: Hello, after reading your description, I thought of a phrase, "Without material love, it is like a scattered sand." Although this phrase may be a bit extreme, it is not without reason. Daisy has become a different person because of her experiences. When women are young, they prioritize emotions and do not care about material things. However, as they age, people become more practical and care more about material possessions. Our teacher once showed us a video, a study conducted in the United States, which found that men tend to seek young and beautiful women as partners, while women tend to seek men with strong economic ability and high social status. According to the explanation of evolutionary psychology, men choose partners based on reproductive and offspring goals, and young and beautiful women imply stronger reproductive ability. Women give birth to children after marriage, and they need a reliable and capable father for their children. Strong economic strength and high social status mean having more resources. In our reality, it is also the case that women tend to seek partners with strong economic ability. Of course, most relationships are still built on a foundation of love. Love and material possessions are both necessary ingredients for a good relationship. Best wishes~.

question: How to reject some overly friendly people?
description: There are a few people in the workplace, mostly women. Whenever they encounter a problem, they would complain about how they cannot handle it and the leaders would easily agree to their requests, sometimes even assigning the tasks to me. They seem very righteous, but in my opinion, these are not big issues and they shouldn't make such a fuss. How should I deal with these kinds of people?

answers.answer_text: Hi OP. Seeing your description, this is indeed a troubling issue. Sending you a virtual hug! I believe you know that having boundaries is necessary in interpersonal relationships. Boundaries can make our relationships more stable and balanced, and they are especially important in the workplace. For example, clear division of responsibilities is a form of boundaries. I won't elaborate on these things that I think you already know, because your concern is "how" to refuse. You want to know how to say no without being disturbed and without offending your leaders and colleagues. Here are some thoughts on how to say no: daring to refuse is difficult for many of us. We always worry that saying no is impolite or cold-hearted. But if we never learn to refuse, we will become more and more boundaryless. We will waste too much time and energy on unnecessary things, and force ourselves to do things we don't want to do or feel we shouldn't do, which will bring feelings of suppression and various negative emotions. So practicing saying no is a required course. In the process of practicing saying no, we also gradually build our courage and become more clear about what we want and what we don't want. We gradually understand and see what we truly think deep in our hearts. We also become more willing to fight for ourselves. Saying no is an important step in helping us become ourselves. When refusing, we should be decisive. We are used to not refusing, so when we start practicing saying no, there is always self-blame and doubt when refusing others. We feel guilty, unsure, and uncertain. Therefore, our refusals are always ambiguous or lack confidence, such as "Let me see if I can do it for you," or "Let me try, but I can't guarantee if I can help." But if we consider these as refusals, we not only make it difficult for ourselves but also hinder others. Because the other person will assume that you have agreed, and if you can't complete it on time due to various reasons, and the other person can't do it themselves in time, not only will you feel guilty, but the other person will also be angry, and it will also delay things and time. Therefore, once we have made up our minds and determined that "I want to refuse this matter, I don't want to do it," a firm refusal is the best choice for both parties: - Accepting our own limitations, "I'm sorry, I really want to help you, but I can't." - Purely not wanting to help: "I'm sorry, I can't help/I can't do it!" You don't always have to find a reason to tell others or convince yourself to have the confidence to refuse. You have the confidence and freedom to say no, so you can refuse without any reason and dare to refuse. This will also earn the respect of others. After a few times, your colleagues and leaders might think to themselves, "Oh, OP has become more capable." They will know that you have boundaries and principles. If your leader is smart, they will definitely see your growth in this aspect and appreciate and value you more. Having boundaries can also provide flexibility. After we learn and dare to refuse, we can have some flexibility based on our feelings and circumstances. Does having flexibility mean not refusing and accepting everything? No, this flexibility is not about sacrificing and not daring to refuse anymore. Now we can refuse with peace of mind. We can choose to help or not. Regardless of our choice, we can be at peace with ourselves. Our inner psychological flexibility will also increase. I hope this is helpful to you. Blessings to you: Smooth sailing in your career! The world and I love you.

Congratulations, it seems that your workplace is a government-funded organization, right? From the looks of it, there are quite a few colleagues in your workplace who like to shirk responsibility and make excuses. You think that what they did wasn't a big deal, but they cunningly exploited it, knowing that you are easily influenced. So, there's a saying, "fight fire with fire." Treat others the way they treat you.

question: My boyfriend has tendencies of depression, what can I do to help him?
description: My boyfriend has been showing signs of depression recently. He doesn't want to talk and just wants to be alone and do nothing. It has been going on for a while now. What can I do to help him? Should I try to cheer him up or just let him be and stay quiet?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, there is a movie called "Husband with Depression" that I recommend you to watch. The production team specially invited a psychiatric expert as a consultant to ensure that there are no medical inaccuracies in the film. This movie realistically portrays the life of an individual and a couple dealing with depression, for example: #The wife learns a lot of knowledge to understand what depression is, its symptoms, and how to treat the patient. #The wife accompanies her husband to quit his job and experiences the daily agony of crowded subway commutes, saying, "I finally realize how hard it is for you to go to work every day. Thank you for all these years." Upon hearing this, the husband feels understood and bursts into tears on the subway. #After quitting his job, the husband attempts suicide in the bathroom due to feeling neglected and impatient by the wife who is busy with her comic drawings. Thankfully, the wife saves him, and they both cry and embrace each other. Support, acceptance, understanding, and care are all vital for individuals with depression, and this movie will surely provide you with a lot of relatability and inspiration. However, as the girlfriend of someone with depression, you also need to take care of your own emotions because living with a person with depression is not easy. I suggest you can, like the female lead, chat with your best friend to ease your emotions or find other ways to avoid breaking down. It's great that your boyfriend has such a caring partner like you. Keep it up!

Hello, it is clear that you care about your boyfriend and want to help him. First of all, we need to determine whether your boyfriend really has a tendency towards depression. There is a difference between having a tendency towards depression and simply having a temporary bad mood. What recent events have caused him to feel depressed? How long has he had this tendency towards depression? Has it started to affect his everyday life? Is it quite serious? By asking these questions, we can have a more accurate assessment of your boyfriend's situation and then think about how to help him. If he is just temporarily feeling down, you can think back to your past experiences and see if there is anything that has been supportive for him, and try to follow those successful experiences. What kind of companionship does he prefer from you? You can also ask for his opinion. In addition, you can face the event that has been affecting his emotions together and think about what you can do to change it, even if it is a small action. Once the issue is resolved, his mood may improve. If he is indeed showing signs of depression, and it has been going on for a while, and it is affecting his daily life, causing constant unhappiness, then in addition to the suggestions mentioned above, you can also suggest that he seek psychological counseling. Seeking help from professionals can give you the strength to make changes in the situation of depression. However, I would like to add one more thing, we should try to avoid "labeling" our friends with their current state, such as using words like "depression tendency". Instead, it is better to describe specific behaviors that have occurred, for example, after taking exams last week, he has been feeling down, avoiding me, no longer watching his favorite matches, and even refusing to play games online. He says he just wants to be alone and quiet. What should I do? The latter approach helps us to solve the actual problems more effectively, and often after describing them, it becomes clearer what we can do. Best wishes, Jiang Jiang.

question: What are the methods of emotion regulation?
description: We may experience various negative emotions in life. So, what methods should we use to regulate when negative emotions come? Are there any practical ones?

answers.answer_text: Here are a few suggestions to regulate your emotions, hoping they can help you: 1. Shift your focus by engaging in activities you enjoy, such as reading jokes or watching funny movies. This can effectively divert your attention. 2. Breath regulation: use meditation techniques to regulate your breathing, which can effectively regulate your emotions. 3. Listen to music: playing soothing background music or your favorite tunes can also effectively regulate your emotions. 4. Release emotions appropriately: choose suitable ways to release your emotions, which can also have a good regulatory effect (such as crying). 5. Self-awareness: effective self-awareness can help you identify the causes of your emotional fluctuations and find solutions.

Negative emotions are possible for everyone, and we can regulate our emotions through various methods. Here, I also provide you with some suggestions that you can try: 1. Maintain a balance between work and rest, pay attention to resting and exercising your body. Nowadays, life is too hectic, causing us to frequently encounter various social pressures. In daily life, don't always be busy without taking breaks. It is important to give yourself time to rest, which can help regulate emotions. Additionally, moderate exercise not only improves physical fitness, but also releases substances that make you happy, making you feel happier. Sleep is also a natural remedy for regulating emotions. When you rest well, you will feel energized and your mood will naturally improve. In summary, it is recommended to have a regular daily schedule, participate in appropriate exercise, and improve physical fitness. The body is the foundation of everything, cherish it, and your body will feel relaxed, which will naturally reflect in your emotions. 2. Be kind to others and establish good interpersonal relationships. Feeling supported by society can also help improve your mood. If a person excels in all aspects but cannot find help during critical moments or someone to share or alleviate their burdens, then their emotions will not find an outlet, and naturally, their emotions will not improve. Therefore, in our daily lives, we should try to interact with others more. There is no need to deliberately please or cater to others, nor should we have excessive demands on others. Remember, in psychology there is a "golden rule": Treat others as you would like to be treated! We don't need to expect any specific response from others, when we treat others well, our inner self can also feel a sense of peace. In fact, most people can also sense your kindness and sincerity, and they will naturally have a certain liking for you and be willing to establish good interpersonal relationships with you. 3. Add some fun to your lifestyle to relieve stress, such as taking a hot bath, going for a walk, listening to relaxing music, practicing meditation, reading, writing, painting, etc. All of these activities can help alleviate your emotions. Before work, give yourself a sense of ritual. In doing so, under the habit that you have developed, following the ritual while doing things won't create too much resistance in your inner self. Having a regular lifestyle will also give you the energy to do more things.

Hello~~~ In modern society, with the accelerated pace of life, people's moods rise and fall with the rapidly changing environment. Emotional release has always been advocated by counselors and many mental health researchers as a way to deal with one's emotions. Reasonably venting and expressing one's emotions has a very good effect on alleviating extreme feelings in individuals. Everyone has different ways of venting their emotions. Common methods include talking to trusted family and friends, exercising, reading, sleeping, etc. In addition, everyone has different ways of relaxation. Painters express their emotions through their works, musicians express their emotions through music. Therefore, it is generally recommended that everyone have a hobby or interest of their own. This is like having an additional way of expression and a path for emotional release when feeling frustrated or upset. I hope this helps.

question: Lack of love, preferring mature women, liking relationships with age differences, is it okay to marry an older woman?
description: Lack of love since childhood, attracted to mature women, sometimes sensitive to women of auntie age, can I marry an auntie in the future?

answers.answer_text: As the OP said, liking mature women can be a manifestation of lacking maternal love, but it is not absolute. Sometimes, the attraction towards someone of the opposite sex can have multiple reasons. Regardless, as long as it is genuine love, age, appearance, and background are just external factors. As long as there are no obstacles in one's own heart, the choice is one's own freedom.

question: Why do I sometimes doubt who I am?
description: I often find myself doubting who I am. What would happen to the people around me if I had never existed in this world? And if I were to leave this world, how would the people around me react? Why do such thoughts come to mind? Is this kind of thinking normal?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, each of us has many unknown things in this world, so we have always approached this world with a curious heart. Having such thoughts is not always a bad thing, but if you constantly think like this, it will affect your normal life. You are yourself, a unique person, there will never be two identical leaves in the world, so for us humans, there will never be two completely identical people. Our existence certainly has meaning. It depends on whether you are willing to make an effort and have eyes to discover beauty. Sometimes being curious about the world is also a good thing because curiosity gives us the motivation to explore. And through exploration, we are more likely to discover our own value. Best wishes~.

question: I feel that my parents are Graland. What should I do?
description: I'm 26 years old, and since I was young, my parents have always been obsessed with money and constantly instilled in me the idea that spending money is sinful. According to the Engel coefficient, our family is considered well-off, but our quality of life is even worse than that of an average family who can afford basic needs. I always feel that my parents love money more than they love me, and because of this, I have harbored a lot of hatred towards them. When I was young, I didn't have much pocket money. It wasn't until middle school that my parents started giving me a little bit. In high school, I only received 400 yuan as monthly allowance, and in my first and second year of university, I only had 500 yuan per month. Elementary and middle school education was free, and in high school, I had a scholarship, so education didn't cost much. When I graduated from university, my parents stopped providing for me. I had to earn and spend money by myself. Previously, I spent 16,000 yuan on a preparatory course for postgraduate studies, which was my own money. In addition to that, I had to pay the mortgage. As a result, my savings were depleted. I had no choice but to ask my parents for money, but the way they looked at me was as if I were asking for their flesh and blood. It made me feel really uncomfortable. Am I not their daughter? I didn't ask for much, just 800 yuan. I just don't understand why it's so difficult for me, while people my age around me seem to ask their parents for money as easily as drinking water.

answers.answer_text: The author's experience is really similar to mine. I am already in my 30s, but the influence from my parents still exists. However, unlike the author, I was the one assimilated, while the author had different opinions and I truly admire that. I have a younger brother and my mom often praises me to others, saying that XX (me) doesn't spend money recklessly like XX (my brother) who spends money all the time. When I was young, parents were everything, so whatever they said was right. I always had this thought that spending money recklessly was wrong and asking parents for money was wrong too. In high school, when I lost some money, I managed to survive with 10 yuan for 7 days, and I didn't feel miserable at all. In fact, I was proud of myself for saving money for the family. I didn't realize this issue until I started dating my partner. I don't not love her, I do love her. I have always had part-time jobs and I give all my salary to her. However, I can't stand going out to eat together. She is a very bourgeois girl and always chooses expensive places to eat. Actually, with our salaries, we can afford it, but I feel extremely uncomfortable and even get angry. But I know deep down that she is right, I have no reason to get angry at her. I was also confused about where my anger was coming from. Later, after some introspection, I realized that I was brainwashed since childhood, brainwashed by my parents. When we go out to eat, at a subconscious level, I would think my partner did something wrong. But at a conscious level, I know there's no issue. For a long time, when we go out, she would eat something nice and I would choose the cheapest option for myself. I love her, but if I hadn't studied psychology, I might have ended up like your parents. I think what hurt the most for the author is feeling that their parents don't love them. No matter who experiences this, it is a very painful thing. And it is indeed the case, if they are not willing to spend money on you, how can they claim to love you? When I was in college, I read the Analects of Confucius and there was a story about Confucius borrowing an umbrella. When it rained and Confucius and his disciples passed by Zixia's house, someone suggested borrowing an umbrella from Zixia. But as soon as Confucius heard it, he said, "No, Zixia is quite stingy. If I borrow it, he won't give it to me, and others will think he disrespects his teacher. If he does give it to me, he will definitely be heartbroken." Nobody is perfect, everyone's situation is different, and the standard for measuring love should also be diverse. Besides money, did your parents make you feel loved in other ways? Did they give you money when you needed it despite being stingy? If they did, then maybe you can forgive or accept your stingy parents. But if they didn't, why should we accept parents who don't love us?

First of all, from the question, it can be seen that the questioner is not so much complaining about their parents caring about money as they believe that their parents value money more than they value their own child. Therefore, let's first analyze the importance that the questioner's parents place on money. Each person's perception of money is developed over a long period of time. During this period, various factors such as illness and poverty can lead to an excessive emphasis on money. So, did the questioner's parents experience setbacks or harm due to lack of money when they were young? Secondly, people's values ​​regarding money are also influenced by the times. In the era of the questioner's parents, you could buy high-quality goods with little money. And in that era, there was also little difference in product quality due to price discrepancies. Therefore, some people who have come from that era might not understand the rise in prices today and insist that goods that are cheap and usable are good. In addition, in the eyes of the older generation of parents, they have a more innocent perception of friendships among classmates. In their understanding, social interactions between classmates do not require money. However, as time goes by, the cost of socializing has also increased. If parents' thinking does not change with the changing times, it can lead to this kind of effect. As for what the questioner said about their parents not valuing them enough, this requires further communication between the questioner and their parents. First, the questioner needs to understand the reason why their parents save money. Many parents save money when they are young for retirement considerations, that is to say, the parents not providing financial support to their child now is to help the child save future expenses for supporting elderly parents. Secondly, the questioner can ask their parents if they have difficulty providing help to themselves due to financial constraints. If the questioner's parents are genuinely struggling to balance their income and expenses and have little surplus, the questioner should be able to understand. However, if the parents are involved in pyramid schemes or other scams, the questioner should be on high alert. In addition, the questioner's parents may have a psychological tendency to avoid responsibility. For example, "I will ask less from you in the future, so I can contribute less to you now." It is difficult to determine the reasons for such situations from the questioner's description, but if such a situation arises, it indicates that the questioner's parents have a lack of security and retain immature values ​​that are somewhat similar to those of young children. If one wants to change this situation, professional intervention is needed.

"It's not that your parents didn't give you money, you can say they are tight-fisted! When you ask them for money, try asking in the form of a loan. Secondly, try to connect the thing you want to do with your parents' interests. For example, if you want to buy a house, tell them that it will also be their home, where they can come and stay often. This is just an example, but remember to link it to their interests when asking them for money. Why do it this way? Because people naturally hate losses. Also, you don't know what kind of past your parents have, they may be very sensitive to money. In psychology, there is a loss aversion effect. It means that when faced with the same amount of [gain] and loss, people find losses more difficult to bear. In other words, people are much more sensitive to losses than to gains. In the past, Nobel Prize-winning economist Daniel Kahneman conducted an experiment where participants flipped a fair coin. If it landed on heads, they would receive $150, and if it landed on tails, they would lose $100. In the long run, this gamble is definitely a win, as the probability of winning and losing are the same, and the winnings are greater than the losses. However, the experimental result was that the majority of people still refused this gamble, because for most people, the pain of losing $100 is far greater than the pleasure of gaining $150. How much more happiness is needed to compensate for the pain of losing $100 for an average person? The answer is $200. People are more sensitive to pain. For most ordinary people, when facing uncertain results, they must have at least twice the guarantee of the risk. In other words, if you want your parents to give you money, you need to offer them a return of at least twice the amount. Of course, I understand that you may not be able to do that right now, but you can promise them. Maybe your aversion to losses is kicking in again and you think this won't work, but you need to know that it's not that your parents are unwilling to give you money, it's that your approach hasn't been effective in winning their hearts."

question: I often feel sad, like living in a dream, and it feels very unreal.
description: When I was very young, my father was diagnosed with kidney failure. Our family was not well-off, so my parents separated. I stayed with my father, but their relationship was very bad. Now I am in my second year of college, and for the past two years, I often think about unhappy things from my past, whether it's about my family or other aspects of my life. It makes me very sad, and I often feel like crying. I cannot concentrate, and everything feels like a dream, as if nothing is real. Sometimes I want to take a deep breath, but I try to appear normal and happy in front of others. Since I was young, I have thought of ending it all, but I always feel like there are still many places I haven't been to, and leaving like this would be such a waste. I also worry about my parents and friends, so I am in great pain. I want to seek psychological treatment, but I am afraid it will worry my parents.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological crisis, counseling and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm so sorry to hear about what you're going through, and I'm sending you a big hug. You are a sensible child who cares about your parents, and even though they have separated, you still love them. I also believe that you are someone who loves life and enjoys traveling, exploring different landscapes, and experiencing different lifestyles. However, the pressure from your family is making you feel very uncomfortable and even affecting your daily life. My suggestion is that you seek psychological therapy and honestly communicate this issue with your parents. In the process of overcoming this hurdle, you need the support and help of your parents. Family is the people who can understand and share your pain, so I believe they will be willing to accompany you to get through this difficult time. Be brave and face your problems, and I wish you all the best. The world and I love you.

Hello. I have been providing psychological counseling to students in college. I fully support you seeking psychological counseling in your situation. Universities have counseling centers that will support you. It seems that you have lacked support since childhood, and it appears that your parents are finding it difficult to take care of you and support you. Despite these conditions, the fact that you are able to attend college shows that there is still inner strength within you. However, being alone for a long time can often make you feel heavy, powerless, and directionless. Your parents' concerns are not what you think. Assuming you don't actively seek help, if your parents care about you, they will be even more worried and helpless. Now they cannot support you, so if you can take the initiative to seek help, it shows that you have the desire to make efforts and gradually struggle out of a difficult situation. How can this make your parents worry? Unless they are too weak to even consider this. They can't handle the slightest disturbance. So, you have even less reason to worry about them. Because if you can't even take care of yourself, how can you take care of them? Right now, you need to stand firm for yourself first, without considering others. Once you have the strength, then you can think about taking care of your parents. In addition, I recommend that you participate in some group therapy sessions. You will meet people who have had similar experiences as you, and everyone is working hard and can support each other in moving forward. It won't feel so powerless. Wishing you the best, Zhang Jinping, a Psychological Counselor.

question: My boyfriend wants to change jobs and is feeling restless inside. How can I help him?
description: My boyfriend is currently twenty-five years old. He used to work on a construction site, earning a decent income but suffering from the hardships and having a poor mental well-being. Therefore, he wants to switch jobs. However, starting a new job means a significant income gap compared to his previous job, and he is afraid to take this step. How can I help him?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: The only thing you need to do to help him is to encourage him to meet new people. If he is the one asking questions, there can be many opportunities for further discussion. But since you are the one being asked, and not directly involved, you don't need to do too much. In my opinion, the two of you have probably discussed everything you could on a rational level, but he hasn't made a firm decision yet, indicating that he is not emotionally prepared. Why should he meet new people? And what kind of people should he meet? These two questions cannot be explained logically. Since he is not emotionally prepared, you need to start from an emotional perspective and use the life he aspires to as a way to motivate his determination. So, it's not just about finding anyone to introduce him to a different lifestyle; it's about finding people who lead the kind of life he aspires to and have similar experiences. Actually, when deciding if a job is what you want, you can look at someone around you who has a similar background and see if the life they are currently living is what you want. Now what you need to do is encourage him to have these kind of people around him. Because knowing these people personally will enhance the sense of connection to this kind of life, and it will be easier for him to believe that he can also achieve it, thus taking the first step to improve his current life. Of course, meeting these people doesn't mean he can proceed without any concerns, so you may still need to discuss some rational aspects. For example, how much salary difference can he accept after changing jobs? How long can he tolerate this gap? Which cities should he consider working in to reduce the gap? There are many questions that you need to discuss again. For now, what you need to do is encourage him to broaden his horizons and see more possibilities in life. Meeting new people is one of the most direct ways, and he can participate in online activities to meet more people. When he faces the job change with a positive attitude, you can also discuss other topics such as building personal competitive advantages, but that involves other content.

When we gain something, we inevitably have to give up something, so we need to learn to make choices. 1. Which is more important, income and job satisfaction, or personal growth? Working at a construction site is indeed tough and exhausting, and the monotonous daily routine can be annoying. However, it offers a decent income, so it is reasonable to trade hard work for high returns in essence. After changing jobs, life will become much easier, even though we may have to start from scratch. As long as our direction is right and the new career we pursue shows promising prospects for development, it is acceptable to accept temporary low income. If after changing jobs, we are not prepared or feel bored with life again, how should we deal with this situation? Sometimes, we should not place all our hopes on changing jobs but rather understand the purpose of the job switch and whether it can truly bring us comfort. 2. Sometimes, choice is more important than effort. If the questioner's boyfriend has a certain foundation, and both parties do not have significant financial pressure for the time being, as well as some savings, we can indeed have backup plans. For example, we can learn in advance about the recent employment situation in the industry we plan to enter, analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the other person, and then make an analysis based on our own abilities and the industry's development to see if there are better ways to handle the situation. If neither of us has significant savings and there is a certain financial burden, then we can try to earn more money together and find ways to improve our abilities in our spare time, encouraging each other and working hard together. I believe the end result will not be too bad. The world and I love you.

Hello, I hope my answer is helpful to you. You are facing a dilemma and suffering because of your boyfriend's career choice. You want to help and support him as a girlfriend, but you're not sure how to do so. Career planning and choices are something we all have to go through in life. You can encourage your boyfriend and have him take a career test to see which jobs may be more suitable for him. You can also sit down together and discuss the issues he is facing in his current job, such as feeling unhappy, mentally exhausted, or lacking a fulfilling personal life. Determine if these problems can be resolved or eased in any way. Is it the job itself, or is he unable to find effective solutions to certain issues? There is no perfect job, and every profession has its hidden difficulties. If your boyfriend decides to change jobs, consider if his current savings can alleviate any financial impact and assess the prospects for the new job, including opportunities for promotion and the skills and conditions required for advancement. Gather information from various sources and help your boyfriend gain a better understanding of potential new jobs, so he can make an informed decision. In this matter, you can listen to your boyfriend more, show understanding and encouragement, and guide him in listing and comparing the pros and cons of his current job and new opportunities, and how they align with his present circumstances. You can also try to relax a bit and understand that this is a hurdle he needs to overcome. Being a supportive girlfriend can give him more strength. Ultimately, whatever decision he makes, you should be supportive. Good luck!

question: I read "No Longer Human," but I feel too suppressed to handle it.
description: I read "No Longer Human", written by Osamu Dazai, who attempted suicide five times. I surprisingly understood the narrative of this book, as I have had a similar experience myself. During my internship, I felt extremely insignificant, trying to please everyone, constantly worrying about how the supervising teacher would perceive me, and afraid of everything. But in the end, I felt like I had become a joke. Reading this book made me want to cry, shout, and rebel. However, I understand what the author wanted to convey, yet at the same time, I don't understand. I wish I could have someone to talk to about this book. Is it possible?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I read the book "No Longer Human" last year too. However, because the content was too negative, I couldn't understand some of the stories and the characters' psychology, so I gave up on it. But based on what I read, I feel that the author may not necessarily be trying to convey any particular ideas. He might just be expressing his own emotions and feelings, and the process of writing might be his way of seeking someone who can understand him. Sometimes, we have to admit that not all words convey so-called life philosophy. Some authors write books just to express and record their emotions, using an artistic approach to intensify their emotions and release everything they have experienced or expressed in real life through words. Therefore, it is enough to achieve emotional resonance, and there is no need to understand what he is talking about. Even if you were to ask the author this question right now, sitting in front of you, he might not be able to give you an accurate answer! Time changes, situations change, and feelings change too! So, just enjoy the spiritual enjoyment it brings you, and don't bring it into your life! Especially negative viewpoints, just understand what they are and don't apply them to yourself. The above is my analysis and suggestion, hoping it will be helpful to you! Take care!

This book is toxic. When I read it in college, I became depressed afterwards. It felt like the author was speaking to the depths of my soul, expressing what I dare not express. Many years have passed, and I have forgotten the specific content, but I still remember the discomfort I felt after reading it. I have long since overcome it, so let me share my experience. First, there is no doubt that this book is very true, it reveals the truth of being human. But why did the author commit suicide after seeing this truth instead of living more clearly? Simply because the author is a weak person. No matter how high his intelligence, he cannot face the world, he is timid. Haven't many great monks and masters also seen the truth of this world? Why do they live so openly? Because they have compassion. A person who only thinks of themselves can only see the cruelty of life, the cruelty of the world, everyone wants to harm them, and no one is worth relying on. But why do you demand others to be good to you, without taking the first step to bring light to this dark world? Osamu Dazai was a cowardly and selfish person. Secondly, we are used to hearing that this world is bright and beautiful, so we are immune to such literature. Osamu Dazai is good at describing the inner world, it is very relatable, but he poses questions without providing answers and he ended up committing suicide himself, which leaves the readers in despair. Does this cruel world really have no answers? It does. This world does have answers, but Osamu Dazai didn't find them. He saw through the cunning nature of the self, the hypocrisy behind the mask, and realized that this world is like a huge masquerade, he couldn't fit in with himself and this kind of world, but why don't others collapse? He didn't want to blend in, but it was so painful. However, so many people resonated with his books, indicating that the world is indeed like that, and it's not his fault. On one hand, he isn't at fault, there's nothing wrong with the truth deep within him. On the other hand, he is at fault, he wore many masks to fit into this world, losing himself, and this false self has problems. He couldn't distinguish between the true self and the false self, slowly getting lost. The false self needs to be corrected, while the true self needs to be upheld, they are not contradictory. After saying so much, I don't even know what I'm saying... Anyway, when I finished reading this book back then, I denied myself to death, felt that life had no meaning, and had no support. However, behind the virtual world, there is a real world. After seeing the false emotions behind the virtual world, there is no need for despair, because this is the path you must take to find the real world. The key is to understand that all beings struggle in the virtual world, just like you. How can you change and become optimistic again? Go to the other side~.

question: I clearly stood up for them, why are they targeting me instead??
description: I remember one year my mom and I excitedly went to attend my younger brother's graduation ceremony. We had a hard time finding him because we didn't know the way, and when we finally found him, his attitude was very cold. We were tired and thirsty from being exposed to the sun, following him around, but he didn't care about us. Even though he knew we were waiting, he was busy taking pictures with others and didn't even bother to take the flowers we specially bought for him. I was very angry, but my mom was still enthusiastic, ignoring the scorching sun and running around with him, wearing high heels. Seeing her like that, I was both angry and frustrated with my brother's behavior, and I felt both heartbroken and puzzled about why my mom, despite his behavior, still acted this way. I blamed her, saying, "Why bother following him when he doesn't even want to acknowledge you?" But she persisted. What surprised me was that on the way back home after leaving the school, she suddenly attacked me, speaking in a harsh and mocking tone, "His school is much better than yours. The female students there dress properly, unlike those in your school." I was stunned. I clearly felt sorry and valued her, and I clearly traveled a long way to celebrate for him, but he didn't want to acknowledge us. So, why... why did I do something wrong? Why did my mom say such things and attack me? Isn't it him who ignored us?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. You and your mom went to your younger brother's graduation ceremony with great excitement, but it was a tiring journey and your brother didn't show much interest in you both. You stood up for your mom, but she scolded you, which made you feel very unjust. I understand your feelings because you know how hard you and your mom have worked. After finding your brother, he didn't show any affection towards you, and he didn't even take the flowers you specially bought for him. You clearly felt sorry for your mom, but ended up being mocked and hurt. However, looking at it from your mom's perspective, she went to her son's school to attend the graduation ceremony. She didn't consider it tiring at all; instead, she saw it as an honor and her own happiness. Even if she had to travel back and forth, she was happy inside. But at this moment, she faced criticism from another son who tried to stop her from doing what she wanted. She must have been somewhat unhappy deep down. So at this moment, the best filial piety we can show is to be obedient. As long as our mom is happy, we should unconditionally support her. Best wishes.

question: I got angry with my parents over trivial matters, and every time they would play the act of sacrifice for you.
description: Today I wanted to drink water, but then I realized there was no hot water. My dad had boiled some water and left it to cool, then he brought it over for me to drink. At that moment, I was in the middle of playing a game, so I told him to leave it there and insisted on drinking later. He said he had gone out of his way to do something nice for me and I didn't appreciate it. I got a little angry and told him to leave it there, I would drink it later. Then he started complaining about how he wanted to drink it himself but held back just to give it to me. Every time my dad does something, he always emphasizes how much he sacrifices and how difficult it is for him. It made me speechless, so I let him drink it first. Then he started saying how playing games is bad and eating outside is bad. I exploded... A tragedy caused by a glass of water. Honestly, it seems easier to interact with strangers from my perspective. Strangers wouldn't care if I drank or not. If they want to be nice to me, they would just give it to me and not bother about it anymore, even if I didn't drink it, they wouldn't make me feel guilty. It almost made me laugh. My family isn't poor at all, but there's always this drama of "how much I love you" and "how much I sacrifice for you". It's like we can't afford good fruit or even water. And then he thinks I don't appreciate it, as if I haven't been doing what he expects, like being deeply moved and doing everything he says, even if it's just a little late, he would nag me to death. So annoying, I don't want to be his daughter anymore.
keywords: family, family relationships, parent communication, family control

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, seeing your question reminds me of a large group of high school students like you who have similar concerns. Fortunately, it seems that your relationship with your parents is still okay, but the last sentence is quite cute and annoying, like you're sulking and throwing a tantrum. However, there are many high school students whose relationships with their parents have been completely messed up because of similar issues, making their parents sad and the children angry, turning their homes into battlefields. Let's take a look at why things turn out this way. - 1. While you were playing a mobile game and getting to the most intense part, I happened to be playing a game too... In your own world, dealing with your matters, you didn't tell your dad what you were doing and how much time you needed when he brought water for you. - 2. Your dad thought you should drink the water first, thinking that the game wasn't as important as hydrating, not knowing that you were dealing with a crucial situation. - 3. Your dad only saw the reality of you playing games without drinking water. This made him think about many things, so he started nagging. - 4. You didn't care about why your dad was nagging, you only heard the content of his nagging, which is the same old stuff, so you started feeling annoyed. Actually, the root cause is a lack of clear communication. If you had told your dad that you were in an intense part of the game and only needed a minute, for example, and asked him to just leave the water there, he probably wouldn't have nagged anymore, and you wouldn't have felt annoyed. Timely communication is very important, and most conflicts between parents and children arise from poor communication. Parents care most about their children's physical and mental health, and what they most want to know is what their children are thinking. If children can express their thoughts and reasons for their actions in a timely manner, it will reduce a lot of conflicts. - Now that we've covered the problem, let's look at some of the things you said in a sulking tone. In my opinion, it's better to interact with strangers. They don't care if I drink or not. If they want to be nice to me, they'll bring it, and once they do, they won't bother anymore, even if I don't drink it, they won't make me feel guilty. I'm almost dying laughing. My family is not poor at all, but every time we have to act out this play of "how much I love you and sacrifice for you," as if we can't afford to eat good fruits or drink water. And then they think I don't appreciate it, as if I didn't follow their expectations, wow, so moved and do it according to what they say, even if it's just a little late, they would nag me to death, so annoying, I don't want to be their daughter anymore. - After reading this, try to feel how you are feeling right now. - Finally, I invite you to answer a question and think back to what just happened: Daughter is playing a game, father boils water, cools it down, and brings it over. Daughter doesn't drink it, father insists on making the daughter drink it, and the daughter starts feeling annoyed. With this scene in front of you, the question is: If you were the parent and your child was playing a game, what would you do?

Your father gets angry because he has an expectation. He thinks that by being good to his daughter and refraining from drinking water, he has done something great and that his daughter will appreciate it. But everything doesn't go as he anticipated. His daughter is playing games and doesn't want to drink the water he painstakingly prepared. In his mind, there is a gap - how come no one sees or appreciates the things he does? So he becomes furious and pours this emotion onto the person who doesn't meet his expectations. Of course, you don't buy into his account. In your mind, you're thinking that it's not like I asked you to pour me water, and besides, when can't water be drunk? I'm busy playing games. So in this scenario, everyone is living in their own script and not considering that real life is unpredictable. Your father is wrong in being too selfless and having high expectations of others. He hopes that his sacrifices will be met with gratitude. He doesn't consider himself and would rather go thirsty to let his daughter drink first, thinking that she will surely be grateful to him, and that will bring him satisfaction. In fact, if he could be more loyal to himself, treat himself better, be a little more selfish, and satisfy himself when thirsty and then give water to his daughter, he wouldn't be so angry. Because his need has been met, he doesn't need others to be grateful to him. And other people's actions and responses are unpredictable, so disappointment is likely. I believe the original poster should also experience this in daily life. For example, if you really like someone and carefully prepare a gift for them, but then find out that they don't like it and even show a bit of disdain, you will inevitably be extremely disappointed and may even blame the friend for not appreciating it and wasting your heartfelt intention. But the friend's reaction is not actually about you, they just didn't have that need, which is something your father needs to learn to recognize. So your father may need some mindset shifts, to love himself, prioritize his own needs rather than expecting others to praise his sacrifices. This way, he won't feel so aggrieved and keep complaining that you haven't responded to his sacrifices. However, if your father becomes a selfish person, as a daughter, you may need to do many things on your own. For example, your father may not boil water for you, so you need to do it yourself and let it cool down. And what you need to do is to understand your father's mindset as much as possible and be understanding. If there are difficulties, you can live independently and do everything yourself. Your father won't be able to do anything for you naturally, and there won't be any expectations.

#You wanted to drink water, but found out there was no water. Your father boiled and cooled some water for you;# Your father wanted you to drink water immediately, but you were in an important moment of the game, which caused your father to become "upset" and talk about many other things;# You were annoyed by your father's "mental blackmail" and "self-sacrifice". 1. What is your role in front of your parents? I don't know how you usually interact with your parents. It is too hasty to infer from just one incident. I guess you may complain about your parents "giving too much and deliberately self-sacrificing", while also enjoying and needing this special care from your parents. For example, if there is no water, why didn't you boil water yourself? You are not an incapable child, so have you taken care of your parents? What is your role in front of your parents, a "child who needs to be taken care of" or a "capable child who can take care of themselves"? The above is not my judgment on you, hoping to provide you with a perspective for consideration. 2. When you change, your parents will also change. This is still following the content of the first point. If you start to try not to rely on your parents, take care of yourself more, and show your parents your ability and determination to take care of yourself, then I think your parents will change accordingly. They will also reflect on whether "my child has grown up, he can take care of himself, should we parents respect the child more and let go." 3. Some practical communication suggestions. Why does your father insist on making you drink water immediately? I guess your father wants you to notice him, pay attention to him, and express gratitude. Next time, I suggest communicating with your father like this: when you see your father bringing water, say, "Wow, dad, you are so thoughtful. Thank you for bringing me water. Dad, are you thirsty? Have you had water? I am in the middle of a game now, but I will drink right after finishing. Thank you, Dad!" Take the initiative to express attention and gratitude to your father, so he won't talk a lot. This is my answer. It may not fully understand your question, but I hope it provides you with some perspectives to consider~.

Actually, it's very simple to solve this problem. Just tell them that you don't want to be with them anymore and stop using their money. That way, you can have complete control over your own time and life, be with any strangers you like, and eat when you have money or work for yourself when you don't. If you're tired, you don't need to seek solace from them, and if someone bullies you, just go to the police. Give it a try. Maybe you will enjoy that kind of freedom. Love and meticulous care can become a burden when you are able to receive this love.

question: I want to retake the undergraduate entrance exam. What is the experience like to study for another year?
description: School just started recently, but I want to go back and redo a year. I am not satisfied with completing a specialized diploma; I want to try again and aim for a bachelor's degree.

answers.answer_text: Hello! From your question, I can see that you are a very proactive and ambitious person. You are not particularly satisfied with your admission to a vocational school and want to strive for it again by repeating the year, giving yourself a chance to make a new choice. Firstly, I want to affirm that your mindset is very positive, which shows that you have goals and are willing to put in the effort to achieve them. Now, should you repeat the year or not? I think first we can rationally analyze your own academic performance and why you didn't do well in this year's college entrance examination. If you usually have good grades but just didn't perform well on the exam, then repeating the year has a higher chance of success. On the other hand, if your foundation is weak and you want to improve your grades in just a few months, the risk is relatively high. Repeating the year is not an easy path. The psychological pressure on repeating students is much higher than for current year students. If you go to a repeating school, you will also have to work harder in your studies. Only with single-minded focus can you possibly achieve good results on the college entrance examination. Are you prepared for all of this? Currently, you are studying at a vocational school, but this doesn't mean it is your ultimate goal in life. Choosing to study calmly at a vocational school also gives you the opportunity to pursue further studies and take the graduate school entrance exam. Choosing to go back and work hard on repeating the year also gives you the opportunity to get into a regular university. Although life's journey is filled with choices at every turning point, it is the effort we put into each choice that will steer us in different directions. No matter what choice you make, the important thing is to decide and not regret it, and look ahead. Keep up the good work, young person! I wish you the best, your world and someone who loves you~

question: The head teacher of high school changed and I feel lost. I have lost motivation to study and I am not happy.
description: In my first year of high school, I particularly admired a teacher. Unexpectedly, in my second year, he became the class teacher. During my second year, I learned a lot because of him, such as how to be tolerant towards others, study methods, and the drawbacks of getting things without putting in effort, etc. In some ways, I developed a sense of dependency on him. I thought that under his guidance, I would smoothly enter my third year and study even harder. However, to my surprise, my class teacher was changed in the third year due to various reasons. As a result, during the past two months of supplementary classes in my third year, I have sometimes lacked motivation, felt like crying, and at the same time, I am worried and disappointed in myself for not being as good as before.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hello: People need role models. The power of role models not only drives oneself forward in behavior, but more importantly, in spirit. This teacher is your role model, and there are many aspects of them that attract you. Therefore, their arrival and departure deeply influence you. Perhaps during this period of time, you still need their presence, but the teachings they left behind should still be in your heart. Analyzing the problem: 1. In high school, you particularly admired a teacher, and unexpectedly, they became your homeroom teacher in the second year. (This is a commendable thing and, for you at that time, I think it was like adding wings to a tiger.) 2. In the second year of high school, because of this teacher, you learned a lot, such as being tolerant towards others, study methods, the disadvantages of getting things without effort, and so on. In some aspects, you developed a sense of dependence on them. (Each of us hopes to have someone in our lives who can lead us and find direction in being a person and doing things. This teacher of yours must be very outstanding, regardless of their actions or deeds. At that stage, having admiration and dependence on them is normal and you are fortunate to have encountered this guiding figure.) 3. You thought that with their guidance, you would smoothly enter the third year and study even harder. But unexpectedly, due to various environmental reasons, the homeroom teacher was changed in the third year. Therefore, in the past two months of tutoring in the third year, sometimes you lack motivation, feel like crying, and at the same time, you worry and feel disappointed because you are not as good as before. (Your role model was suddenly taken away, and you are a bit bewildered. It's hard to adapt to such a quick transition. This teacher, who you entrusted with your spirit, has left, but the methods they taught you are still there, right? Also, don't worry, there will be other role models appearing. Just like that homeroom teacher who suddenly appeared, isn't it? Indeed, there are always changes in the world that we cannot predict. Let's take this as an important lesson in growth, just that it came during your third year. It wants you to understand that although many people and things in the world can change, many beautiful truths will not change. So, don't be afraid of people coming and going, gradually learn the essence, and you will have no fear.) Closing words: I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you can gradually learn to tap into your own energy! If you have any confusion, you can send me a private message.

Hugs and kisses to you. From your description, it seems that you have strong feelings for this teacher and have developed a dependence on him. In your freshman year, you admired him, and in your sophomore year, you were fortunate enough to become his student. However, in your senior year, you couldn't be in his class anymore. This must have caused you a great sense of loss and made you feel very upset. Our admiration and dependence on teachers usually occur during our student years when we don't have a stable belief system and a strong support system, so we tend to rely on our parents, teachers, and sometimes older family members or public figures. We see them as our guiding light, leading us forward. However, one day, when you grow up and become strong enough, you may no longer rely on that feeling of security brought by someone else, but instead rely on yourself to create your own path. But at this stage of your senior year, it may be difficult to adjust right away. So what should you do? Be honest with that teacher about your dependence and distress. Even though he is no longer your class teacher, he will always be your teacher, and you can talk to him about your troubles and sadness. I believe he will be willing to help you and accompany you through your high school journey. You can also talk to your current class teacher about your difficulties and sadness, letting him see the part of you that needs support and strength. I believe your current teacher will also try to assist you, providing you with support and care. Even though he is no longer your class teacher, he surely hopes his students can excel and have the ability to learn independently. He can still be your inspiration and your strength. With his expectations, I invite you to continue working hard and preparing for the college entrance exams. Good luck! I hope this can help you. The world and I love you~.

It is such a fortunate and enviable thing to have encountered a teacher in high school whom you admire and who becomes your homeroom teacher. He taught you so much, both in terms of character and academics. This kind of emotional and psychological dependency you developed towards him is like the feelings one has for an older brother or even a father. The admiration, respect, and admiration you have for him make you hope to become someone like him, and you hope to be accompanied by him until you graduate from high school. However, in your senior year, due to various environmental reasons, you had to change homeroom teachers, which left you extremely disappointed and heartbroken. It felt like losing your most beloved treasure. This sense of loss deeply affected you, and as a result, you lost the motivation and drive you had in your studies before. Actually, you can share your feelings of sadness and sorrow with the teacher you admire. You can call, write a letter, or meet with him to discuss your feelings and current state. I believe he would also not want to be separated from you and your classmates. He can understand your feelings of disappointment and loss because he may also experience a similar sadness in his heart. But I believe this teacher will appear in your life to make you feel this warmth and help you become a better version of yourself, rather than depending on him for motivation. It's like when a young lion is born, the lion's parents teach it many skills. Once the young lion has learned these skills, one day it will be pushed out by its parents to face life on its own, as this is a natural occurrence in the animal kingdom. Whether you are willing to face it or not, you must learn to carry the skills and warmth you learned from that teacher into an independent life, and find your own path. This is the purpose of his presence in your life. One day, when you reach college, you may encounter friends, kindred spirits, or teachers who will reignite your motivation, but one day you will also inevitably separate due to graduation, as parting ways is inevitable. We need to learn to gradually accept and face this inevitability. Blessings to you!

Hello, it seems that your class teacher is not just a class teacher to you, but someone you admire, like, appreciate, and depend on. I wonder who you have transferred your feelings to, your father? An ideal spouse? Or someone else? Therefore, you have developed not only the feelings of a student towards a teacher, but also some other feelings. The reality is that he cannot always be by your side to accompany you, and his departure has caused various discomforts for you, affecting your studies and daily life. You need to adjust your mentality in a timely manner.
