If you have the opportunity, you can find a counselor to explore why you have such strong feelings for him, and why they are different from others and irreplaceable. More importantly, you should be aware of yourself, understand yourself, explore the deep needs within yourself, and learn to satisfy your own needs. My suggestion is to allow yourself to feel a bit uncomfortable at the moment, as this is normal. Do something, write a letter, write down your thoughts, thank him, bid farewell to him, and he doesn’t need to know about these things, just keep it to yourself. Or you can tell him your feelings and gratitude face to face, listen to his advice, and approach it rationally. Remember, no one can accompany you all the time, and we need to learn to take care of ourselves. This is a great opportunity for you to explore and take care of yourself.

Hello. You seem to be someone who is very emotional. You were originally looking forward to starting your third year of high school happily, but now you have to say goodbye to your favorite teacher, and you can't bear to part with him. This unexpected change has caused you to feel a sense of loss. We do encounter people who we don't want to say goodbye to because they have brought us great benefits. They can guide us in our studies and provide us with solutions to our problems. We are willing to learn from them and be guided by them. It gives us a sense of satisfaction knowing that we are learning and being taken care of, so we resist change. The outcome of change is unknown. You don't know if the next teacher will be as good as this one or better, and you have no control over it, so you resent losing what you have. Honey, separation is a big part of growing up, and what you can do is to accept and adapt. As a student in the third year of high school, our main focus should be on our studies. This may sound a bit cold-hearted, but it is our current main task. We are not studying for any particular teacher, right? In the past two years, this class teacher has won you over with his unique charm. Now, why not take a look and see if you have become independent in your learning and growth without him? Have you continued the study attitude and skills he taught you? If the answer is yes, then it means that the previous teacher's influence on you was profound and long-lasting. Also, give the new teacher some trust. At the beginning, you may have some resistance, but if you can let go of your resistance and objectively observe him, you may be pleasantly surprised to find hidden treasures in him. It's hard to repay a teacher's kindness, but you should know that the road ahead is still long. Perhaps in the future, when you have achieved something, the teacher may need your help, and then you might be able to share your journey with him. Actually, the people we admire, whether they are teachers or seniors, are like a beam of light. They have illuminated our path, but as we strive again and again, the number of times we remember them diminishes because we have gradually become our own light. But they will never be forgotten. You will know that in some corner of the world, there is still a beam of light standing there. And you, as someone who has seen the light, will never falter.

It is really sad and frustrating to encounter this problem. I had a similar experience when I was in high school, although it was in my sophomore year, not senior year. I can really understand this feeling of being unable to express the discomfort. Sending you a virtual hug, hoping to bring you some comfort. Let me summarize the problems I saw, and you can check if I got them right. First, you admired a teacher in your freshman year. Second, the teacher you admired became the class teacher in your sophomore year. Third, during the time when your idolized teacher became the class teacher, you developed a deep emotional connection. Fourth, in your senior year, the class teacher was replaced by another teacher. Fifth, you felt extremely upset because of this, as if you lost motivation. Sixth, you were also disappointed with your own performance. Let me share my understanding and feelings. First, you admired this teacher in your freshman year, so it seems that this teacher must have been your subject teacher or a familiar teacher. Otherwise, how could you easily admire someone in your freshman year? Second, based on the degree of liking you have for this teacher, it seems that this teacher not only has good professional abilities but also makes you feel comfortable in their presence. Third, based on the depth of your sadness, I think in your heart, this teacher is not just a teacher but also an elder or friend. I'm reminded of what Confucius said, "A true friend is one who overlooks your failures and tolerates your success." I believe this teacher should meet this standard. Fourth, you felt really upset when the class teacher was changed. I think this is normal, and there is no need to blame yourself. Many times, when we like someone, it is not only about them but also about how we see ourselves in their eyes. In other words, in their presence, we can be a more likable version of ourselves. Fifth, you are somewhat disappointed with your own performance. There is a saying, "Respect leads to awe." Even though this teacher is no longer your class teacher, you still want to be someone who can make them proud, but you haven't achieved that, and you are afraid of disappointing them. Let me give you a few suggestions. First, establish a connection with the teacher. Even though they are no longer your class teacher, they are still a teacher, and even if they are no longer at your school, you can still keep in touch. No matter where they are, their teachings stay in your heart. Second, accept your current state. It is within the normal range to feel upset for a period of time after such a major event. Nobody would handle this kind of thing perfectly. Third, if your distressing emotions are difficult to accept, you can seek counseling. Fourth, tell a teacher you trust about your state. I believe they can give you some help. I hope my answer can be of help to you.

Hello! This question immediately took me back more than ten years ago. At that time, after finishing the first year of high school, we had to choose between the arts and science streams. As someone who chose the science stream, I also faced the same dilemma of leaving beloved and familiar teachers to enter a new environment and start a new life. Later on, when I joined the new class, I discovered that many classmates felt the same way, missing the previous class and teachers so much that they even rejected their current teachers because of it. I think the possible reasons are: ◆ Familiarity often implies a sense of security. Many people naturally resist facing unfamiliar environments and crowds because it makes us feel unsafe and without a sense of belonging, leaving us feeling lost. That's why we often say: Change truly requires courage! ◆ The end of a relationship brings a profound sense of loss. A good teacher's influence on students is truly immense. Like you, I was deeply impacted by a teacher back then. Her care, expectations, and trust in me sparked a strong interest and unwavering motivation for learning. You have also built a deep teacher-student friendship with your teacher, and you may have become somewhat dependent on them. This relationship, which was enough to support you in successfully completing high school, suddenly ending, is bound to bring a deep sense of loss. How to overcome it: In terms of separation, the key is to handle the sense of loss and actively integrate into the new group. 1. Strive to face your true feelings since the change has already occurred, we need to make an effort to face our inner feelings, not resisting or avoiding them, but accepting the pressure, uneasiness, and even harm that this change brings us. 2. Express your emotions. When feeling sad, you can write in a journal, record your life, express your feelings and thoughts, and experience the healing power of words. 3. Say a proper goodbye. You can find a suitable time to have a conversation with your teacher, even prepare a small gift to bid farewell in both form and content. When my mentor and I separated, we exchanged books as a token of comforting each other. 4. Make more friends and integrate into the group. In the face of a new environment, actively participate in group activities and try to get to know some close friends as soon as possible. This way, you will have a sense of belonging and your life will gradually improve. Finally, I wish you a happy life and academic success!

I can understand your feelings. You were very accepting of the class teacher's management style and teaching methods, but it may be difficult to adjust to a new teacher. It's natural to feel discouraged. However, let's look at the problem from a different perspective. Although it's your senior year and there is a lot of pressure, it's important to have your own learning pace and goals. If your learning is affected because of a change in the class teacher, it wouldn't be worth it. From another point of view, you need to learn to adjust and adapt to changes now, so that you can maintain an open mindset. I believe you will benefit from this.

Hello, dear asker. It's as if I can see you through your words. Sending you a warm hug. The academic pressure in senior year is already overwhelming, and now you suddenly feel like you've lost your mental support. It's truly exhausting and life feels hopeless in an instant. Based on your description, it seems like your homeroom teacher is a very caring person who not only helps with academics but also provides you with correct understanding and hope in life. Such a warm-hearted individual, even if they are no longer your homeroom teacher, I believe they would still offer you the help you need if you reach out and depend on them. It wouldn't hurt for you to proactively talk to them and see if you can continue seeking guidance from them. Your study performance has been affected because you lost your mental anchor, but if you regain it, your grades will surely improve. Don't be too hard on yourself or worry too much. The coming year will be tough, but it will also be incredibly fulfilling. Take care, dear asker! My senior year has already passed, as well as the senior year of our generation. We can never go back, but I hope you live your senior year to the fullest, carrying the expectations of our senior year. The world and we will always love you.

Hello, OP. Seeing your question, I wanted to give this kind and warm and perceptive girl (assuming you are a girl based on the words) a big hug. "Whoyoulovewhoyouare," a saying from the West, in short, means that you are what kind of person you like. In psychological terms, this is called "projection." When you see your teacher's efforts, tolerance, responsibility, and so on, that is actually you! Even in your few expressions, I am also inspired and moved by such a teacher. Therefore, we highly appreciate and recognize exemplary figures who become our driving force to strive forward, constantly gaining improvement and growth. Suddenly changing homeroom teacher feels like losing guidance, and your emotions have changed, sometimes unhappy, gradually affecting academic performance, and you may feel anxious, worried, or even disappointed because of your changes. Think about it, what does a teacher want to see the most? It's that their students become their pride, that they see their students become outstanding individuals under their guidance, and that they see their students achieve their life ideals and goals. This is the best feedback for a teacher, an example, and a spiritual mentor. If possible, you can continue to report your learning progress to this spiritual role model and ask them for guidance on learning and life difficulties. "When I grow up, I will become like you," becoming someone positive, responsible, and hardworking like the teacher. I believe in you, you can become the best version of yourself.

question: Always feel unworthy? What kind of life is meaningful?
description: Parents are healthy, brothers and sisters are all happy, men are responsible and ambitious, and children are lively and sensible. Friends are supportive and reliable. However, I feel that I don't have the "ability" to enjoy the benefits that come with it. I always feel unworthy.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) Although you are currently happy, you feel unworthy. (2) You want to know what kind of life is meaningful. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping to help you: (1) Even though you have a happy family, is it because of your own insecurity that you feel unworthy? Or perhaps, having a smooth-sailing life actually makes you feel anxious? (2) You mentioned that you feel lacking in certain abilities, but what abilities are you referring to? Is it the ability to do something for your family? Maybe your existence is their comfort and expectation, don't you think? (3) The meaning of life probably lies in living as your true self, and it's important to enjoy the present moment. # The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

question: High school student, lacks trust with parents, and is also attracted to the same sex, can't go on...
description: I don't do well in my studies. My father forces me to study, he hits me, threatens me. He doesn't trust me and I don't trust him either. I'm very afraid of him, afraid of his cold violence and threats. I also feel that I have feelings for the same sex, that I am gay. My father keeps me locked in the room. I feel extremely suppressed and it feels like I'm only alive to study for him. Life feels meaningless, I want to commit suicide.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, growth process.

answers.answer_text: Hello, topic creator. Parents' pressure and threats regarding their children's studies can easily create a misconception in the child's mind: studying is doing things for the parents, not for oneself. I believe that both parents and children need to understand one thing: studying is one's own responsibility, and the only beneficiary of studying is oneself. Due to your father's pressure, threats, and punishments, your relationship has reached a state of mutual distrust and rigidity, and perhaps both sides have forgotten the initial purpose of urging you to study. Although pressure and threats are a form of harm, we must also acknowledge that this is an expression of your father's care and sense of responsibility, albeit using extreme and wrong methods. We not only need to see the surface behavior but also understand the motivations and reasons behind the behavior: hoping that you can study well and have a good future. Avoidance or rebellion is not the way to improve your relationship with your father. The only way is for you to truly understand that studying is your own responsibility and to be able to do it autonomously, consciously, and diligently. Only then can you regain your father's trust. Whether you are homosexual or not, there is no need to rush to conclusions. You can slowly become aware of your own feelings. Homosexuality is also a normal sexual orientation, and even if you are, you should not burden yourself with excessive psychological pressure. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

In fact, communication is always the most important when dealing with parent-child relationships. However, communication is often what we lack the most with our parents. In fact, high school is already a stage where one can be relatively independent. You can actually tell your parents your true thoughts, and they may open up to you and tell you the purpose behind their actions. There are no parents who do not love their children. Regardless of whether their actions are reasonable or not, they definitely have their intentions. Communicate more with your parents, understand their thoughts, and let them understand yours. Everyone should try to put themselves in each other's shoes, and maybe things won't become so extreme. Regarding homosexuality, simply having a crush on someone of the same sex does not necessarily mean you are homosexual. It is only when you have sexual fantasies and desires towards that person that it can be called homosexuality. Even if you have these traits, it doesn't really matter. Homosexuality is not a disease or an anomaly; it is simply a normal part of our diverse society and deserves respect, sitting on an equal footing with all other groups. So, there's no need to worry too much or feel like you're becoming an outcast. In fact, everyone goes through this phase, where they start to contemplate their own life and the value of life, and they develop greater understanding of their surroundings and themselves. However, as immature individuals, we may not be able to process the information we receive in a comprehensive and rational manner. Based on your current understanding, you may feel lost in finding the meaning and value of life, and you may feel like you are being pushed around. This period also involves the development of self-identity, as mentioned in psychology. What you need to do is to try and become optimistic and cheerful, and actively explore your life goals, gradually firming your beliefs and putting in effort... In fact, being alive is a wonderful thing. As long as you are willing to discover, you will realize that value is everywhere.

Maybe when we are in pain, we feel particularly lonely and helpless inside. Perhaps many people, like the OP, want to ask the world: Why am I so lacking and helpless? Why is there no one who understands and loves me? What is the bottom line of my life? Do I have the qualification to become better?... But if we change the question to a "fair and calm dialogue": In how many ways can I slowly accumulate my own energy? The secret of being understood and loved, where is it hidden in this world? When I have nothing, will the ocean, the sunlight, the mountains and rivers, the trees, and everything else in this world still love me? What does it mean to "become better"? Can I define it?... Does changing the way of questioning also change the feeling?

question: 24 years old, only focused on studying, why don't I have anyone of the opposite sex interested in me or confessing to me?
description: Girl, 24, has only focused on studying and being a good person since childhood and has never had a romantic relationship in school. Although she later had a boyfriend, this regret has always existed. That is, to naturally have someone like me and develop into a romantic relationship, instead of going on blind dates or social events to meet boyfriends. Other girls can have several boyfriends in one semester, but I haven't even had someone confess their feelings to me. I feel really difficult, so difficult. The most beautiful time in life is so short and time doesn't wait. I'm starting to feel hopeless now, crying every day, and even having thoughts of suicide. How can I console myself?

answers.answer_text: You seem to not like yourself very much but are eagerly hoping for boys to like you. The most beautiful time in life is so limited and time waits for no one. You have been using your precious time on regrets, being unable to let go, and crying. Even if time is meant to be wasted, it should be wasted on interesting things, on things that make you comfortable. Do what you love, do what is fun, do things that make you more beautiful. Please yourself, fall in love with yourself, and the boy who loves you will naturally come.

Hello! From your description, I can see your loneliness and inner longing. Teacher gives you a hug! From your description, I can see your self-management skills, you have always been a good obedient girl focused on studying. This is a quality that many people envy and long for. What makes you suffer now is that you still don't have any opposite-sex friends. When you see other girls enjoying their romantic relationships, you feel a sense of loss and a feeling of worthlessness. You can carefully observe how your classmates interact with each other and how you interact with them. If you calm down and analyze it, you may find that in order for more people to like you, you need to engage with them, interact with them, so that they can discover your excellence and inner beauty! Interaction can be through mutual back and forth, such as WeChat video calls, phone calls, etc. In short, making friends is based on mutual understanding and learning to interact, only then can you become friends. Try to take the initiative to contact those who you feel satisfied with and like. Contact and interact, it doesn't necessarily mean dating or becoming friends, but it is definitely an essential process for you to understand the opposite sex and learn to interact with them! Try to let go of your shyness and introversion from childhood and be more active and outgoing! With the blooming of flowers, butterflies will come naturally!

Looking back on my college days, I was also intimidated by the studious girls for the following reasons: 1. These girls are fully focused on their studies, they rarely dress up, and their appearance is almost indistinguishable from boys. 2. Because they are dedicated to their studies and have high expectations for themselves, they come across as cold and distant in communication. The typical femininity such as laughing and being playful is rarely seen in them. In short, they lack the charm of being a woman. Of course, I am not saying this to make you change. In life, there are always trade-offs. You may envy those girls who have multiple boyfriends in just one semester, and they may seem happy on the surface. But in the later stages of their lives, they won't be able to outpace you because they neglected their academic pursuits. As for you, since you are currently not distracted by relationships and focusing on your studies, after graduation, you will have more choices in finding a partner because of your excellence. It's up to you whether you prefer immediate romance or a more long-term perspective.

1. You only see other girls changing boyfriends every semester instead of going on blind dates. This is the established implementation, also known as the result or achievement. There's a saying, "you reap what you sow." You only see that other girls are getting results, but have you paid attention to what they have planted? Perhaps, in order to increase their attractiveness to boys, they spend late nights practicing various talents like dance, splits, or having a six-pack. They exercise and sweat every day to maintain their figure and skin. They work on improving their emotional intelligence by sincerely helping others and selflessly giving without expecting anything in return. They are also tolerant of others' strengths and weaknesses. Everything they do is about self-improvement.

2. There are also girls who are not in pain. They have only known about studying since they were young, and they haven't put much effort into developing their hobbies, talents, self-discipline, physical appearance, emotional intelligence, or IQ. They either feel tired or find it difficult, so they haven't invested much in self-improvement. Therefore, they don't want to change boyfriends frequently in one semester and feel satisfied with being able to meet a boyfriend through blind dates. They are content, so they are not in pain.

3. The third choice is to not choose either of the above two choices. They don't make efforts to improve themselves nor are they content. So, the heavens are angry. How is it possible to not want to put in much effort for self-improvement and still expect many boys to flock around? Such a good thing doesn't exist. They want everything, so the heavens punish such people.

question: Why do some people enjoy watching others' jokes? Shouldn't they sympathize with others?
description: I found that in life, there are many people who like to kick others when they are down, take pleasure in others' misfortune, and even enjoy it. I wonder, why is this the case? Shouldn't they feel sympathy for others?

answers.answer_text: Hello! I understand your feelings and give you a hug. Everyone may have different behavioral responses to the same situation. Our behaviors are influenced by various factors, including our own personalities, ways of thinking, and the environment we are in. Moreover, the same person may have different behavioral responses to different things, or even to the same thing at different times. These are all normal things. Whether we sympathize or take pleasure in others' suffering depends on rational and moral considerations. As for our emotional response, it varies from person to person. We say we should sympathize with others and be kind, which is more about rational thinking and moral perspective. Let's take a specific example. For instance, if someone accidentally bumps into you while you're walking down the street, you may still feel angry. Or you may feel the pain from being bumped. Whether it is anger or pain, it is a fact that cannot be changed and is your genuine reaction. Just like when you mentioned some people take pleasure in others' misfortune, that may be their immediate reaction. Another important question is, can you guarantee that you will always sympathize with others when they are in pain? I don't think anyone can. Let's take an extreme example. If someone suddenly punches you for no reason, and then they fall and hurt themselves, would you sympathize with their pain? Or would you be more likely to think they're silly or feel happy? Another extreme example, if a murderer escapes from prison and is caught shortly after, and during the escape, he is kicked hard by a police officer. Would you sympathize with the pain caused by the kick? I think everyone is ordinary and no one can unconditionally understand everyone. Of course, I want to emphasize that none of this is to encourage people to take pleasure in others' misfortune. It is to say that taking pleasure in others' misfortune may be a normal reaction. Because I think you may not understand why some people have such reactions. And I want to tell you that even if someone has a tendency to take pleasure in others' misfortune, it does not mean they will always do so whenever they see someone in pain. People's reactions can also change. Of course, we should strive to sympathize with others, be kind, and understand others more. Best wishes!

question: Should I take on a part-time job as a real estate assistant to deal with the pressure of high income and housing, or should I learn technical skills and find a stable job?
description: I am an assistant with a basic salary of 1800 yuan and a commission from the store. (The commission fluctuates due to the instability of store performance, sometimes barely enough to make a living, but the store's performance is indeed good.) I also work part-time selling houses. In everyone's eyes, being an assistant is an easy job with high commission, but I am under a lot of pressure and unhappy at work. I don't have many skills, and the salespersons always want me to treat them to meals. If I want to sell a house, I have to spend a lot of money to open up opportunities. Originally, I am not an outgoing person who is good at talking and handling others. My introverted, insecure, gentle, and honest personality is not suitable for sales. I have been in this job for eight months, and luckily sold a house. Maybe things will change in the future. I want to learn a skill, have a stable income, and live a happy and fulfilling life. But I am reluctant to give up on my dream. I'm thinking that if I try hard to sell more houses, I can earn tens of thousands of yuan per month and become successful. I am torn about what kind of job I should do.
keywords: Occupation, career management, job selection skills

answers.answer_text: Girl, you are even more outstanding than you imagine. Give you a hug, hoping to add courage to you. You are already excellent, and should not ignore your strengths - this is a correct understanding I see in your words. I see your inner insecurity and lack of self-awareness. Affirming yourself is the top priority, and seeing growth is a great way to increase confidence. As an assistant, you have to deal with daily affairs and also sell houses, which is a test for a person. But you have done it, and done it very well. Why would you overlook your shining points? Thinking that you are very inferior, very insecure, introverted, and so on, these are just the shortcomings you have magnified. These points will be hidden when you handle your work. Saying that selling a house is good luck, I do not agree with this view unless you also say that luck is a kind of ability. Since you sold the house, there must have been your hard work, tracking, various explanations, and introductions. These are all factors of success, and cannot be summarized with just the word "luck". Following your heart, you are doing what you want - I noticed that from the beginning, you have set a limit for yourself, staying at the assistant level. In fact, you can set a higher plan and goal for yourself, gradually getting closer. This can not only relieve the monotony and unhappiness in your work, but also better achieve your dreams. What has always troubled you is whether the salary is high or low and whether to have a stable life. In general, these things cannot be achieved at the same time. You are more inclined to choose a high-paying and decent job. It is better to be down-to-earth and do what you are doing now, but you need to set various plans for yourself and constantly improve and fulfill them. After persisting for a while, when you are emotionally and mentally stable, then look back and decide whether to stay or learn new skills. Handling relationships, knowing how to refuse and show appropriate weakness - learning to refuse is necessary when doing sales; you are definitely going to deal with all sorts of people and this requires emotional intelligence and the ability to handle situations. No one is born with these skills, but with experience, you will learn naturally. Especially when dealing with colleagues' requests, you must know how to tactfully refuse, at least to say no with a smile on your face. In the face of excessive demands, you must refuse firmly and let others know that you are not to be trifled with. Have a clear attitude, create a good network of relationships at work, and make sure others do not underestimate you. Learn from experience, and you will achieve compounded growth - it seems that you are young, which means there is a lot of room for advancement. At this time, you should be proactive in learning and doing things. Even if you make mistakes, it is still a form of growth. Regardless of success or failure, you must learn from the experience afterwards. When I say "learn from experience", it is not just about making a report or a simple summary. It means summarizing a rule or general experience from all situations and applying this insight to all future work. This requires a very high level of ability, and you should start doing it slowly from the beginning. You may not see significant results in the short term, but it will be of great help in half a year, a year, or even the next ten years. And if you can really apply it to your work, your career path will spiral upwards, with compounded income growth. When I share my thoughts, it feels like I'm speaking to a "beautiful, wealthy, and talented" person. This is my own intuition and sixth sense, and I believe that you can achieve your dreams, and the possibility is very high. It's just that right now, you are in a period of incubation, deep in the ground. When you are mature enough, you will break through the soil and have the most brilliant appearance. If you really want to give up and choose another life, it is not pitiful, and there is no need to struggle because that is also what you want. If you have achieved it, then it is the best.

No matter what industry you work in, as long as you achieve expert level or have access to quality resources, you won't have to worry about not having enough to eat. So it's not just about real estate sales, as you believe, that can make money, and learning technical skills won't earn you much money. Psychologists, doctors, and lawyers all follow a technical path, don't they? These industries don't require you to be extremely outgoing. To a large extent, it depends on how much professional knowledge you have accumulated, as long as you have strong abilities, there will be people willing to hire you. I think, apart from live streaming, which requires good speaking skills to attract attention, most jobs value experience and professional knowledge more. You can quietly research on your own. Even in property sales, you need to know how to promote properties that suit your clients, how to calculate property taxes, how to handle various procedures, and how to go through the loan process, etc. You need to be well-versed in these areas to convince clients. It's not just about being outgoing, it's only helpful for initial communication. In the end, it still involves professional knowledge. I have a friend who has some professional certificates in engineering that very few people have, both domestically and internationally. There's a shortage of talent like that. He earns tens of thousands of dollars every month. Once you become an expert and acquire enough knowledge, earning tens of thousands of dollars a month will be a piece of cake. The questioner is currently doing well in real estate sales, so you can continue to try it out, summarize your experiences and patterns, and build a network. If you can't do well after a year or two, it's not too late to give up. There are many people who do multiple jobs nowadays. Many people in my social circle sell insurance, but it doesn't hinder them from having full-time jobs. Extroversion and introversion aren't necessarily determined by the ability to speak. Introverted people can be good speakers too, they just don't like to talk to others too often, which makes them feel tired. Introverted people tend to prefer thinking on their own, being by themselves makes them happier. On the other hand, extroverted people like to seek energy from external interactions and being with many people makes them feel energized. Ask yourself what kind of work you truly enjoy, do you prefer dealing with people or prefer thinking alone? What are your strengths and what aspects of work bring you a sense of achievement? What experiences do you currently have that can help you find a job? Ultimately, even speaking can be trained in the later stage, but what suits you and what you like requires your own consideration. For example, although I'm not good at speaking, compared to doing research alone in the lab, I prefer communicating with people. So a job that involves frequent interactions with people suits me better. If I feel bothered by crowds and find large group activities boring, and I prefer reading and thinking on my own, then a technical research job might be more suitable. Since the questioner is still in the real estate industry, with some experience and decent income, you might as well stay for now. But that doesn't prevent you from thinking about your future path. You mentioned wanting to learn technical skills, so what specific field of technology is it? If you're particularly interested in one area, you can start by reading books in the relevant field, then pursue certification. After obtaining the certification, you can start working part-time and consider whether or not to switch careers once you do well. It would be risky to blindly change jobs without a clear goal, you might end up with nothing in the end.

Seeing these words, I hope they can bring you a little warmth. Hello, in your words, I see your confusion about the future, contemplation of current life, and fear of the unknown. These are all good, as long as you make up your mind, they will all become your motivation. Now let's look at your questions. Selling houses can be very profitable if done well. But there are two issues: 1. The sustainability of this job. How many years can you sell houses? After you can no longer sell houses, can this experience help you find other jobs? We not only need to consider the present, but also the future. 2. Your level of identification with this job. You mentioned that you are more introverted, which means you will be more passive and less happy in this job. In the short term, it's fine, but in the long run, it may make you feel miserable internally—I think there is a hint of this when you asked this question. So I think learning a skill is a better way out. But be aware that learning a skill is not easy, and life after learning the skill may not be as happy as you imagine. You may feel pain during the learning process, and you may still be confused after learning. So you need to be prepared in two ways: 1. Choose a direction that you relatively like. Interest is a great motivator, it will give you a sense of accomplishment and help you persevere. Especially when you think about the fact that this thing can make money for you, it will give you more motivation. 2. Persevere! Persevere! Persevere! Even if it is something you like, it will make you feel painful during long-term learning, encountering difficulties, and stagnation. At this time, you must persevere. The sun is waiting for you beyond that mountain. Meanwhile, selling houses and learning skills are not contradictory. Do not quit your job without proper preparation, especially when the economic situation is not good. You can prepare in two directions: selling houses and learning at the same time. This will be very hard. While others are playing games or browsing social media, you must study. It's difficult, but it's worth it. Here are a few tips: 1. You can make a list of your dreams and the things you want. Look at it when you feel like giving up or when you achieve a small success. It will motivate and encourage you. 2. Find someone who can supervise you. They must be proactive and strive to be someone you can look up to. Stay away from those who are lazy and not motivated, and who disturb and undermine you while you study. 3. Give yourself a small reward appropriately so that you know that your efforts are not in vain. I believe that as long as you take action and persevere, you will definitely become a completely different person from the current confused self. Keep it up!

Brother, there are no perfect things in this world. Everything requires compromise and comes with a cost. Just like when I first arrived in Guangzhou, I didn't have regular meals, let alone a future plan, but I still persisted in working not just for the salary. Step by step, I sacrificed for learning, for the company, and for the customers, giving up my time and money, but I held onto my values. Do what you enjoy, find the intersection of your interests and abilities. Once you find yourself, everything will fall into place. Wish you the best, work hard, my friend.

Being able to sell a house is also a "technical job". Therefore, in terms of career, learning is lifelong. The more skills you acquire, the higher the chances of making money, resisting risks, and enjoying a comfortable life in the future. So, seemingly contradictory choices are not really a problem (perhaps). Maybe you can have more options, such as selling houses while learning new skills? Consider every challenge as an opportunity to learn. When you have climbed higher mountains, these dilemmas will no longer be dilemmas.

question: New graduates who come to Beijing to find jobs may feel overwhelmed and stressed. How can they manage and alleviate these feelings?
description: I will graduate this year with a major in Chinese and I'm planning to find a job in Beijing. I'm mainly interested in the media and entertainment industry, where there are more opportunities in Beijing. I've been searching for a job for a month and had three internships during the process. However, I gave up on each of them after only working for two or three days because I realized they weren't what I wanted to do and it was causing me a lot of pain. It's so difficult to find a job that I actually want, and the more I search, the worse my mindset becomes. The past two weeks have been tough because of the severe COVID-19 situation in Beijing. I've been at home sending out resumes for a week without any response, and I feel so frustrated. I'm starting to wonder if coming to Beijing was the right decision for me. How can I manage my job search anxiety? Moreover, living alone in a different city makes me feel lonely, and I find myself constantly turning to food for comfort. Whenever I encounter difficulties, I always think about giving up and going back, but I don't want to avoid these challenges. I just don't know how to adjust myself.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP: Hugs to you. Thumbs up to you, you are a child who dares to strive and is not afraid of hardship. I understand your feelings very well. Living alone in Beijing can make you feel helpless and anxious when you encounter difficulties. From your words, I can see the conflicting feelings you have about your job and work location. Don't worry, let's take a look at the issues you mentioned in your writing. "I have been sending resumes at home for a week without any response and I feel very frustrated." (Under the impact of the epidemic this year, the pressure of employment is indeed very high. Many people, including recent graduates, have not been able to find suitable job opportunities quickly. OP, hugs to you. Employment pressure is actually a common problem that many people face.) "I have been looking for a job for a month, and I quit after only working for two or three days in three different trial jobs." (In fact, as a recent graduate, in the current situation of high employment pressure, being able to get offers from at least three companies within a month shows that you are capable. Normally, before officially starting a job, we will have a preliminary understanding of the company and position through online channels or communication with the interviewers. But why did you quit after only working for two or three days in the trial jobs? I think there are two main reasons: 1. Insufficient understanding of the company and the position before accepting the job, and later found that it doesn't match; How to deal with it? I suggest that you learn about the basic situation of the company and the position through websites, communication with the interviewers, and even talking to senior students who have worked in the same position, so that you can shorten the time needed to familiarize yourself with the job after starting. 2. Having excessively high expectations for the job and later finding a discrepancy between it and what you truly desire; This situation is quite common among recent graduates. When entering the workplace for the first time, we often have high expectations for our careers. At this time, adjusting our mindset to have a realistic understanding of the current market conditions is the most rational approach. I suggest that you think about your personality, interests, professional capabilities, and consider what type of company you prefer and are suitable for, and what aspects of career development are most important to you. For example, in the media and entertainment industry, do you prioritize salary or platform? What is your most interested and suitable work direction in this industry? If your interests and abilities do not match, how should you choose?) "Whenever I encounter difficulties, I always think about going back, but I don't want to avoid these challenges." (From this sentence, I see another conflict: the conflict regarding the work location. In Beijing, being alone, feeling a lot of pressure, anxiety, and loneliness, but Beijing also has better job opportunities; going back to the previous city means fewer job opportunities and limited career development, but being surrounded by friends and family makes life relatively easy and stress-free. How to choose? OP, you need to ask your heart. As a recent graduate without work experience, when looking for a job, you have to consider everything at the same time, but the possibility of getting everything is low. Since it's impossible to have everything, what do you truly value in your heart?) Before making a choice, you can try to alleviate your anxiety so that you can make a better decision. There are many ways to relieve anxiety. First, you can relax through exercise, such as doing yoga or going for walks or jogs. These activities can help improve your mood. Second, you can consider relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing exercises and muscle relaxation exercises. These two methods require practicing in advance so that they can be effective when you are feeling stressed. Third, you can talk to someone close to you, such as your family or friends, about your feelings. You mentioned that eating can also help relieve anxiety. Lastly, I would like to tell you that stepping out of the anxious state and asking your heart is the key to what you truly value in your career. If your current abilities do not match your expectations, instead of being anxious and miserable, it's better to face the gap, make changes, and strive for a future where your abilities and dreams can be matched. If you temporarily cannot find a job with the work content you like, it's better to start with what suits you. Because what you truly like is often felt through practice. The best way to relieve anxiety is to make a choice and then work hard towards it. Good luck.

Hello. I am fortunate to give you some advice. After reading your description, I can feel that you are currently feeling disappointed and helpless in your career, which has led to a lack of confidence and confusion. You mentioned that you studied Chinese in university and currently have an interest in the media industry. There is some connection between these two, but at the same time, we also need to realize- *how much connection there is between the two* and *what is your true passion in your heart?* *What are you good at in the Chinese industry? What are you good at in the media industry?* ... These are the questions that need to be pondered upon now, as they relate to- *self-awareness* life planning* career planning* ... Next, let's analyze your current situation objectively and rationally. "Career planning- I don't know where your university is located, but how is the employment situation for the Chinese major in your hometown or the city where your university is located? You mentioned that there are many opportunities to choose from in Beijing, so does this mean that you have already done a detailed analysis of the industry in your hometown and university location, and coming to Beijing is a well-considered decision? Or is it influenced by articles on the internet, and you believe that not coming to Beijing would be regretful, so you firmly believe in it? You have just graduated, which is a good time to strive and also a golden period for trial and error. Being able to learn, experience, and comprehend as much as possible while young will be of great help to your future. Therefore, you should not be afraid of making mistakes at this time and bravely pursue it. "Life planning- Understand your true reasons for coming to Beijing, and let's talk about it from the perspective of life planning. Do you have any thoughts about your future at the moment? Or do you have any role models and hope to be as excellent as them? If so, what specific qualities make them excellent? What is your current state in terms of these excellent qualities? Everyone hopes that their future will be "happy", but at the same time, let's not forget that "accumulation in the early stage is essential", and here are a few words for you- "slow is fast". Nowadays, many of us may have the mindset of "instant realization" because the times are progressing rapidly. While we are in this big environment, let's not forget what we want and not forget our original intentions. Lastly, you mentioned that you have interned at several companies, but after a few days, you feel that it is not suitable or does not meet your expectations. This also goes back to the earlier mentioned "career planning" and "self-awareness". There is no problem with liking the media industry, but we need to clarify *what this industry is like*, *how to apply what we have learned and contribute to the media industry*, and *what is the exact feeling of discomfort when we are actually in the media industry*... Pursuing your passion truly requires courage, and you have done it. The current situation is to combine your own self and gain a deeper understanding of your inner self in order to gradually find your own place. Good luck with everything.

I can feel the pressure on the topic host. Full of longing to go to Beijing to develop, eager to achieve their career ideals, the continuous setbacks in work and the difficulties in interpersonal relationships have made you feel stressed. You may consider starting from two aspects: career planning and adjusting your mindset. Firstly, you have to affirm yourself. Leaving your comfort zone and boldly exploring the unknown is a great move. Tell yourself that the difficulties are temporary. Don't set high goals for yourself. At the beginning, you may not have a clear career path right after graduation. You can start by finding a job that suits you and then seek further development. Many people around me who come to work in big cities don't have very good first jobs, and the salary is not high, but this job gives them the capital to find better jobs later. You can also choose a stepping stone before finding a satisfactory job. Tell yourself that some things are beyond your control to lighten your emotional burden. For example, the epidemic has reduced job opportunities, which does not mean you are wrong or avoiding something. No one can predict such events. You can try to do a career planning. Professional planners will find the most suitable career direction for you based on your abilities and preferences. However, before seeking advice, you can think about a few questions. You mentioned that you quit three jobs. Were all three of them in the media and entertainment industry? What were the reasons for quitting? Besides resigning, do you think there are other ways to overcome the difficulties you have encountered? If you can't find a job that completely satisfies you for the time being, can you start with a job that you can handle? Adjust your goals to establish yourself in Beijing first, then learn and find direction in your work, and finally transition to the job you like. What kind of work do you want to do? Are there specific and clear criteria you can refer to? Which aspect of work do you value the most? Salary? Values? Or job content? If you can't satisfy all of them, can you start with the most important one? What do you think is hindering you right now? Are your abilities matched with the requirements of your ideal job? If they are not matched, what efforts can you make to achieve them? If you feel lonely and bored in your life, you can try online dating or participate in some offline activities, find hobbies for yourself, enrich your spiritual life, and maybe you will unexpectedly get job opportunities while getting to know different people. Socializing itself also has the function of relieving pressure. I hope the topic host doesn't put too much pressure on themselves. As long as the green mountains are preserved, there will be no shortage of firewood. There will always be opportunities, even if not now. If the recent epidemic prevents you from finding a satisfactory job, you can also try other cities or go back home. This is not avoiding or giving up, but a strategy. After all, it's important to live happily.

Daring to venture into Beijing alone, I'm sure you have already prepared yourself to face difficulties! The asker mentioned that in the past two weeks, the COVID-19 situation in Beijing has been severe. They have been sending out resumes from home for a week but haven't received any reply, and they feel very frustrated, wondering if coming to Beijing was the right decision. How should one deal with job search anxiety? Moreover, living alone in a new place makes them feel lonely and isolated, which leads to overeating. Whenever they encounter difficulties, they always think about going back, but they don't want to avoid these challenges. However, they don't know how to adjust themselves. Difficulties are temporary, as long as you have the determination to never give up, and you are willing to endure hardships and try out different jobs, there is a possibility of settling down in Beijing. I understand that you are currently feeling anxious and easily shaken in your beliefs, and it's easy to think of negative things. At this moment, we can adjust our coping strategies and try to think positively. For example, try recording three good things that happen around you every day. This method is very simple. Just take 10 minutes before sleeping each day to write down three good things that happened. For instance, when you finish work, you bought yourself a dessert that you love. Another example is that you have become familiar with life in Beijing. Yet another example is that you accidentally broke a cup in a restaurant, but the boss didn't blame you. It is important to write down why each thing happened, like "Because I was feeling a bit down, I intentionally bought myself a dessert to cheer up." "Because I have been staying here for a while, I know the people around and have become familiar with the place." "After breaking the cup, I quickly apologized to the boss and offered to compensate, so the boss didn't blame me." This method may feel a bit awkward when you first start, but if you stick with it for six months, you will start to like it because the surprises of life are in the small and mundane things. You can give it a try.

It's like that when you first come out. I was like that too at first. This is a very low point in life, so please don't give up on yourself. It's something everyone has to go through in life, as a way to learn and grow, to become independent. Although this process is very painful, here's a comforting hug for you. But you must summon up the courage to face everything. I believe the future will get better. When I first entered a new city, it was the same. I felt lost, lonely, and scared. Filled with despair about the future, not knowing what I could do. Constantly doubting myself and questioning myself. Feeling like the world was falling apart, feeling just like you, constantly wanting to escape back to nature because it feels safe there. It's a way to avoid facing anxiety. Feeling very anxious inside, feeling like I can't keep up with this world. Feeling like everything and everyone is rejecting me. Many of the jobs were not what I had imagined. I entered with confidence and determination, but kept losing to reality. I believe you are experiencing something similar. Feeling helpless, helpless, and scared. Negativity consumes oneself. Here, I will give you my personal opinions and advice, hoping to help you. During this time when the COVID-19 situation in Beijing is severe, it's definitely difficult to find a job. This is not your fault, it's the environment. So don't lose heart. You need to adjust your mindset. This has nothing to do with you, it's just the general environment. Everyone is in the same situation. The early days in society are always tough, that's for sure, because we lack experience and we need to accept the pace of this city and certain basic experiences and rules in our industry. It's a process. Besides accepting this process, we also need to constantly learn and grow in order to integrate and progress. So we need to persevere and learn. In Beijing, a city with a fast pace, because it's developed, everything moves faster, and the pressure is greater than in other cities. It's precisely because of the fast pace and greater pressure that there are more and better opportunities to learn and unleash your potential. Suffering can be endured. But we need to understand that all the experiences we accumulate are to improve ourselves, to promote our own growth, and that is the most important thing. Only then can we achieve what we want more efficiently. We must find a profession that we like. Even if the work is hard and tiring, we have to persist, do it for a while, a few months first, endure even if it's hard, we need to understand it first. The industry we work in has its own rules and experiences on top, and only then can we choose a better path. So this process is very painful. Secondly, we need a job to get a foothold in this city. Home is the warmest and safest place. It's normal to think of home during our suffering and discomfort. But we must learn to grow on our own, to constantly strive. And then we can protect, become the protector of our home. Our parents have protected us for over 20 years, and now it's our turn to grow. The future. It's up to us to protect, as well as our own families. Let's go!

question: How do you adjust when you encounter something beyond your capabilities and lose confidence in life?
description: I have encountered something that is beyond my capabilities but I must solve. I have been unable to solve it for two years and there has been no substantial progress. I have lost confidence and cannot see any hope. I have to rely fully on myself. In the past two months, I have experienced some breakdowns, affecting my physical health. I am in a very bad state, but I am resistant to, and conflicted about, trying to adjust my state.
keywords: Occupation, workplace relationships, work pressure, work exhaustion.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I can feel your helplessness and frustration, and I sympathize with you. First of all, I want you to know that everyone in life will encounter problems that their abilities cannot solve at some point, and they will have similar feelings as you. So what we should consider is analyzing the problem: why can't we solve it ourselves and where are our weaknesses in terms of abilities? Who can compensate for these weaknesses and help us solve these problems? In other words, we should learn to seek support. If we really can't solve the problem and no one can help us, remember that all roads lead to Rome, and in life, there may be ways to bypass this problem and continue moving forward. Life doesn't need to be 100% perfect.

question: Can traditional Chinese medicine treat anxiety disorders? Does herbal medicine really work for treatment?
description: Last April, I fell ill (non-psychological illness) and was blamed by my family. There was also a lot of work pressure. Every time I heard the phone ring, I would feel anxious and even thought I had a psychological illness. Since around May last year, I gradually developed orthostatic hypotension, nausea every morning, fatigue, and drowsiness throughout the day. I started to improve after living alone for two months. During the epidemic, I worked from home and my emotions gradually stabilized. But I don't know if this calmness means I'm really getting better, or if I have just become accustomed to this anxiety and fear. I not only worry about my own affairs, but also become anxious about things that have nothing to do with me. In the past few months, as long as something happens, I will have insomnia at night, shallow sleep, and wake up very early the next day, around 4 o'clock in the morning. I have dreams all night, most of which are nightmares. I saw a Chinese medicine doctor half a month ago who said it was anxiety disorder, and I took Chinese medicine for a while but didn't feel much difference. The questioner mentions having a habit of self-pleasure for several years and wanting to change it. Habits cannot be completely eradicated, but they can be changed. Habits are permanent, but at the same time they are fragile and can easily be replaced by another habit. Habits are formed by cues, and we are more likely to notice obvious cues. Creating vivid visual cues will redirect your attention towards the desired action. If you want a habit to become an important part of your life, make cues an important part of your life first. Understanding this, we can start by eliminating or hiding cues that prompt the habit, such as adult films or explicit images. Replace them with good cues, for example, if the questioner is studying, place study materials in a visible place. Additionally, avoid wearing revealing or loose clothing, as it makes it easier to engage in self-pleasure, which acts as a cue. Furthermore, it is beneficial to have a communal life as it often encourages us to change habits. We have all had the experience of wanting to stay in bed on weekends but being compelled to get up on time to go to class or work when we have to do it with others. This is because we all have a compelling reason to do so, a belief from the depths of our hearts that we must do it. When this belief is reinforced repeatedly with strong determination, it becomes faith and forms a habit. Therefore, when we want to develop a new habit, being in a community is more conducive to its formation. The shared belief and struggle towards a common goal encourages us to continue working hard when we are about to give up. This significantly increases the probability of successfully changing habits. So, to cultivate new good habits, it is advisable to try joining online or offline groups, such as morning routines, vocabulary memorization, English speaking groups, etc.

question: I am very concerned about my girlfriend's past and often unintentionally fantasize about various scenarios.
description: I accidentally looked through my girlfriend's phone and found out that she had been frequenting various nightclubs, bars, and similar places for a long period of time in the past. The comments and messages on her social media were often filled with explicit language from male friends. I had completely missed all of this during the time we've known each other, so this experience completely shattered my perception of her. However, after being together, she has not shown any of these problems again, to the point where I keep imagining disturbing images of her past with other men in my mind.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, I can sense your confusion and uneasiness, and these complex emotions are actually the same as those in your girlfriend's heart. Although she has been to many entertainment places, whether out of curiosity or to relax, deep down, she feels the same as you do, that this is not something a "good and virtuous" girl should do. So, when you started dating, she chose to conceal it. In other words, she split herself internally, denying some of her past experiences and a part of herself. It is evident that she does not accept herself. Of course, it is also because she can sense your lack of acceptance towards these things and worries that it will cause conflicts if you were to find out. We shouldn't judge whether going to bars or similar places is right or wrong; existence itself is reasonable. It is simply a matter of individual lifestyle and should not be used to determine a person's character or quality. However, every person's chosen lifestyle will inevitably bear the resulting consequences. Note, I am referring to consequences, not punishments. When we want to view things truthfully, we must let go of judgment and focus only on the facts and individuals involved. We only need to understand the patterns and directions of things, while right or wrong, good or bad, are based on judgment standards deeply rooted in each person's heart, which are connected to their own personal feelings, societal expectations, upbringing, and education, among other factors. Therefore, there is no need to demand strict standards, as they are not uniform. However, humanity also shares common emotions, one of which is to not harm others. In other words, every action you take, whether you are truly responsible for yourself and others. For example, if a person's way of relaxation borders on indulgence, the most immediate victim will be themselves. Externally, they will expose themselves to a situation where they are more easily harmed, while internally, they will experience strong self-doubt and disgust because they brought it upon themselves. So, whether externally or internally, anyone who does something that harms others will ultimately harm themselves. Your girlfriend's past behavior indicates that she lacks a sense of security deep down. She constantly needs to prove that she is worthy of love and attention. However, her methods will not yield positive feedback and will only make her more lost. Perhaps, after meeting you, she has experienced a long-lost sense of security, although she is still fearful; otherwise, she would not have intentionally concealed it. However, she doesn't know that if you don't see and accept her fully, this sense of security won't be solid. Now, let's talk about your feelings. Any choice we make is never detached from our subconscious. The reason why you chose a girl who enjoys going to bars also has to do with your own reasons. Although you say you were unaware before, if you never doubted her internally, you would not have looked at her phone. The fact that you chose to look at her phone subconsciously indicates a lack of trust in the relationship and in yourself. The traits that one dislikes in others are also a part of their inner shadow. Perhaps, in your own growth experiences, you have experienced betrayal or indulgence. Perhaps, the women around you have engaged in behaviors that you consider shameful. Maybe, during your growth process, these thoughts and behaviors were absorbed by your subconscious. Not everyone has the courage to act on those behaviors, but being aware of the thoughts is sufficient. Shadows don't necessarily manifest externally. You have already tormented yourself repeatedly in your thoughts, and that is the unresolved conflict within you. I think you should find out the reasons behind these accumulated conflicts, why you feel such a strong sense of insecurity towards women and intimate relationships, and why there is this mixture of shame and anger. Only when you confront your own insecurities will you choose turmoil. Any challenges a person faces are of importance to their own being and not randomly generated. You should try to listen to your inner self, examine your experiences, and understand yourself more, rather than getting entangled in these torments and cycles. Any answers given by others are only irresponsible opinions. Ultimately, how to proceed, how to handle the relationship, only you will understand yourself best. There is no so-called correct path, only self-growth and self-responsibility. Regardless of how the relationship develops, as long as each person takes responsibility for themselves and does what they should, it is enough.

As the relationship deepens, the understanding between two people will always be continuously updated. After snooping on your girlfriend's phone, your perception of her has been refreshed, as if it has shattered your idealistic image of her. She is not the innocent girl you originally imagined, nor is she necessarily the promiscuous girl you now imagine. The past is an unchangeable fact, but with changes in perception, the interpretation of the past will also change. Maybe you need to reflect on how you view the fact that she used to go to nightclubs. Become aware of the emotions you feel after discovering this part of her history and explore your true needs. Perhaps you are very concerned about your girlfriend's past not only because of what she has done, but also because of what you have done in the past. Perhaps, deep down, your concern about her past is actually a worry about your future.
