It shows that she has made a great change now. You can talk to her and ask her to assure you that she will not behave like that in the future. You need to treat this matter with a calm mind. In your daily life, try not to deliberately think about this matter and learn to see the strengths of your girlfriend. Take care~.

question: Reluctant to put down the phone, insomnia, feeling tired during the day?
description: I am relatively awake even until 1.2 AM at night, although I can fall asleep quickly once I put down my phone, but I just don't want to put it down. And in the morning, I can't wake up, and I feel unenergetic during the day at work.

answers.answer_text: Hello! It's quite common to prefer playing with your phone rather than sleeping at night. This can also be understood as "revenge sleep procrastination". You can try to assess how many things you did during the day were things you truly wanted to do from the bottom of your heart, and how many were things you had to do. If there were too many things you had to do, it can be emotionally draining and make you feel like you're not living your own life. So, at night, you try to compensate for it by doing things that make you feel relaxed and happy, things that you genuinely want to do. Another situation could be having too many things you want to achieve or feeling anxious and fearful about not being able to achieve them. In that case, it's necessary to sort them out. I recommend writing as a way to organize your scattered thoughts. Suggestions: 1. Adjust your mindset. When faced with something that you don't feel motivated to do, think about the value of that thing and what you can gain from it. Replace the phrase "I have to..." with "I choose to..., because by doing so, I can...". 2. Avoid taking your phone to bed and keep it further away. Instead, engage in bedtime meditation, focusing your attention on your breathing to help you fall asleep. It may take some time if you find yourself getting more awake the more you think about it. Good luck! FF.

Good afternoon, OP. Although you can fall asleep quickly when you put down your phone, you just don't want to. You can't wake up in the morning and lack energy during the day. Based on your description, I have a few thoughts to share with you. One, you can reflect on how long this has been going on. What kind of events before bedtime disrupt your sleep? Two, even though you can quickly fall asleep at night if you put down your phone, you still can't let go of it. What kind of content attracts you while using your phone? What are your thoughts and feelings when you can't let go of your phone? Three, not being able to wake up in the morning and lacking energy during the day is the result of not getting enough rest at night. In order to improve your work performance the next day. During this pandemic, most of us have experienced significant changes in our daily routines. Personally, from January to July, I often stayed up late and had a difficult time waking up in the morning. Based on my own experience, let me share with you. In July, I made adjustments to my daily routine. First, it is important to know the reasons for adjusting our sleep schedule. One, an irregular sleep schedule can negatively impact our physical functions, such as memory decline and lack of energy during the day. So, we need to adjust our daily routine. Two, in this special year, many of us have experienced unemployment or a lack of work opportunities. In such a situation, our laziness might arise. We may find ourselves browsing our phones at night when there is nothing to do during the day. There is a lot of content on our phones that we haven't experienced before or that attracts us, causing us to lose sleep and affecting our ability to wake up in the morning. This can also lead to feelings of emptiness, helplessness, and loneliness. Therefore, it is important to establish a daily routine. This is the first step I took to change my sleep schedule: between 10:00-11:00 PM, struggled to put down my phone and let my consciousness guide my subconscious into sleep. The second step is to listen to soothing music that aids sleep. The third step is to engage in activities during the day, such as exercise or tidying up the house, to keep the body active. Establish a daily exercise and learning schedule to keep yourself occupied during the day, which will help with sleep at night. The fourth step is to maintain a regular and light diet. Avoid heavy meals in the afternoon, as this can reduce the burden on the body and promote sleep. These are some of my own experiences and methods for adjusting my daily routine, which I wanted to share with you, OP. Now, I will share some of my thoughts and advice regarding the issue you described, in the hope of helping you. If you really can't fall asleep, you can try putting down your phone and not be attracted to its content. For example, you can tidy up the house or do some exercise for half an hour before bed. The most important thing is to be aware and remind yourself not to look at your phone, as you have already realized that the reason you can't sleep is because you can't let go of your phone. Therefore, try to shorten the time you spend with your phone and interact more with your family and friends. You can also try listening to some sleep-inducing music, which you can find on platforms like Himalaya.

Give the OP a hug! I can understand the OP's anxiety and restlessness. At night, when not wanting to sleep and having nothing else to do, one can't help but pick up the phone and watch interesting videos or read novels, which increases interest and makes it even harder to fall asleep. The later one stays up, the worse the sleep quality becomes, and the less inclined one is to get out of bed in the morning, resulting in lower energy levels during the day and affecting normal work. Normally, after working all day, both the body and mind should be tired, making it easy to feel drowsy and fall asleep. However, the OP is still wide awake before midnight, so it's curious what the OP has been doing after getting off work. The normal sleep time is between 9 PM and 11 PM, during which it's easy to fall asleep. If one misses this time frame and delays sleep, the longer the delay, the later one falls asleep, and the sleep quality becomes insufficient, affecting one's mental state. The fact that the OP is aware that putting down the phone will allow them to fall asleep but still unwilling to do so shows that the phone holds significant importance for them. Looking at the phone provides a sense of satisfaction that cannot be experienced in real life, which is why the OP is reluctant to put it down. However, the contents of the phone cannot replace reality. The needs of real life must be fulfilled through real life experiences. Over-reliance on the phone will only increase self-denial and exacerbate anxiety and fear of normal social interactions, leading to even stronger dependency on the phone and further impairment of social functioning. The OP can set a decreasing schedule for phone usage, gradually reducing the time spent on it each day. In the remaining time, besides personal activities, they can cultivate hobbies to establish a connection between themselves and society, feel their own existence, and gain corresponding satisfaction. At the same time, this will reduce excessive dependence on and attachment to the phone and increase energy devoted to normal social interactions. Of course, the OP can also make an appointment with a suitable therapist for systematic psychological counseling to address these concerns.

Hello OP! I used to be a member of the night owl team and firmly believed that I was a night person. My habit was to stay up during the day and come alive at night, feeling drowsy during the day and sleepy in the winter. However, everything changed when I learned about neuroscience. Let's analyze the issue of staying up late from a brain perspective. First, why are we still awake and alert around one or two in the morning? It's because of blue light. According to the normal biological rhythm, our body naturally secretes melatonin, which makes us feel sleepy and helps us fall asleep. Exposure to blue light reduces the secretion of melatonin or delays the secretion process, affecting both sleep duration and quality. Solution: To address this, you can adjust your phone settings with a blue light filter. Secondly, why is it so hard to put down our phones? It feels like we can play with them forever! The more exhausted we are, the less we want to sleep and the more we want to use our phones. It's because our brains are uncontrollable when we're extremely tired. The feeling of being excessively tired is similar to being intoxicated. Your brain becomes foggy, memory deteriorates, and your self-control weakens. Try to recall what you specifically did and looked at on your phone in the early morning when you were playing with it. Can you remember? I certainly can't. Solution: When you still have control over yourself, put your phone away and engage in activities you enjoy that are unrelated to your phone, such as reading physical books, drawing, or reflecting on the events of the day with your eyes closed. Put your phone in the kitchen to charge before going to bed and get an alarm clock to wake you up in the morning. Finally, why can you quickly fall asleep when you close your eyes? Scientists have conducted fatigue tests on this matter. They asked participants to lie in bed, turn off the lights, and monitored their sleep. If they naturally fell asleep within five minutes, it indicated that their body was extremely tired. When you are excessively tired, you become more sensitive, anxious, and your reaction speed slows down while your perception declines, affecting your work performance. It's like playing the game of life in hard mode. Adequate sleep is crucial. So, let's do it together! Put your phone in the kitchen to charge one hour before bedtime! Source: "Self-driven Growth: Chapter 7 Sleep: The Most Complete Shutdown Period."

Hello! I understand how you feel, because I went through a similar phase recently. It seemed like I couldn't put my phone down, and before I knew it, time had slipped away and it was already dawn. Instead of thinking about how to put down the phone, why not try not picking it up in the first place? Set a reminder for yourself, it could be an alarm clock or even scheduled shutdown. You can also use the "Healthy Phone Usage" feature on your phone, set a limit on how long you can use certain apps, or use the "Ultra Power Saving" function. Try to avoid picking up your phone before going to bed. It might be challenging at first, but as you mentioned, "putting down the phone can help you fall asleep quickly." With time, you should be able to adapt. Another important point is not to procrastinate, finish the important tasks of the day before going to bed. If you have trouble waking up in the morning, apart from not getting enough sleep the night before, the main reason might be that you don't enjoy your current work, or there are other things during the day that you don't want to face. In this case, it's recommended to do something you enjoy in the morning, so that you wake up motivated every day. If you can't manage to sleep early, then try planning to wake up early. When you have something important to do in the morning, naturally, thoughts of going to bed early will come to mind. Also, thinking about the things you want to do the next day when you wake up, doesn't everything become better? I wish you all the best, the world and I love you.

Hello, even though you know that staying up late and playing on your phone will affect your work performance during the day, you still cannot control yourself and repeat this behavior. Have you ever thought that your subconscious is using playing on your phone to exhaust yourself and fight against the disappointments of work? If it is a job you are passionate about, you will feel motivated to go to bed early and prepare for the next day. However, if you resist the work itself and are forced to engage in it because of the need for a source of livelihood, the suppressed emotions have no outlet and can only be temporarily relieved by playing on your phone to cope with work pressure. It is recommended to deeply contemplate the balance between work and life.

Hello, OP. It seems that it is difficult for you to put down your phone at night, which obviously affects your normal work. I can tell that you want to change your mood. Try to think slowly, have you ever been able to put down your phone once or a few times? What methods did you use at that time, what did you think of, or did you not think of anything? Additionally, you can try using external factors to limit your phone usage, such as setting a timer to shut it off or putting your phone in student mode. These are just some suggestions from me, hoping to help you. Take care!

question: When I was a child, I was sexually abused by my older brother. Now, my inner turmoil is becoming increasingly unbearable. How can I resolve this?
description: When I was a child, my parents did not provide proper sex education to me. At the age of six or seven, I was sexually abused by my own brother, and in my teens, I was molested by him. Now, I am suffering deeply and feeling immense pain. I want to commit suicide. I really want to tell my mother, but I fear she won't believe me. I'm afraid that if I speak out, my family will treat me differently again. However, it was the fault of that beast, why should I have to endure it and accept my relatives' indifference? It is really painful to put on a facade of normalcy during the day, and I can only silently cry alone in the dark at night. How should I handle this situation? What should I do?
keywords: Treatment, psychological crisis, psychological counseling, trauma therapy.

answers.answer_text: Regarding this, I hope you can hear a better answer from a professional to help you. **When you were six or seven years old, how old was your brother? If you were in your childhood, this so-called "sexual abuse" would be more like sexual play, which is a game and exploration conducted by children out of curiosity rather than actual sexual abuse in the true sense.** What was the situation when you were in your teens? Our attitude towards sex should be based on the principles of "autonomy, respect, responsibility, and health." If you were violated, do you feel ashamed? But why should you be ashamed? It's not your fault, it's his fault, right? The sexual organs are just located differently. If we look at it from the perspective of equal organs, is it not similar in meaning to someone punching your face or hitting your head? By understanding it in this way, would you feel a bit better psychologically? We should protect our sexual organs just like we protect other organs. All organs have the right to privacy, right? ε I'm here, the world and I love you.

It's so difficult for you... The person who sexually assaulted you is your own brother, what a huge trauma! Even through the screen, I can feel your helplessness and pain. Legally speaking, your brother's actions constitute child molestation, and he can be sentenced to prison for that. However, has it been a long time since it happened? Did you keep any evidence at the time? Do your parents or relatives believe you? And do you have the courage to face the painful scars of your childhood? These are all things you need to consider. On the other hand, your silence over the years has actually suppressed it deep inside you, forming deep-rooted trauma. Trauma can have a huge impact on a person, and if it is not resolved or supported, it will accompany you like a shadow. What should you do? The conflict between the practical considerations and the desires deep inside you has exhausted you and caused you pain. I have given lectures on adolescent sexual education and preventing sexual abuse of girls to many transient teenagers. For children who have already been violated, I usually advise them to seek positive resources in their lives and professional psychological support. There is also an organization that specifically advocates for the protection of girls. You can follow their public account "Girls' Protection" and contact this group. There are many people who have gone through similar experiences like yours, and you can find support and warmth together. Additionally, there are many people who, with their own traumatic experiences, practice the concept of helping others and helping themselves by teaching about preventing sexual abuse, which can also be a way of healing. As for whether or not to use legal means to punish your own brother, that depends on your own judgment after seeking support and help. Finally, sending you hugs and wishing you well~.

OP, hello~~~ Sending you a warm hug after reading your description, I feel very angry and indignant as well. Your brother's actions have crossed moral and legal boundaries. I feel heartbroken for what you've been through. Firstly, we must stop such actions that hurt us and seek the protection of those capable of protecting us: If you are worried about your parents not believing or unwilling to tell them, we can tell our teachers or other trusted individuals. However, on the other hand, parents can provide the most immediate protection for their children, so this also needs to be considered based on your actual situation. Choose a trusted adult to tell them about your situation as soon as possible. On the other hand, if your brother tries to harm you again, we need to learn to resist and do everything we can to prevent ourselves from getting hurt. Besides the people you know, you can also seek help from legal professionals in society. Don't worry about how your family might treat you if the situation is discovered. As you said, it's not your fault, and you don't need to take any responsibility for it. Instead, your brother should face the appropriate punishment. Let your inner strength grow.

Hello, author, I am 19 years old this year, and I don't know if I am a little older or younger than you. When I was in third grade, I was sexually harassed by a middle-aged man. Only some people in my family know about this, I have never told anyone else. It has been about 10 years, and the memories have slowly faded. I usually act like it never happened and I rarely think about it. But when I saw your question, I was reminded of the past. It's quite a coincidence that I encountered a psychologist on this counseling platform who has had a similar experience. Child victims of this kind of harm are actually not uncommon, and we are actually quite lucky, really lucky, because we at least know that we have been hurt and intend to protect ourselves. Some children don't even know that they have been violated and continue to be harmed without knowing it when they grow up. Some adult women don't even know what happened when they were raped, because they lack knowledge in that area. Now, based on your situation, I will give you some advice. I don't know if it will be helpful or not, because what happened to me when I was a child was never resolved, because it is not realistic to find out who did it. 1. Find out why your brother did this. I think it's likely because of a lack of understanding about sex. Chinese society is still very conservative, and people generally become uncomfortable when talking about sex. Parents' sex education for children is lacking. Most children release their desires through masturbation, watching porn, and reading erotic stories online. Some may even try experimenting with others, such as your brother trying to see what it feels like to have sexual relations with someone else, thereby violating you. 2. Pay attention to self-protection. Be cautious around your brother. Because you can't be sure if he has had sexual relations with others outside, or if he may transmit some diseases to you. So keep your distance from him until it is resolved. 3. You should still tell your parents the truth. Because you are just worried that they won't believe you, but that's not necessarily true. Maybe your parents know about some of your brother's characteristics but haven't told you. And you are also their child. If they don't believe you, you can question them: why do they believe him and not me? 4. I suggest seeing a professional psychologist. Because my knowledge is limited, professional psychologists are more reliable. Rest assured, the content of psychological counseling is confidential. 5. Maybe it can be consulted with a lawyer. 6. You need evidence. For example, using a voice recorder, a small camera, etc., you need evidence to protect yourself. 7. Don't commit suicide!!! Don't commit suicide!!! People who commit suicide are the weakest. If you can't even protect your own life, how can you protect anyone else? Don't lose hope! There are always more solutions than difficulties!

question: Actually, I didn't catch a cold from being exposed to cold air. I just tend to get colds and coughs easily, which attracts attention.
description: The body tends to catch cold and cough easily, but the emotions are relatively stable, and there have been no significant events. I also exercise regularly. It may be related to my family's neglect of me. In my subconscious, I use getting sick to attract their attention. How can I break free from this vicious cycle?

answers.answer_text: Since you, the poster, have realized that it's due to your family's neglect that you feel this way, I suggest some difficult suggestions. Adjust them as you see fit. ① Don't be ashamed to speak up. Communicate honestly (within the family). Overcome shame. Be a little spoiled, show vulnerability, and remember that the squeaky wheel gets the grease. Should family only care about you when you're sick? Will they stay by your side when you need them? Is the attention you receive when you're ill enough to fulfill your needs? (Compared to a child who will keep nagging an indifferent parent until they finally look and say something.) ② Love yourself. (Most effective) This is something that all those lacking love and self-love need to learn. Shift your focus onto yourself and treat yourself better because you lack love. Make yourself a better person (？→_→). ③ Seek love and friendships outside, derive it from there. This is a simpler suggestion, but the results are uncertain. Small mistakes can lead to severe consequences. I recommend following the sequence ②①③.

question: I feel like I understand a lot of principles, but how can I move from knowing to actually doing?
description: I feel like I understand a lot of principles, but there are many things I can't do. How can I go from knowing to doing?

answers.answer_text: Many times, we read a lot of books, learn a lot of principles, and when we see those principles, we can't help but think, "Wow, that's really good, I must do it this way." But many times, those principles are returned to the authors the moment we put down our phones and books. Why is that? Because what you understand is what others have summarized, the principles derived from practice, not something you have realized on your own. Of course, it doesn't mean that other people's principles are useless to you. So how can you apply these "wow, that's great" principles to your life? Very simple, change your cognition, re-digest those principles, and turn them into your own understanding. You will find that there are some principles you agree with, but there are others that you cannot really agree with. And to achieve cognitive upgrading, well, it's not easy. I suggest reading more social science books, such as philosophy, sociology, psychology, economics, management, etc. Philosophy and psychology are the top recommendations, followed by sociology. Occasionally, consult with proactive psychologists, the world loves you and me.

question: Emotions are easily agitated, sometimes even having suicidal thoughts, and unable to sleep at night.
description: My ex-boyfriend came to find me and touched me, but he cannot provide me with legal status. My parents have always known how to scold and beat me since I was young. Whether I did something wrong or not, they would blame me. I feel very wronged.
keywords: Emotions, depressed feelings, anxious feelings, panic helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the description mentioned two aspects of your problems: emotional and family. Are these the main issues currently bothering you? We can discuss them separately. Let's start by talking about the family issue. I understand how you feel. It's frustrating when parents only resort to scolding and don't understand your feelings. Parents have their limitations too. They also come from a background of upbringing, where they may not have received proper care or education. They might have even grown up in an environment of physical punishment. If they haven't reflected and grown as adults, they are likely to adopt the same harsh disciplinary methods. We cannot choose our parents, and complaining about their parenting style won't help. We can try to look at these issues from a deeper perspective, understanding their limitations, and strive to grow and become different from them within our limited conditions. The fact that you're aware of these issues and seeking help here is a good start. Growth takes time and effort, so keep working on it! Now, let's move on to the relationship issue. Since your ex-boyfriend couldn't provide you with legal status, why didn't you reject him? Do you also subject yourself to such mistreatment in other interpersonal relationships? If so, it's easy to accumulate a lot of grievances and feel emotionally repressed. The emotional outbursts you mentioned, even the thoughts of suicide, might be related to this repression. I think in interpersonal relationships, we need to have our own principles and boundaries. We don't need to sacrifice ourselves or compromise just to please others. We can refuse unreasonable demands and respect our own feelings. Interpersonal relationships don't need to be complicated or excessive. Unhealthy relationships can drain our energy and make us feel uncomfortable and miserable. If you're unable to regulate your current psychological state on your own, I suggest seeking help from a psychologist or counselor. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Hello, OP: It sounds like you are experiencing significant mood swings and easily provoked, with thoughts of self-harm, is that correct? May I ask how old you are? How long has this condition been going on? What triggered your anxiety? It is understandable that your ex-boyfriend cannot provide you with a future, and it seems that your parents do not offer much recognition or acceptance, which has made you feel frustrated and aggrieved. It is remarkable that you have sought help on this platform, which demonstrates your courage and wisdom. However, counseling requires more information, possibly even a process. Keep going, and know that I will always love you!

question: 19-year-old female, parents argue, feeling depressed and uncomfortable for no reason at night, don't know why?
description: Now is during the National Day holiday, so let me first wish all the teachers a happy holiday (although it's a bit late). I am a sophomore student. Originally, I was very attached to home, so I chose to go back home for the holiday. But after returning home, I realized it was a wrong decision. All day today, my dad was like a ticking time bomb, venting his anger on everyone and constantly criticizing my mom. It made me feel really depressed all day. Although my dad is 47 years old, his emotional age is like that of a spoiled child. He always thinks he's the boss and that everyone should cater to him. He lectures my mom every now and then, and I can tell my mom feels really frustrated. I had some depressive feelings before, but they improved quite a bit after the start of the new semester. However, seeing my dad scold my mom all day after coming back home, especially when they were wallpapering the walls together in the evening and he kept picking fights, I feel so uncomfortable and depressed. I even wonder if all family atmospheres are like this. From the bottom of my heart, I can say that my dad doesn't have a traditional mindset of favoring sons over daughters. He treats me and my younger sister very well. However, I can't find the words to describe his attitude towards my mom. I'm afraid that my future family environment will be like this too. Tonight, I feel especially depressed and want to cry, but I don't know why.
keywords: Emotions, depressive feelings, healing methods, anxious emotions.

answers.answer_text: Title owner, hello. I have listened to your question. I can sense the anxiety and pain you are experiencing due to your current family situation. You mentioned that your father constantly blames your mother, creating a hostile atmosphere filled with verbal attacks in your family. This can be seen as a stressor for you, triggering your depressive and anxious feelings. It is normal to have such negative emotions when faced with such a family environment that causes distress and discomfort. The fact that you are willing to seek help and ask questions on this platform shows that you are strong and great because you are seeking to find solutions instead of being consumed by your emotions. You are doing well in this regard. Firstly, you asked if all families are like this. The truth is, not all families are like that. Although it is saddening, the most important thing is that when we become aware of problems within our family, we should find ways to solve them instead of staying in that situation. In your description, you mentioned that your father is an immature character who acts like a child. Does your mother primarily take on the responsibility of taking care of all of you in your daily lives? You mentioned that your father treats you and your sister well, but seems to constantly blame your mother. I am curious, does he behave this way towards everyone or only towards your mother? I have a suggestion: perhaps you can find some time to communicate alone with your father and express your feelings to him. For example, you can tell him that you don't like it when he blames your mother. You can also ask him why he constantly blames her. Maybe he has certain emotions towards your mother and uses blame and criticism as a way to express them. I think you can observe more and ask your father about it. Maybe you can discover answers that you haven't thought about before. If face-to-face communication is challenging, you can also try writing a letter or chatting through text. As for your current depressive feelings, you can try shifting your focus and handling this issue when your emotions are more stable. You can also try activities such as meditation, journaling, running, drawing, or any other activity that helps divert your attention or provides a healthy way of expressing your emotions.

Hello, I see that you are feeling down, and returning home to find warmth and comfort from your family but instead experiencing a cold and distant atmosphere has created deep sadness. I want to give you a hug and sincerely tell you that in my surroundings, including my own family and my native family, most couples have the same way of interacting as your parents. It is lucky for children to have a harmonious relationship between their parents. The traumas and pain from our native families are generational, with anxious mothers, irritable fathers, absent fathers, and hardworking, nagging mothers. We unconsciously replicate the patterns of interaction from the previous generation. Although we despise and abhor our parents' behavior, their influence is deeply ingrained in our bones, infiltrating our subconsciousness. Does it mean that we can only passively succumb to the states of powerlessness, fear, sadness, and depression? No, there are self-protective and coping strategies. As children, our mental maturity and fears overwhelm us. We learn psychology for self-healing, seek guidance from external methods, and search within ourselves for awareness, change, growth, and empowerment. 1. Differentiate ourselves from our parents. Our parents' relationship is their own, which has nothing to do with us. Although many of our interpersonal relationships reflect the patterns of interaction in our native families, we need to downplay our connection with our parents, isolate ourselves from it, and understand that their fights and conflicts are not our fault. We should not take responsibility for their mistakes, nor accept the burden of heavy negative emotions, such as fear, guilt, sadness, entanglement, or anxiety. Instead, we should accept these emotional experiences, forgive our parents, and understand them. 2. Soothe our inner child. When we are controlled by this gloom, there are two versions of ourselves in our hearts: the independent, strong, and grown-up version of ourselves and the weak, insecure one. We should let the mature version embrace the vulnerable one and tell ourselves not to be afraid because I am here now and I am capable of soothing and protecting you. 3. Find support and resources. Share your feelings with grandparents, in-laws, or other relatives, or write them down as a form of soothing and expression. This pain itself brings growth, not just negative impacts. It allows us to communicate, argue, and obtain equal rights instead of suppressing and enduring things like our mothers. 4. Shift our focus. Find our own hobbies, read, exercise, take action, do housework, or take on part-time jobs. Write something online or live stream to alleviate our sadness and not give ourselves too much time to sink into it. 5. Give ourselves extra credit. Acknowledge the positives: both parents prioritize education, both parents are healthy, and siblings are beautiful, among other achievements. Seeking help from a professional counselor is also an option. I wish you well.

Hello, the topic creator, a mental health counselor. In your description, I only see the behavioral manifestations. To further investigate, I need more clues. My understanding is as follows, please confirm if it's correct: (1) Your parents are caring and good to you and your sister. (2) You are a child who loves home. (3) You feel depressed and think your father's attitude and behavior towards your mother make you feel that he is childish and needs others to accommodate him. (4) You worry that your future family will be the same. (5) From the comments, it seems that you are a child who likes to read novels. Based on the above, I think you have a high psychological sensitivity and tend to view things with a more authoritative perspective. Do your parents love each other? Has your father always treated your mother this way, or is this recent? How does your mother treat your father? Perhaps there are many things you haven't fully understood and you are looking at behaviors with subjective thoughts, which are always biased. It may be that your father has recently encountered difficulties in his life or work, or perhaps this is the way your parents interact but they love each other. Maybe just as you said, he doesn't treat your mother well, or even doesn't love her, but he has not engaged in extreme behaviors (such as hitting or other harmful actions). It could just be a character flaw of your father's, because does one's character flaw necessarily mean they are unkind to others? It's not necessarily the case. Also, your worry about future marriage shows that you are already thinking about your future life and even dating. Let me assure you, unless for artistic creation, don't easily imagine others' suffering. Perhaps it's much better than you imagine. (3) Feeling depressed is a normal thing. The key is to understand it and determine whether it is real or just fantasy. Above all, I wish you a joyful mood. People with strong subjective consciousness are suitable for artistic creation and innovation. Keep it up!

Hello, first of all, I understand your feelings of helplessness and anger towards your parents' relationship status. However, there is little you can do about it, and I think this may be causing you to feel depressed and down. Let's talk about how to overcome these depressive feelings. Our relationship with our parents is very close, but the reality is that we cannot choose who our parents are or control the state of their relationship with each other. As we grow up, we may have the opportunity to talk to them in a lighthearted manner, such as jokingly expressing a hope for our dad to treat our mom better and show her more care, or playfully being affectionate with dad. I believe if our dad is in a positive mood, he may be able to listen to us. However, it's important not to approach him with anger and emotions because, after all, he is an elder and may not be receptive. Another point I want to make is that regardless of the state of our lives, such as whether our parents' relationship is good or bad, we need to try not to let our emotions be affected by them, otherwise, we will feel very miserable. We need to calm ourselves down and accept the current circumstances, even if they are a bit difficult. When we can accept and calm down, with fewer emotions in our hearts, the answers will become clear. We can also suggest to our parents to do things together occasionally, like going shopping or traveling on weekends, or going to the park to have fun. Changing the environment might make things better. I wish you all the best!

Hello, dear, I can feel your unhappiness from your words and understand that there is no one you can talk to about it. You have chosen to ask for help here, and I hope my words can provide some assistance. As an observer, I will analyze the situation from various aspects. I hope you can reflect on it yourself. 1. Has your father always had such a hot temper, or is it just on National Day? 2. You feel uncomfortable and don't understand your father's attitude towards your mother, but he treats you and your sister well. People tend to sympathize with the weak and feel that your mother is being bullied. It may be a habit for your father to take your mother's side automatically. Does your mother need to adjust her way of getting along with your father? 3. You are afraid and worried about your future family life. It is possible that it may continue to be like this, but it can also be happy. The term "original family" is quite popular, but everyone has a choice. You can choose to be like this or not. The decision is in your hands. There is no book that teaches us how to be good fathers, mothers, husbands or wives. We learn directly on the job, and some learn from the previous generation. However, only you know if the shoes fit. Whether it's marriage or any other relationship, it takes time to adjust and find a comfortable mode of interaction. If you feel that your mother is being bullied, has she expressed her needs? I suggest having a good conversation, expressing your inner feelings. Home is a place of warmth and love. Your father is good to you and your sister, which shows that there is love. However, if you feel uncomfortable in this environment, let your father know. Sometimes parents don't know how to express their love, and sometimes they need their children to teach them. Since there are still a few days left in the National Day holiday, why not have a family meeting and have a sincere and calm conversation, expressing your feelings and allowing love to be expressed. I wish your family harmony and happy growth.

Let's try to look at your family and the issues that arise from the perspective of an outsider. I have many questions and curiosities. I want to know why your father is picking faults and what purpose he hopes to achieve. Is this expression normal or does it only happen when you are home? In your text, you mentioned, from the bottom of your heart, your father does not have a traditional mindset of favoring sons over daughters and treats you and your sister very well, but you are unclear about how to describe his attitude towards your mother. Because we don't want to and don't want to experience this kind of situation again, we are afraid that this kind of thing will happen to us in the future. It may seem like a vicious cycle, but in reality, we can change this cognitive pattern through objective and rational analysis. You can try asking yourself how you would solve the problem if this problem really occurs in the future. Would you act like your parents do now? You will not become like your parents, because you are currently trying to avoid and evade this kind of conflict. How can you argue endlessly? What you can control is to distinguish what you can decide and what you cannot. Your parents' quarrels are their own business, and as an observer, you fundamentally cannot influence their thoughts and actions. So this matter belongs to others, and you just need to say to yourself, "This is my parents' issue, and I will do my best to do what I can, but no matter how much I do, I can accept it." Your current emotional state is up to you to decide, so you have the right and ability to break free from the current environment and restore your own state of mind. We can try using methods such as body relaxation techniques, diaphragmatic breathing, mindfulness meditation, reading books, and writing notes to record your emotions, and so on, to free yourself from the troubles of depression and other negative emotions. Finally, I hope the content and viewpoints mentioned above can help you further understand your family and your own state. I sincerely wish that you can find a suitable way to overcome your current situation for yourself and your family. Good luck.

I can understand how you feel, both your parents are people you deeply love in your heart, and you are also very attached to this family, so you choose to go home for the holidays. So when you see your mom being criticized by your dad, you feel even more upset. But this is something your parents need to deal with. If your mom is willing to endure being spoken to this way all day without resisting or finding a solution, then what can others do? Your mom is also an adult and can make different choices to make herself happier. Your dad is clearly in the wrong, unable to control his temper and always attacking your mom, but your mom hasn't chosen to leave. Either she doesn't feel bothered by what he says, or she has chosen to tolerate it. Regardless of the reason, she has chosen to stay in this marriage, and as children, we can't interfere. If you can persuade your dad not to treat your mom this way, then of course that would be great, but if you can't persuade him, then what we as children can do is actually very limited. I find that unbearable, and I believe you do too, so what do you think you would choose to do? Even if you really encounter such a situation, do you have to stay in an unhappy marriage until the end of your life? Remember that you always have the freedom to choose, so you have the ability to not perpetuate the marriage pattern of your parents.

question: How to determine if there are problems in the prospective partner's family background?
description: My blind date is from a rural area, a male. A few days ago during the Mid-Autumn Festival, he didn't plan to go home. He said it's the busy farming season at home and he didn't want to go back to help with the work because it's tiring. He also doesn't plan to report the progress of our relationship in person, saying that phone contact is enough. After he went home, he complained to me that he had to help his family with cooking, saying that he hasn't escaped from it in 30 years. He came back just one day after going home, and his older brother and sister-in-law brought him back. He described his father as having a low level of education, saying something like "When he scolds me, he's quite smooth...".
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, blind dates.

answers.answer_text: I am glad to answer your questions. Seeing your question, I think this is a question that many young people, especially those who have some understanding of psychology, consider when choosing a partner. [In fact, the majority of people have experienced trauma from their origin family.] The origin family does have a significant impact on the psychological growth and many qualities that are formed under this influence (such as sense of responsibility, ambition, and sense of security in marriage) directly affect the happiness of future marriages and families. If you haven't established a deep emotional connection yet, it is indeed possible to make judgments and identify based on this aspect, in order to make a better choice for yourself. Of course, if you already have a strong emotional foundation, it is recommended to grow together with the guidance of a psychologist, gradually improving the potential impact that the origin family may have on your future family. It is important to know that the majority of us come with some kind of trauma. For different reasons such as cultural level, cognitive ability, and social emphasis on family education, our childhoods have left us with some traumatic experiences. But these "not-so-good" experiences allow us to constantly discover and improve ourselves. In fact, life should be like this. [The relationship patterns in the origin family are a shadow of future relationship patterns.] As for how to judge through the origin family, the relationship pattern is very important. In psychology, it is said that "the relationship pattern in the origin family largely determines future relationship patterns." Therefore, you can infer your future relationship based on observing their interactions with opposite-sex members of their origin family. For example, if their mother is extremely doting and they have a strong dependence on their mother, then you will also be responsible for taking care of them in the future. Similarly, if they have a long-standing tense relationship with their father, they may not handle relationships with same-sex authority figures such as bosses well in the workplace, leading to more obstacles in their work. Of course, these relationship patterns in the origin family are just a microcosm, and if they are aware of the impact of these patterns and make efforts to modify and improve them, there will be significant differences. [The quality of parents' relationship affects their trust in marital emotions.] If they have lived in a family where parents constantly argue, have a troubled relationship, or even experience infidelity, then witnessing these marital conditions from childhood could lead to a lack of trust in marital emotions, resulting in a decreased sense of responsibility in the family and other aspects. In contrast, if they have grown up in a harmonious family where their parents have a good relationship, it will increase their sense of security in marital emotions, giving them more confidence and strength to maintain a happy family and having a stronger ambition in their work. Therefore, paying attention to the quality of their parents' relationship will help you understand their inner values ​​and attitudes towards marital emotions. [Parents' parenting styles affect their approach to future children's education.] If we have not deliberately studied or improved our knowledge of parenting, then after becoming parents, we will most likely continue to use the parenting styles of our origin family, such as the father often scolding them. In the future, they are likely to adopt a similar approach with their children, which perpetuates a repeating problem. Of course, if you can learn and improve together, it will also improve to a certain extent. In summary, when choosing a partner, it is good to consider the situation of their origin family as a reference, but it is best not to make a final decision based solely on this aspect because the influence of the origin family is not absolute. As long as you both make efforts, you can create your own happiness.

Hello, OP: It is often said that getting married means not only marrying the person but also marrying their family. This statement holds some truth in my understanding. I have noticed your question and your search for help, which undoubtedly helps you gain more perspectives on your partner's family background. Now I would like to share my observations, which might help you have a broader perspective. 

1. The relationship patterns we have with others are projections of our relationship patterns with our parents and our family of origin. To a large extent, these patterns determine our future relationship patterns. This is because we internalize the relationship patterns between our parents and our relationship patterns with our parents, thus forming our own internal relationship patterns - the relationship patterns we have with ourselves. When we interact with others, we tend to project our own relationship patterns onto our relationships with them. Therefore, to understand the patterns in your partner's family of origin, you can perhaps make inferences based on your own interactions with your partner. Of course, the accuracy of this inference depends on the extent to which your partner has reconciled with their family of origin. There is no perfect family of origin, but we can strive to be better individuals. If your partner is aware of the influence of their family of origin and has learned to reconcile with them, their internal relationship patterns may be adjusted. However, our relationship patterns often bear the mark of our family of origin. That is why you can observe more about the patterns in your own interactions with your partner and compare them with the information you have about your partner's family of origin. For example, if your partner describes certain traits of their father, you can see if they exhibit any similar traits in your interactions. Pay attention to their relationship with their mother, as this is likely to be the pattern you will encounter in the future.

2. Have a conversation with your prospective partner. During the process of getting to know each other, you can look for opportunities to have frank discussions about your own views on your family of origin, some interesting stories or memorable events that happened in your families, and even discuss your impressions of each other's parents. These conversations provide information on potential issues in their family of origin. The stability of the relationship between parents directly influences a person's attitude towards relationships. The emotional stability of parents affects the atmosphere of a household. Furthermore, if your partner tends to complain, you can also assess whether it is a common trait among their family members, and so on.

3. Family of origin is just a reference. The most important thing in a relationship is the relationship between you and your partner. Knowing what you want will help you determine whether they are suitable for you. No one is perfect. The essence of love is the integration of imperfections. Therefore, the family of origin is just a reference. There may be traumas from the family of origin, but it should not hinder the possibility of your growth together.

While the family of origin is undoubtedly important, ultimately it depends on the person you are with. After all, it is you and your prospective partner who will spend the rest of your lives together, not his family. Even if someone is born into a flawed family, if they are aware of the issue and actively work on improving themselves, then their family of origin shouldn't be a major concern. The individual's subjective willpower is still crucial. From the description provided by the original poster, it seems that the partner's parents have a strong need for control, as evidenced by the fact that the man claims to have never escaped certain responsibilities at home for 30 years, and his father scolds him. However, more detailed descriptions are necessary to understand the situation fully. The partner's parents may have a low level of cultural education, as many people from this era haven't received proper education due to the circumstances of the time. Instead of focusing on the partner's family of origin, it is better to carefully evaluate the individual themselves: how they interact with others, how they treat you, whether they can control their emotions, and whether they are responsible and considerate. Can they respect you and consider your feelings rather than imposing their own will on you and attempting to control you? Many problems in family of origin often arise from a lack of education and outdated thinking. For example, some people don't know how to foster independence and autonomy in their children and instead indulge them excessively. Others have no idea about emotional regulation techniques and allow their emotions to run wild. These issues can be improved through education and training, which is our generation's advantage. Compared to our parents' generation, we have more knowledge, are more open to new ideas, and are aware of the limitations of our parents' generation. Therefore, we can choose not to repeat their mistakes. So, just because his father scolds others doesn't mean he will do the same. Observing the person through daily interactions is a good method. You can also ask their opinion on certain matters to gauge their values. For example, do they believe in traditional gender roles where the man is the provider and the woman takes care of the home? Is it acceptable for a woman to have a career? If circumstances prevent me from having children, would you still be with me? Listen to how they respond and if it aligns with your desires. Similarly, even if someone's family of origin is perfect, it doesn't necessarily mean they are the right person for you. They will still have their own thoughts and values. The key is whether you get along and if your values align. If the original poster still has doubts, observe the situation more, spend more time with the partner. If the partner is already a responsible, independent adult who has the right to make decisions about their own life, then there's no need to focus too much on their family of origin. After all, who hasn't experienced childhood pain?

question: How should the expenses in a romantic relationship be calculated?
description: I am a female and have always had a question. Should we split the expenses equally with men in a romantic relationship, or is it better to have clear boundaries in this way? If the man spends more money than us, would it be a problem? How should we handle the issue of expenses between couples?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! This applies to the issue of consumption as well. You can gradually develop comfortable spending habits in your relationship with your boyfriend. As for the question of who pays more and who pays less, it doesn't need to be divided too clearly, but it also shouldn't be completely ignored. For example, you can pay for a meal this time, and your boyfriend can pay for the next meal. Alternatively, you can split the bill equally, but be more casual when it comes to gifting each other. The most important thing is to find a state where both of you feel comfortable. These are just my suggestions, and I hope they can help you. Best wishes!

question: 25-year-old, after breaking up with a 4-year relationship, found that there are no friends around? What should I do?

question: Why is the psychological construction always completely collapsing to the point of nothingness in the public examination interview?
description: In the past two years, I have participated in public service examinations and made it to the second and first place in the written tests. However, I failed miserably in the interviews. On one hand, it may be due to a lack of knowledge in interview techniques. On the other hand, my overall mental state was not good. Perhaps it has something to do with my family background. I grew up with few elders around, my grandfather and father are both only children. Moreover, my father used to work in the transportation industry and most of my friends have a rough demeanor. I rarely interacted with older relatives in politics. At home, my father and uncle have a very casual attitude, saying whatever they want without much restraint, and occasional clashes are tolerated. I don't have that traditional sense of politeness. Each industry has its own unique atmosphere, so when facing seven or eight older examiners in the examination room, I feel confused and lost. Even if I am well-prepared before the exam, my thoughts become scattered and I can't stick to the questions, leading to disorganized answers. I wonder if this factor affects my psychology and performance. Can you help me analyze the problem? How can I change in order to improve my performance in exams? By the way, I don't get stage fright and perform normally in one-on-one interviews in the private sector, but when there are multiple examiners in public service examinations, I become flustered. What can I do for effective mental development?

answers.answer_text: Your performance in the written test, obtaining first or second place, shows that your knowledge is solid and you have a strong foundation and ability. The mistakes in the interview mainly stem from the use of interview skills and the influence of your mental state in the moment. Public examination interviews are conducted with multiple examiners and the atmosphere on-site can be more serious, which is very different from social interviews and the family environment you have been accustomed to. Therefore, you are facing the pressure of an environmental change, and it is normal to feel nervous, anxious, or even confused when you are unable to adapt to the situation in a timely manner. The written test has been successful, making the interview even more important as it determines whether you can pass. Therefore, you place great importance on the interview, feeling tense and under a lot of pressure, becoming overly concerned and anxious about the outcome. In this state, you will pay more attention to your own performance and the examiner's reaction, and unconsciously amplify them. You may also engage in speculation about the examiner's intentions. Your thinking is inundated with external information and negativity, which can affect your ability to think clearly and contribute to confusion. The way you interact with your father and others at home is equal and relaxed, and their authoritative image is relatively weak for you. In contrast, examiners have a strong authoritative image. It is normal for people to feel nervous in the presence of authority, so your reaction is natural. The change in environmental atmosphere, excessive anxiety about the interview result, and nervousness about authority all contribute to your confused state and underperformance on-site. Therefore, it is recommended that you make the following improvements: first, learn some interview skills, grasp key points in the interview process, and enhance your confidence so that you can better handle challenges from the examiner. Then, adjust your mindset, including: ①Do not obsess over the interview result and prepare yourself mentally to accept any outcome. Do not excessively focus on the examiner's reaction and negativities. As long as you have done your best, regardless of the result, you will have no regrets. Even if this interview doesn't go well, it does not mean you lack ability, as the written test has already proven your capabilities. ②Correct your attitude towards authority. Neither underestimate nor excessively fear it. Understand that the seriousness of the examiner and the interview atmosphere are normal aspects of an examination setting, indicating that the exam is conducted in a formal, fair, and strict manner that all candidates must go through, not just you. ③Understand and adapt to the characteristics of different social situations, timely change your role, and adjust your mindset and behavior. At home, you are a son and a junior, and the older generation treats you kindly and takes care of you in many ways. However, in society, whether it's in an exam room or various work situations, you are a candidate or a social worker, and others are your superiors, colleagues, or assessors. You need to approach them with this role, communicate and interact with them. During such times, it is necessary to have an appropriate level of nervousness and a serious and earnest attitude. The most crucial thing is to understand the characteristics of different social situations and roles, to recognize and accept them, and to promptly adapt yourself. This process will inevitably create some pressure and discomfort, but it is a part of personal growth. Wishing you the ability to quickly adapt to new social roles and better accept new challenges.

Hello, I hope the following answer can help you: First, let's summarize the situation you described: ▲ You ranked first or second in the written exams of two public examinations, but didn't succeed ▲ You feel that your state of mind is not good and that you haven't been disciplined enough by your elders since childhood ▲ When facing older examiners, your thoughts become chaotic and scattered. The civil service exam itself is indeed challenging, involving comprehensive knowledge, aptitude tests, psychology, interviews, etc. It represents the selection of talents at the national level, so it is not that simple. However, from your performance in the written exams, you are obviously very good at exams, ranking in the top two, and can even be described as a top student. It shows that you have made a diligent preparation. Diligent preparation has proven effective for the written exams. However, the interview is different. The interview questions are unknown, testing your ability to perform on the spot and adaptability. This brings up another issue, which is your relationship with the examiner. From a psychological perspective, it is obvious that when facing examiners, you are projecting your relationship with your grandfather and father. Your father has a strong personality, and you and your elders may have some boundary issues, not giving you a proper psychological boundary. So when facing authority, you don't know how to maintain the right mindset; on the other hand, you feel lost when facing authority. Have your elders also given you inappropriate feelings of authority, causing you to have some fear since childhood? In fact, the number of examiners doesn't matter. The main problem is that when facing them, your mind is unsettled, leading to panic, and nervousness can lead to mistakes. This needs to be strengthened in the future. Blessings to you, and I recommend seeking specialized counseling for personal growth. I am here, the world loves you.

First of all, what makes you attach such importance to the civil service examination? Sometimes having a clear goal can contribute to your success. Is it the pressure from your family or your own motivation? This is crucial. You failed in the interviews during the two-year preparation, which may have had an impact on you. Are you still planning to take the civil service exam for the third time? It seems that you feel immense pressure in a one-on-many situation, and you become flustered under pressure. If you have a clear idea in your mind but fail to express it due to nervousness, it is possible to achieve a change through adjustment.

question: Want to lose weight but can't control snacking?
description: As mentioned, every time I make up my mind to lose weight, I just can't help but want to eat as soon as I sit down.
keywords: Behavior, binge eating and restrictive eating

answers.answer_text: Hello there, have you ever sat down and not felt the urge to eat like you did before? What were you thinking at that time? Or were you distracted by other things? You can try to repeat those thoughts or do activities that help shift your attention. Have you ever found yourself in a situation where the more you tried to control your thoughts, the more out of control they became? The more you try to control, the more anxious you become, and your ability to manage becomes worse. Maybe you can try to let go of control. Treat weight loss as something natural, rather than something that requires strict control. Sometimes, letting go of control is true control. These are just some suggestions I have, hope they can help you. Take care!

question: Always stuck in a cycle, why is growing up so difficult?
description: Originally, I was looking for this job to experience personal spiritual growth and to recognize the patterns that always trap me. It wasn't about making money. However, faced with the daily trivialities, contradictions, and entanglements, I couldn't help but fall back into that predetermined mud... How can I see myself in all of this?

answers.answer_text: Hello, in your post, I can see that your original intention is very good, and I would even say that your level of consciousness and awareness is higher than many people, including myself. "At that time, I was looking for this job to experience personal spiritual growth, not to make money." However, after truly immersing myself in the work, I found that "faced with the daily trivialities, contradictions, and entanglements, I couldn't help but fall into that predetermined quagmire again...". I feel somewhat helpless and want to withdraw, to observe myself as an outsider, but I find it impossible. One positive point is that you still hold your original intention, it's just that you feel somewhat powerless. You have also noticed the issue of "seeing the pattern of being trapped in circles", even to the point of compulsive repetition. To solve this, I have two methods: since compulsive repetition is the result of negative emotions accumulated in the subconscious mind commanding our actions, preventing us from behaving according to our subjective and rational consciousness, we must first address our emotional problems and nurture our inner child. Ask yourself how you feel, how to heal those feelings, and once you have healed them. The second step: I have only heard of a psychological technique called "dissociation" in a class, the healthy kind, not the kind associated with mental illness. It involves actively dissociating oneself from negative emotions, and viewing one's own experiences from a higher perspective. By placing oneself at a higher level, because the higher you stand, the further you can see, you can have a more comprehensive view of the problem. By dissociating oneself, you can view things from the perspective of an observer, which is more objective, comprehensive, and long-term. Here, I can see that you have a strong desire to break through the limitations of your thinking. If you can break through the limitations of your thinking, you will live a better life and have a different experience. Maintaining open-mindedness and independent thinking. Open-mindedness refers to the ability to let go of judgments at any time and always maintain curiosity and openness to a diverse world, as well as constantly updating and expanding one's experiences. Maintain a flexible mindset. When the energy of psychological activities is not limited to logical intelligence alone, but can freely experience all emotions and attitudes, a person will not be bound by immature psychological defense mechanisms and can become open and growth-oriented. With this kind of growth, independent thinking becomes possible, so one can not only logically understand and accept the experiences that life provides, but also synthesize and apply them in new social environments and perceptual processes through spontaneity and creativity.

The flowers on the strawberry vines on the grass in the forest have withered. The days are gradually getting longer and the nights shorter. The little mole in the house is feeling itchy feet and feels like going outside to move around. For a mole, the destination is always unpredictable. You may not believe it, but once our little mole actually made its way from the underground passage to the city of Chernivtsi and appeared in the town square. At first, the little mole could only see the sky through the gaps between the chairs. This town square is not something you can easily have all to yourself. Is a place like this worth having all to myself? I should go. The little mole is a wanderer. It hides in its own hole. Sometimes it feels like it owns the whole world, but sometimes the little mole has nothing at all. It climbs around in its castle every day, not knowing what the world above looks like. It really wants people to know that it is happy but also lonely... "People are spinning, but not in place. If you can see this, it means lacking strength. Go find strength."

question: When having different opinions from others and being troubled by their words, how should one maintain a friendship?
description: Finally, I found someone in my new workplace whom I can talk to. I told her that I don't hand-wash clothes for my husband, and he said that my mother-in-law does it for me. After I said that, she immediately replied, "Well, you can say that my mother also hand-washes for me." I have been feeling conflicted about this. I never thought that I needed to argue back when my husband said this. I think he just wants me to take care of him like his mother does. But this person's words make it seem like my husband is bullying me, and now I feel like I need to argue with him. I can't accept it. I care a lot about my husband, and I always feel like this person is implying that he is not good. But at the same time, I feel like it doesn't really matter. I feel so guilty. I shouldn't have discussed my husband with her. Now everything is ruined. I don't know how to be friends anymore. It's so upsetting when I talk to others about something that I care about, and we have different opinions. I don't know whose side I should take. But I really want to stand up for myself. Plus, I'm afraid of getting caught up in personal relationships. It's difficult to find someone I can talk to, and now I'm being influenced again. I'm always thinking about this matter.

answers.answer_text: Dear question asker, I seem to have understood why you say it's so difficult to find someone to talk to. Do you feel burdened when someone presents a different opinion from yours during a conversation? From your conversation with your colleague, she perceived that you wanted to argue back because you think your husband is not good, so she offered her own solution. However, your thoughts are completely different from hers. You can choose to kindly explain your thoughts to her, so she can understand what kind of person you are. Everyone has their own way of thinking, and everyone is different. Even the best relationships can have differences. Express yourself, and she can express herself too. After mutual expression, this matter will be resolved. If you are considering becoming friends, be cautious. If it's just a good coworker relationship, there's no need to overly worry. You and your colleague have just met and aren't at the stage of becoming friends yet. If you have to consider whether to talk about a certain topic, how to talk about it, and whether the two of you will have different opinions, whether she's interfering with me, or if I'm hurting her, then it will naturally be exhausting. Relax and express yourself naturally, and allow others to be different from you. You will gain many good interpersonal relationships.

First of all, I have also encountered such problems before. I am a very sensitive person, and every word that others say makes me think too much. Later, I sought help from my friends, and I think I have some experience that can help you. 1. Don't take other people's words too seriously. Everyone has different thoughts. 2. You can communicate with your friend because if she considers you a friend, she will communicate with you well. Interpersonal relationships require compromise. If you want to continue being good friends with her, you can honestly tell her your thoughts. This will help her understand you better and vice versa, benefiting both of you. 3. Actually, you can try to change your way of thinking and mindset. Perhaps your friend's expression was unintentional, maybe she is just someone who speaks her mind. I remember when I was chatting with a close high school classmate, he unintentionally said something that touched my soul and hurt me, so I felt very sad. But later, I thought it over and decided to talk to him honestly because it would benefit both of us to continue being good friends. If I kept it to myself, he wouldn't know what I was thinking, which would also be a lack of respect for our relationship. After gathering up my courage and expressing my thoughts to him, I explained why I was upset. He said that he didn't actually think that way and that he was only expressing his thoughts unintentionally. He didn't mean to hurt me with that sentence, he simply wanted to share his thoughts. He also told me that he has always considered me an important person to him. So, in fact, your friend doesn't have any malicious intentions, she was just expressing her opinions unintentionally. Everyone has different perspectives, and you can communicate with her about it. In conclusion, I hope what I said can truly help you. Do better in the future and contribute to your better development. Finally, I sincerely wish you and your friend and your husband a sincere and happy relationship. So, when you encounter issues, don't feel sad. Remember, there is the "Answering Hall" community, and the world loves you.

question: 14-year-old girl, these days, I feel like I have lost a lot of memory and can't recall things?
description: I have insomnia at night and have been seeking treatment at the psychiatric department. They prescribed sleeping pills (Suerkang) for me. Last night, after taking the medication, I fell asleep. I remember that at that time my step count was 29,000, which automatically resets to zero at midnight. After taking the sleeping pills, I woke up at half past twelve today. I had set an alarm for 11 o'clock, but I didn't hear it. When I checked my phone, my step count was over 8000. I haven't touched my phone as far as I can recall, except for the alarm. The system shouldn't have any issues, as I have been using the health app for two years. No one in my family has used it either. I have no idea how I got those 8000 steps.

answers.answer_text: Do not worry or be afraid, let's analyze your situation together. You mentioned that you have insomnia at night and have visited a psychiatric department, where you were prescribed sleeping pills (Suirui Kang). Could you please share your current situation? Besides the sleeping pills, were you prescribed any other medications? Do you know what the side effects of these medications are? Last night, after taking the sleeping pills, I fell asleep. I remember at that time my number of steps was 29,000, but it automatically reset at 12 o'clock. After taking the sleeping pills, I got out of bed at 12:30 today. I set an alarm for 11 o'clock, but I did not hear it. When I looked at my phone, my step count was over 8,000. I did not touch my phone, other than when I set the alarm. The system should not have any issues, as I have been using this exercise app for 2 years. My family members did not touch it either. I do not know how the 8,000 steps came about. It is indeed strange that my phone registered over 8,000 steps while I was sleeping. I can deeply feel your fear and panic. Take a deep breath and relax. Based on your current situation, I suggest informing your family members about this situation and seeking a reevaluation at a local tertiary hospital. Inform the doctor about this situation and follow their treatment plan. The world loves you, and I wish you the best. Stay calm and keep going.

question: Vocational high school senior year, the relationship in the dormitory has always been difficult for me to imagine.
description: As a senior in vocational high school (where exams are difficult and subjects are not easy), I have long accepted the poor quality of students. However, ever since I changed dorms in my junior year, the dormitory relationships have been unimaginable for me. Some people stay up all night talking and don't wake up in the morning. Telling them off only works temporarily. As someone who is already sensitive, I cannot sleep when there is noise. When I can't take it anymore, I can only remind them. If reminders don't work, I have to argue (or scold). The relationships are definitely strained. There are also conflicts between other roommates and their friends in the dormitory. One roommate likes to brag, and the other roommate, who is also his good friend, got into an argument with him. It's normal for the two of them to not speak to each other. These few people share a common characteristic: selfishness. On weekends, because of the duty problem, there are instant noodle bags all over the floor, and no one takes care of the garbage bags. Why is my dormitory like this? Why do I feel disgusted (literally nauseous) when I see them? Nowadays, I lose hair every day in handfuls. Perhaps a small amount of words cannot explain everything, but ever since I entered this dormitory, I have been on guard against every single person.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts, roommates, classmates, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: LZ, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I understand that the OP is facing a difficult dorm roommate relationship. Regarding this, I have a few suggestions that I hope can help the OP. First, from the OP's description, it can be seen that the conflicts in the dorm are not limited to just the OP and the other roommates. There are also conflicts among the other roommates themselves. I think that such relationships not only have a negative impact on the OP but also on the other roommates. Therefore, we may try to communicate together and see if we can establish mutually agreed-upon "dorm rules," so that everyone can "benefit" from the rules. This can also increase the likelihood of everyone following the rules. On the other hand, can we try to communicate with the teacher and report the problems in the dorm? If communicating with the roommates doesn't have much effect, we can try to communicate with parents, teachers, or other responsible individuals, expressing the desire to change dorms or find alternative accommodations.

question: A 20-year-old young man is feeling distressed about making money through part-time jobs while being at home due to the pandemic.
description: Due to the pandemic, I haven't been able to attend university much this year. Many of my friends have gone out to do part-time jobs to earn money, and I have also tried applying to a few places, but none of them were suitable. It feels like after going to university, I still have to rely on my parents' allowance to support myself. I feel so anxious.
keywords: Growth, work and studies, self-acceptance, and student development.

answers.answer_text: Don't be too anxious first. You are not alone in this situation. Many college students have the same mentality.
