Due to the epidemic, it is difficult to relieve stress in a reasonable way. Coupled with the delay in starting school and worrying about an uncertain future, these feelings of concern are common. This year is not easy for everyone, whether it's studying or working, they have been greatly impacted. Most people feel pressure to make money, and the downward trend of the economy is quite apparent. For now, the best way for you is to improve yourself. Use this time to learn some skills, whether it's in the online world or in real life. You can polish your skills in various areas. If you have time, you can also engage in self-media, write something, and promote your own growth. You can try to earn some part-time income through the internet or other means, and expand your hobbies and interests. When schools resume and everyone can return to normal study life, it won't be too late to look for work at that time. Life is still long, a brief pause doesn't matter too much. Take your time to adjust your own state, and deal with it when the time comes.

Hello OP: It's better not to do a part-time job if there isn't a suitable one. Forcing yourself to do a job that you don't like or are not good at is no different from wasting time. Why not focus on studying and self-improvement first to continue enhancing your abilities. I can understand your desire for independence and not relying on your parents anymore. However, your parents have raised us for so many years, and although it has been hard for them, they don't expect much from these few years, so there's no need to feel too guilty. What's important is to seize every opportunity to learn now and in the future, have the ability to live independently and take care of your parents. I hope this gives you some enlightenment.

question: Accidentally scratched by a kitten, how to deal with anxiety caused by fear of rabies?
description: I was accidentally scratched by a kitten on the 5th of last month, just a small scratch mark. I had an adverse reaction after receiving the first vaccination. Since then, I have become extremely afraid of rabies. I looked for ways to relieve stress and it did have some effect, but I still feel very anxious. A month has passed, and the pet kitten that scratched me is still doing well; I have also been completely vaccinated against rabies; I know that it is absolutely impossible for me to have rabies. However, every time I feel a little uncomfortable, I can't help but think of rabies and become extremely anxious. I have been to the hospital several times and done various tests, and they all said I'm fine. The last time I went to the hospital, the doctor said I might have anxiety disorder. I feel slightly better during the day, but when I come home at night, my symptoms become severe. I know that I'm fine, but I still become very anxious. I can only smoke and play on my phone to distract myself, and end up playing until three or four in the morning... This situation has been going on for over a month, and I'm finding it difficult to endure... So I want to ask, what should I do in this situation?
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, feelings of anxiety, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hugs to the OP. I hope my response can give you some inspiration as we review the OP's experiences and psychological process: Event cause: Scratched by a cat Emotions: Fear, afraid of being infected with rabies Behavior: Got a rabies vaccine---caused adverse reactions---even more afraid of rabies---repeatedly sought medical treatment A "small scratch" triggered a great fear in the OP's mind and caused a series of psychological reactions and behaviors. Why does this happen? First, the OP's sense of insecurity was shattered as their previously fragile sense of safety and control collapsed. Second, the OP's coping methods are mostly behaviors that can temporarily alleviate their tension and anxiety, rather than genuinely helpful methods. These behaviors are called "safety behaviors" in psychology, which only provide temporary placebo effects, including repeatedly seeing a doctor, smoking, and playing with their phone. Reducing these "safety behaviors" can actually help the OP alleviate their anxiety disorder. Why is that? The cause of the OP's condition lies in their mind, not their body. Going to see a doctor reassured the OP, and their mind was at ease for a while, but when the placebo effect wore off, they became anxious again and sought medical help, relying on the reassurance from the previous visit. It seems a bit like an "addiction". If the OP doesn't seek medical help, their anxiety will rise to a peak, and when the energy of anxiety is exhausted, it will decrease. If possible, they can try psychological counseling, preferably with a therapist who has received training in cognitive behavioral therapy. I recommend a book called "The Path of Mindfulness – Freeing Yourself Little by Little". Best of luck to you!

Hello, OP ~ ※ OP, due to being scratched by a cat, has been left with a psychological shadow and is still afraid, even though they have already received the rabies vaccine. Whenever they feel a little uncomfortable, they associate it with rabies. This situation is caused by excessive psychological tension and anxiety. It is recommended for OP to go to the hospital or research online about scientific knowledge regarding rabies, to understand whether rabies is really as scary as they imagine. Many diseases are not as easy as imagined, and ignorance of knowledge can actually cause more panic. So don't scare yourself, take the initiative to understand it and objectively acquaint yourself with the incubation period, symptoms, and other aspects of rabies. Learn to control your thoughts. Now that you have received the rabies vaccine, from a scientific perspective, your body already has relevant antibodies and you don't need to worry too much about getting rabies. You can exercise more and engage in physical activities in daily life, and try not to be overly anxious! Best wishes!

question: If you feel like you're not being understood by others, what should you do?
description: How can I make myself feel loved? Hmm, it feels like nobody in the world understands me, only someone similar can understand me.

answers.answer_text: Hello, after carefully reading your question, although it is only a short sentence, it seems to express a lot of emotions. You long to be understood, long to be loved, and long to feel the warmth of interpersonal relationships and the temperature of the world. However, you don't know what is wrong with yourself. You don't know why you can't feel the love in this world. This makes you feel confused and annoyed. I want to bring you some inspiration from the following perspectives, hoping to help you. [Living in your own world - longing for others to love you according to your own wishes] Do you know what kind of love you want to feel in your heart? For some people, perhaps just a greeting, a cookie, or a cup of warm water will make them feel warm for a long time, and they will be deeply moved. It can be seen that what is truly lacking is not love, but our way of looking at the world. If you always want others to love you in your own way, for example, they should comfort you when you need it the most and accompany you all the time, this demand is demanding. For others, it is difficult to do because they find it hard to know when you need care the most or when you need consistent care. This mindset is actually living in your own world, where you can only see "me" and not "you". Therefore, everything in this world is based on the will of "me". Any action that does not fulfill the desires of "me" cannot be called love. Therefore, living in your own world rejects the love of this world. [Unspoken expression - I thought the other person knew what I wanted] Another way to not feel love is to let the other person "guess, guess, guess". This is an interesting mode of communication and is common among girls. Some girls have this logic: "If you really love me, then you should know what I want." "If I tell you what I want, what do you need to do?" They seem to believe that someone who loves them should be able to read their minds, and that being loved is synonymous with being completely understood. This inefficient cognitive mode has led to problems in many intimate relationships. Similar ways of thinking include: "If you are really my friend, and we are so similar, you should understand me? You should know what I want, right?" In fact, fundamentally speaking, these ways of thinking are also manifestations of living in one's own world and psychological immaturity. Of course, from the perspective of interpersonal communication, this type of dialogue can be effectively changed. Speak out your needs and let the other person know your current inner state. This is the effective and truthful way of communication. When you learn to express sincerely, you will find that everyone can understand you. They may not understand everything about you, but they will understand a part of you, which is the real way to seek love. I hope the above reply will inspire you.

Hello, OP. The description of "how to make oneself feel loved, feeling like no one in the world understands me" sounds very lonely and heart-wrenching! I wonder if you also feel this way? "Only people who are the same can understand me." So, OP, what kind of person are you? What experiences do you have? Or what kind of personality do you have? Do you have different ways of thinking or behaving? Or are there other reasons? Of course, if there are people with similar backgrounds or situations, it may be easier for them to empathize with you. From your description, it is clear that you long for love and understanding. So what is love and understanding? In psychology, there is a saying, "To see is to love. Love is deep understanding and acceptance." "To see" means to see your emotions and feelings, and to discover the inner needs hidden behind these emotions. In daily life, however, communication between people tends to focus only on the surface level. For example, we are more accustomed to discussing matters at hand, simple evaluations of right and wrong, and easily overlook the emotions and needs in our hearts. Therefore, effective communication methods suggest not just communicating on the surface level, but rather starting from each other's feelings to achieve good communication results. Therefore, the occurrence of love and understanding is, first and foremost, the ability to understand your feelings and emotions and to judge your true inner needs based on them. Conversely, when you feel that you are not understood by others, you can try to learn to express your feelings and emotions, bravely expressing your needs, rather than waiting for others to understand you. When you do this, you will realize that understanding yourself is actually very difficult. Perhaps in this situation, you cannot even grasp your own emotions and feelings, making it even more difficult to see your true inner needs. Thus, it becomes even more challenging for others to understand you. Regarding how to recognize your own feelings and emotions, how to express them, and your needs, I recommend a useful and interesting psychology book called "Nonviolent Communication." I believe it will be of great help to both your self-understanding and helping others understand you.

Hello there! After reading your question, even though it was just a short two lines, I could see a person who is full of hope. Despite feeling lonely and desolate at the moment, he never gives up hope and continues to search persistently for his own sanctuary of the soul in this world, a place where he can warm himself up whenever he needs it. Actually, I want to say that each and every one of us is an independent and very special existence in this world, in this vast universe. Each person has a different appearance, personality, and preferences. There are no two identical people in this world, not even among twins. You said that only someone like you can understand you, but the truth is that this someone like you might not even exist in this world. If there are no identical people in this world, does that mean nobody understands us? Of course not! When we hide ourselves in a corner, it is difficult for others to see us. Only by bravely stepping out of that dark corner and into the sunlight can others see us and we can see ourselves too. One day, when you are able to open yourself up, more people will see and understand you. How do we treat others, and how do we treat ourselves? When we position ourselves as receivers, the love we desire may become someone else's charity, but only when we position ourselves as equals, the love we desire becomes mutual. Therefore, we must learn to love others by first learning to love ourselves. Some say that love is the most precious thing in this world, yet others say that love is the easiest thing to obtain in this world. That's because the prerequisite for love is giving. By giving love, we can receive love. It's just like sowing seeds. In spring, we plant the seeds of love and diligently water and fertilize them. When autumn comes, we can harvest the fruits of love. Whether it's being loved by others or loving others, loving oneself is necessary in order to love the world. Wishing you all the best, the world and I love you~

Hello! Can only people who have had similar experiences understand you? Understanding a person is indeed difficult, but people who have had similar experiences can feel deeply connected and have a closer psychological distance. It's like having empathy for each other, accepting and recognizing each other psychologically, even if they don't say anything, you feel that they understand you. Because of shared experiences, before having a conversation, there is a psychological mindset of "I am right and you are also right." Therefore, you feel that the other person understands you. Similarly, thinking that others don't understand you is also a psychological mindset of "I am right and you are wrong" before the conversation. For example, not understanding the darkness of the night during the day, you are not me, how can you understand my feelings, etc. The distant psychological distance between both parties is caused by this. So how can you feel loved and understood? First of all, believe that you deserve to be loved, and then you can experience others' love for you. The same thing can be perceived differently by different people. For example, parents picking up and dropping off their children to school, some children think that their parents' actions are a manifestation of love for them; some children think that their parents are monitoring them. Why is there such a difference? In psychology, there is a term called "projection," which means that your views on things and objects are projections of your inner self. It means that if you have love in your heart, when you see your parents' actions, you will think that they love you. If you don't have love in your heart, then you will think that your parents' actions are not out of love for you, but only to control you and restrict your freedom, and so on. Therefore, our hearts must be filled with love in order to experience others' love for us. Expressions of love can take various forms, some direct and some indirect. Direct expressions are visible and easy to accept. However, indirect expressions, which may manifest as behaviors that we cannot fully accept, such as harsh criticism, require us to look beyond the surface and recognize that at the core, it is still because of love for the other person. Secondly, we need to learn to love ourselves, to understand ourselves. Someone who loves themselves should learn to take care of themselves, strive to enrich themselves. It is only when you have your own halo that you can attract others' goodwill towards you. Someone who loves themselves also needs to understand themselves. Why am I like this? There are reasons for everything, so accept yourself, forgive yourself, be kinder to yourself, and accept your imperfections. Then strive to become better. I hope this can help you. Good luck!

Hello: If you feel that you are not understood by others, you should consider who is not understanding you. For example, is it everyone or just a few individuals? Among these individuals, what kind of people are they and why don't they understand you? Did you do or say something that caused them to misunderstand you or are they bullying you? Different situations may have different reasons for not being understood. Analyze the problem: 1. How can you feel loved? Well, if you feel like no one in the world understands you, only people who are similar to you can understand you (in general, the reason why you can't feel love is due to emotional isolation. Because your information is limited, I cannot speculate too much. I hope the following analysis can help you a little bit. Emotional isolation means blocking the valves of all emotions, which means nothing can come in from outside and nothing can go out from inside, so you cannot feel the sincerity and flow of emotions. Of course, the biggest advantage is that you won't get hurt. It is a form of self-defense. If you feel like no one in the world understands you, in fact, this is usually understood with anger. I believe that there are people who do not understand others, but I think that there are people who have understood you before, maybe you haven't noticed, or maybe you feel that their understanding is not enough. Yes, people who have been in similar situations will inexplicably sympathize with each other, they will inexplicably connect with each other, that kind of understanding without words, that kind of understanding with just a look is something that others cannot immediately understand. But people who are similar also have disadvantages, such as not being able to see things from a new perspective or being stuck on a certain train of thought together, right? So, we still need fresh ideas, different perspectives to understand things, maybe your understanding will also change gradually? In psychology, we have a therapy called Rational Emotive Therapy. It mainly talks about how if a person has an irrational belief, it will lead to negative emotions, and then bring about negative behaviors. If you have the chance, we can discuss it together. Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you can get out of your predicament soon! If you have any confusion, you can send me a private message!

The various emotions in the world are interconnected but they each have their own uniqueness. You might think you understand, but the other person may feel like you don't. Such scenes are all too common. Even the dearest lovers can misunderstand each other at times. That's why we write all kinds of books, sing different songs, and publish various poetry magazines to express ourselves, or we may seek the company of a few good friends to unwind.

question: 22-year-old male, has partial gynophobia, what should be done?
description: I despise girls who only consider their own feelings and casually vent their emotions on others. They completely disregard other people's feelings when they speak or act. I just want to stay far away from girls like that; being around them genuinely makes me feel physically uncomfortable, even to the point of wanting to vomit. It has become a conditioned reflex, as I find girls who look disdainful repulsive. Or maybe it's just because I simply dislike this girl, thinking that she may have been spoiled as a child. Of course, I also have types of girls that I really like: independent, intellectually mature, gentle, kind-hearted, considerate, and attentive to others' feelings. I have no ill intentions towards such girls; I have a good impression of them.

answers.answer_text: Hello, for people who only consider their own feelings and casually vent their emotions without considering others, it can be very uncomfortable for anyone to interact with them. People with such personalities are not only women, some men also have these traits, although statistically, women may have more of these traits. Let me share a concept called "stimulus generalization" with you. Stimulus generalization refers to the phenomenon where stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus elicit similar conditioned reflexes. For example, if a child has had a painful experience at the dentist, they may fear the dentist, the dental chair, related instruments, and the dentist's white coat. Now, if the child is taken to a hair salon, where there are also chairs and white coats, if the child feels fear in the hair salon, that would be an example of stimulus generalization. The child perceives the similarity between the first and second situations. You may experience physical discomfort and the urge to vomit. Have you experienced any particularly unpleasant events in the past that could explain such a strong reaction? Take a moment to recall and analyze the events, face them rationally, and avoid this stimulus generalization effect. "No one is perfect" - you mentioned that you do have types of girls you really like - independent, mature in thinking, gentle, kind, considerate, and mindful of others' feelings. You have a fondness for these types of girls. So, it means you don't have fear towards all women. Therefore, you can pursue relationships with girls who possess these qualities. However, it is important to remember that nobody is perfect, and everyone can have emotional breakdowns. Even someone who is understanding and considerate may unintentionally hurt others when experiencing their own emotional breakdown. It is important for you to understand this and not hold unrealistic expectations, as it can contribute to your intimate relationships.

Hello, I'm glad to answer your question. The kind of girl you dislike, who speaks and acts without considering others, is a sign of immaturity. Conversely, the type of personality you like is mature and understands others. This can also reflect your personality traits. In reality, you are also a very mature person, right? So you hope that the type you like is also considerate. In fact, the people we like in real life are based on similarity, so we can appreciate each other. [I really dislike girls who only consider themselves and vent their emotions without considering others' feelings. The words and actions they say are completely disregarding others' feelings.] I understand the feeling in your heart, but this is someone else's personality. Although we do not appreciate it, we should also respect it. This is also a display of cultivation. Why do you dislike this kind of girl so much? There may be two reasons. First, because of some bad impressions in the past, it makes it difficult for you to forget. This kind of dislike is targeted. Second, there is no clear target, no reason, I just don't like her. This situation is called a stereotype. You dislike a certain type of girl because you don't understand them. They must also be liked by others, which shows that they are not too detestable, but rather a prejudice against this type of person. The reason for prejudice is that there is no direct understanding and lack of communication. You dislike her because of her behavior, but you may not necessarily dislike her inner attitude. Disliking a person is largely subjective and arbitrary. If we look objectively, the evaluation will be different. Therefore, try to balance your mindset and slowly accept it, it will be fine. In daily life, just a look from others can trigger our emotional reactions. It may also happen unintentionally, but our thoughts are whether they dislike me? Then we start thinking a lot, and the end result is a bad mood. If you encounter this situation again when taking the subway, just take a look and don't pay it any more attention. There's no need to make too many judgments about people you meet by chance. There is no perfect person in the world, and we ourselves have flaws, it's just that we can't see them clearly. While you dislike others, you will also be disliked by some people. It is because of this that we should respect others even more. So, learn to treat others well. I hope you can live well.

Young man, it's good to stay away from girls you don't like, this is self-protection. As for feeling physically uncomfortable or even nauseous, it is indeed a conditioned reflex. Based on the two experiences you mentioned, you have formed some extreme thoughts and connections, and your reactions have been excessive. The reason why those girls behave that way is because they have tasted or expect to taste some benefits. To put it plainly, those people are also pitiful. Their understanding is flawed and biased, but they are unaware of it and even conceited. This is also due to their own experiences. They are passive recipients as well. They have caused you harm for no reason, and you have become victims. Don't feel disgusted anymore. They will sense your malice, which will be unfavorable to you. Think of them as just pitiful people who have been spoiled, like little girls who haven't grown up. They will pay a heavy price for their bad habits in the future. Will thinking like this bring you psychological balance? Will you feel disdain or sympathy for them, and no longer have adverse reactions towards us? What do you think? If you like girls with good qualities, it means you have a strong sense of morality and good taste. You will be able to get along well with such girls and find them as companions. Isn't that great? When faced with things, try to think positively and respond actively. Let go of those negative thoughts. Even if you still dislike those bad girls, don't deliberately distance yourself from them, overcome it. When you encounter someone you know, nod and say hello. This will show our tolerance and leave a better impression on the good girls, making it easier to interact with them, isn't it? Actually, most of those girls who seem distant and respectful are actually good. They are just protecting themselves from being harassed and hurt by others. Giving them a cold shoulder and looking down on them is just a protective color to scare off those flies. If you can truly understand what's inside their hearts, you will find their cuteness and helplessness. Of course, if there are really obnoxious girls, stay far away from them and ignore them. As long as you know they are also pitiful, it won't affect your mood. That's it. Your experiences are just extremely rare cases. Don't treat them as normal phenomena or even serious problems. That won't benefit you at all. Please consider what I've said, it will help you resolve your emotional burden. Wishing you a pleasant mood.

We all say we extremely dislike the first type of girl and should stay away from her, but I don't think it's like that. Because first of all, we have to admit that each of us has many sides. It's only one aspect of this person that we find annoying, while another aspect is understanding and considerate. We can't negate a person or feel disgusted by them just because they did something that annoyed us. Everyone makes countless mistakes in their life, even great people make many fatal mistakes, let alone us who write comments. So if you approach relationships with this mindset, your interpersonal relationships will also encounter problems!

question: 25-year-old girl, for seven years, why has she been unable to like her major?
description: I have a somewhat introverted personality and am thin-skinned or, in other words, somewhat dull. In the past, I couldn't even greet my relatives properly. My parents wanted me to study medicine, but I was more interested in astronomy and art. However, they believed these two fields wouldn't lead to job opportunities. So, out of frustration after the college entrance exam, I applied to all medical universities and was accepted to a second-tier university. At that time, I didn't think I would reach the admission score for a top-tier university, but if I had applied to a few more schools, maybe I could have. And so, I ended up going to medical school. Afterwards, I became less inclined to interact with others, spending my days in bed, glued to my phone, writing articles and chatting with online friends. Over time, I became even more unable to speak in public, even trembling with nerves. I lost interest in my chosen profession and my grades, which used to rank in the top five, dropped to second to last. The more this happened, the more I realized that it was all because I chose a field I didn't like and because of my previous failures (until high school graduation, I always enjoyed taking exams and never feared them. However, before the college entrance exam, I was melancholic for a long time because I had to choose a major that didn't suit my personality). After failing and retaking exams, I began to fear exams and would feel nauseous and sick every time I had one. It has been two years since my graduation, and I still haven't found a job. I opened a store and am preparing for a postgraduate entrance exam. This year, I must find a job, but I have been unable to enjoy or even fear it.
keywords: Occupation, career management, work pressure, work fatigue.

answers.answer_text: First of all, after reading the description, I feel really sorry for the author. It takes a great deal of willpower and courage to choose a major that one doesn't like and even work in that industry. Although the author has gone through a lot in this process, it is commendable that they can persist until now. Secondly, the author mentioned that they have been introverted and thin-skinned since childhood, so it seems like they are not good at socializing. After entering college, they dislike interacting with people even more. This is related to the author's lack of social skills and their way of dealing with problems. Because they were forced to choose a major they don't like, they are even more unwilling to communicate with others, which is a form of avoidance. They even get nervous, scared, and tremble when communicating with others, which is a manifestation of social anxiety. Later, because of exam failure, they went from enjoying exams to feeling nauseous and disgusted at the thought of exams. This is a manifestation of anxiety somatization. This reflects the author's problematic behavioral patterns, which they need to pay more attention to. Finally, here are some suggestions for the author: 1. Regarding emotional issues, from the author's description, it can be felt that they experience anxiety and fear, and there may also be some depression. They should pay more attention to this. If they can't adjust on their own, it is recommended that they seek help from a professional psychological counselor. 2. As for the social aspect, not interacting with people for a long time will only make their problems worse, so it is recommended that the author try to express themselves. For example, they can start by having a gathering with their loved ones or friends and express themselves more. Then, gradually try to express themselves in front of others, and slowly bring about change. 3. As for the issue of not liking their major, I'm not sure if the author has planned their future yet. If they are not working in their field of study, are there any better choices for them? Many people aren't able to work in their dream industry. It's more about finding a suitable industry. However, they can still pursue their interests as hobbies to enrich themselves.

1. Seeing this description, it feels very tragic. This is perhaps the sorrow of most Chinese-style education. Why is that? Both sides are not wrong. Parents want you to study a practical major that can secure your future, while you are interested in pursuing a more romantic major. This is the result of over-indulgent parenting, which makes children unaware of the hardships of life. But even so, as an adult who has now become aware of this issue, it is important to change promptly and become a person with self-awareness and independence.

2. Your parents want you to study medicine, and even though you don't like it, you have applied for all medical majors. But if your parents wanted you to go and fight someone, would you go and fight? This brings up the issue of self. What is self? It means a person having their own thoughts, opinions, and feelings, as well as the ability to independently pursue something. If you honestly reflect, from childhood until now, have you ever accomplished something independently? You mentioned that you couldn't even greet relatives on your own. If you are unable to accomplish such a simple task independently, let alone making choices about your future major, which is just a larger representation of independence. So what you are currently struggling with is not just a question of major A or B, but rather whether or not you can independently do something.

3. There's a saying called "turning misfortune into good fortune," so why not accept the mistake and make the most of it? Since you have already studied medicine and invested the most precious 7 years of your youth, this is an unchangeable fact. Since that's the case, why not give it your all? Is it because you can't independently complete a task that you are using disliking the major as an excuse? This allows you to avoid being independent and diligent, with valid reasons. This is the true reality, even if it sounds harsh. Including all the symptoms, getting a stomach ache before an exam, they are all excuses and shields. Just because you don't like this major, you think you can slack off and shift the responsibility to your parents, and you can even afford to not work for 2 years after graduation.

4. You also mentioned it's been 7 years, and you finally realize it now. I hope you can wake up sooner and not hold grudges for a lifetime. Your parents will grow old eventually, and it's impossible for them to take care of you for a lifetime.

question: What should I do if it's difficult to persevere in reading and easy to give up halfway?
description: When reading, I always have difficulty focusing and find it hard to finish a book. I tend to give up halfway through and my interest fluctuates. Overall, I lack enthusiasm. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm not sure what book you are referring to when you say this situation occurs. If you are reading a book that you are very interested in, this situation should not or rarely happen. I read 8 Agatha Christie detective novels in June, but I didn't finish any of the world classics like "The Plague," "No Longer Human," or "A Thousand Years of Longing." When I read books that interest me, I can finish one in a day, but if I'm not interested, it may take me a month to finish one. I guess the reason you asked this question is because you have a low interest in reading, but you also know that you should read more, which creates this conflict and confusion. Here are a few suggestions for you: 1. Find books that you are interested in. Whether it's detective novels, suspense novels, or even fantasy novels, as long as you are reading, it will be beneficial. There's no need to stick to reading only classical works. 2. You can listen to audiobooks or watch adaptations. Some classics are available in audio format on platforms like Himalaya, and some have been adapted into TV shows or movies. If you can't get into a book, you can try listening to it or watching the adaptation to understand the plot, which might spark your interest in the book. 3. It may have to do with age or the right opportunity. For example, "No Longer Human" might be hard for someone too young to understand, so maybe just skim through it and start with what interests you. Or maybe you just need the right opportunity to want to read it. 4. If you're talking about not being able to get into your school textbooks, I suggest studying with friends or classmates in groups. I hope this helps you!

This shows that those books are not your preferred genre, so there's no need to force yourself to read them and make yourself uncomfortable. If it's a textbook, it means you're not interested in your field of study, so consider switching to a major that you enjoy. I remember a freshman student who ranked first in their class while studying traditional Chinese medicine, but their grades dropped when they had to study Western medicine textbooks because they didn't like them. However, it doesn't matter. Finding your passion is the biggest success.

question: High school students, brought up by their grandparents since the age of 4, why do they lack empathy towards their parents?
description: I'm in high school. I was taken care of by my grandparents since I was 4 years old. My family is not happy, but they have never divorced for the sake of me. When my parents argue or reprimand me, or even when they cry, I don't feel ashamed or uncomfortable. When they argue, I just want to laugh, and when they scold me, I am numb. I don't feel anything when my mother cries either. But I have a strong empathy towards others, or things and characters in literature and the like. I can easily cry by recalling or empathizing from different perspectives. However, whenever I am in a family situation, my emotions become scarce, as if I am detached and just watching a play. I don't lack the love of my parents (when they are by themselves). I have no experience of a happy family of three and I don't understand why. Is it a problem with my morality?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Your parents argue and cry, but you show no signs of empathy, which makes you doubt your own morality. I really want to give you a hug and tell you that this is not your fault. Many times, when parents have relationship problems, they are reluctant to completely sever ties because of their children. So they seek compensation for the missing intimacy in their parent-child relationship. However, this compensation is not a healthy manifestation of a relationship. Even if your parents individually do a lot for you, you can still see their problems and power struggles, and you can feel the pain of being caught in the middle and playing a delicate role. This is also why your parents argue with each other and are exceptionally good to you, but you still feel very distant. In a good family relationship, parents love and understand each other, so they don't need to do anything extra for their children. Children naturally learn healthy ways of emotional communication from their parents' interactions. However, in reality, many parents cannot achieve this. On the contrary, they have too many expectations for their children and hope that their unsolvable problems can be solved through their children. This is also a habit they learned from their own parents, and we cannot demand too much from them. I believe you must be a sensitive and delicate child who can empathize with fictional characters in literary works, but cannot feel sad for your mother's tears. Literature and art are very traditional ways for us to express emotions and thoughts. The fact that you can empathize with characters shows that you have both empathy skills and rich emotions. It's just that the arguments within your family make you feel powerless and hurt. You would rather detach yourself from reality and immerse yourself in pitiful and adorable fictional characters than be immersed in these real and dark scenes. You are still a high school student, and at this stage, you don't have the ability to help your parents solve their problems, nor do you have the responsibility to solve their problems for them. I only hope that you can continue to be sincere and not give up on obtaining emotional support from other social supports. Get along well with your grandparents, make friends who can accept you through shared interests or similar personalities, plan for your own future, study hard, work towards financial independence, and minimize the harm caused by your parents. There may be a period of time when you don't want to talk much with your parents, and that's okay. Time is the best remedy, and sometimes distance is too. In the future, you will develop better ways to deal with family conflicts as you grow. The difficulties you're facing now, when you look back, will just be colorful storms in your life. Don't feel discouraged and don't blame yourself! Keep going.

Hello, from my point of view, it's not that you lack empathy, but rather that you have become numb to the patterns of interaction between your parents. We often talk about the influence of our upbringing on children, and it does have an impact. However, as we grow up, we can't use our upbringing as an excuse not to make changes. Some people, because of such experiences, vow to change and refuse to enter such a cycle, cherishing the people around them and valuing their relationships with others even more. On the other hand, some people feel powerless to make changes and fall into a vicious cycle, projecting the patterns of their upbringing onto others, viewing the world with hostility, as if the whole world owes them. So, I don't know, how would you define yourself? When you can achieve your ideal university placement and live independently, what kind of attitude do you want to have? You mentioned morality, but if you retaliate against your parents in the same way they treated you, the one who will be left with scars is only yourself. We receive a good education, but the previous generation, with a lack of education, did not know how to think about what they could do to make their own lives a little better. The pressure of life made them unaware of how to handle it, so they vented their frustrations on the closest and safest people - their own family. I believe they have done their best to treat you in the way they think is best. That's why as we grow up, with a higher education and our own will to think, I know that it's difficult to forgive them, but try to understand them. They also need to release their stress and be guided by you towards better ways of living. So, you are important; you give them the courage to face the difficulties of life. I wish you and your family well.

question: Middle school students preparing for the high school entrance exam always seem lively and never stay up late. Don't they feel like typical middle school students?
description: I may have done well in the first 5 semesters, and my exam scores were particularly good. However, as the mid-term exam of the second half of Grade 9 approached, the class started to get nervous. But I didn't feel nervous, nor did I have the kind of nervousness that teachers and principals talk about, like losing weight or peeling off a layer of skin. I am always mentally and physically energetic in class, and I never stay up late. But my grades are much better than some students who study better than me. I always feel like I haven't put in as much effort as others, but I perform better in exams. I don't want to study like others do, only sleeping for 5 hours a day. But when I hear about their hard work or watch self-discipline videos on Bilibili, I always feel very anxious. Can I maintain a normal lifestyle like I do during the normal days without participating in the mid-term exam?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, work and study.

answers.answer_text: As long as you are confident, it's possible. In middle school, there were roughly three types of students in my class. One type performed very well and didn't have to worry about anything, similar to your situation. Another type worked very hard and put in effort every day. The third type didn't think they would pass the exam, so they just enjoyed themselves. I think it's the strong confidence behind you that makes you fearless and very certain. Maybe you haven't realized it, but it's true. Actually, studying like this is quite good. Staying up too late and being exhausted every day can also lead to low classroom efficiency, which is not good. However, if you want to get into a good high school and feel a bit uncertain, you can spend some time reviewing. If you have full confidence, then just maintain your current state. No one has defined what a middle school entrance examinee should be like. It's just that in your environment, most people are burning the midnight oil, feeling anxious, stressed, and so on, while your relaxed state and excellent mental state are different from others, making you feel strange and out of place. There are many reasons why you feel anxious because of them. It may be because everyone looks the same, and you appear strange. It may be because you are worried that after others put in so much effort, they will surpass you. You may be worried if you are overestimating yourself and if you will not do well in the exam... Why are you so relaxed? Besides the reasons mentioned earlier, it might also be because you have a mindset (which most people have): you don't want to be the same as others. While in a group, on the one hand, we try to make ourselves the same as others, but on the other hand, we want to appear different. In reality, regardless of what state you are in, as long as it suits you and your performance doesn't decline or other negative consequences arise, then just continue in that state. The best way is the one that suits you. Finally, I wish you the best of luck in your exams.

question: At 14 years old, I have been feeling inexplicably unhappy and empty inside recently.
description: Lately, I can't seem to be happy, and it gets worse when I'm alone in my room. My parents always say, "Who are you making a face for?" when they see me not smiling. Sometimes, even small things make me start crying, and my emotions fluctuate greatly. I always feel empty inside. I have engaged in self-harm and have had thoughts of suicide. I feel useless and like I can't do anything right. I really dislike myself right now. Is there something wrong with me?
keywords: Emotion, depressive mood, expressing emotions, emotion regulation

answers.answer_text: Children, do you have a lot of question marks? I am glad to meet you, but it saddens me to see your problems here. Fourteen is a time of diversity, where you should be carefree and not be disturbed by external factors. You can try taking a piece of paper and writing down all your worries and thoughts, then tear it up and flush it down the toilet, as a way of releasing them. At fourteen, you are at a stage of confusion, where childhood is behind you but adulthood has not yet arrived. You may feel various discomforts and contradictions in your heart. You may see yourself as an adult, while adults treat you as a child, causing a generation gap in communication with your parents. Slowly, you may not want to talk to your mom and dad, feeling that they don't understand you. But you should know that your parents have also experienced the stage you are currently in, and they may have had similar emotions. You can try awakening their memories and talk about what their own experiences were like at this age. When you encounter unsolvable problems, you can talk to your mom and dad, chat with good friends, or treat yourself to a meal of your favorite food. Whenever I am unhappy or happy, I always reward myself with an ice cream. I hope that what you encounter are not major problems, but just small emotions, a combination of the small conflicts that come with adolescence. Try communicating more with your parents, as many adult issues are resolved through communication. If you also see yourself as an adult, why not have a conversation with your parents as adults? You may have unexpected results, and it can help you overcome these small emotions. I hope you can always be happy and carefree in the future.

question: Lost focus on preparing for graduate school exams, going crazy searching online to chat with the opposite sex?
description: I am 26 years old this year and have been graduated from a bachelor's degree for three years. I am currently extremely lost. My original job was an online teacher, but I found this job to be extremely boring and it doesn't allow me to interact with people outside. So, when I met my ex-boyfriend six months ago, I completely got caught up in this relationship. But maybe because I haven't had much contact with people for a long time, I am extremely fragile in this relationship and need to be loved. Of course, he is not a good person, he doesn't even have basic care for me. After the breakup, I decided to take the postgraduate entrance examination...and greatly reduced my course load. Recently, I just got into the studying mode, but I'm not sure if it's because I went on a trip and lost my momentum after coming back. I don't feel like studying every day and I feel confused. I also miss my ex-boyfriend like crazy...and then I go online to chat with the opposite sex as if I had an addiction to the internet...but gradually, I realized that there are many scammers and very few people with whom I can have a good conversation, often it's just a one-day encounter...and I fall into this disappointment, then start looking for online friends to fill the void, and then the cycle of disappointment repeats...and I can't get myself motivated to study...sigh...it's like a death cycle, it feels really uncomfortable...

answers.answer_text: Hugs and kisses to you. Seeing how your past relationship from six months ago has had a big impact on you, it seems that you are craving for love and care from others and feeling emotionally vulnerable. Even during the intense period of studying for the postgraduate entrance exam, you still find yourself desperately missing him and seeking comfort from others online. It seems like you constantly seek and yearn for the care of others in your relationships, indicating a lack of security and support, which makes you feel very uncomfortable. In addition, as a working student who is preparing for the entrance exam, it is already not easy for you. You need to find your own pace and state of mind, which can help you feel more in control during your exam preparation. This stage is already nearing the end of the entrance exam, and the recent trip may have helped you relax, thus requiring some adjustments. The anxiety of the entrance exam combined with the emotional void has made your current state not good, and you feel very uncomfortable. As you mentioned, this is a cycle wherein you feel anxious about the exam, so you seek distractions through chatting, but then feel disappointed, leading to fretting over your exam performance... So, how can we adjust? Regarding relationships: adjust your mindset and understand that a sense of security and emotional fulfillment does not necessarily need to come from the opposite sex. Your family, friends, and even yourself can provide support and strength. You can try to tap into the resources around you and find your social support system to empower yourself. Regarding the entrance exam: first, find your own rhythm and plan your study time well. Making a good plan can help you quickly get into a state of mind. Additionally, try to adjust your mindset and not place too much weight on the success or failure of the exam. If worst comes to worst, you can always continue working. This might help alleviate your anxiety. I hope this can help you. The world and I love you.

OP: Hello! Thank you for trusting me and inviting me to answer your questions. Let me start with your emotions. You mentioned that when you encountered your ex, you were completely immersed in that relationship. I'm not quite sure what you mean by being immersed, did you mean that you loved him very deeply and did things for him? Or did you mean something else? So, in that significant emotional experience for you, what was your specific state? I can't imagine it. But you have summarized it by saying that you were extremely vulnerable in that relationship and needed to be cared for. And he wasn't a good partner, not even providing the basic care you needed. Given this information, I can infer that your emotions in intimate relationships may be unstable and that you feel unloved. Is that correct? You attributed this to possibly not having social contact for a long time. I think that may be one aspect, but perhaps you also need to consider your relationships with significant others in your life. Do you have emotionally satisfying relationships, for example, with your parents? Do you have siblings? Do you have friends you can talk to? Before this boyfriend, did you have any other dating experiences? What were your emotional states like in previous relationships? I'm asking all these questions to invite you to try and observe yourself because theoretically, every interpersonal relationship can be a reflection and reenactment of important relationships from early life. Of course, we also need to consider the traumatic experiences you went through in this relationship. I don't know how long it has been since you broke up with your ex, and whether your current state is still a lingering signal from the past trauma or if you are still in a post-traumatic stress state. Therefore, looking further ahead, you mentioned that you are going crazy searching for strangers to chat with online, as if trying to fill a void. Is this void that you feel a lack of a romantic relationship in your immediate surroundings or a lack of feeling loved internally? After the breakup, you decided to test yourself, seemingly intending to fill the void inside with academic development, but a trip caused you to lose your focus on studying. Did something happen during the trip? Or is the void inside you so deep that neither testing yourself nor dating is a true remedy, causing you to feel stuck in a cycle? It seems that the solutions you can think of are either testing yourself or starting a new romantic relationship. Based on the above considerations, I think you need a stable psychological counseling to help you break out of this cycle. Give it a try! I wish you the best of luck! Chen Yiping (a counselor with five years of experience in psychological counseling, having grown and transformed through counseling sessions, I believe I can accompany you to find a new direction in life).

Hello, author, the time for the postgraduate entrance exam is approaching, and I can feel your inner anxiety and worry. But there are still two to three months left, nearly a hundred days, so hold on! We can win! The topics of heartbreak and the entrance exam have already been discussed by other answerers, so I won't go into detail on that. However, I want to tell you that taking the entrance exam is about improving your abilities and planning for the future. It is something worth striving for. If the direction of the entrance exam aligns with your interests, even better. So believe in your choice and stick to it. What I mainly want to talk about is the change in mood after traveling. I don't know if you've felt this way, but after returning to school after summer vacation, the state of mind is different from when we were attending school. It seems like our hearts are wandering, and we lack motivation to study and need to focus. Traveling is similar to summer vacation. During the journey, we enter a different environment and the things we see bring various impacts. Unlike vacation, the pleasure from traveling is a temporary stimulation, and there may be a sense of emptiness after a long vacation. But after the trip ends, most of the emotions are nostalgia for happiness and fear of returning to the routine. Therefore, it is not wise to travel before a major exam. The brain takes in a large amount of information unrelated to daily life all at once and is in an excited state, wanting to communicate, wander around, and absorb new things. I believe this is why you can't get into the right state and are looking for people to chat with everywhere. Talking to strangers is a novel and interesting experience. Online communication breaks the limitations of time and space, and this stimulation and novelty are similar to traveling. Please remember that you still have an exam to take. If it is what you truly want, value it and then make an effort to adjust your state of mind. You need to switch your brain from an excited mode to a normal mode, instead of giving it more intense stimulation, making it even more excited. Compared to chatting, browsing fragmented information, and scrolling through social media, reading professional books, studying English, and solving political questions may seem less interesting and even boring. However, for the sake of the future and for the better version of yourself, you still need to control yourself and turn your focus to these less interesting things. The brain's state doesn't switch like a computer with just a click. So you need to establish a consistent routine, set a dedicated study time for yourself, during which you can't do anything else except study or daydream, and you can't use your phone either. If your entrance exam includes mathematics, solving math problems is a great way to concentrate. If not, solving multiple-choice questions in some professional courses can also be helpful, or solving multiple-choice questions in political science for the entrance exam. Solve twenty questions first before moving on to other studying, and you will be able to get into the studying zone faster. Try to avoid overly stimulating your brain and making it overly excited. Minimize the use of your phone and social media apps. If that's difficult, then set aside a specific time for stimulation, such as from 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM, as your entertainment time. Actually, my advice is all conventional advice, and there are more and better studying tips from fellow users on Zhihu. However, advice and tips are abstract things, the key is in ourselves. Taking the entrance exam or pursuing a professional certification requires us to make plans, improve our abilities, and put in long-term efforts to achieve our goals. It requires strong self-motivation. If we choose to take the exam or pursue a certification out of the desire to become a better version of ourselves to make others regret or envy us, instead of doing it for our own sake and to create a better future for ourselves, then my advice is to temporarily give it up and carefully consider what kind of future we truly want. Good luck and keep it up!

Hello, OP: I have observed your confusion. Sometimes, the more we seek external validation, the more we feel lacking in care. However, it is brave of you to express your concerns and seek help, as it can help you better understand yourself, identify your deeper needs, and make adjustments. Now, I would like to share my observations, which may help you see your behavior from different perspectives. 1. Our relationships with others are actually projections of our relationship with ourselves. Interpersonal relationships serve as mirrors where we can see our needs. I have noticed that after encountering your ex, you became completely immersed in that relationship. But perhaps it's because I haven't had much interaction with people for a long time, I feel extremely vulnerable in this relationship and in need of care. From this relationship, we can see your deeper need for love and the desire to establish connections with others. Since this need of yours is not being fulfilled, you tirelessly pursue it, only to end up empty-handed. Since our relationships with others are projections of our relationship with ourselves, it means there is an inner child within us who longs to be loved. This child needs to be seen, taken care of, and healed. 2. Nurturing our inner child's growth. Once we have straightened out our relationship with ourselves, our relationships with others will also improve. So, if you want to have the energy to study for your postgraduate entrance exam, perhaps you need to first work on the relationship with yourself, understand the needs of your inner child, and learn to fulfill them. I have noticed that you desperately miss your ex-boyfriend... and then go online and chat with strangers crazily, as if you have developed an addiction... but gradually, you realize that there are many scammers and it is difficult to find someone with whom you can have a true connection; these encounters often end up being fleeting. This leads to disappointment, and then you start the cycle of seeking online friends to fill the void, only to be disappointed again... Have you noticed that you have been constantly seeking external validation? However, the most uncontrollable factors are the external environment and other people. So why not seek within ourselves? We cannot control others, but we can control ourselves. Now that we are adults, when others cannot fulfill our needs, let's not forget that we can fulfill our own needs. So, learn to love your inner child, meet her needs, protect her, and nurture her. This way, she will grow and heal her wounds. 3. Learn to associate freely. The lack of care and our experiences of personal growth are directly related. So, perhaps you can freely associate and reflect on how your need for love came about, review your experiences of personal growth, and reflect. Only then will you better understand yourself, get to know yourself, and understand the underlying causes of your personality. This will solve half of the problem.

Hello: Confused, with unclear goals, unable to find meaning. In fact, the state you describe is not bad, but you can't enjoy your work or life properly, which seems like a feeling of extreme self-isolation. It seems like you want to connect with people, but still feel empty and lonely inside. Actually, this is a common problem for modern people. Analyzing and understanding the problem: 1. You are now 26 years old, graduated from college three years ago, and now you are extremely confused. (Today's college education is different from what it used to be, it seems a bit like graduating from junior high school back then. Confusion, panic, not knowing the future direction. Should you aim for postgraduate studies or work, and what is the purpose of pursuing postgraduate studies? Your confusion is completely understandable, you just lack direction.) 2. Your original job was an online teacher, but you found this job to be extremely boring and unable to connect with the outside world. So when you met your ex half a year ago, you became completely immersed in that relationship. However, maybe because you haven't had much contact with people for a long time, you became extremely vulnerable in this relationship and needed to be cared for. Of course, he is not a decent person, he doesn't even show basic care for you. (Online work seems to be a trend nowadays. The rise of online platforms has given many people opportunities and reduced communication costs, but at the same time, it has also reduced the opportunities for people to meet, communicate, and play offline. Many emotions are also engaged online, so what is left for the parties involved to understand? We are living human beings, unable to have contact with others, it sounds cruel. Love, without mutual concern, admiration, and attraction, what is left?) 3. After the breakup, you decided to prepare for postgraduate studies...but you drastically reduced your courses. You had just entered a good state, but after you went on a trip, you lost that state. Every day, you don't want to study, you feel lost. (Traveling helps people relax, of course, if you relax too much, it becomes slackness. That comfortable state is only because it is not the norm, so once you relax, it's hard to get back on track. But this is also a skill we need to master, which is how to adjust our state in two different environments. When you come back, you need to gather yourself and continue the journey, right?) 4. You still desperately miss your ex-boyfriend...and you go online to chat with strangers like crazy, as if you had internet addiction... (You appear to be crazily missing your ex-boyfriend, but in fact, it is inner restlessness and anxiety, not really missing him. What you lack is not a boyfriend, but someone to accompany you, care for you, be concerned about you, and have emotional interactions with you. So when you chat with strangers online, you simply think that this can reduce your sense of loneliness and relieve your emotions, but in fact, it is not the case.) 5. But gradually, you realize that there are many scammers, and very few people you can connect with, they are usually just passing acquaintances... this makes you feel disappointed, and then you seek online friends to fill the void, and then the cycle of disappointment repeats... and you cannot bring yourself to study... sigh... it feels like a cycle of death, very uncomfortable... (Yes, you have also discovered that there are dishonest people out there. It's not scary if they have a purpose, as long as they are straightforward with you, then you can be cautious and prevent being deceived. Dear, your chosen approach is not correct, please believe that there are good people out there. Think about it, finding a needle in the ocean, the probability is definitely small. You can seek help from professional counselors who can understand your situation and help release the repression and emotions in your heart.) A cycle of death, although it's called "death," as long as there is a cycle, we have the opportunity to break the bad cycle and replace it with a good one. Closing words: I wish you happiness and joy! May you overcome your confusion and open your heart soon! If you have any confusion, feel free to message me!

Hello, it has been 3 years since I graduated from college, and I am extremely lost now. I work as an online teacher, but I find this job particularly boring, and I have no way to interact with people outside. When I met my ex, maybe I was too in need of love and care, so I got involved with him even though I knew he wasn't a good person. After the break-up, I planned to take the postgraduate entrance exam, but after coming back from traveling, I lost my motivation and felt unmotivated, not wanting to do anything. When I try to talk to someone, they usually turn out to be temporary acquaintances, which disappoints me, but I can't stop trying and get caught in a loop. From your description, it seems that you really want to establish connections with the outside world. However, you have chosen to work and make friends online. Even though it seems possible to establish connections online, you still feel like something is missing. You want to be cared for; so, what specific behaviors or actions do you hope for when it comes to being cared for? Daily online greetings? Or something else? Can these ways of care be fulfilled online? You are not motivated to study for the entrance exam, and before traveling, you were in the right mindset, but after traveling, you couldn't find the motivation to study. What was your motivation for wanting to take the entrance exam? What does the entrance exam mean to you? For example, imagine a person who wants to eat spaghetti, but sits in a Guilin rice noodle shop, eating rice noodles, complaining about what's wrong with it, but still continues to eat the next day. At this point, someone might wonder, why doesn't he just go eat spaghetti? This person can provide many reasons, and each person may be different, such as "the spaghetti restaurant is too far away", "the spaghetti takes too long to wait", "the spaghetti is a bit expensive", and so on. However, if you analyze it carefully, the reasons above don't hold up. "The spaghetti restaurant is too far away" -- delivery can be sent downstairs. "The spaghetti takes too long to wait" -- you can call or use a software platform to pre-order. "The spaghetti is a bit expensive" -- it's not more expensive than seafood rice noodles in Guilin. So, does this person really want to eat spaghetti? I hope this answer can inspire you! Karen.

This is not your fault, it's a problem with China's education system. For so many years, schools have been treated like factories, and teachers like engineers, mass producing standardized products in different batches. Let me talk about my eldest son. In those years, he didn't take the college entrance exam because he had to prove that his mother was his mother. He went out to make a living. My eldest son went to Suzhou this year and became a courier for SF Express. Of course, he had to work hard. With a simple life, he earns over 6000 RMB per month, enough to support himself without any problem. He also takes care of some living expenses for his younger sister who is still in university. He can even do some game programming in his spare time, earning some extra income. He is optimistic and doing well in everything. Actually, in terms of many conditions, he may not be as good as you, but he is a man who grew up in a warm and safe family. So he can go out and explore, grow, and be himself with confidence. It is said that programming also requires logical thinking skills, and his math was among the top in Guangzhou at that time. He didn't take the college entrance exam due to policy constraints. He has been searching for himself in Shanghai and Suzhou. So, I think it's better to find yourself and be a genuinely healthy person. Do what you should do, what you want to do, and what you can do. I wish you all the best.

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. After briefly looking at your current situation, you have been working for three years but have lost interest in your job, so you have decided to take the postgraduate entrance exam. However, during the preparation process, you occasionally have expectations for love. After a trip, you find it difficult to focus on studying. First of all, I want to say that interest in something does not come out of thin air. Often, when we have had successful experiences in a certain field, we will be more inclined to enjoy doing things in that field. The same goes for work. However, since you have already chosen to take the postgraduate entrance exam, it is naturally the most important thing for you to prepare well at the moment. Secondly, the mentality during the entrance exam preparation is indeed a very demanding issue. Coincidentally, I am also preparing for the postgraduate entrance exam this year, so I think I can understand your feelings. As a fellow postgraduate entrance exam candidate, I have to say that your expectations for love have nothing to do with your current goals. Temporarily forget about your mentality towards the entrance exam. I think I have adjusted well. My progress is not the fastest, and my foundation is not the best, but I know what I should be doing at the moment. Do you know? Thirdly, about your loss of focus after a trip, I can clearly tell you that even during the postgraduate entrance exam review process, if I only go out and play with friends for one afternoon in a week, I will also lose focus when I come back. Therefore, you need to understand your own control over yourself and try to reduce the time spent going out to play. Of course, moderate relaxation is necessary. Good luck with your postgraduate entrance exam preparation!

Hello, after reading your description, my first reaction is that you may have developed a narcissistic injury due to a failed relationship, and as a result, you have been compensating for this injury by engaging in self-centered behavior. In reality, this is just a coping mechanism, and it usually takes some time for healing. I'm not sure what your ultimate goal is, so I suggest taking some time to reflect on how to feel comfortable in the present moment. This could involve getting back together with your ex, succeeding in your academic pursuits, finding a satisfying job, or anything else that brings you comfort. Once you have determined your objective, you can develop a specific plan to achieve it and try to put it into practice. It may lead to improvement. If you find it difficult to think independently, you can seek professional counseling online or in your local area to engage in a comprehensive exploration of personal growth, covering cognitive aspects and the influence of your family of origin.

question: Why do I doubt other people's affirmation and praise?
description: Today I painted with watercolors for the first time. I was a little excited. While I was painting, my colleague said it looked good. I asked, "Really?" When I said that, my colleague said I didn't believe her. I replied, "It's not that I don't believe you, I just don't believe in myself."

answers.answer_text: Hello! Everyone longs to be sincerely praised, but very few are willing to do so. In fact, it is not strange at all. Many people are actually very afraid of praising others. In childhood, if one receives negative evaluations for a long time, it greatly lowers their self-esteem, undermines their confidence, and might even destroy it. Faced with compliments, there is a reflexive response of "not deserving." They believe they are not worthy of praise. The resistance to compliments may not be about the compliments themselves, but rather, it might trigger memories of past frustrating experiences. This is a defense mechanism with rationalized denial, defending against narcissistic satisfaction when appreciated by denying others' appreciation. The reason for defending against narcissistic satisfaction is to protect oneself from experiencing the pain of narcissistic frustration. Most people are used to speaking negative and hurtful words to themselves and feel that they are constantly living behind a mask. In order to break free from the curse of "I'm not good enough" in their minds, some people study hard but still can't escape its grip. The most important thing is to know oneself, to see one's own strengths and advantages, as well as to recognize one's shortcomings and flaws. Build on strengths, improve weaknesses, build confidence, and happily accept others' compliments. Sincere compliments are a good medicine that can help people progress and grow. With self-awareness, one can clearly identify and disregard insincere compliments while accepting genuine ones. Second, pretend to be confident. The strategy of "pretending to be confident" can help you at least have the opportunity to get many jobs and opportunities, instead of shutting them out from the beginning. Once you have a certain opportunity, the "imposter syndrome" will strive to complete it, and in fact, the results are usually much better than they expected. Sometimes pretending turns into reality. Third, try to believe. Start by learning to believe, believing that others' compliments are true, and believing that you deserve them. The next time someone compliments you, at least respond with "thank you." Over time, you will become more accustomed to compliments and then say, "I am beautiful," "I work hard, and I deserve these achievements." Believe in yourself, you deserve better, you deserve to have it.

question: Frontline employees have a high level of hostility towards logistics personnel. How to ignore others' judgment?
description: The company I work for is a manufacturing enterprise. The production line runs 24 hours a day, with only 8 hours of rest on Sundays, and very few holidays. The frontline staff have a heavy workload, many regulations to follow, and low benefits. There is a high turnover rate among employees. However, the logistics staff work 8-hour days, have weekends off, and work in an office. Because we often have to issue many requirements to the production workshop, this has created a strong animosity from the frontline staff towards us. Whether it's at work or in daily life, they are always ready to confront us. I am not a confident person to begin with, although I am usually cheerful and love sharing moments on social media. But because I have been working in this environment for a long time, I have become even less confident and don't like sharing on social media anymore because I feel that no matter what I say, those employees will criticize me behind my back. So, I hope to become invisible and keep a low profile. Office colleagues face the same challenges, but I may be more concerned about others' opinions. How can I resolve these emotions?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Today is the third time I am answering questions about work. In fact, our lives mostly revolve around work. Sometimes, we spend more time at work than at home, so the pressures of work and life are often intertwined, leading to anxiety, irritability, and even spreading to our families. Anyway, let's move on to the specific issue you mentioned. The company you work for is a production-oriented enterprise, with frontline employees working 24 hours a day, facing heavy workloads and poor working conditions, while management personnel work an 8-hour shift, enjoying better working conditions and benefits, including weekends off, and so on. As you described, different job positions come with different responsibilities and benefits, and this is a normal phenomenon. It is a matter of the company's policies and regulations. As long as you fulfill your duties within the scope of your job responsibilities in accordance with the company's rules, there is nothing wrong with it. The relationship between managers and those being managed will always be a contradictory one, and it can never be completely resolved. The best we can do is constantly adjusting and maintaining a temporary balance. In another sense, you may be in a logistical management position (based on the requirements issued by the company), where managers represent the interests of the owners, while those being managed represent the interests of the employees. It is normal to have grievances about the company's management. New management concepts are being developed to weaken the role of management and strengthen the role of service, with the premise being sound systems, high-quality staff, and advanced scientific and technological means. So, if you are currently involved in establishing a scientifically reasonable management system, you shouldn't have any psychological burdens. Moreover, that is your job responsibility. If you cannot even fulfill your own job, then I believe you would become a burden to the company. A good manager will not disregard the company's interests to be a "people pleaser". Don't aspire to be such a "people pleaser", and shouldn't become one. These are some recommendations from my years of experience in human resources work. I hope it can be helpful to you. Keep up the good work!

question: Lack of independence, what should I do if I'm afraid of standing on my own?
description: I hope to have someone accompany me in everything I do, afraid of making mistakes on my own, and afraid of being alone. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Everyone has unique characteristics. Some people are naturally talented and independent, while others are more supportive and cooperative. Don't criticize yourself, allow yourself to be who you truly are. Just like Zhu Yuanzhang and Zhuge Liang, both are remarkable in their own ways. However, you can also try doing things that showcase your individuality. Afterward, reflect on whether you enjoy it or not. Perhaps this is a hidden potential within you. If you try something and realize you don't like it or even make mistakes, that's okay.
