Life is not about avoiding mistakes; the key is to experience unfamiliar things and understand how they make you feel. Understanding what you do and don't like is more valuable than focusing on right or wrong. Don't fixate on not doing something perfectly; instead, focus on discovering what you truly enjoy and exploring new experiences. Whether you are naturally talented or cooperative, these are just processes that help you discover and understand yourself.

Hello, OP, you realize that as you grow older, you should gradually become more independent, but you worry about doing things alone. Hugs to you~ Maybe you hope to become independent all at once and handle everything by yourself, but as you may have experienced, it seems a bit difficult. How about taking it slowly? Allow yourself to gradually become independent, allow yourself to grow slowly. Start with a small thing that is closest to you and slowly free yourself from relying on others, try to do it yourself. This is just my suggestion, hope it can help you. Take care!

question: What should one do if they feel they are worthless because they have no goals in life?
description: After turning thirty, I have neither a career nor my own small family. I am still on the "pursuit of dreams" path. But in fact, I don't really have any dreams and I don't know what I can do or what I enjoy doing. I have thought about working hard or just marrying someone randomly to fulfill a duty, but I am not willing to do that. I am afraid of regretting it, and I worry that having a child would hurt them. I try to work hard, but I don't have a clear direction. I am considering taking a professional examination, but it always feels too difficult, and I have no self-discipline. I feel like my life is in chaos. Is there any hope for someone like me?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, sending you a warm hug (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You feel like you have no goals, no direction, and lack self-discipline. (2) You want to know if there is still hope for yourself. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: (1) As long as you have not given up on facing life, life will not give up on you! Although everything may seem overwhelming right now, if you can try to maintain a calm mindset and tackle things one by one in order of priority, you may find that things are not as difficult as you think. (2) Regarding age and family, according to Erikson's stages of psychosocial development, it seems that individuals entering society without a partner tend to have lower satisfaction with society. And at the age of 30, it seems to be a time for developing a sense of care, so it is normal to desire a family at this time. I suggest you learn to expand your social circle and meet more potential people. (3) As for life goals, you can actually write down one thing you most want to do at the moment and the kind of person you want to become in the future. Daily records may help you find direction and understand the significance of doing these things in the present! #The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

question: How to cope with the cold period in a romantic relationship when the feelings of passion fade away?
description: Long-distance relationship, haven't seen each other for over two months. The passion is fading, we don't chat as much anymore, feeling low and unmotivated. Every time he calls, I'm at a loss for words, not knowing what to say. I used to have a high need for personal space, I had a lot of self-interests, but it feels like he has taken up a lot of my time. I don't know what to do, I envy those who don't need to contact each other every day but still long for someone far away. I don't like intense and dramatic love, I prefer a more comfortable companionship. Now, I don't know if it's because of me or the emotions he brings, I feel conflicted, I have doubts. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. In a long-distance relationship, even though your boyfriend contacts you every day, you no longer have common topics to discuss. The excitement of the honeymoon phase has faded, and you are only left with low moods. You are unsure if it is caused by this person or this relationship. From your description, I see a contradiction: on one hand, you say you enjoy having your own space, having many interests, and being able to fulfill yourself without the need for constant intimacy and clinginess in a relationship. On the other hand, you feel disappointed because you haven't seen each other for two months in this long-distance relationship and there are no topics to talk about. Behind every contradiction, there is always some truth. It's possible that you have an avoidant attachment style, which means you don't inherently crave love, understanding, and acceptance, and you don't want highly intense emotional relationships. But deep down, you actually need these things more than anyone else. You need your self-worth to be recognized, someone to share the meaning of life with, and someone to understand and accept you. You say you enjoy missing someone from a distance because it allows you to project your imagination onto the other person, making you constantly feel loved and safe. In reality, you really need attention and understanding, but maybe you didn't receive much of it when you were young. So you use the approach of hiding in your own world to protect your heart which was hurt and disappointed in the past. Any emotional relationship will transition from passion to calmness. However, after the excitement fades, some relationships evolve into true love - caring for each other, nurturing each other, and supporting each other. Such relationships may seem calm, but they are stable and gentle. Your contradiction may come from your experiences of growth. What you need to explore yourself is what you truly need - is it what you described? Is the most authentic need really as you said? Once you find that authentic need, you can possibly find a relationship that fulfills your needs. Otherwise, you will find that even though you are in a relationship that seems to fulfill your described needs, you are not happy deep down. I hope you can love yourself and find someone who loves you the right way.

Questioner, good evening! Love has different stages and there are countless ways to get along. There is no one-size-fits-all approach to relationships. What matters is the attitude towards the relationship and the effort you are willing to put into it. People who have been through it all should understand the confusion you are feeling now; it's a fairly normal situation. "Being in a long-distance relationship, it's been over two months since we last saw each other. The passion seems to be fading, we don't chat as much anymore, and I feel low and unexcited." The phrase "long-distance relationship" often comes with a lot of preconceived notions. It seems like there should always be a constant sense of excitement and freshness, but when distance becomes the norm, your relationship dynamic tends to stabilize, and it's only natural for the constant excitement to fade away. "Whenever he calls me, I'm at a loss for words and don't know what to say." This feeling is indeed uncomfortable, almost like being out of control. It makes you feel detached from the relationship, and this seemingly detached awakeness makes us question whether we should withdraw from this relationship, questioning whether we need or are satisfied with this kind of relationship. Many social commentaries on love have mentioned that love is about being comfortable enough to have meaningless conversations, being willing to speak and listen. I strongly agree with this. However, it doesn't mean we have to have those kinds of conversations all the time. Based on your description, you have your own lifestyle and independence, and it's inevitable to have thoughts about returning to your original personal life track when the love transitions from passion to a more ordinary state. This is completely normal. With the limited information provided, it's difficult to analyze further. If you are truly troubled by this, I suggest discussing your thoughts with your boyfriend. View this issue as a necessary stage in the development of your relationship. Facing problems that arise from personal characteristics and lifestyle preferences together will help us better understand each other and foster sincerity. I hope this helps you. The sky is blue, and with you, life can be beautiful! World, I love you!

question: Online dating turns into reality, but always feeling like my girlfriend is deceiving me?
description: We met online, and in less than two months, we became a couple. Before that, we had some arguments, mostly over trivial matters. But recently, I realized that maybe there's something wrong with me. I've been suspecting that she's lying to me. For example, one night when we were on the phone and it was almost 11:30, she suddenly received a message. I asked who it was, and she said it was from a WeChat subscription account. She even showed me a screenshot. But when I looked at the timestamp, it was from 7:30 in the evening. I felt really disappointed. It's not just this incident, I feel like I'm living in a world of deception every day. It's causing me a lot of stress recently, and I can't sleep at night. It's very painful. Can you help me find some answers?
keywords: Love, infidelity, sense of security, love management

answers.answer_text: Because we got to know each other through the internet, many of the real information is not very confirmed, especially some recent small things that are not very reliable, which leads us to suspect whether the other person is hiding a lot of things from us. Firstly, let's not scare ourselves. Some things require solid evidence, not just our speculation. It is indeed a bit late to receive messages at 11:30 pm, but it does not exclude the possibility that the other person also has their own circle of friends. It's just that the screenshot time and her explanation to us are inconsistent, which makes us doubt a bit. Therefore, if there is a similar situation next time, we can jokingly ask the other person if she is a bit tired and the pictures she sent don't add up, and see what explanation she will give us. Secondly, some things can be discussed openly. Since the questioner has his own suspicions, there should be some basis for it, but some suspicions may not be true. Therefore, we can ask the other person for verification, tell them about our concerns, and see if they can give us a reasonable answer. Also, we need to examine whether we have hidden things from each other. If we have similar situations, or if we have told some well-intentioned lies in order to gain the other person's favor, then we can find a time to clarify it, so as not to have too many misunderstandings. Finally, we need to have some confidence in each other. The questioner and her are moving forward together, and they have also experienced some small setbacks. Since they are together now, they can discuss their concerns and future plans together. Don't leave too many mysteries for each other, and communicate with each other when there are problems. The world and I love you.

Talking about a relationship, but unable to trust wholeheartedly, this feeling is really unpleasant. However, many times, the reason why we are deceived is often because we ourselves cannot accept the truth. This does not mean that your girlfriend must be hiding something serious from you, but if a person still cares about the other person's feelings or is not willing to confront conflicts, then it is possible for them to hide things when they find that the other person is easily suspicious or entangled. However, even if the girlfriend is completely genuine, can the questioner really accept it? Or, even if the girlfriend hasn't done anything to hurt the questioner, can she accept a relationship without personal secrets? Because from the description, it is possible that the questioner and his girlfriend have different needs for personal space. To be honest, this kind of relationship can easily create pressure for both parties, and it may not necessarily be a problem that the questioner is faced with alone. Happy relationships are often not forced, therefore, it is important to evaluate the compatibility of your shared life comprehensively and then determine the future direction, perhaps it will be better for both parties. As for the question of whether the questioner is overly sensitive to deception, it cannot be completely judged based solely on the existing information. If necessary, it is recommended to seek more professional help to analyze it systematically. Hope this helps the questioner.

question: How to choose a suitable marriage partner in order to avoid facing societal pressures when reaching the age of 30?
description: Currently 29 years old, I don't want to wait until after 30 to face social pressure, so how can I choose a suitable marriage partner for myself?

answers.answer_text: Hello there, sending you warm hugs~ You have reached a good age for marriage, and you may face some pressure from parents, relatives, and friends regarding getting married. For yourself, when it comes to finding a suitable spouse, you can think about what your ideal partner would be like. Based on your description of your ideal partner, you can ask your parents, relatives, or friends to continue introducing you to potential partners through blind dates, which is an efficient way to meet people of the opposite sex. If you don't like the blind date approach, you can also expand your social circle and get to know the opposite sex through various methods. For example, you can attend more dinner gatherings with friends after work, where you may meet other people. If you feel a connection or attraction, you can try to get to know them better. Best wishes~.

question: Entering high school, I have become disinterested in studying and intentionally feigning sickness to go home, but I ended up getting scolded. I feel very helpless.
description: Just started my first year of high school and I feel that this school is not suitable for me. The school is very strict and tight when it comes to schedule, but the teachers only verbally enforce it and there is no actual management. I feel like I'm just going through the motions every day and I'm afraid I won't be able to get into a good university. I want to transfer schools but I don't know how to tell my parents. I got sick and had a fever for two nights without a blanket, so I went home. But when I got home, my mom scolded me for enjoying myself too much and said that I should be at school. I feel helpless and have thoughts of suicide, but I'm afraid of hurting myself or leaving home and receiving more criticism from my parents.

answers.answer_text: You just started high school and feel that the school is not good and not suitable for you because you feel that the teachers are not implementing effective management and are just slacking off every day, so you feel despair, right? ****** You are dissatisfied with the teachers not implementing effective management, so you hope that the school can have a good school atmosphere and the teachers can play a real role in management. You actually do not want to be influenced by this kind of environment, afraid of slacking off every day and not being able to get into college. This makes you feel disgusted with the current school and want to escape and leave. I see your inner pain and struggle, fighting against the efforts and the environment. The root of this pain lies in the fact that you both want to pursue a better learning environment and the possibility of future development. However, you feel powerless to fight against the environment and have to have conflicts within yourself, which affects your behavior and emotions. Sickness intensifies your disgust and avoidance towards the school, but you cannot get understanding, care, and acceptance from your family, feeling very disappointed and helpless, and wanting to express your struggle and helplessness through self-harm and suicide. You are dissatisfied with the school environment and think that it is not good, but you unconsciously give up your own pursuit and become a member of slacking off, confirming your negative impression and evaluation of the school. ****** The environment does indeed have a great impact on us. A good environment can help us progress more smoothly and achieve our goals. A bad environment can easily become an obstacle and make things less smooth. However, the development of anything is a result of both internal and external factors. In addition to having a good environment, what is more important is whether our internal motivation and strength are strong enough to support us moving forward. Only the internal driving force can help us overcome resistance and continue to strive. Many successful people are able to overcome adverse environments, hone and break through from them, find opportunities, and ultimately overcome the obstacles of a harsh environment, growing into more powerful individuals. So when you complain about the school not being good and you are not satisfied with the environment around you, you should first ask yourself if you really want to study well and go to a good college. Do you place your hopes of realizing your dreams on yourself or on the external world? There is a theory called "locus of control" that explains the attributions of success or failure that individuals often make. Internal locus of control attributes success to their own internal control power, so they tend to believe in their own abilities and are willing to take responsibility and actively seek solutions to problems, striving for their goals. External locus of control attributes success to external factors and relies on external forces to drive things forward, with the success or failure of things determined by external factors, finding excuses for failures and giving up their own power and efforts. This tendency of attributional explanatory style can influence our perception of the external world and ourselves, and therefore affect our actions and confidence. ****** I am not quite clear about the situation in your school. Apart from the poor management of schedule, how are other aspects? For example, the faculty strength, teaching quality, classmates' learning situation, etc., are there really no advantages to be found? Can you see their good side? How can they influence you? You should also ask yourself these questions: How is your current learning situation? What talents and strengths do you have? What can you learn from and gain in this school? Have you set clear goals for yourself? Have you ever believed in your own abilities? Is it the school that makes you slack off, or did you give up on yourself early on? Can you find a way to overcome difficulties and study well? For example, find teachers willing to help you and classmates willing to study together. If you transfer schools, can you guarantee that other schools will fully meet your requirements and that you will be able to motivate yourself to study well? Environmental factors should not be an excuse for avoiding difficulties, and changing the environment cannot completely solve the problem, because the root of the problem lies within yourself - you have both aspirations and desires, but also find excuses to avoid and give up. Even if the environment changes, you still cannot control the environment and fulfill your potential. If the pursuit of future dreams cannot rely on your own power to grasp and achieve, it can only be wishful thinking. Reality shows that many times, the environment is difficult to change. So, do you want to succumb to the environment, be defeated by the environment, or do you want to make an effort to adapt to the environment, change your thinking, adjust your cognition and behavior, and strive to overcome it and break free from this environment? This is a process of training and growth. Disgust, complaints, self-harm, and suicide are not effective forms of positive resistance, but rather a form of escape and giving up. Learn to accept the environment, adapt to the environment, find strength within yourself, and grow in a harsh environment, regain control over your own life, and that is the true form of resistance, allowing you to come closer to your dreams. Think carefully about your dreams and your life, find the source of your own strength, and face the challenges of the environment with confidence. Keep going.

question: Did I get depression because I hardly left the house this year? Should I go to the hospital?
description: Because of emotional and work pressures this year, I have hardly left the house at all. I have no interest in anything, and I often have thoughts of self-harm and suicide. However, I can't let go of my family, and I feel like there is no hope or future. Nothing goes smoothly, even though I know what I should do, I just can't do it. I sit and stare into space all day and can't sleep at night. I've had insomnia for a whole year and can only sleep when it's already daylight.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear reader. Low mood, decreased interest, insomnia, and feelings of hopelessness and lack of future are indeed manifestations of depressive emotions. Due to the dual pressures of work and relationships, you have been living under the shadow of depression for a year, which is truly not easy. My heart goes out to you. You mentioned that you haven't left the house for a year and that being in a confined environment without contact with the outside world can worsen your state of mind. So I suggest you try to go out, take a walk, or communicate with family and friends. It will be helpful for your current state. Additionally, you mentioned that you can't see any hope or future because you haven't planned for the future and haven't taken action. You are in the stage of imagination. When you set some goals for yourself and go from thinking to acting, your perception will change. Furthermore, you know what you should do, but you don't want to take action and spend your days daydreaming. In response to this situation, I recommend that you set small daily goals for yourself, and it's best to start with something that is not too difficult to achieve, which will give you more motivation. During this process, you can also explore your interests and hobbies. As for sleep problems, it's best to ensure a regular sleep schedule and try breathing exercises while lying in bed to help you fall asleep. Lastly, your emotional issues are quite severe at the moment. If you can't regulate them on your own, I suggest seeking assistance from a professional psychological counselor for systematic adjustment. I hope this can help you. Take care!

Feeling the dual pressure and frustration from work and relationships can indeed be tough, even leading to a year of not feeling the desire to go out. I truly sympathize with you! Some of your symptoms resemble depression, such as loss of interest, thoughts of suicide, lack of hope, and a year-long insomnia. It is strongly recommended that you go to the psychiatric department of a relevant hospital for an examination. [Friendly reminder: The purpose of the examination is to diagnose and intervene as soon as possible, so do not fear the results. Many depression patients are eventually able to overcome it, as depression is not an incurable disease. It may affect you for a period of time, but it will not define your whole life. The label will eventually be torn off, and you will conquer it!] In addition to necessary medication, you can also seek assistance from a professional psychological counselor to address your mental issues. There are various therapeutic approaches in psychological counseling, and one that is particularly effective for depression is mindfulness cognitive therapy. This therapy includes many relaxation exercises which, if practiced consistently, can reduce negative emotions such as depression and anxiety, easing mental tension. However, it also depends on whether this therapy is suitable for you. ※Recommended book: "Mindfulness in Plain English." Apart from mindfulness therapy, there is cognitive therapy that specifically targets irrational beliefs and negative thinking patterns. This therapy can help you eliminate pessimistic and negative beliefs, establishing positive and optimistic ones. Narrative therapy, on the other hand, focuses more on your positive experiences rather than negative ones, helping you discover useful resources and uncover the strength within you that you may have overlooked. Collaborating with a therapist with this orientation often brings about a unique feeling, allowing you to see yourself from a different perspective. Regardless of the therapy approach, it is most important that it is suitable for you! Choose a psychological counselor whose orientation matches your needs and go through this difficult time together! Furthermore, scientific research has proven that regular exercise can also have an antidepressant effect. The support and presence of family and friends are your most important resources and pillars. As long as you don't give up, there is hope. Wishing for your rebirth.

Hello, OP, nice to meet you. Firstly, based on your description, it does seem that you have a tendency towards depression, but I would recommend going to a professional institution for a thorough examination to determine whether it is clinical depression. You can choose to visit a reputable hospital with a psychology department for the examination. Secondly, from what you mentioned, although I don't know the specific experiences you've been through, encountering difficulties in both life and relationships can indeed be a significant blow. In such circumstances, it is not easy for you to actively seek help, but it shows that you still have the courage to face the problems in real life. You are just lacking the correct methods and strategies at the moment. This is a typical manifestation of many people with depression, as prolonged stress and negative emotions make us always think of the worst possible outcomes when contemplating any matters. This leads us to become increasingly confused and hesitant to take action and make decisions, which ultimately traps us in a cycle of negative emotions. Lastly, the feeling of not seeing any hope is largely due to being impacted by certain real-life events, leaving you unsure of how to confront them. At the same time, it indicates a possible lack of psychological abilities and resilience. Therefore, by improving your psychological abilities and resilience, you can address this issue. However, the prerequisite for solving any psychological problems is often to address the current emotional issues first, as emotions greatly affect our motivation for action and personal growth. I hope you can overcome this predicament soon through professional means.

Is there depression? This needs to be diagnosed by a doctor. Depression is accompanied by various physical symptoms and negative thoughts, and it is a complex process. If you feel emotionally down and have long-term insomnia, it is recommended to see a doctor to see if your depressive emotions have generalized. Additionally, this year has been stressful for everyone due to the pandemic, and both work and relationships have not been going smoothly. Many people are going through difficult times and are being affected by the objective circumstances, which can inevitably lead to various social dysfunctions and instability. It can be seen that your overall situation is not good right now, whether it is emotional, interpersonal relationships, or work-related factors. Seeking professional help is necessary. For example, you can seek psychological counseling or seek support through helplines to relieve your stress and adjust your state of mind. In your daily life, you can also spend more time with friends and family, and gradually regain a sense of life with their company. After a period of adjustment, your state will slowly improve, and you will no longer have the current symptoms.

The fast pace of modern society leads to excessive psychological stress. If you don't like going out to socialize, you can try using online platforms for socializing. Chat with online friends and share your life. Utilizing your time at home, you can self-study psychology or learn skills like baking, which can be therapeutic for your mind and soul. Simply obtaining a diagnosis from a hospital cannot truly solve your problems. Is that the outcome you are hoping for, my friend?

question: I am a student and I feel a bit tired. I want to walk alone. What should I do?
description: I don't like the way my parents educate me, and I want to run away from home, but I'm afraid that they will worry.
keywords: Family, family relationships, and communication between parents.

answers.answer_text: Give the main topic a hug. Give communication a try and see if it can be effective. However, it still depends on the specific situation of oneself and one's family to consider whether to come. Maybe some families are not suitable. If possible, everyone should sit down and have a calm and peaceful talk. Express your true thoughts and points of discomfort. Come up with strategies together and make adjustments according to the situation. If communication is difficult, give yourself some time regularly to recharge and replenish energy. Just like a phone, when the battery is low, it will be charged. Take a break for yourself, whether it's a few hours or a whole day, it's up to you. Spend time alone or with friends. Put aside all the worries and don't dwell on the unpleasant places. Just do things you enjoy in your own way. Emotions need regular cleansing. Keeping them inside all the time is not a solution. Give yourself a break and clear the unpleasant emotions. Although your language is limited, I can feel that you must love your parents. That's why, even though you don't like it and want to leave, you still worry about them. Parents' love can be quite burdensome. Sometimes, because they haven't done well in certain aspects themselves, they hope their children won't be the same, so they have strict demands in that area; sometimes, because they have gone through the same experience and found it effective, they pass it on to you; sometimes, it's because there's too much information in this society, and it seems that many educational methods are good and suitable... Therefore, for various reasons, it has become the current situation. In any case, I hope that you can be less tired in the future. Take good care of your emotions. Give yourself some free time without being disturbed by anything. Hugs to you. Best wishes.

question: Graduating from vocational high school, I don't know what I can do in the future, where should I go from here?
description: Second and third-tier cities, graduated from vocational high school, over 18 years old, a girl. Just finished the college entrance examination, it feels like participating in a ceremony, others are participants, while I am a bystander. My grades were never that good, and maybe I can spend some money to attend a vocational college, but it doesn't seem to have much meaning. I want to learn something, but just looking at books gives me a headache. Now I wander around every day, eat and then sleep. I don't know what I can do in the future!

answers.answer_text: Just finished the college entrance examination (gaokao), it feels like participating in a ritual - yes, this ritual signifies that you have become an adult, and you are entering society to strive for your own life. Whether you are a participant or an onlooker, you must continue to move forward with the current of life. You don't know what you can do in the future, which makes you feel lost. This is a normal reaction. Many people at your age have just grown up and started entering society. It is a stage of seeking self-identity. In the process of seeking self-identity, we will have many questions about ourselves and the world, and we also hope to explore further and understand questions like "who am I," "what do I want to do," "where should I go," etc. We hope to find our own life goals, self-worth, and social role positioning. Therefore, it is natural to have questions and confusion. In fact, when you ask the question "where to go," it indicates that you have started to think about these life questions. This is the first step in exploring life, and it is also a stage that requires time and patience to face. If you don't know what to do, you can start by focusing on yourself and getting to know yourself better. Think about it, what are your interests and hobbies? What are you good at? What abilities do you have? What resources do you have? What kind of interpersonal relationships do you have? The most important thing is to figure out what kind of person you want to become. These are all things that you need to think about carefully. These questions about the meaning of life may be difficult to understand all at once. It takes time to slowly sort out and ponder, and they may change with time and different stages of life. But for now, you can imagine what kind of person you want to be in five years, what kind of life you want to live, what you want to achieve. And then, trace back from five years in the future and think about what you should do in order to achieve your goals. You feel that a vocational college is not meaningful, and you get a headache when reading books. Maybe it is because there is nothing in it that attracts you or matches your interests, so you have no motivation to invest in it. If you can sincerely think about the questions raised earlier and clarify your goals and direction, then studying at a vocational college or reading books will be a way and method to achieve your goals, and you will find the motivation to invest in it. It is normal to feel tired and reluctant to study after going through intense studying and the gaokao. At this time, you might as well relax, eat and sleep well, and don't rush to think too much about the future and life matters. Give yourself some time to rest and recharge. When you are fully energized, then think about the questions mentioned above. Maybe you will have different ideas and gain the motivation to move forward. Good luck!

question: My boyfriend said he would introduce me to his parents, but he broke his promise. I feel like he doesn't really like me.
description: My boyfriend and I have been dating for almost two months. He has already met my parents. Last week, he said he wanted to take me to his house to meet his parents. But on the day, he didn't say anything to me. I was confused, so I asked him. He said it was too late and let's just forget about it. Usually, he doesn't really take the initiative to ask me out unless I'm sick and he comes to visit me. It's actually me who initiates plans several times. Honestly, I only think about him and want to see and get close to him because I like him. But why do I feel like he doesn't really like me that much? Last time when I got sick, he took me to the hospital, helped me with registration, getting medicine, and carrying things for me. I feel like he feels more guilty than liking me. Basically, he calls me every day after work, but he just doesn't ask me out. Sometimes when I say I miss him, he comes to my place after work.

answers.answer_text: Hello, when it comes to the question of whether the other person "likes" you in an intimate relationship, it is actually clearer to ask the person involved rather than inquiring with a third party. Based on your limited description, I will analyze the situation briefly for you. "I have been dating my boyfriend for almost two months now, and he has already met my parents. Last week, he said he wanted to take me to his home to meet his parents. But on the day, he didn't say anything to me, and I was confused, so I asked him. He said it was too late and forget it." Two months is not long but not short either, and if there is a suitable opportunity to meet each other's parents, it's possible. However, for a two-month-old relationship (it is unknown whether your relationship started from being strangers to partners or from friends to partners), it is still in the early stages of getting to know each other and being in the passionate phase of romance. Based on your description, this relationship seems unstable and uncertain. The reason he gave you for canceling the plan, "it's too late, forget it," is obviously not a convincing and truthful reason, which is why it triggered a series of suspicions for you. Therefore, let's start from here and suggest that you have an open and honest conversation with your partner, asking him the real reason for suggesting to introduce you to his parents and then changing the plan. Was it just a casual remark or did something happen that made him change his view of the relationship, thus thinking that it is inappropriate to bring you to meet his parents? If you can hear the true reason from him, perhaps you will know the extent of his "liking" for you. If he continues to dodge the question, then you should try to stay calm and not focus too much attention on the intimate relationship. Instead, prioritize your studies, work, career, self-improvement, or finding your own interests and hobbies. "Usually, it seems like he doesn't initiate plans unless I am sick, then he will come to see me. But I have initiated plans several times. To be honest, I only think about him and want to meet and be close to him because I like him. However, why do I feel that he doesn't really like me? Last time when I was sick and went to the hospital, he took me there, helped me register, get medicine, and carry things. I feel like he feels guilty toward me more than he likes me. Basically, he calls me every day after work but never asks me out. Sometimes when I say I miss him, he comes to see me after work." It is evident that your partner is not particularly proactive in the relationship. If it is due to his personality, then it can be understood. But if he is not proactive specifically with you, then you need to communicate with him, express your needs, and hope that he will take the initiative to make plans more frequently and create opportunities to strengthen the relationship, rather than making you feel the burden of sustaining the relationship alone. As for the feeling of "guilt rather than liking" that you mentioned, perhaps it is the root cause of his lack of initiation. The story behind this can only be resolved through the joint efforts of both parties in the intimate relationship. For a passionate relationship that has lasted for two months, there haven't been any significant setbacks. The lack of communication between both parties, as seen from your description, has resulted in a lack of confidence and feelings of insecurity on your part, as the other person lacks the same level of investment and effort in the relationship. I suggest you communicate more with your partner, focusing on specific events and emotions. For example, instead of blaming him with statements like "Why did you change your mind about introducing me to your parents? Why don't you initiate plans with me lately? Do you not like me anymore?", express your feelings and ask questions like, "When you mentioned before about introducing me to your parents and then changed your mind, I felt hurt and upset. Did something happen? Or is there something I'm not doing well enough?" Depending on the situation, regardless of the outcome of the communication, I suggest that you freely express your love and not worry about whether the other person likes you or not. Everyone has different standards and ways of showing affection, but the true sign of a good intimate relationship is the mutual growth and development of both parties. I wish you all the best.

Hello, the questioner, nice to meet you. "My boyfriend said he was willing to meet my parents but broke his promise, making me feel like he doesn't like me enough." Your confusion actually indicates that there are some problems in the way you and your boyfriend interact. From your description, it seems like your boyfriend is relatively introverted and not very proactive in relationships. He doesn't open up his feelings easily, which is different from your expectations. So the comfortable way of getting along for him may not meet your needs. Not meeting your parents seems to have triggered something. There are many possibilities for this incident, such as unexpected issues or realizing it was too late to interrupt, etc. However, you directly concluded that he doesn't like you enough based on your previous emotional experiences. [Ask about the true reason for the cancellation and try to establish a suitable way of communication and interaction.] Humans are creatures that tend to imagine. Everyone may have a different interpretation. It shows how rich our imagination can be. Instead of being overly concerned about meeting the parents, it's better to directly ask him why he canceled the plan last minute. By reaching a conclusion, you can also stop negative thoughts from spreading in your mind. You feel that your boyfriend is not proactive in the relationship, which you see as a sign of not liking you enough. The things he did when you were sick seemed more like a repentance for the relationship in your eyes. Some people tend to be more introverted in dealing with emotions, and two months is not a long time. Perhaps he hasn't realized that he needs to adjust his approach towards you. This requires you to communicate with him, express your thoughts, feelings, and requirements seriously, understand the true meaning behind his actions, and make an effort to establish a way of getting along that suits both of you. Best wishes, a mushroom that hopes for a gentle world and gives herself time to grow freely.

Hello, questioner. When it comes to relationships, there will always be various conflicts and dilemmas, and this is normal. It is clear that you really like your boyfriend. You actively express your feelings and longing for him, and are willing to meet his parents to stabilize this relationship. You need to clarify your boyfriend's situation. He tends to be passive and won't take the initiative, but he won't refuse your requests and is willing to satisfy you. It seems that there is less of a romantic feeling and more of a feeling of an old married couple. You can pay attention to whether he is usually more reserved and does not express his emotions too actively. If he is, then you can take more initiative to warm up the relationship. Or maybe he can't bring you to meet his parents due to some issues, and if you can feel his sincerity, you can give him time to adjust. I believe that day will come. Time is the best way to get to know someone, and for uncertain feelings, there is no rush to have a result. Why not give each other time to deepen understanding and deepen the relationship? First, strengthen yourself, so even if there are any problems with the other person, you still have yourself as a support system. This companionship is firm and warm. Best wishes.

Hello, seeing your description, it seems like you care a lot about your boyfriend. Although your boyfriend hasn't explicitly expressed his dislike for you, his lack of clear affection can make you feel unsettled. Have you ever voiced your thoughts about your boyfriend's feelings and meeting your parents? It might be helpful to understand how your boyfriend typically shows care and love towards people, and if this is also how he expresses his affection. When it comes to the issue of feeling like he doesn't like you, are you seeking a definite answer or are there other needs that can be explored? I am a counseling assistant, and these are some personal thoughts I hope can be a little helpful to you. Lastly, I want to share a message from Teacher Chen: "Having lived in the city for a long time, I am still nostalgic for the tranquility and serenity of the countryside. I enjoy the peaceful time of reading, as well as the exhilarating feeling of sweating on the sports field and the satisfaction of completing a full marathon of over 40 kilometers. However, it is only after traveling to dozens of countries across Asia and Europe, experiencing various exotic cultures, that I realized my home is deep within my soul, the most beautiful and warm sanctuary. Through the exploration of the past and present, and witnessing the diverse realities of life, I have come to understand that one's inner self is the source of motivation in life and the harbor of tranquility."

question: Just starting on the job, struggling with the balance between effort and comfort, what should I do?
description: This is a position that I have worked hard to obtain, but I am a sensitive, insecure, and introverted person with social anxiety. Sometimes I think about sacrificing my entertainment and working until late at night. After all, being a teacher is a particularly demanding job, with little personal time and even after work, it's still work. Especially since I am new to the job and not skilled yet, I have to teach several classes. I have to work hard, read books, participate in competitions, write articles, and improve myself. But my personality determines that I will experience immense pain because I cannot communicate and interact smoothly with people, and I have a poor ability to withstand pressure. I easily break down over trivial matters, and when I encounter setbacks in the process of striving, I have to grit my teeth and move forward. I'm worried that I will eventually develop serious psychological problems. Now, if someone criticizes me for not writing lesson plans well, I lose control of my emotions. On my way home, when I see vehicles and rivers, I also have random thoughts. Sometimes I see friends who have an easy job and have nothing to do after work. They play games, watch dramas, and go shopping. I feel very envious and think that life is short, why don't I try to make myself more relaxed? Just being a decent person without doing anything morally wrong, doing my basic work well, without making efforts to gain any professional titles, being able to eat and dress warmly, and occasionally having a cup of milk tea would be very happy. It's okay to always stay in my comfort zone and keep avoiding challenges. Working hard is too painful, while comfortable life makes me feel guilty. I also fear that I will regret not striving when I was young. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Since you're afraid of future regrets, it's better to work a little harder now. Of course, striving and comfort are not necessarily opposites. For example, in a seven-day week, allowing yourself to work hard for five days and have two days of comfort would be a reasonable arrangement. Having aspirations always leads to fulfillment, and without effort, don't expect to achieve results; growth might also be slower.

Hello, dear questioner! First of all, congratulations on becoming a member of the people's teacher team. In recent years, the country has started to tilt towards education in its policies, expanding the teaching workforce, integrating educational resources, and renovating and rebuilding school buildings. All of these actions indicate the importance the country places on the education cause. A strong youth makes a strong nation, and the country needs talents. The revival of the great Chinese nation requires talents, and education is an important thread in talent cultivation. This thread is pulled by the honorable people's teachers. People's teachers bear such a heavy responsibility, so they not only need to have abundant knowledge and strong professional abilities, but more importantly, they need a healthy mindset. Because as a teacher, you not only impart knowledge to the children, but also give them a healthy and noble soul! The majority of your description is still concerned about the future, which has caused you to feel anxious. This will affect your normal work and life. I will offer you some suggestions from the following aspects: First, as you have just passed the selection process and have entered a regular position, your development path will be different from that of contract teachers. Therefore, you must quickly develop your own career plan and consider the conditions that you did not possess before. This will serve as a reference for your future development. Secondly, you should find ways to quickly relieve your negative emotional symptoms. Self-study relaxation training or deep meditation can quickly alleviate feelings of fear and anxiety. These training methods are not restricted by location and require your persistence in practice to become proficient. Thirdly, you should pay attention to striking a balance between work and leisure, and give yourself appropriate stress relief. You are putting too much pressure on yourself right now, and some of it seems unnecessary. Therefore, you need to learn to unwind and separate your life from work. These are personal suggestions I have for you, and I hope they can be helpful. Thank you!

Hello, OP. The job of a teacher is indeed very busy. Although there are relatively more holidays, most of the holiday time is spent studying. I can understand your current dilemma and pain when you worked so hard to get into this position, only to find that you are not experiencing any joy in your work and not receiving the economic rewards that match your efforts. Here's some encouraging words and a virtual hug for you! In fact, behind every job, there are different struggles. You may envy friends who can go shopping and watch dramas after work, but that is because they endure great interpersonal and economic pressures in the workplace. The difference between the workplace and teaching is that the work of people in the workplace is unstable, and once the company encounters problems, they may face the danger of unemployment. Although teachers have busy work, it is very stable, and their salaries will increase with their seniority. Social status is also highly respected. Everything has its pros and cons. Adjust your mindset, focus on teaching itself, and don't overthink. Believe that you can find your sense of value in the process of teaching! Best wishes!

question: Feeling despair about life, thinking that all efforts are useless and things won't get better in the future?
description: Feel like all the previous efforts were in vain, and can't see any hope for the future. Feel like it will only get harder in the future.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, emotion regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, it seems like you feel there is no hope for the future and that your past efforts have not been effective. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Everyone will encounter difficulties and setbacks in their lives. It is normal to feel that your efforts are hopeless and that the future seems bleak. It is within your right to have a negative outlook on life, but your family and friends encourage you to be positive because having a positive mindset can lead to greater happiness. 2. Sometimes, our emotions in response to an event are not determined by the event itself, but by our own cognition. In other words, how we perceive an event determines its impact on us. If you attribute a failed exam to being dumb, and see it as an unchangeable and uncontrollable factor, it is unlikely that you will perform well on the next exam. However, if you attribute the failure to not working hard enough, and see it as something within your control, you have a better chance of doing better next time. Thus, OP, you can try adopting a more positive attribution mindset when reflecting on past issues, and you may discover something different.

question: How to break out of one's comfort zone to face challenging situations, which often involve avoiding difficulties?
description: I like a comfortable life, reading books, drinking tea, and avoiding difficult and challenging things. I always want to procrastinate and find it difficult to change. I also can't stand it when people around me behave this way, why is that?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, I would like to analyze this issue seriously with you. You mentioned that you enjoy comfort and avoid difficulties, but deep down inside, you seem to not accept comfort and want to change. This creates an internal conflict. If there is no internal conflict, you can simply enjoy this comfortable life without any problem. But you have noticed that not only for yourself, you also project this requirement onto others: to step out of the comfort zone! This tension of confrontation is causing you distress. Why? What should you do? I want to explain the reason from Jung's theory of "individuation." Simply put, "individuation" means becoming a complete, unique self, possessing a sense of sacredness while still maintaining human attributes. In the process of pursuing individuation, we will go through seven different stages, namely protection, differentiation, consolidation, integration, guidance, and transcendence. Each stage can also be subdivided into these seven different levels of functionality. The spiral development of human life takes place in these seven stages and levels. I don't know your age, but I think you must be a person with some life experience because you have a desire for personal growth. Based on your description, my initial judgment is that you are in the protection period. On the one hand, you need this comfortable life to nurture and protect you, but on the other hand, you lack strength in action. During the protection period, our energy is not sufficient, and our sense of self is relatively weak. What we need is to accumulate and replenish our energy, and draw nourishment from the external world. So reading books, drinking tea, and other seemingly useless pastimes are good ways for you to recharge yourself. However, you want to experience more possibilities because you know that you cannot always stay in the protection period. Your life needs to develop, your self needs to be perfected, and that is what we call the drive of "individuation" pushing and inspiring you. You have a vague awareness of this unconscious energy but cannot explain the reasons clearly, which creates a conflicting tension. You are anxious but currently powerless. In this regard, Daoism says to follow the way of nature, let everything take its natural course. The Diamond Sutra also says, "All conditioned things are impermanent - work out your own salvation with diligence." This tells us that we should not only focus on "how to do" but also maintain an attitude of doing "without doing" and being calm in our hearts. Therefore, when we currently lack the ability to step out of the comfort zone and cope with difficulties, we don't need to force ourselves to do so. When you have recharged yourself and have sufficient inner strength, you will naturally have the energy to explore and change. What we need to do is to go along with this development and nurture ourselves in the present moment. The same goes for dealing with other people. Everyone is at different stages of life's development. Some people are deeply influenced by childhood trauma and stay in the protection period for a long time, while others have had a relatively smooth life experience, with broad interests and fast stage development, leading to great achievements. So if we look at it from this perspective, we can be more tolerant and understanding of each person's behavior, without making subjective value judgments or projections. I hope my analysis above can help you. Best wishes!

question: My roommate always likes to buy the same things as me. It makes me feel uncomfortable.
description: My roommate is a good roommate, but she always likes to buy the same things as other people. When she sees a classmate carrying a nice bag, she buys the same style but in a different color. If she thinks a friend's shoes look good, she'll say she wants to buy the same pair. Last time, she used one of my cosmetics and then immediately bought the same one. It's not that her behavior is wrong, it's just that I feel a bit uncomfortable inside. I don't really like using the same things as others, especially when I had it first. But I guess there's nothing wrong with her behavior, it's just me feeling a bit unsettled.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and disputes, roommates and classmates, interpersonal boundaries

answers.answer_text:
1. Firstly, I think your roommate is very interesting. Generally speaking, most people's mentality is similar to yours, trying to avoid buying the same things as others. Everyone wants to be unique, so I think your feelings are very genuine and normal.
2. Occasionally, my close friends and I also buy the same things, which represents a close relationship and mutual confidence.
3. As for your roommate's mindset, we cannot make assumptions without grounds. It might be better to find the right moment to ask her and deepen your understanding. Perhaps you can accept the reasons behind her behavior and become good friends, or maybe you still can't accept it, but you can expand your own tolerance. It is important to respect those who are different from us, and our personality will become more mature.

question: Posting on social media but not chatting with me, why is it that only one person takes the initiative in love?
description: For a long time, he ignored my love. I thought he was busy, but he still had time to play games and post on social media, without considering talking to me.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! You have a boyfriend who is willing to share his life on social media and play games with others, but he doesn't want to chat or spend time with you. You feel exhausted from taking the initiative and giving love, yet you can't seem to leave him. It's a bittersweet feeling, isn't it? Is it really like this? A genuine and wonderful relationship should be about emotional connection and nourishment between two people. Both parties should be willing to give and interact on an equal level. However, it seems that your situation is not like that. But the more important question than why you are the one taking the initiative in this relationship is: If you are unhappy in the relationship, why haven't you left? What needs does this relationship still satisfy for you? There are many reasons why you are the only one making an effort, but are there any reasons on your part? Do you enjoy the feeling of longing for something you can't have? Ask yourself these questions honestly and figure out the real reasons behind the current state of your relationship. If your values don't align or if your partner simply doesn't like your type, then leave this relationship and focus on improving yourself and finding someone who is willing to interact and accompany you. If the issue lies in your communication patterns, such as having too high emotional expectations or being sensitive and controlling due to a lack of love, then learn to adjust your communication style and have an open conversation with your boyfriend. If you are aware that your partner doesn't love you but still refuse to leave the relationship, it indicates that this relationship may still fulfill some of your needs. These needs may be subtle and exist in your subconscious, so you need to explore them and be aware of them in order to make adjustments. Otherwise, these subconscious aspects will continue to be factors in your future relationships. May you love yourself and find someone who truly loves you!

Hello. It's clear that he doesn't respect you when he has time but ignores you. People should be equal, like a balance. When someone takes advantage of your liking for them and belittles you or ignores you, it shows a lack of respect. Some things can be expressed gently, but he chose to hurt you in this way. It's not about knowing oneself, but about rejecting this lack of respect and showing him with your actions that he's nothing special and no one is superior to anyone else. Girls should be brave and not let others harm them just because they like them. Through this incident, you have also come to realize his character. It's not that there are no good options elsewhere, but why would a swan like me choose a toad. You should be happy, respect yourself, and wait for him to apologize before forgiving him. You can take care of yourself, change your mindset, go to different places and make new friends. You can also write down your strengths and weaknesses in a notebook, affirm yourself, so that when others underestimate or disrespect you, you can remain composed and elegant. Everyone has the potential to be outstanding, the key is whether you choose to be. Thank you and keep going, my friend!

Hello, you said that for a long time, that person has been indifferent to you. You thought he was busy, but he has time to play games and post on social media, yet he never thought about chatting with you. So you feel confused and can't understand why there's only one person taking the initiative in love. If you want to hear the truth, I'll be straightforward. First, a relationship should not be one-sided. Whether it's love or marriage, it's about mutual affection and commitment. There shouldn't be only one person making all the effort. When a relationship becomes one-sided, the person taking the initiative needs to seriously reflect on whether this relationship is right for them. Second, self-awareness is important. An ancient saying goes, "He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened." As the person in love, you must have a deep understanding of yourself and the other person. You need to carefully weigh and consider what kind of outcome will result from being together. This evaluation needs to be realistic, or else bitterness will be the result. Third, an intimate relationship is the best place for personal growth. It allows two people to be vulnerable with each other, both tormenting and uplifting each other. If the love doesn't have sweetness and affection, how will you spend decades of life together? Therefore, my suggestion is that if you are certain that the other person is truly indifferent to you and always makes excuses for being too busy, it's better to let go. There are plenty of other options out there. There's no need to hang yourself on a crooked tree in a vast world.

question: Why would an 18-year-old boy want to feel loved?
description: If liking someone is a result of psychological emptiness, then I would start liking someone just because they show a little care towards me. How can I make myself feel loved? My relationship with my family is not good, and I don't have many friends.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand your feelings very well. It is normal to want to feel loved. Maslow proposed a hierarchy of needs theory, from low to high, including physiological needs (such as water and food), safety needs, belongingness needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs. When your lower-level needs are met, you naturally strive for higher-level needs. I think you may currently be at the stage of esteem and love needs. At this stage, you desire respect and love, which includes both receiving love and giving love to others. I believe that in order to receive love from others, you must first love others. In interpersonal relationships, there is a principle of reciprocity. We enjoy being appreciated and liked by others, and we are more likely to feel close to those who like us. The same applies to others. So, I believe that as long as you are able to love and respect others, as well as understand them, you will be more likely to be liked and respected by others. Best wishes.

question: A 22-year-old girl, who thinks about death every day and feels like cutting her wrists when she sees them.
description: Every day I feel very tired, can't sleep well, have frequent dreams, and often use the iron wire on the mask to cut my wrists.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Hugs to you. From your message, I can sense that you are not feeling well. You feel tired, have difficulty sleeping, and resort to self-harm in order to find a sense of existence. I feel really sorry for you. In this situation, I suggest you try to find something to distract your attention, focus on the present moment, and focus on what you are currently doing. Here are a few suggestions: 1. Do things you enjoy, such as picking up hobbies you temporarily put aside due to other things; 2. Try new challenges, like learning a language or playing a musical instrument; 3. Chat with friends, have a meal together, and share your inner confusion; 4. Document your life, write in a diary, take photos, shoot videos, etc., to add a sense of ritual to your life; 5. Share your feelings with your family. Trust that your family will help you solve problems and share your burden. If these suggestions don't change your current situation, please seek help from a mental health professional in a timely manner. Professionals can provide guidance and advice. I hope this helps. Take care! The world and I love you.

question: How to maintain healthy boundaries in interpersonal relationships in daily life?
description: Although we often say that we should carefully manage interpersonal boundaries in life, are interpersonal boundaries objectively existent?

answers.answer_text: Hello, this is a very good question. Yes, interpersonal boundaries exist and they exist within everyone's inner self, it is the awareness of interpersonal boundaries. Every individual has different concepts, different understandings of the world and society, and different awareness of oneself. Therefore, there are different degrees of interpersonal boundaries. Some people have a very clear sense of boundary, while others have a blurry sense of interpersonal boundaries, and so on. Polite and high-quality individuals will do so consciously, without needing to follow assigned tasks or adhere to certain restrictions set by others. Because such individuals have internal rules and a strong sense of boundaries, they will not easily trespass others' boundaries, whether it's physical space or inner psychological space. Interpersonal boundaries are stronger for individuals with strong self-awareness, but not necessarily for all. Interpersonal boundaries, especially in our current society, are very important and necessary. This is because society is developing rapidly, time is precious, and efficiency is paramount. Time is money, time is efficiency. Moreover, with the advent of the internet and increased information exchange, maintaining interpersonal boundaries is even more crucial. As an ancient saying goes, only speak three parts when talking to someone, don't reveal your whole heart. My elders have told me to listen to only half of what others say, guess the other half, and understand half. Never push someone to reveal everything, so as not to provoke their displeasure. Humans are social animals, and the people we come into contact with and those around us vary, but they can generally be divided into: loved ones, relatives, friends, acquaintances, and strangers. Relatives can further be categorized into direct relatives and distant relatives based on legal definitions.

question: Having a fight with girlfriend, she got angry and went to be with another guy?
description: Together with my girlfriend for 8 months, we occasionally argue in our long-distance relationship, but we video chat almost every day. 2 days ago, we were discussing celebrities, and she commented on how Yang Chaoyue wasn't working hard enough, so I jokingly said, "Don't you dare talk about my Chaoyue like that." Then she blocked me and said she hates me for being such a crazy fan. But she knows me well. I'm not into celebrity worship, and it was just a joke. No matter how much I try to comfort or explain, it's useless. She said she wants a boyfriend who doesn't like Yang Chaoyue and thought she was joking. But it turns out, she's serious and there's this guy who always tries to hit on her. I kept apologizing afterwards, but she says she regrets it now and doesn't know how to explain it to that guy. I'm thinking of breaking up. Is love really so fickle? I'm also worried that maybe she cheated on me a long time ago, and this is just an excuse. Both of us are 25 years old and working.

answers.answer_text: Even if two people are angry, they still need to have certain boundaries and principles. Based on the behavior of the other party, I personally suggest that the topic starter seriously consider the relationship between the two of them. Firstly, when two people are together, there will inevitably be conflicts and disagreements. However, a seemingly simple joke reflects many issues. Personally, I feel that the other party's previous behavior was just an excuse for herself. The other party and that guy's relationship should have been unclear for a long time. Moreover, due to the long-distance relationship, we are not very clear about what the other party does every day. Therefore, it is not a coincidence that the other party blocked the topic starter and got together with that guy. Secondly, when the topic starter discovered that his girlfriend was flirting with the other guy, if we consider it from a different perspective, how would the other party react if the topic starter was caught flirting with another girl? Trust and loyalty are the most important aspects of a relationship. We trust each other, so we don't have suspicions about many things. However, after this incident happened, will the topic starter still believe in the other party as before? Moreover, the other party is still thinking about how to explain it to the guy, so why doesn't she give the topic starter a chance? Lastly, we need to think clearly about why two people are together. Because the topic starter and the other party are in a long-distance relationship, it is destined to have many practical problems, such as who would sacrifice their job for the other person, what plans will they have in the future, and so on. If neither of them has considered these issues and it's just a simple love, it means that we are not prepared for many things. So it is better to calm down and think about what we really want. The world and I love you.

Hello~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug~ Forgive me for speaking frankly, but it does sound like the other person is being somewhat casual about the relationship. I think they might really mean to break up. A seemingly harmless joke, no matter how it is explained or how much you try to appease, just won't work. If she really wants to leave, then it is indeed difficult for you. After all, if she wants to go, how can you stop her? If communication hasn't been effective, I suggest you calm down first and wait to see her attitude. Maybe you will have a clearer understanding of your relationship. If this relationship can still continue, I suggest discussing future plans with her, and it's best to end the long-distance situation as soon as possible. Try not to let trivial matters affect the relationship. Actually, it's understandable that you say you want to break up. I hope you re-evaluate this relationship and think carefully before acting. "You can never wake up someone who is pretending to sleep." If she has decided to leave, it might be better to be more free-spirited and separate. That means you might really not be suitable for each other. I don't know if you're still feeling complicated or if you've calmed down a bit, but I want to tell you—don't lose heart, there is still a road ahead. Wishing you all the best~.

Hello, it can be seen that you really like this girlfriend, and you have also made some efforts to maintain your relationship, including apologizing and trying to reconcile. I'm not sure how you used to get along with your girlfriend, but have there been situations where she blocked you after small arguments during your time together? It has been eight months already, and I'm not sure if you have been in a long-distance relationship the whole time. Long-distance relationships can be more complicated because you are not physically together and may lack the daily companionship, which can lead to feelings of exhaustion and loneliness. Your intuition also suggests that your girlfriend may not want to break up just because of a "joke," but there may be more unexpressed feelings behind it. If your girlfriend often shows significant emotional fluctuations and blocks you easily, it can be inferred that she may lack a sense of security and has a personality that is easily influenced by emotions. This "joke" may have just triggered her accumulated insecurity. Especially since you were praising another girl, this may make her feel like she failed in comparison with other women. Her actions of blocking you may be a defense mechanism to avoid feeling hurt and unloved. For you, maintaining a long-distance relationship is indeed not easy, and it is normal to feel betrayed and disrespected. You can take some time when you are calm to think about what you value most about your partner in this relationship. Do the parts you like about her still exist? If you still like her, you can try to sincerely express your feelings and try to improve your relationship. If she does not have the willingness to work together to repair the relationship, it may be time to let go and find a relationship that is more suitable for you. I wish you all the best in your intimate relationships.

Hello, it seems that you are concerned and doubtful about your situation with her. However, this is also an opportunity for both of you to grow. You mentioned that two days ago, you were discussing celebrities and she made a comment about how Yang Chaoyue is not working hard enough. You jokingly said, "You're not allowed to say that about my beloved Chaoyue." However, she took it the wrong way and blocked you, saying she hates "crazy fans" like you. You also mentioned that you were joking and she knows that you are not a fan. So why did it escalate to this point? It's because in a girl's mind, she wants to feel cherished and protected. If she doesn't feel cherished and protected, she might become indifferent or even consider ending the relationship. However, if she feels cherished and protected, she will trust you more and become more intimate with you. When she made the comment about Yang Chaoyue, your response of "You're not allowed to say that about my beloved Chaoyue" made her feel like you were standing up for Yang Chaoyue, like you were on her side. That's why she got upset. If you had said, "Yeah, she's not as good as my beloved," she would have felt cherished. And she would have become more intimate with you and trusted you more. When the relationship between two people becomes closer, what others think doesn't matter. I hope this answer is helpful to you.

OP, hello! In a long-distance relationship like yours, it's possible that you invest more in the emotional aspect. You mentioned that you have video contact almost every day, and your joke didn't really escalate to the point where your girlfriend wants to block and break up with you. Now you're starting to doubt your relationship and the foundation of your feelings is shaky. "Is love really so casual?" I understand your distress and worry.※ Take a step back and think about your relationship, you can communicate with each other. Let everyone cool down for now. During this cooling-off period, you can reflect on your relationship. In this situation, you are the one who got hurt. You also emphasized that you both are 25 and working adults, so it's important to take responsibility for your words and actions. It seems like your girlfriend's action of blocking you has caused you to apologize continuously. She says she regrets it but doesn't know how to explain it to the other guy. It's possible that the other guy's passive response and indecisive attitude also made you feel discouraged.※ Enhance communication and understand the whole story. Trust is the foundation of a relationship, and your girlfriend's actions have caused trust to be broken. You have the right to know the truth of the whole situation, of course, knowing the truth also comes with a price. You can consider whether you can accept it. Secondly, if the other person really cheated on you before, can you still accept it? Can this relationship continue? Have you truly let go or are you just settling because you're reluctant to leave? In a relationship, both parties are equal and independent. You have the right to know the truth and make your own choice. Listen to the voice in your heart and find the answer within. Good luck!

The interaction between your girlfriend and you reminds me of the childhood friendships: if you are in my group, I'll be good to you, if not, then I won't. Do you have a sense of familiarity? Obviously, you and your girlfriend have different understandings of love and different levels of emotional maturity. She is more like a child, someone who is good at using emotional manipulation. If you want to continue this relationship, you may have to treat her like a "child" and guide her towards psychological growth (by influencing, not blaming or trying to change her). Of course, the choice is yours.

The original paragraph is as follows:

The OP mentioned that in the past two years, they don't know what kind of person their girlfriend is. First of all, it is not right for the girlfriend to seek attention from other guys and engage in flirtatious conversations. But have you ever considered that your girlfriend might know you're joking? Also, does your girlfriend have any close friends in that city where she plays with the guy? Instead of asking here, it would be better to have a proper conversation with her. Honestly, I am the type of person who is just like your girlfriend. I am most afraid of long-distance relationships, and I am also afraid that he might misunderstand that I actually love him and have very little sense of security. I am also afraid that he might make jokes, even if they have nothing to do with me or are about celebrities. Both of you need to communicate and understand each other.

Based on your description, it's unclear whether she has lost interest in you a long time ago. However, it is apparent that she is not as into you. The state of your relationship, even though long distance, has become abnormal due to an issue as trivial as being a fan or not. Although she is coming back to you now, it feels like you are more of a backup plan. It's important to think deeply about how she truly feels about you and the state of your relationship. I believe you will find the answer. Keep going, I am here with you.

question: Why do some counselors always have better results than others?
description: Professor Bruce E. Wampold, in his book "The Great Psychotherapy Debate," states, "There is a significant difference in the effectiveness of therapists: some therapists consistently achieve better outcomes than others, whether in clinical experiments or practical cases."
