What causes this difference? What are the characteristics of psychologists who consistently achieve positive counseling outcomes? How do they enhance the effectiveness of counseling?

answers.answer_text: The most important factor in determining the effectiveness of counseling is the counseling relationship, which is heavily influenced by the counselor's personality. If a counselor has a gentle, understanding, and patient personality with strong empathetic skills, they have innate advantages and talents in counseling. Even if they may not be highly skilled in counseling techniques, they can easily navigate the counseling relationship. Over time, the counseling effectiveness will gradually manifest. On the other hand, if a counselor has an impatient and controlling personality, and tends to give advice and directives in a dominant manner, the counseling effectiveness will be poorer. Even if they have excellent counseling skills, their ability to improve the effectiveness of counseling will be limited. Many people who study psychological counseling today have a misconception that they focus too much on techniques, striving to learn techniques everywhere, but neglect the cultivation of their own personality, which is detrimental to their work. In addition to the counselor's effectiveness in counseling, the counseling setup also plays a significant role. If a counselor adheres to principles, remains calm, follows proper counseling procedures, sets counseling goals, and establishes good rapport with clients, the counseling effectiveness will be very evident. Conversely, if the counselor's counseling setup is disorganized, such as frequently changing appointment times or being consistently late, the counseling effectiveness will be particularly poor. As a result, clients may become unsatisfied and ultimately leave. This situation tests the counselor's fundamental skills and their ability to manage the counseling setup. Counselors need to accumulate experience through long-term practice, reflect on their mistakes, and continuously improve themselves. Ultimately, they should strive to reach their optimal state in terms of personality, skills, and all other aspects. Counseling abilities grow and develop through continuous accumulation, and the more experience one has, the better their abilities will be. Combined with the counselor's continuous learning, the effectiveness of counseling can be consistently ensured.

Hello! Your professional question is really specialized. I am not very knowledgeable about Western modern psychology, so I will try to answer from the perspective of Eastern psychology theory. The treatment of psychological problems and mental illnesses is actually not much different from seeking medical treatment for physical problems. No patient and case are completely identical, only similarities exist. Similarly, no doctor's treatment ability and level are exactly the same, just like studying in the same prestigious university and the same class, each student's learning ability and practical skills are also different. Psychological therapists will inevitably have differences in treatment outcomes for different patients, even if it is the same patient. From the perspective of Eastern psychology, there are two main reasons: one is individual habits and the other is causal factors. Each of us has different habits, some people are naturally sensitive to music, some people naturally run faster than others, and some people have amazing memory. This is not solely inherited from parents, so being ahead of others in a certain field of ability does not come solely from postnatal learning, but rather from innate habits. The other reason is causal factors, which is more difficult to explain and can only be metaphorically explained. For example, sometimes we meet someone we don't know, but just by listening to their voice, observing their appearance and behavior, we inexplicably feel a sense of closeness and trust, while at other times we may develop negative feelings towards strangers. This inexplicable feeling comes from postnatal formation of one's worldview and value orientations, as well as harmonization or conflict of causality between individuals. This is a bit mysterious, similar to Western astrology and Eastern zodiac signs. Because the mysteries of human beings and self still remain in a state of exploration, don't they? I hope this answer is helpful to you.

question: Where does emotional indifference begin? How can one restore the past passion?
description: Our marriage has been over two years, and we have a son who is over one year old. Our relationship should have started when I found out I was pregnant, about a month or so. After that, we only had a few times of sexual intercourse, and then it never happened again. It seems that our emotions started to fade around that time. The birth of our child brought us a lot of happiness, but our relationship has problems. We have talked about it and discussed the issue of our sex life, but my wife is not very interested. After that, we never talked about this topic again. We both know that our emotions have faded, but we don't know how to move forward.
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, and sexual life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope the following response will be helpful to you. First, let's summarize the situation you described: ▲ You have been married for over two years and have a child who is over one year old. ▲ After your wife got pregnant, you haven't had any sexual intimacy. ▲ While the child brings happiness to the family, there are problems in the relationship. From a psychological perspective, the issue of sexual intimacy is rooted in the marital relationship. Just like women, wives have the need for intimacy driven by love, but if there are problems in the emotional relationship, they may not be able to fulfill their obligations. Therefore, it is necessary to adjust the sexual intimacy by addressing the emotional relationship. You can consider: ++ Do you love her? How much do you love her? Love is extremely important for a woman, and it is the core issue here. ++ What do you love about her? ++ Do you understand her inner needs? ++ Does she love you the same way?... From the perspective of marital relationships, in Sternberg's triangular theory of love, passion, commitment, and intimacy (sex) are all important. So, what else is there in your marriage? Are all three aspects present? How strong are they? Therefore, when considering adjustments in your marital relationship, it's important to think from multiple angles. Your family dynamic is one of happiness without love, which is attributed to the child. There is happiness but marital unhappiness. This type of family dynamic may not be deeply perceived by a young child, but as they grow older, they will sense that the atmosphere of their parents' relationship is not right or healthy. This can cause certain psychological and emotional harm to the child, leading to a sensitive and insecure personality. It's recommended that you seek specialized counseling for psychological development (such as couples counseling). I am here, and the world and I love you.

question: The person I like finds me annoying and doesn't want to chat with me anymore, which makes me extremely upset. What should I do?
description: We have been talking for over two months without a break. The day before yesterday, I messaged him and he didn't reply. Yesterday, I didn't reach out to him and as a result, our chat history was broken. I asked him if he was annoyed with me, and he said yes. I feel so overwhelmed. I asked him if he could stop bothering me until my entrance exam (I'm in eighth grade). He said it's possible, but does that mean we won't have any contact in the future? No one wants to listen to me talk about this, and I can't find anyone to confide in. I'm really afraid that I can't handle it.
keywords: Emotions, emotional regulation, panic and helplessness, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, in the past two months, you have been in constant contact, which has allowed you to understand each other better. Chatting with him has become a habit for you within these two months, and you have become somewhat dependent on him. At this moment, if he suddenly stops contacting you, it is natural for you to feel upset. You don't know why this is happening, maybe during your time together, he realized that you are not compatible. Or perhaps one day the things you said crossed a line and made him angry. Regardless of the reason, he has stopped contacting you now, and I think you should gradually adjust and return to your own life. If you have good friends, you can confide in them and seek their advice to help ease your mind. Stay strong and work hard, because as long as you are excellent and powerful enough, the things you desire will come to you. Best wishes.

question: How to maintain a long-distance relationship?
description: I often share funny videos with my girlfriend, but because I am really busy with school and also have soccer team training, we talk less. answers.answer_text: When we encounter difficulties in a relationship, perhaps we can look back at how the relationship started, what our expectations were for this relationship, what changes have occurred up until now, and how these changes came about. Of course, these questions require both parties to reflect on and be aware of them. The freshness and passion of love will inevitably calm down at times, so what sustains the relationship and emotions at that point? If it is only reliant on passion, then once the passion fades, the relationship may also come to an end. In intimate relationships, besides passion, there is also closeness and responsibility. The harmonization of two individuals moving towards the same goal is a process of seeking common ground while accepting differences. In long-distance relationships, when faced with all aspects of life, many emotional fluctuations may not be resolved in a timely manner, making it even more necessary for both parties to have a strong foundation, mutual recognition of the relationship, as well as personal independence and maturity. In fact, even in relationships where two people are constantly together, they will also face various challenges. Therefore, it is essential to grow ourselves, improve our communication skills, and work together to strengthen our relationship. This might be the fundamental way.

question: How to overcome the feeling of inferiority caused by one's family background?
description: After studying psychology, I realized that the influence of the family of origin on the individual is truly significant. This feeling of inferiority seems to be ingrained in my bones. How can I overcome the feelings of inferiority caused by my family of origin?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! First, let me give you a big hug. When I saw your question, it really resonated with me. Our upbringing can bring us feelings of inferiority from various aspects, such as poverty, negative family relationships or parent-child relationships, physical defects, and so on. Because of these factors, we feel inferior to others, and thus develop a sense of inferiority. As for overcoming inferiority, I have some suggestions for you. First and foremost, we need to face ourselves and accept who we are. This understanding of ourselves needs to be objective. Only by facing ourselves can we understand our strengths and weaknesses. Nobody is perfect, and accepting our imperfect selves allows us to rationally leverage our strengths and mitigate our weaknesses. In this world, no one is perfect, and it is precisely our imperfections that make us closer to perfection. Distance yourself from sources of harm: Since we are unable to confront external sources of harm, why not choose to distance ourselves from them? I had a strained relationship with my parents since childhood, and when I went to university, I chose a city where they were not present. Because we rarely saw each other, their words and actions no longer had a significant impact on me. Of course, distancing ourselves does not mean being disrespectful to our parents; it means establishing boundaries and understanding our differences, without forcing others to accept or be influenced by us. Consequently, my feelings of inferiority in terms of family relationships have also significantly diminished. Maintain distance from sources of harm. Over time, you will forget about them until they no longer affect you. Live in harmony with your feelings of inferiority: It is undeniable that feelings of inferiority bring negative emotions and impact our studies and daily lives. However, appropriate feelings of inferiority can also motivate us to progress and give us the drive to move forward. Face your feelings of inferiority, don't suppress or resist them. Instead, choose methods you enjoy and consider reasonable to release them. When you are unable to control your emotions, slow down and engage in activities you enjoy. After a few hours, you will find that your feelings of inferiority have disappeared, and you will feel more relaxed. Engage in a dialogue with the "other": When your feelings of inferiority arise, write them on the left side of a paper, and then, in the role of an imaginary observer, write their perspective on the right side. For example: Left: "Why am I so inadequate and incapable?" Right: "Don't underestimate yourself. You are good at writing and drawing, and you treat others kindly... You have many strengths; you just haven't realized them yet." This method will gradually help us establish a more accurate cognitive thinking process. In this world, many people are plagued by feelings of inferiority caused by their upbringing. Some fortunate ones overcome the feelings, while others may struggle with them their whole lives. It might be impossible to completely overcome them, but we can become better every day.

Hello, you're right, the influence of the original family is significant, but it can still be changed. You mentioned feeling inferior due to the influence of your original family, and it seems like this sense of inferiority has become ingrained in your bones. Can I understand it as you believing that "inferiority" is the "culture" of your entire family, passed down from generation to generation until your generation couldn't escape this "vicious circle"? Have you ever analyzed the reasons for this? For example, tracing back to ancestors, you find that the family was facing a crisis at that time and had to "endure humiliation and carry heavy burdens," but in the process of passing down, it was misunderstood as "inferiority," and continued to be passed on in this mistaken way. In other words, it is highly possible that the "inferiority" passed down in your family is not inherited from genes, but closely related to the environment and personal subjectivity at that time. I don't know if you've ever heard this saying - "Man's determination can overcome heaven." In fact, many things can be changed. I think to overcome the sense of inferiority brought by the original family, first, you need to have a clear understanding of yourself, including your strengths and weaknesses, when your strengths may turn into weaknesses, and when you may discover that weaknesses become strengths. After this analysis, you will be able to see yourself clearly. Secondly, you need to make targeted adjustments and practice, especially in situations where you often feel inferior. You need to repeatedly rehearse, and I believe that each rehearsal will make you more confident. Lastly, view "inferiority" correctly. In fact, everyone feels inferior at times because "there are always people better than us, and there are always heavens beyond our reach." No one is perfect, and we can only strive to constantly improve ourselves. I believe that having a moderate sense of inferiority is necessary, but we must not excessively belittle ourselves. As long as we become better than the previous day, we have no need for inferiority, because we are on the path to becoming a better version of ourselves! Keep going! You can do it, believe in yourself!

question: After studying psychology, can one understand and manipulate anyone?
description: Can you understand most people after studying "General Psychology" and "Social Psychology"?

answers.answer_text: Hello! First of all, according to the common understanding of "拿下" (which means "take down" in English), it refers to control, conquest, or surpassing. Secondly, assuming that we understand "大部分人" (which means "most people" in English) as referring to more than 50%, there are currently about 20,000 certified consultants in the domestic statistics, and a population of 1.4 billion in China. So let's assume that the "大部分人" you are referring to is either over 10,000 people in the industry or over 700 million people in society. Furthermore, since you put the book titles in quotation marks, I assume you are referring to the books "普通心理学" (General Psychology) and "社会心理学" (Social Psychology) as separate works, not vertical specialized research in these two fields. ● If "普通心理学" refers to a book, it studies the general principles and mechanisms of psychological processes and behaviors in normal adults. It is a basic introductory discipline that includes the theoretical principles and methods of psychology, psychological processes, psychological states, and personality traits. At the same time, it encompasses the research achievements of various branches of psychology and serves as general knowledge and theoretical foundation for these branches. ● If "社会心理学" refers to a book, it is a branch discipline based on "普通心理学", focusing on the psychological and behavioral processes and changes of individuals and groups in social interactions. In summary, the content includes the individual's influence on society, society's influence on individuals, and the mutual influence between social groups. Other branches at the same level include but are not limited to educational psychology, management psychology, consumer psychology, and criminal psychology. Although we all have the wish to simplify things and hope that limited knowledge can serve a large number of people, "拿下" at least 10,000 people is definitely not something that can be achieved simply by finishing reading these two books, let alone "拿下" over 700 million people. Even if you have read 2,000 books and mastered knowledge in multiple fields horizontally and vertically, it does not directly connect with "拿下别人" (to take others down). Knowledge acquisition is not like memorizing jokes to become a topic of conversation, and possessing a small amount of knowledge is not capital, let alone qualification. If our desire is to conquer others and be respected by them, the first mandatory lesson is personal charm, followed by professional cultivation. Both of these require comprehensive qualities, which means having the ability to attract and influence others through personal character and temperament, as well as constantly overcoming challenges and achieving a high level of expertise in the field we are studying. By continuously expanding our learning in various areas, we can make progress in our professional field and achieve some level of success in "taking others down". Thank you for your question!

Hello dear classmate. I saw your question, why is that? Because when I was young and ignorant, I also fantasized about studying all the books at once and becoming invincible. In fact, I was wrong. For example, when we were young, we memorized everything that needed to be memorized in history books. Even for the college entrance examination, we could form a mental picture of any page we flipped to. Unfortunately, even though we knew that the exam tested the content of the books, we still made mistakes and didn't know how to answer. So, your question is, after studying psychology thoroughly, can we understand everyone? My answer is: no. This is similar to reading many books, but still not being able to solve problems. We may understand a lot of theoretical knowledge, but each person is a unique individual. The book teaches you only theoretical knowledge, which is a commonality. However, each person is different, and the book won't teach you specific solutions. Psychology is a constantly developing discipline, and people always have many questions. The range of psychological issues is also becoming more extensive. What we read is just the tip of the iceberg. I hope this helps you.

First of all, let me tell you straightforwardly that after studying "General Psychology" and "Social Psychology," you cannot understand or control the majority of people, not even yourself. Second, I don't really understand what "understanding or controlling the majority" means. Is it about manipulation, comprehension, or getting along with everyone? Regardless of what it refers to, most people cannot be understood or controlled. As someone who has been familiar with psychology for many years, obtained a Level 2 Psychological Counselor certificate, and read numerous psychology books, I can only say that nowadays, I cannot even understand myself. Sometimes, I still fall into unnecessary worries, make mistakes that I should have avoided, and even shout at my child when they don't listen (although I regret it immediately after). Psychology, in a broad sense, studies the occurrence, development, and laws of mental phenomena. The book "Fundamental Psychology" discusses the basic principles of psychology and the general laws of psychological phenomena. "Social Psychology" is a field that studies the psychological and behavioral changes that occur in individuals and groups during social interactions. It is an interdisciplinary subject that combines sociology and psychology, with two basic orientations: "social psychology of psychology" and "social psychology of sociology." This course is taught in both sociology and psychology. Here, the questioner is referring to the psychological approach to social psychology. As for psychological counseling, as a practical application of psychology, a counselor needs to have the theoretical knowledge of psychology, as well as learn various theoretical schools, counseling tools, techniques, etc. The growth of a psychological counselor takes time and requires a lot of money. If the questioner only wants to use the study of psychology to help understand the world, relationships, and improve their own social and personal life, it is still necessary to learn more about psychology, at least by studying "Developmental Psychology," "Abnormal Psychology," "Psychological Measurement," and "Counseling Psychology." However, even after completing all of these studies, one still cannot understand or control the majority of people. First, many psychological theories are based on induction, but we encounter individuals who may be exceptions to these generalizations. Even the most skilled counselor may encounter cases that they are not suitable for. Second, a person's personality and psychology are not static; they undergo continuous changes. Therefore, studying psychology can help us reconcile with the world and live a more relaxed life, allowing us to be logically consistent. As a counselor, I often struggle between being serene and dispirited, occasionally embodying a positive and progressive attitude towards the world.

Hello friend, actually, many people at the beginning of studying psychology can read minds and even control others, but in reality, it's just a fantasy to pass the time. Because you can never fully achieve it, and importantly, others are not foolish. Learning this science is a process of understanding from knowing, from understanding to comprehending oneself: accepting oneself, accepting life, understanding one's social position, establishing a high level of self-identity, reconciling with oneself. Understanding others: accepting others' emotions, feelings, and being able to empathize with others' experiences, recognizing that everyone grows and can grow, thus creating a better social circle for oneself. Understanding society: recognizing the unpredictability of social changes, understanding the process and significance of social activities. Understanding the world: understanding the world's structure, understanding the laws of nature, realizing that all living beings in the world are equal, thereby establishing and possessing an advanced world view. So, this is the true meaning of psychology, as well as the true meaning of all science. If you want to study this science, you need to understand that it is not used to manipulate or control anyone. After you truly start studying psychology, you will gradually understand. Trust me, this kind of thinking you have is something that almost every person studying psychology has to some extent at the beginning, or even in their professional habits. But everyone eventually understands that the true essence of this science is far more advanced and profound than that, much more, much more, much more! I hope my advice can help you!

Hello! From the question, I guess you are quite young and have only recently come in contact with psychology. First of all, I would like to share my feelings after studying psychology. I started reading books about psychology more than 20 years ago because at that time, I didn't understand why people had to "suffer" in life and why I didn't want to live. I wanted to find answers in books and understand why I felt that way. However, even after more than 20 years, although I have resolved my own issues, I sometimes feel very powerless when I see people who are caught in suicidal thoughts, anxiety, and restlessness. It feels like I am separated from them by a thick, soundproof glass. I try to shout at them to leave that dangerous place, but many times they are indifferent, and I often watch them hurt themselves but I am unable to help. Many times, even if I have acquired knowledge and methods, I find that these methods only work for some people, not everyone. Humans are complex beings, each one unique in the world. How can you analyze each unique individual with the same knowledge, methods, and experience written in books? As for the question itself, when you say "after learning," in the process of studying psychology, you will find that the more you learn, the more you realize the vastness of psychological knowledge, and it is worth continuously learning and exploring through practice. I don't know when "after learning" would be considered finished. As for "handling everyone," I don't know what it means to "handle" people. Is it about controlling them, curing them, or understanding them? I think this is an impossible goal to achieve! Of course, setting a lofty goal is a good choice when studying, so that it can motivate you to continuously strive and persist! Congratulations! Both the world and myself love you! Let's learn together and immerse ourselves in the vast sea of psychological knowledge!

I feel that I cannot understand everyone. Sometimes, even after reading dozens of psychology books, I still may not truly comprehend all the content and be able to understand everyone. If your mindset and beliefs have not changed, your communication with others about psychology will still be based on your old way of thinking. I believe that studying psychology is about gradually transforming our incorrect cognition into correct cognition, gradually improving ourselves, discovering and understanding ourselves, and exploring our own potential. Psychology also has a subtle and gradual influence. It can unconsciously affect a person. If you cannot integrate knowledge into action and do not practice, then although you have knowledge in your mind, you will still be the same. You will only stay at the level of knowing without transitioning from subconscious to conscious. Only through one's own transformation, true awakening, and self-awareness can one truly influence others and use their life to impact others' lives. Continuous learning, gradual accumulation, and continuous improvement are necessary.

The content is very different from the title. It is impossible for anyone to achieve it, especially when you can't conquer yourself. Most people won't be able to either. Because this majority is still a very small part. But no matter what, if he can help you open up this world, it's already very good. Especially in the realm of the mind, you have already entered it, congratulations.

question: How to resolve the internal conflict of being a married 32-year-old bisexual man?
description: In the past, I used to struggle with depression due to my sexual orientation. In the past year, it seems like I have started to doubt myself again, or maybe it's not exactly doubt. I am attracted to both men and women, which creates inner conflicts for me. Especially now that I have a family, I know deep down that I should focus on nurturing my family. However, it is inevitable that I encounter men who stir my emotions in everyday life, and this conflict becomes even more intense when I drink.

answers.answer_text: Recently, this conflicting state must be very difficult, right? Hugs to you! There's no need to be depressed because of your sexual orientation. Liking someone, loving someone is uncontrollable, even if they are the same gender. It's just a natural infatuation, not a dilemma. The root cause is a combination of various factors from society and family that make you feel that it shouldn't be this way. There's also the moral condemnation and guilt towards your wife. They are gradually losing against the game of infatuation. There's nothing wrong with being bisexual, getting married, or encountering a boy you have feelings for. But you have been married for 5 years, isn't it a bit cruel for your wife? After all, you were supposed to spend your whole life together with her. Loyalty is a choice to safeguard love in a marriage. If you really like that guy, get a divorce. Otherwise, cut off these thoughts. If your immediate reaction after reading this is that you can't cut off these thoughts, then communicate with your wife. Say sorry and tell her that you've fallen in love with someone else, instead of silently struggling with conflicts, to the point of infidelity, which would bring a series of troubles. Your wife will also meet other people she has feelings for, but she doesn't tell you when she rejects them. If you feel that the feelings between you both have faded, then have a good conversation. If you still have a deep connection with your wife, I hope you can return to your family. After all, love is between two people, adding one more person will spoil it. I hope you can choose carefully and that this can help you!

Hello: It seems like you have deeply felt the conflict within you and the pain you are experiencing. I understand you, but perhaps things are not as serious as you think. Even if it has been clearly defined, looking at this issue from different perspectives may change your "inner conflict." People's conflicts often come from the inability to accept. Directly addressing the issue: "32-year-old married for 5 years, bisexual man, how to resolve inner conflict?" Being 32 years old and married for 5 years, when people are young, they may not truly understand themselves. Most of the time, they are still naive and exploring. Hello, OP. Reading your description, I can sense the conflict you have regarding your sexual orientation and managing your family life. You are aware that you may be bisexual, but society often views this as a marginalized group, which can lead to biases and prejudice. However, science has shown that sexual orientation is influenced by genetics and other factors. Therefore, whether you are homosexual, heterosexual, or bisexual, these are all natural and existing groups in human society. Firstly, there is no need for self-blame or self-doubt. When it comes to managing your family, the most important thing is loyalty. If you wish to maintain a happy and healthy family, resist any temptations. If the conflict becomes too overwhelming and you decide to betray or end your marriage, it is important to communicate honestly with your wife and seek her forgiveness. Best wishes!

question: Refusing to express one's emotions, suppressing oneself, a confused life? (1)
description: Yesterday was the fourth day of the National Day holiday, and I haven't been home this year. My dad took a half-day drive to come to Shanghai to see me for the first time. I came to Shanghai to work after the Chinese New Year last year. It's still the same old questions. One, why are you so disrespectful to your mom; two, why don't you hang out with your male cousins; three, it's time to find a partner; four, xx city is still better. Looking back, the struggle between my mom and me started when I was old enough to remember things. Whenever I wet my pants, everyone in the village knew that I would get beaten. In first grade, I learned to write the word "death," and I wrote my mom's name next to it. I understood what death meant. I not only wished for her death but also had thoughts of suicide. It was back then that I understood what death was. During my senior year of high school, I made one last attempt to communicate with my mom. I told her at her doorstep that I fainted from low blood sugar during running, my head felt empty, like I was dying. Impatiently, she sent me back home without expressing any concern. Holding back tears, I returned to my room, and since then, I haven't talked to her about anything. Similar incidents happened before. Suddenly having a high fever, I told her I wasn't feeling well, she said I was pretending and ignored me. Soon after, I started vomiting, and my dad took me to the hospital. When I was young, I fantasized about my mom being Zixia from "A Chinese Odyssey," which meant she could transform. When she treated me well, she was Zixia, but when she didn't, she became Hongxia.

answers.answer_text: Hello, encountering challenges and feeling lost in life is something that everyone goes through. Don't worry, you're not alone. Everyone is going through their own journey. As a child, one often wishes for a caring and loving mother. A mother's embrace brings warmth and companionship, as well as a connection of love. However, when a mother hurts, it cuts off this connection harshly. This is the true source of pain. Should one continue to be entangled in the unchangeable past, or should one grow and reclaim their own power and decision-making ability from this experience? First and foremost, it is important to understand that we cannot choose our mother in this lifetime. If we think about it, she is also a pitiful person. As much as she is indifferent towards you, she is equally neglectful towards herself. This indifference stems from never having been valued or cared for in childhood, growing up in a family that is just as cold. She treats you with the same indifference as she treats others because she simply doesn't know what it means to care or express emotions. Letting someone who is completely incapable of caring show you affection would only lead to disappointment. Accepting this lesson from your mother's life, even though her own unfinished growth and breakthroughs affected you, it is still a part of your destiny. You have to decide if you want to be like your mother or break free from these constraints and have control over your own life. When children are deprived of their parents' love and care, they face a survival test. However, now that we have grown up, we are fully capable of providing ourselves with the love and care we need. It's just that the unfulfilled needs and the wounds from childhood don't disappear as we age, and at some point in life, we have to face our inner vulnerability. Accept this vulnerability, acknowledge the loss, and allow yourself to experience various emotional states. For example, if you don't want to forgive your mother right now, then don't. If you don't want to see her, then don't. It's not avoiding the situation, but rather temporarily allowing yourself to feel that way, while also clearing the accumulated negative emotions from your body. Engage in physical activities, do things you enjoy, and allow yourself to express your emotions when needed. Writing down your grievances towards your mother or expressing them verbally can help release your inner feelings. Through continuous self-clearing, your inner peace will grow, and you will be able to accept the states of others. They are all experiencing their own destinies, and the question is whether to let others influence your entire life or to live according to your own desires – the choice is yours. Through this process of clearing, you will continuously gain the power to make choices. I wish you to be true to yourself and return to your inner strength. In this return, you can provide yourself with all the care and love you desire. Whether others care for or hurt you, you will still love yourself. Best wishes.

I feel deeply saddened by the emotional pain and grievances you have experienced in your family. Every family has its own difficulties, and your father's various expectations of you have led to classic questioning from the past. Often, these expectations from parents and elders can also be a form of pressure for oneself. If you find that you have your own opinions, perhaps you can be more courageous in expressing them. Your inner being is filled with feelings of oppression and confusion, which need to be released in a more comfortable way. 

◆ Refusing to express your emotions, suppressing yourself, and living in confusion your whole life 
◆ You haven't been home this year, and your father took a half-day trip to Shanghai to see you
◆ Why do you have such a bad attitude towards your mother? The struggle to suppress and fight started early. 

Recalling the past experiences, you may have encountered various forms of neglect and physical violence. There may be various feelings of resentment towards your mother in your inner being. Communication between the two of you is also scarce, and you can only feel overlooked. Your mother's lack of trust in you may also exacerbate the deterioration of your relationship. 

■■■ Establishing flexible boundaries with your parents and creating a blueprint 
You deserve attention and care. Our original families can be hurtful because parents never express their concern in the way you expect. Instead, there are various "sarcastic remarks, lack of trust, denial, oppression, and urging." Having a closer relationship with parents can not only provide us with more support and security, but is also closely related to good health. 

In the process of "conversing" with your mother in the past, you have already felt strong anger and grievance. Perhaps it is necessary to realize that your mother has some flaws in her personal character, and if she cannot change, then you should try to make your own adjustments. Perhaps many parents are not good with words, so there are often misunderstandings. In fact, you don't have many conflicts of interest. If you are already an adult, you can take more control of your own life. It's just that we have already erected thorns during our defense, and those statements sound more piercing, adding a lot of pressure. 

If your mother cannot provide you with care, perhaps you can seek care from others and take care of yourself. Now we can temporarily adjust our emotions. You can temporarily avoid discussing these matters and topics with your parents, but don't forget: you are in charge of your own life. Our anger, discontent, resentment, and grievances are the pain of longing for desires that cannot be fulfilled. If there are things we currently cannot benefit from, then we should think about how to get what we want. 

Sometimes, the estrangement between us and our parents is simply due to a lack of expression of love. There are various generation gaps and differences in beliefs between parents and children. Perhaps in the past, parents didn't understand you, but maybe we can lower our expectations of parents. You can establish your own life plan through your own efforts, and there are still many things to sort out between your family and yourself. You need to see what kind of life you want for yourself.

Always wanting to be treated gently, but always being ignored and abandoned. After reading the three questions posed by the asker, I thought of this sentence. The asker's problem belongs to the realm of personal growth, but it is complicated by the involvement of their relationship with their adoptive parents and their attitude towards their biological father. The asker seems to be refusing to express themselves, suppressing themselves, and feeling confused, but in reality, this may be a silent protest, a hidden attack through undermining or denying the issues they care about, in order to release the suppressed part of themselves to some extent. However, because this hidden attack also involves their future life and genuine inner needs, they negate their future development trajectory and life while releasing the pressure from their adoptive parents (biological father). This is a typical case of losing more than you gain. After a brief release from suppression, there may be long-term melancholy and emptiness. In the problems mentioned by the asker, it is true that their parents are not concerned about the asker nor pay attention to their issues. They are always immersed in their own world and expect the asker to fulfill their demands, or the behavior of their adoptive parents makes the asker feel less like their child and more like a marionette, being asked to do this and that. Therefore, the asker's refusal to express themselves may be due to the inability to express themselves, not being able to even express to their trusted relatives, and even if they speak up, no one can understand. Who can they confide in then? This may be the source of the asker's suppression. The asker's fantasy about their mom ["When I was little, I fantasized that my mom was Zixia from 'The Monkey King' and she could transform. When she was good to me, she was Zixia; when she was not, she was Hongxia"] is actually a hope that their mom can see them, treat them gently, instead of immersing themselves in their own world. Writing up to this point, I remembered a scene I once saw on a bus. A mother was busy talking to others, and her child in her arms kept scratching and poking her, hoping to divert her attention a little and give it to themselves.

National Day, first of all, I wish you a happy holiday. You haven't been home this year, I hope you can find happiness even when you are alone. Hello, I hope the following answer can help you: From your description, it seems to be a problem of respecting parents and foster care. People who have had similar experiences (being adopted) would feel sorry and sad for you after reading your post. People who haven't had similar experiences can't understand or empathize with you. They may say they understand you, but do they really? Do they truly understand? Because you are a girl, your biological parents may have sent you away for reasons like wanting a son. Being sent away, no matter how old you were at that time, is a deeply traumatic separation! The feudal mindset in China that favors boys over girls has harmed so many girls! A girl who was originally like an angel should have received love, but instead was sent away? Therefore, in your growth, your inner self must have been suppressed and confused. You did not receive the love of your biological parents, and many emotions may not have been allowed to be expressed in your foster parents' home. As a result, over time, you may have developed a refusal to express your own emotions. However, how should we face this? Since our origins cannot be chosen, we cannot choose what kind of parents we are born to, what kind of family we are born into. This sense of powerlessness gives us an innate sense of insecurity, making us sensitive and caring. If we do not receive proper psychological healing and growth during our development, its effects will be long-lasting. We are all ordinary people, perhaps not having a good original family. But we are the original family of the next generation. Therefore, starting from "me," we need to consciously work to "block" intergenerational transmission. For example: ##Continuously learn and grow, become a different person from parents.##In the process of learning and growing, realize some issues that exist in parents and the family.##Recognize the marriage patterns in the family, cut off the bad patterns and prevent their "intergenerational transmission."##Make good use of the limited conditions and resources currently available for growth. In the future, when you have your own family, treat your children well, not like your parents did.##Don't be trapped by your own original family, learn to find your own happiness.##Don't get caught in your own emotional traps, grow, live, and work. In the popular TV drama "An Family" this year, the female protagonist, Fang Sijing, was born in a remote village. Her mother strongly favored boys over girls, and was extremely demanding and selfish, only caring about making money to support the family and buying a house for her younger brother. When she was still in the cradle, she was almost abandoned by her mother and left to die in a deep well, but she was fortunately rescued and raised by her grandfather. Fortunately, she was loved by her grandfather. After being exploited by her mother for many years, she decided to bravely be herself...... Bless you. I am here, the world and I love you.

Hello! OP, seeing your experiences, I feel really sad and want to give you a hug. Throughout our upbringing, we have always longed for care and attention, and I can understand how you feel. In your senior year of high school, when you experienced physical discomfort and told your mom, you were hoping to receive her care, but you didn't get the response you wanted. First of all, as an outsider, I don't know the personality traits or qualities of your parents, so it is not convenient or appropriate for me to judge their series of responses to you. But what I want to say is that maybe due to the limited education of your parents' generation, they don't know how to communicate with their children or how to educate them. There is a certain generation gap between us and our parents. So we should also be able to understand some of their behaviors that we consider unfavorable (like your dad's previous questioning). It's not their fault, as there are differences in their thinking compared to ours. They received limited education back then. Secondly, I want to advise you not to reject expressing your emotions and not to suppress yourself, otherwise, it's easy to develop psychological problems. Looking back at the series of unpleasant experiences you had with your mom since elementary school, have you ever proactively asked your mom why she didn't care about you when you said you were uncomfortable? Why did she think you were pretending when you said you were uncomfortable? I think the alienation that occurred is not solely due to one-sided reasons. OP, you should also reflect on your own behavior (of course, here I don't mean to blame you, I hope you won't misunderstand). Communication is the key to effectively solving problems. Openly talk to your parents about the issues that have been a burden on your heart for many years. Of course, you need to control your emotions, stay calm, and constantly remind yourself (they have different ways of thinking, so understand and stay calm). Life is long, and we will all encounter many unpleasant things, that's unavoidable. But we have to learn to handle these emotions ourselves, don't suppress or avoid them. You can confide in your close friends, go for a run, have a good meal (eating out of sorrow), find a place where no one's around and have a good cry or shout into an open space, etc. OP, you can choose a way to vent based on your own situation, but the prerequisite is not to cause trouble or harm to others. After venting, it's a fresh start, remember to give yourself a big smile. You need to actively tell yourself, "Life is long, what you're experiencing now is just a small part of it, no need to dwell on it too much." Let the past be the past, dwelling on past hardships is only tormenting your present self and causing harm to your future self. Whether you feel comfortable or not depends on a single thought. As long as you don't mind and let go, you will feel relaxed. Focus on the present and consider your future is what we should think about. If you're feeling lost, I suggest you calm down and read books. I used to be easily troubled by emotions or unwanted things, feeling very uncomfortable and aggrieved. But as I read more books, I realized that there's nothing major, it was just that I wasn't letting it go. I've also had many periods of confusion, but whenever I felt lost, I would start by doing the current tasks well. In my spare time, I would keep reading books. Slowly, you will start thinking about the future and won't have time to indulge in random thoughts or be unhappy all the time. So, finally, I want to tell you, regardless of what happens, don't have thoughts of ending your life, make sure to take good care of yourself and learn to cherish yourself (if others don't care about you, care about yourself, be assertive). Communicate and interact with others more often, always wear a smile on your face, and over time, you will become a different person. Believe me hehehehe. Well... in conclusion, I hope my above narrative can console you a little bit, and I look forward to seeing the positive changes in you hehehehe, wishing you well!!!

Hug the original poster: No parents are perfect, and during our growth process, we will inevitably experience various influences from life and family. It is evident that you have a tense relationship with your mother, which can be seen from your comments: throughout your growth process, you have always been greatly influenced by your mother. Your mother's inconsistent attitude towards you, often being very domineering and lacking the appropriate relationship with you, has created a serious estrangement within you. The pain from your original family can sometimes encounter generational curses. If you have the opportunity to understand your mother's childhood experiences, perhaps you will find that she is actually a very pitiful person. The child who is most deeply affected by their parents is usually the one closest to them, regardless of whether your attitude towards your mother is tense or loving. She must have spent a lot of time with you, influencing a large part of your life. However, despite the fact that the original family can have a long-lasting impact on a person's life, there are still ways to change it. It may be helpful to recognize the current situation. You have grown up and can confidently break free from the influence of your parents. At this moment, you are yourself, already a person with independent thinking. Perhaps view your mother as a child who never grew up deep inside. After all, she will also gradually grow old. Let the past be the past. If it is difficult to free yourself from hostile emotions towards your mother, you can also try to seek help from a therapist and find someone to guide you.

Seeing this numbered question and the entire prompt, my heart really aches for you. Hugs and I hope to bring you some warmth. I know the problem is not over yet, this is just a part of it. Let's first review the content of this part, and you can check if it's correct. First, you didn't go home this year, and your dad came to see you yesterday. Second, dad came, but communication wasn't smooth. He doesn't understand you or your situation, which makes you very distressed. Third, mom's emotions have always been unstable, sometimes good and sometimes bad. Fourth, mom is always impatient when you need her. Fifth, you "hate" mom because she has caused you a lot of pain. Since the problem is not over yet, let's analyze and answer it together after reading it later. Don't worry, you are not alone no matter what problem you encounter. No matter if it's someone familiar or unfamiliar, you will always find someone to accompany you. So, don't be afraid.

question: Just started college and feeling lost, not sure what to do with myself. I'm introverted and afraid of making eye contact.
description: I was very confused when I first started college, not knowing what to do, feeling very bored. Moreover, I don't have any old friends in this school, and I am introverted by nature, not good at and not particularly fond of socializing. I am afraid of eye contact and easily feel inferior. Can I seek advice for this kind of problem?
keywords: Growth, personality development, student growth, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: It feels like your expression is more like, is this normal for you? My answer is yes, it's normal! I am just like you, initially an introverted person who doesn't dare to make eye contact with others or engage in social activities. I prefer being alone and find life boring, but I also have to interact with people. This confusion used to make me feel very uncomfortable and miserable. However, I had to face this kind of life and live like a zombie every day. Later, by chance, I started to learn about psychology. I find psychology to be a fascinating subject. It's different from other subjects as there isn't one correct answer; it allows for personal interpretations and understanding, and offers a way to explain the world and things happening around us from our own perspectives. Psychology seems to have given me wings like Dumbo, allowing me to gradually overcome my fears, anxieties, timidity, and insecurities. I learned to adapt to my surroundings and interact with others at my own pace and in my own way. Now, I have become more courageous and can communicate with others, comfortably enjoy my own company, have conversations with others, and observe discussions from a detached perspective. Most importantly, I feel a sense of calmness in my heart. I am no longer panic-stricken, lost, or feel inadequate. I can live life with a carefree attitude. So, I suggest that you also learn some psychology. Focus on the knowledge that you think can help you and gradually, you will understand that this world doesn't have as many limitations as we believe. Most of the limitations come from our own insecurities, sensitivity, fears, and aversions. I hope my answer is helpful to you. You are loved by me and the world.

Hello~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a virtual hug~
The main target audience for psychological counseling is generally healthy individuals or those with psychological problems. It is different from extremely healthy individuals and the main target of psychological treatment. So, facing your current issue, if you have the subjective desire to seek counseling, you are completely capable of participating in it. Feeling confused and unsure while in college is quite normal. However, this state also requires your attention, and you may want to find ways to change this sense of confusion. Feeling inferior and afraid to make eye contact with others may hinder your ability to express your needs and establish good social relationships. From this perspective, seeking appropriate psychological counseling can greatly help you improve this issue. If conditions allow, you can consider seeking counseling. Best wishes~

question: My wife left suddenly without any warning, What should I do if my wife runs away?
description: What should I do if my wife suddenly left without any warning? Ah, all these years of simplicity, I just feel...

answers.answer_text: Give the OP a hug! In this situation, it is false to say that one is not nervous or anxious, but being nervous or anxious does not help to find one's wife. It is possible to consider contacting her family or friends to understand the situation and see if they are aware of it, and then choose to report to the police. However, such a sudden event also serves as a warning to the OP. Why did his wife run away? How did he view and treat her in the marriage? What has she done to the family, and what has the OP done to her? These are questions that the OP needs to deeply reflect on. For her, escaping from this family may be a need in her heart or she may feel extremely repressed, especially when facing the OP. Therefore, the OP really needs to consider the above-mentioned questions. Once these issues are clarified and resolved, the two can sit down calmly and discuss and resolve the issues between them when she comes back. This will make her feel that the  OP cares for her and loves her more, and staying with the OP is safer, more secure, and more comfortable. Then, she won't need to run away anymore and they can peacefully and happily live together.

question: How to deal with a friend who has obsessive-compulsive disorder?
description: She has an exaggerated obsession with cleanliness, not only controlling herself but also constantly pointing out and criticizing others. As a roommate, I don't know how to get along with her.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, roommates, classmates, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, when it comes to people you live with day and night, it may require a compromising attitude, where you need to compromise to some extent while also making yourself comfortable. From your description, it is clear that you are feeling frustrated and helpless about your roommate's strong obsession with cleanliness and the demands she has for both of you. You can try communicating with her first, set some boundaries for living together, and establish a level of cleanliness that is acceptable to both parties. You shouldn't just accommodate and tolerate blindly because you will be the one suffering. For example, you can clean the dorm floor on a rotating basis according to her requirements, but each person should have the freedom to choose how they keep their personal area tidy, such as their desks and beds. Even if it makes her feel uncomfortable or "eye-catching," she needs to overcome it herself. By setting these "three rules," include all the details of your living arrangements because the more detailed the "rules" are, the smoother things will go, and it will help save you a lot of trouble. This is a better approach for both parties involved. When conflicts arise due to cleanliness issues, it is crucial to have some sense of tolerance because changing someone else's established habits is much more difficult than changing your own thoughts and behaviors in the moment. Although you may have established agreements and compromises, conflicts may still arise. In those moments, try to consider the situation from the other person's perspective, which will help you stay calm. For instance, she is addressing the cleanliness of the environment, not targeting you personally. If it were someone else, they might also receive "pointers." Once you recognize this, you will feel much more at ease. When you want to persuade her to be less obsessed with cleanliness, pay attention to your words and attitude. Do not let her feel like you are questioning her lifestyle, instead approach it from a caring standpoint, emphasizing that it will save her time, and so on. This might yield better results. When living under the same roof, everyone has their flaws and quirks. It's important to focus on their good side more and try to develop the relationship in a positive and united direction. This is essential for your friendship and living experience. Best wishes.

question: Do people with depression have particularly fragile hearts?
description: Doesn't a little setback in your heart make you unhappy? Even though it's just a small matter, it will keep lingering in your mind and can't be shaken off.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ It is a common misconception that people with depression are simply emotionally fragile. The causes of depression are complex, and the diagnosis is intricate. The phrase "emotionally fragile" cannot explain it at all, and it is not advisable to label people in this way. Feeling unhappy after a minor setback may be due to being more sensitive in personality or having a weaker ability to cope with adversity. Additionally, occasionally feeling unhappy is normal and does not necessarily indicate depression. It is also common for small things to linger in our minds because the more we try to forget something, the harder it becomes to forget. It is recommended to objectively analyze and evaluate a situation from a cognitive perspective.

question: Life committee member, class monitor borrowed class funds and hasn't returned them? What should I do?
description: I want to talk about something that has been bothering me. I am the class monitor in charge of class funds. Last November, a girl in my dormitory who is also the class president asked me to lend her a few thousand yuan from the class funds. We don't have a good relationship as there are only four of us in the dormitory. However, I readily lent her the money, thinking she would return it quickly. But it has been six months now, and yesterday when I asked her for the money, she just said she remembered but didn't mention when she would repay. Her response seemed reluctant and unwilling. I feel even worse now because our relationship was already not good, and asking her for the money will only make it worse. I feel really upset and don't know what to do.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, conflicts, deception and trust.

answers.answer_text: Hello, in light of the fact that the monitor and the author are roommates in the same dormitory, the author must be afraid that urging too much will worsen the relationship. My suggestion is that the author should not press too much, but also should not refrain from urging completely. If the author feels awkward to ask verbally, it is worth trying to use communication tools such as text messages or WeChat to reduce a significant psychological burden. As for how to urge, my advice is to be straightforward, but refrain from using an aggressive tone, and give the other person some respect and room to retreat. You can express that if there are any difficulties in repaying the money on time, she can directly talk to you. If she is willing to express her true feelings, even if the money hasn't been repaid yet, the author will feel a little better. If the other person is simply evading repayment and the author clearly understands this from her language, then the author hopes to request the help of the class teacher and other dormmates to persuade her together. Finally, as a dormitory committee member, I suggest that the author avoid lending large amounts of money to prevent unnecessary accidents. Perhaps my method may not be acceptable to the author, and I apologize for that. I wish the author a quick resolution to the problem!

OP, hello~~~ From the description given by the OP, I understand that on one hand, the OP hopes to recover the class fund as soon as possible, but on the other hand, they also worry that this may strain their relationship with the other person, which makes them feel confused. Firstly, regarding the borrowed money, several thousand is not a small amount, and more importantly, it belongs to the class fund, which is collective property, not something owned by the OP or the class leader personally. Therefore, the OP should carefully consider and try to avoid using the class fund for personal purposes in the future. As for the class leader, the OP is correct in repeatedly requesting the money to be returned. If ordinary verbal reminders are not effective, we can try involving some authoritative figures, such as a teacher. We can tell the other person that the teacher is planning to use this class fund and needs her to return it as soon as possible and give it to the teacher. Or we can find other reasons to make the class leader realize that this class fund is public property. If the OP finds that the class leader still refuses to return the money, it may be necessary to report it to the teacher as soon as possible, depending on the actual situation. This is not a "betrayal" towards that girl, but rather protection for both the OP and her. After all, everyone is still a student, and matters related to public property should be handled by the teacher. We can communicate this to that girl in advance as well.

Hello, in your post, you mentioned that you have a not-so-good relationship with your roommate and you lent her class fees. In this situation, it might be difficult to recover the money. First, did you openly discuss the class fees and have her write an IOU? If so, this matter can be easily resolved. Secondly, if no IOU was written, you can explain the situation to your class teacher and ask for their help. Additionally, you can have a heart-to-heart conversation with your close friends about this matter. There is always a solution to every problem, so don't lose heart and keep going.

question: 23-year-old male, always wanted to have an older sister who I can confide in and who cares about me.
description: I am quite introverted by nature and I really wish I had a sister who could care for me and take care of me. This desire has been getting stronger and stronger. I have been feeling very down emotionally and have a mediocre relationship with my parents. I really don't know what to do.
keywords: Family, family relationships, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: Yes, questioner. When one's inner strength falters, they long for a source of strength. Now, why do you hope for an older sister instead of a younger one? It's because in your heart, an older sister is someone who can offer support, whereas a younger sister would require you to give support. So, please pay attention to this signal. The term "maturity," in its original meaning, refers to a seed sprouting and growing into a seedling, eventually bearing more seeds. Only mature seeds have the ability to contain the energy of life. As for why you can no longer obtain the strength you desire from your parents, it's because you have grown to a stage where your energy is equal to theirs. You are now like a robust corn stalk and your parents are the gradually withering straw; if you were a lamb frolicking on the ground, then your parents would be elderly sheep with slow footsteps. From now on, tell yourself, "I have grown up, I have matured. Not only do I need to give myself strength, but I also need to give strength to my family." Real men should be strong pillars of support. It is only through such thoughts that there is hope for the future, hope for the family, and honor for the lineage.

question: Life is so difficult and exhausting. There is no one in the world who can truly understand and empathize with me, right?
description: I was born in 1997. After graduation, I started my own business, but due to personal reasons, I mismanaged it and accumulated a lot of debt. I've talked to my family three times and they have given me a total of 30,000 yuan, but there is still the lingering issue of online loans. I originally planned to pay it off slowly with my salary, but unexpected incidents keep happening, like ankle fractures and company policy changes, which have derailed my plans. My family is an ordinary one and there is no one capable enough to help me. I'm afraid to tell my girlfriend because it might lead to a breakup. Recently, her family also wants a house for the wedding. I really can't bear it anymore. I have fewer and fewer friends around me, and my home is no longer a safe haven. I'm starting to fear being at home, afraid of social interaction, and scared that I will see the sun rise the next day. I'm only in my early twenties, how come my dream is simply to be an ordinary person who lives a carefree life in the sunshine? I'm truly exhausted. If I could live to see the first snowfall of the season, I think I would be very happy. Good night, world.
keywords: Emotion, depressed mood, panic and helplessness, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand very well the despair and difficulties you faced in your failed entrepreneurial venture, and I'm also glad that you can honestly express your helplessness. Accepting your failure is the first step to moving forward. How likely is it to easily make a fortune and achieve wealth without any obstacles? Young man, you were born in 1997, at the age of 23, and those years are priceless. Your experiences are rare, and you should know that you are already rich enough and outstanding enough. Take some time to read biographies of famous people, like Jack Ma, and see the journey he has gone through. The snowy winter is beautiful, and the autumn sky is refreshing, they are equally beautiful. Go out, observe, learn, reflect upon yourself, and improve yourself. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many people have been infected and lost their lives; many others have found business opportunities; and many are helping others! As long as we are alive, anything is possible. Cherish the present moment and invest in yourself. Believe that you will stand up again and encounter a better version of yourself.

question: Graduated from a vocational college, feeling like my life is at its lowest point, is there still a possibility to turn things around?
description: I am 25 years old, graduated from a vocational college majoring in accounting. I come from a divorced family and was raised by my aunt. I haven't obtained an accounting certificate. Currently, I work as a waiter. For a long time, I was in a state where I couldn't work in an office and didn't want to be a waiter. I don't like being criticized by my boss and I'm afraid of being fired. It may be related to being harshly criticized by my previous supervisor and being deeply rejected in a romantic relationship. Now I seem to have entered into a dilemma, both psychologically and professionally. Psychologically, I can't let go of the hurt from the past rejection. Professionally, being physically exhausted from being a waiter is secondary. The main issue is that this job doesn't give me a sense of value and self-worth. Working from 9 am to 9 pm doing physical labor makes me only want to rest and I have no interest in studying accounting. This way, I can't change or switch industries. My family says I wasted my education and that I'm useless because I don't choose to do anything. When I was in school, my grades were very poor, and my aunt forced me to study. Slowly I also accepted it and later my academic performance improved. I feel like I am very worthless. I always need someone to push me to make progress. I want to ask how to face the difficulties in life and psychology, and how to find inner peace?
keywords: Occupation, career management, work pressure, work fatigue.

answers.answer_text: At this moment, you may feel the most confused and in pain, and it's also difficult for you. But don't lose faith. At the age of 25, you are still relatively young and can strive in the workplace. This stage is about building a foundation and cultivating your abilities. Income may not be the most important thing. What matters is whether you have set goals in your career at this stage, whether you have a reasonable plan, and what direction you want to take in the future. I have a good friend who had a very clear goal. She aimed to become a civil servant for stability, and it took her five years from the age of 22 to 27 to eventually succeed. During those five years, she worked odd jobs to earn a living and used her spare time to study, dedicating all her energy to the exams. During that time, her monthly income was only a couple thousand yuan. After passing the civil service exam, her income and benefits became much more stable, and she now leads a comfortable life. Therefore, you can also carefully think about what you want to do in the future, whether you want to learn a specific skill and develop yourself, or aim to become a civil servant or work for a government institution for a stable life. All of these require thorough consideration. Once you have figured it out, just work hard to face your life. As long as you make efforts, believe that everything will get better in the future.

Life is like a roller coaster, requiring enough motivation to get us to the top of the mountain. 1. In fact, there have always been people accompanying us throughout the years, and that person is ourselves. For many students, studying is indeed a painful thing, but it is never too late to learn skills. The saying "greatness comes with age" may apply to us. As for why we need others to push us forward, it is because changing ourselves is not an easy task. If there is no external force, we need internal motivation. And which one do we lean towards more? Although we have experienced failures, it doesn't mean that we won't stand up again. It's just that this process requires us to change. The service industry does not require a high level of technicality, and it has high turnover and substituteability. Therefore, we need to slowly find our own value. As long as we don't give up, there is hope in life, because we are our own biggest enemy. 2. Learn to face our own problems. If we have tried our best but have failed, then we can look for the reasons behind our failure. If we haven't even tried our best, then it is deserved to be criticized, after all, we and the boss are mutually beneficial. If we don't do well, we won't be appreciated. Therefore, we should not be afraid of how harsh our own problems might sound, because the person pointing out our problems indeed hopes that we can make some changes. It's like when a person is beyond help, we would tell them: eat whatever you want, and when a person can still be saved, we would tell them: these are the things you can't eat. Time is definitely squeezed out. Since we have a certain foundation, why not get the bartender license first? Don't care too much about other people's evaluations because they don't know what we want. The world and I love you.

Hello! Please allow me, who is much older than you, to give you a hug. I want to tell you that you can do it, you just don't believe in your own strength. You need to learn to believe, that belief is powerful and everyone has unlimited potential. If you are not satisfied with the current situation, can you try harder? I am in a similar situation as you now, if you don't push yourself, you will end up like me, with nothing. Actually, deep down inside, we all have a feeling of unwillingness, but we are often scared away by our own timidness. Although it's said that achievers come from every field, but truly, only through acquiring knowledge can we change ourselves. If you are dissatisfied with your boss, resent your work, or long for an intimate relationship, complaining alone is not enough. Make an effort every day, even a small step. Actually, we are all accustomed to seeking help from the outside world, asking others for advice on what we should do, but even if others' advice is good, it is meaningless if we don't take action. Everything depends on our inner drive. As long as we believe in ourselves, believe that we can do it, and are willing to make an effort, everything will turn out fine. You are still young now, and if you improve yourself at this time, you will break out of your cocoon. The world will become more colorful because of your efforts. Life will also become more meaningful. Come on! Young one, seize the tail of your youth, you are the best!!

question: 20-year-old male, my mother extremely dislikes me using skincare products.
description: When I was very young (around seven or eight years old), whenever I applied face cream or hand cream, she would have a strong reaction. As I grew older, using skincare products became even worse... I received intense disdain from my own mother on this matter... We often end up arguing about these issues. I even wonder if she had some kind of experience that caused such a reaction. I don't think it's wrong for boys to care for their skin; on the contrary, I think it's worth promoting and I take it very seriously myself. I don't want to sneak around as if I'm doing something shameful. Maybe it's not me who has a psychological problem; maybe she should see a mental health specialist. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, give you a warm hug. According to your description, your mother is very opposed to you, as a boy, using skincare products. However, at the same time, Phil wants to remind you that both your thoughts and your mother's thoughts are fine. So your sentence "Is it not me who has a psychological problem, should she go see a psychologist?" actually puts the other person in a state of having a problem that needs to be corrected, just like your mother. In this state, holding on to one's own views will only exacerbate the contradiction and make it difficult to resolve the issue. As for the issue of men using skincare products, traditional beliefs have deeply influenced society. Many people still believe that only girls use makeup and skincare products, and that it's unnecessary and even effeminate for a "tough guy." However, with the deepening of gender equality awareness, just as some people emphasize feminism, there are also people who emphasize men's rights and avoiding biases. One of these rights is that men also have the right to use makeup and skincare products because taking care of oneself is not gender-specific. Therefore, Phil believes that your perspective is valid. Let's talk about your mother's perspective. Your mother's strong aversion to this matter may be due to a combination of reasons. Firstly, when you were young, you used to apply face cream and hand cream to yourself, which may have seemed "outrageous" to your mother. Moreover, not just boys, but most girls of your age would likely be scolded for such behaviors, labeled as "makeup is bad" or "at such a young age, all you care about is dressing up," or even told that "you have good skin, you don't need skincare" or "these products are dangerous, they are medicines, you can't touch them," and so on. This form of education where parents are in control can subtly influence children, making them unable to engage in behaviors that may seem strange to their parents or society, even though those behaviors may not be wrong and may simply be unacceptable to the majority. Secondly, she may have been influenced by the thoughts of the time she grew up in. As the saying goes, there is a generation gap every three years. Sometimes, communication with middle or high school students or even younger children can be quite frustrating, let alone our parents who grew up in a different era. They may not have encountered or even dared to think about many things. So misunderstandings are normal. Maybe skincare products were very precious to your mother's generation, and she may have also been influenced by the idea that men cannot engage in "feminine" behaviors. Or maybe she can't understand why her child would do such a thing and wonders if there is something going on in your mind.
