The specific reasons can only be guessed. -- Resolution strategy -- Expressing your thoughts and opinions is not only beneficial for yourself but also helpful in changing your mother's perspective. There are many things in modern society that require our parents to understand and accept. As children, it is our duty to take on the role of "teacher." Or, to be a little selfish, if our parents can accept these things, we can also avoid a lot of trouble. So don't avoid the topic just because it always leads to unpleasantness. Instead, guide and express your views correctly, just as you said, it is not wrong for boys to take care of their skin. When communicating with your mother, try to remember the reasons for each disagreement. Is it because you simply don't want to bring up the topic, or both sides believe they are right and try to convince each other, or one party's words are too extreme and lead to arguments, or there are incompatible beliefs that are hard to accept? If it happens only once or twice, it may be a coincidence or mishandling, but if it happens frequently, it is more likely that one or both individuals have a problem. So when communicating with your mother, also pay attention to whether you have any problems or instances of excessive behavior. Try to empathize and understand your mother's perspective, rather than just standing in your own shoes. Soft tactics may not be necessary, it's a way to ease the situation, just as you said, there may be something happening to your mother or it may simply be that there is no way to communicate and compromise. In that case, you can use this tactic – using products secretly. Out of sight, out of mind. Naturally, your mother won't look for trouble, but this is a strategy that tends to avoid the problem and ultimately isn't ideal. So Phil doesn't really recommend it. I hope my answer can help you (･ω･)ﾉ.

Hello friend. Personally, I appreciate boys who pay attention to their appearance and are willing to admit that they take care of their skin. One thing that must be emphasized is that skincare is not limited to gender. Anyone can do it as long as they are willing. It is unfair to assume that only girls dress up and only girls wear makeup. The rougher a guy looks, the more attractive he is, these are all stereotypes. The conflict between you and your mother seems to stem from her lack of approval for your skincare routine. This kind of conflict is not uncommon and can be attributed to generational gaps and societal factors. 1. Differences in perception between different generations often lead to conflicts. Skincare is just one example. 2. Society as a whole still holds certain biases when it comes to gender. 3. In your mother's generation, there may be a lack of acceptance not only for men taking care of their skin, but also for women who enjoy dressing up. 4. There's no need to convince someone with a different viewpoint. Stand your ground and accept that she has her own perspective, even if it differs from yours. 5. Your choice to take care of your skin is not wrong, just as your mother's dislike of men taking care of their skin is not wrong. These are simply personal choices. In short, if you like oranges and she prefers apples, there's no problem. However, she shouldn't force you to like apples, and you shouldn't expect her to like oranges. You should continue taking care of your skin if you enjoy it, and she can continue being unhappy if she disagrees. These are individual matters. As for the conflicts and discomfort they may cause, here are some suggestions: 1. Accept the reality that this issue may cause ongoing conflicts between you. 2. It is her opposition and her unhappiness, which is her issue. You can choose to be angry or not let it affect you. It depends on your own decision. Dealing with this kind of conflict with a stranger is simpler, just ignore them and keep your distance. But she is your mother and it's impossible to cut ties completely. When it comes to dealing with conflicts with your loved ones, there are some techniques you can use, such as: 1. When the atmosphere is good, gently discuss gender stereotypes and educate your mother on the topic, but evaluate her receptiveness first. If it will cause greater conflicts, then stop. 2. Talk more about the benefits of men's skincare, such as reducing skin diseases and cancer. Prolonged exposure to sunlight can easily lead to skin problems. Nowadays, air pollution and high population density are more likely to cause skin allergies. Skincare can protect the health of the skin and maintain a clean and comfortable appearance, which is conducive to life, work, and study. It also helps in acquiring more opportunities for development and improves interpersonal relationships. 3. Share skincare experiences with your mother and use your own experiences to help her become more beautiful. Everyone likes to look better. 4. Provide more examples. If there are other male examples around you, talk about them more. If you have gained certain conveniences or avoided certain problems because of skincare, share those experiences with her. Basically, sometimes older people just need to be comforted. Having a confrontation often leads to both parties getting angry. As long as you are sure that this is something you like, then continue doing it. It doesn't matter whether or not others accept it, that's their problem, not yours. I hope the above will be helpful to you. Keep being a clean and beautiful person. Best wishes.

Hello. Maybe your mother prefers boys with rough lines and not so attentive to their appearance, after all, there is an age difference, and the aesthetic and views of men by women from every era will definitely be different. Each generation is limited by the times, you can ask your mother what she used when she was young, what skincare products your grandmother used when she was young, and isn't your era filled with a dazzling array of options? Furthermore, you are probably still a student, and your mother may pay more attention to your personal appearance, whether you want to attract girls' attention, whether it will affect your studies, whether skincare will waste too much time, and other related concerns. And humans tend to project themselves onto others, so if she thinks skincare is "bad behavior," she will definitely worry: others will think the same. She may worry that others will say, "Oh, why did you raise a boy who cares about skincare?" She may also worry about external evaluations like this. Another possibility is that the conflict over skincare issues with her makes parents think thoughts like: the child is rebellious, I have lost control over the child. The child has grown wings and doesn't listen to me anymore... and so on, leading to feelings of disappointment and anger. For children, developing independent awareness and voicing their own opinions is a compulsory lesson. For parents, learning to acknowledge that their child has grown up, gradually letting go, and respecting their child's own choices so that the child can grow according to their own wishes (rather than the parents' expectations) is also a compulsory lesson. If the two sides cannot synchronize, then conflicts will naturally arise. So, you don't need to hide or try to change your parents, and you certainly don't need to change yourself. You just need to change your "pinpoint against the wheat" attitude to "gentle words around the fingers." For example, you can say to your mother, "Who made me not naturally beautiful like you? I have to take good care of my skin to catch up to your good skin and look more like your clean and beautiful child. By the way, my friend said after seeing you the other day, he thought I was so lucky to have inherited your good skin. He had no idea how hard I work every day for that compliment. You see, with my good skin, when you take me out, don't you have more face too? If I let myself go, with acne all over my face, would you still want to go out with me? And hey, how about I get a part-time job and use the money to buy you some gloves or lip balm? I want to thank you for your years of sacrifice and constructive criticism. Take some time to pay attention to mom, share your skincare experience with her, help her choose a lipstick color... Your mother is just a woman, and women naturally require a little thought and sweet talking. Once you sweet talk her, she might happily pay for your next skincare set."

question: 26-year-old male with a 3-year college degree, recovered from a car accident, currently feeling anxious and uncertain about career choices.
description: From a young age, my father exerted some pressure on me. I stayed behind for a few years, obedient, kind-hearted, and worked hard in my studies. I spoke well but struggled with interpersonal relationships and didn't know how to handle them at the time. At the age of 12, I was involved in a deadly car accident. I had just started junior high school and was insisting on transferring to another class because I felt the teacher in that class wasn't good, which now seems ridiculous. I underwent multiple major surgeries in Nanjing and Shanghai, and during that time, I felt that my parents still loved me a lot. They didn't speak ill of me in front of others as they did when I was younger. After a year of recuperation (at that time my arm and leg were broken, my skull hadn't been repaired, and my eye had blood clots), when the Chinese New Year came, I returned home from the basement of Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. I lay in bed every day, unable to move, depressed and insecure, with self-attacking thoughts in my mind. I even contemplated suicide and expressed such ideas to my mother, but all she said was not to think nonsense. Relatives even talked about giving birth to a sister for me, which made me feel abandoned. It was extremely, extremely painful. My father always talked about how good teachers, government officials, and doctors were, so I studied hard and even endured verbal bullying. I worked hard even when I couldn't understand math and physics in the second semester. When I told my father about being bullied, he said they were just passing by and that I should focus on studying. The key was when I was in the eighth grade, I watched my mother's belly gradually grow bigger, and that family ties...
keywords: Family, family relationships, growth process, family control.

answers.answer_text: That kind of family relationship, you can imagine, full of resentment. I worked hard, endured it. I wasn't good at high school math, so I studied hard. My interpersonal relationship was also not good, very poor. I only knew how to study hard. My mother loved me very much. I loved her too when my younger brother was born. I often brought him things to eat. At that time, I often got angry with my mother on weekends. After accumulating emotions for six years, they finally exploded!!! I couldn't study anymore at the end of the first semester of my senior year. I was anxious. Until I met this psychologist, I had counseling once a week and vented my years of suffering. I took medication and finally got through the college entrance examination smoothly and was admitted to a junior college. The head teacher even said that I performed beyond expectations in the exam. In college, I was still troubled by interpersonal relationships. I wanted to be a monitor and change myself. I became one, but there was competition with another talented person in the dormitory and the dormitory relationship was terrible. There were only a few good friends in the class. I worked hard for three years to study professional knowledge, but I had average talent, nothing great. The interpersonal relationship in the class was bad, and I didn't consider things thoroughly, but there was no problem with my character. This is the key point. After graduation, I found a job and worked in my major for one year, it was in the reception department. In a company with three people, I was not valued and I switched jobs to a large company for an internship for a month. When I came back home to rest, I had a consultation session, and it was always with this psychologist, without interruption during the summer and winter vacations in college. She meant to say that I had no self and would never succeed. Outside, I would only end up hitting my head and bleeding. She suggested that I go home and work in a well-known catering industry first, work for a year, and find myself. I felt extremely uncomfortable. After all, she saved me. I resigned, and my supervisor didn't understand it either. In a small city in Northern Jiangsu, what can I do with this major? There is no way, I said. I will settle down for a year first. I went for consultations twice, and after six months, he said that I went from kindergarten to about the second grade, not as outstanding and ambitious as before. Perhaps there was some truth to it. I have another four months before the first year is up, and I started a relationship. After breaking up (after one year), I told him, and he meant that I still didn't have the qualifications or ability to have a relationship. The only goal this year was to be steady as the doctor said, and I was also conflicted during the relationship. I was worried about wasting this year, and the breakup was also suggested by the doctor. I followed through with the relationship for half a year at the time. Two months before the outbreak, I was forced to resign, anxiously looking for a job. I made phone calls for two months in an educational institution, wanting to do sales, just to have a transition period, and then venture out after the Chinese New Year. Due to the epidemic, everything was disrupted. I resigned on March 17th. I originally thought I could find a pharmaceutical representative job, but I didn't succeed. I spent three months anxiously looking for a job, and in the end, my father suggested that I work as a property manager. He said it had prospects. I'm not adapting at all. It has been two months. I'm looking for a job online, and I'm extremely anxious. I'm not confident in working in my major, and the salary is 3500. I have to start from scratch, and it's in another city. Being a pharmaceutical representative is not that easy either. The period of dividends may have passed, but it's still profitable. I thought about selling the house, but I also wanted to take the civil service exam or work in a public institution as a teacher, but they all require full-time commitment, and I only have a junior college degree. Working as a property manager is the first development project in the local area, with development prospects. It only takes three years to earn 5000. But I have to deal with all sorts of trivial matters every day, almost working overtime every day to collect property fees. It feels very uncomfortable. Now I wake up very early every day. I worked hard to read books in college, but now I can't continue. I am very grateful to the psychologist for helping me get through that period of anxiety in my senior year. I also have a pessimistic gene in my bones. Now I just want help in choosing a career. I also asked this question last time, but in the end, the one who can implement the solution is only myself. I request your good advice. God has been very kind to me. I survived a major disaster! But I'm in a lot of pain right now! I'm not here to elicit sympathy. I just want to be a happier ordinary person. I'm sorry to trouble you, teachers.

question: Feeling guilty, I told my friends that I had to work overtime because I wanted some alone time.
description: Wanting to be alone to think and study, friends need company, but feeling guilty when saying to work overtime, is it okay to do this?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friendships, deception and trust, empathy.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I completely understand your feelings and also understand why you chose to do this. However, this approach is not ideal because it is essentially deception. In this situation, you can actually be honest with them and explain that you have been going through some difficult times and just need some time alone. Then, you can agree on a specific time to spend with them later. I believe the other person will understand. Of course, I also understand that you chose to say this because you didn't want to hurt their feelings by ignoring them. You thought that giving them the impression that you didn't want to talk to them might damage your friendship. But lying can lead to many problems. When you lie unintentionally, you might use the same approach in the future. With more lies, your relationship will become very artificial. Moreover, after telling one lie, you will need to tell more lies to cover it up. Also, now you are feeling guilty because of the lie. I truly believe that you didn't mean it and maybe you just didn't know how to express yourself. However, honesty is crucial in a friendship. So next time, be an honest person.

question: I fell in love with him because of one action, and it feels really wonderful.
description: But after getting to know him better, I realized that I didn't like this kind of person at all, he's definitely not what I want. However, I still feel a flutter in my heart for him and want to see him. What is love, is this what love feels like?
keywords: Love, heartbreak, being single, and having a crush.

answers.answer_text: Two options: one is to leave him, give up on him because you don't like him, and continuing the relationship will only lead to disappointment. That wouldn't be good, so it's best to cut losses. The second option is to continue the relationship, getting to know him better. Perhaps your dislike for him will change and you will start to appreciate him more. Even the parts you don't like might turn into something you enjoy. Therefore, without deepening the relationship, it's hard to say if it's suitable or not. You need to understand and further develop the relationship to know how things will turn out. As for how you will choose, it depends on what you value in your heart. Good luck!

question: What should I do as a child if my loved one may have bipolar disorder?
description: In the past few years, there was only a slight tendency towards depression. About three years ago, the condition gradually worsened. At first, it was thought to be influenced by diabetes. In the past few months, strong suicidal tendencies and even a desire to harm others have emerged when angry. When not angry, he is like an ordinary person. Now he believes that he is a failure and thinks that our family does not understand or respect him. As an underage child, I dare not directly force him to seek medical help. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Thank you for your trust and invitation. I understand that as the child of someone who has bipolar disorder, you must be going through a tough time. First, here's a strong handshake for you! In the past few years, there were only slight signs of depression. However, about three years ago, the condition gradually worsened. Initially, it was thought to be a side effect of diabetes, but in recent months, there have been intense suicidal tendencies and even a desire to harm others when experiencing anger. Do you remember the events and reasons that triggered the worsening of their condition? If you remember, it's important to avoid similar triggers in the future. Was the diagnosis of your family member's bipolar disorder confirmed at a local top-tier hospital? If so, the hospital should have prescribed some medications for treatment. Is your family member currently taking the medication as prescribed? When not experiencing anger, they are like any other person. However, now they feel like a failure and believe that their family does not understand or respect them. As an underage child, you may not want to directly force them to seek treatment. What should you do? In this context, when you mentioned that "she feels like a failure," is it because of her condition or due to your family's excessive caution? Or is there another reason? Considering that your family member's condition has been confirmed, but they seem to be struggling to accept the reality, I suggest the following: 1. Try not to show a state of excessive nervousness and caution around them, as it may inadvertently add pressure. 2. Help them normalize their perception and acceptance of their condition, and foster a positive attitude towards treatment. However, be careful not to overly rely on logical reasoning and a "it's for your own good" communication tone. The world and I love you. I wish you all the best.

After reading your confession carefully, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1. What is bipolar disorder? It is a combination of depression and mania. Treating the illness is like raising a tiger, a big tiger will definitely harm people. It is because of years of indulgence in depression that the condition has worsened and directly evolved into bipolar disorder, from self-harm to harm to others and destruction of property. 2. "I dare not force him to seek medical treatment directly, what should I do?" You are still young, even if you force him to seek medical treatment, he won't listen. Therefore, you need to find someone who has authority in front of your father to persuade him. Only then will he be more willing to accept it. Otherwise, in his eyes, you are just a child, your words carry no weight, and he won't be able to accept it. 3. Finally, I want to tell you the most important thing. When crossing the river, the mud Buddha only needs to help himself, not others. You are still young now, the most important thing for you is to study. Make yourself an excellent person. Only then will you have the ability to improve your family situation. Thank you for your question. May all the goodness in the world come to you as scheduled.

OP, hello~~~ I want to give you a warm hug~ I can understand your difficulty very well. If you see that your loved one may be in the current situation, you can try these methods to face or deal with it: record the situations when your loved one loses control of their emotions, you can go online and consult a doctor to understand their advice. When your loved one's emotions are stable, you can find time to communicate with them, chat about their thoughts, understand their feelings, and maybe indirectly mention their own thoughts on losing control of their emotions. At the same time, tell them that it's important to communicate with family members when they feel sad, depressed, or any other negative emotions. You can take your loved one out to relax and do something they are interested in, or take them out for a walk and some food to help relieve their mood. When their emotions are stable, you can talk to them about methods to control or vent their emotions, and you can also indirectly ask their opinion on seeing a psychiatrist. Take care!

question: My mom often hits me, and I'm thinking of using death to escape.
description: I was born into a family that was neither wealthy nor poor. My mother often beat me, sometimes harshly, but sometimes lightly, probably because I was spoiled when I was a child. Whenever my mother raised her hand, I would shrink my head. After beating me, my mother always said it was for my own good. Finally, today, I thought of using death as a way to escape. Of course, I had thought about it before, but I didn't go through with it. I don't know why, but today, after being beaten, I really wanted to die. However, I'm afraid of pain. Although I have gotten used to pain, I still have some fear. I asked on Baidu and Baidu recommended me to come here to ask. I really want to know how to die without pain.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, I can sense that your mother hitting you has become a psychological shadow for you. Your upbringing, family environment, and parents are all things that cannot be changed. Our growth is actually a process of slowly stepping out of these issues. Being hit may be an experience that many children have had. Once, I had a chat with a colleague who talked about her childhood experiences, which were very similar to yours. She said that when she was six or seven years old, she was often hit by her mother. After being hit, she would run outside alone and not want to go back home. She would often think of death. Therefore, it is okay for you to feel unhappy and even have thoughts of death after being hit. Having thoughts does not necessarily mean they will turn into actual actions. Thoughts are just a part of our thinking and do not define who we are. We can allow ourselves to have all kinds of thoughts, even evil, negative, or pessimistic ones. Imagine yourself as a platform and your thoughts as different vehicles. The vehicles come and go, and you can quietly observe these thoughts, but don't let them take you away. Sometimes, after seriously and carefully considering something in our minds, we won't actually do it. So if these thoughts only occur occasionally, don't be afraid. However, if you have strong suicidal thoughts and feel that it is difficult to control these impulses, then it is a good idea to see a psychologist or counselor. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Unable to resign, time drags on, has my depression relapsed?
description: I was diagnosed with moderate depression and severe anxiety last year. After taking medication for more than half a year, I felt my condition stabilize and I decided to stop taking medication in January this year. In August, after graduating, I found a job that I honestly dislike. I have to travel frequently for work, and the people I work with are mostly older. Since I joined, I haven't had many conversations with them, and I'm particularly bothered by the business trips. I asked my parents if I could quit, but they strongly disagreed, saying I'm too pampered to even endure this. So I never brought it up again and every day feels like an eternity. Since I started working, my mood becomes unstable when I'm alone, I cry a lot, and the "voices" in my head often talk to me (the doctor was aware of this when I was diagnosed, and it continued even after I stopped taking medication, but since the "voices" don't have malicious intent, I didn't pay much attention). I often feel like I can't breathe, it's a suffocating feeling, and I constantly think that it would be better if I had never come into this world. But at the same time, another voice in my head warns me not to think that way, that it's because I'm not strong enough that I can't even handle a regular job. Moreover, in the past couple of weeks, I have started experiencing insomnia and early morning awakening. Is it coming back to haunt me again?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, panic and helplessness, fragility and tears.

answers.answer_text: 1. If diagnosed with depression, you can ask the doctor to provide you with a sick leave, so that you can rest at home for a period of time. After resting, observe the changes in your emotions and consider whether you want to return to work for the financial security or if your dislike for the job has reached a point where you no longer want to continue, even without financial security. 2. You are not being too sensitive or unable to persevere, you are actually ill. It is inconsiderate for parents to say such things. Some people can adapt to certain jobs, while others are naturally unable to adapt to a particular job, and sometimes perseverance alone cannot lead to improvement. 3. Only by receiving treatment and recovering can you have a better future. Otherwise, constantly doing a job that worsens your mental and physical condition may provide temporary financial security, but in the long run, it's not worth it. Because compared to a few months or even a year's worth of wages, after recovery, you still have decades of opportunities to earn money, so there's no need to rush. 4. For individuals, necessary stress helps enhance abilities, but excessive stress can only crush a person. So while you are gradually getting better, think about what kind of work won't subject you to excessive stress. However, also remind yourself not to avoid necessary stress. Then write down your thoughts and feelings on this matter when searching for a new job or when returning to work, and discuss them with your superiors. For example: excessive stress - frequent business trips; necessary stress - lower salary, lack of peers in the work environment. Only by recognizing the difference between "excessive stress" and "necessary stress" can you avoid getting ill and avoid becoming the kind of person your parents call "sensitive."

Hug the questioner. I saw that you said you were diagnosed with moderate depression and severe anxiety last year and had a history of taking medication. Slowly, you feel that your emotions and state have stabilized. But in the past half month, you have started to experience insomnia and early awakening, and your mood is relatively low, feeling very uncomfortable. I suspect that it might be a recurrence of depression. Seeing your current state, I also feel very worried. Moderate to severe depression does indeed have a chance of recurrence. I believe that now, more than worrying about whether you have relapsed, you hope that your family and the people around you can understand you and give you care and support. I understand that you feel agitated about business trips, and you are still in the process of recovery. The instability brought about by business trips can indeed affect your mood. Understandment and support from your family are important for you. I believe that you are also working hard to improve your state. You can try the following methods to make yourself feel better: The first method is exercise. Exercise is a good way to regulate emotions. It can increase the levels of norepinephrine and dopamine in our blood. Exercise in a scientific way, paying attention to a few things: aerobic exercise, so as not to overdraw your physical strength; moderate intensity, not too intense, sweating slightly as a standard; frequency can be small but frequent, this is most conducive to your persistence. The second is sunlight exposure. You may think this is a common method. But many people, when depressed, do not want to go out or see the sun. In fact, sunlight can stimulate the pineal gland to secrete melatonin, which is the happy hormone that makes us feel happy, and it has a certain anti-depressant effect. The third is practicing mindfulness meditation. In the process of experiencing depression, you will feel pain and discomfort, feeling that others cannot feel and understand you. I hope you can believe that there are people in this world who understand and accompany you through this difficult time and help you overcome depression.

Hug the OP, the OP should be very young, with a long future ahead, and should consider themselves at the moment. I'm 29 years old this year. After graduating from graduate school, I joined a large company. I also didn't like the job at that time, with high pressure and intensity, completely lacking a personal life. So, in a very bad state, after working for three years, I still quit without any backup plan. After returning to my hometown from a big city, I went for a check-up and was diagnosed with moderate depression. However, I didn't take medication under the doctor's advice because I felt that I had improved by half after leaving the previous work environment. I persisted in exercising and started anew after being unemployed for three months. So don't be afraid, we still have time. What's most important now is ourselves. If we feel that the work environment is indeed affecting us, let's gather the courage to change it. Good luck.

I have finished reading your description. I am more concerned about your connection with the outside world rather than the people in your mind. Why do they come out to find you again? It's simple, it's because you also hope to have someone outside to chat with. I think you also long for a life where you can hang out with a small group of friends, laugh, eat, drink, and go shopping together. If this is the life you desire, then you should take this expectation as a goal and consider if your job can bring you closer to this goal. If not, you may consider quitting, regardless of what your parents say. Of course, there is a crucial point: do you have the habit of saving money? Do you have savings? This is important because it may take some time to find a job that matches the life you desire. Our social circle is too small, sometimes we confine our hearts to become smaller and smaller, but deep down, we still yearn for some communication. As an individual, it is necessary to maintain a mutually ventilating state between the inner self and the outside world, allowing emotions and feelings to flow out, while allowing positive influences from the outside to come in, maintaining a state of circulation, which is extremely important. It can be said that all psychological problems are communication problems. If you can live the life that your inner self expects, then you will feel a sense of joy in your heart. We are all striving to live in that direction. Even the people in your mind also have a beautiful expectation.

question: I have filed for bankruptcy four times already. When I have money, I live a luxurious life, but only start reflecting when I run out of money.
description: I'm 28 years old. I was born in a rural area. My family is poor. Because I knew I was poor before, I was very frugal with my expenses. I also led a simple life in college. Because of my simplicity, my financial situation has always been stable, and I even managed to save some money. But after graduating from college, I had good luck and made a lot of money through entrepreneurship. I started to indulge myself, experiencing things I had never experienced before, such as taking beautiful girls on vacations abroad, eating fancy meals, buying luxury goods, engaging in high-risk investments, and relaxing my guard against friends who were after my money. I also spent a lot of money in nightclubs and entertainment apps. I took long vacations, stopped making money, stopped striving for progress, and became arrogant. I became so foolish that I even hated myself. And then I went bankrupt. At first, I was in despair. But then I became eager to learn, ambitious, humble, and hardworking, and I managed to make a lot of money again, which I believed would last for a long time. And then I started to relax slowly. This cycle of bankruptcy has happened four times. The reasons for bankruptcy are different each time, but overall they are the same as the reasons mentioned above. Luckily, I am young and intelligent, and I have managed to get back on my feet each time I went bankrupt. However, it's strange that the suffering after each bankruptcy, as well as the hardships I endured when I had no money, sometimes forced me to meet more useful people and try new things in life. But I am still afraid of stumbling in the future. Where did I go wrong? Do you have any life advice for me?
keywords: Growth, improved personality, character traits, self-development.

answers.answer_text: The easier things come to us, the less likely we are to cherish them. When I was young, my family conditions were poor, and I had to stretch every cent as much as possible. I endured a lot of hardships and received many disapproving glances. Later on, I had some opportunities and earned quite a bit of money. I entered circles that I never dared to dream of before and indulged in what is considered high-end consumption. At that time, the only feeling I had was that having money truly allows one to do whatever they want. Thus, I began a life of indulgence. Under the influence of various temptations, I started losing myself. However, money always runs out eventually. After we ran out of money, the people around us would leave because they knew we were no longer valuable. But fate has been kind to me, and every time I fail, I manage to rise again. However, it seems that I have fallen into a cycle where, once I earn enough to meet my expectations, I go back to living the same way, and once the money is gone, I figure out ways to earn it again. It's just like getting drunk when there's wine available today without thinking about tomorrow. There is no clear goal or ambition, and most of the time, we just settle for what is in front of us. Living in a state of constant indulgence is one kind of life, while trying new things is also a part of life. Each time we stumble and fall, we will surely gain different experiences. We just need to understand the meaning of our own lives and leave ourselves a way out, as Lady Luck won't always favor us. Therefore, we can start by improving our parents' living environment and saving up some retirement money for them. We can also invest in several properties for ourselves, even though property is not meant to be speculated on, it at least serves as an asset and provides us with some security. Additionally, we can explore different lifestyles, meet exceptional people, observe their lives, and see if we are interested in trying something new. Moreover, we should pay attention to our health, as health is something that no amount of money can buy, and excessive indulgence can be detrimental to our well-being. The world loves you, and so do I.

Instant pleasure seekers who relish in the comfort of being moderately wealthy are often faced with the reality that fast wealth also vanishes quickly. This is particularly true for young people who do not take earning money seriously. When faced with the poverty-stricken rural life from before, they start seeking revengeful enjoyment as a way to compensate for their past shortcomings. All problems stem from emotional issues. In the past, life in rural areas was barren and isolated, as if one's life was slowly crawling in a sleeping elevator. But once they enter university and step out into the world, it rushes at them like a roller coaster, with inevitable ups and downs. You also realize that one cannot constantly sleep or be on a roller coaster, but must return to a normal track. Within your heart, there is a yearning for emotions, an emptiness that desires to be filled. When the winds of success blow, you soar high, eager to prove yourself; but when the winds subside, you fall flat on the ground. Luckily, you understand this, so your fighting spirit remains, and opportunities abound. Entrepreneurship is a skill, a capability. Life will progress steadily through cycles of gain and loss, rise and fall. At the same time, extravagance will not be envied by others. Like you said, it is something to be despised, as it represents a superficial lifestyle. People are born weak and strive towards strength, without the need to prove themselves to anyone.

question: Introverted, gentle, and outgoing, how can one resolve internal conflicts (personality conflicts)?
description: 1. Quiet and outgoing. Based on the perspective of others, I can summarize it as follows: I can make some harmless jokes, have many ideas, relatively lively, a bit childish, sometimes a bit carefree but not negligent when I need to be serious. It's like the state of a young girl, good-tempered and easygoing, but internally resilient. I am easygoing but not easily bullied. Based on my self-understanding, I often reflect and am very rational. I am indeed internally resilient and have a strong sense of self-protection. My easygoing nature towards many people is a kind of slightly indifferent easiness. Occasionally being carefree is a way to lower others' expectations of me and make myself feel more relaxed without too much burden. Being outgoing is actually something I learned and evolved from imitating others, because I used to be more introverted when I was young, and many people around me (such as my parents) hoped that I could be lively, cheerful, and open. In conclusion, from the inside out, it is "soft-hard-soft". 2. Quiet, gentle, and good-tempered. After going to college, some things happened (interpersonal relationships and subjects I didn't like or excel in) that forced me to become more gentle from the inside out and accept myself. At that time, it was an immature gentleness. On one hand, I would compromise myself to avoid conflicts, and on the other hand, I had to be gentle with myself to reconcile with the many things I couldn't achieve. Then, I went through a particularly difficult period.
keywords: Growth, improved character, personality traits, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: I am also someone who appears gentle and harmless on the outside but is strong-willed on the inside, so many people who meet me for the first time think that I am a soft girl. Because I am gentle in my dealings with others, some people think that I am easy to bully. For example, when I am angry, I will seriously reason with the other person without obvious emotions in my tone. However, my friends think that I am weak. It seems that in the eyes of most people, if you have been wronged or hurt, you have to shout loudly or show intense emotions in order to appear powerful and strong. Actually, in my opinion, the situation is not bad enough to make me lose control of my emotions. Being gentle is because I still have the strength to control the situation. The OP is gentle when dealing with others because they are kind and considerate of the people around them. However, because they always consider others before themselves, their feelings are suppressed, and they feel aggrieved. The OP is not good at expressing themselves, and because their repressed emotions are not released, they doubt their gentleness and feel that they are a bit hypocritical and unreal. I suggest that the OP learns to bravely express themselves, not be afraid of rejection. If the people around you are always immature and constantly demand that you sacrifice yourself, I suggest that you keep your distance from them and learn to refuse unreasonable demands. Not a professional in psychology, just providing advice from a personal perspective, I hope the OP can be happy being themselves.

question: Is it normal for the mind to constantly think about things 24 hours a day?
description: Hello, I would like to ask a question. Since I was young, my mind has been constantly thinking 24 hours a day. The content of my thoughts is all over the place, such as creating a TV series or animation in my head when I couldn't watch TV as a child. As I grew older, I wasn't as interested in watching TV, but it seems like my mind can't tolerate a second of leisure. It's like playing a movie in my mind without realizing it, sometimes thinking about scenes I've seen on the street, sometimes thinking about things others have said before, sometimes thinking about TV drama plots I've seen, sometimes recalling melodies of songs, and everything is naturally and involuntarily. There is never a moment of emptiness in my mind, even when I'm running or eating, I'm still thinking, and even when I'm listening to someone speak, I'm still thinking. I can't stop my thoughts for a second. But usually, after I finish thinking in one second, I immediately forget what I thought about in the previous second. Can you please tell me if this is normal? Does it have any negative effects on me?

answers.answer_text: Hey there, it seems like you've been stuck in a state of constant overthinking and can't control your racing thoughts. I can tell it's really bothering you. From the moment we wake up in the morning, countless decisions flood our minds. It starts with choosing what to wear, then moves on to deciding what to have for breakfast once we step outside. Throughout the day, our brains have to process thousands of decisions, some challenging and some simple. It's inevitable that this abundance of decisions can disrupt our judgment and lead to making mistakes. Based on your description, "since I was little, my mind has been constantly thinking nonstop," perhaps when you were younger, you could enjoy the company of these wild thoughts. But as you've grown up, you can no longer ignore this state. My guess is that maybe you're exposed to too much and too much varied information every day, causing your brain to process a lot of information, which can easily lead to overload. I suggest you try to focus your attention and control the amount of information you receive in your daily life. If you feel that this situation has already begun to affect your normal life, perhaps you should seek medical attention promptly.

question: If you had one chance, what would you most like to say to the boy who blocked you?
description: A colleague introduced me to a potential blind date at the beginning of the year. Initially, we had good conversations on WeChat and he would actively reach out to chat with me every day. When we eventually met in person, he seemed to have a good impression of me and actively sought out conversations. I also made the effort to initiate meetings with him. However, as we spent more time together, I realized that we had different interests and he started to become increasingly distant. He would ignore my messages as if he didn't see them. When I confronted him in person, he said, "You seem different in real life compared to how you are on WeChat. You're easier to get along with in person." Later on, our WeChat conversations started to have more differences in opinions, but I didn't think it crossed any boundaries. However, he would often say, "Is this interesting to you?" but I was just expressing my own thoughts and never said that it was about being right or wrong. I was just sharing my perspective. Then he accused me of arguing. Later on, on WeChat, he started to make more negative comments about me, such as "You don't act like a girl. 95% of guys wouldn't be able to handle someone like you." This made me doubt myself for a period of time. During our last meeting, I suggested that we could still be friends, and he agreed, but he continued to ignore me on WeChat. I got angry and bombarded him with messages on WeChat (now I realize that I was being foolish). After a few days, I found out that he had deleted me. I used the "Add Friend" feature on WeChat to message him, but after just a few sentences, he blocked me. I'm still single in my 20s and don't know how to handle relationship issues.
keywords: Love, dependency, attachment, getting back an ex, arguing.

answers.answer_text: Hug the original poster! Going through such things can really be troubling! From your description, it's clear that your conversations were not on the same wavelength. In fact, if two people have different interests and values, it's not suitable for them to be together. Moreover, when he becomes more and more indifferent towards you, you should understand that as adults, many things don't need to be spelled out. As long as he cares about you, he will message you, regardless of how busy he is. He always says, "Is this interesting?" If it were me, I wouldn't feel good hearing that, as if talking to me is a bother. And he even said you don't look like a girl? It's really infuriating! No matter who it is, no one should receive such comments! It's really tough for the original poster to encounter someone like this! And you even fell into self-doubt. Actually, there's no need to care about being blocked. Pay more attention to your own emotions. Since he doesn't want to have any contact with you anymore, don't waste your time on him. Why be friends with someone who belittles you? Everyone has dignity, and dignity is not meant to be trampled on by others! Friends should encourage you when you're down and silently applaud you when you succeed. The original poster also felt a bit foolish for messaging him later, which shows that you don't want to do that either and it makes you appear undignified. Don't dwell on unhappy things like this anymore! You will meet better people! Hope this can help you.

question: Why doesn't he love me??? I can't forget him at all, what should I do?
description: I am an ordinary, extremely ordinary girl, very average with no particular interests or talents. I also don't have a good figure or appearance. But the boy I like is very outstanding. He can do everything, sing, dance, and his grades are also good. Many girls like him, and he also likes a very outstanding and elegant girl. However, they haven't confirmed their relationship yet. Every day, I secretly send him some random messages, but he never replies. He even seems a little disgusted. Later on, I slowly understood and slowly accepted that this love will never belong to me. But who can help me? I just can't forget about him, I can't forget. I still pay attention to his every move, and sometimes when he says something similar to what I said, I imagine for a moment that he has liked me too, only to find out later that he sent it to that girl. It turns out that sometimes that girl has similar thoughts to mine, but she is more confident, beautiful, and talented. She holds many positions in school. I also envy and resent her. I know that this kind of feeling is not right. How do I completely forget about all of this and start over? Why do I always fantasize and overthink?

answers.answer_text: Hello, little sister: You said you are an ordinary and unremarkable girl who has developed a crush on a male classmate who excels in every aspect. In your eyes, he is someone worth admiring and liking, like an idol who makes your heart flutter and you hold affection for. First of all, I believe that you have the right to like beautiful things, including the wonderful emotions you have for him. There is nothing wrong with that. You said you tried to communicate with him, but he did not respond and even seemed disgusted, which made you very sad because your feelings were not reciprocated, and that can be really painful. You love him, but he doesn't love you back. This kind of situation is a kind of despair for anyone who pursues beautiful things. In this vast world, with so many people, it is heart-wrenching when we can't have what we desire! You said there is another girl who is confident and talented and this makes you jealous. Yes, it is natural to feel jealous and envious of her because in your eyes, she seems to be more excellent than you. Jealousy is not a crime! So, you start blaming yourself and listing all your flaws, even hating yourself for not being the person he likes. If there were magic in the world, I think we all would want to transform into the ideal image of our loved ones, becoming their princess. I am contemplating a question: If there really were magic in the world that could make us become the ideal and beautiful person, just like the talented girl you mentioned, then where would you be? Even if you became someone else, would the guy you like still like "you"? So, what would "you" do? Where would you go? In reality, there is no magic, and it is impossible for you to become her because your existence is unique and irreplaceable! You are someone who can't be substituted! You are the one and only daughter in your parents' eyes, and the unique you in the eyes of your friends. The Creator is always fair, even though you may think there are many things wrong with you, there will also be different aspects about you, such as realizing that there is something wrong with your emotions. I believe that deep inside, you are a wise and kind-hearted girl. Love's yearning has just made you lose yourself a bit! Because love always makes people lose themselves, that's love! However, what really seems to be making you suffer is your lack of self-confidence, and deep down, you don't seem to like yourself very much. Let me ask you this: if we don't even like ourselves, then who else will like us? "Every person who comes into our lives is here to help us!" Just like that girl, she stimulates you, just like looking at yourself in the mirror, revealing your insecure self and causing you to feel frustrated! I believe that you, being intelligent, can understand what I mean: yes, change! You can also become self-confident because I imagine you have the courage to do so. You are able to courageously admit your flaws and have the courage to change yourself. When you become confident, you will discover your own beauty because that radiates personal charisma. Seize this opportunity to change yourself, get to know yourself, and embrace yourself. "I love myself, and I believe more people will come to love me because I am worthy of love." These few sentences are for you. I sincerely hope that you, this ordinary girl, will bloom your own beauty soon.

I saw a girl struggling in unrequited love. My heart aches for you, sending you a hug~ True love is when both parties have mutual feelings and understanding for each other. But what are the chances of encountering such a perfect love? Most of the time, we have to face and endure the pain of loving someone who doesn't love us back. When we develop feelings for someone, there is often a halo effect, as if that person has stars in their eyes and a sun shining on them. Maybe they are truly exceptional, or maybe it's an exaggerated perception caused by the halo effect. Similarly, the seemingly ordinary and unremarkable version of yourself that you mentioned, is that the real you? Our self-perception is highly subjective. Some people are confident, some are narcissistic, some are excessively self-deprecating, and some have a balanced self-assessment. In your case of unrequited love, it is clear that you underestimate yourself and overestimate the other person. The reality is, you like them but they don't like you back. How can you retract your feelings? It's painful. Love is a very emotional matter, it's not a decision we can rationalize and retract. You mentioned that you often fantasize, like trying to find evidence that they might also like you based on subtle clues. This shows that you are a emotionally sensitive and imaginative girl. It's a characteristic of your personality. It's a double-edged sword. If you can balance your fantasies with realistic considerations, then there's no need for you to deliberately avoid or change anything. But if you are constantly indulging in fantasies, to the point where you lose control of your actions, it will only bring you more harm. In that case, you need some support and help in grounding yourself in reality. It's truly an energy-consuming process. But if you can find balance between fantasy and reality, and learn to see both yourself and the other person without the halo effect, then you will have grown a lot. Growth has never been easy, don't you think? Keep going, and best wishes~.

Hello, first of all, the way we perceive ourselves and others is often different. When looking at ourselves, we often have a critical attitude and judgmental eyes, only focusing on our own flaws and shortcomings. However, when looking at others, we tend to have an appreciative attitude and see their strengths. Comparing their strengths to our own shortcomings can lead to self-doubt and feeling inadequate. You may think that the boy you like and the girl he likes are both excellent, while you consider yourself ordinary and lacking interests, hobbies, and talent, as well as having a bad figure and appearance. This is clearly self-negation. Perhaps, in the eyes of others, you are not like that at all. There was a small experiment conducted by an artist. He invited some people to participate and asked them to describe their own appearance. Based on their descriptions, he painted portraits without seeing them. Then, he asked another group of people to describe the appearance of the first group, and he painted their portraits based on those descriptions. The portraits painted by the same subject, based on their own description, are often less attractive compared to the portraits based on the descriptions of others, as their own descriptions tend to emphasize their flaws. This experiment was made into a video called "You are more beautiful than you think"; you can take a look at it. It's not that you're not good enough, it's just that you haven't seen your own beauty. Our liking or disliking someone is not solely based on whether they are excellent or not, but on many factors. If this guy doesn't like you, it's not because you're not outstanding, but maybe he just feels that you're not compatible with him. So, don't underestimate yourself. If you envy and admire that girl, you can also strive to improve yourself and become the person you admire. If you can't forget for now, just let it be. The more you try to forget, the harder it becomes. Just let things take their natural course. He can also become a motivation for you to strive harder. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Hello, OP. As long as you are willing, there may still be a possibility between you two. However, since you have already seen the excellence in the other person and the plainness in yourself, instead of fantasizing every day and focusing on their every move, it would be better to spend time on yourself, become better and more wonderful. Develop hobbies, maintain a healthy weight, read books, explore the world, both internally and externally, and gradually become worthy of their goodness. Otherwise, even if you do end up together one day, your self-doubt will become a killer for your relationship. In other words, relationships also depend on compatibility and finding a worthy opponent. Relationships with too much disparity often result in bitter love. To obtain a high-quality love, you must first learn to be stable in your emotions and enjoy your own company, and have a love for life. When the time is right, your unique charm will naturally attract them. I wish you happiness.

Hello OP, I think it's common for us to develop such beautiful feelings during our student days, often thinking about and paying attention to every move of the person we like, fantasizing about whether they like us back. This is a normal kind of sentiment. The guy you like is excellent, good at everything, and has good grades. However, he likes a girl who is very outstanding and has a great personality. In comparison, you probably feel very ordinary. But in fact, you are not ordinary at all, and self-confidence is a skill that no one is born with. My advice is: turn your liking into the motivation to become better. We should realize that this guy never replies to your messages, and may even feel a bit annoyed. At this point, we should give ourselves a signal to stop sending him messages, otherwise, it will backfire, isn't it? I suggest that you focus on yourself and make efforts. You may become an even better person than him. When you live a fulfilling and confident life, you will attract people with the same qualities as you and gain a high-quality love.

question: In the first year of high school, sitting in the front row and being too close to the teacher makes me feel very uncomfortable. What should I do?
description: I am in the first year of high school. Recently, I have been sitting in the front row, right next to the blackboard. I am a relatively shy person. Sitting in the front row makes me very uncomfortable, but I can't ask to change seats (class rule: change seats every month). Today in math class, I already struggle with math, and the teacher always sits next to me when we are doing exercises in class, since it's closer to the blackboard. When the teacher sits next to me, I can't solve any problems, not even the simplest ones. It seems like the teacher noticed that I couldn't solve such an easy problem and said to the whole class (it felt like it was directed at me), "If you can't solve such a simple problem, then give up." After hearing this, I felt really sad. I don't know if it's because my teacher is too fearful or something else, ahhhh! It's so heartbreaking. I feel like I'm being controlled when the teacher is nearby. Plus, others in the class are always actively answering questions during class, which makes me even more anxious. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Listen well, first of all, it's not your fault if you can't solve the problem, so you don't have to feel ashamed. Everyone has areas they are not good at. For example, if you're not good at math, I happen to not be good at it either. So, I focus on subjects in the humanities instead. If you feel guilty about it, you can privately ask someone who is good at math for help. In fact, math is not difficult. As long as you listen carefully, understand, and practice the exercises diligently, I believe your classmates will see you in a new light. It has formulas, just plug in the formula and you'll be fine.

question: Feeling stupid and dumb, I don't know the meaning of my existence.
description: I feel dumb and clumsy, with slow reactions. I am short, thin and weak, inherently inferior to others. I have low emotional intelligence, poor social skills, and bad relationships with everyone. Everyone hates me, I'm wasting my parents' money and everyone's time. I have also thought, if my parents had a boy as their first child, would there be no me, my younger brother, and sister? Were they so desperate for a boy to carry on the family line that they had my sister and then got sterilized, so there wouldn't be so many issues, debts, and their pressure wouldn't be so great? There wouldn't be the three of us, and I wouldn't have come into this world, I wouldn't have experienced so much. I don't know why I should continue living.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, growth process.

answers.answer_text: Hello, Lou Yuan! This is Laoyuan. I'm glad to meet you, the only and the best version of yourself in the world. However, it seems like you have encountered some problems, and I hope I can help you. Keywords: family, interpersonal relationships, one's future personality, beliefs, and character are largely influenced by the original family. *Lou Yuan, you mentioned mostly about family matters. From your narration, it seems that you are dissatisfied with the current situation in your family and consider it a "failure." You also feel extremely guilty and disgusted with yourself as you believe it is your own fault. Please listen carefully, regardless of what kind of family you come from, whether it is poor or anything else, it is not your fault, it has never been your fault. Your family, before you were born, was composed of your parents. You didn't have the ability to decide whether it was good or bad, and likewise, it is not your fault if it turned out to be good or bad. There seem to be many sisters in your family, and generally, the middle child rarely receives much attention from parents. However, from your narration, it seems that your parents have a tendency to favor boys over girls. But so what? They are the ones with that bias, not you. What you need is simply to live well and happily. And this brings us to the problem you are facing. *Interpersonal relationships, Lou Yuan, you have a very low self-evaluation, but you don't need to be like that, really. Although people are usually visual creatures, they also seek soulful connections (let's use a little bit of idealism here XD). However, since you are unwilling to talk about your experiences, I can't make a judgment about what you have been through. So, I'll write this paragraph for you, hoping that you can get through the toughest times. Height, weight, and appearance don't matter, I only know that you are an important person in my heart, just like that, simple and straightforward. Many times, we don't fit in with others, and it may not necessarily be our fault. Look around this world, there are always people like you. I hope to meet you in the future, so I hope you can live on and meet that person. Life is inherently lonely, and your temporary loneliness does not mean that your social circle is poor. As long as you focus on being yourself, it will suffice. Why we exist, this question never has an answer. It requires your whole life to answer it. The same goes for meaning and meaninglessness—nothing has inherent meaning, it always needs people to assign meaning to it, whether it's you, him, or anyone else. This world is wonderful, so work hard and enjoy watching this world in the future. The world and I love you. Even in the depths of despair, there will always be twinkling stars to warm you up.

question: You can't help but cry even if you don't want to, what situation does this belong to?
description: I always end up crying whenever something happens, even though I don't want to cry. Sometimes, there's nothing wrong, but I suddenly feel upset for no reason. I become very sensitive to what others say or do, and I find myself crying secretly. Sometimes, it gets so bad that I even think about suicide and come up with various methods, but I don't dare to do it. I am afraid that if I die, my family will blame me for causing trouble and have to handle my affairs. I am also afraid that if the suicide attempt fails, I will wake up to a lot of scolding. I constantly feel like there's something wrong with me, and it has a lot to do with my family. Why is it that sometimes I can be perfectly fine, but once my mood is affected, it becomes that situation?
keywords: Emotions, feelings of depression, expressing emotions, therapeutic methods.

answers.answer_text: Questioner, hello! I can understand how you feel. I used to feel the same way. Actually, our mental state is quite normal. We're just affected by insecurities, timidity, sensitivity, and lack of security. Our emotions are intermittent. When we encounter something that we can't bear, our emotions become pessimistic, compounded by the internal grievances that we sometimes cannot express, and there might be no one to listen to our grievances. That's why tears uncontrollably flow. However, people like us are actually kind and sensitive, willing to help others. This is our strength. Everyone's emotions have ups and downs. Feeling irritated is because something is affecting your cognition, making you feel that it contradicts your inner thoughts or conflicts with others' perspectives. That inexplicable irritation is normal, almost everyone in the world is like that. I don't know if you are afraid to deny or refuse what others say, or if you always compromise and try to be kind when interacting with others. In fact, this goes back to the problem you mentioned about your family background. We're all born the same way, but the different upbringing and education by our parents result in different personalities. It's possible that we weren't valued at home and our families didn't provide us with enough security, leading us to fear and strive to please others. Sometimes even a word or action from others can affect us. But I want to tell you that it's not your fault, and we can change through our own efforts. I am an example. I used to worry that people didn't want to play with me or that my boss didn't like me just because of a look from someone. I tried to please them, but it didn't work. Now, through studying psychology, I have made some changes and learned to love myself. So, you can definitely do it too. When I typed the sentence "I think about suicide, but I'm afraid. And even if I don't die, my family will blame me and I'll be scolded," my heart tightened because it reminded me of the inner dialogue I had in high school. I'm sure you feel very conflicted and tormented. It's okay, be strong and find the right way. We will definitely get better. Actually, people like us are often the most filial, but our parents can't recognize it. It's okay, it's not your fault. In fact, if you browse the Q&A section, you will find many peers who are confused like us. When you choose to seek answers here, I believe that you are willing and even very eager to find a solution to your problems. So, I believe you can do it. Based on the analysis above, I will give you some suggestions: 1) Strengthen your inner self. Our sensitivity and inferiority are due to a weak inner self. Our mental resilience is low, but we can strengthen our inner self through learning and exercise. You need to study more. In your spare time, read more books on psychology. Or you can study psychology to improve yourself. 2) Don't give up and strive hard. Most people are struggling in life, but as long as you live positively and persistently try to improve your state, there will come a day when we will have our own little world. 3) Exercise. I suggest doing more physical activities. You can go for a run, which not only exercises the body but also reduces stress. It's a good healing method. You can also go out more often to broaden your horizons. Seeing more will give us more motivation and even make us dissatisfied with the current situation. Please tell yourself, "I am fine, and I will work hard to make myself even better!"

"Louzhu, hello, sending you a supportive hug. Have you encountered something lately, causing your emotions to be so low? Hugs to you. When emotions are compressed for a long time, it becomes unbearable and needs to be released. It's like a cup filled with water, when it becomes too full, it naturally overflows. Your emotions are the same. Each thing has its own maximum threshold of tolerance, and when it exceeds that threshold, it becomes overwhelming. 'When you cry even though you don't want to, it's because of involuntarily held emotions.' So maybe at that moment, it wasn't the current situation that made you want to cry, but rather the accumulation of stored emotions that had no outlet. 'Always crying when something happens, even though I don't want to, it's because of involuntarily held emotions.' Definitely, someone triggered a certain point within you that has been deeply buried in your subconscious, where you have already been hurt, a deep wound, so deep that you haven't even noticed it. Being triggered by someone, you either become angry or burst into tears. Whether it's anger or tears depends on your current energy level. If your energy is high, you become angry; if it's low, you cry." "In severe cases, you might even think of suicide, think about various methods but lack the courage..." You are just under too much pressure, unable to bear it, wanting to escape. I don't know of any solutions, just wanting to escape. I believe that these are just temporary thoughts, please don't continue thinking about them, don't delve into them further, it's not good to get stuck in a negative mindset. You must think positively, think about what's more convenient, and definitely don't act foolishly. "I'm afraid that after I die, my family will blame me for causing trouble and have to deal with my affairs, and I'm also afraid that if I don't die, I'll wake up to a barrage of criticism." It's not your fault, really, it's not your fault. Don't blame yourself, it's not your fault, not your fault, not your fault. It's a problem with the parents, they have no filter, their words hurt others. They have mouths like blades and hearts like blades. They are used to attacking, it's their problem. Maybe they grew up in an environment like this, where they also didn't receive good treatment from others, so they don't know how to treat you well, it's not your fault. Treat their words like farts, don't take them or believe them too seriously, if according to them you haven't done anything wrong, then you shouldn't care too much, just let it go in one ear and out the other. "I always feel like there's something wrong with me, it has a lot to do with my family." I don't know what your family said to you, but don't take it too seriously, don't take it too much to heart. If you always feel like there's something wrong with you, it's probably because you're in a bad mood, which makes your body feel uncomfortable. It's just a signal, pay attention to your own physical health, care for yourself. "Why do I sometimes feel like a normal person, but my mood is affected in that situation?" Because you've been carrying your emotions for too long, it's difficult to bear. This way, it makes you feel better and more comfortable when you let yourself go with the flow, it's a natural instinctive reaction. Since your brain is commanding you like this, just follow its lead and relax a little. It will make you feel more comfortable and better equipped to deal with future problems. I have been paying attention to and studying content related to emotions. In everyday life, I like to pay attention to things related to emotions. In my studies, I am very attentive to this topic, and based on some learning, I have deep feelings about the issue of emotions. This is how I understand emotions, and I summarize them as follows: I compare emotions to water. Emotions are like water. In many expressions and literary works in our Chinese language, we like to compare them to water: emotions are "like tidal waves surging," "emotions are like floods," "like rushing tidal waves," "emotions burst." In the study of psychology, it tells us that emotions flow. This reinforces my perception and understanding of this abstract concept, and helps me make this abstract noun more tangible, enhancing the accuracy of my understanding. Emotions cannot be controlled. Any book that claims to "control emotions," or inspirational writing, is a misunderstanding and bias towards psychology, because emotions cannot be blocked. If we block emotions in one place, they will be released in another place, making it difficult for us to guard against, just like a flood. Only when we let emotions flow, our pain and unhappiness will be released, and we can share them and have others share the burden. First, emotions have multiple dimensions. According to different degrees, they can be divided into different dimensions, for example, following this example, I'll temporarily divide it into 7 dimensions: depression, mild depression, sadness, normal emotions, happiness, mild agitation, and agitation. Then there's another way to express it, which is depression and anxiety: 1. If it's depression, there will be sadness, irritability, thoughts of suicide, and exhaustion. 2. If it's anxiety, there will be tremors, nervous weakness, rapid heartbeat, and sweating. If it's between the two, it means: 1.2. Restlessness, excessive worry, and confusion.

question: I am hesitating between pursuing further studies and working. I enjoy practical experiences and find it difficult to concentrate on studying. I'm not sure what to do.
description: Many of my older sisters and classmates are taking the postgraduate entrance examination, and my parents also hope that I will do the same. However, they also urge me to find an internship. I also believe that pursuing a postgraduate degree can enhance my knowledge and qualifications. Now I am in my final year of college, with only a few months left, but I have only done a little bit of review. I feel like giving up. I can't concentrate on studying and reviewing, I prefer to go out and engage in practical activities. I am interested in various skills such as dancing, swimming, diving, PR, etc. I don't know what to do.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, life meaning.

answers.answer_text:
From the story provided by the topic owner, I can feel that you are torn between continuing to pursue further education or engaging in practical work at this stage. In terms of practical work, because you have various interests and thoughts about what you want to do, it has created uncertainty about the future and has caused you to feel stressed. I suggest that the topic owner can choose to write down the pros and cons of choosing different paths: 1- Choosing to take the entrance examination for postgraduate studies, what benefits can it bring to me? What advantages and opportunities will it provide for my future career? With less than four months left, what level of achievement can I reach? If I am not accepted, what consequences will I face? Do I need to face the pressure of entering the job market? ... ... 
2- Choosing to follow my own interests, this will make me feel comfortable at present, but while pursuing these interests, do I have enough financial foundation to support them? Will it create pressure for my family? Will the people at home give me additional pressure? Will these interests be helpful for my future development? Can these interests become a direction for my career development? ... ... The topic owner can create a corresponding table based on their own needs, face their true thoughts honestly, and choose the path that they believe is the best.

question: What should a person with depression do if they develop feelings for someone?
description: I am a patient with moderate depression and currently taking medication. I feel very lonely, so I chat with strangers on a social media platform. Lately, I have found myself eager to meet up with nearby strangers. I like to dress up and look glamorous when meeting them, chatting, and smiling, as if I were a normal person. The first person was because I wanted to jump into the lake, but he came to pick me up on his electric scooter. We walked in the playground and then he took me back to my dorm. The second person was because he said he was willing to accompany me to the hospital, which touched me. Then we had a meal together. The third person was because I was bored, and he happened to be on vacation. We met, walked, and chatted. I admired his experience. I don't feel like seeing any of the people I have met again. Until the fourth person, I understood his sadness and academic pressure, and I resonated with him. He tried to do something for me, and I started crying loudly because I was scared. He comforted me and hugged me like comforting a child. In fact, we were both well-dressed, and nothing happened. I realized that I have developed feelings for him, so I deleted everyone else and left only him. However, I stubbornly declined his second invitation. What's wrong with me? Am I better now? But I am still that sad, terrible, wanting-to-disappear me. How should I face myself and this strange feeling?

answers.answer_text: Hi, it's nice to see you here. Major depressive disorder is really unpleasant, I understand. But what I see is an image of someone who, despite feeling uncomfortable and having more darkness in their life than the average person, is still actively seeking redemption. Honestly, it moves me. Your process of meeting strangers through social media is a process of self-redemption. Because you believe that you can be okay, really okay. [To someone who doesn't know your past, you believe in showing a very normal side, even superior to others (because the ability of depression patients to perceive and respect life is beyond average)]. So you are enthusiastic about meeting strangers, believing that there will definitely be a meaningful connection. Indeed, you have achieved that. But on the other hand, you know that this ability cannot be sustained. Depressive disorders cannot maintain a stable emotional state; the random words and actions that occasionally appear in this world will trigger our existing traumatic experiences. It's easy to light the fuse. And more often than not, it's because the explosive inside needs to be released properly. Because we're not okay yet, we can't always control it. And once separated, we don't want to see each other anymore.
