Knowing that the purpose of meeting has been fulfilled, knowing that we are not ready to invest ourselves in such a relationship (regardless of what it may be), we naturally won't meet again, won't seek to continue. Because for our inner feelings, this is enough, we don't have the desire to make something happen or become something in reality! These moments are like when a person sunbathes when they have nothing else to do. They can enjoy the sun, but that's it. The sky cannot always have the sun hanging high, and we are not prepared to be seen when the moon comes out. When the day comes, [when we can take day and night interchangeably, when joy and sadness coexist without feeling uneasy], at that time, we will feel love for ourselves, like ourselves, and hope that this beautiful self can be seen by more people, and believe that this self deserves to be loved by more people. That's when we can truly say we're doing well! Lastly, I want to say that [depression can definitely get better, you have to believe in that]. It's just that this process includes so much that the average person cannot perceive, and as a result, you will ultimately have to understand and accommodate more than others.

question: After my boyfriend had an affair and we got back together, whenever I think about it, I can't help but burst into tears. Please help me.
description: I used to be a very optimistic girl, you could say that I didn't have any worries. A few months ago, my boyfriend was involved in ambiguities with another girl. I heard that he even pursued that girl. Because we work in the same company, when I started studying in the administrative department for less than a month, my colleagues told me about this matter. At that time, I didn't think much about it and just said that I knew about it and they were just ordinary friends. In fact, I didn't know anything. When I went home and asked him, he was in a bad mood towards me, which confirmed the truth. He apologized and showed a good attitude, so I forgave him. A few days later, that girl added me and told me how he pursued her, she mentioned a lot of details. I took my phone and replied to her using his account, admitting that it was him, and then he said some words of greetings, please note that he used the phrase "greetings to each other." Can you use this phrase if there's no problem? Definitely not. Now we have made up, but I feel upset and occasionally cry when I think about this matter. After this incident happened, I couldn't eat for a whole month and lost more than ten kilograms. I love him but I still want to break up, but he doesn't agree. I don't like being suspicious all the time or being constantly depressed and unhappy. I feel like I can't get out of this situation. I hope everyone can help me, I'm really in pain.
keywords: Love, infidelity, sense of security, love management

answers.answer_text: Let's tidy up while chatting: Your demand: You want to break up. His demand: He disagrees. From your description, it seems that he pursued another girl while having a girlfriend. This behavior is unacceptable to any woman, and although you ultimately chose to reconcile, your heart cannot accept this behavior of his. Maintaining a relationship itself is not easy, but he pursued another girl while still in a relationship with you. His attitude towards you is very uncomfortable, and it includes a lack of respect for you and disregards the harm caused by his actions. He chooses to do such things, and no one can stop him because it is his choice and right. But he may not know how deep the hurt caused by this is, you can choose to forgive him, but forgiving does not mean you have to continue a romantic relationship. As you said, you love him but want to break up. This is your right, you have the right to do so. His actions have already hurt your trust in him, and once that trust is damaged, it is difficult to repair in the short term. You can tell him how you feel, whether he agrees or not is not within your consideration, he only needs to know the result. How he faces this result is his own business. You need to do what you think needs to be done. Just as when he pursued that girl, he should be prepared to face such consequences and take responsibility for them. Making the decision to break up is indeed painful, especially since you still love him. But what's more painful is being with him, as his existence itself is like rubbing salt on your wound, very painful. The way you are currently handling the breakup, I think it's quite appropriate to separate for a while. If you can accept him, then you can choose to get back together. If you can't accept it, then the pain of letting go also exists. If you need someone to accompany you through this dark period, feel free to leave a message or private message at any time, and I can chat with you.

It's a choice to still want love despite the pain. It's also a choice to choose separation even when you love someone deeply. In the former case, you may need professional help to alleviate your emotions. Losing over ten kilograms in a month, feeling depressed and unable to move on, you should prioritize and pay attention to your mental health. The latter situation may also be painful, but it can be the start of a healing journey. In relationships, it's important to have boundaries - what is acceptable and what is intolerable. Without knowing our boundaries, we may easily allow others to overstep them, and our forgiveness might become a reason for them to hurt us again. Regarding your situation, it's important to communicate with your boyfriend about his ambiguous behavior and why he pursued another girl despite having you. What did that girl say to you? These are crucial questions that can help you determine if this guy truly loves you. You mentioned that you heard about the ambiguity from a colleague, which means your boyfriend was quite open about pursuing someone else. What do you think about that? Perhaps you just weren't aware. When you asked him, his defensive reaction made you assume it was true. I'm curious, what was the reasoning behind your deduction? Or do you know him well enough that such behavior confirms your view of him? If that's the case, his attitude of admitting fault may not be as good as you think. Think carefully about when he asked for forgiveness. Clearly, he didn't start with a good attitude. His "take care of yourselves" remark led you to think about many things, deepening your pain. Overall, this matter has caused you significant harm, and the crisis of trust is evident. Only by facing the current crisis of trust can emotional repair be possible. However, you may need to ponder whether it is worth forgiving infidelity during a romantic relationship. If you forgive, will your condition improve? It seems not. If you don't forgive, what will it be like? In any case, always listen to your heart and don't let it be mistreated.

Hello, OP. After your boyfriend cheated on you, he became angry and defensive. He only expressed wanting to break up after the other girl contacted you. You are well aware that his infidelity is a fact. However, you are reluctant to let go because his apology holds significant emotional value for you. So, for now, you have chosen to stay in the relationship. But this doesn't relieve the hurt, pain, and injustice you feel inside. Your relationship has already changed as a result, and your trust in him and the relationship has been shattered, tormenting you. Is this true? When someone you like not only betrays the relationship but also learns the details of the affair from the other girl, the inner pain is unquestionable. Therefore, doubting your partner, feeling unloved, and even self-doubt are all stages you may go through. Your boyfriend is the one who dragged you into this "bitter sea," but it may require your own efforts, as well as genuine cooperation from him, to pull you out of it. First of all, in the midst of this pain, strive to understand your true desires and what qualities your boyfriend possesses – whether he can fulfill your genuine aspirations. Any decision should be based on the life and emotional relationship you truly desire. If you find the act of infidelity completely unacceptable and prioritize loyalty, and if your boyfriend has a tendency to have multiple partners (such individuals have a high probability of repeated infidelity), then even if you temporarily remain in the relationship, your inner torment will continue and may even become a vicious cycle in the future. Secondly, if you choose to stay in the relationship, at this stage, you need to propose a plan to rebuild the relationship and get your boyfriend to cooperate with you. The old relationship has already been shattered, and your emotions haven't truly been released yet. Continuing to superficially forgive without any plan will not help rebuild the relationship. You need to present a plan, such as having him answer your calls promptly and come home right after work, etc. You can also propose certain punitive measures (with the goal of compensating for your pain and providing relief to your emotions), such as taking back financial rights. In short, there need to be concrete actions, with both parties cooperating, in order to repair and rebuild the relationship. Finally, focus on yourself and make decisions from the heart. Pouring all your attention into this matter will continually deplete you, causing you pain and leaving you with no other choice. If you redirect your attention to self-improvement, enhancing your value and charm, you will have more options and be able to choose someone you genuinely like who is a better match for you. When comparing the two options, doesn't the latter seem more worthwhile in terms of time invested? May you love yourself and find someone who loves you in the right way.

Oh my goodness, girl, I can't believe I have a similar experience as you. I started dating my boyfriend in high school and we had a long-distance relationship in college, which was going well. I trusted him completely and never doubted him. But things changed when he started working. He started criticizing me all the time, finding faults in everything I did, and even said I wasn't attractive to him anymore. I was shocked and blamed myself, thinking it was my fault. I never expected that it was because of another girl. Later, he confessed to me himself and said that this girl liked him and even wrote a poem about their meeting. I was devastated when he showed me the pictures they took together. I couldn't sleep all night and wanted to break up with him. Later, his family, whom I already knew well, said that there must be a reason for this problem. I reflected on myself and realized that I had neglected him during that time because I was playing games. But that still wasn't a reason for him to cheat. His family told me that if I spoke harshly at this time, it would only push him further away and closer to that girl. I thought about it and realized they were right, so I took the initiative and fought for our relationship. We got back together, and he admitted his mistake and said that he was weak and couldn't resist temptation when he started working. Since then, I have always doubted him, and it's exhausting. Sometimes I think about breaking up, but I don't want to let go. Sometimes when I ask him about the other girl, he gets annoyed, and even after he came back, she still sends him messages. He wants to call her and break things off, but he doesn't want me to listen. The fact that I saw his reply to her message without cutting off contact makes me certain that something happened between them. Later, whenever I thought about this matter, I felt sad, but luckily I managed to get through it. Whether to break up or not depends on your boyfriend's current attitude and whether you can accept this stain. If you were to get a new boyfriend, would you start suspiciously doubting again? If you still have doubts, you will still be miserable. It's better to let this stain pass with your current boyfriend, provided that he admits his mistake and has a good attitude, and nothing substantial happened between them.

question: I think people are really complicated, I don't know how to get along with them. What should I do?
description: Lately, I really feel more and more at a loss on how to get along with the people around me. It seems like my friends are gradually ignoring and distancing themselves from me, but I don't know why. When I am with them, I always consider their emotions, their thoughts, and what they want to do, and I feel like I have been doing my best. However, they are still slowly starting to distance themselves and ignore me. I don't really understand what else I should do. It truly feels difficult and exhausting to be a person.

answers.answer_text: It is more difficult to "be yourself" than to "be human." The OP said that when they are with friends, they always use their friends' emotions and thoughts as their own behavioral standards, but the result is gradually being alienated and ignored by their friends, which they find confusing and exhausting. The OP obviously did not realize the problem with their behavior pattern. The OP can recall a scene of themselves and their friends getting along and take a bystander's perspective to see where they were in that scene. Naturally, there is an OP there in physical space, but if you look closely at the space of interpersonal communication, it is almost impossible to find traces of the OP's presence because they have perfectly hidden themselves. In other words, when the OP is interacting with friends, they "deliberately" make others ignore their existence. When the OP’s friends have become accustomed to ignoring the OP, the manifestation in real life is naturally the neglect and alienation of the OP. And when the OP's friends start to neglect and distance themselves from the OP, the OP cannot effectively hide "themselves" anymore, so they start to feel uncomfortable and ignored, and begin to feel confused. Therefore, what the OP needs to do now is not to seek the attention of friends, but to first see themselves. Only when the OP is no longer a role that should be ignored in their own consciousness can they effectively change their current situation in real life. This pattern of the OP comes largely from their experience of being constantly ignored when they were growing up. Because they have always been neglected, they have accumulated a lot of helplessness, powerlessness, and anger. The OP needs to first see themselves being neglected all the time, and then release those pent-up negative emotions such as helplessness, powerlessness, anger, etc. in order to break the "compulsive repetition" of "always being ignored." When the OP's ingrained behavior pattern is broken and a new behavior pattern is established, the OP will definitely gain new understanding of how to get along with others. Hope this can be helpful to the OP.

Hello, dear poster. Hugs to you. Many times as we go through life, we find that many friends gradually drift away and we have less contact with them. When we go to college, we slowly lose contact with some of our high school friends, leaving only one or two with whom we occasionally talk. After college, the classmates we lived with each go their separate ways, and contact diminishes as well. At work, relationships with our colleagues are all good, but when we change jobs and try to stay in touch, we feel that they are not quite the same as before. We are always meeting people as we grow, and losing people, but there will always be a few who stay by your side. Growing up is full of curiosity, but it can also be mischievous at times, often playing jokes that hurt others. These jokes help us see who people truly are, and in the process, we lose some but keep a few. Don't be afraid. I hope this can help you.

I can perceive the idea that the questioner wants to get along well with the people around them. Indeed, having good interpersonal relationships can make people feel happy. Therefore, most people want to get along well with those around them. When interacting with others, we always consider their emotions and thoughts, prioritizing their needs. You may feel that you have done enough, but people still distance themselves from you and overlook you. It can feel helpless. However, does making friends always require accommodating others? When a person completely accommodates others, is it still a relationship between two individuals? Both you and the other person may end up bearing too much pressure, and naturally, the relationship will not be comfortable. Only when two individuals are independent can it be a healthy relationship, right? Best wishes! Karen.

Hello. Darling, maybe it's because you do too well and ignore your own inner needs a bit. You have a tendency to please others, so you feel exhausted in interpersonal relationships. And indeed, this makes it easy for others to overlook you, giving you a low sense of presence and making you more vulnerable to being bullied or scapegoated. However, one advantage of this is that kind-hearted you will make genuine friends, as long as you can distinguish between the pros and cons, and determine if the other person is worth your investment. In everyday social interactions, before agreeing to anything that requires your time and energy, you might as well not rush to agree and instead ask yourself: Do I really want to spend time and effort on this? Do I have other arrangements? How do I feel about doing this in my heart? Am I happy about it, or do I feel reluctant and troubled? For example, if others ask you to go out and play on the weekend, but you had originally planned to go home. 1. If after asking your inner self, you feel more inclined to go out with everyone, then agree. The premise of agreeing to others is: this is your own choice, and this choice will not make you feel resentful. 2. If after asking your inner self, you feel going home is a better choice for you, then tell everyone: "I'm sorry, although I really want to go, I already have plans for the weekend. Let's make plans for another time." 3. If your inner self is at a loss and unable to make a decision for the moment, you can say: "I can't confirm whether I can go or not yet, I might have other things to do on the weekend. Let me confirm and reply to you as soon as possible." Take care of yourself first, bravely and politely refuse to do things that you are unwilling to do. Then, care for and take care of others, so as not to become a "people-pleaser" who doesn't take initiative in anything, and not become a transparent person where all your efforts are taken for granted and overlooked by others.

In relationships, if someone doesn't have their own needs and only considers others' emotions and thoughts, doing whatever others want them to do, it won't make others feel comfortable. People who appear to only give without having needs themselves actually have more and deeper needs than others. Those deep needs, to be seen and fulfilled, can put a lot of pressure on others. Relationships should be mutually satisfying. Today, you satisfy me and tomorrow, I satisfy you. It's an exchange that makes everyone comfortable. If you don't speak up, express yourself, or make any demands, expecting others to take care of your feelings without getting any feedback, they will have to guess and not know for sure. They won't understand why you are even with them, which can be exhausting. That's why others may distance themselves from you. If you want friends, first recognize that you have such high expectations for yourself as well as others. Once you see this, you won't put all these expectations on others and slowly bring them back to yourself. When you need less from others, it becomes easier to build relationships. Wishing you well, Zhang Jinping, a mental health counselor.

Hello, friend! Reading your description, I want to give you a hug. It seems like you have a longing for friends and hope to have someone who cares about your feelings. I hope we can become closer to each other! Based on your description, it seems that you are a sensitive person. You feel that you have done well in being a friend, but still haven't received their response. You may wonder if they are distancing themselves from you, unwilling to pay attention to you. Maybe you even think that they should treat you the way you treat them - by considering your feelings. Sometimes, this kind of thinking can make you feel unappreciated, uncared for, and misunderstood. You dislike this kind of dynamic between friends.

I'm not sure how you define friends. If you feel that friends must respond to you whenever you reach out and they should be there for you when you need them, that might be a demand from someone who is insecure. Friends can have a pure friendship where they encourage and understand each other. However, friends also have their own daily lives and social circles. When they're together, they can chat endlessly, but when they are apart, they have their own things to attend to. We need to respect that. Sometimes, it's not that the feelings between individuals have become weaker, but rather that they have other things to do besides each other, like family or children. We can try to learn to respect each other. The lack of communication doesn't mean the other person doesn't care about you, and not responding immediately doesn't mean they want to distance themselves from you. It's just that everyone has their own way of living, and you can't expect everyone to be the same. Some people are slow to warm up, and some people don't like looking at their phones. In that case, we can think that they are busy and don't have time to respond to me because they might actually be busy! Try to think from a different perspective, and you may discover a different life and different viewpoints. Your focus should also return to yourself. When you learn to love yourself, others will love you more! The world and I love you!

question: Always thinking about him, but dreaming about someone else, why?
description: Recently, I have been involved in emotional entanglements with a guy. Every time we have sweet moments, I dream sweet dreams at night, and when we fight, I have anxious dreams. But what's strange is that the person in my dreams is never him, but other guys whom I am not in contact with much. In the past, I used to dream about whoever I liked. Why is it happening like this now?

answers.answer_text: Hello! @We often find that dreams are colorful and often do not align with reality. Sometimes, dreams can be vivid, like a science fiction movie. Of course, we also have dreams that reflect our daily experiences. Dreams are so mysterious and profound that people have been studying and exploring their meanings since ancient times. @If you try to understand dreams, you will realize that most of our dreams are wrapped in layers. Superficial dreams may have just a few layers, while complex dreams are like layers of an onion. ○Freud believed that dreams stem from our desires. Jung believed that dreams have a compensatory nature and can convey important messages to us. (This situation probably applies to you.) Adler believed that the main function of dreams is problem-solving, providing a positive outcome. Overall, these theories suggest that dreams are related to our subconscious and understanding your dreams is like glimpsing a corner of the iceberg, helping you understand yourself. @Dream processing involves four mechanisms: condensation, displacement, representation, and secondary elaboration. People or objects in your dreams generally have symbolic meanings. For example, dreaming of a house may symbolize your inner self. Dreaming of a person may imply someone you have in mind. Symbolic meanings can vary for different individuals due to cultural differences, mindset differences, or gender differences, resulting in different interpretations of symbols. ○You mentioned that you are currently experiencing relationship troubles. I think that may be why you are feeling fearful or avoidant, perhaps even afraid of seeing that person. So, in your dreams, that person cannot simply appear directly, but instead takes on the identity of someone else. If you observe carefully, you will find that the person you dream about is not unrelated to the person you have in mind. Let me give you an example: I had a falling out with a friend, and our relationship became strained. One day, we both coincidentally encountered each other on our way home. Initially, we both pretended not to see each other and planned to just pass each other by. Perhaps both of us hesitated, and it became extremely awkward when we reached the point where we couldn't avoid a confrontation. I wanted to quickly walk away, but at that moment, someone with the other person greeted me (we also knew each other). Even though I usually don't think about this person, I knew deep down that I wanted to reconcile. But what could I do? I even dreamt about it, but in my dream, it was the person who greeted me. At first, I was confused until I looked up some information about dreams. I thought, "Oh, this probably represents the desire I long for!" Unfortunately, we never reconciled. Despite not having an obvious connection in dreams like my example, there are instances where a child dreams about a caterpillar wearing a hat. Upon deeper analysis, it was discovered that he was referring to someone he disliked because he noticed the hat resembled that person's. @I think what you want to ask is not about interpreting dreams, but how to resolve your issues. Your dream tells you that you value this relationship. So why not find an opportunity to have a good conversation? Perhaps it is time to address and resolve the problem. The world is loving and supportive of you.

Dear friend: Hello, I saw you talking about dreams and I was wondering why the person in your dream is not your current partner. Dreaming is related to the subconscious and reflects our daily activities and inner desires. In dreams, there are no restrictions, so whatever thoughts you have, there will be corresponding images and emotions. [First], when you have had a sweet and wonderful relationship with a past boyfriend, you may dream about him. This reflects that thoughts during the day manifest in dreams at night. Daytime activities and nighttime emotions come out in the subconscious. [Second], if you are involved in a new romantic situation but dream about being sweet with someone else, it indicates that your current partner cannot meet your requirements. Your unfulfilled needs are entrusted to someone else who can satisfy them. Or it may indicate that your needs have not been satisfied for a long time, and your subconscious is telling you that you have a wish or a need that you want to fulfill. [Third], this shows that you need to understand your deeper desires, or perhaps you really need to communicate with your current partner and find ways to make the relationship more harmonious and satisfying. This is a minor issue, it's nothing serious. Since you are in a relationship, it's best to honestly communicate your needs to each other and have a good conversation. Best wishes! Your friend, Audrey.

Hello, I hope my words can be helpful to you. Recently, I have had some emotional entanglements with a guy. In the past, I would dream about the person I had feelings for, but now I dream about other unrelated people. I want to know if it's because of the recent emotional conflicts that I haven't been dreaming about the guy I like, or if I have never dreamt about him since being together with him. In the past, I would dream about the person I liked, but now I haven't dreamt about the person I like. There could be several possibilities: you dreamt about him but have forgotten. According to modern psychology, dreams, as a form of conscious experience, can be forgotten. You feel like you haven't dreamt about him, but it's possible that you actually dreamt about him but forgot by the time morning arrived. Real-life suppression and escapism in dreams are stored in memory units that correspond to neurons in the brain. Dreams are a weakened conditioned reflex. Since you mentioned "having some emotional entanglements with a guy recently," the person appearing in your dreams might not be him. It's possible that in real life, you don't feel secure about this guy yet, and subconsciously fear any unpleasant experiences with him, choosing to escape instead. Being too concerned, there is a possibility that because you are overly concerned, you really want to meet him in dreams, whether inside or outside of dreams. However, because you are overly concerned, it's like the "Valenda effect" - the more you try to succeed, the bigger the failure. Similarly, being too focused on the outcome, your mind is filled with thoughts of the final result, which often goes against your wishes.

The question posed by the OP is interesting. Dreams can be seen as the release of subconscious self's current pressure and the reflection of emotional feelings. They are also related to current experiences and past experiences, mixed together to satisfy the needs of the subconscious self. Previously, the OP used to dream about someone they liked, but now they constantly dream about someone they used to like. On one hand, this is because there are some differences and changes in the OP's attitude towards relationships compared to before. The OP's age and past experiences influence their perception and expectations of relationships, which can lead to more conflicts in current relationships compared to before. On the other hand, the OP's dreams also reflect the issues in their current relationship. Just like the OP mentioned, dreaming sweet dreams during sweet moments and having anxious dreams during arguments. Dreaming about the previous person they liked represents a denial of the current person and a denial of the relationship. These issues make the OP feel helpless and unsure of what to do, instinctively reminiscing about past relationship experiences to satisfy their emotional needs. Perhaps the OP's inner self is more negative, believing they lack the strength to face and solve these problems, and therefore want to escape from them. However, if the problems are not resolved, they will continue to accumulate and eventually become issues that must be addressed. At that point, the pressure will be even greater. Accepting and facing these problems with an open mind, expressing one's true thoughts and feelings, is not as scary as it may seem.

question: What is the psychological factor when a leader argues with someone and then feels an urge to work harder themselves?
description: Yesterday, due to work requirements, I arranged for an employee to do a task that she had not done before. She was unwilling and immediately said, "I'm busy every day, and now you added more work. What about my salary?" The leader replied on the spot, "We are a private school, and work is something we all do together. Although the salary may not be high, it is still acceptable. If you don't want to do it, you can look for higher-paying jobs elsewhere!" I don't know why, but the next day I really wanted to do more work! I thought if the workload really came to me, I wouldn't be able to handle it! Later, when I calmed down, I wondered what I was doing. Was I afraid of being fired? Or trying to prove that I'm better than others? Seeking approval? A sense of boundarylessness?
keywords: Career, career management, workplace relationships, work stress

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP: Actually, everyone wants to fulfill their own value, just like if you are a boy, you will pursue a successful career. Most boys are proud and hope to have their own realm in their careers. Girls also want to achieve their own value. After all, most girls dislike being called vase and want to prove their abilities through practical actions. Girls' strengths are not just in appearance, but also in professional abilities. This is not blindly pleasing others, at least you are doing it for yourself, or because you want to create value, so you please yourself and comply with yourself. Perhaps you are particularly averse to people who shirk responsibility, and the supervisor's words indeed inspire everyone's initiative. A truly good leader respects the value and choices of employees. I believe in your leader, although he may be strict in some situations, he is mostly calm and can listen to reasonable opinions from subordinates. - The leader said, "It's okay, if I can't handle it, I will tell you and ask for your help." I think this kind of leader has a distinctive style of a general, comforting your uneasiness and giving you an opportunity to showcase yourself in the future. Is he the one who appears to be the most leisurely, but in reality, he shoulders more responsibility and workload than ordinary employees? Some leaders demand strictness from others because they hope their subordinates can create value that is even better than theirs and have higher expectations for the next generation, which inevitably makes us feel under immense pressure. ~ ~ Opportunities are all fought for by ourselves. As the saying goes, "The crying baby gets candy." Although you may have suspicions of showing off and flaunting in front of others, those who truly understand you will always respect your value and give you more platforms. Perhaps you are not entirely wrong to worry. This world already has too many demands and restrictions on female workers. From the perspective of enterprises, they will need people who actively contribute, and male employees have smaller costs and can handle more physical labor. And the supervisor shouldn't demand too much from a girl, as it is neither ethical nor classy. Plus, girls have their own families, and at certain stages, because the woman focuses on the family, she may not be able to handle work matters very well. I think you should feel fortunate. Very few managers genuinely sympathize with people, can think from others' perspectives, and are good at encouraging and comforting others. The employees who work in a 996 or 007 work schedule cannot experience the happiness that you have!

When making decisions, people are always influenced by multiple factors. For example, as for the reasons you reflected on, it's likely that they all existed at the time, but it's hard to determine their respective proportions. Apart from the main factor that led to your decision, I am also curious why you are reflecting on this behavior. Based on your description, it seems that you regret your action because you can assess the impact of taking on this job. Regret often stems from non-acceptance, but there are two types of non-acceptance in this matter: 1. You do not accept the workload after taking on those tasks, 2. You do not accept the behavior of taking on those tasks voluntarily. I guess these might be the reasons for your self-reflection. As for the main factors that led to your voluntary acceptance of the job, personally, if you really want to figure it out, you may need to analyze not just this case. For example, if there have been previous cases of employees being fired in the company, the fear of being dismissed may be the main factor this time; or if there have been multiple occasions before when others made requests and you never refused, regardless of the difficulty, weak boundaries may be the main factor this time. As for "appearing better than others" being the main factor, personally, I tend to think that you wouldn't bring up this question if it were. When encountering a situation that needs to be analyzed, you can recall how the person involved reacted in similar events in the past; you can also think about what events have happened recently that may have had an impact on the person involved. It is difficult to analyze the essence of a matter independently.

question: Studying abroad for undergraduate degree, feeling confused about both learning and emotions, having difficulty falling asleep every day.
description: Studying for my undergraduate degree abroad, but because it was all online courses during this period, I feel confused about what I have learned. It's also difficult to communicate with classmates. Being stuck at home makes me feel depressed. And I have encountered some issues with my girlfriend back in China... It's hard to fall asleep every day.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotion regulation

answers.answer_text:
Hello, OP! It seems like you have been experiencing a process of "nervousness-anxiety-adaptation-irritation" during the COVID-19 pandemic, when you can only attend online classes at home. You may currently be in an "irritated" state, which can leave you feeling a bit overwhelmed and unsure of what to do, causing confusion. The issues you are experiencing in your relationship with your girlfriend have further intensified your anxiety. Let me throw a few questions at you, and you can take some time to reflect on them:

1. Have you ever made plans for your future life or set goals for yourself?
2. Are the problems between you and your girlfriend due to external factors or are they caused by your emotions?

Regarding your current confusion, here's my understanding:

1. If you have previously set goals and made plans for your life, your current confusion may be due to the disruption caused by the pandemic, leading to a temporary feeling of being lost. During a state of crisis like the pandemic, feeling lost and experiencing anxiety is a normal emotional response. Your classmates may be going through similar emotions as well. Try creating a schedule for yourself, organizing your daily tasks, and following the plan. This can help alleviate your current anxiety.

2. If you haven't set goals or made plans for your life before, your current confusion can be seen as a sign of growth. You are beginning to consider the social responsibilities you will undertake and the roles you will play in the future. This is a necessary stage of self-identity development. "Self-identity" refers to having a clear understanding of the responsibilities and roles one will take on in society. Before achieving self-identity, there will inevitably be a stage of confusion. The aforementioned schedule can also be helpful in this situation. While exploring your self-identity, the most important thing is to focus on living in the present moment and completing your current tasks. Continuously develop your abilities and skills, so that when you eventually figure out what you want to do, you will have the resources to pursue your dreams.

Regarding the issues between you and your girlfriend:
1. If the problems arose due to certain events between the two of you, redirect your primary focus on solving those issues together. You and your girlfriend are a team, and you need to confront the situation together. Try discussing the current issues with your girlfriend and brainstorming possible solutions.

2. If the problems between you two are primarily caused by your current state of anxiety, focus on dealing with your own emotions. Try to manage your emotions gradually through the suggested schedule and actively communicate your current emotional state to your girlfriend. Believe that she will understand and support you through this emotional phase.

I hope these suggestions can be helpful to you. Remember, the world and I care about you. All the best!

Hello! First of all, when the novelty of being far away from home fades away, the feelings of homesickness start to spread. Those who haven't left their hometowns may not understand this feeling, but it's truly painful and there's no one to talk to. Even if there are people around to chat with, they may not be close enough to really understand or help. Secondly, when you're not in a good mood, it tends to show in your words and actions. It can affect your normal thinking and communication when interacting with others. I suggest focusing on your studies since not everyone has the opportunity to study abroad. Seize the opportunity to broaden your knowledge and make yourself more competitive in the future! I'm not sure which country you're in, but if possible, you can go for a run, ride a bike, play sports, etc. It can help expend physical and mental energy, which aids sleep. Drinking a cup of warm milk before bed can also help with sleep. You can also try relaxation therapy or guided hypnosis on your own, without the need for a professional therapist. Regarding social relationships, it is recommended to comply with the pandemic prevention regulations of the country you're in. Try to minimize direct contact and use online means for communication. Make new friends and develop hobbies in your free time, which can be achieved through online platforms since online communication is safer.

question: Do I have a mental disorder if I have developed a habit of masturbation and often feel lonely and yawn frequently?
description: When I was a child, I was very scared of the dark and ghosts. It made my whole body stiff, and I developed a habit of masturbation. As I grew older, I needed to read some erotic stories to reach climax. It happens at most once or twice a month, and afterwards I feel very guilty and frustrated. Now in my 30s, I often feel lonely, yawn frequently, and have trouble concentrating. I wonder if it's because of masturbation. I feel like I might be mentally abnormal and will be abandoned by society and live out my old age alone.

answers.answer_text: I don't have much information about you, but I'll try to respond to you: 1) It is completely normal to masturbate 1-2 times a month for any reason, so there is no need to feel guilty or frustrated. It is a natural human need, and the way you satisfy it doesn't affect others. Masturbation is not something to be ashamed of, you know? 2) As you grow older, you may need some erotic content to reach climax. It's like eating the same food for a long time and not feeling the same enjoyment. Erotic content may just be a different chef that enhances sexual arousal, and it is normal. 3) At 30 years old, feeling lonely, frequently yawning, and unable to concentrate. Masturbation is not to blame for these issues. So, you need to think about why you feel lonely. Don't you have any colleagues or friends? As for the lack of concentration, it may be related to your internal struggle, for example, feeling that masturbation is not good and should be avoided, but unable to resist the urge. 4) Do you feel like you have a mental disorder and worry about being abandoned by society when you grow old? I cannot see any abnormality, but if you constantly feel lonely, it would be a good idea to seek help from a mental health counselor to understand why you feel this way. In conclusion, it is necessary to consider your physical health, emotional state, work, and overall life situation to make a preliminary evaluation. However, considering your self-blame and guilt for many years, as well as your current feelings at the age of 30, I believe it would be beneficial for you to seek psychological counseling.

Hello, it seems like you are feeling bored with your life, without any feelings of joy or excitement. Masturbation provides a physical experience and stimulation that may be lacking in your daily life, which is why you turn to it as a way to release your inner loneliness. There is no right or wrong in this matter, as sexual desire is a natural human need. It is normal to satisfy yourself when you have the urge. There is no need to judge your actions. However, relying solely on this method to feel alive and stimulated is something that you need to face and adjust. If there is something else that makes you feel alive, happy, and energized, something that brings fulfillment and joy to your life, would you still choose masturbation as a way to stimulate yourself? I believe not. What you need to change is your state of life, as it is not directly related to masturbation. Find activities that make you feel good, do what you enjoy as much as possible, exercise regularly, and let the energy of life shift from sexual satisfaction to heartfelt experiences. Sex can then become the most wonderful experience in life. I wish you the best in reconnecting with your inner feelings.

question: As an exam retaker for the college entrance examination (gaokao), how can I make myself passionate every day?
description: After experiencing a failed college entrance exam, every day during the summer vacation, I didn't know which direction I should move in and felt very lost in life. The university I wanted to attend is also a bit far from where I am, and I don't know what I should do next!
keywords: Growing up, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: First of all, give up the idea that nobody can be passionate every day, especially when it comes to something that repeats daily. It is okay to maintain a stable state, and it is already good enough to work five days and rest for three days. Secondly, don't set a goal that is too distant as it may have some motivating effects, but the side effects can be significant, such as continuous anxiety. It is recommended to set periodic major directions, such as learning English. For example, "spend 2-4 weeks going through English grammar, practice areas that are weaker" can be a phased direction. Then, move forward in this direction every day. If you make more progress on a certain day, you can give yourself a small reward. If you make less progress on another day, there is no need to be disheartened. There may be many factors affecting the results. Summarize the progress made and the lessons learned every week or two. In this way, one will feel grounded, and the ultimate result will be determined by oneself (often better than expected because we tend to underestimate the power of accumulation over time).

question: Having gone through a period of being in a manipulative relationship, how do I move on from thinking about my ex?
description: I am Les, 24 years old. In May this year, the girl I confessed to ten years ago contacted me and said she wanted to meet me. Later on, our relationship developed into a sexual one without a defined commitment. I discovered that this person inherently likes to belittle me and elevate herself. She has better financial conditions and always wants me to provide her with certain items. I also realized that she takes pleasure in seeing me upset and angry. I went to the hospital and confirmed that I have symptoms of depression. The girl who contacted me turned out to be a pickup artist (PUA). I feel uneasy during the time spent with this PUA, and I often think about my first girlfriend as an adult. I remember the comforting words she said and the things she did that appealed to me when we were dating. However, it has been five years since we broke up. In the past, I used to sleep better by holding onto my ex, but after the breakup, I started hugging my pillow instead. These past few days, I've been playing the sound of a girl breathing and spraying a perfume on my pillow that smells similar to my ex's shampoo. In the middle of the night, I keep thinking about the kind words my ex said to me, and I end up crying uncontrollably. Emotionally, I want to privately discuss and write a short essay to send to my ex, talking about this PUA situation and expressing my gratitude to her for something. But rationally, I tell myself, "This could be bothersome for her, and maybe she won't even read it." Currently, I am still somewhat rational and I want everyone to help me analyze what information my displayed emotions and behaviors are trying to convey to me.
keywords: Love, heartbreak, attachment and dependence, sense of security.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Your current girlfriend loves to belittle you, cannot understand your feelings, and has materialistic needs. When compared to your ex-girlfriend, the "good" of your ex-girlfriend becomes evident. This is what we often say, "Not knowing the true face of Mount Lu, only wishing to be born in this mountain." Without loss or comparison, one would not know their true needs. Being with your ex-girlfriend provided a sense of security, being able to sleep peacefully, and reminiscing about her scent. These all indicate a deep attachment established between you and your ex-girlfriend. But love is complicated. You have already been separated for 5 years, things have changed, and people have changed. Being immersed in memories and longing for the past would make you neglect the desire and anticipation for a better life in the present. The past was so beautiful, yet you didn't grasp it, and you have been plagued by self-blame for a long time. Now, your current girlfriend is also dissatisfied. Am I just inadequate... In this state of mind, your self-worth will continue to diminish, leading to depression. To overcome depression, first, we must face reality. How do we face reality? It is important to change our mindset. What have you learned from each relationship? What are the main takeaways? By comparing your two girlfriends, you can summarize what kind of person is right for you: someone who understands, empathizes, and can soothe your emotions, someone who is financially independent... Understanding your specific needs is essential for choosing friends and finding your ideal partner. It also enables you to face temptations, such as sex. Every experience is a chance for growth, not for regret. In the process of being together, effort should be mutual. We not only hope for the other person to act a certain way but also need to make our own contributions to the relationship. Regularly ask yourself, while being in a relationship, if you treat the other person as you would like to be treated. Do you acknowledge their strengths and virtues as you want them to see yours? Do you offer support, encouragement, and compliments? Do you display understanding and acceptance when they are upset? If we can achieve these things, we can believe that the other person can too. Here are a few suggestions about depression: exercise more, engage in a favorite physical activity consistently. Exercise generates chemicals that bring joy and can alleviate moods. Cultivate interests and hobbies, divert attention, and discover the beauty in life. Think more about the good life that lies ahead.

Dear friend: I saw your personal experience and feel sorry for you. Love is supposed to bring joy, but it has brought you depression because of PUA. I hope you can overcome this darkness soon. The need behind your behavior is actually a lack of security. You want to escape the security issues you don't want to face by reminiscing about past relationships. Spraying the other person's perfume and constantly simulating their presence is to chase after the happiness they once gave you. And these happy memories can make you forget about the security issues you've been trying to avoid. The fact that you are still holding on even though it has been several years since the breakup shows that you have signs of addiction. You lack security and want to fill yourself up through new relationships, but this kind of demanding attitude makes you vulnerable to PUA. They will use your weakness - being addicted to the security that relationships give you - to make you do things against your will, like providing material needs to the other person, just so you can continue feeling a semblance of security. Continuing to be addicted may make you continue to be controlled in relationships. Therefore, finding ways to increase your sense of security and letting go of addictive behaviors is the best solution. [First of all], understand that the most stable sense of security is not given to you by the external world, but it is gained through connecting with everything in the universe and exploring it through your inner self. I suggest you try meditation to heal your sense of security. [Secondly], living in the present moment is what gives you strength, not past memories. If you still think about the other person's tenderness when it's late at night, it may temporarily alleviate your dependence, but in the long run, it will have an impact and prevent you from truly loving yourself. Understanding this, at least, can help you stop relying on addiction and bring yourself back to the present moment. [Thirdly], learn to love yourself. It's not just the outside world that can make you feel loved, but you can do so yourself. The sweet words you used to like to hear, you can say them to yourself and try to feel the love that you give. The things you used to do with your partner, you can do them for yourself as well, but the object of giving and receiving is yourself. [Fourthly], be grateful for yourself. Gratitude is a good way to see the power of your own love. Because you appreciate yourself, you realize that you also have this strength and ability. [Fifthly], gradually reduce the cravings. If you suddenly reduce them, you may feel uncomfortable, so you can gradually reduce them to allow your heart to adapt. [Sixth], formally mourn. When you are ready, you can have a ritual to mourn this relationship. Throw away the things associated with the other person, most importantly, eliminate the sense of dependence on them. The benefit of mourning is that it formally declares to yourself that you are cutting off ties with this person and moving forward. During the mourning period, you can let yourself grieve fully because all the pain and sadness are reasonable during this time. Give yourself a deadline, then gather your emotions and welcome the future. A person who excessively relies on a crutch forgets that they can walk with their own two feet. Someone who overly depends on others for love forgets how to love themselves. So you need to practice more and let go of excessive dependence and obsession with your partner, and become confident and strong yourself. Best wishes! Your friend: Audrey.

Whether it's dealing with exes or female online friends, you seem to be more passive in relationships. When the things they say and do make you feel uncomfortable and belittled, you think back to the reassuring words and actions of your ex that made you feel secure. Through their behaviors, you vaguely express your inner needs: to be acknowledged and cared for. However, it seems that you can't directly articulate these needs yourself. Instead of expressing your preferences, you hope that others will intuitively understand and fulfill them, which is a more dependent state. This is why you become so attached to people who can satisfy you. If you constantly feel that your needs have to be fulfilled by someone else externally, it will leave you feeling powerless. By analyzing your own needs through external reactions, and then further satisfying yourself and learning to express yourself to others, without demanding, you will gradually gain more strength. Wishing you well, Zhang Jinping, a counseling psychologist.

question: I cry over little things, why am I always so prone to crying?
description: I cry over little things (´;︵;`) like not being able to solve difficult problems. I try to control my tears, but I find that I can't.
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I also feel helpless and sad, and even have self-blame. First of all, I want to tell you that this is closely related to your recent state. You may have really encountered some difficulties that make it difficult for you to suppress your sad emotions. Maybe you think "I can bear it a little longer", but your body is clearly expressing to you that it is already overwhelmed. Because you are really sad now, you have really endured a lot in your heart, so you can't control your tears and keep expressing your grievances and sadness. You feel like you can cry over small things, but what's wrong with crying? This might be the time when you need to cry. However, you also need to explore your own thoughts and needs. You can communicate more with people around you, the company of family or friends is also important, or you can seek professional psychological help. But don't hide it all by yourself. Hope this helps you!

question: My father had an affair, should my mother get a divorce? Is that the best choice?
description: My dad is addicted to extramarital affairs and can't change. Over the years, he has been involved with multiple women. But in other aspects, he is good. He gives his salary to my mom (while secretly keeping some money for himself and spending it on the other women). He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol and doesn't have any other vices. He respects and tolerates my mom at home and also helps with household chores. In short, apart from being promiscuous outside, he doesn't have any other flaws. Regardless of any psychological issues my dad may have. However, he doesn't agree to divorce and is very willing to live with us. But he can't control himself and always secretly cheats with other women. My mom doesn't know if she should divorce my dad. If my dad can never change this flaw and my mom can't accept it, is divorce the right choice? Is it the best option?

answers.answer_text: Hello, because of my dad's affair, there's a question of whether my mom should divorce him. I feel that you are very concerned about my mom and also want to help share her worries. I don't know your age, but I see that you're already prepared to shoulder my mother's pain. It hurts my heart, so here's a warm hug for you, you child who loves your mom. I see that you say my dad is good in all other aspects except for his addiction to affairs. You have acceptance in your heart for my dad and also see that he can respect and tolerate my mom, do housework, and so on. Or perhaps, this is the reason why my mom can't decide whether to divorce? The emotional state between my dad and mom, maybe only they themselves truly know. My dad doesn't agree to divorce and is very willing to live with you all, which shows that your family also gives him a sense of comfort and belonging. You and my mom are very attractive and easy to identify with, so my dad can't leave the family. But do they really need to divorce? When should they divorce? I think it's still a life issue that they must face themselves. And what you can do is to accompany my mom and see how difficult it is for her. Also, recognize my dad's contributions to this family. The relationship between my dad and mom has many feelings that cannot be explained clearly to their children. This is the reality that children should see. I think whether they divorce or not, the best choice should be made by them! Wishing you well, the world and I love you!

Hello, I sympathize with you, sending you a hug. Regarding the issue you mentioned about whether or not to divorce in the case of an affair, if we approach it as a topic for discussion, I can confidently give you an answer. However, since it involves your parents, I believe there are other factors to consider. In psychology, we don't provide answers; we help you think and find your own answers because the answer always lies within oneself. Psychology also doesn't give you an answer or make decisions for you. It's a matter of principle. "He gives his salary to my mom. Doesn't smoke or drink, has no other bad habits. He respects and accommodates my mom at home and does some household chores." Looking at these aspects alone, your father is a good man. He is a good husband and perhaps a good father. However, he has committed a fatal issue of principle. Infidelity can be acceptable zero times or countless times. This is indeed a matter of principle and cannot be forgiven. But we must also examine the specific reasons and analyze them. We should also consider where his heart lies, whether it's with the family or outside. One more important point is the status of your parents' relationship. Is it very solid and good? Perhaps you need to take your father for psychological counseling or therapy, or even do couples therapy, as this issue is definitely with your father. However, if he refuses, it will be relatively difficult. Another attitude you may need to express to your mother is as follows: 1. You are aware of the situation, 2. She shouldn't worry about it affecting you, 3. It's okay, 4. You still love them, 5. But you love her more, 6. You want her to be happy, 7. So whether she divorces or not is her own decision, a matter of their relationship, 8. Regardless of divorce, they will always be your parents, 9. You will always love them. You need to stand by your mother's side and support her, otherwise, she will be alone and without support. Sending you a hug, wishing you the best.

My suggestion is that you talk to a trusted older relative who has a good relationship with your parents and have them communicate with your parents and suggest doing systematic family therapy. Because in the family, you are just a child, if you try to communicate this issue with your parents, they may reject or even oppose it. But if a older relative in the family suggests it, they may be more likely to accept it to some extent. Secondly, let's talk about your father's behavior. Normally, we all have something or someone that serves as the "third party" in our lives, whether it's work or hobbies for men, or family and children for women. Why am I mentioning this? It's because in your description, your father firstly doesn't have his own hobbies or interests, his life revolves around work and family, and secondly, he has a relationship with someone else. Of course, this is just a speculation, it's possible that your father is not fulfilling his own needs in the family. This possibility is relatively small because your father is not willing to destroy the family relationship. All of the above are just speculations, so it's important to seek professional help and undergo systematic family therapy to find out why such things are happening.

question: A freshman girl feels that her mother lacks ambition, what should she do?
description: Mom's job is relatively easy and she has a lot of free time, but she always likes to spend it on browsing social media. I always suggest that she read more books, newspapers, and learn English (learning English was her own idea, but she didn't persist), and not constantly focus on other people's lives on her phone. However, she always finds excuses and says she is busy every day, which always leads to arguments. I don't want to argue with her, I just hope she can continue learning. My mother lacks motivation, so how can I persuade her to make a change?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: Let's talk and analyze together: #My mother lacks ambition, how can I persuade her to change?# From this sentence, I perceive that you define your mother's behavior as lacking ambition and you want to change her. You can suggest to her to #read more books, newspapers, and learn English#. If she is willing to do this, it would be ideal, but if she is not willing, you should respect her decision. Although your intention is good for her, it might not be her current real need. If you still want to change her, your actions may cross the boundary of the relationship, which will only increase your distress. As a family member, you can make suggestions, but you do not have the authority to force her to change according to your expectations. If you forcefully change her to meet your expectations, then you are already interfering with her life. Can you understand? There are other methods to bring about change, but they are much more difficult. Would you like to try them?

question: What should I do if I encounter a questioner who doesn't use punctuation and I don't want to answer?
description: I recently saw a few question descriptions from participants that gave me a headache. Not to mention the ones with very simple descriptions, some of them were very long paragraphs without any punctuation. It's a bit frustrating. Why don't the participants use punctuation properly?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP: I really understand your feelings. A paragraph without punctuation takes more time to read and it's not easy for us to understand what the OP wants to express. This is a gathering place for psychology enthusiasts or professionals. When we see a question from the OP, we want to help the other person and provide them with warmth. If we can't understand the question without punctuation, we will also feel anxious. Let's take a look at the possible reasons for typing without punctuation. Maybe it's the OP's habit of not using punctuation when sending WeChat or text messages. It could also be because the OP had an urgent matter when they asked the question and didn't have time to use punctuation. It's even possible that the OP was in a bad emotional state that day and didn't feel like using punctuation. Regardless of the reason, both you and the OP, as well as all of us, are here for the same reason, to communicate through words. Each of us is both the responder and the questioner. We come here to seek help and to help others. When we answer the questions from the OP, it can also help us resolve our own emotional difficulties. When we, as questioners, write a paragraph, we are the ones burdened with pressure, seeking help. Perhaps, a sentence written by someone on the other side of the screen can comfort our souls. I understand your feelings because when I answer questions, I also hope that the description of the question can be clear and well-expressed. This way, we can provide targeted help to the person. But even if it's not clear, I still hope to do my best to help the people I can help. Actually, regardless of whether there are punctuation marks in that paragraph, I think that the people who ask these questions are brave because they dare to write down their pain and sadness in words and courageously seek help from the outside world. And I believe that we should also give more patience and care to the people who ask these questions, because behind the words, they are all individuals with feelings of sadness and loneliness, people who hope to receive help. Best wishes.

Hello there! I completely understand your feelings, and I also get a little frustrated with questions that have no punctuation. It's quite an interesting question, and my first reaction is that if you don't want to answer, you don't have to. As for why there are questions with absolutely no punctuation, there could be several reasons, and it's hard to generalize. Following the principle of "separating the project" (cough...), I'll just talk about this issue from the perspective of an answerer. I believe that every answerer chooses to answer questions for their own reasons. It could be because they want to help others, they have solid expertise in the subject matter, they want to achieve self-help in this way, or they seek recognition and appreciation from others... Additionally, because each answerer is interested in and good at different types of questions, everyone has different schedules, energy allocations, and answering principles. Therefore, we will choose which questions to answer based on our own comprehensive situation. Now, to the point, when we, as answerers, see a question with no punctuation (or punctuation used incorrectly, or with many spelling mistakes), it can affect our decision to answer that question. You may suddenly not want to answer a question you initially wanted to answer. That's actually understandable. It's like when you take an exam and your handwriting is messy, the teacher is likely to deduct many points because of it. This point needs to be understood by the questioner. Of course, as answerers, we still hope to help as many people as possible. If we have some good advice for a particular question and if we have enough time, I'm still willing to sincerely look at that question. Let's not forget the original intention, for it defines our outcome. Because I know that when I see a question, I should think about what I can say, even if it may not be very helpful. Because I know that every person who is brave enough to ask their own question and expose their own shortcomings is incredibly courageous and deserving of admiration. Because I know that behind every seemingly simple question, there may be someone quietly enduring various pressures. As an answerer, I hope to show more respect and understanding for every question. Best wishes!

As an answerer, I believe that first of all, one's intention should be correct, and one should be determined to help others from a perspective of love. When we encounter someone's question, we should first ask ourselves whether we are willing to answer this question or if we have any negative emotions such as boredom or dislike. If we do, I think it would be better not to answer the question. Because if we forcibly answer it with impatience, the answer we give to the questioner may be biased. We all have preferences and likes as well as dislikes, which is normal. The key is to find a way that satisfies both parties in order to achieve a long-lasting solution. These are personal opinions provided for reference only. Thank you for the answerer's sharing.

Hello, OP: It seems that you are a responsible and meticulous answerer! In fact, many OPs come with anxiety, so they want to get help all at once, but they are unwilling to provide more information. There are many explanations for this: First, it could be their personality traits, being careless and not paying attention to details; Second, it could be their way of speaking, without punctuation marks, indicating their urgent anxiety, wanting to say everything at once; Third, it could be their attempt to conceal or feeling insecure due to the platform's settings, so they are not willing to expose themselves. For you, there shouldn't be much concern. Replying to questions and wanting to help someone is your personal right and freedom. If you think the lack of punctuation marks from some OPs is a problem, it may be challenging your perfectionism and causing anxiety.

Hello, I'm going to write down my thoughts. Usually, when I see descriptions without punctuation marks, I generally feel quite uncomfortable. I would guess that the author is going through something and their emotions are erupting at that moment. I don't think I have ever answered that kind of question because it's really difficult to accept. When I see it, I also think to myself that the author doesn't care about others' feelings. With this assumption in mind, I'm afraid I might have unconscious subjective judgments. Since I can't start getting to know the author with a blank mind, I feel that I'm not suitable for the author, at least in that specific moment. Not answering would be better for the author. I don't know under what circumstances the author wrote that paragraph. If I don't understand the situation and still force myself to accept the author, I feel fake. I want to face others sincerely. If given the opportunity to learn more about the author, I would love to share my thoughts on their continuously posted questions. Maybe my first question would be, "What happened to you when you were writing your question without punctuation marks?" I particularly agree with Miss Non-stop's words. The author writing their own question and showing their inner pain to others, seeking help from the outside world, takes a lot of courage. We should cherish the inner world of that stranger and maintain our admiration for them. What if you don't want to answer a question from an author who doesn't use punctuation marks? Simply don't answer. Best wishes.

1. Haha, don't let countertransference affect your diagnosis and treatment. As a qualified psychological counselor, you need to have a strong inner self and fully respect the client. Use a continuous flow of love to dissolve the clouds in the client's heart. Repeat to yourself a few times, "He's also not easy, sigh." Haha, try a few times, it's effective as tested by me. 
2. Also, everyone has different opinions on the same situation. I think it's fine, no need for punctuation, as long as it's coherent, just read it again. Hope it can help you. Feel happy every day, and the world will be yours.

question: Can't find the words to say? What could be the reason?
description: I find that sometimes I can't speak out my thoughts. For example, when the teacher asks a question, I do have thoughts in my mind, but I don't know if it's because I'm afraid of giving the wrong answer and being ridiculed, or if I think the thought is childish, so I can't say it out and can only remain silent. Sometimes, when I meet new classmates, I can't smoothly pronounce their names. It's like my voice gets stuck and can't come out. I don't know what the reason is and if it can be solved. Thank you.

answers.answer_text: Hello, when we are too concerned about what others think and their opinions, it becomes difficult for us to be at ease. This also reflects a lack of confidence and self-esteem; the more insecure we are, the more we seek validation from others and fear not receiving it. In psychology, there is a term called projection, where we project our own thoughts onto others, assuming that others think the same way we do. Therefore, people who lack confidence tend to believe that others may question them, while those who harbor animosity towards others often believe that others harbor animosity towards them as well. In reality, these are merely subjective thoughts and not facts. For example, during a class, if you answer a question, you don't know how others will react. It is just your own disbelief in yourself that leads you to assume that others might mock you or think you are childish. However, these are all subjective imaginations. So, if you want to change, you can only gradually overcome feelings of inferiority and increase your self-confidence. There is no magic solution for this, it requires slow and steady effort. You can give yourself positive self- affirmations and bravely challenge your fears. Summon the courage to act, and perhaps you will find that others' reactions are not what you imagined. When facing new classmates, because you are too worried about how others will perceive you, you become too nervous and stumble. But you should know that the other person may also be just as nervous as you are. In a Japanese drama called "Nagi's New Life," the female protagonist once encountered someone she wanted to greet. She kept thinking in her mind: will I bother the other person? Will they dislike me? Later, she mustered up the courage to say hello, and to her surprise, the person was very happy. In fact, the person also wanted to get to know her, but was just too afraid to take the first step. They were delighted that she took the initiative to say hello. Even if you stumble, don't worry, just smile and you can still show warmth and goodwill, bringing you closer to the other person. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).
Hello, the paragraph you provided is already in English.

question: How can I control someone who tells others my privacy complaints after I confide in her?
description: I shared some private matters and complaints with a trusted person, but she told others, and I unintentionally heard it from someone else. Sometimes, I really don't know what I should say and what I shouldn't say, and I don't know who I should trust. I always worry that what I tell others will be passed on to someone else. I always feel like I don't know how to get along with the people around me.

answers.answer_text: Hello～ I understand your feelings very well, sending you a hug～ It can be really difficult when you share your privacy with someone and that person tells others about it. It does make it hard to trust others. How do you control someone who can't keep their mouth shut? I want to tell you, don't try to control or change anyone. Because they are not you, and you cannot change them. When you want to change someone, it's actually because you feel anxious, and you want to alleviate your own anxiety by changing others. But a better way is to confront your own anxiety. No matter who you tell your privacy to, there is always a risk of it being leaked. In a way, it doesn't have much to do with trusting or not trusting others. It simply means that if you are willing to trust someone, then you are willing to take on that risk. And if you don't trust someone, then you won't share those private matters. For those who leak your privacy, you should keep a distance from them. Don't let them repeatedly hurt or affect you in this way. There are definitely people in this world who are willing to keep your secrets, and there are many of them. Of course, it's still important to be cautious in what you say, unless both parties are willing to open up to each other. Best wishes～.

question: 15-year-old girl, in the past few months I feel like I have a illness?
description: I feel like I have an illness, a mental illness. When I used to argue with that woman, I used to think about death and suicide, but now I can't wait for her to die or just stab him to death. I have had suicidal thoughts and even taken action, but always stopped at the last moment. It's so frustrating. He is very stubborn and nobody can change his mind. I don't want to argue with him. But I can't just let things go in one ear and out the other, I can't stay calm. He speaks very rudely and can't communicate properly. Every time we argue, it's because of something he said, and in the heat of the argument he says I want to kill him. Originally, I didn't have thoughts of killing him, but when I heard that statement, at first I was heartbroken and angry, and now I just want to get rid of him, get rid of the person who brought me into this world, I would be happy if he died. He simply doesn't believe me, doesn't agree with my thoughts, denies my dreams and passions. Our values are completely incompatible. Perhaps it's because of the significant age difference between us. I'm not unreasonable, but he just doesn't listen. I think I'm really annoyed by his pretentious concern and voice. I feel like throwing up when he argues with that high-pitched voice. Maybe I'm actually going crazy. Driven crazy. Perhaps, I really am sick? Oh, so frustrated.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling

answers.answer_text: Hugs to the questioner~ That woman is your mother, and it seems that the conflict between you has led you to no longer see her as a mother, right? She doesn't believe your words, doesn't agree with your thoughts, denies your dreams and passions, and your values don't align. All of this makes you want the person controlling your life to disappear. Every word she says adds to your psychological burden. I want to say that many children have had the thought of making their parents disappear, for various reasons. They might even think about why their parents don't just die because they didn't give them candy. To be honest, I have also had this experience. At first, I would harm myself to calm my emotions, thinking that everyone would be better off if I died. Later, it turned into wanting my mother to die. The first time I had this thought, I was shocked. After calming down, I thought, is it really necessary to take away her life because of what I've been through? The answer is no.
