I was filled with shame and didn't know how to make it through the rest of the class, my face still burning with embarrassment. Since then, whenever I hear my desk mate's voice, I feel uncomfortable and have sexual thoughts, even though I really don't want to, and it makes me feel ashamed. Later on, this happened with any male I encountered. I became increasingly scared in my mind, developing anxiety disorder. Now I'm a senior in high school, and it's still happening. I don't know what's wrong with me or what to do about it. (In my eighth and ninth grade, I also experienced sudden attraction to both teachers and students, but the feeling of embarrassment would go away after a while.)

answers.answer_text: Hello, the described situation "ever since then, whenever I hear my classmate's voice, I have a particularly uncomfortable physical reaction related to sexuality, and the key is that I really don't want it to be this way, and I feel very ashamed. Later on, it became that I would have this reaction whenever I see a male, and I am becoming more and more scared in my mind, it is a fear of them in terms of sexuality." In this paragraph, it seems like you have obsessive thoughts: that is, forcing yourself to suppress a certain thought or thought pattern, but the more you suppress it, the more it will appear frequently in your mind. Another issue is "feelings of being perceived," which is also a cause of shame and anxiety. Feeling perceived is the feeling that one's thoughts or ideas have been noticed by others. These two issues are both psychological problems and belong to neurotic disorders. They are mainly caused by irrational beliefs. Under the pressure of the college entrance examination, emotions and behaviors become compulsive, coupled with inadequate analysis of things, these problems will arise. When it comes to "sex," it is because during this period, sexual desire is mostly suppressed, and your focus is too much on "sex," resulting in problems related to sexuality. Sex cannot be suppressed, of course, it cannot be indulged either, but should be guided and redirected, accepting the comprehensive changes brought about by the college entrance examination emotionally. Sexual fantasies are an important way for individuals to satisfy their sexual needs and are a normal physiological and psychological self-satisfaction outlet. The frequency of sexual fantasies is related to individual consciousness and focus. With less attention, there will be fewer sexual fantasies. You can control your sexual needs yourself, control here means substitution, redirection, and seeking personal achievements, instead of simply satisfying oneself through sexual fantasies or "masturbation." This is cheap, low-value, and easy to fall into moral traps. Over time, psychological distortions will occur, leading to mental illness. Therefore, regardless of your true "sexual orientation" at the moment, you can temporarily accept it and tell yourself that just having thoughts but not acting on them does not have any moral or legal wrongdoing. Just like the old saying goes, "The most wicked act is at the forefront, judge not by superficial appearance but look at one's heart, there are no good people in the world by appearance." In terms of the root cause of neurotic disorders, there is another issue which is unwillingness to grow. Unwillingness to grow means continuing to face new problems or people and things with childish preferences or judgments. This is a social disconnection and a manifestation of delayed personal growth. What you can do is accepting your thoughts or beliefs, but with a positive judgement, establish behavioral standards for yourself and have behaviors that are accepted by society. In a child's time, there is often only right or wrong, or good or bad people, but in the adult world, it is not just about right or wrong, it also involves value and meaning, self-moral standards, and compliance with social rules. So what you need is to look at things with an adult's thinking and perspective. Regarding what your teacher said, that he can tell what someone is thinking by their expression or behavior. It can be clearly said that he might know that you are thinking about sexual or play-related things, but he definitely does not know everything. Because everyone has gone through puberty, it is not surprising to know what students think during this period. If he knows what you are thinking, then he must have also gone through the same stage as you are now, and thought of those strange things, and even more "unconventional" than what you are currently thinking. Furthermore, even if he knows, it doesn't matter, you haven't done anything, he cannot judge you guilty based on your thoughts or things inside your mind. Whether there is guilt or not, it depends on actions, if you have done what you should or should not do, or if you have done something that you shouldn't have done. You should seize this time to expand your understanding of the world, otherwise, the essays you write will definitely be like those of children. The problems you are facing now are hidden problems that need to be solved aside from the knowledge in textbooks before the college entrance examination. Good luck!

Hello there! I sense your anxiety, so here's a virtual hug for you. It's actually very normal to experience sexual fantasies during adolescence. Everyone has their own sexual fantasies, whether it's about a celebrity, someone you know, or even a stranger. The important thing is to have the right understanding of it. Approach sexuality with a calm mindset. When those images pop up in your mind, try to distract yourself and silently say to yourself, "It's normal." Don't get too caught up in it, just treat it as a normal thing, without feeling ashamed or consciously telling yourself not to think about it. You can proactively learn some basic sexual knowledge. Once you have a better understanding, you won't feel afraid, and your curiosity about sexuality will decrease. This is a normal part of growing up, so don't put too much pressure on yourself. It might be that, subconsciously, you've added more stress to yourself when you reached your senior year. Just try to redirect your attention and things will gradually get better. Remember, the world and I love you.

question: How to cope with the distress of body image and appearance dissatisfaction?
description: I am always very dissatisfied with my body shape and appearance, despite the reassurances from people around me. I still can't control it. Can you please tell me how to improve?

answers.answer_text: I feel that no one can do something that makes them uncomfortable in the long term. You said that you can't accept your own appearance, and it's evident that you really want to gain recognition or love from others. I understand how you feel because I am also a chubby girl. I care a lot about how others see me. Whenever someone looks at me, I become sensitive and wonder if they are judging me or finding fault with me. What's so great about them? You're amazing. As time goes by, I am slowly growing up. Instead of trying to change others' thoughts or changing myself, it's better to work hard to become better, of course, if you are willing. When your focus is on yourself, you will naturally radiate and those who are willing to approach you will naturally come closer. Finally, you can ask yourself a question: why do I care so much about how others see me? Best wishes, both me and the world love you.

question: Due to abusive family relationships and pressure, I have run away from home.
description: The partner has always treated me poorly, being forced into marriage by my parents, postpartum depression, a year of continuous loss of personal freedom, and now pregnant again.
keywords: Marriage, marriage management, prenatal and postnatal.

answers.answer_text: Wu Feikong's analysis: 1. From your description, it seems like you are unmarried and pregnant, which can be a cause of concern for parents. After all, marriage has legal significance and can provide protection for the woman and the baby, recognizing the status of the wife and child. 2. You mentioned postpartum depression, which is a problem that needs to be taken seriously. If you are not happy, how can you take care of the baby? Therefore, you can seek help from a psychological counselor to make yourself happy and then consider other matters. 3. The fact that you came here to ask questions shows that you have some self-awareness, which is great. Self-help can be helpful, and I hope you can continue to find ways to overcome your pain. 4. The primary goal is to make yourself happy because, after all, life is meant to be enjoyed. 5. I wish you can find happiness through your own efforts!

Hello, OP. Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand that: (1) You feel that your partner is treating you poorly and that your marriage was forced upon you. (2) You feel like you have been subjected to abuse from your family. Here are my analysis and advice, hoping to help you: (1) First, you mentioned that your partner is treating you poorly and that your parents forced you into this marriage. Undoubtedly, being forced into a marriage like this has trapped you in an environment where you cannot be happy. Although I cannot fully understand your situation, just thinking about this kind of situation makes me feel uneasy. Therefore, even after giving birth to a child, you still feel unhappy. This is why postpartum depression has appeared. (2) Secondly, you mentioned that you have lost your personal freedom for a year and became pregnant again. You ran away from home. Have you ever thought that your situation would improve after having a child? But unexpectedly, your situation remained poor even after having a child. So, did your anxiety escalate after having another child? (3) Finally, I advise you not to continue enduring an unhappy marriage. You can find a way to free yourself from your current situation and seek support from people you trust. Do not sacrifice yourself. #The world and I love you. Wishing you well~.

question: I will graduate with a master's degree next year, but I haven't been able to return to campus due to the pandemic. The stress is overwhelming!
description: Due to the pandemic, we have not been able to return to school until now. I still have one graduation experiment left to complete, and my thesis has not made any progress. How should I cope with this kind of pressure?

answers.answer_text: Hello, you have come for help with great inner distress and even pain. It takes great courage, and I see your inner longing. This year's pandemic has affected many people, including office workers, students, and others. Because home is not naturally a work environment or a study environment, many people have been affected academically. Being away from school makes it harder to stay disciplined and proactive. However, from a psychological perspective, everyone has a tendency to be lazy and want to be spoon-fed. Therefore, it is normal for studying or writing papers to be disrupted by laziness or procrastination, leading to feelings of frustration, disappointment, or even despair. From the perspective of motivation, the lack of discipline, proactivity, and the psychological mechanism of "laziness" may include the following reasons: resistance and "attack" towards tasks or papers expressed through procrastination, not making good choices between rest and work, not fulfilling the desire for rest, possibly having some self-confidence issues resulting in poor quality of work, not experiencing "benefits" especially on a mental level, engaging in psychological self-torture by expressing past mistakes like procrastination and self-punishment through a sense of "not being good enough," longing for motivation but not finding it, hence lacking inner motivation and needing affirmation and praise from others, fear of facing failure that feels uncontrollable, and potentially having an unsound plan. Faced with this, perhaps you should reflect on and prioritize addressing the issues with your graduation thesis. Start small by creating a habit formation plan for yourself for 21 days. Think about the underlying psychological motivation. Consider seeking psychological counseling for support and guidance for a sustained period of time. I wish you the best and recommend seeking specialized counseling for personal growth.

Hello, OP. This year, due to the pandemic, work in various industries has been delayed or disrupted to varying degrees, students cannot go to school, and shops cannot open. Some companies are even facing the tragic situation of closure. As a master's student, you cannot return to campus, conduct graduation experiments, or have any progress on your thesis. It is normal to feel anxious and worried in such a situation. I have experienced this feeling before when school was not in session. But because of the pandemic, schools will have new arrangements. If there is enough time when you return to campus, it is possible to make up for these missed things. If time is tight, the school may also cancel them. Your classmates have not started school yet, so the school will definitely have new plans. Therefore, there is no need to worry too much, just focus on the work at hand and make a reasonable arrangement for the vacation time. It is more important to live the present well. Best wishes~.

question: I have slept a lot, but I still feel tired all the time. What should I do? Is it a physical problem or a mental problem?
description: I have slept a lot, but still feel tired. I don't know if it's a physical issue or if there are psychological problems.

answers.answer_text: Hello, sometimes the more we sleep, the more tired we feel and the more we feel lacking in energy. So it's important to sleep just the right amount each day and have a regular schedule. When it's time to sleep at night, make sure to get a good night's rest, and when it's time to wake up in the morning, get up and do your own things. I think you don't have much to do during the day now, so you feel sleepy. In the future, try to engage in activities that interest you during the day and try to live a more fulfilling life. This way, at least you won't feel sleepy during the day, and gradually you can adjust your schedule. Best wishes~.

question: Worker, life is too bitter and hard. I'm constantly restless, what should I do?
description: I don't know if most young people feel the same way as me, but life feels really tough. It's been over two years since I graduated, and I haven't been able to save a penny. I earn a little over 9,000 yuan per month, but after deducting my mortgage and car loan payments of 6,500 yuan, rent of 600 yuan, phone bill of 200 yuan, and gas expenses of 500 yuan, I only have a little over 2,000 yuan left for my own expenses, including miscellaneous expenses. My parents are getting older (I'm really grateful to them, at least they helped me with having a car and house, I will always love them, haha), and they keep saying that I'm getting older and should settle down. It's true, I'm 26 years old already, but I'm afraid to start a relationship because I don't have money. Being in a relationship requires spending money, and I don't feel comfortable asking my parents for more help. After all, I'm already an adult. But listening to them nagging every day makes me feel anxious and I don't even know what they're talking about anymore, but it's just annoying. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I understand your feelings very well. Nowadays, most young people who have recently graduated are in the same situation. They don't earn enough money to support themselves and face a lot of pressure. Among the many graduates, you are already considered quite outstanding. After all, you have a stable salary and own a house and a car. Many young people who have graduated for one or two years are still unemployed at home, preparing for various exams, without stable jobs, let alone houses and cars. Some of my friends who have just graduated are in this situation. They earn three to four thousand yuan a month in second or third-tier cities, barely enough for their own expenses, let alone saving money to buy houses and cars. Compared with them, your situation is much better. Although you have a higher salary, you have to spend nearly two-thirds of it on mortgage and car payments, leaving only one-third for your own expenses, so you need to budget and manage your finances carefully. If you still feel tight, you can consider looking for a higher-paying job or doing some investments or small businesses. Your parents want you to be in a relationship, so you can meet some girls. Although dating now may require money for meals and movies, the expenses are not necessarily high. Most girls are not materialistic. They have their own jobs and can support themselves. If you really don't have enough money, your parents will definitely be willing to support you. They would prefer you to have a girlfriend now and have a good family in the future. Best wishes~.

question: 14-year-old boy, for three years, feels inexplicably sad. What should be done?
description: Frequently, for a whole day at a time, I would inexplicably feel extremely sad, and then a while later, I would inexplicably feel extremely angry. I have had multiple thoughts of death. My parents don't understand, and I have no friends. I often feel a sense of frustration in my chest, which then leads to chest pains. What should I do?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: There must be something blocked in the chest, wanting to come out but unable to. Even if you ignore it, it will still come out and bother you. 1. When feeling sad: find a quiet and safe place, have a good cry, let the tears flow freely; of course, you can also listen to music that suits you. You can also go to the cinema to watch a suitable tear-jerking movie, the purpose is also to let the tears flow freely. The so-called suitability means that it resonates with you and makes tears flow uncontrollably. 2. When feeling chest pain or anger, still find a safe place and maintain a comfortable posture. Place your hands on your chest and ask yourself: if it wants to speak, what would it say? 3. Before going to bed at night, say a few words to your dreams, express your problems, and let the dreams guide you to find the answers. 4. Seek professional counseling, it will be helpful for you.

14 years old, it's really difficult to feel upset but not be understood by others. I suggest spending 29.9 yuan to find a counselor for a consultation pre-communication, listen to the counselor's opinions. Although the consultation pre-communication is only 20 minutes, you can generally get an idea and receive a treatment or counseling direction. Based on your description, I hope your parents can take it seriously and take you for medical treatment or involve a psychologist as soon as possible to provide psychological assistance. It seems like you may be mentally ill, just like having a common cold; it's treatable, so don't be afraid. Nowadays, many parents have little understanding of psychological problems. Once psychological issues are mentioned, they easily associate it with mental problems, and might feel fear or refuse to believe it, especially if it's happening in their own family. This is a process and can be understood. But as things happen, they will gradually accept it, you can find relevant information for them to read or have a psychologist or doctor communicate with them.

question: Afraid to tell classmates and friends about negative things, afraid of being misunderstood and abandoned.
description: Bad things refer to things that make oneself feel bad, such as being unjustly doubted or slandered by other classmates (I feel uncomfortable so I think it is a bad thing). What should I do to eliminate this kind of thinking? I feel very upset.

answers.answer_text: First of all, what kind of classmates and friends does the questioner want to confide in? If they are just classmates who study together every day without much social interaction, then it is understandable that the questioner may feel misunderstood. However, if the questioner wants to confide in friends who share similar values and judgment, then there is no need to worry excessively. Secondly, regarding the issue of feeling talked about and demeaned. If the questioner has not violated school rules or engaged in behavior deviating from social moral norms, then I believe the main reason for the questioner being demeaned is simply due to a stereotypical impression formed after the first encounter. In fact, the creation of stereotypes is very simple. When people first meet, it could be as trivial as someone wearing clothes that you don't like, which can lead to a negative stereotypical impression of that person. And afterwards, no matter what that person does, you will feel aversion towards them. This may be the reason why the questioner is facing demeaning remarks. However, when faced with such a problem, if the other party has not impacted the questioner's daily life through their actions, then the questioner does not need to pay attention to it. There is a popular saying that goes, "I'm not a currency, and even if I were, there are still people who only like the US Dollar." Therefore, the questioner does not need to doubt themselves because of the bias of a few individuals. In addition, if the questioner wants to confide in someone, my suggestion is to confide in classmates and friends who share the same values. This can help avoid additional troubles for the questioner. And as for being abandoned by friends, the reason why people become friends is because there is something in common between them that makes them belong to the same group. However, when the differences between you outweigh the commonalities, then you can no longer consider yourselves part of the same group. This is not about someone abandoning someone else, it's just because there are differences and disparities between you. Everyone is independent, and where there are similarities, there are differences. When your friends cannot embrace your differences, you can also choose to confide in someone who can understand and accept you.

question: A 20-year-old girl fell in love with herself. Who exactly is this person she refers to?
description: I don't know when it started, but I fell in love with myself. It's like the love between the main characters in novels or TV dramas, where my inner self is very gentle (even though I haven't been in a romantic relationship for 20 years, I can still feel those sweet feelings). And my inner self is always there to speak softly to me, help me, comfort me, and even supervise me in the things that happen to me. I am actually very distressed because I can't be with her in this real world. I would like to know who she really is and how to adjust my mood. Thank you.
keywords: Love, sexual orientation, attachment and dependency.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, seeing your words is like seeing you in person. After reading your description, although you said that the person you like is yourself, in reality, that person is both you and not you. You mentioned that when you encounter something, you share it with your "her" who comforts, encourages, helps, and supervises you. This "her" is actually another personality of yours, perhaps the person you aspire to be. It's important to know that each of us has diversity within ourselves. Some people develop different personalities, called inner personalities, as a result. For example, children who have experienced abuse may develop a personality who feels that the abused child is not them, and they themselves are enjoying a safe distance, which serves as a means of protection. Now, you have developed a separate personality who comforts and accompanies you, allowing you to feel a sense of companionship when facing pain or joy. You love this inner personality because she is what you have created, a beautiful existence. In reality, you won't find someone like her because nobody is perfect. However, you have bestowed all your desires for beauty upon her. So how can you not love her? You can continue to coexist with her, but you shouldn't become too engrossed in this feeling. Otherwise, you may reject people who try to get close to you because no one will treat you like she does. Therefore, you need to try to delve into your true self. You need to understand who this "her" in your heart is and also understand who you truly are because she and you are actually two sides of the same coin. You can love her, but you must love yourself more. Understand every aspect of yourself, including your flaws and strengths. Only then will you have a comprehensive understanding of yourself and know which side to show to others in social and professional situations. When facing setbacks, the "her" in your heart can console you, but you also need to grow and harmoniously coexist with her using your better side. Although she cannot appear in reality, her qualities will gradually influence you. Eventually, you and she will become fully integrated. It is only then that you truly become one. I hope these suggestions can be helpful to you. Click "useful" if you find them so. Grateful to have met you.

I'm glad you have such a refreshing and unconventional hobby - liking yourself! It seems that you like the excellent version of yourself, which is even more worth celebrating. There are many facets to oneself - the younger self, the childhood self, the self who made mistakes, the self from yesterday, and the self of tomorrow. In addition, we have our bodies, wisdom, emotions, senses, social interactions, interactions with the environment, digestion and absorption of nutrients, and souls. Each aspect is like a different part of oneself. I also like myself and I divide myself into two people. For example, when it comes to the self who made mistakes yesterday, I console that ignorant self with the knowledge and growth I have gained today. I thank him for enabling me to grow deeper and bid him farewell. Similarly, I also express gratitude to the present self who is striving today by imagining a better self in the future. It is my efforts that allow him to have a better experience. However, I love myself without expecting my body, emotions, or soul to be present with me in reality. Everyone knows that is impossible. Nevertheless, I still deeply love that self of mine, and I can't distinguish which one is reality and which one is ideal. Anyway, they are all me. For example, I have a strange belief that I do not make mistakes, even if I make a big mistake now and haven't learned from it to grow, I still believe that I do not make mistakes. Whether it's self-deception or not, I just like believing in myself that way. He is both the self of the imagination and the reality. That's all I'll say. I hope you can distinguish between reality and imagination. Since they are all you, let them work together and create a better tomorrow. No need to separate them so clearly. Feel happy! It's not worth your suffering!

Hello, dear questioner. After reading your description, I would like to say that it is truly a wonderful thing that you can love yourself in this way. We know that people's joys and sorrows are different from each other, and in interpersonal relationships, there will inevitably be situations where there is a lack of understanding and empathy. However, you are the person who understands your own feelings the best, knowing when you are happy and when you are sad. If you can understand yourself, accept your feelings, and respond and act accordingly, meeting your own needs, then this kind of "relationship" may be the safest and most fulfilling. However, unfortunately, "she" cannot physically exist in the real world. And romantic relationships in real life may not develop exactly as you imagine, and they may not always be "under control" or constantly "gentle" and "sweet". Instead, they may go through unexpected interactions, and you will only understand these tastes when you personally experience them. Perhaps all kinds of relationships in the world are like this, it is difficult to achieve a "perfect balance", and only after experiencing them will you gain various insights. At this moment, I would like to encourage you, young questioner, to follow your heart, accept your feelings, and enjoy the experience. Because the world is full of infinite possibilities. Whether you want to continue accompanying "yourself" like this, or one day meet someone else you want to be with, both are worth celebrating. As long as you feel comfortable, happy, and satisfied at this moment, then this is a "good relationship" :) I wish you happiness.

question: Can you hit a child while educating them? How to establish authority?
description: The child is disrespectful towards the parents, threatening to harm others with a pair of scissors. Is it appropriate to hit them? What should be done if the child does not listen when spoken to?
keywords: Family, family relationships, the process of growing up, and communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: ~~First, give the poster a hug. From the description, we can understand that: 1. The child disrespects their parents and threatens to hurt someone with scissors. 2. The poster wants to hit the child but considers if it is inappropriate. They don't know how to establish authority with the child without resorting to physical punishment. [Some analysis and suggestions]: 1. The fact that the poster is questioning whether to establish authority with the child shows that they are not inclined to be an authoritarian parent. They hope their child can grow up in a better environment, which is why they feel confused. 2. Punishment may have a place in a child's development, but physical abuse should be avoided as it can cause physical or psychological harm. Finding other ways to let the child know that their behavior is wrong might achieve the desired effect. For example, taking away activities the child enjoys or reducing their screen time can be explained to the child that it was a consequence of their bad behavior. If their behavior improves, the privileges can be restored. 3. Moreover, parental authority is more about setting a good example in everyday life rather than occasional outbursts of anger. Through the child's mistake, the poster can reflect on their and their partner's parenting methods, whether there have been any shortcomings in their teaching, if they themselves or their partner have used scissors to threaten or disrespected elders. Could the child be imitating someone else's behavior? By reflecting on and improving their parenting approach, the child will experience better development. Hope this helps and all the best to the poster.

Preliminarily speaking, there are quite a few issues: 1. Lack of respect for parents, 2. Gesturing with scissors in a way that could harm others, 3. Whether it is appropriate to discipline a child, 4. A disobedient child. To sum up the problem, how can a child grow up to be friendly under the guidance of respectful parents? From a developmental perspective, children naturally have a deep relationship and emotional interaction with their parents, but this interaction develops under the guidance of parents. First, have the child and parents established a good attachment and intimate relationship? This requires parents to give appropriate attention, hugs, and support to their children, allowing them to feel a sense of belonging and security from their parents and forming a good attachment and intimate relationship. Second, are parents setting a good example for their children through their actions and words? This mainly involves combining actions and words because body language is the easiest for children to directly accept and learn from in communication, and it also accounts for a significant portion of communication. Verbal communication is mainly abstract, and the meaning may not be immediately clear to children. Lastly, to establish the parents' authority, it is necessary to establish a relatively stable family order by adhering to social norms, avoiding being overly rigid or excessively flexible, and gradually nurturing the child's characteristics through interactive games.

It can be done, but it should not be done indiscriminately. Specific situations need to be discussed specifically. For this particular issue, several points need to be considered: 1. How old is the child? 2. Why does the child not respect the parents? Do they respect others? 3. Why does the child wave scissors around? Is this behavior common? 4. How is the child's education situation at home? What intervention methods have been used? 5. How is the relationship between other family members? How do they interact on a regular basis? Asking these questions would already involve enough content for a counseling session. Only then can we determine whether it is necessary to resort to physical discipline. If the family relationship and parental education are not major issues, and the child exhibits some excessive misbehavior, it is acceptable to discipline them physically as a means of punishment and establishing behavioral norms. However, it is advisable to administer physical discipline in a matter-of-fact manner, providing proper guidance and not escalating to the point of humiliating the child. If there are problems in the relationships between family members and the parents do not respect the child, or if the parents' previous parenting methods have been problematic (such as excessive neglect, overindulgence, blame, etc.), physically disciplining the child will only intensify conflicts. It would be more effective to address the parents' behavior. This is just a joke, but if this is the situation, it would be necessary to focus on the relationships within the family. Ultimately, whether to physically discipline a child or not depends on the specific circumstances and needs to be analyzed accordingly. I hope both the child and the parents can become happier as the child grows up. ^_^

question: I have been feeling extremely dark inside in the past two years, how can I become happy?
description: The past two years, 2019 and 2020, have felt dark. Although I had never achieved my goals before, my inner self remained positive. However, recently, I have been feeling extremely overwhelmed and defeated as everything around me is not what I desire.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, life purpose.

answers.answer_text: ~I want to give you a warm hug~ Perhaps due to the pressure caused by not achieving goals for a long time, it is easy to feel frustrated. You need to have confidence in yourself, find the areas for improvement, and continue to work hard. Believe that you will be able to achieve your goals in the future. When feeling stressed, maybe you can go to the gym or engage in other sports to release some tension. When negative emotions arise, perhaps you can let go of what you're doing, take a moment to calm down, or go for a walk. In your daily life, you can also communicate more with your family or friends, and arrange activities with friends to strike a balance between work and leisure. This may help you achieve a better mental state and be more efficient in completing tasks.

question: A 20-year-old girl often experiences hallucinations, and she easily cries and feels uncomfortable.
description: I am a 20-year-old girl and I constantly experience hallucinations of spiders or people rising from the ground, as well as strange creatures and the sensation of being touched by them. Sometimes, I hear voices during these hallucinations, but I don't feel them myself. I easily get excited and feel inexplicably uncomfortable and want to cry for no reason.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, disease diagnosis, treatment methods.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. It's great to meet you here. I feel very sorry for your current state, sending you a big hug. The questioner mentioned experiencing hallucinations, such as spiders or strange creatures appearing from the wall, as well as unpredictable bouts of crying and easily getting agitated in daily life. These hallucinations and "unexplained" emotions are not random occurrences. They may not have a direct, explicit cause, but they could be related to your personal experiences, personality, genetics, and other factors. Therefore, these negative emotions, which generate fear at this stage, are more like an alarm for your mental state. First of all, because hallucinations have already occurred, they cannot be easily resolved through emotional venting. Each person has a limited psychological tolerance, and once it exceeds that limit without timely guidance, it can lead to psychological problems or even mental illnesses. So it is important to seek timely psychological and medical assistance, have open communication with professionals, and it can effectively help you get through this stage. At this stage, having enough emotional support from the family can provide a sense of security and confidence. Therefore, I suggest you communicate your current situation with your family. When your emotions are unstable and you feel inexplicably depressed, your family can create a peaceful environment for you. Meanwhile, establishing a good intimate relationship with your family is also a good way to overcome inner fears, loneliness, and feelings of being unseen. No matter what happens, there will always be moments when we feel helpless or even overwhelmed by pain. If you cannot overcome it on your own, it is necessary to seek help from your family and doctors in a timely manner. Keep going! The world and I love you! Take care~ A little mushroom hoping for a gentle world and giving itself time to grow freely.

Hello, I'm concerned about your situation after reading your description, and I suggest that you take it seriously. Hallucinations are generally classified into: (1) auditory hallucinations: which can manifest as meaningless noises or meaningful voices. (2) visual hallucinations: which can involve seeing meaningless colors, flashes, or formed objects, often inducing a feeling of fear, such as seeing spiders or people rising from the ground. (3) olfactory and gustatory hallucinations: these two types of hallucinations often coexist, and result in unpleasant tastes or smells. (4) tactile hallucinations: which can manifest as a sense of touch, crawling sensations, needle pricks, electric shocks, or even a sense of sexual contact. For example, you may feel the presence of strange creatures and the sensation of them touching you. These symptoms suggest the possibility of organic brain lesions or psychiatric issues. I recommend you visit the relevant department at the hospital to rule out any organic brain lesions first, and then seek psychiatric consultation.

Hello, OP. It's strange to feel like crying and feeling uncomfortable without any reason. Perhaps, usually when faced with negative events, you suppress your true emotions and can't express them, causing them to build up. The inability to release this stagnant negative energy reduces your threshold for tolerance, making it easy for you to get agitated and want to express all your emotions when even slightly emotionally stimulated. You can try exercising and meditating to scientifically and healthily release negative emotions. If you are experiencing hallucinations and saying things out of your control, but you are aware that these hallucinations are causing you some trouble, it is recommended that you go to the hospital with the accompaniment of your family to undergo some relevant examinations. Simple question and answer statements may not be able to uncover the underlying causes of hallucinations and provide solutions. Best wishes.

Hugs and kisses to you. I see that you are feeling very uncomfortable and I don't know what to do. I noticed three things in your description: experiencing hallucinations, sometimes saying things, and the presence of "spiders," which could be an intention or represent projections. They are rising from the floor with strange sensations and a feeling of being touched. This could also represent your actions or feelings towards this imagery. You mentioned experiencing hallucinations and saying things, but you are not aware of it yourself. You also tend to get easily agitated and feel inexplicably sad and like crying. These emotions have no apparent cause. Due to the brevity of your description, it is difficult to obtain more useful information and understanding. However, it is important to note that these signs indicate a need for adjustment! Emotions and hallucinations can make you feel strange and uncomfortable, and I am glad that you have noticed these signals. They may not necessarily be caused by any "major event" or something you have done wrong; it could be due to physiological factors. Therefore, if I were to give you any advice, it would be to go to the hospital for a proper diagnosis to determine the specific issue causing these symptoms, and then receive appropriate treatment. I hope this can help you, the world and I love you~.

Hello there. How long have you been experiencing your current state, and have there been any significant recent events? Currently, it seems that you are experiencing symptoms of visual hallucinations, tactile hallucinations, unstable emotions, discomfort, neurotic symptoms, and mental symptoms. It is recommended that you go to a professional hospital for relevant examinations. Generally, if it is considered a mental illness, early detection and treatment can have very good results. Medication treatment can be very effective. (Of course, I am not a doctor, so I cannot make a diagnosis. This is just a suggestion.) It is best to seek medical help and listen to the diagnosis and advice of a professional doctor. In the meantime, try to find ways to help yourself relax and avoid excessive stress, which can lead to greater emotional fluctuations. You can try meditation and observe whether the occurrence of hallucinations and other symptoms is related to stress. Hang in there, and I hope this is helpful to you.

question: Feeling disgusting as a welfare worker, how can I forget this experience?
description: I am actually a girl who is very conscious about cleanliness, to the extent that I didn't have my first love until I was twenty years old, despite having many suitors. But I made a foolish decision and became a cam girl to make quick money, so I joined a small group. I did a video that lasted less than 5 minutes, you know the content, I didn't show my face, and that person paid and then left. In the end, I received thirty dollars. I have been disgusted with myself for a whole day, or only because it has been just one day, I don't know if I will continue to feel disgusted for many more days. I have a boyfriend whom I love very much, and I feel like crying even as I type these words. I really want to see him and hug him, but I know that what I did is unforgivable if he finds out. I truly, I only realized how despicable and disgusting this kind of thing is when I was doing it yesterday afternoon. I really regret it so much. Of course, I will never do such a thing again in the future, but right now, the psychological torment is really severe. I beg you to help me. I truly feel so disgusted with myself, how can I forget about this experience?
keywords: Emotions, guilt and shame, emotional regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I saw your post and I really want to give you a hug. Life is not always perfect and beautiful, and everything we have must be achieved through our own efforts. From your words, I can see that you are someone who pursues perfection, and it is precisely because of this pursuit of perfection that there may be moments of self-destructive behavior or long-term self-loathing. Pursuing perfection can be very tiring, very tiring, more tiring than you can imagine. So you often want to escape, to let go of your burdens, so you have taken another path towards perfection, hoping to find another version of yourself. The clash of these two opposing beliefs is very painful. I can understand this pain. I have a friend who got married and became a mother. She used to have a former mother-in-law who divorced her son. Her former mother-in-law had a daughter-in-law who was married to her son and became his second wife, so she turned legit. This daughter-in-law had gained houses from being a mistress in the town and the county. I'm not encouraging you to sell yourself, but because the daughter-in-law got money from being a mistress, my friend suffered. My friend is the daughter-in-law, independent and self-respecting, but one thing is not good, she has serious psychological issues. She has had a difficult life since she was young, being despised by her sister, who would steal things from home and blame her. Her sister was favored by her parents because she was smart and eloquent, which is why my friend has never had her injustice revealed. Even so, my friend tolerated everything, whether her sister stealing and blaming her, or other cunning remarks, she never took it to heart. She just wanted her sister and parents to live peacefully. But her sister didn't think so. When they worked together, my friend was very capable, and when her sister went home, she would complain to their parents saying that my friend was naive and didn't know that their boss was a pervert, while she tried her best to not get involved with their boss. My friend, on the other hand, no longer worked hard after hearing this and was scolded by her parents. Then her sister would say that she was too playful, and so on. Not only that, they also slandered and controlled my friend together with their relatives and friends. They stirred up their second aunt's prejudice against my friend, saying things like, "She spends too much time with other guys and takes pictures without keeping a distance." They stirred up their uncle's bias against my friend, saying things like, "You are a willful girl. You don't care about how good your sister is to you (their uncle likes their sister)." They also stirred up their brother's bias against my friend, saying things like, "The child my sister gave birth to is so clever. My brother said that this family has really good genes." They even let the neighbors criticize her, saying, "Look at her handwriting, later your sister will say that you are flirtatious." My friend often wanted to change this situation, but she couldn't. She didn't even know why her world was like this. Before marriage, because of these things, she often couldn't work, couldn't date, and every time she had a boyfriend, her sister would have objections, saying that he was not good enough. When she was pursued, her sister would say, "This guy is not bad, you can consider him," but then she would tell others that the guy was not good. When they lived together, after getting pregnant, her sister asked her to have an abortion, saying that the guy was not good, but after the abortion, she said that the guy was good and worth having. But when they turned around, she would cry to other people and ask why my friend liked him... My friend is mentally exhausted every day, unable to work, and because she has been tormented by her sister for a long time, she has become a bit uncontrollably neurotic. She knows she's not good, and she doesn't dare to date successful men, for fear of bringing them down. She married someone who is less successful and has flaws in his personality. She feels that this man can help her release stress and grow together. But the terrible thing is, their house leaks and they don't have a good house. They only have three rooms, can you imagine how big three rooms are? The mother-in-law was influenced by someone else (maybe she also had her own intentions) and did everything possible to make my friend not take care of the child herself and go out to make money, while she took care of the child. So my friend gave the child to her mother-in-law, but the mother-in-law couldn't take care of the child properly. She would go to play mahjong every day, and the child had to go to the provincial hospital once a year, several times to the county hospital, and numerous times to the village clinic every week. My friend took care of the child at home for a long time and the child was fine, but her former mother-in-law didn't stop tormenting her. When the former mother-in-law quarreled at home and went out to cry, she would say that her daughter-in-law was disrespectful and didn't let her take care of her grandchild. But the daughter-in-law actually took care of the child and looked after the shop. My friend's husband runs a water and electricity installation business and sells accessories. No one is watching the shop when they are not there. But the mother-in-law doesn't care, and her daughter-in-law, my friend, suggested that she look after the shop while she takes care of the child, but she was rejected. Now many people speculate and tell my friend, "Maybe your mother-in-law wants you to make money like your sister-in-law, or do something special in the foot massage parlor like someone in the village (many people in this village rely on being mistresses or madams to get rich)." My friend listened and remembered many words and actions of her mother-in-law, such as saying, "It's so difficult for women to start a business. The business world is dominated by men. If you don't have relationships, how can you get promoted or have a good career and money?" Or this former mother-in-law teaching my friend, "Women should love themselves. Men are all selfish creatures. Which man would sincerely give you everything? And then she taught her to get sterilized, otherwise getting pregnant and having an abortion would harm her body." My friend had already discussed it with her husband, and he was going to get sterilized because my friend's health wasn't good. But after the mother-in-law showed her special concern, my friend's husband no longer mentioned getting sterilized. Instead, he avoided the topic when my friend brought it up. If you can read this, what do you think? Is my friend's life good or not? My friend is not bad, but she often has nightmares. There's a voice in her dreams that always says harshly, "You should be a mistress, you are suited for it, you don't deserve to make money." My friend often cries late at night, her relationships with people around her are not good, and when someone shows a little care for her, she becomes even more sad. When she cries to her sister, her sister says, "Stop crying to me. You're so stupid, who would bother with you?" This story is just to tell you that it's not necessary to look down on yourself, and it's not necessary to pursue perfection so much, because life is inherently imperfect. My friend used to work in sales before getting married and was called a scammer by her own brother for more than ten years. They all dislike her. Now my friend has blocked her family's WeChat accounts and lives alone. She says she doesn't want to look back on the past, she doesn't want to go through it again. Some relationships need to be severed even if it's painful. Although my friend has poor health and often feels like she's dying, she says if work is an exam, she can only get 45 points at most. She says she hasn't done well enough at work, and she is afraid of everyone around her. But she still tries to adapt as much as possible. Friend, you are still young, don't be afraid of temporary setbacks. Face your thoughts and ask yourself why you want to be a mistress, because you really need money, or because you admire vanity and only care about fame and wealth? If you really need money, you can learn more and earn it gradually. If it's just vanity, you can consider lowering your living standards a bit, for yourself, your loving boyfriend, your parents, and future children, give them some assurance. Sometimes you will feel tired, but as you keep going, it will pass. Sometimes you will feel bitter, but as you keep eating, the bitterness will fade. Sometimes you will feel hurt, but as time goes on, the pain will diminish. Sometimes you will have certain thoughts, but upon careful consideration, they are unnecessary. If you feel like you've lost control, stop yourself and don't ruin your future. Finally, let me tell you, in that moment of being overwhelmed, my friend also stole. Like you, after stealing, she felt ashamed and dissatisfied with herself, but once her mind returned to normal, she tried to control herself as much as possible. I wish you the same luck, withstand the wind, sun, and rain, and bloom even more beautifully in the future.

1. You feel disgusted with yourself, well, having this feeling is actually evidence that you are quite clean. 2. Forgetting, there are some things that are actually difficult to forget, what we need to do is not let it affect us, so what you need is not to forget, but to face this matter formally and not let it influence you and not blindly succumb to it. 3. The thing has already happened, we cannot make amends, regret is just self-deception. The only thing to do is to continue moving forward, do not look back, if you look back, you lose. 4. If you want to forget, then use the method of diverting your attention and keep yourself occupied. However, I still hope you can face this matter. 5. By the way, about your boyfriend, whether to tell him or not, follow your inner voice, if you want to stay together, then tell him, otherwise, it will become a thorn. Regarding your boyfriend's choice afterward, accept and comfort you, congratulations, you may have found a good boyfriend. If you cannot accept it, well, I don't know what to do either. Let me comfort you for now. Hugs to you. Of course, the final choice is up to you. I hope these are helpful to you.

Hello, OP. I can tell that you deeply regret and blame yourself for your past behavior as a welfare worker. In fact, such things are not uncommon, and our sexual attitudes that we have grown up with are relatively conservative compared to the West, which can lead to intense self-attack after certain events. First of all, we need to acknowledge that the past is irreversible. We need to accept both the good and the bad of our past. Everyone has things they don't want others to know, which can become a burden or a warning to prevent us from engaging in behaviors that may harm ourselves. Secondly, have a conversation with your inner child, deeply from your heart, accepting that child who made a mistake, forgiving her, caring for her, and embracing her. Tell her that it's okay, she made a mistake, but you still love her. I remember Qi Feng once said that the biggest drain on a person is not the depletion of physical or intellectual strength but the war they wage against themselves because in this war, both the enemy and the warrior are provided by oneself, including ammunition and even tactics. So, no one can sustain it. OP, your current pain stems from the struggle you are having with yourself. Your moral self cannot accept any blemish from the past, so it starts attacking, which has a tremendously negative impact on us. Maybe we should change our strategy and accept ourselves with openness, replacing attacks with care. This way, we can face our ideal future self with a positive outlook. Stay well, the world and I love you.

I know you are feeling very sad right now. What's done is done. Don't have thoughts of reminiscing about the past. Keep your emotions in check and try to be happy. Don't dwell on these things. Relax naturally. If you constantly think about these things, you won't be able to accept them. If you feel guilty towards your boyfriend, then love him wholeheartedly now, with time, your feelings will gradually fade. Everything will be fine.

question: Why do people feel disgusted by the intimate relationship with same-sex friends?
description: A female friend who wasn't close suddenly started getting close to me, saying things like "love you" that are commonly said between young girls. It makes me want to stay far away, and sometimes just the thought of it makes me feel disgusted and want to vomit from the bottom of my heart.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friends, interpersonal boundaries, empathy.

answers.answer_text: Questioner, hello, big hug to you! After reading your description, I feel really sympathetic towards your experience of developing a psychological aversion towards your close same-sex friend. question: 43-year-old married woman, suffering from anxiety and tension for decades, experiencing chronic headaches that cannot be relieved.
description: Decades ago, when I was taking the college entrance examination, I was under a lot of pressure and studied intensely for several years without getting in. After that, I sought medical help and was diagnosed with neurosis. Over the next few decades, my condition gradually worsened. My brain always feels strained and in pain, and I struggle to concentrate. I'm not as focused when reading as I used to be. Nowadays, I've started learning some psychology and realize that my personality tends to be repressed, and I get overly anxious and nervous about things. Even small things like my husband being the sole breadwinner and if he has a $100 bill, I constantly worry about how it gets spent, where it goes, whether it's worthwhile, and what to do if it's gone. I'm constantly plagued by self-reproach and inner turmoil. On a larger scale, when my daughter comes home from school, I start to feel time ticking and get anxious if she hasn't done anything after an hour. I look at the clock, and it only increases my anxiety and agitation. I lose control of my emotions and start nagging my daughter. My own mood is also terrible, despite having read so many books on psychology. I just can't seem to control my anxiety and constant nagging towards my daughter. I'm easily agitated and restless when something comes up. Another example is when I try to put my younger child to bed. I set a rule that they must fall asleep by 10:30 PM. I constantly check the time, and the closer it gets to 10:30 PM, the more my brain feels tense, and I become emotionally agitated and anxious. This happens every day, and sometimes my brain feels out of control. I've been suffering like this for decades, and it also affects my sleep. Is this anxiety? Can it be treated?

answers.answer_text: Hello! After reading your description, my heart goes out to you. I feel sorry for the anxiety you have been struggling with since your school days, starting with the anxiety about your college entrance examination. Then you worried about your family's financial sources and expenses, and later on, you became anxious about your child's education and life. As you have noticed, these anxieties uncontrollably emerge in certain situations, affecting not only your mood but also your sleep and parenting your child, which brings you immense pain. You really hope to find a solution. First, explore where your anxiety comes from. Generally, anxiety is often influenced by our family of origin, that is, the influence our parents have on us. Do you remember the things your parents often told you during your upbringing? What did they usually say to you? Did these words make you feel nervous and anxious? If so, I suggest you do the following: 1. Get a pen and paper and write down these words, sentence by sentence. 2. Ask yourself: why did they say these words? What do these words mean to them? 3. What did these words mean to you back then? 4. What do these words mean to you today? 5. How would you respond if you heard them say these words today? Through this exercise, explore the relationship between your current anxiety and your parents' words, helping yourself become aware of the source of your anxiety. Second, manage your anxiety. After years of anxiety, your neurotic impulses have become more automated, including worrying thoughts, emotional restlessness, and behavioral expressions such as nagging and blaming your child. These three are interconnected and mutually influencing. I suggest you take the following methods to manage your anxiety: 1. Be aware of your anxiety. You have already done well in this regard, and you have good self-awareness of your anxiety. 2. Record your anxiety every day, including the thoughts, events, and behaviors that occur when you are anxious. See which events, which thoughts, these anxieties are often related to, and also sort out the ways and methods you have been handling these anxieties. You have also done well in this regard, so continue to maintain your awareness. 3. When anxiety arises, do not engage in any behavioral reactions. Just sit quietly and repeatedly imagine the worst possible consequences in your mind. If the worst outcome is that, slowly your anxiety will lessen. 4. Practice anxiety imagination training 11 to 2 times a day, imagining the worst possible consequences of the events that you usually worry about and feel anxious about. 5. Have 1 to 2 days of separation from your child per week or month, let the child stay with relatives, divert your attention from the child, experience the feeling of relaxation, and thus alleviate your anxiety. Third, sever intergenerational transmission. You are very attentive to raising your children, paying great attention to their life and time management. I believe this is related to both your own studies and your personal growth experience. Your own experience can be both a resource in the process of raising your child and can also have a negative impact on parenting. As you have realized, the anxiety you experienced in your own studies has resurfaced in raising your child. I suggest you try the following methods: 1. Hold a family meeting to establish household guidelines for shared living, including rules for homework and bedtime, etc. 2. Let the older child self-check according to these rules, and parents can give rewards or punishments according to the rules, thus cultivating the child's self-management awareness and ability. 3. Let the older child share the responsibility of taking care of the younger siblings, relieving your pressure and cultivating a sense of responsibility in the older child. 4. If anxiety occurs, follow the advice in the second point. Fourth, show more care for yourself. These years have not been easy for you. It was not easy to repeat the college entrance examination, bearing so much pressure and anxiety. It was not easy to raise two children, enduring so much hard work and carrying so much expectation and worry. Talk to friends and family about your hardships and difficulties. Seek help from a specialist hospital and get some anti-anxiety medication. Take some time to rest and relax. I hope these methods I mentioned above can help you. Welcome to continue the discussion.

Dear, you have been living too hard all these years! Even a small thing can cause tension and anxiety. Your brain keeps pondering over a small matter, as if it needs a clear answer. You are constantly disturbed by various things, unable to find peace. It feels as if you are a speck of dust, easily lifted off the ground by a slight disturbance. Your heart can never settle down. I have also experienced this feeling for decades and don't want to continue like this anymore, so I started studying psychology. My teacher said that after several decades of patterns, it takes at least a few years to change. In fact, a few years may not be enough as the process of change is very slow. But one thing is certain: this long-term pattern of tension and anxiety can be changed! Let me share some insights: 1) Deeply study psychology and start with cognitive changes. You have also realized this, it is the beginning of self-exploration. 2) Seek long-term personal growth counseling. This is essential for exploring your inner patterns and past psychological traumas. It helps heal yourself and continue personal growth. Psychological counseling can work at the subconscious level, which is difficult for us to do ourselves. 3) Write a diary. Write down your feelings and events every day. It helps to organize your emotions, trace the relationships between events, and release emotions. 4) Have a dialogue with yourself. Anxiety, tension, and worries are the inner child telling us about her feelings, and she needs us to see her. If we constantly ponder in our brains, we will never truly see her, so she cannot be healed and will continue to cause us anxiety. Have a conversation with your inner child every night, telling her: you did well today! You deserve to be loved! You deserve a better life! 5) Practice mindfulness meditation. We have become too accustomed to thinking with our brains. To return from the brain to the body, we need to practice; we have been disconnected from our body's sensations and emotions for too long! This is something we can do ourselves, to help us become sensitive to our body's sensations again, which is very important. / In conclusion / Our patterns have been there for forty years, these patterns are also physiological neural circuits. It is truly not easy to change. Let's walk this path together! You deserve to live a comfortable and happy life!

Give the floor owner a hug! I understand the floor owner's inner anxiety and restlessness. This kind of situation has persisted for decades without being resolved, which has greatly affected and troubled the floor owner's normal life, causing immense suffering. Anyone who encounters such a situation would feel unbearable pain. Therefore, the floor owner doesn't need to be so nervous. This situation is "very normal" for the floor owner and has gradually developed from long-term repression and anxiety. The floor owner mentioned having medical examinations in the past, which indicated neurosis, and these symptoms are relatively consistent. However, the floor owner's situation has lasted for decades, and many of the previous lesion symptoms have changed significantly, so it is no longer possible to define the conclusion based on the previous neurosis. Just because someone experiences anxiety does not necessarily mean they have anxiety disorder, but if someone does have anxiety disorder, they will definitely have symptoms of anxiety. The floor owner's anxiety has persisted for decades and is triggered by various things, making it generalized anxiety. When a person's brain and nerves are in a prolonged state of anxiety and unease, they will gradually deteriorate. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the floor owner's condition as an anxiety neurosis. The first step is to have an electroencephalogram (EEG) examination at the local neurology department to see if there are any organic lesions in the brain. If so, traditional Chinese medicine can be used for treatment. As for the floor owner's suppressed emotions and anxiety, after undergoing the EEG examination, it is recommended to schedule an appointment with a suitable therapist for systematic psychological counseling. This will help release the suppressed emotions and reduce the floor owner's stress, allowing them to face their true self and life with ease, naturalness, and peace of mind.

Embrace the topic, the failures in high school have caused years of distress, to the point where I feel anxious and unsettled about my current life. Firstly, even small things like my husband being the sole breadwinner and him spending a long time contemplating even a hundred dollars in his pocket make me lack confidence in our current life. I have a strong desire to control my loved ones, wanting to control my partner and children, knowing their whereabouts, and feeling anxious if they don't tell me the truth. Although I have read many psychology books, I haven't had a clear explanation for the source of this anxiety. Secondly, I get tense and agitated when putting my second child to sleep, insisting they must fall asleep by ten-thirty. I constantly check the time and as it gets closer to ten-thirty, my nerves become more strained, and I feel restless and panicky. From the text, it seems like I may have symptoms of OCD, such as the need for my child to sleep at a specific time and the intense focus on it. This emotional state also affects my child, and I am aware of the problem. Thirdly, this happens every day, and sometimes my mind feels out of control. I have been suffering for decades, and it also affects my sleep. Is this anxiety and stress? Can it be treated? It is evident that I am conscious of my anxiety and OCD, and I hope to receive help, showing a strong willingness and desire to get assistance. From the text, it is clear that I need to find a professional mental health counselor or therapist to systematically understand, help, and treat me, and to have a comprehensive understanding of my behavior. I believe that with your willingness, your anxious feelings will improve, it's just a matter of time and your own willingness. You can try mindfulness training to calm your anxiety, which is a very effective method. Through daily training sessions of ten minutes, twenty minutes, or even longer, you can improve your sleep quality and subsequently achieve improvements in other areas. There is good news waiting for you. I am here, waiting for you!

It has been decades, and you have gone through such a difficult journey! My heart goes out to you. You have been trying to help yourself by reading psychology books, but the results haven't been good. You can try a different approach and talk to a counselor. Through this counseling relationship, you can adjust your relationship with your child and provide them with a relaxed environment. I believe this will be very beneficial for their growth. You can contact me for online counseling.

Yes, it can be treated, but whether it is treated well depends on oneself. Letting go is not just a word, it's not just an action. It is a process that may be related to your original family, but everyone has already formed their own new family and some normal adjustments can be made. Try sports, music, give it a try. I wish you well, as someone who has seen themselves and strives to change.

question: 18-year-old girl, discovered by her parents using adult toys, how to explain?
description: I was caught by my parents using small intimate products... They will definitely question me when they come back from work tonight, how should I explain this?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, I think at this moment you may feel anxious, embarrassed, scared, and nervous... Various unsettling emotions make you unsure of how to respond to the questions from your parents when they come back home. When you think about how to explain, you feel that you don't want your parents to know about the fact that you are using small erotic objects, and you want to come up with a reasonable excuse to cover up this matter. You anticipate that they will question themselves, and you also want to avoid this fact. I can feel that the atmosphere at home is rather strict, oppressive, and discussing sex is considered shameful and something to be avoided. As a teenager in puberty, it is normal to be curious about sex, and this curiosity may lead to looking up information and discussing intimate topics with peers. It is necessary for parents to talk to their children about knowledge of physical development, necessary daily hygiene, and protection, even during this stage or even earlier. So what led you to using small erotic objects to experience sexuality? If your family tends to avoid or reject discussions about sex, for example, they are against seeing intimate acts like kissing and hugging on TV, then this will make children even more curious about why they are not allowed to see those things. These are all negative circumstances. Since these are considered bad things, it is also difficult to communicate them with peers. However, our physical development can lead to sexual impulses, and the conflict between our bodily sensations and moral consciousness is what caused this phenomenon. Regarding the reasons that led to your current behavior, such as wanting to see something or feeling restricted by others, feeling like you don't know anything among your peers, and simply being curious and wanting to understand, you can have an open conversation with your mother about your thoughts. Hopefully, they will allow you to see or talk about what interests you. You haven't done anything wrong, and discussing sex is a normal thing. It's also an opportunity to have a deep conversation with your mother. Good luck to you.

Hello, actually I've experienced the same awkward situation as the OP. When I was 16, I was very curious about male reproductive organs because I had never seen one before, and sexual education was very limited during that time. It was impossible to learn about these things from my parents or school, and they even avoided talking about it. One day, on my way home from school, I was given a box of condoms by a community worker. Although I felt embarrassed, I put the condoms in my pocket because I wanted to see what they looked like. When I got home, my mom asked me to take off my coat and put it in the washing machine. To my surprise, she found the condoms in the pocket of my coat. I felt guilty and I could tell that my mom was startled too. At that moment, she didn't say anything, just told me to go to my room and do my homework. Later, during dinner, I actively communicated with my mom (my dad was away on a business trip). Although these condoms were given to me by the community worker, and not bought by myself, I was genuinely curious about what they were and I felt that no one had ever told me about these things despite my age. At that time, my mom didn't directly answer me. She said that I was still young and would understand when I grew up and got married. I guess my mom didn't know how to talk to me about this topic at that time. However, she found another time and talked to me about many related issues. Based on my own experience, I have the following suggestions: 1. Find a time to talk privately with your mother and discuss your situation. If she is willing to communicate with you, then directly talk to her about these issues. This not only avoids awkwardness but also strengthens your bond with your mother. Through addressing this issue with my own mother, we have come to understand each other better. 2. If your parents are strongly opposed or repelled by this topic, then don't talk to them about it anymore. However, you can let them know that you have grown up, you are an adult now, and you are no longer the little girl in their eyes. 3. Try to avoid the chances of your adult toys appearing in front of your parents again. Of course, you need to ensure cleanliness and follow safety measures when using them, so as not to harm yourself physically. The above are my personal experience and some small suggestions. I hope they can help you!

It's quite awkward, I guess my parents don't know how to bring it up either. They might either pretend they don't know or my mother will come back and talk to me. Do not get angry because of the awkwardness. If my mother is conservative, it's probably best not to try to change her views. Tentatively communicate your thoughts. If my mother is more open-minded, it might be easier. Sex is a normal physiological need, as long as it doesn't harm others or oneself, is consensual and not forced, there shouldn't be a problem. To reassure your parents, you can say reassuring words, such as guaranteeing no premarital sex, always using protection if with a boy, and not letting it affect your studies, etc.

question: Why do you still have to use the method of confiscating my phone to educate me?
description: I waited until late at night to ask this question, so I don't think I'm emotionally upset. I am 18 years old, an only child, and a freshman. I cannot control myself from squeezing pimples, and as a punishment, my mother would take away my meal allowance, confiscate my phone, and other things that greatly affect my study and life. The most frustrating thing is when she takes away my phone. Usually, I keep my phone outside while sleeping and only use it when necessary. Many times, especially when I'm feeling down at night, I want to talk to someone, but who can I turn to? I admit that it's my fault for not being able to resist squeezing pimples, but I am really confused about why she confiscates my phone. Sometimes, the assignments given by the school are not as important as yours, so it wouldn't hurt to take away a child's phone, right? Maybe it's because I don't have enough economic independence, that's why. Overall, I feel helpless about why she forces me to compromise in this way. I get it, I shouldn't squeeze pimples anymore, but then what? I feel controlled and restricted, and it makes me very uncomfortable. It feels difficult to change others, so do you have any suggestions for me? Thank you.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I totally understand your feelings, sending you a big hug~ Parents using the method of deducting food expenses and confiscating your phone to educate you can make you feel confined and controlled. It shows that this approach has caused you more distress, and it is not necessarily the most correct method. Let's first objectively look at this situation. Parents do not want you to pick at your acne, so they take your phone and deduct food expenses. This indicates a lack of communication between you or ineffective communication, so they have resorted to a very direct way to restrain you. Have you previously discussed the specific issue with them? Have you reached a more agreeable agreement or a more gentle solution? After your phone is confiscated, are you able to control yourself and not pick at your acne? From the parents' perspective, they have indeed overlooked your feelings, but due to various reasons, they may not have thought of better methods. Therefore, I suggest that, on the one hand, you should talk to them and explain that you still need to use your phone to check school work and occasionally chat with friends to express your feelings and propose better solutions, seeking mutual understanding. Communication is always the most important. On the other hand, if they are unwilling to compromise, you should also adjust your attitude. They do have your best interests in mind, not wanting you to be constantly on your phone, even though this well-intentioned act might make you feel confined. Once your acne improves, perhaps you can have another good conversation with them. Parental control can indeed easily lead to a rebellious mentality, but you must exercise some restraint. Of course, you can directly express your feelings, making them aware that their decisions may not always be correct. The balance in this situation is something you need to explore on your own. Wishing you all the best~

Hello, it seems that you are facing a conflict with your mother's parenting style not aligning with your desires. Let's break it down into two steps: 1. Is your mother's parenting style reasonable?
