We should not evaluate ourselves in a comprehensive and generalized way based on a certain behavior. We should also not evaluate our wife and children in a comprehensive and generalized way. For example, if our goal is to have a good job and earn a lot of money, but unfortunately, we become unemployed, then in terms of this goal, unemployment is not good, it is a failure because it hinders us from achieving the goal. However, what fails is the action of becoming unemployed, not me as a person. I will not evaluate myself in a comprehensive way just because of unemployment and think that I am a failure. In fact, I can never determine whether I am a failure or a success. I may be unemployed and fail in the job aspect, but I could be kind and filial to my parents and successful in personal character. When we can make such distinctions and learn to see the positive side, our problems will be greatly improved.

question: 14-year-old girl, I always feel various problems arising from the great pressure?
description: I don't get along well with others, I like to be alone and have gotten used to it. But some people try to be friends with me and I don't know how to respond to them, especially the opposite sex. In elementary school, I was bullied by some people which caused me to have a bit of fear now. This makes me very distressed. I am very passive, in other people's eyes I may be seen as a quiet person who hardly speaks. There are also some people who I feel are against me, I don't know who is right or wrong, I don't dare to say if it's me or if it's them. The interpersonal relationships are complicated and messy, and some people specifically target me and insult me, I don't know why, maybe it's because of me? I'm not sure. Because of these things along with the pressure of studying, I completely break down. My academic performance has seriously declined and I even have symptoms I have never had before, like a reluctance to study. Some teachers and classmates want to help me, but I don't know what to do. They say I'm always overthinking, but I can't change that, I don't know why. What is wrong with me? I can only use my phone to escape from reality, I don't want to face it, I always find all sorts of excuses to avoid it. I don't dare to ask for help from others because I can't explain what's wrong with me. It feels so terrible! I don't like my phone, but I have no choice but to use it.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, behavioral abnormalities

answers.answer_text: I feel sorry for your situation and hope that you will recover soon. Bullying in schools is a lesson we have to learn in our growth process. Some children who are bullied are afraid to talk to their parents and suffer silently. I once had a visitor who was 12 years old and being bullied. The visitor's mother was also the teacher of the class, but the parents did not pay attention to the child being bullied. As a result, the child was forced to drop out of school and the mother was unaware of it. The disappointment in parents and teachers turned into self-disappointment. The neglect or indifference of parents and misunderstandings make children feel helpless or unworthy. Even when they encounter problems, they will not seek help from their parents or express themselves to them. They may even be misunderstood as having a problem which leads to them being bullied. Some children may even be physically abused. Children who are bullied at home by their parents are most likely to be bullied at school. Growing up in such an environment fills children with fear but they are unable to express their fear and seek help. Eventually, the self-protective measures born out of fear carry hostility, even if we think we don't have hostility, we instinctively express it. When we cannot protect ourselves and cannot obtain help, the disappointment in parents, teachers, and the environment ultimately turns into a disappointment in ourselves, a self-denial and doubt that we cannot even protect ourselves. If we can't say it out loud, then write it down. We need to learn to seek help, and the first people we should trust are our parents. At school, we should trust our teachers and classmates. Not everyone is a bully, just like not everything you say represents resistance and hostility. Sometimes parents do not express their love, as they have not received training in being parents. Their way of expressing love may be through humiliation, denial, blame, or even verbal abuse. For example, when a mother reminds us to wear warm clothes, she may say, "You deserve to freeze to death," but her intention is "Darling, remember to wear your clothes, it's cold today, be obedient." So, if you can't express your problems and needs clearly in words, you can write them down on paper and express them with notes or letters. Only when we start to express ourselves can we learn how to protect and love ourselves, and only then can we receive the help and love we need. Although you are in middle school now, I feel that there are still many basic growth issues from lower grades that need to be resolved. I recommend the "Psychology for Elementary School Students" comic book series, which can help you face the basic problems encountered in your growth process. Of course, you can also read the more advanced book "Live as an Optimistic You".

question: Eighth-grade girl, recently always feels like she will be killed?
description: I dare not turn off the lights every night when I go to sleep. I always feel that someone will come into the house or that someone in the house wants to kill me. Because of this, I suffer from insomnia, experiencing fear and thinking there is someone behind me. I am afraid that something bad will happen to me, such as a car accident. I often feel inexplicably sad and burst into tears. I frequently shift between extreme happiness and sadness. I feel that people are talking bad about me and that nobody has good intentions towards me. I also have suicidal thoughts and there are many self-inflicted knife marks on my hands. I cannot control my thoughts and don't know what I am thinking. I often speak incoherently and have a strong desire to talk, but I don't know what to say. I heavily rely on my phone. Do I have any mental health problems?

answers.answer_text: Child, when I saw the title of your question "8th grade, ...", I couldn't help but open your post. My child is also in 8th grade, and after reading your story, I feel a sense of empathy and want to give you a virtual hug. Auntie also wants to say, if possible, please think carefully about who you can trust, whether it be a family member, teacher, or an adult who understands psychology, and seek their help, okay? Before seeking help, please take good care of yourself, okay? This may just be a dark period in your life, but please believe that everything has cracks where light can enter. Wishing you well, and know that the world loves you.

Child, I'm really worried about you. If possible, please find someone you trust as soon as possible, it could be your parents, family members, your homeroom teacher, or the school's counselor, and seek help. Before that, please take care of yourself and refrain from any self-harming behavior. Existence is meaningful, so each of us has our own purpose and value. We all encounter difficulties and troubles during the process of growing up, and sometimes we may even experience harm from others. But please believe that there is always a way to solve and overcome these challenges, so seek help. Because it's difficult to find the root of the problem in just a few words on this platform, please understand. Wishing you smooth and good health!

question: Diagnosed with PTSD, my parents say I am using my illness as an excuse.
description: Recently, I was diagnosed with PTSD. These days, my parents mentioned taking me to see a traditional Chinese medicine doctor. I agreed to go today, but I just don't want to go out and I don't want to go. He says I always do whatever I want for a long time and it seems like I really do. He always thinks I'm lying to him or deceiving him. I don't know what to say, I'm just frustrated and have a headache. I feel like running away from home, I want to die, really want to die. I just want to make them suffer. I hate them. He says I don't have an illness anymore, I'm just being stubborn and using my illness as an excuse. I really want to kill them, I really do, I'm so annoyed. I'm crying and gasping for breath, I don't want to take responsibility for myself anymore, I just don't care about the consequences. I'm so damn fed up.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello, how are you? You have been diagnosed with PTSD. What traumatic event did you experience? Since you have been diagnosed with PTSD, it means that you have not fully recovered from this trauma. I suggest continuing to see a psychologist and undergo psychological therapy, combined with medication, which should help alleviate your pain. Many people actually do not understand psychological problems. They often think it's just overthinking and something you can self-regulate. Maybe your parents think the same way. They may not understand PTSD and do not understand that your pain may be something you cannot overcome on your own. They may not understand that going outside may be really difficult for you. It's really painful not to be understood, and I understand your frustration. However, seeking understanding from others is not an easy task, even from our closest and most loved ones. We need more patience and open communication instead of assuming they should understand our mental state, thoughts, and feelings. You are in a lot of pain right now, feeling overwhelmed, and even considering doing something extreme, feeling like you no longer want to take responsibility for yourself. It's okay to occasionally have these thoughts. We all have moments of vulnerability and wanting to escape, and it's okay. You can allow these thoughts to come up, allow yourself to take a break, cry when you need to, and accept the pain. Respect and accept your own feelings. After your feelings are fully accepted, maybe these thoughts will subside, and you will regain your rationality and strength. Of course, if you find it difficult and painful, I suggest seeking help from a psychologist or counselor. Especially when you have extreme thoughts, be careful not to let impulsiveness lead you. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Hi! It seems like you don't have a good relationship with your family because of a lack of understanding between each other. Even though you genuinely don't want to go out, your parents say you're stubborn. They don't understand why you don't want to leave the house, and you're also annoyed by their insistence on making you go out. Lately, you seem to be quite frustrated. Do you have something on your mind? You can talk to a mental health professional who can help you overcome this situation and feel less burdened.

question: Changed shifts, changed dorms, not adapting well, too noisy, what should I do?
description: I'm not very accustomed to it. This dorm is too noisy, but changing rooms all the time is too troublesome and will give the new classmates a bad impression. What should I do?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, roommates and classmates, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ I can sense that you're currently not adjusting well in this dormitory. You're worried about constantly changing dorms, which may have an impact on your roommates or yourself. Therefore, it's important for you to understand the lifestyle in this dormitory. Why are the people in the dormitory so noisy? One reason could be that everyone gets along well and can easily chat and show their true selves in the dormitory. When chatting, you can also try to join them and understand their personalities, which can help you communicate better with them. You can also express your thoughts during the conversation, such as how you're not accustomed to a noisy dormitory. Then, you can discuss with your roommates to find a suitable lifestyle for everyone. For example, there can be times when everyone is happy and lively, and times when everyone is quiet to focus on their own activities. Best wishes~.

question: "What is 'empathy holding technique'? Is it a new counseling method?"
description: "The technique of promoting regression through empathetic holding is employed to facilitate healing for visitors. This therapeutic approach is based on which theory, and is it targeted towards visitors with specific issues? What are the risks associated with such a treatment plan? What should be taken into consideration? Does this technique still have therapeutic effects when visitors are already aware that empathetic holding is a therapeutic intervention?"

answers.answer_text: Hello, this is a very interesting question, let me try to answer it. I don't think that empathic attunement is a "technique," it is more like an "attitude and ability." Empathy was initially proposed by the humanistic representative Carl Rogers, who described it as understanding another person's experiences in the world as if you were that person. However, at the same time, you always remember that you are still different from him; you just understand that person, rather than becoming him. Empathy also means letting the person you empathize with know that you understand them. Rogers said in his article: "Gradually, my understanding of empathy expanded into a counselor's ability to feel. When I empathize with a visitor, I can feel something inexplicable rising in me that needs to be expressed. This may sound strange and perhaps a little elusive. But I have found that whenever I express these unspeakable things, visitors resonate with them and finally find an outlet for their vague thoughts and emotions." As for how to empathize with visitors, there are indeed some technical practices, such as providing content feedback and emotional feedback. This leads to another question in the title: "When visitors already know that this kind of empathy and attunement is a therapeutic method, does it still have a therapeutic effect?" My response to this question is that visitors still have doubts about the attitude of counselors. Repeating my words and reflecting my emotions is just your technique; you are not really willing to understand me, and I don't trust you. In this situation, the counseling relationship is still in the early stage of establishment. Faced with visitors' mistrust, each counselor will have different ways of responding. If it were me, I might say, "I sense that you don't seem to believe me; you are still watching me carefully, worried that I might be another person who could potentially hurt you. This makes me feel a little frustrated and powerless. Would you be willing to tell me how you feel right now?" If the visitor is not willing to approach me, the responsibility of the counselor is to see and allow this, and the gradual process of getting closer is the process of establishing a relationship. Regardless of any techniques, visitors and counselors are both real people, and only through empathy can a healing relationship begin. The world and I love you.

Hello, the title-owner! Empathy and containment can be said to be important techniques in psychological counseling and also very important therapeutic factors that can make psychological counseling effective. Empathy, also known as "entering the spirit," means being able to understand the feelings of the visitor and respond appropriately. This is similar to the interaction between mother and baby: the baby cannot express its needs in language, but the mother understands the baby's non-verbal cues and responds to meet its needs. Containment is the concept proposed by Winnicott or the "holding environment" proposed by Bion. We can imagine the image of a mother holding a baby, which represents a state of embrace and support. When a mother provides a safe environment that contains the baby's anxiety and fear, it provides a containing environment for the baby, which can facilitate the visitor's regression and allow them to be nurtured again. Psychological counseling is a process of re-nurturing, allowing the visitor to re-experience this process. This new experience of being loved, seen, and attended to will be internalized as a new part of their inner self, and will carry this new experience back into their real life, leading to change. That's it. Thank you for your question, I hope it is helpful to you. You can refer to the relevant literature of Klein and Bion.

question: In life, there will always be unexpected events. How can we maintain a positive mindset?
description: There are always unexpected events in life that prevent us from remaining calm. What is the principle behind this and how can it be resolved?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. When I saw your question, it reminded me of the human "fight or flight response." According to Baidu's definition, the fight or flight response is a series of nerve and gland reactions triggered by stress, preparing the body for defense, struggle, or escape. As you mentioned, there are always sudden events in life, so humans need to "not remain calm" in order to cope with these sudden situations. This is our skill and instinct, and it is helpful to us. I thought, instead of using the word "resolve," can we change it to "adjust" to deal with the "non-calm state"? If it is adjusting our response to sudden events, the first thing to consider is to feel the current emotions and physical changes, such as panic or blank mind, rapid or slow breathing, or cold hands and feet. After feeling the psychological and physiological changes, if the situation is not too urgent, you can take some time to make adjustments, such as regulating your breathing to a normal level, rubbing your cold hands, and using a simple meditation to calm your emotions. If the situation is urgent and requires an immediate response, after taking a deep breath, bring yourself to a slightly calm state and start analyzing and responding to reality. The above answer may be a bit broad, but I hope it can still help you~.

question: Feeling exhausted and trapped in a never-ending cycle in life?
description: It's too difficult. I lack the ability, and I constantly feel inferior and doubt myself. My life and work are always a mess. I always feel like I can't handle challenging technical tasks because my brain feels like it's filled with lead and can't function properly. Whenever I encounter a challenge, I want to escape and give up. I always suspect that my superiors have a negative opinion of me, and I feel like they are disappointed in me. I haven't been able to create the value in the company that they expected. Lately, I've been thinking about quitting and running away because I feel like my superiors just haven't figured me out yet. My life seems to be stuck in a loop, and I can't find a way out. My mind feels weak, and it's not functioning properly at all. My work and life are a mess, and I feel powerless to change it. What should I do? Where should I go from here? What is wrong with me??
keywords: Emotions, depressed mood, anxious mood, guilt, shame.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! I see your confusion and want to give you a hug. I hope to bring you some warmth. OP mentioned feeling inferior and unhappy at work, afraid of being looked down upon by superiors. I also had the same confusion as OP, just entering a completely new environment and taking on a new task. Because I wasn't familiar with it, I didn't dare to try, afraid that I wouldn't do well and fearing that I would be the worst. So sometimes I would try to back out of it or choose the simpler tasks to do. But I know that this has a lot to do with my own personality, etc. I tend to be quieter and was not very active before, so I would listen to others' thoughts and follow them in many things. Until later, I became aware of this issue and decided to change myself. So no matter what task comes my way, I take it without hesitation and strive to complete it. I started challenging myself in various areas. Now I have become more confident and no longer just listen to others, because I have my own thoughts, I have learned to think, and I have my own goals and pursuits in life. When I saw OP's confusion, it reminded me of myself in the past. I also want to give OP some advice. 1. OP can try to step out of their comfort zone, try to live according to their own beliefs, find their own pursuits and goals, and have principles and beliefs in their work. This will help us become more content in life and work because we know that we are working for ourselves and not influenced by others. 2. At the same time, OP can go out more, make more friends, socialize more, and participate in more activities. We need to dare to try. We grow in the process of trying out our weaknesses. This can make us more confident and make our lives more colorful. 3. In addition, OP can establish some interests and hobbies of their own. They can start by pursuing their own interests, whether it's for relaxation or anything else. Cultivating interests and hobbies is a great choice. Finally, I hope OP can adjust their mindset, tidy themselves up, and start over. I hope OP can quickly overcome their confusion. You can do it!

Hello, the first thing I want to say is that you are not alone. Many people feel the same way when faced with challenges. It is normal to feel the urge to escape or avoid difficult situations because it is our natural instinct to protect ourselves from potential harm or failure. However, it is important to remember that avoiding challenges will only limit our growth and confidence. Instead, we can try the following steps to overcome this mindset: 

1. Adjust your mindset: Don't let setbacks define your abilities. Embrace the fact that everyone faces obstacles and failures in their journey. See challenges as opportunities for growth and learning. With the right mindset, you can overcome anything.

2. Boost your self-confidence: Recognize your strengths and achievements. Don't compare yourself to others excessively, as it can lead to inappropriate self-evaluation. Focus on your progress and celebrate small victories along the way.

3. Seek feedback: Feedback is crucial for improvement. Whether it is from experienced mentors or self-reflection, constructive feedback helps us identify areas for development and refine our skills.

4. Break down goals: Divide big goals into smaller, achievable tasks. This approach not only makes the journey less overwhelming but also allows you to recognize your progress more easily. Each small achievement will contribute to your overall success.

Remember, building resilience and developing skills takes time and effort. Don't be too hard on yourself during this process. Stay positive and believe in your ability to overcome challenges. Keep pushing forward, and you will grow stronger. Good luck!

Hello questioner, seeing your words, I feel that you have been through a lot of unpleasant things recently, and this series of events ultimately struck you, reinforcing your original inferiority complex and magnifying it. I'm not quite sure about what you experienced in your childhood and adolescence, but there must be many similarities between your past and present self. For example, if your parents were very strict with you or paid little attention to you, it might have influenced your views on life and made you prone to giving up easily or defining yourself negatively. In the first sentence, you said it's too difficult and that you lack the ability, and then you self-doubt, saying that your life and work are always a mess. To what extent have you suffered? In your description, I only see the recent situation at work, and you haven't mentioned specific events. Most of it is you speculating about what your superiors think of you, but there is no actual mention of your superiors telling you that you are incapable as a person, or that your performance in your work is not up to par. I feel like you are stuck in a state of self-doubt. I believe you need to do some self-adjustment and build confidence in yourself. Also, read biographies and novels about people, and you will discover that everyone's life has its ups and downs, and how to overcome setbacks depends mainly on oneself. Of course, it's possible that your current life has had some influence on you, so I suggest seeking psychological counseling. Find your source of infinite motivation and step out of your predicament. I believe you can do it and see your own shining points. Everyone has a different understanding of life, and our reactions to things vary. I don't know much about what you have experienced before, and perhaps my words may not be suitable for you, but I just want to say: no matter what state of life you are in, you must believe in yourself. You may have a negative opinion about these statements, but I think success is achieved step by step, and getting out of a situation also requires planning step by step. By slowly moving forward, you can pull yourself out of the deep pit and not get entrapped further. I'm here, waiting for you! I believe in you!

Actually, you are setting limits on yourself and trapping yourself. Do you know that? Your abilities are not a problem, because your superiors are reluctant to let you go, so you must have the ability. However, constantly doubting yourself is not okay, you need psychological support. Can you hire a counselor to help you for a period of time? Rebuild your confidence, sort out the chaos in work and life, and then easily immerse yourself in work and life.

question: How can a person speak without stammering due to nervousness?
description: I feel scared, nervous, and lacking in confidence when I need to showcase myself in many activities. I dare not speak on stage. As soon as I step onto the stage, my face turns red, my speech becomes stuttered, and I often forget what I wanted to say. I am afraid of making a fool of myself in front of others, and the more afraid I become, the more nervous I get and the more I stutter. Eventually, I have become too scared to speak on stage at all. I used to think that if I prepared what I wanted to say beforehand offstage, I wouldn't be nervous on stage, but it still happens. I want to change this state of turning red and stuttering whenever I am nervous. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hi, hello! The best way to effectively improve your public speaking skills is to practice and speak more frequently. Start by practicing in front of no audience, then gradually progress to speaking in front of an audience, especially strangers. As for the internal methods, you need to identify the underlying reasons for your stage fright. This requires deeper analysis. Additionally, when you feel nervous, you can try deep breathing to relax. Don't panic, as it will only make you more nervous. Good luck! (Cheer up, the world and I love you) Rise up.

question: I am always very impatient with my mother's urging for marriage, and even intentionally ignore her messages.
description: I gradually turned into the kind of person I despise. I really want to get closer to my parents, have occasional video calls, and understand their current situation. But because I am an older unmarried woman, they have arranged many blind dates for me, all of which failed. Because of this, my mother told my sister to make me see a psychologist. Helpless, is not wanting to get married a mental problem? My mother also told me that I was a troublesome child since I was young. While other kids slept at night and cried during the day, I was the opposite, making it difficult for her during her confinement period. She even thought about jumping into our pond while holding me. The latter sentence was said to me during a phone call with another relative. Why did they tell me these things? It was because they were trying to introduce me to a divorced man at that time, saying that he had good conditions and asking me to seize the opportunity. At that time, I had to pretend to agree while tears streamed down my face. I have a reserved personality and am not very close to my parents. I have been working far away from home in recent years, so the distance between my parents and me has grown even bigger. Blind dates continue as usual, exchanging WeChat, chatting, and then nothing happens. I really don't know how to find topics to talk about. Whenever my mother sends me a message alone, I know she is going to introduce someone again. Sometimes I deliberately don't reply to the message. Every time a blind date is unsuccessful, I feel like it's my fault. Maybe there is something wrong with me, but other people also have times when they don't like me. My heart feels so tired...
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, blind date.

answers.answer_text: Let's discuss while sorting it out: Your demand: to find a suitable partner for marriage. #But sometimes others may not be interested in me. #Your parents' demand: for you to find a man and get married. Getting married is a task for them, it must be completed, and the quality of completion is not their concern. Both your demand and your mother's demand are not wrong. The conflict now is that if you don't complete the "marriage" action, she will pressure you. Every time a blind date is unsuccessful, she blames you for all the problems, essentially wanting to undermine your confidence and make you compromise, so that she can complete the task as soon as possible. As for your needs and feelings, she may not have the time to consider them now. Your real needs are not being valued, and you constantly have to cooperate with them to complete the task of marriage, which is exhausting for anyone. This is why you don't want to reply to messages. But if we turn it around, you do want to get married, but do you have any channels to meet potential partners? Can you only solve your needs through blind dates? Because #you have a quiet personality #and are not close to your parents, you may also not know how to communicate with the opposite sex. Your needs and your parents' needs are aligned, but your requirements for a partner are different. So as long as you find a partner you approve of, all the current problems can be solved, right? Suggestions: 1. You can try to learn how to communicate and interact with other people. 2. Expand your channels for meeting the opposite sex, such as through online matchmaking websites or offline matchmaking events. Communication aspects can provide you with some methods. If you need help, you can leave a message or chat.

question: First-year girl does not live in school, mom is sick and being treated in another city, feeling anxious and sad, doesn't want to go to school?
description: A female student in her first year of middle school initially prepared to stay in the school dormitory, but later had an argument with her parents and didn't end up staying. Her mother became ill and needed to undergo surgery in another province, which would take at least two weeks. She left for the other province on the morning of the second day of school. Since then, she has been troubling her relatives to shuttle her (as a side note), feeling absent-minded during class and overwhelmed with a blocked heart, wanting to cry. It may be because of entering a new environment, feeling that she is under a lot of pressure and having trouble adjusting. It is completely different from elementary school and there are no classmates to play with. In addition, it should be because her mother is not at home, which makes her feel insecure and very uncomfortable, extremely anxious and wanting to cry, especially when she thinks about her mother not being able to come back for a long time, she feels anxious and sad. It really is a constant feeling of anxiety, and she even has the thought of not wanting to go to school anymore!
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxiety emotions, panic helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Hugs to you! You are currently feeling anxious and under a lot of pressure. The reasons are: being in a new environment and missing your mother's company. It is normal to feel a bit uncomfortable when starting a new year in high school. Plus, at each stage, there will be new friends, so there's no need to dwell on the old ones. If they are true friends, they won't drift away. How can you quickly make new friends? You can proactively start conversations with your classmates about recent TV shows or anime. Having common interests makes it easier to connect with others. I don't know why you're not staying at the dormitory. You can try staying there; that way, you won't overthink and can spend more time with your classmates. Actively participate in class collective activities, contribute to classroom reports, and join sports events, etc. Relying too much on your parents is a common problem among many middle school students. For you, parents are like a safe haven where you are taken care of. You trust your family, and you can be yourself without having to put too much social pressure on yourself. However, when you enter a new environment, you may worry about not making friends, etc. But we all have to leave our parents and face things on our own. However, it's not necessary to please others just to make friends. The main purpose of going to school is to study. Even if you don't have many friends, there's no need to feel sad.

question: An 18-year-old girl has been unwilling to go out and meet other people for the past six months. How can she improve?
description: In the past half year, I have been on leave at home due to physical and mental reasons. However, I have gradually become unwilling to go out, unwilling to have visitors at home (strangers). I feel very uncomfortable having strangers in my house, and I even hide in my room and spend time online. I also seldom chat with friends, and sometimes I feel anxious and uncomfortable when communicating with strangers on social media. Moreover, I often feel a bit inferior in general. I want to know what is the specific psychological issue and how can I improve it? (I also have symptoms of binge-eating and self-induced vomiting.)

answers.answer_text: Seeing words as if we were facing each other, I hope these words can bring you even a little bit of warmth. When the problem has already affected your daily life, you must go see a doctor! You must go see a doctor! You must go see a doctor! Others can comfort you and help analyze your problems, but they cannot determine where you are uncomfortable, what illness you have, or what treatment you need through just a few words. So you must go see a doctor. I can only share my opinion based on these few words. Due to the impact of the epidemic, many people, including myself, haven't left their homes for almost half a year. When school resumed at the end of July, I found myself filled with fear and disgust at returning to school; after arriving at school, my previously familiar classmates became strangers. Now I feel anxious when I see other people, sometimes experiencing chest tightness and a desire to lock myself up and not see anyone. I am generally introverted, and with such a long time without human contact, my social skills have slowly diminished, which might be similar to your situation. But you seem to have it worse than I do. I noticed that you mentioned symptoms of binge eating and bulimia, and I am unsure if this is due to the "mental problem" you first mentioned or a result of not wanting to see people. However, this is a serious issue, and no matter what, you should never harm your body. I think you may have some social anxiety disorder, which requires professional medical diagnosis and treatment, so don't take it lightly. To improve this, you can start by chatting online, but don't chat for too long, and stop before you feel uncomfortable. Take gradual steps to improve and don't rush. Also, listen to medical advice and actively seek treatment. Furthermore, based on your mention of low self-esteem and binge eating, I would venture to guess that you feel insecure about your body? If that's the case, you must choose exercise and a balanced diet to maintain your body instead of harming yourself. Health is a lifelong matter. I wish you happiness soon and the confidence to show your unique qualities.

Hello! After carefully reading your question, I feel sorry for you and I hope my answer can help you. From your question, I understand that you are unwilling to go out, unwilling to interact with others, and even unwilling to chat with people through messaging apps. However, don't be too anxious. You can try some methods. First, try to find out the reasons why you don't want to go out or meet people. Once you find the reasons, you can find targeted solutions and improvement methods. Second, try to make adjustments in your daily life. Try to deliberately communicate more with good friends or engage in more conversations. If you have something on your mind, don't keep it to yourself. Try talking to someone you trust. Third, try to participate in collective activities that you are interested in or good at. Such activities usually involve communication with others. When you are enjoying yourself, you may unconsciously start to communicate with others and gradually develop the habit. Fourth, if your mental state is severely impacting your life and none of the methods you've tried work, I suggest seeking help from a psychologist. They are professionals who can provide you with professional methods. I hope my answer can be helpful to you. Take care! You are loved by me and the world.

question: "I suddenly improved a lot in my academic performance, but I always fear that others will surpass me."
description: Lately, I've been feeling very anxious. I usually don't have these kinds of thoughts, but recently my grades have suddenly improved a lot. However, I'm afraid that others will surpass me. Every time I see someone else's homework completely correct, I feel upset. I'm scared of being surpassed by others. And during class when I take notes, I feel uneasy. I'm afraid of others noticing my efforts and then surpassing me. And then surpassing me.
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation, emotional intelligence.

answers.answer_text: Hello, author! Considering your question, I have come up with the following response: 1. Actually, this is quite normal. In psychology, it is called excessive worry. You don't need to put so much pressure on yourself because everyone has one or more bad exams at some point. Don't dwell on this exam. When others surpass you, you should think of it as normal because there are no perfect people in the world. 2. If you still feel excessively worried, you can communicate with your parents in a timely manner or talk to your teacher. Explain your worries to the teacher and seek clarification. You can also seek help from a specialized mental health counselor to answer your questions. 3. If you constantly feel behind, you can study more, utilize your spare time to learn more, read more books, and enhance your learning ability as well as broaden your knowledge scope.

Hello~ From your question description, it seems like you might have a little bit of self-doubt. You seem to care too much about what others think of you, living in other people's world. You can be more confident and discover your strengths. You'll find out, "I'm really great!" Accept yourself and appreciate your beauty. Take a look at yourself, like your improved ranking in exams or how well you've mastered certain knowledge points. Dig out your advantages, praise yourself, and put yourself in "my world." Don't deliberately compare yourself with others, compare yourself with your past self instead. Understand your progress and shortcomings, accept your progress, and slowly correct your shortcomings. Keep challenging and improving yourself, that's the best progress. Learn to be proactive rather than defensive. In your question description, you mentioned "scared of others surpassing you." You can change your mindset and think about how much you can improve in the next exam and how you can break through certain barriers, rather than just defending your current position. Learn to be proactive instead of defensive. Only when we're constantly in an attacking state, we won't slack off and we'll get closer to our goals. Relax and be open to sharing. There's no need to worry about others seeing your efforts. Everyone has their own pace, study plan, and goals. In this high-pressure environment, nobody has time to observe each other closely. So, just relax, don't put too much pressure on yourself, and don't feel like others are scrutinizing your every move. Don't burden yourself too much. Relax, focus on yourself, and don't let other things distract your attention. Living in your own world is more exciting. Learn to share and study with classmates, integrate into the big collective of the class, and build pure friendships. Keep going and best wishes!

question: Reason and emotion seem to be detached, severe depression, can I win?
description: At the age of three, my father passed away, leaving me without a father's love for a long time. After finding my current husband, I saw him as my sole emotional support. However, this terrible marriage worsened my unhappiness... Multiple instances of infidelity shattered my psychological defenses, and the pain of divorce far outweighed the pain of forgiving him. In a state of collapse, I ultimately chose to forgive him to escape greater suffering... However, the stress response after the betrayal made me increasingly sensitive. His every action became my entire daily life. If he treated me well, I would be happy; if he showed even the slightest impatience, I would become restless and listless. Finally, recently, I realized that I was trapped in a deep sadness, avoiding social interactions, feeling sluggish, losing a significant amount of weight, and no longer interested in anything around me. I realized that I might be sick. After consulting a psychologist and receiving a diagnosis of severe depression at the hospital... The doctor's explanation finally made me understand a series of abnormalities that I couldn't comprehend before. But it also became clear that my situation is not doing well. I want to actively change this pessimistic situation, but it seems like my rationality and emotions have become separated. I can't control my emotions on my own. My rationality tells me to stay strong and be happy, but the physical pain in my heart and the overwhelming sadness for no apparent reason make it difficult for me to resist... Each episode lasts about two hours, and my family cannot understand...
keywords: Treatment, somatic response, disease diagnosis, treatment methods.

answers.answer_text: Hello. I feel sorry for your current state. In my personal opinion, it is important not to let oneself down when striving wholeheartedly. However, you have diverted all your attention away from yourself and bestowed it upon someone who cannot meet your expectations, relying on their inconsistent emotions to receive meager nourishment in return. In such a structure, the weaker party is easily isolated by the stronger party, and it is destined that no one will ultimately benefit. Reason and emotion, they have always coexisted and contradicted each other. Under normal circumstances, they each have their place and their duties, and there is no conflict. It is only when conflicts arise that we become aware of the struggle and quarrel between reason and emotion. In this situation, either side winning can solve the current dilemma and problem. But when it is difficult to determine the superiority of either, you experience the state where no one can control anyone, as you feel. In the book "Elephant and the Mahout," the author metaphorically compares emotion to an elephant and reason to the mahout riding the elephant. He says: human rationality actually depends heavily on complex emotions, and only when a brain full of emotions operates smoothly can reason function. Your limitation lies in the fact that the mahout has not yet managed to successfully tame the elephant and instead, the elephant has disrupted the whole rhythm. To re-tame the elephant is extremely difficult, so the author also provides some methods: the only way to win is to leave the gambling table; the only way not to care about the ups and downs of life is to meditate. When you give up the joy that winning brings, you also lose the pain that losing brings. Our spirit is like a bird's precious feathers. The bird doesn't ask other birds to comb them and it will never strip itself bare for any reason. Love yourself like a bird cherishes its feathers, and only when you encounter someone who understands and empathizes will you begin to give. Best wishes!

Friend, hello. Reading your message, I feel a strong sense of sadness and pain, which also makes me admire your courage and strength in seeking help. Even in such a situation, you still thought of leaving a message here for help. I think this is a rare and valuable courage and strength, which shows me how strong the resilience and upward motivation of life can be. Thank you for the inspiration you have given me. Also, from the words between the lines, I feel that your choice of words and sentence structure are precise, vivid, and profound, which shows me that you have a cultured side. Thank you for allowing me to see that. At the same time, I also have a curiosity. How do you manage to describe and seek help from others with relatively accurate and profound language, even when you are in pain and discomfort? Going to a relatively professional platform like this or seeking treatment in a hospital, and so on? How do you perceive your awareness and ability to seek help? How do you cope with the current predicament? I provide some questions for you to consider. 1. If you were to give a name to the predicament you currently face, what would you call it? (Let's assume you call it "Trouble Spirit," because I don't know what you would call it, so I'll assume that.) 2. How long has this "Trouble Spirit" been with you? What influence has it had on you? What is the duration, depth, and breadth of the impact? Please think carefully about these questions. 3. What influence does this "Trouble Spirit" have on your relationship with your husband and other family members? What is the duration, depth, and breadth of the impact? Please think carefully about these questions. 4. When did this "Trouble Spirit" have a lesser impact on you? What happened at that time? What did you do to bring about a lessened outcome of the impact? What else can you do to reduce the impact of the "Trouble Spirit" on you? 5. When did this "Trouble Spirit" have a lesser impact on your relationship with your husband and other family members? What happened at that time? What did you do to bring about an improvement in the relationship and thus reduce the harassment from the "Trouble Spirit"? What else can you do to reduce the impact of the "Trouble Spirit" on your interpersonal relationships? 6. If you have done what was mentioned in points 4 and 5, did the "Trouble Spirit" become stronger or did you become stronger? Did your sense of control over the "Trouble Spirit" increase or decrease? Did the harassment from the "Trouble Spirit" in your interpersonal relationships increase or decrease? 7. What else can you do to minimize the impact and harassment from the "Trouble Spirit"? Well, this is the method I have shared. Please be sure to take out pen and paper to carefully think and write it down. And most importantly, take action to fight against the "Trouble Spirit," because only action is the most powerful. Please give it a try. Good luck.

I have experienced severe depression, so I can understand your pain. You don't want to face the reality that your husband doesn't love you anymore, so you think as long as you don't get divorced, he will come back to you, which is just a fantasy. Or maybe you don't want to face the pain of separation or the feeling of being unwanted and betrayed. You also mentioned that your family doesn't understand you, and I have experienced that too. They think depression is not a big deal, maybe they think you're exaggerating or that you're just idle at home all day. I think you may have security issues, but of course, this is just my personal opinion. When depression strikes, do what you want to do. It's okay to cry and let out the pain for a while, but I still suggest that you don't focus on your husband. It's your life, you should be in control and do what you want. You can do anything. Letting go is indeed difficult. Some say it's easy to do, but hard in practice. Reason tells you to leave him, but emotionally you still have fond memories of him, even though he doesn't love me anymore. I think you will find someone better in the future. Losing someone doesn't always have to be a bad thing.

Family and friends may not have professional knowledge about mental health, and it's normal for them to not understand. Seek help from a mental health counselor. When you start to live a normal life, your family will surely appreciate it and benefit from your recovery. Since the doctor has diagnosed it as severe depression, you can take medication and receive psychological counseling at the same time, which will help you endure less pain.

Why not seek help from a mental health professional? Shouldn't you quickly solve the problem if you are suffering so much? I believe that solving problems first requires accepting the issues that appear in oneself, and then letting the doctor help find suitable solutions and cooperate with treatment. Depression is something many people have encountered, and many have recovered. I don't know much about marriage; I have never been married. But if I were to encounter a partner who repeatedly cheats, I definitely would not forgive them. If they no longer love me, why should we stay together? I don't know your specific situation, so you should seriously think about your health and happiness. Keep going!

question: A junior college student cannot control herself and keeps seeking out her ex-boyfriend, what should she do?
description: I have been with my boyfriend for over two years. We broke up numerous times due to the pandemic, with the reason being that he found being together too difficult. He said he still had feelings, but didn't want to be in a relationship. I really like him and have been struggling to accept this reality. We had so many wonderful moments together which make it hard to let go. I have my own things to do in daily life, but I still feel incredibly helpless when alone. I don't know who to reach out to when I open my phone. After a busy day, I really miss and want to see him... There have been a few occasions when I couldn't resist and went to find him, but he was caring yet distant in his tone. He can't explain anything about our emotions. Continuing this relationship is difficult for me, and I'm aware of it. I want a chance to salvage it, but I truly don't want to constantly think of him and reach out to him. I want to ask everyone, how can I control myself and stop thinking about him and reaching out to him?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello! I can sense that you are a very emotional girl. How do you control yourself from thinking about him? 1: Engage in various activities to divert your attention. Building an intimate relationship often requires a lot of effort from both sides. Therefore, when this kind of relationship breaks, the harm it brings to the individual should not be underestimated, and it is very normal to be immersed in thoughts. In order to reduce the frequency of immersing yourself in this painful emotion, try to regulate your emotions and allocate time reasonably. For example, call your good friends out to go shopping, watch movies, sing, or travel together. When you are with friends, it is difficult to have a break in communication, so there will be no chance to immerse in sadness. When a person engages in actual communication with friends, the brain will involuntarily consider the other person's issues. Therefore, you will set two goals in your mind: answering questions and repeating thoughts. So, instead of being deeply immersed in memories, it is better to divert your attention and regulate your emotions. 2. Look at the problem rationally and objectively, and free yourself from fantasies. Generally speaking, the reason why a person cannot forget memories is that they do not want to forget and instead numb themselves, telling themselves: the separation between the two is only temporary. Both sides can rebuild intimacy, so constantly numbing yourself. Look at the facts that have already happened rationally and objectively, accept the breakup with your boyfriend, and break free from this pain. Everyone needs to live for reality. When an intimate relationship breaks, instead of endless self-blame, it is better to face the problem directly and start a new life. After all, the one who accompanies you for the longest time is always yourself, and friendship and love are just condiments in life. You are the most important. 3. Improve yourself and find the next spiritual support. In psychology, this stage is considered one of the most suitable for self-improvement. If you are unable to extricate yourself from emotional immersion, you can shift your focus and find the next spiritual support, such as setting a new goal, getting a certification, losing weight, learning a new skill, or rebuilding your interests and hobbies. Usually, at this time, people's attention will be completely shifted to this new goal. It will not only double your efficiency but also help you quickly free yourself from the pain and memories of heartbreak. In summary, to completely erase emotions, you must maintain your rationality, not find excuses for yourself or others, and not fabricate false illusions. If your emotions are always sad, then go explore things you were once interested in, use excitement to balance sadness, and thus stabilize your emotions. Ultimately, shift your thoughts to things you love. Time is the best medicine. Who can predict how many beautiful people and things the future holds? Thank you, OP, for reading and sharing. The world and I love you.

How is it possible to immediately let go when there is still an emotional foundation but you have to break up? Hugs to the dear OP~ Let's first summarize the OP's information together: The OP mentioned that they have been together with their boyfriend for about two years. Due to the pandemic, they had many arguments and broke up because the boyfriend felt that being together was difficult. He means that there are still feelings, but he doesn't want to be in a relationship. I really like him and have always found it hard to accept this fact. When two people are together, there have been so many beautiful moments, so how can we just let go? The OP mentioned that during the pandemic, they had many arguments with their boyfriend. What kind of difficulty does the boyfriend mean by "being together is difficult"? Is it the difficulty of being in a long-distance relationship and not being able to meet, or is it the instability of your relationship that makes him feel difficult, or something else? How does the OP view the boyfriend's idea of "difficult"? Does the boyfriend have any other pressures in terms of work or life? The OP mentioned that they have their own things to do during normal times, but they always feel very helpless when alone and they don't know who to talk to when they open their phone. After being busy every day, they really want to see and find him... There have been a few times when I can't help but go to find him, and he does care about me, but his tone is quite cold. When I asked him about our relationship, he couldn't explain it clearly. I have gotten used to the daily greetings and company, and suddenly being broken up, there will definitely be a lot of discomfort and sadness, hugs to the OP~ The OP mentioned here that the boyfriend still cares about them, but the tone is very cold. From this, it seems that the boyfriend is actually quite contradictory, having feelings for you but also feeling exhausted. The OP mentioned that when asked about the relationship, the boyfriend couldn't explain it clearly. What does this specifically refer to? The OP mentioned that it is difficult for them to continue this relationship, and they know it, they also want a chance to save it, but they really don't want to frequently think of him. I want to ask everyone how I can control myself and not think of him or find him. Actually, the question the OP is asking, the OP knows it is very difficult for themselves because this is someone they truly love, how is it possible to just forget about them, right? Based on the current period of the OP's breakup, why not give yourself and the other person some time and space to adjust your own state, then calm down and think about your relationship issues. I know the OP might feel it's very difficult, unable to do it, unable to control themselves. But I want to tell the OP, you must restrain yourself because only in this way maybe there will be a new turning point for your relationship. The world and I love you, best wishes to the OP, Jingjingting.

Hello, the questioner! I can tell that you love him very much and care a lot about this relationship. You mentioned that the man feels it is difficult to be together, so did he mention the specific reasons? You mentioned in the text that you had many arguments during the pandemic and then broke up. So, think about what situations or things could cause you to argue? If you were to reconcile, could these issues be resolved? You said you don't want to think about him, but actually want to move on from the habit of having him around, right? Letting go of a relationship or forgetting someone takes time to fade. When I was dumped in the past, I would constantly think about her, so I understand how you feel now. So, how can we get out of this whirlpool? You can try a few methods: 1. Find something to do that you are interested in. 2. Find a job (if you have already graduated) or do part-time work, volunteering is also an option. 3. Avoid revisiting places related to him as much as possible. 4. Be determined to delete everything related to him (depending on your own willingness). Hopefully, my answer can help you!

question: Because of being too thin, I am becoming increasingly irritable and on the verge of a breakdown. What should I do?
description: 155, 76 pounds. Actually, many people have this weight, and I don't feel particularly thin. I eat a lot at school, but my weight still doesn't go up. When I come home from school, my family is overly concerned about my weight, and the neighbors' mockery about my figure makes me feel very frustrated. Just seeing my mom showing concern for me makes me want to beat her up. I guess it's because I feel depressed that I'm getting thinner and thinner.
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Sending you a big, big hug! Hello, OP. Some points of confusion in your description: - The ridicule from your neighbor is making you feel devastated. - Your relationship with your mother is making you irritable. From this, it can be seen that you are currently experiencing conflicting emotions. The ridicule from your neighbor can be devastating, while your mother's concern makes you irritable. When others focus on your physical appearance, you will become caught up in a dilemma: what is the "normal" weight? [Shifting your mindset] Your body shape does not have to satisfy others; your health is the most important thing. When it comes to your concern about your appearance, you can think about the underlying issues. Why are you so concerned about your physical appearance? Are you using others' concern about your body shape to resist or redirect attention from other problems? Occasionally, change your mindset regarding others' concern. Why do they care about us so much? It's because they can't bear to see us make mistakes. The only difference is their way of expressing it, which leads us to feel differently. Learn to communicate with each person using different methods and express your thoughts. This will greatly solve the issue. I wish you all the best! The above is just my personal opinion. If you need further assistance, please feel free to message me. For more professional help, please seek out a professional counselor.

question: Unable to adapt to college life, excessive introversion brings a lot of distress and discomfort.
description: Feeling like others have many good friends, while I am always isolated, and always feel very suffocated in my heart, always wanting to cry.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Hugs to you. It is evident that you are feeling helpless right now because you feel lonely. Friends indeed play a significant role in our lives, always accompanying us and giving us strength. In our lifetime, we can meet many people, but only a few can truly be our sincere friends. We only become good friends with someone when we find someone we can easily connect with, someone we share similarities with or share the same values. Interactions between friends are always the most comfortable, where two people can eat, drink, and laugh without any worries. Being together can bring much happiness. OP, you may not have met this person yet, so you have to wait. Whenever we find ourselves in a new environment, it does require an adjustment phase, and once we overcome this phase, our lives will become better. Actually, university life is not as complicated as we imagine because everyone is in the same boat, having not yet entered society. You can try to overcome this aspect of yourself, starting with greeting others in your daily life. It is indeed not easy to suddenly change your personality that you have had for a long time. Keep going, and I believe you can do it. Best wishes~.

question: A single woman has moved out of her family home for four years, how should she deal with controlling parents?
description: Only daughter in the family, already 29 years old, parents have been arguing since childhood, and have a strong preference for sons over daughters. Because they only have me as a daughter, they have never felt secure and have always had a strong desire to control. It feels like there are two pairs of eyes watching me at home, constantly nitpicking. They have never been satisfied with anything I do. I also give them money for living expenses, and I give them 50,000 yuan a year, including the year-end bonus. But they don't care because they are into stock trading. No matter how valuable the gifts I give them are, they always just throw them aside and don't use or look at them. I invited them to go to Thailand, but they said Thailand is a third world country. When will I take them to the United States? They make me really tired of marriage, and I feel depressed when I'm around them. Later, it was confirmed by the hospital that I have depression. In the end, I found that living alone is great. I graduated from graduate school and have been renting my own place for 4 years. But my parents always think there's something wrong with me for not getting married. When we try to communicate, they don't listen to my thoughts at all, and they think my ideas are useless crap. So, I started to ignore them and we don't contact each other anymore. I take anti-depressant medication while feeling guilty that I haven't done enough to satisfy them. It's really agonizing. They know that I have depression, but they think it's because I'm useless and it has nothing to do with them.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication

answers.answer_text: "How to deal with controlling parents" actually does not require methods or strategies, only a decision. Your delay in making a decision may be because you haven't realized that you are still a pleasing child in front of them, full of expectations and dependency, including "being diagnosed with depression in the hospital". You seem to subconsciously hope or feel that your parents should be responsible for this. The care and attention you desire is probably something you can't get no matter how much you please them, if it were possible, you would have gotten it long ago. One day, when you are no longer that child, perhaps they will look at you with new eyes. It is not your fault to be born a girl, it is the arrangement of fate, and you can confidently face it. Whoever cannot accept reality will suffer."

I don't know how to advise you, because my current situation is even worse than yours. Your parents strictly control you, but my conversations on WeChat and with friends are constantly monitored by my mom. She makes me repeat everything word for word and then criticizes me for how I should say it, and I can't escape from it now. I am not trying to make you feel better with my own sorrow, but parents and children are two equal individuals in my opinion. I have always believed that parents only have more life experience than children, and this experience does not refer to what you eat or drink, but to foresight. Moreover, this foresight only provides advice in a broad direction. So if your parents intervene in trivial matters or in matters of emotions, it is advice that has nothing to do with age. But if it's about marriage or major ethical issues, it can be taken into consideration, why only consider it? Because times have changed. This way, you can know which nagging can be ignored and which are their freedom of expression.

question: Just broke up and not accustomed to being single, even feel that the other person is pretty good?
description: I met a boy online in April this year. He is sensitive and kind, and we have similar interests. He quickly expressed his liking for me, and over time, his thoughtfulness made me start liking him too. I even thought that we might not meet someone so compatible again and even considered the possibility of marriage. So, after three months of knowing each other, I also expressed my liking for him. We just started dating these few days. When we were not together, I would daydream about being together, but now that we are, I feel calm. He seems to like me too much, constantly asking if I love him and wanting me to say it out loud. If I don't reply to his messages, he would call me. I feel passive in this relationship. I am someone who expresses emotions openly, but I don't like how fast this relationship is progressing. Another factor might be that there was someone in high school who really liked me. He doesn't contact me much, so I thought he didn't like me. But whenever we meet, he is kind to me. However, when I liked him, he didn't like me, and when he liked me, I didn't like him. It went back and forth twice. He said that if I didn't have someone I liked by the end of this year, we should try being together. Yesterday I told him I am no longer single, and he asked me to enjoy it and not overthink. He sounded happy. I'm afraid that the person I am with now won't understand me as well as he does.

answers.answer_text: According to the description given by the topic poster, it seems that the guy you met online is more sincere and values you more. Although he may be a bit dependent and clingy, and not very mature, constantly asking if you love him and calling if you don't reply to his messages, it indirectly shows that he cares about you a lot and is willing to have a responsible relationship with you. Moreover, he has a similar personality and common interests, and if your values also match, it may get better with patience and compatibility. Your relationship is relatively equal, and in such a dynamic, the girl is more likely to be happy. On the other hand, the other guy is not in a hurry to confirm the relationship with you, and even mentioned that he would only try with you if there is no one else he likes, which appears to be a bit like keeping a backup option. People who like each other should instinctively hold on firmly, rather than having this kind of laissez-faire attitude. When you told him that you are no longer single, he didn't seem anxious but instead asked you to experience it and his tone was cheerful and relaxed. Either he is pretending and actually feeling hurt inside, or he is an expert at flirting with girls who are below his level. In summary, based on the overall situation, you are more likely to be happy with the first guy, while there's a possibility of getting hurt with the latter. Trust your inner feelings, if you feel that you may not be able to handle this guy and the gap between you is significant, it is usually not suitable, as it can easily lead to being controlled by the other person. It is easier for you to be happy with someone who is similar to you and you can be 100% sure of their feelings for you.

Hello, just being together with this guy, he highly values your worth and makes many small gestures to demand that you also acknowledge him. However, his needs have reached the point of impatience, which has caused you to feel repulsed. This underlying phenomenon indicates that your values are not equal. People instinctively reject those who do not match up in various aspects. At this time, a high school classmate who is indifferent to you appears. He is not very concerned about your worth; to him, you are optional. Otherwise, why haven't you been together already? Is there a chance for someone else to take advantage of the situation? This situation shows that his value is higher than yours, and people are instinctively attracted to those with higher value.

It sounds like you feel more at ease and more comfortable with this person from high school who you have known for a long time, compared to the boyfriend you met online. In your title, however, you mention that you are just out of a relationship and not used to being alone. Which aspect do you find more troubling?

question: A 45-year-old woman doesn't want to continue doing her current job because it is too exhausting. How can she break free from this predicament?
description: I am 45 years old and feel very tired from work. I want to change jobs, but I don't have a high level of education or specific skills. I also don't know which direction to develop in, which is causing a lot of inner turmoil.
keywords: Career, career management, midlife crisis, work fatigue.

answers.answer_text: First of all, give yourself a hug. I believe that you wouldn't be seeking advice here if you weren't feeling tired and miserable. 1. I'm not sure about your current job. How long have you been doing it? Do you have permanent status? How is the salary and benefits? Can your own experience in the current job be of any help to you and become an asset? Have you seen any progress or growth in your current job? What are the prospects for development? Many times, we want to be impulsive and follow our emotions, but afterwards we may regret and blame ourselves. 2. You said that you don't have a high education and skills, which at least shows that you have a clear understanding and orientation of yourself. So, have you considered finding ways to make yourself less tired in your current job? For example, do you have to do everything yourself? Or have you accepted many tasks that don't belong to you? Have you done anything to relieve your exhaustion? Like complaining? Or communicating and giving feedback to your supervisor? 3. In terms of salary that can support yourself, what do you enjoy doing? What are you good at? Are there any hobbies or interests that you can develop? Can you find a job with good salary and benefits? Can you handle it? 4. People feel exhausted and miserable because the salary and benefits are not aligned with their interests and hobbies. The rational "me" and emotional "me" are conflicting, and if they cannot reconcile, you will continue to struggle with this pain. You need to answer the above questions clearly for yourself, and that's the advice I can give. In short, try to find a job that can support yourself, that you enjoy and have interest in, and that offers flexibility in schedule. If not, find ways to balance these aspects in your current job. For example, can you delegate some tasks and not focus only on earning more money?

Hello, one of my current job responsibilities is headhunting, and I would like to analyze this issue based on the current workplace ecosystem. The midlife crisis in the workplace usually starts at the age of 35 because many job positions have an upper age limit of 35. This is not to say that companies discriminate against anyone, but rather it is the reality of the workplace ecosystem. If you are over 35, unless you have a great accumulation (accumulation of skills, expertise, platform, and connections), and can reach a high-level position or hold an irreplaceable position in another company, your career will basically reach a plateau and slowly decline. After a certain period of decline, you will have to seek a new path, which is why middle-aged people are more likely to start their own businesses because they can't find a job with developmental and sustainable opportunities. Now, let's address your current issue, which is also something I am currently facing. The career development of middle-aged people, especially women, is difficult. You are now in your 40s, have no particularly outstanding skills, and are unsure of where to go next. I have the following suggestions that may help you: 1. If you can't find a better direction at the moment, focus on doing your current job well and complete the tasks at hand. 2. Reflect on your inner self, hobbies, resources, skills, and psychological tendencies to create a clear career plan. If you don't have the courage to break free from your current environment right away, you can start by developing a side business. It's both an exploration and a transition time for yourself. (For details on developing a side business and career planning, you can private message me. I participated in a side business training camp and had great results. I can recommend it to you). 3. Determine your track. Everything we do is like a race, running on different tracks. You must be certain that you are on the right track to save yourself time. For example, you might be a headline creator and frequently compare your earnings with others, which can cause a lot of anxiety. But is this the main path you want to pursue in the future? You must be clear about this; otherwise, you will fall into meaningless and involuntary comparisons and anxieties, wasting your time. I sincerely hope that this advice can be helpful to you.

question: I feel so miserable inside. I've been crying all day. Why is life so difficult?
description: I have experienced so much today that I can't do anything anymore. I feel exhausted, living is too tiring. I want someone to see my pain, to take care of me, to hug me. I want everyone to tell me, "Fool, don't be afraid, I am here." Why is life so hard?
keywords: Emotion, depressive emotion, anxious emotion, panic helplessness

answers.answer_text: Give yourself a good hug first. Maybe everyone will encounter such moments when they feel sad and find it hard to live. Hug you again. But by coming here to express yourself, you have already opened a window for yourself, and there will always be light shining into your heart. There are people who will listen to you seriously and accept you completely. This is a safe haven. When you are sad, don't make any major decisions. If you are able to recognize your emotions, slowly let yourself be with these emotions for a while. Just like the movie "Inside Out" tells us, various emotions - joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness - are all normal, that's life. But when you peacefully stay with your emotions for a while, you will understand that emotions come and go, just let nature take its course. Of course, if the feeling of sadness lasts for a long time, you should actively find ways to adjust, such as seeking support, exercising, getting enough rest, and so on. I wish you to firmly believe that there are people who love you unconditionally and support you even when you are sad! You are already wonderful and worthy of love! Hug you again!

We all have a difficult life, regardless of age. After primary school, we lose our childhood. There are entrance exams in middle school, the college entrance examination in high school, job hunting in college, and wages at work. Various problems bother different people. Some cry at night, some are lost during the day, and some are constantly anxious. I am a middle school student, not good at studying, lacking interest in learning, but I desire to be admitted to a top high school more than anyone else. My target score is a hundred points lower than mine. There are only two days left until the third year of middle school, let's survive together. It seems that the only way out is to endure the hardships.

question: Why do some people think nothing of anything, while I am always tormented by inner demons?
description: Why is it that some people can do bad things and still have a good mindset, while I feel such a heavy sense of guilt? Even when it's others who treat me poorly and I argue back, I still feel guilty and distressed. It seems like I'm always mentally tormented, with a particularly strong sense of guilt. Why is it that some people can say hurtful things and still feel at ease, continuing to be happy and carefree? Throughout one's life, it's impossible to always meet kind and good-hearted people; many people are unkind and use harsh words. Why is it that I can't adjust myself and am so greatly influenced by others? Is there a solution to this problem? Could it be that in my past life, I did something wrong and now I have to suffer psychologically in this life? This has been the case for me since childhood, and it's not related to any hidden childhood experiences; it's solely due to my own personality.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's great to "meet" you! Reading your words, I can understand the distress you're experiencing due to the influence of your personality. First, let me give you a big hug. Now, let's analyze your situation together, identify the issues, and try to find ways to solve them. Firstly, you have two main problems. The first is a heavy sense of guilt, and the second is being overly concerned about others. Let's talk about the guilt first. What is guilt? It is a subjective feeling when a person does something that goes against their own conscience and subsequently feels regret or a sense of wrongdoing. Simply put, guilt arises when we go against our own beliefs. Everyone has their own inherent sense of right and wrong. When our actions violate this inherent understanding, we feel guilt. Guilt is also a mechanism of self-restraint. You may wonder why some people can do bad things and not care, while others feel tortured by guilt even when they haven't done anything wrong. This issue is related to the depth of a person's conscience. Some individuals have a shallow conscience and low moral requirements, so they find it difficult to feel guilt.
