On the other hand, those with a deeper conscience tend to feel guilt more easily. That's why some people feel uneasy after doing the same thing, while others can be at peace with themselves. Now, let's discuss being overly concerned about others. What is the direct result of being overly concerned about others? It means neglecting our own feelings. But did you know, everyone has a sense of self? When this sense of self is not valued, it rebels, leading to feelings of repression and lack of freedom. In other words, repressing emotions for a long time can eventually lead to emotional distress. Everyone needs self-identity, self-awareness, and self-acceptance. Therefore, instead of always considering others' feelings first, we should reflect on our own feelings. Is this good for us? From these two issues, we can see some aspects of your personality. You seem to be a very kind person, with high moral standards and sensitivity. You tend to suppress your emotions, care about others' feelings, and worry about how others perceive you. Many of these aspects are psychological issues, so it's important to seek psychological guidance. Firstly, nobody is perfect, so try to relax and not demand perfection in everything. It might be helpful to view things that don't go as planned with a more open mind and tell yourself that it's not a big deal, there's no need to dwell on it. Secondly, shift your focus to doing things you enjoy. It will bring you joy and help you forget your worries. Thirdly, read more books to enrich your spiritual world and enhance self-awareness. Lastly, if the issues are severe, seeking guidance from a psychologist can be beneficial. Remember, it's not an illness, so don't be nervous. It's just like chatting with a professional who can help you understand yourself better and solve problems. I wish you well and hope you can overcome your distress soon!

Hello, a clear heart and a knowing word. Based on your description, you may belong to the group of "highly sensitive individuals". You are more prone to empathy and it is harder for you to let go of the past and easily get stuck in one thing. Your descriptions such as "I feel guilty even though it's others' fault," "I am mentally tormented," "I can't adjust and I am greatly influenced by others," all align with the characteristics of "highly sensitive individuals". However, a specific diagnosis would require further detailed discussion. You can find relevant information to learn more or consult with a counselor for further communication.

You are right when you say that different people have different levels of sensitivity towards the same thing. There is no need to feel unfair because being a "highly sensitive individual" also has many advantages. For example, empathy is a crucial trait for a psychologist, which belongs to the category of "highly sensitive individuals". Counselors need to deeply feel the interviewee's pain and distress. Those who lack empathy cannot experience others' feelings. Many artists are also "highly sensitive individuals" who require more delicate emotions and express them.

You are currently troubled because it feels frustrating and helpless that despite someone else's fault, you are the one deeply affected while others seem unaffected. However, we cannot determine whether this issue bothers others based solely on surface appearances. Furthermore, whether others feel bothered or not is actually not important, as the popular saying goes, "it's none of my business". Due to your "high sensitivity" personality, you need to consciously shut off your emotions when unnecessary to avoid unnecessary interference. This requires self-awareness and self-control, which is not easy at first. In summary, being a "highly sensitive individual" is a personality trait, and personality is neither good nor bad. What you need is to understand and accept yourself, achieve self-regulation, and self-control. In my role as a counselor, I also face many negative emotions daily and need to frequently engage in self-regulation. No one can do it perfectly from the beginning. At the same time, your personality trait actually belongs to the talented category. You need to explore the positive aspects of your personality more. Best wishes!

Hug, I understand your feelings very well. Let's analyze the problems you are facing: You always take things to heart, whether it's your own mistakes or others'. This kind of hypersensitivity is called "neuroticism" in psychology. It is not a big problem, but this excessive sensitivity often brings unpleasant emotions and even troubles. "Neuroticism" often occurs in introverted individuals. Excessive sensitivity is not a disease, but it is a negative psychological quality. If not overcome, it will not only affect work and study but also affect physical and mental health, causing tension in interpersonal relationships. How to overcome it? First, don't speculate on other people's evaluations of yourself. In daily life, maintain a calm mindset and a trusting perspective towards people and things around you. Focus on yourself and change the mindset that thinks someone is always paying attention to you or opposing you. Don't make a big deal out of small matters or treat your imagined feelings as real, as it would add unnecessary psychological pressure. Second, learn to be kind to others. Be tolerant of other people's shortcomings, learn to get along harmoniously with all kinds of people, and focus on the strengths of others. By gaining respect and care from others, avoid being overly picky towards others. This is how others will accept and like you, making yourself happy and making others feel relaxed. Third, manage your expectations properly. Before doing anything, don't set the goal or expectation too high and consider all the unfavorable factors, leaving room for flexibility. If expectations are set too high, disappointment often awaits. Fourth, have a broad mind. Be more optimistic and magnanimous when faced with situations. To achieve success, a person must possess generosity and cultivation and use psychological suggestion to change their sensitive nature and broaden their mind.

Hello, OP! I understand your feelings very well. From your description, I can sense your inner pain and torment. Sending you a hug. [Problem Analysis] Your problem lies in feeling guilty and having a tendency to dwell on things, even if sometimes the problem is not your fault. It can be seen that you are a sensitive person, and because you care too much, you tend to make a big deal out of something that is actually quite normal, which leads to distress and anxiety. [Some Suggestions] Adjust your mindset. The reason you are not happy is because you care too much about what others think. From another perspective, you are also a kind person. After conflicts, you reflect on yourself instead of blaming others, and feel guilty for your actions. But you should remember that life is yours, and the most important thing is to live happily. As long as you have a clear conscience, you don't need to be too hard on yourself about everything. Adjust your mindset and focus on your own feelings. Participate in some activities and interact with people. You can try to participate in some activities to communicate more with the outside world and meet people from different fields and industries. In the process of communicating with them, open up your heart. As you meet more people and experience different things, your perspective on issues and your inner thoughts will change. Maybe things that we used to care about a lot, we later discover are actually very normal and not worth so much attention. Confide in friends and seek their help. Some things, at the time, we care a lot about, and once we become entangled in them, it is difficult to detach ourselves. At such times, it is necessary to express our inner thoughts, confide in friends around us, listen to their advice and opinions, and slowly find a way out with their help. I wish you the ability to ease your mind and live a happy and fulfilling life.

Hello, dear. Each of us is like an independent circle. This circle will undergo some adaptive changes as a result of changes in the people and things around us. However, the stable essence of the circle remains unchanged. But if a person does not have enough secure and stable self, they will easily change shape with the influence of the surrounding environment and things, losing the original stability of their own circle. This is why in life, your emotions often get mixed up with the emotions of others, and you lack a stable sense of self-worth and understanding, and the habit of self-attack. This is how the current state is formed.

Hello, OP, I understand and sympathize with the feelings you're wrestling with. You seem to have a sensitive personality, which is related to your nature. Sensitivity is actually a talent that can be used to better understand oneself and others. However, the downside is that it can lead to emotional strain and a feeling of being mentally exhausted and torn. Fortunately, you have recognized this issue and are consciously working on improving it. One technique is to accept the fact that is causing you distress in your life and then mentally say to yourself, "but whatever." This self-talk can provide you with a mental suggestion to become more fearless. Also, we are all adults, and each person is responsible for their own emotions, so you don't need to worry about how others feel internally. Lastly, even if there are times when you say or do something wrong that leads to turmoil, don't be too hard on yourself because nobody is perfect and it is common for people to say or do wrong things in their daily lives.

Hello, OP. I hope I can help you. It can be seen that you are a very kind person, and whatever you do, you do it with great care and responsibility! In fact, we are the same! Sometimes, even though it would be time-saving and effortless to continue doing something in a certain way, we still feel that it is not excellent enough and does not achieve the desired results! Therefore, we should strive to do our best in everything we do! Firstly, it is not our fault! It is just our responsible and diligent nature! As long as we do things according to our own thoughts without violating principles, it is okay! Keep it up! I hope this helps you!

question: Some things can make you feel frustrated when they are out of control.
description: After losing control of certain things, one may become very irritable. People in the team often become wise after the event.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that 1. When things go out of control, it makes OP feel very irritable. 2. The team members always speak up after the fact, which is annoying. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Most people plan their time and work by setting a schedule for themselves. However, plans often cannot keep up with the changes in life, various minor disturbances, and unexpected events can disrupt the original plan. Feeling irritated in these situations is a normal emotion. Being able to calm down after irritation and continue to deal with problems is already very commendable and enough to accomplish most things in life. 2. OP can start thinking about and gathering the team members for discussions before making a plan. Consider possible errors and reasons for failure, and make efforts to avoid failure. In this way, even if unexpected situations arise later, they can be dealt with promptly.

question: 20-year-old female, has been consistently negative and experiencing intense mood swings over the past year.
description: In the past year, my emotions have been extremely unstable. I often become angry and irritable, even though I try to control my temper. These emotional outbursts are often triggered by trivial matters, such as my parents constantly pressuring me to socialize and discuss future marriage plans (even though I don't enjoy socializing and am not prepared for married life). Sometimes, my friends unknowingly touch on sensitive topics that upset me, or there may be negative events happening online. Drawing helps me temporarily alleviate my mood, but I never know when my mood will unexpectedly plummet again. I strongly resist socializing, although I don't explicitly show my level of dislike. Sometimes, I feel that life is meaningless, and both the world and myself annoy and disgust me, but I don't want to end my life in any way. I believe I have depressive emotions, but there's another voice inside me saying that I'm just pretending and being influenced by reading too many depression case studies. I experience insomnia about once or twice a month.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, expressing emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. I completely understand how the OP feels, as I have had similar experiences myself. I don't know why my mood has been low recently, and I can't help but get angry and become easily agitated. The OP may want to try to think about when these emotions started. Often, when we enter into such emotional states, it may be due to the pressure from school or work, or the influence of family and friends around us. Finding the root cause of the problem is key to finding a better solution. Secondly, choosing activities like drawing to relax is a very good choice. The OP should try to find some activities that can help calm their emotions. On the other hand, when negative emotions become overwhelming and cannot be released, the OP can choose activities that offer more stress relief, such as exercise. The OP can also try "pre-warning" the people around them, and let them help you. See if others are aware of or have noticed your problems. And the most important thing is to not doubt your own judgment. If you feel that these emotions are becoming uncontrollable and are increasingly impacting your normal life, seek professional help in a timely manner.

question: Depression, lately I haven't been taking medication as per the doctor's advice, feeling miserable. Should I consider switching therapists?
description: Depression, recently I no longer cooperate with the doctor to take medication, and I don't want to face the counselor. It is very painful. Because of my poor financial situation, I have a regular counselor. I don't know if we have established a normal and formal counseling relationship. I have not been doing counseling regularly and often only go to her when I have problems or for several consecutive days. The frequency of seeking her help is based on my financial and emotional responses. Anyway, I keep seeking counseling, but I am still constantly suffering. Even though it is intermittent, we have maintained it for over a year. I have also spent a lot of money during this year, and I have formed a dependency on her. Now it seems like I am not satisfied with anything, including her. Today, when I said that I don't want to live anymore, she ignored me. How could this be? What should I do? I have all kinds of problems. I want to give up but also feel that I can't live without her. What should I do? My situation and financial condition are not good. My family can't help, and sometimes I really just want to die. I can't live without her, but at the same time, I hate her. She has already disappointed me several times. Maybe I am projecting my hatred for others onto her. What should I do? What should I resolve? It's all chaos.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, it can be seen that there is resistance and a hidden sense of attack towards taking medication and facing the counselor. The attack is internalized and directed towards oneself. Your reliance on your counselor is because whenever you encounter problems, you go to them, as if there is always an escape route when faced with difficulties. In this situation, it is problematic for the counselor not to advise against it. I remember when I was ridiculed by someone in the past and found myself crying in the bathroom, I called my counselor, and she told me not to always turn to her whenever something happens. She advised me to give myself a buffer period and a stage for reflection, not to rely on her for everything. That was truly the only time I called her in such a situation. So if your counselor hasn't cautioned you about this behavior, then there is a certain issue of irresponsibility. The relationship between counselor and client is a mutual choice, and in the initial contact, it is important to understand as much information and background of each other as possible to assess suitability. You can go to a reputable hospital or local mental health center for a 50-minute session of counseling, which usually does not exceed 200 yuan. If the prices are different in your area, then, if financially possible, you can go once a week. If not, you can go every two weeks or have a fixed monthly session, which will have better results compared to sporadic counseling sessions.

question: Unable to focus on one's emotions, always thinking about finding another option?
description: Every time I'm in a relationship, I can't fully commit. I always have the mindset of "keeping my options open" and flirting with other guys for excitement and novelty.

answers.answer_text: In relationships, what do you want to get? Is it freshness? If you want freshness, then when choosing a partner, you can find a romantic guy who pursues romance. But then again, everyone has their own things to do in life, and it's impossible to be romantic in everything. Can we lower the demand for novelty, because in the end, we have to return to life. Also, when choosing an emotional connection, can this relationship give you a sense of security? If you don't have the ability to restrain yourself or manage a relationship yet, then focus on living your life well for now, and search for it when you are capable.

question: How to treat the transition from imitating and learning from a young age to being indifferent and forgetful?
description: I was adopted, and my adoptive father would send me to stay at my aunt's house since I was little, in exchange for free medical care for me. My aunts always told me that I was an outsider and couldn't cause trouble or make a mess. They would always just go through the motions with me and then tell me to entertain myself. I also learned to be indifferent and just go through the motions with everything, not actively participating in group activities and quickly forgetting about things afterwards. Now that has resulted in me treating my work the same way - just going through the motions and forgetting about it afterwards. I have sleep anxiety and unease. How can I change myself and treat myself? I can't keep forgetting about the content of my work right after finishing it. I need to ensure the quality of my sleep.

answers.answer_text: With a stroke of the pen, the lonely and timid little girl who stayed with her aunt is now vividly depicted on paper. Everyone is innocent, and all past events are embedded in our bodies, seemingly becoming a part of our lives, always there for us to see. If life is a seed, every seed needs abundant psychological nourishment. We have come a long way from learning to walk step by step, and if there is a lack of psychological nourishment within, we will spend our entire lives searching for it. In other words, everyone has an inner child in need of healing. Perhaps the symptoms are just the surface, forgotten or dismissed, but behind the anxiety and unrest, there are many occurrences in the subconscious that need to be acknowledged. Time can't change this, only learning and growth can. If you need it, if you're willing, maybe we can try together to go back to the past, slowly explore, slowly discover, and slowly grow. Give yourself time to harvest the confident and strong version of yourself, okay? I'm here, and the world and I love you.

question: Why is my heart up and down when I haven't completed my task?
description: I want to ask everyone a question. These past few days, I have noticed a situation where when I am almost reaching my goal, but still a little short, my mind becomes restless and I feel very uneasy. I am worried about falling short and constantly feel the need to check on my progress. How can I calmly approach this issue? How can I adjust myself a little? Also, can anyone help me take a look and see what underlying problems I need to address? Thank you for your answers.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~ First, give you a warm hug. I understand your feelings very well. From your post, I learned that you feel very unsettled in your heart when you are close to completing a task. Perhaps you are worried about something or worried that you haven't completed the task, but it's more of a nervous and excited feeling about completing the task. Actually, this is a very common phenomenon. If you have already completed the task but the deadline hasn't arrived yet, you may also have a similar feeling. I believe that there is one situation that everyone has experienced, and that is during exams. In this situation, it's approaching the end time but we haven't finished yet. Another situation is when we have finished, but the end time is approaching. Actually, in both cases, we will feel a sense of nervousness. This is actually very normal. Because our emotions fluctuate not because of whether we have completed the task, but because of the existence of the deadline. Therefore, OP doesn't have to worry about this emotional state. Of course, OP can also try to self-regulate, such as using appropriate self-suggestions or seizing the time to complete the project. Best wishes~.

question: In school, when someone looks at you, it can make you feel very uncomfortable. What should you do?
description: Walking in the school or in the classroom, I feel very uncomfortable whenever someone looks at me, but if I am with friends or going out to play, it doesn't bother me like that.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. The gaze of others may be avoided, but what we truly fear is self-examination and self-discontent. From your description, I can sense your fear and anxiety in the face of the gaze of others. When there are familiar people around, the situation improves. Changing your view of others' gaze, perhaps when you think about it rationally, you will realize that their gaze towards you is not malicious, and not everyone is curious about you. It may be that you actively "focus" the gaze of others on yourself, projecting internal concerns and insecurities. Perhaps these feelings are deeply hidden in your consciousness, but because such feelings are strong and persistent, they will inevitably emerge from the subconscious. For example, when we suddenly have a few pimples on our face one day, we tend to feel that people around us are looking at the pimples on our face, and we feel that we don't look as good as usual, so our mood becomes worse because of the gaze of others. But in fact, the number of times others gaze at us is the same as usual, it's just that we care too much and "increase" their gaze in our psychological perception. Find the reason why you fear the gaze of others, and take practical actions to change it, so that even when you are alone, you can confidently face everyone's gaze. When you go out with friends, it gives you a sense of security invisibly and makes you feel supported internally, even if they haven't done anything, just walking together. Try to increase the number of times you go out alone. When you feel uncomfortable and helpless when being stared at, let yourself think about something easy in your mind, such as subtracting 3 from 789 continuously, or turning your gaze away from the person staring at you and looking at the road or plants nearby, or think of something happy (who you were with, when, what you did, why you felt happy, the more details the better), or hum a song that you remember the lyrics to, etc. The purpose is to relax yourself and not constantly focus your mental resources on the gaze of others. Practice this several times, it's okay to fail at the beginning, just keep going. When you are no longer afraid of the gaze of others, try to interact and communicate freely with others. All of our shortcomings and shortcomings are achieved through day-to-day changes and efforts. Believe in yourself and dare to try. Good luck.

question: 14-year-old girl, recently for the past two weeks, has been having a tendency to overthink and is unable to concentrate on studying.
description: Recently, I always like to think about some very distant or unrealistic things. For example, how I would spend a lot of money in the future, what my ideal type would be when looking for a partner, what life would be like studying abroad... Personally, I know that the above content is not something I should be considering right now and it's of no benefit to me in the present. But sometimes I just can't control myself. In the morning, even though I could wake up at 6:30 am, I end up daydreaming for more than an hour in a daze, and I feel regretful when I finally get up. I really want to find a method to reject or restrain these random thoughts because they have seriously affected my studies. I want to find some specific measures. Thank you!
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ I want to say, what a coincidence! I used to have a tendency to think randomly, pondering about what I will do in the future, how much money I will earn, what kind of life I will have, etc. I even think about these things before going to bed, and sometimes during class. When I realized that my thoughts were becoming more and more idealistic and detached from reality, I tried many methods to suppress these daydreams. I think you can try these methods too: shift your focus. When your brain starts to create scenarios, remind yourself to stop in time and prevent the imagination from going deeper. At this moment, you can shift your focus and concentrate on other things, like seeing what tasks you can do nearby, or reading a book, or writing something, divert your attention to the reality. Prepare small details to remind yourself. You can stick a sticky note on your school desk, with words like "Study diligently, mind don't wander" or similar, you can also use sticky notes at your home desk as reminders, or even stick a small drawing or sticky note on your bedside table. When you fall into imagination again, tell yourself that in order to have such a life in the future, you need to start working hard now. You should develop a series of study plans or life plans, so that you know if you want your dreams to come true, you need to seize the present, and strive to make your life the way you want it to be. Best wishes!

question: Are you particularly anxious about your own life? Do you really have to do a lot of things ahead of time in life?
description: I am particularly anxious about my life, and I am always afraid of missing out on something. I work very hard to get what I want. One consequence of this is that I always want to finish one thing, and if I don't, I will be very anxious, very anxious, and even unable to do anything else. I feel like my coordination skills are very poor, and I cannot shift my attention from one point to another. I went for counseling and found out that I am very anxious to complete my tasks and then avoid confronting them. In fact, the more I want to finish, the more I am actually escaping, right? I am very conflicted, and suddenly I feel like I want to live this whole life and live it perfectly. Do I really need to arrange so much for myself? I hope someone can help me sort out my thoughts and help me adjust.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I want to give you a hug and shake your hand because we are in the same boat. I hope you can feel this little bit of strength. Firstly, there is a clear problem with poor coordination and the inability to shift attention. Is it necessary to live a perfect life and arrange so many things? Secondly, let's break down the problem. From your description, it is evident that you are a very responsible person who knows what you want. You have high demands and maybe even perfectionism. Under these high demands, you don't leave yourself any room for buffering. Once you fail to meet your ideal goals, you fall into anxiety and panic. In other words, you lack elasticity at the moment. You also mentioned that when one task is unfinished, you focus on that particular point and may not be able to do other things. This reflects a problem with "time management" and "planning". In this kind of life, you must be very busy and fulfilled. Even comparing to most people, you are in a high-intensity state. This means you may enjoy the sense of achievement that comes with it, but at the same time, you face an equal amount of pressure. Setting a perfect life or future life plan for yourself is not a problem because everyone has their own desired way of life, it's just that you desire this particular one. However, if you feel uncomfortable, unhappy, or even start experiencing panic and anxiety during this process, then there are certain issues that need attention. Life needs a balance. It is impossible to stay in high gear all the time, as both the body and mind cannot bear it. Thirdly, here are some practical suggestions. Find ways to ease your emotions and create a buffer space for yourself. Nobody can achieve perfection in everything. Your plans may also encounter various difficulties. If you focus all your time on work, not only will it be more harm than good but it will also increase the pressure on your mind and spirit. At this time, you need to create a "buffer space" for yourself. This doesn't necessarily mean having a room or a specific place but rather allowing yourself to stop and relax or contemplate the situation. It is a relatively abstract concept, but if we need to give a specific example, it could be having a cup of coffee, doing something unrelated to the current task, or discussing thoughts and exchanging ideas with people around you. Organizing your work environment in a comfortable and cozy way is even better. Additionally, use the PDCA planning schedule and manage your time scientifically. What is the PDCA principle? P - Plan: including the determination of the policy and objectives, as well as the formulation of activity plans. D - Do: design specific methods, plans, and layouts based on known information; then, carry out specific operations to achieve the content of the plan. C - Check: summarize the results of the implementation plan, distinguish what worked and what didn't, clarify the effect, and identify problems. A - Action: handle the results of the review, affirm the successes and standardize them; summarize the lessons from failures and give them due attention. Unresolved issues should be addressed in the next PDCA cycle. Generally, for each task, we first plan (P), then implement (D), during which we check (C) whether the execution has achieved the expected results. We analyze the influencing factors and the reasons for problems and propose solutions. Then, we improve, implement, and enhance (A) based on the review results. Learn to share with others and don't shoulder everything alone. When you encounter difficulties or have any unresolved problems, try talking to the person closest to you and try different perspectives. If possible, discuss future plans or tasks with your immediate supervisor or subordinates. They may have valuable insights and suggestions. Finally, I still believe that you should find time to relax your nerves. Engage in activities that can completely relax and calm yourself. Here, I suggest you learn about tea or flower art, which can help you experience and discover a different side of yourself in this quiet environment. It will be helpful for both your life and work.

Hello there! Everyone has their own life path, and we don't have to chase after others. Some people run faster, some run slower. We just need to follow our own pace, persevere, and never forget our original intention. We can still live a brilliant life! So, please don't limit yourself. Grandma Moses once said, "Some people always say it's too late. Actually, now is the best time. For someone who truly pursues something, every stage of life is young and timely." In terms of daily matters, ask yourself more: "Do I have to complete this immediately? If so, why?" "Can I take a break?" "What would happen if I completed it later?" "Do I have more important things to do?" Actually, when you stop and think, most things don't need to be completed immediately. Some people say that they are very busy with work and have no time to relax, but I don't believe it! To exaggerate a bit, if they were hit by a car, would they still insist on not going to the hospital because they have to work? You see, what we do and how much time we spend on it are all choices. We have control over them. A friend once said, "Many things that others consider a waste of time are actually what I enjoy, such as daydreaming, looking out the window, typing a sentence and then slowly deleting it, or walking aimlessly. We care a lot about whether something has meaning, but in reality, many things are meaningless. Do you know that finding the meaning of something is not the most important thing? Finding happiness is." Best wishes!

Growth is finding a breakthrough point, changing track, spiraling upward, and becoming a better version of oneself. Personal journey: The author is devoted to pursuing the results in life and is willing to make efforts to achieve what they want. In the pursuit of results, the author strives for perfection and utilitarianism. If the expected results are not achieved, they become anxious, stressed, and frustrated. When facing changes in the process, the author's coordination skills in overcoming difficulties are relatively poor and they tend to get caught up on a certain point. The author sought advice and realized that they were anxious to complete their tasks, and the more anxious they became, the greater the discrepancy with the desired results, which led them to avoid facing the initial expectations. Now the author is conflicted and has overloaded their life journey, seeking perfection. Social circle: The author has many pursuits in life and has high self-expectations. They can be motivated by engaging in tasks, but due to the inability to overcome obstacles, the discrepancy between their expectations and the actual results is significant, which leads the author to be constantly dissatisfied with their current situation. They start to add more activities to their life and avoid facing their imperfect self. This constant cycle of discrepancy and adding more activities causes the author to feel anxious and conflicted. Changing track: Letting go, no one is perfect, and it is impossible for one person to excel in everything. Just completing a few important and key tasks is enough to make oneself proud throughout life. The author has overloaded their schedule and constantly pursued perfection in every aspect, which has become a burden on themselves. The author needs to learn to let go and focus on a few or even one thing. They should let go of things that they do not truly want to do or are not good at, and focus on a few tasks for a period of time, make a determined effort to do well in the remaining foundational tasks. Energy is limited, and it is not easy to excel in one thing that one is proud of. Focus on the process - when doing things, it is important to have optimistic imagination, pessimistic planning, and joyful execution. The author focuses more on the results when doing things and needs to redirect their attention to the process itself. The author tends to get caught up in a specific point during the process due to anxiety in planning and execution. It is important for the author to have pessimistic planning, considering various unexpected situations, and then creating contingency plans, and finally executing the plans with joy. The author needs to put more effort into pessimistic planning to anticipate all kinds of unfavorable situations, so as not to get stuck when faced with problems or have no solution. The author needs to learn to focus on the perfect execution of the process. The process is the staircase that leads to the desired results, and it requires us to climb step by step to reach the end. In the process, let go of the obsession with perfect results. A perfect plan requires strict execution. The author should not worry about the results during the process and focus too much on achieving the results quickly, ignoring the perfect execution of the plan. Just focus on being excellent, and trust that the universe has its own arrangement. Without a perfect process, there will be no perfect results. Let go, focus on the process, let go of the results, change track, spiral growth, and become a better version of oneself.

Hey, I want to give you a hug, OP. I've also struggled with this issue, although now I face these anxieties less frequently. So, I want to share my story with you. I used to be obsessed with certain irrational expectations, like having everything happen exactly as I imagined. Otherwise, I would get extremely anxious and think I was terrible for not being able to handle even the smallest things. I also wanted to do everything perfectly and was afraid of missing out on anything. Just like what you mentioned about feeling anxious and unable to shift focus if you didn't complete a task, I also often assigned myself tasks beyond my capabilities... It's really exhausting to live like that! Constantly being caught in endless internal struggles makes me feel tired and question life. I think you must feel exhausted now too. Hugs to you. So, what can we do? In my experience, an imperfect life is the norm, and only you know whether you're living well or not. I hope my approach can inspire and help you. First, I started self-awareness. Whenever I come out of an emotional state, I look back at the whole process: what happened to make me anxious? What will happen next when the anxiety starts? What expectations and thoughts arose during this process? Which ones are real and which ones are imagined? Which ones can I change and which ones do I have to accept? Self-awareness is crucial, especially in distinguishing between reality and imagination, changeable and unchangeable. This is the first step to walk out of it. Then, I ask myself: the situation I'm facing right now is like this, it didn't happen as I expected, and I feel irritated, thinking I'm terrible. What can I do to make myself feel a little better? Acceptance is the beginning of change. This step is actually very difficult, so it's normal not to be able to accept your imperfections and anxiety in the beginning. Pay more attention to your thoughts, find the irrational aspects, and acceptance will naturally happen gradually. If you're not in a tight financial situation and your emotional state is really bothering you, I suggest finding a reliable teacher who can accompany you in your growth. Lastly, I'll share a healing phrase: you won't miss out on anything you're meant to experience! Best wishes to you! Mwah.

Hello OP: Hugs to you. From your words, I see two sources of confusion: one is an eagerness for your own life, and the other is a desire to make your life more complete and have a perfect life. These two feelings make you feel anxious. OP, I understand your feelings because I used to be just like you, anxious. Don't worry, let's take a look together. First, why do you have these feelings? 1. Pressure from comparing yourself to others In today's society, there is great competition and pressure. The expectations of parents, the success of friends, peers, and even younger generations surpassing you naturally create a fear of falling behind. Seeing the progress of those around us, we feel panic and anxiety because we haven't achieved the same success at the same time. 2. Life is short, and we want to make our lives more perfect. In fact, life and death are the destiny of life. Each of us cannot change death, and we cannot even know when accidents will happen. Because life is short, we want to try different things, pursue different successes, and fill our time with fullness, giving our all in everything to enrich the quality of our lives. However, everyone's energy and abilities are limited, so when we feel inadequate, we tend to blame ourselves and feel anxious. So, how can we change these two states? I hope the following words can help you, OP. 1. Everyone's life is different, and each person has their own rhythm of life. Some people graduate at 21 and find a job at 27; some people graduate at 25 and immediately find a job; some people never go to college but find something they love at 18; some people find a good job and make a lot of money but are not happy; some people take a gap year to find themselves; some people know what they want at 16 but change their minds at 26; some people have children and are still single; some people get married but wait 10 years to have children; some people are in a relationship but love someone else; some people love each other but can't be together. In fact, OP, life is like a marathon, and everyone has their own life plan. The timing of each person's harvest and maturity is different. As long as you have your own life plan, don't feel anxious about the time that hasn't come yet. Every event in our lives should be a result of our own decisions and timing, and should not be swayed by the wishes of others. Those who have achieved success have actually found their own rhythm. 2. Don't let others disrupt your rhythm in the marathon. J.K. Rowling was rejected 12 times before her globally successful "Harry Potter" series was published. If many people had said she didn't have writing talent and should do something else after being rejected, what if she had chosen to give up? Life is never smooth, even if the road is paved for you, there will inevitably be small stones that trip you up. But please be patient, life has infinite possibilities, don't settle, and don't give up lightly. In this long marathon called life, follow your own heart and don't let anyone disrupt your breathing rhythm. 3. Being well-rounded is not perfection. Finding something you care about is another form of perfection. OP, you mentioned that you really want to live a perfect life, so you have made a lot of plans for yourself. You asked, is it necessary? Actually, OP, you have already realized that pursuing perfection in everything is exhausting. We should strive to make our lives rich and colorful, but it doesn't mean that our lives have to be perfect. Because imperfection is the true color of life. Life is short, and none of us has the ability to do everything. We can't engage in several professions we like at the same time, and we can't be experts in many things simultaneously. The objectivity of time determines that we cannot be well-rounded, and we cannot attain everything we want. So, the perfection of being well-rounded actually does not exist. OP, what you should pursue is not the perfection of being well-rounded, but finding something you truly love and putting in your effort for it. In fact, it is precisely because we cannot pursue perfection in everything that we can see and understand what matters most to us on our journey through life. When we give our all in something we truly love, it is also a form of perfect life. Do our best and listen to destiny. After I have done everything I can, even if I don't ultimately achieve what I pursued, I will have no regrets. Because the effort I put in during the pursuit is also another interpretation of perfection. Finally, I want to tell you, OP, that the most touching drama in life is often not about who has the most perfect life, but about those who sincerely perform their own lives. Best wishes.

Hello: I deeply sense your pain, which is a state of [obsessive thinking + perfectionism personality]. You are constantly entangled, or on the way to being entangled, in a panic about things that haven't happened yet, anxious to [finish first]. But it seems like you have discovered something, which is "Is it necessary?" The choice is actually yours, we can analyze, maybe you will find that it is not necessary to analyze and understand the problem: 1) You are particularly anxious about your own life, always afraid of missing out on something, and working hard to get what you want. (We all have the mindset of winning or losing in life, which is a very normal state. However, perhaps there is a reason why people are arranged to live for 70 or 80 years. Enjoying comfort may be more meaningful than simply going through the motions. At least what remains is beautiful, while what is missed is unnecessary.) 2) One result of this is that you particularly want to finish a task, and if you don't finish it, you will be very anxious, anxious to the point where you can't do anything else, and you feel that your coordination skills are very poor, unable to shift attention from one point to another. (It is not wrong to want to do well and finish a task. However, what we need to evaluate is what you mentioned as "is it necessary?" If it is not necessary, why not spend limited time on something that is more necessary instead of wasting time on unnecessary things just to finish them? That would be "not worth it". Having a slightly poor coordination skills is not scary at all. This ability can be learned. We can discuss it further if there is an opportunity.) 3) You sought counseling and found that you are anxious to complete your tasks, and then you don't have to face them anymore. But actually, the more you want to complete them, are you just avoiding them? (Completing tasks is fine, but why the "anxiety"? Right? Completing tasks is a very good quality, but "anxiety" is a bad state. You can connect them together: "anxiously completing tasks, what is the purpose? What is the necessity?" I think you are a very smart person and you will understand.) 4) You are conflicted. Suddenly, you feel that you want to live your whole life and live it perfectly, with many arrangements for yourself. Is it necessary? You hope someone can help clarify your thoughts and help you adjust. (Yes, it is a contradictory mindset, but it's okay. We can slowly unravel it. If you live your whole life, living perfectly and experiencing a lot, can you digest it all at once? To deal with decades of matters in an instant, what will you do in the future? How can you surpass the sense of accomplishment in the future? Won't it be uncomfortable to have no goals or direction for decades? Of course, if you want to, you can.) Confronting the problem: "Are you really in a hurry to finish many things in life?"~~ It's okay to be "anxious", but what is the "purpose" of being anxious? This, we can discuss it in more depth if there is an opportunity. I understand that your anxiety is not intentional, but we can think: our own lives are meant to be in our own hands, whether we are anxious or not, no one will compete with us for credit, so what is the "meaning" of being anxious?~~ Does life really have to complete many things ahead of time? You can choose to do it in advance, but there will be some "side effects". For example, "haste makes waste". Clearly, with decades of things, if you finish them all at once, it's easy to have indigestion! Anything requires a process, and at your speed of thinking, there is no process, otherwise it cannot be completed. But here's the problem, things without a process cannot be considered "completed"! On the other hand, even if everything is achieved, what will you do in the future? Suddenly enjoying the satisfaction of completing everything, the inner self will suddenly feel empty. Because what will you do for the next few decades? There are too many things to discuss here, such as the concept of "imperfect perfection" and endless desires, so I won't discuss them one by one here. I hope we can have a chance for in-depth communication. Closing remarks: I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you can enjoy life/the present moment! If you have any specific confusion, feel free to send me a private message!

Hello, based on your description, I think you should first think about what your definition of life is. The human brain has unlimited freedom to define life and life goals. You can define it however you want, but there are some definitions that can make a person living on Earth feel very painful because they violate some fundamental objective laws and social principles. Let me give you an analogy: if you are a farmer growing crops, and you define your life as harvesting as much food as possible as quickly as possible, believing that having the most food is happiness and success, then you might always feel in pain. This is because growing crops requires tasks such as sowing, tending, and fertilizing, and it follows the growth patterns of the seasons. If you only define success by the final harvest of food, then you won't have any harvest for almost the whole year, and you will consider it unsuccessful and painful. Even if you receive some food at the end of the year, you may not have the most, so you still feel unhappy. I think you should consider the simple and eternal truth: your life is made up of every minute and second of your existence. If you extract the value from every moment, then you will have a life full of value. It's best not to constantly define life with the word "success" because society has overused that term. Especially those contents labeled as "success studies" are actually brainwashing techniques prepared for those who are eager for quick success, unwilling to make efforts, and only want money.

"This is your "time perception." Firstly, if you feel regret about the past, seeing your question reminds me of one aspect of time perception, which is having a negative attitude towards the past and feeling regret for not doing anything. So now you constantly try to make up for the past, but in reality, you are still living in the past and the present. This is why you fear that there will be regrets in life and want to finish your life quickly. Secondly, bid farewell to the past. If you want to solve this problem, you need to wave goodbye to the past and bid farewell to things that make you feel regret. When you are ready, we can enter into a meditation exercise: allow yourself to go back to that regretful event in the past, release yourself to feel the situation at that time, allow yourself to feel sad, allow yourself to feel pity. Then, when you have enough courage, bid farewell to that event. Tell yourself that it has become the past and that you are willing to let go. Thirdly, allow life to have regrets because we are human, we have limitations, and our limitations lead to regrets. Accept that you are imperfect, accept that life has regrets. Lastly, live in the present and do your best. Firstly, there are things in the past that make you regretful, but at the same time, there are also memories that make you extremely happy and worth cherishing, right? Secondly, choose something that suits your talents and needs to learn. Our energy and time are limited, we can't be good at everything. We can only choose what suits us best and what we need the most. Applying what we have learned is more important than being versatile, and it is most important to use our talents. Finally, turn regrets into positive growth and don't fear the future. With experience comes wisdom, and people definitely become more mature as they age. So, rest assured about the future. But no matter what you ultimately choose to do, feeling regret about the past is your perception of time, and through this, you will come to understand yourself better. Wishing you the best, Namaste!"

question: "My mother is in the late stage of cancer, and I have discovered that my father may be having an affair. How can I adjust my emotions?"
description: My mother has had cancer for two years now, and her condition has been deteriorating in recent months. I feel emotionally suppressed every day because of this. Recently, I also discovered that my father is involved with another woman, which has caused me a great deal of pain. How can I adjust myself and avoid falling into this misery?
keywords: Family, family relationships, family member's health.

answers.answer_text: OP, I can tell that you are a sensible child who cares about the whole family. It must have been tough and exhausting for you to deal with your mother's illness and your father's infidelity. At the same time, we cannot control or influence the situations coming from both your mother and father. It feels so powerless and helpless. If possible, I would like to give you a hug right now. When we feel helpless and passive in our environment, we tend to fall into negative emotions. The pain, the unfairness, the anger, and so on, they all arise, making it difficult for us to shake them off, right? However, OP, do you know that humans are also resilient? Even if the surroundings cannot be changed, even if external pressure won't disappear, we can still change the way we perceive things and control our inner selves. For example, in Nazi concentration camps, the physical and mental torment cannot be avoided, but a person's inner faith will not waver because of it. The heart of a person is the freest place. So, how do we make our hearts feel more free? We can try to divert some attention from our parents' difficulties to ourselves, to tend to our own hearts. I believe a sensible child like you must be constantly thinking about how to make your mother happier, how to improve the situation, and how to make your father pay more attention to the family, while neglecting our own needs. Now, let's ask our own hearts what we want to do. Do we want to go out and play with friends? Or do we want to have a nice meal? Or do we want to confide in someone? Then, let's fulfill those desires, just as you show tender care for your mother. Sometimes, we may think, "Mother is in so much pain, how can I seek happiness for myself alone? What right do I have?" If that's the case, then what's the difference between me and my father? But actually, dear OP, you have the right to make yourself happy. Making yourself happy is like recharging yourself, and only a charged battery can bring vitality to the whole family. If our batteries are below 10%, it's impossible to energize the whole family. So, OP, please take care of yourself and do things that fulfill your inner expectations. Once we have fulfilled ourselves, we will have the energy to take care of other family members. Additionally, if it's difficult to find support at home, we can seek companionship and support through communication with close friends and relatives. In the presence of trustworthy friends, try to tell them about your needs and let your vulnerable side be seen. This alone can make us feel better. Lastly, I want to share with you that each of us is weaving our own stories in this lifetime, and these experiences are the materials for our stories. Even if the materials are the same, different people can weave different stories based on how they utilize them. Whether you believe it or not, there are definitely people who have similar experiences to ours and have woven great stories using those materials. And you, too, can be one of them.

Hello, I am currently experiencing the awkward situation of my mother being seriously ill and my father possibly having an affair. I hope that my words can help you, the poster, in the future! "Spending quality time with your mother in her limited life" In this world, many people feel regret and guilt when their loved ones pass away, realizing that they didn't spend enough time with their family. It is difficult to overcome the grief of losing a family member. Huang Lei once said, "No matter how much time I spend with my parents, it's never enough!" Take the opportunity to spend more time with her, even if you can't do anything about her illness. As long as you are there, accompanying her, she won't be alone. This way, you will have fewer regrets in the future! "How to deal with your father's issue" Talk to your father, tell him that this family needs him, and both you and your mother need him. Emphasize the emotional and logical aspects and reason with him to come back to the family! "Do what you can do" Whether it's your mother's illness or your father's feelings, you can't decide for them. Your words can only serve as reference and assistance. So, do your best, take care of yourself, and that's enough. As for the outcome, learn to accept it calmly. You have already done well, learn to affirm yourself, seek help from friends and relatives, and timely release negative emotions. Regardless of the situation, I hope you can live a sunny and hopeful life! Best wishes.

Hello there~ I understand your feelings very well, sending you a hug~ In the journey of life, we do encounter many helpless situations. I'm glad to see that you realize the importance of adjusting your mindset and facing them more positively. Many things are beyond our control, and all we can do is accept the reality calmly and do our best within our abilities. Sometimes, we may experience pain, but we must stay strong and believe that there will be a rainbow after the storm. 1. Your mom has cancer, and her condition has worsened. Hugs to you, understanding and caring. You must be very concerned about your mom. However, don't put too much pressure on yourself. Believe that your mom wants you to be good and happy every day. Can you entrust this issue to the doctors and the higher power? Have faith that the medical treatment will definitely be effective and silently wish and pray for your mom in your heart. One day, we will all say goodbye to our loved ones, so spend more time with them every day to let them feel warmth and love. 2. Your dad is involved with another woman outside the marriage. Try to understand his difficulties, I believe he has also made many sacrifices for the family. Do you communicate with your dad regularly? Try to have a conversation, it may improve the situation. Understand his thoughts and share your feelings. It would be best if he can understand you. 3. Share your feelings appropriately and seek help. You must have good friends whom you can rely on, talk to them, don't keep everything bottled up inside. If you don't have someone suitable to confide in, you can consider seeking counseling, there are many people who can listen and offer support. Additionally, writing a journal is also a good option, write down your feelings and remind yourself to view the problems correctly and positively. In short, none of these things are your fault, don't blame yourself, just do your best in dealing with them. Take care~.

This situation is indeed very bad, and Dad's behavior is indeed hard to accept. I understand your feelings of loneliness, helplessness, and disappointment... How can you regulate your emotions in this situation? I suggest you return to the role of a daughter. Many of these emotions are not generated when you are in the role of a daughter. You haven't stood in the daughter's position, and you have taken on too much for your parents. Of course, this is also due to Mom's illness and Dad's escape, and they haven't been in their parental roles.

Mom and you have both had a hard time. Hugs to you! Keep going! At this time, only you can stand by your mom and support her, so you really should adjust yourself. Try not to let her know about your father's affairs, as this kind of thing is very devastating. It is very difficult to still consider your father as a family member and not let his actions affect you or cause pain. There is research that says, "Men are creatures driven by their lower instincts," meaning that most men would choose instinct over emotions. Once, a woman who cared for her husband, who was in a vegetative state, in the neurosurgery department said that the only ones who wouldn't give up on a patient are parents for their children and wives for their husbands, but it rarely happens the other way around. Your father's actions during your mom's most painful and desperate moments undoubtedly show a lack of consideration for his marital bond. So, don't have too much hope for his humanity. The bigger the hope, the bigger the disappointment. Right now, you can only detach your feelings from him, not dwell on his actions, not pay attention to anything related to him, and especially, don't hate him (you can tell him that you hate his heartlessness and scold him, but don't hold it in your heart, because he hasn't held you all in his heart). When he is just a passerby in your life, you can truly let go. Treat him as the "most familiar stranger," learn to separate "emotion" from behavior, and your pain will be much less.

Take good care of your mother. Be filial to your mother. Be considerate and sympathetic towards your father. Our bodies and skin are given to us by our parents, and it is not easy for anyone to be born. Perhaps you have a lot of worries and confusion in your heart. You may feel resentful towards your parents. You may wonder how to overcome the difficulties in your own life. But why not ask yourself what you truly desire? Do you really want to continue being trapped in such emotions? If you don't genuinely want to, then caring for your parents and understanding their hearts is what you truly need to focus on. If you have made up your mind to take good care of your mother, with a strong desire in your heart, even if the outcome is not as desired, it is still better than constantly blaming yourself. Cherish the people in front of you, especially those who you really want to take care of. They are the most important to you! (In my opinion). Keep going! Fight on!

question: Why can't I cry and why do I laugh when I cry? I feel like I'm not in a good mental state.
description: Recently, I've been feeling inexplicably uncomfortable. I have this urge to cry, but every time I feel tears coming, they disappear, making me feel even more suppressed. When I laugh, it's like I can't control myself. I keep laughing, but then it turns into crying. I feel that my mental state is not good, but I don't know why.
keywords: Emotions, depressed emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it seems like you often feel uncertain about your emotions and get randomly affected by them, right? In reality, everyone experiences emotional distress. Some people get controlled by their emotions and become immersed in them, while others can use their emotions to observe their inner state and turn them into a catalyst for personal growth. The choice of how to deal with emotions ultimately determines one's quality of life. You have the power to decide how to approach your emotions. If you want to surpass their control and have free will, it all starts with acceptance. Accepting emotions is a state of energy that can only be transformed, not eliminated. Based on your reaction, it seems that your past approach to dealing with emotions has been suppressing and resisting them. This accumulation eventually reaches a point where you feel powerless to control it, and it becomes the main theme influencing your behavior, making you willing to face it. Allow your emotions to arise and release the accumulated energy. You mentioned feeling numb and unable to cry, which is like a blocked water pipe, naturally creating a sense of suppression and discomfort. In this situation, you can watch movies that stir your emotions and let your tears flow along with the storyline. Suppressing tears is poison, while letting them flow is like finding pearls. Allow yourself to release and find ways to express your emotions, whether it's shouting, crying, or making a scene. When I am in great pain, I go hiking and find a big tree where I can vent all my grievances, sadness, worries, and anxieties. It's a great way to clear your mind. I also write extensively to release my emotions, and it has been very helpful to me. Regular exercise is also a good way to release the accumulated energy in your body through sweating. As you continue to clear out, your inner self will become clearer, allowing you to have a deeper sense of inner experience and a greater awareness of the underlying cognition behind your emotions. Only by identifying the hidden puppeteer behind the control, whether it's familial or other constraints, can you truly break free from the disturbances brought by your emotions. It is possible for everyone as long as they are willing. Best wishes.

Hello ~ The desire to cry is usually due to having a lot of negative emotions or experiencing something very unpleasant. However, not being able to cry may be because we are trying our best to suppress our negative emotions and not let them be expressed smoothly. Sometimes we have this feeling that crying represents vulnerability, so when we want to cry, we try to show our strong side as much as possible. Sometimes, we may also feel that there is nothing worth crying over. It is normal to cry while laughing. Normally, tear glands secrete a small amount of tears to lubricate and clean the eyes, and also have a weak antibacterial effect through blinking. Tear glands are regulated by the trigeminal nerve and the sympathetic nervous system, and when the sympathetic nervous system is stimulated, tear secretion increases. Therefore, when laughing, being emotionally excited, or excessively sad, the sympathetic nervous system is stimulated, leading to increased tear production. Thus, shedding tears while laughing is a normal physiological phenomenon. Ordinary people only cry when they are very excited. Best wishes ~.

Hello, when I saw your topic, I already felt heartache. This must be such a suffocating and depressing state! Seeing you mention feeling inexplicably uncomfortable, wanting to cry but unable to, feeling the oppression yourself. Feeling that you are in such pain that it tears your heart apart, feeling disappointed and numb. There is no greater sorrow than a dead heart. When a person is extremely sad and grieving, they actually can't cry and should be in a happy state, but you can't stop laughing, and while laughing, you start crying. This shows that this laughter is not genuinely happy laughter. My dear, when you are experiencing this state, what happened to you? What is making you feel so depressed and sad? People may isolate the reasonable emotions that should appear in themselves when they encounter certain stressful events, in order to protect their inner selves. Just like Swiss psychologist Verena Kast said: "A person is often emotionally depressed not because they are excessively sad, but precisely because they have rejected sadness." If you can cry, your emotions can find a way to release. But if you can't cry, you feel like you have lost yourself. Being in a state of lacking appropriate emotional reactions to oneself is even more disappointing. I think at this time, you need a warm embrace to take good care of you. I hope you can overcome the dark clouds soon. The world and I love you!

question: There are many things that are suffocating me, how can I make life meaningful?
description: I can't sleep well. I wake up in the middle of the night. I can't remember anything for the past six months. My grades are also declining. I feel like there's so much weighing me down that I can't breathe. I have no interest in anything. I don't want to socialize. I don't want to go out. Once I'm out, I don't want to go home. What's wrong with me?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, therapeutic methods, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Wisdom Non-empty interpretation: 1. First, give you a warm embrace. Excessive stress can deplete your energy. The longer it lasts, the more overwhelmed you may become. 2. This kind of pressure may come from the outside world, but it only affects you when you confirm it yourself. Are you pursuing perfection too much? Or do you have high demands and are overly critical of yourself? Or is the outside world demanding too much of you? 3. People are not omnipotent. It is impossible to do everything perfectly or be superior in every aspect, although such people do exist, they are rare. 4. Give yourself some leeway. Admitting that you cannot achieve perfection will make you feel much more relaxed. Go into battle lightly and feel more comfortable! 5. Accepting your current situation is the only way to change it in the future. There is no point in suppressing yourself and strangling your throat.

Hello! OP, let me share some of my thoughts in the hope that they will be helpful to you. If a person cannot find peace of mind, it indicates that there are issues that cannot be resolved from within, causing inner turmoil. For example, as a student, if your grades decline and your parents blame or discredit you, it can lead to low mood. When a student's studying doesn't yield satisfactory results and there is no support of love from their parents, it will inevitably affect their mood. So, how can one get rid of this kind of annoyance? To have hope in life, one must find their own inner motivation and act upon it. When both the mind and body are relaxed and stretched out, one naturally feels at ease, untroubled, and gets better sleep. What are some ways to increase inner motivation? 1. Focus on doing one thing. For example, if your grades are generally poor and you don't know what to do, it can be frustrating. In this case, start by finding one subject that you feel you can improve in and study it diligently. Believe that your efforts will definitely lead to better grades. Set small goals to boost your confidence. 2. If you're feeling troubled, exercise can help relieve stress and improve mood by stretching the body. So, go out and run with all your heart, until you reach your limit. After sweating it out, maybe your worries will dissipate too. 3. Find something you excel at apart from academics, believe in yourself, and appreciate your own accomplishments. Recognize that you're not without any positive attributes. In short, to resolve the troubles that burden the heart, one must learn to face, solve, and change. Do not retreat or avoid, otherwise, you will only continue to sink into contemplation. Be brave enough to step out of a bad state of mind. The only one who can save you is your own heart. Self-motivation is also a way to increase inner motivation. If there is not much external support, learn to cheer yourself on and explore the beautiful scenery on your own. Courage and perseverance are very important because the road of life will always have its ups and downs. Don't stop walking if you encounter a difficult path. Instead, learn to navigate through it calmly because there's no turning back, only looking forward. Keep moving forward steadfastly to reach the scenery you want to see. On the journey, learn to let go of burdens and pressures so that you can enter the battlefield lightly and walk more smoothly. Don't hesitate to let go of stress and emotions. Wishing you a speedy recovery and good luck. Believe that you can do it.

question: How to discover what my true mental problems are?
description: I have found that when I try to describe my problems, I tend to imagine what they are and then embellish them with words to make others believe and make myself believe. However, as someone who lacks psychological knowledge, it is easy for me to make mistakes and difficult to correct them. Even most of the time, my initial intuition is wrong.
keywords: Development, improved character, personality traits, self-growth.

answers.answer_text: Let go of your mind and follow the sensations of your body. Because the subconscious exists in our bodies, not in our minds, and it doesn't need the fabrications of the mind. Of course, the mind and body are interconnected, and when you wholeheartedly describe a problem, you may have already sincerely invited the problem. Over time, perhaps the problems will be validated one by one. I am curious about your confusion regarding "how to discover your true psychological problems". Descriptions of psychological problems always have subjective colors, but the emphasis is on details and feelings. Feelings reside more in the body, and our bodies never lie. Therefore, a counselor will pay more attention to how you say it, not just what you say. For example, if you frown and say you're happy, we may question your happiness. Of course, facing the truth requires courage, and some truths may lie in the realm of our subconscious that we haven't even realized yet. This is exactly the significance of counseling work. Follow the sensations of your body, under the guidance of a counselor, and through the awareness of the subconscious, help me see a different side of myself. Learning and growth, we are always on the journey. Hello. The world and I love you.

Hello, from your description, I see that you want to clarify how to determine your mental health status. This reminds me of how someone determines whether their face is clean. There are two methods: one is to observe oneself through a mirror, and the other is to ask others for help to observe and determine. Applying this idea to your question may be feasible. One is to use certain tools for self-assessment, and the other is to ask for assistance from others. These others can be trusted friends, professionals such as psychiatrists, mental health therapists, or counselors. I don't know if this answers your question. Take care of yourself.

question: When my mother scolds me, I am filled with pain and hatred. Is hating one's parents a pathological condition?
description: "I see that you're worthless. Teachers may praise you, but in my eyes, you're just a piece of shit. You'll always be a good-for-nothing. A worthless piece of trash that no one cares about, even if you die outside." These are all direct quotes from my mother, and there are even more offensive ones that I don't want to share. Anyway, she always thinks that I'm inferior to others, that I'm a worthless and insignificant girl who will never amount to anything. Maybe my mother doesn't realize how hurtful her words are, but they make me feel sad and want to cry. I try to talk about things I like, but she never listens for more than a few sentences. If I don't speak, she demands that I do, and I sometimes feel so tired and don't want to provoke her anger. But she doesn't understand why I feel the need to speak. Over time, whenever my mother scolds me, I feel anger and deep hatred in my heart. My life is completely planned by her. What is she so dissatisfied with? I even believe that I'm not as outstanding as others, but I will still work hard to achieve something. But later, I realized that all this effort was worthless. What's the point of getting 100 in physics? Even with an English score of 140, she would say, "Look at you, look at others. Others scored 143, why are you only at 140?" So, I no longer want to meet her expectations, which always result in physical abuse. Once I get into college and have lived for 20 years, I will just go and die. I, being this kind of person, don't deserve to exist."

answers.answer_text: Think about when your parents were born, what kind of education they received, and what kind of family environment they grew up in... I always feel that my parents are not qualified, or rather, they can't meet the standard. They didn't have the opportunity to have a good living environment like us, or an educational environment, or a clear understanding of right and wrong... So we can only understand their attitude, maybe it's really not good. But you must realize and feel that this is not good. You will definitely not treat your children this way~ This is the progress of generations~ Don't expect to change them, it's difficult. Instead of changing them, it's better to improve yourself, and right now, the important thing is to focus on learning. You will definitely have a better future~ So the judgments or criticisms from your parents may not necessarily be true. They are just expressing their emotions. For example, if you get a score of 140 in English and ask the teacher or classmates to evaluate, it must be considered a good score. Grades are meant to objectively and fairly reflect the results of your hard work. Don't doubt your efforts. Whether you are outstanding or not is not determined by a few words from your parents. Your future life starts from accumulating effort in the present. I think you are already doing well in your studies, and I hope you continue to work hard~

question: Unable to feel his sincerity, should a relationship without hope continue?
description: I have been with my partner for half a year, but I can't feel his true feelings towards me. Whenever I try to communicate with him, he never seems to understand my feelings. Whenever we face problems, he always asks me how to solve them. I'm really tired, but he doesn't want to break up yet. I don't know how to continue anymore. I always feel like our relationship has nothing to do with love.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! You've been in a relationship for half a year and you desire for your partner to understand you, empathize with your feelings, accept and tolerate you, and even know and fulfill your needs without you having to ask. But obviously, this person is unable to do that, and may even require your support, understanding, and decision-making. Therefore, you feel tired and hesitant about continuing the relationship, although you don't want to break up either. Is that right? Each of us seeks and establishes relationships because of love and needs. As they say, all relationships have needs. Your relationship is not over yet because both of you are getting some "benefits" from it. Breaking up is a decision made by one person, while staying together requires the agreement of both. You have the power to decide to break up on your own. But your hesitation and reluctance show that you are still finding satisfaction in the relationship. Maybe your partner can't fulfill your need for understanding, but they may fulfill other aspects, such as taking care of you in daily life or alleviating loneliness. You can explore and see if that's the case. No matter how close the relationship, it can't fulfill all your needs. They can fulfill some but not all. Sometimes they can fulfill, sometimes they can't. The key is whether your most important and valued needs are being met. Additionally, is this inability to fulfill due to your extremely high standards or because your emotional patterns don't match? If it's the former, and you require an intense, emotionally volatile relationship, you can try finding someone else, but the probability of encountering a scoundrel is very high. If it's the latter, then you can seek someone else who is a better match since long-term incompatibility can indeed be exhausting. Finally, when you decide to continue in this relationship, you need to learn to satisfy your own emotional needs. By understanding yourself more and taking care of your own feelings, you won't rely as much on your partner's understanding. Then, learn to express your needs correctly and teach your partner to fulfill them. Love can be created.
