The questioner is currently distressed because they really like this man and are afraid of losing him? Or is it because they just want to get attention and love from their boyfriend? If it is fear of losing a boyfriend, we can make some appropriate changes. The love you give may not be the love he wants, similarly, what you understand and express clearly may not be what he can receive! If it is about wanting attention and love, you can use a simple and clear "I statement" which is "I feel..., because..., I hope you...".

question: Why does studying give people such headaches? Where does the motivation for learning come from?
description: Why do games have such a strong allure and can be self-taught? Why does studying cause people so much headache, no matter how you explain it, they just won't listen and immediately go on and on about games?
keywords: Behavior, stress, avoidance, and mobile phone dependency

answers.answer_text: Learning itself is a process of breaking out of one's comfort zone, and this process is quite painful, not easy and enjoyable. Because learning requires more effort, constantly learning and mastering new knowledge and courses, this itself lacks entertainment, so people will feel a sense of hardship when learning. The original intention of games is for entertainment and leisure. It relaxes people's minds and reduces various pressures. Therefore, for most people, games are an "attraction," games = happiness, leisure, and relaxation. In fact, learning itself does not cause headaches. If there is such a thought, it is because learning and pain are equated. Just thinking about learning will trigger a sense of pain. This feeling may come from the outside world, such as continuous lecturing and scolding from parents, combined with the fact that learning itself is not an easy task. However, there are also some people who really enjoy learning, enjoy reading, and enjoy researching. Even if no one urges them to learn, they have an inner motivation to learn. We need to know that everyone is different, and there are differences in interests and hobbies between individuals. If you want your child to have the motivation to learn, you must first consider how to prevent the child from losing motivation and confidence, and not let the child have a negative feeling about learning. Like what you described, if they don't listen even when you speak, it only means that our previous methods were ineffective, and we need to adopt another approach to deal with children's learning. Try to understand the reasons behind the child's behavior.

Hello, based on your question, I would like to provide you with the following analysis and advice in the hopes of helping you! Your love for gaming and being self-taught stem from your interests. You have a great interest in gaming, so naturally, you are willing to spend time and energy studying it, mastering various gaming skills, and understanding game content. You find studying boring and lack motivation because studying requires a significant amount of time and effort, and coincidentally, you have no interest in studying, so you are unwilling to invest time and energy, resulting in an inability to concentrate and headaches. Every one of us finds things that we are not interested in to be boring and uninteresting. You need to find a balance between gaming and studying. This doesn't mean abandoning gaming but rather prioritizing and allocating time reasonably. Treat gaming as a form of relaxation and entertainment while ensuring that it doesn't affect your studies. Try to find enjoyment in learning, discover learning methods that suit you, and give yourself appropriate rewards to provide motivation and encourage yourself to study (you can use a planner or journal to organize and record your life and studies). By excelling at studying, you can also excel at gaming. Think more and read more. Have a clear understanding of your thoughts and how to act upon them. Set long-term goals and short-term objectives. Use goals to motivate yourself and gradually become a better version of yourself. We all have a tendency to be lazy, and compared to challenging tasks, we naturally prefer easy ones. I hope that you can make studying as interesting and easy as gaming, and become a more diligent and self-disciplined person. Your personal mental health advisor who is here for you. May my words bring you warmth! I would also like to thank occasional passersby for reading this, and feel free to follow me and mark it as "helpful"!

question: What to do when experiencing emotional outbursts due to stress or encountering individuals who violate social norms?
description: I am someone who dislikes trouble in life and often tries to avoid it. However, when others (not just one or two people) insist that I do something I don't want to do, I can't avoid it and become very assertive. My emotions can suddenly explode. In my neighborhood, people often take others' parking spaces. Once, someone used someone else's parking space for a funeral in the neighborhood, which is not allowed according to the rules and it affected my life. But no one said anything to them, and I became angry, just like the situation I described above, and did something irrational. It's also a parking space issue when someone occupies my family's parking space, but they act like it's not what they did, and I get furious. When I become angry, I feel like I am a different person from my usual self. The reason for my anger is not understood by those around me. According to people around me, I should change this, but I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Hello, are you okay? Whether you need to make adjustments and changes is up to you to decide. Other people's opinions can only be taken as reference. In simple terms, if you feel uncomfortable, then make a change. If you don't feel uncomfortable, then there's no need to change. Firstly, it is normal. Anyone would feel unhappy when they feel offended, but the intensity may vary. Anger often stems from fear. "I am someone who doesn't like trouble in my life and often tries to avoid it." Many people with social anxiety disorder have similar expressions. It's not really about being afraid of bothering others, but rather being afraid of having their requests rejected. Once rejected, they feel a strong sense of insecurity and then use anger as a way to "arm" themselves, to hide their inner fear and "confront" the imagined "danger". Typically, people with this personality type are sensitive, kind-hearted, and fragile. "When I get angry, I feel like it's a different person compared to my usual self. Nobody around me understands the reason for my anger." Yes, occasionally loss of control may occur during anger. We can interpret this situation as a form of PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder). In fact, this situation is indeed caused by strong stimuli and has not received appropriate psychological counseling in a timely manner. Generally, other people may find it difficult to understand. Many times, they may think: "It's just a small matter, it's not a big deal, why get so angry?" and so on. Another possibility, according to psychoanalysis, is that libidinal energy is fixated on the "anal stage", which needs to be traced back to issues in the original family. Different schools of thought have different treatment methods, and if the current situation is causing you considerable distress, you can try seeking psychological counseling to resolve it. Wishing you a happy life!

In the expression of anger, it does not mean that you are argumentative, but you may also be someone who knows how to protect yourself and know when to advance and retreat. There is no problem with that. We need to constantly examine ourselves and not immediately act on our emotions. Think about what you would say. ①Sometimes when we are angry and irritable, we need to distance ourselves from the conversation. ②If others are not reasonable, then please make yourself a more tolerant person. Sometimes we also need to detach ourselves from the conversation. ③Think about why you are sensitive to that kind of behavior of ignoring certain people. ④Try to see what you can learn from these things. These people who violate social rules ultimately need to take responsibility for them, so as to handle things well and stabilize your inner world. Good luck!

Hello, first of all, thank you for the invitation to answer. The situation you described makes me feel that there is a lot of anger about to explode within you. Perhaps the things that make you angry are just the tipping point, and the anger within you may have been pent up for a long time, stemming from past experiences or build-up over time. It is not the primary task to simply get rid of these anger-inducing events, as it is not easy to change them and it does not fundamentally solve the problem. The priority is to remind yourself to look at the source and root causes of these anger issues, which is actually a good opportunity for self-exploration.

question: Do not trust people after being attacked, keep a distance from those who smile at me.
description: I have a colleague who used to be quite cheerful and always smiling. However, due to work-related reasons, she attacked me once. Now whenever I see someone who looks friendly and smiles at me, I feel scared and even think that they might attack me or have ulterior motives. But in reality, they are genuinely friendly. It's just that because of being attacked before, I actually prefer to interact with people who always reject me and keep my distance from those who smile at me. This has resulted in me having no friends and it bothers me.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, and social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello~ Everyone has their own vision of the world, which is the way they believe the real world looks like. It also serves as a basis for their actions and interactions with others in this world. However, when unpleasant things happen, these visions may be shattered, inevitably threatening their sense of security. In this process, psychological trauma may occur, and one manifestation is not being able to trust people who seem friendly, as you mentioned. The first and most important step is to acknowledge your feelings, emotions, and concerns, instead of denying, avoiding, or ignoring them. By recognizing these emotions, you can search for or understand the things that cause you pain, sadness, or sorrow. This allows you to proactively address these things and strive to prevent their reoccurrence in future relationships. It is necessary to address and rebuild trust in new relationships, not just perceive it as emotional distress. Specifically, find friends who are friendly and trustworthy (you probably already have many such friends) and change your mindset while interacting with them to rebuild the trust in the world and others. More importantly, rebuild trust in yourself. The best outcome is that you will no longer associate friendliness with being harmed by someone, and your distress will no longer exist. Best wishes~.

Many times, when someone attacks, it is not to hurt you, but rather to protect themselves. The more aggressive a person is, the more fragile they actually are and easily break down. You don't need to bear the burden of their fragility; you just need to step back and see how fragile they are, how they are trying to protect themselves. If you are willing to help them, you can ask them, "I understand how you feel right now. What can I do for you?" Nothing is absolute or guaranteed, just like an earthquake today doesn't mean there will be earthquakes every day in the future, and encountering an attacking person today doesn't mean everyone you meet in the future will be attacking. See others, see yourself, see emotions.

"Eat a loss, gain wisdom. With more exposure to genuine and fake laughter, one can learn to differentiate between them. Avoiding situations entirely will not improve one's discernment ability and may result in missing out on sincere friendships. If you are unsure whether someone's behavior is genuine, try using a tit-for-tat strategy. Start by unconditionally trusting others, but if you get deceived, make sure to retaliate heavily (ensuring the other person suffers at least the same amount or more losses). If the other person initiates reconciliation, then give them another chance. In the long run, this will help create a low-cost trust environment around you, which is both reasonable and more likely to attract sincere individuals to your side."

question: How can I improve my energy and live a vibrant life when I frequently experience emotional fluctuations over minor things?
description: Often, there is a significant emotional fluctuation over small matters. After encountering something minor, I may get stuck in it for several days or even longer. Whenever I think about that thing later on, my mood becomes even more unpleasant. Is there any way to "remove" those negative emotions?
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, the condition where emotions fluctuate greatly over small matters and then linger for several days, or even longer, is known as being stuck in those emotions. The more one thinks about these matters, the more their mood worsens. They want to "detach" themselves from these emotions. First, let's understand what emotions are. Emotions are a collective term for a series of subjective cognitive experiences. They are a psychological activity mediated by individual desires and needs. They encompass an individual's attitude and experiences towards objective things, as well as corresponding behavioral reactions. In other words, emotions do not come out of nowhere. They are accompanied by an individual's desires, needs, attitudes, experiences, and behavioral reactions towards objective things. For example, if someone forgets their keys when leaving for work in the morning, they become very annoyed when they think about it. Why are they annoyed? Because they have a need: "They want to go straight home after work, and forgetting their keys means they won't be able to enter their house when they finish work. They will need to bother the locksmith company, which is very inconvenient for them." However, if the person who forgets their keys in the morning lives with family members and there is always someone at home, will this matter of forgetting the keys still cause them to feel "annoyed"? Most likely not. Since there was no mention of specific small matters in the description, it is not possible to analyze and provide help. But you can think about what desires or wishes you have when these small matters provoke emotional fluctuations in you. Furthermore, the fluctuation of emotions allows us to see our own needs. When those needs are fulfilled, the emotions naturally disappear. However, in the description, you mentioned that emotional fluctuations make you stuck and unable to come out of them. Perhaps it is not the emotions that prevent you from coming out, but rather you are not willing to let yourself come out. Let's take the above-mentioned situation as an example: forgetting the keys when leaving for work in the morning. This matter originally caused the person to feel "annoyed" emotionally. However, instead of recognizing the reason for their annoyance, which is not having the keys to enter home, they end up thinking, "I should have brought the keys. Forgetting the keys is because of my terrible memory. I blame myself for always being forgetful!" This kind of thinking is also called rumination, which refers to the repeated and passive thinking about negative events, one's negative emotional state, and the potential causes and consequences of them. When they think about this matter, they start to blame and criticize themselves, falling into automatic thinking, and strengthening their negative emotions towards the negative event. So how can one escape from rumination and detach themselves from negative emotions? The answer lies in recognizing one's own needs, satisfying those needs, and finding positive meaning from negative events. For the person who forgets their keys, their need is to have a key to enter their home. So, what can they learn from forgetting the keys? They need a reminder to bring their keys or switch to a lock that doesn't require keys. Once the situation is resolved, will this matter still be a source of their troubles? Best regards, Karen.

Hello, good afternoon! I sense the emotional fluctuations deep within you, which may be a result of the accumulation of negative emotions reaching a certain level or a generally low psychological state, preventing you from achieving a sense of internal and external balance through personal efforts. This state can be quite tormenting and distressing, creating a negative cycle. However, we must also recognize the positive starting point: you have realized the need to stop this current state promptly and gradually reverse or break free from this emotional loop through a positive cycle. From a psychoanalytic perspective, it may be necessary to trace the source of stress, that is, the initial factor, but this approach requires a relatively long-term commitment and cannot be explained in a few words. It necessitates mutual openness and honesty in a supportive environment. Aside from seeking psychological counseling, another option is to engage in activities such as support groups or discussions with close friends and family. By expressing your feelings, the accumulated negative emotions will be partially relieved. As the level of psychological stress decreases, self-regulation abilities, similar to immune response, will gradually adjust to a better state, allowing a formation of a positive cycle again. In terms of short-term cognitive therapy, such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), it provides targeted adjustments for anxiety or depressive emotions, resulting in a relatively quick decrease in stress. However, the downside is that an individual's thinking patterns cannot be fundamentally adjusted in the short term. Additionally, if other external factors, such as living or work environments, relationship patterns, etc., are not adjusted accordingly, there is a high possibility of reverting back to the previous state. It has a certain degree of rebound. In this regard, you can also learn from self-help books and courses. From the perspective of positive psychology, why not focus on your own strengths? By amplifying positive emotions and learning a sense of optimism, repeatedly reinforcing good habits that improve our mood and adjusting our mindset, we can refer to online psychological courses for specific techniques. In conclusion, I wish you well. Let's work together to heal the world!

Hello friend, I hope the following answer can be helpful to you. I used to be a person who easily gets emotional, but my way of expression is being irritable and then feeling better after venting. As I grew older, gained more experiences, and explored myself deeply, I can now say that I am the master of my own emotions. Let me share my methods with you: 1. "Accepting" your emotions: When emotions arise, give yourself a hug first. We need to first recognize that being "emotional" is not wrong, and having "negative emotions" is not wrong either. It is certain that something triggered the known or unknown traumas within us, resulting in corresponding emotions. At this time, negative emotions are like a wounded child, they need to be seen and comforted by us. Giving yourself a hug is like giving a candy to this child. Then, it will happily play on its own. 2. "Releasing" your emotions: From your description, it seems that you tend to suppress your emotions and chew on them silently. I think emotions need an outlet, let them flow, and they won't trap you anymore. For example, you can try confiding in a good friend when you're not in a good mood; or go to a karaoke to sing; or write them down. Often, emotional energy can also be a form of creativity. Many poets and writers' works are products of their emotions. So, try to let your emotions flow, give them an outlet, and you will gain relaxation! 3. "Redirecting" the focus of emotional energy: In fact, being emotional is another aspect of having good sensitivity. Being easily emotional indicates that you are sensitive to the people and things around you, and it is easy to generate corresponding emotions. A person's emotional energy is limited. If you focus the energy on things that easily bring about negative emotions, then the energy available for things that can generate positive emotions will be reduced accordingly. Therefore, why not try to "redirect" your emotional energy? Focus on things that can make you feel beauty, joy, happiness, and other positive emotions. Friend, I hope the above suggestions are helpful to you. Let's become happy masters of our emotions together!

Hello! I understand your concerns. When I was young, I used to feel this way often too. However, through learning and practice, I made significant changes. I would like to share my understanding with you, hoping it will inspire you. Awareness is the first step towards change. If we are unwilling to be troubled by minor emotional fluctuations and have the desire to develop in the direction we hope for, it will happen. The ABC theory of emotions was developed by American psychologist Ellis. A represents the triggering events, B represents the beliefs we form in response to these events, our interpretations and views about them. C represents the emotions and behaviors we generate as a result. You can try to recall what kind of events trigger your emotions and how you perceive them. Try looking at these events from different perspectives. For example, in the past, when a colleague showed a cold attitude towards me, I would feel unhappy and think maybe it was my fault. But now, I would think that perhaps they are busy or have other things going on in their life and did not consider their attitude towards me. This thought helps dissipate my unhappy emotions. I have also let go of the idea of constantly demanding how others should act. It is important to distinguish whose issue it is. If someone's behavior does bother me, even if they are really in the wrong, I reflect on what I can do myself. For example, if someone in the office does not pay attention to cleanliness and takes advantage of others, leading to others disliking them, I used to get angry when I told them about it, and they gave me all sorts of excuses. But I changed my thinking. We cannot change others, so I tried communicating and setting my own boundaries. I am no longer troubled by it. Furthermore, reading more books, learning, and improving oneself, loving and accepting oneself, and breaking through the limitations of our previous perceptions, trying to see things from a higher perspective, will give us completely different views than before. Lastly, I wish you well!

Frequently having mood swings over small matters, I think you might have a perfectionism complex. You demand perfection from yourself and others, and if even the tiniest thing or certain details don't meet your expectations, you dwell on it and can't move on. Is that the case? Much of our unhappiness actually stems from the various thoughts that swirl in our minds. We attach too much importance to these thoughts that are not necessarily true. These thoughts come from the input we received as children and have become ingrained thinking patterns. If you had strict or perfectionist parents who criticized you for any slight mistake, you are more likely to develop a perfectionist or obsessive-compulsive personality. You can't let go of things when it comes to dealing with people, situations, or yourself. Changing this is a long-term process. First, your awareness takes the first step. In the future, when you encounter similar events, you can examine what is truly bothering you and whether those things that are holding you back are small matters that can be let go. Secondly, write down those small matters on paper and analyze them one by one. See what emotions they bring and what you truly desire behind those emotions. Do your best to accomplish what you can and satisfy your needs that can be met, and rationalize the things you can't do well and the negative emotions. Thirdly, learn to confide in and seek support from family, friends, or mental health professionals, slowly releasing those small emotions and not allowing them to hold you captive. Perfection is a positive term, but demanding perfection excessively can be harmful to yourself and others. Don't force yourself to reach some high standard, just be true to yourself. Self-acceptance and self-joy are the most important. Best wishes!

Title, hello! Seeing your story about experiencing some small things and having strong and long-lasting emotional fluctuations troubles me. It makes me feel that your inner world is very sensitive and delicate, and you have high expectations for yourself and others in interpersonal relationships. You hope to break free from this vicious cycle and regain control of your emotions. Emotions are messengers, and the signals they want to convey require our exploration. Emotions are our attitude and reaction after our desires are fulfilled. They have polarity, and when our desires are fulfilled, positive and pleasant emotions may arise; when our desires are not fulfilled, negative and low spirits may arise. Emotions are like the flu, they are contagious. In our interactions with others, we are constantly being influenced by their emotions. Therefore, it is particularly important to clarify the boundaries between others' emotions and our own. When something happens in life and triggers negative emotions, it is necessary to pause and ask yourself: what is happening in my inner world right now? What is making me feel so upset? Recognizing and accepting your current emotions, reducing the reliance on others' evaluations of you, is the key to improving your emotional state. The power of reframing. Our emotions come from our cognition and thoughts, and our cognition affects the duration of our emotions. Changing our thoughts gives us the opportunity to change our emotions. I invite you to look at things from a more diverse perspective after encountering an event. This may broaden your horizons and change your mood. [Here are some self-help methods recommended for you] - Mindfulness meditation or mindfulness. Scientific studies have shown that people who practice mindfulness meditation regularly have increased secretion of happiness hormones (also known as stress-reducing hormones), such as dopamine and oxytocin. These two hormones play an important role in maintaining a calm state of mind and adjusting negative emotions. - Read books on emotional management. For example, Dr. Hailan's series of books on emotional management, such as "Imperfection is Beauty," can help you understand the knowledge and methods of emotional management, allowing you to handle things with more composure. - Confide in and seek support from trusted friends. You can confide in your most intimate friends about your inner struggles and invite them to provide different perspectives and viewpoints, enhancing your ability for self-reflection. - You can also join or participate in personal growth groups or courses online or offline, allowing yourself to access a continuous social support system. I hope my humble advice can provide you with a little inspiration and help. I wish you the best state of emotions and a better life!

Give the OP a hug! They often experience extreme mood swings over trivial matters. When something happens, they can get stuck in it for several days or even longer. Just thinking about it makes their mood even worse. It seems like the OP has been suppressing a lot of emotions, like a "can of bottled emotions." Even a small external stimulus can trigger a powerful reaction, resulting in intense mood swings with significant differences in behavior. This means that deep inside the OP, there is already a "powder keg" filled with emotions. External stimuli are like the "fuse." Although the powder doesn't explode when it ignites, it still has a strong impact, causing noticeable changes in the OP's psychological and emotional state. At this point, their sense of self-empowerment can enter into this space. However, currently, their self-empowerment can only squeeze so much space and release so much emotional pressure. question: Remarriage, my husband is not very accepting of my son who is from a previous marriage, what should I do?

Recently, my son came back to the city where I live with his father. I often pick him up on weekends. However, this week, my mother came, and he suddenly changed his attitude. He seems unhappy and no longer accepts it! I don't know if he dislikes my mother or my child! This situation will definitely become normal in the future. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Hello. According to your sharing, this is a problem of unequal needs. It might be a good idea to find a time to have an honest conversation with him, understand his purpose in getting married, and tell him your purpose, expressing each other's needs clearly. Best wishes~.

question: "Why am I so useless? Why do I start crying whenever I get angry?"

answers.answer_text: Is the main reason for your tears due to feeling wronged? Is there something that you need that has not been fulfilled? What is causing you to feel hurt, which is why you are angry? Once you understand your true feelings and needs, you can then go back and not blame the person, as it will only make them angry too. Talk to the person about why you feel sad/unhappy/uncomfortable because of something, express your feelings, and explain what you want them to do. Communicate effectively and see if they can understand, try to make the other person understand your true emotions and needs.

question: Why does my girlfriend deliberately dress provocatively? How can I change her?
description: My girlfriend is in her sophomore year. She is good-looking and has a good figure, but she is quite introverted. However, she always dresses in a revealing way, with backless, shoulder-baring, and midriff-exposing clothes. She even intentionally wears super short skirts and low-cut tops that could easily lead to wardrobe malfunctions. If it were just because of the hot weather in summer or occasionally for the sake of looking good, I could let it slide. But she dresses like this every day in summer, and even in winter, she wears revealing clothes underneath and takes off her outerwear when indoors. I have only seen her wear non-revealing clothes in formal occasions, and she changes immediately afterward. She even likes to take pictures of herself in revealing clothes and share them with others. She says she feels restricted and suppressed when wearing non-revealing clothes and gets uncomfortable if she doesn't show some skin. She started wearing revealing clothes when she was in primary school, and since then, she has become more and more accustomed to it, developing a strong aversion to non-revealing clothes to the point where she feels she must show skin. Why is this? I don't want to interfere with her freedom to dress, but from a safety perspective and considering her future in society, she should get used to wearing non-revealing clothes. How can I change her?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I read your question carefully and from it, I can sense that you feel conflicted and distressed about your girlfriend's clothing choices. On one hand, you are concerned about the safety risks that come with her revealing clothing, but on the other hand, you don't want to interfere with someone's freedom of dressing. So, how should we approach this issue? [Considering that dress style reflects one's inner personality, it is difficult for personality traits to change quickly] From a psychological perspective, dress style is an outward expression of one's inner personality traits. Conservative or open clothing is a form of implicit psychological language that hints at one's preferred communication style in interpersonal relationships. Generally speaking, people who dress conservatively tend to have introverted and reserved personalities, and they tend to passively cope with interpersonal relationships. On the other hand, people who dress more provocatively tend to have extroverted personalities and take a more proactive approach in interpersonal interactions. Therefore, from this perspective, dress style is closely related to personality traits, and unless there are special significant events, it is unlikely to change in the short term. As a boyfriend, I suggest that you focus on preparing for safety concerns and respecting personal privacy. As for her views on clothing when she enters society, perhaps encountering unforeseen circumstances may change her perspective on dress. [Consider whether there may be underlying trauma causing the "compulsive behavior" of revealing clothing] In your question, I noticed that your girlfriend has an introverted personality, yet she dresses in a very revealing manner, which contradicts our conventional understanding that clothing reflects one's degree of openness. Additionally, you mentioned that she can't help but wear such clothes on various occasions and feels uncomfortable if she doesn't, even going to great lengths to wear them in winter. These behaviors seem to have a certain compulsive tendency, where dressing up is no longer about feeling happy and joyful, but rather appears to be a way to escape from uncomfortable feelings. Of course, this aspect needs further guidance from a professional psychology teacher. Perhaps behind her dressing style, there may be some past traumatic experiences. I hope the above response is helpful to you.

Hello, I think this is a very good question, which is a problem that many people can resonate with. I'm sure you're also very conflicted. First, let's summarize the problem as I see it. First, you, the questioner, are a male with a girlfriend who is a sophomore. Second, your girlfriend has a good figure and appearance but has an introverted personality and dresses revealingly. Third, her choice of clothing is causing you some confusion. Fourth, she is very resistant to wearing clothes that are not revealing. Fifth, you want to know how to change her. Now, let me analyze and give my understanding of the situation. First, according to the question, your girlfriend has had this style since primary school, which means she was already like this before you met her. But you still chose her to be your girlfriend, so how did you think back then? Second, the whole question is about her having a habit that you think is not good and you want her to change, but she can't. This is similar to smoking, drinking, or staying up late. These habits are not good for the body, and we hope the other person can change. Surface-level, it seems like we are doing it for their own good, but they really can't change. What should we do? First, I think the harm may not be that great. In many cases, this habit may not cause her much harm. She hasn't been freezing or harassed, and the reasons you mentioned seem to be imagined. In fact, she hasn't experienced any harm. Furthermore, who is the most uncomfortable person in this situation? It's you, not her. What can you do if you feel uncomfortable? There are two ways: you can change or she can change. You chose to make her change so you can get what you want without changing yourself. Do you think this is good for her? Third, why are you so uncomfortable? When you chose her initially, it should have been because you liked everything about her. If not, then it's your problem. If it is, then it's still your problem that you now want her to change. So when did your discomfort start and why does it exist? From your question, you think your demands are reasonable, but it seems like a defense mechanism called "rationalization" in psychology. Simply put, it means thinking that your views are reasonable and your discomfort is also reasonable. This is called a defense mechanism because if you don't think this way, you will make different discoveries and trigger even greater discomfort. For example, if you think your demands are unreasonable and she is right, what would happen? That would mean you are controlling, and only someone who doesn't feel secure inside would want to control the outside world. So where does this lack of inner security come from? Many of them come from painful memories, especially from the original family. So, have you ever had similar feelings in your past life? These feelings must be even more uncomfortable. In order to prevent these feelings from coming out, you must find a way to suppress them layer by layer. Of course, this is just my experience, and the specific situation needs to be explored. Fourth, there was an episode of the show "Qi Pashuo" where they discussed whether or not girlfriends should wear hot pants. One of the debaters used a quote from the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau that I think is very good. It goes like this: "You can wear all the pretty skirts you want, and we'll catch the perverts." Fifth, in fact, I think your girlfriend knows the reasons you mentioned, but she must have her own reasons for not wanting to dress less revealingly. If you can find a way for her to achieve her goals without exposing herself, I think she would be willing to change. If not, it might be more difficult. After all, it's not easy to change yourself, let alone change others. Now, here are a few suggestions for you: First, if you're willing, you can both see a therapist together. If you can communicate with each other, that's even better. Second, the world of men and women is different, so try to understand each other more and maybe there will be fewer conflicts. Third, you can try meditation, there are good resources on the Meditation Planet, you both can give it a try. I hope my answer can be helpful to you.

As a boyfriend, the only thing you can do is provide support, acceptance, and understanding. You need to see the little girl hidden in your girlfriend's heart who desires to be the center of attention, that's it.③ When communicating your uneasiness, try not to use love as a means of restraint. Do not try to deny the legitimacy of her clothing choices with fancy justifications or directly label them as "revealing." You can directly【 express your jealousy and uneasiness 】, let her see your vulnerable side, and see if expressing yourself in this way can warm up your relationship. When the emotional connection deepens, you will understand her better, and maybe she will change, and perhaps you will no longer be critical and persistent. ▶️Finally, I wish you to let go of this sweet burden as soon as possible️.

Title, hello! I understand your dilemma. Your girlfriend dresses provocatively and you don't want to interfere, but you feel she should dress more conservatively and want to change her. What I want to tell you is: first, let go of the idea of changing her. I believe you genuinely care for her in this matter, looking out for her safety and considering her future in society. However, there must be an underlying subconscious desire for her to dress this way. For example, she may feel liberated and beautiful, using her clothing as a form of self-expression. Dressing up is a highly effective means of showcasing one's personality. Nowadays, many people prefer their outfits to be unique and stand out. The psychology behind rebellious dressing reflects a strong emotional factor, displaying a radical way of dressing that expresses one's individuality. When you wear a certain style of clothing, it can change your inner self and how you present yourself in daily life. Your girlfriend wearing revealing clothes may be a way of expressing herself because she may be more introverted and wants to portray a more extroverted and cheerful image. The understanding of clothing cognition provides a scientific basis. When we dress, we should focus on the feeling we want rather than our current feelings as a standard. Which clothes can make us feel confident, sexy, in control, or wealthy? The clothing we choose conveys a message to the people around us and also to ourselves. Everyone has different perspectives on a particular issue. In the West, revealing clothing is very common, while in the East, it tends to be more conservative. For your girlfriend, perhaps she experienced some form of suppression during her upbringing, which makes her want to dress more boldly. And she has become accustomed to this dressing style. Women have the freedom to dress, and you can share your views, such as dressing appropriately for different occasions and locations. When she enters the workplace in the future, dressing appropriately will be more important than dressing beautifully. Therefore, try to gradually influence her rather than change her. You can also try to explore with her, why does she dress this way? Are there other reasons besides not wanting to be restricted? Does she feel insecure? And so on. Often, when we let go of the mentality of changing the other person, they feel at ease to be themselves, both in your presence and in their own hearts, and their way of dressing may no longer be a problem. For example, if she wants compliments, compliment her as a person rather than her clothes. If she wants attention, give her the attention she desires. Additionally, you can also express to her that you value elegance, modesty, and refinement, and this may subtly influence her clothing choices. In doing so, you may also change, and this issue may no longer be a cause of distress. Finally, I wish you the best!

First of all, it is not necessarily wrong for a young girl to show off her figure and appearance. Moreover, it seems that she knows to dress "modestly" in formal occasions, which means she still understands social norms. From one perspective, she craves attention from others and likes to be the center of attention. From an inner feeling, she may feel that she hasn't received enough attention. You mentioned that she is "introverted," which seems contradictory to her revealing clothing. She may not know how to establish deep connections with others in alternative ways, so she uses an impactful external expression to quickly connect with others. From your perspective, choosing a girlfriend like this may also indirectly indicate that you also need attention, but your need is fulfilled through your girlfriend. You can reflect on this aspect. Best wishes. Rongxin Psychology, Liu Mi.

Hello on Sunday night! The first question I want to ask is related to your question, which is, what qualities of your girlfriend initially attracted you? Is it related to her revealing clothing? In this question, the issue of your girlfriend wearing revealing clothing is more like a sociological problem, while your inability to accept her revealing clothing is more like an individual psychological problem. Your thinking needs to be based on more understanding and empathy. In your question, you have already explained why your girlfriend chooses to wear revealing clothes, and a big part of it is habit, right? Without any judgment, let's look at this habit. Your girlfriend still dresses professionally for formal occasions and sensibly wears a coat when it's cold outside. We need to further understand why we are so concerned about our girlfriend's revealing clothing. The premise of changing her is enough respect for each other and enough self-understanding, and using sufficient understanding, care, and love to have non-violent communication with each other. If we fulfill our obligations and communicate responsibly, and the other party still doesn't want to change, then we need to respect their opinion, just as you said, "I don't want to interfere with someone's freedom to dress." Since your girlfriend has already given what she believes to be a reasonable explanation, our focus should shift back to our own cognition. If it's because we're afraid of the harmful people in society who might harm those who wear revealing clothing, we need to first build confidence that a girlfriend who knows to wear a coat when it's cold or dress formally for formal occasions will have self-protection instincts. I hope this inspires and helps you!

question: 29 years old, after having a pleasant time with my boyfriend, we often end up having big arguments. What's going on?
description: My partner and I get along fine most of the time, relatively calm, but we often have big fights after getting along very well, and it's always me who starts it. For example, last night we didn't cook, we ordered takeout, enjoyed a delicious meal, and both of us were very happy. But during breakfast today, we ended up having a big argument over a small matter. When I calm down, I realize that every time we have a pleasant time together, we inevitably end up fighting, and I am the one who starts the war. I can't figure out why I do this. In my upbringing, my family was often in turmoil, my parents often fought, and my brother and I often fought as well, but back then I was always provoked by my brother. Parents and children also often had conflicts, and our family of four was very chaotic. Our noisy and peaceful states were exactly the opposite of other families, and peaceful harmony was rare in my memory. Why am I doing this now, unconsciously starting a fight after a pleasant time with my partner? Am I not allowing myself to have a good life? Does my subconscious feel that a harmonious and happy life does not belong to me? Do I want to ruin it? How can I find the specific reasons for doing this, I want to solve this problem! Thank you.

answers.answer_text: After reading the description, I realized that we don't always start arguing when we are getting along, but rather, we don't use a gentler approach to resolve our anger. 1. The way our family interacts has made arguing the norm. Due to the influence of our original family, it's difficult for us to communicate effectively. Any issues are always resolved through arguments, especially when it becomes a habit. Subconsciously, we avoid positive communication. I have tried to communicate calmly with them, but their responses are difficult to understand, which reignites my anger and makes me reluctant to communicate with them. It's the same when I interact with my partner. We don't want to back down, while the other person may not want to argue, but rather explain things to us. However, in our irrational state, we fail to realize this. We just want to be comforted rather than hear a bunch of reasoning, leading to another argument. 2. I've recognized my own issues and learned to calm my emotions. Subconsciously, we use arguments as a way to protect ourselves, so that we won't be taken advantage of. However, our partner is not our family, and they try to resolve problems in a more peaceful manner. Therefore, we need to let go of our defensive facade. If every time we argue, our partner tries to convince us with reasoning, we can tell them if they can refrain from doing so for a while. They can give us a chance to vent or just give us a simple hug. We can let them know that we don't actually want to argue, but that we need to gradually change some of our habits, and we hope they can give us more time. At the same time, we should also reassure our partner afterwards, telling them that when we are angry, we need to be comforted. However, we need to set boundaries and not demand that they always give in. Respect should be mutual. The world and I love you.

Hello there! When I saw this title, it made me think of my own relationship with my boyfriend. We have a great time together, but sometimes I would pick a fight with him over a small disagreement and blow it out of proportion, leading to arguments. After every argument, I would reflect on why we fought in the first place. Most of the time, I realized that we were just arguing for the sake of arguing. Maybe it's because life feels too ordinary, and we need some ups and downs to spice things up a bit (laughs). So, first of all, you can ask yourself why you argue. Is there really a conflict or are you just used to arguing? It's good to see that you have self-awareness and recognize the pattern of arguing in your family. Childhood experiences have a significant impact on one's personality and interpersonal relationships. The family is the earliest classroom, and parents are the earliest teachers. If you grew up in a "turbulent" environment, it might be ingrained in your subconscious that connections with others are formed through arguing. (While others have peaceful and harmonious relationships within their families, yours is established through arguments and fights, and even expresses "affection" through these means.) Indeed, arguing can be a way to establish connections. During arguments, everyone can express their inner anger and expose themselves, effectively making the other person understand them. However, you don't want to establish connections through arguing, right? You want to have a harmonious and happy life. "Wanting" to change is the most important step towards change. I suggest you first communicate with your boyfriend, tell him about your childhood family environment and your self-reflections after every argument, and listen to his thoughts. You can say something like, "Every time we argue, I reflect and realize that it's always me who starts it. I don't want to argue, but maybe I don't know how to build intimate relationships peacefully. My parents and my siblings used to argue all the time, and I disliked it but also got used to it, which unintentionally made me become like them." At the same time, I also wonder if you have a lot of insecurity that makes you worry that the happy and peaceful environment will disappear and something bad will happen. The more you worry, the more likely it is to happen, so your subconscious leads you to "create conflicts." Ask yourself, what are you really afraid of behind these arguments? Once you identify the problem, invite your boyfriend to help you overcome it and gain more security.

You are wondering if you are unable to have a harmonious life, as if scenes from your childhood are replaying themselves. But in my view, you are seeking healing. Life is like a mirror, sometimes childhood and adulthood reflect each other, sometimes oneself and others reflect each other. But all reflections are because we are not enough yet, not enough because true traumas have not been healed, not satisfied yet. Experiences will always replay, sometimes from different perspectives. It's just because we still have unresolved issues inside us, that we want to understand, understand a bit more. That's how the mind works. When it fully understands, becomes clear, it will say, "That's enough, it's good, this is it." But before that, it will create many opportunities for itself to have repeated experiences. The solution is, you can have a good talk with your boyfriend, not necessarily about your past, but about the psychological processes you both go through during arguments. It helps strengthen clear experiences and bring satisfaction earlier. Of course, you can also find a counselor and reenact your psychological processes, which allows for a more comprehensive, multi-dimensional observation and understanding of yourself, so that you can say "this is it" earlier. Today is your cuckoo, pay attention, let's together see the state of the mind.

There is a lifestyle called "sadomasochism" where they coexist like a pair of twins. Psychoanalytic psychodynamics mainly reveal how "past events influence the present." The past was tumultuous, that was the experienced one, whether it was the older brother who inflicted pain or the parents, or oneself who endured it. In fact, the inner self has already accepted this pattern, and calmness will make those accustomed to this habit uncomfortable. There are both disadvantages and advantages to not being accustomed to inflicting pain – it gives a sense of control, a feeling of superiority! Just like the feeling the older brother had back then, when there was no power, becoming like that perhaps was a childhood dream, and now there is a chance to fulfill it!

You are very good at making associations. When you were young, there were more arguments than peace in your family. Now, if your own small family is too harmonious and pleasant, it is different from your family before. Therefore, you want to stir up trouble and revisit the scene of arguments that you are familiar with. People can only truly experience the original "flavor" in familiar situations. By the way, let your partner know that you used to always be the one provoked, but now you finally have the opportunity to be the one provoking, bringing them into your camp. The above may not be the real reason, but if you don't want to argue, tell your partner that you agree to a rule where as long as one party calls for a stop during an argument, the other party must agree. Give this a try, and maybe you can gradually establish your own family atmosphere.

This type of "invisible crisis anxiety" is generally formed as a result of early family environment, and it cannot be sorted out simply through communication with your husband, nor can it be attributed to a problem of organizing logical thinking. Based on your personal birth date and registered photo, I can provide you with effective solutions combining modern psychology. Stay strong! Good luck to you.

question: I am in the third year of high school. I have no motivation to study and cannot make progress. What should I do?
description: This is a critical moment of survival or extinction. I am studying at a top high school in my province, but I feel like I haven't done much in the past two years. Now I feel a bit tired of studying (I felt the same before), and the benefits of studying don't really inspire me that much!! I'm really anxious myself (maybe feeling guilty), and I've realized that I think I have some unique qualities (like the potential to be awesome) but also a bit arrogant. I've tried many methods, but they haven't been very effective (maybe because my execution ability is not enough, but I have tried). It's really hard for me to fully invest myself and I feel uncomfortable when I try to do it. Thank you all for your help. I hope to receive your advice.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from the description, it is clear that the original poster is currently feeling confused and encountering difficulties in their studies. I hope that my response and personal experience can help you. 1. Before discussing the present, let's not talk about the past two years when you felt you didn't accomplish much. It can be seen that your mindset is still good; at least you're not wasting your time and understand the principle of being unable to change the past. As a soon-to-be senior high school student in a prestigious school, apart from realizing that you need to seize the present, you also need to understand the following: 1) your starting point is higher than others. Although you feel tired of studying (even in the past), the benefits of studying don't have much impact on you! Having a higher starting point is your advantage, but it can also become your disadvantage. You mentioned that the benefits of studying don't have much impact on you, so let me talk about the disadvantages of not studying.  #If you choose comfort at a crucial age for striving, you might not have to endure the hardship of studying now, but in the future, you'll have to endure the hardships of life, and these hardships come with high interest rates. The later you endure them, the more bitter they will be. #Furthermore, not striving means that your performance in next year's college entrance examination may not reach your initial expectations when you entered high school, causing others and even yourself to feel disappointed. Do you want that? #Finally, do you not feel jealous and regretful seeing friends who previously didn't perform as well as you and couldn't enter a prestigious high school, but then scored better than you in the college entrance examination and got into a better university? If you don't know what you want, you might as well think about what you don't want. This way, you may find the source of motivation that resonates with you! 2. It's more fearful to pretend to strive than to not strive at all. You need to find a study method that suits you. Maybe you didn't work hard enough in the first two years of high school, but as long as the college entrance examination hasn't arrived, you still have a chance to start over. You might want to think about when is the best time for you to study, concentrate during that time, and keep a clear mind. Don't force yourself to study blindly, as it may seem like you're serious, but it's actually inefficient self-deception. It doesn't benefit your learning and may decrease your motivation and confidence due to a lack of progress. Don't worry, think about what kind of results you want to achieve in the college entrance examination, consider the distance between you and the university you desire, identify your weak and strong subjects, and once you have a clear understanding, make a plan for yourself and start again! There's still time for everything! Finally, I'll leave you with a saying that I stuck on my desk during the college entrance examination: "There is nothing difficult in the world, only those who can overcome hardships will find joy in life." Wishing you success in the college entrance examination!

Hello, the summary of the problems you mentioned are as follows: 1. You dislike studying, both in the past and present. 2. You believe that the benefits of studying are not significant and lack motivation, but now you feel guilty and anxious about your current situation. 3. You have a somewhat arrogant personality and feel unique. 4. You have tried various methods but ultimately failed, and you also struggle with lack of discipline. Here are some suggestions I can offer: ▼ Overcoming your dislike for studying and suddenly developing a love for it is a difficult task. However, you can start by accepting it more openly and not rejecting it. For example, when solving a problem, approach it as if it were a game or a challenge. Each difficult question you successfully tackle will give you a sense of accomplishment. ▼ Recognize the benefits of studying by setting clear goals for yourself, such as getting into a specific university or pursuing a particular profession. Once you have defined your goals, you will realize that achieving them requires dedicated studying. You can also seek out friends who have attended university and listen to their experiences, discovering how different the learning experience can be at prestigious institutions. (It's important not to assume that all universities are the same, based on my personal experience. After not performing well on the college entrance examination, I attended a vocational college. However, after interacting with bachelor's degree students, I discovered many differences and realized how outstanding they were. Their achievements motivated me to pursue a bachelor's degree as well.) ▼ While it's good to acknowledge that you consider yourself unique, it's even better to recognize your weaknesses because it provides an opportunity for improvement. Although you dislike studying, attending a prestigious high school indicates that your academic performance is not poor, and you possess some confidence. However, it's important to be humble and seek help when encountering unfamiliar topics. In your daily life, try toning down your arrogant personality. ▼ You mentioned that you have tried different methods, but often failed and lack discipline. The fact that you have attempted different approaches shows that you want to change, and your willingness to embrace failure is admirable. Persistence is challenging for everyone. Many people enthusiastically create study plans but struggle to stick to them. If you lack discipline, seek assistance from others, or collaborate with someone who has similar academic achievements. Challenge each other, discuss difficult problems, and support one another to progress together. Finally, I wish you happiness every day, smooth learning, and continuous improvement.

Hello there! OP, after reading what you wrote, I feel like you might be struggling with studying. Here are my thoughts, and I hope they can help you. Being confident is not a bad thing. In the text, I noticed that you mentioned that you tend to boast but lack the ability to follow through. It's normal for people to like boasting, and it can be a fun thing to do sometimes. Don't feel troubled by it. When it comes to being disciplined, you need to have direction and set goals. Set a time frame to complete a task, and make sure you don't procrastinate. Have confidence in yourself and follow your own plan. Learn to take notes and write down your thoughts and goals, both short-term and long-term. Then, gradually work towards achieving them according to what you've written. When you realize that you've accomplished a lot at the end of each day, you'll feel fulfilled and motivated, and your ability to follow through will improve. Believe in yourself and believe that you can succeed. Don't be afraid to take things one step at a time and make progress gradually. When you work hard and inspire yourself, you will realize that you have already achieved success. I understand the pressure of the college entrance examination. It's truly brutal. It feels like crossing a narrow bridge amidst thousands of competitors. Getting into a good university really means accessing a different learning environment. So, as a high school senior, your focus should be on studying well for the college entrance examination. Don't let your senior year leave you with any regrets. Strive to get into a university that you like. Embrace life, do what makes you happy, and turn life into a source of joy. Live with confidence. Lastly, I believe that you will overcome your confusion and become even more confident! Hehe.

Hug hug! One thing I can relate to is that I also felt somewhat unique during high school. However, many facts have proven that "the more capable a person is, the more humble they tend to be". My previous arrogance taught me a lesson about repeating a grade. As someone who has been through it, I hope you can learn from my negative example and not make the same mistake. Reflecting on myself, I am now about to enter my sophomore year of college and I haven't fully achieved the humble and considerate qualities of the outstanding seniors. But as someone who has gone through it, I can tell you that "hard work doesn't always guarantee success, but without hard work, you won't achieve anything". When I was about to enter my senior year of high school, I lacked motivation. Even though I didn't fail the exams, my performance wasn't ideal, and repeating a year gave me the motivation I needed. One reason was the "inspiring success stories and motivational articles on Zhihu". I would read them every now and then, and after reading, I would have a feeling of "successful people are all working hard, so why should I settle for mediocrity?", and then I would fully immerse myself in studying. Another reason was "setting a goal for a university". While I was preparing for exams, I had a picture of the university I aspired to on my desk. Even when I was tired and sleepy in class, I wouldn't dare to sleep when I saw the picture. Later on, even though I still haven't achieved my goal, I can honestly say that I gave it my all, and now I'm moving towards that university with the goal of taking the postgraduate entrance exams. It doesn't matter if the road is long, as long as you keep going, you will eventually reach your destination.︴A pearl will not be covered in dust forever. Before that, it is important to "have a correct understanding of oneself". Analyzing oneself requires great courage, facing one's strengths and weaknesses, regularly recalling and even listing the efforts made in the past, and seeing if one has truly "absorbed" the knowledge rather than just superficially learning it. This is crucial in order to promptly correct one's study methods and attitudes and ensure that one's efforts yield results. "Self-control and discipline" are also important. Without self-discipline (including regular sleep schedule, healthy diet, etc.), efforts can easily be wasted. If one cannot discipline oneself, then "forced discipline" can be implemented (by deleting entertainment apps on the phone or handing over the phone, computer, or tablet to a reliable person, using it at scheduled times and in controlled amounts), creating a clean and focused study environment. Is it important to get into a good college? Yes, it is. Does it determine one's entire life? Absolutely not. It can only influence the speed and path to "success". The ultimate determining factors in life are one's own choices and attitude. Don't stress too much; as long as you have no regrets, that's what matters. Do you understand what kind of person you want to become in the future? "When the heart is set, one can traverse any path". Let us encourage each other. I hope you will eventually achieve your wishes and "enjoy the blossoms of Chang'an in a day".

Hello! Seeing your question, I can feel your distress and anxiety. The fact that you are in a prestigious high school shows that you are a very capable student, which makes me feel a sense of familiarity because I have been teaching the top 10% of students in a prestigious high school. This year, I am focusing on researching the factors that influence students' learning motivation. From your description, I can see that you have a tendency to underestimate your achievements in the past two years. You also mentioned feeling somewhat unique (like a potential genius) and a bit arrogant. There is a belief that intelligent people don't need to work hard, and diligent effort is a sign of foolishness. Do you agree with this belief? If you do, please think seriously about whether it is correct. If not, that's great because you understand that learning requires effort. Regardless of the past, here are a few suggestions for you to seriously consider: think about why you are studying, or in other words, why you want to study? When you can't figure out the answer to this question, your motivation will often be lacking. If you really can't figure it out, try to force yourself to study. Set up a study plan, force yourself to start taking action, and use your efforts to exchange for good results. Reward yourself with positive results. Also, consider talking to a professional psychologist to see if you have any irrational beliefs. Irrational beliefs often lead to wrong actions, which in turn lead to academic failures and a lack of enjoyment in learning, resulting in a lack of motivation. However, it is fortunate that you want to study hard and seek help here, which clearly shows your determination. A professional psychologist will be able to assist you. I wish you the strength to find your way and set sail!

You set the bar too high for yourself. Please make sure to read it all. Although the words may be harsh, please remove the thorn in your heart. After all, you are an ordinary person, just like me. I am not worthy, but those big shots are. We should be like those big shots, oblivious to outside matters, and focus only on reading sage books. I can do it too, but I don't want to. What if I work as hard as them but don't achieve the same level of success? Can I, who is so proud, accept setbacks? What should I do? My parents put so much pressure on me, and I don't want them to feel guilty for my poor academic performance. What should I do? Well, I really understand your feelings and sense of guilt (not a typo, the person who builds their own prison is ourselves, and it's not someone else who traps us, but ourselves). Understood! Actually, being called a big shot is quite delightful, hehehehehehe. You are also a super big shot. Big shot, how do you feel when you see someone better than you? Do you feel inferior to them? Have you really understood the feelings you had when you were not doing well in your studies and were looked down upon by others? Have you truly accepted the fact that your journey to success was not easy, rather than humiliating? Have you truly faced and valued your emotions? Have you asked your heart if you really don't want to study? Is it really because you cannot achieve what you want? Actually, that's not true. What troubles you is not just peer pressure, right? It's the feeling of not being the top student that you have always overlooked, isn't it? Is it the guilt of hurting others with the arrogance that should be displayed when you were one of the best students, under the constant praise of teachers and the scrutiny of others? You have never forgiven yourself, forgiven others for looking down on you when you were not outstanding yet. You have never forgiven yourself, forgiven yourself for the shortcomings and mockery you faced on your journey towards improvement. Have you not forgiven yourself for not experiencing the same things as others and not empathizing with them? Have you not forgiven yourself for disregarding the emotions that you kept ignoring during that desperate time? You have never forgiven yourself, forgiven others for their arrogance when they excel, which is why you have always hated or even despised such arrogance. But you dare not truly face your own vulnerability and the guilt behind that arrogance. I truly understand your feelings, and I believe many students can deeply empathize with you because they have experienced similar struggles. The pain of doing well in academics and the pain of not doing well are certainly not the "responsibility" borne by you alone. Often, we say we have a lot of pressure, a huge burden. But actually, this burden, this pressure, is the counteraction imposed by us. It is the emotions and difficulties that we keep ignoring and dare not admit. Because we believe that with our weak emotions and bodies, how can we survive in the "great outdoors"? We can only grow little by little in a greenhouse, where people keep adding fertilizer. We can only rely on this soil, this plastic greenhouse to grow. How can some flowers grow better than us in the wilderness? Why aren't these flowers yearning to live outside the greenhouse? Why can some flowers grow well inside the greenhouse? Are we stupid? We always carry this guilt, the feeling of being better than most flowers that grow in the greenhouse. Why can't I come out? Can I really grow well if I come out? Can I really grow well in the greenhouse? If I can't, how can others help me? What should I do? This seems to be your constant inner voice, making me feel that this age is so special! You can continually worry and think about life issues in your own way. It's great! My answer to the feelings you conveyed is: Believe in yourself, there are no limits in life, and shift the "true perspective of the world" to your own perspective. Find your true feelings and desires in the emotions that you feel are important but maybe others don't. Don't criticize yourself from any side, but slowly learn how to love yourself. You don't need to be like anyone else; everyone has their own aspirations. Maybe most people have certain aspirations, but it happens that this is how I grow, this is the kind of flower I am. Sometimes, we intentionally overlook others' lives, the feelings of those extraordinary plants in the greenhouse, and how they appear as ordinary people, students. Under the pressure of the clouds, are the feelings we ignore truly pressure, or are they companions? Why don't we truly face the feelings of different people and accept our own feelings? As for learning, the learning paths of each flower are different. Which flower is truly superior? Which flower cannot learn? Which flower is not a flower? Save, a little less, up and down. In my understanding, look at yourself with the eyes you used when you were a child, and find your true feelings and true desires. Don't consider yourself inferior from any perspective. I believe everyone's perspective is different, but which one is bad? Wishing you peace, joy, and happiness, gratefulness and appreciation.

Hello classmate, I also had thoughts like this in high school. I used to feel like going to school was not very important to me and I disliked learning those dry and rigid things. I often wondered why, why do I have to go to school, why do I have to study, are the things that others consider important and successful really important to me? That is the reason why I developed a dislike for studying. I was also often mentioned as a negative example, skipping classes and not paying attention in class, but later I was also mentioned for how mischievous I was and in the end, I turned over a new leaf and walked the right path. I don't dislike learning, I just dislike the standardized and uniform things in school. Actually, you don't dislike learning either, since you can develop an interest and an eagerness for knowledge in other things. The exploration of anything and involvement in any aspect is learning. It's just that now you're a bit confused about why you have to do it this way. I hope you can calm down and think about what you really want and what you yearn for deep inside. Learning is not just about the subjects in arts and sciences or the college entrance examination, all things that can bring positive value to yourself can be called learning, like cooking, gardening, yoga, and handicrafts. This age is a beautiful time, you must study well because now with the current policies, the college entrance examination is the only way out for most people. Grades and diplomas cannot determine a person's goodness or badness, we learn knowledge and skills in school, not human relationships and worldly affairs. My current major is design. I liked drawing in middle school, but others said it was useless and the teacher even tore my drawing in class. But now, I still make a living with my art. What they said wasn't right, drawing is very useful to me. So you must calm down and think about what you really want to do well. Now is the perfect time. I only discovered my interest in geology right before the college entrance examination, but it was too late, I couldn't apply for that major anymore. I was limited in my choice of majors and could only choose fine arts. But you are different now, you still have one year to study and first improve your grades, and then think about the subjects you mentioned that you are interested in. Start studying hard now, and in a year, you can go to the school and major you like, it's a wonderful thing. I am satisfied with my current major, but I still carry a sense of regret because I didn't understand why I was studying in high school and missed the best opportunity to improve my grades. I only realized what I truly aspired to study later, but by then it was too late. So I sincerely hope that you can study seriously. The college entrance examination is the foundation, it's like the structure of a building. Only by doing well now can you truly achieve your dreams, laying a solid foundation before building a tall building, achieving a refined decoration from a basic structure. Finally, I genuinely wish that you can pursue what you love from the bottom of your heart, follow your own thoughts, and it won't go wrong. The confusion and bewilderment you feel now, time will provide you with an answer. Let me share a poem with you, "Regardless of peak or plain, stunning vistas are sure to wane. After gathering flowers for honeyed gains, who labors for whose weal and bane?" Don't be like a bee, working hard but not knowing why. You must study, only then can you live the life you want, and meet like-minded companions. Keep going, I wish you a bright future, even if this path is not recognized, even if there are obstacles ahead. Don't leave yourself with regrets, you must persevere. Don't be afraid of others not understanding, "Don’t worry that the road ahead has no kindred spirit, for in this world, who does not recognize you?" Those who strive, progress, and excel in any field will shine wherever they are. Keep going, it's never too late to start from now. I wish for you to grow into someone you admire in the future.

Based on your description, it seems that there are two aspects that need adjustment: lack of motivation in studying, and lack of perseverance. However, both of these aspects serve a goal, so there is a third and most important aspect, which is "what does the senior year of high school mean to you in terms of exam-oriented learning?" or "what goal do you hope to achieve through the senior year of exam-oriented learning?" Perhaps you will find that the description here is not about "reading" or "studying," but about "the senior year of exam-oriented learning." Because "reading" and "studying" are broader concepts that encompass lifelong learning, and "learning" includes many aspects such as ideas and skills. So, you may not like "reading" or "studying," as long as it is the lifestyle you choose. However, now you are facing a specific task, which is to continue "going to school" through a year of exam-oriented learning at school and at home, and what kind of school to continue is the actual goal. If what you mean by "reading" is going to school, then do you feel that there is no benefit or meaning in continuing to go to school or pursuing "university education" or "better university education"? If so, is it related to your potential as a "cool and capable person" and your arrogance? For example, do you feel that you are so awesome to the point where you don't need better university education to live the life you want? Is this the aspect that makes you different from others? You don't need to follow the path that the general public follows and can find your own path to success? Or is it that the life you want to live doesn't require attending a better university to achieve it? In short, your action and perseverance during your senior year are related to your intrinsic motivation for learning, and intrinsic motivation for learning is related to your specific goals, and specific goals are guided by what kind of life you want to live. Therefore, perhaps you can start by asking yourself: What kind of life do I want to live in the future? What conditions do I need to possess to achieve this kind of life? Can attending a better university help me meet these conditions faster? Thinking about it this way, perhaps your thinking will become clearer.

question: Middle school girl, likes her teacher, am I a lesbian? What is wrong with me?
description: Middle school student, female, but I have a crush on my teacher. She is around 42 years old, and she is really, really adorable. I can't really tell if I admire and idolize her or if I am in love with her. But whenever I see her, my heart flutters. I become shy when she talks to me. Am I a lesbian? Why do I develop feelings of love for someone of the same gender?
