answers.answer_text: Dear asker, hello! From your words, I can see a brave little girl who is trying her best to find answers. Hugs to such a lovely asker! Let's go back to the description you provided. You think your teacher is very, very cute, and you feel shy when you're around her, so you like her. You then concluded that you like the same sex and are curious why you have feelings for the same sex. Regarding your liking for your teacher, can you point out some cute behaviors or attractive qualities of your teacher that caught your attention? It might help to keep a teacher observation log, where you can record your little emotions and help organize your feelings. What does your liking for your teacher look like? Is it because of her maturity, gentleness, thoughtfulness...? Actually, liking a teacher can be about the person herself or her behavior. Both answers are correct because there must be something about the teacher that you aspire to. She has experienced the years we haven't and has the maturity that we hope to have. So, take some time to think about what liking looks like to you. Regarding the psychological studies related to homosexuality, it has been found that just like the preference for using the right hand or left hand, sexual orientation is a continuous process. There is a broad range between complete heterosexuality and complete homosexuality. Those who are only interested in the same sex are called homosexuals, those who are only interested in the opposite sex are called heterosexuals, and those who are interested in both sexes are called bisexuals. In short, whether it is homosexuality or heterosexuality, as a social phenomenon, it has always accompanied humanity's journey. From a purely romantic perspective, since age is not a factor, why should there be gender restrictions? So, no matter what your sexual orientation is, you deserve to be embraced by the world. Returning to your question, you wonder if you are a homosexual because you have a good impression of a same-sex teacher. So, is it too quick to conclude that you are a homosexual? You are still in middle school and very young. You have plenty of time to build your own knowledge system, so there is no need to rush to label yourself. Why not explore more knowledge and learn the stories behind things in this colorful world? I believe that with a rich experience, you will be able to give yourself a definite answer. No matter who you are, the world and I love you.

Homosexuality is generally considered innate and cannot be corrected through treatment. Nowadays, we advocate for respecting homosexuality. As you are only in middle school, it is too early to determine if you are homosexual, and no one should make such a diagnosis. Therefore, I suggest you relax and channel your attraction towards your teacher into motivation for studying well. As for the distress about homosexuality, it is best to evaluate it when you are an adult.

question: Feeling like I am being imitated by a girl around me, am I too sensitive? How can I change this?
description: I feel like there's a girl around me who is always imitating me. Whatever type of clothes I wear, she starts wearing similar clothes in a few days, sometimes even exactly the same. This is quite obvious, but there are also less noticeable things, such as: 1. Whatever food I buy, she buys it shortly after. Actually, this is a very ordinary thing, and I only realized it after noticing the clothing issue. 2. I try a new hairstyle, and she does the same. 3. I buy a new eyeshadow palette and try a new makeup look, and she follows suit. I've also heard a saying, "Everyone thinks they are unique, but in reality, 90% of people think the same." I don't know if I'm being too sensitive, but her silent behavior really annoys and frustrates me. Is it just me overthinking? What should I do to change my mindset or her behavior?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, conflicts, roommates, classmates.

answers.answer_text: Hello, fellow, warm hug to you (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand that: (1) You feel uncomfortable because there's a girl who seems to be imitating you recently. (2) You want to know if it's because you're overthinking. (3) You also want to know how to change your own mindset or deal with the other person's behavior. Here are my analysis and advice, hoping to help you: (1) First of all, everyone has the right to dress up, and nowadays, fashion trends are similar, so it's normal for everyone to dress similarly. However, if it's exactly the same, it might be a bit problematic. (2) Secondly, imitation can also be a form of recognition. Maybe the other person feels it's easier to pick things without making mistakes by following you, so they just copy everything. (3) Finally, since the other person seems to appreciate your taste so much, why not be friends with them and understand their real thoughts, helping them find a style that suits them. #The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

question: The child is about to enter middle school, what is the best relationship with the child like?
description: My child is about to enter middle school, and I haven't been able to spend much time with them since they were young. Now, their personality and habits are really bad, and I don't know how to make them change.
keywords: Family, family relationships, the process of growing up, and communication between parents and children.

answers.answer_text: My friend, from your description, I can feel your care and concern for your child and your desire to do better! I'm glad to meet parents like you who are willing to seek professional help. So, let me give you some suggestions: First, don't argue with your child. Why is this the first piece of advice? It is determined by the psychological development of teenagers. They are currently experiencing conflicts between physical maturity and psychological immaturity, often wanting to appear like adults and show off their capabilities. However, they don't always have good control over their abilities, and sometimes they go too far. The specific manifestation is arguing with parents and talking back. Many parents don't understand their children's desire to express themselves, and take it seriously. The child says something, the parent responds, and communication turns into an argument. The second piece of advice follows: Pay attention to the purpose of communication, which is to exchange, not to win or lose. As parents, we don't need to insist on winning, but we shouldn't always give in either. When a child's behavior violates social norms and laws, we should clearly convey the message that making such choices has consequences. However, during the communication process, do not judge the child's behavior, just let them know that there will be consequences. Don't perfunctorily deal with the child, be sincere. At this time, the child is sensitive and can easily sense your impatience and minor irritations towards them. When talking to the child, avoid playing with your phone or being distracted. It is essential to maintain sincerity and consistency. Grow together with your child. This is your first time being parents, and it's also your child's first time being a child. When you were your child's age, you might have done a lot of housework, which they have never experienced. They can't go back to the past to experience it. However, when they are the same age as you, they will face competition pressures that you have never experienced. But you can experience the little things in life together with them because at this moment, you and your child are in the same era. You can be weaker than your child, and allow them to occasionally excel, such as in knowledge related to the internet. Give them confidence, treat them as equals, and they will love you more.

Hello OP! Your child entering middle school indicates that they are still in their adolescence, a period that is generally more rebellious. Additionally, since you did not raise them yourself but rather they were raised by their grandparents or other family members, their personality and habits may differ from what you prefer and accept. These differences will take time to change, as they cannot be changed quickly. Firstly, you need to accept your child's habits and personality. Try to interact with them slowly and observe which habits can be changed and how to change them. Secondly, be more tolerant and accepting of your child. If they make a mistake, don't rush to scold them. Instead, calmly talk to them in a gentle manner. Otherwise, you might trigger their rebelliousness. Lastly, communicate more with your child. Communication is crucial within a family, as many conflicts arise from a lack of communication. If there are habits or aspects of your child's personality that need improvement, talk to them about it and help them understand that they need to change. Take it slow. These are my personal views and suggestions, for your reference. I hope it can help you.

question: Is it a mental problem to always have too much suspicion in a relationship, leading to frequent arguments?
description: I often suspect that someone is interested in my partner or my partner is interested in someone else just because they are chatting. My partner thinks I'm being unreasonable. Can you tell me if there's something wrong with my mental health?
keywords: Love, sense of security, arguments, love management

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~ First, let me give you an encouraging hug. I completely understand how you're feeling right now. It's normal to feel uncomfortable and even argue when your partner is chatting with other guys. It's a typical behavior of jealousy. Jealousy is a normal phenomenon and it shows that you care about your partner. However, it's important to find a balance because being overly jealous can cause significant damage to your relationship. First and foremost, you need to give your partner enough trust. Chatting could simply be with friends, buddies, or brothers. Don't always suspect that your partner will have a negative impact on you. Of course, your behavior could be related to your childhood experiences, especially between the ages of 0 to 1. It could be due to insufficient companionship from your parents or inappropriate parenting methods, which have resulted in you not developing a strong sense of security. That's why you find it difficult to trust your partner in a romantic relationship. If you don't address this issue in a timely manner, it could have a greater impact on the relationship between the two of you in the future. You can also seek help from professional psychologists or counselors. Best wishes~.

Hello, I understand your feelings. You love your girlfriend very much and hope that she can be wholeheartedly devoted to you. You really enjoy the time spent with your girlfriend and cherish it. You are very careful to protect it and don't allow others to disturb it. There's nothing wrong with your mentality. In every relationship, there will be exclusiveness, which is a normal reaction and also the mystery of love. However, everything should be done in moderation. Loving her doesn't mean you should monitor her or control all her social interactions and behaviors or prohibit her from having any contact with the opposite sex. It doesn't mean you should restrict her life to only revolve around you. After all, as a social being, we all need to interact and communicate with others to fulfill our sociability and to live a normal life. Your doubts and arguments partly stem from your lack of self-confidence. You are afraid of losing her and others taking her away, which may be related to your past experiences. You can enhance your self-confidence through various ways such as your appearance, speech, career, life, and travel. You can also read some professional books, which will be helpful. Part of it is because you haven't learned how to handle certain issues in a relationship. When you have doubts and thoughts, it's better to express them face to face and make your attitude clear. Love should be exclusive and monogamous. You can directly explain to her about her behaviors and request improvements. Quarrels can sometimes hurt feelings and cause both of you to be hurt. Love is built on trust, acceptance, understanding, and support. I believe you can handle the problems in your relationship and achieve a sweet love.

question: College life can be difficult, how to control emotions and negative thoughts?
description: I now have to exhaust myself every day in order to fall asleep (after 3 am), otherwise I can't sleep at all. I chose this major because of my father's ignorance, he even used suicide to threaten me. I now feel very emotionally sensitive, and my university life is really difficult. I also have a hard time controlling my emotions now, sometimes I suddenly want to get angry over small things, and when I collapse, I really want to commit suicide. Every time I think of my father, I have a headache, but he acts like nothing happened, thinking that he helped me choose a good path. I have no talent for studying this, nor do I want to study this major. I don't understand why he insisted on me choosing it. The employment prospects for this major are also very difficult, even if I excel in it, it's still hard to find a job. His arrogance and ignorance have ruined me for a lifetime. I really don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Your negative feelings and discouragement about the future make you nervously anxious, mentally exhausted, and emotionally anxious. You are easily triggered and tend to release your emotions. You easily feel offended. In fact, all of these are the sensations and memories from within. Emotions are not controlled but rather enhanced through positive experiences, self-empowerment, and inner cognition. By working on these aspects, the emotional mechanism will gradually change, and negative emotions will not be produced naturally, thus eliminating the need for control and suppression.

question: I have a close opposite-sex friend that I care about a lot. Should I resolve the situation or let go completely?
description: I have been friends with a senior student on WeChat for two and a half years. He has been very helpful with my studies and work, and I always feel happy when chatting with him. However, we have only met once (he treated me to a meal). He has turned down my invitations multiple times, probably because he has a girlfriend. When I ask him for advice, he is always enthusiastic. He graduated and now works in Beijing. One day, he mentioned on WeChat that if I come to Beijing for an internship, I should let him know and he would treat me to a meal. Now I am interning in Beijing and even posted it on my moments, and he liked it, so he must know that I have come to Beijing, but he hasn't asked me out. Was he just being polite? Or does he really want to meet? He has already graduated and I will graduate next year, so our paths will cross less in the future. If we don't meet in Beijing this time, we may never have a chance to meet again, and there will be no reason to keep in touch. I care a lot about this. But because we have only met once, I don't even remember what he looks like anymore. Perhaps I am insignificant to him, or maybe he didn't wait for me to contact him? Did he never consider me a friend and forget about me? Should I reach out to him and meet for the second time, or never contact him again? It's because we don't have much interaction in real life, but enjoy chatting online, that I feel so disappointed. I have a very unreal feeling, and it makes me very uncomfortable.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friendship, deceiving and trust.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I received your invitation to answer your question. Thank you for trusting me! Based on your description, I can tell that you have a strong liking for this older student. As you mentioned, you care a lot about his reaction towards you. I can sense that you have developed some sort of emotional dependence on him and may have some ambiguous feelings. However, you have been restraining yourself because you know he has a girlfriend. You can only maintain boundaries and distance, but you can't control your inner desires. Deep down, you hope to be different in his eyes. You wish that he would also care and value you. It is because of these expectations that you feel so disappointed and conflicted, right? I strongly suggest that you take the initiative to invite him out and openly tell him that you are in Beijing, allowing him to show hospitality. Because he already knows that you are here. There could be various reasons why he didn't invite you to dinner, such as being polite or not being able to judge the situation well, or maybe he's afraid of rejection, etc. By taking the initiative and observing his reaction, especially during the meal, it will help you dispel many illusions and see the truth. Regardless of what the truth may be, it will allow you to not keep yourself hanging in the air, unsure of how to proceed, and enable you to have a grounded understanding of what's next. This will be particularly helpful for you in dealing with your relationship. Otherwise, your heart will be left hanging, and all sorts of assumptions and speculations will not only make you suffer but also create misunderstandings. You won't know how to interact with him next. Be bold and make the appointment, bravely face the truth. Good luck to you, young lady.

From what you've described, it seems like he was not only helping you but you also had some small expectations of him, right? As you mentioned, he has a girlfriend, so he politely declined your invitation. Actually, I think this kind of guy is really good. He knows how to set boundaries when interacting with the opposite sex. He doesn't want other girls to have expectations or misunderstandings because he has a girlfriend. What do you think? When he said he would treat you to a meal in Beijing, it could either be a sincere offer or just a polite remark. Only he knows for sure. If you just post something on your social media, it could be seen as a hint. But to be honest, hints don't work for everyone, especially for a guy who already has a girlfriend. It might be even less effective. Now that you are in Beijing, if you really want to meet him or just want to thank him, you can boldly invite him: "Senior, I'm in Beijing. I would like to treat you and your girlfriend to a meal. Are you available?" I don't know what will happen next, but at least it's better than just thinking about it here. What do you think?

question: Fantasizing about being great, forcing oneself, feeling pain and discomfort, what should I do?
description: Recently, I feel like I'm pressuring myself again. Fantasizing about being really good at everything. Quick and not falling behind. I think the training instructors are weak, nobody listens to them, and their efficiency is too low, I can't stand it. If it were me, I would do better, I would do this and that. I want to read a new novel, but I keep forcing myself to read the old one. I want to read this one, but I keep forcing myself to read that one. This week, I want to try a few more counselors on campus, but I'm afraid the teachers will recognize me, so I force myself to think about whether to go or not and tell myself to hold on. I want to eat this, but I tell myself to hold on. It feels really uncomfortable not being able to do whatever I want to do like before. It's like I'm pressuring myself. The counselor couldn't make calls during military training, and I kept looking for and switching to a suitable counselor. I can't open up to my mom. I try to please others, I don't want to take photos but I still do. Is a career counselor the same as a counselor? Can I trust them? Can I switch again? Will the five counselors in the counseling department discuss this student and talk about me? When they see me, will they tell her that I'm doing fine? In my previous appointment, I switched to another counselor. I didn't say hello to her and I'm afraid she'll recognize me. What exactly do I want? I still feel so miserable. I can't do what I want. What do I want to read? Why do I end up not having time to read what I really want to read?

answers.answer_text: Title, good evening. The stream of consciousness-like words can be a bit confusing, but let's break it down. Let's reflect on what makes us overwhelmed. In my opinion, it's caring too much. What does it mean to care too much? Take insomnia as an example. When a person has insomnia, the more they resist it and ask themselves, "What should I do? How can I fall asleep? Why can't I sleep? How did I end up like this?" The more they fight against it, the more difficult it becomes to fall asleep. Instead, we can try thinking like this: everything is fine, everything is the best arrangement. No matter what we have experienced before, in this moment, right now, we exist in our own breath. Isn't every breath we take real? In each breath, we feel our own existence, which brings us a sense of peace, ease, and the growing realization that we can be accepted, understood, and perceived. When our sense of peace, ease, acceptance, understanding, and perception merge with ourselves, we become authentic, regardless of what we have experienced before. With that said, the world and I love you!

question: There are six people in the dormitory who are suffering from insomnia and physical exhaustion due to one person snoring.
description: I am currently a college student and I can't sleep at night because my roommate snores. I am extremely sensitive to it, especially my clinical friend. It really messes with my mind. Even though other roommates snore loudly, I can still fall asleep. But when he snores, I am very sensitive to it. Of course, the other roommates don't snore all night, only he snores loudly all night long. And as soon as he lies on the pillow, he starts snoring. In our daily lives, our relationship seems fine on the surface, but deep down I really dislike his snoring and remember his character because of it. I am mentally and physically exhausted because of his snoring, and I don't want to interact with him anymore. Sometimes he says he tries to avoid snoring but it doesn't work. What kind of psychological problem is this? How can I overcome it?

answers.answer_text: Hello, [it is indeed uncomfortable to hear someone snoring while trying to sleep]. Snoring, as we know, is primarily caused by physiological factors and is beyond our control. Therefore, even if the person tries to avoid snoring, it may not work. It's similar to the situation when we urgently need to use the restroom in important occasions. Even though we tell ourselves that it's not appropriate to leave at that moment, the feeling of needing to use the restroom is something we cannot control. The solution is either to change the other person or change ourselves. Firstly, changing dorms is one option. It could be either the other person changing dorms or ourselves. If we have both choices, I believe everyone would prefer the other person to change, but we know that it is often more difficult than changing ourselves. Secondly, behavior change. Similarly, there are two directions: changing the other person or changing ourselves. Encourage our roommate to see a doctor and explore treatment options. If the other person cannot be cured, we can only change ourselves by wearing earplugs or using sleep aids before going to bed. [If a specific roommate not only snores but also manipulates, and these two things make you unable to bear it and not want to deepen the relationship.] Since you don't want to deepen the relationship, what is preventing you from implementing your ideas? What benefits does maintaining this superficial relationship have for you? Sometimes we cannot be honest with ourselves and have consistent words and actions, often because such behavior brings us benefits. When we were young, adults often took us to visit relatives and we were expected to greet them. However, sometimes when we didn't want to greet a certain relative, we felt conflicted internally. Why? It's because there was a contradiction between not wanting to greet them and the expectation from the adults. In the end, we still greeted them to show politeness. This has a benefit of maintaining the image of being a "polite child," and adults would praise us, which is a form of reward. Looking back on these childhood experiences now as adults, if we don't seek praise from adults, would we still feel conflicted and be able to respect ourselves more? Some may think that it's easy to say but difficult to do. And this is indeed the case. But change has never been an easy task, has it? Best wishes! Karen.

Hello, the problem of snoring is not something that the person can control once they fall asleep, you can only adjust yourself. I am also a very light sleeper, once I hear any snoring, going to the bathroom, or walking sounds, I immediately wake up and can't fall back asleep. There was even a time when I heard the washing machine downstairs doing laundry in the middle of the night, so my sleep quality is really poor. Later on, I started wearing earplugs, and they did have some effect. You can also try using earplugs or other sleep aid products to help you resist the interference. Generally, snoring is caused by some problems in the respiratory tract, so you can regard your roommate as a patient and be considerate, which should help a little bit.

Hello, snoring is indeed very annoying, especially when you're in a bad mood and have to listen to it all night long, it can really drive you crazy. The original poster mentioned that they are not very sensitive to other classmates' snoring, but they feel extremely annoyed by this person's snoring. They also mentioned that they feel repulsed by him because he is calculative. Perhaps it is this aspect that intensifies their aversion towards his snoring. For example, let's say your annoyance towards snoring is a 1, and let's say you find this person irritating, their snoring might amplify the annoyance to an 8. Maybe the original poster is bothered by some of this person's characteristics, such as his calculating behavior. 1. Klein, a famous psychology expert, believes that we are all born with good and bad qualities, and in order to avoid experiencing our own bad qualities, we project them onto others. For example, in early years, we project those qualities onto our mother, like biting her nipple while breastfeeding, etc. In order to avoid facing our own bad qualities, we use a split defense mechanism to believe that these bad qualities don't belong to us, but to others. This pattern or psychological motivation still exists in adults, it just presents itself in a different way. We project the parts of ourselves that we cannot accept onto others. For example, if you cannot accept your own calculating nature, you attribute that bad quality to others and dislike them to defend yourself from experiencing that aspect of yourself. I don't know if there is anyone in your life who is calculating. 2. Another theory is that in our relationship with our parents, they have many expectations of us or respond to us in a strict manner, such as asking us to be generous and kind to others and to give away all the good things to others. In order to win their love, we start to mold ourselves according to their expectations and gradually internalize a superego that wants to be a generous person and not to be calculating. However, it is in human nature to take advantage of others, and each of us has this quality, but it has been repressed in you. When you encounter a person who is calculating, your superego comes out and you dislike them. Actually, what you dislike is what your heart desires. It's just that you are not able to express it due to the experiences from earlier years. These are different explanations from psychology. The original poster can reflect on themselves. Of course, it is completely fine to distance yourself from people you don't like. There's no need to make yourself uncomfortable. You can also talk to them and express your feelings or listen to others' opinions about them. Disliking someone is not a bad thing; it can serve as an opportunity for self-reflection and personal growth. Every person we encounter can be our benefactor and help us become a better version of ourselves.

question: Is my roommate coughing at the same time as me an attack on me?
description: Why do my roommate and classmates stare at me? Whenever I speak, they cough. They even change their ringtone to match mine. If I make a movement, they do the same. I can't figure out what I have done to offend them. They always sit behind me in class, and whenever I pick up a pen or a book, they cough loudly. They cough frequently, but why does their cough always coincide with my actions? Am I just "lucky"? How should I handle this situation?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and tensions, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello! First, I can empathize with the issue you're experiencing. At your age, you may still be going through adolescence and seeking identity, so it's normal to care about whether your peers accept you. Humans have a need for connection, so your inner longing is completely understandable. Second, it seems like your roommates are imitating your behavior, actions, habits, and even interests. This may leave you feeling confused. Looking at it from a positive perspective, perhaps they appreciate and admire you, which is why they imitate you. Third, from a negative angle, they might be jealous or engaging in what you perceive as subtle attacks. If that's the case, we need to analyze what might have led to your roommates' unfriendly treatment. Fourth, it's possible that you stand out in the group, receiving affirmation and favor from teachers. This might cause others to feel psychologically inferior, thus leading to their oppositional emotions and the behaviors described in your post. Fifth, perhaps you are somewhat sensitive? Their actions might not be directed solely at you; maybe they find it enjoyable to behave this way. After all, young people seek excitement and novelty in their actions, which is perfectly normal. Sixth, regardless of which analysis holds more truth, the bottom line is you should communicate and connect with them, clearing up any misunderstandings. You can also try to integrate into their circle, or even if you do not wish to be with them, find your own group where you share common interests. Birds of a feather flock together, as they say. Seventh, humans are social animals, especially at your current stage when identity recognition is important. Therefore, it's meaningful for you to actively engage in communication, cooperation, sharing, and acquiring a sense of belonging within the group.

question: Is my boyfriend considered to have a tendency for violence? Please answer this question directly.
description: My boyfriend jokes with me and says things like "I really want to kick your butt" and "I'll knock out your teeth," etc. In the past, during our most intense arguments, I would push him and pinch him, but he never fought back and let me hit him. When I asked him why he was glaring at me, he replied, "I'm restraining myself from hitting you." When I pressed him further, asking if he ever wanted to hit me, he got angry and said he did, but when I pushed him again, he said he didn't. (He already had scars from when I scratched him.) Occasionally, when I insult him, he will playfully make a gesture like he wants to hit me, but when I ask him what he's doing, he immediately stops. In fact, he has never hurt me, but I often pinch him and leave scars all over his body. When we argue and he doesn't respond to my messages, he calls me several times. One night, when I wanted to leave home without wearing warm clothes, I hit him countless times, but he pulled me back and stopped me from getting off the elevator. In a previous incident, when I said it hurt and asked him to let me go, he didn't release my arm immediately, and it hurt for a long time. There was another time when I hit his face with a blanket, and he warned me by poking me with his finger. I always worry. I have a very strong desire for control and feel that he must listen to me and do things according to my thoughts. I often say to him, "Are you going to do it or not? Are you going to listen or not?" Every time, he just clenches his fists and gets angry. Therefore, I want to know if he has a tendency towards violence.

answers.answer_text: Hello, title owner. We meet again. I saw that you asked a question before about whether your boyfriend has a tendency for violence, and I replied to it. But it seems that you haven't resolved your doubts and still want to figure out whether your boyfriend does have a tendency for violence. The definition of a tendency for violence is: "a trait of certain individuals who tend to solve problems with force and violence. They believe that reasoning and persuasion are unnecessary. Their worldview may be influenced by their unique upbringing, life experiences, peer influence, and so on. Previous violent behavior has given them an advantage in interpersonal relationships, making them feel superior and successful, thus reinforcing their ongoing and escalating tendency for violence." People with a tendency for violence generally exhibit the following behaviors: 1. Poor emotional control, easily getting angry and verbally abusing others even over minor issues; 2. Engaging in violent behavior before marriage, expressing anger through throwing and smashing objects; 3. Frequently getting into conflicts and using violence to show off in their daily life. They feel no shame in their violent actions, but rather take pride in them; 4. Cruelty towards animals, lack of empathy; 5. Always shifting blame onto others and refusing to admit their own mistakes; 6. Engaging in verbal violence, often preceding physical violence; 7. Fantasizing about harming others in their daily life. Based on these behaviors, you can assess whether your boyfriend fits the criteria for having a tendency for violence. In fact, many answerers, myself included, have provided you with reasonable analysis and explanations in response to your previous questions. Many of us believe that your boyfriend's behavior is just him defending his boundaries, but it seems that this still hasn't dispelled your suspicions about whether he has a tendency for violence. Seeing your question raised again today, I think we can work on the concept of "tendency for violence." Here are some questions for you to consider: 1. What do you associate with the term "tendency for violence"? How is it connected to your upbringing experiences? My personal speculation is that in your upbringing, one of your caregivers displayed a tendency for violence. Perhaps you have suffered from violence yourself or witnessed others experiencing it. That has made you highly sensitive to violent behavior, always on the lookout for signs of a tendency for violence. For example, if your boyfriend jokingly says, "I really want to kick your butt," or "I'll knock out your teeth if you keep laughing," you would associate these remarks with a tendency for violence. Pay attention to the fact that you might treat your thoughts as reality. Just because someone has violent thoughts in their mind doesn't mean they will actually act on them. You can distinguish between what is imagined and what is real. When you find yourself lost in thoughts again, try bringing yourself back to the present moment and observe the reality around you. 2. From your recent similar questions, I have a feeling that you hope to hear the answer: yes, your boyfriend does have a tendency for violence. So, imagine if I were to tell you, "Yes, based on your description, your boyfriend does indeed have a tendency for violence," how would you feel? Would you feel a sense of "I knew it, he is exactly the person I thought he was. I was right!"? And do you feel scared, but also a slight satisfaction of "I got it right"? If you have these feelings, it is highly likely that you are repeating a childhood pattern. As I mentioned earlier, during your upbringing, there was an important caregiver with a tendency for violence, and your behaviors towards your boyfriend are largely learned from this caregiver's behavior. On the other hand, you also feel worried and afraid, afraid that your boyfriend is really that kind of person. Another aspect is that you don't fully accept your own actions. If your boyfriend is the same as you, maybe you would feel a little better. It's important to recognize that the past and the present are completely different, and the person you faced in the past is not the same as the person you face now. Our internal relationship patterns can also be corrected through real-world experiences. If conditions allow, you can seek help from a professional counselor. There are many details worth exploring, and a professional counselor can provide you with more systematic and comprehensive assistance. That is my answer, and I hope it helps you. Best wishes to you.

Hello there, it's evident that you are genuinely concerned about whether your boyfriend has a violent tendency or not, and in order to confirm your suspicions, you have done things that have affected your relationship. Hugs to you. I'm curious to know why you have such a nearly paranoid level of concern about your boyfriend's violent tendencies. Can you please explain the reason behind this? When did this worry begin? Is it because your father had serious violent tendencies and harmed you and your mother? Or is it because you witnessed such examples around you? Or perhaps it's due to the negative news about domestic violence that you've come across online recently, which affects your trust in intimate relationships? It is true that there are people with violent tendencies, but we shouldn't let that stop us, right? Traffic accidents happen every day, and cars on the road may have issues, but we don't choose to never ride in a car because there might be a potential accident. What we need to do is take preventive measures. How can we do that? First, we make sure to regularly maintain our vehicles. Second, when driving, we follow traffic rules and drive carefully. And lastly, if problems occur, we prioritize our own safety. Perhaps this is a bit off-topic because what you want is a clear answer about whether the other person has violent tendencies. Unfortunately, I can't definitively answer that question. From your current description, it can be said with certainty that he doesn't have violent tendencies. However, if you continue to try to test and validate in this way, it's not impossible that this may change in the future. In your description, you mentioned, "He has never hurt me, but I often pinch him and leave him covered in bruises." Perhaps you both deeply love each other, so in the face of you hitting him, arguing with him, and even sometimes demonstrating cold violence (actually, it seems like you are the one with violent tendencies), both of you silently endure and tolerate it. And you may just lack a sense of security, which is why you repeatedly need to verify whether he has violent tendencies. In psychology, there is a common phenomenon called "self-fulfilling prophecy," where when you have a certain suspicion, you unconsciously act according to that suspicion, eventually making it come true. Perhaps, instead of discussing whether your boyfriend has violent tendencies here, what you really need to do is open up to your boyfriend and honestly express your true thoughts, share your concerns and insecurities, and communicate your boundaries. It is truly not easy for two people to meet, get to know each other, and fall in love, so why not cherish the person right in front of you? However, if he does exhibit violent behavior and hurt you, it is crucial to leave immediately. Best wishes, and remember that the world and I love you.

No, I have not. I see that other respondents have given you a textbook standard. You can refer to it again. Based on your description, it seems more like you are testing, or even trying to gather evidence, to prove that he has violent tendencies. This is actually very dangerous. Even a person who originally did not have violent tendencies is very likely to behave as you expect under such suggestions. The result is likely that a person who normally does not have violent tendencies when with others suddenly exhibits violent behavior while conducting these tests. When he does not exhibit violent behavior, you will continue to suspect, but once he does, you will feel relieved instead. There is a relaxed feeling of "I knew you were this kind of person." Do you also have this kind of suspicion with previous partners? Is your anxiety and unease solely because of this person's appearance? Or are you familiar with this sense of insecurity? Have you had similar feelings in your childhood?

Honey, hugs and kisses to you. I see that you have some confusion in your intimate relationship. In your description, you mentioned that your boyfriend sometimes makes jokes about hurting you verbally. But during the most intense fights, he never fights back physically, only using eye contact and gestures to imply things. Normally, he allows you to hit him and even frequently ends up covered in scars because of you. The only time he physically stopped you was when you were trying to leave home in the middle of the night without warm clothes. To determine if he has a tendency for violence, first see if he has actually harmed you or had the intention to harm you but failed. This can be judged from your life together. Also, in the instance when he didn't let go of your arm, causing you pain, you can think about whether his intention was to hold onto you or to hurt you. I would also like to share my own perspective. Love is a mutual experience, involving the feelings and actions of both parties. If you want to hit him, you should be prepared for him to fight back; otherwise, you should try to communicate more calmly in your daily life. If your boyfriend has always been in a suppressed state, playing the role of being "hit," it's hard to say if, when it accumulates to a certain extent, he will give it all back to you. Lastly, you have also realized that you have a strong desire for control. You can also put yourself in his shoes and consider if your boyfriend treated you this way, would you also clench your fists in anger? Or would you have other more extreme behaviors? I hope this can help you. The world and I love you~.

Hello, he doesn't have it, but you seem to be fostering this violent tendency in him. If he later exhibits violent behavior, you have contributed to it and cultivated it. Just like you mentioned your "strong desire for control," when you assume your boyfriend has violent tendencies, you will also try to control yourself and induce your boyfriend to conform to your suspicions of his violent tendencies. This is clearly about your own anxiety and self-control issues. Your anxiety makes you want to control. When you feel like you may have gained control and your anxiety subsides slightly, you will observe even more potential risks and possibilities, which will deepen your anxiety and make you want to take even more control. Unfortunately, control cannot eliminate anxiety, so it can only increase in the constant pursuit of control. This is a vicious cycle. To a certain extent, you may prefer mutual destruction rather than letting your suspicions escape your control. Lastly, attempting to gain a sense of security by controlling others is unrealistic, and facing your own internal anxiety requires great courage and the ability to face the pain of losing control. Both are not easy, but it seems easier to control others than to face oneself.

Title Owner, hello In my opinion, your boyfriend does not have a tendency towards violence, and I feel that the sudden violence from you is unexpected. Violence is a trait of a certain type of person, who tends to use force to solve problems and resort to violence easily. They may believe that using reason and morality to persuade others is unnecessary. Their worldview may be shaped by their unique upbringing, life experiences, the influence and persuasion of friends and parties, etc. Previous acts of violence have given them an advantage in interpersonal relationships, making others feel afraid, submissive, and in awe, which gives them a sense of superiority and achievement, thus reinforcing their continued and escalated violence. The definition clearly states that people with a tendency towards violence tend to use force to solve problems and resort to violence! But your boyfriend is not like that. Instead, he cares about you. The only time he caused you pain was because he wanted to keep you. You mentioned that you have a strong desire for control and have used force on your boyfriend many times! I suggest you can seek professional counseling️, hoping it can help you.

Hello, friend. At least from your description, I don't feel that your boyfriend can be considered to have a violent tendency. Although he admits to having thoughts of using physical force during arguments with you, before focusing on his reactions, please first reflect on your own behavior. Think carefully, have you used language and actions to provoke and irritate him? But why do you keep provoking him? I believe no one likes to be treated violently, so of course you don't want your boyfriend to have this tendency. And the reason why you keep wanting to confirm this matter is most likely because you want to prove that you are loved and cherished, or in other words, you are afraid of losing him. How can you express your value to someone or something important to you in the long run? Of course, by cherishing it. Since you keep testing him and he keeps accommodating you, I would like to congratulate you: you have found a man who loves you. Now, you can confidently go and be good to him. This way, your relationship will enter a virtuous cycle, and you will become happier and happier. Yes, that's right. Don't worry, love is by your side and between the two of you.

I can understand your complex feelings, and your relationship seems to be very difficult. ● Currently, there is no indication of violent tendencies from him. ● However, currently does not mean there will never be, and with your current behavior of physical aggression, even someone with a good temper may develop violent tendencies because of your training. ● Whether it is for self-protection or for the sake of your relationship, please try to be more gentle with him. Resorting to physical violence will not solve any problem and may also harm yourself.

question: My parents' strained relationship makes me feel anxious all the time, and I'm afraid of becoming depressed.
description: When I was a child, my parents often fought. My father, when he was young, liked to play mahjong and often stole money from my mother. He even hit my mother in front of me, although it only happened once or twice. He had a very bad temper, and it was difficult to communicate with him about everyday things. He would explode in anger, especially with my mother, although he treated me relatively well. My mother also had many problems. She did not respect my father and was too dominant. When she was young, she had another lover (I caught them together, but I don't know if my father knows). Since I was young, I have often heard my mother say all sorts of bad things about my father, saying that he had no money and did not care about the family. She would also include me in denouncing my father's faults, as if that was her way of seeking recognition. After enduring my school years, I left home, but now, because I am pregnant and expecting a baby, I have to live with my parents again. I feel that their relationship is still not good, with discord between their words and their hearts. A few years ago, my father had another lover, but that may have ended, although they definitely don't want to divorce anymore, especially since my mother found out. Whenever my mother calls my father, I get nervous, feeling that she is actually trying to monitor him. Sometimes, when the call ends, she calls again after half an hour. Sometimes, just a few words from them can start a fight. Thinking about having to listen to this kind of argument in recent years, I am afraid I will develop postpartum depression because of my parents...
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parental communication

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a hug. From your description, I can understand that 1. Your parents have a strained relationship, and you have been living in this kind of family atmosphere since you were young, which makes you uncomfortable. 2. Now that you are pregnant, you have to live with your parents, and you are worried that the tense atmosphere caused by their relationship will lead to depression. [A little analysis and advice] 1. Living in such an environment, whether you are pregnant or not, is not good for your physical health. But since you have been living with your parents since childhood, you have some understanding of their relationship, which means you can prepare yourself mentally in advance. In your daily life, especially recently, don't suppress your thoughts. If you don't want to hear your parents speak ill of each other in front of you, refuse them, or talk to your husband and other friends about these troubles. Expressing your feelings can help relieve your mood. 2. fundamentally, changing this situation requires communication with your parents. After all, they are your parents. Sit down and have a talk with them. Express to them that "I need to maintain a calm mood during my pregnancy. The conflicts in the family may harm the child. I hope that my parents can temporarily avoid arguments during this period, just for the sake of your daughter." Your parents will probably be willing to accept this. I hope this helps.

question: At the age of 18, what should I do when my will to live becomes increasingly low? How can I carry on?
description: 18 years old, the situation has been on and off for four years. I have self-harmed by cutting my wrist, attempted suicide by taking a large quantity of pills twice, have low appetite, slow reaction, easily irritable and anxious, and sometimes unable to recognize my own emotions for a longer period of time. The reasons mainly relate to academics, family origin, and relationships. It seems that I have lost my awe for death, as in a recent suicide attempt, I swallowed over forty antidepressant pills, vomited throughout the night and the following day, received oxygen and intravenous therapy for three days, but didn't tell the doctor or family that I wanted to die. When taking the pills, I felt no fear, no regret, just a very calm feeling, perhaps even a sense of relief. I also know that there is a high probability that I won't die, but the consequences of swallowing the pills have further weakened my already fragile digestive system and liver function, and I think to myself, even if I can live one day less, it might be better. The reason I want to seek help is because I can still perceive that tiny bit of will to live deep inside of me. I'm currently having trouble breathing all day long, have no desire to move, eat, drink, or communicate. Occasionally, I pinch myself to make sure I can still feel, and when I'm irritable, I hit the wall hard to numb myself. I often lie by the window and watch the road, repeatedly thinking about the possibility of ending my own life. But I don't want to disrupt other people's lives. Perhaps I still want to see what the sky looks like at nineteen. So, I'm reaching out for help. How can I continue on?
keywords: Treatment, mental crisis, psychological counseling, sharing and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the problem you mentioned has been going on for four years, which is indeed not a short period of time. During this time, have you considered seeking professional psychological help? When we have physical problems, we usually know to see a doctor. Diseases don't just disappear by toughing it out. However, when it comes to mental issues, we often think that we might be overthinking or just need to be more open-minded, and that as long as we make an effort to adjust ourselves or give it some time, everything will be fine. But in reality, mental problems, just like physical problems, also require professional treatment. By trying to endure it and delaying seeking help, the problem will only become more serious. You can feel that deep inside, you still have the will to live. So why not consider seeing a psychologist and seeking professional help? There are two forces struggling within you right now: one side wants to die, while the other wants to live. It's like driving a car and simultaneously stepping on the gas and the brake, causing the car to consume a lot of energy. Our inner selves are also enduring such torment. Go see a doctor, they may be able to help alleviate your current suffering and reduce the desire to die. Believe that you will see the sky of being nineteen! Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

I can feel that you are very gentle. Life always allows us to endure some painful injuries in the best years of our lives, in order to achieve growth. We can try to have a little hope for the future, even just a little bit. In case one day in the future you win a big prize and splurge on yourself, or in case someone patient appears in your life and makes it beautiful, or at the very least, in case a medicine is developed that can relieve the pain of death, we can rely on our imagination to get through our lives. We don't know what will happen in the next ten or twenty years, right? You already have a calm mindset towards death, and I believe you will be able to live calmly, even if only as an observer of this world. It's okay to be carefree, as long as you pass the days without any worries, simply watching from a distance.

question: My child actually dared to hit me? I feel like such a failure as a human being.
description: I am 26 years old, divorced, and have a 5-year-old child who has been with me since he was little. Today, he had a little disagreement with me over something trivial and refused to admit his mistake. When his grandmother got angry and threw away his drink, he became even more upset and immediately started hitting his grandmother. I rushed over and even got hit myself. Oh my goodness, is this still my son? At such a young age, he dares to hit me. I was so angry and upset that I ended up hitting him too. He hit me even harder. I never had the heart to hit him too hard, but I am truly devastated. Have I spoiled him too much? I don't think so, but why does he have this terrible habit of not admitting his mistakes and hitting elders? When he has conflicts with other children outside, he doesn't have the courage, but at home, he behaves like this. I am really angry and crying. I feel like I have failed as a person. What have I raised?
keywords: Family, Growth process, Communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: Hello there. Seeing your words is like seeing you in person. First, let me give you a warm hug, and I hope my answer can help you. First of all, dear, I truly understand you because I have a relative who is in a similar situation as your child. He is 6 years old and currently being fostered in my home. He can be quite aggressive, and when he has conflicts with my brother, he will try to hit him hard, saying things like "I want to kill you." So based on my relative's situation and your description, let me analyze what might be behind your son's behavior. Despite being young, he has matured emotionally due to his unique family structure. Just like my relative, who is 6 years old but becomes quiet whenever his mother is mentioned and doesn't allow anyone to bring her up. Sometimes, when he hurts my brother badly, and my mom gets angry and tells him to leave, he starts acting pitiful, saying things like "my mom... my dad... my grandma is old and has nowhere to go." You see, he is only 6 years old, but he knows exactly what's happening in his family. So, I think your son is also aware of the absence of his father and this family structure, and it might contribute to his early rebellious behavior. Perhaps, in his heart, he holds resentment towards you and his grandmother, and he blames you for his lack of a father figure. Just like you said, you love your son, so you can't bring yourself to hit him. Could it be that his violent behavior towards you is a way to vent his hatred? How to solve this? If he truly holds resentment towards this family, you need to sit down with him and have a good talk, looking into his eyes. Ask him, "Son, do you not like Mom? What is it that you don't like about Mom? Tell me, and Mom will make changes." Additionally, children from divorced families are naturally more sensitive than average children, so you should pay more attention to caring for him and making him feel loved. Of course, there is a difference between caring and spoiling. You need to teach him the right values and ask him about his thoughts and feelings, rather than assuming that you know what love should be and imposing it on him. Also, every child is like a blank canvas when they are born. How did he learn to hit others? Have you or his grandmother ever hit him before? I want to say that violence towards children is highly inappropriate and should be completely eliminated in this modern era. In your future interactions, regardless of what happens, you must calmly and rationally explain things to your child. Absolutely no hitting. And in your description, you mentioned how "his grandmother gets angry and throws away his drink." You see, this is a very rough approach! If you treat your child like this in every aspect of life whenever you're angry, how can the child feel loved? Don't just think about the child, even for an adult, hurting them once cannot be offset by 100 instances of what you think is being good to them. So, once again, remember to handle things calmly and rationally, and make sure to be gentle and let him feel loved. I hope this helps resolve your issue. Good luck!

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. [Question] 1) The child physically assaulted their grandmother and mother - a small conflict escalated when the grandmother threw away the child's drink. 2) The child refuses to admit when they've done something wrong - in front of many people, the child conflicts with their mother and refuses to compromise or surrender. [My analysis] 1) The child's rebellious attitude may be related to behaviors exhibited by the parents. As elders, we should better understand the child's true needs. When the grandmother spilled the child's drink over a small matter, the child naturally felt bullied and wanted to protect themselves. This may require further understanding from the original poster about the changes in the child's personality traits and the underlying causes. 2) The child refusing to admit their mistakes and retaliating after being assaulted could be related to experiences they've encountered while growing up. For example, if they feel a lack of presence when interacting with other children, they may seek attention at home. Therefore, regardless of whether it's a good or bad way, as long as it captures the parents' attention, they will continue doing it. What we need to do is correct the child's behavior and address the issues. [My suggestions] 1) Communicate timely and understand the child's situation. Abnormal behavior from children is always rooted in a reason. To understand these reasons, it is necessary to communicate with the child and comprehend their issues and emotions. If direct communication is not possible, talking with the child's friends or teachers can also provide insight into their true needs. 2) Lead by example through actions. Sometimes, as elders, we just tell the child what they can or cannot do. However, children often have resistance in their minds. What the original poster needs to do is to be respectful to the child and persuade them with reason. By creating a positive atmosphere, the child will naturally want to emulate it. 3) Reevaluate parenting styles by observing the child's behavior. For example, if the original poster sees the child physically assaulting the grandmother and then tries to educate them but ends up being assaulted themselves, they need to reflect on their own parenting style and make adjustments accordingly. This requires gradual exploration by the original poster. 4) Approach conflicts with a good attitude and ease the atmosphere. When conflicts arise with the child, it is important to avoid shouting, as it will only lead to two outcomes: the child crying loudly or the child becoming more defiant. If the original poster adopts a gentle attitude, the child will naturally feel that it is not appropriate to raise their voice, and the conflicts between them will diminish. This will prevent embarrassing situations from happening in public. Educating the younger generation is a challenging task, and the path to success is long and winding. In the process of raising children, we are also scrutinizing ourselves. Growing and progressing together with our children is truly wonderful. I wish you the best.

As the mother who is closest to the child, who cares the most and loves the child the most, when the child speaks harsh words or even uses physical force against oneself, there is shock, grievance, anger, and even a sense of shame toward oneself. So many complex emotions flood the heart when facing one's own mother. You hope the child will become better, hope the child's growth will be more solid. As a single mother, you have made a lot of sacrifices and have been trying to think about how to provide better parenting for your child. You and your child are currently facing some difficulties, so let's see if the following can provide you with some inspiration: A five-year-old child is in a phase where some self-awareness is just beginning to emerge, a "rebellious period". They start to have their own thoughts and even try to express their own emotions. A five-year-old child may not yet fully understand how their emotional expression can affect others and how others will react. That's why they usually start trying to express their emotions and feelings with the people closest to them. By expressing their emotions to you, in a way, it is their way of showing that they see your relationship as one they can trust. Children of this age may not always be able to verbalize their emotions and feelings, and their inability to do so can make them very angry. When they are unable to express their anger verbally, children are more likely to express it through physical gestures. So, as the child gradually enters the process of socialization, you can try expressing yourself to them in this way: "Mom knows you're very angry, you're angry because of ****" (give them feedback and help them articulate their current emotions), "But when you hit Mom, it hurts. Mom's body hurts, and Mom's heart hurts, because ***. I really hope we can ****, can we?" In divorced families, children are more likely to be influenced by the family structure itself and may exhibit some temporary personality deviations. As for yourself, you probably have a strong desire for independence and self-reliance, and you may hope that your child can have a more complete environment in which to grow, etc. These beautiful wishes will also to some extent impact your child, and you may also have some expectations placed on your child. For both you and your child, these are very difficult things. The child is just a child, continuously growing, and many so-called problems will "correct" themselves as they grow up. Lastly, don't set such high goals for yourself or put so much pressure on yourself. From your request for help, it's clear that you are such a responsible mother. Take good care of yourself, and the child will see your self-assurance and you both will get better and better.

Hello OP, as a young single mother, it must be tough for you. It's really not easy to persevere in the midst of external distractions. First of all, when things happen, I can sense the feelings of shame, surprise, doubt about self-education, love and unwillingness towards your son, and disappointment in your own heart. But there is no need to be disappointed or self-critical. Let your emotions flow freely and acknowledge that it was just a collision of emotions between the child and the adult at that moment. It's just a small matter, and it's enough for us to grow from it. But we can guide the child through it. You can carefully reflect on whether this is the first time the child has displayed such intense emotions or if this has happened before. What are the triggers behind each occurrence? Was it good food, fun activities? The child had needs that were not met, and so on. Based on your description, children from single-parent families may be more sensitive. We need to analyze the psychology behind the child's behavior. Have a deep conversation with the child, calmly and gently tell him: Darling, hitting mommy and grandma hurt us, and we were a bit sad. But I believe that such a sensible child must have a reason. Can you tell mommy what the reason is? In the future, no matter how angry or sad we are, we can always communicate first. Hitting someone can cause them harm, remember that. Slowly guide the child and let him experience different ways of handling emotions. We can then shift the perspective to ourselves. Why did the child's actions trigger so many emotions and disturbances in me? After divorce, did I put all the focus of my life on the child? Do I feel guilty and want to compensate him more? And what about myself? Have I neglected myself during this time and endured a lot of grievances? Do I want to make myself incredibly strong and capable, taking on experiences beyond my peers? And I want to say: it's okay. When life tests us, we can take it slowly. Being strong doesn't mean we have to be invulnerable and unshakeable. We can have moments of "fragility". Before being a "mother", you always belong to yourself. You can engage in things you like, and it won't affect you being a good mother in the least. Moreover, we can involve the child appropriately, letting him be a "little man" and saying: Mommy is tired, can the baby help mommy? Let him do some small things within his abilities and experience the role of a caregiver. Let yourself experience the feeling of "being taken care of", which can enhance your relationship. Help the child develop his abilities and relieve your sense of grievance. Slowly, there will be different changes. Finally... I hope that while being a mother, you don't forget to love yourself well.

I understand very well how difficult it is to be a mother. I am a mother myself and deeply feel its challenges. The growth of the child and the absence of the father is extremely irresponsible. Every woman was once a little girl and undergoes a transformation to become a mother. Only those who have experienced it deeply understand its difficulties. Who can share this sadness with me? When his grandmother got angry, she threw away his drink, which made him even more frustrated and immediately started hitting her. Is this the first time he has hit his grandmother? First of all, it is wrong to hit one's grandmother and it should be criticized. Similarly, in his understanding, the drink was his favorite and he was infuriated because his grandmother threw it away. This led to his act of violence. Throwing away his favorite drink is a rude and direct behavior, which requires reflection. How do we usually interact with children? He doesn't have much courage and still acts like this at home. I am really angry. Many children are like this because they know that their family loves and cares for them and will forgive them. They choose to be a child, express themselves, and be themselves in front of their family. He is already 5 years old, so I think it's time to reason with him. Children, even though they are small, can understand. I play a game with him to let him know that hitting hurts. When he hits me, I pretend to be in pain. Then he comes to hug me and says, "Mom, it doesn't hurt. I will protect you." On one hand, it teaches him that hitting hurts, and on the other hand, when he hits me, I hit him back to teach him that it's not okay to hit people, as they might hit back. The road of educating a child is long, so do not be impatient. The world and I love you.

In "Teacher Wang Xiao's 5 Lessons on Happiness", we can help identify these 4 incorrect ways of behavior based on the emotions displayed by the other person. In the case of conflict between a mother and her child, there is an explanation like this: The child says hurtful words to you, such as, "I hate you! You are a bad mother." My emotion: Hurt. Hurt feels like a sharp knife cutting through you. Similar emotions include disappointment, disbelief, and disgust. It is very likely that you have hurt him first, and he retaliates to find fairness. In your "hurt" emotion, you may think, "How can you treat me like this!" So, you retaliate, but the result is that he will escalate. His need: Fairness and justice. His password information: I have been treated unfairly, please acknowledge my feelings. Perhaps both of you are in a state of hurt, so you can first deal with the emotions. For example: Method - I just compared you to your sister, you must be hurt, I'm sorry! - You just said I am a bad mother, it really makes me sad because I love you so much. - Come, give me a hug! Love is connection, love is seeing. Ask yourself: What is his emotional password? Step one: What is my emotion? Step two: What is his need? Step three: Now that I know his password, what better way can I handle this?

Hahaha, congratulations, there is one thing you have succeeded in, he can express "I disagree with your actions or thoughts", but his language expression has not yet developed to an adult level. At least he has normal human emotional responses. What needs to be taught is the way to express dissatisfaction, of course, it is better for adults to correct their own way of expression to influence the child. Leading by example, we lack "leading by example".

After carefully reading your confession, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1. Why would the child physically hurt their grandma and you? The reason lies in your divorced family, where the child did not receive the fatherly love they should have. They say that a strict father and a kind mother are ideal. In this family, the child lacks the awe-inspiring presence of a father. As a result, they indulge their own temper, throwing tantrums and disrespecting elders. 2. Because of the divorced family, while other children receive their father's love, this child does not. It is inevitable to become an outsider among the children. When bullied, they would say, "I will tell my dad to beat you up." Other children have their fathers' protection, but this child does not. This creates an imbalance in their heart. Over time, it leads to a distorted inner world. 3. The law is impermanent, discussions subject to change, water has no fixed state, and the great Tao is natural. We should not overly control children. Control equals losing control. Control equals oppression. Oppression equals resistance. The accumulation of negative energy in their heart will eventually explode, leading to physical violence. In daily life, it is better to educate children through guidance. Clear rewards and punishments. Praise and reward for good behavior, criticism and punishment for bad behavior. Spend more time with children, play games with them, take them out for activities, and teach them lessons through practical experiences. Gradually guide them to establish the correct values. Thank you for your question. May the beauty of the world come to you as promised.

question: Isolated, irritable, unworthy of studying, unworthy of playing games, unworthy of living?
description: Clearly, when other people write down what they hear, they get everything right. But what about me? I make mistakes like a complete idiot, especially with the pronunciation symbols. My little sister can cry as much as she wants, but when I cry, I just get yelled at. It's obvious that she was the one scribbling on my paper, but she insists that it was me. Other people draw so nicely, their handwriting is so beautiful, while mine looks like crap. Well, fine, I don't deserve it. I don't deserve to study, play games, or even be alive. I'm just a worthless piece of trash.

answers.answer_text: Hello there *hug* After reading your message, it seems that besides feeling frustrated with studying, you are also troubled by the expectations and criticism from your parents as well as the comparisons between peers. 【Life has different colors】 You mentioned that you are not as good at drawing or writing as others, but everyone is unique. Just like how some people excel in painting and others in singing, each person has their own area where they can shine. Maybe you haven't discovered it yet, but don't worry. You can slowly cultivate your interests, and one day you might suddenly realize that there is something you can do really well. And you don't need to focus on comparing yourself with peers. What you truly need to surpass is yourself in the present. You can become more confident and more serious about studying. Your handwriting can become neater and more beautiful than before. 【Some suggestions】 1. Be more careful with your studies. Believe that you can listen closely and understand the teacher's requirements. Concentrate on doing one thing well, and if you haven't understood or remembered something, go over it a few more times. You will definitely make progress. 2. It's true that in life, parents tend to have stricter expectations for older children compared to younger ones. Sometimes parents may not fully understand the situation and blame the older child first because they subconsciously think that the older child is more sensible and mature and can better understand why they are angry. So, don't complain about your parents having higher expectations for you, because in their hearts, you are better than your sister. If your parents wrongly accuse you, you can explain the situation to them and believe that they will understand. 3. Younger children sometimes enjoy causing trouble. When your sister does something wrong next time, you can criticize her appropriately and tell her that it's not right. Also, inform your parents about the situation, so that your sister understands that doing something wrong will be criticized. Be more confident, smile at yourself, and bravely change yourself. I hope you can meet a better version of yourself. The little sun will always support you. Wishing you the best! The world and I love you.

You say you're worthless, and I understand that it hurts to say that, right? Maybe belittling yourself feels somewhat cathartic. But it's not fair to yourself. If you were truly worthless, you wouldn't be here asking questions. If you were truly worthless, you would have witnessed a miracle, because I have never seen a true worthless person, never. Only deceiving yourself, treating yourself unfairly, and being unwilling to accept yourself, reluctantly and painfully labeling yourself. That's not fair to yourself. From your brief question, my impression of you is that you are motivated, eager to improve, otherwise you wouldn't be here asking. You may not have done well on this dictation and even included the phonetic symbols, and you are unsatisfied with your performance this time. But this does not mean that you can't learn anything or do anything. You are not worthless. You said, "Even if my little sister cries, it's fine, but when I cry, I get scolded. Even though she clearly scribbled on my test paper, she said I did it." What I see here is that this incident made you feel very wronged. You can learn to be kind to yourself when you have already been misunderstood and wronged. Start with understanding yourself! You envy others for their beautiful drawings and handwriting. Your present may not be beautiful yet, but it is precisely because you have the ability to appreciate beauty and a pursuit of it that enables you to recognize the beauty in others' drawings and handwriting. This also tells me that you have the potential to do something slightly more beautiful than what you are doing now. Your expression of unworthiness, paired with the energy and vitality it brings behind it, inspires me to desire better for myself. I hope you can transform this sense of unworthiness into motivation for wanting to become a better version of yourself. Start by truly understanding and accepting yourself, and shape the path towards a better you! Just like a caterpillar, after going through difficult times, it transforms into a cicada and sings and dances on the branches. Keep going!

question: Eighth grader, recently feeling more and more tired, and even not sure what I should do.
description: Recently, all students are very busy, and I am no exception. It's fine in school, but every time I go home, I feel lost. My parents don't understand me and sometimes behave unreasonably. I understand that they are tired from work, but they always take out their anger on me. I really hate it. There have been many times when I felt like they were happy, but I had to pretend to be happy too, and when they were angry, I had to be their punching bag. My mom started working when I was in second grade, and her temper has always been unpredictable. From second to fourth grade, there was not a single day when I wasn't scolded. I love her, and I know she does it for my own good, but I really don't understand this. Even though I'm only in my second year of junior high, I understand a lot of things. I have thought about suicide more than once, and I feel like I'm too fragile, worrying about such trivial matters. But these emotions are really hard to control. My grades are above average, but I don't want to go to the best high school. I just want to go to a boarding school that is far away from home. I really want to leave this living environment as soon as possible. It's so exhausting. Will not going to the best high school mean being irresponsible to myself...
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: I sense from the description that you feel conflicted about your parents. You love them very much but have difficulty accepting some of their behaviors. This is a common situation, and it's important to remember that parents don't intend to act that way. They also love us, but sometimes they don't know how to handle certain situations, which leads them to unintentionally take out their frustrations on us. Based on your description, I can tell that you truly understand your parents, but you struggle with accepting their behavior towards you.
