Here are some suggestions: First, try to show more concern for your parents in your daily life. They are going through their own challenges, so try to approach their temper with understanding. However, this doesn't mean you should tolerate their behavior. You can have a candid conversation with your parents and gently point out the issues they have while explaining how their actions affect you. They love you and are likely to accept your feedback. Through your combined effort, you can find a solution that helps them find a suitable outlet for their frustrations while also resolving your current dilemma. Secondly, the desire you mentioned to distance yourself from your family is something I have also experienced before, and it is normal. However, running away cannot solve the problem. Even if you temporarily leave home, you will eventually have to return, and if the issues are not resolved, they may resurface and impact your relationship with your family. Lastly, remember that the ultimate decision is yours. Whether you choose to attend a prestigious high school or distance yourself from home, it's up to you to make the decision. You are already in eighth grade and becoming more of an adult. Take some time to think about the advantages and disadvantages of both options before making a decision. This is just my personal opinion, and I hope it can help you. Best wishes!

question: Because of some small things, I feel irritated, always wanting to get angry and throw things.
description: I always get irritated by small things and feel like throwing things. For example, when I'm cutting vegetables for lunch, I put them on the cutting board but they keep falling on the ground. Every time I pick one up, another one falls down. It's so frustrating and it makes me feel agitated. I even feel like throwing the cutting board.

answers.answer_text: Hug you ~ I can feel that you are already aware of your emotions, which is very good. At the same time, I hope you can do something to relax yourself, calm down, and accept your emotions. We know that emotions are a very instinctual energy in our lives. In the process of our growth, some emotions often cannot flow normally because our parents or the social culture we live in do not allow us to do so. For example, "No crying, I'll count to three", "It's nothing, stop throwing a tantrum", "You are being proud again, be humble"... Over time, we will feel that some emotions are inappropriate, so we suppress them and become more and more numb and dull. Meanwhile, some emotions become stronger and beyond our control. In other words, there is a inner child in each of us, and this inner child is those emotions we cannot face and suppress. These emotions accumulate in our bodies, making some people more emotionally unstable and others prone to illness... I recommend you to do some meditation exercises, relax yourself, empty your mind, and allow and trust yourself more. Allow yourself to open up, allow more people to come in, learn to accept yourself, and treat yourself well. I hope this can help you, good luck!

OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I can sense that the OP feels anxious about their "always irritable" emotions. First, the OP can take a deep breath and calm down. Regarding the irritable temper, it is easy for us to get trapped in such a "state of mind," just like the situation described by the OP. In the beginning, we may think that a small matter leads to a bad mood, which can also affect the next task and increase the chance of making mistakes. And making mistakes can further worsen our mood, creating a seemingly endless cycle. In this regard, the OP can try to temporarily stop their actions when faced with an irritable mood, take a deep breath, or listen to some relaxing music to calm down before proceeding with the task at hand. The same applies to other things, which can help us avoid compromising our efficiency due to being influenced by our emotions. Another method is to redirect our attention in a timely manner in order to relax our mood. When encountering something that may trigger irritation, try not to dwell on it and instead attempt to divert our attention elsewhere, engaging in activities such as deep breathing to regulate our emotions.

question: There are many people who have friends and no friends at the same time. They always have friends to do things with, but they are always alone.
description: A few days ago, I was diagnosed with depression at the hospital, but I realized that there were many things I didn't tell the doctor when I came back. Now I have two problems that are troubling me. Firstly, the doctor said that what I lack the most is care and attention, but there are people around me who are very good to me. However, the better they treat me, the more fearful and resistant I become towards them, especially when it comes to the opposite sex. Why is that? Secondly, I always have friends, but I often feel lonely when I do things alone. Why is that?

answers.answer_text: I think your two issues are actually one issue. There is a type of attachment called anxious-resistant attachment, which perfectly aligns with what you described and what the doctor mentioned about a lack of care and attention. As an aside, the treatment plan the doctor prescribed should involve medication and therapy. You can discuss all your issues with a therapist. Remember to take your medication on time. From a quote on Baidu: "An anxious-resistant child with insecure attachment appears 'distressed' when entering a playroom and shows relatively little interest in the new environment. They constantly worry about the whereabouts of their mother and feel extremely upset when she leaves. When the mother returns, they display ambivalent behavior, seeking contact and resisting contact, finding it difficult to calm down and exhibiting signs of unease and distress throughout the entire process. They do not actively approach strangers and show negative social adaptation." In scientific experiments and your work situation, it seems to fit perfectly, but I'm not sure if your inner state aligns with the case study. Like you mentioned, the fear of lacking others and being abandoned is a very scary thing. As you've been doing, rejecting others is the most effective way to punish them (subconsciously, that's what you believe), and you don't know how to ask others to give you what you want. You don't even know what you truly want, so you've never been satisfied by anyone, and you resent them for not giving you what you want. You want to punish them, and you believe that the only way to do so is through rejection, indifference, and disregard. You want to punish them for not giving you what you need. What you hope for is also what you think is the only capital that can punish others. You want to receive it, but at the same time, you hope they never gave it to you and are punished. So you do want to receive care, you want it. At the same time, you also want to punish others for not giving you the care you wanted. This is why you now believe that you are not worth being loved, and you don't believe that you deserve to be loved. You think that those who love you must have a reason for loving you, so you want to reject them. I don't have any comforting words, to be honest. Your current state is really consistent with your belief that you are not worth being loved, so your feelings are correct. You still hope to be loved and accepted unconditionally. This is a normal psychological need that every person has. So are you planning to give up on proving that you are worthy of love? To prove a false proposition, this is what you are doing. You probably haven't loved yourself yet. What state are you in when you are in that state? It's hard for me to say, and it's difficult to express the feeling. When I'm not loved by others, I realize that the most fulfilling love is the love I give myself, not the love I used to believe would fill the void. That void is called thinking that I am not worthy of being loved. How do I love myself? Here's what I do: 1. I am who I am. It's true that I am cold, just as you say. I don't even know how to love myself, so how can I love others? You are right. 2. I don't know how to love at all, even if I try to learn, it will only be a tiny bit of progress. I will love 1% and be cold 99%, which will inevitably hurt others and they will inevitably leave me. I don't ask you to stay, I just want to learn a little bit of love, you should leave if you need to. I'm not trying to prove that I am worth being loved, I am not worthy of being loved, and if you find that, you should leave. (Learning to love, in my shallow understanding, means expressing your needs and wants through non-violent communication. There are many books on nonviolent communication) 3. Life seems to have more than just the happiness of being loved. There is the joy of traveling, gaming, good food, the first time skydiving, the first time at the beach. Being loved at the beginning is really important, but as time goes on, I find other small amounts of happiness slowly lighting up. 4. Yes, in the end, life adds many bright spots and happiness, but the feeling of not being loved will never disappear. It will resurface from time to time, it's just that when I have other happiness, the feeling of not being loved is not constant anymore. It may come once a day, once a week, and eventually once a year. Yes, it will never truly disappear. But it only shows up once a month or once every few months. This is the past you, that unique you. It is the evidence of your existence, the youth you've lived through, no matter how unbearable that youth was, it is still my past.

OP, hello~~~ First, sending you a hug. From the description, we can understand that: 1. There are friends taking care of you, but you feel panicked about their concern. 2. You always have friends, but you still feel lonely when doing things alone. A little analysis and advice: 1. Although there are friends taking care of you, perhaps deep down you don't consider them as friends, but rather as outsiders trying to invade your life. Only those who you truly want to share your inner thoughts with and feel close to are your friends who can provide the social support and care you need. 2. Even though you always have friends, it's normal to feel lonely when doing things alone because friends can be there for us due to having compatible personalities and helping each other, not because they will have the exact same interests and hobbies for a lifetime. There are still many things in life that we need to do alone.

question: After being called a fraud by my boss, I got into a car accident, and now the teachers at this institution are calling me a spy.
description: I have encountered many setbacks in my life. I don't know if I am sick, but currently I am unemployed. When I was young, I was afraid to speak up when my teacher punished me. At 18, some colleagues at my workplace were not very friendly. Later, I chose a major I liked in college, but the teachers didn't seem to like me either. They didn't bother to look at my assignments. My boss at work said I was a cheat for not obeying orders. Today, when I went to an institution for a class, the teacher even asked if I was a spy... I don't know where I went wrong... What else can I do...

answers.answer_text: Hug to the questioner, seeing so many things piling up, makes me really want to empathize with you. I feel very sorry for your life experiences. Throughout your life, you have been constantly negated, enduring various criticisms and negativity. Your lack of self-confidence and negative attitude towards life now cause a great sense of contradiction in your interpersonal relationships, and you don't know how to handle it when you want to. In your current experiences, I wonder if your childhood experiences, such as strict discipline from your parents or lack of love from them, and various incidents during your upbringing, have left you feeling lost and unsure how to navigate the relationships between studying, living, and friends, not knowing how to protect yourself to the fullest. Did that childhood experience make you feel helpless, so that in the process of interacting with others, you cannot be confident, but rather in a humble state? As an adult, there are more and more unfavorable things happening in your life, and you also feel anxious and restless deep inside. Are you really helpless about the unfairness of life? As I write this, I really want to hug the questioner, to let you vent the grievances in your heart, to let go of everything about the world, forget the unhappiness in the past, and let life get to know you again. I have a few suggestions for you to consider: 1) Communicate more with a psychotherapist, such as how to build relationships with others, how you approach relationships, methods, and organizing your language, etc. Let a professional guide you. 2) Read some books on interpersonal communication, such as how to communicate with others, what to pay attention to in communication, etc. Improve your communication skills. 3) Increase your confidence in interacting with others, believe in yourself, and be kind to yourself. Seeing your message, I think it is possible that there may be some deficiencies in your handling of interpersonal relationships in daily life. If we just pay a little attention to it in life, it will be fine. I believe you are fine, and everything will get better and better! I am here, waiting for you all the time!

question: How to help an 8-year-old boy who lacks confidence?
description: The child walks with their head down all the time, and they easily cry in a low voice. They feel nervous when reciting ancient poems and their behavior seems unnatural.
keywords: Growth, personality development, student growth, child development.

answers.answer_text: First of all, I want to give a big hug to the questioner. The questioner mentioned that the child always walks with their head down and lacks confidence. I would like to ask if the child has always been like this or if it suddenly happened one day. If it has always been like this, it may be because the child is sensitive and anxious by nature. Parents can create a relaxed learning environment for their children. Try not to use a demanding tone to urge children to study, and encourage them every day. Avoid comparing your child with children from other families. One common thing Chinese parents tend to do is unconsciously compare and talk about their children's "stupid things" with others. Although parents may think it's nothing, it can leave psychological issues for the child and affect their self-esteem. If the child suddenly became like this, parents should try to understand whether there are people or incidents in school or class that have caused the child's situation, or whether the teacher unintentionally or intentionally said something about reciting ancient poems. Children in primary school are easily influenced by their teachers' comments on their subconscious and emotions. Finally, regardless of the situation, I suggest parents have equal conversations with their children, ask them about recent events and what they think, encourage them, and trust what they say. Finally, best wishes.

Hello, questioner. 1. It is necessary to create a harmonious family atmosphere so that the child can grow up in a relaxed and harmonious environment, which will increase his sense of security. 2. Parents should encourage children to do things on their own and not do everything for them. 3. Parents should fully respect the child's wishes, even for something as small as choosing a dish, even if the dish turns out to be not tasty, there is no need for excessive comments, just respect the child's choice. 4. Establish clear principles and rules for the child. Reward and punishment should be clear. 5. Encourage the child to try, and even if they are not successful, encouragement should be emphasized. At the same time, parents should set an example, for example, performing with a confident style at home to show the child. 6. Allow the child to play with their friends independently. There is no need for the company of parents. I hope this is helpful to you.

Thank you for your question. The primary school stage is an important period for children to develop confidence. Good development during this stage is based on smooth growth in previous stages. On one hand, it is related to the child's own temperament. For example, whether they are easily crying and difficult to soothe, or if they cry loudly from the beginning. If these characteristics exist from birth, parents need to be very careful and meticulous in taking care of them. Sensitive children require a lot of parental attention. Encourage the child to complete achievable tasks and provide timely positive feedback. Crying is not a terrible thing as it helps the child release emotions. However, through discussions after crying, the child can gradually stop using negative thinking to understand what happened, especially when experiencing feelings of frustration. Please be patient and supportive instead of criticizing or blaming the child. Guide them to learn from failures. Regardless of how different your child may be compared to other children, please remember to encourage them. Every child is unique, so don't expect them to meet the expectations of others. It is the parent's responsibility to help them become a better version of themselves. I hope this helps you.

Sincere and accurate praise!!!!!! The most important thing is companionship! In the process of accompanying, observe and discover his strengths, sincerely and accurately praise these strengths! Even if they are not considered conventional strengths, they can still be praised! As long as he completes or achieves something, give a corresponding response! Being a warm mirror for children is the best way to boost their confidence!

question: My son and I always clash with each other. Is hypnosis helpful for resolving problems?
description: My son and I always clash with each other. I ask him to study, but he says he will but doesn't actually do it. I don't allow him to drink soda, but he secretly buys it for himself. So, I feel that there may be some underlying issues between us. I want to try using hypnosis as a technique. If anyone understands, please give me some advice. Thank you.
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: Children often rebel against their parents and have their own thoughts and ideas. It is important to find a suitable and reasonable way to communicate with them. Hypnotherapy is mainly used for treating mental and neurological disorders caused by psychological factors. It involves establishing a special trust relationship between the therapist and the patient through language and a specific environment. The patient is then induced into a special state of consciousness, where they focus solely on the therapist's information to achieve the therapeutic goal. Common training characteristics include eliminating distractions, total body relaxation, deep slow breathing, and repetitive training, all of which directly target the underlying causes of the illness.

question: My mother is too controlling of me. My father passed away when I was 16 years old. I suspect that I have an Oedipus complex.
description: First, let me talk about my situation. When I was young, my mother took care of me more, while my father didn't take care of me much, but I was afraid of him. Later, when I was 16 years old, my father passed away. About a year and a half ago, my mother remarried. During that time, not long after, I had a dream about having a sexual relationship with my mother. It was just an impression, and my sexual dreams don't have any specific details. I felt very uncomfortable when I woke up, so I consulted a doctor, and the doctor said that I might have been too worried about whether my mother was happy. Then, a year ago, I had another dream. In the dream, I knew it was my mother, but it still seemed like a sexual relationship happened. There was only a little sense of it, no specific details, but I still felt very uncomfortable when I woke up. The emotions in the dream were not because it was my mother, but just a sexual desire for a physical relationship. In reality, I have never had any thoughts about my mother. During adolescence, I did have sexual urges towards older women, but it was only a sexual impulse. Of course, I have also liked people my own age, confessed to girls, and had sexual impulses towards girls my age. As I grew older, I no longer have such thoughts about older women. Sometimes, when I come across memories of those novel-like situations with older neighbors or something similar, I may have some sexual thoughts, but if I were asked to act on them, I would feel disgusted. I am a bit of a germaphobe, and now I find the idea of being with someone much older than me repulsive.

answers.answer_text: Thank you for the invitation. Using the perspective of a dream interpretation book, dreaming of having sexual relations with someone you consider impossible or haven't even thought of is a very common phenomenon, such as family members, acquaintances, or colleagues. The core of sexual intercourse is to bring two people's bodies as close as possible, merging into one. If we remove all the pornography, awkwardness, and shame, this image is actually very pure. Anyone who appears in a sexual scenario unconsciously expresses a desire to merge their "characteristics" with another person. The sexual dream occurred not long after your mother remarried, and waking up feeling uncomfortable may indeed be related to the doctor's statement about "being overly worried about whether your mother is happy." Since your mother was strict with you when you were young and you had a closer relationship with her, it is unknown how her rebuilding a family has affected the care between you. Perhaps, through the dream, you expressed a desire to maintain an intimate connection with her. And being in a peak period of sexual desire, it is natural for you to sometimes immerse yourself in the fantasy world of novels and have sexual dreams. Dream interpretation requires some in-depth exploration. It is particularly recommended to do one-on-one counseling.

Hello, after reading your description, there is a sentence that says, "In the dream, the emotion is not excited because it's my mother, but simply a sexual desire for a relationship." It's good that you noticed the details of the emotions in your dream, and personally, I think your analysis is correct. According to what you said about your age, around 17 years old, it's a stage approaching sexual maturity. In addition, your mother remarried during that stage, which means subconsciousl

I have a question. I find those two dreams very strange, what do they represent? I have never had inappropriate thoughts about my mother. Recently, I dreamed about having a sexual relationship with a woman of the same age as my aunt, but nothing actually happened. I woke up feeling disgusted. I find that age group disgusting. However, my life experiences and exposure to certain novel plots have given me the impression that there is a certain allure to those scenarios, but in reality, I find them repulsive. In the past year, I have been in relationships with two girlfriends, and we have had sexual encounters. My ex-girlfriend was two years younger than me, and my current girlfriend is a few months older than me. We are planning to get married, and everything is going well in all aspects. Is this considered a mother complex? I'm really confused.

question: As a team leader, do you always ignore some people when it comes to submitting assignments?
description: As a team leader, I have a problem that cannot be ignored - I always neglect some people when submitting assignments, only submitting some people's work. This is terrible, as it seems to disregard others and be self-centered... um, that might be me. I often intentionally ignore people who can affect my mood in order to maintain a positive emotional state, and that might be the reason I forget to collect assignments... So, is there any way to balance both aspects? Orz

answers.answer_text: In the conflicting social norms between "taking care of one's own emotions" and "work responsibilities", work responsibilities are considered more important than personal needs and emotions. (It is necessary to recognize one's own abilities.) Social norms dictate that judgments should be made based on actions rather than individuals, in order to maintain social stability. It is advised to create a window for one's own heart. In the face of people who can affect one's mood, close the window. Stick to professionalism, focus on the task rather than the person. At the beginning, it requires practice and self-persuasion. If the pressure becomes overwhelming, it is recommended to consider quitting the job.

question: 20-year-old female, has had no desire to go out in the past year, what should she do if she doesn't want to go home?
description: I don't want to go out. I only reluctantly go out when I feel hungry. I feel a bit anxious when I go out by myself, so I have to prepare myself. A few years ago, I used to cry a lot when going out, but my mom ordered me to go out and buy groceries every day, so I reluctantly got better. This past year, it's like that again, but not as serious as before. And my mood hasn't been great this month. I've thought about cutting my wrists, but I dare not do it because I'm afraid of blood. I don't want to stay at school now, nor do I want to go home, what should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, you can also call me Xiaofan Guo. I wonder if besides social interactions in real life, do you have any other good friends on the internet? Actually, many people have social anxiety and are unwilling to communicate with others, but I feel that you are not unwilling to make friends, just worried about conflicts or unsure how to communicate with others. So, let's start with the online world. For example, if you have any thoughts or things you want to share, we can express them through writing, and then we can interact with other users. Through these discussions and exchanges, we will discover that there are many interesting things in the world. For example, we can talk about when you started not wanting to go out and if you have had any bad experiences. When encountering problems, how do you handle and resolve them? We can also list some anticipated situations and contingency plans, then analyze them in combination with the actual circumstances, distinguishing between what we imagine and what we actually experience, gradually developing self-solving abilities. Mom's request for us to go out and buy groceries is not a mandatory command, but a hope that we can try to communicate with others. During the process of buying groceries, you may have some interesting stories. Can you share them with Xiaofan Guo? Self-harm is indeed very painful, so can we find another way? For example, coming here to chat with other friends and share our feelings, together releasing the inner pressures. School and home can provide us with a relatively safe space. I wonder where you want to go and what you hope to find there. Let's discuss it together. The world loves you.

After reading your description, I feel so sorry for you. Hugs to you! Being 20 years old is the most beautiful age, it's the time of youth, with love, going to college, working... But for you, it's not that wonderful. You feel anxious even going out, you have to work on your mental health or your mom pushes you to go grocery shopping so you can leave the house. In the past few years, you would feel like crying when going out, your emotions were very bad, and you even had thoughts of self-harm like cutting your wrists. Why did this happen? What happened... Did you drop out of school? Maybe you had your own dreams, what you wanted to do when you grew up, what kind of person you wanted to become, what kind of things you wanted to do... Do you not remember anymore? What will you be like in 5 years? What about 10 years from now? Do you want to live like this your whole life? Coming into this world, don't you want to shine brightly? Right now, you don't want to stay at home, nor at school, you're not feeling comfortable. If you're sick and need help, you can go see a doctor or seek psychological counseling. Sometimes, it's really not easy to face this world alone.

question: My husband loses his temper in public, and I keep quiet. I feel like I'm being timid.
description: Today when we went out to play, my husband yelled at me loudly in public because I didn't notice our son needed to pee. I feel that this kind of behavior is really inappropriate, and he often does this. I didn't say anything because there were other people around, and I didn't want to make a scene. But deep down, I'm really angry. It makes me feel weak and defeated.

answers.answer_text: Teacher Cong said, "Anger is because of fear." If that's the case, what is your husband afraid of? Does he care about his reputation? Is he worried about being looked down upon or mocked for not raising the child properly and letting the child pee in inappropriate places? He immediately yelled at you and shifted the blame onto you, distancing himself from the situation. It's highly likely that he is repeating the way his parents solved problems. However, he doesn't realize that losing control and shouting loudly in public is a display of poor manners and leaves a worse impression on others. When he calms down and is in a good mood, communicate with him about similar issues. It's not necessary to resolve problems in this intense way every time. Instead, solve problems when they arise; yelling won't make the problems disappear. If he really wants to shift responsibility, he can express it properly without the need for such aggressive methods to make others comply. At the same time, it's commendable that you didn't lose control of your emotions because of his anger. It shows that you have a stronger and more mature psychological endurance. This effectively prevents arguments from escalating and affecting your image and relationship. It also prevents harm to the child (here, I really want to praise the original poster for not transferring anger and dissatisfaction onto the child, truly a strong and secure mother). Solving the issue of anger means solving his fear. Find his fear, strengthen his inner self, and don't care about how others perceive him. Some problems can be completely avoided, such as when the child is too young and cannot control their bodily functions. Putting on a diaper when going out can save a lot of trouble. If the child is a bit older, teach them to express their need to go to the bathroom correctly and tell them to only do their business in the toilet, etc.

Hello, the host, your husband always shouts at you without considering your feelings when facing problems in front of others. However, in front of others, you still swallow your grievances to protect your husband's self-esteem, allowing yourself to be wronged. Your dedication is heart-wrenching. Not retaliating loudly against your husband can't be described as "cowardly", it can only be said that you are trying to compromise. Being able to do this shows that you have made efforts for your relationship, which is admirable. However, in a relationship, this kind of compromise may become a time bomb if it goes on for too long, with a stronger impact and deeper wounds. Therefore, I suggest that you can have a good conversation with your husband at the right time, express your emotions, and let him understand your feelings. I believe your husband should reflect on it.

question: I don't know if it's my own psychological problem or if it's my mom's psychological problem.
description: Female, 24 years old, education major. Before graduating, my mom was pushing me to take the civil service exam. We had many arguments about it, with her sometimes saying it's up to me whether I want to take it or not, but the next day she would force me to take it. I took the exam in the first half of this year and passed, but I feel even more overwhelmed now. During the political review, she started frantically searching online for information about it. (Once, I had an experience of not properly resigning from a private school because they unlawfully withheld my teaching qualification certificate.) Her search history was full of political review-related searches, and she would often ask me and even suspect my dad of having a criminal record or bad credit. A few days ago, the announcement of the medical examination results was posted online, and I told her about it and explained. Still, she continued to search on her own. The first time she saw a notice that wasn't for our region, and the second time she looked, her expression turned strange. After about an hour, she said, "How come you were pushed down by one place? That person must have a powerful connection. But don't worry, the person in front of you definitely had a problem in their medical exam" (I desperately explained that this isn't a ranking, and the medical exam was only because the person hadn't finished their re-examination yet). When filling out the family relationship section, she told me not to include her because she doesn't have a job. She wanted me to list my aunt and other relatives who work in government institutions instead.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, family control.

answers.answer_text: Friend, I can feel that you're feeling wronged. Some of your relatives have achieved a certain level of success and happiness in their work and life, something that your mother has always longed for but couldn't achieve. She may have projected these inner expectations onto you, seeing your success as a way to compensate for her own shortcomings. This desire may be so strong that it disregards your feelings. However, it's important to understand that there are limits between people, and establishing those limits is a process of mutual understanding. First, ask yourself if you are willing to accept everything that has happened. If you can accept and enjoy this kind of work, especially because there are role models in your family, then you can accept your mother's approach as a way of expressing love through personal taste. At the same time, communicate your thoughts to her and make her feel at ease. If you don't feel excited about this arrangement, bravely express your feelings to your mother and ask her to respect your thoughts. Boldly expressing yourself is the beginning of setting boundaries. I hope everything goes well and your mother understands. Best wishes.

Hello! Before you graduated, your mother forced you to pursue a "glamorous and stable" civil service job, and she was very anxious about your exam results. She even asked you, after you passed the exam, not to fill in her information as unemployed, but to provide information about relatives with stable jobs. It seems like you have always been a tool for her to prove herself, and she has always controlled major events in your life. So, you feel unreasonable, but unable to escape. Is that right? From your description, I see a mother who cannot validate herself, cannot value herself, and even feels ashamed of her "lack of social worth." Therefore, she wants to achieve all her perceived value through you. She hopes that you can obtain a prestigious job that will bring social recognition, and perhaps even a glamorous marriage in the future. In the past, you did not dare to resist because you relied on your parents for survival. You satisfied her expectations and appeased her anxieties because you feared being abandoned by your mother. But now that you have grown up, you feel aggrieved and angry about being used as a tool for so long. You have the impulse to resist, such as arguing, but ultimately, you still surrender. So, who has the problem between the two of you? In fact, it is the result of your joint efforts, long-term interactions, and the establishment of this pattern together. If possible, I suggest that you seek professional family therapy from a psychological counselor to explore the underlying psychological patterns for each of you and engage in some work and changes together. Your mother may have a very fragile sense of self internally, so I recommend that you frequently validate her through words and actions and satisfy this aspect of her needs. Now that you have grown up, you no longer need to submit out of fear. You can appropriately maintain your boundaries and make decisions about your own life based on your inner desires.

question: Is there no hope for a 16-year-old boy who always argues, even when he is wrong?
description: I am a person who is vain and loves showing off. I enjoy pretending to be someone I'm not, and I even argue with others when I know I am wrong. I want to have a high status in everyone's eyes. When I was 18 years old, I was still in the second year of junior high school. It was during the National Day holiday when I had a fight with my parents, so I ran away from home. It was my first time running away, and I was gone for almost a month. I thought I could make it on my own, but that period of time had a great impact on me. I was completely confused by this society and my understanding of money reached a new level. During that month, I barely got by, giving ten yuan to one friend and ten yuan to another friend every day. In November, I returned home and my dad made me feel loved. Suddenly, I also felt that this world could be warm.
keywords: Growth, student growth, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: A person who can withstand a great deal of slander can also withstand a great deal of honor. Admiring vanity is a behavior that many people have, but everyone's upbringing is different, so the way each person expresses it is also different. The asker's family conditions are good, so they haven't suffered much since childhood. If my guess is correct, the asker should have been a spoiled child who provided material things to other children, and the other children would try to please them in order to gain more benefits, which sometimes leads to a mistaken understanding of oneself. Actually, a truly capable person is not judged by how many people are around them when they are successful, but by how many people stand by their side when they are down and out. When I was the same age as the asker, I also envied those so-called "kings" in school, thinking that they were very impressive, surrounded by followers, and had many girls around them. Meanwhile, I sometimes felt like an ugly duckling in the corner. However, I have a few really reliable buddies, and whenever I need help, they always step forward. There was one time when I accidentally bumped into a troublemaker in school, and despite apologizing, the other person refused to accept and continued to push and make a fuss. Eventually, a few of my buddies couldn't stand it and a conflict occurred. It almost escalated to a physical fight, but it ended without consequences because one of them had a well-connected older brother. Everyone has a young and foolish period in their lives, so we shouldn't think that missing one opportunity means we will never have a chance to turn things around again. After all, if young people don't do some impulsive things, they're not truly young. We're only 16 years old now, and life has just begun. Since we have missed opportunities and experienced some turbulence, we now have a more mature mindset than our peers. We can also reduce the cost of making mistakes, so if there's a chance, we should still make an effort to try. If we have the courage to leave this world, can't we also have the ability to change ourselves? After all, what can scare someone who no longer fears death? The world and I love you.

Give you a big hug. I think you're very talented, a young man who exudes determination, which will ensure your future success. However, at this age, it's important to focus on your education. You must have your own skills to establish yourself in society. Otherwise, no matter how wealthy or how many friends you have, you won't be able to sustain it. There are too many temptations in society, so I hope you can settle down and study hard. If you can't do that, at least learn a technical skill. Whatever it may be, it will provide you with a career in the future. Running away from home or stealing are immature behaviors. Take advantage of your youth and learn more things, enrich yourself, and make yourself more valuable, rather than being like those troublemakers. Hope this can help you, keep going!

Hello, are you currently in college? Many young people have run away from home when they are full of energy. From your description, it seems like you gained a lot from being away for a month and realized that life is not easy. In fact, your parents love you very much. Maybe you haven't felt the hardships of life when you were living carefree, but parents have to bear all the responsibilities. You will understand this when you get married and have children in the future.

Now all of my previously good friends, my sister, and so-called brothers have left me. I can't understand why this happened, as I come from a well-off family. Even my parents have lost hope in me. Now, all I want is to repay my parents and live a better life myself. I want to make life more interesting. I also have a strong desire to leave this world and see where I'll go after death and what kind of experiences await me.

I used to have a little brother who was quite grudgeful. He went around my hometown talking bad about me. People of our age group easily understand and don't think too much when they hear negative comments. As a result, everyone distanced themselves from me. I am someone who is afraid of being alone. When I had money before, those friends would always be by my side. Now that I don't have money, they all consider me a despicable person. In reality, I am well aware of what happened and why. From that moment, I felt my only growth; I no longer pursue fame and fortune, or engage in arguments with others. I simply remain silent, unwilling to argue with them anymore. Because I know that they are now in the same situation I was before. I don't blame them; I can only blame the world. From that moment, all I think about is how to make money. I am confident in my own abilities and have indeed earned a considerable amount of money. I also want to grow up quickly and start my own life. Suddenly, I feel guilty towards my parents for holding them back. I am sorry to my whole family, but most of all, I am sorry to myself.

Since then, I would run away from a school within 10 days. This caused my relationship with my family to deteriorate, and I stopped studying. Because compared to the closed school, I was attracted to society. I regretted it later. At that time, I had many friends, but I only wanted to show off. Later, I ran out of money, and the support from my family couldn't sustain my reputation outside anymore. I felt miserable without money. In October, a friend told me that he was going to work in Myanmar and would earn a lot of money, millions and millions. He asked me to go with him. At that time, I had no money, and my family had completely lost hope in me. So, I went with him. However, when we got there, all we did was involved in telecom fraud. It was a scam. Because I was too straightforward, I didn't make a single penny from cheating. I had no achievements. When we returned in December, the company compensated us, including the cost of illegal immigration. I had to borrow money from my family. It was the first time I saw the cruelty of society. I was relieved I wasn't caught and safely returned to my hometown. However, what happened after I returned home made the burden in my heart even heavier. I didn't want to live in this world anymore.

After I started drinking, I had money. I felt embarrassed to have her around me. I often pushed her away. I would hang out with my friends at bars, clubs, and such. They wanted to get hotel rooms and I would pay for it. I never asked them for money. This kind of money was gone very quickly. Get alcohol, sell it. Spend the money, get alcohol, sell it. It was a cycle I was stuck in. Step by step, it led me into the abyss. There was one time when we were in her room. Maybe it was intentional, but we had sexual relations. But I still treated her like my little sister and forced her to do many things. Yet she still loved me and I loved her too. But it was the temptation of money and the laziness of human nature that dragged me down. I couldn't help it. I took out the Maotai liquor from both of her family's houses. Actually, at that time, there were a few social big brothers who owned pawnshops guiding me to go and get liquor from her family. I didn't want to harm them in my heart. But the abyss was getting deeper step by step. I couldn't break free.

But it was also in November that I encountered something that would impact me for a lifetime. I met a girl. Because my family was well-off, I attended prestigious schools at the time. She loved me deeply, to the point where her mother had piles of Maotai liquor at home. She disregarded everything in order to please me and make me love her. She gave me Maotai liquor for the first time. At that time, a bottle of Maotai liquor could easily be sold for around 3,000 yuan. Each bottle in her house was even more premium than the last. When I first received it, I only took a few bottles. But the tens of thousands of yuan I received at the time led this 15-year-old boy down a path to ruin. Because I was mischievous at the time, she said she saw me as a brother, and I, with good intentions, allowed her to be like a sister to me.

question: Feeling very sad and dark, nothing seems to have meaning anymore, thinking about ways to end the pain through suicide.
description: I don't need anyone to persuade me, but I am wondering if there is any painless way to commit suicide. I'm very scared of pain... I just want to know the answer. I have been thinking about it for a long time.
keywords: Emotions, fragile and prone to tears.

answers.answer_text: Regarding this topic, Xiaofan Guo has also had similar experiences and thought about leaving this world, but did not want it to be too painful. At first, he thought about suffocating himself and even attempted it, but ultimately gave up due to the instinctive reaction of his body and the unbearable pain. He also thought about jumping from a height, but looking at the empty space below and feeling a bit scared and worried, afraid that he might not leave and become disabled, which would be even more painful for himself, and that moment would be very painful as well. He also thought about some accidents happening, with different thoughts and attempts in his mind, but he denied them one by one. He wanted a dignified way to leave, without causing too much trouble and distress to others. Although that kind of pain is sometimes momentary, he still worries and is afraid. In those dark days, he always felt that his sky was dim and did not want to communicate with others, and felt that he had no hope of change, as if the whole world had only him left. Looking back now, Xiaofan Guo does not know how he survived, but he is grateful that he did not take that final step, so we have the chance to meet again. I don't know if there is a way to leave without pain, because pain is inevitable. Some pain is physical, some is psychological. So, in order to leave without pain, can we try to wait until the last moment of life? After all, no one knows what will happen in the future, so let's persevere a little longer, okay? The world and I love you.

question: Crying when talking to others alone, trembling when there are many people around, whether it is classmates, parents, or teachers.
description: The single mother I live with practices a somewhat closed-off style of parenting and often resorts to moral coercion. She constantly pressures me to attend the high school that she wants me to go to, using reasons like her health condition and the fact that she didn't inform me about her marriage and the arrival of a man I don't know. This situation has been going on for two years.

answers.answer_text: When a person is cold, they will shiver. When others see you shivering, they will ask if you're cold. When a person is scared, they will tremble and things will shake out of their hands. When a person feels guilty, they will tremble, especially when others already know they have done something wrong. When a person is happy, they may also tremble, shaking off the tension. Crying is a normal reaction when feeling sad or extremely happy. When these normal reactions are overly interpreted, it becomes twisted, meaning that the mind is in too much pain and the thinking becomes rigid. In other words, the brain is tired and needs rest, and the body cannot bear it and needs to relax. You are not a parent, just a child. Child, you have suffered. I hope all the hardships are worth it, and I hope you can ride the waves in the new era.

question: I have always wanted to break away from the therapist deep inside, and I don't want to continue anymore.
description: I have been experiencing with my counselor for over two years, but I have always been indecisive and unable to settle down and truly feel myself. Recently, this feeling has resurfaced, and I keep finding faults with my counselor. Upon reflection, I realize that this is my pattern, and the real goal is to stop doing counseling. So, should I continue to persevere or follow my heart?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. From your description, I understand that you have been unable to calm down and truly feel yourself during the two years of counseling. You want to end it, but you fear that it may be your own problem, causing you confusion. The goal of psychological counseling is to gradually free you from inner confusion, help you find yourself, and rediscover happiness. If you haven't experienced any progress or growth during the two-year counseling period, perhaps the current counselor isn't suitable for you. I suggest you temporarily pause the counseling and carefully consider two options: (1) Continue with this counselor: Express your counseling experience to them, reassess yourself psychologically, and establish new counseling goals. (2) Find a new counselor: End the current counseling relationship and seek a new counselor. Before starting formal counseling, let the counselor know your expectations and which counseling approach you would like to use. Find a counseling approach that suits you. Best wishes!

More than two years is not a short time, and the relationship with the counselor still doesn't give you enough sense of safety and trust. Is this pattern also present in your intimate or important relationships? This is something worth discussing with your counselor. You mentioned that your purpose in being "picky" is to end the relationship with the counselor, so what do you want by ending it? What is making you hesitate and find it difficult to make a decision to end it? Is this kind of hesitation and contradiction something you often encounter in life? Perhaps this is an opportunity to explore the object relationship patterns deep within your heart through the difficulties presented in your counseling relationship. When you see how the motivations behind your actions are influencing you, maybe you can choose more freely.

question: A first-grade child is very anxious and cries every day, saying they miss their mom. What should I do?
description: The child has started first grade. Normally, they are very cheerful. It has been four days since the first day of school, and they have been crying every day, saying they miss their mother! I have tried various ways to comfort and encourage them, but it doesn't seem to work at all! The child still seems very low-spirited, and even during the weekend at home, they are not very happy. I'm worried that this might have a more serious impact on their mental well-being! The child I see now is not the daughter I know.
keywords: Growth, development patterns, stress management, child development.

answers.answer_text: Hello! The new semester has started, and children who have just entered elementary school are still in the adaptation period for the first month. The second month is the adjustment period, and the third month will be another adaptation period. Some children may only start getting into the groove in the fourth month. For a child transitioning from kindergarten to first grade, she will face various challenges such as changes in the school environment, teachers, learning tasks, playmates, and behavioral norms. For example, in kindergarten, each class had two teachers who could take care of each child. But now in elementary school, there is only one teacher for the whole class, so it is natural for children to feel a gap and discomfort. Even as adults, sudden changes can be difficult for us to adapt to. For your daughter, she also needs to adapt to these unexpected changes. I suggest using the following "six questions" to help your child ease through the starting period. Firstly, you can ask: What did you do to help the teacher/friends today? After asking this question, parents can guide their child to activate their memory and reflect on their interactions with the teacher and friends throughout the day. This will help boost their confidence, sense of honor, and make them love going to school. Secondly, you can ask: Who is your best friend? Why do you like them? By asking this question, consciously encourage your child to communicate and interact with their classmates, and help them find their own best friend. At the same time, let them know the strengths of their classmates, establish values, and reinforce their memory of the positive aspects of school. Thirdly, you can ask: What interesting things happened in class today? When your child answers, don't rush to comment, but focus on listening and guide them to express their opinions. After they finish, discuss with them, which can increase your understanding of your child and convey the correct perspective and values during the discussion. Fourthly, you can ask: Is there anything you don't understand and need Mom and Dad's help with? This question allows your child to feel that you care and they can always come to you with questions, thereby gaining their trust and helping them open up, so they no longer resist school due to various unsolvable issues. Fifthly, you can ask: What games did you play with your friends today? This specific question makes it clear what to answer, and it ignites their desire to respond. The more the child says, the better parents can understand their child's situation at school and stimulate their interest in school. Lastly, you can ask: Can you teach Mom how to make the paper boat you learned today? Use specific, detailed questions to discuss topics that interest your child. Gradually, your child will enjoy sharing their daily school life with you.

Hello, OP!【The child has started first grade. Normally, he/she is very cheerful. It's already the fourth day since the first day of school, but he/she cries every day, saying that he/she misses mom! I've tried various ways to comfort and encourage, but nothing seems to work!】 Children are the cutest. You said the child has started first grade, it's just the beginning of the school year, and he/she cries every day. Could it be that there's something that's upsetting the child's mind, and that's why he/she seeks help from mom? Starting school is exciting for children because they're curious about the outside world. As a lovely mom, it's understandable that you have no resistance to your baby's crying. It's heartbreaking. At this time, I hope you can adjust your own emotions and comfort yourself first. If you are panicking and the child is crying nonstop, it's difficult to handle the situation. Although the child has gone through the kindergarten stage, going to elementary school and being able to make new friends can also be exciting. If the child cries every day, it's probably because he/she feels reluctant and sad about being separated from previous playmates or something has happened at school. It's best to comfort the child and sincerely ask for the reason. In addition, it might be that the child feels insecure deep down due to being in a bigger and unfamiliar environment with new classmates and teachers. As a mom, you can inquire about the child's thoughts on the new school, new teachers, and new classmates, and use descriptive imagery to inform the child about the advantages of the new school and new friends. Encourage the child and gradually foster independence in his/her mind, letting him/her understand that as a first-grader, he/she has the right to learn to make new friends and explore more interesting things. The most important thing is to make it clear to the child that mom will always lend a helping hand when needed, and he/she can share any joyful or unhappy experiences with mom and solve them together, without having to shoulder everything alone. Only when the child understands that mom will always be there, will he/she slowly overcome fear and anxiety. 🥑 A very important point in life is that children can develop a sense of responsibility only by participating in their parents' lives. As a mom, you want to take care of everything for your child. However, for a child starting elementary school, the necessary independence needs to start gradually from gradually reducing parental help. At this time, you can formally inform the child that he/she has grown up to become a beautiful and capable little adult, and his/her own affairs need to be taken care of independently. Only through serious communication with the child and making him/her understand these principles and situations will he/she grasp independence and seek help from within rather than crying every time something happens. Because girls' hearts are more delicate and sensitive than boys', they are easily influenced by emotions in many matters. Therefore, they need even more independence and inner strength, particularly an open-minded personality. Children are all fascinating individuals. They have their own thoughts. Coming into this world, they experience many conflicts in their hearts and much confusion. As we tell them more and more things, they will have a deeper understanding of this world and their parents. Because "cognition" is a subjective term, they will see the world as we do. So please be patient with them, not just loving them. Many mistakes themselves stem from love, and spoiling and favoritism are the biggest stumbling blocks in a child's life. I wish you well, a happy and content life!

Hello! Hugs to you! From your statement, I can sense that you may be anxious about your daughter starting school. When transitioning from kindergarten to first grade, a child may encounter changes in school environment, teachers, learning tasks, playmates, and behavior norms, among others. Even as adults, sudden changes are difficult for us to adapt to, so it is also necessary for your daughter to adapt to the new circumstances. In daily life, we can guide our children to speak about what happens at school, to see if they have encountered any unhappy situations, and provide timely feedback on their emotions. At the same time, we can also communicate with the teachers to understand your daughter's situation in school, see what her state is like, and whether she plays with other children. Regardless of her mood, as parents, we should first know about her experiences at school and then decide what specific actions to take. From your statement, it seems that your daughter may be afraid of separation, which is referred to as separation anxiety. For your daughter, she may be afraid of leaving her mother. As a mother, you can let her know that you have always been there, and even though you go to work while she goes to school, she will see you when she comes back home. If possible, try to arrive early during pick-up time so your child knows that what you say is true. As parents, we need to have patience first, as we are our child's first teachers. We can share our own examples and experiences every day, showing our child bravery and perseverance, and encouraging her to be like us. As parents, providing comfort and encouragement to our children is essential. Additionally, we can find some picture books about going to school and read them to her during rest time. Through subtle influence, we can help her understand the lessons conveyed in the books. For your daughter, the sudden change in environment may leave her confused, and this may require the company and patience of her parents to help her through this adjustment period, and then slowly guide her to develop independent abilities. I hope these suggestions will be helpful to you. Best wishes!

Hello OP! I hope the following methods can help you with your child's situation~ As school begins, there is crying at the entrance of kindergartens, and parents' hearts ache. If the child doesn't go to school, there is a fear of falling behind in learning and missing out on group experiences. But if the child does go to school, they cry their hearts out, causing anguish for the parents. The child is attached to their parents, afraid of being separated, so crying is a very normal emotional response. When they come to an unfamiliar environment and meet unfamiliar people, the child feels lonely and scared, feeling helpless and wanting to escape the kindergarten and go home. To the child, school is unknown and vast, which can cause fear and a desire to escape. This is a natural instinct of self-preservation. For some children, it is not an exaggeration to describe the situation as a life-or-death separation, as if they cannot survive without their parents. If we continuously say, "What is there to be afraid of?" the child will feel like they are the only ones feeling afraid and that no one understands them. This will only result in increased fear and loneliness for the child. Only by understanding the child's fear and sadness can we provide the support they need from their perspective, so that the child doesn't feel alone in facing their fears. For children with separation anxiety, parents and teachers can work together to help these children transition through the anxious period. Shenzhen Xinhaiwan Psychological Counseling expert Ai Kunzhen has provided parents with some small methods for reference: 1. Transitional objects: Bring along a toy/blanket/towel that the child is particularly attached to and likes to school. The child's favorite toy can become their psychological reliance. In psychology, this toy is called a transitional object, like a trusted companion that provides comfort and counteracts fear and anxiety. The support parents give their child takes a long time to internalize in the child's mind. Once internalized, the child knows that even if mom and dad are not physically present, they are in their heart, providing a sense of reliance, security, and strength. However, for some two or three-year-old children, before their parents' support has been internalized, they need such a transitional object to accompany them when their parents are not around, providing comfort, security, and a sense of control. For teachers, they can talk to the child's toy/blanket/towel and interact with them. For the child, these objects are alive, with their own emotions and thoughts (the child projects their own emotions and feelings onto them). Patiently understanding and accompanying their feelings helps establish a familiar and trusting relationship between the child and the teacher, reducing anxiety towards school. 2. Patiently comfort the child: Parents can crouch down, hug the child, and say, "Baby, you're afraid of being separated from mommy/daddy, right? Mommy/daddy knows your fear..." This way, stay with and hug the child for a while (don't expect an immediate improvement in their emotions; each child has a different level of attachment and fear, so the time needed for comfort varies). When the child's emotions have calmed down, agree on a specific time and activity to do together (determine the specific details based on what the child likes the most). 3. Increase the child's sense of security: Get to know the children in the class beforehand and see if there are any children from the same neighborhood. Schedule playdates after meals together, creating opportunities for the children to play together. When a child has more familiar playmates, it increases their sense of security and reduces the sense of unfamiliarity towards school. Many parents love their children, and all their efforts and sacrifices are made for the sake of their children's better growth. However, when we don't understand the child's state, we can become very anxious and not know how to deal with them. Therefore, along with love, we also need to understand the child and respect their individual pace of growth, in order to better support their development.

Hello, I can sense your distress from your words, and I sincerely hope that I can help you through words. You mentioned that your child is now in the first grade and used to be cheerful, but for the past four days since starting school, they cry every day and say they miss their mother. Despite your comforting and encouraging efforts, your child still lacks energy and isn't very happy even on weekends at home. September is another back-to-school season, a new semester, and your child has just entered a new environment and is exposed to new learning materials, which can definitely cause discomfort, especially going from the relaxed atmosphere of pre-school to gradually entering a learning environment. There's also the factor of spending too much time at home during the pandemic, so going back to school is bound to cause some post-vacation syndrome. This is unrelated to age; just like us adults, when we haven't done certain things for a long time, it takes time for us to readjust. If your child is usually cheerful but lacks energy now because of school, then we can infer that they are facing problems at school. Starting school means leaving parents' side, leaving home for school, and at the same time, we have to interact with unfamiliar teachers and classmates, and learn new knowledge and complete assignments. All of these can lead to your child's discomfort and confusion. It's really great that you can observe your child's emotions and seek help from the outside world, and I hope I can also help you, so here are a few suggestions: 1. Guide your child to express their feelings. Many children are not good at expressing their emotions to the outside world. Sometimes, they can only seek help by crying. At this time, it's up to us as parents to identify their problems and patiently inquire about their true feelings. 2. Find happiness for your child. When children come to a new environment, they need to get to know new people again. If they are not good at communicating with their classmates and teachers, they will encounter difficulties in socializing and feel lonely. So, they will seek out someone who makes them feel secure, like your child always saying "I miss my mom." 3. Accompany your child in their learning. Going into first grade means that they are starting to truly learn academically. This is also an important stage for their education, which will determine whether they develop an interest in learning and lay a solid foundation. I suggest that parents can accompany their child in doing homework and provide guidance, so that the child can enjoy learning and find pleasure in it. 4. Communicate with the teacher. In a classroom, it can be difficult for a teacher to attend to the emotional needs of every student, and at the same time, parents may find it hard to understand their child's situation at school. Therefore, it is best for parents to communicate with the teacher. This allows the teacher to understand the child's condition and cater to their needs, and it also helps the parents to understand their child's situation at school. I hope this can be helpful to you.

Hello! I can definitely sense your anxiety, as my own child is also starting preschool this year. As parents, what can we do for our children when they leave us and enter into a new environment? Let's discuss this together and hopefully find some inspiration and help. First of all, let's talk about the psychological characteristics of children in the first grade, which is around 6-7 years old. According to Yale University's research on children aged 0-14, "He lives in his own secret garden, full of melancholy. He may feel that others don't like him and intentionally cause trouble for him. A 7-year-old child easily imagines things in a negative way." This stage can be considered as the second so-called "rebellious period" for children, but from your description, it seems that your child is experiencing more of a separation anxiety feeling. In this situation, on one hand, you shouldn't give up easily but rather think that she needs you more than the school does. Eventually, children will have to enter their own stage of growth, and going to school is not only about acquiring necessary knowledge and skills but more importantly, it is about stepping into a collective life and laying a good foundation for their future integration into society. She also needs her own friends, companions, and friendships. At this time, parents should first regulate their own psychological state and not be so anxious, accepting the reactions caused by the change in environment. You and your partner can create a safer and more comfortable environment, making the child believe in herself. The premise is that as parents, you must believe in your child, believe that she can grow and adapt. Of course, this doesn't mean to be heartless parents, letting the child's anxiety spread uncontrollably. You can provide the child with some adaptation experience when you started elementary school, so that the child can understand that this is a necessary path for everyone's growth and going to school is not that scary. Make the child enjoy school, teachers, classmates, and the collective atmosphere. Clearly tell the child that she goes to school, mom and dad go to work, and who will pick her up after school, so that the child can study and live at ease during the day. In addition, maintain a positive mindset and communication with the school system, teachers, and believe that everyone has gone through this stage. Try not to express dissatisfaction about the school or teachers in front of the child. You can discuss it privately with your partner, which is more appropriate for quickly adapting the child to the collective school life. Be a learning parent, face it and grow together with the child. Finally, believe that everything is arranged for the best, and the world loves you!

Children have just entered elementary school and are not used to the school life, so they may have difficulty adapting for a while. They may feel nervous, curious, and deal with new relationships on their own. It may be easier for outgoing and lively children to go through this process quickly, while introverted children may need some time to adapt to this state. In the face of this situation, parents and teachers should not be too anxious. 
1. Teachers and parents should cooperate and not put too much pressure on children. According to the child's situation, a gradual approach should be taken to help the child gradually adapt to the faster pace of elementary school learning. Teachers should also take as much responsibility as possible for the child's learning and homework, while parents should cooperate and not focus too much on academic performance. They should actively communicate with their children to ease their psychological pressure and overly sensitive traits.
2. Let children participate more in society. For children who are overly sensitive, it is recommended that mothers do not take children out alone, but rather take them to participate in team activities and let them experience social life and meet different people. Through these aspects, help children expand their interpersonal relationships and adapt to society.
3. Accompany children to read more books. Since the child is only in first grade, there may be some books that they cannot fully understand, but it doesn't matter. Mothers can read to them before bed. Generally, extensive reading will allow children to have a better understanding of themselves and understand reasoning. This is beneficial for broadening their horizons, widening their perspectives, and helping them resolve some psychological issues. They will gradually resolve internal conflicts through reading.
4. Seek help from a psychologist. If the child is under too much pressure and neither teachers nor parents can solve it, the mother can take the child to see a psychologist. There is no need to be embarrassed, and the psychology department should not be seen as a psychiatry department. It is important to approach this situation rationally. Actively seeking medical help and seeking assistance from a doctor may quickly reveal the child's problem. This way, teachers, parents, and doctors can work together to find the right solution and improve the child's situation.
5. Regardless, as a parent, it is important to unconditionally care for the child with love and regularly encourage them. Labels should not be attached to the child, and comparisons with other children should be avoided. By starting from the details of daily life, identifying the causes of the child's problems, and providing targeted solutions, children can grow up happily and joyfully.

After reading your description, I can sense that you have some concerns, but mainly you hope that your child can quickly adapt to this new environment. The connection between mother and child is deep, and entering a new environment can be a big challenge. When transitioning from a comfortable and safe environment to an unfamiliar and challenging one, everyone will have some reactions, especially a first-grade child who may have difficulty expressing their feelings. Making the child feel safe is something we can do. 1. Adjust your own state and acknowledge her anxiety. Say things to her that she can understand, like "Mom knows that you might feel uneasy in the new environment, but it's okay. Mom will be waiting for you at home and Mom believes in you. Let's face this challenge together." 2. Also, during other times at home, do things to increase the child's sense of security, have one-on-one interactions with her, and give more hugs. 3. Try asking about the good things at school. When the child can describe some positive experiences, the attractiveness of the school will increase. 4. Give timely rewards and focus only on the positive aspects. When she improves even just a little bit compared to the previous day, appreciate her and let her understand that she's making progress. Take it slowly, this process is not easy, but remember that your child is slowly transitioning and starting her socialization. It's a process of growth for both her and you.

question: After waiting for a year and investing time and money, I found out that my name was not on the list.
description: I am a fresh graduate this year and I wanted to go somewhere to work and learn. However, my parents said that I haven't worked for a year and they have invested so much in me. But today, my name is not on the registration list. I really feel like I can't go on living anymore. I feel like my future is going to be spent in a small county town. It's really frustrating to not have a job after a whole year, and I don't want to live like this anymore.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, guilt and shame, vulnerability and tears.

answers.answer_text: Hug the questioner. I have experienced a similar situation before. I was in my senior year when I spent several months learning and my family arranged for an expert to train me through connections. I passed the written test but during the interview, I found out that the competitor was the daughter of a unit leader. As long as I didn't surpass the other person by a large margin, they would prioritize choosing her. When I first learned about the result, I was devastated and felt hopeless. It took me some time to recover. [Problem analysis] From the question, we can see that both you and your family have put in a lot of effort for this job, which is why you can't accept the outcome. In addition, you don't want to stay in a small county and hope to move to a better city, so it feels even more painful now. [Understanding and analysis] 1. Because I have experienced a similar situation, I can understand your pain. The main reason I was able to move on was the comfort of my parents. They quickly accepted the result and comforted me. They also allowed me to take a break at home without looking for a job until I recovered. Therefore, I think you can talk to your parents about your feelings, and explain your efforts and distress. I believe your parents can understand and support you. 2. Apply the ABC theory of emotions reasonably. According to the ABC theory of emotions, the current unpleasant emotions are not caused by the event itself, but by our cognition. In your cognition, you think this failure is extremely bad and believe that it cannot be changed, which leads to extreme emotions. In fact, one failure does not represent anything. You have just graduated, and there are still many opportunities in life. After all, even people who have been working for many years like us may resign or change jobs due to dissatisfaction with work. 3. Learn to do career planning and utilize it to re-plan your career path. Since you want to leave the small county, we can make a 3-year plan to enrich yourself and at the same time pay attention to better job opportunities while working. Once again, hug the questioner. A major failure can indeed be a huge blow, but the most important thing is to analyze the problems and avoid making the same mistakes in the future. I hope my understanding and analysis can help you.

Title, hello~ Hugs to you. Life is bound to encounter various setbacks and difficulties, but never ever think negatively. There are many beautiful things in life, such as the care of parents, the love of friends, and so on. But have you ever thought about what these setbacks can bring us? They temper our will and allow us to see our own shortcomings. In fact, these are things we can change. It's not necessarily true that putting in a lot of effort will yield good results. Without enough qualifications, we may not be able to persist until the end. So, there are still many things we can do and change. Although finding a job may be difficult, we can always find one eventually. Sometimes it's not that we can't, but that we lack confidence. Sometimes, it's not that we can't do it, but that our standards are too high. We can try to lower our expectations, start working, and gradually, step by step, we will achieve good results.
