Don't lose heart, keep up the good work! Good luck~ The world and I love you!

Hello! I understand your disappointment, sending you a hug! Because your name is not on the registration list, you may feel that all the effort you put in before seems to be in vain. You feel very disappointed and defeated, thinking that you won't be able to make it in the county in the future and even have thoughts of not wanting to live anymore. Perhaps, based on your current experiences and knowledge, experiencing something like this seems like a huge blow, and you feel that your future is bleak. However, if we look at it from a longer-term perspective, from a broader point of view, no single event can determine our entire life. We often easily fall into a pessimistic and negative mindset, thinking that if we encounter setbacks now, there will be no hope in the future; thinking that the current situation is terrible, so everything else will be terrible too. However, the reality is not like that. If you don't believe it, look back at the setbacks you faced before, and now looking back, does everything seem trivial? Many things in our lives are like this. We feel that they are a big deal at the time, but after going through that period, the rain clears and you will find that all the anxiety, disappointment, and even despair were just temporary. Just as the ancient poem says: "Mountains and rivers may block our way, but when the willows are dim, again blooms a village." So, don't be pessimistic, and most importantly, don't lose hope. Just focus on what you can do at the moment and wait patiently for the right time. You never know what might happen next moment, and perhaps, a pleasant surprise awaits you. Just like the saying goes: "Misfortune may be a blessing in disguise." Maybe, not being on the list this time means that there will be better choices and opportunities ahead. Sending you another hug, the world and I love you!

Thank you for bringing back memories of my early days after graduating. I also had a hard time finding a job right after graduation, and when I finally found one, it was challenging to get through the probation period. With each setback, it was inevitable to feel pessimistic. I would return home feeling dejected. The first few days were alright, and everything felt harmonious. My wounded heart was slowly being healed. However, as time went by, my healed heart became pessimistic again. In the whole village, everyone my age had jobs, and I was the only young person wandering around. How would you feel in such a situation? I gradually stopped going out, too ashamed to face the world. Being at home was boring, so I ended up lying in bed all day, unable to sleep. My parents started nagging constantly. Anger, discomfort, and pessimism filled my mind. How did I overcome this? Firstly, I had to build up my confidence. Regardless of how life kept knocking me down, I had to remain confident. I constantly repeated to myself, "I can do it." Secondly, I had to be proactive. I actively sought for jobs, without setting my sights too high, without envying others' jobs and salaries. I had to have a humble mindset and be willing to start from the bottom. Thirdly, I needed to communicate more with my classmates. If it was possible to go out, I shouldn't stay at home. Job hunting with classmates would provide mutual encouragement and assistance. Lastly, I needed to have a relaxed and open mindset.

question: Refusing to grow in terms of parent-child relationships, what defense mechanism is being exalted?
description: I have studied psychology for many years and have always been entangled in my own family and personal issues, always wanting to grow myself. My relationship with my eight-year-old son is always awkward, but I refuse to learn about parenting courses, even resisting it. I know that the main problem at present is the issue of educating my child, but I refuse to grow in this area. What defense mechanism is at play here?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP ~ The impact that the origin family has on you is significant. Even though you have been studying psychology for many years, you still have a aversion to parent-child relationships! After studying psychology for so many years, I believe you are familiar with psychology, and it has subtly changed and grown you a lot. Some traumas cannot simply be forgotten or forgiven. Many times, we maintain happiness, but it's not truly happiness, it's just superficial. Psychology is a very good subject. If you study it well, it can help us solve many emotional problems in life and bring us more happiness. This requires a process. Original family vs parent-child relationships: follow your own feelings. The harm caused by the origin family has been a long time ago. If you want to study psychology, then study psychology. If you don't want to study parent-child relationships, then don't force yourself to learn. Parent-child relationships are actually about interpersonal relationships. If you become excellent and a role model for your child, they will naturally be close to you. Communicate with your child, tell them your thoughts, sit down with them for a serious conversation. You can tell them that you love them but you need time to adjust yourself, and hope they can give you some time. In life, you should do well for yourself, don't do things you don't like, do what you want to do, study other aspects of psychology well. It will be growth for you and will have an impact on your child!

Hello, when I saw your question, I felt the conflict within you. At this moment, it seems like you are in a struggle between prioritizing yourself or your son. I have been studying psychology for several years and have always believed that personal growth is very important. However, because of the relationship with your son, you feel that learning about parenting is also important for you. From your description, it seems like deep down in your heart, you want to prioritize your own growth, but external pressures make you feel that dealing with the parent-child relationship is also important. Therefore, you are now caught in a dilemma of whether to focus on your personal growth first or to learn how to handle the parent-child relationship first. Is this the case? It seems like you are putting this choice on opposite ends. If you choose to focus on your own growth, it seems like you won't be able to pay enough attention to the parent-child relationship. And if you choose to learn about parenting, it seems like you won't have the time and energy to take care of yourself and grow personally. Is this really the case? Personal growth and the parent-child relationship are not opposing ends. Especially in relationships, it's the mutual influence between two people. I believe that your growth and changes can be felt and influenced by your child. So I understand that your reluctance to learn about parenting is not a defense mechanism, but rather a deep belief that personal growth is more important. If you don't grow personally, no matter how much knowledge you acquire about parenting, it won't be effective. Therefore, follow your inner self and focus on your own growth first. This process is not easy, and I wish you all the best!

question: I am now afraid of falling in love with someone because I am afraid of the fear of losing and gaining. What should I do?
description: In my first relationship, I placed my entire life on my ex-boyfriend's shoulders. We were together for two years and then broke up amicably. Now, during this blind date, I met a mature and outstanding guy. I'm afraid, afraid that if I start to like him, I will feel inferior, thinking that I'm not good enough. I'm afraid that I will depend on him, afraid of the fear of losing out on something, and even longing to lose it so that I won't feel this fear. But, I can't just choose to lose when I meet someone I like and evade it, right?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. The mentality of relying on love and feeling inferior and afraid of losing reflect what? You said, "I have entrusted my whole life to my ex-boyfriend." By emphasizing the word "entrust," it shows a state of wanting to depend on others. In a healthy intimate relationship, two independent individuals should be together, not one person bearing the emotional weight of two people. You also said, "When I meet a mature and outstanding guy, I am afraid and feel inferior." The fear of not being good enough when encountering someone outstanding is because you stubbornly believe that you have no outstanding qualities that can match them, and thus fear being abandoned. In fact, the definition of strengths is broad, whether it is fair skin, beauty, long legs, or being calm/funny/gentle/empathetic, they are all manifestations of different strengths in different people. Under the influence of losing oneself and fearing not being good enough, you develop a tendency to avoid love in order to avoid the idea of losing. So, how can you fill yourself and become confident and outstanding? It can be through small daily things, such as starting to learn a hobby like drawing/calligraphy/exercising/running, or by frequently fulfilling your little desires, like buying clothes you like/small toys/trying out your favorite food. When you start satisfying yourself and enriching your spiritual world, you are filling yourself, becoming confident, and gaining a sense of self-worth. You will no longer be an empty shell that always wants to depend on others and entrust everything to them, fearing being abandoned. On the contrary, a self with a sense of value will become a person with agency, actively choosing to start or end a relationship, rather than passively fearing loss.

【Love is beautiful, losing it may not necessarily be a bad thing】【First of all】, those conflicting thoughts in your mind show that you actually have a strong desire for love. It's just that because you desire it so much, wanting to keep it forever, you become afraid of losing it. 【Secondly】, love is beautiful. It makes people feel sweet, warm, happy, loved, cared for, and even protected. It is something that many people yearn for because it truly is something wonderful, and everyone deserves to have it! 【Thirdly】, losing love may not necessarily be a bad thing. I understand that people are afraid of separation, the more we lose, the more intense our emotions become. But in reality, there are benefits to a breakup: 1. You can do things that you've always wanted to do but didn't have time for. 2. You can rediscover yourself and realize: Oh, so this is what I'm like. 3. You can readjust yourself because upon discovering the new you, you will be willing to adjust your thoughts and behaviors and continue to be true to yourself. 4. You can fall in love with yourself again. Many times, we neglect our own needs and desires because of external circumstances. Take this opportunity to see and fulfill your own wishes. 【Fourth】, say "yes" to your original self. In a relationship, many people forget about themselves, just like how you magnify your partner's strengths but forget that you also have strengths. In fact, you are someone who knows how to appreciate others, but it would be even better if you stop denying yourself. You should know that even if you feel inferior, you are still deserving of love. You have already done well, and everyone likes you the way you are. 【Fifth】, relationships are equal. Boys also have moments of insecurity. He is also afraid of losing you because you are unique. You have strengths and weaknesses, and so does he. 【Sixth】, he belongs only to himself. Whether in a relationship or after a breakup, from beginning to end, he does not belong to you, he only belongs to himself. If you have never possessed him, then why fear losing him? The same goes for you, you only belong to yourself, you don't belong to anyone else. It's important to learn to set boundaries, not excessively rely on or possess someone. When someone has a strong possessive desire, they lose more, but by relaxing and letting go, they find serenity and gain more. 【Seventh】, life is impermanent. Life is like a train heading towards the grave. Whether you like it or not, there will definitely be people getting on and off along the way. This is a matter of fate and also a plan of a higher power. It is something within the boundaries set by a higher power, and it is not up to us to control. When we get involved, we invite troubles. 【Eighth】, you have done your best. Even if you lose, you have already done your best. Learn to accept that we are all human and have our limitations. But as long as you have done your best, there will be no regrets. It is enough to do what is within your boundaries. 【Ninth】, live in the present. The things you worry about are things in the future. If both of you truly love each other, then take this opportunity to seize the present and try to build a relationship. Love, just like work, can be learned and developed as you go. Communicate more, be honest, and there will be fewer misunderstandings and less worries. May you enjoy the present, wishing you the best, Namaste！

Title sponsor, Saturday, hug you! The shadow of the previous relationship has left a mark on your heart, causing you to worry and fear the next one. Since it has already happened, can we just accept it? Your inner instinct wants to avoid the possibility of further hurt by escaping. While accepting it, let's also understand that it is for our own good, okay? I believe you have already been able to completely move on from the previous relationship. What remains in our hearts is only the outcome and memories, which can also be seen as a growth experience, right? Your awakening has made you realize that relying solely on instinctive goodwill is not enough to invest in the next relationship. In this new relationship, he seems outstanding and attractive, and the worries of gain and loss are instincts trying to protect us in their own way. Thank them and confidently lift your head, telling yourself that you are capable of taking care of yourself and are ready for the next relationship. Regardless of the outcome, this is your choice, and you are the one in charge of your own life. Above all, the world and I love you! If you need further consultation or have any concerns, feel free to message me.

The questioner is right. We can't always choose to lose and avoid when we meet someone we like. So what should we do? The reason why we feel afraid and choose to lose is because we use our previous emotional experiences as reference and fear encountering the same results, thus falling into a state of obsession. Once we understand this, we can actively change our behavior, break the cycle of obsession. How do we do that? By recording our thinking process, there are three aspects to record: thoughts, feelings, and actions. This is because when in a state of obsession, it's often difficult for people to control their thoughts and feelings. Just like you said, "When you meet a mature and excellent boy, you feel afraid. Afraid that after liking him, you'll feel inferior and think you're not good enough. Afraid of getting attached, and afraid of losing and being ambivalent." So, in order to break free from this, an important method is to separate thoughts, feelings, and actions, and break free from the interference of thoughts and feelings by learning to control our actions. First, learn to control our actions and then use the change in actions to influence the change in thoughts and feelings. So, how do we differentiate thoughts, feelings, and actions? When recording, you can refer to the following six questions. Firstly, what causes these thoughts? Secondly, what thoughts come to mind? Thirdly, what feelings do you have? Fourthly, what do you want to do? Fifthly, what did you do? And finally, what was the result? By effectively distinguishing our thoughts, feelings, and actions through recording, and then controlling our actions, we can free ourselves from the interference of thoughts and feelings, thus breaking the cycle of obsession and living the happy life we desire.

There is no right or wrong in life, only problems and emotions. When you insist on right and wrong, emotions arise, and emotions become problems. This is the first sentence. Facing problems and generating emotions, emotions become new problems, even igniting a series of emotions. This is the second sentence. Whether it's problems or emotions, the way to face them is to let go or accept them. Don't use tolerance and patience to replace them, thus covering up emotions and problems. This is the third sentence. Emotions and problems can arise in life anytime and anywhere. When you repeatedly practice the above three sentences, if you still have emotions, it's really necessary to generate more and bigger emotions and problems to awaken you. Let go and accept, everything returns to its original state. Continuously holding on, below is a simplest problem - paying the bill. This bill needs to be paid by yourself, but some people may never have the opportunity to pay such a bill in their entire lives. Let go of the past and start anew. Wish you well.

question: What should I do if I feel very oppressed when I apologize and admit my mistakes, but still get blamed?
description: A year ago, I had a lot on my plate because I was taking extra courses and working part-time. I would stay up late and wake up early, which affected my dorm roommates' rest and led to a sudden outbreak of conflict with one roommate who I already had a strained relationship with. Because I was busy with my studies and gradually drifting apart from the other two roommates, the situation inexplicably worsened. Due to the exhaustion I felt both physically and mentally, I unintentionally exhibited some self-centered behaviors, coupled with my roommates complaining about me to other classmates, I believe that my peers also view me with a certain bias. But what I didn't expect was that the counselor and teachers also hold similar opinions of me, for example, the counselor criticized me through a voice message for being too arrogant and self-centered. For instance, this year, a new teacher I didn't know started our conversation by saying that I'm a very self-centered student. I'm actually quite confused and upset. I have always admitted that it was my fault to disturb my classmates' sleep, and I have apologized to them and tried my best to finish my work earlier and go to bed earlier. Even when the workload reached its peak, I would find a hotel or study room to stay overnight. It's true that I was in the wrong for disturbing others' sleep, but I feel really wronged. Now I feel like nothing I do has any meaning, and everything I say is considered low emotional intelligence and incorrect. I really want to escape from this world.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, roommates, classmates, and interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello there, I feel sorry and empathetic when I see you are feeling distressed. From your description, it seems that your late nights and early mornings due to academic and part-time work have had an impact on your roommate's rest, causing a rift between you and the other two roommates. In addition, due to fatigue, you unconsciously made some independent decisions. However, what surprised and upset you the most is not only the judgment from your classmates, but also the criticism from the counselor and teachers, including the new ones, which has made you feel very sad and upset. You have recognized that your behavior was inappropriate, and you have apologized to them and made the greatest effort to improve. But this has left you feeling unjust, making you question the meaning of everything you do and feeling that anything you say or do is wrong due to low emotional intelligence. I can sense the frustration and isolation you are experiencing. Especially when admitting a mistake only leads to criticism, it is even more frustrating and suppressing. In psychology, it is said that emotions matter more than facts. The first thing you need to do is to release your emotions. Exercise or spending time in nature are good ways to do this. Additionally, "writing therapy" is also a method worth mentioning. It consists of four stages: releasing stress, filling inner voids, enjoying body and mind, and daring to create. The book "I Write with My Heart" is worth reading and practicing. Moreover, you can use mindfulness meditation to be aware of your emotions at all times and carefully observe them, allowing the intensity and strength of your emotions to decrease and become more peaceful. These two points are not only useful for your current emotions but also for your studies, part-time work, and even future paths in life. As for the conflicts with your classmates, you have already apologized, but perhaps it did not have the desired effect, and this is indeed infuriating. However, we cannot change others, so maybe we can think of a few more ways from our own perspective. For example, regarding the effectiveness of communication, you can read "Nonviolent Communication," which uses the steps of observation, feeling, need, and request to more peacefully achieve your goals. The book "The Art of Communication" provides a comprehensive and systematic introduction to the principles and methods of communication, which may also be helpful. Relationships are the basis of everything. From your description, it seems that your current focus has always been on academics and part-time work, resulting in the impact on your current interpersonal relationships. It is not wrong to prioritize studying, but on the other hand, we also need to understand that interpersonal relationships are important in this world. Even the misunderstandings from your teachers may be related to not putting effort into building these relationships. We are social beings. Whether we are in school or enter society in the future, without relationships, it may be difficult for us to make progress. It is not too late to mend the fence. If you realize the importance of relationships, you may take the initiative to communicate with teachers and classmates. In this regard, you can refer to cognitive courses taught by Professor Li Songwei to improve yourself. I hope my response can provide you with some inspiration and thoughts. The world and I love you.

From your question, I can sense your frustration and helplessness. Firstly, it is commendable that you have the ability to reflect and be self-aware. For example, you are aware that your actions have indeed affected others' sleep and rest, and you are willing to take responsibility by apologizing. These are aspects worth acknowledging. However, it is important for you to understand that even if you have done your best in a particular matter - such as trying to complete your work early and go to bed early, or not returning to the dormitory during peak workload to avoid disturbing others - your standards may not necessarily align with others. Each person has their own threshold, and these differences in standards are neither right nor wrong, just different. Even if you have tried your best, it may still be insufficient based on the standards of some people. I hope you can accept this difference in a heartfelt manner. 

Secondly, stereotypes are a common phenomenon in interpersonal relationships, which is why many people value social impression management. Perhaps it is not scientifically sound, but it does exist in reality. The initial impression you have given others may indeed be difficult to erase, as you mentioned, even with an apology. This is also an objective phenomenon. What I want to say is that existence is reasonable. Perhaps you feel that it is unfair, but the phenomenon of stereotypes is not specifically targeted at you, it just exists. We can try our best to accept this objective existence. 

Thirdly, your feelings of frustration and powerlessness are, to some extent, a sense of frustration caused by a lack of control. Perhaps subconsciously you hold the belief that although you may not have done well in the past, you have now made changes and apologized, so others should change their perception of you. When this desire is not fulfilled, it can lead to deep feelings of frustration and powerlessness, and the desire to escape. I understand your feelings very well, but if you bring this subconscious belief into consciousness, you may notice that this "should" itself is an imagination. In simple terms, I am voicing out to the world, but the world may not respond as I wish, isn't that right? In the above three points, I have said some things that may be painful to hear, but they may be closer to the objective reality. The truth is often cruel and unfair from our individual perspective, but these feelings are only measured from our own perspective. From an objective perspective, their existence has its rationale. I often quote the words of psychologist Thomas Moore: the best treatment for someone is to shorten the distance between them and the truth. Perhaps these truths make you feel discouraged, but only by truly acknowledging their existence can our troubles truly diminish. Of course, this does not mean you should resign yourself to it; it means that I hope you can seek more favorable methods based on accepting the truth. Just as Romain Rolland said: There is only one kind of heroism in the world: to love life even after understanding the truth of life. You can try the following: First, step out of the feeling of "nothing I do matters, whatever I say is wrong, and it's low emotional intelligence." Just as what I said earlier may be closer to objective reality, feeling like nothing matters and thinking that everything you say is wrong and reflects low emotional intelligence are your current “feelings,” not objective reality. In life, we are often influenced by feelings and emotions, thus losing our connection with the real world. At such times, maybe you need to remind yourself on a conscious level that although I feel discouraged, I still have one freedom: the freedom to choose whether to accept this feeling and let it manipulate me or not accept it and try other alternatives. Your sense of powerlessness is a feeling, and you can coexist with it, but the choice to determine your own fate always lies in your hands. Second, try genuine expression and effective communication. The essence of genuine expression is sincere expression without judgment. You can express your feelings, expectations, and goodwill. Many people are unwilling to express themselves genuinely because they subconsciously believe that by doing so, they become "weak" and this perceived vulnerability triggers strong feelings of shame. But this is still a feeling rooted in early experiences, not a fact. In fact, only true courage allows us to face ourselves and express ourselves sincerely. Third, accept the real world and continually align your feelings with reality. I believe this is the most important point. When you continually step out of your own world, you will gradually see that every person in this world has different standards and perspectives, and they each have their reasons, most of whom believe their own perspective is the most correct. However, true experts know that there is more than one standard. Similarly, whether others accept or misunderstand you often has less to do with what you have done, but rather what they project onto you. "We can only change what we can change ourselves," you have definitely heard this sentence, but truly understanding it may require more effort. We cannot control others' standards, perspectives, or judgments, but we can continually enhance our own cognition. When you can overlook the world, accept that life is a complex ecological balance, perhaps you will truly find serenity. Wishing you the best. I am Tang Tang, a nationally certified level 2 psychological consultant with a focus on motivational psychology. I am a contracted author on multiple platforms and also a mentor dedicated to spreading psychological knowledge. If you have any psychological issues, feel free to send me a private message.

Hello, the title owner is facing a heavy workload due to studying and part-time work, resulting in staying up late and waking up early, which has affected the rest of the roommate. As a result, the relationship with the roommate has become abnormally tense and gradually worsened. The title owner realizes that they have behaved selfishly, causing trouble for classmates. Although they know they were wrong and have apologized, they have found that they have not been forgiven by everyone. Now, everyone seems to have formed a consensus that you are a "selfish person," even teachers who don't know you have made this judgment, which has made you feel very troubled and unsure of what to do. When I saw the title owner's question, it reminded me of a classic Japanese drama called "The Wild Pig Transformation." The male protagonist, Shuji, was originally the most popular person in school, loved by all classmates. But in reality, he was working hard to maintain relationships with everyone and couldn't refuse any requests. However, due to a series of misunderstandings, such as being afraid of getting involved in disputes and not stepping in to help a classmate who was being beaten, Shuji was perceived as a "selfish person" by everyone, and his classmates began to isolate him. Despite his attempts to explain, it seemed that "no one would believe him." Adolescence is a crucial period for the development of self-identity, and we especially want to fit in because being part of a group gives us a sense of belonging and worth. The female lead in "The Wild Pig Transformation," Kotani, was not popular from a young age due to childhood trauma and was also subjected to bullying by others. But she was determined to become popular. In the process of being transformed, Kotani didn't try to please everyone like Shuji did. Instead, she had her principles, remained true to herself, and sincerely interacted with others, offering help. In the end, everyone liked the original Kotani. As for Shuji, after being isolated by his classmates, he discovered that true friends will always believe in him because they have seen the genuine side of each other. "We believe in the people we want to believe in." So, although he appeared to have lost a large social circle, he actually had stronger friendships. After saying so much, I just want the title owner to feel a bit more relieved. If you have sincerely apologized, maybe what's left is not to keep emphasizing or forcing others to forgive you, but to use more concrete actions and gradually change everyone's perception of you, showing them that you also care about others and value friendship. Moreover, I believe there are friends who trust and understand you. Talk to them more, and you can also get a lot of help from them. Keep it up!

Dear friend: I read your story about the difficult relationships with people at school, and it's clear that you're not happy. You feel misunderstood and unaccepted. Sending you a hug. First of all, it takes courage to take responsibility for your actions, admit your mistakes, and apologize. You have also made concessions by finding accommodation in hotels and other classrooms, but unfortunately, no one understands or sees the effort you put in. It must have been embarrassing when the teacher publicly criticized you, making you feel like you're being discriminated against by those around you. All of these things have made you suffer, and you're afraid and unsure how long it will last, making you want to escape the future. But please don't be impulsive. Many problems can be solved. [Firstly] Release emotions and let go of all the pain. Since you are feeling so burdened and suffering, it's important to release it all. Find a place where there is no one and let out all the pain. No matter how grievances, painful, or sad you are, you can let it all out. There's no need to keep it all inside. If you feel like crying, go ahead, as tears can release hormones that can help relieve stress. Try to remove your negative emotions. [Secondly], understand and accept that you haven't been abandoned. You long for people around you to understand and accept you again, but unfortunately, they don't. However, don't lose hope because what you long for hasn't been taken away. You yourself can understand and accept yourself. Let go of the self-blame from the past, forgive yourself for your mistakes. Know that errors are also part of the learning process. Understand yourself well, see the improvements you have made, and accept yourself again. [Thirdly] Live in the present and let go of the past. Leave the past behind and draw a line between it and the present. Don't dwell on the past or let it hurt you again. Other people's opinions and comments are their own business, but at least don't mentally hurt and damage yourself anymore. Focus on the present, learn the professional knowledge well, and do your part-time job well. [Fourthly] Learn nonviolent communication. Communication problems between people often stem from a methodological issue. They think they are right, and you think you are right too. In order to argue about right and wrong, things can quickly escalate and explode. But by doing so, both sides hinder the understanding of the truth, as the explosion of emotions blocks the real exchange. By learning, you may not prevent others from blaming or exploding, but you can learn not to explode and instead speak from your heart. In fact, your article already shows shades of nonviolent communication, indicating that you have the potential to learn. Everything that happens has a reason. It's not trying to drive us away, but rather wants us to learn to change or accept. There's no need to be too pessimistic. The occurrence of events might not be as bad as we think; it's our worries that make it seem worse. I hope you can forgive yourself, pick yourself up, and become a renewed version of yourself! Best wishes! Your friend, Audrey.

Hello child! Seeing your question, first and foremost, I want to give you a hug. You are such a hardworking child, but you haven't received understanding from your classmates and teachers. You try your best to please them, but they become even more unreasonable. This is not your fault. You are a positive and proactive person. As teachers, they should encourage students to progress and inspire them to strive for excellence. As we enter higher education, it's not just about learning textbook knowledge, but also gradually interacting with society. This is a transitional period with society. Taking on part-time jobs is a good way to interact with society in advance and understand how society operates. This way, when you truly leave the campus, you won't be afraid of feeling lost or directionless, nor will you worry about struggling to survive or casually taking any job to get by. You can also earn some money while doing part-time work. Do what you think is right. Have you heard of the 80/20 rule? Eighty percent of the world revolves around the other twenty percent. Although you don't know if you will be part of that twenty percent in the future, at least your current efforts will someday reward you. Stick to doing what you love without being influenced. Try to do it in a way that everyone can accept, like renting a hotel, to show that you are someone who can persist, endure hardships, and have ideas. You don't need to feel distressed or even give up yourself like others just because others don't understand. Be yourself, and it's the one who laughs last that wins. You don't need to care about others' words. A person who dares to dream and work hard is worth being treated gently by society. I hope you can persevere for your goals. Cheer up, the world and I love you!

question: I feel uncomfortable as soon as I arrive at work. What should I do if I am allergic to work?
description: At first, I thought I was allergic to formaldehyde in the classroom. My neck felt tight and my hair stood on end. When I felt uncomfortable, I couldn't breathe properly. Later, I went to the hospital for examination and found out that it was due to excessive psychological stress. Whenever I was in class, I felt uncomfortable, just thinking about things in class made me feel uneasy. Even after work, I still couldn't relax because of the issues at work. For example, unfair treatment by the class monitor, leaders giving me difficult tasks, and not knowing how to greet people I interact with at work. I feel angry and blame myself at the same time. The main problem is that I can't control my physical reactions, my neck feels uncomfortable and I get headaches. However, as soon as I leave the classroom environment, I feel much better. I want to take a leave of absence, but I don't know what reason to give. I don't know what kind of job to look for because I have no strengths, abilities, good image, or good social skills. I also have poor physical endurance, and I recently injured my ligament. I am currently in a state of helplessness and despair. If I lose my job and can't find another one, I'm afraid I will become even more anxious. Even having food to eat will become a problem.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand the stress and difficulties that work and interpersonal relationships can bring to you. You also experience physical pain as a physiological response to psychological stress, and you fear not being able to find another job, which causes you anxiety. Regarding your current situation and mindset, let's analyze it together and try to find a breakthrough. Problem analysis: You experience headaches and difficulty breathing whenever you are at work, and medical examinations have confirmed that it is caused by psychological factors. You feel helpless and self-blame due to the unfairness at work and your inability to handle interpersonal relationships with colleagues. The physical discomfort is an external manifestation of your inner struggle and reminds you that changes need to be made. However, your first thought is to avoid it, take a leave of absence, and find another job, which only increases your anxiety. You are uncertain about what reason to give for taking leave and afraid of not finding a new job. The unfairness at work is an uncontrollable external factor, while establishing relationships with colleagues and improving skills and appearance are controllable internal factors. Your pain stems from a lack of control over life, which leads to existential anxiety. You overlook the fact that you can improve and take control of things through your own efforts. Suggestions: 1. Don't get too caught up in uncontrollable external factors. Focus on doing your own work well. However, if you find it difficult to accept the unfairness at work and the company's corporate culture, leaving the current environment and finding a company that aligns with your values is the best choice. You can continue working while seeking other job opportunities. 2. Focus on what you can control. Don't attribute your current situation to bad luck. If you are physically weak, you can strengthen your body through exercise. If your skills are lacking, you can focus on skill improvement and become an excellent person. If your appearance is not good, you can dress neatly and cleanly. When you take responsibility for your life, you will have more opportunities for choices. 3. To deal with your current anxiety, you can actively cope with it through exercise, mindfulness meditation, and most importantly, facing the challenges in life. When you regain a sense of control over yourself and become proactive, you will have the confidence to bring about change.

Hello, the immense psychological pressure has caused severe physical reactions in you. In my opinion, some of this psychological pressure indeed comes from external sources, but most of it comes from yourself. From your text, I read the following traits in you: 1. You do not have clear boundaries between work and life, often allowing work to affect your personal life. 2. You have shortcomings in handling interpersonal relationships. 3. You lack confidence and have low self-worth, filled with anxiety about the future. 4. You tend to attribute problems internally when confronted with them. These traits are gradually developed during our growth process and are the result of everyone adapting to the environment at that time. When the surrounding environment changes, our coping patterns also need to change. If we rigidly adhere to our old coping patterns without distinction, not only will we not be able to cope with current difficulties, but it will also cause internal conflicts and discomfort. Therefore, it is necessary to make self-adjustments to our coping patterns. Here are some suggestions: 1. Change your beliefs. What triggers our emotions is not the event itself, but our perception of the event. When faced with events that trouble us, if we can change our perspective or switch roles to look at the situation, we may have a different discovery and perhaps gain a different understanding of the event. 2. Make adjustments in behavior. It is necessary to reflect on ourselves in a timely manner and constantly monitor our emotions. When emotional reactions have already occurred, we can use methods such as deep breathing, redirecting our attention, and engaging in activities that make us happy to timely liberate ourselves from negative emotions. 3. Make changes in problem-solving approaches. Usually, there are more than three solutions to every problem. One correct approach to problem-solving is "effective thinking, reasonable action, and timely adjustment." When we can control our emotions and calmly face problems, we have the best beginning to solving them. After effective thinking, the action plan derived needs to be implemented. This plan may not be something we are good at, so we need to execute it through reasonable actions instead of letting it remain just a plan. Finally, after taking action, it is necessary to summarize in a timely manner, confirm the effectiveness, and if the result is not satisfactory, make timely adjustments and redevelop the plan. Through these adjustments, we can solve troubles promptly when encountering them, and I believe you will gradually build confidence and a sense of self-worth. If you still struggle to make adjustments, you can seek professional psychological counseling. Additionally, regarding the work issues you described, here are two points for your reference: 1. Accept the problems you are facing and communicate with your stable-minded workplace leaders, describing the difficulties you are encountering (as objective facts rather than personal judgments), such as the physiological reactions that occur when entering your current job position or practical difficulties you have encountered. Seek solutions through communication with your leaders. 2. Make a long-term career plan for yourself (you can seek help from professionals), clearly define your future direction and methods of achievement, and then pursue it unwaveringly. I hope the above is helpful to you.

Hello, I can see that you feel helpless and desperate, and it pains me to see that. I want to give you a big hug, and another hug, and another hug. "Feeling uncomfortable as soon as you arrive at work and being allergic to work," "Even after work, you still can't get over the issues from work," "Feeling angry while also feeling guilty. The main issue is that I can't control my physical reactions, and I feel uncomfortable in my neck and have headaches." What a terrible experience. The fact that you can endure in such an environment where your body, emotions, and thoughts are so uncomfortable shows how much courage and endurance you have. I want to give you a big thumbs up. When you mentioned feeling "helpless and desperate," if you were to rate these feelings on a scale of 0-10, with 0 being the best and 10 being the worst, what score would you give yourself in your current state? If it is a low score, then you can continue to persevere and find a breakthrough. However, based on your descriptions of your body, emotions, and thoughts, it seems like you're on the verge of a breakdown. So, do you still need to persevere, or is this perseverance pointless? This is something you should think about. In this bad state, it seems uncomfortable to continue, but if you don't continue, you worry about not being able to find another job. In everyday life, there is a way of thinking called "stop-loss thinking." "Stop-loss," usually referred to as "cutting losses," is mainly used in investment areas and refers to a protective behavior that aims to avoid greater losses. "Stop-loss thinking" allows us to stop our current actions in a timely manner to avoid greater losses later on. It sets a red line for our goals, and once we cross that red line, no matter how much effort we have put into something, we need to immediately make changes. In your current state, when your work is seriously affecting your work-life balance, you can set a stop-loss line, such as continuing for another month or two, and if it still doesn't meet your expectations, immediately switch jobs. I once held a leadership role for two years and experienced something similar to what you're going through. In a situation where I couldn't continue to persevere, I resolutely chose to resign and start over. Maybe if I had continued to persevere, I wouldn't be here discussing this issue with you. Stopping on the wrong path is progress; every extra second spent on the wrong thing is a waste of time. If you feel the need, take a good rest. Taking a good rest is for a better life. I can sense your pain when you say "I don't know what job to look for because I have no strengths, abilities, good appearance, or good interpersonal skills, and I am not physically fit either. I injured my ligament recently." I don't know who gave you such a terrible evaluation. If it was yourself, since when have you had so many negative assessments of yourself? There is a book called "One Thought Turns the Tide" that asks four questions. You can ask yourself: Is it true? Can you be certain that it is true? How do you react when you hold this thought? Can you find a reason to let go of that thought? Can you find a reason to hold that thought without anxiety? What kind of person are you without that thought? At least, from the beginning of my response, I can tell that you are a brave person. Being able to identify and express your confusion smoothly indicates that you are resourceful and seek help. In a situation where even eating may be a problem, you offered a reward of 10 yuan. In your daily life, you may be a generous person. Seeking help proactively shows that you have a strong inner drive. Just from this paragraph, I can see that you have so many strengths, but you can't see them. You need to cherish and embrace yourself. Zhang Defen, a famous author, said, "Dear, there is no one outside, only yourself." So, who allows you to evaluate yourself like this? Who lets you see the world in such a dim way? Is it your parents, your teachers, or someone else? What kind of people and experiences have you encountered from childhood to now? Actually, it doesn't matter who has evaluated you in the past, and it doesn't matter how you used to view yourself. You just need to know that it's not your fault now, and it wasn't your fault in the past. You formed and accepted these evaluations because you wanted to live well, even if it meant enduring humiliation and carrying a heavy burden. I give you another thumbs up for your bravery and hard work. You have grown up and can determine your own life and perceptions. You can heal yourself. From now on, start loving yourself. You can read countless books, travel thousands of miles, meet countless people, seek guidance from experts, or seek enlightenment on your own. When your perspective broadens, the world becomes bigger, and when you change, the world changes. I hope my response can give you some food for thought and guidance. The world and I love you.

It sounds like you may be feeling frustrated, angry, and suppressed in your work, which is leading to your current physical symptoms. Let's try a couple of strategies: 1) Continue working, but if the physical symptoms persist, consider using medication to provide relief. 2) Learn to switch perspectives or find solutions: unfair treatment from a supervisor - there are many instances of unfairness in the workplace, and sometimes we are powerless to change it. At these times, we need to ask ourselves why we insist on fairness and which past experiences are connected to the discomfort we feel. Apart from enduring it, are there any other options, such as appealing to the company's resources or talking to the HR department or leadership? Of course, these complaints can be kept confidential. If everyone's feedback can explain that it is not unfair, your thinking should adjust, and your anxiety will reduce. 3) If possible, seek out a mental health consultant. 4) Try to find a breakthrough point. In the workplace, not liking your boss, not getting along with colleagues, and struggling with communication can make your work environment lonely, have you noticed? Consider which direction could lead to a breakthrough. Otherwise, in such a social setting, you will lose a lot of support, and it's easy to imagine that your work won't go well. 5) Stop blaming and criticizing yourself because it is not only useless but also decreases your energy and increases anxiety. A better approach is to find three or more options for yourself in the face of setbacks and consider how you can make things better. This requires practicing repeatedly in daily life to enhance your mental resilience. Overall, you may need to focus on personal growth, such as emotional management and adapting to the workplace, to alleviate anxiety. There is a meditation platform called Mindfulness Planet that you can check out – it may help improve self-confidence and reduce anxiety.

【Finding Yourself and Feeling More Clear-minded】Dear friend: Good evening! I can sense that you are very worried, anxious, and have lost confidence. At the same time, you really want to break free from your current troubles. You feel like you have no strengths and are afraid of not being able to find a job, all because you have lost confidence and don't trust in your own worth. Your health is not good either, which makes you even more concerned. Let's tackle each issue one by one. 【First】Regarding the unfair treatment from your team leader, who made you wear children's clothing? If it was done by them, either talk to them about the impact their behavior has on you, or if you can't change it, then just ignore it. Don't worry about things that are beyond your control; instead, focus on keeping your own state of mind clear. 【Second】Returning to yourself: 1. Recognize your own strengths and worth; if you can't see them, then go and discover them. Think about your strengths, recognize them, and appreciate them. 2. Believe in yourself unconditionally, without needing any evidence; just have faith in yourself. Believe in yourself when faced with setbacks, and believe in yourself when you succeed. 3. Take good care of your body, see a doctor, or take some time to rest; don't let yourself get hurt any further. 【Third】If you have evaluated the pros and cons, then go ahead and make a decision. Whether you quit or stay doesn't really matter; what really matters is that you believe in yourself. However, don't excessively feed negativity into your mind. You can make assumptions, you can assess the risks, but don't be overly pessimistic. Such negative suggestions can affect your performance. In fact, I have also experienced workplace unfairness and being targeted unfairly, and I have heard others intentionally creating such situations, and my friends have also encountered them. It's not to say that it's good, but rather that it's not uncommon. However, the more you encounter such situations, the more resilient you become in facing the pressure. Remember, some things are just troubles, and once you separate yourself from them, you will feel much clearer and find yourself again. Your friend, Audrey.

Hello! After reading your description, I understand your allergies and troubles. Sending you a powerful hug~ Due to work stress, many people suffer from similar mental health issues, but the symptoms may vary. Some people may feel physical discomfort, others may become irritable, and some may experience confused thinking. Does it resemble a child's reluctance to go to school? I would like to give you some specific advice in the hopes that it will be helpful. [1] First of all, accept the current situation and carry medication with you. Your physical discomfort can be seen as a physical manifestation of workplace stress and a form of psychosomatic illness. Anxiety, workplace pressure, and disharmonious interpersonal relationships in the workplace can all lead to these symptoms. For the time being, if you can carry medication with you, try to see if it will improve your condition. At least it can alleviate the physical discomfort. At this point, medicine acts as a placebo. Additionally, when you feel uncomfortable at work, do you have the opportunity to take a break and relax for a while? Take a break from work every couple of hours? Knowing that it is caused by stress, and as we temporarily cannot leave this environment, it might be worth trying to accept it and see if there is any improvement. There was a time when I had difficulty breathing in crowded and enclosed places. I read many books and started carrying medicine, knowing that it wasn't so severe. I stopped placing too much emphasis on it in my mind and with a little medication, things gradually improved. [2] Try changing your perspective on the workplace. Many people feel helpless because there are indeed unfair phenomena that exist, and when we cannot change certain things, the pressure and sense of helplessness become stronger. Since we are currently still weak, let's focus less on these things that we are temporarily powerless to change and instead focus on what we can change. For example, when your physical condition is slightly better, try to do the tasks assigned by your supervisor as well as possible. In this process, see if you can learn something. Or learn from your colleagues. Or learn something about communication with others. There is a saying that I think is great: "Others pay you a salary, you gain skills." Now that someone is paying you a salary, why not learn more work skills and methods? Don't dwell on unfairness, change your perspective, and consider work as a form of learning. When you become stronger in the future, you will have more methods to handle injustice, don't you think? [3] Practice meditation, exercise, rest well, and chat with friends and family. Meditation and exercise can slowly improve your physical fitness. You mentioned that you have no strengths or abilities, a poor image, and bad interpersonal relationships. It seems that you lack self-confidence. Through continuous learning, you will have a different understanding. If you can find a friend or family member to chat with, it can effectively relieve stress and tension and also provide inspiration through communication. Believe in yourself like a growing tree, becoming stronger and fearless in the face of storms. We can make ourselves stronger and stronger. However, this process requires personal exploration, finding methods that suit you, and taking it step by step. If you encounter difficulties, remember that there are people here to support you! Best wishes!

Hello, first of all, I want to give you a hug and say that I really understand how you feel. It must be tough for you. Based on your description, it seems that you are experiencing physical and mental discomfort due to excessive work pressure, and I feel sorry for you. You need to adjust your mentality and try to adapt to the work environment. Here are some suggestions for you, hoping they will be helpful. First, you need to analyze the specific reasons that are causing you stress at work. Is it because of a lack of skills, or maybe your mental resilience is weaker, or is it some other reason? Secondly, based on your analysis, make corresponding adjustment strategies. If it's a lack of job skills, try to study more after work and become more knowledgeable to overcome work difficulties. Gradually, your situation will improve. If it's tension at the psychological level or lack of confidence, I hope you can face yourself, believe in yourself, and not overly stress or worry. If necessary, you can consider visiting a mental health clinic where doctors can help you adjust your mentality. Lastly, engage in moderate exercise. Exercise can help improve your mood, relieve mental stress, and relax your body. It can also stimulate the brain to release endorphins, which have an anti-anxiety and stress-relieving effect. I hope these suggestions will be useful to you. Take care!

Hello! Good afternoon! I feel heartbroken when I see your question. On one hand, you have to go to work for a living; on the other hand, the physical and mental exhaustion from work is taking a toll on your body and soul, which is really tough. Hugs to you. Now, should we continue going to this job? From a purely rational perspective, there are a few possible solutions: 1. Simply don't go to work anymore. After all, we can't sacrifice our health for work, right? Think about it, life is short, why push ourselves so hard? But based on your description, this possibility seems unlikely. 2. Keep going to work, grit your teeth, endure it, because for survival, there is no obstacle that humans can't overcome. However, from what you described, this double blow to your body and mind is something that would be hard for anyone to bear. Is there a third option? I believe there is. First, the situations you mentioned are things that can be openly discussed. Is there a chance to have a heart-to-heart conversation with your leader, with the diagnosis from the hospital as proof? Maybe you're thinking, "I'm afraid. I'm afraid of losing my job." But now, you even have the inclination to resign, so why be afraid? Maybe your leader can also be understanding about this. We can try to communicate non-violently about this. Also, I noticed that your sense of self-identity, self-worth, and judgment of yourself seem a bit low. Can we aspire to be an optimistic and positive person in the future? Sometimes, when our mindset improves, our luck seems to change too (have you heard the saying, "God helps those who help themselves"?). There are many specific methods you can try, you can refer to some suggestions from positive psychology. That's all. Wishing you well, the world loves you!

question: What is meant by hostile interpersonal perception?
description: What is meant by hostile interpersonal perception? A friend told me that if I always tend to interpret other people's relationships in a negative way, my child will subconsciously learn my thinking patterns and may develop a hostile interpersonal perception. Could you please explain what is meant by hostile interpersonal perception?
keywords: Interpersonal, communication, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hi OP: You love your child very much, and when others talk to your child, you often feel that it is directed at you and has hostile intentions. But your friends and family tell you that others don't have that intention and are not targeting you. Why do you perceive things differently from others? OP, you are confused. At the same time, you also know that if you judge incorrectly, your own subjective thinking can also affect your child. So you came here seeking help. Don't worry, let's first take a look at the concept of hostile interpersonal perception. Interpersonal perception refers to the perception of relationships between people, including understanding of a person's external characteristics, personality traits, and judgments and understanding of their behavior. Hostile interpersonal perception is actually when the perceiver feels that all interpersonal interactions are filled with negativity. The perceiver often feels that the other party in interpersonal interactions is hostile towards them and targeting them. The formation of hostile interpersonal perception is often the result of automatic thinking. Automatic thinking is often our unconscious judgments and understanding of something without thinking. When we face something, we often associate it with similar experiences we have had in the past, resulting in automatic thinking (for example, if we failed an exam and received harsh criticism from our parents, this scenario will be deeply ingrained in us, so every time we fail an exam afterwards, we will assume that our parents will criticize and scold us again. So equating exam failure with criticism and scolding is the result of automatic thinking.) In addition, the formation of hostile interpersonal perception is also one of the expressions of psychological defense mechanisms (projection). Projection refers to attributing our own desires to others and asserting that the other person has these thoughts. For example, if we dislike someone who drinks excessively, during the process of interpersonal interaction with that person, we will develop our own psychological defense mechanisms and end up feeling that the person who drinks excessively also dislikes us. So, OP, as you can see, whether it is the result of automatic thinking or psychological defense mechanisms, it makes us lose objectivity when looking at the problem and makes us unconsciously think in a hostile manner during interpersonal interactions. So, what can be done to change our unconscious cognition? I hope the following suggestions can help you. 1. Understand the reasons for your hostile interpersonal perception. Hostile interpersonal perception is the result of automatic thinking or psychological defense mechanisms. When you feel that others have hostile intentions toward your child and targeting you, try to recall similar situations in your past life experiences. Have you ever been rejected or targeted by others? Have you experienced difficulties in interpersonal interactions that have had a significant impact on you? 2. Tell yourself to objectively view the problem. If the answer to the above question is "yes," then when you have hostile interpersonal perception, remember to remind yourself that this is the instinctive response of your automatic thinking and psychological defense mechanisms. Only when you realize that your thinking and judgment criteria are not objective can you better accept the advice of others and truly see whether the other party is targeting you or has hostile intentions towards you. Only by taking off the emotional outerwear and avoiding the influence of automatic thinking can our perspective on the world become objective. At that time, maybe, OP, you will find that the opinions of your friends and family are correct, and the other party really does not have any intentions against you. 3. Use positive thinking to view the problem. If the above two points can be called cognitive restructuring, then in this step, what we need to do is to replace the old unreasonable cognition with new cognition. OP, you can keep a journal and record your negative interpersonal cognitions, and replace them with positive and objective interpersonal cognitions that dispel hostility. For example, you can tell yourself that what others say to your child is because they find your child cute and are just joking, not with any hostile intentions; for example, the advice others give to you is objective and helpful, not targeting me, deliberately saying that I am not good enough, and so on. Through continuous practice, I believe that OP can deliberately change and gradually transition to positive automatic thinking, thus truly replacing negative, hostile thinking. Finally, I want to say to OP that it is evident that you love your child very much. You are worried that your thinking patterns will affect your child, so you seek change. Kudos to you, OP, you have taken the first step towards change. Moving forward, I believe you will continue to improve. Best wishes.

Hello poster: Thank you for your trust and for sharing your detailed response. From your detailed description, it is clear that the previous incident has had a significant impact on you, leading to your current perception of interpersonal hostility. Now, let's take a look at the issues you mentioned in your reply. "My son heard a girl calling her dog Wang Cai, and my son said that the name doesn't suit the dog and suggested that the girl's dog should be called Wang Hei because it is black." (Children often speak their minds, expressing objective facts. However, for adults, the words may carry a different meaning. The girl might interpret your son's innocent remarks as insulting her dog intentionally, as if she was being insulted when people comment on someone being overweight. Children may not have ill intentions, but for the person who hears those remarks, it may feel like they are being looked down upon. Adults often analyze and think about things based on their own established patterns of thinking.) "Then I asked my son if he remembered the name of our previous dog. My son said our dog was named Xiao Bai. One of the girls said, 'Then your dog must be very white, right?' My son and I ignored her." (In the eyes of most people, they would likely prefer a white dog. When you asked that question, you simply wanted to interact with your child. But in the eyes of that girl, it might be perceived as showing off. Your and your son's lack of response to her questions deepened her feeling that you both looked down upon her and disrespected her. That's why she made that offensive joke later.) "When that girl said that, she was already soaking her feet, and her face turned red when she finished speaking and my son still ignored her." (After that girl saw that your son ignored her, she turned red. Actually, in that instant, she realized that it was an insulting joke and started to regret her actions. Otherwise, there wouldn't be the characteristic of blushing.) "I even told my son, 'You can't hit people, hitting is wrong and impolite.' So my son held back and didn't hit her." (I want to applaud your previous actions. You stopped your son from the impulse to hit someone and told him that it is wrong. In life, we often face defamation and contempt, but not all defamation and contempt can be responded to with insults. In this experience, I want to tell you that you did the right thing. After the incident, you can also talk to your son and see what he was thinking at the time, whether he felt angry and wanted to hit the person. You can tell your son that you understand his feelings, that the auntie's words were wrong, but we can't learn from her, we can't hit people, we can't solve other people's mistakes using the wrong methods. Parents are role models for children, and you made the right choice before. We don't need to punish ourselves using other people's mistakes. The incident has already happened, and the importance of subsequent education for children is more important than constantly regretting not retaliating. Moreover, your actions at the time were not wrong.) "Every time my son and I drink milk, I think of that incident and regret not verbally counterattacking that girl." (Your situation can be called an unfinished business syndrome. In your heart, you have always regretted not retaliating against that girl. So, it is easy for you to develop a perception of interpersonal hostility. Now, let's go back to your question about the perception of interpersonal hostility. Why do you feel that others are targeting you in subsequent interactions while your friends don't perceive it the same way? Is this situation similar to the case with that girl? A child's innocent remark may seem harmless to others, but why did it become an insult and contempt in her eyes? This shows that a sentence itself may not be a problem, but due to different patterns of thinking, various interpretations can arise. Think about whether you have now become the same as that girl in terms of thinking, and whether the people you feel are targeting and looking down on you are similar to your past self and your child. Finally, there are two questions that you need to consider: 1) Are all the situations you have encountered since then the same as the one with that girl? 2) If the situations are different and others are not targeting you, should you make a change in response to automated thinking? Wishing you all the best.)

question: Eighth grade, even though many people envy my family, why am I still imagining sinking?
description: I'm 13 years old this year and I'm starting the second year of junior high school. I feel that my family environment is very good, and my parents are relatively open-minded. Many classmates envy me. My mom is very nice to me and often accompanies me to read novels and watch anime. My dad is also good, with average expectations of me, but he often encourages me. Why are many of my classmates more outgoing and better at interpersonal communication than me? Clearly, I feel that my life is very good, why have I been experiencing moderate depression and anxiety in three consecutive tests? Why am I becoming more and more fragile in this environment, to the point of even thinking about suicide? Why do I keep sinking deeper and deeper into my imagination even though I know I need to face reality? Why?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello there! Being outgoing and good at socializing is related to individual personality traits rather than the environment one lives in. The results of a test can only be used as a reference, but from your description, it seems like you're really feeling down. Since you mentioned having a good relationship with your parents, I recommend talking to them about this and seeing if you can seek help from a mental health counselor. The causes of depression and anxiety vary from person to person and may not necessarily be due to family issues. They could arise from interpersonal relationships, academic pressure, the loss of a loved one, or a past traumatic experience... The specific reasons would need further exploration. I noticed that you mentioned having thoughts of suicide, and I'm not sure what you're feeling. It could be a starting point for a breakthrough though. When you feel suicidal, try reaching out to your parents for help.

Hello, OP. There are many factors that can contribute to depression, not just the family background. It is related to the individual's education, the culture of the society they live in, specific events they have experienced, as well as their personality and temperament. As you mentioned, you have a good relationship with your mother and can enjoy reading novels and comics together. Although your father may have certain expectations, he also encourages you. This indicates that your depression may not stem from your family, but there may be other reasons for its occurrence. I don't know if you have had any significant experiences outside of your family that could have a negative impact on you, leading to self-doubt and low self-esteem. Some people have outgoing personalities, while others may be more introverted. Some are good at socializing, while others are not. Both are normal, and the key is to achieve a state of mental and physical harmony in your own life. If you have tested for moderate depression three times, it is recommended that you communicate with your parents and inform them about your current mental state. Seek the help of a counselor with the support of your parents to explore the causes of your depression and find a solution to this problem. Don't shy away from seeking medical help and don't delay the optimal treatment time. Best wishes!

question: Is weight loss about lack of self-confidence or is it for health reasons? How to differentiate?
description: After giving birth to my second child, I injured my foot while trying to lose weight. My husband said it was because I lacked confidence in my own weight. However, I believe that weight loss is not only about vanity and lack of confidence, but also about maintaining good health. I want both beauty and health, but what is the difference between confidence and vanity?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! In the current social environment, weight is highly valued. One common belief is that "thin is beautiful." However, the perception of body shape as beautiful or not is greatly influenced by the development of society. For example, during the Tang Dynasty, being overweight was considered beautiful, while nowadays being thin is seen as attractive. This perception of body shape is largely influenced by the media's promotion of models and celebrities. Some people engage in weight loss for health reasons, some due to lack of confidence, and many because of a combination of both. Regardless of the reason for weight loss, there is no right or wrong; however, we advocate for healthy weight loss. Excessive weight carries a burden on our bodies and negatively affects our health, so it is recommended to maintain weight within an appropriate range. Some people excessively focus on their body shape and resort to extreme methods for weight loss, such as fasting or vomiting, which may be related to negative mother-child relationships. This excessive obsession with body shape, striving to reach an excessively thin state to feel satisfied with weight loss, is a manifestation of insecurity. There is no clear distinction between lack of confidence and the desire for beauty, as these factors are intertwined. Some people only engage in weight loss when they are truly overweight, and while health may be a factor, there may also be a small component of beauty motivation and a slight influence of insecurity. Others may have a normal weight range but are still unsatisfied with their body shape and excessively control their weight, where insecurity plays a larger role and beauty motivation has a smaller influence. Whether weight loss is driven by the desire for beauty, lack of confidence, or for health reasons, it is best to keep the weight within a healthy range. There is no need to strive for an extremely light weight like celebrities since our profession is not to look good on camera. I hope this information can be helpful to you. Take care, and have a great day!

question: Feeling tense, anxious, and having trouble sleeping, how to untie the knot in the heart?
description: Since last year, I have been having trouble sleeping. I think there are several reasons: first, I met a boyfriend online and because I felt insecure, I was always worried and couldn't sleep well at night, and in the end, we broke up. Second, I was raised by my grandparents, and my grandmother, who had always been good to me, lost contact with our family because of issues with dividing my grandfather's inheritance. I never thought that my grandmother, who had been so good to me, would be estranged from our family because of property. My grandmother thought that our family was fighting over the inheritance, and then my aunt played mind games with us and then they both disappeared, and my grandmother wouldn't meet with us even when we finally reached her by phone. Because my childhood experiences were relatively happy, it caused a huge contrast with this matter, and I couldn't accept it. It was my grandmother who taught me principles in life, but it was also my grandmother who did something against those principles. I know that society is very realistic, but I never thought that such a realistic situation would happen to me. It's easier to deal with outsiders, but I really can't accept this happening within my own family. Although my emotions have improved a lot this year, the prolonged contemplation from last year may have caused imbalances in my body, leading to insomnia, and I often wake up early. I still have unresolved feelings about my grandmother and that situation.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, mental disorders, counseling and listening.

answers.answer_text: You can see that you deeply care about your grandmother, who is an important person in your life. She has taught you the principles of how to conduct yourself, but her actions at this time are confusing you. Your inner self believes that it is your grandmother who taught you these principles, yet she is also going against them. This contradiction in teaching and actions from the same person can lead to a confusion of values. It may take you some time to resolve this current dilemma and slowly adapt to this harsh reality. Then, you can consider what you can do in the future and how you can uphold your values.

Hello, after reading your description, I noticed a subtle relationship between your two psychological concerns: 1) your attachment to online dating and fear of losing it, and 2) your thoughts about your grandmother. It seems that both stem from your emotional investment, but when the other person does not respond, it leaves you disappointed and unable to vent. It feels strange, like throwing a stone into water and seeing no ripples. The accumulation of your emotions without an outlet has become a knot in your heart, making you more and more anxious. Although we cannot change other people's thoughts, we can adjust our own cognition. By expanding your activities appropriately, engaging in outdoor sports, and trying meditation, these can all help you adjust your somatization symptoms and break free from the vicious cycle.

We can temporarily suspend matters of the heart, but a sense of security must always come from within ourselves, after all, we are our own greatest support. Grandma's situation is indeed a stumbling block for us, but we also need to consider some factors. 1. Does Grandma have enough financial resources? Often, inheritance disputes arise from desires. For Grandma, what does she want the inheritance for? If Grandma doesn't have a stable financial source, her children don't provide much, and there's no one to take care of her, then it is understandable for her to fight for her own interests because, after all, it's easy for elderly people to be despised. 2. Auntie's scheming has influenced Grandma. Although Grandma is reasonable, old age can make people confused, especially after Grandpa passed away, leaving her without a backbone. At this time, Auntie happened to say some negative things, and there may have been some things taken advantage of by the other side in our family, which led Grandma to develop a bias against us, and as a result, we haven't been able to sit down and have a proper conversation. Some misunderstandings require mutual understanding and resolution. If we can't get over our own internal obstacles, how can we expect others to reconcile with us? Therefore, we shouldn't have too many preconceived notions. We can try to delve into some matters, but of course, the prerequisite is that we have the ability to take care of ourselves and regulate our own emotions. The world loves you and me.

Hello!
