I can understand the moral role model in your mind (especially if this role model was your kind grandmother who treated you well before) and how a misunderstanding has caused you to reflect on human nature. The two reasons you mentioned may be causing your sleep problems. However, the causes of your anxious and tense mood still need further exploration. Based on your experiences in relationships and with your grandmother, the teacher sees the need to reflect on your own attachment style. Why do you react this way? Additionally, you can try some relaxation exercises before sleep and adjust yourself through exercise. You can search online for some health-related public accounts or websites for more information. If self-adjustment is not effective, it is recommended to seek help from a professional psychological counselor. I wish you a happy life! (From the Heart, Psychologist Yuan Lanlan).

question: I always feel like there's a wall between me and everyone else. How can I get closer to the people around me?
description: I feel it's difficult for me to get close to people, always feeling like there's a wall between me and everyone else. Even if I feel closer to someone due to spending time together, they quickly become distant and polite again due to time and distance.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, we can understand that 1. it is difficult to get close to others, and it feels like there is a wall between them. 2. Close friends have become distant over time. [A little bit of analysis and advice] 1. The distance in friendships can vary greatly depending on the personalities and habits of both parties. Friends who are warm and outgoing and rely on each other may be intimate enough to share everything they see and do on a daily basis, while friends who are relatively independent emotionally may meet up regularly to hang out and talk about their troubles, but may not have as much to say. 2. Long-lasting friendships are not solely maintained by proximity, but require initiative from both sides. After being physically distant, if you miss the other person, take the initiative to chat with them and regularly reach out to maintain the connection. Only then can the relationship last. If distance causes one to forget about the friend and only remember to talk to them when in need, then the relationship won't last. I hope this helps OP.

question: How to overcome extreme blushing and sweating when talking to people?
description: Sometimes I suddenly get nervous when someone starts a conversation with me, especially if it's someone of the opposite sex. I may blush, feel hot, and sometimes even feel nauseous when it gets really bad. I don't like crowded places and I don't like going out alone. Are these symptoms of social anxiety? How can I overcome them?

answers.answer_text: Hello! There are two main symptoms of social anxiety: 1) obvious nervousness and fear when communicating and interacting with others; 2) avoidance of social situations. The reasons for blushing and feeling hot during social interactions need to be analyzed specifically. For example, what do you feel when talking to the opposite sex? What are you worried about? Common concerns include performing poorly, receiving negative evaluations, being afraid of blushing, and appearing embarrassed, etc. You can try to relax yourself, change irrational thoughts that cause anxiety and nervousness, and you should also exercise regularly. Don't avoid interacting with the opposite sex just because you feel nervous. That will only make you more anxious. It is necessary to participate in social groups to give yourself more opportunities to communicate with others. Of course, to completely change the symptoms of social anxiety, systematic psychological counseling intervention is required.

question: After my father passed away, I am afraid of the concern and pity from relatives. Why am I like this?
description: In the 8th grade, I have a very open perspective on life and death. My father's departure didn't impact me greatly, but I fear the concern and pity from other relatives. I even dislike them. I also don't want to tell my classmates, not because I'm afraid they will gossip or anything, but because I'm afraid they will pity me and treat me differently. What's wrong with me?

answers.answer_text: Hello, when your father passed away, it seemed like you didn't feel much pain. Instead, the concern, greetings, and consolation from relatives and friends made you feel conflicted, as if it made you appear pitiful. Perhaps you think that care and comfort are meant for the weak, and you don't want to feel weak. This includes feeling sadness if you have it due to your father's departure, as it would make you feel weak. You are rejecting the feeling of sadness in your heart. Therefore, you are rejecting the care from your loved ones because such care would bring up feelings of sadness for you.

question: How can we improve the issue of excessive smartphone use?
description: How can we improve the issue of excessive phone use? Whenever we have free time, we just instinctively reach for our phones. We know that constantly using our phones is not good for us, but how can we control this habit?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Just as you said, when you have free time, you always want to pick up your phone. But what about when you're not free? Maybe this is a method to suppress playing with your phone, a method that works for you! So, if you feel that you're not working hard enough right now, then make yourself busy and continue to enrich yourself! On the other hand, is playing with your phone always a bad thing? Not necessarily! I am currently using my phone to answer your question! If my answer is helpful to you, is that not something worth doing? If I pick up my phone this time, will it not make me feel guilty because I have helped someone? It is advisable to strike a balance between work and rest, but it mainly depends on what you use your phone for! It is inherently dual-faced, so it still depends on how you manage your life. A person with a plan and goals will always have a more exciting life! Best wishes!

question: Knowing each other for 3 years and dating for 1 year, how can we find an absolute balance point with my girlfriend?
description: I have known my girlfriend for 3 years and we have been in a relationship for a year and a half, which can be considered successful. However, recently there have been some problems. Since I started working and she is still in school, our perspectives have changed. I now feel that I can't find a balance in our relationship. In the past six months, I have been putting in a lot of effort, both in terms of time and money, and I don't mind that. The problem lies in her attitude towards me, which has become indifferent. I can't say anything to her, reasoning doesn't work either. She always feels that anyone's opinions, except mine, are correct. She goes out and hangs out with both male and female friends, and I couldn't care less about that now. But she constantly interferes in my affairs and even wants to be involved in my work. Even if I just talk to someone of the opposite sex, she gets angry. When I point these things out to her, she simply brushes them off as friendships. It's really starting to frustrate me.

answers.answer_text:
Title owner, good Wednesday morning! After carefully reading your question repeatedly, I can feel your confusion and annoyance. Let's calm down and communicate, explore together. First of all, I want to directly answer the question in the title, there is no absolute point of balance. Why? Because in any relationship, due to different understandings and feelings of giving and receiving from both sides, different standards exist, and absolute balance is nonexistent. When I say this, I wonder if you understand, some people give a lot without feeling it is difficult because it comes from love, while others are accustomed to being taken care of and think it is only natural. There are various situations involved here. Let's dissolve this obsession with absolute balance, which may be helpful for improving the relationship in the next step. #We have known each other for 3 years and have been dating for a year and a half, which can be considered successful. The actual duration is not the most important thing. What matters is how much time in the 3 years of knowing each other and the year and a half of dating have you been able to communicate your deep thoughts and explore deeper aspects of each other, such as life views, values, and perspectives on marriage. This is also an important question. Judging from the following, it is evident that you have moved beyond the infatuation stage. So, the next step requires more and deeper understanding, instead of guessing or resenting each other. How to manage this relationship well requires joint efforts from both of you. And you, the questioner, have this idea and can take the initiative. From the moment you raised the question, it was already the beginning of awareness and potential transformation. #But here comes the recent problem. Due to me working and her still being in school, there have been changes in attitudes. I now feel I can't find an absolute point of balance in the relationship. In the past six months, it hasn't been a one-sided giving in terms of time and money, which doesn't matter. But actually, these things do matter. Why? Material things are another form of spiritual manifestation that symbolizes the emotional entity you give to the other person. Everyone knows how hard it is to make money. Of course, objectively speaking, your girlfriend doesn't have a job yet, and you understand this very well. So, your expectation is that when you give to her, she should at least say thank you, right? (Even if she doesn't say it directly, can you sense it in her tone, expressions, and gestures?) #The key is her attitude towards me has become optional, and I feel the same about her now. Optional, remote, but it's just a feeling, which may also be an illusion. And you, the questioner, are also trying to retaliate against her using seemingly similar means, which will only make the relationship more distant, akin to a form of subtle violence. Let's go back to the period when we understood each other and established the relationship. During this time, how much time did we truly communicate our emotions, feelings, and thoughts? You can express your feelings to her, but not by ignoring her or being cold, but by speaking up. "Heart-to-heart communication" is just an artistic technique, in reality, if you don't say it, the other person won't be able to guess. When you speak, focus on expressing your true feelings and make a relatively objective observation-based connection between these feelings and specific behaviors of the other person (rather than judgment). To develop and expand on this, you can read "Nonviolent Communication". #I can't talk to her, reasoning doesn't work, she always feels that except for me, everyone else is right, her so-called friends, both male and female, she goes out with them to chat and have fun. I'm already too lazy to care about these things. Most women can't listen to reason, can they? You are using a man's rationality and a woman's sensibility to communicate. You need to adjust the frequency, tune in to a channel that the other person can understand. When she complains to you, are you willing to listen? What kind of communication truly builds a close relationship? In simple terms, it means listening to the other person's complaints. If you can put yourself in her shoes and also complain a bit, that's a higher level. If you can truly listen with empathy, even without saying anything, it's great. She needs someone to confide in, and she chose so-called friends. Why? One possibility is that she feels annoyed when she talks to you. Besides that, her normal socializing, you can fully accept, right? She is yours, and she will eventually come back to you. It's just a matter of establishing a closer relationship and better communication. That's my advice to you. #But she always likes to interfere in my affairs, including my work. Even when I talk to people of the opposite sex, she gets jealous. When I mention these things to her, she only says they are just friends. Now it's getting on my nerves. My interpretation is different from yours. She lacks a sense of security even more than you, right? You are already employed, but she doesn't have a source of income yet. She wants you to know that she is also a part of this relationship. Isn't it a good thing for her to understand your work and what you do every day? What's wrong with listening to her opinions? (Getting jealous when talking to people of the opposite sex, isn't that just being possessive? She probably won't do this with strangers, right?) 
After we improve our previous close relationship and communication style, using the interpretative approach of nonviolent communication to perceive each other's emotional needs, I believe your romantic relationship will undergo substantial improvement. Best wishes to you! The world and I love you!

1. Love is a dynamic and balanced relationship. There is no "absolute equilibrium point" where everything stays the same. Relationships are always fluctuating, with ups and downs, better or worse. The two individuals constantly interact and adjust, which is the norm. If you feel like you are "putting in more effort," it may be a reminder that you are feeling tired and dissatisfied with the relationship. Take a moment to recall the initial stages of being in love, when you may have felt that your partner was so adorable and your efforts were not enough. Love is not a simple, linear progression; it has its ups and downs. In a relationship, both individuals are independent beings who have grown in different environments. There will always be the issue of balancing and coordinating between the two, necessitating timely adjustments to match each other's changes. Otherwise, there may be a mismatch. However, this is all normal and inevitable. Therefore, in love, it is important to constantly observe the changes in the relationship and actively adapt to them. You have already realized that your relationship has undergone some mismatches, which is a good thing. In the face of such changes, you can ponder why these changes have occurred and what you can do. A significant part of the reason might be the changes in your own circumstances; you are already working and facing society while she is still in a relatively simple school environment. The problems you both face, the concerns you have, and even some of your beliefs may have changed, making your differences more apparent. Have you discussed these issues with each other?

2. Genuine communication is crucial. You sense that she no longer values you as much. In fact, she believes that what others say, apart from you, is correct, and she likes to interfere in your affairs. When you express your opinions, she becomes explosive. All these indicate her dissatisfaction and ideological disagreement towards you. When she disagrees with you, the weight of your words diminishes in her mind. So where did the differences between you arise? This requires deep communication, understanding, listening, and exploring whether the appearance of the problem stems from a fundamental disagreement or whether there are just some barriers and misunderstandings between you that can be resolved through communication, leading to consensus or tolerance, and enabling you to continue together. This is a test for both of you. Moreover, you mentioned that she chats with some male and female friends, but she gets angry when you talk to the opposite sex. This shows that you also have some dissatisfaction with her. So what are these dissatisfactions? What are your expectations? What can't you accept? What do you like about her? Seize this opportunity to think it through and discuss it with her. Problems also create opportunities. So now is an opportunity for both of you to deepen your understanding of each other. Through genuine communication, see if you have the foundation, determination, and wisdom to continue together. The longevity of a relationship relies not on surface harmony but on true spiritual connection and genuine openness. Only with sufficient understanding and trust can we attain true love.

To be honest, you've already been together for three years, which is considered quite long. Many couples can't even make it to three years. But we also know that in a relationship, there are both passionate and dull periods. And what you're going through now can be considered a dull period, which requires you to get through it together. Your girlfriend is still a student while you're working, which means your current living environments are different. And when the environments are different, the things you encounter are also different, which makes it harder for you to understand each other's behaviors. I think the most important thing now is tolerance and trust. Maybe gradually, your common topics have become fewer, so both parties need to make efforts to get closer to each other. It's not enough for just one person to make an effort. As for her tendency to meddle in your matters, think about it from a different perspective. Could it be because you haven't provided her with enough sense of security, and so on? And she also needs to reflect on her attitude and approach towards you. After all, if two people want to be together for a long time, they must be tolerant of each other's differences. It requires adjustment and, more importantly, trust. You might want to sit down together and find a calm moment to talk about things you can't tolerate about each other but the other person is unaware of. This way, you'll both know what led to this situation. I hope this answer can help you!

After carefully reading your outpouring, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a gentle breeze to soothe your inner troubles. Here is my analysis: 1. When you care too much about someone, the more you care, the less they care about you. The less you care, the more they care about you. It is because you have constantly met her needs that over time, you have become dispensable. 2. Tolerance in love can make the relationship more beautiful, but indulgence will only sink love into a quagmire. Eventually, you will helplessly witness it slowly dissipating. It is because you repeatedly indulged her that she could indulge herself repeatedly. In the end, she could go out with other men and women, frequently chat and keep in touch. Instead of reflecting on herself, she interfered with you. This is the result of indulgence, being spoiled. 3. Love yourself seven parts and love others three parts. Love yourself professionally and love others in your spare time. People who truly love you don't require you to give too much. It's useless to give too much to someone who doesn't love you. Take good care of yourself and be the best partner for the other person. This is the best torment for her, the torment of love. If you have enough charm, she can't live without you. If your charm is not enough, you can't keep her. Thank you for your question, may all the goodness in the world come to you as expected.

Everyone has different ways of getting along, and finding a balance is not easy, especially for working professionals. On one hand, they have to be busy with work, feeling overwhelmed, and on the other hand, they have to take care of their girlfriend's emotions, creating a growing gap. As conflicts increase, the relationship between both parties will suffer, and eventually be unable to face it. In this case, it is best to cultivate a sense of ritual. For girls, the best way is to pay attention to the small details, such as giving gifts on Valentine's Day and birthdays, and showing care when they are sick. If these things are done well, girls won't have much to complain about. The frequent quarrels and interference in everyday life are just a lack of security, feeling neglected and indifferent, resulting in such feelings. If guys can handle emotional matters well, there will be fewer complaints. Being together for three years and being in a relationship for a year and a half is quite long, and maintaining this relationship is not easy. If you can still be together, it's best to try to persist and resolve your own troubles.

Hello, you and your girlfriend have been in a relationship for a year and a half and have always gotten along well. However, recent changes in the environment have affected the pace of your interactions. The work and study situations are completely different, as you encounter more people in the workplace and have to focus on work-related issues, unlike the carefree atmosphere at school. This situation is similar to when a man is busy with his career while the woman is a full-time homemaker, as it is easier for her to have idle thoughts. Because you are in different life situations, your perspectives and focuses have shifted. Your girlfriend is still studying and tends to become more involved in your affairs. She has a certain need for control, which may stem from her lack of security in the relationship. She wants to maintain her "dominance" by having access to all the information concerning you. Think about how your previous interactions and ways of getting along were like, and whether your approach towards her has changed since you started working. Due to her heightened sensitivity, she may feel that you are now "different" from before. While she was studying, she had more time to hang out with friends and wanted to have her own social circle, which is understandable. Another possibility is that she is trying to get your "attention," so she goes out with other people deliberately, both men and women, to incite jealousy and gauge how much you care about her. She also feels insecure when you talk to members of the opposite sex, as she is concerned about your behavior. You are also worried about losing her, but currently, both of you are in a phase of "doubting each other." You feel that she is caring less about you, while she feels that you are no longer providing her with the same sense of security as before. Well, actually, you are in love with each other, but you haven't established a good sense of "trust." To eliminate these suspicions and differences in your hearts, you can only honestly express your feelings to each other. Your concerns stem from love and care, and you are willing to trust her and not interfere with her freedom, because as long as she is happy, you can accommodate anything. Let her understand that you actually care about her. Perhaps, because of work lately, you may be under some pressure and your words and actions may change, causing unnecessary misunderstandings. If she truly loves you, she will understand you. I hope you continue to walk together and be happy~.

question: 30-year-old woman, very afraid of loneliness, no one to talk to, afraid of being alone?
description: I have been feeling depressed and unhappy all day today. I feel a heavy tightness in my chest. After taking a leave, I have returned to a work place that I didn't want to stay in before. It's relatively closed off here, and everyone feels lonely. I'm very afraid of being alone, but unfortunately, I'm always by myself. This constant state of fear and anxiety has been ongoing, and there is no one to talk to.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, friends, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello, I want to give you a big hug and sympathize with you! Here I would like to express my opinion. Whether it's a child or an adult, everyone experiences loneliness at times. Living with friends and family is the source of our happiness. If you often find yourself alone and feeling lonely, there are many ways to make yourself happier. Firstly, learn to cultivate your own hobbies and interests. When you are alone, don't let yourself be idle. Develop a few hobbies, and naturally you will meet like-minded people. Secondly, it is important to establish your own career aspirations. When you are alone, don't give up on yourself. Focus on your work. Economic independence is essential at any time to boost your confidence. Furthermore, let yourself experience different challenges. During your leisure time, try different lifestyles and learn various interpersonal skills. Make your life more colorful. Lastly, learn to accept and enjoy solitude. Occasional solitude is normal. Don't settle for a companion just to avoid loneliness. Enrich your mind and strive to become a better version of yourself!

question: Introverted, sometimes hesitant to make direct eye contact when speaking to others.
description: Sometimes when relatives come, I am afraid to call them relatives. I don't know why, but I feel resistant in my heart. This has been the case since I was 14 years old, and it continues until now, at 25 years old. Then, when I converse with people, I can never find a topic and don't know what to say.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, communication, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Sometimes when relatives come, I am afraid to call them and I don't know the reason. I feel resistance in my heart. This has been happening since I was 14 years old, and it continues until now at 25. Also, when I talk to people, I can never find a topic and don't know what to say. From the description, I can feel that you are a sensitive person, somewhat insecure, and not good at socializing. You are 25 years old now, and I wonder if you have asked yourself why you are afraid to talk to others? Is it because you don't know how to start a conversation, or are you afraid of being hurt by your own words? Ask yourself what the reason is, and then we can find a solution! Based on your language, I feel that you are not very confident in yourself, and you seem a bit insecure. Is this insecurity coming from your family? For example, being a left-behind child, receiving critical education, experiencing domestic violence, or school bullying. Try to find the root cause, bravely face those bad memories, gradually overcome the sense of insecurity, build self-confidence, and most importantly, learn to love yourself! This way, self-confidence will gradually be established. By then, you won't be afraid to look into other people's eyes!

question: 24-year-old girl, always feels that her mother is biased, is it because she hasn't been weaned yet?
description: When I was young, I was a left-behind child, while my younger brother was raised by our parents. As I grew up (just started working as a teacher, and my brother also went to college), I had summer vacation, and so did my brother. My brother went back to our hometown to practice driving, and my mom went with him, spending the whole summer there. So, I asked her to come back earlier, and though she agreed, she kept postponing it. I was about to start school, but she still didn't come back, and I felt very upset.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. As the older sister in a sibling family, I want to give you a warm hug. I have also experienced many similar feelings. Favoring sons over daughters is an unavoidable issue in sibling families. Every biased parent tilts the balance of affection to an extreme, causing great harm to the neglected child (usually a daughter). But we find it difficult to change our parents' mindset. Although I have protested countless times, my mom always dismisses it casually. So, I have learned not to dwell on this unsolvable problem. I choose to invest more emotions and energy in myself, trying to make myself happy and improve myself, so that I can become more calm and stronger. This is not to defy my parents, but through this process, I have gained a lot of meaning. Therefore, even though I can understand you, I hope you can gradually move away from such a relationship and embrace a broader world, to find the true meaning of life.

question: Mother only cares about price, not quality. How to deal with distorted values?
description: My mother always cares only about the price and not the quality. She often suffers a big loss by being greedy for small advantages. She is very calculative and spends a lot of energy obsessing over small amounts of money, even down to the decimal point.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! Everyone has different values ​​because of their upbringing, family experiences, and life events, among other things, all of which contribute to their values ​​and beliefs. In real life, the majority of ordinary mothers, when they reach a certain age, or even before that, care a lot about prices. When they spend money, they are reluctant to spend too much and would prefer to buy better things for less money. However, they are often deceived by the products of merchants, but it is understandable for our mothers because they have raised us with so much love and want to give us the best. I think it is necessary for you to communicate with your mother about this matter because as her beloved child, she will definitely listen to you. Furthermore, you must also tell your mother about the existence of unscrupulous merchants in order to prevent being deceived again, as many people have fallen victim to scams, losing tens of thousands or even hundreds of thousands. Therefore, it is important to teach your mother about some knowledge about products as early as possible, which will be beneficial for her to avoid being deceived in the future. Lastly, OP, you don't have to dwell too much on this matter, as it is just a very small thing in life. Our parents have many things they don't understand, which require us children to patiently teach and care for them. Finally, I wish you happiness!

question: A 26-year-old woman constantly thinks, "Wouldn't it be nice if I fell asleep and never woke up again?"
description: I graduated from an ordinary college with a major in accounting, but I'm not interested in it. Throughout my four years in university, I was quite good at English and even achieved a high score on the American business graduate exam, ranking in the top 20% of global candidates. However, due to the high tuition fees and my clear realization that I didn't want to pursue a business career, I ultimately gave up on going to the United States for graduate studies. Despite having a seemingly decent background, I have made it quite messy. Later on, I started working in online English education, earning a decent but unstable salary. As a result, I decided to prepare for the translation master's program entrance examination. However, during the preparation process, a lot of things happened that made me feel extremely frustrated, and I don't know what to do. ① There is family pressure; both my parents are incapable and in their fifties with no savings. They manage to get by and I grew up relying on others. I also have a younger brother and sister who need to go to college. Yesterday, my mom asked to borrow 20,000 yuan from me to pay off credit card debt. It's highly unlikely that I will ever get this money back if I lend it to her, and I've only saved a little over 20,000 yuan in the past year... My mom keeps instilling the idea that I have to support my younger siblings, although she stubbornly denies it.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello: Another example of the eldest child in the family carrying the responsibility of their parents. When parents are incapable, they pass the pressure on to their children, causing them to struggle in living their own lives and unable to fully utilize their energy and opportunities. It is a sad situation. However, life is meant to be lived for oneself, so please do not think that this is nonsense. If one day you truly have the ability, then you can take care of your younger siblings. But first, you need to develop your own skills and knowledge. Here is an analysis of your situation: 1. You graduated from an ordinary university with a major in accounting, but you are not interested in it. Throughout your four years of university, your English proficiency was relatively good, and you even passed the exam for American business graduate school, ranking in the top 20% of global candidates. (Although I don't understand what you mean by American business graduate school, the fact that you ranked in the top 20% is impressive. Many people have studied different majors and ended up not working in those fields, but those majors still provide valuable support later in life.) 2. However, you ultimately gave up on pursuing a master's degree in the United States due to the high tuition fees and your clear decision to not pursue a career in business. Despite these setbacks, you ended up working in online English education, where your salary is decent but unstable. (It seems unreasonable to blame yourself for the confusion. The expensive tuition fees are an objective problem, and not wanting to work in business is a subjective one. Your proficiency in foreign languages will bring you a lot of value and sense of accomplishment in this job, just like my love for psychology, which allows me to "find myself." Perhaps stability and qualifications are also factors, right? Nothing happens overnight, and you are still young, which is an advantage.) 3. So you decided to prepare for the translation master's exam. However, many things happened during your preparation that made you feel defeated and unsure of what to do. ① There is the pressure from your family. Your parents are incapable and have no savings even though they are in their fifties. They live day by day, and you also have a younger brother and sister who need to go to college. (We understand the principle of "drinking water and remembering its source," but what you need to understand now is that you need to stand up first in order to have the opportunity to help them. Otherwise, both of you will fall down together. I understand your pressure, with the loveable younger siblings on one hand and your own future on the other, but the responsibility for raising children lies with the parents, not the eldest child.) 4. Yesterday, your mother asked you to borrow 20,000 yuan to pay off her credit card. It is unlikely that this money will be returned, and you only managed to save a little over 20,000 yuan in the past year. Your mom always instills in you the idea that you should support your younger siblings, although she denies it. (Dear, if you don't want to do it, you can simply say "no." You don't need to endure or take on unnecessary responsibilities because it is not your duty. If this money can help you do something better for your own future, why not do it? They will find a way, they are adults.) ② You experienced a breakup. The guy broke up with you because of the long-distance relationship. Even if you had made a poor choice, it still causes significant emotional fluctuations because it was your first relationship. Coupled with your family situation, you feel like you will never be loved in this realistic society. After all, who would like a burden with a bad background? (It's the same issue again. You have wrapped yourself up in your family, but you are still you, and your family members are still your family. He was in a relationship with you, not with your family. If you can distinguish this, someone who loves you will also be able to distinguish it. If you can't, someone who loves you will not be able to either.) ③ The issue of preparing for the exam. Due to the breakup, your original plan for the exam was put on hold for several months. You know that you shouldn't blame anyone, but the loss of a few months has greatly diminished your confidence. And with little support from your family (mostly opposition), you feel even more uncomfortable. (So, do you want to take the exam or not? If you want to, then do it. If you don't, then don't do it. Don't think about doing something you don't want to do and add conflict to your inner self. Remember, what others think doesn't matter. What matters now is whether you want to take the exam. Everything else is just an excuse and a reason.) Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I wish you to respect your own future, as only by respecting yourself can you truly love others! If you have any confusion, feel free to message me!

When you don't know what to do, it's best to focus on what you can do well. The questioner says they are preparing to take the postgraduate entrance exam for translation studies. However, many things have happened during their preparation, which has left them feeling frustrated and unsure of what to do. In the current situation, the questioner needs to adjust their emotions, concentrate their energy on what they consider to be more important, such as online English education, and then focus on exam preparation. In addition, they need to learn to stretch their time and give themselves sufficient buffer zone. Making good use of "time and space awareness" can make one's life more resilient. Why is this important? Because some people are prone to anger or emotional sadness, and their logic is: "If I have a desire, it must be fulfilled immediately." If it cannot be fulfilled, they become angry and desire destruction. They will attack external objects, and if they can't, they will turn to attacking themselves, such as punching trees or even banging their heads against walls. They don't know how to take a detour or step back and wait for the right opportunity. This is because they lack a sense of time and space. It's important to remember that many things don't need to be rushed. If you extend the timeline for these things, the possibility of achieving your desires becomes infinitely greater in this longer river of time. Delayed gratification is popular nowadays, and it actually means increasing your sense of time. Because when time is extended and more investment is made, there are more opportunities, and therefore, the possibility of being satisfied increases.

Hello, I can feel your continuous efforts, constant progress, and excellence. You know what you want and you strive hard for it, which has led you to work in online English education. It seems like many things have happened that have made you frustrated. Yes, life is often full of disappointments, and perfect things don't exist, that's the truth. Your parents seem incapable, having no savings, and even asking you for money to support your younger siblings. I can sense that your parents have burdened you with heavy responsibilities, which can be overwhelming. This is one perspective, but let's also look at it from another angle. Your parents, during your underage years, managed to send you to college, which is better than many parents who can't afford to support their children's education. In the past, you had no means to earn money, but now you have savings and you have been constantly striving. You can see your inner strength that has brought you to where you are now. The world is not perfect, and we need to do what we can while allowing for some things to be beyond our control. We can help our families and younger siblings, but we can only do what we are capable of, and we need to establish our own boundaries. Changing our parents is difficult; we can only focus on what we can do ourselves. Allow for imperfections, acknowledge that there are things we cannot accomplish, and give yourself the permission to help your younger siblings or refuse to do so. Remember, you have grown up, and as long as you are willing, you can make choices that align with your true self.

Hello~ After reading your testimony, I can feel that you are quite desperate and unsure about the goal and direction of your life. In this period of time, as you summarized, all the things are overwhelming you and making it hard to breathe. Let's take it step by step to sort things out. Actually, when you mentioned that you took the exam for a business graduate program and ranked in the top 20% globally, it shows that you are very capable. You have a strong focus and execution ability in your studies. Even in this confusing moment, you are able to reflect on the source of your stress, which is probably more intricate than you imagined. Maybe I can share a bit more about stress with you. Firstly, concerning the people around you, it seems like they have gotten used to pushing all the stress onto themselves. Your mother, for example, puts the financial pressure on you, asking for money from you. She has "pushed" the responsibility and obligation of taking care of her children onto you. Perhaps she also pushes the pressure of survival onto you. You didn't mention your father's situation or work. It is very possible that you bear the burden of the whole family's living and also the pressure in terms of speech and mental well-being. Secondly, concerning love or relationships. When you describe some traits of your family, you may realize that in your family, it seems like you haven't experienced genuine "love". It seems like your family doesn't care about you and you haven't received love from them. Even if, as you mentioned, you have encountered unsuitable relationships and maybe "not worthy," there is still a feeling inside you that believes you are worthy of being loved. When it disappears, you feel that you won't feel loved in this life. And your self-value, something you are proud of, is also suppressed. Your abilities are belittled by yourself. Thirdly, regarding the topic of the graduate entrance examination, it accumulates the previous two and delays the things that you were originally proud of. At this time, the opposition from your family members makes you more devastated. In fact, deep down, you really hope that the people around you can encourage and appreciate you and also hope to hear them say, "It's okay, take your time." But perhaps it is an extravagant hope. Overall, you have taken on a lot of external pressure, including the unreasonable expectations your parents have for you, which squeeze your time, energy, and money. They don't think about how much harm and pressure their actions bring to you, just like Fan Shengmei in the drama "Ode to Joy." It's a void that can't be filled. Maybe you can think about some questions. First, learn to establish boundaries with your family, which also means protecting yourself from the pressure from their speech and mental aspects. As an adult, your mother should do some things on her own. What is she capable of? As a child, what is beyond your ability? Second, encourage and affirm yourself more. You naturally hope to receive recognition, encouragement, and support from others, but it's important to acknowledge your own value from within yourself, to recognize what you believe in. Because sometimes, in order to gain others' recognition, companionship, and support, we tend to follow their words. I hope to receive their approval. Third, establish a good social support system. When you encounter setbacks and hardships, find people who can rationalize and help you by listening to your venting, analyzing, and giving suggestions that are suitable for your situation, without judgment. It could be someone with life experience or a mental health counselor, etc. Also, you don't always have to hear negative news whenever you are in a difficult time. Lastly, and the most important point, learn to focus on yourself, pay attention to your joys, angers, sorrows, and happiness, things you like and dislike. You are important. You don't live for others.

② I experienced a heartbreak. The guy I was in a long-distance relationship with chose to break up with me. Since it was my first relationship, even if it was a bad match, it still caused a major emotional rollercoaster. Coupled with issues in my family, the heartbreak makes me feel like I will never be loved in this realistic society. Because no one will like someone with a disadvantaged background, right?  ③ The issue of taking the postgraduate entrance exam. Because of the heartbreak, my plans to take the exam have been put on hold for a few months. I know I shouldn't blame anyone, but losing a few months of time has greatly diminished my confidence. Additionally, my family had little support for the idea (there were mostly opposing voices), which makes me feel even worse. When everything piles up, I truly feel hopeless. I wish something unexpected would happen one day so that I could leave this world without blame.

question: I always nitpick about trivial matters and easily become impatient. How can I change this?
description: I feel annoyed whenever my friends say something, I even roll my eyes and don't respond. I get angry and uncomfortable when someone puts their things on my desk. I instinctively avoid it when others criticize me. I pay too much attention to other people's small actions and subtle expressions. I always look down on others and point out their flaws. I can't stand it when people talk to me or bother me when I'm studying. I have been like this since I was young, how can I change?
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-development

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. Based on your situation, it can be seen that you care a lot about what others think of you, but you haven't been able to express yourself clearly. To a large extent, the subconscious mind of the questioner is a manifestation of the self, but it is not obvious. The feeling of disgust arises because your subconscious mind is in conflict with the behavior of others, and you feel that the outcome is not what you want. Since you have selfishness, you also don't understand what others say to you. However, standing from your own perspective sometimes burdens you involuntarily. We all know that there is a gap between reality and our expectations, and each person is imperfect. However, you are a sensitive person. You are easily fragile, care about what others think, and are unable to control your emotions. You also have a slight tendency toward compulsion. These are the issues you need to resolve at present. We can all understand. Being oneself may seem like an easy thing to say, but it is difficult to act upon. At the same time, you also need to consider the feelings of others and find a comfortable way to interact with them. My suggestion is to learn to express your inner thoughts appropriately, and sometimes you need others to understand you. Search for the source of your emotions, do your best in every present task to reduce anxiety. Listen to music, watch movies, and gain different insights from lyrics or plotlines. Put yourself in the shoes of others and think about their feelings, whether your words have hurt them. Having a friendship is a joyful thing. Try new things, broaden your horizons, and make each day fulfilling. I hope my answer is helpful to the questioner. Thank you~.

I always fuss over trivial matters, what should I do? Hello, first of all, I understand and empathize with your situation. I want to give you a big hug so you can feel the warmth of the world. If your personality has been like this since childhood, there may be many factors that influenced you, such as the influence of family members who lead by example, or maybe someone around you or a classmate/friend who set a bad example for you. So, you need to find the reasons why you are like this in order to make appropriate changes. Because most of the time, making friends is about connecting at heart, not showing impatience or that unpleasant feeling. If you are always picky with your friends and always act dismissively towards them, they will feel that you are being insincere and not showing your true self. So, you also need to have a broad mind, because if you never pay attention to those small actions or glances, and contemptuously pick on others' faults, it means that your mind is relatively narrow. Even if a person is perfect, you will find faults in them, indicating that you are not accommodating and accepting of others. It's possible that you have high demands on others but are more tolerant and relaxed towards yourself. You've reversed the concept of being strict with yourself and lenient with others. It's also possible that you have high demands on yourself, which is why you have high demands on others. In this case, you need to pay attention to this attitude and personality by reflecting on and examining yourself. Otherwise, the people around you will distance themselves from you, and you will end up without friends, feeling lonely and isolated, like staying away from a crowd. But we are social creatures and cannot survive on our own; we always need social interaction. Therefore, maintaining good interpersonal relationships in society is essential. The reason you might think what others say is nonsense is that you perceive yourself as the center and think that whatever you say is right, while others are like clowns performing around you. It's as if you haven't achieved the basic respect for others. In fact, if you do achieve it, many friends will feel more comfortable. If you don't treat others seriously, they won't treat you seriously either. The key to human interaction is mutual trust and respect, not being self-centered and thinking that others are talking nonsense. Otherwise, others will also feel that you lack respect for them, and they won't have the desire to interact with you. Starting from now, it might be helpful to learn to praise the friends around you more, with sincerity. For example, if someone is wearing a nice outfit, you can compliment them and say, "Your outfit looks great, I want to buy something like that too." Say things that will make others happy. Everyone loves to hear compliments rather than criticisms. Furthermore, if someone helps you, say thank you, and remember to return the favor next time. When someone is talking, restrain yourself and try not to roll your eyes with negative emotions. Resist these bad behavior habits. Try to show respect for what others say. You may not agree, but you should allow others the freedom to express themselves. You can make eye contact with them, and if you think what they said is right, you can nod and smile slightly to show approval. Wishing the poster happiness and joy!

Hello, you mentioned that you are a second-level national psychological counselor. From your description, it seems that you can be quite easily provoked and bothered by trivial matters. Even small things can make you irritable and impatient. However, at the same time, you are very sensitive to the minor actions of others. I feel sorry for your state. It must be very difficult for you to relax in this state. You are constantly on edge, either feeling uncomfortable here or worried about something there. This state is something you experience. 1. When did this state start to appear? If it is a recent occurrence, has something happened recently that made you feel uncomfortable? If it has always been there, what has recently made you feel uncomfortable? 2. How often does this state occur? Is it only when you are with certain people, or does it happen with everyone? Does it happen every day or only occasionally in specific situations? 3. What is the situation when this state occurs? What are your thoughts at that time? 4. When this state occurs, do you immediately take action, or can you stop and feel your own emotions? 5. Imagine if you were to react differently in a certain situation, what would the result be? Would you feel more comfortable or even more uncomfortable with that result? If this "being particular" state often occurs, it can really affect your life. On the one hand, you feel uncomfortable, and on the other hand, the people around you are unsure how to deal with it. So what is hindering you from enjoying life? I guess it's because you have some rules that you haven't noticed, a lot of places where you don't accept yourself and others, and a state of uncertainty. I hope these questions can help you sort things out. Give them a try, and if they give you a different feeling, please let me know.

question: Is it my fault that my mother still doesn't understand my binge eating disorder? Am I being too much?
description: I found that every symptom of bulimia nervosa matches my situation. A doctor on Baidu suggested that I take Clomipramine, but after doing some research on Baidu, I found that the side effects are quite severe. So I told my mom about it and asked her to learn more about bulimia nervosa, and I said I want to go to the hospital tomorrow to get checked. She immediately replied, "You can go by yourself every day, I have to go to work." And then I started crying for no reason. My mom saw and came in to find me, and she took out her phone to search. My mom said she doesn't think I fit the diagnosis (even though she barely spends an hour with me each day, and I have plenty of time to engage in bingeing and purging in places she can't see). So I told her about my bingeing and purging behavior that started last year. At its worst, there were four to five episodes every day for one or two months in a row. She said she doesn't understand why I think I'm fat, and I told her that among our age group, I am the heaviest, exceeding the average weight by twenty pounds. Plus, I have to wear a uniform to school, and in the summer, we have to wear skirts. My legs are very thick, and the uniform sizes run small. Even the XXXL uniform pants are tight on me (I'm studying to become a flight attendant). But my mom still doesn't understand me and says it's a problem with my lack of self-discipline for not being able to stick to a diet. What should I do? Is it really my own issue? Am I being too much?
keywords: Behavior, anxiety, binge eating and dieting.

answers.answer_text: Hello, author! I can feel your sadness and helplessness regarding your mother's lack of understanding and the frustration of not being able to find a solution to your mental health issues. Neurotic binge eating disorder is a subtype of eating disorders. Although your mother doesn't understand your pain, she does have a point - you need to confirm whether you have neurotic binge eating disorder. I consulted the DSM-5 book on mental disorders and looked up professional symptom criteria and diagnostic standards. I can tell you that you can self-assess based on the following: Individuals with neurotic binge eating disorder often eat compulsively, consuming astonishing amounts of food, usually several thousand calories that are high in sugar, carbohydrates, and fat. They can eat quickly, sometimes even without tasting, devouring their food. Usually, binge eating stops only when they are interrupted by others, fall asleep, or experience stomach pain from overeating. Individuals with neurotic binge eating disorder may be slightly below normal weight, normal weight, overweight, or even obese. They often diet and engage in intense exercise to lose weight but cannot reach the low weight levels seen in individuals with neurotic anorexia. During binge episodes, individuals feel a loss of control. After binge eating, they may induce vomiting or use laxatives, often due to stomach pain and concern about weight gain. This cycle repeats at least several times a week. Diagnostic criteria for neurotic binge eating disorder include the following: 1. Recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by the following symptoms: a. Eating an excessively large amount of food within a specific period of time (e.g., within 2 hours) that is much more than what most individuals would eat in that same period; b. Feeling a sense of loss of control over eating during the episode (e.g., feeling that one cannot stop eating or control how much food one is eating); c. Engaging in unhealthy compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise; d. Binge eating and compensatory behaviors occur, on average, at least once a week for three months; e. Extreme concern with body weight and shape; f. These symptoms do not occur exclusively during episodes of neurotic anorexia. The number of unhealthy compensatory behaviors occurring per week indicates the severity of the disorder. Occupational, academic, family, or friendship problems can also contribute to rating: - Mild: 1-3 compensatory episodes per week - Moderate: 4-7 compensatory episodes per week - Severe: 8-13 compensatory episodes per week - Extreme: 14 or more compensatory episodes per week. You can self-assess based on the above criteria. If you confirm that you have neurotic binge eating disorder, I recommend seeking treatment at a hospital as this disorder may require medication as it is a type of mental disorder. Relying solely on self-regulation or allowing it to develop further may not be very effective. Although your mother may not fully understand you, it's important for you to stay determined. When you're sick, you must seek treatment and not delay your condition. Keep going! I support you! Feel free to message me when you're feeling down! Take care!

question: What is the mindset of those who play games with their ex?
description: After breaking up, shouldn't we just quietly move on and let each other move forward? So I'm very confused, what are the thoughts of those who can still play games together with their exes after breaking up?

answers.answer_text: Hello, this may be something that everyone who has experienced a breakup will go through. The perspective of the original poster is that after a breakup, it is best to cut off all contact with the ex-partner to avoid unnecessary trouble. The original poster believes that this is good for both parties because after a breakup, we will miss each other, and if we frequently contact each other, it is not conducive to ending the relationship and will make both people very painful. However, some people may not be able to do this. Perhaps they still think about each other but have no other way to interact, so they occasionally invite the other person to play a game. Maybe some people have completely let go of their ex and can be friends with them in a candid manner, playing games occasionally, which is also normal. As long as it doesn't affect the other person's life, it's fine.

question: Married for 10 years with my spouse, have a 6-year-old child, but not happy in life, can only tough it out?
description: I have been married to my partner for ten years, and our child is six years old, but I am not happy. They are always critical of me, finding fault in everything I say or do. I am truly exhausted. I sometimes think that death is the only way for it all to end, but I can't bear to leave my child behind. I have to keep going, even though it's tough. Many nights, I have to motivate myself to sleep. I have already purchased sleeping pills, fearing that one day I might just end it all. Whenever they're unhappy, we end up in a cold war, which lasts for a long time. I have to lower my head, apologize, and try to please them, only then can we move on. At home, they yell at me, always saying that things would be better without me. In the more than ten years we've been together, they have never once said sorry. They have never felt that they were wrong - they always believe they are right. Sometimes I question if I was born into this world by mistake, that I shouldn't have been born. It's just too tiring to grow up, dealing with being a parent, work, and marriage.

answers.answer_text: Darling, I know you have been enduring and suffering in silence. But life belongs to you, and it should not be influenced by others. Like you said, you cannot let go of your child because that is love and responsibility. When there are difficulties in your family, don't stay silent and wait for others to understand you. Take the initiative and have a serious discussion with your spouse in a gentle manner about your issues. When it comes to the serious topic of life, everything else becomes unimportant. Consider yourself more, as life is also your responsibility. Besides life, there are many other things. You just need a temporary rest and time to digest the accumulated matters. Give yourself some relaxation and pleasure. Even if the discussion doesn't result in a resolution, you will still live beautifully and freely on your own. It's not your fault, don't keep compromising. People are equal, and no one is obligated to endure discomfort. Family requires the commitment of two individuals. Hugs to you, you must stay strong! When you encounter problems, solve them instead of overthinking, as it will worsen your sleep issues. You are the one who has been wronged, and it must not be you who leaves. Many people need you, and someone who only hurts you will never cherish you. We all hope you stay and live beautifully.

question: Depressed and suspicious, unsure if this relationship can continue, what should I do?
description: I have been feeling a bit depressed recently. I am unsure whether my significant other is intentionally or unintentionally neglecting me, as they often take a long time to reply to messages and their responses seem rather perfunctory. I don't know if this relationship can continue.

answers.answer_text: The topic mentioned two issues. One is feeling depressed recently, and the other is suspicion towards the boyfriend. Regarding the "neglect" from the boyfriend, it's unclear whether he suddenly started responding to messages slowly or if he has always had a similar pace but the topic starter used to understand it and now feels it's too slow due to their own mood issues. Since there is doubt, why not just ask him directly? Speculating won't lead to any answers and it doesn't help with one's own mood or the relationship. It'll only create trouble for oneself. If there are problems between the two, then face them directly, communicate, and resolve them. If he does have other thoughts, then cutting losses in a timely manner can also be a gain. If the topic starter's own state is not good and their attitude towards the boyfriend's usual behavior has changed, then it brings up the well-known ABC theory from psychology. Our emotional state (C) is not directly determined by the event (A), but by our attitude (B) towards it. This brings us back to the topic starter's judgment of their current state. Depression usually has a reason or trigger event that leads to the depressive mood. Once this issue is resolved, the emotions will also adjust. We all need support from those around us - family, friends, and of course, the boyfriend is very important. Even if he can't directly solve the problem, he can listen to the topic starter vent, accompany them for a meal, and show understanding and acceptance towards their distressing emotions and conflicts. This can greatly help alleviate the depressive state. Maybe the boyfriend is unsure of what to do or feels helpless and avoids the topic because the topic starter is unwilling to share their feelings or rejects his attempts to provide help.

question: What is the significance of the theme of separation in the final session of the mental growth group?
description: Today is the last session of the personal growth group that I have been attending. In the previous six sessions, the facilitator did not mention the topic beforehand. It was only after the members arrived that the facilitator slowly guided us to open up ourselves. However, before the last session, the facilitator informed us early on that the theme would be "separation". During today's session, I thought there would be a summary from each person or some kind of farewell message from the facilitator, but there was none of that. We just chatted and hugged each other before it ended. I had prepared my thoughts for this session for a week, but they were not needed. Why did the facilitator emphasize this session? Is it because she wants us to walk our own path without relying on her? Or is she concerned that some individual members might keep bothering her with questions after the group sessions end?

answers.answer_text: What kind of person is your advisor? I think in the past it was his teaching style, but now that it's almost over, let's have something special, everyone relax, and let ourselves relax too? Don't you think those two words are cool? Hehe, maybe his intention is very pure, just want to propose a theme, just like someone who only likes red, if you say it likes red, it means something about it... Maybe the advisor's purpose is to make you understand purity? You can read "Forbidden Fruit" in the book "The Left-Handed Genius and the Right-Handed Madman" (recommended by a friend).

question: After the calmness in a marriage, should we continue or say goodbye?
description: 30 years old, female, married for 2 years, daughter is 1 and a half years old, in a long-distance marriage. Both husband and wife are employed, and both come from farming backgrounds. I bought a house where I work, and my mother-in-law helps to take care of the child. I pay the mortgage, as well as the living expenses for myself, my child, and my mother-in-law. In the early stages of my husband's job, his salary was low, and he often needed financial support from me. Later, I discovered that he had taken out loans to invest in stocks. Despite earning more than me, he lost all the money through stock trading, and now owes over 170,000 yuan. When I asked for the reason, he said he wanted to become rich and buy a house, which is why he invested in stocks. Later, he also bought amber and continued to use loans to invest in stocks. Every time he received his salary, he used it all to buy amber. When I advised him to make rational investments, he claimed that the returns from amber were higher. When I asked him for some living expenses, he said he had no money and was in debt. Currently, I am the one supporting the family and paying the mortgage, living paycheck to paycheck. He claims to be earning money to pay the mortgage but refuses to provide any living expenses. However, he continues to buy amber every month. Occasionally, when he comes home, he does nothing except cooking and ignores all the household chores. Our relationship has reached a point where we no longer argue about anything and we don't even want to stay in touch. Can this marriage continue? I am exhausted and no longer in love, but I still hold onto a little hope that things might get better in the future. Sometimes I think that ending the long-distance aspect of our relationship by moving to his city might improve things, but what if I lose my job and have no financial security?

answers.answer_text: Hello asker. I see a resilient and optimistic personality in you, but I also sense the endurance and suffering between the lines. You are torn between going left or right in the face of the current situation. In your analysis, your husband's desire for money is not based on rational analysis, leading to repeated investment failures. These investment failures may not be greatly improved by your compromise and concession. Therefore, personally, I think quitting your job is a big risk considering the current circumstances. Choosing to develop in his city may not be a wise choice, and it is even possible to lose your source of income due to your resignation, leading to even greater anxiety. Your current state seems to be under a lot of pressure, and when you have thoughts about whether to continue the marriage, it already indicates that you have doubts about your relationship and are wavering in your confidence to continue. However, holding onto a glimmer of hope, you are ready to face life's struggles and become a warrior. Your husband is putting all his thoughts into investments, stuck in a colorful dream of getting rich. Excessive obsession often makes it difficult to see the reality, and he is unwilling to create happiness through steady accumulation. He is more like a playful child, while you are the responsible caregiver, shouldering most of the burden. Perhaps you can understand his investment plans by communicating with him and ask what his intentions are. Regardless, to avoid unnecessary risks, it is really not advisable for you to quit your job until your husband's situation improves. As for whether to continue this marriage, others cannot give direct opinions. Only advice is to not easily tilt too many resources towards the other person, no matter what decision you make in the future. Holding onto essential conditions will give you enough confidence.

Whether to continue or say goodbye depends on when the other person can truly understand life and how long we can hold on. 1. Survivorship bias Many people can only see others making money from stock trading but fail to see those who have lost everything and even lost their lives because of it. It is common knowledge that there are risks in investments, but how many people can remain calm when they see others' assets multiply several times in a short period of time? The husband certainly saw others' gains and was tempted himself, so he started trying it out. Of course, during this process, he also tasted some success. However, due to the gambler's mentality, he wanted even higher returns, which led to repeatedly buying at the top, eventually accumulating significant debt. 2. Facing reality, what we should do now is first figure out how much debt the other person has accumulated outside and how these loans were obtained. When necessary, we can consult a lawyer to see if the other person's debt is related to our lives and pre-existing assets because, for many debt collectors, they only care about money, not emotions. At the same time, we also need to be honest with each other and set a deadline. If the other person fails to understand the importance of cutting losses in a timely manner, then we also need to consider ourselves and our children, after all, the cost of their education will only increase. Meanwhile, the other person has never fulfilled their responsibilities as a husband and father. The world and I still love you.

Hello, getting married and having young children, with your mother-in-law taking care of the child while you work to pay the mortgage and living expenses. However, your husband not only doesn't make money but also invests in stocks and owes a lot of debts. It seems that you are quite angry about his irresponsible behavior that affects the whole family. Marriage is actually a mutual effort and requires contributions from both partners. It seems like your husband is not fulfilling his responsibilities as a husband, father, or son, but rather focuses on his own interests such as stock trading and investment. Regarding whether to continue the marriage or pursue a divorce, you should consider the pros and cons. If you choose not to divorce, you must accept that your husband may not change and will continue to not contribute and accumulate debts. Can you tolerate this? If you choose to divorce, you need to consider if you can take care of the child without your husband and mother-in-law's support, and also assess your financial capability. Both choices have their advantages and disadvantages, and your life will be different from the current one. What you need to consider is whether you can take responsibility for your decision and not regret it. You don't need to rush into making a decision; instead, analyze the situation rationally, weigh the pros and cons, respect your true needs, listen to the opinions of family and friends, and then make the best choice for yourself at the moment.

Hello dear, sending you a warm hug! Your description vividly portrays the image of a hardworking mother who has to work to support the family and pay the mortgage, while also taking care of her children. I believe that you will also be their hope when both parents need it. You are a great mom, you work so hard! Hugs to you. On the other hand, your husband is completely different. In a long-distance marriage, he is more like a "single" young man, working and earning money for his own dreams of being a "rich man". When you compare the two, you realize that you contribute more to the marriage, both emotionally and financially. So, you may have a lot of reluctance, while your husband seems to just follow the script of life, getting married and having children, without needing to put in so much effort. The unequal state of your marriage has left both of you tired. Of course, there is a possibility to change the current situation through adjustments. When you don't have financial security or haven't found a way out, it is not recommended to give up your current life and job to move to your husband's city and live together. Unless you already have a job or your husband can temporarily support you and your child. Otherwise, your shared life will be even more difficult. If you have a better plan and reach an agreement with your husband, you can try living together, which will make your life easier with someone to share the load. But if your husband is not ready and doesn't have the ability to take responsibility, it's better not to live together immediately, otherwise there will be more conflicts. Your husband needs to be more practical, face reality, and work hard. Of course, investing in stocks or amber may make big money, but not everyone can do it. I hope your husband understands this sooner and wakes up. May your family of three live in harmony and happiness!

Hello, questioner! From your description, I understand that you are a hardworking and financially stressed individual. I can see that you put a lot of effort into your family but do not receive warmth and understanding from your husband. Being in a long-distance marriage is truly difficult for you. The hardships you face can only be understood by yourself. Perhaps your husband's stock trading is partly to earn more money for the family, to provide you with a better life. On the other hand, in a long-distance marriage, your husband is also left alone in an empty house, unable to escape from feelings of loneliness and isolation. Stock trading might be one way for him to alleviate that loneliness. When stock trading experiences a downturn, it can also affect his mood and cause him to be anxious and helpless. Just imagine, if you were not in a long-distance relationship, he could be with his wife, children, and his own mother, and he might not have as much time to invest in stock trading. He might prioritize taking care of various household chores, right? Both spouses need to sit down and communicate calmly. Stock trading is just a temporary psychological escape. The money earned through hard work truly belongs to oneself. Weighing between family and career, ending the long-distance marriage as soon as possible might be the best solution. Otherwise, the cracks between husband and wife will grow larger, posing a threat to the marriage. Such days may become increasingly difficult to sustain.

First of all, thank you for your trust and invitation to discuss. I see that you are exhausted and desperate in your current marriage, but there is also a hint of nostalgia. Perhaps you need some space and time to explore what makes you nostalgic about this marriage. What has disappointed you in this marriage? What kind of married life do you desire? Is it in line with what your husband wants? What changes can both of you make to improve the quality of the marriage? Once you have a clear understanding of these aspects, you may have better and more suitable choices. Best wishes!

question: 29-year-old woman, how can she improve her focus?
description: Nowadays, I always find it hard to concentrate on tasks. I easily get distracted, constantly wanting to check my phone or do something else. I fail to focus my energy on what I truly need to do. How can I improve my ability to concentrate?

answers.answer_text: Hello, to improve your focus, you can make the following improvements. Clarify your motivation for doing this task. Before doing something, you should think carefully about why you are doing it and what goals you want to achieve. By clarifying your motivation, you will be more motivated to do things. Cultivate indirect interest in this matter. Interest is the best teacher. If we are interested in something, we will unconsciously want to do it. However, we are not interested in everything that we must do, so we need to cultivate our interest in the matter. Organize activities reasonably. When doing things, you should balance work and rest. After working for a while, give your brain and body a rest. Working in a tired state will definitely lead to more distractions. Avoid irrelevant distractions. We should not rely too much on our willpower and should avoid distractions from unrelated matters while working. For example, you can turn off your phone and work in a quiet environment. These are just some of my suggestions. You can give them a try. Good luck~.

OP, hello! After reading your description, I have a certain understanding of the question you want to ask, and I also give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can feel that you have a good analysis of yourself and know where you are not doing well. Furthermore, you are seeking help from others on social platforms, which is better than what most people do. Thumbs up for that. Actually, to some extent, everyone has difficulty concentrating well. This is also a normal social phenomenon, given that we live in an era of technology and convenience, such as smartphones and computers. But at the same time, these temptations also distract our attention and make us spend a lot of time using them every day. So, if you want to improve your focus, it doesn't mean completely avoiding electronic devices, but rather using them appropriately at the right time and place. When it's time to complete your tasks, focus on them instead of thinking about playing with your phone. Therefore, I have summarized some methods that I hope can help you: (1) Categorize the things you need to do, know some strategies, start with easier tasks and gradually tackle the more difficult ones. Don't panic, and don't put too much pressure on yourself. (2) Find the motivation for the task you need to do, that is, understand the impact it can have on yourself. This will increase your interest in doing the task. (3) Give yourself positive affirmations, such as telling yourself that you can do it. Don't give up before even starting. (4) Develop the habit of focusing on small things every day, called "gazing technique." Pay attention to concentrate with determination to overcome distractions. With focus, your awareness will gradually narrow to a narrow range, allowing your mind to gather and be invigorated. (5) Create a schedule to record what you should do at specific times to keep yourself organized. The world and I love you, wishing you all the best!

question: Regretting breaking up with your ex-partner, can you go and find her now?
description: Because I was too young and immature before, it led to our break up. After the break up, she started dating another guy. Now it seems like they have broken up. I'm just wondering if I should go and find her.
keywords: Love, how to win back your ex.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. Emotions are unpredictable. Some relationships can be patched up after breaking, while others cannot be repaired once broken. It depends on the intentions and determination of both parties.
