Do you know the story of hedgehogs keeping warm? In winter, two hedgehogs were very warm, and there were no other ways to keep warm around them. So they thought of getting close to each other. However, when they got really close, the spines on their bodies caused pain to each other, so they had to move away. This is the dilemma that exists in the interpersonal relationships of some people. The occurrence of this situation is related to our long-term relationship patterns with others, especially significant others. For example, if we have a very intrusive mother who controls intimate expressions, we will be very afraid of intimate relationships. But I don't know why you feel this way, perhaps we will gradually find the answer in the counseling session.

Title owner, hello. Based on your description, there may actually be many reasons, but the most crucial aspect is how you felt at that time and what thoughts you had. It is because of these thoughts that you took further action. Here, let's analyze two possible reasons. 1. When others are good to you, it can bring a lot of pressure, and this pressure can lead to you being torn between "others are so good to me, am I good to them? How can I be better to them?" This pressure, along with the potential thoughts of wanting to reciprocate the same or better, is what prevents you from feeling too much pressure and maintains a sense of fairness and reciprocity, similar to a "fair trade" feeling. It is because of this feeling that you may feel the pressure, dislike it, and unintentionally reject the goodwill from others. 2. When people become close to you, there may be ulterior motives, causing you to develop a sense of self-protection and push away the kindness of others. Thoughts such as "Why is this person so good to me? Do they have any demands or hidden agendas?" create an atmosphere of uncertainty and self-doubt, making you feel unsafe. In order to protect yourself, you subconsciously push away the kindness of others, as there is no such thing as unconditional kindness. As mentioned at the beginning, the most important thing is to reflect on what thoughts and self-awareness you had when others became close to you. Only by calmly observing your situation at that time can you understand why you pushed away the kindness of others. This will prevent you from feeling regret or experiencing other negative emotions. Remember, as long as the choices you made at that time were the best in your opinion, there will be no regrets. Being a individual: managing oneself, taking responsibility for gains and losses, keeping things simple and straightforward, without complex relationships, controls, or conflicts, and avoiding the pain of separation.

Hello dear friend! Your description is simple but contains a lot of information! Allow me to analyze it in detail and give you a warm hug (づ●─●)づ～～ You mentioned that you always push away the kindness of others and resist getting close to them. On one hand, as you said, it is because you lack a sense of security and want to maintain a certain distance from others in order to ensure your own safety, which is reasonable! On the other hand, our behaviors and emotions often follow our subconscious rather than our conscious mind. Your tendency to always push away the kindness of others today is likely influenced by a "voice" in your subconscious. You can try to be aware of the thoughts or voices that appear in your mind when you push away the kindness of others. Additionally, based on my personal experience, this may be related to your upbringing! It could be an extension or replication of certain negative relationship patterns from your early years in your social sphere. Would you mind sharing some information about your family background? For example, how was the intimacy between you and your parents from childhood to adulthood? How was the marital relationship between your parents? How much "love language" (smiles, hugs, praises) did you receive throughout your life? Of course, I respect your privacy and only if you feel comfortable sharing.

Hello! I noticed that you have a tendency to push away people who are close to you, which is somewhat similar to "avoidant attachment personality." It is a fear of intimate relationships, where you prefer to keep yourself in an uncertain relationship and when the other person expresses a desire to get closer to you, you want to escape. This mindset is related to your upbringing in your original family, as the way you interacted with your family members during your childhood has influenced your cognition. The lack of affection, being easily neglected, feeling inferior, and lacking a sense of security can make you overly cautious with others. Have you ever thought if you are this kind of person? Wanting to escape is a reflection of self-doubt: am I worthy of others' affection? Can I have a stable intimate relationship? Perhaps you have been hurt in past intimate relationships, which is why you do not trust them and do not believe that you can have intimate relationships. I recommend seeking counseling or exploring the underlying reasons based on your specific circumstances. Engaging in some psychological training activities could also help you improve sooner. Best wishes!

question: Why am I afraid of the wind blowing through the car window?
description: I am very afraid when driving with the car window open and the wind blowing on my face. I don't feel scared no matter how strong the wind is when I walk on the road, but I feel very scared when the wind blows into the car. My heart starts to race, so I have to close the window every time I ride in a car. Why is that?

answers.answer_text: Hello, let me tell you: about my thoughts, I hope it will be helpful to you. Riding in a car itself can give a sense of insecurity, and the blowing wind may increase your feelings of insecurity. Therefore, you may be afraid and have palpitations. Riding in a car is different from walking, with different speeds, different sensations, and different levels of control. Therefore, the sense of insecurity brought by riding in a car is stronger. Coupled with the wind blowing in through the window, it may increase your feelings of insecurity and anxiety, causing you to be afraid and have palpitations. Perhaps you have had a bad experience in the past of riding in a car with the wind blowing, so the fear and palpitations are conditioned reflexes. Maybe you have experienced or heard of such bad experiences of opening the car window and feeling the wind, perhaps when you were younger, you can't remember clearly, or you have heard or seen such things, so as soon as you open the window and feel the wind, you will have a conditioned reflex and a corresponding reaction. Perhaps the wind blowing through the window can cause discomfort in your body, and you are also afraid and have palpitations. Many people will have a runny nose or sneezing when the wind blows, and may have symptoms of rhinitis. So you may also be afraid of the wind blowing, and perhaps you also have early signs of such physical discomfort, but it has not been very obvious yet.

After reading your description, two conditions for fear have been established. The first one is a vehicle, and the second one is wind. Let's talk about the first condition. What kind of vehicle will trigger this reaction? Will it happen if you take a bus? Will you have that feeling if you ride in an open-air vehicle with a back seat? As for the second condition, the fear differs between a light breeze and a stronger wind. If there is another person sitting next to you by the window, how intense is the feeling of fear? To address this, you can use either desensitization therapy or integrate a fixed conditioned reflex. I prefer the latter, which involves associating the feeling of relaxation and happiness with a specific posture, such as pinching the thumb, index finger, middle finger, and ring finger of your right hand together. Feel that relaxed and happy sensation, and hold the pinch for more than three seconds. Remember that feeling and repeat it. Once this relaxed and happy feeling occurs, bring together all four fingers and deepen that sensation. After repeating this process at least five times, the conditioned reflex will be established. Next, when the fear arises during a car journey, utilize this specific action. It will effectively eliminate your sense of fear. You can give it a try.

question: Parents are separated in two different places to help their brother and sister-in-law take care of their grandchildren. What should be done if there are signs of infidelity?
description: The older brother and sister-in-law have two children. The first child has already started attending kindergarten, and in the beginning, the mother used to go alone to their house to help take care of the child because the father hadn't retired yet. Now that the father has retired and the second child is only two years old, a boy, both parents are taking care of the children at the brother and sister-in-law's house. However, the father has recently suggested taking turns to spend half a month taking care of the children and the other half at home. My mom doesn't really want to do this. A few days ago, while at the seldom-used house with my mom, I noticed extra child pillows, women's socks on the bed, and magazines. My mom also found a piece of fabric for making children's clothes on her bed. Both of us are suspicious. My parents are already 60 years old, and my mother wants companionship in her old age, so she doesn't want to reveal anything. When I was 12 years old, my dad had an affair, so my mom has always been very sad. Their upbringings were very different, with my dad's side being poor and my mom's dad being a director. My mom has feelings of inferiority. I want to protect my mom and help them improve their relationship. Now, the plan is for one person to go and see the children for half a month, which gives my dad an opportunity to have an affair. What should I do to save this family? Can I install cameras? Does anyone have any good suggestions?

answers.answer_text: Hello, after reading your question, I can feel the distress and turmoil this situation involving your family has caused you. It also reminds me of a female friend whose father had a habit of cheating and her mother, upon discovering it, would often be subjected to domestic violence. When the children grew up, they asked their mother why she didn't divorce him, and she always said it was because they were still young. There were five children in the family, who witnessed their mother being beaten from a young age. As they grew up, the mother would constantly complain to the children about their father, saying he was still cheating. Four out of the five children had conflicts with their father and expressed the desire to cut ties with him. Every time they tried to convince their mother to divorce him, she would say she was afraid of being laughed at because of her age. As a result, although the mother seemed to have accepted the situation, the anger still lingered inside her, and she would call the children to complain, causing them to distance themselves from her. At the same time, the children themselves also became trapped in the pain. Seeing their mother's vulnerability, suggesting that she leave him would fall on deaf ears. However, her daily phone calls complaining about him would cause her unbearable headaches, severely impacting her life. The mother became disconnected from society. At the age of 48, she had no skills, never having worked since getting married, so she had fear of change and didn't know what she could do if she divorced. Furthermore, her husband's infidelity was a shameful matter for her, and she believed that her own weakness and incompetence had led to his cheating. Every time she saw him, it was as if she was seeing her own incompetence, which made her very angry and led to arguments. But she was "afraid" to divorce... This example shows that the older generation's aversion to divorce is partly due to the belief that "divorce" is a shameful thing, and if it becomes public, it's like proving their own incompetence. On the other hand, as the children grow up and have children who will "stand up" for them (a saying indicating that enduring will pay off once the children grow up), the children will naturally "punish" the father. This gives them a sense of revenge and balances their emotions. At the same time, as they get older, remarrying involves too many issues, so they are hesitant to divorce, fearing they will have no one to rely on in old age. There is also the fact that they have been detached from reality for too long, with no personal life or interpersonal support outside the family, which fills them with fear of the unknown, etc. [Getting back to the main topic] Based on your description of the current situation in your family, your father has previously cheated and your mother is used to self-denial, and now she suspects your father is cheating again. [Analysis] This suspicion is built on the foundation of previous mistrust in your father, and it is normal to have this mindset when trust has been broken in a relationship. However, humans are also peculiar creatures. There is a psychological phenomenon called "self-fulfilling prophecy," which means that how you perceive something will subconsciously push it towards that direction. For example, after the mother experienced her husband's adultery, she believes that he is someone who enjoys cheating. So although she seems to have forgiven him, seeing him still causes her distress and pain, and she suspects he will cheat again. As a result, she becomes angry and doesn't give him a warm reception when she sees him. Humans need emotional support, and when they don't receive it from their spouse and children, they often seek it outside the family. (I personally don't like this explanation, as it makes it seem like infidelity is someone else's fault. But for the older generation who haven't studied psychology, they are more easily controlled by emotions and primal instincts, which is indeed a fact.) [What can you do?] Your current concern is how to solve the problem without damaging the emotional foundation. First of all, try to ascertain the facts and not blow the problem out of proportion. Don't go around telling everyone in the family about it, as this will cause more harm. On the factual level, you can directly ask about the suspicions of infidelity, but this will only startle the snake in the grass, even if there is something going on, he won't admit it, and it will damage the relationship. As for whether to install surveillance cameras, as long as it doesn't violate any legal issues, it may be worth considering. However, it is important to understand that installing cameras is just to make yourself clear about the situation. Regardless of the outcome, you can tell your mother that your father didn't cheat (since it's her desire), and you don't need to let them know about the cameras. Next: if you find out he didn't cheat, you can put it to rest for now. If you find out he did cheat, you can talk to him about the previous incident of cheating and the harm it caused to the family, and express that you are willing to forgive his previous behavior, but if it happens again, you will choose to stand with your mother, and the family will not forgive him again. (Since he is worried about retirement issues, expressing it in this way can also be a deterrent.) Lastly, encourage your mother to go out more in the evenings, join in some square dancing, and open up her body, as an open body leads to an open mind, gradually avoiding negative thinking. Organize more family gatherings and outings to distract and experience the beauty of life. Every family has their own difficult experiences, so imagine if this happened in my own family, I would probably handle it more decisively, and I think my mother's personality would also have less tolerance. So, with different family situations, think more about your own approach, as you are the one who knows the family situation best. Home is a place where love is cherished, so cherish it. If love can solve the problem, try not to resort to dark methods. I hope this is helpful to you and good luck~.

"It is crucial that Mom keeps it a secret. She wants to maintain the current relationship, and as a woman, I sympathize with her. Maybe for herself, but mostly for the children, she chooses to bear everything alone. Personal suggestions: 1. Understand the root of their relationship issues and see if it is possible to resolve the infidelity problem (without divorce). It could be a mismatch in lifestyle or too much negative emotion from Dad, so finding a "soulmate" and entering the heart might be helpful. An affair is rarely intended to betray, but rather to be with someone they enjoy doing happy things with, usually due to problems in the intimate relationship. 2. Listen to your brother's opinion. 3. The significant difference in both of their personal status might lead to an unequal pattern in their relationship. 4. Mom has been hurt before, and you are her strong support. She doesn't want to bring up old wounds. You can indirectly care about her life, provide emotional support, be concerned about her physical health, and let her know that her efforts are worthwhile. 5. "I am already of such an age, so I should..." is a phrase often spoken by the older generation, as they feel time slipping away and want to pursue special meaning or a sense of value. 6. If objective conditions allow, have your brother's children stay at your parents' home. 7. Find an opportunity to talk to Dad one-on-one, in a quiet environment, when he is in a good mood. Communicate without emotions, gradually entering the subject without blame. As a father, he will come up with countless excuses to avoid being accused by the children. It is still speculative that Dad is having an affair; the above is just analysis. Give yourself a psychological suggestion: "Sometimes what we see and hear might not be true." Remember: Do not install cameras and do not cause further harm! This would harm not only one person but an entire family, maybe several families. Don't act impulsively, don't be curious, and don't seek the truth. In this matter, the main characters are only Mom and Dad, and you are just a supporting role, but you can play a certain role. Do not hold onto others' mistakes, but think about ways to solve the problem. If you decide not to separate, tell Mom that Dad is her only "VIP" and that the way they interact needs to change."

Hello, the landlord suspects that their father is having an affair and their mother also suspects it, but their mother doesn't want to get a divorce. The landlord doesn't know what to do. I understand the landlord's feelings very well. As children, we definitely do not want our parents to get a divorce. We love them both very much, but the father's actions are hurting the mother and also hurting the landlord. Suggestions: 1. This is a matter between the parents, whether to get a divorce or how to handle it should be up to the parents themselves. As children, we should also respect their marriage. 2. The landlord should first ask their mother for her opinion, what she wants to do, and if she needs the landlord's help. How to choose to handle it is up to the mother to decide, as she has her own methods and reasons. Just spend more time with the mother. 3. The landlord is just suspicious, and this is an uncertain matter. They can privately talk to the father and approach it strategically. They can ask something like: "Why are there so many extra pillows on the bed? And women's stockings? Dad, you're getting older. I hope you haven't lost your morals. Mom told me she goes to see the kids alone every other month, and she's really worried about you. She wants to be with you to go see the kids and come back home together. We don't have many years left, so she hopes to spend more time with you. She really loves you!" 4. Approach the topic casually during a conversation. 5. I don't recommend directly confronting or setting up cameras. Regardless of whether there is evidence or not, at least your mother doesn't want to know the truth. Therefore, the landlord should take a more indirect approach. 6. Observe the father in secret and subtly hint to him when they are alone. They can give an example of how they would feel and handle it if their parents were in a similar situation. Let him understand the landlord's thoughts. 7. Subtly shake him up, but not to the point of exposing everything, as the mother doesn't want that. The past trauma has hurt the mother, and given that she comes from a well-off family, the father must love her very much. However, the differences or feelings between them are only known to them. The father's affair is not right, but at least the mother has tolerated it. There are reasons of their own. 8. The mother has self-esteem issues, and it's not about external conditions, but it's related to her own feelings and her early life experiences. It's her own issue. 9. It's natural to feel resentment, but if the mother doesn't want to separate, we should try our best to keep them together and find a solution that doesn't damage their dignity. This is the biggest principle in handling this matter. 10. It is strongly recommended that they go see the children together and not be separated. They can discuss with their brother whether they can consider finding another way, so that their parents don't have to part ways, and to avoid the possibility that the reality of separation might help the affair.

Hello, the main issue you're facing is indeed difficult to handle. On one hand, your father has a history of infidelity and there are signs of it happening again. On the other hand, your mother is unwilling to break up the family. Your concern is for your mother and you don't want her to be mistreated or hurt, so you want to save your parents' relationship. However, you are also worried about how to handle the situation if your father's infidelity is confirmed, and feel caught in a dilemma.

Firstly, I believe it is necessary to find out the truth. Unfounded speculation about loved ones, as well as deliberate concealment, often end up causing harm. Perhaps you need to have a deep conversation with your father. Trust that someone of his age can make an appropriate choice, whether he can give a reasonable explanation or confirm your suspicions. At least you will know the truth and his true thoughts.

Secondly, take care of your mother's well-being. In this unclear situation, your mother is likely to be in pain. If your suspicions are wrong, that would be the best outcome and your mother can relieve her worries. If your father is indeed having an affair, your mother also needs to know the truth in order to make her own choices.

Lastly, you need to bridge the gap between your parents. Communication is the most effective and least damaging way to solve problems. From your description, it is clear that there are some issues between your parents. Only by addressing these problems can you uncover the underlying issues and find ways to deal with them.

Ultimately, trust your parents. They have been living together for a lifetime and know what each other needs. Regardless of the decisions they make, trust that they have carefully considered them and believe that they will make the right choices.

question: Did I ruin my life after failing the postgraduate entrance exam?
description: I failed the postgraduate entrance examination this year, and my attempt to transfer failed due to low scores. I feel like I have lost all hope in life and have no direction. I want to give it another try, but I don't have the courage. I spend every day in a daze at home, not knowing what to do. My family wants me to work, but I have lost all confidence and feel like a total failure.

answers.answer_text: Hello! The failure in the postgraduate entrance examination has greatly affected your spirits, and you feel disheartened. The teacher understands your current feelings! Think carefully, why do you feel disheartened? Is it because you consider the failure in the postgraduate entrance examination as your entire self? Can it really be like that? The postgraduate entrance examination is just a part of your life experience. Just like the college entrance examination, one failure only represents that specific instance, not your entire life. Both work and postgraduate studies are your goals. Take a careful inventory and consider whether you currently want to pursue postgraduate studies or work more. Choose what you truly want, what you most want to do, and what is most likely to lead to success. By doing so, you will find the real you and live as your authentic self.

question: A 15-year-old girl, why does she always feel unworthy of living?
description: All my previous boyfriends were with me for money, so now I feel like I want to become a strong independent woman, but I can't do anything well.

answers.answer_text: Fifteen years old is still young and too immature. At this age, you should be enjoying yourself in the campus, not worrying about a boy. It's great to want to become a strong woman, but success doesn't come overnight. Everything takes time, and the more impatient you are, the more likely you are to fail. It's okay if things don't go as planned, the key is to learn from the process to prevent making the same mistakes again. It doesn't matter whether you do something well or not, what matters is whether you did your best. Don't let unrelated people influence your original intentions. You can only break free from constraints by boldly letting go of the outcome. Live freely according to your true and beautiful thoughts, instead of letting others dictate your self-doubt.

question: More and more emotional numbness, a heart as calm as still water, is it good or bad?
description: I feel that I am becoming more and more emotionless lately. Every day feels like a calm sea, as if there is nothing that can make me happy or sad. Is it good or bad to be neither happy nor sad like this?

answers.answer_text: Dear questioner, how are you? After reading your description, I can sense your confusion and a slight sigh of helplessness. Hugs to you~ Actually, when you asked this question, it shows that you do not think the current state of "a calm heart" is good. It feels more like a helplessness towards the fact that reality can no longer bring you a vibrant and passionate life. There is a sense of being forced to have a "calm heart" or a "dead heart". I don't know if I am right or not? Some people consider "neither sad nor happy" as a high state and deliberately pursue this feeling. In reality, we can only achieve a state of "neither sad nor happy" when our inner self remains peaceful and stable regardless of what happens externally. Our hearts will be at ease and filled with a faint joy. There is no right or wrong for each state of mind. If your current state, fully accepting it, allows you to feel peace and tranquility, then it is good. If it makes you feel uncomfortable, then it is not good. Wishing you a pleasant life!

question: How much does mental counseling and therapy generally cost? I need to earn money to treat my illness.
description: 1\How much does psychological counseling and therapy usually cost? I need to earn money to afford treatment.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I sense your urgent need for psychological healing. Here, I will do my best to share the information I know with you. Psychological counseling and therapy are actually different concepts. Psychological counseling deals with general or severe psychological problems, personality disorders, various neuroses, and so on. On the other hand, psychological therapy may involve more in the realm of mental disorders and require intervention from the field of medical knowledge, possibly in conjunction with medication. These two different concepts will have different fee systems. If it falls within the category of psychological counseling, the fees can vary, ranging from free consultations to over a thousand per session (0-1000+). The pricing criteria depend on the counselor's training background, personal experience, and case history. However, if you are facing financial difficulties, with a sincere effort, you may discover that various psychological platforms and organizations often offer free counseling or group-buying activities. Although some may be one-time analysis and answers, they might still be helpful to you, so it's worth a try. Furthermore, if the issues requiring counseling are more complex, it is recommended to find a reliable counselor. Although they may charge a few hundred dollars per session, they may professionally solve your problems in a small number of sessions. If the issue involves mental disorders and requires psychological therapy, you can go to a hospital's psychiatric department or specialized mental health institution. Make an appointment through registration for consultation. The fees charged will also have a relatively transparent standard; you can refer to the hospital's consultation prices when selecting doctors of different qualifications. In short, the specific costs depend on assessing your situation and severity.

question: We have been together for a year and have been cheated on by a third party. What should we do?
description: We have been together for a year, and prior to that, I made sure that he was not married or in a relationship. Recently, he suddenly became distant and told me to leave him. Initially, I thought it was because of my own shortcomings and that he was cheating on me. But later, I discovered that he had actually been married before he met me, and they are now planning their wedding banquet. Knowing this, I felt devastated. What should I do? His wife is also innocent. Should I tell her?

answers.answer_text: Hello, the title holder! After dating for over a year, it was discovered that the partner is already married. The pain of breaking up is mixed with the feeling of being deceived and the anger of betrayal. I really want to retaliate against him, to let his wife see his true nature, for her to leave him or to create chaos. It seems like only then can I find psychological balance. On further examination, perhaps this reveals a hint of a destructive mindset that might ruin my own chances? Is that so? Obviously, this "ex-boyfriend" used deceitful behavior to gain your emotional and physical investment, which is enough to show that his character is flawed. Every relationship begins with looks and stays loyal to character. With someone who has such questionable character, even if it wasn't an issue today and even if you were to marry, there would still be great harm waiting for you. So, from this perspective, breaking up is a good thing for you. Of course, feeling deceived and aggrieved, angry, jealous, and regretful are all very normal reactions. It takes time to gradually resolve these feelings. Firstly, if you want to find relief by telling his wife, make sure you are not acting under emotional control. Don't do it impulsively, as it may actually affect your own physical and mental well-being. Secondly, every relationship is a mirror and every experience is meant to teach us something, to increase our wisdom and help us grow. Sometimes, we are willing to bless those who have hurt us, and be grateful for the growth and understanding they have brought us. These realizations will be precious assets in your life. There is a story about blessings, roughly meaning: A and B were friends, but A owed B a large sum of money and ran away, which was a significant amount for B. B had every reason to be angry and curse A, but he chose to bless him, wishing him success and prosperity. One day, A did indeed become successful again and found B to return the money. So, after venting your emotions, ask yourself, what have you learned in this over a year? Have you gained any understanding of the purpose the "universe" wants to teach you?!

question: Is it normal for a 16-year-old girl to frequently talk to herself when she is alone?
description: 16-year-old girl considers herself to be more introverted, appearing average among people, but outgoing among friends. She comes from a harmonious and intact family, and has not experienced any significant setbacks or psychological deficiencies in elementary and middle school. Her personality started to form in junior high school, and she began to have her own opinions and thoughts about things. During her alone time, she particularly enjoys talking to herself. Recently, she realized that she does it quite frequently. Talking to herself feels relaxed and pleasant, such as summarizing the day, reviewing study materials, or explaining things to herself while cooking noodles, for example. Friends and family think she is quite mature for her age, and she also believes so. As for the reasons why she does it, she thinks that speaking things out loud is more direct. Additionally, influenced by various vlogs and commentaries around fifth or sixth grade, she started talking to herself. After recently discovering this, she searched for some Q&A and used to think that it was just her way of being alone, perhaps similar to some other people. But it seems like that might not be the case, so does this form of solitude need to be changed? Is it normal? Are there others who are as "middle school-esque" as her? (doge)
keywords: Growth, improved personality, character traits, self-development.

answers.answer_text: Haha, what a coincidence! I'm also someone who is more introverted and tends to talk to myself. However, often times my self-talk is self-criticism. When I don't do something well, I would mutter to myself in a low voice, "Oh my, why did I do it like this? Can't you do better?" But there are also other situations, like when I draw a picture that I like, I would happily talk to myself, "Wow, I actually drew so well. I'm amazing." Hahaha. From the description of your question, I feel that you don't have a strong aversion to this trait of self-talk. Instead, you seem to derive a sense of contentment and enjoyment from it. I think that's great. This is a way for you to enjoy being alone and it doesn't have any impact on others. Therefore, you can openly allow yourself to have this way of being alone. And I find it quite cute. As long as it makes you feel comfortable and happy, whatever form it takes, no matter how unique or different it may be, we can allow its existence. This is a way of interacting with yourself that you have developed, it is not something forced upon you by the outside world or something others are pushing you to do. Therefore, you can fully accept and appreciate it. Because not everyone has such a method, and the fact that you can derive pleasure from it shows that it suits you. So, just embrace and appreciate it, and be proud of this unique trait of yours.

Hello, dear questioner, your question is very interesting. As I was reading it, I couldn't help but laugh. How can there be such an adorable child like you? Therefore, I would love to discuss it with you. First of all, you are a child with self-awareness and have a clear understanding of yourself. This is rare and also comes with some demanding aspects. For example, you consider yourself somewhat introverted, someone who appears average in a crowd but is very outgoing among friends. Do you know? This is a very rare quality and ability to have. In China, there is a saying, "A noble person is slow in speech but prompt in action" and "Exuding dignity, yet warm when approached." Truly cultured people are not usually flashy in a crowd. When I am with my friends, we engage in lively discussions, passionately exchanging words and opinions, guiding the world. However, in our daily lives, we are calm, introverted, and have a clear understanding. That is why we can achieve great things. Secondly, your family is complete and harmonious, and there haven't been any setbacks or psychological deficiencies in your nine years of primary and middle school. Your personality started to form in junior high, and you began developing your own thoughts and opinions. When you are alone, you particularly enjoy talking to yourself. Recently, you discovered that you have been talking to yourself quite frequently. This process of talking to yourself is relaxing and enjoyable, such as summarizing the day, reviewing study materials, or even commenting while cooking noodles. Your friends and family find you quite mature for your age, and you also feel that way about yourself. Look, this kind of self-talk is actually a reasonable emotional release. So why worry about it? Thirdly, you analyzed the reasons for your self-talk. You think that speaking out things directly is easier, and also, around the fifth or sixth grade, you were influenced by vlogs and various narrations, which made you start talking to yourself. You have already figured out the reasons, and throughout the whole process, you haven't had any painful emotional reactions. So why do you call yourself "weird"? Why force yourself to change? Enjoy life and the joy that talking to yourself brings you!

Abstract thinking in humans requires language as a medium, meaning that whenever a person is thinking, their mind will engage in self-talk. Some individuals speak aloud, while others simply think in their minds. As long as you are not shouting and disturbing others, I don't see any problem. Additionally, you may not be well-suited for confidential work... like being a spy or something.

question: My emotions fluctuate greatly. I was feeling fine just a moment ago, but suddenly I started feeling very depressed.
description: Nothing happened, but the mood suddenly became low, feeling annoyed, and would wonder why I am alive.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I don't know if you are currently in your adolescence. One of the main characteristics of adolescence is unstable emotions, so it is normal to feel down. I believe that all worries have reasons, big or small, but maybe you are not aware of them or don't know what is influencing you subconsciously. That's why you have been feeling unhappy. When we have daily troubles and unclear life goals, we start questioning why we are alive. In reality, the concept of why we are alive is something we give ourselves. Each person has their own definition of what it means to live or their own goals. Only you know where your meaning lies. If you are unsure, you can start by thinking about what kind of person you want to become in the future or what kind of work you would like to do. Gradually, you will find your own goals. And these goals will become the driving force in your life, so you won't feel that life is meaningless. Best wishes!

question: How do you deal with someone you don't like when you don't want to show your emotions?
description: While studying, for some unknown reason, I particularly disliked a person who always seemed to be in front of me. In the past, I didn't know how to handle it, so I would directly show a bad attitude. Looking back now, I realize that I didn't know how to control my emotions. Adults should not easily reveal their emotions. So, what should one do if they encounter someone they don't like now?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts, interpersonal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, I can see your worries. For this issue, I don't have an immediate solution that you can use and will be effective, because emotions are a very individual and personal experience. However, this problem reminds me of another issue: "What should you do when someone treats you to a meal and serves a dish you don't like?" I suppose the coping method would be to suggest changing the dish or simply not eating it, depending on how familiar you are with the person treating you. When it comes to encountering someone you don't like, who keeps appearing in front of you from time to time, it can indeed make you uncomfortable, and there's no way to avoid it. In that case, maybe you can take inspiration from the second approach I mentioned earlier - if you can't change the situation, just "turn a blind eye" to it. Although it may seem a bit "negative," at least it can help improve your mood.

question: How to learn to let go and not always dwell on the past, but live in the present?
description: Always regretting and lingering on past events, how can one learn to live in the present without regretting the past? How can one broaden their perspective and have a long-term vision, not always clinging to the past and the present moment, but instead becoming a magnanimous person?

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! Thank you for the invitation~1. Many people have a dream of "time travel", hoping to have a chance to "start over" in their own lives. People often regret and entangle themselves with things in the past, always thinking that if they had another chance, they would do better than before and the outcome would be different. As a result, they can't help but feel regret and self-blame. However, what we don't know is that any choice you made in the past was the best choice you could make based on your limited resources at that time, such as your level of knowledge, maturity, abilities, and state of mind. In that state, you did your best. Even if you could go back in time and start over, you would still make imperfect choices with the same limited resources. The reason you regret the past today is because the present you, in all aspects, is more mature and capable than the past you. 2. Holding onto the past and what is happening right now is because you haven't learned how to forgive and let go. I guess maybe when you were a child, you were also held onto by adults because of a minor mistake. It is because we haven't experienced forgiveness and tolerance that we cannot forgive and let go of ourselves and others. It's just that we often don't realize our own behavior and even can't trust ourselves, and all of this comes from the push of our subconscious. If you want to know how to change, you first need to know why, where the root of these behaviors lies. 3. Being entangled in and trapped by the past not only blocks the door to future happiness but also deprives you of the right to enjoy every moment of the present. The past is already gone, it has long disappeared in the river of time, and it no longer exists objectively. However, the unpleasantness of the past still lingers in our hearts, becoming an obstacle, a burden. Therefore, the first thing we need to do is to understand why we are like this, so that we can take targeted actions; secondly, based on what we know, we can heal. Perhaps it is necessary for you to go back to scenes from your childhood that you cannot forget, and heal that child, releasing the suppressed emotions such as grievances, sadness, anger, etc. Only when the emotions are processed can rationality return, forgiveness and tolerance can be discussed, and we can move forward better. If emotions are unresolved, rationality cannot emerge, let alone talk about change. If conditions permit, you can seek help from suitable professionals for psychological counseling. 4. A broad perspective and a generous attitude are developed through continuous growth, much like leveling up and fighting monsters, and facing pain is inevitable. If you want to help yourself, you can search for some self-help books on psychology. Books by Wu Zhihong, Cong Feicong, Yu Mengcheng, and other teachers are very good and may be helpful to you. You can also participate in some online or offline workshops to help yourself heal. Finally, I'm sending you an article related to your question, hope it can be helpful to you. Wish you all the best!

Hello, the author mentioned regretting past events and it reminded me of a psychological effect called the Zeigarnik effect. It is a memory effect that suggests that people remember unfinished tasks better than completed tasks. It is also known as the Zeigarnik effect or the "itch to finish." This effect suggests that people have a natural drive to complete tasks, and they tend to forget about completed tasks because the motivation to complete them has been satisfied. If a task is still unfinished, the same motivation will leave a deeper impression. If you find it difficult to let go and move on, it may be due to an "unfinished business" or an "unresolved issue" in psychology, which refers to the tendency to seek compensation for not completing something. You may have thoughts like "if only that thing hadn't happened" and other related thoughts such as "if only I had done this or that," believing that it would have prevented the situation from occurring. In order to explore whether you have an unresolved issue, it is necessary to examine your own feelings. Sometimes, when reality does not meet our expectations, we cannot accept what is happening and wish things had gone according to our plans. The first step is to acknowledge your emotions and address them in a rational manner. For instance, if a situation makes you feel anxious or fearful about not being able to complete it, try to soothe your own emotions. Secondly, try not to resist reality. What has happened has already happened, and accepting that you cannot change the past is crucial. Finally, ask yourself what you really want and what actions you can take to achieve it.

We always talk about living in the present moment. But in reality, most of us (including myself) either live in regrets and remorse over past experiences (depression), or in anxiety about unfulfilled events in the future (anxiety). This is probably a common issue for modern people. Each person has their own worries to a greater or lesser extent. And we are all continuous beings, which includes the past, present, and future. The experiences in the past shape who we are today, and within those experiences, there are many of our own emotional attachments. So, as you mentioned, letting go of the past and living in the present is a higher state of being. But how can we let go of the past? It's not as simple as just deciding to let go. The decision to let go is at the rational level, but the attachment is at the emotional level. When rationality and emotions clash, rationality often loses. [Two methods to achieve letting go] 1. Many Buddhist and Taoist practices focus on mindfulness, meditation, and other techniques to directly cultivate living in the present moment. (Don't laugh, I am serious.) It might take around 2 years of practice to see some progress. (Maybe even less time.) However, for modern people, with their restless thoughts, it's difficult to continue practicing. After just 5 minutes, their mind becomes restless and uneasy. But by persisting for a longer period, it benefits both physical and mental health with the goal of overcoming worries. The advantage is that you can do it yourself and it requires little cost. 2. For modern people, with such a fast pace of living, some might not be able to accept this method. In that case, there is another option which is psychological counseling, but it involves paying someone else. Psychological counseling is about addressing the issues of time and space. When we talk about letting go, truly letting go means reconnecting with the past on a deeper level, so we can pick it up before letting it go again. Therefore, the first step to letting go is actually picking it up. Otherwise, telling ourselves to let go at the rational level has little effect. I am using both of the above methods. They each have their own benefits. I hope this helps you.

It is a common psychological problem for us to often indulge in reminiscing about the past and regretting our past decisions. If we constantly dwell on past memories, it will hinder our progress and affect our everyday life and work. We need to look forward in order to not be stuck in the past and prevent ourselves from feeling depressed. I have also experienced being trapped in a whirlpool of regret due to certain decisions I made in the past. I suffered from insomnia for a whole year. However, I managed to overcome this by persisting with three small methods, and now I have become much more cheerful. First, I tell myself that the past has become history. If I keep replaying the scenes from the past, I will only become more emotional and turn into an emotional scavenger, constantly getting stuck and unable to free myself. Then, I engage in more social activities. If I have hobbies and interests, I find like-minded friends to discuss them with. This helps me open up and focus my attention on things I am interested in, so that I do not obsess over other issues. Finally, I engage in physical exercise and fitness activities, and read books that I had always wanted to read but never got the chance to. I strive to be a disciplined person. The most direct way to overcome negative emotions is through physical fitness, as it not only exercises our bodies but also uplifts our spirits. Reading is the simplest way to broaden our horizons.

Shakespeare said, "All that is past is prologue." Proust also wrote, "The life in memories is more real than the life happening at the present time and place." Humans are amphibious creatures, sinking both into the past and the present, living in the territories of now and then, carrying conscious and unconscious experiences with them. Before we become aware, we compulsively repeat the past, even living entirely in it. The past cannot be changed, and the feelings associated with it cannot be eliminated. To learn how to let go, perhaps we first need to know why we picked them up in the first place, sometimes with the help of others, we can safely remove the burdensome stones from our hearts. There is a popular saying on the internet: in the adult world, there is a lot of "let it go." However, whether it is openness or resignation, only oneself knows the warmth and coldness. It is impossible for a person to not think about the past, as it is what determines their future. The past is like ultraviolet light, revealing the hidden destiny text in the book of life that is not easily visible. It is a prophecy that provides footnotes for the entire book of life. Finding release does not necessarily mean abandoning something; it may also mean finally moving forward with them after sorting them out and lightening the load.

Hello, I always regret and dwell on past events. This is a normal human psychology because what we do cannot be perfect. We are human, not gods, so it is natural to dwell on regrets. However, it should be done in moderation. We should learn from past experiences and become more mature in dealing with things in the future, striving to minimize regrets as much as possible. How to live in the present when the pandemic is not over yet, especially now that humanity is experiencing the 11th round of Ebola virus? Some people say that in 2020 and every year thereafter, the greatest wish is to live well. As long as we are alive, there is hope and a future. Instead of clinging to the past, we should focus on living our present lives well. Set reasonable goals for ourselves, read books, do things we are interested in, and feel the effort and joy of living in the present moment. If we are in a satisfied state, we won't cling to the past. To become a magnanimous person, we need to be fearless of the future, not dwell on the past, and live in the present. I believe you can do it! Keep it up. Best wishes!

We are all first-time participants in life, and each person is exploring how to live a good life. Therefore, don't be too hard on yourself for past choices. Galway suggests forgetting the self at the mental level and instead using the self of the body and subconscious to relax and focus on doing something, so that one can live in the present. It is best if we have neither positive nor negative expectations of ourselves, neither praise nor criticism; the mind is only used to analyze and understand things, not to judge right from wrong. Therefore, let go of the judgment of yourself and the past, there is no right or wrong. May you find peace of mind. Heal yourself through psychology.

Hello, in response to your question, because I am not clear about the specific things you regret and dwell on in the past, my answer may not be comprehensive. Regarding the part where you mentioned living in the present, my response will only address a certain perspective or aspect of living in the present. I hope this limited content can be helpful to you. Constantly regretting and dwelling on past events, even though you rationalize and try to let go, you still feel attached to them emotionally. The reason why you can't let go is not because of how poorly you did at that time. It's because you are dissatisfied with the way things happened. Living in the present is difficult because in each present moment, we have many thoughts and motivations. But no matter which thought or motivation we attend to, there will always be an unresolved part that lingers within us. Living in the present is easy because in each present moment, we just need to be able to see that the choice we made, out of all our thoughts and motivations, is the best choice for ourselves at that moment. Perhaps in the future, when faced with the same situation, we may have a different choice, or maybe our thoughts and choices will change in the next moment. But at that specific moment, the choice we made was the one that our past self accepted. Often, the reason we can't let go is because our present self doesn't accept our self or the course of events at that moment in the past. The key is that our present self is not the same as our past self. Our past self deserves respect and that's what our present self needs to recognize.

Always regretting and entangling with past events, let the past be in the past, dust to dust, let them disappear in the dust of history. Some people like to collect pearls, some people like to collect farts. What is a pearl? Good and happy things are pearls. What is a fart? Regretful, painful things are farts. So, do you want to collect pearls or farts? How can we learn to live in the present, not regret the past, and have a broader perspective, a longer-term vision, not always clinging to the past and the present, and become a magnanimous person? Live each moment, each minute well in the present. People either do things or think things. If you think too much, you'll think of bad things, then comes the suffering, depression, entanglement, and these things happen. How can we stop all of this? Start with doing things. As you do things, you stop thinking. Doing is the most powerful force. As you do more things, experience more, your life experience becomes richer. A person with rich life experiences naturally has a larger perspective. This way, you can become a magnanimous person.

Dear OP: Hello! I believe that regretting the past is always "dissatisfaction with the present and anxiety about the future." Your inner subconscious actually hopes for a better future. So first, you need to ask yourself: What am I dissatisfied with now, is it relationships or career? What does my ideal life look like? If you can think about it carefully, I believe you can take the first step. This is also a very important step, which I call substitution: the past is gone, and all we can do is replace it with the future. As the saying goes: "If a person has no long-term plan, they will have immediate worries!" Proper anxiety is actually the driving force that promotes progress. But it must not be excessive. Once excessive anxiety leads to fear, even depression, it will affect mental and physical health. On the path of longing for the future and realizing dreams, we will definitely encounter many difficulties, which may also bring psychological troubles. But I want to tell you, "Life is wonderful because of its uncertainty." Embrace dreams and hope, long for a better future, and strive forward. That is the essence of life! Given the limited information you have provided, this is all I can say for now. Sincerely hope it can help you!

question: What psychological condition is it when someone lacks seriousness in their personality and has been assimilated?
description: No matter what I do, I have a carefree mindset, very "Buddhist-like." I don't know when I became like this... Looking back, I used to feel very serious, taking everything seriously. But progress was slow and inefficient that way, and most importantly, when everyone around me was being casual, I got assimilated. What kind of mentality is this... I want to change, but I don't know where to start. Please guide me...

answers.answer_text: Hugs to the OP. In social psychology, there is a term called "conformity," which means that when the people around us are engaged in a common pattern of behavior, we may be assimilated into the group under the pressure of invisible psychological factors. The OP may be influenced by this psychological factor. In addition, past negative experiences, such as feeling frustrated when working hard but not making ideal progress, can also contribute to the current distress. These multiple factors may be causing the current predicament for the OP. Actually, when the OP becomes aware of their current state and has a vague feeling about the underlying reasons, it already becomes an opportunity and trend towards positive change. The OP can relax a little. Regarding the situation of feeling inefficient when working seriously, the OP can try different methods and communicate with classmates and friends to learn from their suggestions. This might provide some inspiration for finding an efficient way that suits the OP. I hope my answer can help you. Keep going!

question: Did my best friend distance herself? Started to wonder if we have changed or if our hearts have grown apart.
description: The classmates I grew up with, the friends I fought together with as we grew up, we experienced so much laughter and joy together. You used to understand my joys and sorrows so well, I thought we would be good friends for life. But halfway through this journey of life, one by one, you all drifted away. Distance has made us strangers, to the point where our contact information sits in each other's phones, yet this number will never ring again. Only in dreams do I see us as we once were. Should I awaken to the realization that this is the norm in life, or lament that friendships and love have expired and turned sour? Perhaps my world is no longer a place for you to linger and wait.

answers.answer_text: Hi there! I can see that you're feeling distressed because your friends are growing apart from you. I sympathize with your situation. Based on your description of your "close friend becoming distant and friends not keeping in touch," it seems like you're confused and unsure about this change. Personally, I believe that both emotions and material things tend to change over time. Whether it's friendship or any other kind of relationship, they usually evolve based on our own needs. Thus, these changes are "relative" rather than complete. If you feel that you still have the time and experience to maintain your friendship, then you can take action now to preserve it. I understand your regret about growing apart from your friends, but one of the first things we learn in life is how to face goodbyes. We can cherish our precious memories, carefully store them, and carry them forward into the future. These beautiful experiences can empower us to face future challenges.

question: If someone has dreams every day, what should they do?
description: If someone dreams every day, what should be done?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, psychological counseling, behavioral abnormalities

answers.answer_text: Hello, the Jungian psychology understands dreams as a compensation of unconscious deviations from consciousness. Dreams have both compensatory and predictive effects. In most cases, if a person frequently dreams, it means that they may have significant psychological conflicts internally that cannot be expressed at the conscious level or realized in reality. They are compensated for through dreams at the unconscious level. On the other hand, dreams are also a healing process, repairing inner repression and conflicts. Through dreaming, healing occurs. Dreams are alive and the language of the unconscious. If you feel that there are a large number of dreams occurring during a certain period of time, it is worth noticing if there are any untransformed repression and conflicts within. You can seek a psychoanalyst to analyze your dreams. The scenes, characters, and symbols in dreams all represent the manifestation of your inner world and certain aspects or traits of your personality. Through dream analysis, you can understand the unconscious symbols, respect the unconscious itself, and achieve a balanced and developed relationship between consciousness and unconsciousness. Additionally, if there are always rich dreams, it also indicates that you have a very rich inner world and significant inner energy. Dreams are vivid, lively, and can bring creativity. Therefore, people who dream a lot have great creative potential. Dreams also have a predictive effect. Through dream analysis, dreams can be more than just imagination; they can be realized and dreams can come true.

Hello OP: I don't know what dreams are troubling you so much. Some people worry every day that they won't dream, while you worry about dreaming too much. Why do people dream? Research shows that about 1/3 of a person's life is spent in sleep, with 1/5 of that time spent dreaming. The saying "daytime thoughts lead to nighttime dreams" holds some truth. Dreams are ultimately brain activities. When the body is awake, it instinctively reacts to external stimuli. However, during sleep, not all organs are in a state of rest. Your brain does not stop functioning and continues to operate as it does during the day. Only the body's muscles are at rest, and experiences from the day are likely to appear in dreams. In general, some people dream at night due to stimuli they experienced during the day, while others dream because of excessive workload. This is the brain's way of regulating one's mental state and protecting the subconscious. It helps alleviate pressure and may act as a projection of one's inner thoughts, reminding them to complete certain tasks. Some great scientific discoveries were inspired by dreams. In 1825, British scientist Faraday discovered benzene, which is one of the main pillars of organic chemistry. One winter day in 1864, German scientist Kekulé dozed off in front of a fireplace. Atoms and molecules began to dance in his hallucination, with a carbon atom chain biting its own tail, spinning before his eyes. Startled, Kekulé realized that the benzene molecule forms a ring, the familiar hexagon now found in organic chemistry textbooks. I don't know what dreams you've had. They may be frightening or lovely, but the contrast between dreams and reality might be hard for you to handle. Perhaps you feel exhausted from dreaming. However, regardless of the situation, dreams still have a positive impact. If you avoid sleep out of fear, it will harm you even more.

Hello, friend! Actually, everyone dreams every day. Dreaming is a very normal psychological activity. I don't know what issue is troubling you, but if it's about dreaming, you don't need to worry. Modern scientists have discovered through sleep research that people's eyeballs are actually still during sleep, and rapid eye movement only occurs during shallow sleep. These two states alternate and change in a cyclical manner during sleep. When sleep enters the rapid eye movement (REM) stage, the sleeper is often dreaming. So far, most sleep laboratories report a dream recall rate of 90% to 95% after awakening from REM sleep. Therefore, REM sleep is also called dream sleep, while non-REM sleep is called dreamless sleep. Dream sleep and dreamless sleep together constitute the entire sleep process. Therefore, dreams rely entirely on the sleep process and are a special phenomenon that occurs during sleep. In people's lives, many people are greatly troubled by their dreams and always worry that their dreams will affect their physical health. From the perspective of psychoanalysis, dreams have the meaning of satisfying desires. Whether you are a noble person or a humble person, our minds contain too many desires that we are willing or able to express and desires that we are unwilling or unable to express. Among these endless desires, many cannot be immediately fulfilled or cannot be fulfilled in real life. Unfulfilled or impossible desires in real life can be satisfied psychologically in dreams, helping to regulate mental balance. Without dreams, the multitude of desires, big and small, would make it impossible for us to sleep peacefully. Even if we sometimes feel anxious and uneasy in our dreams, we can still dream and sleep soundly. Dreaming can also relieve fatigue and rejuvenate the body. Dreaming helps brain function. Dreaming can cause highly active chemical reactions within the brain, peak synthesis and renewal of protein in brain cells, while swiftly flowing blood brings oxygen and nutrients, and carries away waste, allowing brain cells that cannot normally renew themselves to quickly update their proteins. Actually, I am someone who dreams a lot. We are more likely to remember our dreams when we wake up from a light sleep state, while we cannot remember our dreams when we wake up from a deep sleep state, but that doesn't mean we didn't dream. Are you worried if your dreams are nightmares or something else? I hope my answer can be helpful to you. Your friend, Lan.

Poster, hello~~~ On the topic of dreaming, there have been many discussions even before the formal emergence of the field of psychology and the exploration of people's inner thoughts. Different theorists have different understandings of dreams, and due to the difficulty in studying dreams themselves, there is no completely correct and orthodox theory. Freud believed that dreams are the expression of content that is repressed and not acknowledged by one's consciousness, and they are formed after being disguised. On the other hand, some scholars believe that dreams are a way to release repressed emotions from the daytime. If you are interested, you can try searching online for books and theories on dream interpretation. Regardless of which theory is used to explain it, dreaming itself is not a bad thing. It may be due to an improper sleeping position, recent thoughts in your mind, or the pressures of study and life. Don't worry too much about it. I hope this helps you.

question: How can one determine the meaning of life and avoid wasting it when they have no major aspirations?
description: Feeling stressed when seeing accomplished individuals, but lacking significant aspirations oneself, can lead to feelings of disappointment and wasting one's life.

answers.answer_text: "What is success, what is wasting time. When we have such doubts, it indicates that we are seeking room for improvement. Everyone has different values ​​and orientations. We only see one side of other people's lives. Perhaps while we envy others' lives, others also envy our lives. Take a moment to ask yourself, what kind of life do you want, what kind of life do you want. What goals are you pursuing? Don't always just focus on other people's success, but focus more on your own progress. Define success in a more refined way, then you will often see your own small successes. Keep it up, worker."

question: 36-year-old woman, baby is eight months old, feels psychologically abnormal after giving birth to the child?
description: Because of lack of sleep, my mood is very bad and easily irritable. Whenever I hear my in-laws speak, I feel disgusted and I can't be bothered to listen to what they say. Especially when they gossip a lot, I feel even more repulsed. My in-laws are the type that talks a lot and talks randomly. Ever since they moved in, my husband and I have been arguing a lot and our relationship is not good anymore. It's not that my in-laws are bad, they do the grocery shopping and cooking, but I just feel like there's not enough personal space anymore. I have to speak to my husband secretly and after we had a child, we hardly have any private conversations. Now we barely speak at all, when we're taking care of the child, he doesn't want to talk and I don't want to talk either, we just silently watch. He plays with his phone and I take care of the child.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Through your narration, I have gathered a few key pieces of information: (1) Life stage: 36 years old (just gave birth to a son) (2) Major conflicts: between you and your spouse (reduced communication, decreased personal space), with your parents-in-law (encroachment on the personal space of you and your spouse) (3) Emotional manifestations: lack of sleep, easily irritable mood. Based on the issues you described, the possible causes might be: (1) Physical reasons: having just given birth to a child, you are in the postpartum period. At this stage, the hormonal levels in a woman's body experience a sharp decline, resulting in increased emotional fluctuations. Your body becomes fragile and exhausted due to childbirth, and your mental state can also become sensitive during this phase. Therefore, it is easy to experience emotional problems after giving birth. I recommend going to the hospital for a physical examination and consulting with a doctor about appropriate medication for professional postpartum recovery. (2) Psychological reasons: as mentioned above, your psychological state becomes sensitive and prone to emotional fluctuations due to the abrupt hormonal changes. Additionally, the lack of personal space and the inability to have intimate communication with your husband further diminish your sense of security and belonging. Subconsciously attributing this negative emotion to your parents-in-law can escalate family issues. I suggest communicating with your husband, explaining your situation to him, and letting him address the problem with your parents-in-law. If necessary, seek help from a therapist to alleviate your emotional problems. Make sure to pay attention to the issue to prevent it from developing into more severe psychological problems. This is my analysis and advice, I hope it helps you! Best wishes!

question: How to resolve the conflict in Oedipus Rex? Would feeling guilty if one surpasses their parents?
description: After graduating, I have been working in Shanghai. Due to the epidemic this year, my previous company dissolved, so I went back to my hometown to live with my parents. During this period, I have been feeling strange for no reason. For example, I feel awkward when I have to put on makeup and wear a nice dress for job interviews. When I see the way my mom looks at me when I come home, I feel embarrassed and weird. They are used to living frugally, so even when I buy snacks or ice cream, it feels strange. I feel like enjoying life a little is a kind of guilt, and at the same time, I feel that I don't deserve to live a good life or to have a good job. I came across a quote by Teacher Zeng Qifeng before: "Anything related to suppressing one's abilities may be related to the Oedipus complex." I feel like I am suppressing my own abilities, making myself live in hardship, because if I surpass my parents, there seems to be a particularly difficult to eliminate feeling of guilt, or you could say I am betraying them (it's hard to describe this feeling). I would like to ask the teachers for guidance on how to resolve this conflict. Would it be better for me to live alone away from my parents?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, you mentioned that once you are in front of your parents, you suppress your desires and abilities because they have had a difficult life. If you surpass them, you will have an indelible guilt. I have also had similar experiences and can understand the awkwardness and discomfort you mentioned. You also mentioned the "Oedipus conflict" theory discussed by Teacher Zeng Qifeng. This theory can explain your feelings to a certain extent, but there can be other explanations as well. Let me share my opinion for your reference. First, feeling awkward or ashamed in front of your parents when you are able to have things or a life better than theirs shows your "sympathy" or "empathy". It is true that our parents have lived a harder life than us, which is related to the era they grew up in. Your awareness of their hardships shows humility and understanding, and this emotion enables you to have more compassion and be more considerate towards them. Second, it is normal to feel a sense of unworthiness in front of our parents when we can enjoy the many good things in life. This is because we were indeed born in a peaceful era, and the foundation that our parents have worked hard for allows us to have a comfortable life. Perhaps when you were young, your parents had strict expectations of you, which made you feel that everything you have must come at a great cost. However, in reality, as long as it is not obtained through theft, it is reasonable for you to use money that you have earned to consume. Lastly, you mentioned if it would be better to live alone away from your parents. In my opinion, it can indeed improve your situation. You can reflect on whether you still have such emotions when you live alone. If not, it means it works. If you cannot leave your parents, when you are at home and realize that you have feelings of awkwardness or guilt, you can simply say "Thank you for your hard work" to them, or cook something delicious for them, or pour them a glass of water. You can give it a try and see if it helps you feel a little better. Best wishes, Sauce.

Indeed, children have a natural loyalty towards their parents, and if they live their lives differently from their parents, they may feel a sense of betrayal. Under the burden of this guilt, it will be difficult to transcend oneself. At this time, if one can leave their parents and live independently for a period of time, complete their own growth, and form a stable state of personality, then when they reconnect with their parents, they may be able to better assert themselves. If the questioner already feels that they don't fit in with their parents in many ways, then perhaps it's time to leave.

question: Feeling depressed! Feeling very down during the test! What should I do?
description: I have been feeling very depressed lately. I wish I could just leave, but I can't bear to do it. Everything seems annoying, and I can see through people and things very clearly. It all feels meaningless. I don't have a sense of accomplishment either. I can't find anyone to confide in, as nobody seems reliable.
keywords: Treatment, psychological counseling, sharing and listening.

answers.answer_text: Relationships are an important issue and channel for us. The flow of emotions plays a very important role in our stability and sense of security. If you feel unreliable and can't find someone to confide in, you can find a professional psychologist. Through 1-2 sessions of interviews, you can see if you and the counselor are a good match, and then decide whether to open up more. Trust that a professional psychologist can make you feel a "safe and protected" space. Hope this helps. Best wishes.

question: 30-year-old male, I get angry whenever someone's behavior doesn't meet my expectations.
description: My wife goes to the supermarket to buy things while I wait. If she takes longer than my psychological time, I get angry. I hold onto things that are difficult to hold, and my wife walks ahead of me (she also has things in her hands, but they are easier to hold). She doesn't put the things on the chair by the door in advance and open the door for me to put them down. In an instant, I explode. I have set standards for everything in my mind, and I get angry whenever something doesn't meet these standards or doesn't happen as I expected, no matter who it is. I have looked it up online, and this indicates a younger psychological age (even though I am already 30), excessive self-centeredness, and a need for control that is not being fulfilled. The solution is to find the underlying reasons behind the anger and communicate my feelings with others. I need to have empathy and try to think from others' perspectives. I am willing to try these methods, but there are two things I feel I cannot overcome. 1. I get angry immediately whenever I encounter a similar situation, almost instinctively. I cannot control it at all. 2. When I am treated unfairly (like in the situation above, when I am holding things that are difficult to hold and about to drop them, and if someone fails to notice or help, I get angry), I usually end up having a big argument. I just don't want to say anything. The reasons why I want to change are: 1. I don't want my wife and children to be affected. 2. It can affect my interactions with others in all aspects. 3. My inner emotions are constantly affected.
keywords: Growth, character development, personality traits, self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello friend, thank you very much for your response. After reading your reply, I felt a pang of sourness in my heart. It is really hard to imagine how you managed to overcome the deep trauma in your original family. Moreover, despite the profound trauma in your original family, you are still able to say that "I should be considered middle-class through hard work, my wife and I make a combined income of nearly one million RMB per year, my wife is virtuous and kind, and we had a child last year, our small family is happy." This fully demonstrates how strong your vitality is! Because there are many visitors with similar experiences to your upbringing, and they often cannot achieve the same level of career success as you. Just based on this point, I want to give you a thumbs up and applause. The summary of your reply can be as follows: 1. The experience of being a "left-behind child" during childhood led to a serious lack of "parental love" for you! Coupled with the fact that "your family was poor when you were young, and you were looked down upon by others," you also couldn't feel much "love" from those around you! This has resulted in your deep inner "emotional box" being in a prolonged state of "emptiness" without filling it with "love"! In the long-term absence of love, you are prone to various "irrational" behaviors! Your current "desire for control" is one such result! 2. The relationship between your parents is not good, and it often exists in a "war mode"! Among them, your father often suspects your mother of "having an affair"; your mother likes to "scold" your father... Being in such an environment for a long time, you unknowingly succumbed to the "poison" of this family atmosphere! Moreover, you have unconsciously "copied" this relationship pattern between your parents into your current family relationships and daily interpersonal relationships! In Freud's words, this is called "compulsive repetition"! 3.
