It seems that your mother wants you to have a job that can provide a stable and easy life, while you want a job that offers freedom in terms of time and a good working atmosphere. I guess your mother wants a job that is stable and does not require much effort. On the other hand, her own work or life might make her feel exhausted and stressed. To put it in trendy terms, she wants to "lie down and win." She doesn't have the ability to live such a life herself, but as her imagined father figure, she hopes you can fulfill this dream for her. If you don't comply, it would mean her dream would be shattered. Of course, you are not obligated to fulfill her dreams. The biggest role of a mother for her child is to be an emotional container. Your mother wants you to understand and accept her viewpoint, just like she does. The more she needs these emotions, the more she lacks them. Finally, it's about herself. It's clear that your mom tends to nag and negate your opinions, and deep down, she knows very well how you would feel when she treats you this way. The emotions between you and her are mutually responsive. That's human nature. Furthermore, you see each other as father and mother figures in your own shoes. As someone who has worked in the public security system for five years, I can say that having free time is indeed difficult, but I honestly don't feel the strict hierarchy you mentioned. What I want to say is this: firstly, there are superiors and subordinates in any place, or in other words, there are rules everywhere. Secondly, the world is what you think it is. You believe that lawyers are great, free, and have simple social interactions, but let me tell you, being a lawyer is also extremely tiring and demanding, and working overtime is common. Social interactions are not easy either, as wherever there are people, there will be intrigue. Watch fewer TV dramas; they are all made for your entertainment. In other words, a lawyer, to you, is like an utopia that only exists in fantasies, not in reality. Of course, you can choose your job according to your own preferences, but I just suggest that you get a real understanding of this profession and be mentally prepared. After all, ideals are full, but reality is harsh. Lastly, I and this world love you, mwah!

If your mother has a low level of education, you can simply say, "Your profession doesn't match, you can't apply, there are no spots available," and be done with it. If your mother is educated, it becomes more difficult. The best solution is to marry an open-minded husband and have an open-minded mother-in-law. Then, choose a job with a lot of free time and move away from home.

question: At 14 years old, in the past year, I have been thinking that my mom has paranoid delusions.
description: My mother often curses people on her QQ and even curses people in WeChat groups where all relatives and friends are present. She even says that our neighbors and many people on the upper floor want to harm her. I have argued with her many times, but no matter what I say, it's useless. She even curses mental health doctors.
keywords: Treatment, psychological counseling, mental disorders, expression and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I see that your mother has these inappropriate thoughts and is not aware of them. You feel very worried in your heart and hope that your mother will immediately understand her mistakes. I can sense your concern for your mother, but can you try not to argue with her in the future? The more you argue and negate her thoughts, the more it will provoke her resistance and feeling of being misunderstood, which will deepen her erroneous beliefs. Have you tried communicating with your father? Try to communicate with your mother together in a gentle and friendly manner to help her alleviate the tension and pressure in her mind, and then persuade her to seek timely medical treatment. Whether it is paranoid delusion requires diagnosis by a psychiatrist from a tertiary psychiatric hospital. Medication may be needed for treatment. These are just my suggestions, I hope they can help you. Best wishes!

question: 17-year-old girl, feeling very depressed in class, how to adjust her mindset?
description: I'm not good at speaking and I'm afraid of being criticized by others. Moreover, I have noticed that people tend to be happier in their replies if the other person is happy when talking. However, if the person I am chatting with is not happy, the replies also tend to be not very happy. But, I generally have a bad mood in class. How can I get along with others happily?
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, communication, roommate, classmates.

answers.answer_text: Hello, emotions can be contagious. The phenomenon you observed, where if one person is happy, the other person will also be happy, might be the transmission of emotions. During conversation, the speaker can transfer their emotional state to the listener and influence them. However, when interacting with others, it's not limited to only having happy conversations. I believe it's wonderful to be able to honestly share your worries and concerns with someone, even if they are not happy things. Can you try finding someone you trust and honestly express your worries and feelings? Perhaps others can understand your feelings and provide encouragement and help. Your worries are just subjective assumptions and not facts. No one is naturally good at speaking, it can be learned. You can learn some interpersonal communication and conversation skills. What's more important is to apply what you've learned and have the courage to try and practice. With more learning and practice, your speaking abilities and communication skills will continue to improve. Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-)

question: Lying in bed, there is a particularly chaotic jumble of images in my head, with an amplified sense of racing sounds.
description: What's going on? This is the second time it has happened. It only occurs when I am lying in bed with nothing to do. The images in my mind are unusually chaotic and appear in waves.

answers.answer_text: Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand that the poster feels that they have random images appearing in their mind when lying in bed. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help the poster: (1) The poster mentioned that this is the second time these images have appeared in their mind. I wonder if the poster has noticed what these random images resemble and how they feel about it. Try describing these images and recording your own feelings. You can do some simple analysis on your own in your daily life. (2) Of course, the poster can also try to tell a counselor about these feelings, describing them more specifically. Perhaps they can help you better. #The world and I love you.

question: I'm afraid of thunder myself, how should I communicate with my mom about it?
description: I am afraid of thunder and lightning, and I want to tell my mom, but my mom says, "What is there to be afraid of? What's so scary?" But I am really scared, how should I talk to my mom about it?
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, guilt, shame, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: I saw your question about "how to communicate with your mom." I think you don't want to just tell your mom "I'm afraid of thunderstorms," but you hope to get some kind of response from her after sharing your feelings. You said, "But my mom says what is there to be afraid of, why be scared." I feel that when you tell your mom "I get very scared when there's thunder," your feelings are invalidated by her response. It's as if her response is saying "There's no need to be afraid of thunder; there's nothing to be scared of." This can make you feel like you're offering something to your mom (your feelings) and hoping she can receive it and discuss it with you (communicate). However, your mom says, "There's nothing there (nothing to be afraid of), nothing to discuss." It's as if in your mom's eyes, your fear shouldn't exist, let alone be discussed. I think perhaps this is why you feel like you can't communicate with your mom. I don't know how you feel about this. As for how to communicate with your mom, it may also depend on your mom's state and trying to communicate with her in a way she can easily understand. Your mom thinks there's no need to be scared of thunder, but you can still insist that thunder scares you. Maybe you can say something like this: "Mom, for you, thunder is nothing to be afraid of, it's not a big deal. But for me, thunder makes me feel very scared. I don't know if talking about it this way will make it easier for my mom to hear my feelings and start communicating with me, but if you're willing, maybe you can try and see if there's any change."

What do you actually want your mom to respond to? When your mom says "don't be afraid," it means "child, there's really nothing to be afraid of when there's thunder and lightning." So, I'm curious, what else do you want to say to your mom? Do you want to tell her why you're afraid? Why are you afraid? It might be the stimulation of the sound and light that makes our heart rate speed up, which is anxiety. We might think that's fear. It could also be the negative impressions left in our subconscious by TV dramas. Who knows? To overcome fear, you can close the curtains, wear headphones to watch your favorite shows, listen to your favorite music, or meditate to calm down and fall asleep. After a period of time, when thunder and lightning no longer make you anxious, the information you receive will change, and you'll realize that thunder and lightning are nothing to be afraid of.

Hello, when I saw your question, I couldn't help but laugh because I am also afraid of thunder. I've been afraid since I was little, and even now, in my fifties, I'm still scared. I guess there are more than just the two of us who are scared of thunder. I'm curious, why can't you tell your mother that you're afraid of thunder? Are you worried about something? Are there some things in your life that you can't talk to your mother about? If so, what kind of things are they? What kind of impact would it have on you if you do or don't talk about these things? I guess deep down inside, you may have a hope that after you tell your mother about your fear of thunder, she won't need to explain or say much, just respond with "thunder is indeed scary." Am I right? I apologize for responding to your question with more questions. I don't know if this series of questions will help you find the answer to your problem. Take care of yourself.

description: I really want to go home but I dare not take leave. I feel so conflicted. I have realized that my whole life is like this, full of uncertainty.

question: There is a sister who likes to criticize me, how to deal with the disgust of having such a sister?
description: My older sister is a very sarcastic person. She always likes to criticize and belittle me in every aspect, to show that she is superior and more excellent than me. In the past, she said that I would be disliked by others when I got married. Now that I am married, she still tells my husband that I am messy and have body odor. She even says that we have the same mother, but she doesn't have these problems. I really dislike having such a sister who always compares me unfavorably in every aspect, likes to elevate herself, and keeps pointing out my flaws in a condescending manner. I really want to completely cut ties with her and never have any contact with her until the end of our lives.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, family control

answers.answer_text: Hi, I can sense your frustration. Your sister's behavior and words have been affecting your mood negatively. However, because she is your sister, you are unsure of how to express your discontent appropriately. My best friend also has a similar issue with her childhood friend. He constantly says things that make her unhappy, thinking that he knows her well just because they are childhood friends. He often criticizes her behavior. Although my friend is very angry, she doesn't want to ruin their relationship and thus has chosen to make her boundaries and thoughts clear to her childhood friend. When facing words and actions that make her uncomfortable, she will tell him directly, hoping that it won't happen again. At the same time, she also finds an appropriate time to privately communicate with her childhood friend, asking why he says those things and does those actions, trying to understand his thoughts and attitudes. This approach can help her make better decisions on how to resolve the issue. I don't know if your sister is generally "sarcastic" with everyone, but if her personality is like that, I think as her younger sister, you still need to point out this problem to her. After all, it makes everyone around her feel unpleasant. However, before addressing this issue, it's important to control your emotions and not let negative feelings escalate. You can also talk to your parents, as communication among family members might be more effective. On the other hand, regarding the impact on you, be careful not to let your sister's words affect your judgment. Next time you face such a situation, you can try to distance yourself from the environment where you spend time with your sister. When she says things that are untrue, you can try to back up your statements with facts to make her "shut up." Although family members are closer, there are still boundaries that need to be respected. You don't have to keep giving in, and I hope you won't have to ruin your relationship. I hope you can find a suitable way to resolve the issue.

I'm sorry to hear that you have such a sister. Let me tell you a secret, your sister belittles you to elevate herself, but it's actually because she is jealous and lacks confidence. You can observe this. For example, at home, she may say that you have a body odor, but see if your parents pay more attention to you and treat you better (even if it may not be true, in your sister's eyes, she might feel that your parents care more about you and see herself as unwelcome). Once you truly understand your sister's internal thoughts, I believe you won't be too bothered by her words, but instead, you may feel sympathetic towards her. Additionally, when she says these things, you can respond to her by saying, "Yes, you're right, that's exactly how I am," or "I am just a different sister from you, but isn't it normal for people to be different?" Slowly try not to respond emotionally, and she will find it uninteresting and stop saying it.

There is such a troublesome older sister, and it is difficult to completely avoid dealing with her. However, there are some response techniques that may be helpful for you: ① You don't need to justify or try to prove that you are not what your sister says you are. Also, try not to show that you are very angry. The more obvious your reaction, the more she will feel "successful." ② When she talks about you, face her with seriousness and coldness, and say firmly, "Sister, I don't like this kind of joke." After saying it, continue to face her with a serious expression, making the atmosphere awkward. ③ Alternatively, you can face her with seriousness and coldness, and go along with what your sister says. For example, if she says you are messy and smelly, you can say with a serious expression, "Yes, I am just a dirty commoner, unlike my sister who is a fragrant fairy. Even if I don't take a shower for 10 years, I still smell great." ④ If you do as mentioned above, your sister will find herself in an awkward situation and may say that you are "petty and can't take a joke." Don't back down or be afraid of being called that, and don't be afraid of the awkwardness because she is the one feeling awkward. You can simply respond, "Yes, sister, I am petty and can't take a joke, so please don't make jokes like this with me in the future." (Attach a smiling face.jpg) Let your sister know your boundaries and feel that there are limits with you, so she won't dare to easily offend you anymore.

question: I am in my third year of graduate school, and she is in her second year. I am feeling very upset because I have been rejected by a girl I was pursuing. What should I do?
description: I posted a personal ad on a WeChat official account, and she added me. She knew my basic information (including income, education, family conditions, personality, hobbies, and photos). I'm currently in my third year of graduate school, and she's in her second year. She said she found me attractive and that people in the scientific research field are pure, so she reached out to me. Since school hasn't started yet, I went to her hometown to visit her for two days a few days ago. The first day was fine, she shared trivial matters in her life (parents, relatives, friends), future career plans, attitude towards marriage, and there was some physical contact. But for some reason, she changed on the second day. She kept looking down at her phone, avoided eye contact with me, and rushed to go home, saying she didn't have time to spend with me. I felt uncomfortable, so when I came back, I questioned whether she couldn't forget her ex-girlfriend or if there was something wrong with me, and accused her of neglecting me. She said I could be a good senior or friend, but she felt something was off, and said maybe it's her own problem, and suggested focusing on graduating and finding a job first. I don't know what to do now. One detail is that on the second day, when we talked about her ex-boyfriend, I suddenly started to cry...
keywords: Love, attachment, sense of security, fondness

answers.answer_text: Hello, author, sending you a warm hug (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) you have been rejected by a girl and feel very sad about it, (2) you want to know what to do next. Here's my analysis and advice, hoping to help you: (1) First, it can be seen that the girl actually has feelings for you, otherwise she wouldn't chat so openly with you and even meet up with you. So don't feel like it's your fault and don't feel defeated. (2) Secondly, why did the girl avoid you the next day and even cry when talking about her ex-boyfriend? It's probably because she still can't forget her ex and may still love him. You may have some similar qualities to her ex, so some of your actions may have triggered her memories. She chose to give up and not continue with you because she doesn't want to repeat the same mistakes or evoke memories. (3) Finally, since you can still be friends now, you can be friends for a while. If you really like her, you can take it slow. Give her some time, maybe she needs time to realize that you are not her ex. #The world and I love you, take care~.

question: Parents being too accomplished can lead to children feeling inadequate, what should be done?
description: My parents are college graduates, but my grades are mediocre. I often don't do things as well as my parents do, and I get criticized for being so stupid when I make even the slightest mistake. I have also tried to catch up with my parents and become an equally outstanding person, but I have to admit that I am really not that smart. I always feel inferior when I am with my parents, like I am embarrassing them. Am I unworthy of being their child?
keywords: Family, parental communication, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: High intelligence may be the most shining aspect of your parents? However, you have come to this family not to inherit it. The parents (genes) provide the child with a library, and the child only needs to select a portion of the materials from this library to build what they need. Sometimes, they may not choose the most "valuable" parts in the library. The reason why "value" needs to be in quotation marks is because value is a judgment, and judgments have standards that can change. For example, suppose the parents of the author are both university graduates but have average physical attributes (this is a assumption). If the author combines a less intelligent but robust physique from the library provided by their parents, it may seem like a "decline" in an era where intelligence is widely used, but in an era where physical strength determines the quality of life, it could be considered as "evolution". The author's parents "are often criticized for being stupid" and seem to be unaware that the child is not their private possession, but rather an obligation they owe to the world. They should provide an environment suitable for the characteristics of this individual that came from them, which shows they may be intelligent, but not necessarily wise? The author does not need to take their parents' evaluations as definitive. If a family is like a plant, then the child is like the seed of this plant. Strictly speaking, the seed is not part of the plant. In order to fulfill itself, it must leave the mother plant, go to a new land, and grow into a new plant on its own.

#You are already their child, there is no question of whether you deserve it or not. The only question is how to communicate and get along with them. #Often, there are many things that you don't do as well as your parents, and even a slight mistake will be criticized for being so dumb. #People are inherently different, and your learning ability is closely related to your family environment. When you say this sentence, you assume that your parents know how to educate children and then draw this conclusion. But many parents themselves have graduated from prestigious schools, but it does not mean that they know how to educate their children in the current environment; now the methods of educating children are much more complex than before, requiring not only time, but also methods, an understanding of the different needs of children at different stages, and an understanding of the domestic education system, assisting children in analyzing the educational environment, and choosing the most suitable plan. Just sending them to prestigious schools is not enough. #I have also tried to catch up with my parents and become an outstanding person like them. #The current environment is completely different from the environment they were in, and the opportunities are also different, so it's not comparable. The same opportunities you have now are harder to obtain than the opportunities your parents had at that time, and they also require advance planning. #I always feel inferior when I'm with my parents, and I feel embarrassed in front of them. #If you are comparing yourself to your parents, ignoring the objective environment, this kind of comparison is one-dimensional and cannot explain anything. Are you ignoring the objective fact that they may not know how to educate their children? Moreover, regardless, they definitely haven't given up on you, they just don't know how to communicate with you, don't know what to do. That's why you have such feelings. Have you ever tried telling them how you feel? If you need help, you can private message me.

If highly educated parents (for now let's assume they are your parents) were to have children, they would definitely be better or stable at the same level as their parents. But the society we live in now is not like that (perhaps it has long ceased to exist). This thought is a hypothetical assumption with a sense of entitlement. I wonder if this can be comforting to you? Maybe it can, and you can sigh with relief. You have the right not to be like them. Furthermore, you can have a life without comparison, especially with your parents who grew up in a completely different era. Maybe it can't, and you think to yourself, "I really can't make it." Because deep down, you have expectations for yourself that are different from the present. I hope that your expectations for yourself come from you, not as someone's child. By the way, if my child were to think, "I don't deserve to be my parents' child", I might feel that it is I who don't deserve to be their parent.

question: At the age of 20, I have wasted my life due to laziness. What should I do next?
description: From a young age, I have been lazy, lazy to think and dislike reading. I had poor grades in middle school, which led to low self-esteem and social anxiety. However, I am afraid and incapable of taking action to change. Now, I feel useless both physically and in character. I am unable to express myself clearly. The autumn recruitment for senior year has already started, but I am not prepared for anything, and I am feeling anxious. What's even more important is that I don't know what kind of life and job I want. I have no hobbies and no opinions on many things. I don't even know who I am. Gradually, I have become numb. I chose a major in college casually, which has led to the possibility of unemployment after graduation. I feel like I have no expectations in my life anymore. I have never been in a relationship, and I don't want to establish any connection with anyone. I don't know how to love others, and I don't know how to love myself. At 20 years old, it seems like there is a promising future ahead, but at the same time, it feels like I can see the end at a glance. I don't know how to navigate my future life. It's exhausting.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Seeing the question asked by the OP, it felt like I was looking at myself from last year. During campus recruitment, I felt unprepared and was unsure about what I wanted for the future, feeling very lost. The OP has three questions: 1. Uncertain about what they want, lacking life goals and hobbies. 2. Feeling worthless and fearful of campus recruitment. 3. Not knowing how to love themselves. Not knowing what they want can be discovered through trying new things. Our lives and goals are not just magically conjured while sitting alone in a room. They are found through constant exploration, reading various books, talking to different people, and doing various things. Some people may find their goals quickly and have a clear direction from a young age. Others may find it later in life. So don't feel distressed by not having something specific to do at the moment. Goals can be gradually found, and hobbies can be developed over time. For now, we need to find a job that can support ourselves and continue learning and gaining experience along the way, slowly adjusting our lives. Of course, we can also choose to pursue further education. There are many paths for us to take. Feeling worthless, in fact, each of us has our own characteristics and things we are good at. I believe there are no worthless people in the world, it's just that we haven't discovered our strengths yet. How can we discover our strengths? We can seek help from people around us and ask them what kind of person they think we are. Sometimes, we can't see our own strengths, but others might notice them. Recall some past achievements that gave us a sense of accomplishment and think about what we did at that time and what abilities we demonstrated. Don't say that there are no such things, there definitely are, we just have hidden them too deeply. The fear of campus recruitment is actually my personal feeling, it could also be my personal projection. Because that's how I felt back then. I felt that I had no competitiveness, no company would hire me, and I was afraid of rejection, so I didn't even want to submit my resume. However, we can change our perspective. Employment is a mutual decision, if we are rejected, it's because we currently can't meet their requirements. So, it's also an opportunity for us to evaluate what we are lacking and gradually improve ourselves. Do you remember my advice for the first question? Try more things. Only by trying more, can we better understand the world, broaden our thinking, and broaden our horizons, gradually growing in the process. Don't be afraid, we still have time to prepare. Research the company, understand the skills required by the position, look for recruitment experiences, and keep networking. We will find a job. Regarding how to love oneself, I'm sorry, I can't answer that because I haven't learned to love myself yet either. But I am in the process of gradually accepting myself. I think to love oneself, we must first accept ourselves. Only by accepting ourselves can we truly understand what we want and avoid forcing ourselves. Finally, I want to give the OP a hug and hope they can feel some warmth. I also want to thank the OP, as it reminded me of the past and allowed me to provide some answers for myself.

OP, it's not too late to make efforts now. Maybe you don't have a direction at the moment, maybe you feel that your abilities are not enough, and you may even find life difficult. But as long as you are willing to work hard, everything is possible. Perhaps for now, you can first find a job that you are relatively interested in, give it a try, learn and develop in-depth. You may gradually find yourself liking this job more and more; but if later on you don't really like this job, it's okay too. Maybe you can pay attention to opportunities in life, and try to seize them. Opportunities are everywhere in life, as long as you are willing to work hard and be attentive, you will definitely be able to seize an opportunity that belongs to you. In life, you may also need to communicate more with others, talk to your parents at home, actively chat with classmates at school, and invite classmates to participate in activities together, etc. I hope you can believe in yourself, it's not too late now, as long as you are willing to focus and not sink into despair, there is still a long time ahead for you to explore. Keep going! Best wishes!

question: How to deal with the problem of being unable to control a masturbation addiction and not being able to change it even if there are physical problems?
description: "I am addicted to watching pornography and masturbating. Every time I masturbate multiple times in a row. I have already developed erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation, but I still can't control myself from watching porn and masturbating. I have experienced many physical symptoms, including kidney deficiency. But I just can't quit. What should I do?"

answers.answer_text: Sending you a big hug. Engaging in moderate physical activity can help release energy and promote a healthier and happier lifestyle. It is best to avoid watching adult content, as it often promotes incorrect values and unhealthy sexual behavior, which can have a negative impact on one's personality. Hope this advice helps you overcome some minor troubles. Wishing you a joyful life.

question: Why is it necessary to have a good mental preparation from the beginning in doing things?
description: Why is it important to have the right mental preparation from the beginning? It feels like if we don't start off well, it will be difficult to make adjustments later and we may easily get stuck.
keywords: Growth, personality traits, developmental patterns, work, and learning.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm trying to provide some references from the perspective of the knowledge I have learned. From the topic and description you provided, I can see that you are actually asking about the issues related to security and positioning. This can be explained from the perspective of human evolution. Primitive humans lived by hunting in the forests, and in the vast sea of ​​forests, they needed to make preparations for positioning in order to hunt accurately. At the same time, having a clear position in mind can also protect oneself and be prepared to fight or flee when encountering fierce animals. Over the years, this part of the gene has been passed down from generation to generation in human development. That's why I said the problem you described is about positioning and security. In addition, our modern human brain has evolved. Apart from needing a sense of security and positioning at the beginning to do things more steadily, we also have the advanced abilities of thinking, judgment, and learning in our brains. At the same time, we also have the ability to be flexible and adapt. So, is it true that "if things are not done well from the beginning, it will be difficult to adjust properly later and easy to stagnate", as you mentioned? Is everything like this? Then we would often be trapped. Because no matter how meticulous the plan is, it can never keep up with changes. The only thing that remains unchanged in this world is "change". Therefore, when dealing with things, we should focus on the results, persist when it is effective, change when it is ineffective, and persist while being flexible and flexible while being persistent.

question: Should I consider the issue of salary when helping my boyfriend's father with his company?
description: It has been five years with him, but we haven't gotten engaged. His business failed, so he and his father started working at a construction site, and I joined them too to help out. It's been about two months now, but we don't have any income. I help out with some administrative tasks at his father's company, and his father always assigns them to him, even though he knows that I'm the one doing them. I feel like I'm being taken advantage of, and it's been two months and I haven't earned a penny, but he treats me well. Occasionally, he takes me out to eat or buy shoes. But I don't have the freedom to spend money, and I hesitate whenever I want to buy something. Even though we have some savings, I still feel anxious deep down. Despite many people saying that I'm just helping out his father with our own business, why do I feel like I'm begging to do these things on my own? This feeling of being down and helpless, with no income, is really uncomfortable. I'm thinking about going back to my mom's and finding a job there... maybe things will be better.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP, sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ Based on your description, I understand that: (1) You help your boyfriend's father's company but do not receive any salary. (2) You feel very upset and are hesitant about whether to return to your mother to work. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: (1) First of all, it is important for you to receive a salary when working for any company. Since you and your boyfriend are not yet married and are only boyfriend and girlfriend, you have a coworker relationship within the company. Therefore, if you help with these tasks, you should receive compensation consciously. Even if not, your boyfriend should think of taking you out to eat or buy clothes, as this is a normal thing. (2) Secondly, you are already feeling sad and aggrieved in this situation, which clearly shows that you are uncomfortable in this kind of relationship. We should never compromise ourselves in any relationship, don't you think so? So, if you put in labor, it is important to stand up for your rights. Of course, since the other person is your boyfriend, you can express your thoughts in a way that belongs to both of you, let him know, and see his reaction. (3) Finally, since you are helping both elderly parents, I suggest you consider going back to help your mother. This way, not only will you receive a salary, but you will also feel happy. Of course, this may mean being in a long-distance relationship with your boyfriend, but you can discuss and find a solution together. Communication can solve 80% of problems, so don't be stuck and upset by yourself! #The world loves you and I love you, wishing you all the best~.

I don't know much about this, but I have a few questions. First, did his dad start paying your boyfriend a salary? And why is his dad assigning tasks to your boyfriend instead of directly to you? Are you really sure his dad knows that you are the one doing all the work? Are you helping your boyfriend or your father-in-law? Lastly, does he know about your financial situation? If it were me, I wouldn't do this kind of work for free because I have to support myself. If you are financially well-off, maybe he didn't think about it, and you can bring up the point that your concern is not about the salary, but the inequality. It feels like you have to rely on each other unequally, and you are not engaged, so there is no sense of security. I have only heard of fiancées helping their father-in-law's company, not boyfriends helping each other. It's possible that his dad wanted to train him, and then you stepped in. Do you not have your own goals or plans for your career? The above is only my personal opinion and is for reference only.

question: A 21-year-old woman in her junior year is about to start an internship. How can she change her straightforward personality?
description: I am a 21-year-old female, a senior in college, and about to start an internship. I am a sensitive person who is not afraid to express my emotions, especially towards people I like. I show my admiration for them clearly. However, the same goes for people I don't like - my dislike is evident, and this kind of personality often leads me to offend others easily. Many people advise me to change my character because it can create many problems in social and work environments. They say it is not suitable for surviving in society. So, how can I hide my emotions towards others?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, empathy, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. First, sending you a warm hug. I'm a female student in my third year and will soon start my internship. How can I change my straightforward personality? I am sensitive, expressive with my emotions, and when I like someone, I openly express my appreciation for them. Conversely, when I dislike someone, it's evident. How can I hide my emotions from others? Being straightforward can easily offend people in everyday life. Why? In fact, try putting yourself in someone else's shoes. If someone directly points out your flaws and shortcomings, you would definitely feel embarrassed or even upset because nobody likes to hear negative comments. Everyone prefers to hear words of praise. Thinking from another person's perspective makes it easier to understand. I used to believe that if I like or dislike someone, I should express it directly without hiding anything. However, later I realized that this approach could hurt others. Another reason is not wanting to see others' fake side and wanting to point it out directly. This can also easily offend people. It's better to keep a mental note of others' true nature without having to say it out loud. Speaking out may only be detrimental to oneself. If you still want to be straightforward or struggle to hide your emotions, you can try counting down from 10 to calm yourself down. Think about the consequences of your words and then decide whether or not to say them. I hope this helps you and wish you a great day, OP.

If possible, start by making small changes and gradually progress. For example, try not to express your opinions about people you don't like or reduce the aggression in your language. If that's not enough, focus on playing to your strengths and avoiding your weaknesses. Find a job that suits your personality and try to stay within your own circle at work, avoiding people you dislike.

question: Yes, it's all my fault. Will the world be better off if I die?
description: Yes, yes, yes, it's my fault, it's all my fault. If I die, the world would be better.

answers.answer_text: Give the OP a hug! I can feel the OP's inner repression of emotions and despair. I'm curious about what led the OP to have such cognitive thinking and thoughts. What makes the OP believe that their "destructive power" is so great that one person can "destroy" the peace and tranquility of the entire world, making the world so "bad" that only when the OP dies will it become "good" again? The OP says it's all their fault, so what mistakes has the OP made? If it's something terribly wrong, at the very least, they should face legal repercussions and take responsibility. But the fact that the OP is posting for help here means that maybe their actions aren't that "wrong," right? Defining their behavior as right or wrong shows that the OP has a strong sense of moral conscience, seeks perfection, and rejects and denies themselves. Since the OP doesn't believe in accepting and approving themselves, where do these "right or wrong" standards come from? Are they set by the OP themselves or by others? If they are set by the OP themselves, why is the OP so hard on themselves, and what do they gain from doing so? If they are set by others, why doesn't the OP refuse to accept them and instead suppress and endure, and what do they gain from doing so? Others cannot see or hear the inner suppression of emotions, which causes a great deal of pressure on the mind and makes one physically and mentally exhausted. Not being understood, accepted, or approved by others only adds to the suffering and distress. It may be worth trying not to force themselves to suppress their thoughts and feelings, to express these thoughts and feelings, to release and alleviate the pressure within, and to give others the opportunity to understand them while also learning about others' thoughts and feelings. Only then can there be enough understanding, acceptance, and approval between each other, and only then can a stable and harmonious intimate relationship be established, allowing for an easier, natural, and joyful approach to life.

Hello, can you please tell me what happened? Why do you feel like everything is your fault? I believe that many things in this world are often caused by multiple factors, such as environmental influences, coincidences, personal strength, and the influence of others, etc. Whatever you're talking about, I firmly believe that it is definitely not solely your fault. You need to believe in this yourself and forgive yourself. Because each of us is capable of making mistakes, it is inevitable. Even if you make a mistake, you should not be too hard on yourself. You said that if you die, the world will be better, but I don't believe that. The birth of every life requires the efforts and contributions of many people. Similarly, when someone leaves this world, it often leaves behind a lot of sadness and regrets. If you were to die, your family, friends, the people you love, and those who love you would all be devastated and it would take them a long time to recover from the grief. At least, their world wouldn't become better at all, it would only become worse. If you want this world to be better, then live your life well and bring more beauty to this world with your warmth. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Not knowing the meaning of life, not knowing what people live for, don't know?
description: I have no motivation for life and don't know why I am alive. I am 16 years old this year.
keywords: Growth, developmental laws, self-acceptance, life meaning

answers.answer_text: You are only 16 years old, it's really rare for you to start thinking about the meaning of life at such a young age, so I want to give you a thumbs-up. Your self-awareness is rapidly developing, you have just started to come into contact with society and understand the world. Your current life mainly revolves around studying, the people you interact with are mostly friends, classmates, and teachers around your parents, and the world you often see is mainly the things around you. In this limited environment, you may think that this is all there is to life, and you may feel that life is monotonous, boring, and meaningless. But actually, this is not the end, the world outside is much bigger than what you see, and there are many things to experience ahead. This requires you to grow while experiencing and exploring. In this process of growth, we will inevitably experience confusion and questioning, and we will be curious about life, existence, and the world. This process of seeking answers is our search for identity. People in late adolescence often have strong curiosity and questions about themselves, form a certain understanding of their self-worth and social roles, and pursue the integration of self and identity. When you understand the meaning of this world and life, clarify your values and beliefs, and have a clear idea of what kind of person you want to become in the future, you will form a unique and stable self-identity. Pay more attention to the outside world, understand the wonders of the world, broaden your horizons; get to know more friends and expand your social circle; try and experience different activities, find joy in life and discover your interests and hobbies. Also, study hard and improve your skills and academic level, so that you will have the capital and opportunities to go further, see more, and discover the meaning of life. At 16, the magnificent drama of life is just beginning, don't rush to give yourself a conclusion or write an ending. No one can give you definite answers right now, the answers in your heart still need to be sought. Keep going!

Hello, I have important information to share. Everyone has the power to give meaning to their own life. If you want more joy in life, embrace happiness. If you want more vitality, make your life more vibrant. Some people believe that they are powerless to change the world, but we all have the ability to make a difference. If we pity ourselves, the world will become a little more pessimistic. If we show kindness to others, the world will become a little kinder. From the moment we are born, we begin the journey of discovering our true selves. Our true selves will guide us towards the life we desire. For example, someone who yearns for beauty will constantly seek it through engaging in artistic or aesthetic work. Someone who craves challenges will seek out uncertain or competitive endeavors to fulfill their true self. Living is a way of respecting life. When life is respected, its true meaning will be defined by our true selves.

question: I spoke to my boyfriend about whether or not we should have sexual relations before marriage, and my mom said I have no shame?
description: We just discussed the value and significance of this existence, and whether it is necessary. I don't know how shameless I can be, I'm very upset. How could she say that?
keywords: Family, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hug the questioner tightly through the screen!!! I also have a mother who has the exact same mindset as the questioner in this aspect!!! First of all, we need to understand a big premise - this kind of thinking from mothers stems from "motherly love". In their generation, they have seen a lot of cases where girls became unwed mothers or married because of pregnancy, and they think that these girls lack self-respect and are wasting their lives. They are afraid that we will repeat the mistakes of those so-called "undignified women" and accidentally ruin our lives. When they call us "shameless," it's also just an angry outburst, don't take it to heart too much, sister!! After all, there's a generation gap, and their perspectives are definitely much more conservative than ours as young people today. It's basically impossible to make them change this kind of mindset if they are not open-minded parents. My mom is like this too, the more I talk to her, the less she takes me seriously, and if I make her angry, she even says things like "just pretend you don't have a mom like me." Questioner, remember me as a negative example, don't force her to change her perspective, otherwise the conflicts could escalate. Whether or not to have premarital sex ultimately belongs to one's own private matters. It's already 2020! We have the right to enjoy sexual freedom equally - for girls, there's only one requirement: make sure to take safety precautions!!! Don't believe in the safety period method, don't believe in the nonsense about men ejaculating outside, and don't casually take contraception pills that can harm your body! - That's what true "self-respect" means in modern society. Marriage and love are two different things, and harmonious sexual life is also an important element in maintaining the balance of love and marriage. We're adults now, and making love out of love is a beautiful thing, so there's no need to bear too much psychological burden. As for the conservative views of the older generation, "follow them verbally" is the best solution, and "in actions, do what you think is right" - this is the private life of an adult, there's no need to announce it to others, not even parents have the right to pry into it - - Provided that you can protect yourself - - so, sister, when your mother says something like that, it's just her heartfelt words out of love and anxiety. The next time she brings it up, just say, "Yes, I understand, I will." Going along with her line of thinking will reduce a lot of arguments, and it's enough to do things that you think are correct and won't regret. Sincerely wishing you, sister, can take care of your heart!

OP, hello. It's normal to have differences and disagreements, but simply judging right and wrong will narrow your thinking. From your description, it can be seen that you are surprised and angry at your mother's attitude towards premarital sex and don't understand why she would scold you for being shameless. However, when you calm down, you may realize that the difference between you is not just about different views on this matter. Your birth era, upbringing, and inner thoughts are all different. Maybe in your perception, discussing this topic is necessary and helps to understand marriage and sexual relationships. However, for your mother, openly discussing sexual behavior comes with a strong sense of shame. She may feel it's indecent and not something that should be talked about, at least not openly. Your mother has conservative views and thoughts that are shaped by the times, her personal experiences, and her values, just as you may find it difficult to understand the thoughts of the post-2000s and post-2005s generations and find it all very strange. Seeing the differences may bring more understanding. Your mother scolding you is not a reflection of your personal worthiness, and she might not be able to accept anyone discussing these topics. If you think you can change your mother's thoughts, you can express your own thoughts to her and she might find a different way to approach the matter. However, in reality, the most likely situation is that we cannot change our parents' conservative and stubborn thoughts. We can only change ourselves or choose to "let it go" and handle things according to our own beliefs, without being influenced by them. Best wishes.

Hello, OP~ For our parents, their beliefs are still stuck in the last century. They believe that discussions about sexual knowledge and premarital sex are immoral and should not be happening. Mom's overreaction is a result of the clash between generations' views on sexuality, not because discussing it is shameful. It's difficult to change Mom's long-held beliefs, and it's also hard to make her understand your views and actions. So, the first thing you need to do is to clarify that discussing premarital topics is a normal behavior, not something to be ashamed of. Secondly, don't try to change your parents' thoughts, and don't let their thoughts and actions affect you. Try your best to avoid this issue when you're around them. Mom's beliefs have deepened over the years, and it's not worth wasting your energy on something that won't change. Lastly, balance the differences between your own beliefs about sexuality or other aspects and your parents' views. Approach their views with an understanding attitude, and don't get too caught up in whether your opinions align. As long as you're not making major mistakes, both of you can hold onto your own thoughts! Best wishes!

*Hello! I hope I can help you! First of all, I can understand that you are feeling distressed. We need to be clear that a mother is the person who loves us the most in the world, there is no one else. This love comes from a kind of love (maternal love) and maternal love is great! Secondly, it is important to understand what you want. Mothers come from a different era with their own thoughts. We need to communicate patiently with our parents to avoid unnecessary conflicts. Ultimately, it all stems from a mother's love for us, right? Of course, it is crucial to take necessary precautions before getting married! Next time, try not to argue with your parents, just respond with a positive "yes". You can decide for yourself what you want to do after that. But it is always best to choose self-respect. Keep going! I hope you become happier and happier!!

question: Feeling very frustrated, becoming more and more unhappy after changing jobs?
description: After changing jobs, I became increasingly unhappy. At first, I was forced to switch jobs, and later I found myself working with a group of colleagues who are older and have higher positions than me. I feel very inferior at work, as we don't have much in common and I have to endure it. I feel like I am less important than others, and I have very few friends around me. Even they are all focused on their own lives, I can no longer receive warmth and comfort. I find life very dull and difficult to bear, and I feel hopeless.
keywords: Career, career management, workplace interpersonal relationships, work exhaustion.

answers.answer_text: Hello! From your description, I can sense that you are not very happy right now. Being forced to change jobs and struggling to adapt to the new environment has had an impact on your overall well-being. You are feeling frustrated, disappointed, and even experiencing low self-esteem. I completely understand how you feel and can see the distress you are going through. One of your concerns is being forced to change jobs. I am not sure what kind of organization you work for, but being "forced" into this situation must not have been your choice. It would be helpful to consider the reasons behind this decision and the intentions of your superiors. We need to approach the matter of job transfer based on the actual circumstances. Perhaps they are hoping that you will gain more work experience in the new position, which could lead to other benefits. Another concern you have is feeling inferior. This experience stems from comparing yourself to your new colleagues. You perceive them to have a higher status and more experience due to their age and position. The characteristics of these colleagues are that they are experienced professionals but lack the warmth and enthusiasm of younger individuals. This might make you feel suppressed and unsupported, as if you are not recognized or cared for. However, it is important to remember that you are not on the same starting line as these older colleagues and thus there is no need for comparison. As a new member of the team, it is beneficial to humble yourself and learn from those with more experience and expertise. Embrace this opportunity to accumulate your own professional skills and knowledge. Moreover, shifting your focus to learning from them can help alleviate the pressure and allow you to develop positive relationships. Lastly, you mentioned feeling lonely and having a dull life without friends. Within the workplace, try connecting with colleagues who are relatively easy-going, engage in conversations, seek advice on work matters, and naturally the relationship will improve. It is also possible to establish friendships outside of work with people of similar age, which can help alleviate work-related stress and add more joy to your life. In your career, every effort you make adds to your repertoire. Every difficult situation is an opportunity. Sometimes our worries arise from being unable to detach ourselves from the situation and view it objectively. This can result in being trapped within our own thoughts and becoming more frustrated. However, what we can do is consider our goals and prioritize accordingly at each stage. By focusing on the main objectives and gradually addressing the secondary aspects, we create opportunities for turning things around and achieving success.

Hello~ I completely understand how you feel, sending you a hug~ I can imagine the situation you're in at work, and it can truly be a place lacking warmth, making you feel lonely and helpless. However, you need to change your mindset and realize that the workplace is the workplace, it has its own unique characteristics, and sometimes it can be harsh, such as the "survival of the fittest" mentality. Here are a few suggestions - 1. Learn to communicate, but remember to find the right balance, making communication a medium to increase trust, understanding, and familiarity among coworkers. In the workplace, communication can be difficult, but it's always possible to find common topics to talk about, both in personal and work-related aspects. Be careful not to make jokes randomly or talk about irrelevant matters. 2. Focus on doing your own job well. Only by doing your job well can you qualify and have the ability to help others, and also earn dignity for yourself. When your skills are strong enough, so-called interpersonal skills and relationships will naturally improve. 3. When faced with problems, try to find solutions on your own first. If you really can't solve them, then ask others for help. In the workplace, there are always more solutions than difficulties. As long as you are willing to try, there will definitely be a way, even if the final outcome is not what you and the company wanted, at least you made an effort, which is better than just complaining without taking any action. 4. Clarify your own position. Going to work is for work, not for making friends. If you have various frustrations, you can talk to trusted family and friends about them; your coworkers are not obligated to share the burden with you. Wishing you well~

Hello, I noticed that you're becoming increasingly unhappy because of your job change. I've also gone through a similar experience and would like to share with you, in hopes that it might give you some reference. Before I retired, I was forced to transfer to a new organization due to restructuring. When I arrived there, everything was unfamiliar and the work wasn't going smoothly. Due to their exclusion, I didn't have much work to do, which was very uncomfortable for someone like me who was used to being busy. I felt really frustrated, just like how you're feeling now. During that time, I started attending classes and found various psychology-related courses online. I categorized and compiled the ones that interested me, and began designing courses, focusing on attention training and memory improvement for primary and secondary school students. It was during this period that I found my passion. So, I have a few suggestions for you. First, it's understandable that you're feeling all kinds of emotions like frustration and loneliness. There may be people who sympathize with you, but based on my experience in the workplace, such sympathy is short-lived and superficial. Once it comes to vested interests, people's true colors are revealed. Therefore, I suggest that you gather yourself and be a smiling tiger, facing everyone with a smile. Second, complete your job duties without compromise. By doing so, you are demonstrating your work capabilities and establishing your position within the team. Third, when it comes to tasks assigned by your superiors, while accepting the work, make sure to ask for the final deadline and complete it before that deadline. However, don't rush to submit it, instead, keep it with you. This way, you can carve out some time that belongs entirely to you, to do things you enjoy. Fourth, take advantage of this period when you aren't closely acquainted with your colleagues and maintain a certain distance from them for the time being. This will allow you to observe each person, secretly learn a new subject, skill, or delve into your favorite field, laying a solid foundation for future job adjustments. There is a saying from our childhood: "Moscow doesn't believe in tears." In fact, this is true everywhere; no one sympathizes with the weak. When conditions are not yet favorable, when we can only be mediocre and unremarkable, we should first settle ourselves, become an ordinary person, and find joy and capability within that ordinariness. I believe you will find your happiness!

Good morning! OP, seeing your question, I feel your frustration. Work is indeed the most time-consuming aspect of our lives, and if we constantly feel miserable during this time, it's like having a dark cloud over our heads that refuses to dissipate, and we can't feel the brightness and sunshine. After carefully reading your description, I thought of the following problems that you are facing, and let's take a look at the possible underlying truths behind these problems, and try to see if I can be of help to you. 

1. Forced job change: OP mentioned being forced to change jobs, is this pressure coming from your parents? If it's from your family, I can think of two aspects. [Parent-child relationship] Being forced reflects the parent-child relationship or the interaction pattern between parents and children. Since it is described as being forced, it means that the parents did not really consider the child's thoughts and instead made decisions on behalf of the child from the perspective of doing what is best for the child. [Acceptance] OP is already of working age, indicating that they have reached adulthood biologically, but in the end, they accepted their parents' advice. Perhaps OP has many reasons for accepting, but they can reflect on whether there is a need for them in this job change event. There is always a reason behind human behavior, whether it's believing that this job still has benefits or not being able to overturn their parents' decision, all of these can be reasons. OP can introspectively ask themselves a few "whys". [Boundaries] When OP's parents forced them to accept a job change, they may have in fact crossed the boundaries between themselves and their child. Parents may be acting from a responsible standpoint, believing that this is the best thing for their child. At this time, the child is weak and the parents are strong. So, what reasons led the parents to continue playing the role of the powerful one even after the child became an adult, and to set the child in a position of weakness? Is the child genuinely weak or just pretending to be weak? Can the child take responsibility for their own decisions? Or can parents trust that their child can handle their own affairs? Parents have their own lessons to learn, and OP has their own lessons as well. 

2. Inferiority: After entering the new job, OP feels inferior when facing people older and with higher positions than themselves, enduring situations where they don't have a common language and feeling inferior. [Value system] Our evaluation of human worth and self-value may come more from the influence of our family of origin. People with higher positions may be seen as "authority" figures, and OP's interaction with colleagues may mirror their reaction patterns towards authority figures, which then ties into their self-worth. [Self-appraisal] OP primarily evaluates themselves in comparison to the outside world based on their position, neglecting their inner worth as a person. Of course, many of us have this problem, and if we understand this problem, it will weaken feelings of inferiority. I suggest that OP can read some books on Adlerian psychology, particularly about inferiority. 

3. Friends: OP has almost no friends in the new workplace, and colleagues mind their own business without offering warmth and comfort. Some organizations are like this, or maybe some people just put on a facade. If OP cannot leave their current workplace, they can take the initiative to actively help their colleagues and improve intimacy. On the other hand, they can also seek friends outside of the workplace, such as former colleagues or classmates, and continue to build their social circle, finding close friends who can support and encourage each other. I wish you good luck in resolving the problems you are currently facing.

Give the OP a hug! I can feel the OP's suppressed anger and anxiety. Being forced to change jobs, anyone would find it hard to be happy. And on top of that, working with colleagues who are older and have a higher status adds to the pressure and makes the OP feel inferior. With few friends around and distant relationships, the OP cannot find comfort and warmth from friends, which makes life more boring and unhappy. The fact that the OP is able to work means they are an independent adult with their own thoughts and actions. It makes me curious about who can "force" the OP to change jobs against their will, and why the OP didn't refuse but chose to accept and endure it. This makes me wonder what the OP is trying to express and what they hope to gain by suppressing themselves. Suppressing and forbearing might be a way for the OP to satisfy themselves, but the person who "forces" the OP to accept it might mistakenly believe that the OP understands and accepts the "force", thinking it's reasonable and doesn't realize the extent of the OP's suppressed emotions. The distant relationship with friends reflects this emotional "isolation" and affects the development of their emotional relationship. This kind of interaction can be seen as an extension and reflection of family intimacy, which means the OP's relationship with their parents is not intimate enough and somewhat distant, making them feel insecure and easily anxious, leading them to seek acceptance and appease their family. Therefore, the issue troubling the OP comes from their family relationships. As an adult, the OP can try talking to their parents, expressing their thoughts and feelings, and listening to what they have to say to promote deeper communication and understanding, reduce inner stress, improve their relationship with their parents, or consider making an appointment with a suitable therapist for systematic psychological counseling to solve the issues that are troubling them.

I don't want to change jobs, but I am being forced to change jobs, which is frustrating. I find it difficult to adapt to the new work environment, and it is mentally challenging. It's normal to experience such fluctuations, and I'm giving you a hug. In the workplace, there may be some harsh elements. Since you have the opportunity to work in such a strong and esteemed circle, I think it is both a challenge for us and a psychological burden. I remember when I was gradually advancing in the workplace, I faced people who wished I couldn't adapt to the job, and there were also sarcastic comments. I even cried. But I persevered, made progress step by step, learned from my experiences, and moved forward steadily. Looking back, the things that I thought were very difficult in the past now seem like a piece of cake. I am truly happy with my growth and progress. The first point is to adjust your mindset. Since you are surrounded by many excellent senior colleagues, we know our abilities may not match theirs, but each person is an opportunity for us to learn. Learn from the strengths of others, and even if we are not as capable as them now, as long as we find our own position and bridge the gap, step by step with effort, we will be successful with a clear conscience. Use the time of self-doubt and self-negation to improve our capabilities, and believe that we will gain more. The second point is to learn to communicate. As newcomers in a new environment, our colleagues may not initiate much interaction with us, but we can take the initiative to communicate with them, even if it means being more proactive. Some may perceive us as average, but so what? They might even want to help us feel accomplished. So, showing vulnerability may not be a bad thing; it might even be a way to preserve our strength. It is also normal to have a few people who are difficult to communicate with, as there are all kinds of people. Start by communicating with those who are easier to talk to and gradually expand our communication network. The third point is the skill of getting along with others. In the workplace, getting along with others is crucial, especially for newbies. Take on a humble attitude, be observant, help your colleagues pour a glass of water, wipe the table, and so on. These are just examples; the specific actions should be decided based on the actual situation. When faced with difficulties, we all need comfort and encouragement. It's normal. Take your time to adjust, read books on interpersonal communication, such as "The Harvard Emotional Intelligence Course," and keep going!

First of all, I want to give a virtual hug to the questioner. The complex interpersonal relationships in the workplace often leave us mentally and physically exhausted. *After changing jobs, you have become increasingly unhappy. In the beginning, you were forced to change jobs, and you yourself are very clear that this job was obtained unwillingly or, in other words, with inner resistance. Perhaps this unwillingness has sowed the seeds for future burdens. So, let's think about where this coercion comes from. Parents? Family? Economic reasons? Understanding this objective fact will help us further solve the problem. Subjectively, we must believe that at any moment, we have the power to make our own decisions. *Later, facing a group of older colleagues with higher positions, you feel inferior at work. There is no common language and you have to endure. If the previous situation was the cause and deep-rooted, then what follows is the current reality that you face every day. Purely from a work perspective, have you ever thought about what kind of work you like, what kind of work suits you, and what kind of work you can do? Facing people who are better than us can give us invisible pressure, but often, the pressure itself is not the problem. The problem lies in how we perceive and interpret the pressure. Pressure can also be seen as a motivation. While adjusting our interpretation, we also need to respect our own feelings and not rush to find a one-time solution. Take your time to understand yourself. *Feeling inferior and having only a few friends around who are also dealing with their own problems, no longer able to receive warmth and comfort, life feels dreary, and you feel hopeless. The above feelings seem to be the questioner's extended worries. The decline in work status has led to doubts and lack of self-confidence, as well as a lack of friends to talk to. The beginning is always difficult. First of all, we are not fighting alone. Since there are so many people on this platform who vent their troubles daily, it proves that we are all human beings, born in this world, and troubles are also part of life. Open your heart, take the initiative to make friends, but first adjust your mindset and state. I hope the above will inspire or help the questioner. The world and I love you.

Hello, OP: I have noticed a change in your mood since changing jobs, and I also noticed that you have actively expressed your emotional distress and sought help from others, which undoubtedly helps you to better understand yourself and your work. You mentioned that you have been unhappy since changing jobs, so does that mean you were satisfied with your previous job? Now, I will share my observations from your post, which may help you gain a more diverse perspective on yourself and your work. 1. Your pain stems from not accepting. I don't know what reasons you have for staying in this job, but if this job is really causing you such pain, perhaps you can leave. If you cannot leave, then what ways can help you adjust your emotions? My understanding is to accept reality. From your post, I observed that you seem to express more dissatisfaction with your current job, noticing that your colleagues are older and have higher positions than you, and there is no common language, requiring patience, and feeling a lack of warmth, making you feel inferior. So where do these feelings come from? I think they come from comparing with your previous job! You have not learned to accept the current situation, and you are physically present but mentally absent. Therefore, you cannot see the advantages of this job. So if this situation cannot be changed at the moment, then learn to accept reality. 2. Learn to accept yourself and build your own internal evaluation system. Inferiority is actually not accepting yourself. Not allowing yourself to be inferior to others. So when you work with older people and people with higher positions, it is easy to generate feelings of inferiority. In fact, being strict with ourselves can be the last straw that breaks us, on the contrary, being gentle and caring with ourselves can give us the strength to go further. In the face of these colleagues, perhaps you can learn to accept that you are not as good as them in some aspects, but you are not completely bad either! You also need to learn to see your strengths. For example, you are young! So if you are willing to work hard, then you will have the opportunity to have more ability and status than your colleagues when you reach their age! So the important thing is to accept yourself now, see your strengths, and accept your weaknesses. Accept the parts that cannot be changed and focus on the parts that you can change, instead of constantly draining your energy. Don't generalize. Build your own internal evaluation system. In fact, self-confidence is not really related to excellence, but to our own recognition and interpretation of ourselves. 3. Learn to see the positive aspects of your work. Yes, your current job has brought you great pain, but it has also given you the opportunity to reacquaint yourself and adjust yourself. For example, you have seen your own insecurities, so you have the opportunity to adjust your insecurities and reconcile with them. Develop a healthier personality. We can imagine that if we were to stay in our previous job, we might never see these aspects of our personality and materials. So the probability of this happening in our lifetime is very small. So facing it earlier is better! I also noticed that you feel there is no warmth in your work, but it is also an opportunity for you to spend time with yourself! Learn to console and embrace yourself. In life, there are many times when others can meet our needs, which is fortunate and happy. But if others cannot fulfill us, don't forget that we have the ability to fulfill ourselves. We are responsible for ourselves and our emotions. Your colleagues, their higher positions, so you can observe how they handle themselves and learn from their strengths, combined with your own advantages. So if you learn, will your achievements in the future be lower than theirs? So learn to see the positive aspects of work. See how work helps us grow, not just consume us. Lastly, if you want to receive warmth, you must first give warmth. Because no one owes you anything at work. Be warm to others, but also do not compromise yourself.

Due to some special reasons, we have had to leave our previous work environment. There is no sense of warmth, no friends, no common language, and even the people around us are much more outstanding than ourselves. Under various pressures, we may feel that life is hopeless. 1. It is best to separate work and personal life. In our work, we will encounter many problems, and sometimes it is inevitable that we need to collaborate with others. If the people around us can provide us with appropriate help and encouragement, it would be greatly appreciated by newcomers in the workplace. Even if it means working hard and feeling tired, it doesn't matter because we know that it is a way to exercise and grow. However, the reality is often far from ideal, especially in a workplace that is relatively outdated, where the people around us have already become seasoned professionals who know how to protect their own interests. Many times, they are only friends in appearance. For us, it can be difficult to adapt to such an environment, but work is work, and personal life is personal life. We still need to keep them separate. For things within our job responsibilities, we should try our best to do our job well and try not to bother others with tasks that we can independently handle. If there are tasks that we truly cannot complete on our own, we should raise questions to our superiors. When collaborating with others, we should try our best not to cause trouble for them. We should focus on doing what we are supposed to do and not feel inferior just because they have higher positions, because we receive corresponding rewards based on our own efforts. Mutual respect is important in the workplace. 2. We need to have our own ways to release stress in life. If we are doing a job that we don't like and have no hobbies or friends during our spare time, we often bring our dissatisfaction from work into our personal lives. Therefore, we need to distinguish between work and personal life. We should do our own tasks well during work hours and not dwell on work-related issues after work. We should have our own social circle and hobbies. For example, we can chat with good friends and vent our frustrations, cultivate new hobbies, or do things that make us happy. We can also write down unhappy experiences anonymously online. In fact, happiness and unhappiness both make up a day. Why not choose to be a little happier? The world loves you.

"It's okay, I understand you. First of all, what does it feel like to be rejected by the strong? It feels uncomfortable, as if no one accepts you, and no one sees you. You are often pressured to be excellent, otherwise we will all reject you, you don't meet the standards, you don't deserve to be seen, and you are not worthy of love. Do you feel this kind of pressure? It can be exhausting, and you may start to doubt yourself and even look down on yourself, right? However, chasing excellence will only make you feel that you are not good enough. Only those who constantly pursue excellence and look down on those who are slightly inferior do this. Allow yourself to set boundaries with these people. How others see you is their own business, if we cross that line, we will be involved in their trauma. Allow yourself to be yourself, without the need to please or hate. Desiring love and validation can actually be fulfilled with the help of a higher power. Because humans always have limitations, just like when you feel lonely and no friends understand you. Friends are also busy and have their own troubles. Sometimes they cannot immediately understand and answer you. Only a higher power is infinite, it loves and accepts you at all times and places. It allows you to be yourself, it allows us to be imperfect, it allows us to be ordinary. Love yourself a little more every day. You can do things you like, such as watching movies, listening to music, and nourishing your heart first. Giving yourself mental energy is the most important. Accept that this society is like this because everyone has their limitations. "Looking down" on others is the norm for many people.
