They are indifferent because they can't even take care of themselves and have no energy to care for you. Forgive them, because you will also have limited energy and limitations. You have done your best, and they have also done their best. See your strengths and realize that you are already good enough. We are born as human beings, and that in itself is beautiful. Our existence is wonderful, a value, and an achievement. We are already good enough. There is no need to chase perfection or excellence anymore. Believe me, you are already good. Blessings to you, namaste!"

question: My parents scolded me many times for trivial matters, and after being scolded, I often have the urge to self-harm.
description: Parents have scolded me many times, and I don't know why. They suddenly yell at me when I speak in a normal tone. Sometimes, they even chase after me and continue scolding me when I lock the door. I have nowhere to vent my frustrations and have been constantly suppressing them. After crying, I sometimes have the urge to self-harm. I used to be able to adjust my emotions, but now it's getting harder and harder. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner, here's a warm hug for you. You mentioned two things: 1. Your parents repeatedly reprimand you for trivial matters, causing you significant psychological pressure. 2. Your mood is not very good, and you feel that you are becoming slower in adjusting your mental state. You feel that your ability to withstand stress has decreased. Firstly, let's talk about the issue of your parents reprimanding you. Everyone has different standards for evaluating things. Sometimes, what you may consider a small matter, your family may see as a bigger issue. Therefore, they adopt a serious attitude towards you. Compared to your dismissive attitude, they feel that you don't value this matter, which generates even greater dissatisfaction and may lead to more intense behaviors towards you. Secondly, another reason may be that your family might have recently encountered some annoying things, combined with the things happening at home, causing them to suddenly vent their frustration. They may not even realize it themselves. In this aspect, you may need to understand them a bit more. You can try to communicate with them. They are your parents, but also ordinary individuals with their own emotions, who also need care and love from their family. Lastly, everyone has a certain level of psychological resilience. If negative emotions persist for a long time or occur repeatedly, it may slow down your adjustment process, just like some machines that may operate slightly slower after prolonged use. Therefore, you need to find more effective ways to adjust or quickly improve your relationship with your family through communication. Wishing you all the best! The world and I love you.

question: I am tormented every day by the fact that my boyfriend still can't fully let go of his ex with depression.
description: My boyfriend's ex-girlfriend went to prison because of some company issues (it seems like fraud). It happened in November last year. At the end of March this year, someone from a website called him and said that his ex-girlfriend still owed money and her phone was also turned off. My boyfriend got scared that she might commit suicide because she has depression. Later, he asked his friends and found out that she was indeed in prison and owed several tens of thousands of dollars on multiple websites, saying that she spent money recklessly after they broke up. My boyfriend felt guilty because of her depression. He even gave her back around 13,000 yuan and added her mom on WeChat. Her mom said that they couldn't repay the money now because they needed to raise money for legal matters. As his current girlfriend, I feel really upset. We have broken up many times before because of his ex-girlfriend. I really can't stand it when he talks about depression... A month ago, I asked him to delete his ex-girlfriend's WeChat, but he said he can't delete it yet because she hasn't been released. I had a breakdown that night. I cried for a long time and kept asking myself what to do. Breaking up really hurts. I had dreams countless times of him being with his ex-girlfriend. Every time I wake up, I feel very uncomfortable, insecure, and afraid that I might lose him all of a sudden. I'm in college now and he is working. We have been together almost a year.

answers.answer_text: Hello the person asking the question, I want to give you a warm hug. Based on your description, I would like to know if you have ever met or interacted with his ex-girlfriend. I am not sure about the situation with his ex-girlfriend in prison. It seems like a trap with the scam company and website owing money. Even though you cannot see his ex-girlfriend, her connections are still there, and they are taking advantage of your boyfriend's kindness and guilt by making him repay the debt. It is important to first verify if the situation is genuine and then decide whether or not to help. Of course, your boyfriend's choice to help repay the debt shows that he is a very kind person and feels guilty about his ex-girlfriend's depression caused by their breakup. However, he does not have any lingering feelings, and I believe that after the breakup, his ex-girlfriend definitely contacted him and struggled to get back together. But in the end, he chose to be with you and chose you. I understand your discomfort, and I believe that he must have very attractive qualities that make you like him and not want to break up with him. I believe his ex-girlfriend feels the same way. Regarding deleting WeChat, can he give you a deadline? For example, wait until she is released from prison or until the debt is fully repaid. Communication can be made, and if this issue is not resolved properly, it can become a ticking time bomb in your relationship, ready to explode at any moment. However, it is really not worth it. Right now, the two of you are together, so enjoy your happy life together and create your own happiness. It is truly unnecessary to make yourself unhappy because of past events.

question: Depression, failed to pass the probation period in several jobs, how to overcome the fear of work?
description: Depression, feeling low, working several jobs, but only lasted one to two months in each, none of them passed the probation period, feeling a bit scared now.

answers.answer_text: Do you have depression? Are you currently receiving treatment? Is it because of depression that you are unable to perform your job well? These jobs are not long-lasting, and you haven't even passed the probation period. What are some common characteristics they have? Maybe we should look for some solutions to overcome this. In addition, the treatment of depression is of paramount importance. Constant failures will definitely make you more frustrated. Therefore, when your depression has improved, it would be more suitable for you to engage in normal social interactions and perform the job you want to do.

question: Why can some people confidently and unabashedly trouble others?
description: I don't really like to bother others. I prefer to solve things on my own. If I can't solve it, I try to minimize the trouble for others before asking for help. However, some people seem to enjoy bothering others. Even if they have their own things to do, when they come across something fun, they completely ignore their responsibilities and let others do it for them. I really can't understand it, and I don't like it. Why are they so confident about bothering others?

answers.answer_text: Different people may have different answers when it comes to how to view troubling others. Although it is the same matter, our different upbringing and experiences result in different understandings and values. Therefore, our perspectives on the world will also differ. For example, some people do not like to trouble others and try to do things themselves as much as possible, but at the same time they may not like others troubling them. On the other hand, some people enjoy troubling others but are also willing to help and face the troubles caused by others. Which one is better? Perhaps different people will have different answers at different stages.

question: I've been in this position for two years, and now the senior mentor is guiding a new person. Should I consider changing to a new job position?
description: I have been working in this position for two years, constantly asking the senior workers for guidance, but now the new supervisor wants the senior worker to train the new employees. When I first started, I took on the dirtiest and most tiring tasks, hoping to learn something, but they always avoided me. However, in front of the supervisor, they claim that they want to teach me. The senior worker is now very attentive in training the new employees, even buying them food and explaining everything in detail. I feel like I should change to a different position, but I'm afraid it will be awkward when we meet again. They would definitely not want to let the students they have trained go elsewhere, and once the new employees are well trained, I, as an inexperienced worker, will be left behind after doing all the hard work. I have always been passive and don't want to be pushed away by others anymore. Now I want to request a job transfer, but I feel too embarrassed to do so.
keywords: Occupation, career management, workplace interpersonal relationships

answers.answer_text: Reading about your confession reminded me of myself 20 years ago, when I first entered the workplace. It was eerily similar to the predicament I once found myself in. Back then, I was learning related business skills from a mentor in a workshop. I couldn't tell if I was simply unsuited for the job or if there was some clash of fate with this particular mentor. I could feel the disdain in his eyes, which made me extremely uncomfortable. As you can imagine, he believed I wasn't cut out for this line of work, so I often faced scrutiny and criticism in public. Initially, I thought maybe I was lucky to have encountered a strict mentor and believed it was his unique teaching method. However, as I continued my learning journey, I truly experienced that it wasn't just his strictness or unique teaching style but that he genuinely believed I was unsuitable for the job. He directly told me that it wasn't that he didn't want to teach but that I simply wasn't cut out for it. He advised me to consider switching jobs. After much deliberation, I thought his words made sense. Perhaps I indeed lacked interest in this line of work and the persistence required for learning. In the end, I chose to give up and left that company. Today, after 20 years, when I came across your question, it suddenly reminded me of my experience. I feel that if your mentor truly cared about you, even if he didn't want to teach you, he would sincerely tell you so, just like my mentor did. From your confession, I can't sense such thoughts from your mentor; instead, it seems like he's just paying lip service in front of his superiors. However, when it comes to training newcomers, your mentor displays an extremely strong enthusiasm for teaching. This is something you should seriously consider. Is your mentor intentionally trying to make you give up through provocative methods, or does this novice have a special relationship with the leadership that makes it necessary for your mentor to put in extra effort? This is a question you need to clarify. If it's the former, after two years, if you're still stagnating in this position, I personally don't recommend wasting more time, and I support you in finding a new job. As for feeling sorry for not meeting again, that kind of thinking can be disregarded when it comes to your own future. If it's the latter, then you really need to reassess this mentor. Despite some constraints, fundamentally, following this kind of mentor makes it difficult for you to have a bright future. Whether to stay or leave, switch or not, all of these depend on your inner self. Don't complicate matters. In this situation, listen to the voice within you.

According to the information you provided, it can be said that the analysis that can be done has been done by you. From an outsider's perspective, it seems like you are not ready to take action yet. Any action has its gains and losses. For example, if you don't change jobs, you don't have to face the awkwardness, but your professional growth may be limited. If you do change jobs, you must be confident that you will gain better professional growth, but you may feel uncomfortable facing your previous mentors. Both choices have advantages and disadvantages. Obviously, you no longer want to bear the disadvantages of the first choice, but unfortunately, you are not prepared to bear the disadvantages of the second choice either. I don't believe that all problems can be solved through communication, but it is indeed necessary to express your own attitude. How do you see your work? The underlying logic of work is exchange, which is true, but many people always prioritize their own interests, even though it may not be correct. Because in the workplace, few people purely focus on interests, and the word "interests" means different things to different people. For example, if I don't like you and find you annoying, your presence in front of me every day can also be considered an "interest". I don't know what has happened in your work, but let's suppose that your mentors just don't like you. If you change jobs and leave, everyone will be happy, and you won't have to feel embarrassed or awkward, right? Two years should be enough time, and if you really can't get along, there is no need to force it. Out of sight, out of mind. However, how you perceive and take responsibility for your work and actions ultimately needs to be decided by you.

question: Fallen angel, how can I save you?
description: I realize that my mentality/thinking has become problematic. I feel very negative and cannot uplift myself. I have been trying to adjust my state of mind for two days, but it's still not working. I cannot overcome difficulties and conquer myself. This not only affects my life and work but also impacts the people who care about me. I feel guilty, but I cannot redeem myself. Am I a lost cause? I want to do things well, but I cannot succeed. I feel anxious and restless, overthinking everything, and unable to focus on work. I keep making mistakes and things are getting out of control.
keywords: Emotions, depressed mood, emotional regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: ~~Give the questioner a warm hug. From the description, I can feel the questioner's desire for improvement, and I understand that the questioner has been experiencing some negative emotions recently, but doesn't know how to deal with them. First, I want to tell the questioner that there are many people around who are supporting and helping the questioner with the problems and difficulties we are currently facing. So, instead of always relying on ourselves to solve problems, we can seek help from the people around us. This will not bother others with our depressed emotions. The questioner can reflect on whether there have been any events in the recent past that might have caused our bad mood? Is it due to work, study, or other reasons? We can try to discover and find possible influencing factors. On the other hand, the questioner may consider whether there are any exceptional situations in life: are there any exceptions when our mood temporarily improves or stabilizes? These exceptional situations may be helpful in solving problems and relieving emotions. Take a look at these moments, and think about the people, events, or activities that made us feel better during those times.

question: Wife's infidelity in marriage, choose to forgive once for the sake of the family but feeling very painful.
description: In order to have a high income for my family, I work as a senior executive in a well-known real estate company in another city. In May of this year, my wife had an affair and had sexual intercourse with another man while traveling outside. I didn't notice their contact when I returned home during the May Day holiday, but eventually my mother discovered them separating at the entrance of our building. After the truth came out, the third party even sent me a video of their sexual activity, clearly showing that they were willing participants. They also sent photos of them kissing and enjoying themselves while traveling. We have two young children, and I have been working away from home for a long time, always prioritizing my family. I am deeply hurt. After the incident was exposed, my wife begged me bitterly, saying that she was temporarily blinded and fell into someone else's trap, and she wishes to return to the family. In order to keep our family intact, especially because our children are only 6 and 3 years old, I have to endure something that no man in the world can tolerate. I am willing to forgive her for this mistake, but I'm worried that by forgiving, I might be indulging her behavior. Additionally, whenever I close my eyes, I can't help but think about their video of sexual activity. I feel that this woman will never be clean again, mentally and physically dirty. I don't know how to face her in daily life even if I decide to forgive her. Whether to divorce or not, she has left a shadow in my heart, and I am in immense pain!

answers.answer_text: 【Take it as a learning opportunity】Dear friend: Hello! After reading your words, I feel that you are a very rational person who understands that the key is not whether to divorce. You know that divorce cannot solve the problem. The key issue is your concern about being betrayed again, how to face her, and how to repair this relationship. Why does a third party appear in a marriage? 1. Someone said it right: if there are no problems in the relationship between husband and wife, a third party cannot intervene. If the husband and wife are united, the third party cannot break them apart. 2. It is a common habit in China to not speak up about problems. Because of face-saving and embarrassment, it is a cultural habit not to actively understand each other's views on this matter or their own behavior. Therefore, like a snowball, the problem grows bigger and bigger. 3. If there is no common goal in life and the family atmosphere is not good, some families may appear normal to outsiders, but inside, they are full of problems. There is a lack of care, unity, trust, or boundaries between the husband and wife. Therefore, if you want to face her and want to have a happy family again, you must have the determination to reconcile. 【First】Release anger. Dealing with this matter with anger is futile. Try releasing it, maybe try hitting a pillow. 【Second】Labeling and trying to forgive. If you keep looking down on her and continue to despise her, it will only make you feel that you didn't have good judgement in the first place and hurt your self-esteem. It may even create more negative atmosphere. No one grows up aspiring to be an "unfaithful woman". There must be reasons behind it. I have found that the person who hurts others suffers twice as much pain as the person being hurt, or even more. Try to separate the person from the actions, deal with this matter properly, and think about why you fell in love with this person in the first place. 【Third】Have a calm face-to-face conversation. Take this opportunity to express your feelings about this matter. Let her understand the impact this has had on you. Understand the reasons behind her infidelity and her satisfaction with this marriage. Through this matter, understand each other's true feelings. You have to understand that having a high income is just one aspect of fulfilling family responsibilities. If a homemaker in a high-income family cheats, it may be because she feels too empty. You have to understand that money cannot replace other types of love. Confidence, intimacy, service, dedication... these cannot be bought with money. Check if you have put her first. The proper order of a healthy family is: spouse, children, parents. Is the relationship between husband and wife equal? Often, different incomes can cause the higher earner to look down on the other, creating an imbalance in status and conflicts. 【Fourth】Rebuilding trust requires time and fulfillment of promises. Try to have her write a commitment letter. Let her understand the importance of this commitment. This will make you feel more at ease and also serve as a wake-up call for her. 【Fifth】Don't demand a perfect marriage. Since no one is perfect, how can a marriage be perfect? Take this incident as an opportunity to learn. Marriage is not the end of happiness, but another beginning of learning in life. Approach marriage with a learning attitude and invite your partner to face the problems together. Don't shoulder the burden of marriage alone. Try to openly express your feelings and let the other person understand you and love you. Give yourself and your partner time, and consider yourself and her as classmates or partners.

You, who were wholeheartedly devoted to your family, have experienced betrayal. The pain must be heart-wrenching! The question is, how should you face her in your future life? The shadow left by divorce or not getting divorced has caused me great anguish! I understand, but it's not your fault. Let me tell you a method to alleviate the pain! If you have painful, sad thoughts appear in your mind, simply say thank you to them. Just say thank you, thank you for reminding me, that's enough. Engage in a dialogue with those thoughts, even imagine their voice as Donald Duck's voice. This can have a dissociative effect. Dissociation is a very important technique in this therapy. However, we need to understand that the purpose of dissociation is not to eliminate unpleasant thoughts. Once the unpleasant thoughts arise, they have arisen. We don't aim to get rid of them, but rather to understand the essence of the thoughts. By seeing their essence, sometimes thoughts will naturally disappear, and sometimes they won't. But if we expect them to disappear in advance, that would be setting ourselves up for disappointment. This method is not an instant solution where you become happy immediately by using it. Sometimes you will feel happy, sometimes you will let go. But don't expect it. You just need to separate yourself from those thoughts, just the ability to observe them is enough. Don't expect these techniques to make you feel good. In general, after dissociating from a trouble-causing thought, you will indeed feel a little better, but that is just an extra benefit, not the main goal. The main goal of dissociation is to free ourselves from the tyranny of thoughts, so that we can focus on more important matters. Bringing ourselves back to the present moment is the method to alleviate the pain.

Money cannot replace other forms of love. Affirmation, intimacy, service, focus...these are things that money cannot buy. I don't know if men understand the meaning of this statement, but when a woman's needs are not met, it is actually the husband's greatest failure and negligence. If you earn money to support the family and she gives birth and raises children, then these contributions to the family should offset each other, right? If you are not fulfilling your role as a husband, then she naturally doesn't have to fulfill her role as a wife. Isn't that also offsetting each other? If you feel imbalanced, then take up the responsibility as a husband to fulfill your wife's needs. Without giving, there is no receiving. So why blame your wife instead of reflecting on yourself?

Your pain has nothing to do with your wife, it is about your dignity and family. I agree with your divorce because, as you said, family is important, but you have not reflected on yourself. Since you despise your wife so much, it's better to let each other go rather than suffering and causing further imbalance in your mind and doing even more unreliable and irreparable things. It is a man's duty to earn money and support the family, there is no need to boast, but it doesn't prevent you from caring for your wife. If you pay attention to her all the time, this green-eyed monster wouldn't have come into your life. Brother, you have been careless and hasty.

question: Many pieces of children's literature have been taken down. Where is the boundary for children's education?
description: Recently, there have been many children's literature books being taken down, as some of the content is deemed unsuitable for children. For example, it includes quarrels and name-calling among classmates. Setting aside inappropriate content, suicide, and other negative factors, can we incorporate real-life issues into children's education? Quarrels and name-calling are actually common occurrences in schools. If we give children a pristine world through books, does it truly benefit them in their real lives?

answers.answer_text: Can a negative social environment be caused by children's literature? Do books have such a function? There are very few children who actively choose to read children's literature books on their own - they are burdened with academics, attending various training classes, and busy with makeup classes. Where is the time to read? And how many parents are willing to buy books for their children? In certain foreign countries where literature is prevalent, they don't make such a big deal out of it, nor do they have the notion that books corrupt children, right? I'm afraid it's a group of people who have no investigations whatsoever, indulging in their own delusions and creating a "scapegoat"! Even if all children's literature works were banned, these phenomena would still continue to occur, repeatedly defying prohibition. Would they not be embarrassed then? I believe not, as they would just find a new "scapegoat". Nowadays, many children have smartphones, and a lot of the content they exchange with each other comes from online gaming conversations. The language used in these conversations is mostly vulgar, rude, violent, and even obscene. Additionally, while browsing online, if you are not careful, inappropriate images can pop up, as well as various adult novels and websites. At the same time, some parents, apart from handing over their children's education to school, simply use smartphones to occupy their children's time. Many times they can't even control their own mouths, resorting to scolding, insulting, suppressing, and filling their speech with obscenities. How can they expect their children to become pure angels? It's simply impossible.

Hello, recently there have indeed been a lot of news about children's literature being taken down, seemingly to create a "clean" world for children. However, these actions have caused a lot of questioning online because such treatment is indeed inappropriate. It's a perfunctory and one-size-fits-all behavior. When it comes to children's education, from books to practice, from principles to life, it has always been a relatively reliable method. It's better to let them know that the world has various hardships and then tell them that although there are various hardships, we can help each other and face these problems together. However, cutting literature off completely is like raising children in cotton, not knowing that the ground outside is hard and has pebbles. When they grow up, they will be thrown out to face the world directly. It's truly not an effective way to rectify the situation.

question: Is there any advantage or disadvantage to sexual desire?
description: Why is it that when sexual desire is used in the right context and manner, it is like honey, beneficial for physical and mental health, but when used in the wrong place or manner, it becomes poison, sometimes even poison disguised in a sweet candy coating, appearing pleasurable to the senses but harmful and unbeneficial to personal development and growth?

answers.answer_text: Hello! From a psychological perspective, Freud believed that the energy of human mental activity comes from instinct, which is the inner driving force that propels individual behavior. Instincts dominate individuals on an unconscious level and manifest in both normal and abnormal behavior. There are two basic types of instincts in humans: life instincts and death instincts or aggressive instincts. Life instincts include sexual instincts and individual survival instincts, aiming to maintain the procreation of the species and the individual's survival. Psychologists generally agree that sexual desire is one of the instincts of humans. We need to have a correct understanding of sexuality and approach it in the right way. As a natural instinct, sexual desire is actually unrelated to right or wrong. Therefore, whether it is good or bad depends on the choices made by the individual themselves. In intimate love and marriage, sexual activity is something very normal. The expression of sexual desire is also a part of love, so we find it very sweet. However, if sexual desire is used in inappropriate ways, it can become very difficult to accept. Because sex and love are often intertwined, if someone simply indulges in their sexual desires without love between individuals, this situation would also be morally unacceptable. Good luck!

Question asker, good evening! I am fortunate to come across this question, encounter your inquiry, and engage in inner reflection on it. Sexual desire, a product of ancient evolution inherent in the physical body, is neither good nor bad. It is the result of acquired cognition that gives it various colors. Today, while I was taking a walk, I was still thinking about which is higher and which is lower between the physical body and the mind. Could it be that the mind is nobler than the physical body? I once read a book called "The Selfish Gene." Where does the gene's selfishness manifest? It manifests in the endless pursuit of survival, replication, and reproduction. From this, one can infer that the true purpose of sexual desire is to ensure one's own survival. This is a realization that comes close to the original essence of life. When a person has already settled down, established a career, and even has offspring, is sexual desire still necessary? This becomes a struggle between intellect and genes. The only viable solution is to accept this composition. In fact, humans are inherently flawed. There are many suboptimal designs in the human body structure. Since humans themselves are imperfect, why strive for absolute freedom? (Unable to transcend sexual desire, from a different perspective, it can be sublimated into a higher desire for creation.) Let us explore together and heal the world!

Sexual desire is a biological instinct in humans, and without it, humans would not have survived to this day. So, you're asking whether sexual desire is good or not? However, since sexual desire is a type of desire, it needs to be considered from two aspects, intensity and direction. Firstly, excessive indulgence in sexual desires is definitely not good. If there is no sexual intimacy in a relationship, it is also not beneficial for the maintenance and development of the relationship, as Platonic love, after all, is idealistic. Secondly, if there is no proper direction for sexual desires, it may lead to deviations. It is clearly against morals if this occurs within a marriage. If it hasn't entered marriage yet, having multiple sexual partners may not be illegal or morally wrong, but it may cause inner psychological conflicts. As for the occasion and manner of sexual activities, in my understanding, the occasion should be more private and the manner should be acceptable to the partner. I'm not sure if my understanding and response are appropriate.

question: What can I do when I'm always anxious or excited and can't sleep before an exam?
description: Every time I encounter a big exam, I easily get excited the night before, thinking about different things and unable to control myself. As a result, I end up sleeping very late and the next day I feel tired, my thoughts are confused, and my reactions are slower than usual. Therefore, my grades also fluctuate.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, it seems like you feel that the exam is coming the next day and you've been thinking about it all the time. Many people might feel anxious and unable to sleep because they think they haven't prepared enough for the exam. But, in your case, it seems like you are excited and unable to sleep. This won't work, as not getting enough rest will affect your mental state the next day for sure. If your mental state is not good, how can you ensure that you will be able to take the exam properly? It is true that we should study well, but it is also important to prioritize our health. Learning is important, but taking care of our bodies is equally important, as our health comes first. Since the exam is the next day, regardless of how you have prepared, your grades are already set. So, don't think about anything, rest peacefully and make sure to take care of yourself. Good luck~.

question: Our relationship of eight years feels like it has reached its end...
description: Can't go back anymore! It's so sad, everything in the past makes people want to cry! It hurts deeply, meeting someone who doesn't understand me, both of us are so pitiful! His stubbornness cannot be changed, and I can't hold on to accommodating anymore! And there are two poor children, I love them, I can't bear to leave them!
keywords: Marriage, marriage concept, divorce, marriage management

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope the following answer can help you: 8 years of relationship have become the past, husband, children, family... all of these are difficult to let go of. However, as you said, "his stubbornness cannot be changed, and I can't accommodate it anymore!" Some things, some people, can never be changed. You have chosen to be yourself, which is a good choice from the perspective of self-growth, of course, it also requires courage. When your partner doesn't understand you and causes barriers or even hurts each other, it will eventually become unsustainable. Breaking up is a helpless choice and a necessary self-redemption. At the moment you made the decision, you must have felt that you were right. That's enough, at least you know what you are doing. As for the children, if parents can provide good care, they may actually grow up better than children who grow up in a strained relationship. In the future, they will understand their parents' choices. Even though you are not together, your love can still accompany them, right? I'm here, the world and I love you.

question: My mom has a bad temper, how to deal with others' bad temper?
description: My mother has a bad temper and scolds me in a blaming tone for everything I do. It is really annoying that nothing seems to meet her expectations. I have talked to her about it, but she doesn't care at all and I have to live in this environment every day. It is very stressful and I can't move out due to certain reasons. I don't know what to do.
keywords: Family, family relationships, and parental communication

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, everyone's temperament and nature are not easily changed. Patience in communication and understanding the needs and feelings of others while expressing your own feelings freely during interaction is important. From your description, I can feel your strong pain and helplessness when your mother always gets angry and blames you. On one hand, you have had unfruitful communication with her and her behavior continues to happen, and on the other hand, your emotions have accumulated to the point where you are about to explode and collapse. Take a serious look at why your mother gets angry. Is it because of her own character traits of irritability and restlessness, or is it because she is dissatisfied with what you do? Or perhaps she has some suppressed and evasive things in her heart that she projects onto you? Figure out these reasons, and then take action to make changes. If it is due to her character, you may need to consider the problem from her perspective. A temper built over decades cannot be changed overnight. When she is calm, you can teach her some methods to manage her emotions, and discuss and suggest them as a way of learning from each other, instead of making her feel like you are controlling and educating her, which can trigger her emotional outburst. Also, the next time she has an emotional outburst, you can accompany her in practicing the effectiveness of various methods. If it is because of something you have done, express your feelings about the matter. If it is indeed your fault, apologize sincerely. If it is not, let her know your emotions, your stress, and your way of looking at the problem. These are things that you must explain and communicate to her in the face of repeated blame. Do not be afraid of arguments and conflicts, as these allow us to see more aspects of each other and help us avoid arguments of the same kind in the future. If it is due to her own emotions, which she has not dealt with well and unconsciously projects onto you, you may need to listen better and guide her in expressing her feelings, providing care and firm support. Because parents are always silent, even if they have negative and negative things in their hearts, they think of us as their children and choose not to confide in us. When we earnestly look into their eyes and patiently accompany them, just ask, "Mom, has anything been bothering you recently? I can tell you're not feeling happy," they might feel warmth and love. Create more opportunities to have serious conversations with your mother, so that both of your feelings can be understood. Don't burden yourself and also see the suppressed emotions of your mother, gradually changing the way you interact. Mothers have also been daughters, and they may need us to become emotionally strong before they can rely on us. Best wishes.

question: I don't know why it has become like this now, and I don't know why I'm alive...
description: I don't know why I have become like this, fake, lazy, rebellious, and everyone dislikes me. My mother often says, "Why aren't you dead yet?" I also don't know why I am alive, what's the point of living? I'm afraid of pain, I'm afraid of the cold. I think, if I were dead, I wouldn't feel pain or cold anymore, right?
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, emotional regulation, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Thank you for the invitation, dear. Sending you a hug. The bolded texts are my responses to you. If you have any questions, you can contact me. Fake, lazy, rebellious, nobody likes me. I don't care about others, I want to know if you like yourself. My mom often says why don't you go die. Life comes into this world through a mother, the mother gives birth to the child, and unconsciously sees the child as a part of herself. When she feels powerless and resentful, she may say things like "death" to ease her own emotional stress. Life has many disappointments and pressures. Everyone has moments of powerlessness and hopes for a bit of rescue. When your mother says these words to you, she is actually asking for help. I apologize for burdening you, as you are already unable to handle your mother's emotions. I also don't know why I am alive, what is the meaning of being alive? Being alive means creating your own life. This is the ultimate question for everyone. We don't get to choose the family we are born into or the kind of parents we have. But when we start asking why we are alive, it means our life is entering a stage of self-creation. What kind of life do I hope for? How can I show my vitality? How do I want to experience happiness and joy in the future? PS: The stage of creation requires breaking through the limitations imposed by others in the past... it is the process of transforming from a cocoon into a butterfly. It's like the transformation from a caterpillar to a butterfly. 1. Stillness---seeing one's own current situation, including emotions, cognition, and beliefs. 2. Transformation---abandoning emotions, cognition, and beliefs that are incompatible with the present reality. 3. Breaking the cocoon---establishing new emotional patterns, beliefs, and behaviors... I'm afraid of pain, I'm afraid of the cold, I think, if I died, I wouldn't feel pain or cold anymore, right? I can't answer this here because I don't know the situation on the other side. If some stories are true, then the current situation should be the lesson in front of us. Instead of running away, it's better to face it well. Just like playing a game, if you don't pass a level, you start over and it's the same level. Only by passing the level can we experience the joy of victory. Life has hope. But are you willing to have a little patience and make efforts? And the process of making efforts requires enduring the pain of transformation. Do you have the courage to do that? Come on, be a warrior of life. Help will always be there, asking questions here is the beginning of help. The teachers here are all professionals. There are also corresponding activities and helplines. Best wishes.

question: I often doubt whether others' love for me is genuine, and I want to push away someone and end a relationship.
description: In intimate relationships, there is often a push-pull dynamic, especially during periods of conflict and disagreement. The more the other person seeks me, the more I resist. When the other person calms down and withdraws, I may feel the urge to provoke them again, hoping they will continue to seek me or try to reconcile. I feel like there's something wrong with me. Often, after investing myself in the relationship, I constantly think about pushing this person and the relationship away, wanting to go back to square one. I also frequently doubt whether this person truly loves me. I tend to magnify small details and think, "See, he doesn't love me or care about me." I silently keep track of these instances until they accumulate and eventually lead to a complete break. I don't know why I act this way. It's as if I am emotionally unstable and lack the ability to sustain a stable intimate relationship. I also believe that I can't hold onto any relationship.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, friends, and interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, the way you handle intimate relationships resembles the ambivalent attachment style in psychology. Ambivalent attachment is a type of insecure attachment that was discovered in the study of mother-infant relationships. It was proposed by American psychologist Ainsworth in 1978 based on the Strange Situation Test. Babies with this attachment style appear to be very vigilant when their mother is about to leave, and they become extremely distressed and resistant when the mother leaves, often crying loudly during even brief separations. However, when they are with their mother, they are unable to use her as a secure base for exploration. When the mother returns, their attitude toward her is conflicting, as they seek contact with her while also resisting it. They may get angry and push her away when she comes close. It seems difficult for them to return to playing games, as they frequently look towards the mother. (Information sourced from Baidu Baike) The attachment style established between an infant and their mother in early stages of development is often replicated in adult intimate relationships. Therefore, in your description, I see elements of the "the more someone pursues me, the less I agree" pattern and the desire to provoke the other person after they have calmed down or stepped back, to make them continue pursuing or to maintain the posture of retention. Furthermore, you often push away this person and the relationship over minor things, wanting to go back to square one, and frequently doubting whether this person truly loves you, often magnifying small details. These characteristics all appear to resemble the ambivalent attachment pattern. It seems that deep within your heart, there is a hidden belief: a lack of belief in being loved. To prove this belief, you try every possible way to collect "evidence" that this person doesn't love you enough, and unconsciously sabotage the relationship again and again. To improve these beliefs and establish a secure attachment style, it is recommended that you seek psychological counseling if conditions permit.

Hey, OP. After reading your description, I want to give you a hug. It seems that your current pattern of dealing with problems traces back to your childhood, and it's likely that you have developed an ambivalent attachment style. This might be because, when you were young, your parents' care and comfort were not consistent, or their own unstable emotions affected you, causing inner instability. As a result, your relationship with caregivers became contradictory - you wanted closeness but also feared it, and even when close, you still felt unsafe. Early attachment patterns can indeed influence adult intimate relationships, often leading to a repetition of the past attachment patterns with partners. However, we cannot go back to childhood, and it's important to acknowledge that our parents also had their difficulties at that time. Blaming them excessively now serves no purpose. What we can do is focus on managing our current emotions, gradually stabilizing and feeling safe within ourselves. When we are caught in an ambivalent attachment style, our right brain becomes overly active, making it easy for emotions to overwhelm us, just like you mentioned - a small detail can be blown out of proportion and accumulate until it bursts. Therefore, it's crucial to learn how to manage our emotions. Here are some suggestions for you: 1. Cultivate the ability to recognize your inner emotional states. "Recognize it, tame it" is the first step toward building language capabilities in the left brain and linking them with more primitive, spontaneous emotions in the right brain. You can simply describe your feelings without having to explain them. 2. Keeping a journal can be very helpful for you. By using our left brain to tell a linear, logical, and language-based story about our lives, we can connect and integrate the left and right hemispheres of the brain. 3. Understand your emotions. Remember that emotions are not facts. This will help you categorize and organize your intense and rapid internal emotional world. For example, feeling rejected activates the same neural circuitry in the right brain as feeling physical pain. Once you understand this, you can use the "recognize it, tame it" method to acknowledge the pain of feeling rejected, but also realize that it's not necessarily true. By reflecting on it, you can restore calmness within yourself. 4. As your left brain continues to develop and collaborate closely with the right brain, explore how you can engage in more satisfying interactions with close relationships. Always remember that regardless of the emotions that arise, they are not facts. Sometimes, you might be overly sensitive to signals from others, allowing their emotions to impact you and lose your sense of self. At other times, your own internal feelings might make you feel unable to rely on others, although this assessment may be accurate, it can also be interfered with by an overly active attachment system. To feel safe, an overactive attachment system is highly vigilant about emotional connections. At such times, it's necessary to first understand your own psychology, empathize with others, understand their psychology, and then integrate, using the brain to combine different aspects into an internally connected whole. 5. An attachment relationship can feel like a matter of life and death. When we were very young, we relied on parents or other caregivers for food, water, and protection... If those who took care of us were unpredictable and uncertain, then when we enter adolescence or adulthood and stressful events occur in our lives, we feel very afraid and believe that no one can protect us, sometimes even feeling like our lives are at stake. Understanding this can be very helpful for you in identifying this feeling and not letting it consume you. 6. Strengthen your ability to observe your inner self. When you realize that past confusing or violently angry experiences were not because of any problem on your part but rather reflected emotional communication between you and your caregivers, you will be able to see that your current emotional responses are just echoes of the past. Allow the inner observer to provide you emotional space through narrating the course of events, so that your inner self becomes calm and you can see what is happening more clearly. Transformation is a process, so take it slow. It will get better over time (*￣︶￣*).

Dear OP, hello. From your description, it can be seen that you are very conflicted. You desire intimacy, but at the same time, you are afraid and want to push away. You hope that the other person will constantly pursue you and be in a state of chasing you in order to make you feel safe. Once conflicts arise, you want to escape, and if you return to the starting point, everything will be peaceful and beautiful, and these contradictions will no longer exist. In the process of getting along with the other person, you start from the conclusion of "he doesn't love me" and constantly gather evidence that he doesn't love you. Dear, do you feel tired in such a relationship? I have also been in a stage like yours, constantly worrying and doubting whether the other person loves me. I would blow a small thing out of proportion, while the other person's intentions are actually good. What the world lacks is not love but the eyes to see love. When we are in such a state, try to imagine that the other person is also tired. They have to constantly put aside their dignity and plead, and the love they give is constantly questioned and denied. First, you need to think about whether you love him. If you do, do you feel sorry for him being so tired? Can you consider his perspective? Monica and Chandler from the classic American sitcom "Friends" are a couple I really like, and their relationship is enviable. Chandler, due to a difficult childhood, has always lacked a sense of security. After a big fight with Monica, he used to say to her, "I think we're done?" Monica was very surprised and asked, "What? Why?" Chandler said, "Because we just had a big fight." Monica found it unbelievable and said, "A fight doesn't mean it's over." Chandler foolishly felt relieved and asked, "Really?!" Monica gave him a hug and said, "Welcome to the world of adult love." I also want to introduce you to a new world of adult love. A mismatched communication or an uncomfortable experience does not mean that the other person doesn't love you or that the relationship should end. Even now, when conflicts arise, I still feel uneasy and want to push away from this relationship. But there is another voice in my heart telling me that this is not a mature mindset. Dealing with conflicts and solving the problem itself in a positive way is the mature thing to do. What you say about him not loving you or not caring about you is just your perception, not the reality itself. What you feel is based on how you interpret the facts. I have a friend whose husband is a bit reserved and not very romantic, but she thinks it's great. Sometimes, engineer-type guys need to be guided, and she is naturally romantic, so they can complement each other. Why not change your perspective and look for the small details of how he loves you? I believe there are many. Wishing you happiness.

In other words, you don't want to be "trapped" in intimate relationships. Therefore, you don't seek to understand, learn, or develop methods for maintaining a stable intimate relationship. What you desire in a relationship is respect, maintaining distance, and preserving individual lives without interfering with each other's choices. When personal choices conflict with the stability of the relationship, personal choices take precedence over the other person's need for relationship stability. This is just my speculation, so it may not apply to you. Assuming my speculation is correct, you have taken the following actions to assert a dominant position in the relationship in order to fulfill your needs. "In an intimate relationship, there is often a push-and-pull dynamic, especially during conflicts and disagreements. The more the other person seeks me, the less I am willing to agree. When the other person calms down and withdraws, I may feel the desire to provoke them again, to make them continue to pursue me or maintain a stance of retention." "After investing myself in the relationship, I often find myself wanting to push away this person and the relationship after a disharmonious conversation, an uncomfortable experience, or even a small thing. I often doubt whether this person truly loves me. I tend to magnify small details and think to myself, 'See, he doesn't love me or care about me.' I silently keep these thoughts in mind until they accumulate and eventually explode, leading to a complete departure." I don't have any specific suggestions if my speculation is correct. You can choose to accept yourself in this way, face your needs, and seek someone who can accept this type of relationship (you may need to search worldwide). Of course, it is difficult to find such a person. They need to understand your worldview and be willing to break free from existing moral and universal values. They should be willing to try this kind of relationship and stand with you against societal constraints. However, be prepared for the possibility that they may revert to the common societal norms. Of course, I might be wrong, and you may have a different state of mind. Is there any misunderstanding about intimate relationships? You can choose to believe that a relationship can evolve into the state you imagine. Believe that two people can establish a stable relationship and that there are people who genuinely love you. Control your doubts about whether the other person loves you and base them on concrete evidence rather than subjective speculations... Of course, the cost is that you have to work hard to convince yourself to believe in the above content and to resist your inner self. Convince yourself to try this in every relationship and withstand it for a period of time (at least a observation period of no less than 3 months) before it can be considered as valid evidence. Of course, you can also choose to maintain the current situation, continue to repeat such behavior until you get bored, and then choose one of the two above options to try. There are other choices as well. If you are willing to provide more information, we can continue the discussion.

Hello~ It seems like you're caught in a "self-fulfilling prophecy" cycle as you enter into intimate relationships, repeatedly proving that the other person doesn't love you. This is a worrisome and changeable pattern of interaction. Self-fulfilling prophecy is a common phenomenon in psychology, which means that people unconsciously act in accordance with known prophecies, ultimately making the prophecies come true. It also means that expectations of others can influence their behavior, causing them to act according to those expectations. "I often doubt whether this person really loves me. I magnify every small detail and say to myself, 'See, he just doesn't love me...' And this often becomes the ending of the story." "Everyone has their own script of destiny," and sometimes we unconsciously act according to our own scripts, making the same mistakes over and over again. I suggest that you seek psychological counseling to understand your patterns of interaction in intimate relationships and, guided by appropriate methods, change yourself to gain a sense of security in your intimate relationships. Best wishes~.

From your description, it seems that you really enjoy being pampered, being paid attention to the details, and pursuing the absolute perfection in your ideal. However, in reality, finding someone who can completely pamper you and revolve around you, reaching the state of perfection, is almost impossible. Even if you search for 10,000 people, you may not find one. Do you really want to continue searching like this? If your goal is to prove that a perfect lover exists in this world, then you can do that. But if your goal is to live a happy life, then I suggest you adjust your expectations: find someone who can pamper you most of the time, and allow some arguments with them on certain issues. They should show their care for you on important occasions like birthdays, illnesses, and understanding your feelings, etc. However, don't get too caught up if they occasionally forget to reply to you when they are shopping, drinking with friends, or getting engrossed in a game. It won't be easy in the beginning, for sure. Your emotions may take over your mind. But if we don't overcome and ignore our emotions, we will forever be prisoners of our emotions, right? After all, emotions are never-ending, only reason can bring true value.

Dear, hello. Seeing your description, I seem to see your helpless appearance in an intimate relationship. Please give yourself a loving hug. In daily life, many people have not formed healthy attachment relationships. In your relationship, you desire to be in an advantageous position, which may also be a manifestation of a lack of security. In love, it is not about who wins or loses, but about being able to promote each other's growth in the relationship. Perhaps you have been influenced by your family and feel that you are unable to keep someone, and in the end, anyone may leave you. Such beliefs will affect your thoughts and make you anxious about always losing, which will create more doubts. Whenever you discover something that aligns with your thoughts and coincidentally verifies your doubts, you will fall into a cycle. I think the best way is to honestly tell him your feelings, be your true self, and communication based on trust will promote the relationship. Lastly, be confident in yourself, recognize and believe in yourself, and be the best version of yourself. If you bloom, the gentle breeze will come. Best wishes!

Hello! I accidentally pressed "Complete" before finishing, and the content was already published. I don't know how to edit it, so I'm starting again. In my previous answer, I mentioned that you seem to be playing a love game. How do you feel about it? Playing this kind of game too often can make both parties feel tired and even resentful. Do you agree? From an attachment perspective, there may be some contradictions in your attachment relationship with your parents, especially with your mother, which makes you both want to get close and afraid to get close. The love given by your parents may make you feel conditional love. In adulthood, many intimate relationships often repeat the relationship with parents, making it difficult for you to determine whether the other person truly loves you in an intimate relationship, so you repeatedly use this push-pull method to confirm this love. Is it like this? From a cognitive perspective, you may have a belief in your heart that "I am not lovable". When this belief is triggered, you may feel pain and unease, and you try to prove your loveability through this push-pull method. Is it like this? If my guesses have offended you, please forgive me. If you really want to build a sincere and loving intimate relationship, you may need some time for psychological counseling to explore yourself and your relationships.

"Often doubting whether this person truly loves me" may seem like doubting others, but in essence, it's not believing in oneself, not believing that one is worthy of being loved. So no matter how much the other person loves you, it's useless because you don't believe it. At the same time, precisely because of this lack of belief (unwillingness to accept that nobody loves you), there is a greater longing to be truly loved, not tolerating any mistreatment. If you want to improve your ability to enter into intimate relationships, it is recommended to seek systematic counseling and allow yourself to grow in the capacity to love and be loved.

question: What should be done if a child has poor mental resilience and gets nervous when it comes to crucial moments in a competition?
description: When my child is playing badminton, they become nervous and lose their original level when they encounter opponents who are about the same skill level, especially when there is only one point difference. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, when I saw your question, it immediately reminded me of my time in my final year of high school. During my senior year, I started living at home as I used to live with my relatives because it was closer to school. When I started living at home during my senior year, I would play table tennis with my father a few times a week. If I won, I would get a reward, but if I lost, I had to clean the house. Maybe because my father and I had similar table tennis skills, we would often play 7 games and it would usually come down to 10-10 or 9-10. Winning meant getting a reward, but losing meant having to clean the house, which was a tiring task since I had to squat and clean. So, I really didn't want to lose. During that time, my father would sometimes play unfairly, but I didn't really care, I just needed to win one more point. The main thing was not to let it affect my mindset. Maybe it was because of this constant challenge that on the day of my college entrance exam, I encountered unexpected problems in the math section. I didn't answer three major questions, but I was still able to handle it and concentrate on the other subjects for the exam the next day, thanks to my consistent performance in those subjects. Ultimately, I achieved a good score. I'm sharing this story with you to say that every child's growth opportunity might be different. What parents can do is patiently wait and be there for their children. Secondly, encourage them when they do things right. Although I don't think my father's way of encouragement can exactly be called encouragement, back then I really just wanted to win because I disliked cleaning the house. Maybe it indirectly motivated me to win. Lastly, encouragement doesn't necessarily have to be related to table tennis. Encouragement in other areas of life, through other small things, can also boost a child's confidence and influence their performance in table tennis, even in the final point. Finally, encourage reading, especially biographies of famous people. I used to read a lot of books about famous people and discovered how many of them overcame adversity in their lives. I would think about how to overcome my own challenges. In my heart, I developed a mindset of not being afraid of losing. Gradually, it started to affect my studies and daily life.

Hello there~ Nervousness may be due to poor mental resilience, but for children, this is very normal. Improving a person's mental resilience is not an overnight process. It primarily requires their own initiative to want to improve, while others can only guide. Don't place too much importance on the outcome, allow yourself to lose, allow yourself to fail. Being too concerned with gains and losses will make one worry excessively and add a lot of pressure. As a parent, you should tell them that it's okay to lose, as long as they try their best. Hone oneself through repeated competitions. This is the most direct and effective method. You should encourage them to have an objective view of the competition results, to objectively assess their own growth, and not judge success or failure based on the outcome. Encourage them to value the process more than the result, to prioritize attitude over winning or losing. Read countless books, travel thousands of miles, and help them find their life's value and the things that can give them strength. Take it slow. Best wishes~.

question: My mother tells me every day that I am fat. How should I adjust my mindset?
description: I am 160 centimeters tall and weigh 108 catties, which makes me slightly chubby with a pear-shaped body. I was chatting with my colleague about weight, and she said that because I have a small frame and a small face, I don't look fat, but I'm not very thin either. However, my mom keeps on criticizing me every single day. As soon as I get home from work, she starts saying things like, "Why are you so fat? Look at your legs and your double chin. Who would want you like this?" (I have a boyfriend, and she seems pretty satisfied with him.) Today, after I finished eating and had a drink, she saw and said, "One day you will be killed by being overweight," speaking very definitively. I have had this weight for about four or five years now (before that, I was always very thin, around 90 catties, but I gained weight after falling in love), and she has been saying these things to me for four or five years. It's not an exaggeration to say that she says it every day. But the problem is, she is a little bit shorter than me and about 20 catties heavier than me. So why does she still act like I'm extraordinarily fat? I have told her before, "Can you please stop talking about me? I will lose weight if I feel fat." But then she starts making sarcastic comments, and she refuses to have a proper conversation with me; she only wants to say whatever pleases her. I'm frustrated every day, and if she keeps going on like this, I might go crazy.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, family control

answers.answer_text: Hello, when I saw your question, I felt like I found another version of myself. It's truly the same world and the same maternal figure, dear friend. Beauty in this world should not be limited to just one form. Different body types have their own beauty, whether it's being curvy or slim, each has its own charm. I hope you can understand this. Other people's definition of you does not fully represent who you are. Your beauty should not only be defined by being "slim". I have also been through similar experiences as a woman, and I hope my answer can provide you with some advice and warmth. First, your body shape is not really that bad. Everyone has a different perception of weight and body size. According to your description: (1) your body proportions are within the healthy range. With a height of 160cm and a weight of 108 catties (approximately 120 pounds), to be honest, you are not considered overweight at all. Your weight-to-height ratio is very healthy, and this body shape will not put a great burden on your body. (2) Although your weight and height are normal, your body shape may not be ideal. You have a slightly pear-shaped body. The thing to understand is that there is a difference between "body shape" and "body weight". Some people may not weigh much (108 catties for someone who is 160cm is not considered heavy), but they may lack the effort to shape their own body. For example, if you often look down at your phone with your head lowered, it can lead to wrinkles on your chin and neck. For example, if you frequently slouch and don't straighten your back, it can lead to a hunched back. Actually, you are not really fat, but your body shape needs some adjustment. (3) Having a small face is an advantage. It doesn't appear fat, but if you don't learn how to enhance yourself and improve your temperament, even a small face like yours can appear chubby. Based on your description, your colleague mentioned that because of your small bone structure and face, you don't look fat, but you are also not considered very thin. In other words, your problem is not really about your weight, but rather about your self-image. The desire for beauty is something everyone has. Every woman, regardless of height or weight, hopes to have her own unique charm in the eyes of others. As a girl, you shouldn't belittle yourself. Second, your psychological issues don't really stem from your weight, but rather from the emotional and love-related traumas you have experienced. True beauty comes from within. I hope you can find the root cause of why you are being belittled in front of your mother. Only then can you overcome the psychological shadows she has caused you. (1) Reason one: Your mother is imposing her aesthetic standards on you, making you feel guilty. To be honest, your mother has indeed hurt you. Even though our parents rarely engage in self-reflection, they may even believe that being critical of their children is a form of love. But why does your mother care so much about your weight? It is very likely that she herself is someone who is very focused on her own body shape. Even if you have one extra drink, your mother will respond with a decisive remark that has a negative impact on you. Because in your mother's heart, she has an invisible expectation for you. She wants you to become slim and beautiful just like her ideal, and she may even hope that you can fulfill her unfulfilled dreams of being slender. But we cannot live in our parents' fantasies forever. Even though we are born and raised by our parents, it does not mean that we are their possessions. You have your own aesthetic sense, your own world. And this is something your mother doesn't understand. (2) Reason two: The biggest fear of every mother who has a daughter is to see her child get hurt in relationships. Whether your mother's messages are reminders or strikes, they actually stem from her unconscious fear of losing you. I have experienced gaining weight while being in love. When two people in a relationship enjoy eating, drinking, and having fun together, the happy calories inevitably increase. Even though I weighed around 80 pounds at that time, after being in a relationship, I gained weight and reached 100 pounds. At that time, I was actually happy, as my partner (my ex now) always said that a slightly overweight girl is cute. But mothers who have experienced the vicissitudes of life have even more crisis awareness. They fear that you will lose yourself in love, neglect your own appearance, and end up becoming unattractive due to being caught up in a hazy love. They fear that if you become overweight due to love, you will be hurt by the other person. They fear that you will be immersed in love and forget the discipline of self-control that a girl should maintain. And their biggest fear is that once you fall in love, you will no longer care about her. At this moment, a mother feels lonely. Actually, your mother has always used various forms of criticism, strikes, and sometimes even hurtful words because she has a sense of "crisis". She fears that once you have someone you like, you will no longer care about her. In this world, she genuinely cares about you. However, she has chosen the wrong approach. I hope you don't resent your mother excessively. If possible, I hope you can see yourself through your mother's eyes. You will discover that beneath the teasing and hurtful words, there is her grievances. Third, my mom criticizes me for being fat every day. How can I adjust my mindset? I would like to provide the following suggestions. When you understand why your mother treats you this way, perhaps you can learn to reconcile with her. It can also be an opportunity for you to become a better, more independent, and confident person. Suggestion one: Open and honest communication will always make a difference in resolving conflicts with family members rather than resorting to passive aggression. Share your feelings with your mom. In fact, mothers are also women. Mothers also have strong self-esteem, so they have their own pride. At times like this, instead of having a cold war or arguing with your mother, it's better to find an opportunity to sit down calmly and have a heart-to-heart conversation. Your mother worries about your weight and fears you will be hurt in relationships. You need to let your mother know that no matter who you become in the future, whether as a wife or a mother, you will always be the daughter who loves her. You want to give her peace of mind, so you also need to earn her trust. Through parent-child communication, let down your guard against each other. Let your mother know that you have grown up and some of her words have hurt your self-esteem. Only with mutual understanding can you avoid conflicts. Suggestion two: If you want to improve your relationship with your mother, you need to learn to be tolerant and patient. Mothers also need to be comforted. They say a kind word can warm you in the winter, but a hurtful word can make you feel cold in June. We must acknowledge that your mother actually has some personality problems, and when you face her criticism, you may feel pain. The pain produces anxiety in both parties, which is not conducive to your psychological well-being. Your mother must have a straightforward personality and sometimes speaks without considering the feelings of the listener. So, when your mother keeps nagging, you can choose to mentally "drift away." Maybe she's just having a bad day or lost money while playing cards, or she's upset because the groceries were more expensive. She just wants to vent her frustrations by picking on you. In these moments, do not argue with her. You can try nodding, smiling in silence, or even giving her a warm hug. My own mother often scolds me, even now that she's past her fifties, her words often make me sad. But I know that parents endure many grievances in their own world. So, when she is unhappy, I would go out and buy her a bunch of her favorite red roses. When she is in a bad mood, I would give her a beautiful lipstick. Even though she still speaks harshly, I would tell her that I will work hard to lose weight and not let myself become overweight. At this point, she won't say anything further because she knows she has received my warmth. Suggestion three: Being a pear-shaped woman doesn't necessarily mean you should feel inferior. Learn to dress up and make yourself even more beautiful! I am also a pear-shaped woman, with wide shoulders and hips. Even if my weight does not increase, I always feel like the clothes I wear are not flattering enough. In reality, there are no "ugly" girls in this world, only lazy girls. It requires effort on your part. My suggestions are: (1) You must learn to enhance your appearance and compensate for any shortcomings through clothing. Improve your fashion sense. You can watch videos by fashionable bloggers to learn about different clothing styles that suit you. Find out which hairstyle and accessories suit you. You will discover that even pear-shaped girls can showcase their own sense of style. (2) Learn to accentuate your strengths and avoid focusing on weaknesses. Maintain a basic skincare routine and regularly hydrate and cleanse your face. If possible, treat yourself to a full-body beauty spa once a month. It can help you relax and improve your skin quality, delaying the aging process. (3) Beauty comes from self-discipline. I hope you can improve your confidence by shaping yourself. As a working woman, your life is busy. Modern society puts more pressure on women, and work worries, daily trivialities, and family conflicts can make you feel exhausted. So, when you are in love, it's easy for us to neglect self-management. However, self-discipline will result in a higher quality of life. Therefore, no matter how busy life gets, I hope you do not neglect self-care. Consider joining a dance class, yoga class, or trying out a gym. Persist in doing some aerobic exercises, such as running, on a weekly basis. Cultivate good habits of going to bed and waking up early. Only by doing so, will you earn more respect and praise. Fourth, a woman's confidence comes from within. Only you can define your own beauty. Regardless of your age or weight, as long as you are willing, you can radiate your own unique charm. Don't lose yourself because of others' opinions. Adjust your mindset, live seriously, and know that you deserve all the happiness. Thank you for reading. Feel free to like and follow me.

Hug you, dear OP, it must be really difficult for you to live under your mother's criticism every day! #My mom calls me fat every day, how should I adjust my mindset? In fact, a survey once showed that only 20% of people are satisfied with their body shape, and among women, only 4% are satisfied with their own body shape. Everyone may have more or less expectations, and your mother may be the same. Although she thinks she is doing it for your own good, these "nagging" words make us feel uncomfortable. It's like a story I once heard; a wife loves her husband very much and would cut apples and put toothpicks in them every day, waiting for him to eat. But the husband doesn't like apples at all, so he said to his wife, "Are you crazy? Why do you peel apples for me every day?" The wife feels very wronged, "I love you so much, I peel the apples for you every day, why do you criticize me like this?" However, the wife didn't realize that the husband hates eating apples. Sometimes people in life will do the same, they will say things that make us uncomfortable in the name of love. But we cannot deny that they care about us, it's just that their way of showing it is not what we want. Actually, we have grown up and can take responsibility for our own choices and actions. At such times, excessive interference from parents in our lives will make us feel like we have lost our boundaries. If you violate my boundaries, then I won't be myself anymore, and naturally, I will feel uncomfortable. For words like this, perhaps all we need to know is that they care about us, but they have used the wrong method. Just let it go, and then tell them, "I know you want what's best for me, thank you for your concern, but I am already an adult who can take responsibility for my own actions. But still, thank you." After all, we are all adults now.

Hug you (づ￣▽￣)づ It must be really difficult for you to have a mother who constantly belittles you, undermines you, constantly nitpicks, and can't communicate with you. Hug you. Actually, your figure is very good, not fat at all. The dearest mother who should love you, care for you, and cherish you, actually criticizes her daughter like this. Even if you have a correct understanding of yourself, it is still inevitable to be sad.■ What was your attachment relationship with your mother like when you were a child? ■ What is your mother's personality like? ■ Does she treat others the same way she treats you? Don't be sad.1. {She's a little shorter than me and about 20 pounds heavier than me, but why does she still say I'm so fat.} Your mother is so concerned about your figure that based on her own condition, she must be very dissatisfied with her own figure.■ "Projection effect" refers to the tendency to attribute one's own characteristics to others. In cognition and forming impressions of others, people assume that others have similar traits to themselves, projecting their own emotions, wills, and characteristics onto others and imposing them on others, which is a cognitive obstacle of pushing oneself onto others.
