"Projection makes people perceive others according to what kind of person they are, rather than perceiving them according to the true situation of the observed person." (Baidu) Your mother is not just scolding you, but also herself, her dissatisfaction with her own figure is hidden in her subconscious. Your mother is actually very insecure about her own figure, but she wants to maintain her "dominant" dominance in front of her daughter, so she always sees (projects) her own shortcomings in your gradual weight gain. The emotions resulting from her dissatisfaction with her figure are vented through verbal attacks on you. Therefore, she won't communicate with you in a good way, she has to say it to feel relieved.2. {As soon as I get home, she starts saying how fat I am, look at your legs and double chin, who would want you (I have a boyfriend, she is quite satisfied with that kind).} Seeing this, I can't help but be curious about your father and mother's relationship, whether your father has ever despised your mother's figure. But what can be certain is that your mother worries that she will be rejected or abandoned by her boyfriend after she becomes fat. She is afraid that you will continue to gain weight and become like her. Is this a kind of love from your mother? If she didn't love you, she would be more likely to let you continue to gain weight and not care about you. It's just that her approach has changed from persuasion to verbal attacks, which hurts you. 3. {I have had this weight for about four or five years (four or five years ago, I used to be very thin, around 90 pounds, but gained weight after falling in love), and she has been saying this to me for four or five years, not an exaggeration, every day.} According to research, being in love does make it easy for people to gain weight. However, is your mother worried about your growth, your future, and the loss of self in love? 4. {In addition to calling me fat, she also suppresses me in other ways, in her eyes, I have no shining points.} Hug you~ being oppressed by your mother all the time, you must have lived a very stifled life. Every word your mother says stabs you like a knife, breaking your heart over and over again. But you must believe in yourself, you have shining points of your own.■ (My mother often disapproves of me too, often scolds me in rough language. I also often think that she can't see my strengths, she doesn't trust me, she doesn't believe in my abilities. But we love each other. She just wants me to become better and more outstanding.) Also, I want to ask, how do you evaluate your mother? Does your mother have any shining points in your eyes? You mentioned your grandmother in the quiet comments, was your grandmother the reason for your mother's transformation? ■ Verbal expression doesn't work with your mother. Have you tried written communication? Would written expression be better? Write a letter or send a message to your mother. ■ When writing, writing or typing will give your brain more time to think, so that your mother will no longer be influenced by projection effects and can calmly consider her own language. ■ (What can you do when your mother belittles you? Of course, forgive her. Invite your mother to lose weight together. Make vegetable salads together, eat together, go for a run together. Let your mother know that you are taking practical actions to lose weight, not just talking. Wishing you and your mother can solve problems together and make progress together! The world and I love you.)

Sometimes it's not our fault, and we can't calm ourselves down no matter how much we try to adjust. It's clear that the OP's mother is verbally attacking them, and I think it's important for you to have a serious conversation with your mother and let her know that her words are hurting you, and ask her to stop. If she continues to say hurtful things, then you need to distance yourself from her for the sake of your mental and physical health. Some people are just very negative and can find fault in anything, and they don't even realize that they're hurting others. Their words are irrational and purely emotional venting. There are so many truly overweight people in the world, does everyone have someone in their life who dislikes them for being overweight? Even if you succeed in losing weight, she might still criticize your salary or your boyfriend's looks, and so on. You will never be able to meet the demands of such people. But that's not our problem. We need the courage to separate ourselves from these people and surround ourselves with those who value and respect us. Give your mother a few chances, but in your heart, you need to have a sense of how long this situation can continue. After a few chances, you need to make it clear where you stand and move out to protect your emotions. For now, try to keep your distance from her and reduce the time you spend with her. If reasoning with her isn't possible, then you can only avoid her. Then actively plan your own life, because in the future, you will be living with your partner, not with your mother for the rest of your life. You can move out first and have your own life. Once you become independent, you'll have a voice, and the distance between you two won't be so close, so her temper should become more restrained. Keep going, because we all need to grow up and not be trapped in the gloom of a negative family forever. Give yourself some patience and time, and believe that you deserve a better life and people.

Do you have any evidence to prove that being fat is the most reliable? Marked: The normal range of body fat ratio for Chinese women is 20 to 25. With a height of 160 cm and a weight of 54 kg, according to the BMI calculation method in our country, your body fat ratio is 21.1, which is considered normal and slightly thin. Therefore, your mother's statement has no factual basis and therefore lacks credibility. Let's take a look at the pear-shaped body type. According to Zhihu: Chinese name - pear-shaped body, English name - pear shape, target group - women with narrow shoulders, slim waist, wide hips, and full thighs. Advantages - helps prevent diabetes and promote longevity. The narrow shoulders are visually slimming, and the full hips not only reflect healthy reproductive ability but also highlight the slim waist, showing feminine beauty. It looks thin while still having some flesh. It cannot be determined whether it can prevent diabetes, but from the perspective of a healthy body shape, longevity seems plausible. Now, you can properly accept your body shape and figure. As for your mother's baseless talk, it's just her own complaint. Just listen to it and let it go with a graceful smile. Relax and enjoy the health of your body and the happiness of love. If you are concerned about the pear-shaped body and worried about the perceived imperfections based on prevailing aesthetic standards, there are various ways to enhance visual effects through clothing, such as avoiding tight-fitting pants, wearing high-waisted pencil skirts, fitted dresses, and slim tops with wide-legged pants, which can both lengthen the body proportion and showcase a graceful and sexy figure.

Hello, I've seen your troubles and hope to be able to help you. From your description, it's clear that your mom is extremely concerned about your weight and figure, and she mentions it almost every day, which has caused you a lot of pressure. I truly understand your feelings and emotions. Let's try to adjust and improve from several aspects: First, understanding your mom's anxiety. What is the reason behind her putting so much energy into focusing on your weight? Is her constant emphasis on this matter to some extent a reflection of her anxiety? What is it that truly makes her anxious? Is there a personal reason for her, and is your weight just a topic she borrowed? Or is this truly her way of expressing her concern for you? Or is it that some inner needs of hers haven't been fulfilled? Similar to the example "Your mom thinks you're cold," your mom thinking you're fat might also be a reflex of habitually wanting control. Some things that seem like her dissatisfaction with you may actually be her dissatisfaction with herself… Carefully consider these questions and try to look at this matter from a different perspective; you will gain new understanding and knowledge about your mom, which may alleviate your resistance to some extent. Secondly, have a correct perception of yourself. The reason your mom's nagging makes you feel pressured is probably because what she says is also what you care about. If you truly care, then put more energy into actually executing weight loss, don't let anxious emotions carry you away, as excessive pressure can also lead to weight gain. Try telling your mom that you understand her good intentions and hope she can help you find more effective methods for weight loss instead of adding more pressure. Thirdly, encourage your mom to establish her own social circle. If your mom has more hobbies and her own social circle, her excessive focus on you will be reduced. Try helping your mom cultivate meaningful and beneficial hobbies, so she can direct more attention back to herself. Increase the expression of your care, try to change the pattern of negation between each other, and learn to establish positive emotional interactions through warm language. It can also help both you and her overcome anxiety. If you can't change others, then strive to become a better version of yourself. Wishing you new achievements every day.

In this society where thinness is considered beautiful, being called fat is like an attack for girls. It is being criticized for not being good enough, not beautiful enough, even though you are not actually fat. Being constantly criticized and blamed by the closest person to you, your own mother, it must be really difficult for you. Maybe when your mother criticizes you, it's not because there is something you need to correct, but because she herself has some unresolved issues or emotions. From your description, I have a feeling that you are like a scapegoat, bearing what your mother cannot bear herself. Maybe she is not satisfied with herself, especially if she is overweight, and she doesn't want or doesn't have the ability to change it. So, she channels this dissatisfaction, criticism, and blame onto you, because it is easier to blame others than to reflect on oneself. Perhaps your mother herself has always been criticized, belittled, or grew up in a habitual blaming family, so she has learned this communication style. Another possibility is that you have obtained something that your mother wants but cannot have, so she is happy for you on one hand, but unconsciously jealous and unconsciously attacks you on the other. Maybe your boyfriend perfectly fits the type that your mother is satisfied with, while your father currently doesn't meet her expectations. Your current relationship might trigger many associations for her. Daughters are spiritually connected with their mothers, so try to understand the reasons behind your mother's constant criticisms. Maybe then you can find a way to resolve the issue. Being constantly criticized is uncomfortable, and arguing back is often ineffective. You can try giving her positive feedback instead. For example, if she says you are fat, you can respond, "Mom, do you want me to be prettier?" Break the cycle of blame, praise your mother at the right time, and encourage her to learn how to praise instead of learning how to criticize from you.

Dear questioner, hello! I'm glad to be able to help you with your questions, and I hope my answer can be of assistance to you. [Question] 1) The mother feels that the questioner is overweight, so she always brings up the issue of weight. [My analysis] 1) Based on the description of the questioner's own situation, this body proportions cannot be considered overweight at all. If you insist on becoming as skinny as a celebrity, it will actually harm your health. So, the questioner must not overly worry about whether their weight is overweight. 2) You have maintained this weight for nearly four to five years, and your mother has been commenting on it for that same length of time. The questioner mentioned that their mother is even more overweight than them by over twenty catties. Perhaps that is why she wants her daughter to achieve the body image that she desires. However, things in life are unpredictable, and not everything will go as desired. What you need to do is to strive to change your mother's mistaken thinking. 3) The questioner already has a boyfriend who is satisfied with their weight, so you have found someone who accepts you despite your imperfections. This is happiness! [My advice] 1) Work together with your boyfriend to communicate with your mother. Let your mother understand the importance of being healthy before being beautiful. The so-called health means that the weight and height ratio meets the BM international health standards. Then, tell your mother that your body is under your own control, and she shouldn't impose requirements on you that you cannot meet. This way, both parties can coexist harmoniously. Since we are destined to be mother and daughter, why can't we enjoy the fate of meeting each other? Merely lecturing and criticizing will never solve the problem, but only create greater conflicts. 2) Take some time apart from each other and open up your hearts to have a sincere conversation. If you don't want to talk face to face, you can express your grievances through WeChat or other text messages. Then, spend some time apart from each other, allowing your mother to reflect on her own mistakes. Time is a good medicine that can heal the soul and also heal the relationship. 3) Have a balanced diet and exercise. Your mother's initial intention of criticizing is nothing more than wanting you to become beautiful, slim, and to become her source of pride. But you must believe: only the closest people will argue with you, and that doesn't mean that your mother's approach is correct. Both parties need to compromise. You can talk to your mother about your recent fitness and dietary plans. Make an effort to win a good figure through exercise, which will not only satisfy your mother, but also greatly improve your own temperament and physical fitness. In conclusion, take action. Success only requires two steps: starting and persevering. Best wishes~.

Hello! According to your current situation, you are not considered overweight based on different calculation methods. So don't be discouraged! Perhaps your mother's comment about you being fat is mainly based on your previous weight. Maybe she just wants to stimulate you to lose weight and return to your previous weight through sarcastic remarks. The state of the human body itself is dynamically balanced, so maybe you can try telling her not to discuss weight issues in a sarcastic way. It's not good for you to compare your weight with your mother's weight and feel that she is heavier than you and that you are fat. After all, different stages of life have different body conditions, and there will be differences in weight. I hope you can maintain a positive mindset. Finally, I wish you a pleasant mood and a quick resolution to this issue!

Hello, actually, your body proportions cannot be considered as overweight. With a height of 160 cm and a weight of 108 jin, as long as you engage in moderate exercise and have a balanced diet, I believe you can maintain a very good physique. The issues you mentioned are more related to the psychological aspect. In a family, a mother plays a significant role and is often referred to as "family style". From your description, it seems more like you lack a sense of security and recognition. Due to your own difficulties in certain areas, maybe you redirect your anger towards related people or things as a way to vent your inner imbalance. If we only consider your physical condition, it may be a bit far-fetched. More importantly, it is reflected in your overall life performance that she excessively interferes with and cares about you. Honestly, this type of care makes you feel uncomfortable, as if others commenting positively means they don't understand you, and her not saying anything good deeply hurts you. Of course, it cannot be ruled out that there are other aspects that she considers as problematic. Therefore, it is difficult to say how sunny and happy our inner world is when growing up under the scrutiny of such elders. In your case, what you feel most is the sense of injustice. Her criticisms may indeed be well-intentioned, but due to her strong personality and improper approach, it has created a conflict between you. In psychology, there is a term called "killing kinship", the closer the person is to you, the more they want to change and influence you to become the person they hope you to be. At the same time, it casts a shadow on our young hearts, a psychological desire to "grow up quickly, leave her and this environment as soon as possible, and preferably never have any contact again", silently growing as we age. So, why do you have such a strong sense of resistance within yourself? Let's start with our own personality and environment—where there is oppression, there will be resistance, especially for those who appear to be strong-willed and independent on the surface, but have a strong contradictory personality internally, similar to Su Mingyu in the TV series "All Is Well". Family relationships do indeed have a significant impact on our emotions. A fragile heart is hidden beneath a strong aura. In fact, each of us is insecure, to varying degrees, preventing us from controlling our emotions and leading to the venting of emotions and releasing of pressure. Therefore, I can understand your current confusion and distress. Here are a few suggestions you can consider: 1. Your relationship has become so strained that neither of you is willing to take a step back to resolve this conflict. In this case, rely on time and distance to resolve it. The more she tries to control you, the more you resist. However, further improvement may be achieved through the distance of time and space, as distance makes the heart grow fonder. 2. In fact, for this type of parent, try using appeasement as a way to handle the situation. This is their weakness. When you display strength, they naturally won't know how to respond. Perhaps your personality is unwilling to accept and adopt this approach, otherwise the relationship would have improved a long time ago. However, I still suggest you give it a try. 3. Most of the time, you express your complaints or grievances. When you have the ability to change everything, the surrounding environment will treat you gently. Do not treat people who are not on the same level as you with equal courtesy. Show generosity, and life will naturally reward you with more and better things. Refer to the story of "Fang Bao's Filial Piety" for inspiration. 4. In the face of family troubles, we can escape to society. But if we encounter many people like this in society, how will you choose? We need to learn effective abilities to judge people and cope with situations. Consider studying color psychology. 5. She has her hardships and you have your own helplessness. When you cannot change reality, learn to adapt and influence it. This type of personality is inherently dominant internally but timid and weak externally. Character flaws have already made you experience a lot of injustices. I hope that the hardships we experience can lead us to greater achievements. No one is born entitled to anything. Treating others and yourself with magnanimity is an important practice in life's journey. I hope this helps. Best of luck in everything.

question: How to control anger, as it is difficult to manage this emotion? How can one prevent oneself from getting angry?
description: My aunt came to my grandmother's house and regardless of my father's and my attitude, she verbally abused my grandmother with extremely malicious language. Although my grandmother is not an easy target either, it makes me very angry. This place is equivalent to my home, so what gives her the right to curse here? It really upsets everyone, and my good mood is completely destroyed. I can't believe that after not cursing enough in her own home, she comes to mine. I really don't want to say those unpleasant words, but I'm becoming angrier and angrier. How can I control this kind of emotion? What should I do in the face of such verbal attacks?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, nice to meet you. First of all, I understand your situation from the description. It is indeed uncomfortable and even disheartening when something like this happens with a family member, and it must have had a significant impact on your life and family. In this situation, the fact that you can still control your emotions and seek solutions shows that you are really composed and it's not easy. Secondly, a person's personality is usually more or less influenced by their original family. From what you mentioned about your aunt and grandmother, it seems that there may be some influence and correlation between their behavior. This kind of situation also angers your emotions, which can be related to your personality. And from a psychological perspective, a person's emotions are usually a projection of their inner self, and different emotions represent different inner desires. The anger you mentioned indicates that you have certain expectations for the words and actions of your family members in your heart, but in reality, their behavior doesn't meet your inner expectations, which is why you feel angry. In such a situation, if it happens at the time, I suggest that you can choose to distance yourself from the source of stimulation, then adjust your breathing and calm yourself down. At this time, using diaphragmatic breathing can be helpful and relieving for you. However, one thing to note is that you must focus on your breathing and it must be diaphragmatic! If you are not proficient at first, you can put your hand on your abdomen and feel the rise and fall of your abdomen with each breath. Remember: Do not use chest breathing, as it will only make you angrier. Lastly, the above methods are only addressing the symptoms, not the root cause. I suggest that if you want to improve your emotional control ability from the source, you can choose to seek professional counseling in personal growth to further enhance your emotional mastery. I hope that the current situation in your family can change as soon as possible so that you are no longer affected.

question: 23-year-old male with bipolar disorder, recently experiencing recurring violent thoughts in his mind for the past year.
description: I am 23 years old and a patient with bipolar disorder. It was probably when I was 13 or 14 years old, during junior high school, that my classmates gave me a derogatory nickname. At that time, I didn't know how to express anger and dissatisfaction. I suppressed my anger for a long time without anyone to confide in. Gradually, I realized that I might have depression (around the age of 16) and was diagnosed with depression at the hospital. After long-term observation, the doctor found that I have bipolar disorder (depression combined with mania). Then, in the past year, I had the courage to curse the classmate who gave me the nickname in the WeChat class group using foul language, but he did not respond at all. I thought that by doing this, I would be able to let go of this matter, but I couldn't. The conflict with them continues to play out in my mind, both verbally and physically. I can easily beat down weaker opponents. But when facing a stronger opponent than me, all I can do is endure their mockery and turn away. I rush forward, grab his neck, and forcefully dig out his eyeballs with my two fingers. This is how my anger manifests (these are not thoughts I intentionally imagine). Right now, there is even the thought flashing in my mind, "I can only find relief by killing him." I feel like I'm going crazy.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, psychological crisis, mental disorders

answers.answer_text: Hello, after carefully reading your question, you mentioned some of your past experiences that have caused you a lot of distress and worry. When recalling those memories, you still remember the nicknames your classmates gave you in middle school, which made you feel humiliated, embarrassed, and aggrieved. However, you have not spoken to anyone about this inner pain and have instead kept it deeply suppressed in your heart. Did you know that each of our hearts is like a bottle? When it is filled with suppressed negative emotions such as anger, resentment, and pain, if we don't process them for a long time, these negative emotions will fill our hearts like dirty water. As a result, you may feel pain, a sense of being overwhelmed, and terrifying images appearing in your mind, which are actually reminding you that "your heart is already filled with dirty water and can't take anymore." This overflowing dirty water beyond your control expresses itself in the form of images. Therefore, what you need to do now is to release your negative emotions. Of course, the release of these negative emotions requires the guidance of a professional teacher. Although you have made some attempts before (insulting others in a WeChat group), and it had some effect, the accumulated dirty water from many years cannot be poured out quickly in a short period of time, and it may require more direct methods. After gradually releasing these emotions, we can truly begin to adjust our cognition and beliefs, and step by step move forward. Explore your inner self and find the deep-rooted reasons for your habit of suppressing emotions. Although these uncomfortable events are caused by the group of classmates in middle school, there seems to be a deeper reason behind it. I wonder when you learned to suppress emotions in your childhood memories and no longer express yourself to people around you, even unwilling to talk to your own parents about your own affairs? These experiences may be the roots of your habit of suppressing yourself. If you truly want to break free from this state, dealing with the previous negative emotions is only the first step. It is more important to improve your way of expressing emotions, otherwise, the bottle in your heart will gradually accumulate dirty water and similar problems will arise again. I hope the above reply is helpful to you.

The main subject feels that everything that comes to mind is not something they subjectively want to do. It is just that when we are most helpless and need help from others, no one stands up, and some even mock us, causing us to accumulate negative emotions. I wonder how the main subject's family has viewed this matter over the past few years, and whether they have given us enough care and help? In fact, many people encounter situations similar to the main subject's when they are studying. I remember when I was in school, I was also given some derogatory nicknames by others. At that time, I was also small and wanted to resist but didn't dare to. I secretly wiped away tears on several occasions. Later, I met an upperclassman who told me that many people have nicknames, but some are given by people who are closer to us, while others are intentionally given by people who want to demean others. Therefore, we need to understand what this nickname means to ourselves. If the other person is just intentionally demeaning us, then such a person is not worthy of respect. The best way to deal with it is to ignore them. If we confront this kind of person, they will only get more aggressive, but if we completely ignore them, they will lose their power. If it's a good friend of ours, then we can tell them that we don't like this nickname and hope they can consider our feelings. I believe they will be more restrained. The main subject said that they later cursed at the other person in a WeChat group, and although it felt somewhat relieving at the time, the other person did not respond. Is there a sense of helplessness? The conflicts from before still come to mind. It seems that only by eliminating them can we erase the grievances we have suffered. But I believe that the main subject is not a bad person, nor do they really want to hurt others. It's just that we haven't released our negative emotions, which has caused our internal anger to grow. Therefore, we can try to say goodbye to the past and let go of some things slowly. If necessary, we can talk to a professional counselor and use a combination of medication and therapy. At the same time, we can communicate with our family to see if we can get their support. Believe in yourself, we can overcome this. The world loves you.

Perhaps, everyone has a little monster in their hearts, roaring inside, maybe trying to tell us something. Ten years ago, classmates gave you a nickname, and you didn't know how to express your anger and discontent. Later, you developed bipolar disorder. A year ago, you cursed the classmates who gave you the nickname, but still couldn't let go, and conflicts with them played out in your mind. As far as I know, many primary and secondary school students give each other nicknames, and some of these nicknames are insulting and demeaning, which can cause conflicts. As we grow older, we gradually let go of the jokes from our youth. Ten years have passed, and you still hold on to that nickname. Perhaps, at that time, this incident had a big impact on you, and you didn't express your anger and dissatisfaction, leaving it bottled up inside you. Generally speaking, adolescence is a time of impulsivity. Your current behavior is much like that of an impulsive teenager, not quite like a mature 23-year-old. It feels like you want to fulfill a wish that you couldn't fulfill in your youth. Perhaps all these years, what you can't forgive is not the classmates who gave you the nickname, but yourself for not fiercely retaliating back then. Maybe you weren't suppressing your anger, but enjoying exacting revenge. Your life would have been very different. Many gruesome cases show that impulsivity is the devil. Your initial choice wasn't too bad; true heroes are those who can endure. Like Han Xin. Ten years ago, none of you were mature, so forgive them and forgive yourself. Let go of past grievances and move forward with strength. You are now a powerful young person, and the future is promising.

question: Why do I constantly force myself to drool?
description: I feel like I have obsessive-compulsive disorder, and it's quite severe. I frequently have insomnia and believe that I will always be in a constant state, continuously going on without stopping. I'm truly mentally exhausted.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, psychological counseling, mental disorders

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. You have a behavior of forcing yourself to salivate and your sleep quality is not great. You can feel that you are mentally exhausted in this state and you want to get rid of it. You mentioned that you believe you will always be in a certain state, a type that will continue indefinitely. Have you ever tried to think that you may temporarily be unable to change your current state? Maybe it's related to the definition you have given yourself, that you cannot change. In daily life, whenever a similar behavior occurs, you think, "I am someone who cannot change," and then your behavior really cannot be changed, following that line of thought. However, with the right approach, your current state can be changed. Have you ever tried to think about whether you can control yourself from salivating in daily life? Isn't it a great progress if you can control yourself once? Don't worry, you just need to gently divert your thoughts away from the idea of salivating and focus on what you are currently doing. If you are not successful at once, don't rush, it's normal, take it slowly. Additionally, I suggest that you seek help from a top-tier hospital's mental health department and consult with a doctor. Professional treatment can help you recover gradually. These are just some suggestions I have, I hope they can help you. Best wishes!

question: Doing things that other people think is right or being praised for it makes me feel fake and unhappy.
description: I have always felt unhappy, but recently I realized that it is fake self that is causing me a lot of pain. For example, I am very selfish, but I know that selfish people have no friends. When relatives give me things, I say I don't want them, but deep down I really want them, and I take them. Next time, I will return the favor because I am afraid that others will say I am selfish. This kind of transactional interaction is very tiring for me. My aunt often says that there are things in her house that I can take home, and in reality, I really want them. But I immediately say I don't want them, because I start worrying that they might say I am very selfish and always want to take things home. When I go out to eat with friends, if I pay the bill, I feel resentful, but if she pays the bill, I worry that she will say I am selfish or splitting the bill seems awkward. When others ask me for help, I don't want to help at all, but I reluctantly do it. I think I calculate things very clearly: you help me, I will help you, but deep down, I am selfish and don't want to share, don't want to help. I have a sense of detachment from the world. Maybe it has to do with the fact that I was given away to someone else when I was born. In my foster mother's home, I was stubborn, but when my mother hit me, I became afraid to express my emotions and thoughts. Each time, I only did what others thought was right or what would earn me praise.
keywords: Growth, personality traits, self-acceptance, and life meaning.

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, I can feel that you are not happy with what you are doing, and I am also touched by your courage. Sending you warm hugs! From your description, I have summarized a few points: fearing being called selfish, finding reciprocation tiring, always doing things that make others happy and gain their approval, and not knowing how to say no appropriately. In light of your description, let me share my thoughts: good friends are there to trouble each other. Building interpersonal relationships is based on continuous interaction, and good interpersonal relationships make both parties feel comfortable and recognized. Ultimately, good interpersonal relationships satisfy our need for recognition. I don't know if you feel the same way, but after helping others, whether or not we receive material rewards or just a simple "thank you," or seeing the other person improve under our help, we feel a sense of fulfillment. Good interpersonal relationships contain this feeling and involve mutual giving. On the surface, it may seem like I give you something and you give me something in return, but in this give-and-take process, both parties can feel the care and recognition from each other. It's not a process of mutual cancellation, but a process of strengthening each other's relationship. It's not 1-1=0, but 1+1=2. We are not currency, so we don't need to and can't please everyone. We need to learn to say no appropriately. Some of the troubles in life exist because we do things that we shouldn't be doing and think that by helping others, they will recognize us and our "sense of accomplishment" will increase. However, reality may not be like that. Those things we shouldn't be doing and don't enjoy doing bring us more troubles instead of a "sense of accomplishment." Learning to say no appropriately is the foundation of becoming a confident person.

The relationship between people needs constant mutual effort to be sustained. Selfishness is human nature because seeking advantages and avoiding harm is our instinct. We willingly accept things that benefit us, but we tend to avoid those that harm us. The biggest difference between us and other species is that we have more thoughts and emotions. For many children, selfishness is a characteristic that most of them possess, while those who appear mature and selfless are often shaped by the frequent guidance of adults. For example, when going out to eat with friends, going Dutch every time seems awkward, but paying for ourselves every time is somewhat reluctant. If we often let the other person pay, it may not be appropriate either. Therefore, we can divide the situation and the matter. If it's on our home ground, we can give more, as a way of showing hospitality. If it's in the other person's territory and they also show similar behavior, we shouldn't feel embarrassed either, because the relationship between us and the other person is mutually beneficial. If the other person calculates everything clearly and doesn't want to spend anything, then experiencing certain things once is enough; there's no need to overly consider the final gains and losses since this way of getting along is difficult to sustain. In life, we only need to be true to ourselves, treat others well if they treat us well, and also play along if others are insincere towards us. We mustn't live in other people's thoughts but have our own ideas. The world loves you and so do I.

Just remembered that I personally have similar feelings to you, mainly in the interaction with relatives. I tend to calculate things very clearly, mainly because of my mother's urging. Her belief is that if someone gives you something, you should also give something in return. But this belief makes me feel rigid and uncomfortable. It's understandable to have a slight deviation, but whether I give a better or worse gift, I will be criticized by my mother. The source of my discomfort comes from my mother's criticism. Although I personally also don't like sharing or helping others in terms of material things, I acknowledge my own belief. Is it selfish not to share or help? I haven't harmed anyone's interests, I just don't want others to harm my interests either. In places my mother can't see, I also calculate things very carefully. But I believe in my belief of not wanting to share, I think it's not selfish, it's self-love. Only by loving oneself and having enough energy can one have the ability to love and help others. But you mainly equate not wanting to share or help with selfishness, and cannot accept it in your heart. When you have the emotional desire to reciprocate, no matter how much reciprocity is involved, your heart will not truly accept the relationship with the other person, and the other person may also not accept your help because of your emotions. My suggestion is that when you don't feel like sharing emotionally, don't force yourself to do it. Be courageous in expressing yourself. Actually, I used to be like you, always being too accommodating. But during college, I discovered that there are some classmates who I think are quite selfish. Sometimes, they let others treat them and clearly refuse others' moral pressure. Slowly, I realized that they are just more self-loving. They don't intentionally behave like this, they just don't overthink things. But upon closer observation, it can be seen that these people generally have good interpersonal relationships with classmates and friends, and they don't carry as much negative energy.

question: The results are not as good as before, should I change my counselor?
description: After going through a nearly five-year counseling process, I have now reached a stage of transference. I feel that the effectiveness of the counseling is not as good as before. It's confusing and lacks direction. It seems that there is no chemistry between me and the counselor, and I don't have much motivation either. Should I change counselors in this situation? It would be a pity to do so, after all, this counselor knows me the best and seems to understand me the most. However, they may not be able to see the root of the problem. If I switch to a new counselor, it feels like I will have to start from scratch and go through a period of adjustment.

answers.answer_text: After five years of continuous counseling and still being able to stick with the same counselor, it seems that the questioner is a person who is able to persevere in their actions. I applaud you for that. Any relationship goes through three stages: the honeymoon phase, the stage of exhaustion and adjustment, and finally the stage of acceptance. In reality, it is not difficult for a person to seek counseling, what is difficult is finding a counselor who is a good match for oneself, and being able to blend and trust each other, which is quite challenging. You feel a sense of unprecedented chaos and directionlessness, to the point where even the rapport and motivation between both parties is lost. Therefore, it is normal to consider the idea of changing counselors. Since the relationship between the questioner and their counselor has developed for five years, I believe this counselor is still suitable for the questioner. During the counseling process, it will encompass all the contradictions and aspects of your life experiences. It can be said that it is an abbreviation of your life experiences. So, in the beginning, the surface-level aspects go smoothly. However, as you delve deeper, both parties need to put in more effort and cooperation. The confusion you are experiencing may be a stage of readjustment, and this stage happens to be a point you need to confront. The current stage for the questioner may be the so-called stage of exhaustion, a bottleneck stage. This stage gives rise to a lot of feelings and thoughts. In reality, every thought has its significance. If you feel very uncomfortable and lack motivation, then we can stop and take a look at what has happened exactly. If you cannot figure it out, you can communicate your deep-seated thoughts to your counselor, even thoughts of wanting to change counselors. Perhaps in the process of talking, some things will emerge. You may see unprecedented scenery. However, if you give up and change counselors, then what awaits you may be the scene of spinning in place every time you reach this point. No matter who you change to, when you reach this place, what awaits you is that part that spins in place. Therefore, I believe that the issue at hand has little to do with changing counselors. Confronting the problem directly is the key.

OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that 1. OP has been in counseling for a long time and is now entering the transference stage. The rapport with the therapist seems to have been lost. 2. OP is considering whether or not to change therapists, but is also concerned that it may take longer to adjust from the beginning if they do. 【A little analysis and advice】1. First, as the client, OP has the right to express dissatisfaction and the right to choose their own therapist or to communicate with the therapist about the recent ineffective treatment experience. However, OP mentioned entering the transference stage, indicating that the treatment process has indeed reached a difficult turning point. If this turning point is a necessary part of the treatment process and not due to a lack of compatibility between the therapist and OP, then changing therapists would require starting the adjustment process again, ultimately still facing the current transference stage. This would be a waste of time and money for OP. 2. If OP is willing, they can try expressing their inner feelings to the therapist and then cooperate with the therapist's treatment plan modifications as requested. This might lead to effective progress. However, if there has been a long period of no progress in communication between OP and the therapist, and the therapist has not proposed any other measures to change this situation, it may be more suitable for OP to change therapists.

question: Is it true that people who have extreme feelings of insecurity have a strong desire for control? How can they improve?
description: Recently, I experienced something that made me realize that I have a strong desire for control. Someone had mentioned it to me before, and at that time, I felt very wronged. My mom is someone with a strong desire for control and likes to escape. I have never been able to understand why I have such strong resentment towards my mom in recent years. It feels like I am being tightly held by her, and it feels suffocating. I really want to escape from home, so I often work away from home and don't come back. I have always felt that there is something wrong with me, that I don't understand gratitude, and I feel guilty. Until now, I increasingly feel like my mom, lacking a sense of security and having a strong desire for control. My younger sister has always been very close to me, but recently she has decided to go on blind dates and get married, which has caused me great fear and panic. It feels like I am going to lose her. I realize now that this is all about control. I am the one who is most miserable. I seek advice on how to improve this situation.
keywords: Personal growth, character development, self-improvement, self-acceptance.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I saw your distress and hope I can help you. From your description, I can see your awareness of your need for control and the struggles and resistance you have experienced due to your mother's strong need for control. I understand your feelings and emotions very well, and we can try to analyze and improve the situation. First, reconcile with your mother. Understand the reasons behind her lack of security due to her upbringing, empathize with the impact of traumatic events that the older generation may have faced, and see that your mother's strictness is just a result of improper methods, but with good intentions. Truly understanding her and resolving her emotions is also a way to resolve the guilt that arises from your opposition to her, and to reconcile with the fear-driven self that constantly blames yourself. Try to see and amplify the positive influence she has on you, which can also help you better accept yourself. Secondly, focus on your own personal growth. Shift your focus to your own demands and planning. Improving your abilities and self-worth can increase your self-confidence and sense of security, and help you reduce dependence on and control of others. Thirdly, establish more connections. Actively engage in positive interactions with friends and family, and cultivate hobbies that benefit your mind and body. This will broaden your social interaction and also reduce your excessive focus on certain people or things, which can lead to a need for control. A sense of security comes more from self-awareness and self-control. Attractiveness is more powerful than control when it comes to dealing with others. Wishing you new achievements every day.

Hello, after carefully reading the description of your story, I am particularly pleased to see the efforts you have made in your personal growth. Our self-growth actually begins with inner self-awareness. When you start to discover similarities between yourself and your mother's personality, and realize that you have strong and controlling tendencies in dealing with others' emotions, you are already starting to transform. Therefore, this is something worth acknowledging first. From exploring the "triggers" that cause you pain and discomfort in life, I wonder how your first self-discovery came about? I think this kind of approach may help you further explore and understand yourself. It's important to know that exploring our inner selves means continually being aware of and discovering ourselves, and gaining a better understanding of ourselves, which is the beginning of change. In this regard, I suggest starting with those moments in life that make you very unhappy and uncomfortable. For example, you mentioned in your question that you don't want to go home, but at the same time, you feel pain and guilt. You can reflect on where this self-reproach comes from. For example, when you feel just as uncomfortable as if you had lost a loved one when you see your sister going on a blind date, you can think about how your discomfort arises. It is important to note that these moments, if they were to happen to someone else, might not necessarily cause the same pain and discomfort. This suffering and discomfort will only manifest in you, which may be due to different cognitive perspectives and beliefs. If it is the loss of a loved one, a breakup, etc., these moments are painful for anyone, regardless of comparison. Starting from these special moments, find the root causes of the discomfort you feel inside yourself. This is self-awareness and introspection. When these special moments come, you will always be overwhelmed by the pain and emotions inside, and lose the ability to think rationally. At this time, you should always make yourself aware and try to look at what you are experiencing from the perspective of an observer. This is the observer's perspective in awareness. Of course, this may still not relieve the pain inside you, but you must always understand that this pain is not real, but rather a trigger of emotions from past memories. Otherwise, why wouldn't others feel the same pain? More importantly, never try to confront or even eliminate this pain, as it will only amplify its impact. The more you care about it and try to suppress it, the more you will provide it with new psychological energy, creating a vicious cycle. When you just let it flow quietly, truly feel it, you will find that pain, like flowing water, comes and goes, but never truly hurts you. Lastly, I want to say that psychological growth is a slow but exciting process. If possible, please join this platform and gradually learn more about awareness and ways to improve yourself by participating in knowledge courses, live broadcasts, and more. I hope to grow together with you.

Hello, based on your description, I can understand your current state to some extent. It seems that you feel uncomfortable because your mother is quite dominant, but gradually you realize that you have also been influenced by her and become somewhat dominant, wanting to control others. The recent example is that you feel afraid of losing your sister as she wants to get married. Our primary family does indeed have a significant impact on us, such as the behavioral patterns of our parents. We tend to inherit what we like and reject what we don't like. These subconscious memories are deeply ingrained, so sometimes unconsciously, we end up adopting these behaviors that we don't like. However, this is not absolute and unchangeable. For example, the influence of our primary family on us can be taken as a whole or there are ways to deal with it. I think your self-reflection is meaningful because many times, when we have many thoughts, if we are not aware of them, we lack that sense of observation and are not proactive or planned. Now that you are aware of the changes in your psychological state, you have already taken the first step. So let's discuss how to improve your relationship with your mother, and even improve your relationships with other people, especially regarding the desire to control others. As you mentioned, constantly trying to control others can make them feel suffocated, which is why you want to escape and find work in other places to avoid your mother. In that case, I suggest that when both of you are in a good relationship and in a calm state of mind, you can talk to her about these topics. For example, discuss what your mother thinks and how you personally feel about her actions. You can express that you know she cares for you, but you may prefer a gentler approach, and having an open conversation, I believe your mother will be able to understand. Slowly, this relationship will ease. Regarding your sister, as well as other people, I don't think you need to deliberately do too much. For example, when you notice a strong desire to control others, just the act of noticing it is a success. Because when you have this awareness, it becomes difficult for you to act on that impulse, right? So, you don't need to blame yourself too much. Whenever the thought of controlling others arises, we can promptly become aware of it and get ourselves back on the right track. This way, there won't be a big problem. I feel that you have good control over your own mind and your psychological state is generally fine. Keep up the good work!

Regarding the desire for control, it is actually not easy to detect, especially for individuals with a relatively low level of education, who are less likely to be aware of this aspect. Let me give you an example: if a couple has a bad relationship, the mother may unconsciously engage in behaviors that keep the child close to her, causing the child to also have a poor relationship with the father. The mother's behaviors are mostly unconscious, and what she knows is that if she can't get the husband's care and love, she will give all of her love and care to the child. After receiving the mother's love, the child will easily stay by her side and never leave. Because the child is young and lacks a discerning ability, it is difficult for them to objectively assess their parents' relationship, and they unknowingly become a group controlled by the mother's emotions. As the child grows up and begins to see more clearly the interaction patterns between the parents, they may realize that they were once emotionally controlled and unable to objectively view their parents. Sometimes, they may even harbor guilt towards the father and resentment towards the mother. You can try to become aware of what your need for control is about. It is understandable that you don't want your sister to leave, and you can certainly think that way. However, I don't think you would actually prevent your sister from leaving, right? If that's the case, then it may not be related to a desire for control. In daily life, if you feel like your mother has you tightly locked down, does it mean that you are unable to do what you want because she always gives you advice, suggestions, and even makes decisions for you without considering your feelings? If you don't like this way of doing things and would rather be yourself while allowing others to be themselves, maybe you can try to become a person with clear psychological boundaries. For example, you can accept that your mother is the way she is, but say, "I'm sorry, but I don't want to live according to your expectations. I respect that we are different, but I will live according to my own beliefs." It's easy to say but not easy to do, and it may require overcoming the fear of conflict that lurks within you... Take it slowly and don't label yourself as having a strong desire for control, because people's thoughts are dynamic and you will adjust according to your current needs. Believe in yourself!

Everyone encounters different problems in life, and not all of these problems are already known. There are also some that have yet to be discovered, the first-time discoveries. That's just life. Through experiencing certain things, you may realize that you are a controlling person. Maybe at this moment, you are learning to see and observe things around you. You are also becoming aware of who you truly are. As people grow up, they will have their own choices and circumstances, so it is normal to separate. However, even if you are separated, you are still sisters, just distanced from each other. In the future, she will have her own family and life, no longer clinging to you like when you were younger. It is normal to have a hard time accepting the possibility of separation. Try to think from a different perspective to ease yourself. She has her own life, just like how you have your own job. Give yourself some time to adjust and adapt. If there were things you didn't do well enough in the past, things you didn't observe carefully, make adjustments based on that. For example, make regular phone calls and greetings to bring each other closer. Some things may not have been realized, and some may have been caused by immaturity, so don't blame yourself. Just do your best to care for your family. You can have more conversations with your sister about her future life - her plans, the type of person she likes, and understand her thoughts. When appropriate, you can also offer your suggestions. I don't think it's about control when it comes to your sister, maybe it's just that you haven't adapted to the idea of being separated yet.

question: How to chat with strangers online and not know what to say all the time?
description: I don't have many friends, and sometimes I feel lonely. I want to chat with someone, but I never know what to say. After saying "hello" a few times, I don't know what else to talk about and it becomes awkward. Asking about age and work feels too personal, and even if they answer, I still don't know what to say next. I feel like I can't fit into these conversations, like an outsider. I say things just to get by, while wondering how others would respond. I'm always worried about saying the wrong things because I don't know what I mean myself. I'm just imitating, maybe I'm suppressing myself? But I really have a strong desire to chat. What am I lacking?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, social networking applications

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, every suppressed soul lacks the opportunity to be seen by others and the courage to express themselves truly. From your description, I can feel your strong sense of loneliness and the helplessness of not being understood or known by others. You may not be very skilled in socializing, but you have a strong desire to express yourself and establish connections with others. It seems like you hesitate a lot when chatting with strangers, probably because you feel too lonely. When it comes to starting a conversation, you might need to have different topics for different people. When you know absolutely nothing about the other person, including their gender, you can choose some trivial topics that everyone can talk about. For example, the weather, popular TV shows, and music. Focus on the other person and initiate topics that give them a sense of being cared for and valued. When they ask you questions, answer them sincerely based on your own feelings. If you feel comfortable answering, do so sincerely; if you feel it exceeds your boundaries, politely decline. In the virtual world of the internet, to be understood, seen, and have stable relationships, you may need to chat continuously and steadily with one person, genuinely making friends. With time, as you talk about more topics and get to know each other better, the topics will become more personal and relatable, and the relationship may become more stable. Additionally, you only have the desire to ask questions when you genuinely want to know about the other person. If your goal is to meet a stranger and expect them to understand you and become your confidant with just a few words, the chances are extremely slim. Don't force conversations. When one day the topic can no longer continue, you can wait until the next day or the day after to ask some questions you genuinely want to know. Respect the other person's privacy and interests, and don't interrogate them. Start with simple topics like hobbies and interests. This might give the other person a better impression and a sense of trust. Lastly, be sincere. There are many people making friends online, and their motives can be complex. Learn to identify and stay away from such people. As for those who sincerely answer your questions, be equally sincere in expressing your feelings and who you are because we can sense whether the other person is being perfunctory or genuine. Best wishes.

question: My roommate is always overly cautious and distrustful of others, and it's exhausting for me...
description: I know that as people grow older, their hearts become more fragile and they become less trusting of others. This is an experience shared by many. But I believe that there should at least be a basic level of trust between people. However, I have a roommate who really makes me feel exhausted when I interact with her. She is someone who doesn't like to talk much and has strong opinions, but she always seems to think that people have ulterior motives when they do things for her. For example, I try to help her out of kindness, but she seems to reject others' attempts to get close to her. I feel like I'm putting in so much effort to get close to someone who doesn't reciprocate. After a few times, I also feel tired. She always prioritizes her own interests, which also makes me feel emotionally drained. We're all going to live together for four years, so why be so nitpicky? I just want to have a pleasant time with my roommates during college.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, roommates and classmates, personal boundaries, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hello, there is no rule that says you must get along well with every person around you. If you feel hurt by someone several times, it might be because your personalities clash or you're just not meant to be friends. Although most people will say that it's important to get along with those around you, everyone's environment and personalities are different. Everyone has different likes, dislikes, and values. Besides the mainstream notion of getting along well with others, if you can't get along, you can choose to ignore them. There's no need to please someone you don't like. There are so many people in the world, so why bother yourself? Ignoring them is also a way of getting along with others. Best wishes.

question: How can I communicate with my child who always takes pleasure in others' misfortune?
description: Every time I feel embarrassed, it is when the child is the happiest. This makes me angry, even a little furious.

answers.answer_text: Hello, although your problem description is only a few words, I can still feel your confusion and dissatisfaction, even anger. I wonder how old your child is now? From your description, I see that every time you feel embarrassed, your child is the happiest, which may make us parents feel ashamed. As parents, it can be embarrassing when our shortcomings are exposed, as it affects our dignity and identity. The reaction from the child, such as laughter, jumping, or mocking, intensifies our sense of shame and leads to feelings of anger. Let's first consider the age of the child: If they are preschool-age children, seeing their parents embarrassed may seem funny and normal to them. Because in their minds, they might think that parents are infallible. When they suddenly see their parents making mistakes and being embarrassed, it is a very novel experience for them, something they find amusing, so it's not difficult to understand why they feel happy. On the other hand, children at this stage are still developing their brains and need to actively understand the embarrassment their parents feel after making mistakes and give them the feedback they desire. It is also challenging to teach them how to handle situations correctly. If the child is already in elementary school or older, under normal circumstances, they can perceive their parents' sense of embarrassment. However, their happiest moments coinciding with their parents' embarrassment may give the impression that they are "fighting against" their parents. So, the following are some questions that you need to consider. How do you perceive your parent-child relationship? When your child encounters difficulties, feels embarrassed or helpless, are you able to understand their feelings in a timely manner and provide the expected feedback and support? As parents, we are our children's most important mentors. From the analysis above, it is evident that regardless of the age of the child, parents' education, guidance, and leading by example are crucial references for their imitation and learning.

Actually, it's not just children who exhibit such behaviors and reactions. In our daily lives, when we see someone embarrassing themselves, we also tend to feel a sense of enjoyment. I don't know how the questioner usually communicates and interacts with their child, but if we are usually harsh with our child and exhibit unfriendly behavior towards them, even when they haven't done anything wrong, it is quite normal for the child to display such behaviors. Therefore, we need to learn to control our own emotions. Just like when we feel angry and annoyed when our child takes pleasure in others' misfortunes, we may even pass on this negative emotion to the child. We can communicate with the child during normal times and let them know that most people experience moments of embarrassment and awkwardness. If they encounter such situations, they should learn how the people around them view and cope with them. If the child doesn't want others to laugh at them, we should teach them about the attitude we should have towards others and how others will reciprocate accordingly. We should teach the child to consider others' perspectives. Also, try not to find amusement in embarrassing situations, because our unintended actions may cause harm to others. Therefore, we should teach the child to respect others and help others alleviate their embarrassment when necessary, and make the child learn to be helpful. We can lead by example and encourage the child during our communication with them, guiding them to learn the meaning of growth. The world and I love you.

Hello. I'm not sure how old your child is. If your child is still young, he may not understand what embarrassment is yet. So when he's happy in such situations, sometimes he may just think it's fun to play with mom and dad, or even think that mom and dad are playing a game with him. This is very normal for young children. At this time, on the one hand, we need to understand that your child's understanding is still at a very basic stage. On the other hand, we can ask ourselves, when we feel embarrassed and our child is happy, what do we think of or feel? For example, someone shared with me that they think of their father as an authority figure, so if they embarrass themselves or can't do something in front of their child, they feel like a failure. So maybe their anger is not because the child is happy, but because the child's happiness triggers their sense of failure. So for you, what is the answer to this question? You may need to ask yourself if you are feeling or thinking about something. If your child is older and can understand these things, you can take the opportunity to sit down and honestly tell your child your true feelings when these things happen. You can also listen carefully to why your child was so happy at that time. Sometimes when children exhibit certain behaviors, they may not necessarily know what kind of feelings these behaviors will bring to others. Good luck.

Children hope for authority to collapse, children crave independence, children long for equality. Therefore, as children enter another stage of growth, they undergo changes, and as parents, we need to change to match our children's changes. Parents need to examine their previous ideas and beliefs, to rebuild or amend and optimize these notions, and then make adjustments in their actions. I can only provide an example because families and children are all different: Parents' words are always right, turns into parents' words are not necessarily always right. "Listen to your parents" turns into "be able to communicate with your parents". "Children don't know anything" turns into "children know quite a lot and make sense". "The child is still young" turns into "the child is becoming independent and is about to grow up and separate" and so on. Anger and fury are the perfect opportunity to note down the reasons, beliefs, and principles behind the anger, and then work through these things. It is very nourishing. Good luck to you!

Hello questioner. The child may truly not understand what embarrassment is and may find the mother's behavior at the time amusing. It can also be said that the child does not yet have the ability to empathize. In the process of cultivating the child's qualities in daily life, parents should also pay attention to cultivating empathy, so that the child learns to understand the discomfort of others, and thus develops more sympathy and kindness. The child's empathy can also help them learn to treat their family members well. If the child shows schadenfreude, then parents should consider whether their empathy education has been done well. Parents are the best teachers for their children, and of course, the best role models for empathy education are the parents themselves. Our every word and action invisibly influence the child's qualities. Guide our children to understand and manage their own emotions and to understand the feelings of others. If similar situations arise again, you must communicate patiently with the child and make them understand your feelings. Or ask them to think from the other person's perspective - how would they feel if they were in the same situation and you found joy in their misfortune? Whether it's between adults or between adults and children, communication is crucial. Only when communication is effective, many problems can be solved. Hope this can help you.

question: Is it possible to still have trouble sleeping even after taking sleeping pills due to a fear of sleep?
description: Severe depression, mild anxiety, been taking medication for 3 years, including sleeping pills which also induce fear of sleep. I have always been resistant to sleep, to the point where even with sleeping pills, I still struggle to fall asleep. I take the maximum dosage of sleeping pills.
keywords: Treatment, physical response, treatment methods, psychological assessment.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I can really understand your pain. Because like you, I have also been consumed by insomnia day after day in the swamp. Including now, I also need to take sleeping pills, also known as tranquilizers, in order to achieve relatively stable sleep. First, why do we need to sleep at night? (1) Work at sunrise and rest at sunset. This is the order that the universe and nature have given to humans. Humans can never escape the laws of nature. Our bodies are not made of iron, and the laws of nature will allow us to choose to pause the activity of our bodies at specific times. Just like plants need photosynthesis during the day, humans also need to be active during the day. And sleep at night to detoxify our bodies. But what embarrasses us is that although the arrival of the night makes our bodies feel exhausted, our thoughts and consciousness often go against our physiological mechanisms. This is the fundamental cause of insomnia. The body is tired, but the mind is difficult to stop, this tug-of-war brings us suffering. I'm sure you are well aware, no matter how big your psychological problems are, your doctor will repeatedly tell you to sleep well at night. That's why you take some medication as an aid. (2) Chronic insomnia creates a negative "butterfly effect". The suffering caused by insomnia is not just the depression and anxiety of not being able to sleep at night. It is a series of long-term physical and psychological torment. 1. When you have insomnia for the first night, it will be difficult for you to get up in the morning, and even if you get up, you feel like you want to sleep. You feel drowsy and have low efficiency in daily life and work, decreased memory and prone to mistakes. You can't help but try to "catch up on sleep" and "sleep back" during the day. 2. When it comes to the second night, you will have insomnia again. Because your brain has been exhausted during the day and has been in a semi-calm state, if you take a nap during the day, your brain will think that you should be awake now. You will feel energetic and want to use your phone. As a result, you toss and turn and can't sleep. 3. When you have been in this state of "day and night reversed" for a week, your biological clock will be completely disrupted. In this situation, the brain that controls your emotions will experience functional disorders due to your long-term insomnia. And your body will be overdrawn due to lack of sleep. It is easy to feel tired all over the body during the day, limbs ache, lack of concentration, and frequent mood swings. Insomnia can cause people to become more depressed and anxious under stress. And friends who originally had depression and anxiety will exacerbate psychological problems due to insomnia. Second, if you already have psychological problems and insomnia is getting worse. Is it still possible to get better? Friends with chronic insomnia always say the word "desperate". But in fact, based on my personal experience of long-term battles with insomnia, I think insomnia can be overcome. Because of work reasons, I used to stay up late frequently. Later, it evolved from not being able to sleep to not being able to sleep at all. I felt tired all day and could only rely on coffee to stay awake. At night, I would lie in bed and try to fall asleep but couldn't. Now, I still need medication to improve the quality of my sleep, but through my efforts and adjustments for a period of time, I can now go to bed around 10 pm and wake up at 6 am every day. I want to tell you through my experience, dear friend, although insomnia is really terrifying. But this is not a bottomless abyss of despair. As long as you have hope and strive to change, you can also develop good habits of going to bed early and waking up early, and have a vibrant life! Third, how should we get out of the predicament of insomnia? I have three suggestions to share with you. Insomnia is scary, and even scarier is the "learned helplessness" psychology that we develop when facing insomnia. Faced with the frustration of insomnia, many people surrender, even if they use sleep aids, it is difficult to get better. The person will become more and more powerless. As a mental health practitioner, I must responsibly tell you that although sleep aids can indeed reduce the activity of your brain to a certain extent and promote the secretion of melatonin, if you excessively rely on medication without making comprehensive adjustments to your body and mind, even the best sleep aids can easily develop resistance in your body and become addictive. Just increasing the dosage of medication to force yourself to fall asleep may eventually lead to the medication becoming ineffective and unnecessary harm to your body. To overcome insomnia, you need internal and external adjustments. Only you can change yourself. I suggest the following, hope you can adopt it: Suggestion 1: Pay attention to the problem of insomnia, adopt the 21-day habit formation method, and conduct sleep training to adjust your biological clock. Many people can't get out of insomnia because they always underestimate it and treat it as a minor problem. Finally, it becomes difficult to recover. So, when you feel that insomnia has become unbearable, you need to make overcoming insomnia your most urgent goal. To succeed, you must plan ahead and meet your needs. I personally made a 21-day chart for myself. And I would check off the goal of going to bed and waking up early in the chart every day. I will share my 21-day sleep adjustment method with you. (1) Step one: In the first week, I would require myself to finish washing up at 10 pm, go to bed at 11 pm, and fall asleep at 12 am. (2) Step two: In the second week, I would require myself to finish washing up at 9:30 pm, go to bed at 10:30 pm, and fall asleep at 11 pm. (3) Step three: In the third week, I would stick to the schedule of the second week and strictly follow it. Here are some important tips to remember: Key point one: Set an alarm on your phone to remind yourself, and when it's time to sleep, turn off your phone. Avoid unnecessary temptations. At the beginning, it is the most difficult because there are many things on your mind at night, and you can't help but think about them. However, when I think of how uncomfortable I will be the next day, I force myself to follow the schedule. Key point two: It is recommended to take sleep aids at 8 pm. Because it takes time for the medication to digest and take effect. Key point three: In this process, there will inevitably be temptations. So before starting the 21-day sleep execution plan, I will inform all my friends that I will not participate in any evening entertainment activities, including playing games, singing, watching movies, etc. And I will ask the people around me to supervise me. After 3 weeks, you will find that your body and brain have completely formed a "conditioned reflex" of going to bed and waking up early, and good habits have been formed. Sleeping on time is no longer a problem. The inertia that human beings possess will keep you persisting in going to bed and waking up early. Suggestion 2: In order to avoid insomnia at night, you must fully engage in activities during the day to consume energy. This ensures that you have excess energy at night. Many people can't sleep at night because they sleep too much during the day. Our bodies naturally seek balance. If you put the things that should be done during the day at night and the things that should be done at night during the day, it will eventually lead to a reversal of day and night, and create a vicious cycle. Therefore, I suggest that you find a way to make your daytime activities more fulfilling and not procrastinate or be lazy. (1) For example, you can try participating in activities that consume a lot of energy during the day, such as running or swimming. Exercise can release the body's energy, and it can also secrete dopamine to bring a sense of pleasure. More importantly, it can help your body better sense the signal of rest at night, and improve sleep. (2) For example, you can change the way you work and study, try to be more efficient during the day. Many people work overtime and stay up late not because they are really busy, but because they procrastinate. If you want to sleep well, then the things that should be done during the day should not be done at night. If there is not much work recently, you can try cleaning the house, organizing items, or taking a walk in the neighborhood garden. Don't lock yourself inside and spend every day lying in bed using your phone. Chinese culture emphasizes balance between yin and yang, and only by practicing it can you overcome insomnia. Suggestion 3: To overcome insomnia, you need to create a conducive sleep environment for yourself and adjust your nutritional status. (1) To sleep well, you must create a good sleep atmosphere. If you still listen to heavy metal and watch episode after episode of TV shows at night, and the lights are bright, then your central nervous system will mistakenly think that it is still daytime. This will make it more difficult for you to fall asleep. I suggest you change your sleep environment. For example, listen to soothing music before bed, buy pillows and bedding that suit your sleep, wear comfortable pajamas, and use the softest lighting in the room before bed.
