You can even use lavender aromatherapy to relax yourself. A good sleep environment can bring a sense of security to your mood and alleviate your anxiety and depression to some extent. It is helpful to you. (2) Try meditation and breathing relaxation exercises before bed to better enter deep sleep. Many people have a lot on their minds and are unable to let go of the problems they encountered during the day when they lie down. This burdensome and psychological baggage on top of the already heavy burden will make it difficult for you to sleep well. If you want to sleep well, you need to let go of the burden on your mind before bed. Relax completely. Choose a comfortable position, or you can sit cross-legged. Then let your brain relax completely, meditate. Breathe in a rhythmic manner, drive away the troubles of the day completely. Through meditation and breathing exercises, you can calm your mind, and you can sleep soundly. (3) In order to sleep well, you should pay attention to your eating and drinking habits. Many people can't help but have an extra meal at night, eat spicy and stimulating food, and even drink too much coffee or alcohol. This increases the burden on the stomach and intestines. The organs that should rest at night have to accompany you in staying up late because of your desire for food and drinks. Of course, you will not sleep well. It is of no benefit and only harms your physical health. Therefore, do not eat cold and spicy foods before bed, and avoid drinking stimulating teas and coffee. Control your diet, and you will have better sleep. Before bed, you can try drinking mild beverages like milk to help with sleep, and during the day, try not to overindulge in food and drink to avoid burdening your body. These are all my analysis and suggestions. Insomnia is really a painful enemy. Not being able to sleep well deprives us of vitality during the day and makes us increasingly unhappy. The body becomes worse and worse like a deflated balloon. Only by breaking it can we make progress. In the miserable cycle of insomnia, it is better to boldly overcome insomnia. Come on! Thank you for reading, please like and follow!

Give the OP a hug! One can feel the extreme fear in the OP's heart. Even after taking the maximum dosage of sleeping pills, they are still afraid of sleep and have a strong aversion to it. This indirectly reflects a very obvious problem, that the internal conflict in the OP's heart is intense. The conscious self realizes the need for good sleep to maintain physical health, but the subconscious self's repressed fear is overpowering and beyond the control of the conscious self, resulting in the current situation faced by the OP. Perhaps the OP is not aware that it is the internal conflict that forces them to do things they don't want to do, suppressing too many emotions that need to be released and satisfied, which leads to the OP's heart carrying so much pressure. They do not know what is going on or how to solve it, which causes their inner anxiety and fear. Among the repressed emotions in the OP's heart, fear is perhaps the most obvious and "strongest". And the source of these fears is closely related to certain traumatic events that occurred during their previous sleep, such as experiencing strong fear during sleep and leaving this fear in the deep memories of the OP's subconscious self. When encountering similar external stimuli, these feelings can be triggered and activated, greatly affecting the OP's normal sleep and daily life. To solve this problem, the repressed fear in the OP's heart needs to be released, and past traumas need to be repaired. Consider making an appointment with a skilled hypnotherapy therapist for psychological counseling to help solve the current issues and allow the OP to have a relaxed and natural sleep life.

Fear of sleep conflicts with sleep, I understand you. I haven't had the same experience as you, but I have helped numerous visitors like you with good results. Why don't you give it a try? 1. Find the root causes of your anxiety and depression and make peace with them: Facing and accepting them is the key to reconciliation. 2. Tell yourself before bed: Sleep if you feel like it, don't sleep if you don't. Only get in bed when you feel sleepy, and there should be no items like phones or books in bed. 3. If you don't feel like sleeping, don't get in bed. You can do something like reading, soaking your feet, or meditation. If you follow these steps, you will likely be able to sleep. Otherwise, you can make an appointment for counseling.

Dear, sleeping is a blissful thing. But you are troubled by insomnia every night. Your body is exhausted but your mind is still tense, feeling fearful and anxious. This state is torturous! And it's the same every day, like an unsolvable cycle, truly making one feel depressed! I have also experienced the same situation, experiencing the fear of sleep, tossing and turning restlessly in bed, even worrying about insomnia as soon as night falls. And indeed, insomnia comes again, deepening the fear of sleep and further depressing oneself. The fear of sleep is mostly the feelings and emotions left behind by past experiences, which have not been recognized and soothed in a timely manner, but have been repressed into the subconscious. Every time the same circumstance arises, fear is triggered, affecting our choices. Your fear of sleep is so intense that not even sleeping pills can gain the trust of your inner self. It is evident that past experiences have had a strong impact on you. You cannot trust the outside world, don't believe that the outside world is safe, and don't believe that you can be protected. You can only stay awake, control the situation yourself, and then it will be safe. The reason for depression is mostly our lack of control over ourselves or the outside world, feeling helpless. This stems from the subconscious evaluation of oneself: I have no value; I am not good, nobody likes me; I always make mistakes... The healing method is to sacrifice one's own well-being to gain a sense of control and security, but it will only make oneself more tired and more discouraged. So how can you sleep peacefully? 1. Increase the sense of control: the body and mind are closely connected. If possible, engage in moderate exercise, just enough to break a light sweat. Don't force yourself to do too much, and don't judge yourself. 2. Find one positive trait every day: there must be a positive trait in your body. Praise one positive trait of yourself every night, even repeating it is okay. 3. Accommodate your own capabilities: do anything within your capabilities, don't demand too much from yourself. Do as much as you can without judging yourself. 4. Acknowledge the fact of insomnia: if you can't sleep, then so be it. Perhaps you will be tired the next day, but let yourself be tired, don't struggle with yourself. Even if you can't sleep, do not criticize yourself. 5. Talk to yourself: treat the subconscious as a frightened child, perhaps something during the night frightened him/her, and he/she is so small, completely scared. Every night before bed, lie down, breathe calmly, and say to that child, "You must have been scared! You don't dare to fall asleep anymore, you think it's dangerous to fall asleep. Don't be afraid! I will hold you, protect you, and accompany you to sleep. You are safe now, you can sleep peacefully, you can sleep soundly." 6. Seek professional help: during periods of severe depression, your own strength may be weak, not enough to support your own changes. Find a hypnotic psychotherapist, have a conversation with your subconscious, change the subconscious's perception of sleep, have regular sessions, let them accompany and support you. This is a very effective approach. 7. Improve your relationship with yourself: no matter what you do, no matter how it is, never judge or criticize yourself again. If it's done, it's done. Don't evaluate it, don't evaluate it, don't evaluate it! Just affirm yourself, even if you went to bed a minute earlier, praise yourself, well done! 8. Love yourself: we are all sacred lives, regardless of our background or character traits, we all deserve to live the best life! 9. Improve the environment: clear away things in the bedroom that are unrelated to sleep, and place items that make you feel safe. Changing old patterns takes a long time, take it slowly! No matter how you do it, don't judge yourself! No matter what, you can have deep sleep! You deserve to live the best life!

Hello, asker! Your situation indeed requires a lot of attention and care. You can help yourself, and improvement is definitely possible. Let's cheer each other on!…………………………………………[Intentional and Unintentional] You may have heard of being intentional or unintentional. Yes, we need to intentionally treat our own problems. Face them, acknowledge them, and take treatment seriously. Listen to the doctor's arrangements, follow the healing plan that you know deep inside. Persist, practice intentionally. Practice loving life, practice doing things you enjoy, take it slowly, it's okay to make mistakes, take a break when you feel tired, and when you are not in a good state, tell yourself, "Here comes that awful feeling again, I'll hold on a little longer, it will leave sooner." Let's do our best together! This feeling is like baking in the kitchen, where the ingredients start off separate and clear, then become sticky and mixed together, and finally take shape and fill the room with a sweet fragrance. The whole room is filled with the taste of happiness and success. Yes, we don't need to deliberately remind ourselves of the details. Details are just details, referring to the intricate steps in doing things, and also referring to feelings that we temporarily don't want to accept. Don't deliberately remind yourself, all of these will pass, right? Or perhaps there are other methods we can try, right? In any case, don't deliberately remind yourself, don't influence yourself. [Sleep, to sleep or not to sleep] As the name implies, sleep includes both sleeping and resting. Sleeping is a verb, the willingness to sleep, while rest is a state, a relaxation of the mind. Together, it becomes a method, we need to go to sleep with the intention to sleep, and then relax our mind and body to the fullest. The significance of sleep is something that every mother understands. Sleep is so important for a baby's growth and establishing happiness. So we can talk to ourselves about the benefits of sleep. I think it's best for you to do this yourself, ask yourself and refer to books. You have enough life experience, right? Here, what I want to say is the intention to sleep, combined with the earlier notion of not being intentional. I feel that there shouldn't be a set time, silently tell yourself the benefits of sleep, that you need sleep, and then find a suitable time, use some sleep methods, and based on the doctor's advice, go to sleep. Believe in sleep, and rest will follow. Don't rush, take some time to experience it. [Music and Mindfulness] Happiness is also very meaningful. Find ways to make yourself happy, music and exercise are highly recommended! Find music that you like, or a type of music that could potentially help you, and listen to it consistently. Also, try to do some exercise that is within your capabilities, if you can stick with it, even achieving the desired physique is possible. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ The pressure in society nowadays is indeed high, and certain things are indeed difficult to handle. Let's accept the difficulty and the temporary mismatch with us, but we can keep going. There will always be methods to achieve it. The sky is blue and you're here, life can be beautiful! The world, and I love you!

Hello, you seem to have a fear of sleep and resistance towards it. It appears that you are very afraid of going to sleep, and I suspect it is related to something that happened in the past. I don't know this for sure, so I won't analyze it at the moment. Let's talk about the emotion of fear. First of all, fear is an emotion, just like happiness, sadness, and anger. This fear is your emotion, just like depression is your emotion, but they are not you. You can have various emotional experiences, including joy, happiness, and delight. I guess you have spent many years trying to get rid of negative emotions such as depression, anxiety, and fear. You have tried to fight against them and overcome them. However, it seems that even taking the highest dose of medication does not help you truly recover. So what can be effective if medication and fighting are not working? The answer is allowing and accepting, going with the flow, living in the present moment, and doing what needs to be done. By using the methods of Morita therapy and mindfulness, focus your attention on the present moment, train yourself to be aware of your emotions at all times, what happened, how you feel, and what underlying needs are behind them. Pull your attention back from the past and the future to the present moment. You can also practice mindful body scanning and mindful breathing. Go with the flow, allow emotions to come and go like clouds, accepting their presence without resistance, just being aware of their arrival and adjusting to the changes in your body. Do what needs to be done, continue living your life with all these strategies, eating, sleeping, reading, going out for a walk, try going to a new place, buying something new, and try doing something you want to do every day, starting from small things. Recognize all the things you currently have, your family, your friends, the people who help you, and see your own persistence, efforts, and strength. Yes, you don't need to sleep well, and you are already doing well. You can see, you can hear, you have all your limbs intact, you can still ask questions, and you can think. Yes, you are already doing great. You already have all the resources and abilities you need. From now on, live each day to the fullest, set small goals for yourself, do something within your capabilities, and that's enough. Then, just carry on with these troubles in your life, if you don't know what to do, just focus on doing basic things like eating and going for walks every day, and if you have something you want to do, go ahead and do it. That's it, allow yourself to have emotions, accept them and be present with them, no longer fight against them, resist them, or dwell on resentment. Allow them to be with you, allow them to be here in this moment, allow yourself to still have resistance, allow yourself to not fall asleep, allow everything that happens to you. Yes, live in the present moment, allow everything to happen. When you can allow yourself to not fall asleep at this very moment, then you can allow yourself to fall asleep in the next second. That's it.

Everyone has already explained it in detail, let me share a little thinking technique. If you treat sleep as a little person, when you have insomnia, you are begging this little person: with tears streaming down your face, you kneel down and grab onto the hem of sleep's pants, saying, "Please, sleep! I'll promise you anything!" We will find that often at this time, sleep does not listen to our requests. The more desperately you beg for sleep, the more stubborn it becomes and refuses to sleep! Haha, that's right! Sleep can be quite stubborn! The approach I'm suggesting is not to beg for sleep but to reverse the power structure. Can't sleep? Great! I can read a book, do some housework, or listen to the midnight radio while lying down! What if I'm tired tomorrow? Who cares! If sleep doesn't cooperate, what can I do? When you ignore sleep, you will find yourself the winner because physiologically, how can you truly not sleep? Soon you will realize that as long as you endure long enough, it will be sleep, with tears streaming down its face, kneeling down and grabbing onto your pants, saying, "Please, let me sleep! I'll promise you anything!" Then you can elegantly extend your hand and say, "Fine, since you insist...then sleep!"

First of all, I want to praise you. It takes courage to openly admit your vulnerability, which means you already have the courage to change. To be honest, you are truly remarkable. Despite suffering from severe depression and mild anxiety, you are willing to undergo psychological treatment and continue taking medication. As for your resistance to sleep, to the point where even sleeping pills don't work and you take them at the maximum dosage, I think it may also be related to your emotional state. You should be eager to overcome depression and have good sleep. Haste makes waste, depression is like a black dog. If you can't drive it away, try to befriend it. Also, you have provided very limited information, please open up more about your inner self. Only then can others better help you. I hope you can smile more often.

question: In sophomore year, I am kind to others, but the feedback I receive from them is always negative.
description: I'm okay with my classmates, but recently I encountered a problem. I heard negative evaluations about myself from another classmate. It feels like I treat the whole world well, but the world has abandoned me. I don't know why. Is it because I'm not good at studying?

answers.answer_text: Dear, hugs (｡･ω･｡)ﾉ Just now I analyzed one of them, but I missed another one. That is, sometimes, when you are too kind to people, they will take advantage of you. I understand this feeling, it can really give you a chill in the heart. I feel like playing the song "Cold" for myself. In fact, I used to be like this too. At that time, as a transfer student, I was not familiar with the new environment and really hoped to have a better relationship with a classmate so that I could establish myself in the class. So I treated my desk mate very well. At first, other classmates envied it and my desk mate was grateful. But as I got to know more classmates, my desk mate was no longer "special" to me. Over time, she started to resent me, and the classmates got used to my kindness. If one day I no longer took the initiative to help them, they would say I have changed. Because my "indiscriminate treatment" gave people the impression that I am always like this! Therefore, in life, it is necessary to have "different treatments"! All those "selflessness", "great love", "selfless dedication"... sometimes need to be considered in different situations and circumstances. This is actually an unwritten rule in our society. There are many unwritten rules in our interpersonal relationships, so we should observe more and interact with people who have good relationships. As the saying goes, "he who walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed!" Hope my answer can help you! Take care!

Dear, hugs ⊙ω⊙ I understand your feelings - sadness and disbelief that you would think, I have always treated others with kindness, why do they not appreciate but rather criticize me? Actually, it's not entirely their fault. Let me give you an example: A's colleague, B, was organizing files and halfway through, suddenly wanted to use the restroom, so B left for a while. During B's absence, A saw that B's desk was messy, so A tidied it up and neatly placed everything on the desk. When B came back and saw the neatly stacked pile of files on the desk, A smiled and said, "I saw your desk was messy, so I helped you tidy up." What could B say at this point? They could only politely respond on the surface, but secretly feel that A was interfering. This kind of phenomenon is actually quite common. Clearly, the protagonist in the story thought they helped their colleague B, but in reality, they ruined the half-done work with their good intentions. Therefore, it is natural for colleague B to get angry. Speaking of which, I remember watching a video on Douyin: there was an elderly lady crossing the street, and a young man noticed and went over to help her. When they reached the other side of the road, the young man casually said, "You're welcome!" But unexpectedly, the elderly lady stared at him and said, "I finally made it across, why did you bring me back?" So not all good intentions are actually good. We also need to understand the specific situation and see if the other person truly needs our kind help. Lastly, I hope my answer can be helpful to you! Take care!

Hello, OP. Hugs to you. The negative comments from others have consumed a lot of your energy and made you unhappy. It's okay, I will send you some strength and replenish your energy. Honestly, I used to be just like you, I can deeply understand your pain. Just a few months ago, I was the same, always being a good person, exhausting myself. Fortunately, recently I came across a book called "The Courage to Be Disliked", learning to reject others and no longer care about being good to them, because many times our efforts cannot be undone, so just consider it given, a gift to them. Sometimes, when others give you negative feedback, it's just because you didn't go along with their intentions, but that doesn't mean you are not good enough. It's just that everyone has different opinions and values about the same thing. No matter how hard we try to conform to others, there will always be parts that others can't understand. Trying to please and accommodate others is actually very exhausting and goes against our own values and thoughts. Many times, this situation occurs because others only want apples, but you gave them pears, which is why they think you're not good. In reality, it's just a difference in perspectives and values, it doesn't mean you're not good, it just means you haven't found someone who understands you. In fact, it's very rare for people outside to unconditionally like us, and if we do encounter such people, it is very precious and worth cherishing. In fact, even ourselves find it difficult to do this. We have many flaws that we may not even see ourselves, so we can't expect others to do so. Let me introduce a song to you, hoping it can bring you strength and motivate you. It's "Unconditional" by Eason Chan. In fact, for many high school students, hmm, if you have a lot of interaction with classmates, you will often find that whether classmates like you or not usually depends on some interests they have, either because you have good grades or because you have something that benefits them in some way. They like you not simply because of who you are, but because of the meaning or benefits associated with you. This is a very realistic problem, and most people are like this. Hanging out together, playing together, doesn't necessarily mean they are really good friends; sometimes it's just superficial, and everyone has a different distance in their hearts. It's not necessarily close. Be yourself, focus on building your inner self, and cultivate a strong inner self. Look for some good classmates or friends to interact with gradually. Start with those who are more sincere, ask them about their true thoughts, talk privately, communicate, have heart-to-heart conversations. Just ask about your concerns, maybe it can help you in some way. Ask about what their thoughts were with certain actions, and whether it had anything to do with you.

question: Feeling psychologically insecure, how to achieve the ability to freely engage in conversations?
description: Feeling mentally inferior, lacking self-confidence in everything I do, always feeling like someone is targeting me behind my back, how can I overcome this feeling?

answers.answer_text: If you feel lacking in confidence, it means you still know your abilities well. Being unable to speak up in a group is just a lack of talent in that area. Most talents are actually developed through childhood habits and experiences. If you don't have the talent, just go learn. It's never too late to start studying and exercising. Watch how others start conversations, how they communicate in the middle, and the emotions and expressions they use when speaking. It's easy to learn. If you feel tired, just endure it. What isn't tiring to learn? Once you've learned, it won't be tiring anymore. Even if you have an introverted personality, it just means you don't want to communicate, not that you can't. In fact, introverted people can become masters of communication. Introversion means you can only communicate with close friends, but once your communication skills improve and you can have enjoyable conversations with others, you won't be introverted anymore. 1. Make peace with yourself, truly like and accept yourself. Don't always think that you lack social skills and don't compare yourself excessively with people who are socially capable. Too much comparison will only hold you back and make you lose confidence. 2. Read more useful books to improve yourself.

OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. I can also understand the OP's feelings very well, especially when there are many people around, there is always a sense of discomfort as if others are paying attention to oneself. It may even feel physically uncomfortable. First of all, we need to understand and face the fact that, although this feeling may seem "real", it is often just an illusion: others are not actually discussing or paying attention to us. We need to first acknowledge this and constantly remind ourselves. On the other hand, the reason we care so much about other people's "judgments" may be due to our own lack of confidence, fear of not being accepted, or the assumption that others have negative thoughts about us. In response to this, the most important thing is to improve our self-confidence, to enhance and enrich ourselves through learning, exercise, and various other ways.

question: Tired of a monotonous life within the system, what should I do?
description: What should you do when you are tired of the same routine work and life within the system?

answers.answer_text: I am tired of the monotonous life, so I don't even consider working within the system. But people around me keep persuading me to take the civil service exam because it offers stability and good benefits, among other things. Every job has its drawbacks. Just like the uncertainty of working outside the system, I believe many people have experienced it during this year's pandemic. Many of my friends have decided to take the civil service exam after the epidemic. I want to share this point to remind you that if you want to leave the system, you need to consider the shortcomings of other jobs. They may be unstable, have poor benefits, high pressure, and monotonous work content. We need to think carefully about what we truly want. Are we prepared for it? If not, we can try something different after work hours.

question: I don't know since when I have been easily startled.
description: Once, I clearly saw this person coming towards me, but when he patted my shoulder, I still got startled. Another time, when I was leaving work, a colleague walked towards me with some food given by the company and patted me while speaking, asking me to have some. I got so scared that my body trembled, my heart raced, and I felt dizzy and feverish. Usually, even if the volume is a bit loud or if there's a loud noise from someone's accessories, I would still shake. One time, I slept with my mom, and a few days later, she said I was so easily scared that even if she just let out a breath, I would still tremble. But I don't feel it myself. Every time after being scared, when I snap out of it, it feels like I was absent-minded before being scared, but when I recall, I don't remember being absent-minded. More than one person around me has said I'm timid, but I don't feel like I am. Sometimes, when I get scared, I feel frustrated, helpless, and annoyed. Sigh.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear OP. According to your description, I have captured several pieces of information: (1) Physical symptoms: body shaking, feeling heart palpitations, palpitations, feeling anxious, and feeling feverish. (2) Psychological symptoms: irritability, helplessness, feeling wronged, and being timid. Some of your reactions partly match the symptoms of panic disorder, but due to the limited information provided, I am unable to make an accurate judgment. I will inform you about the criteria for panic disorder, and you can evaluate yourself first: the core symptom of panic disorder is panic attacks, which occur repeatedly without warning. During an attack, there is a sudden intense fear and discomfort, including chest pain, rapid breathing, etc. The diagnosis of this disorder can be made if the following symptoms are present: (1) Recurring panic attacks without warning. Panic attacks refer to the sudden onset of intense fear or discomfort. During an attack, at least four of the following symptoms are present: accelerated heart rate, sweating, trembling or shaking, shortness of breath, feeling of choking, chest pain, nausea or abdominal pain, dizziness or feeling light-headed, feeling cold or hot, numbness, feeling detached from reality or unrelated to the outside world, fear of losing control or "going crazy," fear of dying. (2) Following a sudden panic attack, there is at least one or both of the following symptoms for at least one month: persistent worry about having another panic attack and concern about what might happen during an attack (e.g., fear of losing control, "going crazy"). Significant behavioral changes in an effort to avoid another attack (e.g., avoiding exercise or unfamiliar places). Panic attacks are not caused by other physical illnesses, drug, alcohol, or medication use, or other mental disorders. The above information is based on my consultation of the DSM-5 mental disorders book, for reference only. I hope it helps! Take care!

OP, or it may be that you are in a state of nervous anxiety, causing you to be afraid of physical contact in interpersonal communication. Maybe you can try these methods: 1. Relax. Communicate with others in a relaxed manner, and you might even try initiating physical contact with others, such as patting someone on the shoulder or shaking hands. 2. When you see someone approaching you, you can mentally tell yourself to relax and not be nervous. When walking on the street, you can also greet others from a distance (without physical contact) to try to alleviate anxiety. 3. You can talk to your family or friends about these situations and ask them to try physical contact with you, such as patting your shoulder or shaking hands. Best wishes!

question: The elderly person is always angry because someone else is occupying their property. How can we calm their emotions?
description: There is an elderly person in the family who unconditionally gifted a portion of their assets to their stepson. It was originally agreed verbally that the elderly person could continue living there until their passing. However, after the property was transferred, the stepson and his wife evicted the elderly person. The elderly person has been psychologically affected and has suffered from multiple illnesses due to the stress. How can we improve the elderly person's emotional state and help them heal from this traumatic experience as quickly as possible, so that they can move on from this situation and live the rest of their days happily?

answers.answer_text: There have always been heartless and rebellious individuals, and I think there can be legal means to deal with them. Let that rebellious person lose everything. It is still possible, unless that person is a martial arts expert, then we should be cautious. He will not accept any public opinion or moral persuasion. Doing such a thing is already going against the natural order. Kind words are useless. We don't have to wait for the villain to act, we can take preemptive action.

Hello, OP: The anger and resentment of the elderly person stem from being betrayed and abandoned by their stepson, which is related to a significant traumatic event in reality. So, if possible, find a lawyer as soon as possible to see if it's possible to reclaim part of the gifted property. Additionally, leverage self-media and public media to exert public opinion pressure on the stepson and reclaim some justice.

question: Failing the college entrance exam, I feel really devastated and even want to die. I am feeling lost.
description: The college entrance exam scores came out, and I made a serious mistake in performance. I'm really devastated and feel like dying. I'm especially lost.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study

answers.answer_text: Don't think like that. Although I haven't experienced the college entrance examination, I can feel the atmosphere of it (I am a student in the third year of junior high school). Failing the exam or failing the college entrance examination can make people feel overwhelmed. But you have to think again, if you die, you can't get over the shame of not doing well in the exam, you can't get into your dream university, you can't pursue your favorite career. Don't forget, you can retake the college entrance examination, but you can't retake the middle school entrance examination. You have already endured the middle school entrance examination, which cannot be retaken, so why worry about this college entrance examination that can be retaken? Agree? If you're confused, then continue to bury yourself in piles of books and prepare for the next year's college entrance examination (actually, I don't know the specifics of the college entrance examination, so it's just a general idea).

question: How to face my mom and make the remaining days for her a little happier?
description: Mother grew up in a household full of unfinished housework, never catching up with the classroom, occasionally facing grandma's insults and grandpa's beatings. I always feel that she has a rebellious spirit; otherwise, why would she run away from home in the midst of everyone's numbness to this kind of life? The outside world is indeed as she desired. She takes care of herself properly, and looking back now, those few years may have been the happiest time in her life. Later, she fell in love, but her partner cheated on her. Devastated, she returned home and entered into an arranged marriage. She had me, only to discover that her partner was a fraud. She divorced and took me away, only to leave home again. She met someone else, who deceived her once more, but she couldn't go through the turmoil again. Until I fell ill, that person refused to treat me, so mother brought me back home. (A bit dramatic). Afterwards, due to various reasons, she became increasingly irritable. In 2018, she was diagnosed with a recurrence of her breast cancer. My condition also deteriorated greatly, both mentally and physically. Despite all that, we managed to get through the days in a blur. I got accepted into college, and her illness improved somewhat. Sigh, I just want to make the remaining days for her a little happier. However, when she yells and insults me, I really can't control myself and end up arguing back. So, I want to ask if there is any way for me to calmly face her.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, parent communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Hearing your story, I feel deeply sorry for you and your mother. You both deserved a better upbringing and life, but you were repeatedly hurt by the people you loved. It's not your fault. Everyone goes through some kind of trauma in their upbringing, and as adults, we all have to face these traumas and seek healing. Let's chat together and see if I can give you some tips to improve your life. Try to understand your mother. Her difficult childhood experiences were not her fault, and she couldn't control them. She didn't grow up in a loving environment, so she never learned how to love others. She doesn't know how to express her love for you in the right way because she never learned how! A person's childhood and their relationship with their parents form the basis of all their relationships. If they didn't have a good parent-child relationship or were mistreated by their parents, they will accept all the evaluations their parents gave them. When they grow up and choose a partner, they will look for someone who confirms those evaluations. That's why she keeps getting hurt by others. Maybe she's also in pain and wants to escape all the suffering from the past. Her temper flare-ups are probably a reaction to the pressures of life. It's because she's overwhelmed by the various difficulties in life, and negative emotions keep piling up without suitable ways to release them, so she becomes easily angered. I believe no matter how unbearable her life experiences have been, she wants to love you and give you a good life, hoping that you can be healthy and happy. This, you must feel deeply. In fact, she also needs someone to care for her, help her, and accompany her, so she can feel a little bit of love and be empowered to live a good life. When you get into college, your mother will find some relief. This might indicate that she has a bit more peace of mind about you and is happy that you have a good future. So, you are her strongest support at this moment, and you can say that you are her best mental pillar. Take good care of yourself so that you can take care of your mother in a better way. Please believe in yourself. Next, you need to see the real mother and understand her upbringing. This will help you reach a resolution with your inner "mother," allowing you to understand that your mother's attitude is not your fault, and you can interact with her peacefully and calmly. Spend more time with your mother! Chat with her, talk about the past, care for the injured mother, and give her more care and love. Your love will slowly heal her, allowing her to reconcile with her past and let go of any grudges towards those who hurt her, enabling her to live freely and relaxed. If conditions permit, take your mother out for a walk! Nature also has a healing effect, making a person feel relaxed and open-minded. Try to find your mother's hobbies and engage in them together, just like good sisters. Let her experience more happiness and joy. I believe that in the process of helping your mother live happily, you will also find healing. We all have our own wounds, and we have to overcome them on our own. Please believe in yourself and have the courage and power to live a good life. Then, you will have the confidence and bravery to let go of all the pain, and you will rebuild a new and better self. Don't give up. The world and I love you, and there will always be someone willing to accompany you and help you through the toughest stages of life. I look forward to hearing good news from you. Best wishes and keep going!

I can understand the feelings of the person asking the question, after all, it is their own mother. But you cannot deny that her insults are a form of harm to you. Faced with the people who hurt us, we are also very powerless. It is already impressive if we can protect ourselves from getting hurt, so how can we be calm? We are not saints, managing our own lives is already a challenging task for us, and often we have no time to care about others. Even if we want to help others, it should be based on their respect and recognition of us. How can you calmly face someone who yells and insults you? I think it is difficult to do so because others are causing harm to you. We are not gods, just ordinary people, and in the face of harm, all we can do is leave and protect ourselves. Why do you endure someone insulting you? Do you think it is worth helping someone who insults you? Even if it is your parent, the relationship should be based on equality and mutual respect. Regardless of how miserable your mother is, this is her own life. She has made various choices in her life and has reached this point. It is her responsibility to face and resolve it, not yours. What you need to do is to provide help within your ability, as you cannot bear too much interference. The only way to avoid arguing back is to distance yourself from your mother. When she insults you, leave quickly and maintain your mental health instead of being dragged down by her. If possible, try to communicate and find a psychological counselor for your mother, so that professionals can handle it professionally, and her emotions may improve. Right now, what you need to do is take care of yourself, make yourself happier, try more pleasant experiences, take care of your own health, so that you will have the energy to help others. Remember, your own life is the most important. Focus on yourself, not others. Only then can you help yourself navigate life's directions and avoid getting lost and suffering in various circumstances and choices.

Hello! You are a very filial child. You feel sorry for your mother's unhappy childhood and sympathize with the hardships she has faced in her life. All of this actually stems from your deep love for your mother. You have also done well by getting into university, which brings some comfort to your mother. However, you now feel a sense of guilt because every time your mother gets angry and loses her temper, you find yourself unable to control your response and end up arguing back. You are afraid that this will hurt your mother, so you hope to find a way to calmly face her anger. In order to understand what to do, let's first examine why your mother is so prone to anger and why you can't help but argue back. The childhood that you described for your mother was an unhappy one, with a grandmother who had no love and a grandfather who didn't care. Growing up in such an environment, children carry a lot of frustration and suppress a lot of emotions. They have a strong need for love, but their hearts are often deprived of it. This is one of the reasons why they repeatedly experience heartbreak in their romantic relationships. Longing for love but being deceived time and time again in reality, is another layer of hurt for them. In the end, your mother gave up her aspirations for the outside world because of her love for her child and returned home to raise you alone. However, her deep-seated desires and suppressed emotions have never found a way to be satisfied or expressed, and they continue to accumulate, resulting in increasingly frequent bouts of anger. Her illness is actually related to her negative emotions. As for you, living in an environment with an emotionally troubled mother for a long time, although she loves you from the bottom of her heart, her inner strength is lacking. As a result, she unconsciously radiates negative energy. Over time, you have also learned some of your mother's patterns. So when your mother yells at you, you can't control your emotions and argue back, even though you don't want to. Now, the first step is to heal yourself. What hurts have you experienced in the process of growing up? What pain have you felt? What suppressed emotions do you have? Start by healing those wounds and giving an outlet to the emotions you have been holding onto. Then you will have the strength to face your mother. With her, you can try to make her feel your love, accept her, understand her, and warm her. I recommend reading some books related to psychology, which might give you some inspiration. For example, "May You Have a Life Illuminated by Love." Finally, I wish you and your mother happiness and joy every day!

Hello, sending you a big warm hug! Your mother's life has been so difficult, and I'm sure you have also experienced a lot of hardships while living with her. Taking care of your terminally ill, irritable mother while dealing with your own health issues is truly heartbreaking. I see that you are a very kind and filial child. Despite your own illness, you are trying your best to remain calm in the face of your mother's outbursts and insults, and you are determined to make her last days a little happier. Your filial piety truly touches me. Despite the difficult circumstances your mother has faced, she was able to leave home in search of her own happiness and take care of herself with dignity, which shows that she has always been strong in very challenging living conditions. At the same time, I also see that you are equally strong and admirable. Under your careful attention, your mother's condition has improved and you have been accepted into university. This is truly something worth recognizing and praising! As you said, no matter what we go through, life goes on day by day. In the face of life's hardships, some people may be knocked down, while others become even stronger, just like a tree that has weathered storms and stands taller. Your question is how to remain calm when faced with your mother's yelling and insults, and how to make her last days a little happier. What I want to tell you is, my dear child, you have already done your best. Your mother's condition has been truly challenging for you. I believe you have shown utmost patience in dealing with her, but you also have your own health issues and have undoubtedly endured a great deal of stress. So first and foremost, take care of yourself. Understand that there are limits to what we can do as humans. We cannot make everything perfect, but as long as we try our best, we can be at peace with ourselves. I also hope you can reach out to other support systems in society so that other relatives of your mother can provide help. Don't bear the burden all alone. I believe that you, who have gone through hardships and storms, will become stronger and more outstanding in your future life. Hugs to you once again!

It's not easy to see the experiences that the OP's mother and the OP have gone through. Maybe it's because they have seen the hardships in their lives that the OP hopes to make their mother's life better with their own strength in the remaining years. It's really touching. How old is the OP now, and how old is their mother? From the "conflict" between you and your mother, it seems that there may be many things that you are not consciously aware of at the level of consciousness: for example, the suppressed things in your mother's past life and the suppressed things in your shared life. In reality, it seems that it is your mother yelling and insulting you, but it may be more about her yelling and insulting someone from the past life, and "you" are just unintentionally being her "mediator," or unintentionally becoming a substitute for "certain individuals." Maybe your mother yells and insults you because she learned it from her own mother and only knows how to communicate with her children in this way, not using other methods. Maybe your mother yells and insults you due to health reasons. The OP can talk to their mother when she is in a calm mood and find out what happened at that moment from her perspective. They can also express their feelings to their mother in writing. I hope my reply can help you. Best wishes!

Hello, based on your description, I feel really sorry for your experiences. Your mother's difficult life is truly heart-wrenching. Your and your mother's struggles really make me want to give both of you a big hug. First, regarding your mother's illness, it is actually related to her upbringing and emotions. Throughout her life, your mother has been repressing herself. I believe that she has dissatisfaction, emotions, and pain from her past. But it seems like none of it can be resolved. One thing after another, your mother pretends that everything is fine, as you mentioned. She takes care of herself on the surface, but underneath, there is so much more going on with her. However, no one can truly care for your mother. After long-term repression, your mother eventually became sick. It can be said that her illness is largely due to psychological factors. Your mother's current bad temper, when you think about it, why is that? Take notice of how your mother expresses her love for you. Some people don't know how to express it, so even though they love, it comes out as anger, insults, blame, criticism, rejection, coldness... When your illness worsens, how does your mother react? Sit down and have a conversation with your mother, see where her emotional blockages lie. Perhaps you will see some changes and I hope this can help you.

Dear~, thank you for coming to my Answering Hall. Although I may not have the same experiences as you, we can still chat about the pattern of a person's life. It is similar to doing homework in school, from primary school to middle school, high school, and even entering society. Each stage has different tasks for us to complete. You may not be good at Chinese, and I may not be good at math. You may be excellent in English, and I may excel in history. So, let's see your strengths and advantages and start from there, focusing on what we can do. Here are a few tips for you: in your heart, say to your mother, "Everything is my fault, I'm sorry, please forgive me," 1008 times a day. Say "Thank you, I love you" 1080 times a day, and see if there is any improvement. There should be, as we have made many attempts. Looking forward to your feedback. Good luck!

question: Always speaking in contradictions? Why do friends talk in such a weird way?
description: When chatting with others, for example, when pursuing a girlfriend, he will speak in a sarcastic manner, saying that the girlfriend is the one pursuing him; for example, when borrowing a car, he will post on social media claiming it as his new ride; for example, when he only invested a few thousand in business, he will exaggerate and say that he invested over tens of thousands. What kind of mentality is this??

answers.answer_text: Hello. First, allow me to talk about my impression of you: * It seems that you are having difficulty understanding some of your friend's behaviors, such as bragging and exaggerating. This makes you feel uncomfortable and even seemingly disgusted. * It seems like you are mainly talking about your friend, and I haven't seen much information about you. * However, you seem to prefer a straightforward and factual way of expression and thinking. Now, allow me to share some of my thoughts: * Although the main content of your venting is about your perception of others, I guess your subconscious is actually trying to express some of your feelings and thoughts through evaluating others. * In classical psychoanalysis in psychology, a person's personality structure is divided into the id, ego, and superego. The id seeks to do pleasurable things regardless of consequences, the superego imposes strict moral standards on you, and the ego represents the real you, torn between the two. Perhaps you are familiar with this concept as well. * One possibility is that your superego does not allow you to boast or exaggerate, and emphasizes being factual. However, maybe your id actually craves the images of wealth, popularity, and status, even though you can't experience them yourself. Indulging in fantasizing about it might be satisfying to a certain extent. Your ego may lean more towards following the guidance of the superego, so you rarely speak bombastically like your friend. Your friend's id and superego may be similar to yours, but his ego couldn't resist the temptations of the id, leading to the expression of those desires in his exaggerated words and actions. * Your lack of understanding and even disdain towards your friend actually aligns with the demands of your superego within your personality. If you didn't evaluate your friend's behavior and words in this way, your ego might start questioning the restrictions imposed by your superego, and in the end, you might become unsure or gradually succumb to the desires of the id. * There can be many perspectives to understand both you and your friend. But understanding you necessitates knowing more about you, including your personality and values. So, please feel free to share more about your story. Take care.

Hello, what you're saying is actually more like vanity. To put it simply, it's bragging. So, we need to answer three questions: 1. What is vanity? 2. Factors that lead to vanity. 3. How to deal with people who have strong vanity? 1. What is vanity? Vanity is the excessive manifestation of self-esteem distortion. It is a character defect that pursues superficial appearances and is an abnormal social emotion and psychological state displayed by people in order to gain honor and attract general attention. 2. Factors that lead to vanity: a. Social and family environment In business families and rural families, exaggerated descriptions are often heard. The former is to increase one's own value in order to gain more benefits, while the latter is to cover up their embarrassment. In the internet industry, everyone has titles stacked up to a dozen, and it's inevitable to encounter some relatives of national leaders on the green-skin train. Of course, this is just an analogy without any discriminatory meaning. It's just that these phenomena are more common in these environments. Solid entrepreneurs and pragmatic farmers are the mainstream. b. Personal factors One reason may be that they have many friends who like to boast, or their reference frame is much better than theirs, and they are temporarily unable to catch up (for example, a junior clerk may have nothing special in the office, but can proudly say that they work for the government - just an analogy). Another reason may be to cover up the fact that they are not as outstanding as they appear. However, the essence is that their expectations for themselves are far from being met, so they show off verbally, just like we often say, the essence of arrogance is actually self-insecurity. 3. How to deal with people who have strong vanity? If you just dislike them, it's better not to say it out loud. Taking it a step further, you can slightly compliment them, and they will be very happy. If you want to correct them, perhaps it should be based on a good relationship with them, subtly influencing them with emotions and reasoning.

question: 16-year-old girl is very sensitive and easily experiences emotional breakdowns. What should she do if she is afraid of being abandoned?
description: Over the past five or six years, I've been particularly afraid of being disliked and feeling unworthy of love. I constantly worry about being abandoned and fear losing people. I don't know if I have a bit of social withdrawal, as I always prefer to be alone and instinctively avoid others when they approach me. Many people have grown tired of listening to my troubles, so now I keep everything to myself and don't talk to anyone anymore. I easily lose control and break down emotionally when facing certain situations, and I tend to rely on my boyfriend to help regulate my emotions. I am heavily influenced by my boyfriend, and my mood can easily turn for the better or worse. But the more I care about him, the more I fear losing him. I am particularly sensitive and have been diagnosed with depression. Whenever depressive feelings arise, it's difficult for me to adjust. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hi, dear questioner. It's fortunate to be the same age and gender as you. I can understand how girls feel happy, angry, sad, and joyful. The first question is whether it is worth being loved. Why would you doubt yourself, dear? Being sixteen is the most beautiful age for a girl. You shouldn't let yourself be trapped by depression. Such a lovely girl like you definitely deserves to be treated gently. It's normal for you to instinctively push people away when they approach you. I don't like it when people approach me either. Everyone has different ways of dealing with things. Some people are naturally good at socializing and become the center of attention in a crowd, while others are not good at interacting. Don't worry, dear. It's just a natural character trait. You don't need to think too much, dear. Girls are naturally sensitive to negative emotions and find it harder to recover from them. It seems unbearable for you to keep telling others about your problems repeatedly. Your heart is always restless. But even if others don't want to listen to your problems, don't keep them to yourself, dear. You can do more of the things you like and think about starting new things. For example, when I'm unhappy, I listen to English songs, which makes me feel much better. You can try it, dear. Regarding losing control of emotions, dear, please pay more attention to controlling them. Don't let your emotions become your master. Choose a healthy way to release them. Depression is not terrifying, dear. Look at it from a positive perspective. It will get better.

Hello, I hope my response can bring you some insights. First of all, I can see that the lovely person who asked the question has already realized their existing problems and has a desire to change, which is already great! So now, we should immediately seek positive changes. Here are a few small suggestions for your question: Get to know yourself again and find out the causes of depression. Fully utilize your strengths. Once you have identified your strengths, make full use of them. This will help increase your self-identity and become more confident. Don't pursue perfection. Nobody is perfect, so don't deny yourself completely because of a setback. If you immerse yourself in a sense of failure, you will feel disappointed, frustrated, and even helpless. Therefore, shift your focus to your strengths and don't just focus on your shortcomings. Accept yourself. No matter what kind of person you are, you are unique. Learn to be happy for yourself. Because you don't need everyone's approval, and you don't need to live like others. Accept your true self. I hope this can help you. If you have more questions or concerns, feel free to private message me or follow our official WeChat account: Mental Health Pro.

question: When angry, it is easy to tear up when trying to express thoughts or when being yelled at by others. What's going on?
description: When I was a child, I would easily cry when my parents criticized me and raised their voices at me. When I had thoughts and wanted to argue with them, I would start crying while talking. I try my best to control it because it makes me appear insecure. Nowadays, I mostly keep my thoughts to myself, but sometimes I really want to express my thoughts and frustrations. However, I still find my voice trembling and my emotions unstable. What's wrong with me? I don't like this because it makes it difficult for me to express my emotions properly. What should I do?
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, vulnerability and tears.

answers.answer_text: Post author, hello~ First, sending you a warm hug. I completely understand how you feel. The influence of childhood can have varying degrees of impact on our entire lives. As mentioned by the original poster, being criticized and yelled at during childhood because of being too weak and unable to reason with adults, crying became the best way to vent frustration. Over time, this emotional response became a reflex to protect oneself. So, when faced with similar situations as adults, we tend to cry just like when we were children. This is not a problem specific to the original poster. I suggest that next time you encounter such a situation, try to calm down and express yourself after your emotions have settled. Don't worry about what others might say about you or how they might criticize you. As long as you can articulate what you want to say, then it's a success. I hope the original poster can resolve their inner confusion and successfully overcome themselves. Best wishes.

question: I gave my first time to my boyfriend, but we broke up. I'm so scared, what should I do?
description: I gave myself to him for the first time... At that time, I didn't think we would separate. But now that we've broken up, I feel dirty about myself? I'm so scared... I actually mind if a guy is not a virgin, because I feel jealous thinking about the person I like being with someone else like that. But I'm not a virgin anymore either...? I can't help but dislike myself.
keywords: Love, managing relationships, sexual behavior, virginity complex.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP. In our early lives, our parents placed a great importance on sexual activity and sexual life due to moral and self-protection considerations. This was valuable to us when we were young, as it prevented us from experiencing forbidden fruit and getting hurt at a tender age. We protected ourselves with these simple moral values. However, now that we have grown up and become mature, at an age where we can take responsibility for ourselves and experience love, these moral concepts have become a hindrance and cause us distress. When we start a relationship, it is not because of the other person's sexual activity or whether they are a virgin or not, but because they meet our expectations. Please remember your first love; in the beginning, all you cared about were their appearance, attitude, and behavior towards you. When you were together, you only focused on the sweetness of the moment. Please rest assured that not only the beginning of your first love, but every relationship you will experience in the future will be the same. The topic of virginity will only be considered when it comes to the next stage of love and involves sexual activity. You mentioned that you would mind if the other person is not a virgin and would feel jealous. Even if the other person is a virgin, but has emotional experiences, you may still feel jealous. Even if the other person has no emotional experiences and simply passes by a beautiful woman on the street and takes a few extra glances, you may still feel jealous. Jealousy and possessiveness are normal emotions in love, and these emotions add sweetness and passion to love. Ultimately, jealousy and possessiveness stem from the fear of losing. We are afraid of losing something valuable and precious to us. If your next partner feels jealous for this reason, it indicates that you are cherished and loved by them. We don't care whether a stranger has emotional experiences or not because they have no relevance to us. Your value is not determined by whether you have engaged in sexual activity or have sexual experiences. I believe you should understand this point as well. You may be cute, have a sweet smile, or have a lively personality. These are your values, the beautiful parts of yourself that you show to the world, and they attract others to love and understand you. Please have confidence and do not describe yourself as "dirty". Even though you have separated and said goodbye to your previous relationship, I believe you also gained sweetness in that relationship. You entrusted your body to them, surely after careful consideration, but unfortunately, you couldn't continue that relationship. Sexual intimacy is a joyful experience that enhances our love life and is a natural progression in a relationship. I hope my personal insights can provide you with some insignificant help and I hope you can let go of the past and bravely embrace a new beginning.

Hello, Yiye Mingxin, I want you to know that some of the thoughts in our minds do not originate from within us, but rather from external influences. Just like your situation with the "first-night syndrome". Giving your first time to your ex-boyfriend and feeling dirty after the breakup, and believing that other boys are also dirty if they are not someone's first, is a result of social conditioning. 1. Social role: The initial social role of the "first-night syndrome" was a tool used by the upper class in feudal society to control women and restrict their conscious adherence to chastity. 2. Physiological effects: Since you have just ended your first relationship and may not have had many previous partners, this feeling is understandable. Indeed, promiscuity can lead to diseases, and your feeling of being "dirty" also partly stems from the physiological aversion to promiscuity. 3. Psychological effects: Jealousy arises from the thought of the person you like being with someone else, and you find yourself in the same situation, so you feel afraid and dislike yourself. This is also related to the lack of sex education in our country, where sex is a topic that's difficult to talk about, and we cannot view sexual relationships properly. Talking about sex always has associations with being "dirty". You need to change your preconceptions. Here's a simple example: animals do not have as much moral condemnation towards "sex". They follow their instincts. On the one hand, this can be seen as animals being "inferior", but on the other hand, it's actually humans being restrained by "morality". I am not advocating for people to behave like animals, but sometimes humans need to return to their true nature and embrace their natural instincts. Sex is not as important or as disgraceful as we imagine it to be. It is merely a part of natural selection, but humans have assigned many other attributes to it. You can watch scientific documentaries that depict human sexuality in a formal manner, without holding onto prejudice. You are not wrong, and there is no need to dislike yourself. Face sexuality and face yourself. Good luck.

The first time and all that are just shackles imposed on women by society. But you can't lock yourself up because of this. You are an individual, a free individual, and your sexuality is your own freedom with anyone. In principle, you have no obligation to remain pure for anyone. In ancient times, the requirement for women to remain pure was mainly to ensure that the child belonged to the man. Women were subordinate to men in a patriarchal society. But now, men and women are equal. No one is anyone's possession, so how can there be a concept of being "dirty"? If anyone despises you for not being pure, then this person, this boyfriend, is not worth it. After all, the most important thing in a relationship is sex, and if it completely overshadows any spiritual connection and makes him have opinions of you, then being together with him has no meaning at all.

Hello, scared girl, I don't think there's anything wrong with your thoughts. Everyone has their own views on love and sex. It's great to want to save your first time for someone you truly love, and it's also theirs to have as well. Being completely loyal to each other, after meeting amidst countless others, and staying together for a long time, isn't that beautiful? What's wrong with that? We have the right to choose our own views on love and sex in this open world. To only date and have sex with one person in our lifetime. Why can't we choose such thoughts? Why can't we choose this kind of love? I say it's good because I have witnessed this beauty. It happened with a couple who knew each other in high school and were dating throughout college. After graduating, they entered society and dated for many years. The man had normal sexual desires, how could he not? But the woman remained steadfast, believing that if the man truly loved her, he would understand, accept her decision, and if he threatened to break up, then it would prove that he didn't love her enough. They had intense arguments and fights, but the woman stood her ground because she believed in the purity and beauty of a lifelong commitment to one person. She shared her desires with the man. This pure and beautiful love touched the man's heart, and they reconciled. They started their relationship without sex and continued to adjust until they got married. Besides their views on sex, they also had differences in lifestyle habits, etc. What kind of fairy tale love is this? In this modern society where both men and women are so open-minded, there's actually a woman like her who holds on to such a belief, and she also found a man who is willing to accept and accompany her. So, I always remember and marvel at the existence of such beautiful reality. The only thing you did wrong is that you didn't hold on to your boundaries, you didn't stick to your choices. When your boyfriend wanted to have sex for the first time, did you hesitate? Did you refuse? After your boyfriend brought up the idea of breaking up, did you have any regrets? Did you regret giving yourself away so easily? Since you have chosen a lifelong commitment to one person, you should stick to it. Only have sex on your wedding night, this is a principle and a boundary. Failing to hold onto your boundaries is a very scary thing. Think about your fear and despair now, what you lost was the beautiful life you always wanted. I think this incident, girl, you should always remember and be a person with principles and boundaries. Learn to say no and stick to your own choices. Otherwise, there will be other things happening in the future that will make you feel dark and wonder why things have turned out this way against your will. For example, if your mother-in-law keeps demanding things, or classmates keep borrowing money, or giving in to your children over and over again. Think about how many principles you have in your life, please stick to them. Stick to your principles and boundaries, and give yourself a clear conscience. Good luck, girl. Forgot to mention, the incident has already happened, and you can choose a different attitude towards life. You can choose to have sex while dating. Having a harmonious sexual life in marriage is also important. What if you find out after getting married that your sex life is not harmonious? Divorce? The only thing to note is to take precautions before marriage, stick to your principles, and always use protection, or consistently take short-acting contraceptives. Based on your initial conservative choices, let me inform you again that things like withdrawal method and safe period are not reliable at all. Only condoms are the safest and most reliable contraceptive method, and they also help prevent gynecological diseases. Remember to use a condom consistently. Forgetting to take short-acting contraceptives may also reduce their effectiveness. Read more about sexual health education for women, protect yourself, and remember you have the right to make decisions. Hopefully, you can see that it doesn't matter whether you're a virgin or not, you are still you, and you can even be better. Be a woman with principles and charm. Keep going!

Hello, sweetheart. This psychological issue is influenced by traditional moral and cultural understandings as well as mainstream societal norms. However, with the progress of society, this problem has been increasingly addressed with equality and openness. Ultimately, it comes down to one's own sense of self-worth and whether they feel good about themselves. Besides taking responsibility for their own choices, individuals should also realize that it is not entirely their fault. Therefore, it's important to treat oneself better and truly love oneself first in order to have the ability to choose someone who treats them better.

It is good to have such thoughts, but it can also be dangerous. Good, because it shows that you value and love yourself. Dangerous, because this mindset can increase the risk of developing depression in the future. It is said that love leads to sex, and we should approach love and sex from a correct perspective and starting point. Life is incomplete without love or just sex. Whether it is in life or in relationships, we need to have a correct attitude. Take yourself as an example: if you are not willing for your boyfriend to give his "first time" to someone else, then how do you think guys would feel about you? So, don't overly obsess about each other's so-called "first time." If you truly encounter someone you love and who loves you, then the concept of "first time" will not be as important. Let the past be a beautiful memory of your first love. I hope that in the future, you will not be bound by the concept of sex, but rather be true to yourself. In life, always look forward. Even if you look back, it will only be fragments of memories from your journey of growth. Love yourself, love your family, and eventually find someone who loves and is loved by you. Keep going!

I used to think that way too. I thought we would never separate, but reality gave me a hard slap. I can only say that the girl is not right for you, you can find someone better. Remember, you are the only one who can love yourself in this world. Of course, if you can find someone who loves you more, they will never mind your first time. Although everyone wants to be with their most loved person for the first time. But this is really not a big deal. After all, there are still many people who love you in this world. I'll give you a little advice, you need to learn to accept it slowly. Seriously, first enhance your own capacity for happiness. Seriously, learn to smile even when things are tough. First, learn to forgive yourself. At the same time, think about what you want to do. Unless you never want to date or get married in the future. I hope you meet someone you love and who loves you! I'm not a psychologist. I just hope you have a better future. You're amazing for being able to talk about this, beautiful girl. I think you're great. Why am I talking like an old person? I've been like this since my twenties, haha.

question: I have a friend who seems to have a dissociative identity disorder. How can I comfort her?
description: I have a friend who told me that her dad often hits and scolds her at home, and sometimes he gets so overwhelmed that he wants to commit suicide. She hears a voice in her head that comforts her, and she is particularly sensitive to that voice. Sometimes, she feels a bit dizzy in her mind, and the world around her feels a bit unreal. I want to ask if her alter ego has already awakened?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Nice to meet you! I hope my answer can help you. Please don't jump to conclusions. If you notice any symptoms, you can take your friend to a tertiary hospital at the city level or above for a medical check-up and receive scientific treatment. This is the best approach. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. I hope my answer can be helpful to you. I am very willing to listen to your story!!!

question: Sometimes when I joke with my husband, why do I always feel like he lacks magnanimity?
description: I am actually very generous, but sometimes I want to joke with my husband or just act cute in front of him to tease him, intentionally not giving him the food I am eating. However, he gets very angry and seriously says that our eldest son is just like me, very selfish! Then he doesn't like my behavior or I see the disgusted expression on his face. I don't think so, I just think he is not open-minded enough, too petty.
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, and marriage management.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner! Hugs to you~ After reading your description, it seems that you're not quite satisfied with your husband's personality. Maybe you're more easygoing in life, which is causing a difference in personalities between you two. Based on your description, it appears that your husband doesn't quite understand when you're just joking around in your daily life. In my opinion, the examples you gave are just small matters, but why do they trigger such a big reaction from your husband? Perhaps you need to take this seriously. Since I don't know much about your family situation, I can only offer advice based on my own experience. I suggest that after noticing a change in your husband's attitude, you can explain the situation to him in a timely manner and let him understand the context. Because everyone has different personalities, the degree to which we accept jokes also varies. Sometimes what we think is a joke may not be seen that way by others. Maybe your husband is more cautious by nature. So, it's necessary for you to explore the level of joking in your daily life and make sure that the jokes are ones that the other person can accept. Most importantly, communication is key. You can try to understand why he reacts so strongly, as communication can solve most problems.

question: Depressed, suppressed, lacking passion, lacking energy, not interested in socializing, what should I do?
description: Talk about my own problems: 1. I don't like dealing with the same person all the time, like a colleague who constantly asks trivial questions and talks about insignificant things. No matter how annoyed I am, he always smiles and it makes me feel very oppressed. 2. Sometimes I temporarily ignore my girlfriend, and she would send me messages like "why did other people in the group get red envelopes (money) and not tell me about it?" Do I have to be the second to grab the red envelope and then go over and say, "Quickly grab the red envelope before it's gone?" Or make fun of her, like "someone else sent red envelopes and you didn't grab them, hahaha..." Because of this, I am really hurt by the questioning, feeling emotionally low, and lacking energy in everything I do. I often embarrass myself at work, although I know that not all the problems are because of my girlfriend. 3. When others make jokes about my girlfriend in public, I don't immediately stand up for her and I don't know if it's appropriate. When my girlfriend is upset, I feel very discouraged and I think, am I heartless? My girlfriend also questions me like this. People's hearts are made of flesh, so why can't I feel anything?

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I can see that you have listed three issues that bother you: problems with interpersonal relationships with others, intimacy issues with your girlfriend, and perhaps you have also noticed that there are problems in dealing with yourself. Regarding the first problem that troubles you, feeling unable to get along with a certain colleague and not liking to deal with him, but he always asks this and that, making you feel oppressed. First, if you are sure that this colleague is really bothering you, making it unbearable for you, then I suggest you keep your distance and try to have as little contact with him as possible. Or you can express your feelings indirectly, that you need peace and quiet, and let the other person understand your boundaries and please do not disturb. But if you feel that it might be due to your own bad mood, low spirits, and irritability, and being with others makes you feel like a psychological burden, then we can regulate our emotions. I recommend practicing mindfulness and meditation, having a calm conversation with yourself, understanding your inner self, listening to the voice within, and trying to understand and accept your inner self, learning to get along and "communicate" with yourself, "seeing" and comforting our inner emotions. It's an important lesson for our growth~ The second and third issues are about the problems you have in your relationship with your girlfriend, feeling upset and lacking vitality due to being questioned by your girlfriend over small matters. Also, because you didn't help your girlfriend and didn't consider her feelings, she became very angry and felt that you were indifferent.
