It makes you start doubting yourself, whether you are really like what your girlfriend says, unable to figure out what's wrong with you~ From your descriptions, I can sense that your emotions are not very stable, you are easily influenced by the outside world or others, and you become a bit unable to control your emotions~ You feel depressed, oppressed, lacking passion, vitality, and having difficulty in communication — perhaps you have encountered a bottleneck or confusion in life, unable to find yourself, losing your goals to strive for; or you have encountered someone or something that troubles you and you can't handle or solve it, causing distress, frustration, and helplessness. You have fallen into a depressed and anxious state, unable to relieve or get out of negative emotions~ I suggest that you communicate and exchange more with your family, girlfriend, and friends, try to express your inner feelings to someone you trust, even if they may not necessarily be able to help, at least you can vent your feelings and let them "see" you, which may make you feel better in your inner self. In addition to the aforementioned meditation practice, you can also write psychological notes, record your true inner feelings. This is another way to "release" and have a good soothing effect on emotions, which is also helpful for relieving emotions. I hope you can be confident, strong, and have faith, which will also be helpful for yourself. Persist in being yourself and believe that it will bring more sense of security to your girlfriend, allowing her to feel that you are more reliable and trustworthy. What do you think?

How old are you? How long has this situation been going on? What were you like before? Have there been any incidents? From the description, it seems that you are a sensitive and cautious person. You can keenly perceive your own emotions, but you have difficulty expressing them. I'm not sure if you don't know how to express yourself, if you're afraid to express yourself, or if you're not sure if you should express yourself. If you don't know how to express yourself, you can directly explain your feelings and emotions to the other person. For example, in the first situation, you can say, "I'm feeling annoyed right now and not in the mood to listen. I need some time to be alone." This way, you can express yourself without making the other person uncomfortable. If you're afraid to express yourself, think about what consequences you're afraid of after expressing yourself. Are those consequences really worth being afraid of? If you really can't handle the consequences, you can write down your emotions that you can't express verbally. If you're unsure, think about whether the situation and context are suitable for expressing your emotions. Then, later on, try to understand what happened, what caused it, and how you can handle such situations better in the future. In fact, most of us don't know how to respond appropriately in emergency situations. Even if you realize afterwards that your reaction was less than ideal, there's no need to blame or feel guilty. Trust that at that time, you made the safest and most reliable choice for yourself. Throughout our lives, we are constantly on the path of self-development and growth. Don't rush, take it slowly, and everything will be alright!

Hello, thank you very much for your trust. I see the three issues you mentioned. I can feel your clear depression, and I really hope that you can express your emotions and needs clearly. But at that moment, it is difficult for you to express your needs, show care for others, and refuse some things. Regarding your situation, the main problems you are currently facing are in interpersonal relationships. One is with colleagues or less close relationships, and the other is with intimate relationships, like your girlfriend. For these two situations, I would like to offer some suggestions. 1. For relationships with colleagues, you can assertively express your boundaries, for example, saying that you are a bit busy at the moment and may not be able to help them. Or explain that you are not really interested in what they are talking about and may not have any valuable advice to offer. 2. For intimate relationships, if you find it difficult to deeply experience the emotions of this girlfriend, you can observe a few things about her. One is her tone of voice, and another is her facial expressions. You can say something regularly, like "You seem angry. I don't know how to help you in front of all these people. I feel disappointed too. In the future, please let me know what you would like me to say and how you want me to act." These are just some simple answers to your problems. If needed, you can search for me and contact me. I hope you find happiness!

Hello! After reading your description, I feel that your mood is quite low, and you are experiencing distress about relationships in your life. These worries have accumulated and are causing you trouble. Although it is normal to experience emotional fluctuations, it can bring different feelings and experiences to different people from the same situation. In your description, you mentioned your colleague, and when he rambles and asks questions, you feel annoyed. However, you mentioned that he is still smiling. You feel suppressed and frustrated, so how do you express your feelings to him? I believe this must have happened repeatedly to make you feel so suppressed. In fact, I just want to say, have you expressed your feelings to him? If you are reluctant to express yourself, perhaps he is completely unaware of your feelings. In your interaction with your girlfriend, you also feel demanded. This part seems similar to your interaction with your colleague, as they both have demands on you, whether it's asking questions or blaming you for not reminding her about someone giving out red envelopes. It seems that you feel overwhelmed by all these demands. I cannot know how you usually interact with people in your daily life, but from these few sentences of description, I can sense that your feelings seem to have been overlooked, and they are all taking from you (or making demands), while you are struggling and feeling exhausted. As for the third point on your emotional perception, I think that based on the descriptions of the previous two points, you are able to perceive emotions. However, you are always being asked to experience others' needs. Many times, we also need others to see our feelings, and we need to see our own feelings as well. Otherwise, it can be very difficult!

Personal opinion: ① You can think about why others would do this. ② Treat others as yourself, if you receive the treatment from others, whether good or bad, how would you respond? ③ It may be helpful to give the other person some response, for example, when someone greets you, you can also greet them in return. ④ Your girlfriend questions why you "can't feel the hearts of others." From the incident of "you didn't remind her to grab the red envelope and she complained," perhaps she is complaining that "you haven't been caring about her." Care is the sincere understanding and love that one person gives to another, whether it is spontaneous or begged by the other person. Therefore, you may need to pay more attention to how many times you have treated your girlfriend like this, whether it's your problem or her problem. ⑤ Your behavior may be a subconscious psychological response formed in some familiar environments in the past. If that's the case and you want to change, you may consider watching some related videos to help change yourself. ⑥ You didn't remind your girlfriend to grab the red envelope, so why not remind her in similar situations in the future? I don't know the mechanism of grabbing red envelopes, but maybe if you remind her to grab the second-to-last one, she will feel comforted. ⑦ If it really isn't your problem but someone else's, if someone is causing trouble and being unreasonable, such as repeatedly making trouble without reason, you can choose how to respond on your own.

Having a girlfriend is better for communication than being alone. By being with each other, you can fully exercise your communication skills. Pay more attention to her and talk to her more, you will become more active yourself. If you don't find the discussion topics interesting, it may be because you are not involved in them and therefore cannot feel the fun. Gradually, you may think that all these things are boring. If she likes grabbing red envelopes, you can remind her more often, sometimes grabbing red envelopes can be a source of joy. Being too focused on yourself, when you spend more time caring about her and your surroundings, your inner conflicts will be reduced. Try to break free from just being trapped in your own situation and think more about the other person. Now you have a girlfriend to accompany you, at least you won't be lonely. If you feel depressed, for example, if you are motionless, it is better to do something, even if it is discussing what to eat today or how to spend the weekend with her. Being silent all the time will only keep you in the same state, so it is better to do something, at least it can reduce negative feelings.

Hello, dear host. First, when someone smiles at you, even when you are impatient with them, it means that you haven't made it clear to them how you're feeling. Additionally, you haven't learned to express your emotions clearly, which has led to the lack of understanding from the other person. If you encounter this situation again, you can directly tell them. Sometimes, being dismissive can hurt more than being straightforward. The second and third points can be summarized together. It's true that your girlfriend's behavior is biased, but from your description, it doesn't seem like you have strong feelings for her. You don't seem to be very invested in your girlfriend's issues, and the relationship might be superficial. Furthermore, if you really like someone, you would certainly want to go along with their wishes. Based on your actions, it's obvious that you are not like that. You should seriously consider the current status of your relationship with your girlfriend and its future development. As for your lack of passion, feeling suppressed, and being depressed, it's mostly likely due to not having any goals or things you enjoy. Only when you have passion for everything will you have a sense of anticipation for the world. You can try developing some interests and hobbies.

question: "No matter how outstanding or amazing you may be, the question always remains: what is the meaning of life?"
description: What is the purpose of being alive? As it is now, life is in a cycle, repeating over and over again. In the current human life, generation after generation tries to live, have children, and when they grow up, it's the same cycle. It continues to repeat. Whether you are an exceptional person or an ordinary person, you are still repeating. Also, all life, one by one, disappears and reappears. But what is its significance?

answers.answer_text: I feel like it might be the sense of experience. From a macro perspective, the lives of any person, animal, or plant are like dust; compared to the billions of years of Earth's history, a person's life of a few decades cannot leave much of a trace. However, this macro perspective is made up of countless micro moments like a year, a day, an hour. Each day in our lives is experienced one by one. How we spend each day in the span of a few decades, what we can experience is completely different. Although we go to work every Monday to Friday, the work content is similar every day, such as browsing resumes, making phone calls to schedule interviews, interviewing, negotiating salaries, and arranging new employee onboarding... But today, maybe we will come across a particularly suitable resume, have a particularly smooth phone conversation, and directly schedule an interview for the next day. When we hang up the phone, we feel really good and think about buying a big cup of hazelnut latte at noon to relax under the sun. The next day, the candidate stands us up and doesn't come, it's really disappointing. Every day, there will be different experiences. After experiencing disappointment, maybe there will be an even better resume tomorrow! Colleagues, friends, family, children are changing every day, giving us different challenges and emotions every day. A high school classmate who hasn't been in contact for many years may suddenly come to town and invite us for a meal, and on the way, we help a mother pushing a stroller by holding the door for her, receiving her heartfelt thanks... Every little thing can bring us special experiences, good or bad, pleasant, sad, angry, painful, and disappointing... These experiences may enrich our inner selves and make us who we are now, and we can become an even better version of ourselves in the future.

question: After resigning, the company tries to retain me. Should I stay?
description: I am currently working in an overseas branch of a trading company. This company has a family-style management model and emphasizes loyalty. They hired me to do some optimization work, but after I arrived, I discovered various problems. For example, non-professionals are dominating the work of professionals, and there is chaos and lack of trust in management, to the point where I cannot carry out my work properly. Later, I decided to resign because of an incident, but the company has been trying to retain me. I told them that I still wanted to leave, but I would like to try doing things my way for two months first. However, I encountered significant resistance when I tried to implement my ideas. At the same time, through a friend's introduction, I interviewed with another company in the same city. The interview went well, but the salary offered was lower than what I'm getting in my current company. Taking other factors into consideration, I politely declined the offer. Later, I found out that the person in charge of the company where I interviewed knows the leader of my current company. They called to inquire about my situation, and now everyone in my current company knows about my job interview with the other company, but they still want others to convince me to stay. Just today, the company I interviewed with called me again, expressing their desire for me to work there. I am now torn about whether I should resign and go there.
keywords: Occupation, career management, workplace relationships, work pressure.

answers.answer_text: This is the fourth question I am answering, hoping to be helpful to you. As the saying goes, the workplace is like a battlefield, in the workplace, apart from interests, there is nothing else! This point must be clear, everything is about profit for the company and for you! In order to help you make a good choice, let's analyze the situation you are in and your subconscious mind. 1. Regarding the current situation: you are relatively satisfied with the salary of your current job, but you are not satisfied with the operation mode of the current company and some criticisms of a traditional family business. You have even reached the point of considering leaving the job, although you have not resigned temporarily and are struggling to push the work in your own way. However, the fact that you have already interviewed with another company has happened and you have been recognized. In your subconscious, you also have expectations for the new company, but the salary is not as expected. In addition, because the two company's bosses have connections, your intention to seek another way has also been known by the boss of the current company. The current situation may be a bit awkward and there may be more uncertain risks in the future, so you are struggling to decide whether to stay or leave. 2. About the risks: firstly, the direct reduction of salary is definitely the most basic consideration and will have the most direct impact. In addition, the importance of loyalty in family businesses will directly affect the development of your current work. This is a big taboo in similar family businesses, unless the boss makes a wise decision or you are truly outstanding in your abilities, otherwise there will definitely be hidden dangers in the future, which will eventually have an impact. Finally, the decision to stay or leave, when we work outside, we are all tools, and the goal is to support ourselves and our families through work. The company values certain values that are beneficial to its development. Considering your current situation, there are risks whether you stay or leave, and you can only weigh the pros and cons and make a choice based on maximizing your interests. 3. About the decision: this is a comprehensive consideration and requires an overall analysis, such as money, pressure, career prospects, reputation, interpersonal relationships, and so on. This is a difficult process, and I believe you have been struggling with it. Let's make it simple and use the anticipated results to deduce how to choose. Result 1: stay in the current company. In a family business, they despise employees who do not follow their rules. They only look at the results and whether they bring benefits. If there is any slight mistake, it will be blamed on you, and you will eventually be replaced sooner or later. In addition, they will bring up the issue of loyalty, and they must have grievances about it, so you have to be on guard. Of course, it also depends on your ability and the company's degree of need. If you are truly outstanding and the company cannot do without you, or if the boss really recognizes you, then have an open and honest communication with the company, explain everything clearly, and enhance consensus, then stay in the company, after all, more money! Result 2: leave! Go to the new company. There are two possibilities. One is that you find the opportunity is good after joining, the company is of high quality, there are no criticisms of a family business, no restrictions, and you can truly achieve results and realize your value. In that case, I think you should just go. The other possibility is that you find no change after joining, you are still a tool, you have no say, you receive even less money than in the previous company, and you may even be more passive in your work. This is difficult to avoid, and it is not a good idea to go back to the previous company, so you must clarify again in the employment contract to reduce unnecessary risks. In summary, there are two outcomes and two choices. I can only help you analyze but not decide. In life, we face multiple choices, and this time, I hope you make the right choice. It is best to listen to your inner self and remember that the future journey is long. Based on comprehensive risk avoidance, you must consider all aspects and make every effort to protect your own maximum interests.

You can't have your cake and eat it too, the meaning of this phrase is that if we want to get something, we must give up another part of it. So, working in a company will definitely have its good side, such as a high salary, but there will also be aspects that you find unfavorable, like chaotic management or lack of opportunities for personal growth. To be more specific, you can make a list of the advantages and benefits of this company, and then compare it with the reasons for wanting to quit. Write down each point and see which one has more benefits for you or which one you don't want to leave. Next, analyze your own reasons, is it because of management issues that you're unable to develop at work? Or what efforts can you make personally to change the work environment for the better? There's a saying that "people strive for higher goals, while water flows to lower ground," but there's also another saying that "when one mountain looks at another, it always appears higher." When we don't know much about a place, we tend to have more idealized fantasies about it. However, when we are actually in that place, we are more likely to be bothered by its shortcomings and dissatisfaction. So, you can try to see if there really isn't anything worth staying in your current situation? If that's really the case, then it might be time to make up your mind and leave. Talking about the company, proper management indeed requires scientific management methods. However, previous research has shown that scientific management, especially in small and medium-sized enterprises in China, accounts for a very small proportion, as little as 20%. So, on the one hand, we can search for companies that have scientific management to work for, or we can use the knowledge and experience we have gained to provide feedback and implement more scientific and optimized management, guiding the company onto a more correct path. You can suggest communication and urge the managers to consider whether outdated management methods can be changed to improve the scientific nature of management. When we enter society, we will face choices, and how to choose becomes a subject that we need to learn. Can we make choices? Do we have methods to choose, or do we have reasons we can't choose? Is it impossible to refuse? Do we want to change others? Can't we make changes ourselves? If a person has a strong sense of self, they would hope that the environment would cooperate with them more. But with rational thinking, this is not possible. Therefore, while maintaining a certain sense of self, we also have to adapt to the environment and make changes. Each person needs to think, grasp, experience, and decide on this balance. I hope my answer is helpful to you, and know that the world loves you.

I think the original poster has already made a decision whether to stay or leave. In the early stages, there was already an answer - "the interview went well, but the salary was lower than the current company, so I politely declined." The reason for the internal conflict now may be more because "the current company knows about my interview with another company." Perhaps you are afraid that if you stay, you will occasionally think about your past "betrayal" and feel ashamed and guilty. Perhaps you are afraid that if you stay, the current company might "play tricks" on you due to your past "betrayal," and ultimately things might end badly or harm your reputation. Similarly, I feel that if you go to the new company, you will also face these two concerns. You should know that these two companies are in the same city, and the leaders of both companies know each other, so it seems that their relationship should be good. Otherwise, the leader of the new company wouldn't just call and ask the leader of the previous company. Such situations are not uncommon in reality. You haven't done anything outrageous, so whether you stay or leave, please follow your heart. As long as you do things sincerely and with a clear conscience, that's enough.

Let's first talk about your previous company. From your disclosure, it seems that you were involved in management work. It's hard for me to imagine that a company with military-style management like this would have problems with chaos and mistrust in management. It seems that this militarized management is only superficial and hasn't truly integrated military principles into it. I'm not sure what position you held in this company, but based on the management chaos and mistrust you mentioned, if you weren't in the top management level, no matter how capable you are, it would be difficult to change this situation. I can imagine the resistance you would face is unimaginable. Personally, I think if you were to play such a role in this company (without core control and the power to revise systems), in the end, you would only tire yourself out without achieving any results, which is what they call "working hard but with no gain". Even if you are relatively satisfied with the salary, internally, it would still feel very oppressive. Speaking from the perspective of job choices, I think for you personally, where you choose to work is your right. Because we have the power to choose, there is no reason to say which companies are good or bad. Making the final choice is only based on our own work demands. As for who knows whom, it's not really relevant to us, and you don't need to worry too much about it. Whether leaving this current company means someone will speak ill of you or hold a grudge against you, a capable person never fears these things, and potential companies won't care about them either. They only care about one thing: who can bring the company maximum profits. Talking about anything else is just nonsense. I hope my shallow insights can be of some help to you, and I wish you to find a suitable company as soon as possible, to do the work you love and achieve the value of life.

Hello! It seems that you are more concerned about the compatibility between the corporate culture and your own. A company that has come this far must have developed its own unique style and inertia. It is indeed difficult to completely change it in a short period of time. If there is a significant difference between a company's culture and your values, it may be difficult for you to identify and continue to survive. The intention of the company's efforts to keep you may depend on whether you can reach a consensus through sincere communication. If your work can benefit the company and help you find your own value, that would be great.

question: Do you constantly reflect on every sentence and belittle yourself?
description: I need to reflect on myself after every sentence I say, and I feel really awful about myself.

answers.answer_text: Hello, hug. I don't know how long this kind of self-evaluation "feeling bad about yourself" has been around. Every time you say something, you have to reflect on yourself. It's so tiring and unrewarding, constantly lingering in your ears. I imagine you must be very upset. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ In your impression, do you remember the first time you evaluated yourself like this, when and what happened? Who were the people around you at the time? How did you feel when you evaluated yourself? What did you do? What did you say? What kind of expression was on your face? Now, looking back, if the current you stood in front of the past you, what would you like to say or do to the past you? If it were me, I would definitely hug the sad me and say, "You've been working hard. I know you've done well!" -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ Psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud proposed the structural theory of the id, ego, and superego. The id (completely unconscious) represents desire, suppressed by consciousness. The ego (mostly conscious) is responsible for dealing with the real world. The superego (partially conscious) is the conscience or internal moral judgment. The superego is the regulator in the personality structure, governed by the principle of perfection, monitoring the ego and internalizing the symbols of the father figure and cultural norms. In other words, the formation of the superego is mainly related to important caregivers in childhood, judging whether a person is "good" or "bad" and what one "should" or "should not" do. From this perspective, "feeling bad about yourself" may be the definition of yourself given by important others in your childhood, which gradually transforms into the judgment of your superego towards yourself. So, who is this important other person? In your memory, do you remember any occasions when something like this happened? What was his facial expression when he said "you're bad"? What did he do? How did you feel? I imagine that, like now, you were very sad and upset at that time. However, it is not your fault. In childhood, in order to survive and grow up, we had to rely on others and let them evaluate us indiscriminately. In fact, you are very brave. In such a sad situation, you have overcome it time after time. Now, you have grown up and can take responsibility for yourself and cheer yourself on. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ Now, please ask yourself the following four questions. Is it true that you feel bad about yourself? Can you be sure it is true? How do you react when you hold this idea? Can you find a reason to let go of that idea? Can you find a reason to hold that idea without any anxiety? What kind of person are you when you don't have that idea? These are four sentences from the book "A Turn of Mind," which has helped many people. I wonder what answers or different experiences you will get after asking yourself. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ In addition, you can ask yourself, you said every time you say something, you reflect on yourself and feel bad about yourself. So, are there any exceptions? Have you ever said something and felt that you are not so bad? When was that? What happened? When you say you feel bad about yourself, if you give a score of 0-10 to bad, with 0 indicating good and 10 indicating very bad, can you define a score for each thing or each sentence? Observe how you act when it's a 0 or 1. Perhaps this can be your direction for improvement next time. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ I hope my answer can give you some references and thoughts. The world and I love you.

Hello, first of all, I want to give you a hug and sympathize with you. Constantly belittling yourself and feeling inadequate indicates that you are a person who is more sensitive and lacks confidence. This may be related to your past experiences. During your growth process, your parents may not have given you positive responses and feedback. They may have often criticized or belittled you, lacking praise and encouragement. Over time, you will start to feel inferior. The family environment has a great influence on a person. Different treatments can lead to different personalities and self-evaluations. Over time, you will often put yourself down, fearing making mistakes, and speaking cautiously. You can improve the habit of self-degradation through conscious correction. First, you should try to learn to accept yourself. Accept your current state, allow yourself to make mistakes, and don't be too strict with yourself. Secondly, you need to find the true reasons for your self-deprecation. Explore the specific reasons that lead you to always doubt yourself, and then take corresponding actions to stop when you start belittling yourself. Finally, find a hobby or interest that you enjoy. Start with something you are good at, and over time, you will improve and gain a sense of accomplishment, thereby enhancing your self-confidence. I hope these suggestions can help you. Keep going! Best wishes!

question: Why do I feel very inferior and think that I am useless, and I don't know how to make efforts?
description: I used to suffer from depression, but I got better under the doctor's treatment. I have already stopped taking medication. However, for the past month, I can't sleep at night and have trouble getting up during the day. I feel like I'm a worthless person and can't accomplish anything. I have a lot of self-doubt. Even if I start studying, I still feel like I am useless.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, guilt and shame, fear and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Do you think there is a connection between feelings of inferiority and depression? Is it possible to have feelings of inferiority during a depressive episode and then feel much better after the depression improves? You mentioned that you stopped taking medication after your depression improved, but recently you've been experiencing poor sleep and low mood. Could it be that your depression is recurring? It is important to keep up with regular check-ups while treating depression. I suggest you go to the hospital for a check-up in a timely manner. Everyone has strengths and weaknesses, and you are no exception. If it's difficult to think of your strengths for now, it's okay. That's because your mood is currently low, and you are focusing too much on negative things while neglecting your own shining points. You can try thinking about the good things you did or the progress you made each day before going to bed. It can be anything, even small things like going to bed five minutes earlier today. Don't underestimate those five minutes. Many small steps add up to significant progress. Don't rush, take it slow. Keep going! These are just some suggestions that I hope can help you. Take care!

question: What should I do if I have a habit of hiding myself and want to change?
description: I feel very uncomfortable when people notice what I am doing during social interactions, such as what music I am listening to or what book I am reading. If someone notices, I feel embarrassed and believe that others will definitely make fun of me. In reality, I understand that others are not really concerned about these things and they might even have similar interests. However, deep down, I still try to hide my actions. Do you have any suggestions on how to change this?
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ It might be a manifestation of our lack of security in the environment when we hide our behavior. The surrounding environment includes people or the interpersonal atmosphere. What causes us to lack a sense of security? The OP needs to further observe themselves and can do so by looking back on past experiences. Have there been experiences of being laughed at by others in the past? I think we can change ourselves from these aspects: building self-confidence. To make friends, it is necessary to expose ourselves to some extent. This exposure means letting others know what we are interested in, such as books or favorite songs, which will help others understand us to a certain extent. We should realize that there is nothing embarrassing about letting others know us appropriately. Everyone is the same, not perfect, and is growing slowly. Try to communicate with others with an open mindset. Try to be a little more courageous and proactive, and maybe you will make friends. Don't be afraid; everyone has the same mindset when they are not familiar with each other at the beginning.

Hello, after reading your description, I feel like I see myself! I used to be the same way. When I was in school, I always preferred to sit in the concealed corner next to the wall, rather than in the middle of the classroom where I would stand out. During meetings, I would instinctively choose a seat in the back row and avoid sitting in the front row where I would be noticed. I didn't want others to see me! Fortunately, like you, I have become aware of this habit. Through continuous self-reflection and understanding, I realized that it might be because of fear! Fear of being laughed at, fear of being rejected, fear of being criticized, fear... To avoid all of this, I would hide myself, in order to safely evade what I was afraid of! If we want to change this habit of hiding ourselves, we need to have the courage to face our fears! So what if someone mocks us? So what if someone rejects us? So what if someone criticizes us? What do these things mean? They mean: I am not good enough. We are afraid of others saying that we are not good enough! Why are we so afraid of others saying that we are not good enough? It is because deep down inside us, there is a belief: I am not good enough! When we can fully accept ourselves, both the good and the not-so-good, it is all part of who we are, the real us. We are not afraid of being judged by others because we know ourselves. It's like if I'm bald, and you call me bald, I won't be angry because I know myself and I accept my baldness! So, the fundamental solution is to understand ourselves, accept ourselves, both the good and the not-so-good, because all of it is who I am, the unique and different me!

Hello, I understand your feelings very well. I've experienced being hesitant to let others see what I was doing before, probably due to low self-esteem or shyness. However, later on, I gradually became willing to let others see what I was doing. On one hand, it was because I became more confident, and on the other hand, I realized that everyone does similar things and what you do is something others have also done. So, they won't make fun of you or be surprised. And even if it's something different, everyone has different preferences, and it can still be accepted by others because they are very accepting. When interacting with others, we should have the courage to show our true selves. The next time someone looks at you, you can try to confidently and openly show what you're doing. You will find that there's nothing significant about showing the real you. Best wishes~.

Hello, OP: Actually, your thoughts are normal. You are afraid that the things you like are different from others. You worry that in the eyes of others, you are an outcast. You are worried that your lifestyle may make you unable to fit in and be accepted by others. You are not like others who are outgoing and prefer to be quiet and read a book by yourself. You belong to the introverted and artistic type. But in fact, everyone's personality is different, and being introverted also has its advantages. You can join a book club and share the books you like. Every book has its specific readership, and even niche songs have their own uniqueness. Pursue the life you want in a way you like. Be brave. Those friends who share the same aspirations with you will not dislike you because of your differences. On the contrary, they will see it as your characteristic, your most adorable trait. Don't shut yourself inside an ivory tower. Open a window, leave a door. Take the initiative to participate in various activities. You are not an isolated island. You have a special connection with the friends around you. It just requires you to be more proactive and enthusiastic, and have a defensive mentality towards the things around you. It is not wrong. The key is how to control it to the extent that others will not see you as a cold-hearted person.

question: I know that studying is important, but I can't concentrate on it. Life feels exhausting, and I feel desperate and want to die.
description: I know that studying is important, but I just can't absorb the material. I feel a lot of pressure, and my family members are ill. I'm not mentally well every day. I really don't want to live anymore.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear. I understand that you know how important studying is but sometimes it's hard to concentrate. Don't blame yourself for it. We all have moments when we know what we should do but can't seem to do it. It's okay. We all have a rational side and an emotional side. The rational side is often easier because we know many things and understand what we should and shouldn't do. However, the emotional side can be influenced by our moods and feelings, and we can't always stay rational and do what we should do. Right now, you know on a rational level that studying is important and you want to do well, but you feel overwhelmed and just want to escape. I think what you need to do right now is not constantly remind yourself how important studying is, but find ways to relieve your stress. It's important to work hard, but when you feel tired, it's also important to allow yourself to take a break. It's okay; life is not a race, and you don't need to constantly push forward without stopping. So, when you feel tired, adjust your mood, give yourself some time, and relax. In this period of time, you can allow yourself to not think about anything, not even studying or your sick family member, just completely relax. There are some relaxing meditation exercises you can follow with guided instructions. Give yourself a little time every day, even if it's short, to relax, and it can effectively relieve your stress. It's understandable that you feel stressed and tired because your family member is sick, but remember that there are three things in the world: God's will, other people's matters, and your own matters. Your family member's illness is God's will. Do your best, follow the circumstances, and take care of them as much as possible. Don't worry too much, and no matter what the ultimate result is, don't blame yourself. Sending you a hug. The world and I love you! (^_-).

Hello classmate, reading your words, I feel sorry and think you're still too young. If you think you study hard but your grades are not ideal, at least you are responsible for yourself. In the future, you will feel that you have tried your best: others may not understand you, but you understand yourself. You don't need to live according to others' expectations, but instead choose to live the way you want to be. Also, if you feel that you don't want to live anymore, I feel that you still have hope for life. Otherwise, you wouldn't express your inner thoughts. I can't feel exactly what you're going through, but I sincerely hope that you can embrace this world again. When you feel tired, just get a good sleep and don't think about anything. When you wake up, everything can be solved. Treat yourself to the things you like to eat. You will feel that there are beautiful things in this world that make you want to strive for them. When you feel that you can't stay in your current environment anymore, take a two-dollar bus ride and empty your mind. Through the window, you will find yourself on the road. The feeling of drifting will make you feel that there is still a place called home. Actually, all the difficulties you are facing right now are only temporary. They are not your future.

question: I am already forty and I still have three questions in doubt.
description: I'm already forty and still confused about three questions that have been bothering me: Who am I exactly? Where do I come from? What am I here for in this world? Haha, maybe it sounds like a joke, but that's just how I am. Can anyone help me solve this world puzzle?
keywords: Growth, development patterns, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I sense your confusion about yourself, where do I come from? Where am I going? These are the three most basic philosophical questions. These three philosophical questions are mainly for us to explore ourselves and to understand ourselves. Exploring and understanding ourselves is a sign of growth for each of us. Adolescents, for example, go through rebellion and various experiments to explore and understand themselves and to grow. This is an important stage of growth. After going through adolescence, a child's personality tends to become more perfect. So, the questions you have now are actually about exploring yourself and wanting to grow. This growth is an inner growth. It is never too late to grow at any time, so it is normal for you to have these doubts at the age of 40. It is commendable that you want to grow. In my opinion, you are not getting more confused as you live on, but rather becoming clearer. Actually, these three questions are about understanding our past, knowing our future, and finding our value and meaning in society. Maybe after you answer these three questions, your life will open up a new chapter. To answer these three questions, you need to first understand your past and your roots. The past is easy, you can recall your past experiences. Understanding your roots may require you to ask your parents or elders. To find your future and value, you may need to try more and read more books. Perhaps you can find the answers from books. Well, that's all for my answer. I hope you can find yourself, find your value and meaning, and find happiness and joy. Best wishes to you.

Confucius said, "At fifteen, I set my mind on learning. At thirty, I was established. At forty, I had no more doubts. At fifty, I understood the will of heaven. At sixty, my ear was obedient. At seventy, I followed my heart's desires without overstepping the boundaries." This is Confucius' progression, which ordinary people cannot achieve, so it is normal to still have doubts at forty. Regarding the question, "Who am I? Where do I come from? What am I here for in this world?" You can imagine yourself as a student who took a math test and only scored 58 points yesterday. You reflected on the reasons for getting this score and identified areas where you were lacking. You plan to do five targeted exercises tomorrow to make up for those deficiencies. As the night fell yesterday, you went to sleep, and this morning, you woke up. Who woke up? It's a person defined by all the past moments before awakening. Where did you come from? From the past. What are you going to do today? Accomplish the plan and fill in the gaps. The intention of why you came into this world is similar, aiming for evolution/improvement, both for individuals, the Earth, and the universe.

question: The child graduated and joined a company, wanting to work and do things, but colleagues everywhere are making things difficult and bullying.
description: After graduating and entering the workplace, my child wants to work and do things, but colleagues constantly give them a hard time. They don't assign any tasks, refuse to teach, and they can't learn from reading books. Every time, they are belittled and their speech is suppressed. They feel anxious and depressed, as if they are being stepped on. They just want to work properly. They reported the situation to the leader, but got ostracized. As a parent, I'm very anxious. I initially thought that as an adult, my child shouldn't get involved in this, but in this kind of environment, my child cries every day. Should I communicate with the leader as a parent, or will it be detrimental to my child? This situation is unbearable for everyone involved.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I hope my humble efforts can help you. Question: Your child is being excluded at work, without anyone teaching them, and being belittled, leading to anxiety and depression. Analysis: Based on your question, it seems that your child is currently living at home and just started working, and probably hasn't made many new friends due to the pressure. As parents, if you know about your child's troubles, you can guide them in communication and encourage them to speak more while you listen. Let them vent their negative emotions. However, you should not take too much control and dominate the situation, as it is not conducive to their growth. Actually, this is a common problem for newcomers in the workplace. If they haven't encountered a good leader and a harmonious working environment, they are often disliked and looked down upon. Newcomers have areas where they fall short, and some people intentionally make things difficult. If they really don't have tasks to do, they can find things to occupy themselves, such as reading and learning. Developing a growth mindset is essential for entering the workforce, and reading is an important stage for cultivating this mindset. Nowadays, besides reading, there are also many free or paid online courses available, where one can pay to learn from relevant teachers. Learning both workplace skills and mindset should never stop. As parents, other than listening, you can accompany your child and relax with them during leisure time, have a chat, and guide them to make more friends outside. It is not good to suppress all emotions and let the frustrations accumulated in the workplace stay inside, as it will pose significant harm to their physical and mental health in the long run. Personal growth in the workplace is similar to the iceberg theory, and we often overlook what is beneath the surface of the iceberg. The surface represents the skills relevant to the position, while what lies beneath represents character, ability, and mindset. Hard skills can be learned by anyone who is willing, but what truly determines a person's work capability are the elements beneath the surface. If your child has been in this environment for a long time without any changes, and if their efforts cannot change others, they can exercise their own abilities and be ready to leave at any time. As someone who has been in the workplace for a few years, I can say that the environment and leadership are indeed important. If you can't fit in here, then find another environment. As long as you have the necessary skills, you will be needed anywhere. I recommend your child to watch the Korean drama "Misaeng," as it may provide some answers.

Hello, the situation can be seen from both sides. From an individual perspective, the essence of entering society is to integrate into a group and adapt to the environment. Regardless of whether the leadership values you or if you face difficulties, it is important to start with self-improvement. Since you have just entered the workplace, many rules are still being established, and you need to change yourself for the objective environment. This includes your mindset, emotions, and interpersonal skills. It is not important if others look down on you, what matters is that you have self-respect. Being too concerned about others' opinions will only confuse yourself. It is necessary to evaluate yourself objectively, learn from experienced colleagues, and gain recognition from your leaders through continuous efforts. This is the issue we need to pay attention to in the company. From an organizational perspective, every individual who enters the company is working together to achieve the organization's goals. In reality, rules are not changed because of certain individuals. Only by adapting can one become familiar with the rules of the "jungle". Both leaders and the company hope that individuals can become valuable contributors in the organization. Here are some suggestions: 1. To gain recognition from the company and leadership, the best way is to learn and practice. Not all colleagues will become your friends. Remember that you are here to work, not make friends. Strive for a balance between input and output. 2. Being able to talk does not mean being able to communicate effectively. Check if there are any problems with communication and focus on learning how to build relationships, especially in a professional and social setting. 3. Build confidence by achieving small goals. It is important to plan, supervise, and control tasks, and to reflect on them afterwards. This will lead to unexpected results. 4. Understand the importance of time management and learn to complete designated tasks and goals within a specific timeframe, and persevere. 5. Intelligence is a minimum requirement, emotional intelligence is the upper limit. Treat everyone sincerely and become a person of value to others. Surround yourself with positive energy and negative people and things will stay away from you. 6. The world is vast, and there are all kinds of people. If you become a confident person, you won't be afraid in any situation. Focus on your current strengths and improve them, such as learning professional skills and communication techniques, and find like-minded friends to exchange ideas with. Ultimately, the only one who can help you is yourself, not your family. It's like when two kids fight and it turns into a conflict between their parents, it becomes a lose-lose situation. Similarly, if you rely on family to handle your work problems, in the future, when it comes to relationships, which are even more complex, can your family handle everything? Obviously, it's not realistic. Providing guidance is not as effective as teaching someone to fish. Children need to face and handle things on their own, as it is the foundation for their growth, maturity, and improvement. This is only for reference. I wish you all the best.

Seeing children enter the workplace and facing various realistic problems, it is understandable for parents to feel anxious. But if we talk about how to solve this situation, in my personal opinion, it is best to let them integrate into the workplace and gradually adapt on their own, because there is no quick and effective method that can surpass practical workplace experience. If you feel sorry for your child and provide them with help through your connections, it will weaken their real experience in the workplace. The workplace itself is brutal, just like the law of the jungle in nature. To survive in the natural world, one should learn to run, learn hunting skills, and instinctively avoid danger. All of this cannot be given by others, because they need you to truly experience it before they will gradually understand the essence of the workplace. What you give them may be better than their current situation, but at the same time, you cruelly stifle their ability to survive independently in the future. It is better for your child to shed tears now than to have difficulties adapting to the workplace and being ruthlessly eliminated in the future. When children first enter the workplace, they may experience something different from what they imagined, and when they encounter difficulties and setbacks, they may feel helpless. As parents, what we should provide them with is more encouragement and guidance, rather than indirect shortcuts. Remember to talk to them every day, share your own work experiences, and help them gain a clearer understanding of the workplace. When children grow up, just like little birds leaving the nest, it is inevitable that they have to return to nature. In the process of returning to nature, they will encounter storms, thunder and other harsh weather conditions. But you have to tell them that the birds flying in the sky are just like them, learning to spread their wings and fly to the blue sky. Whether they fly high or low, Mom and Dad are always watching and cheering for them. We can no longer help them fly just because they have suffered a little injury, because then they may never be able to fly to the blue sky on their own again!

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. Your child just graduated and entered the workplace, but they are being marginalized and suppressed at work, which is affecting their emotions and causing them to become anxious and cry every day. From your question, it can be seen that your child is probably more introverted in personality and has not experienced too much in life. They may also be having some difficulties adjusting to the workplace. Parents should not interfere too much in their child's work life. I personally believe that it is absolutely not acceptable for parents to communicate this issue with the leaders. Although in the eyes of parents, their child is still just a child, but they are already an adult, they have already passed the age of reporting to the teacher when being bullied. If parents communicate with the leaders, it will not be good for the child, and the leader may think that they are already an adult and don't need their parents to communicate for them. So parents should not interfere too much in their child's work, even if they are being treated unfairly. When children enter society, they also need to grow, and this is a part of their growth experience. Can you help them once, and then help them communicate with the leaders a second time? Moreover, if it spreads to colleagues, your child may still be talked about by colleagues. It is common for newbies in the workplace to be suppressed when they start their internships. Because everyone is usually busy and there is no time to teach a new person, it is important to explore on one's own. In the work, it is rare to encounter a good boss and company, most of the time, you have to rely on yourself. In the work, no one assigns work to them, and no one teaches them how to work. It is advised that they can observe how their colleagues work in their usual time and learn from them. For more professional knowledge, they still need to study and understand it themselves. If they can't understand it through reading, they can search for explanatory videos to help them understand. In their free time, they can find things to do themselves, such as helping colleagues make copies of documents or assisting with other tasks to promote good relationships with colleagues. They can also use this time to learn about things related to work. By learning, even if they are assigned tasks later on, they can accept them well. Parents should provide more emotional support to their child. It is good that your child will share the grievances they have experienced with you, instead of keeping it all inside and consuming themselves. You can offer guidance and comparison from your own experiences and provide comfort to their inner world. If possible, let them take a break, go out for a breath of fresh air, and have some fun to relieve their mood. You can also teach them some interpersonal skills to get along with colleagues and facilitate future work. As you mentioned, your family will always be their backing. If they are truly unhappy, then they can consider resigning and finding a better job. While they are young, they should try and experience more. These are my suggestions, I hope they can help you. Wish you all the best!

question: Should you tell both sets of parents that your husband spends a lot of money buying gifts for female live streamers on Douyin?
description: My husband has been playing Douyin and sending gifts to female live streamers for the past two months, totaling over a hundred thousand yuan. He even added them as friends on WeChat. At first, I didn't say anything when I noticed he was chatting with people, as there was nothing inappropriate. But then I checked Alipay and couldn't believe he spent over a hundred thousand yuan. This money was hard-earned, and he also has several tens of thousands of yuan in debt, which I discovered. Otherwise, he wouldn't have told me. He regrets it now and says he couldn't control himself. I don't know if I should tell both sets of parents. They are all frugal and would go insane hearing this. I don't know if I should forgive him either, but I don't want to get a divorce because we have children.
keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, and management of marriage.

answers.answer_text: Hello! You discovered that your husband is giving money to other women on TikTok, and the amount is not small. As a woman, seeing such behavior really makes you angry and frustrated, hating that he's not being responsible. But at the same time, you feel powerless. The teacher understands your feelings. You don't know whether you should tell his parents about this issue, especially since you know they are frugal and may not be able to handle the financial burden. It's clear that you are a kind person who knows how to take care of others and consider their feelings. Your husband is already an adult, an independent individual who is responsible for his own actions, and this is a matter that both of you as a couple need to deal with. Telling his parents will only make things more chaotic, and if something unexpected happens to his parents, it will bring you even more pressure and pain. The teacher suggests that you handle this yourselves, carefully help your husband understand the reasons behind his obsession with TikTok, and negotiate a solution together. To a large extent, problems like this arise when one lacks ambition, goals, and ideals in life, feeling bored and seeking happiness through TikTok, seeking validation through likes and rewards. Help your husband plan his career, keep him busy, so that he can find a sense of presence through his busyness, experience the joy of accomplishing results, and make his life goals clear and direction clear, so that naturally, his attention and energy will be focused on his career and maintaining your marriage.

question: What is the experience of staying up late at night and studying?
description: What experience is it to stay up all night and study instead of sleeping?

answers.answer_text: It's something that happens frequently. I almost study psychology, answer questions, and write stories every night. I do this continuously every day, except when I'm sick and need to sleep early. Usually, I study until I'm really tired and fall asleep. Sometimes, while answering questions, my brain stops working and I fall asleep. I'm not sure if I completed the answers or not. Sometimes I miss the deadline. Actually, my daily life is very busy. Besides working during the day, I sometimes have to work overtime and do various things at work. When I get home at night, there are many things to do, and I usually finish around eleven or twelve o'clock. So I can only study and check in at this time. Like this September, I just joined a mental health activity, and there are still many things I don't know how to use. This month, because of being sick, I took several days off and had some free time, so that's why I learned more than usual in a few months. During this period, I have been troubled by many things in life, and my mood is bad. I can't sleep alone in the long nights, and it's very painful, extremely painful. Sometimes, when I'm in a bad mood, I come here to read articles, listen to mental health FM, and answer questions, hoping to get some guidance from here. At the same time, I also try to guide others. I think this may make my mental state a little better, or in other words, coming here is a method I hope can help with my insomnia problem and hope it can be beneficial to myself. At the beginning, I don't know how effective it is. If possible, I would still choose to do these things earlier, if conditions allow, so that I won't be bothered by insomnia. Generally, if you have the habit of going to bed and getting up early and have a fast-paced lifestyle, I think it is advisable to study earlier and not stay up too late. This may be relatively better for the body. After all, staying up late at night can harm the liver and spleen, as well as other parts of the body. It's not good for the future and can easily harm the cardiovascular system.

Hello, giving you a warm hug. (･ω･)ﾉ Although psychology is interesting to learn, don't overdo it~ I hope you can spend your time during the day instead of staying up late at night and exhausting your brain. It will only make you more exhausted the next day. Additionally, I recommend putting this kind of question in the category of story collections, creating a story collection to facilitate better communication among everyone. I hope my answer can help you. (･ω･)ﾉ.

question: Want to retaliate against the bourgeoisie? Because it feels so pleasurable.
description: I want to retaliate against the bourgeoisie, I want to kill all the monopolistic bourgeoisie and monopoly capitalists.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand that you want to retaliate against the bourgeoisie because you feel the unfairness of wealth distribution in society, right? However, the current economic situation is not caused by certain individuals, but rather a result of various factors such as social, historical, and policy-related influences. Some people just seize opportunities and temporarily gain more wealth. This lack of fairness has not only been present in modern society, but throughout human development, in slave societies, feudal societies, and more. Those who are at the bottom may never escape the constraints of their social class, no matter how hard they strive. Modern society still has many inequalities, but it is getting better. At least now, as long as we are not lazy, we can support ourselves; as long as we are willing to work hard, there is hope for upward mobility; and as long as we are creative and innovative, we have the potential to accumulate wealth. The monopolies you mentioned are not solely due to personal factors, but also due to policies and individual abilities. It is through grasping difficult-to-obtain technologies and resources that monopolies can be achieved. Therefore, instead of seeking revenge against the bourgeoisie, it's better to strive and work hard, accumulate personal assets, and create value for society. Hugs to you, the world loves you! (^_-).

question: Parents urgently need money, but I can't come up with any, and I feel so helpless...
description: My parents urgently need money, but I am helpless and cannot provide the money needed. I feel so incapable and my job is also not secure. Sigh...
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Your parents are continuing to support you financially, but you feel incapable of contributing. This makes you feel inadequate and judgmental towards yourself, as well as guilty towards your parents. However, your current situation is not very optimistic, as you are still struggling to secure a job. This outcome may not be what you desire, but you currently cannot think of better alternatives. Your parents will understand you. Blaming and feeling guilty will not solve any problems. What you need now is to focus on yourself and work towards resolving your employment issues as soon as possible. Go out and look for jobs, try to find a suitable one. If you haven't found a job that meets all your expectations yet, you can temporarily settle for something similar as a transitional period. Regardless, as long as you have something to do, you will not feel like you are wasting your time. Best wishes!

question: My girlfriend has some things she only wants to tell the therapist and can't say to me. What should I do?
description: My girlfriend is feeling anxious and is receiving psychological counseling. There are some things that she only feels comfortable discussing with the counselor in the therapy room and doesn't tell me. However, it's inevitable that everyday conversations may touch on topics that make her anxious. Without proper communication, I can't help her, and both she and I feel distressed. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, my dear questioner. After reading your description, it's really hard to understand your thoughts. You are very concerned about your girlfriend's mental state and want to help her through your own efforts. According to your description, your girlfriend wants to only share certain things with a therapist and not with you. I can understand your desire to help your girlfriend, but she may feel that it's best to leave it to the professionals, as therapists are recognized by society and perhaps she has had positive experiences with them in the past, which makes her trust their expertise. It may also be that she doesn't want to burden you with her negative emotions. If you don't mind her bad mood, perhaps you can discuss this issue with her and address her concerns. It's also possible that there have been unpleasant discussions when you tried to talk about this topic before, and she wants to avoid arguments and not jeopardize your relationship. However, these are just speculations. I don't know the specific situation, so it's important for you to communicate with her.

question: Those six years of nightmare, I felt like I had tainted the world...
description: Six years ago, when I was eleven years old, I was deceived by a kind boy I met online. My parents and teachers never taught me about sex education, so I didn't understand or know how to protect myself. I met up with him and many things happened, including forced sexual acts, being coerced into prostitution, self-harm, and suicide attempts. I eventually lost hope in myself and felt dirty, thinking I couldn't be with anyone else and could only be with him. After six years, he no longer wanted me and his mother told me to die. I attempted suicide by drinking poison and was hospitalized. It has been several years now, but I am still afraid and can't forget. I feel so much hatred. I haven't had a good night's sleep in years, especially recently when I've been feeling even more reluctant to sleep. I constantly think about suicide and go to the rooftop. I feel like I have stained the world.
keywords: Treatment, psychological counseling, trauma therapy, behavioral abnormalities.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I feel very sorry for what you have been through. Hugs to you. 1. You are a pure and kind-hearted person. Even though you have been hurt a lot, you would never choose to retaliate or harm others. You feel like you have lost your "innocence," so you have been following him. But, dear girl, by staying with him, you will actually suffer even greater harm. He doesn't want to be with you, and that is actually your liberation, a new beginning in your life. Do you think so? 2. The unfortunate experiences in your childhood were not entirely your fault. Firstly, it was the fault of bad people who hurt you deeply. Secondly, it was also due to the negligence of your parents and teachers. But ultimately, you bore the brunt of the damage. Don't be afraid. No matter what kind of harm you have experienced before, you can still piece together the broken fragments of your heart. In fact, many people's childhoods are not perfect. It is precisely because of these small cracks that we can let the outside world seep in. 3. What you may be afraid of now is that no one will accept you in the future, and you may also feel pain when you think of past hurts... In situations where emotions are extremely difficult to regulate, I suggest that you not only confide in your family but also seek help from a professional psychologist or counselor. I believe you will get better. Wishing you all the best! The world and I love you.

It's not that you have dirtied the world. It's that the world has dirtied you. Ask yourself, do you really feel dirty because of those who have dirtied you? Your past experiences cannot be changed, no matter what you do or who you become. So what? Does that mean you're stuck like this, unable to change? Why? Why should you give up on yourself for those people? If there is even a slight desire to not give up, we can find ways to persevere. If you can't love someone, that's okay because life is not meant to be lived for love. There are many happy single people out there, and it's often those who suffer in love. If you don't have any skills, go learn, go search. Don't be picky or afraid. You can choose a safe job and work hard at it. You can avoid dealing with others. If you're not good at one job, then try another that you can excel at. If you want to study, be brave and face it. Study well because school is safer than society. Then try to change your future. You can also learn a trade. There are many industries. Go out on the streets, observe, and start as an apprentice. Learn well, and you can support yourself. - These are my opinions - Now, let me express my concerns. 1. Regularly go for gynecological checkups. Don't be scared or shy. It's a natural matter. Whether you're a minor or an adult woman, you should go for regular checkups. Besides sexual activities, staying up late, getting inflamed, diet, drinking, and smoking can all lead to various degrees of inflammation and symptoms. Regular checkups and proper treatment are the best protection for yourself. 2. When you can't sleep, try not to engage in behaviors that are harmful to your body, such as smoking, drinking, or taking medication. You can continuously read books, watch shows, listen to music, dance, practice calligraphy, draw, or exercise. Choose one activity that tires you out, and then you will fall asleep. 3. You can hate anyone, but don't hate the version of yourself that stepped into darkness. She is innocent, and you can still lead her out. Really. 4. Don't give up on yourself, okay? // You remind me of a plant - the lotus. I don't know if you have ever dug up lotus roots. They are usually grown in ponds filled with mud, which is smelly and slippery. But the lotus flowers that grow from it are clean and pure, and the lotus leaves are not even soaked by water. The lotus roots that grow in the mud are also clean and delicious. Patting your head, I blame God for forgetting to remind you to wear shoes when you came into this world. That's why you accidentally dirtied your feet.

I hope that if there are people who have experienced the same thing as me, they must speak out bravely, tell their parents, tell the people around them, and don't let these people take advantage of the situation. Some boys may manipulate you for their own romantic purposes. Parents say that these are bad people, and maybe some boys really are bad people. You should believe what your parents say!

question: Junior year, the relationships and interpersonal communication with friends are a mess. What should I do?
description: I am currently a junior. Since I was a child, I have always had good friends at every stage. During primary school, I had a friend whom I felt sincere towards, and they were also good to me. We went to school and played together, feeling like we could talk about anything. However, later on, this friend made new friends and treated them very well, while leaving me behind. This made me feel mentally upset, as if I had lost a friend. I felt that I regarded them as a good friend, but they treated others well while I felt lonely. Suddenly, I felt like my friend didn't see me as a close friend anymore, just a regular friend. This hurt me a lot, and as a result, I became indifferent towards my friends and gradually distanced myself from them. They didn't understand me, and I didn't speak up either. This situation continued through middle school and high school, and eventually, I started avoiding social interactions with friends more and more. It made me feel very upset, giving me headaches. In college, when I see others getting along so well, I always feel a sense of unease, but I still act cold and resistant towards people. It's very painful, and my social interactions are a mess. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I understand your concerns. During elementary school, you had a good friend and got along well. However, as your friend made new friends, you felt uncomfortable and grew apart. This situation continued in middle school and high school. Now, you have become resistant towards people. I want to share with you what I understand and hope it will inspire you. During childhood, friendships can indeed be exclusive. As we grow older, we realize that friendship is more about support and cooperation between friends. Exclusivity makes both us and our friends unhappy. Because of your past experiences, you feel hurt and may still not have recovered. However, now that we have grown up and recognized the problem, change is possible. I guess you understand that appreciating, understanding, accepting, and supporting each other without exclusivity, having a genuine and trusting friendship, is a lifelong treasure that is not easy to come by. I believe friendship can also be learned. Since you were able to make good friends in your childhood, even though there are some difficulties now, it does not prevent us from starting afresh and enjoying the happiness of being with friends. Making friends relies on building relationships. You need to spend time doing things together with friends and having shared experiences. If you find it difficult to make new friends, you can also try reconnecting with old friends who you haven't been in contact with for a long time. The changes in your friends through renewed contact and communication can give you a direct comparison and reference. This is also a rare experience. Friends also need to be more understanding. The past is over, so try to break free from the old patterns of making friends and approach interactions with others from a new perspective. For example, sincerely compliment others, not to please them or manipulate relationships, but to see compliments as an opportunity to bring joy to others. A simple compliment can make someone happy for a whole day. If you have the ability to make others happy because of you, it will be a very fulfilling thing. In interactions, communication difficulties are common. The usual approach is either blaming others for being unreasonable or learning how to communicate better. But what is the fundamental solution? It is actually understanding the other person's personality, compromising appropriately, and sticking to principles. This is the key to maintaining friendships. In the process of interaction between two people, at least one of them must be proactive. Friends are those who spend time with us, making us feel warm and willing to make efforts. We can also be that proactive person at the beginning. Start by trying, but also don't force yourself. Believe that your sincerity and kindness will bring you friends who will nurture and enrich your life. Action is important, take it slowly. As long as we open our hearts appropriately, friends may gradually come closer to us. Finally, I wish you all the best!

Junior year, relationships with friends and interpersonal communication are chaotic, what should I do? Hello, OP. First of all, I understand and sympathize with your situation, and I want to give you a big hug. Feeling the warmth of the world is not just you, many people are like this. In each stage of life, there are different good friends. Most of the time, we get along well with friends in that stage, cherishing the moments together. But when we enter a new stage, we make new friends, and everyone goes through cycles of changing friends. Even good friends have their own good friends, so often we need to think from their perspective instead of feeling lonely and uncomfortable when they have new friends. It's because we also have our own good friends. If we are truly good friends with someone, we should allow them to have their own good friends. Maybe the friend doesn't think of you as just an ordinary friend, but in the current stage, they may be closer to the new friends they just made. The stage you had together may have passed, but I believe your friend still cherishes your friendship. Just because your friend doesn't consider you as a close friend anymore, doesn't mean you need to be cold to them. If you still consider them as a memory of your youth, you might not be so distant to them either. They may not understand your feelings of jealousy when they make new friends, as this is often not easy to notice. So sometimes what you need to do is just communicate your discomfort to your friend. If you don't say anything and keep it to yourself, very few people will truly understand your thoughts, and they may think you're acting strange, asking why everything was fine before, but now you're acting cold. Actually, what you're feeling is very normal. You feel upset because you're not being valued as much when your good friend has new friends. But your pride doesn't allow you to reach out to them. So you become distant, trying to protect yourself from being hurt. But are you really not being hurt anymore? However, your friend may also not understand your behavior and find it strange. Why were you all so close before, but now you're acting cold? Often, as long as you open up and talk to your friend about how you feel, if your friend truly cares about you, they may reassess their previous lack of concern and value you more.
