Then your friendship will reconnect instead of creating a distance. So, OP, why not be brave and express your feelings to your friend? Good luck! (ง•̀_•́)ง

● A one-on-one relationship does not belong to the category of friendship, as it is only the modern institution of marriage that stipulates monogamy. ● Can you guarantee that you will only have one friend for your entire life? If you cannot, why would you demand that from others? ● If you want someone to view you as unique, then enter into a romantic relationship. Romantic relationships have legitimate reasons to reject third parties.

Hello OP, whether it's in dating or any other aspect of life, if you approach it with a mindset of fairness, it will require extra effort. It's all subjective and it's easy for situations to arise where you consider something as important while the other person may not. It's great if the other person pursues you instead, as you won't lose out either way. But if it's the other way around, it can feel like a deficit every month, and it's hard to maintain a positive mood in that situation. The key to a good relationship is whether you can do things together, eat together, have conversations, joke around, play games, etc. If you can do these things like normal friends, face challenges and difficulties together, then you're true friends. If you can learn together, support each other, share life experiences, and grow together, then you're best friends. As long as you can do things with others, you will always be able to find friends.

question: Why do I always envy other people's lives, even though I am young?
description: A 20-year-old boy feels like everyone has their own goals, knowing what they should do and which path to take, while he feels like a "blind person" who can't see anything clearly and doesn't know the direction. Is it normal to envy other people's lives?

answers.answer_text: Hello, at the age of 20, you have just entered a stage where you are growing up but still inexperienced. It can be considered officially adulthood. I would like to share my perspective. My sister's daughter loves to read picture books because she doesn't know how to read yet but enjoys watching animations, pictures, and picture books. She is curious and imaginative about the outside world. And why do we enjoy watching movies? It's because we can quickly see someone's whole life and set an example for ourselves to strive and work hard for. It's about wanting to have a beautiful life and become that kind of person.

question: 19-year-old male, from the end of the college entrance examination until now, what problems are there in the relationship between lovers?
description: I met her in the last semester of high school when we transferred classes. Our relationship has always been good. We used to eat together every day at school, but occasionally we would have some small conflicts. I am a sensitive person with a fragile personality. When we were together, she was very kind and considerate. After the college entrance examination, I went to her city to visit her. We held hands, ate and played together. We also took many precious photos together. However, sometimes when I wanted her to post some photos or group shots of us on social media, she always refused, saying she was shy. In fact, I'm used to seeing the sweetness between other couples, and I really want to show our relationship in front of friends and receive their blessings. So I have been encouraging her and even begged her for many days, but she always remained indifferent. Later, due to my disappointing college entrance exam results and some trivial family matters, we started arguing. It even escalated into intense fights, and I don't even know what I have become. It's like I can't untie this knot if I can't satisfy this vanity. Later, I became suspicious and thought she had someone else in her heart. I really want to go back to the way we were before, being that sweet couple again, but I just can't untie this knot...

answers.answer_text: Hello, ###, give each other more time and try to understand your girlfriend. You and your girlfriend met in the last semester of high school, so your time together isn't particularly long. I suggest being patient, caring, and providing a sense of security to your girlfriend. Her reluctance to post photos together may not just be due to being introverted or shy, but there may be various other reasons. ① She may not want to publicly announce your relationship, fearing pressure from parents, classmates, teachers, and others who know her. She just wants to have a good relationship and enjoy the sweetness it brings. ② If the issue of not posting photos escalates to intense arguments, as you mentioned, along with disappointing college admission results and other family issues, it's important to stabilize your emotions. Your sensitivity and the desire to prove your girlfriend's love for you through photos may make her feel pressured and uncomfortable, which is not conducive to the development of your relationship. ****** How can you resolve this? As you mentioned, you are sensitive and have a fragile heart. If you cannot satisfy this vanity, you will not be able to resolve this emotional conflict. You become suspicious, thinking that she hasn't fully committed to you. ① Respect your girlfriend's wishes. You lack a sense of security and like to affirm your girlfriend's love for you through official announcements and photos. It's important to carefully consider your wording and avoid being too forceful or intense when expressing your needs. When your expectations and needs are not met, your attitude should be balanced. Engaging in arguments or giving her the silent treatment will only make your girlfriend feel more insecure. ② Seek common ground while respecting differences. Understand and respect your girlfriend's reluctance to take photos. Sincerely express your own emotional state of sensitivity and insecurity. Can you find more indirect ways, such as using social media to express your love through a special nickname or sharing love letters, to communicate your affection for each other? ③ Adjust your internal state. You described yourself as sensitive, having a fragile heart, and seeking validation. Learn about emotional management through books, articles, and audio materials to stabilize your emotions and build self-confidence. Believe that you are worthy of love. Good luck, and the world loves you.

Hello, the topic you mentioned is both simple and complex. You actually have some self-awareness, such as being sensitive, having vanity, and having emotional issues. It seems like you understand that "Oh, this is my vanity at work, but I just want to take photos and show off my relationship in front of others." Your rationality tells you that this is not good, it is a manifestation of vanity, but your emotions tell you otherwise, saying "No, I used to envy others showing off their relationships, now I want to do the same." So your rationality and emotions are in conflict, neither can convince the other, and the result is that both you and your girlfriend are suffering. Don't try to change your girlfriend. From a rational perspective, changing a person is difficult, and from an emotional perspective, I believe you don't want to make your girlfriend go through pain and distress by forcing her to do something she doesn't want to do. What you need to do, in my opinion, is to deepen your self-awareness. Why is it so important for you to show off a photo? What is its deeper meaning to you? I believe it's not as simple as "seeing others doing it, so I want to do it too." If your girlfriend keeps refusing you, what is your innermost thinking, your concerns, your associations? When you view this matter from different perspectives, you will find the direction in your heart.

Hello~ It is normal for conflicts and arguments to occur in relationships, but quarreling does indeed affect the relationship between two people. You really hope that the other person can post your photos on social media, and you really want the relationship to be exposed. Maybe in your mind, doing these things is possessive. How does it make you feel when it is not exposed? Obviously, the other person is not planning to publicize it temporarily. I think it is necessary to respect the other person's wishes. Young relationships may have immaturity, but love is mutual, and respecting and understanding each other is important. And in relationships, it's not just about sweetness, but also friction and arguments. Try to communicate with the other person calmly. Your insecurity and sensitivity will make you value this relationship and hope to maintain its existence through external forces, such as exposure on social platforms or meeting friends. This is a bit of a confusion of priorities. Sustaining a relationship requires the effort of both people, and it is about respecting and understanding your partner. What you want to do is more to satisfy yourself, and it is easy to overlook the other person's feelings and hurt her. It is recommended that you communicate well. You can express your own needs, but whether the other person is willing is her right. Try to lower your expectations appropriately, while also affirming yourself. You are worthy of love. Since the second half of your senior year, your relationship is still not stable enough, and it needs more time and interaction. Young relationships are easy to hurt each other, like a hedgehog with thorns using its thorns to protect itself, but it didn't expect to be more hurt. Take it slow, communicate well, find the real cause of the argument, and find ways to face it.

question: Recent graduates, lately experiencing frequent breakdowns, often burst into tears, become enraged, and even resort to self-harm by hitting and pinching themselves.
description: I've been experiencing insomnia on and off for several years. Every year, there would be a period of time when I have trouble sleeping. I have tried going to the hospital for treatment and taking Chinese herbal medicine, but even when I manage to fall asleep, I would wake up multiple times during the night. Sometimes, I would suddenly sit up in bed while sleeping. This is my sleep problem. Since about two years ago, I have been easily overwhelmed and would burst into tears or have tantrums over trivial matters. I can only resort to pinching myself to calm down. I often feel anxious and worried about my relationship with my boyfriend... I always feel like I'm sick, and sometimes I would suddenly have an indescribable feeling in my heart, feeling suffocated and unable to breathe. I want to understand what is really going on with myself. I feel extremely suppressed and on the verge of collapse.
keywords: Emotions, depressed emotions, healing methods, anxious emotions

answers.answer_text: Hello, the possibility of your insomnia could be due to psychological factors or a physical problem. It is recommended that you continue to see a doctor as this symptom may have a complex cause and may not be resolved immediately by one hospital or doctor. If you feel that drinking Chinese medicine has some effect, you can continue with the treatment. If you feel it is ineffective, you can try another hospital. From your description, it seems that you are in a very suppressed and anxious state, possibly because some past emotions have not been dealt with in a timely manner and have been suppressed deep inside. However, they have not disappeared. To give an analogy, it's like a trash can that keeps filling up with garbage but never gets emptied. Over time, this garbage may ferment and become foul. Our emotions are similar. Emotions that have not been dealt with in the past, when suppressed, do not disappear, they just manifest in other forms such as anxiety, tension, or insomnia. These emotions can also be triggered by small things, leading to outbursts or breakdowns. Therefore, if possible, it is recommended to see a psychologist or counselor. With their support, you can explore your inner self, find the emotional garbage remaining in your heart, clear it out, and release it. You will feel much lighter. You can also try exploring your inner self and find out what things are affecting your mood. If it's something from the past, try to let it go. If it's something in the present, try to find ways to solve it. If it's something in the future, focus on the present. As a recent graduate, what are your plans? Are you planning to continue studying or start working? This year's situation is special, so don't rush. Take it slowly and try things out gradually. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Go seek professional psychological therapy. You haven't mentioned the reasons, but it's clear that you are feeling a lot of suppression. There is uncertainty and insecurity about the future, as well as anxiety about leaving campus. There may also be some lamentation about the past. Life is new every day, and the past is not as important as you imagine it to be. The future is not as terrifying as you fear. Most people live their lives with the fear that the sky might fall, leading ordinary and uneventful lives.

question: I can't control my fantasies and I have trouble concentrating. Do I have a mental illness?
description: I always have a lack of focus. I also have a tendency to daydream and fantasize. I feel particularly anxious. My mind is always filled with fantasies, such as fantasizing about how powerful and excellent I am, imagining that many people admire me. Or thinking about what to do tomorrow, what to do tonight, basically just constantly thinking about irrelevant things. I can't concentrate during class and I often drift off. This greatly reduces my productivity and I often feel headaches, which may be due to this reason. I constantly daydream and I don't know what's happening to me. I wasn't like this when I was younger. I'm also quite insecure.
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, anxiety, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Title owner, hello, sending you a warm hug~ After reading your description, it seems that you are prone to fantasizing, like daydreaming fantasies. I can tell that you have difficulty controlling these thoughts, and I truly sympathize with your situation. Based on your description, "I always have poor concentration. And I fantasize and imagine a lot. I also feel particularly anxious." You also fantasize about scenes of your own success. Perhaps deep inside, you yearn for success, but there are many factors in real life that hinder you and make you feel helpless. Maybe those factors are the reason why you can't step out of your comfort zone. Perhaps you should try to live in the present, because only by putting in the same amount of effort can you achieve the same level of reward. It's possible that self-discipline and learning activities may be difficult for us to stick to and even bring discomfort, but being obsessed with comfort will not make us grow.

question: The pressure on first-year students is a bit high, but I just don't put in effort.
description: I feel exhausted and have self-harmed before, and even thought about suicide. I feel extremely useless and want to put in effort, but I'm just lazy. I know all the right things to do, but I just don't do them. My English and math skills are especially bad, but I just don't want to learn. I feel like I won't understand anything in class and I feel embarrassed when the teacher asks me questions. I'm incredibly tired and don't know what to do, feeling a bit lost. I have a habit of staying up late until one or two in the morning, and then I struggle to stay awake during class, my mind wandering. I feel like I'm not as good as other people.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text: Young people who don't work hard will regret it when they grow old. It is important to work hard, but your efforts should come from the heart and follow the natural order. Don't force yourself, don't be mentally stressed, and don't ruin your health. Firstly, avoid staying up late and try to wake up early. That's how I studied. Later, I tried to be cunning, and as a result, my college entrance exam results were disastrous. Now, 30 years have passed, and it's only when my own child goes through the college entrance exam that my past wishes are finally fulfilled. It's a painful realization after 30 years. Effort can be done in a proper way. Best wishes to you.

question: Is constantly questioning the details after my wife cheated on me considered ineffective communication?
description: My wife had an affair, but there were instances of deception and threats. I have chosen to forgive her, but I can't help asking her detailed questions, such as what positions they used during sex, whether she found it more pleasurable than with me, or what her state of mind was at the time. I would like to know if this kind of communication is ineffective, or if there are more effective ways to communicate.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I can understand your current state and mood. In fact, anyone can cheat, regardless of gender. If your wife cheated but was deceived or threatened, some people may not have a clear understanding of others. Cheating entails certain consequences, whether it be financial, the loss of youth, or facing the dissolution of the family, etc. About forgiveness, the fact that you still can't help but ask her detailed questions, such as the positions they used during sex, whether she felt more comfortable than with me, or her state of mind at the time, actually shows that you still have such concerns deep inside and haven't completely forgiven. There are many examples that show many people who appear to forgive infidelity do so for the sake of the family, the remaining love in their hearts, and their responsibilities, etc. That's why you have such behavior of asking for details. This can be understood because nobody is perfect, and it's not possible to immediately do well and relax. Can you please tell me if this is ineffective communication or if there are other more effective ways of communication? In regards to communication, this behavior of asking for many details about infidelity is not communication. It might be to satisfy your curiosity and possessiveness. You are puzzled about certain things and wonder if you weren't good enough for her to cheat. You're just not brave enough to face it, but your questioning happens to imply these things. So, if you want to communicate, you should openly share your true thoughts deep inside with your wife, don't suppress them too much, otherwise, it may become a hidden danger in the future. Asking for details about infidelity is also not effective communication. Better suggestions are: 1. Arrange a meeting with your wife to recreate the feelings you had when you were in love to strengthen your relationship. 2. If you have children, especially young ones, go to an amusement park together as a family to experience a warm atmosphere. 3. Do nothing, just sit and have a good conversation with your wife, but be tactful. It's not an interrogation. You can recall the past together, look at old photos, and then raise the questions that you hesitate to ask in your heart to resolve them as soon as possible. I wish you happiness and joy!

Hello, thank you for inviting me to answer. Going through such a traumatic event, you must be under a lot of psychological stress. As a man, this is also a devastating blow to your self-confidence. It is clear that you care deeply about your wife. Although she was the one who had an affair, you still empathize with her, believing she was deceived or threatened. You have chosen to forgive her, but you can't help but ask for the details (a sign that you haven't completely forgiven her), all from her perspective: what positions "she" had sex in, whether "she" felt more satisfied than with you, or "her" emotions at that time... You care deeply about her. Your constant questioning about the details of the affair and her feelings at that time may be because you are always accustomed to neglecting your own feelings. You always need verbal affirmation from others to gain confidence in yourself. I would like you to redirect your attention and think about your own inner feelings: being deceived by the person sleeping next to you, what do you feel? Confusion, anger, sadness, and...? How do you convince yourself to vent or let go of these emotions? Or maybe you haven't let go of your emotions yet and are just habitually forcing yourself to ignore them? Or perhaps, through questioning and seeking details from her, you are repeatedly digesting your own inner pain and confusion? Are you asking yourself whether she still loves you, what she loves about you, and why she betrayed you? They say a knot can only be untied if it is untangled. Fear lies only in not trying to untangle it. Don't get entangled with her and the past events for now. Take some time for yourself, spend some time alone, understand the difficulties you are facing, and experience your inner feelings, then think about the problems that have existed during your years of being together, etc. Let your thoughts fly freely for a while. Straighten yourself out first, so that your choices don't seem so blurry.

Hello, a leaf brightens the mind, a word knows you. 1. If your partner has cheated, you choose to forgive but can't help asking for details, such as... you are currently in a state where you intellectually accept it but emotionally haven't fully accepted it. Your partner's infidelity makes you feel betrayed physically, something that was once "exclusive" to you (this description does not mean the possessions of a male or female, but rather a description of a psychological state) has been taken by someone else. Subconsciously, it triggers your biological instinct of competition. Therefore, you behave by constantly asking for details, whether it will make you feel more comfortable than your partner and focusing on her state of mind at that time is a "competitive" and "comparative" attitude. 2. I also noticed the situation of being deceived or threatened, but you did not elaborate. If that is the case, your partner is actually the victim in the "cheating" relationship. So, when you can't help but ask for details, will it remind your partner of the "past hurt" she does not want to recall from previous intimate experiences? Of course, you did not describe your partner's thoughts on this matter and other details, so I cannot further analyze it for you. But I need to remind you that this is a matter of family relationships, and it may not only be you who is troubled by it. 3. Your last question is whether this belongs to "ineffective communication" and you want more effective communication. The effectiveness or ineffectiveness of communication depends on whether the problem is resolved. Since you can't help but want to ask now, it shows that you still haven't fully digested this matter, you just don't know how to effectively resolve it. In the case of family relationships and involving a third party, I suggest that you and your partner seek psychological counseling together, which will be more beneficial in resolving your issues.

Hello, your wife has cheated on you, although you know that she was coerced, you have made the rational decision to forgive her, but you have been threatened. The part where you feel threatened is that you feel compared to someone else, you are no longer confident in your sexual abilities, and as a result, you lack confidence in your own abilities and your wife's attractiveness. You worry that the other person is better than you in terms of sexual performance, and you worry that your wife's heart leans towards that person. Your wife feels that you are inferior to the other person. When you ask for details from your wife, it is a way of comparing yourself, and you are looking to prove that you are not inferior to him. You wonder if asking for details from your wife has led to ineffective communication between you two, and you are potentially seeking an effective way to communicate. In reality, what you need is self-acceptance and confidence in yourself.

question: As someone with depression and anxiety, what reasons should I have to apply for overnight stays?
description: Three new roommates often stay up late, making me only able to sleep at 3:30 a.m. as someone with anxiety and depression, staying up late makes me feel uncomfortable in my heart, nauseous, with a sore neck, and as if my head is being crushed by bricks. I feel like I'm about to have a heart attack. I want to apply for off-campus accommodation, but the school closure means everyone is staying on campus. I also dare not let the school know about my anxiety and depression. I only have half a year left before I graduate and start my internship, and I don't want to be expelled for falling ill. What reason should I use to apply for off-campus accommodation? Thank you.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, communication, conflicts and resolutions, roommates and classmates.

answers.answer_text: Do you know if you have been officially diagnosed with anxiety and depression? Have you been taking medication or receiving psychological counseling? Staying away from home is one method of solving problems, but it's not the only one. I understand your concerns about applying to stay away from home. Perhaps you can consider how you can cope with each possible situation and decide if you can handle it after organizing your thoughts.

question: "Just turned 16, my boyfriend secretly took inappropriate photos of me while wearing a dress. Should we break up?"
description: In the summer, I went to the library with him wearing a long skirt. I fell asleep cross-legged on the floor, and my skirt may have slipped off. He took a secret photo of my private area on his phone. I suddenly woke up and saw a glimpse of it, but when I wanted to take a closer look, he took it back. At that moment, I didn't know how to respond and wasn't sure about anything. I was just a little angry, so I left by car. He kept apologizing throughout the journey and asking what was wrong. He even knelt down in the library. He said he would never do it again, but he didn't specify what he wouldn't do. Earlier, he also touched my chest, just a simple touch, but I really disliked it. Maybe he thought I was angry because of that. Later, when we got back home, he sent a message saying that the photo was accidentally taken when the screen was touched. Should I believe him? He's a good person, quite straightforward and has a good temper. He spoils me a lot, and I really like him. I don't know if I should break up with him.

answers.answer_text: During puberty, boys sometimes do inappropriate things, so we need to learn how to protect ourselves. 1. If the other person cannot control their behavior, it's best for girls to avoid giving them a chance to be alone. Whether it's their past actions or present voyeurism, it shows a lack of respect for the subject, and the other person's apology is a bit extreme, especially when they kneel down and say they won't do it again. From this incident, it can be inferred that the other person probably had strict upbringing, but they also have a rebellious side. They may apologize sincerely whenever they do something wrong, but they rarely realize their own issues. So, we need to learn how to protect ourselves. If one day the other person does something even more outrageous, but again apologizes by kneeling down, should we choose to forgive them? 2. Not refusing something doesn't mean we are consenting to it. Because teenagers nowadays mature early, they may have more knowledge about certain things, but they might also have some misconceptions, such as thinking that not saying no is the same as saying yes, or that if they apologize for their mistakes, everything is okay. If the girl hadn't discovered the other person's voyeuristic behavior, would they have continued to deny it? After all, some things involve personal privacy, and therefore require our consent. The other person failed to do that, so we really need to be cautious. Whether or not to break up is a decision the girl needs to make for herself, but we need to clearly communicate our boundaries to the other person. At the same time, we also need to protect ourselves. Someone who truly loves us will never force us to do things we don't like. The world loves you, and so do I.

Hello, OP! Sending warm hugs your way! After reading your description, I understand your dilemma and pain. On one hand, you really like this guy, but on the other hand, he does things that you cannot tolerate! You don't know how to make a decision! So, let's analyze it from these three points! Whether or not to be together ultimately requires your own consideration and decision, after all, you have to find your own path. Firstly, considering your age, you should be in high school, right? At your age, it's okay to have a crush, but for girls, once they become deeply involved, it can easily affect their studies. I recommend maintaining an appropriate distance from your boyfriend and prioritizing your studies. Secondly, judging from your boyfriend's actions, it's not worth getting too close to him at this stage. He doesn't seem to have good self-control around the opposite sex, and taking inappropriate photos in the library shows a lack of restraint and awareness of the setting. If you get too close without truly knowing what he wants, it might be risky! To protect yourself, it is advisable to maintain a healthy distance and not get too intimate. Lastly, based on your situation, since you like this guy, learn to set boundaries! Don't let yourself get too deeply involved and jeopardize your future. Once a girl has her first relationship in high school, she tends to place special importance on the first guy when it comes to future relationships. If this guy separates from you in terms of education or other aspects in the future, it can be emotionally distressing for you. Moreover, if you get too close and face an unexpected pregnancy or something similar, it would be irresponsible towards yourself, and the guy may not be able to handle it either! In conclusion, this boyfriend of yours has already shown various frivolous and inappropriate behaviors, so be mindful of maintaining distance! If he can control himself and learn to respect you, you can continue the relationship. But if he doesn't understand how to restrain himself, you should consider your own situation. Self-protection is key! Focus on your studies. I hope this advice is helpful to you.

I think the female protagonist still needs to pay attention to maintaining boundaries with the opposite sex. Girls should have their own principles and bottom line. During middle school, it is still promoted for male and female students to have normal interactions and be friends. Firstly, our main task is to study. Secondly, at this age, we are still relatively naive, and our understanding is limited. It is normal to have a liking for someone of the opposite sex. When we enter puberty and see male or female classmates that we admire, we may have many little thoughts. We need to have a correct understanding of this and accept it. Do not think of it as something shameful and avoid it, which would affect the normal interaction and communication among classmates. But we also cannot be completely ignorant and not consider anything, disregarding the consequences and losing ourselves. Girls need to protect themselves. It is recommended not to spend too much time alone with male classmates, and if possible, not to use the terms boyfriend or girlfriend too early. Learn to refuse and say no. For certain things, it is important to clearly express one's stance and attitude to avoid being passive and awkward, and even irreversible situations. When it comes to male classmates' requests, it is necessary to selectively agree and interact. Love is a wonderful emotion, so it is recommended to keep this liking in one's heart for now. You can learn from the good qualities of others.

Hello girl, please take care of yourself. Be pure and simple, be happy without being weighed down by materialism, and don't bear the burden of sexual pressure too early. It's great that you had the right reaction to your friend's inappropriate behavior. People with inappropriate behavior will always try to take advantage of you as a young girl. You want him, a young boy, to talk about responsibility and the future with you, but everything is still uncertain and impossible. As teenagers, you should maintain a certain distance in your interactions, at least show mutual respect and caution towards each other. When faced with inappropriate behavior, be brave enough to say "no" and then turn and escape danger. You did the right thing, but did you handle it well? What does it mean to handle it well? It means feeling satisfied with yourself, feeling that he received the punishment he deserved, and ensuring your own safety. His behavior, for a boy going through puberty, is a normal sexual impulse, but it is an immoral behavior. If it's not stopped soon, worse behaviors may occur, possibly even breaking the law. I think you should understand the seriousness of the situation and maintain a certain distance from him. For a 16-year-old student, although dating is not legally prohibited, it mostly brings more harm than good to both parties' physical and mental development and future prospects. I won't make any judgments here. It is best to maintain a pure and friendly relationship, without getting caught up in sexual desires or indulging in the "forbidden fruit" too early. If early pregnancy, repeating a grade, dropping out of school, impacting further education, or causing harm to oneself occurs, it would be a big "regret" for both the boy and girl involved. Hearing your attitude towards "just touching" really worries people. If you don't strongly reprimand and leave immediately, that would be indulging. There will be a second line, a third line, and even more than just touching the chest or private parts. This is already a serious offense. Girl, it's better not to be friends with someone like this, be cautious! Your parents probably know about this and are likely to educate him or even have thoughts of wanting to harm him. As for your lack of caution, your parents may even have thoughts of strangling you (the response of real parents). If it were me, I would end the friendship! Be cautious, very cautious!

Child, good afternoon! I feel the sadness deep inside you. I give you a hug and let's sit down and talk, hoping to inspire and help you. 16 years old is the high school stage, where physical and mental changes happen rapidly. Since you and your partner have confirmed your romantic relationship, even if it may not be seen as serious in the eyes of parents or teachers, it is still very important to you. Trust and respect are essential elements in a romantic relationship. It is beneficial for long-term development. You can communicate your anger and sadness directly with your boyfriend, but his explanation is obviously unclear. In this incident, instinct overcame reason and emotion. Whether or not to break up is something only you can decide. Set your own boundaries, fight for your legitimate rights, protect your physical and mental well-being, and then focus on romantic relationships. Having said that, I wish you the best! The world and I love you!

Hello, OP~ Objectively speaking, boys around the age of 16 or 17 are experiencing rapid development in both their sexual physiology and psychology. At this age, they start to develop an interest in the opposite sex and may have thoughts about engaging in sexual activities. There could be two reasons why your boyfriend took your private photos: first, out of curiosity about the female body, and second, driven by sexual desire. These thoughts are common for most boys in this age group, but some boys have better self-control and can regulate themselves appropriately. Others may engage in some inappropriate behaviors initially or seek relief by watching explicit videos. Such thoughts are a normal phenomenon, but engaging in such behaviors would be inappropriate. Because you are both underage, exploring sexuality should be about understanding it but not attempting it. Taking someone's private photos without their knowledge is considered an invasion of personal privacy and even sexual harassment from a legal perspective. If he is interested in sexuality, he should seek knowledge in a reasonable manner and not engage in such inappropriate behavior. You need to make it clear to him that this behavior is wrong and not allowed emotionally or legally. As for whether to break up or not, that depends on your inner feelings. It is understandable that there can be some intimate actions between boyfriends and girlfriends. However, the level of intimacy should be limited due to your age. For minors, it is best to avoid overly intimate actions. You can talk to him and let him know your boundaries. If he is willing to respect your feelings, then the relationship can continue. If he disregards your feelings and crosses your boundaries, then you need to make a clear decision. Best wishes!

question: Can I trust my boyfriend if he has hired prostitutes before?
description: I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year. He is eight years older than me, treats me well, and is very filial to his parents. He has set up the fingerprint recognition on his phone for me, so I can access it anytime. Usually, I don't go through his phone because I trust him. But last month, I accidentally stumbled upon some pornographic groups he had joined on his phone. Upon further investigation, I also found messages from prostitutes contacting him. Although he didn't reply to those messages, he didn't delete them either; he just let them stay on his phone. He admitted that he had visited prostitutes before we started dating, but that was years ago, and he promised that he hasn't done so again since being with me and won't in the future. As for why he didn't delete the messages immediately, he said it was because he was too busy with work and didn't have time to organize them. I don't know if I should believe him because if he truly values our relationship, why wouldn't he delete those inappropriate things and continue to keep them? Is he keeping them for future use? He said it was from many years ago, but I saw the time when those messages were sent, and it was in the first few months of our relationship. Although only the messages from the prostitutes were there, why would he keep them? I don't know if I should believe him or if I can still accept him.
keywords: Emotions, depressed feelings, anxious feelings, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hugs~ Although my experience in love is not very extensive, only once, I have always believed that there is no deceit in love. No matter what the reason, it should not let me live in lies. Women in love should be grateful for the honesty of men. Willingness to show their vulnerable side is also a trust in women. Women need to grow in love, learn from their mistakes. Getting lost in the fog is not a woman's fault, but getting lost in lies is a woman's sorrow. Women should believe in their own instincts, believe in their inner voice. If there are concerns, dismiss them, if they cannot be resolved, then part ways. Women need to protect themselves first in order to demand protection from others when necessary. Men can leave at any time, with any excuse. Are we women just supposed to stay in the background of men? If we don't want to be bothered, to become obsessively worried due to our lack of trust, then we should take the initiative to make decisions. Women can also hold the power of initiative. If your bottom line is being a prostitute, regardless of whether there is any deception, the answer is no. Don't give in easily.

question: I am always worried about my loved ones having an accident, and I feel restless every day.
description: Since I started working and earning money, I have returned to my hometown and have been in close proximity to my family. My mother is overly protective of me and constantly worries about my safety. After going through my mother's surgery and my grandmother's hospitalization, I have become as cautious as my mother, always worrying about my family's accidents or illnesses. When I am alone, I easily have random thoughts and constantly remind them to be careful, feeling restless every day.
keywords: Treatment, psychological counseling, sharing and listening.

answers.answer_text:
- Always worried about family members having accidents or getting sick, and having random thoughts when alone.
- Constantly reminding them to be safe, feeling restless every day. Hello, asker. Worries are everywhere in life. People who have been hit by a car may have lingering fear of vehicles on the road. People who have been bitten by dogs may panic when they see a dog. When you personally experience your mother's surgery and your grandmother's hospitalization, this experience deepens your emotions of worry. Assuming that your mother and grandmother have not experienced the troubles of illness, you would not see them in pain, and you would not have so much anxiety. Because illness means a threat to life and health, according to Maslow's theory, safety is a basic instinct for humans. When we feel that our life (health) is being threatened, our focus will be entirely on safety, and other things that revolve around the well-being of body and mind will become insignificant. You are always in a state of worry and anxiety, constantly reminding them to be safe. You are using past experiences to judge your current life, worrying about things that are beyond your control. But we know that no matter what worries us, nothing will change because of it. Similarly, not worrying does not mean that they will not happen. Faced with a complex and ever-changing reality, trying to predict what may happen and wanting them to happen as we wish is unrealistic. Otherwise, we will fall into a vicious cycle of more anxiety the more we think about it. And you can actually see that your mother and grandmother can be treated through medical interventions. Although it is currently impossible to avoid any pain, it is at least controllable. People can rely on money and measures to successfully achieve health and safety in life. In that case, besides worry, we can also purchase insurance for our family and ourselves, undergo regular check-ups, and engage in activities that we enjoy to feel fulfilled and reduce worries. In addition, compared to those who are unaware of certain misfortunes in life due to their carefree nature, a person who maintains a certain level of worry can be more vigilant, responsible, and also experience a sense of value from this responsible attitude. It's just a matter of adjusting the degree of worry so as not to let this anxious emotion interfere with your life. Best wishes.

question: How to practice accepting the fact that you are an ordinary person?
description: Sometimes it feels very difficult to accept that I am not as good as others in certain aspects. When I try to accept it, there is a deep sense of fear that arises from within, which makes me very scared. I don't know what this is about. But in some areas where I want to be better than others, but my actual abilities are not enough and cannot be improved in a short period of time, I feel anxious and struggle. I think giving up might be a good choice for someone like me who is often anxious because I am not omnipotent, but I often can't truly give up from the bottom of my heart, which makes me feel ordinary and inferior to others, somewhat embarrassed. How can I practice accepting some of my imperfections?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hi there, may I give you a virtual hug? After reading your description, you feel upset and helpless because you view yourself as an ordinary person. I can totally understand your thoughts. Maybe we all had dreams of becoming extraordinary when we were young, but as we grow up, we gradually feel that we are not as special as we imagined. Based on your description, you want to know how to practice accepting your imperfections, but you are afraid to face this fact. Although I don't know what kind of environment you grew up in or what kind of work you do, personally, I believe that most people in society are ordinary, and only a small number of people are exceptionally outstanding. There are also lucky ordinary people who have received attention and cultivation for their talents, so they can become what they dream of. Maybe we are not as ordinary as we think, it's just that our talents haven't been nurtured and valued. If we can receive support and opportunities, perhaps we can also be extraordinary. But we still have the chance to change, we can rely on our own efforts to develop our talents. I suggest you read some books. When reading, it's easy to resonate with the author's viewpoints and feel the validation and support of those perspectives. At the same time, don't pay too much attention to the news reports, as they may disrupt your judgment. Most of what is reported in the news are rare events.

question: 21-year-old, female, likes someone, feeling confused and hesitant, should I confess my feelings or not?
description: Uncle, hello, I don't know if you can see my message, but I still want to talk about it. I really don't know who to talk to. Have you ever experienced a crush? I don't know what to call my current situation. I found myself unknowingly liking a guy. But I know very little about him. We don't even chat on WeChat. But I have this feeling of being attracted to him. We met while playing badminton in college. He is really good at badminton, in my opinion. Of course, most of the time we just play badminton and don't really communicate much, just sports buddies. Considering that he is two years older than me, he is now working, probably near the school, but this is just my guess. Because he came to play badminton at school during the National Day holiday. And then I saw him again. I used to think that my crush would end as long as he graduated, but his appearance made me realize that my thoughts are back again. Lately, I've been thinking about whether I should be brave and confess, but when I think about the distance between us, I feel like it's not realistic. Also, I live in a dorm with three other people, and they all have boyfriends. I'm afraid that I only want to be in a relationship because of their influence. I'm starting to feel confused and tangled up.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. It's not necessary to consider too much when you like someone. Before you have confirmed that they are the lifelong partner you want, go ahead and give it a try. Be courageous and confess your feelings. Even if you get rejected and the crush ends, it won't be too difficult to get back to normal life. Crushes are beautiful, but it's painful to have an unrequited crush that doesn't lead to anything. You, being 21 years old, are referred to as a "big brother" by him, so age is definitely not an obstacle to love, that's for sure. I don't know why you haven't expressed your feelings yet. Is it because you're afraid? Uncertain if this relationship will have any results? I understand your dilemma. You thought you could move on after he graduated from college, but you met him during the National Day holiday and now your heart is stirred again. It means you haven't moved on yet and still have hope. The longer you have a crush on someone, the more difficult it is to suppress the fantasies of confessing. When you have a crush on someone without their knowledge, without them knowing your feelings, for them, nothing happens. But it doesn't feel good in your heart, so you need to have a bit of confidence. Don't think too much about other factors. The only thing in front of you is whether you like him or not. If you like something, you have to fight for it. Love is the same. One side will always have to make an effort first. The other three people in your dorm have boyfriends, maybe that affects you and makes you feel envious. But girl, liking someone is not about comparing, it's about knowing that I am happy in our little moments together. Even if I don't have a boyfriend, I can still live well and be happy. This is my life and I am in charge. You have little knowledge about guys, but you were drawn to him when playing badminton, so there must be something about him that you appreciate. In psychology, there is a phenomenon called the halo effect: it means having a very good impression of someone, so everything about that person is considered good. Have you not yet noticed his flaws because you don't know him well enough? Because of lack of understanding, the mystery amplifies your expectations of him, and you feel attracted to him. The longer the time goes on, the stronger this feeling becomes. If you're not in a hurry, my suggestion is to start from being friends first, get to know him better, and then find the right moment to confess. I hope my answer can help you. I wish you find your own happiness soon.

Hello there! Should you confess your feelings to someone you like? Sometimes we say, since you like him, why not confess your feelings? Yes, confessing once is not such a big deal for your life, so if you have such thoughts, you can go ahead. But based on your description, there is a very important question - are you mentally prepared for the outcome after confessing? In other words, he is very likely to reject you, and of course, rejection is his right, isn't it? So, if you are okay with being rejected and can adjust your mindset, then it's fine, and confessing is something you can do if you want. Actually, based on your description, I feel that the level of understanding between you is not enough, maybe he has no impression of you at all, and in this case, the chances of success after confessing will be very low. The establishment of any relationship requires acquaintance, understanding, and familiarity. There must be such a process, otherwise, it's just a gamble. Actually, objectively speaking, whether your roommate has a boyfriend or not has nothing to do with you. You should not be easily influenced by them. You should have your own opinion. Being single is not so scary or terrible. Good luck!

Hello downstairs, your message has been received. However, I am not an uncle, so I'm not sure if your question requires a specific uncle to answer. Here is my response for your reference. Based on your description, it seems that your current state is a secret crush. You established a friendship through playing basketball, and at that time, you started having feelings for him. However, because he graduated and left the school, you felt that the possibility of building a relationship was low, so you let it go. But fate works in mysterious ways, as the person you thought you would never see again came back to the school to play basketball during the holidays. Perhaps this time, you realize that your feelings for him and the desire to get closer have become even stronger. On the other hand, you don't know much about other aspects of him. But some information is actually very important, such as whether he is single, his character, personality, employment situation, etc. You also feel uncertain about your own feelings. Are you really experiencing a crush? Or is it because of hidden pressure in your living environment? So you feel anxious and conflicted, which is normal. It also shows that you have both sensitivity and rationality when it comes to dealing with emotions, which is a great advantage. I suggest not confessing your feelings right away, but rather developing a friendship as basketball buddies. You have a common interest and you are already WeChat friends, which is a great platform for communication and opportunities. As a girl, you can take the initiative to invite him to participate in some basketball activities, gradually increasing time spent together and opportunities to get to know each other. This process is important for both of you. As you get to know each other better, you will also be able to understand your own feelings more clearly, whether you truly like him or it's just because you feel lonely. Facing love requires courage and wisdom. Good luck!

Hello, OP. It seems that there is a little bit of ambiguity between you and him when playing basketball together. If he doesn't have anyone else in his heart, then it's easy for you to be a little more proactive. As for whether or not to make a move, if you really like him, why not go for it? Don't worry about other influences, just take care of yourself. It's a good thing to date multiple people before getting married. Going through a romantic relationship, regardless of the outcome, is always an important experience for personal growth. Give it a try, so that you'll have fewer regrets in the future. And if this relationship succeeds, it will truly be a beautiful thing in life. Good luck!

question: My younger brother has been blaming himself and feeling depressed since his girlfriend's suicide. How can I persuade him to see a doctor?
description: The younger brother feels guilty and falls into depression due to his girlfriend's suicide. He becomes unsociable, has little emotional connection with his family, and stopped seeing a doctor after one visit. Currently, he is unemployed and drifting alone outside.

answers.answer_text: This is a very complicated matter. The emotional blockage still needs psychological treatment. If we can find out the reasons for the girl's suicide, and let the younger brother know that the girl's suicide has nothing to do with him, and understand the whole story clearly, it would be the best. The second method is to introduce him to a girlfriend, and gradually shift his mental focus away, so that he can slowly overcome the shadows.

question: Why do people choose loyalty and faithfulness? Can't they follow their instincts?
description: I am 19 years old and have a long-distance boyfriend who is really great. But even though I have this amazing boyfriend, I still find myself attracted to others and worried that I won't be able to resist temptation. I just don't understand why people choose to have a monogamous life instead of being free to love and follow their instincts. It seems so much better to be irresponsible and do whatever you want. Besides external factors like money and morals, I want to know what makes someone willingly choose to spend their life with one person instead of being free and unrestricted.

answers.answer_text: Hello! I think this is really a great question. It's thought-provoking. Many people may have thought about it vaguely, but you asked it explicitly. You have the courage and the ability to think. I'll share my understanding with you, and we can explore it together. Our instincts may tell us that it would be great to follow our hearts, to love multiple people without being tied to one person for life. It seems more in line with human nature. But when we think about it on a deeper level, it may not necessarily be true. Setting aside morals, in real life, infidelity is not uncommon even in monogamous relationships. However, if we have no constraints of marriage, we may go to another extreme. Just imagine. It's okay if only a few people have the idea of loving multiple people, the impact on society may not be significant. But what if everyone is like that? It's unimaginable, right? Society may become chaotic. Looking at it from a psychological perspective: people achieve a dynamic balance between constraint and freedom. If there is only freedom, it may not necessarily be good for the individual. People have reason and can recognize their own existence, as well as phenomena such as aging and death. So people develop a feeling: loneliness. And with loneliness comes fear, fear of losing connection to the outside world, fear of being overwhelmed by the world. Therefore, the greatest need for people is to overcome the feeling of loneliness and reestablish connections with others and the whole world. But indulgence cannot drive away loneliness. The unity achieved through indulgence is temporary. Once the effect of the pleasure wears off, people become clear-headed again and the feeling of loneliness resurfaces. So indulgent people have to repeat this process over and over again. Only love can bring people closer, allowing them to form new unions and truly overcome loneliness and fear, and find meaning in their existence. Moreover, it cannot be all-encompassing love. Sometimes, loving too many people may not deepen the connection with individuals. Because love also implies responsibility. I'm not saying that one should only love one person for their whole life, but there may be many differences between loving one person wholeheartedly and loving multiple people at the same time. Love is a giving, not a taking. In the process of giving to each other, both parties awaken the vitality within each other, and obtain happiness and fulfillment. That's the beauty of love. Perhaps one day, you will willingly choose to love only one person. Erich Fromm said: positive love also requires four essential elements: care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge. I would like to recommend a book to you called "The Art of Loving". I gained a lot from reading it. As the questioner, you are young, go explore and experience it yourself. I believe life will give you the answer. Wishing you all the best!

First of all, to answer your first confusion, the premise of following instincts is that the other party can also accept it. The freedom we always talk about is also under legal constraints. Why do we need that? It is because personal desires and instincts are conducted without harming others. So, if your boyfriend confirms that he will not be hurt by you having another lover, then of course you can follow your instincts and interact with others, there is no problem with that. But on the other hand, if personal desires harm others, then we should try to avoid such issues. The second confusion is what makes a person willingly choose to spend their whole life with someone, rather than being free and unconstrained. I think there are two possibilities. First, in the eyes of these people, choosing to spend their life with someone does not conflict with being free and unconstrained. They are not interested in other people, and their spouse is someone who can understand them and resonate with them mentally, so even if they have a partner or get married, they still remain free and unconstrained. Second, in the eyes of some people, freedom and unconstraint are not that important, as they rank them lower in their life, while family and their partner rank higher in priority. After all, life presents infinite possibilities, what may be more important to you, like honey to a bee, may not be that important to others. These are my own answers to your two questions, I hope they can bring you some reflection and inspiration. Good luck~.

The original post is now 19 years old and self-esteem is still in the expansion period. The constraints felt are mainly external, so loyalty and loyalty in the original post are also due to "money, moral and other external reasons". Under this assumption, the essence of the original post's question is why should we obey external constraints instead of listening to our inner voice? In fact, when we do things, we should listen to our inner voice. However, we need to be very vigilant here and not confuse instincts with our inner voice. There is a simple way to distinguish between them, which is whether the driving force comes from enjoyment or responsibility. And in this drive, is it only about oneself or the whole world? Instinct is a capability that the body possesses itself without any effort from the individual. When thirsty, one wants to drink. When hungry, one wants to eat. When seeing someone you like, you want to be with them. These satisfactions are all about enjoyment, and in these enjoyments, there is only oneself, not others. For example, the original post asks why it is not possible to love multiple people at the same time. When you think "how nice it would be to be able to be irresponsible and do as you please," the man you have a connection with faces the possibility of being abandoned at any time. Put yourself in the shoes of potentially being abandoned at any time and see how it feels. Perhaps you would say, "I'm willing to take the risk and accept being abandoned if I can't hold onto that man's heart." Then a new question arises, what is being improved or sublimated in this process? Nothing. It's just living like an animal. What is the meaning of being human in that case? When you follow your inner voice, you will feel that your inner light becomes brighter and your inner strength becomes stronger. If you continue to follow it, you will experience a kind of fulfillment and happiness. On the other hand, the driving force of instinct is an insatiable emptiness. You can only love multiple people because none of them can fill that emptiness. However, the voice of the inner self is very small, while the voice of instinct is loud. To restrain instinct and make it quiet, so that we can hear the voice of the inner self. Therefore, in many people, the voice of the inner self has never been heard. "Do as you please without going beyond boundaries" is about following the inner light, while doing as the instinct pleases is just about desire.

OP, hello! I also think this is a topic worth contemplating. The pursuit of "novelty and excitement" may be an inherent human nature! From my personal perspective, if I were to choose a lifelong commitment, disregarding moral, responsibility, financial factors, it would probably be because - compared to novelty and excitement, I prefer a relationship that is intimate and comforting. (Of course, this is just my personal preference.) If I/my partner is someone who is whimsical and easily attracted to new things, then in this relationship, I would be reluctant to invest myself completely and would hold back, because we both know that this relationship will eventually come to an end. In that case, my first thought would definitely be how to minimize the hurt I would feel when the relationship ends, and as a result, the intimate experience brought by this relationship would be very limited. Sternberg proposed three elements of perfect love: intimacy, loyalty, and passion. Without intimacy and loyalty, only passion remains, becoming "obsessive love." This is also the choice of many people nowadays, including the previously popular "Pua" technique, which has some shadows in it. Over time, it is likely that the ability to love someone and maintain a high-quality relationship will be lost! Just like a very good friend of mine who just broke up last night. He is someone who lives in the moment, as the girl said, love is about being willing and happy, and he secretly dates many girls as well. Although he has very good conditions, every relationship cannot last. Of course, this is the lifestyle he has chosen, I don't know how much hurt each broken relationship has caused him, but at least last night, he got drunk like a dog. There is a very common saying - loving someone is like picking shells on the beach, don't pick the biggest or the most beautiful, just pick the one you like the most, and once you've found it, never go to the beach again. We can think of it like this, maybe, after meeting you, the other person has also met better and more outstanding individuals, but they still chose you! Finally, I wish you a happy life and a happy future!

Hello, this is a very good question. I also have such thoughts, although I may not be able to answer you, let me just talk about my own feelings. First of all, I think humans are just animals, or so-called higher animals. Let's talk about the attributes of larger animals or animals in general. In fact, except for a few exceptions, like swans having only one mate for life, most animals have multiple mates throughout their lives. What I want to say is that this kind of multiple mates is a natural instinct of most animals, including humans. The reason humans are considered superior is because we have established some rules and systems, which may not necessarily conform to our nature. They are more in line with social governance or national will. So, if we look at many laws or moral standards, many of them do not conform to human nature. Freud's theory of personality posits three states of being: the id, the ego, and the superego. Each of us wants to act according to the state of our id, but social rules force us to develop towards the state of our superego. When we achieve a balance as individuals, we will take into account the id and the superego, and act according to our own principles. Finally, what I want to say is that we are inherently social beings, so first and foremost, you must abide by the law. For example, adhering to monogamy, otherwise, you could be charged with bigamy and face legal punishment. Secondly, even if you don't get married, having multiple boyfriends or girlfriends at the same time may face moral condemnation. Perhaps you may not care about these things, but you may face pressure from parents and friends because we are still social beings. The above is my understanding of intimate relationships, for reference only.

Hello, OP. It's as if we're talking face to face. You've raised a very good question. In reality, many people are like this, always pursuing their desires, easily distracted, and irresponsible. They follow their instincts and prioritize themselves. But in the end, what do they really achieve? Humans have both animalistic and humanistic sides, and the animalistic side is the most basic part of human nature. The animalistic side refers to our instincts, such as eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, mostly for ourselves. This is human nature and instinct. However, successful people are more skilled at controlling this aspect of human nature, and they gain a lot from this process. This sets them apart and ultimately leads to success and extraordinary achievements. In fact, all the outcomes that make us better go against our animalistic nature. For example, if you want a good physique, you have to exercise and eat a balanced diet. However, our animalistic nature is to eat excessively and be lazy in bed. If we want to gain the cooperation and trust of others, we must learn to be understanding and loyal. Only then will others be willing to collaborate with us, whether it's in a team or in a marriage. So, if someone always acts on their whims or constantly changes their mind, over time, if others are aware of this trait, who would want to establish a long-term relationship with them? But does every project, every collaboration, every relationship have to reach a certain point before there can be a breakthrough, before there can be bigger gains? Likewise, ordinary people won't collaborate on a big project with someone they don't know well or haven't worked with for a long time because they don't know if they can trust that person. The same goes for relationships. If you only seek quick, short-lived romance and aren't prepared for something long-lasting, then you might not receive genuine affection from the other person. You may fall in love with multiple people, but you may not receive genuine love from anyone. The Golden Rule applies here as well: if you want others to be genuine towards you, you must first be genuine towards them. Don't be easily swayed by new opportunities. If you want someone to stay with you forever, then you should also remain committed to them. Otherwise, if your interactions are superficial and short-lived, you will find that when you're sad and seek comfort or when you're happy and want to share, there's no one by your side who truly understands your happiness or comforts you in sadness. Both understanding others and others understanding you require time. Cultivate your focus, cultivate your loyalty. This not only applies to others but also helps you become a better person. All the things that make you better go against your natural inclinations and may make you feel uncomfortable. So, do you choose comfortable decadence or uncomfortable excellence? Love yourself and keep going. I hope this advice is helpful to you. Click "useful" if it is. Thank you for crossing paths with me.

Hello! Giving you a warm hug. Your question goes beyond the current reality. In ancient societies, this may have been possible. With fewer people, the male humans would go out hunting for food, while females would not stay at home and would seek other males. As a result, it was difficult to determine the paternity of children. As society developed, the institution of marriage emerged to constrain women and provide legitimacy to children. In feudal society, men had multiple wives and concubines, while women were expected to stay at home and raise children. As women started gaining education and equality, they began to feel the imbalance in the institution of marriage. To address this, the new China was established, implementing a monogamous marriage system that imposed constraints on both men and women based on moral values. Therefore, in today's society and from a moral perspective, marriage is a mutual commitment that suits societal development and our national situation. To bring about change, there must be better physical or institutional alternatives that gradually replace the current system. Speaking of instincts, both men and women have desires, but it comes down to self-control and personal restraint in managing intense desires. Without rules and constraints in society, one can only imagine the consequences on the country, society, and families. In addition to pursuing a partner, we also have other things in life that we can focus on. Why not shift our attention and live in the present, avoiding unrealistic fantasies that only bring anxiety? In other words, if a woman is involved with multiple men or a man has multiple female partners, can they handle it? It would only create more trouble. So, let go of assumptions and fantasies, face reality, and focus on actionable things. If your long-distance boyfriend makes you feel lonely and unhappy, and you are not getting what you want, you can choose to continue the relationship or end it, and decide if you want to pursue a new romantic relationship. You are in control of your own life.

question: Do female bisexuals need to come out of the closet?
description: I am a girl, and in recent years, I have discovered that I have that kind of inclination. So far, I have developed a secret crush on three girls. Sometimes, I feel that they can attract me more than boys can....

answers.answer_text: Hello. I couldn't resist answering your question when I saw it. Regarding sexual orientation, it is still a sensitive topic in our country, but you don't have to worry too much. Because you didn't mention your age in your question, I will analyze it from the perspectives of youth and maturity, hoping to help you. 1. If you are still young, please don't rush to conclusions about your sexual orientation, but also don't suppress your preferences. Give yourself more time to determine through emotional experiences in life. 2. If you have reached a mature mindset, it will be easier for you. You just need to face bisexuality correctly, consider rationally whether to come out or not, and what it means for your life, and then make a choice. Regardless of age, whether heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, or transgender, as long as you don't harm others and love sincerely, you will receive support. In terms of openness in our country, young people actually don't have too many opinions about sexual orientation. But, as you mentioned, what troubles you is whether you can come out to your family. If your family is very open-minded and accepting, I am really happy for you. Otherwise, you may receive some doubts, but I also hope you understand that they don't not love you, they just don't understand and need more time to accept. Your mindset is also important, don't feel like you did something wrong. Having diverse sexual orientations is not wrong. What's wrong is that people lack a deep understanding of it. Keep it up!

question: Why do people always say things that I don't understand?
description: Will feel disgusted towards people who like themselves, get inexplicably excited when seeing rainy weather, experience intermittent breakdowns, say things that they cannot understand at midnight, and then cry while holding their head in their hands, with their body trembling uncontrollably.

answers.answer_text: Give the op a hug! Welcome to the warm nest of depression. I'm a little stove in the nest, hoping to bring some warmth and light to the op's heart, dispelling the coldness and darkness. Based on the information provided by the op, there are still many issues troubling them. Without providing age, gender, and specific experiences, but only these symptoms, I can only share some personal opinions based on this limited information for the op to consider. Feeling disgusted by people who like you can be seen as a subconscious reaction of the op's self. Others' liking of the op can be seen as understanding, acceptance, and recognition, but the op feels disgusted by this understanding and acceptance, which is a denial of others' feelings and indirectly a denial of oneself. Getting excited for no reason when seeing rainy days is usually a mood depressant for many people, but the op's reaction is completely opposite. This may be related to some events in the op's past that occurred on rainy days, leaving a deep impression on their heart. Intermittent breakdowns, saying things they can't understand in the middle of the night, crying with their head in their hands and body trembling involuntarily, typically occur when one's conscious self-defense is relaxed and their subconscious self is released. These symptoms reflect extreme suppression and fear in the op's heart. It is very difficult and uncomfortable to carry such great pressure inside oneself, but no one can hear or see it. The op can try to first accept these problems, then write them down, find a place where nobody is around to scream them out, or release them through exercise. They can also schedule an appointment with a suitable therapist for structured psychological counseling to release and alleviate the internal pressure. This will bring relief from pain and enable the op to face life with ease.

Hello, OP. Sending warm hugs to you (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand that your state of mind is not great. Here is my analysis and advice, hoping it can help you: Based on your description, it seems that your thoughts are not very clear and your state of mind is not good. I wonder how long this has been going on for you? Perhaps what you need to know is that sometimes we not only need our own strength, but also someone who can lend us a hand. This is where the role of a psychologist becomes especially important. So, I suggest you consider seeing a counselor, as they may accelerate your recovery! #The world and I love you, take care~.

question: Is it solely the guy's fault for the breakup because the girl found him too clingy?
description: Is it always the fault of the boys to break up because they are too clingy... Why are they so clingy~ For me, that is love...

answers.answer_text: Hello! (≧∇≦)/ I think you, the original poster, are a very lovely guy. You seem to be understanding and caring. I like that, so I hope you don't take things too much to heart. Everyone has different preferences and not everyone can truly understand or support the relationships you seek that are unnecessary to force. It's okay, just let it be. This kind of personality may be too much for some girls to handle. They might think, "Why is her boyfriend more clingy than she is?" and that could lead to various resentments towards you. Girls need comfort and care, but because of your personality, she may not be able to fully depend on you. Also, your desire for the care of others may intrude on your girlfriend's rest time and suffocate her. She needs to be able to independently handle her own affairs. She has her own studies and daily schedule, and during those times, she may not appreciate being disturbed by you. Moreover, you should trust that she can handle her own issues. Excessive worry can have the opposite effect. It shows your need for control and possessiveness, and it can make the other person feel restricted and without freedom. I don't know about your family situation, but generally, children who lack love tend to seek dependence on others. Perhaps in your life, your parents often say that they control you because they love you. They restrict your life and confine you to their side forever. But the problem is, people always learn to live independently and relying on others too much shows a lack of confidence in yourself. Although the things your girlfriend says may be excuses to put you off and not the real reasons for rejection, you should reflect on yourself. Have you always been demanding the care of others without truly giving back? I hope you encounter a better kind of love and become more responsible in nurturing that purity.

Hello, giving you a warm hug. Different couples have different ways of getting along. Some chase each other, some appear distant but they are close, and some even take on a parent or elder role. However, the most important thing is whether we have found a way of getting along that makes both of us comfortable. In your question, you mentioned being broken up because you were too clingy. Actually, being clingy itself is not necessarily right or wrong. Just like you said, you think it's love, and you're not wrong. It is a form of love. However, it's important to note that even with someone close, a certain distance needs to be maintained. Perhaps your clingy behavior happened to touch a boundary that made the other person uncomfortable, and you haven't realized it yet. Coupled with a lack of effective communication, it resulted in this outcome. This doesn't mean you were wrong, nor does it mean the other person was wrong. I hope my answer can help you (･ω･)ﾉ.

question: Added an online friend, maybe it was blank at the time, why am I only able to respond with "uh-huh"?
description: I am a girl. I added an online friend, and looking back, I really feel like I can't be bothered to talk to boys or something. However, it's the same when facing a boy I like. I don't really know how to find topics, and I'm afraid of awkwardness. If I'm not familiar with someone, I won't naturally engage in conversation. I either just say "yeah" or let them do most of the talking, making me seem uninterested. Why am I like this? Actually, I don't talk much, only occasionally, and I'm also slow to warm up. I'm afraid of saying the wrong thing, and when faced with someone, my mind goes blank. Is this because I like them or am I just lazy?
