Well, when I'm alone, I can come up with some interesting topics, but when a boy asks me if I have any questions for him, I couldn't think of anything. Maybe I was just blank at that moment and I'm confused about myself. Do I have a problem? I doubt myself. I'm better with friends who are more familiar to me.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, communication, interpersonal boundaries

answers.answer_text: A person answering "uh huh" can have many different states. It could be agreement, it could be perfunctory, or it could be not knowing how to respond. It also depends on how the other person interprets it. According to your description, I'm not sure if I understand correctly, but you are confused about not knowing what to say to unfamiliar people or to a guy you like, your mind goes blank and you can only reply with "uh huh". You don't know if this is okay, and you doubt if there is something wrong with you. So, can I understand that you are currently not fond of your interpersonal communication state with strangers and feel the need to change? Is your not knowing what to say due to nerves? Or is it because you genuinely don't know what to say? Or are you afraid of saying something wrong and making a bad impression? Or do you just feel like you don't have anything to say? Find the reason and then address the problem accordingly. There are many books on the art of speaking, such as "How to Win Friends and Influence People" by Dale Carnegie, "The Art of Communication - Looking into People, Seeing Beyond People" and "Crucial Conversations: Tools for Talking When Stakes Are High", etc. I believe it's more important to understand and accept oneself. So, I also recommend "Knowing Yourself, Accepting Yourself", "The Power of Self-Care" and "Nourishing and Settling Our Mind". However, we often experience anxiety in life when things don't go well. "Coping with Anxiety", "Managing Anxiety" and "Anxious Thoughts" can also help alleviate some of it. And in our lives, we always need the courage and wisdom to strengthen ourselves. "The Courage to be Disliked", "The Road Less Traveled", "Insecurity and Beyond" and "The Wisdom of Life" hope to give you some guidance. Finally, books are other people's experiences that we can learn from, but we don't have to fully agree with them. Everyone has their own unique experiences, and authenticity is more important than perfection. Many things in life are interconnected. Just strive to live your own life. You may be disappointed, hesitate, but you will also gain and feel proud of yourself. Best wishes!

OP, hello, I feel so sorry to see you in such distress, *hugs* to you. It's really difficult for introverted people. Normally, they don't have the courage to communicate with others too much, but suddenly they crave to share interesting things they've seen with others. However, they may not be familiar with those people and are afraid of disturbing them or feeling awkward. After all, friends who get along well are not by our side all the time, so it's not a bad thing to develop more friendly relationships. From your description, it's normal to have a blank mind and be afraid of saying the wrong thing when facing someone you like. You're totally fine. I remember one time when I cared a lot about maintaining a conversational atmosphere with a guy, I asked a friend for advice. She said to me, "Just be sincere, there's no special method." I instantly admired her, I couldn't believe that she, who normally jokes around, was so serious. As long as the other person feels your sincerity, you don't need too many strategies to maintain the relationship. It seems that you're not satisfied with your online behavior at that time, but I feel that whether it's with friends or online acquaintances, typing and chatting online is always unable to accurately express what we want to say and our emotions. Compared to face-to-face conversation in real life, there's an additional emotional barrier. Perhaps it's not your fault after all, you don't have to feel so remorseful for not performing well. I suggest you speak up more in front of unfamiliar classmates, raise your voice a little, and complain about common annoyances. This is your common topic. Don't worry too much about not having anything to say. Many people are willing to express themselves. Maybe you can be a good listener and gradually your relationship with them will get closer. You can also express yourself appropriately and get to know each other.

OP, hello~~~ Give the OP an encouraging hug. After reading the OP's description, I understand that the OP feels a bit "at a loss" when facing boys, especially those they have feelings for, as if their language function has "gone on standby". But this doesn't necessarily mean that we have a problem: for some people, when facing strangers or when starting to interact with someone they care about, similar situations may arise. Because when we face them, our hearts subconsciously become nervous, coupled with previous experiences of "blanking out", this can create a feeling that we will inevitably face an awkward situation this time as well, causing our nervousness to escalate and affecting our language organization, and so on. In light of this, we might as well touch on such scenarios in our daily lives, choosing someone to treat as the boy we care about, and practice more, gradually getting used to this nervous emotion. On the other hand, we can also learn some social skills appropriately.

question: I have severe depression accompanied by schizophrenia. Should I take a leave of absence from school?
description: This year, I was diagnosed with severe depression and schizophrenia, making it impossible for me to study normally. As a result, I took a long-term leave of absence. When it comes to the question of whether to continue studying or not, my family has different opinions. My mom believes that after resting well, I should return to school. However, other relatives believe that my health is the most important and that I should temporarily stay in a quiet and comfortable environment to recuperate before returning to school. Because I have a strong sense of self-protection, I have had a few sessions of psychological counseling, but the effects were not very obvious. I am a bit inclined to return to school because I'm afraid of delaying my studies, but at the same time, I'm also afraid that uncontrollable things might happen when I go back to school.

answers.answer_text: No matter how strong your self-protective awareness is, severe depression accompanied by schizophrenia cannot be effectively treated with just a few psychological consultations. As the saying goes, it takes time to accumulate severe depression, and it also takes time to solve it. In my work, there are students who have similar situations as you. They feel that going to school may make them feel better, but usually they cannot stick to it for even a day. The next time they feel they can go, they can't even last half a day. I still suggest that you take good care of yourself and continue with psychological counseling. This is an important way for you to stay connected with others while staying at home. Medication can be effective, but combining it with long-term psychological counseling ensures better results. This is a conclusion drawn from many, many cases.

You are depressed, and there must be a problem with your family environment. From the fact that your mother is anxious for you to go to school, she has put a lot of pressure on you. It is suggested to stay with friendly relatives for a period of time, and also involve your mother in psychological therapy. If there is no improvement after some time, try switching to a different psychologist.

question: I have a boyfriend, but I have feelings for another guy, what should I do?
description:
Gender: Female
Age: 22
Occupation: Graduate student
Problem description: I met a boy online, we got along very well and I had feelings for him. I could sense that he also had feelings for me, but I couldn't accept it because I already have a boyfriend. So I rejected his confession and he blocked me. However, my emotions and productivity have been affected lately, and I often miss him. Request: I would like to ask the teachers if there are any methods that can help me quickly overcome my current state of confusion.

answers.answer_text: Generally speaking, in the early stages of a relationship that has not yet deepened, people tend to have more doubts and attachments. This is because the perfect fantasy of the other person in their subconscious has not been shattered by reality, making it difficult to let go. If you try to "forget about him" too hard, it means that you are still keeping your attention tied to him. It is better to focus on other things that interest you more and invest more time and energy in life, study, work, etc. You don't always have to try to forget about him, it's okay to fully allow yourself to think about him when you miss him. With the decrease of hormones, this kind of longing will naturally subside.

Hello! After reading the description, I still have two small doubts. First, does the other person know that you have a boyfriend? Second, what is the content of the confession? Do they want to be your boyfriend or just maintain a friends with benefits relationship? This seemingly unsuccessful "love" is actually just an emotion for you. You get along very well with an opposite sex online friend, and it seems like you have found a soul mate, but it is likely that the other person is just providing you with emotional value that you cannot get from your boyfriend. You are lacking in this aspect, like encountering a refreshing rain. Fortunately, your subconscious and rationality saved you. They held you back before you crossed the line and let you reject the confession. You instinctively know that the other person is just providing you with emotions. If it really comes to reality, it's very likely that your current boyfriend won't truly treat you well, nor continue to provide you with emotional value. So, in order to free yourself from the current dilemma, there is only one method, and that is to see the "truth". At the same time, you need to reflect on why you would invest so much emotion or sentiment in an online acquaintance. Why do you desire emotional value so much? What needs in your real-life relationships are not being fulfilled? Can you communicate with your boyfriend to fulfill those needs? Stepping out of those lonely imaginings, only real relationships have the potential to heal your inner lack, only real relationships can bring you healing.

Feeling conflicted is actually a signal from within: you need to pause and carefully examine what is happening. If you use certain methods to temporarily escape this discomfort, you will miss an opportunity to understand and experience yourself. The feeling is spontaneous and cannot be truly eliminated. The more you try to get rid of it, the more it will remind you in stronger ways of its existence, because it is a part of you. If possible, it may be better to consult with a teacher.

question: Will people feel happier with the increasing number of internet products?
description: With such a rich variety of internet products available today, there are numerous options for software consumption alone. Does this abundance of internet products increase or decrease people's sense of happiness?

answers.answer_text: Recently, I happened to be reading "Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience," and the author's mentioned concept of psychic entropy can be used to explain the issues raised by the original poster. Entropy, in a sense, describes the degree of disorder and chaos in things. The higher the level of disorder, the higher the entropy value. Applied to the realm of the mind/thoughts, we call it psychic entropy. The abundance of products provides a plethora of information, and the influx of a large amount of information can increase psychic entropy. Happiness, on the other hand, can only be experienced when the entropy value is sufficiently low. Therefore, if the abundance of internet products only leads to an increase in a person's psychic entropy, it will diminish their sense of happiness. However, if a person has strong integrative abilities, the abundance of information will provide them with more materials, and from this perspective it may help them lower their psychic entropy (incorporating previously disordered/unable to integrate aspects through the addition of new materials). So, to sum up, I feel that internet products and other forms of information are the same - they can be used to your advantage if you can handle them, but if you are controlled/drowned by them, they can harm you.

question: How to overcome innate fears of certain animals?
description: I have been scared of snakes since I was a child, even if they appear on TV or are toy snakes. I know they won't harm me, but I still feel very afraid. It's the same with some small insects. Why is that? How can I overcome this natural fear?

answers.answer_text: ※How to overcome natural fear of certain animals? I, like the original poster, am also very afraid of snake-like animals. Even seeing toys similar to snakes can make my heart race. I think everyone has their own fears and disappointments. Just like you and I are afraid of snakes, snake owners can live with them. For example, some people are afraid of dogs, but many people love dogs. This is not a psychological problem, but rather a difference in understanding and perception between different beings, which can lead to different cognitive and behavioral responses. Therefore, do not worry too much, accepting one's own fear is also a way to face and deal with it. If you want to overcome this state, you can try the behaviorist method of 'systematic desensitization'. Try to be with the thing you are afraid of and see if it is as scary as you imagine. At first, you can spend a shorter amount of time together and then gradually increase it. Eventually, you won't be so afraid of it anymore. It is important to have someone present during these desensitization behaviors to prevent any accidents, and it is preferable to have a professional present.

question: Should I let my child exhibit Sheldon-like behavior since they show signs of autism?
description: I have a child with a tendency towards autism, who is now facing the problem of choosing a major. This child is interested in programming and also enjoys design. The majority of teachers suggest that the child should study theoretical computing, but I am worried that the independent nature of theoretical computing work will exacerbate their tendency towards loneliness. Should I let the child pursue this field of study?
keywords: Growth, developmental patterns, and child development.

answers.answer_text: First, it is important to respect the child's opinions because in the future, they will need a job that they are good at and enjoy, which will bring them the greatest happiness. I understand as a parent, you also hope that your child will not only have a good job but also good social relationships. If the child is unsure, you can have them take a test to determine their innate temperament. If they have a cheerful temperament, they may be more suitable for jobs that involve interacting with people. If they have a calm temperament, they may be more suitable for jobs that involve theoretical or computational work. If they have a more adventurous temperament, they may have leadership potential. Everyone has five different types of innate temperament, it's just that the proportions vary. As long as we as parents provide sufficient psychological nourishment, every child can shine brilliantly.

question: Good work may not be sustained for a long time, as it can become dull over time.
description: At the beginning of the job application, I was full of energy and made a very good first impression on others. I also felt great about myself and thought the nature of the work was decent. However, when I just started doing it, I felt very anxious and worried about whether I was doing well. But as I gradually got the hang of it and time went by, I felt unenthusiastic and thought it became boring.

answers.answer_text: ~~I can very much understand the emotions described by the questioner. I think this is also a struggle that many working people face. This process of going from anticipation to nervousness and then to familiarity doesn't just happen in work, it can happen in many things. Because we cannot always maintain a perfect level of enthusiasm and motivation towards something, the same goes for work. We will always have days where we are used to the current work mode. Not all jobs can bring us a sense of freshness every day. But we can try to find motivation for ourselves, such as giving ourselves regular rewards, feeling the self-worth that comes from achieving results, and so on. On the other hand, during our spare time from work, let's not forget to enrich our lives and make work just a part of life, not everything.

question: The girl I like has been acting distant recently. She said she is timid. What should I do?
description: I have a good conversation with the girl I like, we have been on two dates. The chatting and atmosphere before, during, and after the dates were great. However, a week after the second date, she started becoming a bit distant. We chat less on WeChat, and she didn't directly agree to go on another date. The atmosphere has been low for about two weeks. Yesterday, I opened up and asked her why our recent contact has been fading. Her reply was as follows: She said she doesn't lack a sense of security, but she always feels pretty good being alone and is capable of enjoying herself. However, she thinks being in a relationship is easily controlling, so she is hesitant. Sometimes she wonders if it would be better not to harm others and is unsure if she can really accept someone. She feels that I am sincere in our interactions, which makes her scared. She is a very timid person – as soon as things get serious, she becomes hesitant. Teachers, please give me advice on what to do. Thank you.
keywords: Love, sense of security, love management, liking

answers.answer_text: Hello, @From your description, I can understand that the girl you like is in an avoidant state when it comes to building intimate relationships with others. There can be many reasons for this avoidance, but from her explanation, it does seem like it's not your fault. In the book "Trap of Personality," the concept of emotional deprivation is mentioned. People with this defect have low expectations of others and believe that they are lonely, with no one truly capable of loving them. They may initially feel a flutter of attraction but quickly dismiss the other person. Perhaps the reasons the girl gave were just a cover-up, and emotional deprivation may be the real reason for her rejection. Based on the reasons the girl provided, I think she is someone who is open-minded or craves freedom, yet is afraid of being tied down and taking on responsibilities. This applies even to romantic relationships. It often implies that our daily routines will change because of another person. Being together as partners often requires spending time to maintain the relationship, and there may be occasional disagreements. Emotional fluctuations may also become more significant, for example, during the sweet phase of being in love, happiness bubbles up, but sometimes it can also delay tasks. Getting angry and arguing can also disturb oneself, and one must learn how to communicate and coexist. In fact, friendships also require maintenance, but romantic relationships are more intimate and require investment of time. At the same time, possessiveness, security, personal space, and other issues exist within romantic relationships. <<Is the purpose of your question to know how to change the girl's mindset and accept being with you? I think you could try the following: 1. The girl may be someone who values personal space and personal life very much. Which girl wouldn't want a partner who is serious about emotions? Perhaps your seriousness makes her retreat, probably due to self-issues because you highly value this relationship and her, which might make her fear your possessiveness. You can communicate with the girl about each other's ideas of a rational partner. If your ideal intimate relationship is similar to the girl's, your compatibility will make both of you more confident in getting along and being in a romantic relationship. 2. Don't be impatient. If you really like her, show your patience. Use actions to dispel her doubts. Let her know that while the concerns she has about being in a relationship may indeed happen, it will also bring many wonderful experiences. Intimate relationships are also a learning process. In the process of dating, through getting along, compromising, and accommodating each other, a stable state can be reached. Isn't that how life is? Encourage her to take this step with you. If she's really not ready for a romantic relationship, then don't force it! I hope my answer can help you!

Hello, the person asking the question. Seeing your words is like meeting face to face. Each of us may have uncertainties when entering new relationships, and the other person may be concerned that this relationship will become a constraint for her.【The girl I like became distant on our second meeting】From the process of your interaction with her, it seems that she may not have no interest in you. However, she started to become distant from the second meeting, which made you feel a discrepancy. "I don't lack a sense of security, but I always feel good about myself and can enjoy being alone. However, being in a relationship makes it easy to be controlled, so I hesitate. Sometimes I think, maybe it's better not to cause trouble for others, I'm not sure if I can accept someone else. When she interacts with me, she feels that I am sincere, and that scares her." This avoidance of relationships may stem from concerns that entering a romantic relationship will disrupt her existing life order and experiences. In a romantic relationship, time and energy need to be allocated to maintain the relationship, and being together all the time is a disruption to her personal independence. She also worries that she may not be a good partner. So, all these thoughts combined make her hesitant, and her "coldness" towards you is the manifestation of this hesitation.【If you want to continue, you need to give her more time】Her resistance to romantic relationships stems from her own uncertainties and worries about not being able to fulfill responsibilities. So, if you can confirm that she does have feelings for you, why not lower your expectations a bit and give each other a longer period of time to get to know each other and dispel concerns. In relationships, someone always needs to take that first step. If you are truly sure of your feelings, then helping the person you like overcome their hesitations about future relationships is an important step in establishing a sense of security and confidence in love. I believe that you have shown her your determination and love, and she may have the courage to take that step for you. Of course, if you personally feel that you cannot accept such a prolonged wait, or if you feel that the other person is constantly unable to enter a certain state during the waiting process, then giving up is also a timely step to cut losses. Although meeting someone you like is not easy, you shouldn't keep running on a road with no end in sight. Best wishes, a little mushroom hoping for a gentle world and giving herself ample time to grow.

Thank you for the invitation, I'll try to see if we can figure things out together. Whether or not you accept a girl's reasons to continue the relationship depends on how much courage you have to handle the possibility of being deceived or betrayed. Let's take an extreme example: if Jack Ma, when he first started his business, talked to you about his dreams and asked you to invest, what would your choice be? It's the same in romantic relationships. However, if it's a scam from the beginning, that's not within the scope of this discussion. How can you tell whether the other person is genuinely refusing or there's another hidden reason? It's impossible to determine accurately! Because both the probability of being wrong or right is 50%. In romantic and interpersonal relationships, we can never know the other person's true thoughts with 100% certainty, but we can be 100% sure of our own true thoughts. How do you determine if you have fallen in love with someone? How do you differentiate between having a fondness for someone and genuine feelings? How do you handle rejection from the other person? How do you express your refusal to them?... These are all questions that can be self-clarified. The clearer you are about your true motivations, the more certain you will be when faced with events. How do you deal with past emotional hurts? I suspect your hesitation stems from having a strong liking for the other person, but past emotional hurts have made you afraid to try again. If that's the case, I strongly recommend finding a trusted counselor to explore your views on love and marriage. This is also related to your own growth process, family influences, and your parents' marital status. Exploring these areas can help clarify your "capacity for love". Our capacity needs constant refinement and improvement through love. Being hurt in the past makes us worry or fear losing again, but as you delve into counseling, you will find that your ability to face "loss" will also change. As you become increasingly capable of love, you will also gain clarity on the kind of love you desire... Congratulations!

It actually depends on the questioner, what do you think? Do you want to continue developing with her? If she says she's hesitant, can you be braver and firm in your thoughts? The girl has expressed some rejection, but it's hard to tell whether it's a polite refusal or she's genuinely afraid of romance. So the only thing that can be confirmed now is your thoughts and attitude. If you think she's great and don't want to give up on her, you can definitely try again. If you can't meet up for now, you can chat and share daily life, and then try to make plans after some time has passed. After all, you don't have much to lose, right? If the other party doesn't verbally reject you and asks you not to bother her anymore, it's also not a bad thing to temporarily maintain a normal friendship. Of course, this should be based on your comfort level. If you feel that your efforts are not being reciprocated and you don't get a definite response from the other person, you will feel distressed. Maybe you're not suitable for this kind of interaction. Perhaps you can jokingly tell the other person that you're not afraid of her causing trouble, you're afraid that she won't cause trouble for you. Tell her to take it slow, it's okay, no need to force yourself into a relationship. With a relaxed and comfortable mindset, don't pressure each other, maybe things will take a turn for the better. Building a relationship slowly also means building trust. If the other person lacks a sense of security, they will gradually be moved by you and keep in touch with you. If they are truly not interested in you, they will reply less and less, and will not go on dates with you anymore, and then you'll understand. Just respect the other person.

Hello, dear questioner. I can truly feel your emotions right now, and I sincerely hope that my words can help you. After reading your description, I am happy that you have the courage to raise questions and find ways to solve them. This is really great because we can only solve problems by identifying them. The girl said, "I don't lack a sense of security, I just feel that I can be fine on my own. There is no need for an additional boyfriend and a romantic relationship." She is afraid of harming others and is unsure if she can accept someone else. The girl is a bit timid and afraid of your sincerity, afraid of being serious. She feels that she is fine on her own and can have fun alone, and feels that being in a romantic relationship means being controlled. Actually, this kind of thinking is quite common for both girls and boys. Just like when I asked a male friend of mine why he doesn't date, I couldn't refute his answer. He said, "I like playing games. Isn't it great to play games alone or with roommates? Why do I have to have a girlfriend and argue with her?" Although this kind of thinking cannot experience the beauty of love, it also reflects that many people enjoy a solitary life and are afraid of disturbance. My suggestion is to learn to show vulnerability. Show the girl that you need her, and let her see her value in your life. As for being unsure if she can accept someone else, I think it is necessary to give each other time and space, but be patient during this process and maintain contact. Alternatively, you can discuss whether to try a "few days as a couple" experience, where you spend a few days living as a couple to see if it suits you. In relationships, sometimes it seems that we really need skills, but it is actually about having a heart, sincerity, thoughtfulness, and patience. I hope she can see your efforts. Wishing you a happy life!

Hello! After reading your description, your current dilemma is that the girl you like is afraid that being in a relationship with you will disrupt her current stable and independent life. How should you proceed? First, understand her concerns. She has clearly expressed that she believes being in a relationship will restrict her freedom and disrupt her single life. It can be seen that she does have feelings for you, as she has gone on two dates with you. However, her level of affection may not be as deep as "cannot live without you." So, you need to make her understand that being in a relationship doesn't mean sacrificing freedom. Your presence is a form of protection and companionship for her. The life of being in a relationship can also be comfortable and wonderful. Second, give her time to experience your love and grow accustomed to your presence. Show her care and concern, but don't make her feel burdened. While getting closer to her, respect her feelings. Don't rush to define the relationship or make her feel pressured. Continue to be by her side and let her get used to your presence. When her impression of you deepens, it will be easier to enter into a romantic relationship. I wish you the best!

Hello! I can sense that you are hesitant and unsure. Let's take a look at the issue you are facing. You met a girl whom you had a good conversation with, and you thought things were progressing well. However, she suddenly became distant. You were not satisfied with ending things like this without an explanation, so you candidly asked her for the reason. She also candidly expressed her thoughts. It turned out that she didn't have any issues with you but had her own personal reasons for wanting to retreat. Therefore, you feel uncertain about what to do. Regarding this matter, there are two options: either continue or walk away. For you, giving up right now feels a bit unsatisfactory because meeting someone with whom you can connect is not easy. Therefore, you are unwilling to let go. However, if you choose to continue, you don't know if you can eventually make her accept you or if it will end up being a waste of time. I don't know what choice you will make, but there is a method you can consider. Before starting something, think about the worst possible outcome. If you can accept that worst outcome, then go ahead and start. If you cannot accept it, then evaluate the situation and see if you can handle the risks involved. Additionally, I want to remind you that we shouldn't have the notion that we can change others. What we can do is influence others through our actions and personal growth. Whether or not they develop in the direction we expect is unpredictable. No one can mold another person into the exact image they desire, like a gardener trimming a bush. I hope this can be helpful to you.

Hello, I think the girl has been single for a while and has become accustomed to being independent, so she feels that being alone is good. The current dilemma is like knowing that she should start dating, but she has a lot of concerns about being in a relationship, and she is in a state of both wanting and not wanting. So what she needs is time. If you really like the girl, give her some time so that she understands that being in a relationship with you will not affect her personal space. You should even try to make her feel that being together with you is better than being alone, but of course you need to strike a balance. Good luck to you.

question: When faced with oppression from people close to you, constantly shedding tears, how can one overcome it?
description: Being suppressed by important figures such as the boss, boyfriend, or family can create a sense of worthlessness and inadequacy. It causes a great deal of emotional pain, leading to immense internal suffering and an overwhelming feeling of sadness, as if being torn apart. The desire to leave the company and distance oneself from those who suppress can be strong. Although not opposed to receiving advice, it becomes intolerable when it is unreasonable and leads to arguments and emotional distress. There is a strong desire to slack off at work and increase social interactions since being unappreciated. However, accepting these thoughts and feeling at peace with them is difficult and leads to profound sadness, potential difficulty in coping, and even depression.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Before answering, give me a hug! I see that you often suffer from oppression and criticism from close people, which causes you pain. It shows that deep down, you long for their approval and praise. But why do we need constant validation and praise from others? Dr. Chapman, a famous American psychologist, found in his years of psychological research that in all psychological games, there are three roles: persecutor, savior, and victim, and everyone constantly switches between these three roles. The person in the victim role often appears very aggrieved and pained, but in reality, they receive a lot without giving much in return. Although the other person may seem selfish and indifferent, resembling a persecutor, they actually bear a lot of responsibility and give a lot. You can try to see if you unconsciously put yourself in the position of the weak and the victim in relationships. Common clues include feeling helpless, weak, vulnerable, and pitiful, often feeling lonely and helpless, perceiving others as selfish and indifferent or untrustworthy and capable of harming you, avoiding or relying on others when faced with issues while resisting others' demands and suggestions, often abandoning tasks or having a good start but not following through, often longing to go back to childhood or the past, imagining a carefree and worry-free state... So, by catering to their ideas and making ourselves so unbearable, we are actually using self-harming behaviors to make the other person feel guilty. However, this method may not always be effective and may instead cause us more pain, even leading to depression. It may be helpful to replace ourselves with the perspective of a strong person, objectively view others' evaluations, face our own strengths and weaknesses, and strengthen our inner selves in order to better face ourselves and the real world. When hearing oppression from others: Do not see it as their evaluation of you. Sometimes when expressing opinions about specific events, people may mistakenly associate the event with the person. We need to judge whether what they say is only about that particular event, whether it is due to our failure to take responsibility, or whether it is a difference in concepts and ideas between us. In any case, do not see it as an evaluation of you. Lowering self-evaluation can lead to feelings of depression and low self-esteem, causing painful thoughts. Selective listening: In the current educational environment, many people have experienced oppressive communication. Therefore, when communicating, it is inevitable to continue the communication methods they have experienced before. So we need to determine the underlying perspective of the oppression. What does the other person want to express? Does he really deny everything about you? Or is he just dissatisfied with a certain event or action? If the other person is verbally abusive, it is their problem, their pain. Even the people closest to us have a partial and subjective understanding of us. When accepting criticism, selectively consider the viewpoints that you think are correct and beneficial to your growth. If you feel that it doesn't reflect the actual situation, you can ignore their opinions. Continuously arguing and explaining will only worsen the relationship. Harsh words can be beneficial. The surrounding language cannot be changed, so change your own perspective. You can turn these words into motivation to move forward. Growth is not smooth sailing, but we can become stronger because of these words. When faced with doubt, give yourself positive mental suggestions like, "I am capable of doing well! Next time, I will prove myself!" Be calm when accepting different opinions. Be aware of your own patterns of interaction with others. Don't punish yourself for others' mistakes and hinder your own growth. Try to communicate your feelings and thoughts with others, so that they can understand better ways to communicate with you. Only by making ourselves stronger and having a comprehensive and objective understanding of ourselves, can we avoid using words as weapons to harm ourselves and others. I hope this answer is helpful to you! Wishing you happiness.

Hello, I saw that you are feeling very sad and upset because of the suppression from important people in your life, so here's a big hug for you. We all care about how others perceive us, especially those who are important to us, such as our parents, friends, partners, colleagues, bosses, etc. When we hear negative evaluations from them, it's easy for us to get hurt and internalize those evaluations, leading to self-deprecation and lack of confidence. First, let's give a hug to that little girl inside who has been hurt. She feels so helpless, sad, and upset. Secondly, let's think about why you feel sad and upset. The reason why we care about their evaluations is because we want to receive their recognition and praise. When we don't get that satisfaction, we easily get hurt. You care a lot about the evaluations from your boss and your boyfriend's family because you want their recognition. You want to prove your worthiness in their eyes. Based on the analysis above, here are my suggestions: 1) First, understand that the suppression and claims of incompetence from your boss and your boyfriend's family are not the reality. These evaluations are only based on their own perspectives, and they only see certain aspects of you, not your entirety. Moreover, there are definitely shining points about you as well. When you feel very sad, try to focus more on those shining points. 2) When we encounter such situations, arguing and cold war are not the best solutions. They will escalate conflicts and confirm their beliefs. When you hear them say those things, first adjust your own emotions, and then express your inner feelings to them. You can say something like, "When I hear you evaluate me like this, I feel really sad and hurt. I want to receive your recognition and praise. Maybe I haven't done well enough in certain behaviors, but I hope you can point them out to me, and I will make improvements." 3) Additionally, if you feel unappreciated and start doing things according to their standards, it is actually a form of negative resistance. This is not beneficial to you, and it will only make their influence on you stronger. You will find yourself losing your own identity and being controlled by others completely. Your mood will also worsen. So, I hope you don't use this negative approach to deal with the problem, but rather find a positive way to solve it. When you solve these problems, I believe your mood will improve significantly. Alright, that's the end of my answer. I hope it helps you.

question: Is it really that troublesome for me to go through all the efforts for a year but still have a high probability of failing the postgraduate entrance examination?
description: I am a senior this year, and it is highly likely that I will not be able to pass the postgraduate entrance exam. I know how much I lack compared to others, so I plan to study for another year. I am currently studying at home. Although I know it would be more efficient to study at school, I am causing trouble for my roommate in the dormitory (because I turn over in my sleep) and she cannot sleep. I feel very guilty and also can't sleep myself (mentally exhausted + feeling wronged + stressed + guilty). I have mentioned many times before that I can't control myself from turning over, but the response I get is cold violence. Every time, she deliberately ignores me, probably because I constantly express my guilt about turning over. Another roommate who has a good relationship with her posted something sarcastic about me on social media (probably cursing at me). So, I came back home. My mom said I am stupid and that I brought this upon myself and should not have let them bother me. It's troublesome and there are many issues at home. I think she is right. In order to resist many temptations, I moved to an empty house to live in. I bought a desk and brought all my study materials with me. My mom helped me pack everything. However, my studies this year have not been going well. My mom said that if I can't pass the exam, I shouldn't tell so many people that I want to take the postgraduate entrance exam. It's troublesome for others and it costs a lot of money, but if I still can't pass, it would be very embarrassing. Isn't failure normal? I wanted to go to the library to study and apply for a bus card, but my mom said I have too many things going on.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I see your helplessness and tenacity, and my concern for you is less than the inspiring feeling of being happy for your resilience. There is a saying that both parents are toxic and harmful. They control and manipulate your thoughts and actions under the guise of doing it for your own good and love for you. They unload their anxieties, worries, and fears onto you without thinking, in order to relieve their own pressure. They criticize, deny, doubt, and lack encouragement, support, and unconditional love, which lowers your sense of existence, value, worth, and self-esteem. You clearly recognize the interference and influence of your mother's irrational arguments and express it clearly and insightfully. Your self-awareness prevents you from being caught up in it but leads to deep self-blame and inferiority. I applaud you for that. Firstly, accept the current situation and take responsibility for changing it. Differentiate yourself from your mother and don't let her anxious emotions affect you. Feel the sense of sadness and frustration she brings, then try to understand her. After all, you can vent your stress and negative emotions to her. Your mother is also worried, exhausted by supporting and laboring for various aspects of your life. On the other hand, her venting is also an unintentional mistake. There is an Oedipus complex that mentally kills parents. Do not accept their denial, criticism, doubt, and many flaws transposed onto the children. We have to form our own independent personalities and strive for ourselves, not to learn from them, not to continue their unfinished lives. You can write down your feelings and thoughts, and release your emotions. Both those who succeed and fail in the postgraduate entrance exam exist in my circle. Life is a process of exploration, always pursuing self-fulfillment. Taking responsibility for the consequences is a sign of growth and maturity. Everyone pays attention to themselves and has no psychological energy to focus on others. When your mother says others care about the embarrassment of your postgraduate entrance exam, it is just her own concern, others do not have the time to pay attention. Each person has a lot of personal matters to attend to. Three things: God's matter, one's own matter, and other people's matter. Focus on doing our own thing. Another three things: past matters, present matters, and future matters. Let's focus on what we are doing at the moment. Brave face life, embrace failure, fall down, succeed, and use our lives to create life. We are all facing the scorching sun, born to face death. Practice mindfulness meditation, exercise, read more, and give yourself more bonus points. Don't blame yourself and others too harshly, don't have absolute demands on yourself and others, don't make sweeping judgments about people or things, don't overly worry about things, and don't overthink about the future because the scenarios you worry about excessively have never happened. The world and I love you!

OP, hello. I can sense your distress, helplessness, and worries, and I hope my response can offer you some assistance. The way I see it, you are a very kind person who considers the feelings of others and takes your mother's advice into consideration. Because of this, you feel guilty, blame yourself, and doubt yourself. Yes, sometimes we need to consider the feelings of others, but at the same time, we also need to take care of our own feelings and find a balance between the two. We should neither intentionally attack others nor oppress ourselves, or even attack ourselves. What we need to do is accept, accept ourselves, and also accept the other person. Your mother is right, that is just her personality, and she doesn't want to change, no one can change her. So we accept her, that's just the way she is. This way, when she behaves in a certain way, we won't oppose her, and we can save more energy to do what we need to do. Now you have a separate room for studying, which is great. It seems like this is the best way you have found that can help isolate many factors that hinder your studying. Since you've made this decision, you should make an effort and not worry too much. Focus on your studies, adhere to your plan, value the process, and don't obsess over the outcome. Because you can only control the process, the outcome actually has some uncertain factors. If you keep worrying about whether you will pass or not, it won't help your studying very much. Instead, it will drain your energy, make you feel exhausted, and prevent you from entering a good state for studying. Stay confident, follow your plan, study diligently, keep the learning process firmly in your hands, and work hard. If you do your best, you won't have any regrets! Stay strong, and take care.

Hello, I hope my answer can help you. 1. Sleep is the most relaxing state for people, it is unconscious. It is difficult to excessively demand or restrain the sleep state because it is being overly strict on oneself. 2. Regarding others' accusations about your sleep state, do you really think it is your responsibility to bear? Don't you think there are actually many ways to solve this problem, but your classmates have chosen a very strict approach, and you have accepted their strictness. Is this attitude limited to only them or is it the same with other people as well? You can think about it and it can help sort out your interpersonal relationships! 3. You are preparing for the postgraduate entrance examination, and the pressure itself is already huge. Have you arranged for appropriate relaxation and activities? If you only have stress without understanding and empathy for your own situation, it will be really exhausting, becoming more and more tiring. I hope you can find a balanced and relaxing way of life and get through this important period of time.

I think you should separate these two things. Not being able to pass the postgraduate entrance examination is just your speculation. Go and take the exam first, finish it, and then we'll see. It may not be like what you imagine. Even if you don't pass, it doesn't prove anything. One failure? Failure is normal. No one is without failures. How many times did Edison fail before inventing the light bulb? Probably thousands of times. If he found it troublesome, we might not even have electric lights now. Moreover, even if you fail, it doesn't mean you didn't try, it's just that the result is not what you imagined. It has nothing to do with your worth as a person. The postgraduate entrance examination itself is difficult, so don't put too much pressure on yourself. Relax, take it easy, and the result may be better. That's the only thing you can do. You may be under too much pressure. If you're very troubled, you can talk to a counselor. Take care!

Hello, OP! First, here's a big hug for you~ Let's take a look at your problem: You feel like there's a high probability of not passing the postgraduate entrance exam in December, mainly because of your roommate's issue and having to go back home. OP, don't blame yourself too much for this matter. Every postgraduate student is under a lot of pressure, and getting enough good sleep is crucial for having sufficient energy. You mentioned that your roommate is being emotionally abusive towards you because of this situation. I think this really affects your mood, and you must be feeling really uncomfortable as well. However, this is not a valid reason for you to think of yourself as troublesome. There are some things we can't control. In such situations, finding a solution is the best way forward. OP, don't feel inferior or troubled just because your roommate treats you differently. When your mom scolds you for being stupid and having a lot of issues, and you feel like you've spent a lot of money and connections but still can't pass, try to think from a different perspective. Instead of thinking that you have too many issues, think about why your mom has such thoughts. It's not that you have too many problems, but rather you rely on your parents for financial support. And when they provide the money but don't see the expected return, they vent their dissatisfaction through blaming you. It's common to have a second or even third attempt at the postgraduate entrance exam. OP, don't burden yourself too much. If you have a strong belief, then strive to take the exam and believe that you will succeed. Here are some suggestions for you: Maintain a positive mindset. If you have decided to take the exam again and will still need financial support from your parents during this period, considering your current situation, you will likely hear more hurtful words from them in the coming year. At this time, having a good mindset is crucial. Believe in yourself, learn to ignore their words, stay firm in your beliefs, and don't question yourself because of others' opinions. Find suitable ways to relieve stress. During your second attempt, there will still be pressure from your studies and your parents. You need to learn how to release that pressure in a suitable way. Start each day of your preparation with a positive and optimistic mindset. Maintain sufficient sleep. During your preparation period, getting enough sleep is crucial. It will give you better energy for studying and also help you alleviate stress. The above is just my personal opinion, I hope it can help you. Best wishes~

Hello, thank you for the invitation. Based on your description, it seems like you always need to satisfy others completely in whatever you do. You want to satisfy your mom and your roommate as well. You need to understand that it is impossible to make everyone 100% satisfied because there are factors beyond your control, such as moving while sleeping, something you cannot control once you are asleep. Some of the troubles caused to your mom, like spending money or owing someone a favor, are responsibilities that your mom should naturally bear. If your mom complains, it is her own problem and something she needs to work on. Well, that's all I have to say. Good luck!

Hello, based on the information you provided, I hope my answer can be helpful to you. First of all, as a mother, you have your own life and there should be boundaries. Parents should no longer dominate your life, nor should they control or restrict you. A mother's complaints about life stem from a sense of powerlessness and the need for external validation. She desires to have allies in confronting your father, but this is actually childish behavior, indicating a failure to grow up. No matter how you handle the situation, there will always be aspects that are not appropriate. Helping your mother attack your father or helping your father attack your mother will not solve the root cause. In the end, they are a married couple, and you are their daughter... Do not be anyone's garbage bin. Emotions accumulate little by little, so learn to say no. It is not a bad thing to reject certain things. You also have your own life!

Looking back on your life, have you ever fought for yourself? - From the beginning, when I saw your question, I voluntarily assumed that you are a person with low self-esteem. When I saw you say, "Isn't failure normal?" a possibly impolite idiom came to my mind, which is "a salted fish." - I saw three things in total: 1. Taking the postgraduate exam. 2. Getting along with your mother. 3. Getting along with your roommate. I don't know if you chose to take the postgraduate exam because it is your goal, or because you don't know what to do after graduation, so you decide to take it. There are thousands of people taking the postgraduate exam every year. How many people understand why they want to take it? Is it for a degree or to enrich their lives? If you have decided to take the postgraduate exam, you should study hard, choose a suitable major, and work hard. This will require you to devote your time, energy, and money, just like a certain investment with certainty. You invest your time, energy, and money, and as long as you study well, you will definitely succeed in the end. Everyone who takes the postgraduate exam is the same. It's not an easy thing in itself. If it were simple, there wouldn't be so many people working so hard to take the exam. This is not something that can be left to chance. - As for your parents, they have all gone through hardships. Those who have suffered know that the process is not important, only the result is the truth. Without results, all the hardships you have endured are in vain. Regarding your parents, if you want to prove yourself, then just show them the results. If you can't show results, are they not allowed to say anything? So, have you ever proved yourself to your parents? Have you proved that you are not a troublesome person? - Getting along with a roommate is determined by personality. True good friends, even if you pick your feet in front of them, they won't really dislike you. You and your roommate are just not truly good friends. You are being extremely careful, but the more careful you are, the easier it is to make mistakes. In fact, you don't have to. People who don't get along in life don't have to accommodate each other. You have paid the same tuition and accommodation fees to live together, why should you have to accommodate others? Because you are too easy to bully? Change your mindset, if you can't get along with them, just move somewhere else, instead of thinking that you are a person who causes trouble to others. Have you ever thought from a different perspective? Isn't it troublesome to be a person who can be easily awakened by being turned over while sleeping? What did you do? Why do you always think it's your fault? - Others' opinions are their own attitudes, don't deny yourself. If you want to take the postgraduate exam, work hard; if you don't want to, find a job. As for your parents, they just like to nag, don't take it to heart, just show them the results. If you can't show results, then prepare to be nagged all the time. As for others, just follow the rules and laws, focus on your own things, no matter what others do, it's just them causing trouble for you. Fight for yourself. - Lastly, keep up the good work. (From my personal perspective, these things are not considered troublesome, they fall under the normal range. When you truly encounter troubles, that's when it's troublesome.) Above all, I hope this is helpful.

question: In terms of salary, the promise made initially was not fulfilled. Should I be honest with my boss about it?
description: Should we be completely open and honest? Originally, the basic salary was said to be 2500, but now it's 2000. And we are expected to accept a 7-day emotional recovery without any compensation, which was not mentioned when we were recruited.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. In a world with rules, following those rules may make relationships simpler. From your description, it can be seen that you are dissatisfied with your boss not providing the promised compensation, but you are hesitant about whether to communicate with the boss to obtain what you deserve. You can first ask the experienced employees about their situations, whether they have experienced similar things, and what suggestions they have. Also, inquire about the boss's usual demeanor and style of work – whether they are amiable or authoritative, whether they separate personal matters from business matters, or if they value personal relationships. These pieces of information are for reference only. If you communicate rashly, it may make the boss unhappy. After consulting people who can help you, make your decision and consider the pros and cons of speaking up. Expressing your thoughts might make the boss pay attention to the issue and compensate you as you deserve, appreciating your spirit of raising concerns. On the other hand, the boss may feel disappointed with your behavior or find excuses to maintain the current arrangements. Even if they give you the proper compensation, they might still have some resentment, thinking that you challenged their authority. Not expressing yourself may cause feelings of injustice and make you feel that your efforts are not valued. It feels frustrating when you have something important to say but remain silent. Over time, this incident might affect your work attitude, causing negligence or negative evaluations of the boss's qualities and character. Fighting for what you deserve is respecting the efforts you have made. Don't be afraid of problems arising, nor fear the consequences of your actions. As long as your behavior is reasonable, there is nothing that should be compromised. You can communicate with your boss in a tactful manner, even if not face to face. Sending an email or using other forms of contact can help make your feelings known. Relationships between bosses and employees, as well as companies and staff, and even our relationship with ourselves, might be seen differently. But what is important is to realize our own value and strive for the rewards we deserve. Business and work may prioritize efficiency more, so it may be easier to adapt by being decisive and straightforward. So be brave and fight for your interests. Best wishes.

question: I am the first, my girlfriend told me it was her first time, but it wasn't?
description: Everything is my first time. I also wanted my partner to be my first time. I asked her, and she said besides her first kiss with someone else, everything else is her first time. Then we shared a room and I was very nervous. After we started, I realized she wasn't very tight and of course there was no bleeding. I believed everything she said, including that she was a virgin. But then she didn't seem to feel any pain. I thought I couldn't satisfy her, so I searched a lot of information. I thought if she was a virgin, there should be no bleeding or pain the first time. It left a shadow on me. I kept researching and wondered if it was because I was not good enough. Later, I gathered the courage to ask her, and she admitted that she was not a virgin. I asked her how many boyfriends she had before, and she said she had one before me. I asked how many times they had sex, and she said they did it twice, both times in one night. After that, she realized the guy was a scumbag, so they didn't do it anymore. I still believe her, but I always feel like it's too loose and she doesn't seem to be in pain. They only did it twice, so how is this possible? Sometimes, I lose my erection halfway because I feel like she's not in pain, and it has had a big impact on me. She seems like an experienced person, while I know nothing. She naturally takes the initiative. What should I do? I don't want to leave her.

answers.answer_text: Hello on Sunday night! Your concern, in a certain perspective, is completely understandable because, as you said, you have reserved every first for the person you care most about. Let's try to have a calm conversation and see if we can find some inspiration and help. While understanding ourselves, let me ask you, are we also equally persistent in other aspects? Everyone cares about different things, right? What may be extremely important to one person may not be so important to another person. Can you accept this? Of course, from the entire process of communication with your girlfriend, she was ultimately able to be honest with you, wasn't she? Now, the most crucial thing might be two aspects. On one hand, it is about how to accept the current reality. Going back to what was mentioned earlier, you linked the first time and love together, and your girlfriend also cannot say that she doesn't care about this matter at all. If she didn't care about your relationship at all, why would she finally be honest? Perhaps she is afraid that telling the truth will harm this relationship. Wouldn't that mean that the scumbag wins? On the other hand, it is the issue of your psychological barrier. We need to untangle this problem ourselves. This concern still needs to be further discussed with your girlfriend. As for the specifics, it depends on the development of the relationship and the level of acceptance from both parties. Looking at it from a different perspective, if you really break up with your current girlfriend because of this, won't the next girlfriend also face the same issue of you not being the first? I hope this provides some inspiration and help. The world and I love you!

I really have trauma now, and I care a lot about the first time. Don't tell me I don't love her enough or anything like that. If you end up being with her in the future and you haven't experienced what it's like, will you regret it? I am quite disciplined with myself, so I keep everything for the first time, and I have given her all my firsts, only to realize that she has deceived me. And every night, I can think of all these things, I feel very isolated. I'm very conflicted, I am a traditional person, I keep everything for the first time, and it's not unreasonable to expect others to do the same for the first time. The problem is that she lied to me, and it's not just once.

question: Just started working and have poor coping skills. What should I do?
description: Just starting work, the job is relatively easy. I am a teacher and also a homeroom teacher. I have 12 regular classes per week, plus morning and evening self-study, which may add up to about 20 classes. However, I feel very anxious and under a lot of pressure. When I lie down, I think about what I haven't finished yet. Having to give public lessons and mentorship classes also annoys me. Even during my student days, I often felt this way. Just a small thing would make me feel anxious and irritated. I would procrastinate by playing games until I had no choice but to face it. How can I relieve my stress? My partner says that my work is already considered easy, but when I come home, I still feel lethargic and exhausted. I feel like I have poor coping skills. Just managing the class, preparing lessons, being observed by other teachers, and grading papers, all these things make me feel like I can't hold on any longer.

answers.answer_text: Being able to feel the desire to do a good job and at the same time make oneself relaxed and happy. When feeling overwhelmed and anxious, you can ask the part that feels annoyed and anxious (scan your body up and down) and try to communicate with it: What do you want? Instead of resisting and fighting against it. Try accepting this situation first. You can also seek help from professionals to adjust this pattern, which may be more effective.

question: Female, if you both like and feel a bit repulsed by someone, does that mean there is a psychological problem?
description: I am a girl, and I went on a date with my boyfriend today. When we held hands, my mind went blank and I felt extremely happy~ He even secretly bought me a flower. But there is always a moment when I have a psychological rejection towards him, even feeling troublesome and wanting to end this relationship. I am deeply touched when he treats me well, it's so contradictory... I truly feel that there's something wrong with my mental state.

answers.answer_text: Female, having both love and some aversion towards someone, does it indicate psychological issues? Hello, OP, first of all, I want to express my understanding and sympathy for your situation, and I want to give you a big hug and let you feel the warmth of the world. I'm glad that you have encountered a boy who treats you well; after all, meeting someone is fate, and staying together is even more difficult, so it needs to be cherished. So, the problem you need to solve now is that you feel there is something wrong with your mind. You mentioned that there are moments when you feel a sense of aversion towards him, feeling troublesome, and wanting to end such a relationship. But at the same time, you are moved by his kindness. This is a conflicting mindset. I am not very clear about what specific moments you feel aversion towards him. Is it something you cannot accept, something you cannot tolerate, or some improper behavior of his? Regardless of the situation, if you really want to continue with him, it's best to communicate with him clearly about your aversion towards him. Maybe after speaking out, you can work together to improve. In fact, there will be many problems in a relationship. However, if you accumulate these small problems without resolving them, they will eventually build up to a certain extent and burst out as a great force. That kind of energy is resentment and the greatest sadness towards your relationship. Therefore, if this boy himself does not have any particularly unlikable aspects, what you need to do is to communicate with him. Why do you feel aversion towards his behavior? Or maybe he did something wrong, or maybe it's just a point in your own psychology that you can't overcome. Only by speaking it out and letting him and everyone help you, can your relationship have a chance to continue. Lingering, conflicting mindset is very detrimental to this relationship. When you hesitate and vacillate, wanting to move forward but also stepping back, such a awkward relationship is the most difficult to continue. My suggestion is that you can talk to your friends about what specific point you feel aversion towards and see if they can help you. Or you can read books and find answers yourself. If you think your psychological problem is very serious, you can consult with a psychologist. You can also divert your attention to something else to give yourself temporary relief. Wishing you happiness and joy, OP.

Hello! I understand your feelings very well. Sending you a hug. I'm not quite sure about your ages, your identities, or how long you have known each other, but if this is your first time in a romantic relationship, it is normal to have conflicting emotions like this. Liking someone because they touched you, because they bought you a flower, these actions make you feel acknowledged and cared for. Just now, I wanted to remind you that being touched doesn't necessarily mean love, there is a difference between the two. Many people can make you feel touched, but it doesn't mean that the person who touches you loves you. Feeling hesitant is also normal because when you first enter an intimate relationship, people tend to have some insecurities. And these insecurities are related to whether you know him well enough and trust him. How well do you think you know him? Do you trust him a lot? Speaking in a long term sense, do you believe he can care for you forever and give you a good future? Maybe you can't confidently answer these questions yet, so you might feel hesitant and resistant. In this situation, I think you can continue to spend time with him and get to know each other more. Best wishes.

#Want to end this relationship#You don't really want to develop this first relationship. So there will always be a moment when you have a psychological aversion to him, even feeling troublesome. Once the other person behaves unsatisfactorily, you will feel a sense of rejection. This is not what your inner self truly needs. It is normal to feel moved when someone treats you well. But this is not a reason to continue being together and cannot convince yourself to be with him. I also want to ask, is the development of this relationship something you actively want or is it passive?

Everyone will have a moment of disgust towards someone, even their best friend or closest parents. But that's just human nature. We ourselves are the same. It's all about whether your liking for them can make you tolerate or overlook their imperfections and whether the happiness they bring you outweighs the troubles. If the answer is yes to both, then this relationship is beneficial for you.

question: Does it mean that if you don't have a formal job, it's not considered work?
description: It feels like my parents really want me to have a stable job. Isn't the purpose of working to earn money?

answers.answer_text: Hugging the title owner because there is not much information in your description, so I speculate, is it because you have your own way of making money, but this method is different from the work understood by your parents, so they don’t understand it very well, or they hope that you can find a more stable job? Actually, your idea is correct. Work is to make money, and your parents' idea is also correct because in their era, only a stable job could mean a stable income. Maybe in this information-rich internet era, there are many jobs that don't require working from nine to five every day, but can still bring considerable income. But from your parents' perspective, it is difficult for them to understand this. At the same time, they will worry that your job is not stable and there may be no income at any time, so they will say such things. I would like to invite you to switch perspectives and try to see the care behind their nagging. Then tell them, "I know you are suggesting this because you are worried about my future stability." I can also feel your concern. At the same time, explain to them the nature of the work you are currently doing that can make money, and let them know that you have grown up. Although it is different from their understanding of a "stable" job, you can still have income to take care of your life.

Come, let me give you a hug. Your parents hope for a formal job because they want you to have a stable future. In their generation, there were only two types of jobs: ones within the system and ones outside the system. Most people worked within the system, meaning they had jobs in government institutions or state-run factories and enterprises, which were considered secure positions. In other words, they had a guaranteed income and the backing of their workplace throughout their entire life. However, with the reform of state-owned enterprises, many people lost their jobs. But they still believe that working for the government is considered having a job. I have a brother-in-law who is 20 years older than me. He works for a government department and has arranged for his son, daughter-in-law, daughter, son-in-law, nephew, and others to become civil servants. He has given them a clear path: go to university, return to their hometown, and take the civil service examination. And that's exactly what they did. State civil servants and state-owned enterprises have been undergoing reforms. But there's no doubt that being a civil servant is still considered a secure position among the older generation. The number of people taking the national civil service exam every year is proof of that. However, it's understandable if some people don't like working within the system. After all, nowadays, it seems that even a secure position is not so secure anymore. We can understand the concerns and worries of our parents. If you can prove that even if you don't have what they consider a formal job, you can still live a good life – for example, if you have a high income and a happy family – you may be able to ease some of their concerns. So, the key is for you to be strong enough on your own. You can have a good conversation with your parents, discussing your career plans and your future. The main goal is to reassure them. The world and I love you.

Hello, OP, give you a hug. I understand your confusion and your parents' concerns. In the era when your parents were living, having a stable, formal job was considered the best and safest thing in society, a "iron rice bowl" that you didn't have to worry about. In that era, there were many social classes, and formal employment in an organization was the highest class. In a society with instability and unrest, many people lost their jobs, but having a formal job in an organization provided relatively stronger resistance to risk. It meant experiencing fewer storms and not going hungry. However, with the development of the times and changes in the economic situation, there has been a huge transformation and change in the economic structure. The ways to make money have become more diverse, and people's sources of income have become increasingly varied. Therefore, you are seeing the new changes, opportunities, and prospects that the new era has brought. With the pandemic this year, the economic situation has also changed, and some industries are not as good as before, facing closures. So, considering the current situation this year, having a job within the system is relatively stable. For parents who have been worrying about us for more than 20 years, it's already too tiring and difficult. If there is a formal job within the system, they won't have to worry about our future lives anymore, and they won't have to worry about us not finding a job and not being able to support ourselves in the future. Their sense of security in their old age will also be greatly improved. You can discuss your thoughts with your parents and communicate with them. For example, talk about your plans, whether you have found a suitable and enjoyable job, the future prospects of that job, and how you envision your future. Most importantly, what your parents need is for you to be able to support yourself and not worry about your livelihood and future. Best wishes to you.

question: Easily influenced by others, thinking of some negative things, how to handle coworker relationships?
description: Emotions are easily influenced by others. Even though I am busy myself, I still have to help others when they ask for it, and they may think that I am free and relaxed. When I realized this, I felt very disappointed with this colleague. How should I handle my relationship with such a colleague?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, interpersonal boundaries, colleagues, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hug hug to you~ You are a kind, pure, and adorable girl who is diligent, proactive, and hardworking in your work. Your behavior and attitude in the workplace remind me of the "Post-it Note Girl" from the drama "Nothing But Thirty" - Zhong Xiaoqin. She is always being "bossed around" by others, even if she is busy and overwhelmed herself, she will rush to help others. She takes on the daily tasks of almost all her colleagues, which delays her own work. She never refuses others and always responds to their requests. Until Zhong Xiaoyang encourages her to "learn to say no". "A person who doesn't know how to refuse. Everything you accept is cheap! (This little brother makes sense!)" When she bravely says "no! It's not on my way, you can do it yourself" to her colleague, although her tone may be a bit unnatural, she has already taken the first step. You are easily influenced by others, afraid of being disliked by your colleagues, afraid of losing value if you don't do things, and afraid of conflicts with others. Have you learned from the drama that after Zhong Xiaoqin refused, her colleagues did not resent her? Others will not force you to do things for them without compensation. You don't have to worry about the impact on your relationship with them. "You are very busy, but your colleagues think you are free, so they ask you for help, and you feel disappointed with them." Have you made it clear to them that you are very busy? Tell them that you are not free at all. If you cannot directly tell them (still worried about the relationship with your colleagues), you can also gently and simply tell them how much work you still have. Learning to say no requires practice and exercise multiple times. If your colleagues know that you are busy but still ask you for help, you must explicitly tell them that you are busy. In this way, how much "face" does it take for them to ask you to do things? You need to tell yourself in your heart, "helping you is goodwill, not helping you is just doing my job." How can you refuse others nicely? In terms of dealing with relationships, are you disappointed in your colleagues because you feel that they intentionally give you things to do while they slack off? Or is it because your colleagues did not realize that you are very busy and you feel disappointed? Of course, your colleague may be a bit selfish, lazy, or have difficulty putting themselves in others' shoes, but it is also possible that they are genuinely anxious and have not noticed that you are busy or they are accustomed to seeking help. They ask for your help because you are outstanding and always willing to assist others, so you are the first person they think of when they need help. If you were not busy yourself, you would feel the sense of being needed, right? Now, how to handle your relationship with that colleague depends on your relationship with them and the interests involved in the workplace, and so on. Some suggestions: "If I have time, I would help you with this and that, but currently, I have something important... that is not yet completed, and I have to finish it immediately. I'm sorry, I can't help you right now. If you want to..., you can do..." (Just saying, not doing). Wishing you a successful career! The world and I love you.
