question: My mother has recently been diagnosed with malignancy. How can we alleviate her preoperative anxiety?
description: Last week, my mother was diagnosed with breast cancer. Faced with this fact, she has been unwilling to accept it and has been extremely pessimistic. She has not yet undergone further diagnosis and treatment. She constantly talks about how long she has left to live and resists treatment. She is an emotionally uncontrollable and pessimistic person who always thinks that bad things will turn worse. She has an attachment personality and tendencies toward depression. Since she needs to undergo preoperative examinations to confirm the stage of the tumor and treatment plan, she has insomnia every night. She always gets up to walk and cry alone around four or five in the morning. I am really worried about her condition, but because I am pregnant, I cannot accompany her all night. Our family members are trying to convince her to have proactive treatment, but she resists it in her heart and has no hope of recovery. I am really concerned. How can we alleviate her preoperative anxiety?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, family members' health.

answers.answer_text: Hello: You are asking on behalf of your mother. If you want your mother's emotional state to be good, it may be necessary for her to seek psychological counseling herself. It may be helpful for her surgery and also relieve her physical condition. But if you are inquiring, it may be necessary to adjust your own emotions. It is understandable that you are overly worried about your mother, but you are carrying a baby after all, and too much stress can also affect the baby's development. Analyzing and understanding the problem: 1. Last week, your mother was diagnosed with breast cancer. Faced with this fact, she has been unwilling to accept it and is extremely pessimistic. She has not yet undergone further diagnosis and treatment, and constantly talks about how she may not live long. Moreover, she is resistant to treatment and constantly wants to give up. She is a person with uncontrollable emotions and pessimistic outlook. ("Tumors" and the location of tumor growth, from the perspective of "psychological healing of psychosomatic diseases," also have reasons. If tumors occur in the breasts, uterus, and other parts of women, it means that the patient has been attacking these parts inwardly for a long time. This leads to poor blood circulation, toxins unable to be eliminated properly, and weakened immune system. Your mother has been negative and pessimistic for a long time, unable to release the pressure outside, all directed towards herself, which in psychology is called "internal projection," causing long-term pathological changes. Therefore, it is important for her to open up her mood. She should be allowed to release her stress, complain, or even scold others, as long as it helps her.) 2. Bad things always come to mind, with an attachment personality and a tendency towards depression. Because she needs to undergo preoperative examinations to confirm the stage of the tumor and the treatment plan, she has insomnia every night and always gets up to walk and cry between four and five in the morning. You are really worried about her state. (Hmm, she has stress at the moment, but the pressure she has put on herself has increased many times over. Since she has an attachment personality, let the people she depends on accompany her more, understand her, and temporarily alleviate some of her stress. If she can receive psychological counseling and constantly release her emotions, it is absolutely possible to cure a benign tumor.) 3. However, because you are pregnant, you cannot stay with her all night. The family is trying to persuade her to actively seek treatment, but she resists treatment and has a hopeless attitude towards recovery, which makes you really worried. How can her preoperative anxiety be relieved? (She must have some psychological barriers. If that barrier is not broken, she will get hung up on certain things. As a daughter, it is understandable that you feel sorry for your mother. But now you need to take care of yourself because you are about to become a mother too. Your other family members will take good care of your mother. It is best to have a dedicated person to take care of her, as her current state is prone to extremes.) Conclusion: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope your mother recovers physically and mentally soon! If you have any confusion, please feel free to message me!

Hello, Yiye, you are a very filial daughter. Your mother's illness not only worries about her physical health but also her mental health, which is a very correct approach. Mental health must focus on the person being treated. If only the people around are anxious, the therapist cannot do much, and the ultimate effect can be imagined. Your mother's condition needs the efforts of people around her, and more importantly, it needs to stimulate her positivity. 1. As for you: you mentioned that she is a person who cannot control her emotions and is pessimistic. When something bad happens, she always thinks of worse situations. She has an attachment personality and tends to be depressed. Your description shows that you have a considerable knowledge of psychology and have made certain judgments about your mother. I suggest you take a look at the knowledge of rehabilitation psychology, which is about the psychological process of patients. It will help you better understand your mother's psychology. You are also pregnant, so while worrying about your mother, do not neglect your own mental health. 2. As for family members: when other relatives and friends visit your mother, they can say more positive and encouraging words and share similar experiences from other provinces. This can help alleviate your mother's current fear and worry about the disease. You, your father, and other relatives and friends are your mother's solid support at the moment. You need to make her believe that she is not alone in facing the disease. 3. As for doctors: after all, doctors have a better understanding of the condition, and ordinary people who do not understand relevant knowledge are more likely to have unfounded thoughts. After detailed communication with the doctor, it is necessary to abandon unnecessary emotions, recognize reality, and have the courage and rationality to face the disease. Although your mother is emotional, you can communicate with her that being emotional is not beneficial to treatment. Believe in doctors, believe in science, cooperate well with treatment, and it is the right thing to do now. Instead of thinking about what can't be done, think about what can be done, actively cooperate with the doctor, and maintain a pleasant mood, which is beneficial to recovery. 4. As for your mother herself: you can first mobilize the above-mentioned forces to work on her thoughts. Having the support of family members and the treatment of doctors will greatly alleviate her anxious mentality. You can also directly take her for psychological counseling. Face-to-face communication is more conducive for the therapist to understand her fears and solve the problem better. I wish your mother a speedy recovery, and I wish you a healthy baby. Best wishes!

【Encourage Her to Do Her Best】Dear friend: Good afternoon! I saw your message and felt regretful. You must love your mother very much because I can sense your anxiety and worry, fearing that she might give up on herself. It's natural for family members to worry when something happens to their loved ones. Let's try to understand why your mother is having such a negative reaction. Generally, people who are facing death or suffering from a terminal illness go through several stages of expression, and your mother is currently in the first stage, "denial". On one hand, it's because of the fear of death, and on the other hand, death came too suddenly. Her negative attitude stems from her fear of having hope because the bigger the hope, the bigger the disappointment. She is afraid of failing in her treatment and doesn't know how to face it. It's alright, I think we can still help her manage her emotions. 【First】Release the fear and let her acknowledge it so that the fear in her heart can be released. Who wouldn't be afraid in the face of death? Because we all have a reverence for death. Let her understand that if she fears death, then she must truly love life! 【Second】Apologize to Regret it is regrettable to discover a malignant tumor, as it deviates from our pursuit of good health. We can express our regrets by saying, "I'm sorry, please forgive me." 【Third】Appreciate the Effort Let your mother know that we have already tried every possible way to live a healthy life. Every day, we take care of our bodies, make an effort to go to bed and wake up early, and strive for the best health. We have done our best! Let her appreciate herself! Appreciate her body, which has already done its best! 【Fourth】Let Her Be the Best Version of Herself Nobody can guarantee that everything will be fine after being cured, or that health will definitely be restored. But if we don't seek treatment, we won't be healthy for sure. Treatment is the opportunity that God has given us. It is also the chance for us to make one last effort for our own lives. We cannot expect everything to go perfectly or fight against fate, but at least we have tried. Even if we ultimately fail and have to leave, we can say to ourselves, "I have done my best, no regrets!" When we are sick, having family members accompany and support us is already providing confidence and strength to the patient! I wish you and your family well! Your friend: Audrey.

Hello~ I completely understand your feelings and give you a hug~ Overwhelming worries about surgery can cause insomnia and hormonal imbalances, ultimately leading to weakened immune system, disrupted menstrual cycles, and even surgery rescheduling. Such "worries" are not worth it. It is normal to feel slight anxiety due to lack of understanding or even fear of surgery. I suggest you talk more with your mom and encourage her to communicate with the doctor. Through proper communication with the doctor, any doubts about the surgery can be answered correctly, instead of relying on hearsay and scaring oneself. You can talk to your mom from a more positive perspective, telling her about the ideal situation and help her imagine the scene of a smooth recovery after the surgery, which may alleviate her anxiety. Furthermore, with the advancing medical technology, it is highly possible for the surgery to go smoothly. Engaging in appropriate exercise, taking baths, and other relaxing activities can also help maintain a pleasant mood, which can be beneficial for the surgery. In summary, her anxiety mostly stems from a lack of understanding and excessive pessimism. You can guide her more and provide her with more hope and a sense of security. It is also possible to tell some well-intentioned lies to help her feel more at ease~ Wishing the surgery to go smoothly and your aunt's speedy recovery~

Hello, I'm sorry to hear this unfortunate news. My suggestion to you is to find some time to calm down and have a heartfelt conversation with your mother. Regarding her condition, most patients experience preoperative anxiety due to the following reasons: 1. Worrying about the low success rate of the surgery and being afraid of the consequences of surgical failure. 2. Not wanting to burden the family with excessive financial pressure, thinking that they are already old or the illness is too complicated. 3. Feeling hopeless about their own future, carrying a heavy psychological burden, and enduring both physical and mental pain caused by the illness, which makes it difficult for them to persevere and wish for a quick relief. Based on your conversation with your mother, you can understand her situation. First, if you want to persuade your mother to undergo the surgery, you must give her hope for a successful outcome. Even if the surgery does not go smoothly, the result won't be particularly disastrous. You must offer her hope to make her willing to undergo the surgery. Second, since you mentioned that your mother tends to be depressed and may sometimes find life dull, if possible, I suggest you take her out more often to relax and experience the pleasures of life. Let her have hope and tell her that she can enjoy many wonderful things in life. At the same time, respect her decision and ask about her preferences in life. Use her interests to encourage her. You can give examples to illustrate that many people live happily after successful surgeries. You can also share some inspiring stories of battling illness, such as a patient who once had a terminal illness. The doctors said there was no cure, but he persisted in exercising every day, running regularly. Eventually, a miracle happened, and he recovered from his illness. This story even made it to the news. You can also use personal examples around you to tell her that illness is not so scary and that the recovery from illness is somewhat related to one's mindset. The patient I mentioned earlier had a positive attitude, forgot about having a terminal illness, exercised diligently every day, and ultimately achieved a successful recovery. Lastly, you must spend more time with her, making her feel that she is not a burden and reducing her sense of guilt. I hope my suggestions will be helpful to you.

Hello! 1⃣️1. You are pregnant and need to take care of yourself. 2. Understand your concerns about your mother. 3. You understand psychology well and understand your mother's personality and usual emotions. 2⃣️ Life is unpredictable, happiness and pain coexist, but people prefer to accept happiness and avoid pain, which is normal. 3⃣️ Body relaxation method: 1. Place your hand on your chest and say, "I'm sorry, I didn't take good care of you." 2. "Please forgive me for not taking good care of you." 3. "Thank you for reminding me in this way." 4. "I love you, and from now on, I will be with you." 4⃣️ Rebuilding thought process: 1. The psychological reason for breast problems is refusing to provide oneself with nourishment. Putting others above oneself, excessive care for others, excessive protection of others, and excessive tolerance of others. 2. New mindset: I am important, I have value, I now nourish myself with love and joy, I allow others to be free and become the person they want to be, we are all safe and free. I wish your mother a speedy recovery.

Hello, OP, nice to meet you. I feel really sorry for your current situation and I want to give you a big hug. It must have been a huge shock for you when your mother was diagnosed with a malignant tumor, but you quickly adjusted and sought help. I have to commend you for being so strong. Now, let's analyze the situation based on what I read and I hope you can follow my train of thought. The situation started when your mother went to the hospital and was diagnosed with a malignant tumor, although it was not mentioned whether it is acute. At the same time, you mentioned that you are pregnant, so congratulations on becoming a mother soon. I hope you won't worry too much because your family is comforting you and we will all try to help you find solutions. Based on this, I have a few suggestions, although the actual situation may be different from what I imagine. You can consider them. 1. Your mother is in a pessimistic mood, and it is not uncommon for emotions to affect the progression of the disease. Therefore, we need to give her a goal or hope. For example, you and her grandchild are important to her, so increase her desire to undergo surgery. 2. Explain the specific steps to her and let her understand the process of the surgery to alleviate the scary image of a malignant tumor just by hearing the words. 3. I hope you take good care of yourself. You can't become ill due to worries, which would make your mother feel worse. Finally, I wish your mother a successful surgery. I hope you can always keep smiling in the future.

question: It's easy to overthink and become impulsive, ignoring advice. How to manage emotions effectively?
description: Every time I argue with my girlfriend, I easily become overwhelmed and start thinking of the worst possible outcome. Even when she tries to pacify me, I can't calm down and it often leads to even bigger problems. I can't seem to control my emotions.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Recognizing that one's emotions can be managed and controlled is important, and deliberately redirecting them through various methods can help develop the habit of managing emotions over time. From your description, it's evident that you feel frustrated and anxious because you struggle to control your emotions during conflicts with your girlfriend. When conflicts arise, try to calm yourself down first. You can try taking deep breaths or counting numbers in your mind or out loud, turning any hurtful things you want to say into numerical descriptions. Learn to express your thoughts. Are you able to express your thoughts during arguments? How do you feel? What triggers your anger? What words or actions from the other person hurt you? How does she handle your emotions to help you calm down quickly? Release and express all your emotions instead of staying silent or acting impulsively. Learn to think rationally and analyze events, whether in romantic relationships or other interpersonal relationships. Perhaps you love and care about your girlfriend a lot, which is why you invest your emotions and mental energy in her. You can definitely express how important she is to you, which might be the underlying reason behind your anger. We don't get angry with strangers because we have no emotional connection with them. When you're contemplating and worrying about something, try to look at it from multiple angles. If there's a worst-case scenario, what would the best outcome be? How can you achieve a good result? When your girlfriend comforts you, it shows that she cares and is concerned about you. After you've calmed down, do you express gratitude and appreciation for her actions? One reason you might be easily swept away by emotions is because you struggle to view the problem comprehensively. When you and your girlfriend argue, focus on resolving the issue and conflict, not attacking your girlfriend. I believe that with your own efforts and attempts, you will gradually become more emotionally stable. Best wishes.

Hello, OP, it's great that you can recognize the issue of your poor emotional management skills and actively seek help here. It is essential to be aware of your problems and actively seek ways to solve them in order to ultimately find a solution. You mentioned that you tend to get worked up and imagine the worst possible outcomes when you argue with your girlfriend. Have there been any times when you were able to control your emotions to some extent? Were there moments when you felt relatively less irritable? What were you doing or thinking during those times? Can you try to record the process of your arguments with your girlfriend? Think about why you were arguing, was it because of something one of you said? What specific words triggered your emotional outburst? How did you respond to your girlfriend? And how did you gradually calm down in the end? Try to record the entire process in as much detail as possible. Take your time, observe in your future life, and then, when you are calm, analyze the process. It will be helpful for you. These are just some suggestions, and I hope they can be of assistance to you. Good luck!

question: Working for ten years, day in and day out, without passion, always thinking about changing the way of life?
description: Recently, I've been constantly thinking about resigning and quitting this job that I've been doing for ten years. It feels monotonous and I want to try out many different things and change my way of life. However, I am conflicted because if I don't work, I have responsibilities to take care of my elderly parents and young children, and I'm afraid I won't be able to handle it.

answers.answer_text: Hello! It seems that you are experiencing career burnout and want to try a different lifestyle, but you are pressured by the demands of life and fear losing a stable income, so you are in a constant state of dilemma. Perhaps in front of you, there are two paths: maintain your current job or resign and try a new job. If you choose to maintain your current job, you may need to rediscover what this job has brought you in the past ten years and understand the reasons why you are now tired of it. If it's just because it's monotonous, you can try to make it less monotonous. For example, you can request to transfer to a different position within the same company or strive for promotion to a higher level of management. You can also use your spare time at work to learn new knowledge in your areas of interest and see if you can apply it to your job, bringing about a new change in your accustomed work mode. Another option is to give yourself a longer vacation to relax and rejuvenate. Perhaps after a period of adjustment, returning to your job will bring a different feeling. If you choose to resign, you mentioned that you need to take care of your family and the pressure of life, so quitting impulsively is not advisable. If you really want to resign, it is recommended to plan ahead, think about what kind of job you want to do, and start sending out resumes or attending interviews. Once a new job is confirmed, you can resign without delay. If you want to have a more flexible type of work, such as starting a business or freelancing, it is also important to conduct research in advance, consider the current economic situation, determine what you like, and make a decision after comprehensive consideration. Of course, the best job is one that combines your interests, as this can bring higher enthusiasm and make you happier. You may want to communicate with yourself more, find your strengths and characteristics, and determine what kind of things make you feel happy. If these happy things can also bring you income, then believe in yourself, and nothing is impossible. I hope my answer can provide you with some inspiration.

Hello friend, I hope the following answers can be helpful to you. It's great and takes a lot of courage to have the idea of trying many things and wanting to change your lifestyle after working monotonously for ten years! Thumbs up to you! If you are not married yet, I would encourage you to go for it without a second thought. Now, with the responsibility of having older parents and young children, it is indeed a big responsibility and not a "impulsive" stage. Therefore, my suggestion is: 1. Make a plan before making a change. After working for ten years, you must have rich life experience. Spend a weekend seriously listing the things you want to do next, ranking them in order of importance. Find something you want to do and are good at, and see if there is a possibility of turning it into work or even a career. If possible, make a plan on how to achieve it. There's no need to rush to switch right away. If the goal is a bit far away, then take it step by step closer to it. 2. Spend some time every day on something you enjoy, even if it's just 30 minutes. The current job may be monotonous, but don't forget the time we live in. Outside of work, have you made good use of your time? Sometimes, changing your lifestyle doesn't necessarily have to be done by immediately changing your job. You can start with the small things in daily life. Find what you enjoy doing in point 1, or something that makes you feel meaningful when doing it, and spend at least 30 minutes on it every day. Stick to it, and you will find that life starts to change, and work will be more motivated! Because that thing fills you with energy! 3. Regarding dealing with the confusion of life, I recommend these two books: (1) "The Cafe at the End of the World": a self-help book in psychology, especially suitable for reading when feeling lost in life. After I finished reading it, I strongly recommend that everyone who wants to learn time management should read this book first. For me, it is the theoretical guide to time management. (2) "Visualizing Time": This book not only helps us understand ourselves but also provides a step-by-step method of time allocation. It is equivalent to practical guidance for time management. At the same time, it is very helpful for us to write down plans for our lives. I hope the above will be helpful to you.

question: 20-year-old college male, feeling upset from enduring grievances, feeling annoyed.
description: There was an event that needed to borrow a classroom. I went to borrow the classroom through the proper procedures. However, when the event was about to start today, someone suddenly told me that the classroom was also borrowed by members of the Student Union. Moreover, I heard that there were some problems with the equipment in that classroom, so I switched to another classroom. Then the people in our association said that I was being timid. I mentioned that the equipment was faulty, but they kept trying to prove themselves right. They kept talking about this matter in our group chat of several department heads. Although the event was not ultimately affected, I found it annoying. I think the event is most important, so why not focus on organizing the event first and deal with other matters later, instead of constantly proving oneself in the large group.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, when you needed to borrow a classroom for an event, you encountered some grievances. For certain reasons, you swallowed those grievances, so now you're feeling very agitated and want to vent. The reason why you feel agitated is because you clearly did your job well. You borrowed a classroom and when you heard that there were issues with the equipment, you went to exchange it for another classroom. However, that classroom was already borrowed by someone from the student union. This is an objective factor that cannot be changed. As a result, the members of your association not only didn't recognize your efforts, but also said that you were weak. I believe at this time you must feel really disappointed. Clearly, you are wholeheartedly dedicated to the association, but your efforts are not being acknowledged. You're inexplicably upset. However, it is right for you to choose not to argue with them. Because sometimes there is no point arguing about something, it's better to avoid getting red-faced and straining relationships than arguing about it. Not all people are reasonable and can communicate seriously. When faced with those who cannot be communicated with, the best way is to stay silent. But our emotions also need an outlet. When you feel wronged, you can confide in your trusted family and friends, or engage in some sports activities to release your emotions. Don't keep it all inside. As long as we appropriately release our emotions, our mood will quickly improve. Best wishes~.

question: How do I deal with my mom who always compares me to others and annoys me?
description: I hate my mother. She always compares me with others, which makes me feel very uncomfortable. I don't know why I have this tendency to compare myself with others. It's all my fault. The most common thing she says is, "Look at how well other people are doing in their studies!" At home, no matter what I do, it is never enough for her. I feel rebellious. I have had thoughts of suicide since I was 11 years old. Sometimes, I even think about killing her first and then committing suicide. But she will always show care for me the next day. I don't know what to do.
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, family control.

answers.answer_text: First, my mom has no choice, this kind of blood relationship cannot be changed. Secondly, it is possible but very difficult to change my mom's mentality of comparing with others and her way of talking, unless she realizes the harm it brings to me and actively changes. Then, can the feeling caused by my mom's comparing be changed? This depends entirely on me. As long as I am willing and find a method, it can be changed. Push back and ask her in the same way, can you be like that parent who accompanies their child with homework every day and takes them to the science museum or zoo every month? Whether she listens or not is up to her, maybe she doesn't care whether I listen or not, she just satisfies her own cravings. If I listen and find that other classmates are indeed better than me in certain aspects, I can ask them for advice and learn from them, to make up for my weaknesses, and then tell my mom, I also think that person is better than me, and I am already planning to ask them for advice, so don't worry!... There are definitely more ways for me to improve my mood and feelings. Maybe right now, my thoughts are filled with "she's so annoying, why is she so annoying!" and I don't have the spare energy to think about how to improve. Relax with the activities I enjoy, relieve the irritability and make some space in my mind. I will definitely find the most suitable way to deal with my mom and make myself better!

question: As a high school student, I always have a feeling of not knowing who I am. What should I do?
description: High school student. Over the past five years, I haven't been very sure about who I really am. I am good at observing the connection between people's emotions, facial expressions, and experiences. And I always put myself into the shoes of a movie character or someone else. My words, expressions, and even walking style would match those of the person I am imitating. I turn every action of the person I imitate into my own behavioral standard. I have no idea how I should be. And when I can't achieve it, I start to self-doubt and feel worthless. I feel like I can become anyone, except for myself. I can't feel my own existence. This makes me very painful because it's like acting for a lifetime, never being "real". My emotions are also unpredictable, one moment I can laugh heartily, and the next moment I can be silent and quiet like a statue. These are genuine emotions, without any deliberate intention. Others describe me as "sometimes like an old man, sometimes like a little kid." I am confused about myself, I have studied others thoroughly but know nothing about myself.

answers.answer_text: Congratulations, you have the question of who you are, which shows that you have begun the process of separating from others. When we were very young, we were in a symbiotic state with our mothers. Infants would feel that their mother is me and I am my mother, we are one person. They wouldn't have the concept of imitation. You become aware of yourself imitating when you realize that you and the person you are imitating are independent individuals. The existence of "me" is what allows me to imitate others. Your confusion may lie in whether there should be a very clear boundary between me and others, whether I should be very different from others, and whether I need to be unique in order to distinguish myself from others and see my own existence. Indeed, everyone has their own characteristics, but it cannot be denied that we also have some commonalities as humans. Self does not necessarily mean being unique. Even if you make the same choices as others, it is still your choice. Ninety percent of what a person experiences in their lives is learned, and imitation is a very common learning behavior. Your experiences, personality, and environment are all different from his, so it is difficult for you to replicate his path. The person you are imitating must have something that you desire, perhaps his achievements, his relationships with others, or certain qualities he possesses. You desire these things, but you are not sure how he acquired them or what conditions are needed. So you use the methods you are capable of to approach your goal and imitate his every word and action. You can become aware of what you envy in him, and if you were to become that person, what would make you happiest? What conditions are needed to achieve this, and what conditions does he have that I do not? Under the current conditions I have, are there other ways to achieve my goals? Growth is a marathon-like, long-term process, not a fixed standard. In different stages, you will find that the self also changes, and you will not always stay at a certain point in the river of time. Your body will change, your environment will change, your needs will also change. Personality is only a relatively stable thing, and in fact, there are countless subtle differences. I am thirty years old this year, and I am still exploring internally and still searching for the answer to who I am. I believe that even when I am eighty years old, I will still be moving forward on this path until the day my life ends. Although we may not have the same experiences and feelings, we are all on the path of searching for ourselves. I hope this solitary lamp can provide you with some company.

question: Why does looking at certain issues from an emotional perspective make the original small problems seem bigger?
description: Why does viewing certain issues through an emotional lens make small problems seem bigger? For example, someone else's words may be triggering, but if we approach it rationally, we should remain calm. However, if we view it emotionally, we may make incorrect judgments.
keywords: Growth, development patterns, work and study, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. It's nice to virtually meet you. I think emotions and rationality are like a pair of enemies who can never get along. When you want to lose weight but feel extremely hungry, rationality comes forward and says, "Don't eat, you are already overweight. If you want to slim down, you should resist." But emotions tell you, "It's okay to eat a little, you should be kind to yourself, being overweight is not a big problem." So, the question is, do you eat or not? Both rationality and emotions have their benefits and drawbacks, it mainly depends on how we balance the relationship between them. For example, when encountering touching events, if you are too rational, it can make others perceive you as cold-hearted. So, how do we handle the relationship between emotions and rationality well? 1) Use your brain to think through problems instead of being impulsive. Rationality and emotions are often just one thought apart. When you need self-restraint, rationality should step forward. If you need to express your emotions, then it should be more emotional. Neither overreact nor be impulsive. If you encounter a serious matter that requires a rational approach, and you overlook this and only focus on your own emotions, it won't work. Thus, rationality and emotions should be used in the appropriate context to truly become a rational person. 2) Whether overly rational or overly emotional, don't blame yourself. Some people may wonder why they are always so rational/emotional. They feel their behavior is abnormal, leading to a self-disgust. However, this is completely unnecessary. If you are a rational person, it doesn't mean you are cold-hearted; to some extent, you are more composed and calm than others. If you are an emotional person, it simply means you are more sensitive, more prone to catching feelings, and it is not a big deal. Therefore, change is possible, but try to accept and understand the problems that exist within your emotions. 3) In the balance between rationality and emotions, what suits you best is the ideal choice. For example, if you are a male but constantly live in an emotional state, easily shedding tears in a sentimental manner, it can easily lead others to form strange opinions or give you strange looks. So, be true to yourself and act according to your own characteristics. Acting against your own nature is the strangest behavior. What suits you best is the most ideal choice, whether it's emotions or rationality.

Hello, indeed, the existence of the same problem itself is neutral. If we look at it from different perspectives and react differently, the results will also be different. However, is the difference completely distinguished by "sensibility" and "rationality"? Let's take the example provided by the questioner as an example. When we hear words from others that may stimulate ourselves, if we approach it from a sensibility perspective, we may make "wrong judgments". The so-called wrong judgment from sensibility may refer to making decisions influenced by emotions, exhibiting aggressive feedback, or venting in other ways. However, can we really "remain calm" by approaching it "rationally"? Perhaps by eliminating emotional disturbances and conducting a logical analysis of pros and cons completely, it is indeed a good strategy to solve many problems. However, in practical terms, human emotions cannot simply disappear. What appears to be calm on the surface is actually a form of control and suppression of emotions. It may help solve problems at times, but it can also lead to uncontrolled emotional outbursts due to the accumulation of emotions. Furthermore, does "sensibility" really only bring problems? Just as everything has two sides, in some moments it may cause "indecisiveness" and "emotional interference", but in other moments, it can also bring you important "empathy". The positive and pleasant emotions can also enhance the efficiency of handling events. Even fear and anxiety are signals that our inner selves generate to express certain information, which helps us better understand our needs and feelings. "Rationality" and "sensibility" are both results of a long evolution of living beings, and their essence is like two forces. How to properly utilize them, how to be aware of them in different situations, and how to balance them all determine the final outcome of events :).

question: 16-year-old girl, feels very confused about her future and lacks motivation for no reason.
description: Starting from my first year of high school, I have been lacking motivation and feeling very insecure. I want to be recognized, so I have been forcing myself to study. As a result, my grades have improved significantly, and I always rank in the top ten of my class. However, now during the summer break, I feel extremely exhausted. I have been trying to find motivation, but as soon as I find it, it disappears. I don't know what I should do. The temporary motivation I have found now is that I can achieve my dreams. I took a test for the IELTS, and I passed the first three sections. However, my writing score is very low, only 5. I didn't meet the requirement, so I bought past test papers and some study materials and have been using them for about a month. I have a daily schedule. Today, I completely lost motivation. I can't focus at all, and I keep telling myself that I need to get into that university so I can study the subject I have always wanted. But deep down, I have no hope or motivation. I really want to cry and don't know what to do...
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, the meaning of life

answers.answer_text: Hello! After reading your description, I can understand your sense of confusion at this stage. Sometimes, the motivation to study may only be a temporary trigger that allows us to concentrate and work hard for a while, but cannot be sustained in the long run. I can tell that you are a very capable person, you understand your current situation, and you want to find a way to solve the current dilemma. So I have two small suggestions for you to consider. Relax appropriately: Sometimes we can't focus on something because our brain is already exhausted and is producing strong resistance. So at this time, we can relax appropriately and adjust our state before we engage in studying. You can write your goals in a place where you can always see them, such as sticking them in front of your study desk or the first page of a book you read every day. In short, it should be a place where you can frequently see it, reminding yourself constantly.

Due to information asymmetry, I feel that something is not quite right overall. I can sense your anxiety, but let's first sort out this matter. To put it simply, we can summarize the situation as follows: the effectiveness of your efforts in studying did not meet your goals. From this perspective, we can discuss two points: 1. study plan; 2. goals. Let's start with the study plan. I see that you have made a schedule, which shows your dedication. However, when you mentioned a lack of motivation, usually it means "I don't know why I should do this." So, I'm wondering if the reason for your lack of motivation is that you genuinely feel the study plan is unable to help you achieve your goals. Can we consider changing the plan? I don't know about your current study plan, and I have never paid much attention to the IELTS exam, so what I'm suggesting may not be accurate. But I'm thinking, can you look for other people's experiences? Or ask someone around you who has done well in the IELTS for advice based on your specific questions? If your financial situation allows, you could even consider paying for assistance in resolving your current issues. I believe you may feel that looking back on what you learned in elementary and middle school, the difficulty level appears much simpler compared to when you first studied it. This is because your knowledge level is now higher, so perhaps applying higher-level knowledge to help with your current situation is a worthwhile consideration. Now, regarding your goals, from your description, it seems like you only want to study that specific major at that particular school. Here, I'd like to ask whether this major is only offered at that school. Are there other schools that offer this major, but the difference in prestige between schools is not significant? Alternatively, could you consider pursuing this major at that school at the graduate level? I'm not entirely sure if this goal is an absolute must for you. If it isn't, perhaps we can set some intermediate goals before reaching this ultimate goal. Additionally, if possible, I'd like to hear why you chose this specific major at this specific school as your goal. I'd like to hear you talk about what makes this major interesting.

Hello, I understand how you feel because I also didn't have any goals or motivation in high school, so I would often set goals for myself. Goals can be simple, from small to big, from day to week, month, or even year. For example, if I have weaknesses in a certain subject, my goal would be to improve my score in the next exam. It doesn't have to be some grand and abstract ideal. Or it could be how many questions I plan to solve or what I'll review today, those can also be small goals. Additionally, learning is about finding a balance between work and leisure. While studying, it's important to relax and not put too much pressure on yourself. If you don't have goals, you may lack motivation to study and it could be because you're putting too much pressure on yourself and your mind can't handle it. Now it's summer vacation, so you can take some time to relax. Go for a walk and listen to some soothing music. Maybe when you relax and really listen to yourself, you'll know what you truly want.

question: Should I pretend to be a loving couple with my child's father in my life now?
description: We have been together for 13 years despite our incompatible personalities, often arguing over trivial matters. Our child has been living in this discordant environment since kindergarten. Now, at 14 years old, I always try, consciously or unconsciously, to create a harmonious atmosphere when talking to his father, in order to provide him with a harmonious environment. I wonder if this is appropriate? Also, I feel that my son harbors resentment towards his father. What should I do? Lastly, is it still possible to arrange training for my son's attention skills after I recover from my illness?
keywords: Marriage, perception of marriage, marriage management.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's not easy to live with someone you don't love for 13 years. First, the pretending harmony between parents. Children are very sensitive to the relationship between adults. Although you and your father pretend to be harmonious, the child can still feel it. And when the child realizes that you are pretending, they will be very hurt and feel that their parents are not genuine. Children tend to imitate adult behaviors and emotional expressions. If you disguise your true emotions, the child will also disguise their true emotions in life, pretending to be happy and ignoring their own emotions and needs. In China, many couples who don't love each other stay together for the sake of their children. This easily makes children feel fearful of marriage and it also makes children feel guilty for making their parents unhappy. It may be the best choice for two people who don't love each other to separate. However, before separating, it is important to explain to the child that the parents' choice is to seek happiness, and it is not the child's fault, and the love for the child will not diminish after the separation. The second issue is that the child hates the father. The child's hatred for the father is closely related to the mother's attitude towards the father and the father's temperament. If one spouse is in a disadvantaged position, the child will definitely help the disadvantaged one. When the child hates the father, the mother can communicate with the child to understand why they hate and what aspects they hate. The mother can praise the father's positive qualities in front of the child. The father also needs to communicate with the child more and understand and accompany the child, establishing a good parent-child relationship. The third issue is the child's attention training. The child is now in their teens, I don't know how their attention is, but it's better to start training attention earlier. You can inquire at specialized institutions. I hope my answer is helpful to you.

question: Now that I have advanced to high school ahead of time, I have no interest and no confidence in studying. What should I do?
description: High school entrance exams are coming up, and all my classmates around me are getting into prestigious schools, while I didn't get accepted into any top universities. I had hoped to do well in high school and have a chance, but after seeing the admission standards for this year's college entrance exams, it seems very unlikely. If my grades in physics and chemistry in ninth grade were good, I might have a chance at getting into a prestigious university. I have taken extra classes outside of school, but I haven't seen any improvement and my confidence is decreasing. Now that I am starting high school, my classmates are studying an average of 4-5 subjects a day. I'm only able to study 3 subjects a day, and I easily fall asleep in class. I want to do well in school, but I have no interest in studying. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello. I am fortunate to give you some advice. From your description, I can feel that you are a person who is "striving for progress" and has "high self-demands". Facing the "failure" in this mid-term exam, your "confidence" has been greatly impacted, especially when your classmates have excellent grades, which further leads to self-doubt. However, what I want to say is that your past is already behind you, and reviewing and reflecting on it will help you move forward. Next, let's analyze your thoughts one by one. The actual sequence of your first two paragraphs is: "poor performance in physics and chemistry", "ineffective tutoring", "not getting into a better college", and "worrying about whether you can achieve your university goals". In the path of learning, everyone's performance at different stages depends on "personal experiences", "environment", "level of acceptance", "areas of expertise", and so on. As for your current situation, first of all, "the mid-term exam" does not represent the outcome of high school grades, let alone the outcome of the college entrance exam, because every group of students and their respective teachers are different. It is not completely negated that there might be "sparks" when different teachers and students "come together". As a new high school student, facing the possible predictions of high school, we need to accept it while being anxious. Because you did your best in middle school, but the level of acceptance at that time was not maximized, this is our inner recognition of our "learning ability", so we should be rational and objective in the face of mid-term exam scores. In addition, high school life has not started yet, and everything is unknown and "full of expectations". If we only focus on the future based on the current "high school entrance situation", I think we need to consider: the teaching experience of your high school head teacher and subject teachers, as schools hope to cultivate more talents as time goes on. Finally, let's analyze the content of your last paragraph - studying high school content in advance but finding low acceptance. This problem you mentioned can be viewed in conjunction with what we mentioned earlier about the "ineffectiveness of tutoring in middle school". Based on this situation, we need to adjust: whether the current study methods are suitable for you? (In other words, under the current methods, how do you feel each time you study? What are your thoughts?) After the mid-term exam, your learning ability and other aspects will be different from before. Therefore, at this moment, think about how you can improve your results in the current learning situation, what can you do better? Regarding high school life, and even college life, what plans do you have? After considering these aspects, I believe you will have a new understanding of yourself. Do your best based on what you can achieve. Best of luck.

Thank you for inviting me to answer! As the saying goes, interest is the best teacher. If you are not interested in studying, you won't have the internal motivation to actively learn, and your learning will not be good, which will naturally lead to a lack of confidence in yourself. I don't know if you are not interested in studying itself or just not interested in materialism. Many people actually have a tendency to favor certain subjects, but in order to maintain their grades, they have to study even if they don't want to. Studying against your will is definitely a painful thing. Some students even have aversions to learning, but they persist for their future. If you have a tendency to favor certain subjects, it's easy, as long as you don't give up, you can make up for it. Here, I recommend a less painful method for you: establish a relationship with the textbooks and teachers of these subjects, and gradually develop an interest in them. We all know that if you like a teacher, you will enjoy his/her classes. If you like a subject, you don't need a teacher, you can understand it yourself. Therefore, building a relationship with them will yield twice the result with half the effort. But how do you build a relationship with textbooks and teachers? You just need to have a dialogue with them in your mind, sincerely think about their merits, and express your liking for them. If you have any feelings of rejection, express them in your mind and ask the textbooks and teachers to be understanding. This interaction is something you do in your own mind, with the purpose of changing your perception and emotional attitude towards them. If you are not interested in studying itself, you can introspect your psychology and see what is blocking it. If you are not aiming for top universities because you didn't enter a prestigious high school, then you can still try, just because others can't get in doesn't mean you have no hope. If you don't even try, then you definitely have no hope. The past doesn't represent the present, and the school doesn't define you. You have a desire to do well and you have just entered high school, which is a fresh start. Just because others study 4 or 5 subjects doesn't necessarily mean they study better than you studying 3 subjects. Dozing off in class doesn't mean you didn't absorb anything, you might have subconsciously absorbed some things. If you have a regular routine and develop an interest in learning, your energy will improve, you won't fall asleep in class, and things will be even better. Also, you can consider whether the lack of interest and lack of confidence only manifest in your studies? If you have a dull character and lack self-confidence, you need to solve the problem from the root. Good luck!

Hey, how's it going? Actually, I once had a similar experience to what you're going through, but it was in high school. Let me share my perspective on the issue you mentioned about "lack of interest." It's natural to have difficulty being interested in things we don't feel competent in. Just like in high school, I wasn't very good at math, so I never really had much interest in it. But don't get discouraged, because interests can be cultivated, right? And I believe you value your academic performance, which is a crucial attitude that determines your level of self-awareness and persistence in learning. Firstly, it's important to lower your expectations of yourself and allow yourself to relax a bit when studying. Only a relatively relaxed sponge can absorb water, and only a humble and open person can learn new knowledge. By lowering your expectations, you will find it easier to make progress. After studying a course, a specific topic, or a unit, you can assess your learning achievements by doing timed exercises or practice exams. This gradually develops your sense of control over your learning - a sense of mastery. During this "hands-on" process, you can set specific small goals in advance, such as aiming for at least a 90% on this basic exam or striving for a perfect score on this unit test... As you gradually achieve these goals and make progress bit by bit, you will start to feel proud of yourself - a sense of accomplishment. When you have a humble attitude, a sense of control over your learning, and a sense of achievement from your progress, I believe you will gradually overcome this predicament!

Hug you! Just finished the high school entrance exam, the pressure must be very high, right? Especially during the pandemic, it may be difficult to focus on work or study. Plus, the classmates around you are especially diligent and outstanding, so your anxiety is not unfounded. However, don't push yourself too hard because of others. Everyone has their own pace, and your classmates may just be suitable for high-intensity studying, but that's not necessarily the case for you. You should know that the real competition is with yourself. Don't pay too much attention to other people's grades. The best achievement is to make progress compared to your previous self. As for schools, if you get into a prestigious high school, the resources may be slightly better, but it's not absolute. Even prestigious schools have underachieving students, and conversely, even non-prestigious schools can have excellent students. It's up to the individual to determine their performance, and the most important thing is that you want to learn. Since you want to do well, it is very likely that you can. At this critical moment, don't rush. Achievements lead to interest, so set one or two small goals for yourself every day, not too many, just suitable for you; then, when you complete these small goals, check them off. Keep doing this every day, and after a week, you will see your achievements and gain more confidence to continue persevering. Over time, you will cultivate an interest in learning. In addition, it's important to build a solid foundation for studying. This summer vacation, it's better to consolidate your knowledge from middle school, fill in any gaps, rather than rushing to preview high school textbooks. I myself didn't clarify some things in middle school and just moved on to high school knowledge, so I was always falling behind and lost interest. But later, I followed the teacher and studied the basics diligently, and I made great progress. When you don't feel like studying, take a break, clear your mind, think about what you want and how to achieve it. Once you figure it out, continue studying hard. I believe that with your abilities, as long as you steadily and consistently work during the three years of high school, you will definitely make great progress and achieve admission to an ideal university! I hope my answer is helpful to you. Wish you academic progress!

question: What can be done about anxiety and fear? How can one repair the pain caused by a broken relationship?
description: I am a female, a sophomore in college. When I was in elementary and middle school, I always had good friends to play with, and I had a trusting relationship with others and spoke freely. However, in my second year of high school, I had a falling out with my best friend for some reasons, which resulted in me not having any friends in the class. It was a painful and difficult period for me. This experience has made me cautious and anxious in interpersonal relationships. I am afraid to trust others and easily feel anxious and frightened, fearing to be hurt again. I also tend to have extreme thoughts and easily become pessimistic, looking at things from a negative perspective. The relationships with the friends I met in college are also very superficial, and I don't have any close friends. I often doubt myself and feel a sense of pity, constantly worrying about being left out and rejected by others. How can I heal the psychological pain caused by the rupture in past interpersonal relationships? How can I rebuild my confidence and sense of security in interpersonal relationships?
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, friends, roommates, classmates

answers.answer_text: OP, sometimes we need to show our sincerity first in order to gain the trust of others. Trust is something that is given mutually. If we are cautious with others, they will notice. I feel really sorry for you. On one hand, you want to trust others and make genuine friends, but on the other hand, you are scared to step out of your comfort zone. Even within your comfort zone, you still feel anxious about people and things outside. You can try to adjust your irrational thoughts and see things from a different perspective. Everyone has their own inherent way of thinking, and you tend to approach things from a pessimistic and negative angle. This is your characteristic, but if this way of thinking makes you feel restricted and uncomfortable, then it's time to change. When you start closing yourself off, your vision will also become narrow. It’s good to focus on yourself, but when you feel helpless, doubt your self-worth, and deny your abilities and qualities, neglecting your strengths and advantages, these are all thoughts that need to be changed. When we feel that we are not worthy of attention and care, the world around us seems to have a malicious intent. But when we have a positive mindset, even in the face of difficulties, we are still willing to actively resolve and challenge them, the world and the people around us may not seem so bad. Give yourself some courage to socialize and maintain relationships, and sincerely express your value and needs in relationships. By giving your care and love to others, you will receive care and support in return. Friendships are built up gradually. Those friendships that start off superficial can become very close through serious interaction, sharing, and supporting each other through difficult times. On the other hand, even friendships that started off strong can fade due to negligence from one party or both. Both you and the relationships you are involved in are in a process of change. The past pain has already cost you a lot, and if you don't cherish the people around you who can potentially become friends, you will also miss out on a period of time in each other's lives. Approach the people you want to get to know with your sincerity and feelings, be a little brave, because you are capable of making friends, you just sealed off your heart due to some negative experiences. If you want to break free from that and rebuild intimacy in your relationships, don't be afraid of rejection, don't be afraid of being ignored. Solve problems when they arise, don't run away like you did when you were a child, because some people, once lost, will be lost forever. So, solve the problems that occur between each other, instead of thinking about giving up on each other and sacrificing the relationship. I believe that you can have friends who value you greatly, and likewise, the other person cares about and cherishes you. Best wishes.

question: 29-year-old woman, pessimistic, feels that life has no meaning.
description: Pessimistic and sensitive, growing up feeling neglected, with a sense of meaninglessness in life, unable to feel inner happiness, this has been a state that is quite distressing from childhood to adulthood. How can one make themselves a little happier in life?
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods, panic helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Pessimism - having a crisis consciousness, particularly easy to see negative possibilities. Sensitivity - being cautious in observing changes in people or things, often overlooked. Growing up - valuing relationships more, caring about being seen, wanting to do better. A label is not just how others see us, but also the meaning we give it. If the meaning we give it is unhappy, then we will be unhappy. So why not call these three qualities advantages? Furthermore, I personally do not think happiness equals to being content. It's fine to not be happy, as many negative emotions actually remind us of things we need to do and express. Regret, disappointment, sadness, etc., without exception, remind us to pay attention or care. Embrace your negative emotions, and you will become "happy," because it is not just sensory pleasure, but also the fulfillment and tranquility of body, mind, and soul.

Hello, it's nice to communicate with you here. First of all, I would like to give you a virtual hug. Your upbringing may have caused some of the problems you are experiencing now. This is something that we may not want to see. Now that you have grown up, we can make up for this deficiency in our own way. There are many beautiful things in our world, so don't give up on finding happiness. Perhaps at the moment you have not found some suitable ways to find things you enjoy. Maybe thinking more positively will make you more optimistic. If happiness does not come to you, you should take the initiative to find it! There are many ways to find happiness. For example, take up a hobby. When you truly have a hobby, you may find happiness and consolation from it. A long-term hobby is like a good friend, it inspires, encourages, and gives you peace of mind. For example, engage in appropriate exercise. Exercise stimulates the release of dopamine in our bodies, making us feel more joyful. While exercising, we rarely think about other things and focus solely on the activity, leaving behind worldly worries and unhappiness. Another example is to find like-minded friends. Like-minded friends make us happy, and in our interactions with them, we feel comfortable. They can also be a great support system when we have troubles. Perhaps it would be helpful for you to meet with a reliable therapist. Even something as simple as a chat, I believe, can have a positive impact. I hope my response is helpful to you. Best wishes!

question: Due to the pandemic, I have been staying at home for 7 months. How can I better control my emotions?
description: Due to the epidemic situation, I have been staying at home for seven months. At the beginning, my mood was quite good, but now I can't control my emotions. I can't help but get angry and feel regretful after each outburst. I also frequently experience low mood, overthinking, and I don't want to continue like this anymore.
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, healing methods, and emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: It is normal to have difficulty controlling emotions during the pandemic. Try not to feel stressed or anxious about it. The outbreak has affected various aspects of our lives, such as work and studies, making it difficult to face the situation as we normally would. Feeling dissatisfied with the current situation and fearful about the future can cause psychological distress, leading to overthinking and imagining negative scenarios. So, what can be done in such situations? First, it's important to adjust your mindset and maintain a regular daily routine, including regular meals and sleep. Try to avoid getting too bothered or overwhelmed by daily challenges to prevent emotional breakdowns. Secondly, set realistic goals and make a schedule for both leisure and work/study activities. Prioritize creating a relaxed and enjoyable state for yourself, while also taking care of your mental well-being. Lastly, find calming activities such as mindfulness meditation or reading books to help quiet your mind. As the pandemic gradually subsides and stabilizes, your emotions will also improve.

Staying at home for a long time can become boring, and one's mood may become low or unstable, which is a normal phenomenon. Now that the domestic epidemic is gradually stabilizing and non-epidemic areas are already able to go out, if the local situation is not serious, you can go for a walk after taking sufficient precautions. It is beneficial for relieving tension (wear a mask, wash hands when returning home, disinfect clothes with alcohol outside the house, and avoid contact with public facilities when going out, as all of these can serve as protective measures). If you still cannot go out due to the epidemic, you can exercise indoors, such as yoga or meditation, to calm yourself. You can try to contact friends through video or other means to adjust to the monotonous life. Pay attention to positive news about the domestic epidemic and gradually return to a relaxed mindset. Congratulations.

question: 20-year-old girl, I feel like I have two personalities, one within and one in my actions.
description: I am actually a person with a bad temper. I don't like to be treated unfairly and I don't enjoy doing things that make me unhappy. Recently, I had a big fight with my boyfriend, to the point where I thought I would never see him again. But we made up in the end. I usually don't want to contact him, it's always him who initiates contact now. Honestly, I don't really want to be with him anymore, but I still maintain peace on the surface. I feel that my inner self and my actions are gradually separating, like sometimes I can be very gentle, but the next second I can be irritable over insignificant matters.

answers.answer_text: Hello, our behavior is often an external manifestation of our brain's thinking process. As mentioned, one moment we can be gentle, and the next moment we can become irritable. One's stable temperament may be influenced by the care received in childhood. If a mother's nurturing was adequate, then one's mood may be relatively calm. However, if there were significant fluctuations, it may be related to inadequate maternal care in early childhood. It is important to follow your own inner thoughts. When your behavior conflicts with what you think, it can cause inner discomfort. If you experience significant changes in emotions, you can try training yourself through techniques such as meditation. Best wishes.

question: After graduating from high school, I dyed my hair and was criticized for being wasteful and not working hard.
description: After graduating from high school, I just wanted to dye my hair. At first, my parents didn't agree, but I kept talking about it for several days, so they finally allowed me to do it. My mother even watched me as I did it. However, when I came back after getting my hair dyed, she started scolding me, saying that I wasted money during the holidays and didn't do any work. I feel helpless.
keywords: Family, family relationships, and parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner, nice to meet you. I'm not sure what your relationship with your parents is like, but there must be some issues in your communication with them. Wanting to dye your hair is something that can be understood. I think the conflict between you and your parents is not about whether or not you can dye your hair, but about whether you have done anything meaningful during this break. They say you don't work and spend money recklessly during your break. You should first reflect on whether this is true or not. Did you plan something for yourself during this break? Graduating from high school is like a signal, a feeling of growing up and being able to do what we want. We are eager to break free, unleash ourselves, and embrace the new life. But at the same time, it also means that we need to start taking responsibility for our own future. Besides studying, we cannot just focus on eating, drinking, and having fun. During this break, you need to have a plan for your future and do something meaningful, such as learning a new skill, participating in charity activities, or finding an internship to experience life. Therefore, your parents are expressing their concern for you in an inappropriate way. Try to communicate with them properly and pay attention to the way and methods of communication. I recommend a book on communication called "Nonviolent Communication". Both you and your parents can read it.

After reading your narrative, what I want to ask is, if next time you want to do something you want to do, but your family is unwilling, and you don't have the economic means, how do you avoid being scolded again after doing it? Focusing only on the issue of dyeing your hair doesn't make much sense. For things like this, you can also reflect on your parents' behavior and reactions. Since you are asking such questions on this psychological platform, you can also consider this issue from the perspective of psychology. If you are interested in psychology, you can think about it from the psychoanalytic perspective, or from the behavioral cognitive perspective, or even from the hypnosis perspective, how to influence your parents' behavior. Isn't this an interesting thing? The problem ultimately needs to be solved, at least it should develop in the direction you want. Therefore, the solution is what's important. Along this line of thinking, let's conduct an experiment with your parents.

When you use the money you earn yourself to take care of your hair, the results are different, especially in times of economic difficulties. At this age, you also start to pay attention to beauty and hope to become more beautiful. However, currently, you haven't reached an agreement with your family about it, and it took a few days of persuasion before you could go and dye your hair. From this passage, you can feel their desire for money, so they don't want you to spend money recklessly. They may also not understand your desire to dye your hair. When you don't have the ability and rely on others' abilities to accomplish something, your words will carry less weight. In the future, I hope to provide for myself with my own abilities.

Child, good afternoon! The desire for beauty is inherent in everyone, including young people like you. However, there seems to be a discrepancy in your parents' understanding of this matter, causing you to feel very upset. Here, let me give you a hug. The circumstances of being born into a certain family and having certain parents are not something we can choose. We must try to accept and embrace this situation. Based on this foundation, we should continuously learn, grow, broaden our knowledge, and expand our horizons. Perhaps, from the beginning of your communication with your parents, there has been a lack of understanding between each other. The last sentence, "I feel helpless," seems to imply that there has been poor communication, whether it is their lack of support for your desire to dye your hair or your insistence on doing so. You yearn for independence and individuality, and the desire for beauty is understandable. If you can combine these desires with the ability to put yourself in your parents' shoes, perhaps it would be even better. I'm not sure if you can agree with this idea. After all, you are still in the stage of studying and need financial support from your parents. During the communication process, try to focus on expressing your own feelings rather than blaming the other party, then maybe the outcome will be more desirable. You can refer to the article I wrote about nonviolent communication on my homepage for more information on this point. In addition, economic factors can indeed diminish people's happiness. By taking on more household chores and speaking kind words, you can provide significant support to your parents both in practical actions and emotionally. Remember, the world and I love you!

question: Feeling like my emotions are being suppressed by something?
description: In life, emotions are suppressed. When feeling sad, it doesn't hurt as much as it used to. Any emotional feelings don't feel as distinct as they used to be.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, psychological assessment

answers.answer_text: Do you feel like your emotions are being suppressed? Humans have seven emotions: joy, anger, sadness, happiness, sorrow, fear, and surprise. A vibrant and lively life cannot be separated from sensual and beautiful emotional experiences. If one detaches from vivid sensibility and rich emotions, their life may become stiff and devoid of color. Humans are born with pure sensations. The objective world and external events evoke various feelings within a person, corresponding to different emotional experiences. Emotions need to be expressed. When the external environment doesn't allow for expression, or when individuals are reluctant to acknowledge external events, their true feelings may be repressed or isolated. At this point, it seems like individuals have lost their emotions. Okay, gradually become aware and try to express yourself, perhaps through counseling and personal growth. We are always on the journey of learning and growing. I wish you can find your true inner self soon. In that moment, you may experience a heartwarming delight. The world loves you.

question: Recently, many women have been having immoral thoughts and are feeling very distressed.
description: Recently, I have been experiencing a clear sense of immorality when being around women, regardless of age, and it has been causing me great distress.

answers.answer_text: Hello, based on your description, it seems that there is a strong conflict between "fantasy" and "morality" within you. Speaking of "fantasy," in fact, any fantasy is not wrong. Each of us has had some bad, forbidden, and immoral dark, pornographic, and violent fantasies, some of which are expressed through writing, movies, etc. These are all fine. The important thing is "not acting upon them." If fantasies are turned into actions, it can lead to legal consequences and punishments. Therefore, as far as fantasies are concerned, any fantasies are our freedom, as long as we don't act upon them, there is nothing wrong. Why then do we feel such conflict within ourselves? Sigmund Freud proposed the famous personality structure of the "superego, ego, and id." The superego is the internalized norms and moral standards we learn. We gradually learn what we should do, should not do, what we should think, and what we should not think through society and culture. So, when we autonomously generate some "immoral" thoughts, we receive punishment and criticism from the superego to suppress these immoral ideas, causing inner conflict and struggle. As long as we limit fantasies to our minds and do not turn them into actions, we can tell ourselves that there is nothing wrong with them and thereby alleviate the inner conflict. Wishing you all the best!

question: What is expressive writing? How can one avoid feeling more down while writing about their emotions?
description: I used to have a habit of writing because it was my only way of venting. However, I always felt worse the more I wrote, unlike what my friends said about feeling relaxed after writing. Why is it like this? What is a more effective way of writing?

answers.answer_text: Here is a writing therapy checklist that can help you see your emotions. Look at your list as if you were a stranger, and you will find where the problems lie. Just complaining won't let us see ourselves. Write with sincerity, reflect with awakening, and seek answers with wisdom. Life organization and writing therapy checklist goals: understanding yourself, knowing yourself, discovering yourself, accepting yourself, and loving yourself. Self-portrait + self-evaluation: 1. Introduce yourself. 2. What are your interests and hobbies? How do you use them? 3. How do you make a living? Is it the way you like? If not, how do you feel and what are your plans? 4. What kind of people do you dislike? Have you been hurt by this dislike? 7. Describe your views on money, values, life, and the world. 8. What kind of life do you long for? 9. Who or what makes you confident? What does confidence feel like? 10. Who or what makes you feel inferior? What is the biggest trauma caused by this inferiority? 11. Describe your current life situation, occupation, and self-growth. 12. What are you currently most satisfied and dissatisfied with yourself? Why? 13. Have you ever bought yourself any gifts? Do you ever feel like you have clothes in your wardrobe that you never wear? 16. Where do you feel relatively safe? At home or at work? 17. Do you prefer to be alone or in a group? 18.
