Each person's inner thoughts are different, and nobody has the ability to see into others' thoughts. We can only rely on guesswork, sometimes leading to misunderstandings. Therefore, it is better to calmly communicate our inner thoughts with our parents, and discuss gradually what we can do and how to do it. Make a good plan for yourself and let your parents see your abilities. Not being motivated is not a way to retaliate against our parents but rather a lack of responsibility towards our own life. You can make a plan based on your abilities and strengths, and then implement it. This is being responsible for yourself and also shows your parents that they can let go of you. This is a proactive approach. I hope my answer is helpful to you. Best wishes!

You spend money recklessly to retaliate against your parents' lack of understanding and disobedience towards you. You have your own needs deep inside, hoping that your parents can fulfill them. However, their reactions and behavior are unable to satisfy you or make you feel content. This has led to resentment and negative emotions within you. But you don't know how to release these emotions, so you end up spending money impulsively as a way to attack your parents and vent your emotions. You believe that this reckless spending will hurt your parents, make them angry, and make them realize the consequences of not understanding and obeying you. However, since your parents are unaware of your impulsive spending, this act of defiance has no impact on them and is therefore meaningless. This has left you feeling confused, as your negative emotions have not been relieved. Is that correct? Reckless spending can indeed release some negative emotions. If your financial situation allows, it is not a problem to spend some money to make yourself feel comfortable. However, if you are using this behavior as a way to protest and retaliate against your parents, it also depends on whether your parents have a special focus on money and control, and whether spending money can truly stimulate and affect them. If you seek to retaliate against your parents through this behavior but cannot achieve the desired effect, this behavior loses its meaning and intensifies your feelings of resentment and frustration. When communication with your parents becomes difficult and they are unable to understand and support you, it does not feel good, and you may even feel very angry. Perhaps your parents have their own reasons, or perhaps your previous communication was not sufficient enough to understand each other. To solve the problem and relieve the emotions, communication is still necessary. You can continue to communicate with your parents, explain the reasons behind your requests, why they should listen to you, and the reasons for your parents' opposition. Are both sides' reasons reasonable? Is there room for negotiation and coordination? Are there other ways to satisfy and resolve the situation? Due to the different roles and positions between parents and children, they often only think from their own perspectives, which can lead to a lack of understanding and refusal to fulfill each other's requests. It is important to continue to communicate and try to empathize with each other in order to gradually understand each other and reach a consensus. Best wishes.

Hello, it seems that your actions towards your parents may be related to some childhood traumas. It's possible that your parents were very strict with you during your early years and you had no means to resist. Now that you have grown up and have the ability, you are starting to rebel against and "retaliate" your parents. You need to reflect on the traumas caused by your parents during your childhood. Whenever your parents say something, you feel the need to oppose it, and whenever they behave in a certain way, you resist. Only when you understand yourself, understand the wounds you have suffered, and understand the triggers that lead to your disobedience, can you make changes for the better. From your writing, I can sense that you are not very satisfied with the current situation and you do not want to spend money recklessly or lack ambition. However, your relationship with your parents is not good, coupled with past pains, which makes you unwilling to change the current situation. But even so, I hope you can make some changes. If a person continues to live in past traumas or dissatisfaction, they cannot progress. You are currently engaged in power struggles with your parents and retaliating against their lack of understanding through your own defiant behaviors (such as spending money recklessly or lacking ambition). However, the person responsible for your own life is not others, not your parents, not your friends, it's only yourself. If you focus your energy and time on these areas, are you not being responsible for your own life? Therefore, if possible, it would be worth trying to repair your relationship with your parents. Regardless of whether they understand you or discipline you harshly, their love for you still exists. I have seen many professionals in my circle who often get angry at work because of a colleague or boss's comment, but later they realize that they also get angry when their parents say similar things. So, if you want to improve your relationships with friends and colleagues, you also need to repair your relationship with your parents. It may feel strange to suddenly try to repair a long-standing issue, and you may need to constantly reassure yourself. But it is also about taking responsibility for yourself, in order to live a happier life and have better relationships. It's not a bad thing to have a conversation with your parents and be open-hearted during a holiday or birthday. Although this process may make you angry, you can tell your parents the reason for your anger and let them understand how their words hurt you. Let your parents understand you. It's a bit sad that as children grow up, chances for communication with their parents become fewer and parents become less understanding, and sometimes stubborn. But in the end, when children and parents understand each other, they will realize that those little things from before can be laughed off. So, you can think about your past experiences and find opportunities to talk to your parents, and see if it helps. Best wishes.

Hello! You mentioned that spending money recklessly and lacking ambition is a way to retaliate against your parents for their lack of understanding and disobedience. Let's first examine the effectiveness of this retaliatory behavior. Who is suffering or facing the consequences of your lack of ambition, and what does it mean for your future? Lacking ambition could potentially ruin your abilities and capabilities in the future. Your inner self is blaming your parents for not understanding you, not seeing you, and not obeying you, and you want to see how they can destroy you. I can imagine the pain and anger of not being understood by one's parents, who often fail to see or even ignore you, or control you. Taking revenge is a coping strategy to avoid the pain of not being understood. First, we need to understand what this coping strategy means for you. Can we find another way to avoid the pain and helplessness in my inner self, and ensure that my future social functioning is not hindered? I suggest finding a counselor to help you understand and comprehend how your inner self operates. Why do you adopt such behavioral patterns, and what does it mean for you? What is the pain that you are avoiding?

Hello, I can sense your strong desire for your parents to understand your needs, and I want to give you a warm hug. Since you can't get your parents' understanding, you try to get their attention by "spending money recklessly and not being motivated," perhaps to relieve the pressure in your heart. However, from your feelings, it seems that this method hasn't achieved the result you wanted. Your parents continue to misunderstand, and you are still confused. Indeed, there is inevitably a deep generation gap between parents and children, and they have different perceptions. It is not easy to seek consensus and understanding. Therefore, we need to analyze specific problems specifically. What do you want your parents to understand? What are your needs? What result do you hope to achieve? Then, we can see how to communicate with our parents to reach this result. How to apply the right medicine, whether it's verbal communication or actions, whether it's a long-term gradual process or a decisive approach, whether to persuade them ourselves or seek help from others. Do we really need to convince our parents? Do we really need to make them understand 100%? Or can we rely on ourselves and be independent? Don't worry if you don't achieve the desired result at first. We can allow ourselves to try again and again in order to find the most suitable way of communication between you and your parents. Keep going and good luck :)

question: Don't know how to get along with the opposite sex, don't know how to start a conversation?
description: Actually, I don't interact well with girls either, probably due to being more introverted. I don't know what to say or how to start conversations. It's even worse when it comes to the opposite sex. I hope to receive some suggestions to help me gradually integrate with more people.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand your current mood, as the saying goes, "A kind word warms you for three days, but a harsh word chills you for three winters." Communication has become a common problem for many people. My suggestion is: "Try to make the other person say 'yes' as much as possible." The more "yes" we get from others, the more we can assert our own opinions, whether it is selling products or convincing others of something. This principle is very effective. When communicating with others, when we refrain from saying "no," or when we already have this thought in our minds, we are already approaching the other person because we understand their needs very well. Consequently, they will also pay attention to us. However, when the other person says "no," or has a mindset of refusal, the situation changes. When our questions seem to have nothing to do with them, it is equivalent to us not caring about what they want. They will definitely get angry because a person's "self-esteem" stems from this. Therefore, if we cannot get a "yes" response from the other person when dealing with them, it is best for us to try to prevent them from saying "no." So how can we make the other person say "yes" as much as possible? The method is to learn the art of questioning and guide the other person to talk more. Questioning is when we ask ourselves questions and answer them, knowingly asking but not blindly. However, knowingly asking is not just asking randomly; we should ask about things that interest the other person, that they are proud of, such as their brilliant achievements, successful experiences, current concerns, and their areas of interest. Questioning is a powerful tool for understanding the other person's psychology and the best way to approach those who are difficult to approach. Through clever questioning, make the other person talk more about themselves. It is important to know that people are always happy when discussing themselves. Once they are engaged, it becomes easier to interact with you. Additionally, find common ground between both parties and guide the other person to agree with your opinions and give a "yes" response. Therefore, it can be said that there are no people who cannot be convinced, only people who do not know how to communicate. In order to succeed in the business and professional fields, one must take control of the conversation and guide the other person towards the goals we set. We should strive to obtain a "yes" response as much as possible. Finally, I hope my suggestion can help you and be applied to your life. I hope that you can become someone who can chat with anyone.

question: How to adjust when encountering specific events triggers depressive emotions?
description: I am currently working, and I have been experiencing headaches since high school. I have been accompanied by depressive moods every day (I have consulted a professional counseling service), and until now, while working, I have been in a state of depression for about ten years. I work in data-related jobs, and I left my job for a long time due to depression. After receiving counseling and doing things I like, the depressive state has improved a lot. My daily mood, need for social interaction, and interests have all improved. The anxiety, loneliness, and palpitations that used to exist have also been alleviated, and I don't even feel them anymore. Then I wanted to return to work, but as long as I think about certain aspects of my job, for example, doing SPSS, even if I haven't done any regression analysis before, just listening to a course about what SPSS software is, I start to get headaches, palpitations, and uncontrollable depressive moods. I can't handle it whenever it is mentioned, and it takes one or two days or even a week to not think about it in order to relieve the symptoms. I have also considered not doing this kind of work, but I do need a job right now, and it is difficult to find other jobs, especially in the current pandemic situation. I hope that if...
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, I feel sorry for the long time you have been troubled by depressive emotions. Based on your description, it seems that your depression mainly stems from dissatisfaction with work. You rationalize and force yourself to accept it, which not only fails to improve work efficiency but also intensifies resistance psychologically. So, let's analyze the problem together and try to find ways to alleviate your emotions. Problem analysis: * After a period of treatment, relapse of depression upon returning to work. You have made great improvement after receiving proper counseling, indicating that when the counselor guided you to do what you enjoy, you were able to return to a normal state of life and no longer be plagued by negative emotions. Since high school, headaches, depression, and negativity have seemingly prevented you from experiencing positive emotions such as happiness and fulfillment in life. Your life always feels dull and uncontrollable, and you appear passive in life. It wasn't until you encountered something you genuinely loved that your subjective initiative was maximally stimulated, bringing hope to your life. Consequently, during that period, you naturally switched from a pessimistic and negative mindset to a positive attitude. Upon returning to work, the stark contrast between the previous dreary and monotonous experience and the happiness brought by self-directed creativity was evident. Your rational consciousness tells you that you cannot do without this job, and it is difficult to find another job. Meanwhile, your subconscious strongly desires for you to do what you love to maintain vitality. As a result, conflict arises between your consciousness and subconsciousness, which is manifested in your extreme resistance to returning to work. Your current approach is to suppress the impulse of your subconsciousness in order to control your depressive emotions. You attempt to alleviate your unhappiness by thinking about happy things when doing unhappy tasks. However, unhappiness and happiness coexist and cannot be fundamentally resolved. When faced with unhappiness, you always try to suppress it with happiness, which only makes you more exhausted. It is as if you have become very proficient in the stress response of your body and brain, which is a result of excessive internal consumption. Here are some small suggestions: 1. Face your true inner thoughts and no longer suppress the impulse of your subconsciousness with rational consciousness. Explore the possibility of developing long-term work from the things you used to enjoy doing. If your focus is only on the present, your long-standing thought patterns will be trapped by shortsightedness, making it more difficult to make changes. 2. Balance work and leisure. You already understand that the purpose of work is to obtain survival resources and to live a more comfortable life in this world. If priorities are reversed and life is already uncomfortable, the purpose of work to make life better cannot be achieved. You don't have to force yourself to immediately accept the current situation. If your interests cannot develop into long-term work, you can also combine them with your current job, properly distribute your energy, and then see if you can alleviate the inner conflict. I wish you can live the life you truly want.

Hello, it seems that you have described the issue very professionally. You have also realized that the statistics data is a source of depression for you. Every time you encounter related work or hear about it, it triggers your depressive emotions, causing you anxiety and negative feelings. During the time you were away from this position, you experienced the positive and pleasant feelings that came from leaving this source. So now, when you have to return to this job, these sources of depression and anxiety bring back negative feelings. Why go back to something that you have already experienced the benefits of leaving? You mentioned that it may be difficult to find another job, which is also causing you anxiety and urgency. It adds to the pressure you feel from the statistics data, and when you study or engage with things related to this job again, you naturally associate it with the pressure to find employment, leading to unpleasant feelings. So how can we adjust? The simplest solution is, of course, to leave it. If being pricked by a needle hurts, who would want to stay in a place where they are continuously pricked? However, when you feel that you truly cannot leave, don't force yourself to accept it, as it will only bring greater resistance. Just let this dislike reside here and continue your work, or try to identify the root of your dislike and find targeted ways to alleviate it. You can also think about your past successes, why you chose this job in the first place, and reflect on your original intentions. Or recall the sense of achievement and pleasure you have experienced in your work, and then think about how you approached this matter initially. These observations may help you adjust your emotions. The world loves you~.

Hello, the topic owner. After reading your description and the comments in the reply section, it seems that you have a clear understanding of your own problems. You have also sought psychological counseling and gained some knowledge of psychological healing concepts, such as the "rational emotive therapy" that you mentioned in your reply, and you are actively practicing it. That's great. I will give you a thumbs up and applaud you. "Every time I think about some aspects of work, I experience symptoms such as headaches and anxiety. For example, when it comes to doing SPSS, maybe you haven't even started conducting regression analysis and have only listened to lectures about what the SPSS software is, but you start experiencing uncontrollable emotions like headaches, heart palpitations, and depression. It takes one or two days, or even a week, without thinking about this matter to alleviate the symptoms. It happens every time." In short, whenever you think about or hear about work-related content, you experience symptoms such as headaches, anxiety, and depression (often accompanied by anxiety). Essentially, these emotions are derived from fear! I remember there's a line in "Fear Motivates" (also known as "Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway"): "Human nature is incomplete without experiencing fear!" The fact that you can still feel fear means that your human nature is "complete", and you are still a normal person. This is exactly the beginning of your journey towards "wholeness"! In order to fundamentally solve your current problem, you need to try to resolve the deep-seated "source of fear" within you. You can try to "concretize" and "quantify" your fear of work: 1) What exactly are you afraid of when it comes to work? Are you afraid that the content is too difficult, that you won't understand, and that you won't be able to perform well when you need to use them in your work, resulting in criticism from your superiors, deductions from your salary and bonuses, or even the loss of your job? Or is it something else? 2) How likely do you think the things you fear will actually happen? Can you try to express it as a percentage? 3) Even if the things you fear actually happen, what would be the worst outcome? 4) Do you have any resources around you that can help you deal with this fear? "Back when I was in school, I have been experiencing headaches and accompanying depression every day starting from high school (I have sought counseling in a formal psychological counseling agency)." It can be seen that your current problem has been going on for more than just a few days. It is the "total outbreak" of accumulated problems over the years! Regarding this, may I ask you a few questions, if you feel comfortable answering them: 1. What happened during your high school years that made you experience headaches and be surrounded by depression? Was it because the difficulty of the high school curriculum suddenly increased, leading to high academic pressure? Or was it due to problems in interpersonal relationships? 2. Apart from seeking counseling in psychological institutions, have your family members provided any help? How is the level of intimacy between you and your family members from childhood to adulthood? In terms of the "language of love" you receive from your family members, such as smiles, hugs, and praise, has it been abundant? Of course, these questions involve your personal privacy, and I respect your personal wishes.

Hello, I wonder how this type of work is connected to your previous experiences that have caused you such anxiety and distress. It is evident that you are forced to do this job due to real-life circumstances, but it is causing you a lot of pain. You mentioned that you feel good when you are doing something you are interested in. This indicates a strong association between your depression and this job. Since you are unable to perform this job better at the moment, it would be beneficial to adjust your emotional state before engaging in work. Temporary life pressures can be alleviated through other means or work.

Hello, thank you for your question. After reading through it, I have a feeling that you've come to understand what causes depression and why it can be so severe. You have also found effective treatment methods and hope to continue this positive progress. However, you still have fears, which is why you are seeking support through your question. Am I right? 🥙 I am glad to see that your depression has received good treatment. It is important to know that depression has become one of the leading causes of death globally, with a mortality rate that has at times surpassed that of cancer. The long-term effects and complications it can cause need not be mentioned. Perhaps you have narrowly escaped death? Whether to cherish this new life and how to cherish it is up to you. Is life valuable or is a job you don't like valuable? Is a healthy and happy life important or is the fear of relapsing into depression and having an unhappy job more important? I believe you understand this better than us based on your personal experience. What kind of life do you want, or more specifically, what kind of state do you feel comfortable in? What defines life quality? Is it not based on physical and mental health? Otherwise, who is the quality for? 🥪 It seems that you have doubts about completely quitting your job. On the other hand, working in this job is causing you great pain and there is a possibility of a relapse. So, is it possible to find a compromise? Perhaps try to find a less demanding job for now, while devoting more time and energy to things and places you enjoy. Take it slowly, no need to rush. Step by step, accumulate strength, and when the time comes to make a living and live the life you love, then consider quitting this type of job completely. Just like personal growth, there is always a process and it may involve twists and turns. I hope you can face your inner self and accept that life is not always sweet. With this mindset, I believe you will have more confidence in developing your desired career and life. The world and I love you.

Because I couldn't bear the headaches and depression, I left my previous job and also sought formal counseling. Even after all this time, going back to my old job, I still can't adapt. You mentioned that you have considered Adler's teleology. Have you tried Freud's psychoanalysis? Go and see what happened in the past? What caused it? Because you mentioned that it started from your high school years until now. So I suggest you find a counselor from the psychoanalytic school and seek counseling. Different schools have different solutions. I hope you can resolve your confusion soon.

Dear friend, keep going! So, I also have a problem with headaches. Later on, I started using essential oils, so I can apply it anytime I feel the pain. I also meditate and increase my rest time to adjust my state... And if the headaches persist without relief, try mentioning it to your psychiatrist and see if there are any other methods that may be more suitable and helpful for you. Keep going, I hope you get better and may happiness, health, and good luck be with you always.

Feeling.ism, right? You're very intelligent. But I want to say, in a sense, feelings are useless, and you're deeply trapped in them. Don't you understand that practice determines knowledge, and matter determines consciousness? This is the simplest philosophy, and you definitely understand it. But by relying on so-called psychological suggestions, even hypnosis, you're essentially unable to solve the current situation, but rather a fundamental problem of how you attempt to overcome your emotional attachment to this matter. Maybe you feel that this approach gives you a different and mysterious experience, but I want to say, first, overcome this. Perhaps you haven't realized it in your life. If my answer makes sense, let's continue the discussion. If you think it's absurd, just take it as a look.

It seems like the topic wasn't fully discussed, so I'll add some more. If possible, I hope to find a method to deal with this. I kind of understand the mechanism - it's like being bitten by a snake once and being scared of ropes for ten years. From an Adlerian perspective, it's not the situation itself that leads to depressive emotions, but rather what I attribute to it. I've also tried using imagination and imagery dialogue to give this situation a different feeling. For example, while doing this task, I think about happy things, or when feeling depressed, I envision a little person in my mind gradually calming down. But this only provides some relief, the effect is not significant. I'm not sure if it's because I've been in a depressive environment for too long, and the stress response of my body and brain has become very proficient.

question: Is it acceptable if friends and family members have moral issues?
description: A long time ago, my mother had an affair, and later she encouraged my father to do the same and asked him not to intervene with her. My father wanted a divorce but ultimately didn't go through with it and told me that he never considered me before making that decision. However, a few months ago, I discovered that both of my parents were having affairs. I was deeply hurt, and since then, I have been constantly doubting myself, reflecting on every detail of my life to see if I'm right or wrong. I haven't stopped overthinking obsessively, and more importantly, questioning my moral beliefs. Despite wanting to respect and accept everyone around me, I'm confused about how I can accept their actions. Recently, I found out that my roommate is cheating on her boyfriend, and she casually mentioned it to me and another friend. At that moment, I thought of my parents, and I don't know how to face my friend or the moral standards I know. In fact, I don't even understand my relationship with the world. I know nothing, I don't know what's right or wrong, and it's immature to always seek to judge. But I choose to treat them as if I know nothing, maybe that's safer. Is this a normal phenomenon? Is the other person's private life irrelevant to my relationship with them? I shouldn't judge, but how should I interact with them?

answers.answer_text: Hello! This is indeed a relatively normal social phenomenon. You think they have moral problems, it is the discomfort caused by the difference in your moral sense and theirs that makes you feel uncomfortable. Of course, you can make your own judgment. However, the meaning of this judgment is not to make others become the same as you, or to make yourself become the same as them, but to let this judgment guide your desired attitude towards life. When the moral values of others conflict with ours, emotions naturally first tell us that we cannot accept or understand them. When we find that we are powerless to change or interfere with these established facts, reason tells us some reasons that we must accept. In this way, the inner balance can be achieved, so as to avoid mental breakdown and madness. Your parents and friends, as the people who are in close proximity to you, no matter how they are divided and detached, you are all like fish in the same pond, and you will inevitably influence each other. Therefore, when they have problems, you will reflect on yourself, as if there is something wrong with you. But their problems are only their problems, and you only need to take care of yourself as much as possible to avoid being affected. What we understand as the appearance of life is only a small piece of the whole life, and its depth is mostly hidden in those inconvenient words. When you see these various forms that differ from the original imagination, it is also when you gradually understand the essence of life. It can be beautiful, but also dirty; it can sometimes bring hope, sometimes disappointment. Ethics is a human civilization, but it is not like gravity, which is truth. There are a thousand Hamlets in a thousand people, and there are a thousand moral standards, and these standards will also change with circumstances. The so-called moral sense has become more of a personal emotion, without a guideline. Therefore, morality cannot objectively punish people, but can only subjectively condemn them. When we find that others' approach to private life is inconsistent with ours and we cannot understand it, it is polite to keep a distance and be the person we want to be within the concept that makes us comfortable.

Hello, OP, I'll start by giving you a big hug~ Let's take a look at your problem: the infidelity of your parents and roommate has made you question your moral values. You don't know how to face your friends and family, and you doubt the correctness of the morals you believed in. I want to tell you that your moral values are not wrong. The infidelity of your parents and roommate, regardless of the reasons behind it, is their own fault. Their morals are compromised, and they have betrayed their sense of responsibility. Truly moral and responsible individuals always have their own principles and boundaries. No matter what problems they face, they will uphold their boundaries. Take the issue of infidelity as an example: if your parents and roommate had a sense of morals and responsibility, they would have chosen to divorce or break up before cheating instead. Does their personal life have anything to do with you? Should you pretend not to know? How should you interact with them? I want to tell you that no matter how close your relationship is with someone, you are not them, and you have no right to interfere with their personal life. As friends or children, we can reasonably and tactfully inform them of their unethical or wrong behavior, but whether they choose to correct themselves is not your concern. We can only ensure that we have a clear conscience and not forcibly demand that others change. If you have friends or family members who repeatedly engage in unethical behavior and you have already reminded them, but they haven't made any changes, it's best for you not to know about such matters in the future. How should we interact with friends and family members who have moral issues? For family members: advise them and inform them of the consequences. Family members are our loved ones, and they usually listen to our opinions. We can explain to them the harm and impact of these unethical behaviors and help them understand their importance. Leading by example is the best way to influence others. By silently influencing our family members through our interactions with them, we can help them understand their mistakes and unethical behavior. For friends: persuade and inform them of the consequences. We can still advise our friends and make them understand the negative consequences of their actions. However, friends are different from family, and we must maintain a certain boundary so that both parties won't feel uncomfortable. Inform them of your principles and boundaries. Let them know your principles and moral boundaries. If someone genuinely wants to be your friend, even if they engage in unethical behavior, they will try to avoid letting you know about it to prevent you from getting hurt. It's also okay to distance yourself from insincere people. These are just personal opinions, and I hope they can help you. Take care~

1. Friendships and interpersonal relationships are inherently subjective. Why is it that you become friends with some people while others become strangers? Therefore, what matters is whether you consider "faithfulness" as a criterion for making friends. This criterion is no different from a series of other friendship criteria, such as "not liking spicy food" or "enjoying playing games." In my opinion, not wanting to be friends with unfaithful people does not mean judging others; it is simply one of your criteria for making friends. However, this is only your criterion and may not apply to others. Conversely, if you believe that your criterion of "faithfulness" is righteous and that others should follow suit and ostracize this unfaithful roommate, then you are interfering with others' friendships and acting as a judge. 

2. Parental relationships may be a little more complicated than friendships, but they are fundamentally no different. One thing to keep in mind is that you always need to examine and observe your own moral principles. From my perspective, as long as your decisions do not harm others' immediate interests, there is no right or wrong~ Just stick to and abide by your own principles. We cannot control or change others, but as long as we are not changed by others, that's what matters~ By the way, your parents' actions are evidently affecting your interests~ In my opinion, it is no longer just a personal matter unrelated to right or wrong~ It's quite significant~ I hope my answer can bring some reflection and inspiration to the asker~ Best wishes~

We should not and have no need to judge anyone because we are not responsible for other people's lives, and we do not know what they have experienced or what they are truly thinking. Except for judges who need to judge and convict someone according to the laws and regulations, and rehabilitate and punish others, let's leave the rest to God. Criticizing others serves no purpose other than making them feel repulsed and resistant towards you, and creating distance between you. Others will not feel good or change because of your criticism. It is a person's right to live their own life, and it is not up to anyone else. Not to mention infidelity, even murderers have lawyers to defend them and may even be released due to lack of evidence. Recently, I happened to see a photo posted by a girl showing her selfie and she wrote that everyone has different standards, as long as she feels beautiful, it is enough. Unexpectedly, the keyboard warriors started commenting, saying things like, "Why post it when you dress like that?" "Sometimes it's better to listen to others' opinions," "If I looked like that, I wouldn't post selfies"… It hurts me to see this. Maybe the girl is not conventionally beautiful, but what business is it of theirs? Why do they want to hurt someone like that? Criticism has no positive effect, but it can cause a lot of harm. Values are not right or wrong, they are just different from yours, your parents', or your roommates'. You may think loyalty is paramount and believe that there should be no infidelity among loved ones, but others may think that faithfulness is not the most important thing and they value other aspects more. If you try to deprive them of their right to pursue what they want because of this, isn't it going beyond your boundaries? You will never find someone who is exactly like you. If every time the other person's understanding and behavior do not match yours, and you feel the need to criticize and attempt to correct them, won't you feel exhausted? Will you still have any friends? I think what the topic creator needs to focus on is how other people's infidelity affects you? Does it cause you any harm? If someone's infidelity caused harm to your boyfriend and hurt you, then of course you should distance yourself from that person. But if the other person is cheating on their boyfriend and your parents are okay with it, what does it have to do with you? It doesn't harm you in any way. If you do not approve of these values, then it is better not to be close to them. Just be casual friends and there is no need for deep communication. As long as you do not engage in such behavior yourself, it is sufficient. The world is not black and white, and there is no absolute right or wrong. Many things exposed on the surface are just the tip of the iceberg, and what we see may not be the truth. Therefore, not criticizing anyone is what we should do, giving others the freedom to do what they want, and perhaps your emotions can improve a little bit.

Hello friend, grateful for our encounter! After reading your question, I sense your confusion, indecision, contradictions, and the distress that comes with being human. Even through the screen, I want to give you a big hug. Judgment is one of the functions of the brain, and it can happen unconsciously. Your question is well posed – does other people's matters concern me? In psychology, there is a cognitive-behavioral therapy that emphasizes personal boundaries. Whose matter is it? Mine? Yours? God's? In reality, boundaries are not so easily defined. Whose matter is it if it concerns your parents? It's their matter, easy to determine. But can you truly separate your parents' matters from your own? Clearly, that's not possible. The matter of both parents having an affair has caused you great harm, psychologically known as post-traumatic stress disorder. You are especially sensitive about personal moral issues, and overthinking is called "rumination" in psychology. Rumination refers to repeatedly thinking about negative events, negative emotions about oneself, and the causes and possible consequences of events. For example, "Why did this happen to me?" "Why am I often unhappy while others are happy?" "Will being frequently unhappy lead to depression?" In severe cases, thoughts may become incessant. It is as if everyone in life is a nail, and you happen to be holding the hammer. Both judgment and sensitivity to moral issues are present at this stage, and it is who you are in this moment. Accepting their existence might bring you some ease. Thank you~.

Hello, good evening! After reading your description, I really want to give you a virtual hug. These kinds of events can be confusing and even bewildering, causing you to question your own moral standards. Let me share my humble opinion, hoping to provide you with a different perspective to reexamine this situation. 1. Infidelity - what is infidelity? In my understanding, it refers to developing a relationship with someone else while already being in a marriage or committed relationship, indicating a partial detachment from the family or partner and thus considered unethical. It is clear that both infidelity and morality are concepts created by people. The root cause of infidelity lies in unmet internal needs being fulfilled externally. 2. The truth of the hurt - I believe you must be very sad and upset about the situation with your parents. This sadness and upset are not caused by the infidelity itself; rather, infidelity represents the division of your parents, indicating that the once united family seems to have been torn apart and no longer cohesive. Perhaps your parents' actions have deeply hurt you, as infidelity almost shatters the secure foundation you relied upon, leaving nothing but an empty shell. This is the truth of the hurt. 3. Judgment - I understand that you must be confused about this. Traditional education often leads us to unconsciously pass judgment, regardless of right or wrong. However, you should not question whether you are right or wrong; this is an automatic reaction. 4. Boundaries - Each person is an independent individual, and the actions of your parents or roommates are their own choices, their own needs. You only need to act according to your own values, guarding your boundaries, which is the greatest respect for yourself and others. Everyone will have their own needs, and morality is a definition created by people. Whether you adhere to it or deviate from it, it all stems from internal needs. It is also someone else's matter. By following your own heart, protecting and nurturing yourself, you are doing the most important thing. Good luck to you!

Hello, this is a very headache-inducing and distressing issue, and I understand you.① How to view "infidelity"? "Morality" is a social convention, and it has a social background. Morality is not defined by any specific standards, so each person has their own moral standards. You, your parents, your friends, and roommates are all independent individuals, and each of you will have your own moral standards. Is "infidelity" right or wrong? In the movie "The Love That Ties Us Together," both spouses acknowledge that they have their own "boyfriends" and "girlfriends," which are extramarital lovers. They even meet and get to know each other's "boyfriends" and "girlfriends," and introduce them to their children. It's a scene of "joyful harmony." In the past, or in certain countries and regions today, men could have multiple wives and concubines. In such social contexts, how is "male infidelity" defined in terms of morality? So, you will also have your own view on "infidelity" and your own moral standards. You just need to live according to your own moral standards. You don't have to "accept" their moral system, and in reality, it is difficult to understand their moral system as well. Of course, you can evaluate their moral system internally and whether you should "correct" their moral system and make them align with yours is another matter that requires consideration. ② How to get along with "infidel family and friends"? For someone who doesn't accept infidelity, it is difficult to face it easily when it comes to close relatives and friends. You can only say that this is just a part of them, although this part is very important to you. They also have many other parts, such as taking care of you when you are sick or being kind to others, etc. Try your best (can only say try your best) to see a more comprehensive picture of them, instead of solely focusing on their infidelity and rejecting them in various ways. If it is really uncomfortable to face them, then reduce the opportunities for interaction with them. As for ourselves, we need to clarify what kind of person we want to be and focus on being the best version of ourselves. I hope you can refrain from immersing yourself in thinking about these things every day, as it will make you unhappy. If there are things you can't understand now, just save them for later when you become more mature and revisit them then.

First, give the author a hug. I think you have your own perspective on the issue of infidelity. Based on your description, your mother cheated when you were young and even encouraged your father to do the same, and she denigrated him in front of you, saying "If he did the same, he never considered me." She said this because she harbored resentment towards your father. Perhaps she didn't realize the impact of this statement on you and the serious blow it dealt to your beliefs. It's clear that your parents' dual infidelity had a significant impact on you, to the point where you punish yourself by constantly reflecting on every detail of your life and questioning whether you're right or wrong. Here, I'd like you to consider something: if your mother hadn't said that to you, would your father have cheated? It's hard to say, as that was his decision. Do you really think that anything you do could change the outcome of both your parents' infidelity? The truth is, it can't, because your parents made decisions that were not responsible toward you. You don't really need to bear the consequences of their mistakes. It's precisely because the issue of your parents' infidelity hasn't been resolved that your trauma has been triggered again when your roommate openly discusses infidelity in the dormitory. Perhaps your roommate has a different belief system, thinking "It's my ability to snatch other people's boyfriends." That's why she talks about it in the dormitory and boasts about it. You feel uncomfortable about it, and personally, I also dislike infidelity, so I find myself judging when I listen to other people's experiences of infidelity. Such emotions and psychological reactions are normal because your views differ. However, everyone's formation of their own views is closely related to their upbringing and surrounding environment. Therefore, we have to accept one viewpoint, which is that things in this society are not as black and white or righteous triumphing over evil like in childhood cartoons. Instead, there are many gray areas. Good people also have undisclosed stories, and bad people have situations that led them down the wrong path. When you grow up, perhaps one day you will understand that even though people have different views, these views can coexist, and what each person says is not right or wrong, but rather a reflection of their perspective and position. If you can't accept her viewpoint, I don't think you need to force yourself to accept it. Just keep your distance respectfully, as you said, "Choose to treat them like I don't know anything, perhaps that's safer." I think that is a good way to resolve the situation. Then you can choose to be friends with people who share the same values as you. But as for the trauma of your parents' infidelity, I suggest you seek counseling to resolve it, as it will be triggered by similar situations, and this is something you need to address. I hope you continue to get better.

question: Do local people here seem selfish and narrow-minded? Is it just me being narrow-minded? What should I do?
description: I really feel that the locals here are selfish and narrow-minded, and it's not just me who feels this way. In one department, out of four people, three are somehow related, while the other one being isolated is considered normal. And I am the outsider who is isolated. It makes sense for the company to have a policy against dating colleagues. The three of them are all from the 80s, and all they talk about every day is their families and relatives. I have absolutely no common ground with them!! I can't hold on much longer. What should I do? Is it because I am too narrow-minded and unwilling to communicate with them? Is it my problem?

answers.answer_text: That's right, it's your problem because you chose this company, and it seems that people in this company think that everyone in this city is the same. First of all, it's a matter of values. I don't know what kind of company you are in, but it doesn't seem very busy. As for the issue of nepotism, you didn't explain it clearly, so let's ignore that information for now. It's well known that it's difficult for people with different values to get along. Based on your description, it seems that this company has a problem with their values. They not only focus on work but also interfere with personal emotions. This is like behaving as if they are your elders! A company or organization should focus on creating value for society or maintaining certain aspects of social operations, instead of trying to act as elders for their employees. And what's more frustrating is that they may want to act like caring elders without taking up the responsibilities that come with it! It's ridiculous! Only someone like you, who can tolerate such things, would stay in a place with such a culture for a long time. People with less patience would have already planned their escape. In a company or organization with such a culture, it's normal to have three colleagues like yours. The saying "birds of a feather flock together" is extremely practical when the scope is small and options are available. Secondly, people often have no choice when it comes to their geographical location. So naturally, there will be some people living in this place who can't stand the things you can't stand. Therefore, when you think that people in this place are the same as the people in your department, it just means that you have no interaction with the other people here to the extent that you can't see this group of people. This also means that if you can change companies, units, or departments, you have no idea where to go. This is why you don't know what to do, because you don't know where to go to make your life less miserable. So if you really want to take action, you need to learn about this place, how other companies or organizations are, and get insider information by getting to know people. Expanding your network of friends is something you must do, and you can start by participating in some online activities. If you still refuse to take this action, then you have the problem of "knowing that you've fallen into a pit but refusing to climb out."

OP, in an organization with a total of four people, three of them are already acquainted and naturally tend to communicate more with each other. The remaining person may feel like they have been left out and have difficulty fitting in. In addition, if you are not familiar with or interested in the topics they discuss, naturally you will feel like you have very few common topics with them. This is not because you are narrow-minded or unwilling to communicate with them; it is a common feeling. Because you are from out of town and not very familiar with the local area, and you don't have many acquaintances, it is normal to feel like you haven't integrated into the group. Perhaps you can proactively talk to them about work-related matters or discuss any problems you encounter in your life. Maybe you can also look for colleagues in other departments who you get along well with and develop a friendship with them. It may make you feel much better. In your daily life, you can also participate in community activities and go shopping or take walks during your days off. Maybe you will meet new friends. Best wishes!

question: A high school senior girl is having conflicts with her classmates, they see each other constantly and dislike her?
description: Originally, Girl A, Girl B, and I were good friends. At the beginning of this semester, Girl A told me that she felt like neither Girl B nor I considered her a genuine friend. She said that she couldn't fit in with us and that she was very sensitive. At that time, I was a little angry because I treated both of them the same and considered them good friends. Later on, we talked it out and made up. Normally, I would eat meals with Girl A, but last week, she suddenly wrote me a note saying that she no longer wanted to eat with me. I was very angry, and I didn't understand what thoughts were going through her sensitive and suspicious mind. With the overwhelming pressure of senior year, I really didn't want to listen to her complaints. So, I wrote her a strongly worded letter in response. She also wrote me a letter, and the entire letter was full of accusations, bringing up insignificant details from when we were together before, such as me taking too long to get ready one day, or not talking because I didn't want to be with her during physical education class. I never paid any attention to these things, but she took them to heart and made me feel exhausted. That letter was written as if I had committed some sort of violence on campus against her. Now, we are in a big fight, and our relationship is very tense. Girl B has been friends with me for a longer time, but she still treats Girl A the same way, which makes me feel uncomfortable. Thinking about all of these things, I am very annoyed. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Hugs to you! From your statement, I understand that you may be feeling anxious right now, facing academic pressure and dealing with interpersonal relationships. You and female friends A and B are good friends, with A being more sensitive and perceptive. A felt that you treated her and B differently, but eventually, you made up. However, last week, A suddenly wrote a note saying she didn't want to eat with you anymore. In response, you wrote a strongly-worded letter, and she replied with accusations, making you feel uncomfortable, and causing a rift between you two. But B continues to treat A the same way, which also makes you uncomfortable. From what you've told me, you treated A and B the same, so why is A angry with you while B isn't? Perhaps it has to do with each person's own experiences and personalities. Everyone has their own way of living, and for A, she may feel angry because it's not how she sees things should be, while for B, it may not matter as much. Everyone has different ways of thinking, and we don't know what A has been through. If we can't change a person, maybe we can try to consider things from their perspective. In other words, the way she presents herself and handles things has always been like this and not directed at anyone in particular. One part that you might not understand is why B can still treat A the same way, even though you met her first. Let's try thinking from a different perspective. A and B have not had a conflict, and A has always treated B the same way. So, B will continue to interact with A as usual. In other words, although you had a conflict with A, I didn't, so I can still have contact with her the same way. Everyone sees other people differently, and maybe for B, it's just a normal interaction between classmates. For you, you're currently in your final year of high school and will soon face the national college entrance exam, which is a lot of pressure. We can try communicating with A to ease the relationship and stabilize your emotions, so you can fully focus on your studies. Lastly, I hope you can be admitted to your dream university. Good luck!

Hello, OP~
I can feel your frustration and distress. You're having a conflict with one of your close friends for some reason, and you don't know how to handle the relationship between the three of you. I understand your feelings very well. As a senior facing immense academic pressure, you're also troubled by interpersonal issues. It's evident that you have a great relationship with the other two friends, but your personality differs from that of friend A. She is more sensitive and tends to overanalyze your language and behavior towards friend B, even though you and friend B don't see it as excluding her. You both have exchanged letters where she criticized your past actions because these are things you never paid attention to, so they held no significance for you. However, they greatly troubled friend A, causing her to overthink and feel that you are indifferent towards her. OP and friend A have differing personalities, with OP being more carefree and not bothered by small things, while friend A is sensitive and tends to overanalyze minor actions. In reality, both of you care about each other and value this friendship, but have different ways of approaching the problem. OP can try to empathize with friend A's point of view and understand if the issues she raised truly exist and if OP would have similar thoughts if it happened to them. Of course, the most important thing is to communicate face-to-face, express your thoughts, and share your feelings. Additionally, OP should pay more attention to friend A in future interactions. Wishing OP can overcome the distress soon~.

Hello, OP, I understand that there is a lot of academic pressure in your senior year, and the difficulties in getting along with friends have added to your worries. Your friend is more attentive to details, while you don't place much importance on these details, which has led to conflicts between you. In a fit of anger, you wrote a strongly-worded letter to your friend, which made them feel attacked and they also started blaming you, expressing their grievances. You mentioned that you consider them a good friend. In fact, since you consider each other good friends, you need sincere communication and understanding. The conflicts that arise are not solely one person's fault. Without proper communication, misunderstandings can easily occur when everyone's needs are not met. Whenever you think about this incident, it makes you annoyed and regretful. It is probably not your intention to come to this point today. Senior year is also a time when friends need to learn from and encourage each other. Having conflicts at this time is detrimental to everyone. It may be better to find a suitable time to communicate with your friend, without blaming each other, both take a step back, and see if the conflict can be resolved.

Hello, after reading your question, I can fully understand your concerns and inner distress. During the high school third year exam preparation stage, due to high levels of anxiety, many things can be magnified, leading to difficulty concentrating and being easily influenced by emotions. Friendship issues at this time are the result of both external and internal factors. Here, I can provide the following analysis and advice, hoping it can help you. Your friend "a" is a sensitive person, and in your previous interactions, she did not express any dissatisfaction with your relationship. However, choosing to speak up during the third year may be due to the increasing pressure of heavy academic workload this semester, leading to greater internal stress with nowhere to vent. When reflecting on your interactions, it is easy to generate feelings of dissatisfaction. But obviously, this doesn't mean that either of you is solely at fault, it only suggests that there may have been a lack of sufficient communication and exchange between you in the past, which has now surfaced during this particular period. The paper note exchange between you and "a" was not the best way to solve this problem. At that time, both of you were deeply entrenched in negative emotions and unable to handle the problem calmly. If you want to resolve the issue with your friend "a" properly, I hope you can sit down calmly and have a heartfelt conversation, fully understanding each other and making the other person feel the bond between you. A good friendship also requires cultivation, finding and resolving issues, and having conflicts is not a big deal as long as they can be resolved, it can make both of you closer. As for the issue between the three of you: there is often the saying "in a friendship of three, there will always be one person extra" on the internet, but clearly, this is incorrect. The trust and attraction between the three of you are the key factors maintaining your friendship. Regarding friend "b's" attitude towards friend "a," I hope you can look at it objectively and calmly. Each person is an independent individual, and while you were attracted to each other to become friends, it doesn't mean that one person owns the other. The temporary conflicts between you and friend "a" are only your business and have nothing to do with others. Adjust your mindset, don't let this issue affect you too much. You can take the initiative to have a chat with "a" and express your attitude and proposed solutions, and see how "a" responds. Resolve the issue as soon as possible, whether it is continuing to be together or going your separate ways, both are good results. Don't feel troubled, after all, you have had good memories. In the journey of life, people come and go, some friends can accompany you to the end, some can accompany you for a certain distance, but they are all good companions on your life path, your wealth. Finally, I hope you can adjust your mindset as soon as possible and strive for the college entrance examination. Stay strong! Your personal mental health advisor around you. May my words bring you warmth! Also, thank you for reading, occasional passerby friends. Feel free to follow me and mark it as "Helpful"!

Dear friend: After reading your story, it seems that your friendship is very complex and fragile. Originally, your relationship was good, but it suddenly changed, and it's understandable that you find it difficult to cope with. Everyone hopes to get along harmoniously with the people around them, but because of the differences, it can be frustrating for you. I can empathize with you. Based on your words, it seems that A is indeed very sensitive. However, you don't agree with her perception of you, you can't accept her "sensitivity." You are close friends with B, and you secretly desire B's validation. Seeing their unwavering friendship only makes you feel more lonely and unhappy. There are a few methods to free yourself from this pain. [First], openly express your feelings and meet up with A. Confess your vulnerability and let her know how much you suffer when you see her notes. You can tell her about your discomfort within. Also, tell her what you truly want. Open up to B as well and share your feelings about their friendship, expressing your sense of loneliness. Let A and B understand you, and at the same time, you can release your stress and emotions. [Second], try the empty chair therapy. Pretend to be different people and sit in three different positions, representing you, A, and B respectively, then have a conversation. There will be two possible outcomes: reconciliation or an understanding that resolving the issue is impossible. Through this method, you can understand each other's situations, realize your true feelings, and relieve stress. [Third], acceptance and respect are important. Whether it's through an honest conversation or role-playing, we must accept reality and respect fate. Accepting reality means acknowledging that your classmate is a sensitive person. Even if you don't agree with her, it's her fate, and respecting her fate and personality is a form of respect. Whether it’s classmates, friends, or colleagues, we cannot change each other. Your upbringing has shaped you into who you are today, and it cannot be easily changed unless you choose to. Understand that in the world, there are both sensitive and non-sensitive people. There is no right or wrong, only existence, and they can coexist. Accept, respect, and forgive the differences and distinctions among everyone. [Fourth], leave it to fate. Inevitably, there will always be differences among people, and if certain areas cannot reach a consensus, you can entrust the problem to fate. After all, people have different limitations. Satisfying you may not satisfy others and vice versa. Therefore, for these unsolvable issues, you can leave it to fate and reduce some pressure on yourself. [Fifth], reflect on why you liked your classmate in the first place? When you initially considered her a friend, there must have been qualities that attracted you to her. Remembering these qualities can awaken the appreciation you initially had for her. Focusing on the benefits of the relationship can help reduce your sense of rejection and pain. Relationships always encounter obstacles. Trying to respect and accept, while letting go of the notion of right and wrong, will make it less difficult for you. The more you get to know someone, the more unexpected things you will discover. Therefore, respect and acceptance are lifelong lessons. I hope you won't be unhappy anymore! Your Friend: Audrey ---------------- Respecting, loving, uniting, and forgiving.️.

Hello, after carefully reading what you wrote, I can understand your feelings. In our middle and high school years, we also had some small conflicts among friends, and now looking back, it's really beautiful. Let me say this, I hope you can relax. In fact, these innocent friendships are especially precious in the future. Once you enter college, the pace will accelerate, and it will be difficult to find such pure emotions, so cherish them. Secondly, let me try to help you address your current concerns. Overall, I think the three of you have a good relationship and care about each other, otherwise you wouldn't write these words or talk about your troubles, and she wouldn't say those insincere things in anger. Sometimes our words and actions are actually disguises and defenses for our true thoughts. For example, Girl A cares a lot about you and feels uncomfortable when she sees you being close with Girl B. She has told you that she feels like she doesn't fit in, and maybe you didn't fully understand or you didn't think it was a big deal, so she angrily said she won't have meals with you anymore. In response to her words, you also wrote a strongly worded letter out of anger, which further fueled her anger... The root cause is still that you both care about each other, and actually have a good friendship, showing concern for each other, but neither is willing to lower their head and admit their true feelings, admit their jealousy, and admit that they care about each other. Instead, you both use the opposite approach to make each other guess. Since you said you are already in your senior year, you really shouldn't spend too much energy on these things, especially friends should not engage in inner conflicts. So, I think you can save your friendship and also improve your mood. When you calm down, you can take the opportunity to write a sincere letter to Girl A, expressing your true thoughts and asking about her true thoughts, such as how you can all get along better, or what specific actions she hopes for. She will be happier with that. People all want others to care about and respect them, so when you say such things, she should feel embarrassed to stay angry. Everyone can let go of their past grievances and focus on studying. I don't think you have any major problems with each other. Don't let these small things affect your relationship or your academics. Also, you can joke around privately and girls should also be a bit more assertive. Don't be too sentimental, just focus on studying and help each other, working towards your goal of getting into college together! Best wishes to all of you!

It seems that interacting with your classmates has brought you some troubles. Each individual is independent when we interact with others, so we all have different feelings. And everyone's feelings are important. I can see that because of the feedback from person A and person B, it triggers angry emotions in you. Have you ever thought about the reason why it makes you angry? Perhaps by seriously considering this question, you may find some answers.

question: We have been together for six years and have broken up over thirty times. Are my boyfriend and I suitable for each other?
description: We have been together for six years, and have broken up over thirty times. It was always me who initiated the breakups. He treated me very well, and being together felt very relaxed. However, we have different perspectives, especially when under a lot of pressure, we can't communicate and often blame and criticize each other, saying the most hurtful things. Every time I am going through a difficult time, our conflicts escalate into a full-blown cold war. This has made me lose hope in the future of our marriage, and I have countless sleepless nights, tears, and depression. Many of his habits are things I dislike, for example, we have argued countless times over him not carrying a backpack when going out, and we have broken up numerous times over it. It took him over two years to realize that carrying a bag for his girlfriend is not embarrassing and finally compromise. I feel like I have used my entire youth to teach him how to love a girl, and I am exhausted. I have given up countless times, but at the same time, I am moved by his persistence, insistence, and his limited companionship. I have realized more than once that our values are not aligned. Although there have been times when our values were aligned, they were mostly during times when we had time and energy for romance. As soon as the pressure builds up, no matter how many times we try, we cannot communicate. I want a relationship where we understand and respect each other. I am confused if we are truly suitable for each other. Is this relationship constantly draining me?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Love for six years, whenever there is pressure, you both can't face it together, but instead blame each other and project your own anxieties onto each other, expecting the other person to comfort you. You repeat the same communication pattern over and over again, without learning from it, without making any improvements, and without growing. You only resolve your emotions by breaking up and giving each other the cold shoulder. Is that right? This entangled relationship may satisfy your emotional needs. Some girls just like this kind of entangled relationship because only in this high-intensity emotional interaction can you feel a sense of existence, feel loved, and gain some sense of value. But ultimately, it's all because you lack love. This is the "emotional value" that the other person cooperates with you, or you both cooperate with each other. However, over time, this unbalanced, entangled, and exhausting relationship will eventually come to an end. When one party is unwilling to cooperate, the relationship will end. The reason why you can still be entangled now is because you are both still gaining something from this relationship. A good relationship can nourish each other and become a driving force to resist risks and pressures together. It seems that neither of you have grown, and you don't truly love each other. Both of you are more in love with yourselves. You may fight with the guy over not wanting him to carry your backpack, but you completely disregard his wishes, and that is not love. If you have the opportunity, girl, you really need to reflect on yourself from past experiences and look at your emotional patterns. Don't always blame it on mismatched values. Even if you don't end up with this person, only when you grow, can you attract the right person and have a good relationship. Grow first, and then pursue love! May you love yourself and find someone who truly loves you!

question: 23-year-old male, unable to follow the methods in books, unsure how to manage emotions.
description: I don't know how to deal with my emotions anymore. I've been trying to change and manage my emotions, but I still find myself frequently avoiding and feeling low, just like before. I want to know if it would be better to not overthink things too much now. Previously, my emotions had a big impact on my actions, and I didn't know how to manage them. So, I read books and tried some methods from them to manage my emotions, but the results were not satisfactory because I couldn't achieve them consistently. I realized that I tend to overthink things a lot, and I would often get scared of things I imagine before doing something, which leads me to frequently avoid them. My weight has been increasing since I started college due to anxiety. I don't know what to do anymore, and I would like to hear everyone's opinions.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand how you feel right now, and I want to give you a hug! Psychological research shows that extreme emotional reactions often stem from long-term anger and feelings of inferiority. This anger is not directed towards the outside world, but towards dissatisfaction with oneself and a sense of powerlessness to control the world. This internal chaos and loss of control are just one step away from affecting others. We must understand that life is full of disappointments, and it is impossible for a person to experience smooth sailing throughout their entire life without any dissatisfaction. Everyone has their bad days, but the seed of negativity lies dormant within us, waiting to stir up trouble. It silently lurks in the shadows, observing our thoughts, and once it finds the slightest opportunity to exploit, it will seize it and provoke a response, causing you to either become despondent or explode in anger, leading to actions that harm yourself and others. No matter what challenges you encounter, remember that life is short. Instead of letting your emotions control you, it is better to adjust your mindset, let go of absolutist perspectives, and try to approach everything with an optimistic attitude. Make yourself the master of your emotions and "smile in the face of adversity, and take losses lightly." Approach your emotions scientifically, distinguish between different types of emotions, manage them well, and live each day in happiness. Finally, I'll leave you with this phrase: "Smile in the face of adversity, and take losses lightly." Keep giving yourself a smile every day and persevere, because you are a winner...

question: The couple's relationship is not very strong, and their child has a rare disease. How should they face it?
description: The child is now less than 2 years old and has been diagnosed with a rare disease. The chances of a cure are very small. Every day, the child is going through changes, both physically and behaviorally. When alone, the child bursts into tears. The child's fate is really unfair and heartbreaking. I don't know how to go on every day, especially because my relationship with my husband is not very stable. The child's situation makes it even harder for me to face everything in life rationally.

answers.answer_text: In your description, I can see your confusion and helplessness. I hope to give you a warm and empowering hug. A rare disease in a child under the age of 2 has made you even more perplexed, especially when your relationship with your spouse was already unstable. Life is supposed to be full of joy, but for you, it has been full of hardships. While life is inherently equal, your child was born different from others. Heaven is fair, but also unfair. Right now, the most important thing may be for you to accept this fragile child from your heart and care for him with the best love, embodying your humanity and motherhood. We also know that love can work miracles in many cases. Like this story: Relatives and friends anxiously asked a mother, "Why does your child always daydream alone? Does he have a mental problem? Shouldn't you take him to the hospital for a check-up?" The mother firmly replied, "My child is perfectly fine. You don't understand. He is not daydreaming, he is contemplating. He will become an extraordinary university professor in the future." That young boy was Albert Einstein, one of the greatest scientists of the 20th century. Perhaps it was an unintentional remark from the parents, but for a young child, it was a massive affirmation and encouragement, filling the child's future with hope and making him more confident and brave to pursue his dreams... A few words from parents can truly impact a child's entire life! At the same time, consider nurturing your relationship with your husband. A loving foundation is essential for a child's happiness. It is recommended to seek support from a counselor for personal growth. I am here, and the world loves you.

question: Can I take leave if I work for a state-owned enterprise and suffer from depression?
description: I work at the power supply bureau, and due to work pressure and the separation from my wife and children, I have developed depression. Can I take sick leave from my company?

answers.answer_text: Hello there. In your situation, you can take a leave of absence. First, you need to understand the leave policy within your company. Since this involves personal privacy, it is best to resolve it privately and protect your personal privacy. It would be ideal to assess your recovery progress and severity. If you have been under a lot of work pressure recently, you can use your vacation time to adjust your mood, consider it as giving yourself a break, and allocate more time for yourself. Shift your focus and do many things that you didn't have time to do before due to work. The most important aspect of treating depression is to understand your own feelings. Spend more time with your family, experience the love and warmth in everyday life, which can help you recover and maintain a positive state of mind. Your health is the most important thing. After you have regulated your emotions, you can better embrace the future. Best wishes to you.

OP, hello. I hope my response can bring you some help. OP mentioned that they work at the power supply bureau and have developed depression due to work stress and being separated from their spouse and children. They are unsure if they can take sick leave from their company. Of course, you can. Depression is no different from any other illness. If you are sick, it's just like having pneumonia or any other physical illness. You need to take leave. Additionally, I suggest actively seeking treatment and not ignoring depression. Keep fighting and get better. I have a few suggestions for treating depression: 1. Don't hide it, and don't feel ashamed. Depression is a common illness in modern society. We should treat it just like we treat physical illnesses - actively take medication and seek treatment. 2. Alongside medication, consider psychological counseling to help with recovery. Depression can have psychological causes in addition to physiological ones. With the help of a counselor, you can receive professional guidance to manage emotions and adjust your thinking. 3. Connect with others who have experienced depression. When you are with others, you won't feel alone or isolated. You can search for the "Overcoming" public account on WeChat. It is a social support group for depression initiated by Dr. Zhang Jin. The members have either experienced depression or are currently undergoing treatment. You can gain a lot of related knowledge and support from there. 4. Stay connected with society.
