If possible, take some time to go home and talk to friends, have heartfelt conversations, awaken the inner strength, feel the vitality of society, and relieve the pressure in your heart. Keep persevering, and I wish you a speedy recovery!

Hello, first of all, I want to give you a warm embrace and let you feel that at this moment, you are not alone in facing all of this. "Depression" is a diagnosis term that we are familiar with and increasingly encountering in our lives, whether it is in state-owned enterprises or elsewhere, it can generally be understood to some extent. The truth is that everyone has a certain probability of experiencing depressive emotions, maybe due to external environmental pressures, or perhaps originating from physiological reasons... The causes are complex. For you, the pressures from work and being separated from your wife and children are definitely factors worth considering. However, before labeling yourself with this "label," it is necessary to go to the psychology department of a hospital for a proper diagnosis by a professional doctor. So, if you receive a diagnosis, you can ask the doctor if they can provide you with a sick leave note for a few days. With a sick leave note, it should be relatively smoother for you to take sick leave in the company. Of course, we also need to recognize the fact that the experiences of individuals may not completely resonate with each other. It is possible that the personnel of the company may not fully empathize with your feelings of depression. In this case, we may need to understand this and explain our situation with the sick leave note from the doctor, expressing our needs and feelings in a calm manner. Generally, companies have privacy and confidentiality settings regarding employees' health conditions, so there is no need to worry too much about it affecting yourself. Finally, I want to say that regardless of whether the company or others can understand, your inner feelings are the most important. "Depression" itself is actually neutral, like a small signal from within, telling you that perhaps your heart is a bit weary and needs some rest; perhaps your life is facing significant pressure and requires understanding and change. So, please give yourself more time to recover, more tolerance and acceptance. You will certainly be able to get through this period well. Hang in there!

Hello! Everyone has already analyzed a lot and analyzed it well. I would like to give you some new perspectives from my point of view, hoping it will be helpful to you: 1. If it is diagnosed as depression, depression is also a type of illness, and you can definitely take sick leave. However, if your depression is caused by being separated from your wife and child, a short-term sick leave may just be a temporary solution, while a long-term sick leave may mean that you will be in a low-income state for a long time. So, taking sick leave is only a temporary solution, and you need to think about what to do next, whether it's changing jobs or adjusting your own mental state to overcome it. This is a question you need to consider. 2. Is your work the type that can be done remotely? My husband and I are living abroad, and my husband also works in a distant place. However, considering the psychological state of our family and employees, the company allows us to work remotely as appropriate. Have you considered discussing with your employer about changing the current way of working based on your current mental condition?

Hello, it seems that you have summarized a lot of content in just a few sentences, and I can feel your inner embarrassment. Whether or not to take a leave of absence and how to do it are matters between you and the company's human resources department. It is worth paying attention to your depression caused by your work stress and the separation from your spouse and children. Do you feel more stressed from work or from being away from your spouse and children? The work stress is rated on a scale of 5, with higher scores indicating greater pressure. The same goes for the separation from your spouse and children, with ratings based on the same criteria. After self-evaluation, if you find that work stress is too high, consider whether it is due to interpersonal relationships or simply a heavy workload. If it is the pressure from being away from your spouse and children that is greater, then go back home, as life always involves weighing and making sacrifices.

Not necessarily a reply, and I'm not sure if it will help you, but it's quite a coincidence, our situations are nearly the same, except I'm currently unmarried. We both work for the power company, work away from home, and suffer from anxiety and depression. The depression assessment indicates moderate depression, and I've even had suicidal thoughts. I've been working for a year and a half, and this state started in August of this year (I changed positions in August and often receive late-night phone calls and messages). I completely broke down last week and talked to my family about it. My parents agreed that I should change jobs (because I work in a city not far from their hometown in the northwest). Currently, finding another job in my field is not a problem, and I could also take the civil service exam. The only downside is that the benefits will be lower, probably around 60-70% of what I currently earn, and I will lose the company pension. However, I value my health more than money. I would rather choose good health than be miserable every day, eventually getting sick, both physically and mentally. Not long ago, I had unexplained stomach pain and would vomit when I got angry. The tests couldn't find any reasons. I'm not ready to quit my job just yet, and I also considered whether I could take some time off from work for my depression. However, I realized that I haven't gone to the hospital for a check-up, so I can't be certain if it's depression or just a low mood (I've looked up information and it seems more like a low mood). Also, because I'm unmarried, there will definitely be situations like yours in the future, and I will probably settle in the provincial capital city in order to have better healthcare and education. So, for my current situation, my plan is to take the civil service exam while still employed, and if I pass, I will quit my job. Also, I've become a bit shameless, once I finish my work, I don't work overtime, and if others are willing to work extra hours, I let them. I utilize my free time to study and try not to get caught up in the competitiveness. This week, it's only Tuesday, but I already feel much better. They are working overtime on the weekends, but my work is done, so I don't go back to the office (my current position is a special one). I suggest you consider carefully what you want and what is most important to you. Also think about the possibility of either you or your wife transferring jobs or one of you quitting and finding work in the other's location. Consider which option would be more beneficial for the whole family, including financially and in terms of work intensity. I also noticed that you have children, so you need to think about their education as well. No matter what, the fact that we are actively seeking advice indicates that our psychological state hasn't deteriorated completely. Keep going! There will always be a solution.

Hello OP, first of all, I understand and sympathize with your situation. I want to give you a big hug and let you feel the warmth of the world. Regarding the question of whether you can take leave, I think it depends on the severity of your depression. If it is seriously affecting your work, studies, or if you need a vacation to recover and adjust yourself, then it is necessary. However, if it's only mild and not too severe, perhaps you can try to rely on daily social interactions or other external forces to help yourself recover. After all, depression can vary in severity. If you don't take it seriously from the beginning, it will only worsen over time, which is not beneficial to your health and work. So, the first thing you need to assess right now is how severe your depression is. Have you sought professional consultation or evaluation for your depression? If your depression has already severely affected your studies, work, and life, then as long as you provide a report showing your condition, I believe your company will grant you leave. After all, as the number of people with depression increases, more attention will be given to this issue, and there will be more caring and support for this group. I wish you happiness and joy, OP.

You want to take leave and reunite with your wife and children, but you're a bit worried, as if you're afraid it will affect your work or that your leave will not be understood or approved due to depression. Generally speaking, mild to moderate depression can be treated while working, but severe depression often hinders daily work performance. Depression is gradually becoming better known, and if your supervisor has some understanding of depression, they may approve your leave and allow you to take the time off to recover before returning to work. However, there are still some people who cannot understand the suffering of those with depression and may think it's just a matter of not being able to handle things or making a fuss out of nothing. If you encounter such a leader, you may encounter some trouble if you use depression as a reason for leave, which could potentially affect your future career development. While work is important, so is your health. Only with mental and physical well-being can you perform better at work. If you feel that your mental and physical condition is not good and you need time to recover, you must take timely rest and seek treatment. Sometimes, the occurrence of physical and mental illnesses is our body's silent expression, revealing some needs that are difficult to express in words. While the work stress and being apart from your wife and children that you mentioned may indeed be the practical causes of depression, these practical factors are just part of the many factors that can lead to illness, and they can be adjusted and changed. For a better recovery, you may need the help of a psychologist to find your inner causes and to grow and change.

question: Whenever I hear bad news, I always hope that there is someone who will make jokes with me.
description: I always thought that I was accepted into No.1 High School, but on the day when the acceptance letter arrived, my mother called the teacher to ask whether I was accepted into No.1 High School or No.3 High School. The teacher said No.3 High School. At that moment, I really hoped that the teacher would call again and say that they had read it wrong, and that I was accepted into No.1 High School.

answers.answer_text: ～I want to give you a warm hug～ I understand your feelings very well. I also feel the same way. When I hear news that is not ideal, I hope others will tell me that it is not true. But actually, these are just excuses for us to "escape". Avoiding something doesn't mean that it will happen again. So no matter what happens, we have to learn to accept it. It's normal to feel upset when we encounter undesirable things or results. But since we can't change it, after feeling upset for a while, let's quickly tidy up our emotions and accept the result. Maybe we don't need to imagine the unexpected result as so terrible. It is a result and also a new beginning. Just like being admitted to the third high school, it will be your new start. As long as you study diligently and complete the tasks, you will ultimately achieve the same good result.

question: Should I get a divorce if my husband and child disrespect me by being defiant or ignoring me?
description: My child is ten years old, and recently they have been using harsh language to confront me, saying things like "Aren't you annoying?" or "So what if I don't do my homework?" The same words, when said by my husband, are followed by immediate compliance from the child. I personally analyze this as an influence from my husband who has always lacked respect towards me. He often rolls his eyes or ignores what I say. Even when the child was young, they would tell me that they felt I liked their father but he didn't like them. My husband often finds fault with me in front of the child. On the other hand, I show more respect for my husband's opinions and often speak positively about him in front of the child. I don't know if this environment has caused the child's attitude towards me and I don't know how to handle it. Should I get a divorce in this kind of family?
keywords: Marriage, marriage concept, divorce, marriage management

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. In your usual married life, your husband always disrespects you, which leads to your 10-year-old child constantly challenging you with strong language. I can feel your helplessness in not being respected in this family. It's good to know that you are making efforts to solve this problem. This matter needs to be considered on a case-by-case basis. Your relationship with each other is actually not bad, but he doesn't know how to express himself or communicate with you. Your husband doesn't love you that much, so he shows impatience and blames you in daily life. If it's the first situation, you need to communicate with him, tell him your thoughts, and discuss together to both make changes. I believe that through your joint efforts, this situation will definitely improve. You and your husband need to educate your child together and teach him to respect his parents. If it's the second situation, if you don't want to continue with the current life, you can choose to divorce. After all, life is short, and you should choose a happier life. Best wishes.

The one lacking personal charm is you, and the one being brazen, rough, and ignorant is your husband. Try doing the following: 1. Stop showing your respect and tolerance towards your husband in front of the children. 2. Develop shared interests with your son and use the advantage of adult thinking to appropriately challenge and defeat him, gaining his admiration. 3. Speak less and do more, avoiding opportunities for your husband to ignore you. Good luck.

question: Reading motivational and psychology books, what can psychological counseling really help me with?
description: I have read some books on success, inspiration, and psychology. For example, many books talk about how great it is to become a confident person. But even after reading them, I don't find them helpful. Do I not already know that I need to become a confident, optimistic, and brave person? I just don't know how to become one. However, the books don't provide any methods. Do I need to figure it out on my own? I have some issues in my mind. I know their causes, but I don't know how to solve them. Will seeking counseling help me find solutions? Or ultimately, do I have to rely on myself? Am I too dependent on mental counseling?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, student growth, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I can feel your confusion and worries from your description. It is true that many things we are not unaware of their importance, but knowing is one thing, and being able to do it is another. Sometimes we may even encounter a situation where we know the solution, but still can't do it. This is another kind of pain. Psychological counseling can first help us understand the reasons behind our current state, such as the lack of self-confidence, optimism, courage, and so on that you mentioned. There are also many different schools of thought in psychological counseling, and the approaches of different schools are also different. Some schools may help you adjust from a relational perspective, while others may focus on cognitive adjustment. But the general working principle is that the counselor and the client work together. In psychological counseling, the counselor is not only a guide or savior. In addition to cooperation, the client also needs to put in a great deal of effort and explore and discover together with the counselor, to achieve self-awareness and change. Therefore, psychological counseling does not solely rely on the counselor, nor is it for the client to solve their own problems alone. It is a collaborative work based on a therapeutic alliance to achieve counseling goals.

Hello, classmate. In fact, self-confidence means "believing in yourself". When you see a book and think it's terrible, but others tell you it's a good book, what would you do? Would you doubt yourself, make yourself surrender, and force yourself to read the book? When you start doing something, do you hear a voice deep inside you implying that you definitely can't do it, and then feel a bit panicked and anxious? If you have just realized this, then you are still in the first stage: doubting yourself, not recognizing yourself, feeling inferior. In the second stage, you will start to resent, throw tantrums while studying, learn to complain, cry, feel uncomfortable, and feel that no one loves you in this world. Finally, you will enter the third stage and begin to acknowledge your own opinions, contemplate your existence and value. That being said, you need to personally experience and perceive these three stages. Many people stop at the first stage and believe that they are just such terrible people. Although I understand this concept, I just can't do it. Psychological counseling and reading can help speed up the entire process, making you realize that something is not right, "Why am I so terrible when we are all human beings? Why can others do it but not me? This is unfair." I understand how you feel. There are various psychology books, success literature, and motivational books on the market, some good and some not so much, full of a lot of inspirational stories and anxiety-inducing content. Of course, these books have specific target audiences and there are people who like them and need them. As a reader, you need to select books that suit you and distinguish which ones are useful and which ones are not. If your family upbringing is terrible and you are demanded too much by your parents, often sacrificing yourself to meet others' requests, if you need to vent and let out your anger, "Wu Zhihong's book is a great outlet. She will tell you: Yes, these parents are indeed terrible parents." And if you want to find a way to deal with demanding parents, teachers, and elders, you need to read "The Gaslight Effect" because you are being manipulated like a puppet. If you feel inferior but are unsure where your inferiority comes from, Adler's "Inferiority Complex" is a great answer. However, Adler's solutions may leave you puzzled, as he actually says: Love others is to love oneself! At this point, you can read "The Courage to Be Disliked" by Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga. It provides specific case studies to address your doubts. If you are a good child but feel repressed, "Not Good" by Kato Daisan can help you understand your problems, then start thinking about whether you should rebel a little. However, when you rebel, you will find yourself lost because after denying everything before, you will discover that you feel exhausted and have no direction. At this time, Viktor Frankl's "Man's Search for Meaning" can help you acknowledge your own meaning and value. The above are books I have read and found useful for myself. Of course, the effect of reading is subjective and varies from person to person. Each book has its own specific audience. If you don't like a book, please don't continue reading it and accept your own point of view: it's just not suitable for you. Please trust your own judgment. Psychological counseling is similar to reading. You need to find a therapist you like, let go of your guard, trust and acknowledge them, so that your treatment will be more effective. The whole process is painful and lengthy. You need to struggle with the voices in your mind over and over again, work hard to affirm yourself, and resist with all your might the voices saying "you're not good" or "you're terrible". But as long as you are willing to start, your efforts will definitely be rewarded.

Hello! After reading your question, I think that while you are reading books, you are also reflecting and have your own confusion. Why is it that despite reading so many books, you still can't feel confident? When we read books, different books provide us with new perspectives and ways of thinking, allowing us to explore new things. Some books share personal experiences that we can relate to. We may also compare and categorize information to apply to ourselves. So why is it that reading so many books doesn't increase our confidence? Reading a book to gain new perspectives and ways of thinking is just the first step. Once we understand what we want or who we want to become, it is simply a goal. Next, we need to understand the benefits of confidence. While we can see the positive aspects, we have never experienced being a confident person and how it can change our lives. For example, when you lack confidence, you may be in a state of self-doubt, worrying about not doing well and feeling inadequate. In this case, try completing a small task and recognize or reward yourself emotionally or materially. Pay attention to how it makes you feel. You can also try telling yourself "I'm going to doubt myself" whenever you feel the need to criticize yourself. Instead, focus on the task itself and think about how you can do it well. Notice how this shift in mindset feels. Psychological counseling can also be helpful. In a communication and interpersonal interactive relationship, your suffering and lack of confidence need to be seen and understood. Allowing yourself to express these negative feelings can provide a sense of relief. From there, you can explore the reasons for these negative states and develop strategies to overcome them. It is a process of personal growth in terms of emotional experiences. I hope my answer can help you. Best of luck in encountering the best version of yourself on your growth journey!

Hello, why do some people say "knowing so much but not living a good life"? This is somewhat similar to your confusion. Wang Yangming once proposed the concept of "the unity of knowledge and action", and some people say "the furthest distance in the world is the distance between knowing and doing". Regardless of how it is expressed, I believe it is relatively understandable. Many contents in books belong to the knowledge category, and many knowledge needs to be transformed into skills in order to be useful to me. During this transformation, persistence is also required to develop the right habits. In this process, there is a major factor called mindset. Therefore, "The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People" summarized such a formula: KASH, a person who wants to succeed (or grow) needs to continuously grow in terms of knowledge, attitude, skills, and habits. Reading books or seeking psychological counseling cannot help you establish a stable habit because only you know whether you will do what the book says or what the counselor advises after putting down the books or leaving the counseling room. For example, there must be books that say improving self-confidence can be done like this: start by doing small things or things you are good at, experience the feeling of success, and then you will establish the belief that "I can do it". Then keep challenging yourself to continuously improve your abilities. However, what exactly are the "small things" that you are good at or can try to do, the books or counselors may not be able to tell you. Some people may feel that cooking can give them a sense of accomplishment, some people may think it's a certain sport, and some may be public speaking... So, to turn the knowledge from books or the counseling room into your own skills, you have to do it yourself and persist. I hope the above suggestions will inspire you. Thank you.

If you come here to ask for advice, of course, I would recommend that you read books on psychology. I enjoy psychology, and it has brought me many benefits. However, everyone is different, what I want may not be what you like, and what you want may not be what I know. What you should read depends on what goals you want to achieve. If you want to become a confident person, you need to understand your uniqueness and believe in your abilities. If you want to become an optimistic person, you need to love life. As for being brave, you need to have the courage to take responsibility. I have read some books on psychology and inspiration, and I have also read some books on communication. They can be helpful at times and guide us when we reflect later, preventing us from going astray. But saying they are not useful doesn't have much impact, after all, our emotions can vary when reading new books, and we may not fully understand or believe them. The most important thing is that the true essence of someone's thoughts cannot be fully expressed in a book, that is called tacit knowledge, and it is difficult to express in words. If you like reading, let me recommend a book to you. It's not about inspiration, nor can it be classified as psychology. It feels more like philosophy. It's about the philosophy of love, titled "The Art of Loving" by Erich Fromm. The advantage of this theme is that even if we understand a little, it can be helpful to us, regardless of whether we use it in everyday life or not. Fromm, from a dialectical perspective, tells us what love is and what it is not, what mature love is and what it is not, how love accompanies our growth, the development of love throughout history, and its manifestations in the present, among many theories of love. And in the end, there are practical methods. This book has been very helpful to me. I recently found a good physical copy, and I have read it more, gaining even more insights. I recommend it to almost everyone. If you have read books on psychology and inspiration, this one should complement them and have a one plus one greater than two effect. If you like my answer, be sure to give it a thumbs up. Remember my recommendation, it will be helpful to you. I wish you confidence and humility, optimism and openness, bravery and skill, becoming someone who is truly capable of love.

Hello, I will try to answer your questions. First, about methods to build confidence. There are two ways, internal and external. Externally, we can observe confident people and imitate their behavior. For example, walking with a straight posture, head held high, and a confident pace. Speaking with strength, expressing opinions, looking others in the eye, and being at ease. Being able to get along with colleagues and friends while maintaining one's own personality. Internal confidence is the true confidence. It comes from self-awareness and personal growth. Recognizing strengths and weaknesses, facing one's own shortcomings, and maintaining a balanced attitude toward others. Finally, regarding the role of counseling in personal growth. Counseling is the process where trained professionals use psychological techniques to assist individuals in resolving their psychological issues. The keyword here is "assistance." The change comes from you, and the counselor is just there to assist you. The goal of cognitive-behavioral counseling is to help individuals become their own counselors in the future. I hope this answer can provide some guidance and inspiration for you.

Hello, your question is very good, just like you said, "in the end, it's up to oneself"! The biggest difference between psychological counseling and studying on your own is that, after learning some methods, gaining knowledge, and adjusting cognition, you can gradually establish a new mode of interaction with others and yourself through continuous practice and confirmation in genuine contact with a real person. It's like giving yourself an internship period. A psychotherapist will provide a "warm, supportive, non-judgmental" and safe environment in their work, helping the individual change step by step, and at the same time, assisting the individual in gradually applying these new experiences to real life. The above is my personal point of view, for reference only.

After reading your description, it shows that you have thought it through seriously and have indeed approached the practical application level rather than just staying at the theoretical level to think about the issue. This is a very good idea. If I tell you that self-confidence or inferiority is actually a pseudoproposition, a set of words constructed, I don't know what you would think? And within the field of psychology, each school interprets the meaning of inferiority and self-confidence differently. So, which interpretation are you willing to accept? Generally speaking, self-confidence or inferiority is the result of positive reinforcement and negative reinforcement. In the end, the operable part of this theory is to start from the little things in your life. If you think you can do it and have no problem doing it, then you have self-confidence. That's what self-confidence is all about. So, it's right for you to apply your thoughts to methods. You just need to approach the problem with a method, then test and verify it to see if it works for you. In the end, you will have your own experience, thoughts, and thinking patterns. That's progress. I'm actually saying all of this for one useful point, which is to start with the things around you that you still feel able to do and gradually do them to the extreme, just like challenging levels. You can let go of the words self-confidence and inferiority and directly approach the specific problems you are facing. This will give you a tangible object in front of you, not empty or vague.

question: This morning, I finally lost the only stranger who was close to me because of my indifference.
description: Ihatetheworld. Only when experiencing insomnia can one truly understand their own heart, with all the black venomous snakes creeping out, like zombies resurrecting, gnashing their teeth and claws, vying with one another. Unexplainable anger, rage, fleeing for one's life, speechless, only left with foul language, only left with wickedness. In this world, power and money reign supreme, no one gives a shit about me, no one to rely on. Only oneself can become strong. What does it mean when they say poor people have sensitive and inferior thinking, while rich people have honest, peaceful, and optimistic thinking? What is one's worldview? What does it mean when they say I haven't formed the correct perspective on things? What does it mean to be abnormal? Life is so absurd. What is warmth? Nobody fucking cares about me. Am I selfish? Can I not care about others? Speechless. Speechless. Poured my heart out on an app, no one pays attention to me. Participated in a topic, "What did you give up in 2020?" I wrote two words, "speaking". In this cynical world, why would anyone give it a thumbs-up? Thumbs-up? Who invented that? I'm just flamboyant and selfish. I'm just a jerk. I'm just anti-social. I want to kill people. I hate you all. My indifference drove away the only person who approached me, she bid farewell to me this morning. I built up high walls, no one comes near. Once someone tries to connect, it becomes awkward and stiff. I have lost the ability to love. "Notes from the Underground" "The Piano Teacher."

answers.answer_text: No, you don't lose the ability to love. Love and being loved are instinctual for humans, they don't need to be learned. The reason why you may not be able to love others is possibly due to some social barriers that prevent you from loving and caring for others. We need to understand that our past experiences of being disliked can affect us, but it only has power over our present behavior if we allow it. We can start making changes from small details in the present, by being proactive in showing kindness and goodwill to others, even with simple gestures like a smile! The more gentle our tone, the more likely it is to be reciprocated with kindness. Of course, we can also solve specific problems by practicing and preparing in advance (people with social barriers are usually very nervous and afraid, the core fear being the fear of being rejected, laughed at, or not being accepted). You can list the situations where you may feel social anxiety, such as meetings, events, speaking engagements, or presentations. You can rehearse the entire process and imagine which points make you most anxious. How do you plan to resolve and care for yourself? Lastly, consider what the worst possible outcome might be, and how you would handle it. After attempting these steps, you can summarize the results as follows: 1. What did I do well or make progress on in this situation? 2. What areas can be improved? 3. How can I do better next time? By thinking of targeted coping strategies, you will naturally display your instinct to love and be loved. This way, you can improve and grow in every social experience.

question: I have never experienced a complete love, what is missing deep inside me?
description: I'm 24 years old this year, and from my early teens until now, I have never had a complete love experience or had a girlfriend. When I was young, my family would treat me well one moment and then scold and hit me the next, which led to my habit of overeating when I get angry. During middle school, I became overweight and felt that many people were making fun of me. Later, I started to lose weight, and there was a girl I found very beautiful. I told my friends about her and they encouraged me to confess my feelings to her. I did so through writing a letter, but all I got back was a letter from her with a pig drawing and a rejection. I felt really responsible and down at that time. Since then, I have never truly confessed my feelings to anyone, whether online or in real life. I always think in my heart that I will meet them again when I become a bit thinner. Later on, besides being in a severe car accident, I felt that I cannot have any regrets. But I realized that I tend to get emotional when the relationship is not yet confirmed. I'm always worried that they will leave, and if they mention their ex-boyfriends, I feel a bit unhappy and unfair. If they don't answer my calls or messages, I start to write long paragraphs. I know it's my own problem, but this issue has been bothering me for a long time.

answers.answer_text: Hello there~ Sending you a big hug. I can sense your sadness from your words and I can understand how you feel. It's okay, everything will slowly get better. Let me share a bit of my perspective with you, hoping it can help you. Regardless of anything, please believe in yourself. The main confusion for the author seems to be about what is missing deep inside their heart. I think it might be due to their childhood family environment leading to emotional eating and weight gain, which resulted in a lack of confidence due to being teased. Here, I want to share a quote that I really like: "The reason why humans can accomplish is because they believe that they can." So no matter what you encounter, the first thing you need to do is believe in yourself. The famous Dunning-Kruger effect states that the strong may not necessarily be winners, but eventually the winners will be those who have confidence. In other words, if you only accept the best, then what you will ultimately get is often the best. As long as you have confidence, your ability to succeed in something is 85% determined by your attitude and 15% by your intelligence. Therefore, a person's success depends on whether they are confident. If someone is insecure, that insecurity will strangle their intelligence and wear down their willpower. I feel really sorry for what the author experienced in their childhood, but now we have grown up and there are many things that we have control over. Let go of the past and start becoming confident from now on. Tell yourself every day, "I am the best." Constantly use positive affirmations to motivate yourself, and I believe you will gradually build up your self-confidence. Be brave and try new things. Gu Cheng once said, "You don't want to plant flowers because you don't want to see them wither away bit by bit. Yes, in order to avoid the end, you avoid all beginnings." In fact, some things need to be tried in order to know the results. Even though you were rejected when confessing your feelings before, it's okay. The path of love is always bumpy, and it is because of this that love is so desirable. Everyone has their own opinions, and just because you were rejected before doesn't mean you will be rejected now and in the future. There will always be someone who recognizes your worth and comes running towards you in the vast ocean of people. So, dear author, be brave from now on. Take one small step at a time, and eventually it will become a big step. Meeting someone you like is not easy, don't miss out. Even if you get rejected, you won't regret it because at least you tried. Make a plan and strive to become excellent. From your description, it seems like you don't like it when the other person brings up their previous partner and you are afraid that they won't respond to you. This might be due to a lack of security and to some extent, it might be because you care too much about the other person, leading to feelings of anxiety. Try to focus on yourself and become strong. Take care of your body. Pursue your interests and find your own strengths and passions. Learn to love yourself and others. It's not to say that you are not already great, but there is always room for improvement, as no one is perfect. Because excellent people are attractive to each other, in this way, perhaps you won't worry about them leaving. Lastly, I hope you can get out of your current state as soon as possible and meet a girl who only comes for you. Good luck!

Hello. What you lack in your heart is love, which has led to a lack of self-confidence and a lack of security. It may be due to being scolded and inconsistent behavior from your family when you were young, which made you feel unloved. Later on, gaining weight and being mocked by others, even being cruelly rejected by the girl you liked, caused a lack of self-confidence. These emotional experiences also made you lack a sense of security when it comes to relationships, always worrying that they will leave or stop liking you. To address your smaller issue, if you can't receive love from others, you should first learn to love yourself and make peace with yourself. If it's your weight that causes your lack of self-confidence, then lose weight. You will love yourself when you become thinner. Learn to appreciate the qualities you have. If you are not aware of your own strengths, develop them through learning, such as being good at fashion or being empathetic. When you achieve something, remember to praise yourself by saying "I am really awesome!" When you make others happy, praise yourself with "I am a little sun." This is an expression of your value in life, giving positive influence to others. Life is not just about romantic love. If you are not yet sure how to love someone, you can start by making friends. Make more friends, and with guys, it's more about who you are as a person, your inner self. In most cases, it won't make you feel inferior and may even help you slowly build self-confidence. Also, guys tend to value brotherhood, which might make you feel loved. When you are in a relationship, focus your sensitivity on your girlfriend, like sensitively noticing her small emotions and then cheering her up. Remember, not answering calls or messages may not be intentional, so don't blow small things out of proportion and don't overthink. If you repeatedly cause emotional conflicts with your girlfriend, it may exhaust her and harm your relationship. Don't worry, you are only 24 years old, the future is still long, and you don't have to rush into relationships. Solve your problems step by step. When you become confident and outstanding, you won't be afraid of not being liked by anyone. When you learn to love yourself, you will be able to love others well, and it will be easier to navigate relationships. Keep going, the future is promising! I hope this solves your confusion. Good luck!

Hello, the experiences you've had in life are truly heartbreaking. Sending you a warm hug. It must have been tough and conflicting to receive both love and abuse from your family during your childhood. This led to emotional distress and binge eating, causing weight gain and ridicule from peers. At an age when one begins to desire love, you bravely confessed your feelings only to receive a derogatory painting of a pig and a rejection. This left you feeling low and hurt, and you decided to protect yourself from further heartache by not expressing your feelings anymore. Experiencing a car accident made you realize the importance of living without regrets and made you become emotionally volatile and anxious about your loved ones leaving. In a relationship, neither your family nor friends provided enough support or care, leading to feelings of insecurity, instability, and a lack of self-confidence. You both long for and fear love, and don't quite know how to navigate relationships. Firstly, it's important to accept yourself and embrace all your various states. Whether you're overweight or thin, have confidence in yourself. If you're not satisfied with your appearance, you can exercise and work on improving it, but remember that self-acceptance is key. If you don't love yourself, how can you expect others to love and accept you? Secondly, try adjusting your attitude toward social interactions. Don't rush to make commitments; focus on developing social skills and maintaining harmonious relationships with others. Learn to regulate your emotions. Lastly, try to establish harmony and a sense of belonging within your family. I hope everything goes well for you.

Hello, One Heart Ming, One Word Knows You. In your description, I wonder if you have noticed that you have set up a contrast between "me" and "them". "Worrying that they would leave", "They bring up their ex-boyfriends", "They don't answer the phone", "They don't like..." indicates that deep down, you haven't fully accepted the individual traits of "them", and consciously or unconsciously, you have created a disconnect between yourself and "them". This is the first issue I noticed. Typically, in emotional counseling, visitors may be entangled in past emotions with a particular person, but your example is quite unique. You classify "them" as a group, disregarding the individual traits of these girls, and placing yourself in an oppositional position to them. 1. "Since my early teens until now, I haven't experienced a complete love." From this, it can be seen that you have had relationships quite early on, but you emphasize "not a single complete one", which I do not fully understand. In your opinion, what constitutes a "complete love"? 2. When I was young, my family treated me well but also beat me, which made me angry and indulge in binge eating. Then you describe a failed confession in junior high school due to weight issues, and you describe it quite clearly, indicating that this incident had a deep impact on you and influenced your view on love in the future. "Wait until I lose weight before meeting" indicates the stimulation this incident had on you, leading to a lack of self-confidence and the fear of meeting. This can also be understood. Indeed, what that junior high school girl did was a bit excessive; she did not consider your feelings. However, you should also try to understand her. At that time, she was just an immature junior high school student who didn't know how to protect others' self-esteem. But she had the right to reject you; she just chose the wrong way to refuse and shouldn't have mocked you. When you realize that the fault in that incident did not lie with you, please also understand yourself and free yourself from the past. Do not punish yourself because of others' mistakes and let them affect your future happiness. 3. You asked, "I want to know what is lacking in my heart". I want to say: first and foremost, you lack confidence and self-love. In matters of emotions, only when you are filled with love and self-confidence can you distribute the excess love to others. Otherwise, if you don't even have enough love for yourself, how can you give it to others or share it? Firstly, you need to reconcile with yourself and establish self-confidence. Secondly, you have projected the resentment towards that girl from the past onto the girls you have encountered later. Even before starting a proper relationship, you stick the label of "untrustworthy" on them, categorizing each lively, lovely, distinct individual as "them", becoming your imaginary enemies. Just think about it, aren't these girls also being unfairly treated? Lastly, you need to express your confusion more openly. Sometimes, just speaking out the problem is already solving half of it, because you have already started to face and want to change. The counselor will accompany you to untie the knot together. Good luck, I wish you can untie this knot soon, face yourself and the girls truthfully, and have a beautiful romantic relationship.

Hello! Your upbringing and childhood experiences are really sad, sending you a virtual hug! I believe that you have developed a sense of inferiority since childhood, which is why you tend to overthink and find it hard to believe in a happy relationship. Don't worry, during adolescence, regardless of whether one is a boy or a girl, their mental maturity is not fully developed. She doesn't realize the extent of the hurt she caused you, so you need to let go of this situation. She simply doesn't know how to appreciate your qualities. But you will eventually meet someone who understands and appreciates your inner and outer beauty. This is not an empty statement, it is the truth. Speaking from my own experience, during my adolescence, I liked someone who played with emotions and tried to get involved with me despite having a partner. This made me distrust the opposite sex until I met my first love at the age of 23, who gradually made me believe in love again. So, don't be afraid. Regardless of height, weight, or appearance, you have the right to be loved. You mentioned feeling unsettled when your girlfriend talks about her exes, but there's no need to feel that way. I can relate to this feeling, as I also used to mind my partner's past relationships. However, I could feel that he was fully committed to me. The past is the past and cannot be changed. We are moving forward, so there's no need to compete with someone who is no longer in the picture. Be more confident, you have your own strengths, and you can engage in various activities to improve yourself, becoming more and more outstanding. As you become less anxious and more confident and happy, perhaps the right person will appear. Best wishes!

Perhaps the main issue here is to accept yourself more, feel proud of yourself, so that no one's rejection can truly hurt you, because you are very aware of your own worth and not swayed by others' standards. Another thing is to see the sweet side of emotions, the caring and loving side of the other person, so that you won't be constantly affected by negative events. For example, if the other person doesn't answer your calls or reply to your messages, do they really not like you? What are the signs of care and affection from the other person? Can you recall the sweet experiences you had before? Maybe after finding evidence, you'll feel more at ease. There are many possible reasons why the other person may not reply to messages, such as being busy or not being interested in the topic. Maybe you've had experiences of rejection in the past, which made you feel deeply hurt, but that was just one girl, and being rejected doesn't necessarily mean you're not good enough; perhaps the other person just doesn't like your type. Not everyone in the world can like you, and similarly, there must be someone who likes you; we exist in that middle ground, where some people like us while others don't, but it doesn't have much to do with our essence. If a girl draws a pig, it might be unintentional, but because you're particularly sensitive about your body shape, you feel she's mocking you. Is the content of her reply mocking or hurting you? Or is it simply a rejection? If you can treat yourself or others with more goodwill, maybe the other person's intention was unintentional or just a joke, and you won't be so easily hurt. The main character is still very young, and there aren't many people at this age who have had proper relationships, especially for introverted people. This doesn't mean there's something wrong with yourself. When you're ready, you can have a serious relationship that can lead to marriage, isn't that romantic? My friend didn't start dating until she was 30, and then she got married directly, without experiencing the pain of heartbreak, and she's very happy now. Another friend is in her forties and still single, but she has many friends and her own career, which doesn't hinder her from living happily. The most important thing is that they are both forgiving toward themselves and don't harshly judge themselves for not meeting so-called societal standards. In this state, whether or not they have a partner doesn't really matter, they are already happy enough. The main character can focus more on themselves, do things they like, enrich their inner world, and maybe they won't concentrate all their attention on others. When someone doesn't reply to your messages, you can choose to do other things, like reading, exercising, etc., to distract your attention, and maybe things will get better.

Let's analyze the problems. When you were a child, your parents' discipline made you feel helpless, and your only way of emotional release was through overeating (now you can develop more ways, such as listening to music, exercising, and writing a diary). Due to body image issues, you have been hurt and left with trauma (you can write a letter to your younger self and to the person who hurt you). I feel that the emotional fluctuations before establishing a relationship are partly due to lack of confidence and partly because you have never been in a relationship and are bothered by their "ex-boyfriends". First of all, if they are "ex-boyfriends", it means they are not suitable. Secondly, don't think that their past relationships are to your disadvantage. Truly liking someone means wishing that they have also been cared for and accompanied by someone before you appeared. And don't think that not having had a girlfriend is something embarrassing. Everyone has different standards for choosing a partner. How many people are not "left behind" but simply "haven't felt that connection". You can boost your confidence from other aspects. Insecurity can be seen as a driving force for human progress. Success in career or academics may also help you move forward in relationships. Think about it, ask your heart, what do you want to do? I recommend the book "Inferiority Complex and Its Overcoming."

You deserve to be loved and to have a wonderful love. It's not that you don't want love, but the experience of being beaten when you were young has left a shadow in your heart. You seek comfort through binge eating, which is emotional eating. The only confession you made ended in humiliation, so you, who were already hurt, prefer to wrap yourself up and no longer reveal your true emotions. So you have a deep sense of unworthiness. Let go of your self-judgment; being beaten when you were young was not your fault. It's very likely that your father or mother went through the same thing when they were young. Let go of self-blame. Beautiful things and pursuing love are rights that belong to each of us. When you accept yourself more and regain your confidence, believe that love is waiting for you in the next moment. Keep going.

Growth is about finding a breakthrough point, changing trajectory, spiraling upward, and becoming a better version of oneself. Personal Journey: The author, who is 24 years old, desires love but has never had a complete romantic relationship or a girlfriend. The author has experienced rejection and humiliation in a previous romantic pursuit, which has deeply hurt and stayed with them. Since then, the author has not sought love again but still longs for it. Later, the author was involved in a serious car accident, and realizing the importance of not having regrets, they gathered the courage to start a romantic relationship. However, the author often worries about being abandoned, is sensitive to their partners' actions, and tends to overthink. Any deviation from the author's expectations would lead to self-blame and confusion. Social Circle: In the realm of romance, the author always finds themselves in a strong sense of control over their partner but lacks a strong sense of security. They pursue love due to their longing for it but feel that they cannot fully control their partner, who has their own life, leading the author into deep conflict. Changing Trajectory: Understanding needs: The author still has a strong desire for love but has never experienced it. They need to understand what the other party needs in terms of love and form their own ideal image of a partner based on popular preferences. Making changes: The author realizes that they are slightly overweight and need to develop self-discipline. They must challenge and change themselves according to their desired image. Trying different social circles: The author should try different social circles, establish connections with people, and interact with different groups, thereby expanding their social network and gradually building confidence and opening up their personality. Understanding needs - Making changes - Trying different social circles - Changing trajectory - Spiraling upward - Becoming a better version of oneself.

question: Lost the motivation, passion, and concentration to work, making it difficult to carry out planned tasks.
description: I am fundamentally a very positive and proactive person, with clear goals and plans for my work, and I always strive to execute them efficiently. However, in the past two years, I have experienced many ups and downs, and now it's hard for me to regain the enthusiasm for work. Although my goals are still clear, my interest has significantly diminished. It is difficult for me to get back to the state of focusing on executing the plans like before. I feel constantly confused and tend to avoid facing everything in front of me. I always don't feel like doing anything and just want to go to sleep. I constantly feel anxious, and can only temporarily alleviate my mood by eating. Even though I have recently achieved some accomplishments that others may find difficult to reach, it still hasn't brought me a sense of achievement or changed my current state. This state has been persisting for a year.

answers.answer_text: Hello. I understand your current state of mind very well. Going from a positive person to an anxious person, your anxiety lies in feeling a decline in interest over a long period of time. It's difficult for you to get back to how you used to feel, and even when faced with challenges, you don't feel stimulated. You also find it hard to get interested in other things. Although your goals are clear, the lack of interest and motivation leads you to avoid things and seek relief in eating, thinking that it will help you relax and improve your mood. But in reality, this is the beginning of a vicious cycle. Just like when you choose to procrastinate on a task, you still have to do it, but you end up hating it more and more. In terms of losing interest itself, you feel that your achievements don't mean much to you because you don't truly love what you're doing, you just see it as a duty and a task that you should complete. Here are some suggestions: try to make your goals more concrete and display them using images rather than mundane text. Look at them repeatedly to stimulate your brain's desire for a better life. Persist in changing your state of mind and do things you enjoy, of course, after completing your basic tasks. Use more time to cultivate hobbies and interests that are unfamiliar and intriguing to you. Spend time with positive people or talk to friends, maintaining a cheerful and positive mindset. Consider your future plans and have a clear vision for yourself, not settling for the present. On a piece of paper, compare your past and current self, noting your strengths and weaknesses. Within the amount of words written, you will find the answers. I hope my response can be helpful to you. Wish you the best. Good night.

Hug the original poster. The shift from "being proactive and progressive" to "chaotic avoidance" is mainly due to experiencing ups and downs. The key to adjusting one's state lies in the things that are not described in this paragraph. I don't know what kind of ups and downs the original poster has experienced, and I hope they can share more about it. Based on this content, we can then discuss how to make adjustments. Finally, the original poster mentioned "recently achieving some achievements that others may find difficult to reach." I believe that the essence of being proactive and progressive still exists within the original poster, but they are feeling off. Together, we can look at the ups and downs, analyze the pros and cons, facts, and feelings involved, and then return to the original poster's peak moments.

I provide supervisory counseling to accompany people in overcoming procrastination and setting goals. Among the participants, I found that one of them has always been proactive and has clear goals but has been feeling frustrated for the past two years. The reasons in between are not mentioned. She said she actually thought about it for a month before reaching out to me. We chat every day about her emotions, thoughts, and past situations, as well as the current situation. Gradually, her emotions stabilize. One day, she told me that she wants to set a ten-year goal and hoped that I would accompany her for ten years, if possible. After much thought, I said, "You tell me about your goals first." Then I saw her write a ten-year major goal, as well as the goals to be achieved each year and the weekly review plans. It was specific, clear, and executable. I said, "Okay, let's give it a try." After that, I also started setting my ten-year goals. We agreed that we can consider giving up 999 times, but try our best first. So, I think in your case, having clear goals is actually hindered by past emotions. Under my daily companionship, she also understood why she has been feeling this way for the past two years. Once she understood, she could move forward with stable emotions. Therefore, I hope you can do a review for yourself. The past, the present, and the future. After sorting it out, move forward again and review regularly. This may solve your problem.

question: I always think about suicide to escape from reality when I fail. I have tried suffocating myself several times, and I am always afraid that one day I will really die.
description: I am a child from a poor family, and I am not very outstanding. However, my parents care a lot about their reputation and go around telling people that I am very excellent. After failing the postgraduate entrance exam and multiple job interviews, I kept thinking about suicide and tried suffocating myself in different ways. Later, I felt sorry for them. But my mother told everyone about my failures and even blamed the people who tried to help me but were unsuccessful. I am in so much pain. Since failing the postgraduate entrance exam, I feel very bad about myself and I am exhausted. This is just the recent event; there were many small incidents before. My parents always say they love me, but they keep bringing up my past failures and never comfort or encourage me. I had a good job offer in another city, but my parents didn't agree. They cried and made a fuss, insisting that I join a worse company in the local area. I didn't go to the other city, hoping to find a good opportunity here. But now, I have failed repeatedly in local job interviews, and they still blame me for being incompetent. I know I am not good enough, but why do they keep talking about it? Whenever others see me, they tell me to be aware of my own abilities. They even suspect that I lied to them about the job offer from the other city. Yesterday, I tried to commit suicide by using a pillow to suffocate myself, thinking about the end of the world. I have been feeling like this for a long time, and I have thought about suicide several times. I am afraid I won't be able to take it anymore!

answers.answer_text: "#A phrase for the frustrated#" Have you ever had an experience of storing memories in an object? For example, preserving a beautiful memory on a train ticket. Keep this ticket and, in the future, when you see it, you will recall those days. You can also seal unpleasant memories in an item, like a small glass bottle, write down the incident, place it in the bottle, and use a permanent marker to write "Open again on November 25, 2029."

question: Why do some people choose to restrain their negative emotions while others choose to retaliate?
description: Why do some people choose to restrain themselves and shift their focus to continue working, studying, waking up early, being proactive, and staying focused, regardless of conflicts and negative emotions arising from others? Meanwhile, why do some people choose to take extreme measures and harm themselves or others as a form of retaliation, instead of taking a step back and letting things go? What accounts for the significant difference between the two approaches?
keywords: Emotion, expressing emotions, emotion regulation, emotional intelligence

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Seeing your question, it can be said that many people may have similar confusions as you, and your question is representative. From the psychological point of view, a person's emotions are a projection and reaction to their inner true demands. Behind every emotion, there is an inner true demand. When these demands cannot be satisfied, people are prone to have emotions. Secondly, everyone's handling of emotional issues is closely related to their character formation and past experiences during their growth. This is why there are differences in how people handle emotions. The human mind is delicate, just as no two leaves are alike. Similarly, every person lives in different environments and grows up with different family educations. Therefore, the way people handle emotional issues is naturally different. The way each person deals with emotions is not fixed and can be adjusted and changed through personal growth. However, both restraining and retaliating are not the best ways to deal with emotions. Finally, often suppressing and repressing oneself will result in many negative emotions. For example, imagine each person's mind as a limited-size water pool, and negative emotions in life are like water being poured into the pool. If we only pour water into the pool without draining it, over time, the water will overflow and flood ourselves or those around us, leading to the possibility of depression. On the other hand, people who choose to retaliate may develop antisocial personality disorders and other problems over time. In simple terms, the biggest difference between these two situations is that the former is more likely to harm oneself, while the latter is more likely to harm people around them. Therefore, if you have emotional issues that you cannot resolve on your own, it is recommended to seek professional psychological counseling to release those emotions. Additionally, you can also enhance your ability to control emotions through personal growth, becoming the master of your emotions rather than being dominated by them.

OP, hello, your question is very interesting and worth thinking about. I hope my answer can provide you with some help. The difference between the two actually lies in different modes of thinking. Have you heard of Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy (REBT)? Its foundational theory is the ABC theory. According to this theory, emotional and behavioral disorders in individuals are not directly caused by a particular triggering event, but rather by the individual's incorrect cognition and evaluation of that event, leading to different beliefs and ultimately resulting in different emotions and behaviors in specific situations. Therefore, although two people may encounter the same problem or situation, their beliefs and perspectives may differ, and thus their behaviors will also be different. Choosing to restrain oneself and shift attention to doing things that are more important to oneself not only avoids conflicts but also calms emotions. It is a positive attitude. Those who choose forgiveness no longer dwell on things because they know they cannot control others' actions and thoughts; they can only control their own. On the other hand, those who choose revenge do not forgive others, so their attention is always focused on others, making it difficult to focus on their own affairs. They feel conflicted and harm both others and themselves. If they understand forgiveness, they will understand that forgiving others is forgiving oneself. When they learn to let go, their inner peace will also improve significantly. After letting go, their attention will no longer be focused on the other person, and they can do their own things properly. Best wishes.

question: Why do I feel so hopeless every night? It has happened so many times.
description: Every evening, I feel extremely hopeless and have thoughts of death, but the next day, everything is fine again. This has happened a few times and lasts for a period of time each time. I feel that one day, these thoughts may actually become a reality. Is there any solution to this?
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation, fragile tears

answers.answer_text: Dear. Are you okay? I had thoughts of death recently too. It's like the moment when you cut your wrist and separate from the lively world. But lying in bed, I still have some nostalgia. There is a faint spark in the dust of millennia. Seeing vitality. I think of leaving this world. If I leave, someone from the depths of their soul will cry their hearts out. Lost forever. I am selfish. I only care about not wanting to live, not about my family. But as I live until now, my body, my appearance, they raised me. I feel reluctant, indebted. So I want to work and save some money for my parents to have a better life in their later years, even if it's only half. And also for my brother's future marriage. This way, I can freely die. I won't take immediate action. I've started saving money. In the process, because I had thoughts of dying, I started looking at things differently. What is most important? Why do I want to die? I gave up on some things and suddenly realized that there is happiness in that insignificant life. Maybe it's just me turning a blind eye. Now, I no longer have thoughts of death. Though my mood is low. But I'm working hard to adjust myself and become better. Even though she is ordinary and unremarkable, that's my thought. That's who I am. Dear, I think you're also going through something. But the world is so vast, and there are still some things worth cherishing. Wishing you well, my friend.

question: 23-year-old young man, feels like his whole life is being controlled, how can he find liberation?
description: Whether it's school or relationships, even the choice of a mental health professional isn't up to me. Since I was very young, I have been tightly controlled by my family and couldn't breathe. The clearest memory I have is when I was in first grade, my parents forced me to practice calligraphy every day. I didn't enjoy it, but if I didn't practice, I would get scolded. I am actually a very introverted person, and many times I secretly cry. I feel very sad, and I hope to be free soon.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, counseling and listening.

answers.answer_text: OP, because of your family's control, this "authoritarian parenting style" is suffocating you. Perhaps the most direct way is to communicate with your parents, telling them your true thoughts and the pain and depression you are feeling inside. You hope that your parents can understand your feelings, and at the same time, you can express your understanding towards them. Both sides should try to think from each other's perspective, which may make it easier to achieve mutual understanding. Maybe you can go for a walk and relax your mood when you feel suppressed, or talk to friends about your frustration. Perhaps you can also talk to your grandparents and ask them to act as intermediaries to communicate with your parents again. Best wishes!

question: Education issues, when a child says that school is boring, how should we respond?
description: A child in 5th grade tells me that school is boring, with teachers who only lecture and no humor or entertainment. How should I respond? #Family relationships #Growing up #Communication with children
keywords: Family, family relationships, growth process, communication between children and parents.

answers.answer_text: Hello. Elementary school is a stage where children learn to read and write, master basic study methods, and develop basic interests in learning. However, there is no doubt that the cramming education method still dominates the education field. Teachers speak and students listen, and teachers force-feed students with knowledge. The advantage lies in the wide dissemination of basic knowledge, but the drawback is that it cannot fully consider each child's interests and abilities. Adolescents are not carefree little children; every moment they are in a crucial stage of life. The pressures they face are beyond the comprehension of parents and teachers. Parental expectations, teachers' high hopes, ranking in academic competition among classmates, and even the abundance of extracurricular activities all directly determine a child's strengths and weaknesses under ruthless evaluation. In this inevitable high-pressure environment, whether it is a cramming or an exploratory approach, children may feel bored with reading, leading to a dislike for learning. We cannot solely blame the child; instead, we need to consider the various factors that contribute to the situation from multiple dimensions. ●Family, the origin of character. Besides providing daily care, does the family provide effective emotional encouragement and mental guidance for the child? Is the family atmosphere supportive enough for the child to overcome most obstacles? ●School, the place for cultivating talents. It is also a platform for social interaction. Besides school rules and discipline, does the school provide a comfortable and pleasant campus environment for the child? Apart from the bell ringing for classes, are there joyful bird songs and classmates' happy singing? ●Teachers, the disseminators of knowledge. Those who can cater to the child's interests are undoubtedly the best for teaching. A high-quality teacher possesses flexibility, broad and deep knowledge, and strong comprehension and acceptance. Has the child encountered a teacher who rigidly adheres to teaching theories and forcibly imparts textbook content? ●Classmates, companions during growth. In a large social circle, students inevitably form small groups and cliques. Has the child already formed a stable circle of friends, and do these friends have obvious positive qualities? It is outdated and ineffective to solely rely on lecturing the child with reasoning to promote their healthy development. ●If the school adopts a cramming approach, the family should be more exploratory. Pay more attention to the child's emotions and moods, whether they are happy or sad, content or frustrated. It is not enough to ask questions such as "Did you finish your homework?" or "Your mom is calling you for dinner." Every child has immense potential for positive growth and does not have inexplicable negativity or laziness. ●If the teacher rigidly adheres to teaching theories, the family should be more dynamic. If the teacher says that winter is the season of snow, the family should find ways to let the child know that there is also the possibility of blooming flowers in the winter. Increase the child's proactive thinking and capture their surprise at any small progress. ●If the child does not have a stable friendship, the family should be more harmonious. Any good relationship provides strong support for an individual. On one hand, try to create and maintain harmony within the family; on the other hand, assist the child in building relationships outside the family, such as inviting a few favorite classmates for a get-together at home. It takes ten years to grow a tree, and a hundred years to cultivate a person. Bringing up a successful child is not easy, and raising a child successfully is even more challenging. Only when parents and children both put in efforts can there be fruitful outcomes. The interaction between parents and schools, parents and teachers, parents and children, parents and parents, and children and children is indispensable. A multidimensional focus and positive guidance can help children find interest instead of boredom and enable them to face setbacks and difficulties correctly.

Hello: First, you can appreciate the child's expression. The child is very honest and willing to tell you the truth. You can try to understand the child's feelings and thoughts. It's not fun to be like this every day, and the pressure of learning is gradually increasing. Then ask the child, besides the teacher's lectures not being humorous, what else is fun? For example, interactions with classmates, or what subjects the child likes? You can also ask the child if there are other reasons besides what he/she mentioned. Is there any pressure? Or maybe classmates are bullying him/her? It is important to note that as parents, we should not get too anxious when the child expresses reluctance to go to school. We should relax a bit. It is not a problem for the child to express their thoughts. The problem is how we as parents respond. Fifth grade is also gradually entering puberty, and there is a lot of pressure in terms of learning. The child undergoes psychological changes, emotional changes, and physical changes. Parents should pay more attention to these aspects and show more care. It's not about constantly focusing on studying or grades. This will also make the child feel the care and love from parents, which will also increase their inner strength.

Hello, as a parent, you are very concerned about your child's studies. However, not all children can meet our expectations and achieve satisfactory academic results. The problem could stem from various factors, including the child's own reasons, the parent's reasons, and even the school's reasons. Each factor needs to be addressed separately.

First, as a parent, you should consider your own reasons. Have you been paying attention to cultivating your child's interests and hobbies? Are you allowing your child to have more sources of happiness? Or are you solely focusing on their academic performance and neglecting the development of their personality? If your child lacks enthusiasm in doing tasks at home, naturally, they will find studying boring. At this point, you should reflect on your own educational methods and consider whether you have provided a happy and exploratory environment for your child's growth.

If your child is positive and proactive at home but struggles with the school's educational methods, a particular subject or teacher's teaching style, or even dislikes the overall atmosphere of the school, the most effective solution might be transferring them to a different school. My son is a good example of this. After changing schools and teachers, his attitude towards learning became positive, and his grades improved significantly. If transferring schools is not feasible, you can start by focusing on the subjects that interest your child and gradually help them find joy in learning. This requires parents to patiently accompany and allow their children greater freedom. Do not judge your child based solely on temporary grades, as this will only make them more resistant to learning.

If possible, communicate with the teacher and let them know about your child's attitude towards learning and that they need more time. Assure the teacher that you, as a parent, are fully committed to supporting your child's improvement in grades, and request that they refrain from judging or criticizing your child based on temporary grades. Restoring your child's confidence in learning is crucial.

If you have tried various efforts, but your child still shows no interest in studying, then you need to accept this fact. Perhaps they are just not inclined towards academic pursuits. In this case, you can set a minimum requirement for their grades. Once your child meets this requirement, you can stop pressuring them to study and allow them more time to develop their own interests. As long as they have hobbies and are willing to make an effort, it is a good thing. What we fear is that they become disinterested in everything. As a parent, you should provide greater allowance for that. Being your child's authentic self is the key to their happiness. Good luck!

Hello! Good morning! Seeing your question, on one hand, I can feel your care and attention for your child. Thumbs up for that! On the other hand, I also deeply understand the challenges of being a parent nowadays. It's difficult to balance work and self-learning on how to educate our children. Firstly, there are certain aspects of the overall environment, including the education system, that we cannot change. We need to acknowledge the progressiveness of the times. Compared to when we were young, many hardware and educational concepts have improved. In this regard, we need to accept the current situation and cultivate a calm mindset to face today's educational issues. Then, based on this calm mindset, we can try to communicate with our children. It is important to analyze specific problems. For example, if a child says that teachers only lecture every day, this is a relatively absolute judgment. It is impossible for all teachers to be the same, right? Which teacher is it specifically? Which subject? If there is no sense of humor or entertainment, perhaps this teacher's educational philosophy is to impart the knowledge system from the textbooks comprehensively. Is the child simply not very interested in this subject? We need to have further communication with the child, combining our own past experiences, and communicate calmly and vividly with the child. At the very least, we need to ensure what aspects of this subject need to be guaranteed for grades. Also, we need to determine if other students have similar reactions or if it is an individual case for the child. Further understanding is required in these aspects.
