Education is a slow process, we cannot be impatient or hasty in making judgments. As for individualized teaching, given the current national situation, as parents, we can play a role in fostering the cultivation of stimulating the child's interest in learning. By working together with the school, we can ensure a good education for our children. I hope this helps and inspires you. The world and I love you!

Hello, I hope my answer can be helpful to you. From the perspective of the child's educational environment, the fifth grade is a time when the child is preparing to transition into adolescence. Children will gradually develop their own judgments and opinions about people and things, which is a sign and process of growth and maturity. Indeed, the Chinese education system only values academic achievements and the gaokao (college entrance examination). The overall educational environment has a great impact on parents. In the eyes of Chinese parents, studying is the only goal, grades are the only goal, and the gaokao is the only goal. So, if a child doesn't perform well academically, it's considered a failure in everything, which is an extreme and disrespectful attitude towards the child. Recently, a friend who has lived abroad for many years came back and talked about the issue of education. There is no harm without comparison. Starting from elementary school, Chinese parents hope their children can score higher and higher in exams. Children start learning elementary school subjects in preschool, middle school subjects in elementary school, and so on, which goes against the natural development of human beings. Their young minds are not ready to handle the content they are being taught, it's just pushing them too hard. In contrast, in other countries, if a child in second grade gets a perfect score, the principal and teacher will question it, and even call the parents for a meeting to provide them with psychological education: your child shouldn't be getting perfect scores at this age according to their mental development, this pressure and perfectionism is something that needs to be corrected. So, in fact, it's not your personal fault that you have this anxiety. Really. From the perspective of the child's psychological motivation, today's children lack the minimum survival anxiety, which is an important source of motivation. The harder a person works, the higher their anxiety, while those who don't work hard have lower anxiety levels, and self-esteem follows a similar pattern. From the perspective of your generation and your family's background and circumstances, the situation is undoubtedly different. Most children in this generation come from relatively well-off families and don't have to worry about their basic needs. They are born into a life with a house and a car, without the need to struggle or work in the fields. They grow up in a sheltered environment in the city, so what do they have to worry about? It can be said that they lack the minimum survival anxiety. Whereas our generation has this minimum survival anxiety, which drives us to work hard, improve ourselves, and constantly strive for excellence. Of course, more importantly, each child has their own potential and direction to develop. You just need to teach them according to their characteristics. Each era has its own characteristics, and each has its own path to success. We cannot force them to be the same as us, to have good grades and to work extremely hard. Also, can we guarantee that they will achieve good grades if we demand it from them? Not necessarily. In their thinking, they were born into a life with a house and a car, without the need to struggle or work in the fields, so why should they work hard? That's why we need to guide their growth, such as through hardship education and teaching them how to deal with setbacks. It's not too late for a fifth-grade child, and it would be even better to provide them with labor and hardship education before their second stage of rebellion arrives, around the ages of seven or eight. The method and approach are very important. Bless you. I am here, and the world and I love you.

Hello parents and friends: I believe the first step is to respond to the child's feelings, saying something like "Oh, you feel bored at school." This way, the child can feel that you are sincerely listening to him, and he will express how boring it is and to what extent. Once the child has expressed these feelings of boredom, he will feel relieved. As a parent, you just need to patiently listen carefully. Perhaps after the child has finished speaking, he will act as if nothing happened and go on with whatever he needs to do. As parents, we don't need to overly concern or worry about whether the child will stop loving school or dislike learning! In fact, every child will go through feelings of boredom with school. There's no need to make a big deal out of it. Otherwise, it will have the opposite effect. Just for your reference. Of course, if the child says this every day and shows signs of not completing homework or not going to school, that's another matter. However, in general, children who express their emotions to their parents usually only talk about it. Parents just need to show understanding and listen.

question: 26-year-old female, for several years, she has been afraid to speak in public and never speaks up even when there is something important.
description: In the past few years, there has been a problem that has been distressing me... Every time I enter the company and face my colleagues, or in school when facing classmates in the classroom or dormitory, I dare not speak. I always delay when it comes to asking for help from others, fearing that something embarrassing might happen. Eventually, I just give up on communication and handling things, sometimes even hurting others. Even when I tell myself to speak up, I still can't say anything. I am always afraid and worried about not handling things well, feeling helpless in the end. I feel like I have lost the ability to socialize with people. I feel mentally exhausted every day, and now, just a few days after starting a new job, I am considering quitting because I lack confidence in my work, and I feel like I have let down my leader's trust. Should I choose a job where I don't have to face people directly, like working from home? I feel relaxed at home, without that overwhelming feeling, and my mood improves. Maybe I should first adjust my confidence and emotions before embarking on work?
keywords: Interpersonal relations, communication, colleagues, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: It is unclear about your upbringing, but typically this situation stems from traumatic experiences. One possibility is that you had traumatic experiences during early communication with others, leading to a low sense of self-worth and fear of expressing your true self, afraid of being ignored, invalidated, or rejected. With the motive of self-protection, you avoid interactions with others, fearing to be hurt again. Another possibility is that, after being hurt by others, you have suppressed a lot of anger and aggression, projecting it outward, believing that others might want to harm you, which leads to fear. In order to no longer fear when interacting with people in the present, you need to heal from the traumatic experiences you had in the past when interacting with others.

question: College, whenever I come home, I feel very unhappy.
description: Every time I come home, as long as I say a few words to my mother, she becomes unhappy. No matter what I say, she will be unhappy. She often acts as if she didn't hear me speaking and frequently stops talking after just a couple of sentences. If I ask her again, she gets upset and says a few words to me. In short, it's very annoying, and I don't know how to resolve it. I'm thinking that maybe I should just not come home in the future.
keywords: Family, family relationships, and parental communication.

answers.answer_text: Hello! You can tell that you are a filial child who always wants to chat with your mom, but you can't make her happy, so you are very frustrated and have thoughts of avoiding it: "I might as well not go home." Actually, you probably can't do that because each of us is very attached to our parents who gave birth to and raised us. Having them around gives us a sense of home, even if this home doesn't make us very happy. Yet, we still can't leave it, right? This is also the reason why you came to this platform to seek solutions, isn't it? You are in college, and judging from your age, your mom is still in her prime and has abundant experience and energy. She should be a key figure in her workplace, in her golden period of career. Of course, this is also a time when she is under a lot of pressure, a period where not progressing means regression in her career. So, her thoughts might not be solely focused on you like before you attended college, and she may not pay as much attention to your thoughts and feelings, resulting in a response that is not in line with your expectations and even making you feel that she is unhappy. Now, let's switch the roles. You have already become an adult and started your college life, which is also a new beginning in your life. At this time, would it be better to turn the care and protection your mom used to give you into care and protection from you to her? Actually, moms also need to be cared for and protected. After sending you to college, the family burden may have decreased, but the social pressure has increased. As you start a new life in college, it is also a very big change for her. From a life centered around you to one centered around herself and her career, this is also a significant challenge. Can you try to understand your mom and feel her joys and sorrows, and when you come home, try to cooperate with her as much as possible? I think if you try to change yourself, your mom will be happy because of your changes. Best wishes to you!

question: How to commit suicide without pain.
description: Don't want to live anymore...

answers.answer_text: Hello, in the past I saw a topic on Zhihu about suicide. In this topic, there is a series of related posts titled "Don't use ** method to commit suicide". It mentions many methods, almost covering most of the methods we can think of, detailing the pain and process of each method. After reading it, I think there is indeed no painless way. Death is painful, and living also brings pain. So why not live well? At least, living is not just about pain. If you don't want to live anymore, what happened? Can you talk about it? We can help analyze it together, give you suggestions, and find solutions. If you are really facing difficulties, don't endure it alone. You can seek help, ask for assistance from people around you, call the helpline 95, see a psychologist or counselor. There will always be someone who can help you. Please live well. Problems are always temporary. When you get through this challenge and look back on this journey, you will be grateful for your current perseverance. In retrospect, everything may seem insignificant. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

I don't want to live anymore, I really want to hug the person who posted this question and share the pain you're feeling. Life is like living in an ocean of suffering, we are pursuing the unknown shore, and sometimes when we get tired of swimming alone, we feel like giving up. In the ocean of suffering, our self is our solid support, it can be a bridge, a ship, helping us temporarily escape from hardship and move forward. However, one day the bridge may collapse and the ship may leak, at this time we often think that it would be better to give up on life. But, a collapsed bridge can be repaired, even better than before, and a leaking ship can be fixed, even reinforced. As long as you don't give up hope, hope is by your side, please don't easily give up on yourself.

Dear questioner, at this moment you still feel pain. When we let pain flow through our bodies, it will slowly nourish us, and perhaps in the future gain a new strength from it. Don't forget, you can take a break, pause for a while. Time is meant to be felt, we still have time. When tired, take a rest.

question: Is there a way to cure schizophrenia?
description: The thoughts in one's mind can be heard by people around, leading to being attacked and gossiped about, affecting social interactions and daily life. This also comes with anxiety and obsessive thinking, being afraid and fearful of talking to others. Under such fear, how can one work well?
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, diagnosis of illness, treatment methods

answers.answer_text: Thoughts do not vocalize. This state is probably being too deeply immersed in thinking. I suggest practicing mindfulness, observing one's own behavior and actions in daily life, and distinguishing them from one's thoughts. Examine what kind of behavior is caused by the surrounding environment and what kind of thoughts lead to one's actions. Then, practice improvement.

question: Is it appropriate for a 19-year-old girl who has graduated to not be accustomed to actively contacting friends?
description: I have graduated from high school and had two good friends, who were also my roommates. They have always been proactive in maintaining contact with me, but due to my habit, I rarely reach out unless there is something important. However, now they are actively reaching out to me, and combined with the tension between us in the past, I feel like I should take the initiative to talk to them, but I always find it difficult to find topics and it feels forced and awkward. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello. Have you ever considered being a good listener as a friend? With your personality, you prefer purposeful communication, getting straight to the point, which is a common communication style for many people. There are many ways to interact with friends, but regardless of the method, whether active or passive, taking a rational and sincere approach is the key to maintaining stable and lasting relationships. You're 19 years old and likely still in school, so your understanding of friendship may be somewhat simplistic due to the innocence of campus life. Some people believe that it's necessary to initiate communication, sharing activities, thoughts, and feelings. However, everyone has different standards for friendship. Just like how you don't enjoy chatting and prefer to spend limited time doing things you like, your friends may enjoy contacting you actively. Your different approaches do not harm anyone, it's just a matter of preference, so don't feel obliged. Additionally, I'm not sure if any grievances between you and your friend have been resolved. If not, spending time together may feel a little awkward. In this case, one of you should take the initiative to address the issue. If the disagreement is already in the past, you and your friend can maintain your original styles and build a sincere and understanding relationship. This advice is based on your preference not to change your communication style. Accordingly, if you maintain a more passive attitude, over time, you may gradually develop a more casual bond with your friends. However, if you wish to delve deeper into your friends' emotions and have more meaningful communication, you can adjust your perspective. Consider sharing your daily trivia with your friends, just like chatting with family, and increase the frequency of your communication. If you aren't good at communicating, you can also arrange to participate in activities together, which will increase your presence in your friends' eyes. It seems that you also prefer not to change your approach to making friends while eliminating the psychological concerns that come with not contacting them actively. At this point, ask yourself if you want a deeper relationship with your friends. Can you accept it if one day, because of your lack of initiative, they gradually drift away? Regardless of the communication style you choose, it's important to prioritize your own comfort. Wishing you happiness.

question: The people around me are excellent, and the pressure is high. How should I deal with my intense mood swings?
description: I'm actually a person who is quite competitive, and I really don't like feeling inferior to others. Before entering university, although I wasn't one of the top students in my grade, I was frequently praised by teachers and parents, and I thought highly of myself. However, after entering university, I discovered that everyone in my class is very outstanding. Not only are they good at academics, but they also have various talents and are good-looking. Compared to them, I feel like I'm not at their level at all. Every time in class, someone would blurt out the answer to the teacher's question, and I feel the pressure coming at me. The more this happens, the harder it is for me to study, and my grades keep dropping. I'm gradually becoming afraid of attending classes, afraid of socializing, and I often feel like crying. Moreover, my emotions fluctuate greatly, and I feel like I'm becoming more and more pessimistic, unable to live a normal life. I even suspect if there's something wrong with my mental health... What should I do...
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, self-acceptance

answers.answer_text: From middle school to college, everyone goes through a round of elimination, so naturally, the overall level of the people around you will be higher than before, which is normal. Some people are accustomed to receiving praise as a source of security or self-esteem since childhood, to the point where they find it difficult to affirm themselves or feel like they are being abandoned by the world when they don't receive praise. In fact, this is a form of trauma from their upbringing. What you need to realize is that academic achievements do not prove a person's excellence or lack thereof; it is just because you rely on praise to gain self-esteem and have not found the true source of self-esteem—your true talents and passions. Everyone has their strengths, and there is no one who is better than others. It's just that everyone has different talents and traits. Those classmates that you consider excellent may only have talents in certain subjects or simply excel in classroom learning—your strengths may lie in other domains, not necessarily in comparing yourself to others in classroom learning. Grades are only one aspect of people's abilities; outstanding individuals in society are not necessarily those with good grades, and nobody can be excellent in all areas or professional fields. Find out what your unique value is and gradually let go of comparing yourself with others or seeking affirmation from others to confirm your self-worth.

First of all, let me give you a hug and ask you to think about what your definition of excellence is. Maybe it's outstanding academic or work abilities, or perhaps it's exceptional good looks, or maybe it's having a natural talent for socializing. However, as the saying goes, "nobody is perfect" and "everyone has their strengths and weaknesses." No one is absolutely excellent, and in some ways, you may have magnified the strengths of others. Secondly, are you underestimating yourself too much subconsciously? When you magnify the excellence of those around you to an infinite extent, your subconscious mind starts to belittle yourself. This suppressive thinking makes it difficult for you to make progress on the path of self-improvement. In other words, the efforts you have made are like carrying a burden, and it would be much easier if you embarked on your journey with a light heart. However, the invisible psychological pressure is like a hidden chronic poison, constantly eroding your positive and upward mindset. Lastly, you need to set your mindset right. All judgments of right and wrong, good and bad, and aesthetic standards are man-made and can change with the times. How can you continue to improve yourself under such defined circumstances without losing your direction? The answer lies in thinking, meditating, and analyzing yourself more. Shift your focus from others to yourself, know your strengths and weaknesses, further improve yourself, and engage in effective practices. The uniqueness of life is what I believe is most precious. No matter how excellent and talented your friends are, they can never become you in this lifetime. That's why I always push myself, because of my uniqueness. So, instead of chasing other people's light, let yourself shine! Best wishes!

question: I am currently feeling disgusted with my work and I don't know what I really want to do. What should I do?
description: I've changed many jobs, all of which I started out with full confidence. But after a few days, I became dispirited. Either I felt things were going against my wishes, or I found fault with everything, or I just felt tired. I couldn't help but nitpick, but deep down, I didn't really want to leave because where else would I go? Just sit at home and do nothing like I did before? However, I don't know what I really want deep down. I feel frustrated and depressed. I show my complaints to the outside world.
keywords: Career, career management, career selection skills, work pressure

answers.answer_text: You have a relatively clear understanding of your current state. As you said, on one hand, you don't know what you really want on the inside, so you are always unwilling to persist in your work. It seems like there is a feeling of frustration. On the other hand, it manifests as complaining. In fact, external complaints are often a result of unclear internal feelings. For example, you may be very dissatisfied with life and work, and internally there may be a strong anger towards the inability to change externally, or a depressive feeling of helplessness after the inability to change. These deep emotions arise, and only after enduring them can you possibly understand what you want and know how to proceed. However, these feelings may be too uncomfortable, so when they arise, you choose to "vent" externally, i.e. complain. As a result, it feels like you are "stuck". Resolving this issue requires gradually reclaiming these emotions and learning how to tolerate them step by step. Of course, this is not something that can be achieved overnight. But you can start by practicing with small uncomfortable feelings and resisting the urge to speak out. Naturally, the internal feelings will become clearer as they intensify.

question: Girls are often too sensitive and emotional, and they often cannot control themselves when their emotions affect them.
description: Feeling like my emotions are too sensitive, my ability to associate is too strong. Once someone around me says something or does something, it affects me for a long time. I worry if I did something wrong and care a lot about what others think. Normally when I read novels, watch TV dramas, or look at old photos, or even listen to songs, if there are sad or nostalgic themes, my mood would be affected for a long time. It can even lead to longing for the past and worrying about the future. Very sensitive and sentimental, heavily reliant on others, always being influenced by my own emotions but unable to control them.

answers.answer_text: Sensitive people can use the following methods to proactively adjust their emotions and mindset: 1. Build self-confidence and maintain an independent personality. Never excessively focus on the actions of others or their evaluations of oneself. Especially in the current situation, it is crucial to focus on one's own affairs. No matter what others say, one should make life fulfilling by doing well in daily work and life. 2. Make efforts to redirect attention. Do not excessively indulge in sensitive and suspicious issues, which can harm daily life. Engage in activities that one is interested in, such as traveling, sightseeing, photography, enjoying good food, and breathing fresh air. These activities can effectively shift attention and enrich life, allowing oneself to gain a fulfilling life. Only by maintaining a positive and optimistic mindset can one overcome sensitivity issues. 3. Actively communicate and interact with others, especially when feeling overly sensitive and anxious. It is crucial not to keep everything inside but to learn to express oneself and confide in friends and family. Expressing negative emotions to others can help alleviate sensitivity issues and gain understanding of others' true attitudes, ultimately fostering friendships and trust. The above methods are all effective.

question: My younger brother is so aggressive because he has the support of our mother's side behind him, I'm really tired, what should I do?
description: My younger brother got angry at me for no reason again today. Even when I tried to make peace, he refused to back down. He arrogantly said to me, "Do you dare ignore me?" In all our past arguments, he acted like they didn't matter to him. But he can be happy and get along with our mother without any issues. It's clearly his fault, yet sometimes I have to beg him to apologize, but he still won't. So, for a month or two, I didn't talk to anyone and nobody talked to me. But seeing them together, it hurts me inside. I haven't done anything wrong, so why am I being treated like this? Sometimes, they really seem like a family, and I cried all night, but nobody cared or asked what was wrong. They just told me to stop crying. I know my brother acts this way because he has our mother and her family supporting him, but I'm truly in pain. My eyes hurt from crying, and I feel hopeless.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. In family relationships, if you have negative feelings, you must try to express them and let the people around you understand and care about you, rather than suppressing your emotions. From your description, it can be seen that you feel sad and hopeless because your brother has the support of family members while you are alone. You don't know how to express yourself or how to gain support and love from your family. It is evident that you feel very lonely at home, especially in an environment where your brother is heavily favored, which intensifies this feeling. You should try to confide your feelings to family members who are more concerned about you, express your desire for their care, attention, confidence, and happiness, instead of only being able to cry alone in a corner. Interaction within the family is two-sided. Your brother may pout and directly express his desires to your parents, cry and demand attention. Meanwhile, you may be very well-behaved and silently endure a lot of pain, not expressing yourself, and not daring to ask for love. You may fear that your family won't like you and think that you have too many issues, and so on. But what I want to tell you is that family members are not mind readers and won't know what our needs are unless we tell them. They may unintentionally overlook them. For example, if there's a dish on the dinner table that both you and your brother like, your brother directly tells the family that he wants to eat it, pouts or creates a fuss, cries, etc., so your parents satisfy him. And you also want to eat it, but for various reasons, you don't dare to say it or help yourself. You watch them happily eat while feeling bitter inside. The same goes for other things, have you noticed? You may need to tell them what you need and when you need it for them to pay attention to you, feel your needs, and find ways to meet them, instead of hiding and waiting for them to satisfy you or pretending that nothing is wrong when they show concern. Learn to bravely express yourself, whether it's needs, dissatisfaction, anger, etc. Only in this way can there be a possibility of mutual understanding with your family, and there will be less conflict and feelings of isolation. Best wishes.

question: Diagnosed with moderate depression, the desire to live is not strong, becoming increasingly low, wanting liberation?
description: The 20-year-old woman was diagnosed with moderate depression on June 12 last year, and then with severe depression on November 14 of the same year. In fact, she has been suffering for many years, but it was only last year that she was diagnosed, which had a great impact on her. During this period of time, she has been oscillating between thoughts of death and continuing to live. She doesn't know what's wrong, can't understand herself, and doesn't listen to others' advice. She is immersed in dark emotions and cannot make a direct choice. The thought of death brings tears to her family and friends, but she also lacks the motivation to continue living. She has been struggling and collapsing continuously, and now feels that she is being pulled over by the Reaper. She wants to irresponsibly free herself from the rooftop.

answers.answer_text: Hello, have you actively cooperated with the doctor's treatment after being diagnosed with moderate and severe depression? Treatment often takes time to take effect and alleviate symptoms, so don't be impatient. Give yourself some time, persist with the treatment, and your situation will gradually improve. Despite suffering for many years and facing the brink of collapse, you have been making efforts to keep going because of your family and friends, and your sense of responsibility. From this perspective, you are already extraordinary. In the past, you could do it, and I believe you can continue to do so in the future. If it becomes too difficult to endure on your own, you can try seeking help from others. Find someone you trust, express your feelings of pain, and perhaps it will make things a little bit easier. It's okay, you are not alone, and you don't have to silently bear all this pain by yourself. You may feel that you have lost the motivation to continue living, but remember, we can find the motivation ourselves; you just haven't found it yet. Think about the dreams, aspirations, and expectations you've had before. You need to know that as long as you don't give up on yourself, these things are very likely to come true. Society is constantly developing and changing, and so are we. Believe that life will not always be so terrible. Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: Seems to have no interest in anything, overflowing with a sense of worthlessness.
description: Lack of interest in everything, overwhelming sense of worthlessness. Unwilling to do household chores that can be accomplished, unwilling to do work that cannot be accomplished. Feeling a lot of pressure. Wanting to relax, but once I slow down, I can't even enjoy watching TV shows.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~ I wonder what you have experienced that has caused you to lose interest in life. Here's a warm hug for you first~ The way to regain enthusiasm for life is to discover its meaning. If you find yourself uninterested in everything around you, maybe give yourself a chance to breathe and go out for a walk, relax yourself. It's also a good choice to immerse yourself in nature. If possible, chat with friends more, gather together for a meal or some team building activities, anything that can make you happy. Don't keep that feeling bottled up inside. Sometimes, just talking to friends, family (or anyone who can make you feel better) can relieve that sense of emptiness. Things that you wanted to do before but lacked motivation or courage (such as rock climbing), now is the time to push yourself and gather the courage to accomplish it~ After completing it, you will realize that there are so many things waiting for us to do and so many goals waiting for us to achieve. I hope the above suggestions are helpful to you. Best wishes~.

question: Do you still give gifts in this situation when you don't like him as much?
description: It is possible that the lack of strong affection for him stems from the need for care and attention, so it's best to maintain contact. Now that it's clear, I know that I don't like him that much, so I shouldn't have any expectations for the future. However, I have already bought a birthday present for him that I prepared. Should I still give it to him? If I do, how will he perceive it and will he think of me when he sees this gift in the future? Would it be better not to give it?
keywords: Love, heartbreak, managing relationships, liking someone.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm sorry, but I don't have hope for the future anymore. However, I have already bought a gift. I don't know whether I should give it to him or not. If I give the gift, should I give it as a friend or as someone who likes him? Can you try to think about it? If you hadn't bought the gift, and his birthday was coming up and you realized that you don't actually like him that much, would you still prepare a gift for him? Try to think about these questions, it might help you. That's my suggestion, I hope it can help you. Best wishes!

question: 24-year-old man, particularly repelled by the possibility of future marriage life, what should he do?
description: I used to have a crush on a girl and had a simple romantic relationship, but in the past two years, I don't know if people have become more complicated or what, but I don't want to be in a relationship anymore. I even feel repulsed at the thought of married life. I just want to go to work and do things I love in my spare time. I don't know if my two failed relationships and my mother's menopause have anything to do with it. Right now, besides the need to reproduce, marriage feels like a burden and women feel like shackles to me. I can no longer approach relationships with the same mindset as a few years ago when my eyes were filled with only you. I have recently been chatting with two girls quite well, but now when facing a potential romantic relationship, I can only think about whether I am just a backup or how much dowry she would demand. Is she serious? Why should I pursue her? Does being in a relationship mean I have to take care of her in addition to my work? But I can't even take care of myself. Do I have to give her my salary after getting married? Do I have to always compromise during arguments? How can I handle her menopause? Thinking about all these things, I no longer have any desire for love and I even feel a bit tired of women. I no longer believe in relationships. And this lack of trust in relationships has slowly transformed into a lack of trust in all kinds of interpersonal relationships, and I have become more and more indifferent, although no one can tell in my daily life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, my questioner, seeing your words is like seeing you in person. From your words, I can tell that you have a lack of trust in relationships. In this era, more and more people choose to be single, living freely and enjoying their own lives. This may be related to the social environment. We all have the right to choose whether to get married or not, and we should choose the life we want based on our own values. However, we cannot deny the value of marriage. If you strongly reject marriage, there is no need to force yourself to get married. Your understanding of marriage is too extreme, "having had two failed relationships, with your mother going through menopause, you feel that marriage is a burden and women are shackles." The influence of previous failed relationships, your mother's situation, and the various unhappy marriages you see around you or online have led to misunderstandings and rejection of love and marriage. You have fallen into a victim mentality towards marriage and unconsciously put yourself in a victim position, thinking that marriage will bring you various types of harm. You want to avoid this harm, so you reject marriage. However, everything has two or even more sides. In your description, you only see the negative impact of marriage, and a large part of these negative impacts are imagined by you. You need to see the positive side of marriage, seriously understand marriage, and make a choice that you won't regret based on your own values. How to improve the current situation and correctly understand marriage: Marriage is a stage in our life journey, a choice we make. During this process, conflicts and arguments may occur, and it may change the rhythm of our previous lives. However, we cannot deny the value of marriage. It is also a carrier of happiness and stability. If, on a non-extreme basis, you do not want to enter into marriage, that is also okay. Face your own thoughts with a peaceful mentality and do not reject marriage in the midst of marriage. This will make you even more negative and affect your usual interpersonal relationships. Love is mutual, it involves two people, it's not about one person giving and the other person enjoying. If that's how your previous relationships were, then it means you haven't met the right person. Is she serious? Do I still have to take care of her after work? Do I always have to compromise in arguments? These questions are not really problems. Love requires mutual tolerance and understanding. If you achieve these two points, you won't have these problems anymore. Think carefully about your choices and what kind of life you want to live. Whether or not you want to enter into marriage, everything comes with a cost. Choosing freedom inevitably means giving up the warmth and happiness of family; choosing marriage means dealing with family trivialities and communication with family members. Make a good choice, adjust your mindset, and face what you have to face with a peaceful mentality. I hope my answer can help you.

If we simply compare the relationship between dating and marriage, marriage is undoubtedly much more complicated, after all, most of the time dating is between two individuals, while marriage involves two families. Moreover, marriage implies more responsibilities. For example, when dating, people may not expect you to have a stable job and a house, but marriage is different, especially in society, where many practical issues need to be considered. From the description, it feels like sometimes the situation becomes a deadlock, as if we are the ones constantly giving while the other party is just taking. However, if we think carefully, if a marriage can truly last a long time, it definitely cannot rely solely on one person's effort. In simple terms, even though we men don't personally experience the hardships of carrying a child for nine months, we still have some understanding of how tiring and difficult it is. Therefore, marriage cannot be sustained by one person alone. If the girl's parents are reasonable and understand the difficulties their child goes through, as long as the two individuals are determined to put in the effort and have a decent income, I believe that open-minded parents will not force their children into marriage because they understand what happiness means to their child. If the girl's parents only value material things and don't care about the emotional life of the couple, how long such a marriage can last depends on how long the man's wallet can support it, so we need to carefully evaluate such a marriage ourselves. Of course, whether or not to choose marriage and love is our own freedom. Loving someone may be about wanting to give them a stable home, letting them know that there is someone who will take care of them when they are tired, giving them a place to rest when they are weary, and working together to solve and face any problems. The world loves you.

After listening to your venting, I feel like you are someone who doesn't bother with the pursuit of love. You said you no longer believe in love, but it seems more like you're afraid to love again. People who cannot love often do so because they are too concerned about the outcome of love. It is precisely because of this excessive concern that their attention is not focused on enjoying the present, but on worrying about various possibilities. This worry restricts their ability to enjoy and be free. Sometimes, it's not that we don't want to be in a relationship, but that we truly dare not. I hope at this age, we can understand and accept reality. Love is not as perfect as we imagine. I think you are well aware of this, as in this world, nothing is perfect. Accepting and acknowledging the true nature of love, not having overly high expectations, and not making it the sole focus are crucial. When a relationship or several relationships break down, I personally believe that no one is worth sacrificing yourself for. When you realize that you are being hurt, it's important to cut your losses and not fear the criticism and judgment of others because we don't live our lives to please others. At this age, perhaps your experiences with love have been more tumultuous than others, and I think that's okay too. After going through emotional pain, when a relationship comes to an end, mourn it properly and don't dwell in past relationships because it's not a symbol of your failure, nor should you doubt yourself too much. Walk your own path well and believe that happiness will come as expected.

24? It's still early. If you don't want to talk about it, then don't. Right now, you're rejecting this matter and only considering the negative issues. If you have these concerns about being a backup option, dowry, and sincerity, it's mostly because your subconscious is analyzing the high risks and warning you about the problems that may exist in these two girls. A really good girl will make you have no worries at all and make you feel like you're the only one in her eyes. So, take it easy and wait until you meet a girl who makes your heart flutter. Don't let it affect your mood. Just focus on doing well at work and living your life. There's nothing wrong with being single for a while.

question: Bipolar disorder, social anxiety disorder, feeling like one's entire self is about to collapse, what should be done?
description: Bipolar disorder, mild social anxiety and introversion. I was previously isolated and dropped out of school due to living in a dormitory. I worked for a while and now I want to go back to school, but I'm afraid of being isolated again. I don't know how to interact with many people and feel very uncomfortable. I feel anxious in crowded places and feel like I'm going to collapse. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello: In your writing, you mentioned that you have bipolar disorder and are currently experiencing social anxiety, afraid of being isolated and feeling uncomfortable. Hugs to you, I feel for you. Bipolar disorder is a common mental disorder characterized by episodes of mania or hypomania and depression. During manic episodes, patients may exhibit elevated mood, increased speech, and increased energy. During depressive episodes, patients may experience low mood, loss of pleasure, decreased speech, and fatigue. The best treatment for bipolar disorder is a combination of medication and psychological counseling. I don't know if you have sought medical help or if your bipolar disorder has improved. However, I have some small suggestions for your social anxiety, hoping that it can help you. 1. Shift your focus, relax your mind When you feel fearful, you can try to shift your focus and take deep breaths to relax your mind. It can greatly improve your situation. 2. Take the first step Since you have social anxiety and don't know how to interact with people, the best way to combat fear is to take action. In psychology, there is a term called systematic desensitization. You can try breaking down your behavior into several steps and start with something that brings you the least fear. For example, the first time, you can try having a conversation with a classmate and express your thoughts; the second time, you can try participating in a conversation in your dormitory and responding to others' thoughts; the third time, you can try expressing your opinions in a group of classmates... Actually, your fear stems from your past experiences and the fear of being isolated again. However, when you start to make changes, people's perspectives towards you and their attitudes will also change. You are different now, so people's attitudes towards you will be different as well. And when we actually do the things that we fear, the fear itself is not as terrifying. 3. Learn from others' social skills in school, you can try learning how other classmates interact with each other. Perhaps you will gradually realize that your classmate A also feels nervous and uncomfortable when talking to strangers; you may also find that there are classmates around you who are introverted but reliable in their actions, and classmates who are extroverted and good at socializing. You may also discover that those classmates who feel uncomfortable when interacting with strangers are also working hard to overcome their own fears; perhaps you will find that communication is not as difficult as you think... I hope you can become a better version of yourself. Take care.

question: I don't have any feelings towards people. I'm a bit worried if there's something wrong with my mental health?
description: I am usually considered relatively normal. I cry when watching inspirational movies or reading books about life and death. I can be moved and saddened. Last year, my mother underwent a major surgery, which was very serious and life-threatening. However, I had no reaction at all (no crying, no feeling of pressure), and I didn't feel sad or distressed. I was emotionally numb. This year, my father injured his leg, and it's also very serious, with the risk of paralysis. My family and relatives are very worried, and my mother cries every day because of this, developing anxiety disorder. But I don't have much reaction to this. My subconscious tells me, "Anyway, I am not the one with the leg injury, so it has nothing to do with me." Now I am a little worried if there is something wrong with my mental state.
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ Based on your description, it seems like you have a certain level of emotional detachment. #Science Education: Emotional detachment refers to a state of being unconcerned and indifferent towards things. Emotional disorders typically manifest in three forms: changes in the nature of emotions, changes in emotional fluctuations, and changes in emotional coordination. #From the events you described, it appears that you didn't have much emotional reaction to your family members' health conditions. It could be because you have distant relationships with your family members, so you feel like you don't have much connection with them, leading to a lack of emotional fluctuations. It could also be due to emotional detachment, but this aspect would require a diagnostic assessment at a hospital for a clear understanding. Take care~.

question: Recently, there have been significant fluctuations in emotions. Why is it not easy to get out of the low mood once I fall into it?
description: There was nothing significant that happened, and quitting during the pandemic caused some tension. Currently, I am doing a job that I enjoy, but sometimes I feel low, like everything is hopeless and I have no attachments. This feeling doesn't last long though. My sleep is also not good, I have trouble falling asleep and sometimes only get 2-3 hours a night. I don't think about anything and just play with my phone.

answers.answer_text: Congratulations, OP, on doing a job you love! Have you ever thought about how feeling down and staying up late are like a set of dominoes? Staying up late can make you feel down, especially if you're just playing with your phone instead of studying or enriching yourself. Is it because you feel like you're wasting time and lack self-discipline, which leads to feelings of sadness? If so, it's time to take action! Look for your interests, exercise, read books, and break free from being a slave to your phone. During the pandemic, I also went through a period of feeling down and not wanting to do anything, but realizing that I was wasting time made me even more depressed. So I enrolled in programming and writing courses, started exercising, and made good use of my time. The sense of despair disappeared because I felt like I had a plan! Time no longer passed slowly. Effort will yield results. I've maintained my six-pack abs and earned money from my writing. You can also achieve success in your favorite field! What you need to do now is to overcome procrastination, make a plan, and take action! I hope this can help you.

First, it is necessary to check if the thyroid function is normal. If there is hypothyroidism, symptoms of depression may appear inexplicably. Second, ruling out physical factors, we need to consider the following: 1) What is the impact of resigning on you? Are there any unresolved issues? If so, they may need to be addressed. 2) How much do you enjoy the job you are doing? Do you really enjoy it? 3) Under what circumstances do you feel low, and what can you do to improve the situation? 4) When did your sleep problems start? Is it difficulty falling asleep or waking up in the middle of the night and not being able to sleep? If the above symptoms have been present for a short period of time, it is recommended to try the following actions: 1) Maintain a regular sleep schedule, avoid using your phone one or two hours before bedtime, and instead, soak your feet, listen to music, or read a book. If you can't fall asleep after getting into bed, you can try activities such as meditation or focusing on your breathing to redirect your attention and facilitate sleep. 2) When you notice that you are not feeling well, get up immediately and move your body, make a phone call, take a walk, or pat your pillow, etc. 3) When you catch yourself overthinking, stop it immediately. You can repeat a sentence that you like, the name of someone you miss, or lyrics. In short, say something unrelated that can interrupt your overthinking. 4) Try to avoid negative news and depressing movies or TV shows recently. Engage in more relaxing activities such as cleaning your room, cooking a meal, or making a dessert, etc. If there is no improvement after continuing these actions for a week, it is recommended to seek help from a psychological counselor.

Hello, are you feeling low since you resigned during the pandemic? Perhaps the anxiety you felt when resigning was not resolved at the time and has continued until now. Firstly, I am glad that you have found a job that you enjoy after resigning. Can you try to think about why you felt down after resigning? Was it because you were worried about not finding a suitable job? Can you try to think about it again? If you still feel a bit low in mood, is it because there are some hidden worries in your heart? You mentioned that you enjoy the work you are currently doing, so can you try to think about what things in your job have made you happy since you started? Take your time, even the smallest things can be noted down to help you gradually experience positive emotions. You mentioned that your sleep is not great at the moment, have you tried practicing meditation before bed? Long-term meditation is very helpful for promoting sleep and maintaining emotional stability. If you experience difficulty concentrating when starting meditation, don't worry, it's normal. Take it slow. These are just a few suggestions, and I hope they can help you. Take care!

OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a virtual hug. From your description, I understand that you resigned during the pandemic and have now found a suitable job. However, sometimes you lack motivation and have trouble sleeping at night because you just want to play with your phone. You are aware that this state is not good and you want to change, which in itself is a positive signal for change and something to be happy about. 【A bit of analysis and advice】1. The pandemic and resignation are actually two types of life changes. Everyone has their own fixed rhythm of life and anticipated plans. The pandemic has disrupted almost everyone's plans. Students cannot go to school, employees cannot go to work, and some people resign. This in itself is a negative impact of the pandemic on people. Moreover, after a prolonged holiday period during the pandemic, it is normal for you to have difficulty returning to a normal work state. It will take some time for adjustment and buffering to get back to your original state. 2. My advice is not to rush. For things that you currently cannot do or do not want to do, divide them based on importance and urgency. Do a little bit each day or do a bit more each day. It cannot be achieved all at once. Perhaps you will gradually return to your previous work state.

question: It is easy to be influenced by intense emotions and feel distracted. What should I do?
description: I am easily influenced by strong emotions and unable to complete current tasks. I am constantly affected by events that have happened. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand how you feel. Lately, you have been easily affected by strong emotions and distractions. What I want to tell you is that it is not the events themselves that affect your emotions, but rather your perception of them. Our personal interpretation of the causes of events forms our final perspective on them, which in turn affects our emotions and triggers different behaviors. I don't know if you have heard of the "ABC theory". This theory was proposed by American psychologist Ellis in the 1960s. It emphasizes that it is our cognitive evaluation of something that triggers our negative or positive emotions and behavioral responses, not the events themselves. Every day, many things happen to everyone, and we continuously make explanations for the causes of these events. Over time, our brains develop a relatively stable explanatory style. Therefore, in many cases, even before we realize the process of interpretation, we have already subconsciously responded to events. This is why some people feel pessimistic and disappointed in the face of the same event, leading to negative actions, while others are motivated and start to strive continuously, ultimately achieving success. This shows that a person's explanatory style profoundly influences their physiological and psychological positive or negative changes and determines their persistence and success or failure. I hope you can correctly perceive your emotions and strive for true moments of happiness. Sometimes, putting yourself in someone else's shoes can bring unexpected results. Lastly, I wish you a happy and joyful life every day.

question: 31-year-old female, every job, interpersonal relationships being excluded and bullied?
description: In the office, I work in statistics and personnel. They talk about me behind my back, commenting on my weight whether I'm too fat or can't lose weight, even turning it into a song that I'm a fool and singing it all day long. When I got angry, I told HR, and they advised me to be mindful of my words, saying that those people are just immature. Later, I realized that the other two people are really close, making fun of me being fat and intentionally or unintentionally excluding me in their conversations. When I directly asked them, they denied it. I feel extremely upset, while they happily hang out together and show off in front of me every day.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts and disputes, deception and trust, colleagues.

answers.answer_text: Understanding the questioner's current mood, they work very hard at their job. However, they never expected to be made fun of by others for being overweight. It is difficult for them to accept and it makes them angry. They often hear people making fun of others who are not present in social situations, at work, or during offline gatherings. For example, they say things like, "Oh my, what kind of taste does he/she have?", "Who does he/she think they are?", "He/she is so dumb, why do they pretend to be something they're not?", "Whose person is he/she? How did they even get in here?", "He/she was so bizarre that day..." followed by laughter. Sometimes when the questioner is present, everyone laughs, and they feel they have to laugh too; otherwise, it would be awkward. After laughing, they actually feel that they shouldn't have joined in making fun of that person and can't help but think: since everyone likes to talk behind people's backs, they probably talk about them too when they're not around. This has been a way for people to maintain social connections throughout history and there's no need to worry too much about what others say behind our backs because we can't control their mouths. When people enjoy mocking and belittling others, they feel superior and their self-esteem and pride are greatly satisfied. Additionally, it is a process of self-growth and self-discipline. Especially in the workplace and work-related socializing, one must maintain their own work ability and professional standards, resist the urge to speak ill of others behind their backs, even though it feels good to laugh. A person with true leadership focuses more on self-improvement and tends to overlook others. It is believed that in the workplace, truly outstanding individuals don't waste their valuable time on trivial matters, but only those with inadequate abilities who want others' attention would enjoy mocking others behind their backs. When such a group of people is around, it is natural to block them out, ignore their presence, and focus on one's own abilities, qualities, and personal cultivation. Suggestions: 1- Don't take it to heart, strengthen your inner self and self-confidence. 2- If it really affects your happiness at work, your life, sleep, and you're unable to release stress, learn to establish your boundaries: politely tell the other person they have gone too far. Say "no" without being submissive or overbearing. 3- If the second suggestion is difficult, it is advised to establish good relationships with their superiors, supervisors, and leaders. Sometimes saying hello or socializing with them and returning to the office can slightly change the atmosphere. 4- Let's encourage each other. The most important thing is not to let it shake your confidence. I'm here, waiting for you!

Caring about what others think can either indicate lack of confidence, where one internalizes others' opinions and feels unwilling to be mocked or excluded, or a need for validation, an inability to tolerate loneliness, and a fear of being isolated. Therefore, 1. If one is indeed a bit overweight (which they say is true), they can change their lifestyle to lose weight, and then others won't be able to say anything. 2. If one doesn't care, it doesn't matter whether others are sincere or cunning, or whether they unite against you; it's all irrelevant. Just focus on doing your own thing and ignore them if you don't want to listen. After all, others have the right to speak. Perhaps they bully others to derive pleasure from their own unhappiness. When you get angry, they are happy. So, being indifferent and carrying on with what you should be doing is the best way to retaliate. 3. Improve yourself and become their superior; they will immediately change their attitude and try to please and flatter you every day.

Hello! You are a lovely and innocent little sister! Don't be sad, I'm here to help you! Firstly, it's most important to walk your own path. Be yourself, live your own life, without the need for others' evaluation and approval. This is a belief, a principle, and a correct outlook on life. Secondly, be brave in facing contradictions. If you indeed have flaws, don't be stubborn and unrepentant. On one hand, actively correct your interpersonal problems or inherent problems, and on the other hand, strive to change your image and actively show goodwill to them.
