Maintaining a suitable weight and paying attention to your health and managing your image are all important. This is a long-term process of persistence. I hope this helps you. If you need to contact me again, thank you!

Hello! I saw your anger, frustration, and helplessness in the office. How we handle relationships determines how they will be presented. Take a look at your other relationship patterns, perhaps you are not just having difficulty in the office. To handle relationships well, first understand yourself: what kind of person am I, do I have the courage to present my true self, how do I want to be treated, what will I think if others don't behave as I expect, why does others' attitude affect me... Many times, when we are true to ourselves, others dare not ridicule us. Those who ridicule you don't know how big the world is. Best wishes!

question: Do a person's strengths change with time and different life experiences?
description: I used to check Gallup for learning purposes. Now, in the assessment, the first advantage is creative thinking.
keywords: Occupation, occupational management, workplace interpersonal relationships, career choice skills.

answers.answer_text: Can strengths change? A baby won first place in a crawling competition, beating all the children in the family and all the babies in the hospital. At the age of two, they learned to walk and started walking and running every day. When they were four years old, their family still talked about their victory in the crawling competition. So they found a hospital to compete with the babies there, only to find that they couldn't beat the new champion in crawling. Why? Because for the past two years, they have been learning to walk and learning numbers, so they haven't crawled for a long time! Can people change? The questioner may have the belief that some people never change, but psychological assessments only reflect current states and are not fortune-telling. From the perspective of progress or decline, people have a lot of room for growth and a lot of potential for decline. As long as you make an effort, you can change. However, we can also discuss what can change and what cannot. Psychology defines two things: innate temperament and acquired character traits. Both are usually relatively stable, helping us understand a person's makeup. Even if character traits are acquired, they are still difficult to change. In China, there are many sayings that describe this, such as "the nature of the land is hard to change." This describes how difficult it is for a person's character to change. It's not impossible to change, just challenging. In long-term psychoanalytic therapy, many people have spent many years resolving their issues and embracing life again, breaking the cycle of their problems. It's difficult, but change is possible. As for temperament and character, they are very similar, but we define temperament as the innate part of character, so we won't discuss the part that can change. However, the advantage you mentioned is different, it is more like "ability" when compared to character. Abilities can be developed and nurtured. Schools, work, life, and interests constantly shape our lives. We have always known that they can change, and we have been actively changing them.

question: I have always felt somewhat awkward in front of people at times.
description: I am a lonely person with no friends. When I am in a good state of mind, I can take care of myself and live quite well. Even though I do things alone, I feel happy inside. But many times, my mood is not good and I feel lonely among crowds without any friends. My thoughts are conflicting, and I cannot control them. I feel that my body is stiff and clumsy, and I am very reserved in front of people. I am in so much pain...

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope my answer can provide you with some help. I sense that you are troubled by interpersonal problems and lack of friends. You have moments of happiness when you are alone, but also experience a lot of pain. You mentioned that your mood is often not good, you feel lonely in crowds, and you are shy and awkward in front of others. You are currently 20 years old, and I wonder if you have been lonely throughout your middle and high school years? If so, I want to give you a warm hug, because it must have been very difficult for many years to have a hard time opening up to others. In your process of growing up, something might have happened, not necessarily something big, but small setbacks that gradually led you to choose to close yourself off. This way of protecting yourself may have served its purpose in the past, but our lives will face different challenges. For example, you are now in university, which is the last "exercise" before entering society. In the university campus, you must have come across many new things and learned about the existence of many peers. Even if you are alone, there may be moments when you ponder about the future or when you look at others in groups. Being 20 years old is a stage of growth. Everyone has an inherent motivation to live positively, and at this stage, the self-protective strategy that you used in the past may now become the isolation barrier that keeps you lonely. You cannot solve the problem of loneliness on your own. Humans are social creatures, and although it may be difficult to find close friends or genuine connections, even having casual acquaintances can help alleviate loneliness. So, why not start with simple social interactions? You can create a list of social challenges ranked from easy to difficult, and start with the easiest one. You can learn some basic social skills, such as asking closed or polite questions about someone's career, education, family, or life experiences; asking open-ended questions to gather more information (for example, if you see someone reading a travel book, you can ask if they are planning to visit an interesting place); making positive or light-hearted comments; sincerely expressing praise; exchanging personal information and introducing yourself. Just be with yourself in front of others and do not judge your reactions. "I feel stiff and awkward in front of people" - I don't know if this is the main reason preventing you from talking to others, but the principle is the same. First, identify the behaviors or thoughts that prevent you from communicating with others. Usually, it's because you fear being rejected by others, and this fear leads you to self-rejection, and then you decide that as long as you don't take the first step, you won't be rejected. This self-rejection may come from your upbringing. If you rarely received encouragement and approval during childhood interactions with others, and instead received rejection and criticism, it is natural for you to avoid communication with others. So, accept yourself as you are now and acknowledge the survival skills that have brought you to this point. However, you also have the power to choose and change. Accept the awkward and stiff body reactions in front of others, try to relax, or you can even make it more tense, and you will find that these physical stiffness or social awkwardness do not have any catastrophic consequences, and you can still say what you want to say. Best wishes! The world and I love you.

Good evening, questioner! Rather than saying that the questioner has no friends, it might be more accurate to say that the questioner wishes to have friends who can seemingly get along so well with others. However, once the questioner truly understands the friendships they envy, they may have different thoughts. For example, how much effort is required to maintain these friendships? Or, as the saying goes, "a true friend is enough in life." Or even, "celebration is the loneliness of a group." In saying all this, the core point is that friends might not be as simple as the questioner imagines, and one may not be as lonely as one imagines. Each of us has our own unique personality; some people are good at socializing while others prefer solitude. Friends can be casual acquaintances, playmates, mutual users, or even toxic friends, but of course, there are also beneficial friends, truthful friends. It is not easy to gain a true friendship, as it requires mutual tempering and the passage of time. Let's not jump to conclusions so easily. On the whole, loneliness is something that everyone needs to face. No one is with oneself at every moment, faithfully accompanying oneself for a lifetime. Learn to face oneself calmly, and when in a good state, it might be worthwhile to try to break through and make friends with people who might become friends. This is a lifelong lesson that we all need to do. That's all, the world and I love you!

question: What is the reason why a 24-year-old man cannot feel close to anyone?
description: There is nothing wrong specifically, but I have noticed that I am in a state where I don't feel close to anyone, and I only feel comfortable and at ease when I am alone. Interactions with other people are only out of politeness or when I need something from them. Even when I go out with friends, I am not willing to actively engage with them. Is this state not normal? Is there a psychological disorder behind it?

answers.answer_text: It is not a mental illness, don't worry~ Generally speaking, people have an inner world and an outer world. What we understand as introverted people are actually people with a rich inner world. The energy within them is sufficient to support their daily life, so they don't need to seek energy from others. Therefore, they may appear quiet and immersed in their own world. On the other hand, extroverted people are the opposite. They enjoy hanging out with friends and gaining energy through social interactions, finding their value in relationships. In my opinion, you seem to be a bit like the introverted person I mentioned earlier, and that's a good thing, so don't worry. For difficult mental health questions, personal psychological healing and growth, visit our WeChat account: xdxl33.

question: 33 years old, working together, want to break up, difficult to let go, what should I do?
description: Over time, feelings developed and I ended up being with my boss after drinking too much. He is five years younger than me, and now it has been over seven months. I tend to overthink things, and he has been in a seven-year-long relationship without getting married. He promised me that he would break up with her after another six months when the new store stabilizes. Every day feels like torture, but we work together, so we see each other every day. We truly love each other and can't be apart. I keep telling myself to let go, but I can't do it. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, I can tell that you are going through a lot of pain right now, and you don't know what to do. Because you got drunk, you ended up being involved with your boss, and now you are in a romantic relationship with him. However, he already has a girlfriend, and they have been together for 7 years. It's possible that he doesn't have strong feelings for you since you were only together because of alcohol. If he really wanted to break up with his girlfriend, he wouldn't have to wait until things are stable. Maybe he is just observing their relationship. You might not even be considered as a backup plan in his mind. If you can't let go, you can express your worries and your true feelings to him. It's time to put an end to your relationship and if he is willing to be with you, he should break up with his girlfriend immediately. But if he can't do that, you have to make the decision to leave decisively and not drag it out. Because in the end, you will be the one hurt. It might also hurt the other person involved. But what's certain is that you and his girlfriend will be equally hurt. Best wishes~.

question: How to have more topics to talk about with parents?
description: I am a freshman and when I entered university, I saw my roommates having enjoyable conversations with their parents. I feel a bit envious. When I talk to my parents on the phone, we can only talk about recent events or discuss matters that need to be resolved. After that, we don't know what else to talk about. They also don't say much and just tell me to study hard and do my best. Actually, I want to talk about other things, but I don't know how to bring them up. Maybe I'm just a bit introverted. How can I start a conversation with them?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, our parents are our first teachers. They gave us life and raised us, and now we have entered the university stage. There are so many college students in this world, and everyone's experiences are different, as well as the level of relationship with their parents in the family. Those who have a good relationship may have no secrets and can talk about anything, while others may feel a barrier and differentiate what they can and cannot say before speaking. I believe that the topics your roommate talks about with their parents on the phone should not be much different from yours. They probably talk about their recent situation or when there is something to discuss. Maybe your roommate also thinks that you have a good relationship with your parents. If you want to improve your relationship with your parents, you can make some appropriate jokes during phone calls to enhance your bond. You can also observe the tone they use when talking to their parents on a regular basis. Best wishes~.

question: My mother is excessively concerned about me and excessively worried. Is my mother sick?
description: I am the only child in my family. Since I started studying and working in a different city from my mom, she has been excessively concerned about me. The specific behaviors are a bit strange, but I can't quite put my finger on it. For example, my mom starts sending me WeChat messages saying "good morning" before 6 a.m. every day. Then she asks me how I'm feeling every day, always assuming that I must not be in a good mood, even though I never tell her that. Actually, I'm in a pretty good mood, but her constant questioning about my mood makes me feel a bit unsettled. And when she doesn't feel well herself, like catching a cold or having diarrhea, she assumes that I must have the same symptoms. It's the weirdest thing. So, I wanted to ask if my mom is sick.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, family health.

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your venting, it is clear that you are also very worried about your mother. You are a sensible and filial child, and I commend you for that. As a mother with only one child, especially when the child goes to another city for studying or working, it is natural for her to be concerned. The outside world is big, exciting, and full of dangers. However, I understand that excessive attention makes you uncomfortable. I think your mother might not have many hobbies or have a light workload, so she focuses all her energy on you. You can suggest your mother to expand her social circle and cultivate some hobbies, like sports, singing, dancing, yoga, etc., to shift her attention and prioritize her own life. Best wishes to you!

question: 20 years old, recently for the past half month, every day I can't help but want to cry because of various things...?
description: In the past half month, I have been feeling sad every day because of being ignored by my friends. When I talk to them about it, they don't feel like they have ignored me and think that I am overthinking. I have experienced similar situations before, but in the past half month, I have been so sad every day that I can't help but want to cry. This emotional state has made it difficult for me to complete my daily tasks normally, and the ups and downs of these emotions make me feel exhausted. I don't feel like socializing and just want to be in my own space.

answers.answer_text: We humans are constantly battling with ourselves throughout our lives. When our emotions become overly negative, we try to rescue ourselves and pull ourselves out of the vortex of unhappiness. When our emotions become too high and we become excited, even under the influence of alcohol, our brains quickly calm ourselves down to prevent impulsive regret. I hope you can learn to control your emotions and understand how they affect your life and career. I hope my answer can bring you some enlightenment. First, negative restlessness and excited excitement are like two ends of a balance scale. As human beings with seven emotions and six desires, we are naturally influenced by all kinds of emotional stimuli. We become very unstable because we cannot control our mindset. Just like a bowl of water swaying, you will feel very restless. The vicious effects of extreme emotions will follow one after another. (1) You need to become the master of your own emotions, not a slave to them. Only when you can control your emotions can you avoid being overwhelmed by them. Our brains are signal receivers for emotions, and we need to constantly judge, filter, and process the information in our minds. We then make rational behavioral responses based on this information. In this process, we weigh the pros and cons and make decisions and choices as quickly as possible. In this way, people can better balance gains and losses, not only avoiding harm to ourselves, but also ensuring that our genuine reactions do not attack our friends, family, or loved ones. However, it is impossible for a person to always achieve emotional perfection. When we are sensitive and disturbed, we become irritated; when we are complacent, we may blurt out things we shouldn't. These are all caused by our overly extreme emotions, whether it's excitement or distress, both can make you feel pain. So, once you find that you cannot control your emotions for a long time and you are deeply troubled, you must calm yourself down and try to regain control of your emotions with rationality.

Hello, OP. I understand your helplessness. Problem analysis: Recently, you have frequently felt upset because you feel that your friends are not paying enough attention to you and are ignoring you. However, when you try to confirm your subjective feelings with your friends, they think they haven't been ignoring you and believe that you're just being oversensitive. It seems that your pain stems from a discrepancy between your subjective feelings and your friends' actual behavior. In the past, you faced similar situations. So how did you handle those situations and alleviate your emotions? Aside from feeling neglected by your friends, are there any other events that make you want to cry? It seems like you have been experiencing this urge to cry every day for the past two weeks, and you don't want to socialize, just wanting to be alone. It appears that you may be in a state of depression. Suggestions: 1. Recognize the connection between specific incidents with your friends and your emotions, and communicate your thoughts to them. Give them suggestions, such as pointing out that when they don't ask for your opinion during meal times, it makes you feel neglected, and you hope they can consult you next time. 2. Considering that your negative state has been ongoing for two weeks without improvement and has caused significant distress in your life, with your family accompanying you, you can go to the hospital for some examinations related to depressive symptoms. If there are any issues, you can receive timely intervention and treatment. 3. Choose effective ways to relieve and ease your emotions, such as exercising/meditating, confiding in trusted individuals, or scheduling appointments with professional counselors to delve deeper into the roots of your emotions. Best wishes.

Hello, OP. First of all, hugs to you. Indeed, I have also experienced a period of being prone to crying and having emotions. It seems that your description may not be complete, for example, is it just recently that you started crying, or have you been crying over certain things before? In the past half month, besides feeling ignored by your friends, have you also encountered other situations that made you more sensitive and easily emotional? Crying is actually not a bad thing. First, you need to accept your emotions and state of mind. To some extent, being able to cry is a way to relieve and detoxify your soul, so you should not think of yourself as having a big problem. Secondly, let's see if we can find more rational solutions together. After each cry, we should not let it be in vain. We can summarize with friends so that the next time you won't feel as saddened, and avoid repeatedly using crying to solve problems. This process of reflection is actually quite important. For example, you can chat with friends and express your anxiety and worries. They will deny one by one and say that those things won't happen, then you should firmly believe in their understanding: trust your friends and believe that it's just your overthinking. If we often think this way, we will easily break free from anxious and negative thinking patterns and not let them affect us. Additionally, you can take the time to reflect on your childhood experiences and whether you have experienced neglect from your family. In the past, when you felt helpless, did you often try to alleviate your emotions with sadness and crying? If that's the case, your frequent crying now is actually a learned way of dealing with things from your childhood. Because some basic coping mechanisms are easily ingrained in us from a very young age. Therefore, it requires us to empathize with and accept our younger selves, understand our emotions at that time, and allow our present selves to no longer live in the shadows. Keep going, there is no major problem. I hope that after you cry, every day will be a sunny day for you!

Hello friend! Every day, I feel upset because of my friends' neglect, but they think there is actually nothing wrong. This is simply a difference in perception. Let me tell you a story: There was a person who really liked a certain car. However, because they didn't have the money to buy it at that time, they had to put it aside. Recently, due to their hard work at work, they received a reward from their boss and finally bought the car they had always wanted. They were very happy and drove the car back. However, on the way, they saw many cars similar to their own, either in appearance, color, or brand. They thought to themselves, "So many people like this type of car!" However, in reality, the styles of the cars were all similar, but they had failed to notice it before. Now that they have bought their own car, their focus has shifted, and they tend to associate any similar cars they see with their own. Why is this? It is mainly because they have bought a car and their subconscious attention has changed, so they tend to notice many cars that are similar to their own. What is the message I want to convey? Is it possible that recent events have reminded you of some memories and triggered certain thoughts that just won't go away, making you feel uneasy and ignored? Therefore, in your interactions with friends, you are eagerly searching for evidence to support this uneasiness. As a result, your friends' normal behavior is interpreted as neglect towards you, even though they do not have such intentions. Many times, emotions come without warning, and we have no idea what triggered them. It is likely that memories hidden in our subconscious mind are being activated. Since they are hidden in the subconscious, we are unable to detect what caused our feelings. Of course, this is just a personal speculation, hoping to give you a different perspective to understand yourself. Lastly, I want to say that no matter what, the world and I love you!

question: You are never satisfied with your romantic relationships. How to manage and nurture relationships between genders?

Is it related to one's sense of security in relationships or to how one manages the relationship, or is it related to the partner? If someone often thinks about someone they used to have a crush on, what does that person mean to them? Take some time to think about the type of romantic relationship one desires and the qualities they want in a partner. I suddenly thought of a lyric, "'What is unattainable is always in turmoil, those who are favored have nothing to fear". Hello, from your question I can see that despite being dissatisfied with your romantic relationship, you are still trying to improve it. Hello! From your description, I understand that you are not satisfied with your romantic relationship. I don't know your age or occupation, but I wonder if you have reached the age for marriage. If you are not satisfied with your romantic relationship, take some time to reflect on what kind of person you need as a lifetime partner. question: Feel like many of it was "cheated" into their hands, lacking a sense of achievement?
description: I feel that the money I earn and the excellent girlfriends I have had are mostly obtained through "deception". answers.answer_text: My response: Hello! I saw your question. You are able to observe your behavior and reflect on it, which is wiser than most people and shows your agile thinking. However, I also see your confusion. According to your description, I see several issues that may be your life challenges. As long as it doesn't violate morals, ethics, or laws, you also need to accept yourself. The "lack of a sense of accomplishment" you mentioned is just a surface phenomenon, actually reflecting the emptiness in your heart. Where is your value? What contributions have you made to society? Accept your "techniques" because it is your style of doing things. You can't change it all at once, and you don't want to lose all the skills you have acquired through so much effort. Accept yourself as you are and strive to become your true self. 2. You can try changing some of your thoughts, for example, while asking questions, also reflect on yourself. This is great, as it is the first step towards change. For example, you can find a blank piece of paper, write down the things that are important to you, and then cross out everything else, leaving only one thing. That one thing is what you truly want. 3. Exchange sincerity with sincerity. If you are sincere enough, everyone will be able to feel it and will definitely respond to you sincerely. Best wishes and grateful to have connected with you.

Hello! Through careful reading of your description, I can deeply feel that you care about this sense of achievement, which is actually a reflection of a sense of inner lack. Because you yourself know that you have obtained a so-called girlfriend or money through certain methods, the word "cheater" you used can help imagine a very elusive feeling, it does not exist in reality. And our conscience, that is, our inner essence, in order to truly feel comfortable, we should live in the present moment, truly love and truly exist. This will make us feel more grounded and at peace. Ah, now you are experiencing the feeling of being a cheater and lacking a sense of achievement, these two words you used, I think they represent your current emotions and psychological state. From that perspective, you are more eager for true love, or the genuine love that comes from the bottom of your heart, and after obtaining that, you can gain a wealth of energy and a sense of fulfillment. In fact, when you are talking to your girlfriend or trying to get money from clients, when you use the word "cheater," you can feel that throughout the whole process, your energy is scattered outward instead of being absorbed inward. As a result, you gradually feel a lack of achievement. So, if you have time, I suggest you engage in some public welfare activities, such as visiting children in welfare homes or children with autism, or helping stray dogs. You can find some organizations in your city and go once a week or for a period of time. By doing this, it will help fulfill your other energy needs. When you go there, it should be voluntary and just a simple act of helping them. You will feel a different sense of energy. Best wishes.

Feel that many things are "cheated" to get, lack of a sense of achievement? Hello, OP, first of all, I understand and sympathize with your situation, and I want to give you a big hug to make you feel the warmth of the world. In fact, regarding your situation, we can explain it in terms of your need for achievements. The reason why you feel that you lack a sense of achievement is based on Maslow's hierarchy of needs. There are five levels of human needs, and after satisfying basic physiological and safety needs, we pursue higher levels. For example, the sense of achievement you are currently seeking, if you cannot find a girlfriend or make money, you will not talk about the so-called sense of achievement. Only when you have a girlfriend or make money, you will feel that your sense of achievement is not high enough. So, you do not lack a sense of achievement, but you feel that this sense of achievement comes too easily and does not meet your desired level and needs. Therefore, we might as well slow down, set goals gradually, that is, what things can truly achieve your so-called sense of achievement, rather than just focusing on making money and "cheating" a girlfriend. For example, if you go to the gym or running today, or if you don't have supper, etc., doing some self-disciplined things, often you will gain a higher sense of achievement. So what OP needs now is to seek something beyond your cognitive range in order to achieve a higher sense of achievement, rather than staying in the fixed circle of making money and "cheating" a girlfriend, where you can find a so-called sense of achievement. But I also hope that OP can recognize one fact, which is that no matter what, you are very intelligent and capable, because that kind of "cheating" is not entirely in the true sense, but rather you understand people's psychology and make choices and actions based on that. Wish OP happiness and joy.

Hello, OP. If you believe that the money you've earned and the excellent girlfriend you have are all obtained through deception, then you're really something. Actually, whether it's packaging or not, it doesn't matter. At least you have the ability to package yourself, which is a skill just like sales. Selling oneself requires packaging oneself and using sales techniques to increase credibility and improve product sales. What you're doing is not selling products, but selling yourself. You have successfully sold yourself. In this process, you enjoy a great sense of accomplishment because you have succeeded. However, afterwards, you're afraid that this success is only fake and not the real you. So the question you're contemplating is: what does the un-packaged version of yourself look like? What kind of person does the excellent girlfriend like? If you were to let go of the packaging, would the girlfriend break up with you? The establishment of a relationship cannot be based on deception. So, what are you seeking? Maybe you would say that you are seeking her excellence. But if, after being together for a long time, you discover her imperfections, would you stop loving her and consider breaking up? Nobody is perfect. The reason you think all of this is a deception is that you lack confidence in your true self. You know your imperfections, and you are smart enough to know what others like about you. That's why you hide your weaknesses and package your strengths to become a successful person in the eyes of others, and then gain a sense of achievement. When you strip away all of this, anxiety arises. Why don't we try accepting our imperfections? Just like how you have encountered many people and surely discovered their imperfections, including those excellent girlfriends, how do they deal with their imperfections? Try accepting them, and then interact with them calmly. You will find that those flaws you have been hiding, the girlfriend has long since discovered, but she still loves you for who you are.

Hello, OP, I hope my answer can be of some help to you. After carefully reading your description, it seems that you feel that the money you earn and the girlfriends you have had are mostly obtained through "deception". You believe that it is because you have used strategies and techniques that you have acquired these things, and you feel that they did not initially like you but only grew to like you through your inducements and techniques. And if you don't use these inducements and techniques, you believe that you would not be able to obtain these things, hence feeling a lack of a sense of accomplishment. Is this correct? My feeling is that you want to be a more authentic version of yourself, hoping that when earning money and being in a relationship, you can be true to yourself rather than meeting the other person's needs and making them depend on you. Isn't that right? You hope that they like the real you and in all types of relationships, you can let go of overthinking, and this version of you without any "strategies" or "inducements" is also someone they would like. Isn't that right? Now from another perspective, is that version of you that is able to meet their needs the real you? Or perhaps, you can sincerely ask them why they like you and are willing to pay money to you, what qualities of yours do they value, maybe it's different from what you imagine. In reality, perhaps this matter has nothing to do with others, it's just that you don't like this version of yourself. Notice the voice within your heart, reflect on why you have such thoughts, and what kind of self do you desire? Take it slow, as long as we are willing, we can definitely get closer and closer to the self we desire.

question: Is it normal to have a poor emotional connection with parents and siblings?
description: I have always felt that the emotional connection between myself and my parents, as well as my siblings, has not been good since I was little (although it may be just my one-sided perception). However, there are still moments when I am moved and deeply touched. A few days ago, a friend came to my house and talked to me for a long time, and she cried a lot. She said she feels sorry for her parents and wants to treat them well, but she just can't seem to do it.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: OP, your parents and siblings are the closest people to you, and they all love you very much. Maybe some of their behaviors may seem inappropriate to you, but I hope you can open your heart and communicate more with your family. Take the initiative to talk to them about your thoughts and feelings. Your family is always the strongest support system, and home is the warmest harbor. If you want to be good to your parents but can't do it, it may be because you're not very good at expressing your emotions. Perhaps you can give yourself more psychological hints on a regular basis. You can also communicate more with your parents. Maybe you can express your emotions to your parents every day, frequently saying things like "I love you" and "thank you." Perhaps you can also help with household chores at home to share the burden with your parents. I believe you can definitely express your love for your parents. Best wishes!

question: What should I do if I start to like someone? I always have trouble concentrating in class.
description: I am constantly attracted by the boy sitting next to me. I can't concentrate in class and can't help but glance at him. Even when I'm doing homework at home, my mind is filled with thoughts of him. But I always feel like he's not interested in me. We don't interact much, and he spends all his time playing with other girls. My close friends advise me to give up, but even though I say I will, I still like him. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, don't suppress your emotions. Whatever is suppressed will eventually come to the surface. Handle your emotions and feelings in an appropriate way that doesn't affect your normal studying and life. From your description, it seems that you have developed feelings for a boy, and you miss him and pay attention to his every move, which is affecting your normal state. First, identify your own feelings. Do you like him? What specific aspects of him attract you? You need to answer these questions yourself because the things that attract us are often things we lack ourselves. When you have a clear understanding that you like him, and it's romantic attraction rather than just admiration, then you may know what to do. Having romantic feelings is not a bad thing. Caring about and getting close to someone can teach us many things, such as giving and waiting. Analyze your current state of mind, understand your purpose in this matter so that you won't be entangled or in pain. Did you choose to give up because he doesn't have feelings for you? Or because you can't have a relationship yet or it would affect your studies, so you can't take the next step? Or do you want to forget about him or not like him, in order to focus on your classes and studies? If your goal is to focus on your studies, you can try to concentrate your attention in class. It's okay to take a glance, but then bring your focus back to the lesson and use your willpower to redirect your attention instead of constantly getting immersed in thoughts about him. In the early stages of liking someone, they can indeed occupy our minds, but as long as we repeatedly bring our attention back to ourselves, gradually, we can control our yearning and daydreaming. If your goal is to be together, regardless of who opposes it, you can naturally get closer to him and gradually let him know your feelings, learn to give and express your care. If his response is cold and distant, you may need to quickly withdraw your emotions. However, you still need to maintain your studying state. Even if you and him are in a relationship, the two of you need to discuss and plan how to maintain a positive and supportive relationship without affecting your studies, your friendships, and your relationships with family, etc. You can care for each other and be there for each other, but it should always be a result of 1+1>2, rather than causing any harm to either of you. Good luck.

question: Does having the first child determine the rest of one's life?
description: As I sit here typing, my eyes are feeling a bit sore. I don't know how I got through that period, and I don't even know where to begin. In May of this year, I had an abortion for my first child. I dreamt that it was a little girl. Only God knows... Now, I'm moody and unwilling to communicate with the outside world. I can spend every day at home, with my sleep time gradually getting longer. Perhaps you can understand, and I'm glad to have someone who can empathize. If you don't understand, then I have nothing more to say.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, emotional regulation, fragile tears.

answers.answer_text: ~~Give the OP a warm hug. From the description, I can feel the OP's emotions. I also feel very sorry for the loss of the first baby. I feel heartbroken for what you are going through right now. I believe that every mother considers their children of utmost importance, even if they are no longer with us. I'm sure the OP has very complex but sincere feelings for the baby. Therefore, I can understand these thoughts of the OP very well. On the other hand, I am also very worried about the OP's current emotional state. From the description, I feel that the OP may already have depressive emotions (note that this is not the same as clinical depression). We may not be able to start over and make up for past regrets, but the future is still waiting for us to get better. For these current low emotions, I think it would be best for the OP to seek help from professionals who can provide more detailed assistance. On the other hand, the OP may consider starting with trusted and close people around them to increase communication, which can also help us relieve our emotions.

question: How can I overcome my fear of advocating for my own interests and feeling powerless?
description: I dare not take the initiative to fight for my own interests, I am always afraid of arguing with others, would rather suffer in silence, avoid problems, and cannot face them. I feel powerless and do not know how to change. I always have a negative view of myself and feel useless. What should I do in this situation?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I carefully read your question. In your question, I see that you have always felt like you are in a passive state in interpersonal relationships, unable to effectively protect your own interests. You often feel a lack of inner strength and have been wanting to change but cannot find a way to do so. This feeling can be distressing, as the sense of powerlessness and frustration of not being able to attain what you desire can lead to a cycle of defeat and loss. So, how should we view and improve our own issues? In understanding your interpersonal communication style, communication styles can be divided into five types: competitive, accommodating, avoiding, compromising, and collaborating. These differences in human personality are actually differentiated based on the dimensions of "concern for interests" and "value for relationships". In your question, you value both your interests and relationships, without leaning excessively towards one dimension. However, for some reason, you ultimately choose to avoid problem-solving, seemingly feeling uncomfortable facing the issues, but also unable to let go of your interests and relationships. Therefore, you seem more like someone with an "avoiding" communication style. This style is actually the least beneficial in interpersonal interactions since it leads to neither gaining interests nor relationships. The resulting inner turmoil can make you feel exceptionally uncomfortable. Therefore, we need to think about how to improve our communication style. Explore the underlying stories behind your "avoiding" style. When you have feelings and states such as "fear," "feeling wronged," and "feeling powerless" in interpersonal relationships, what do you associate them with? In your mind, when did these feelings start? I don't know what experiences you have been through, but certain memories have made you fearful and anxious about the external environment. Although these images have become blurred over time, these emotions remain intact and are inadvertently activated. Therefore, what I want to tell you is that the fear and anxiety you feel in current interpersonal relationships are actually manifestations of past feelings, a "misjudgment" of the current environment. Because of those memories, you developed a subconscious signal that says "the external environment is dangerous," and this subconscious language has become the background color of your interpersonal relationships. All your thoughts and ideas are based on the cognition that "I believe the environment is very dangerous." As a result, you feel afraid, sensitive, and fearful. Of course, exploring your own story cannot directly solve the problem, but it can help you generate awareness, enabling you to recognize when you are in a state of "misjudgment" when facing problems in the future. This can allow you to try to break free from this biased perception and create possibilities for establishing new communication relationships. By consciously becoming a "collaborator" in relationships, both internally and externally, you can construct a better communication style. To become a collaborative communicator, the most important thing is to give up a one-sided mindset – the idea that believes the benefits of a matter are limited: "If I take 40%, you will have only 60% left." This is a typical zero-sum game thinking. In this mindset, the benefits are predefined from the beginning, leaving no possibility for creating new value and interests. However, collaboration fundamentally changes this thinking. It allows us to see that the value and benefits of a matter can be expanded through collaboration, creating more possibilities. In collaboration, we can gain more than 100% satisfaction. This is a better outcome for both parties, as you can not only gain relationships but also benefits. Therefore, when you encounter an issue related to interests, try to first become aware of yourself and then actively consider the communication style you want to adopt. Learn to see the collaborative increment in the matter. Gradually, through effort and change, you will gain a sense of value and confidence, thereby improving your interpersonal communication style. I hope the above response is helpful to you.

Hi there. Are you feeling frustrated, helpless, and worthless because you don't dare to assert yourself, always give up your own interests, and avoid problems? Since you're here asking for advice, it indicates that you have the desire to change and to become more empowered in facing and handling issues, as well as being more resilient in dealing with the difficulties that might arise. Your passive surrendering is not entirely a bad thing, and it must have brought you some benefits. It can be inferred that your coping strategy for dealing with problems has mainly been avoidance, compromise, and giving up, which may have caused you to lose out on what was rightfully yours. However, isn't there any silver lining to this approach? From what I can see, there are advantages, such as not having to argue with others, avoiding truly confronting and addressing problems, and not having to endure the frustration of failure in seeking what you want. In summary, it has saved you a lot of effort and spared you the difficulties and pain. On the other hand, if you make an effort to fight for what you deserve, you will have to face and handle the aforementioned problems and endure various uncertainties. Of course, the benefit is an increased chance of obtaining what you want. So, both choices have their advantages. Your behavior merely aligns with what you believe deep down. When you feel increasingly aggrieved and unhappy, you need to ask yourself, which benefits do you lean more towards when comparing the two choices? In other words, which kind of pain do you prefer or can better bear? If you can discern your own true answer, I believe you will find the path you should take. The reasons that caused you to feel this way are not important, and the problems that hinder you from taking action are also not important. We often analyze why an individual has formed their unique patterns of thinking and behavior, and we also list the factors that prevent us from reaching our goals. However, people will also find themselves stuck and unable to move forward, even after understanding the cause and effect and identifying the problem. This is because problems constantly arise and never disappear. Does this mean we should just keep standing still? This is the point I want to share: all those aforementioned things are not important. What is important is that you genuinely need to take action. It is certainly easier to take action when there are no difficulties, but even when facing difficulties, there is a way to take action. Find your own resources and strengths, and truly act. Before you take action, remember: if you don't succeed in fighting for something, it's normal; it simply means that this time, this particular matter was unsuccessful, but it doesn't mean you have failed. Gain more experience, build different interpersonal relationships, listen to how others evaluate you, and avoid getting trapped in a cycle of self-denial. What you think others say negatively about you may not be true; it may be something you imagined. You can find ways to access resources, including but not limited to: 1) Do you have any examples from your past where you successfully stood your ground or fought for your own success? Anything will do. If you do, think about how you felt and what you learned from that experience. 2) How do people around you fight for their own interests, and what methods and approaches can you learn from and emulate? 3) Do you have someone in your life who can offer advice and help in this area? 4) Practice from daily trivial matters; start experiencing what it feels like to defend your position, and when you succeed, summarize it and continue practicing. In short, any change starts with tiny steps. No matter how much you ponder, it can't compare to the impact of a genuine experience. I sincerely wish you can soon overcome this predicament and become the person you want to be. Good luck.

Hello OP! I see your question: "I don't dare to actively fight for my own interests and feel powerless. What should I do? I'm afraid of conflicts because I've been seriously deprived of my rights before, and since then, I feel unworthy. The fear of conflicts stems from past conflicts that have created inner conflicts within myself, making me afraid to confront them directly. If you want to fight for your interests without relying on fair distribution, it is likely that others have overstepped their boundaries and failed to allocate them correctly to you. In this situation, it is possible that the impression you give others is relatively weak, allowing them to believe they can take advantage, or even though you strongly desire it internally, you give off an impression of not wanting to engage with the world, naturally leading others to not lean towards you. When you give in, you only burden yourself; when you avoid problems, you face them alone. Where does your strength come from? First, you must not deplete your own strength, which means not avoiding or victimizing yourself. Unite all your strength and project it outwardly. When fighting for your own interests, there will inevitably be arguments with others. As long as it is within reasonable limits, once you obtain what rightfully belongs to you, what can others say? What right do they have to obstruct your interests? As long as you express yourself with reason and evidence, with courtesy and composure, without using attacking language and attitude to argue, you won't have face-to-face conflicts with others. You can use those voices that used to deny yourself to encourage and motivate yourself. In your heart, consider yourself and others as equals, with a friendly mindset, and face yourself and others accordingly. The fears and retreats you experienced in the past belong to the past. The people you encounter are different, and their attitudes towards you are different. Only by daring to speak up for yourself can others truly respect you. You can start training from now on, affirm yourself more, find your own strengths, praise yourself more, and encourage yourself to try to defend your legitimate rights. Every little progress you make and every bit of strength you gain will increase your confidence and help you become a strong and confident version of yourself in the future! I hope this answer can help you. Cheering for you!

When we were young, our elders always taught us that suffering is a blessing, but they did not tell us that this is a dog-eat-dog society, which has led to many people being submissive when they enter society. 1. Opportunities are for those who are prepared, but we also need to seize the opportunity. Let's take an example in the workplace: there are often situations where the project period is tight, and the superiors entrust us with important tasks and promise some benefits. However, after the project is launched, they take all the credit for themselves and do not mention the previous commitments at all. How should we handle this? We can choose to be patient and hope that the other party will promote us if they have a conscience. But in similar situations in the future, will we still give our all? Will we hold any grudges? Or we can choose to confront the other party, take some time to talk to them and ask how they plan to handle this matter. If the other party promises again, it's best to keep some audio or written evidence for potential needs. If the other party refuses to admit it, or even threatens us, we can also keep some evidence to protect our legitimate interests. In fact, the most important point is our own value. If this matter is indispensable, then our value is irreplaceable. We will be proactive. But if we are dispensable and can be replaced at any time, then most of the time we will be passive. Therefore, accumulation and self-improvement in daily life are very important, especially when we have opportunities to showcase our abilities. If we have the ability to challenge, it is best not to be afraid, because if the leader is willing to give us the opportunity, it means that they have already considered the possibility of failure, so all we need to do is try our best. 2. Start with small things and simple tasks. Many times, we look down on small things or doubt ourselves, thinking that we are not competent and dare not try. In fact, every big thing is composed of small things, and what we need to do is start from small things, try first, and not be afraid of failure, gradually finding our own value. Let's take an example: our superiors assign us a task that we have never encountered before. How should we approach it? First, we can look for relevant cases and see if there are any areas we can learn from. Create a rough outline and process. Then, learn to make good use of the resources around us. If our superiors have experience in this area, we can consult them about our plan. If they are also handling it for the first time, we can report the progress and direction to them. Finally, learn to regularly review and adjust the direction, as things may not go as expected and plans may change. So, we need to be adaptable. We can learn from failures and not be too proud of successes, as losing is not scary because we won't keep falling in the same place. The world loves you and so do I.

Hello there!※ I don't dare to actively pursue my own interests, always afraid of arguing with others, would rather suffer in silence, avoid problems, and not face them. I feel powerless, and I want to change but don't know how. I always have negative thoughts about myself and feel useless. I don't dare to fight for my own interests and always criticize myself internally. The main reason is lack of self-confidence, which results in low self-esteem and the absence of the courage to express oneself or fight for one's rights. Therefore, the key to solving this problem lies in overcoming self-doubt and building self-confidence. Self-confidence itself is a kind of positivity, an optimistic attitude towards self-evaluation. The lack of self-confidence leads to weak, incomplete, and low-effective positivity. Self-confidence is a heartfelt self-affirmation and belief. It is crucial in interpersonal relationships, careers, and work. Only when you believe in yourself will others believe in you. Social psychologist Bandura proposed a theory called self-efficacy, which refers to "the degree of confidence in one's ability to utilize the skills one possesses to accomplish a certain task." In addition to outcome expectations, Bandura also emphasized the importance of efficacy expectations. Outcome expectations refer to people's predictions about the consequences of their behavior. If people anticipate that a particular behavior will lead to a specific outcome, that behavior is more likely to be activated and chosen. Therefore, the key to building self-confidence is to believe that you can succeed, not only in terms of the expected results but also in having confidence in yourself to do the task. Only by establishing a strong sense of self-efficacy can one overcome self-doubt and regain self-confidence. In work and study, do not constantly negate yourself. Give yourself some encouragement and do not impose limitations on yourself before even starting. Break free from these limiting beliefs and find the feeling of confidence and freedom within yourself! Best wishes!

Hello Questioner! I'm glad to answer your inner concerns. "I am afraid to actively pursue my own interests, always afraid of arguing with others, would rather endure grievances, avoid problems, and not dare to face them. I feel powerless in my heart and want to change but don't know how to change? I always have a negative view of myself and feel useless. What should I do in this situation?" Due to factors such as our innate temperament, genetic factors, and upbringing, we have developed our current thinking and behavior patterns. When you feel uncomfortable with your self-perception and way of dealing with things, I believe it is also the moment you start to become aware of yourself. When you reflect on yourself, it is also the first step towards change. Not daring to actively pursue your own interests indicates that you have a weak sense of self-boundary or no sense of self-boundary. When your sovereignty is violated by others but you dare not resist, I believe it will make you feel very suppressed, uncomfortable, and even hurt. Assertiveness is a person's vitality. When a person lacks assertiveness outwardly, their assertiveness will turn inward and attack themselves. Attacking oneself internally creates a sense of repression, grievances, a belief of being useless, and can even lead to depression. So, I understand your terrible feelings. Sometimes we think that when we feel uncomfortable being violated, we would rather suppress ourselves and not attack others because we are afraid of offending them, making them unhappy, hurting them, or affecting the image they have of us in their minds, and so on. However, sometimes the consequence of doing so is that others will take advantage of us even more and disrespect us. Having appropriate assertiveness and healthy assertive behavior is about safeguarding our sovereignty and gaining respect from others. This is a powerful approach. Why do we all envy those who have very smooth emotions? It is because they have their own boundaries and sovereignty, which they maintain. This makes people live more openly and allows others to realize their boundaries, without affecting the relationship between them. Therefore, to be a refreshing person, it is necessary to have our own boundary of sovereignty. We also have an obligation to safeguard our own boundary of sovereignty and have a responsibility to live our lives more smoothly. I hope my analysis and advice can help you a little. The road to change is difficult, but I believe you can do it! Keep going! The world will always love you.

Hello, dear questioner. After reading your question, I can sense your anxiety about wanting to change yourself but not knowing how to take action. Your lack of self-confidence leads to constant self-denial, and your somewhat weak personality prevents you from being brave enough to actively pursue your own interests, causing you to choose to escape. Here, I will provide you with a few suggestions in the hopes that they can help you! Build self-confidence: Adjust your mindset, encourage yourself more, give yourself positive psychological suggestions, affirm your own value, objectively evaluate yourself, and make yourself more confident. Only with a strong inner strength can you have the power to pursue opportunities and interests, and face difficulties and setbacks. Find your position and constantly improve your abilities: Improve yourself through learning, reading, and other means, so that you can obtain substantial accumulation and progress, making yourself more competitive and confident in your work, and better equipped to pursue your own interests. Dare to take the first step and fight for your own interests: When we lack the courage to do something, we tend to magnify its difficulty and fear, giving ourselves negative psychological suggestions, which further discourage us from taking action. Dare to take the first step, challenge yourself. When you successfully take the first step, regardless of the outcome, you will gain new experiences and greater courage. Cultivate your interests, enrich your life: Through hobbies and interests, make your life more exciting, focus on yourself, see a different side of yourself, experience a different life, and change your mindset. Recognize your possibilities and diversity, and it also helps you find like-minded friends. Take the initiative to communicate with friends: Each of us has a different personality. Taking the initiative to communicate with friends, confide in them about your troubles, and try to accept their suggestions and ways of dealing with things, you can experience different perspectives and methods that can help you find a better way to solve problems that suits you. I hope you become braver, believe in yourself, and affirm yourself! Best wishes! Your personal mental health consultant by your side. May my words bring warmth to you! Also, thank you to the occasional passing friend who read this. Feel free to follow me and click "useful"!

Hello, from your words, it can be seen that you have the desire to change. Since you have the courage to ask, it is the beginning of facing your fears. I guess when you were a child, you may have received less encouragement from your father and mother, so you lacked a sense of security and self-worth. Especially for children after the age of six, the power of courage is particularly in need of affirmation from their father. If this part was missing during our childhood, we would try to gain our parents' love through pleasing them, and gradually neglect our self-worth, making it difficult to express our assertiveness. The power and courage of a person is actually the manifestation of our own assertiveness, our ability to bravely defend our rights. One is that we have the power, and the other is that our boundaries are clear. If our parents didn't allow us to be ourselves when we were young and always made decisions for us, it is possible that our boundaries were disrupted by our parents, and we will not be able to assert our rights. I suggest that you start with small things around you and gradually make changes while constantly encouraging yourself. I believe you will gradually change, so keep it up!

question: Highly educated mother loves to eat leftovers, causing conflicts between mother and daughter, what should be done?
description: I come from a single-parent family and live with my mom and our dog. I am 26 years old, and my mom is 52 and works as a teacher. Our financial condition is good, but my mom always hesitates to throw away leftover food, which leads to frequent arguments between us. My mom prefers to cook a large pot of food at once for convenience since there are only two of us in the family. We can't finish the leftovers, and the remaining dishes have to be eaten for several days. She is very stubborn, and when I tell her that there are fewer people in the house and she should cook less food, as eating overnight dishes can affect our health, she doesn't listen. Because I don't want to eat leftover food, but if I don't eat, she will get angry and scold me, saying, "You're not rich, having food to eat is already good enough." Then she says, "Eating leftover food won't make you sick. Even elderly people who live a long life also eat leftover food. Haven't they survived until such an old age? Life and death are fated, and prosperity is determined by heaven. How long one can live is already predetermined!" They all ate leftover food during their time; where else would they find fresh vegetables to eat?" (I can't argue against these words, but I always feel something is off). If I insist on not eating, she ends up feeding the leftovers to my dog, which makes me very angry because I consider my dog as my baby. If my dog gets sick from eating it, I would be heartbroken, but my mom says that stray dogs eat from garbage cans and yet still live well. What should I do?
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between parents.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope my answer can help you. Issue: Your mother likes to cook excessive amounts and eat leftovers. This causes frequent arguments between you two. Analysis: One, your mother is a teacher, and you said she cooks a large amount of food for convenience. Is it because she is busy with work and tired, so she wants to make cooking easier and solve several meals at once? Or maybe your mother does not enjoy cooking herself, like my mother, who doesn't like cooking because she was forced to start cooking at a very young age due to family reasons, so she has a sense of aversion and fear towards it. Methods: 1. Communicate with your mother to understand if she is too busy with work and doesn't have extra energy to cook, but still tries her best to cook for you. Understand if there were any unpleasant experiences in her childhood that make her dislike cooking. 2. Since you are already 26 years old, if possible, you can take the initiative to cook, control the portion size yourself, and avoid the situation of eating leftovers. 3. Try to understand and respect her, don't always argue and force her to accept your viewpoint, as it will only escalate the conflict between you two. If you don't want to eat leftovers, and your mother scolds you for not being wealthy, give the leftovers to your pet dog, as even stray dogs can live well by eating from the trash. Although your mother is highly educated, the living standards were generally low in the 70s or so, so the food they ate was definitely not good. This is why your mother also dislikes wasting food, it's related to her experiences. Like myself, even though I'm just in my twenties, I really dislike wasting food because I grew up in the countryside and did a lot of farm work, so I know that food is not easy to come by. It's all related to the upbringing environment. It's unlikely that you can suddenly change your mother's mindset, it can only happen through your long-term persistence. Methods: 1. Respect your mother's viewpoint, after all, you both grew up in different eras. You can refuse your mother's behavior, but you should respect her true thoughts. At this age, both of you already have mature views, and it's difficult to have any major changes, so mutual respect is necessary. 2. Frequently communicate that the dog is an important companion and family member to you, so your mother can understand your emotions. It's all about communication and deep connection, conveying your true thoughts instead of always focusing on surface-level problems, as arguing won't solve anything. 3. Let your mother know that you care about her and worry about her health, conveying your love. At 52 years old, your mother should be at the age where regular check-ups are needed. When you take your mother to the hospital, have the doctor explain the negative impacts of eating leftovers. Although she may act tough, she definitely still loves you and hopes to spend more time with you. Hearing this from a more authoritative doctor may have a better effect. You must adjust your own mindset, as this matter requires subtle influence on your mother, making her first respect your viewpoint and then slowly accept the idea of avoiding eating leftovers. You need to have more patience, more communication, and less arguing. Discover the hidden secrets behind this issue.

Hug the original poster ~ I can feel your distress because we are both children who are troubled by lifestyle differences. To summarize your problem, it mainly involves the following points: your mother likes to cook a large pot of food at once, resulting in you both constantly eating leftovers; you believe that leftovers are not conducive to good health, but your mother always has reasons that seem reasonable but actually don't make much sense; you don't want to eat them, and your mother gets angry and gives the leftovers to the dog, which makes you worry for the dog. Regarding the differences in lifestyle between you and your parents, my suggestion is to seek common ground while respecting each other's ways of life, and then find ways that can make everyone comfortable without affecting harmony. [First, respect your mother's habits.] Does eating leftovers affect health? In a general sense, it definitely does. However, there are individual differences, and some people can eat leftovers all their life and still live long, just like what your mother said. You are trying to persuade your mother based on a general sense, while your mother believes in an exception, and you cannot prove that your mother does not belong to this exception. On this point, I feel that you can't reach a consensus between you, and even if you continue to dwell on this point, the relationship will become strained and everyone will be unhappy. Therefore, it might be better to respect your mother's thoughts. If you are worried about her health, you can regularly take her for check-ups and pay more attention to her physical condition. [Then, let's try some solutions that can make everyone comfortable without affecting harmony.] For example, can you be the one to cook? Your mother likes to cook a lot at once, and sometimes she may find it troublesome to cook new dishes and feels tired after a day of work. Can you try cooking by yourself? If you don't have time to cook every day, you can also share the cooking responsibilities with your mother. This way, you can avoid constantly eating leftovers and also improve the relationship between mother and daughter. Another example, can you discuss with your mother about adopting a meal-preparation method? In fact, cooking simple dishes doesn't take up much time, it's just time-consuming when handling the ingredients. We can discuss with our mother and see if it's possible to plan the meals for the week on Sunday, wash and cook the ingredients, and vacuum-pack them to be stored, so that they can be directly cooked when needed. At the same time, in order to lighten your mother's workload, we can be more diligent in things like washing dishes and cleaning the kitchen. Is it possible to keep a distance of a bowl of soup from your mother? Sometimes distance really enhances beauty. If it's really impossible to accept each other's ways of life, we can also try moving out. However, since you and your mother rely on each other, it wouldn't be good to move too far. We can maintain a distance of a bowl of soup, so that you can go home every now and then, have a meal of your mother's cooking, and also conveniently take care of your mother. You asked this question because you care about your mother's health, and in my opinion, if I had to choose between health and happiness, I would definitely choose happiness. After all, your mother has been living for over fifty years and is accustomed to this way of life, so I still suggest that you respect your mother's lifestyle and seek common ground while accommodating differences.

Hello, Luolu. After reading your description, Lalan understands and wants to give you a hug first. Based on your description, Lalan has come up with several points: (1) Although your family conditions are good, your mother has inherited the habit of frugality and doesn't want to waste leftover food. (2) Your mother also cooks a large pot of food for convenience, and it's difficult to estimate the amount needed for two people, resulting in leftovers. (3) Nowadays, leftover food is not as safe as before, and it can be harmful to the body. However, your mother believes she is an exception to good health, and you often argue about this. Lalan has some suggestions and hopes they can help you: First, it is challenging to change habits developed over decades, but you can gradually explain the harm of leftover food to your mother. Nowadays, compared to before, the pollution in food is severe, so the harm of leftovers cannot be ignored. However, please remember not to have conflicts with your mother if the conversation isn't successful. Your intention is to care for her health, right? If you not only fail to solve the issue of leftover food but also make her upset, it will be counterproductive and go against your original intention. Second, your mother cooks a large pot of food because it is troublesome and difficult to estimate the portion for two people. So instead of getting angry for the sake of your mother's health, it would be better for you to cook yourself and control the portion or buy only the amount needed for one meal. If your mother enjoys cooking, you can do it together, ensuring the portion and making your time together more enjoyable. Third, you can try to change your mother's habit indirectly through interactive games. For example, play a game where the loser has to discard the leftover food. Over time, she may change because of the concern about waste. Finally, Lalan wants to say, please approach your mother about this matter with understanding and an attitude of reasoning. Don't let it result in conflicts. Lalan hopes you can resolve this issue soon. Best wishes.

Hello, OP: Eating leftovers is a habit that has been passed down from the older generation, who grew up in difficult conditions and learned to save and be frugal. Even though living conditions have improved now, they still maintain a thrifty lifestyle. First, I think it's important to understand why my mother likes to eat leftovers, and then try to persuade her not to eat leftovers through communication. You can search the internet for the dangers of eating leftovers and show them to your mother. If possible, you can take your mother to see a doctor for advice, as I think the doctor's opinion will be effective.

Your mom is quite cute. She's willful and stubborn like a child. There are many cooking videos online. You're already 26 years old, so you can take over the cooking and make meals for her - only make enough for the two of you, so she won't have to feed the dog leftovers for days. Since you're not cooking the food, it's normal that you don't have a say in it. There's a joke: Why are picky eaters always children, while parents are not picky? Because they buy and cook the food they love, so of course they can have it their way.

Can you forward some articles about the hazards of eating leftover food to your mom, so that she doesn't think she's just talking nonsense? Use other authoritative means and methods to help her understand. I think it should be fine for dogs to eat leftovers because their stomachs are strong, and besides, if the food is bad, the dogs probably won't eat it. I hope this can resolve your conflicts. Best wishes to you both!

question: There is no way to control one's feelings and stop liking someone. However, if that person already has a girlfriend, what should you do?
description: I am a freshman in college. I was attracted to a male classmate and we joined the same club, gradually getting to know each other. I started developing feelings for him. I wanted to chat with him more often to cultivate our relationship, but one day he suddenly posted a birthday wish for his girlfriend on his social media, which made me very sad. However, I realized that as long as he is always around me, I can't help but like him. I feel very troubled. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Based on your description, I understand the conflict in your heart right now! It's like a song that sings, feeling like you have "loved someone you shouldn't love." You feel that it's morally wrong to further develop feelings for a guy who has a girlfriend, but you can't control your liking for him deep down, so it's a contradictory struggle for you! First of all, if the guy doesn't have a girlfriend, would you be together? You interact in a club, do you think you can get closer to him? Is your liking for him just admiration, or does he show signs of caring for you? If not, it's just unrequited love; secondly, you feel sad when you see him post on social media. Is it worth expressing your feelings and pursuing love at this moment? Everything you're feeling right now is one-sided, so why bother getting so upset? Being able to be in the same club is already a kind of friendship fate, so why not cherish it! If you really express your love and he doesn't agree, it will be very embarrassing for you, and I believe you won't feel good about it. If he agrees to your admiration and breaks up with his current girlfriend, would you dare to be with this kind of guy? If he can be disloyal to his current girlfriend, he will also be disloyal to you in the future! I suggest keeping your love to yourself! Being able to interact together and help each other in the club is already a form of growth; finally, don't let yourself fall, believe in your own excellence, and you will definitely meet someone who is compatible with you. Liking someone means that some traits of that person have attracted you! But it doesn't mean that he is necessarily suitable for you! If you want your love to bloom and bear fruit, you need to first become excellent and attractive, so that guys will come closer to you, and at the same time, you will have enough charm to not be afraid of other girls stealing your boyfriend, what do you think? In short, society always imposes many moral and ethical constraints on women, and although sometimes we may be reluctant, we still need to consider and abide by them, otherwise, our character will always be questioned. I hope this sharing is helpful to you!

question: 31-year-old woman, finds it difficult to feel happy and a sense of accomplishment on her own, has a hard time pleasing herself.
description: In the past year, I have found it difficult to feel happy. My work results are good, but I don't feel a sense of accomplishment. Instead, any imperfection in my work makes me feel like a failure. I wonder why I am so harsh on myself. It's too hard to please myself.
keywords: Personal growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, and the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~ From what I've heard, are you a perfectionist? Undoubtedly, perfectionists are very serious, responsible, and excellent, but they are also in pain. Because they are always longing for perfection – striving for perfection and discovering imperfections – it's a cycle that suppresses oneself. Based on this, I have a few suggestions: 1. Change your mindset and accept your imperfections. We must recognize that no one can be perfect. Everyone has some flaws, to a greater or lesser extent. Just like the duality of philosophy, you cannot only demand one side and ignore the other. Such thoughts and ideas are biased. 2. Explore the inner child and find the inherent value of yourself. Everyone's existence has its own value, which is not purely determined by external excellence. Confident individuals will persist in their inherent self-worth even when life mercilessly crushes them. The failure to do something well is influenced by various factors, not just because one is not excellent enough. Therefore, don't magnify internal factors and overlook the influence of external factors. 3. Pleasing oneself is actually quite simple, it is self-acceptance. So every day, you can try to give yourself more positive encouragement and support, telling yourself to do your best. Be happy when you succeed and not be saddened by failure.
