Acknowledge your successes and be generous in accepting failure. Accept any behavior of yours that does not violate morality, and be free and happy. These are my analysis and suggestions, I hope they can be helpful to you! Best wishes!

question: 19 years old, I almost forgot what I used to look like. Am I the mirror you talk about?
description: At the age of 19, I don't understand what you mean by "maturity" in your words. It seems different from my understanding. You want me to be obedient, so I'll be obedient. You want me to be sensible, so I'll be sensible. It's like I've almost forgotten what I originally looked like. My self-awareness is shallow, I don't know what I'm really like. I always want to understand myself through others' words, or in other words, I care about how others see me. Actually, I don't like it. I like cool people, but I'm not that cool. I like a carefree life, but I feel restricted in every aspect of life. I hope I can have my own style and find my own place. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: I have many people around me who have also experienced this kind of dilemma. I believe that this is a process of growth: starting to seriously think about what kind of person we are and what kind of person we want to become. Firstly, as teenagers in today's society, as we grow older, we will pay more and more attention to our image and how others perceive us. We will hope to be outstanding in the eyes of others and deliberately decorate ourselves. This is a normal thing and doesn't need to be overly worried about. Secondly, our minds are slowly maturing and we have our own goals and images of who we want to become. But we still lack experience and abilities in handling things, which can lead to conflicts between "who we want to become" and "who we are seen as". This can make us feel conflicted. In response to this, I have the following suggestions that you can consider! You can think about the similarities and differences between the person you "want to become" and the person you are "seen as". For the similarities, you can continue moving towards your goal. For the differences, develop both aspects without losing yourself, but this also tests your ability to deal with and handle things. Seek advice and help from friends, so that you can discuss specific situations and have a clearer understanding of the conflicts between "who you want to become" and "who you are seen as". As the saying goes, "those involved are in a maze, while outsiders can see things clearly." At the same time, by expressing your worries, your inner self will feel much better. Regardless, I believe it is important to stay true to your original intentions and strive towards becoming a better version of yourself. Also, it's important to prioritize your own happiness!

Think about what kind of season 19 years old is, it could be happy, sad, or bursting with ambition. Everyone has a different world. Perhaps at this blossoming age, sadness occupies the minds of most people. It is a common denominator to feel lost during a stage of breaking away from the constraints of parents and moving towards self-independence. For us, the majority of Chinese parents see their children as their "personal belongings". They always hope that their children will live the life they want in their own way, under the guise of "it's for your own good". What they don't know is that we need to be ourselves and realize our own value according to our own path, instead of being their "shadow". If you know what you want, strive in that direction, because that is the meaning of your existence. Don't be restricted by the outside world and give up on soaring. 19 years old is just the beginning of life, even if temporarily lost, we must gather strength and strive to soar. Take the time to cultivate yourself, such as reading, traveling, and running, as these are ways to seek the meaning of one's existence. Keep going, as long as you strive forward, you will have a brilliant life.

After reading the description, one can feel the perplexity and helplessness in the questioner's heart towards the world. Hugs to the questioner. From the description, we can roughly see the following questions that the questioner has: What exactly is maturity? The questioner's understanding of maturity is different from what "you guys" understand as maturity. Always knowing about oneself from others' words, not liking this state. Hoping to have one's own style and find one's own position. Analyzing the reasons behind these questions, the term "maturity" is a man-made term. On Baidu Encyclopedia, there are three explanations: 1) The development of a plant's fruit or fruit to the degree of harvestability. 2) A metaphor for things developing to a perfect degree. 3) Referring to the change of a person's thoughts and ideas, which often occurs in conjunction with changes in the surrounding environment, including the influence of others. Here, we are using the third meaning of "maturity". There is a key point in the explanation: the change of thoughts and ideas. This is the interpretation given to us in writing. I think that whether it's the "maturity" in the questioner's words or the "maturity" in others' words, it is not a fixed and unchanging standard. It will change with time. In other words, when someone says to you, "whether you are mature or not", it is what they are considering from their perspective, and it cannot affect our individual maturity. Therefore, our maturity is determined by considering whether there has been a change in our thoughts and ideas, standing in our own position, compared to the past. The questioner also said, "If you guys want me to be obedient, then I will be obedient. If you want me to be sensible, then I will be sensible, as if I have almost forgotten what I originally looked like." In today's social environment, it can be said that most of us may be living in the world that others perceive, rarely considering what we originally looked like. It should be a natural thing to have a curious heart to understand this world, to understand ourselves. Life is like a practice, a process of constantly getting to know ourselves. In the process of getting to know ourselves, we can constantly understand ourselves. In the end, we need to find and become our true selves! Now that we know the reasons, what should we do? 1) Accept people's expectations of you, but you don't have to follow them completely. Do things that you think can improve yourself. Every day, keep striving so that you can have the ability to live the way you want. (Before having the ability, our choices are often limited) 2) If you encounter setbacks in the process of practice, accept your imperfections. 3) Do things that you enjoy doing (legitimate things), constantly explore, and discover your truest self. Finally, I hope the questioner can find and become their true selves! I am "Living Meaningfully," a young person who engages in conversations from the heart. Can you give me a thumbs up to help me out? Let's progress together!

Hello, at 19 years old, it is normal to start exploring who you are and feeling confused. Most people go through a period of confusion where they don't know who they are, and then gradually become aware of their true self and develop into unique, free, authentic, and mature individuals. First of all, it is important to allow yourself to be confused and not know what maturity means, because not knowing is normal. At the same time, continue to learn, explore, discuss with others, and ask for their opinions on what kind of person you are. Explore your strengths, weaknesses, and what makes you special. When you know who you are, your characteristics, similarities, and differences with others, your personality will gradually become whole, and your inner self will become stronger. You will become more confident, cheerful, and able to face anything that comes your way without doubting yourself because you know who you are and have a stable sense of self. So what should you do? My advice is to allow yourself to be confused and immature for now, but also believe that you will mature in the future. In the meantime, learn various knowledge, interpersonal skills, and psychological knowledge about your own personality. Actively improve your social skills, learn new skills, and try different things to gain experience. In this process, you will discover what you like, what suits you, and what kind of person you are. You will also become more mature and complete internally. Remember, you can continue to move forward even with feelings of confusion. Moving forward is the only direction.

Hello, OP! From your description, it can be seen that you care a lot about other people's opinions and become what they want you to be, losing yourself. I think, firstly, you need to take external evaluations into proper perspective and have self-awareness. After all, other people's opinions are just one way for us to know ourselves. The main way for us to know ourselves is through self-awareness. We shouldn't let others' evaluations determine who we are. Otherwise, we would lose ourselves and go with the flow. Don't be influenced by the outside world, go out and find your own style. Don't be held back, listen to your own inner thoughts, and find yourself. The above are just my personal views, and I hope they can help you.

question: Should a teacher display obvious bias in the classroom?
description: In today's class, I felt that the teacher had a clear bias towards a certain thing (let's call it "a"). I felt that the teacher was subtly implying a change in our perception of a. He intentionally described the role of a as a random event, and it seemed like he was forcing his own opinion onto the students. Is this kind of behavior acceptable? It is similar to when a teacher used to support Hong Kong independence. If they openly influenced students in the classroom, how many students would subconsciously follow the teacher? I believe that in the classroom, teachers should not impart their biased views to students, and at the very least, should remain neutral in their speech.

answers.answer_text: Hello, because you did not specifically mention what the teacher was commenting on, it is not appropriate to make presumptions and judge whether the teacher's words were right or wrong. However, one point you mentioned is particularly important, that is, "feeling that he is imposing his own opinions on students." If the teacher's views align with social morality, laws, and general norms, then it's alright, just need to be more mindful of the methods in the future. If not, it can be potentially harmful for students and for education as a whole. From your description, I can see that you are a person who thinks critically and does not blindly follow, and that is commendable. Take care of yourself.

question: Boy, others say I'm too gentle, and I don't feel confident at all now.
description: Feeling like people say I'm too gentle, I'm a boy. It's really upsetting to be constantly told that, and now I feel scared to talk to others. I feel like I want to live as someone else, like a celebrity I admire. But it seems like I can't achieve that and it makes me really sad. I feel like I have no confidence at all. I'm afraid to talk to others, worried that they'll call me effeminate or something. I feel like such a loser.
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I am not a professional expert, but I really wanted to reply to this question. First of all, I want to give you a hug. It is indeed very painful to not accept yourself. But from your description, I see that you care a lot about what others say. Other people's opinions can be like mirrors, providing guidance, but these mirrors themselves have subjective thoughts. And when you try to find yourself in the eyes of others, you will never truly find yourself. It's like there are a thousand Hamlets in a thousand people's eyes. Different people see you differently. Why bother so much? As humans, we are born as unique individuals and don't need to mold ourselves into a specific template. There is no standard template for personality. We can appreciate good qualities in others and strive to emulate them, but that doesn't mean we have to completely erase ourselves. A person's personality is shaped by genes, environment, and experiences. You are who you are, a unique individual, and we should always strive to be ourselves. I noticed in the question you're concerned about being "gentle." I think you have a stereotypical impression of men. Why can't men be gentle? Gentleness is not the same as weakness, nor is it synonymous with indecisiveness. It is not a derogatory term. I don't know what is troubling you, but courage and gentleness can coexist. Gentleness will not hinder you from becoming a real man. Before the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil, CCTV reporter Liu Xiaoxuan risked his life to interview drug dealers in the favelas of Brazil and collected videos showing the drug trafficking process. I suggest you watch it. From the video, you can see that the reporter is also a gentle person, and it does not hinder my admiration for him. It is evident that you care a lot about what others think. However, in reality, the vast majority of people in our lives are just passing through. It is up to you to decide what kind of person you want to become. You are important to yourself, and your own perception of yourself will affect your emotions, mindset, and even your health. A truly strong person is not someone who appears dominant and dictates others, but someone who understands what they want and relentlessly pursues it. I hope you, the questioner, can accept yourself or become the person you truly want to be as soon as possible. Best wishes! ^_^

question: Why do I always regret and forget to say thank you every time I communicate with others?
description: Every time I ask someone to do something for me, I always fail to express myself clearly. After I say it, I always regret why I didn't say thank you again.

answers.answer_text: Hmm, it seems like you have forgetfulness. However, if they don't really care about your personality, it doesn't matter. You can consider buying some small gifts for them to show your appreciation. Occasionally treating them to a meal is also an option, but you don't have to do it every month. Whoever has helped you the most, you can simply invite them to have a meal as a gesture of thanks. Thank you for your care, and I hope everyone can understand.

question: Why do you repeatedly avoid something? The result is still the same when the matter is reopened.
description: At the beginning of 2019, I added someone on a software who seemed familiar, but he absolutely refused to admit that he was the person I liked. Actually, I never add strangers on WeChat, even if I do, I wouldn't develop any emotional attachment because I find it difficult to trust and feel secure around people in general, let alone making friends on WeChat. I only mistook him because of his hints. He stubbornly denied it, saying he was looking for another girl and was just casually chatting with me. Even when I told him I wasn't the person he was looking for, he still insisted on saying good morning and goodnight to me every day. Being someone with a naturally suspicious mind, I argued with him several times, scolded him, but also feared that he might actually be the person I liked and it would hurt him. However, it really annoyed me when a stranger would say good morning and goodnight to me. During this time, I deleted him several times, but he always added me back and hinted that he was the person I liked. It's not realistic as we can't even meet in real life. This back and forth has been going on. I scolded him many times and my emotions were torn between believing and not believing him. If it's him, then I enter his script with a sense of mistrust and doubt, and it feels like betraying my loyalty to him. Even if he is just playing around, he never asks if I'm feeling sad or not.

answers.answer_text: Every time I add him back now, he either pretends to be his brother or pretends to like another girl. There is always hatred. Every time I can scare him away and delete him, I'm afraid of being abandoned, ashamed and seemingly chatting with his brother. I need to start over, and he is around my Weibo, painful, no one can understand him. Yes, I can't help but want to search for news about him.

So back and forth, we wasted two years. Every time I deleted him, he would tell me through Weibo that he found another girl. If I admit that I guessed it was him, he would feel ashamed that he didn't leave a good impression at first, so he kept fabricating that I added his good friend on WeChat. This is also an insult to me, as I ended up being intimate and affectionate with other guys. Do you know how complicated this emotion is? But during this time, I discovered that I have a lot of unresolved issues from my dysfunctional family, such as being distant from people, not making friends, and not having long-lasting relationships with anyone. These issues manifested themselves after I started liking him. Being single for ten years in society, I've never felt strange about myself. He also has his own small problems, but they are not as severe as mine, but I made them worse. I don't blame him for not understanding me. The problem now is that I want to continue with him. He hinted that it was him on WeChat, but every time we communicate on WeChat, he ignores the content and just jokes around as if nothing happened. I feel like he or his friends are playing tricks on me. So I deleted him. From the wording on Weibo, he likes me, but I don't know how to continue. He posted an animated short film, where a whale in the sea encountered a bird trapped in a cage. At first, they played happily together, but then a big wave was about to engulf the birdcage. The whale tried to push the birdcage out to sea, but the birdcage sank to the bottom of the ocean. The bird died, and that bird is me, and I know it. We can't communicate. Every time I add him back on WeChat, I end up deleting him again, multiple times. I always feel that if I add him on WeChat, someone will harm me.

question: I don't know why I need to go for a run. What's happening to me lately?
description: Sometimes I don't feel like running, and I don't know why I should run. But then I persuade myself to run by reminding myself of the many benefits it brings. Now I run three times a week. I don't know what's been happening with me lately.

answers.answer_text: Hugging the host is really impressive for being able to persist in running, and still being able to do it three times a week. I wonder what initially motivated the host to start wanting to persist in running? Now, when you say you don't know why, is it because the initial goals and motivations have changed? Running is indeed a sport with many benefits, and even without a specific reason, the process itself can relax the mind. During exercise, endorphins and dopamine are released, which can create a feeling of pleasure. Recently, I also want to start exercising regularly. Perhaps the host can teach me the secret to being able to persist in running three times a week.

Hello, runner, it's great that you enjoy running because it not only helps us exercise but also allows us to release stress. Overall, it's a good thing. When running, you can find your true self. It's during running that you can reach a completely relaxed state, which is why you've been enjoying running lately. However, I think it's important to schedule a suitable time for running. For example, you can go for a morning run or run half an hour after dinner. These are all acceptable. It should be arranged at a reasonable time. Everything should be done in moderation. It's not good if running too frequently interferes with your normal life. Also, if you have too much stress, you can choose other ways to relieve it, such as going for a walk outside or listening to music and playing sports. These are all excellent ways to release stress. Best wishes.

question: Is turning on the lights to sleep because of a fear of darkness? I want to change this habit.
description: Sleeping with the lights on, I know it's not good for my health, but whenever I turn off the lights, I feel like there are many, many monsters around me trying to eat me. Sometimes the night light runs out of battery and automatically turns off in the middle of the night, and then I can wake up instantly, no matter how deep I am asleep.

answers.answer_text: Poster, hello. The method to gradually overcome fear and return to normal is to be willing to confront fear and gradually drive it away. You can seriously consider the reasons why you are afraid of the dark. When did you start going to sleep? Have you always been someone who sleeps alone, or were you often alone at home as a child? Did anything scary happen to you while you were asleep? Have you heard stories about monsters appearing and eating children after the lights go out? There is always a cause for things happening. Find this cause and overcome it accordingly. Think of some specific methods to help yourself slowly return to normal. You can start by buying a small lamp with adjustable brightness and gradually adjust it from bright to dark, allowing yourself to adapt to very dim or even no light. If you feel scared, you can listen to music to help you fall asleep, or do some exercises before bed to help you fall asleep faster. Alternatively, you can sleep with the lights on but wear an eye mask, so that you know in your heart that the outside world is bright and monsters do not appear. This also protects your eyes. When you feel scared, you can briefly remove the eye mask and then put it back on. Another option is to have a family member accompany you to sleep for a while after the lights are turned off, comforting you and driving away the monsters. Gradually, they can quietly leave after you fall asleep, so that you can slowly become brave enough to sleep on your own. Lastly, monsters don't eat you while you're sleeping because even monsters need to sleep. Moreover, they have already become vegetarians and don't come out at night. So sleep peacefully. Best wishes.

question: Feeling uneasy and bothered due to a single comment from a friend?
description: I am a girl, and recently I had some unused items at home, so I planned to give them to a friend. Later, my friend said, "Are you planning to give me everything in your house?" This sentence made me feel really uncomfortable. This friend is someone I usually get along well with, but I didn't expect them to say something like this. It doesn't sit well with me psychologically.

answers.answer_text: You said that you care about a friend's comment and feel uncomfortable. I wonder what kind of "uncomfortable" feeling it is? You said that when you heard your friend say, "Are you ready to give me everything in your house," you felt particularly uncomfortable. I wonder what kind of discomfort it is? From this sentence, what kind of information did you hear, what kind of feelings did it evoke, what does it mean to you, and why does it make you feel so uncomfortable? I don't know what expression and tone of voice your friend used when saying this sentence, different expressions and tones of voice can convey completely different meanings. For example, A: a light tone, and laughing as they say this sentence, it might be a joke, like "You've given me so many things!" B: a tone of contempt and a disdainful expression, which might mean: "You're giving me things from your home, and I'm not happy about it." C: a hesitant tone, with a questioning expression, which might be confirming, "Will you give me more things?" Of course, I don't know what your friend meant when saying this sentence, perhaps only she knows what she meant. But regardless of what your friend meant, this sentence makes you feel uncomfortable, and it is possible that you "perceive" something that makes you uncomfortable from it. For example, A: your friend is joking and teasing you, and you feel "being teased" is a very uncomfortable experience, or you feel that such things shouldn't be joked about at all. B: it's also possible that you detect scorn from this sentence and feel hurt that you are being given things and still being looked down upon, which makes you feel uncomfortable. C: maybe when you hear this sentence, you feel like "what else does my friend want from me?", and you think your friend is too greedy, so it makes you feel uncomfortable to think, "I've already given you so many things, and you still want more." D: maybe it's something I can't guess, that allows you to understand some meanings and have some "uncomfortable" feelings. But based on the information in the prompt, it's impossible to determine which possibility it is. Perhaps all the guesses are not consistent with your feelings. But you can try to organize the attitudes, meanings, and feelings you understand from this sentence, and maybe you can figure out how it makes you uncomfortable. You said this friend is usually easy-going, but you didn't expect her to say such things. It feels like this kind of sentence is a very negative and uncomfortable presence in your heart. When this sentence is spoken by a friend who is "usually easy-going," it not only makes you uncomfortable but also surprised, unexpected. So, in the past, have there been people who had bad relationships with you, or people who you didn't get along with, or people with a bad attitude, who said similar things to you? Perhaps in the past, when you heard those people say this sentence, you always felt very uncomfortable. In the end, every time you hear this sentence, no matter who says it, in what tone, and to express what, you automatically think of those terrible experiences and feel "uncomfortable." However, the friend who said this is "usually easy-going," which is likely different from the people you have had the previous experience with who "say this sentence," so what the friend expresses is not necessarily the same as what others have expressed in the past. If you are willing, maybe you can discuss it with your friend, what does she mean by saying this sentence? Then you can reevaluate your feelings about this sentence based on your friend's meaning.

Hello, OP. You mentioned that you felt uncomfortable hearing this phrase. I'm not sure what specifically made you feel uneasy, so I'll give you two interpretations of the phrase: "Are you ready to give me everything in your house?" The first interpretation is that it's a joke, asking if you're willing to give everything in your house to the person. The second interpretation is that the person is telling you to give them everything in your house. However, I think the first interpretation is more likely. If someone were to speak to me in this way, as an ordinary person, I would feel that they are impolite and disrespectful. But if this person is your close friend and you have a good relationship, I think it's quite reasonable for them to say this to you. They expressed it in a relatively tactful manner, but you may still find it uncomfortable because it sounds quite direct. So why does this statement make you feel uncomfortable? I think it's because they struck a nerve deep within you, making you feel somewhat ashamed and uneasy. This is what they call "unpleasant truth." However, in reality, they didn't have any malicious intentions. It was just a joke, so there's no need to take it to heart too much, especially since you are so familiar with each other. It's common for a girl to clear out unused items at home, and it's nice to give them to friends. On one hand, it avoids waste and not throwing things away, and on the other hand, it's a gesture of goodwill. However, because these items are not new but second-hand, it is important to consider the other person's feelings when giving them away. It's better to ask if the friend needs them first before giving them. Otherwise, the person may feel a bit inferior, as they say, "don't bite the hand that feeds you." So, the recipient might feel a bit embarrassed. This feeling of embarrassment can easily lead to other thoughts and might hurt one's self-esteem. If the person already feels a bit insecure, they might start thinking in the opposite direction and wonder if the person giving them the items looks down on them. Moreover, most people are generally well-off and not desperate for money or those items, so they would pay more attention to their pride. Of course, it's true that those in financial difficulties would have stronger self-esteem. So, when giving away unused items, it's better to be a bit more considerate.

question: When it comes to hiding one's personality, what should one do when being looked down upon by others?
description: What should I do when I am looked down upon by my own relatives? I am particularly sensitive and always hide my true personality. I pretend to get along well with people I don't like and I always help others when they ask, but I regret it afterwards. I think too much about these things in my daily life. What kind of personality is considered normal and how can I gain others' approval? Should I be more slick or should I stay true to myself? Can I just discard people and things that I don't like?

answers.answer_text: 【The most important thing is to value yourself】【First】, understanding that feeling down and looking down on oneself already carries a sense of disdain and disrespect. I understand your feelings and it must be very difficult. 【Second】, instead of relying on others, it's better to learn to appreciate yourself first. If you have already communicated with the external world and know that it has its limitations, meaning that the other party does not know how to respect you, then you must learn to respect yourself. 1. Learn to appreciate your own strengths. When you truly like yourself, others will like you too. Learn to appreciate your own strengths and learn to love yourself. 2. Learn to accept yourself unconditionally. Accept your shortcomings and allow yourself to be imperfect and not outstanding. In fact, it is perfectly fine to be imperfect and not outstanding. This is also safe. 3. Learn to encourage yourself. Some things may only be lacking motivation or a better method that suits you. With improvements, you will be able to do it and achieve success. 4. Learn to feel proud of yourself. We can be looked down upon or hurt because of shame. Shame and pride are opposite to each other. On one hand, you need to let go of shame, and on the other hand, you need to learn to feel proud of yourself. When you feel proud of yourself, it doesn't matter if others look down on you or not. You feel hurt because you desire affirmation or pride from others. Next time when you feel hurt, remember your existence. The external world may not always meet your needs, therefore, in that moment, you need to learn to love yourself and fulfill your own needs. Wishing you well, Namaste!

A long time ago, my parents taught me to be kind to others so that they wouldn't bully me. I followed this method and helped my graduate school classmate farm for three years. However, in the end, she scammed me out of 1000 RMB. For someone who only had a monthly allowance of 300 RMB, this was a large sum of money. Moreover, the feeling of being betrayed was extremely angry and sad. Later on, I slowly realized that if you don't refuse anyone, others will indeed like you. Who wouldn't like someone who helps them? But I wasn't happy because people won't repay you just because you are kind. When I started refusing others, I found that many friends around me started leaving one by one. However, there were still some who stayed by my side. Even after more than 20 years, my close friends will always help me no matter when or what. After struggling in society, I discovered that besides childhood friends and lifelong friends, most people are driven by self-interest. So, when you become strong, you realize that you can have so many friends. When I first graduated, I joined a large company and became a high-level executive. At class reunions, everyone was enthusiastic, and I even helped some primary school classmates solve work problems. But good times didn't last long—the boss passed away, and the new job I found was unsatisfactory. During the next reunion, the atmosphere had completely changed. For shallow relationships, the maintenance of the relationship depends on your value. The higher your hidden value, the more willing others are to flatter and fawn over you. Conversely, the lower your hidden value, the more distant and contemptuous others become. However, for strong relationships, the maintenance depends on shared interests, appreciation for one another, and how you get along. Based on your situation, I think you should focus on two things: choice and personal growth. First, understand that not all relationships are the same. There are many types of relationships, some of which have high maintenance costs but low benefits. You should distance yourself from those people. There are also relationships with low maintenance costs but high benefits. Be grateful for these people, like your former teachers. Whenever I have questions about psychology, I still consult my old teachers, and they are always eager to help, simply because I was their student. Of course, not all teachers are like this, but most are. There are also relationships with high maintenance costs but high benefits. These are often business partners who cooperate with each other and support one another. Some relationships have low maintenance costs with low benefits. These are simply playmates. Therefore, for each type of relationship, you should respond differently in order to handle them properly. Second, personal growth. We are inherently attracted to resources. This desire is deeply embedded in our genes. We like beautiful people because they possess excellent physical resources. We like to be friends with the wealthy because they have vast amounts of wealth and connections. This attraction to resources makes our society lean towards the rich and disregard the poor. Therefore, if you want to live a good life, you must focus on personal growth. Human abilities gradually increase. It may be slow, but as long as you don't give up and continue to learn and strive, you will eventually become a towering tree. Often, mastering a skill can sustain yourself. For example, my second uncle was a primary school teacher his whole life. However, he became an expert in teaching methods and curriculum content. He devoted 20 years to perfecting his craft and reaped many rewards. He gained the respect of many parents and has a comfortable life with a monthly pension of seven to eight thousand. Is he exceptionally talented? Not at all. Twenty years ago, our elementary school couldn't even pay teachers, so the whole school, with more than 20 classes, had only one teacher. All the other teachers had left. My second uncle, who had only completed primary school education, was asked by the principal to be a substitute teacher. He learned step by step and became an outstanding educator. Find your ideal path and stick to it. Eventually, you will become a leader in your industry. Never give up on personal growth.

Hello, I see that you have high self-expectations and inner conflicts when it comes to focusing on others' flaws, which leads to anxiety and distress. When you feel sensitive and upset because of how your relatives view you, it may be due to your high standards and perfectionism, as well as dissatisfaction and lack of self-confidence projected onto yourself. It is important to accept your imperfections, avoid setting absolute standards for yourself and others, and give yourself credit for your strengths rather than magnifying your weaknesses. In reality, 99% of people are more concerned about themselves rather than others, especially in the age of the internet where social circles have expanded infinitely. It is difficult to please everyone, and pretending to be friendly and helpful while not actually liking someone can lead to regret. The people-pleaser personality is also formed by lack of self-confidence. Be true to yourself, sincerely express your thoughts and emotions, and avoid using aggressive words and actions when rejecting or negating others as it can harm yourself more than them. Whether to adapt or be true to your own character and seek validation, it is not easy to completely isolate people you don't like because humans are social beings. Be courageous enough to accept being disliked, as you will not like everyone and not everyone will like you. This is a fact and a rule, as no one is perfect. When interacting with others, adopt a more mature and balanced mindset, avoiding the childish binary thinking of black and white extremes, and analyze things rationally and dialectically. Best wishes.

Hello, OP. It must be exhausting to constantly hide your true personality in everything you do. Sending you a hug. #Being particularly sensitive, I always hide my true personality. When I encounter people I don't like, I pretend to get along with them. I'm always willing to help when someone asks, but I often regret it afterward. (Is it because we believe subconsciously that only by doing so, others will like and approve of us? So we are afraid of rejecting others and being rejected by them. This makes us feel like we are not being recognized. But can a good relationship be destroyed because of our refusal to do certain things? If we always have to compromise in order to maintain a relationship, isn't it too exhausting? #Overthinking: What kind of personality is considered the standard? How should we behave to gain the approval of others? Should we be smooth or should we have our own personality? Can we just discard people and things we don't like? (Qiān qiān really likes the saying: "Don't be smooth, become a star with edges and corners, and still shine." Actually, there is no standard personality. Each personality has its own advantages and disadvantages. For example, a personality like yours, OP, must also be liked by many people. However, I don't know how you define "recognition." Do we need the approval of everyone to feel recognized? Or is it only when we succeed in accomplishing something that we feel recognized? "Being smooth" also has its benefits. For example, it can help us build better relationships and gain more resources, thereby getting what we want. However, it also makes us uncomfortable, as we constantly feel the need to please the other person and gain their approval. So being smooth is not always a bad thing. As for people and things we don't like, if we discard them, we may feel satisfied, but we may also miss out on certain resources. If we choose to be smooth, we may feel exhausted.

Hello. It's nice to "meet" you. First, I want to give you a warm hug, and I hope my answer can help you. Dear, let me start by asking you a question, or you can ask yourself this question: Do you think you are living happily? How much benefit do you think your current behavior brings to yourself? Life is short, and we only have one chance, so why make things difficult for ourselves? Why live unhappily? You need to learn to love yourself first, and then others will love you. Don't care too much about what others think or say, otherwise, how should those who are being bullied online live? Other people's opinions may not always be correct. You need to have your own sense of right and wrong, firmly holding onto your own beliefs instead of living for others. So let those people and things you dislike stay away from you! Why should personality have a standard answer? If everyone lives according to a certain type of personality, how boring would the world be? So just be yourself, be happy, and live for yourself. No need to hide your personality. If someone looks down on you, first reflect on yourself. Do you look down on yourself? Some people just enjoy criticizing you, they can't stand to see you doing well, they act as if you're nothing. Why bother paying attention to such situations? We know our own abilities, and that's enough. If you think you're not good enough, then work hard. It's for the purpose of becoming a better version of yourself, and that is living for yourself. Keep going, dear. You can live a better and more remarkable life. I believe in you!

Hello, it seems like when it comes to personality, you have a lot of question marks. I'll divide your description into the following four points: 1. Sensitivity, not knowing how to face the disdain of your relatives. 2. Trying to please others, not being able to refuse help from others, and regretting it afterwards. 3. What kind of personality is the standard personality? 4. How can you gain others' approval? These seem like four separate questions, but they are actually closely related. The core issue may be that you rely on external approval to determine your own self-worth. Because you desire others' approval, you want to know how to gain it, you want to understand if there is a standard personality, and you have difficulty refusing others and are sensitive. In reality, there is no such thing as a "standard personality". People's personalities vary greatly. Our self-worth is not determined by others' evaluations, but by our own definition. You can try bravely saying "no" to others, starting with small things, and take the first step. I'm not sure if it's a fact that your relatives look down on you or if it's a misunderstanding caused by your sensitivity. Because I don't know what exactly happened, you can think about it yourself. It's not important if others look down on you, but you mustn't look down on yourself. That's the key. Self-acceptance from within is more important than others' approval.

question: Is psychological counseling effective? How can we evaluate the effectiveness of psychological counseling?
description: After completing the counseling session, how can we assess its effectiveness? And how can we evaluate whether the psychological counseling has been effective or not?

answers.answer_text: Before discussing how to evaluate the effectiveness of psychological counseling, let's talk about when we can go to a counselor for a chat. When life becomes unbearable and we are entangled with certain emotions and states of mind, it feels like life is a mess. We feel terrible, and the world seems gray. We feel isolated from the whole world, and no one understands us. Marriage is causing us great pain, and we long for a happy life, but continuous arguments leave us exhausted. When we face difficulties in life, long-term low mood, insomnia, etc., seeking a conversation with a counselor is one option for us. Moreover, when our bodies feel unwell and doctors cannot find any illness, we experience a general discomfort that is difficult to express. Every part of our body may feel uncomfortable, and sometimes even painful. Despite medical examinations and doctors' diagnoses indicating no issues, we still feel uncomfortable. In some cases, these discomforts may even cause us to take time off work or school. At these times, someone may suggest consulting a professional counselor to find out what is going on. In the event of a major incident, frequent flashbacks, or being unable to cope with life events, such as heartbreak, conflicts in the dormitory, family disputes, exam failures, natural disasters, etc., if we encounter sudden changes and cannot handle them ourselves, and if there is no reliable person around us, a counselor is a good choice. Psychological counseling is a way of life and the relationship within it is neither that of a teacher nor a friend, but rather a pure presence. The counselor will be there to accompany and listen. They will listen to what you find difficult to express and what you feel the world does not allow you to say. In that period of time, it will be an exclusive space for two people, or three people, or a family. Combining the mentioned situations can make it clearer whether the counseling is effective. The effectiveness is reflected in: · being able to cope with life · feeling at ease in our bodies · being able to handle situations that we previously couldn't handle. Finally, when it comes to learning, there is a question to ponder: should counselors charge based on renting their time or based on the effectiveness of the counseling? In my opinion, it's the former. I am willing to use my expertise, concentrate, and accompany the person in front of me, impacting lives with my own life. May words accompany you.

Whether psychological counseling is effective and the quality of its effects can be evaluated from the following aspects: subjective psychological distress: whether there is a change in psychological distress, whether it increases or decreases, or even eliminates psychological distress. If you feel increasingly distressed after a period of psychological counseling, it is important to look into the reasons. Social functioning: if you were previously unable to study or work and can now do so normally, then it definitely indicates a positive effect. Interpersonal relationships: have interpersonal relationships become more harmonious? Are you still arguing every day? Can you establish intimate relationships? Has there been an improvement in overly close or distant and conflictual family relationships? Psychological/physiological symptoms: have various discomfort or distressing symptoms improved? Improvement in insomnia, relief from anxiety and depressive emotions are all evident outcomes of counseling. Psychometric results: Psychological measurements can also be conducted before and after psychological counseling to quantify its effectiveness.

question: During my first year of high school, I deceived someone on Xianyu and now I feel very guilty. What should I do about this guilt?
description: I remember when I was in the first year of high school, I was not very mature. I loved to play and blindly compare myself to others. I remember one time when my friend had a birthday and I didn't have enough money, so I posted my phone for sale on idle fish (an online marketplace). After that day, someone contacted me on idle fish. We hadn't said much, but he asked me to give him my Alipay account so he could transfer money to me. When the money arrived, I had a selfish thought. I genuinely wanted to sell the phone, but in the end, I selfishly took the money. Since that incident, I have constantly thought about it during nearly every quiz and exam in my second year of high school. And even now, as I'm about to enter my third year, I deeply regret it. This incident has made me feel guilty about everything I do. During this time, I have continuously tried to change myself and do many things to help others, but I still think about the mistake I made. I have also tried to find that buyer, but it has been a long time and I still can't find him. I feel very uneasy about it. Now that I'm about to enter my third year of high school, I don't want to be held back because of this one thing. I also feel remorseful about it. I hope everyone can help me and give me some advice. Thank you, everyone.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Everyone makes mistakes when they're young. Making mistakes is an important part of our growth process. Fortunately, you realize your mistake and are willing to make amends. I applaud your courage and kindness in admitting your mistake. First, let's define the nature of what you mentioned "cheating someone out of 750 yuan" behavior in terms of its nature. Only individuals who are over 14 years old but under 16 years old and commit intentional murder, intentional injury resulting in serious injury or death, rape, robbery, drug trafficking, arson, explosion, poisoning, are considered criminal and need to bear criminal responsibility. If a minor commits crimes other than those mentioned above before and after turning 16, only the criminal responsibility for the behavior after turning 16 will be pursued, and the behavior before the age of 16 will not be considered a crime. When you were a freshman in high school, you were probably only fifteen or sixteen years old, still a minor. According to the aforementioned legal provisions, the behavior you exhibited does not constitute a criminal offense, and you need to understand that. Secondly, from a moral perspective, indeed, cheating others out of their money is an unethical and deceitful behavior. I believe this is also why you feel remorse. So, I have a few suggestions for you: (1) Transactions on the e-commerce platform you mentioned are all recorded. Find the transaction record, contact the buyer from back then, return the 750 yuan to them, and apologize sincerely. This is a direct solution to the problem. (2) If the first option doesn't work, then you need to reconcile with yourself and compensate for your shortcomings by engaging in some charitable activities. However, don't blame yourself excessively. If this incident helps you grow into a kind, honest, and useful member of society, then I believe that is the true meaning behind this incident. Perhaps, the buyer from back then has already forgiven you, as they didn't report to the police or pursue legal action after realizing they were deceived. So, don't put too much psychological pressure on yourself. Be a person of kindness and integrity from now on! The above is my analysis and advice, hope it helps you! Take care!

OP, you may feel conflicted and unable to let go of a mistake you made unintentionally, which goes against your conscience. This actually shows that you are an honest and kind-hearted person because despite initially benefiting from it, you have been trying to make amends. For that matter, you didn't take pleasure in obtaining that money for nothing, instead, you have been feeling guilty because you made a mistake in the moment. A mistake is a mistake, and once something happens, it happens; there is no chance to start over. I know you are torn and uncomfortable inside, but the way to alleviate this conflict may be to proactively accept the past wrongdoing and accept the person you were back then. You may not be able to fully compensate for this incident, but perhaps you can awaken yourself in the future to not commit the same mistake again. You have been helping others, and I think you are doing well. This may reduce the guilt in your heart. Besides, you can also caution yourself not to do anything that goes against your conscience due to selfish motives or entertain any dishonest thoughts. This incident might be something you can't forget, and I understand your conflict, anxiety, and uneasiness. But perhaps what you need to do is to accept it. Treat it as an unexpected event in your life, apart from making efforts in other aspects to alleviate the unease in your conscience, you can also use it as a reminder in your heart to not repeat the same mistake in the future. It used to be a hurdle that you couldn't overcome in your heart, but from now on, turn it into a warning sign in your life, guiding your path so that there will be no more moral deviations. Best wishes!

question: Being particularly concerned about others' evaluations, I have become even more anxious after being promoted.
description: I have always been insecure and particularly concerned about others' opinions. I strive for perfection in everything I do and can't handle any negative feedback. Recently, I was promoted because of my good performance at work, but I am even more anxious now. I'm afraid that I won't be able to handle my new responsibilities. On one hand, I feel anxious about my job and even consider quitting. On the other hand, I blame myself for being useless and wonder why I get so anxious over such small things. Why can everyone else do it, but not me? I really don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ I want to give you a warm hug first. First, I want to say congratulations on your promotion. This is a recognition of your abilities by your superiors. After observing so many employees, they finally chose to promote you, which proves that you have good capabilities. It is because they believe in you and believe that you can handle this job that they promoted you. Your superiors believe in you, how can you not be confident? Perhaps the promotion will bring more work pressure and greater difficulty, but maybe you can see it as a new challenge. What you need to do is to work hard to complete it, instead of feeling anxious about it. You need to overcome it, instead of being afraid of it. Believe in yourself, don't pay too much attention to other people's opinions, as their opinions don't provide substantial help to you. If you still care about other people's opinions and judgments, then you need to do this job even better and make others look at you with new eyes.

question: I am homosexual and have fallen in love with a married person. I am very distressed, should I continue or not?
description: I am 23 and he is 31, married with children. We met on a dating app, which was quite a serendipitous encounter. We have known each other for almost 4 years and talked for 2 years before meeting in person and living together for over a year. However, he already has a child and a partner. After being together for six months, his partner found out about us and told her family. This year he wants to get a divorce. I don't know whether I should step back or continue. I feel like I am the third party, as he never answers my calls when his partner is around. I even attempted suicide and ended up in the hospital because of these issues. We are also in a long-distance relationship. I don't know if it's worth it to continue like this. We love each other very much, but with his 2-3 year-old child, I'm not sure if it's good for me to continue in this way. Whenever I call him, he seems annoyed. I want to ask if this relationship should still continue, and if so, how it will be.

answers.answer_text: There is no fundamental difference between same-sex love and opposite-sex love. In the current domestic environment, sometimes gay men marrying women and having children is a result of circumstances, objectively causing harm to the women involved, but I believe that moral judgments cannot be made simplistically. Coming out after marrying is different from a heterosexual man having an affair. Whether you are there or not, he will ultimately come out. Furthermore, he should bear and make up for the harm he has caused to the woman, rather than you being primarily responsible. I suggest putting aside moral judgments and looking at your relationship purely from a emotional perspective, whether it is appropriate or should continue. As for the issue of children, research in the United States has shown that the harm caused to children by a broken marriage is greater than the harm caused by divorce. What children need is love and attention, not the form of marriage. Sometimes adults reluctantly maintain a marriage because they feel it is shameful to divorce, but in reality, the harm to children is greater. If you both raise the child, research in the United States also shows that children raised by same-sex couples are no different from children raised in heterosexual families (contrary to concerns about influencing the child's sexual orientation, decades of empirical research show it does not happen). What matters here is still love and attention, not the form of marriage. Considering the domestic environment, it is advisable to consider living in culturally open first-tier or second-tier cities, where the societal pressure against homosexuality may be slightly lesser.

Hello, OP! Regardless of whether you are homosexual or involved as a third party, let's first talk about self-esteem. In this relationship, it seems that you have placed yourself in a very low position. You are 23 years old, he is 31 years old, clearly you are younger and have more possibilities, but in this relationship, you have more attachment tendencies and suffer greatly, constantly debating whether to end or continue. You mentioned that you met him on a social app, and it took two years of chatting before moving in together. Perhaps you are somewhat introverted and have set up multiple barriers, not letting others easily touch your fragile heart. Throughout the two years of communication, he slowly dismantled your defenses, making you emotionally dependent on him, and you believed and approved of him, ultimately choosing him as your partner. But in my opinion, this relationship is unequal. You have given everything to him, while he holds back. He is simultaneously maintaining a family and a relationship with you, and you have had conflicts with him, but what was the outcome? I think he probably used sweet words to make you choose to trust him again, and then this matter was swept under the rug, right? He is older than you and has more life experience, he has a wife and probably has had other same-sex or different-sex partners, and he works longer hours and holds a certain social status. These are not issues in a relationship, but the question is, is he using these to manipulate your emotions and keep you in a passive and suppressed state in this relationship? In your statement, you constantly belittle yourself, saying you are a male third party, but you are deeply in love. He wants to divorce but doesn't want to because of his child. You don't know whether to continue or give up. Regardless, please consider yourself more. Maybe you have strong psychological defenses and feel that it is difficult to find a suitable same-sex partner, and there may even be some conflicts with your family (because you only mentioned his family, not yours, so I'm simply speculating). Nevertheless, please have more confidence and understand your true thoughts. In this relationship, do you experience more self-confidence, self-love, comfort, safety, and happiness, or do you feel inferior, insecure, constantly frustrated, and afraid? If it's the latter, please detach yourself from this relationship in a timely manner. The future is unknown, it may be better or worse. But please believe in yourself and strive to unfold your life in a positive direction!

Give the original poster a hug! It is clear that the original poster is feeling anxious and conflicted in their heart. On one hand, they have known this person for a long time and have been living together, so there are bound to be emotions involved. It's not realistic to just let go. On the other hand, this person has a family with a wife and children, which means that they cannot openly live together in the long term. Acceptance of homosexuality is still limited in our country. Although some people can understand and accept it, there is still a large portion of the population who cannot. The pressure on the original poster and their partner is immense. Same-sex marriage is not legally recognized in our country, which means that same-sex relationships lack protection and support. If there are any unstable factors in the relationship, one person can easily leave without any responsibility, just like when the original poster's partner doesn't answer their phone when they are with their wife. The original poster feels helpless in this situation and can only hurt themselves to punish and torment themselves, causing both physical and mental distress. For the original poster, what they may want is a relationship they desire, but in reality, there are age differences and differences in how they approach and perceive relationships. The original poster is a single man, while the other person has a family and children. From both a legal and ethical standpoint, there are significant conflicts and pressures between the original poster's feelings and the realities of society. Additionally, the original poster mentioned that the other person has a 3-year-old son whom they are responsible for caring for. If they were to be together, the original poster would have to take on the role of a stepmother and bear the corresponding responsibilities, which would be a great pressure for them. On the other hand, if they were to separate, the original poster would no longer have to bear such great pressure and could live a more relaxed and enjoyable life. This relationship has already caused the original poster a lot of distress and pain, so they need to think about what they truly want: a light-hearted, happy, and sweet love, or a painful and difficult relationship. They need to put themselves in the right place, clarify their goals and direction in relationships, and accept their inner conflicts. By making a choice, they may find the answer they're looking for.

After carefully reading your confession, I deeply understand your pain. I send you a breath of fresh air to calm your inner unease. Here is my analysis: 1. "I want to ask if this relationship still needs to continue?" It is evident that you have made many sacrifices for him, including knowing each other for four years and living together. You even attempted suicide for him. You truly love him. So, ask yourself, does this relationship bring you happiness or pain? If it brings happiness, then continue. If it brings pain, then let it go. That would be the solution. 2. "What will happen if it continues?" If it continues, you can already see the future. Your relationship is not recognized by the law nor accepted by society. Even if he divorces, he may start a new family. You cannot become husband and wife. You will always have to be secretive about your relationship. Similarly, you will both face pressure from each other's families. 3. Of course, you can also follow the example of Jin Xing and undergo gender reassignment. However, this comes with expensive surgery costs and a series of postoperative complications. Do you think you can afford it? These are the series of questions I have analyzed for you. The most important thing is for you to be happy. Anything that goes against the principle of happiness is wrong. If being in a same-sex relationship brings you unprecedented happiness, then hold on. I send you blessings from afar. Thank you for your question, and may the beauty of the world reach you as planned.

Since you can't think clearly at the moment, it's best to separate and calm down for a while. It doesn't mean I want you to break up, just temporarily not to contact each other, to give yourself some time to think things through, and also give the other person some time. I understand that you have a guilty conscience, but you need to understand that life is complicated and there isn't always a right or wrong. Whether or not you are willing to bear the conscience condemnation that comes with loving someone is up to you. Whether or not he is willing to give up his family for you is his decision, don't interfere with it in any way. Whether or not to continue is not solely your decision, I suggest you have an honest conversation with the other person and decide together if you should separate or continue. If the other person has a clear plan and will arrange things with his wife and children before being with you, that would be a responsible approach and a future worth entrusting to. If the other person is indecisive and unwilling to let go of either side, I suggest you let go. You're only 23, there's no need to entangle yourself with a greedy person.

I feel that loving someone means wanting them to be better. If they also love you and can negotiate with their other half to peacefully separate, then everyone will be happy. If they don't love you, of course, you can choose to continue loving them. That is your right, but you also need to maintain a distance. This is your responsibility. Love has no right or wrong. I hope you keep your original intention.

Take a moment to reflect on why you like this person and what you hope to gain from them. You have a whole lifetime ahead of you, with many beautiful things to come, whereas this person already has a family and responsibilities. It's unclear what you want from this relationship, but some sense of security that others can offer can easily be lost. It is advisable to let go of these desires and aspirations. Years from now, when you look back on this experience, you will gain new insights. There are other things in life waiting for you to pursue.

Hello, I can really understand your feelings. Because when I was in college, I also liked a guy who was in a different city. He was handsome, considerate, and attracted me. He was honest and responsible, telling me everything, and I knew everything, including the fact that he had a boyfriend, so I sometimes felt like a third person. Later, I chose to be good friends and didn't expect any specific outcome. Because I liked him, I just wanted every conversation to be a beautiful memory. I can only share my experience with you: there is no right or wrong in love, and I respect the choices you are about to make. I hope I can give you some warmth.

question: Because of the accident, I have developed a mild case of obsessive-compulsive disorder, and now I'm hesitating about whether or not to learn more about it.
description: Before, I was unsuccessful in helping a stranger. During the rescue process, I realized that the real situation was very different from what I learned in class. The person was seriously injured and passed away. Afterward, I have been self-funding my study of some first aid courses. After some time, I compelled myself to study again, thinking that I could better cope with similar situations. However, the content of each course is more or less the same. Now, I hesitate whether I should continue studying the related materials or not.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! First of all, sending you a warm hug. Secondly, I want to tell you, "It's not your fault." I can sense that you are a kind-hearted and compassionate person, so when you encountered a stranger in need before, you didn't hesitate to step forward and help. Unfortunately, despite your best efforts, the person still passed away due to severe injuries. It seems that since then, you have been feeling a lot of guilt, and you have been repeatedly forcing yourself to take first aid courses, even at your own expense. I understand that you want to be prepared in case you encounter a similar situation in the future, so that you can assist others better and try to make up for the regret of the previous incident. However, I want to say that you have already done very well within your capabilities. Although the outcome is regrettable, his passing is not your fault, and you don't have to blame yourself excessively. Even skilled doctors sometimes encounter patients that cannot be saved. So please, really, don't be too hard on yourself. It's not your fault. Once again, sending you a warm hug. Now, should you continue to learn more about this topic? In the description, you mentioned that you have already forced yourself to learn a lot of related knowledge, and the content of each course is similar. In that case, I suggest that you focus on mastering the courses you have already learned. After all, repeatedly paying for and studying courses with the same content would be a waste of money. Additionally, tasks that you force yourself to do usually don't yield the best results. Dealing with someone in need of emergency assistance is also a low probability event, so don't put too much mental pressure on yourself. What should you do if you encounter such a situation? I think the first thing to do is to call for emergency assistance. Professional matters should be left to the professionals, and the equipment in a hospital is more helpful for treating patients. After making the call, we need to remain calm. Before the ambulance arrives, apply the first aid techniques you have learned immediately to the person in need, and buy more time for the medical staff. Lastly, I admire your kindness. Kudos to you!

question: Do all people with "hoarding disorder" have a mental illness? How to communicate with them?
description: Seeing my sister always hoarding various notebooks and jars has reached almost a crazy level. I don't know how to communicate with her and ask her to tidy up a bit. There is now only space for walking and the bed in her room. Does her "hoarding disorder" represent a mental illness?

answers.answer_text: Hello! The person you described with hoarding disorder has a house filled with only a bed and walking space, which can be really distressing. From a psychological perspective, people with hoarding tendencies feel unable to discard objects that may seem worthless or useless to others. Typically, individuals with this compulsive hoarding behavior have a strong possessiveness and struggle to part with even insignificant items. These objects take up living space and can disrupt or hinder normal functioning in daily life. Compulsive hoarding is often related to "trauma psychology" and may serve as a way of self-expression and emotional release. Some individuals frequently experience remorse and self-blame after hoarding, yet they find themselves unable to control the urge to hoard, indicating an inner conflict. Since the hoarding behavior significantly impairs normal daily functioning and generates numerous negative emotions, over time these negative emotions can severely impact both mental and physical health. It is recommended to take your sister to see a professional counselor or psychologist.

question: No one has ever truly seen the real me, they've only seen my mask?
description: I have many friends, but there are definitely no more than two people who truly know the real me. Even that person doesn't understand me completely. I feel like I'm being fake in my life, but I can't help it. I can never open up and trust others completely. There was also a period of time when I felt like I was emotionless, with an empty mind and no thoughts. I just felt like, "Ah, whatever, it doesn't matter, it's always like this." Am I sick? I often doubt myself, but I don't want to tell my parents that something is wrong with my mental health. I don't think it's necessary. It doesn't matter to me, anyway, because it's always like this.

answers.answer_text: Hello, young soul, this is not an illness. Most people have this kind of distress, unable to show their true selves to close ones. On one hand, they are afraid that others won't understand or accept their true selves, and on the other hand, they are protecting their inner selves from harm. The fact that you have many friends suggests that, in their eyes, you and they are compatible in some aspects. The incomplete understanding of your closest friend might make you feel a sense of emptiness. If someone knows everything about you, do you think you would feel exposed in front of them? Your "pretense" with friends may just be the definition you have given yourself for not expressing your true self, while friends don't see it as "pretense." Having no emotions and feeling empty inside is a state of emptiness, perhaps occurring when your mind wanders while with friends. No one knows you better than yourself. Firstly, you need to understand yourself, to understand your own mental state and emotions. Then, you need to accept yourself, accepting your good and bad aspects. Finally, you need to reconcile with yourself, doing more things that interest you to fill the sense of emptiness inside. When you fully accept yourself, you will naturally share more of your true self with friends. Thank you for meeting.

question: Why is self-discipline poor and self-indulgence easy when being alone?
description: It's past 10 o'clock at night, and everyone has gone to sleep. I was really tired and sleepy, and I also wanted to sleep. Suddenly, I felt that I finally had some free time without being disturbed, so I opened my phone to read a novel. I initially planned to go to bed at 11 o'clock, but I lost control and ended up staying up until 1 o'clock in the morning. I'm so confused, why is it easy to indulge myself when I'm alone?
keywords: Behavior, confusion, smartphone dependence, staying up late.

answers.answer_text: Questioner, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description, you have noticed that you have poor self-discipline when being alone at night, and you tend to stay up out of revenge. Perhaps you feel confused about this behavior of yours, and I can relate to it too. Based on your description, you were already really tired and wanted to sleep at night, but the thought of finally having your own alone time made you indulge in reading novels, thereby sacrificing your rest time. The result of staying up out of revenge is that you will feel mentally off the next day, and your efficiency in studying or working will decrease. I noticed that you mentioned feeling a sense of freedom and being undisturbed suddenly. Although I don't know your specific situation, I think you may not have enough rest time during the day, as all of your time is occupied by work or studying. The quiet atmosphere at night may make you relax, easily leading to the idea of staying up. I suggest you learn about the mindful way of thinking, and the simplest way is to consider all the tasks of the day as your own time, regardless of whether you like doing them. It may seem simple, but often, the feeling of laziness we experience when facing work is because we don't consider the time spent on it as our own time.

I originally planned to sleep at 11 o'clock, but ended up delaying it until 1 o'clock. I wanted to give myself some time and plan it, but it became an abyss that I couldn't escape from. I guess many people can relate to this as well, right? At least after reading this, I also realize that being alone requires the prefrontal lobe to make decisions about interests, while indulging in solitude allows the limbic system to provide feedback. Whether to indulge or discipline oneself ultimately depends on individual choices. Perhaps it is because I wanted to give myself time and enjoy the "freedom and relaxation" that I ended up using more time. How much impact the event itself has on me and whether it is necessary to change, if it is not necessary, maybe it's just better to enjoy it. It is difficult to satisfy both the prefrontal lobe and the limbic system at the same time, and the anxiety of trying to achieve both may be even more painful. Maybe you can set aside a few days specifically for indulgence, which might be better?

question: After getting into a relationship, I feel really uncomfortable when my partner interacts with other girls. Am I being too possessive?
description: Since June of this year when my boyfriend and I officially started dating, my parents have been pressuring me to get engaged because they think he is excellent. This has made me feel hesitant because he has a prosthetic leg and I want to take more time to see how well we can adjust to this. Recently, my parents heard a rumor that someone had introduced another girl to my boyfriend after we started dating. He even saw the girl's photo. My boyfriend claims he declined the offer, but when I jokingly asked to see the photo, he refused, saying he had already deleted it. I feel like he is lying. My parents blame me for not quickly getting engaged to him and say my emotional intelligence is low, even suggesting that I need someone to teach me how to date. I feel really hurt that my boyfriend has been in contact with another girl while we were already in a committed relationship and he kept it a secret for half a month. I'm really conflicted now and don't want to get engaged. Am I being too petty?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Your parents think he is excellent and want you to get engaged as soon as possible. Firstly, in this relationship, it's your parents who think he is excellent and want you to marry him. Moreover, you only confirmed your relationship in June, and the foundation of your feelings is not strong yet. This kind of marriage feels like the arranged marriages in ancient times, where parents of both sides think it's a good match and make the arrangements. Modern society promotes freedom - freedom in marriage, freedom in love. Even if the other person is excellent, so what? If you get married and are unhappy and end up divorcing, what's the point of getting married? Find someone who loves you and is focused on you, and you won't have to worry about them cheating. Isn't that the ideal marriage? After your boyfriend confirmed the relationship with you, when he heard about him going on blind dates, whether it was his parents forcing him or him rejecting them, he still implicitly allowed such a thing to happen and also hid it from you. I think you need to carefully consider someone like that. Just like how your parents think he is excellent and want you to marry him, does that mean he and his parents are also seeking a better match? This also indirectly reflects that his parents don't approve of you much. If your in-laws and husband don't love you, your life will be very difficult after you get married. If you feel wronged, there will be no one to confide in because your family likes your husband-to-be, and you will feel like it's your fault if you complain. Marriage is a lifelong commitment and the most important choice for a woman's life. If you make the right choice, your life will become increasingly happy. So, I hope OP carefully considers and understands their own feelings and chooses what they think is right!

Hello, since you and your boyfriend became official, your parents have been putting pressure on you to get engaged because they think highly of him. However, for various reasons, you have concerns and have not made this decision. Regardless of what these concerns mean to your parents or to your relationship with them, they are important and meaningful to you. Marriage may involve both families, but ultimately it is the two of you who will be living your lives together. During this period of adjustment, you heard that your boyfriend went on a blind date with another girl, even though nothing came of it. This action made you feel uncomfortable. It is evident that you have certain principles and thoughts when it comes to relationships. Being in a relationship means mutual trust, and your partner's actions undoubtedly crossed a boundary, which most people find unacceptable. Therefore, it is normal to feel uneasy. This does not mean you are being narrow-minded; it reflects your perspective on relationships. If someone accepts the idea of cohabitation before marriage and believes that any relationship before marriage is not official, then having ambiguous encounters with potential partners may be acceptable to them. However, for those who don't accept this viewpoint, it is naturally unacceptable, and most people would feel the same. Perhaps through this incident, you can reflect on what kind of relationship and marriage you truly want. At the same time, have a deep and meaningful conversation with your partner about their thoughts on this matter and why they took that action, in order to resolve any tension between the two of you. Best wishes! Karen.

Thank you for the invitation and thank you for the question. First of all, let's not overthink anything.
