Let's calm down and put everything aside for now, like prosthetics, parents, etc. Ask yourself a question. Just go with your gut instinct, your first reaction. Do you have confidence in marrying him now and having a happy and fulfilling life together? If you have an answer, great. Questioner, is your boyfriend truly outstanding, or do your parents think he is outstanding? Do your parents really think he is outstanding, or do they think that he is the best you can get compared to others, so they consider him outstanding? You, as the questioner, are a normal person with normal intelligence. You should be able to figure this out. Questioner, love and marriage are your own matters. Starting a romantic relationship or getting married just because of pressure, without really wanting to, is not advisable. If it leads to an unhappy outcome, even if you entered into a relationship and marriage due to pressure from others, you will be the one who bears the consequences of that unhappiness and harm. Have you thought about that? Who will help you bear the burden if it turns out to be unhappy? I do not recommend rushing into marriage without being prepared, including being mentally prepared. Moreover, an unhappy marriage cannot keep anyone tied down. At most, it will only wear down both parties in the unhappy marriage, and may even result in mutual harm. At that point, some parents might think it wasn't worth it. Young lady, it is not marriage that keeps someone tied down. If things don't work out, some people will divorce, and sometimes it can be a messy and negative experience that affects the rest of their lives. Furthermore, ask yourself, are you truly satisfied with your boyfriend? For example, with his prosthetics, which you mentioned. Are you satisfied to the point where you can marry him with peace of mind? Questioner, are you not concerned at all about this somewhat forced engagement? If it's true that he went on blind dates with others, then why blame you for not being able to keep a man? How can a man who is not wholeheartedly focused on one woman be kept by that woman? It's not this woman's fault if he is not single-minded in this matter. You are already engaged, yet he still goes on blind dates with others. If that is indeed the case, Questioner, do you think he respects you? If he behaves this way now, what about after marriage? Will he suddenly start to respect you and your family? Will it not instead lead to a strange kind of self-confidence? After all, he has done all of this, and someone is pushing their daughter onto him. How desperate must she be to get married? Questioner, have you thought about the prospect of being looked down upon in your married life? And can you guarantee that after agreeing to the engagement, he won't hide anything from you and your family in the future? Young lady, when it comes to marriage or dating, the most important thing to consider is character, isn't it? Otherwise, jumping into a fire pit, how will you get out of it later on? Everyone has the right to pursue a happy married life, but the prerequisite is based on mutual respect and understanding. If it is because your parents feel that due to certain reasons, like a supermarket selling discounted remaining fruits in order to keep them fresh, you are being married off or taking a bride. Then this already violates the baseline of equality and mutual respect. I'm afraid that such a marriage is bound to be unhappy from the beginning. Being stuck in a situation where you constantly compare what you have with what you could have, isn't that a kind of itching in your heart? Do you think it's just your pettiness or could it be that they are also not so sure about you and are also feeling forced? Young lady, whether a person is happy or not may depend on how they accept their true selves, how they strive for a life they enjoy, how they believe in themselves in difficult times, how effectively they communicate with themselves and others, etc. Entrusting the rest of your life to an engagement and marriage that feels rushed and forced, like quickly selling leftover fruit, isn't the risk too great? And it's not because you have a small-mindedness, is it?

Actually, when it comes to your feelings, you have your own thoughts and may want to see how things develop. However, at the same time, there is another voice around you, coming from your parents, who hope you can quickly hold onto this person simply because they are outstanding. So, I think comparing these two voices makes you question whether you are being too narrow-minded in not wanting to get engaged. Understand that you are not being narrow-minded. Marriage is about the rest of your life, so it is normal to take more time to observe and consider. Since you already have some intuition, it is even more important not to rush into making a major life decision. You should carefully examine the situation. So, in this matter, you can also listen to your own voice, because your voice understands you the best. From your parents' perspective, they also have your best interest at heart and want to quickly catch onto this outstanding person. However, in the long run, if you feel that you need more time to assess, then you should listen to yourself. Understand that whatever decision or doubt you have, there is a reason behind it, so don't think that your doubts should not exist. Allow yourself to raise questions.

"...Serious indecisiveness... is absolutely unforgivable. It is very correct for you to re-evaluate your relationship with him, and I give you a thumbs-up for that. He must give you a very reasonable and acceptable reason; his attitude will determine the future of your emotions. From the information you have provided so far, it is unclear what makes you satisfied with him, whether it is good looks, wealth, or talent, everything is unknown... The choices for a good life cannot be influenced by the bickering of people around you... Listen to your inner voice and keep going!"

question: Is it normal to feel anxious and fearful in busy places where there are bright lights and a lot of alcohol?
description: I am very afraid of places that are full of bright lights, revelry, and bustle. Every time I travel or go out and enter similar places, I feel a great sense of insecurity and want to escape. Over time, I don't like going out or traveling. Is this normal? What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP, nice to meet you through words. First of all, from your description, I can imagine that such a state must have had a significant impact on your life and some interpersonal relationships. It takes a lot of courage to actively explore and find ways to solve the problem, which is not easy. Secondly, the situation you described belongs to a specific space phobia. This kind of situation is a relatively common problem, but each person presents it differently. However, the anxiety and fear you mentioned belong to typical problems of weak psychological abilities and resilience. Emotions are usually a projection of people's inner feelings, that is, their true inner demands. Fear is a manifestation of a lack of control over possible or imminent events. In other words, you are very worried that you will not be able to control and solve problems that may occur in such situations, so your instinct of self-protection will choose to escape. In this situation, you can try diaphragmatic breathing when you feel scared or anxious, which will help you relax and make you feel less uncomfortable. But it is important to focus your attention on your breathing and make sure that it is diaphragmatic breathing!!! If you are not familiar with it, you can place your hand on your abdomen to feel the rise and fall with each breath. Remember: do not use chest breathing, as it will only make you more anxious. Lastly, the formation of all psychological problems is not something that happens overnight. Therefore, if you want to solve the problem from its roots, you need to figure out why you developed such specific fears. You can try to recall the scene when you first encountered this situation or what happened at that time. This will be beneficial to help you find the cause of the problem. Alternatively, you can seek professional psychological counseling to explore personal growth and discover the reasons behind the issue. By doing so, you can enhance your psychological abilities and resilience, as well as regain control and a sense of security in such situations.

question: When visitors develop transference, how should a novice counselor solve it?
description: Transference is something that frequently occurs in counseling sessions. If transference is handled properly, the counseling relationship may become more stable and breakthroughs can be made in the visitor's problems. However, dealing with transference can be somewhat challenging for novice counselors. So, how can novice counselors learn to address the visitor's transference?

answers.answer_text: In dealing with transference, I personally believe that the first step is to clearly inform the other person once this situation is discovered. Secondly, after informing the other person about this situation, it is possible to explore why the counseling party has a transference effect and then address the problem directly. In addition, in most cases, people who come for counseling experience transference because the counselor, as a listener, shows understanding towards their experiences. Therefore, for many counseling subjects who have existing issues, this becomes a way for them to gain self-identity and a sense of security. Until they have other ways to obtain self-identity and a sense of security, they will develop a dependency on the counselor. This is similar to relying on floating logs in a flood. In this regard, my personal suggestion is to recommend that counseling subjects participate in group activities with homogeneity. This way, the scope of their venting is no longer limited to the counselor alone, reducing their dependency and transference towards the counselor.

question: 13-year-old wants to die
description: Attempted suicide…………………………………………

answers.answer_text: Dear darling, although I don't know what happened to you, let me give you a hug first (´∩ω∩｀). I hope I can bring you a little warmth through the screen. What was I doing at thirteen? I was probably getting close to my high school entrance exam. It's quite a coincidence when I think about it. At that time, I was immersed in time-travel novels and firmly believed that I would time-travel before the exam. Even though the exam was approaching, I didn't study at all because I truly believed I wouldn't need it. Unfortunately, in the end, I took the exam just like in a dream and did terribly. The perplexed looks from my parents, the pain of shattered dreams, the high cost of attending a different school, and the guilt in my heart overwhelmed me. Going to a strange school, unfamiliar environment, and high-pressure studying all made me wonder why I had to endure all of this. Later, with the company of friends and the encouragement from my parents, I slowly regained the joy of life. So, my sweetheart, there are still many things in this world worth exploring. If possible, we are willing to listen to your venting. I hope I can bring you a bit of warmth in this world. I love the world, and I love you too. Take care.

OP, hello~~~ First, give you a hug, if you're willing, could you please talk in detail about your emotions and troubles? Feeling sad and upset are common in life, encountering unpleasant things is also normal, so it's not unusual for most people to have had thoughts of ending their own lives at some point in their lives. But can OP give your family and friends another chance to talk with everyone? Everyone has the right to decide their own future, I don't know what has happened to OP, maybe I can't understand your sadness, but I still hope that OP can have a good rest for now, wake up and have a cup of warm milk, then slowly think about your own things. Maybe by that time, OP's feelings will be completely different. Hope it helps OP.

I have also had moments like this. But all things are not valid reasons for you to feel unworthy of living; you have lost yourself. You have experienced so much pain, but it will eventually become your wealth in the future, as others have told me. It seems like you are being covered by something, unable to see the truth, just like a math problem that you can't seem to solve, causing you unbearable pain, as if you are the dumbest person in the world. But who knows, one day you will suddenly have an insight! It's just a math problem, what will happen if you don't solve it?! You just haven't seen that there are billions of people who can't solve even simpler problems.

question: Why do I always think about giving up? How can I get rid of this childish idea?
description: In the past few days, I have been sleeping around 10 o'clock and waking up at 4 o'clock to study. These days, I have been sleeping around 12 o'clock and waking up at six or seven. How can I stop staying up so late? Moreover, I always convince myself that I can study without going to the study room, but in reality, I can't study properly. It's frustrating because on one hand, I want to pass the exam, but on the other hand, I don't want to be too tired. How can I get rid of this childish mindset?

answers.answer_text: Hello! You are struggling with yourself, with an id and a superego. But in reality, the id has taken the upper hand, causing confusion in the self. How can you have the best of both worlds? It is clear that your idea of having the best of both worlds is impossible, so you yourself feel that you need to get rid of this childish idea. Great! You have started to realize and hope to find a solution. Thumbs up to you! For the past few days, you have been sleeping at around ten o'clock and waking up at around four in the morning to study. These days, you have been sleeping around twelve o'clock and waking up at six or seven. This actually refers to two different study methods, with no right or wrong, just whether they are suitable for you or not! Why did you change from sleeping at around ten o'clock to twelve o'clock? Did it affect your studying? Both methods are not easy, just choose the one that works better for you and stick with it! Some people have higher efficiency studying at night, so they sleep and wake up later. As long as you feel energized the next day and can continue studying efficiently, this is also a good method! Don't be too concerned about the process, the process is just a means to an end. As long as the process helps you achieve your goals, it is worth persevering. Of course, the study environment does have an impact on your studying efficiency. Some people choose to study in noisy environments to train their willpower. This is not a scientific approach because willpower is limited. If you use it to deal with a noisy environment, you'll have less willpower for studying. Therefore, a study room is a relatively good study environment. Use the environment to help improve your studying efficiency. I hope you can stay firm in your goals, overcome the current difficulties, and a bright future awaits you! Good luck!

question: Is it a problem of consumption and values if one has strong desires but poor self-control?
description: I grew up in a relatively poor rural area and had never experienced much in the world. Although I spent money carelessly, I never borrowed money. Until I met a friend who introduced me to hot pot for the first time and brainwashed me into buying an iPhone. Although iPhones are indeed very good, they are quite expensive. When I bought it, I was allowed to pay in installments. It was the first time I did something like that, and since then, I have changed. I started buying things in installments, such as cosmetic surgery and games. Although I used to spend a lot on games, I never borrowed money or made in-game purchases. I also have strong desires and poor self-control. I always say that once I have something, I won't pursue anything else, but I always can't resist. At first, I started spending money on games because I might have been emotionally affected, and even in games, there are different levels of hierarchy. How can I change?

answers.answer_text: Hello! Here's a hug for you! I can also understand that your self-control is poor and your desire for shopping and consumption is strong. But you are lucky, as you are now aware of this. I believe there are three reasons that may have led to this mindset. Firstly, you experienced the immediate pleasure of consumption, which reinforced that experience. As you mentioned, you used to live in a relatively poor rural area. So, when you came out, you were dazzled by the outside world and wanted to try everything, see everything, and Alipay and credit cards allowed you to consume beyond your means. This undoubtedly provided you with the conditions for consumption. The joyful feeling of spending money kept increasing, so you couldn't control yourself anymore, even though you already had a lot of debt to pay off. The right to freely dispose of money increased. In the past, my parents controlled my money very strictly, so when I had the freedom to use money, I also spent without restraint because the feeling of having the freedom to dispose of money was too good. After you started working, it should be the same for you, having the freedom to use your own salary to buy whatever you want. There was no correct concept established. Our beliefs are actually influenced by the environment. I hope this doesn't offend you, but I assume that you didn't continue your education and started working after leaving the rural area. I guess you are also not very old. And at this age, it's important for us to establish our own core values. Were the values of getting cosmetic surgery and ranking high in games passed on to you by the people around you, and then you were influenced by them? Seeing this, I hope you don't get discouraged. Nothing is difficult if you put your heart into it! As long as we start making efforts to change ourselves now, it's never too late! My suggestion is to practice self-control. You can start by not playing games, and if you can't do it all at once, limit yourself to only one game per day. The general idea is to start practicing self-control with small things. Learn. If you have time, consider enrolling in adult education classes to enrich yourself. If you don't have time, buy a few books and read a little bit at a time. Regardless of which option, as long as you are learning, you are enriching yourself. Plan your finances reasonably. You can take online courses on financial management or buy books to do some simple financial planning for yourself. Meditate. Have a dialogue with yourself, let yourself settle down, and practicing meditation can also improve self-control, killing two birds with one stone!

question: How to heal after a breakup that happened over a year ago?
description: Last year we broke up, it has been over a year now. Even though it seemed like I initiated the breakup, it was actually because we were giving each other the silent treatment for a week, and I couldn't control myself from asking and questioning him why he was acting that way. When we first broke up, I often suffered from insomnia and played games all the time, and even playing games was because of him, so I would often lose control of my emotions while playing. I constantly questioned myself why this happened when everything was fine before. I would go back and forth between understanding and being torn. This went on repeatedly. He didn't do anything particularly wrong, he just did what a boyfriend should do. But I'm still very attached to him and can't let go. Later on, things started to get back to normal, and it was because there was an earthquake where I was, and I only called him. He never answered, and at that moment, I was thinking if I died, would he feel any pain inside. In that sense of disappointment, the pain became less evident. Slowly, I didn't miss him as much. Recently, the yearning for him has become strong again. I suddenly realized that I might not be able to move on, even though I may come across someone who sparks my interest now, but as soon as I contemplate going further, I start losing interest. We were in a long-distance relationship, relying mostly on video calls, and I was the one who always went to see him.

answers.answer_text: Hello, the core issue: unable to let go after more than a year of breakup and difficulty accepting new relationships. Analysis: from the overall description, it seems that the entire post revolves around 'him', discussing how he treated you, what he did while in a relationship, and even whether he would be sad if an earthquake happened... Have you noticed, you were originally an independent individual, but you have become like an empty shell without personal thoughts, constantly revolving around his actions and thoughts, and absorbing the negative energy emitted by him to sustain yourself. You cannot find a sense of self-worth in love relationships, so once someone establishes a connection with you, you completely entrust yourself to another person. As psychologist Wu Zhihong said, the other person feels that you want to cling to them, hang on them, which is very burdensome and instinctively makes them want to escape. So even if you question him, why? He can only feel a choking discomfort and cannot give you a precise answer. Therefore, even if you now enter into a new relationship, you still feel helpless, and your sense of self is empty or even occupied by your ex, inevitably losing motivation and interest. If you don't realize the seriousness of lacking self-identity/self-worth, no matter how many relationships you have, they will be filled with the fear of being abandoned. Suggestions: since the reason you still can't let go of a relationship that has been separated for a year is due to a lack of self-identity/self-worth, in simple terms, it means you don't know how to love yourself. Loving oneself is an abstract concept, so now I'll give you some specific feasible practices. Transform the habit of focusing on others' feelings into first being aware of your own feelings in everything, for example, in a situation, first recognize your emotion: sadness/anger/happiness, etc. Persist in engaging in activities that are beneficial for self-improvement and building self-confidence, such as practicing hobbies like drawing/calligraphy/music/reading, or doing exercise and fitness. Physical fitness also to some extent determines confidence. Strengthen the belief in self-affirmation, give yourself suggestions before sleeping, "I am great, I am worthy", and bring self-affirmation into the subconscious. Surround yourself with positive and appreciative people who inspire you, they will unconsciously influence your self-confidence. When you fully do the above points, you will understand the meaning of the phrase "if you bloom, butterflies will come", relationships are the result of mutual attraction, not simply one person blindly pursuing and unequal giving can bring good results.

First of all, I see that being heartbroken has caused you a lot of pain this past year, and I also see that you have been trying hard to overcome this pain and have achieved some results. However, recently, this pain has surged back and made you feel like you can't move forward. You hope to get help in healing your wounds. Before answering your question, I want to give you a hug to express my comfort to you. It is normal to feel pain and sadness for a period of time after a heartbreak, but if you cannot get over it and cannot enter into a new relationship, even if you meet someone you are interested in, you start losing interest once you think about taking it further. In psychology, this is called "generalization," where you associate the pain from previous heartbreaks with any future relationship. In order to improve your current state, you should start with the following aspects: 1. Restore a normal daily life and adjust your emotional state. Stick to a regular daily routine, preferably with a strict schedule, and check every day if you have been following it. This is the first step in adjusting your emotional state. Only with a normal life can you stabilize your emotions and recover from the pain of a heartbreak. 2. Participate in more recreational and social activities. These activities are effective ways to adjust your emotional state. Through recreational activities and social interactions, you can fully release the suppressed feelings of pain and sadness, further adjusting your emotional state. By communicating and connecting with others, you can listen to their opinions and experiences about heartbreak, which can also help release your own emotional pain. 3. Use some positive affirmations to boost your confidence. As your emotional state recovers, you can start using positive affirmations, such as "the previous relationship is in the past, and I need to start a new one," or "what's done is done, only by ending it can I truly start again." This can better help you restore and boost your confidence. 4. Reflect on the lessons learned and start a new relationship. Only when your emotions are stable can you truly analyze the problems in your previous relationships. As the saying goes, it takes two to tango. You need to analyze your own strengths and weaknesses and acknowledge the areas where you may have fallen short, as well as recognize the areas where your ex-partner may have been at fault. This will provide you with valuable experience and lessons for your next relationship.

Hello, OP. Long-distance relationships rely on video calls, and it is you who takes the initiative to reach out to him each time. You hope to receive a strong response and a high level of attention from him, but it never happens. After a cold war, you blame and question him, eventually leading to a breakup. Immersed in the pain of losing him, you found a sense of existence. You desperately hope that even after the breakup, you still hold the most important place in his heart. However, reality seems to slap you in the face once again. The intense desire to have what you cannot obtain, the strong attachment and entanglement, the inability to heal, the fear, the distress... Is it like this? Many people experience the pain of a breakup. The rupture of a relationship indeed causes one's self to collapse for a certain period of time, and it does require time for rebuilding and healing. However, over the past year, it seems that you haven't really rebuilt yourself, and this wound has even worsened. It might seem like the reason for the breakup is responsible for the current situation, but from your description, it can be seen that this trauma may have existed long before, and the breakup only triggered its manifestation. And subconsciously, you chose to stay in the same place to "savor" the pain instead of choosing personal growth because pain and lack of love are the most familiar feelings to you. Therefore, I hope that you can be more vigilant and reflect on yourself at this stage. What is your emotional pattern? What was the reason for your breakup? Do you need to take responsibility for it? Did you fail to establish an attachment with your family and parents? Do you believe in love? Do you believe that you deserve to be loved? With awareness, observe that wounded and fragile little girl within you, give her love and acceptance, and then you can reduce excessive demands and emotional reactions. As for how to break up with your ex-boyfriend, I recommend watching the course by Teacher Lu Qi. They use the theory of cognitive psychology to establish a systematic approach on how to break up and how to get through the healing period after a breakup. I won't go into further detail here. In life, we will always encounter the pain of separation and breakup. Only through pain, self-growth, and self-responsibility can you truly help yourself move away from pain and heal. Self-growth is a path you can choose at any time. May you love yourself, and may someone who truly deserves you love you. For more emotional Q&A, please follow "Xie Xie You Ke"~

Why did you first suggest breaking up? Maybe when you suggested the breakup, deep down you didn't really want to break up, but rather wanted to see your boyfriend's reaction to prove something or give you a sense of certainty? Think about what you need, tell him directly, face your own needs and his real response to your needs, maybe it can help you make a decision faster, whether to go or stay?

question: There are always many negative images that appear, escaping from reality, feeling unhappy oneself.
description: There are many negative feelings coming out of my head. Something very private has been known by everyone, and I feel very hurt and unhappy! I feel very suppressed! I really want to resign and don't want to go to work! These thoughts of escaping reality make me unhappy.

answers.answer_text: Hello! It's frustrating when someone knows a private matter in your mind. Take a moment to think about it, how did you find out that someone knew about your privacy? Or did you imagine it yourself? Instead of worrying about it, why not investigate if that privacy really leaked? By addressing anxiety promptly, you can give yourself a relieved heart and lead a peaceful life.

question: I no longer care about my mom now, am I really sick? Or am I just selfish?
description: I used to care a lot about whether my mom was healthy and if she was safe on the road. I was afraid something might happen to her, maybe because I didn't know how to handle it. And I really wanted her to be happy because I knew she had a hard life, so I wanted to make money and support her. But later, I went through a heartbreak and some other things, and I became numb to her tears. I just felt annoyed and didn't want to cause her trouble. I just wanted to die. I hoped she could live well, and I didn't care whether she was in pain or not. Anyway, I just stopped caring about her. I feel like my emotions are hard to control sometimes, but at the time, I knew clearly what I was doing. But now, when I'm calm, I don't quite understand why I acted like that. Is it because I'm sick or just pretending to be sick to be selfish? I think I still have thoughts, but I just let myself go.
keywords: Emotions, expressing emotions, emotional regulation, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text:
Hello, I see your concerns and I hope I can help you. From your description, I can see that you are a responsible and caring son who wants to bring happiness and joy to your mother. Your filial piety is commendable. I also understand that you are not entirely satisfied with your current state due to a breakup and other reasons, but you don't want it to affect your mother. I can understand your emotions and feelings when facing your mother's inquiries. Let's try to look at these situations from a different perspective. 

Firstly, take responsibility for yourself. Whether it's a breakup or other worries, it's something that many people go through in this stage of life. Don't doubt yourself because of it, especially for a breakup, as it's not something you can decide on your own. There are many objective reasons behind it. Don't beat yourself up over it, instead, see it as a process of gaining experience. Allow others to not accept you and allow yourself to experience heartbreak temporarily. It's okay to feel sad, but also remember that love is just a part of life and it doesn't determine everything. Take responsibility for yourself.

Secondly, let your mother know. It's evident that you love your mother very much. Due to your reasons, you may genuinely not want to tell her and worry her. There's nothing wrong with that, but at the same time, you might overlook that your concealment may make her more worried and anxious. It's clear that your mother also relies on you emotionally, which is why she expresses her concerns through tears. Therefore, you need to find a way to make her understand the difficulties and problems you are facing in your growth. Even if she may not be able to help you, sharing with each other is a relatively safe way to release emotions and reduce unnecessary misunderstandings between you. Together, you can face potential difficulties and create a virtuous cycle.

Thirdly, become better. Life is like a rushing river, occasionally changing its course but never turning back. Draw a small end to the unhappiness of the past and make yourself better from a new starting point. Let both yourself and your mother have a present and future where you can smile again. Don't dwell on self-doubt. As intelligent as you are, I'm sure you have your own direction in mind. Keep going! Wishing you the best.

【Loving oneself is the greatest way to repay parents】I feel heartbroken to hear that you are contemplating suicide. There must be something that has made you feel so frustrated and hopeless. At the same time, I can see that you love your mother very much, even excessively. Why do I say that? Let's take a look together. 【Firstly】, you have mentioned your mother multiple times. "I used to care a lot about my mother's health and safety on the road. I was afraid that something might happen to her, and I didn't know what to do if it did. I also wanted her to be happy because I knew she had a difficult life, so I wanted to earn money to repay her. But after I experienced heartbreak and other things, I became indifferent to her tears. I just felt annoyed and didn't want to cause her any trouble. I just wanted to die, hoping that she could live well. I stopped caring whether she was suffering or not. Basically, I stopped caring about her." Two-thirds of your words are about your mother, how you understand her, and how you don't want to burden her. It is evident that you prioritize your mother's feelings over your own and dedicate yourself to her. This reflects a people-pleasing personality. 【Secondly】, your heartbreak was a turning point for you. Why do I say that? It is because, as a habit, you always give psychological strength to your mother first. When it came to your own heartbreak, your psychological strength was actually lower than usual. The first layer of relationship is the relationship with oneself, which means you should love yourself first. But you have reversed the order, prioritizing external feelings over yourself. This is undoubtedly an unhealthy arrangement. However, it was this heartbreak that made you redirect your focus onto yourself and prioritize self-care. 【Thirdly】, following traditional filial piety has made you feel unfilial. We have all grown up under traditional Chinese education, and "filial piety" is undoubtedly the most difficult thing to grasp. Because our parents are our elders, once they accuse us of being "unfilial," we feel a strong sense of guilt and shame. To avoid carrying the label of "unfilial," we often try to meet our parents' unreasonable expectations, and sometimes even assume the role of being the parent. However, this approach brings more harm than good. 【Fourthly】, the consequences of misplacing the order between parents and oneself. By taking over the responsibilities of parents and doing things that we should not do for ourselves, such as being responsible for our mother's personal safety, we neglect our own personal safety. According to this erroneous order, you will become someone who is not responsible for yourself. 【Fifthly】, how to achieve "neutral filial piety"? 1. This can also be understood as "being filial but not submissive." In other words, we only need to respect and acknowledge our parents. Because a part of who we are comes from them, denying them is equivalent to denying ourselves. Parents came to this family before we did, so we should respect them, their limitations, and their fate. We should not meddle unnecessarily. "Parents are our pride, and we are their achievements." 2. Be grateful to your parents and appreciate the life they have given you. Their love and care is already sufficient. Deeply appreciate it! The rest, we can handle ourselves. 3. We don't need to please our parents or necessarily like them. Some parents indeed do not know how to respect or love their children because they themselves have never been respected or loved. These parents may be irresponsible or disrespectful towards their children. In such cases, we don't need to like them or please them. Parents are not always right, so we can disagree when they are wrong. 4. Become your own source of light and let it radiate to others, illuminating them. You should love yourself first, and then others. Fill yourself with psychological energy and then give love within your capacity. Love yourself well. Self-love is not selfish; it is an expression of responsibility towards oneself. Being irresponsible to oneself and pushing responsibility onto others is what selfishness entails. Wishing you the best, namaste!

Hello, I think you just sometimes have intense emotions. In the past, we were closest to our mother, so naturally we would care about her every move. Now that we're older, especially after falling in love, our attention shifts from one person to another. After a heartbreak, we have many emotions that we can't process on our own. It's difficult to take care of our mother's emotions when we can't even take care of ourselves properly, after all, everyone's energy is limited. From your question, I can see that you feel guilty, but in reality, you just don't have enough energy to care about your mother. Just trust that your mother will take care of herself, after all, she was fine before you came into this world. Right now, what you need the most is to take care of yourself and handle the separation from your girlfriend. Best wishes!

The OP may be affected by a series of negative events recently, such as a breakup, which has affected their mood and made them feel down, even finding it difficult to control their emotions. This is a normal reaction when facing adversity and it takes time to slowly recover. However, if the OP has been in this state for several months, to the point where it is affecting their daily life, it is recommended to seek psychological counseling to help them recover. It seems that the OP had a close relationship with their mother, perhaps slightly beyond the normal boundaries. I also care about my mother, but I still have confidence in her. Based on her daily mental and physical condition, I don't need to worry about her all the time or have the fear that something might happen to her. Could the OP be overly anxious? While your mother is important, you also need to have your own life, and your own life is more important. You can't revolve everything around your mother. Your mother raised you to experience the beauty of the world as an independent individual. She can only accompany you for a short distance, and the rest of your life is for you to experience on your own. Perhaps when facing some challenges, you feel your own vulnerability and think that you don't have the ability to take care of your mother as much anymore. This is also very normal. In a crisis, it is important to take care of yourself first. Besides, your mother is not a baby anymore and doesn't need your 24-hour care. So, focus on yourself now, take good care of yourself, improve your mood. You are not being selfish, you are just tired and a bit hurt. You need to love yourself and let yourself recover. Consider yourself more, do things you like, talk to good friends, and distract yourself. If you are really struggling, don't forget to seek help in a timely manner.

From your words, I can sense your confusion because it seems like there have been some changes in you. You used to care a lot about your mother, but now you don't feel much towards her. However, you seem to be confused about these changes and want some confirmation, such as whether you're "sick or selfish." Maybe you really want to find a relationship or position to be with your mother. Before, you always cared about her and worried about her safety. It seems like you didn't know how to face your life without her, so at that moment, you couldn't allow her to leave. But when you experienced a heartbreak, the relationship between you and your mother started to change. You no longer cared as much about her, and you hoped to leave her by fantasizing about your own departure. Separation from parents is a topic that everyone encounters in their lives. This topic is so heavy, complicated, entangled, and ever-changing. However, it is a topic that we must face in order to grow and become independent. I think you are troubled by it too. You know what you're doing, but it's difficult to control your emotions at that moment. The outburst of emotions may bring guilt or feelings of being self-centered, so you may doubt whether you are "sick or selfish." Perhaps you are already capable of being who you need to be and don't need anyone else to tell you what to do. Stay in those feelings, immerse yourself, sort them out, and you will find your answers. This is the beginning of independence and separation from parents.

Hello, based on your description, it seems that you no longer want to bear the burden of your mother's heavy love, is that right? I wonder how old you are now? I can tell that you love your mother very much, and I assume that she has done a lot for you. In the past, you used to worry about your mother and wanted to earn money to repay her. But later on, you didn't want to let your mother know about your troubles. On one hand, you hoped to have your own privacy space, and on the other hand, you didn't want to burden your mother – that is, what you called not thinking about whether your mother is suffering, feeling "selfish." In fact, it is because you want to start separating from your mother. You don't need to depend on each other anymore, but rather be two independent minds, souls, and lives. Is there such a possibility? Separation always makes people suffer. Finally, you mentioned that you feel difficult to control your emotions. Is it "difficult to control" or "don't want to control"? Under your emotional state, could it be that you desire some things deep inside? If necessary, I recommend seeking help from a counselor on the platform! Best wishes~.

Dear, is it because of a lot of unresolved emotional stress that you're feeling? Maybe what we really need is more love and care. Perhaps start by taking care of yourself, so that you can better take care of others. The fact that you're able to talk about it means you're already on the path to finding a solution. It might take some time, but it's okay, take it slow and steady. Believe that you will eventually find ways to improve. Keep it up.

question: It's about to have mid-term exams, and I keep arguing with my mom. She speaks really offensive words. I can't take it anymore.
description: There are only 15 days left until the high school entrance examination. She keeps bothering me and used to talk about suicide. Other people say I'm making a big deal out of nothing and that I'm just pretending. I seriously can't go on anymore. I always feel suffocated. I feel like I'm perfectly fine and not sick, but everyone says I have depression. What should I do?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello, with only fifteen days left until the final exam, this period of time before the exam is probably the most difficult to endure. However, each day passes one by one, so if you make the most of each day, half a month will quickly go by. During this time, you may be under a lot of pressure, and I think your mother may also be under a significant amount of pressure. She will worry about you, but unfortunately, she cannot study for you. The only thing she can do is to add pressure to you. This is her way of expressing her own anxiety. So, no matter what she says, you don't need to take it too seriously or let it get to you. There's no need to argue with her either. When we argue, the things we say are often irrational and it doesn't solve any problems, but rather hurts each other. Other people cannot know what we truly think inside, and it's normal for them to not understand. We also don't need everyone's approval. Walk your own path and let others say what they want. If someone says you have depression, I don't know what basis their judgment is on. If you have some symptoms related to depression, you can consider seeing a psychologist. As the exam is coming up and there is a lot of mental pressure, it's actually helpful to talk to a psychologist or counselor. By expressing your thoughts and feelings, you will feel more relaxed. If your school has a counselor, you can also talk to them. Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

I really understand and sympathize with the situation and feelings of the OP. In a way, isn't this also a kind of experience for the OP? The child from a poor family becomes mature early, and an imperfect parent can actually help a child become more mature and independent at an early age. If the OP wants to change the current situation, they can only start from themselves, let go of their fantasies about their mother. Many conflicts might arise because our expectations are too high. Accepting her is just like that. Then naturally, you will focus on yourself.

question: At the age of 14, would cutting your wrist be very painful? How long would it take to die? Where is the major artery located?
description: Hello, I am a 14-year-old girl. I have been thinking of dying for two years now, and today I have made the decision to commit suicide. Just now, at 16:00, I went downstairs to the pharmacy to buy sleeping pills, but the doctor said I need a prescription from the hospital, and they don't have them here. So I have decided to cut my wrists. Actually, jumping off a building would be the best method since it is quick, but I remembered that my grandmother had jumped off our house before to commit suicide, so I gave up on that. I have already looked up a lot of suicide methods before, and online it says that cutting your wrists and soaking them in warm water won't be too painful. As for the timing, I need to check again. I still hope that kind-hearted people can tell me the exact location of the major artery. Thank you. I plan to commit suicide at 18:00 today. Please don't try to console me if you are reading this. I don't know why, but whenever I see or hear comforting words, I feel even worse and guilty. It makes me feel very uncomfortable. Of course, I would also like to talk to someone who understands the same feelings as me. If possible, could we die together for love? [laughs]

answers.answer_text: Before responding to the original poster's question, countless thoughts flashed through my mind, and I couldn't decide which one to use. After thinking about it, I decided to share a little story with the original poster first. A few days ago, while taking a shower, the bathroom heater fell off from where it was hanging and broke the toilet bowl underneath (it's hard to believe that ceramic could break plastic like that). Although I could have glued it back together, the bond wouldn't be tight and it would easily leak water. So, I took a hammer and smashed the toilet bowl. Before smashing it, I didn't realize how sharp the ceramic pieces were, and they cut my hand in several places. A lot of blood flowed out, and it didn't hurt much at the time. But after washing my hands and a few seconds passed, it started to hurt. So, I quickly put on gloves to prevent further cuts. Even a small cut on the skin hurts, let alone an artery. The pain is much stronger, to the point where it's unbearable. Watching the blood flow out of my own body and feeling life slipping away while being helpless is a terrifying and painful experience. It's definitely not something fun to go through. As for how long it would take to die, I don't know, since I've never tried. I'm afraid of pain and didn't dare to attempt it. As for where the major arteries are, I can only say they are in the body. However, the original poster is a 14-year-old girl, and I believe she is someone who values cleanliness and beauty. If she were to cut herself, not only would her body become covered in blood and dirty, but it would also attract flies and ants due to the smell of blood. At that point, it would be difficult to even move a finger, let alone try to kill these flies and ants. One would just have to watch them crawl all over their body. Very few people would be willing to endure such a feeling. I'm curious about what made the original poster have such thoughts and only decided to act on them two years later. What happened during those two years that brought such a significant stimulation to the original poster's inner self, to the point where she can no longer bear such pressure and wants to give up her desire for a better life? Whatever thoughts and emotions one has, if they are kept suppressed inside oneself, others won't be able to see or hear them. After all, no one has the "superpower" to directly see into someone else's inner world. Only by expressing these thoughts and emotions in a reasonable and appropriate manner can they be known and understood by others, and only then can they be accepted and recognized. Others will understand what the original poster wants, and then consider whether they can provide the corresponding satisfaction. In other words, if the original poster wants to obtain the desired satisfaction from others, she must let others know what she needs. The clearer and more detailed these needs are expressed, the easier it will be for others to understand, accept, and then possibly provide the desired satisfaction. However, all of these satisfactions can't be achieved through suicide. If one kills their own body, they will lose everything they can let go or can't let go of, including their hopes. There won't be any liberation. If one wants to escape from pain, they need to understand how their pain is generated, stay away from people and things that cause them pain, do things they want to do and can do, and give themselves some satisfaction, which can bring them a lot of happiness. For example, if one wants to sing, they can sing outside of class as long as it doesn't affect others. If one wants to dance, they can also dance outside of class. These are things that one can freely decide and are within their own abilities.

question: Should I tell the original partner after discovering I have been cheated on for a year?
description: We were together for a year, and when I got to know him, I confirmed multiple times that he didn't have a girlfriend before getting close to him. We had a lot of contact, and there was no way to tell that he was married, because they lived in different places and didn't communicate much on a daily basis, nor did they meet frequently, making it difficult to find out. This month, he suddenly became distant, initially breaking up with me for other reasons, but in the end, he admitted that he had already gotten married before we met. This month, he is preparing for a wedding banquet because his wife unexpectedly became pregnant three months ago, which prompted him to decide to hold the banquet. Should I tell his wife?

answers.answer_text: Hello, thank you for your trust. From your description, I can see that you have experienced a year of romantic relationship and eventually discovered that there was a third party involved, which is really infuriating! At the same time, you also want to take a stance of "unawareness" for yourself, right? So, is it based on this consideration that you want to inform his fiancé, or do you have other considerations as well? Whatever you do, as long as it is not impulsive and you also consider the consequences of your actions, it is okay. There is one principle that needs to be valued, which is to protect yourself and avoid further harm.

What is the purpose of telling his wife what kind of person you are? First, you need to be clear about it. Is it to let his wife know of your existence and make her leave him so that you can be together? Or is it to tell his wife that he cheated on her with you and confront them both together? Or perhaps to tell his wife that their relationship is broken and then break up with him as well? There may be more possibilities. I haven't sensed what your emotions are like.

question: How to overcome psychological imbalance when one tends to compare themselves with others unconsciously?
description: Will people feel jealous and resentful when their friends, who used to look similar to themselves, become more beautiful through plastic surgery? I also compare myself with colleagues from time to time and feel jealous. Even with my own sister, I feel the same way. I feel extremely inferior, leading to excessive vanity. I feel uncomfortable whenever I think someone is better than me. How can I overcome this mindset?

answers.answer_text: Based on the description provided by the questioner, whether it's feeling jealous when a friend becomes more beautiful or feeling upset when someone doesn't attend their wedding, these feelings of psychological imbalance stem from "unconscious comparison with others." Social psychologist Festinger proposed a theory called "social comparison theory," which suggests that people often use comparisons with others to understand and evaluate themselves. Furthermore, this comparison is an unconscious and spontaneous process that occurs automatically when we are exposed to information about others. Comparing oneself to someone who is better off is called upward social comparison, such as comparing wealth with someone like Wang Sicong. Comparing oneself to someone less fortunate is called downward social comparison, such as comparing height with someone like Guo Xingming. The saying goes, "There is always someone better than you, but also someone better than them." Downward social comparison can enhance positive emotions and self-esteem, while upward social comparison can lower self-evaluation and self-esteem. Social comparison is a universal psychological phenomenon that we have all experienced. Taking a quote from the movie "Ex-Files 2" and modifying it a bit: "We live to compare. Women compare beauty, men compare wealth. Love is sweeter, marriage is destiny. By comparing, we seek to determine who wins and loses. Winners gain a sense of security, while losers lose confidence. We use emotions to bring people closer, but use comparison to create distance." Unfortunately, the questioner has been engaged in upward social comparison, resulting in a lower level of self-esteem. At the same time, their degree of social comparison exceeds that of the average person. Why do you always compare yourself to others? 1. You feel unable to control yourself or your life. In our lives, there are times when we lose control of what is happening. Life is full of unexpected challenges and events, and when you experience these, you naturally feel unsettled. When your sense of security is threatened, you may excessively focus on others and what they do or don't have. You use "comparison" to deepen your sense of security and control. 2. You lack self-awareness. A child who has never been treated honestly and deeply by their parents will not learn to see themselves honestly and deeply. Many children are emotionally neglected by their parents from an early age, and their emotional needs receive little attention and recognition. To attract their parents' attention, they gradually hide their true selves and try to conform to others' expectations. Growing up in this lack of self-awareness makes it easier to compare oneself to others and to determine one's own worth. 3. You have low self-worth. Low self-worth may drive you to seek out people who make you feel superior, but in reality, it may be the opposite. You may find and gravitate towards people who seem better off than you because there will always be someone better than you. The self-esteem built through social comparison is unstable. You engage in social comparison because of your low self-worth, and this social comparison, in turn, deepens your sense of low self-worth. 4. In your upbringing, you were often compared to your siblings. Some parents are not aware that comparing their children to each other is harmful. Some parents intentionally do this because they believe it will motivate the children. If you grew up in a family that focused on comparisons, you learned this pattern and continue to repeat it with the people around you as an adult. How can you stop excessively comparing yourself to others? 1. Increase your awareness of comparison. To change this deeply ingrained habit, you need to increase your awareness. You may have been comparing yourself without even realizing it. To change this, you first need to become aware of it. So, whenever you catch yourself starting to compare, you need to be vigilant and mindful. When you have increased awareness, stop the comparison before it fully takes hold. For example, when you notice yourself starting to compare, visualize a prominent red stop sign in your mind and silently say "stop," or find another method that works for you. 2. Focus on your true inner self. Take some time to reflect, or seek the help of a psychologist, to help you sort through these questions: What do you want? What do you like? What do you not like or need? As an independent individual, what are your true strengths and weaknesses? What kind of person do you want to become? 3. Remember that everyone is a complete but imperfect person. Everyone is multi-faceted, and just like everyone else in this world, you have major strengths and minor weaknesses, small talents and major flaws. Only when you see, know, and accept everything about yourself, good and bad, beautiful and ugly, and add them all up, will you discover something amazing. When you no longer focus on individual aspects of yourself and instead pull back your attention to see the bigger picture, you will see how all the pieces of your personality fit together. You will realize that you are a complete person, even if not perfect, but that's who you are. What's important is that when you integrate all these parts and see the complete picture, you may find that you are already good enough. Lastly, the meditation planet also has a meditation exercise for dealing with jealousy. You can try it out.------------ Meditation Planet App, a one-stop meditation personal coach that effectively helps with sleep, stress reduction, relaxation, and focus.

question: My girlfriend has become disillusioned and no longer wants me. How can I win her back?
description: I have been with my girlfriend for three years. There weren't many problems in the first two years, but in the last year, I became a bit selfish and didn't consider my girlfriend's feelings. I even acted cold and controlling towards her, displaying male chauvinism. Now she is feeling disheartened and distant from me. I want to change, but she is not giving me a chance.
keywords: Love, heartbreak, and winning back a former partner.

answers.answer_text: Hello, ~~ give the OP a warm hug~ From the OP's description, it can be seen that the OP still can't let go and hopes to rekindle this relationship, which means that you still have feelings for your girlfriend. Here, I would like to offer you some advice in the hope that it will be helpful to you. 1. Self-reflection #You have been together with your girlfriend for three years, and there weren't many problems in the first two years, but you became a bit selfish in the third year#. The OP may want to reflect on why you became somewhat selfish in the third year together. Is it because of increased work pressure or something that caused you to lose patience with life and accumulate negative energy that couldn't be resolved, ultimately leading to your selfishness? There are many reasons that have led to your change in character. If you want to win back your girlfriend, you can only find the reasons that have influenced you in this aspect, solve the problems, and learn to adjust your emotions reasonably, so that you can change the "selfish" side of you and become the person your girlfriend likes again. 2. Self-change It can be seen that after the separation, the OP has reflected on oneself in order to discover their own mistakes. Failing to consider the feelings of your girlfriend, being emotionally abusive, and having a patriarchal attitude, the OP has summarized the above shortcomings. But have you thought about how to change? The bottom line when forgiving someone is not making them realize where they went wrong and what mistakes they made, because these things are not helpful, right? What we care about is that you know you made a mistake, know how to change, and how you can make amends in the future. These are what we want. Before asking for reconciliation, the OP may want to think about how to change their shortcomings and how to make your former girlfriend believe that you can start over and make changes. Or, when your girlfriend sees you next time, she can feel the changes you have made through your behavior. 3. Correct your mindset and do your best The opportunity is for those who are prepared. If the OP still can't let go of the past, then you should work hard to change yourself and gain the chance of reconciliation. If in the end, you can't go back to the past, at least you have gotten rid of bad habits and gained a better version of yourself. In relationships, there are never absolutes, and often, doing your best is enough. Good luck!

You can describe her current state towards you as being disheartened and indifferent, which implies that your relationship has become very cold. I won't lecture you with clichés, as I assume you're no longer a child and should understand the advice that is typically given. You should be well aware that it is impossible for a cup of water with a certain temperature to suddenly drop below freezing in a very short period of time. If this is true for actual water, then it is even more true for a relationship. Three years may not be considered long, but it is also not short. I believe there are certainly beautiful moments worth reminiscing about, but I don't mean to discourage you when I say that it will be difficult for you to restore this relationship. I think, before she became disheartened and indifferent, with your three-year relationship, she wouldn't have just given up without giving you any chance at all. When there were issues in this relationship (especially as you mentioned in the past year), I believe she must have talked to you about these problems and asked you to improve, but you carelessly let them slip away. In other words, you ended up losing this relationship yourself and completely shattered her kind heart. How can you expect someone who has lost all hope in you to believe that you can change for the better? She would rather believe that her choice was wrong than turn back. This is how relationships work. When you have them, you think you can have them or not have them in your heart, but when you truly realize that you like someone, it is their absence that makes you acutely aware of the value of that relationship. Unfortunately, everything is too late. Just like water that has turned cold, it can be reheated to the desired temperature, but overnight water will always have a different taste. When a relationship cools down, it doesn't mean it's absolutely irreparable, but it is indeed quite difficult. Even if you manage to salvage it, you may never feel the same as before. Consider it a life experience. If you can salvage the relationship, of course, that would be the best outcome. But if you can't, after grieving, you must wipe away your tears. Perhaps you will become more mature in the process.

Give the OP a virtual hug. When it comes to getting along with the opposite sex, there are often environmental factors, compatibility in personality, and the ability to communicate effectively when facing problems. Love is ultimately a symbol of compatibility, which is influenced by many factors, such as the environment, personality, and abilities mentioned earlier. I believe that both of you were deeply in love at one point, but because of the way you communicated during times of trouble, it caused repeated hurt. As the hurt accumulated without any other positive factors to mend the wounded hearts, the compatibility of love inevitably decreases and may even disappear. I believe you are feeling regretful at this moment, regretful for missing out on so much before realizing it. You want to salvage the relationship, but you are also anxious about whether you will be able to handle love well if you reconcile. Therefore, as the male figure in the relationship, I hope you can truly rationalize the situation, analyze which aspects have low compatibility between both of you, and whether both parties are willing and able to eliminate the barriers. After you have thought it through, have a conversation again. If you make it through this time, then the next time you encounter problems, you will be able to recover. However, if you cannot reconcile, part ways peacefully and take care of yourselves.

Hello, dear asker! It's great that you are able to recognize your shortcomings. It is often said that men and women think differently, with men being more rational and women more emotional. Based on this, it is generally easier to win back a girl than a boy. You mentioned that the girl is unwilling to give you a chance; may I ask how long it has been since you broke up? Personally, I believe that after a breakup, it is important to give the other person some time to forget the negative feelings and remember the good things about you. This is where the tried and true method of "no contact" comes in. Of course, the duration of "no contact" should be determined based on your understanding of your girlfriend's personality. When you feel that she is no longer as angry or sad, try to reach out and communicate with her. Share your thoughts and try to console her. During this time, it is essential to genuinely address your shortcomings, especially any form of emotional abuse, as it is the most hurtful. Show her your changes and care for her. If you truly love her, be willing to give it another shot. The success of winning her back largely depends on your mentality. The following words may be a bit discouraging, but I still want to suggest that if you have made efforts and find no hope of reconciliation, it may be better to let go. The more you invest in something, the harder it is to let go, and it may become about proving yourself rather than the girl. This might also lead to a breakdown in the quality of your relationship once you win her back. Therefore, think carefully about whether you can handle giving without getting a response. In a relationship, most girls just want to see your love in the little things, your willingness to strive for a better future together, and above all, your attitude. A three-year relationship is already quite good in today's fast-paced dating scene, so I hope you can win back your beloved girl. Good luck!

question: Not fond of men, but still want to get close, always feel like they have ulterior motives?
description: There is a inexplicable aggression towards men, always feeling that they have ulterior motives, either to get close to me or they must have something going on. I just don't believe in friendship, so I either dislike them or want to avoid them. I don't want to connect or be friends. It's like a sense of insecurity. But with women, it's natural for me to just think that they want to be friends. They are very friendly and not guarded.
keywords: Romance, dependence, attachment, relationship management, affection.

answers.answer_text: Not liking men but wanting to get close, always feeling that they have ulterior motives? First of all, I understand and sympathize with your situation, and I want to give you a hug to let you feel the warmth of the world. How can I put it? It seems like you have a sort of androphobia, but in reality, you are curious about and fantasize about the opposite sex, but at the same time, you are afraid to get close to them, thinking that their intentions are impure. However, most of the time, these are just our own fantasies. Our clients self-label, and our preconceptions box us into a certain cognitive framework, so you need to break free from this way of thinking and try to accept and see pure friendship between men and women. Because if you develop an avoidant personality mechanism, it is detrimental to your physical and mental well-being. The feeling of unease stems from your lack of confidence in yourself. You feel that you cannot mix well with boys and that you cannot handle them, which is a kind of insecure behavior. Of course, there are girls in reality who disdain playing with boys, but they are a minority, because most of them are curious and expectant about boys. So, my suggestion is that you might as well open your heart and try to make friends with one or two male friends, and naturally interact with them generously. You don't have to assume that he has a motive or whether he wants to say something to you. In fact, most of the time, the conversations between males and females are not because they want to do something. It's just the mutual attraction between sexes. I now feel that the problem with you, the OP, is just that you are not relaxed, you are very nervous, and you dare not relax and interact with the opposite sex. So, if you want to break this feeling, you need to overcome it yourself and take the first step. You might as well ask your female friends who get along well with boys, how they feel. Maybe it's not as terrifying as you imagine. Everything is just your perception; you have not personally taken the initiative to understand.

Friendship with the opposite sex is quite delicate, and it's difficult to control the boundaries. If the relationship becomes too intimate, it's inevitable to consider going beyond friendship. If it's not intimate enough, it's just like having an acquaintance relationship, such as with a male colleague. It doesn't trigger any ripples in your heart, and there's no need to stay in contact frequently. There's no need to harbor any hostility, just treat them as ordinary people. What you need to be mindful of is the significant other you will eventually live with, there's no need to think too much about other men. I don't have many opposite-sex friends either, but I don't hold any hostility towards them. Just maintain a distance. In short, simply don't care about them. The questioner can also adopt this attitude, focusing on matters at hand, withdrawing when there's nothing to talk about. There's no need to have too much interaction, if you don't want to get close, then just stay away. Why must you force yourself to like men or make friends with them? Isn't a girlfriend enough? It's easy for accidents to happen with opposite-sex friends, so it's good to be cautious. So, relax your mindset now, it's not abnormal to not make friends with the opposite sex, having friends is enough. It's also possible that you haven't met the right guy for you, maybe one day you will suddenly find a guy who is very compatible with you and knowledgeable, and then you can be friends with that kind of person.

Hello dear. You said that you dislike men but want to be close to them. This actually shows that your consciousness does not like men, meaning that your rational level does not like men, but subconsciously you want to be close to them. This subconscious desire to be close is likely based on physiological mechanisms or a deep level of psychological judgment. This deep level of psychological judgment, namely subconscious judgment, believes that your rational consciousness judgment is incorrect. However, because you are not aware of it, you find yourself in a state of disliking men but wanting to be close to them. The aggression towards men may stem from life experiences. It's possible that in past experiences, men purposefully approached you. These experiences you may have forgotten, but your subconscious has not. What you have forgotten is only at the conscious level. In these experiences, some men may have hurt you, causing you to feel insecure. This may have led you to seek a sense of security and be precautious. Seeking security is a non-rational belief of the female seeking safety. Your beliefs include absolutes, such as female friends only wanting to be friends, having a sense of security, and no need for defense. But are all women really just interested in being friends? Are all women truly friendly and without the need for defense? Obviously, this is not true. Absolute judgments often come with incorrect biases. In life, you need to retrace your life experiences and find what caused your biases and approach them with rationality. Acknowledge that you hold a dislike for men based on past experiences and accept that you dislike those few men from your past experiences. However, we cannot condemn all men based on those few experiences. Follow our subconsciousness and make an effort to discern the men you encounter in the future.

question: Recently, I have been growing to dislike my mother more and more. I feel annoyed by her and feel both angry and helpless. What should I do?
description: I feel like my mom is really hypocritical. If I forget to do something, like forgetting to clean the pot, she will constantly nag at me, saying I'm useless. She doesn't do anything herself but doesn't allow others to criticize her. Every day, she makes me clean her dirty shoes, and if I refuse, she calls me lazy. It's really annoying, and I feel like I'm becoming more and more impatient when talking to her. Sometimes I even want to run away from home. She talks bad about others every day and jokes with the neighbors about things I have never said. Sigh, I'm both angry and helpless, so frustrated. What should I do?!

answers.answer_text: Hello, hope I can help you, OP: (1) First of all, some nagging and urging from mothers stem from their concern and love for their children, fearing that OP might not do well in the future and take care of themselves properly. However, it could also come from the way your grandmother treated you when you were little, so that's why OP's mother treats OP like this. (2) Furthermore, OP can think about whether their mother really doesn't do anything, or if it's the result of OP's mother being constantly spoiled by their grandmother and father? (3) Lastly, it is suggested that OP first understand the reasons behind their mother's behavior and then choose to have a calm conversation with her, such as doing household chores together, or seeking support from their father. Running away from home is not a good solution, oh! #The world and I love you, wishing you the best~.

question: The days are going okay, suddenly feeling very empty, what should I do?
description: I'm not lacking money, and life is still okay. My girlfriend treats me well. I also have plans for the future. But for some reason, I still feel very hollow and lonely. Whenever it's late at night and everything is quiet, this feeling comes over me...
keywords: Growth, self-growth, self-acceptance, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. You mentioned this feeling of emptiness and loneliness, which I had a few years ago. I should say that I study psychology, which has allowed my inner self to grow and understand many truths. It has enabled me to better experience life. Actually, the things I faced did not change much, but my state of mind did. In 2013, when I learned that I could be admitted to Zhejiang University to pursue a PhD, I also found out that I was pregnant. Since I was studying engineering, the PhD program required a lot of experiments. My advisor said, if you're pregnant, you can either choose to have the child first and pursue the PhD later, or you can choose to pursue the PhD now but not have the child. I promptly chose to have the child, thinking that I would give birth and then pursue the PhD. Later, the child was born, but things didn't happen as I had imagined. Although I took care of the child and continued preparing for the PhD exams, I also persisted in taking the exams for two years. However, my life quietly changed. My husband was very capable at work and able to provide for our family financially. Due to this situation, he rarely took care of the household and the child, and he hoped that I would focus on taking care of the child and the family at home, while he could focus on his career outside. Although he supported my pursuit of a PhD, he couldn't be there with me to raise the child; he could only offer financial support. During that time, others saw me as very happy—no need to work, no need to worry about money, just take care of the child and enjoy freedom. But deep inside, I felt extremely bored and empty. I lost direction in life because pursuing a PhD seemed like an impossible goal, a distant dream—I couldn't abandon my child's company and education for the sake of a PhD. But is there a way to have the best of both worlds? I have always been seeking, trying to find a balance. The reason I wanted to pursue a PhD was to teach at a university in the future, but I actually didn't like my original field of study because it involved experiments. If I pursued a PhD, I would have to enter the lab again and conduct a lot of experiments, which didn't attract me much. In 2017, I came into contact with psychology and obtained a certificate as a second-level psychological counselor. Later, I studied child education and developmental psychology in the doctoral program at the Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Through continuous learning, I finally found the direction of my life again. My passion for psychology drove me to learn various aspects of the field. During my study of psychology, I have always been highly motivated because I am genuinely interested, and interest is the best teacher. Now, I do online counseling and participate in local psychological education events. I also believe that in the future, I will definitely stand on the university stage, spreading knowledge of psychology and still fulfilling my dream. What I want to say to you, OP, is that we need to find something we love, which will make us feel that life is meaningful. Additionally, in the ordinary life, we should appreciate the extraordinariness of each day, set small goals for ourselves, and strive to achieve them. You will discover that you can do many things and that your life can be rich and colorful. Let's encourage each other.

Today I heard a story and want to share it with you. There was a person who had a very successful business and earned a lot of money. However, even after achieving success and fame, he still wasn't happy. He always thought that he wanted to have his own career. Eventually, he did have a career and he thought that he wanted to have a lot of money. And he did have a lot of money. But in the end, he still felt unhappy and empty. He didn't know what he needed.
