One day, he finally understood that what he truly desired was a sense of recognition and value. He wanted to feel useful and help others. So, he started doing charity work. However, he still felt empty inside, so he continued to search for answers. One day, he found a teacher who helped him understand himself. With the guidance of the teacher, he finally realized that all along, he had been trying to prove his worth to others and that it didn't matter. When he was able to affirm his own value, acknowledge his strengths and weaknesses, and accept his true existence, he finally found the answer. He discovered that it is only when a person affirms themselves that they are truly valuable. While seeking affirmation and praise from others may bring temporary joy, it fades away and leaves him feeling empty again. I don't know if you have had similar experiences or faced similar challenges as this person and his teacher, but try to find out the root cause of your emptiness. Each person knows themselves best, so the answer lies within you. Maybe you are afraid to reveal it or maybe you don't know how to reveal it yet, but as long as you keep searching for the answer, one day it will become clear. Reading books about psychology might be helpful to you. I hope my answer is helpful to you, and remember that I and the world love you.

Hello, congratulations on having a pretty good life. Living without worries, smooth work, and happy family, this is something that many people cannot attain. You're feeling empty right now, maybe because you have a lot of free time and aren't busy with things you like. So you feel empty. I suggest: 1. Learn some new skills, such as calligraphy, painting, baking, etc., to acquire new knowledge and increase the joy in life. At the same time, you can also meet new friends and expand your social circle. 2. Use your free time to do some volunteer work, such as helping at welfare homes or social care homes, to help those in need and create value in your life. Giving to others is always more gratifying than receiving, and it can increase your happiness index. 3. If you like animals, you can adopt a small pet and play with it during your free time to increase your joy in life. Finally, I hope you have eternal happiness.

It is impossible for life to always be fulfilling, it is okay to feel empty. The emptiness that the asker is experiencing is what many people want but cannot obtain. Most ordinary people are busy working hard to survive or seeking a long-term partner. The sweet troubles that the asker is experiencing are also what many people want. If the asker wants to have everything, a successful career, no money worries, and a loving partner, and still feel full and fulfilled every day without emptiness, is that asking for too much? I know many celebrities, after making a lot of money, use charity work to realize their own value. The asker can try to help the people around them and do good deeds daily, maybe they will live a more open life and reduce the feeling of emptiness.

question: I have a girl at home, she is 7 years old. Why has she been disobedient all the time in the last month?
description: I have a daughter who is 7 years old. Recently, I don't know what's going on, but ever since summer vacation, it seems like my child has become unruly. She doesn't listen no matter what I say, and she confronts me. I've tried everything from threatening and tempting her to saying both good and bad things, but nothing has worked. What should I do?
keywords: Family, family relationships, communication between parents and children.

answers.answer_text: Hello, seeing your words, I can feel that you are a mother who cares a lot about her daughter and loves her very much. Your child is seven years old now and is already in elementary school. At this age, girls have a lot of small ideas. Since the summer vacation, your child has been rebellious and seems to have her own opinions. As parents, how can we open the door for communication and ease the relationship when our child is disobedient? We can try the following thoughts to see if we can find the answers within ourselves. 1. Release your anxiety and emotional stress and calm yourself so that you can better accompany your child. As parents, we are our child's first teachers. When we face difficulties, we don't know what to do, so the child becomes even more unsure. Therefore, release your own stress first and face the present calmly. 2. Understand your child's physical and mental needs and let her express herself. Let the child speak up because she must have thoughts. Take the time to ask the child how she feels about her recent experiences, her mood, and how she is adapting to school. Let the child express her own state. Perhaps her current state is an expectation to attract the attention of her parents, and she needs us adults to slow down and listen. 3. Squat down and face the child together, growing together. The parent-child relationship is more important than the method of education. Our original intention in raising our children is to hope that they grow up healthy and happy, so we will definitely encounter difficulties along the way. Don't avoid or fear the difficulties, face them together with the child. Believe in the child, believe in yourself, and she will help you find the answers together.

Hello, first of all, congratulations on your child growing up and developing their own independent thoughts. As a parent, I would like to share my perspective and hope to learn together with you. 

1. Children aged 7 tend to enjoy their own alone time more. Whether it's during sports, work, or reading, they prefer to spend a longer time completing a task and often immerse themselves in their own world. At this stage, even quiet and well-behaved 7-year-olds will respond strongly if adults disturb or oppose what they are doing. They will gradually have their own opinions. Sometimes, adults' behavior can suppress their thoughts. As parents, it is important to guide and support their opinions and give encouragement. This will win the child's favor. 

2. Children's opinions should not be suppressed because it helps them learn independence. We should listen to their ideas and thoughts, which can teach them how to listen to others' opinions. As parents, we should listen more to their opinions and understand what they are thinking. Only then can we guide our children appropriately. 

3. Children aged 7 will gradually develop their own personalities, and adult guidance needs to be more carefully observed and responded to. Different strategies should be used for children with different personalities. Encourage more and criticize less for children with strong self-esteem, give more care to introverted children, and give clear rewards and punishments for extroverted children. 

4. Children will grow up gradually, and as parents, we need to constantly update our parenting concepts along with their growth. We need to learn to let go gradually and give children enough space. Only then can children grow healthily. After all, being "obedient" is not the only criterion for measuring a child's excellence. Wishing you happiness and joy.

"A few days ago, I went to school to register my sister. I asked her if she wanted to go to Sun Yat-sen University, but she didn't answer. question: I can no longer afford to keep my pet, and I regret why I got it. I feel very sad, what should I do?
description: A year ago, I got a guinea pig and I really liked it. At that time, I was very lonely in college, so having it made me feel like I wasn't depressed. Now that I have graduated, I brought it back to my hometown. I am in a difficult situation now because I have to go out of town but my family won't take care of it. I tried once to let them take care of it, but when I came back, the guinea pig was in a terrible condition. I hoped my friends could help, but they also rejected me. Now I have to go out of town and can't take it with me. I don't know what to do. Since I came back to my hometown, I have had various troubles. I thought about getting rid of it, but the thought of it dying in the wild scares me. It would be like killing it myself. I regret why I got it. Now I feel like I'm in a deep darkness. Your university life is very lonely, so you got a guinea pig as a pet to bring some joy into your life and prevent depression. But because your pet is somewhat unique, although guinea pigs are cute, your parents and friends might think it's dirty and not know how to care for it, which naturally leads them to feel some resistance towards it. I also understand your feelings of guilt and self-blame. You have taken care of it and it has accompanied you through difficult times, but now you feel trapped and believe that the only solution is to get rid of it, which makes you feel very dark. Lastly, my suggestions are: 1. Have a good conversation with your parents and friends. The reason your parents and friends are unwilling to help is very likely because they hold certain biases against your pet. I come from a rural area, and my impression of pigs is that they eat and sleep a lot, and the second impression is that they are dirty. Until a few years ago, I never thought of someone keeping it as a pet, and even now I haven't seen many people keeping it as a pet, so very few people have impressions of it and are unwilling to consider it a suitable pet. Therefore, I think you can have a good conversation with your family and friends, let them see the cute and adorable side of guinea pigs, and I believe this will simplify things. 2. Tell your parents how important it is to you. Your parents are not willing to help because one possible reason is that they find it troublesome, and another reason might be that they don't think this pet is important and not worth keeping. But you are very clear that this is not the case, so I think you can let your parents know why you want to keep this guinea pig and what it brings to you. I believe parents love their children very much and will understand you. 3. Offer some benefits. British Prime Minister Palmerston once said, "There are no permanent friends, only permanent interests." This sentence reveals a truth: people are constantly comparing and choosing, in order to obtain the most beneficial results for themselves. Therefore, I think you can offer some tempting conditions to your friends to help take care of your guinea pig. However, be cautious not to give them all the benefits at once, in case they do not take good care of your guinea pig afterwards. Although we should believe in our friends, sometimes we still need to follow the old saying "Never let down your guard against others." 4. Do your best and don't blame yourself too much. Unfortunately, one day, when I wasn't paying attention, it was hit by a car and died. Since then, I realized that every pet I keep doesn't live long: they are either poisoned, bitten by snakes, hit by a car, or get lost. I always go from being happy to being sad, so now I dare not keep any pets. I'm afraid of goodbyes, really, sometimes it's difficult to give our pets a good future. I'm glad that you still have that enthusiasm for pets and a sense of responsibility towards them. But regardless of the outcome, don't be too sad. You have already done your best. Of course, you should focus on your work. If one day you have another pet, you can give it a warm home. Finally, I wish you all the best and a happy life.

question: 33-year-old male, feels that sexual behavior is dirty and is unable to fully engage. What should he do?
description: 33-year-old male, feels that sex is dirty and cannot accept sexual behavior, always feels that engaging in sexual activity will result in disease, especially afraid of contracting AIDS, even if he wears a condom, he still worries about it breaking, how to become fully engaged in sexual behavior?

answers.answer_text: From your description, I can see someone who is troubled and anxious due to sexual issues. **From a perspective of sexual development, the "stigmatization" of sex has been prevalent throughout human history, especially in patriarchal societies. For example: ++sex is dirty, ++sexual organs are dirty, ++sexual behavior is dirty, ++anything related to sex is bad, ++menstruation is bad, ++virginity is valued, non-virgins are impure, etc. However, upon closer examination, one would realize that these are all socially constructed beliefs. If sex is dirty, then it's quite funny that procreation requires sexual activity, isn't it? If sex is dirty, then the history of human sexuality and reproductive worship is quite laughable, isn't it?** Therefore, even in the 21st century, we still have the responsibility to redefine sex: @@sex is beautiful, @@sexual organs and other parts of the human body are equal and not dirty, they should not be stigmatized just because they are located below the waist, such as the penis and vagina; this is extremely harmful. @@Menstruation is not dirty, it is a natural part of a woman's physiology. @@Purity is not determined by virginity, but by a person's thoughts and soul. @@Sexual acts done with love are beautiful, including oral sex, kissing, etc., these are all normal behaviors.** Our sexuality and love only need to be based on the five principles of "autonomy, respect, responsibility, health, and happiness". ##If you engage in sex and love based on voluntary consent, it's okay; otherwise, it's not. ##If it's based on mutual respect, it's okay; if there is no mutual respect, then there is a problem with that sexual relationship. ##Both parties need to be responsible for each other and for themselves, if not, then don't do it. ##It needs to be conducted with the principles of health and hygiene, which involves being aware of diseases. ##Sex and love should bring happiness, if there is no happiness and it goes against the wishes of the partner, then obviously there is a problem.** Your anxiety comes from both your understanding of sex and love, as well as misconceptions about condoms, AIDS, etc.** I wish you well, and for your situation, I recommend seeking counseling for psychological development and adjustment (specifically regarding sexual psychology). εI am here, the world and I love you.

Hello, OP. It seems that your situation involves an aversion and repulsion towards sex, but essentially, it is a dislike of your own sexuality. Feeling that your sexuality is dirty mainly stems from self-attack. There can be many reasons for this aggression, such as exposure to adult content during sexual education or family upbringing. You mentioned societal judgments and other factors in your environment. Saying that sex is dirty is actually saying that you are dirty, that you are not good, and that sex will ruin you. It is essentially believing that allowing yourself to be free will destroy you. From what I gather, you may also feel repressed in certain aspects of your daily life and restrict yourself. This belief has nothing to do with which person you have sex with. Even if you know it is impossible to contract a disease, you still have these concerns because they originate from within yourself. So, I ask you, are you really that bad? Are you truly such an awful person? I believe not. Sometimes, we perceive ourselves as bad people through self-attacking thoughts and end up behaving poorly. If I believe I am a bad person, I cannot display my goodness. Instead, I exhibit my perceived badness and truly become a bad person. In such situations, we need to transcend our current perceptions and adopt a more macroscopic view of ourselves. Then, we will see a truly beautiful version of ourselves. I sincerely hope that you can break free from your current situation and enjoy a fulfilling and happy sexual life.

question: 20-year-old male, he feels nauseous when he gets nervous. How can he face situations with confidence?
description: I am a student who repeated a year. When I was in my final year of high school, I experienced exam anxiety and would have slight nausea. In my final year, the pressure increased, and I would experience nausea whenever I had an exam. During the period leading up to the college entrance examination, it became more severe, to the point where even small tests would make me nauseous (drinking water would temporarily alleviate the symptoms). In college, as I participated in more activities, the habit of feeling nauseous when faced with new situations from high school continued. Now, every time I go out, I have to carry a bottle of mineral water, which has greatly affected my daily life. I really don't know how to deal with it. I would like to ask if there are any medications that can alleviate this nausea???
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, treatment methods, mental disorders.

answers.answer_text: Hello. I read your description and I can imagine how uncomfortable you feel. I can also understand your nervousness and anxiety at that time. Boldly guessing, it seems that you had high expectations for the event and hoped that your performance would be recognized by others. As a result, you were very concerned about it. The more you care, the more nervous you become, the more pressure you feel, and the more you want to escape. But you know that you can't really escape, so your body (dry heaving) helps you express your emotions - to say what you can't say. What can you do? I'm not a doctor, so I can't give advice on medication. But from a psychological perspective, let's see if there are some actions you can try: 1. Lower your expectations and participate in exams or activities with a calm mind. Occasionally showing imperfections does not mean that you are not capable or not trying hard enough. Perhaps it is an opportunity to understand yourself and improve yourself. No matter how things develop, you are always the best. Because you are strong, hardworking, and brave... 2. When you feel nervous and anxious, try relaxing more. Take deep breaths, relax your body (I often use the method of tightly clenching my fists and slowly releasing them, stretching my palms back and forth a few times). If you experience dry heaving again, don't reject it or blame yourself for this behavior. Tell yourself: "Darling, I know you have something to express, I know you are a bit anxious, I know you care about your performance. No matter what, I will face it with you." 3. Believe in yourself, you are capable of handling both emotions and situations. You see, when you have emotions, your body reacts and you can sense your nervousness and anxiety. You will think about drinking water to relieve the tension. This means you have thoughts, attempts, and actions. Can we think of other ways to relieve tension besides just this one? I believe you can come up with them, and I believe you are willing to try more. Sometimes, the body's reaction is trying to express some emotions, trying to tell us something. Strengthening the connection with our bodies is also a good way to understand ourselves. Of course, if your physical discomfort is severe, seeing a doctor is necessary.

Hello: Nervousness can cause dry heaving, which appears to be a psychosomatic illness, a physical illness caused by psychological factors. Often, we tend to see problems from only one perspective, but in fact, there are many factors that support this symptom and contribute to its stubbornness. Don't be afraid. How to gain self-confidence is a big topic that requires solving the underlying factors causing the nervousness. Analyzing and understanding the problem: 1. You are a student who repeated a year, and in your senior year of high school, you became very nervous during exams and had mild dry heaving. In your senior year, as the pressure increased, you started experiencing dry heaving whenever there was an exam. It became more severe during the period leading up to the college entrance examination, and even small quizzes would cause dry heaving (drinking water can temporarily relax you). (Exam nervousness can be categorized into several situations: a) pressure from parents' expectations; b) pressure from comparing yourself to peers; c) pressure from the exam-oriented education system, including pressure from teachers and schools, and so on. When a person is in an extremely nervous state, their physiological functions rapidly decline, and their immune system also rapidly decreases. At this time, the stress-induced energy is directed towards different organs in the body, leading to the occurrence of symptoms. Because there is a way for symptoms to occur, the next time you encounter a similar problem, it will automatically jump into this pattern. For example, "being nervous about an exam, previously experienced dry heaving, so next time it will continue to happen," and so on. The reason for experiencing dry heaving during small quizzes is a manifestation of "generalization of the problem." When drinking water, the process of water passing through the mouth, throat, and gastrointestinal tract is a way to relieve nervousness because water is gentle, and at that moment, your focus shifts to the water, allowing you to temporarily relax. This is a good method, but it only addresses the symptoms and not the root cause.) 2. In college, as you participated in more activities, the habit of getting dry heaving when faced with challenges during high school has continued. Now, whenever you participate in new activities, you experience dry heaving, which has caused you to carry a bottle of mineral water whenever you go out, severely impacting your daily life. (Yes, the problem has not been solved. Perhaps if you carefully think about it, this problem may also affect other aspects of your life. "New activities" give you a sense of stress and uncertainty, which is a feeling you are familiar with from high school. Perhaps the specific circumstances have changed, but that anxious feeling remains. Carrying mineral water is not a big deal, so you shouldn't overthink it, but my concern is whether this problem will continue to generalize to other things in the future? This is the key to the problem and the reason why you need to address the root cause.) 3. I really don't know how to deal with it now. Are there any medications that can alleviate dry heaving??? (First of all, this is a physical symptom caused by psychological factors. We need to use psychological medicine for mental illness. Secondly, as psychological counselors, we have strict ethical regulations and cannot provide medication or prescribe drugs to visitors. Personally, my advice is, if you still want to use medication for treatment, go to a proper hospital to seek advice. However, it would be best to find a suitable psychotherapist, as they are the key factor in solving this problem.) Closing remarks: I wish you happiness and joy! I hope you soon overcome the influence of this psychological issue! If you have any confusion, feel free to send a private message!

OP, hello! Thank you for inviting me to answer your question. I hope my thoughts can help you to some extent. After reading your description, I have understood your question to a certain degree, and thus, I want to give you a virtual hug. From your description, I can feel that you are under a lot of pressure, possibly due to exams or high expectations from teachers and parents. This has led you to develop a defense mechanism, which you mentioned as dry heaving. The so-called defense mechanism is used to avoid dangers, anxiety, and unpleasant feelings caused by instinctive needs. It is a function to adjust the conflict between the id and external reality. To some extent, defense mechanisms can protect us from certain harms and help us avoid painful situations. However, when defense mechanisms are excessive, they can have an impact on our physical and mental well-being. In fact, when you were in your final year of high school, you would get nervous and have dry heaving during exams. This indicates that you were under a lot of pressure, and this pressure has not been released properly, so your body has started to manifest illness in another way, which you mentioned as dry heaving. Perhaps at first, you thought it would only last for a while, but over time, every time you have an exam, you feel nervous and have dry heaving. In behaviorism, it can be explained that the presence of a stimulus (exams) leads to the development of a certain behavior (dry heaving), and this phenomenon is continuously reinforced, gradually forming this behavior. Now, this behavior has even generalized to other aspects, as you mentioned that participating in new activities also triggers dry heaving. This suggests that your current situation is quite serious, which is why you seek help on social platforms. The so-called generalization refers to when a certain response forms a conditional association with a specific stimulus, this response will also form a certain degree of conditional association with similar stimuli. Based on this, I have summarized some methods to help alleviate your current situation. (1) If conditions allow, seek professional help, such as consulting a psychologist or a doctor at a hospital, as they will use more professional methods to help you overcome the current situation. (2) Try to reduce stress because excessive stress is not conducive to physical and mental health. Therefore, it is especially important to release stress through exercise or other means. (3) Talk to close friends or family members about your thoughts and further release your emotions. Don't keep too many things bottled up inside because if you hold it in for too long, you will break down. (4) Strengthen your ability to cope with setbacks and learn to encourage yourself from within, don't be too afraid of new things. (5) Don't put too much pressure on yourself, learn to relax, and even if there are many difficulties, there are always ways to solve them. The world and I love you. Good wishes.

In the above description, I see that you feel very anxious when encountering certain things, and this anxiety can lead to the occurrence of minor symptoms such as dry heaving. I imagine that this situation must be very distressing for you. However, I would like to invite you to change your perspective on this matter. When you feel anxious and experience dry heaving, does your attention shift slightly from the thing that is making you anxious to yourself? Perhaps when you consciously acknowledge your own anxiety, the "symptom" of dry heaving will gradually lose its significance and start to change. Would you be willing to try something new?

I can understand the anxiety that the OP, as a freshman, feels about the nervous habits brought from high school. First, it should be clarified that this kind of nausea caused by nervousness is not a physiological illness and it is not recommended to use medication to alleviate it. Resolving the psychological causes of this nausea is the fundamental approach. From the OP's account, the nausea that occurs when they feel nervous started during their senior year of high school, indicating that the initial cause of this nausea was the pressure of entering university. Due to the desire for further education and lack of confidence in their own grades, a conflict was formed within them. They wanted to work hard to achieve a certain result but were afraid that they couldn't. In order to alleviate the discomfort caused by this internal conflict, their body manifested symptoms of nausea. As an OP who has already entered college, these physical symptoms caused by the pressure of further education have not only not disappeared but have even worsened in some aspects. Now, they experience nausea whenever they participate in new activities. This indicates that the OP has entered a vicious cycle where physical symptoms caused by psychological reasons exacerbate their mental burden. Therefore, what the OP needs to do now is to break this vicious cycle. Firstly, the OP needs to recognize that this nausea is due to their high expectations for a certain matter, which have turned into pressure. Nausea is the body's response to this pressure. Therefore, the focus should not be on eliminating the symptoms of nausea, but on strengthening the ability to withstand pressure. This can be done in two ways: first, by enhancing resilience to pressure, and second, by correctly understanding the pressure that a matter brings and not making a big deal out of everything. Enhancing resilience to pressure is most effectively achieved by boosting self-confidence. When we have a comprehensive understanding of ourselves and affirm ourselves in all aspects, it is difficult for a single event to exert significant pressure on us, as deep down we firmly believe that failure in one aspect does not mean failure as a whole person. Therefore, the OP can start from here. For example, list their strengths, even the smallest ones, and don't miss a single one. Engage in activities they are best at and are interested in, and strive for success. Accomplish tasks that require little effort but can bring success, especially in terms of helping others. Respect, appreciate, and praise others. By self-motivation, self-acknowledgment, as well as motivation and acknowledgment from others, they can gain self-confidence. Have self-confidence at all times and use inner language to motivate themselves, such as "I'm great," "I'm doing well," "People like me." Have a correct understanding of every matter we encounter. In a person's life journey, they will encounter countless events. No one can guarantee that they can handle every event perfectly. The failure of one event does not mean failure in the entire life. Therefore, do not force oneself to make everything perfect. This is a standard that no one can reach. The saying goes "there is no perfect gold, and no perfect person." Accept that one is not perfect and appropriately lower standards and expectations, which may actually help one reach a higher level. Even if the symptoms of nausea do not immediately disappear, it's okay. Do not consciously think about the nausea, accept it with a calm mindset, and say to oneself, "It's just nausea, there's nothing serious about it!" In other words, treat oneself, who experiences nausea when faced with something, with equanimity, and don't see it as a big deal, just like dealing with changes in weather—adapt to nature, say and do what needs to be done, and persist in doing what one should and can do well. Over time, when the OP notices nausea again, they will likely find that at some point unknown to them, the symptoms of nausea have completely disappeared. The above suggestions are hoped to be helpful to the OP.

I don't know what kind of state you're referring to when you say "nervous". In your family, do you occasionally feel nervous with your parents or other relatives? Do you feel nauseous when you are with your best friend and feeling nervous? Or do you feel nauseous when you are with other classmates and feeling nervous? Or are there times when you feel nervous but don't feel nauseous? When do you start feeling nauseous when you're nervous? Please try to record the scene before you feel nauseous, who was present, where were you, or any situations when you feel nervous but don't feel nauseous. This way, we can first identify some possible causes for your nausea and find the appropriate solutions. Of course, you can also try some behavioral training to practice being confident when facing nervousness, gradually overcoming it. In fact, the opposite of nervousness is relaxation. You can try some relaxation exercises that can help you relax quickly, even in a short period of time and anywhere. You can search on Baidu for many relaxation techniques to practice. It's normal for a 20-year-old young man who has just come of age to have limited social experience and feel nervous in certain situations. As you grow older and gain more experience and knowledge, this state will gradually diminish, and you will become more confident.

In my personal opinion, perhaps you don't take your nausea seriously, thinking that you should be nervous for exams and that nausea is a normal response. If you get used to this kind of thinking after a few times, maybe your nausea will decrease. Also, you should know one thing, are students still afraid of exams? For students, exams are just like eating, don't you think? Think carefully, what can I do when it's exam time? Even if I get nervous, what can I do? Although nausea is uncomfortable, just vomit if you need to, and it will be alright afterwards. Exams are the same, once they are over, you'll feel relieved and no longer anxious.

question: There seems to be something strange in my relationship with my boyfriend. Is it him who is repressing or is it me? It feels like our relationship has hit a wall.
description: The relationship with my boyfriend seems quite strange. I don't know if it's him suppressing his emotions or if it's me. We often feel like our relationship is stagnant and only get better after an argument. He loves posting on social media, seeking recognition and attention. When I ask why he doesn't reach out to me, he says I can reach out to him. I get angry and express my frustration before he makes time to chat with me. If he's not happy, I'm not happy either. If I bring up breaking up, he will try to salvage the relationship and ask if there's something wrong with him. But if we don't break up, our relationship feels suffocating. Over time, I also realize that I'm not actually happy when he does reach out and I don't know what to talk about. We are in a long-distance relationship and he is often busy with other things, not physically there. Sometimes I even feel reluctant to have him around me, thinking that he seems burdened with too many things and not truly happy. Do I not love him? But when he gets upset, I unconsciously want to comfort him and hesitate to break up because I don't want to hurt him. He believes he needs to have some money before we can get married. We hardly ever see each other and communication is scarce. He is a typical straight guy, only focusing on work. Apart from initially finding him somewhat attractive, I feel like he has no other qualities. The entire relationship up until now has been particularly awkward. I can't pinpoint what's wrong, it feels like I'm being tormented. I don't have any specific expectations from him. Maybe I just need a relationship? Or is it that all relationships eventually become tasteless?
keywords: Love, dependency and attachment, love management.

answers.answer_text: Hello, it's nice to have the opportunity to answer your question. In the process of being in a long-distance relationship, due to the distance issue, the chances of contact between you will also decrease, and both of you will live your own lives with very little overlap. I think only genuine feelings will bring you a sense of security, and learning to be independent is also important. In the "Law of Mutual Attraction in Love", the more you provide pleasant experiences, happiness, and social assistance to your partner, the stronger your attractiveness will be. On the contrary, if you frequently argue with him and do not make efforts to maintain the relationship, your attractiveness will decrease. However, if you can't communicate with each other, and it's like a cold war, even though you know the other person exists, they are just a presence, a title. If you can't resolve the grievances you suffer in a timely manner, the possibility of a relationship crisis will greatly increase. If you don't know how to chat, learn to share each other's lives and let the other person know what you are both doing. Even if there is distance, you can feel like your time is synced. When he talks about a topic, you can join in, you are familiar with his friends, and he knows about your life. This approach can make the other person feel at ease and increase the communication in the relationship. Sometimes it's not that the other person doesn't love you anymore, but rather the factors that attract each other have diminished. So, communication can solve this problem. You don't not love him, you just need to learn to adapt. From being familiar to becoming strangers, and from strangers to becoming familiar, what we need is time. If you can't bear to break up, it's because you still love him. Even if he wants to get rich before getting married again, it shows that he is a responsible person, and you are already part of his future plans. Of course, he wants to offer you a better life. We also need understanding and acceptance, and we will eventually be together, going through life together. All relationships are not tasteless because you have experienced a lot together and have many beautiful memories. It's just a test of time now, to see if you can hold on. You must have confidence in yourself and in him. Keep going and good luck! I hope my answer is helpful to you, wishing you all the best.

#Maybe I just need a relationship? Or is it that all relationships ultimately become meaningless?# This sentence is quite interesting, you may really just need a relationship. The other person may be the same as you. Maybe both you and him are relatively suitable choices in the current situation. In your description, the relationship of "friends" is not mentioned. I assume that if your friends see you in such a relationship, they would probably advise you to break up and introduce male friends around you, or ask you to go on blind dates, right? That's how I understand it. But I don't know what your true situation is like. #Or is it that all relationships ultimately become meaningless# Assuming you do need a relationship, but you need to find a suitable reason to maintain a relationship, the latter sentence is a very appropriate "reason". Because you described so much before, it's just discussing that your relationship with your current boyfriend is average, tasteless, and dull. Do you really want to get married? Or do you not want to get married and just need a partner to accompany you? And it seems that you don't have the general anxiety of women about getting married, so I'm more inclined to think that you may need a relationship. Shall we talk about it?

Hello OP, first of all, I understand and empathize with your situation. I want to give you a big hug and let you feel the warmth of the world. I can actually understand your feelings and predicament. Right now, you and your boyfriend are not breaking up, but you are also not staying together. It's a very awkward situation, stuck in a dilemma, wanting to find an outlet to vent. Maybe that way, you will feel a little better. I think the biggest problem between you two may be that the busyness and hustle of life has worn off the initial love. The last trace of warmth in your relationship has disappeared. Because many love stories start with passion and gradually become mundane, but not to the point of extinguishing. Only when life becomes stagnant, many trivial matters happen within the love relationship, and that's when the relationship may be in crisis. And now, the problem between you two is that the freshness in that love is gone, and what's worse is the long-distance issue, which prevents you from frequently meeting and giving each other a little surprise. Don't say that even with a relationship where you see each other every day, there will still be times when you want to ignore each other and situations where you have nothing to talk about, let alone a long-distance relationship. So, in order to maintain a relationship and bring it back to its initial state, both of you need to work on it together. For example, creating small surprises and giving small gifts during holidays. That will make the other person very happy. If you always argue when you meet, maybe, only comforting each other when angry, then the relationship might seem feeble. So, if you want to save this relationship or if you don't want to continue this stalemate, the best solution is for both of you to communicate and express what you really think. Instead of always being in this tense relationship, it is best for you to often stay in an environment where there is no expectation or freshness. I believe nobody wants a stagnant life and relationship. As human beings, we have subjectivity and can create many unexpected things. Therefore, you can communicate and perhaps revisit the places you have been to, watch the movies you watched, and relive all the experiences you had together. That will make the love rekindle its previous beauty. Wishing you happiness and joy, OP.

question: Lately, I always feel like the world doesn't really exist, and in reality, everyone is just virtual.
description: Lately, I have constantly felt that the world doesn't really exist, and have been having fantasies about the entire world and even the universe, as well as the origin of humanity, and so on. It feels as if we ourselves are just creations or merely playing a role in this world.

answers.answer_text: What exists and what does not exist is a philosophical question. It is not easy to find undisputed reasons for what exists and what does not exist. It is normal to feel confused and have some fantasies and strange feelings about this cognitively. It would be nice if, after meals and in leisure time, there was a chance to experience this feeling or engage in some thinking - that's what the ancient Greeks (of course, their aristocracy) used to do. However, our society now lacks that kind of culture - each person has let the idea of being well-fed occupy too much of their spiritual world.

question: Seemingly extravagant, but in reality, it hurts every time I spend money. What could be the reason for this?
description: I just feel reluctant to spend money on myself, there are plenty of good things but I can't find anything suitable for myself.

answers.answer_text: The questioner's question is a bit vague, and we need to clarify first: 1. The questioner is someone who cares a lot about money and feels a lot of pain whenever they spend money, but they still behave extravagantly. They are confused about themselves and hope someone can help answer this confusion. 2. The questioner sees a lot of good things in life but feels that they are not suitable for themselves. They believe that they cannot bring themselves to spend money on these things and feel that this is not right, but they cannot resolve it. Let's first look at the first issue, the extravagant spending behavior: There are two possibilities: 1. They genuinely spend a lot, buying things that they believe have little practical value, such as buying expensive luxury handbags or clothes that far exceed their income level, or buying items that are not used much at home. Or, when eating or traveling with classmates, friends, or others, they always play the role of a big spender, deliberately paying for meals or buying things they don't actually need or want in front of others. 2. They spend money within a normal range, such as comparing their spending with classmates, friends, or colleagues and finding that their spending is average. Even compared to their income (or living expenses), it is still within an affordable range. However, they feel that they shouldn't be spending so much and that there are things they shouldn't buy, so they feel guilty. If it is the first possibility, then it is necessary to regulate their spending behavior. However, the premise of this regulation is to first understand the reasons and motivations behind their overspending or excessive consumption. Is it because they are worried about being looked down upon by others or because they simply cannot control their desire to purchase and consume? If they are concerned about how others perceive them, it means their self-esteem or self-inferiority complex is influencing them. The questioner needs to explore why they have developed this pattern, especially since it has caused them distress (feeling guilty after spending money). The motivations behind the same behavior can be different, so naturally, the solutions will also be different. It is impossible to make further suggestions without knowing the specific circumstances, so I cannot provide any further advice. If they can't control their desire to purchase and consume, it may be because they are using this behavior as compensation for some unmet needs or desires from their past. They use purchasing and consuming as a way to compensate, and this form of compensation also carries a punishment element that causes them pain. What are they compensating for? Perhaps the questioner already has their own answer. Now let's look at the second possibility. Personally, I think the questioner is more likely to fall into the second possibility because based on their question, they hesitate to spend money on themselves and buy nice things. They feel guilty about spending money when in fact, they are not excessively extravagant. They simply think they are spending beyond their own acceptable limits, feeling guilty about buying things they shouldn't buy. Why can't they bring themselves to buy nice things for themselves, especially when their finances allow for it? Do they feel they don't deserve to have nice things? Do they believe that if they have these nice things, they won't be considered a good child, student, employee, or spouse (or husband, sorry, I don't know your gender or current occupation)? If they are not a good child, good student, good employee, or good partner, who will like them? Who will abandon them? What will be the consequences of being abandoned or not being liked by that person? Will it create a crisis of being destroyed? I just happened to read a book by Mr. Hayao Kawai, and there is an explanation of this type of situation. I am not sure if it applies to the questioner's situation, but I think it provides some valuable insights. Mr. Kawai says, "In a child's eyes, their world with their parents (especially their mother) is absolute. Once another person (their younger sibling) enters, their world is destroyed, and they need to readjust their worldview." Many children will adjust themselves to become "good children" who don't spend recklessly, study seriously, take care of their younger siblings, show manners, be considerate of their parents, as if they suddenly become mature and responsible. Such children are more likely to receive recognition and appreciation from their parents who already have a second child, and this recognition and appreciation mean that they won't be abandoned. (Of course, these are my own words, not a direct quote from the book). Which situation does the questioner belong to? Perhaps only they know the answer. If they find self-exploration painful, I suggest seeking help from a professional counselor to explore together.

question: 43-year-old unmarried man, recently diagnosed with a illness, feeling low in mood, what should I do?
description: My boyfriend is 43 years old and unmarried. Last month, he was diagnosed with coronary heart disease and has been feeling very down. A few days ago, he was also diagnosed with mild anxiety and started taking anti-anxiety medication (Yinuosi, he showed me a picture of it). His mood is very unstable, and we haven't seen each other for two weeks. We also rarely chat on WeChat. How should I comfort him? I bought him a book called "I Am Truly Amazing" and send him customized mood messages. He says he can handle it himself, but his mood fluctuates and he has trouble sleeping. What should I do? Thank you, everyone.
keywords: Treatment, methods of treatment, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello, since your boyfriend has been diagnosed with mild anxiety and is currently undergoing medication treatment, the most important thing at the moment is to actively cooperate with the doctor's treatment and take the medication on time. You have bought him books and customized mood messages, but I think that this kind of encouraging and inspirational books may have limited help to him. When his emotions are unstable and he feels down, I think what he needs most is not encouragement and motivation, but understanding and acceptance. If only encouragement is given, he may feel that it is not good or allowed to have low moods. In psychological counseling, there is a principle of "acceptance without pursuit." Even the best counselor cannot have much effect if the person themselves does not have the desire for help. The same principle applies when we try to comfort and advise others. We should respect their personal wishes and not force them. So, if your boyfriend expresses that he is not in a good mood, there is no need to force yourself to comfort and advise him. You can allow him to be quiet. If he says he can regulate himself, you can choose to respect his choice. Your boyfriend has his own problems to face, such as heart disease and anxiety disorder. If he actively seeks your help and wants to confide in you, then patiently listen to him. If not, then you can enjoy your own life. Besides your boyfriend, you should also have your own life, don't you? Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-)

Thank you for the invitation. It is evident that you are very concerned about your boyfriend. I genuinely hope that he will get better. What I want to say is that his emotional anxiety and physical ailment (coronary heart disease) may be interrelated, as coronary heart disease can lead to emotional depression and anxiety. In this case, giving him confidence and companionship should be very helpful for his recovery. Encouraging him to take his medication on time and occasionally checking in on him may be the most important thing for him. Good luck.

I can understand the concern of the questioner. You mentioned that your boyfriend's emotions are very unstable, and you haven't seen each other for two weeks. I suggest you spend more time with him, care for him, and accompany him. Take him out for a walk, and try to persuade him to seek psychological counseling. If he is unwilling to go, respect his decision. The best thing you can do is to take care of yourself first and then support and accompany him through this difficult time.

question: I used to have schizophrenia, but now I am preparing to stop taking medication. Will a girl accept that?
description: Now, taking medication is similar to a normal person's routine and I am almost ready to stop it. But no matter what, I will definitely disclose it before getting married.

answers.answer_text: You used to have schizophrenia, but now you are almost like a normal person. You are preparing to stop taking medication, intending to find a girlfriend or even get married, but you are worried that girls may not accept you. Whether you have had an illness or not, there will always be some people who cannot accept you, and there will always be some people who can. Nowadays, many guys have trouble finding girlfriends, which is a complex social issue, not just a personal problem. Some people do indeed harbor fears and prejudices towards mental illnesses, and as patients or family members, they often experience shame and insecurity. However, these phenomena are gradually changing with the development of medicine and people's awareness. Now, the majority of mental illness patients, after receiving proper treatment, can lead normal lives. You can absolutely pursue the life you desire, but inevitably, you may encounter setbacks. No one's life is always smooth sailing, and relationships, including dating and marriage, are inherently prone to obstacles. Stay calm, be brave in pursuing your goals, and go with the flow.

Hello, the title holder. I used to suffer from schizophrenia, but now I am preparing to stop taking medication. Whether a woman can accept it or not, I think it varies from person to person and there is no definite answer. Some women have a strong sense of tolerance for various issues and will not care too much as long as they like someone; while others may be concerned about certain aspects such as money, physical health, or mental health. So, no matter what, I think it is right to inform the other person before marriage. I think it can be done earlier, after a certain emotional foundation has been established in the early stages of the relationship. Those who can accept it will naturally stay, and those who cannot accept it will not waste each other's time. This is a form of respect for the other person and for oneself. You are now preparing to stop taking medication. Is that the doctor's advice? Although you can maintain normality by taking medication now, it is important to listen to the doctor's advice on whether to stop medication. Do not stop taking medication without consulting a doctor as it may cause a relapse of the condition. Even if the doctor advises stopping medication, it is best to have regular check-ups to monitor your mental state. If you notice any abnormalities, it is important to see a doctor promptly. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

First of all, thank you for your trust in allowing me to respond to your question, and give you a hug. Please also give a hug to your injured self. You have schizophrenia and are currently taking medication. If that is the doctor's recommendation, it means you are in the process of recovery. I hope you will receive proper treatment and remember to take your medication on time. When discontinuing the medication, it is also important to follow the prescribed procedures to monitor your own condition. If possible, you should also undergo some rehabilitation psychological therapy. As for whether a girl can accept it, everyone is different. It is best to be honest about your true condition from the beginning to the other person, without hiding anything. This is not only responsible to yourself but also respects the other person's thoughts. Don't force yourself or others. Those who can accept it will naturally accept it, and those who cannot accept it should allow the other person not to accept it. Psychological therapy is a long process that requires gradual progress. I believe you can overcome difficulties. When you truly recover and heal yourself, I believe you will also find your own happiness. I wish you good health and happiness!

Since you are preparing to stop taking medication, it means that you have already trended towards stability, which is no different from a normal person. Please have more confidence in yourself, you are a person who deserves to love and be loved. Just like what you said, you will definitely inform your partner before marriage. Marrying someone is mainly based on the accumulation of mutual feelings and the alignment of attitudes towards life. So, as someone who has once suffered from an illness but has now recovered, of course you are qualified to enjoy love, right? Of course, in the future, you should pay more attention to your mental state, make timely adjustments and preventive measures, and believe in yourself. You will have your own love story. Keep it up!

question: Vocational college graduates often feel uneasy about their employment prospects. It is regrettable that they have to decide whether it is better to pursue further education or focus on finding a job.
description: I am currently studying at a vocational college, majoring in the food industry. I feel uncertain about finding a good job in this field. I searched on Baidu and it seems like I can take the elementary school teacher qualification exam. I plan to prepare for it. I also want to further my studies and obtain a bachelor's degree, but I'm not sure if my parents will support me. I was born in 1999, so pursuing a bachelor's degree will require an additional two years of study. I'm about to enter my sophomore year, so if I add two years, I still have three years to go. I also don't know if I can pass the exams for further studies. I feel regretful that my previous exam results have not been satisfactory. I really want to make up for it. I may not be smart, but I am willing to work hard. That's how I plan things. I don't have a detailed plan, only a rough one.
keywords: Growth, developmental patterns, work, studies, student growth.

answers.answer_text: Remember one thing, if you are eligible for further education, prioritize further education because you will find that after further education, you will have better job opportunities. Even if you fail in further education, you can still choose employment. The two are not contradictory. Since the questioner is about to enter their sophomore year, here is my personal opinion: first, apply for a self-study undergraduate program, choose a humanities major with fewer courses, and try to exempt as many subjects as possible (such as management or Chinese language). In the sophomore year, only take four professional courses each semester and no need to take general courses (unless there is an on-the-spot exam that day). In the junior year, temporarily stop taking self-study courses and focus on studying for the regular undergraduate program. Once you pass the regular program, continue with the self-study courses while completing the regular program, or apply for exemptions. (How about a dual degree?) If you fail, you can directly enter the workforce, but you can still complete the self-study undergraduate program, which will allow you to make another choice after graduating with a bachelor's degree (whether to continue working at your current workplace or find a new job with a bachelor's degree). If the questioner is studying in Hubei or Tibet, it may not be possible to study for an associate degree and take the undergraduate program at the same time, but that's okay. As long as you focus on studying for the regular program in the junior year and pass, you can switch to employment if you fail. Choose a job that allows for more free time and study for a teaching qualification in your free time (it is recommended to choose primary school subjects). As for the questioner's desire to obtain a teaching qualification certificate, my suggestion is that if you succeed in further education (even if you only graduate with a self-study undergraduate degree), you can go for the high school teaching qualification certificate. If further education is completely unsuccessful (e.g., failed subjects in the self-study program or unable to pass the regular program), it is better to find a job with fewer working hours after graduation, sign a tripartite agreement, and prepare for the primary school teaching certificate in your free time.

Hello, I hope my answer can give you some help. I believe that for you and your classmates who have been in a similar situation, this is indeed a difficult decision to make. But a good point is that you have seriously analyzed and considered your future. First of all, nobody's life is without regrets. I also regret not having worked harder before, "If only I had tried harder!" I guess that's something everyone has thought about. But there is no regret medicine in the world. Since everything is already set, we can only accept it and work hard to make the future better. You want to take the teacher qualification exam and pursue a bachelor's degree. I believe you have listened to the voice inside you, so go ahead and give it a try. I think it's possible to do both, even though there will be many difficulties on this path. If you're worried about your parents' thoughts, then talk to them. Don't just dwell on your worries. It's no use worrying without taking action. I think your parents will understand and support your decision. If they don't, then find a solution. In any case, take action! From your words, I can also see your concerns about whether you can succeed in pursuing a bachelor's degree. I want to tell you that I have also had the same concerns. I have also worried about whether to pursue further studies or find a job. There are indeed risks in pursuing further studies, and the uncertainty is too great. I'm also afraid of not succeeding and missing out on a year of internship experience. However, I have also received advice from others that truly resolved my dilemma: can you imagine if you found your dream job, would you still not pursue a bachelor's degree? If the answer is yes, then perhaps you don't really want to pursue a bachelor's degree. In that case, your motivation to study will be smaller, and you may not wholeheartedly devote yourself to pursuing a bachelor's degree. So, I suggest you seriously consider whether to choose to pursue a bachelor's degree. For me, the answer is no. Although there are many difficulties and uncertainties on this path, I do regret not going to a better school. I want my life to be richer and better, and even though I'm scared, I will wholeheartedly strive for it. Maybe I will fail, but I won't regret choosing this path. I believe that throughout this process, I have improved in terms of knowledge and mindset. And if I hadn't tried, I would have regretted it all along! No matter how much advice others give you, ultimately you have to make your own decision. Once you've made a choice, don't be afraid. Take the brave step forward! Finally, I wish you success in your studies.

question: Will you feel relieved after committing suicide? Does that mean I am not important?
description: Why is it that when I buy snacks for my friends to eat, my mom beats me and says I don't give any to my sister? Does that mean I'm not important?
keywords: Family, family relationships, and growth process.

answers.answer_text: Dear questioner, at this very moment, you still feel pain. When we allow pain to flow through our bodies, it slowly nourishes us, and perhaps in the future, we may gain a new strength from it. Also, don't forget that you can take a break and pause. Time is to be experienced, and we still have time. When you're tired, take a rest.

question: Always feeling like a greedy, ugly, and fake person, what kind of psychological state is this?
description: Being greedy for wealth, fame, and status used to be my goal. But now, even if I were to attain all of these, I don't think I would be happy. I wonder if my pursuit of happiness is also excessive. Although I constantly remind myself to be helpful and kind, deep down I sometimes feel unwilling. There are times when I dislike someone in my heart, yet I dare not offend them and choose to peacefully coexist instead. I feel like such a hypocrite.

answers.answer_text: ~I want to give you a warm hug~ The pursuit of material possessions and happiness is something that everyone has. Most people cannot achieve the so-called "indifference to fame and fortune" and only pursue spiritual satisfaction. Since there is something to pursue, there will be a process of striving for it, in which people generally put in some effort or means. Actually, whether or not a person should pursue a desire, or how to accomplish something, is a personal choice. Do what you want to do, don't doubt yourself, maybe the way of thinking about things has changed, the ideas have simplified, the mood has relaxed, and happiness will come.

question: For a period of time, there are intense and calm moments about certain things, unstable.
description: For some things, like "poetry and distant places," there are times when thinking about them fills me with excitement and passion, firmly believing that this is what I've been seeking my whole life, and I am filled with determination. But after a while, when I think about these things, my heart remains calm and I feel no excitement. I have no emotions, and I feel down and lack motivation. This keeps happening in a cycle. It's not because of so-called growth or different thoughts at different ages. It's just that for half a month or a month, I feel passionate about this matter, and then for a period of time, I feel no passion. After another month, I am filled with excitement again. These two states keep changing in a cycle, and neither state lasts for a long time. I want to know why this happens and what causes these changes in states or mindsets. How can I maintain relative stability?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, life purpose.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP~ For a while, you were passionate about "poetry and faraway places", but then you lost that passion, and after a while, it came back again. This kind of cycle repeats itself, and eventually, even you start to doubt yourself. From your description, it can be seen that you really like "poetry and faraway places". After a period of calm, when you regain your state, you still have the same passionate enthusiasm as before. Isn't liking something supposed to be a continuous and persistent love? According to common sense, it should be like this, so why does this kind of state occur? *Why is the term "period of fatigue" mentioned? In our lives, we often have periods of fatigue, for example, during this time, you really want to do something, but after a while, you seem to lose interest, and then after a while, you want to do it again, and this repeats. The period in between when we don't want to do something is our period of fatigue. Right now, you are in this state, and you might even think that maybe there is something wrong with your mindset, but actually, you don't have to worry too much.———————————————————————————————————— #Set clear goals and make wise use of time. "Poetry and faraway places" is what you love, but when love comes, it's too passionate, as if you feel like you can do "poetry and faraway places" for 24 hours a day. So, set a goal for yourself, such as how much poetry you want to read every day, how long you want to spend reading books, it doesn't have to be too much, an hour or two, according to your own time, stick to it every day, and avoid excessive learning. #Relax appropriately and keep your brain awake. You can exercise and listen to music in your spare time to relax yourself. After finishing studying, give your brain some relaxation so that the next day you can have a better spirit for learning and growth! Hope you can enjoy "poetry and faraway places" every day, and enjoy immersing yourself in the happy moments and the beauty!

question: Dropped out of graduate school after starting, feeling useless, can't understand the meaning of life?
description: Due to personal reasons, I dropped out of graduate school after more than two years. I didn't enjoy the life of being a graduate student and it felt like I had suppressed my emotions for over two years until they suddenly exploded and became uncontrollable. Additionally, because of the pandemic, I have been at home for over six months. I worked at an insurance company for a month recently, but I quit because I didn't like the atmosphere there. Now that the pandemic is over, it's time for me to find a job. However, as a beginner in the professional world who gave up on my field, I have no idea where to start. I'm just passing time at home day by day. To be honest, it was the same during those two years of graduate school. I would procrastinate on tasks and lacked motivation and drive. I also don't know the meaning of my existence. The only concern I have is how my parents would cope if I were to die. From childhood to adulthood, I have always been the type of child who did what my parents told me to do. Perhaps a small part of the reason why I dropped out of school is due to wanting a different life. I feel like a soulless puppet living my life. Also, due to several unsuccessful romantic relationships in the past, I have a negative view not only towards love but also towards life in general. From love, I've learned to give up. If I can't achieve it, then I might as well give up.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: I am not confident about my appearance either. I had severe acne from eighth grade to sophomore year of college, and just when it finally got better in my sophomore year, I started experiencing hair loss in my senior year. Now, I am really afraid to be seen by others. I have previously seen a psychologist, and it did seem effective at the time, but it couldn't completely save me. I am a very stubborn person, once I have made up my mind about something, it's difficult to change, whether it's right or wrong. I feel like there is something wrong with me, or maybe having a mental illness is the most convenient excuse for my current thoughts and feelings.

question: I am being driven crazy by procrastination. Procrastination leads to anxiety and insomnia. What should I do?
description: I have a severe case of procrastination. I know I need to handle certain things right away, but there is a resistant and unwillingness in my mind to do them, which leads to procrastination. Procrastination leads to anxiety, insomnia, and a chain of negative emotions. It has already seriously affected my life and work. What should I do? I'm going crazy!!! Can anyone help me?!
keywords: Growth, personality development, self-growth, stress management

answers.answer_text: Hello, you mentioned that you procrastinate until it makes you anxious. I give you a hug. You choose to procrastinate because procrastination, not doing this thing, is more meaningful to you. Maybe you don't want to do this thing at all, but not doing it will make you feel a sense of loss of control, and you will think that a series of bad things will happen, which leads to anxiety. This situation is to avoid something, and what you avoid may be a certain situation and feeling from the past. And now, you have less power, so you automatically avoid it. You want to control the outcome and cannot accept the uncontrollable, as well as face a certain scene from the past and the fear it brings you. This fear is especially terrifying for you, and it is normal. That fear was really terrifying for you at that time, and it is normal that you cannot accept it. But because you refuse fear, you are controlling the circulation of this energy. You want to control and not experience fear, but actually, you can't control it. If you are willing to try, let yourself experience fear. When the emotional maximum of fear is reached, it will naturally come down, and after it comes down, you will find that you are okay. You can find a safe environment and say to yourself, "Let's experience fear together. I'm with you." Then experience this very fearful feeling. No matter what scary things you think of in your mind, when the fear reaches its peak, it will come down, and the intense feeling of fear will disappear, but you are still in that place and you are fine. If you can't do it, you need some external help to help you see the fear and release it, such as seeking help from a counselor, etc. I wish you well.

Hello! After carefully reading your experience, I can feel that you are being held back by procrastination, which is seriously affecting your life and work. This is indeed a very unpleasant feeling. The existence of procrastination represents our inner desire for perfection. Procrastination and the pursuit of perfection are twin brothers. Sometimes, the pursuit of perfection wears the cloak of procrastination, causing us to feel dissatisfied with ourselves. Your procrastination in dealing with urgent events leads to a feeling of resistance to taking action. I invite you to reflect on the psychological motivations behind this. For example, you may care about how others perceive you or hope to surpass the expectation of perfection in completing tasks. Procrastination can lead to a series of negative emotions, resulting in your insomnia, which is a natural stress response. When you do not meet your own perfect goals, it will inevitably trigger a lot of emotional feedback, such as anxiety, self-blame, grievances, anger, etc. The appearance of these emotions is also a hope for you to hear your true inner voice. What do you truly want? When you see the deeper expectations behind your pursuit of perfection, allow yourself to not be "perfect." Here are some suggestions: 1) Change your mindset: Completion is more important than perfection. In each task, shift some of your focus to the process of thinking and taking action, breaking it down into achievable small goals. Give yourself positive affirmations for each small goal achieved. Taking the first step from 0 to 1 won't be so difficult. 2) Let go: Learn to gradually let go of external evaluations of yourself. Every imperfection represents that you are an action-taker, making progress step by step. Find different ways to record and appreciate each step of achievement. For example, write a gratitude journal or list three good things that happened each day. These practices can help enhance your self-identity and reduce your focus on external evaluations. 3) Take action: Most procrastinators tend to overthink and exhaust their energy on cognitive aspects, leaving no energy for action. Therefore, it is highly recommended that you prioritize action and allow action to improve your ability to handle tasks effectively. 4) Meditation: I suggest using mindfulness meditation to enhance your focus. This is a very effective method for addressing procrastination. However, it requires strict self-discipline and persistence. Finally, I strongly recommend seeking help from a professional mental health counselor if conditions permit. The existence of procrastination has significant implications for personal growth. With the help of a counselor, you can analyze your personal growth experiences and gain insights that will empower you to face procrastination more effectively. I hope my answer has provided you with some inspiration and assistance. Best wishes for overcoming your perplexed emotions soon!

Hello, OP~ I completely understand your feelings. Procrastination is very common, and many people experience it to some extent. Even though there are many things to do, we always keep delaying them and only find motivation to complete them when the deadline approaches. Procrastination can be categorized into three types: avoidance procrastination, decision procrastination, and encouraging procrastination. Avoidance procrastination involves avoiding the tasks themselves, either because they are too overwhelming to confront, or due to past failures that have instilled fear, lack of confidence, and worry about inadequate abilities to complete them. Decision procrastination refers to having detailed plans but delaying their execution for a long time. Encouraging procrastination occurs when someone believes they work more efficiently at the last minute and that time pressure gives them a sense of satisfaction. [Some suggestions]: Break down tasks into smaller ones. When faced with a lot of work, it can be stressful and difficult to know where to start. Breaking down big tasks into smaller ones, assigning a deadline for each small task, and gradually completing them can make implementation easier. Give yourself rewards. After completing a task, reward yourself with something you enjoy, such as a delicious meal, a movie, or a small gift, to motivate yourself further. Set realistic plans. Without a plan, you may feel directionless. However, if your plans are too excessive and packed, you may feel overwhelmed without any breathing room, causing significant stress, escape, and anxiety. Set realistic plans according to your own circumstances, balance work and leisure, and allow yourself to relax. I hope you can get rid of your troubles soon~.

Dear, hello! Regarding your question, I understand, because such situations often occur during our student days. I used to be someone who procrastinated a lot during my student days. Even though an assignment was due at 8:15, I would wait until 8:10 to start it. Even though I could have submitted a draft a day in advance, I would wait until the last day. Actually, I'm well aware that submitting early could alleviate a lot of stress and make things easier for me, but I just don't want to do it in advance!!! This has always been a problem that troubles me. But in reality, is procrastination really that terrible? Actually, no. Procrastination and laziness have similar meanings, with the most obvious difference being that procrastination means you eventually complete the task, while laziness means you never do the task until the last moment. They are different in terms of the final result. Laziness may be difficult to overcome, but procrastination is not. Procrastination is related to time; it is relative to the length of time. So the most important point in improving your procrastination is to make your time more compact. If the deadline for a paper is the day after tomorrow, tell yourself in your mind that tomorrow is the deadline, and it has to be submitted tomorrow. Of course, just thinking this way won't alleviate the situation, so when necessary, you still have to coerce yourself. If you fail to submit the paper tomorrow, then don't buy lipstick or eat a chicken leg. We all know that when we use a very important bargaining chip to force ourselves forward, we often achieve good results. Break the task into smaller tasks and gradually complete them. Completing a task immediately is impossible because you can't see the process of its realization, so you will feel overwhelmed and procrastinate. But dear, if we break it down, is it still that difficult? Let me give you an example. I want to write a viral article with over 100,000 views, but achieving over 100,000 views is really difficult. If I keep thinking about this goal, I'm sure I will give up. So I came up with a solution to break down this seemingly distant idea. To achieve a viral article with over 100,000 views, you need sufficient awareness of social hot topics and material. So I set a goal to organize one topic and write about a hundred words or so about my perspective on the hot topic every day. In the long run, I have indeed made real progress and have achieved a viral article with over 100,000 views. When you break down the goal, procrastination becomes easier to overcome. The most important thing is to use something you like to limit your procrastination. If you don't complete the task, then you won't be able to buy something you like. This method is even more effective than what I mentioned above. Finally, take care.

Hello! I deeply understand your troubles. When you have resistance and don't want to do something, you tend to procrastinate, leading to anxiety, insomnia, and negative emotions. I will share my knowledge with you, hoping to inspire you. Almost everyone, or at least the majority of people, may experience procrastination. When faced with things that they are not particularly willing to do or have difficulty accepting, they tend to postpone them, some eventually complete them, while others do not. Try to accept that you have procrastination tendencies. In fact, procrastination is most common in people who pursue perfection and take their responsibilities seriously. Are you such a person? Another reason is that the consequences of procrastination are not severe enough to force immediate action. You may think, for the things you enjoy doing, do you procrastinate? So, remove this label from yourself. You may have experienced some hidden benefits from procrastination. Try to think about it yourself. Additionally, procrastination is different from laziness. Laziness means not wanting to do something at all, while procrastination means knowing that you need to do something but not taking action.
