Procrastination can have varying degrees of harm to both work and study. Non-acceptance and rejection of yourself is what makes it difficult for you to change, according to the teacher. In fact, procrastination is a form of self-protection, so you can easily accept it by saying, "I am tired, I don't want to do anything now, I don't want to change." By doing this, you will have less internal conflict and find it easier to change. Conversely, people who constantly procrastinate are constantly blaming themselves without accepting themselves. Their internal dialogue is: "I don't like my current self, so I have to change." Their energy is being depleted, causing them to remain stuck. When facing procrastination, we should increase rather than change. I don't reject procrastination, but I am willing to develop the courage to face reality and improve my resilience. No longer entangled in the problem of procrastination, there are many ways to overcome it. For example, set clear and achievable goals. The key feature of clear goals is that they must be observable. For example, for the task you don't want to do, how much do you want to complete today? Each time you achieve a clear goal, your confidence increases. When facing immense pressure at work, many people procrastinate because they consider a project too complex and impossible to complete in a short period of time, and therefore avoid doing it. However, the complex task can be broken down into smaller, easily accomplishable sub-tasks, reducing our psychological pressure and making it easier to complete the work. Avoiding perfectionism can also help alleviate procrastination. Perfectionists with maladaptive tendencies often set high standards for themselves, fear failure, and use procrastination to avoid taking action. If they don't act, there won't be any results, and they won't fail. Change your attitude and learn to approach problems with a positive mindset. Put aside the obstacles and difficulties that hinder immediate action, focus on what we currently have, and then take action! If procrastination is severe, consider seeking professional help and see a psychologist. Finally, I wish you a speedy recovery from the troubles of procrastination!

You have three problems: 1. When there is an event that requires immediate action, you feel resistant internally, so you procrastinate. 2. Because you procrastinate and do not take action, things worsen, and you cannot accept or bear the consequences of losing control. 3. The frequent occurrence of bad situations forms a negative impression that you are not capable or good enough, leading to anxiety, insomnia, and uneasiness. To address these issues, you need to: 1. Change your cognition. 2. Take immediate action. 3. Strengthen self-discipline. 4. Increase self-acceptance. 5. Persistently adhere to the above four points to establish a positive cycle. The most crucial and important aspect here is changing your cognition. First, ask yourself why you naturally have an emotion of resistance and unwillingness when it comes to tasks that need to be dealt with immediately. This emotion is crucial, but where does it come from? Why does it arise? You need to pay special attention to this point and explore it further, uncovering important aspects that you have never discovered before. I suggest that you seek the help of a counselor to find and explore this first point together. Improving the habit of procrastination necessitates taking immediate action, but your attention is focused on resistance, struggling with tasks that you have no choice but to do but refuse to do. You are unable to take action and have lost the ability to act. I suggest that you put aside all your thoughts, emotions, resistance, and hesitation, and immediately start taking action. You can also involve others to collaborate with you and supervise you to enhance your ability to handle tasks. Self-discipline, as the third matter, relies on having a foundation to accomplish the first two points. I want to emphasize the fourth point: self-acceptance is a major issue that you currently face. You believe that you have a serious case of procrastination and judge yourself as being sick. Well, if you're sick, you should seek treatment, right? But no, you don't want to seek treatment or change; you just wait for someone else to help you. Do you think having someone help you will magically solve everything? You think you won't procrastinate anymore? Therefore, I suggest that you seek psychological counseling and receive long-term follow-up treatment from a counselor, as that will be the most effective in helping you. So, if you really don't want to go crazy, if you truly want to improve your bad habit of procrastination, take action. Believe in yourself, I also believe in you! Keep going!

Hello! Believe in yourself, you can definitely overcome procrastination! The scary thing about procrastination is that you always think, "It's okay, I'll do it tomorrow." But when tomorrow comes, you convince yourself of the same thing. Procrastination sufferers always have countless "tomorrows," but never grasp the opportunity of today. As a result, procrastination becomes a habit, an addiction that is difficult to break. So when critical moments arrive, you have to spend even more energy and time, making yourself nervous, anxious, and uncomfortable. The solution is actually simple: make a plan, learn self-discipline, use time wisely, strive to persist, not easily slack off, and not let laziness become a habit. The approach is simple, but putting it into practice is difficult. A specific breakdown can be as follows: 1. First, try to accept that you have procrastination, and in fact, most people have procrastination. In fact, procrastination is most common in those who strive for perfection and take their responsibilities seriously. It is precisely because "if I do anything, I want to do it to the best of my ability" that leads to constant delays and hesitations. Yet, often at the last moment, they manage to complete the task, which shows that procrastinators are actually very smart. If they start too early, they may change their minds and waste time. It is better to do it in one go when there is a sense of urgency. 2. Regularly ask yourself, "Is what I am doing now the most important thing at the moment?" This is the experience of Mark Zuckerberg, the founder of "Facebook." He is very busy but never procrastinates. Every year, he can complete many seemingly impossible tasks and plans. He relies on this simple but powerful question. 3. Set fixed time and develop a habit: for example, sit diligently at your desk without playing with your phone or games from 7 to 9 pm every night. It may seem boring, but you have to do something. So start working, and you will find that you can complete many tasks ahead of time, to your own surprise. Moreover, it becomes easier and easier, boosting your confidence and alleviating your psychological burden. Remember to reward yourself too. 4. Learn to prioritize. Classify tasks into urgent and important, important but not urgent, urgent but not important, and neither urgent nor important, then complete them accordingly. Break down large tasks into smaller ones. 5. Eliminate distractions. Close QQ, turn off music, turn off the TV... Turn off everything that may affect your work efficiency and focus wholeheartedly on your tasks. 6. Mutual supervision. Find friends who can overcome this bad habit together. It's easier than fighting alone. 7. Set more specific goals. If your plan is "I want to lose weight and maintain a good figure," it is likely to fail. But if your plan is "I will get up for a run three times a week at 7 am," it will likely be followed through. So, consider dividing tasks into manageable small goals. 8. Don't give yourself too much time. Psychologist Fournier found that graduate students who took two years to complete their theses always left some time to relax and reorganize. Those who took three years or more to write their theses spent almost every minute collecting data and writing. Therefore, sometimes the longer you extend your work time, the lower your work efficiency. 9. Don't glorify stress. Don't believe in sayings like "under pressure, heroes emerge." You can create a timetable with short-term, medium-term, and long-term goals to avoid postponing everything until the last minute. 10. Seek professional help. If procrastination is severe and affecting your future, consider seeking help from a psychologist. Cognitive-behavioral therapy might be effective. In summary, take action immediately. It may be difficult to completely overcome procrastination, but improving it is definitely possible.

Hello, OP. First of all, from your description, I can sense that such situation often puts your life out of control and has a serious impact on your life and work. It's like a vicious circle. Being unable to sleep at night makes you lack energy for work the next day. But this situation also indicates that there may be an imbalance in your inner self. Only when a person is in a state of inner imbalance, he/she needs to compensate through some forms of escape or procrastination. In simpler terms, because deep down in your heart, you resist the things you have to do, hence the subconscious resistance and procrastination. Secondly, although I don't know when this situation started for you, since you have such a problem, it suggests that to some extent, you have weak autonomy in your growth process, and this is closely related to your early growth experiences. At the same time, anxiety and insomnia are also due to a lack of control over the procrastinated tasks, which is a manifestation of weak psychological abilities and qualities. Therefore, I suggest you seek professional psychological counseling for personal growth to enhance the corresponding psychological abilities and qualities, and establish time management and efficiency improvement skills from the root. Finally, insomnia and anxiety are often physiological responses. You can try relaxation exercises before sleep, such as abdominal breathing. This can help reduce your highly stressed, anxious emotions and better enter a state of relaxation and sleep. However, please pay attention that your focus should be on your own breath, and it must be abdominal breathing! If you are not skilled at it initially, you can place your hands on your abdomen and feel the rise and fall of your abdomen with each breath. Remember: do not use chest breathing, as it will only make you more tense. I hope you can solve this problem and live a better life soon.

How severe is your procrastination? What are the things that you won't procrastinate on? When it comes to those tasks that you procrastinate, what is it that you resist? Is it a feeling of rebellion, anxiety, or something else? Different reasons behind procrastination require different approaches to deal with. Some procrastination may be a form of resistance or expression of anger towards certain things or people. It is possible that by managing these emotions well, you can avoid using procrastination as a way to cope. Also, when did your procrastination start? How did it develop into the way it is now? Although many people have procrastination, everyone's procrastination may look different, so it is necessary to understand it in detail.

Hello, procrastination is a popular behavior habit these days, but it seems like your procrastination is more serious, almost driving you crazy and causing anxiety and insomnia. It seems like it has reached a point where it needs to be resolved. Let's take a look together at what good methods there are. First, in order to address this symptom, we need to create some behavior charts. Currently, I am using a micro habit formation chart myself, listing out some small habits that need to be developed every day, such as reading ten pages of a book or doing push-ups once a day. Check off the completed tasks on the chart every day and give yourself rewards. Every evening, I write down the tasks I need to do tomorrow in a notebook and prioritize them into four categories: important and urgent, urgent but not important, important but not urgent, not important and not urgent. The next day, I start by completing the tasks that are important and urgent, and so on. Also, we have many fragmented periods of time throughout the day, and if used effectively, they can be quite productive. Sometimes, you can complete a small task in 15 minutes or a medium-sized task in half an hour, and you can accomplish something significant in an hour. List out all the tasks that need to be completed and check them off as you finish each one. Completing a few tasks can be rewarded. Additionally, set aside half an hour each day for meditation to calm your mind and reflect on what you have accomplished and what is still left to be done. Habits are developed gradually, so you can practice these techniques for a month to see what happens. Finally, I'm concerned about your anxiety symptoms. You can go to a psychology department and take a test. If it turns out to be true, you also need to address your anxiety.

question: I'm tired, but I know I won't give up. There's a battle going on in my mind.
description: Sometimes I really want to die, but what's the point of living on? I don't want to forgive him, but I know eventually I will forgive all the harm he caused me. However, my current state of mind is not calm. I don't want to forgive. All the hurts are done in the name of love. If I could remember, it would be great to retaliate, but I can't. I know in the end I will be kind to others, not because I force myself, but because I know I have the choice. I won't be troubled by these things, but this is all in the end, the very end. I will always be shot down. Do you know that I'm not taking care of myself right now? I have no control, no hope for life. I'm an adult, but I feel learned helplessness. I know I'm improving, but it's slow. Not only that, no one supports me. My family uses love as a way to strike and oppress me. Can I let go? If there is a next life, please don't let me meet them again. I'm tired. If not, I really don't want to be human anymore. It would be better to be a flower, a tree, or even just a blade of grass. Spring glory, autumn withering, or even falling beneath a footprint. I'm exhausted, but I know I won't end it. Heaven is helping me heal. This is what I need to encounter in my lifetime. I will certainly find clarity in living. In the future, I don't need them, but blood ties force me to accept this burden. This is the reconciliation of life.

answers.answer_text: You hurt me, but I will find a way to reconcile with myself. In this pattern, I need to survive, but I will also become tired. I will get tired, and no one knows, but I will still live. One's life needs to be taken slowly. It has been several months, and I can't hurry. I know I need to slowly reconcile. I will be happy. I have a future. I can't change you, but I need to survive. That's what it means to be human, not a flower, not a tree, not grass, perhaps it is also an honor.

question: What should I do when I find myself deeply involved after accepting someone's confession, but it's causing me a lot of distress?
description: The day before yesterday, I just received a confession from my blind date and we even kissed. I realized that I have fallen too deeply into this, and every day I keep recalling these memories. He doesn't contact me, which makes me feel disappointed. I'm afraid that I'm becoming too dependent and losing myself. I've also started to feel insecure and unwilling to engage with his social circle. I think I'm falling in love, but I'm also experiencing anxiety and insecurity. What should I do?
keywords: Love, dependency and attachment, the management of love.

answers.answer_text: It seems that the original poster both desires and fears entering into an intimate relationship, afraid of experiencing various emotions such as longing, worry, sadness, and anxiety, as well as losing oneself. If one wants to grow, the best way is to experience and hone oneself in relationships. So my advice is to boldly invest in it, because after getting immersed, you will go through both joy and pain, including unexpected experiences. Whether it ends in a successful relationship, whether it is a happy process, and even if you lose yourself in the process—all of these do not matter. But this experience will surely greatly temper and elevate your personality.

Based on the OP's description, I can sense your struggle and lack of security. You take relationships seriously, which is why you get too deeply involved. You don't want to be too reliant because you're afraid of being too clingy to the other person, but at the same time, you still want to be close to them. It's a state of wrestling and feeling unsure. The feeling of being lost is simple - why hasn't he replied to my message? Why is he so busy? Actually, you don't have to be together every day. If he tells you he's busy beforehand, you can relax and stop overthinking. Because everyone has work and their own things going on, it's not possible to give their full attention to everything. When it comes to relationships, there is happiness and powerlessness because we are all exploring in the face of emotions. I hope you don't feel distressed anymore and find happiness.

question: Recurring dreams and fear, is it self-suggestion or something else?
description: I often have the same dream and I wake up scared every time. In the dream, I want to eat something, but I find that my teeth are falling out one by one, all falling into my mouth. I try to hold on to them but I can't, and I feel very afraid. After a while, a new set of teeth will grow again, but the same result will repeat. It seems that every time I have this kind of dream, I get sick afterwards. I don't know if it's self-suggestion or something else.
keywords: Emotion, expressing emotions, panic and helplessness.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I carefully read your question. There are many interpretations for dream meanings, but the most important thing is to analyze them based on the dreamer's feelings. Here, I can only provide some guidance. [Consider the main elements in the dream.] The main elements of the dream: teeth, eating. These two elements actually imply your life state, specifically regarding self-care. You mentioned in your question that you often get sick after having this dream, so the meaning of these two dreams is more like a warning and reminder. When you neglect taking care of yourself for a period of time, the dream of eating will appear. No matter how you eat, your teeth will fall out, which might suggest that you may be too exhausted during this period, implying that you should consider your own health. [Consider the emotional state in the dream and after waking up.] It seems that in the dream, your emotional state is frightened, and you still feel worried after waking up. These emotional states actually imply some negative information that the dream may convey. They mostly point to possible crisis events that may occur in life. Therefore, if you have such dreams again, please remember to check your recent life status. If you have been overextended, please adjust your lifestyle in a timely manner. I hope the above reply is helpful to you.

The theme of the OP's dream seems to be destruction and rebirth. When facing destruction, our consciousness is often filled with absolute fear. However, our subconscious knows that destruction is not just the end, but also a necessary prerequisite for new beginnings. Every occurrence and development has a process, but we often only recognize it when things have already come to a result (actually approaching an end), such as getting sick. Initially, it starts with something minor, but during this stage, we often don't realize that we are already in the course of the illness. We usually have to wait until various symptoms become quite noticeable before we can define it with a certain name. With this defined name, we then consciously acknowledge that we are sick. However, the subconscious confirms the presence of the illness much earlier, and it expresses it in the form of dreams. For consciousness, this dream becomes a kind of omen.

question: Why are people so sensitive to sound and light when they're tired?
description: Why, when feeling exhausted, do I feel disgusted and find the world bleak when hearing others' voices? I also lose interest in things around me. After recovering my energy, it feels like I had a dream. How can I improve this?

answers.answer_text: Why is it that when you are very tired, hearing other people's voices can be very irritating? This is because you want to rest in peace. When you are very tired, you need rest, you need quiet, and you don't want to be bothered or stressed with anything. This situation also indicates that even during your rest, you still maintain a sense of alertness and have a high level of vigilance. This is a stress response. When a person is threatened or stimulated, their sympathetic nervous system is activated, and a large amount of stress hormone (cortisol) is released, putting the whole body in an emergency state. At this time, the heart rate increases, muscles become tense, blood pressure rises, breathing becomes rapid, and the senses become sharp. When you are in this state of stress, you naturally become sensitive to sound and light and perceive others as a threat. Perhaps it is your environment that has fostered this habit of vigilance. If you want to change, you need to first examine whether your environment has changed. For example, if you have left your original home and now live in a safe community, you can tell yourself, "It is safe and harmonious here, I am relaxed." This will suggest to yourself that there is no sense of tension here. In addition, you can exercise for at least 30 minutes every day. A certain amount of exercise can not only stimulate the release of endorphins but also have a certain inhibitory effect on cortisol release. Furthermore, maintaining harmonious intimate relationships is important. It is said that home is a harbor for people, and interacting with loved ones can indeed calm people's restlessness. If you feel stressed, you can return to your family and immerse yourself in the family atmosphere. Good intimate relationships can help maintain blood pressure levels within a normal range and promote the release of dopamine and endorphins, which are happiness factors in the body.

After careful reading of your confession, I deeply understand your pain. Sending you a warm hug. Here is my analysis: 1. "Why do I feel a strong aversion to hearing other people's voices when I'm tired?" When our bodies are tired, we tend to sleep. And sleep requires a quiet environment, without any disturbances. Similarly, when our minds are tired, they also need rest. Therefore, we don't want to be disturbed by external voices. This is the reason why you feel a strong aversion to hearing other people's voices. 2. "I feel like the world is very gloomy." When we are tired, our mental energy drops to its lowest point. Consequently, our hearts become fragile and susceptible to negative suggestions. Therefore, our perception of the world changes, and we start to feel that it is gloomy. 3. "How can I improve?" Cultivate a hobby for yourself. By engaging in something you love, you can quickly replenish your energy and fill yourself with strength. Thank you for your question, and may the goodness of the world come to you as expected.

Hello, OP! I want to give you a big hug for feeling tired. The feeling of "tiredness" is a result of the interaction between body and mind. Your body brings your awareness back to itself, focusing on itself. At this time, your senses become heightened and more sensitive to the external world. That's why sounds, light, and other stimuli can be more bothersome. Based on your description, I understand that this "tiredness" is more of what people call "mental exhaustion" rather than physical fatigue. OP, you can take some time in a relaxed and comfortable environment to reflect: Has this situation occurred recently, or has it been going on for a long time? Is there any pattern to its occurrence? What kind of things might be causing it? Body and mind are interconnected, and often our bodies know the answers to emotional and psychological confusion that we may not consciously realize. By becoming more self-aware, we can address the root of this problem more effectively. Lastly, when you're tired, why not take a rest? After all, life is like a marathon, isn't it? External judgments and standards are products of society, but our own life experiences are ultimately our own. Let's encourage each other.

question: Emotional delay and slow reactions can greatly impact one's daily life. What should be done in such a situation?
description: Hello teachers! I'm 29 years old and have been working for three years. I have noticed that my emotional responses are slow and it is affecting my life. Here's what happened: I am currently on a holiday and recently started learning to drive. Last week, my instructor suddenly did something inappropriate (watching inappropriate videos, using provocative language, and touching me) during the lesson. At that moment, my mind went blank and I forcefully pushed him away. It took me two days to realize what had happened and I felt angry! How could he treat me like this? I felt fearful afterwards because it posed a threat to my safety. Only then did I take action to warn him and change instructors. I have always been slower in my reactions since I was in school, but back then, I just thought of myself as being slow-paced in character. It was only after I started working that I noticed it takes me a few days to realize when I have been treated unfairly. This slowness creates an impression that I am easy to take advantage of, causing some distress. Some good friends of mine have also mentioned that I give off a cold first impression and it takes some time for me to show warmth. However, I am certain that I am not completely emotionally incapable. I can immediately feel emotions when it comes to people I trust, and even through text messages, I can feel the tenderness. I would like to know: 1) based on this initial assessment, could this be a disease or a psychological barrier? 2) What can I do to achieve timely responses?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, I want to give you a hug. From the description, it can be understood that you have a delayed reaction to certain dangerous and negative situations and emotionally you seem to be a slow-tempered person. These factors are starting to affect your life, and you wonder if it might be a psychological disorder. [A little bit of analysis and advice] 1. For now, it is important to immediately alleviate the negative impact of the delayed reaction on yourself, such as not being able to perceive danger in a timely manner. You could seek help from your family and friends. It would be best if you have a close friend with whom you have a good relationship, understanding and trust, someone willing to share life experiences with you. Tell them about strange or interesting events that happened to you or things that you don't understand the meaning of, allowing your friend to provide an objective judgment. 2. Develop a habit of reflecting on and reviewing your experiences. You can set aside some time to write in a journal every evening or every few days, recalling events and making reflections. By improving your ability to think, your thinking speed will gradually increase. 3. A slow reaction is not considered a typical psychological disorder, but if it is negatively impacting your life and work, it is best to seek help from a professional psychological counselor and find systematic methods to solve the problem.

question: "I am a 19-year-old female college freshman who feels hopeless and very distressed with life. What should I do?"
description: A 19-year-old girl, a freshman in a vocational college majoring in electronic commerce. She had amblyopia since childhood, resulting in blindness in her right eye and severe myopia of over 500 in her left eye. Her eyes are deformed and prone to eye fatigue. She has severe dental caries and average academic performance. She pursues perfection in her work but often feels incapable of doing things well, leading to low self-worth. She has experienced insomnia and vivid dreams for over five years and hasn't truly felt happy. She also struggles to maintain good relationships with her classmates. Since January, she has been dreaming about quarrels and negative evaluations from others almost every night. Her family wanted her to take medication but she didn't dare to since she hadn't seen a doctor. She often feels irritated and loses her temper due to things others say or do. In March, she was diagnosed with mild hyperthyroidism, but she is now better. She constantly recalls negative events, which keep looping in her mind. She thinks she can't do anything well or pass exams, and is easily influenced by negative comments from others. Thinking about the future, where she needs to advance to a university, she is worried that her eyes will deteriorate further, as she only has one functional eye, making her more prone to fatigue and fear. She remembers her parents saying that those with high myopia are fine, so she should be fine too, but she is scared.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development

answers.answer_text:
Hello, I hope my answer can bring you some useful insights. First of all, it's great to see that you have recognized the issues you are facing and have the desire to change. Now, after regret, it is important to actively seek change. Here are some small suggestions on how to boost your self-confidence: 

1. Understand yourself again and identify the reasons for your lack of confidence. Is it due to being introverted or shy, or do you feel inadequate in certain areas? Understanding the root causes will help you find more targeted methods to change yourself.

2. Emphasize your strengths. Once you have identified your strengths, make sure to fully utilize them. This will improve your self-identification and ultimately boost your confidence.

3. Avoid striving for perfection. Remember, nobody is perfect. Don't let setbacks completely negate your self-worth. Allowing yourself to sink into a sense of failure will only make you feel disappointed, frustrated, and even helpless. Instead, focus on your strengths and don't dwell solely on your weaknesses.

4. Accept yourself. No matter how you are, you are unique. Learn to be happy with yourself. For example, you may have labeled yourself as shy, which makes you hesitate to speak up in social situations. However, being shy doesn't mean you are strange or abnormal. Accept yourself for who you are, because you don't need everyone's approval, and you don't need to live like everyone else. Embrace the real you.

In the second part, confident appearance and demeanor matter. It is true that people are visual creatures, so your clothing and hairstyle can make an impact. Of course, I'm not suggesting you buy expensive clothes or get a fancy hairstyle, but instead, focus on being neat and presentable. Consider participating in courses, training programs, or joining clubs or organizations. Cultivating a hobby will make you feel more fulfilled. Finally, reading more can also be beneficial. As the saying goes, "In books, you can find a golden house and beautiful faces." Reading can enhance your inner qualities in ways that other methods may not be able to achieve.

I hope this can help you. If you have more questions or concerns, feel free to message me or follow our WeChat public account: Mentalhealth Pro.

question: How to persuade a long-distance friend who wants to commit suicide?
description: I went to work in a different place, and I don't have the opportunity to see her or accompany her while studying. I have done this kind of thing before and was rescued by the police, but I still want to commit suicide. I have social anxiety there and no relatives or friends. I don't want to go home due to conflicts with my family. I feel helpless and can't find a job there. I don't want to do anything and feel confused and lacking confidence in everything. She says there's nothing she cares about or wants. Nobody wants to believe, so let it be. Her family is not particularly concerned about this. How can I advise her as a long-distance friend?

answers.answer_text: Seeing your question, I feel that you are a very caring, kind, and warm person, and you are very concerned about your friend. Because you are working in a different place, you don't have the opportunity to be with your friend. Your friend has had suicidal thoughts before, luckily you were able to save them in time. However, your friend still has the desire to commit suicide, and you want to persuade her, but you don't know how to do it. Actually, the only one who can help oneself is oneself. Because, to untie a bell, the person who tied it must do it. Only when your friend has the willingness to seek help can the problem potentially be solved. From your description, I feel that your friend might want to be seen and cared for. But because you are not her, your description is just your perception. And I can only make assumptions based on your description, so it may not be accurate. I don't know if your friend is willing to receive psychological counseling or seek medical help? If possible, can you suggest that she seek timely medical or psychological counseling to address the related issues? It can help her find the root cause of the problem. If she herself has no such intention, as a friend, if she needs it, I suggest you can care for her in a way she can accept, help her get through the difficult times, and build confidence. You can suggest that she engage in exercise or practice meditation, as exercise or meditation can improve a person's mood. Regardless of what you do, you can only provide her with care and advice. As for what choices to make and how to act, what matters most is your friend's own willingness and decision.

question: What is the difference in controlling sexual desire before and after falling in love and getting married?
description: Regardless of whether one is single or not, it is important to learn how to control sexual desire. In the stage of being single, one may have limited knowledge and experience in terms of sexuality. What are the differences in terms of controlling sexual desire between this stage and the stage after entering a relationship or getting married and having sexual experiences?

answers.answer_text: Subject, hello, I am honored to have the opportunity to communicate with you! Sex is an ancient topic and a very common one, but due to factors such as our country's culture, we rarely discuss it. Sex is something that everyone has, and it is the foundation for the continuation of the species. After the age of 16 for males and 14 for females, they slowly begin to mature and have some understanding of sex. Parents, teachers, or peers need to provide guidance and popularize knowledge in this regard so that there won't be so many questions, allowing people to focus more on learning and life and reduce unnecessary worries. When single, it is important to control sexual desire. First of all, it is necessary to accept and understand that having sexual desires is normal, and there is no need to deliberately control it. When in a relationship or after getting married, it is also important to control sexual desire. If one has a partner, they can communicate and understand each other more, and there is no need to overly control it. May I ask why do you always want to control it (sexual desire)?

question: 25-year-old woman, in a relationship with another woman, has a tendency to throw things and push people during arguments. What should I do?
description: I and my partner (two girls) are in a foreign country. We have been together for almost four years. Similar incidents have happened before when we were together. In the past two years, she has broken three phones and damaged the necklace she gave me. These were all done when she couldn't control her anger. Although I am the one who starts the fights, it always ends with her breaking things. I don't want to escalate the conflict, so I always avoid it when it comes to this point. But today, she started pushing me and grabbed my collar. I'm a bit scared and don't dare to go home. I also don't have anywhere else to go in this foreign country, and I don't want to go to my colleagues as it would spread rumors. I can't buy a plane ticket back to my home country now because of the pandemic, and the apartment we are living in is under my name. I paid for it and signed a one-year contract, so breaking it would incur a penalty. I don't know what to do now.
keywords: Love, sense of security, argument, love management

answers.answer_text: Each person has different reactions when their emotions fluctuate greatly. Some people choose to escape, some people choose to throw things, and some people choose to argue. 1. What is the reason for each argument? In fact, many arguments in life are caused by small things. These small things may seem insignificant, but when they explode, they will explode like small grenades, suddenly bursting out. Therefore, we can simply think back to how two people usually deal with problems. Have they engaged in self-reflection and self-improvement? If both parties insist on their own arguments and are unwilling to compromise, and each argument is avoided, then the problems will only increase. Therefore, we can first ask ourselves if there is a possibility of continuing this relationship. If so, will both parties be willing to make changes? If not, how can we minimize the damage? 2. Give each other some time. I don't know if the other person is aware of their own problems. Every time violence occurs, it does bring us some shadows and harm. If possible, we can give each other a period of calm. If the house we live in has two bedrooms, we can temporarily live separately for a while. We can also reflect on our own problems, think about each other's good qualities, and think about our own shortcomings. We can also record the things we think the other person has done well, and consider why we want to be together and how to solve problems when they arise. When necessary, we can give each other a simple hug and say, "Can we temporarily calm down, take a few deep breaths, and not blame each other, okay?" If, after trying various methods, it is still not suitable, then we can have a frank talk with each other, after all, a forced melon will not be sweet. The world and I love you.

After reading your question carefully, I feel sorry for your situation. I'm sending you a heartfelt hug and hoping to give you more strength while comforting you. The essence of love remains unchanged, whether it is between same-sex or opposite-sex partners. However, romantic relationships between same-sex partners can be more sensitive and require understanding and support from each other. Both sides may face more pressure. But don't worry, this process will also help you mature and deepen your understanding of women and yourself.

You mentioned that you are the one who always initiates fights. So, can you try to control your emotions? Can you try a relatively calm way of communication? A good partnership is the result of cooperation between both sides. Having two reasonable partners doesn't guarantee harmony, and having one dominant and one submissive partner doesn't mean they won't get along well. Psychologist Chen Haixian once said that a good partner is not determined by the individuals themselves, but by how well they cooperate when they are together. Communication between partners is like dancing in pairs. Just looking at their dance moves alone cannot determine if they are good or bad. What matters is their coordination. The dance steps between partners, or their habitual ways of cooperation, form the relationship pattern between them.

Chen Haixian believes that good relationship patterns often have two characteristics: positive symmetry and effective complementarity. Positive symmetry means that both partners inspire each other with positive language and behavior. For example, suppose your partner says to you, "These past four years haven't been easy. Thank you for always being by my side." When you hear this, you respond, "You have also been with me. Having you makes me feel at ease." This mutual recognition will inspire and create a virtuous cycle. In our interactions, we should focus more on the good parts of the relationship and affirm each other. When problems arise, try not to blame or criticize each other, which can avoid stimulating each other to release more negative relationship information and forming negative symmetry. If this happens, the more you argue, the angrier you both become, leading to violence. This can create a vicious cycle. Effective complementarity means that one person's words and actions provoke a completely different response from the other, creating a mutual complement. For example, suppose you see your partner getting angry during an argument. Instead of continuing to argue, you stop and wait for them to calm down before communicating and talking to them. This is also an effective complement. When conflicts arise in a relationship, don't provoke each other. Many times, the violence from the other person is likely triggered by the negative relationship pattern between you both.

How can you improve the relationship pattern? Chen Haixian believes that two things are essential: "cooperation" and "cycle." "Cooperation" does not mean that we should make efforts on our own to match the other person. Thinking this way would attribute all the problems to the other person. We need to see how our behavior influences the other person in the relationship. When you are not aware of how your actions affect the other person, you tend to push all the blame to the other person, thinking that as long as the other person changes, everything will be fine. However, you rarely consider what you can change to improve the way you interact with each other. The so-called "cycle" means that one person's behavior is stimulated by the other person. Therefore, your change can also lead to changes in the other person. For example, when you no longer provoke conflicts or use a relatively calm way to communicate with your partner, their temper may also improve. You can try asking yourself, "What did I do to make her become like this?" "What can I do to improve our current way of getting along?" Avoiding communication will not solve the problem. Try to face it and improve it. If you feel unsafe, you can try to invite her out, to a restaurant or park, for a conversation. Treat it as a date, go out together to relax, chat, and wait for her to calm down before returning home together.

Hello. Seeing your question, I want to give you a warm hug first, and I hope my answer can help you. It seems that you want to change your current situation, as your partner has a temper and even tends to be violent, which scares you a bit. If we want her to change, we need to understand the root cause of her temperament and find the right solution. In many cases I have seen, such temperaments are usually influenced by their family upbringing. If the father frequently abuses the mother or the children, the child's violent tendencies can manifest in two ways: one is being violent towards others, and the other is self-harm, or self-violence. Usually, children who grow up in a home with domestic violence have uncontrollable violence. They are aware of the horror of violence and do not want to be violent, but they simply cannot control it. If your partner frequently throws things and pushes people, she falls into the category of being violent towards others. Does she also engage in self-harm? Does she constantly have self-inflicted wounds on her body? You can observe or ask her directly. When she is calm, gently communicate with her. If she has feelings for you, she actually does not want to be violent towards you, but she cannot control herself. Generally, she will feel some regret afterwards. So, ask her if she realizes her problem - her tendency towards violence - and ask her if it is because of her family upbringing. If it is indeed the case, then she also does not want to be like this. It will be relatively easy for you to persuade her to change. You can tell her about your feelings - fear. Let her know that this behavior affects the relationship between the two of you. Changing this temperament is not easy and will take time. First, try to understand the difficulties her family has faced, and control your own emotions, avoiding fights and angering her. Secondly, even if you don't know what to do and she becomes angry again, having violent tendencies, you should still be patient with her and at this time, try to calm her down: "Darling, please calm down. Remember, you said you don't want to be like this. Why have you started again? Come on, calm down." You need to bring her out of her angry state. What should you do now? Maybe find a hotel to stay in for a few days. When you feel she has calmed down a bit, start trying to communicate with her. During the conversation, apologize first, and it would be good to buy a gift and have it delivered to the place you are staying to make her happy. If you still want to continue this relationship, it may require more effort and understanding on your part. Of course, not continuing may bring you relief. You can decide for yourself. I hope I can help resolve your confusion. The world and I love you.

From the description given by the poster, I can sense their fear, worry, dismay, and helplessness... First, I want to send a warm virtual hug to the poster, who is far away from their home country. I hope to provide you with a bit of comfort in your time of helplessness. The poster mentioned at the end, "I don't know what to do." To be honest, no one really knows what to do because this is your life, not theirs. I hope the following analysis can help you. 
1. Throwing things: The poster mentioned that their girlfriend often throws things when she is angry, and they tend to avoid the situation when this happens. First, this behavior pattern of the girlfriend likely stems from her past experiences, where she might have encountered similar situations, and this behavior pattern proved to be successful for her. The poster's avoidance behavior further reinforces this pattern. Have you ever communicated about this issue with your girlfriend when both of you are relatively calm and the atmosphere is more harmonious? Have you clearly expressed to her that you do not like this behavior pattern and your temporary avoidance is to prevent further escalation of conflicts, rather than admitting defeat? The fact that this situation has occurred multiple times in the span of four years suggests that you haven't had effective communication with your girlfriend about this issue. Therefore, I suggest that you seriously communicate with her about this issue, at least making sure she is aware of your dislike or even fear of this behavior pattern. 
2. Physical aggression: Similarly, this is a problem that needs to be urgently resolved. Although the first time it was just pushing and grabbing the collar, it is easy to imagine that subsequent actions will escalate rapidly if they are not firmly stopped. The poster mentioned feeling "a little scared and afraid to go home" after such behavior occurred. Did you immediately leave home when your girlfriend displayed this behavior? If so, then maybe you can temporarily find a public place or stay in a hotel for a while. Take some time to calm down and think about how you want to handle this situation. If it was the day after the argument, for example, after work, and you didn't want to go home because of the previous argument and your partner's behavior, then your issue might stem from not knowing how you want to handle this relationship. 
3. Trigger: The poster mentioned, "Every time we argue, it's because of something I did." This makes me curious - did you intentionally provoke the conflict? Or is it that you know your words or actions will incite an argument, but you can't control yourself? And once your partner exhibits some uncontrollable behavior, you immediately resort to avoidance, presenting yourself as a frightened weakling. If this pattern keeps recurring, do you also have a behavior pattern of "provoking the argument, waiting for the other person to lose control, and then avoiding"? Please reflect on whether you have learned this behavior pattern from previous experiences. If it is not a learned behavior, it might be easier to resolve. The prerequisite for resolving it, however, is that you become aware of your behavior pattern and are willing to work on it. Ultimately, the main problem lies in what you really want. Do you want to improve the way you two interact, or do you want to end this relationship? Regardless of what you want, I want to remind you that "safety comes first." Even in an unfamiliar foreign land, there are still many sources of help available. Don't always imagine yourself to be in a "lonely and helpless" situation. I hope the above suggestions are helpful to you.

Hello, OP, first, let me give you a big hug~ Suggestions: ① Self-control: OP said that although they start the arguments every time, it always ends with the girl throwing things, and OP doesn't want to escalate the conflict, so they usually avoid it at this point. Therefore, OP unintentionally creates conflicts but is unable to resolve them and doesn't want the situation to worsen, resulting in the current state. OP can ask themselves questions like: | What did I say to cause such a strong reaction from the girl? | Was my way of speaking extreme? After thinking about it, OP can avoid communicating with the girl in these circles. ② Wait for her to calm down: OP said that they have been together for nearly four years, and similar incidents have occurred more than once during their time together. Within two years, she has thrown and damaged three phones and broke the necklace she gave as a gift when she couldn't control her anger. From this perspective, it seems that the girl's emotions are easily agitated and uncontrollable. In this situation, no matter what measures OP takes, she won't listen and may even escalate things further due to OP's opposing opinions. So everything should be addressed after she calms down. OP can first stay in another hotel for a few days to calm their own emotions and understand their own thoughts. ③ Come up with measures: After the girl has cooled down, OP can express their fear of dealing with her outbursts, and then establish rules with her. If she acts the same way again, there should be "punishment" measures. For example, the two can easily talk about the things they are unhappy with towards each other, and OP can bring up the issue of her outbursts. And they can plan that if OP makes the same mistake again or if the girl is unable to control herself again, they will contribute money to a joint account, which can be used as a travel fund or something else. ④ Follow-up plans: All the above measures are based on OP's desire to continue with the girl. How does OP really feel about these outbursts deep down? If OP wants to continue with the girl, they need to reflect on whether their words were inappropriate and have a calm conversation with the girl, asking her what specifically caused her to develop this kind of personality. Once they find out, they can try to help her resolve her issues and express their love and understanding towards her. If OP no longer wants to continue, they should still wait until the girl calms down before telling her about this decision. If they can't bear it anymore, letting go is also a kind of relief. Lastly, warm wishes to OP for a happy life and fulfilling love.

question: What are some good study methods to read a book and take note of the key points?
description: I am reading a book on procrastination psychology. I've read it once and took notes, but I feel that many parts are still unclear. When I look at my messy notes, I start organizing them again, trying to connect all the methods mentioned in the book. I feel that the book is not very clear in its content. It starts by helping me understand my own procrastination tendencies (through self-reflection) and then suggests a one-week experiment. I feel like the book is just repeating common sense, explaining the factors of procrastination and providing some small techniques. I think of summarizing the procrastination factors as headings and taking notes for each technique. Once I organize the experiment from the week, it's almost like I've finished the book. I've realized that the content of the ebook I downloaded online is slightly different, but overall the same. On the app, it has been revised and looks more organized, without as many stories. I'm thinking of buying the book on the app (since there are many versions of the physical book and I don't understand why they all have the same author and cover, but the size feels more like a manual). I'm thinking of buying an ebook and reading it again. I've gone through the process of reading, taking notes, and organizing them three times already, but I'm still considering buying another ebook. Is it necessary? Do you have any good reading methods or note-taking formats that can help me remember the key points by just reading it once?
keywords: Growth, self-growth, work and study, student growth

answers.answer_text: Hello! Actually, if I say it's necessary, would you continue to do it? If I say it's not necessary, would you be more determined that there are deficiencies in your study methods? I suggest that you follow your own feelings. Whether this study method is really suitable for you, after all, it varies from person to person. Other people's advice can only be auxiliary and cannot make the final decision. Many times when we read a book, we are focused on the present feelings and once we finish reading, it's done. After a while, maybe we remember a little about the characters and plot, or maybe we forget everything completely. This is actually normal. "But you can go further: read while reflecting on what is good about this book, why is it good? What is not good, how can it be improved? What can I learn from it, what can I think about?" For example, recently I've been reading "So, is everything the fault of childhood?" I wanted to read this book to understand the influence of my family of origin on me. (Reading with a purpose) What's good about this book is that it will help me understand myself better and also introduce me to many knowledge areas I haven't encountered before. What's not good is that it has a lot of technical terms, not many examples, and personally, I find it a bit dry. It would be better if it could include more examples from everyday life. I can learn from it how to analyze myself from my family of origin, how to get to know myself again, and how to build good relationships with others. (During the process, I use mind maps to jot down important information from the book, and I also recommend you to try it. Mind maps can be done with software or handwritten, depending on your preference.) So, many times, what we read from a book is not necessarily important. What you think during this process is the most important. Because in this process, you are thinking and internalizing knowledge. Remember, when we are learning, the most difficult part is not collecting or organizing reading notes, but internalizing. Internalizing is the process of turning information into knowledge and then into the ability to solve problems. This process is not easy, so much so that many people feel like they've read a lot of books but don't feel like they've learned anything, it's a bit superficial. I recommend you to read Mr. Cheng Jia's "Study Effectively". I've been reading it recently too. Let's study well together. I hope this can help you. Have a good morning, afternoon, and night.

Hello there, you are a very serious person!! Warmly feels that in regards to the reading method you mentioned, it is effective to read the table of contents before reading the book. The table of contents is like a mind map summarized by the author. Of course, it's not just a quick glance, but rather to imagine based on the table of contents, think about what each chapter is about, and note down any doubts or questions next to the corresponding chapter. When you come across those parts while reading the book, read and savor them carefully. Warmly likes to make marks in the book, especially for books with strong academic nature. Of course, if you think marking in the book is messy, you can skip this step. Because Warmly feels that taking notes often involves copying the content of the book word by word. Without your own understanding, blindly copying the book may not have a good effect. Moreover, our thinking will focus more on copying, without deeper thinking. Warmly believes that reading is for the purpose of practical application, rather than just reading for the sake of it. A good book is definitely not simply expressing the author's views. It has been refined over time, and can still inspire modern readers in the present. Warmly likes to let their imagination run wild when reading, relating many things in their own life to the theories mentioned in the book. Warmly enjoys reading in a relaxed state, because "without the distraction of music, without the toil of documents". Moreover, when you are relaxed, the utilitarian aspect is not as strong, and you may achieve unexpected results. Finally, I hope this is helpful to you!

question: 16-year-old girl, starting from a very young age, fantasizes about one or several non-existent people?
description: I am quite sensitive and stubborn in my heart, and I am unwilling to confide in others no matter what happens. I feel really uncomfortable inside, so I imagine having a "sister" to accompany me and talk to her every day. Later, I gradually perfected her, from her name and background to how we met. Her identity also changed from sister to lover, and I have always controlled and balanced it with normal life. However, recently, I have encountered some bad things, and she became somewhat uncontrollable. The things she tells me have become more and more negative. She now tells me that nobody loves me, only she can be with me all the time. She says I'm crazy, and in my consciousness, we even fight each other, but she always suppresses me. Now my behavior and way of thinking are becoming more and more like hers. I feel like she wants to imprison me. Am I sick? What should I do?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: I have carefully read your question, and your current confusion is about not being able to control the person you have created in your imagination, which has even started to seriously affect you and worry if you are actually sick. In your question, I can feel the importance of this "sister" to you when you feel lonely and uncomfortable being alone, but find it difficult to reach out and communicate with others. She is like the other half of you inside your body, where you understand each other without words and deeply trust each other. This is the only place where you can find solace. In the presence of this "sister," you feel safe and don't have to worry about the harm and troubles that exist in real-life relationships between people. This is your corner and yours alone, reserved for your "sister." However, you are aware that all of this is just a figment of your imagination, and that the "sister" can only exist in your mind. What's heartwarming is that even though you know that this "sister" is just a product of your own mind, you still embrace her warmly. However, you are still confused as to why your "sister" has recently become somewhat uncontrollable. Perhaps you have noticed that you are undergoing changes, which are the growth and transformation within yourself. Just like when we were children and fantasized about being a doctor or a teacher, except we didn't expand and enrich our imagination to that extent, but this internal "object" has always silently influenced us until one day it emerges from within and becomes our true self. This is the growth of our soul. Therefore, there is no need to worry. On the contrary, you can calm down and listen to what message this "sister" wants to convey to you. If you truly experience this transformative growth, I wonder what you would say to your past self? You can hold a farewell ceremony for yourself and truly learn to grow and respect your growth. Of course, we hope that you can step into the real world, hone and improve yourself in the state and feeling of the "sister."

Hello! When children don't have playmates, they may play and interact with toys, and they may also communicate and play with imaginary companions. In children's movies, the protagonists often have a little sprite as their companion. So it is normal for you to imagine having a sister to accompany you when you were young. Now that you are 16 years old, it is a period when your sense of self begins to form, and you start to think about many questions. For example, who am I? What kind of person am I? What kind of person do I want to be? In this process, you care a lot about how others perceive you, and whether their perception matches your own. What are your strengths and weaknesses? What are your abilities? These thoughts trouble you. Because you don't want to confide in others, you can't find a way to relieve your inner anguish. Therefore, you have continued to use the methods from your childhood, letting your imaginary sister grow with you. The conflict between you and your sister is actually a conflict between your subjective self (i.e. your sister) and your objective self. The subjective self refers to how you see yourself. The objective self refers to how others see you. If you feel that your sister is becoming more and more negative, it indicates that you are currently dissatisfied with yourself because others think your negativity and negative energy are not good. And you cannot find a way to change the situation. Therefore, you feel like your sister is increasingly out of control, but it is actually because you can't control yourself. So what should we do? First, reconcile with your sister. Understand why she cannot be controlled, and once you accept her, you accept yourself. Second, communicate with your sister using positive, encouraging words. Third, in real life, dare to find someone you can trust and confide in them about your thoughts, seeking help and understanding, gradually distancing yourself from your imaginary sister. Fourth, you should recognize that you are now older and have your own independent thoughts and emotions. You can grow by learning and using the power of knowledge. Fifth, if you can't solve the problem yourself, seek help from a psychologist. I hope I can help you. Best wishes!

Hello OP, after reading your description, it seems like your situation is quite concerning. Research in psychology has found that when people are unable to cope with difficulties in their real life or can't tolerate emotional distress, they may temporarily detach themselves from reality and imagine how they would handle those difficulties, creating a world of fantasy where they can find inner balance and achieve satisfaction that they can't experience in real life. Based on your description, when you feel lonely, you imagine this sister figure who can accompany you and talk to you, and later she transforms into a romantic partner. Essentially, you are using fantasy to fulfill needs that cannot be met in reality. This is a defense mechanism that you have developed since a young age. However, from a perspective of mental health development, fantasy is a more primitive defense mechanism that is commonly used by younger children. As we grow older, we should gradually adapt to the real world and transition from fantasy to reality. If you continue to stay in the world of fantasy and even struggle to distinguish between fantasy and reality, it can be quite dangerous. As you mentioned, when your state of mind is not stable, she becomes somewhat uncontrollable, and her words become increasingly negative. In your consciousness, you may even have fights with her, but your behavior and way of thinking more and more resemble her. You feel that she wants to imprison you. All of these are fantasies that blur the boundary between fantasy and reality, and it is something that requires serious attention from you! My suggestion is to seek psychological counseling. Pay more attention to your breathing and the sensations in your body, engage your five senses - eyes, ears, mouth, nose, and body. Be more aware of and accept yourself, live in the present moment, return to reality, and experience what is true!

Hello! Actually, in life, most people have their own fantasies. But as long as it can be controlled by one's own will, it is fine. However, from your question, it seems that the object of your recent fantasy is no longer under control. Moreover, at present, this person you fantasize about seems to be becoming more specific, as if it truly exists in your heart. So I would like to ask a question, have you been experiencing auditory hallucinations? You mentioned that your will is not being controlled, and in your thoughts you argue with her, and she always says negative things. This sounds like auditory hallucinations. I suggest you go to a professional hospital and have a medical examination. Don't put too much pressure on yourself, relax more. Try to find friends in reality, communicate more with people in real life, don't immerse yourself too much in fantasies, as this can easily lead to psychological problems. You can also try activities like running, drawing, listening to music, etc., to help relax and distract your attention. I hope this helps you, keep going!

question: Want to improve myself, but having conflicts with my husband, feeling misunderstood in my pursuit for success.

keywords: Marriage, concept of marriage, marriage management

answers.answer_text: Hello! Based on your description and comprehensive analysis, I support your perseverance in learning and enriching yourself. The pace of social development is now very fast, and the knowledge we possess today may be replaced by new knowledge tomorrow. If we don't actively explore and learn, we will quickly fall behind the pace of social development and eventually be eliminated by society. question: Feeling that a memory is not real, but unable to defeat it logically?
description: I just realized something very important, and I feel like it's a false memory. However, I can't convince myself logically. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Memories are generally related to emotions and can be activated by situations. Memory is the brain's ability to recognize, retain, reproduce, or recognize things based on past experiences. When memories are false, the process of recognition is affected if our emotions are too tense or we experience excessive stress, stimulating the brain and causing hormonal imbalances. Alternatively, if there is poor circulation or reasons like experiencing chills or palpitations during sleep, hormonal imbalance may occur, preventing the brain from resting completely. Furthermore, dissatisfaction with the current situation in the subconscious mind may lead to a sense of false memory. It is also possible that memories are "misplaced" during the storage process, referring to the process of meaningful encoding where the coding is mistakenly assigned. This can also create a sense of falseness. You can try to relax and then recall that portion of memory. May the words accompany you.

question: 13-year-old girl, no emotional impact during the day, but becomes distraught and tears up at night, with thoughts of self-harm.
description: I have experienced many bad things around me, and I try to escape from them, but I find myself getting deeper and deeper into it. I have been suffering from insomnia for a long time, crying, and having unstable emotions. I cannot control my temper in front of my parents, but I am very good-tempered towards others. I use self-harm as a way to release stress, and I pretend to hide my emotions, becoming disinterested in everything. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, in your life, many bad things have happened and you want to escape. But you have also realized that escaping cannot truly solve the problem, right? Our minds are very complex, like an iceberg. What we can consciously perceive and be aware of is often only a small part above the water's surface, while the larger part is submerged, unseen by us. The problems we dare not face and choose to avoid have not truly disappeared; they have just been suppressed deep within our hearts, where we cannot see them. However, just because we cannot see them does not mean they do not exist; they still deeply impact us. During the day, we may still have rational control, but at night, these suppressed parts often emerge more recklessly. Your insomnia, unstable emotions, tears, and difficulty controlling your temper may all be expressions of these suppressed emotions. I wonder what exactly the "bad things" you mentioned are. Is there a better way than choosing to run away? For example, can you talk to someone about it or seek help from others? You may lose your temper with your parents because they are the closest people to you, and you feel safest in front of them. Perhaps your suppressed emotions are related to your parents, and they are more likely to trigger your emotional switch. So, instead of getting angry, can you have a good conversation with your parents? Expressing your anger is your way of communication, but in your parents' eyes, they cannot understand it. They only see your temper, but they cannot see the pain in your heart. Self-harm and disguising yourself are just temporary solutions that do not address the root cause. If these issues are already out of control and beyond your own ability to regulate, I suggest letting your parents take you to see a mental health professional. Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

question: After breaking up, are there any medications that can alleviate your emotions?

question: How do I console a girl who was sexually assaulted when she was a child?
description: As a novice counselor, how can I comfort a girl who was sexually abused in her childhood? I feel so heartbroken after listening to her experience. As a fellow girl, why did she have to go through such a thing?

answers.answer_text: Hello, may I help you? I'm glad to answer your questions. I've read your question. I know that you have studied psychology and are currently a novice counselor, and the visitor you encountered does indeed need help for the trauma she has experienced, which will likely require a long-term process. If you want to conduct in-depth counseling, it is recommended to do so under the supervision of a professional teacher. As a novice counselor, we can help her with simple "bandaging". In your question, you expressed sympathy and sorrow for this little girl, which is understandable. However, as counselors, we should be aware that these emotions can bring us potential problems. [Potential Problems] First, these emotions may affect the normal progress of our counseling sessions. In psychology, this phenomenon is called "countertransference," which refers to the counselor resonating with the emotions and feelings in the visitor's experiences. If these emotions are not dealt with in a timely manner, they can easily affect ourselves and prevent us from effectively helping the visitor. If these emotions accumulate for a long time, they may also have adverse effects on our mental health as counselors. Here, I recommend a psychological technique called "detachment," which is to have a good awareness of the negative emotions that arise in us during counseling. When we find that our emotions are similar to those of the visitor, we should remind ourselves, "These emotions come from the visitor, not from me. I should prevent these emotions from affecting me." Secondly, these emotions can convey our sympathy to the visitor, which may make the visitor feel that her experience is shameful and unacceptable. As counselors, we have studied psychology and need to distinguish between general emotional experiences and the counseling relationship. Although sympathy can convey care and help, because of the counselor's special identity, if sympathy is conveyed, it means that we have a negative evaluation of the visitor's experience, and we believe that the visitor's experience is shameful and unacceptable. This potential message transmission makes it more difficult for the visitor to accept her own experience and is not conducive to her recovery from the painful experience. Therefore, as counselors, we should approach any experience and issue from the visitor with a neutral attitude, without any evaluative attitude or emotions, even if the visitor tells us something that makes us angry. We must maintain a neutral attitude in our questioning and counseling. Only when we, as counselors, feel that this experience is not a big deal can the visitor truly find a sense of security and identification from the counselor and gradually be guided out of the shadows to embrace a better future.

question: 37-year-old woman, why have I been feeling inexplicably sad all of a sudden in the past six months?
description: Feel that the first half of life left behind many regrets, but life is already more than halfway, so it's too late to change. Often regretting my decisions, could it be a bit of depression?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I think there are too many regrets in the first half of my life. Nothing has developed in the direction I imagined, and I often regret the decisions I have made and envision the outcome of another decision. There are always regrets in life, but without regrets, you won't know how things would have developed according to what you wanted. Actually, when I saw your title, I had a question: how can a 37-year-old woman consider her life half over? Everyone defines their own life, so why is the life you defined for yourself so short? As time passes, what remains are deep imprints and many scars on your body, along with a weathered heart. The regrets I wanted to leave you, deeply regretted but unable to change, can also bring learning. It is through making that choice that you learned the answer you wanted, deeply engraved in your mind, laying the foundation for your future choices. Life is halfway over, unable to be changed, but there are changes that you have yet to understand. Pondering your own life after several decades have passed, if it doesn't go as you wished, at this point in time, perhaps unexpected setbacks have appeared on your life path, and you have realized that you made the wrong choices. Imagine the scene when you made that choice. Did it bring you happiness and joy, even if it was fleeting? Every choice has its pros and cons, just like choosing the science track for the college entrance exam. But if your grades have not improved, you may regret why you didn't choose the humanities track. However, for that student, memory was not their strong point, and their logical thinking abilities could earn more points. It's just that they did not utilize that period of time well - not quite at their prime, yet unable to retire peacefully. But this age is the most critical period for you to make changes. You can't abandon everything, but please love yourself. The past can't be repeated, but you can still make changes for yourself. Even if you may bear a heavy burden of responsibility, the road ahead is still long. How can you live for yourself if you let this burden crush you? Suggestions: 1. Start by setting a goal for your future path and gradually work towards achieving it. 2. If you don't have a goal, try exploring a direction that you like and can accept, and find your life goal.

Life is inevitably filled with many regrets; not many people can say they have never regretted anything. Recently, I heard a teacher say that our brains actually have biases when it comes to memories of the past, and there are often negative biases, especially when it comes to self-evaluation. Once a negative evaluation is formed, the brain continuously organizes "evidence" to prove it, thus weaving a lot of evidence that we are not good enough. However, from an objective perspective, this may not necessarily be true. For example, if you were to ask a trustworthy and impartial friend, they would evaluate you based on your objective achievements and so on. Rationally speaking, knowing that this brings many undesirable effects, we unconsciously spend a lot of time and energy on this matter. We must train ourselves to frequently recognize this point and be aware of its impact. The past can only be remembered and cannot be changed, but the future is uncertain and can be different. Instead of expending energy dwelling on the past, it is better to spend energy envisioning the future. Imagine if this current worry suddenly disappeared and no longer affected your life, and everything that followed developed as you wished, that would be an impossible miracle. What would you see yourself as in ten years? What kind of life would you have? And how does this miracle relate to the first small thing you do when you open your eyes tomorrow? What is that thing? Who will be the first to notice the difference in you?

OP, everyone's life will have many regrets, and everyone will have things they haven't accomplished or ideal states they haven't reached. Perhaps when looking back on the past, these regrets become the most dazzling things on your journey, they can help you recall many experiences. They may also serve as warning signs on your future path, helping you reduce some regrets and regrets in your future life. There is still a long life waiting for you to explore in the future, and these past regrets can help you more keenly discover opportunities or help you try not to miss out on things. In the future, you may be more cautious and serious in striving for what you want, while also gaining more experience. I hope you can relax physically and mentally in your daily life. The past is the past, and when facing similar situations in the future, you can think back to past regrets to help you accomplish things more effectively. However, maybe don't easily dwell on or ponder about it in your daily life, as it may make you fall into the pain and regret of reminiscence. Best wishes!

question: The motivation to learn English sometimes fluctuates, and it feels like the more I study, the more tired I get.
description: I have been working for seven years after graduating from college. I really liked English when I was in college, and now I want to learn English in my spare time.
