So I bought an online course. But why do I feel more and more tired when I study during normal times? I feel particularly sleepy when learning new words and phrases. However, when I try to read English books before bedtime, I feel wide awake. It's like when I want to be awake, I feel tired, and when I don't want to be awake, I feel energized. What's wrong with me? Can you give me some advice, experts? Thank you!

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear author. It's nice to meet you. First of all, I really admire your motivation. Not everyone can pick up past knowledge like you do. However, I think learning English now must be very different from before, at least in terms of learning environment and mindset, so it's understandable that you are having some difficulties adjusting.-----------------------------------------------------During your college years, you liked English a lot, but it has been seven years since graduation. Now, during your free time, you bought an online course and wanted to continue learning. However, you found that you get increasingly tired when studying. In occupational physiology, there is a description that "fatigue" and "fatigue-like state" are actually different. One is the actual feeling of energy being exhausted and projected by the body, and the other is an individual stress state caused by little change in the work environment, including decreased alertness and boredom. And both of them can create a feeling of fatigue. I used to experience the same thing during a long period of learning English. I spent money and treated it as a task that had to be completed. Moreover, the process of learning new words was very boring, which ultimately triggered a stress state: I slept enough, but felt sleepy as soon as I started studying. Of course, this is also related to the mindset you hold: you may have been more focused and dedicated to studying in college because you had an academic reason that required you to learn English, and the positive feedback was also quicker. But now, having a job, learning English is actually an extra thing, not a necessity. When it becomes something you have to do (because you bought the course), there is resistance in your heart, and the delayed feedback creates a vicious cycle of resistance and "feeling tired". However, the English book you read at night is a continuous argument, not a few isolated words and phrases, so the level of boredom is reduced. And when we no longer see it as a task that must be completed, the pressure is reduced, and our more emotional favoritism may be aroused, so you become more spirited the more you read it.-----------------------------------------------------Based on my personal life experience, I hope these thoughts will be helpful to you. It is very important to find a goal or reason to persist in learning. If you still consider learning English as a leisure activity, with a mindset of being able to learn or not, the situation of getting more and more tired may not improve. For example, deciding to take an exam and setting a goal will give you a direction to strive for. Choose a learning method that suits you. You feel more energized when reading English books, so reading books may be a suitable learning method for you. Learning new words and phrases is already a very boring process, and you have also devoted energy to your job since you graduated many years ago. Therefore, a suitable, enjoyable, and flexible learning method is even more important, such as listening to English songs or speeches. Give yourself a sense of ritual when studying, clear the desk, switch your phone to airplane mode, and then quietly give yourself 45 minutes of uninterrupted study time. This is also a way to concentrate. Finally, if you have trouble sleeping, you can try doing some bedtime yoga or meditation. I hope my thoughts can be helpful to you.

Hello, I will try to provide a few explanations from a psychoanalytic perspective. Seeing your state of learning English, I can imagine you dozing off when you see English books or words, which is very cute! I think this is also the state that everyone who wants to learn English but struggles with it experiences. So let me do a little analysis: not being able to learn English well may be due to a poor relationship with English or a poor relationship with learning. Why is it not good? Because since childhood, there has never been a time when you studied for yourself. You completed homework for the teacher, took exams for your parents, and did summer homework. None of it was for your own curiosity and interest. Try to repair and heal your relationship with "learning", just like you did when you fell in love. From the initial acquaintance to getting along, from getting along to falling in love, and then being in love. Have a relationship with this "student" named "learning" without breaking up, plan a few imperfect "dates," create some occasional "surprises," and prepare some "gifts" for them. The relationship will gradually warm up, and the immediate effect of learning will start to appear. Not being able to learn English well may be because we fear betraying our native language's defense. Teacher Zeng Qifeng once told a little story: after teaching for over 30 years and visiting various places around the world, he still retains a Hubei accent, and his Mandarin has never been very good. The reason is that his subconscious needs to hold onto loyalty to himself and to Hubei. Otherwise, he may feel guilty for betraying his native language and culture, and the internal social morality (the superego) may punish and suppress him. When we see this reason in our subconscious, we can understand our confusion and anxiety in not being able to learn English well. We can tell ourselves that learning English will not cause our superego to suppress or punish us, but rather, it will allow us to better disseminate culture, our thoughts, feelings, etc. Then you will gradually find yourself on the path to learning English. Thank you for meeting, and I look forward to your acceptance.

Title: Hello! I heard that you have picked up your love for learning English and are interested in studying through online courses. However, you feel that your motivation to learn is sometimes strong and sometimes weak, and you don't have control over it, right? Why not compare your current learning environment with the past? In the past, there were several external factors that were beneficial, such as face-to-face teaching from teachers to help with study plans and progress, studying with classmates, and the motivation provided by exams as goals. Now, online courses can barely replace teachers, and these two external factors, classmates and exams, are not as clear. If the online course has a learning community, you may find the feeling of "classmates" there. If the online course does not have a platform or forum for communication, you can also try going to other online communities where English enthusiasts gather to explore and gain insights on their learning methods, recommended reading materials, and their learning experiences. This way, you can broaden your horizons and share the benefits that come from learning together. Ideally, online courses should have a course framework and unit tests, which can be fully utilized to guide your learning progress. However, please be mindful not to progress too quickly. It is more appropriate to choose a pace that is suitable for your leisure learning. After all, unlike when you were a student, learning is now only done after work, and you have less energy and time compared to before, so it is important to manage the pace of your learning. Perhaps you need some time to find the right pace, so even if your learning progress is inconsistent in the early stages of taking online courses, you don't have to worry too much. As long as your interest in learning remains, you naturally won't easily give up on learning and will have perseverance. This means that even if you are not consciously aware of it, as long as you persist in learning, you are embodying confidence. Through patient perseverance, you will find the learning pace that suits you. Additionally, in terms of learning methods, you can also categorize the learning contents and allocate time for studying based on the different content. For example, reading before bed is suitable, while other free time before bed may be better spent on online courses. Because online course learning can be more stressful compared to reading, it may not be suitable for the relaxed state of mind needed before bed.

Hello. I can see your love for English. Otherwise, you wouldn't be so energized at night reading English books. After all, people are full of energy when they're doing something they love. Regarding online courses, they can become like lullabies. This can only mean that the teaching method of the online course you signed up for didn't suit you or even appeal to you. I am an example myself. During my free time, I signed up for an online course, but the teaching method didn't engage me. After being at home during the pandemic for more than half a year, I didn't feel like studying. Later, I signed up for another online course at a different training institution that I really enjoyed. Even now, despite being busy with work, I continue to study every day, even when I'm tired at night. I feel that if the teaching method doesn't click with you, it's better not to study at all. Otherwise, it will wear down your motivation and dampen your enthusiasm for English. Find a learning method that you can connect with, and look for courses that cater to your learning habits. It may be a waste of some money, but you can regain your hope for English. Good luck.

I think the questioner can change their language learning method. Memorizing vocabulary and taking online courses are too focused on exams and can be very painful. Language learning should ultimately be applied in daily life to remember it well, without becoming too dull. If you're not in a hurry to take a test, you can completely learn a language by watching American TV shows, reading original novels, and conversing with native speakers. Then, you can consolidate what you've learned by rephrasing or writing down the content you've seen in your own language. Like the questioner, if you feel drowsy when memorizing vocabulary (because it's too boring), but feel energetic when reading foreign books (because it's content you're interested in), doesn't that show something? Reading foreign books is also a form of learning and is much more efficient than just reading grammar books and memorizing vocabulary. So why not learn in a way that is more comfortable and interesting to you? In your free time, you can pay more attention to foreign English websites or social media, immerse yourself in the language as much as possible, increase exposure and familiarity. Maybe one day you'll suddenly find yourself effortlessly speaking fluent English. As for reading before bed to help you sleep, I suggest choosing some very difficult and hard-to-understand professional books. I believe that after reading for a while, you'll feel sleepy. Do not choose captivating novels, as you will only get more engrossed the more you read.

Studying after work is not easy. There are work-related matters that require mental effort, and in the spare time, one must concentrate on learning. It really requires self-discipline. Many people may just think about it, but you have already bought online courses and put them into action. Well done. Now, after a period of studying, you have found that your state of mind is not quite right and you want to find some methods to make adjustments, right? I have thought of three points that I hope will be useful to you. 1. Motivation: Increase some factors that can drive yourself. First of all, you liked English very much in college, and it is probably something that you are good at. This intrinsic motivation is already there. Why did you like English at that time? From this perspective, is it possible to dig out some more motivation? Also, is it possible to find some external motivation to push yourself, such as having an exam tomorrow, which would greatly increase our motivation to study. Another question, what is the underlying need for wanting to learn this English? What help would achieving the level you want provide for you? 2. Strategy: Strategically speaking, besides taking online courses, are there any other supplementary methods, or are there more opportunities to implement the specific methods advocated in the online courses, assuming they are available. What methods did you use in college? If studying with a partner can lead to mutual reinforcement, are there any small groups in the online course or friends around you who are studying together? Sharing and receiving feedback after studying can promote enthusiasm for learning. Having practical applications can also lead to a sense of achievement. 3. Energy: You mentioned that sometimes you are energetic, sometimes not. So, besides the above points, it is also necessary to see when you have more energy and which time period is more suitable for studying English. It may not be possible to do too much. If there is a certain period of time in a day when you can concentrate and focus, that would be great. Having some is better than having none. 4. Environment: The environment is also very important. Set a fixed time and environment for yourself to form a habit. Gradually, when you are in this environment at this time, you will be able to quickly get into the right state. Have you set up such a suitable environment? There is no perfect solution, adjustments need to be made through practice. Keep it up!

Hello, friend! As an English enthusiast, I can understand the confusion you are experiencing and can relate to your current state of mind. Coincidentally, I have been helping my relative's child with their English studies recently, and I would like to share some insights with you. Why do you want to learn English? Continuing to study English after many years of work is not something that ordinary people do, and I genuinely admire your determination and courage. I would like to ask: do you have any specific goals for learning English this time? Such as promotion, job titles, or improving professional skills... From your narrative, I did not find a clear objective. Allow me to speculate: perhaps it is out of interest and a desire for knowledge. If I guessed wrong, you can add the correct answer. Thank you. A clear goal + time limit + appropriate methods are needed to successfully reach the finish line. My goal in tutoring my relative's child in English is to improve their scores on next year's college entrance exam by 10-20 points, and I have developed a three-stage plan. Having a goal is necessary to have a plan and the possibility of achieving it. Have you found a continuous source of joy in learning English? Feeling more overwhelmed the more you learn may be because the teacher's delivery is not engaging enough, and it may not necessarily be your problem. I spend 20-30 minutes every day tutoring online, and the young girl cooperates actively. She never slacks off and always attends the sessions punctually. We call it a bedtime chat. Of course, as I have been entrusted with this task, I am tireless in teaching. I carefully design our sessions. In the beginning, the focus is on increasing interest and using a rough-and-ready teaching style. Does anyone refuse fun and exciting new information? Why do new words and phrases make you feel sleepy? Are they too difficult? Are they too boring? If new words can be connected to old words, if they can lead to a story, if they can be associated with a movie, would you still want to sleep? Starting from easy and simple learning to reduce difficulty might be a good attempt. Will you still be unenergetic with timely positive feedback? What is the best way to hypnotize? A lullaby from a mother. Trying to learn English by reading before bed may awaken deep anxiety. At that point, the biological clock has already surrendered, and the brain will be stimulated in reverse. If you want to study, study; if you want to sleep, sleep. Learn to listen to your body's signals, replenish energy in a timely manner, and perhaps the brain will be more obedient. The above are my personal experiences, and I hope they can be helpful to you. The road to learning is arduous and lonely. I wish you to achieve a better version of yourself soon. Thank you for allowing me to encounter like-minded individuals and progress together!

I don't know how OP arranges their time to learn English. It's best to learn new words and phrases when you are mentally refreshed in the morning. As for not being able to sleep at night, that's another issue. It could mean that OP's biological clock needs some adjustment, and adjusting it can also help with learning new things. I suggest planning your time, not necessarily following the same routine every day. For example, study new words intermittently every few days, and read and review the easier ones in the evening, and then study more carefully the next day during the daytime. Also, if watching online courses, when feeling sleepy, you can try listening to some energetic music. Many people do this, and if it's English music, it can help you to know more words and generate more motivation.

Hello, thank you for your perseverance and motivation in learning. Not everyone can continue to work hard according to their own interests after graduating for 7 years like you. Since you have already bought online courses and started learning, it shows that you really want to learn English. But now things are different from when you were in school. We have work, social life, and many family matters to take care of. Moreover, after putting down studying for so many years, it's natural to have situations like new words that you can't remember and feeling sleepy. Another possibility is that you might be too tired and want to sleep, or your subconscious mind is resisting learning because it doesn't want you to be too tired. During this time, I suggest that no matter what emotions or state you encounter, accept them first and see the needs behind them. Allow yourself to slow down and accumulate and make changes little by little. At the same time, look at the progress you have made in your learning, give yourself positive affirmation and motivation for your efforts, encourage yourself, and allow yourself to gradually change and better integrate with your current learning pace. Only then can you learn English better. In addition, perhaps without the pressure of memorizing words from English newspapers, you are truly interested in things like content, which is where your interest lies. This is why you won't be hypnotized. I suggest that you follow your true interests, and slowly find a learning pace that suits you. This way, you can achieve more with less effort. Keep it up.

question: At the age of 19, a girl feels guilty in her heart and believes she has let her parents down after having sexual intercourse with her partner.
description: We have been dating for over two years. My partner and I haven't seen each other for a while, but we are meeting tomorrow. Sometimes, I feel happy but also upset and frustrated. Thoughts about intimacy occasionally make me feel guilty and I have this psychological feeling of letting my parents down.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope the following answers can help you: In your description, I see your struggles, conflicts, and inner turmoil. In the traditional history of sexual development, we can see many unscientific views on sex due to social gender roles and societal constructs, filled with sexual "stigmatization," which have influenced generation after generation. For example: ++ sex is dirty, ++ sexual organs are dirty, ++ sexual behavior is dirty, ++ anything related to sex is bad, ++ menstruation is bad and dirty, ++ virginity is good, non-virginity is impure, ++ men can be free, women should be modest, ... These deeply affect our gender perspective, views on sex, and basic sexual concepts. Obviously, in your upbringing, you and your parents have been deeply influenced by this, and cannot truly have a scientific understanding of sex education and sexual issues. However, hidden behind these issues are questions about chastity and fidelity. Whose eyes is chastity really for? In fact, it is a product of a patriarchal society. This also involves the issue of bodily autonomy. In many authoritarian families, children will believe that their bodies are owned by their parents and cannot be disposed of at will, and mistakes need to be determined by their parents, etc. This reflects the old notion of bodily submission. Therefore, in your view, even though you are now an adult, you are still doubting whether you can have sex with someone by using your own body. In the process of sexual development, what we should emphasize more is the right to sexual privacy rather than feelings of shame or bodily submission. Sex and Love: Sex is beautiful, because with love, sex can be beautiful too. Sex is not dirty or sinful. In the process of sex and sexual behavior, the attitude and principles we need are summarized in ten words: "autonomy, respect, responsibility, health, happiness." ## If you engage in sex and love based on voluntary principles, it is okay, otherwise, it is not. ## If it is based on mutual respect, it is okay, if there is no mutual respect, such sexual love is problematic. ## Both parties need to be responsible for each other and themselves, if not, then do not do it. ## It should be conducted based on health and hygiene principles, which require attention to diseases. ## Sex and love should be joyful; if there is no joy and it goes against the will of the partner, then clearly there is a problem. ε I wish you well. I am here, and the world and I love you.

Give you a big hug. First, you need to understand clearly that you belong to yourself, not to your parents. You are an independent individual, and your parents are just the ones who brought you into the world. You have the freedom to live your own life and make your own choices. Secondly, you need to know what you want for yourself. Can you take care of yourself? Can you be responsible for your own body? Can you take protective measures to prevent harm? As an adult, you have the right to decide how to live your life. But you need to think carefully about whether the current life you're living is the one you truly desire. If you're uncertain, don't rush into anything. Take the time to reflect and follow your heart once you've made up your mind. If you want love, love openly and enjoy the process. If you're stuck, hit the pause button and live a peaceful life until you find clarity. Don't live a stressful life! Wishing you well!

question: Worked hard for four years and didn't get into graduate school, feeling sad, no hope for the future?
description: In my four years of college, I studied diligently every day to secure a spot in the postgraduate recommendation. I sacrificed a lot to achieve a top ranking in my year. In the end, I ranked fifth, as our school only accepts five students each year. However, I was not selected in the end. The explanation I received from the teacher was that there were only four spots available, despite five people being listed on the application form. I suspect that someone used connections to take my place. It is now already in October, and I hastily prepared for the graduate entrance exam, but unfortunately, I did not pass. The deadlines for other state-owned enterprise exams have also passed. Those classmates who played games all day and had low GPAs are now being recruited by companies. Meanwhile, I feel like I have achieved nothing and I'm very upset. I see my friends showing off their grades, employment, and relationships on social media, and it really makes me jealous. I can't get over it, and I don't know how to motivate myself. I feel like I wasted four years, and I am still without any achievements.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, life meaning.

answers.answer_text: Hug the questioner, you can do it. Having a good academic background means that you have a good foundation. If you have the opportunity in the future, you can try taking the postgraduate entrance examination, if you are willing. Perhaps the concept conveyed by today's society is that of achieving fame and wealth at a young age. It has a great influence on people. In fact, how is it possible to succeed without going through long-term struggles, without experiencing the test of time, without undergoing various tests? There are very few exceptions. We are just ordinary people, extreme outliers. We can only rely on time to slowly accumulate wealth, connections, reputation... There are indeed some people who, after leaving school, have a smooth job and career, everything goes so smoothly, and they still look glamorous. I think it's like everyone running on the same starting line, each person's track is different, so the scenery will be different. But who is the first person to reach the finish line may not necessarily be the one on the innermost lane, and it may not necessarily not be the one on the outermost lane. Everything is just beginning. No accomplishment does not necessarily mean anything, we cannot judge solely based on these. It would be unfair to ourselves. In fact, when you turn around and look back, you will find that many people are not as good as you, whether in the past or now. When you are tired, look back at those who are not as good as you. When you feel a little proud of yourself, look at those who are more excellent ahead. Here is a sentence from "To Kill a Mockingbird": Bravery is when you know you're licked before you begin, but you begin anyway and see it through no matter what. You rarely win, but sometimes you do. I don't think it's a losing situation for ourselves, right?

question: My best friend heard my mom say that she is not a good person? How should I handle our relationship with my best friend?
description: When I was on the phone with my mother, my best friend accidentally overheard my mother saying that she is not a good person.

answers.answer_text: The person you spend time with is yourself, and you know best why you have become best friends with her. There must be something about her that attracts you. Your mom does not have close interaction with your best friend, so her evaluation might be one-sided and influenced by some conservative thinking. You can communicate with your mom about the positive aspects of your best friend, and reassure her not to worry too much but to support your friendship. You should also help your best friend adjust her negative emotions because being labeled by elders for no reason can make her feel hurt and upset. You should provide her with warmth and care. As for whether your best friend is a good person, you have your own judgment. No one is perfect, and everyone has strengths and weaknesses. We make friends because we appreciate their strengths and can accept their shortcomings, and we grow and play together as companions.

question: 23-year-old girl, afraid of finding a job, feels guilty towards her parents.
description: A 23-year-old female with an introverted personality and some insecurities. Due to the impact of the epidemic, she hasn't been working for many days and has become more reluctant to leave home. She believes she is not suitable for this job and eventually quit. Her parents are anxious for her to find a job, leading to several arguments. For some reason, she is extremely fearful of finding a job, but also feels guilty towards her parents, thinking she is worthless and a burden. She has considered death multiple times as a means to relieve herself, but is also terrified and conflicted about it. She feels that she should die at this moment, to mitigate any further burden on her parents and allow them to live more comfortably.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, guilt and shame, vulnerability and tears.

answers.answer_text: Hello, because I am introverted and have low self-esteem, and because of the epidemic, I have been staying at home for a long time and have reduced contact with people. I feel unfamiliar with the outside world and feel fearful, which is understandable. Because of fear, you want to escape. Our actions, emotions, thoughts, etc. all influence each other and form a continuous cycle. Good feelings will make us take positive actions, so as to obtain more positive feelings. Positive feelings can help us do better, thus forming a positive cycle; while emotions such as fear and anxiety will make us withdraw. Withdrawal behavior will lead to self-doubt, so we dare not take action, forming a negative cycle. You may now be in such an important negative cycle. However, do not be afraid. The beginning is always difficult, but as long as you take the first step and move from a negative cycle to a positive cycle, everything will go in a better direction one step at a time. Don't rush, give yourself some time, slowly readjust to this society. You can start with simple and enjoyable things, start with work that does not require too much interaction with others, gradually integrate into this society. Once you start taking action, you will find that it is not as difficult as you imagine. You are an adult now, and it is understandable that parents are worried when they see you not working. They may not know about your fear. But you should know that they are just worrying about you and do not really think you are a trouble. If you leave, it will not make them feel relieved, but will plunge them into endless pain. Can you bear it? Don't be afraid, take it slow, keep going! I believe in you! Hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Without you, how could they be doing well? Is their concern for your work just an attempt to take your salary? Of course not. Are they eager for you to make money? No, they are not. They are worried about your future, so they may put some pressure on you. If your future is such a concern for them, how could they not be worried about your safety? Don't easily think that it would be better without yourself because of anyone or anything. The world will still go on without anyone, but a family cannot afford to lose anyone. As for work, I cannot give you good advice. Currently, the pandemic has made finding a job more difficult than before. If you really can't find a job, it's better to take the time to enrich yourself, make a career plan, take care of your family's meals at home, and pay more attention to household hygiene. This way, at least you will feel fulfilled and not useless. Cook a delicious meal, help your parents with the laundry, even if you don't work, your parents will praise you for being responsible. At the same time, think about why you quit your previous job. Did you not like it? What do you like then? Did you find the salary too low? How much salary do you think you can strive for? Set a goal. Is it because you lacked skills? Where are you lacking? What do you want to do? What else do you need besides work experience? Considering these things is much better than being stuck in a dead end. If you really need money, you can consider doing some work from home. For example, drawing portraits for others using a graphics tablet, writing novels online, or doing some game leveling, etc. Life is full of opportunities! Being 23 years old is a good time, and there is still plenty of time to learn some new skills.

question: The spouse's speech is always negative criticism, never speaks nicely. What should I do when I am angry?
description: My spouse always speaks in a blaming tone, lacks patience with our child and me. They frequently get angry and nitpick. Whenever I try to have a calm conversation with them, they get annoyed. I don't know what to do.
keywords: Emotions, expression of emotions, healing methods.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Understanding that negative communication always has an impact on both you and your child, you can tell her about your feelings and ask her what she ultimately wants with this expression. Is there anything that you haven't done that she expects? If it's reasonable, we can make adjustments; if it's unreasonable, we can discuss better solutions. If communication is not going smoothly between both parties, you can also make an appointment with a mental health teacher on the platform to communicate together.

question: About to study abroad, the overseas epidemic is not under control, my parents don't understand?
description: I just graduated from my senior year as a male student. I was supposed to study abroad this year, but due to the pandemic, I don't think I can go anymore. However, my parents don't understand and think that I am just being playful or unable to get into a good school. They even insult me with their words. I told them that I can go next year instead, but they believe that I just want to have fun. The truth is, I want to study hard when I go abroad, not just for the sake of showing off. My parents keep bringing up the fact that they have spent a lot of money on me, and I don't feel confident enough to take the domestic postgraduate entrance exam. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: The question is quite simple, and the solution is not difficult either. I had a friend who was in a similar situation as you. He said that before going abroad to study, he couldn't travel due to various circumstances and ended up staying at home and playing around. His parents would ridicule and make sarcastic comments about him daily. Eventually, he felt frustrated and decided to adopt a strategy of "acting like a pig to eat the tiger." Every day, he would make a plan for himself and deliberately schedule time for studying and reading when his parents were around. He would pick up a book and read for a while before allowing himself to play. When his parents would criticize him again, he would show them the completed task list of his plan and say, "I'm following my plan every day. I am studying, and you can see it too. It's not appropriate to mock me." After doing this for a while, his parents couldn't find a valid reason to argue anymore and they stopped. It is quite common to face a lack of understanding from parents. You can find ways and strategies to prevent them from blaming you too much. Whether you are too playful or not, whether you want to study abroad or not, only you know your own situation best. Due to the impact of the pandemic, it is inevitable to lack confidence and a sense of security in both life and studies. It's normal to feel confused about the future as well. I believe that you will study hard when you go abroad, but you can also consider the domestic situation for now. The pandemic is still quite severe overseas. Take advantage of this time to make a good plan and adjust your state of life. Once the pandemic is over, I believe your studying life will be back on track.

Hello! You have a very objective understanding of the current studying abroad situation. Indeed, the overseas pandemic has not been brought under control, leading to escalating social unrest. Therefore, going abroad now does carry a higher risk. How do you plan to make an effective transition this year and adequately prepare for studying abroad next year? For example, you can utilize this window of time to find social practice opportunities in China that are relevant to your future field of study. You may also need to make some foundational preparations for your academic studies. If you have a clear plan, communicate it with your parents and take proactive actions, I believe your relationship with them will gradually improve.

question: Can hypnosis be done remotely? I want to recover childhood traumatic experiences.
description: I seem to recall being sexually abused or molested when I was a child, but I can't remember clearly. I definitely experienced molestation, but I'm unsure if it went any further. I feel very uneasy and I really want to know what happened back then. It's a knot in my mind, and thinking about it makes me feel depressed. But I have no memory of it anymore. When I first found out, I was absolutely certain it was sexual abuse, but I really can't remember. (However, I did fall down when I was a child.) Perhaps the truth can't be retrieved. I'm considering remote hypnosis, not sure if it's possible, or maybe I have to meet a hypnotherapist in person.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, trauma therapy

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. Remote hypnosis is not infeasible, but it is not recommended. I can't remember whether it was sexual abuse or molestation in childhood; but now, I want to know what happened back then since my innocence is no longer there. It's not that remote hypnosis is completely impossible. After evaluating the problems of some visitors, it has been determined that remote (online) methods can indeed be used, such as adjusting the subconscious mind. If the questioner wants to find the trauma imprint from those years, then remote hypnosis may have some difficult limitations to overcome, such as the possibility of incomplete observation and blind spots. Therefore, if the questioner has to resort to remote hypnosis due to various conditions, the first thing to do is to discuss with the hypnotherapist, who will make a comprehensive evaluation to determine whether remote hypnosis is possible. If it is possible, then there are a few points that must be paid special attention to: ① Is there a match between the hypnotherapist and the visitor? We won't discuss orientation, etc., as hypnosis is a process of establishing a relationship with the visitor's subconscious mind, so whether the visitor can enter the state set by the hypnotherapist is crucial. ② The spatial and hardware settings during hypnosis. In the hypnosis process, great importance is attached to the nonverbal information of the visitor, and the hypnotherapist will cleverly intervene at the appropriate time. In remote hypnosis, the opportunity for actual light touch to reinforce the trauma imprint is lacking. Therefore, if the hypnotherapist cannot observe the nonverbal information in detail, as well as transmit and communicate clearly, it is easy to understand the deviation and will hinder the hypnosis process. It should be noted: the observation point of the video, clarity, stability of the network signal, uninterrupted space and time, etc. ③ Does the hypnotherapist have the competence for remote hypnosis? ④ Do the visitor and hypnotherapist have the ability to overcome the limitations of remote hypnosis? Remote hypnosis is an indirect interpersonal interaction, sometimes unable to see each other's movements, postures, etc., in real time. This not only easily overlooks many valuable information but also, in case the visitor falls into the experience of past trauma, how to effectively return to the present in remote hypnosis, and how to effectively set up psychological safety island techniques? In conclusion, my suggestion is: for questioners who involve recalling trauma, those with severe mental illness or psychological disorders, or those who find it difficult to enter a hypnotic state, it is best to have face-to-face hypnotherapy. Best wishes to the questioner.

Give OP a hug! For many people, sexual abuse can be a serious harm to self, especially when they are young. The damage caused by such behavior is even greater. Now, OP wants to retrieve past memories through hypnosis. In theory, it is possible, but the amount that can be retrieved is unknown. The younger the age, the more difficult it is for self-consciousness to understand, accept, and recognize such things, and the deeper the suppression. This means that only when in a deep state of hypnosis, such memories may be presented and released. This requires the hypnotherapist to constantly pay attention to the changes of OP's mind and body. At this time, many emotional and mental states are expressed through body language. Online hypnosis generally uses audio or video methods, but this method has a drawback. It cannot clearly see the overall facial expressions and body movements of the hypnotized person, making it impossible to promptly discover and interpret the psychological and emotional states of the hypnotized person. This results in a lack of timely and effective understanding, acceptance, and recognition of the emotional and mental states of the hypnotized person, leading to secondary harm. Of course, remote hypnosis can also start by releasing inner emotions in a relaxed manner before repairing past traumas. However, this can also be affected by weather conditions that impact the network signal, and hence the effectiveness of hypnosis. In comparison, face-to-face hypnosis can avoid these problems. However, in such a situation, one should consider choosing a hypnotherapist of the same gender, or choose a suitable hypnotherapist with the presence of family members.

Dear, for oneself, harassment or sexual assault are significant events, and it must be very painful to have such a significant event not clear in one's mind. Hugs to you! I have experienced both face-to-face hypnosis and remote hypnosis, so I will share my experience with you: / Lost traumatic experience / In this situation, when a child experiences a traumatic event, because the event is too intense, the child will choose to forget the event, in order to defend against the enormous impact on oneself. However, even though it is forgotten in the mind, the body will still have memories. Through hypnosis, we can communicate with the subconscious, evoke bodily and emotional memories, and perhaps you can remember something. / Releasing emotions / Traumatic experiences usually bring tremendous emotions to the victims. We cannot be sure how this childhood experience occurred and how the parents dealt with it. Because the way parents handle it is also significant to a child who has already been injured. If parents can comfort the child well, then the trauma may be more easily accepted by the child; if parents feel ashamed and cannot comfort the child, then it is a secondary injury to the child, and the child will still suppress emotions. "Suppression" is mentioned in the description, I wonder what exactly the suppression is? / Hypnosis / Hypnosis can evoke traumatic memories or emotions, but the focus is on processing the traumatic experience and emotions. It's like a wound being exposed, it needs a doctor to clean it and close it up again, so that the wound will gradually heal. Remote video hypnosis can be performed, but you need to have enough sense of safety in your space. However, the advantage of hypnosis in the counseling room is that there is a trusted hypnotist accompanying you. When your emotions come out, the hypnotist can hold you or place their hands on yours, giving you a sense of safety and support, which is helpful for healing the pain. Whether face-to-face or remote hypnosis, the prerequisite is to establish enough trust with the hypnotist. I hope you can open up your emotional knot and have a wonderful future!

question: Why do visitors always cry when they are doing psychological counseling?
description: Made several psychological consultations, each time was a crying consultation. How can visitors adjust their emotions well? They tend to cry uncontrollably during the consultation, and they don't feel good about themselves. They feel awkward and embarrassed to make eye contact and talk to the counselor. What should they do?

answers.answer_text: Hugging the topic host in consultation and crying uncontrollably may indicate that a deep and safe environment and connection have been established between the visitor and the counselor. Actually, for the effectiveness of counseling, it is meaningful. Crying while discussing certain things indicates that these things must be very important, and in the present moment of counseling, the real emotions are touched. When emotions flow, some changes quietly occur. I think counselors are also willing to see visitors release their suppressed sadness and grievances through tears. When visitors mention certain things and cannot help but cry, it must be because certain points in these matters easily touch their emotions, so it is normal to cry as soon as they mention it. The significance of counseling is sometimes to provide visitors with a process of being able to be themselves, to let their emotions be seen and flow freely, and there is nothing to feel embarrassed about. Counselors will not judge visitors for crying.

question: Do everything quickly, okay? Am I unable to empathize?
description: I do everything very quickly, but I am also very irritable. A few days ago, when discussing reading habits with friends, I realized that I read quickly while they take their time. They said I don't love reading, but I actually feel that I do love reading. Maybe I have difficulty empathizing with them?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, everyone has their own way of handling things, each has their own strengths and weaknesses, and what matters is whether it helps you grow and reflect. From your description, it seems that you are confused about whether your fast-paced and sometimes impatient way of doing things is good or not. Being quick in your actions may indicate that you are proactive, dislike procrastination, and have decisiveness, not hesitating. However, as you mentioned, there may be some drawbacks, such as impulsiveness, carelessness, or not grasping the essence. It is important to have a comprehensive understanding of these pros and cons, neither underestimating nor becoming arrogant. If this way of doing things affects the people around you or causes you some distress and minor troubles, you can learn to be calm and think before acting. Before taking action, spend a few minutes contemplating or listening to others' suggestions, and then start after considering as many pros and cons as possible, gradually developing this awareness. Pay more attention to the possibilities of things, rather than having a narrow view that blinds you. Reading habits vary from person to person, and it is enough to gain what you want from it. It has weak correlation with the ability of empathy, but not strongly related. By carefully reading and experiencing the stories in the book, and scrutinizing the characteristics and personalities of each character, our ability to empathize can indeed be enhanced. However, empathy is based on understanding. If your fast reading method allows you to have the same profound understanding of characters and stories, it can also generate empathy. Fast reading might help you obtain more information in a certain period of time, knowing the full picture of a story faster than others, but whether you truly understand it depends on your personal abilities, such as memory, thinking, summarizing, etc. Choose a way of handling things that suits you, as long as it doesn't harm others' interests. Choose a reading speed that allows you to understand and grasp the content of the book. Live your life in a way that makes you comfortable. You can listen to others' advice and ideas, but whether you will ultimately change to adapt depends on you. Best wishes.

question: Should I break up or drag on with my boyfriend who says he won't marry me if I don't have children?
description: My boyfriend and I have been together for two or three years. We get along very well and like each other. Now we are at the stage of discussing marriage. I personally don't want to have children, but he does. We have analyzed the pros and cons from various aspects, but we cannot convince each other. One of his reasons for wanting children is because his parents want grandchildren. Otherwise, they won't support us being together. His mother even privately talked to my mother, asking her to persuade me to have children (and even two). I feel angry about his parents' thoughts and intrusive behavior because I believe that whether or not to have children is a decision for the couple and parents have no right to interfere. I have also expressed concerns about his parents' interference in our married life, but he hasn't come up with a reasonable solution. I have talked to him two or three times, but I haven't gotten the outcome I wanted. Should I break up with him or continue the relationship? (But besides this issue, we get along very well in other aspects).
keywords: Marriage, pre-marriage, and views on childbirth.

answers.answer_text: Why did his mother secretly contact your mother and ask you to have children when you haven't even gotten married? This is too much! It's a complete lack of boundaries, no sense of limits. They can't even distinguish between what matters should be managed and what matters should not be managed. It's really infuriating! You are not children anymore. Should the decision of whether or not to have children, or whether or not to be parents, be made by grandparents? It's really ridiculous. Now, with so many conflicting opinions, there will be even more problems after having a child. Moreover, children who are raised by parents with such strong control issues will have a high risk of problems in their future lives. There will be more and more situations where opinions cannot be reconciled. Be mentally prepared to face these challenges before considering any further plans.

Well, other than this, everything else is good - this issue should be relatively insignificant during the dating phase, not worth mentioning. But if we shift our perspective to the marital relationship after marriage, this difference in values can be disastrous. Both mothers can openly interfere in your lives, the husband will undecisively shift the pressure of childbirth onto you, and you will be left to face various trivial matters alone. My advice is that you can persuade him, or let yourself be persuaded, but please take this issue seriously and proceed into marriage cautiously before reaching a conclusion.

In this issue, it is known that the "enemy" is his parents who sway him towards his potential enemy, while your parents have a different perspective. It is difficult to change the perspective of 3-5 people with just one person's opinion. Moreover, opinions on the traditional issue of "continuing the family line" in China are often biased and realistic. It is unlikely that we will reach a consensus now or in the future. Also, personally, I think the reason why he didn't provide guidance is because he also wants children. So, on this issue, if both sides have conflicting views, how can we discuss it? In a marriage, either you take a step back or he and his parents take a step back. Imagine who would eventually compromise? Also, imagine what kind of outcome the marriage would lead to if neither side compromises on this issue? If this continues to be dragged on, it will waste precious time for finding a compatible spouse.

question: How can he withdraw so quickly? Is it cruelty or rationality?
description: We are in a long-distance relationship. Why didn't my boyfriend reply to my messages from noon until the evening? The next day, when I expressed that I was upset and unhappy, he said he was helpless. (Because he's busy with work and overtime?) Neither of us reached out to each other for the next two days, because there have been many instances before where he didn't reply to my messages. In the evening, I posted on my Moments (social media) saying "letting go," and I noticed that he deleted the QQ (chat platform) status that said he wanted me to accompany him. Hoping that he would take the initiative to comfort me, but instead, he left even faster. I posted another Moments post, sobbing uncontrollably, and attached our favorite photo together, saying it was our final goodbye. He still didn't contact me. Why doesn't he feel sorry for me when I say I'm crying? He continuously avoids contacting me, can he really remain so calm? I'm not demanding anything specific, even if we are separating, is it not worth it for him to take a moment to say something? Does he really think that there is no relationship between us just because I said I want to let go? Does anything I do, whether happy or sad, have nothing to do with him? How can he detach himself so quickly? Isn't there any bit of emotion left? Even if we were just regular friends, if I knew they were crying, I would politely comfort them, right? Last time, we were on the verge of breaking up because of this. He didn't contact me for five days, and in the end, it was still me who took the initiative to contact him and reluctantly maintain our relationship.
keywords: Love, heartbreak, sense of security, love management

answers.answer_text: Owner, hello! I feel very sorry for what you have been through. It seems that your boyfriend is not as invested in your relationship as you are, and he is slowly distancing himself from the relationship. I'm not sure about your usual interactions, but based on his reactions to your two social media posts, it seems like he is using a "cold treatment" approach to force you to break up. As you mentioned, this issue has been going on for a while, and each time it basically ends with "you show weakness, initiate contact, reluctantly maintain the relationship." In the lyrics of the song "Red Rose," there is a line that says, "Those who are favored have no fear." Either he believes that you will not leave him and uses that to control you, or he wants you to take the initiative to break up and end the relationship. Regardless of the result, this relationship is difficult to sustain in the long run. "If I say that I want to let go, does he think that we have no relationship at all? Whatever I do, whether I'm happy or sad, has nothing to do with him anymore? How can he detach himself so quickly? Is there no emotion left at all? Even if we are just ordinary friends, wouldn't they politely comfort you if they knew you were crying?" Every question is like a knife, stabbing at your heart, visible and heartbreaking. Maybe the other person is not indifferent, but rather does not want to remain entangled in the relationship and hopes to end it with a clean break. However, he hopes that you will be the one to propose a breakup, perhaps to alleviate his guilt. I believe that when everyone first says "I love you," they are sincere and hope to grow old together. But life cannot always be like the first meeting, and we may not be so lucky to meet the right person right away. In fact, owner, you can muster up the courage to sit down and talk to your boyfriend, listen to his true thoughts. Even if it is an unwanted outcome, it is better than being deceived and tortured in the relationship. Perhaps everyone will experience the pain of a breakup, which is the darkest period of life. I remember when I broke up with my first love, everything seemed colorless, there was no light in the world, and I couldn't find the meaning and hope in life. However, it was precisely because of this difficult time that I gained more understanding of love, personal growth, and met better people. Perhaps others hurt us back then, but they also helped us grow and find better happiness. I also wish you, the girl, to have a happier future one day. While I'm at it, I'll share the methods I used to get over a breakup: ①Accept the facts and stop expecting anything from him. ②Release your emotions: write emotional diaries, confide in good friends, go on trips to relax, listen to your favorite songs, find a quiet corner to cry and shout, do aerobic exercises. ③Read books and study to find peace and become better. ④Try developing some new hobbies to shift your focus. ⑤Give yourself affirmation and positive responses every day, give yourself confidence and strength. ⑥Think more about his shortcomings and flaws. ⑦When feeling extremely unhappy, watch funny videos, they can bring us a lot of joy!

Hello! Giving you a warm hug. Reading your description, I truly understand your current state of mind. You are feeling very sad because your boyfriend didn't respond after multiple attempts to test him. You feel that even if he wants to break up, he should say it out loud. Why is he avoiding it? Why doesn't he respond directly to you? What response from your boyfriend would make you feel comforted? First of all, every girl in a relationship hopes that her boyfriend will protect and cherish her, and always keep her in his thoughts. But reality is not like this. Now imagine if you were the boy, how exhausted would you be? Besides enduring work pressure, you would also have to constantly find ways to please her and always reply to her messages. In that case, how can he concentrate on doing his job well? If he can't do his job well, then how can he have a future with you? Boys with ambition prioritize work over relationships because only with a stable foundation can they have the confidence and resources to pursue love. Secondly, from your description, it seems like you have been constantly testing your boyfriend's love for you. You need to pay attention to the way you do it. You believe that if he doesn't reply to your messages, it means he doesn't love you. If he ignores something related to your social circle, it means he doesn't love you. And if you mention breaking up and he doesn't respond, it means he doesn't love you. So, let me ask you, where does your love for him show? In what ways do you demonstrate your love for your boyfriend? Love is built on mutual trust. If you want to receive love from the other person, you need to show your love through understanding and tolerance and give positive love! For example, when your boyfriend comes back from work, do you make him a delicious meal and show your care? Do you give him space to think when he is under work pressure? If you really want to be with him, do you post positive messages on social media to remind him of the wonderful times you've had together? Finally, in order to make someone love you, you must first learn to love others. Everyone's character and habits are formed in their family environment, and when two people come together, there is an adjustment period. During this process, if you impose your subjective thoughts and demands on the other person, it will inevitably cause resentment. We should use our own changes to influence the other person's perception of our kindness towards them, and in turn, they will also change. In conclusion, learn to trust, learn to communicate, learn to understand, and learn to love others. Only in this way will the love you desire come to you.

Hello Miss, I am sorry to hear about what you've been through. As a guy, I have also done such excessive things to my ex in the past. The root cause is definitely some issues that arose during our interaction, such as excessive stress in life, inability to communicate well, and long-term accumulation, all leading to the current situation. My suggestion is to give the other person some time, let both parties calm down, and then find an opportunity to calmly talk things through. I truly understand your current mood. A woman only has expectations and love for her man, which can lead to feelings of dissatisfaction and anxiety, just like what you are experiencing. However, you also need to understand that in times when your relationship is not good, such as now, everything you do will make him feel annoyed, and he will find it difficult to perceive your love. I myself, due to immaturity and a lack of understanding of the love I received from my ex at the time, ended up disappointing someone who didn't deserve it. I hope you both can reconcile and improve your relationship.

Long-distance relationships increase the depth of longing but also make communication more difficult. Not being able to physically touch or see each other, combined with the lack of timely replies in messages without WeChat voice and video capabilities, can definitely drive a person crazy, leading to constant self-doubt and overthinking. Sending warm hugs to the author. From reading the entire passage, it seems like the author is a sensitive and emotionally rich girl, perhaps more dependent on emotions. Perhaps these aspects also add a lot of psychological pressure to the author's boyfriend. Initially, one may be able to reply to their girlfriend's messages promptly every day, but after the relationship stabilizes, more time and energy will be focused on career and social relationships. It is inevitable to neglect your partner, which indeed requires more understanding. At the same time, shift the focus more on yourself, cultivate hobbies, and engage in activities you enjoy during leisure time. This way, you may not be as concerned about whether your partner replies promptly. It seems that the author can only passively guess their boyfriend's thoughts through his friend circle's dynamics. Both of them are hinting at each other through these dynamics. Why not just call directly to understand each other's true feelings? What are you worried or afraid of? Instead of being unwilling to understand and overthinking on this side, why not ask directly for clarification or simply go to his place to find out the truth, saving time and energy? What if this relationship is the main course for you but just a seasoning for the other person?

Hello, the questioner. In fact, when we enter a relationship, we consider what we can gain from it, and we have a sense of gain and loss. If we can see ourselves as complete and meeting someone else is just sharing our completeness with them, instead of meeting someone else to complete us, then we are truly complete. With this mindset, we can truly be ourselves and the other person can be themselves in our interactions. I can feel the questioner's impatience and longing to be with him. But the person you missed is not the right person, as the right person will not be missed. Each person has someone who can resonate with them in their current state. The so-called missing out indicates that there is no longer resonance between you. We can only truly understand what happiness is after experiencing pain. We endure the hardships of so-called love in order to recognize happiness when we experience it. And happiness is innate, it has nothing to do with how others treat you. You can try gradually letting go of the hand you have been holding tightly, imagine slowly relaxing the hand you are holding, and the energy will return to yourself from him. Then you will regain your own power. No matter what you are experiencing, who you love, or who you don't love, always maintain a sense of awareness, as if the higher self is watching you in the present moment, so you know, "I am acting" "This is a script", watch yourself acting, and then smile, this script is really wonderful!

I have managed to maintain it for two weeks, and now it's the same problem again. Maybe there is no solution to this problem between us. I really don't ask for much, just a little bit of his time is enough, but he still refuses. I am truly disappointed and yet reluctant. I feel very uncomfortable and it hasn't even been 24 hours since we separated. I already feel like I can't bear the future life. How can I get through this? Sometimes I really hope that he can take the initiative to come to me, and I will forgive him, but he is still so resolute, so resolute not to come to me...

question: Broke up already, still living with the ex, but constantly affected emotionally. What should I do?
description: Due to certain circumstances, I ended up living with my ex-partner after the pandemic. We had a peaceful breakup, but perhaps due to various reasons, our previous relationship was not very deep. However, I had developed strong feelings for him. We promised to become friends, but I found that I overestimated myself. The process of moving on has been slow, and I am constantly influenced by him in my daily life. This leads to fluctuating emotions and even affects my work efficiency. For example, when he goes out for dinner or has unusual emotions, I am affected and unable to focus. I tell myself not to pay too much attention to him and treat him as a normal friend, but I can't help but repeatedly check on him. I know I still hold on to some unresolved feelings, but I want to move on from this state and accept the fact that it is no longer possible. I understand this is difficult, but I believe it's a necessary step. I would like to ask if anyone has had a similar experience and can share their advice. As for living together, I'm advised not to, but for at least a period of time, we still have to live together. Considering the current situation, I hope to stabilize my emotions and be more at peace. Thank you in advance. Also, both of us are male.
keywords: Love, heartbreak, dependency and attachment, sense of security.

answers.answer_text: Even if it's just keeping a pet, you have to take care of when it should eat, when it should go to the bathroom, when it should get a haircut, when it should bathe, when it should go for a walk, and so on. Even if it's just installing a bookshelf and a mattress, you have to consider where to put it, how much space it takes up, if it obstructs the way, if it's satisfactory to use, if it's comfortable to lie on, and so on. It will also affect your feelings and attention. Moreover, living with a living person, who doesn't have the ability to be invisible or silence themselves, is a difficult problem to not pay attention to or be influenced by. Does telling yourself not to think about an elephant work? No. Does telling yourself not to pay attention to promises and being good friends work? No. You use the same space, the same furniture, appliances, toilets, and kitchen. You have shared experiences and emotions. It is normal for a normal person to be affected. If you are not affected, you must have truly become enlightened. The point is not whether or not you should be influenced, or if being influenced is normal. The point is, no matter what kind of relationship you have with the person you live with, how can you not be "tangled up"? You can break down the walls of thought to look at this issue. Many people look at their ex's social media updates, follow their daily steps, indirectly inquire if they have started dating someone else. If they are happier and better off than us, we are likely to feel annoyed, and may even begin to resent and harass them. To put it more plainly, this is merely a curiosity and an unfulfilled possessiveness. Whether or not you live together doesn't have a direct relationship to it. Your ex is not an idol, burdening them with expectations is something they can't bear. And you are not their lifelong follower, so don't end up finding yourself following after them again, there may only be the smell of their rear end there. We pay attention to our own friends, hoping they feel valued by us and hoping they reciprocate the same feelings. It is also just a self-satisfying form of giving and taking. If we can understand the inherent reciprocity in these relationships and seek mutual benefits within them, it will reduce the magnitude and frequency of emotional fluctuations. Excessive emotional squandering is useless and even harmful. If you can't be good with your current partner and can't be good friends, then either treat each other as strangers and passersby (which may not seem possible), or reuse the relationship, as ambiguity is another kind of beauty and reunion is another kind of flavor and happiness.

Isn't it? Sir A, the clever wife can't make a meal without rice. Sir A's gender is not an issue, it's purely a matter of personal freedom. But this difficulty is comparable to the Riemann Hypothesis... It's like putting a piece of meat in front of someone who hasn't eaten for three days and nights, not allowing them to eat and not allowing them to drool... How about this, think more about why you guys broke up, and then quickly find someone else... My ability is limited, I can only help you this much... Good luck, my friend!

Hello, OP. First, I give you a small hug. Please think about a question: Compared to the two, do you love him more or love yourself more? I believe the answer is the latter. But in our lives, why do we hurt ourselves for someone who is not important to us and may have very little overlap in the future? I know this is not what you want. What we can do is to make an effort to stay away from this pain. Let's sort out your problem. Because of the pandemic, you live with your ex, you still have deep feelings for him, even though you broke up amicably, you still constantly care about him, get sad for him, and let him affect you. So why do you have these problems? 1. You still love him. 2. You are reluctant to let go of your past relationship. 3. You are lonely inside and long for the care and love he used to give you. So what can we do to alleviate our pain? Carefully consider if your sadness comes from your love for him or from your unwillingness to lose the relationship. It's like a child who has a bunch of different flavored candies. Once they eat a candy, it becomes hard to find another one with the same flavor that you like. So when that candy is gone and we don't have a new satisfactory candy to eat, we naturally miss it and think about it, even though it may not have been the best candy inside, it's just that we no longer have it. Don't think too much. Let me use a common phrase from Buddhism, "Nothing exists from the beginning, not even dust". Actually, your concern for him may not necessarily mean that you still love him, it's just that he used to be close to you, so naturally you care about him. This concern is normal, but you have misinterpreted it and caused unnecessary worries. I remember my first confession target, also the only one I ever confessed to. I found out only after I finished saying everything that he had a girlfriend, and what's even more terrifying is that he was sitting right in front of me (we were students). I looked at his back every day and couldn't stop thinking, and even had evil thoughts like they would break up tomorrow. Of course, that was just a needless worry. It took me a week to move on and understand one thing: don't think too much, just love yourself. Find something to do. When we have nothing to do, our minds will think about more things involuntarily. But when we have something to do every day, something that may slightly exceed our abilities, we become incredibly focused and don't have time to think about other problems. When we finally accomplish it, we not only receive immense happiness and a sense of achievement, but we also become a better version of ourselves. Improve yourself. Love is mutual, if we want to have the love we desire, if we hope that the person we like will also like us, then a better version of ourselves is indispensable. Love requires mutual attraction, you need to have something shining on you for him to come towards you. Cai Kangyong once said: When you're 15, you think swimming is difficult and you give up. When you're 18 and meet someone you like who asks you to swim, you can only say, "I don't know how." When you're 18, you think English is difficult and give up. When you're 28 and find a very good job that requires English skills, you can only say, "I don't know how." Right? Opportunities are always reserved for those who are prepared. Start preparing for a new relationship. A new beginning is the end of the old. When you feel ready, start and let your destined person appear to spend the rest of your life with you. Finally, I wish you, OP, to get rid of this trouble early and be happy. Keep going!

This is an inclusive world. Whether you are same-sex or live together is not important. What matters is that everyone can accept you, and you should also accept yourself! If you can't move on, then don't force it. If you think of him, just think of him. There is no need to deliberately forget or blame yourself. This way, your emotions will be relatively easier. Regardless of age and who you are with, a breakup is always a long process, especially when you have invested genuine emotions. Fortunately, both parties have reached a consensus to break up, instead of having a confusing and unclear relationship. This is already good! You have already been responsible for yourself, so don't put too much pressure on yourself. Take your time, and believe that you will eventually move on.

I understand your feelings because emotions can be contagious, and being together inevitably influences each other's emotions. I don't know what happened, but recently you still have to be together and adjust your mood. This is the beginning of your growth, and in this situation, you can take a deep breath and focus on doing your own things. Two boys living together, and he is your ex, these words indicate that you are homosexual? Are you dealing with emotional issues or are you dissatisfied with your sexual orientation? You can seek help from a professional counselor with these questions.

Actually, you have a good understanding of your current mental state and you are aware of it. You know that you haven't let go. If you don't want to get better and choose to continue like this, it is your right. Or you can think of any way to move forward, it is possible. If one day you decide to change this situation, you may need to do something that interests you to reduce your attention to him. For example, expanding your circle of friends, making new friends, exploring new hobbies, such as reading books, swimming, hiking, and so on. When your life is filled with other things, your attention to him will naturally decrease. Don't forget, allow yourself to not forget, it's also okay to keep him in a certain place in your heart until the day you make a new decision.

Because of some reasons, I came back and lived together with my ex due to the pandemic. We had a peaceful breakup. Perhaps because of various reasons, the famous Chinese sexologist, Li Yinhe, said: "In my opinion, homosexuality is just as normal as heterosexuality, and they are equal in personality." At present, traditional Chinese beliefs still represent the majority, so we can only say, "You are very brave!" As for what you said, "You advised me not to live together, but at least for a period of time, we still have to live together." Of course, you sincerely only want to be ordinary friends without any thoughts of getting back together, right? It doesn't seem like it. Even if there are some unavoidable problems (such as not having a place to rent or money for meals), is cohabitation the only option? Your true inner thoughts should be that you don't want to give up. So, just let things take their course. You used to get what you were missing from him, and before finding a replacement, you weren't so willing to let go. Humans are emotional creatures, and the more invested they are, the harder it is to let go. Forcing yourself to let go will only lead to a dead end of "not being able to let go". (Negative feedback) What you can do is to stop reminding yourself every day to "forget" him, delete all WeChat, Weibo, and QQ related to him, so that you won't be tempted to "snoop" on his life. Some people become addicted to others by starting with "snooping". You can keep his phone number and contact him when necessary. Living under the same roof, don't deliberately create opportunities to meet, but greet him openly and naturally if you happen to run into each other. What are you doing now? Do you have any career plans? Are you continuously learning? How is your working platform? Does it have the potential for advancement? If a person does not have life goals and lacks initiative, they often rely on others and develop habits. Improve your vocational skills or find some fulfilling side projects to do. This is very important.

First of all, whether or not you like someone is not something you can control. If you could control it, then there would be no words like "settling," "unrequited love," "backup plan," or "self-sacrifice." I can use reason to demand myself to like or not like him (her). Emotions are independent from reason, they are two completely different things. Right now, you are asking reason to help you solve emotional problems, so it's not possible. You don't need to deliberately emphasize that you are both men. In my opinion, liking someone doesn't have much to do with gender, otherwise some countries wouldn't have legalized same-sex marriage. Currently, you cannot separate from him due to objective conditions, but the fact is, even if you separate from him, you may still be affected. In ancient times, even when travel was difficult or due to social upheaval, two people who loved each other could eventually reunite after being apart for years. So, living together or not is not the key, the key is your feelings for each other. Based on what you said about your situation, I assume that his feelings for you are not as deep as yours. Therefore, while being with him, you will inevitably have to endure more pain. If someone can make you have no emotional fluctuations while being with the person you love, then you have become emotionally numb, and in the future, you won't be able to fall in love with someone else or have any other emotional experiences.

question: Why do we consider studying as a tedious task? How can we change this mentality?
description: I am currently a undergraduate student majoring in science and engineering. I have found myself getting tired of studying, feeling distracted in class, but I'm unsure where this negative mindset comes from. I know that passive learning is less efficient compared to active learning, and it can cause me mental and physical distress if the study load becomes too heavy. I see some classmates around me who are in the same situation, but regardless of how they are doing, I want to change my current state of listlessness, yet I don't know where to start. Since studying is for my own benefit, why do I still feel a aversion towards it? How can I change this dislike for studying?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. It's great that you have realized your problem and come here actively seeking support and help from people around you. I can see your motivation in wanting to change your anxious mindset. I can also see that you are aware that you are currently in a passive learning state and the benefits of active learning. Can you try to think about which specific subject you are not so fed up with in your major, and which part of the knowledge in this subject interests you the most? Can you start by actively engaging with this part first? Experience the joy that comes with learning. You mentioned that you feel a high level of stress when the learning intensity is too strong. Can you try setting yourself a goal that has less intensity, is specific, and executable? These are my suggestions, and I hope they can help you. Best wishes!

question: When the victim mentality is changed in a relationship, no longer self-pitying, but instead becomes angry?
description: Formerly, I would always fall into self-pity and excessively seek love, often feeling like I would be abandoned. Recently, with the help of a therapist, I have slowly come out of this pattern. However, I have now started to become angry.
