Sometimes, when the other person does not meet my expectations, I enter a mode of sulking alone and resenting them in my heart. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, character development, personality traits, self-improvement.

answers.answer_text: Hello OP! In the past, I had a lot of insecurity, often feeling like I would be abandoned. I always blamed others, thinking that the pain I'm currently feeling is caused by them. I had an excessive need for validation and tried to control everything. With the help of a counselor, it seems like you're not as worried about being abandoned anymore and have been able to break out of the victim mentality. However, you still feel angry when others can't meet your needs. Is that correct? Psychoanalysis introduces the concept of grandiose narcissism. As an infant, they think that the entire world, especially their mother, should respond and fulfill their needs. If a baby's grandiose narcissism is fulfilled, their life force shines. However, if during infancy, their parents, especially their mother, did not take good care of them or establish a good attachment, their psychological development might be stuck at the infant stage, which is what Wu Zhihong refers to as "giant baby". When the grandiose narcissism is not fulfilled, the internal response becomes complete helplessness, which represents your past victim mentality. Externally, it manifests as grandiose rage, which is likely your current state: when your needs are not met, you become extremely angry. It may seem like you have broken out of the victim mentality, but in reality, your psychological development level is still at the infant stage. You are unable to take responsibility for your own needs and hope that everything and everyone will revolve around fulfilling them. Therefore, I suggest that you continue long-term counseling with your therapist and keep exploring and sorting through your emotions. Gradually work on your psychological development level. Also, let go of attachment and take responsibility for yourself. True growth means taking responsibility for yourself. While you are raging because others can't meet your needs, ask yourself, what have you done for your own needs? Have you taken care of yourself properly? Take self-responsibility, self-nurturing. When you no longer rely entirely on others to provide you with "safety and happiness," even the slightest bit of support from others will be shining, and your life will be fulfilling!

question: Can you become a mental health counselor without going to college?
description: I am currently in a state of depression and took a break from my studies. I am supposed to return to school in September for my senior year, but even though I have completed the necessary procedures for the leave of absence, I still worry that the school won't allow me to come back and continue my studies. I'm afraid that the school won't want me anymore. If I really can't return to school, then I will have to find a job. I wonder if a person who doesn't study will never amount to anything. Actually, ever since I experienced depression, I have always had the idea of becoming a psychological counselor. If the school doesn't want me, does that mean I won't be able to become a psychological counselor either?

answers.answer_text: Hello, the mental health counselor certificate has been canceled. According to the current requirements for mental health counselors in society, education is the best proof of qualification for this profession. The requirements for education in the field of mental health counseling are quite high. Even an assistant psychologist requires at least an undergraduate degree. Being a mental health counselor, similar to being a doctor or professor, is a profession that requires a long growth period. In addition to the necessary school specialization studies like Manager Yang, extensive practical learning is also needed. It is really a pity that you are currently on a leave of absence due to depression. You must actively cooperate with the treatment and relieve your own pain as soon as possible. Also, I suggest that you do not give up on your education. Even if you end up going to a less prestigious school for the college entrance examination, you can continue to improve your education. The national policies at the moment are very favorable, so you must have confidence. Best wishes~

question: Letting go of the obsession with my mother, but not contacting her again, is it too cold?
description: I have lived my entire life in a family where my mother has a serious preference for boys over girls. My older brother is now 40 years old and my mom still gives him 20,000 RMB each year, while I have been working since I was 17 and she has always been asking me for money. Back then, I was only earning 350 RMB a month. I always tried my best to prove that I am also her child and to have a clear conversation with her, but I ended up being even more disappointed. It wasn't until I realized that my upbringing was affecting my relationships and parenting beliefs that I sought psychological counseling. Now, I have a much better mindset. I have largely let go of my obsession with her and no longer have the desire to fight or prove anything to her. I can live every day happily and easily for myself and my child. However, it seems like I have entered another phase where I almost forget about my parents. It feels like I haven't called my mom in six months, and I only occasionally remember to wish everyone a happy holiday in the family group chat. Last time I wished her a happy Mother's Day, she didn't reply. In the past, this would have made me sensitive and upset, wondering why she only interacts with my brother in the group but ignores me. But now, I don't feel that way anymore. If she doesn't reply, then she doesn't. I have said what I needed to say. I often feel that the current me is very different from the past me. I used to be full of hatred and obsession, but now, am I too indifferent?
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, growth process

answers.answer_text: Hug you. The TV drama "All Is Well" is popular not only because of its star-studded cast, but also because it touches on the pain points of human nature. What is human nature? It means you will live in the way you hate the most, even beyond that. The reason why people suffer is because they cannot let go of their obsessions. Without understanding pain, how can we recognize it, let alone let it go? You are just responding to your dissatisfaction by ignoring your mother, but your original dissatisfaction is being ignored! The reason why humans are advanced beings is because of emotions, and pain comes from emotions overpowering reason. The brain thinks: receiving is only natural, let alone fair. The problem is we all want to receive, but it is difficult for us to be fair ourselves. Because absolute fairness does not exist. Our urgent needs come from unconscious unsatisfied desires that formed during childhood, leading to insufficient conscious self-construction in adulthood. Only through understanding can we resolve resentment, and only through learning can we promote growth and live up to the expectations that surpass our parents. I recommend "All Is Well" to you to understand the growth trajectory of previous generations and the weaknesses of human nature, so that we can let go instead of suppressing.

question: Half of the summer vacation has passed for high school seniors, but they feel like their academic performance hasn't improved. What should they do?
description: Just when I started my vacation, I had the idea of improving myself and surpassing others during the break. However, every morning I wake up early, do some early reading, and then start playing with my phone. I haven't been serious about doing homework. I finish playing with my phone before actually starting my homework. Even when I do my homework, I feel like I'm not making any progress and there's no sense of achievement. Now, the vacation is already halfway over and I feel very anxious. High school is starting soon, and I don't know what to do now. Even though I know I need to study hard, every time I try to focus and study, it seems like it's not effective. I feel like I'm just doing mechanical tasks all day long.
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and study, student development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Creating a schedule and learning to manage your time and energy is important. Don't rush for instant success, and accept that growth and progress take time. From your description, it seems that you are frustrated and anxious because you struggle to concentrate on your studies and improve your learning ability. However, it's clear that you are a diligent and hardworking individual, as you are trying your best to achieve your goals, which is commendable. Your challenge may lie in lacking self-discipline and not efficiently utilizing your time. Even when you are doing things, your productivity is low, and you don't feel a sense of progress, which leads to frustration. You can try to make your schedule more detailed and include aspects such as studying, eating, resting, exercising, and leisure activities. Implement it for a few days, adjust your state accordingly, and if it doesn't go smoothly, you can modify the plan by reducing or increasing your tasks. Strive to comfortably get through each day. It's okay to have some growth and progress each day; don't aim for too much too fast. If you can consistently follow your plan, the remaining half of your summer vacation will bring significant progress. Reflect on your study methods—is there anything flawed? In addition to learning new knowledge every day, you should also review and reflect on the materials you've covered. Identify the reasons for mistakes and redo the exercises. Timely review the previously memorized information to reinforce your memory; otherwise, it will be quickly forgotten. Take it slow; when you are determined to improve and elevate yourself, you will undoubtedly achieve the results you desire; it just takes time. Good luck.

question: Homosexuality, object is monosexual and may have anxiety disorder, what should I do?
description: She is a high school senior. She has excellent grades and a nice appearance and figure, so you could say she has a natural glow. answers.answer_text: Hello OP: You have pursued a girl relentlessly, and after experiencing failed heterosexual relationships, she accepted your pursuit. She said she really likes you, but doesn't know how to love you. As a result, you feel very confused, unsure how to face her and how to handle your feelings for each other. I completely understand your feelings, sending you a hug. As a high school student, you are in the stage of adolescence, exploring both your sexual orientation and romance. From your words, I see that you describe yourself as having unrequited love and possibly anxiety disorder, while you describe her as a lesbian. Don't worry, let's look at the following questions together. 1. About this girl - unrequited love, lack of love, possibly accompanied by anxiety. Unrequited love is a symptom caused by a lack of love. You mentioned that this girl's family loves her, but her parents often argue and use verbal violence. Therefore, in this girl's heart, her childhood was one devoid of love. The insecure attachment style from childhood extends into adulthood, forming an avoidant attachment style when it comes to intimate relationships. Moreover, people with unrequited love tend to enjoy fantasies and can easily interrupt intimate relationships, struggling to respond to the love given to them by others. You mentioned that you pursued her aggressively, and after some time, she said she really likes you. But can we call this feeling love? This girl has not had a pleasant experience in past relationships, and your appearance has given her a sense of being cared for and loved, which is something she has been lacking. On the surface, there may be many people pursuing her, but deep down, she still longs to be loved. Even unrequited love is an expression of this lack of love. So your appearance satisfied this need of hers. But now that you have fallen in love with her, her psychological state of lacking love may actually make her feel insecure and unsure how to face you. Sometimes, when we push someone away, it's not because we don't love them, but because we are afraid to. Those who lack love often feel that the other person will leave them one day. They lack confidence in themselves and mistrust in relationships. Additionally, you mentioned that this girl may have anxiety disorder. We may like someone, but our actions end up pushing them away. In the end, we don't even know how to handle someone's kindness towards us. This dilemma and confusion easily lead to anxiety. 2. About yourself - being a lesbian, pursuing this girl fiercely. I don't know your age, but from your words, you mentioned that this girl has excellent grades and good looks, radiating a certain aura. During our childhood or adolescence, both our sexual orientation and love are in the process of exploration. A girl with good grades and good looks is very popular and can easily make us admire her. So, what is your real desire in pursuing this girl? Is it because you are a lesbian and genuinely like her, or is it out of admiration or vanity? I suggest you ask your heart and understand your true desires. Only when your desires are clear, can you make the right choices. As for her, she needs to consider whether she is a lesbian or heterosexual, whether her liking for you is a crush or simply because you fulfill her need for being loved. As for you, you need to see clearly whether you actually like her or if it's just admiration or possessiveness towards a beautiful girl. Furthermore, you also need to consider if you are a lesbian. Regardless of whether you ultimately decide to be together, understanding each other's desires and making decisions that align with your inner needs is the most important thing. Best wishes.

question: I have made many plans for myself, but I always fail to complete them. Is there any way to help myself?
description: Often, I set myself some small goals, like dieting, exercising to lose weight, and saving money every month to buy something I desire. However, I always fail to achieve them. Is there any method to help myself?

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner: I can understand where you are right now. For the question you raised, is it a common problem for many people nowadays? Is it a problem that everyone wants to solve? To really become the master of time, we should learn to allocate our time reasonably. To achieve our goals, we should consider how much time we have spent on them. How we allocate our time determines the optimal path to achieve our goals. Do you know about the four quadrants of time management? These four quadrants are divided based on a coordinate system: important and urgent, important but not urgent, urgent but not important, and not urgent and not important. We should prioritize and tackle the urgent and important matters first, followed by the important but not urgent ones, then the urgent but not important ones, and finally the not urgent and not important ones. However, in actual action, we often prioritize the "urgent matters" regardless of their importance. In fact, finding the focus of work is not so difficult. I believe that the Pareto Principle can well illustrate this. 80% of our work results come from 20% of the key tasks. Outstanding individuals are those who can identify these 20% key tasks. For example, you can further divide your tasks. If you can only do 5 things a day, what are the most important 5 things? We can contemplate our life plan—what kind of person we want to become and what kind of life we hope to live. What are the 5 things I most want to achieve in my life? What efforts have you made towards this goal? What steps can you take to achieve it? Set yourself a detailed plan. I think the answer to this question is different for everyone. When we have the ability to distinguish what matters and what doesn't, we naturally spend time on things we consider important, and you will also find methods and arrange your time reasonably for this goal. Finally, I hope my suggestions can illuminate your path forward and bring you help.

question: He makes me feel like our meeting is not important, can we be late for the agreed time?
description: The first time we met, he said we would meet at eleven, but he actually arrived after one o'clock. The second time, he said we would meet at three, but he arrived after three o'clock. This makes me feel like I am not being taken seriously. I don't know if he just gave a rough estimate of the time or if he has no concept of time. In any case, he makes me feel like our meeting is not important, but at the same time, I feel like he considers me important. However, not being punctual can be disappointing.

answers.answer_text: Is he really valuing you or not? When you meet, he's always late, and in this matter, you can definitely feel that he doesn't value you. But in other things, he does make you feel valued. This is not contradictory, just like a table of dishes, if only one dish is not tasty, would you refuse the whole table of delicacies? You really need him to value you, but can you accept that he occasionally doesn't value you in some situations or at certain times? Other possible reasons for not being on time: 1) He believes that you consider him important and are willing to tolerate him, so he can be confidently late. 2) It's just a habit of his to be late, not just with you, but with others and other things too. What can you do for yourself? If it really matters to you that your boyfriend arrives on time, you can sincerely tell him that it hurts you. For example, you can say, "Dear, every time we meet, you're always late, and I feel very hurt. Your actions make me feel like you don't value me. Are you willing to take care of my feelings and leave earlier next time?"

OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that an important person to OP has been repeatedly late for their meetings, which makes OP feel ignored. Attribution of the event can generate different emotions and influence the subsequent development. So, when trying to explain and find the reasons for this matter, it is necessary to think comprehensively. OP can ask others if the person is always late for everyone or in any occasion. If being late is due to their own habitual behavior and lack of time management skills, it may not be a reflection of their attitude towards the matter or the level of their respect for people. Perhaps by thinking this way, OP will feel better. 2. Clearly express your thoughts. question: I feel inferior and don't know how to communicate with my parents.
description: 12-year-old girl, recently in the past couple of weeks, I have been inexplicably resistant in crowded places, feeling like I don't belong here. keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: I want to give you a warm hug. Perhaps it's because you're not a local. And your mother told you that you might only stay at this school for a year, which could reduce your sense of belonging to the school. question: How to find your true passion and motivate yourself to be disciplined?
description: Recently, the third-year junior high school student has been spending every day in a state of decadence. I want to be self-disciplined, but I can't control myself and indulge in it. Someone once said that self-discipline is to abandon present desires for greater future desires. I also tried to figure out what I want, but I found that when my dreams are far from reality, they cannot motivate me to move forward. Right now, I need to find something that can support and motivate me to work hard in order to achieve self-discipline. Previously, I wanted to make a lot of money when I grew up, but that goal was not enough to motivate me. I also wanted to get into Tsinghua University, but that goal was not enough to motivate me either. I wanted to be ranked first in my class, but that wasn't enough either. I think the reason is that making money is too far away from us, getting into Tsinghua University is also far away from me now, and I have never been the top student in class, so I haven't enjoyed the treatment of being the first and therefore don't crave it so much. Therefore, I would like to ask how I can get out of this state of decadence and maintain a continuous state of self-discipline. Thank you!
keywords: Growing up, self-growth, student growth, meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Although you say that you spend every day in a state of decadence, I can see that you are actively contemplating your life and have a desire and pursuit of dreams deep within your heart. This shows your self-awareness and proves that you are not inherently decadent. As a middle school student, it is truly rare for you to engage in this kind of introspection. I see that you have envisioned many future dreams but constantly dismiss them, feeling that these dreams are unrealistic and difficult to achieve. However, regardless of the circumstances, your perspective has already glimpsed a far-reaching future, which is quite extraordinary. In lesson 01, let's explore what a dream is. Why do you feel that dreams are difficult to achieve? Let's take a look at what a dream actually is. A dream is a pursuit in our lives, an aspiration for what kind of person we want to become in the future and what we hope to attain. Dreams can be big and numerous, but the most important thing is that they are your inner desires and pursuits, what you truly want for yourself, and not what others want you to become or attain. So when you dismiss a certain "dream," first consider whether that dream is truly what you want deep inside. If it is not what you truly want, then it is easy for you to give up on it. In lesson 02, let us differentiate between dreams and means. Dreams and the process of achieving them are actually two different things. Dreams are the end goal, while the methods and experiences encountered in the process of achieving dreams are the means. Making a lot of money, getting into top universities, or ranking first in the class are all means and processes towards achieving dreams. They are not dreams in the true sense. You should ask yourself: why do you want to make a lot of money? Why do you want to rank first in the class or get into top universities? The "why" behind these desires is what truly brings you closer to your dreams. For example, if my dream is to become a traveler, then the reason I want to make a lot of money is to financially support myself to travel around the world, to various places. Earning money is a means and a condition for realizing my dream. How can I make a lot of money? Perhaps by studying hard, getting into a prestigious university, gaining more social resources, and finding a good job, it would be easier to earn more money. Getting into college is also a means and condition. Do you understand? The reason you so easily dismiss previous ideas and feel that dreams are unrealistic and difficult to achieve is because those were not your true inner desires, and you mistook means and process for dreams. So now you can take the time to rethink and ask yourself once again. In lesson 03, let's discuss how to achieve dreams. When you are able to differentiate between dreams and means, you will know that no matter how far or big a dream is, there is always a possibility to achieve it, and there are methods and paths to realize it. Only when dreams are grounded and made into reality, are they reasonable and possible to achieve. To make dreams a reality, you need to find the methods and paths that lead to them. You can try using the following steps to think about it: 1) Clarify your current situation - Dreams are about the future, but first, we need to clarify our current situation in order to see how far away we are from our dreams, which direction we should go, and how to proceed. You need to understand what your current situation is, what skills and advantages you possess, and what resources and social support systems you have. How will these factors contribute to achieving your dreams? 2) Write down three dreams - Our lives have various possibilities, so we can have more than one dream, and it is highly possible for all of them to be realized. Therefore, write down your three inner dreams on paper, let's call them Plan A, Plan B, and Plan C, and indicate when you hope to achieve these three dreams. For example, my dream A is to become a traveler, dream B is to become a writer, and dream C is to become a popular teacher. They are all equally important and there is no ranking among them. The latter two dreams are not just backup plans for the first dream. This allows for more possibilities in your life and provides more choices and attempts in the process of pursuing dreams. Of course, due to certain objective limitations, some unrealistic dreams need to be discarded decisively. For example, if you want to become a general, but your physical fitness does not meet the requirements for enlisting or attending military academies, it is highly unlikely that you will become a general. (However, if you can enlist or attend a military academy, there is still a possibility of becoming a general.) 3) Reverse planning - Reverse planning is based on the previously listed dreams and timelines. Start from where you are currently and work backward. Typically, divide the timeline into three or five-year intervals. Then, set goals and make plans for each stage. Think about what conditions you need to achieve in order to realize your dreams. For example, I am currently 16 years old and I hope to become a traveler at the age of 26, which is 10 years later. So, working backward, during the age of 22 to 26, I need to earn 1 million dollars to support my global travel. This means I need to have a high-paying job or engage in a side business to earn that money. Besides earning money, I also need to familiarize myself with information about different parts of the world, understand travel planning, have good photography skills, and maintain good physical health, among other things. This is all the preparation I need to make to realize my dream. For the three-year period from 19 to 21, I should strive to get into a good university, study well in my major, improve my skills, and actively engage in internships to prepare for finding a good job after graduation. For the three-year period from 16 to 18, I should strive to get into a good high school, study hard, aim for good grades in each grade exam, and diligently prepare for the college entrance exam in order to have a chance to get into a good university. The above is an example of reverse planning for a dream. Essentially, this involves looking into the future and considering how to achieve it starting from now, setting goals and methods. By reverse-planning from the future to the present, dreams become more tangible and realistic, with many possibilities for realization. It also helps us understand how to proceed on the path ahead. In the process of thinking and planning, you may also discover potential difficulties. How can you solve them? Are your ideas and plans reasonable and feasible? How can they be adjusted? Or should you try a different dream at a certain time? If you only have "dreams" but no concrete goals and direction, no actionable means and methods, then it remains as unrealistic "fantasy." I hope my answer can bring you some inspiration, and I hope you can rethink your future and dreams, finding the direction and path to make them come true. When you find the direction of your life and are willing to pursue and achieve it, you will have the greatest motivation to be proactive and self-disciplined.

Hello~ Share a phrase - "Look up at the stars while keeping your feet on the ground." Having dreams is a good thing, but having a dream doesn't mean I have to achieve it immediately. Many times, what's more important is personal growth in the process of realizing the dream. Whether it's making money, getting into Tsinghua University, or ranking first in class, they all present some difficulty for you at the moment. They are distant dreams that seem somewhat out of reach. So, the most important thing for you now is to set reasonable expectations for yourself. For example, if you can't be the number one in the class, can you be in the top three, top ten, or top thirty? Setting some realistic goals can greatly boost your confidence and motivation. When you feel that you can do it, you will be more willing to do it. So, at this time, don't think too much about so-called dreams, they are not very practical. Goals should not be too high, as that will make them feel very difficult and you might start to hesitate before even starting. Goals should not be too low, as that will make them feel uninteresting. So, how about aiming for a top position in the class first? Best wishes~.

question: Why do I always can't help but cry in the past two months, as an 18-year-old girl?
description: I used to be very cheerful. In the past month, I started having random thoughts, and I began crying involuntarily. It has made me increasingly miserable, even to the point of wanting to die. This feeling has left me utterly devastated.
keywords: Emotions, depressed emotions, fragility leading to tears.

answers.answer_text: Hello, has anything special happened in the past two months that caused such a big change? Emotions don't come out of nowhere, we need to understand where they come from in order to know where they should go. Take some time to think about what happened before the change. What are the things that come to your mind most often when you daydream? In what situations do you feel like crying? These questions might help you find the root cause and understand what is affecting you. Once you identify the root cause, see if you can find ways to solve the problems that are troubling you. If you can't solve them on your own, consider changing your mindset and seeking help from others. Remember, you are not alone. No matter what problems you face, you don't have to deal with them on your own. Seeking help is an act of self-love. If you can't find the reasons yourself, it is recommended to see a psychologist. With the help of a psychologist, you can explore your inner world and figure out what has happened. Sending you a hug, the world loves you! (^_-).

question: Gambling addiction, social anxiety, want to know if there are mental health specialists in Ningbo specializing in these areas?
description: Yesterday, I lost 13,000 yuan, which was the money I saved up for a year. I usually spend money very frugally, only buying necessary things like food and some clothes and shoes. I don't spend money on random things or go to bars, and I rarely spend money on games. But I am very obsessed with making money. In March of last year, I won 300 yuan on a gambling website, but then I lost 6,000 yuan. Then in October of last year, I spent 2,000 yuan on two pieces of clothing worth 100 yuan each just to use a 30 yuan voucher. The day before yesterday, I made about 3,000 yuan, but yesterday I lost almost all of it. Why am I so eager to take big risks with large sums of money in these situations where there is a high chance of losing everything, even though I am someone who considers whether it is cost-effective to eat out or order takeout in daily life? I am only a sophomore in college, and I know I still have the opportunity to make up for these losses, but today I lost another 1,000 yuan. I have lost control, and I want to find a doctor to help me.

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, in fact, the main topic already understands the meaning of gambling. Gambling may have uncertain factors in the short term, and in the long term, gambling is definitely a losing proposition! Elderly people always remind us, "When you enter society, never get involved in gambling, prostitution, or drugs!" But even though we understand these principles, why can't we stop? This is the weakness of human nature! *Greed*, refusing to admit defeat, and refusing to admit mistakes all stem from a mentality of hoping to get lucky. This is similar to the mentality of the elderly who knowingly keep purchasing health products. People often refuse to admit their mistakes and would rather use another mistake to cover up their previous mistakes, but not admit to them. Confucius' disciple Zigong was a successful businessman, and he once said, "A noble person treasures wealth, but only acquires it through legitimate means." The attitude towards gambling may be influenced by your upbringing and environment. You should correct your thinking and understand that money is a medium of material exchange, which should be obtained through real means. The mentality of getting rich quick and speculation should be abandoned. At the same time, you should also learn to control your emotions. If you don't stop, it may ruin your life. San Shan has seen too many people around him whose lives have been ruined by gambling such as "pushing Pai Gow, buying lottery tickets, and betting on sports".

Why do gamblers often struggle to restrain themselves? It's because they always believe that they won't keep having bad luck, and that their previous failures were simply due to not having enough good luck. As long as they keep trying, they will eventually have a comeback. But the reality is that many gamblers end up losing everything and even accumulate a large debt. In truth, the real winners in the casino are always the house, but gamblers are often blinded by the desire to win and the potential gain, and as a result, they rarely see things correctly. Think about why you gamble. It's probably to gain more rewards, which is why you keep investing your money. And in the early stages of online gambling, you may have won, which makes you a little obsessed. Now imagine how long it took you to save up $10,000, and how much effort you put into it. But in the casino, money becomes just a series of numbers, and before you know it, your money is gone. And after losing so much money, don't you become even more determined not to lose? We don't think it's because of our lack of skills, but because of poor luck, so we always comfort ourselves and believe that we can turn things around if we try a few more times. Once we have this mentality, we are bound to lose because the casino is never fair, and many things can be manipulated. One person has a calculating mind, while the other relies solely on luck. Who do you think will win in the end? The world and I love you.

question: How to resolve sexual fantasies towards a male counselor?
description: I have encountered many inquiries like this before, and I personally have experienced it too. I can understand that it is a normal psychological issue. However, I wonder if male counselors can also sense it? I feel unsafe, ashamed, and inferior.

answers.answer_text: Sending you warm hugs (づ′▽`)づ From your description, I understand the following: (1) You feel that you may have sexual fantasies towards male counselors. (2) You feel insecurity, shame, and low self-esteem. Now, here is my analysis and advice, hoping that it can help you: During the counseling process, the counselor's kindness and acceptance make us feel that we are being understood and that we can be at ease here. question: I think my colleague has a terrible personality. I really dislike her. How should I get along with her?
description: I am 90 years old, 158 cm tall, and weigh 120 kg. I have a college degree and have always been told that I am fat. I told them that I want to lose weight. They said, "Oh please, you? You want to lose weight?" They called me stupid. They only graduated from vocational high school, bought an adult college degree, and even claimed to have a bachelor's degree when new people arrived. Their husband is an auxiliary police officer but claims to be a civil servant to others. They don't even understand the difference between centimeters and decimeters, nor can they distinguish between the Korean ethnicity and the Northeastern region. They said that my husband lacks work ability, but my husband graduated from college and earns more than their husband. My family has four apartments from the demolition, while their husband had to take a loan to buy a house and couldn't put their name on it because of too much debt. They have always been nagging at me, so I had a fight with them later on. They also said that I am stingy and just joking with me. They see that I earn more than them, so they even went to negotiate a raise, even though they only work for three hours a day. I have more things to do than them. They clearly have no money, but they said their husband saved 20,000 yuan and gave 18,000 yuan to their child for early education. All their debts are paid by their husband. They even said that their husband never buys them gifts. Last year, they bought a gold bracelet themselves. Their family's conditions are average, with their father being a security guard and their mother retired, but they can't stand seeing others doing well. They even intentionally threw away a document with my name on it in the hallway, but it was actually an export bill of lading. I really hate them. Many of the things they know were only recently told to me by the new personnel. They try to please the new personnel. Anyway, I really dislike them.

answers.answer_text: From your description, it seems that your colleague's personal and family conditions are worse off compared to yours. The reason she often targets you is clearly due to jealousy. She frequently belittles you, spreads rumors, and boasts about her family conditions, which actually reflects her inner feelings of inferiority. Through comparison, she knows that her conditions are not as good as yours or others', which makes her feel insecure. However, she wants to maintain her image and is afraid of being ridiculed by others. She also can't stand seeing others doing well, so she seizes upon your or others' shortcomings to attack and defame, in order to hide her jealousy and negative aspects and protect her self-esteem and reputation. It's difficult to change her personality, mindset, and behavior, and it's also impossible to eliminate her feelings of inferiority and jealousy. Keeping a distance and not responding is the best way to deal with such people. As long as her words and actions don't affect your normal work, try to keep your distance, avoid contact, and stay away from her social circle. Now that you understand the psychological root of her behavior, you can also understand these behaviors. Everyone is at different levels, so there is no basis for comparison, and it's not worth paying too much attention to or caring about. You can calmly deal with her negative words and actions and not waste time and energy on it. If she says things that ignore the facts and hurt you, then boldly refute and present the truth, using facts to counter her claims.

Hello, seeing the details you described, I feel a bit helpless. Obviously, your colleague has some imperfections in terms of personality - narrow-minded, vain, selfish, and cannot stand others being better than herself. Because you are much better than her in various aspects, she can only attack your self-esteem with her figure in order to boost her own sense of superiority. Actually, this kind of person is quite pitiful, being both inferior and arrogant, relying on belittling others to satisfy her own pathetic self-esteem. She doesn't understand that true confidence comes from within and has nothing to do with external conditions. I suggest that you keep a certain distance from her, not allowing yourself to be influenced by her all the time and not letting yourself get caught up in this atmosphere of comparison and competition. If you really can't avoid her, just firmly reject her when you feel annoyed, tell her that you dislike what she says and don't want to hear it anymore. Clearly communicate your thoughts to her and make her stop this boring show-off. Wishing you happiness.

question: A woman is facing divorce and is struggling with whether or not to have children.
description: I am currently torn about getting a divorce and whether or not to take my child with me. He is a boy who is less than 4 weeks old. My husband has a complicated relationship with his mother. They seem like a couple, but they're actually mother and son. I can't take it anymore and am planning to raise the child on my own. I will only remarry if I find someone who will treat me and my child perfectly. Otherwise, I will never marry again in my life. This will provide me with support and security in my old age. But if I don't take the child with me, he won't be close to me when he grows up. Currently, he is being taught to distance himself from me, and there is a possibility that he will be given to his older sister and her family, who have two daughters. I am not willing to accept this, why should I? Furthermore, I am already at an age where it will be difficult for me to have another child, and the risks will be higher. I'm 33 years old and it will be hard to find the right person again. I'm constantly torn and would appreciate any advice.
keywords: Marriage, divorce, in-laws, and contraception beliefs.

answers.answer_text: From the reality you mentioned, it can be viewed from several dimensions: age, children, and remarriage status are all difficult choices. First of all, speaking of age, it's not too old or too young, but it mainly depends on your children and the factor of remarriage. If you remarry without children, age is not a problem. If you remarry with children, the age may be a concern when forming a new family and determining the role of the children. Leaving aside whether the ex-husband wants to or not, the responsibility of parenting needs to be fulfilled, and even if you decide to stay, based on your current temperament, you may not be too willing. So, considering this, you can objectively evaluate various possibilities. While it is manageable to raise children on your own, there will be pressure and personal emotional issues to deal with. Therefore, it is important to consider thoroughly. On the other hand, if you leave the children with the ex-husband, regular check-ins are also possible. Although the family may not be intact in form, the love of both parents will not be absent. Your current dilemma is only about whether the ex-husband can take care of the children well and whether the children will suffer. Taking into account your own concerns, it is difficult for women, and it is even more difficult to raise children. Especially when considering various uncertainties in the future, I hope you won't act impulsively and handle such issues based on your own temperament. There are many examples that tell us that reality is more important than anything else. As for the relationship between your ex-husband and his mother, I don't know their family situation, but one thing is certain: the mother is dependent on her son, a typical "mama's boy." This is why it has come to this point. Your ex-husband's personality has always been lukewarm, which has led to his mother's dominant nature of making decisions on everything. Objectively speaking, your personality and mother-in-law are incompatible. It takes two hands to clap. If we look at it from an urgent and important perspective, the child's issue is the biggest focus right now. Here are some suggestions for your reference: Whether to leave the child or not is only a matter of form. Currently, it may be a matter of face and unwillingness for you. In fact, there is no need to fight over this matter. Since both grandparents want the grandson and son to be together, you can let them take care of the child for now. After all, the child is their grandchild too. It is not ideal for the man to remarry in a situation where he has to take care of the child, so there is no need to worry too much about the stepmother treating the child poorly. As for you, losing one big tree means having a whole forest. There is nothing to regret. It is an opportunity to start a new relationship, and more importantly, to provide yourself and your child with a better hope and future. The economic foundation determines the superstructure, and even with good emotions, it may not be able to withstand reality. So, this point is very important. If you find a suitable partner according to your own wishes, there is no harm in taking the child back later. After all, it is supported, as long as it is within the legal conditions, for either parent, who is more capable of providing a better environment for the child. The child's journey is a long one, and sometimes we have to follow the trend. There is no need to be so rigid in the relationship with your ex-husband and mother-in-law. What you need to do is to live a better life, improve your quality, become a better person, and let them regret it. If you haven't divorced yet, then it depends on the possibility of reconciliation. If the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, then face it bravely. If you truly want a divorce and there is no intention or possibility from your ex-husband's family to save this relationship, why should you force it? You can face the new life only by breaking free. Sometimes, missing out may not be the best option. In almost all family relationships, the relationship between husband and wife is the top priority, followed by the relationship with children, and the relationship with parents is the third. If the order is wrong, it can lead to serious problems. No matter how bad the original family is, we hope that the new family can effectively avoid some negative and unfavorable possibilities. I hope you can get out of the shadow of life soon and embrace the sunshine of life. Best wishes for everything.

question: Boyfriend cheats, apologizes and tries to repent after being caught, how to move on?
description: My boyfriend cheated on me, and then the other girl sent me all the messages and videos. My boyfriend admitted his mistake and begged for forgiveness, promising it won't happen again. But I can't get over it. We have argued countless times, and I can't stand the thought of those details. I want to break up, but I don't want to give up on this relationship because we do have happy moments together and I can feel his sincerity. Is it really because he doesn't love me enough that he cheated? Is it only once or multiple times? I'm constantly torn and in a lot of pain. Should I break up? Is letting go of someone like this the only way to move on?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! From your description, it seems that you are enduring the pain caused by your boyfriend's infidelity. Let me start by giving you a big hug and warming you up in your moment of loss! From your description, it is apparent that you had a good foundation in your relationship, and during the time you spent together, you experienced the warmth of true love and the sincerity of the other person. The memories of your mutual love are deeply etched in your life's journey. What saddens you is that while you were enjoying the sweetness of love, your boyfriend cheated on you. This undoubtedly was a fatal blow and injury to someone who deeply loved him, and it is unfair for every girl in love to face such an outcome. Your boyfriend has already promised to change his ways. You are torn between whether or not to break up. It truly is a painful choice for you to make. Take a moment to calm down and reflect: can you let go of this relationship after a breakup? What were the true motives behind your boyfriend's infidelity? Do you love him, like him, does he truly love and like you? Are your values and beliefs truly aligned? Is he truly worth entrusting your lifetime to? Is he the person you need? Have you truly forgiven him for his infidelity? Are you forgiving the person or the act? You must seriously contemplate and carefully analyze these questions before making a decision. Once your thoughts are clear, the answer will be in your heart, and you won't feel as anxious and helpless. Making a choice is a very painful thing. Be your own master!

Hello, I believe you need to reevaluate this relationship, because even if you forgive now, whether it will be brought up in your unhappy times in the future and become a stumbling block in your future relationship life. If you can completely ignore it, I think it's okay to continue. Or you can give your relationship another chance: a period of time or an event, such as giving another three months. If you are still entangled and unable to accept it, then break up; if you have already let go, then continue. For example, if your boyfriend is still unclear about his affair and hasn't ended it properly, then let yourself go.

question: 25-year-old female, does not trust males and marriage, afraid of having children, what should she do?
description: I did not have a good upbringing. It wasn't until I was diagnosed with schizophrenia that my family showed me nothing but domestic violence (not just physical violence, but also verbal and emotional abuse). Since my teenage years, I have not wanted to get married or have children. I find it difficult to trust the opposite sex and believe that I cannot find happiness (I think I have been brainwashed by my family's verbal abuse), and even if I were to experience happiness now, it would eventually shatter. I am afraid of giving and receiving love, afraid of being hurt, and afraid of pain (due to being beaten). Currently, I have an arranged date and we are in the observation period. Although I have asked him a series of questions and his answers somewhat satisfy me, I still cannot find inner peace. I am still scared of marriage, scared of having children, and want to remain single for the rest of my life, wanting to end it alone. But I also worry that my future self will regret it. I do not have much education and my salary is average. When I mentioned to my family that I want to grow old alone, they were all against it, with my father even threatening to squander the family fortune. I know I am not independent enough. However, I also hope that nobody will scold me; if possible, I hope I can become an independent and strong-willed woman.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I hope the following answer can be helpful to you.️ **First, let's summarize the situation you described as follows: ▲ The upbringing process is not filled with verbal and emotional abuse, ▲ since adolescence, you don't want to get married and have children and find it difficult to trust marriage, ▲ facing a satisfactory blind date partner, but afraid and don't know what to do?** Schizoid personality disorder belongs to the healthy end of the spectrum, often not much different from an average person. In terms of cause, the origin of splitting mechanism can be traced back to the paranoid splitting state commonly found in infants early on. Schizoid personality disorder is similar to avoidant attachment (insecure attachment) in children, where the mother is not only rough and unreasoning, emotionally lacking, but also repulsed by physical contact with the child. Neglectful parents who disregard the child's needs may raise a child who is self-satisfied and avoids others. Individuals who have experienced isolation and neglect in their early years, out of helplessness, may avoid closeness with others and deal with external stimuli based on their own imagination. They often have a mother who has a close relationship or crosses boundaries, and a father who is cold, strict, and violent. Schizoid personality disorder includes two aspects of "splitting": the split between self and the external world, and the split between self-experience and instinctual desires. Analytical theory believes that the schizoid experience of splitting generally refers to a sense of alienation, a dissociation from a certain part of themselves or from real life. The main relationship conflicts for splitting individuals include closeness and distance, attachment and fear. In their subjective world, there is deep conflict in attachment. They long for intimacy but fear being engulfed. They want to maintain distance but cannot tolerate loneliness. They do not want to risk losing an object and also do not want to lose themselves. Therefore, they are unable to engage in relationships and cannot tolerate solitude. The famous fable of "Hedgehogs in the Cold Night" by Schopenhauer is a vivid depiction of the dilemma faced by split individuals: when they approach each other to seek warmth, they prick each other; unable to bear the pain, they separate from each other, but have to endure the cold. This conflict manifests in life, starting with a passionate and short-lived relationship, and eventually ending with long-term avoidance. This dynamic phenomenon can be summarized as, "Please come close to me to comfort my loneliness, but please maintain your distance because I don't want to be intruded upon." Your case fully embodies this point – your inner self desires warmth and love, but you are too afraid of getting hurt to get close to intimate relationships. Therefore, it is necessary to focus on personal growth, cultivate a strong inner self, and become someone who bravely faces life, the future, and intimacy. If you feel that the blind date partner meets your expectations and you are satisfied, then pursue the relationship boldly. Marriage and love are your own matters that require your own decision. Parents cannot choose for you. Faced with such parents, what can we do? We cannot choose, as it is not a matter of choice. The protagonist Su Mingyu in the TV series "All Is Well" has suffered since childhood due to being a girl and having a poor family background. She has two older brothers and has never felt warmth at home. The family used all their resources, even selling the house, to support the eldest brother's education at Stanford University in the United States and to find connections for the second brother to get into a good university and find a job. As for herself, because her brother went to college, her room was sold by her mother and she had to sleep in the living room. Despite being qualified for the prestigious class, her mother did not allow her to attend and insisted that she pursue a teacher training program instead because she is a girl and should rely on marriage in the future. It can be imagined how painful Su Mingyu's internal struggles were. However, she did not let her upbringing hinder her dreams. She remained diligent and worked hard. In the end, she found a sales job, became a white-collar worker, and even climbed up to senior management. These scenes can serve as classic examples for us to learn from. Compensation for what is lacking is needed. From a psychological compensation mechanism perspective, what was lacking in childhood will be desperately sought for in adulthood. If there is a lack of adequate psychological compensation and growth during the upbringing process, the impact can be long-lasting. As adults, regardless of the circumstances, the first thing we need to do is face ourselves, both internally and externally, including parents, family, siblings, etc. We can only have what we already possess, and that cannot be changed. Accepting and growing ourselves is the first step to living a good life. Wishing you the best, and I recommend seeking specialized counseling for psychological development (personal growth). ε I'm here, and the world and I love you.

Hello. Thank you for inviting me to answer your question. First, I want to give you a big hug and send a little warmth your way. I am also a parent, and my son is a few years older than you. I have come across several situations like yours before, and every time I see these kinds of questions, I feel a little emotional. If even a mother hen knows how to care for her chicks, why is it that humans, who are supposed to be intelligent, cannot do the same? I can really empathize with you. I don't know what kind of mindset your parents have. Is it because they favor your brother over you or some other reason? Why do they treat you this way? Having experienced twenty years of verbal and emotional abuse, to the point of causing you to have a split personality, is truly chilling! So, it is understandable that you fear marriage and having children. From a psychological perspective, what you are experiencing is learned helplessness. However, life must go on, and we cannot change the past, but we can change ourselves. I have a few suggestions for you. First, heal yourself. We cannot choose our parents, but we can choose to nurture ourselves and become our own parents. You can arm yourself by learning some knowledge about psychology and make your inner self stronger. I recommend reading books such as "Why Family Hurts Us," "The Original Family," "The Wisdom of Life," and "Encountering the Unknown Self." Books are the mentors and best companions of human beings. Second, enjoy love. People's lives are multifaceted, including family love, romantic love, and friendship. Currently, you may not be able to enjoy family love, which is a major regret in life, but you can make up for it with romantic love. If you encounter someone who likes you, and you also like him, please don't reject it. Seize the opportunity and enjoy love. Third, be a good mother. It is understandable that you do not want to have children right now because you haven't adjusted your state of mind. Your thoughts may change once you have love in your life. Having children will bring you a different feeling and make your later years more fulfilling. If you have children, study well and be a capable mother. Don't let your misfortune extend to the next generation. There are also many books on parenting education. I recommend reading books like "Nonviolent Communication" and "Parenting Awakening." Fourth, forgive your parents. Not all parents are qualified. Being a parent is not easy. Perhaps because of poor family conditions and high life pressures, your parents express their emotions through violence. Maybe they are not good at learning and only use traditional ways of education, which is unintentional. You can communicate with your parents once and preferably write down your feelings over the past few years, so that they can realize and reflect on it. Forgiving your parents means letting go of the past and reconciling with your own inner self. Lastly, I want to share a quote that I like with you: "Nobody is allowed to harm me without my permission!" Hang in there, and I wish you the strength to overcome your difficulties and live a happy and fulfilling life.

Hello, I also have the same thought. I feel that my life is going well and I don't need to find someone to make me angry or share unnecessary troubles. There is no rule that states a person cannot live alone. Being afraid of interacting with males is a psychological issue, perhaps related to your childhood. I dislike boys because a boy in junior high school kept pursuing me, and since then I have found boys to be very scary. So this is a psychological effect. In fact, everyone has good intentions towards you. It's just that when we see some people being too enthusiastic towards us, we feel that they have ulterior motives and reject them time and time again, eventually causing this situation. You can participate in more social activities, get to know more people, go out more and see other people's lives. You can also talk to your friends about your feelings, understand other people's lives more, try to accept a relationship, and let yourself adapt first. Communicate more with others. Having children is not scary. Maybe you have read too many negative stories. A person's life is just repeating over and over again. Having children and getting married is to add some color to your life, to make you feel less empty. When you come home, you will find someone waiting for you, which is also a kind of happiness, isn't it? I wish you, and all of us, can overcome psychological barriers and accept new lives and challenges!

Hello, I admire your strength and resilience from reading about your past experiences. You possess such a strong inner power, and I believe you will become a mentally strong individual in the future. Your goals are clear, so keep striving to become that strong version of yourself! I believe in you, keep going and make some plans to accomplish this goal one by one.

question: Is it my fault for being too kind and allowing myself to be bullied and isolated in college?
description: I was bullied throughout university because I was too easy-going. I felt frustrated and lost my temper, causing everyone to isolate me. When I caught a cold, they all said their immune system was weak and kept their distance from me. What should I do? I'm really annoyed and feel like I'm being subjected to school violence. I feel like the only way to please them is by jumping out of the window myself, but I'm not willing to do that. Why is it that I'm not at fault, yet I have to endure everything? Is it because I'm too honest and easy to bully? I tried talking to the teachers about changing dorms, but they don't care. It's university, and there are still two years to go. Do I have to continue like this, constantly encountering these problems no matter where I go?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, conflicts, roommates and classmates, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~ Give OP a warm hug~ From the description, it can be seen that OP was initially too easy-going, then was bullied, and later became angry but was isolated. When OP was sick, they were also mocked and ridiculed. I can really understand OP's feelings. It seems that OP is usually a very gentle person. There are always people who like us and people who don't like us. Therefore, I hope OP doesn't get discouraged. We can step out of the dormitory, step out of the classroom, broaden our attention, and slowly break free from the constraints of the surrounding environment. Try to find new friends, find people who can listen to us and care about us. Being isolated and subjected to campus violence is not your fault. We can continue to communicate with teachers in depth, explain the ins and outs of the situation. If conditions permit, we can also seek help from the school's counseling center. If we can't change the environment, then let's change ourselves. Find more meaningful things to do and make our lives rich and fulfilling. If you bloom, the breeze will come. Best wishes.

question: After my ex had an affair, I developed a constant feeling of suspicion and doubt in my current relationship. How can I change this?
description: When I was with my ex-girlfriend for a year and a half, we broke up due to her using emotional violence. A few days later, I found out that it was because there was another guy she was interested in at the time, and she broke up with me for him. They got together and even slept together, which was really disturbing for me. Although it has been four and a half years now, and I believe that I have moved on, and have a new girlfriend, I still have this lingering fear. Whenever she acts a little bit distant, I start doubting if she still loves me. It really hurts to see her chatting with other guys on WeChat, and I often fantasize about her cheating on me. Sometimes I'm okay, but when my emotions get really bad, it affects my sleep and work. I feel like this is exhausting for both her and me. Please advise me on how to change this.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, trauma therapy

answers.answer_text: Friend, hello! When I saw your final question about what to do, many people may say that the ex is the ex, and the current is the current, they are completely different, and it is unnecessary to let the pain from the ex affect the current relationship. This is unfair to the current partner and not worth it. So why are we still unable to get rid of the troubles brought by the ex? Let me share my understanding. Firstly, you must have invested a lot of genuine emotions in your previous girlfriend. The more we invest, the more we fear losing because losing means all our efforts are negated. Then we start to doubt ourselves, which is serious. In reality, it may just be that the ex-girlfriend is uncertain about her own feelings, which is why she was entangled with someone else even after having a boyfriend and eventually left you. I remember hearing a saying which put it well: when someone who doesn't love us leaves, the one who suffered the loss is them, not us, because they lost someone who loved them, while we only lost someone who didn't love us. Secondly, when we doubt ourselves, it also reflects our lack of self-confidence. Perhaps in today's society, many men lack confidence, especially when it comes to love. That's why there are so many "simps" who give their all but end up with nothing. Honestly, it's really not our fault, it's the result of certain toxic ideas in society, which have given women blind confidence and arrogance, making them unable to distinguish between reality and the virtual world. I want to say, let them live in their own world, and it's best not to remind them. Lastly, I want to conclude with the words of teacher Chen Guo: when we like someone, we should just be wholeheartedly good to them. As for whether we can end up together in the end, I no longer care, because I've done everything I can, and the rest is up to fate. Being true to oneself is something you can't escape from, what isn't meant for you, you can't hold on to. The world and I love you!

Hello, creator! "Once bitten by a snake, one will be fearful of a rope for ten years" is actually a reflexive self-protection mechanism. Due to past emotional trauma, it has affected your confidence in relationships, resulting in a lack of security in your current relationship. Like many things, self-protection mechanisms are a double-edged sword. They can help us avoid similar harm, but if the mechanism is too sensitive, it can make us overly cautious and lose our rational judgment. First, you need to understand that your ex is your ex, and your current partner is your current partner. Secondly, feeling secure in a relationship should not solely rely on the other person, as no one can constantly deeply love someone every hour of every day, all year round. Loving someone too intensely will exhaust not only yourself but also the other person. You can try to imagine what it feels like to have someone cling to you 24/7, enthusiastic about you like a wound-up toy that never tires. Thirdly, try to learn to understand, respect, and trust your partner. In the world of adults, in addition to love, there is also life, right? Unpleasant things happen in life, such as being criticized by a boss, having conflicts with family members, or feeling unwell during menstruation, etc. You should allow your partner to have moments of sadness, and not equate it with not loving you just because they seem a bit distant. Love does not reset to zero at midnight. It does not require grand gestures every day. Lastly, I hope you can learn to love your partner. Each person's needs for expressing love are different. If you have the time, you can read the book "The 5 Love Languages" and communicate with your partner about the type of love expression you each need. Loving someone in the right way may have a more effective result with half the effort. Finally, if the harm caused by your ex is too great for you to digest and handle on your own, I suggest seeking help from a professional mental health counselor. Good luck! The world and I love you.

Title, hello~ 1. Analysis of the causes of suspicion: 1. Lack of security Due to lack of security and past experiences, they constantly need affirmation from their partners in order to feel loved and secure. When there is uncertainty in the relationship, they become anxious and try various means to seek reassurance. This behavior can make the other person feel difficult to tolerate or even become annoyed. 2. Infatuation mentality "Infatuation mentality" refers to a thinking pattern where one places love above everything else. These individuals focus all their energy and thoughts on love and their partners. This can make them sensitive, emotional, extreme in their actions, and have a radical attitude towards relationships, often confusing whether they are pursuing a perfect love or truly loving the person. 2. Some suggestions 1. Have confidence in your partner Since you have chosen to be together and entered into a relationship, trust your partner. Don't constantly question their whereabouts, who they are with, or whether they have spent time with someone of the opposite sex. As the questioner, you should have a certain understanding of your partner, their character, personality, and habits, so do not easily doubt them. When faced with a situation, try to consider it from their perspective. Think about what you would do if you were in their shoes. By placing yourself in their position, you will be less inclined to doubt them. 2. Learn to express your feelings Instead of questioning or accusing your girlfriend when she enjoys talking with her male friends, you should aim for good communication first. This will make her feel trusted. You can directly express your thoughts, concerns, and how you would like her to respond, letting her know that you care about her rather than trying to control her. Communication When faced with doubts and constant suspicion, it is important to engage in open and positive communication with your partner. Share your feelings, explain the reasons for your anger, express your worries and concerns, and then discuss and find a solution that both of you can accept. Everyone has different ways of dealing with friendships with the opposite sex. If your girlfriend values these friendships and there is no ambiguity in their relationship, you do not need to force her to stop talking to him. Don't let your partner's actions affect your emotions In a relationship, constantly doubting your partner and allowing their actions to affect your emotions is not constructive. Instead of expecting others to provide you with a sense of security, focus on building your own sense of security. When you have a strong sense of security, you will be better able to learn how to love and be loved. This way, your emotions will not be affected by your partner's actions, and you will not have reasons to doubt them anymore. Constantly improve yourself If you tend to doubt your partner in relationships, it is important to continually work on yourself. When you become stronger, you will gain confidence and attract the things you desire. Best wishes~

OP, hello! I can completely understand how you feel. It seems like you are still being troubled by a relationship that happened four or five years ago, indicating that you haven't completely moved on from its impact. For the one who was cheated on and broken up with, the first thing to face is the sudden halt in the development of the relationship, and the need to come to terms with the loss. On the other hand, the one initiating the breakup has already completed the ending and doesn't face such distress. At the same time, the one being broken up with also has to deal with feelings of abandonment, self-worth depreciation, and doubt, all of which can cause a great deal of suffering. You asked about how to reduce the current distress, and here are my suggestions: 1. The breakup in the past had multiple reasons. 2. The current partner and the ex are not the same person and won't have exactly the same behavioral patterns, so you need to be able to distinguish between them. 3. A lack of affection can have various reasons and may not necessarily be a precursor to a breakup. It could also be due to other troubles or physical discomfort. In such situations, it's important for both sides to communicate fully, express what's on their minds, and ask each other about any concerns, rather than assuming things or waiting for others to guess what they're thinking. The next time you have such thoughts, try telling yourself to consider multiple possibilities regarding the situation. 4. If negative thoughts start overwhelming you again, try practicing deep breathing and focus your attention on your breath or the sensations in your body; it might help. 5. Accept that the only constant in this world is change. No one can promise anyone a lifetime together, so focus on living each day well and savoring every moment. Best wishes! FF.

Dear moderator, hello. "Once bitten by a snake, one is scared of a rope for ten years." This applies to anyone. After all, we have a set of self-protection mechanisms since birth, and we adopt evasion, avoidance, anger, fear, and other methods to protect ourselves. That's also why many people, after experiencing intense love, are afraid to love again. However, we also need to understand that everyone's growth environment is different, and we cannot conclude that everyone is the same based on one person's behavior. In an intimate relationship, if we want the relationship to last and develop healthily, refusing emotional abuse, self-change is the most important. Only when we free ourselves from the shackles, introspect our own hearts, and establish a strong sense of security, can we manage a relationship well with anyone. If you can write down the answers to the last eight questions clearly on paper and open up your heart to discuss any issues with your current partner, I believe your relationship will definitely change. Keep going! The following text is applicable to both men and women. The way men and women interact can be mutually beneficial. Do you happen to have watched the drama "Mr. Right"? Jiang Shuying plays a girl who has been hurt in love, unemployed abroad, and meets Song Ningyu on a flight back to China. The man shows his interest in her at first sight, drives her home, accompanies her shopping and eating, buys her flowers and a necklace, and takes her to various parties, making her look like a lady. He even finds her a place to live, taking care of every aspect of her life. Jiang Shuying is lucky to meet such a man, but after a period of getting along, she becomes suspicious and mistrustful of him. In the drama, Jiang Shuying finds out that the house her boyfriend found for her is actually his own. Because of this, they start giving each other the silent treatment, not speaking to each other, taunting each other coldly. Later, they have big arguments and she walks out on him. In our lives, similar scenes often occur. When the husband comes home with a briefcase, the wife quietly walks into the living room and cautiously unzips it to check if he has been having an affair with other women. Or on special occasions, if the wife does not receive the expected red envelope gift, she sulks and pretends not to hear her husband speaking, with a downcast face, causing her partner to be bewildered. The wife cannot stand her husband's silence and relentlessly demands a definite answer and result, while the other half of the couple curls up in their own shell like a snail. The final result is that the husband remains indifferent to everything the wife has done, and the wife, thinking, "I have hinted to you for so long, but you haven't shown any response," loses patience with the man and erupts like a volcano. Whether it is controlling your husband and watching him closely or resorting to emotional abuse, both will make him dislike you more and distance himself from you. So, how can you make your partner feel that you understand him and enter his heart, so that he will love you more? Skillfully using the cave mechanism makes a man feel understood. In psychology, there is a term called the "cave mechanism." When facing pressure, men tend to hide in their caves until they come up with the final solution, and only then will they proactively emerge from their caves. If you disturb him at that time, it will undoubtedly aggravate his burden and make him feel that you don't understand him. At this time, the best thing you can do is focus on yourself, such as reading a book you like, watching a movie you enjoy, or reflecting on the day's events. Men will feel your trust in them. On the contrary, your care and concern will make him feel that you don't believe in his ability to handle his own affairs. A reassuring look or a small action is more effective than a thousand words of nagging. Paying attention to what he likes - In a relationship, wives or husbands may experience two psychological states: imbalance and guilt. One party may feel guilty because they have endured too much, always feeling that what they give and what the other gives cannot be equated. But we should know that giving is never about who gives more; willing and voluntary giving is the best choice. The other state is imbalance. "I have given so much to you, why do you hurt me without appreciation?" Treat others as you would like to be treated. Is what you give what the other person wants? If you originally wanted to have a quiet evening, but your husband suddenly asks you to play a video game with him, you will definitely feel impatient. Spending time on effective communication - Before building a good intimate relationship, we need to become someone who can communicate effectively; otherwise, everything is pointless. Here, I will share eight key questions for effective communication: 1. What do I want? 2. Are there any misunderstandings that need to be clarified first? 3. Which of the emotions I express are absolutely true, and which are imagined? 4. Do my partner's or my emotions feel familiar? 5. How did this emotion arise? 6. How should I respond to this emotion? 7. What feelings lie behind the emotion? 8. Can I respond to these feelings with love? Do you remember these eight questions? They are the premise of building an intimate relationship and effective communication. Find out the problems, respect and understand each other's feelings and behaviors; behind every action, there are hidden needs and motives. Next time there is a conflict in your relationship with your partner or other interpersonal relationships, try using these questions. You will be amazed at their magic. It turns out that our fights are really foolish. They not only hinder the progress of matters but also damage the relationship with the person we love most. In "Mr. Right," Jiang Shuying once had dinner with Song Ningyu at a Western restaurant and complained about her boring meetings with her boss and how she often blamed her wrongly. Song Ningyu constantly responded with "Mm" and "Ah." She knew that her boyfriend was not really listening to her, so she raised her voice, asking him if he was actually listening to her. He looked around awkwardly until he confirmed that no one was watching them, and then he responded to her in the same manner, frowning and sarcastically saying that he couldn't help her with all her complaints. You see, they both complain and vent but never consider each other's true thoughts and needs. They pretend not to care when conflicts arise, but their words are full of criticism, blame, mockery, and complaints.
