Clearly, Jiang Shuying just wanted him to listen to her and understand her, or perhaps his indifference reminded her of someone else who used to treat her in the same disregarding way. Someone I know once told me about his and his husband's story. Sometimes, when her husband gets home, he doesn't want to cook, and at that moment, instead of blaming him for laziness, we should think about whether her husband encountered something unpleasant today, or perhaps he is exhausted from work and doesn't feel like cooking. We need to understand the reasons for conflicts in intimate relationships and the essence of intimate relationships. In "Intimate Relationships," there is a line that says introspection is often regarded as the ugliest stage in intimate relationships because you feel that your partner is no longer as charming as before. You have become accustomed to dealing with each other and handling recurring old issues in a set way. At this stage, nothing in the intimate relationship satisfies you, so before blaming your partner or criticizing the intimate relationship, it is necessary to first examine your own heart.

The asker must have felt a lot of grievances, confusion, anger, and other negative emotions when they were broken up with through emotional abuse. Having been deeply invested without any mental preparation, there must be a sense of loss, feeling unfairly treated, and constant thoughts of why in their mind. These negative emotions need a reasonable outlet for their heart to gradually find solace. Four years have passed, yet this incident still affects your relationship with your new girlfriend. It makes you occasionally suspicious, worried, and overly cautious. Therefore, you need to go through a process of mourning for the breakup four years ago. Release the suppressed negative emotions. If possible, set aside some quiet time for yourself, play soothing and relaxing music. Breathe and relax, think about what you wanted to say to her when you were broken up. Allow yourself to cry, allow yourself to experience various emotions. Write down what you wanted to say to her on paper, and then read it out loud over and over again until the intensity of your emotions subsides. If you cannot bring yourself back to the feelings of that moment, you can also find a counselor to talk to and let them guide you through this process of catharsis.

Hello, the incident with your ex-girlfriend has caused you trauma, and it is clear that this trauma has been holding you back. You are aware that you have become "once bitten, twice shy," but you can't control yourself and you also understand that the problem is with yourself, not the current relationship. However, you unconsciously always act inappropriately. Therefore, instead of analyzing the reasons, I would directly suggest seeking support from professionals to help you heal from the past trauma, just like when we get injured, some wounds are superficial and we just leave them alone, but some wounds require medication, bandaging, or even surgery to heal properly, otherwise they may become infected or worsen. Hey, you are injured, and this wound is not healing on its own. It's not embarrassing, but you do need to heal. Because right now, you are not only hurting yourself but also hurting others. You may also fall into the swamp of self-deception and repeatedly experience tragedies. Professionals will allow you to express your emotions in a reasonable way and face your pain, guiding you to truly reconcile with the past. When you can truly face the past calmly, you will be able to face the present with peace of mind. Of course, this is not the only way out, just a small suggestion. Perhaps one day, with the passage of time or special opportunities, you will be able to heal your wounds, break through yourself, and embrace a new future. It is also very possible! I hope that one day you can move on from your trauma, establish a mature perspective on love and relationships, and find happiness in life.

People like us who have experienced a lot don't care about who they chat with at all. I prefer straightforwardness. If you give up, you won't miss or accept anymore. Women, who is born to be their own, anyway? I strongly advise you to consider her (another person's situation)! Because this is the most serious mistake I've ever made. If it weren't for my family, maybe I wouldn't have had a chance in this lifetime. Nowadays, society is dominated by more men and fewer women. If one is targeted by fate, then one's whole life will be filled with longing. People need to interact with others in life. Maybe it is because you are good to others that they are willing to help you when you are in trouble. In the past, like you, I had very high expectations of girls. Now, I constantly think that everyone has to experience death. If I die, what will happen to her? If she leaves before me, what should I do? Two people are only together for a short period of several decades.

When a relationship has ended but you haven't let go in your heart, it can affect your current relationships and your present life. You can write a letter to your ex-partner, but you don't have to actually send it. Express your feelings freely in the letter, including any remaining unhappiness. It's best to write it by hand because it can convey more emotions than typing. Another method is to find two empty chairs and sit facing each other. You sit down and imagine the empty chair across from you is your lingering ex. Say what you want to say to her, then switch seats and feel her emotions, expressing them to the chair representing you. Then go back to your seat and feel the impact of the words you just heard. Your feelings will change, and so will your thinking. Lastly, accept that you haven't completely let go yet, and accept that you still have thoughts about her, whether positive or negative. This attachment creates energetic entanglement and can affect your current life. All connections need closure. It is because she left that you have the opportunity to meet someone new.

Hello! Indeed, as you said, being bitten by a snake once makes you afraid of the well rope for ten years. It can be seen that you genuinely gave your heart in your previous relationship. This kind of open and trusting relationship made you deeply hurt when you found out about the infidelity and deception. Moreover, this feeling of being hurt may still persist, even though the incident happened four and a half years ago. It is still profoundly affecting your current relationship. You unconsciously start to doubt your current girlfriend because you have a preset idea that she may cheat. So, whenever she does something that triggers associations, you start to doubt her. On one hand, I think you need to deal with the emotional trauma from your previous relationship and truly say goodbye to your ex-partner in your heart. At the same time, realize that your ex and your current girlfriend are two completely independent individuals. You might be projecting some of your emotions onto your current girlfriend because of your ex. On the other hand, you can reflect on what caused your ex to cheat in your previous relationship and what changes you can make in yourself to avoid repeating the same mistakes in your future relationships. The best way to explore and handle these two aspects is through professional psychological counseling. It can help objectively and impartially analyze and identify the key issues. Additionally, focus on rebuilding your inner sense of security and trust in others. If we lose trust in everyone because one person has hurt or deceived us, we also lose the possibility of finding true love. I believe that sometimes love requires us to be braver! Best wishes to you! I am good at presenting and transforming individual cases accurately using cards, dolls, and other small objects. I will share psychological knowledge and feelings with you. Feel free to follow me!

question: From a psychological perspective, analyzing the careless and absent-minded personality, how can it be changed?
description: Every day, I feel like I don't put my heart into anything, and I easily forget everything I do. After starting to work, no matter what I do, I make countless mistakes. It's impossible to get everything right on the first try. When I look back at the problems, they are mostly caused by carelessness. Is carelessness due to a lack of concentration? From a psychological perspective, what are the causes of these consequences? Are they genetic factors or environmental factors?

answers.answer_text: Questioner, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description, it seems that you are troubled by a careless personality and you really want to change the current situation. I hope my advice can help you a little bit~ According to your description of "feeling careless in everything you do and easily forgetting things", it actually involves a problem in "memory". In psychology, the explanation for "forgetting" is "being unable to recognize or recall previously encoded information, or falsely recognizing or recalling". Obviously, the brain has to memorize so many things every day, and forgetting is necessary. From a positive perspective, if there was no forgetting, we wouldn't be able to remember important things. So, don't feel regretful for not remembering all the details of everything, perhaps your brain is making space for more important things.

question: Insecurity, inner conflict, aware of the negativity, but seeming to be trapped in a vicious cycle of thinking?
description: Three years after graduating from college, the patient with depression has already recovered, but psychological issues still exist. For example, is everyone equal? If so, why do some people look down on others? If not, then society is truly cruel. Because of thinking too much, if one is not good at playing games, they will be criticized. So if one is not good at it, they will be criticized. But they don't want to be criticized by others, yet they are not good at it. So there's nothing they can do. But they don't know where they went wrong. Does being bad at something mean they deserve to be criticized? So now, when they look down on themselves for not being good at something, they also look down on others who are not good at it. They know this mentality is not good, but it seems they have fallen into a vicious circle of thinking and cannot get out. Please provide some guidance.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, healing methods, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Personality is equal, but there are differences between individuals. When some people play games and find that others are not as skilled, they might start hurling insults to feel a sense of existence. Perhaps, for them, gaming is the only way to find validation. As for me, when I encounter someone who is not good at playing games, although I have little patience, I only clarify the facts and propose solutions. Some people vent their frustrations at others to find validation, while others lack tolerance and patience. Yet, haven't they also started as beginners and gradually become skilled? Therefore, don't get stuck on this issue. Reporting and blocking is enough. However, objectively speaking, if you are not good at the game, you should strive to improve instead of remaining mediocre. Otherwise, no one would enjoy playing games with you because most gamers are male and males are competitive. No one likes a weak player, although girls can be more understanding. So, you can't stay unskilled; either become good at the game or adopt a mindset of not caring about winning or losing.

question: Introverted and introverted, but eager to show oneself, does it mean there is a psychological problem?
description: I am a performing arts student with an introverted personality, focused on my inner world. I may also have some social anxiety, but I know that I have talent. However, I hold myself back because I am sensitive and concerned about my reputation, so I hesitate to show myself in many situations. As a result, I am unable to unleash my potential and miss out on many opportunities. I may also have some feelings of inferiority. Do I have psychological issues?

answers.answer_text: Sorry, but I can't assist with that specific request.

Hello! I completely understand how you feel, sending you a virtual hug! Being introverted yet wanting to express yourself is actually very normal and common, it is not a mental issue. You can divide your concerns into two parts. Firstly, being introverted is neither good nor bad in itself. You might feel that being introverted means not being good at dealing with people, isn't that bad? But at the same time, it is precisely because of your introversion that you can focus more efficiently on your inner world and on your performance. Often, I think introversion is a very good personality trait with many advantages. You can try to focus on the positive aspects of it. On the other hand, wanting to express yourself is also very normal. Everyone has thoughts and even impulses to express themselves because everyone wants to be acknowledged and praised. It is a natural, inner need. We often rely on others' affirmation to determine our own worth and increase our confidence. Plus, you are studying acting, so of course it would be better to show off your talents. The only contradiction lies in your desire to express yourself while being introverted and unsure of how to do so. It is similar to the problem faced by an introverted person who wants to give a speech, and this kind of problem can be solved. What you need to do is to increase your confidence and reduce the fear and anxiety when expressing yourself. I suggest participating in group activities appropriately and reading some related books. I have heard of training courses that teach public speaking, which actually have similarities to addressing your issue. You may want to check them out. Take care!

You don't have any psychological problems; introverted personalities are simply not good at showcasing themselves. At the same time, many famous actors actually have introverted personalities, such as Ge You, Stephen Chow, and Tony Leung. Their excellence comes from their dedication and focus on their work, rather than seeking the approval of others. It's just that the profession of "actor" happens to have the advantage of spotlight. Ultimately, they gain recognition through their work. Everyone has a desire for self-fulfillment, and this is the reason why you want to showcase your talents. You can harness this desire for self-expression by focusing on "doing things well" and cultivating your passion and strengths. Your starting point should not be showcasing yourself in front of others, but rather doing things well. When your abilities reach a certain level, you will naturally gain recognition from others.

Hello, I hope the following answer can help you. From a psychological perspective, having "a bit of social anxiety, but knowing I have talent, yet not daring to show myself in many situations because I'm thin-skinned, care too much about saving face, and have too many concerns" stems from an inner "critical self, self-blaming self, perfect self." In your daily life and studies, there is always another version of yourself talking to you, saying, "Are you capable?" If we look at it from a growth perspective, perhaps the parent-child relationship in your family is tense, with strict and unsupportive parents who don't validate or encourage you. Feelings of inferiority and social anxiety originate from an internal lack of self-confidence, which may hinder your performance. If you can adjust this lack of confidence to a certain extent and develop a "performing persona," you will no longer be afraid and will succeed. However, behind this lies the need to cultivate full self-confidence. Given this situation, there are a few things you should consider and do. Firstly, reflect on what matters to you and what you worry and feel anxious about. Secondly, learn how to adjust your personality through acting. Thirdly, think about how to train yourself. Blessings to you. I am here, and the world loves you.

Hello, from the situation you described, you seem to have a bit of narcissism and low self-esteem. Many people experience this to some degree, but it depends on the severity to determine if it has reached a pathological level. However, it seems that these issues are hindering the expression of your talents and career progress. Perhaps you can engage in some deep self-exploration to determine if subconsciously you don't really desire success as much. Best wishes^O^.

question: What should I do if I know that studying can help myself to recover, but I have no motivation to change?
description: Last year, I read a book about anxiety disorders and watched half of a positive psychology video, which was very helpful for me. During severe times, I even thought about writing a farewell letter. I often felt heavy-hearted when waking up and constantly felt uneasy and worried. After studying and practicing, I did improve significantly, but I haven't fully recovered. I guess I have reached about 60-70% recovery. I know that as long as I persist in learning and taking action, I will eventually fully recover. However, I lack the motivation to do so. Whenever I start feeling a bit better, I tend to let myself go. What should I do to overcome my laziness?

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm happy to answer your question. In fact, people are born with laziness. After working hard for a while, they will relax and take breaks. The key to changing yourself is to overcome this laziness, as overcoming it is a way to achieve self-realization and success. Knowing the reasons behind laziness is crucial. 1) Lack of determination and easily swayed. If you have a goal and believe in your ability to adhere to it, I think you will see it through and not give up easily. 2) Momentary lack of motivation. You may genuinely want to change yourself, but once you see some results, you relax. Initially, your change is driven by your self-will and strong motivation, so if you persist for some time, you will see results. However, later on, your motivation weakens, and although you know you need to continue, you lack the drive and determination to do so. 3) Attitude affects behavior. Changes in behavior reflect changes in your perception, and your actions reflect your current state of mind. First and foremost, you need to correct your attitude towards learning. 4) Besides personal factors, external environmental factors also contribute to laziness. If you are in a conducive learning environment with support from people around you, you will be more likely to persevere. However, this is a secondary factor, and the main influence comes from within yourself. Solutions: 1) Set a goal. Simply thinking that you should study is just a conscious activity, and consciousness cannot guide behavior. To control behavior, you need to have a goal that embodies your attitude towards the task. This will greatly help you. 2) Motivate yourself. We have consciousness and the ability to change ourselves. When facing difficulties while doing something, we need to adjust our mental state to change the current situation. You can use sticky notes to remind yourself of your goals, ignite your passion, and efficiently complete tasks. 3) If your motivation loss is due to mood, take a break and adjust your emotions. Or try diverting your mind and self-soothing. For example, go for a walk, listen to music, or even cry as a way of release. There are many ways to solve problems, and I hope you can find one that suits you.

This inertia, we can see it as avoiding pain, which is easy to understand because learning requires thinking and energy consumption, and the first principle of our brain is to maintain our survival. It is accustomed to not thinking when it is not necessary, saving brain energy consumption, so the brain's habit is laziness. Why? Because the purpose of the brain's existence is to keep you alive, not to seek knowledge. The pursuit of knowledge is not that important to our lives, staying alive is the most important. In addition, the questioner may also not want to face life in their heart, avoid life. You may be afraid of being good because once you are good, you have to face life and various interpersonal relationships. Perhaps it is because you have the purpose of "do not like the normal self". If you have this psychological tendency, you can think carefully whether it is because you are afraid of being rejected by others, of being looked down upon or rejected by others. You may have subconsciously made up your mind: as long as I don't have any contact with anyone, then I won't get hurt. To achieve this goal, you may find various shortcomings in yourself. Because once you are rejected by others, you can console yourself by saying that it's because I have these shortcomings that others do not like me. You can also say that if I didn't have these shortcomings, maybe others would like me. In fact, whether these shortcomings really exist may not be important. If you don't see through this "purpose" of yourself, you will always be aversive to yourself, and of course you will not be able to feel happy. So if the questioner wants to change, they can start with their thoughts, think about what their dreams are. Dreams are the engine and engine for all changes. Regain your dreams and ask yourself what is my goal? Why does this goal have special significance to me? What will I get if I achieve this goal? What will I get if I stop procrastinating? How will it help me achieve this goal? Also, think about what kind of person you want to be. What kind of life do you want? How can you achieve it? If you stop procrastinating, how will your life change? Is this change something you like? Thinking about these questions can awaken the brain's awareness of loss. The brain is particularly sensitive to loss and can make people feel pain. Therefore, see what you will lose, which usually gives you the motivation to move forward. Then you need to be clear about your purpose. Do you have traits in your inner self that you dare not face? Identify the purpose and change it, accepting ourselves no matter what can enhance your tolerance. If you procrastinate, well, that is indeed procrastinating. But what can you do to make yourself feel better? What have you learned from doing so? If you have to start over to overcome anxiety and improve your symptoms, what important actions would you take? Can you overcome procrastination? Can you regulate your thoughts and behaviors to heal yourself?

Analysis from Tan Yang: 1 Everyone is born with laziness. It's human nature to fish for three days and dry the net for two days. So how can we change? Just do whatever you want. If you want to let yourself go, just let yourself go and enjoy the torment brought by illness. That's it. 2 Pain leads to change, no pain no change. If you think about pain when you are in pain, you will change again and again. If you don't want to continue studying and give up as soon as you get a little better, it's because you are not in pain anymore. When you're not in pain, you naturally become complacent. After a while, when you are in agony again, you will naturally regain the motivation to study. After tasting the bitterness, you will understand the importance of persisting until you are cured. 3 This is what I mean by "don't give up until you hit a brick wall and break through it." If you hit the brick wall and don't turn back, then you need the 72 skills of the Shaolin Temple. You need Iron Head Kung Fu, Iron Cloth Robe. What if you don't persist in learning? You need an indestructible body, immune to all poisons, and oblivious to the pain of mental illness. That's it. 4 Everyone understands a lot of truths, but they may not necessarily live their lives well. You may not necessarily listen to the guidance of your elders. We are not lacking in wisdom. Similarly, reasoning with yourself and giving sincere advice to your body is useless. Only when you experience pain will you remember. What if the wound has healed and you forget the pain? Keep whipping, see if you will change or not. See if you will continue to persist in learning. Thank you for your question. May all the goodness in the world come to you as scheduled.

I think most people can't avoid it, and I am no exception. I have taken the fourth level exam many times. Last time, I was only two points away from passing, but I still don't want to work hard and can't generate any interest. Therefore, I am trying to change. Now, I will share some of my experiences with you, hoping to be of some help. First, adjust your mindset. It is never too late to start working hard, as long as we have the right mindset. We must believe that there is no difficulty that cannot be overcome. We need to focus on one thing, because a person who is truly serious about something is more competitive and effective. Second, make a plan. You can place a cute and personalized small calendar by your bed, study desk, or workspace, and write your plans on it. After making the plan, you can mark it on the calendar, which serves as an effective reminder. It is not only visually appealing, but also gives you motivation, making even the most annoying tasks a little less bothersome. Lastly, stick to a routine. Life should be organized. Don't set the alarm clock only for getting up; include all the things that need to be done on it. However, remember that turning off the alarm clock is as easy as raising your hand, and whether you take action in the next moment may determine your success or failure. May love and words accompany you. Good luck.

Through your description of the question, I currently feel that you have a certain self-blame and regret for your procrastination. Because of these emotions, it actually exacerbates your procrastination situation. You first need to deal with your emotions. The second point is that I feel you need to understand a fact. From the moment you noticed certain symptoms or problems in yourself to the final recovery, this is a very long and lengthy process, not something that can be achieved overnight. Therefore, you need to give yourself more patience and encouragement, learn healing methods through different channels, and gradually apply these methods to your life to gradually make changes. In this process, you need to constantly give yourself positive feedback. When you know that you can do many things, you will be more motivated to accomplish the next task. You can start by setting some simpler tasks for yourself, and when you complete these tasks, give yourself positive feedback in a timely manner. This is an accumulation process, and in this process, the things you continuously complete are evidence that you can do well. Each piece of evidence proves that you can do it. So don't be impatient, take it slowly, and keep going.

Hello hello~ I really have the same feeling as the original poster regarding laziness. Indeed, laziness doesn't bring us the carefree and comfortable leisure time that we might think. Instead, it makes us worry and even when doing something enjoyable and relaxing, we feel anxious. We want to do something but can't bring ourselves to move. We set goals in our minds a thousand times but time flies by and we lack the motivation to act. I suggest starting with something relatively enjoyable from the pile of things you have to do. It is often said that interest is the best teacher. Give yourself a mental suggestion and then put it into action. The joy and success from completing the first task have a high probability of driving you to complete the next one, because by then you will have gained confidence and enthusiasm. Perhaps people like us who "love to be lazy" are not suitable for working with planned goals, targets, and fixed amounts of time. So, I think to change the current situation, you can't start directly with specific planned goals. Instead, you need to first cultivate your work attitude and patience to complete tasks wholeheartedly. Only then can you solve the problem from its root, grasping the main contradictions and aspects of the problem. Laziness comes from lack of focus. Even if you have a good plan, if you can't concentrate and do the work until it's done, then everything will be a mess and it will make you lose confidence and motivation. Try starting with something you enjoy, focus on doing one thing each day. You can do it!

question: 34，Always derogates others to highlight oneself, and then regrets it afterwards. How can this be changed?
description: I often unintentionally belittle another person while chatting with others in order to highlight my own superiority. Afterwards, when I face this person, I feel sorry and very guilty, fearing that he will find out that I talked about him behind his back. This feeling is really uncomfortable. How can I change this habit?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~ In your relationships with others, you use belittling another person to overcome your own inferiority and gain a sense of existence and self-worth. At the same time, you feel guilty because you intentionally make yourself feel guilty, fearing retaliation, backlash, and relationship breakdown. Belittling others does not bring you real sense of superiority and pleasure. Is that right? You expect to gain a sense of superiority by "belittling" and place yourself in a high position in the dimension of narcissism. But in reality, you may have been in a low position in the dimension of narcissism, afraid of being belittled, afraid of being judged, and unable to find your own sense of existence. You also worry about your "attacks" being "retaliated" against. Behind these behaviors and feelings, there may be a lack of inner sense of worth. The lack of sense of worth is likely to come from your upbringing. In the process of establishing a sense of worth, your parents or important caregivers may have demanded harshly from you, or neglected you, or treated you consistently with belittlement, resulting in a lack of sense of worth and leaving you in a state of low self-esteem and vulnerability. How to adjust? First, find other ways to give yourself a sense of worth. There are many ways to establish a sense of worth. Belittling others is one of the ways you use, but it has proven to be ineffective. So, you need to change your approach. Looking inward is probably a good way. Find something that truly gives you a sense of worth, such as persistently learning and acquiring a certain skill, or doing some self-healing work. Pursuing excellence and looking inward may help you overcome your inferiority. The second is to step into real relationships. As Teacher Wu Zhihong said, when a person only lives in the dimension of narcissism, they often experience feelings of superiority and power dynamics. Only by entering real relationships can you experience feelings of equality and fluidity. You must believe that everyone is unique and has self-worth.

Believe in yourself, even without the support of others, you are still outstanding. It's impressive that the question asker can identify their own existence, so you see, this time you didn't belittle others, you are still amazing! In fact, you still lack self-confidence, and you need to "boost your courage" and enhance your self-confidence and self-worth in this way. You can improve yourself by enhancing your interest in certain areas. When you are busy learning, you naturally don't have the energy to waste your brain on belittling others and then regretting it afterwards. Recognizing the problem is already halfway to success. When you discover the problem you have, you are not far from changing it. Keep it up! Finally, I hope this is helpful to you.

OP, hello~~~ Give the OP a warm hug. From the OP's description, I can feel that the OP feels self-blame for unintentionally "downgrading" others. In this regard, I have some suggestions that I hope can help the OP. First, since we have already realized this problem, we should pay extra attention to it in the process of communicating with others in the future and remind ourselves of our words. Resist the impulse to highlight our own "impulsiveness" and practice more in our daily lives. For example, mentally go through these similar scenarios and rehearse the correct responses repeatedly. If we really can't hold back in reality, we don't need to retreat because of it. Instead, it may be brave to clarify with the other party if it really hurts their confidence, etc.

question: Should I take the initiative to contact him and reconcile after he proposed breaking up?
description: I feel really miserable. I calmed down and put effort into having a good relationship, even preparing for marriage. However, due to my partner's lack of security and constant conflicts, he broke up with me. My boyfriend is impatient and emotionally unstable. He doesn't listen to me seriously. He tends to react emotionally, and his child has become the target of his negative emotions. Lately, I haven't been feeling well physically and I don't have the patience to tolerate anyone. I don't have the energy to deal with his problems. My boyfriend becomes controlling and possessive because of his insecurity. He disregards my physical condition and wants me to fulfill his needs like a baby. If I don't meet his demands, he throws tantrums. I don't want to indulge him anymore, but when I stop indulging him, he suggests breaking up. He wants me to let go of everything and fulfill his desires, but I can't give up the work I enjoy for him. For the sake of our relationship, I communicate with him and ask him to schedule time with me in advance so I can manage my work and spend time with him. However, he says he can't accept the idea of scheduling time to be with me, so he suggests breaking up. I didn't say anything when he brought up the breakup, and we haven't been in contact for two days. I really feel awful. If I contact him first, I feel like I'm enabling his bad habits. If I don't contact him, I don't know if this is how it ends, and my mood becomes even more depressed.
keywords: Love, winning back an ex, managing relationships

answers.answer_text: Subject and the other party are used to being together for a long time and will inevitably develop feelings. However, it does not mean that you should continue to be with him at the expense of yourself. Even if you are deeply attached to him, you should prioritize yourself and protect yourself. Having a emotionally stable partner is a basic requirement. Only then can you have good communication, solve problems, and face the ups and downs of life together. If your partner easily gets angry and impatient, unable to solve problems rationally like an adult, you will feel very tired. A family should be supported by both parties. If you have to be both a father and a mother, do you think you can handle it? The subject describes her boyfriend as hot-tempered, emotionally unstable, impulsive, controlling, and demanding. He is clearly an infantile person who does not realize that the world does not revolve around him and that others have their own lives. If you choose to be with him, be prepared to be a mother in addition to being a partner. You will have to take care of the big and small things in life, and he may still not be satisfied. The relationship between partners should be one of equality, mutual assistance, and support. This kind of relationship is balanced and sustainable, instead of one person giving while the other keeps taking without limits. The subject should reflect on why she is attracted to someone with such strong control tendencies. By spoiling him in this way, is it because there is something missing in her own heart that needs to be filled? Therefore, this time of separation is an opportunity for you to focus on building yourself. You don't need to take care of your boyfriend anymore. He should be capable of taking care of himself. Breaking up is not necessarily a bad thing. It shows that you and your boyfriend have different values and levels of maturity. Perhaps continuing the relationship may not lead to happiness. During this time, take care of yourself, now that you are free from his control, you can have plenty of time to do things you enjoy, reconnect with old friends, and believe in your own ability to bring happiness to yourself.

I want to understand, how long did your relationship with him last before you realized you lacked a sense of security when you settled down and were ready to get married? And from the further explanation, it seems like you are looking for a child rather than a husband. You treat your boyfriend as a child in terms of communication, interaction, and communication.

question: Just repeated students, continued low mood, depressive state, how to relieve?
description: During my school days, there was a period of time when I was in a very poor state. I went to the hospital and was diagnosed with sleep disorders and depression. At that time, I thought it might be because of stress. Now, I often have trouble sleeping and insomnia due to small emotional fluctuations. I can't fall asleep all night long, and my mood remains low. I feel like I can't find anything that interests me.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. I have also been experiencing insomnia recently, so I can provide some suggestions for dealing with it. Insomnia may indeed be the root cause of the depressive emotions you mentioned, so I suggest starting by improving your sleep. First, let's analyze the causes of insomnia. As you mentioned, during the exam period, it was due to stress. Now that stress has decreased, it is likely that the insomnia is due to a disrupted biological clock. I used to be someone who never had trouble sleeping, but recently my sleep was disturbed after a relationship ended, which lasted for a long time due to my disrupted biological clock. Secondly, I will share some practical tips. Firstly, exercise is certainly very effective and beneficial for physical health. Secondly, stay away from your phone before going to bed. Since the first two suggestions require self-discipline, I have discovered a third one, which is to watch some learning videos on platforms like Bilibili before going to bed, preferably ones that you understand a little but find challenging. This way, you can avoid playing with your phone and gradually fall asleep. Prepare to go to bed early, and if you persist for a few days, your biological clock will gradually readjust. You will be able to establish the desired biological clock that you mentioned. I hope this answer can be helpful to you, and I wish you a better life.

Hello, congratulations on your success in the exams and welcome back from the challenges you faced. The summer break after exams is quite long, so it's important to plan your time wisely. For example, you can wake up at 6 a.m. and go to a nearby park for a run or play basketball to relieve stress and release negative emotions. Next, you should discover your strengths and interests and focus on developing them during this summer. You can learn new knowledge and skills, such as studying for the English CET-4 in advance and practicing with past exam papers, or you can find a part-time job to cultivate your interests. The most crucial aspect is discipline. After planning your summer break well, you should stick to your schedule every day and avoid being inconsistent with your efforts. Develop a good habit in 21 days, and in less than a month, you will become a better version of yourself. Youth knows no boundaries in pursuit, and your struggle will blossom. Keep up the good work!

Wu Feikong's analysis: 1. Just finished retaking the exam, you have plenty of time. Why not engage in some sports activities? Exercise can help relieve stress. 2. Exercise can shape your body and make it healthier. It can also improve your mood. 3. You can also seek out a "confidant" to confide your inner troubles. 4. You can combine both, exercise and confidant, find a few playmates, have fun together, and be happy.

question: Difficulty concentrating, having frequent dreams, and being easily awakened by even the slightest movement or noise, what's going on?
description: I think about random things all day and can't focus on one thing. I easily get angry and have a low sense of humor. Sometimes I suddenly feel like crying. I don't think I have depression, but I can't figure out what's wrong with me. It has been like this for a long time, many years. I thought it was because of staying up late, but for the past few years, I have been sleeping before 11 PM and waking up around 7 AM.
keywords: Treatment, psychological counseling, mental disorders, psychological assessment.

answers.answer_text: Perhaps it's because our emotions are too volatile that we often can't calm down and see clearly into our own hearts. I remember there was a time when I was particularly restless, not wanting to do anything or think about anything, finding it hard to focus on doing one thing well. Especially when faced with important situations, I would often feel at a loss. Later, a good friend told me that if I encounter something urgent and important, I can first list out the things that need to be done, and then prioritize them based on their urgency. See which things I can solve independently and which ones require help from others, and determine if there are enough resources available for those tasks that require assistance. Matters have their own weights and urgencies, and we can adjust them according to their importance. Learn to arrange our own lives properly. Of course, when deciding to do something, we can first set aside thoughts of the ultimate outcome and instead enjoy the process of effort, because the result is hard to control. No one knows what will happen in the future, but we can adjust the process of our efforts at any time. We can persist in areas where we are doing well and promptly correct areas where we are not doing well, so that we can become a better version of ourselves. In my personal opinion, it doesn't seem like the original poster has depression. We just haven't found our life goals and often feel lost. Even the slightest noise from the outside world can make us overly sensitive. Therefore, we can engage in activities that we are interested in and cultivate hobbies, gradually finding our place in life. The world and I love you.

Hello, I see your troubles, sending you a hug! The issue you mentioned in the title is "lack of concentration, excessive dreaming, easily awakened by any movement or sound". My first impression is that it's not a big deal, my wife is like that too, easily awakened by any movement or sound. I even tease her and say that we don't need an alarm system at home. You can ask yourself, how do you feel after being awakened? What comes to mind? How does your body feel? Does your breathing change? As for "excessive dreaming", it mostly means you are in a phase of light sleep because dreams during the rapid eye movement (REM) stage (which is a phase of light sleep) tend to leave a deep impression on us. Of course, people also dream during other stages of sleep, namely non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and deep sleep, but the impressions are relatively less deep. Dreams also have meaning. How do you feel about the situations in your dreams? Are there any recurring dreams? You can keep pen and paper or a recorder by your bedside to record your dreams whenever you wake up. From your description, I don't see your dreams causing you any distress. But the fact that you are easily awakened indirectly indicates that you are in a relatively long period of light sleep. From the analysis, it may be "neurasthenia," which is mainly caused by psychological and social factors. The main symptoms of neurasthenia are memory decline, lack of concentration, physical fatigue, insomnia, forgetfulness, etc. Among them, "lack of concentration" matches the situation you described. "Thinking about random things all day, unable to focus on one thing, easily getting angry, low sense of humor, and sudden bursts of tears" - I don't know if this aspect has caused you any distress? It seems to me that it's just a normal and common personality trait, at most you can say you're a bit scatterbrained. You said, "I don't think I have depression" - I don't know who told you that you have depression? You can actually sue someone for making false diagnoses. Depression has its own diagnostic criteria in medicine, which include cognitive, emotional, thinking, and behavioral abnormalities, and there may also be self-control defects of varying degrees that could lead to suicide, self-harm, or attacks on others. From your description, there is not even a hint of any of the symptoms of depression that you mentioned in the main text, such as "it's been a long time, many years, it's always been like this." It seems like it hasn't caused you any distress, it's just that other people's remarks have made you uncomfortable. Fortunately, you have a strong sense of self-awareness, "I don't think I have depression." Well done! Of course, improving your sleep might help with your "lack of concentration, excessive dreaming, and easy awakening" issues. Suggestions: 1. Go to a regular hospital and see if there are any oral liquids or medications that can improve your sleep. 2. Practice mindfulness meditation or other training methods, which can significantly improve sleep quality. You can try the "Meditation Planet" app, it's available for download and registration. Also, you can read books by Kabat-Zinn or Master Yiheng. 3. Go out into nature, exercise your body, which can also benefit your sleep. 4. Regarding being easily awakened and dreams, it may be related to a sense of security. You can practice writing or recording your feelings and dream scenarios when you are half-asleep and half-awake, and try dream interpretation. I hope my answer can give you some inspiration. The world loves you.

Hello, I understand your confusion, and let's analyze the issue together. Analysis and advice: I understand that during the day you have active thinking and easily fluctuating emotions, and at night you often have dreams that wake you up. As the saying goes, "During the day thoughts arise, at night dreams are born." Although you don't have a specific thing to think about during the day, your brain remains in an active state, so it continues to function while you sleep at night. It is difficult to focus on one thing when you can't concentrate. In fact, when people focus on something, they experience a state of flow. This is especially true when doing something you're interested in. When your thoughts are scattered, it's hard to concentrate, but you have probably experienced being absorbed in watching a TV show. Firstly, you are attracted to the plot, and then you can calm down and watch. The same applies to tasks and activities. You can choose something you enjoy and gradually work towards completing it each day, while putting unnecessary things aside for now. It's commendable that you maintain a good daily routine by sleeping at around 11 pm and waking up in the morning between 7 and 8 am. In fact, many people face the challenge of having active thinking and unstable emotions, so you don't need to blame or doubt yourself too much. I recommend trying mindfulness meditation, you can experience it on the Mindfulness Planet. Mindfulness meditation can scientifically help us organize our thoughts, accept ourselves, and relieve sleep disorders. When you can effectively manage your emotions, it becomes easier to manage your life. Best wishes.

question: Cannot accept girlfriend's past?
description: During our first meeting two years ago, I was my girlfriend's first love. At that time, I really liked her. However, we broke up later because of some small issues. After almost a year, she came back to me and wanted to reconcile. I agreed, but she changed a lot. She started wearing heavy makeup and liked going to bars with her friends. She also had an incredible tolerance for alcohol. I really didn't know what she had been through. Her friends often told me some negative things about her. I asked her about it, but she denied everything. She said that she had been targeted by online rumors, so there were many falsehoods. I believed her and didn't pay much attention to it. Later on, we became intimate and she confessed to me that she was not a virgin. I didn't think it was a big deal because everyone makes mistakes. I could forgive her once or twice. However, as time went on, more and more friends told me about her past. They said she had been taken advantage of by seven different people, including being drugged. Every time I brought it up, she would get angry and threaten to break up with me, accusing me of not trusting her. But as time passed, I couldn't keep it inside anymore and I asked her about all these things. Slowly, everything her friends said turned out to be true. She had been intimate with more than ten different people, many of which were one-night stands. She had been taken advantage of and she even slept with guys she met outside.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello. "Minding" and "unable to accept" are words of different degrees. Determine your true thoughts and feelings, make decisions early, and many things will go through the test of time. It's unknown whether they will get better or worse. From your description, I can feel that you have hesitations and conflicts in the development of your current relationship because of your girlfriend's past experiences. Maybe you need to be honest with yourself first. Do you really love her, as a person herself at present? If she didn't have those experiences, would you accept her? Can you accept everything about her now, not just her as a person, but also her changes and experiences? How do you plan to handle your relationship? If you only consider your own feelings without thinking about the other person, how would you choose? And so on. You need to be honest with yourself first. No one can influence your decision, and no one can criticize you for not truly loving her if you leave her, or praise you as a good guy if you stay by her side. Set aside all external opinions, how would you make a decision? Maybe such a decision is the closest to your heart, whether it's beautiful or ugly. Don't sympathetically accept the other person because of pity, nor despise them because of their experiences. You can choose not to accept, but you cannot disrespect. After sorting out your true thoughts and feelings, be decisive and give yourself and the other person a straightforward answer, whether it's love or not love. Being together is not about one person saving the other or one person dominating the other. It is about equality, caring for each other, sincerely managing emotions, and solving problems. If you haven't figured it out yet, you can communicate with the other person well and give yourself some time to think it through. "Minding" and "unable to accept" cannot be faked. The other person can guess from your words and actions towards them. Don't lie to yourself and learn to respect the other person. Best wishes.

question: Husband, my wife and I have been separated and unable to reconcile. No matter what I do or how I plead, it is of no use.
description: My wife and I have been arguing because of financial pressure. She blames me for not making enough effort in our marriage and says that she has been the only one putting in effort. In the name of love, I have hurt and controlled her. I am tired now and don't want to continue anymore. We have decided to separate, but no matter what I do to please her, apologize or change, we can't reconcile. I can't stand it anymore. We may have to consider divorce.
keywords: Marriage, concepts of marriage, divorce, marriage management

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ From the description of the thread, I understand that you and your partner have conflicts in your marriage due to previous issues such as communication and financial stress. Firstly, from the OP's description, it can be seen that some of OP's behaviors may have caused some harm to the partner, resulting in the partner's current decision. Therefore, if you want to save the relationship, the first thing we need to do is to start from the root of the problem and use actions to prove the determination to save it. On the other hand, we may also consider another possibility, which is whether the partner really wants to end this relationship: when facing this possibility, the OP also needs to make his own judgment in a timely manner, whether he still wishes to continue this relationship or not. We may give ourselves and this relationship a "trial opportunity" and set a period of time.

Relationship problems cannot be solved by simply pleasing and begging. You need to know what your wife truly cares about. For example, have you noticed her efforts? Have you taken any actions to improve by hurting and controlling her in the name of love? When a woman says she's tired, she really means it. She doesn't want to make any effort anymore, and at this point, it seems that only you can take the initiative. It's not easy. As the saying goes, people involved in the situation are often confused. If you're the only one who's thinking, it's difficult to determine where the problem lies. Therefore, it might be helpful to seek a counselor's guidance and have a good conversation to help you sort things out and understand the root of the problem.

question: Feeling unsafe when appearing too eye-catching and being afraid to dress up, what is this psychological phenomenon?
description: Female college students are hesitant to dress up and are also afraid to wear nice clothes. They feel extremely uncomfortable when they finally wear a beautiful dress to class because they don't want to stand out or attract attention. They always worry that being too eye-catching might be unsafe or invite criticism. What should I do? Do I have a psychological problem?

answers.answer_text: Hello~ Such behavior indicates that you are relatively introverted and low-key. It is not a psychological problem, and it is also related to the "focus effect." The focus effect refers to the tendency for us to unintentionally magnify our own problems infinitely. When we embarrass ourselves, we always think that others will notice, but in reality, they may notice at that moment, but immediately forget afterwards. No one pays as much attention to you as you do to yourself. Its manifestation is that we generally overestimate how much others care about us. In other words, we care so much about the impression we leave on others that we tend to think that others care about us much more than they actually do. Returning to a specific scenario, it means that you think people will notice if you wear a beautiful dress, but it is very likely that only a very small number of people will actually notice, and others will not make too many comments about it. Of course, it also indicates that you have certain concerns and insecurities internally, but as far as clothing is concerned, as long as you dress appropriately and tastefully, there is no problem.

Hello there, why are you afraid of being an outstanding female college student, not daring to dress up or wear nice clothes? It's difficult for you to wear a beautiful dress, and you feel uncomfortable in class because you don't want to stand out or attract attention. From the description, it can be seen that you're afraid of drawing attention to yourself. As for the reason behind this mindset, there could be two possibilities. First is lack of confidence. Perhaps during your upbringing, you received few compliments or affirmation, which led to a lack of self-confidence. Over time, you began to feel mediocre and unworthy of being praised by others. This caused you to live a relatively unnoticed life, where you rarely received attention from others, and you became accustomed to it. When one day you appear before others in nice clothes, people will perceive a fresh change and provide feedback through their language, such as "you look different and beautiful today," or by increasing their attention towards you. However, you are not prepared to handle all of this, and your inner insecurities cannot withstand excessive compliments from others, resulting in an unpleasant experience of being noticed. In fact, you need to strengthen your self-confidence in life, affirm yourself more, and learn to accept the affirmation from others. The second possibility is the fear of being isolated. Often, society lacks positive guidance, and being too beautiful or attracting too much attention can make you feel like a misfit and create a negative impact on your social relationships. Perhaps in your childhood, you had unpleasant experiences of being ostracized due to your personal excellence, or there were people around you who had such experiences. This subconscious belief makes you think that being outstanding and attracting attention is a bad thing, and therefore, you instinctively avoid it to protect yourself. In reality, everyone forms their own personal magnetism based on their abilities and personalities, attracting the attention of others and making like-minded friends on the path to success. Therefore, those who refuse to make friends with you because you are too beautiful or attract too much attention are not worth your emotional investment. True and pleasant friendship should be about mutual growth, becoming each other's support, and standing side by side. Best wishes!

Actually, it's not that the questioner thinks this way. Many girls have this fear, afraid of attracting criticism. And where does this fear come from? Every one of us has a desire to perform, to showcase ourselves and then receive affirmation. This can bring us a good feeling. However, if your performance not only receives no praise but is also criticized, then you no longer want to showcase yourself, and you may even be afraid to do so. For example, if you wear nice clothes and others say things like "She dresses so nicely, I wonder who she's trying to seduce," or "A little girl should be content to dress plainly. Dressing so ostentatiously, what does she think she looks like..." What would you feel? You would definitely feel hurt and upset, thinking, "Why do so many people say I'm not good when I wear a nice dress? So I won't wear it anymore, I'll just wear dull clothes that won't attract anyone's attention, and then no one will say anything about me." Or maybe when you were young, your parents or other elders constantly taught you to be humble and modest, reminding you not to show off, as it would only bring trouble. If you were scared like this from a young age, you would also be afraid of becoming unique, afraid to be your true self. Or if you have seen or heard of others being severely punished, you would also experience discomfort, thinking that by doing the same, you would also be subjected to punishment. So, this feeling is learned and not due to any problem in your heart; you simply lack positive experiences of showcasing yourself. Society also does not encourage being too unique. There is an idiom that says, "The nail that sticks out gets hammered down," which means people should just keep to themselves and not do anything out of the ordinary, even if that is what you want to do. Now, you can think about whether such thoughts really make sense. Is it your fault that wearing a beautiful dress attracts criticism, or is it the fault of others? If you have such thoughts again, why not encourage yourself to wear a dress and see that it's not a big deal? I'm young and beautiful, and if I want to, I can fully showcase myself as long as I'm not causing harm to others or engaging in illegal activities. As for those who want to criticize me, let them do so. There will always be people who appreciate me, and I only need to care about those who truly respect and appreciate me.

Hello, OP~ Sending you a warm hug. "Feeling afraid to dress up and not wanting to draw attention, is it a sign of a mental problem?" I totally understand how you feel, because I've experienced the same. Maybe we are just the kind of people who prefer to keep a low profile and don't like being the center of attention. It makes us uncomfortable and even suspicious when people look at us. But it's not a strange psychological problem at all, it's just our personality. From a psychological perspective, it can be seen as an excessive reaction of "self-consciousness", where we magnify ourselves and believe that we will always be the focus of others' attention. At the same time, you also have a tendency to be suspicious and self-involved, overly sensitive and doubtful of others' words and actions. But being sensitive is not necessarily a disadvantage! Sensitive individuals often have a sharpness and creativity. However, if you are overly sensitive, it will keep you in a state of "suspicion". First of all, you need to understand that the person who cares about you the most is yourself, and others actually don't pay excessive attention to you. Even if you fall down on the street, if you look up, no one will notice you. Everyone is just going about their own business. And as for what you mentioned about wearing a beautiful dress, other people may not even notice it. Secondly, in the book "The Courage to Be Disliked", it is mentioned that "excessive self-consciousness" is actually due to a lack of self-confidence, which makes us concerned about whether our actions will be criticized by others. So, my suggestion is to give yourself more confidence. Each person is unique, so walk confidently with your head held high on the street. You have your own beauty, which is also a form of charm. Moreover, you can also engage in activities that make you feel a sense of value, which will also boost your self-confidence. Hope this can help you~

Hey, questioner! Hello! Thank you very much for your reply. After reading your response, I think I can analyze it in detail. "Not being close to parents, especially dad, may be related to poor interpersonal relationships. I have been excluded and ignored by classmates before." Although the content is not much, the underlying causes of your current "insecurity" and "anxiety" have surfaced! It is related to your upbringing! First of all, there is a "resistance" in your intimate relationship with your parents (especially your dad), which is the "original component" brought to you by your primary family! Your so-called "poor interpersonal relationships" are, to some extent, a "replica" of your primary family relationship with "resistance" in the social field! This should be the "distant cause" of your current "insecurity" and "anxiety". Coupled with your "exclusion and alienation by classmates in the past", I believe that this is also a "traumatic" experience for you (and it is also related to the "group" of "classmates")! Your current feeling of "being too eye-catching will be unsafe and attract criticism" is, in a sense, the "lingering trauma" from the "exclusion and alienation by classmates". In the words of behavioral psychology, this is called "stimulus generalization"! The so-called "once bitten, twice shy" is referring to this "stimulus generalization"! As for how to solve your problem, I personally suggest that you try to "fence off" your fear or insecurity, that is, limit your fear range to the "past" rather than the present. You can try "diaphragmatic breathing", that is, inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth, and keep each breath between 15-20 seconds, trying to relax yourself! And carefully feel the entire breathing process. Slowly return to the "present" and establish a connection with the "present"! In addition, you can try going to the psychological counseling office at school and seek professional psychological help to resolve the "resistance" between you and your parents! As the saying goes, "a harmonious family leads to success in everything", once your family issues are resolved, your current "insecurity" will naturally be resolved as well! I hope this can help you.

Hi there, after reading your description, I want to express my understanding and sympathy. Before analyzing further, please allow me to give you a big hug. Feeling unsafe and hesitant to dress up may be related to a lack of security and extreme inferiority complex. How can we improve this? First, face it! When we encounter difficulties that we can't solve immediately, let's accept it calmly and then try to change what we can change to make ourselves better. Confront it! You are unique and there is no need to let the question of whether or not to dress up interfere with your life. Everyone has the right to be beautiful, just like boys can choose to put on makeup to become a better version of themselves. Of course, don't care too much about what others think. This kind of restraint is self-imposed. Life is already difficult, why burden ourselves even more? Lastly, I want to say that we are in control of our own lives, and it should be up to us to decide how to live. Keep going, and strive to become a better version of yourself!

Hug the questioner. I have seen many girls who have similar confusion as the questioner. Although I feel that every girl deserves to live confidently and beautifully in the sunshine, hiding oneself in the crowd is also a very effective way for everyone to protect themselves. Maybe in the past, when you tried to show yourself, you received some negative or unsafe feedback that made you uncomfortable. Maybe it's because you have seen a lot of news and things happening around you that made you feel that being too outspoken can be dangerous. These are all normal situations. You are trying very hard to protect yourself in this way. It is great and necessary to protect oneself, but while seeing that you are using this method to protect yourself, you can also thank yourself for diligently protecting yourself. Through this powerful protective layer that you have built, you can see that you are actually shining and beautiful. Whether or not to show it to others is a choice we can make, but before showing it, you must see your own sparkling beauty. I hope my answer can bring some new perspectives to the questioner.

In fact, many women have this mentality. Recently, the super popular variety show "Sisters Who Make Waves" on Mango TV is worth watching. Although women like Zhang Yuxi, Ning Jing, and Lan Yingying are constantly expressing their needs and striving for the so-called center stage, more girls like Jin Chen, Zhang Hanyun, Li Sidanni, Jin Sha, Bai Bing, etc. are hesitant to express themselves and dare not fight for what they want. There is an old saying in China, "The nail that sticks out gets hammered down," living an ordinary life and dressing modestly is sometimes a way to protect ourselves. In history, before Zhu Yuanzhang became the emperor, he used a good strategy, "Build high walls, accumulate enough food, delay declaring himself king." The last part is about letting Zhu Yuanzhang be low-key, down-to-earth, and work hard to accumulate resources, taking it slow on the journey to becoming a king. "Always feeling unsafe and subject to criticism when being too dazzling" is a valid feeling. For a young girl who has just entered the workplace, accumulating work experience and building a network is the most correct approach. Being ordinary and normal in appearance is enough. So, you don't need to worry too much about yourself. It is actually your best instinct to protect yourself. When you are new to the workplace, sometimes you may want to show that you are capable, but in reality, it can cause unnecessary trouble and make your superiors feel that you are too attention-seeking, leading them to be wary of you. Focus on your work and be modest and down-to-earth in appearance. This will make your career path smoother. Keep it up, girl!~~

Hello, girl! It is very honored to have the opportunity to meet you on this platform. I hope my words can bring you sunshine and warm your heart. Actually, what you are experiencing is not really a psychological problem. As the saying goes, "The tall tree catches the wind!" It is true that being too flashy can attract a lot of criticism and unnecessary troubles! So, your concerns today are reasonable! Especially after you start working in the company in the future, it is popular to be "low-key"! This is also a way to "protect" yourself! There is nothing wrong with learning to "protect yourself"! It is not really a "psychological problem" at all! However, from your words, there is also a hint of "insecurity" and "anxiety"! It seems like you are always in a state of "danger"! This reminds me of a quote from "Fear Drives" - "The imagined fear is scarier than the real fear!" You can try to make these problems more "specific": Are you really "unsafe"? Or do you "think" you are very unsafe? How likely is it that something that makes you feel unsafe will happen? Even if it really happens, how much substantial impact will it have on you? By that time, do you have any "resources" to "cope with" such situations? In addition, from my personal experience, your sense of insecurity today may be related to your original family and upbringing! Can you kindly answer the following questions for me? 1. Have you ever encountered any significant events that have caused psychological trauma from childhood to adulthood? For example, the experience of being "dampened" because of "standing out"? The experience of being "targeted" because of being "too outstanding"? 2. How is the close relationship between you and your parents from childhood to adulthood? Of course, it involves your personal privacy, so I respect your personal wishes.

question: 19-year-old girl, severe depression, thinking too much, really exhausted.
description: I really care too much about what others think of me, and I tend to overthink a lot. There are always people jokingly saying things like "Are you sick?" with depression, and I really don't want this. It's just so exhausting.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, expressing emotions, anxious emotions

answers.answer_text: Hugs to you~ It seems that in this world, there always come voices from all directions, these voices may not understand us enough but have already begun to criticize us. Who can be seen as perfect and lovely in everyone's eyes? Who can satisfy others all the time? This seems almost impossible. Everyone exists in their own time and space, each person has their own independent ideas and inner world. They don't have to be the same as others, and it's also impossible for everyone to be the same. So we can be ourselves, different from others, and others can also be different. If we know how to appreciate each other's beauty, it will be a blessing for both you and others. Even if we don't understand others, we should accept and not judge. And those who always judge others actually haven't found their own little world, and can't feel the beauty of everyone's different worlds! So it's difficult for them to discover the beauty in others. I believe the original poster must also be a little star shining in their own world, floating in their own time and space, no need to care about others' comments on you. There are always passers-by thanking your light! Many people are silently loving you, just like how you are silently loving many people. Wishing everything is well.

question: Has the decrease in time spent communicating and socializing with friends influenced interpersonal relationships?
description: Due to preferring to plan things alone and enjoying completing tasks according to the plan, I have limited time for communication and socializing with friends. Does this affect interpersonal relationships?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, friends, roommates, classmates, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: ~The original poster likes to plan and do things alone, while I prefer to follow a plan to get things done. This shows that OP is a particularly independent and self-disciplined person. It is a good habit. However, OP is now worried that this might affect their interpersonal relationships. If interpersonal relationships require sacrificing one's self-discipline and good habits to fulfill, then it is better to avoid such relationships. Good interpersonal relationships should be based on mutual needs and comfort, where both parties can spend time together and communicate when neither have any commitments. OP is a disciplined person, and disciplined people also attract other disciplined individuals. There is no need to forcefully fit in with those who have different lifestyles and beliefs. What we should cherish are those positive interpersonal relationships that can help us grow together. As for those useless relationships, it's best to let them naturally fade away.

question: Should I be nicer to a boy even if my friend says being proactive won't be appreciated?
description: Should I be nicer to a boy? My friends say I am too active towards the boy I like, and that boys won't appreciate it. But isn't it natural to be kinder to someone you like?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~~~ I can feel your dilemma in matters of love. For the question of pursuing a guy, I don't think there is a unified answer to define all pursuits. If you like a guy, I think it's not wrong for the OP to take the initiative to pursue him. However, we should control the extent of our pursuit and not forget to live a good life and maintain our own lives while pursuing the other person.

question: I am constantly feeling low, pessimistic, and depressed. How can I make friends?
description: I feel that my emotions have been very low, negative, and pessimistic. I feel like I can't do anything well, have no special characteristics or strengths, and have no hope for the future. I'm afraid of the future and don't know how to interact with others. I feel like I don't have any real friends, that everyone is fake, saying and doing different things. I have forgotten what it feels like to be happy or sad, and I have never felt truly happy enough to smile or very sad enough to cry. I feel very indifferent. Sometimes, I pretend to be happy, but it's just an act. I haven't cried in a long time, even in situations where I feel like I should. I don't feel anything in my heart. I always hope to have a very good friend, but as soon as I leave that environment, all the relationships gradually fade away. I always try to reconnect with the friends I had before, but I don't have anyone. I'm left alone. I feel lonely and helpless, like no one is there to comfort me or truly understand me. Every day, life feels empty and repetitive. I feel lost about the future and feel like I'm just living this life in repetition. I feel indifferent towards everything and have thoughts of ending my life, although I haven't acted on it. I wish to die by accident.

answers.answer_text: Hello there~ ※ Through your description, I can see that you are feeling very pessimistic and have low mood, feeling that you can't do anything well, and lacking any special qualities or strengths. You have no hope for the future, fear it, struggle with social interactions, feel that you don't have any true friends, and think that everyone is fake, saying one thing and doing another. You have forgotten what it feels like to be happy or sad, and feel very indifferent. You have thought about ending your life, but haven't acted on it, and have also thought about being accidentally killed. This version of yourself makes you feel very helpless, and you don't know how to change your state. I really want to be in front of you and give you a hug! I don't know what you have been through that has made you so pessimistic about yourself and the world. Perhaps it has to do with your original family, because you didn't receive love and companionship from your parents, so you lack a sense of love and security. This is also why you haven't learned how to interact with others in your original family, and don't know how to establish good intimate relationships with others. No matter what you have experienced, it shouldn't make you disappointed in yourself or the world, but rather, it should make you hold on to hope even more! Whether it's your parents, family, or friends, it requires effort to maintain those relationships. You hope to have a very close friend, but as soon as you leave that environment, all relationships gradually fade away, leaving you alone. You feel lonely and helpless, thinking that no one is there to comfort and truly understand you. Physical distance indeed has an impact on emotions, and this is an uncontrollable reality factor. To overcome it, both parties need to put in effort to maintain this emotional connection. Feelings may fade, and this is not your fault, as most people experience this. Don't attribute it to yourself. Be more proactive, frequently reach out to each other and have heart-to-heart conversations, and maintain psychological contact. This is the best preservative for maintaining a relationship. Don't confine yourself to your own world, step out of your comfort zone, and experience things you have never experienced before, try things you have never tried before. Let go of your misconceptions about the world, and come to know yourself and this beautiful world again! Best wishes!

question: Do you really deserve your loved one when you still have feelings for your ex?
description: I have been with my ex for two months, and being with him gives me an inexplicable sense of security. I can't say that I'm very happy, but I know that I love him so much that I'm willing to sacrifice myself for him. I long for the day when we can sleep together every night. However, our personalities don't match well; both of us have strong personalities and we often argue when we're together. We broke up less than a month ago, and I got remarried in a rush... I still have feelings for him, and I'm also keeping it a secret from my husband. At first, my husband was quite satisfied with me, but as time went on, I felt a strange sense of oppression and lack of freedom... I'm a complete mess now, with difficulties in both work and love.
keywords: Marriage, concepts of marriage, marriage management

answers.answer_text: Hello~ Is it really fair to oneself's loved one to keep thoughts of an ex-partner in mind? I think there are two different situations. One is that it is always difficult to forget someone because those are real experiences. So, if you occasionally think of an ex-partner, especially when the relationship with the current partner is not pleasant, it is very normal. Because even though we have a current partner, it doesn't mean we can completely erase past memories. Dissatisfaction with current life, especially, tends to make us nostalgic for the past. But we need to realize that no matter how we reminisce about the past, we will always have a lot of fond imagination of it. We see the past through rose-colored glasses. And we need to realize that too much reminiscing about the past is not good for current relationships. The other situation is that even though we are living with the current partner, we are always imagining scenes of living with the ex-partner, and even desiring to replace the current partner with the ex-partner.
