This kind of imagination is not very loyal to the current relationship. Because being like this all the time will greatly affect the relationship between the two people now, and you may even feel like you are living with someone you don't like at all. And a very important point is that the other person is completely unaware of this, which means you still have elements of concealment and deception in this matter.

#Both individuals are too dominant, and they often argue when they are together. After separating, I got into a flash marriage within a month. How did your parents manage it? He still remained in my heart, while also keeping it a secret from my husband. At first, my husband was quite satisfied, but over time, I started feeling an inexplicable sense of oppression and a lack of freedom. Let's change the order of this sentence: (At first, my husband was quite satisfied, but over time, I started feeling an inexplicable sense of oppression and a lack of freedom. He still lived in my heart, while also keeping it a secret from my husband). What happened between you and your husband? What does it mean to have no freedom and feel oppressed? What specific events occurred? When people are dissatisfied with current circumstances, they tend to reminisce about the past as a way to avoid dealing with or feeling incapable of resolving current issues.

question: Are you constantly arguing with your husband over trivial matters? Should you get a divorce?
description: After being married for five years, I am 32 years old and my husband is 35 years old. We constantly argue over trivial matters in our daily lives, which has left me emotionally exhausted. My parents, seeing our constant fighting, have even suggested that we get a divorce, especially since we don't have any children. These petty arguments include things like: 1. If I cook less food than he wanted, he gets angry. 2. If I cook too much food, especially if it's something he doesn't like, he gets angry and tells me to eat it all by myself. 3. If I make pork soup and he thinks it smells bad, he gets angry and blames me for using too much water. 4. If I accidentally buy the wrong groceries, such as fruits or vegetables he doesn't like, or if I buy too much or spend too much money, he gets angry. 5. If dinner isn't ready when he comes home from work and he's hungry, he will likely explode in anger. 6. If I boil too much water and waste it, he gets angry. 7. We rarely go out to eat, but when we do, he is usually unhappy with either the taste of the food or cleanliness of the restaurant, so we end up leaving. These are just a few examples of the various situations we constantly face. Due to the pandemic this year, we both returned to our hometown. Before that, we were both working outside. In light of these situations, I try to endure and remain silent, but his anger and harsh words make it difficult. Sometimes, I can't help but engage in a big fight.

answers.answer_text:
Thank you for the invitation. Hello beautiful! After reading your situation, I understand that you are in pain. Hugs! I have been thinking about how to answer your question of "whether to divorce", and I feel that it cannot be explained in just a few words. Regardless of the specific circumstances, deciding whether to divorce or not is indeed a difficult decision, both for the parties involved and for friends and family. Here, I can only offer you some of my understanding and advice for your reference, hoping that it will be helpful to you. 
1. Regarding love and marriage, although there are no standardized criteria, there are usually some general situations. Love is a matter between two people, and it cannot be achieved by the efforts of one person alone. A happy marriage is when both husband and wife walk towards each other. In a happy marriage, themes of life together include tolerance, understanding, respect, shared responsibilities, and love for each other. Unhappy marriages vary. Unhappy marriages generally have three outcomes: divorce, compromising to get by, or actively making changes to achieve happiness.
2. Marriage is a major event in life and should not be easily given up. After marriage, everyone may go through a period of adaptation. Some last a long time, while others are short. If the adaptation is good and both parties can adjust, the marriage will be normal. If the adjustment is not good and even becomes worn out, as conflicts escalate, it is likely to lead to a breakup. During the adjustment process, both individuals should be honest and walk towards each other. This is a responsible attitude. It is responsible for both the other person and oneself. After all, if a marriage fails, it will harm both parties and even the family. Therefore, making efforts to improve oneself, being understanding and tolerant towards the other person, and trying their best to adapt to the relationship is a responsible attitude. Through these efforts, if it is truly believed that there is no need to maintain a marriage that has no hope of happiness, it may lead to a breakup.
3. Divorce can bring many problems, especially for women, it may be more complicated. Here, mainly referring to the issue of marriage gradient. In marriage, men generally tend to look for women who are younger, shorter, and have lower education levels than themselves. Therefore, the options for women to remarry are mostly limited to those who are older, have higher education levels, and taller. It is obvious that suitable partners are relatively limited. Another possibility is to stay single. After divorce, there is generally a long period of adjustment, especially influenced by traditional social norms, so good psychological adjustment is needed.
4. Some suggestions: 1) Analyze the focal point of conflicts in the marriage seriously and make efforts to resolve these main issues as soon as possible. 2) Strengthen learning and strive to improve oneself, trying to perfect oneself as much as possible. Many trivial matters in life can be avoided by paying attention and improving oneself. For example, the art of language communication, patience, and frankness in dealing with others, etc. Whether the outcome is divorce or not, in fact, a person should improve oneself throughout one's lifetime. Only by constantly becoming better can one appear more perfect and lovely. If there are further discomforts, I hope you can seek professional psychological counseling. Wishing you all the best! The world and I love you.

Divorce is just a way of having no way out. Of course, if both parties have really tried their best and the relationship still hasn't improved, then separation is also a method. Life itself is made up of one thing after another, and what we can do is how to handle the emotions of these little things. For example, as mentioned by the topic creator, the cooking issue. The topic creator and the other party have been living together for a long time, so they should have some understanding of each other's eating habits. Therefore, the next time a similar situation arises, we can be a little more considerate, remember the other person's dietary restrictions, and make something that slightly suits their taste. But regarding the other party's frequent temper outbursts, we can communicate with them. Generally speaking, people with a quick temper tend to have an impatient nature. They don't have bad intentions, but when faced with problems, they often act without thinking and don't take things to heart or consider others' feelings. Therefore, we can make some agreements with the other party, such as whether they can take a few minutes to calm down when there's a problem, or if they can hold back any hurtful words. We can also record some of the things the other party says and let them listen to it after they have calmed down, to see if they realize that they may have a certain problem. Of course, this needs to be communicated with the other party and should not be done if they do not agree. In daily life, it is inevitable for couples to argue. What we have to do is learn to understand and empathize with each other. Sometimes we can tell the other person our true thoughts. In fact, both parties have put a lot of effort into this family, but they just can't put themselves in each other's shoes. So sometimes, we need to understand each other and see if the other person can do the same. Getting angry and having a temper won't solve the problem, so can we try a different approach and grow together, face things together? If the other person is willing to accept and change, then we can make an effort together. But if the other person continues to do things their own way, or even think that we are constantly making a fuss for no reason, then we can first protect and take care of ourselves, and then decide how to proceed. The world loves you.

question: It's late at night, I want to sleep but can't fall asleep... Why is my younger sister like this?
description: It is late at night and I can't sleep... My brother-in-law keeps sending messages, saying: "Sister, please help me! Can you ask her if she will come back and continue our life together? Please make her consider coming back... Sigh, reading these words makes me feel so sad. My sister is really stubborn, always acting like a child, doing things based on her own preferences. Her father-in-law is seriously ill, on the verge of death, and he hopes that she can bring the child back to see him. But she is unwilling to return... Oh, this stubbornness of hers, always causing various troubles and straining relationships with family and her husband. Regardless, I believe she needs to go and show a little filial piety to the elderly. Today, I talked to her a lot, she has been staying at her parents' home for 2 years and hasn't returned. She complains about the long distance from her husband's province and even dislikes that he is not wealthy despite his hard work. She says she will never work, believing that even the hardest-working poor person will always be poor! Sigh, I don't know how to communicate with her, it just doesn't seem right... I don't know how to persuade her to go back and have a look...
keywords: Family, family relationships, and the process of growing up.

answers.answer_text: Hello. The key point is: regardless of the situation, you think that no matter what, your sister needs to go see her father-in-law in his final moments, to fulfill the last bit of filial piety for the elderly man and satisfy the wishes of her husband's family. However, this is completely different from your sister's thoughts. question: Unable to establish intimate relationships, feeling overwhelmed and avoiding and rejecting beyond one's limits?
description: From childhood to adulthood, regardless of whether they are same sex or opposite sex friends, once they feel that their relationship exceeds their so-called boundaries, they will avoid and reject it. Sometimes there is a sense of inexplicable loneliness for no reason, tired of everything around them, and wanting to escape. They do not know how to interact with the opposite sex, and have been single until now.

answers.answer_text: Many people who have experienced childhood trauma related to their parents are afraid of getting close to others. For example, those who have had controlling and dominant parents. There is nothing wrong with not wanting to be in a romantic relationship. The belief that one must spend their whole life with another person is not necessarily true in this day and age. If you have always been content with being alone, it simply means that this state doesn't make you particularly uncomfortable. If there comes a day when this state becomes unbearable for you, you will naturally find a way out of it. And you will no longer believe that you are incapable of getting close to others. For example, if one day you meet someone who truly captivates you, it would be difficult for you to stay away from them. The current situation only means that this person has not yet stirred your heart enough. Of course, there are also benefits to being alone, and there is nothing wrong with that. However, if you truly desire a life with someone else, there are a few preparations you can make: 1. Seek professional psychological counseling to re-experience relationships. Through the guidance of a therapist, learn how to be completely open with the other person, understand that vulnerability does not necessarily lead to violation, gradually desensitize the fear within you, and then you will start getting used to letting others see all aspects of you. 2. There is also a need to practice setting boundaries, but this can be addressed later. The fear of letting people get close to you is actually due to difficulty in maintaining boundaries and protecting yourself, which is why you choose to keep your distance from the start. If you have the ability to set boundaries, you will not be afraid of others getting close to you. This can also be learned through guidance from a therapist.

question: What should I do if I'm a junior in college and my parents never approve of me, leaving me with very little self-confidence?
description: I am a junior female student. It seems that my parents haven't approved of me since high school. My grades in high school were fine, and teachers and classmates all thought I would easily pass the college entrance exam, but my parents never believed in me and always thought I was only capable of getting into a second-tier university. Even when I actually did pass the exam and received my admission letter, they were still worried that there might be a mistake in the scores. Today, a relative's child got their exam results and did really well. My mom said that on the day when I got my results, others would also think highly of me. I went along with it and said that I was just average, but my mom said, "You are indeed average, just a mediocre student." I always feel very uneasy about this. After all, I exceeded the minimum score for the top tier university by quite a bit and got into a prestigious one, surpassing many others. But in their eyes, I am still just average. Lately, I have been preparing for the postgraduate entrance exam and studying for long hours every day. When they found out about it, the first thing they said was, "Try your best and have no regrets." Even though I haven't started yet, they already believe I won't be able to pass. I envy those whose parents praise their children for being good-looking. From childhood to adulthood, my parents have never complimented me. Even if a classmate or their colleague says I'm good-looking, my mom would say, "They said you're good-looking, is that true? You're just average. This is how we look, where could you possibly be good-looking?"
keywords: Family, family relationships, parent communication, and the process of growth.

answers.answer_text: Many Chinese parents believe that they can instil humility, diligence, and progress in their children by belittling them, which is a strange misconception. Sometimes they belittle their children just to prevent them from being too ambitious and unrealistic, but they fail to understand the psychological impact that this "belittling" can have on their children - not only does it not necessarily achieve the intended purpose, but it can also lead to other consequences such as low self-esteem and loss of self. In light of this, we must first understand that parents are just ordinary people, not some all-powerful figures, and their views, just like those of everyone else, have their limitations. We do not need to view their opinions as sacred authority. This is a matter of awareness. In the subconscious, it is important to cultivate a healthy self-esteem and replace the need for validation from parents with a sense of self-worth. This involves some personal psychological growth work. Finding something that you truly enjoy and deriving your own value from it, rather than seeking validation from your parents, is crucial. Seeking psychological counseling can also help you rediscover your core values and establish a connection between your inner confidence and worth. As you grow older, your parents' views will no longer have excessive influence, and you will be able to fully listen to your inner voice and make choices and decisions. Stop trying to prove yourself to your parents through your actions. That only leads to losing yourself. Moreover, no matter how much you do to prove yourself to your parents, the underlying subconscious suggestion is actually reinforcing the idea that "I need to prove myself because I am not good enough."

question: What kind of counselor is a good counselor?
description: Want to know, what kind of therapist can be considered a good therapist? What aspects are included?

answers.answer_text: ■What kind of counselor is considered a good counselor? A good counselor can possess many excellent qualities, while a bad counselor can also have many disharmonious aspects. It is important to pay attention to subjective evaluations by the counselor or the visitors, as well as evaluations from the industry and supervisory evaluations. Perhaps the most important aspect for a mental health counselor is to maintain a good and accepting counseling relationship with the visitor. The visitor is the counselor's client, so as the host, the counselor should have good customer service skills and make the visitor feel that their money is well spent. This kind of psychological service is worth trying again and persisting in the long term. A long-term relationship must follow many ethical and logical guidelines. There are things that the visitor must know, and there are things that the visitor can choose not to know. There may also be lies in the counseling relationship, as visitors lie. This is already a very common and well-researched fact. We lie every day, even in the counseling room. Counselors need to maintain neutrality and objectivity, meaning that the possibility of self-disclosure is relatively low. Self-disclosure contains many pieces of information that one does not want others to know, and visitors may also not want counselors to know. Maintaining a certain good impression is also a potential need in the visitor's mind. The lies in the counseling room not only mean mistrust, but also represent the resistance to revealing information. Some very difficult and fragile aspects also need to be dealt with. How the counselor handles lies to a large extent affects the trust in the later stages of the counseling relationship. The counseling relationship requires subjective trust and experiential effects. We need to know who is the subject of counseling. Are visitors coming to the counseling room just for chatting and venting? Don't visitors have friends or anyone to confide in? Are visitors seeking advice? A good counselor can continuously and actively guide visitors to think and gradually become independent. As a psychological experience itself, the effectiveness of the counseling relationship may depend not only on the counselor's ability, professional perspective, ethics, and personal charm, but also on whether it can attract trust and make visitors feel dignified, valuable, and willing to love life during the counseling experience. Slowly, it can help them address counseling goals and improve their personality traits. In addition to having stable cases, counselors also need self-improvement and supervision. They can maintain empathy and self-awareness at any time, and know where their current professional position lies. They can contemplate and address the problems encountered in counseling or career positioning, identify the challenges and bottlenecks they face in their career, and strive to overcome difficulties.
