question: Avoiding something, for the past six months, I have been having nightmares whenever I think about it. Feeling lost and confused when it comes to facing things head-on.
description: I have been doing online business for almost half a year. (I am already an adult, with clear thinking.) I have met many positive people and have been to many places. Through weight loss products, I started to learn about the brand and developed understanding and trust. I have been to training sessions and have always trusted that this might be my lifelong career. It has made me feel passionate and I have become more outgoing. I have learned a lot of knowledge and skills. I think this might be a career that I can persist in, and I have achieved good results. However, my sleep schedule is irregular. Before this period of outgoing growth, I was more introverted and didn't like to show myself. Sometimes, when I don't respond or send messages for a long time, many people try to reach out to me. I get nervous and can't bring myself to look at the messages. The longer it goes on, the more afraid I become, because it has caused me to miss out on many things. It has been a while since this happened, but I remember that my online partners have always been very good to me and taking care of me. There is one senior sister who is the best to me. That time, I asked all my customers to add her because I was busy with exams and was afraid that the customers couldn't find me. Afterwards, I felt reassured, as if I had a premonition that I would do this. One day, I decided to take half a day off, and until now, it has been almost six months. For some reason, I stopped talking online and I'm afraid of being asked why by others. I'm also afraid of interacting with my previous circle of friends. I have had dreams related to this more than ten times, and I feel very confused.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I understand how you feel. You are doing a microbusiness, "it makes me feel passionate, I become more outgoing, I learn a lot of knowledge and skills, and I feel that this could be a career that I can persist in, and I have achieved good results." From what you have expressed, you love and affirm this profession, and you feel that it has been very helpful to you. You stopped replying to messages and even avoided looking at them, and in order to avoid communication, you even referred customers to others. As a microbusiness owner, this conflicts with your profession. What are the reasons behind these conflicts, is it just because you have always been introverted, or have you encountered certain people and events? You are now not speaking on the internet, afraid of interacting with your previous social circle. It seems that you are avoiding some past events and people. On one hand, your introverted personality is related to your upbringing. Whether someone is introverted or extroverted is not a matter of good or bad, as long as you feel it is suitable and adapt to the needs of work and life, there is nothing wrong with it. On the other hand, from the perspective of psychoanalysis, Freud divided people into ego, id, and superego. 1. The id is located at the lowest level of the personality structure, composed of innate instincts and desires, and includes various physiological needs. The id is unconscious and irrational, following the pleasure principle. 2. The ego is located in the middle layer of the personality structure, differentiated from the id, and its function is to regulate the conflicts between the id and the superego, following the reality principle. 3. The superego is located at the highest level of the personality structure. It is the moralizing self. Its function is to suppress the impulses of the id, monitor the ego, and pursue a state of perfection, following the moral principle. Freud also divided psychological processes into preconscious, conscious, and subconscious. The subconscious includes a person's primal impulses and various instincts, as well as the desires generated by these instincts, which are not understood and suppressed by customs and moral values below the threshold of consciousness. Although the subconscious mind is not perceived by people, it governs a person's entire life. You mentioned that you have "dreamed about related dreams" multiple times. What are the contents of your dreams? From the perspective of psychoanalysis, dreams may reflect one's inner desires. I suggest you sort out your psychological processes and the contents of your dreams to understand what you truly want, what the current problem is, and what kind of life you envision. This may help reduce some confusion.

Hello, from your description, I can tell that you were very passionate about the microbusiness before, and it brought about many positive changes for you. You gained friends and trust, making your life more colorful. However, at the same time, you also experienced some other changes, such as irregular sleep patterns, worrying about missing phone messages, and constantly thinking about online matters. Suddenly, you stopped talking online and didn't want to touch on your past experiences and life, you just wanted to rest, but also felt lost, thinking that you were avoiding something. My guess is that you may be experiencing occupational burnout. The intense dedication you put in the past has caused the tight string to break, and it will take some time to repair. According to normal work schedules, working 8 hours a day is enough, and the remaining time should belong to life. However, microbusiness does not have fixed working hours. You need to constantly pay attention to phone messages, there is no specific time to go offline and rest. In this situation, it's easy to exhaust one's enthusiasm. You can completely relax yourself, do something else, and refresh your rejection towards microbusiness work. When you feel like doing it again, you can come back. Protect your enthusiasm for something and stop when you are 60-80% satisfied. We need to sleep every night, and we have two days off each week. These are all determined by the physiological and psychological laws of human beings. Respect your inner feelings, accept your decision to want to take a break. If you're tired, take a break. The future still belongs to you, and you can come back whenever you want. Best wishes, Jiangjiang.

The transformation from introversion to extroversion, does this process make you feel uncomfortable or painful? Irregular daily routines can easily lead to lack of energy and physical exhaustion. Facing meaningless social interactions can easily lead to occupational burnout. Firstly, one reason is that your original personality did not enjoy socializing, but after participating in network marketing, you felt that you had changed a lot. At first, you thought this change was good, but after a long time, you realized that this change made you feel miserable because it conflicted with your inner personality. You feel mentally and physically exhausted when dealing with things related to network marketing and even social interactions. You just want to escape and avoid facing them, and just want to live more comfortably. Another reason is a lack of career responsibility. You mentioned earlier that you initially intended to develop a career but eventually gave it up. Is it because you feel it is no longer suitable to continue developing in this career, or is it because you feel pain when facing it? In fact, it mainly depends on how we perceive the situation itself, and how we self-observe and self-regulate, in order to ultimately adapt to society. I hope my perspective can be helpful to you.

question: I am a person who follows the rules, but I also feel anxious about my own stagnation.
description: I make a weekly schedule list for myself, specifying what to do at each time of the day, and I mark it with a check mark (√) after completing each task. If by the end of the week, I see that the entire list is filled with check marks, I feel accomplished. But if I can't complete everything, I feel frustrated. I am willing to spend every day following my plan, but at the same time, I look down on myself for not having any surprises or adventures! I also have my son live and study within this framework. If I miss a day without a plan, I feel anxious and like I am wasting my life.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Feeling out of control can make people anxious, while too much stability can also cause anxiety. Going with the flow can make people anxious, as can achieving success and fame. There is no life that will always satisfy us; there are only wise individuals who are content with their current lives. From your description, it seems that you have formed a fixed routine and want your child to follow your way of life. Although there may be a sense of fulfillment in accomplishing tasks, there is also a sense of numbness without novelty or surprises. This has left you feeling conflicted and confused. I'm truly impressed by how you plan your daily activities. You may find it boring, but for some people, it is a challenging exercise in discipline and effective time management. Living a planned life gives a sense of security, making people feel at ease without having to "think" or face new risks and challenges, which is its advantage. However, like any other way of living, it also has its drawbacks, such as monotony, lack of creativity, rigidity, and a lack of passion for life. It's important to recognize that there are life experiences that cannot be completed, just like some of the tasks in your weekly routine. Try leaving some "empty" time within your week without pre-planned activities, and use your imagination and embrace action to try new things. Give your well-structured life a little chaos. As long as life is lived earnestly, it shouldn't be wasted. Allow your child the autonomy to make choices and avoid imposing your own will upon them. They need to create their own lives. It seems that you have high expectations for yourself, hoping that everything remains within your control. However, future society and events will not always go according to plan. Teach your child the ability to handle unexpected changes instead of planning every day of their life in advance. It seems like you have anxiety about time, believing that it should always be meaningful. But many experiences in life are meaningless, such as daydreaming, feeling bored, watching the sunset, or listening to beautiful music. Leave some time in your life to do meaningless things because if we spend our whole lives doing only meaningful and valuable things, it would be very sad and dull. Don't be afraid to "go off track" and try a more spontaneous way of life. You may have a different experience because you are already doing well in your current planned life. Give yourself the opportunity to break free from it. Wishing you the best.

I totally agree with the answer from the above commenter, and I think the original poster can give themselves some freedom and relaxation. At the same time, I also believe that keeping a high level of planning and execution is not contradictory to having surprises and adventures, because the content of "plans" can be changed. Besides daily tasks, you can plan a murder mystery game for the weekend, a family vacation during a short break, or even a professional qualification exam half a year later... As long as the content is not monotonously repetitive, it will constantly bring new ideas. Moreover, many times, the unexpected surprises that are not prepared in advance and taken step by step can turn out to be distressing "shocks". The original poster also mentioned their son, and I think it is very correct and worthwhile to cultivate planning awareness and execution ability in children from a young age. By having these two abilities, at least when others are constantly procrastinating and being complacent, your child will be able to finish everything they need to do early and have time and energy to think about how to make their own life more colorful.

question: I am afraid of being touched by others, and in severe cases, I will tremble all over and feel the urge to scream.
description: Because I have experienced sexual harassment, which was quite terrifying at the time, I told my mother, but she didn't tell me what to do. Until now, whenever someone touches me, I feel disgusted and panicked, like a momentary breakdown.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, trauma therapy, behavioral abnormality.

answers.answer_text: OP, hello~~~ First, give OP a hug. From the description, it can be understood that OP has encountered sexual harassment in the past. Although it has passed, OP is still afraid of others' touch and wants to change this situation but doesn't know where to start. [A few suggestions] 1. OP can try desensitization. With the cooperation of the closest friends, start by sitting closer together and gradually get used to it. Then, try to let friends touch OP's arm... Take it step by step, it may feel uncomfortable at first, but through a period of adaptation, the discomfort will decrease and progress can be made. Until eventually, OP can go shopping hand in hand with friends. 2. However, if this problem seriously affects OP's study and life, it is recommended to seek professional counseling in a psychological consultation room. There are mature methods to deal with this situation, which can provide more thorough and effective help to OP.

question: Is the fee system included in the counselor's confidentiality agreement reasonable?
description: Recently, I have been receiving psychological counseling at a local consulting room. Last week, I signed a confidentiality agreement. However, there is a clause stating that if I cancel my appointment at short notice, I will be charged a corresponding fee. I'm wondering if this clause is reasonable.

answers.answer_text: Hello! Makes sense, but not perfect. This regulation mainly protects the interests of the counselor, and the core idea is: canceling a consultation would cause financial loss to the counselor, so the responsibility should be borne by the party who proposed the cancellation. In physical transactions, even if a product is returned, it can still be resold. However, counselors are selling "time," so objectively speaking, canceling an appointment can indeed cause financial loss to the counselor. If the cancellation is caused unilaterally by the visitor, it is reasonable for the visitor to bear the responsibility. The reason why it is not perfect is because this regulation does not consider the time cost of the visitor. In other words, if the consultation is canceled due to the visitor's reasons, and the visitor bears the counselor's loss as well as their own, then correspondingly, if the consultation is canceled due to the counselor's reasons, the counselor should also bear the potential loss of the visitor, but this aspect is missing in the regulation. Additionally, there is a problem of "difficult burden of proof." The counselor's time has a "clear price," while it is difficult to "value" the visitor's time. The economic loss caused by canceling an appointment with an ordinary person is obviously different from canceling an appointment with Jack Ma. This requires the industry to introduce specific standards to treat everyone equally. But in reality, it usually doesn't escalate to "this extent," and there is still a lot of room for negotiation and resolution between both parties. Generally speaking, the counselor would express understanding to the visitor and not make them bear this cost, but rather reschedule the appointment. Wish you a happy life!

Hello, regarding the fee standard, the rights and responsibilities of both parties, and other related content, they are usually clearly specified in the counseling agreement, which also includes the principle of confidentiality. As for the issue you mentioned, it depends on the specific circumstances of canceling the counseling session. If there is a mutual agreement to change the time, it will be executed as agreed. If it is caused by one party, that party will bear the responsibility. If it is due to the counselor, they will provide one free counseling session to make up for it. If it is due to the visitor, the regular counseling fee will be charged according to the agreement. It's worth noting that there should be a clear agreement on the deadline for changing the appointment time, and both parties should be informed and agree.

question: From childhood, I have been shy. In college, I am afraid to participate in group activities. What should I do?
description: I have been timid since childhood, but I am well aware that I cannot always be afraid to communicate with strangers, especially when I go to college and enter society. Later, I mustered up the courage to sign up for a project design activity, but I couldn't speak up in the design group. I felt like an invisible person, and every time I wanted to speak, I would feel awkward and unable to find the right words. I have not grown at all in terms of social interaction.

answers.answer_text: Thank you for your trust. 1. "I have been timid since childhood," indicating that you have been in a "timid" state for many years. The fact that this has continued for so many years shows that being "timid" has been helpful to you. 2. "But I am very aware that I cannot always be afraid to communicate with strangers." From childhood to adulthood, I believe you have had friends, classmates, teachers, etc. You must have experienced many occasions where you went from being strangers to being familiar with others. Regardless of the number or whether it was voluntary, you have definitely not been "constantly" afraid to communicate with strangers, so you are not as "afraid" as you think, you just haven't been as "bold" as you expected. 3. Since "I have been timid since childhood" and I am not always "afraid," when you occasionally "dare" to do something, give yourself a pat on the back.

Hello, topic starter! Hugs for you! After reading your description, "being shy since childhood, fearing participation in group activities in college," and analyzing your detailed situation, I personally feel that your behavior is very similar to social anxiety disorder. Although this condition is not a mental illness, it can still make us feel troubled and distressed. Over time, it can exhaust us and make us withdraw, which has a very negative impact on our growth. Based on your description, although you have been shy since childhood, you still "gathered up the courage to sign up for a project design activity," which is a great change in thinking for you and worth celebrating as progress. So, if you are not satisfied with your current situation, it would be like feeling ignored and frustrated in a team, putting too much pressure on yourself and eventually not seeing your progress. Finally, regarding the "project design activity" you participated in, the awards in design-related activities have a great impact on students majoring in design. However, if your major is not design, treat it as a hobby and don't put too much pressure on yourself. If you have the opportunity, join some clubs or organizations that require less interpersonal interaction, first allowing yourself to adapt and then challenging yourself in a gentle and gradual manner.

question: High school art student, cares about what others say, loses confidence in life and loses oneself.
description: High school students in key schools think that I am an art student and take shortcuts in class, so they look at me differently. The teachers also don't like me because my academic performance is not good, and they always give me a hard time. I feel nervous during class and can't understand the lessons. I feel like I am a failure. My family cares about transferring schools, but I am afraid of facing new environments and new classmates, and all the difficulties seem magnified. I dare not think about the future and have no confidence. I cry every day until I can't stop, and I have been having insomnia for over a month. I get angry with my family and spend my days in a haze of confused thoughts.
keywords: Emotions, anxious emotions, panic helplessness, fragile and tearful.

answers.answer_text: Hello, because I care about what others say, I've been feeling bad for over a month, and it hurts my heart. The high school courses are one level higher in difficulty compared to middle school. You said you can't understand because you're worried about not studying well and feeling too anxious. Try to do more relaxation exercises, meditation, and other practices to reduce your anxiety level. It will benefit your state. Being able to take the artistic route means you definitely have some artistic talent, but you stand out among the ordinary students. The learning environment you are in focuses on grades, not strengths. If there were a test for artistic talent, you would surely be one of the best. In other words, you are not completely without achievement. I suggest that you put more effort into your strengths, strive to get into an art school, and fully develop your advantages. I see that your family also cares about you. If you have any discomfort, please tell your family in time and ask for their help. In reality, there are indeed many teachers who don't like students with poor grades, especially in prestigious high schools. Have you discussed with your parents and talked to the teacher about their unreasonable demands? How do your parents see the situation? Is it possible that the teacher has higher expectations for you, and you feel it's difficult to meet them? Having trouble sleeping for over a month and being in a bad mood, I suggest you go to the psychiatric department of the hospital and undergo a specialized evaluation of your emotional state. Please also ask the doctor for advice on how to help you. I hope you can soon break free from this gloom, as the world and I love you!

Questioner, hello, hugs to you~ After reading your description of your studying and living situation, I feel that you have really encountered many difficulties. I really sympathize with you. When I read your description of crying non-stop every day, having insomnia for over a month, getting angry at your family, and obsessing all day, the first thing I noticed is that you have had insomnia for over a month. Insomnia is actually a state that greatly harms the body. Your emotions also have significant fluctuations. If you feel any discomfort, you must seek medical help in a timely manner. Based on your description of your family suggesting transferring schools, but also fearing new environments and new classmates, and magnifying all kinds of difficulties, it is apparent that you understand your own psyche very well. You are able to judge that you have magnified the difficulties, which suggests that you are only hesitating and have not completely rejected your family's suggestion to transfer schools. It's just that you may need a push to give you the courage to make a decision. The courage to make brave choices comes from sufficient support and understanding. Perhaps your family can provide you with this kind of support. I hope you can communicate more with your family, help them understand your anxiety and sadness, try to gain your family's support, and then consider whether to transfer schools. Because as you described, "they're always making things difficult for me," actually most teachers have a strong sense of morality, but the teacher you encountered may not be suitable for educating students in various ways, which has led to you not being able to adapt to the environment. The reason is not because of your academic performance, but rather the people and things you happened to encounter were unsatisfactory.

question: Raised by a generation other than my parents, I constantly feel a lack of security and a constant fear of being judged by others.
description: I have been raised by my grandparents since I was little. I went to kindergarten with them, and I have always tried to be a well-behaved child in their eyes. Sometimes, I even worry that if I don't do things according to their expectations, I will be abandoned. I have developed a deep emotional bond with my grandparents since I was little. I feel like they are my parents, but they never care about what I like to eat or what my hobbies are. They just arrange my life according to what they think is right for me. I have been living with them for ten years, but they never try to understand my needs. I feel like I lack love and I have no sense of security. Whenever I express my needs, I feel anxious and automatically assume that they won't agree with me. As I grew older, I also felt uncomfortable at school. Going outside makes me feel uneasy and I'm afraid of being judged by others. Moreover, whenever I have my own thoughts or feelings, I instinctively wonder if what I am doing is right and if others will agree with my actions. I feel hopeless and don't know if there is any hope for me. All I want is to do things that I like and have the right to be myself, not being deprived of the power to express my own feelings. What should I do?
keywords: Family, family trauma, family relationships, growing process.

answers.answer_text: You may need a stable, accepting, and understanding relationship. It can make you truly feel that I am not so bad after all, that I will not be judged and attacked, and that as long as I want to do something, the other person will support it... This new kind of relationship will make you feel that the world actually welcomes you. You can also accept yourself. One of the ways to obtain this kind of relationship is through counseling.

question: I am a boy, what should I do if I have feelings for boys? Is there something wrong with me?
description: I discovered that I am a male and I am interested in other males. I don't have much interest in females.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. Warm hugs to you (づ′▽`)づ (1) First of all, OP has already realized that their orientation is towards boys. Is this really a problem? If it causes difficulties in OP's life and they want to get rid of this issue, then it is a problem. But if OP enjoys liking boys and doesn't feel any pain because of it, then it cannot be called a problem. (2) Secondly, whether you like boys or girls, as long as it is a sincere emotion, it deserves respect and blessings. Love is a free thing, regardless of gender. As long as OP doesn't reject their own orientation, it is good. (3) Lastly, perhaps if others become aware of this matter, OP might face some controversy. But I still hope that OP knows that it doesn't matter what others say, your own feelings and experiences are the most important. It's your world and you are in charge. #The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

Wu Feikong's analysis: 
1. Life is long, but humans always pass through it stage by stage. In each stage of life, we will encounter some wonderful people who make us feel admiration, including both boys and girls. When we are young, we may like many people. As we grow older, the number of people we like becomes fewer and fewer. When we are mature, we will gradually choose someone to love forever and hope to be with him (her) forever. This is the law of life.
2. I don't know how old you are now. However, regardless of which stage you are in, you have the right to like someone, but love requires caution. Because love means loyalty and self-restraint. This has nothing to do with gender.
3. It is normal to like or not like someone. However, at any time, one person cannot represent a whole group.
4. Allowing oneself to be free and not being attached is a carefree attitude towards life. Being responsible for oneself and pleasing oneself and others is the right path in life.
5. Wish you happiness!

question: Eighth grade girl, recently feeling a bit mentally unstable?
description: 8th grade girl, 1. Even though I can't find much happiness on the internet, I still find myself addicted to it. 2. I didn't finish my homework and my mom criticized me for it. Although I know it's my own fault, why do I still feel aggrieved and sad? It's like I'm "self-pitying" myself. I feel like I've become "overly emotional." 3. I always engage in "self-criticism" for no reason... It's like there's someone in my mind who constantly likes to criticize me. 4. Umm, this is quite... I just don't like it when my family reads my compositions... But if it's a teacher or a classmate reading them, I don't really mind.

answers.answer_text: Giving you a hug~ From your description, it is evident that you are a sensitive girl with rich inner thoughts and high self-expectations. Your first issue is not finding happiness on the internet and still becoming addicted to it. I wonder what you primarily do online? If the addiction is not due to finding happiness, could it be because of boredom or other reasons? It is apparent that you do not consider internet addiction to be a good thing. In that case, you can try finding hobbies in real life that bring you joy and gradually replace the time spent online. This will naturally help you break free from internet addiction. The second issue is feeling upset and self-conscious when criticized by your mother. Actually, feeling hurt when criticized is a normal reaction. Even if you believe that you should accept criticism when you make mistakes, it is inevitable to feel upset, right? In fact, it would be strange if you did not feel upset. So, there is no need to dwell on your emotions. Just let them flow naturally. It is healthy to cry when you need to and laugh when you want to. The third issue is having a tendency to self-criticize for no reason. Actually, self-criticism is a manifestation of having high self-expectations and a desire to improve oneself. Moderate self-criticism is beneficial for personal and mental growth. However, once you understand your own shortcomings, you can try to reduce self-criticism and instead, encourage and motivate yourself more. It will make you even better! The fourth issue is not liking to show essays to your family. Actually, as we grow up, we spend more time in school than at home, and gradually, classmates and teachers seem to understand us better than our parents. It is normal to be less willing to share academic matters with parents sometimes. However, you can share more about daily life with your family! I hope this is helpful to you~ *^_^* Believe that you will always be the excellent you! No more doubts.

question: Feeling restless, unable to control the urge to order takeout, and feeling self-blame after eating?
description: Since September of last year, every time I open my computer to search for articles and write my thesis, I start browsing food delivery apps on my phone. I end up spending a long time scrolling through them and almost every day I end up ordering takeout. After eating, I feel guilty and I can't seem to control myself from ordering takeout or spending money. Now it seems like I can't function without ordering food or spending money. I can't control myself and I have to eat, but when I do, I become even more irritated and angry, and I still can't write my thesis. Every day is so painful, and life feels meaningless and joyless. I have no interest in this damn thesis at all, I hate it! It's this thesis that's ruining me! Even other work-related matters are going wrong all the time, and I have a short temper. I really want to argue with my advisor, I hate that damn woman. Clearly, she was the one at fault first, but she tried to cover it up and blamed me instead. What a bastard! I am suffering every day now, what a damn waste of time studying! Selling socks on the street is better than this! Stupid thesis! Whoever loves writing it should go ahead and write it! Now I just can't control myself, I order takeout and eat eat eat every day. I really hate myself for eating like this, but I can't control it! What should I do? Just chop off my hands.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner, I understand your frustration and anxiety. Here, I would like to share some of my thoughts to see if they can help you. First, let's clarify the root cause of your irritability. Is it about ordering food, feeling guilty about spending money, struggling with writing a paper, or having emotional resistance towards your teacher? You have mentioned multiple reasons, so prioritize them based on their importance and tackle them one by one. When you figure out how to address these psychological burdens, you will feel much lighter. Secondly, I sense that your emotions are strongly related to the paper and your teacher. Is there a conflict or an unfriendly relationship with your teacher? Or is it that your teacher assigned the paper and you're frustrated with that? Clarify what you really want. Writing a paper can be difficult and demanding, but it is an essential academic task that must be completed on time. So, accept it calmly and work on it according to the deadlines. Emotions will only cloud your thoughts and hinder your ability to complete the paper. Lastly, I believe that there are many templates available for papers and teachers are usually willing to give guidance. Maintain a positive attitude, concentrate, and write with peace of mind. You will definitely be able to complete it, believe in yourself. As for ordering food, it may have started as a convenience, but gradually became a habit and made you lazy to cook or go out to eat. I suggest that if you have the opportunity on weekends, try cooking some homemade dishes yourself. When you are busy with studying or work, take a break and go out for some fresh air, and enjoy a delicious meal. If you spend too much time in your room and order food all the time, it is natural to feel restless. So, if you are capable, try to cook your own food. If you can't, go out to eat. To maintain a good mood, you must be active and activate those stagnant cells. Keep going, I believe you can do it.

Thank you for your answers. I was in a hurry and didn't go into details. The woman I dislike is not my supervisor, just someone I encountered at work who has hindered my progress. My own supervisor is very good to me and doesn't pressure me about the paper. It's just that I've been writing for over half a year and haven't even finished a review, which makes me extremely upset and feel stupid. It's a kind of self-denial and self-loathing. The fundamental issue is my paper, which I find incredibly painful to write. Ordering takeout is a way for me to escape and release my anxiety and resentment. The paper is not just about the graduation requirement, but it makes me feel that my career is bleak and without prospects. In my industry, if I want to become a top professional, I have to keep writing this damn thing. It's really painful. The current pain is all because of the shitty decisions I made when applying.

I and you are the same kind of people, and there are also people who I find very unpleasant. There are also some things that I have to do, and I understand this emotion as "making mistakes with responsibility." Ordering takeout is an expensive behavior, but I still want to do it because I am irritable. Besides eating, we can't find any other way to vent. But after eating, I calm down and feel that I have done wrong. Why? Because I spent money. Money doesn't come easy, so where does this guilt come from? As for writing papers, it's not a big deal. It's not like I'm writing for a teacher, and I don't owe her anything. It's just to give myself an account.

question: I feel like all my friends have started to hate me. Should I leave?
description: I used to be in a romantic relationship with a friend, but only the two of us knew. Later, we broke up for certain reasons, and they quickly found someone new, while I have not. Afterwards, I became just a regular friend to them, and things were going well. But then things started to feel off. They began to dislike me more and more, and their partner also started to dislike me as well. They would double standards, maliciously speculate about me, and nitpick on every little thing. These accumulated incidents kept increasing in frequency. I've thought about leaving them a few times, but they always pull me back, claiming it was just a joke. Should I completely cut ties with them and leave?
keywords: Interpersonal, communication, friends, deceit and trust.

answers.answer_text: Sometimes, a person's intuition is very accurate, especially when it comes to someone they care about. Your feelings are probably correct if you think they dislike you. People's emotions are complex and ever-changing. The reason why they dislike you is not that important because it's hard to figure out and not worth it. Secondly, if they try to bring you back, is it out of genuine feelings for you? I don't think so. Managing a friend who is optional is easier than maintaining a completely disconnected friend. They don't want to be the bad person; they are trying to salvage the situation so that in their hearts, they don't feel responsible for the breakdown in your relationship. What is a friend? It's a relationship based on mutual tolerance, understanding, and making each other's lives happier. If this relationship only brings criticism and adds to your sadness, then the meaning of being friends is lost. Are they still friends? So, don't worry about what they think of you. Just quietly walk away. When they turn around, they will realize that you have already gone far because it's not worth giving them a grand ending.

Hello, OP: It sounds like you are currently conflicted, feeling that your friends are starting to dislike you and you are hesitating to leave. I'm not clear on how you and your former romantic friend broke up. What was the foundation of their relationship like? Have you considered that by becoming just a regular friend, you might be affecting the further development of their relationship? Additionally, I'm not sure how you feel in this relationship among the three of you. How does their excessive intimacy make you feel? I'm speculating blindly here, but is there perhaps some envy in your heart? Suppressing this envy may be causing your attitude and tone to create an awkward atmosphere between you all. So, is their dislike towards you because they feel that you are constantly sabotaging the further development of their intimate relationship?

It sounds like you want to improve your life and leaving is a good choice. You can think about what this relationship has brought you. After breaking up, he got a girlfriend and still remains friends with you. How do you feel at this point? Are you relaxed, happy, accepting, or anxious, uneasy, and even a little jealous at times? So, what makes you hesitate when you're unhappy? Do you not have other friends? Are you afraid of losing? Take it easy. Having had a romantic relationship shows that you have the ability to attract others. Even if you leave this group of friends, you will still have other friends, won't you? Being comfortable in a relationship is important. Caring for each other, needing each other, not necessarily always being together, but thinking about each other feels good, not seeing each other is fine, and seeing each other is also good. Sometimes, when we interact with others, we find that our mental energy keeps decreasing, and our state of mind gets worse. At least it means that this interaction may not be suitable. It doesn't necessarily mean who is right or wrong, but you can decisively leave or gradually distance yourself.

Don't think that people dislike you, because they are all very busy. Adjust your attitude and love them no matter what! You are not Chinese currency, not everyone will like you. Disliking you is just a phase in life, once this phase is over, everything will be fine. In three years of middle school, you will meet different people, high school will also be lively, and university will be a whole new world. Each stage lasts only three to four years, once you get through it, everything will be a fresh start. Why be so obsessed with the present? Your worth will be recognized by someone, and there will always be people willing to be friends with you. In the future, everyone will truly grow up. You may be kind to others, but they may not necessarily be kind to you. However, they will never turn around and hurt you. So, your good intentions will always be seen by someone. May you wait patiently and face things calmly.

question: It's still the same, feeling like my hands and feet are on my boyfriend's body.
description: In the past, it was considered normal for me to depend on my boyfriend. Then, in the six months since the lifting of the pandemic lockdown, being alone at home for a long time, negative emotions have been increasing day by day. I started talking to my boyfriend about all my negative thoughts every day. Later, we met, and it started from that meeting. We almost meet every weekend, either him finding me or me finding him. During this time of meeting, my negative emotions have not improved. I just particularly enjoy the feeling of being comforted by him and the feeling of having him by my side. As we meet more times, my dependence on him becomes greater. When it's time for me to go home, I start to be extremely afraid of going back. So I desperately ask him if I can go back a bit later. I always feel like I can stay a little longer, so I can see him by my side for a bit longer. And if he can't come this weekend due to work reasons, I must make him come. Otherwise, I feel extremely uncomfortable, so uncomfortable that I want to die. He has tolerated my tantrums countless times. In the midst of my tantrums, he has mentioned breaking up twice. I thought there was nothing scarier than a breakup. I have promised him at the moment of breaking up and making up, and I have told myself that I won't be stubborn anymore. But I didn't expect that after we make up, I'm still the same.

answers.answer_text: Author, hello, I understand your inner distress and I hope my response can help you. I want to say the following to you: 1. You love your boyfriend very much, and he loves you too. In this vast world, it's not easy to find someone you love and who loves you back. So please cherish it. However, cherishing does not mean being together all the time. If you're together all the time, it could have a negative effect. Distance can be beautiful. 2. Your dependence on your boyfriend can actually be transferred to other aspects. I suggest seeking support from people other than your boyfriend, such as good female friends, other family members, or any other suitable person. When your boyfriend can't be with you, you can find someone else to accompany you. You will discover that besides your boyfriend, there are many other people who care about you. They also care about you and you can feel the warmth of being supported and understood. If they can't be with you physically, calling them is also a great way. 3. Engage in activities that you enjoy and don't focus all your attention on your boyfriend. Set yourself a suitable goal and work hard to achieve it. In the process of achieving your goal, you will focus your attention on what you need to do and won't be so concerned about your boyfriend's company. I remember when I was a junior in college, my boyfriend had already graduated and it would take him six months to come back and see me. It was difficult at first and I would cry for a long time when we separated. Later, I focused my energy on preparing for postgraduate exams and we would talk on the phone three times a day. This helped me avoid the emotions of dependence and longing. 4. Find other ways to relieve negative emotions. You can try writing, listening to music, exercising, spending time in nature, meditating, or any other activity that helps you relax. Everyone is an independent individual, and while emotions need mutual dependence, they also need independence. I hope you can find the right balance, enjoy intimacy, and focus on being yourself.

Hello, OP. It is evident that you love your boyfriend very much. So, you always want to be with him, wanting to stick to him all the time. Due to the pandemic, you haven't seen each other for a long time, and because of this, you want to be with him all the time. At first, your boyfriend may also feel comfortable, but in the long run, both of you may feel annoyed. Everyone has their own life, even though you are in a romantic relationship, but you not only have a love life but also have work and regular life. It is not easy to have someone who loves you and whom you also love, but we cannot lose our original selves because of him. From your words, I feel that you have lost yourself in this relationship. You don't know why you are doing this, but you just want to do it. As a result, your boyfriend is annoyed and even wants to break up with you. Sometimes, it is necessary for both men and women to think from each other's perspective and consider things more. In my personal opinion, the best way for two people to get along is to feel at ease even if they don't meet each other, and they know what the other person is doing. And then, in both of your free time, you can focus on your relationship. Isn't that a beautiful thing? While being in a relationship is important, we cannot make it our whole life. Best wishes~.

question: High school freshman girl, has a strained relationship with her mother, how to ease it?
description: My mother has a strong prejudice against me. She always thinks of me the same way as my biological father. Selfish, disregarding the family, greedy. Once, in extreme circumstances, she yelled out and said, "You are indeed just like your father." So in the past few years, I have been trying to regulate my behavior and actions, striving not to be associated with those few words. My biological father is a taboo topic. In this family, no one wants to mention him, but she always brings him up. In short, she always tears through that layer of paper first. I also have a younger brother, born to my stepfather, who is seven years younger than me. That boy is willful and spiteful towards me for some reason, always opposing me in every way. My mother also blindly favors him, never taking my side. Even though we share blood and family ties, they all seem distant and cold in the face of these constant hurtful words. But unfortunately, I have a strong emphasis on family values. I always believe that without family, it would feel like missing half the sky. I can't accept this change, so I try to please them in every way. Maybe that's what society calls a people pleaser. However, as my younger brother grew older, even with my mother's constant guidance, his academic performance remained poor. My stepfather always plans for him. The daughter who spends her days and nights with him might not be able to compare to the sweet nothings whispered by my stepfather. And so, I don't know when I became a person who is greedy for money and ungrateful. I'm so tired.
keywords: Treatment, treatment methods, psychological counseling, venting and listening.

answers.answer_text: Hello, dear questioner. Hugs to you! After reading your description, it seems that you haven't received enough care from your family, and the influence of your mother has left you confused about the future. I truly sympathize with what you have been through. You mentioned that your mother has transferred some of her dislike for your biological father onto you, and in order to make her happy, you have been shaping your personality in a way that she can accept. However, this has had a negative impact on your own development. You mentioned that you feel conflicted inside, and it reminds me of a saying, "In the end, we all become the person we used to dislike the most." Perhaps this is not your intention, but because your mother constantly brings up the image of your father, it has formed a psychological suggestion. The more you don't want something, the more it comes to you; the more you don't want to become a certain person, the more you tend to develop in the direction you least want. In psychology, this phenomenon is described by Murphy's Law. Maybe you can give yourself positive psychological suggestions and remind yourself to be grateful.

question: A 12-year-old boy is exhibiting unusual behavior in class. What should I do?
description: I worked as a teacher at a tutoring institution during the summer break. In our class, there is a boy, a (tall and chubby), and his desk mate, b (thin). They often playfully tease each other, but they have never argued. They always sit together in all the classes, so I thought they were friends. However, today I noticed that whenever class ends, a would always come up from behind and hug b, then shake him from behind. B said, "Stop doing this to me." Because it was the end of class and everyone was playing, no one noticed anything unusual. After class, b ignored a. I felt really uncomfortable about this. It's normal for fifth graders to have good relationships with their same-sex friends, but I don't understand why a would do this. Is this normal behavior? I'm a college student with no teaching experience. What can I do for them in this situation? Should I intervene?
keywords: Development, personality improvement, student growth, child development.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. I want to say that you're amazing for noticing such subtle phenomena during your internship. It's normal for children to get along well with those of the same sex, especially when these two boys are desk mates and sit closer to each other. In their minds, they may trust each other more due to the proximity. This could have led to the action A took towards B. For A, it may symbolize friendly interaction with a friend and show that they have a close relationship. However, at the same time, this action may not be as pleasant for B. After all, everyone has different behavior patterns, ways of getting along, and ways of expressing emotions, which can lead to misunderstandings. Perhaps you can talk to A about how he perceives his relationship with B and whether he considers B a close friend (since there is an apparent difference in their body size). You can remind him to be more mindful of his actions at times and to consider the comfort of both friends in their interactions. Additionally, you can also talk to B and help explain that A's actions may indicate that they have a good relationship. You might suggest to B that he discuss his thoughts with A as sometimes being angry and ignoring him may not be conducive to their friendship. Best wishes!

question: Loneliness, solitude, isolation, independence, what do they all mean?
description: Loneliness, solitude, isolation, independence, sometimes all these feelings come together, and I don't know who is who, what are they?

answers.answer_text: Hello, poster, hello, the following are some of my understanding, I would like to share with you: (1) About loneliness and solitude: In my opinion, loneliness and solitude are both states and feelings. We feel lonely because we do not feel understood by others. In fact, we long to be understood and cared for. The emphasis on "one" implies being alone, but this "one" is a forced state. (2) Isolation, on the other hand, refers to a relationship where one consciously ignores the other party, it is a distancing in terms of a relationship. Isolation means being left alone, if one is being isolated, they can be passive and alone. (3) Independence is a form of self-reliance and proactive choice. It means I can choose the kind of life I want by my own abilities. Independence doesn't mean being distant from others, but rather maintaining one's own unique values and approach to handling things, having one's own judgments. (4) When all these emotions fill the heart, the poster needs to know whether their current situation is a result of proactive choice or being forced to accept it. Or in other words, how can we turn passivity into proactivity, this is something the poster needs to consider. #The world and I love you, wishing you well~.

Loneliness: No one to accompany, no one can enter one's own world, not understood. Solitude: Constantly mocking oneself, unwilling to communicate with others, compared to the arrogance of loneliness, solitude is often the result of low self-esteem. Isolation: I think it is a paranoid existence, also a strong existence, knowing how to strive in pain. Independence: A person with a very strong inner self, not caring about any emotions, viewing friendship, family relationship, and love as insignificant. However, independent people may still rely on one of these emotions, but not all at the same time.

question: Mother always scolds people, what methods can make her change?
description: My mother always criticizes and scolds people. She finds fault with everything. I really want her to change this bad habit of speaking impulsively, but I often feel helpless and don't know what to do. Is there any way to help her change this bad habit and also make our family more harmonious?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Give you a warm hug. From OP's description, I understand that the behavior of criticizing others is a long-term habit developed by their mother. It may be difficult to completely correct it, but we can try the following methods to help her alleviate this behavior. First, we need to make her aware of this problem through communication, so that she can understand the impact of her behavior on others and the possible damage to family relationships. Secondly, invite her to participate in activities and practices that help improve her mood, so that she can know some ways to calm herself down when her emotions are intense. We can also learn these methods to promptly calm the other person down when they want to get angry, and avoid direct conflicts at the moment.

It may be possible to change, but definitely very difficult. Criticism is the way the subject's mother communicates with others, it is her way of expressing her views, attracting attention, and it is also the way she has learned to speak from her own parents, partners, and environment over the decades. She should be able to get what she wants through this method, the attention of her parents, the compromise of her partner, the obedience of her child... If this method has caused her great harm or loss of important opportunities, she would have changed it a long time ago, right? She has her own life, we have our own life; we cannot change her life, nor do we want to be influenced by her anymore; all we can do is to isolate ourselves from her life, not to be entangled, and live our own life well.

question: Why do I want to ignore my best friend more and more? I want to end the friendship but I don't know how to say it.
description: Seeing the messages my best friend sends me always brings great pressure and makes me feel anxious and irritable. I don't want to reply to her messages, and I especially dislike it when she sends voice messages and video calls. She is an idol fan, and she often argues with me because her idol is different from mine. She is into fandom culture, but I'm not. She often tells me negative things about my idol and criticizes his character. Then she tries to persuade me to like her idol by highlighting his positive aspects. I really hate this behavior, but I tolerate it. She also likes to playfully hit people and when she gets excited, she would suddenly slap you. I have complained to her about it, but she responds by saying, "You're so sensitive. It's just a light slap, it's not that serious." She also likes to call me fat, saying things like, "Why are you so fat? You're so chubby." She also gets angry if someone says another girl looks better than her, and she would pick a fight with that person. Sometimes, if I say something wrong, she would also start insulting people. I haven't done anything, I just endure it. Now that we have graduated and are in different cities, I don't know if this friendship can continue. I want to end the friendship, but I don't know how to say it and I'm afraid to say it.

answers.answer_text: OP, your best friend may be a more laid-back person, self-centered, and easily influenced by her own thoughts without much empathy for others. Perhaps distance creates beauty, and university life is more complex than before. Perhaps after entering university and joining different social circles, she has gradually matured and some of her inappropriate behaviors or thoughts may change over time. Maybe after entering university, both of you have formed new social circles and your contact may not be as close as before. If you usually chat with each other or when she confides in you or talks about unhappy things, maybe you can discuss with her some issues she might need to pay attention to. This way, it can improve your friendship and help her adapt better to the new social circles. Best wishes!

question: The child is a little troublesome, how can I become a qualified mother?
description: The child can be a bit troublesome, as parents, how should we handle them and be better parents?
keywords: Growth and developmental patterns, children's growth.

answers.answer_text: How can I become a better parent? This question needs to be differentiated by the child's age, and different parenting methods should be adopted according to different stages of the child's development. When I saw you say that your child can be a bit difficult, I wonder if your child is still a baby. Babies need complete parents. We need to differentiate whether the child is being difficult because their needs are not being met, or if the child is naturally high-maintenance. The method of differentiation is simple. As parents, you need to observe your child with patience. What does the child need when they are being difficult? Are they hungry and want to eat? Do they need a diaper change? Or are they feeling bored and want their mother to comfort them? If you observe and meet these needs in a timely manner, then observe if the child is still being difficult. If they are still being difficult, we can conclude that this child is basically high-maintenance. Having a high-maintenance child is not a big problem, but parents need to be more patient in dealing with them, patiently soothing and comforting them, treating them gently and mildly, giving them enough love, securing their sense of safety, and providing sufficient emotional support. As a result, the child's difficult behavior will gradually diminish, and as they grow older, parents will find it less worrisome. Best wishes, the world and I love you!

Babies communicate with the outside world through crying, which can sometimes be annoying. The care provided by parents is crucial for children aged one or two. It depends on whether the caregivers are sensitive enough, and whether their emotions are stable. It is important to take care of one's emotions on a regular basis and, based on understanding and fully accepting one's emotions, use reason to think and control one's actions. The fundamental goal of emotional management is to prevent emotions from affecting decision-making. No matter how "bad" your emotions may be, the emotions themselves are not the problem. What truly troubles you, what makes you feel bad, is not your "emotions," but the feelings that emotions bring to you and your negative understanding of emotions. First, face and experience your emotions. Acceptance means fully experiencing and feeling your emotions. Experiencing and feeling emotions means that "you" have control, and emotions become objects, so they can no longer control you. Second, analyze your emotions. There are two sets of thinking systems in humans. One is automated thinking, which is unconscious reflex formed in millions of years of evolution and your personal growth process. The other is rational thinking, which is the choice you make after thinking about something. We need to first determine whether the reminders received from the emotional system are correct before we can decide how to handle them. Third, think rationally. The ultimate goal of emotional management is to enable you to think rationally about problems. You can learn to cut off the influence of emotions on your decision-making system when your emotions are excited; rational thinking can be acquired through continuous practice. Take care of a crying baby in a stable emotional state. Reasons for a baby's crying: 1. It's too hot or too cold. 2. It's too dry. 3. Indigestion, poor digestion, getting hot or eating too much at night can also lead to restless sleep. 4. Uncomfortable blankets or sleeping positions, and many other reasons. It is advisable to consult a professional doctor for other possible reasons. May these words accompany you.

question: I am feeling conflicted while eating from a bowl and thinking about what's in the pot. What should I do?
description: I am a girl, currently in my second year of college. Here's what happened: during the final exams of last semester, I met an older student who was pursuing a master's degree in the study room (he actively introduced himself to me and added me on WeChat). I could feel that he had feelings for me. After the exams, he took me out for a meal. I also had feelings for him and things were going well. However, when the break started and I went home, he stopped contacting me, and I didn't contact him either. But during the break, he contacted me once, saying that he was busy studying for exams. Now that school has started again, we haven't been in touch. But I still have feelings for him. As for why I say I'm having the cake and wanting to eat it too, it's because during the summer break, I met a boy and we had strong feelings for each other. We got together in a short period of time. But after cooling down, I realized I still had feelings for that older student. During the summer break, I broke up with this boy twice. A big part of the reason was that we were only together for a few days before having to be in a long-distance relationship, which made me feel insecure. Another part of the reason was because of this older student. I also confessed to this boy about my feelings for the older student. I'm afraid that when I go back to school, I will end up liking the older student and not liking him anymore, which would make things really difficult. But this boy seems to have genuinely fallen for me, he

answers.answer_text: Your response to emotions relies on a sense of dependency and warmth, which is an inner psychological need of yours that may be influenced by your upbringing. You seek emotional connections in intimate relationships in order to comfort yourself. It is recommended to seek psychological counseling to fulfill these inner needs. This way, your approach to emotions will be based on genuine emotional needs rather than serving as internal compensation. I recommend reading the book "Encountering Your Unknown Self" to explore your inner self, establish a connection with it, and find yourself.

He is very persistent with me. I feel very comfortable and at ease when I am with him, and I am also attached to the feeling of being held and pampered by him. He now gives me enough sense of security, and he is not the kind of guy who takes relationships lightly. I am not someone who takes relationships lightly either, but even after coming to school, I still miss this senior and secretly hope to meet him. I even want to take the initiative to contact him and test his attitude towards me now. I know that this senior may not like me as much, but I still think that if I had contacted him after his exams in the summer vacation, maybe things wouldn't be like this now? I feel that my current thoughts are very dangerous. I'm afraid that if I really go find this senior, I will be betraying my current boyfriend, especially since we are in a long-distance relationship. I don't know what has gotten into me. I feel like a terrible woman.

question: Recently, I have been making a lot of mistakes at work. How can I relieve work stress?
description: Lately, I have been making mistakes at work and feeling stressed and upset. What should I do?

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP. First, let me give you a big hug. Let's take a look at your problem: making mistakes at work and feeling a lot of stress. We don't know what is causing you to make mistakes at work. Is it carelessness? Restlessness? Or is it due to the pressure from your personal and professional life? I suggest that you identify the reasons for your mistakes and then work on overcoming them. If it's due to carelessness, try to be more meticulous by double-checking documents, contracts, and so on. If you're feeling restless, engage in activities that you enjoy and that bring you happiness to improve your mood. Once you've calmed down, you can continue with your work. If you're experiencing a lot of pressure, find ways to release that pressure before tackling your tasks with a relaxed mindset. Let me share a few methods for stress relief with you. It is said that sharing happiness with others doubles the joy, and sharing pain reduces the suffering by half. Expressing yourself is important and necessary. You can choose to confide in friends and family, seeking comfort and solutions from them, or you can vent your negative emotions into an inanimate object. Trust me, you will feel much more relaxed after pouring your heart out. Find healthy and enjoyable ways to decompress, such as going for a run, listening to music, or treating yourself to something delicious. Through these activities, you can release your stress and embrace a better life that awaits you. Finally, do what you love. We often possess tolerance and patience when it comes to the things we love. Engaging in activities we enjoy not only helps us de-stress but also gives us a sense of fulfillment. This sense of accomplishment will benefit you in completing both your work and the issues weighing you down in your personal life.

question: A 22-year-old girl has been lacking passion towards life for a long time.
description: Since high school up till now, it has always been like this. I am happy for a minute or two when I have good food, but then I quickly calm down. Even when walking on the street, I always think that at any given moment, I might fall into a sewer and disappear, or when I see a river, I imagine being swept away and disappearing. However, I don't feel afraid, instead, I find it somewhat amusing. Sometimes, I have the impulse to jump, but I'm afraid of pain. My parents want me to stay by their side and work, but I only want to go to the northwest, to be buried in the yellow soil, living a simple life doesn't matter to me. I can eat plain boiled vegetables for a month without getting tired, it doesn't really matter, I just want to stay alive. It doesn't matter if I die the next second, it would be a waste if my organs cannot be donated. I always think about what my parents' lives will be like after I'm gone. After thinking about it, it's actually just like that, I feel sorry for them, but it only lasts for a while. People always have to go alone in the end. My body is very healthy, just lacking desires. I used to have a passion for things I liked, but now it only lasts for a minute at best. Anyway, no matter what I do, I lack enthusiasm. I want to find a job, but I also dislike interacting with people. I even find it disgusting when my family members try to be affectionate with me. When a close relative of mine fell seriously ill, I couldn't feel any distress, but I could cry for a stranger's passing. My sister raised me, when her child died, the whole family was in mourning, but I remained indifferent. It's difficult for me to empathize with their pain.
keywords: Interpersonal, social anxiety, empathy, social adaptation

answers.answer_text: Hello, from your description, I sense a feeling of emptiness and loneliness. It saddens me to hear what you've been through at the age of 22, as if you don't want to care too much about it. Although you have parents, a sister, and loved ones, it seems like you lack intimate experiences. You mentioned that you would cry for the death of a stranger, but feel nothing for the grief of your loved ones. Could this be a silent rebellion? We often feel the freedom to express our true emotions towards strangers, but when it comes to loved ones, we are often bound by many expectations. It's as if you "should" feel grateful, "should" be obedient, "should" be filial, "should" take care of your parents, and so on. As a result, when it's "supposed" to be difficult, you can't even feel that discomfort anymore. You mentioned that this state began in high school, which is a period of personal identity development. During this period, our inner desires are easily overshadowed by academic pressure and uncomprehending family members. There is always a need to live within the demands of others, but no one, including yourself, can prioritize your own feelings. It creates a disconnect between you and your emotions, and your body, leading to that feeling of emptiness and loneliness, "losing enthusiasm for life." To establish enthusiasm for life, you first need to establish a connection with yourself, become aware of and value your own feelings, sincerely face yourself, and bravely express yourself to the outside world, even if it means anger or conflict. Let the withered true self within you sprout and grow. Only then can you give space to your own emotions, feel the "flavor" of the world, and rediscover where your enthusiasm lies.

Hello there, living a life without passion and hope for a long time, the world becomes gray. It must be tough. I hope that my following answer can help you and bring some color to your life. When did you start feeling peaceful about the world, being lack of enthusiasm resembles living with post-traumatic stress disorder after experiencing a major trauma. Is there any obstacle that you find difficult to overcome? Dear, if you can't let go of the past, it will continue to affect your present and even your future. So, in order to live in this world, you need to learn to accept yourself and reconcile with your past self in order to live in the present moment. You might try to solve the problems that trouble you and then try to live a new life. Although you are less sensitive to external stimuli, you are not completely numb. At least you still feel fear and pain. This proves that you still have a strong will to survive. Since you have to live, you should live well and not waste your life and the good years. You are still young, and the future holds endless possibilities. Don't easily confine yourself to a particular circle, thinking that you will live your whole life like that. Learn to empathize with the people around you. You are a very rational person, and at least you know what you should do. You just temporarily lack the ability to do so. So you might try to communicate with your family, make a plan, and try to understand yourself and build emotional connections with others by reading some books on communication skills. Cultivate your interests. Everyone has their own hobbies and interests, which can bring joy and motivation to our lives. Although you currently lack interest in anything around you, you will change, and things will change with time. With sincere effort, you will always find things that interest you. I hope that at that time, you can persist and cultivate your interests and love life. Good luck!

Hello, thank you for the invitation. Who are you trying to punish with this "neither alive nor dead" state? (This was my immediate reaction when I saw your message.) If we were in a counseling room, I might discuss what happened in high school, when these symptoms began, and what you were like before. There is too much to understand, and it can only be uncovered in a counseling session. Since this is a public screen response, I can only try to help you based on limited information: 1. Have you received professional assessments for depression or other psychological factors? These assessments are usually conducted by professional doctors to determine if medication is necessary. Psychological counseling is an auxiliary method in conjunction with medication. Medication can help our damaged brains regain rational functioning, which allows psychological counseling/treatment to better identify the causes of harm. question: Every time I communicate with people, I feel nervous, scared, and afraid when looking into their eyes.
description: There's no way to maintain prolonged eye contact with people. My facial expression becomes increasingly stiff, as do my eyes. I also panic when others stare at me, and my facial expressions become unnatural. I'm afraid that people will notice and try to avoid and escape from their gaze. Once others stop paying attention to me, the pain subsides. This lack of social interaction has seriously affected my life and work! How can I overcome this?
keywords: Treatment, disease diagnosis, treatment methods, psychological counseling.

answers.answer_text: Hello! As the old saying goes, "the eyes are the windows to the soul." There is a lot we can tell from someone's eyes, including their emotions and thoughts. It's normal to feel nervous when being stared at for a long time or when staring at others. However, there is a condition called "fear of eye contact," which is a type of social anxiety disorder and a form of neurosis. It is most common in teenagers between the ages of fifteen to twenty. They fear making eye contact with others and avoid speaking in social situations. They often believe that people are staring at them or talking about them. The main symptoms include nervousness, difficulty concentrating, obsessive thoughts and ideas, as well as accompanying negative emotions such as anxiety, depression, irritability, and fear. Many people with this condition have trouble with normal social interactions, greatly impacting their daily life and work. However, there is no need to worry excessively. Neurosis is essentially a temporary dysregulation of higher neural activity, and fear of eye contact is a common and prevalent condition during adolescence. It occurs due to the rapid physical development during puberty, which can be challenging to adapt to psychologically, compounded by the stress of education and work, resulting in poor adaptation of the nervous system. First and foremost, it is important to maintain a positive mindset and believe that you can overcome your current difficulties. Consciously engage in more social activities and start conversations with people you are familiar with, making sure not to deliberately avoid eye contact. Trust in yourself, you can do it! Keep going, keep going, keep going!

Speaking while looking into the other person's eyes also conveys a sense of confidence and sincerity. If you experience panic, stiffness, or the desire to escape, it reflects a strong self-protective awareness within you, a lack of security, and an unwillingness to reveal your own emotions and thoughts to the outside world. You are highly sensitive to external contact and feel that being stared at by others is an invasion, hence the fear and retreat, fearing that others will see your inner thoughts and lack of confidence through your eyes. In interpersonal communication, it is necessary to maintain eye contact to appear polite. Here's a little trick for you: when you want to look at someone, you don't have to stare directly into their eyes. Instead, focus on their nose. This way, you won't feel nervous, and the other person will think you are looking into their eyes and not consider it impolite. In addition, you can prepare some props based on the content of the conversation. For example, if you need to discuss work with a boss or colleague, have a notebook in front of you. During the conversation, you can occasionally shift your gaze to the notebook, pretending to be looking at work-related content. This can help alleviate your nervousness. However, the most fundamental aspect is to improve from within by facing your fears and insecurities head-on. Find ways to strengthen your sense of security and self-confidence. question: My foreign girlfriend, 27 years old, has been suffering from depression for 7 years and has trouble sleeping. How can I help her?

I feel tired, but my mind keeps flooding with all kinds of things, thoughts, and so on. I try to control it, but it doesn't work. Every night, I can only stay awake until I'm very tired before falling asleep. This is causing me a lot of distress. Do I have a mental problem?

answers.answer_text: Hello, it seems that you are experiencing symptoms of insomnia recently. Did anything special happen a week ago? What event or situation has been affecting you? It's important to identify the cause in order to find a solution and address the problem at its root. I hope my response can help you, and I wish you well.

question: 32-year-old woman, what is the cause of the obstacles in her work?
description: I followed my grandmother as a child, while my parents worked outside with my younger brother. My grandmother spoiled me a bit, not letting me do anything, even at the age of eight or nine, she still dressed me in socks, shoes, and clothes! She wouldn't let me do anything at home, only study and play! After graduating, I found myself unable to do things, lacking the ability to complete tasks properly, even though I understand the theory! There are obstacles in completing tasks, and I can't do things properly, whether it's work or household chores. Unless someone is commanding me, it will be slightly better! As a result, I have been laid off multiple times. Can anyone help analyze this situation?

answers.answer_text: In the process of being arranged and substituted from a young age, it has led to a series of issues in your life and career! To put it more bluntly: you are unable to take the responsibility for your own life that you should. When a person lacks the courage to face and accept their responsibilities, life will present them with many problems, forcing them to grow up. Only when you can see these responsibilities and willingly take them on, can you truly be reborn! Give it a try, it is never too late to grow up again, as long as you are truly willing to embrace this awakening and see your own brilliance! The family is the embryonic form of the workplace. When a child participates in household chores from a young age, they understand that their personal efforts can contribute to the collective improvement. Such children will have better teamwork skills, be more independent and reliable. At the same time, when helping with household chores, children also develop empathy and are better able to identify the difficulties that everyone faces, which is important professional soft skills. For example, "when a child takes out the trash or brings out the clothes, they will realize that we need to do something to integrate into life. Life is not just about me, it's not just about my immediate needs, I am part of the entire ecosystem. I am a member of the family and when I grow up, I will be a member of the workforce." You don't get what you "want," you only get what you "work" for. A child becomes a useful adult not because of what you do for them, but by teaching them to do it themselves!
