Help your inner child grow up, starting now, from this moment! I hope what I said is helpful to you.

Hello, I'm glad to be able to answer your question. From your description, it seems that your grandmother has been overly doting on you since you were young. She doesn't let you do anything, even at the age of eight or nine, she doesn't let you wear socks, shoes, or clothes, and she doesn't let you do anything at home either, only studying and playing. From this description, it seems that you feel obstructed when doing things, and you often feel that there is only one method, and that method is ineffective. Apart from this method, the only other method is to stop. It seems that when doing things, there are only these two methods, and you get stuck in a predicament. We say that actually there are always at least three solutions to every problem. What you lack is the ability to think in multiple ways, which is called divergent thinking. It's not that we lack the neural network for divergent thinking, but rather that we have been instilled with too many limiting beliefs since childhood, which create many frameworks and rules within the neural network. This is not allowed, that is not allowed, so your original neural network has not been released and utilized. Therefore, breaking these rules and frameworks is the first step in enhancing divergent thinking. Here's a simple example: if you encounter a similar problem in the future, you can think, "If it's possible to do this thing, where could it be possible: who/what/where could I find?" This way of thinking can help us broaden our thinking network, and then we can find ways to do things instead of staying in the mindset of "there is only one method, and if it doesn't work, I'll stop," and not being able to make progress. In addition, this pattern may have led to a learned helplessness and a low sense of self-worth and self-efficacy. At this time, even before doing anything, you may already deny yourself. You said that you understand the theory, but in practice, from theory to implementation, from knowing to doing, it requires practice. Continuous practice, reflection, learning, and practice again is the process. So in the future, you can look for opportunities to do the following thinking exercises: randomly choose a goal, for example, from Shenzhen to Shanghai, and imagine three different methods to reach the destination; or you can think of a question like "how can I see new books without spending money?" and come up with three different methods, and after thinking about it, tell yourself that you're not allowed to think about the previous three methods and think of new methods. Repeat this kind of thinking exercise multiple times to expand your thinking network, and then stop. In fact, you will be very happy during this process because you will start to appreciate your wild ideas, stimulate your sense of humor, problem-solving abilities, and the creative part of your neural network. Finally, I wish you a breakthrough!

At the age when one is supposed to be able to do things independently, it is a realization that many things cannot be done well. This state of affairs indeed makes people feel frustrated, helpless, and powerless. From your own experience of growing up, you must have felt some grievances and regrets from not being with your parents since childhood, right? Perhaps there is also some anger? Your grandmother's doting on you caused you to not know how to handle some household chores, and you only knew how to study and play. You think this is also one of the reasons why you are facing difficulties in your work now. ※ Learn to accept yourself: Find a quiet place, quiet down, and read a prayer of self-acceptance. Accept your body, accept your anxiety, accept your strengths, and also accept your weaknesses. Baidu search "prayer of self-acceptance" and you will find such a paragraph. Read it once a day, and gradually, you will find that your level of self-acceptance is much better, and your perception of things around you will also be different. ※ Nurture the inner child: Take a look back at that little you who was left at home. Although you were a bit lonely, your grandmother treated you well. When you were young, you didn't need to worry about so many trivial matters; you could rely on your grandmother for help. Now, you have grown up and become an adult who is capable of taking responsibility for yourself. You no longer need others to help or instruct you on what to do; you can learn to do it yourself. ※ Find inner strength: Tear off those labels on yourself, and follow your heart to do things. Don't judge, what you do is the best. No matter what, many things are not accomplished in one fell swoop. Compliment yourself every day, see where you have done well, give yourself some positive suggestions, and gradually improve!

Hello, the host cannot do anything well on their own and needs someone else to direct them in order to do things well. This state of affairs makes the host feel a little frustrated and they also hope that they can do things well, both in work and in life. The fact that the host has come here seeking answers also indicates a strong desire for change. The most important thing in achieving something is to have the motivation to change. When the host was young, they lived with their grandmother who doted on them and didn't let them do anything. Although the host knew how to do things, they still lacked the initiative. From a psychological perspective, the behavior and thoughts of an adult are related to the patterns of interaction with their primary caregivers during early childhood or the early stages of life. The lack of motivation, from a self-psychology perspective, is because the primary caregivers did not provide long-term, stable affirmation, appreciation, or response during the preverbal period, nor did they have idealized role models or sufficient satisfaction, resulting in the child lacking self-confidence and lacking motivation to do anything. The grandmother prevented the child from doing anything, ostensibly out of love and concern, but in fact, such indulgence made the child realize their own incompetence. This has led to the child subconsciously feeling that they are not good enough and can't do anything well, and these subconscious beliefs are controlling the host and preventing them from taking initiative. Suggestions: 1. The host can examine the psychological motivations behind their inability to do things, what has happened in the past, and what impact it has had on them. 2. In real life, the host can set some simple and achievable tasks, starting with small things around them, gradually building self-confidence. 3. The host can also seek help from friends or family members who provide a sense of security to help them persist in doing something, providing supervision and support.

Questioner, hello, I feel really sorry for this problem and I give you a hug. I hope to bring you some warmth and comfort. [Feedback Summary] First, let's summarize the problem I saw, you take a look if it's right. 1. The questioner, female, 32 years old. 2. Your parents work outside with your younger brother, while you are a left-behind child. 3. You grew up with your grandmother since you were young, and she spoils you a lot and does many things she shouldn't do for you. 4. After graduating and entering society, you found that you don't know how to do many things. 5. You realize that you know the theory behind many things, but when it comes to actually doing them, you encounter obstacles unless someone is instructing you. 6. As a result, you have been fired many times, and you want to know what is going on. [Understanding and Analysis] Let me talk about my understanding and analysis. First, let's talk about the issue with your parents. Only one sentence mentions your parents, that they work outside with your younger brother while you have been with your grandmother since you were young. What surprised me is that there is no resentment expressed here. For an adult, it is reasonable to understand their own parents, but it is somewhat unusual for a child to not have any thoughts about the differential treatment from their parents. Regardless of how well your grandmother treats you, your parents chose to bring your younger brother with them instead of you, and you accepted it calmly as if nothing happened. I think there is some element of unreasonableness or suppressed feelings. Second, let's talk about your grandmother's spoiling. You said your grandmother spoils you a lot. Actually, many children enjoy being spoiled, but I sense a hint of complaint between the lines from you. It seems that your grandmother's spoiling has caused the current problems, but is it really the case? Is it true that not doing anything when you were young means you can't do anything when you grow up? I think it's not necessarily true. Third, after graduating, you can't do anything well unless someone guides you. In other words, you can do things when there is someone instructing you. This reminds me of Adler's "teleology," which means that "all human behavior has a purpose." Based on this theory, let's think about where the purpose of not being able to do things well lies. Based on the information given in the problem, I feel that the purpose of not being able to do things well is to want someone to guide you. Why is it like this? My understanding is "compulsive repetition" and "unfinished events." In psychoanalysis theory, there is a concept called "compulsive repetition," which means that people tend to unconsciously repeat traumatic experiences from early years. In psychology, there is a concept called "unfinished business" for what we call "unfinished episodes." Simply put, the unfinished event that keeps haunting you, the one that you still can't let go of after many years, the one that happened long ago but still affects your decision-making and behavior, is your unfinished business. Fourth, my understanding of the whole situation is that the reason you can't do anything well now is to obtain someone's guidance, and you have always lacked guidance, especially when you were young. When we were children, what we wanted most was the guidance of our parents, but your parents were not with you, so you have never fulfilled the desire to receive guidance from your parents in your childhood. As a result, you continue to compulsively repeat the scenes from your early years in order to complete the unfinished business from back then. [Method Recommendations] Here are some suggestions for you: First, I suggest you find a counselor to talk to, preferably one with a background in psychoanalysis. Of course, if you are not ready yet, don't force yourself. Second, you can try meditation. There are many resources on meditation planets, both paid and free, which are good options for you to try. Third, you can write in a journal or write a letter to your younger self. Fourth, communicate with your parents and understand their thoughts back then. I hope my answer can help you. I wish everything will get better!

Hello- if things have been going smoothly, it's important to know that no one is naturally good at everything and has divine assistance. Perhaps you only see their surface success but don't see the effort and time they put into it behind the scenes. Maybe being excessively pampered by your grandmother has prevented you from having any experience in solving problems on your own from childhood to adulthood. This pattern may continue when you start working, but it's okay because it can be corrected. As long as you change your perspective, recognize the shortcomings in your approach that lead to difficulties, and make improvements to enhance and perfect yourself. If things are not going smoothly in your work, have you ever summarized the specific reasons? Have you thought about making some changes?

No matter how old one is, as long as they have not learned or experienced something, it is all new to them, and they may encounter difficulties in the learning process. So don't think of it as an obstacle. As long as you want to change, even if you have to start from scratch, so what? People who have been overly indulged may lack education in responsibilities, gratitude, and social adaptation. So let's make up for it! At the age of 32, as long as you consciously learn these things, you can gain the courage to overcome difficulties. Give it a try. You can also try to find a counselor to understand why you were dismissed and identify your own shortcomings, and then make up for them.

Hello, the topic owner. I saw your question. You described that you have been with your grandmother since childhood, while your parents took your younger brother to work outside. So, how do you feel and what do you think about your parents taking your younger brother and leaving you with your grandmother? You mentioned that your grandmother is somewhat overindulgent, not letting you do anything and still dressing you, even when you're eight or nine years old! At home, she doesn't let you do anything except study and play! From another perspective, it seems that in your grandmother's eyes, there are things that you may not be able to do well and can only rely on others' help. In her eyes, you will always be a child who never grows up. But after graduating, you started to enter society and face many difficulties and things you need to do on your own. They will no longer be able to take care of everything for you like your grandmother did. So your state now is that you don't know how to do things and can't do things well unless someone directs you, just like when your grandmother used to help you and give you instructions to do things. Actually, I can feel your grandmother's love and kindness towards you, but this kind of love is too intrusive and depriving. Children develop a sense of autonomy from the age of three. They want to do many things on their own that they are capable of doing. This is how their sense of competence develops. When they face many challenges in the future, they will believe in themselves. But if, during this time, they have many things done for them by others or have their efforts denied, then when they grow up, they will feel like they can't do anything well  and they won't dare to do things. I asked about your thoughts and feelings about your parents taking your younger brother away in the beginning because from a psychological perspective, children have a strong need for their parents. They might have only understood that your parents love your younger brother and not you when you were so young and they took your younger brother away and left you behind. This might have given you a strong sense of abandonment and made you think that you're not good enough, which would have accompanied you throughout your life. Of course, our analysis of these things is not meant to blame your grandmother and parents. After all, your grandmother only loved you in the way that she knew. And now that you have grown up and experienced some things, you also have started to think about the difficulties you are facing and want to make changes. We often say that awareness is the beginning of change. I hope my answer can be helpful to you. Good luck!

When faced with a situation, you always subconsciously feel that there will always be someone to take care of you, like your grandma, and tell you what to do. But you must remember to tell yourself that you have grown up, become independent, and can do things on your own that you used to fear. Don't be afraid of getting hurt, and don't be afraid of falling down. Open your heart, have the courage to try and do things. How would you know your own strength if you don't give it a try? Wishing you well.

question: Recently, I have become completely hopeless with my boyfriend, but he is persistently clinging onto me. What should I do?
description: I turned eighteen recently and started dating a boyfriend. However, he did some things that showed he doesn't pay attention to details and doesn't even know when I'm mad. When I checked his messages with girls, he agreed to their requests without hesitation and even tried to reason with them. He even took screenshots and sent them to me. One night, he couldn't understand my feelings and I cried all night. I have given up on him and no longer love him, but he keeps bothering me and won't let go. He wants to change, but I have realized that nothing he does impresses me anymore...

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP! Sending you warm hugs~ In your relationship dynamic, it seems like you need emotional comfort and validation. You are a detail-oriented person, but your boyfriend, on the other hand, is more careless and doesn't pay much attention to your sensitive thoughts. He loves you, but he has been loving you in his own way. Both of you are not accustomed to each other's methods, which may cause you to drift apart and ultimately lead to an unsatisfactory end to this relationship. If you no longer love him and want to end this relationship, it might be better to reject him more rationally when facing his persistence. You can express your thoughts and needs to him, but also mention that he has not fulfilled your emotional requirements, and it has come to an end. I hope he can live his life well, and being direct about your stance will be more effective than discussing emotions with him. If he continues to pursue you after you have made your rejection clear, you can choose to cut off contact with him. Best wishes~.

question: When dating a boy two years younger, one always feels like taking a little brother out.
description: Hello everyone, I am dating a guy who is two years younger than me. I feel like I unintentionally criticize him for being immature. One day, KK bought a new bag and came to show me. When I saw his clothes and bag, I had an extreme aversion in my heart. I felt like he dressed like a little boy, while I was dressed professionally that day. It felt like I was going out with my little brother. I don't feel good about this internally, and I don't want to change his sense of fashion, but I do wish he could dress more maturely. Is there a better way to handle this?

answers.answer_text: OP, hello, it is necessary to clarify what you need in a relationship, to distinguish between your true feelings and the opinions from society and those around you. From your description, I can sense your internal conflict and dilemma. On one hand, you unintentionally care about the smallness and immaturity of the other person, and you may be concerned that when you go out, people around you or strangers may comment on it. On the other hand, you may also like the other person and believe that asking them to change their dress taste is not right. It can be seen that you are a rational person who does not have a desire to control the other person in a romantic relationship, but will consider the other person's feelings and not impose your own ideas on them, which is commendable. You can seriously think about why you were initially attracted to the other person. What are the qualities that you like about them? Maybe you initially considered the factor of age, but still chose to be together. This liking and attraction need to be valued. The other person is younger and naturally cannot compare to the charm of some mature men. His dress taste is a symbol of his own preferences and style. Just imagine, do you want the other person to dress more maturely so as not to be criticized by friends and others, or do you want the other person to be more psychologically mature, even if their dress taste is not that good? Is the reason you care about the other person's age because you feel they are young and don't have a certain economic foundation and competitive strength? Or are you afraid that people around you will know that you are dating a younger boyfriend? Is it about "face" or "age" that you care about? With inner confusion and dilemma, you can express yourself openly and honestly to your boyfriend. If he is willing to change, it may be because he loves you very much. If he cannot change, also respect his own growth trajectory. You can express your feelings and thoughts to your boyfriend, without hurting his self-esteem. For example, you can suggest that he tries some new dressing styles and see if he likes them or not. If he feels uncomfortable, also fully respect him. Regarding your concerns about his maturity, you can also communicate seriously. Express your worries and discomfort, such as fear of being ridiculed by colleagues and family, fear of not being firm enough, fear that your future does not have some security, etc. All of these can be talked about. If you want to seriously move forward together, these issues that you care about should not be hidden. Furthermore, encourage and support the other person to grow at their own pace. Since you both chose to be together and love each other, it is best not to force the other person to change for yourself. Although you may compromise and accommodate each other, you should not suppress your concerns and dissatisfaction. Appreciate each other's strengths and charms, as well as accept each other's shortcomings and things that cannot be obtained temporarily. Accompany each other's growth and withstand storms together. This may be the best emotional relationship. Good luck.

question: Bipolar disorder, haven't taken medication for two to three months, having nightmares and experiencing neurotic tinnitus, what should I do?
description: This June, my relationship with my parents became very tense and volatile. I have been receiving psychological therapy on a platform to improve and mediate our relationship. Before that, I used to go to the hospital and take medication on my own for 7 years. Yesterday, I sent them some information about bipolar disorder, hoping they would not scold me or pressure me to go on blind dates. I told them about the seriousness of my condition, including the fact that I may not be able to get married or have children, and that I may have to take medication for the rest of my life. Surprisingly, my parents only realized the severity of the situation now. Even when I had cried and told them before that I might not live past 30, they didn't react this strongly. Now they are crying and sending me messages on WeChat, asking why it has become so serious again. Weren't you getting treatment? Aren't you better now? Can we change hospitals? I originally thought they would get a taste of the pain I had endured before, and I felt a little happy about it. But last night, I had nightmares about being chased, and this afternoon my tinnitus started again, which scares me a lot. I hadn't experienced tinnitus for over a year, and I didn't expect their emotional reaction to trigger it again. I was too blindly confident. I've been consulting with a therapist for the past five months, and I thought my emotions had improved and stabilized, so I stopped going to the hospital and taking medication for about three to four months. Now I'm really anxious about this tinnitus, not knowing when it will return to normal.
keywords: Treatment, physical reactions, disease diagnosis, treatment methods.

answers.answer_text: Many parents do not understand bipolar disorder. In most cases, they think it is just a result of their child being too dramatic. After enlightening parents about the disorder, they feel an invisible pressure and realize the severity of the problem, although they are not aware of the length of time needed for treatment. Nonetheless, this is at least a good start. The family is beginning to accept it, and we can share some successful cases to let parents know that it is not incurable, but rather requires a relatively long time and enough patience. People are always a little afraid of the unknown, especially those with severe symptoms who may feel like leaving this world. Therefore, we should first adjust our own mindset. Parents recognizing the severity of the problem is a good start. We can then face and resolve the problem together with them, and also provide them with some treatment options. When necessary, we can have a psychological counseling session with parents, allowing them to experience it themselves. At the same time, we can also inform the counselor. I believe that with the company and support of family, we will definitely get better. The ringing in the ears may be caused by other factors. We can go to the hospital for an examination to determine the cause and then prescribe the appropriate treatment. The world loves you and so do I.

Hello, OP. I understand that when you were explaining your condition to your parents, you made it sound quite serious. On one hand, this caused your parents to pay attention and made you feel cared for, but on the other hand, you were also affected by their intense emotions, resulting in negative experiences such as nightmares and tinnitus. I am glad that you have been persisting in receiving psychological counseling and experiencing some improvement. It has been over a year since you last experienced tinnitus, but it reappeared after communicating with your parents, which has been distressing for you. Reflecting back, what happened during the period when the tinnitus improved and disappeared? Was it because your emotions and life situation were relatively stable? Perhaps there is some correlation with suddenly being immersed in these negative emotions again. Of course, it is also necessary to go to the hospital for some relevant examinations to rule out any organic lesions causing the tinnitus, but since you have had successful experiences in overcoming it before, there is no need to panic too much; have confidence in yourself. Furthermore, you need to consciously control yourself within a positive environment, avoid excessive exposure to negative emotions, and not deliberately create a negative atmosphere. You can try mindfulness meditation and running exercise to alleviate and release emotions. At the same time, since you have received your parents' attention, it is also important to reconcile with them and communicate with them calmly, expressing your true needs. In this situation, they will surely support and understand you. Best wishes.

question: Love has been on and off for three years, and although I love the other person very much, I feel exhausted and want to escape.
description: I really feel that if I'm not with this person, I'll be living alone, and I feel like I won't find anyone else who makes me feel the urge to get married (PS: we have been in love many times). He also said the same. I don't know if it's because of the long-distance relationship, but I feel like he can live without me. I have the desire to tell him about the big and small things in my life, but he doesn't. Sometimes when I chat with him, I feel like he's just appeasing me, and he seems to be happy living his own life, as if he doesn't need me. And I've always wanted to end the long-distance relationship, and I've been wanting to get married, but I know that my current life situation is not suitable. But I always have this feeling that even if everything in my life is financially and emotionally stable, he would still hesitate to get married. I want to stay overseas, but I don't know what his plans are. It's like I can't see the future, and on top of that, the longer we talk, it seems like I don't have to do anything special for him, and now I just feel so exhausted from talking. I always feel like running away. But when we're apart, I really miss him.

answers.answer_text: Dear questioner, hello. Getting married is a courageous decision. The longer the relationship, the less eager one may feel about getting married. Each person strives to adapt to their environment and ultimately live in the most comfortable way possible. Getting married inevitably brings about significant changes. The couple needs to decide on a consistent location for their life together and synchronize their lifestyles. This can be a challenging task for a couple who has been in a long-distance relationship. It is understandable that both of you may have doubts about marriage. As you mentioned, you feel that your current life situation is still satisfactory. If you choose to get married, you will need to end the long-distance aspect of your relationship. Either you will have to return to your home country, or he will have to come to your country. Is this an issue that can be reconciled? It seems that neither of you have fully considered or prepared for marriage. That's alright, don't rush to a conclusion. Can you carefully consider it? Marriage is something that should come naturally when two people who love each other want to establish a family; it is not something to force or settle for. There are some things that may not be decided upon now, but there will always be a day when a decision can be made. I hope you will carefully think about it. In many cases, maintaining the status quo is not due to love, but rather due to habit. Therefore, we must distinguish between love and habit. Differentiate between subjective choices, instead of passively giving up on making a choice. I wish you happiness.

Hello, really good entanglement? From the description of the question master, my feeling is that we are in a long-distance relationship, and I feel that he doesn't love me so much. The idea of getting married is our own, and breaking up seems like there won't be a person I want to marry. What should I do? I don't know if my feelings are correct or not. Whether they are correct or not, I want to say that there is seemingly no need to feel inferior in a relationship, and not only in relationships, but also in other aspects of life, you should have confidence. ■ Inferiority is the killer of love. Once you love someone and develop a sense of inferiority, you will break up sooner or later! Emotional advice: When you have a sense of inferiority in love, it is the most powerless time. Inferiority will not only affect your mood, but also your actions. If you can change your state of inferiority through your efforts, that's fine. If you feel inferior and can't see a way out, you will be crushed by your inferiority sooner or later. Faced with the love that you want to support but can't, you will unconsciously want to escape, to let go. Once you have a sense of inferiority in love, you will be tied up and unable to satisfy yourself no matter what you do, even if the other party says nothing, that sense of inferiority will not disappear. There is no way, if you insist on pursuing a love that you can't support, the ending can only be a tragedy. The sense of inferiority in love can only be digested by you, don't expect your lover to comfort you or consider you. It is even more wrong to be angry with your partner because of your own inferiority. It is your own incompetence, you don't have the ability to love her and yet you get angry at her, that is accelerating the death of love. If you feel too inferior, then give yourself a way out and stop clinging to a love that you can't support. You should know that when your condition cannot be improved in a short period of time, even if you cling to a love that you can't support, you will eventually break up because your change cannot keep up with the other person's pace and you will always live in inferiority. What I want to say is, "Love is not just about maintaining a romantic relationship, it needs to be managed with emotions, financial resources, and material resources. None of them can be lacking. If you feel inferior because you don't have the ability to support love, then you can only let go." ■ Live your own life, live brilliantly, love yourself well, and only then will the people who love you love you more.

Now he is the one who has the urge to get married for you. You have broken up and reconciled many times, and must have experienced a lot. What were the reasons for the on-and-off relationship? What are the similarities and differences? I don't know how long you have been in a long-distance relationship? I don't know how old you are now. It feels like he can live without you in his life, but you hope to be more involved in his life, to understand him and to be a part of it. Because of the distance, there aren't many ways for you to participate in and understand his life. The way you're used to is telling him about the big and small things in your life, but it seems like he's not used to this way. When you chat with him, sometimes you feel like he's just going through the motions, as if he can live happily without you. (When do you feel like he's just going through the motions? When do you feel like he can live happily without you? Have you expressed this to him?) And I've always wanted to end the long-distance relationship, and I've always wanted to push for marriage, but I know that my current life situation is not suitable. (I really want to be closer to him, but there are some reasons that prevent you. This makes you very conflicted) But I always have a feeling that even if everything is financially and situationally suitable right now, he would still hesitate about marriage. (It seems like it's about financial situation, but at the same time, you feel like it's not just about financial situation. It seems like you need him to express some determination and do some firm things, so that you can dare to take the plunge.) I want to stay overseas, but I don't know about his plans. (You feel like you can't figure out his thoughts, and you also feel unsure.) It's like I can't see the future, and on top of that, it seems like there's no need to put in effort in the relationship anymore. It feels exhausting to keep talking about it. I always feel like running away. But when we're apart, I really miss him. (It can be really tiring like this, wanting to get closer but not being able to, wanting to break up but not being willing to let go. It seems like the source of it all lies with him, but do you think there might be other reasons?)

From your description, it seems that your current emotional state is a bit tired, and you don't know if you can continue to get along in the future. There is doubt in your heart, and the long-distance factor also lacks a sense of security. You always feel that this relationship is not very suitable. We have known each other for three years and have plans to get married, but you also worry that he may not agree or still hesitate about the future. It can be seen that you still really like him, but you also have some worries about the future. It is suggested that you communicate with him about these issues and see what plans you both have for the future, whether to stay abroad or return to your home country. Both parties need to handle this issue well because long-distance relationships are most afraid of having different goals and differences in opinions. If this problem can be resolved, the probability of being together will increase. In addition, you can consider the issue of future life and goals, how to plan and what the future holds for both of you. Matters of the heart are complicated, involving not only emotional factors but also the realities of the situation, which need to be faced together. If both parties can handle the practical difficulties and have no major problems with a unanimous opinion, then the probability of being together in the future is very high. Relationships are not easy, and it will be difficult to be apart. If it is possible to be together, try to be together.

Hello there, reading your words, I sense a contradictory entanglement. On one hand, you have an urge for "marriage" with him, but on the other hand, you feel that he is "neglecting" you in terms of emotional life, making you feel insecure and unable to see a future. First, let me give you a warm hug (づ●─●)づ Based on my personal experience, your dissatisfaction with your boyfriend and the inevitable "contradiction" could be related to some subconscious "complex" or "shadow" concerning intimate relationships that has not been resolved. Moreover, when you say "both of us have had many relationships", and "the other party has said the same", it indicates that both you and him have encountered similar issues regarding intimate relationships. The fact that you two have come together suggests a high level of similarity in your "vibrational frequencies" and have therefore "resonated" with each other. So, before delving deeper into analyzing your problem, could you please tell me a bit about your and his upbringing? Of course, if it involves your personal privacy, I will respect your wishes!

Looks like you not only have a long-distance relationship, but it seems like it's an international one. Are you both in different cities abroad, or is one of you in a different country? Three years may seem long or short for a relationship. Your conflicting emotions suggest that you are uncertain and insecure about this kind of relationship. You can schedule a time to talk to him about your future and understand each other's thoughts, and find a mutually acceptable way forward.

After reading the OP’s confession, I deeply understand their current situation. I want to bring you warmth like the sun. Here is my analysis: 1. It is clear that you truly love him. You are a good girl. Just like in relationships, good people are always easily hurt. So in the end, they always end up being taken advantage of. Girls are the same way. You care too much about him, and when you care too much, he stops caring about you. 2. Long-distance relationships never have good outcomes. So it is correct that you want to end the long-distance situation. You have been through a lot, so you don't want to give up on this relationship easily. But in love, if you want to keep someone's heart, you need to have a strategy. 3. If you love him, you should torture him. You have to torture him to the point of suffering, and then he will love you with all his heart. How should you torture him? Improve your own charm, this is the best way to torture him. Make your life exciting, make friends, cultivate hobbies, work or study well, and make yourself more outstanding. These are all the best ways to torture him. Thank you for your question, may all the beauty in the world come to you as scheduled.

question: Marriage problems have been going on for a long time but I don't dare to get a divorce, what should I do?
description: I have encountered an issue in my marriage that I cannot repair after infidelity, and divorce may be imminent. The person involved is my husband. I believed that there was no hope left in our marriage before deciding to have an affair, but even after trying, we are unable to mend the deep-seated mistrust in our hearts. When it comes to actually getting a divorce, I am afraid of losing the current state of my life and fearful of going through with it. This back-and-forth is causing me a lot of discomfort. I hope to understand my feelings better and determine how I truly view marriage - whether I want to continue or leave - and what exactly I am afraid of.

answers.answer_text: If marriage is a form of protection, everything else is uncertain. No matter what kind of marriage, even a seemingly perfect match in the eyes of others, there will always be unsatisfactory aspects. It's just that marriage is sacred, and most people choose to compromise and separate only when they have no other choice. There is a world of difference between being led astray unintentionally and doing so intentionally. You said you came prepared, but now you hesitate, which indicates that you are uncertain about your own choices. There is a saying for scolding others that you must be familiar with: "Can't make up your mind?!" Indeed, many times we are unclear about our wants and needs. Like a fallen autumn leaf, helplessly unaware of where it is drifting; like a boat in the vast ocean, unable to see the shore... To address this uncertainty, we need to take on the responsibility. Taking on responsibility will allow us to drive carefully and choose our direction wisely. We cannot be impulsive like during the Singles' Day shopping spree, only to end up broke the next month. Regardless of the choice we make, it is only when we willingly accept it that we can avoid being lost. Wanting everything will lead to losing our way.

question: I am still a high school student, but I am completely overwhelmed by the current life.
description: I'm sorry to bother you. I am a 16-year-old boy in a boarding school. I feel like I am an unnecessary person in front of my classmates and relatives. I used to think I was lively, but as I grew up, I realized that it wasn't being lively, but being annoying and foolish. I have tried everything to make friends, pretending to be feminine, trying to make others laugh. When I took money to find these so-called "friends," they would accept me warmly, but when I had no money, they would say, "Get lost, idiot." I don't know why they do this. Now, I can no longer be brave. Despite being 6'3" tall, I am being bullied by people shorter than 5'7". Although I am still a student, I feel completely defeated by the current life. The rejection from classmates, the insults from teachers, the lack of understanding from my parents, what should I do? Sorry for the disturbance.
keywords: Growth, self-growth, stress management, student growth.

answers.answer_text: Hello! You are a polite and well-behaved child. From your description, I can see that you actively attribute things to yourself and try to do them positively, but it doesn't work, which makes you very frustrated. First of all, in order to please your friends, you have used the wrong methods, thinking that you can maintain relationships through money or demeaning yourself. In fact, you haven't figured out what genuine friendship is and how to maintain it. True friendship doesn't need to be maintained in this way. During your student stage, the friendship between you should be free from financial interests and more about the need for companionship. You are all consumers, and there is no need for economic transactions. You cannot rely on money to maintain it. If you demean yourself, it will only make your friends look down on you even more and distance themselves from you. What you can offer is genuine understanding and mutual care, progress together in studies, and help each other in life. Secondly, you are currently in adolescence, a period of transition from adolescence to adulthood, with rapid physical and psychological changes, which can leave many people at a loss. If not properly guided, it is easy to experience psychological problems, with feeling of not being understood being a key issue. Considering your current situation, if possible, it would be best to talk to your teacher or communicate with the school's counseling teacher. They can give you the most direct and effective advice. Finally, you need to re-examine yourself, try to introspect, and re-evaluate yourself, establishing correct self-awareness. Try to analyze your strengths and weaknesses, the roles you played in the things that happened, what you did well, and what needs improvement, etc. By introspecting for a few minutes every day, over time, you will feel growth. I hope the above suggestions can help you get rid of useless things and focus on studying. Being full of sunshine and confidence is what you should possess. Keep up the good work!＾０＾~!

question: My son needs counseling from a mental health teacher, but the teacher feels too tired from work and doesn't want to put in effort.
description: The company is organizing an event and wants employees to arrive early to the factory. However, my son doesn't want to go early and thinks he should arrive at the scheduled work time. When I talked to him about this, he got angry and said he would rather die than work here. He said if he can't make it, he would rather die. As a father, I am extremely worried and don't know how to deal with him. Whenever there is an argument with family members, he runs away from home.
keywords: Family, growth process, communication with children

answers.answer_text: How old is your son? How long has he been working? Since he's working, I assume he's an adult now. Why does he still need you, his father, to worry about him? Is it because you "think" he can't live his life well, or does he really need you to take care of him? Considering he's already working, he should have the ability to take care of himself. From what you've described, it seems like you're more anxious about your son not working than he is. It's as if it's your own problem. You're worrying for him and taking care of everything for him, so of course he doesn't need to "worry" anymore. "Rather die than work here, I'll live if I can, die if I can't." I wonder where your son's resentment comes from. Generally speaking, he chose his job and his life, they were his own choices. If they're not suitable, he can choose again, there's no need to threaten himself or others with death. Who is your son challenging with this behavior? Who took away his right and freedom to choose his job and life? I suggest you shift your focus from your son to yourself. Live your life well, be a role model for your son, and show him that dad is amazing. At the same time, give your son a chance to prove himself and show what he can do.

question: After giving birth, the temper becomes increasingly irritable, and there is also some sexual frigidity. What is the matter?
description: After having a baby, my temper has become increasingly irritable, and I also feel somewhat frigid. I find everything annoying and easily become angry.
keywords: Marriage, prenatal and postnatal, sexual life.

answers.answer_text: #After giving birth, my temper becomes more and more irritable, and I also feel somewhat frigid. Everything seems frustrating and I easily get angry. #The information provided is too little, so the following is only speculation. 1. You have needs that are not being met, and expressing them directly doesn't get others' attention. So, you express your needs by getting angry to let the people around you know that you need to be valued. 2. Feeling frigid indicates that your recent state of mind is not good, and your husband has almost not noticed your state and asked you about it. By being frigid, you are telling him that your relationship has deteriorated to the point where you don't even want to have sexual activity. The change in the family structure after giving birth can make many familiar aspects of life unfamiliar, making it difficult for new mothers to adjust. If at this time, the husband doesn't perceive and timely attend to the needs of the wife, and provide sufficient psychological support, the wife will resort to expressing herself in a terribly unfavorable state, indicating "I have needs, I need to communicate with you all." This is a way of engaging in a passive conversation. So, what situations at home after giving birth have made you feel so irritable? If you would like to talk about it, you can continue to leave a message.

As a woman who has had similar experiences, I will try to share my understanding: irritability comes from a sense of powerlessness towards reality. Having children makes life busier and more chaotic, with the responsibilities of work, family, and children. There are too many things that need to be done, and you as one person don't have enough strength or ability to handle it all. Secondly, there is a lack of fulfillment. Your husband, who is closest to you, may not provide the support and care you desire. Disappointment in these areas can lead to frustration. Therefore, a lack of interest in sex, as you mentioned, is a natural outcome. Women value love first, and then the desire for physical intimacy arises. So don't label yourself too easily. Just think about what has happened to you. Start by taking care of yourself and learn to delegate tasks that you are unable to handle yourself. After all, what is more important than yourself? If you want others to value you, you must start by valuing yourself and taking care of your physical and mental well-being. Secondly, from your attitude towards your husband, it is clear that you are dissatisfied with him. So what do you want him to do? Have you communicated your needs to him? How have you expressed them? Has he not listened to you? Why? Hu Shin Chi once said, "Any relationship is the result of collaboration by both parties." When you are irritable and dissatisfied with your relationship, think about what role you have played. Have you been maintaining or damaging the relationship? I just saw a saying: change begins with the person who wants to change! So you can't change your husband, you can only change yourself. Therefore, start with yourself, change what you can, and perhaps your husband will be influenced by your changes. In conclusion: learn self-care! Learn to express your needs! Learn to change yourself!

question: I am always afraid of other people being indifferent towards me. How can I become more confident?
description: I was a bit introverted when I was young, but it didn't affect my life. Later in fifth grade, I developed alopecia areata and lost all my hair, becoming an outcast in class. From then until junior high school graduation, I was constantly bullied in class. In high school, the classmates around me became more mature, and the situation improved a lot. However, there was still psychological bullying. I remember in my senior year, my best friend suddenly became cold towards me because he found out that I was trying to "quit masturbation" (I was confused at the time and deeply believed in the "quitting masturbation" theory I found online). Since then, I have been very concerned about what others think of me. I feel extremely frustrated when he treats me bad, and it feels like my brain is going to explode. Normally, I don't get angry with others because I'm afraid they will ignore me in the future, and I rarely refuse others' requests. I'm really distressed. How did I become like this? Now I'm in my sophomore year, and a few days ago, my next-door roommate suddenly became cold towards me, but in fact, he is still nice to me. But I always worry that he will ignore me and constantly seek confirmation. It's so tiring. I keep telling myself that I'm overthinking and need to be more confident, but it still feels uncomfortable. Is there something wrong with me psychologically? What should I do?
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-growth

answers.answer_text: Author, hello. First of all, your description reminds me of the famous "Scar Experiment" in psychology. It tells the story of psychologists inviting makeup artists to draw blood and scars on the faces of 10 participants, and then letting them look in the mirror, remembering their terrifying appearance. Then, they took the mirrors away and told the participants that the makeup artists would add some powder to make the scars look more realistic and last longer. In reality, the makeup artists quietly wiped off the scars and bloodstains drawn on their faces with cotton swabs. Afterwards, the participants were taken to the hospital and dressed up as patients, pretending to wait for their turn, to observe and experience people's reactions. After the experiment, the participants described their feelings, and surprisingly, they all agreed that others showed disgust and lacked kindness towards their scarred selves, and their eyes were constantly fixed on their scars. Did you notice? It turns out that people's perceptions about themselves can profoundly affect and change their perceptions of the outside world. Sometimes, because of the "scar in their hearts", they perceive others in a completely different way than before. So, is it possible that for you, the "scars" from fifth grade have been retained all this time, making you extremely sensitive to people's reactions and labeling certain unintentional words and actions from others as "indifference," which are then repeatedly "confirmed" in your interactions, and then you truly face a "cold" world? As for what to do, you can try to keep some distance from the feeling of being "rejected and ignored," and become aware that others' reactions and the meanings they convey may differ from what you think. Awareness is paramount; once you have awareness, there is room to do something different and bring about change.

question: 31 years old, without money, how to continue a love that cannot progress?
description: Me and my partner are both 31, and we are considered as young adults in our thirties. I've only known him for less than a year, and we met online. I chose him because I believe he is kind, responsible, ambitious, and upright. We have been together for about ten months now, and there have been many difficulties. First, his family is very poor, with three brothers, and they are from a remote area in Northwest China. They rely solely on themselves for support, as his parents have no money. He managed to buy a house on his own, but the mortgage and credit loans amount to nearly 20,000 RMB per month, and I have to support him, which has significantly affected my quality of life. Not only do I have to contribute to the mortgage every month, but I also have to support him financially. However, I have never criticized him for that, and my parents have not mentioned the issue of dowry either, which could be waived if necessary, as we both don't want to hurt his self-esteem. Second, he lied about his educational background. Initially, he told me he was a graduate student, but later revealed that he wasn't. When I asked for proof of his education, he absolutely refused to show me any, and he continued to brush it off. I am very angry because I feel deceived by him. I have a master's degree from a prestigious university in China, so I initially had certain requirements regarding education. I hoped my partner would at least have a bachelor's degree, if not a master's. Third, we have had some small conflicts during the adjustment period, and I feel that we are not on the same wavelength. I can't bear to break up with him.

answers.answer_text: Hello, questioner. Love is ideal, marriage is reality. Both of you are already over 30, and it can also be said that your relationship is aimed at marriage. Marriage and family are things that everyone needs to face. Whether the marriage is happy, the family is stable, including whether the children will have a healthy and happy living environment in the future, and whether the parents will have a relatively happy old age, these are all issues that we need to consider. Marriage is like a woman's rebirth, don't you already have the answer in your heart? [He is kind, responsible, and ambitious, and a person of integrity.] He is seen as a potential stock by many parents. This kind of boyfriend can be said to be one in a hundred, but for marriage, these conditions alone are not enough. The foundation of marriage should be love. Although everyone has different understandings and pursuits of love, some people pursue pure and irrational passionate love, and some people pursue rational and long-lasting love. However, once we enter the realm of daily life, we have to consider very practical issues. Even if we know that two people who are similar in every way, even if they are twins, will still have differences, so we need to seek common ground while reserving differences. But if we find that two people have major differences in values and outlook on life, then we must take it seriously and not compromise. After all, once we add other social relationships, it is difficult to "detach ourselves." You have listed three difficulties. The first and second difficulties may be the reason why he deceived you (which can be understood). If we return to reality, the two of you are not a good match. [He—has three brothers, comes from the northwest, and his family is very poor, so he can only rely on himself; You—come from a relatively good family, and you can feel it from the fact that your parents don't mention dowry money.] He- bought the house by himself (which deserves praise), and the monthly mortgage and credit loans amount to nearly 20,000 yuan (the credit loan should not exceed three years, I don't know how much the mortgage is). You-have to pay the mortgage together with him and still support his livelihood, which seriously affects your quality of life. (In other words, his income is not enough to pay the mortgage. If the house was purchased before the relationship was confirmed, and there were no special circumstances in between, it is indeed a bit unrealistic. This is also a slight flaw in his personality. If it was purchased after the relationship was confirmed, then you really need to assess yourself). Although marriage is not purely materialistic, our attitude towards money also reflects our attitude towards things. [Not a soulmate]- just because of this, you have to be careful about whether to enter marriage in this relationship. Because rational love is a process of choice, seeking common ground while reserving differences, and discovering major differences that cannot be compromised. We will find that many couples, after discovering differences, feel that they have had a long time of relationship, have feelings, are reluctant to let go, or can't bear the other party's sincere pursuit, or because of external pressure, etc., often tend to cover up differences emotionally, and even try to maintain the relationship by getting married quickly. It will be difficult to repair the relationship if it encounters a crisis in the future. Girl, since you have your own ideas, why not communicate openly with your boyfriend, regardless of whether you choose to get married or not, these issues need to be discussed. The union of two people is also the union of two families. Before marriage, the relationship between the two parties is limited to emotions, but after marriage, not only do you have to deal with various practical problems, but it will also increase many social relationships, and it is more likely to cause family conflicts. A person's age can be divided into: social age, mental age, and genetic age. The country requires women to register for marriage no earlier than 20 years of age in terms of social age. Therefore, at 31 years old, if you think getting married is early, then you are not considered a late bloomer. If you think it's time to get married, then it's not too late. So, here are a few suggestions: ① Reflect on yourself and find out what you really want in this relationship. What are your future plans? ② Communicate with your boyfriend about your true feelings, including the series of feelings he has given you, but do not be emotional, see if your boyfriend can calmly understand you. ③ In matters of marriage, understand the attitudes of each other's parents towards your relationship. Life is short, I think you have your own pursuits, so it's not a bad idea to first focus on your inner self and feel your own feelings. No matter what choice you make, it is still a choice. No matter what kind of choice you make, it is the best choice you subconsciously believe is best for yourself. Best of luck to you.

Based on your description, I feel like you are considering him as a potential marriage partner and have plans to get married. However, his financial situation and other practical factors don't meet your requirements, so you feel torn and uncertain about whether to continue with him or not, right? His family's conditions are poor, and he relies on his own hard work, but he also has to bear a large mortgage. In order to support him, you've decided to share the burden of the mortgage, but it has caused a decline in your quality of life. It's not easy for him to be able to buy a house through his own efforts in such a difficult family situation, which indicates a certain level of capability. If he is ambitious, willing to continue striving and has a promising career, then I believe the current difficulties and pressures are only temporary, and the future will bring improvements in your life. So it depends on how well you know and understand him, and whether you're willing to give him some time and persevere through this tough period. However, I need to remind you that from the perspective of protecting your own rights, you haven't officially registered for marriage yet, but you're sharing the burden of the mortgage. If in the future you don't get married and instead break up, the house belongs to him, and the mortgage payments you made won't be returned to you, causing you certain financial losses. If you're willing to make these sacrifices without expecting anything in return, then there won't be a problem. It seems you're kind and gentle, caring for him, but the fact that you're here questioning this issue shows that your quality of life has been affected. You're even hesitant to directly address issues involving money, such as the bride price, which indicates that you do have concerns about this aspect, and also reflects his sensitivity and inferiority complex when it comes to money, which has had an impact on your relationship. This is a very realistic problem. His mindset is a result of long-term accumulation influenced by his upbringing, and it's difficult to change overnight, so you need to face and acknowledge this. When two people come together to build a family and live together, in addition to sharing the same life values and outlook, money attitudes are also important. How both sides view and plan for wealth, and whether there are any differences, will all impact family life and marital relationships, so it's something that needs to be understood and prepared for in advance. Regarding his current state and the impact on you, you need to be mentally prepared. If you're willing to accept the situation, it may continue for a while. As for the issue of education, his deception may stem from various psychological reasons. It's possible that he feels inferior compared to you in terms of education, or he wants to develop a good love relationship with you and knows that your expectations are high, so he decided to keep it a secret. If it's not done out of ill intentions, I think his behavior can still be understood. After all, educational background doesn't completely represent a person's character, abilities, and future prospects; it requires a comprehensive evaluation. As for the small conflicts that arise during your adjustment period, in love, conflicts and friction are common. Two people rarely have a perfect fit right from the start; they need to go through an adjustment process, seeking common ground while respecting differences, and having a mindset of tolerance, understanding, and trust. The most crucial aspect is whether both of you can reach a consensus on values, have shared life goals, and are willing to strive for them. 
You mentioned that you feel like you're not deeply connected on an emotional level, but I'm not sure what exactly you mean by that. Could there be misunderstandings due to communication issues? You can try to engage in more sincere communication to clear up any misunderstandings. Marriage is a major decision in life and requires careful consideration. Love and marriage are like shoes, only you know whether they fit or not. You need to think and weigh it for yourself; others can only offer advice from different perspectives and cannot make the decision for you. If you already have an answer in your heart, then you don't need anyone else's support, and you can make a decision that suits you. Best wishes!

Education is a common concern for many people. You are doing well, and your family doesn't care about your background. Having a master's degree is intimidating for many people. If someone tells you about their education during the first conversation, you might just pass them by. Underneath the lies lies self-esteem, a reluctance to give up, and a fear of loss. The gap cannot be filled, but they want to be closer to you and worry about what others might say. If everything else is compatible, education, background, appearance, and so on, are not issues. However, facing difficulties together may be more challenging.

question: Finally in the industry that I like, but I always hesitate to speak and lack confidence.
description: I previously worked in a paid position doing odd jobs. I used my spare time to review and finally passed the professional title examination to work in a pharmacy. However, I always feel inferior to others and hesitate to speak up. I feel anxious and lacking in confidence because I have never done this before. I'm not afraid of hard work, but I suffer from various kinds of apprehension.

answers.answer_text: I don't know if your job requires you to talk a lot. If not, then simply focus on doing your job well and accumulating relevant experience. Many successful people are not particularly talkative. Each personality has its own strengths and suitable jobs. However, if you believe that "speaking up" is an important aspect of life, then you should exercise your proactive expression and cultivate the ability to speak up. Don't mind success or failure, persistently take small steps and gradually become more natural at it. Actually, often the qualities that people admire are usually hidden aspects of their own potential personality, which may have been concealed due to certain childhood experiences or upbringing. However, through self-breakthroughs, they can also be freed.

Hello, OP, congratulations on passing the big pharmacy exam through your own efforts and persistence. You should be happy and proud, and you should have confidence because your hard work has paid off. It is evident that you are a person who can endure hardship, as you mentioned that you are not afraid of being tired. There is no need to be timid all the time, because everyone is the same. You are not inferior to anyone else, you have to believe that you are the best. Believe that your efforts will definitely be rewarded. Best wishes~.

Seeking external attention, even if the goal is achieved, will still feel empty. If you truly believe it is important, you can experience it first. A better approach is to explore your talents and strengths to see what suits you best and immerse yourself in things you enjoy. This will bring you fulfillment, happiness, and enjoyment. Compared to experiencing this, the joy of being noticed usually feels much less significant. Of course, if you have that unresolved longing, it may be worth pursuing attention until you become tired of it.

question: I don't want to live in the dormitory in high school. I'm afraid of feeling helpless and not being able to separate myself from the outside world without my phone.
description: Since junior high school, I have been very afraid of going to school. Whenever I am at school or think about going to school, I feel uncomfortable. I miss home a lot when I am at school, and when I return home, I feel unhappy and uncomfortable too. I don't want to speak, I just want to cry. I feel unsafe, mentally drained, heavy-hearted, and depressed. Everything feels dark, and I don't know how to describe that feeling. I really want to die and can't go on living. I feel uncomfortable in my heart every day, except for a few moments when I suddenly feel a little better for a few minutes, and then the discomfort returns.
keywords: Emotions, depressive emotions, anxious emotions, emotion regulation.

answers.answer_text: The pace of growth cannot be stopped, and your problem lies in your strong dependence. You need to take the initiative to take an independent step. From the perspective of someone like me, being a boarding student is probably the happiest thing. You don't have to face constant nagging at home, nor do you have to deal with the trivialities of life. You can focus on studying, writing, and doing things you want to do at school. Having a cellphone is just for gaming and such, and it is not very useful. But everyone needs to step out of their comfort zone, and I am no exception. The pace of growth cannot be stopped.

The poster may have started their boarding school life early. Perhaps they were initially reluctant, but their parents might have wanted them to focus on their studies, their own busy work schedules, or to encourage their independence. In this situation, we were not mentally prepared and left home early. Or we may have tried to voice our thoughts but were dismissed by our parents, resulting in less communication over time. We encounter difficulties and problems that we cannot solve ourselves, and we are unable to release and express ourselves timely, which leads to excessive psychological pressure. We develop a resistance towards school, and when we return home, we do not know how to express ourselves. In this new environment, we are always used to wrapping ourselves up.

question: A second-year middle school student, his mother at home is very strict about his studies, would she beat him up if he doesn't listen?
description: My mother is very strict. I want to learn music, painting, and playing games, but she doesn't allow me to do so. Moreover, my mother feels that I am hopeless and not focused on my studies. She checks my phone records and phone bills every day, and doesn't let me call or message anyone. She even hits me when she closes the door. What should I do?
keywords: Family, communication with parents, family control.

answers.answer_text: On the day I received the college acceptance letter, I told my dad that I really don't like going to school. I've been studying for so long, and now I have to continue. My dad said it's because I'm not brave enough. If I give up and stop studying, no one can force me. After all, I am my own person and it's up to me how I live in the future. I guess it's true. I always worry that learning dance will cost a lot of money. What if my dad doesn't provide it? I would have to work outside and be tired every day. Will I still have time to practice dance? Can I persevere? I think about a lot of things and end up procrastinating. Then I went to college, and it's not as good as before to learn dance. If you have figured out the problems you will face, make a decision early. Or take advantage of the long summer vacation to go out and gain some experience. You will consider it more thoroughly.

I am much older than you and have also experienced such situations. Now I'm telling you, this is not good. It's easy to develop low self-esteem as you grow up. It's easy to have interpersonal problems. Baby, that's what I call you. Don't mind it. You can try talking to your mom, but with her strong personality, there may need to be some prerequisites, such as how many points you can get in a certain subject or how many places you can move up in ranking. Of course, if you are afraid to speak up, you can find someone you are not afraid of to persuade your mom and discuss conditions. Baby, your mom loves you, maybe her way is not right. But her love for you is genuine, so you can try negotiating. Besides, students are in the learning stage, so they should still focus on studying. If your grades are not very good, you can try focusing on improving one subject, take it slow and gradually improve. Actually, after you start working, you will find that having a certain skill is quite important. If you don't have a degree by then, finding a job and surviving will be difficult. So young one, keep up the good work!

question: Why do male teachers get nervous and blush when they come near themselves?
description: My male teacher is my geography teacher for this semester. He looks good and is gentle. He doesn't scold or treat people harshly. He is a typical kind-hearted man. On the first day when the teacher came to class, I felt scared. But slowly, I found that he is not strict at all and very gentle. I started to develop a little bit of liking towards this teacher. He is very active in class, and I really like this kind of teacher. At the beginning, the teacher didn't notice my presence. I didn't feel nervous at all during class. Then, in one class, the teacher noticed me. Since then, I was almost always called upon to answer questions in class. I didn't think much of it, but one time, when the teacher called me to answer a question, I was in a bad mood and got angry. The teacher thought I was unwilling to answer the question. After that, the teacher never called on me to answer questions again. But every time the teacher comes close to me, I get nervous and my face turns red. What's wrong with me?
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, guilt and shame.

answers.answer_text: Excuse me, are you a boy or a girl? How old are you? Why is there no punctuation throughout the text? Did you feel nervous and a little shy while writing this paragraph? It is normal for us to find someone or a certain type of person attractive because certain qualities of that person may attract us and make us feel that they are wonderful or remind us of someone who was once wonderful. In this text, sometimes you hope that your teacher can understand your needs and emotions. This situation may be achievable when you are very young with your family, but as you grow older, it may be difficult for the people around you to provide the same care and understanding as your family. Therefore, your internal thoughts need to be known and expressed by the other party. No matter what kind of emotions you experience, please remember to respect the other person and protect yourself. Interactions between people require time to understand, and involve many aspects. You can also try to further explore them. Emotions have no right or wrong, but actions should have limits. Mutual respect is important. Take good care of the person who brings you positive feelings, but more importantly, take good care of yourself because no matter what, you are the most precious. Best wishes~

question: I feel like I'm really bad at speaking and I'm afraid of being disliked by others. How can I change this?
description: 16-year-old girl, my parents have always been saying that I speak without thinking, especially silly, saying whatever comes to mind. But I just can't develop the habit of thinking things over. My friends also say that I don't know how to control myself, and I'm really afraid of being disliked by others. How can I change? Thank you.
keywords: Growth, personality development, character traits, self-acceptance

answers.answer_text: Hello classmate, based on your description, I feel like you are a very straightforward person. Actually, straightforward people can be quite adorable sometimes. However, if our words hurt others, it may be necessary to make some appropriate changes. When expressing our opinions to others, it is best to consider their feelings. If you want to give praise, you can say it directly, but when it comes to criticism and reproach, it's better to use a more tactful approach. Especially when dealing with important people in our lives, we may unconsciously speak without reservation because we know deep down that they won't leave. However, constantly pointing out the other person's flaws can actually push them further away. We say that relationships require us to put in effort to maintain them. I suggest that before expressing our feelings and opinions, we take a few seconds to think and consider whether the way we say it will make the other person unhappy, and if there might be another way to express ourselves. Before going to bed each day, we can also reflect on whether we have been too straightforward, and try to think from the other person's perspective - how would we feel if we heard those words ourselves? When someone directly points out that our words have hurt them, we can appropriately apologize or explain any misunderstandings. Sometimes, it may be our own incorrect way of expressing ourselves that causes others to misunderstand us.

question: How to get rid of the influence brought by the original family and change this character to reshape oneself?
description: In 97, my three older sisters, on average, are 10 years older than me. My parents are in their 60s and there is a significant generation gap when communicating with them. My sisters are much older than me, and we don't have much in common, resulting in very little communication with my family. We only contact each other over the phone when necessary, and there is no sense of intimacy. My parents' approach to my upbringing has been criticism and punishment, with no mention of praise when deserved, fearing that I would become conceited. Pointing out my mistakes is for my own good, I know, but it has led to deep-seated insecurities in my personality. I am afraid and unable to love someone, and I struggle to maintain long-term intimate relationships. I am afraid of getting close to people, my personality tends to be extreme, and I rarely communicate with my father because his emotional intelligence is really low, and talking to him always leads to arguments and frustration. Overall, I rarely call my family unless it's necessary. Materially, I am willing to give everything for them, but emotional communication is truly a challenge. Spending too much time at home can induce social anxiety. As an adult, I became fascinated with psychology and philosophy and discovered that my personality and mental state are actually unhealthy. It's like being trapped within a wall and I long to break free, but I feel powerless to do so. I often find myself trapped in feelings of anxiety and depression. I once told my family that I might have depression, but they don't believe it, and everything is always my fault, I'm not good enough... I don't know how to undergo a rebirth, to completely change and transform all of this.
keywords: Family, family relationships, parental communication, growth process

answers.answer_text: China's parents are the best parents in the world, but also the worst parents. They can give us everything they have, but in terms of thoughts, they often neglect us. It is so difficult to hear a word of recognition from our parents. I can understand the feelings of the OP because I grew up in the same way. Due to a lack of communication and guidance from parents, when faced with problems, we have to bear them alone because seeking help is meaningless. Our parents won't come to help, and they might even bring us setbacks. So we always solve problems on our own, which leads to a lack of desire for other interpersonal relationships because we don't believe that they will like or help us. Moreover, due to a lack of communication, it is difficult to approach problems from multiple perspectives, and our ability to solve problems will be limited. So how can we break through? I think it is to interact more with people. Walking in society, you will find that no matter what kind of person someone is, there will be people who like them and people who don't. Kind people may be seen as foolish, while troublemakers may be seen as cool. Interacting with more people and finding those who appreciate you, their attitude and behavior towards you will make you feel that you are worthy of love. Then, internalize it as your own self-evaluation, and your confidence will gradually build up. But everything has two sides. The wrong person will only intensify your anxiety and inferiority.
