It is crucial to provide limited re-nurturing and guidance to overcome abandonment and deprivation. A counselor can act as a stable and affirming role, helping you internalize your shining aspects, regain confidence, and teach you how to deal with relationships and choose the right people. Of course, you can also handle these things on your own. You can take a look at the book "Attachment Therapy," it might be helpful for you.

question: I lack confidence in my intelligence and always avoid thinking. What should I do?
description: It is possible that I was previously criticized for being stupid, and I am very worried about my intelligence. Every time I try to think, I always avoid it. I feel annoyed every time, and I lose my enthusiasm for thinking. Whenever I encounter unfamiliar knowledge, I tend to memorize it blindly. Even if I feel like I have figured it out, I still have a strange feeling of uncertainty. Even if the answer is correct, I still feel something is odd. I feel like I have been avoiding it all the time, and my intellect has decreased. What should I do?
keywords: Growth, character refinement, self-acceptance, and student development.

answers.answer_text: You may not be good at logical thinking, and that's okay. Everyone has different intellectual structures, and you may have talents in other areas such as memory, perception, aesthetics, sense of rhythm, etc., which are all normal. Look for and develop your strengths, you don't have to limit yourself to comparing with others in areas where you have fewer talents. Thinking ability is just one of the many abilities of humans, and it is not necessary for everyone to possess it, nor is it a standard for judging whether a person is intelligent or not. Increasing reading can also be beneficial to a person.

question: I have sexual relations with my father and do not know what to do?
description: In the past few months, I have been having sexual relations with my father and it has continued until now. I don't know what to do.

answers.answer_text: Hello, OP~ I don't know how old you are this year. Are you already an adult? You and your father have the closest blood relationship, and engaging in a sexual relationship is inappropriate behavior. If you are still underage, I suggest you explain your situation to your mother and try to move away from your father, or ask your father to move out of the family. From a legal perspective, if your father forces you to engage in a sexual relationship before you reach adulthood, it is not only a violation of morals but also against the law. You can use legal means to protect yourself. However, you are the biggest victim in this matter, and you still have your own life to live. The best thing to do is to break away from this unhealthy relationship as soon as possible, for the sake of yourself and your family. Don't be ashamed to speak up, you must tell your mother. In your family, she is now the only person who can protect you! Best wishes!

question: I have a same-sex friend, and during our conversation, she said she has no interest in men.
description: I know a married female friend. I am a woman with short hair and a slightly masculine vibe. I don't know how we hit it off, but we eventually became good friends. We have known each other for almost two years. During a conversation, she mentioned that she is not interested in men. I don't know if it's true or not, but when I asked her about her sexual orientation via text, she avoided answering. I really don't understand. Sometimes, when I playfully scare her, she tells me to go away, but other times she will say things like "you should die" during our conversations. Sometimes I feel like she might have feelings for me, but other times I think she is genuinely happy with men. If I don't contact her for two days, she will reach out to me. Once, as a joke, I said that there is a guy who likes her, and she responded by saying that she is not interested in him. I then asked her who she is interested in, and I felt like she was a bit embarrassed. Could it be that I am the one she is interested in? I am really curious because it's rare to meet someone in real life who is like you, but she never speaks openly about it. Maybe she is just reserved. She is very beautiful.

answers.answer_text: Title owner, hello. I apologize that I cannot answer whether your friend is of the same sex or not. I believe your main concern is whether she likes you or not. I don't know if your friend likes you, but I suspect you might have feelings for her. Whether it's a same-sex or opposite-sex attraction, being good friends shows that there is some level of liking between you. It could be just a friendly liking, or it could be the "attraction between both sexes" as you mentioned. However, please note that your friend is a married woman. Regardless of same-sex or opposite-sex love, it is important for it to be based on a stable relationship between two people. Setting aside other factors, although society's acceptance of homosexuality has indeed improved, overall, a person revealing themselves as homosexual still carries some concerns. When you asked about your friend's sexual orientation, whether the answer is yes or no, avoiding the topic can help avoid risks and make one feel safe. You have been trying to find out if your friend is of the same sex, but you have never gotten an answer. "It is hard to meet someone in the real world who is the same as you." Have you told your friend about your sexual orientation? If not, what is the reason? Perhaps if you think about it, you will understand why your friend hasn't told you. Best wishes.

It is difficult to determine from her words whether she has homosexual thoughts or if she likes you. She says she has no interest in men, but a major reason could be that the man she is interested in has not appeared yet, or she is not ready to enter into a new relationship. When we don't understand anything but realize that there are fundamental differences between the sexes, on the one hand, there is an unstoppable curiosity and exploration, while on the other hand, there is intentional alienation, exclusion, and differentiation, and a preference for same-sex companionship to seek a sense of gender belonging. At this time, an intimate feeling with same-sex friends arises because there are more "secrets of growth" to share and communicate. So, there are endless whispered conversations when you are together. This can be understood. Based on the above understanding, she just wants someone to talk to and does not have any other intentions. Perhaps she is showing some dependence on you, but same-sex dependency is essentially about a sense of gender belonging, emotional reliance, and even worship of gender. It does not involve the physical aspect. Adolescence is a process of moving from confusion to order in terms of sexual orientation, accepting one's gender role with joy, and properly knowing oneself while finding the most suitable position in interpersonal relationships. Same-sex dependence is just a very normal phenomenon in this process full of doubts, novelty, and ups and downs. So, don't overthink it, isn't it great to have someone you can talk to?

Analysis from Tan Yang:1 "During a conversation, she mentioned that she has no interest in men." In this world, besides men, there are also women. If she has no interest in men, then naturally she must be interested in women. This is a matter of privacy, why would she tell you? Either she wants to confide in you, seeking support, understanding, or to share her pain and confusion. However, if she doesn't have a girlfriend, then what is the purpose of this statement? What do you think? 2 "Sometimes I feel like she likes me, but other times I feel like she is happy with men." A woman's sixth sense is often accurate. However, besides homosexuality and heterosexuality, there is also a category called bisexuality. There might even be more people in this category than homosexuals. 3 "Could it be that I am her type?" Regardless of whether you realize that you are open to homosexuality, your words and actions reveal that you have feelings for her. You like her, but you don't know if she would accept you. Homosexual relationships are more complicated than those of heterosexuals. Additionally, she already has a family, so her thoughts are contradictory and complex. It is not something that can easily be decided upon to establish such a relationship with you and officially date. Thank you for your question, may the beauty of the world come to you as expected.

question: I am 27 years old, extremely low self-esteem, often thinking about death, unable to sleep at night and crying all the time.
description: All my friends around me are getting married, and my relatives are also urging me. However, I feel extremely insecure and fearful of dating and marriage. But I don't want to worry my parents. I stay up very late every night, and sometimes even contemplate suicide. I become extremely sensitive and take even the slightest little thing personally, and then I start crying. My mood is extremely low.
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, anxiety, emotional regulation.

answers.answer_text: Dear friend, hello! I can see that you are feeling anxious, and I understand why. Besides not being married yet, what else makes you feel inferior? Take some time to really get to know and understand yourself. Recognize the compliments from your friends, appreciate the care from your family, and relish in the joy of past successes. If you think about these things, you will realize that you are someone worthy of love and are capable of loving others. It is your own belief that you are inadequate and insecure that prevents you from making more effort and being proactive in relationships. It stops you from pursuing someone you really like, and it also prevents those who have feelings for you from getting closer to you. Dear friend, if you are unable to resolve these feelings of insecurity and thoughts of suicide, I suggest seeking professional psychological help. Believe in yourself, and you will find that you are capable.

question: In my freshman year, I feel like I am very plain and unsophisticated. How can I truly become confident from the inside out?
description: I am a freshman student, and my family condition is pretty good. My life is harmonious and relatively happy. My grades are also acceptable, but not outstanding. The aspect I am most unsatisfied with is my appearance and fashion sense. I feel like I look plain and unfashionable. When I encounter people who are exceptional or attractive, I feel inferior. However, I am not the type who outwardly appears timid and hesitant to speak. I just constantly belittle myself in my own mind. My friends always tell me that confident girls are the most beautiful, but I don't know how to truly be confident from the inside out, and this causes me distress.

answers.answer_text: Hello there! From your description, I can sense that you care a lot about your appearance and clothing, and that it has been bothering you. Sending you a hug. It is common for people to have a desire to look beautiful, so this is not your fault. We all want to better ourselves, and this is a common psychological trait. As a student, it is important to dress appropriately within your means and not compare yourself to others. Within your financial capabilities, you can dress up appropriately. As the saying goes, "a well-read person has an air of elegance". I believe you are aware of this. So, first and foremost, start from within. Having a good personality and working on improving yourself inside and out is necessary. Therefore, start by studying more. This can be in many aspects, such as learning from watching TV shows and movies, observing the mannerisms of sophisticated individuals. On the other hand, read more books, especially those with depth, and spend time contemplating to deepen your understanding of various topics. You can also browse online shopping platforms or read fashion magazines to improve your taste. Enhancing your perspective will help address this issue. Secondly, the simplest way is to find someone with good taste and fashion sense to accompany you when buying clothes and help you with styling. Regarding makeup, it is not necessary to know everything. Simply apply a little BB cream and learn how to do your eyebrows. Adding a touch of lipstick when going out is enough. Next, focus on your outward appearance, starting with your hairstyle. Keep it fresh and clean, avoiding those overly exaggerated colors. As for clothing, it doesn't have to be expensive, but it should be simple, elegant, and clean. You can visit clothing stores, try on different outfits, but you don't necessarily have to buy them. Remember, it's not about being expensive, just find what suits you. Surround yourself with fashionable girls, the more you observe, the more you will naturally change any bad habits. Take regular showers, change clothes, and keep things clean and tidy. Over time, you will gradually become elegant and refined. Work on improving those aspects of your personality that need change. Show care and consideration towards others, and you will become beautiful because of your loveliness. Keep up the good work! The most important thing is to cultivate your inner character. Some people may have a good appearance, but still give off the impression of being unsophisticated, simply because they lack inner cultivation. A person with inner cultivation will possess an external temperament and an extraordinary image. Improving oneself internally means refining one's own cultivation. This refers to enhancing one's temperament through culture, reading more books, improving cultural literacy, and presenting oneself as extraordinary in interactions and behavior. Additionally, maintaining a positive mindset is essential. In modern society, where material possessions are relatively abundant, many people's desires tend to expand, and the tendency to compare oneself with others is strong. However, if one is not easily satisfied, it is difficult to maintain a positive mindset. A person with a negative mindset who constantly complains about the unfairness of the world and the darkness of society, with a face full of resentment, will certainly come across as unsophisticated. It is challenging for someone with a negative mindset to have a good appearance and demeanor, so a positive mindset is also a treasure for enhancing one's own temperament. It is common for people to desire beauty, as everyone wants to improve themselves. Of course, pursuing a westernized aesthetic excessively and always striving for a westernized appearance might make people think that you are trying too hard and come across as unsophisticated.

Hug the post author 🤗~ After reading the post author's description, I would like to give them a thumbs up! Overall, the post author already has a preliminary understanding and sorting out of their confusion and finally raised the question of "how to achieve true self-confidence from the inside out". Below, I will provide some suggestions in the hope of helping the post author. Firstly, if you want to achieve self-confidence from the inside out, the first thing you need to do is to accept your current self. No matter how plain or unsatisfactory you think you are, it cannot be denied that this is who you are now. And there is nothing wrong or bad about this version of yourself, and from your description, your past life seems to have been quite good. So when you encounter someone who is outstanding or good-looking, you can appreciate their excellence and beauty, but there is no need to belittle yourself because your life was also happy before meeting them. And the appearance of these people is just providing some possibilities for you to become even better and more outstanding. Secondly, take some time to think about what is considered excellent or good-looking in your eyes. What kind of outfit can immediately attract your attention and make you want to take another look? What kind of person do you sincerely think is outstanding? When you encounter those who are outstanding or good-looking, you might as well think about these questions. There must be certain qualities in them that move you, and by grasping these qualities, you will find your future goals and direction. Thirdly, taking the first step is always difficult, although the idea is perfect. When you realize what you truly appreciate about them, you can do your best to find ways to achieve it. For example, in terms of dressing, you can go on Xiaohongshu or Weibo to watch videos or articles about fashion bloggers, find the type that you like, and watch more of that type of dressing, and then start to change your own style. Finally, I want to tell the post author that self-confidence from the inside out is based on affirming and accepting oneself. When a person fully accepts and appreciates themselves, they will have self-confidence from the inside out. I hope that my answer can help you~.

Dear op, hello~ I'm happy to see your post and that you're only in your freshman year. You have plenty of time and energy to study and enrich yourself. I understand your feelings very well. Even though your own conditions are not bad, you can't help but feel inferior in the presence of outstanding or attractive people. However, it doesn't affect your normal social interactions, and you tend to belittle yourself psychologically. It seems that in front of them, our confidence disappears and every move we make seems to be within their predictable reactions. We can try changing our mindset when interacting with them, approaching it more like a learning experience. If there are things to learn from them, we can make improvements; if not, we should strive to better ourselves. Perhaps this will work better, and we will also realize that they are not perfect in daily interactions. "My family conditions are decent, and my life is harmonious and relatively happy. My grades are also good, but not exceptionally outstanding." Look, these are your strengths, or rather, what sets you apart from others. Moreover, you have a happy and beautiful family. Everyone is born different, with their own strengths and weaknesses. It's just that when we're in a state of inferiority, our strengths are diminished while our weaknesses are magnified until we can't breathe. This forms a vicious cycle, and if we don't adjust in time, we will start to deny ourselves in more aspects. So, try affirming the differences between yourself and others, and recognize the happiness you have. Boldly acknowledge the excellence in others and approach them with an equal heart. The reason we lack confidence in front of outstanding individuals is because, subconsciously, we fear authority. To overcome this fear, one way is to establish a proximal psychological defense mechanism, which means nurturing your inner self and enhancing your sense of self-worth, to build a strong mental will. You need to have an independent, complete cognitive and value system about things, reaching almost a level of belief. Imagine that a Buddhist or a Christian would at least not feel authority fear towards secular objects because they already have their own beliefs. Second, you need to establish a long-distance psychological defense mechanism, read more books, and arm yourself with cultural symbols. These two points are actually extremely important in your current learning process. Dear op, you describe your clothing style as "rustic and plain." I used to be troubled by this issue too, but I later found that clothes can actually reflect your current state of mind. If you don't know which style suits you best, it may also be a reflection of inner confusion. Try doing things you like or inclined to like, find your own identity, and perhaps you will naturally know how to dress. Simply put, "imitate" and look for dressing styles that you really like, and through imitation, you'll gain insight. Dear op, if my advice is even slightly helpful to you, I would be very happy, even if it just warms your heart. My actions will have meaning~~.

question: A girl, who doesn't have many friends in class, what should she do?
description: Girls, I don't have many friends in class. Other female classmates always go out to eat and use the restroom together, but I'm always left alone. Previously, I used to hang out with them, but something happened and it seems like they don't want to hang out with me anymore, so I just naturally withdrew. Since it's a science class, there are only four girls, and I don't have a good relationship with the other girl besides them. Although I have good relationships with male classmates, it's not convenient to always hang out with them. I always feel like I'm not good enough or interesting enough to have friends, but I study computer science abroad, and I'm a top student. I have read many books in both English and Chinese, so I think I should be a valuable person. However, I still can't fit in with them. What should I do? I feel very lonely, so lonely that it drives me crazy. What should I do?
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, roommates, classmates, social adaptation.

answers.answer_text: Hello girls~ After reading your description, it seems that you are having a hard time fitting in with your four female classmates in the science class. Feeling excluded is making you frustrated and lonely, is that right? You mentioned that you used to hang out with them and had a good relationship, but something happened and they no longer want to play with you. So, did something unpleasant happen between you and your friends? Or was there a misunderstanding and a lack of communication that led to the end of your friendship? It seems that you still care about your relationship with those two female classmates, right? If there were indeed some misunderstandings causing distance between you, making you feel uncomfortable, after thinking about it calmly, you could take the initiative to have a good chat with them. Whether through text messages or meeting in person, communicate and address the issues, and maybe you can rebuild a friendly relationship. There is no need to feel inadequate or unworthy of having friends because of misunderstandings or because of them. Negative thoughts like these are not helpful. Many times, when we are not recognized, it is easy to develop a sense of inferiority or self-doubt. Feeling that among them, we have lost our value and have been excluded because of our own problems, constantly doubting ourselves and leaving ourselves in a state of isolation. I can sense that deep down, you may lack a sense of security. I'm not sure about your childhood upbringing and your experiences that have shaped you. Perhaps you have been rejected, not recognized, or not valued before, which has made you sensitive and easily feel that others treat you unfriendly, leading you to constantly think that you are "targeted" or "disliked." First of all, you need to break free from this mindset and cycle. You are studying abroad, excelling in computer science, proficient in both Chinese and English, well-read, knowledgeable... these are your shining points and reflect your worth. You should acknowledge and accept these strengths, as they are the result of your hard work. Don't let others' lack of understanding or lack of support make you negate or bury yourself. At the same time, learn to understand yourself. At this stage, you may have a relatively shallow self-identification and your own recognition is built upon others' values. You are very concerned about others' evaluations and opinions of you, making it easy for you to lose yourself. You need to strengthen your subjective awareness and focus less on others, but rather on yourself. Accept your strengths and weaknesses. You have a strong learning ability, but you don't get along well with some classmates. It's okay, relationships are always mutual and the good or bad of a relationship may have reasons from both sides. It doesn't necessarily mean it's all your fault. Everyone needs to constantly learn and grow in relationships. When facing difficulties and problems, if you can firmly stand by your principles and beliefs while also being able to tolerate, understand, accept, and make progress with each other, that would be a healthy, friendly, and positive relationship worth cherishing and salvaging. If it can't withstand the test, breaks with just one slight push, become distant, and even prevent you from being yourself, leading to self-dislike and self-denial, then I think it's better to let go or distance yourself. Do you agree? There is a saying, "Different circles don't necessarily need to forcefully merge." If it is difficult to fit into a "circle of friends," why force yourself? We can still get to know more like-minded friends and companions. As long as we are sincere and genuinely want to be friends with others, they will feel it and treat us with sincerity. The most important thing is not to restrict ourselves and not to get trapped, which will only cause internal conflict. Lastly, I want to say that loneliness is a normal state for humans. It may be related to how well you get along with others. The main thing is to rely on yourself to regulate, learn to be alone with yourself, which is an important and necessary lesson in relationships. Keep up the good work and believe that you are always awesome!

OP, hello ~~~ First, give OP a hug. I can understand from the description that 1. OP and the girls in the class are not close, and OP feels lonely every day. 2. OP feels that they may not be good enough, but can't figure out why they can't have a good relationship with them. [A little analysis and advice] 1. OP mentioned that there aren't many girls in their class, and most of the friends they can make are similar to themselves. OP also mentioned that they have read many books and are essentially an excellent girl. Perhaps it is these parts that OP considers excellent that make other girls feel that there is no conversation or intimacy with OP. But this is also due to the small scope of friends that can be chosen in the class. When OP enters a broader world in the future, perhaps they will be able to find friends who are suitable for them. 2. In addition, to solve the problems in interpersonal relationships, most of the time, one needs to find their own issues in conflicts and make changes. OP should think about the things that caused a distance between them and some friends, and whether there are any lingering concerns. Considering these questions may be helpful for OP's current interpersonal communication. I hope this is helpful for OP.

question: Should I break off this relationship? I have developed feelings for my therapist, what should I do?
description: I went to the school counseling office in Japan to seek advice after a failed presentation in class. The counselor was a professor at the school, but we had no other interaction besides the counseling sessions. I have been going for counseling for two months. I was able to successfully complete the second presentation in class. The counseling was supposed to end, but because I thought this teacher was nice, I ended up chatting with him about some personal things, like my frustrations as an international student and some family matters. Surprisingly, we have been talking for almost a year. I feel like I'm starting to like him more and more, but I don't really know him outside of the counseling room. The sessions are mainly focused on me talking and he occasionally says a few things. He rarely talks about himself. I asked if I could see him more often, but was rejected. I also wanted to give him a gift to show my gratitude, but that was also refused. Finally, I asked him if he didn't like me, and he said it's not a romantic relationship but that doesn't mean he doesn't like me. So, I know that I have been rejected again. But I just wanted to hear him say that he doesn't like me, so I can focus on studying, graduate, and go back home. I don't want to be given any hope. I'm wondering if I should cut off this relationship.

answers.answer_text: Author, hello! Reading your description, what comes to mind is transference of a sexual nature, where the visitor falls in love with the counselor. This type of transference often occurs in opposite-sex counseling relationships. The counseling relationship is a special kind of relationship, unlike any other in daily life, especially considering you are in a foreign land. I understand the warmth and support you receive through counseling! I also understand that studying abroad can be challenging! Sending you a hug! Based on your description, your counselor is adhering to ethical guidelines and counseling boundaries. They did not accept your gifts, did not meet with you outside of counseling sessions, and did not engage in a romantic relationship with you. Let me first introduce the counseling ethics I remember: Establishing clear counseling boundaries is very important, including determining the duration of each counseling session, setting a fixed counseling frequency and time, addressing counseling fees, etc. These boundaries serve to protect both the counselor and the client, and any violation of these boundaries is significant and worth discussing. During counseling, there should be no physical contact, no relationships outside of counseling, no acceptance of gifts, and no romantic relationships between the counselor and client for three years after counseling ends, among other things. These boundaries also provide protection for both the counselor and the client. The counselor should strive to maintain objectivity, neutrality, and anonymity as much as possible. Based on these guidelines, what are your thoughts? Have you discussed this situation with your counselor? If not, I suggest you bring it up and perhaps you will find some answers or reasons. If you have already discussed it and your situation has not changed, you may want to consider discussing it with your counselor again or even considering finding a new counselor. Wishing you the best.

I really understand the current state of the questioner. It is indeed easy for visitors to generate other emotional feelings for counselors because in this process, we express our inner thoughts and emotions to each other, which can easily form dependence. We call this transference. However, it is important to note that because of this, we need to think more about whether this feeling is really a normal love as usual, or if it is mixed with other factors. We may want to calmly think about it and try to have a rational judgement. On the other hand, because the other person is our therapist, it is best to communicate such feelings to them, as it is likely to affect the effectiveness of counseling treatment. The therapist also needs to judge and adjust the treatment plan accordingly.

question: 17-year-old girl, preparing for the college entrance examination, has poor mental state and is very anxious, how to adjust?
description: I used to think that I was doing fine. I could come up with ideas that my classmates couldn't think of. But since this semester started, I feel like my brain doesn't work as well. I have to think for a long time even for simple questions, and I often daydream during class. Even though I know I should work harder, I just can't seem to get motivated. I don't go to bed late at night, but I feel tired during the day. As the college entrance examination is approaching, I feel more and more anxious. I get scared when it's time for exams, and I feel sleepy when I try to study. Is this a problem with my mindset? How can I adjust it? [Feeling frustrated]

answers.answer_text: Hi there, my friend! Reading your description, it seems like you're going through a crucial period of intense studying in your third year of high school, but you're having trouble adjusting your mental state. I completely understand your anxiety. Based on your description, it seems that your state of mind hasn't been as good as before since the beginning of this semester. Your efficiency in studying has decreased, and your sleep quality has also been poor. If you feel like your state of mind has significantly and persistently affected your normal academic life, I recommend seeking medical advice. However, in most cases, the situation can be resolved through appropriate relaxation and rest. One of my friends was particularly anxious before the college entrance exam. Her parents took her on a week-long trip, and they even visited some universities. After returning to school, her state of mind significantly improved, and her grades even improved by a hundred places. So, I suggest not putting too much pressure on yourself and setting aside some time to relax. You might achieve higher efficiency and better results. Remember, learning is a long-term activity that requires perseverance. Face the challenges of each stage with the best possible state of mind.

question: Is it true when they always say everything is for your own good?
description: Is it really for my own good when you always say that all of this is for my own good? I just don't feel it.
keywords: Interpersonal relationships, deception and trust, interpersonal boundaries.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I believe that many people will experience situations like the one you described. In our daily lives, we often hear things like that, all for your own good. Whether it's from parents or relatives and friends, they might all say the same thing. But whether it's good or not, I think each person will measure it according to their own standards. Let's take parents as an example. Parents always say that their decisions are for our own good. We can analyze this. First of all, they would never harm us, and they definitely want us to have a better life. Compared to us, they have much more life experience and knowledge, so we should seriously consider their advice. As for other people, if you feel they aren't looking out for your best interest, you can have your own criteria and you have the right to choose whether to do something or not. If you really think it's not helpful or not for your own good, you can choose not to do it. Best wishes!

question: Aunt Flo is coming soon, and I get easily irritable before her arrival. How can I control my temper?
description: Before Aunt Flo comes, my emotions are always bad. I'm easily irritated and extremely sensitive. How can I avoid feeling so agitated and irritable?

answers.answer_text: "Louzhu, hello~ First, let me give you an encouraging hug. I completely understand how you're feeling right now. This is actually a very normal phenomenon, and many little fairies experience Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS). Although the causes of PMS are still unclear in the medical field, it is generally believed to be related to the roller coaster-like changes in hormones during the luteal phase. In addition to causing uncontrollable mood swings and irritability, it may also lead to bloating, breast tenderness, abdominal discomfort, increased appetite, acne breakouts, and other undesirable conditions. 1. Adjust your lifestyle: a balanced diet and nutrition, regular exercise, and reducing or eliminating the intake of smoking, salt, and coffee can help little fairies smoothly get through the premenstrual phase. 2. Psychological therapy: relax, stay optimistic, and avoid being too hard on yourself. Also, let the people around you know about this, so they can be more understanding and caring. 3. Dietary supplements: Research has shown that daily intake of 80mg of vitamin B6 can help reduce emotional symptoms caused by PMS. (Reference: Baidu) Wish you the best~."

question: Should older single young women stay in first-tier cities or return to their hometown in third-tier cities?
description: I graduated at the age of 24 and moved to Guangzhou. Now, I have been drifting in Guangzhou for 8 years. My career hasn't made much progress, and I am a 32-year-old single woman. My hometown is a third-tier city, and it is very difficult to find a partner at the age of 32. The working environment is not good, and there aren't many good companies. I have never lived in the capital city of my hometown, and I have no relatives there. I have a few classmates, but I am not very familiar with them. If I go back, I will have to start from scratch. Currently, I work in a state-owned enterprise in Guangzhou, and my take-home salary is about 10,000 yuan per month. Over the years, I haven't made any close friends or have any relatives here. I am facing difficulties at work and I feel excluded from the environment, so I want to switch jobs. It is basically like starting from scratch. I handle everything by myself in my work and life in Guangzhou, and I feel very lonely, tired, and exhausted both physically and mentally. Will my work situation be better if I go back? Will it be difficult to find a partner? Guangzhou has much better conditions than my hometown in all aspects. Should I continue to persevere? Should I go back to my hometown or continue to stay in Guangzhou?
keywords: Growth, stress management, work and learning, the meaning of life.

answers.answer_text: Actually, this issue is essentially a lifestyle problem. First of all, you should understand that people have social attributes and are not machines that work without any thoughts after being switched on. People need friends and social activities, otherwise they are prone to psychological problems or mental instability. If, as you said, you only have work and no friends in Guangzhou, then it is imaginable that you may appear exciting in the eyes of others, but when you close the door, you feel like you are nothing. If you think you can accept this situation, then you can continue to stay. But if you feel that you genuinely need a few good friends to occasionally enjoy the good life, or often go out with relatives and friends to travel and have fun, then you can quit your job, use your saved money, and return to your hometown. With that money, you can open a small store to make a living, and then happily paddle with relatives and friends~.

Hello, questioner. The question you asked seems to be about life choices, but in reality, it's about how you perceive yourself. After living in a big city for eight years, you suddenly consider returning to your hometown because you have encountered setbacks in your life here, and you want to solve these setbacks with a simple method - going back home. When you realize that this is your way of thinking, you will realize that it actually cannot solve the problem. Love, work, and interpersonal relationships are all life issues that everyone encounters. Every problem requires wisdom and a calm emotional state to solve. What you need is not someone telling you what choice to make, but asking yourself in your heart, what do you want. And every answer we get comes with both opportunities and challenges. I hope you can find your own answer.

question: I feel empty inside and always hope that someone can take care of and pay attention to me.
description: I recently always involuntarily do things that attract attention or evokes pity. I really hope to have someone to take care of me and pay attention to me, but I can't find anyone. I feel empty inside, and I always subconsciously seek attention from others, which makes people look down on me. What's wrong with me now? How can I find someone like that? How can I stop doing these subconscious things?
keywords: Behavior, please, stay up late, emptiness.

answers.answer_text: Hug, OP~ I can totally understand how you feel. Everyone craves to be cared for, and it's completely normal. [Problem Analysis] The main issue for the OP is the desire for attention, leading them to do things that seek attention or sympathy in the hope of being taken care of. This leads to a sense of emptiness inside, but they don't know how to find someone like that, or how to stop doing things just to seek attention, causing them to feel stuck and upset. [How to Solve] 1. Do things you enjoy and keep yourself busy. If the OP feels a sense of emptiness inside, they can try things they haven't done before or complete things they wanted to do but never got around to due to various reasons. Keeping oneself busy, whether it's reading, writing, traveling, trying different foods, hiking, or exercising, can make one's life more fulfilling and gradually reduce the feeling of emptiness. 2. Showcase your strengths and make more friends. Participate in activities or competitions, make use of your strengths, let more people see your shining points, and at the same time, make friends with different people and get to know others. When your strengths are recognized and you meet like-minded friends, the possibility of finding someone who cares and takes care of you will increase. 3. Strive to improve oneself and naturally attract more attention. People who receive attention usually have outstanding looks, exceptional abilities, or excellent social skills. If you want to be cared for and receive attention, you need to constantly improve yourself. Only when you become outstanding will you attract more people's attention. No need to rush, take it slow, focus on your own development, and everything you want will come. It's not something to worry about; go with the flow and don't let it bother you too much. Wishing you a happy and joyful life, OP~.

Title master, hello, from your description I can feel your loneliness, and I really hope to have someone around to care for and love oneself. Nobel Laureate Koestler once said, "Each person is an island." Perhaps, we have many social relationships and can have many people around us, but in the spiritual sense, we are all islands, and it is difficult for us to surpass our own harbors and reach others' islands. I think dealing with loneliness is a topic that everyone needs to learn. From the moment we separate from our mother's womb, we feel lonely. We must survive as independent individuals. In the process of everyone's growth, parents or caregivers cannot give us 100% unconditional attention and love. We will all have a scarcity of love to some extent. This loneliness and scarcity still exist after adulthood, so we would really like to have someone to care for us, like how parents care for their children. If a person can meet someone who is willing to accompany them unconditionally, it is truly a happy and healing thing. But, dear one, we need to understand that every adult needs to be responsible for themselves. When we were small, we did not have the ability and resources to meet our own needs, so we could only rely on our parents. But now we have grown up and can rely on ourselves to satisfy ourselves, to be the best parents to ourselves. Let's think about what we can do for ourselves when facing loneliness. When we redirect our attention back to ourselves, instead of craving others' approval, we will find that there are many things we can do and many joys to discover in life. I would like to share some things I personally enjoy with you: 1. I have been fond of meditation in recent years, which is a very useful tool for practicing self-connection. When we have emotions, we can also observe them through meditation. 2. Reading and writing. Since 2018, I have been exposed to psychology and have read many books related to psychology, which have greatly helped my life. Domestic authors in the field of psychology, such as Wu Zhihong, Li Xue, and Zhang Defen, as well as foreign authors such as Susan Forward, Scott Peck, and Patsy Evans, are all authors I admire. 3. Try to cultivate an interest for yourself, such as learning a musical instrument, practicing yoga, or taking a course. When we see that we have the ability to accomplish something, it enhances our sense of worth and meaning, and such positive feelings become a driving force for us to move forward, thus forming a virtuous cycle. I have always believed in "I am already complete". Everyone can satisfy themselves and be responsible for themselves through their own efforts. When we start to learn to take responsibility for ourselves, we will realize that happiness is actually in our own hands. I hope my answer can help you. Best wishes to you!

Understandable, the questioner said, "I feel empty inside, and I subconsciously seek attention from others, which makes me feel inferior. What's happening to me?" Understandable, everyone has a psychological need to be loved, a need to be loved. What is the psychology of being loved? It means that we long for recognition, appreciation, and affirmation from others. Getting love from others fundamentally makes us feel that we are being paid attention to, for example, being noticed when we appear, being noticed by our name, listening to our opinions, forgiving our faults, and taking care of our needs. In fact, since childhood, being paid attention to and praised by others is a fundamental need of human beings, and it continues throughout our lives. So the state of mind of the questioner is understandable, as each of us is naturally eager to receive love, comfort, connection, and a sense of security. This longing for a strong and deep emotional connection with someone is called attachment in psychology. Attachment initially stems from our attachment to our parents during infancy and early childhood. When our primitive longing for a response from our parents is met, we feel a sense of fulfillment and security. However, when our longing is rejected or ignored, we feel anxious and restless, and a deep panic about losing contact arises. Although we are now adults, the attachment patterns formed in childhood continue to influence us. The questioner also asks, "How can I find such a person?" In interpersonal relationships, there is a rule: "Treat others as you want to be treated." In other words, if you want someone to love you, you may need to love others first. Although there may be some energy loss in this process, most of it will be reciprocated.

Hello, a big hug for you. Don't feel ashamed, it's very normal. Who hasn't felt empty and lonely at some point? To be honest, I went through a similar phase recently, feeling particularly isolated and wanting someone to accompany me, someone to pay attention to me. So, I downloaded a bunch of social apps and chatted with people, played voice matching games, and stayed up all night chatting. At that time, I really wanted to find someone to be with me. But soon after, I deleted all those apps. I realized that they didn't relieve my loneliness, but instead made me feel worse. Despite chatting with so many people, I couldn't find that person. I gradually understood that some things can't be rushed. The best things take time. Being idle is when the feeling of loneliness is the strongest. Humans need social interaction. We need a sense of belonging. Nowadays, the pace of social life is getting faster and faster, and we're under a lot of mental pressure. We feel our existence is very small, and we need to find someone to vent to. But that person can't be found just by looking for them. We may appear to be living in a group, but inside, we feel incredibly lonely. Those subconscious actions of seeking attention are also meant to let others know that we exist, to briefly make ourselves feel not alone. In reality, it's a way to mask our inner insecurities and anxieties. But the feeling of loneliness has surely been there for a long time, so why does it become particularly strong at certain times? It's all because we have nothing to do. During the period when my loneliness was particularly strong, it was also a time when I didn't know what I should be doing, and I was trapped by inertia and procrastination. When we have nothing to do, we are most susceptible to wandering thoughts (laughs and cries). We need to give ourselves something to do and adjust our mindset, facing this loneliness, emptiness, and solitude with a calm attitude. Keep ourselves busy. Do the things that need to be done well today, don't put them off until tomorrow. Use free time to do the things we love, don't let ourselves get bored. When we do what we need to do well, there will be a sense of pride and satisfaction in our hearts, and we will find the value of our existence. The feeling of not having a presence for others will disappear. As for those subconscious actions to attract attention, don't pay too much attention to them. Constantly improve ourselves and become excellent. At that point, we will confidently believe that we don't need to attract others, just be ourselves. Those actions will gradually fade away. I hope my answer is helpful to you.

Hello! I can sense your anxiety between the lines and I'm sending you a strong hug. I hope my response can be helpful to you. Feeling empty is something that everyone experiences and there's no need to feel ashamed about it. Feeling empty indicates a spiritual void, and if not remedied in a timely manner, it can worsen. So how can we fill this void? First, keep yourself busy: 1. Focus on your work and find your own value and goals within it. Alternatively, use your spare time to learn new skills, which not only keeps you occupied but also helps you become more excellent. 2. Use your free time to read books. When we read, our thoughts travel through other people's stories, and we have less energy to feel bored. Secondly, keep moving: Invite friends to go hiking or running during your free time, or develop a habit of jogging every morning. Physical exhaustion can help offset mental exhaustion. Lastly, regarding your question about how to find someone who can take care of you, I believe it's better to make yourself excellent first. This way, you will meet more outstanding people. Just like planting a field while waiting for a horse to be attracted naturally.

Hello there! It is normal for each of us to want attention and to be understood by others. However, at this moment, your desire for this may be stronger, to the point where you involuntarily do things to seek attention from others. But remember, the person who understands you the most in this world is yourself! The story of finding a likeminded person amidst the mountains and rivers is beautiful because many people long to find their likeminded person, but most people do not succeed. How can you find such a person, you ask? I cannot provide you with something standardized like a mathematical formula to help you find that person. But what I can tell you is that only when you truly be yourself will you encounter them! Your authenticity may sometimes bring you trouble or make you feel troubled yourself, but please trust your own judgment, constantly improve yourself, and one day, that person will appear! There will be a day when the person you want to find will come, and they will be attracted to the real you. Just like a butterfly finding a flower by following its scent! The real you does not need to actively seek attention from others. How can you stop doing those subconscious actions, you ask? My answer is by being focused on yourself. You understand your true feelings, you know your strengths and weaknesses, you understand that there are ways to make your inner self feel happy and fulfilled without just having someone who understands you. You have many secrets that bring you personal joy, and you have many goals that don't need to be announced, but only require you to take one step at a time... It would be lucky to have someone who understands you, right! But we don't need to pursue this kind of luck too ardently, you just need to confidently be yourself. When you become an excellent person who lives up to your own expectations, rather than just trying to meet the expectations of others, when you are content enough to make yourself happy, you may quietly encounter this fortune. Of course, even if you don't, it's okay! Because as you are now, you are already good enough, enough to make yourself happy and content, isn't that right? I hope my answer can help you become your own happiness and understanding!

I relate to that feeling. I have had this feeling for a long time until I came across a book called "The Neglected Child". It doesn't talk about children, but rather about the feeling of being neglected, which can cause a sense of loss and emptiness from seemingly unnoticed small things. The book also provides guidance on how to deal with these feelings as we grow older. I haven't finished reading it yet. I recommend that you take a look and give yourself a hug.

I have experienced a period of extreme despair and loneliness before. I want to share it with you in the hope that it will help you. I used to have two really good colleagues and friends, and we were together for 8 years. We would talk about everything and we were very happy! How many happy 8 years can one have in life? But after a quarrel in June last year, they cut off all contact with me. Since then, I have become a lonely person, feeling very hopeless and empty. Just yesterday, we were happily leaving work together to eat hot pot, take selfies, and go shopping. And now, I have been forced to be alone, while they continue to enjoy hot pot, take selfies, and post on social media. What can I do? After feeling hopeless, I gradually started reading books, learning, exercising, doing yoga, and swimming. I realized that I can do a lot of things by myself! At least these are things I wouldn't have done when there were three of us, because we would always gossip and never run out of things to talk about! And now, I am even seriously and sincerely replying to you, something I couldn't do before. My life has entered a different state of fulfillment now, so am I still lonely? Yes, I am. Every evening, I come home alone after work, and there are no more dinner dates or gatherings. I admit that I still feel lonely, but I know that even if the whole world abandons me, at least I still have books to accompany me! In other words, you can find things that interest you, give yourself energy, and excel secretly. Even being alone can have good weather!

question: 20 years old, especially lacking love (warmth in the family), especially feeling insecure.
description: Why do other people's fathers love their children so much, always thinking about them and considering them in everything? My father always ignores me and tonight he even scolded me because I accidentally dropped a pot. I'm already 20 years old and it's been a long time since someone scolded me like this. I really don't understand, is it necessary to make such a big deal out of something so small? I feel like my father doesn't know anything except for scolding me.

answers.answer_text: Hello, hug you, who is already twenty years old, but was scolded by your dad for breaking a pot. It's indeed a bit frustrating. Have you tried to communicate with your dad? Can you guess why your dad made a big deal out of this small matter? From your description, it seems that there is not much emotional communication between you and your dad. Is it because your dad never expresses his own emotions, or is it because you have different opinions on certain issues? When your mood calms down, try to communicate with your dad properly, changing what can be changed and accepting what cannot be changed, seeking common ground while respecting differences.

question: I do not like my husband's family, often having suicidal thoughts, but I cannot bear to leave my child...
description: and her husband got to know each other and dated for a year and a half. They met each other's parents a few times during this period, once at her parents' house, and each time she would carefully prepare gifts for his parents. The time they went to her house, she led him to the supermarket to buy things. They got married and had a traditional dowry custom in her hometown in 2016. Her parents were rural people, but they were considerate and open-minded. Before the marriage, they had talked to her about the dowry, and they said they would give all the dowry back to her for their life together. Her parents brought up the question of dowry, and her husband initially agreed. However, her future in-laws got involved later on. She could clearly hear her future mother-in-law yelling on the phone, saying that they wanted more dowry. In their village, the bride's parents had already paid the down payment for the house. This was said loudly and clearly, without the speakerphone on. The issue went on for many days, but she, who was severely suffering from morning sickness, couldn't intervene. Eventually, her husband also felt that there was no reason to give his mother money for the wedding. His entire family also doubted the credibility of her parents' words, thinking that they wanted the money for her younger brother's wedding. Her simple and honest parents, I dare not say anything else, but I know that they would never play any tricks on me. They are just trying to make a compromise between the customs of their relatives and friends and their love for me. They just want to transfer the money quickly. They considered everyone's interests. Finally, before they got their marriage certificate, her husband transferred 130,000 yuan to her and even specifically said that if she insisted on giving it to her parents and the money ran out, it would be her problem.
keywords: marriage, concept of marriage, marriage management

answers.answer_text: OP, this will have an impact on both your body and the baby's. Your parents have good intentions, and your husband also cares about you. However, there may be different customs regarding dowries due to regional differences, which lead to different beliefs. I understand that you may feel angry or upset at this time. At this time, perhaps you can communicate with your husband and directly explain your parents' thoughts and the customs in your family. The dowry received can be used for yourselves. I hope that the issue of dowry does not cause harm to you or your relationship with your husband. Communicate with your husband more if there are any issues. Best wishes!

question: How can I forget the person I love after breaking up?
description: I am deeply in love with a girl. We were very happy together. After knowing each other for 7 months, I started to doubt her. For example, I expected her to respond to my messages instantly, and if it took too long, I would think she was chatting with someone else. At the beginning of our relationship, our meetings were normal and she was always happy when we met. But later on, our meetings became fewer and even when I suggested meeting up, she didn't seem very enthusiastic. Sometimes she would even say she had something else to do and would meet next time. I feel like she was just placating me. Does this mean she doesn't love me anymore? We have broken up now, but I still can't forget her. Even if I tell myself to forget her and be resolute, I just can't do it. We haven't contacted each other for a week now. She hasn't reached out to me, and I haven't reached out to her either. But every day, I think of her, and I miss her so much, especially the time we spent together. I can't focus on anything and I feel terrible mentally. I can't let go, and every day feels so exhausting. Please, is there any way to relieve this emotional burden?

answers.answer_text: You love the girl very much and pay a lot of attention to her. However, love often makes people worry and doubt, causing them to have uncontrollable thoughts. These thoughts will unconsciously affect your behavior and attitude, causing cracks in the relationship. Why do we always remember past love affairs? From your description, I see that the previous relationship between you and her was mostly based on your own speculation and doubt, with a lot of "I think", but without deep communication and feedback from her or a definite answer. Therefore, you carry a lot of regrets and unwillingness in your heart, unable to find peace due to this unknown answer. Psychologically, there is a phenomenon called "Zeigarnik effect", which refers to an unfinished emotional attachment. We often worry about and cannot let go of things that are unfinished or without results, attracting a great deal of attention. For example, if we don't end up with our first love, getting married and having children, we will always remember it and give it many beautiful imaginations and speculations, so many people regard first love as the most wonderful emotional experience of their lives. For example, if we start doing something or performing a task, but halfway through we stop and have to do something else, we will inevitably still have concerns about the previous thing, unable to let go and constantly thinking about going back to finish it, resulting in the current task being affected and unable to be done properly. Your current state is because this relationship did not have a satisfying ending, and you didn't get a definite answer. So you carry a lot of regrets and speculations in your heart. This relationship, this girl will continue to occupy a space in your mind until you can find a way to put an end to it. How to have an effective farewell? Numerous speculations and imaginations are not as effective as a real action. Does she not love me? How does she view our relationship? How is she doing now? Do we still have a chance?... Many of your doubts can only be answered by her, and only she can write the complete ending for you. If you are willing, try to gather up the courage to contact her and have an open conversation, express your thoughts and understand her thoughts and attitude, let her answer your questions. Then both parties can part ways amicably. Whether there is still a possibility between you two, whether there is a chance to start again, or whether you can continue as friends, or say goodbye to each other and stop contacting each other, it depends on your own thoughts. Even if she firmly rejects you and does not want to continue contact and communication, it means that she has a clear attitude and response, and you have also obtained a definite answer. Perhaps then you can let go and move on. This is not a form of entanglement, but a responsible attitude, being responsible for her and for yourself. Perhaps she also has many speculations and regrets in her heart. A love affair can begin because of a mysterious fate, but only by parting on good terms and writing a complete ending will there be no regrets. You can also perform some ritualistic acts to bid farewell to this love affair in your heart. For example, pack up items related to her and put them away or throw them away; go on a trip to say goodbye; write down your thoughts and farewell words on paper, then seal them in an envelope; if she is willing, you can go to a place you used to frequent together, spend some time there to properly say goodbye, and then go your separate ways... How to move forward and live for yourself? After bidding farewell to this previous relationship, you need to keep moving forward --① Face your previous emotional experience bravely, review and summarize the lessons you have learned, and see in which aspects you didn't do well enough that led to problems in the relationship, and whether you can change in the future. ② Focus on your own life, pay attention to the people and things around you, and connect with those around you, discovering new opportunities for love in the process. ③ Cultivate your own interests and hobbies, do things that make you happy, and play with people who share the same interests. ④ Think carefully about your life goals and directions, and consider what you need to do to achieve them. Live for yourself and not in the shadow of someone else's past. Then, leave everything to time and let time heal your regrets. Love can make people grow, strive to become better, and you will also find new emotions.

Hello, first of all, I want to give you a hug. I feel like I see someone who yearns for love and is repeatedly overlooked and unable to be satisfied. So, I want to give you a hug and appreciate your perseverance. Now, the question you raised is how to forget someone you love, which means that to some extent, you still love her. Completely forgetting someone you love may take a long time and be somewhat difficult. However, there are some methods to simply let go of this love. First, engage in intimate relationships with others, whether it's a romantic partner or friends. Both individuals will experience a deep integration as the relationship deepens, resulting in a state of "you in me, and me in you." The sudden separation will hurt your sense of self and create a feeling of emptiness from losing a part of yourself. So, on one hand, give yourself some time to heal emotionally. On the other hand, express your pain to trusted family and friends, deepening your relationships, filling the void left by your loved one's departure, and finding warmth through the support of others. Secondly, romantic relationships have the power to alter our hormones. Especially when you truly love someone, the sudden surge of dopamine and serotonin can make you feel great and powerful, like a breath of fresh air. But the sudden heartbreak can cause these hormone levels to rapidly decrease, leading to immense pain, which may even manifest as physical pain. The body's cells renew themselves in approximately 90 days, so as mentioned earlier, give yourself time to let go of the past. Meanwhile, do more things that make you happy, like going out for exercise, reading books, watching movies, socializing with friends, learning new skills, traveling to places you have longed to visit, or treating yourself to something you have wanted to buy for a while. Also, pay attention to maintaining a regular and healthy lifestyle to speed up your body's metabolism and help you recover a stable mindset as soon as possible. Lastly, after discussing emotions and the body, let's talk about memory and thinking. You mentioned that you keep thinking about her, so forcefully trying not to think about her may backfire, causing you to think about her even more. Instead, you can try a different approach - set aside a specific time each day to reminisce about the past, but do so from the perspective of a friend or an outsider, and objectively evaluate everything that happened. Also, clean up your room and your mind, get rid of things related to your loved one that you don't need anymore, and put away the things you still need in a place that is not very visible and not seen on a regular basis. Of course, it should be noted that even if you have forgotten about your loved one, there may still be people and things in the future that will bring back memories. But there's no need to feel disheartened because those are the marks of time and proof of your growth. We grow up through constantly falling and getting back up. The world and I love you.

Hello, dear poster. After reading your words, I feel really sorry for you. It's painful to love someone and then break up. Not being able to have the one you love and being obsessed with pain after the breakup is really difficult. Here's a virtual hug for you. It seems like you still love this person even after the breakup, as you think about them every day and can't do anything without them. I wonder why you broke up and what your thoughts are about this relationship. You mentioned that after being together for seven months, you started to doubt your partner and would message them, hoping for an immediate response. What caused this suspicion? Is there any evidence to support it? How would you feel if they replied immediately? And what if they don't? Does this lack of security in the relationship stem from something that happened? Maybe you could try to reflect on your own state in this relationship and analyze it to gain a better understanding of yourself. As for dealing with your current depression, I have a few suggestions for you: 1. Schedule more activities for yourself each day to keep your mind from wandering. 2. Talk to your family and friends; don't isolate yourself. 3. Go out and get some fresh air, exposing yourself to different environments to help relax your mind. 4. If you find that you can't change on your own, seek help from a professional psychotherapist. Hopefully, these suggestions can be of help to you. Wish you all the best!

Hello, I personally think that you need to examine whether you truly love her. If you do, then it does indeed take some time to move on from the relationship. If, after examining yourself, you realize that you only have a possessive desire for her rather than what is known as love, then there is no need to say that you really need to move on. It just means that you haven't found someone else to confide in yet. Thank you.

question: 14-year-old girl, parents divorced when she was young and have been quarreling. Then both found new partners.
description: When I was young, my family was quite wealthy. However, my father loved playing mahjong and ended up selling the car and house to invest in a distant relative's business. But that relative took the money and ran away. After that, my parents always fought. First, my father had an affair, and I think I found out before my mother because she was not at home for a short period of time. Later, my father also left, leaving just my mother and me. Recently, my mother has been bringing a man from her workplace to have dinner at home several times. They also chat on WeChat, probably thinking that I don't know. I don't know where she got the three necklaces worth over 5000 dollars that she has been wearing recently. I feel anxious every day.
keywords: Emotions, healing methods, anxiety emotions, emotional regulation

answers.answer_text: Hello, seeing your situation, I feel very sorry for you and want to give you a big hug! Your parents' divorce has caused you harm and made you feel insecure, especially now that your only source of support, your mother, has a boyfriend. You are afraid that she will leave you like your father did. Here are a few suggestions that I hope can help you: 1. Have a serious conversation with your parents about your condition, why you feel anxious, and express that you don't want to lose them and hope they can show you more love. Don't let the start or end of a relationship sever your blood and kinship. 2. Confide in close friends or classmates about your current feelings. It's okay to cry and not keep suppressing yourself. 3. If you don't have any close friends, you can also talk to your teacher about your situation. 4. Shift your focus to things you enjoy and try not to dwell on things that upset you, or devote yourself to your studies. 5. Read good books and learn more to improve your current situation. I recommend a book called "Lolisa in Dilemma" (Imaginary National Children's Book) to you, hoping it can help you. Once again, a hug to you, sweetheart, every child is an angel! Lastly, I still hope that divorced parents pay more attention to their children's growth, as they are the most innocent. Don't let them be harmed because of you, affecting their entire lives!

question: It's very sad and dark, nothing has meaning anymore, and I want to end the pain by committing suicide.
description: I just want to know if there is any suicide method that is painless and not distressing, as I feel very sad and dark, and everything seems meaningless.

answers.answer_text: Hello, I'm glad to answer for you. I understand your pain and feeling that many things have no meaning. What happened to you that made you so sad? Or is it something else? Since you are in this world, you should live for yourself. My situation now is similar to yours, and I also feel that life is very bleak. I have no motivation and I hate myself, but even though I am suffering, I am still persevering. Sometimes I cry a lot and feel exhausted. Living every day with a blank expression. There are many people in this world who are trying to live, and life is indeed tough. Don't you have any attachment to this world? Have you encountered any difficulties? Try talking to someone and expressing your feelings, it may make a difference. It will be very uncomfortable to keep everything inside. Suicide will be very painful, so be strong. You're still so young, there are many wonderful things to see. Whatever you are sad about, we can all help you. Speak out, okay? Crying it out will make you feel much better. I hope you can bravely face it, we are always here to support you, right behind you.

Hello, I'm sorry to hear that you're not feeling well. I really feel for you. 1. You mentioned that you want a painless way to commit suicide. This kind of thought probably comes from your fear of pain and your desire to avoid the difficulties you're facing. But dear, the pain that comes with suicide can be far greater than the pain of facing and solving problems. Moreover, if you unfortunately succeed, you will transfer even greater pain onto your loved ones and friends. If you fail, you may also be left with long-term consequences. So I hope you can take a moment to calm down, take a deep breath, get a good night's sleep, and think about how you can solve the problems tomorrow. 2. Here are some personal suggestions: you can confide in your friends and family, ask them to help you come up with solutions; if you feel your emotions are abnormal and can't resolve them, I suggest seeking help from a counselor or psychologist; take care of yourself and stay away from things that make you want to harm yourself. I hope this can help you. Take care! The world loves you.

I don't know what you have been through that made you think of suicide. You are afraid of pain and don't want to endure the pain of being alive. You hope for a painless way to commit suicide. I have thought about it carefully, but it seems that there is no foolproof painless method. The methods that seem "painless" in movies, to be realistic, all have their own pains, and some have a high probability of failure, resulting in disabling consequences. If you are willing, you can privately message me and tell me your story. I'm not sure if I can help you, but as a mother, I can't bear to see a young life leaving like this. I always hope that every child who comes into this world can experience happiness.

Dear OP, at this moment, you still feel pain. When we let pain flow within our bodies, it will gradually nourish us, and perhaps in the future, we will gain a new strength from it. Also, don't forget that you can take a break, pause for a moment. Time is meant to be felt, and we still have time. When you're tired, take a rest.

question: How to overcome the fear caused by wandering thoughts?
description: When alone at home, sometimes a person may inexplicably worry if there are bad people hiding behind the door or under the bed. They may wonder if there are thieves or burglars breaking in. How does this happen and how can one avoid scaring themselves with such imagined thoughts?

answers.answer_text: Hello ~ I understand your feelings very well, sending you a hug ~ Sometimes having such thoughts is quite normal, but it may be due to some underlying insecurity. First of all, I suggest closing the doors and windows when you are at home, as it will give you a sense of being protected. Secondly, since it is the content of your imagination that makes you feel worried, you can fully utilize your imagination. You can buy a doll resembling a police officer or a superhero and imagine that they are very powerful and can easily deal with all the bad guys. You can place it in the living room or bedroom. You can also imagine yourself having superpowers and defeating the villains in various ways. Of course, if your worries are happening frequently and at a high level, you may need to undergo some psychological evaluation.

question: 16 years old, in sophomore year of high school, always feels inexplicably anxious, occurring every two days, lasting for a year and a half?
description: Eighth grade, first semester of high school, physical discomfort combined with stress and some academic matters, I always fall asleep in class, which then leads to anxiety. I thought this could be resolved, but even when I try to adjust and restore my study state, this anxiety comes back every two days. I break out in a cold sweat, lose my appetite (I used to be a foodie), feel restless, have a confused and tight mind, and speak uncontrollably fast. I am anxious about all of these things. It comes suddenly without any warning signs, but it has a very negative impact on me.

answers.answer_text: "OP, hello~~~ Sending you a warm hug. From your description, I understand that you are currently troubled by some inexplicable anxiety that occurs periodically. I don't know how to deal with it either. First, let's try to identify the reasons for our anxiety. In your description, you mentioned that these problems began in ninth grade. Let's recall whether it was caused by certain things in ninth grade, such as the pressure of the high school entrance exam, etc. On the other hand, we can try to record our emotions and the events that occur before and after each episode of anxiety to see if there are any commonalities, such as if it always happens before exams, etc. These commonalities may be important factors influencing it. Secondly, in dealing with these emotions, we can try to find solutions from exceptional situations, referring to situations where these emotional fluctuations do not occur. See if there are any favorable factors that help us get through this process. These are some possible ways that I thought of that may be helpful in resolving the issue. However, if you find that these situations are becoming increasingly severe and you are unable to control them, we also need to seek help from professionals for diagnosis and analysis."

question: I am a mother of two children, how can I determine if I am mentally healthy?
description: I think I have some psychological problems. I was very introverted when I was a child, and I hardly had any friends. Even now, as a mother of two children, I still don't have any friends. I worry that my eldest child will be like me, having poor interpersonal relationships, and I don't know what to do about it.

answers.answer_text: Hello~ I completely understand your feelings, sending you a big hug~ If you have any concerns about your mental health, you can go for a professional and comprehensive mental health test. This method will help you have a better understanding of your psychological state and also provide you with methods to improve your condition. Parents have a significant influence on their children, but it doesn't mean that children will have the same problems as their parents. Often, we should trust that children can handle their own matters and provide them with enough trust and care. Being introverted itself is not a problem, and the development of interpersonal relationships is also influenced by many factors. Perhaps what you need to pay more attention to is your current state of anxiety. Do not pass on your anxiety to your child; instead, create a safe and calm environment for them. It is important to realize that no one is perfect, including parents. Children do not need parents to do too much for them; what is crucial is providing them with emotional support and care. Wishing you well~

question: "People say that even if it is advice, it is difficult to have a positive attitude to face it."
